## English text

# Genesis

The Apostolic Bible. Public domain. https://apostolic-bible.ysys9.chatgpt.site/license.html


## Chapter 1

Genesis 1:1 In the beginning, God made the heaven and the earth.
Genesis 1:2 But the earth was invisible and unprepared, and darkness was over the abyss, and the Spirit of God was moving over the water.
Genesis 1:3 And God said: Let light come to be, and light came to be.
Genesis 1:4 And God saw the light, that it was good: and God separated the light from the darkness.
Genesis 1:5 And God called the light day, and he called the darkness night. Evening and morning happened: Day One.
Genesis 1:6 And God said: Let there come to be a firmament in the midst of the water, and let it divide water from water: and it happened this way.
Genesis 1:7 And God made the firmament, and God divided the water which was below the firmament from the water which was above the firmament.
Genesis 1:8 And God called the firmament heaven, and God saw that it was good. Evening and morning happened: The Second Day.
Genesis 1:9 And God said: Let the water beneath the heaven be gathered into one gathering, and let dry land appear, and the water beneath the heaven was gathered together into their gatherings, and the dry land appeared.
Genesis 1:10 And God called the dry land earth, and he called the gatherings of the waters the seas. And God saw that it was good.
Genesis 1:11 And God said: Let the earth bring forth vegetation: plants with seeds of the same kind of plant, and fruit trees with fruit containing seeds of the same kind of tree on the earth: and it happened this way.
Genesis 1:12 And the earth grew plants: plants that produce seeds of the same kind of plant, and fruit-growing trees that produce fruit containing seeds of the same kind of fruit tree on the earth: And God saw that it was good.
Genesis 1:13 And evening and morning happened: the Third Day.
Genesis 1:14 And God said let there come to be lights in the firmament of heaven, for the illumination of the earth: For the distinguishing of the middle of the day from the middle of the night. And let them be for signs, seasons, days, and years.
Genesis 1:15 And let them be for illumination in the firmament of heaven, so as to shine upon the earth: and it happened this way.
Genesis 1:16 And God made the stars and two great lights, the greater for ruling the day, and the lesser for ruling the night.
Genesis 1:17 And God placed them in the firmament of heaven so as to shine upon the earth.
Genesis 1:18 To rule the day and the night, and to separate light from darkness. And God saw that it was good.
Genesis 1:19 And evening and morning happened: The Fourth Day.
Genesis 1:20 And God said: let the waters bring forth crawling creatures with souls, and living flying creatures that fly over the earth along the firmament of the heaven. And it happened this way.
Genesis 1:21 And God made the large sea creatures: Every kind of living and creeping creature that the waters brought forth, and every kind of flying creature: And God saw that it was good.
Genesis 1:22 And God blessed them, saying: Increase, multiply, and fill the waters in the seas. And let the flying creatures multiply upon the earth.
Genesis 1:23 And evening and morning happened: The Fifth Day.
Genesis 1:24 And God said: let the earth bring forth living creatures with souls: four footed creatures, creeping creatures, and wild animals each according to their own kind: and it happened this way.
Genesis 1:25 And God made the wild animals of the earth according to their kind, and the livestock according to their kind, and all the creatures that crawl on the earth according to their kind. And God saw that it was good.
Genesis 1:26 And God said: let us make man according to our image and according to our likeness, and let them rule the fish of the sea, the flying creatures of the sky, the livestock, and all the creatures that crawl upon the earth.
Genesis 1:27 And God made the man in the image of God: he made them male and female.
Genesis 1:28 And God blessed them, saying: Increase, multiply, and fill the earth. Rule over it, and rule the fish of the sea, and the flying creatures in the sky, and all the livestock, and every creature that crawls on the earth.
Genesis 1:29 And God said: Behold, I have given you every seed producing plant on earth, and every fruit tree that grows fruits containing seeds as food for you.
Genesis 1:30 And to all the wild animals on earth, and to all the flying creatures in the sky, and to every creature that crawls on earth that has a soul, I have given every green plant as food. And it happened this way.
Genesis 1:31 And God beheld that all of the things he had made were exceedingly good. And evening and morning happened: The Sixth Day. 

## Chapter 2

Genesis 2:1 And the heaven and the earth were finished, and the whole cosmos of them. 
Genesis 2:2 And on the Sixth Day God finished the works which he made, and he rested on the Seventh Day from all the works which he made.
Genesis 2:3 And God blessed the Seventh Day and sanctified it, because in it God ceased from all his works that he began to do.
Genesis 2:4 This is the book of the genesis of heaven and earth, when they were made, the day God made the heaven and the earth,
Genesis 2:5 And every green plant of the field before growing on the earth, and every plant of the field before it sprang up, for God had not yet caused it to rain upon the earth, and there was no man to cultivate the earth.
Genesis 2:6 But a spring was flowing up from the earth and watering the whole face of the earth.
Genesis 2:7 And God formed the man from the dust of the earth, and breathed onto his face the breath of life, and the man became a living soul.
Genesis 2:8 And towards the east the Lord God planted a paradise in Eden, and placed the man he had made there.
Genesis 2:9 And God caused every tree beautiful to behold and good for food to spring up from the earth, and the tree of life in the middle of paradise, and the tree of knowing knowledge of good and evil.
Genesis 2:10 And a river flows from Eden to water the paradise; thence it is divided into four heads.
Genesis 2:11 The name of one is Phison, this is the one which encircles all the land of Evilat, where there is gold.
Genesis 2:12 And the gold of that land is good, and there is carbuncle and green stone.
Genesis 2:13 And the name of the second river is Geon, this one encircles all of the land of Ethiopia.
Genesis 2:14 And the third river is the Tigris, this one flows across from the Assyrians. And the fourth river is the Euphrates.
Genesis 2:15 And the Lord God took the man that he made, and placed him in paradise to cultivate it and to guard it.
Genesis 2:16 And the Lord God commanded Adam, saying, you shall eat from every tree in paradise.
Genesis 2:17 But you shall not eat from the tree of knowing good and evil, and whatever day you eat from it, you shall die the death.
Genesis 2:18 And the Lord God said: it is not good for the man to be alone, let us make a suitable helper for him.
Genesis 2:19 And God formed all the beasts of the field and birds of heaven from the earth, and brought them to Adam to see what he would call them, and every living soul was named whatever Adam called it. 
Genesis 2:20 And Adam called names for all the cattle and for all the flying creatures of heaven and for all the beasts of the field, but for Adam no helper like him was found. –
Genesis 2:21 And God cast a trance upon Adam, and put him to sleep; and he took one of his sides and filled up flesh in its place.
Genesis 2:22 And the Lord God built the side, which he took from Adam, into a woman and brought her to Adam.
Genesis 2:23 And Adam said: This now is bone from my bones and flesh from my flesh; she shall be called Woman, because she was taken from her man.
Genesis 2:24 Because of this, a man will leave his father and his mother and will be joined to his woman, and the two will be one flesh.
Genesis 2:25 And the two were naked, both Adam and his woman, and they were not ashamed.

## Chapter 3

Genesis 3:1 But the serpent was the most discerning of all the beasts upon the earth, which the Lord God made; and the serpent said to the woman: Why is it that God said: You shall certainly not eat from every tree that is in the paradise?
Genesis 3:2 And the woman said to the serpent: From fruit of a tree of the paradise we shall eat,
Genesis 3:3 but from fruit of the tree which is in the middle of the paradise, God said: You shall not eat from it, nor shall you touch it at all, lest you die.
Genesis 3:4 And the serpent said to the woman: You shall not die the death;
Genesis 3:5 for God knew that on whatever day you eat from it, your eyes will be opened, and you will be as gods, knowing good and evil.
Genesis 3:6 And the woman saw that the tree was good for food, and that it was pleasing for the eyes to see, and it was beautiful for understanding; and having taken from its fruit, she ate. And she also gave to her man with her, and they ate.
Genesis 3:7 And the eyes of the two were opened, and they knew that they were naked, and they sewed leaves of a fig tree and made girdles for themselves.
Genesis 3:8 And they heard the voice of the Lord God walking in the paradise toward evening, and both Adam and his woman hid themselves from the face of the Lord God in the midst of the tree of the paradise.
Genesis 3:9 And the Lord God called Adam and said to him: Adam, where are you?
Genesis 3:10 And he said to him: I heard your voice while you were walking in the paradise, and I was afraid, because I am naked, and I hid myself.
Genesis 3:11 And he said to him: Who announced to you that you are naked? Did you eat from the tree of which I commanded you—this alone—not to eat from it?
Genesis 3:12 And Adam said: The woman whom you gave with me, she gave me from the tree, and I ate.
Genesis 3:13 And the Lord God said to the woman: What is this you did? And the woman said: The serpent deceived me, and I ate.
Genesis 3:14 And the Lord God said to the serpent: Because you did this, accursed are you from all the cattle and from all the beasts of the earth; upon your breast and your belly you shall go, and earth you shall eat all the days of your life.
Genesis 3:15 And I will set enmity between you and between the woman, and between your seed and between her seed; he will watch your head, and you will watch his heel.
Genesis 3:16 And to the woman he said: Multiplying, I will multiply your sorrows and your groaning; in sorrows you shall bear children. And your turning will be toward your man, and he will rule over you.
Genesis 3:17 But to Adam he said: Because you listened to the voice of your woman and ate from the tree of which I commanded you—this alone—not to eat from it, accursed is the earth in your works; in sorrows you shall eat it all the days of your life.
Genesis 3:18 It will cause thorns and thistles to spring up for you, and you shall eat the grass of the field.
Genesis 3:19 In the sweat of your face you shall eat your bread until your returning to the earth from which you were taken; because you are earth, and into earth you will depart. –
Genesis 3:20 And Adam called the name of his woman Life, because she was the mother of all the living.
Genesis 3:21 And the Lord God made tunics of skin for Adam and his woman and clothed them. –
Genesis 3:22 And God said: Behold, Adam has become as one of us, to know good and evil, and now, lest he stretch out his hand and take from the tree of life and eat and live forever.
Genesis 3:23 And the Lord God sent him out from the paradise of delight to work the earth from which he was taken.
Genesis 3:24 And he cast Adam out and settled him opposite the paradise of delight, and appointed the cherubim and the flaming sword that turns, to guard the way of the tree of life.

## Chapter 4

Genesis 4:1 Now Adam knew Eva his woman, and having conceived she bore Cain and said: I acquired a man through God.
Genesis 4:2 And she added to bear his brother Abel. And Abel became a shepherd of sheep, but Cain was working the earth.
Genesis 4:3 And it happened after days that Cain brought from the fruits of the earth a sacrifice to the Lord,
Genesis 4:4 and Abel also brought from the firstborn of his sheep and from their fat portions. And God looked upon Abel and upon his gifts,
Genesis 4:5 but to Cain and to his sacrifices he did not attend. And Cain was exceedingly grieved, and his face fell.
Genesis 4:6 And the Lord God said to Cain: Why have you become deeply grieved, and why has your face fallen?
Genesis 4:7 Is it not that, if you offer rightly but do not divide rightly, you sinned? Be still; his turning is toward you, and you shall rule over him.
Genesis 4:8 And Cain said to Abel his brother: Let us go through into the plain. And it happened while they were in the plain that Cain rose against Abel his brother and killed him.
Genesis 4:9 And God said to Cain: Where is Abel your brother? But he said: I do not know. Am I my brother’s guard?
Genesis 4:10 And God said: What did you do? A voice of your brother’s blood cries to me from the earth.
Genesis 4:11 And now, accursed are you from the earth, which opened wide her mouth to receive your brother’s blood from your hand;
Genesis 4:12 because you work the earth, it will no longer continue to give its strength to you; groaning and trembling you will be upon the earth.
Genesis 4:13 And Cain said to the Lord: My guilt is greater than that I be forgiven;
Genesis 4:14 if you cast me out today from the face of the earth, and from your face I shall be hidden, then I will be groaning and trembling upon the earth, and it will be that everyone finding me will kill me.
Genesis 4:15 And the Lord God said to him: Not so; everyone who kills Cain shall suffer seven avenging penalties. And the Lord God placed a sign for Cain so that no one finding him would kill him.
Genesis 4:16 And Cain went out from the face of God and dwelt in the land of Naid opposite Edem.
Genesis 4:17 And Cain knew his woman, and having conceived she bore Enoch; and he was building a city, and he named the city after the name of his son Enoch.
Genesis 4:18 And to Enoch was born Gaidad, and Gaidad begot Maiel, and Maiel begot Mathousala, and Mathousala begot Lamech.
Genesis 4:19 And Lamech took two women for himself; the name of the one was Ada, and the name of the second Sella.
Genesis 4:20 And Ada bore Jobel; he was the father of those dwelling in tents, cattle breeders.
Genesis 4:21 And the name of his brother was Joubal; he was the one who demonstrated psaltery and lyre.
Genesis 4:22 And Sella also bore Thobel, and he was a hammering smith of bronze and iron; and the sister of Thobel was Noema.
Genesis 4:23 And Lamech said to his women: Ada and Sella, hear my voice; women of Lamech, give ear to my words, because I killed a man for a wound to me and a young man for a bruise to me,
Genesis 4:24 because vengeance has been exacted seven times from Cain, but seventy-seven times from Lamech.
Genesis 4:25 And Adam knew Eva his woman, and having conceived she bore a son and named his name Seth, saying: For God raised up another seed for me in place of Abel, whom Cain killed.
Genesis 4:26 And to Seth there came to be a son, and he named his name Enos; he hoped to call upon the name of the Lord God.

## Chapter 5

Genesis 5:1 This is the book of the genesis of men; on the day God made Adam, according to God’s image he made him;
Genesis 5:2 male and female he made them, and he blessed them. And he named their name Adam on the day he made them.
Genesis 5:3 And Adam lived two hundred thirty years and begot according to his form and according to his image, and named his name Seth.
Genesis 5:4 And the days of Adam after his begetting Seth were seven hundred years, and he begot sons and daughters.
Genesis 5:5 And all the days of Adam which he lived were nine hundred thirty years, and he died.
Genesis 5:6 And Seth lived two hundred five years and begot Enos.
Genesis 5:7 And Seth lived after his begetting Enos seven hundred seven years, and he begot sons and daughters.
Genesis 5:8 And all the days of Seth were nine hundred twelve years, and he died.
Genesis 5:9 And Enos lived one hundred ninety years and begot Cainan.
Genesis 5:10 And Enos lived after his begetting Cainan seven hundred fifteen years, and he begot sons and daughters.
Genesis 5:11 And all the days of Enos were nine hundred five years, and he died.
Genesis 5:12 And Cainan lived one hundred seventy years and begot Maleleel.
Genesis 5:13 And Cainan lived after his begetting Maleleel seven hundred forty years, and he begot sons and daughters.
Genesis 5:14 And all the days of Cainan were nine hundred ten years, and he died.
Genesis 5:15 And Maleleel lived one hundred sixty-five years and begot Jared.
Genesis 5:16 And Maleleel lived after his begetting Jared seven hundred thirty years, and he begot sons and daughters.
Genesis 5:17 And all the days of Maleleel were eight hundred ninety-five years, and he died.
Genesis 5:18 And Jared lived one hundred sixty-two years and begot Enoch.
Genesis 5:19 And Jared lived after his begetting Enoch eight hundred years, and he begot sons and daughters.
Genesis 5:20 And all the days of Jared were nine hundred sixty-two years, and he died.
Genesis 5:21 And Enoch lived one hundred sixty-five years and begot Mathousala.
Genesis 5:22 And Enoch pleased God for two hundred years after his begetting Mathousala, and he begot sons and daughters.
Genesis 5:23 And all the days of Enoch were three hundred sixty-five years.
Genesis 5:24 And Enoch pleased God and was not found, because God transferred him.
Genesis 5:25 And Mathousala lived one hundred sixty-seven years and begot Lamech.
Genesis 5:26 And Mathousala lived after his begetting Lamech eight hundred two years, and he begot sons and daughters.
Genesis 5:27 And all the days of Mathousala which he lived were nine hundred sixty-nine years, and he died.
Genesis 5:28 And Lamech lived one hundred eighty-eight years and begot a son
Genesis 5:29 and named his name Noah, saying: This one will give us rest from our works and from the sorrows of our hands and from the earth which the Lord God cursed.
Genesis 5:30 And Lamech lived after his begetting Noah five hundred sixty-five years, and he begot sons and daughters.
Genesis 5:31 And all the days of Lamech were seven hundred fifty-three years, and he died.
Genesis 5:32 And Noah was five hundred years old, and Noah begot three sons: Sem, Cham, Japheth.

## Chapter 6

Genesis 6:1 And it happened when men began to become many upon the earth, and daughters were born to them.
Genesis 6:2 And the sons of God, seeing the daughters of men, that they were beautiful, took women for themselves from all whom they chose.
Genesis 6:3 And the Lord God said: My spirit shall certainly not remain in these men forever, because they are flesh; but their days will be one hundred twenty years.
Genesis 6:4 Now the giants were upon the earth in those days and after that, whenever the sons of God would go in to the daughters of men and would beget for themselves; those were the giants of old, the renowned men.
Genesis 6:5 And the Lord God, seeing that the evils of men had multiplied upon the earth, and that everyone carefully thinks in his heart upon evil things all the days,
Genesis 6:6 then God considered that he had made man upon the earth, and he pondered.
Genesis 6:7 And God said: I will wipe away man whom I made from the face of the earth, from man as far as cattle and from creeping creatures as far as the flying creatures of heaven, because I became angry that I made them.
Genesis 6:8 But Noah found grace before the Lord God.
Genesis 6:9 Now these are the generations of Noah. Noah was a just man, being perfect in his generation; Noah pleased God.
Genesis 6:10 And Noah begot three sons: Sem, Cham, Japheth.
Genesis 6:11 But the earth was corrupted before God, and the earth was filled with injustice.
Genesis 6:12 And the Lord God saw the earth, and it was corrupted, because every flesh corrupted his way upon the earth.
Genesis 6:13 And God said to Noah: The time of every man has come before me, because the earth was filled with injustice from them; and behold, I am destroying them and the earth.
Genesis 6:14 Therefore make yourself an ark from squared timbers. You shall make the ark into nests and asphalt it inside and outside with asphalt.
Genesis 6:15 And thus you shall make the ark: the length of the ark shall be three hundred cubits, and the width fifty cubits, and its height thirty cubits.
Genesis 6:16 Gathering together, you shall make the ark, and you shall finish it to a cubit above. And you shall make the door of the ark from the sides; with lower, second, and third stories you shall make it.
Genesis 6:17 But I, behold, am bringing the flood, water upon the earth, to destroy every flesh in which there is a spirit of life beneath heaven; and whatever is upon the earth will come to an end.
Genesis 6:18 And I will establish my covenant with you; and you shall enter into the ark, you and your sons and your woman and the women of your sons with you.
Genesis 6:19 And from all the cattle and from all the creeping creatures and from all the beasts and from every flesh, two by two from all you shall bring into the ark, so that you may nourish them with yourself; male and female they shall be.
Genesis 6:20 From all the birds, the flying creatures according to kind, and from all the cattle according to kind, and from all the creeping creatures that creep upon the earth according to their kind, two by two from all will enter toward you to be nourished with you, male and female.
Genesis 6:21 And you shall take for yourself from all the foods which you will eat and gather them to yourself, and it shall be for you and for them to eat.
Genesis 6:22 And Noah did all things, as many as the Lord God commanded him; thus he did.

## Chapter 7

Genesis 7:1 And the Lord God said to Noah: Enter, you and all your house, into the ark, because I saw you as just before me in this generation.
Genesis 7:2 And from the clean cattle bring in toward you seven by seven, male and female, but from the cattle that are not clean two by two, male and female,
Genesis 7:3 and from the clean flying creatures of heaven seven by seven, male and female, and from the flying creatures that are not clean two by two, male and female, to sustain seed upon all the earth.
Genesis 7:4 For yet seven days, and I am bringing rain upon the earth for forty days and forty nights, and I will wipe away every thing that has arisen which I made from the face of the earth.
Genesis 7:5 And Noah did all things, as many as the Lord God commanded him.
Genesis 7:6 Now Noah was six hundred years old, and the flood of water came to be upon the earth.
Genesis 7:7 And Noah and his sons and his woman and the women of his sons with him entered into the ark because of the water of the flood.
Genesis 7:8 And from the flying creatures and from the clean cattle and from the cattle that were not clean and from all the creeping creatures upon the earth,
Genesis 7:9 two by two they entered toward Noah into the ark, male and female, just as God commanded him.
Genesis 7:10 And it happened after the seven days that the water of the flood came to be upon the earth.
Genesis 7:11 In the six hundredth year in the life of Noah, in the second month, on the twenty-seventh of the month, on that day all the springs of the abyss burst, and the floodgates of heaven were opened,
Genesis 7:12 and the rain came upon the earth for forty days and forty nights.
Genesis 7:13 On that day Noah, Sem, Cham, Japheth, the sons of Noah, and Noah’s woman and the three women of his sons with him entered into the ark.
Genesis 7:14 And all the beasts according to kind and all the cattle according to kind and every creeping creature moving upon the earth according to kind and every flying creature according to kind
Genesis 7:15 entered toward Noah into the ark, two by two from every flesh in which there is a spirit of life.
Genesis 7:16 And those entering, male and female from every flesh, entered, just as God commanded Noah. And the Lord God closed the ark from outside him.
Genesis 7:17 And the flood came to be for forty days and forty nights upon the earth, and the water multiplied and lifted the ark, and it was raised from the earth.
Genesis 7:18 And the water prevailed and multiplied exceedingly upon the earth, and the ark was borne above the water.
Genesis 7:19 And the water prevailed exceedingly, exceedingly upon the earth and covered all the high mountains which were beneath heaven.
Genesis 7:20 The water was raised fifteen cubits above and covered all the high mountains.
Genesis 7:21 And every flesh moving upon the earth died—of the flying creatures and the cattle and the beasts—and every creeping creature moving upon the earth, and every man.
Genesis 7:22 And all things that have breath of life, and everyone who was upon dry land, died.
Genesis 7:23 And he wiped away every standing thing which was upon the face of all the earth, from man as far as cattle and creeping creatures and the flying creatures of heaven, and they were wiped away from the earth. And Noah alone was left, and those with him in the ark.
Genesis 7:24 And the water was raised upon the earth for one hundred fifty days.

## Chapter 8

Genesis 8:1 And God remembered Noah and all the beasts and all the cattle and all the flying creatures and all the creeping creatures, as many as were with him in the ark; and God brought a wind upon the earth, and the water subsided,
Genesis 8:2 and the springs of the abyss and the floodgates of heaven were covered, and the rain from heaven was held back.
Genesis 8:3 And the water was receding as it went from the earth; the water receded and diminished after one hundred fifty days.
Genesis 8:4 And the ark settled in the seventh month, on the twenty-seventh of the month, upon the mountains of Ararat.
Genesis 8:5 And the water, as it went, diminished until the tenth month; but in the eleventh month, on the first of the month, the heads of the mountains were seen. –
Genesis 8:6 And it happened after forty days that Noah opened the window of the ark which he made,
Genesis 8:7 and sent out the raven to see whether the water had abated; and having gone out, it did not return until the water dried from the earth.
Genesis 8:8 And he sent out the dove after it to see whether the water had abated from the face of the earth;
Genesis 8:9 and the dove, not finding a resting place for its feet, returned to him into the ark, because water was over every face of all the earth; and stretching out his hand, he took it and brought it in to himself into the ark.
Genesis 8:10 And having waited yet another seven days, he again sent the dove out from the ark.
Genesis 8:11 And the dove returned to him toward evening and had an olive leaf, a twig, in its mouth, and Noah knew that the water had abated from the earth.
Genesis 8:12 And having waited yet another seven days, he again sent the dove out, and it did not continue to return to him any more. –
Genesis 8:13 And it happened in the six hundred first year in the life of Noah, in the first month, on the first of the month, that the water disappeared from the earth; and Noah uncovered the roof of the ark which he made and saw that the water had disappeared from the face of the earth.
Genesis 8:14 And in the second month, on the twenty-seventh of the month, the earth was dried.
Genesis 8:15 And the Lord God said to Noah, saying:
Genesis 8:16 Come out from the ark, you and your woman and your sons and the women of your sons with you,
Genesis 8:17 and bring out with yourself all the beasts, as many as are with you, and every flesh from flying creatures as far as cattle, and every creeping creature moving upon the earth; and increase and multiply upon the earth.
Genesis 8:18 And Noah and his woman and his sons and the women of his sons with him came out,
Genesis 8:19 and all the beasts and all the cattle and every flying creature and every creeping creature moving upon the earth according to their kind came out from the ark.
Genesis 8:20 And Noah built an altar to God and took from all the clean cattle and from all the clean flying creatures and offered whole burnt offerings upon the altar.
Genesis 8:21 And the Lord God smelled a scent of fragrance, and the Lord God, having considered, said: I will no longer continue to curse the earth because of the works of men, because the mind of man is carefully set upon evil things from youth; therefore I will no longer continue to strike every living flesh as I did.
Genesis 8:22 All the days of the earth, seedtime and harvest, cold and heat, summer and spring, day and night, shall not cease.

## Chapter 9

Genesis 9:1 And God blessed Noah and his sons and said to them: Increase and multiply and fill the earth and rule over it.
Genesis 9:2 And your terror and fear will be upon all the beasts of the earth and upon all the birds of heaven and upon all the things moving upon the earth and upon all the fish of the sea; I have given them under your hands.
Genesis 9:3 And every creeping thing that is living shall be food for you; as the green plants, I have given you all things.
Genesis 9:4 Only, flesh with blood of life you shall not eat.
Genesis 9:5 For indeed your blood, that of your souls, I will require; from the hand of every beast I will require it, and from the hand of a man, a brother, I will require the soul of man.
Genesis 9:6 The one pouring out a man’s blood shall be poured out in exchange for his blood, because in God’s image I made man.
Genesis 9:7 But you, increase and multiply and fill the earth and multiply upon it.
Genesis 9:8 And God said to Noah and to his sons with him, saying:
Genesis 9:9 I, behold, raise up my covenant with you and with your seed after you,
Genesis 9:10 and with every living soul with you, from birds and from cattle and all the beasts of the earth, as many as are with you, from all those who came out from the ark.
Genesis 9:11 And I will establish my covenant with you, and every flesh will no longer die from the water of the flood, and there will no longer be a flood of water to destroy all the earth. –
Genesis 9:12 And the Lord God said to Noah: This is the sign of the covenant which I give between me and you and between every living soul which is with you, into eternal generations.
Genesis 9:13 I place my bow in the cloud, and it shall be a sign of a covenant between me and the earth.
Genesis 9:14 And it shall be, when I gather clouds over the earth, that my bow will be seen in the cloud,
Genesis 9:15 and I will remember my covenant which is between me and you and between every living soul in every flesh, and the water will no longer become a flood so as to wipe away every flesh.
Genesis 9:16 And my bow will be in the cloud, and I will see it so as to remember an eternal covenant between me and between every living soul in every flesh which is upon the earth.
Genesis 9:17 And God said to Noah: This is the sign of the covenant which I set between me and between every flesh which is upon the earth.
Genesis 9:18 Now the sons of Noah who came out from the ark were Sem, Cham, Japheth; Cham was the father of Chanaan.
Genesis 9:19 These three are the sons of Noah; from these they were scattered over all the earth.
Genesis 9:20 And Noah began to be a man cultivating the earth, and he planted a vineyard.
Genesis 9:21 And he drank from the wine and became drunk and was stripped naked in his house.
Genesis 9:22 And Cham, the father of Chanaan, saw the nakedness of his father and, having gone out, announced it to his two brothers outside.
Genesis 9:23 And Sem and Japheth, having taken the garment, placed it upon their two backs and went backward-facing and covered the nakedness of their father; and their faces were backward-facing, and they did not see the nakedness of their father.
Genesis 9:24 And Noah sobered up from the wine and knew what his younger son had done to him,
Genesis 9:25 and he said: Accursed is Chanaan; a servant, a household slave, he shall be to his brothers.
Genesis 9:26 And he said: Blessed be the Lord, the God of Sem, and Chanaan shall be his servant.
Genesis 9:27 May God broaden for Japheth, and let him dwell in the houses of Sem, and let Chanaan become their servant.
Genesis 9:28 And Noah lived after the flood three hundred fifty years.
Genesis 9:29 And all the days of Noah were nine hundred fifty years, and he died.

## Chapter 10

Genesis 10:1 Now these are the generations of the sons of Noah—Sem, Cham, Japheth—and sons were born to them after the flood.
Genesis 10:2 The sons of Japheth: Gamer and Magog and Madai and Jovan and Elisa and Thobel and Mosoch and Thiras.
Genesis 10:3 And the sons of Gamer: Aschanaz and Riphath and Thorgama.
Genesis 10:4 And the sons of Jovan: Elisa and Tharsis, Kitians, Rhodians.
Genesis 10:5 From these the islands of the nations were separated in their land, each according to language, in their tribes and in their nations.
Genesis 10:6 And the sons of Cham: Chous and Mesraim, Phoud and Chanaan.
Genesis 10:7 And the sons of Chous: Saba and Evila and Sabatha and Regma and Sabacatha. And the sons of Regma: Saba and Dadan.
Genesis 10:8 And Chous begot Nebrod. He began to be a giant upon the earth.
Genesis 10:9 He was a giant hunter before the Lord God; therefore they will say: Like Nebrod, a giant hunter before the Lord.
Genesis 10:10 And the beginning of his kingdom was Babylon and Orech and Archad and Chalanne in the land of Sennaar.
Genesis 10:11 From that land Assour went out and built Nineve and the city Rooboth and Chalach,
Genesis 10:12 and Dasem between Nineve and Chalach; this is the great city. –
Genesis 10:13 And Mesraim begot the Loudeim and the Enemetiim and the Labiim and the Nephthaliim,
Genesis 10:14 and the Patrosoniim and the Chasloniim, from where the Phylistiim went out from there, and the Caphthoriim. –
Genesis 10:15 And Chanaan begot Sidon the firstborn and the Chettite,
Genesis 10:16 and the Jebousite and the Amorrite and the Gergesite,
Genesis 10:17 and the Evite and the Aroukite and the Asennite,
Genesis 10:18 and the Aradian and the Samarite and Amathi. And after this the tribes of the Chananeans were scattered,
Genesis 10:19 and the boundaries of the Chananeans came to be from Sidon until coming to Gerara and Gaza, until coming to Sodoma and Gomorra, Adama and Seboim, as far as Lasa. –
Genesis 10:20 These are the sons of Cham in their tribes, according to their languages, in their countries and in their nations.
Genesis 10:21 And to Sem also, the father of all the sons of Eber and brother of Japheth the elder, sons were born.
Genesis 10:22 The sons of Sem: Ailam and Assour and Arphaxad and Loud and Aram and Cainan.
Genesis 10:23 And the sons of Aram: Os and Oul and Gather and Mosoch.
Genesis 10:24 And Arphaxad begot Cainan, and Cainan begot Sala, and Sala begot Eber.
Genesis 10:25 And to Eber came to be two sons; the name of the one was Phalek, because in his days the earth was divided, and the name of his brother was Jektan.
Genesis 10:26 And Jektan begot Elmodad and Saleph and Asarmoth and Jarach,
Genesis 10:27 and Odorra and Aizel and Dekla,
Genesis 10:28 and Abimeel and Sabeu,
Genesis 10:29 and Ouphir and Evila and Jobab. All these were sons of Jektan.
Genesis 10:30 And their dwelling was from Masse until coming to Sophira, a mountain of the east.
Genesis 10:31 These are the sons of Sem in their tribes, according to their languages, in their countries and in their nations.
Genesis 10:32 These are the tribes of the sons of Noah according to their generations, according to their nations; from these the islands of the nations were scattered upon the earth after the flood.

## Chapter 11

Genesis 11:1 And the whole earth was one lip, and one voice for all.
Genesis 11:2 And it happened, when they moved from the east, that they found a plain in the land of Sennaar and dwelt there.
Genesis 11:3 And a man said to his neighbor: Come, let us make bricks and bake them with fire. And the brick became stone for them, and asphalt was their clay.
Genesis 11:4 And they said: Come, let us build for ourselves a city and a tower whose head will be as far as heaven, and let us make a name for ourselves before being scattered over the face of all the earth.
Genesis 11:5 And the Lord descended to see the city and the tower which the sons of men built.
Genesis 11:6 And the Lord said: Behold, one race and one lip belong to all, and this they began to do; and now nothing of all that they may set themselves to do will fail them.
Genesis 11:7 Come, and having descended, let us confuse their tongue there, so that each may not hear the voice of his neighbor.
Genesis 11:8 And the Lord scattered them from there over the face of all the earth, and they ceased building the city and the tower.
Genesis 11:9 Because of this its name was called Confusion, because there the Lord confused the lips of all the earth, and from there the Lord God scattered them over the face of all the earth.
Genesis 11:10 And these are the generations of Sem. Sem was one hundred years old when he begot Arphaxad, in the second year after the flood.
Genesis 11:11 And Sem lived five hundred years after his begetting Arphaxad, and he begot sons and daughters, and he died.
Genesis 11:12 And Arphaxad lived one hundred thirty-five years and begot Cainan.
Genesis 11:13 And Arphaxad lived four hundred thirty years after his begetting Cainan, and he begot sons and daughters, and he died. And Cainan lived one hundred thirty years and begot Sala. And Cainan lived three hundred thirty years after his begetting Sala, and he begot sons and daughters, and he died.
Genesis 11:14 And Sala lived one hundred thirty years and begot Eber.
Genesis 11:15 And Sala lived three hundred thirty years after his begetting Eber, and he begot sons and daughters, and he died.
Genesis 11:16 And Eber lived one hundred thirty-four years and begot Phalek.
Genesis 11:17 And Eber lived three hundred seventy years after his begetting Phalek, and he begot sons and daughters, and he died.
Genesis 11:18 And Phalek lived one hundred thirty years and begot Ragau.
Genesis 11:19 And Phalek lived two hundred nine years after his begetting Ragau, and he begot sons and daughters, and he died.
Genesis 11:20 And Ragau lived one hundred thirty-two years and begot Serouch.
Genesis 11:21 And Ragau lived two hundred seven years after his begetting Serouch, and he begot sons and daughters, and he died.
Genesis 11:22 And Serouch lived one hundred thirty years and begot Nachor.
Genesis 11:23 And Serouch lived two hundred years after his begetting Nachor, and he begot sons and daughters, and he died.
Genesis 11:24 And Nachor lived seventy-nine years and begot Thara.
Genesis 11:25 And Nachor lived one hundred twenty-nine years after his begetting Thara, and he begot sons and daughters, and he died.
Genesis 11:26 And Thara lived seventy years and begot Abram and Nachor and Arran.
Genesis 11:27 Now these are the generations of Thara. Thara begot Abram and Nachor and Arran, and Arran begot Lot.
Genesis 11:28 And Arran died before Thara his father in the land in which he was born, in the country of the Chaldeans.
Genesis 11:29 And Abram and Nachor took women for themselves; the name of Abram’s woman was Sara, and the name of Nachor’s woman was Melcha, daughter of Arran, father of Melcha and father of Jescha.
Genesis 11:30 And Sara was barren and did not bear children.
Genesis 11:31 And Thara took Abram his son and Lot, son of Arran, son of his son, and Sara his daughter-in-law, woman of Abram his son, and brought them out from the country of the Chaldeans to go into the land of Chanaan; and he came as far as Charran and dwelt there.
Genesis 11:32 And the days of Thara in Charran were two hundred five years, and Thara died in Charran.

## Chapter 12

Genesis 12:1 And the Lord said to Abram: Go out from your land and from your kin and from the house of your father into the land which I may show you;
Genesis 12:2 and I will make you into a great nation and bless you and magnify your name, and you shall be blessed;
Genesis 12:3 and I will bless those blessing you, and those cursing you I will curse; and in you all the tribes of the earth will be blessed.
Genesis 12:4 And Abram went just as the Lord spoke to him, and Lot went with him. And Abram was seventy-five years old when he went out from Charran.
Genesis 12:5 And Abram took Sara his woman and Lot the son of his brother and all their possessions, as many as they acquired, and every soul which they acquired in Charran, and they went out to go into the land of Chanaan, and they came into the land of Chanaan. –
Genesis 12:6 And Abram traveled through the land along its length as far as the place Sychem, at the high oak; and the Chananeans then dwelt in the land.
Genesis 12:7 And the Lord appeared to Abram and said to him: To your seed I will give this land. And there Abram built an altar to the Lord who appeared to him.
Genesis 12:8 And he departed from there to the mountain east of Baethel and set up his tent there, Baethel toward the sea and Angai toward the east; and there he built an altar to the Lord and called upon the name of the Lord.
Genesis 12:9 And Abram struck camp and, having gone, encamped in the wilderness.
Genesis 12:10 And a famine came upon the land, and Abram went down into Egypt to sojourn there, because the famine grew strong upon the land.
Genesis 12:11 And it happened when Abram drew near to enter into Egypt that Abram said to Sara his woman: I know that you are a woman beautiful in face;
Genesis 12:12 therefore it will be, whenever the Egyptians see you, that they will say: This is his woman, and they will kill me, but they will preserve you.
Genesis 12:13 Therefore say: I am his sister, so that it may be well for me because of you, and my soul will live on account of you.
Genesis 12:14 And it happened when Abram entered into Egypt that the Egyptians, seeing the woman, that she was exceedingly beautiful,
Genesis 12:15 and the rulers of Pharao saw her and praised her to Pharao and brought her into the house of Pharao.
Genesis 12:16 And they treated Abram well because of her, and he came to have sheep and calves and donkeys, male servants and female servants, mules and camels.
Genesis 12:17 And God tested Pharao and his house with great and evil tests concerning Sara, the woman of Abram.
Genesis 12:18 And Pharao called Abram and said: What is this you did to me, that you did not announce to me that she is your woman?
Genesis 12:19 Why did you say: She is my sister? And I took her for myself as a woman. And now, behold, your woman is before you; take her and run away.
Genesis 12:20 And Pharao commanded men concerning Abram, to escort him and his woman and all that he had, and Lot with him.

## Chapter 13

Genesis 13:1 And Abram went up from Egypt, he and his woman and all that was his and Lot with him, into the wilderness.
Genesis 13:2 And Abram was exceedingly rich in cattle and silver and gold.
Genesis 13:3 And he went from where he came, into the wilderness as far as Baethel, as far as the place where his tent formerly was, between Baethel and Angai,
Genesis 13:4 to the place of the altar which he made there at first; and there Abram called upon the name of the Lord.
Genesis 13:5 And Lot, who was journeying with Abram, had sheep and cattle and tents.
Genesis 13:6 And the land did not have room for them to dwell together, because their possessions were many, and they could not dwell together.
Genesis 13:7 And there was a conflict between the shepherds of Abram’s cattle and the shepherds of Lot’s cattle; and the Chananeans and the Pherezites then dwelt in the land.
Genesis 13:8 And Abram said to Lot: Let there be no conflict between me and you and between my shepherds and your shepherds, because we are men, brothers.
Genesis 13:9 Is not, behold, all the land before you? Separate from me; if you go to the left, I will go to the right, but if you go to the right, I will go to the left.
Genesis 13:10 And Lot, lifting his eyes, saw all the region of the Jordan, that all of it was irrigated—before God destroyed Sodoma and Gomorra—like the paradise of God and like the land of Egypt until coming to Zogora.
Genesis 13:11 And Lot chose for himself all the region of the Jordan, and Lot departed from the east, and they separated, each from his brother.
Genesis 13:12 And Abram dwelt in the land of Chanaan, but Lot dwelt in a city of the region and tented in Sodoma.
Genesis 13:13 But the men in Sodoma were evil and exceedingly sinful before God.
Genesis 13:14 And God said to Abram after Lot separated from him: Looking up with your eyes, see from the place where you now are toward north and southwest and east and sea;
Genesis 13:15 because all the land which you see, I will give it to you and to your seed forever.
Genesis 13:16 And I will make your seed like the sand of the earth; if anyone is able to count the sand of the earth, then your seed will be counted.
Genesis 13:17 Rise and travel through the land, both its length and its width, because I will give it to you.
Genesis 13:18 And Abram, having moved his tent, came and dwelt beside the oak Mamre, which was in Chebron, and there he built an altar to the Lord.

## Chapter 14

Genesis 14:1 And it happened in the reign of Amarfal king of Sennaar, Arioch king of Ellasar and Chodollogomor king of Ailam and Thargal king of nations
Genesis 14:2 made war with Balla king of Sodoma and with Barsa king of Gomorra and Sennaar king of Adama and Symobor king of Seboim and the king of Balak [this is Segor].
Genesis 14:3 All these agreed together at the salt ravine [this is the sea of salts].
Genesis 14:4 For twelve years they served Chodollogomor, but in the thirteenth year they revolted.
Genesis 14:5 And in the fourteenth year Chodollogomor and the kings with him came and cut down the giants in Astaroth Karnain and strong nations together with them and the Ommaeans in the city Saue,
Genesis 14:6 and the Chorraeans in the mountains of Seir as far as the terebinth of Pharan, which is in the wilderness.
Genesis 14:7 And having returned, they came to the spring of Judgment [this is Kades] and cut down all the rulers of Amalek and the Amorrites dwelling in Asasanthamar.
Genesis 14:8 And the king of Sodoma and the king of Gomorra and the king of Adama and the king of Seboim and the king of Balak [this is Segor] went out and drew themselves up against them for war in the salt valley,
Genesis 14:9 against Chodollogomor king of Ailam and Thargal king of nations and Amarfal king of Sennaar and Arioch king of Ellasar, the four kings against the five.
Genesis 14:10 And the salt valley was wells, wells of asphalt; and the king of Sodoma and the king of Gomorra fled and fell there, but those remaining fled into the hill country.
Genesis 14:11 And they took all the horse of Sodoma and Gomorra and all their foods and departed.
Genesis 14:12 And they also took Lot, the son of Abram’s brother, and his baggage and went away, for he was dwelling in Sodoma.
Genesis 14:13 And one of those who were saved arrived and announced it to Abram the passer. Now he dwelt by the oak of Mamre the Amorite, brother of Eschol and brother of Aunan, who were sworn allies of Abram.
Genesis 14:14 And Abram, hearing that Lot his brother had been taken captive, counted his own homeborn men, three hundred eighteen, and pursued after them as far as Dan.
Genesis 14:15 And he fell upon them at night, he and his servants, and struck them and pursued them as far as Choba, which is to the left of Damascus.
Genesis 14:16 And he returned all the horse of Sodoma, and returned Lot his brother and his possessions and the women and the people.
Genesis 14:17 And the king of Sodoma went out to meet him—after his returning from the cutting down of Chodollogomor and the kings with him—to the valley Saue [this was the plain of the king].
Genesis 14:18 And Melchisedek king of Salem brought out breads and wine; and he was priest of God Most High.
Genesis 14:19 And he blessed Abram and said: Blessed is Abram by God Most High, who created heaven and earth,
Genesis 14:20 and blessed is God Most High, who delivered your enemies under your hand. And he gave him a tenth from all.
Genesis 14:21 And the king of Sodoma said to Abram: Give me the men, but take the horse for yourself.
Genesis 14:22 And Abram said to the king of Sodoma: I will stretch out my hand toward God Most High, who created heaven and earth,
Genesis 14:23 if I take from a cord as far as a shoe-fastener from all that is yours, so that you may not say: I made Abram rich;
Genesis 14:24 except what the young men ate and the share of the men who journeyed with me—Eschol, Aunan, Mamre—these shall take a share.

## Chapter 15

Genesis 15:1 And after these words a word of the Lord came to Abram in a vision, saying: Do not be afraid, Abram; I defend you. Your reward will be exceedingly great.
Genesis 15:2 And Abram says: Master, what will you give me? But I am being released childless, and the son of Masek, my homeborn woman, is this Damascus Eliezer.
Genesis 15:3 And Abram said: Since you did not give me seed, my homeborn servant will inherit me.
Genesis 15:4 And immediately a voice of the Lord came to him, saying: This one will not inherit you, but one who will come out from you, he will inherit you.
Genesis 15:5 And he brought him outside and said to him: Look up now into heaven and count the stars, if you are able to count them. And he said: Thus shall your seed be.
Genesis 15:6 And Abram believed God, and it was reckoned to him for righteousness.
Genesis 15:7 And he said to him: I am God who brought you out from the country of the Chaldeans so as to give you this land to inherit.
Genesis 15:8 And he said: Master, Lord, according to what shall I know that I will inherit it?
Genesis 15:9 And he said to him: Take for me a three-year-old heifer and a three-year-old goat and a three-year-old ram and a turtledove and a dove.
Genesis 15:10 And he took all these for him and divided them in the middle and placed them facing one another, but he did not divide the birds.
Genesis 15:11 And birds came down upon the bodies, their divided pieces, and Abram sat together with them.
Genesis 15:12 And near sunset a trance fell upon Abram, and behold, a great dark fear was falling upon him.
Genesis 15:13 And it was said to Abram: Knowing, you shall know that your seed will be a sojourner in a land not its own, and they will enslave them and harm them and humble them for four hundred years.
Genesis 15:14 But the nation which they may serve, I will judge; and after these things they will come out here with much baggage.
Genesis 15:15 But you will depart to your fathers with peace, buried in a good old age.
Genesis 15:16 And in the fourth generation they will return here, for the sins of the Amorrites have not yet been filled up until now.
Genesis 15:17 And when the sun was becoming toward setting, a flame came to be, and behold, a smoking oven and torches of fire which passed between these divided pieces.
Genesis 15:18 On that day the Lord made a covenant with Abram, saying: To your seed I will give this land, from the river of Egypt as far as the great river, the river Euphrates,
Genesis 15:19 the Kainites and the Kenezites and the Kedmoneans,
Genesis 15:20 and the Chettites and the Pherezites and the Raphain,
Genesis 15:21 and the Amorrites and the Chananeans and the Evites and the Gergesites and the Jebousites.

## Chapter 16

Genesis 16:1 Now Sara, the woman of Abram, did not bear for him. And she had an Egyptian female servant whose name was Agar.
Genesis 16:2 And Sara said to Abram: Behold, the Lord has shut me up from bearing; therefore go in to my female servant, so that you may father children from her. And Abram listened to the voice of Sara.
Genesis 16:3 And Sara, the woman of Abram, took Agar the Egyptian, her own female servant—after Abram had dwelt ten years in the land of Chanaan—and gave her to Abram her man, to him as a woman.
Genesis 16:4 And he went in to Agar, and she conceived and saw that she had in the womb, and her mistress was dishonored before her.
Genesis 16:5 And Sara said to Abram: I am wronged from you. I gave my female servant into your bosom, but seeing that she had in the womb, I was dishonored before her. May God judge between me and you.
Genesis 16:6 And Abram said to Sara: Behold, your female servant is in your hands; deal with her as may be pleasing to you. And Sara harmed her, and she fled from her face.
Genesis 16:7 And an angel of the Lord found her at the spring of water in the wilderness, at the spring on the way to Sour.
Genesis 16:8 And the angel of the Lord said to her: Agar, female servant of Sara, from where are you coming, and where are you going? And she said: I am fleeing away from the face of Sara my mistress.
Genesis 16:9 And the angel of the Lord said to her: Return to your mistress and be humbled under her hands.
Genesis 16:10 And the angel of the Lord said to her: Multiplying, I will multiply your seed, and it will not be numbered because of the multitude.
Genesis 16:11 And the angel of the Lord said to her: Behold, you have in the womb and will bear a son, and you shall call his name Ismael, because the Lord listened to your humiliation.
Genesis 16:12 He will be a rustic man; his hands will be against all, and the hands of all against him, and he will dwell before the face of all his brothers.
Genesis 16:13 And Agar called the name of the Lord who was speaking to her: You are God who looked upon me; because she said: For even face-to-face I saw him who appeared to me.
Genesis 16:14 Because of this she called the well Well Where I Saw Face-to-face; behold, it is between Kades and Barad.
Genesis 16:15 And Agar bore a son for Abram, and Abram called the name of his son, whom Agar bore for him, Ismael.
Genesis 16:16 And Abram was eighty-six years old when Agar bore Ismael for Abram.

## Chapter 17

Genesis 17:1 And Abram came to be ninety-nine years old, and the Lord appeared to Abram and said to him: I am your God; be well pleasing before me and become blameless,
Genesis 17:2 and I will set my covenant between me and between you and multiply you exceedingly.
Genesis 17:3 And Abram fell upon his face, and God spoke to him, saying:
Genesis 17:4 And I, behold, my covenant is with you, and you shall be father of a multitude of nations.
Genesis 17:5 And your name will no longer be called Abram, but your name shall be Abraham, because I have made you father of many nations.
Genesis 17:6 And I will increase you exceedingly, exceedingly, and make you into nations, and kings will come out from you.
Genesis 17:7 And I will establish my covenant between me and between you and between your seed after you throughout their generations, as an eternal covenant, to be God of you and of your seed after you.
Genesis 17:8 And I will give to you and to your seed after you the land in which you sojourn, all the land of Chanaan, as an eternal possession, and I will be God to them. –
Genesis 17:9 And God said to Abraham: But you shall preserve my covenant, you and your seed after you throughout their generations.
Genesis 17:10 And this is the covenant which you shall preserve between me and you and between your seed after you throughout their generations: every male of yours shall be circumcised,
Genesis 17:11 and you shall circumcise the flesh of your foreskin, and it shall be as a sign of a covenant between me and you.
Genesis 17:12 And every male child of yours eight days old shall be circumcised throughout your generations, the homeborn of your house and the one bought with silver from any foreigner’s son who is not from your seed.
Genesis 17:13 With circumcision shall the homeborn of your house and the one bought with silver be circumcised, and my covenant shall be upon your flesh as an eternal covenant.
Genesis 17:14 And an uncircumcised male who will not be circumcised in the flesh of his foreskin on the eighth day—that soul will be utterly destroyed from its race, because he scattered my covenant.
Genesis 17:15 And God said to Abraham: Sara your woman—her name shall not be called Sara, but Sarra shall be her name.
Genesis 17:16 And I will bless her and give you a child from her; and I will bless him, and he will become nations, and kings of nations will be from him.
Genesis 17:17 And Abraham fell upon his face and laughed and said in his mind, saying: Will one be born to a hundred-year-old, and will Sarra, being ninety years old, give birth?
Genesis 17:18 And Abraham said to God: Let this Ismael live before you.
Genesis 17:19 And God said to Abraham: Yes; behold, Sarra your woman will bear you a son, and you shall call his name Isaac, and I will establish my covenant with him as an eternal covenant and with his seed after him.
Genesis 17:20 And concerning Ismael, behold, I listened to you. Behold, I have blessed him, and I will increase him and multiply him exceedingly. He will beget twelve nations, and I will make him into a great nation.
Genesis 17:21 But my covenant I will establish with Isaac, whom Sarra will bear for you at this time in the other year.
Genesis 17:22 And he finished speaking to him, and God ascended from Abraham.
Genesis 17:23 And Abraham took Ismael his son and all his homeborn men and all those bought with silver and every male of the men in Abraham’s house and circumcised their foreskins at the time of that day, just as God spoke to him.
Genesis 17:24 And Abraham was ninety-nine years old when he circumcised the flesh of his foreskin.
Genesis 17:25 And Ismael his son was thirteen years old when he was circumcised in the flesh of his foreskin.
Genesis 17:26 At the time of that day Abraham and Ismael his son were circumcised;
Genesis 17:27 and all the men of his house and the homeborn and those bought with silver from foreign nations, he circumcised them.

## Chapter 18

Genesis 18:1 And God appeared to him by the oak Mamre while he was sitting at the door of his tent at midday.
Genesis 18:2 And looking up with his eyes, he saw, and behold, three men stood above him; and seeing them, he ran from the door of his tent to meet them and bowed to the earth
Genesis 18:3 and said: Lord, if indeed I found grace before you, do not pass by your servant.
Genesis 18:4 Let water now be taken, and let them wash your feet, and cool yourselves under the tree;
Genesis 18:5 and I will take bread, and you will eat, and after this you will pass on into your way, for this reason you turned aside toward your servant. And they said: Do thus, just as you have said.
Genesis 18:6 And Abraham hurried to the tent to Sarra and said to her: Hurry and mix three measures of fine flour and make ash-cakes.
Genesis 18:7 And Abraham ran to the cattle and took a tender and good calf and gave it to the servant, and he hurried to prepare it.
Genesis 18:8 And he took butter and milk and the calf which he prepared and set them before them, and they ate; and he stood beside them under the tree.
Genesis 18:9 And he said to him: Where is Sarra your woman? And answering, he said: Behold, in the tent.
Genesis 18:10 And he said: Returning, I will come to you at this time, at the appointed hour, and Sarra your woman will have a son. And Sarra heard at the door of the tent, being behind him.
Genesis 18:11 And Abraham and Sarra were old, advanced in days, and it had ceased for Sarra to have the things of women.
Genesis 18:12 And Sarra laughed within herself, saying: It has not yet happened to me until now, and my lord is old.
Genesis 18:13 And the Lord said to Abraham: Why is it that Sarra laughed within herself, saying: Will I then truly give birth? But I have grown old.
Genesis 18:14 Is a word powerless with God? At this time, at the appointed hour, I will return to you, and Sarra will have a son.
Genesis 18:15 But Sarra denied it, saying: I did not laugh, for she was afraid. And he said: No, but you laughed.
Genesis 18:16 And the men, rising up from there, looked down upon the face of Sodoma and Gomorra, and Abraham journeyed with them, escorting them.
Genesis 18:17 And the Lord said: Shall I hide from Abraham my servant the things which I am doing?
Genesis 18:18 And Abraham, coming to be, will be a great and numerous nation, and in him all the nations of the earth will be blessed.
Genesis 18:19 For I knew that he will command his sons and his house after him, and they will guard the ways of the Lord, to do righteousness and judgment, so that the Lord may bring upon Abraham all the things which he spoke to him.
Genesis 18:20 And the Lord said: The cry of Sodoma and Gomorra has multiplied, and their sins are exceedingly great;
Genesis 18:21 therefore, having gone down, I will see whether they are being completed according to their cry which is coming to me, but if not, so that I may know.
Genesis 18:22 And the men, turning away from there, came into Sodoma, but Abraham was standing before the Lord.
Genesis 18:23 And Abraham drew near and said: Surely you will not destroy a righteous one together with an impious one, and the righteous one will be as the impious one?
Genesis 18:24 If there are fifty righteous ones in the city, will you destroy them? Will you not spare the whole place on account of the fifty righteous ones, if they are in it?
Genesis 18:25 In no way will you act according to this word, to kill a righteous one together with an impious one, and the righteous one will be as the impious one. In no way; will you, the one judging all the earth, not do judgment?
Genesis 18:26 And the Lord said: If I find in Sodoma fifty righteous ones in the city, I will spare the whole place because of them.
Genesis 18:27 And Abraham answered and said: Now I began to speak to the Lord, but I am earth and ashes.
Genesis 18:28 But if the fifty righteous ones are diminished by five, will you destroy all the city because of the five? And he said: I will certainly not destroy it if I find forty-five there.
Genesis 18:29 And he continued still to speak to him and said: But if forty are found there? And he said: I will certainly not destroy it on account of the forty.
Genesis 18:30 And he said: Let it not be, Lord, if I speak: But if thirty are found there? And he said: I will certainly not destroy it if I find thirty there.
Genesis 18:31 And he said: Since I have to speak to the Lord: But if twenty are found there? And he said: I will certainly not destroy it on account of the twenty.
Genesis 18:32 And he said: Let it not be, Lord, if I speak yet once: But if ten are found there? And he said: I will certainly not destroy it on account of the ten.
Genesis 18:33 And the Lord departed when he ceased speaking to Abraham, and Abraham returned to his place.

## Chapter 19

Genesis 19:1 And the two angels came into Sodoma at evening; and Lot was sitting by the gate of Sodoma. And Lot, seeing them, rose up to meet them and bowed with his face to the earth
Genesis 19:2 and said: Behold, lords, turn aside into the house of your servant and lodge and wash your feet, and having risen early, you will depart into your way. But they said: No, but we will lodge in the square.
Genesis 19:3 And he pressed them strongly, and they turned aside toward him and entered into his house. And he made a drinking feast for them and baked unleavened loaves for them, and they ate.
Genesis 19:4 Before they lay down, the men of the city, the Sodomites, surrounded the house, from young man as far as elder, all the people together,
Genesis 19:5 and they called Lot out and said to him: Where are the men who entered toward you at night? Bring them out toward us, so that we may have intercourse with them.
Genesis 19:6 And Lot went out toward them to the forecourt, and he shut the door behind him.
Genesis 19:7 And he said to them: By no means, brothers; do not act wickedly.
Genesis 19:8 And I have two daughters who have not known a man; I will bring them out toward you, and use them just as may please you. Only do nothing unjust to these men, for this reason they came under the shelter of my beams.
Genesis 19:9 But they said: Stand away there. You alone came to sojourn; surely also to judge judgment? Therefore now we will harm you more than them. And they pressed the man Lot exceedingly and drew near to crush the door.
Genesis 19:10 But the men, stretching out their hands, drew Lot inward toward themselves into the house and shut the door of the house.
Genesis 19:11 And they struck the men who were at the door of the house with blindness, from small as far as great, and they were exhausted seeking the door.
Genesis 19:12 And the men said to Lot: Is there anyone of yours here—sons-in-law or sons or daughters? Or if anyone else of yours is in the city, bring them out from this place,
Genesis 19:13 because we are destroying this place, because their cry was raised before the Lord, and the Lord sent us to wipe it out.
Genesis 19:14 And Lot went out and spoke to his sons-in-law who had taken his daughters and said: Rise and go out from this place, because the Lord is wiping out the city. But he seemed to be joking before his sons-in-law.
Genesis 19:15 And when dawn was coming, the angels hurried Lot, saying: Arise, take your woman and your two daughters whom you have, and go out, lest you perish together with the lawless deeds of the city.
Genesis 19:16 And they were troubled; and the angels seized his hand and the hand of his woman and the hands of his two daughters, when the Lord spared him.
Genesis 19:17 And it happened when they brought them outside that they said: Saving, save your own soul. Do not look around to the things behind, nor stand in all the region; save yourself to the mountain, lest you be taken along with them.
Genesis 19:18 And Lot said to them: I beg, Lord;
Genesis 19:19 since your servant found mercy before you and you magnified your righteousness which you do upon me, for my soul to live, but I will not be able to be brought safely to the mountain, lest the evil things overtake me and I die,
Genesis 19:20 behold, this city is near for me to take refuge there, and it is small; there I will be saved. Is it not small? And my soul will live.
Genesis 19:21 And he said to him: Behold, I have marveled at your face also in this matter, so as not to overthrow the city concerning which you spoke.
Genesis 19:22 Therefore hurry to be saved there, for I will not be able to do a thing until you enter there. Because of this he called the name of that city Segor.
Genesis 19:23 The sun came out upon the earth, and Lot entered into Segor,
Genesis 19:24 and the Lord rained sulfur and fire upon Sodoma and Gomorra from the Lord out of heaven,
Genesis 19:25 and overthrew these cities and all the surrounding region and all those dwelling in the cities and all the things springing up from the earth.
Genesis 19:26 And his woman looked to the things behind and became a pillar of salt.
Genesis 19:27 And Abraham rose early in the morning to the place where he had stood before the Lord,
Genesis 19:28 and he looked upon the face of Sodoma and Gomorra and upon the face of the land of the region and saw, and behold, a flame of the earth was ascending like steam of a furnace.
Genesis 19:29 And it happened, when the Lord wiped out all the cities of the surrounding region, that God remembered Abraham and sent Lot out from the midst of the overthrow when the Lord overthrew the cities in which Lot dwelt.
Genesis 19:30 And Lot went up from Segor and sat in the mountain, and his two daughters with him, for he was afraid to dwell in Segor. And he dwelt in the cave, he and his two daughters with him.
Genesis 19:31 And the elder said to the younger: Our father is older, and there is no one upon the earth who will go in toward us, as is fitting to all the earth.
Genesis 19:32 Come, and let us give our father wine to drink and lie with him, and let us raise up seed from our father.
Genesis 19:33 And they gave their father wine to drink on this night, and the elder went in and lay with her father that night, and he did not know when she lay down and rose.
Genesis 19:34 And it happened on the next day that the elder said to the younger: Behold, I lay yesterday with our father. Let us give him wine to drink this night also, and go in and lie with him, and let us raise up seed from our father.
Genesis 19:35 And on that night also they gave their father wine to drink, and the younger went in and lay with her father, and he did not know when she lay down and rose.
Genesis 19:36 And the two daughters of Lot conceived from their father.
Genesis 19:37 And the elder bore a son and called his name Moab, saying: From my father. He is the father of the Moabites until today.
Genesis 19:38 And the younger also bore a son and called his name Amman, Son of My Race. He is the father of the Ammanites until today.

## Chapter 20

Genesis 20:1 And Abraham moved from there into the land toward the southwest and dwelt between Kades and Sour and sojourned in Gerara.
Genesis 20:2 And Abraham said concerning Sarra his woman: She is my sister, for he was afraid to say: She is my woman, lest the men of the city kill him because of her. And Abimelech king of Gerara sent and took Sarra.
Genesis 20:3 And God entered toward Abimelech in sleep at night and said: Behold, you are dying concerning the woman whom you took, but she is one who lives with a man.
Genesis 20:4 But Abimelech had not touched her, and he said: Lord, will you destroy an ignorant and righteous nation?
Genesis 20:5 Did he not say to me: She is my sister? And she said to me: He is my brother. In a clean heart and in righteousness of hands I did this.
Genesis 20:6 And God said to him in sleep: I also knew that you did this in a clean heart, and I spared you so that you would not sin against me; because of this I did not permit you to touch her.
Genesis 20:7 But now give the woman back to the man, because he is a prophet, and he will pray for you and you will live; but if you do not give her back, know that you will die, you and all that is yours.
Genesis 20:8 And Abimelech rose early in the morning and called all his servants and spoke all these words into their ears, and all the men were exceedingly afraid.
Genesis 20:9 And Abimelech called Abraham and said to him: What is this you did to us? Did we perhaps sin against you, that you brought upon me and upon my kingdom a great sin? A deed which no one will do, you have done to me.
Genesis 20:10 And Abimelech said to Abraham: What did you see that you did this?
Genesis 20:11 And Abraham said: For I said: Perhaps there is no reverence for God in this place, and they will kill me on account of my woman.
Genesis 20:12 For indeed she truly is my sister from my father, but not from my mother; and she became my woman.
Genesis 20:13 And it happened when God brought me out from my father’s house that I said to her: This righteousness you shall do upon me: in every place into which we may enter there, say of me: He is my brother.
Genesis 20:14 And Abimelech took one thousand didrachmas, sheep and calves and male servants and female servants, and gave them to Abraham, and he gave Sarra his woman back to him.
Genesis 20:15 And Abimelech said to Abraham: Behold, my land is before you; dwell wherever may please you.
Genesis 20:16 And to Sarra he said: Behold, I have given one thousand didrachmas to your brother; these shall be for you as honor of your face and for all the women with you; and speak truth in all things.
Genesis 20:17 And Abraham prayed to God, and God healed Abimelech and his woman and his female servants, and they bore children;
Genesis 20:18 because, shutting, the Lord shut every womb from outside in the house of Abimelech on account of Sarra, the woman of Abraham.

## Chapter 21

Genesis 21:1 And the Lord visited Sarra, just as he said, and the Lord did to Sarra just as he spoke,
Genesis 21:2 and having conceived, Sarra bore a son for Abraham in his old age, at the time just as the Lord spoke to him.
Genesis 21:3 And Abraham called the name of his son who came to be for him, whom Sarra bore for him, Isaac.
Genesis 21:4 And Abraham circumcised Isaac on the eighth day, just as God commanded him.
Genesis 21:5 And Abraham was one hundred years old when Isaac his son came to be for him.
Genesis 21:6 And Sarra said: The Lord made laughter for me; for whoever may hear will rejoice with me.
Genesis 21:7 And she said: Who will announce to Abraham that Sarra nurses a child? For I bore a son in my old age.
Genesis 21:8 And the child grew and was weaned, and Abraham made a great reception on the day Isaac his son was weaned.
Genesis 21:9 And Sarra saw the son of Agar the Egyptian, who came to be for Abraham, playing with Isaac her son,
Genesis 21:10 and she said to Abraham: Cast out this female servant and her son, for the son of this female servant will not inherit with my son Isaac.
Genesis 21:11 And the word appeared exceedingly hard before Abraham concerning his son.
Genesis 21:12 And God said to Abraham: Let the word not be hard before you concerning the child and concerning the female servant. As many things as Sarra may say to you, listen to her voice, because in Isaac seed will be called for you.
Genesis 21:13 And the son of this female servant also, I will make him into a great nation, because he is your seed.
Genesis 21:14 And Abraham rose in the morning and took breads and a skin of water and gave them to Agar and placed them and the child upon her shoulder and sent her away. And having departed, she wandered in the wilderness by the Well of the Oath.
Genesis 21:15 And the water failed from the skin, and she threw the child beneath one fir tree.
Genesis 21:16 And having departed, she sat opposite him far away, about a bowshot, for she said: I shall certainly not see the death of my child. And she sat opposite him, and the child, crying aloud, wept.
Genesis 21:17 And God listened to the voice of the child from the place where he was, and an angel of God called Agar from heaven and said to her: What is it, Agar? Do not be afraid, for God has heard the voice of your child from the place where he is.
Genesis 21:18 Rise, take the child and hold him with your hand, for I will make him into a great nation.
Genesis 21:19 And God opened her eyes, and she saw a well of living water and went and filled the skin with water and gave the child a drink.
Genesis 21:20 And God was with the child, and he grew. And he dwelt in the wilderness and became an archer.
Genesis 21:21 And he dwelt in the wilderness of Pharan, and his mother took a woman for him from the land of Egypt.
Genesis 21:22 And it happened at that time that Abimelech and Ochozath his bride-conductor and Phicol the commander-in-chief of his force said to Abraham, saying: God is with you in all things which you may do.
Genesis 21:23 Now therefore swear to me by God that you will not wrong me nor my seed nor my name, but according to the righteousness which I did with you, you will do with me and with the land in which you sojourned.
Genesis 21:24 And Abraham said: I will swear.
Genesis 21:25 And Abraham reproved Abimelech concerning the wells of water which Abimelech’s servants took away.
Genesis 21:26 And Abimelech said to him: I did not know who did this thing, nor did you announce it to me, nor did I hear except today.
Genesis 21:27 And Abraham took sheep and calves and gave them to Abimelech, and both made a covenant.
Genesis 21:28 And Abraham set seven ewe lambs of the sheep alone.
Genesis 21:29 And Abimelech said to Abraham: What are these seven ewe lambs of the sheep which you set alone?
Genesis 21:30 And Abraham said: You shall take these seven ewe lambs from me so that they may be a testimony for me that I dug this well.
Genesis 21:31 Because of this he named the name of that place Well of the Oath, because there both swore.
Genesis 21:32 And they made a covenant at the Well of the Oath. And Abimelech and Ochozath his bride-conductor and Phicol the commander-in-chief of his force rose and returned into the land of the Phylistiim.
Genesis 21:33 And Abraham planted a field at the Well of the Oath and there called upon the name of the Lord, Eternal God.
Genesis 21:34 And Abraham sojourned in the land of the Phylistiim many days.

## Chapter 22

Genesis 22:1 And it happened after these words that God was testing Abraham and said to him: Abraham, Abraham. And he said: Behold, I am here.
Genesis 22:2 And he said: Take your beloved son, whom you loved, Isaac, and go into the high land and offer him there as a whole burnt offering upon one of the mountains which I may tell you.
Genesis 22:3 And Abraham rose in the morning and saddled his donkey; and he took with himself two servants and Isaac his son, and having split wood for a whole burnt offering, he rose and went and came to the place which God told him.
Genesis 22:4 And on the third day Abraham looked up with his eyes and saw the place from far away.
Genesis 22:5 And Abraham said to his servants: Sit here with the donkey, but I and the child will go through as far as there, and having worshiped, we will return to you.
Genesis 22:6 And Abraham took the wood of the whole burnt offering and placed it upon Isaac his son; and he also took the fire in hand and the knife, and the two went together.
Genesis 22:7 And Isaac spoke to Abraham his father, saying: Father. And he said: What is it, child? And he said: Behold, the fire and the wood; where is the sheep for a whole burnt offering?
Genesis 22:8 And Abraham said: God will see for himself a sheep for a whole burnt offering, child. And both went together
Genesis 22:9 and came to the place which God told him. And there Abraham built an altar and placed the wood, and having bound together the feet of Isaac his son, he placed him upon the altar above the wood.
Genesis 22:10 And Abraham stretched out his hand to take the knife to slaughter his son.
Genesis 22:11 And an angel of the Lord called him from heaven and said to him: Abraham, Abraham. And he said: Behold, I am here.
Genesis 22:12 And he said: Do not lay your hand upon the child, nor do anything to him; for now I know that you fear God, you, and did not spare your beloved son because of me.
Genesis 22:13 And Abraham looked up with his eyes and saw, and behold, one ram held in a plant Sabek by the horns. And Abraham went and took the ram and offered it as a whole burnt offering in place of Isaac his son.
Genesis 22:14 And Abraham called the name of that place The Lord Saw, so that they may say today: In the mountain the Lord appeared.
Genesis 22:15 And an angel of the Lord called Abraham a second time from heaven,
Genesis 22:16 saying: By myself I swore, says the Lord, because you did this thing and did not spare your beloved son because of me,
Genesis 22:17 surely indeed, blessing, I will bless you, and multiplying, I will multiply your seed like the stars of heaven and like the sand beside the lip of the sea, and your seed will inherit the cities of the adversaries.
Genesis 22:18 And in your seed all the nations of the earth will be blessed, because you listened to my voice.
Genesis 22:19 And Abraham returned to his servants, and rising, they went together to the Well of the Oath. And Abraham dwelt at the Well of the Oath.
Genesis 22:20 And it happened after these words that it was announced to Abraham, saying: Behold, Melcha also has borne sons to Nachor your brother:
Genesis 22:21 Ox the firstborn and Baux his brother and Kamouel the father of Syrians,
Genesis 22:22 and Chasad and Azau and Phaldas and Jedlaph and Bathouel;
Genesis 22:23 and Bathouel begot Rebekka. These are eight sons whom Melcha bore to Nachor, the brother of Abraham.
Genesis 22:24 And his concubine, whose name was Rheuma, also bore Tabek and Gaam and Tochos and Mocha.

## Chapter 23

Genesis 23:1 And the life of Sarra was one hundred twenty-seven years.
