Genesis 23:2 And Sarra died in the city Arbok, which is in the hollow [this is Chebron], in the land of Chanaan. And Abraham came to lament Sarra and mourn.
Genesis 23:3 And Abraham rose from his dead body and said to the sons of Chet, saying:
Genesis 23:4 I am a sojourner and a stranger with you; therefore give me a possession for a tomb among you, and I will bury my dead away from me.
Genesis 23:5 And the sons of Chet answered Abraham, saying:
Genesis 23:6 No, lord; but hear us. You are a king from God among us; bury your dead in our chosen tombs, for no one of us will withhold his tomb from you so as to bury your dead there.
Genesis 23:7 And Abraham rose and bowed to the people of the land, the sons of Chet,
Genesis 23:8 and Abraham spoke to them, saying: If you have it in your soul that I bury my dead away from my face, hear me and speak concerning me to Ephron the son of Saar,
Genesis 23:9 and let him give me the double cave which is his, which is at the edge of his field; for silver of its worth, let him give it to me among you as a possession for a tomb.
Genesis 23:10 And Ephron was sitting in the midst of the sons of Chet; and Ephron the Chettite answered Abraham in the hearing of the sons of Chet and of all those entering into the city, saying:
Genesis 23:11 Be with me, lord, and hear me. I give you the field and the cave which is in it; before all my fellow citizens I have given it to you. Bury your dead.
Genesis 23:12 And Abraham bowed before the people of the land
Genesis 23:13 and said to Ephron in the ears of the people of the land: Since you are for me, hear me; take the silver of the field from me, and I will bury my dead there.
Genesis 23:14 And Ephron answered Abraham, saying:
Genesis 23:15 No, lord; I have heard. Land worth four hundred didrachmas of silver—what might this be between me and you? But you, bury your dead.
Genesis 23:16 And Abraham listened to Ephron, and Abraham paid Ephron the silver which he spoke in the ears of the sons of Chet, four hundred didrachmas of silver approved by merchants.
Genesis 23:17 And the field of Ephron which was in the double cave, which is opposite Mamre, stood confirmed—the field and the cave which was in it and every tree which was in the field, which is within its boundaries all around—
Genesis 23:18 as a possession for Abraham before the sons of Chet and all those entering into the city.
Genesis 23:19 After these things Abraham buried Sarra his woman in the cave of the double field, which is opposite Mamre [this is Chebron], in the land of Chanaan.
Genesis 23:20 And the field and the cave which was in it were confirmed for Abraham as a possession for a tomb from the sons of Chet.

## Chapter 24

Genesis 24:1 And Abraham was old, advanced in days, and the Lord blessed Abraham in all things.
Genesis 24:2 And Abraham said to his servant, the elder of his house, who ruled all that was his: Place your hand under my thigh,
Genesis 24:3 and I adjure you by the Lord, the God of heaven and the God of earth, that you do not take a woman for my son Isaac from the daughters of the Chananeans among whom I dwell,
Genesis 24:4 but you shall go into my land, where I came to be, and into my tribe, and from there you shall take a woman for my son Isaac.
Genesis 24:5 And the servant said to him: Perhaps the woman is not willing to go with me back into this land; shall I return your son into the land from where you came out?
Genesis 24:6 And Abraham said to him: Attend to yourself, lest you return my son there.
Genesis 24:7 The Lord, the God of heaven and the God of earth, who took me from the house of my father and from the land in which I was born, who spoke to me and swore to me, saying: To you and to your seed I will give this land—he will send his angel before you, and from there you shall take a woman for my son Isaac.
Genesis 24:8 But if the woman is not willing to go with you into this land, you shall be clean from this oath; only do not return my son there.
Genesis 24:9 And the servant placed his hand under the thigh of Abraham his lord and swore to him concerning this word.
Genesis 24:10 And the servant took ten camels from the camels of his lord and some of all the good things of his lord with himself, and rising, he went into Mesopotamia, into the city of Nachor.
Genesis 24:11 And he made the camels lie outside the city beside the well of water toward evening, when the women drawing water go out.
Genesis 24:12 And he said: Lord, God of my lord Abraham, prosper me before you today and do mercy with my lord Abraham.
Genesis 24:13 Behold, I am standing at the spring of water, and the daughters of those dwelling in the city are going out to draw water,
Genesis 24:14 and it shall be that the maiden to whom I may say: Incline your jug so that I may drink, and she may say to me: Drink, and I will give your camels a drink until they cease drinking—this one you prepared for your servant Isaac, and by this I will know that you did mercy to my lord Abraham.
Genesis 24:15 And it happened before he finished speaking in his mind that, behold, Rebekka came out, who was born to Bathouel, son of Melcha the woman of Nachor, the brother of Abraham, having the jug upon her shoulders.
Genesis 24:16 And the maiden was exceedingly beautiful in appearance; she was a virgin, a man had not known her. And having descended to the spring, she filled the jug and came up.
Genesis 24:17 And the servant ran to meet her and said: Give me a little water to drink from your jug.
Genesis 24:18 And she said: Drink, lord. And she hurried and lowered the jug upon her arm and gave him a drink,
Genesis 24:19 until he ceased drinking. And she said: I will also draw water for your camels until they all drink.
Genesis 24:20 And she hurried and emptied the jug into the watering trough and ran again to the well to draw and drew water for all the camels.
Genesis 24:21 And the man was studying her and remaining silent, to know whether the Lord had prospered his way or not.
Genesis 24:22 And it happened when all the camels ceased drinking that the man took gold earrings, each a drachma in weight, and two bracelets for her hands, ten gold pieces in their weight.
Genesis 24:23 And he questioned her and said: Whose daughter are you? Announce it to me. Is there a place with your father for us to lodge?
Genesis 24:24 And she said to him: I am a daughter of Bathouel, the son of Melcha, whom she bore to Nachor.
Genesis 24:25 And she said to him: There is both much straw and fodder with us, and a place to lodge.
Genesis 24:26 And the man, being well pleased, worshiped the Lord
Genesis 24:27 and said: Blessed is the Lord, the God of my lord Abraham, who did not forsake his righteousness and truth toward my lord. The Lord prospered me into the house of my lord’s brother.
Genesis 24:28 And the girl ran and announced these words in the house of her mother.
Genesis 24:29 And Rebekka had a brother whose name was Laban; and Laban ran outside to the man at the spring.
Genesis 24:30 And it happened when he saw the earrings and the bracelets upon the hands of his sister, and when he heard the words of Rebekka his sister, saying: Thus the man spoke to me, that he came to the man as he was standing by the camels at the spring,
Genesis 24:31 and said to him: Come, enter. Blessed is the Lord. Why are you standing outside? I have prepared the house and a place for the camels.
Genesis 24:32 And the man entered into the house and unsaddled the camels. And he gave straw and fodder to the camels and water to wash his feet and the feet of the men with him.
Genesis 24:33 And he set breads before them to eat. And he said: I shall certainly not eat until I speak my words. And they said: Speak.
Genesis 24:34 And he said: I am a servant of Abraham.
Genesis 24:35 And the Lord blessed my lord exceedingly, and he was exalted; and he gave him sheep and calves, silver and gold, male servants and female servants, camels and donkeys.
Genesis 24:36 And Sarra, the woman of my lord, bore one son to my lord after he grew old, and he gave him as many things as were his.
Genesis 24:37 And my lord made me swear, saying: You shall not take a woman for my son from the daughters of the Chananeans among whom I sojourn in their land,
Genesis 24:38 but you shall go into the house of my father and into my tribe and from there take a woman for my son.
Genesis 24:39 And I said to my lord: Perhaps the woman will not go with me.
Genesis 24:40 And he said to me: The Lord, before whom I was well pleasing, will send his angel with you and prosper your way, and you shall take a woman for my son from my tribe and from the house of my father.
Genesis 24:41 Then you shall be innocent from my curse; for whenever you come into my tribe and they do not give her to you, then you shall be innocent from my oath.
Genesis 24:42 And coming today to the spring, I said: Lord, God of my lord Abraham, if you are prospering my way upon which I am now going,
Genesis 24:43 behold, I am standing at the spring of water, and the daughters of the men of the city will go out to draw water, and it shall be that the maiden to whom I may say: Give me a little water to drink from your jug,
Genesis 24:44 and she may say to me: You also drink, and I will draw water for your camels—this is the woman whom the Lord prepared for his own attendant Isaac, and by this I will know that you have done mercy to my lord Abraham.
Genesis 24:45 And it happened before I finished speaking in my mind that immediately Rebekka came out, having the jug upon her shoulders, and went down to the spring and drew water. And I said to her: Give me a drink.
Genesis 24:46 And hurrying, she lowered her jug from herself and said: You drink, and I will give your camels a drink. And I drank, and she gave my camels a drink.
Genesis 24:47 And I asked her and said: Whose daughter are you? And she said: I am the daughter of Bathouel, the son of Nachor, whom Melcha bore to him. And I placed the earrings upon her and the bracelets around her hands.
Genesis 24:48 And being well pleased, I worshiped the Lord and blessed the Lord, the God of my lord Abraham, who prospered me in a way of truth, to take the daughter of my lord’s brother for his son.
Genesis 24:49 If therefore you are doing mercy and righteousness toward my lord, announce it to me; but if not, announce it to me, so that I may turn to the right or to the left.
Genesis 24:50 And Laban and Bathouel answered and said: This command came out from the Lord; therefore we will not be able to speak against you, evil for good.
Genesis 24:51 Behold, Rebekka is before you; take her and run away, and let her be a woman for your lord’s son, just as the Lord spoke.
Genesis 24:52 And it happened when the servant of Abraham heard these words that he worshiped the Lord upon the earth.
Genesis 24:53 And the servant brought out vessels of silver and gold and clothing and gave them to Rebekka, and he gave gifts to her brother and her mother.
Genesis 24:54 And he and the men who were with him ate and drank and lay down. And rising in the morning, he said: Send me out, so that I may depart to my lord.
Genesis 24:55 But her brothers and her mother said: Let the maiden remain with us about ten days, and after these things she will depart.
Genesis 24:56 But he said to them: Do not hold me back, and the Lord has prospered my way; send me out, so that I may depart to my lord.
Genesis 24:57 And they said: Let us call the girl and ask her mouth.
Genesis 24:58 And they called Rebekka and said to her: Will you go with this man? And she said: I will go.
Genesis 24:59 And they sent out Rebekka their sister and her possessions and the servant of Abraham and those with him.
Genesis 24:60 And they blessed Rebekka their sister and said to her: You are our sister; become thousands of myriads, and let your seed inherit the cities of the adversaries.
Genesis 24:61 And Rebekka and her maidens rose and mounted the camels and went with the man, and the servant took Rebekka and departed.
Genesis 24:62 And Isaac was journeying through the wilderness by the Well of the Vision; and he dwelt in the land toward the southwest.
Genesis 24:63 And Isaac went out to meditate in the field toward evening, and looking up with his eyes, he saw camels coming.
Genesis 24:64 And Rebekka, looking up with her eyes, saw Isaac and jumped down from the camel
Genesis 24:65 and said to the servant: Who is that man journeying in the field to meet us? And the servant said: He is my lord. And she took the veil and wrapped herself.
Genesis 24:66 And the servant recounted to Isaac all the things which he did.
Genesis 24:67 And Isaac entered into the house of his mother and took Rebekka, and she became his woman, and he loved her; and Isaac was comforted concerning Sarra his mother.

## Chapter 25

Genesis 25:1 And Abraham, in addition, took a woman whose name was Chettoura.
Genesis 25:2 And she bore him Zemran and Jexan and Madan and Madiam and Jesbok and Soue.
Genesis 25:3 And Jexan begot Saba and Thaiman and Daidan; and the sons of Daidan came to be Ragouel and Nabdeel and Assouriim and Latousiim and Loomim.
Genesis 25:4 And the sons of Madiam: Gaipha and Apher and Enoch and Abira and Elraga. All these were sons of Chettoura.
Genesis 25:5 And Abraham gave all his possessions to Isaac his son,
Genesis 25:6 and Abraham gave gifts to the sons of his concubines and sent them away from Isaac his son while he was still living, toward the east, into a land of the east.
Genesis 25:7 And these are the years of the days of Abraham’s life, as many as he lived: one hundred seventy-five years.
Genesis 25:8 And failing, Abraham died in a good old age, old and full of days, and was added to his people.
Genesis 25:9 And Isaac and Ismael his sons buried him in the double cave, in the field of Ephron the son of Saar the Chettite, which is opposite Mamre,
Genesis 25:10 the field and the cave which Abraham acquired from the sons of Chet; there they buried Abraham and Sarra his woman.
Genesis 25:11 And it happened after Abraham died that God blessed Isaac his son; and Isaac dwelt beside the Well of the Vision.
Genesis 25:12 Now these are the generations of Ismael the son of Abraham, whom Agar the female servant of Sarra bore for Abraham,
Genesis 25:13 and these are the names of the sons of Ismael, by name according to his generations: the firstborn of Ismael, Nabaioth, and Kedar and Nabdeel and Massam,
Genesis 25:14 and Masma and Idouma and Masse,
Genesis 25:15 and Choddad and Thaiman and Jetour and Naphes and Kedma.
Genesis 25:16 These are the sons of Ismael, and these are their names in their tents and in their settlements: twelve rulers according to their nations.
Genesis 25:17 And these are the years of the life of Ismael: one hundred thirty-seven years; and failing, he died and was added to his race.
Genesis 25:18 And he dwelt from Evilat as far as Sour, which is opposite Egypt, until coming toward the Assyrians; before the face of all his brothers he dwelt.
Genesis 25:19 And these are the generations of Isaac the son of Abraham. Abraham begot Isaac.
Genesis 25:20 And Isaac was forty years old when he took Rebekka, daughter of Bathouel the Syrian from Mesopotamia and sister of Laban the Syrian, as a woman for himself.
Genesis 25:21 And Isaac entreated the Lord concerning Rebekka his woman, because she was barren; and God listened to him, and Rebekka his woman conceived.
Genesis 25:22 And the children were leaping within her; and she said: If it is going to be thus for me, why is this to me? And she went to inquire from the Lord,
Genesis 25:23 and the Lord said to her: Two nations are in your womb, and two peoples will be separated from your belly; and a people will surpass a people, and the greater will serve the lesser.
Genesis 25:24 And the days for her to give birth were fulfilled, and behold, there were twins in her belly.
Genesis 25:25 And the firstborn son came out reddish, all hairy like a hide; and he named his name Esau.
Genesis 25:26 And after this his brother came out, and his hand was holding the heel of Esau; and he called his name Jacob. And Isaac was sixty years old when Rebekka bore them.
Genesis 25:27 And the young men grew, and Esau was a man knowing how to hunt, a rustic, but Jacob was a simple man dwelling in a house.
Genesis 25:28 And Isaac loved Esau, because his game was food for him; but Rebekka loved Jacob.
Genesis 25:29 And Jacob boiled a boiled dish; and Esau came from the field, failing,
Genesis 25:30 and Esau said to Jacob: Give me a taste from this red boiled dish, because I am failing. Because of this his name was called Edom.
Genesis 25:31 And Jacob said to Esau: Give me your birthright today.
Genesis 25:32 And Esau said: Behold, I am going to die, and why is this birthright for me?
Genesis 25:33 And Jacob said to him: Swear to me today. And he swore to him; and Esau gave the birthright to Jacob.
Genesis 25:34 And Jacob gave Esau bread and a boiled dish of lentils, and he ate and drank and rose and went away; and Esau treated the birthright as worthless.

## Chapter 26

Genesis 26:1 And a famine came upon the land besides the former famine which came in the time of Abraham; and Isaac went to Abimelech king of the Phylistiim in Gerara.
Genesis 26:2 And the Lord appeared to him and said: Do not go down into Egypt; but dwell in the land which I may tell you.
Genesis 26:3 And sojourn in this land, and I will be with you and bless you; for to you and to your seed I will give all this land, and I will establish my oath which I swore to Abraham your father.
Genesis 26:4 And I will multiply your seed like the stars of heaven and give to your seed all this land, and in your seed all the nations of the earth will be blessed,
Genesis 26:5 because Abraham your father listened to my voice and guarded my directives and my commandments and my ordinances and my laws.
Genesis 26:6 And Isaac dwelt in Gerara.
Genesis 26:7 And the men of the place questioned him concerning Rebekka his woman, and he said: She is my sister, for he was afraid to say: She is my woman, lest the men of the place kill him concerning Rebekka, because she was beautiful in appearance.
Genesis 26:8 And he spent a long time there; and Abimelech king of Gerara, peering through the window, saw Isaac playing with Rebekka his woman.
Genesis 26:9 And Abimelech called Isaac and said to him: Then indeed she is your woman; why is it that you said: She is my sister? And Isaac said to him: For I said: Lest I die because of her.
Genesis 26:10 And Abimelech said to him: What is this you did to us? One of my race almost lay with your woman, and you brought ignorance upon us.
Genesis 26:11 And Abimelech commanded all his people, saying: Everyone who touches this man or his woman will be liable to death.
Genesis 26:12 And Isaac sowed in that land and found in that year barley bearing a hundredfold; and the Lord blessed him.
Genesis 26:13 And the man was exalted and, proceeding, became greater until he became exceedingly great.
Genesis 26:14 And he came to have livestock of sheep and livestock of cattle and much agriculture. And the Phylistiim envied him,
Genesis 26:15 and all the wells which the servants of his father dug in the time of his father, the Phylistiim stopped them and filled them with earth.
Genesis 26:16 And Abimelech said to Isaac: Depart from us, because you became exceedingly more powerful than we.
Genesis 26:17 And Isaac departed from there and lodged in the ravine of Gerara and dwelt there.
Genesis 26:18 And again Isaac dug the wells of water which the servants of Abraham his father dug and the Phylistiim stopped after Abraham his father died, and he named names for them according to the names which Abraham his father named.
Genesis 26:19 And the servants of Isaac dug in the ravine of Gerara and found there a well of living water.
Genesis 26:20 And the shepherds of Gerara fought with the shepherds of Isaac, asserting that the water was theirs; and he called the name of the well Injustice, for they wronged him.
Genesis 26:21 And Isaac departed from there and dug another well, and they also disputed concerning that one; and he named its name Enmity.
Genesis 26:22 And he departed from there and dug another well, and they did not fight concerning it; and he named its name Broad Place, saying: Because now the Lord has widened for us and increased us upon the earth.
Genesis 26:23 And he went up from there to the Well of the Oath.
Genesis 26:24 And the Lord appeared to him on that night and said: I am the God of Abraham your father. Do not be afraid, for I am with you and have blessed you, and I will multiply your seed because of Abraham your father.
Genesis 26:25 And he built an altar there and called upon the name of the Lord and pitched his tent there; and the servants of Isaac dug a well there.
Genesis 26:26 And Abimelech went to him from Gerara, and Ochozath his bride-conductor and Phicol the commander-in-chief of his force.
Genesis 26:27 And Isaac said to them: Why did you come to me? But you hated me and sent me away from you.
Genesis 26:28 And they said: Seeing, we have seen that the Lord was with you, and we said: Let a curse come to be between us and between you, and we will make a covenant with you,
Genesis 26:29 that you will not do evil with us, since we did not abhor you, and in the manner that we treated you well and sent you away with peace. And now you are blessed by the Lord.
Genesis 26:30 And he made a reception for them, and they ate and drank.
Genesis 26:31 And rising in the morning, a man swore to his neighbor, and Isaac sent them away, and they departed from him with safety.
Genesis 26:32 And it happened on that day that the servants of Isaac arrived and announced to him concerning the well which they dug, and they said: We did not find water.
Genesis 26:33 And he called it Oath; because of this the name of the city is Well of the Oath until today.
Genesis 26:34 And Esau was forty years old and took as a woman Joudin the daughter of Beer the Chettite and Basemmath the daughter of Ailon the Evaean.
Genesis 26:35 And they were quarreling with Isaac and Rebekka.

## Chapter 27

Genesis 27:1 And it happened after Isaac grew old and his eyes were dulled from seeing that he called Esau his elder son and said to him: My son. And he said: Behold, I am here.
Genesis 27:2 And he said: Behold, I have grown old and do not know the day of my end.
Genesis 27:3 Now therefore take your equipment, both the quiver and the bow, and go out into the field and hunt game for me,
Genesis 27:4 and make delicacies for me, as I love, and bring them to me so that I may eat, that my soul may bless you before I die.
Genesis 27:5 And Rebekka heard Isaac speaking to Esau his son. And Esau went into the field to hunt game for his father.
Genesis 27:6 And Rebekka said to Jacob her lesser son: See, I heard your father speaking to Esau your brother, saying:
Genesis 27:7 Bring me game and make delicacies for me, and having eaten, I will bless you before the Lord before I die.
Genesis 27:8 Now therefore, son, listen to me, according to the things which I command you,
Genesis 27:9 and having gone to the sheep, take for me from there two tender and good kids, and I will make them into delicacies for your father, as he loves,
Genesis 27:10 and you shall bring them in to your father, and he will eat, so that your father may bless you before he dies.
Genesis 27:11 And Jacob said to Rebekka his mother: Esau my brother is a hairy man, but I am a smooth man.
Genesis 27:12 Perhaps my father will feel me, and I will be before him as one treating him with contempt, and I will bring a curse upon myself and not a blessing.
Genesis 27:13 And his mother said to him: Your curse be upon me, child; only listen to my voice, and having gone, bring them to me.
Genesis 27:14 And having gone, he took and brought them to his mother, and his mother made delicacies just as his father loved.
Genesis 27:15 And Rebekka took the good robe of Esau her elder son, which was with her in the house, and clothed Jacob her younger son,
Genesis 27:16 and she placed the skins of the kids upon his arms and upon the bare parts of his neck,
Genesis 27:17 and she gave the delicacies and the breads which she made into the hands of Jacob her son.
Genesis 27:18 And he brought them in to his father. And he said: Father. And he said: Behold, I am here. Who are you, child?
Genesis 27:19 And Jacob said to his father: I am Esau your firstborn. I did just as you spoke to me. Rise, sit and eat from my game, so that your soul may bless me.
Genesis 27:20 And Isaac said to his son: What is this which you found quickly, O child? And he said: That which the Lord your God delivered before me.
Genesis 27:21 And Isaac said to Jacob: Draw near to me, and I will feel you, child, whether you are my son Esau or not.
Genesis 27:22 And Jacob drew near to Isaac his father, and he felt him and said: The voice is the voice of Jacob, but the hands are the hands of Esau.
Genesis 27:23 And he did not recognize him, for his hands were hairy like the hands of Esau his brother; and he blessed him.
Genesis 27:24 And he said: Are you my son Esau? And he said: I am.
Genesis 27:25 And he said: Bring it near to me, and I will eat from your game, child, so that my soul may bless you. And he brought it near to him, and he ate; and he brought wine in to him, and he drank.
Genesis 27:26 And Isaac his father said to him: Draw near to me and kiss me, child.
Genesis 27:27 And drawing near, he kissed him, and he smelled the scent of his garments and blessed him and said: Behold, the scent of my son is like the scent of a full field which the Lord blessed.
Genesis 27:28 And may God give you from the dew of heaven and from the richness of the earth and a multitude of grain and wine.
Genesis 27:29 And let nations serve you, and rulers will bow to you; and become lord of your brother, and the sons of your father will bow to you. The one cursing you is accursed, but the one blessing you is blessed.
Genesis 27:30 And it happened after Isaac ceased blessing Jacob his son, and it happened as Jacob went out from the face of Isaac his father, that Esau his brother came from the hunt.
Genesis 27:31 And he also made delicacies and brought them to his father and said to his father: Let my father rise and eat from the game of his son, so that your soul may bless me.
Genesis 27:32 And Isaac his father said to him: Who are you? And he said: I am your firstborn son Esau.
Genesis 27:33 And Isaac was astonished with exceedingly great astonishment and said: Who then is the one who hunted game for me and brought it in to me? And I ate from all before you came and blessed him, and let him be blessed.
Genesis 27:34 And it happened when Esau heard the words of Isaac his father that he cried out with an exceedingly great and bitter voice and said: Bless me also, father.
Genesis 27:35 And he said to him: Your brother came with deceit and took your blessing.
Genesis 27:36 And he said: Rightly was his name called Jacob, for he has heeled me already, this second time; he has taken both my birthright and now my blessing. And Esau said to his father: Did you not leave a blessing for me, father?
Genesis 27:37 And Isaac answered and said to Esau: If I made him your lord and made all his brothers his household servants and supported him with grain and wine, then what shall I do for you, child?
Genesis 27:38 And Esau said to his father: Is there only one blessing with you, father? Bless me also, father. And when Isaac was pierced, Esau cried aloud and wept.
Genesis 27:39 And Isaac his father answered and said to him: Behold, from the richness of the earth shall your dwelling be, and from the dew of heaven above.
Genesis 27:40 And upon your sword you shall live, and you shall serve your brother; but it will be that whenever you take him down, you will loosen his yoke from your neck.
Genesis 27:41 And Esau held a grudge against Jacob concerning the blessing with which his father blessed him; and Esau said in his mind: Let the days of mourning for my father draw near, so that I may kill Jacob my brother.
Genesis 27:42 And the words of Esau her elder son were announced to Rebekka, and sending, she called Jacob her younger son and said to him: Behold, Esau your brother threatens you, to kill you.
Genesis 27:43 Now therefore, child, listen to my voice and rise and flee into Mesopotamia to Laban my brother, into Charran,
Genesis 27:44 and dwell with him some days until the wrath
Genesis 27:45 and the anger of your brother turn away from you, and he forgets the things you have done to him, and sending, I will summon you from there, lest I be made childless from both of you in one day.
Genesis 27:46 And Rebekka said to Isaac: I am vexed with my life because of the daughters of the sons of Chet; if Jacob takes a woman from the daughters of this land, why should I live?

## Chapter 28

Genesis 28:1 And Isaac summoned Jacob and blessed him and commanded him, saying: You shall not take a woman from the daughters of Chanaan.
Genesis 28:2 Rise and flee into Mesopotamia, into the house of Bathouel the father of your mother, and take for yourself from there a woman from the daughters of Laban, your mother’s brother.
Genesis 28:3 And may my God bless you and increase you and multiply you, and you shall become congregations of nations.
Genesis 28:4 And may he give you the blessing of Abraham my father, to you and to your seed after you, to inherit the land of your sojourning which God gave to Abraham.
Genesis 28:5 And Isaac sent Jacob away, and he went into Mesopotamia to Laban the son of Bathouel the Syrian, the brother of Rebekka, the mother of Jacob and Esau.
Genesis 28:6 And Esau saw that Isaac blessed Jacob and that he went away into Mesopotamia of Syria to take for himself a woman from there, and that when he blessed him he commanded him, saying: You shall not take a woman from the daughters of Chanaan,
Genesis 28:7 and that Jacob listened to his father and his mother and went into Mesopotamia of Syria.
Genesis 28:8 And Esau saw that the daughters of Chanaan were evil before Isaac his father,
Genesis 28:9 and Esau went to Ismael and took Maeleth, daughter of Ismael the son of Abraham and sister of Nabaioth, in addition to his women, as a woman.
Genesis 28:10 And Jacob went out from the Well of the Oath and went into Charran.
Genesis 28:11 And he met a place and slept there, for the sun set; and he took from the stones of the place and placed one toward his head and slept in that place.
Genesis 28:12 And he dreamed, and behold, a ladder fixed in the earth, whose head reached into heaven, and the angels of God were ascending and descending upon it.
Genesis 28:13 And the Lord had stood upon it and said: I am the Lord, the God of Abraham your father and the God of Isaac. Do not be afraid. The land upon which you sleep, I will give it to you and to your seed.
Genesis 28:14 And your seed will be like the sand of the earth and will be broadened toward the sea and toward the southwest and toward the north and toward the east, and in you all the tribes of the earth will be blessed, and in your seed.
Genesis 28:15 And behold, I am with you, guarding you throughout every way wherever you may go, and I will return you into this land, because I shall certainly not abandon you until I do all the things which I spoke to you.
Genesis 28:16 And Jacob awoke from his sleep and said: The Lord is in this place, but I did not know.
Genesis 28:17 And he was afraid and said: How fearsome is this place. This is none other than a house of God, and this is the gate of heaven.
Genesis 28:18 And Jacob rose in the morning and took the stone which he placed there toward his head and set it as a pillar and poured oil upon its top.
Genesis 28:19 And Jacob called the name of that place House of God; and Oulamlous was formerly the name of the city.
Genesis 28:20 And Jacob vowed a vow, saying: If the Lord God is with me and guards me on this way which I am going and gives me bread to eat and a garment to put around myself,
Genesis 28:21 and returns me with safety into the house of my father, then the Lord shall be God for me,
Genesis 28:22 and this stone which I set as a pillar shall be a house of God for me, and of all the things which you may give me, I will tithe a tenth of them to you.

## Chapter 29

Genesis 29:1 And Jacob, lifting his feet, went into a land of the east toward Laban the son of Bathouel the Syrian, the brother of Rebekka, mother of Jacob and Esau.
Genesis 29:2 And he sees, and behold, a well in the plain, and there were three flocks of sheep resting upon it; for from that well they gave the flocks a drink, and there was a large stone upon the mouth of the well.
Genesis 29:3 And all the flocks would be gathered there, and they would roll the stone from the mouth of the well and give the sheep a drink and restore the stone upon the mouth of the well to its place.
Genesis 29:4 And Jacob said to them: Brothers, from where are you? And they said: We are from Charran.
Genesis 29:5 And he said to them: Do you know Laban the son of Nachor? And they said: We know him.
Genesis 29:6 And he said to them: Is he healthy? And they said: He is healthy. And behold, Rachel his daughter was coming with the sheep.
Genesis 29:7 And Jacob said: There is still much day; it is not yet time for the cattle to be gathered. Give the sheep a drink and depart and pasture them.
Genesis 29:8 And they said: We will not be able until all the shepherds are gathered and they roll the stone from the mouth of the well, and then we will give the sheep a drink.
Genesis 29:9 While he was still speaking to them, Rachel the daughter of Laban was also coming with the sheep of her father, for she pastured the sheep of her father.
Genesis 29:10 And it happened when Jacob saw Rachel, daughter of Laban the brother of his mother, and the sheep of Laban the brother of his mother, that Jacob drew near and rolled the stone from the mouth of the well and gave the sheep of Laban, the brother of his mother, a drink.
Genesis 29:11 And Jacob kissed Rachel and, crying out with his voice, wept.
Genesis 29:12 And he announced to Rachel that he was the brother of her father and that he was a son of Rebekka, and running, she announced these words to her father.
Genesis 29:13 And it happened when Laban heard the name of Jacob, the son of his sister, that he ran to meet him and embraced him and kissed him and brought him into his house. And he recounted to Laban all these words.
Genesis 29:14 And Laban said to him: You are from my bones and from my flesh. And he was with him a month of days.
Genesis 29:15 And Laban said to Jacob: Because you are my brother, you will not serve me for nothing; announce to me what your wage is.
Genesis 29:16 And Laban had two daughters; the name of the elder was Leia, and the name of the younger Rachel.
Genesis 29:17 And the eyes of Leia were weak, but Rachel was beautiful in form and lovely in appearance.
Genesis 29:18 And Jacob loved Rachel and said: I will serve you seven years for Rachel your younger daughter.
Genesis 29:19 And Laban said to him: It is better for me to give her to you than for me to give her to another man; dwell with me.
Genesis 29:20 And Jacob served seven years for Rachel, and they were before him like a few days because of his loving her. –
Genesis 29:21 And Jacob said to Laban: Give back my woman, for my days have been fulfilled, so that I may go in to her.
Genesis 29:22 And Laban gathered all the men of the place and made a wedding.
Genesis 29:23 And evening came, and Laban took Leia his daughter and brought her in to Jacob, and Jacob went in to her.
Genesis 29:24 And Laban gave Zelpha his female servant to Leia his daughter as her female servant.
Genesis 29:25 And morning came, and behold, it was Leia. And Jacob said to Laban: What is this you did to me? Did I not serve with you for Rachel? And why did you deceive me?
Genesis 29:26 And Laban said: It is not thus in our place, to give the younger before the elder.
Genesis 29:27 Therefore complete the seven days of this one, and I will also give you this one in exchange for the labor which you will work with me for yet another seven years.
Genesis 29:28 And Jacob did thus and completed the seven days of this one, and Laban gave him Rachel his daughter as his woman.
Genesis 29:29 And Laban gave Balla his female servant to Rachel his daughter as her female servant.
Genesis 29:30 And he went in to Rachel; and he loved Rachel more than Leia, and he served him another seven years.
Genesis 29:31 And the Lord, seeing that Leia was hated, opened her womb; but Rachel was barren.
Genesis 29:32 And Leia conceived and bore a son to Jacob; and she called his name Rouben, saying: Because the Lord saw my humiliation; now my man will love me.
Genesis 29:33 And Leia conceived again and bore a second son to Jacob and said: Because the Lord heard that I am hated, he also gave me this one; and she called his name Symeon.
Genesis 29:34 And she conceived yet again and bore a son and said: At the present time my man will be toward me, for I bore him three sons; because of this she called his name Levi.
Genesis 29:35 And conceiving yet again, she bore a son and said: Now yet this time I will acknowledge the Lord; because of this she called his name Juda. And she stopped bearing.

## Chapter 30

Genesis 30:1 And Rachel, seeing that she had not borne for Jacob, envied her sister and said to Jacob: Give me children; but if not, I will come to an end.
Genesis 30:2 And Jacob became angry with Rachel and said to her: Am I in place of God, who deprived you of fruit of the belly?
Genesis 30:3 And Rachel said to Jacob: Behold, my female servant Balla; go in to her, and she will bear upon my knees, and I also will have children from her.
Genesis 30:4 And she gave him Balla her female servant as a woman for him; and Jacob went in to her.
Genesis 30:5 And Balla the female servant of Rachel conceived and bore a son to Jacob.
Genesis 30:6 And Rachel said: God judged for me and listened to my voice and gave me a son; because of this she called his name Dan.
Genesis 30:7 And Balla the female servant of Rachel conceived yet again and bore a second son to Jacob.
Genesis 30:8 And Rachel said: God helped me, and I joined in contest with my sister and prevailed; and she called his name Nephthali.
Genesis 30:9 And Leia saw that she stopped bearing, and she took Zelpha her female servant and gave her to Jacob as a woman.
Genesis 30:10 And Jacob went in to her, and Zelpha the female servant of Leia conceived and bore a son to Jacob.
Genesis 30:11 And Leia said: In fortune; and she named his name Gad.
Genesis 30:12 And Zelpha the female servant of Leia conceived and bore yet a second son to Jacob.
Genesis 30:13 And Leia said: Blessed am I, because the women call me blessed; and she called his name Aser.
Genesis 30:14 And Rouben went in the days of the wheat harvest and found mandrake apples in the field and brought them to Leia his mother. And Rachel said to Leia: Give me some of your son’s mandrakes.
Genesis 30:15 And Leia said: Is it not enough for you that you took my man? Will you also take the mandrakes of my son? And Rachel said: Not so; let him lie with you this night in exchange for the mandrakes of your son.
Genesis 30:16 And Jacob entered from the field at evening, and Leia went out to meet him and said: You shall come in to me today, for I have hired you in exchange for the mandrakes of my son. And he lay with her that night.
Genesis 30:17 And God listened to Leia, and conceiving, she bore a fifth son to Jacob.
Genesis 30:18 And Leia said: God gave my wage in return for my giving my female servant to my man; and she called his name Issachar, which is Wage.
Genesis 30:19 And Leia conceived yet again and bore a sixth son to Jacob.
Genesis 30:20 And Leia said: God has given me a good gift; at the present time my man will choose me, for I bore him six sons. And she called his name Zaboulon.
Genesis 30:21 And after this she bore a daughter and called her name Dina.
Genesis 30:22 And God remembered Rachel, and God listened to her and opened her womb,
Genesis 30:23 and conceiving, she bore a son to Jacob. And Rachel said: My God removed my reproach;
Genesis 30:24 and she called his name Joseph, saying: May God add another son for me.
Genesis 30:25 And it happened when Rachel bore Joseph that Jacob said to Laban: Send me away, so that I may depart into my place and into my land.
Genesis 30:26 Give back my women and the children for whom I have served you, so that I may depart; for you know the service which I have served you.
Genesis 30:27 And Laban said to him: If I found grace before you, I would have divined; for God blessed me at your entrance.
Genesis 30:28 Specify your wage to me, and I will give it.
Genesis 30:29 And Jacob said to him: You know the things for which I have served you and how many of your cattle were with me;
Genesis 30:30 for the things which were yours before me were few, and they increased into a multitude, and the Lord blessed you at my foot. Now therefore, when will I also make a house for myself?
Genesis 30:31 And Laban said to him: What shall I give you? And Jacob said to him: You shall give me nothing. If you do this thing for me, I will again shepherd your sheep and guard them.
Genesis 30:32 Let all your sheep pass today, and separate from there every gray sheep among the lambs and every white-spotted and speckled one among the goats; it shall be my wage.
Genesis 30:33 And my righteousness will answer for me on the day tomorrow, because my wage is before you: every one which is not speckled and white-spotted among the goats and gray among the lambs will be stolen if found with me.
Genesis 30:34 And Laban said to him: Let it be according to your word.
Genesis 30:35 And on that day he separated the speckled and white-spotted male goats and all the speckled and white-spotted female goats and every one which had white in them and every one which was gray among the lambs, and he gave them by the hand of his sons.
Genesis 30:36 And he set a journey of three days between them and between Jacob; and Jacob shepherded the remaining sheep of Laban. –
Genesis 30:37 And Jacob took for himself green rods of storax and walnut and plane tree, and Jacob peeled them with white peelings, stripping off the green; and the white which he peeled appeared variegated upon the rods.
Genesis 30:38 And he placed the rods which he peeled in the troughs of the watering basins, so that whenever the sheep came to drink before the rods, when they came to drink,
Genesis 30:39 the sheep might conceive at the rods; and the sheep bore white-spotted and variegated and ash-colored speckled young.
Genesis 30:40 And Jacob separated the lambs and set before the sheep a white-spotted ram and every variegated one among the lambs; and he separated flocks for himself by themselves and did not mix them with the sheep of Laban.
Genesis 30:41 And it happened at the time when the sheep that were becoming pregnant conceived that Jacob placed the rods before the sheep in the troughs, so that they might conceive by the rods.
Genesis 30:42 But whenever the sheep bore, he did not place them; and the unmarked became Laban’s, but the marked Jacob’s.
Genesis 30:43 And the man became exceedingly, exceedingly rich, and he came to have many cattle and cattle and male servants and female servants and camels and donkeys.

## Chapter 31

Genesis 31:1 And Jacob heard the words of Laban’s sons, saying: Jacob has taken all the things of our father, and from the things of our father he has made all this glory.
Genesis 31:2 And Jacob saw the face of Laban, and behold, it was not toward him as yesterday and the third day.
Genesis 31:3 And the Lord said to Jacob: Return into the land of your father and into your generation, and I will be with you.
Genesis 31:4 And Jacob sent and called Rachel and Leia into the field where the flocks were,
Genesis 31:5 and said to them: I see the face of your father, that it is not toward me as yesterday and the third day; but the God of my father was with me.
Genesis 31:6 And you yourselves know that I have served your father with all my strength.
Genesis 31:7 But your father deceived me and changed my wage of ten lambs, and God did not permit him to harm me.
Genesis 31:8 If he would say thus: The variegated shall be your wage, then all the sheep would bear variegated young; but if he would say: The white shall be your wage, then all the sheep would bear white young.
Genesis 31:9 And God took away all the cattle of your father and gave them to me.
Genesis 31:10 And it happened when the sheep were conceiving that I saw them with my eyes in sleep, and behold, the male goats and the rams mounting the sheep and the female goats were white-spotted and variegated and ash-colored speckled.
Genesis 31:11 And the angel of God said to me in sleep: Jacob. And I said: What is it?
Genesis 31:12 And he said: Look up with your eyes and see the male goats and the rams mounting the sheep and the female goats, white-spotted and variegated and ash-colored speckled, for I have seen as many things as Laban is doing to you.
Genesis 31:13 I am God who appeared to you in Place of God, where you anointed a pillar for me and vowed a vow to me. Now therefore rise and go out from this land and depart into the land of your birth, and I will be with you.
Genesis 31:14 And Rachel and Leia answered and said to him: Is there still a portion or inheritance for us in the house of our father?
Genesis 31:15 Have we not been regarded by him as foreigners? For he sold us and devoured our silver with devouring.
Genesis 31:16 All the wealth and the glory which God took away from our father shall be for us and for our children. Now therefore do as many things as God has said to you.
Genesis 31:17 And Jacob rose and took his women and his children upon the camels,
Genesis 31:18 and led away all his possessions and all his baggage which he acquired in Mesopotamia, and all that was his, to depart to Isaac his father in the land of Chanaan.
Genesis 31:19 And Laban had gone to shear his sheep; and Rachel stole the idols of her father.
Genesis 31:20 And Jacob concealed from Laban the Syrian by not announcing to him that he was fleeing,
Genesis 31:21 and he fled, he and all that was his, and crossed the river and rushed toward the mountain Galaad.
Genesis 31:22 And it was announced to Laban the Syrian on the third day that Jacob had fled,
Genesis 31:23 and taking all his brothers with himself, he pursued after him a journey of seven days and overtook him at the mountain Galaad.
Genesis 31:24 And God came to Laban the Syrian in sleep at night and said to him: Guard yourself, lest you speak evil things with Jacob.
Genesis 31:25 And Laban overtook Jacob; and Jacob pitched his tent in the mountain, but Laban stationed his brothers in the mountain Galaad.
Genesis 31:26 And Laban said to Jacob: What did you do? Why did you secretly flee and carry me off by theft and lead away my daughters like captives of the sword?
Genesis 31:27 And if you had announced it to me, I would have sent you away with gladness and with music, drums and lyre.
Genesis 31:28 I was not deemed worthy to kiss my children and my daughters. But now you acted senselessly.
Genesis 31:29 And now my hand has strength to harm you; but the God of your father spoke to me yesterday, saying: Guard yourself, lest you speak evil things with Jacob.
Genesis 31:30 Now therefore you have gone, for with desire you desired to depart into the house of your father; why did you steal my gods?
Genesis 31:31 And Jacob answered and said to Laban: For I said: Lest you take your daughters away from me, and all that is mine.
Genesis 31:32 Recognize what of yours is with me and take it. And he did not recognize anything with him. And Jacob said to him: With whomever you may find your gods, he shall not live before our brothers. But Jacob did not know that Rachel his woman stole them.
Genesis 31:33 And Laban entered and searched the house of Leia and did not find them; and going out from the house of Leia, he searched the house of Jacob and the house of the two female servants and did not find them. And he also entered into the house of Rachel.
Genesis 31:34 But Rachel took the idols and put them into the saddles of the camel and sat upon them.
Genesis 31:35 And she said to her father: Do not bear it heavily, lord; I am not able to rise before you, because the custom of women is mine. And Laban searched in the whole house and did not find the idols.
Genesis 31:36 And Jacob became angry and fought with Laban; and Jacob answered and said to Laban: What is my injustice and what is my sin, that you pursued after me
Genesis 31:37 and searched all my vessels? What did you find from all the vessels of your house? Place it here before my brothers and your brothers, and let them expose what is between the two of us.
Genesis 31:38 These twenty years I have been with you; your sheep and your female goats did not become childless; the rams of your sheep I did not eat.
Genesis 31:39 What was caught by a beast I did not bring to you; I paid from myself the thefts of day and the thefts of night.
Genesis 31:40 By day I was scorched by heat and by night by frost, and sleep departed from my eyes.
Genesis 31:41 These twenty years I have been in your house; I served you fourteen years in exchange for your two daughters and six years among your sheep, and you deceived me concerning my wage by ten lambs.
Genesis 31:42 If the God of my father Abraham and the Fear of Isaac had not been for me, now you would have sent me away empty. God saw my humiliation and the toil of my hands and rebuked you yesterday.
Genesis 31:43 And Laban answered and said to Jacob: The daughters are my daughters, and the sons my sons, and the cattle my cattle, and all the things which you see are mine and my daughters’. What shall I do to these today, or to their children whom they bore?
Genesis 31:44 Now therefore come, let us make a covenant, I and you, and it shall be a testimony between me and you. And he said to him: Behold, no one is with us; see, God is witness between me and you.
Genesis 31:45 And Jacob took a stone and set it as a pillar.
Genesis 31:46 And Jacob said to his brothers: Gather stones. And they gathered stones and made a mound, and ate and drank there upon the mound. And Laban said to him: This mound testifies between me and you today.
Genesis 31:47 And Laban called it Mound of the Testimony, but Jacob called it Mound Witness.
Genesis 31:48 And Laban said to Jacob: Behold, this mound and this pillar which I set between me and you; this mound testifies and this pillar testifies. Because of this its name was called Mound Testifies,
Genesis 31:49 and The Vision, of which he said: May God look between me and you, because we will depart from one another.
Genesis 31:50 If you humiliate my daughters, if you take women in addition to my daughters, see, no one is with us.
Genesis 31:52 For if I do not cross toward you, nor you cross toward me, this mound and this pillar for evil,
Genesis 31:53 the God of Abraham and the God of Nachor will judge between us. And Jacob swore by the Fear of his father Isaac.
Genesis 31:54 And Jacob sacrificed a sacrifice in the mountain and called his brothers, and they ate and drank and slept in the mountain.

## Chapter 32

Genesis 32:1 And Laban rose in the morning and kissed his sons and his daughters and blessed them, and Laban turned and departed to his place.
Genesis 32:2 And Jacob departed on his own way. And looking up, he saw an encampment of God encamped, and the angels of God met him.
Genesis 32:3 And Jacob said when he saw them: This is an encampment of God; and he called the name of that place Encampments.
Genesis 32:4 And Jacob sent messengers before him to Esau his brother, into the land Seir, into the country Edom,
Genesis 32:5 and commanded them, saying: Thus you shall say to my lord Esau: Thus says your servant Jacob: I sojourned with Laban and delayed until now,
Genesis 32:6 and I came to have cattle and donkeys and sheep and male servants and female servants, and I sent to announce it to my lord Esau, so that your servant may find grace before you.
Genesis 32:7 And the messengers returned to Jacob, saying: We came to your brother Esau, and behold, he is coming to meet you, and four hundred men with him.
Genesis 32:8 And Jacob was exceedingly afraid and perplexed. And he divided the people with him and the cattle and the sheep into two encampments,
Genesis 32:9 and Jacob said: If Esau comes into one encampment and cuts it down, then the second encampment will be for being saved.
Genesis 32:10 And Jacob said: God of my father Abraham and God of my father Isaac, Lord who said to me: Run away into the land of your birth, and I will do you good,
Genesis 32:11 it is enough for me from all the righteousness and from all the truth which you did for your servant; for with my staff I crossed this Jordan, but now I have become two encampments.
Genesis 32:12 Deliver me from the hand of my brother Esau, because I am afraid of him, lest he come and strike me and mother upon children.
Genesis 32:13 But you said: Well, I will do you good and make your seed like the sand of the sea, which will not be numbered because of the multitude.
Genesis 32:14 And he slept there that night. And he took from the things he was carrying as gifts and sent them to Esau his brother:
Genesis 32:15 two hundred female goats, twenty male goats, two hundred sheep, twenty rams,
Genesis 32:16 thirty nursing camels and their children, forty cattle, ten bulls, twenty female donkeys and ten foals.
Genesis 32:17 And he gave each flock separately by the hand to his servants. And he said to his servants: Go before me and make a space between flock and flock.
Genesis 32:18 And he commanded the first, saying: If Esau my brother meets you and asks you, saying: Whose are you, and where are you going, and whose are these things going before you?
Genesis 32:19 You shall say: They are your servant Jacob’s; he has sent gifts to my lord Esau, and behold, he is behind us.
Genesis 32:20 And he commanded the first and the second and the third and all those going behind these flocks, saying: According to this word speak to Esau when you find him,
Genesis 32:21 and you shall say: Behold, your servant Jacob is arriving behind us. For he said: I will propitiate his face with the gifts going before his face, and after this I will see his face, for perhaps he will accept my face.
Genesis 32:22 And the gifts were passing before his face, but he slept that night in the encampment.
Genesis 32:23 And rising that night, he took his two women and the two female servants and his eleven children and crossed the crossing of Jabok.
Genesis 32:24 And he took them and crossed the torrent and caused all that was his to cross.
Genesis 32:25 And Jacob was left alone, and a man was wrestling with him until morning.
Genesis 32:26 And he saw that he was not able against him, and touched the breadth of his thigh, and the breadth of Jacob’s thigh became numb while he wrestled with him.
Genesis 32:27 And he said to him: Send me away, for dawn has risen. But he said: I shall certainly not send you away unless you bless me.
Genesis 32:28 And he said to him: What is your name? And he said: Jacob.
Genesis 32:29 And he said to him: Your name shall no longer be called Jacob, but Israel shall be your name, because you were strong with God and powerful with men.
Genesis 32:30 And Jacob asked and said: Announce your name to me. And he said: Why is it that you ask my name? And he blessed him there.
Genesis 32:31 And Jacob called the name of that place Appearance of God; for I saw God face to face, and my soul was saved.
Genesis 32:32 And the sun rose upon him when he passed the Appearance of God; and he was limping on his thigh.
Genesis 32:33 Because of this the sons of Israel certainly do not eat the sinew which became numb, which is upon the breadth of the thigh, until this day, because he touched the breadth of Jacob’s thigh, the sinew, and it became numb.

## Chapter 33

Genesis 33:1 And Jacob looked up and saw, and behold, Esau his brother was coming, and four hundred men with him. And Jacob further divided the children among Leia and Rachel and the two female servants.
Genesis 33:2 And he placed the two female servants and their sons first, and Leia and her children behind, and Rachel and Joseph last.
Genesis 33:3 But he himself went ahead before them and bowed down upon the ground seven times, until he drew near to his brother.
Genesis 33:4 And Esau ran to meet him, and embracing him, he kissed him and fell upon his neck; and both wept.
Genesis 33:5 And looking up, he saw the women and the children and said: What are these to you? And he said: The children with whom God had mercy on your servant.
Genesis 33:6 And the female servants and their children drew near and bowed down.
Genesis 33:7 And Leia and her children drew near and bowed down; and after these Rachel and Joseph drew near and bowed down.
Genesis 33:8 And he said: What are all these encampments to you, which I met? And he said: That your servant may find grace before you, lord.
Genesis 33:9 And Esau said: I have plenty, brother; let what is yours be yours.
Genesis 33:10 And Jacob said: If I have found grace before you, receive the gifts from my hands; because of this I saw your face as one might see the face of God, and you will be well pleased with me.
Genesis 33:11 Take my blessings, which I brought you, because God had mercy on me and I have all things. And he pressed him, and he took them.
Genesis 33:12 And he said: Having set out, we shall journey straight ahead.
Genesis 33:13 But he said to him: My lord knows that the children are more tender and the sheep and the cattle are giving birth under my care; if therefore I drive them hard for one day, all the livestock will die.
Genesis 33:14 Let my lord go ahead before his servant, and I will strengthen myself on the way according to the slow pace of the journey before me and according to the foot of the children, until I come to my lord at Seir.
Genesis 33:15 And Esau said: I will leave with you some of the people who are with me. But he said: Why this? It is enough that I found grace before you, lord.
Genesis 33:16 And Esau returned that day on his way to Seir.
Genesis 33:17 And Jacob departed for Tents; and he made houses for himself there, and for his livestock he made tents. Because of this he called the name of that place Tents.
Genesis 33:18 And Jacob came to Salem, a city of Sikima, which is in the land of Chanaan, when he came from Mesopotamia of Syria, and he encamped facing the city.
Genesis 33:19 And he acquired the portion of the field where he set his tent there from Emmor, the father of Sychem, for a hundred lambs.
Genesis 33:20 And he set up an altar there and called upon the God of Israel.

## Chapter 34

Genesis 34:1 And Dina, the daughter of Leia, whom she bore to Jacob, went out to observe closely the daughters of the inhabitants.
Genesis 34:2 And Sychem the son of Emmor, the Chorrite, the ruler of the land, saw her, and taking her, he slept with her and humbled her.
Genesis 34:3 And he attended to the soul of Dina the daughter of Jacob, and he loved the maiden and spoke to her according to the mind of the maiden.
Genesis 34:4 And Sychem spoke to Emmor his father, saying: Take this young woman for me as a wife.
Genesis 34:5 And Jacob heard that the son of Emmor had defiled Dina his daughter; but his sons were with his livestock in the plain, and Jacob kept silent until they came.
Genesis 34:6 And Emmor the father of Sychem went out to Jacob to speak to him.
Genesis 34:7 And the sons of Jacob came from the plain; and when they heard, the men were pierced, and it was exceedingly grievous to them, because he had done a shameful thing in Israel by sleeping with the daughter of Jacob; and it shall not be so.
Genesis 34:8 And Emmor spoke to them, saying: Sychem my son chose your daughter in his soul; therefore give her to him as a wife.
Genesis 34:9 Intermarry with us; give your daughters to us, and take our daughters for your sons.
Genesis 34:10 And dwell among us, and behold, the land is broad before you; dwell and trade upon it and acquire possessions in it.
Genesis 34:11 And Sychem said to her father and to her brothers: May I find grace before you, and whatever you say, we will give.
Genesis 34:12 Increase the dowry greatly, and I will give it, whatever you tell me, and you shall give this girl to me as a wife.
Genesis 34:13 But the sons of Jacob answered Sychem and Emmor his father with guile and spoke to them, because they had defiled Dina their sister.
Genesis 34:14 And Symeon and Levi, the brothers of Dina and sons of Leia, said to them: We shall not be able to do this thing, to give our sister to a man who has a foreskin; for it is a reproach to us.
Genesis 34:15 In this we shall be made like you and dwell among you, if you also become as we are, by having every male of yours circumcised.
Genesis 34:16 And we will give our daughters to you, and from your daughters we will take wives for ourselves, and we will dwell beside you and be as one race.
Genesis 34:17 But if you do not listen to us, to be circumcised, we will take our daughters and go away.
Genesis 34:18 And the words were pleasing before Emmor and before Sychem the son of Emmor.
Genesis 34:19 And the young man did not delay to do this thing, for he was devoted to the daughter of Jacob; and he was the most honored of all those in the house of his father.
Genesis 34:20 And Emmor and Sychem his son came to the gate of their city and spoke to the men of their city, saying:
Genesis 34:21 These men are peaceful with us; let them dwell upon the land and trade upon it, and behold, the land is broad before them. We will take their daughters as wives for ourselves, and we will give our daughters to them.
Genesis 34:22 Only in this will the men be made like us, so as to dwell with us and be one people: in every male of ours being circumcised, just as they themselves are circumcised.
Genesis 34:23 And will not their livestock and their possessions and their quadrupeds be ours? Only in this let us be made like them, and they will dwell with us.
Genesis 34:24 And all who went out through the gate of their city listened to Emmor and Sychem his son, and every male circumcised the flesh of his foreskin.
Genesis 34:25 And it happened on the third day, when they were in pain, that the two sons of Jacob, Symeon and Levi, the brothers of Dina, each took his sword and entered the city securely and killed every male.
Genesis 34:26 And they killed both Emmor and Sychem his son by the edge of the sword, and they took Dina from the house of Sychem and went out.
Genesis 34:27 And the sons of Jacob went in upon the wounded and plundered the city in which they had defiled Dina their sister.
Genesis 34:28 And they took their sheep and their cattle and their donkeys, both whatever was in the city and whatever was in the plain.
Genesis 34:29 And they took captive all their bodies and all their baggage and their women, and they plundered both whatever was in the city and whatever was in the houses.
Genesis 34:30 And Jacob said to Symeon and Levi: You have made me hated, so that I am evil to all those who inhabit the land, among both the Chanaanites and the Pherezites; but I am few in number, and when they gather against me, they will cut me down, and I shall be wiped out, I and my house.
Genesis 34:31 But they said: Shall they use our sister as a prostitute?

## Chapter 35

Genesis 35:1 And God said to Jacob: Arise, go up to the place Baethel and dwell there, and make an altar there to the God who appeared to you when you were running away from the face of Esau your brother.
Genesis 35:2 And Jacob said to his house and to all those with him: Remove the foreign gods that are with you from your midst, and cleanse yourselves and change your robes.
Genesis 35:3 And arising, let us go up to Baethel and make an altar there to the God who listened to me in the day of affliction, who was with me and brought me safely through the way in which I journeyed.
Genesis 35:4 And they gave Jacob the foreign gods that were in their hands and the earrings that were in their ears, and Jacob hid them under the terebinth in Sikima and destroyed them until this day.
Genesis 35:5 And Israel departed from Sikima, and the fear of God came upon the cities around them, and they did not pursue after the sons of Israel.
Genesis 35:6 And Jacob came to Louza, which is in the land of Chanaan, which is Baethel, he and all the people who were with him.
Genesis 35:7 And he built an altar there and called the name of the place Baethel; for there God appeared to him when he was running away from the face of Esau his brother.
Genesis 35:8 And Debbora, the nurse of Rebekka, died below Baethel under the oak, and Jacob called its name Oak of Mourning.
Genesis 35:9 And God appeared to Jacob while he was still in Louza, when he arrived from Mesopotamia of Syria, and God blessed him.
Genesis 35:10 And God said to him: Your name is Jacob; your name shall no longer be called Jacob, but Israel shall be your name.
Genesis 35:11 And God said to him: I am your God; increase and multiply; nations and congregations of nations will be from you, and kings will come out from your loin.
Genesis 35:12 And the land that I have given to Abraham and Isaac, I have given it to you; it shall be yours, and to your seed after you I will give this land.
Genesis 35:13 And God went up from him, out of the place where he spoke with him.
Genesis 35:14 And Jacob set up a pillar in the place where he spoke with him, a stone pillar, and he poured a libation upon it and poured oil upon it.
Genesis 35:15 And Jacob called the name of the place in which God spoke with him there Baethel.
Genesis 35:16 And Jacob departed from Baethel and pitched his tent beyond the tower of Gader. And it happened when he drew near Chabratha, to come into the land Ephratha, that Rachel gave birth and had a difficult labor in the birth.
Genesis 35:17 And it happened while she was giving birth with difficulty that the midwife said to her: Take courage, for this one also is a son for you.
Genesis 35:18 And it happened as she let go her soul—for she was dying—that she called his name Son of My Pain; but his father called him Benjamin.
Genesis 35:19 And Rachel died and was buried on the road to Ephratha [this is Bethlehem].
Genesis 35:20 And Jacob set up a pillar upon her memorial; this is the pillar of Rachel’s memorial until this day.
Genesis 35:22 And it happened when Israel dwelt in that land that Reuben went and slept with Balla, his father’s concubine; and Israel heard, and it appeared evil before him. And the sons of Jacob were twelve.
Genesis 35:23 The sons of Leia: Reuben, Jacob’s firstborn, Symeon, Levi, Judas, Issachar, Zabulon.
Genesis 35:24 And the sons of Rachel: Joseph and Benjamin.
Genesis 35:25 And the sons of Balla, the female servant of Rachel: Dan and Nephthali.
Genesis 35:26 And the sons of Zelpha, the female servant of Leia: Gad and Aser. These are the sons of Jacob who were born to him in Mesopotamia of Syria.
Genesis 35:27 And Jacob came to Isaac his father at Mambre, to the city of the plain [this is Chebron], in the land of Chanaan, where Abraham and Isaac sojourned.
Genesis 35:28 And the days of Isaac that he lived were a hundred eighty years.
Genesis 35:29 And expiring, he died and was added to his race, older and full of days; and Esau and Jacob his sons buried him.

## Chapter 36

Genesis 36:1 And these are the generations of Esau [he is Edom].
Genesis 36:2 And Esau took women for himself from the daughters of the Chanaanites: Ada the daughter of Ailon the Chettite, and Elibema the daughter of Ana the son of Sebegon the Evite,
Genesis 36:3 and Basemmath the daughter of Ismael, the sister of Nabaioth.
Genesis 36:4 And Ada bore Eliphas to Esau, and Basemmath bore Raguel,
Genesis 36:5 and Elibema bore Jeous and Jeglom and Kore. These are the sons of Esau who were born to him in the land of Chanaan.
Genesis 36:6 And Esau took his women and his sons and his daughters and all the bodies of his house and all his possessions and all his livestock and everything that he acquired and everything that he procured in the land of Chanaan, and he journeyed from the land of Chanaan, away from the face of Jacob his brother.
Genesis 36:7 For their possessions were too many for them to dwell together, and the land of their sojourning was not able to bear them because of the multitude of their possessions.
Genesis 36:8 And Esau dwelt on Mount Seir [Esau himself is Edom].
Genesis 36:9 And these are the generations of Esau, the father of Edom, on Mount Seir,
Genesis 36:10 and these are the names of the sons of Esau: Eliphas the son of Ada, the woman of Esau, and Raguel the son of Basemmath, the woman of Esau.
Genesis 36:11 And the sons of Eliphas were: Thaiman, Omar, Sophar, Gothom, and Kenez.
Genesis 36:12 And Thamna was a concubine of Eliphas the son of Esau, and she bore Amalek to Eliphas. These are the sons of Ada, the woman of Esau.
Genesis 36:13 And these are the sons of Raguel: Nachoth, Zare, Some, and Moze. These were the sons of Basemmath, the woman of Esau.
Genesis 36:14 And these were the sons of Elibema, the daughter of Ana the son of Sebegon, the woman of Esau; and she bore Jeous and Jeglom and Kore to Esau. –
Genesis 36:15 These are the rulers, the sons of Esau. The sons of Eliphas, the firstborn of Esau: ruler Thaiman, ruler Omar, ruler Sophar, ruler Kenez,
Genesis 36:16 ruler Kore, ruler Gothom, ruler Amalek. These are the rulers of Eliphas in the land of Idoumea; these are the sons of Ada.
Genesis 36:17 And these are the sons of Raguel, the son of Esau: ruler Nachoth, ruler Zare, ruler Some, ruler Moze. These are the rulers of Raguel in the land of Edom; these are the sons of Basemmath, the woman of Esau.
Genesis 36:18 And these are the sons of Elibema, the woman of Esau: ruler Jeous, ruler Jeglom, ruler Kore. These are the rulers of Elibema. –
Genesis 36:19 These are the sons of Esau, and these are their rulers. These are the sons of Edom.
Genesis 36:20 And these are the sons of Seir the Chorrite who inhabits the land: Lotan, Sobal, Sebegon, Ana,
Genesis 36:21 and Deson and Asar and Rison. These are the rulers of the Chorrite, the son of Seir, in the land of Edom.
Genesis 36:22 And the sons of Lotan were: Chorri and Aiman; and the sister of Lotan was Thamna.
Genesis 36:23 And these are the sons of Sobal: Golon and Manachath and Gaibel, Soph and Oman.
Genesis 36:24 And these are the sons of Sebegon: Aie and Onan. This is Onas, who found Jamin in the wilderness when he was tending the draft animals of Sebegon his father.
Genesis 36:25 And these are the sons of Ana: Deson; and Elibema was a daughter of Ana.
Genesis 36:26 And these are the sons of Deson: Amada and Asban and Jethran and Charran.
Genesis 36:27 And these are the sons of Asar: Balaan and Zoukam and Jooukam and Oukan.
Genesis 36:28 And these are the sons of Rison: Os and Aram. –
Genesis 36:29 These are the rulers of Chorri: ruler Lotan, ruler Sobal, ruler Sebegon, ruler Ana,
Genesis 36:30 ruler Deson, ruler Asar, ruler Rison. These are the rulers of Chorri in their rulerships in the land of Edom.
Genesis 36:31 And these are the kings who reigned in Edom before a king reigned in Israel.
Genesis 36:32 And Balak the son of Beor reigned in Edom, and the name of his city was Dennaba.
Genesis 36:33 And Balak died, and Jobab the son of Zara from Bosorra reigned instead of him.
Genesis 36:34 And Jobab died, and Asom from the land of the Thaimanites reigned instead of him.
Genesis 36:35 And Asom died, and Adad the son of Barad, who cut down Madiam in the plain of Moab, reigned instead of him, and the name of his city was Geththaim.
Genesis 36:36 And Adad died, and Samala from Masekka reigned instead of him.
Genesis 36:37 And Samala died, and Saul from Rooboth by the river reigned instead of him.
Genesis 36:38 And Saul died, and Balaennon the son of Achobor reigned instead of him.
Genesis 36:39 And Balaennon the son of Achobor died, and Arad the son of Barad reigned instead of him, and the name of his city was Phogor; and the name of his woman was Maitabeel, the daughter of Matraith the son of Maizoob.
Genesis 36:40 These are the names of the rulers of Esau in their tribes, according to their place, in their territories and in their nations: ruler Thamna, ruler Gola, ruler Jether,
Genesis 36:41 ruler Elibemas, ruler Elas, ruler Phinon,
Genesis 36:42 ruler Kenez, ruler Thaiman, ruler Mazar,
Genesis 36:43 ruler Megediel, ruler Zaphoim. These are the rulers of Edom in the inhabited places in the land of their possession. This is Esau, the father of Edom.

## Chapter 37

Genesis 37:1 And Jacob dwelt in the land where his father sojourned, in the land of Chanaan.
Genesis 37:2 And these are the generations of Jacob. Joseph was seventeen years old, shepherding the sheep with his brothers while young, with the sons of Balla and with the sons of Zelpha, the women of his father; and Joseph brought an evil reproach to Israel their father.
Genesis 37:3 And Jacob loved Joseph beyond all his sons, because he was a son of old age to him; and he made him a multicolored tunic.
Genesis 37:4 And when his brothers saw that their father loved him from among all his sons, they hated him and were not able to speak anything peaceful to him.
Genesis 37:5 And Joseph dreamed a dream and reported it to his brothers,
Genesis 37:6 and he said to them: Hear this dream that I dreamed.
Genesis 37:7 I thought we were binding bundles in the midst of the plain, and my bundle arose and stood upright, and your bundles turned around and bowed down to my bundle.
Genesis 37:8 And his brothers said to him: Reigning, will you reign over us, or ruling, will you rule us? And they added still more to their hatred of him because of his dreams and because of his words. –
Genesis 37:9 And he saw another dream and related it to his father and to his brothers and said: Behold, I dreamed another dream, as though the sun and the moon and eleven stars were bowing down to me.
Genesis 37:10 And his father rebuked him and said to him: What is this dream that you dreamed? Having come, shall we indeed come—I and your mother and your brothers—to bow down to you upon the ground?
Genesis 37:11 And his brothers envied him, but his father preserved the word.
Genesis 37:12 And his brothers journeyed to shepherd the sheep of their father in Sychem.
Genesis 37:13 And Israel said to Joseph: Are not your brothers shepherding in Sychem? Come, I will send you to them. And he said to him: Behold, I am here.
Genesis 37:14 And Israel said to him: Go and see whether your brothers and the sheep are healthy, and report to me. And he sent him from the valley of Chebron, and he came to Sychem.
Genesis 37:15 And a man found him wandering in the plain; and the man questioned him, saying: What are you seeking?
Genesis 37:16 And he said: I am seeking my brothers; report to me where they are shepherding.
Genesis 37:17 And the man said to him: They have departed from here, for I heard them saying: Let us journey to Dothaim. And Joseph journeyed after his brothers and found them in Dothaim.
Genesis 37:18 And they foresaw him from far away, before he drew near to them, and they plotted evil to kill him.
Genesis 37:19 And each said to his brother: Behold, that dreamer is coming.
Genesis 37:20 Now therefore, come, let us kill him and throw him into one of the pits, and we will say: An evil beast devoured him. And we will see what his dreams will be.
Genesis 37:21 But Reuben heard and rescued him from their hands and said: We shall not strike him to death.
Genesis 37:22 And Reuben said to them: Do not shed blood; cast him into this pit in the wilderness, but do not bring a hand upon him—so that he might rescue him from their hands and restore him to his father.
Genesis 37:23 And it happened when Joseph came to his brothers that they stripped Joseph of the multicolored tunic that was around him,
Genesis 37:24 and taking him, they threw him into the pit; and the pit was empty and had no water.
Genesis 37:25 And they sat down to eat bread, and looking up with their eyes, they saw, and behold, Ismaelite travelers were coming from Galaad, and their camels were loaded with incense and resin and stacte; and they were journeying to bring them down into Egypt.
Genesis 37:26 And Judas said to his brothers: What use is it if we kill our brother and hide his blood?
Genesis 37:27 Come, let us sell him to these Ismaelites, but let our hands not be upon him, because he is our brother and our flesh. And his brothers listened.
Genesis 37:28 And the Madianite men, the merchants, were passing by, and they pulled and brought Joseph up out of the pit and sold Joseph to the Ismaelites for twenty gold pieces, and they brought Joseph down into Egypt.
Genesis 37:29 And Reuben returned to the pit and did not see Joseph in the pit, and he tore his garments.
Genesis 37:30 And he returned to his brothers and said: The boy is not here; and I, where am I to go now?
Genesis 37:31 And taking the tunic of Joseph, they slaughtered a kid of the goats and stained the tunic with the blood.
Genesis 37:32 And they sent the multicolored tunic and brought it to their father and said: We found this; recognize whether it is the tunic of your son or not.
Genesis 37:33 And he recognized it and said: It is the tunic of my son; an evil beast devoured him, a beast seized Joseph.
Genesis 37:34 And Jacob tore his garments and put sackcloth upon his loin and mourned his son for many days.
Genesis 37:35 And all his sons and daughters gathered and came to comfort him, and he did not wish to be comforted, saying: I shall go down to my son mourning, into Hades. And his father wept for him. –
Genesis 37:36 And the Madianites sold Joseph in Egypt to Petephres, the eunuch of Pharao, the chief cook.

## Chapter 38

Genesis 38:1 And it happened at that time that Judas went down from his brothers and arrived as far as a certain Odollamite man whose name was Iras.
Genesis 38:2 And Judas saw there the daughter of a Chanaanite man whose name was Saua, and he took her and went in to her.
Genesis 38:3 And conceiving, she bore a son and called his name Er.
Genesis 38:4 And conceiving again, she bore a son and called his name Aunan.
Genesis 38:5 And adding again, she bore a son and called his name Selom. And she was in Chasbi when she bore them.
Genesis 38:6 And Judas took a woman for Er his firstborn, whose name was Thamar.
Genesis 38:7 And Er, the firstborn of Judas, became evil before the Lord, and God killed him.
Genesis 38:8 And Judas said to Aunan: Go in to the woman of your brother, and perform the duty of a brother-in-law with her, and raise up seed for your brother.
Genesis 38:9 But Aunan, knowing that the seed would not be his, would, whenever he went in to the woman of his brother, pour it out upon the ground so as not to give seed to his brother.
Genesis 38:10 And it appeared evil before God that he did this, and he put this one to death also.
Genesis 38:11 And Judas said to Thamar his daughter-in-law: Sit as a widow in the house of your father until Selom my son becomes grown. For he said: Lest this one also die like his brothers. And Thamar went away and sat in the house of her father.
Genesis 38:12 And the days were multiplied, and Saua the woman of Judas died; and being comforted, Judas went up to those shearing his sheep, he and Iras his shepherd, the Odollamite, to Thamna.
Genesis 38:13 And it was reported to Thamar his daughter-in-law, saying: Behold, your father-in-law is going up to Thamna to shear his sheep.
