Genesis 38:14 And removing the garments of her widowhood from herself, she put on a veil and beautified herself and sat by the gates of Ainan, which is on the way to Thamna; for she saw that Selom had become grown, but he had not given her to him as a woman.
Genesis 38:15 And Judas saw her and thought her to be a prostitute, for she had covered her face, and he did not recognize her.
Genesis 38:16 And he turned aside from the road toward her and said to her: Allow me to go in to you; for he did not know that she was his daughter-in-law. And she said: What will you give me if you go in to me?
Genesis 38:17 And he said: I will send you a kid of the goats from the sheep. And she said: If you give a pledge until you send it.
Genesis 38:18 And he said: What pledge shall I give you? And she said: Your ring and necklace and the staff that is in your hand. And he gave them to her and went in to her, and she conceived by him.
Genesis 38:19 And arising, she went away and removed the veil from herself and put on the garments of her widowhood.
Genesis 38:20 And Judas sent the kid from the goats by the hand of his shepherd, the Odollamite, to recover the pledge from the woman, and he did not find her.
Genesis 38:21 And he questioned the men from the place: Where is the prostitute who was in Ainan by the road? And they said: There was no prostitute here.
Genesis 38:22 And he returned to Judas and said: I did not find her, and the men from the place say that there is no prostitute here.
Genesis 38:23 And Judas said: Let her have them, but let us not perhaps be laughed at; I sent this kid, but you did not find her.
Genesis 38:24 And it happened after three months that it was reported to Judas, saying: Thamar your daughter-in-law has prostituted herself, and behold, she is pregnant from prostitution. And Judas said: Bring her out, and let her be burned.
Genesis 38:25 And as she was being led away, she sent to her father-in-law, saying: By the man whose these things are, I am pregnant. And she said: Recognize whose ring and necklace and staff these are.
Genesis 38:26 And Judas recognized them and said: Thamar has been justified rather than I, because I did not give her to Selom my son. And he did not add again to know her.
Genesis 38:27 And it happened when she was giving birth, and there were twins in her womb.
Genesis 38:28 And it happened while she was giving birth that one put his hand out first; and the midwife took it and bound scarlet upon his hand, saying: This one will come out first.
Genesis 38:29 But when he drew his hand back, immediately his brother came out. And she said: Why was a barrier cut through because of you? And she called his name Phares.
Genesis 38:30 And after this his brother came out, upon whose hand was the scarlet; and she called his name Zara.

## Chapter 39

Genesis 39:1 And Joseph was brought down into Egypt, and Petephres, the eunuch of Pharao, the chief cook, an Egyptian man, acquired him from the hand of the Ismaelites who brought him down there.
Genesis 39:2 And the Lord was with Joseph, and he was a man succeeding, and he came to be in the house beside his Egyptian lord.
Genesis 39:3 And his lord knew that the Lord was with him, and whatever he did, the Lord prospered it in his hands.
Genesis 39:4 And Joseph found grace before his lord and was pleasing to him, and he appointed him over his house, and everything that was his he gave through the hand of Joseph.
Genesis 39:5 And it happened after he was appointed over his house and over everything that was his that the Lord blessed the house of the Egyptian because of Joseph, and the blessing of the Lord came to be in all his possessions in the house and in the field.
Genesis 39:6 And he entrusted everything that was his into the hands of Joseph, and he knew nothing of his own affairs except the bread that he himself ate. And Joseph was handsome in form and exceedingly beautiful in appearance.
Genesis 39:7 And it happened after these words that the woman of his lord cast her eyes upon Joseph and said: Sleep with me.
Genesis 39:8 But he did not wish to, and he said to the woman of his lord: If my lord knows nothing in his house because of me and has given everything that is his into my hands,
Genesis 39:9 and nothing in this house is above me, nor has anything been withheld from me except you, because you are his woman, then how shall I do this evil thing and sin before God?
Genesis 39:10 And when she spoke to Joseph day after day, he did not listen to her, to sleep with her, to be with her. –
Genesis 39:11 And it happened on a certain such day that Joseph entered the house to do his works, and no one of those in the house was inside,
Genesis 39:12 and she dragged him by his garments, saying: Sleep with me. And leaving his garments in her hands, he fled and went out outside.
Genesis 39:13 And it happened when she saw that he had left his garments in her hands and fled and went out outside,
Genesis 39:14 that she called those who were in the house and spoke to them, saying: See, he brought a Hebrew servant in to us to mock us; he came in to me, saying: Sleep with me, and I cried out with a great voice.
Genesis 39:15 And when he heard that I raised my voice and cried out, he left his garments beside me and fled and went out outside.
Genesis 39:16 And she leaves the garments beside herself until the lord came to his house.
Genesis 39:17 And she spoke to him according to these words, saying: The Hebrew servant whom you brought in to us came in to me to mock me and said to me: I shall sleep with you.
Genesis 39:18 But when he heard that I raised my voice and cried out, he left his garments beside me and fled and went out outside.
Genesis 39:19 And it happened when his lord heard the words of his woman, as many as she spoke to him, saying: Thus your servant did to me, that he became angry with wrath.
Genesis 39:20 And the lord of Joseph took him and cast him into the fortress, into the place in which the prisoners of the king are held there in the fortress.
Genesis 39:21 And the Lord was with Joseph and poured mercy over him and gave him grace before the chief jailer.
Genesis 39:22 And the chief jailer gave the prison through the hand of Joseph, and all those who had been led away, as many as were in the prison, and everything that they do there.
Genesis 39:23 The chief jailer of the prison knew nothing because of him, for everything was through the hand of Joseph, because the Lord was with him; and whatever he did, the Lord prospered it in his hands.

## Chapter 40

Genesis 40:1 And it happened after these words that the chief wine-pourer of the king of Egypt and the chief baker sinned against their lord, the king of Egypt.
Genesis 40:2 And Pharao was angry with his two eunuchs, with the chief wine-pourer and with the chief baker,
Genesis 40:3 and he placed them in custody beside the jailer, in the prison, in the place where Joseph had been led away, there.
Genesis 40:4 And the chief jailer entrusted them to Joseph, and he attended them; and they were days in custody. –
Genesis 40:5 And both saw a dream, each his dream, in one night, the vision of his dream—the chief wine-pourer and the chief baker, who belonged to the king of Egypt, who were in the prison.
Genesis 40:6 And Joseph came in to them in the morning and saw them, and they were troubled.
Genesis 40:7 And he questioned the eunuchs of Pharao who were with him in custody beside his lord, saying: Why are your faces gloomy today?
Genesis 40:8 And they said to him: We saw a dream, and there is no one interpreting it. And Joseph said to them: Is not their explanation through God? Therefore relate them to me. –
Genesis 40:9 And the chief wine-pourer related his dream to Joseph and said: In my sleep a vine was before me,
Genesis 40:10 and in the vine were three stems, and it was blooming, having produced shoots; the clusters of grapes were ripe.
Genesis 40:11 And the cup of Pharao was in my hand, and I took the cluster of grapes and squeezed it into the cup and gave the cup into the hands of Pharao.
Genesis 40:12 And Joseph said to him: This is its interpretation: the three stems are three days.
Genesis 40:13 Yet three days, and Pharao will remember your office and restore you to your office of chief wine-pourer, and you will give the cup of Pharao into his hand according to your former office, as you were pouring wine.
Genesis 40:14 But remember me through yourself when it becomes well for you, and you will do mercy with me and remind Pharao about me and bring me out of this fortress.
Genesis 40:15 For by theft I was stolen from the land of the Hebrews, and here I did nothing, but they cast me into this pit. –
Genesis 40:16 And the chief baker saw that he had interpreted rightly and said to Joseph: I also saw a dream, and I thought I was carrying three baskets of coarse loaves upon my head,
Genesis 40:17 and in the upper basket were some of all the kinds that King Pharao eats, the work of a baker, and the birds of heaven were devouring them from the basket above my head.
Genesis 40:18 And Joseph answered and said to him: This is its interpretation: the three baskets are three days.
Genesis 40:19 Yet three days, and Pharao will remove your head from you and hang you upon wood, and the birds of heaven will eat your flesh from you. –
Genesis 40:20 And it happened on the third day—it was the birthday of Pharao—and he made a drinking feast for all his servants. And he remembered the office of the chief wine-pourer and the office of the chief baker in the midst of his servants,
Genesis 40:21 and he restored the chief wine-pourer to his office, and he gave the cup into the hand of Pharao,
Genesis 40:22 but he hanged the chief baker, just as Joseph had interpreted to them.
Genesis 40:23 But the chief wine-pourer did not remember Joseph, but forgot him.

## Chapter 41

Genesis 41:1 And it happened after two years of days that Pharao saw a dream. He thought he was standing upon the river,
Genesis 41:2 and behold, as though from the river seven cows were coming up, beautiful in appearance and choice in flesh, and were grazing in the marsh grass.
Genesis 41:3 And seven other cows were coming up after these from the river, ugly in appearance and thin in flesh, and were grazing beside the cows by the lip of the river.
Genesis 41:4 And the seven cows that were ugly and thin in flesh devoured the seven cows that were beautiful in appearance and choice. And Pharao awoke. –
Genesis 41:5 And he dreamed a second time, and behold, seven ears of grain were coming up on one stalk, choice and beautiful.
Genesis 41:6 And seven other ears, thin and wind-blasted, were sprouting after them.
Genesis 41:7 And the seven thin and wind-blasted ears swallowed the seven choice and full ears. And Pharao awoke, and it was a dream.
Genesis 41:8 And morning came, and his soul was troubled; and sending, he called all the interpreters of Egypt and all its wise men, and Pharao related the dream to them, and there was no one who could report it to Pharao.
Genesis 41:9 And the chief wine-pourer spoke to Pharao, saying: I call my sin to remembrance today.
Genesis 41:10 Pharao was angry with his servants and placed us in custody in the house of the chief cook, both me and the chief baker.
Genesis 41:11 And we saw a dream in one night, both I and he; we each saw according to his own dream.
Genesis 41:12 And a young man was there with us, a Hebrew servant of the chief cook, and we related them to him, and he interpreted them for us.
Genesis 41:13 And it happened just as he interpreted them for us; thus it also came to pass: I was restored to my office, but that one was hanged.
Genesis 41:14 And Pharao sent and called Joseph, and they brought him out of the fortress and shaved him and changed his robe, and he came to Pharao.
Genesis 41:15 And Pharao said to Joseph: I have seen a dream, and there is no one interpreting it; but I have heard people saying about you that when you hear dreams, you interpret them.
Genesis 41:16 And Joseph answered Pharao and said: Without God, the salvation of Pharao will not be answered.
Genesis 41:17 And Pharao spoke to Joseph, saying: In my sleep I thought I was standing beside the lip of the river,
Genesis 41:18 and as though from the river seven cows were coming up, beautiful in appearance and choice in flesh, and were grazing in the marsh grass.
Genesis 41:19 And behold, seven other cows were coming up behind them from the river, evil and ugly in appearance and thin in flesh, such as I did not see uglier than these in the whole land of Egypt.
Genesis 41:20 And the seven ugly and thin cows devoured the first seven beautiful and choice cows,
Genesis 41:21 and they entered their bellies, and it did not become evident that they had entered their bellies, and their appearances were ugly just as at the beginning. And having awakened, I slept,
Genesis 41:22 and again I saw in my sleep, and as though seven ears of grain were coming up on one stalk, full and beautiful.
Genesis 41:23 And seven other ears, thin and wind-blasted, were sprouting next to them.
Genesis 41:24 And the seven thin and wind-blasted ears swallowed the seven beautiful and full ears. Therefore I spoke to the interpreters, and there was no one who could report it to me.
Genesis 41:25 And Joseph said to Pharao: The dream of Pharao is one. As many things as God is doing, he has shown to Pharao.
Genesis 41:26 The seven beautiful cows are seven years, and the seven beautiful ears are seven years; the dream of Pharao is one.
Genesis 41:27 And the seven thin cows coming up behind them are seven years, and the seven thin and wind-blasted ears will be seven years of famine.
Genesis 41:28 And as for the word that I have said to Pharao: As many things as God is doing, he has shown to Pharao.
Genesis 41:29 Behold, seven years are coming, a great abundance in all the land of Egypt.
Genesis 41:30 But seven years of famine will come after these, and they will forget the fullness in the whole land of Egypt, and the famine will consume the land.
Genesis 41:31 And the abundance will not be recognized upon the land because of the famine that will be after these, for it will be exceedingly severe.
Genesis 41:32 And concerning the dream of Pharao being repeated twice: it is because the word from God will be true, and God will hasten to do it.
Genesis 41:33 Now therefore, look for a prudent and intelligent man and appoint him over the land of Egypt.
Genesis 41:34 And let Pharao act and appoint district rulers over the land, and let them take a fifth of all the produce of the land of Egypt during the seven years of abundance.
Genesis 41:35 And let them gather all the foods of these seven coming good years, and let the grain be gathered under the hand of Pharao; let foods be guarded in the cities.
Genesis 41:36 And the foods will be kept for the land for the seven years of famine that will be in the land of Egypt, and the land will not be destroyed in the famine.
Genesis 41:37 And the words were pleasing before Pharao and before all his servants.
Genesis 41:38 And Pharao said to all his servants: Shall we find such a man, who has the spirit of God in him?
Genesis 41:39 And Pharao said to Joseph: Since God has shown you all these things, there is no man more prudent and intelligent than you.
Genesis 41:40 You will be over my house, and all my people will obey at your mouth; only in the throne will I be above you.
Genesis 41:41 And Pharao said to Joseph: Behold, today I appoint you over all the land of Egypt.
Genesis 41:42 And Pharao removed the ring from his hand and put it upon the hand of Joseph, and clothed him in a linen robe and put a golden collar around his neck.
Genesis 41:43 And he mounted him upon his second chariot, and a herald proclaimed before him; and he appointed him over the whole land of Egypt.
Genesis 41:44 And Pharao said to Joseph: I am Pharao; without you no one will lift his hand in all the land of Egypt.
Genesis 41:45 And Pharao called the name of Joseph Psonthomphanech; and he gave him Asenneth, the daughter of Petephre, priest of the City of the Sun, as a woman for him.
Genesis 41:46 And Joseph was thirty years old when he stood before Pharao, king of Egypt. And Joseph went out from the face of Pharao and passed through all the land of Egypt.
Genesis 41:47 And in the seven years of abundance the land produced bundles.
Genesis 41:48 And he gathered all the foods of the seven years in which there was abundance in the land of Egypt and placed the foods in the cities; the foods of the fields around each city he placed in it.
Genesis 41:49 And Joseph gathered grain like the sand of the sea, exceedingly much, until they were not able to count it, for there was no number.
Genesis 41:50 And two sons were born to Joseph before the seven years of famine came, whom Asenneth the daughter of Petephre, priest of the City of the Sun, bore to him.
Genesis 41:51 And Joseph called the name of the firstborn Manasse, because: God made me forget all my pains and all the things of my father.
Genesis 41:52 And he called the name of the second Ephraim, because: God increased me in the land of my humiliation.
Genesis 41:53 And the seven years of abundance that came to be in the land of Egypt passed.
Genesis 41:54 And the seven years of famine began to come, just as Joseph said. And famine came to be in all the land, but in all the land of Egypt there were breads.
Genesis 41:55 And all the land of Egypt hungered, and the people cried to Pharao concerning breads; and Pharao said to all the Egyptians: Go to Joseph, and whatever he tells you, do.
Genesis 41:56 And the famine was upon the face of all the land; and Joseph opened all the granaries and sold to all the Egyptians.
Genesis 41:57 And all the regions came into Egypt to buy from Joseph, for the famine prevailed in all the land.

## Chapter 42

Genesis 42:1 And Jacob saw that there was a sale in Egypt and said to his sons: Why are you idle?
Genesis 42:2 Behold, I have heard that there is grain in Egypt; go down there and buy us a little food, so that we may live and not die.
Genesis 42:3 And the ten brothers of Joseph went down to buy grain from Egypt.
Genesis 42:4 But Benjamin, the brother of Joseph, he did not send with his brothers, for he said: Lest some weakness happen to him.
Genesis 42:5 And the sons of Israel came to buy with those who were coming, for the famine was in the land of Chanaan.
Genesis 42:6 And Joseph was ruler of the land; he was the one selling to all the people of the land. And the brothers of Joseph came and bowed down to him upon their faces upon the ground.
Genesis 42:7 And Joseph saw his brothers and recognized them, and he estranged himself from them and spoke harsh things to them and said to them: From where have you come? And they said: From the land of Chanaan, to buy food.
Genesis 42:8 And Joseph recognized his brothers, but they did not recognize him.
Genesis 42:9 And Joseph remembered the dreams that he himself had seen and said to them: You are spies; you have come to examine the tracks of the country.
Genesis 42:10 And they said: No, lord; your servants came to buy food.
Genesis 42:11 We are all sons of one man; we are peaceful; your servants are not spies.
Genesis 42:12 And he said to them: No, but you came to see the tracks of the land.
Genesis 42:13 And they said: We, your servants, are twelve brothers in the land of Chanaan, and behold, the youngest is with our father today, but the other does not exist.
Genesis 42:14 And Joseph said to them: This is what I have said to you, saying that you are spies.
Genesis 42:15 By this you will be made manifest: by the health of Pharao, you shall certainly not leave from here unless your youngest brother comes here.
Genesis 42:16 Send one from among you and take your brother, but you are to be led away until your words become manifest, whether you speak truth or not; but if not, by the health of Pharao, surely you are spies.
Genesis 42:17 And he placed them in custody for three days.
Genesis 42:18 And he said to them on the third day: Do this and you will live—for I fear God—
Genesis 42:19 if you are peaceful, let one of your brothers be held in custody, but you yourselves walk and carry away the purchase of your grain-ration,
Genesis 42:20 and bring your youngest brother to me, and your words will be believed; but if not, you will die. And they did so. –
Genesis 42:21 And each said to his brother: Yes, for we are in sin concerning our brother, because we overlooked the affliction of his soul when he pleaded with us, and we did not listen to him; on account of this, this affliction has come upon us.
Genesis 42:22 And Reuben answered and said to them: Did I not speak to you, saying: Do not wrong the boy? And you did not listen to me; and behold, his blood is sought.
Genesis 42:23 But they did not know that Joseph was hearing, for the interpreter was between them.
Genesis 42:24 And Joseph turned away from them and wept. – And again he came to them and spoke to them, and he took Symeon from them and bound him before them.
Genesis 42:25 And Joseph commanded that their vessels be filled with grain and that each one’s silver be returned into his sack and that provisions be given to them for the way. And thus it came to be for them.
Genesis 42:26 And placing the grain upon their donkeys, they went away from there. –
Genesis 42:27 And one loosened his purse to give fodder to his donkeys where they lodged, and he saw the bundle of his silver, and it was on top of the mouth of the purse.
Genesis 42:28 And he said to his brothers: My silver was returned to me, and behold, this is in my purse. And their heart was astonished, and they were troubled with one another, saying: What is this that God has done to us?
Genesis 42:29 And they came to Jacob their father in the land of Chanaan and reported to him everything that had happened to them, saying:
Genesis 42:30 The man, the lord of the land, has spoken harsh things to us and placed us in custody as men spying out the land.
Genesis 42:31 And we said to him: We are peaceful; we are not spies.
Genesis 42:32 We are twelve brothers, sons of our father; the one does not exist, but the youngest is with our father today in the land of Chanaan.
Genesis 42:33 And the man, the lord of the land, said to us: By this I will know that you are peaceful: leave one brother here with me, but take the purchase of the grain-ration of your house and go away,
Genesis 42:34 and bring your youngest brother to me, and I will know that you are not spies but are peaceful, and I will restore your brother to you, and trade in the land.
Genesis 42:35 And it happened while they were emptying their sacks that the bundle of each one’s silver was in their sack; and they and their father saw the bundles of their silver and were afraid.
Genesis 42:36 And Jacob their father said to them: You have made me childless; Joseph does not exist, Symeon does not exist, and you will take Benjamin. All these things have come upon me.
Genesis 42:37 And Reuben spoke to his father, saying: Kill my two sons if I do not bring him to you; give him into my hand, and I will bring him back to you.
Genesis 42:38 But he said: My son shall not go down with you, because his brother died and he alone has been left; and it will happen that he is afflicted by weakness on the way in which you journey, and you will bring my old age down with sorrow into Hades.

## Chapter 43

Genesis 43:1 And the famine grew strong upon the land.
Genesis 43:2 And it happened when they finished eating the grain that they had brought from Egypt that their father said to them: Go again and buy us a little food.
Genesis 43:3 And Judas spoke to him, saying: With a testimony the man testified to us, saying: You shall not see my face unless your youngest brother is with you.
Genesis 43:4 If therefore you send our brother with us, we will go down and buy food for you.
Genesis 43:5 But if you do not send our brother with us, we will not journey, for the man said to us: You shall not see my face unless your youngest brother is with you.
Genesis 43:6 And Israel said: Why did you harm me by reporting to the man whether you had a brother?
Genesis 43:7 And they said: Questioning, the man questioned us and our family, saying: Is your father still living? Do you have a brother? And we reported to him according to this questioning. Surely we did not know that he would say to us: Bring your brother.
Genesis 43:8 And Judas said to Israel his father: Send the boy with me, and arising, we shall journey, so that we may live and not die, both we and you and our baggage.
Genesis 43:9 And I receive responsibility for him; seek him from my hand. If I do not bring him to you and stand him before you, I will have sinned against you all the days.
Genesis 43:10 For if we had not delayed, we would already have returned twice.
Genesis 43:11 And Israel their father said to them: If it is so, do this: take some of the fruits of the land in your vessels and bring gifts down to the man—some resin and honey, incense and stacte and terebinth and nuts.
Genesis 43:12 And take double silver in your hands; return with you the silver that was returned in your purses, lest perhaps it was a mistake.
Genesis 43:13 And take your brother, and arise and go down to the man.
Genesis 43:14 And may my God give you grace before the man and send away your one brother and Benjamin; but as for me, just as I have been made childless, I have been made childless.
Genesis 43:15 And the men took these gifts and took the double silver in their hands and Benjamin, and arising, they went down into Egypt and stood before Joseph.
Genesis 43:16 And Joseph saw them and Benjamin his brother from the same mother and said to the one over his house: Bring the men into the house, and slaughter sacrifices and prepare, for the men will eat breads with me at midday.
Genesis 43:17 And the man did just as Joseph said and brought the men into the house of Joseph. –
Genesis 43:18 And when the men saw that they had been brought into the house of Joseph, they said: Because of the silver that was returned in our purses at the beginning, we are being brought in, to accuse us falsely and attack us, to take us as servants, and our donkeys.
Genesis 43:19 And approaching the man who was over the house of Joseph, they spoke to him in the gateway of the house,
Genesis 43:20 saying: We beseech you, lord; we came down at the beginning to buy food.
Genesis 43:21 And it happened when we came to lodge and opened our purses that here was the silver of each one in his purse; and our silver by weight we have now returned in our hands.
Genesis 43:22 And we brought other silver with ourselves to buy food; we do not know who put the silver into our purses.
Genesis 43:23 And he said to them: Mercy be to you; do not fear. Your God and the God of your fathers gave you treasures in your purses, but I have received your silver as approved payment. And he brought Symeon out to them,
Genesis 43:24 and he brought water to wash their feet and gave fodder to their donkeys.
Genesis 43:25 And they prepared the gifts until Joseph came at midday, for they heard that he was going to eat lunch there.
Genesis 43:26 And Joseph entered the house, and they brought him the gifts that they had in their hands into the house and bowed down to him upon their faces upon the ground.
Genesis 43:27 And he questioned them: How are you? And he said to them: Is your elderly father, whom you mentioned, healthy? Is he still living?
Genesis 43:28 And they said: Your servant our father is healthy; he is still living. And he said: Blessed is that man by God. And bending down, they bowed down to him.
Genesis 43:29 And Joseph looked up with his eyes and saw Benjamin his brother from the same mother and said: Is this your youngest brother, whom you said you would bring to me? And he said: May God have mercy on you, child.
Genesis 43:30 And Joseph was troubled—for his inward parts were twisting over his brother—and he sought to weep; and entering the private chamber, he wept there.
Genesis 43:31 And washing his face, he came out and restrained himself and said: Set out breads.
Genesis 43:32 And they set out for him alone, and for them by themselves, and for the Egyptians dining with him by themselves; for the Egyptians were not able to eat breads together with the Hebrews, for it is an abomination to the Egyptians.
Genesis 43:33 And they sat before him, the firstborn according to his seniority and the youngest according to his youth; and the men were astonished, each toward his brother.
Genesis 43:34 And they lifted portions from him toward themselves; but the portion of Benjamin was made greater than the portions of all, fivefold compared with theirs. And they drank and became drunk with him.

## Chapter 44

Genesis 44:1 And Joseph commanded the one who was over his house, saying: Fill the purses of the men with as much food as they are able to carry, and put each one’s silver at the mouth of his purse,
Genesis 44:2 and put my silver cup into the purse of the youngest, along with the price of his grain. And it happened according to the word of Joseph, just as he said. –
Genesis 44:3 The morning dawned, and the men were sent away, they and their donkeys.
Genesis 44:4 And when they had gone out of the city [they were not far away], Joseph said to the one over his house: Arise, pursue after the men and overtake them, and say to them: Why is it that you repaid evil in place of good?
Genesis 44:5 Why did you steal my silver cup? Is this not that in which my lord drinks? And by divination he practices divination in it. You have brought to completion evil things that you have done.
Genesis 44:6 And finding them, he spoke to them according to these words.
Genesis 44:7 And they said to him: Why does the lord speak according to these words? May it not happen that your servants do according to this word.
Genesis 44:8 If we returned to you from the land of Chanaan the silver that we found in our purses, how could we steal silver or gold from the house of your lord?
Genesis 44:9 With whomever among your servants the cup is found, let him die; and we also will be servants to our lord.
Genesis 44:10 And he said: Even now, as you say, so it will be; the man with whom the cup is found, he will be my servant, but you will be clean.
Genesis 44:11 And they hastened, and each brought his purse down upon the ground, and each opened his purse.
Genesis 44:12 And he searched, beginning from the eldest until he came to the youngest, and he found the cup in the purse of Benjamin.
Genesis 44:13 And they tore their garments, and each placed his purse upon his donkey, and they returned to the city.
Genesis 44:14 And Judas and his brothers entered to Joseph while he was still there, and they fell before him upon the ground.
Genesis 44:15 And Joseph said to them: What is this deed that you have done? Do you not know that by divination a man such as I practices divination?
Genesis 44:16 And Judas said: What shall we answer our lord, or what shall we speak, or how shall we be justified? But God has found the unrighteousness of your servants. Behold, we are household servants to our lord, both we and he with whom the cup was found.
Genesis 44:17 And Joseph said: May it not happen to me to do this thing; the man with whom the cup was found, he will be my servant, but you go up with salvation to your father.
Genesis 44:18 And Judas drew near to him and said: I beseech you, lord, let your servant speak a word before you, and do not be angry with your servant, because you are with Pharao.
Genesis 44:19 Lord, you questioned your servants, saying: Do you have a father or a brother?
Genesis 44:20 And we said to the lord: We have an elderly father and a younger child of old age for him, and his brother died, and he alone was left to his mother, and his father loved him.
Genesis 44:21 And you said to your servants: Bring him down to me, and I will care for him.
Genesis 44:22 And we said to the lord: The child will not be able to leave his father; but if he leaves his father, he will die.
Genesis 44:23 But you said to your servants: Unless your youngest brother comes down with you, you shall not add again to see my face.
Genesis 44:24 And it happened when we went up to your servant, namely our father, that we reported the words of the lord to him.
Genesis 44:25 And our father said to us: Walk again; buy us a little food.
Genesis 44:26 But we said: We will not be able to go down; but if our youngest brother goes down with us, we will go down, for we will not be able to see the face of the man if our youngest brother is not with us.
Genesis 44:27 And your servant our father said to us: You know that my woman bore me two.
Genesis 44:28 And the one went out from me, and you said that he had become beast-eaten, and I have not seen him still even now.
Genesis 44:29 If therefore you take this one also from my face and some weakness happens to him on the way, then you will bring my old age down with sorrow into Hades.
Genesis 44:30 Now therefore, if I enter to your servant, namely our father, and the boy is not with us—his soul hangs from this one’s soul—
Genesis 44:31 then it will happen when he sees that the boy is not with us that he will die, and your servants will bring the old age of your servant, namely our father, down with pain into Hades.
Genesis 44:32 For your servant has received responsibility for the boy from the father, saying: If I do not bring him to you and stand him before you, I will have sinned against the father all the days.
Genesis 44:33 Now therefore, I will remain beside you as a servant in place of the boy, a household servant of the lord; but let the boy go up with his brothers.
Genesis 44:34 For how shall I go up to the father when the boy is not with us? Let me not see the evils that will find my father.

## Chapter 45

Genesis 45:1 And Joseph was not able to endure all those standing beside him, but said: Send everyone away from me. And no one was still standing beside Joseph when he made himself known to his brothers.
Genesis 45:2 And he let out his voice with weeping; and all the Egyptians heard, and it became audible in the house of Pharao.
Genesis 45:3 And Joseph said to his brothers: I am Joseph. Is my father still living? And his brothers were not able to answer him, for they were troubled.
Genesis 45:4 And Joseph said to his brothers: Draw near to me. And they drew near. And he said: I am Joseph your brother, whom you sold into Egypt.
Genesis 45:5 Now therefore, do not be grieved, nor let it appear hard to you that you sold me here, for God sent me before you for life.
Genesis 45:6 For this is the second year that famine is upon the land, and there are still five years remaining in which there will be neither plowing nor harvest.
Genesis 45:7 For God sent me before you so that a remnant of you might be left upon the earth and to nourish a great remnant of you.
Genesis 45:8 Now therefore, you did not send me here, but rather God; and he made me as a father to Pharao and lord of all his house and ruler of all the land of Egypt.
Genesis 45:9 Therefore hasten and go up to my father and say to him: Thus says your son Joseph: God made me lord of all the land of Egypt; therefore come down to me and do not remain.
Genesis 45:10 And you will dwell in the land of Gesem of Arabia and will be near me, you and your sons and the sons of your sons, your sheep and your cattle and whatever is yours.
Genesis 45:11 And I will nourish you there—for there are still five years of famine—so that you are not wiped out, you and your sons and all your possessions.
Genesis 45:12 Behold, your eyes see, and the eyes of Benjamin my brother, that it is my mouth speaking to you.
Genesis 45:13 Therefore report to my father all my glory that is in Egypt and everything that you saw, and hasten and bring my father down here.
Genesis 45:14 And falling upon the neck of Benjamin his brother, he wept over him, and Benjamin wept upon his neck.
Genesis 45:15 And kissing all his brothers, he wept over them; and after these things his brothers spoke to him.
Genesis 45:16 And the report was spread into the house of Pharao, saying: The brothers of Joseph have come. And Pharao and his attendants rejoiced.
Genesis 45:17 And Pharao said to Joseph: Say to your brothers: Do this: load your conveyances and go away into the land of Chanaan,
Genesis 45:18 and take your father and your possessions and come to me, and I will give you some of all the good things of Egypt, and you will eat the marrow of the land.
Genesis 45:19 And you, command these things: that they take wagons from the land of Egypt for your children and your women, and take up your father and come.
Genesis 45:20 And do not spare your goods with your eyes, for all the good things of Egypt will be yours.
Genesis 45:21 And the sons of Israel did so; and Joseph gave them wagons according to the things spoken by Pharao the king and gave them provisions for the way.
Genesis 45:22 And he gave double robes to all, but to Benjamin he gave three hundred gold pieces and five changes of robes.
Genesis 45:23 And to his father he sent the same, and ten donkeys carrying some of all the good things of Egypt and ten she-mules carrying breads for his father for the way.
Genesis 45:24 And he sent his brothers away, and they journeyed; and he said to them: Do not be angry on the way.
Genesis 45:25 And they went up from Egypt and came into the land of Chanaan to Jacob their father,
Genesis 45:26 and they reported to him, saying: Your son Joseph is living, and he rules all the land of Egypt. And the mind of Jacob was beside itself, for he did not believe them.
Genesis 45:27 And they spoke to him all the things spoken by Joseph, as many as he had said to them. And when he saw the wagons that Joseph had sent to take him up, the spirit of Jacob their father was rekindled.
Genesis 45:28 And Israel said: It is great to me if Joseph my son is still living; I will journey and see him before I die.

## Chapter 46

Genesis 46:1 And Israel departed, he and all that was his, and came to the Well of the Oath and sacrificed a sacrifice to the God of his father Isaac.
Genesis 46:2 And God spoke to Israel in a vision of the night, having said: Jacob, Jacob. And he said: What is it?
Genesis 46:3 saying: I am the God of your fathers; do not be afraid to go down into Egypt, for there I will make you into a great nation.
Genesis 46:4 And I will go down with you into Egypt, and I will bring you up to the end, and Joseph will lay his hands upon your eyes.
Genesis 46:5 And Jacob arose from the Well of the Oath, and the sons of Israel took up their father and their baggage and their women upon the wagons that Joseph had sent to carry him.
Genesis 46:6 And taking up their possessions and all the property that they had acquired in the land of Chanaan, they entered into Egypt, Jacob and all his seed with him,
Genesis 46:7 sons and the sons of his sons with him, daughters and the daughters of his sons; and he brought all his seed into Egypt.
Genesis 46:8 And these are the names of the sons of Israel who entered into Egypt, Jacob and his sons: the firstborn of Jacob, Reuben.
Genesis 46:9 And the sons of Reuben: Enoch and Phallous, Asron and Charmi.
Genesis 46:10 And the sons of Symeon: Jemouel and Jamin and Aod and Jachin and Saar and Saul, the son of the Chanaanite woman.
Genesis 46:11 And the sons of Levi: Gerson, Kaath, and Merari.
Genesis 46:12 And the sons of Judas: Er and Aunan and Selom and Phares and Zara; and Er and Aunan died in the land of Chanaan. And the sons of Phares were Asron and Jemouel.
Genesis 46:13 And the sons of Issachar: Thola and Phoua and Jasoub and Zambram.
Genesis 46:14 And the sons of Zabulon: Sered and Allon and Aloel.
Genesis 46:15 These are the sons of Leia whom she bore to Jacob in Mesopotamia of Syria, and Dina his daughter; all the souls, sons and daughters, were thirty-three. –
Genesis 46:16 And the sons of Gad: Saphon and Aggis and Saunis and Thasoban and Aedis and Aroedis and Aroelis.
Genesis 46:17 And the sons of Aser: Jemna and Jesoua and Jeoul and Baria, and Sara their sister. And the sons of Baria: Chobor and Melchiel.
Genesis 46:18 These are the sons of Zelpha, whom Laban gave to Leia his daughter, who bore these to Jacob, sixteen souls. –
Genesis 46:19 And the sons of Rachel, the woman of Jacob: Joseph and Benjamin.
Genesis 46:20 And sons were born to Joseph in the land of Egypt, whom Asenneth the daughter of Petephre, priest of the City of the Sun, bore to him: Manasse and Ephraim. And sons were born to Manasse, whom his Syrian concubine bore to him: Machir; and Machir begot Galaad. And the sons of Ephraim, the brother of Manasse: Soutalaam and Taam. And the sons of Soutalaam: Edem.
Genesis 46:21 And the sons of Benjamin: Bala and Chobor and Asbel. And the sons of Bala were Gera and Noeman and Anchis and Ros and Mamphin and Ophimin; and Gera begot Arad.
Genesis 46:22 These are the sons of Rachel whom she bore to Jacob; all the souls were eighteen. –
Genesis 46:23 And the sons of Dan: Asom.
Genesis 46:24 And the sons of Nephthali: Asiel and Goyni and Issaar and Syllem.
Genesis 46:25 These are the sons of Balla, whom Laban gave to Rachel his daughter, who bore these to Jacob; all the souls were seven. –
Genesis 46:26 And all the souls who entered with Jacob into Egypt, those who came out from his thighs, apart from the women of the sons of Jacob—all the souls were sixty-six.
Genesis 46:27 And the sons of Joseph who were born to him in the land of Egypt were nine souls. All the souls of the house of Jacob who entered into Egypt were seventy-five.
Genesis 46:28 And he sent Judas before him to Joseph to meet him by the City of Heroes, into the land of Ramesses.
Genesis 46:29 And Joseph yoked his chariots and went up to meet Israel his father by the City of Heroes, and when he appeared to him, he fell upon his neck and wept with greater weeping.
Genesis 46:30 And Israel said to Joseph: I will die from now on, since I have seen your face, for you are still living.
Genesis 46:31 And Joseph said to his brothers: I will go up and report to Pharao and say to him: My brothers and the house of my father, who were in the land of Chanaan, have come to me.
Genesis 46:32 And the men are shepherds—for they were men who raise livestock—and they have brought the livestock and the cattle and all that is theirs.
Genesis 46:33 Therefore, if Pharao calls you and says to you: What is your occupation?
Genesis 46:34 then you shall say: We your servants are men who raise livestock, from childhood until now, both we and our fathers, so that you may dwell in the land of Gesem in Arabia; for every shepherd of sheep is an abomination to the Egyptians.

## Chapter 47

Genesis 47:1 And Joseph came and reported to Pharao, saying: My father and my brothers and their livestock and cattle and all that is theirs have come from the land of Chanaan, and behold, they are in the land of Gesem.
Genesis 47:2 And he took five men from among his brothers and stood them before Pharao.
Genesis 47:3 And Pharao said to the brothers of Joseph: What is your occupation? And they said to Pharao: Your servants are shepherds of sheep, both we and our fathers.
Genesis 47:4 And they said to Pharao: We have come to sojourn in the land, for there is no pasture for the livestock of your servants, for the famine has grown strong in the land of Chanaan; now therefore, we your servants will dwell in the land of Gesem.
Genesis 47:5 And Pharao said to Joseph: Let them dwell in the land of Gesem; and if you know that there are capable men among them, appoint them rulers of my livestock. And Jacob and his sons came into Egypt to Joseph, and Pharao king of Egypt heard. And Pharao spoke to Joseph, saying: Your father and your brothers have come to you.
Genesis 47:6 Behold, the land of Egypt is before you; settle your father and your brothers in the best land.
Genesis 47:7 And Joseph brought in Jacob his father and stood him before Pharao, and Jacob blessed Pharao.
Genesis 47:8 And Pharao said to Jacob: How many are the years of the days of your life?
Genesis 47:9 And Jacob said to Pharao: The days of the years of my life in which I sojourn are a hundred thirty years. Few and evil have been the days of the years of my life; they have not reached the days of the years of the life of my fathers, the days in which they sojourned.
Genesis 47:10 And Jacob blessed Pharao and went out from him.
Genesis 47:11 And Joseph settled his father and his brothers and gave them a holding in the land of Egypt, in the best land, in the land of Ramesses, just as Pharao commanded.
Genesis 47:12 And Joseph measured grain to his father and his brothers and all the house of his father, grain according to each body.
Genesis 47:13 And there was no grain in all the land, for the famine grew exceedingly strong; and the land of Egypt and the land of Chanaan failed because of the famine.
Genesis 47:14 And Joseph gathered all the silver found in the land of Egypt and in the land of Chanaan for the grain that they were buying and that he was measuring to them, and Joseph brought all the silver into the house of Pharao.
Genesis 47:15 And all the silver from the land of Egypt and from the land of Chanaan failed. And all the Egyptians came to Joseph, saying: Give us breads, and why should we die before you? For our silver has failed.
Genesis 47:16 And Joseph said to them: Bring your livestock, and I will give you breads in exchange for your livestock, if the silver has failed.
Genesis 47:17 And they brought the livestock to Joseph, and Joseph gave them breads in exchange for the horses and in exchange for the sheep and in exchange for the cattle and in exchange for the donkeys, and he nourished them with breads in exchange for all their livestock in that year. –
Genesis 47:18 And that year went out, and they came to him in the second year and said to him: Lest we be destroyed from our lord; for if the silver and the possessions and the livestock have failed to you the lord, then nothing is left for us before our lord except our own body and our land.
Genesis 47:19 Therefore, so that we do not die before you and the land is made desolate, acquire us and our land in exchange for breads, and we and our land will be servants of Pharao. Give seed so that we may sow and live and not die, and the land will not be made desolate.
Genesis 47:20 And Joseph acquired all the land of the Egyptians for Pharao, for the Egyptians sold their land to Pharao because the famine prevailed over them; and the land became Pharao’s.
Genesis 47:21 And he enslaved the people to him as servants, from the extremities of the boundaries of Egypt as far as the extremities,
Genesis 47:22 apart from the land of the priests alone; Joseph did not acquire this, for Pharao gave a gift to the priests as an allowance, and they ate the allowance that Pharao gave them; because of this, they did not sell their land.
Genesis 47:23 And Joseph said to all the Egyptians: Behold, today I have acquired you and your land for Pharao; take seed for yourselves and sow the land.
Genesis 47:24 And it shall be that of its produce you will give the fifth part to Pharao, but the four parts will be for you yourselves, for seed for the land and for food for you and all those in your houses.
Genesis 47:25 And they said: You have saved us; we have found grace before our lord, and we will be servants of Pharao.
Genesis 47:26 And Joseph set it for them as an ordinance until this day over the land of Egypt, to give a fifth to Pharao, apart from the land of the priests alone; it was not Pharao’s.
Genesis 47:27 And Israel dwelt in the land of Egypt upon the land of Gesem, and they inherited upon it and increased and multiplied exceedingly. –
Genesis 47:28 And Jacob lived on in the land of Egypt for seventeen years; and the days of Jacob, the years of his life, were a hundred forty-seven years.
Genesis 47:29 And the days of Israel drew near for him to die, and he called his son Joseph and said to him: If I have found grace before you, put your hand under my thigh and do mercy and truth with me, that you not bury me in Egypt.
Genesis 47:30 But I will sleep with my fathers, and you will carry me from Egypt and bury me in their tomb. And he said: I will do according to your word.
Genesis 47:31 And he said: Swear to me. And he swore to him. And Israel bowed down upon the tip of his staff.

## Chapter 48

Genesis 48:1 And it happened after these words that it was reported to Joseph: Your father is ill. And taking his two sons, Manasse and Ephraim, he came to Jacob.
Genesis 48:2 And it was reported to Jacob, saying: Behold, your son Joseph is coming to you. And Israel strengthened himself and sat upon the bed.
Genesis 48:3 And Jacob said to Joseph: My God appeared to me in Louza in the land of Chanaan and blessed me,
Genesis 48:4 and said to me: Behold, I will increase you and multiply you and make you into congregations of nations, and I will give this land to you and to your seed after you as an eternal holding.
Genesis 48:5 Now therefore, your two sons who were born to you in Egypt before I came to you in Egypt are mine; Ephraim and Manasse will be mine as Reuben and Symeon.
Genesis 48:6 But the offspring whom you beget after these will be yours; they will be called upon the name of their brothers in their inheritances.
Genesis 48:7 And as for me, when I was coming from Mesopotamia of Syria, Rachel your mother died in the land of Chanaan as I was drawing near, by the hippodrome, Chabratha of the land, on the way to Ephratha; and I buried her on the road of the hippodrome [this is Bethlehem]. –
Genesis 48:8 And Israel saw the sons of Joseph and said: Who are these to you?
Genesis 48:9 And Joseph said to his father: They are my sons, whom God gave me here. And Jacob said: Bring them near to me, so that I may bless them.
Genesis 48:10 And the eyes of Israel had grown heavy from old age, and he was not able to see; and he brought them near to him, and he kissed them and embraced them.
Genesis 48:11 And Israel said to Joseph: Behold, I was not deprived of your face, and behold, God showed me also your seed.
Genesis 48:12 And Joseph brought them out from his knees, and they bowed down to him upon their faces upon the ground.
Genesis 48:13 And Joseph took his two sons, Ephraim in his right hand, to the left of Israel, and Manasse in his left hand, to the right of Israel, and brought them near to him.
Genesis 48:14 And Israel stretched out his right hand and laid it upon the head of Ephraim—but he was the younger—and his left hand upon the head of Manasse, crossing his hands.
Genesis 48:15 And he blessed them and said: The God before whom my fathers Abraham and Isaac were pleasing, the God who nourishes me from youth until this day,
Genesis 48:16 the angel who delivers me from all evils, may he bless these children; and my name and the name of my fathers Abraham and Isaac shall be called upon them, and may they be multiplied into a great multitude upon the earth.
Genesis 48:17 And Joseph saw that his father had laid his right hand upon the head of Ephraim, and it appeared grievous to him; and Joseph took hold of his father’s hand to remove it from the head of Ephraim to the head of Manasse.
Genesis 48:18 And Joseph said to his father: Not so, father, for this one is the firstborn; place your right hand upon his head.
Genesis 48:19 And he did not wish to, but said: I know, child, I know. This one also will become a people, and this one also will be exalted, but his younger brother will be greater than he, and his seed will become a multitude of nations.
Genesis 48:20 And he blessed them on that day, saying: In you Israel will be blessed, with people saying: May God make you as Ephraim and as Manasse. And he placed Ephraim before Manasse. –
Genesis 48:21 And Israel said to Joseph: Behold, I am dying, and God will be with you and return you to the land of your fathers.
Genesis 48:22 And I give you Sikima as an exceptional portion beyond your brothers, which I took from the hand of the Amorrites with my sword and bow.

## Chapter 49

Genesis 49:1 And Jacob called his sons and said: Gather together, so that I may report to you what will meet you at the last of the days.
Genesis 49:2 Assemble and hear, sons of Jacob; hear Israel your father.
Genesis 49:3 Reuben, you are my firstborn, my strength and the beginning of my children, hard to endure and hard, self-willed.
Genesis 49:4 You acted outrageously like water; do not boil over. For you went up upon the bed of your father; then you defiled the bedding where you went up.
Genesis 49:5 Symeon and Levi are brothers; they brought unrighteousness to completion by their choice.
Genesis 49:6 May my soul not come into their counsel, and may my liver not rest upon their conspiracy, because in their anger they killed men, and in their desire they hamstrung a bull.
Genesis 49:7 Accursed is their anger, because it is self-willed, and their wrath, because it was hardened. I will divide them in Jacob and scatter them in Israel.
Genesis 49:8 Judas, may your brothers praise you; your hands are upon the back of your enemies; the sons of your father will bow down to you.
Genesis 49:9 Judas is a lion’s whelp; from a shoot, my son, you went up. Reclining, you slept like a lion and like a whelp; who will awaken him?
Genesis 49:10 A ruler will not fail from Judas, nor a leader from his thighs, until the things laid up for him come, and he is the expectation of nations.
Genesis 49:11 He binds his colt to a vine and the foal of his donkey to the tendril; he will wash his robe in wine and his wrapping in the blood of a grape.
Genesis 49:12 His eyes are gladdened from wine, and his teeth are whiter than milk.
Genesis 49:13 Zabulon will dwell by the sea, and he will be by a harbor of ships, and he will extend as far as Sidon.
Genesis 49:14 Issachar desired the good, resting between the inheritances.
Genesis 49:15 And seeing that the rest was good and that the land was rich, he put his shoulder to labor and became a man who works the land.
Genesis 49:16 Dan will judge his own people, as also one tribe in Israel.
Genesis 49:17 And let Dan become a serpent upon the road, sitting in ambush upon the path, biting the heel of a horse, and the rider will fall backward.
Genesis 49:18 I await the salvation of the Lord.
Genesis 49:19 Gad—a raiding party will raid him, but he will raid them at their heels.
Genesis 49:20 Aser—his bread is rich, and he will give delicacy to rulers.
Genesis 49:21 Nephthali is a loosened stem, bestowing beauty in the produce.
Genesis 49:22 A son increased is Joseph, a son increased, envied, my youngest son; return to me.
Genesis 49:23 Against him those taking counsel reviled, and masters of arrows held hostility toward him.
Genesis 49:24 And their bows were crushed with power, and the sinews of the arms of their hands were loosened through the hand of the mighty one of Jacob; from there is the one who strengthened Israel.
Genesis 49:25 From the God of your father; and my God helped you and blessed you with a blessing of heaven above and a blessing of the earth possessing all things, for the sake of the blessing of breasts and womb,
Genesis 49:26 the blessing of your father and your mother. It prevailed over the blessings of the permanent mountains and over the blessings of the ever-flowing dunes; they will be upon the head of Joseph and upon the crown of the brothers whom he led.
Genesis 49:27 Benjamin is a ravenous wolf; in the morning he will still eat, and by evening he will distribute food.
Genesis 49:28 All these are the twelve sons of Jacob, and these things their father spoke to them and blessed them; each according to his blessing he blessed them.
Genesis 49:29 And he said to them: I am being added to my people; bury me with my fathers in the cave that is in the field of Ephron the Chettite,
Genesis 49:30 in the double cave opposite Mambre in the land of Chanaan, the cave that Abraham acquired from Ephron the Chettite as a possession for a memorial.
Genesis 49:31 There they buried Abraham and Sarra his woman; there they buried Isaac and Rebekka his woman; and there I buried Leia,
Genesis 49:32 in the possession of the field and the cave that is in it, from the sons of Chet.
Genesis 49:33 And Jacob ceased commanding his sons, and lifting his feet onto the bed, he expired and was added to his people.

## Chapter 50

Genesis 50:1 And Joseph fell upon the face of his father and wept over him and kissed him.
Genesis 50:2 And Joseph commanded his servants, the embalmers, to embalm his father, and the embalmers embalmed Israel.
Genesis 50:3 And they completed forty days for him, for thus the days of burial are counted; and Egypt mourned him for seventy days.
Genesis 50:4 And when the days of mourning had passed, Joseph spoke to the mighty men of Pharao, saying: If I have found grace before you, speak about me in the ears of Pharao, saying:
Genesis 50:5 My father made me swear, saying: In the memorial that I dug for myself in the land of Chanaan, there you shall bury me. Now therefore, I will go up and bury my father and return.
Genesis 50:6 And Pharao said: Go up; bury your father, just as he made you swear.
Genesis 50:7 And Joseph went up to bury his father, and all the servants of Pharao and the elders of his house and all the elders of the land of Egypt went up with him,
Genesis 50:8 and all the household of Joseph and his brothers and all his paternal house; but they left the kindred and the sheep and the cattle behind in the land of Gesem.
Genesis 50:9 And chariots and horsemen also went up with him, and the encampment became exceedingly great.
Genesis 50:10 And they arrived at the threshing floor of Atad, which is beyond the Jordan, and they mourned him with a great and exceedingly strong mourning; and he made mourning for his father for seven days.
Genesis 50:11 And the inhabitants of the land of Chanaan saw the mourning at the threshing floor of Atad and said: This is a great mourning for the Egyptians. Because of this he called its name Mourning of Egypt, which is beyond the Jordan.
Genesis 50:12 And his sons did so for him and buried him there.
Genesis 50:13 And his sons took him up into the land of Chanaan and buried him in the double cave, the cave that Abraham acquired from Ephron the Chettite opposite Mambre as a possession for a memorial.
Genesis 50:14 And Joseph returned to Egypt, he and his brothers and those who had gone up with him to bury his father.
Genesis 50:15 And when the brothers of Joseph saw that their father had died, they said: Perhaps Joseph may bear a grudge against us and repay us as repayment all the evils that we displayed to him.
Genesis 50:16 And they came to Joseph, saying: Your father made us swear before he died, saying:
Genesis 50:17 Thus say to Joseph: Forgive them their unrighteousness and their sin, because they displayed evil things to you; and now accept the unrighteousness of the attendants of the God of your father. And Joseph wept while they were speaking to him.
Genesis 50:18 And coming to him, they said: Here we are, your household servants.
Genesis 50:19 And Joseph said to them: Do not fear, for I am God’s.
Genesis 50:20 You planned against me for evil things, but God planned concerning me for good things, so that it might become as today, that many people might be nourished.
Genesis 50:21 And he said to them: Do not fear; I will nourish you and your households. And he comforted them and spoke into their heart.
Genesis 50:22 And Joseph dwelt in Egypt, he and his brothers and all the household of his father. And Joseph lived a hundred ten years.
Genesis 50:23 And Joseph saw children of Ephraim as far as the third generation, and sons of Machir the son of Manasse were born upon the thighs of Joseph.
Genesis 50:24 And Joseph spoke to his brothers, saying: I am dying; but with a visitation God will visit you and bring you up from this land into the land that God swore to our fathers Abraham and Isaac and Jacob.
Genesis 50:25 And Joseph made the sons of Israel swear, saying: In the visitation with which God visits you, you shall also carry my bones up from here with you.
Genesis 50:26 And Joseph died, a hundred ten years old; and they buried him and placed him in the coffin in Egypt.

# Exodus

The Apostolic Bible. Public domain. https://apostolic-bible.ysys9.chatgpt.site/license.html


## Chapter 1

Exodus 1:1 These are the names of the sons of Israel who had entered into Egypt together with Jacob their father—each entered with his whole household—
Exodus 1:2 Reuben, Symeon, Levi, Judas,
Exodus 1:3 Issachar, Zabulon, and Benjamin,
Exodus 1:4 Dan and Nephthali, Gad and Aser.
Exodus 1:5 And Joseph was in Egypt. And all the souls from Jacob were seventy-five.
Exodus 1:6 And Joseph died, and all his brothers and all that generation.
Exodus 1:7 But the sons of Israel increased and multiplied and became abundant and grew exceedingly, exceedingly strong, and the land multiplied them.
Exodus 1:8 And another king arose over Egypt who did not know Joseph.
Exodus 1:9 And he said to his nation: Behold, the race of the sons of Israel is a great multitude and is stronger than we.
Exodus 1:10 Come therefore, let us act craftily toward them, lest they multiply and, whenever war happens to us, these also be added to the adversaries, and having made war against us, they depart from the land.
Exodus 1:11 And he set overseers of the works over them so that they might afflict them in the works; and they built fortified cities for Pharao: Pithom and Ramesses and On, which is the City of the Sun.
Exodus 1:12 But according as they humbled them, by so much they became more numerous and grew exceedingly, exceedingly strong; and the Egyptians abhorred the sons of Israel.
Exodus 1:13 And the Egyptians oppressed the sons of Israel by force
Exodus 1:14 and pained their life with hard works, with clay and brickmaking and all the works in the plains, according to all the works with which they enslaved them by force.
Exodus 1:15 And the king of the Egyptians spoke to the midwives of the Hebrews, to the one of them whose name was Sepphora, and the name of the second was Phoua,
Exodus 1:16 and he said: When you serve as midwives to the Hebrew women and they are about to give birth, if it is male, kill it, but if female, preserve it alive.
Exodus 1:17 But the midwives feared God and did not do according as the king of Egypt commanded them, and they kept the males alive.
Exodus 1:18 And the king of Egypt called the midwives and said to them: Why is it that you did this deed and keep the males alive?
Exodus 1:19 And the midwives said to Pharao: The Hebrew women are not like the women of Egypt, for they give birth before the midwives enter to them; and they were giving birth.
Exodus 1:20 And God did well to the midwives, and the people multiplied and grew strong exceedingly.
Exodus 1:21 Since the midwives feared God, they made houses for themselves. –
Exodus 1:22 And Pharao commanded all his people, saying: Every male that is born to the Hebrews, throw into the river; and every female, keep it alive.

## Chapter 2

Exodus 2:1 And there was someone from the tribe of Levi who took one of the daughters of Levi and had her.
Exodus 2:2 And she conceived and bore a male; and seeing that it was handsome, they sheltered it for three months.
Exodus 2:3 But when they were no longer able to hide it, his mother took a basket for him and coated it with asphalt-pitch and put the child into it and placed it in the marsh beside the river.
Exodus 2:4 And his sister was watching from far away to learn what would happen to him.
Exodus 2:5 And the daughter of Pharao came down to bathe at the river, and her maidens were walking beside the river; and seeing the basket in the marsh, she sent the maiden and took it up.
Exodus 2:6 And opening it, she sees a child crying in the basket, and the daughter of Pharao spared him and said: This is one of the children of the Hebrews.
Exodus 2:7 And his sister said to the daughter of Pharao: Do you want me to call for you a nursing woman from the Hebrews, and she will nurse the child for you?
Exodus 2:8 And the daughter of Pharao said to her: Go. And the young woman went and called the mother of the child.
Exodus 2:9 And the daughter of Pharao said to her: Keep this child for me and nurse it for me, and I will give you the wage. And the woman took the child and nursed it.
Exodus 2:10 And when the child had grown, she brought him to the daughter of Pharao, and he became a son to her; and she named his name Moses, saying: I took him up out of the water.
Exodus 2:11 And it happened in those many days, when Moses had become grown, that he went out to his brothers, the sons of Israel. And observing their labor, he sees an Egyptian man beating a certain Hebrew, one of his own brothers, the sons of Israel.
Exodus 2:12 And looking around here and there, he sees no one, and striking the Egyptian, he hid him in the sand.
Exodus 2:13 And going out on the second day, he sees two Hebrew men fighting and says to the one doing wrong: Why do you strike your neighbor?
Exodus 2:14 And he said: Who appointed you ruler and judge over us? Do you wish to kill me in the manner that you killed the Egyptian yesterday? And Moses was afraid and said: Has this matter thus become manifest?
Exodus 2:15 And Pharao heard this matter and sought to kill Moses; but Moses withdrew from the face of Pharao and dwelt in the land of Madiam. And coming into the land of Madiam, he sat upon the well.
Exodus 2:16 And the priest of Madiam had seven daughters who were shepherding the sheep of Jothor their father; and coming, they were drawing water until they filled the troughs to give the sheep of Jothor their father a drink.
Exodus 2:17 And the shepherds came and drove them away; but Moses arose and rescued them and drew water for them and gave their sheep a drink.
Exodus 2:18 And they came to Ragouel their father; and he said to them: Why is it that you hastened to come today?
Exodus 2:19 And they said: An Egyptian man rescued us from the shepherds and drew water for us and gave our sheep a drink.
Exodus 2:20 And he said to his daughters: And where is he? And why have you thus left the man behind? Therefore call him, so that he may eat bread.
Exodus 2:21 And Moses was settled beside the man, and he gave out Sepphora his daughter to Moses as a woman.
Exodus 2:22 And the woman conceived and bore a son, and Moses named his name Gersam, saying: I am a sojourner in a foreign land.
Exodus 2:23 And after those many days the king of Egypt died. And the sons of Israel groaned because of the works and cried out, and their cry went up to God because of the works.
Exodus 2:24 And God listened to their groaning, and God remembered his covenant with Abraham and Isaac and Jacob.
Exodus 2:25 And God looked upon the sons of Israel and became known to them.

## Chapter 3

Exodus 3:1 And Moses was shepherding the sheep of Jothor his father-in-law, the priest of Madiam, and he led the sheep beneath the wilderness and came to Mount Choreb.
Exodus 3:2 And an angel of the Lord appeared to him in a flame of fire from the bush, and he sees that the bush burns with fire, but the bush was not burned up.
Exodus 3:3 And Moses said: Passing by, I will see this great vision, why the bush is not burned up.
Exodus 3:4 And when the Lord saw that he was drawing near to see, the Lord called him from the bush, saying: Moses, Moses. And he said: What is it?
Exodus 3:5 And he said: Do not draw near here; loosen the sandal from your feet, for the place in which you stand is holy ground.
Exodus 3:6 And he said to him: I am the God of your father, the God of Abraham and the God of Isaac and the God of Jacob. And Moses turned his face away, for he was reverent about looking directly before God.
Exodus 3:7 And the Lord said to Moses: Seeing, I saw the affliction of my people who are in Egypt, and I have heard their cry because of the taskmasters, for I know their pain.
Exodus 3:8 And I came down to rescue them from the hand of the Egyptians and to bring them out of that land and bring them into a good and large land, into a land flowing with milk and honey, into the place of the Chanaanites and Chettites and Amorrites and Pherezites and Gergesites and Evites and Jebousites.
Exodus 3:9 And now, behold, the cry of the sons of Israel has come to me, and I have seen the oppression with which the Egyptians oppress them.
Exodus 3:10 And now come, I will send you to Pharao king of Egypt, and you shall bring my people, the sons of Israel, out of the land of Egypt. –
Exodus 3:11 And Moses said to God: Who am I, that I should journey to Pharao king of Egypt and that I should bring the sons of Israel out of the land of Egypt?
Exodus 3:12 And God spoke to Moses, saying: I will be with you, and this is the sign for you that I am sending you out: when you bring my people out of Egypt, you will also serve God on this mountain.
Exodus 3:13 And Moses said to God: Behold, I will go to the sons of Israel and will say to them: The God of your fathers has sent me to you. They will ask me: What name is to him? What shall I say to them?
Exodus 3:14 And God said to Moses: I am the One Who Is. And he said: Thus you shall say to the sons of Israel: The One Who Is has sent me to you.
Exodus 3:15 And God said again to Moses: Thus you shall say to the sons of Israel: The Lord, the God of your fathers, the God of Abraham and the God of Isaac and the God of Jacob, has sent me to you. This is my eternal name and a memorial of generations to generations.
Exodus 3:16 Therefore go and gather the council of elders of the sons of Israel and say to them: The Lord, the God of your fathers, the God of Abraham and the God of Isaac and the God of Jacob, has appeared to me, saying: With a visitation I have visited you and whatever has happened to you in Egypt.
Exodus 3:17 And I said: I will bring you up from the affliction of the Egyptians into the land of the Chanaanites and Chettites and Amorrites and Pherezites and Gergesites and Evites and Jebousites, into a land flowing with milk and honey.
Exodus 3:18 And they will listen to your voice; and you and the council of elders of Israel shall enter to Pharao king of Egypt, and you shall say to him: The God of the Hebrews has called us to himself; therefore let us journey a journey of three days into the wilderness so that we may sacrifice to our God.
Exodus 3:19 But I know that Pharao king of Egypt will not permit you to journey unless with a mighty hand.
Exodus 3:20 And stretching out my hand, I will strike the Egyptians with all my wonders that I will do among them, and after these things he will send you away.
Exodus 3:21 And I will give grace to this people before the Egyptians; and when you run away, you will not go away empty.
Exodus 3:22 A woman shall ask from her neighbor and her tentmate vessels of silver and gold and clothing, and you will place them upon your sons and upon your daughters, and you will plunder the Egyptians. –

## Chapter 4

Exodus 4:1 And Moses answered and said: If therefore they do not believe me or listen to my voice—for they will say: God has not appeared to you—what shall I say to them?
Exodus 4:2 And the Lord said to him: What is this thing in your hand? And he said: A staff.
Exodus 4:3 And he said: Throw it upon the ground. And he threw it upon the ground, and it became a serpent; and Moses fled from it.
Exodus 4:4 And the Lord said to Moses: Stretch out your hand and take hold of the tail. Therefore he stretched out his hand and took hold of the tail, and it became a staff in his hand,
Exodus 4:5 so that they may believe you, that the Lord, the God of their fathers, the God of Abraham and the God of Isaac and the God of Jacob, has appeared to you.
Exodus 4:6 And the Lord said to him again: Bring your hand into your bosom. And he brought his hand into his bosom; and he brought his hand out from his bosom, and his hand became as snow.
Exodus 4:7 And he said: Again bring your hand into your bosom. And he brought his hand into his bosom; and he brought it out from his bosom, and again it was restored to the color of his flesh.
Exodus 4:8 But if they do not believe you or listen to the voice of the first sign, they will believe you because of the voice of the last sign.
Exodus 4:9 And it shall be that if they do not believe you because of these two signs or listen to your voice, you shall take some of the water of the river and pour it upon the dry land, and the water that you take from the river will become blood upon the dry land. –
Exodus 4:10 And Moses said to the Lord: I beseech you, Lord, I am not sufficient before yesterday, nor before the third day, nor since you began to speak to your attendant; I am thin-voiced and slow-tongued.
Exodus 4:11 And the Lord said to Moses: Who gave a mouth to man, and who made one hard of hearing and deaf, seeing and blind? Is it not I, God?
Exodus 4:12 And now journey, and I will open your mouth and instruct you in what you are about to speak.
Exodus 4:13 And Moses said: I beseech you, Lord, select another who is capable, whom you will send.
Exodus 4:14 And the Lord became angry with wrath at Moses and said: Is not Aaron your brother, the Levite, here? I know that speaking, he will speak for you; and behold, he will go out to meet you, and seeing you, he will rejoice within himself.
Exodus 4:15 And you shall speak to him and give my words into his mouth; and I will open your mouth and his mouth and instruct you in what you shall do.
Exodus 4:16 And he will speak for you to the people, and he will be a mouth for you, but you will be for him the things pertaining to God.
Exodus 4:17 And you shall take in your hand this staff that was turned into a serpent, with which you will perform the signs.
Exodus 4:18 And Moses journeyed and returned to Jothor his father-in-law and said: I will journey and return to my brothers who are in Egypt and see whether they are still living. And Jothor said to Moses: Walk in health.
Exodus 4:19 And after those many days the king of Egypt died. And the Lord said to Moses in Madiam: Walk; go away into Egypt, for all those seeking your life have died.
Exodus 4:20 And Moses took his woman and his children and mounted them upon the draft animals and returned into Egypt; and Moses took the staff from God in his hand.
Exodus 4:21 And the Lord said to Moses: As you journey and return into Egypt, see that you perform before Pharao all the wonders that I gave into your hands; but I will harden his heart, and he shall certainly not send the people away.
Exodus 4:22 And you shall say to Pharao: Thus says the Lord: Israel is my firstborn son.
Exodus 4:23 And I said to you: Send my people away so that they may serve me; therefore, if you do not wish to send them away, behold, I will kill your firstborn son.
Exodus 4:24 And it happened on the way, at the lodging place, that an angel of the Lord met him and sought to kill him.
Exodus 4:25 And Sepphora took a pebble and circumcised the foreskin of her son and fell at the feet and said: The blood of the circumcision of my child has stood.
Exodus 4:26 And he went away from him, because she said: The blood of the circumcision of my child has stood.
Exodus 4:27 And the Lord said to Aaron: Journey to meet Moses in the wilderness. And he journeyed and met him at the mountain of God, and they kissed one another.
Exodus 4:28 And Moses reported to Aaron all the words of the Lord for which he had sent him, and all the signs that he had commanded him.
Exodus 4:29 And Moses and Aaron journeyed and gathered the council of elders of the sons of Israel.
Exodus 4:30 And Aaron spoke all these words that God had spoken to Moses, and he performed the signs before the people.
Exodus 4:31 And the people believed and rejoiced, because God had visited the sons of Israel and because he had seen their affliction; and the people bent down and bowed.

## Chapter 5

Exodus 5:1 And after these things Moses and Aaron entered to Pharao and said to him: Thus says the Lord, the God of Israel: Send my people away so that they may keep a festival to me in the wilderness.
Exodus 5:2 And Pharao said: Who is he whose voice I shall hear, so as to send away the sons of Israel? I do not know the Lord, and I will not send Israel away.
Exodus 5:3 And they say to him: The God of the Hebrews has called us to himself; therefore we shall journey a journey of three days into the wilderness so that we may sacrifice to our God, lest death or slaughter meet us.
Exodus 5:4 And the king of Egypt said to them: Why, Moses and Aaron, do you turn my people away from the works? Go away, each of you to his works.
Exodus 5:5 And Pharao said: Behold, now the people are very numerous; shall we therefore make them cease from the works?
Exodus 5:6 And Pharao commanded the taskmasters of the people and the scribes, saying:
Exodus 5:7 It shall no longer be added to give straw to the people for brickmaking, just as yesterday and the third day; let them journey and gather straw for themselves.
Exodus 5:8 And you shall impose upon them the quota of brickmaking that they themselves make each day; you shall take nothing away, for they are idle. Because of this they have cried out, saying: Let us journey and sacrifice to our God.
Exodus 5:9 Let the works of these men be made heavy, and let them be concerned with these and not be concerned with empty words.
Exodus 5:10 And the taskmasters and the scribes were hurrying them and spoke to the people, saying: Thus says Pharao: I no longer give you straw.
Exodus 5:11 You yourselves journey and gather straw for yourselves from wherever you may find it, for nothing is taken away from your quota.
Exodus 5:12 And the people were scattered in all Egypt to gather stubble for straw.
Exodus 5:13 And the taskmasters were hurrying them, saying: Complete the works required each day, just as also when the straw was given to you.
Exodus 5:14 And the scribes of the race of the sons of Israel who had been appointed over them by the overseers of Pharao were flogged, saying: Why did you not complete your quotas of brickmaking, just as yesterday and the third day, and that of today?
Exodus 5:15 And the scribes of the sons of Israel entered and cried out to Pharao, saying: Why do you do thus to your household servants?
Exodus 5:16 Straw is not given to your household servants, and they tell us to make the brick, and behold, your servants have been flogged; therefore you will wrong your people.
Exodus 5:17 And he said to them: You are idle; you are idlers. Because of this you say: Let us journey and sacrifice to our God.
Exodus 5:18 Now therefore, journey and work; for the straw will not be given to you, and you will render the quota of brickmaking.
Exodus 5:19 And the scribes of the sons of Israel saw themselves in evils when they were told: You shall not leave off the daily requirement of brickmaking.
Exodus 5:20 And they met Moses and Aaron coming to meet them as they were going out from Pharao,
Exodus 5:21 and they said to them: May God see you and judge, because you made our odor abominable before Pharao and before his attendants, to give a broadsword into his hands to kill us.
Exodus 5:22 And Moses returned to the Lord and said: Lord, why did you harm this people? And why did you send me?
Exodus 5:23 And since I journeyed to Pharao to speak in your name, he has harmed this people, and you did not rescue your people.

## Chapter 6

Exodus 6:1 And the Lord said to Moses: Already you will see what I will do to Pharao, for with a mighty hand he will send them away, and with a high arm he will drive them out of his land.
Exodus 6:2 And God spoke to Moses and said to him: I am the Lord.
