Exodus 6:3 And I appeared to Abraham and Isaac and Jacob, being their God, and I did not disclose to them my name, Lord.
Exodus 6:4 And I established my covenant with them so as to give them the land of the Chanaanites, the land in which they have sojourned, in which they also sojourned upon it.
Exodus 6:5 And I listened to the groaning of the sons of Israel, whom the Egyptians enslave, and I remembered your covenant.
Exodus 6:6 Walk; speak to the sons of Israel, saying: I am the Lord, and I will bring you out from the oppression of the Egyptians and rescue you from slavery and redeem you with a high arm and great judgment.
Exodus 6:7 And I will take you to myself as a people for me and will be your God, and you will know that I am the Lord your God who brought you out from the oppression of the Egyptians.
Exodus 6:8 And I will bring you into the land into which I stretched out my hand to give it to Abraham and Isaac and Jacob, and I will give it to you as an inheritance. I am the Lord.
Exodus 6:9 And Moses spoke thus to the sons of Israel, and they did not listen to Moses because of smallness of soul and because of the hard works.
Exodus 6:10 And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying:
Exodus 6:11 Enter; speak to Pharao king of Egypt so that he may send the sons of Israel away from his land.
Exodus 6:12 And Moses spoke before the Lord, saying: Behold, the sons of Israel did not listen to me, and how will Pharao listen to me? And I am speechless.
Exodus 6:13 And the Lord spoke to Moses and Aaron and commanded them concerning Pharao king of Egypt so as to send the sons of Israel away from the land of Egypt.
Exodus 6:14 And these are the chiefs of their paternal houses. The sons of Reuben, the firstborn of Israel: Enoch and Phallous, Asron and Charmi. This is the family of Reuben.
Exodus 6:15 And the sons of Symeon: Jemouel and Jamin and Aod and Jachin and Saar and Saul, the one from the Phoenician woman. These are the paternal families of the sons of Symeon.
Exodus 6:16 And these are the names of the sons of Levi according to their families: Gedson, Kaath, and Merari. And the years of the life of Levi were a hundred thirty-seven.
Exodus 6:17 And these are the sons of Gedson: Lobeni and Semei, the houses of their paternal family.
Exodus 6:18 And the sons of Kaath: Ambram and Issaar, Chebron and Oziel. And the years of the life of Kaath were a hundred thirty years.
Exodus 6:19 And the sons of Merari: Mooli and Omousi. These are the paternal houses of Levi according to their families.
Exodus 6:20 And Ambram took Jochabed, the daughter of the brother of his father, for himself as a woman, and she bore him Aaron and Moses and Mariam their sister. And the years of the life of Ambram were a hundred thirty-two years.
Exodus 6:21 And the sons of Issaar: Kore and Naphek and Zechri.
Exodus 6:22 And the sons of Oziel: Elisaphan and Setri.
Exodus 6:23 And Aaron took Elisabeth, the daughter of Aminadab, the sister of Naasson, as a woman for himself, and she bore him Nadab and Abioud and Eleazar and Ithamar.
Exodus 6:24 And the sons of Kore: Asir and Elkana and Abiasaph. These are the generations of Kore.
Exodus 6:25 And Eleazar the son of Aaron took one of the daughters of Phoutiel as a woman for himself, and she bore him Phinees. These are the beginnings of the paternal family of the Levites according to their generations.
Exodus 6:26 This is Aaron and Moses, to whom God said to bring the sons of Israel out of the land of Egypt with their force.
Exodus 6:27 These are the ones speaking with Pharao king of Egypt, and they brought the sons of Israel out of Egypt; it is Aaron and Moses.
Exodus 6:28 On the day when the Lord spoke to Moses in the land of Egypt,
Exodus 6:29 the Lord also spoke to Moses, saying: I am the Lord; speak to Pharao king of Egypt as many things as I say to you.
Exodus 6:30 And Moses said before the Lord: Behold, I am thin-voiced, and how will Pharao listen to me?

## Chapter 7

Exodus 7:1 And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying: Behold, I have made you a god to Pharao, and Aaron your brother will be your prophet.
Exodus 7:2 And you shall speak to him everything that I command you, but Aaron your brother will speak to Pharao so as to send the sons of Israel away from his land.
Exodus 7:3 But I will harden the heart of Pharao and multiply my signs and wonders in the land of Egypt.
Exodus 7:4 And Pharao will not listen to you; and I will lay my hand upon Egypt and bring out with my force my people, the sons of Israel, from the land of Egypt with great vengeance.
Exodus 7:5 And all the Egyptians will know that I am the Lord, stretching out my hand upon Egypt, and I will bring the sons of Israel out from their midst.
Exodus 7:6 And Moses and Aaron did just as the Lord commanded them; thus they did.
Exodus 7:7 And Moses was eighty years old, and Aaron his brother was eighty-three years old, when he spoke to Pharao.
Exodus 7:8 And the Lord spoke to Moses and Aaron, saying:
Exodus 7:9 And if Pharao speaks to you, saying: Give us a sign or a wonder, then you shall say to Aaron your brother: Take the staff and throw it upon the ground before Pharao and before his attendants, and it will become a dragon.
Exodus 7:10 And Moses and Aaron entered before Pharao and his attendants and did so, just as the Lord commanded them; and Aaron threw the staff before Pharao and before his attendants, and it became a dragon.
Exodus 7:11 And Pharao called together the sophists of Egypt and the sorcerers, and the enchanters of the Egyptians also did likewise with their sorceries.
Exodus 7:12 And each threw his staff, and they became dragons; and Aaron’s staff swallowed their staffs.
Exodus 7:13 And the heart of Pharao grew strong, and he did not listen to them, just as the Lord had spoken to them.
Exodus 7:14 And the Lord said to Moses: The heart of Pharao has been made heavy so as not to send the people away.
Exodus 7:15 Walk to Pharao in the morning; behold, he goes out to the water, and you shall stand to meet him at the lip of the river, and you shall take in your hand the staff that was turned into a serpent.
Exodus 7:16 And you shall say to him: The Lord, the God of the Hebrews, has sent me to you, saying: Send my people away so that they may serve me in the wilderness. And behold, you have not listened until now.
Exodus 7:17 Thus says the Lord: By this you will know that I am the Lord. Behold, I strike with the staff in my hand upon the water that is in the river, and it will change into blood.
Exodus 7:18 And the fish that are in the river will die, and the river will stink, and the Egyptians will not be able to drink water from the river.
Exodus 7:19 And the Lord said to Moses: Say to Aaron your brother: Take your staff and stretch out your hand over the waters of Egypt and over their rivers and over their channels and over their marshes and over all their standing water, and it will become blood. And blood came to be in all the land of Egypt, both in wood and in stone.
Exodus 7:20 And Moses and Aaron did so, just as the Lord commanded them; and lifting with his staff, he struck the water that was in the river before Pharao and before his attendants and changed all the water that was in the river into blood.
Exodus 7:21 And the fish that were in the river died, and the river stank, and the Egyptians were not able to drink water from the river, and the blood was in all the land of Egypt.
Exodus 7:22 And the enchanters of the Egyptians also did likewise with their sorceries; and the heart of Pharao was hardened, and he did not listen to them, just as the Lord said.
Exodus 7:23 And Pharao turned and entered his house and did not set his mind even on this.
Exodus 7:24 And all the Egyptians dug around the river so as to drink water, and they were not able to drink water from the river.
Exodus 7:25 And seven days were completed after the Lord struck the river.
Exodus 7:26 And the Lord said to Moses: Enter to Pharao and say to him: Thus says the Lord: Send my people away so that they may serve me.
Exodus 7:27 But if you do not wish to send them away, behold, I strike all your borders with frogs.
Exodus 7:28 And the river will belch out frogs, and they will go up and enter into your houses and into the private chambers of your bedchambers and upon your beds and into the houses of your attendants and your people and in your doughs and in your ovens.
Exodus 7:29 And the frogs will go up upon you and upon your attendants and upon your people.

## Chapter 8

Exodus 8:1 And the Lord said to Moses: Say to Aaron your brother: Stretch out your staff with your hand over the rivers and over the channels and over the marshes, and bring up the frogs.
Exodus 8:2 And Aaron stretched out his hand over the waters of Egypt and brought up the frogs; and the frog was brought up and covered the land of Egypt.
Exodus 8:3 And the enchanters of the Egyptians also did likewise with their sorceries and brought the frogs up upon the land of Egypt.
Exodus 8:4 And Pharao called Moses and Aaron and said: Pray concerning me to the Lord, and let him remove the frogs from me and from my people, and I will send the people away, and let them sacrifice to the Lord.
Exodus 8:5 And Moses said to Pharao: Appoint for me when I shall pray concerning you and concerning your attendants and concerning your people, to make the frogs disappear from you and from your people and from your houses; only in the river will they be left.
Exodus 8:6 And he said: Tomorrow. Therefore he said: As you have spoken, so that you may know that there is no other except the Lord.
Exodus 8:7 And the frogs will be removed from you and from your houses and from the farmsteads and from your attendants and from your people; only in the river will they be left.
Exodus 8:8 And Moses and Aaron went out from Pharao; and Moses cried out to the Lord concerning the appointed limit of the frogs, as Pharao had appointed.
Exodus 8:9 And the Lord did just as Moses said, and the frogs died from the houses and from the farmsteads and from the fields.
Exodus 8:10 And they gathered them into heaps upon heaps, and the land stank.
Exodus 8:11 And Pharao saw that there was relief, and his heart became heavy, and he did not listen to them, just as the Lord had spoken.
Exodus 8:12 And the Lord said to Moses: Say to Aaron: Stretch out your staff with your hand and strike the dust of the land, and there will be gnats among both the humans and the quadrupeds and in all the land of Egypt.
Exodus 8:13 Therefore Aaron stretched out the staff with his hand and struck the dust of the land, and the gnats came to be among both the humans and the quadrupeds, and in all the dust of the land the gnats came to be in all the land of Egypt.
Exodus 8:14 And the enchanters also did likewise with their sorceries to bring out the gnat, and they were not able. And the gnats came to be among the humans and among the quadrupeds.
Exodus 8:15 Therefore the enchanters said to Pharao: This is the finger of God. And the heart of Pharao was hardened, and he did not listen to them, just as the Lord had spoken.
Exodus 8:16 And the Lord said to Moses: Rise early in the morning and stand before Pharao; and behold, he will go out to the water, and you shall say to him: Thus says the Lord: Send my people away so that they may serve me in the wilderness.
Exodus 8:17 But if you do not wish to send my people away, behold, I send the dog-fly upon you and upon your attendants and upon your people and upon your houses, and the houses of the Egyptians will be filled with the dog-fly, and the land upon which they are.
Exodus 8:18 And on that day I will distinguish the land of Gesem, upon which my people are, where the dog-fly will not be, so that you may know that I am the Lord, Lord of all the earth.
Exodus 8:19 And I will make a distinction between my people and between your people; and tomorrow this sign will be upon the land.
Exodus 8:20 And the Lord did so, and the dog-fly came as a multitude into the houses of Pharao and into the houses of his attendants and into all the land of Egypt, and the land was destroyed by the dog-fly.
Exodus 8:21 And Pharao called Moses and Aaron, saying: Go and sacrifice to your God in the land.
Exodus 8:22 And Moses said: It is not possible for it to be so, for we will sacrifice the abominations of the Egyptians to the Lord our God; for if we sacrifice the abominations of the Egyptians before them, we will be stoned.
Exodus 8:23 We will journey a journey of three days into the wilderness and sacrifice to the Lord our God, just as he told us.
Exodus 8:24 And Pharao said: I will send you away, and sacrifice to the Lord your God in the wilderness, but do not extend far in journeying; therefore pray concerning me to the Lord.
Exodus 8:25 And Moses said: Here, I will go out from you and pray to God, and the dog-fly will go away from you and from your attendants and your people tomorrow. Do not add again, Pharao, to deceive by not sending the people away to sacrifice to the Lord.
Exodus 8:26 And Moses went out from Pharao and prayed to God.
Exodus 8:27 And the Lord did just as Moses said and removed the dog-fly from Pharao and his attendants and his people, and not one was left.
Exodus 8:28 And Pharao made his heart heavy on this occasion also and did not wish to send the people away.

## Chapter 9

Exodus 9:1 And the Lord said to Moses: Enter to Pharao and say to him: Thus says the Lord, the God of the Hebrews: Send my people away so that they may serve me.
Exodus 9:2 Therefore, if you do not wish to send my people away but still retain them,
Exodus 9:3 behold, the hand of the Lord will be upon your livestock in the fields, upon the horses and the draft animals and the camels and cattle and sheep: an exceedingly great death.
Exodus 9:4 And at that time I will make a distinction between the livestock of the Egyptians and between the livestock of the sons of Israel; not one thing from all that belongs to the sons of Israel will die.
Exodus 9:5 And God set a limit, saying: Tomorrow the Lord will do this thing upon the land.
Exodus 9:6 And the Lord did this thing on the next day, and all the livestock of the Egyptians died, but none of the livestock of the sons of Israel died.
Exodus 9:7 And Pharao saw that none of all the livestock of the sons of Israel had died, and the heart of Pharao became heavy, and he did not send the people away.
Exodus 9:8 And the Lord spoke to Moses and Aaron, saying: Take for yourselves hands full of furnace soot, and let Moses sprinkle it toward heaven before Pharao and before his attendants.
Exodus 9:9 And let it become dust upon all the land of Egypt, and there will be ulcers upon the humans and upon the quadrupeds, blisters boiling up among both the humans and the quadrupeds and in all the land of Egypt.
Exodus 9:10 And he took the furnace soot before Pharao, and Moses sprinkled it toward heaven, and there came to be ulcers, blisters boiling up, among the humans and among the quadrupeds.
Exodus 9:11 And the sorcerers were not able to stand before Moses because of the ulcers, for the ulcers came to be among the sorcerers and in all the land of Egypt.
Exodus 9:12 But the Lord hardened the heart of Pharao, and he did not listen to them, just as the Lord commanded.
Exodus 9:13 And the Lord said to Moses: Rise early in the morning and stand before Pharao and say to him: Thus says the Lord, the God of the Hebrews: Send my people away so that they may serve me.
Exodus 9:14 For at this present time I am sending all my encounters into your heart and those of your attendants and your people, so that you may know that there is no other like me in all the earth.
Exodus 9:15 For now, sending my hand, I will strike you and your people with death, and you will be destroyed from the earth.
Exodus 9:16 And because of this you were preserved, so that I may display my strength in you and so that my name may be proclaimed in all the earth.
Exodus 9:17 Still, therefore, you lay hold of my people so as not to send them away.
Exodus 9:18 Behold, at this hour tomorrow I rain exceedingly much hail, such as has not come to be in Egypt from the day it was founded until this day.
Exodus 9:19 Now therefore, hasten to gather your livestock and whatever is yours in the field, for all the humans and livestock, whatever is found in the field and does not enter a house, when the hail falls upon them, will die.
Exodus 9:20 The one among the attendants of Pharao who feared the word of the Lord gathered his livestock into the houses.
Exodus 9:21 But the one who did not apply his mind to the word of the Lord left the livestock in the fields. –
Exodus 9:22 And the Lord said to Moses: Stretch out your hand toward heaven, and there will be hail upon all the land of Egypt, upon the humans and the livestock and every plant that is upon the land.
Exodus 9:23 And Moses stretched out his hand toward heaven, and the Lord gave voices and hail, and the fire was running upon the land, and the Lord rained hail upon all the land of Egypt.
Exodus 9:24 And there was hail and fire flaming in the hail; and the hail was exceedingly, exceedingly great, such as had not come to be in Egypt since a nation came to be upon it.
Exodus 9:25 And the hail struck throughout all the land of Egypt, from human to livestock, and the hail struck every plant in the field, and the hail shattered all the trees in the fields.
Exodus 9:26 Only in the land of Gesem, where the sons of Israel were, did the hail not come to be.
Exodus 9:27 And Pharao sent and called Moses and Aaron and said to them: I have sinned this time; the Lord is righteous, but I and my people are impious.
Exodus 9:28 Therefore pray concerning me to the Lord, and let the voices of God and the hail and fire cease; and I will send you away, and you shall no longer add to remain.
Exodus 9:29 And Moses said to him: When I go out of the city, I will spread out my hands to the Lord, and the voices will cease, and the hail and the rain will be no more, so that you may know that the earth is the Lord’s.
Exodus 9:30 And as for you and your attendants, I know that you have not yet feared the Lord.
Exodus 9:31 And the flax and the barley were struck, for the barley was standing and the flax was seeding.
Exodus 9:32 But the wheat and the spelt were not struck, for they were late.
Exodus 9:33 And Moses went out from Pharao, outside the city, and spread out his hands to the Lord, and the voices and the hail ceased, and the rain no longer dripped upon the land.
Exodus 9:34 And Pharao saw that the rain and the hail and the voices had ceased, and he added to sin and made his heart and the heart of his attendants heavy.
Exodus 9:35 And the heart of Pharao was hardened, and he did not send the sons of Israel away, just as the Lord had spoken to Moses.

## Chapter 10

Exodus 10:1 And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying: Enter to Pharao, for I have hardened his heart and the heart of his attendants so that these signs may come upon them in succession,
Exodus 10:2 so that you may relate in the ears of your children and to the children of your children as many things as I have mocked the Egyptians with, and my signs that I performed among them, and you will know that I am the Lord.
Exodus 10:3 And Moses and Aaron entered before Pharao and said to him: Thus says the Lord, the God of the Hebrews: How long do you not wish to show regard for me? Send my people away so that they may serve me.
Exodus 10:4 But if you do not wish to send my people away, behold, at this hour tomorrow I bring a great locust upon all your borders.
Exodus 10:5 And it will cover the face of the land, and you will not be able to look down at the land, and it will devour all the remainder of the land that was left, which the hail left for you, and it will devour every tree growing for you upon the land.
Exodus 10:6 And your houses and the houses of your attendants and all the houses in all the land of the Egyptians will be filled, which your fathers and their forefathers have never seen from the day they came to be upon the land until this day. And Moses turned away and went out from Pharao.
Exodus 10:7 And the attendants of Pharao say to him: How long will this be a stumbling block to us? Send the men away so that they may serve their God. Or do you wish to know that Egypt has perished?
Exodus 10:8 And they returned both Moses and Aaron to Pharao, and he said to them: Journey and serve your God; but who and who are those journeying?
Exodus 10:9 And Moses says: We will journey with the young and the elders, with our sons and daughters and sheep and cattle, for it is a festival of the Lord our God.
Exodus 10:10 And he said to them: Let it be so; may the Lord be with you. As I send you, shall I not also send your baggage? See that evil lies before you.
Exodus 10:11 Not so; but let the men journey, and serve God, for this is what you yourselves seek. And they drove them out from the face of Pharao. –
Exodus 10:12 And the Lord said to Moses: Stretch out your hand over the land of Egypt, and let the locust go up upon the land and devour every plant of the land and all the fruit of the trees that the hail left behind.
Exodus 10:13 And Moses raised the staff toward heaven, and the Lord brought a south wind upon the land that whole day and whole night; morning came, and the south wind took up the locust
Exodus 10:14 and brought it up upon all the land of Egypt, and it settled upon all the borders of Egypt, exceedingly great. Before it no such locust had come to be, and after these things it will not be so.
Exodus 10:15 And it covered the face of the land, and the land was destroyed; and it devoured every plant of the land and all the fruit of the trees that had been left by the hail. Nothing green was left among the trees or among any plant of the field in all the land of Egypt.
Exodus 10:16 And Pharao hastened to call Moses and Aaron, saying: I have sinned before the Lord your God and against you.
Exodus 10:17 Therefore accept my sin still now and pray to the Lord your God, and let him remove this death from me.
Exodus 10:18 And Moses went out from Pharao and prayed to God.
Exodus 10:19 And the Lord changed it to a strong wind from the sea, and it took up the locust and cast it into the Red Sea, and not one locust was left in all the land of Egypt.
Exodus 10:20 And the Lord hardened the heart of Pharao, and he did not send the sons of Israel away.
Exodus 10:21 And the Lord said to Moses: Stretch out your hand toward heaven, and let darkness come to be upon the land of Egypt, a palpable darkness.
Exodus 10:22 And Moses stretched out his hand toward heaven, and darkness, gloom, and storm came to be upon all the land of Egypt for three days.
Exodus 10:23 And no one saw his brother for three days, and no one rose from his bed for three days; but for all the sons of Israel there was light in all the places in which they were.
Exodus 10:24 And Pharao called Moses and Aaron, saying: Walk; serve the Lord your God. Only leave behind the sheep and the cattle, and let your baggage run away with you.
Exodus 10:25 And Moses said: But you also will give us whole burnt offerings and sacrifices that we will make to the Lord our God.
Exodus 10:26 And our livestock will journey with us, and we will not leave a hoof behind, for from them we will take to serve the Lord our God; but we do not know what we shall serve to the Lord our God until we come there.
Exodus 10:27 But the Lord hardened the heart of Pharao, and he did not wish to send them away.
Exodus 10:28 And Pharao says: Go away from me; take heed to yourself not to add again to see my face. On whatever day you appear to me, you will die.
Exodus 10:29 And Moses says: You have spoken; I will no longer appear to you face to face.

## Chapter 11

Exodus 11:1 And the Lord said to Moses: I will bring one more plague upon Pharao and upon Egypt, and after these things he will send you away from here; and when he sends you away, he will drive you out with everything, with an expulsion.
Exodus 11:2 Therefore speak secretly into the ears of the people, and let each man ask from his neighbor and a woman from her neighbor vessels of silver and gold and clothing.
Exodus 11:3 And the Lord gave grace to his people before the Egyptians, and they lent to them; and the man Moses became exceedingly great before the Egyptians and before Pharao and before all his attendants.
Exodus 11:4 And Moses said: Thus says the Lord: About the middle of the night I am entering into the midst of Egypt,
Exodus 11:5 and every firstborn in the land of Egypt will die, from the firstborn of Pharao who sits upon the throne as far as the firstborn of the maidservant who is beside the mill, and as far as the firstborn of every livestock animal.
Exodus 11:6 And there will be a great cry throughout all the land of Egypt, such as has not come to be and such as will no longer be added.
Exodus 11:7 But among all the sons of Israel a dog will not growl with its tongue, from human to livestock, so that you may know how greatly the Lord will distinguish between the Egyptians and Israel.
Exodus 11:8 And all these servants of yours will come down to me and bow down to me, saying: Go out, you and all your people whom you lead; and after these things I will go out. And Moses went out from Pharao with wrath.
Exodus 11:9 And the Lord said to Moses: Pharao will not listen to you, so that multiplying, I may multiply my signs and wonders in the land of Egypt.
Exodus 11:10 And Moses and Aaron performed all these signs and wonders in the land of Egypt before Pharao; but the Lord hardened the heart of Pharao, and he did not wish to send the sons of Israel away from the land of Egypt.

## Chapter 12

Exodus 12:1 And the Lord spoke to Moses and Aaron in the land of Egypt, saying:
Exodus 12:2 This month is for you the beginning of months; it is the first for you among the months of the year.
Exodus 12:3 Speak to all the congregation of the sons of Israel, saying: On the tenth of this month, let them each take a sheep according to their paternal houses, each a sheep according to a house.
Exodus 12:4 But if those in the house are too few so as not to be sufficient for a sheep, he shall take together with himself his neighbor who is near him, according to the number of souls; each shall be counted for the sheep according to what is sufficient for him.
Exodus 12:5 The sheep shall be perfect, male, a year old, for you; you shall take it from the lambs and the kids.
Exodus 12:6 And it shall be kept for you until the fourteenth of this month, and all the multitude of the congregation of the sons of Israel shall slaughter it toward evening.
Exodus 12:7 And they shall take some of the blood and place it upon the two doorposts and upon the lintel in the houses in which they eat it.
Exodus 12:8 And they shall eat the meats in this night; roasted with fire, they shall eat them with unleavened bread upon bitter herbs.
Exodus 12:9 You shall not eat any of them raw or boiled in water, but only roasted with fire, the head together with the feet and the entrails.
Exodus 12:10 You shall not leave any of it until morning, and you shall not break a bone of it; but the things left from it until morning you shall burn up with fire.
Exodus 12:11 And thus you shall eat it: your loins girded, and the footwear on your feet, and the staffs in your hands; and you shall eat it with haste. It is a pascha to the Lord.
Exodus 12:12 And I will pass through the land of Egypt in this night and strike every firstborn in the land of Egypt, from human to livestock, and among all the gods of the Egyptians I will execute vengeance. I am the Lord.
Exodus 12:13 And the blood will be for you as a sign upon the houses in which you are there, and I will see the blood and shelter you, and there will not be among you a plague for destruction when I strike in the land of Egypt.
Exodus 12:14 And this day will be a memorial for you, and you shall keep it as a festival to the Lord throughout all your generations; you shall keep it as an eternal ordinance.
Exodus 12:15 For seven days you shall eat unleavened bread, and from the first day you shall make yeast disappear from your houses; every soul who eats yeast will be utterly destroyed from Israel, from the first day until the seventh day.
Exodus 12:16 And the first day shall be called holy, and the seventh day shall be called holy for you; you shall do no servile work on them, except as many things as will be prepared for every soul—this alone shall be prepared by you.
Exodus 12:17 And you shall keep this commandment, for on this day I will bring your force out of the land of Egypt, and you shall make this day an eternal ordinance throughout your generations.
Exodus 12:18 Beginning on the fourteenth day of the first month, from evening you shall eat unleavened bread until the twenty-first day of the month, until evening.
Exodus 12:19 For seven days yeast shall not be found in your houses; every soul who eats something leavened will be utterly destroyed from the congregation of Israel, both among the resident aliens and the natives of the land.
Exodus 12:20 You shall not eat anything leavened; in every dwelling place of yours you shall eat unleavened bread.
Exodus 12:21 And Moses called all the council of elders of the sons of Israel and said to them: Go away and take a sheep for yourselves according to your families, and sacrifice the pascha.
Exodus 12:22 And you shall take a bundle of hyssop and, dipping it in some of the blood beside the door, touch the lintel and both doorposts with some of the blood that is beside the door; but none of you shall go out through the door of his house until morning.
Exodus 12:23 And the Lord will pass by to strike the Egyptians and will see the blood upon the lintel and upon both doorposts, and the Lord will pass by the door and will not permit the destroyer to enter your houses to strike.
Exodus 12:24 And you shall keep this word as an ordinance for yourself and for your sons forever.
Exodus 12:25 And if you enter into the land that the Lord gives you, just as he spoke, you shall keep this service.
Exodus 12:26 And it shall be, if your sons say to you: What is this service?
Exodus 12:27 Then you shall say to them: This pascha is a sacrifice to the Lord, as he sheltered the houses of the sons of Israel in Egypt when he struck the Egyptians but rescued our houses. And the people bent down and bowed.
Exodus 12:28 And the sons of Israel went away and did just as the Lord commanded Moses and Aaron; thus they did.
Exodus 12:29 And it happened in the middle of the night that the Lord struck every firstborn in the land of Egypt, from the firstborn of Pharao who sat upon the throne as far as the firstborn of the captive woman who was in the pit, and as far as the firstborn of every livestock animal.
Exodus 12:30 And Pharao arose by night, and all his attendants and all the Egyptians, and a great cry came to be in all the land of Egypt, for there was no house in which there was not someone dead.
Exodus 12:31 And Pharao called Moses and Aaron by night and said to them: Arise and go out from my people, both you and the sons of Israel; walk and serve the Lord your God, just as you say.
Exodus 12:32 And take up your sheep and cattle and journey, and bless me also.
Exodus 12:33 And the Egyptians were forcing the people with haste to drive them out of the land, for they said: We are all dying.
Exodus 12:34 And the people took up the dough before it was leavened, their kneading bowls bound in their garments upon their shoulders.
Exodus 12:35 And the sons of Israel did just as Moses commanded them, and they asked from the Egyptians vessels of silver and gold and clothing.
Exodus 12:36 And the Lord gave grace to his people before the Egyptians, and they lent to them; and they plundered the Egyptians.
Exodus 12:37 And the sons of Israel departed from Ramesses to Sokchotha, about six hundred thousand men on foot, apart from the baggage.
Exodus 12:38 And a great mixed company went up together with them, and sheep and cattle and exceedingly many livestock animals.
Exodus 12:39 And they baked the dough that they had brought out of Egypt into unleavened baked cakes, for it was not leavened; for the Egyptians drove them out, and they were not able to remain, nor did they prepare provisions for themselves for the way.
Exodus 12:40 And the dwelling of the sons of Israel, which they dwelt in the land of Egypt and in the land of Chanaan, was four hundred thirty years.
Exodus 12:41 And it happened after the four hundred thirty years that all the force of the Lord went out from the land of Egypt.
Exodus 12:42 It is a night of advance-watch for the Lord so as to bring them out of the land of Egypt; that night is this advance-watch for the Lord, so as to be for all the sons of Israel throughout their generations.
Exodus 12:43 And the Lord spoke to Moses and Aaron, saying: This is the law of the pascha: no foreigner shall eat of it.
Exodus 12:44 And every household servant of someone, or one bought with silver, you shall circumcise him, and then he shall eat of it.
Exodus 12:45 A sojourner or a hired worker shall not eat of it.
Exodus 12:46 It shall be eaten in one house, and you shall not carry any of the meats outside from the house; and you shall not break a bone of it.
Exodus 12:47 All the congregation of the sons of Israel shall perform it.
Exodus 12:48 And if any proselyte approaches you to perform the pascha to the Lord, you shall circumcise every male of his, and then he shall approach to perform it and will be just as the native of the land; no uncircumcised person shall eat of it.
Exodus 12:49 There shall be one law for the inhabitant and for the proselyte who approaches among you.
Exodus 12:50 And the sons of Israel did just as the Lord commanded Moses and Aaron for them; thus they did. –
Exodus 12:51 And it happened on that day that the Lord brought the sons of Israel out of the land of Egypt with their force.

## Chapter 13

Exodus 13:1 And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying:
Exodus 13:2 Sanctify to me every firstborn, the first-generated that opens every womb among the sons of Israel, from human to livestock; it is mine.
Exodus 13:3 And Moses said to the people: Remember this day in which you came out of the land of Egypt, out of a house of slavery, for with a mighty hand the Lord brought you out from here; and yeast shall not be eaten.
Exodus 13:4 For today you are going out, in the month of the new things.
Exodus 13:5 And it shall be whenever the Lord your God brings you into the land of the Chanaanites and Chettites and Evites and Gergesites and Amorrites and Pherezites and Jebousites, which he swore to your fathers to give you, a land flowing with milk and honey, that you shall perform this service in this month.
Exodus 13:6 For six days you shall eat unleavened bread, but on the seventh day is a festival of the Lord.
Exodus 13:7 You shall eat unleavened bread for the seven days; nothing leavened shall be seen with you, nor shall yeast be yours within all your borders.
Exodus 13:8 And on that day you shall report to your son, saying: Because of this the Lord God acted for me as I was going out from Egypt.
Exodus 13:9 And it shall be a sign for you upon your hand and a memorial before your eyes, so that the law of the Lord may be in your mouth; for with a mighty hand the Lord God brought you out of Egypt.
Exodus 13:10 And you shall keep this law according to the appointed times of seasons, from days to days.
Exodus 13:11 And it shall be when the Lord your God brings you into the land of the Chanaanites in the manner that he swore to your fathers and gives it to you,
Exodus 13:12 that you shall set apart every male that opens a womb to the Lord; every one that opens a womb from the herds or among your livestock, as many as are born to you, the males, you shall sanctify to the Lord.
Exodus 13:13 Every one that opens the womb of a donkey you shall exchange for a sheep; but if you do not exchange it, you shall redeem it. Every human firstborn among your sons you shall redeem.
Exodus 13:14 And if your son asks you after these things, saying: What is this? Then you shall say to him: With a mighty hand the Lord brought us out of the land of Egypt, out of a house of slavery.
Exodus 13:15 And when Pharao was hardened about sending us away, he killed every firstborn in the land of Egypt, from the firstborn of humans as far as the firstborn of livestock. Because of this I sacrifice to the Lord every male that opens a womb, and I will redeem every firstborn of my sons.
Exodus 13:16 And it shall be as a sign upon your hand and an immovable thing before your eyes, for with a mighty hand the Lord brought you out of Egypt.
Exodus 13:17 And when Pharao sent the people away, God did not guide them by the way of the land of the Phylistiim, because it was near; for God said: Lest the people repent when they see war and return to Egypt.
Exodus 13:18 And God led the people around by the way into the wilderness, toward the Red Sea. And in the fifth generation the sons of Israel went up from the land of Egypt.
Exodus 13:19 And Moses took the bones of Joseph with himself, for with an oath Joseph had made the sons of Israel swear, saying: With a visitation the Lord will visit you, and you shall also carry my bones up from here with you.
Exodus 13:20 And the sons of Israel departed from Sokchoth and encamped in Othom beside the wilderness.
Exodus 13:21 And God was leading them, by day in a pillar of cloud to show them the way, and by night in a pillar of fire.
Exodus 13:22 The pillar of cloud by day and the pillar of fire by night did not fail before all the people.

## Chapter 14

Exodus 14:1 And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying:
Exodus 14:2 Speak to the sons of Israel, and let them turn back and encamp opposite the farmstead, between Magdolum and the sea, opposite Beelsepphon; before them you shall encamp by the sea.
Exodus 14:3 And Pharao will say to his people: These sons of Israel are wandering in the land, for the wilderness has shut them in.
Exodus 14:4 But I will harden the heart of Pharao, and he will pursue after them; and I will be glorified in Pharao and in all his army, and all the Egyptians will know that I am the Lord. And they did so.
Exodus 14:5 And it was reported to the king of the Egyptians that the people had fled; and the heart of Pharao and his attendants was changed toward the people, and they said: What is this that we have done, sending the sons of Israel away so as not to serve us?
Exodus 14:6 Therefore Pharao yoked his chariots and took all his people away with himself,
Exodus 14:7 and he took six hundred chosen chariots and all the horse force of the Egyptians and captains over all of them.
Exodus 14:8 And the Lord hardened the heart of Pharao king of Egypt and of his attendants, and he pursued after the sons of Israel; but the sons of Israel were going out with a high hand.
Exodus 14:9 And the Egyptians pursued after them and found them encamped beside the sea, and all the horse force and the chariots of Pharao and the riders and his army were opposite the farmstead, across from Beelsepphon.
Exodus 14:10 And Pharao was drawing near; and the sons of Israel looked up with their eyes and see, and the Egyptians encamped behind them, and they were exceedingly afraid. And the sons of Israel cried out to the Lord.
Exodus 14:11 And they said to Moses: Was it because tombs do not exist in the land of Egypt that you brought us out to put us to death in the wilderness? What is this that you did to us by bringing us out of Egypt?
Exodus 14:12 Was this not the word that we spoke to you in Egypt, saying: Let us be, so that we may serve the Egyptians? For it is better for us to serve the Egyptians than to die in this wilderness.
Exodus 14:13 And Moses said to the people: Take courage; stand and see the salvation from God that he will perform for us today. For in the manner that you have seen the Egyptians today, you shall no longer add again to see them for all time.
Exodus 14:14 The Lord will fight for you, and you will be silent.
Exodus 14:15 And the Lord said to Moses: Why do you cry out to me? Speak to the sons of Israel, and let them decamp.
Exodus 14:16 And you, lift with your staff and stretch out your hand over the sea and rend it, and let the sons of Israel enter into the midst of the sea along the dry land.
Exodus 14:17 And behold, I will harden the heart of Pharao and of all the Egyptians, and they will enter after them; and I will be glorified in Pharao and in all his army and in his chariots and horses.
Exodus 14:18 And all the Egyptians will know that I am the Lord when I am glorified in Pharao and in his chariots and horses.
Exodus 14:19 And the angel of God who was going before the encampment of the sons of Israel departed and journeyed behind them; and the pillar of cloud also departed from before their face and stood behind them.
Exodus 14:20 And it entered between the encampment of the Egyptians and between the encampment of Israel and stood; and darkness and gloom came to be, and the night passed, and they did not mix with one another the whole night.
Exodus 14:21 And Moses stretched out his hand over the sea, and the Lord drove the sea with a violent south wind the whole night and made the sea dry, and the water was split.
Exodus 14:22 And the sons of Israel entered into the midst of the sea along the dry land, and the water was a wall for them on the right and a wall on the left.
Exodus 14:23 And the Egyptians pursued and entered after them, all the horse force of Pharao and the chariots and the riders, into the midst of the sea.
Exodus 14:24 And it happened in the morning watch that the Lord looked upon the encampment of the Egyptians in the pillar of fire and cloud and threw the encampment of the Egyptians into confusion.
Exodus 14:25 And he bound the axles of their chariots and led them with force. And the Egyptians said: Let us flee from the face of Israel, for the Lord fights for them against the Egyptians.
Exodus 14:26 And the Lord said to Moses: Stretch out your hand over the sea, and let the water be restored and cover the Egyptians, both the chariots and the riders.
Exodus 14:27 And Moses stretched out his hand over the sea, and toward day the water was restored to its place; and the Egyptians fled under the water, and the Lord shook the Egyptians off into the midst of the sea.
Exodus 14:28 And the water turned back and covered the chariots and the riders and all the force of Pharao who had entered after them into the sea, and not even one of them was left.
Exodus 14:29 But the sons of Israel journeyed through dry land in the midst of the sea, and the water was a wall for them on the right and a wall on the left.
Exodus 14:30 And the Lord rescued Israel on that day from the hand of the Egyptians; and Israel saw the Egyptians dead beside the lip of the sea.
Exodus 14:31 And Israel saw the great hand, the things that the Lord did to the Egyptians; and the people feared the Lord and believed God and Moses his attendant.

## Chapter 15

Exodus 15:1 Then Moses and the sons of Israel sang this song to God and spoke, saying: Let us sing to the Lord, for he has been gloriously glorified; horse and rider he cast into the sea.
Exodus 15:2 He became a helper and protector to me for salvation; this is my God, and I will glorify him, the God of my father, and I will exalt him.
Exodus 15:3 The Lord crushes wars; Lord is his name.
Exodus 15:4 The chariots of Pharao and his force he cast into the sea; chosen riders, captains, he drowned in the Red Sea.
Exodus 15:5 He covered them with the sea; they sank into the deep like a stone.
Exodus 15:6 Your right hand, Lord, has been glorified in strength; your right hand, Lord, shattered enemies.
Exodus 15:7 And by the multitude of your glory you crushed the adversaries; you sent your wrath, and it devoured them like stubble.
Exodus 15:8 And through the breath of your anger the water stood apart; the waters congealed like a wall, the waves congealed in the midst of the sea.
Exodus 15:9 The enemy said: Pursuing, I will overtake; I will divide spoils; I will fill my soul; I will kill with my sword; my hand will have dominion.
Exodus 15:10 You sent your wind; the sea covered them. They sank like lead in violent water.
Exodus 15:11 Who is like you among gods, Lord? Who is like you, glorified among holy ones, wondrous in glories, performing wonders?
Exodus 15:12 You stretched out your right hand; the earth swallowed them.
Exodus 15:13 In your righteousness you guided this people of yours whom you redeemed; by your strength you called them into your holy lodging.
Exodus 15:14 Nations heard and became angry; pangs seized the inhabitants of Phylistiim.
Exodus 15:15 Then the rulers of Edom hastened, and trembling seized the rulers of the Moabites; all the inhabitants of Chanaan melted.
Exodus 15:16 May fear and trembling fall upon them; by the greatness of your arm, let them become stone until your people pass by, Lord, until this people of yours whom you acquired pass by.
Exodus 15:17 Having brought them in, plant them on the mountain of your inheritance, in your prepared dwelling place that you worked, Lord, a sanctuary, Lord, that your hands prepared.
Exodus 15:18 The Lord reigns for the age and upon the age and still.
Exodus 15:19 For the horse of Pharao entered with the chariots and riders into the sea, and the Lord brought the water of the sea upon them; but the sons of Israel journeyed through dry land in the midst of the sea.
Exodus 15:20 And Mariam the prophet, the sister of Aaron, took the hand-drum in her hand, and all the women went out behind her with hand-drums and dances.
Exodus 15:21 And Mariam began for them, saying: Let us sing to the Lord, for he has been gloriously glorified; horse and rider he cast into the sea.
Exodus 15:22 And Moses led the sons of Israel away from the Red Sea and brought them into the wilderness of Sour; and they journeyed three days in the wilderness and did not find water to drink.
Exodus 15:23 And they came to Merra and were not able to drink from Merra, for it was bitter; because of this the name of that place was named Bitterness.
Exodus 15:24 And the people were grumbling against Moses, saying: What shall we drink?
Exodus 15:25 And Moses cried out to the Lord; and the Lord showed him a piece of wood, and he cast it into the water, and the water was made sweet. There he set ordinances and judgments for him, and there he tested him.
Exodus 15:26 And he said: If by hearing you hear the voice of the Lord your God and do the things pleasing before him and incline your ear to his commandments and keep all his ordinances, I will not bring upon you any disease that I brought upon the Egyptians; for I am the Lord who heals you.
Exodus 15:27 And they came to Ailim, and there were twelve springs of waters and seventy trunks of palm trees there; and they encamped there beside the waters.

## Chapter 16

Exodus 16:1 And they departed from Ailim, and all the congregation of the sons of Israel came into the wilderness of Sin, which is between Ailim and Sina, on the fifteenth day of the second month after they had gone out of the land of Egypt.
Exodus 16:2 And all the congregation of the sons of Israel was grumbling against Moses and Aaron.
Exodus 16:3 And the sons of Israel said to them: Would that we had died, struck by the Lord in the land of Egypt, when we sat at the pots of meats and ate breads to fullness, because you brought us out into this wilderness to kill all this congregation with famine.
Exodus 16:4 And the Lord said to Moses: Behold, I rain breads for you from heaven, and the people will go out and gather what is for the day, day by day, so that I may test them, whether they will walk by my law or not.
Exodus 16:5 And it shall be on the sixth day that they will prepare whatever they bring in, and whatever they gather day by day will be double.
Exodus 16:6 And Moses and Aaron said to all the congregation of the sons of Israel: In the evening you will know that the Lord brought you out of the land of Egypt,
Exodus 16:7 and in the morning you will see the glory of the Lord when he listens to your grumbling against God; but what are we, that you grumble against us?
Exodus 16:8 And Moses said: When the Lord gives you meats in the evening to eat and breads in the morning to fullness, because the Lord listens to your grumbling that you grumble against us—but what are we? For your grumbling is not against us but against God.
Exodus 16:9 And Moses said to Aaron: Say to all the congregation of the sons of Israel: Approach before God, for he has listened to your grumbling.
Exodus 16:10 And while Aaron was speaking to all the congregation of the sons of Israel, they turned toward the wilderness, and the glory of the Lord appeared in a cloud.
Exodus 16:11 And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying:
Exodus 16:12 I have listened to the grumbling of the sons of Israel. Speak to them, saying: Toward evening you shall eat meats, and in the morning you shall be filled with breads; and you will know that I am the Lord your God.
Exodus 16:13 And evening came, and a quail came up and covered the encampment; morning came as the dew was coming to rest around the encampment,
Exodus 16:14 and behold, upon the face of the wilderness was something thin, like white coriander, like frost upon the land.
Exodus 16:15 And when the sons of Israel saw it, they said one to another: What is this? For they did not know what it was. And Moses said to them: This is the bread that the Lord gave you to eat.
Exodus 16:16 This is the word that the Lord commanded: Gather some of it, each according to those due, a gomor per head according to the number of your souls; each gather with your tentmates.
Exodus 16:17 And the sons of Israel did so and gathered, one the much and one the less.
Exodus 16:18 And measuring with the gomor, the one with the much had no surplus, and the one with the less had no lack; each gathered according to those due with himself.
Exodus 16:19 And Moses said to them: Let no one leave any of it for the morning.
Exodus 16:20 And they did not listen to Moses, but some left some of it for the morning; and it boiled forth worms and stank, and Moses was embittered at them.
Exodus 16:21 And they gathered it morning by morning, each what was due to him; but when the sun grew warm, it melted.
Exodus 16:22 And it happened on the sixth day that they gathered double what was needed, two gomors for one; and all the rulers of the congregation entered and reported to Moses.
Exodus 16:23 And Moses said to them: This is the word that the Lord spoke: Tomorrow is sabbaths, a holy rest to the Lord. As many things as you bake, bake, and as many things as you boil, boil; and leave all the surplus in storage for the morning.
Exodus 16:24 And they left some of it for the morning, just as Moses commanded them; and it did not stink, nor did a worm come to be in it.
Exodus 16:25 And Moses said: Eat today, for today is sabbaths to the Lord; it will not be found in the field.
Exodus 16:26 For six days you shall gather; but on the seventh day is sabbaths, because there will be none on it.
Exodus 16:27 And it happened on the seventh day that some of the people went out to gather and did not find any.
Exodus 16:28 And the Lord said to Moses: How long do you not wish to listen to my commandments and my law?
Exodus 16:29 See, for the Lord gave you the sabbaths on this day; because of this he gave you on the sixth day breads for two days. Each of you shall sit in your houses; let no one go out from his place on the seventh day.
Exodus 16:30 And the people kept sabbaths on the seventh day.
Exodus 16:31 And the sons of Israel named its name man; and it was like white coriander seed, and its taste was like a cake with honey.
Exodus 16:32 And Moses said: This is the word that the Lord commanded: Fill the gomor with man for storage throughout your generations, so that they may see the bread that you ate in the wilderness when the Lord brought you out of the land of Egypt.
Exodus 16:33 And Moses said to Aaron: Take one golden jar and put a full gomor of man into it, and you shall store it before God for preservation throughout your generations.
Exodus 16:34 In the manner that the Lord commanded Moses, Aaron also stored it before the testimony for preservation.
Exodus 16:35 And the sons of Israel ate the man for forty years, until they came into inhabited land; they ate the man until they arrived at a part of Phoenicia.
Exodus 16:36 And the gomor was a tenth of the three measures.

## Chapter 17

Exodus 17:1 And all the congregation of the sons of Israel departed from the wilderness of Sin according to their encampments through the word of the Lord and encamped in Raphidin; but there was no water for the people to drink.
Exodus 17:2 And the people were reviling Moses, saying: Give us water so that we may drink. And Moses said to them: Why do you revile me, and why do you test the Lord?
Exodus 17:3 And the people thirsted there for water, and the people were grumbling there against Moses, saying: Why is this, that you brought us up from Egypt to kill us and our children and livestock with thirst?
Exodus 17:4 And Moses cried out to the Lord, saying: What shall I do with this people? Yet a little, and they will stone me.
Exodus 17:5 And the Lord said to Moses: Go before this people, and take with yourself some of the elders of the people; and take in your hand the staff with which you struck the river and journey.
Exodus 17:6 Here, I stand before you there upon the rock in Choreb; and you shall strike the rock, and water will come out from it, and my people will drink. And Moses did so before the sons of Israel.
Exodus 17:7 And he named the name of that place Temptation and Reviling because of the reviling of the sons of Israel and because they tested the Lord, saying: Is the Lord among us or not?
Exodus 17:8 And Amalek came and was making war against Israel in Raphidin.
Exodus 17:9 And Moses said to Jesus: Choose capable men for yourself and go out and array yourself against Amalek tomorrow, and behold, I will stand upon the top of the hill, and the staff of God will be in my hand.
Exodus 17:10 And Jesus did just as Moses told him, and going out, he arrayed himself against Amalek; and Moses and Aaron and Or went up upon the top of the hill.
Exodus 17:11 And it happened that whenever Moses raised his hands, Israel was growing strong; but whenever he lowered his hands, Amalek was growing strong.
Exodus 17:12 And the hands of Moses were heavy; and taking a stone, they placed it under him, and he sat upon it, and Aaron and Or were supporting his hands, one from here and one from there; and the hands of Moses became supported until the setting of the sun.
Exodus 17:13 And Jesus routed Amalek and all his people with slaughter of the sword.
Exodus 17:14 And the Lord said to Moses: Write this down as a memorial in a book and give it into the ears of Jesus, because: With an obliteration I will obliterate the memorial of Amalek from under heaven.
Exodus 17:15 And Moses built an altar to the Lord and named its name My Lord Is Refuge,
Exodus 17:16 because with a hidden hand the Lord wages war upon Amalek from generations to generations.

## Chapter 18

Exodus 18:1 And Jothor the priest of Madiam, the father-in-law of Moses, heard everything that the Lord did for Israel his own people, for the Lord brought Israel out of Egypt.
Exodus 18:2 And Jothor the father-in-law of Moses took Sepphora the woman of Moses after her dismissal,
Exodus 18:3 and his two sons; the name of one of them was Gersam, saying: I was a sojourner in a foreign land.
Exodus 18:4 And the name of the second was Eliezer, saying: For the God of my father is my helper and rescued me from the hand of Pharao.
Exodus 18:5 And Jothor the father-in-law of Moses went out, and the sons and the woman, to Moses into the wilderness where he had encamped at the mountain of God.
Exodus 18:6 And it was reported to Moses, saying: Behold, Jothor your father-in-law is coming to you, and your woman and your two sons with him.
Exodus 18:7 And Moses went out to meet his father-in-law and bowed down to him and kissed him, and they greeted one another; and he brought him into the tent.
Exodus 18:8 And Moses related to his father-in-law everything that the Lord had done to Pharao and the Egyptians for the sake of Israel, and all the toil that had come to them on the way, and that the Lord rescued them from the hand of Pharao and from the hand of the Egyptians.
Exodus 18:9 And Jothor was astonished at all the good things that the Lord had done for them, that he rescued them from the hand of the Egyptians and from the hand of Pharao.
Exodus 18:10 And Jothor said: Blessed is the Lord, because he rescued his people from the hand of the Egyptians and from the hand of Pharao.
Exodus 18:11 Now I know that the Lord is great beyond all the gods, because of this, because they set themselves upon them.
Exodus 18:12 And Jothor the father-in-law of Moses took whole burnt offerings and sacrifices for God; and Aaron and all the elders of Israel came to eat bread together with the father-in-law of Moses before God.
Exodus 18:13 And it happened after the next day that Moses sat together to judge the people; and all the people stood beside Moses from morning until evening.
Exodus 18:14 And Jothor saw everything that he was doing for the people and says: What is this that you are doing for the people? Why do you sit alone, but all the people stand beside you from morning until afternoon?
Exodus 18:15 And Moses says to his father-in-law: Because the people come to me to seek judgment from God.
Exodus 18:16 For whenever a dispute comes to be for them and they come to me, I judge each and instruct them in the ordinances of God and his law.
Exodus 18:17 And the father-in-law of Moses said to him: You do not do this thing rightly.
Exodus 18:18 With destruction you will be utterly destroyed by something unbearable, both you and all this people who are with you. This matter is heavy for you; you will not be able to do it alone.
Exodus 18:19 Now therefore, listen to me, and I will counsel you, and God will be with you. You be for the people the things pertaining to God, and you shall bring their words to God.
Exodus 18:20 And you shall testify to them the ordinances of God and his law and indicate to them the ways in which they will journey and the works that they will do.
Exodus 18:21 And look out for yourself from all the people capable men who fear God, righteous men who hate pride, and you shall appoint them over them as rulers of thousands and rulers of hundreds and rulers of fifties and rulers of tens.
Exodus 18:22 And they will judge the people at every hour; but the weighty matter they will bring to you, and the short judgments they will judge themselves, and they will lighten it from you and help you.
Exodus 18:23 If you do this thing, God will strengthen you, and you will be able to stand, and all this people will come to their own place with peace.
Exodus 18:24 And Moses listened to the voice of his father-in-law and did as many things as he told him.
Exodus 18:25 And Moses chose capable men from all Israel and made them rulers of thousands and rulers of hundreds and rulers of fifties and rulers of tens over them.
Exodus 18:26 And they judged the people at every hour; but every weighty matter they brought to Moses, and every light matter they judged themselves.
Exodus 18:27 And Moses sent his own father-in-law away, and he went away into his land.

## Chapter 19

Exodus 19:1 And in the third month of the exodus of the sons of Israel from the land of Egypt, on this day, they came into the wilderness of Sina.
Exodus 19:2 And they departed from Raphidin and came into the wilderness of Sina, and Israel encamped there opposite the mountain.
Exodus 19:3 And Moses went up into the mountain of God; and God called him from the mountain, saying: Thus you shall speak to the house of Jacob and report to the sons of Israel:
Exodus 19:4 You yourselves have seen as many things as I have done to the Egyptians, and I took you up as though upon wings of eagles and brought you to myself.
Exodus 19:5 And now, if by hearing you hear my voice and keep my covenant, you will be for me a peculiar people from all the nations, for all the earth is mine.
Exodus 19:6 And you will be for me a royal priesthood and a holy nation. These are the words that you shall speak to the sons of Israel.
Exodus 19:7 And Moses came and called the elders of the people and set before them all these words that God had commanded him.
Exodus 19:8 And all the people answered with one accord and said: Everything that God said we will do, and we will hear. And Moses brought the words of the people to God.
Exodus 19:9 And the Lord said to Moses: Behold, I am coming to you in a pillar of cloud, so that the people may hear me speaking to you and may believe you forever. And Moses reported the words of the people to the Lord.
Exodus 19:10 And the Lord said to Moses: Go down and testify to the people and purify them today and tomorrow, and let them wash their garments.
Exodus 19:11 And let them be ready for the third day, for on the third day the Lord will come down upon Mount Sina before all the people.
Exodus 19:12 And you shall mark off the people all around, saying: Take heed to yourselves not to go up into the mountain or touch any part of it; everyone who touches the mountain will die by death.
Exodus 19:13 A hand shall not touch him, for he will be stoned with stones or shot down with a missile; whether livestock animal or human, he shall not live. When the voices and the trumpets and the cloud depart from the mountain, those shall go up upon the mountain.
Exodus 19:14 And Moses went down from the mountain to the people and sanctified them, and they washed their garments.
Exodus 19:15 And he said to the people: Become ready for three days; do not approach a woman.
Exodus 19:16 And it happened on the third day, when it became near dawn, that there were voices and lightning and a dark cloud upon Mount Sina; the sound of the trumpet sounded loudly, and all the people in the encampment were terrified.
Exodus 19:17 And Moses brought the people out from the encampment to meet God, and they stood beneath the mountain.
Exodus 19:18 And all Mount Sina was smoking because God had come down upon it in fire, and the smoke was rising like the smoke of a furnace, and all the people were exceedingly astonished.
Exodus 19:19 And the sounds of the trumpet were advancing, exceedingly stronger; Moses was speaking, and God was answering him by a voice.
Exodus 19:20 And the Lord came down upon Mount Sina, upon the top of the mountain; and the Lord called Moses to the top of the mountain, and Moses went up.
Exodus 19:21 And God spoke to Moses, saying: Go down and testify to the people, lest they draw near to God to observe and a multitude of them fall.
Exodus 19:22 And let the priests who draw near to the Lord God be sanctified, lest the Lord destroy some from among them.
Exodus 19:23 And Moses said to God: The people will not be able to go up to Mount Sina, for you testified to us, saying: Mark off the mountain and sanctify it.
Exodus 19:24 And the Lord said to him: Walk; go down and come up, you and Aaron with you. But let not the priests and the people force their way to go up to God, lest the Lord destroy some from among them.
Exodus 19:25 And Moses went down to the people and spoke to them.

## Chapter 20

Exodus 20:1 And the Lord spoke all these words, saying:
Exodus 20:2 I am the Lord your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt, out of a house of slavery.
Exodus 20:3 There shall be no other gods for you except me. –
Exodus 20:4 You shall not make for yourself an idol or any likeness of as many things as are in heaven above and as many things as are on the earth below and as many things as are in the waters beneath the earth.
Exodus 20:5 You shall not bow down to them, nor shall you ever serve them, for I am the Lord your God, a jealous God, repaying the sins of fathers upon children as far as the third and fourth generation to those who hate me,
Exodus 20:6 and doing mercy to thousands, to those who love me and those who keep my ordinances. –
Exodus 20:7 You shall not take the name of the Lord your God in vain, for the Lord will certainly not cleanse the one who takes his name in vain. –
Exodus 20:8 Remember the day of the sabbaths, to sanctify it.
Exodus 20:9 For six days you shall labor and do all your works.
Exodus 20:10 But on the seventh day are sabbaths to the Lord your God. You shall not do any work on it, you and your son and your daughter, your servant and your female servant, your ox and your draft animal and all your livestock and the proselyte who sojourns within you.
Exodus 20:11 For in six days the Lord made heaven and earth and the sea and everything in them, and he rested on the seventh day; because of this the Lord blessed the seventh day and sanctified it. –
Exodus 20:12 Honor your father and mother, so that it may become well for you and so that you may become long-lived upon the good land that the Lord your God gives you. –
Exodus 20:13 You shall not commit adultery. –
Exodus 20:14 You shall not steal. –
Exodus 20:15 You shall not murder. –
Exodus 20:16 You shall not bear false witness against your neighbor, false testimony. –
Exodus 20:17 You shall not desire the woman of your neighbor. You shall not desire the house of your neighbor, nor his field, nor his servant, nor his female servant, nor his ox, nor his draft animal, nor any of his livestock, nor as many things as belong to your neighbor.
Exodus 20:18 And all the people were seeing the voice and the flashes and the voice of the trumpet and the smoking mountain; and being afraid, all the people stood far away.
Exodus 20:19 And they said to Moses: You speak to us, and do not let God speak to us, lest we die.
Exodus 20:20 And Moses says to them: Take courage, for God has come to you for the sake of testing you, so that his fear may be among you, so that you do not sin.
Exodus 20:21 And the people stood far away, but Moses entered into the gloom where God was.
Exodus 20:22 And the Lord said to Moses: Thus you shall speak to the house of Jacob and report to the sons of Israel: You have seen that I have spoken to you from heaven.
Exodus 20:23 You shall not make silver gods for yourselves, and you shall not make golden gods for yourselves.
Exodus 20:24 You shall make an altar of earth for me and sacrifice upon it your whole burnt offerings and your salvation offerings, your sheep and your calves, in every place where I name my name there; and I will come to you and bless you.
Exodus 20:25 But if you make an altar of stones for me, you shall not build them hewn, for you have laid your dagger upon them, and they have been defiled.
Exodus 20:26 You shall not go up by steps upon my altar, so that you do not uncover your indecency upon it.

## Chapter 21

Exodus 21:1 And these are the ordinances which you shall set before them.
Exodus 21:2 If you acquire a Hebrew servant, he shall serve you six years; but in the seventh year he shall go away free, without payment.
Exodus 21:3 If he enters alone, he shall also go out alone; but if a woman enters with him, the woman shall also go out with him.
Exodus 21:4 But if his master gives him a woman, and she bears him sons or daughters, the woman and the children shall belong to his master, but he alone shall go out.
Exodus 21:5 But if the servant, answering, says: I have loved my master and the woman and the children; I do not run away free;
Exodus 21:6 his master shall bring him to the judgment seat of God and then shall bring him to the door, to the doorpost, and his master shall pierce his ear with the awl, and he shall serve him for the age. –
Exodus 21:7 But if anyone sells his own daughter as a household servant, she shall not go away as the female slaves run away.
Exodus 21:8 If she does not please her master, to whom he had agreed upon her for himself, he shall ransom her; but he has no authority to sell her to a foreign nation, because he dealt faithlessly with her.
Exodus 21:9 But if he agrees upon her for his son, he shall do for her according to the ordinance of daughters.
Exodus 21:10 But if he takes another for himself, he shall not deprive her of what is due, her clothing, and her marital intercourse.
Exodus 21:11 But if he does not do these three things for her, she shall go out freely, without silver.
Exodus 21:12 But if anyone strikes someone and he dies, he shall be put to death by death;
Exodus 21:13 but if he did not do it willingly, but God delivered him into his hands, I will give you a place to which the killer shall flee.
Exodus 21:14 But if anyone sets upon his neighbor to kill him by deceit and seeks refuge, you shall take him from my altar to put him to death. –
Exodus 21:15 Whoever strikes his father or his mother shall be put to death by death.
Exodus 21:16 Whoever speaks evil of his father or his mother shall end by death. –
Exodus 21:17 Whoever steals someone from the sons of Israel and, having overpowered him, sells him, and he is found with him, let him end by death. –
Exodus 21:18 But if two men revile one another and someone strikes his neighbor with a stone or with his fist, and he does not die but is laid upon the bed,
Exodus 21:19 if the man rises up and walks outside upon a staff, the one who struck him shall be guiltless; only he shall repay his lost time and the medical expenses. –
Exodus 21:20 But if anyone strikes his servant or his female servant with a rod, and he dies under his hands, vengeance shall be exacted by judgment.
Exodus 21:21 But if he survives one day or two, he shall not be avenged, for he is his silver. –
Exodus 21:22 But if two men fight and strike a woman who has a child in the womb, and her child comes out not fully formed, he shall be fined with a fine; whatever the woman’s husband imposes, he shall give according to assessment;
Exodus 21:23 but if it was fully formed, he shall give life in exchange for life,
Exodus 21:24 eye in exchange for eye, tooth in exchange for tooth, hand in exchange for hand, foot in exchange for foot,
Exodus 21:25 burn in exchange for burn, wound in exchange for wound, bruise in exchange for bruise. –
Exodus 21:26 But if anyone strikes the eye of his household servant or the eye of his female attendant and blinds it, he shall send them away free in exchange for their eye.
Exodus 21:27 But if he knocks out the tooth of his household servant or the tooth of his female attendant, he shall send them away free in exchange for their tooth.
Exodus 21:28 But if an ox gores a man or a woman and the person dies, the ox shall be stoned with stones, and its flesh shall not be eaten; but the master of the ox shall be guiltless.
Exodus 21:29 But if the ox was a gorer before yesterday and before the third day, and they testify to its master, and he does not remove it, but it kills a man or a woman, the ox shall be stoned, and its master shall also die.
Exodus 21:30 But if a ransom is imposed upon him, he shall give a ransom for his soul, as much as they impose upon him.
Exodus 21:31 But if it gores a son or a daughter, they shall do to him according to this ordinance.
Exodus 21:32 But if the ox gores a servant or a female servant, he shall give their master thirty didrachmas of silver, and the ox shall be stoned. –
Exodus 21:33 But if anyone opens a pit or quarries a pit and does not cover it, and a calf or a donkey falls there,
Exodus 21:34 the master of the pit shall repay; he shall give silver to their master, but the dead animal shall be his. –
Exodus 21:35 But if anyone’s ox gores his neighbor’s ox and it dies, they shall sell the living ox and divide its silver, and they shall divide the dead ox.
Exodus 21:36 But if the ox is known to be a gorer before yesterday and before the third day, and they have testified to its master, and he does not remove it, he shall repay ox in exchange for ox, but the dead one shall be his.
Exodus 21:37 But if anyone steals a calf or a sheep and slaughters it or sells it, he shall repay five calves in exchange for the calf and four sheep in exchange for the sheep.

## Chapter 22

Exodus 22:1 But if the thief is found in the breaking-in and, being struck, dies, there is no bloodguilt for him;
Exodus 22:2 but if the sun rises upon him, he is guilty and shall die in return. But if he has nothing, let him be sold in exchange for the theft.
Exodus 22:3 But if he is caught and the stolen thing is found alive in his hand, from a donkey as far as a sheep, he shall repay them double. –
Exodus 22:4 But if anyone grazes down a field or a vineyard and lets his animal graze down another field, he shall repay from his field according to its produce; but if it grazes down the whole field, he shall repay the best of his field and the best of his vineyard. –
Exodus 22:5 But if fire goes out and finds thorns and sets fire to a threshing floor or ears of grain or a field, the one who kindled the fire shall repay. –
Exodus 22:6 But if anyone gives his neighbor silver or vessels to keep, and it is stolen from the man’s house, if the one who stole is found, he shall repay double;
Exodus 22:7 but if the one who stole is not found, the master of the house shall come before God and shall swear that surely he himself has not acted wickedly regarding the whole deposit of his neighbor.
Exodus 22:8 For every specified wrongdoing concerning calf and pack animal and sheep and garment and every loss that is alleged, whatever it may be, the judgment of both shall come before God, and the one convicted through God shall repay his neighbor double. –
Exodus 22:9 But if anyone gives his neighbor a pack animal or a calf or a sheep or any beast to keep, and it is broken or dies or becomes captive, and no one knows,
Exodus 22:10 there shall be an oath of God between both that surely he himself has not acted wickedly regarding the whole deposit of his neighbor; and thus its master shall accept it, and he shall not repay.
Exodus 22:11 But if it is stolen from him, he shall repay its master.
Exodus 22:12 But if it becomes caught by a beast, he shall bring it to the prey and shall not repay. –
Exodus 22:13 But if anyone borrows from his neighbor, and it is broken or dies or becomes captive, but its master is not with it, he shall repay;
Exodus 22:14 but if its master is with it, he shall not repay; but if it is hired, it shall be to him in exchange for its hire.
Exodus 22:15 But if anyone deceives an unbetrothed virgin and lies with her, with a dowry he shall endow her as a woman for himself.
Exodus 22:16 But if her father refuses with a refusal and is not willing to give her to him as a woman, he shall repay silver to the father according to the amount that is the dowry of virgins. –
Exodus 22:17 You shall not preserve sorcerers alive. –
Exodus 22:18 Everything that lies with livestock—you shall kill them by death. –
Exodus 22:19 The one who sacrifices to gods shall be destroyed by death, except to the Lord alone.
Exodus 22:20 And you shall not mistreat a resident alien, nor shall you oppress him; for you were resident aliens in the land of Egypt. –
Exodus 22:21 You shall not mistreat any widow or orphan;
Exodus 22:22 but if with wickedness you mistreat them and, crying out, they cry out to me, I will hear their voice with hearing,
Exodus 22:23 and I will be angry with wrath and kill you with the sword, and your women shall be widows and your children orphans. –
Exodus 22:24 But if you lend silver to your poor brother beside you, you shall not be one who presses him; you shall not impose interest upon him.
Exodus 22:25 But if you take your neighbor’s garment as a pledge, before the setting of the sun you shall return it to him;
Exodus 22:26 for this is his covering, this alone is the garment of his nakedness; in what will he sleep? Therefore, if he cries out to me, I will hear him, for I am merciful. –
Exodus 22:27 You shall not revile gods, and you shall not speak evil of rulers of your people. –
Exodus 22:28 You shall not delay the firstfruits of your threshing floor and winepress; you shall give me the firstborn of your sons.
Exodus 22:29 Thus you shall do with your calf and your sheep and your pack animal; seven days it shall be under its mother, but on the eighth day you shall give it to me. –
Exodus 22:30 And you shall be holy men to me. And you shall not eat flesh caught by a beast; cast it to the dog.

## Chapter 23

Exodus 23:1 You shall not accept a vain report. You shall not agree with the unjust person to become an unjust witness.
Exodus 23:2 You shall not be with the majority for evil. You shall not join with a multitude to turn aside with the majority, so as to pervert judgment.
Exodus 23:3 And you shall not show mercy to a poor person in judgment. –
Exodus 23:4 But if you encounter your enemy’s ox or his pack animal wandering, by turning it back you shall return it to him.
Exodus 23:5 But if you see your enemy’s pack animal fallen under its load, you shall not pass it by, but you shall raise it together with him. –
Exodus 23:6 You shall not distort the judgment of a poor person in his judgment.
Exodus 23:7 You shall withdraw from every unjust word; you shall not kill an innocent and righteous person, and you shall not justify the impious person because of gifts.
Exodus 23:8 And you shall not receive gifts, for gifts blind the eyes of those who see and ruin righteous words. –
Exodus 23:9 And you shall not oppress a resident alien; for you know the soul of the resident alien, for you yourselves were resident aliens in the land of Egypt.
Exodus 23:10 Six years you shall sow your land and gather its produce;
Exodus 23:11 but in the seventh you shall make a release and leave it, and the poor of your nation shall eat, and the wild beasts shall eat the things left over. Thus you shall do with your vineyard and your olive grove. –
Exodus 23:12 Six days you shall do your works, but on the seventh day there shall be rest, so that your ox and your pack animal may rest, and so that the son of your female servant and the resident alien may breathe. –
Exodus 23:13 Guard all the things that I have said to you. And you shall not remember the name of other gods, nor shall it be heard from your mouth.
Exodus 23:14 Three seasons of the year you shall keep a feast to me.
Exodus 23:15 Guard the feast of unleavened bread to perform it; seven days you shall eat unleavened bread, just as I commanded you, at the season of the month of the new things, for in it you came out of Egypt. You shall not appear before me empty.
Exodus 23:16 And you shall make the feast of harvest of the first produce of your works, whatever you sow in your field, and the feast of completion at the departure of the year, in the gathering of your works from your field.
Exodus 23:17 Three seasons of the year every male of yours shall appear before the Lord your God.
Exodus 23:18 For when I drive out nations from your presence and broaden your boundaries, you shall not sacrifice the blood of my sacrifice upon leaven, nor shall the fat of my feast sleep until morning.
Exodus 23:19 You shall bring the firstfruits of the first produce of your land into the house of the Lord your God. You shall not boil a lamb in its mother’s milk.
Exodus 23:20 And behold, I send my angel before your face, that he may guard you on the way, so that he may bring you into the land that I prepared for you.
Exodus 23:21 Attend to yourself and hear him, and do not disobey him; for he will certainly not withdraw from you, for my name is upon him.
