Leviticus 1:4 And he shall place his hand upon the head of the offering, acceptable for him to make atonement concerning him.
Leviticus 1:5 And they shall slaughter the calf before the Lord, and the sons of Aaron, the priests, shall bring the blood and pour the blood upon the altar all around, the one at the doors of the tabernacle of testimony.
Leviticus 1:6 And having skinned the whole burnt offering, they shall divide it limb by limb,
Leviticus 1:7 and the sons of Aaron, the priests, shall place fire upon the altar and heap wood upon the fire,
Leviticus 1:8 and the sons of Aaron, the priests, shall heap the divided parts and the head and the fat upon the wood that is upon the fire that is upon the altar,
Leviticus 1:9 but they shall wash the inward parts and the feet with water, and the priests shall place all the things upon the altar; it is an offering, a sacrifice, an odor of sweetness to the Lord.
Leviticus 1:10 But if his gift to the Lord is from the sheep, from the lambs or from the kids, as a whole burnt offering, he shall present it as an unblemished male and place his hand upon its head.
Leviticus 1:11 And they shall slaughter it beside the altar toward the north before the Lord, and the sons of Aaron, the priests, shall pour its blood upon the altar all around.
Leviticus 1:12 And they shall divide it limb by limb, and the head and the fat, and the priests shall heap them upon the wood that is upon the fire upon the altar.
Leviticus 1:13 And they shall wash the inward parts and the feet with water, and the priest shall bring all the things and place them upon the altar; it is an offering, a sacrifice, an odor of sweetness to the Lord.
Leviticus 1:14 But if you offer an offering from the flying creatures as a gift to the Lord, then he shall bring his gift from the turtledoves or from the pigeons.
Leviticus 1:15 And the priest shall bring it to the altar and pinch off the head, and the priest shall place it upon the altar and drain the blood toward the base of the altar.
Leviticus 1:16 And he shall remove the crop together with the feathers and cast it beside the altar toward the east, into the place of the ashes.
Leviticus 1:17 And he shall break it from the wings and shall not divide it, and the priest shall place it upon the altar upon the wood that is upon the fire; it is an offering, a sacrifice, an odor of sweetness to the Lord.

## Chapter 2

Leviticus 2:1 But if a soul offers a gift, a sacrifice to the Lord, his gift shall be fine flour, and he shall pour oil upon it and place frankincense upon it; it is a sacrifice.
Leviticus 2:2 And he shall bring it to the sons of Aaron, the priests, and taking from it a handful full of the fine flour together with the oil and all its frankincense, the priest shall place its memorial upon the altar; a sacrifice, an odor of sweetness to the Lord.
Leviticus 2:3 And the remainder from the sacrifice shall be for Aaron and his sons; Holy of Holies from the sacrifices of the Lord. –
Leviticus 2:4 But if you offer a gift, a sacrifice baked in an oven, a gift to the Lord from fine flour, it shall be unleavened loaves mixed with oil and unleavened flatcakes anointed throughout with oil. –
Leviticus 2:5 But if your gift is a sacrifice from a pan, it shall be fine flour mixed with oil, unleavened;
Leviticus 2:6 and you shall break them into pieces and pour oil upon them; it is a sacrifice to the Lord. –
Leviticus 2:7 But if your gift is a sacrifice from a grate, fine flour shall be made with oil.
Leviticus 2:8 And he shall bring the sacrifice that he makes from these things to the Lord; and he shall bring it to the priest, and approaching the altar,
Leviticus 2:9 the priest shall remove its memorial from the sacrifice, and the priest shall place it upon the altar; an offering, an odor of sweetness to the Lord.
Leviticus 2:10 But the thing remaining from the sacrifice shall be for Aaron and his sons; Holy of Holies from the offerings of the Lord.
Leviticus 2:11 Every sacrifice that you offer to the Lord you shall not make leavened; for you shall not bring any leaven or any honey from it to offer to the Lord.
Leviticus 2:12 As a gift of firstfruit you shall bring them to the Lord, but it shall not be brought up upon the altar as an odor of sweetness to the Lord.
Leviticus 2:13 And every gift of your sacrifice shall be salted with salt; you shall not cease the salt of the covenant of the Lord from your sacrifices; upon every gift of yours you shall bring salt to the Lord your God. –
Leviticus 2:14 But if you offer a sacrifice of first produce to the Lord, new roasted groats, pounded, to the Lord, then you shall bring the sacrifice of the first produce,
Leviticus 2:15 and you shall pour oil upon it and place frankincense upon it; it is a sacrifice.
Leviticus 2:16 And the priest shall offer its memorial from the groats together with the oil and all its frankincense; it is an offering to the Lord.

## Chapter 3

Leviticus 3:1 But if his gift to the Lord is a sacrifice of salvation, if he presents it from his cattle, whether male or female, he shall present it unblemished before the Lord.
Leviticus 3:2 And he shall place his hands upon the head of the gift and slaughter it beside the doors of the tabernacle of testimony, and the sons of Aaron, the priests, shall pour the blood upon the altar of whole burnt offerings all around.
Leviticus 3:3 And they shall present from the sacrifice of salvation an offering to the Lord: the fat covering the belly and all the fat upon the belly,
Leviticus 3:4 and the two kidneys and the fat upon them that is upon the thighs and the lobe upon the liver [together with the kidneys he shall remove it],
Leviticus 3:5 and the sons of Aaron, the priests, shall offer them upon the altar, upon the whole burnt offerings, upon the wood that is upon the fire upon the altar; an offering, an odor of sweetness to the Lord.
Leviticus 3:6 But if his gift is from the sheep, a sacrifice of salvation to the Lord, he shall bring it, male or female, unblemished.
Leviticus 3:7 If he presents a lamb as his gift, he shall present it before the Lord,
Leviticus 3:8 and he shall place his hands upon the head of his gift and slaughter it beside the doors of the tabernacle of testimony, and the sons of Aaron, the priests, shall pour the blood upon the altar all around.
Leviticus 3:9 And he shall bring from the sacrifice of salvation an offering to God: the fat and the unblemished loin [together with the loin muscles he shall remove it] and the fat of the belly,
Leviticus 3:10 and both kidneys and the fat upon them that is upon the thighs and the lobe upon the liver [removing it together with the kidneys],
Leviticus 3:11 the priest shall offer it upon the altar; an odor of sweetness, an offering to the Lord.
Leviticus 3:12 But if his gift is from the goats, then he shall present it before the Lord,
Leviticus 3:13 and he shall place his hands upon its head, and they shall slaughter it before the Lord beside the doors of the tabernacle of testimony, and the sons of Aaron, the priests, shall pour the blood upon the altar all around.
Leviticus 3:14 And he shall offer from it an offering to the Lord: the fat covering the belly and all the fat upon the belly,
Leviticus 3:15 and both kidneys and all the fat upon them that is upon the thighs and the lobe of the liver [together with the kidneys he shall remove it],
Leviticus 3:16 and the priest shall offer it upon the altar; an offering, an odor of sweetness to the Lord. All the fat belongs to the Lord;
Leviticus 3:17 an ordinance for the age for your generations in every dwelling of yours: you shall not eat any fat or any blood.

## Chapter 4

Leviticus 4:1 And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying:
Leviticus 4:2 Speak to the sons of Israel, saying: If a soul sins involuntarily before the Lord from the ordinances of the Lord that ought not to be done, and does any one of them;
Leviticus 4:3 if the anointed high priest sins so that the people sin, then for his sin that he sinned he shall present an unblemished calf from the cattle to the Lord for his sin.
Leviticus 4:4 And he shall present the calf beside the door of the tabernacle of testimony before the Lord and place his hand upon the head of the calf before the Lord and slaughter the calf before the Lord.
Leviticus 4:5 And the anointed priest whose hands have been perfected, taking from the blood of the calf, shall bring it into the tabernacle of testimony;
Leviticus 4:6 and the priest shall dip his finger into the blood and sprinkle from the blood seven times before the Lord, along the holy veil;
Leviticus 4:7 and the priest shall place some of the blood of the calf upon the horns of the altar of compound incense before the Lord, which is in the tabernacle of testimony; and all the blood of the calf he shall pour out beside the base of the altar of whole burnt offerings, which is beside the doors of the tabernacle of testimony.
Leviticus 4:8 And he shall remove from it all the fat of the calf of sin: the fat covering the inward parts and all the fat upon the inward parts,
Leviticus 4:9 and the two kidneys and the fat upon them that is upon the thighs and the lobe upon the liver [together with the kidneys he shall remove it],
Leviticus 4:10 in the manner that it is removed from the calf of the sacrifice of salvation, and the priest shall offer it upon the altar of offering.
Leviticus 4:11 And the skin of the calf and all its flesh together with the head and the extremities and the belly and the dung,
Leviticus 4:12 and they shall carry the whole calf outside the camp into a clean place, where they pour out the ashes, and burn it upon wood with fire; it shall be burned upon the outpouring of the ashes.
Leviticus 4:13 But if the whole congregation of Israel is involuntarily ignorant and a matter escapes the eyes of the congregation, and they do one of all the commandments of the Lord that shall not be done, and they trespass,
Leviticus 4:14 and the sin in which they sinned becomes known to them, then the congregation shall present an unblemished calf from the cattle for the sin and present it beside the doors of the tabernacle of testimony.
Leviticus 4:15 And the elders of the congregation shall place their hands upon the head of the calf before the Lord and shall slaughter the calf before the Lord.
Leviticus 4:16 And the anointed priest shall bring some of the blood of the calf into the tabernacle of testimony;
Leviticus 4:17 and the priest shall dip his finger into some of the blood of the calf and sprinkle seven times before the Lord, directly before the veil of the holy place;
Leviticus 4:18 and the priest shall place some of the blood upon the horns of the altar of compound incense offerings that is before the Lord, which is in the tabernacle of testimony; and all the blood he shall pour toward the base of the altar of offerings that is beside the door of the tabernacle of testimony.
Leviticus 4:19 And he shall remove all the fat from it and offer it upon the altar;
Leviticus 4:20 and he shall do with the calf in the manner that he did with the calf of sin, thus it shall be done; and the priest shall make atonement concerning them, and the sin shall be forgiven them.
Leviticus 4:21 And they shall carry the whole calf outside the camp and burn the calf in the manner that they burned the former calf. It is the sin of the congregation.
Leviticus 4:22 But if the ruler sins and involuntarily does one of all the commandments of the Lord their God that shall not be done, and sins and trespasses,
Leviticus 4:23 and the sin in which he sinned becomes known to him, then he shall bring his gift, a male kid from the goats, unblemished.
Leviticus 4:24 And he shall place his hand upon the head of the kid, and they shall slaughter it in the place where they slaughter the whole burnt offerings before the Lord; it is sin.
Leviticus 4:25 And the priest shall place some of the blood of the thing of sin with his finger upon the horns of the altar of whole burnt offerings; and all its blood he shall pour out beside the base of the altar of whole burnt offerings.
Leviticus 4:26 And he shall offer all its fat upon the altar, like the fat of a sacrifice of salvation. And the priest shall make atonement concerning him from his sin, and it shall be forgiven him.
Leviticus 4:27 But if one soul from the people of the land sins involuntarily by doing one of all the commandments of the Lord that shall not be done, and trespasses,
Leviticus 4:28 and the sin in which he sinned becomes known to him, then he shall bring a female kid from the goats, unblemished; he shall bring it for the sin that he sinned.
Leviticus 4:29 And he shall place his hand upon the head of his sin, and they shall slaughter the she-goat of sin in the place where they slaughter the whole burnt offerings.
Leviticus 4:30 And the priest shall take some of its blood with his finger and place it upon the horns of the altar of whole burnt offerings; and all its blood he shall pour out beside the base of the altar.
Leviticus 4:31 And he shall remove all the fat in the manner that fat is removed from a sacrifice of salvation, and the priest shall offer it upon the altar for an odor of sweetness to the Lord. And the priest shall make atonement concerning him, and it shall be forgiven him. –
Leviticus 4:32 But if he presents a sheep as his gift for sin, he shall bring it as an unblemished female.
Leviticus 4:33 And he shall place his hand upon the head of the thing of sin, and they shall slaughter it in the place where they slaughter the whole burnt offerings.
Leviticus 4:34 And the priest, taking some of the blood of the thing of sin with his finger, shall place it upon the horns of the altar of whole burnt offering; and all its blood he shall pour out beside the base of the altar of whole burnt offering.
Leviticus 4:35 And he shall remove all its fat in the manner that the fat of a sheep is removed from the sacrifice of salvation, and the priest shall place it upon the altar, upon the whole burnt offering of the Lord. And the priest shall make atonement concerning him for the sin that he sinned, and it shall be forgiven him.

## Chapter 5

Leviticus 5:1 But if a soul sins and hears the voice of an oath, and he is a witness [either he saw or knows], if he does not report it, he shall bear the sin;
Leviticus 5:2 or a soul that touches any unclean thing, whether an unclean carcass or an unclean thing caught by a beast or any of the carcasses or any of the unclean abominations or any of the carcasses of unclean livestock,
Leviticus 5:3 or touches any human uncleanness, any of his uncleanness by which, having touched it, he is defiled, and it escapes him, but after this he knows and trespasses,
Leviticus 5:4 or a soul that swears, defining with the lips to do evil or to do good according to anything a man defines with an oath, and it escapes him before his eyes, and he knows and sins in any one of these,
Leviticus 5:5 then he shall declare openly the sin concerning the things in which he sinned against it,
Leviticus 5:6 and for the things in which he trespassed he shall bring to the Lord, for the sin that he sinned, a female from the sheep, a ewe lamb or a she-goat from the goats, for sin; and the priest shall make atonement concerning him for his sin that he sinned, and the sin shall be forgiven him.
Leviticus 5:7 But if his hand is not strong enough for what is sufficient for a sheep, he shall bring for his sin that he sinned two turtledoves or two young pigeons to the Lord, one for sin and one as a whole burnt offering.
Leviticus 5:8 And he shall bring them to the priest, and the priest shall present the one for sin first; and the priest shall pinch off its head from the neck and shall not divide it;
Leviticus 5:9 and he shall sprinkle some of the blood of the thing for sin upon the wall of the altar, but the remainder of the blood he shall drain down upon the base of the altar; for it is of sin.
Leviticus 5:10 And he shall make the second a whole burnt offering, as is fitting. And the priest shall make atonement concerning his sin that he sinned, and it shall be forgiven him. –
Leviticus 5:11 But if his hand does not find a pair of turtledoves or two young pigeons, then he shall bring his gift for that in which he sinned, a tenth of an oiphi of fine flour for sin; he shall not pour oil upon it or place frankincense upon it, because it is for sin;
Leviticus 5:12 and he shall bring it to the priest. And the priest, taking from it a handful full, shall place its memorial upon the altar of whole burnt offerings to the Lord; it is sin.
Leviticus 5:13 And the priest shall make atonement concerning him for his sin that he sinned in any one of these, and it shall be forgiven him. But the thing remaining shall be for the priest, like the sacrifice of fine flour.
Leviticus 5:14 And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying:
Leviticus 5:15 If forgetfulness escapes a soul and he sins involuntarily from the holy things of the Lord, then for his trespass he shall bring to the Lord an unblemished ram from the sheep, of a value in silver shekels according to the shekel of the holy things, for that in which he trespassed.
Leviticus 5:16 And that in which he sinned from the holy things, he shall repay it and add the fifth part upon it and give it to the priest; and the priest shall make atonement concerning him with the ram of trespass, and it shall be forgiven him.
Leviticus 5:17 And the soul that sins and does one of all the commandments of the Lord that ought not to be done, and did not know, and trespasses and bears the sin,
Leviticus 5:18 shall bring an unblemished ram from the sheep, of a value in silver, for trespass, to the priest; and the priest shall make atonement concerning him for his ignorance in which he was ignorant and he himself did not know, and it shall be forgiven him;
Leviticus 5:19 for he trespassed a trespass before the Lord.
Leviticus 5:20 And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying:
Leviticus 5:21 If a soul sins and, overlooking, overlooks the commandments of the Lord, and lies in matters concerning his neighbor, concerning a deposit or concerning partnership or concerning robbery, or wrongs his neighbor in anything,
Leviticus 5:22 or finds a lost thing and lies concerning it and swears unjustly concerning any one of all the things a man may do so as to sin in these,
Leviticus 5:23 then it shall be, whenever he sins and trespasses, that he shall return the thing stolen that he stole, or the wrong by which he wronged, or the deposit that was entrusted to him, or the lost thing that he found,
Leviticus 5:24 from every matter concerning which he swore unjustly, and he shall repay the principal and add the fifth part upon it; to whomever it belongs, to him he shall return it on the day when he is convicted.
Leviticus 5:25 And for his trespass he shall bring to the Lord an unblemished ram from the sheep, of a value for that in which he trespassed against him.
Leviticus 5:26 And the priest shall make atonement concerning him before the Lord, and it shall be forgiven him concerning any one of all the things that he did and trespassed against him.

## Chapter 6

Leviticus 6:1 And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying:
Leviticus 6:2 Command Aaron and his sons, saying: This is the law of the whole burnt offering. This whole burnt offering shall be upon its burning upon the altar the whole night until morning, and the fire of the altar shall burn upon it; it shall not be extinguished.
Leviticus 6:3 And the priest shall put on a linen tunic and shall put linen breeches around his body and shall remove the consumed offering that the fire consumes from the whole burnt offering from the altar and place it beside the altar.
Leviticus 6:4 And he shall take off his vestment and put on another vestment and carry the consumed offering outside the camp into a clean place.
Leviticus 6:5 And fire shall burn upon the altar from it and shall not be extinguished, and the priest shall burn wood upon it in the morning and heap the whole burnt offering upon it and place upon it the fat of the salvation offering;
Leviticus 6:6 and fire shall burn continually upon the altar; it shall not be extinguished.
Leviticus 6:7 This is the law of the sacrifice that the sons of Aaron shall present before the Lord opposite the altar;
Leviticus 6:8 and he shall remove from it with a handful some of the fine flour of the sacrifice, together with its oil and together with its frankincense that are upon the sacrifice, and shall offer it upon the altar as an offering; an odor of sweetness, its memorial to the Lord.
Leviticus 6:9 But Aaron and his sons shall eat the thing remaining from it; it shall be eaten unleavened in a holy place; in the court of the tabernacle of testimony they shall eat it.
Leviticus 6:10 It shall not be baked leavened; I have given it to them as a portion from the offerings of the Lord; Holy of Holies, like the thing of sin and like the thing of trespass.
Leviticus 6:11 Every male of the priests shall eat it; an eternal ordinance for your generations from the offerings of the Lord. Everyone who touches them shall be sanctified.
Leviticus 6:12 And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying:
Leviticus 6:13 This is the gift of Aaron and his sons that they shall bring to the Lord on the day when you anoint him: a tenth of an oiphi of fine flour as a sacrifice continually, half of it in the morning and half of it in the evening.
Leviticus 6:14 It shall be made upon a pan with oil; mixed, you shall bring it, rolled, a sacrifice from pieces, a sacrifice as an odor of sweetness to the Lord.
Leviticus 6:15 The anointed priest in his place from among his sons shall make it; an eternal law, the whole shall be fully offered.
Leviticus 6:16 And every sacrifice of a priest shall be entirely burned and shall not be eaten.
Leviticus 6:17 And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying:
Leviticus 6:18 Speak to Aaron and his sons, saying: This is the law of sin. In the place where they slaughter the whole burnt offering, they shall slaughter the things for sin before the Lord; it is Holy of Holies.
Leviticus 6:19 The priest who offers it shall eat it; it shall be eaten in a holy place, in the court of the tabernacle of testimony.
Leviticus 6:20 Everyone who touches its flesh shall be sanctified; and whatever garment is sprinkled from its blood, the thing sprinkled upon it shall be washed in a holy place.
Leviticus 6:21 And an earthen vessel in which it is boiled shall be shattered; but if it is boiled in a bronze vessel, he shall scour it out and rinse it with water.
Leviticus 6:22 Every male among the priests shall eat them; it is Holy of Holies of the Lord.
Leviticus 6:23 And none of the things for sin, from whose blood any is brought into the tabernacle of testimony to make atonement in the holy place, shall be eaten; it shall be burned with fire.

## Chapter 7

Leviticus 7:1 And this is the law of the ram for trespass; it is Holy of Holies.
Leviticus 7:2 In the place where they slaughter the whole burnt offering, they shall slaughter the ram of trespass before the Lord, and he shall pour the blood upon the base of the altar all around.
Leviticus 7:3 And he shall bring from it all its fat, and the loin and all the fat covering the inward parts and all the fat upon the inward parts,
Leviticus 7:4 and the two kidneys and the fat upon them that is upon the thighs and the lobe upon the liver [together with the kidneys he shall remove them],
Leviticus 7:5 and the priest shall offer them upon the altar as an offering to the Lord; it is for trespass.
Leviticus 7:6 Every male from the priests shall eat them; in a holy place they shall eat them; it is Holy of Holies.
Leviticus 7:7 As the thing for sin, so also the thing of trespass; there is one law for them; it shall belong to the priest who makes atonement with it.
Leviticus 7:8 And the priest who presents a man’s whole burnt offering, the skin of the whole burnt offering that he himself offers shall belong to him.
Leviticus 7:9 And every sacrifice that is made in the oven, and every one that is made upon a grate or upon a pan, shall belong to the priest who offers it.
Leviticus 7:10 And every sacrifice mixed with oil and not mixed shall belong to all the sons of Aaron, an equal share to each.
Leviticus 7:11 This is the law of a sacrifice of salvation that they shall bring to the Lord.
Leviticus 7:12 If he offers it for praise, then upon the sacrifice of praise he shall bring loaves from fine flour mixed with oil, unleavened flatcakes anointed throughout with oil, and fine flour mixed with oil;
Leviticus 7:13 with leavened loaves he shall bring his gifts upon a sacrifice of praise of salvation.
Leviticus 7:14 And he shall present one from all his gifts as a removal offering to the Lord; it shall belong to the priest who pours the blood of the salvation offering.
Leviticus 7:15 And the flesh of a sacrifice of praise of salvation shall belong to him, and it shall be eaten on the day on which it is given; they shall not leave any of it until morning.
Leviticus 7:16 And if he sacrifices his gift as a vow or a voluntary gift, it shall be eaten on the day on which he presents his sacrifice and on the morrow;
Leviticus 7:17 and the thing remaining from the flesh of the sacrifice until the third day shall be burned with fire.
Leviticus 7:18 But if, eating, he eats from the flesh on the third day, it shall not be accepted for the one who offers it, it shall not be reckoned to him; it is a defilement; and the soul that eats from it shall bear the sin.
Leviticus 7:19 And any flesh that touches anything unclean shall not be eaten; it shall be burned with fire. Everyone clean shall eat flesh.
Leviticus 7:20 But the soul that eats from the flesh of the sacrifice of salvation that belongs to the Lord while his uncleanness is upon him, that soul shall perish from his people.
Leviticus 7:21 And a soul that touches any unclean thing, whether from human uncleanness or from unclean quadrupeds or from any unclean abomination, and eats from the flesh of the sacrifice of salvation that belongs to the Lord, that soul shall perish from his people.
Leviticus 7:22 And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying:
Leviticus 7:23 Speak to the sons of Israel, saying: You shall not eat any fat of cattle and sheep and goats.
Leviticus 7:24 And fat from carcasses and from what is caught by a beast may be used for any work, but it shall not be eaten as food.
Leviticus 7:25 Everyone who eats fat from the livestock from which he brings an offering to the Lord, that soul shall perish from his people.
Leviticus 7:26 You shall not eat any blood in any of your dwellings, whether from flying creatures or from livestock.
Leviticus 7:27 Every soul that eats blood, that soul shall perish from his people.
Leviticus 7:28 And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying:
Leviticus 7:29 And you shall speak to the sons of Israel, saying: The one who offers a sacrifice of salvation to the Lord shall bring his gift to the Lord from the sacrifice of salvation.
Leviticus 7:30 His hands shall bring the offerings to the Lord; the fat upon the breast and the lobe of the liver, he shall bring them so as to place a gift before the Lord.
Leviticus 7:31 And the priest shall offer the fat upon the altar, and the breast shall belong to Aaron and his sons.
Leviticus 7:32 And you shall give the right arm as a removal offering to the priest from your sacrifices of salvation;
Leviticus 7:33 the one from the sons of Aaron who offers the blood of the salvation offering and the fat, the right arm shall be a portion for him.
Leviticus 7:34 For I have taken the breast of the placement and the arm of the removal offering from the sons of Israel, from your sacrifices of salvation, and have given them to Aaron the priest and his sons as an eternal ordinance from the sons of Israel.
Leviticus 7:35 This is the anointing of Aaron and the anointing of his sons from the offerings of the Lord on the day when he brought them near to serve the Lord as priests,
Leviticus 7:36 just as the Lord commanded to give them on the day when he anointed them, from the sons of Israel; an eternal ordinance for their generations.
Leviticus 7:37 This is the law of the whole burnt offerings and sacrifice and the thing for sin and the thing of trespass and the perfection and the sacrifice of salvation,
Leviticus 7:38 in the manner that the Lord commanded Moses on Mount Sina on the day when he commanded the sons of Israel to bring their gifts before the Lord in the wilderness of Sina.

## Chapter 8

Leviticus 8:1 And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying:
Leviticus 8:2 Take Aaron and his sons and his vestments and the oil of anointing and the calf for sin and the two rams and the basket of unleavened things,
Leviticus 8:3 and assemble the whole congregation at the door of the tabernacle of testimony.
Leviticus 8:4 And Moses did in the manner that the Lord commanded him, and he assembled the congregation at the door of the tabernacle of testimony.
Leviticus 8:5 And Moses said to the congregation: This is the word that the Lord commanded to be done.
Leviticus 8:6 And Moses brought Aaron and his sons near and washed them with water;
Leviticus 8:7 and he clothed him with the tunic and girded him with the sash and clothed him with the undergarment and placed the shoulder piece upon him and bound him according to the workmanship of the shoulder piece and fastened him with it;
Leviticus 8:8 and he placed the oracle upon it and placed the Manifestation and the Truth upon the oracle;
Leviticus 8:9 and he placed the miter upon his head and placed upon the miter, toward his face, the golden plate, the sanctified holy thing, in the manner that the Lord commanded Moses.
Leviticus 8:10 And Moses took from the oil of anointing,
Leviticus 8:11 and sprinkled some of it upon the altar seven times and anointed the altar and sanctified it and all its vessels and the washing basin and its base and sanctified them; and he anointed the tabernacle and all the things in it and sanctified it.
Leviticus 8:12 And Moses poured some of the oil of anointing upon the head of Aaron and anointed him and sanctified him.
Leviticus 8:13 And Moses brought the sons of Aaron near and clothed them with tunics and girded them with sashes and placed turbans around them, just as the Lord commanded Moses.
Leviticus 8:14 And Moses brought the calf for sin near, and Aaron and his sons placed their hands upon the head of the calf of sin.
Leviticus 8:15 And he slaughtered it, and Moses took some of the blood and placed it upon the horns of the altar all around with his finger and cleansed the altar; and he poured the blood upon the base of the altar and sanctified it, to make atonement upon it.
Leviticus 8:16 And Moses took all the fat upon the inward parts and the lobe upon the liver and both kidneys and the fat upon them, and Moses offered them upon the altar;
Leviticus 8:17 and the calf and its hide and its flesh and its dung, and he burned them with fire outside the camp, in the manner that the Lord commanded Moses.
Leviticus 8:18 And Moses brought near the ram for a whole burnt offering, and Aaron and his sons placed their hands upon the head of the ram.
Leviticus 8:19 And Moses slaughtered the ram, and Moses poured the blood upon the altar all around.
Leviticus 8:20 And he cut the ram into flesh limb by limb, and Moses offered the head and the limbs and the fat;
Leviticus 8:21 and he washed the belly and the feet with water, and Moses offered the whole ram upon the altar; a whole burnt offering, which is for an odor of sweetness, it is an offering to the Lord, just as the Lord commanded Moses.
Leviticus 8:22 And Moses brought the second ram near, a ram of perfection; and Aaron and his sons placed their hands upon the head of the ram.
Leviticus 8:23 And he slaughtered it, and Moses took some of its blood and placed it upon the lobe of Aaron’s right ear and upon the tip of his right hand and upon the tip of his right foot.
Leviticus 8:24 And Moses brought the sons of Aaron near, and Moses placed some of the blood upon the lobes of their right ears and upon the tips of their right hands and upon the tips of their right feet, and Moses poured the blood upon the altar all around.
Leviticus 8:25 And he took the fat and the loin and the fat upon the belly and the lobe of the liver and the two kidneys and the fat upon them and the right arm;
Leviticus 8:26 and from the basket of perfection that was before the Lord he took one unleavened loaf and one loaf made with oil and one flatcake and placed them upon the fat and the right arm;
Leviticus 8:27 and he placed all the things upon the hands of Aaron and upon the hands of his sons and offered them as a removal offering before the Lord.
Leviticus 8:28 And Moses took them from their hands, and Moses offered them upon the altar, upon the whole burnt offering of perfection, which is an odor of sweetness; it is an offering to the Lord.
Leviticus 8:29 And Moses, taking the breast, removed it as a placement before the Lord from the ram of perfection, and it became a portion for Moses, just as the Lord commanded Moses.
Leviticus 8:30 And Moses took some of the oil of anointing and some of the blood upon the altar and sprinkled it upon Aaron and his vestments and his sons and the vestments of his sons with him and sanctified Aaron and his vestments and his sons and the vestments of his sons with him.
Leviticus 8:31 And Moses said to Aaron and his sons: Boil the flesh in the court of the tabernacle of testimony, in a holy place, and there you shall eat it and the loaves in the basket of perfection, in the manner that it has been commanded to me, saying: Aaron and his sons shall eat them;
Leviticus 8:32 and the thing remaining from the flesh and the loaves shall be burned with fire.
Leviticus 8:33 And you shall not go out from the door of the tabernacle of testimony for seven days, until the day is fulfilled, the day of your perfection; for he shall perfect your hands for seven days.
Leviticus 8:34 Just as he did on this day, the Lord commanded it to be done so as to make atonement concerning you.
Leviticus 8:35 And you shall sit at the door of the tabernacle of testimony for seven days, day and night; you shall keep the guardings of the Lord, so that you do not die; for thus the Lord God commanded me.
Leviticus 8:36 And Aaron and his sons did all the words that the Lord commanded Moses.

## Chapter 9

Leviticus 9:1 And it happened on the eighth day that Moses called Aaron and his sons and the council of elders of Israel.
Leviticus 9:2 And Moses said to Aaron: Take for yourself a calf from the cattle for sin and an unblemished ram as a whole burnt offering, and offer them before the Lord;
Leviticus 9:3 and speak to the council of elders of Israel, saying: Take one male kid from the goats for sin and a calf and a year-old lamb for a whole offering, unblemished,
Leviticus 9:4 and a calf and a ram as a sacrifice of salvation before the Lord and fine flour mixed with oil, because today the Lord shall appear among you.
Leviticus 9:5 And they took the things, as Moses commanded, opposite the tabernacle of testimony, and the whole congregation approached and stood before the Lord.
Leviticus 9:6 And Moses said: Do this word that the Lord spoke, and the glory of the Lord shall appear among you.
Leviticus 9:7 And Moses said to Aaron: Approach the altar and make the thing for your sin and your whole burnt offering and make atonement concerning yourself and your house; and make the gifts of the people and make atonement concerning them, just as the Lord commanded Moses.
Leviticus 9:8 And Aaron approached the altar and slaughtered the calf for sin;
Leviticus 9:9 and the sons of Aaron brought the blood to him, and he dipped his finger into the blood and placed it upon the horns of the altar and poured the blood upon the base of the altar;
Leviticus 9:10 and the fat and the kidneys and the lobe of the liver of the thing for sin he offered upon the altar, in the manner that the Lord commanded Moses;
Leviticus 9:11 and the flesh and the hide, he burned them with fire outside the camp.
Leviticus 9:12 And he slaughtered the whole burnt offering; and the sons of Aaron brought the blood to him, and he poured it upon the altar all around;
Leviticus 9:13 and they brought the whole burnt offering to him limb by limb, them and the head, and he placed them upon the altar;
Leviticus 9:14 and he washed the belly and the feet with water and placed them upon the whole burnt offering upon the altar.
Leviticus 9:15 And they brought the gift of the people; and he took the male kid for the sin of the people and slaughtered it just as also the first.
Leviticus 9:16 And he brought the whole burnt offering and made it as is fitting.
Leviticus 9:17 And he brought the sacrifice and filled his hands from it and placed it upon the altar apart from the morning whole burnt offering.
Leviticus 9:18 And he slaughtered the calf and the ram of the sacrifice of salvation of the people; and the sons of Aaron brought the blood to him, and he poured it toward the altar all around;
Leviticus 9:19 and the fat from the calf and the ram, the loin and the fat covering upon the belly and the two kidneys and the fat upon them and the lobe upon the liver,
Leviticus 9:20 and he placed the fats upon the breasts, and they offered the fats upon the altar.
Leviticus 9:21 And Aaron removed the breast and the right arm as a removal offering before the Lord, in the manner that the Lord commanded Moses. –
Leviticus 9:22 And Aaron, lifting his hands over the people, blessed them; and he came down after making the thing for sin and the whole burnt offerings and the things of salvation.
Leviticus 9:23 And Moses and Aaron entered into the tabernacle of testimony and, going out, blessed all the people, and the glory of the Lord appeared to all the people.
Leviticus 9:24 And fire came out from the Lord and consumed the things upon the altar, both the whole burnt offerings and the fats, and all the people saw and were astonished and fell upon their face.

## Chapter 10

Leviticus 10:1 And the two sons of Aaron, Nadab and Abioud, each taking his fire-pan, placed fire upon it and put incense upon it and brought strange fire before the Lord, which the Lord had not commanded them.
Leviticus 10:2 And fire came out from the Lord and consumed them, and they died before the Lord.
Leviticus 10:3 And Moses said to Aaron: This is what the Lord spoke, saying: Among those who draw near to me I will be sanctified, and in the whole congregation I will be glorified. And Aaron was pierced with grief.
Leviticus 10:4 And Moses called Misadai and Elisaphan, sons of Oziel, sons of the brother of Aaron’s father, and said to them: Approach and carry your brothers away from the face of the holy things, outside the camp.
Leviticus 10:5 And they approached and carried them in their tunics outside the camp, in the manner that Moses said.
Leviticus 10:6 And Moses said to Aaron and Eleazar and Ithamar, his sons who remained: You shall not remove the turbans from your heads, and you shall not tear your garments, so that you do not die and there is wrath upon the whole congregation; your brothers, the whole house of Israel, shall weep for the burning with which they were burned by the Lord.
Leviticus 10:7 And you shall not go out from the door of the tabernacle of testimony, so that you do not die; for the oil of anointing from the Lord is upon you. And they did according to the word of Moses.
Leviticus 10:8 And the Lord spoke to Aaron, saying:
Leviticus 10:9 You shall not drink wine or sikera, you and your sons with you, whenever you enter into the tabernacle of testimony or when you approach the altar, and you shall certainly not die [an eternal ordinance for your generations],
Leviticus 10:10 to distinguish between the holy things and the profane things and between the unclean things and the clean things.
Leviticus 10:11 And you shall instruct the sons of Israel in all the ordinances that the Lord spoke to them by the hand of Moses.
Leviticus 10:12 And Moses said to Aaron and to Eleazar and Ithamar, the sons of Aaron who remained: Take the sacrifice remaining from the offerings of the Lord and eat it unleavened beside the altar; it is Holy of Holies.
Leviticus 10:13 And you shall eat it in a holy place; for this is an ordinance for you and an ordinance for your sons from the offerings of the Lord; for thus it has been commanded to me.
Leviticus 10:14 And you and your sons and your household with you shall eat the breast of separation and the arm of the removal offering in a holy place; for it was given as an ordinance for you and an ordinance for your sons from the sacrifices of salvation of the sons of Israel.
Leviticus 10:15 They shall bring the arm of the removal offering and the breast of separation upon the offerings of the fats, to separate them as a separation before the Lord; and it shall be an eternal ordinance for you and your sons and your daughters with you, in the manner that the Lord commanded Moses.
Leviticus 10:16 And seeking, Moses sought out the male kid for sin, and behold, it had been burned; and Moses was angered against Eleazar and Ithamar, the sons of Aaron who remained, saying:
Leviticus 10:17 Why did you not eat the thing for sin in a holy place? For it is Holy of Holies; he gave this to you to eat so that you may take away the sin of the congregation and make atonement concerning them before the Lord;
Leviticus 10:18 for none of its blood was brought into the holy place; toward the front, inside, you shall eat it in a holy place, in the manner that the Lord commanded me.
Leviticus 10:19 And Aaron spoke to Moses, saying: If today they have brought the things for their sin and their whole burnt offerings before the Lord, and these things have happened to me, and I eat the things for sin today, will it be pleasing to the Lord?
Leviticus 10:20 And Moses heard, and it pleased him.

## Chapter 11

Leviticus 11:1 And the Lord spoke to Moses and Aaron, saying:
Leviticus 11:2 Speak to the sons of Israel, saying: These are the animals that you shall eat from all the animals that are upon the earth:
Leviticus 11:3 every animal that divides the hoof and splits the claws into two divisions of the hoof and brings up cud among the animals, these you shall eat.
Leviticus 11:4 Except from these you shall not eat: from those that bring up cud and from those that divide the hooves and split the claws: the camel, because it brings up cud, but does not divide the hoof; this is unclean for you;
Leviticus 11:5 and the hare, because it brings up cud but does not divide the hoof; this is unclean for you;
Leviticus 11:6 and the hyrax, because it brings up cud but does not divide the hoof; this is unclean for you;
Leviticus 11:7 and the pig, because it divides the hoof and splits the claws of the hoof, but it does not bring up cud; this is unclean for you.
Leviticus 11:8 You shall not eat from their flesh, and you shall not touch their carcasses; these are unclean for you.
Leviticus 11:9 And these are what you shall eat from all the things in the waters: all those that have fins and scales in the waters and in the seas and in the torrents, these you shall eat.
Leviticus 11:10 And all those that do not have fins or scales in the water or in the seas and in the torrents, from all that the waters belch forth and from every living soul that is in the water, are an abomination;
Leviticus 11:11 and they shall be abominations for you; you shall not eat from their flesh, and you shall abominate their carcasses.
Leviticus 11:12 And all those that do not have fins and scales, among the things in the water, this is an abomination for you.
Leviticus 11:13 And these you shall abominate from among the birds, and they shall not be eaten; they are an abomination: the eagle and the griffon-vulture and the sea eagle,
Leviticus 11:14 and the vulture and the kite and those like it,
Leviticus 11:15 and the raven and those like it,
Leviticus 11:16 and the ostrich and the owl and the gull and those like it and the hawk and those like it,
Leviticus 11:17 and the night raven and the cormorant and the ibis,
Leviticus 11:18 and the purple swamphen and the pelican and the swan,
Leviticus 11:19 and the owl and the heron and the plover and those like it and the hoopoe and the bat. –
Leviticus 11:20 And all the creeping things among the birds that go upon four are abominations for you.
Leviticus 11:21 But these you shall eat from among the creeping things of the birds that go upon four: those that have legs above their feet, to leap with them upon the earth.
Leviticus 11:22 And these you shall eat from among them: the bruchus and those like it and the attakes and those like it and the locust and those like it and the serpent-fighter and those like it.
Leviticus 11:23 Every creeping thing from among the birds that has four feet is an abomination for you. –
Leviticus 11:24 And by these you shall be defiled; everyone who touches their carcasses shall be unclean until evening,
Leviticus 11:25 and everyone who carries any of their carcasses shall wash his garments and shall be unclean until evening.
Leviticus 11:26 Among all the animals, whatever divides the hoof and splits the claws but does not chew cud shall be unclean for you; everyone who touches their carcasses shall be unclean until evening.
Leviticus 11:27 And every one that goes upon its hands among all the wild animals that go upon four shall be unclean for you; everyone who touches their carcasses shall be unclean until evening.
Leviticus 11:28 And the one who carries their carcasses shall wash his garments and shall be unclean until evening; these are unclean for you.
Leviticus 11:29 And these are unclean for you from among the creeping things that creep upon the earth: the weasel and the mouse and the land crocodile,
Leviticus 11:30 the shrew and the chameleon and the kalabotes and the lizard and the mole.
Leviticus 11:31 These are unclean for you from among all the creeping things that are upon the earth; everyone who touches them when they are dead shall be unclean until evening.
Leviticus 11:32 And everything upon which any of them falls when they are dead shall be unclean, whether any wooden vessel or garment or hide or sack; every vessel by which work is done shall be dipped into water and shall be unclean until evening, and then it shall be clean.
Leviticus 11:33 And every earthen vessel into which any of these falls inside, whatever is inside shall be unclean, and it shall be broken.
Leviticus 11:34 And every food that is eaten, upon which water comes, shall be unclean; and every drink that is drunk in any vessel shall be unclean.
Leviticus 11:35 And everything upon which any of their carcasses falls shall be unclean; ovens and pot-stands shall be pulled down; these are unclean and these shall be unclean for you.
Leviticus 11:36 Except for springs of waters and a cistern and a gathering of water, it shall be clean; but the one who touches their carcasses shall be unclean.
Leviticus 11:37 And if any of their carcasses falls upon any seed for sowing that shall be sown, it shall be clean;
Leviticus 11:38 but if water is poured upon any seed and any of their carcasses falls upon it, it is unclean for you.
Leviticus 11:39 And if one of the animals that is permitted for you to eat dies, the one who touches its carcass shall be unclean until evening.
Leviticus 11:40 And the one who eats from these carcasses shall wash his garments and shall be unclean until evening; and the one who carries any of their carcasses shall wash his garments and bathe in water and shall be unclean until evening.
Leviticus 11:41 And every creeping thing that creeps upon the earth, this shall be an abomination for you; it shall not be eaten.
Leviticus 11:42 And every one that goes upon its belly and every one that goes continually upon four, which multiplies in feet among all the creeping things that creep upon the earth, you shall not eat it, because it is an abomination for you.
Leviticus 11:43 And you shall certainly not make your souls abominable by any of the creeping things that creep upon the earth, and you shall not be defiled by these, and you shall not be unclean by them;
Leviticus 11:44 because I am the Lord your God, and you shall be sanctified and shall be holy, because I am holy, I the Lord your God; and you shall not defile your souls by any of the creeping things that move upon the earth;
Leviticus 11:45 because I am the Lord who brought you up from the land of Egypt to be your God, and you shall be holy, because I am holy, I the Lord.
Leviticus 11:46 This is the law concerning the animals and the birds and every soul that moves in the water and every soul that creeps upon the earth,
Leviticus 11:47 to distinguish between the unclean and the clean and between the live-bearing creatures that are eaten and the live-bearing creatures that are not eaten.

## Chapter 12

Leviticus 12:1 And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying:
Leviticus 12:2 Speak to the sons of Israel, and you shall say to them: A woman, if she receives seed and bears a male, shall be unclean seven days; according to the days of the separation of her menstruation she shall be unclean.
Leviticus 12:3 And on the eighth day he shall circumcise the flesh of his foreskin.
Leviticus 12:4 And she shall remain thirty-three days in her unclean blood; she shall not touch any holy thing and shall not enter into the sanctuary until the days of her cleansing are fulfilled.
Leviticus 12:5 But if she bears a female, she shall be unclean twice seven days, according to the menstruation; and sixty-six days she shall remain in her unclean blood.
Leviticus 12:6 And when the days of her cleansing for a son or for a daughter are completed, she shall offer a year-old unblemished lamb as a whole burnt offering and a young pigeon or a turtledove concerning sin at the door of the tabernacle of testimony to the priest;
Leviticus 12:7 and he shall offer it before the Lord, and the priest shall make atonement concerning her and cleanse her from the fountain of her blood. This is the law of the one who bears a male or a female.
Leviticus 12:8 But if her hand does not find what is sufficient for a lamb, then she shall take two turtledoves or two young pigeons, one as a whole burnt offering and one concerning sin, and the priest shall make atonement concerning her, and she shall be cleansed.

## Chapter 13

Leviticus 13:1 And the Lord spoke to Moses and Aaron, saying:
Leviticus 13:2 If there arises in the skin of the body of any person a scar, a conspicuously bright mark, and there arises in the skin of his body a leprous lesion, then he shall be brought to Aaron the priest or to one of his sons the priests.
Leviticus 13:3 And the priest shall see the lesion in the skin of his body, and if the hair in the lesion has changed white and the appearance of the lesion is lower than the skin of the body, it is a leprous lesion; and the priest shall see it and shall defile him.
Leviticus 13:4 But if there is a white bright mark in the skin of the body, and its appearance is not lower than the skin, and its hair has not changed to white hair, but it is dim, then the priest shall set the lesion apart seven days.
Leviticus 13:5 And the priest shall see the lesion on the seventh day, and behold, the lesion remains before him; the lesion has not advanced in the skin, and the priest shall set him apart seven days a second time.
Leviticus 13:6 And the priest shall see him on the seventh day a second time, and behold, the lesion is dim; the lesion has not advanced in the skin; the priest shall cleanse him, for it is a mark; and when he has washed his garments, he shall be clean.
Leviticus 13:7 But if the mark, changing, advances in the skin after he has seen the priest for him to cleanse him, then he shall appear to the priest a second time;
Leviticus 13:8 and the priest shall see him, and behold, the mark has advanced in the skin, and the priest shall defile him; it is leprosy.
Leviticus 13:9 And if a leprous lesion arises in a person, then he shall come to the priest;
Leviticus 13:10 and the priest shall see, and behold, a white scar is in the skin, and it has changed hair white, and some of the sound living flesh is in the scar;
Leviticus 13:11 it is an old-growing leprosy; it is in the skin of his body, and the priest shall defile him and set him apart, because he is unclean.
Leviticus 13:12 But if, blossoming, the leprosy blossoms in the skin, and the leprosy covers all the skin of the lesion from head to feet, throughout the whole sight of the priest,
Leviticus 13:13 then the priest shall see, and behold, the leprosy has covered all the skin of the body, and the priest shall cleanse him of the lesion, because all of it has changed white; it is clean.
Leviticus 13:14 And on whatever day living skin appears in him, he shall be defiled;
Leviticus 13:15 and the priest shall see the sound skin, and the sound skin shall defile him, because he is unclean; it is leprosy.
Leviticus 13:16 But if the sound skin is restored and changes white, then he shall come to the priest;
Leviticus 13:17 and the priest shall see, and behold, the lesion has changed to white, and the priest shall cleanse the lesion; he is clean.
Leviticus 13:18 And if an ulcer arises in the skin of his flesh and heals,
Leviticus 13:19 and there arises in the place of the ulcer a white scar or a bright spot whitening or reddening, then it shall appear to the priest;
Leviticus 13:20 and the priest shall see, and behold, its appearance is lower than the skin and its hair has changed to white, and the priest shall defile him; it is leprosy; it has blossomed in the ulcer.
Leviticus 13:21 But if the priest sees, and behold, there is no white hair in it, and it is not lower than the skin of the body, and it is dim, then the priest shall set him apart seven days.
Leviticus 13:22 But if it spreads in the skin, then the priest shall defile him; it is a leprous lesion; it has blossomed in the ulcer.
Leviticus 13:23 But if the bright spot remains in its place and does not spread, it is the scar of the ulcer, and the priest shall cleanse him.
Leviticus 13:24 And if there arises in the skin of his flesh a burn of fire, and the healed part of the burn in his skin becomes a shining bright white spot tending red or very white,
Leviticus 13:25 then the priest shall see him, and behold, white hair has changed in the shining spot and its appearance is lower than the skin; it is leprosy; it has blossomed in the burn, and the priest shall defile him; it is a leprous lesion.
Leviticus 13:26 But if the priest sees, and behold, there is no white hair in the shining spot, and it is not lower than the skin, but it is dim, then the priest shall set him apart seven days.
Leviticus 13:27 And the priest shall see him on the seventh day; but if, with spreading, it spreads in the skin, then the priest shall defile him; it is a leprous lesion; it has blossomed in the ulcer.
Leviticus 13:28 But if the shining spot remains in its place and does not spread in the skin, and it is dim, it is the scar of the burn, and the priest shall cleanse him, for it is the mark of the burn.
Leviticus 13:29 And if there arises in a man or a woman a leprous lesion on the head or on the beard,
Leviticus 13:30 then the priest shall see the lesion, and behold, its appearance is more hollow than the skin and there is thin yellowish hair in it, and the priest shall defile him; it is a scall, a leprosy of the head or a leprosy of the beard.
Leviticus 13:31 And if the priest sees the lesion of the scall, and behold, its appearance is not more hollow than the skin and there is no yellowish hair in it, then the priest shall set apart the lesion of the scall seven days.
Leviticus 13:32 And the priest shall see the lesion on the seventh day, and behold, the scall has not spread, and there is no yellowish hair in it, and the appearance of the scall is not hollow beneath the skin;
Leviticus 13:33 then the skin shall be shaved, but the scall shall not be shaved, and the priest shall set apart the scall seven days a second time.
Leviticus 13:34 And the priest shall see the scall on the seventh day, and behold, the scall has not spread in the skin after he has been shaved, and the appearance of the scall is not hollow beneath the skin; then the priest shall cleanse him, and when he has washed his garments, he shall be clean.
Leviticus 13:35 But if, with spreading, the scall spreads in the skin after he has been cleansed,
Leviticus 13:36 then the priest shall see, and behold, the scall has spread in the skin; the priest shall not examine concerning the yellow hair, because he is unclean.
Leviticus 13:37 But if the scall remains before him in its place and black hair springs up in it, the scall has healed; he is clean, and the priest shall cleanse him.
Leviticus 13:38 And if there arise in a man or a woman, in the skin of his flesh, shining spots that shine whitish,
Leviticus 13:39 then the priest shall see, and behold, in the skin of his flesh are shining spots that shine whitish; it is alphos; he is clean; it blossoms in the skin of his flesh; he is clean.
Leviticus 13:40 And if the head of anyone loses its hair, he is bald; he is clean.
Leviticus 13:41 But if his head loses its hair toward the front, he is bald in front; he is clean.
Leviticus 13:42 But if there arises in his baldness or in his frontal baldness a white or reddening lesion, it is leprosy in his baldness or in his frontal baldness;
Leviticus 13:43 and the priest shall see him, and behold, the appearance of the lesion is white, reddening in his baldness or in his frontal baldness, like the appearance of leprosy in the skin of his flesh;
Leviticus 13:44 he is a leprous person; with defiling the priest shall defile him; his lesion is on his head.
Leviticus 13:45 And the leprous person in whom the lesion is, let his garments be loosened and his head uncovered, and let him wrap something around his mouth, and he shall be called unclean.
Leviticus 13:46 All the days for which the lesion is upon him, being unclean, he shall be unclean; he shall sit apart; his dwelling shall be outside the camp.
Leviticus 13:47 And if there arises in a garment a leprous lesion, in a woolen garment or in a flaxen garment,
Leviticus 13:48 or in warp or in woof or in the linen things or in the woolen things or in a hide or in any worked hide,
Leviticus 13:49 and the lesion becomes greenish or reddish in the hide or in the garment or in the warp or in the woof or in any vessel worked from hide, it is a leprous lesion, and it shall be shown to the priest.
Leviticus 13:50 And the priest shall see the lesion, and the priest shall set the lesion apart seven days.
Leviticus 13:51 And the priest shall see the lesion on the seventh day; but if the lesion spreads in the garment or in the warp or in the woof or in the hide, in regard to anything for which hides are made in the work, the lesion is a persistent leprosy; it is unclean.
Leviticus 13:52 He shall burn the garment or the warp or the woof among the woolen things or among the linen things or any vessel of hide in which the lesion is, because it is a persistent leprosy; it shall be burned with fire.
Leviticus 13:53 But if the priest sees, and the lesion does not spread in the garment or in the warp or in the woof or in any vessel of hide,
Leviticus 13:54 then the priest shall command, and he shall wash that upon which the lesion is, and the priest shall set the lesion apart seven days a second time.
Leviticus 13:55 And the priest shall see the lesion after it has been washed, and if the lesion has not changed its appearance and the lesion does not spread, it is unclean; it shall be burned with fire; it is fixed in the garment or in the warp or in the woof.
Leviticus 13:56 And if the priest sees, and the lesion is dim after it has been washed, he shall tear it away from the garment or from the hide or from the warp or from the woof.
Leviticus 13:57 But if it still appears in the garment or in the warp or in the woof or in any vessel of hide, it is a blossoming leprosy; that in which the lesion is shall be burned with fire.
Leviticus 13:58 And the garment or the warp or the woof or every vessel of hide that is washed and from which the lesion departs shall also be washed a second time and shall be clean.
Leviticus 13:59 This is the law of a leprous lesion in a woolen or flaxen garment or warp or woof or any vessel of hide, for cleansing it or defiling it.

## Chapter 14

Leviticus 14:1 And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying:
Leviticus 14:2 This is the law of the leprous person, on whatever day he is cleansed; and he shall be brought to the priest.
Leviticus 14:3 And the priest shall go out, outside the camp, and the priest shall see, and behold, the leprous lesion has healed from the leprous person;
Leviticus 14:4 and the priest shall command, and they shall take for the one who has been cleansed two living clean birds and cedar wood and spun scarlet and hyssop.
Leviticus 14:5 And the priest shall command, and they shall slaughter the one bird into an earthen vessel over living water.
Leviticus 14:6 And as for the living bird, he shall take it and the cedar wood and the spun scarlet and the hyssop and shall dip them and the living bird into the blood of the bird that was slaughtered over living water;
Leviticus 14:7 and he shall sprinkle upon the one cleansed from the leprosy seven times, and he shall be clean; and he shall release the living bird into the plain.
Leviticus 14:8 And the one who has been cleansed shall wash his garments and shall shave off all his hair and shall bathe in water and shall be clean; and after these things he shall enter into the camp and shall remain outside his house seven days.
Leviticus 14:9 And it shall be on the seventh day that he shall shave off all his hair: his head and his beard and his eyebrows, and he shall shave off all his hair; and he shall wash his garments and bathe his body in water and shall be clean. –
Leviticus 14:10 And on the eighth day he shall take two year-old unblemished lambs and one year-old unblemished sheep and three tenths of fine flour as a sacrifice, mixed with oil, and one kotyle of oil;
Leviticus 14:11 and the priest who cleanses shall stand the person who is being cleansed and these things before the Lord at the door of the tabernacle of testimony.
Leviticus 14:12 And the priest shall take the one lamb and bring it for trespass, and the kotyle of oil, and shall set it apart as a separation before the Lord.
Leviticus 14:13 And they shall slaughter the lamb in the place where they slaughter the whole burnt offerings and the things concerning sin, in a holy place; for the thing concerning sin is like the thing of trespass; it belongs to the priest; it is Holy of Holies.
Leviticus 14:14 And the priest shall take from the blood of the thing of trespass, and the priest shall place it upon the lobe of the right ear of the one who is being cleansed and upon the tip of the right hand and upon the tip of the right foot.
Leviticus 14:15 And the priest, taking from the kotyle of oil, shall pour it upon the priest’s left hand;
Leviticus 14:16 and he shall dip his right finger into the oil that is upon his left hand and shall sprinkle with his finger seven times before the Lord.
Leviticus 14:17 And the remaining oil that is in his hand the priest shall place upon the lobe of the right ear of the one who is being cleansed and upon the tip of the right hand and upon the tip of the right foot, upon the place of the blood of the thing of trespass.
Leviticus 14:18 And the remaining oil that is upon the priest’s hand, the priest shall place upon the head of the one who has been cleansed, and the priest shall make atonement concerning him before the Lord.
Leviticus 14:19 And the priest shall make the thing concerning sin, and the priest shall make atonement concerning the unclean person who is being cleansed from his sin; and after this the priest shall slaughter the whole burnt offering.
Leviticus 14:20 And the priest shall offer the whole burnt offering and the sacrifice upon the altar before the Lord; and the priest shall make atonement concerning him, and he shall be cleansed.
Leviticus 14:21 But if he is poor and his hand does not find enough, he shall take one lamb for that in which he trespassed, as a removal offering, so as to make atonement concerning him, and a tenth of fine flour mixed with oil as a sacrifice and one kotyle of oil,
Leviticus 14:22 and two turtledoves or two young pigeons, whatever his hand has found, and the one shall be concerning sin and the one as a whole burnt offering.
Leviticus 14:23 And he shall bring them on the eighth day for cleansing him, to the priest, at the door of the tabernacle of testimony before the Lord.
Leviticus 14:24 And the priest, taking the lamb of trespass and the kotyle of oil, shall place them as a presentation before the Lord.
Leviticus 14:25 And he shall slaughter the lamb of trespass, and the priest shall take from the blood of the thing of trespass and shall place it upon the lobe of the right ear of the one who is being cleansed and upon the tip of the right hand and upon the tip of the right foot.
Leviticus 14:26 And the priest shall pour some of the oil upon the priest’s left hand;
Leviticus 14:27 and the priest shall sprinkle with his right finger some of the oil that is in his left hand seven times before the Lord.
Leviticus 14:28 And the priest shall place some of the oil that is upon his hand upon the lobe of the right ear of the one who is being cleansed and upon the tip of his right hand and upon the tip of his right foot, upon the place of the blood of the thing of trespass.
Leviticus 14:29 And the remainder of the oil that is upon the priest’s hand he shall place upon the head of the one who has been cleansed, and the priest shall make atonement concerning him before the Lord.
Leviticus 14:30 And he shall make one of the turtledoves or of the young pigeons, according to what his hand has found,
Leviticus 14:31 the one concerning sin and the one as a whole burnt offering with the sacrifice; and the priest shall make atonement concerning the one who is being cleansed before the Lord.
Leviticus 14:32 This is the law for one in whom is the leprous lesion and whose hand does not find enough for his cleansing.
Leviticus 14:33 And the Lord spoke to Moses and Aaron, saying:
Leviticus 14:34 Whenever you enter into the land of the Chanaanites, which I give to you as a possession, and I give a leprous lesion in the houses of the land acquired by you,
Leviticus 14:35 then he whose house it is shall come and report to the priest, saying: Something like a lesion has appeared to me in the house.
Leviticus 14:36 And the priest shall command that the house be cleared out before the priest enters to see the lesion, so that the things that are in the house certainly do not become unclean; and after these things the priest shall enter to examine the house.
Leviticus 14:37 And he shall see the lesion in the walls of the house, greenish or reddish cavities, and their appearance lower than the walls;
Leviticus 14:38 and the priest, going out from the house to the door of the house, shall set the house apart seven days.
Leviticus 14:39 And the priest shall return on the seventh day and shall see the house, and behold, the lesion has not spread in the walls of the house;
Leviticus 14:40 and the priest shall command, and they shall take out the stones in which the lesion is, and they shall cast them outside the city into an unclean place.
Leviticus 14:41 And they shall scrape the house inside all around and shall pour out the dust outside the city into an unclean place.
Leviticus 14:42 And they shall take other scraped stones and put them in place of the stones, and they shall take other dust and plaster the house.
Leviticus 14:43 But if the lesion comes again and springs up in the house after the stones have been taken out and after the house has been scraped and after it has been plastered,
Leviticus 14:44 then the priest shall enter and shall see; if the lesion has spread in the house, it is a persistent leprosy in the house; it is unclean.
Leviticus 14:45 And they shall pull down the house, and they shall carry its timbers and its stones and all the dust outside the city into an unclean place.
Leviticus 14:46 And the one who enters into the house during all the days for which it is set apart shall be unclean until evening.
Leviticus 14:47 And the one who sleeps in the house shall wash his garments and shall be unclean until evening; and the one who eats in the house shall wash his garments and shall be unclean until evening.
Leviticus 14:48 But if the priest, arriving, enters and sees, and behold, with spreading the lesion does not spread in the house after the house has been plastered, then the priest shall cleanse the house, because the lesion has healed.
Leviticus 14:49 And he shall take, to purify the house, two living clean birds and cedar wood and spun scarlet and hyssop;
Leviticus 14:50 and he shall slaughter the one bird into an earthen vessel over living water,
Leviticus 14:51 and he shall take the cedar wood and the spun scarlet and the hyssop and the living bird and shall dip it into the blood of the bird that was slaughtered over living water and shall sprinkle the house with them seven times.
Leviticus 14:52 And he shall purify the house with the blood of the bird and with the living water and with the living bird and with the cedar wood and with the hyssop and with the spun scarlet.
Leviticus 14:53 And he shall release the living bird outside the city into the plain and shall make atonement concerning the house, and it shall be clean.
Leviticus 14:54 This is the law concerning every leprous lesion and scall,
Leviticus 14:55 and the leprosy of a garment and a house,
Leviticus 14:56 and a scar and a mark and the shining spot,
Leviticus 14:57 and for explaining on what day it is unclean and on what day it shall be cleansed; this is the law of leprosy.

## Chapter 15

Leviticus 15:1 And the Lord spoke to Moses and Aaron, saying:
Leviticus 15:2 Speak to the sons of Israel, and you shall say to them: For any man in whom there is a discharge from his body, his discharge is unclean.
Leviticus 15:3 And this is the law of his uncleanness: whether seed flows from his body from the discharge by which his body has become constricted through the discharge, this is his uncleanness in him; all the days of the discharge of his body, by which his body has become constricted through the discharge, it is his uncleanness.
Leviticus 15:4 Every bed upon which the man with the seminal discharge sleeps is unclean, and every vessel upon which the man with the seminal discharge sits shall be unclean.
Leviticus 15:5 And a person who touches his bed shall wash his garments and bathe in water and shall be unclean until evening.
Leviticus 15:6 And the one who sits upon the vessel upon which the man with the seminal discharge sits shall wash his garments and bathe in water and shall be unclean until evening.
Leviticus 15:7 And the one who touches the body of the man with the seminal discharge shall wash his garments and bathe in water and shall be unclean until evening.
Leviticus 15:8 But if the man with the seminal discharge spits upon the clean person, he shall wash his garments and bathe in water and shall be unclean until evening.
Leviticus 15:9 And every saddle of a donkey upon which the man with the seminal discharge rides shall be unclean until evening.
Leviticus 15:10 And everyone who touches anything that is beneath him shall be unclean until evening; and the one who carries them shall wash his garments and bathe in water and shall be unclean until evening.
Leviticus 15:11 And anyone whom the man with the seminal discharge touches while he has not washed his hands shall wash his garments and bathe his body in water and shall be unclean until evening.
Leviticus 15:12 And an earthen vessel that the man with the seminal discharge touches shall be broken; and a wooden vessel shall be rinsed with water and shall be clean. –
Leviticus 15:13 But if the man with the seminal discharge is cleansed from his discharge, then seven days shall be counted for him for cleansing, and he shall wash his garments and bathe his body in water and shall be clean.
Leviticus 15:14 And on the eighth day he shall take for himself two turtledoves or two young pigeons and shall bring them before the Lord at the doors of the tabernacle of testimony and shall give them to the priest.
Leviticus 15:15 And the priest shall make them, one concerning sin and one as a whole burnt offering, and the priest shall make atonement concerning him before the Lord for his discharge.
Leviticus 15:16 And a man from whom an emission of semen goes out shall bathe his whole body in water and shall be unclean until evening.
Leviticus 15:17 And every garment and every hide upon which there is an emission of semen shall also be washed with water and shall be unclean until evening.
Leviticus 15:18 And a woman, if a man lies with her with an emission of semen, they shall both bathe in water and shall be unclean until evening.
Leviticus 15:19 And a woman, if she is flowing with blood and her discharge is in her body, shall be in her menstruation seven days; everyone who touches her shall be unclean until evening.
Leviticus 15:20 And everything upon which she lies during her menstruation shall be unclean, and everything upon which she sits shall be unclean.
Leviticus 15:21 And everyone who touches her bed shall wash his garments and bathe his body in water and shall be unclean until evening.
Leviticus 15:22 And everyone who touches any vessel upon which she sits shall wash his garments and bathe in water and shall be unclean until evening.
Leviticus 15:23 But if he touches her while she is on her bed or upon the vessel upon which she sits, he shall be unclean until evening.
Leviticus 15:24 But if anyone lies in bed with her and her uncleanness comes upon him, then he shall be unclean seven days, and every bed upon which he sleeps shall be unclean.
Leviticus 15:25 And a woman, if she flows with a flow of blood for more days, not at the time of her menstruation, or if she also flows after her menstruation, all the days of the flow of her uncleanness shall be like the days of her menstruation; she shall be unclean.
Leviticus 15:26 And every bed upon which she sleeps during all the days of her flow shall be for her like the bed of her menstruation, and every vessel upon which she sits shall be unclean according to the uncleanness of her menstruation.
Leviticus 15:27 Everyone who touches her shall be unclean and shall wash his garments and bathe his body in water and shall be unclean until evening.
Leviticus 15:28 But if she is cleansed from the discharge, then seven days shall be counted for her, and after these she shall be cleansed.
Leviticus 15:29 And on the eighth day she shall take for herself two turtledoves or two young pigeons and shall bring them to the priest at the door of the tabernacle of testimony.
Leviticus 15:30 And the priest shall make the one concerning sin and the one as a whole burnt offering, and the priest shall make atonement concerning her before the Lord for the flow of her uncleanness.
Leviticus 15:31 And you shall make the sons of Israel cautious of their uncleannesses, and they shall not die because of their uncleanness when they defile my tabernacle that is among them. –
Leviticus 15:32 This is the law of the man with the seminal discharge and of anyone from whom an emission of semen goes out so that he is defiled by it,
Leviticus 15:33 and of the woman flowing blood in her menstruation and the one with a seminal discharge in his discharge, for the male or for the female, and of the man who lies with one sitting apart.

## Chapter 16

Leviticus 16:1 And the Lord spoke to Moses after the two sons of Aaron died when they brought strange fire before the Lord, and they died.
Leviticus 16:2 And the Lord said to Moses: Speak to Aaron your brother, and let him not enter at every time into the holy place inside the veil, before the propitiatory that is upon the ark of testimony, and he shall not die; for I shall appear in a cloud upon the propitiatory.
Leviticus 16:3 Thus Aaron shall enter into the holy place: with a calf from the cattle concerning sin and a ram as a whole burnt offering.
Leviticus 16:4 And he shall put on a sanctified linen tunic, and linen drawers shall be upon his body, and he shall gird himself with a linen sash and put on a linen turban; they are holy garments, and he shall bathe his whole body in water and put them on.
Leviticus 16:5 And from the congregation of the sons of Israel he shall take two male kids from the goats concerning sin and one ram as a whole burnt offering.
Leviticus 16:6 And Aaron shall bring the calf concerning his sin and shall make atonement concerning himself and his house.
Leviticus 16:7 And he shall take the two male kids and stand them before the Lord beside the door of the tabernacle of testimony.
Leviticus 16:8 And Aaron shall place lots upon the two male kids, one lot for the Lord and one lot for the one sent away.
Leviticus 16:9 And Aaron shall bring the male kid upon which the lot for the Lord fell and shall offer it concerning sin.
Leviticus 16:10 And the male kid upon which the lot of the one sent away fell, he shall stand it alive before the Lord, to make atonement upon it so as to send it away for dismissal; he shall release it into the wilderness. –
Leviticus 16:11 And Aaron shall bring the calf concerning his sin, his own and that of his house alone, and shall make atonement concerning himself and his house, and he shall slaughter the calf concerning his own sin.
Leviticus 16:12 And he shall take the fire-pan full of coals of fire from the altar that is before the Lord and shall fill his hands with fine compounded incense and bring it inside the veil.
Leviticus 16:13 And he shall place the incense upon the fire before the Lord, and the vapor of the incense shall cover the propitiatory that is upon the testimonies, and he shall not die.
Leviticus 16:14 And he shall take some of the blood of the calf and shall sprinkle it with his finger upon the propitiatory toward the east; before the propitiatory he shall sprinkle some of the blood with his finger seven times.
Leviticus 16:15 And he shall slaughter the male kid concerning the sin of the people before the Lord and shall bring some of its blood inside the veil and shall do with its blood in the manner that he did with the blood of the calf, and he shall sprinkle its blood upon the propitiatory, before the propitiatory.
Leviticus 16:16 And he shall make atonement for the holy place from the uncleannesses of the sons of Israel and from their injustices concerning all their sins; and thus he shall do to the tabernacle of testimony that was built among them in the midst of their uncleanness.
Leviticus 16:17 And no person shall be in the tabernacle of testimony when he enters to make atonement in the holy place, until he comes out; and he shall make atonement concerning himself and his house and concerning the whole congregation of the sons of Israel.
Leviticus 16:18 And he shall go out to the altar that is before the Lord and shall make atonement upon it; and he shall take some of the blood of the calf and some of the blood of the male kid and shall place it upon the horns of the altar all around.
Leviticus 16:19 And he shall sprinkle some of the blood upon it with his finger seven times and shall cleanse it and sanctify it from the uncleannesses of the sons of Israel.
