Numbers 34:23 from the sons of Joseph, from the tribe of the sons of Manasse, the ruler Aniel son of Ouphi;
Numbers 34:24 from the tribe of the sons of Ephraim, the ruler Kamouel son of Sabatha;
Numbers 34:25 from the tribe of Zaboulon, the ruler Elisaphan son of Pharnach;
Numbers 34:26 from the tribe of the sons of Issachar, the ruler Phaltiel son of Oza;
Numbers 34:27 from the tribe of the sons of Aser, the ruler Achior son of Selemi;
Numbers 34:28 from the tribe of Nephthali, the ruler Phadael son of Benamioud.
Numbers 34:29 These are the ones whom the Lord commanded to apportion for the sons of Israel in the land of Chanaan.

## Chapter 35

Numbers 35:1 And the Lord spoke to Moses at the west of Moab beside the Jordan opposite Jericho, saying:
Numbers 35:2 Prescribe to the sons of Israel, and they shall give to the Levites, from the allotments of their possession, cities to dwell in; and they shall give the suburbs of the cities around them to the Levites.
Numbers 35:3 And the cities shall be for them to dwell in, and their separations shall be for their livestock and for all their quadrupeds.
Numbers 35:4 And the things adjoining the cities that you shall give to the Levites shall be from the wall of the city and outward two thousand cubits around.
Numbers 35:5 And you shall measure outside the city the side toward east, two thousand cubits, and the side toward southwest, two thousand cubits, and the side toward the sea, two thousand cubits, and the side toward north, two thousand cubits; and the city shall be in the middle of this for you, and the neighboring lands of the cities.
Numbers 35:6 And the cities you shall give to the Levites shall be the six cities of exile, which you shall give for the one who killed to flee there, and besides these, forty-two cities.
Numbers 35:7 All the cities you shall give to the Levites shall be forty-eight cities, these and their suburbs.
Numbers 35:8 And the cities that you shall give from the possession of the sons of Israel: from those with many, many, and from the lesser, fewer. Each, according to his inheritance that they shall inherit, they shall give from the cities to the Levites.
Numbers 35:9 And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying:
Numbers 35:10 Speak to the sons of Israel, and you shall say to them: You are crossing over the Jordan into the land of Chanaan,
Numbers 35:11 and you shall distinguish cities for yourselves. They shall be exile places for you, for the killer to flee there, everyone who struck a soul involuntarily.
Numbers 35:12 And the cities shall be exile places for you from the one acting as kinsman for the blood, and the one who kills shall certainly not die until he stands before the congregation for judgment.
Numbers 35:13 And the cities that you shall give, the six cities, shall be exile places for you.
Numbers 35:14 You shall give the three cities beyond the Jordan, and you shall give the three cities in the land of Chanaan.
Numbers 35:15 It shall be a place of exile for the sons of Israel, and for the proselyte and the sojourner among you these cities shall be as an exile place, for everyone who struck a soul involuntarily to flee there. –
Numbers 35:16 But if he strikes him with an iron implement and he comes to an end, he is a killer; by death let the killer be put to death.
Numbers 35:17 But if with a stone from a hand, by which he will die in it, he strikes him, and he dies, he is a killer; by death let the killer be put to death.
Numbers 35:18 But if with a wooden implement from a hand, by which he will die in it, he strikes him, and he dies, he is a killer; by death let the killer be put to death.
Numbers 35:19 The one acting as kinsman for the blood, this one shall kill the one who killed; whenever he meets him, this one shall kill him.
Numbers 35:20 But if through hatred he pushes him and throws upon him any implement from ambush, and he dies,
Numbers 35:21 or through anger he struck him with the hand, and he dies, by death let the one who struck be put to death; he is a killer. By death let the one who kills be put to death. The one acting as kinsman for the blood shall kill the one who killed when he meets him. –
Numbers 35:22 But if suddenly, not through hatred, he pushes him, or throws upon him any implement, not from ambush,
Numbers 35:23 or with any stone by which he will die in it, without knowing, and it falls upon him, and he dies, though he was not his enemy nor was seeking to harm him,
Numbers 35:24 then the congregation shall judge between the one who struck and between the one acting as kinsman for the blood according to these judgments.
Numbers 35:25 And the congregation shall rescue the one who killed from the one acting as kinsman for the blood, and they, the congregation, shall restore him to the city of his place of exile, where he had fled, and he shall dwell there until the great priest whom they anointed with the holy oil dies.
Numbers 35:26 But if the one who killed goes out by an exit beyond the borders of the city into which he fled there,
Numbers 35:27 and the one acting as kinsman for the blood finds him outside the borders of his city of refuge, and the one acting as kinsman for the blood kills the one who killed, he is not liable.
Numbers 35:28 For let him dwell in the city of refuge until the great priest dies, and after the great priest dies, the one who killed shall return to the land of his possession.
Numbers 35:29 And these things shall be for you as an ordinance of judgment for your generations in all your dwellings. –
Numbers 35:30 Everyone who struck a soul: through witnesses you shall kill the one who killed, and one witness shall not testify against a soul for it to die.
Numbers 35:31 And you shall not take ransom concerning a soul from the one who killed, who is liable to be killed; for by death he shall be put to death.
Numbers 35:32 You shall not take ransom for fleeing into a city of exile places, to dwell again upon the land, until the great priest dies.
Numbers 35:33 And you shall certainly not murder the land in which you dwell; for this blood murders the land, and the land shall not be atoned from the blood shed upon it except upon the blood of the one shedding it.
Numbers 35:34 And you shall not defile the land upon which you dwell, upon which I shall encamp among you; for I am the Lord encamping in the midst of the sons of Israel.

## Chapter 36

Numbers 36:1 And the rulers of the tribe of the sons of Galaad son of Machir son of Manasse, from the tribe of the sons of Joseph, approached and spoke before Moses and before Eleazar the priest and before the rulers of the houses of the paternal families of the sons of Israel,
Numbers 36:2 and they said: The Lord commanded our lord to assign the land of the inheritance by allotment to the sons of Israel, and the Lord prescribed to our lord to give the inheritance of Salpaad our brother to his daughters.
Numbers 36:3 And they shall become wives to one of the tribes of the sons of Israel, and their allotment shall be removed from the possession of our fathers and shall be added to the inheritance of the tribe to whom they become wives, and it shall be removed from the allotment of our inheritance.
Numbers 36:4 But if the release of the sons of Israel comes, then their inheritance shall be added upon the inheritance of the tribe to whom they become wives, and their inheritance shall be removed from the inheritance of the tribe of our paternal family.
Numbers 36:5 And Moses commanded the sons of Israel by the command of the Lord, saying: Thus the tribe of the sons of Joseph say.
Numbers 36:6 This is the word that the Lord prescribed to the daughters of Salpaad, saying: Where it is pleasing before them, let them become wives; only from the community of their father let them become wives,
Numbers 36:7 and an inheritance for the sons of Israel shall not be turned around from tribe to tribe, because the sons of Israel shall each be joined in the inheritance of the tribe of his paternal family.
Numbers 36:8 And every daughter acting as next-of-kin to an inheritance from the tribes of the sons of Israel shall become a wife to one from the community of her father, so that the sons of Israel may each act as next-of-kin to his paternal inheritance.
Numbers 36:9 And an allotment shall not be turned around from a tribe to another tribe, but the sons of Israel shall each be joined in his inheritance.
Numbers 36:10 In the manner that the Lord prescribed to Moses, thus the daughters of Salpaad did,
Numbers 36:11 and Thersa and Egla and Melcha and Noua and Maala, daughters of Salpaad, became wives to their cousins.
Numbers 36:12 From the community of Manasse of the sons of Joseph they became wives, and their inheritance came upon the tribe of the community of their father.
Numbers 36:13 These are the commandments and the ordinances and the judgments that the Lord commanded by the hand of Moses at the west of Moab on the Jordan opposite Jericho.

# Deuteronomy

The Apostolic Bible. Public domain. https://apostolic-bible.ysys9.chatgpt.site/license.html


## Chapter 1

Deuteronomy 1:1 These are the words that Moses spoke to all Israel beyond the Jordan, in the wilderness toward the west near the Red Sea, between Pharan, Tophol and Lobon and Aulon and Katachrysea.
Deuteronomy 1:2 An eleven-days’ road in Choreb, toward Mount Seir, as far as Cades Barne.
Deuteronomy 1:3 And it happened in the fortieth year, in the eleventh month, on the first of the month, Moses spoke to all the sons of Israel according to all the things that the Lord commanded him for them,
Deuteronomy 1:4 after striking Seon king of the Amorrites, who dwelt in Esebon, and Og king of Basan, who dwelt in Astaroth and in Edrain.
Deuteronomy 1:5 Beyond the Jordan in the land of Moab, Moses began to make this law clear, saying:
Deuteronomy 1:6 The Lord our God spoke to us in Choreb, saying: Let it be sufficient for you to dwell on this mountain.
Deuteronomy 1:7 Turn and set out, you, and enter into the mountain of the Amorrites and toward all those dwelling around Araba, into the mountain and the plain and toward the southwest and the coast, the land of the Chananites and Antilibanus, as far as the great river Euphrates.
Deuteronomy 1:8 See, I have delivered the land before you. Enter and inherit the land that I swore to your fathers, Abraham and Isaac and Jacob, to give to them and to their seed after them.
Deuteronomy 1:9 And I spoke to you at that time, saying: I shall not be able to bear you alone.
Deuteronomy 1:10 The Lord your God multiplied you, and behold, today you are like the stars of heaven in multitude.
Deuteronomy 1:11 May the Lord, the God of your fathers, add to you as you are, a thousandfold, and bless you, just as he spoke to you.
Deuteronomy 1:12 How shall I be able to bear alone your toil and your substance and your disputes?
Deuteronomy 1:13 Give yourselves men who are wise and knowledgeable and understanding for your tribes, and I shall appoint them over you as your leaders.
Deuteronomy 1:14 And you answered me and said: The word that you spoke to do is good.
Deuteronomy 1:15 And I took from you men who were wise and knowledgeable and understanding and appointed them to lead over you as commanders of thousands and commanders of hundreds and commanders of fifties and commanders of tens and document-introducers for your judges.
Deuteronomy 1:16 And I commanded your judges at that time, saying: Hear thoroughly between your brothers, and judge justly between a man and between his brother and between his proselyte.
Deuteronomy 1:17 You shall not recognize a face in judgment; according to the small and according to the great you shall judge. You shall certainly not shrink from a person’s face, because the judgment is God’s. And the matter that may be hard for you, you shall bring up to me, and I shall hear it.
Deuteronomy 1:18 And I commanded you at that time all the words that you shall do.
Deuteronomy 1:19 And setting out from Choreb, we traveled through all that great and fearful wilderness that you saw, by the road of the mountain of the Amorrite, just as the Lord our God commanded us, and we came as far as Cades Barne.
Deuteronomy 1:20 And I said to you: You have come as far as the mountain of the Amorrite, which the Lord our God is giving you.
Deuteronomy 1:21 See, the Lord your God has delivered the land to you before your face. Go up and inherit it, in the manner that the Lord, the God of your fathers, said to you. Do not fear or be cowardly.
Deuteronomy 1:22 And you all approached me and said: Let us send men ahead of us, and let them survey the land for us and report to us an answer, the road by which we shall go up in it and the cities into which we shall enter.
Deuteronomy 1:23 And the word was pleasing before me, and I took from you twelve men, one man for each tribe.
Deuteronomy 1:24 And turning, they went up into the mountain and came as far as the Ravine of the Cluster and spied it out.
Deuteronomy 1:25 And they took in their hands some of the fruit of the land and brought it down to us and said: The land that the Lord our God is giving us is good.
Deuteronomy 1:26 And you were not willing to go up, and you disobeyed the word of the Lord your God,
Deuteronomy 1:27 and you murmured in your tents and said: Because the Lord hates us, he brought us out from the land of Egypt to hand us into the hands of the Amorrites, to utterly destroy us.
Deuteronomy 1:28 Where are we going up? Your brothers turned away your heart, saying: A great and numerous nation, and more powerful than us, and great cities walled as far as heaven; but we also saw sons of giants there.
Deuteronomy 1:29 And I said to you: Do not be terrified or be afraid of them.
Deuteronomy 1:30 The Lord your God, the one going before your face, he shall fight them together with you according to all the things that he did for you in the land of Egypt
Deuteronomy 1:31 and in this wilderness that you saw, how the Lord your God nourished you, as a person would nourish his son, along all the road that you traveled until you came to this place.
Deuteronomy 1:32 And in this word you did not put trust in the Lord your God,
Deuteronomy 1:33 who goes ahead of you on the road to choose a place for you, guiding you by fire at night, showing you the road upon which you go, and by a cloud by day.
Deuteronomy 1:34 And the Lord heard the voice of your words and, being provoked, swore, saying:
Deuteronomy 1:35 Surely no one of these men shall see this good land that I swore to their fathers,
Deuteronomy 1:36 except Chaleb son of Jephonne; he shall see it, and to him and to his sons I shall give the land upon which he stepped, because he was attached to the things toward the Lord.
Deuteronomy 1:37 And the Lord was enraged at me because of you, saying: Not even you shall certainly enter there.
Deuteronomy 1:38 Jesus son of Nave, who stands beside you, he shall enter there. Strengthen him, because he shall cause Israel to inherit it.
Deuteronomy 1:39 And every young child who today does not know good or evil, these shall enter there, and to these I shall give it, and they shall inherit it.
Deuteronomy 1:40 And you, turn and encamp in the wilderness by the road at the Red Sea.
Deuteronomy 1:41 And you answered me and said: We sinned before the Lord our God; we, going up, shall wage war according to all the things that the Lord our God commanded us. And each taking up his implements of war and gathering together, you were going up into the mountain.
Deuteronomy 1:42 And the Lord said to me: Say to them: You shall not go up, nor shall you wage war, for I am not with you; and you shall certainly not be crushed before your enemies.
Deuteronomy 1:43 And I spoke to you, and you did not listen to me, and you transgressed the word of the Lord and, forcing your way, went up into the mountain.
Deuteronomy 1:44 And the Amorrite who dwelt on that mountain went out to meet you, and they pursued you as if the bees might do, and they were wounding you from Seir as far as Herma.
Deuteronomy 1:45 And sitting down, you wept before the Lord, and the Lord did not listen to your voice or pay attention to you.
Deuteronomy 1:46 And you sat in Cades many days, as many days as you ever sat.

## Chapter 2

Deuteronomy 2:1 And turning, we departed into the wilderness by the road toward Red Sea, in the manner that the Lord spoke to me, and we went around Mount Seir for many days.
Deuteronomy 2:2 And the Lord said to me:
Deuteronomy 2:3 Let it be sufficient for you to go around this mountain; therefore turn toward north.
Deuteronomy 2:4 And command the people, saying: You are passing by through the borders of your brothers, the sons of Esau, who dwell in Seir, and they shall fear you and shall be very wary of you.
Deuteronomy 2:5 Do not join war against them, for I shall certainly not give you any of their land, not even a step of a foot, because I have given Mount Seir to the sons of Esau as an allotment.
Deuteronomy 2:6 Buy foods from them for silver and eat, and you shall take water by measure from them for silver and drink.
Deuteronomy 2:7 For the Lord our God blessed you in every work of your hands. Know thoroughly how you passed through that great and fearful wilderness. Behold, for forty years the Lord your God has been with you; you did not lack a thing. –
Deuteronomy 2:8 And we passed by our brothers, the sons of Esau who dwell in Seir, along the road of Araba from Ailon and from Gasiongaber; and turning, we passed by the road through the wilderness of Moab.
Deuteronomy 2:9 And the Lord said to me: Do not be hostile toward the Moabites, and do not join war against them, for I shall certainly not give you any of their land as an allotment, because I have given Seir to the sons of Lot to inherit.
Deuteronomy 2:10 [The Ommin formerly sat upon it, a great and numerous nation, and strong like the Enakim.
Deuteronomy 2:11 They also shall be reckoned as Raphain like the Enakim, and the Moabites name them Ommin.
Deuteronomy 2:12 And in Seir the Chorraean formerly sat, and the sons of Esau destroyed them and wiped them out from their face and settled in their place, in the manner that Israel did to the land of his inheritance, which the Lord gave them.]
Deuteronomy 2:13 Now therefore rise and set out, you, and pass by the Ravine of Zaret. And we passed by the Ravine of Zaret.
Deuteronomy 2:14 And the days in which we traveled from Cades Barne until we passed by the Ravine of Zaret were thirty-eight years, until the entire generation of warrior men fell away dying from the camp, just as God swore to them.
Deuteronomy 2:15 And the hand of God was upon them to utterly consume them from the camp, until they fell away. –
Deuteronomy 2:16 And it happened when all the warrior men had fallen away dying from the midst of the people,
Deuteronomy 2:17 that the Lord spoke to me, saying:
Deuteronomy 2:18 You shall pass today by the borders of Moab, Seir,
Deuteronomy 2:19 and you shall draw near to the sons of Amman. Do not be hostile toward them, and do not join them in war, for I shall certainly not give you any of the land of the sons of Amman as an allotment, because I have given it to the sons of Lot as an allotment.
Deuteronomy 2:20 [It shall be reckoned as a land of Raphain, for the Raphain also formerly dwelt upon it, and the Ammanites name them Zomzommin,
Deuteronomy 2:21 a great and numerous nation, and more powerful than you, like the Enakim; and the Lord destroyed them before their face, and they inherited and settled in their place until this day,
Deuteronomy 2:22 just as they did for the sons of Esau who dwell in Seir, in the manner that they wiped out the Chorraean from their face and inherited and settled in their place until this day.
Deuteronomy 2:23 And the Evaites who dwelt in Aseroth as far as Gaza, and the Cappadocians who came out of Cappadocia, wiped them out and settled in their place.]
Deuteronomy 2:24 Now therefore rise and set out and pass by the Ravine of Arnon, you. Behold, I have delivered into your hands Seon king of Esebon, the Amorrite, and his land. Begin to inherit; join war against him.
Deuteronomy 2:25 On this day begin to give your trembling and your fear upon the face of all the nations beneath heaven, who, when they hear your name, shall be troubled and shall have birth pangs from your face.
Deuteronomy 2:26 And I sent envoys from the wilderness of Kedamoth to Seon king of Esebon with peaceable words, saying:
Deuteronomy 2:27 I shall pass through your land; on the road I shall pass. I shall not turn aside right or left.
Deuteronomy 2:28 You shall give me food for silver, and I shall eat, and you shall give me water for silver, and I shall drink; only that I shall pass through on foot,
Deuteronomy 2:29 just as the sons of Esau who dwell in Seir and the Moabites who dwell in Aroer did for me, until I cross the Jordan into the land that the Lord our God is giving us.
Deuteronomy 2:30 And Seon king of Esebon was not willing to let us pass through him, because the Lord our God hardened his spirit and strengthened his heart so that he might be delivered into your hands, as on this day.
Deuteronomy 2:31 And the Lord said to me: Behold, I have begun to deliver before your face Seon king of Esebon, the Amorrite, and his land. Begin to inherit his land.
Deuteronomy 2:32 And Seon king of Esebon went out to meet us, he and all his people, for war at Jassa.
Deuteronomy 2:33 And the Lord our God delivered him before our face, and we struck him and his sons and all his people,
Deuteronomy 2:34 and we took control of all his cities at that time and utterly destroyed every city in succession and their women and their children; we left no living captive.
Deuteronomy 2:35 Except the livestock we plundered, and we took the spoils of the cities.
Deuteronomy 2:36 From Aroer, which is beside the lip of the winter-stream Arnon, and the city that is in the ravine, and as far as the mountain of Galaad, there was no city that escaped us; the Lord our God delivered them all into our hands.
Deuteronomy 2:37 But we did not approach the land of the sons of Ammon, all the things adjoining the winter-stream Jabok and the cities in the hill country, just as the Lord our God commanded us. –

## Chapter 3

Deuteronomy 3:1 And turning, we went up by the road into Basan, and Og king of Basan went out to meet us, he and all his people, for war at Edrain.
Deuteronomy 3:2 And the Lord said to me: Do not fear him, because I have delivered him and all his people and all his land into your hands, and you shall do to him as you did to Seon king of the Amorrites, who dwelt in Esebon.
Deuteronomy 3:3 And the Lord our God delivered him into our hands, Og king of Basan and all his people, and we struck him until no seed of his was left.
Deuteronomy 3:4 And we took control of all his cities at that time; there was no city that we did not take from them: sixty cities, all the country around Argob of the kingdom of Og in Basan,
Deuteronomy 3:5 all fortified cities, high walls, gates and bars, apart from the very many cities of the Pherezites.
Deuteronomy 3:6 We utterly destroyed them, as we did to Seon king of Esebon, and we utterly destroyed every city in succession and the women and the children.
Deuteronomy 3:7 And all the livestock and the spoils of the cities we plundered for ourselves.
Deuteronomy 3:8 And at that time we took from the hands of the two kings of the Amorrites the land that was beyond the Jordan, from the winter-stream Arnon and as far as Aermon
Deuteronomy 3:9 [the Phoenicians name Aermon Sanior, and the Amorrite named it Sanir],
Deuteronomy 3:10 all the cities of Misor and all Galaad and all Basan as far as Selcha and Edrain, cities of the kingdom of Og in Basan.
Deuteronomy 3:11 Because only Og king of Basan was left from the Raphain. Behold, his bed was an iron bed; behold, it is at the citadel of the sons of Ammon, nine cubits its length and four cubits its width, by the cubit of a man.
Deuteronomy 3:12 And we inherited that land at that time. From Aroer, which is on the lip of the winter-stream Arnon, and half of Mount Galaad and its cities I gave to Reuben and to Gad.
Deuteronomy 3:13 And the remainder of Galaad and all Basan, the kingdom of Og, I gave to half the tribe of Manasse, and all the country around Argob, all that Basan; it shall be reckoned as land of Raphain.
Deuteronomy 3:14 And Jair son of Manasse took all the country around Argob as far as the borders of Gergasi and Omachathi; he named them after his name, Basan Auoth Jair, until this day.
Deuteronomy 3:15 And to Machir I gave Galaad.
Deuteronomy 3:16 And to Reuben and to Gad I have given from Galaad as far as the winter-stream Arnon [the middle of the winter-stream is a border] and as far as Jabok; the winter-stream is a border for the sons of Amman.
Deuteronomy 3:17 And Araba and the Jordan are a border of Machanareth and as far as the Sea of Araba, the Salt Sea, under Asedoth Phasga toward east. –
Deuteronomy 3:18 And I commanded you at that time, saying: The Lord your God gave you this land as an allotment. Armed, go ahead before the face of your brothers, the sons of Israel, every powerful man.
Deuteronomy 3:19 Except your wives and your children and your livestock – I know that you have much livestock – let them dwell in your cities that I gave you,
Deuteronomy 3:20 until the Lord your God gives your brothers rest as also you, and these also shall inherit the land that the Lord our God is giving them beyond the Jordan, and you shall each return to his inheritance that I gave you.
Deuteronomy 3:21 And I commanded Jesus at that time, saying: Your eyes have seen all the things that the Lord our God did to these two kings; thus the Lord our God shall do to all the kingdoms upon which you cross there.
Deuteronomy 3:22 You shall not fear, because the Lord our God himself shall fight for you. –
Deuteronomy 3:23 And I entreated the Lord at that time, saying:
Deuteronomy 3:24 Lord, Lord, you began to show your attendant your strength and your power and the mighty hand and the high arm; for what god is there in heaven or upon the earth who shall do just as you did and according to your strength?
Deuteronomy 3:25 Having crossed over, therefore, I shall see this good land that is beyond the Jordan, this good mountain and Antilibanus.
Deuteronomy 3:26 And the Lord overlooked me because of you and did not listen to me, and the Lord said to me: Let it be sufficient for you; do not add still more to speak this word.
Deuteronomy 3:27 Go up to the summit of the Hewn One, and lifting your eyes, look toward the sea and north and southwest and east, and see with your eyes, because you shall not cross this Jordan.
Deuteronomy 3:28 And command Jesus and strengthen him and encourage him, because he shall cross before the face of this people, and he shall cause them to inherit the land that you have seen. –
Deuteronomy 3:29 And we sat in a wooded valley very near the house of Phogor.

## Chapter 4

Deuteronomy 4:1 And now, Israel, hear the ordinances and the judgments, as many as I teach you today to do, so that you may live and be multiplied and, entering, inherit the land that the Lord, the God of your fathers, is giving you.
Deuteronomy 4:2 You shall not add to the word that I command you, and you shall not remove from it. Guard the commandments of the Lord your God, as many as I command you today.
Deuteronomy 4:3 Your eyes have seen all the things that the Lord our God did to Beelphogor, because every person who went after Beelphogor, the Lord your God wiped him out from among you.
Deuteronomy 4:4 But you who are attached to the Lord your God all live on this day.
Deuteronomy 4:5 See, I have shown you ordinances and judgments, just as the Lord commanded me, to do thus in the land into which you are entering there to inherit it.
Deuteronomy 4:6 And you shall guard and do them, because this is your wisdom and understanding before all the nations, whoever hear all these ordinances and shall say: Behold, a wise and knowledgeable people, this great nation.
Deuteronomy 4:7 For what great nation is there that has a god drawing near to them, as the Lord our God is in all things for which we may call upon him?
Deuteronomy 4:8 And what great nation is there that has righteous ordinances and judgments according to all this law that I give before you today?
Deuteronomy 4:9 Attend to yourself and guard your soul greatly, lest you forget all the words that your eyes have seen; and let them not depart from your heart all the days of your life, and you shall instruct your sons and the sons of your sons
Deuteronomy 4:10 the day on which you stood before the Lord your God in Choreb on the day of the assembly, when the Lord said to me: Assemble the people to me, and let them hear my words, so that they may learn to fear me all the days that they live upon the land and may teach their sons.
Deuteronomy 4:11 And you approached and stood beneath the mountain, and the mountain was burning with fire as far as heaven: darkness, gloom, storm, a loud voice.
Deuteronomy 4:12 And the Lord spoke to you from the midst of the fire; you heard a voice of words and saw no likeness, except a voice.
Deuteronomy 4:13 And he reported to you his covenant, which he commanded you to do, the ten words, and he wrote them upon two stone tablets.
Deuteronomy 4:14 And the Lord commanded me at that time to teach you ordinances and judgments, for you to do them upon the land into which you are entering there to inherit it.
Deuteronomy 4:15 And guard your souls greatly, because you saw no likeness on the day when the Lord spoke to you in Choreb on the mountain from the midst of the fire,
Deuteronomy 4:16 lest you act lawlessly and make for yourselves a carved likeness, every image, a likeness of a male or female,
Deuteronomy 4:17 a likeness of every animal that is upon the land, a likeness of every winged bird that flies beneath heaven,
Deuteronomy 4:18 a likeness of every creeping thing that creeps upon the land, a likeness of every fish, as many as are in the waters beneath the land.
Deuteronomy 4:19 And do not, having looked up into heaven and seen the sun and the moon and the stars and all the order of heaven, being led astray, bow to them and serve them, which the Lord your God apportioned, them, to all the nations beneath heaven.
Deuteronomy 4:20 But God took you and brought you out from the iron furnace, from Egypt, to be an allotted people for him, as on this day.
Deuteronomy 4:21 And the Lord was enraged at me concerning the things said by you and swore that I would not cross this Jordan and would not enter into the land that the Lord God is giving you as an allotment.
Deuteronomy 4:22 For I am dying in this land and am not crossing this Jordan, but you are crossing and shall inherit this good land.
Deuteronomy 4:23 Pay attention, lest you forget the covenant of the Lord your God that he established with you and make for yourselves a carved likeness of all things that the Lord your God prescribed.
Deuteronomy 4:24 Because the Lord your God is a consuming fire, a jealous god.
Deuteronomy 4:25 But if you bear sons and sons of your sons and you remain long upon the land and act lawlessly and make a carved likeness of anything and do wicked things before the Lord your God to provoke him,
Deuteronomy 4:26 I call both heaven and earth to witness to you today that by destruction you shall be destroyed from the land into which you are crossing the Jordan there to inherit it. You shall not prolong days upon it, but rather by wiping out you shall be wiped out.
Deuteronomy 4:27 And the Lord shall scatter you among all the nations, and you shall be left few by number among the nations into which the Lord shall lead you there.
Deuteronomy 4:28 And there you shall serve other gods, works of human hands, wood and stones, who shall not see or certainly hear, neither certainly eat nor certainly smell.
Deuteronomy 4:29 And there you shall seek the Lord your God and shall find him whenever you search him out from your whole heart and from your whole soul in your affliction.
Deuteronomy 4:30 And all these words shall find you at the end of the days, and you shall turn to the Lord your God and listen to his voice,
Deuteronomy 4:31 because the Lord your God is a compassionate god; he shall not abandon you or certainly wipe you out, and he shall not forget the covenant of your fathers that he swore to them.
Deuteronomy 4:32 Ask about the former days that came before you, from the day on which God created a human upon the land, and from one end of heaven as far as the other end of heaven, whether anything has happened according to this great word, whether anything like it has been heard:
Deuteronomy 4:33 whether a nation has heard a voice of a living god speaking from the midst of the fire, in the manner that you have heard, and lived;
Deuteronomy 4:34 whether God attempted, entering, to take for himself a nation from the midst of a nation, by trial and by signs and by wonders and by war and by a mighty hand and by a high arm and by great visions, according to all the things that the Lord our God did in Egypt before you while you watched,
Deuteronomy 4:35 so that you would know that the Lord your God, he is God, and there is no one else besides him.
Deuteronomy 4:36 From heaven his voice became audible to discipline you, and upon the land he showed you his great fire, and you heard his words from the midst of the fire.
Deuteronomy 4:37 Because he loved your fathers, and he chose their seed after them, you, and he himself brought you out by his great strength from Egypt,
Deuteronomy 4:38 to utterly destroy great nations stronger than you from before your face, to bring you in, to give you their land to inherit, just as you have today.
Deuteronomy 4:39 And you shall know today and turn in your mind that the Lord your God, he is God in heaven above and upon the land below, and there is no one else besides him.
Deuteronomy 4:40 And you shall guard his ordinances and his commandments, as many as I command you today, so that it may become well for you and for your sons after you, so that you may become long-lived upon the land that the Lord your God is giving you for all the days.
Deuteronomy 4:41 Then Moses separated three cities beyond the Jordan from the east of the sun,
Deuteronomy 4:42 for the killer to flee there who kills his neighbor without knowing and was not hating him before yesterday and the third day; and he shall flee to one of these cities and live:
Deuteronomy 4:43 Bosor in the wilderness in the plain land for Reuben, and Ramoth in Galaad for Gaddi, and Gaulon in Basan for Manasse.
Deuteronomy 4:44 This is the law that Moses set before the sons of Israel.
Deuteronomy 4:45 These are the testimonies and the ordinances and the judgments, as many as Moses spoke to the sons of Israel in the wilderness when they had gone out from the land of Egypt,
Deuteronomy 4:46 beyond the Jordan in a ravine near the house of Phogor, in the land of Seon king of the Amorrites, who dwelt in Esebon, whom Moses and the sons of Israel struck when they had gone out from the land of Egypt.
Deuteronomy 4:47 And they inherited his land and the land of Og king of Basan, two kings of the Amorrites who were beyond the Jordan toward the east of the sun,
Deuteronomy 4:48 from Aroer, which is on the lip of the winter-stream Arnon, and upon Mount Seon, which is Aermon,
Deuteronomy 4:49 all Araba beyond the Jordan toward the east of the sun, under Asedoth the Hewn.

## Chapter 5

Deuteronomy 5:1 And Moses called all Israel and said to them: Hear, Israel, the ordinances and the judgments, as many as I speak in your ears on this day, and you shall learn them and guard to do them.
Deuteronomy 5:2 The Lord your God established a covenant with you in Choreb.
Deuteronomy 5:3 The Lord did not establish this covenant with your fathers, but rather with you, you who are all here living today.
Deuteronomy 5:4 Face against face the Lord spoke to you on the mountain from the midst of the fire –
Deuteronomy 5:5 and I had stood between the Lord and you at that time to report to you the words of the Lord, because you were afraid from before the fire and did not go up into the mountain – saying:
Deuteronomy 5:6 I am the Lord your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt, out of a house of slavery.
Deuteronomy 5:7 There shall be no other gods for you before my face. –
Deuteronomy 5:8 You shall not make for yourself an idol or any likeness of as many things as are in heaven above and as many things as are on the land below and as many things as are in the waters beneath the land.
Deuteronomy 5:9 You shall not bow down to them, nor shall you ever serve them, because I am the Lord your God, a jealous god, repaying the sins of fathers upon children as far as the third and fourth generation to those who hate me,
Deuteronomy 5:10 and doing mercy to thousands, to those who love me and those who keep my ordinances. –
Deuteronomy 5:11 You shall not take the name of the Lord your God in vain, for the Lord will certainly not cleanse the one who takes his name in vain. –
Deuteronomy 5:12 Guard the day of the sabbaths, to sanctify it, in the manner that the Lord your God commanded you.
Deuteronomy 5:13 Six days you shall labor and do all your works.
Deuteronomy 5:14 But on the seventh day are sabbaths to the Lord your God. You shall not do any work on it, you and your sons and your daughter, your servant and your female servant, your ox and your draft animal and all your livestock and the proselyte who sojourns within you, so that your servant and your female servant may rest just as you.
Deuteronomy 5:15 And you shall remember that you were a household servant in the land of Egypt and the Lord your God brought you out from there by a mighty hand and by a high arm. Because of this the Lord your God prescribed to you that you guard the day of the sabbaths and sanctify it. –
Deuteronomy 5:16 Honor your father and your mother, in the manner that the Lord your God commanded you, so that it may become well for you and so that you may become long-lived upon the land that the Lord your God gives you. –
Deuteronomy 5:17 You shall not commit adultery. –
Deuteronomy 5:18 You shall not murder. –
Deuteronomy 5:19 You shall not steal. –
Deuteronomy 5:20 You shall not bear false witness against your neighbor, false testimony. –
Deuteronomy 5:21 You shall not desire the woman of your neighbor. You shall not desire the house of your neighbor, nor his field, nor his servant, nor his female servant, nor his ox, nor his draft animal, nor any of his livestock, nor as many things as belong to your neighbor.
Deuteronomy 5:22 These words the Lord spoke to your entire congregation on the mountain from the midst of the fire: darkness, gloom, storm, a loud voice; and he did not add. And he wrote them upon two stone tablets and gave them to me.
Deuteronomy 5:23 And it happened when you heard the voice from the midst of the fire and the mountain was burning with fire, that you approached me, all the leaders of your tribes and your council of elders,
Deuteronomy 5:24 and you were saying: Behold, the Lord our God showed us his glory, and we heard his voice from the midst of the fire. On this day we saw that God shall speak to a person and he shall live.
Deuteronomy 5:25 And now, let us not die, because this great fire shall utterly consume us. If we ourselves continue to hear the voice of the Lord our God any longer, then we shall die.
Deuteronomy 5:26 For what flesh is there that has heard a voice of a living god speaking from the midst of the fire as we have and shall live?
Deuteronomy 5:27 You approach and hear as many things as the Lord our God may say, and you shall speak to us all the things that the Lord our God may speak to you, and we shall hear and do them.
Deuteronomy 5:28 And the Lord heard the voice of your words as you were speaking to me, and the Lord said to me: I heard the voice of the words of this people, as many things as they spoke to you; all the things that they spoke were correct.
Deuteronomy 5:29 Who shall give their heart to be thus in them, so as to fear me and guard my commandments all the days, so that it may be well for them and for their sons through the age?
Deuteronomy 5:30 Walk, say to them: Turn back, you, to your houses.
Deuteronomy 5:31 But you, stand here with me, and I shall speak to you the commandments and the ordinances and the judgments, as many as you shall teach them, and let them do them in the land that I am giving them as an allotment.
Deuteronomy 5:32 And you shall guard to do in the manner that the Lord your God commanded you; you shall not turn aside to the right or to the left,
Deuteronomy 5:33 according to all the road that the Lord your God commanded you to walk upon, so that he may give you rest and it may be well for you and you may become long-lived upon the land that you shall inherit.

## Chapter 6

Deuteronomy 6:1 And these are the commandments and the ordinances and the judgments, as many as the Lord our God commanded to teach you to do thus in the land into which you are entering there to inherit it,
Deuteronomy 6:2 so that you may fear the Lord your God by guarding all his ordinances and his commandments, as many as I command you today, you and your sons and the sons of your sons, all the days of your life, so that you may become long-lived.
Deuteronomy 6:3 And hear, Israel, and guard to do them, so that it may be well for you and so that you may be multiplied greatly, just as the Lord, the God of your fathers, spoke, to give you a land flowing with milk and honey.
Deuteronomy 6:4 And these are the ordinances and the judgments, as many as the Lord commanded the sons of Israel in the wilderness when they had gone out from the land of Egypt: Hear, Israel; the Lord our God is one Lord.
Deuteronomy 6:5 And you shall love the Lord your God from your whole heart and from your whole soul and from your whole power.
Deuteronomy 6:6 And these words, as many as I command you today, shall be in your heart and in your soul.
Deuteronomy 6:7 And you shall teach them to your sons and speak about them while sitting in your house and traveling on the road and lying down and rising up.
Deuteronomy 6:8 And you shall fasten them as a sign upon your hand, and it shall be immovable before your eyes.
Deuteronomy 6:9 And you shall write them upon the doorposts of your houses and of your gates.
Deuteronomy 6:10 And it shall be when the Lord your God brings you into the land that he swore to your fathers, Abraham and Isaac and Jacob, to give you, great and beautiful cities that you did not build,
Deuteronomy 6:11 houses full of all good things that you did not fill, hewn pits that you did not hew out, vineyards and olive groves that you did not plant, and when you have eaten and been filled,
Deuteronomy 6:12 pay attention to yourself, lest you forget the Lord your God, who brought you out from the land of Egypt, out of a house of slavery.
Deuteronomy 6:13 You shall fear the Lord your God, and you shall serve him and be joined to him and swear by his name.
Deuteronomy 6:14 You shall not go after other gods, from the gods of the nations around you,
Deuteronomy 6:15 because the Lord your God among you is a jealous god, lest the Lord your God, becoming angry, be enraged at you and utterly destroy you from the face of the land.
Deuteronomy 6:16 You shall not put the Lord your God to the test, in the manner that you put him to the test at Temptation.
Deuteronomy 6:17 By guarding, you shall guard the commandments of the Lord your God, the testimonies and the ordinances, as many as he commanded you.
Deuteronomy 6:18 And you shall do what is pleasing and good before the Lord your God, so that it may become well for you and you may enter and inherit the good land that the Lord swore to your fathers,
Deuteronomy 6:19 to drive out all your enemies from before your face, just as he spoke.
Deuteronomy 6:20 And it shall be when your son asks you tomorrow, saying: What are the testimonies and the ordinances and the judgments, as many as the Lord our God commanded us?
Deuteronomy 6:21 And you shall say to your son: We were household servants to Pharao in the land of Egypt, and the Lord brought us out from there by a mighty hand and by a high arm.
Deuteronomy 6:22 And the Lord gave signs and wonders, great and evil, in Egypt, in Pharao and in his house, before us.
Deuteronomy 6:23 And he brought us out from there so that he might bring us in, to give us this land that he swore to give to our fathers.
Deuteronomy 6:24 And the Lord commanded us to do all these ordinances, to fear the Lord our God, so that it may be well for us all the days, so that we may live just as also today.
Deuteronomy 6:25 And mercy shall be for us if we guard to do all these commandments before the Lord our God, just as the Lord commanded us.

## Chapter 7

Deuteronomy 7:1 But if the Lord your God brings you into the land into which you are entering there to inherit it, and removes great nations from before your face, the Chettite and Gergesite and Amorrite and Chanaanite and Pherezite and Evite and Jebousite, seven nations, numerous and stronger than you,
Deuteronomy 7:2 and the Lord your God shall deliver them into your hands and you shall strike them, with obliteration you shall obliterate them. You shall not establish a covenant with them, nor shall you ever show them mercy.
Deuteronomy 7:3 Nor shall you ever intermarry with them. You shall not give your daughter to his son, and you shall not take his daughter for your son.
Deuteronomy 7:4 For he shall turn your son away from me, and he shall serve other gods, and the Lord shall be angered with wrath against you and shall utterly destroy you quickly.
Deuteronomy 7:5 But thus you shall do to them: You shall take down their altars and crush their pillars and cut down their groves and burn the carved images of their gods with fire.
Deuteronomy 7:6 Because you are a holy people to the Lord your God, and the Lord your God preferred you to be a peculiar people for him beyond all the nations that are upon the face of the land.
Deuteronomy 7:7 It was not because you are more numerous than all the nations that the Lord preferred you and chose you – for you are the fewest of all the nations –
Deuteronomy 7:8 but because the Lord loves you and keeps the oath that he swore to your fathers, the Lord brought you out by a mighty hand and by a high arm and redeemed you out of a house of slavery, from the hand of Pharao king of Egypt.
Deuteronomy 7:9 And you shall know that the Lord your God, he is God, a faithful god, who guards covenant and mercy for those who love him and those who guard his commandments, for a thousand generations,
Deuteronomy 7:10 and repays those who hate him to their face, to utterly destroy them. And he shall not delay toward those who hate him; to their face he shall repay them.
Deuteronomy 7:11 And you shall guard these commandments and ordinances and judgments, as many as I command you today to do.
Deuteronomy 7:12 And it shall be whenever you hear all these ordinances and guard and do them, that the Lord your God shall also safeguard for you the covenant and the mercy that he swore to your fathers.
Deuteronomy 7:13 And he shall love you and bless you and multiply you, and he shall bless the offspring of your womb and the fruit of your land, your wheat and your wine and your oil, the herds of your cattle and the flocks of your sheep, upon the land that the Lord swore to your fathers to give you.
Deuteronomy 7:14 You shall be blessed beyond all the nations. There shall be no childless man or barren woman among you, or among your livestock.
Deuteronomy 7:15 And the Lord shall remove from you every infirmity, and all the evil diseases of Egypt that you have seen and as many as you knew, he shall not place upon you, but he shall place them upon all those who hate you.
Deuteronomy 7:16 And you shall eat all the spoils of the nations that the Lord your God is giving you. Your eye shall not spare them, and you shall not serve their gods, because this is a stumbling block for you.
Deuteronomy 7:17 But if you say in your mind: This nation is more numerous than I am; how shall I be able utterly to destroy them?
Deuteronomy 7:18 You shall not fear them. By remembrance you shall remember the things that the Lord your God did to Pharao and to all the Egyptians,
Deuteronomy 7:19 the great trials that your eyes saw, those great signs and wonders, the mighty hand and the high arm, how the Lord your God brought you out. Thus the Lord our God shall do to all the nations whose face you fear.
Deuteronomy 7:20 And the Lord your God shall send the hornets against them until those left behind and those hidden from you are wiped out.
Deuteronomy 7:21 You shall not be wounded from before their face, because the Lord your God is among you, a great and mighty god.
Deuteronomy 7:22 And the Lord your God shall consume these nations from before your face little by little. You shall not be able utterly to consume them quickly, lest the land become desolate and the wild beasts multiply against you.
Deuteronomy 7:23 And the Lord your God shall deliver them into your hands and shall destroy them with great destruction until he utterly destroys them.
Deuteronomy 7:24 And he shall deliver their kings into your hands, and their name shall perish from that place. No one shall stand against your face until you utterly destroy them.
Deuteronomy 7:25 You shall burn the carved images of their gods with fire. You shall not desire silver or gold from them and shall not take it for yourself, lest you stumble because of it, because it is an abomination to the Lord your God.
Deuteronomy 7:26 And you shall not bring an abomination into your house, and you shall be an anathema like it. With loathing you shall loathe it, and with abomination you shall abhor it, because it is an anathema.

## Chapter 8

Deuteronomy 8:1 All the commandments that I command you today you shall guard to do, so that you may live and be multiplied and enter and inherit the land that the Lord your God swore to your fathers.
Deuteronomy 8:2 And you shall remember all the road by which the Lord your God led you in the wilderness, so that he might afflict you and put you to the test and the things in your heart might be discerned, whether you would guard his commandments or not.
Deuteronomy 8:3 And he afflicted you and made you hungry and fed you the manna, which your fathers did not know, so that he might declare to you that a person shall not live on bread alone, but a person shall live on every word that proceeds through the mouth of God.
Deuteronomy 8:4 Your garments were not worn down from you; your feet did not become callused. Behold, forty years.
Deuteronomy 8:5 And you shall know in your heart that as if a person might discipline his son, thus the Lord your God shall discipline you.
Deuteronomy 8:6 And you shall guard the commandments of the Lord your God, to walk in his ways and to fear him.
Deuteronomy 8:7 For the Lord your God is bringing you into a good and extensive land, where there are winter-streams of water and springs of depths coming out through the plains and through the mountains,
Deuteronomy 8:8 a land of wheat and barley, vines, fig trees, pomegranates, a land of olive oil and honey,
Deuteronomy 8:9 a land upon which you shall eat your bread not with poverty and shall lack nothing upon it, a land whose stones are iron and from whose mountains you shall mine copper.
Deuteronomy 8:10 And you shall eat and be filled and bless the Lord your God upon the good land that he gave you.
Deuteronomy 8:11 Pay attention to yourself, lest you forget the Lord your God by not guarding his commandments and his judgments and ordinances, as many as I command you today,
Deuteronomy 8:12 lest, after eating and being filled and building beautiful houses and dwelling in them,
Deuteronomy 8:13 and when your cattle and your sheep have been multiplied for you, silver and gold have been multiplied for you, and everything that you shall have has been multiplied for you,
Deuteronomy 8:14 you be exalted in heart and forget the Lord your God, who brought you out from the land of Egypt, out of a house of slavery,
Deuteronomy 8:15 who led you through that great and fearful wilderness, where there were a biting snake and a scorpion and thirst, where there was no water, who brought out for you from a sheer rock a spring of water,
Deuteronomy 8:16 who fed you the manna in the wilderness, which your fathers did not know, so that he might afflict you and put you to the test and do you good at the end of your days.
Deuteronomy 8:17 Do not say in your heart: My strength and the might of my hand made this great power for me.
Deuteronomy 8:18 And you shall remember the Lord your God, because he gives you strength to make power and so that he may establish his covenant that the Lord swore to your fathers, as today.
Deuteronomy 8:19 And it shall be if by forgetting you forget the Lord your God and go after other gods and serve them and bow to them, I call both heaven and earth to witness to you today that by destruction you shall be destroyed.
Deuteronomy 8:20 Just as also the remaining nations that the Lord destroys from before your face, thus you shall be destroyed, because you did not listen to the voice of the Lord your God.

## Chapter 9

Deuteronomy 9:1 Hear, Israel: You are crossing the Jordan today to enter and inherit nations great and stronger than you, great cities walled as far as heaven,
Deuteronomy 9:2 a great and numerous and tall people, sons of Enak, whom you know and of whom you have heard: Who shall stand against the face of the sons of Enak?
Deuteronomy 9:3 And you shall know today that the Lord your God, he goes before your face. He is a consuming fire. He shall utterly destroy them, and he shall turn them away from before your face, and you shall destroy them, just as the Lord said to you.
Deuteronomy 9:4 Do not say in your heart when the Lord your God utterly consumes these nations from before your face, saying: Because of my righteousnesses the Lord brought me in to inherit this good land. But because of the impiety of these nations the Lord shall utterly destroy them from before your face.
Deuteronomy 9:5 It is not because of your righteousness or because of the piety of your heart that you are entering to inherit their land, but because of the impiety of these nations the Lord shall utterly destroy them from before your face, and so that he may establish his covenant that he swore to your fathers, Abraham and Isaac and Jacob.
Deuteronomy 9:6 And you shall know today that it is not because of your righteousnesses that the Lord your God is giving you this good land to inherit, because you are a stiff-necked people.
Deuteronomy 9:7 Remember; do not forget how much you provoked the Lord your God in the wilderness. From the day that you went out from Egypt until you came to this place, you continued being disobedient in the things toward the Lord.
Deuteronomy 9:8 And in Choreb you provoked the Lord, and the Lord was enraged against you, to utterly destroy you,
Deuteronomy 9:9 when I went up into the mountain to receive the stone tablets, tablets of the covenant that the Lord established with you. And I remained on the mountain forty days and forty nights; I did not eat bread and did not drink water.
Deuteronomy 9:10 And the Lord gave me the two stone tablets written by the finger of God, and on them had been written all the words that the Lord spoke to you on the mountain on the day of the assembly.
Deuteronomy 9:11 And it happened after forty days and forty nights that the Lord gave me the two stone tablets, tablets of the covenant.
Deuteronomy 9:12 And the Lord said to me: Rise, go down quickly from here, because your people whom you brought out from the land of Egypt acted lawlessly. They quickly transgressed from the road that you commanded them; they made for themselves a cast thing.
Deuteronomy 9:13 And the Lord said to me: I have spoken to you once and twice, saying: I have seen this people, and behold, they are a stiff-necked people.
Deuteronomy 9:14 Leave me to utterly destroy them, and I shall wipe away their name from beneath heaven and make you into a nation great and strong and much more numerous than this one.
Deuteronomy 9:15 And turning, I went down from the mountain, and the mountain was burning with fire, and the two tablets were upon my two hands.
Deuteronomy 9:16 And when I saw that you had sinned before the Lord your God and made for yourselves a cast thing and transgressed from the road that the Lord commanded you,
Deuteronomy 9:17 then, taking hold of the two tablets, I threw them from my two hands and crushed them before you.
Deuteronomy 9:18 And I entreated before the Lord a second time, just as also the first, for forty days and forty nights – I did not eat bread and did not drink water – concerning all your sins by which you sinned, doing what was wicked before the Lord your God, to provoke him.
Deuteronomy 9:19 And I am terrified because of the anger and the wrath, because the Lord was provoked against you, to utterly destroy you. And the Lord listened to me also at this time.
Deuteronomy 9:20 And the Lord was greatly enraged against Aaron, to utterly destroy him, and I prayed also concerning Aaron at that time.
Deuteronomy 9:21 And your sin that you made, the calf, I took and burned it with fire and broke it in pieces, grinding it thoroughly until it became fine. And it became like dust, and I threw the dust into the winter-stream that descends from the mountain. –
Deuteronomy 9:22 And at Burning and at Temptation and at the Memorials of Desire you were provoking the Lord your God.
Deuteronomy 9:23 And when the Lord sent you out from Cades Barne, saying: Go up and inherit the land that I am giving you, you disobeyed the word of the Lord your God and did not trust him and did not listen to his voice.
Deuteronomy 9:24 You were disobedient in the things toward the Lord from the day when he became known to you. –
Deuteronomy 9:25 And I entreated before the Lord for forty days and forty nights, as many as I entreated – for the Lord said to utterly destroy you –
Deuteronomy 9:26 and I prayed to God and said: Lord, Lord, King of the gods, do not utterly destroy your people and your portion, whom you redeemed by your great strength, whom you brought out from the land of Egypt by your great strength and by your mighty hand and by your high arm.
Deuteronomy 9:27 Remember Abraham and Isaac and Jacob, your attendants, to whom you swore by yourself. Do not look upon the hardness of this people and their impieties and their sins,
Deuteronomy 9:28 lest those dwelling in the land from which you brought us say: Because the Lord was not able to bring them into the land that he told them of, and because he hated them, he brought them out to kill them in the wilderness.
Deuteronomy 9:29 And these are your people and your allotment, whom you brought out from the land of Egypt by your great strength and by your high arm.

## Chapter 10

Deuteronomy 10:1 At that time the Lord said to me: Hew for yourself two stone tablets like the first ones and come up to me onto the mountain. And you shall make for yourself a wooden ark.
Deuteronomy 10:2 And I shall write upon the tablets the words that were in the first tablets, which you crushed, and you shall put them into the ark.
Deuteronomy 10:3 And I made an ark from incorruptible wood and hewed the two stone tablets like the first ones. And I went up into the mountain, and the two tablets were upon my hands.
Deuteronomy 10:4 And he wrote upon the tablets, according to the first writing, the ten words that the Lord spoke to you on the mountain from the midst of the fire, and the Lord gave them to me.
Deuteronomy 10:5 And turning, I went down from the mountain and put the tablets into the ark that I made, and they were there, just as the Lord commanded me. –
Deuteronomy 10:6 And the sons of Israel departed from Beroth of the sons of Jakim Misadai. There Aaron died and was buried there, and Eleazar his son served as priest in his place.
Deuteronomy 10:7 From there they departed to Gadgad, and from Gadgad to Etebatha, a land of winter-streams of water.
Deuteronomy 10:8 At that time the Lord distinguished the tribe of Levi to carry the ark of the covenant of the Lord, to stand before the Lord, to minister, and to invoke his name until this day.
Deuteronomy 10:9 Because of this there is no portion and allotment for the Levites among their brothers. The Lord himself is his allotment, just as he said to him.
Deuteronomy 10:10 And I had stood on the mountain forty days and forty nights, and the Lord listened to me also at this time, and the Lord was not willing utterly to destroy you.
Deuteronomy 10:11 And the Lord said to me: Walk, set out before this people, and let them enter and inherit the land that I swore to their fathers to give them.
Deuteronomy 10:12 And now, Israel, what does the Lord your God request from you except to fear the Lord your God, to walk in all his ways and to love him and to serve the Lord your God from your whole heart and from your whole soul,
Deuteronomy 10:13 to guard the commandments of the Lord your God and his ordinances, as many as I command you today, so that it may be well for you?
Deuteronomy 10:14 Behold, the heaven and the heaven of heaven, the land and all that is in it, belong to the Lord your God.
Deuteronomy 10:15 Nevertheless, the Lord preferred your fathers, to love them, and chose their seed after them, you, beyond all the nations, as on this day.
Deuteronomy 10:16 And you shall circumcise your hard-heartedness, and you shall no longer harden your neck.
Deuteronomy 10:17 For the Lord your God, he is God of the gods and Lord of the lords, the great and strong and fearsome God, who does not marvel at a face, nor shall he certainly take a gift,
Deuteronomy 10:18 who does judgment for the proselyte and orphan and widow, and loves the proselyte, to give him bread and a garment.
Deuteronomy 10:19 And you shall love the proselyte, for you were proselytes in the land of Egypt.
Deuteronomy 10:20 You shall fear the Lord your God, and you shall serve him and be joined to him and swear by his name.
Deuteronomy 10:21 He is your boast and he is your God, who did among you these great and glorious things that your eyes saw.
Deuteronomy 10:22 With seventy souls your fathers went down into Egypt, but now the Lord your God made you like the stars of heaven in multitude.

## Chapter 11

Deuteronomy 11:1 And you shall love the Lord your God and guard his observances and his ordinances and his judgments all the days.
Deuteronomy 11:2 And you shall know today that it was not your children, as many as do not know and did not see the discipline of the Lord your God and his great deeds and the mighty hand and the high arm,
Deuteronomy 11:3 and his signs and his wonders, as many as he did in the midst of Egypt to Pharao king of Egypt and to all his land,
Deuteronomy 11:4 and as many things as he did to the force of the Egyptians, their chariots and their horse force, how the water of the Red Sea flooded over their face as they pursued from behind you, and the Lord destroyed them until this day,
Deuteronomy 11:5 and as many things as he did to you in the wilderness until you came to this place,
Deuteronomy 11:6 and as many things as he did to Dathan and Abiron, sons of Eliab son of Reuben, whom the land, opening its mouth, swallowed, and their houses and their tents and all their substance that was with them, in the midst of all Israel,
Deuteronomy 11:7 because your eyes have seen all the great works of the Lord, as many as he did to you today.
Deuteronomy 11:8 And you shall guard all his commandments, as many as I command you today, so that you may live and be multiplied and, entering, inherit the land into which you are crossing the Jordan there to inherit it,
Deuteronomy 11:9 so that you may become long-lived upon the land that the Lord swore to your fathers to give to them and to their seed after them, a land flowing with milk and honey.
Deuteronomy 11:10 For the land into which you are entering there to inherit it is not like the land of Egypt from which you went out, where they sow the seed and water it with their feet like a vegetable garden.
Deuteronomy 11:11 But the land into which you are entering there to inherit it is a mountainous and plain land; it drinks water from the rain of heaven,
Deuteronomy 11:12 a land that the Lord your God oversees. Continually the eyes of the Lord your God are upon it, from the beginning of the year even until the completion of the year.
Deuteronomy 11:13 But if by hearing you listen to all his commandments, as many as I command you today, to love the Lord your God and to serve him from your whole heart and from your whole soul,
Deuteronomy 11:14 then he shall give the rain to your land in season, early and late, and you shall bring in your wheat and your wine and your oil.
Deuteronomy 11:15 And he shall give fodder in your fields for your livestock, and when you have eaten and been filled,
Deuteronomy 11:16 pay attention to yourself, lest your heart be broadened and you transgress and serve other gods and bow to them,
Deuteronomy 11:17 and the Lord, enraged with anger against you, close up heaven, and there shall be no rain, and the land shall not give its fruit, and you shall perish quickly from the good land that the Lord gave you.
Deuteronomy 11:18 And you shall put these words into your heart and into your soul, and you shall fasten them as a sign upon your hand, and it shall be immovable before your eyes.
Deuteronomy 11:19 And you shall teach your children to speak them while sitting in the house and traveling on the road and lying down and rising up.
Deuteronomy 11:20 And you shall write them upon the doorposts of your houses and of your gates,
Deuteronomy 11:21 so that you may live many days, and the days of your sons upon the land that the Lord swore to your fathers to give them may be many, like the days of heaven upon the land.
Deuteronomy 11:22 And it shall be if by hearing you hear all these commandments, as many as I command you today to do, to love the Lord our God and to walk in all his ways and to be joined to him,
Deuteronomy 11:23 that the Lord shall drive out all these nations from before your face, and you shall inherit nations great and stronger than you.
Deuteronomy 11:24 Every place where the track of your foot may tread shall be yours. From the wilderness and Antilibanus and from the great river, the river Euphrates, and as far as the sea toward the west shall be your borders.
Deuteronomy 11:25 No one shall stand against your face. The Lord your God shall place your trembling and your fear upon the face of all the land on which you may set foot, in the manner that the Lord spoke to you.
Deuteronomy 11:26 Behold, I give before you today a blessing and a curse:
Deuteronomy 11:27 the blessing, if you hear the commandments of the Lord your God that I command you today,
Deuteronomy 11:28 and the curses, if you do not hear the commandments of the Lord your God, as many as I command you today, and you are led astray from the road that I commanded you, going to serve other gods that you do not know.
Deuteronomy 11:29 And it shall be when the Lord your God brings you into the land into which you are crossing there to inherit it, that you shall give the blessing upon Mount Garizin and the curse upon Mount Gaibal.
Deuteronomy 11:30 [Behold, are these not beyond the Jordan, behind the road of the setting of the sun, in the land of Chanaan, the one dwelling toward the west, adjoining Golgol, near the high oak?]
Deuteronomy 11:31 For you are crossing the Jordan, entering to inherit the land that the Lord your God is giving you as an allotment all the days, and you shall inherit it and dwell in it.
Deuteronomy 11:32 And you shall guard yourselves to do all his commands and these judgments, as many as I give before you today.

## Chapter 12

Deuteronomy 12:1 And these are the commands and the judgments that you shall guard to do upon the land that the Lord, the God of your fathers, is giving you as an allotment, all the days that you live upon the land.
Deuteronomy 12:2 By destruction you shall destroy all the places in which those whom you are inheriting served their gods there, upon the high mountains and upon the dunes and beneath a dense tree.
Deuteronomy 12:3 And you shall dig down their altars and crush their pillars and cut down their groves and burn the carved images of their gods with fire, and their name shall perish from that place.
Deuteronomy 12:4 You shall not do thus to the Lord your God,
Deuteronomy 12:5 but rather to the place that the Lord your God may choose in one of your tribes, to name his name there, for it to be called upon; and you shall seek out and enter there.
Deuteronomy 12:6 And you shall bring there your whole burnt offerings and your sacrifices and your firstfruits and your vows and your voluntary offerings and the firstborn of your cattle and of your sheep.
Deuteronomy 12:7 And you shall eat there before the Lord your God and rejoice over everything upon which you may lay your hand, you and your houses, because the Lord your God blessed you.
Deuteronomy 12:8 You shall not do all the things that we do here today, each doing what is pleasing before him,
Deuteronomy 12:9 for you have not come until now into the rest and into the inheritance that the Lord your God is giving you.
Deuteronomy 12:10 And you shall cross the Jordan and dwell upon the land that the Lord your God is causing you to inherit, and he shall give you rest from all your enemies around you, and you shall dwell with security.
Deuteronomy 12:11 And the place that the Lord your God may choose for his name to be called there shall be the place to which you shall bring all the things that I command you today: your whole burnt offerings and your sacrifices and your tithes and the firstfruits of your hands and your gifts and every choice thing among your gifts, as many as you may vow to your God.
Deuteronomy 12:12 And you shall rejoice before the Lord your God, you and your sons and your daughters, your servants and your female servants and the Levite who is at your gates, because there is no portion or allotment for him with you.
Deuteronomy 12:13 Pay attention to yourself, lest you offer up your whole burnt offerings in every place that you may see,
Deuteronomy 12:14 but rather in the place that the Lord your God may choose in one of your tribes. There you shall bring up your whole burnt offerings, and there you shall do all the things that I command you today.
Deuteronomy 12:15 But according to every desire of yours you shall slaughter and eat meat according to the blessing of the Lord your God that he gave you in every city. The unclean among you and the clean shall eat it together, like a gazelle or a deer.
Deuteronomy 12:16 Except you shall not eat the blood; you shall pour it out upon the land like water.
Deuteronomy 12:17 You shall not be able to eat in your cities the tithe of your wheat and your wine and your oil, the firstborn of your cattle and your sheep, and all the vows, as many as you may vow, and your acknowledgments and the firstfruits of your hands,
Deuteronomy 12:18 but rather you shall eat them before the Lord your God in the place that the Lord your God may choose for himself, you and your son and your daughter, your servant and your female servant and the proselyte who is in your cities, and you shall rejoice before the Lord your God over everything upon which you may lay your hand.
Deuteronomy 12:19 Pay attention to yourself, lest you abandon the Levite for all the time that you may live upon the land.
Deuteronomy 12:20 But if the Lord your God widens your borders, just as he spoke to you, and you say: I shall eat meat, if your soul desires so as to eat meat, then according to every desire of your soul you shall eat meat.
Deuteronomy 12:21 But if the place that the Lord your God may choose for his name to be called there is farther away from you, then you shall slaughter from your cattle and from your sheep that God may give you, in the manner that I commanded you, and you shall eat in your cities according to the desire of your soul.
Deuteronomy 12:22 As the gazelle and the deer are eaten, thus you shall eat it; the unclean among you and the clean shall eat it alike.
Deuteronomy 12:23 Pay close attention not to eat blood, because its blood is soul. The soul shall not be eaten with the meat.
Deuteronomy 12:24 You shall not eat it; you shall pour it out upon the land like water.
Deuteronomy 12:25 You shall not eat it, so that it may become well for you and for your sons after you, if you do what is good and pleasing before the Lord your God.
Deuteronomy 12:26 Except your holy things, if they come to be for you, and your vows, taking them, you shall come to the place that the Lord your God may choose for his name to be called there.
Deuteronomy 12:27 And you shall make your whole burnt offerings. You shall bring the meat up upon the altar of the Lord your God, but you shall pour the blood of your sacrifices toward the base of the altar of the Lord your God, and you shall eat the meat.
Deuteronomy 12:28 Guard and hear and you shall do all the words that I command you, so that it may become well for you and for your sons through the age, if you do what is good and pleasing before the Lord your God.
Deuteronomy 12:29 But if the Lord your God utterly destroys from before your face the nations into which you are entering there to inherit their land, and you inherit them and dwell in their land,
Deuteronomy 12:30 pay attention to yourself, lest you seek out to follow them after they have been utterly destroyed from before your face. You shall certainly not seek out their gods, saying: How do these nations act toward their gods? I also shall do so.
Deuteronomy 12:31 You shall not do thus to the Lord your God, for they did for their gods the abominations that the Lord hated, because they burn their sons and their daughters with fire for their gods.

## Chapter 13

Deuteronomy 13:1 Every word that I command you today, this you shall guard to do. You shall not add to it or remove from it.
Deuteronomy 13:2 But if a prophet or one dreaming a dream rises among you and gives you a sign or a wonder,
Deuteronomy 13:3 and the sign or the wonder of which he spoke to you comes, saying: Let us go and serve other gods that you do not know,
Deuteronomy 13:4 you shall not listen to the words of that prophet or of that one dreaming that dream, because the Lord your God is testing you, to know whether you love the Lord your God from your whole heart and from your whole soul.
Deuteronomy 13:5 After the Lord your God you shall go, and you shall fear him and guard his commandments and listen to his voice and be added to him.
Deuteronomy 13:6 And that prophet or that one dreaming the dream shall die, for he spoke to lead you astray from the Lord your God, who brought you out from the land of Egypt, who redeemed you from slavery, to thrust you out from the road upon which the Lord your God commanded you to walk. And you shall make the evil one disappear from among you yourselves.
Deuteronomy 13:7 But if your brother from your father or from your mother, or your son or your daughter or the woman who is in your bosom or the friend equal to your soul secretly urges you, saying: Let us walk and serve other gods that you and your fathers did not know,
Deuteronomy 13:8 from the gods of the nations around you, those near you or those far from you, from one end of the land as far as the other end of the land,
Deuteronomy 13:9 you shall not consent with him and shall not listen to him, and your eye shall not spare him; you shall not yearn for him, nor shall you ever shelter him.
Deuteronomy 13:10 By reporting, you shall report concerning him. Your hands shall be upon him first to kill him, and the hands of all the people last.
Deuteronomy 13:11 And they shall stone him with stones, and he shall die, because he sought to turn you away from the Lord your God, who brought you out from the land of Egypt, out of a house of slavery.
Deuteronomy 13:12 And all Israel, hearing, shall fear, and they shall not add still more to do according to this wicked matter among you.
Deuteronomy 13:13 But if you hear, in one of your cities that the Lord your God is giving you to dwell there, people saying:
Deuteronomy 13:14 Lawless men came out from among you and turned away all those dwelling in their city, saying: Let us go and serve other gods that you did not know,
Deuteronomy 13:15 then you shall inquire and investigate thoroughly, and behold, the word is clearly true: this abomination has happened among you,
Deuteronomy 13:16 by killing you shall kill all those dwelling in that city with slaughter by the sword. With an anathema you shall anathematize it and everything in it.
Deuteronomy 13:17 And you shall gather all its spoils into its thoroughfares and burn the city with fire and all its spoils all together before the Lord your God, and it shall be uninhabited through the age; it shall not be rebuilt any longer.
Deuteronomy 13:18 Nothing from the anathema shall be joined to your hand, so that the Lord may turn from the rage of his anger and give you mercy and show you mercy and multiply you, in the manner that the Lord swore to your fathers,
Deuteronomy 13:19 if you listen to the voice of the Lord your God, to guard all his commandments, as many as I command you today, to do what is good and pleasing before the Lord your God.

## Chapter 14

Deuteronomy 14:1 You are sons of the Lord your God. You shall not gash yourselves, and you shall not place a bald patch between your eyes over a dead person.
Deuteronomy 14:2 Because you are a holy people to the Lord your God, and the Lord your God chose you to become a peculiar people for him from all the nations upon the face of the land.
Deuteronomy 14:3 You shall not eat any abomination.
Deuteronomy 14:4 These are the animals that you shall eat: a calf from cattle and a lamb from sheep and a young goat from goats,
Deuteronomy 14:5 a deer and a gazelle and a buffalo and a goat-deer and a white-rump, an oryx and a camelopard.
Deuteronomy 14:6 Every animal that divides the hoof and splits the claws into two divisions of the hoof and brings up cud among the animals, these you shall eat.
Deuteronomy 14:7 And these you shall not eat from those that bring up cud and from those that divide the hooves and split the claws: the camel and the hare and the hyrax, because they bring up cud but do not divide the hoof; these are unclean for you.
Deuteronomy 14:8 And the pig, because it divides the hoof and splits the claws of the hoof but does not chew cud, this is unclean for you. You shall not eat from their flesh and shall not touch their carcasses. –
Deuteronomy 14:9 And these you shall eat from all the things in the waters: all the things in them that have fins and scales you shall eat.
Deuteronomy 14:10 And all the things that do not have fins and scales you shall not eat; they are unclean for you. –
Deuteronomy 14:11 Every clean bird you shall eat.
Deuteronomy 14:12 And these you shall not eat from among them: the eagle and the griffon-vulture and the sea eagle,
Deuteronomy 14:13 and the vulture and the kite and those like it,
Deuteronomy 14:14 and every raven and those like it,
Deuteronomy 14:15 and the ostrich and the owl and the gull,
Deuteronomy 14:16 and the heron and the swan and the ibis,
Deuteronomy 14:17 and the cormorant and the hawk and those like it and the hoopoe and the night raven,
Deuteronomy 14:18 and the pelican and the plover and those like it and the purple swamphen and the bat.
