Deuteronomy 14:19 All the creeping things among the flying creatures are unclean for you; you shall not eat from them.
Deuteronomy 14:20 Every clean flying creature you shall eat. –
Deuteronomy 14:21 You shall not eat anything dead of itself. It shall be given to the sojourner who is in your cities, and he shall eat it, or you shall give it over to the foreigner, because you are a holy people to the Lord your God. – You shall not boil a lamb in its mother’s milk.
Deuteronomy 14:22 You shall tithe a tenth of every yield of your seed, the yield of your field, year by year,
Deuteronomy 14:23 and you shall eat it before the Lord your God in the place that the Lord your God may choose for his name to be called there. You shall bring the tithes of your wheat and your wine and your oil, the firstborn of your cattle and your sheep, so that you may learn to fear the Lord your God all the days.
Deuteronomy 14:24 But if the road becomes far from you and you are not able to bring them up, because the place that the Lord your God may choose for his name to be called there is far from you, because the Lord your God shall bless you,
Deuteronomy 14:25 then you shall exchange them for silver and take the silver in your hands and travel to the place that the Lord your God may choose.
Deuteronomy 14:26 And you shall give the silver for anything that your soul may desire, for cattle or for sheep, for wine or for sikera or for anything that your soul may desire, and you shall eat there before the Lord your God and rejoice, you and your house,
Deuteronomy 14:27 and the Levite who is in your cities, because there is no portion or allotment for him with you. –
Deuteronomy 14:28 After three years you shall bring out all the tithe of your yields; in that year you shall place it in your cities,
Deuteronomy 14:29 and the Levite shall come, because there is no portion or allotment for him with you, and the proselyte and the orphan and the widow who is in your cities, and they shall eat and be filled, so that the Lord your God may bless you in all the works that you may do.

## Chapter 15

Deuteronomy 15:1 After seven years you shall make a release.
Deuteronomy 15:2 And thus is the command of the release: You shall release every private debt that your neighbor owes you, and you shall not exact it from your brother, because a release has been proclaimed to the Lord your God.
Deuteronomy 15:3 From the foreigner you shall exact whatever of yours may be with him, but for your brother you shall make a release of your debt.
Deuteronomy 15:4 Because there shall be no needy person among you, because by blessing the Lord your God shall bless you in the land that the Lord your God is giving you as an allotment to inherit it,
Deuteronomy 15:5 if by hearing you listen to the voice of the Lord your God, to guard and do all these commandments, as many as I command you today.
Deuteronomy 15:6 Because the Lord your God blessed you in the manner that he spoke to you, and you shall lend to many nations, but you shall not borrow, and you shall rule many nations, but they shall not rule you.
Deuteronomy 15:7 But if there comes to be among you a needy person from among your brothers, in one of your cities in the land that the Lord your God is giving you, you shall not withhold your heart, nor shall you ever tightly close your hand from your brother who is in need.
Deuteronomy 15:8 By opening, you shall open your hands to him; with a loan you shall lend him as much as he needs, according to as much as he lacks.
Deuteronomy 15:9 Pay attention to yourself, lest there be a secret matter in your heart, a lawless thing, saying: The seventh year, the year of release, is drawing near, and your eye becomes wicked toward your brother who is in need, and you shall not give to him, and he shall cry against you to the Lord, and there shall be great sin among you.
Deuteronomy 15:10 By giving, you shall give to him, and with a loan you shall lend him as much as he needs, and you shall not be grieved in your heart while you give to him, because on account of this matter the Lord your God shall bless you in all your works and in everything upon which you may lay your hand.
Deuteronomy 15:11 For a needy person shall certainly not cease from the land. Because of this I command you to do this matter, saying: By opening, you shall open your hands to your poor brother and to the one in need who is upon your land.
Deuteronomy 15:12 But if your brother, a Hebrew man or a Hebrew woman, is sold to you, he shall serve you six years, and in the seventh you shall send him out free from you.
Deuteronomy 15:13 But when you send him out free from you, you shall not send him out empty.
Deuteronomy 15:14 With provisions you shall provision him from your sheep and from your grain and from your winepress. Just as the Lord your God blessed you, you shall give to him.
Deuteronomy 15:15 And you shall remember that you were a household servant in the land of Egypt and the Lord your God redeemed you from there. Because of this I command you to do this matter.
Deuteronomy 15:16 But if he says to you: I shall not go out from you, because he has loved you and your house, because it is well for him beside you,
Deuteronomy 15:17 then you shall take the awl and pierce his ear against the door, and he shall be a household servant for you through the age. And you shall do likewise to your female servant.
Deuteronomy 15:18 It shall not be hard before you when they are sent out free from you, because for the annual wage of a hired worker he served you six years. And the Lord your God shall bless you in all the things that you may do.
Deuteronomy 15:19 Every firstborn that may be born among your cattle and among your sheep, the males, you shall sanctify to the Lord your God. You shall not work with your firstborn calf, and you shall certainly not shear the firstborn of your sheep.
Deuteronomy 15:20 Before the Lord you shall eat it year from year in the place that the Lord your God may choose, you and your house.
Deuteronomy 15:21 But if there is a blemish in it, lame or blind or indeed any evil blemish, you shall not sacrifice it to the Lord your God.
Deuteronomy 15:22 In your cities you shall eat it; the unclean among you and the clean shall eat it alike, like a gazelle or a deer.
Deuteronomy 15:23 Except you shall not eat the blood; you shall pour it out upon the land like water.

## Chapter 16

Deuteronomy 16:1 Guard the month of the new things, and you shall make the pascha for the Lord your God, because in the month of the new things you went out from Egypt by night.
Deuteronomy 16:2 And you shall sacrifice the pascha to the Lord your God, sheep and cattle, in the place that the Lord your God may choose for his name to be called there.
Deuteronomy 16:3 You shall not eat leaven with it. Seven days you shall eat unleavened things with it, bread of affliction, because you went out from Egypt in haste, so that you may remember the day of your departure from the land of Egypt all the days of your life.
Deuteronomy 16:4 Leaven shall not be seen among you in all your borders for seven days, and none of the meat that you may sacrifice in the evening on the first day shall lie overnight until morning.
Deuteronomy 16:5 You shall not be able to sacrifice the pascha in any of your cities that the Lord your God is giving you,
Deuteronomy 16:6 but rather in the place that the Lord your God may choose for his name to be called there you shall sacrifice the pascha in the evening toward the setting of the sun, at the time when you went out from Egypt,
Deuteronomy 16:7 and you shall boil and roast and eat it in the place that the Lord your God may choose, and you shall turn back in the morning and go to your houses.
Deuteronomy 16:8 Six days you shall eat unleavened things, and on the seventh day a departure, a feast to the Lord your God. You shall do no work in it except as much as shall be done for a soul. –
Deuteronomy 16:9 Seven complete weeks you shall count out for yourself. When you begin the sickle upon the harvest, you shall begin to count out seven weeks.
Deuteronomy 16:10 And you shall make a feast of weeks for the Lord your God according as your hand has strength, as much as he may give you, according as the Lord your God has blessed you.
Deuteronomy 16:11 And you shall rejoice before the Lord your God, you and your son and your daughter, your servant and your female servant and the Levite in your cities and the proselyte and the orphan and the widow among you, in the place that the Lord your God may choose for his name to be called there,
Deuteronomy 16:12 and you shall remember that you were a household servant in the land of Egypt, and you shall guard and do these commandments. –
Deuteronomy 16:13 You shall make a feast of tents for yourself for seven days when you gather in from your threshing floor and from your winepress,
Deuteronomy 16:14 and you shall rejoice in your feast, you and your son and your daughter, your servant and your female servant and the Levite and the proselyte and the orphan and the widow who is in your cities.
Deuteronomy 16:15 Seven days you shall celebrate a feast for the Lord your God in the place that the Lord your God may choose for himself. And if the Lord your God blesses you in all your yields and in every work of your hands, you shall be rejoicing. –
Deuteronomy 16:16 Three times in the year every male of yours shall appear before the Lord your God in the place that the Lord may choose, at the feast of unleavened things and at the feast of weeks and at the feast of tent-pitching. You shall not appear before the Lord your God empty.
Deuteronomy 16:17 Each according to the strength of your hands, according to the blessing of the Lord your God that he gave you.
Deuteronomy 16:18 Judges and scribal officers you shall appoint for yourself in all your cities that the Lord your God is giving you, by tribes, and they shall judge the people with just judgment.
Deuteronomy 16:19 They shall not turn aside judgment; they shall not recognize a face or take a gift, for gifts blind the eyes of the wise and remove the words of the righteous.
Deuteronomy 16:20 Justly you shall pursue what is just, so that you may live and, entering, inherit the land that the Lord your God is giving you.
Deuteronomy 16:21 You shall not plant for yourself a grove, any tree, beside the altar of the Lord your God that you make for yourself.
Deuteronomy 16:22 You shall not set up for yourself a pillar, which the Lord your God hated.

## Chapter 17

Deuteronomy 17:1 You shall not sacrifice to the Lord your God a calf or a sheep in which there is a blemish, any evil thing, because it is an abomination to the Lord your God.
Deuteronomy 17:2 But if there is found among you, in one of your cities that the Lord your God is giving you, a man or a woman who does what is evil before the Lord your God, to transgress his covenant,
Deuteronomy 17:3 and, going, they serve other gods and bow to them, to the sun or the moon or any of the things of the order of heaven, which he did not command,
Deuteronomy 17:4 and it is reported to you, you shall seek out thoroughly, and behold, the matter has truly happened, this abomination has happened in Israel,
Deuteronomy 17:5 then you shall bring out that man or that woman, and you shall stone them with stones, and they shall die.
Deuteronomy 17:6 Upon two witnesses or upon three witnesses the one who is to die shall die; he shall not die upon one witness.
Deuteronomy 17:7 And the hand of the witnesses shall be upon him first to put him to death, and the hand of all the people last; and you shall remove the evil one from among you yourselves.
Deuteronomy 17:8 But if a matter in judgment is beyond your ability, between blood and blood and between judgment and judgment and between touch and touch and between dispute and dispute, matters of judgment in your cities, then, rising, you shall go up to the place that the Lord your God may choose for his name to be called there,
Deuteronomy 17:9 and you shall come to the priests, the Levites, and to the judge who may be in those days, and after seeking out they shall report the judgment to you.
Deuteronomy 17:10 And you shall do according to the matter that they may report to you from the place that the Lord your God may choose for his name to be called there, and you shall carefully guard to do according to everything that may be laid down as law for you.
Deuteronomy 17:11 According to the law and according to the judgment that they may tell you, you shall do; you shall not turn aside from the word that they may report to you, right or left.
Deuteronomy 17:12 And the man who may act in arrogance so as not to obey the priest who stands to minister in the name of the Lord your God or the judge who may be in those days, that man shall die, and you shall remove the evil one from Israel.
Deuteronomy 17:13 And all the people, hearing, shall fear and shall not act impiously any longer.
Deuteronomy 17:14 But if you enter the land that the Lord your God is giving you as an allotment and inherit it and dwell upon it and say: I shall appoint a ruler over myself just as the other nations around me,
Deuteronomy 17:15 by appointing you shall appoint over yourself a ruler whom the Lord your God may choose. From your brothers you shall appoint a ruler over yourself; you shall not be able to appoint over yourself a foreign man, because he is not your brother.
Deuteronomy 17:16 Because he shall not multiply horses for himself, nor shall he ever turn the people back to Egypt so that he may multiply horses for himself, for the Lord said: You shall not add to return by this road any longer.
Deuteronomy 17:17 And he shall not multiply wives for himself, nor shall his heart turn away; and silver and gold he shall not multiply for himself exceedingly.
Deuteronomy 17:18 And it shall be when he sits upon his rule, he shall write for himself this second law into a book from the Levitical priests,
Deuteronomy 17:19 and it shall be with him, and he shall read in it all the days of his life, so that he may learn to fear the Lord his God, to guard all these commandments and to do these ordinances,
Deuteronomy 17:20 so that his heart may not be raised above his brothers, so that he may not transgress from the commandments right or left, that he and his sons may live long in his rule among the sons of Israel.

## Chapter 18

Deuteronomy 18:1 The priests, the Levites, the whole tribe of Levi, shall have no portion or allotment with Israel. The Lord’s fruit-offerings are their allotment; they shall eat them.
Deuteronomy 18:2 But they shall have no allotment among their brothers; the Lord himself is his allotment, just as he said to him.
Deuteronomy 18:3 And this is the judgment for the priests, the things from the people, from those sacrificing the sacrifices, whether a calf or a sheep: he shall give to the priest the arm and the jaws and the stomach.
Deuteronomy 18:4 And the firstfruits of your wheat and your wine and your oil and the firstfruit of the shearings of your sheep you shall give to him,
Deuteronomy 18:5 because the Lord your God chose him from all your tribes to stand before the Lord your God to minister and to bless in his name, he and his sons among the sons of Israel. –
Deuteronomy 18:6 But if the Levite comes from one of your cities, from among all the sons of Israel, where he sojourns, as his soul desires, to the place that the Lord may choose,
Deuteronomy 18:7 then he shall minister in the name of the Lord his God like all his brothers the Levites who stand there before the Lord.
Deuteronomy 18:8 An apportioned portion he shall eat, apart from the sale according to family.
Deuteronomy 18:9 But if you enter the land that the Lord your God is giving you, you shall not learn to do according to the abominations of those nations.
Deuteronomy 18:10 There shall not be found among you one purifying his son or his daughter in fire, one divining a divination, one taking omens from utterances and one auguring, a sorcerer,
Deuteronomy 18:11 one chanting a charm, a belly-speaker and an observer of portents, one questioning the dead.
Deuteronomy 18:12 For everyone doing these things is an abomination to the Lord your God, and because of these abominations the Lord shall utterly destroy them from you.
Deuteronomy 18:13 You shall be complete before the Lord your God.
Deuteronomy 18:14 For these nations, whom you are inheriting, will listen to omens and divinations, but to you the Lord your God has not given thus.
Deuteronomy 18:15 A prophet from your brothers like me the Lord your God shall raise up for you; you shall listen to him
Deuteronomy 18:16 according to all that you asked from the Lord your God at Choreb on the day of the assembly, saying: We shall not add to hear the voice of the Lord our God, and we shall not see this great fire any longer, nor shall we die.
Deuteronomy 18:17 And the Lord said to me: All that they spoke is right.
Deuteronomy 18:18 I shall raise up for them a prophet from their brothers like you and put my word in his mouth, and he shall speak to them according to all that I may command him.
Deuteronomy 18:19 And the man who does not listen to all that the prophet may speak in my name, I shall exact it from him.
Deuteronomy 18:20 Except the prophet who may act impiously to speak in my name a word that I did not command him to speak, and who may speak in the name of other gods: that prophet shall die.
Deuteronomy 18:21 But if you say in your heart: How shall we know the word that the Lord did not speak?
Deuteronomy 18:22 Whatever the prophet may speak in the name of the Lord, and the word does not happen and does not come about, this is the word that the Lord did not speak. That prophet spoke in impiety; you shall not keep away from him.

## Chapter 19

Deuteronomy 19:1 But if the Lord your God makes disappear the nations whose land your God is giving you, and you inherit them and dwell in their cities and in their houses,
Deuteronomy 19:2 you shall set apart three cities for yourself in the midst of your land that the Lord your God is giving you.
Deuteronomy 19:3 Measure out the road for yourself and divide into three the borders of your land that the Lord your God divides for you, and there shall be refuge there for every killer.
Deuteronomy 19:4 And this shall be the command concerning the killer who may flee there and live: whoever strikes his neighbor involuntarily, not having hated him before yesterday and before the third day,
Deuteronomy 19:5 and whoever enters the thicket with his neighbor to gather wood, and his hand is knocked away with the axe while cutting the wood, and the iron, falling out from the wood, happens upon his neighbor and he dies, this one shall flee to one of these cities and live,
Deuteronomy 19:6 lest the near kinsman of the blood pursue after the killer, because his heart is overheated, and overtake him if the road is longer, and strike his soul, and he dies, though for this man there is no judgment of death, because he had not hated him before yesterday and before the third day.
Deuteronomy 19:7 Because of this I command you this word, saying: Three cities you shall set apart for yourself.
Deuteronomy 19:8 But if the Lord your God widens your borders in the manner that he swore to your fathers, and the Lord gives you all the land that he said he would give to your fathers,
Deuteronomy 19:9 if you listen to do all these commandments that I command you today, to love the Lord your God, to walk in all his ways all the days, then you shall add for yourself three more cities to these three,
Deuteronomy 19:10 and innocent blood shall not be poured out in your land that the Lord your God is giving you as an allotment, and you shall not be liable for blood.
Deuteronomy 19:11 But if there comes to be a man hating his neighbor, and he lies in wait for him and rises against him and strikes his soul, and he dies, and the man flees to one of these cities,
Deuteronomy 19:12 then the council of elders of his city shall send and take him from there and hand him into the hands of the near kinsman of the blood, and he shall die.
Deuteronomy 19:13 Your eye shall not spare him, and you shall cleanse the innocent blood from Israel, and it shall be well for you.
Deuteronomy 19:14 You shall not move the boundaries of your neighbor that your fathers set in your inheritance, which you inherited in the land that the Lord your God is giving you as an allotment.
Deuteronomy 19:15 One witness shall not stand to testify against a person concerning any injustice and concerning any wrongdoing and concerning any sin that he may sin. Upon the mouth of two witnesses and upon the mouth of three witnesses every matter shall stand.
Deuteronomy 19:16 But if an unjust witness takes his stand against a person, recounting his impiety,
Deuteronomy 19:17 then the two men who have the dispute shall stand before the Lord and before the priests and before the judges who may be in those days,
Deuteronomy 19:18 and the judges shall examine carefully, and behold, an unjust witness has testified unjustly; he stood against his brother,
Deuteronomy 19:19 and you shall do to him in the manner that he acted wickedly to do against his brother, and you shall remove the evil one from among you yourselves.
Deuteronomy 19:20 And those remaining, hearing, shall fear and shall not add still more to do according to this evil matter among you.
Deuteronomy 19:21 Your eye shall not spare him: soul for soul, eye for eye, tooth for tooth, hand for hand, foot for foot.

## Chapter 20

Deuteronomy 20:1 But if you go out to war against your enemies and see horse and rider and a people more numerous than you, you shall not fear them, because the Lord your God is with you, the one who brought you up from the land of Egypt.
Deuteronomy 20:2 And it shall be when you draw near to the war, the priest, drawing near, shall speak to the people
Deuteronomy 20:3 and say to them: Hear, Israel. You are going today to war against your enemies. Let not your heart be weakened; do not fear or be shattered or turn aside from before their face,
Deuteronomy 20:4 because the Lord your God goes before with you to fight together with you against your enemies, to rescue you.
Deuteronomy 20:5 And the scribes shall speak to the people, saying: Who is the man who built a new house and has not inaugurated it? Let him go and return to his house, lest he die in the war and another man inaugurate it.
Deuteronomy 20:6 And who is the man who planted a vineyard and has not rejoiced from it? Let him go and return to his house, lest he die in the war and another man rejoice from it.
Deuteronomy 20:7 And who is the man who has betrothed a woman and has not taken her? Let him go and return to his house, lest he die in the war and another man take her.
Deuteronomy 20:8 And the scribes shall add to speak to the people and say: Who is the man who is afraid and cowardly in heart? Let him go and return to his house, so that he may not make the heart of his brother cowardly like his own.
Deuteronomy 20:9 And it shall be when the scribes cease speaking to the people, they shall appoint rulers of the army leading the people.
Deuteronomy 20:10 But if you approach a city to make war against it and call them out with peace,
Deuteronomy 20:11 If they answer you peaceably and open to you, then all the people found in it shall be subject to tribute for you and obedient to you.
Deuteronomy 20:12 But if they do not obey you and make war against you, you shall besiege it,
Deuteronomy 20:13 and the Lord your God shall hand it into your hands, and you shall strike every male of it with slaughter by the sword,
Deuteronomy 20:14 except the women and the baggage and all the livestock and everything that may be in the city; and all the equipment you shall plunder for yourself, and you shall eat all the plunder of your enemies that the Lord your God is giving you.
Deuteronomy 20:15 Thus you shall do to all the cities that are very far from you, which are not from the cities of these nations.
Deuteronomy 20:16 But behold, from the cities of these nations whose land the Lord your God is giving you to inherit, you shall not capture alive from them anything breathing,
Deuteronomy 20:17 but with an anathema you shall anathematize them: the Chettite and Amorrite and Chanaanite and Pherezite and Evite and Jebousite and Gergesite, in the manner that the Lord your God commanded you,
Deuteronomy 20:18 so that they may not teach you to do all their abominations that they did for their gods, and you shall sin before the Lord your God.
Deuteronomy 20:19 But if you sit around a city for many days to make war against it for its capture, you shall not utterly destroy its trees by laying iron upon them; rather, you shall eat from it, but you shall not cut it down. Is the tree in the field a human to enter from before your face into the palisade?
Deuteronomy 20:20 But a tree that you know is not fruit-eatable, this you shall utterly destroy and cut down and build a palisade against the city that makes war against you, until it is handed over.

## Chapter 21

Deuteronomy 21:1 But if a wounded person is found in the land that the Lord your God is giving you to inherit, fallen in the plain, and they do not know who struck him,
Deuteronomy 21:2 your council of elders and your judges shall go out and measure to the cities around the wounded person,
Deuteronomy 21:3 and it shall be the city nearest the wounded person; the council of elders of that city shall take a heifer from the cattle that has not worked and has not drawn a yoke,
Deuteronomy 21:4 and the council of elders of that city shall bring the heifer down into a rugged ravine that has not been worked or sown, and they shall cut the sinews of the heifer in the ravine.
Deuteronomy 21:5 And the priests, the Levites, shall come near – because the Lord your God chose them to stand beside him and to bless upon his name, and upon their mouth shall be every dispute and every touch – ,
Deuteronomy 21:6 and all the council of elders of that city, those nearest the wounded person, shall wash their hands upon the head of the heifer whose sinews were cut in the ravine,
Deuteronomy 21:7 and answering they shall say: Our hands did not pour out this blood, and our eyes have not seen.
Deuteronomy 21:8 Be gracious to your people Israel, whom you redeemed, Lord, from the land of Egypt, so that innocent blood may not come to be among your people Israel. And the blood shall be atoned for them.
Deuteronomy 21:9 But you shall remove the innocent blood from among you yourselves if you do what is good and pleasing before the Lord your God.
Deuteronomy 21:10 But if you go out to war against your enemies and the Lord your God hands them into your hands and you plunder their plunder
Deuteronomy 21:11 and see among the plunder a woman beautiful in appearance and set your mind on her and take her for yourself as a wife,
Deuteronomy 21:12 you shall bring her inside into your house and shave her head and pare her nails
Deuteronomy 21:13 and remove the garments of her captivity from her, and she shall sit in your house and weep for her father and mother a month of days, and after these things you shall enter to her and dwell together with her, and she shall be your wife.
Deuteronomy 21:14 And it shall be if you do not want her, you shall send her out free, and by sale she shall not be sold for silver. You shall not disregard her, because you humbled her.
Deuteronomy 21:15 But if a man comes to have two wives, one of them loved and one of them hated, and the loved and the hated bear children to him, and a firstborn son comes to be of the hated one,
Deuteronomy 21:16 then it shall be on whatever day he allots his possessions as an inheritance to his sons, he shall not be able to make the loved one’s son firstborn, overlooking the firstborn son of the hated one,
Deuteronomy 21:17 but he shall recognize the firstborn son of the hated one, to give him double from everything that may be found for him, because this one is the beginning of his children, and the firstborn rights belong to him.
Deuteronomy 21:18 But if someone has a son disobedient and a provoker, not obeying the voice of his father and the voice of his mother, and they discipline him and he does not listen to them,
Deuteronomy 21:19 then his father and his mother shall take hold of him and bring him out to the council of elders of his city and to the gate of his place
Deuteronomy 21:20 and say to the men of their city: This son of ours disobeys and provokes, does not obey our voice; feasting at banquets, he is drunk with wine.
Deuteronomy 21:21 And the men of his city shall stone him with stones, and he shall die; and you shall remove the evil one from among you yourselves, and those remaining, hearing, shall fear.
Deuteronomy 21:22 But if there comes to be in someone a sin, a judgment of death, and he dies and you hang him on wood,
Deuteronomy 21:23 his body shall not sleep overnight on the wood, but with burial you shall bury him on that day, because everyone hanging on wood is cursed by God; and you shall not defile the land that the Lord your God is giving you as an allotment.

## Chapter 22

Deuteronomy 22:1 Do not, upon seeing your brother’s calf or his sheep wandering on the road, overlook them. By turning you shall turn them back to your brother and return them to him.
Deuteronomy 22:2 But if your brother is not near you and you do not know him, you shall gather them inside into your house, and they shall be with you until your brother seeks them, and you shall return them to him.
Deuteronomy 22:3 Thus you shall do for his donkey, and thus you shall do for his garment, and thus you shall do for every loss of your brother, whatever may be lost by him and you find; you shall not be able to overlook it. –
Deuteronomy 22:4 Do not, when you see your brother’s donkey or his calf fallen on the road, overlook them; by raising you shall raise them with him.
Deuteronomy 22:5 The gear of a man shall not be upon a woman, nor shall a man ever put on a woman’s robe, because everyone doing these things is an abomination to the Lord your God.
Deuteronomy 22:6 But if you encounter a nest of birds before your face on the road or on any tree or on the ground, with chicks or eggs, and the mother warms the chicks or the eggs, you shall not take the mother with the children.
Deuteronomy 22:7 By sending you shall send the mother away, but you shall take the children for yourself, so that it may become well for you and you may be long-lived.
Deuteronomy 22:8 But if you build a new house, you shall make a crown for your roof; and you shall not cause a killing in your house if the one falling falls from it.
Deuteronomy 22:9 You shall not sow your vineyard with something different, lest the yield and the seed that you sow together with the yield of your vineyard be sanctified. –
Deuteronomy 22:10 You shall not plow with a calf and a donkey together. –
Deuteronomy 22:11 You shall not put on adulterated cloth, wool and linen together.
Deuteronomy 22:12 You shall make twisted cords for yourself on the four borders of your coverings with which you may cover yourself.
Deuteronomy 22:13 But if someone takes a woman and lives with her and hates her
Deuteronomy 22:14 and places pretextual words upon her and brings an evil name upon her and says: I took this woman and, coming to her, did not find signs of her virginity,
Deuteronomy 22:15 then the girl’s father and mother shall take and bring out the signs of the girl’s virginity to the council of elders at the gate,
Deuteronomy 22:16 and the girl’s father shall say to the council of elders: I gave this daughter of mine to this man as a wife, and he, hating her,
Deuteronomy 22:17 now places pretextual words upon her, saying: I did not find signs of virginity in your daughter. And these are the signs of my daughter’s virginity. And they shall unfold the garment before the council of elders of the city.
Deuteronomy 22:18 And the council of elders of that city shall take that man and discipline him
Deuteronomy 22:19 and fine him a hundred shekels and give them to the father of the young woman, because he brought an evil name upon an Israelite virgin; and she shall be his wife, and he shall not be able to send her out for all time.
Deuteronomy 22:20 But if this matter truly comes to be and signs of virginity are not found for the young woman,
Deuteronomy 22:21 then they shall bring the young woman out to the doors of her father’s house, and the men of her city shall stone her with stones, and she shall die, because she did a senseless thing among the sons of Israel by prostituting her father’s house; and you shall remove the evil one from among you yourselves.
Deuteronomy 22:22 But if a man is found lying with a woman who lives together with a man, you shall kill both, the man lying with the woman and the woman; and you shall remove the evil one from Israel.
Deuteronomy 22:23 But if there comes to be a virgin girl betrothed to a man, and a man finding her in a city lies with her,
Deuteronomy 22:24 you shall bring both out to the gate of their city, and they shall be stoned with stones and die: the young woman because she did not cry out in the city, and the man because he humbled the wife of his neighbor; and you shall remove the evil one from among you yourselves. –
Deuteronomy 22:25 But if a man finds the betrothed girl in the plain and, using force, lies with her, you shall kill only the man who lay with her,
Deuteronomy 22:26 and you shall do nothing to the young woman; there is no sin of death in the young woman, because as if a man rose against his neighbor and murdered his soul, so is this matter,
Deuteronomy 22:27 because he found her in the field; the betrothed young woman cried out, and there was no one to help her.
Deuteronomy 22:28 But if someone finds a virgin girl who is not betrothed and, using force, lies with her and is found,
Deuteronomy 22:29 the man who lay with her shall give the young woman’s father fifty didrachmas of silver, and she shall be his wife, because he humbled her; he shall not be able to send her out for all time.

## Chapter 23

Deuteronomy 23:1 A man shall not take his father’s wife, and he shall not uncover his father’s covering.
Deuteronomy 23:2 A man with crushed parts and one who has been cut off shall not enter the assembly of the Lord.
Deuteronomy 23:3 One from a prostitute shall not enter the assembly of the Lord.
Deuteronomy 23:4 An Ammanite and a Moabite shall not enter the assembly of the Lord; even to the tenth generation he shall not enter the assembly of the Lord, even forever,
Deuteronomy 23:5 because they did not meet you with bread and water on the way when you were going out from Egypt, and because they hired Balaam son of Beor from Mesopotamia against you to curse you;
Deuteronomy 23:6 and the Lord your God did not wish to listen to Balaam, and the Lord your God turned the curses into blessing, because the Lord your God loved you.
Deuteronomy 23:7 You shall not address peaceful things to them and things advantageous to them all your days, forever.
Deuteronomy 23:8 You shall not abhor an Idumaean, because he is your brother; you shall not abhor an Egyptian, because you became a sojourner in his land;
Deuteronomy 23:9 if sons are born to them, in the third generation they shall enter the assembly of the Lord.
Deuteronomy 23:10 And if you go out to encamp against your enemies, you shall guard yourself from every evil word.
Deuteronomy 23:11 If there is among you a man who is not clean because of his discharge by night, he shall go outside the camp and shall not enter the camp;
Deuteronomy 23:12 and it shall be that toward evening he shall wash his body with water, and when the sun has set he shall enter the camp.
Deuteronomy 23:13 And you shall have a place outside the camp, and you shall go out there;
Deuteronomy 23:14 and you shall have a peg on your belt, and it shall be that when you sit down outside, you shall dig with it and, bringing the earth back, cover your indecency with it;
Deuteronomy 23:15 because the Lord your God walks about in your camp to deliver you and to hand over your enemy before your face; and your camp shall be holy, and an indecency of a thing shall not be seen among you, and he shall turn away from you.
Deuteronomy 23:16 You shall not hand over to his master a servant who has joined himself to you from his master;
Deuteronomy 23:17 he shall dwell with you, he shall dwell among you in every place wherever it pleases him; you shall not afflict him.
Deuteronomy 23:18 There shall not be a prostitute from the daughters of Israel, and there shall not be a man prostituting himself from the sons of Israel; there shall not be a female bearer of rites from the daughters of Israel, and there shall not be a man being initiated from the sons of Israel.
Deuteronomy 23:19 You shall not bring the hire of a prostitute nor the exchange of a dog into the house of the Lord your God for any vow, because both are an abomination to the Lord your God.
Deuteronomy 23:20 You shall not lend at interest to your brother interest on silver or interest on food or interest on anything that you lend;
Deuteronomy 23:21 to the foreigner you shall lend at interest, but to your brother you shall not lend at interest, so that the Lord your God may bless you in all your works upon the land into which you are entering there to inherit it.
Deuteronomy 23:22 And if you vow a vow to the Lord your God, you shall not delay to pay it, because the Lord your God will surely require it of you, and there shall be sin in you;
Deuteronomy 23:23 but if you do not wish to vow, there is no sin in you.
Deuteronomy 23:24 What goes forth through your lips you shall guard and do, in the manner that you vowed a gift to the Lord your God, which you spoke with your mouth.
Deuteronomy 23:25 And if you enter your neighbor’s harvest, you shall gather ears with your hands, but you shall certainly not put a sickle to your neighbor’s harvest. –
Deuteronomy 23:26 And if you enter your neighbor’s vineyard, you may eat grapes as much as to fill your soul, but you shall not put any into a vessel.

## Chapter 24

Deuteronomy 24:1 And if someone takes a wife and lives with her, and it comes to pass that she does not find favor before him because he has found an indecent thing in her, he shall write her a document of separation and give it into her hands and send her out of his house,
Deuteronomy 24:2 and she, having gone away, becomes another man’s wife,
Deuteronomy 24:3 and the latter man hates her and writes her a document of separation and gives it into her hands and sends her out of his house, or the latter man who took her for himself as a wife dies,
Deuteronomy 24:4 the former man who sent her out shall not be able to turn back and take her for himself as a wife after she has been defiled, because it is an abomination before the Lord your God; and you shall not defile the land that the Lord your God gives you as an inheritance.
Deuteronomy 24:5 And if someone takes a wife recently, he shall not go out to war, and no matter shall be laid upon him; he shall be free in his house for one year; he shall gladden his wife whom he took.
Deuteronomy 24:6 You shall not take a mill or an upper millstone as a pledge, because this takes a life as a pledge.
Deuteronomy 24:7 And if a man is caught stealing a person from his brothers, the sons of Israel, and, having oppressed him, sells him, that thief shall die; and you shall remove the evil from among yourselves.
Deuteronomy 24:8 Take heed to yourself in the affliction of leprosy; you shall be very careful to do according to all the law that the priests, the Levites, announce to you; as I commanded you, take care to do.
Deuteronomy 24:9 Remember all that the Lord your God did to Mariam on the way when you were going out from Egypt.
Deuteronomy 24:10 If there is a debt with your neighbor, any debt whatever, you shall not enter his house to take the pledge as a pledge;
Deuteronomy 24:11 you shall stand outside, and the man with whom your loan rests shall bring the pledge out to you.
Deuteronomy 24:12 And if the man is poor, you shall not sleep with his pledge;
Deuteronomy 24:13 you shall certainly give back his pledge around sunset, and he shall sleep in his garment and bless you, and it shall be mercy for you before the Lord your God.
Deuteronomy 24:14 You shall not wrong the wage of a poor and needy person from your brothers or from the sojourners in your cities;
Deuteronomy 24:15 on the same day you shall pay his wage; the sun shall not set upon it, because he is poor and has his hope in it; and he shall not cry out against you to the Lord, and there shall be sin in you.
Deuteronomy 24:16 Fathers shall not die for children, and sons shall not die for fathers; each shall die for his own sin.
Deuteronomy 24:17 You shall not turn aside the judgment of a sojourner and an orphan and a widow, and you shall not take a widow’s garment as a pledge;
Deuteronomy 24:18 and you shall remember that you were a household servant in the land of Egypt and the Lord your God redeemed you from there; therefore I command you to do this thing.
Deuteronomy 24:19 And if you reap a harvest in your field and forget a sheaf in your field, you shall not go back to take it; it shall be for the poor person and the sojourner and the orphan and the widow, so that the Lord your God may bless you in all the works of your hands.
Deuteronomy 24:20 And if you gather olives, you shall not go back to glean what is behind you; it shall be for the sojourner and the orphan and the widow; and you shall remember that you were a household servant in the land of Egypt; therefore I command you to do this thing.
Deuteronomy 24:21 And if you gather grapes from your vineyard, you shall not go back to gather the grapes behind you; it shall be for the sojourner and the orphan and the widow;
Deuteronomy 24:22 and you shall remember that you were a household servant in the land of Egypt; therefore I command you to do this thing.

## Chapter 25

Deuteronomy 25:1 And if a dispute arises between people and they come to judgment, and they judge and justify the righteous and condemn the ungodly,
Deuteronomy 25:2 and it shall be, if the one acting ungodly is worthy of blows, you shall set him down before the judges, and they shall whip him before them according to his ungodliness, by number.
Deuteronomy 25:3 They shall whip him forty times; they shall not add to it. But if they add to whipping him more blows beyond these, your brother shall be disgraced before you.
Deuteronomy 25:4 You shall not muzzle an ox while it is threshing.
Deuteronomy 25:5 And if brothers dwell together and one of them dies, and he has no offspring, the wife of the dead man shall not be for an outside man who is not near; her husband’s brother shall go in to her and take her for himself as a wife and live with her.
Deuteronomy 25:6 And it shall be that the child whom she bears shall be established under the name of the one who has died, and his name shall not be wiped out from Israel.
Deuteronomy 25:7 But if the man does not wish to take his brother’s wife, the woman shall go up to the gate to the council of elders and say, “My husband’s brother does not wish to raise up his brother’s name in Israel; my husband’s brother did not wish to.”
Deuteronomy 25:8 And the council of elders of his city shall call him and speak to him, and standing he says, “I do not wish to take her,”
Deuteronomy 25:9 then his brother’s wife shall come forward before the council of elders and loosen his one sandal from his foot and spit in his face, and answering she shall say, “Thus they shall do to the man who will not build up his brother’s house”;
Deuteronomy 25:10 and his name shall be called in Israel “House of the one whose sandal was loosened.”
Deuteronomy 25:11 And if people fight together, a man with his brother, and the wife of one of them comes forward to rescue her husband from the hand of the one striking him, and stretching out her hand takes hold of his testicles,
Deuteronomy 25:12 you shall cut off her hand; your eye shall not spare her.
Deuteronomy 25:13 There shall not be in your purse a weight and a weight, large or small;
Deuteronomy 25:14 there shall not be in your house a measure and a measure, large or small;
Deuteronomy 25:15 you shall have a true and just weight, and you shall have a true and just measure, so that you may become long-lived upon the land that the Lord your God gives you as an inheritance;
Deuteronomy 25:16 because everyone doing these things, everyone doing injustice, is an abomination to the Lord your God.
Deuteronomy 25:17 Remember all that Amalek did to you on the way when you were going out from Egypt,
Deuteronomy 25:18 how he opposed you on the way and cut off your rear guard, those who were weary behind you, while you were hungry and weary; and he did not fear God.
Deuteronomy 25:19 And it shall be, when the Lord your God gives you rest from all your enemies around you in the land that the Lord your God gives you as an inheritance to inherit, you shall wipe out the name of Amalek from under heaven, and you shall certainly not forget.

## Chapter 26

Deuteronomy 26:1 And it shall be, if you enter the land that the Lord your God gives you as an inheritance and inherit it and dwell upon it,
Deuteronomy 26:2 you shall take from the first fruits of the fruit of your land that the Lord your God gives you and put it into a basket and go to the place that the Lord your God chooses for his name to be called there,
Deuteronomy 26:3 and you shall come to the priest who is in those days and say to him, “I declare today to the Lord my God that I have entered the land that the Lord swore to our fathers to give to us.”
Deuteronomy 26:4 And the priest shall take the basket from your hands and place it before the altar of the Lord your God,
Deuteronomy 26:5 and you shall answer and say before the Lord your God, “My father cast off Syria and went down into Egypt and sojourned there with a small number, and there he became a great nation and a numerous and great multitude;
Deuteronomy 26:6 and the Egyptians afflicted us and humbled us and laid hard works upon us;
Deuteronomy 26:7 and we cried aloud to the Lord, the God of our fathers, and the Lord listened to our voice and saw our humiliation and our toil and our affliction;
Deuteronomy 26:8 and the Lord himself brought us out of Egypt with great strength and with a mighty hand and with his uplifted arm and with great visions and with signs and with wonders,
Deuteronomy 26:9 and brought us into this place and gave us this land, a land flowing with milk and honey;
Deuteronomy 26:10 and now, behold, I have brought the first fruits of the produce of the land that you gave me, Lord, a land flowing with milk and honey.” And you shall leave them before the Lord your God and bow down there before the Lord your God;
Deuteronomy 26:11 and you shall rejoice in all the good things that the Lord your God gave to you and your household, you and the Levite and the sojourner among you.
Deuteronomy 26:12 And if you finish tithing all the tenth part of the produce of your land in the third year, you shall give the second tenth part to the Levite and to the sojourner and to the orphan and to the widow, and they shall eat in your cities and be filled.
Deuteronomy 26:13 And you shall say before the Lord your God, “I have cleared the holy things out of my house and given them to the Levite and the sojourner and the orphan and the widow according to all the commandments that you commanded me; I did not transgress your commandment and I did not forget;
Deuteronomy 26:14 and I did not eat of them in my pain, nor did I make use of any of them for an unclean thing, nor did I give any of them to the dead; I obeyed the voice of the Lord my God; I did as you commanded me.
Deuteronomy 26:15 Look down from your holy house, from heaven, and bless your people Israel and the land that you gave them, as you swore to our fathers to give to us a land flowing with milk and honey.”
Deuteronomy 26:16 On this day the Lord your God commanded you to do all these ordinances and judgments, and you shall guard and do them with all your heart and with all your soul.
Deuteronomy 26:17 You chose God today to be your God and to walk in his ways and to guard his ordinances and his judgments and to obey his voice;
Deuteronomy 26:18 and the Lord chose you today to become for him a special people, just as he said to you, to guard all his commandments,
Deuteronomy 26:19 and for you to be above all the nations, as he made you renowned and a boast and glorified, for you to be a holy people to the Lord your God, as he spoke.

## Chapter 27

Deuteronomy 27:1 And Moses and the council of elders of Israel commanded, saying, “Guard all these commandments that I command you today.
Deuteronomy 27:2 And it shall be on the day when you cross the Jordan into the land that the Lord your God gives you, you shall set up large stones for yourself and plaster them with plaster
Deuteronomy 27:3 and write upon the stones all the words of this law when you cross the Jordan, when you enter the land that the Lord, the God of your fathers, gives you, a land flowing with milk and honey, as the Lord, the God of your fathers, said to you;
Deuteronomy 27:4 and it shall be, when you cross the Jordan, you shall set up these stones that I command you today on Mount Gaibal and plaster them with plaster.
Deuteronomy 27:5 And you shall build there an altar to the Lord your God, an altar of stones; you shall not put iron upon them;
Deuteronomy 27:6 with whole stones you shall build an altar to the Lord your God and offer upon it whole burnt offerings to the Lord your God,
Deuteronomy 27:7 and you shall sacrifice there a sacrifice of salvation to the Lord your God and eat and be filled and rejoice before the Lord your God.
Deuteronomy 27:8 And you shall write upon the stones all this law very clearly.”
Deuteronomy 27:9 And Moses and the priests, the Levites, spoke to all Israel, saying, “Be silent and hear, Israel; on this day you have become a people to the Lord your God;
Deuteronomy 27:10 and you shall listen to the voice of the Lord your God and do all his commandments and his ordinances that I command you today.”
Deuteronomy 27:11 And Moses commanded the people on that day, saying,
Deuteronomy 27:12 “These shall stand to bless the people on Mount Garizin, having crossed the Jordan: Symeon, Levi, Judas, Issachar, Joseph, and Benjamin.
Deuteronomy 27:13 And these shall stand for the curse on Mount Gaibal: Reuben, Gad and Aser, Zabulon, Dan and Nephthali.”
Deuteronomy 27:14 And the Levites shall answer and say to all Israel with a loud voice,
Deuteronomy 27:15 “Accursed is the man who makes a carved and cast thing, an abomination to the Lord, the work of a craftsman’s hands, and places it in secret.” And all the people shall answer and say, “May it be so.”
Deuteronomy 27:16 “Accursed is the one who dishonors his father or his mother.” And all the people shall say, “May it be so.”
Deuteronomy 27:17 “Accursed is the one who moves the boundaries of his neighbor.” And all the people shall say, “May it be so.”
Deuteronomy 27:18 “Accursed is the one who leads a blind person astray on the road.” And all the people shall say, “May it be so.”
Deuteronomy 27:19 “Accursed is whoever turns aside the judgment of a sojourner and an orphan and a widow.” And all the people shall say, “May it be so.”
Deuteronomy 27:20 “Accursed is the one who sleeps with his father’s wife, because he uncovered his father’s covering.” And all the people shall say, “May it be so.”
Deuteronomy 27:21 “Accursed is the one who sleeps with any animal.” And all the people shall say, “May it be so.”
Deuteronomy 27:22 “Accursed is the one who sleeps with his sister from his father or from his mother.” And all the people shall say, “May it be so.”
Deuteronomy 27:23 “Accursed is the one who sleeps with his mother-in-law.” And all the people shall say, “May it be so.” “Accursed is the one who sleeps with his wife’s sister.” And all the people shall say, “May it be so.”
Deuteronomy 27:24 “Accursed is the one who strikes his neighbor deceitfully.” And all the people shall say, “May it be so.”
Deuteronomy 27:25 “Accursed is whoever takes gifts to strike a person of innocent blood.” And all the people shall say, “May it be so.”
Deuteronomy 27:26 “Accursed is every person who does not remain in all the words of this law to do them.” And all the people shall say, “May it be so.”

## Chapter 28

Deuteronomy 28:1 And it shall be when you cross the Jordan into the land that the Lord your God gives you, if you diligently listen to the voice of the Lord your God to guard and do all his commandments that I command you today, the Lord your God will set you above all the nations of the earth,
Deuteronomy 28:2 and all these blessings shall come upon you and find you if you listen to the voice of the Lord your God.
Deuteronomy 28:3 Blessed are you in the city, and blessed are you in the field;
Deuteronomy 28:4 blessed are the offspring of your womb and the produce of your land, the herds of your cattle and the flocks of your sheep;
Deuteronomy 28:5 blessed are your storehouses and what you leave behind;
Deuteronomy 28:6 blessed are you when you enter, and blessed are you when you go out.
Deuteronomy 28:7 May the Lord your God hand over your enemies who oppose you, broken before your face; by one road they shall come out against you and by seven roads they shall flee from before your face.
Deuteronomy 28:8 May the Lord send the blessing upon you in your storerooms and in everything to which you put your hand, upon the land that the Lord your God gives you.
Deuteronomy 28:9 May the Lord your God establish you for himself as a holy people, as he swore to your fathers, if you listen to the voice of the Lord your God and walk in his ways;
Deuteronomy 28:10 and all the nations of the earth shall see you, that the name of the Lord has been called upon you, and they shall fear you.
Deuteronomy 28:11 And the Lord your God shall multiply you for good in the offspring of your womb and in the produce of your land and in the offspring of your animals upon the land that the Lord swore to your fathers to give you.
Deuteronomy 28:12 May the Lord open to you his good treasure, heaven, to give rain to your land in its season, to bless all the works of your hands; and you shall lend to many nations, but you shall not borrow, and you shall rule many nations, but they shall not rule you.
Deuteronomy 28:13 May the Lord your God set you as head and not as tail, and you shall then be above and shall not be below, if you listen to the commandments of the Lord your God that I command you today to guard and do;
Deuteronomy 28:14 you shall not turn aside from any of the words that I command you today, right or left, to go after other gods to serve them.
Deuteronomy 28:15 And it shall be, if you do not listen to the voice of the Lord your God to guard and do all his commandments that I command you today, all these curses shall come upon you and overtake you.
Deuteronomy 28:16 Accursed are you in the city, and accursed are you in the field;
Deuteronomy 28:17 accursed are your storehouses and what you leave behind;
Deuteronomy 28:18 accursed are the offspring of your womb and the produce of your land, the herds of your cattle and the flocks of your sheep;
Deuteronomy 28:19 accursed are you when you go out, and accursed are you when you enter.
Deuteronomy 28:20 May the Lord send upon you want and famine and consumption in everything to which you put your hand, whatever you do, until he destroys you and until he causes you to perish quickly because of your evil practices, because you forsook me.
Deuteronomy 28:21 May the Lord make death cling to you until he consumes you from the land into which you are entering to inherit it.
Deuteronomy 28:22 May the Lord strike you with distress and fever and chills and inflammation and slaughter and wind-blight and pallor, and they shall pursue you until they destroy you.
Deuteronomy 28:23 And the heaven over your head shall be bronze, and the earth beneath you iron.
Deuteronomy 28:24 May the Lord give dust as the rain of your land, and earth shall come down upon you from heaven until he wears you away and until he destroys you.
Deuteronomy 28:25 May the Lord give you defeat before your enemies; by one road you shall go out against them and by seven roads you shall flee from before their face; and you shall be scattered among all the kingdoms of the earth.
Deuteronomy 28:26 And your dead shall be food for the birds of heaven and the beasts of the earth, and there shall be no one to drive them away.
Deuteronomy 28:27 May the Lord strike you with an Egyptian sore on the seats of the body, and with wild scab and itching, so that you cannot be healed.
Deuteronomy 28:28 May the Lord strike you with paralysis and blindness and derangement of mind,
Deuteronomy 28:29 and you shall be groping at midday as a blind person gropes in darkness, and your ways shall not prosper; and you shall then be wronged and plundered all your days, and there shall be no one to help you.
Deuteronomy 28:30 You shall take a wife, and another man shall have her; you shall build a house and shall not dwell in it; you shall plant a vineyard and shall not gather its grapes;
Deuteronomy 28:31 your calf shall be slaughtered before you, and you shall not eat of it; your donkey shall be snatched away from you and shall not be returned to you; your sheep shall be given to your enemies, and there shall be no one to help you;
Deuteronomy 28:32 your sons and daughters shall be given to another nation, and your eyes shall look toward them, wasting away, and your hand shall have no strength;
Deuteronomy 28:33 the produce of your land and all your labors a nation that you do not know shall eat, and you shall be wronged and crushed all your days;
Deuteronomy 28:34 and you shall be deranged because of the sights of your eyes that you see.
Deuteronomy 28:35 May the Lord strike you with an evil sore on the knees and on the shins so that you cannot be healed, from the sole of your feet to your crown.
Deuteronomy 28:36 May the Lord lead you and your rulers whom you set over yourself away to a nation that you and your fathers do not know, and there you shall serve other gods, wood and stones.
Deuteronomy 28:37 And there you shall be a riddle and a parable and a tale among all the nations to which the Lord leads you away.
Deuteronomy 28:38 You shall carry much seed out to the plain and bring little in, because the locust shall devour it.
Deuteronomy 28:39 You shall plant a vineyard and cultivate it and shall not drink wine or rejoice from it, because the worm shall devour it.
Deuteronomy 28:40 You shall have olives within all your borders, and you shall not anoint yourself with oil, because your olive shall fall off.
Deuteronomy 28:41 You shall beget sons and daughters, and they shall not be yours, for they shall go away into captivity.
Deuteronomy 28:42 Rust shall consume all your trees and the produce of your land.
Deuteronomy 28:43 The sojourner who is among you shall rise above you, higher and higher, but you shall descend lower and lower;
Deuteronomy 28:44 he shall lend to you, but you shall not lend to him; he shall be head, but you shall be tail.
Deuteronomy 28:45 And all these curses shall come upon you and pursue you and overtake you until he destroys you and until he causes you to perish, because you did not listen to the voice of the Lord your God to guard his commandments and his ordinances that he commanded you.
Deuteronomy 28:46 And they shall be among you as signs and wonders, and among your offspring forever,
Deuteronomy 28:47 because you did not serve the Lord your God with joy and a good heart on account of the abundance of all things.
Deuteronomy 28:48 And you shall serve your enemies whom the Lord will send upon you, in famine and in thirst and in nakedness and in lack of all things; and he shall put an iron collar upon your neck until he destroys you.
Deuteronomy 28:49 The Lord shall bring against you a nation from afar, from the end of the earth, like the swoop of an eagle, a nation whose voice you shall not hear,
Deuteronomy 28:50 a nation shameless in face, which shall not regard the face of an old person and shall not have mercy on a young person,
Deuteronomy 28:51 and it shall devour the offspring of your animals and the produce of your land, leaving you neither grain nor wine nor oil, the herds of your cattle nor the flocks of your sheep, until it causes you to perish
Deuteronomy 28:52 and wears you away in all your cities until your high and fortified walls in which you trust are torn down throughout all your land; and it shall afflict you in all your cities that the Lord your God gave you.
Deuteronomy 28:53 And you shall eat the offspring of your womb, the flesh of your sons and daughters whom the Lord your God gave you, in your confinement and your affliction with which your enemy shall afflict you.
Deuteronomy 28:54 The tender and very delicate man among you shall look with an evil eye upon his brother and the wife in his bosom and the children left to him,
Deuteronomy 28:55 so as to give one of them some of the flesh of his children that he eats, because nothing is left to him in your confinement and your affliction with which your enemies shall afflict you in all your cities.
Deuteronomy 28:56 And the tender and very delicate woman among you, whose foot has not had experience treading upon the ground because of delicacy and tenderness, shall look with an evil eye upon her husband in her bosom and upon her son and her daughter
Deuteronomy 28:57 and her afterbirth that comes out from between her thighs and the child whom she bears; for she shall eat them secretly because of the lack of all things in your confinement and your affliction with which your enemy shall afflict you in all your cities.
Deuteronomy 28:58 If you do not listen to do all the words of this law written in this book, to fear this honored and wonderful name, the Lord your God,
Deuteronomy 28:59 then the Lord shall make your blows and the blows of your offspring extraordinary, great and wonderful blows, and evil and lasting diseases;
Deuteronomy 28:60 and he shall turn back upon you every evil pain of Egypt that you dreaded before them, and they shall cling to you.
Deuteronomy 28:61 And every sickness and every blow not written in the book of this law the Lord shall bring upon you until he destroys you.
Deuteronomy 28:62 And you shall be left few in number, whereas you were like the stars of heaven in multitude, because you did not listen to the voice of the Lord your God.
Deuteronomy 28:63 And it shall be, in the manner that the Lord rejoiced over you to do you good and multiply you, so the Lord shall rejoice over you to destroy you, and you shall be removed from the land into which you are entering to inherit it.
Deuteronomy 28:64 And the Lord your God shall scatter you among all the nations, from one end of the earth to the other end of the earth, and there you shall serve other gods, wood and stones, which neither you nor your fathers knew.
Deuteronomy 28:65 But also among those nations he shall not give you rest, nor shall there be a standing place for the sole of your foot, and the Lord shall give you there a disheartened heart and failing eyes and a melting soul.
Deuteronomy 28:66 And your life shall hang before your eyes, and you shall be afraid day and night and shall not trust in your life;
Deuteronomy 28:67 in the morning you shall say, “How might it become evening?” and in the evening you shall say, “How might it become morning?” because of the fear of your heart that you shall fear and because of the sights of your eyes that you shall see.
Deuteronomy 28:68 And the Lord shall turn you back to Egypt in ships and on the road of which I said, “You shall not again see it”; and there you shall be sold to your enemies as male and female servants, and there shall be no buyer.
Deuteronomy 28:69 These are the words of the covenant that the Lord commanded Moses to establish for the sons of Israel in the land of Moab, besides the covenant that he made with them at Choreb.

## Chapter 29

Deuteronomy 29:1 And Moses called all the sons of Israel and said to them, “You have seen all that the Lord did in the land of Egypt before you to Pharaoh and his attendants and all his land,
Deuteronomy 29:2 the great trials that your eyes have seen, those great signs and wonders;
Deuteronomy 29:3 and the Lord God has not given you a heart to know and eyes to see and ears to hear until this day.
Deuteronomy 29:4 And he led you forty years in the wilderness; your garments did not grow old, and your sandals were not worn away from your feet;
Deuteronomy 29:5 you did not eat bread, you did not drink wine and strong drink, so that you might know that this is the Lord your God.
Deuteronomy 29:6 And you came as far as this place, and Seon king of Esebon and Og king of Basan came out to meet us in war, and we struck them
Deuteronomy 29:7 and took their land, and I gave it as an inheritance to Reuben and Gaddi and the half tribe of Manasse.
Deuteronomy 29:8 And you shall take care to do all the words of this covenant, so that you may understand all that you do.
Deuteronomy 29:9 You all stand today before the Lord your God, your tribal chiefs and your council of elders and your judges and your scribal instructors, every man of Israel,
Deuteronomy 29:10 your women and your offspring and the sojourner in the midst of your camp, from your woodcutter to your water carrier,
Deuteronomy 29:11 to enter into the covenant of the Lord your God and into his curses, which the Lord your God is making with you today,
Deuteronomy 29:12 so that he may establish you for himself as a people, and he shall be your God, as he said to you and as he swore to your fathers Abraham and Isaac and Jacob.
Deuteronomy 29:13 And it is not with you alone that I make this covenant and this curse,
Deuteronomy 29:14 but also with those who are here with us today before the Lord your God and those who are not here with us today.
Deuteronomy 29:15 For you know how we dwelt in the land of Egypt and passed through the midst of the nations through which you passed,
Deuteronomy 29:16 and you saw their abominations and their idols, wood and stone, silver and gold, which are among them.
Deuteronomy 29:17 Is there perhaps among you a man or woman or family or tribe whose mind has turned away from the Lord your God to go and serve the gods of those nations? Is there perhaps among you a root growing upward in gall and bitterness?
Deuteronomy 29:18 And it shall be, if he hears the words of this curse and blesses himself in his heart, saying, “May holy things be mine, because I shall walk in the wandering of my heart,” so that the sinner may not destroy the sinless one along with him,
Deuteronomy 29:19 God will certainly not wish to be gracious to him; rather, then the anger of the Lord and his zeal shall burn against that man, and all the curses of this covenant written in this book of the law shall cling to him, and the Lord shall wipe out his name from under heaven;
Deuteronomy 29:20 and the Lord shall set him apart for evil from all the sons of Israel according to all the curses of the covenant written in this book of the law.
Deuteronomy 29:21 And the other generation, your sons who shall rise after you, and the foreigner who comes from a distant land shall speak, and they shall see the blows upon that land and its diseases that the Lord sent upon it –
Deuteronomy 29:22 sulfur and salt, burned; all its land shall not be sown nor sprout, nor shall any green thing grow upon it, as Sodom and Gomorra, Adama and Seboim were overthrown, which the Lord overthrew in fury and anger –
Deuteronomy 29:23 and all the nations shall say, “Why did the Lord do thus to this land? What is this great fury of anger?”
Deuteronomy 29:24 And they shall say, “Because they abandoned the covenant of the Lord, the God of their fathers, which he made with their fathers when he brought them out of the land of Egypt,
Deuteronomy 29:25 and they went and served other gods and bowed down to them, whom they did not know and whom he had not allotted to them;
Deuteronomy 29:26 and the Lord was angered in fury against that land, to bring upon it all the curses written in this book of the law,
Deuteronomy 29:27 and the Lord removed them from their land in fury and anger and very great provocation and cast them into another land, as now.”
Deuteronomy 29:28 The hidden things belong to the Lord our God, but the revealed things to us and to our children forever, to do all the words of this law.

## Chapter 30

Deuteronomy 30:1 And it shall be when all these words come upon you, the blessing and the curse that I set before your face, and you receive them into your heart among all the nations wherever the Lord scatters you,
Deuteronomy 30:2 and you turn to the Lord your God and obey his voice according to all that I command you today with all your heart and with all your soul,
Deuteronomy 30:3 then the Lord shall heal your sins and have mercy on you and gather you again from all the nations among which the Lord scattered you.
Deuteronomy 30:4 If your dispersion is from one end of heaven to the other end of heaven, from there the Lord your God shall gather you, and from there the Lord your God shall take you;
Deuteronomy 30:5 and the Lord your God shall bring you into the land that your fathers inherited, and you shall inherit it; and he shall do you good and make you more numerous than your fathers.
Deuteronomy 30:6 And the Lord shall cleanse your heart and the heart of your offspring, to love the Lord your God with all your heart and with all your soul, so that you may live.
Deuteronomy 30:7 And the Lord your God shall put these curses upon your enemies and upon those who hate you, who pursued you.
Deuteronomy 30:8 And you shall turn and listen to the voice of the Lord your God and do his commandments that I command you today,
Deuteronomy 30:9 and the Lord your God shall make you abundant in every work of your hands, in the offspring of your womb and in the produce of your land and in the offspring of your animals; because the Lord your God shall turn again to rejoice over you for good, as he rejoiced over your fathers,
Deuteronomy 30:10 if you listen to the voice of the Lord your God to guard and do all his commandments and his ordinances and his judgments written in this book of the law, if you turn to the Lord your God with all your heart and with all your soul.
Deuteronomy 30:11 For this commandment that I command you today is not excessive, nor is it far from you.
Deuteronomy 30:12 It is not up in heaven, saying, “Who shall ascend for us into heaven and take it for us? And having heard it, we shall do it.”
Deuteronomy 30:13 Nor is it beyond the sea, saying, “Who shall cross over for us to the other side of the sea and take it for us? And he shall make it heard by us, and we shall do it.”
Deuteronomy 30:14 The word is very near you, in your mouth and in your heart and in your hands, to do it.
Deuteronomy 30:15 Behold, I have set before your face today life and death, good and evil.
Deuteronomy 30:16 If you listen to the commandments of the Lord your God that I command you today, to love the Lord your God, to walk in all his ways, to guard his ordinances and his judgments, then you shall live and be many, and the Lord your God shall bless you in all the land into which you are entering to inherit it.
Deuteronomy 30:17 But if your heart turns away and you do not listen and, being led astray, bow down to other gods and serve them,
Deuteronomy 30:18 I announce to you today that you shall surely perish and shall certainly not become long-lived upon the land that the Lord your God gives you, into which you are crossing the Jordan to inherit it.
Deuteronomy 30:19 I call heaven and earth to witness to you today: I have set before your face life and death, blessing and curse; choose life, so that you and your offspring may live,
Deuteronomy 30:20 to love the Lord your God, to listen to his voice and to hold fast to him; for this is your life and the length of your days, for you to dwell upon the land that the Lord swore to your fathers Abraham and Isaac and Jacob to give them.

## Chapter 31

Deuteronomy 31:1 And Moses finished speaking all these words to all the sons of Israel;
Deuteronomy 31:2 and he said to them, “I am one hundred and twenty years old today; I can no longer go in and go out, and the Lord said to me, ‘You shall not cross this Jordan.’
Deuteronomy 31:3 The Lord your God, who goes before your face, he shall destroy these nations from before your face, and you shall inherit them; and Jesus shall go before your face, as the Lord spoke.
Deuteronomy 31:4 And the Lord shall do to them as he did to Seon and Og, the two kings of the Amorites who were beyond the Jordan, and to their land, when he destroyed them.
Deuteronomy 31:5 And the Lord has handed them over to you, and you shall do to them as I commanded you.
Deuteronomy 31:6 Be manly and strong; do not fear, nor be cowardly, nor be terrified before their face, because the Lord your God, who goes ahead with you among you, shall certainly not let you go nor forsake you.”
Deuteronomy 31:7 And Moses called Jesus and said to him before all Israel, “Be manly and strong; for you shall go in before this people into the land that the Lord swore to our fathers to give them, and you shall cause them to inherit it;
Deuteronomy 31:8 and the Lord who goes with you shall not let you go nor forsake you; do not fear nor be cowardly.”
Deuteronomy 31:9 And Moses wrote the words of this law in a book and gave it to the priests, the sons of Levi who carry the ark of the Lord’s covenant, and to the elders of the sons of Israel.
Deuteronomy 31:10 And Moses commanded them on that day, saying, “After seven years, at the time of the year of release, at the feast of the setting up of tents,
Deuteronomy 31:11 when all Israel comes together to appear before the Lord your God at the place the Lord chooses, you shall read this law before all Israel in their ears;
Deuteronomy 31:12 assemble the people, the men and the women and the offspring and the sojourner in your cities, so that they may hear and learn to fear the Lord your God, and they shall listen to do all the words of this law;
Deuteronomy 31:13 and their sons who do not know shall hear and learn to fear the Lord your God all the days that they live upon the land into which you are crossing the Jordan to inherit it.”
Deuteronomy 31:14 And the Lord said to Moses, “Behold, the days of your death have drawn near; call Jesus and stand by the doors of the tent of testimony, and I shall command him.” And Moses and Jesus went to the tent of testimony and stood by the doors of the tent of testimony.
Deuteronomy 31:15 And the Lord came down in a cloud and stood by the doors of the tent of testimony, and the pillar of cloud stood by the doors of the tent.
Deuteronomy 31:16 And the Lord said to Moses, “Behold, you are sleeping with your fathers, and this people shall arise and prostitute themselves after foreign gods of the land into which they are entering, and they shall forsake me and scatter my covenant that I made with them.
Deuteronomy 31:17 And I shall be angered in fury against them on that day and forsake them and turn my face away from them, and the people shall become food, and many evils and afflictions shall find him; and he shall say on that day, ‘Because the Lord my God is not among me, these evils have found me.’
Deuteronomy 31:18 But I shall surely turn my face away from them on that day because of all the wicked things they did, because they turned to foreign gods.
Deuteronomy 31:19 And now write the words of this song and teach it to the sons of Israel and put it into their mouth, so that this song may be a witness for me among the sons of Israel.
Deuteronomy 31:20 For I shall bring them into the good land that I swore to their fathers to give them, a land flowing with milk and honey, and they shall eat and, being filled, be sated; and they shall turn to foreign gods and serve them and provoke me and scatter my covenant.
Deuteronomy 31:21 And this song shall stand against them, testifying before their face, for it shall not be forgotten from their mouth and from the mouth of their offspring; for I know their wickedness, all that they do here today before I bring them into the good land that I swore to their fathers.”
Deuteronomy 31:22 And Moses wrote this song on that day and taught it to the sons of Israel.
Deuteronomy 31:23 And Moses commanded Jesus and said to him, “Be manly and strong; for you shall bring the sons of Israel into the land that the Lord swore to them, and he himself shall be with you.”
Deuteronomy 31:24 And when Moses finished writing all the words of this law in a book to the end,
Deuteronomy 31:25 he commanded the Levites who carry the ark of the Lord’s covenant, saying,
Deuteronomy 31:26 “Take the book of this law and place it beside the ark of the covenant of the Lord your God, and it shall be there among you as a witness.
Deuteronomy 31:27 For I know your provocation and your stiff neck; for even while I am alive with you today, you have been embittering matters toward God; how much more after my death?
Deuteronomy 31:28 Gather to me your tribal leaders and your elders and your judges and your scribal instructors, so that I may speak all these words into their ears and call heaven and earth to witness to them;
Deuteronomy 31:29 for I know that after my death you shall surely act lawlessly and turn aside from the way that I commanded you, and evils shall meet you at the end of days, because you shall do what is evil before the Lord, provoking him to anger by the works of your hands.”
Deuteronomy 31:30 And Moses spoke into the ears of all the assembly of Israel the words of this song to the end.

## Chapter 32

Deuteronomy 32:1 Attend, heaven, and I shall speak, and let earth hear words from my mouth.
Deuteronomy 32:2 Let my utterance be awaited as rain, and let my words come down as dew, like a shower upon grass and like snow upon herbage.
Deuteronomy 32:3 For I called upon the name of the Lord; give greatness to our God.
Deuteronomy 32:4 God—his works are true, and all his ways are judgments; a faithful God, and there is no injustice; righteous and holy is the Lord.
Deuteronomy 32:5 Blemished children sinned, not against him, a crooked and twisted generation.
Deuteronomy 32:6 Do you repay the Lord thus, foolish and unwise people? Is he not your father who acquired you and made you and created you?
Deuteronomy 32:7 Remember days of old, understand years of generation after generations; ask your father, and he shall tell you, your elders, and they shall say to you.
Deuteronomy 32:8 When the Most High divided nations, when he scattered the sons of Adam, he set the boundaries of nations according to the number of angels of God,
Deuteronomy 32:9 and the Lord’s portion became his people Jacob, the measured allotment of his inheritance Israel.
Deuteronomy 32:10 He provided for him in a wilderness land, in a thirst of heat in a waterless place; he encircled him and instructed him and guarded him as the pupil of an eye,
Deuteronomy 32:11 as an eagle might shelter its nest and yearned over its young; spreading its wings it received them and took them up on its back.
Deuteronomy 32:12 The Lord alone led them, and no foreign god was with them.
