Deuteronomy 32:13 He brought them up upon the strength of the land, fed them produce of fields; they suckled honey from a rock and oil from a solid rock,
Deuteronomy 32:14 butter of cattle and milk of sheep with fat of lambs and rams, sons of bulls and goats, with fat of kidneys of wheat; and they drank wine, blood of the grape.
Deuteronomy 32:15 And Jacob ate and was filled, and the beloved one kicked; he grew fat, grew heavy, grew broad; and he forsook God who made him and departed from God his savior.
Deuteronomy 32:16 They provoked me with foreign things; with their abominations they made me bitter;
Deuteronomy 32:17 they sacrificed to demons and not to God, to gods whom they did not know; new ones, recently arrived, whom their fathers did not know.
Deuteronomy 32:18 You forsook God who begot you and forgot God who nourished you.
Deuteronomy 32:19 And the Lord saw and was jealous and was provoked by the anger of his sons and daughters,
Deuteronomy 32:20 and said, “I shall turn my face away from them and show what shall befall them at the end; for they are a perverse generation, sons in whom there is no faith.”
Deuteronomy 32:21 They made me jealous over what is no god; they provoked me to anger with their idols; and I shall make them jealous over what is no nation; over an uncomprehending nation I shall provoke them to anger.
Deuteronomy 32:22 For fire has been kindled from my fury; it shall burn down to Hades below, devour the land and its produce, and burn the foundations of mountains.
Deuteronomy 32:23 I shall gather evils against them and spend my arrows on them.
Deuteronomy 32:24 Melting with famine and the eating of birds and incurable backward-stiffening; I shall send the teeth of beasts against them, with the fury of things crawling upon the ground.
Deuteronomy 32:25 Outside, a sword shall make them childless, and from the storerooms, fear; young man with virgin, nursing child with a settled elder.
Deuteronomy 32:26 I said, ‘I shall scatter them; I shall put an end to their remembrance among people,’
Deuteronomy 32:27 if not for the anger of enemies, so that they might not last long and so that the adversaries might not join together, lest they say, ‘Our hand is high, and it was not the Lord who did all these things.’
Deuteronomy 32:28 For they are a nation that has lost counsel, and there is no knowledge in them.
Deuteronomy 32:29 They did not think to understand these things; let them receive them for the time to come.
Deuteronomy 32:30 How shall one pursue a thousand and two dislodge myriads, unless God sold them and the Lord handed them over?
Deuteronomy 32:31 For their gods are not as our God; but our enemies are senseless.
Deuteronomy 32:32 For their vine is from the vine of Sodom, and their branch from Gomorra; their grape is a grape of gall, a cluster of bitterness for them;
Deuteronomy 32:33 their wine is the fury of dragons and the incurable fury of asps.
Deuteronomy 32:34 Are not these things gathered with me and sealed in my treasuries?
Deuteronomy 32:35 On a day of vengeance I shall repay, at a time when their foot slips; for the day of their destruction is near, and things are ready for you.
Deuteronomy 32:36 For the Lord shall judge his people, and concerning his servants he shall be comforted; for he saw them paralyzed and exhausted under assault and laid low.
Deuteronomy 32:37 And the Lord said, ‘Where are their gods in whom they trusted,
Deuteronomy 32:38 whose sacrifices’ fat you ate and whose libations’ wine you drank? Let them rise and help you, and let them become shelters for you.
Deuteronomy 32:39 See, see that I am, and there is no god besides me; I shall kill and make alive, I shall strike and I shall heal, and there is no one who shall rescue from my hands.
Deuteronomy 32:40 For I shall raise my hand to heaven and swear by my right hand and say, “I live forever,
Deuteronomy 32:41 for I shall sharpen my sword like lightning, and my hand shall take hold of judgment, and I shall repay justice to enemies and repay those who hate me;
Deuteronomy 32:42 I shall make my arrows drunk with blood, and my sword shall devour flesh, from the blood of the wounded and of captivity, from the head of rulers of enemies.
Deuteronomy 32:43 Rejoice, heavens, with him, and let all sons of God bow down to him; rejoice, nations, with his people, and let all angels of God strengthen him; for he avenges the blood of his sons, and he shall avenge and repay justice to enemies and repay those who hate him, and the Lord shall cleanse the land of his people.”
Deuteronomy 32:44 And Moses wrote this song on that day and taught it to the sons of Israel. And Moses entered and spoke all the words of this law into the ears of the people, he and Jesus son of Naue.
Deuteronomy 32:45 And Moses finished speaking to all Israel
Deuteronomy 32:46 and said to them, “Attend with your heart to all these words that I testify to you today, which you shall command your sons to guard and do, all the words of this law;
Deuteronomy 32:47 for this is not an empty word for you, because this is your life, and because of this word you shall live long upon the land into which you are crossing the Jordan to inherit it.”
Deuteronomy 32:48 And the Lord spoke to Moses on this day, saying,
Deuteronomy 32:49 “Go up to this mountain of Abarin, Mount Nabau, which is in the land of Moab opposite Jericho, and see the land of Canaan that I give the sons of Israel for a possession,
Deuteronomy 32:50 and die on the mountain to which you go up and be added to your people, as Aaron your brother died on Mount Or and was added to his people,
Deuteronomy 32:51 because you disobeyed my word among the sons of Israel at the water of dispute of Kades in the wilderness of Sin, because you did not sanctify me among the sons of Israel;
Deuteronomy 32:52 for you shall see the land from opposite it, but you shall not enter there.”

## Chapter 33

Deuteronomy 33:1 And this is the blessing with which Moses, the man of God, blessed the sons of Israel before his death;
Deuteronomy 33:2 and he said, “The Lord has come from Sina and appeared from Seir to us and hastened from Mount Pharan with myriads of Kades; at his right hand angels were with him.
Deuteronomy 33:3 And he spared his people, and all the sanctified ones are under your hands; and these are under you, and he received from his words
Deuteronomy 33:4 a law that Moses commanded us, an inheritance for the assemblies of Jacob.
Deuteronomy 33:5 And there shall be a ruler among the beloved one, when rulers of peoples are gathered together with the tribes of Israel.
Deuteronomy 33:6 Let Reuben live and not die, and let him be many in number.
Deuteronomy 33:7 And this is for Judas: ‘Hear, Lord, the voice of Judas, and may they come into his people; his hands shall decide for him, and you shall be a helper against his enemies.’
Deuteronomy 33:8 And to Levi he said, ‘Give Levi his manifest things and his truth to the holy man whom they tested in a trial and reviled at the water of dispute;
Deuteronomy 33:9 the one who says to his father and mother, “I have not seen you,” and did not acknowledge his brothers and disowned his sons; he guarded your oracles and kept your covenant.
Deuteronomy 33:10 They shall make your ordinances known to Jacob and your law to Israel; they shall put incense in your anger continually upon your altar.
Deuteronomy 33:11 Bless, Lord, his strength, and receive the works of his hands; break the loins of enemies rising against him, and let those who hate him not rise.’
Deuteronomy 33:12 And to Benjamin he said, ‘Beloved by the Lord, he shall dwell in trust, and God shades him all the days, and between his shoulders he rested.’
Deuteronomy 33:13 And to Joseph he said, ‘From the blessing of the Lord is his land, from the seasons of heaven and dew and from the deep springs below
Deuteronomy 33:14 and according to the season of the produce of the sun’s turnings and from the conjunctions of months
Deuteronomy 33:15 and from the summit of mountains of the beginning and from the summit of everlasting hills
Deuteronomy 33:16 and according to the season of the earth’s fullness. And may the things acceptable to the one who appeared in the bush come upon Joseph’s head, and upon the crown of the one glorified among brothers.
Deuteronomy 33:17 His beauty is a bull’s firstborn; his horns are horns of a one-horned beast; with them he shall gore nations together to the end of the earth. These are Ephraim’s myriads, and these are Manasse’s thousands.’
Deuteronomy 33:18 And to Zabulon he said, ‘Rejoice, Zabulon, in your going out, and Issachar in his dwellings.
Deuteronomy 33:19 They shall destroy nations, and you shall call upon there and sacrifice a sacrifice of righteousness, because the wealth of the sea shall suckle you and the trade of those dwelling by the sea.’
Deuteronomy 33:20 And to Gad he said, ‘Blessed is the one who broadens Gad; like a lion he rested, having broken arm and ruler.
Deuteronomy 33:21 And he saw his first fruits, because there a land of rulers was allotted, assembled together with leaders of peoples; the Lord did righteousness and his judgment with Israel.’
Deuteronomy 33:22 And to Dan he said, ‘Dan is a lion’s cub and shall leap out from Basan.’
Deuteronomy 33:23 And to Nephthali he said, ‘Nephthali is a fullness of acceptable things, and let him be filled with blessing from the Lord; he shall inherit sea and south.’
Deuteronomy 33:24 And to Aser he said, ‘Blessed among children is Aser, and he shall be acceptable to his brothers; he shall dip his foot in oil;
Deuteronomy 33:25 iron and bronze shall be his sandal, and as your days, so your strength.
Deuteronomy 33:26 There is none like the God of the beloved one, who rides upon heaven as your helper, and the majestic one of the firmament.
Deuteronomy 33:27 And the covering of God is of the beginning and beneath the strength of everlasting arms; and he shall cast out the enemy from before your face, saying, “Perish.”
Deuteronomy 33:28 And Israel shall dwell alone in trust upon the land of Jacob, upon grain and wine, and the heaven for him is clouded with dew.
Deuteronomy 33:29 Blessed are you, Israel; who is like you, a people saved by the Lord? Your helper shall shield you, and the sword is your boast; and your enemies shall lie to you, and you shall tread upon their necks.’

## Chapter 34

Deuteronomy 34:1 And Moses went up from Araboth Moab to Mount Nabau, to the summit of Phasga, which is opposite Jericho, and the Lord showed him all the land of Galaad as far as Dan
Deuteronomy 34:2 and all the land of Nephthali and all the land of Ephraim and Manasse and all the land of Judas as far as the farthest sea
Deuteronomy 34:3 and the wilderness and the regions around Jericho, the city of palms, as far as Segor.
Deuteronomy 34:4 And the Lord said to Moses, “This is the land that I swore to Abraham and Isaac and Jacob, saying, ‘I shall give it to your offspring’; and I have shown it to your eyes, but you shall not enter there.”
Deuteronomy 34:5 And Moses, household servant of the Lord, died in the land of Moab by the word of the Lord.
Deuteronomy 34:6 And they buried him in Gai in the land of Moab near the house of Phogor; and no one knows his burial place to this day.
Deuteronomy 34:7 And Moses was one hundred and twenty years old when he died; his eyes were not dimmed, nor were his chelynia worn out.
Deuteronomy 34:8 And the sons of Israel wept for Moses in Araboth Moab by the Jordan opposite Jericho for thirty days; and the days of mourning and weeping for Moses were completed.
Deuteronomy 34:9 And Jesus son of Naue was filled with a spirit of understanding, for Moses had laid his hands upon him; and the sons of Israel listened to him and did as the Lord commanded Moses.
Deuteronomy 34:10 And no prophet arose again in Israel like Moses, whom the Lord knew face to face,
Deuteronomy 34:11 in all the signs and wonders that the Lord sent him to do in the land of Egypt before Pharaoh and his attendants and all his land,
Deuteronomy 34:12 the great marvels and the mighty hand that Moses performed before all Israel.

# Joshua

The Apostolic Bible. Public domain. https://apostolic-bible.ysys9.chatgpt.site/license.html


## Chapter 1

Joshua 1:1 And it happened after the death of Moses that the Lord spoke to Jesus son of Naue, the assistant of Moses, saying,
Joshua 1:2 “Moses my attendant has died; now therefore rise and cross the Jordan, you and all this people, into the land that I give them.
Joshua 1:3 Every place upon which you set the sole of your feet I shall give to you, as I said to Moses;
Joshua 1:4 the wilderness and Antilibanos as far as the great river, the river Euphrates, and as far as the farthest sea from the setting of the sun shall be your boundaries.
Joshua 1:5 No person shall stand against you all the days of your life, and as I was with Moses, so I shall be with you, and I shall not forsake you nor overlook you.
Joshua 1:6 Be strong and manly; for you shall allot to this people the land that I swore to your fathers to give them.
Joshua 1:7 Therefore be strong and manly, to guard and do as Moses my servant commanded you, and you shall not turn aside from them to right or left, so that you may understand in all that you do.
Joshua 1:8 And the book of this law shall not depart from your mouth, and you shall meditate on it day and night, so that you may understand to do all that is written; then you shall prosper and make your ways prosper, and then you shall understand.
Joshua 1:9 Behold, I have commanded you; be strong and manly, do not be cowardly nor afraid, because the Lord your God is with you in every place wherever you go.”
Joshua 1:10 And Jesus commanded the scribes of the people, saying,
Joshua 1:11 “Go through the midst of the people’s camp and command the people, saying, ‘Prepare provisions, because in yet three days you are crossing this Jordan to enter and take possession of the land that the Lord, the God of your fathers, gives you.’”
Joshua 1:12 And to Reuben and Gad and the half tribe of Manasse Jesus said,
Joshua 1:13 “Remember the word of the Lord that Moses, the servant of the Lord, commanded you, saying, ‘The Lord your God has given you rest and has given you this land.
Joshua 1:14 Let your wives and your children and your animals dwell in the land that he gave you; but you shall cross over lightly equipped ahead of your brothers, every strong man, and fight alongside them,
Joshua 1:15 until the Lord your God gives your brothers rest as he did you, and they too inherit the land that the Lord our God gives them; and each of you shall go away to his inheritance that Moses gave you beyond the Jordan toward the rising of the sun.’”
Joshua 1:16 And answering Jesus they said, “Everything you command us we shall do, and to every place wherever you send us we shall go;
Joshua 1:17 in every way that we listened to Moses, we shall listen to you, only may the Lord our God be with you as he was with Moses.
Joshua 1:18 And the person who disobeys you and does not listen to your words, as you command him, let him die. But be strong and manly.”

## Chapter 2

Joshua 2:1 And Jesus son of Naue sent two young men from Sattin to spy, saying, “Go up and see the land and Jericho.” And the two young men went and entered Jericho and entered the house of a prostitute woman named Raab and lodged there.
Joshua 2:2 And it was reported to the king of Jericho, saying, “Men of the sons of Israel have come in here to spy out the land.”
Joshua 2:3 And the king of Jericho sent and said to Raab, saying, “Bring out the men who entered your house in the night; for they have come to spy out the land.”
Joshua 2:4 And the woman took the men and hid them and said to them, “The men have come to me;
Joshua 2:5 but when the gate was being shut in the darkness, the men went out; I do not know where they have gone. Pursue after them, if you can overtake them.”
Joshua 2:6 But she had brought them up onto the roof and hidden them among the stalks of flax that she had piled on the roof.
Joshua 2:7 And the men pursued after them on the road to the Jordan, toward the crossings, and the gate was shut. And it happened when those pursuing them had gone out
Joshua 2:8 and before they themselves went to sleep, she went up onto the roof to them
Joshua 2:9 and said to them, “I know that the Lord has given you the land, for fear of you has fallen upon us;
Joshua 2:10 for we have heard that the Lord God dried up the Red Sea before your face when you went out from the land of Egypt, and what he did to the two kings of the Amorites beyond the Jordan, Seon and Og, whom you destroyed;
Joshua 2:11 and when we heard, we were beside ourselves in our hearts, and no spirit remained in any of us before your face, because the Lord your God is God in heaven above and on the earth below.
Joshua 2:12 And now swear to me by the Lord God that, as I show you mercy, you too shall show mercy to my father’s house
Joshua 2:13 and preserve alive my father’s house and my mother and my brothers and all my household and all that belongs to them, and you shall deliver my life from death.”
Joshua 2:14 And the men said to her, “Our life in place of yours unto death.” And she said, “When the Lord hands the city over to you, you shall show me mercy and truth.”
Joshua 2:15 And she lowered them through the window
Joshua 2:16 and said to them, “Go away to the hill country, lest those pursuing meet you, and hide there for three days until those pursuing you turn back; and after that you shall go on your way.”
Joshua 2:17 And the men said to her, “We are innocent of this oath of yours;
Joshua 2:18 behold, we are entering a part of the city, and you shall set the sign: you shall tie this red cord in the window through which you lowered us, and you shall gather your father and your mother and your brothers and all your father’s household to yourself into your house.
Joshua 2:19 And it shall be that everyone who goes out the door of your house outside shall be liable for himself, but we shall be innocent of this oath of yours; and all who are with you in your house, we shall be liable.
Joshua 2:20 But if anyone wrongs us or reveals these words of ours, we shall be innocent of this oath of yours.”
Joshua 2:21 And she said to them, “According to your word, so let it be”; and she sent them away.
Joshua 2:22 And they went and came to the hill country and remained there three days; and those pursuing searched all the roads and did not find them.
Joshua 2:23 And the two young men returned and came down from the mountain and crossed over to Jesus son of Naue and related to him everything that had happened to them.
Joshua 2:24 And they said to Jesus, “The Lord has handed over all the land into our hand, and everyone dwelling in that land has cowered before us.”

## Chapter 3

Joshua 3:1 And Jesus rose early in the morning, and they set out from Sattin and came as far as the Jordan and lodged there before crossing.
Joshua 3:2 And it happened after three days that the scribes passed through the camp
Joshua 3:3 and commanded the people, saying, “When you see the ark of the covenant of the Lord our God and our priests and the Levites carrying it, set out from your places and go behind it;
Joshua 3:4 but let there be a distance between you and it of about two thousand cubits; you shall stand, not come near it, so that you may know the way you go; for you have not gone this way yesterday or the day before.”
Joshua 3:5 And Jesus said to the people, “Purify yourselves for tomorrow, because tomorrow the Lord shall do wonders among you.”
Joshua 3:6 And Jesus said to the priests, “Take up the ark of the Lord’s covenant and go before the people.” And the priests took up the ark of the Lord’s covenant and went before the people.
Joshua 3:7 And the Lord said to Jesus, “On this day I begin to exalt you before all the sons of Israel, so that they may know that as I was with Moses, so I shall be with you.
Joshua 3:8 And now command the priests who carry the ark of the covenant, saying, ‘When you enter the edge of the water of the Jordan, you shall stand in the Jordan.’”
Joshua 3:9 And Jesus said to the sons of Israel, “Come here and hear the word of the Lord our God.
Joshua 3:10 By this you shall know that the living God is among you and that he shall surely destroy from before our face the Canaanite and the Chettite and the Pherezite and the Euaite and the Amorite and the Gergesite and the Jebusite;
Joshua 3:11 behold, the ark of the covenant of the Lord of all the earth crosses the Jordan.
Joshua 3:12 Choose for yourselves twelve men from the sons of Israel, one from each tribe.
Joshua 3:13 And it shall be that when the feet of the priests carrying the ark of the covenant of the Lord of all the earth rest in the water of the Jordan, the water of the Jordan shall fail, but the water coming down shall stand.”
Joshua 3:14 And the people set out from their dwellings to cross the Jordan, and the priests carried the ark of the Lord’s covenant ahead of the people.
Joshua 3:15 And when the priests carrying the ark of the covenant entered the Jordan and the feet of the priests carrying the ark of the Lord’s covenant were dipped into the edge of the Jordan’s water—the Jordan filled all along its bank as in the days of wheat harvest—,
Joshua 3:16 the waters coming down from above stood; they stood in one mass very far away as far as the region of Kariathiarim, but what was coming down went down into the sea of Araba, the Salt Sea, until it failed completely; and the people stood opposite Jericho.
Joshua 3:17 And the priests carrying the ark of the Lord’s covenant stood on dry ground in the middle of the Jordan; and all the sons of Israel crossed on dry ground until all the people had finished crossing the Jordan.

## Chapter 4

Joshua 4:1 And when all the people had finished crossing the Jordan, the Lord said to Jesus, saying,
Joshua 4:2 “Take men from the people, one from each tribe,
Joshua 4:3 and instruct them, saying, ‘Take up twelve prepared stones from the middle of the Jordan and carry them with yourselves and put them in your camp wherever you camp tonight.’”
Joshua 4:4 And Jesus called twelve men of distinction from the sons of Israel, one from each tribe,
Joshua 4:5 and said to them, “Come forward before me, before the Lord, into the middle of the Jordan, and let each take up a stone from there and carry it on his shoulders according to the number of the twelve tribes of Israel,
Joshua 4:6 so that these may be a sign for you, set down always, so that when your son asks you tomorrow, saying, ‘What are these stones to you?’
Joshua 4:7 you shall explain to your son, saying, ‘The river Jordan failed before the ark of the covenant of the Lord of all the earth as it crossed it’; and these stones shall be a memorial for you, for the sons of Israel, forever.”
Joshua 4:8 And the sons of Israel did thus as the Lord commanded Jesus, and took twelve stones from the middle of the Jordan, as the Lord instructed Jesus at the completion of the sons of Israel’s crossing, and carried them with themselves into the camp and laid them there.
Joshua 4:9 And Jesus also set up twelve other stones in the Jordan itself at the place beneath the feet of the priests who carried the ark of the Lord’s covenant, and they are there to this day.
Joshua 4:10 And the priests who carried the ark of the covenant stood in the Jordan until Jesus had finished everything that the Lord commanded him to tell the people, and the people hurried and crossed.
Joshua 4:11 And it happened when all the people had finished crossing that the ark of the Lord’s covenant crossed, and the stones before them.
Joshua 4:12 And the sons of Reuben and the sons of Gad and the half of the tribe of Manasse crossed equipped before the sons of Israel, as Moses commanded them.
Joshua 4:13 Forty thousand lightly equipped for battle crossed before the Lord for war toward the city of Jericho.
Joshua 4:14 On that day the Lord exalted Jesus before all the race of Israel, and they feared him as they did Moses as long as he lived.
Joshua 4:15 And the Lord said to Jesus, saying,
Joshua 4:16 “Command the priests who carry the ark of the covenant of the Lord’s testimony to come up out of the Jordan.”
Joshua 4:17 And Jesus commanded the priests, saying, “Come up out of the Jordan.”
Joshua 4:18 And it happened when the priests carrying the ark of the Lord’s covenant had come up out of the Jordan and set their feet upon the land, the water of the Jordan rushed back to its place and flowed as yesterday and the day before along all its bank.
Joshua 4:19 And the people came up out of the Jordan on the tenth of the first month; and the sons of Israel camped in Galgalois in the part toward the sunrise from Jericho.
Joshua 4:20 And these twelve stones that he took from the Jordan Jesus set up in Galgalois,
Joshua 4:21 saying, “When your sons ask you, saying, ‘What are these stones?’
Joshua 4:22 tell your sons that Israel crossed the Jordan on dry ground,
Joshua 4:23 the Lord our God having dried up the water of the Jordan before them until they crossed, just as the Lord our God did to the Red Sea, which the Lord our God dried up before us until we passed through,
Joshua 4:24 so that all the nations of the earth may know that the power of the Lord is strong and that you may revere the Lord your God at all times.”

## Chapter 5

Joshua 5:1 And it happened when the kings of the Amorites who were beyond the Jordan and the kings of Phoenicia by the sea heard that the Lord God had dried up the river Jordan before the sons of Israel as they crossed, their minds melted and they were astonished, and no understanding at all remained in them before the sons of Israel.
Joshua 5:2 At that time the Lord said to Jesus, “Make for yourself stone knives from a sharp-edged stone and, sitting down, circumcise the sons of Israel.”
Joshua 5:3 And Jesus made sharp-edged stone knives and circumcised the sons of Israel at the place called Hill of the Foreskins.
Joshua 5:4 And in the manner in which Jesus purified the sons of Israel, however many had been born on the way and however many of those who had gone out from Egypt were uncircumcised,
Joshua 5:5 Jesus circumcised all these;
Joshua 5:6 for Israel had spent forty-two years in the Madbarite wilderness, and for this reason most of them, the fighting men who had gone out from the land of Egypt and had disobeyed God’s commandments, were uncircumcised; to these he also determined that they would not see the land that the Lord swore to their fathers to give us, a land flowing with milk and honey.
Joshua 5:7 And in place of these he raised up their sons, whom Jesus circumcised because they had been born uncircumcised along the way.
Joshua 5:8 And having been circumcised, they rested there, sitting in the camp until they were healed.
Joshua 5:9 And the Lord said to Jesus son of Naue, “On this very day I have removed the reproach of Egypt from you.” And he called the name of that place Galgala.
Joshua 5:10 And the sons of Israel observed the Passover on the fourteenth day of the month from evening, west of Jericho beyond the Jordan in the plain,
Joshua 5:11 and they ate from the grain of the land, unleavened things and new things, on this day.
Joshua 5:12 The manna ceased after they had eaten from the grain of the land, and manna was no longer available to the sons of Israel; but they partook of the region of the Phoenicians in that year.
Joshua 5:13 And it happened when Jesus was in Jericho that he looked up with his eyes and saw a man standing before him, and a drawn sword was in his hand. And Jesus came forward and said to him, “Are you ours or one of our adversaries?”
Joshua 5:14 And he said to him, “I have now arrived as commander-in-chief of the Lord’s force.” And Jesus fell face down to the ground and said to him, “Master, what do you command your household servant?”
Joshua 5:15 And the commander-in-chief of the Lord says to Jesus, “Loosen the sandal from your feet; for the place upon which you stand is holy.”

## Chapter 6

Joshua 6:1 And Jericho was shut up and fortified, and no one went out of it or went in.
Joshua 6:2 And the Lord said to Jesus, “Behold, I hand over Jericho under your hand, and its king and the strong ones in it who are mighty in strength;
Joshua 6:3 but you shall station the fighting men around it,
Joshua 6:5 and it shall be that when you sound the trumpet, let all the people shout together, and when they shout, the walls of the city shall fall of themselves, and all the people shall enter, each rushing straight ahead into the city.”
Joshua 6:6 And Jesus son of Naue went in to the priests
Joshua 6:7 and said to them, “Command the people to go around and encircle the city, and let the fighting men pass armed before the Lord;
Joshua 6:8 and let seven priests having seven sacred trumpets likewise pass before the Lord and sound them strongly, and let the ark of the Lord’s covenant follow;
Joshua 6:9 and let the fighting men pass in front, and the priests bringing up the rear go behind the ark of the Lord’s covenant, walking and sounding the trumpets.”
Joshua 6:10 And Jesus commanded the people, saying, “Do not shout, nor let any of you hear the voice, until the day he announces to shout; then you shall shout.”
Joshua 6:11 And the ark of God’s covenant, having gone around the city, immediately went away to the camp and slept there.
Joshua 6:12 And on the second day Jesus arose early in the morning, and the priests took up the ark of the Lord’s covenant,
Joshua 6:13 and the seven priests carrying the seven trumpets went ahead before the Lord, and after them the fighting men came in and the rest of the crowd behind the ark of the Lord’s covenant; and the priests sounded the trumpets, and all the rest of the crowd encircled the city nearby
Joshua 6:14 and went away again to the camp. Thus he did for six days.
Joshua 6:15 And on the seventh day they rose at dawn and went around the city six times;
Joshua 6:16 and on the seventh circuit the priests sounded the trumpets, and Jesus said to the sons of Israel, “Shout; for the Lord has handed the city over to you.
Joshua 6:17 And the city shall be devoted, it and everything in it, to the Lord Sabaoth; except Raab the prostitute, preserve her and all who are in her house.
Joshua 6:18 But you, guard yourselves very carefully from the devoted thing, lest, considering it, you yourselves take from the devoted thing and make the camp of the sons of Israel devoted and wear us away;
Joshua 6:19 and all silver or gold or bronze or iron shall be holy to the Lord; it shall be brought into the Lord’s treasury.”
Joshua 6:20 And the priests sounded the trumpets; and when the people heard the sound of the trumpets, all the people together shouted with a great and strong shout. And the whole wall fell all around, and all the people went up into the city.
Joshua 6:21 And Jesus devoted it and everything that was in the city, from man to woman, from young man to elder and to calf and beast of burden, by the edge of the sword.
Joshua 6:22 And Jesus said to the two young men who had spied, “Enter the woman’s house and bring her out from there and everything that belongs to her.”
Joshua 6:23 And the two young men who had spied out the city entered the woman’s house and brought out Raab the prostitute and her father and her mother and her brothers and everything that belonged to her and all her kin, and set her outside Israel’s camp.
Joshua 6:24 And the city was burned with fire with everything in it, except that silver and gold and bronze and iron they gave to be brought into the Lord’s treasury.
Joshua 6:25 And Jesus kept Raab the prostitute and all her father’s household alive, and she dwelt in Israel until this day, because she hid the spies whom Jesus sent to spy out Jericho. –
Joshua 6:26 And Jesus made an oath on that day before the Lord, saying, “Accursed is the man who builds that city; with his firstborn he shall lay its foundation, and with his youngest he shall set up its gates.” And Ozan from Baethel did so; with Abiron his firstborn he founded it, and with his youngest, who survived, he set up its gates.
Joshua 6:27 And the Lord was with Jesus, and his name was throughout all the land.

## Chapter 7

Joshua 7:1 And the sons of Israel committed a great trespass and appropriated from the devoted thing; and Achar son of Charmi son of Zambri son of Zara from the tribe of Judas took from the devoted thing; and the Lord was fiercely angered with the sons of Israel.
Joshua 7:2 And Jesus sent men to Gai, which is by Baethel, saying, “Spy out Gai”; and the men went up and spied out Gai.
Joshua 7:3 And they returned to Jesus and said to him, “Do not let all the people go up; let about two or three thousand men go up and besiege the city; do not bring all the people there, for they are few.”
Joshua 7:4 And about three thousand men went up and fled before the men of Gai.
Joshua 7:5 And the men of Gai killed about thirty-six men of them and pursued them from the gate and crushed them on the slope; and the people’s heart was terrified and became like water.
Joshua 7:6 And Jesus tore his garments, and Jesus fell on the ground on his face before the Lord until evening, he and the elders of Israel, and they put earth on their heads.
Joshua 7:7 And Jesus said, “I pray, Lord, why did your servant bring this people across the Jordan to hand them over to the Amorite to destroy us? If only we had remained and dwelt beside the Jordan.
Joshua 7:8 And what shall I say, since Israel has turned the neck before its enemy?
Joshua 7:9 And when the Canaanite and all the inhabitants of the land hear, they shall surround us and wear us away from the land; and what shall you do for your great name?”
Joshua 7:10 And the Lord said to Jesus, “Arise; why have you fallen on your face like this?
Joshua 7:11 The people have sinned and transgressed the covenant that I made with them, and, having stolen from the devoted thing, put it among their vessels.
Joshua 7:12 The sons of Israel shall certainly not be able to stand before their enemies; they shall turn their neck before their enemies, because they have become devoted; I shall no longer continue to be with you unless you remove the devoted thing from among yourselves.
Joshua 7:13 Rise, sanctify the people and tell them to be sanctified for tomorrow; thus says the Lord, the God of Israel: ‘The devoted thing is among you; you shall not be able to stand before your enemies until you remove the devoted thing from among you.’
Joshua 7:14 And you shall all be gathered in the morning by tribes, and the tribe that the Lord shows you shall bring forward by clans; and the clan that the Lord shows you shall bring forward by household; and the household that the Lord shows you shall bring forward man by man;
Joshua 7:15 and whoever is indicated shall be burned with fire, he and everything that belongs to him, because he transgressed the Lord’s covenant and committed lawlessness in Israel.” –
Joshua 7:16 And Jesus rose early and brought forward the people by tribes, and the tribe of Judas was indicated;
Joshua 7:17 and it was brought forward by clans, and the clan of Zara was indicated; and it was brought forward man by man,
Joshua 7:18 and Achar son of Zambri son of Zara was indicated.
Joshua 7:19 And Jesus said to Achar, “Give glory today to the Lord God of Israel and give the confession and tell me what you have done; do not hide it from me.”
Joshua 7:20 And Achar answered Jesus and said, “Truly I sinned before the Lord God of Israel; thus and thus I did;
Joshua 7:21 I saw among the spoil a fine, variegated, beautiful thing, and two hundred didrachmas of silver and one golden tongue of fifty didrachmas, and having thought about them I took them, and behold, they are hidden in the earth in my tent, and the silver is hidden beneath them.”
Joshua 7:22 And Jesus sent messengers, and they ran to the tent in the camp; and these things were hidden in the tent, and the silver beneath them.
Joshua 7:23 And they brought them out of the tent and brought them to Jesus and the elders of Israel, and set them before the Lord.
Joshua 7:24 And Jesus took Achar son of Zara and brought him into the ravine of Achor, and his sons and his daughters and his calves and his beasts of burden and all his sheep and his tent and everything that belonged to him, and all the people with him; and he brought them into Emekachor.
Joshua 7:25 And Jesus said to Achar, “Why did you destroy us? May the Lord destroy you, as today.” And all Israel stoned him with stones.
Joshua 7:26 And they raised a great heap of stones over him. And the Lord ceased from the fury of his anger. Therefore he named it Emekachor to this day.

## Chapter 8

Joshua 8:1 And the Lord said to Jesus, “Do not fear nor be cowardly; take with you all the fighting men and rise and go up to Gai; behold, I have given into your hands the king of Gai and his land.
Joshua 8:2 And you shall do to Gai as you did to Jericho and its king, and you shall take the spoil of the animals for yourself. But set an ambush for yourself behind the city.”
Joshua 8:3 And Jesus and all the fighting people arose to go up to Gai. And Jesus chose thirty thousand men strong in might and sent them by night.
Joshua 8:4 And he commanded them, saying, “You shall lie in ambush behind the city; do not be far from the city, and all of you shall be ready.
Joshua 8:5 And I and all those with me shall approach the city, and it shall be that when the inhabitants of Gai come out to meet us as before, we shall flee before them.
Joshua 8:6 And when they come out after us, we shall draw them away from the city; and they shall say, ‘These flee before us as they did before.’
Joshua 8:7 But you shall rise up from the ambush and go into the city.
Joshua 8:8 You shall do according to this word; behold, I have commanded you.”
Joshua 8:9 And Jesus sent them, and they went to the ambush and lay between Baethel and Gai, to the west of Gai.
Joshua 8:10 And Jesus rose early in the morning and inspected the people; and he and the elders went up before the people toward Gai.
Joshua 8:11 And all the fighting people with him went up and, proceeding, came opposite the city from the east,
Joshua 8:12 and the city’s ambush was from the west.
Joshua 8:14 And it happened when the king of Gai saw, he hastened and went out to meet them directly for battle, he and all the people with him; and he did not know that there was an ambush for him behind the city.
Joshua 8:15 And Jesus and Israel saw and withdrew before them.
Joshua 8:16 And they pursued after the sons of Israel, and they themselves moved away from the city;
Joshua 8:17 no one was left in Gai who did not pursue after Israel; and they left the city open and pursued after Israel.
Joshua 8:18 And the Lord said to Jesus, “Stretch out your hand with the javelin in your hand toward the city—for I have handed it into your hands—and the ambush shall rise quickly from its place.” And Jesus stretched out his hand, the javelin, toward the city,
Joshua 8:19 and the ambush rose quickly from its place and went out when he stretched out his hand, and they came upon the city and seized it and hurried to burn the city with fire.
Joshua 8:20 And the inhabitants of Gai looked behind them and saw smoke rising from the city to heaven; and they no longer had anywhere to flee, here or there.
Joshua 8:21 And Jesus and all Israel saw that the ambush had taken the city and that the smoke of the city had risen to heaven, and they turned and struck the men of Gai.
Joshua 8:22 And these came out from the city to meet them, and they were between the camp, these on this side and those on that side; and they struck them until none of them remained saved or escaped.
Joshua 8:23 And they seized the king of Gai alive and brought him to Jesus.
Joshua 8:24 And when the sons of Israel finished killing all those of Gai in the plains and on the mountain on the descent, where they pursued them from it to the end, Jesus turned back to Gai and struck it with the edge of the sword.
Joshua 8:25 And those who fell that day, from man to woman, were twelve thousand, all the inhabitants of Gai,
Joshua 8:27 except for the animals and the spoils in the city, all that the sons of Israel took as spoil according to the Lord’s command, as the Lord instructed Jesus.
Joshua 8:28 And Jesus burned the city with fire; he made it an uninhabited mound forever, until this day.
Joshua 8:29 And he hung the king of Gai on a double tree, and he was on the tree until evening; and when the sun was setting, Jesus gave an order, and they took his body down from the tree and threw him into the pit and set a heap of stones over him until this day.

## Chapter 9

Joshua 9:1 And when the kings of the Amorites beyond the Jordan, those in the hill country and those in the plain and those along the whole shore of the Great Sea and those near Antilibanos, and the Chettites and the Canaanites and the Pherezites and the Euaites and the Amorites and the Gergesites and the Jebusites heard,
Joshua 9:2 they all gathered together to wage war against Jesus and Israel together.
Joshua 9:2 a Then Jesus built an altar to the Lord, the God of Israel, on Mount Gaibal,
Joshua 9:3 as Moses the attendant of the Lord commanded the sons of Israel, as it is written in Moses’ law, an altar of whole stones upon which no iron had been laid, and there he offered whole burnt offerings to the Lord and a sacrifice of salvation.
Joshua 9:4 And Jesus wrote upon the stones the second law, the law of Moses that he wrote before the sons of Israel.
Joshua 9:5 And all Israel and their elders and their judges and their scribes passed on this side and that opposite the ark, and the priests and the Levites carried the ark of the Lord’s covenant, and the sojourner and the native-born, half of them near Mount Garizin and half of them near Mount Gaibal, as Moses the attendant of the Lord commanded, to bless the people first.
Joshua 9:6 And after these things Jesus thus read all the words of this law, the blessings and the curses, according to all that is written in Moses’ law;
Joshua 9:7 there was no word among all that Moses commanded Jesus that Jesus did not read into the ears of all the assembly of the sons of Israel, to the men and women and children and the sojourners who joined Israel.
Joshua 9:3 And the inhabitants of Gabaon heard all that the Lord had done to Jericho and Gai.
Joshua 9:4 And they too acted with cunning and, coming, provisioned themselves and prepared themselves and took old sacks on their donkeys and old, torn, tied-up wineskins,
Joshua 9:5 and the hollow parts of their shoes and their sandals were old and resoled on their feet, and their garments worn out upon them, and their provision bread dry and moldy and eaten away.
Joshua 9:6 And they came to Jesus in the camp of Israel at Galgala and said to Jesus and Israel, “We have come from a distant land, and now make a covenant with us.”
Joshua 9:7 And the sons of Israel said to the Chorraite, “See that you are not dwelling among me; and how shall I make a covenant with you?”
Joshua 9:8 And they said to Jesus, “We are your household servants.” And Jesus said to them, “Where are you from, and whence have you come?”
Joshua 9:9 And they said, “Your servants have come from a very distant land in the name of the Lord your God; for we have heard his name and all that he did in Egypt
Joshua 9:10 and all that he did to the kings of the Amorites who were beyond the Jordan, to Seon king of Esebon and Og king of Basan, who dwelt in Astaroth and Edraim.
Joshua 9:11 And having heard, our elders and all the inhabitants of our land said to us, ‘Take provisions for yourselves for the journey and go to meet them and say to them, “We are your household servants, and now make a covenant with us.”’
Joshua 9:12 These loaves we provisioned while hot on the day we went out to come to you, but now they have dried and become eaten away;
Joshua 9:13 and these wineskins that we filled when new, these have torn; and our garments and our shoes have worn out from the very long journey.”
Joshua 9:14 And the rulers took from their provisions and did not inquire of the Lord.
Joshua 9:15 And Jesus made peace with them and made a covenant with them to preserve them, and the rulers of the assembly swore to them. –
Joshua 9:16 And it happened three days after making a covenant with them that they heard that they were near them and dwelt among them.
Joshua 9:17 And the sons of Israel set out and came to their cities; and their cities were Gabaon and Kephira and Beroth and the city of Iarin.
Joshua 9:18 And the sons of Israel did not fight them, because all the rulers had sworn to them by the Lord, the God of Israel; and all the assembly murmured against the rulers.
Joshua 9:19 And the rulers said to all the assembly, “We swore to them by the Lord, the God of Israel, and now we cannot touch them;
Joshua 9:20 this we shall do: keep them alive, and we shall preserve them, and there shall be no anger against us because of the oath that we swore to them;
Joshua 9:21 they shall live and be woodcutters and water carriers for all the assembly,” as the rulers said to them.
Joshua 9:22 And Jesus called them together and said to them, “Why did you deceive me, saying, ‘We are very far from you,’ when you are local people among those dwelling with us?
Joshua 9:23 And now you are accursed; a servant and a woodcutter for me and my God shall certainly not cease from among you.”
Joshua 9:24 And they answered Jesus, saying, “We were told all that the Lord your God instructed Moses his servant, to give you this land and to destroy us and all who dwell upon it before your face, and we greatly feared for our lives before your face and did this thing.
Joshua 9:25 And now behold, we are under your hands; do to us as pleases you and as seems good to you.”
Joshua 9:26 And they did thus to them; and Jesus rescued them that day from the hands of the sons of Israel, and they did not kill them.
Joshua 9:27 And Jesus appointed them on that day as woodcutters and water carriers for all the assembly and for the altar of God; for this reason the inhabitants of Gabaon became woodcutters and water carriers for the altar of God until this day and for the place that the Lord shall choose.

## Chapter 10

Joshua 10:1 And when Adonibezek king of Jerusalem heard that Jesus had taken Gai and destroyed it—as they did to Jericho and its king, so they did to Gai and its king—and that the inhabitants of Gabaon had gone over to Jesus and Israel,
Joshua 10:2 they were very afraid among themselves; for he knew that Gabaon was a great city, like one of the chief cities, and all its men were strong.
Joshua 10:3 And Adonibezek king of Jerusalem sent to Ailam king of Chebron and to Phidon king of Jerimuth and to Jephtha king of Lachis and to Dabir king of Odollam, saying,
Joshua 10:4 “Come, go up to me and help me, and let us wage war against Gabaon; for they have gone over to Jesus and the sons of Israel.”
Joshua 10:5 And the five kings of the Jebusites went up, the king of Jerusalem and the king of Chebron and the king of Jerimuth and the king of Lachis and the king of Odollam, they and all their people, and encamped around Gabaon and besieged it.
Joshua 10:6 And the inhabitants of Gabaon sent to Jesus at Israel’s camp in Galgala, saying, “Do not relax your hands from your servants; come up to us quickly and deliver us and help us, for all the kings of the Amorites who dwell in the hill country are gathered against us.”
Joshua 10:7 And Jesus went up from Galgala, he and all the fighting people with him, everyone strong in might.
Joshua 10:8 And the Lord said to Jesus, “Do not fear them; for I have handed them into your hands; no one of them shall remain before you.”
Joshua 10:9 And Jesus came upon them suddenly; he had traveled all night from Galgala.
Joshua 10:10 And the Lord threw them into confusion before the sons of Israel, and the Lord crushed them with a great crushing in Gabaon, and they pursued them along the road of the ascent of Oronin and cut them down as far as Azeka and as far as Makeda.
Joshua 10:11 And as they fled before the sons of Israel on the descent of Oronin, the Lord cast hailstones upon them from heaven as far as Azeka, and more died from the hailstones than the sons of Israel killed with the sword in battle.
Joshua 10:12 Then Jesus spoke to the Lord on the day when God handed the Amorite under Israel’s hand, when he crushed them in Gabaon and they were crushed before the sons of Israel, and Jesus said, “Let the sun stand still over Gabaon and the moon over the ravine of Ailon.”
Joshua 10:13 And the sun stood still and the moon stood in place until God defended them against their enemies. And the sun stood in the middle of heaven and did not go ahead toward setting for the end of one whole day.
Joshua 10:14 And there was no such day before or afterward in which God listened to a person, because the Lord fought alongside Israel.
Joshua 10:16 And these five kings fled and hid in the cave in Makeda.
Joshua 10:17 And it was reported to Jesus, saying, “The five kings have been found hidden in the cave in Makeda.”
Joshua 10:18 And Jesus said, “Roll stones over the mouth of the cave and appoint men to guard them,
Joshua 10:19 but you must not stand still; pursue after your enemies and overtake their rear guard and do not let them enter their cities; for the Lord our God has handed them into our hands.”
Joshua 10:20 And it happened when Jesus and all the sons of Israel finished striking them with a very great blow to the end, and those escaping escaped into the fortified cities,
Joshua 10:21 all the people returned to Jesus at Makeda unharmed, and none of the sons of Israel made a sound with his tongue.
Joshua 10:22 And Jesus said, “Open the cave and bring these five kings out of the cave.”
Joshua 10:23 And they brought the five kings out of the cave: the king of Jerusalem and the king of Chebron and the king of Jerimuth and the king of Lachis and the king of Odollam.
Joshua 10:24 And when they brought them to Jesus, Jesus called together all Israel and the leaders of the war who went with him, saying to them, “Come forward and put your feet upon their necks.” And they came forward and put their feet upon their necks.
Joshua 10:25 And Jesus said to them, “Do not fear them or be cowardly; be manly and strong, because thus the Lord shall do to all your enemies against whom you wage war.”
Joshua 10:26 And Jesus killed them and hung them on five trees, and they hung on the trees until evening.
Joshua 10:27 And at sunset Jesus commanded, and they took them down from the trees and threw them into the cave into which they had fled, and rolled stones over the cave until this day.
Joshua 10:28 And they took Makeda on that day and killed it with the edge of the sword and destroyed every breathing thing in it, and no one saved or escaped remained in it; and they did to the king of Makeda as they had done to the king of Jericho.
Joshua 10:29 And Jesus and all Israel with him went from Makeda to Lebna and besieged Lebna.
Joshua 10:30 And the Lord handed it into Israel’s hands, and they took it and its king and killed it with the edge of the sword and every breathing thing in it, and not even one saved or escaped remained in it; and they did to its king as they had done to the king of Jericho.
Joshua 10:31 And Jesus and all Israel with him went from Lebna to Lachis and encamped around it and besieged it.
Joshua 10:32 And the Lord handed Lachis into Israel’s hands, and he took it on the second day, and they killed it with the edge of the sword and destroyed it, as they had done to Lebna. –
Joshua 10:33 Then Ailam king of Gazer went up to help Lachis, and Jesus struck him with the edge of the sword and his people, until none of them remained saved or escaped.
Joshua 10:34 And Jesus and all Israel with him went from Lachis to Odollam and encamped around it and besieged it.
Joshua 10:35 And the Lord handed it into Israel’s hand, and he took it on that day and killed it with the edge of the sword, and they killed every breathing thing in it, as they had done to Lachis.
Joshua 10:36 And Jesus and all Israel with him went to Chebron and encamped around it.
Joshua 10:37 And he struck it with the edge of the sword and every breathing thing in it; there was no survivor; as they had done to Odollam, they destroyed it and everything in it.
Joshua 10:38 And Jesus and all Israel returned to Dabir and encamped around it,
Joshua 10:39 and they took it and its king and its villages and struck it with the edge of the sword and destroyed it and every breathing thing in it and left no survivor in it; as they had done to Chebron and its king, so they did to Dabir and its king.
Joshua 10:40 And Jesus struck all the land of the hill country and the Nageb and the plain and Asedoth and its kings; they left no survivor among them; and he destroyed every living, breathing thing, as the Lord, the God of Israel, had commanded,
Joshua 10:41 from Kades Barne to Gaza, all Gosom as far as Gabaon,
Joshua 10:42 and Jesus struck all their kings and their land at once, because the Lord, the God of Israel, fought alongside Israel.

## Chapter 11

Joshua 11:1 And when Jabin king of Asor heard, he sent to Jobab king of Marron and to the king of Symoon and to the king of Aziph
Joshua 11:2 and to the kings by great Sidon, into the hill country and into Raba opposite Keneroth and into the plain and into Napheddor
Joshua 11:3 and to the coastal Canaanites from the east and to the coastal Amorites and Euaites and Jebusites and Pherezites in the mountain and the Chettites below Aermon in the land of Massepha.
Joshua 11:4 And they and their kings with them came out, like the sand of the sea in multitude, and very many horses and chariots.
Joshua 11:5 And all these kings gathered and came together and encamped by the water of Marron to fight Israel.
Joshua 11:6 And the Lord said to Jesus, “Do not fear before them, because tomorrow at this hour I shall hand them over routed before Israel; you shall cut the tendons of their horses and burn their chariots with fire.”
Joshua 11:7 And Jesus and all the fighting people came upon them by the water of Marron suddenly and fell upon them in the hill country.
Joshua 11:8 And the Lord handed them under Israel’s hand, and, striking them, they pursued as far as great Sidon and as far as Maserōn and as far as the plains of Massoch toward the east, and cut them down until none remained saved.
Joshua 11:9 And Jesus did to them as the Lord commanded him; he cut the tendons of their horses and burned their chariots with fire.
Joshua 11:10 And Jesus turned back at that time and seized Asor and its king; Asor had formerly ruled all these kingdoms.
Joshua 11:11 And they killed every breathing thing in it with the sword and destroyed all, and no breathing thing remained in it; and they burned Asor with fire.
Joshua 11:12 And Jesus took all the cities of the kings and their kings and killed them with the edge of the sword, and they destroyed them, as Moses the servant of the Lord instructed.
Joshua 11:13 But Israel did not burn all the cities built upon mounds; Jesus burned Asor alone.
Joshua 11:14 And the sons of Israel took all its spoils for themselves, but destroyed all of them with the edge of the sword until he had destroyed them; they left not one breathing thing among them.
Joshua 11:15 As the Lord instructed Moses his servant, so Moses commanded Jesus, and thus Jesus did; he transgressed nothing of all that Moses instructed him.
Joshua 11:16 And Jesus took all the hill country and all the Nageb and all the land of Gosom and the plain and the western region and the mountain of Israel and the lowlands,
Joshua 11:17 the regions by the mountain from Mount Achel and what rises toward Seir and as far as Baalgad and the plains of Lebanon below Mount Aermon; and he took all their kings and killed them and put them to death.
Joshua 11:18 And Jesus waged war against these kings for many days,
Joshua 11:19 and there was no city that Israel did not take; they took all in war.
Joshua 11:20 For it came about through the Lord that their heart was made strong to meet Israel in war, so that they would be destroyed, so that mercy would not be given them, but that they would be destroyed, as the Lord said to Moses.
Joshua 11:21 And Jesus came at that time and destroyed the Enakim from the hill country, from Chebron and Dabir and Anaboth and from all the race of Israel and from all the mountain of Judas with their cities; and Jesus destroyed them.
Joshua 11:22 None of the Enakim remained from the sons of Israel, except that some remained in Gaza and Geth and Asedoth.
Joshua 11:23 And Jesus took all the land as the Lord commanded Moses, and Jesus gave them as an inheritance to Israel in divisions according to their tribes. And the land rested from being at war.

## Chapter 12

Joshua 12:1 And these are the kings of the land whom the sons of Israel killed and whose land they inherited beyond the Jordan toward the rising of the sun, from the ravine of Arnon as far as Mount Aermon and all the land of Araba to the east:
Joshua 12:2 Seon king of the Amorites, who dwelt in Esebon and ruled from Aroer, which is in the ravine, along part of the ravine and half of Galaad as far as Jabok, the boundary of the sons of Ammon,
Joshua 12:3 and Araba as far as the Sea of Chenereth to the east and as far as the Sea of Araba, the Sea of Salt, from the east, the road by Asimoth, from Thaiman below Asedoth Phasga;
Joshua 12:4 and Og king of Basan, who was left of the giants, dwelling in Astaroth and Edraim,
Joshua 12:5 ruling from Mount Aermon and from Selcha and all Basan as far as the boundaries of Gesuri and Machati and half of Galaad, the boundary of Seon king of Esebon.
Joshua 12:6 Moses the servant of the Lord and the sons of Israel struck them, and Moses gave it as an inheritance to Reuben and Gad and the half tribe of Manasse.
Joshua 12:7 And these are the kings of the Amorites whom Jesus and the sons of Israel killed beyond the Jordan by the sea, Baalgad in the plain of Lebanon and as far as Mount Chelcha on the ascent to Seir, and Jesus gave it to the tribes of Israel to inherit according to their allotment,
Joshua 12:8 in the mountain and in the plain and in Araba and in Asedoth and in the wilderness and in Nageb: the Chettite and the Amorite and the Canaanite and the Pherezite and the Euaite and the Jebusite;
Joshua 12:9 the king of Jericho and the king of Gai, which is near Baethel,
Joshua 12:10 king of Jerusalem, king of Chebron,
Joshua 12:11 king of Jerimuth, king of Lachis,
Joshua 12:12 king of Ailam, king of Gazer,
Joshua 12:13 king of Dabir, king of Gader,
Joshua 12:14 king of Ermath, king of Arath,
Joshua 12:15 king of Lebna, king of Odollam,
Joshua 12:16 king of Makeda,
Joshua 12:17 king of Taphoug, king of Opher,
Joshua 12:18 king of Aphek of Saron,
Joshua 12:19 king of Asor,
Joshua 12:20 king of Symoon, king of Marron, king of Aziph,
Joshua 12:21 king of Kades, king of Tanach,
Joshua 12:22 king of Magedon, king of Jekonam of Chermel,
Joshua 12:23 king of Dor of Napheddor, king of Goim of Galilee,
Joshua 12:24 king of Tharsa; all these were twenty-nine kings.

## Chapter 13

Joshua 13:1 And Jesus was old, advanced in days. And the Lord said to Jesus, “You are advanced in days, and much land remains for an inheritance.
Joshua 13:2 And this is the land left: the territories of the Philistines, the Gesirite and the Canaanite;
Joshua 13:3 from the uninhabited region opposite Egypt to the boundaries of Akkaron, from the left of the Canaanites, it is reckoned to the five satrapies of the Philistines, to the Gazaite and the Azotite and the Ascalonite and the Getthite and the Akkaronite; and to the Euaite
Joshua 13:4 from Thaiman and all the land of Canaan opposite Gaza, and the Sidonians as far as Aphek, as far as the boundaries of the Amorites,
Joshua 13:5 and all the land of the Gabli Philistines and all Lebanon toward the sunrise from Galgal below Mount Aermon as far as the entrance of Emath;
Joshua 13:6 every inhabitant of the hill country from Lebanon as far as Maserephothmaim, all the Sidonians, I shall destroy them from before Israel; but distribute it as an inheritance to Israel, as I commanded you.
Joshua 13:7 And now divide this land as an inheritance to the nine tribes and the half tribe of Manasse; from the Jordan to the Great Sea toward the setting of the sun you shall give it; the Great Sea shall bound it.
Joshua 13:8 But to the two tribes and the half tribe of Manasse, to Reuben and Gad, Moses gave beyond the Jordan toward the sunrise; Moses the servant of the Lord gave it
Joshua 13:9 from Aroer, which is on the edge of the torrent Arnon, and the city in the middle of the ravine and all Misor from Maidaba to Daiban,
Joshua 13:10 all the cities of Seon king of the Amorites, who reigned in Esebon, as far as the boundaries of the sons of Ammon
Joshua 13:11 and the Galaadite region and the boundaries of Gesiri and Machati, all Mount Aermon and all the Basanite region as far as Selcha,
Joshua 13:12 all the kingdom of Og in the Basanite region, who reigned in Astaroth and Edraim; he was left of the giants, and Moses struck him and destroyed him.
Joshua 13:13 And the sons of Israel did not destroy the Gesirite and the Machatite and the Canaanite, and the king of Gesiri and the Machatite dwelt among the sons of Israel until this day.
Joshua 13:14 Except to the tribe of Levi no inheritance was given; the Lord, the God of Israel, he is their inheritance, as the Lord said to them. And this is the division that Moses divided to the sons of Israel in Araboth Moab beyond the Jordan opposite Jericho.
Joshua 13:15 And Moses gave to the tribe of Reuben according to their clans.
Joshua 13:16 And their boundaries were from Aroer, which is opposite the ravine of Arnon, and the city in the ravine of Arnon and all Misor
Joshua 13:17 as far as Esebon and all the cities in Misor, and Daibon and Bamothbaal and the house of Beelmon
Joshua 13:18 and Jassa and Kedemoth and Mephaath
Joshua 13:19 and Kariathaim and Sebama and Serada and Sior on Mount Emak
Joshua 13:20 and Baethphogor and Asedoth Phasga and Baethasimoth
Joshua 13:21 and all the cities of Misor and all the kingdom of Seon king of the Amorites, whom Moses struck, him and the leaders of Madian and Eui and Rokom and Sour and Our and Robe, rulers beside Seon and the inhabitants of the land.
Joshua 13:22 And Balaam son of Beor, the seer, they killed in the turn.
Joshua 13:23 And the boundary of Reuben was the Jordan as boundary. This is the inheritance of the sons of Reuben according to their clans, their cities and their settlements.
Joshua 13:24 And Moses gave to the sons of Gad according to their clans.
Joshua 13:25 And their boundaries were Jazer, all the cities of Galaad and half the land of the sons of Ammon as far as Aroer, which is opposite Rabba,
Joshua 13:26 and from Esebon as far as Ramoth by Massepha and Botanin and Maanain as far as the boundaries of Dabir
Joshua 13:27 and in Emek, Baetharam and Baethanabra and Sokchotha and Saphan and the rest of the kingdom of Seon king of Esebon, and the Jordan shall bound it as far as the region of the Sea of Chenereth beyond the Jordan to the east.
Joshua 13:28 This is the inheritance of the sons of Gad according to their clans, their cities and their settlements.
Joshua 13:29 And Moses gave to the half tribe of Manasse according to their clans.
Joshua 13:30 And their boundaries were from Maanain and all the kingdom of Basani and all the kingdom of Og king of Basan and all the villages of Jair that are in the Basanite region, sixty cities,
Joshua 13:31 and half of Galaad and in Astaroth and Edraim, cities of Og’s kingdom in the Basanite region; and they were given to the sons of Machir son of Manasse and to the half of the sons of Machir son of Manasse according to their clans.
Joshua 13:32 These are those whom Moses made inherit beyond the Jordan in Araboth Moab beyond the Jordan opposite Jericho to the east.

## Chapter 14

Joshua 14:1 And these are those of the sons of Israel who inherited in the land of Canaan, to whom Eleazar the priest and Jesus son of Naue and the leaders of the families of the tribes of the sons of Israel allotted it.
Joshua 14:2 By lots they inherited, as the Lord commanded by the hand of Jesus for the nine tribes and the half tribe,
Joshua 14:3 from beyond the Jordan, and to the Levites he did not give an allotment among them;
Joshua 14:4 because the sons of Joseph were two tribes, Manasse and Ephraim, and no portion in the land was given to the Levites except cities to dwell in and their set-apart areas for the animals and their animals.
Joshua 14:5 As the Lord commanded Moses, so the sons of Israel did and divided the land.
Joshua 14:6 And the sons of Judas came to Jesus in Galgal, and Chaleb son of Jephonne the Kenezite said to him, “You know the word that the Lord spoke to Moses, the man of God, concerning me and you in Kades Barne;
Joshua 14:7 for I was forty years old when Moses the servant of God sent me from Kades Barne to spy out the land, and I answered him a word according to his mind,
Joshua 14:8 but my brothers who went up with me shifted the people’s heart, whereas I attached myself to follow the Lord my God,
Joshua 14:9 and Moses swore on that day, saying, ‘The land upon which you set foot shall be yours as an inheritance and your children’s forever, because you attached yourself to follow after the Lord our God.’
Joshua 14:10 And now the Lord has sustained me, as he said, this forty-fifth year since the Lord spoke this word to Moses and Israel walked in the wilderness. And now behold, I am eighty-five years old today;
Joshua 14:11 I am still strong today as when Moses sent me; likewise I am strong now to go out and enter into war.
Joshua 14:12 And now I ask you for this mountain, as the Lord said on that day; for you heard this word on that day. But now the Enakim are there, fortified and great cities; if then the Lord is with me, I shall destroy them, as the Lord said to me.”
Joshua 14:13 And Jesus blessed him and gave Chebron to Chaleb son of Jephonne son of Kenez as an inheritance.
Joshua 14:14 For this reason Chebron became the inheritance of Chaleb son of Jephonne the Kenezite until this day because he followed the command of the Lord, the God of Israel.
Joshua 14:15 And the name of Chebron formerly was City of Arbok; this was a chief city of the Enakim. And the land ceased from war.

## Chapter 15

Joshua 15:1 And the boundaries of the tribe of Judas according to their clans were from the boundaries of Idumaea, from the wilderness of Sin as far as Kades toward the south.
Joshua 15:2 And their boundaries were from the south as far as the region of the Salt Sea, from the ridge that runs toward the south,
Joshua 15:3 and it goes across opposite the ascent of Akrabin and circles Senna and ascends from the south to Kades Barne and goes out to Asoron and ascends to Addara and goes around the western side of Kades
Joshua 15:4 and goes to Asemona and passes as far as the ravine of Egypt, and its boundary shall have its outlet at the sea; these are their boundaries from the south.
Joshua 15:5 And the boundaries from the east: the whole Salt Sea as far as the Jordan. And their boundaries from the north, from the ridge of the sea and from the region of the Jordan:
Joshua 15:6 the boundary goes up to Baethagla and passes on the north to Baetharaba, and the boundary ascends to the stone of Baion son of Reuben,
Joshua 15:7 and the boundary ascends to the fourth part of the ravine of Achor and descends to Galgal, which is opposite the approach of Addamin, which is to the south of the ravine, and passes to the water of the Spring of the Sun, and its outlet shall be the spring Rogel,
Joshua 15:8 and the boundary ascends to the ravine of Onom on the back of Jebus from the south [this is Jerusalem], and the boundary passes to the summit of the mountain that is opposite the ravine of Onom toward the sea, which is from the region of the land of Raphain to the north,
Joshua 15:9 and the boundary passes from the summit of the mountain to the spring of the water of Naphtho and passes to Mount Ephron, and the boundary leads out to Baal [this is the city of Iarim],
Joshua 15:10 and the boundary shall go around from Baal toward the sea and pass to Mount Assares on the back, the city of Iarim on the north [this is Chaslon], and shall descend to the City of the Sun and pass to the south,
Joshua 15:11 and the boundary shall pass by the back of Akkaron to the north, and the boundaries shall pass to Sakcharona and pass Mount Bala and pass to Jabnel, and the outlet of the boundaries shall be at the sea.
Joshua 15:12 And their boundaries from the west: the Great Sea shall bound them. These are the boundaries of the sons of Judas all around according to their clans. –
Joshua 15:13 And to Chaleb son of Jephonne he gave a portion among the sons of Judas by God’s command, and Jesus gave him the city of Arbok, chief city of Enak [this is Chebron].
Joshua 15:14 And Chaleb son of Jephonne destroyed from there the three sons of Enak, Sousi and Tholmi and Achima.
Joshua 15:15 And Chaleb went up from there against the inhabitants of Dabir; the name of Dabir had formerly been City of Letters.
Joshua 15:16 And Chaleb said, “Whoever takes and cuts down the City of Letters and rules it, to him I shall give my daughter Achsa as a wife.”
Joshua 15:17 And Gothoniel son of Kenez, the younger brother of Chaleb, took it, and he gave him his daughter Achsa as a wife.
Joshua 15:18 And it happened as she was entering that she advised him, saying, “I shall ask my father for a field”; and she cried out from the donkey. And Chaleb said to her, “What is it with you?”
Joshua 15:19 And she said to him, “Give me a blessing, because you gave me into the land of Nageb; give me Golathmain.” And Chaleb gave her Upper Golathmain and Lower Golathmain. –
Joshua 15:20 This is the inheritance of the tribe of the sons of Judas.
Joshua 15:21 And their cities were: the first city of the tribe of the sons of Judas at the boundaries of Edom in the wilderness, Kaibaiseleel and Ara and Asor
Joshua 15:22 and Ikam and Regma and Arouel
Joshua 15:23 and Kades and Asorionain
Joshua 15:24 and Mainam and Balmainan and their villages
Joshua 15:25 and the cities Aseron [this is Asor]
Joshua 15:26 and Sen and Salmaa and Molada
Joshua 15:27 and Seri and Baiphalad
Joshua 15:28 and Cholaseola and Bersabee and their villages and their settlements,
Joshua 15:29 Bala and Bakok and Asom
Joshua 15:30 and Elbouda and Baethel and Erma
Joshua 15:31 and Sekelak and Macharim and Sethennak
Joshua 15:32 and Labos and Sale and Eromoth, twenty-nine cities and their villages.
Joshua 15:33 In the plain: Astaol and Raa and Assa
Joshua 15:34 and Ramen and Tano and Ilouthoth and Maiani
Joshua 15:35 and Jermouth and Odollam and Membra and Saōcho and Azeka
Joshua 15:36 and Sakarim and Gadera and its settlements, fourteen cities and their villages;
Joshua 15:37 Senna and Adasan and Magadagad
Joshua 15:38 and Dalal and Maspha and Jakareel
Joshua 15:39 and Lachēs and Basedoth and Ideadalea
Joshua 15:40 and Chabra and Maches and Maachos
Joshua 15:41 and Geddor and Bagadiel and Noman and Makedan, sixteen cities and their villages;
Joshua 15:42 Lemna and Ithak
Joshua 15:43 and Anoch and Jana and Nasib
Joshua 15:44 and Keilam and Akiezi and Kezib and Bathesar and Ailon, ten cities and their villages;
Joshua 15:45 Akkaron and its villages and their settlements;
Joshua 15:46 from Akkaron, Gemna and all those near Asedoth and their villages;
Joshua 15:47 Asiedoth and its villages and its settlements; Gaza and its villages and its settlements as far as the torrent of Egypt; and the Great Sea bounds them.
Joshua 15:48 And in the hill country: Samir and Jether and Socha
Joshua 15:49 and Renna and City of Letters [this is Dabir]
Joshua 15:50 and Anon and Eskaiman and Aisam
Joshua 15:51 and Gosom and Chalou and Channa, eleven cities and their villages;
Joshua 15:52 Airem and Remna and Soma
Joshua 15:53 and Jemain and Baethachou and Phakoua
Joshua 15:54 and Euma and City of Arbok [this is Chebron] and Sorth, nine cities and their settlements;
Joshua 15:55 Maor and Chermel and Ozib and Itan
Joshua 15:56 and Jariel and Jarikam and Zakanaiim
Joshua 15:57 and Gabaa and Thamnatha, nine cities and their villages;
Joshua 15:58 Aloua and Baethsour and Geddon
Joshua 15:59 and Magaroth and Baethanam and Thekoum, six cities and their villages;
Joshua 15:59 a Theko and Ephratha [this is Baethleem] and Phagor and Aitan and Koulon and Tatam and Eobes and Karem and Galem and Thether and Manocho, eleven cities and their villages;
Joshua 15:60 Kariathbaal [this is the city of Iarim] and Sōtheba, two cities and their settlements;
Joshua 15:61 and Baddargis and Tharabaam and Ainon and Aichioza
Joshua 15:62 and Naphlazon and the cities Sadom and Ankades, seven cities and their villages.
Joshua 15:63 And the Jebusite dwelt in Jerusalem, and the sons of Judas were not able to destroy them; and the Jebusites dwelt in Jerusalem until that day.

## Chapter 16

Joshua 16:1 And the boundaries of the sons of Joseph were from the Jordan by Jericho on the east, and it shall ascend from Jericho into the hill country, the wilderness, to Baethel Louza
Joshua 16:2 and shall go out to Baethel and pass to the boundaries of Chatarothi
Joshua 16:3 and shall pass toward the sea to the boundaries of Aptalim as far as the boundaries of Lower Baethoron, and their outlet shall be at the sea.
Joshua 16:4 And the sons of Joseph, Ephraim and Manasse, inherited;
Joshua 16:5 and the boundaries of the sons of Ephraim according to their clans were these: the boundaries of their inheritance from the east were Ataroth and Erok as far as Upper Baethoron and Gazara,
Joshua 16:6 and the boundaries shall pass toward the sea to Ikasmon from north Therma, shall go around toward the east to Thenasa and Sellēsa and pass from the east to Janoka
Joshua 16:7 and to Macho and Ataroth and their villages and come to Jericho and pass out to the Jordan,
Joshua 16:8 and from Taphou the boundaries shall go toward the sea to Chelkana, and their outlet shall be at the sea; this is the inheritance of the tribe of Ephraim according to their clans.
Joshua 16:9 And the cities set apart for the sons of Ephraim in the midst of the inheritance of the sons of Manasse, all the cities and their villages. –
Joshua 16:10 And Ephraim did not destroy the Canaanite dwelling in Gazer, and the Canaanite dwelt in Ephraim until this day, until Pharaoh king of Egypt went up and took it and burned it with fire, and they pierced through the Canaanites and the Pherezites and those dwelling in Gazer, and Pharaoh gave it as a dowry to his daughter.

## Chapter 17

Joshua 17:1 And the boundaries of the tribe of the sons of Manasse were, because he was Joseph’s firstborn, for Machir, Manasse’s firstborn, father of Galaad [for he was a fighting man], in the Galaadite and Basanite regions.
Joshua 17:2 And it was for the remaining sons of Manasse according to their clans, for the sons of Jezer and the sons of Kelez and the sons of Jeziel and the sons of Sychem and the sons of Symarim and the sons of Opher; these were the males according to their clans.
Joshua 17:3 And Salpaad son of Opher had no sons but only daughters, and these are the names of Salpaad’s daughters: Maala and Noua and Egla and Melcha and Thersa.
Joshua 17:4 And they stood before Eleazar the priest and before Jesus and before the rulers, saying, “God commanded through the hand of Moses to give us an inheritance among our brothers.” And an allotment was given them by the Lord’s command among their father’s brothers.
Joshua 17:5 And their measured allotment fell from Anassa and the plain of Labek from Galaad, which is beyond the Jordan;
Joshua 17:6 for the daughters of the sons of Manasse inherited an allotment among their brothers; but the land of Galaad became the portion of the sons of Manasse who remained.
Joshua 17:7 And the boundaries of the sons of Manasse were Delanath, which is opposite the sons of Anath, and it goes along the boundaries to Jamin and Jassib to the spring Thaphthoth;
Joshua 17:8 it shall be for Manasse, and Thapheth on the boundaries of Manasse for the sons of Ephraim.
Joshua 17:9 And the boundaries shall descend to the ravine of Karana on the south along the ravine of Jariel, a terebinth for Ephraim in the midst of a city of Manasse; and the boundaries of Manasse to the north to the torrent, and its outlet shall be the sea.
Joshua 17:10 From the south for Ephraim, and on the north Manasse, and the sea shall be their boundary; and they shall adjoin Aser on the north and Issachar on the east.
Joshua 17:11 And for Manasse in Issachar and Aser shall be Baethsan and its villages and the inhabitants of Dor and its villages and the inhabitants of Mageddo and its villages and a third of Napheta and its villages.
Joshua 17:12 And the sons of Manasse were not able to destroy these cities, and the Canaanite began to dwell in that land;
Joshua 17:13 and it happened that when the sons of Israel grew strong, they made the Canaanites subject, but they did not destroy them utterly.
Joshua 17:14 And the sons of Joseph answered Jesus, saying, “Why have you given us one lot and one measured portion as an inheritance? Yet I am a numerous people, and God has blessed me.”
Joshua 17:15 And Jesus said to them, “If you are a numerous people, go up into the wooded land and clear it for yourself, if Mount Ephraim confines you.”
Joshua 17:16 And they said, “Mount Ephraim will not suffice for us, and the Canaanite who dwells there in Baethsan and its villages in the valley of Jezrael has a chosen horse and iron.”
Joshua 17:17 And Jesus said to the sons of Joseph, “If you are a numerous people and have great strength, you shall not have one lot;
Joshua 17:18 for the wooded land shall be yours, because it is wooded land and you shall clear it and it shall be yours; and when you destroy the Canaanite, for he has a chosen horse, you are stronger than he.”

## Chapter 18

Joshua 18:1 And all the assembly of the sons of Israel was called together at Selo, and they pitched the tent of testimony there, and the land was held by them.
Joshua 18:2 And seven tribes of the sons of Israel remained that had not inherited.
Joshua 18:3 And Jesus said to the sons of Israel, “How long will you grow slack about inheriting the land that the Lord our God gave?
Joshua 18:4 Give three men from each tribe from among you, and let them arise and go through the land and draw it out before me as it must be divided. [And they came to him,
Joshua 18:5 and he divided it for them into seven portions.] Judas shall be their boundary on the south, and the sons of Joseph shall be theirs on the north.
Joshua 18:6 But you divide the land into seven portions and bring them to me here, and I shall bring out a lot for you before the Lord our God.
Joshua 18:7 For the sons of Levi have no portion among you, for the Lord’s priesthood is his portion; and Gad and Reuben and the half tribe of Manasse received their inheritance beyond the Jordan on the east that Moses the servant of the Lord gave them.”
Joshua 18:8 And the men arose and went, and Jesus commanded the men going to traverse the land, saying, “Go and traverse the land and come to me, and here I shall bring out a lot for you before the Lord in Selo.”
Joshua 18:9 And they went and traversed the land and saw it and wrote it by its cities in seven portions in a book and brought it to Jesus.
Joshua 18:10 And Jesus cast a lot for them in Selo before the Lord.
