1 Judges 9:15 And the bramble said to the trees: If in truth you anoint me king over you, come, trust in my shade; and if not, may fire go out from the bramble and devour the cedars of Lebanon. –
1 Judges 9:16 And now, if in truth and in completeness you acted and made Abimelech king, and if you did well with Ierobaal and with his house, and if you acted toward him according to the recompense of his hand,
1 Judges 9:17 – as my father fought on your behalf and cast his soul opposite and rescued you from the hand of Madiam,
1 Judges 9:18 and you rose up against my father's house today and killed his sons, seventy men upon one stone, and made Abimelech the son of his maidservant king over the men of Sikimois because he is your brother, –
1 Judges 9:19 and if in truth and completeness you acted with Ierobaal and his house on this day, may you be blessed and rejoice in Abimelech, and may he also rejoice in you.
1 Judges 9:20 And if not, may fire go out from Abimelech and devour the men of Sikimois and the house of Maallon; and if not, may fire go out from the men of Sikimois and from the house of Maallon and devour Abimelech. –
1 Judges 9:21 And Ioatham ran away and went on the road and fled to Rara and dwelt there because of Abimelech his brother.
1 Judges 9:22 And Abimelech ruled over Israel three years.
1 Judges 9:23 And God sent an evil spirit between Abimelech and the men of Sikimois, and the men of Sikimois acted treacherously in the house of Abimelech,
1 Judges 9:24 to bring the injustice against the seventy sons of Ierobaal and to place their blood upon Abimelech their brother who killed them and upon the men of Sikimois who strengthened his hands to kill his brothers.
1 Judges 9:25 And the men of Sikimois placed an ambush for him on the tops of the mountains and seized all who passed by them on the road; and it was reported to Abimelech.
1 Judges 9:26 And Gaal son of Abed and his brothers came to Sikima, and the men of Sikimois trusted in him.
1 Judges 9:27 And they went into the field and harvested their vineyards and trod them and made dances and entered the house of their god and ate and drank and cursed Abimelech.
1 Judges 9:28 And Gaal son of Abed said: What is Abimelech, and who is the son of Sychem, that we should serve him? Is this one not a son of Ierobaal, and Zeboul his overseer his servant with the men of Emmor father of Sychem? And why should we serve him?
1 Judges 9:29 And who would give this people into my hand? And I would remove Abimelech and say to Abimelech: Multiply your force and come out.
1 Judges 9:30 And Zeboul the ruler of the city heard the words of Gaal son of Abed and was angry with wrath.
1 Judges 9:31 And he sent messengers to Abimelech with gifts, saying: Behold, Gaal son of Abed and his brothers have come to Sikima, and these are besieging the city against you;
1 Judges 9:32 and now arise by night, you and the people with you, and lie in ambush in the field,
1 Judges 9:33 and it will be in the morning, as the sun rises, that you will rise early and stretch out against the city, and behold, he and the people with him will come out toward you, and you shall do to him as your hand finds.
1 Judges 9:34 And Abimelech and all the people with him arose by night and lay in ambush against Sikima in four groups.
1 Judges 9:35 And morning came, and Gaal son of Abed went out and stood by the door of the gate of the city, and Abimelech and the people with him arose from the ambushes.
1 Judges 9:36 And Gaal son of Abed saw the people and said to Zeboul: Behold, people coming down from the tops of the mountains. And Zeboul said to him: You see the shadow of the mountains as men.
1 Judges 9:37 And Gaal continued to speak and said: Behold, people coming down toward the sea from beside the navel of the land, and one group is arriving from the way of the oak of those looking out.
1 Judges 9:38 And Zeboul said to him: Where now is your mouth that said, Who is Abimelech, that we should serve him? Are these not the people whom you despised? Go out now and fight against him.
1 Judges 9:39 And Gaal went out before the men of Sikimois and fought against Abimelech.
1 Judges 9:40 And Abimelech pursued him, and he fled from before him; and many wounded fell as far as the doors of the city.
1 Judges 9:41 And Abimelech sat in Arima; and Zeboul drove out Gaal and his brothers so that they would not dwell in Sikimois.
1 Judges 9:42 And it happened the next day that the people went out into the plain, and it was reported to Abimelech.
1 Judges 9:43 And he took the people and divided them into three groups and lay in ambush in it; and he saw, and behold, people came out of the city, and he rose against them and struck them.
1 Judges 9:44 And Abimelech and the groups with him spread out and stood by the gate of the city, and the two groups poured out upon all those in the field, and he struck them.
1 Judges 9:45 And Abimelech fought in the city all that day, and they took the city, and he killed the people in it and pulled down the city and sowed it with salt.
1 Judges 9:46 And all the men of the tower of Sikimois heard and entered the stronghold of the house of Baal of the Covenant.
1 Judges 9:47 And it was reported to Abimelech that all the men of the tower of Sikimois had gathered.
1 Judges 9:48 And Abimelech went up to Mount Selmon, he and all the people with him, and Abimelech took an ax in his hand and cut a load of wood and took it and put it on his shoulders and said to the people with him: What you have seen me doing, quickly do as I also do.
1 Judges 9:49 And they too each cut a load and lifted it and went after Abimelech and put it against the stronghold and burned the stronghold over them with fire, and all the men of the tower of Sikimois died, about a thousand men and women.
1 Judges 9:50 And Abimelech went to Thebes and encamped around it and took it first.
1 Judges 9:51 And there was a strong tower in the middle of the city, and all the men and women and all the leaders of the city fled there and shut themselves in and went up onto the roof of the tower.
1 Judges 9:52 And Abimelech came as far as the tower, and they fought against him; and Abimelech drew near to the door of the tower to burn it with fire.
1 Judges 9:53 And one woman threw a fragment of a millstone upon Abimelech's head and crushed his skull.
1 Judges 9:54 And he cried out quickly to the young man carrying his equipment and said to him: Draw your knife and put me to death, lest they say, A woman killed him. And his young man pierced him through, and Abimelech died.
1 Judges 9:55 And a man of Israel saw that Abimelech had died, and each man went to his place.
1 Judges 9:56 And God turned back upon Abimelech the evil which he did to his father by killing his seventy brothers.
1 Judges 9:57 And all the evil of the men of Sikimois God turned back upon their head, and the curse of Ioatham son of Ierobaal came upon them.

## Chapter 10

1 Judges 10:1 And after Abimelech, Thola son of Phoua, son of his father's brother, a man of Issachar, arose to save Israel, and he dwelt in Samaria in Mount Ephraim.
1 Judges 10:2 And he judged Israel twenty-three years and died and was buried in Samaria.
1 Judges 10:3 And after him Iair the Galaadite arose and judged Israel twenty-two years.
1 Judges 10:4 And he had thirty-two sons mounted on thirty-two colts; and they had thirty-two cities, and he called them the Settlements of Iair until this day, which are in the land of Galaad.
1 Judges 10:5 And Iair died and was buried in Rammo.
1 Judges 10:6 And the sons of Israel again did evil before the Lord and served the Baalim and the Astaroth and the gods of Sidon and the gods of Moab and the gods of the sons of Ammon and the gods of the foreigners and abandoned the Lord and did not serve him.
1 Judges 10:7 And the Lord became angry in wrath with Israel and sold them into the hand of foreigners and into the hand of the sons of Ammon.
1 Judges 10:8 And they broke down and crushed the sons of Israel in that year, eighteen years, all the sons of Israel beyond the Jordan in the land of the Amorite in Galaaditis.
1 Judges 10:9 And the sons of Ammon crossed the Jordan to wage war also in Judah and Benjamin and in the house of Ephraim, and the sons of Israel were pressed very hard.
1 Judges 10:10 And the sons of Israel cried out to the Lord, saying: We have sinned against you, because we abandoned our God and served the Baalim.
1 Judges 10:11 And the Lord said to the sons of Israel: Did not the Egyptians and the Amorites and the sons of Ammon and Moab and the foreigners
1 Judges 10:12 and Sidonians and Madiam and Amalek press you? And you cried out to me, and I saved you from their hand.
1 Judges 10:13 And you abandoned me and served other gods; therefore I will no longer continue to save you.
1 Judges 10:14 Go and cry out to the gods whom you chose for yourselves, and let them save you in the time of your affliction.
1 Judges 10:15 And the sons of Israel said to the Lord: We have sinned; do to us according to all that is pleasing before you, only, Lord, rescue us on this day.
1 Judges 10:16 And they removed the foreign gods from among them and served the Lord; and he was not well pleased among the people, and he grew fainthearted in the toil of Israel.
1 Judges 10:17 And the sons of Ammon went up and encamped in Galaad, and the sons of Israel went out and encamped in Massepha.
1 Judges 10:18 And the rulers of the people of Galaad said, each man to his neighbor: Who is the man who will begin to fight against the sons of Ammon? He shall be head of all those dwelling in Galaad.

## Chapter 11

1 Judges 11:1 And Iephthae the Galaadite was mighty in strength; and he was the son of a prostitute, and she bore Iephthae to Galaad.
1 Judges 11:2 And the wife of Galaad bore him sons; and the sons of the wife grew strong and drove out Iephthae and said to him: You shall not inherit in our father's house, because you are the son of a courtesan.
1 Judges 11:3 And Iephthae fled from before his brothers and dwelt in the land of Tob, and plain men gathered to Iephthae and went out with him.
1 Judges 11:4 And it happened after days that the sons of Ammon fought with Israel.
1 Judges 11:5 And it happened when the sons of Ammon fought with Israel that the elders of Galaad went to take Iephthae from the land of Tob
1 Judges 11:6 and said to Iephthae: Come and be our leader, and let us fight against the sons of Ammon.
1 Judges 11:7 And Iephthae said to the elders of Galaad: Did you not hate me and drive me out of my father's house and send me away from you? And why have you come to me when you are afflicted?
1 Judges 11:8 And the elders of Galaad said to Iephthae: Not so; now we have come to you, and you will go with us, and we will fight against the sons of Ammon; and you will be head for us, for all those dwelling in Galaad.
1 Judges 11:9 And Iephthae said to the elders of Galaad: If you bring me back to fight against the sons of Ammon and the Lord delivers them before me, I will be your head.
1 Judges 11:10 And the elders of Galaad said to Iephthae: The Lord will be the one who hears between us if we do not act thus according to your word.
1 Judges 11:11 And Iephthae went with the elders of Galaad, and they appointed him over them as head and leader. And Iephthae spoke all his words before the Lord in Massepha.
1 Judges 11:12 And Iephthae sent messengers to the king of the sons of Ammon, saying: What is there between me and you, that you have come to me to fight me in my land?
1 Judges 11:13 And the king of the sons of Ammon said to the messengers of Iephthae: Because Israel took my land when he came up from Egypt, from Arnon as far as Iabok and as far as the Jordan; and now return those lands in peace.
1 Judges 11:14 And the messengers returned to Iephthae. And Iephthae sent messengers to the king of the sons of Ammon
1 Judges 11:15 saying: Thus says Iephthae: Israel did not take the land of Moab or the land of the sons of Ammon
1 Judges 11:16 when they came up from Egypt, but Israel went in the wilderness as far as the Red Sea and came as far as Kades.
1 Judges 11:17 And Israel sent messengers to the king of Edom, saying: I will pass through your land; and the king of Edom did not listen. And he also sent to the king of Moab, and he was unwilling. And Israel sat in Kades.
1 Judges 11:18 And he passed through the wilderness and went around the land of Edom and the land of Moab and came to the east of the land of Moab and encamped beyond Arnon and did not enter the boundary of Moab, because Arnon was the boundary of Moab.
1 Judges 11:19 And Israel sent messengers to Seon king of Esebon, the Amorite, and Israel said to him: I will pass through your land as far as my place.
1 Judges 11:20 And Seon was unwilling to let Israel pass through his boundaries; and Seon gathered all his people and encamped at Iassa and fought with Israel.
1 Judges 11:21 And the Lord the God of Israel delivered Seon and all his people into the hand of Israel, and he struck them; and Israel inherited all the land of the Amorite dwelling in the land.
1 Judges 11:22 And he inherited all the boundary of the Amorite from Arnon as far as Iabok and from the wilderness as far as the Jordan.
1 Judges 11:23 And now the Lord the God of Israel removed the Amorite from before his people Israel, and will you inherit him for yourself?
1 Judges 11:24 Will you not inherit whatever Chamos your god allotted you to inherit? And everything that the Lord our God allotted us to inherit from before us, we will inherit.
1 Judges 11:25 And now are you any better than Balak son of Sepphor, king of Moab? Did he contend in a contest with Israel or fight them in war?
1 Judges 11:26 While the house of Israel was in Esebon and its daughter towns and in Iazer and its daughter towns and in all the cities beside the Jordan for three hundred years, why did they not rescue them in that time?
1 Judges 11:27 And I have not sinned against you, but you are doing evil with me by fighting against me; may the Lord, the one who judges, judge today between the sons of Israel and the sons of Ammon.
1 Judges 11:28 And the king of the sons of Ammon did not listen and did not listen to the words of Iephthae which he sent to him.
1 Judges 11:29 And the spirit of the Lord came upon Iephthae, and he passed through the land of Galaad and Manasse and passed through the lookout of Galaad and from the lookout of Galaad to the other side of the sons of Ammon.
1 Judges 11:30 And Iephthae vowed a vow to the Lord and said: If you indeed deliver the sons of Ammon into my hand,
1 Judges 11:31 then whoever comes out from the doors of my house to meet me when I return in peace from the sons of Ammon shall be for the Lord, and I will offer him up as a whole burnt offering.
1 Judges 11:32 And Iephthae crossed over to the sons of Ammon to fight against them, and the Lord delivered them into his hand.
1 Judges 11:33 And he struck them from Aroer as far as coming to Semoith, twenty cities as far as Abel of the vineyards, a very great blow, and the sons of Ammon were put to shame before the sons of Israel.
1 Judges 11:34 And Iephthae came to Massepha to his house, and behold, his daughter came out to meet him with drums and dances; and she was his only beloved child, and he had no son or daughter besides her.
1 Judges 11:35 And it happened when he saw her that he tore his garments and said: Woe is me, my daughter, you have impeded me, you became a thorn in my eyes, and I opened my mouth concerning you to the Lord and will not be able to turn back.
1 Judges 11:36 And she said to him: My father, if you opened your mouth to the Lord concerning me, do to me in the manner that came out of your mouth, since the Lord has made vengeance for you upon your enemies, the sons of Ammon.
1 Judges 11:37 And she said to her father: And do this thing for me: Let me be for two months, and I will go and descend upon the mountains and weep over my virginity, I and my companions.
1 Judges 11:38 And he said: Go; and he sent her away for two months. And she went, she and her companions, and wept over her virginity on the mountains.
1 Judges 11:39 And it happened after the end of two months that she returned to her father, and Iephthae fulfilled his vow which he had vowed; and she had not known a man. And it became an ordinance in Israel;
1 Judges 11:40 from days to days the daughters of Israel went together to lament the daughter of Iephthae the Galaadite four days in the year.

## Chapter 12

1 Judges 12:1 And the sons of Ephraim gathered and came to Sephina and said to Iephthae: Why did you go to fight against the sons of Ammon and not call us to go with you? We will burn your house with fire.
1 Judges 12:2 And Iephthae said to them: I and my people were a man in dispute, and the sons of Ammon humbled me greatly; and I cried out to you, and you did not save me from their hand.
1 Judges 12:3 And I saw that there was no one saving, and I placed my soul in my hand and crossed over to the sons of Ammon, and the Lord delivered them into my hand; and why have you come up to me today to fight against me?
1 Judges 12:4 And Iephthae gathered all the men of Galaad and fought Ephraim, and the men of Galaad struck Ephraim, because they said: You are those who have escaped from Ephraim, Galaad in the midst of Ephraim and in the midst of Manasse.
1 Judges 12:5 And the men of Galaad seized ahead of time the crossings of the Jordan belonging to Ephraim, and it happened that those who had escaped from Ephraim said, Let us cross, and the men of Galaad said to them: Are you from Ephraim? And they said: We are not.
1 Judges 12:6 And they said to them: Say, please, Password; and they could not manage to speak thus. And they seized them and slaughtered them at the crossings of the Jordan, and forty-two thousand from Ephraim fell at that time.
1 Judges 12:7 And Iephthae judged Israel six years. And Iephthae the Galaadite died and was buried in his city of Galaad.
1 Judges 12:8 And after him Esebon from Bethlehem judged Israel.
1 Judges 12:9 And he had thirty sons and thirty daughters sent outside, and he brought in thirty women from outside for his sons. And he judged Israel seven years.
1 Judges 12:10 And Esebon died and was buried in Bethlehem.
1 Judges 12:11 And after him Ailon the Zabulonite judged Israel. And he judged Israel ten years.
1 Judges 12:12 And Ailon the Zabulonite died in Ailim, and they buried him in the land of Zabulon.
1 Judges 12:13 And after him Labdon son of Sellem the Phraathonite judged Israel.
1 Judges 12:14 And he had forty sons and thirty sons of his sons mounted on seventy colts. And he judged Israel eight years.
1 Judges 12:15 And Labdon son of Sellem the Phraathonite died and was buried in Phraathon in the land of Ephraim on Mount Lanak.

## Chapter 13

1 Judges 13:1 And the sons of Israel again did evil before the Lord, and the Lord delivered them into the hand of the foreigners for forty years.
1 Judges 13:2 And there was a man from Saraa of the tribe of Dan, and his name was Manoe, and his wife was barren and did not bear.
1 Judges 13:3 And an angel of the Lord appeared to the woman and said to her: Behold, you are barren and have not borne; and you will conceive and bear a son.
1 Judges 13:4 And now take care and do not drink wine or strong drink and do not eat anything unclean;
1 Judges 13:5 for behold, you will conceive and bear a son, and iron shall not rise upon his head, because the child will be a consecrated Nazirite to God from the womb, and he will begin to save Israel from the hand of the foreigners.
1 Judges 13:6 And the woman came and told her husband, saying: A man of God came to me, and his appearance was like the appearance of an angel of God, very conspicuous; and I asked where he was from, and he did not tell me his name.
1 Judges 13:7 And he said to me: Behold, you will conceive and bear a son; and now do not drink wine or strong drink and do not eat any uncleanness, because the child will be a Nazirite of God from the womb until the day of his death.
1 Judges 13:8 And Manoe entreated the Lord and said: In me, Lord, let the man of God whom you sent to us come, please, to us and enlighten us as to what we should do with the child who is to be born.
1 Judges 13:9 And God listened to the voice of Manoe, and the angel of God came again to the woman while she was sitting in the field, and Manoe her husband was not with her.
1 Judges 13:10 And the woman hurried and ran out and reported to her husband and said to him: Behold, the man who came to me on that day has appeared to me.
1 Judges 13:11 And Manoe arose and went after his wife to the man and said to him: Are you the man who spoke to the woman? And the angel said: I am.
1 Judges 13:12 And Manoe said: Now, when your word comes, what will be the judgment of the child and his works?
1 Judges 13:13 And the angel of the Lord said to Manoe: Let her guard herself from all the things of which I spoke to the woman;
1 Judges 13:14 let her eat none of all that comes from the vine, and let her not drink wine or strong drink and not eat anything unclean; let her keep all that I commanded her.
1 Judges 13:15 And Manoe said to the angel of the Lord: Let us press you, please, and we will prepare a kid of the goats before you.
1 Judges 13:16 And the angel of the Lord said to Manoe: If you press me, I will not eat your bread, and if you prepare a whole burnt offering, offer it to the Lord; for Manoe did not know that he was an angel of the Lord.
1 Judges 13:17 And Manoe said to the angel of the Lord: What is your name, so that when your word comes we may glorify you?
1 Judges 13:18 And the angel of the Lord said to him: Why do you ask this, my name? And it is wonderful.
1 Judges 13:19 And Manoe took the kid of the goats and the sacrifice and offered it on the rock to the Lord, to the Lord who does wonders; and Manoe and his wife watched.
1 Judges 13:20 And it happened as the flame went up from above the altar into heaven that the angel of the Lord went up in the flame, and Manoe and his wife watched and fell upon their faces to the ground.
1 Judges 13:21 And the angel of the Lord no longer appeared to Manoe and his wife; then Manoe knew that he was an angel of the Lord.
1 Judges 13:22 And Manoe said to his wife: We shall surely die, for we have seen God.
1 Judges 13:23 And his wife said to him: If the Lord wished to put us to death, he would not have accepted from our hands a whole burnt offering and sacrifice and would not have enlightened us about all these things and would not have made these things heard by us.
1 Judges 13:24 And the woman bore a son and called his name Sampson; and the Lord blessed him, and the child grew.
1 Judges 13:25 And a spirit of the Lord began to go with him in the camp of Dan between Saraa and Esthaol.

## Chapter 14

1 Judges 14:1 And Sampson went down to Thamnatha and saw a woman in Thamnatha from the daughters of the foreigners, and she was pleasing before him.
1 Judges 14:2 And he went up and reported to his father and mother and said: I have seen a woman in Thamnatha from the daughters of the foreigners, and now take her for me as a wife.
1 Judges 14:3 And his father and mother said to him: Is there no woman among the daughters of your brothers and among all my people, that you go to take a wife from the uncircumcised foreigners? And Sampson said to his father: Take this one for me, because she is pleasing in my eyes.
1 Judges 14:4 And his father and mother did not know that it was from the Lord, because he was seeking recompense from the foreigners; and at that time the foreigners ruled over the sons of Israel.
1 Judges 14:5 And Sampson and his father and mother went down to Thamnatha. And he turned aside into a vineyard of Thamnatha, and behold, a young lion roaring came to meet him;
1 Judges 14:6 and a spirit of the Lord guided itself upon him, and he tore it apart as one tears apart a kid of the goats, and there was nothing in his hand. And he did not tell his father or mother what he had done.
1 Judges 14:7 And they went down and spoke to the woman, and she was pleasing before Sampson.
1 Judges 14:8 And after days he returned to take her and turned aside to see the carcass of the lion, and behold, a cluster of bees in the mouth of the lion, and there was honey.
1 Judges 14:9 And he took it out into his mouth and went on walking and eating; and he went to his father and mother and gave them some, and they ate; and he did not tell them that he took the honey from the condition of the lion.
1 Judges 14:10 And his father went down to the woman; and Sampson made a drinking feast there for seven days, because the young men did thus.
1 Judges 14:11 And it happened when they feared him that they appointed thirty companions for him, and they were with him.
1 Judges 14:12 And Sampson said to them: I will put a riddle to you, and if you tell me the riddle within the seven days of the feast, I will give you thirty linen cloths and thirty garments;
1 Judges 14:13 and if you are unable to tell me, you will give me thirty linen cloths and thirty sets of clothing. And they said to him: Put forth your riddle, and we will hear it.
1 Judges 14:14 And he said to them: Out of the eater came food, and out of the strong came sweetness. And they were unable to tell the riddle for three days.
1 Judges 14:15 And it happened on the fourth day that they said to Sampson's wife: Deceive your husband, please, and let him tell you the riddle, lest we burn you and your father's house with fire; did you call us to become poor?
1 Judges 14:16 And Sampson's wife wept upon him and said to him: You have hated me and have not loved me, because the riddle which you put to the sons of my people you did not tell even me. And Sampson said to her: Behold, I did not tell my father or mother, and shall I tell you?
1 Judges 14:17 And she wept upon him during the seven days in which the feast was held; and it happened on the seventh day that he told her, because she troubled him; and she told the sons of her people.
1 Judges 14:18 And the men of the city said to him on the seventh day before the sun set: What is sweeter than honey, and what is stronger than a lion? And Sampson said to them: If you had not tamed my heifer, you would not have found my riddle.
1 Judges 14:19 And a spirit of the Lord guided itself upon him, and he went down to Ascalon and struck thirty men there and took their garments and gave them to those who told the riddle. And Sampson was angry in wrath and went up to his father's house.
1 Judges 14:20 And Sampson's wife lived with his bridegroom attendant, who was his companion.

## Chapter 15

1 Judges 15:1 And it happened after days in the days of the wheat harvest that Sampson visited his wife carrying a kid of the goats and said: I will enter to my wife into the bedchamber; and her father did not allow him to enter to her.
1 Judges 15:2 And her father said: Saying, I said that you had utterly hated her, and I gave her to your companion; behold, is her younger sister not better than she? Let her be yours in her place.
1 Judges 15:3 And Sampson said to him: I am innocent this once of the foreigners, because I am doing evils among you.
1 Judges 15:4 And Sampson went and caught three hundred foxes and took torches and tied tail to tail and placed one torch between the two tails in the middle;
1 Judges 15:5 and he kindled fire in the torches and sent them into the sheaves of the foreigners and burned the ears of grain and what had been harvested before, from the stack as far as what was standing and as far as vineyard and olive tree.
1 Judges 15:6 And the foreigners said: Who did these things? And they said: Sampson the son-in-law of the Thamnathaite, because he took his wife and gave her to his companion; and the foreigners went up and burned the house of her father and her and her father with fire.
1 Judges 15:7 And Sampson said to them: If you do thus, I will not be satisfied, but I will take my vengeance from each and every one of you.
1 Judges 15:8 And he struck them upon the thigh with a great blow; and he went down and dwelt by the torrent in the cave of Etam.
1 Judges 15:9 And the foreigners went up and encamped against Judah and spread out in Lechi.
1 Judges 15:10 And every man of Judah said to them: Why have you come up against us? And the foreigners said: To bind Sampson and to do to him in the manner he did to us.
1 Judges 15:11 And three thousand men from Judah went down to the opening of the rock of Etam and said to Sampson: Do you not know that the foreigners rule over us, and why have you done these things to us? And Sampson said to them: As they did to us, so I did to them.
1 Judges 15:12 And they said to him: We came down to bind you and deliver you into the hands of the foreigners. And Sampson said to them: Swear to me that you yourselves will not kill me and deliver me to them, lest you yourselves meet against me.
1 Judges 15:13 And they swore to him, saying: No, but we will bind you with a bond and deliver you into their hands, but we will certainly not put you to death; and they bound him with two new cords and brought him up from the rock.
1 Judges 15:14 And he came as far as Siagon; and the foreigners shouted to meet him and ran to meet him; and a spirit of the Lord directed itself upon him, and the cords on his arms became like tow when it smells fire, and the bonds dissolved from his arms.
1 Judges 15:15 And he found a jawbone of a donkey cast on the road and stretched out his hand and took it and struck a thousand men with it.
1 Judges 15:16 And Sampson said: With a jawbone of a donkey, wiping out I wiped them out, because with a jawbone of a donkey I struck a thousand men.
1 Judges 15:17 And it happened when he finished speaking that he cast the jawbone from his hand; and he called that place Removal of the Jawbone.
1 Judges 15:18 And he was very thirsty; and he cried out to the Lord and said: You gave into the hand of your servant this great deliverance, and now shall I die of thirst and fall into the hand of the uncircumcised?
1 Judges 15:19 And God opened the wound of the jawbone, and waters came out of it, and he drank, and his spirit returned within him, and he revived. Therefore its name was called Spring Called of the Jawbone until this day. –
1 Judges 15:20 And he judged Israel in the days of the foreigners twenty years.

## Chapter 16

1 Judges 16:1 And Sampson went from there to Gaza; and he saw a prostitute there and went in to her.
1 Judges 16:2 And it was reported to the Gazites, saying: Sampson has come here. And they surrounded and lay in wait for him all night at the city gate and kept silent all night, saying: Let us wait until the light in the morning and kill him.
1 Judges 16:3 And Sampson slept until midnight; and he arose around midnight and took hold of the doors of the city gate and the two posts and lifted them with the bar and put them upon his shoulder and carried them up to the summit of the mountain which faces Chebron and placed them there.
1 Judges 16:4 And it happened after these things that he loved a woman by the torrent Sorech, and her name was Dalila.
1 Judges 16:5 And the satraps of the foreigners went up to her and said to her: Deceive him and see in what his great strength lies and by what we can prevail against him and bind him so as to humble him, and we will each give you one thousand one hundred pieces of silver.
1 Judges 16:6 And Dalila said to Sampson: Tell me in what your great strength lies and with what you may be bound to be humbled.
1 Judges 16:7 And Sampson said to her: If they bind me with seven moist sinews not dried out, I will grow weak and be like one of the people.
1 Judges 16:8 And the satraps of the foreigners brought her seven moist sinews not dried out, and she bound him with them;
1 Judges 16:9 and his ambush sat in the inner room; and she said to him: The foreigners are upon you, Sampson; and he tore the sinews as a strand of the waste fiber is torn when it smells fire; and his strength was not known.
1 Judges 16:10 And Dalila said to Sampson: Behold, you have deceived me and spoken lies to me; now therefore tell me, please, with what you may be bound.
1 Judges 16:11 And he said to her: If they bind me firmly with seven new cords with which no work has been done, I will grow weak and be like one of the people.
1 Judges 16:12 And Dalila took new cords for him and bound him with them and said to him: The foreigners are upon you, Sampson; and the ambush sat in the inner room; and he tore them from his arms like thread.
1 Judges 16:13 And Dalila said to Sampson: Until now you have deceived me and spoken lies to me; tell me, please, with what you may be bound. And he said to her: If you weave the seven strands of my head with the warp and drive them into the peg in the wall, I will be weak like one of the people.
1 Judges 16:14 And Dalila made him sleep and wove the seven locks of his head with the stretching and drove them with the pegs into the wall and said to him: The foreigners are upon you, Sampson; and he awoke from his sleep and pulled the pegs with the woven cloth from the wall and the warp, and his strength was not known.
1 Judges 16:15 And Dalila said to him: How can you say, I have loved you, when your heart is not with me? This is the third time you have deceived me and have not told me in what your great strength lies.
1 Judges 16:16 And it happened when she wore him down with her words all night and troubled him that he grew fainthearted to the point of death;
1 Judges 16:17 and he told her everything from his heart and said to her: A razor shall not rise upon my head, for I am a Nazirite of God from my mother's womb, and if I am shaved, my strength will depart from me and I will grow weak and be like all people.
1 Judges 16:18 And Dalila saw that he had told her everything from his heart and sent and called all the satraps of the foreigners, saying: Come up this once, for he has told me all his heart; and all the satrapies of the foreigners went up to her and brought the silver in their hands.
1 Judges 16:19 And she made him sleep between her knees; and she called the barber, and he shaved the seven locks of his head; and he began to be humbled, and his strength departed from him.
1 Judges 16:20 And Dalila said to him: The foreigners are upon you, Sampson. And he awoke from his sleep and said: I will go out and do as always and shake myself free; and he did not know that the Lord had departed from him.
1 Judges 16:21 And the foreigners seized him and gouged out his eyes; and they brought him down to Gaza and bound him with bronze fetters, and he was grinding in the prison house.
1 Judges 16:22 And the hair of his head began to grow when it had been shaved.
1 Judges 16:23 And the satraps of the foreigners gathered to sacrifice a great sacrifice to Dagon their god and to rejoice, and they said: Our god has delivered Sampson our enemy into our hand.
1 Judges 16:24 And the people saw him and praised their gods and said: Our god has delivered our enemy into our hand, the one who laid waste our land, who multiplied our wounded.
1 Judges 16:25 And it happened when their heart became glad that they said: Call Sampson from the prison house, and let him play before us. And they called Sampson from the prison house and mocked him and stood him between the two pillars.
1 Judges 16:26 And Sampson said to the young man leading him by the hand: Let me rest, please, and let me feel the pillars on which the house rests, and I will lean upon them; and the servant did so.
1 Judges 16:27 And the house was full of men and women, and all the satraps of the foreigners were there, and on the roof about three thousand men and women looking at Sampson being mocked.
1 Judges 16:28 And Sampson cried out to the Lord and said: Lord, Lord, remember me and strengthen me, please, just this once more, and I will take one vengeance for my two eyes from the foreigners.
1 Judges 16:29 And Sampson embraced the two middle pillars upon which the house rested, and leaned upon them, one with his right hand and one with his left.
1 Judges 16:30 And Sampson said: Let my soul die with the foreigners; and he bent with strength, and the house fell upon the satraps and upon all the people in it; and those who died whom Sampson put to death in his death were more than those whom he put to death in his life.
1 Judges 16:31 And his brothers and all his father's house went down and took him and went up and buried him between Saraa and Esthaol in the tomb of Manoe his father. And he judged Israel twenty years.

## Chapter 17

1 Judges 17:1 And there was a man from Mount Ephraim, and his name was Micha.
1 Judges 17:2 And he said to his mother: The one thousand one hundred pieces of silver taken from you, about which you adjured and spoke in my ears, behold, the silver is with me; I took it. And his mother said: May my son be blessed by the Lord.
1 Judges 17:3 And he returned the one thousand one hundred pieces of silver to his mother, and his mother said: With consecration I consecrated the silver to the Lord from my hand alone to make a carved and molten image, and now I will return them to you and give it back to you.
1 Judges 17:4 And he returned the silver to his mother; and his mother took two hundred pieces of silver and gave it to the founder, and he made it a carved and molten image, and it was in Micha's house.
1 Judges 17:5 And the man Micha had a house of God; and he made an ephoud and theraphin and filled the hand of one of his sons, and he became his priest. –
1 Judges 17:6 In those days there was no king in Israel; each man did what was good in his own eyes.
1 Judges 17:7 And there was a young man from Bethlehem of the division of Judah, of the kin of Judah, and he was a Levite, and he sojourned there.
1 Judges 17:8 And the man went from the city of Judah, from Bethlehem, to sojourn wherever he might find, and came into Mount Ephraim as far as Micha's house to make his way.
1 Judges 17:9 And Micha said to him: Where do you come from? And he said to him: I am a Levite from Bethlehem of Judah, and I am going to sojourn wherever I might find.
1 Judges 17:10 And Micha said to him: Sit with me and become a father and priest for me, and I will give you ten pieces of silver for days and a pair of garments and what is needed for your living. And the Levite went
1 Judges 17:11 and began to sojourn with the man, and the young man became like one of his sons to him.
1 Judges 17:12 And Micha filled the Levite's hand, and the young man became his priest and was in Micha's house.
1 Judges 17:13 And Micha said: Now I know that the Lord has done me good, because the Levite became my priest.

## Chapter 18

1 Judges 18:1 In those days there was no king in Israel. And in those days the tribe of Dan sought an inheritance for itself to dwell in, because an inheritance had not fallen to it until those days among the tribes of Israel.
1 Judges 18:2 And the sons of Dan sent from their kin five men from their number, sons of strength from Saraa and Esthaol, to inspect the land and trace it out, and said to them: Go and search out the land. And they came to Mount Ephraim as far as Micha's house and rested there.
1 Judges 18:3 While they were by Micha's house they recognized the voice of the younger Levite servant and turned aside there and said to him: Who brought you here, and what are you doing here, and what do you have here?
1 Judges 18:4 And he said to them: Thus and thus Micha did for me and hired me, and I became his priest.
1 Judges 18:5 And they said to him: Ask, please, by God, and we will know whether our way upon which we are going prospers.
1 Judges 18:6 And the priest said to them: Go in peace; before the Lord is your way in which you are going.
1 Judges 18:7 And the five men went and came to Laisa; and they saw the people dwelling in it sitting in confidence according to the manner of the Sidonians, quiet in confidence and unable to speak a word, because they were far from Sidon, and they had no dealings with Syria.
1 Judges 18:8 And the five men came to their brothers in Saraa and Esthaol, and their brothers said to them: Why do you sit?
1 Judges 18:9 And they said: Arise and let us go up against them; because we entered and walked about in the land as far as Laisa and saw the people dwelling in it in confidence after the manner of the Sidonians, and far away from Sidon, and they had no dealings with Syria; but arise and let us go up against them, for we have found the land and behold, it is very good. And are you silent? Do not hesitate to go to come and inherit the land.
1 Judges 18:10 When you enter, you will come to a trusting people, and the land is spacious, for God has delivered it into your hand, a place where there is no lack of any thing that is in the land.
1 Judges 18:11 And six hundred men from the kin of Dan set out from Saraa and Esthaol, girded with implements of war.
1 Judges 18:12 And they went up and encamped in Kariathiarim in Judah; therefore that place was called Camp of Dan until this day, behold, behind Kariathiarim.
1 Judges 18:13 They passed from there and came as far as Mount Ephraim and came as far as Micha's house.
1 Judges 18:14 And the five men who had gone to inspect the land answered and said to their brothers: Do you know that in these houses there are an ephoud and theraphin and a carved and a molten image? And now know what you will do.
1 Judges 18:15 And they turned aside there and entered the house of the young Levite, Micha's house, and greeted him.
1 Judges 18:16 And the six hundred men girded with implements of war stood fixed by the entrance of the gateway, those from the sons of Dan.
1 Judges 18:17 And the five men who had gone to inspect the land went up; coming there they took the carved image and the ephoud and the theraphin and the molten image, while the priest stood fixed by the entrance of the gateway with the six hundred men girded with implements of war.
1 Judges 18:18 And these entered Micha's house and took the carved image and the ephoud and the theraphin and the molten image. And the priest said to them: What are you doing?
1 Judges 18:19 And they said to him: Be silent, put your hand upon your mouth and come with us, and you will be a father and priest for us; is it not better for you to be priest of one man's house than to become priest of a tribe and kin in Israel?
1 Judges 18:20 And the priest's heart became glad, and he took the ephoud and the theraphin and the carved image and the molten image and went into the midst of the people.
1 Judges 18:21 And they turned and departed; and they set the whole household and his splendid property before them.
1 Judges 18:22 When they had gone far from Micha's house, behold, Micha and the men with the house with Micha cried out after the sons of Dan.
1 Judges 18:23 And the sons of Dan turned their faces and said to Micha: What is the matter with you, that you cried out?
1 Judges 18:24 And Micha said: Because you took my carved image which I made for myself and the priest and departed; and what do I still have? And why do you say to me, Why are you crying out?
1 Judges 18:25 And the sons of Dan said to him: Let your voice not be heard with us, lest men pained in soul meet you, and you will add your soul and the soul of your house.
1 Judges 18:26 And the sons of Dan went on their way; and Micha saw that they were stronger than he and turned aside and returned to his house.
1 Judges 18:27 And they took what Micha made and the priest who was his, and came as far as Laisa against a quiet and trusting people and struck them with the edge of the sword and burned the city;
1 Judges 18:28 and there was no one to rescue, because it was far from the Sidonians, and they had no dealings with people, and it was in the valley belonging to the house of Roob. And they built the city and dwelt in it
1 Judges 18:29 and called the name of the city Dan after the name of their father who was born to Israel; and Lais was the city's name formerly.
1 Judges 18:30 And the sons of Dan set up for themselves Micha's carved image; and Ionathan son of Gersom son of Moses, he and his sons were priests for the tribe of Dan until the day of the deportation of the land.
1 Judges 18:31 And they placed for themselves Micha's carved image which he made all the days that the house of God was in Selo.

## Chapter 19

1 Judges 19:1 And it happened in those days, and there was no king in Israel. And there was a Levite man sojourning in the flanks of Mount Ephraim, and the man took for himself a woman, a concubine, from Bethlehem of Judah.
1 Judges 19:2 And his concubine became angry with him and departed from him to her father's house in Bethlehem of Judah and was there for four months of days.
1 Judges 19:3 And her man arose and went after her to speak to her heart, to reconcile her to himself and lead her back to him, and his young servant with him and a pair of beasts of burden; and he went as far as her father's house, and the young woman's father saw him and was there to meet him.
1 Judges 19:4 And his father-in-law, the young woman's father, brought him in, and he sat with him three days, and they ate and drank and slept there.
1 Judges 19:5 And it happened on the fourth day that they arose early in the morning, and he arose to depart; and the young woman's father said to his son-in-law: Support your heart with a piece of bread, and after this go.
1 Judges 19:6 And both sat and ate together and drank; and the young woman's father said to the man: Begin to lodge, and let your heart be glad.
1 Judges 19:7 And the man arose to depart; and his father-in-law pressed him, and he lodged there again.
1 Judges 19:8 And he rose early in the morning on the fifth day to depart; and the young woman's father said: Support your heart with bread and march when the day inclines; and both ate and drank.
1 Judges 19:9 And the man arose to depart, he and his concubine and his young servant; and his father-in-law, the young woman's father, said to him: Behold, the day has now inclined toward evening; lodge here still today, and let your heart be glad, and you will rise early tomorrow for your way, and depart to your dwelling.
1 Judges 19:10 And the man did not wish to lodge and arose and departed, and they came opposite Iebous [this is Jerusalem], and with him a pair of saddled beasts of burden, and his concubine with him.
1 Judges 19:11 While they were still near Iebous and the day had inclined greatly, the young servant said to his master: Come, please, and let us turn aside into this city of the Iebusite and lodge in it.
1 Judges 19:12 And his master said to him: I will not turn aside into a city of a foreigner which is not of the sons of Israel, and we will pass on as far as Gabaa.
1 Judges 19:13 And he said to his young servant: Come and let us enter one of the places and lodge in Gabaa or in Rama.
1 Judges 19:14 And they passed on and departed; for the sun set near Gabaa, which belongs to Benjamin.
1 Judges 19:15 And they turned aside there to enter and lodge in Gabaa; and they entered and sat in the square of the city, and there was no man to bring them into a house to lodge.
1 Judges 19:16 And behold, an old man came from his work in the field in the evening; and the man was from Mount Ephraim, and he sojourned in Gabaa, and the men of the place were sons of Benjamin.
1 Judges 19:17 And looking up with his eyes he saw the traveling man in the square of the city; and the old man said: Where are you going and where do you come from?
1 Judges 19:18 And he said to him: We are passing from Bethlehem of Judah to the flanks of Mount Ephraim; and I am from there and went as far as Bethlehem of Judah, and I am running back to my house, and there is no man to bring me into a house;
1 Judges 19:19 and indeed there is straw and fodder for our donkeys, and there is bread and wine for me and your servant woman and the young servant, your servants; there is no lack of anything.
1 Judges 19:20 And the old man said: Peace to you; only let all your lack be upon me; only do not lodge in the square.
1 Judges 19:21 And he brought him into his house and placed fodder before his beasts of burden, and they washed their feet and ate and drank.
1 Judges 19:22 And as their hearts became glad, behold, the men of the city, sons of lawless men, surrounded the house and struck the door and said to the old man, the master of the house: Bring out the man who entered your house so that we may know him.
1 Judges 19:23 And the man, the master of the house, went out to them and said to them: By no means, brothers, please do not do evil; after this man has entered my house, do not do this foolishness;
1 Judges 19:24 behold, my virgin daughter and his concubine, I will bring them out, and humble them and do to them what is good in your eyes; but to this man do not do the deed of this foolishness.
1 Judges 19:25 And the men were unwilling to listen to him. And the man seized his concubine and brought her out to them outside, and they knew her and mocked her all night until morning; and they sent her away as dawn rose.
1 Judges 19:26 And the woman came toward morning and fell by the door of the gateway of the man's house, where her master was, until it grew light.
1 Judges 19:27 And her master arose in the morning and opened the doors of the house and went out to depart on his way, and behold, his concubine had fallen by the door, and her hands were on the threshold.
1 Judges 19:28 And he said to her: Arise and let us go; and she did not answer him, but had died. And he lifted her onto the beast of burden, and the man arose and departed to his place.
1 Judges 19:29 And he entered his house and took the knife and seized his concubine and divided her according to her bones into twelve portions and sent them to all the tribes of Israel.
1 Judges 19:30 And it happened that everyone who saw said: Neither has such a thing happened nor has it been seen from the day the sons of Israel came up from Egypt until this day. And he commanded the men to whom he sent them, saying: Thus you shall say to every man of Israel: Has there been anything like this deed from the day the sons of Israel came up from Egypt until this day? Set counsel for yourselves about it, please, and speak.

## Chapter 20

1 Judges 20:1 And all the sons of Israel went out, and the whole congregation assembled as one man from Dan as far as Bersabee and the land of Galaad to the Lord at Massepha.
1 Judges 20:2 And the position of all the people stood, all the tribes of Israel, in the assembly of the people of God, four hundred thousand footmen drawing the sword.
1 Judges 20:3 And the sons of Benjamin heard that the sons of Israel had gone up to the Lord at Massepha. And the sons of Israel said: Speak, where did this evil happen?
1 Judges 20:4 And the Levite man, the man of the woman who had been murdered, answered and said: I and my concubine came to Gabaa of Benjamin to lodge.
1 Judges 20:5 And the men from Gabaa rose against me and surrounded the house against me by night and wished to kill me, and they humbled my concubine and mocked her, and she died.
1 Judges 20:6 And I seized my concubine and divided her and sent her throughout every boundary of Israel's inheritance, because they did foolishness in Israel.
1 Judges 20:7 Behold, all of you, the sons of Israel, give yourselves a word and counsel.
1 Judges 20:8 And all the people arose as one man, saying: No man of us shall enter his dwelling and no man of us shall turn aside to his house.
1 Judges 20:9 And now this is the thing we will do to Gabaa: we will go up against it by lot
1 Judges 20:10 and take ten men for the hundred and a hundred for the thousand and a thousand for the ten thousand to take provisions for the people entering to carry out against Gabaa of Benjamin according to all the foolishness which they did in Israel.
1 Judges 20:11 And every man of Israel gathered from the cities, coming as one man.
1 Judges 20:12 And the tribes of Israel sent men throughout the tribe of Benjamin, saying: What is this evil that happened among you?
1 Judges 20:13 And now give up the impious men in Gabaa, the sons of Belial, and we will put them to death and remove evil from Israel. And the sons of Benjamin were unwilling to listen to the voice of their brothers, the sons of Israel.
1 Judges 20:14 And the sons of Benjamin gathered from their cities to Gabaa to go out to fight with the sons of Israel.
1 Judges 20:15 And the sons of Benjamin were counted on that day from the cities, twenty-five thousand men drawing the sword, apart from those dwelling in Gabaa; these were counted as seven hundred chosen young men
1 Judges 20:16 right-handed on both sides; all these were slingers casting stones at a hair and not missing.
1 Judges 20:17 And all the men of Israel were counted apart from the sons of Benjamin, four hundred thousand men drawing the sword; all these were men of war.
1 Judges 20:18 And they arose and went up to Bethel and asked by God, and the sons of Israel said: Who will go up for us, taking the lead to fight with Benjamin? And the Lord said: Judah shall go up taking the lead.
1 Judges 20:19 And the sons of Israel arose and encamped against Gabaa.
1 Judges 20:20 And every man of Israel went out to war with Benjamin, and the men of Israel drew up against them for war at Gabaa.
1 Judges 20:21 And the sons of Benjamin went out from the city and destroyed among Israel on that day twenty-two thousand men upon the ground.
1 Judges 20:22 And the men of Israel grew strong and again drew up for war in the place where they had drawn up there on the first day.
1 Judges 20:23 And the sons of Israel went up and wept before the Lord until evening and asked by the Lord, saying: Shall I again draw near to war with Benjamin my brother? And the Lord said: Go up against him.
1 Judges 20:24 And the sons of Israel approached Benjamin on the second day.
1 Judges 20:25 And Benjamin went out to meet them from Gabaa on the second day and destroyed eighteen thousand men from the people upon the ground; all these had drawn the sword.
1 Judges 20:26 And all the sons of Israel and all the people went up and came to Bethel and wept before the Lord and fasted on that day and offered whole burnt offerings of deliverance before the Lord,
1 Judges 20:27 and the sons of Israel asked by the Lord; and the ark of the covenant of the Lord was there in those days,
1 Judges 20:28 and Phinees son of Eleazar son of Aaron stood before it in those days, saying: Shall I again go out to war with the sons of Benjamin my brother, or shall I cease? And the Lord said: Go up, for tomorrow I will deliver him into your hand.
1 Judges 20:29 And the sons of Israel placed an ambush around Gabaa.
1 Judges 20:30 And Israel drew up against Benjamin on the third day and drew up against Gabaa as once and once.
1 Judges 20:31 And the sons of Benjamin went out to meet the people and were drawn out of the city and began to strike some of the people as once and once on the roads, one of which goes up to Bethel and one goes up to Gabaa in the field, about thirty men among Israel.
1 Judges 20:32 And the sons of Benjamin said: They stumble before us as before. And the sons of Israel said: Let us flee and draw them out of the city onto the roads.
1 Judges 20:33 And every man of Israel arose from his place and drew up at Baalthamar, and the ambush of Israel wrestled from its place west of Gabaa.
1 Judges 20:34 And ten thousand chosen men from all Israel came opposite Gabaa, and the battle grew heavy; and they did not know that evil had fastened upon them.
1 Judges 20:35 And the Lord routed Benjamin before Israel, and the sons of Israel destroyed among Benjamin on that day twenty-five thousand one hundred men; all these drew the sword.
1 Judges 20:36 And Benjamin saw that he had been routed; and the men of Israel gave ground to Benjamin because they trusted in the ambush which they had placed against Gabaa.
1 Judges 20:37 And the ambush rushed and poured out toward Gabaa, and the ambush went and struck the whole city with the edge of the sword.
1 Judges 20:38 And the arrangement for the men of Israel with the ambush was that they should raise a torch of the smoke of the city.
1 Judges 20:39 And the men of Israel turned in the battle, and Benjamin had begun to strike wounded men among the men of Israel, about thirty men, because they said: Surely he is being routed before us as in the former battle.
1 Judges 20:40 And the torch began to rise from the city, a column of smoke; and Benjamin looked behind him, and behold, the destruction of the city rose to heaven.
1 Judges 20:41 And the men of Israel turned back, and the men of Benjamin hastened and saw that evil had seized him.
1 Judges 20:42 And they turned before the men of Israel onto the way of the wilderness, and the battle overtook him, and those from the cities destroyed him in their midst.
1 Judges 20:43 And they cut down Benjamin, to make him rest with a rest, and trampled him as far as opposite Gabaa from the rising of the sun.
1 Judges 20:44 And eighteen thousand men from Benjamin fell; with all these were mighty men.
1 Judges 20:45 And they turned aside and fled to the wilderness toward the rock of Remmon, and they gleaned five thousand men on the roads; and they clung after him as far as Gadaam and struck two thousand men from them.
1 Judges 20:46 And all those who fell among Benjamin were twenty-five thousand men drawing the sword on that day; with all these were mighty men.
1 Judges 20:47 And six hundred men turned aside and fled to the wilderness toward the rock of Remmon and sat at the rock of Remmon for four months.
1 Judges 20:48 And the men of Israel shut off the sons of Benjamin and struck them with the edge of the sword from city in succession as far as cattle, as far as everything found in all the cities; and the cities found they sent up in fire.

## Chapter 21

1 Judges 21:1 And a man of Israel swore at Massepha, saying: No man of us will give his daughter to Benjamin as a wife.
1 Judges 21:2 And all the people came to Massepha and Bethel and sat there until evening before God and raised their voice and wept a great weeping
1 Judges 21:3 and said: Why, Lord the God of Israel, has this happened in Israel, that one tribe should be missing from Israel today?
1 Judges 21:4 And it happened the next day that the people rose early and built an altar there and offered whole burnt offerings of deliverance.
1 Judges 21:5 And the sons of Israel said: Who did not come up in the assembly from all the tribes of Israel to the Lord? For there was a great oath concerning the one who did not come up to the Lord at Massepha, saying: He shall surely die.
1 Judges 21:6 And the sons of Israel were moved concerning Benjamin their brother and said: One tribe has been taken away from Israel today;
1 Judges 21:7 what shall we do for those who remain concerning wives? And we swore by the Lord not to give them any of our daughters as wives.
1 Judges 21:8 And they said: Which one of the tribes of Israel did not go up to the Lord at Massepha? And behold, no man from Iabis Galaad came to the camp for the assembly.
1 Judges 21:9 And the people were counted, and behold, there was no man there from those dwelling in Iabis Galaad.
1 Judges 21:10 And the congregation sent there twelve thousand men from the sons of strength and commanded them, saying: Go and strike all those dwelling in Iabis Galaad with the edge of the sword, the women and the people.
1 Judges 21:11 And this is the thing you shall do: Every male and every woman who knows the bed of a male you shall devote.
1 Judges 21:12 And they found from those dwelling in Iabis Galaad four hundred young virgin women who had not known a man in the bed of a male, and they led them to the camp at Selo, which is in the land of Canaan.
1 Judges 21:13 And all the congregation sent and spoke to Benjamin at the rock of Remmon and called them to peace.
1 Judges 21:14 And Benjamin returned to the sons of Israel at that time, and they gave them the women who were from the women of Iabis Galaad; and it pleased them thus.
1 Judges 21:15 And the people were moved for Benjamin, because the Lord had made a breach among the tribes of Israel.
1 Judges 21:16 And the elders of the congregation said: What shall we do for the remaining ones concerning wives? For women have disappeared from Benjamin.
1 Judges 21:17 And they said: An inheritance has been saved for Benjamin, and a tribe shall certainly not be wiped out from Israel;
1 Judges 21:18 and we will not be able to give them wives from our daughters, because we, the sons of Israel, swore, saying: Cursed is the one who gives a wife to Benjamin.
1 Judges 21:19 And they said: There is a feast to the Lord in Selo from days to days, which is north of Bethel toward the rising of the sun on the road that goes up from Bethel to Sikima and south of Lebanon of Lebona.
1 Judges 21:20 And they commanded the sons of Benjamin, saying: Go through and lie in ambush in the vineyards;
1 Judges 21:21 and you will watch, and behold, when the daughters of those dwelling in Selo come out in Selo to dance in dances, you will go out from the vineyards and each man seize a wife for himself from the daughters of Selo and go away to the land of Benjamin.
1 Judges 21:22 And it will be that when their fathers or their brothers come to plead with you, we will say to them: Show them mercy, because each man did not take his wife in the war; for you did not give them to them; at the time you committed an offense.
1 Judges 21:23 And the sons of Benjamin did so and took wives according to their number from the dancing women whom they seized; and they departed and returned to their inheritance and built cities for themselves and dwelt in them.
1 Judges 21:24 And the sons of Israel walked away from there at that time, each man to his tribe and to his kin, and they departed from there, each man to his inheritance. –
1 Judges 21:25 In those days there was no king in Israel; each man did what was right in his own eyes.

# 2 Judges

The Apostolic Bible. Public domain. https://apostolic-bible.ysys9.chatgpt.site/license.html


## Chapter 1

2 Judges 1:1 And it happened after the death of Jesus that the sons of Israel asked through the Lord, saying: Who will go up for us against the Canaanites, taking the lead to fight against them?
2 Judges 1:2 And the Lord said: Judah will go up; behold, I have given the land into his hand.
2 Judges 1:3 And Judah said to Symeon his brother: Come up with me in my lot, and let us draw up against the Canaanites, and I too will go with you in your lot. And Symeon went with him.
2 Judges 1:4 And Judah went up, and the Lord delivered the Canaanite and the Pherezite into their hands, and they cut down ten thousand men at Bezek,
2 Judges 1:5 and they took Adonibezek at Bezek and drew up against him and cut down the Canaanite and the Pherezite.
2 Judges 1:6 And Adonibezek fled, and they ran after him and took him and cut off the extremities of his hands and the extremities of his feet.
2 Judges 1:7 And Adonibezek said: Seventy kings, with the extremities of their hands and the extremities of their feet cut off, were gathering what was under my table; as I did, so God has repaid me. And they bring him to Jerusalem, and he died there.
2 Judges 1:8 And the sons of Judah fought Jerusalem and took it and struck it with the edge of the sword and burned the city with fire.
2 Judges 1:9 And after these things the sons of Judah went down to fight against the Canaanite dwelling in the hill country and the south and the plain.
2 Judges 1:10 And Judah went against the Canaanite dwelling in Chebron, and Chebron came out opposite; and the name of Chebron formerly was Kariatharboxepher. And they struck Sessi and Achinaan and Tholmin, offspring of Enak.
2 Judges 1:11 And they went up from there against those dwelling in Dabir; but the name of Dabir formerly was Kariathsophar, City of Letters.
2 Judges 1:12 And Chaleb said: Whoever strikes the City of Letters and takes it first, I will give him Ascha my daughter for a wife.
2 Judges 1:13 And Gothoniel son of Kenez brother of Chaleb, the younger, took it first, and Chaleb gave him Ascha his daughter for a wife.
2 Judges 1:14 And it happened as she entered that Gothoniel urged her to ask her father for a field, and she murmured and cried out from the beast of burden: You have given me away into a land of the south. And Chaleb said to her: What is it for you?
2 Judges 1:15 And Ascha said to him: Give me, please, a blessing, because you have given me away into a land of the south, and you will give me a redemption of water. And Chaleb gave her according to her heart a redemption of the heights and a redemption of the lowlands.
2 Judges 1:16 And the sons of Iothor the Kenite, the father-in-law of Moses, went up from the city of palms with the sons of Judah into the wilderness in the south of Judah, which is by the descent of Arad, and dwelt with the people. –
2 Judges 1:17 And Judah went with Symeon his brother and cut down the Canaanite dwelling in Sephek; and they destroyed them and called the name of the city Devoted Thing.
2 Judges 1:18 And Judah did not inherit Gaza nor its boundaries nor Ascalon nor its boundaries nor Akkaron nor its boundaries nor Azotus nor its surrounding lands.
2 Judges 1:19 And the Lord was with Judah, and he inherited the mountain; because they were unable to destroy those dwelling in the valley, because Rechab had divided it for them.
2 Judges 1:20 And they gave Chebron to Chaleb, as Moses spoke, and he inherited from there the three cities of the sons of Enak.
2 Judges 1:21 And the sons of Benjamin did not inherit the Iebusite dwelling in Jerusalem, and the Iebusite dwelt with the sons of Benjamin in Jerusalem until this day.
2 Judges 1:22 And the sons of Joseph, they too, went up to Bethel, and the Lord was with them.
2 Judges 1:23 And they encamped against and inspected Bethel; but the name of their city formerly was Louza.
2 Judges 1:24 And those keeping watch saw, and behold, a man was going out of the city; and they took him and said to him: Show us the entrance of the city, and we will deal mercifully with you.
2 Judges 1:25 And he showed them the entrance of the city, and they struck the city with the edge of the sword, but the man and his kin they sent away.
2 Judges 1:26 And the man went to the land of the Chettites and built a city there and called its name Louza; that is its name until this day.
2 Judges 1:27 And Manasse did not remove Baithsan, which is the city of the Scythians, nor its daughter towns nor its surrounding inhabitants, nor Thanak nor its daughter towns, nor those dwelling in Dor nor its daughter towns, nor the one dwelling in Balak nor its surrounding inhabitants nor its daughter towns, nor those dwelling in Magedo nor its surrounding inhabitants nor its daughter towns, nor those dwelling in Ieblaam nor its surrounding inhabitants nor its daughter towns; and the Canaanite began to dwell in this land.
2 Judges 1:28 And it happened when Israel grew strong that he made the Canaanite tribute, and in removing him he did not remove him.
2 Judges 1:29 And Ephraim did not remove the Canaanite dwelling in Gazer; and the Canaanite dwelt in his midst in Gazer and became tribute.
2 Judges 1:30 And Zabulon did not remove those dwelling in Kedron nor those dwelling in Domana; and the Canaanite dwelt in their midst and became tribute for him.
2 Judges 1:31 And Aser did not remove those dwelling in Akcho, and it became tribute for him, nor those dwelling in Dor and those dwelling in Sidon and those dwelling in Aalaph and Aschazi and Chelba and Nai and Ereo.
2 Judges 1:32 And Aser dwelt in the midst of the Canaanite dwelling in the land, because he was unable to remove him.
2 Judges 1:33 And Nephthali did not remove those dwelling in Baithsamys and those dwelling in Baithanath, and Nephthali dwelt in the midst of the Canaanite dwelling in the land; but those dwelling in Baithsamys and Baitheneth became tribute for them.
2 Judges 1:34 And the Amorite pressed the sons of Dan into the mountain, because they did not allow him to go down into the valley.
2 Judges 1:35 And the Amorite began to dwell in the sherd-like mountain, where the bears were and where the foxes were, in Myrsinon and in Thalabin; and the hand of the house of Joseph was heavy upon the Amorite, and he became tribute for them.
2 Judges 1:36 And the boundary of the Amorite was from the ascent of Akrabin, from the Rock and upward.

## Chapter 2

2 Judges 2:1 And an angel of the Lord went up from Galgal to Klauchmon and to Bethel and to the house of Israel and said to them: Thus says the Lord: I brought you up from Egypt and brought you into the land which I swore to your fathers, and I said: I will not scatter my covenant with you forever;
2 Judges 2:2 and you shall not make a covenant with those settled in this land nor bow down to their gods, but you shall shatter their carved images and pull down their altars. And you did not listen to my voice, because you did these things.
2 Judges 2:3 And I said: I will certainly not remove them from before you, and they will be constraints for you, and their gods will be a stumbling block for you.
2 Judges 2:4 And it happened when the angel of the Lord spoke these words to all the sons of Israel that the people raised their voice and wept.
2 Judges 2:5 And they named that place Weepings; and they sacrificed there to the Lord.
2 Judges 2:6 And Jesus sent the people away, and each man came to his inheritance to inherit the land.
2 Judges 2:7 And the people served the Lord all the days of Jesus and all the days of the elders who lived long after Jesus, who knew all the great work of the Lord which he did in Israel.
2 Judges 2:8 And Jesus son of Naue, servant of the Lord, died at one hundred and ten years of age.
2 Judges 2:9 And they buried him within the boundary of his inheritance in Thamnathares in Mount Ephraim to the north of Mount Gaas.
2 Judges 2:10 And indeed all that generation were added to their fathers, and another generation arose after them who did not know the Lord nor indeed the work which he did in Israel.
2 Judges 2:11 And the sons of Israel did evil before the Lord and served the Baalim.
2 Judges 2:12 And they abandoned the Lord the God of their fathers who brought them out of the land of Egypt and went after other gods from the gods of the nations around them and bowed down to them and provoked the Lord to anger,
2 Judges 2:13 and they abandoned him and served Baal and the Astartes.
2 Judges 2:14 And the Lord was angry in wrath with Israel and delivered them into the hands of plunderers, and they plundered them thoroughly; and he sold them into the hands of their enemies round about, and they were no longer able to stand before their enemies.
2 Judges 2:15 In all the things in which they went out, the hand of the Lord was upon them for evils, as the Lord spoke and as the Lord swore to them, and he pressed them very hard.
2 Judges 2:16 And the Lord raised up judges, and the Lord saved them from the hand of those plundering them.
2 Judges 2:17 And even the judges they did not obey, because they went whoring after other gods and bowed down to them; and they turned aside quickly from the way in which their fathers walked to listen to the words of the Lord; they did not do thus.
2 Judges 2:18 And because the Lord raised up judges for them, the Lord was with the judge and saved them from the hand of their enemies all the days of the judge, because the Lord was moved by their groaning before those besieging them and pressing them.
2 Judges 2:19 And it happened when the judge died that they turned back and again acted more corruptly than their fathers, going after other gods to serve them and bow down to them; they did not cast aside their practices and their hard ways.
2 Judges 2:20 And the Lord was angry in wrath with Israel and said: Because this nation abandoned my covenant which I commanded their fathers and did not listen to my voice,
2 Judges 2:21 I too will no longer continue to remove a man from before them from the nations which Jesus son of Naue left in the land and allowed to remain,
2 Judges 2:22 to test Israel by them, whether they keep the way of the Lord to walk in it as their fathers kept it, or not.
2 Judges 2:23 And the Lord allowed these nations to remain, not removing them quickly, and did not deliver them into the hand of Jesus.

## Chapter 3

2 Judges 3:1 And these are the nations which the Lord allowed to remain so as to test Israel by them, all those who had not known the wars of Canaan,
2 Judges 3:2 except on account of the generations of the sons of Israel to teach them war, except that those before them had not known them;
2 Judges 3:3 the five satrapies of the foreigners and all the Canaanite and the Sidonian and the Euaite dwelling in Lebanon from Mount Aermon as far as Labohamath.
2 Judges 3:4 And it happened so as to test Israel by them, to know whether they would listen to the commandments of the Lord which he commanded their fathers by the hand of Moses.
2 Judges 3:5 And the sons of Israel dwelt among the Canaanite and the Chettite and the Amorite and the Pherezite and the Euaite and the Iebusite,
2 Judges 3:6 and took their daughters for themselves as wives and gave their daughters to their sons and served their gods.
2 Judges 3:7 And the sons of Israel did evil before the Lord and forgot the Lord their God and served the Baalim and the groves.
2 Judges 3:8 And the Lord was angry in wrath with Israel and sold them into the hand of Chousarsathaim king of Syria of the Rivers. And the sons of Israel served Chousarsathaim eight years.
2 Judges 3:9 And the sons of Israel cried out to the Lord; and the Lord raised up a savior for Israel and saved them, Gothoniel son of Kenez brother of Chaleb, younger than he,
2 Judges 3:10 and a spirit of the Lord came upon him, and he judged Israel and went out to war against Chousarsathaim; and the Lord delivered Chousarsathaim king of Syria of the Rivers into his hand, and his hand became strong against Chousarsathaim.
2 Judges 3:11 And the land was quiet forty years; and Gothoniel son of Kenez died.
2 Judges 3:12 And the sons of Israel again did evil before the Lord. And the Lord strengthened Eglom king of Moab against Israel because they had done evil before the Lord.
2 Judges 3:13 And he gathered to himself all the sons of Ammon and Amalek and went and struck Israel and inherited the city of palms.
2 Judges 3:14 And the sons of Israel served Eglom king of Moab eighteen years.
2 Judges 3:15 And the sons of Israel cried out to the Lord; and he raised up for them a savior, Aod son of Gera son of the Iemeni, a man right-handed on both sides. And the sons of Israel sent gifts by his hand to Eglom king of Moab.
2 Judges 3:16 And Aod made for himself a double-edged knife, a span in its length, and girded it under the cloak on his right thigh.
2 Judges 3:17 And he went and brought the gifts to Eglom king of Moab; and Eglom was a very handsome man.
2 Judges 3:18 And it happened when Aod finished bringing the gifts, he sent away those carrying the gifts;
2 Judges 3:19 and he himself returned from the carved images by Galgal. And Aod said, I have a secret word for you, O king. And Eglom said to him, Be silent; and he sent away from himself all those attending him.
2 Judges 3:20 And Aod entered to him, and he was sitting in his summer upper room, by himself alone. And Aod said, I have a word of God for you, O king; and Eglom rose from the throne near him.
2 Judges 3:21 And it happened as he rose that Aod stretched out his left hand and took the knife from above his right thigh and thrust it into his belly.
2 Judges 3:22 And he drove in even the handle after the blade, and the fat closed over the blade, for he did not draw the knife out of his belly. And Aod went out to the porch
2 Judges 3:23 and went out past those stationed there and shut the doors of the upper room upon him and wedged them shut;
2 Judges 3:24 and he went out. And his servants entered and saw, and behold, the doors of the upper room were wedged shut, and they said, Perhaps he is emptying his feet in the summer chamber?
2 Judges 3:25 And they waited until they were ashamed, and behold, there was no one opening the doors of the upper room; and they took the key and opened, and behold, their lord had fallen upon the ground, dead.
2 Judges 3:26 And Aod escaped while they were in confusion, and there was no one taking notice of him; and he passed the carved images and escaped to Setirotha.
2 Judges 3:27 And it happened when Aod came to the land of Israel that he sounded a horn in the hill country of Ephraim; and the sons of Israel came down with him from the mountain, and he was before them.
2 Judges 3:28 And he said to them, Come down after me, for the Lord God has delivered our enemies, Moab, into our hand. And they came down after him and seized beforehand the crossings of the Jordan belonging to Moab, and he did not permit a man to cross.
2 Judges 3:29 And they struck Moab on that day, about ten thousand men, every stout man and every man of strength, and no man escaped.
2 Judges 3:30 And Moab was put to shame on that day under the hand of Israel, and the land rested eighty years, and Aod judged them until he died.
2 Judges 3:31 And after him Samegar son of Dinach arose and struck the foreigners, six hundred men, with the oxgoad; and he too saved Israel.

## Chapter 4

2 Judges 4:1 And the sons of Israel continued to do evil before the Lord; and Aod died.
2 Judges 4:2 And the Lord gave them over into the hand of Jabin king of Canaan, who reigned in Asor; and the commander of his force was Sisara, and he dwelt in Arisoth of the nations.
2 Judges 4:3 And the sons of Israel cried out to the Lord, for he had nine hundred iron chariots, and he oppressed Israel with force for twenty years.
2 Judges 4:4 And Debbora, a woman, a prophetess, wife of Laphidoth, judged Israel at that time.
2 Judges 4:5 And she sat under the palm tree of Debbora between Rama and Bethel in the hill country of Ephraim, and the sons of Israel went up to her for judgment.
2 Judges 4:6 And Debbora sent and called Barak son of Abineem from Kades of Nephthali and said to him, Did not the Lord God of Israel command you, And you shall go to Mount Thabor and take with yourself ten thousand men from the sons of Nephthali and from the sons of Zabulon?
2 Judges 4:7 And I will bring to you, to the torrent Kison, Sisara the commander of Jabin's force and his chariots and his multitude, and I will deliver him into your hands.
2 Judges 4:8 And Barak said to her, If you go with me, I will go, and if you do not go, I will not go; for I do not know the day on which the Lord prospers the angel with me.
2 Judges 4:9 And she said, Going, I will go with you; nevertheless know that your preeminence will not be upon the way in which you go, for into a woman's hand the Lord will deliver Sisara. And Debbora rose and went with Barak from Kades.
2 Judges 4:10 And Barak summoned Zabulon and Nephthali from Kades, and ten thousand men went up at his feet; and Debbora went up with him.
2 Judges 4:11 And Chaber the Kenite had separated from Kain, from the sons of Iobab, Moses' father-in-law, and pitched his tent as far as the oak of those seeking advantage, which is near Kedes.
2 Judges 4:12 And it was reported to Sisara that Barak son of Abineem had gone up to Mount Thabor.
2 Judges 4:13 And Sisara summoned all his chariots, nine hundred iron chariots, and all the people with him, from Arisoth of the nations to the torrent Kison.
