2 Judges 4:14 And Debbora said to Barak, Rise, for this is the day on which the Lord has delivered Sisara into your hand, for the Lord will go out before you. And Barak went down from Mount Thabor, and ten thousand men after him.
2 Judges 4:15 And the Lord threw Sisara and all his chariots and all his camp into confusion by the edge of the sword before Barak; and Sisara came down from upon his chariot and fled on his feet.
2 Judges 4:16 And Barak pursued after the chariots and after the camp as far as Arisoth of the nations; and all the camp of Sisara fell by the edge of the sword, not one was left.
2 Judges 4:17 And Sisara fled on his feet to the tent of Jael, wife of Chaber, companion of the Kenite, for there was peace between Jabin king of Asor and the house of Chaber the Kenite.
2 Judges 4:18 And Jael went out to meet Sisara and said to him, Turn aside, my lord, turn aside to me; do not fear. And he turned aside to her into the tent, and she covered him with a covering.
2 Judges 4:19 And Sisara said to her, Give me, please, a little water to drink, for I am thirsty. And she opened the skin of milk and gave him drink and covered him.
2 Judges 4:20 And Sisara said to her, Stand, please, at the door of the tent, and it shall be, if a man comes to you and asks you and says, Is there a man here? then you shall say, There is not.
2 Judges 4:21 And Jael wife of Chaber took the tent peg and put the hammer in her hand and entered to him secretly and drove the peg into his temple, and it passed through into the ground; and he, being beside himself, grew dark and died.
2 Judges 4:22 And behold, Barak was pursuing Sisara, and Jael went out to meet him and said to him, Come and I will show you the man whom you seek. And he entered to her, and behold, Sisara was cast down dead, and the peg was in his temple.
2 Judges 4:23 And God routed Jabin king of Canaan on that day before the sons of Israel.
2 Judges 4:24 And the hand of the sons of Israel went on, going and growing hard against Jabin king of Canaan, until they utterly destroyed Jabin king of Canaan.

## Chapter 5

2 Judges 5:1 And Debbora and Barak son of Abineem sang on that day, saying,
2 Judges 5:2 A covering was uncovered in Israel; when the people volunteered, bless the Lord.
2 Judges 5:3 Hear, kings, and give ear, satraps; I am for the Lord, I am, I will sing, I will make music to the Lord, the God of Israel.
2 Judges 5:4 Lord, when you went out in Seir, when you departed from the field of Edom, the earth shook, and the heaven dripped dews, and the clouds dripped water;
2 Judges 5:5 mountains were shaken before the Lord Eloi, this Sinai before the Lord God of Israel.
2 Judges 5:6 In the days of Samegar son of Anath, in the days of Jael, roads ceased, and they traveled paths, they traveled crooked roads;
2 Judges 5:7 strong ones ceased in Israel, they ceased, until Debbora arose, until a mother arose in Israel.
2 Judges 5:8 They chose new gods; then cities of rulers fought; if a shield and spear should be seen among forty thousand in Israel.
2 Judges 5:9 My heart is toward those appointed in Israel; those volunteering among the people, bless the Lord.
2 Judges 5:10 You who ride upon a female donkey of midday, who sit upon a judgment seat, and who travel upon roads of councilors on the way,
2 Judges 5:11 tell of it from the voice of those striking up among those drawing water; there they will give righteous acts to the Lord, righteous acts, increase in Israel. Then the Lord's people went down to the cities.
2 Judges 5:12 Awake, awake, Debbora, awake, awake, speak a song; rise, Barak, and take captive your captivity, son of Abineem.
2 Judges 5:13 Then a remnant went down to the strong; the Lord's people went down to him among the mighty.
2 Judges 5:14 From me Ephraim rooted them out in Amalek; after you, Benjamin, among your peoples. With me from Machir came down searchers, and from Zabulon those drawing with a scribe's rod of narration.
2 Judges 5:15 And leaders in Issachar were with Debbora and Barak; so Barak sent into the valleys at his feet. In the divisions of Reuben there were great reachings of heart.
2 Judges 5:16 Why did they sit among the twofold allotment to hear the whistling of messengers? In the divisions of Reuben there were great examinations of heart.
2 Judges 5:17 Galaad encamped beyond the Jordan; and Dan, why does he sojourn by ships? Aser sat on the seacoast and will encamp at his outlets.
2 Judges 5:18 Zabulon is a people who reproached his soul unto death, and Nephthali upon the heights of the field.
2 Judges 5:19 Their kings came, they drew up for battle; then kings of Canaan fought in Thanaach by the water of Megeddo; they took no gift of silver.
2 Judges 5:20 From heaven the stars drew up for battle; from their paths they drew up against Sisara.
2 Judges 5:21 The torrent Kison swept them away, the torrent of ancient ones, the torrent Kison; my mighty soul will trample him.
2 Judges 5:22 Then the heels of a horse were impeded; with haste his mighty ones hastened.
2 Judges 5:23 Curse Meroz, said an angel of the Lord; curse, utterly accursed is everyone dwelling in it, for they did not come to the Lord's aid, to aid among the mighty.
2 Judges 5:24 May Jael wife of Chaber the Kenite be blessed among women; above women in tents may she be blessed.
2 Judges 5:25 He asked for water; she gave milk; in a basin of those who excel she brought butter.
2 Judges 5:26 Her left hand she stretched toward the peg and her right toward the hammer of those who toil; and she hammered Sisara, nailed through his head and struck, nailed through his temple.
2 Judges 5:27 Between her feet he rolled down, fell and slept; between her feet, reclining, he fell; as he reclined, there he fell, spent.
2 Judges 5:28 Through the window the mother of Sisara peered out beyond the lattice: Why was his chariot ashamed? Why have the feet of his chariots delayed?
2 Judges 5:29 Her wise ruling women answered her, and she herself returned her words to herself:
2 Judges 5:30 Will they not find him dividing spoils? A merciful one will show mercy for the head of a man; spoils of dyed fabrics for Sisara, spoils of dyed fabrics of embroidery, embroidered dyed fabrics themselves, spoils for his neck.
2 Judges 5:31 Thus may all your enemies perish, Lord; and those who love him are like the going forth of the sun in its strength. And the land rested forty years.

## Chapter 6

2 Judges 6:1 And the sons of Israel did evil before the Lord, and the Lord gave them into the hand of Madiam for seven years.
2 Judges 6:2 And the hand of Madiam grew strong over Israel; and the sons of Israel made for themselves, because of Madiam, the holes in the mountains and the caves and the hanging places.
2 Judges 6:3 And it happened whenever the sons of Israel sowed, Madiam and Amalek came up, and the sons of the east came up with them;
2 Judges 6:4 and they encamped against them and destroyed their crops as far as Gaza, and left no means of life in the land of Israel, nor among the flocks an ox and a donkey;
2 Judges 6:5 for they and their possessions came up, and their tents arrived like a multitude of locusts, and there was no number for them and their camels, and they came into the land of Israel and destroyed it.
2 Judges 6:6 And Israel was very impoverished because of Madiam, and the sons of Israel cried out to the Lord
2 Judges 6:7 because of Madiam.
2 Judges 6:8 And the Lord sent a man, a prophet, to the sons of Israel, and he said to them, Thus says the Lord God of Israel: I am he who brought you up from the land of Egypt and led you out from your house of slavery
2 Judges 6:9 and delivered you from the hand of Egypt and from the hand of all who oppressed you, and cast them out before you and gave you their land,
2 Judges 6:10 and said to you, I am the Lord your God; you shall not fear the gods of the Amorite, among whom you will dwell in their land. And you did not listen to my voice.
2 Judges 6:11 And an angel of the Lord came and sat under the terebinth in Ephratha belonging to Ioas father of Esdri, and Gedeon his son was beating wheat in a winepress to escape from Madiam.
2 Judges 6:12 And the angel of the Lord appeared to him and said to him, The Lord is with you, mighty one of forces.
2 Judges 6:13 And Gedeon said to him, In me, my lord, and if the Lord is with us, why have these evils found us? And where are all his wonders which our fathers recounted to us, saying, Did not the Lord bring us up out of Egypt? And now he has cast us off and given us into the hand of Madiam.
2 Judges 6:14 And the angel of the Lord turned to him and said, Go in this strength of yours and save Israel from the hand of Madiam; behold, I have sent you.
2 Judges 6:15 And Gedeon said to him, In me, my lord, by what shall I save Israel? Behold, my thousand has become weak in Manasse, and I am the least in my father's house.
2 Judges 6:16 And the angel of the Lord said to him, The Lord will be with you, and you shall strike Madiam as one man.
2 Judges 6:17 And Gedeon said to him, But if I have found mercy in your eyes, then you will do for me today all that you have spoken with me;
2 Judges 6:18 do not depart from here until I come to you, and I will bring out the sacrifice and set it before you. And he said, I will sit until you return.
2 Judges 6:19 And Gedeon went in and prepared a kid of the goats and unleavened bread from an ephah of flour, and put the meat in a basket and poured the broth into a pot and brought them out to him under the terebinth and came near.
2 Judges 6:20 And the angel of God said to him, Take the meat and the unleavened bread and place them by that rock and pour out the broth beside it; and he did so.
2 Judges 6:21 And the angel of the Lord extended the tip of the staff in his hand and touched the meat and the unleavened bread, and fire rose up from the rock and consumed the meat and the unleavened bread; and the angel of the Lord went from his sight.
2 Judges 6:22 And Gedeon saw that this was an angel of the Lord, and Gedeon said, Ah, ah, my lord Lord, for I have seen an angel of the Lord face to face.
2 Judges 6:23 And the Lord said to him, Peace to you; do not fear; you shall certainly not die.
2 Judges 6:24 And Gedeon built an altar there to the Lord and called it Peace of the Lord; to this day it is still in Ephratha of the father of Esdri.
2 Judges 6:25 And it happened on that night that the Lord said to him, Take the calf, the bull that belongs to your father, and a second calf, seven years old, and you shall tear down the altar of Baal that belongs to your father, and destroy the grove upon it;
2 Judges 6:26 and you shall build an altar to the Lord your God upon the summit of this Maouek in the array, and take the second calf and offer a whole burnt offering with the wood of the grove which you shall destroy.
2 Judges 6:27 And Gedeon took ten men from his servants and did as the Lord had spoken to him; and it happened that, because he feared his father's house and the men of the city to do it by day, he did it by night.
2 Judges 6:28 And the men of the city rose early in the morning, and behold, the altar of Baal had been torn down and the grove upon it destroyed; and they saw the second calf which he had offered upon the altar that had been built.
2 Judges 6:29 And each man said to his neighbor, Who did this thing? And they sought and investigated and learned that Gedeon son of Ioas had done this thing.
2 Judges 6:30 And the men of the city said to Ioas, Bring out your son, and let him die, because he tore down Baal's altar and destroyed the grove upon it.
2 Judges 6:31 And Ioas said to all the men who rose against him, Are you now pleading on behalf of Baal? Or will you save him? Whoever pleads for him, let him be put to death by morning; if he is a god, let him plead for himself, because he tore down his altar.
2 Judges 6:32 And he called him Iarbaal on that day, saying, Let Baal plead against him, because his altar was torn down.
2 Judges 6:33 And all Madiam and Amalek and the sons of the east assembled together and encamped in the valley of Ezreel.
2 Judges 6:34 And the spirit of the Lord strengthened Gedeon, and he sounded a horn, and Abiezer was afraid behind him.
2 Judges 6:35 And he sent messengers into all Manasse and into Aser and into Zabulon and Nephthali, and he went up to meet them.
2 Judges 6:36 And Gedeon said to God, If you save Israel by my hand, as you have spoken,
2 Judges 6:37 behold, I am placing the fleece of wool on the threshing floor; if dew comes upon the fleece alone and dryness upon all the ground, I shall know that you will save Israel by my hand, as you have spoken.
2 Judges 6:38 And it happened thus; and he rose early on the next day and squeezed the fleece, and dew dripped from the fleece, a full basin of water.
2 Judges 6:39 And Gedeon said to God, Let your anger, please, not be kindled against me, and I shall speak once more; and I shall make trial once more with the fleece: let dryness come upon the fleece alone, and upon all the ground let there be dew.
2 Judges 6:40 And God did thus on that night, and there was dryness upon the fleece alone, and upon all the ground there was dew.

## Chapter 7

2 Judges 7:1 And Iarbal [that is Gedeon] and all the people with him rose early and encamped by the spring of Arad, and the camp of Madiam was to his north from Gabaath Amora in the valley.
2 Judges 7:2 And the Lord said to Gedeon, The people with you are too many for me to deliver Madiam into their hand, lest Israel boast against me, saying, My hand saved me;
2 Judges 7:3 and now speak, please, in the ears of the people, saying, Who is fearful and timid? Let him return and withdraw from Mount Galaad. And twenty-two thousand returned from the people, and ten thousand remained.
2 Judges 7:4 And the Lord said to Gedeon, The people are still many; bring them down to the water, and I shall sift them for you there; and it shall be that whoever I say to you, This one shall go with you, he shall go with you; and anyone of whom I say to you, This one shall not go with you, he shall not go with you.
2 Judges 7:5 And he brought the people down to the water; and the Lord said to Gedeon, Everyone who laps with his tongue from the water as a dog laps, you shall set him apart, and everyone who bends upon his knees to drink.
2 Judges 7:6 And the number of those who lapped with their hand to their mouth was three hundred men, and all the rest of the people bent upon their knees to drink water.
2 Judges 7:7 And the Lord said to Gedeon, With the three hundred men who lapped I will save you and give Madiam into your hand, and all the people shall go, each man to his place.
2 Judges 7:8 And they took the people's provisions in their hand and their horns, and he sent every man of Israel away, each to his tent, and kept the three hundred men. And the camp of Madiam was below him in the valley.
2 Judges 7:9 And it happened on that night that the Lord said to him, Rise and go down into the camp, for I have delivered it into your hand;
2 Judges 7:10 and if you fear to go down, go down, you and Phara your servant, into the camp
2 Judges 7:11 and hear what they will say; and after this your hands will grow strong, and you will go down into the camp. And he and Phara his servant went down toward the beginning of the fifty who were in the camp.
2 Judges 7:12 And Madiam and Amalek and all the sons of the east were spread out in the valley like locusts in multitude, and their camels had no number, but were like sand upon the seashore in multitude.
2 Judges 7:13 And Gedeon came, and behold, a man was telling a dream to his neighbor and said, Behold, I dreamed a dream, and behold, a cake of barley bread rolled in the camp of Madiam and came as far as the tent and struck it, and it fell, and turned it upward, and the tent fell.
2 Judges 7:14 And his neighbor answered and said, This is nothing other than the sword of Gedeon son of Ioas, a man of Israel; God has delivered Madiam and all the camp into his hand.
2 Judges 7:15 And it happened when Gedeon heard the account of the dream and its interpretation that he bowed down to the Lord and returned to the camp of Israel and said, Rise, for the Lord has delivered the camp of Madiam into our hand.
2 Judges 7:16 And he divided the three hundred men into three companies and gave horns into everyone's hand and empty jars and torches in the jars
2 Judges 7:17 and said to them, Watch me, and thus you shall do; and behold, I am entering at the edge of the camp, and it shall be that as I do, so shall you do;
2 Judges 7:18 and I shall sound the horn, I and all with me; sound your horns around the whole camp and say, For the Lord and for Gedeon.
2 Judges 7:19 And Gedeon and the hundred men with him entered at the edge of the camp at the beginning of the middle watch, and, rousing, they roused the guards and sounded the horns and shook out the jars in their hands.
2 Judges 7:20 And the three companies sounded the horns and broke the jars and held the torches in their left hands and the horns for sounding in their right hands and cried out, A sword for the Lord and for Gedeon.
2 Judges 7:21 And each man stood in his place around the camp, and all the camp ran and signaled and fled.
2 Judges 7:22 And they sounded the three hundred horns, and the Lord set each man's sword against his neighbor throughout the camp, and the camp fled as far as Bethseedta Garagatha, as far as the edge of Abomeoula by Tabath.
2 Judges 7:23 And the men of Israel from Nephthali and from Aser and from all Manasse were summoned and pursued Madiam.
2 Judges 7:24 And Gedeon sent messengers throughout all the hill country of Ephraim, saying, Come down to meet Madiam and seize the water for yourselves as far as Baithera and the Jordan; and every man of Ephraim was summoned, and they seized the water beforehand as far as Baithera and the Jordan.
2 Judges 7:25 And they captured the rulers of Madiam, Oreb and Zeb, and killed Oreb at Sour and killed Zeb at Iakephzeph and pursued Madiam; and they brought the heads of Oreb and Zeb to Gedeon from beyond the Jordan.

## Chapter 8

2 Judges 8:1 And the men of Ephraim said to Gedeon, What is this thing you have done to us, not calling us when you went to fight against Madiam? And they disputed with him strongly.
2 Judges 8:2 And he said to them, What have I done now compared with you? Is not Ephraim's gleaning better than Abiezer's harvest?
2 Judges 8:3 Into your hand the Lord delivered the rulers of Madiam, Oreb and Zeb; and what was I able to do like you? Then their spirit relaxed toward him when he spoke this word.
2 Judges 8:4 And Gedeon came to the Jordan, and he and the three hundred men with him crossed, hungry and pursuing.
2 Judges 8:5 And he said to the men of Sokchoth, Give, please, loaves for food to this people at my feet, for they are failing, and behold, I am pursuing Zebee and Selmana, kings of Madiam.
2 Judges 8:6 And the rulers of Sokchoth said, Are the hands of Zebee and Selmana now in your hand? We shall not give loaves to your force.
2 Judges 8:7 And Gedeon said, Therefore when the Lord gives Zebee and Selmana into my hand, I shall thresh your flesh with the thorns of the wilderness and with the abarkenin.
2 Judges 8:8 And he went up from there to Phanouel and spoke to them likewise, and the men of Phanouel answered him as the men of Sokchoth had answered.
2 Judges 8:9 And Gedeon said to the men of Phanouel, When I return in peace I shall tear down this tower. –
2 Judges 8:10 And Zebee and Selmana were in Karkar, and their camp with them, about fifteen thousand, all those left from the whole camp of the foreigners; and those who had fallen were a hundred and twenty thousand men drawing a sword.
2 Judges 8:11 And Gedeon went up by the road of those dwelling in tents east of Nabai and Iegebal; and he struck the camp, while the camp was confident.
2 Judges 8:12 And Zebee and Selmana fled, and he pursued them and seized the two kings of Madiam, Zebee and Selmana, and threw the whole camp into confusion. –
2 Judges 8:13 And Gedeon son of Ioas returned from the battle from above the battle line of Ares.
2 Judges 8:14 And he captured a young man of the men of Sokchoth and questioned him, and he wrote for him the names of the rulers of Sokchoth and their elders, seventy-seven men.
2 Judges 8:15 And Gedeon came to the rulers of Sokchoth and said, Behold Zebee and Selmana, concerning whom you reproached me, saying, Are the hands of Zebee and Selmana now in your hand, that we should give loaves to the men who are failing?
2 Judges 8:16 And he took the elders of the city with the thorns of the wilderness and the barakenim and threshed the men of the city with them.
2 Judges 8:17 And he tore down the tower of Phanouel and killed the men of the city. –
2 Judges 8:18 And he said to Zebee and Selmana, Where are the men whom you killed in Thabor? And they said, Like you, so were they, in the likeness of a king's son.
2 Judges 8:19 And Gedeon said, They were my brothers and sons of my mother; as the Lord lives, if you had kept them alive, I would not have killed you.
2 Judges 8:20 And he said to Iether his firstborn, Rise and kill them; and the young man did not draw his sword, for he was afraid, for he was still younger.
2 Judges 8:21 And Zebee and Selmana said, Rise yourself and fall upon us, for your strength is as a man's. And Gedeon rose and killed Zebee and Selmana and took the crescents on the necks of their camels.
2 Judges 8:22 And the men of Israel said to Gedeon, Lord, rule us, both you and your son, for you saved us from the hand of Madiam.
2 Judges 8:23 And Gedeon said to them, I shall not rule, and my son shall not rule among you; the Lord shall rule you.
2 Judges 8:24 And Gedeon said to them, I shall ask a request of you: each man give me an earring from his spoils; for they had gold earrings, for they were Ishmaelites.
2 Judges 8:25 And they said, Giving, we shall give; and he spread out his cloak, and each man cast there an earring from his spoils.
2 Judges 8:26 And the weight of the gold earrings which he asked for was a thousand and five hundred gold pieces, apart from the crescents and the necklaces and the garments and purple garments upon the kings of Madiam, and besides the ornaments on the necks of their camels.
2 Judges 8:27 And Gedeon made it into an ephod and set it up in his city, Ephratha; and all Israel went whoring after it there, and it became a stumbling block to Gedeon and his house.
2 Judges 8:28 And Madiam was brought low before the sons of Israel and did not again lift up its head. And the land rested forty years in the days of Gedeon. –
2 Judges 8:29 And Ierobaal son of Ioas went and dwelt in his house.
2 Judges 8:30 And Gedeon had seventy sons who came forth from his thighs, for he had many wives.
2 Judges 8:31 And his concubine was in Sychem; and she too bore him a son, and he gave him the name Abimelech.
2 Judges 8:32 And Gedeon son of Ioas died in his city and was buried in the tomb of Ioas his father in Ephratha of Abiesdri.
2 Judges 8:33 And it happened when Gedeon died that the sons of Israel turned back and went whoring after the Baals, and they made Baal of the covenant their god.
2 Judges 8:34 And the sons of Israel did not remember the Lord God who had delivered them from the hand of all those oppressing them all around.
2 Judges 8:35 And they did not show mercy to the house of Ierobaal [that is Gedeon] according to all the good that he had done with Israel.

## Chapter 9

2 Judges 9:1 And Abimelech son of Ierobaal went to Sychem to his mother's brothers and spoke to them and to all the kin of his mother's father's house, saying,
2 Judges 9:2 Speak, please, in the ears of all the men of Sychem: What is better for you, that seventy men, all sons of Ierobaal, rule you, or that one man rule you? And remember that I am your bone and your flesh.
2 Judges 9:3 And his mother's brothers spoke concerning him in the ears of all the men of Sychem all these words, and their heart inclined after Abimelech, for they said, He is our brother.
2 Judges 9:4 And they gave him seventy pieces of silver from the house of Baalberith, and Abimelech hired for himself empty and timid men, and they went after him.
2 Judges 9:5 And he entered his father's house in Ephratha and killed his brothers, the sons of Ierobaal, seventy men, upon one stone; and Ioathan son of Ierobaal, the youngest, was left, for he hid.
2 Judges 9:6 And all the men of Sikimoi and all the house of Bethmaalon gathered and went and made Abimelech king beside the oak that was found by the standing place in Sikimoi.
2 Judges 9:7 And it was reported to Ioathan, and he went and stood upon the summit of Mount Garizin and raised his voice and wept and said to them, Hear me, men of Sikimoi, and God will hear you.
2 Judges 9:8 Going, the trees went to anoint a king over themselves and said to the olive tree, Reign over us.
2 Judges 9:9 And the olive tree said to them, Shall I leave my richness, by which men glorify God, and go to sway over the trees?
2 Judges 9:10 And the trees said to the fig tree, Come, reign over us.
2 Judges 9:11 And the fig tree said to them, Shall I leave my sweetness and my good produce and go to sway over the trees?
2 Judges 9:12 And the trees said to the vine, Come, you reign over us.
2 Judges 9:13 And the vine said to them, Shall I leave my wine, which gladdens God and men, and go to sway over the trees?
2 Judges 9:14 And all the trees said to the bramble, Come, you reign over us.
2 Judges 9:15 And the bramble said to the trees, If in truth you anoint me to reign over you, come and stand in my shade; but if not, may fire go out from me and consume the cedars of Lebanon. –
2 Judges 9:16 And now, if in truth and integrity you acted and made Abimelech king, and if you showed goodness to Ierobaal and to his house, and if you acted toward him according to the repayment of his hand,
2 Judges 9:17 – as my father fought for you and cast away his life in opposition and delivered you from the hand of Madiam,
2 Judges 9:18 and you rose against my father's house today and killed his sons, seventy men upon one stone, and made Abimelech, the son of his maidservant, king over the men of Sikimoi because he is your brother –
2 Judges 9:19 and if in truth and integrity you acted toward Ierobaal and his house on this day, may you rejoice in Abimelech, and may he too rejoice over you.
2 Judges 9:20 But if not, may fire come out from Abimelech and consume the men of Sikimoi and the house of Bethmaallon, and may fire come out from the men of Sikimoi and from the house of Bethmaallon and consume Abimelech. –
2 Judges 9:21 And Ioathan fled and escaped and went as far as Baier and lived there because of Abimelech his brother.
2 Judges 9:22 And Abimelech ruled over Israel for three years.
2 Judges 9:23 And God sent an evil spirit between Abimelech and the men of Sikimoi, and the men of Sikimoi dealt treacherously with the house of Abimelech,
2 Judges 9:24 to bring the injustice against the seventy sons of Ierobaal and lay their blood upon Abimelech their brother who killed them, and upon the men of Sikimoi because they strengthened his hands to kill his brothers.
2 Judges 9:25 And the men of Sikimoi set men in ambush for him on the mountain tops, and they plundered everyone passing by them on the road; and it was reported to King Abimelech.
2 Judges 9:26 And Gaal son of Iobel and his brothers came and passed into Sikimoi, and the men of Sikimoi put their hope in him.
2 Judges 9:27 And they went out into the field and harvested their vineyards and trod and made elloulim and brought them into the house of their god and ate and drank and cursed Abimelech.
2 Judges 9:28 And Gaal son of Iobel said, Who is Abimelech and who is the son of Sychem that we should serve him? Is he not a son of Ierobaal, and Zeboul his overseer his servant, with the men of Emmor father of Sychem? And why should we serve him?
2 Judges 9:29 And who would put this people in my hand? I would remove Abimelech and say to him, Increase your force and come out.
2 Judges 9:30 And Zeboul, ruler of the city, heard the words of Gaal son of Iobel and became angry with wrath.
2 Judges 9:31 And he sent messengers to Abimelech secretly, saying, Behold, Gaal son of Iobel and his brothers are coming to Sychem, and behold, they are besieging the city against you;
2 Judges 9:32 and now rise by night, you and the people with you, and lie in ambush in the field,
2 Judges 9:33 and it shall be in the morning, as the sun rises, rise early and spread out against the city, and behold, he and the people with him will come out to you, and you shall do to him whatever your hand finds.
2 Judges 9:34 And Abimelech and all the people with him rose by night and lay in ambush against Sychem in four companies.
2 Judges 9:35 And Gaal son of Iobel went out and stood by the door of the city gate, and Abimelech and the people with him rose from the ambush.
2 Judges 9:36 And Gaal son of Iobel saw the people and said to Zeboul, Behold, people are coming down from the mountain tops. And Zeboul said to him, You are seeing the shadow of the mountains as men.
2 Judges 9:37 And Gaal continued to speak and said, Behold, people are coming down toward the sea from near the navel of the land, and another company is coming by the road of Elonmaonenim.
2 Judges 9:38 And Zeboul said to him, And where is your mouth with which you said, Who is Abimelech, that we should serve him? Is this not the people whom you despised? Go out now, please, and fight him.
2 Judges 9:39 And Gaal went out before the men of Sychem and fought Abimelech.
2 Judges 9:40 And Abimelech pursued him, and he fled from him; and many wounded fell as far as the door of the gate.
2 Judges 9:41 And Abimelech entered Arema; and Zeboul drove out Gaal and his brothers so that they would not dwell in Sychem.
2 Judges 9:42 And it happened on the next day that the people went out into the field, and it was reported to Abimelech.
2 Judges 9:43 And he took the people and divided them into three companies and lay in ambush in the field; and he saw, and behold, the people came out of the city, and he rose against them and struck them.
2 Judges 9:44 And Abimelech and the leaders with him spread out and stood by the door of the city gate, and the two companies spread out against all those in the field and struck them.
2 Judges 9:45 And Abimelech fought in the city all that day and took the city and killed the people in it and tore down the city and sowed it with salt.
2 Judges 9:46 And all the men of the towers of Sychem heard and came to the assembly of Baithelberith.
2 Judges 9:47 And it was reported to Abimelech that all the men of the towers of Sychem had gathered.
2 Judges 9:48 And Abimelech and all the people with him went up Mount Hermon, and Abimelech took the axes in his hand and cut a branch of a tree and lifted it and set it on his shoulders and said to the people with him, What you have seen me doing, do quickly as I did.
2 Judges 9:49 And every man likewise cut a branch and went after Abimelech and put them against the assembly and set fire to the assembly over them; and all the men of the tower of Sikimoi died too, about a thousand men and women.
2 Judges 9:50 And Abimelech went from Baithelberith and encamped at Thebes and took it.
2 Judges 9:51 And a strong tower was in the middle of the city, and all the men and women of the city fled there and shut it from outside themselves and went up onto the roof of the tower.
2 Judges 9:52 And Abimelech came as far as the tower, and they drew up against him; and Abimelech approached as far as the tower door to burn it with fire.
2 Judges 9:53 And one woman threw a piece of an upper millstone onto Abimelech's head and broke his skull.
2 Judges 9:54 And he quickly called to the young man carrying his equipment and said to him, Draw my sword and put me to death, lest they say, A woman killed him. And his young man pierced him through, and he died.
2 Judges 9:55 And the men of Israel saw that Abimelech had died, and they went, each man to his place.
2 Judges 9:56 And God returned upon Abimelech the evil that he did to his father by killing his seventy brothers.
2 Judges 9:57 And God returned all the evil of the men of Sychem upon their heads, and the curse of Ioathan son of Ierobaal came upon them.

## Chapter 10

2 Judges 10:1 And after Abimelech Thola son of Phoua, son of his father's brother, a man of Issachar, arose to save Israel, and he dwelt in Samir in the hill country of Ephraim.
2 Judges 10:2 And he judged Israel twenty-three years and died and was buried in Samir.
2 Judges 10:3 And after him Iair the Galaadite arose and judged Israel twenty-two years.
2 Judges 10:4 And he had thirty-two sons riding on thirty-two colts; and they had thirty-two cities, and they called them the Hamlets of Iair to this day in the land of Galaad.
2 Judges 10:5 And Iair died and was buried in Ramnon.
2 Judges 10:6 And the sons of Israel continued to do evil before the Lord and served the Baals and the Astaroths and the gods of Arad and the gods of Sidon and the gods of Moab and the gods of the sons of Ammon and the gods of the Philistines and abandoned the Lord and did not serve him.
2 Judges 10:7 And the Lord became angry with wrath against Israel and gave them over into the hand of the Philistines and into the hand of the sons of Ammon.
2 Judges 10:8 And they oppressed and crushed the sons of Israel at that time for eighteen years, all the sons of Israel beyond the Jordan in the land of the Amorite in Galaad.
2 Judges 10:9 And the sons of Ammon crossed the Jordan to fight against Judah and Benjamin and Ephraim, and Israel was greatly oppressed.
2 Judges 10:10 And the sons of Israel cried out to the Lord, saying, We sinned against you, for we abandoned God and served the Baals.
2 Judges 10:11 And the Lord said to the sons of Israel, Did I not save you from Egypt and from the Amorite and from the sons of Ammon and from the Philistines
2 Judges 10:12 and the Sidonians and Amalek and Madiam, who oppressed you, when you cried out to me, and I saved you from their hand?
2 Judges 10:13 And you abandoned me and served other gods; therefore I will no longer save you.
2 Judges 10:14 Go and cry out to the gods whom you chose for yourselves, and let them save you in the time of your affliction.
2 Judges 10:15 And the sons of Israel said to the Lord, We sinned; do to us according to all that is good in your eyes, only rescue us on this day.
2 Judges 10:16 And they put aside the foreign gods from their midst and served the Lord alone, and his soul was shortened by Israel's toil.
2 Judges 10:17 And the sons of Ammon came up and encamped in Galaad, and the sons of Israel gathered and encamped in the lookout place.
2 Judges 10:18 And the people, the rulers of Galaad, said to one another, Who is the man who will begin to fight against the sons of Ammon? He shall be ruler over all who dwell in Galaad.

## Chapter 11

2 Judges 11:1 And Iephthae the Galaadite was exalted in strength; and he was the son of a prostitute, who bore Iephthae to Galaad.
2 Judges 11:2 And Galaad's wife bore him sons; and the sons of the wife grew up and drove out Iephthae and said to him, You shall not inherit in our father's house, for you are a son of a companion woman.
2 Judges 11:3 And Iephthae fled from his brothers and dwelt in the land of Tob, and empty men gathered to Iephthae and went out with him.
2 Judges 11:5 And it happened when the sons of Ammon fought against Israel that the elders of Galaad went to take Iephthae from the land of Tob
2 Judges 11:6 and said to Iephthae, Come and be our leader, and let us fight against the sons of Ammon.
2 Judges 11:7 And Iephthae said to the elders of Galaad, Was it not you who hated me and drove me from my father's house and sent me away from you? And why have you come to me now when you have need?
2 Judges 11:8 And the elders of Galaad said to Iephthae, For this reason we have now returned to you, and you shall go with us and fight against the sons of Ammon; and you shall be ruler for us, over all who dwell in Galaad.
2 Judges 11:9 And Iephthae said to the elders of Galaad, If you bring me back to fight against the sons of Ammon and the Lord delivers them before me, then I shall be ruler for you.
2 Judges 11:10 And the elders of Galaad said to Iephthae, Let the Lord be hearing between us if we do not act thus according to your word.
2 Judges 11:11 And Iephthae went with the elders of Galaad, and the people set him over them as head and leader. And Iephthae spoke all his words before the Lord in Massepha.
2 Judges 11:12 And Iephthae sent messengers to the king of the sons of Ammon, saying, What is there between me and you, that you came against me to fight in my land?
2 Judges 11:13 And the king of the sons of Ammon said to Iephthae's messengers, Because Israel took my land when he came up from Egypt, from Arnon as far as Iabok and as far as the Jordan; and now return those lands in peace, and I will go.
2 Judges 11:14 And Iephthae continued and sent messengers again to the king of the sons of Ammon
2 Judges 11:15 and said to him, Thus says Iephthae: Israel did not take the land of Moab or the land of the sons of Ammon.
2 Judges 11:16 For when they came up from Egypt, Israel traveled in the wilderness as far as the Sea of Siph and came to Kades.
2 Judges 11:17 And Israel sent messengers to the king of Edom, saying, Let me pass, please, through your land; and the king of Edom did not listen. And he sent to the king of Moab, and he did not consent. And Israel dwelt in Kades.
2 Judges 11:18 And he traveled in the wilderness and went around the land of Edom and the land of Moab and came from the east to the land of Moab and encamped beyond Arnon and did not enter the borders of Moab, for Arnon was the border of Moab.
2 Judges 11:19 And Israel sent messengers to Seon king of the Amorite, king of Esebon, and Israel said to him, Let us pass, please, through your land to our place.
2 Judges 11:20 And Seon did not trust Israel to pass through his territory; and Seon gathered all his people, and they encamped at Iasa, and he fought against Israel.
2 Judges 11:21 And the Lord God of Israel delivered Seon and all his people into the hand of Israel, and he struck him; and Israel inherited all the land of the Amorite who dwelt in that land,
2 Judges 11:22 from Arnon as far as Iabok and from the wilderness as far as the Jordan.
2 Judges 11:23 And now the Lord God of Israel has removed the Amorite from before his people Israel, and will you inherit him?
2 Judges 11:24 Will you not inherit whatever Chamos your god causes you to inherit? And all those whom the Lord our God has removed from before us, we shall inherit them.
2 Judges 11:25 And now are you in goodness better than Balak son of Sepphor, king of Moab? Did he contend in contention with Israel, or wage war against him in war?
2 Judges 11:26 During the three hundred years of dwelling in Esebon and its borders and in the land of Aroer and its borders and in all the cities along the Jordan, why did you not rescue them at that time?
2 Judges 11:27 And now I have not sinned against you, and you do evil to me by fighting against me; let the Lord, the judge, judge today between the sons of Israel and the sons of Ammon.
2 Judges 11:28 And the king of the sons of Ammon did not listen to the words of Iephthae which he sent to him.
2 Judges 11:29 And the spirit of the Lord came upon Iephthae, and he passed through Galaad and Manasse and passed through the lookout place of Galaad to the far side of the sons of Ammon.
2 Judges 11:30 And Iephthae vowed a vow to the Lord and said, If you indeed give the sons of Ammon into my hand,
2 Judges 11:31 then whoever comes out, who comes out from the door of my house to meet me when I return in peace from the sons of Ammon, shall be for the Lord; I shall offer him as a whole burnt offering.
2 Judges 11:32 And Iephthae passed over to the sons of Ammon to fight them, and the Lord delivered them into his hand.
2 Judges 11:33 And he struck them from Aroer as far as Arnon, twenty cities in number, and as far as Ebelcharmin with a very great blow, and the sons of Ammon were brought low before the sons of Israel.
2 Judges 11:34 And Iephthae came to his house in Massepha, and behold, his daughter was coming out to meet him with tambourines and dances; and she was an only child, and he had no other son or daughter.
2 Judges 11:35 And it happened when he saw her that he tore his garments and said, Ah, ah, my daughter, with trouble you have troubled me, and you were in my trouble, and I have opened my mouth against you to the Lord and cannot turn back.
2 Judges 11:36 And she said to him, Father, you opened your mouth to the Lord; do to me as it came out of your mouth, since the Lord has wrought vengeance for you upon your enemies, the sons of Ammon.
2 Judges 11:37 And she said this to her father: Let my father do this thing, please; leave me two months, and I will go and descend upon the mountains and weep over my virginity, I and my companions.
2 Judges 11:38 And he said, Go; and he sent her away for two months. And she went, she and her companions, and wept over her virginity upon the mountains.
2 Judges 11:39 And it happened at the end of the two months that she returned to her father, and he did to her his vow that he had vowed; and she had not known a man. And it became a statute in Israel:
2 Judges 11:40 from days to days the daughters of Israel went to lament the daughter of Iephthae of Galaad for four days in the year.

## Chapter 12

2 Judges 12:1 And the men of Ephraim were summoned and crossed to the north and said to Iephthae, Why did you cross to fight against the sons of Ammon and not call us to go with you? We shall burn your house over you with fire.
2 Judges 12:2 And Iephthae said to them, I and my people were men of battle, and the sons of Ammon greatly so; and I called you, and you did not save me from their hand.
2 Judges 12:3 And I saw that you were no savior, and I put my life in my hand and crossed to the sons of Ammon, and the Lord gave them into my hand; and why did you come up against me on this day to fight me?
2 Judges 12:4 And Iephthae gathered all the men of Galaad and fought Ephraim, and the men of Galaad struck Ephraim, because they said, You are the escaped ones of Ephraim, Galaad in the midst of Ephraim and in the midst of Manasse.
2 Judges 12:5 And Galaad seized beforehand the crossings of the Jordan belonging to Ephraim, and the escaped ones of Ephraim said to them, Let us cross, and the men of Galaad said to them, Are you an Ephrathite? And he said, No.
2 Judges 12:6 And they said to him, Say, please, Stachys; and he did not manage to say it thus. And they seized him and slaughtered him by the crossings of the Jordan, and forty-two thousand of Ephraim fell at that time.
2 Judges 12:7 And Iephthae judged Israel sixty years. And Iephthae the Galaadite died and was buried in his city in Galaad.
2 Judges 12:8 And after him Abaisan from Bethlehem judged Israel.
2 Judges 12:9 And he had thirty sons and thirty daughters whom he sent outside, and he brought thirty daughters from outside for his sons. And he judged Israel seven years.
2 Judges 12:10 And Abaisan died and was buried in Bethlehem.
2 Judges 12:11 And after him Ailom the Zabulonite judged Israel ten years.
2 Judges 12:12 And Ailom the Zabulonite died and was buried in Ailom in the land of Zabulon.
2 Judges 12:13 And after him Abdon son of Ellel the Pharathonite judged Israel.
2 Judges 12:14 And he had forty sons and thirty sons of sons, riding on seventy colts. And he judged Israel eight years.
2 Judges 12:15 And Abdon son of Ellel the Pharathonite died and was buried in Pharathom in the land of Ephraim, in the hill country of Amalek.

## Chapter 13

2 Judges 13:1 And the sons of Israel continued to do evil before the Lord, and the Lord delivered them into the hand of the Philistines for forty years.
2 Judges 13:2 And there was one man from Saraa, from a district of the kin of Dan, and his name was Manoe, and his wife was barren and had not borne.
2 Judges 13:3 And an angel of the Lord appeared to the woman and said to her, Behold, you are barren and have not borne; and you shall conceive a son.
2 Judges 13:4 And now take care, please, and do not drink wine or strong drink and do not eat anything unclean;
2 Judges 13:5 for behold, you have in your womb and shall bear a son, and iron shall not come up upon his head, for the child shall be a nazir of God from the womb, and he shall begin to save Israel from the hand of the Philistines.
2 Judges 13:6 And the woman went in and said to her husband, saying, A man of God came to me, and his appearance was like the appearance of an angel of God, very fearsome; and I did not ask him where he was from, and he did not tell me his name.
2 Judges 13:7 And he said to me, Behold, you have in your womb and shall bear a son; and now do not drink wine or strong drink and do not eat anything unclean, for the child shall be holy to God from the womb until the day of his death.
2 Judges 13:8 And Manoe prayed to the Lord and said, In me, Lord Adonaie, let the man of God whom you sent come again to us, please, and instruct us what we shall do for the child being born.
2 Judges 13:9 And God listened to the voice of Manoe, and the angel of God came again to the woman, and she sat in the field, and Manoe her husband was not with her.
2 Judges 13:10 And the woman hurried and ran and reported to her husband and said to him, Behold, the man who came to me on that day has appeared to me.
2 Judges 13:11 And Manoe rose and went after his wife and came to the man and said to him, Are you the man who spoke to the woman? And the angel said, I am.
2 Judges 13:12 And Manoe said, Now your word will come; what shall be the judgment of the child and his deeds?
2 Judges 13:13 And the angel of the Lord said to Manoe, From all that I have said to the woman she shall keep herself;
2 Judges 13:14 she shall not eat of anything that comes forth from the vine of wine, and she shall not drink wine or sikera, strong drink, and shall not eat anything unclean; everything that I commanded her she shall keep.
2 Judges 13:15 And Manoe said to the angel of the Lord, Let us keep you here and prepare a kid of the goats before you.
2 Judges 13:16 And the angel of the Lord said to Manoe, If you keep me, I shall not eat of your bread, and if you make a whole burnt offering, to the Lord you shall offer it; for Manoe did not know that he was an angel of the Lord.
2 Judges 13:17 And Manoe said to the angel of the Lord, What is your name? For when your word comes, we shall glorify you.
2 Judges 13:18 And the angel of the Lord said to him, Why do you ask this, my name? It is wondrous.
2 Judges 13:19 And Manoe took the kid of the goats and the sacrifice and offered it upon the rock to the Lord; and he made a distinction to act, while Manoe and his wife watched.
2 Judges 13:20 And it happened as the flame rose above the altar toward heaven that the angel of the Lord went up in the flame of the altar, and Manoe and his wife were watching and fell on their faces to the ground.
2 Judges 13:21 And the angel of the Lord did not again appear to Manoe and his wife; then Manoe knew that this was an angel of the Lord.
2 Judges 13:22 And Manoe said to his wife, By death we shall die, for we have seen God.
2 Judges 13:23 And his wife said to him, If the Lord wished to put us to death, he would not have taken from our hand a whole burnt offering and sacrifice, nor would he have shown us all these things, and at this time he would not have caused us to hear these things.
2 Judges 13:24 And the woman bore a son and called his name Sampson; and the child grew up, and the Lord blessed him.
2 Judges 13:25 And the spirit of the Lord began to go out together with him in the camp of Dan, between Saraa and Esthaol.

## Chapter 14

2 Judges 14:1 And Sampson went down to Thamnatha and saw a woman in Thamnatha from the daughters of the foreigners.
2 Judges 14:2 And he went up and told his father and mother and said, I have seen a woman in Thamnatha from the daughters of the Philistines, and now take her for me as wife.
2 Judges 14:3 And his father and mother said to him, Are there no daughters among your brothers and among all my people, that you go to take a wife from the uncircumcised foreigners? And Sampson said to his father, Take this one for me, for she is right in my eyes.
2 Judges 14:4 And his father and mother did not know that this was from the Lord, for he was seeking vengeance from the foreigners; and at that time the foreigners ruled in Israel.
2 Judges 14:5 And Sampson and his father and mother went down to Thamnatha. And he came as far as the vineyard of Thamnatha, and behold, a young lion roared to meet him;
2 Judges 14:6 and the spirit of the Lord leaped upon him, and he tore it apart as one would tear apart a kid, and nothing was in his hands. And he did not tell his father and mother what he had done.
2 Judges 14:7 And they went down and spoke to the woman, and she was right in Sampson's eyes.
2 Judges 14:8 And after days he returned to take her and turned aside to see the carcass of the lion, and behold, a gathering of bees in the mouth of the lion and honey.
2 Judges 14:9 And he took it out into his hands and went along, walking and eating; and he went to his father and mother and gave them some, and they ate; and he did not tell them that he took the honey out of the lion's mouth.
2 Judges 14:10 And his father went down to the woman; and Sampson held a feast there for seven days, for thus the young men do.
2 Judges 14:11 And it happened when they saw him that they took thirty invited men, and they were with him.
2 Judges 14:12 And Sampson said to them, I shall pose a riddle to you; if you indeed tell it within the seven days of the feast and find it, I shall give you thirty linen cloths and thirty sets of garments;
2 Judges 14:13 but if you cannot tell it to me, you shall give me thirty linen cloths and thirty changing sets of garments. And they said to him, Pose the riddle, and we shall hear it.
2 Judges 14:14 And he said to them, What edible thing came forth from an eater, and what sweet thing from a strong one? And they could not tell the riddle for three days.
2 Judges 14:15 And it happened on the fourth day that they said to Sampson's wife, Deceive your husband, please, and let him tell you the riddle, lest we burn you and your father's house with fire; have you called us to extort us?
2 Judges 14:16 And Sampson's wife wept to him and said, Indeed, you have hated me and have not loved me, for you have not told me the riddle that you posed to the sons of my people. And Sampson said to her, If I have not told my father and mother, shall I tell you?
2 Judges 14:17 And she wept to him through the seven days that their feast lasted; and it happened on the seventh day that he told her, for she pressed him; and she told the sons of her people.
2 Judges 14:18 And the men of the city said to him on the seventh day before the sun rose, What is sweeter than honey, and what is stronger than a lion? And Sampson said to them, If you had not plowed with my heifer, you would not have known my riddle.
2 Judges 14:19 And the spirit of the Lord leaped upon him, and he went down to Ascalon and struck thirty men from among them and took their garments and gave the sets to those who had told the riddle. And Sampson became angry with wrath and went up to his father's house.
2 Judges 14:20 And Sampson's wife became the wife of one of his friends whom he had befriended.

## Chapter 15

2 Judges 15:1 And it happened after days, in the days of the wheat harvest, that Sampson visited his wife with a kid of the goats and said, I shall go in to my wife in the chamber; and her father did not allow him to enter.
2 Judges 15:2 And her father said, I said, saying, that you surely hated her, and I gave her to one of your friends; is not her younger sister better than she? Let her be yours instead of her.
2 Judges 15:3 And Sampson said to them, I have been made innocent even this once regarding the foreigners, for I shall do evil to them.
2 Judges 15:4 And Sampson went and caught three hundred foxes and took torches and turned tail toward tail and put one torch between two tails and bound them;
2 Judges 15:5 and he lit fire in the torches and sent them into the grain of the foreigners, and they burned from the threshing floor as far as standing grain and as far as vineyard and olive tree.
2 Judges 15:6 And the foreigners said, Who did these things? And they said, Sampson, the son-in-law of the Thamnite, because he took his wife and gave her to one of his friends; and the foreigners came up and burned her and her father with fire.
2 Judges 15:7 And Sampson said to them, If you do this, then surely I shall take vengeance on you, and at last I shall cease.
2 Judges 15:8 And he struck them shin upon thigh with a great blow; and he went down and dwelt in a hole of the rock of Etam.
2 Judges 15:9 And the foreigners came up and encamped in Judah and spread out in Leui.
2 Judges 15:10 And the men of Judah said, Why have you come up against us? And the foreigners said, We have come up to bind Sampson and do to him as he did to us.
2 Judges 15:11 And three thousand men from Judah went down to the hole in the rock of Etam and said to Sampson, Do you not know that the foreigners rule us, and what is this you have done to us? And Sampson said to them, As they did to me, so I did to them.
2 Judges 15:12 And they said to him, We have come down to bind you, to give you into the hand of the foreigners. And Sampson said to them, Swear to me that you yourselves will not fall upon me.
2 Judges 15:13 And they said to him, saying, No, for we shall only bind you with a bond and hand you over into their hand, and we shall certainly not put you to death; and they bound him with two new cords and brought him up from that rock.
2 Judges 15:14 And they came as far as Siagon; and the foreigners shouted and ran to meet him; and the spirit of the Lord leaped upon him, and the cords on his arms became like tow burned in fire, and his bonds melted from his hands.
2 Judges 15:15 And he found a discarded jawbone of a donkey and stretched out his hand and took it and struck a thousand men with it.
2 Judges 15:16 And Sampson said, With a donkey's jawbone, wiping out, I wiped them out, for with the donkey's jawbone I struck a thousand men.
2 Judges 15:17 And it happened when he ceased speaking that he threw the jawbone from his hand; and he called that place Removal of the Jawbone.
2 Judges 15:18 And he became very thirsty; and he cried to the Lord and said, You favored this great salvation by the hand of your servant, and now I shall die of thirst and fall into the hand of the uncircumcised.
2 Judges 15:19 And God split the hollow in the jawbone, and water came out of it, and he drank, and his spirit returned and he lived. Therefore its name was called Spring of the One Calling, which is in Siagon to this day. –
2 Judges 15:20 And he judged Israel in the days of the foreigners twenty years.

## Chapter 16

2 Judges 16:1 And Sampson went to Gaza; and he saw a prostitute there and went in to her.
2 Judges 16:2 And it was reported to the Gazites, saying, Sampson has come here. And they surrounded him and lay in ambush for him all night at the city gate and kept silent all night, saying, Until dawn breaks, and let us kill him.
2 Judges 16:3 And Sampson slept until midnight; and he rose in the middle of the night and seized the doors of the city gate with the two posts and lifted them with the bar and set them on his shoulders and went up to the summit of the mountain facing Chebron and set them there.
2 Judges 16:4 And it happened after this that he loved a woman in Alsorech, and her name was Dalida.
2 Judges 16:5 And the rulers of the foreigners went up to her and said to her, Deceive him and see wherein his great strength lies and by what means we shall be able to prevail over him and bind him to humble him, and we shall each give you one thousand one hundred pieces of silver.
2 Judges 16:6 And Dalida said to Sampson, Tell me, please, wherein your great strength lies and by what means you could be bound so that you might be humbled.
2 Judges 16:7 And Sampson said to her, If they bind me with seven fresh sinews that have not been spoiled, then I shall grow weak and be like one of the people.
2 Judges 16:8 And the rulers of the foreigners brought her seven fresh sinews that had not been spoiled, and she bound him with them;
2 Judges 16:9 and an ambush for her sat in the chamber; and she said to him, Foreigners upon you, Sampson! And he tore apart the sinews as someone might break a strand of tow when it smells fire; and his strength was not known.
2 Judges 16:10 And Dalida said to Sampson, Behold, you have deceived me and spoken lies to me; now therefore tell me by what means you could be bound.
2 Judges 16:11 And he said to her, If they bind me securely with new cords with which no work has been done, then I shall grow weak and be like one of the people.
2 Judges 16:12 And Dalida took new cords and bound him with them; and the ambush came out of the chamber; and she said, Foreigners upon you, Sampson! And he tore them from his arms like a little rope.
2 Judges 16:13 And Dalida said to Sampson, Behold, you have deceived me and spoken lies to me; tell me, please, by what means you could be bound. And he said to her, If you weave the seven locks of my head with the web and hammer them with the peg into the wall, then I shall be weak like one of the people.
2 Judges 16:14 And it happened while he slept that Dalida took the seven locks of his head and wove them in the web and fixed it with the peg into the wall and said, Foreigners upon you, Sampson! And he awoke from his sleep and pulled the peg of the woven fabric from the wall.
2 Judges 16:15 And Dalida said to Sampson, How do you say, I love you, when your heart is not with me? This third time you have deceived me and not told me wherein your great strength lies.
2 Judges 16:16 And it happened as she pressed him with her words all the days and distressed him that he became faint of soul to the point of death;
2 Judges 16:17 and he told her all his heart and said to her, Iron has not come up upon my head, for I am holy to God from my mother's womb; if then I am shaved, my strength will depart from me, and I shall grow weak and be like all people.
2 Judges 16:18 And Dalida saw that he had told her all his heart, and sent and summoned the rulers of the foreigners, saying, Come up yet this once, for he has told me all his heart; and the rulers of the foreigners came up to her and brought the silver in their hands.
2 Judges 16:19 And Dalida made Sampson sleep upon her knees; and she called a man, and he shaved the seven locks of his head; and she began to humble him, and his strength departed from him.
2 Judges 16:20 And Dalida said, Foreigners upon you, Sampson. And he awoke from his sleep and said, I shall go out as time and again and shake myself free; and he did not know that the Lord had departed from upon him.
2 Judges 16:21 And the foreigners seized him and gouged out his eyes; and they brought him down to Gaza and bound him with bronze fetters, and he was grinding in the prison house.
2 Judges 16:22 And the hair of his head began to sprout after it had been shaved.
2 Judges 16:23 And the rulers of the foreigners gathered to sacrifice a great sacrifice to Dagon their god and to rejoice, and said, God has given Sampson our enemy into our hand.
2 Judges 16:24 And the people saw him and praised their god, for, Our god has delivered our enemy into our hand, the one who devastated our land and multiplied our wounded.
2 Judges 16:25 And when their heart became glad, they said, Call Sampson from the guardhouse, and let him play before us. And they called Sampson from the prison house, and he played before them, and they slapped him and stood him between the pillars.
2 Judges 16:26 And Sampson said to the young man holding his hand, Let me go and I shall feel the pillars upon which the house stands and lean upon them.
2 Judges 16:27 And the house was full of men and women, and all the rulers of the foreigners were there, and upon the roof were about seven hundred men and women watching Sampson's games.
2 Judges 16:28 And Sampson cried to the Lord and said, Adonaie Lord, remember me now, please, and strengthen me yet this once, God, and I shall repay one repayment for my two eyes to the foreigners.
2 Judges 16:29 And Sampson embraced the two pillars of the house on which the house stood, and leaned upon them and grasped one with his right hand and one with his left.
2 Judges 16:30 And Sampson said, Let my soul die with the foreigners; and he bore down with strength, and the house fell upon the rulers and upon all the people in it; and the dead whom Sampson put to death in his death were more than those he put to death in his life.
2 Judges 16:31 And his brothers and his father's house came down and took him and went up and buried him between Saraa and Esthaol in the tomb of Manoe his father. And he judged Israel twenty years.

## Chapter 17

2 Judges 17:1 And there was a man from the hill country of Ephraim, and his name was Michaias.
2 Judges 17:2 And he said to his mother, The one thousand one hundred pieces of silver that you took for yourself and about which you cursed me and spoke in my ears: behold, the silver is with me; I took it. And his mother said, Blessed is my son to the Lord.
2 Judges 17:3 And he returned the one thousand one hundred pieces of silver to his mother; and his mother said, Consecrating, I have consecrated the silver to the Lord from my hand for my son to make a carved and a cast image, and now I shall return it to you.
2 Judges 17:4 And he returned the silver to his mother; and his mother took two hundred pieces of silver and gave it to a silversmith, and he made it into a carved and a cast image; and it was in the house of Michaias.
2 Judges 17:5 And the house of Michaias was for him a house of God; and he made an ephod and theraphin and filled the hand of one of his sons, and he became his priest. –
2 Judges 17:6 And in those days there was no king in Israel; each man did what was right in his own eyes.
2 Judges 17:7 And there was a young man from Bethlehem of the district of Judah, and he was a Levite and sojourned there.
2 Judges 17:8 And the man went from Bethlehem, the city of Judah, to sojourn wherever he might find a place, and came as far as the hill country of Ephraim and as far as the house of Michaias to make his way.
2 Judges 17:9 And Michaias said to him, Where do you come from? And he said to him, I am a Levite from Bethlehem of Judah, and I am going to sojourn wherever I may find a place.
2 Judges 17:10 And Michaias said to him, Sit with me and be a father and a priest to me, and I shall give you ten pieces of silver per day and a set of garments and what is needed for your living. And the Levite went
2 Judges 17:11 and began to sojourn with the man, and the young man became to him like one of his sons.
2 Judges 17:12 And Michaias filled the hand of the Levite, and he became his priest and was in the house of Michaias.
2 Judges 17:13 And Michaias said, Now I know that the Lord will do good to me, for the Levite has become my priest.

## Chapter 18

2 Judges 18:1 In those days there was no king in Israel. And in those days the tribe of Dan sought for itself an inheritance to dwell in, for until that day no inheritance had fallen to it among the tribes of Israel.
2 Judges 18:2 And the sons of Dan sent from their districts five men, sons of strength, from Saraa and Esthaol to examine the land and trace it out, and said to them, Go and trace out the land. And they came as far as the hill country of Ephraim, as far as the house of Michaias, and lodged there.
2 Judges 18:3 They were at the house of Michaias, and they recognized the voice of the young Levite and turned aside there and said to him, Who brought you here, and what are you doing in this place, and what do you have here?
2 Judges 18:4 And he said to them, Thus and thus Michaias did for me and hired me, and I became his priest.
2 Judges 18:5 And they said to him, Inquire, please, by God, and we shall know whether our way in which we travel will prosper.
2 Judges 18:6 And the priest said to them, Go in peace; before the Lord is your way in which you travel.
2 Judges 18:7 And the five men went and came to Laisa; and they saw the people within it dwelling in confidence, like the judgment of the Sidonians at rest, and there is no one turning aside or shaming a word in the land, an heir pressing treasure out, and they are far from the Sidonians and have no dealings with any person.
2 Judges 18:8 And the five men came to their brothers in Saraa and Esthaol and said to their brothers, Why do you sit?
2 Judges 18:9 And they said, Rise and let us go up against them, for we have seen the land, and behold, it is very good; and do you remain quiet? Do not hesitate to go and enter to inherit the land.
2 Judges 18:10 And when you come, you will enter to a people in confidence, and the land is broad, for God has given it into your hand, a place where there is no lack of any thing in the land.
2 Judges 18:11 And six hundred men from the districts of Dan set out from there, from Saraa and Esthaol, girded with implements of battle.
2 Judges 18:12 And they went up and encamped in Kariathiarim in Judah; therefore that place was called Camp of Dan to this day, behold, behind Kariathiarim.
2 Judges 18:13 And they passed from there through the hill country of Ephraim and came as far as the house of Michaias.
2 Judges 18:14 And the five men who had gone to examine the land of Laisa answered and said to their brothers, Do you know that in this house there are an ephod and theraphin and a carved and a cast image? And now know what you will do.
2 Judges 18:15 And they turned aside there and entered the house of the young Levite, the house of Michaias, and asked him concerning peace.
2 Judges 18:16 And the six hundred men from the sons of Dan, girded with their implements of battle, stood by the door of the gate.
2 Judges 18:17 And the five men who had gone to examine the land went up
2 Judges 18:18 and entered there into the house of Michaias, while the priest stood there; and they took the carved image and the ephod and the theraphin and the cast image. And the priest said to them, What are you doing?
2 Judges 18:19 And they said to him, Be silent, put your hand on your mouth and come with us and become our father and priest; is it not good for you to be priest of one man's house, or to become priest of a tribe and a house in a district of Israel?
2 Judges 18:20 And the priest's heart grew glad, and he took the ephod and the theraphin and the carved and the cast image and came among the people.
2 Judges 18:21 And they turned and went away; and they put the children and the possessions and the baggage before them.
2 Judges 18:22 They went far from the house of Michaias, and behold, Michaias and the men in the houses by the house of Michaias cried out and caught up with the sons of Dan.
2 Judges 18:23 And the sons of Dan turned their faces and said to Michaias, What is the matter with you, that you cried out?
2 Judges 18:24 And Michaias said, You took my carved image which I made, and the priest, and went away; and what do I still have? And why do you say this to me, Why do you cry out?
2 Judges 18:25 And the sons of Dan said to him, Let your voice not be heard with us, lest men bitter of soul fall upon us and take away your life and the life of your house.
2 Judges 18:26 And the sons of Dan went on their way; and Michaias saw that they were stronger than he, and returned to his house.
2 Judges 18:27 And the sons of Dan took what Michaias had made and the priest he had, and came against Laisa, against a people at rest and trusting in confidence, and struck them by the edge of the sword and burned the city with fire;
2 Judges 18:28 and there was no deliverer, for it was far from the Sidonians, and they had no dealings with anyone, and it was in the valley of the house of Raab. And they built the city and settled in it
2 Judges 18:29 and called the city's name Dan after the name of Dan their father, who was born to Israel; and Oulamais was the city's name formerly.
2 Judges 18:30 And the sons of Dan set up the carved image for themselves; and Ionatham son of Gersom son of Manasse, he and his sons, were priests to the tribe of Dan until the day of the exile of the land.
2 Judges 18:31 And they set up for themselves the carved image which Michaias made all the days that the house of God was in Selom.

## Chapter 19

2 Judges 19:1 And it happened in those days, and there was no king in Israel. And there was a Levite man sojourning in the flanks of the hill country of Ephraim, and he took for himself a woman, a concubine, from Bethlehem of Judah.
2 Judges 19:2 And his concubine went away from him and departed from him to her father's house in Bethlehem of Judah, and was there days of four months.
2 Judges 19:3 And her husband rose and went after her to speak to her heart to bring her back to him, with his young man and a pair of donkeys; and she brought him into her father's house, and the father of the young woman saw him and rejoiced to meet him.
2 Judges 19:4 And his father-in-law, the young woman's father, kept him, and he stayed with him for three days, and they ate and drank and lodged there.
2 Judges 19:5 And it happened on the fourth day that they rose early in the morning, and he rose to go; and the young woman's father said to his son-in-law, Strengthen your heart with a morsel of bread, and after this you shall go.
2 Judges 19:6 And he sat, and the two ate together and drank; and the young woman's father said to the man, Come now, lodge here, and your heart will become glad.
2 Judges 19:7 And the man rose to go; and his father-in-law pressed him, and he sat and lodged there.
2 Judges 19:8 And he rose early in the morning on the fifth day to go; and the young woman's father said, Strengthen your heart, please, and march until the day declines; and the two ate.
2 Judges 19:9 And the man rose to go, he and his concubine and his young man; and his father-in-law, the young woman's father, said to him, Behold, please, the day has grown weak toward evening; lodge here, and your heart will become glad, and you shall rise early tomorrow for your way and go to your dwelling.
2 Judges 19:10 And the man did not consent to lodge and rose and departed and came as far as opposite Iebous [this is Jerusalem], and with him was a pair of saddled donkeys, and his concubine with him.
2 Judges 19:11 And they came as far as Iebous, and the day had advanced greatly; and the young man said to his master, Come, please, and let us turn aside into this city of the Iebusite and lodge in it.
2 Judges 19:12 And his master said to him, We shall not turn aside into a foreign city in which none of the sons of Israel are here, and we shall pass on as far as Gabaa.
2 Judges 19:13 And he said to his young man, Come and let us approach one of the places and lodge in Gabaa or in Rama.
2 Judges 19:14 And they passed and traveled, and the sun set on them near Gabaa, which belongs to Benjamin.
2 Judges 19:15 And they turned aside there to enter and lodge in Gabaa; and they entered and sat in the city square, and there was no man taking them into a house to lodge.
2 Judges 19:16 And behold, an old man was coming from his work in the field in the evening; and the man was from the hill country of Ephraim, and he sojourned in Gabaa, and the men of the place were sons of Benjamin.
2 Judges 19:17 And he lifted his eyes and saw the traveling man in the city square; and the old man said, Where are you going, and where do you come from?
2 Judges 19:18 And he said to him, We are passing from Bethlehem of Judah to the flanks of the hill country of Ephraim; I am from there, and I went to Bethlehem of Judah, and I am going to my house, and there is no man taking me into the house;
2 Judges 19:19 and indeed there is straw and fodder for our donkeys, and bread and wine for me and the maidservant and the young man with your servants; there is no lack of anything.
2 Judges 19:20 And the old man said, Peace to you, only let all your lack be upon me; only you shall certainly not lodge in the square.
2 Judges 19:21 And he brought him into his house and made a place for the donkeys, and they washed their feet and ate and drank.
2 Judges 19:22 And as they gladdened their hearts, behold, men of the city, sons of lawless men, surrounded the house, knocking at the door, and said to the old man, the master of the house, saying, Bring out the man who entered your house so that we may know him.
2 Judges 19:23 And the man, master of the house, went out to them and said, No, brothers, please do not do evil; after this man has entered my house, do not do this folly;
2 Judges 19:24 behold, my virgin daughter and his concubine; I shall bring them out, and humble them and do to them what is good in your eyes; but to this man you shall not do this thing of folly.
2 Judges 19:25 And the men did not consent to listen to him. And the man seized his concubine and brought her out to them outside, and they knew her and abused her all night until morning; and they sent her away as morning rose.
2 Judges 19:26 And the woman came toward dawn and fell by the door of the house where her husband was, until daylight.
2 Judges 19:27 And her husband rose in the morning and opened the doors of the house and went out to go on his way, and behold, the woman, his concubine, had fallen beside the doors of the house, with her hands on the threshold.
2 Judges 19:28 And he said to her, Rise and let us go; and she did not answer, for she was dead. And he put her upon the donkey and went to his place.
2 Judges 19:29 And he took the sword and seized his concubine and cut her into twelve pieces and sent them throughout all the territory of Israel.
2 Judges 19:30 And it happened that everyone who saw it said, Such a thing has neither happened nor been seen from the day the sons of Israel came up from the land of Egypt until this day; set counsel for yourselves upon it and speak.

## Chapter 20

2 Judges 20:1 And all the sons of Israel went out, and the assembly was convened as one man, from Dan to Bersabee and the land of Galaad, to the Lord at Massepha.
2 Judges 20:2 And all the tribes of Israel stood before the Lord in the assembly of the people of God, four hundred thousand footmen drawing a sword.
2 Judges 20:3 And the sons of Benjamin heard that the sons of Israel had gone up to Massepha. And the sons of Israel came and said, Tell where this evil happened.
2 Judges 20:4 And the Levite man, the husband of the murdered woman, answered and said, I and my concubine came to Gabaa of Benjamin to lodge.
2 Judges 20:5 And the men of Gabaa rose against me and surrounded the house against me at night; they wished to murder me, and they humbled my concubine, and she died.
2 Judges 20:6 And I seized my concubine and cut her into pieces and sent them throughout all the territory of the inheritance of the sons of Israel, for they did an obscene thing and an abomination in Israel.
2 Judges 20:7 Behold, all of you, sons of Israel, give yourselves a word and counsel there.
2 Judges 20:8 And all the people rose as one man, saying, No man of us shall go to his dwelling, and no man shall return to his house.
2 Judges 20:9 And now this is the thing that shall be done to Gabaa: we shall go up against it by lot,
2 Judges 20:10 but we shall take ten men out of a hundred from all the tribes of Israel, and a hundred out of a thousand and a thousand out of ten thousand, to take provisions so that they can go to Gabaa of Benjamin to do to it according to all the abomination which it did in Israel.
2 Judges 20:11 And all the men of Israel gathered against the city as one man.
2 Judges 20:12 And the tribes of Israel sent men throughout the tribe of Benjamin, saying, What is this evil that has happened among you?
2 Judges 20:13 And now give up the men, sons of lawless men, in Gabaa, and we shall put them to death and cleanse evil from Israel. And the sons of Benjamin did not consent to listen to the voice of their brothers, the sons of Israel.
2 Judges 20:14 And the sons of Benjamin gathered from their cities to Gabaa to go out to battle against the sons of Israel.
2 Judges 20:15 And the sons of Benjamin from the cities were counted on that day, twenty-three thousand men drawing a sword, apart from the inhabitants of Gabaa, who were counted, seven hundred chosen men
2 Judges 20:16 from all the people, right-handed on both sides; all these were slingers of stones at a hair and did not miss.
2 Judges 20:17 And the men of Israel apart from Benjamin were counted, four hundred thousand men drawing a sword; all these were men of battle.
2 Judges 20:18 And they rose and went up to Bethel and inquired of God, and the sons of Israel said, Who shall go up first for us to battle against the sons of Benjamin? And the Lord said, Judah shall go up first, leading.
2 Judges 20:19 And the sons of Israel rose in the morning and encamped against Gabaa.
2 Judges 20:20 And every man of Israel went out to battle against Benjamin and joined battle with them at Gabaa.
2 Judges 20:21 And the sons of Benjamin came out from Gabaa and destroyed twenty-two thousand men of Israel upon the ground on that day.
2 Judges 20:22 And the men of Israel strengthened themselves and continued to join battle in the place where they had joined it on the first day.
2 Judges 20:23 And the sons of Israel went up and wept before the Lord until evening and inquired of the Lord, saying, Shall we again approach in battle against the sons of Benjamin our brothers? And the Lord said, Go up against them.
2 Judges 20:24 And the sons of Israel approached the sons of Benjamin on the second day.
2 Judges 20:25 And the sons of Benjamin came out from Gabaa to meet them on the second day and destroyed a further eighteen thousand men of the sons of Israel upon the ground; all these drew a sword.
2 Judges 20:26 And all the sons of Israel and all the people went up and came to Bethel and wept and sat there before the Lord and fasted on that day until evening and offered whole burnt offerings and complete offerings before the Lord;
2 Judges 20:27 for the ark of the covenant of the Lord God was there,
2 Judges 20:28 and Phinees son of Eleazar son of Aaron stood before it in those days. And the sons of Israel inquired of the Lord, saying, Shall we again go out to battle against the sons of Benjamin our brothers, or shall we hold back? And the Lord said, Go up, for tomorrow I shall give them into your hands.
2 Judges 20:29 And the sons of Israel set ambushes around Gabaa.
2 Judges 20:30 And the sons of Israel went up against the sons of Benjamin on the third day and joined battle against Gabaa as time and again.
2 Judges 20:31 And the sons of Benjamin came out to meet the people and were drawn away from the city and began to strike wounded men from the people as time and again on the roads, one of which goes up to Bethel and one to Gabaa in the field, about thirty men of Israel.
2 Judges 20:32 And the sons of Benjamin said, They are falling before us as at first. And the sons of Israel said, Let us flee and draw them away from the city onto the roads; and they did so.
2 Judges 20:33 And every man rose from his place and joined battle at Baalthamar, and Israel's ambush came from its place from Maaragabe.
