2 Judges 20:34 And ten thousand chosen men from all Israel came opposite Gabaa, and the battle was heavy; and they did not know that evil was overtaking them.
2 Judges 20:35 And the Lord struck Benjamin before the sons of Israel, and the sons of Israel destroyed from Benjamin on that day twenty-five thousand one hundred men; all these drew a sword.
2 Judges 20:36 And the sons of Benjamin saw that they were struck; and the men of Israel gave ground to Benjamin, because they trusted in the ambush which they had set against Gabaa.
2 Judges 20:37 And as they withdrew, the ambush moved and spread out against Gabaa, and the ambush poured out and struck the city by the edge of the sword.
2 Judges 20:38 And there was a sign for the sons of Israel with the battle ambush: that they should raise a signal of smoke from the city.
2 Judges 20:39 And the sons of Israel saw that the ambush had seized Gabaa beforehand, and they stood in the battle, and Benjamin began to strike wounded men among the men of Israel, about thirty men, for they said, Again they are surely falling before us as in the first battle.
2 Judges 20:40 And the signal rose more over the city like a pillar of smoke; and Benjamin looked behind him, and behold, the destruction of the city went up to heaven.
2 Judges 20:41 And the men of Israel turned back, and the men of Benjamin hurried, for they saw that evil had met them.
2 Judges 20:42 And they turned before the sons of Israel toward the wilderness road and fled, and the battle overtook them, and those from the cities destroyed them in their midst.
2 Judges 20:43 And they cut down Benjamin and pursued him from Noua at his heels as far as opposite Gabaa toward the sunrise.
2 Judges 20:44 And eighteen thousand men of Benjamin fell; all these were men of strength.
2 Judges 20:45 And the rest turned and fled toward the rock of Remmon in the wilderness, and the sons of Israel gleaned five thousand men from them; and the sons of Israel went down after them as far as Gedan and struck two thousand men from them.
2 Judges 20:46 And all those who fell from Benjamin on that day were twenty-five thousand men drawing a sword; all these were men of strength.
2 Judges 20:47 And the rest turned and fled toward the rock of Remmon in the wilderness, six hundred men, and stayed at the rock of Remmon four months.
2 Judges 20:48 And the sons of Israel turned against the sons of Benjamin and struck them by the edge of the sword, from the city of Methla as far as the livestock and as far as everything found in all the cities; and the cities that were found they burned with fire.

## Chapter 21

2 Judges 21:1 And the sons of Israel swore at Massepha, saying, No man among us shall give his daughter to Benjamin as wife.
2 Judges 21:2 And the people came to Bethel and sat there until evening before God and raised their voice and wept with great weeping
2 Judges 21:3 and said, Why, Lord God of Israel, has this happened, for one tribe to be missing today from Israel?
2 Judges 21:4 And it happened on the next day that the people rose early and built an altar there and offered whole burnt offerings and complete offerings.
2 Judges 21:5 And the sons of Israel said, Who did not come up in the assembly from all the tribes of Israel to the Lord? For there was a great oath concerning those who had not come up to the Lord at Massepha, saying, He shall certainly be put to death.
2 Judges 21:6 And the sons of Israel were comforted concerning Benjamin their brother and said, One tribe has been cut off from Israel today;
2 Judges 21:7 what shall we do for the remaining ones for wives? And we have sworn by the Lord not to give them any of our daughters as wives.
2 Judges 21:8 And they said, Which one from the tribes of Israel did not go up to the Lord at Massepha? And behold, no man from Iabis Galaad had come to the camp for the assembly.
2 Judges 21:9 And the people were counted, and no man from the inhabitants of Iabis Galaad was there.
2 Judges 21:10 And the congregation sent there twelve thousand men from the sons of strength and commanded them, saying, Go and strike the inhabitants of Iabis Galaad by the edge of the sword.
2 Judges 21:11 And this you shall do: devote to destruction every male and every woman who has known the bed of a male, but preserve the virgins. And they did so.
2 Judges 21:12 And they found among the inhabitants of Iabis Galaad four hundred young virgin women who had not known a man in the bed of a male, and brought them to the camp at Selon in the land of Canaan.
2 Judges 21:13 And all the congregation sent and spoke to the sons of Benjamin at the rock of Remmon and called them to peace.
2 Judges 21:14 And Benjamin returned to the sons of Israel at that time, and the sons of Israel gave them the women whom they had kept alive from the daughters of Iabis Galaad; and thus it pleased them.
2 Judges 21:15 And the people were comforted concerning Benjamin, for the Lord had made a breach among the tribes of Israel.
2 Judges 21:16 And the elders of the congregation said, What shall we do for wives for those remaining? For woman has been destroyed from Benjamin.
2 Judges 21:17 And they said, An inheritance of the escaped ones belongs to Benjamin, and a tribe shall not be wiped out from Israel;
2 Judges 21:18 for we cannot give them wives from our daughters, for we swore among the sons of Israel, saying, Accursed is he who gives a wife to Benjamin.
2 Judges 21:19 And they said, Behold, a feast of the Lord is in Selon from days to days, which is north of Bethel, toward sunrise on the road that goes up from Bethel to Sychem and south of Lebona.
2 Judges 21:20 And they commanded the sons of Benjamin, saying, Go, lie in ambush in the vineyards;
2 Judges 21:21 and you shall watch, and behold, if the daughters of the inhabitants of Selon come out to dance in the dances, then you shall come out from the vineyards and seize for yourselves each man a wife from the daughters of Selon and go to the land of Benjamin.
2 Judges 21:22 And it shall be when their fathers or brothers come to plead with you that we shall say to them, Show us mercy regarding them, for we did not take each man his wife in the battle, for you did not give them to them; as at this time you have transgressed.
2 Judges 21:23 And the sons of Benjamin did so and took wives according to their number from the dancing women whom they seized; and they went and returned to their inheritance and built the cities and dwelt in them.
2 Judges 21:24 And the sons of Israel went about from there at that time, each man to his tribe and his kin, and they went out from there, each man to his inheritance. –
2 Judges 21:25 And in those days there was no king in Israel; each man did what was right before him.

# Ruth

The Apostolic Bible. Public domain. https://apostolic-bible.ysys9.chatgpt.site/license.html


## Chapter 1

Ruth 1:1 And it happened when the judges judged that there was a famine in the land, and a man went from Bethlehem of Judah to sojourn in the field of Moab, he and his wife and his sons.
Ruth 1:2 And the man's name was Abimelech, and his wife's name Noemin, and the names of his two sons Maalon and Chelaion, Ephrathites from Bethlehem of Judah; and they came to the field of Moab and were there.
Ruth 1:3 And Abimelech, Noemin's husband, died, and she and her two sons were left.
Ruth 1:4 And they took Moabite women for themselves as wives, the name of one Orpha and the name of the second Ruth; and they dwelt there about ten years.
Ruth 1:5 And both Maalon and Chelaion also died, and the woman was left without her husband and her two sons.
Ruth 1:6 And she rose, she and her two daughters-in-law, and they returned from the field of Moab, for they had heard in the field of Moab that the Lord had visited his people to give them bread.
Ruth 1:7 And she went out from the place where she was, and her two daughters-in-law with her; and they traveled on the road to return to the land of Judah.
Ruth 1:8 And Noemin said to her daughters-in-law, Go, please, return each to her mother's house; may the Lord show mercy to you as you showed to the dead and to me;
Ruth 1:9 may the Lord grant you that each find rest in her husband's house. And she kissed them, and they raised their voices and wept.
Ruth 1:10 And they said to her, With you we return to your people.
Ruth 1:11 And Noemin said, Return, please, my daughters; and why do you go with me? Do I still have sons in my womb who will be husbands for you?
Ruth 1:12 Return, please, my daughters, for I have grown old so as not to be with a husband; for if I said that I have means to come to be with a husband and bear sons,
Ruth 1:13 would you wait for them until they grew up? Or would you be held back for them from coming to be with a husband? No, please, my daughters, for it has become more bitter for me than for you, because the Lord's hand has gone out against me.
Ruth 1:14 And they raised their voices and wept again; and Orpha kissed her mother-in-law and returned to her people, but Ruth followed her.
Ruth 1:15 And Noemin said to Ruth, Behold, your fellow daughter-in-law has returned to her people and to her gods; return, please, you too, after your fellow daughter-in-law.
Ruth 1:16 But Ruth said, Do not confront me to leave you or to turn back from behind you; for wherever you go, I shall go, and wherever you lodge, I shall lodge; your people are my people and your God my God;
Ruth 1:17 and wherever you die, I shall die, and there I shall be buried; thus may the Lord do to me and thus may he add, for death shall separate between me and you.
Ruth 1:18 And Noemin, seeing that she was determined to go with her, ceased speaking to her further.
Ruth 1:19 And both traveled until they came to Bethlehem. And the whole city sounded out over them and said, Is this Noemin?
Ruth 1:20 And she said to them, Do not call me Noemin, call me Bitter, for the Sufficient One has made it very bitter for me;
Ruth 1:21 I went away full, and the Lord returned me empty; and why do you call me Noemin? The Lord has humbled me, and the Sufficient One has afflicted me.
Ruth 1:22 And Noemin returned, and Ruth the Moabite, her daughter-in-law, returning from the field of Moab; and they came to Bethlehem at the beginning of the barley harvest.

## Chapter 2

Ruth 2:1 And Noemin had a man known to her husband; the man was mighty in strength, from the kin of Abimelech, and his name was Boos.
Ruth 2:2 And Ruth the Moabite said to Noemin, Let me go, please, into the field and gather among the ears behind someone in whose eyes I find favor. And she said to her, Go, daughter.
Ruth 2:3 And she went and gleaned in the field behind the reapers; and by chance she happened upon the portion of the field of Boos, who was of the kin of Abimelech.
Ruth 2:4 And behold, Boos came from Bethlehem and said to the reapers, The Lord be with you; and they said to him, May the Lord bless you.
Ruth 2:5 And Boos said to his young man who stood over the reapers, Whose young woman is this?
Ruth 2:6 And the young man who stood over the reapers answered and said, She is the Moabite girl who returned with Noemin from the field of Moab
Ruth 2:7 and said, Let me glean, please, and gather among the sheaves behind the reapers; and she came and stood from morning until evening, and she rested only a little in the field.
Ruth 2:8 And Boos said to Ruth, Have you not heard, daughter? Do not go to glean in another field, and do not go from here; here attach yourself to my young women;
Ruth 2:9 let your eyes be on the field where they reap, and go behind them; behold, I have commanded the young men not to touch you; and whenever you thirst, go to the vessels and drink from where the young men draw water.
Ruth 2:10 And she fell on her face and bowed to the ground and said to him, Why have I found favor in your eyes that you should recognize me, when I am a foreigner?
Ruth 2:11 And Boos answered and said to her, By a report it was reported to me all that you have done for your mother-in-law after your husband died, and how you left your father and mother and the land of your birth and went to a people whom you did not know yesterday or the third day;
Ruth 2:12 may the Lord repay your work, and may your wage be full from the Lord God of Israel, to whom you have come to trust under his wings.
Ruth 2:13 And she said, May I find favor in your eyes, lord, for you have comforted me and spoken to the heart of your servant, and behold, I shall be like one of your maidservants.
Ruth 2:14 And Boos said to her, Already at the hour of eating, come here and eat of the bread and dip your morsel in the vinegar. And Ruth sat beside the reapers, and Boos heaped up parched grain for her, and she ate and was filled and left some.
Ruth 2:15 And she rose to glean, and Boos commanded his young men, saying, Let her glean even among the sheaves, and do not shame her;
Ruth 2:16 and carrying, carry for her, and also dropping, drop for her from the heaps, and leave it and she will glean, and do not rebuke her.
Ruth 2:17 And she gleaned in the field until evening; and she beat out what she had gathered, and it was about an ephah of barley.
Ruth 2:18 And she lifted it and entered the city, and her mother-in-law saw what she had gleaned, and Ruth brought out and gave her what she had left from that with which she had been filled.
Ruth 2:19 And her mother-in-law said to her, Where did you glean today and where did you work? May the one who recognized you be blessed. And Ruth told her mother-in-law where she had worked and said, The name of the man with whom I worked today is Boos.
Ruth 2:20 And Noemin said to her daughter-in-law, Blessed is he to the Lord, for he has not abandoned his mercy with the living and the dead. And Noemin said to her, The man is near to us; he is among those who are near kin to us.
Ruth 2:21 And Ruth said to her mother-in-law, Moreover, he said to me, Attach yourself to my young men until they finish all the harvest that belongs to me.
Ruth 2:22 And Noemin said to Ruth her daughter-in-law, Good, daughter, that you went with his young women, and they will not meet you in another field.
Ruth 2:23 And Ruth attached herself to the young women of Boos to glean until the barley harvest and the wheat harvest were finished. And she dwelt with her mother-in-law.

## Chapter 3

Ruth 3:1 And Noemin her mother-in-law said to her, Daughter, shall I not seek rest for you, that it may go well with you?
Ruth 3:2 And now is not Boos our acquaintance, with whose young women you were? Behold, he winnows the barley threshing floor tonight.
Ruth 3:3 And you shall wash and anoint yourself and put your clothing upon yourself and go up to the threshing floor; do not make yourself known to the man until he finishes drinking and eating;
Ruth 3:4 and it shall be when he lies down, you shall know the place where he lies, and you shall come and uncover the place by his feet and lie down, and he will tell you what you shall do.
Ruth 3:5 And Ruth said to her, Everything that you say, I shall do.
Ruth 3:6 And she went down to the threshing floor and did according to everything her mother-in-law commanded her.
Ruth 3:7 And Boos ate, and his heart grew glad, and he came to lie down by a part of the heap; and she came secretly and uncovered the place by his feet.
Ruth 3:8 And it happened at midnight that the man was startled and disturbed, and behold, a woman was lying by his feet.
Ruth 3:9 And he said, Who are you? And she said, I am Ruth your servant, and you shall spread your wing over your servant, for you are a near kinsman.
Ruth 3:10 And Boos said, Blessed are you to the Lord God, daughter, for you made your latter mercy better than the first, in that you did not go after young men, whether poor or rich.
Ruth 3:11 And now, daughter, do not fear; all that you say I shall do for you, for all the tribe of my people knows that you are a woman of strength,
Ruth 3:12 and that I truly am a near kinsman, yet there is a nearer kinsman than I.
Ruth 3:13 Lodge tonight, and it shall be in the morning, if he acts as near kin for you, good, let him act as near kin; but if he does not wish to act as near kin for you, I shall act as near kin for you, as the Lord lives; lie down until morning.
Ruth 3:14 And she lay by his feet until morning. And she rose before a man could recognize his neighbor; and Boos said, Let it not be known that a woman came to the threshing floor.
Ruth 3:15 And he said to her, Bring the wrap that is upon you. And she held it, and he measured six of barley and placed it upon her; and he entered the city.
Ruth 3:16 And Ruth entered to her mother-in-law; and she said, Who are you, daughter? And she told her all that the man had done for her.
Ruth 3:17 And she said to her, These six of barley he gave me, for he said to me, Do not go in empty to your mother-in-law.
Ruth 3:18 And she said, Sit, daughter, until you learn how the matter will fall; for the man shall certainly not rest until he finishes the matter today.

## Chapter 4

Ruth 4:1 And Boos went up to the gate and sat there, and behold, the near kinsman of whom Boos spoke was passing by. And Boos said to him, Turn aside and sit here, hidden one; and he turned aside and sat.
Ruth 4:2 And Boos took ten men from the elders of the city and said, Sit here; and they sat.
Ruth 4:3 And Boos said to the near kinsman, The portion of the field that belonged to our brother Abimelech, which has been given to Noemin who returned from the field of Moab,
Ruth 4:4 I said, I shall uncover your ear, saying, Acquire it before those sitting and before the elders of my people; if you act as near kin, act as near kin, but if you do not, tell me and I shall know; for there is no one besides you to act as near kin, and I am after you. And he said, I shall act as near kin.
Ruth 4:5 And Boos said, On the day you acquire the field from Noemin's hand and from Ruth the Moabite, wife of the dead man, you must acquire her too, so as to raise up the name of the dead man upon his inheritance.
Ruth 4:6 And the near kinsman said, I cannot act as near kin for myself, lest I ruin my inheritance; act as near kin for yourself in my near kinship, for I cannot act as near kin.
Ruth 4:7 And this was the ordinance formerly in Israel regarding near kinship and regarding exchange to establish every matter: a man would take off his sandal and give it to his neighbor who acted in his near kinship, and this was a witness in Israel.
Ruth 4:8 And the near kinsman said to Boos, Acquire my near kinship for yourself; and he took off his sandal and gave it to him.
Ruth 4:9 And Boos said to the elders and to all the people, You are witnesses today that I have acquired all that belonged to Abimelech and all that belongs to Chelaion and Maalon from Noemin's hand;
Ruth 4:10 and indeed Ruth the Moabite, wife of Maalon, I have acquired for myself as wife, to raise up the dead man's name upon his inheritance, and the dead man's name shall not be destroyed from among his brothers and from the tribe of his people; you are witnesses today.
Ruth 4:11 And all the people at the gate said, Witnesses. And the elders said, May the Lord make your wife who comes into your house like Rachel and like Leia, who both built the house of Israel and made strength in Ephratha, and may there be a name in Bethlehem;
Ruth 4:12 and may your house become like the house of Phares, whom Thamar bore to Judah, from the seed that the Lord will give you from this maidservant.
Ruth 4:13 And Boos took Ruth, and she became his wife, and he went in to her, and the Lord gave her conception, and she bore a son.
Ruth 4:14 And the women said to Noemin, Blessed is the Lord, who has not ended your near kinsman today, and may your name be called in Israel,
Ruth 4:15 and he shall be for you one who returns your soul and nourishes your old age, for your daughter-in-law who loves you bore him, she who is better to you than seven sons.
Ruth 4:16 And Noemin took the child and placed him in her bosom and became a nurse to him.
Ruth 4:17 And the neighbor women called him a name, saying, A son has been born to Noemin; and they called his name Obed; he is father of Iessai, father of David.
Ruth 4:18 And these are the generations of Phares: Phares fathered Esron,
Ruth 4:19 and Esron fathered Arran, and Arran fathered Aminadab,
Ruth 4:20 and Aminadab fathered Naasson, and Naasson fathered Salman,
Ruth 4:21 and Salman fathered Boos, and Boos fathered Obed,
Ruth 4:22 and Obed fathered Iessai, and Iessai fathered David.

# 1 Samuel

The Apostolic Bible. Public domain. https://apostolic-bible.ysys9.chatgpt.site/license.html


## Chapter 1

1 Samuel 1:1 There was a man from Armathaim Sipha, from the hill country of Ephraim, and his name was Elkana son of Ieremeel son of Eliou son of Thoke in Nasib of Ephraim.
1 Samuel 1:2 And he had two wives; the name of one was Anna, and the name of the second Phennana; and Phennana had children, but Anna had no child.
1 Samuel 1:3 And the man went up from days to days from his city, from Armathaim, to worship and sacrifice to the Lord God Sabaoth at Selo; and there were Eli and his two sons Ophni and Phinees, priests of the Lord.
1 Samuel 1:4 And it happened on a day that Elkana sacrificed and gave portions to Phennana his wife and her sons and daughters;
1 Samuel 1:5 and to Anna he gave one portion, for she had no child; nevertheless Elkana loved Anna more than her, and the Lord had shut the parts about her womb;
1 Samuel 1:6 for the Lord had not given her a child according to her affliction and according to the despondency of her affliction, and she was despondent because of this, for the Lord had closed the parts about her womb so as not to give her a child.
1 Samuel 1:7 Thus she did year by year when she went up to the Lord's house; and she was despondent and wept and did not eat.
1 Samuel 1:8 And Elkana her husband said to her, Anna. And she said to him, Behold, I am here, lord. And he said to her, What is the matter with you, that you weep? And why do you not eat? And why does your heart strike you? Am I not better to you than ten children?
1 Samuel 1:9 And Anna rose after they ate in Selo and stood before the Lord, and Eli the priest sat upon the seat by the doorposts of the Lord's temple.
1 Samuel 1:10 And she, pained in soul, prayed to the Lord and wept with weeping
1 Samuel 1:11 and vowed a vow to the Lord, saying, Adonai Lord Eloai Sabaoth, if you indeed look upon the humiliation of your servant and remember me and give your servant male seed, I shall give him before you as a gift until the day of his death, and he shall not drink wine or strong drink, and iron shall not come up upon his head.
1 Samuel 1:12 And it happened while she multiplied her praying before the Lord that Eli the priest watched her mouth;
1 Samuel 1:13 and she spoke in her heart, and her lips moved, but her voice was not heard; and Eli reckoned her drunk.
1 Samuel 1:14 And the young servant of Eli said to her, How long will you be drunk? Remove your wine and go from before the Lord.
1 Samuel 1:15 And Anna answered and said, No, lord; I am a woman for whom the day is hard, and I have drunk neither wine nor strong drink, and I pour out my soul before the Lord;
1 Samuel 1:16 do not count your servant a daughter of pestilence, for out of the abundance of my talk I have extended myself until now.
1 Samuel 1:17 And Eli answered and said to her, Go in peace; may the God of Israel give you every request of yours that you have asked of him.
1 Samuel 1:18 And she said, Your servant has found favor in your eyes. And the woman went on her way and entered her lodging and ate with her husband and drank, and her face no longer fell.
1 Samuel 1:19 And they rose early in the morning and worshiped the Lord and went on their way. And Elkana entered his house in Armathaim and knew Anna his wife, and the Lord remembered her,
1 Samuel 1:20 and she conceived. And it happened at the time of days that she bore a son; and she called his name Samuel and said, Because I asked him from the Lord God Sabaoth.
1 Samuel 1:21 And the man Elkana and all his house went up to sacrifice at Selom the sacrifice of the days and his vows and all the tithes of his land;
1 Samuel 1:22 but Anna did not go up with him, for she said to her husband, Until the child goes up, if I wean him, and he shall appear before the Lord's face and remain there forever.
1 Samuel 1:23 And Elkana her husband said to her, Do what is good in your eyes; stay until you wean him; only may the Lord establish what went out from your mouth. And the woman stayed and nursed her son until she weaned him.
1 Samuel 1:24 And she went up with him to Selom with a three-year-old calf and loaves and an ephah of fine flour and a skin of wine and entered the Lord's house at Selom, and the child was with them.
1 Samuel 1:25 And they brought him before the Lord, and his father slaughtered the sacrifice which he made from days to days to the Lord, and brought the child and slaughtered the calf. And Anna the child's mother brought him to Eli
1 Samuel 1:26 and said, In me, lord; as your soul lives, I am the woman who stood before you when praying to the Lord;
1 Samuel 1:27 for this child I prayed, and the Lord gave me my request which I asked of him;
1 Samuel 1:28 and I lend him to the Lord for all the days that he lives, a use for the Lord.

## Chapter 2

1 Samuel 2:1 And she said, My heart was strengthened in the Lord, my horn was exalted in my God; my mouth was opened wide against enemies, I rejoiced in your salvation.
1 Samuel 2:2 For there is none holy like the Lord, and none righteous like our God; there is none holy besides you.
1 Samuel 2:3 Do not boast and do not speak lofty things; let no grand speech go out of your mouth, for the Lord is a God of knowledge and a God who prepares his deeds.
1 Samuel 2:4 The bow of mighty ones grew weak, and the weak girded themselves with strength;
1 Samuel 2:5 those full of bread were diminished, and the hungry let land go; for a barren woman bore seven, and she who had many children grew weak.
1 Samuel 2:6 The Lord puts to death and brings to life, brings down to Hades and brings up;
1 Samuel 2:7 the Lord makes poor and makes rich, humbles and raises up.
1 Samuel 2:8 He raises a needy one from the ground and lifts a poor one from a dung heap to seat him with the rulers of peoples, granting them a throne of glory as an inheritance.
1 Samuel 2:9 Giving a vow to one who vows, and he blessed the years of a righteous one; for a man is not strong by strength,
1 Samuel 2:10 the Lord will make his adversary weak, the Lord is holy. Let the wise not boast in his wisdom, and let the mighty not boast in his might, and let the rich not boast in his riches, but let one who boasts boast in this: to understand and know the Lord and to do judgment and righteousness in the midst of the earth. The Lord went up to the heavens and thundered; he will judge the ends of the earth and gives strength to our kings and will exalt the horn of his anointed.
1 Samuel 2:11 And they left him there before the Lord and departed to Armathaim, and the child ministered before the Lord in the presence of Eli the priest.
1 Samuel 2:12 And the sons of Eli the priest were pestilent sons, not knowing the Lord.
1 Samuel 2:13 And the priest's due from the people, from everyone sacrificing: the priest's young man came when the meat was boiled, with a three-pronged meat hook in his hand,
1 Samuel 2:14 and thrust it into the great cauldron or into the bronze vessel or into the pot; whatever came up on the hook the priest took for himself; thus they did to all Israel who came to sacrifice to the Lord at Selom.
1 Samuel 2:15 And before the fat was burned as incense, the priest's young man came and said to the man sacrificing, Give meat to roast for the priest, and I shall certainly not take boiled meat from you out of the cauldron.
1 Samuel 2:16 And the man sacrificing would say, Let the fat first be burned as incense, as is fitting, and take for yourself from everything that your soul desires. And he said, No, for you shall give it now, and if not, I shall take it by force.
1 Samuel 2:17 And the sin of the young men before the Lord was very great, for they rejected the Lord's sacrifice. –
1 Samuel 2:18 And Samuel was ministering before the Lord, a child girded with an ephoud bar,
1 Samuel 2:19 and his mother made him a little double cloak and brought it to him from days to days when she went up with her husband to sacrifice the sacrifice of the days.
1 Samuel 2:20 And Eli blessed Elkana and his wife, saying, May the Lord repay you with seed from this woman in place of the debt which you lent to the Lord. And the man went to his place,
1 Samuel 2:21 and the Lord visited Anna, and she bore three more sons and two daughters. And the child Samuel grew great before the Lord.
1 Samuel 2:22 And Eli was very old; and he heard what his sons were doing to the sons of Israel,
1 Samuel 2:23 and said to them, Why do you do according to this thing which I hear from the mouth of all the Lord's people?
1 Samuel 2:24 No, children, for the report I hear is not good; do not do thus, for the reports I hear, of a people not serving God, are not good.
1 Samuel 2:25 If a man sins against a man, they will pray for him to the Lord; but if he sins against the Lord, who will pray for him? And they did not listen to their father's voice, for the Lord indeed wished to destroy them. –
1 Samuel 2:26 And the child Samuel went on and grew great and was good both with the Lord and with people. –
1 Samuel 2:27 And a man of God came to Eli and said, Thus says the Lord: Revealing myself, I revealed myself to your father's house when they were in the land of Egypt, slaves to Pharaoh's house,
1 Samuel 2:28 and I chose your father's house from all the scepters of Israel to be priest for me and to go up to my altar and burn incense and bear an ephoud, and I gave your father's house all the fire offerings of the sons of Israel for food;
1 Samuel 2:29 and why did you look upon my incense and my sacrifice with a shameless eye and honor your sons above me, to be blessed with the first portion of every sacrifice of Israel before me?
1 Samuel 2:30 Therefore thus said the Lord God of Israel: I said, Your house and your father's house shall walk before me forever; and now the Lord says, By no means for me, for those who honor me I shall honor, and one who despises me shall be dishonored.
1 Samuel 2:31 Behold, days are coming, and I shall destroy your seed and the seed of your father's house,
1 Samuel 2:32 and you shall have no elder in my house all the days;
1 Samuel 2:33 and I shall not destroy a man of yours from my altar, to make his eyes fail and his soul melt away, and all the survivors of your house shall fall by men's sword.
1 Samuel 2:34 And this is the sign for you which shall come upon these two sons of yours, Ophni and Phinees: on one day both shall die.
1 Samuel 2:35 And I shall raise up for myself a faithful priest who will do all that is in my heart and soul; and I shall build him a faithful house, and he shall walk before my anointed all the days.
1 Samuel 2:36 And it shall be that the survivor in your house will come to bow before him for an obol of silver, saying, Cast me into one of your priestly offices to eat bread.

## Chapter 3

1 Samuel 3:1 And the child Samuel ministered to the Lord before Eli the priest; and a word of the Lord was precious in those days, and there was no vision making distinctions.
1 Samuel 3:2 And it happened on that day that Eli slept in his place, and his eyes had begun to grow heavy, and he could not see,
1 Samuel 3:3 and before the lamp of God was tended, Samuel slept in the temple where the ark of God was,
1 Samuel 3:4 and the Lord called, Samuel, Samuel; and he said, Behold, I am here.
1 Samuel 3:5 And he ran to Eli and said, Behold, I am here, for you have called me; and he said, I did not call you; return and sleep. And he returned and slept.
1 Samuel 3:6 And the Lord continued and called, Samuel, Samuel; and he went to Eli a second time and said, Behold, I am here, for you have called me; and he said, I did not call you; return and sleep;
1 Samuel 3:7 and Samuel had not yet known God or had a word of the Lord revealed to him.
1 Samuel 3:8 And the Lord continued to call Samuel a third time; and he rose and went to Eli and said, Behold, I am here, for you have called me. And Eli understood that the Lord had called the child,
1 Samuel 3:9 and said, Return and sleep, child, and it shall be if he calls you, say, Speak, Lord, for your servant hears. And Samuel went and lay down in his place.
1 Samuel 3:10 And the Lord came and stood and called him as time and again, and Samuel said, Speak, for your servant hears.
1 Samuel 3:11 And the Lord said to Samuel, Behold, I am doing my words in Israel so that both ears of everyone who hears them will ring.
1 Samuel 3:12 On that day I shall raise up against Eli everything that I spoke concerning his house; I shall begin and finish.
1 Samuel 3:13 And I have told him that I shall exact punishment on his house forever for the injustices of his sons, for his sons spoke evil of God, and he did not admonish them, not even thus.
1 Samuel 3:14 I swore concerning Eli's house: The injustice of Eli's house shall certainly not be atoned for with incense and sacrifices forever.
1 Samuel 3:15 And Samuel slept until morning and rose early in the morning and opened the doors of the Lord's house; and Samuel feared to tell the vision to Eli.
1 Samuel 3:16 And Eli said to Samuel, Samuel, child; and he said, Behold, I am here.
1 Samuel 3:17 And he said, What was the word spoken to you? Do not hide it from me, please; thus may God do to you and thus may he add if you hide from me a word of all the words spoken in your ears.
1 Samuel 3:18 And Samuel told all the words and hid nothing from him, and Eli said, He is the Lord; he will do what is good before him.
1 Samuel 3:19 And Samuel grew great, and the Lord was with him, and none of all his words fell to the ground.
1 Samuel 3:20 And all Israel from Dan to Bersabee knew that Samuel was faithful as a prophet to the Lord.
1 Samuel 3:21 And the Lord continued to reveal himself in Selom, for the Lord was revealed to Samuel; and Samuel was entrusted to become a prophet to the Lord for all Israel from the ends of the land to the ends. And Eli was very old, and his sons went on their way, and their way was evil before the Lord.

## Chapter 4

1 Samuel 4:1 And it happened in those days that the foreigners gathered for war against Israel; and Israel went out to meet them in war and encamped by Abenezer, and the foreigners encamped in Aphek.
1 Samuel 4:2 And the foreigners drew up for war against Israel; and the battle turned, and the men of Israel stumbled before the foreigners, and four thousand men were struck in the battle in the field.
1 Samuel 4:3 And the people came to the camp, and the elders of Israel said, Why did the Lord make us stumble today before the foreigners? Let us take the ark of our God from Selom, and let it go out among us and save us from the hand of our enemies.
1 Samuel 4:4 And the people sent to Selom, and they carried from there the ark of the Lord who sits upon cherubim; and both sons of Eli were with the ark, Ophni and Phinees.
1 Samuel 4:5 And it happened when the ark of the Lord came into the camp that all Israel cried out with a loud voice, and the earth sounded.
1 Samuel 4:6 And the foreigners heard the cry and said, What is this great cry in the Hebrews' camp? And they learned that the ark of the Lord had come into the camp.
1 Samuel 4:7 And the foreigners feared and said, These gods have come to them into the camp; woe to us! Deliver us, Lord, today, for such a thing has not happened yesterday or the third day.
1 Samuel 4:8 Woe to us! Who will deliver us from the hand of these strong gods? These are the gods who struck Egypt with every blow and in the wilderness.
1 Samuel 4:9 Be strong and become men, foreigners, lest you serve the Hebrews as they served us; and be men and fight them.
1 Samuel 4:10 And they fought them; and the men of Israel stumbled, and each fled to his dwelling; and there was a very great blow, and thirty thousand of Israel's ranks fell.
1 Samuel 4:11 And the ark of God was taken, and both sons of Eli died, Ophni and Phinees.
1 Samuel 4:12 And a Ieminite man ran from the battle and came to Selom on that day, with his garments torn and earth upon his head.
1 Samuel 4:13 And he came, and behold, Eli sat on the seat by the gate watching the road, for his heart was beside itself concerning the ark of God; and the man entered the city to report, and the city cried out.
1 Samuel 4:14 And Eli heard the sound of the cry and said, What is the cry of this sound? And the man hurried in and reported to Eli.
1 Samuel 4:15 And Eli was a son of ninety years, and his eyes had risen up, and he could not see; and Eli said to the men standing around him, What is the sound of this noise?
1 Samuel 4:16 And the man hurried and approached Eli and said to him, I am the one who has come from the camp, and I fled from the battle today. And he said, What is the thing that happened, child?
1 Samuel 4:17 And the young man answered and said, The men of Israel have fled before the foreigners, and there was a great blow among the people, and both your sons are dead, and the ark of God was taken.
1 Samuel 4:18 And it happened when he mentioned the ark of God that Eli fell backward from the seat near the gate, and his back was broken and he died, for the man was old and heavy; and he had judged Israel twenty years.
1 Samuel 4:19 And his daughter-in-law, Phinees' wife, was pregnant and about to give birth; and she heard the report that the ark of God had been taken and that her father-in-law and husband were dead, and she bent down and gave birth, for her pains turned upon her.
1 Samuel 4:20 And at her time she was dying, and the women standing by her said to her, Do not fear, for you have borne a son; and she did not answer, and her heart did not take notice.
1 Samuel 4:21 And she called the child Ouai Barchaboth because of the ark of God and because of her father-in-law and husband.
1 Samuel 4:22 And they said, The glory of Israel has gone into exile when the ark of the Lord was taken.

## Chapter 5

1 Samuel 5:1 And the foreigners took the ark of God and brought it from Abennezer to Azotus.
1 Samuel 5:2 And the foreigners took the ark of the Lord and brought it into the house of Dagon and set it beside Dagon.
1 Samuel 5:3 And the Azotians rose early and entered Dagon's house and saw, and behold, Dagon had fallen on his face before the ark of God; and they raised Dagon and set him in his place. And the Lord's hand grew heavy upon the Azotians and tormented them and struck them in their seats, Azotus and its borders.
1 Samuel 5:4 And it happened when they rose early in the morning that behold, Dagon had fallen on his face before the ark of the Lord's covenant, and Dagon's head and both traces of his hands had been removed to the front of amaphet, each one, and both wrists of his hands had fallen upon the threshold; only Dagon's back was left.
1 Samuel 5:5 For this reason Dagon's priests and everyone entering Dagon's house do not step upon the step of Dagon's house in Azotus to this day, for they step over it. –
1 Samuel 5:6 And the Lord's hand grew heavy upon Azotus, and he brought upon them, and it boiled up for them into the ships, and mice sprang up in the midst of their country, and there was great confusion of death in the city.
1 Samuel 5:7 And the men of Azotus saw that it was thus and said, The ark of the God of Israel shall not remain with us, for his hand is hard upon us and upon Dagon our god.
1 Samuel 5:8 And they sent and gathered the satraps of the foreigners to them and said, What shall we do with the ark of the God of Israel? And the Getthites said, Let the ark of God move to us; and the ark of God moved to Gettha.
1 Samuel 5:9 And it happened after it moved that the Lord's hand came upon the city, a very great disturbance, and he struck the men of the city from small to great and struck them in their seats, and the Getthites made seats for themselves.
1 Samuel 5:10 And they sent the ark of God to Ascalon, and it happened when the ark of God entered Ascalon that the Ascalonites cried out, saying, Why did you send the ark of the God of Israel back to us to put us and our people to death?
1 Samuel 5:11 And they sent and gathered the satraps of the foreigners and said, Send away the ark of the God of Israel, and let it settle in its place and it shall certainly not put us and our people to death; for a very heavy confusion of death came upon the whole city when the ark of the God of Israel entered there,
1 Samuel 5:12 and those alive who had not died were struck in their seats, and the cry of the city went up to heaven.

## Chapter 6

1 Samuel 6:1 And the ark was in the field of the foreigners seven months, and their land boiled up with mice.
1 Samuel 6:2 And the foreigners called their priests and their diviners and their enchanters, saying, What shall we do with the ark of the Lord? Make known to us with what we shall send it to its place.
1 Samuel 6:3 And they said, If you send away the ark of the covenant of the Lord God of Israel, do not send it away empty, but surely return to it a payment for the torment; then you shall be healed, and atonement shall be made for you, lest his hand fail to depart from you.
1 Samuel 6:4 And they said, What payment for the torment shall we return to it? And they said, According to the number of the satraps of the foreigners, five golden seats, for there is one stumbling for you and your rulers and the people,
1 Samuel 6:5 and golden mice, likenesses of your mice that are destroying the land; and you shall give glory to the Lord, so that he may lighten his hand from upon you and from your gods and from your land.
1 Samuel 6:6 And why do you make your hearts heavy, as Egypt and Pharaoh made their heart heavy? Was it not when he made sport of them that they sent them away and they departed?
1 Samuel 6:7 And now take and make a new wagon and two cows giving birth for the first time, without their offspring, and yoke the cows to the wagon and lead their offspring away from behind them into the house;
1 Samuel 6:8 and you shall take the ark and put it upon the wagon, and the golden objects you shall return to it for the torment and put in a container, bersechthan, beside it, and you shall send it away and drive it away, and it shall depart;
1 Samuel 6:9 and you shall watch: if it travels on the road to its territory toward Baithsamys, he has done this great evil to us; but if not, we shall know that his hand has not touched us, but this has happened to us by chance.
1 Samuel 6:10 And the foreigners did thus and took two cows giving birth for the first time and yoked them to the wagon and held their offspring back in the house
1 Samuel 6:11 and put the ark upon the wagon and the container, ergab, and the golden mice.
1 Samuel 6:12 And the cows went straight on the road toward Baithsamys; they traveled on one path and labored and did not turn to the right or left; and the satraps of the foreigners went after it as far as the territory of Baithsamys.
1 Samuel 6:13 And those in Baithsamys were harvesting the wheat harvest in the valley; and they lifted their eyes and saw the ark of the Lord and rejoiced to meet it.
1 Samuel 6:14 And the wagon entered the field of Osee in Baithsamys, and they stood a great stone there beside it and split the wood of the wagon and offered the cows as a whole burnt offering to the Lord.
1 Samuel 6:15 And the Levites lifted up the ark of the Lord and the container, ergab, with it and the golden objects upon it and set them upon the great stone, and the men of Baithsamys offered whole burnt offerings and sacrifices to the Lord on that day.
1 Samuel 6:16 And the five satraps of the foreigners watched and returned to Ascalon on that day.
1 Samuel 6:17 And these are the golden seats which the foreigners returned to the Lord for the torment: one for Azotus, one for Gaza, one for Ascalon, one for Geth, one for Akkaron.
1 Samuel 6:18 And the golden mice were according to the number of all the cities of the foreigners of the five satraps, from a fortified city to a village of the Pherezite and as far as the great stone upon which they placed the ark of the Lord's covenant, which is in the field of Osee the Baithsamysite.
1 Samuel 6:19 And the sons of Iechonias among the men of Baithsamys did not welcome it, because they saw the ark of the Lord; and he struck among them seventy men and fifty thousand men. And the people mourned, for the Lord had struck among the people a very great blow.
1 Samuel 6:20 And the men from Baithsamys said, Who shall be able to pass before this holy Lord? And to whom shall the ark of the Lord go up from us?
1 Samuel 6:21 And they sent messengers to the inhabitants of Kariathiarim, saying, The foreigners have returned the ark of the Lord; come down and bring it up to yourselves.

## Chapter 7

1 Samuel 7:1 And the men of Kariathiarim came and brought up the ark of the Lord's covenant and brought it into the house of Aminadab on the hill; and they consecrated Eleazar his son to guard the ark of the Lord's covenant.
1 Samuel 7:2 And it happened from the day the ark was in Kariathiarim that the days multiplied and became twenty years, and all the house of Israel looked after the Lord.
1 Samuel 7:3 And Samuel said to all the house of Israel, saying, If you are returning to the Lord with all your heart, remove the foreign gods from your midst and the groves and prepare your hearts for the Lord and serve him alone, and he will deliver you from the hand of the foreigners.
1 Samuel 7:4 And the sons of Israel removed the Baals and the groves of Astaroth and served the Lord alone.
1 Samuel 7:5 And Samuel said, Gather all Israel to Massephath, and I shall pray for you to the Lord.
1 Samuel 7:6 And they gathered at Massephath and drew water and poured it on the ground before the Lord and fasted on that day and said, We have sinned before the Lord; and Samuel judged the sons of Israel at Massephath.
1 Samuel 7:7 And the foreigners heard that all the sons of Israel had gathered at Massephath, and the satraps of the foreigners came up against Israel; and the sons of Israel heard and feared before the foreigners.
1 Samuel 7:8 And the sons of Israel said to Samuel, Do not fall silent from us, so as not to cry out to the Lord your God, and he will save us from the hand of the foreigners.
1 Samuel 7:9 And Samuel took one suckling lamb and offered it as a whole burnt offering with all the people to the Lord, and Samuel cried to the Lord for Israel, and the Lord listened to him.
1 Samuel 7:10 And Samuel was offering up the whole burnt offering, and the foreigners approached to wage war against Israel. And the Lord thundered with a great voice on that day against the foreigners, and they were thrown into confusion and stumbled before Israel.
1 Samuel 7:11 And the men of Israel went out from Massephath and pursued the foreigners and struck them as far as below Baithchor.
1 Samuel 7:12 And Samuel took one stone and set it between Massephath and the old place and called its name Abenezer, Stone of the Helper, and said, Thus far the Lord has helped us.
1 Samuel 7:13 And the Lord humbled the foreigners, and they no longer continued to approach the territory of Israel; and the Lord's hand was upon the foreigners all the days of Samuel.
1 Samuel 7:14 And the cities which the foreigners had taken from the sons of Israel were returned, and they returned them to Israel from Ascalon as far as Azob, and they took Israel's territory from the hand of the foreigners. And there was peace between Israel and the Amorite.
1 Samuel 7:15 And Samuel judged Israel all the days of his life;
1 Samuel 7:16 and he went year by year and made a circuit of Bethel and Galgala and Massephath and judged Israel in all these consecrated places,
1 Samuel 7:17 but his return was to Armathaim, for his house was there, and he judged Israel there and built an altar there to the Lord.

## Chapter 8

1 Samuel 8:1 And it happened when Samuel grew old that he appointed his sons judges for Israel.
1 Samuel 8:2 And these are the names of his sons: the firstborn Ioel, and the name of the second Abia, judges in Bersabee.
1 Samuel 8:3 And his sons did not walk in his way but turned aside after the completion and took gifts and bent judgments.
1 Samuel 8:4 And the men of Israel gathered and came to Samuel at Armathaim
1 Samuel 8:5 and said to him, Behold, you have grown old, and your sons do not walk in your way; and now appoint a king over us to judge us, as also the remaining nations have.
1 Samuel 8:6 And the thing was evil in Samuel's eyes when they said, Give us a king to judge us; and Samuel prayed to the Lord.
1 Samuel 8:7 And the Lord said to Samuel, Listen to the voice of the people as they speak to you; for they have not despised you, but have despised me, that I should not reign over them.
1 Samuel 8:8 According to all the deeds they have done to me from the day I brought them up from Egypt until this day, and they abandoned me and served other gods, thus they are doing to you also.
1 Samuel 8:9 And now listen to their voice; nevertheless solemnly bear witness to them and tell them the ordinance of the king who shall reign over them.
1 Samuel 8:10 And Samuel spoke every word of the Lord to the people who asked him for a king
1 Samuel 8:11 and said, This shall be the ordinance of the king who shall reign over you: he will take your sons and place them among his chariots and his horsemen and as runners before his chariots,
1 Samuel 8:12 and appoint them for himself as commanders of thousands and commanders of hundreds, and to reap his harvest and gather his vintage and make his weapons of war and the equipment of his chariots;
1 Samuel 8:13 and he will take your daughters as perfumers and cooks and bakers;
1 Samuel 8:14 and he will take your good fields and your vineyards and your olive groves and give them to his servants;
1 Samuel 8:15 and he will take a tenth of your seed and your vineyards and give it to his eunuchs and his servants;
1 Samuel 8:16 and he will take your male servants and female servants and your good cattle herds and your donkeys and take a tenth for his work,
1 Samuel 8:17 and he will take a tenth of your flocks; and you shall be his servants.
1 Samuel 8:18 And you shall cry out on that day because of your king whom you chose for yourselves, and the Lord will not listen to you in those days, for you chose a king for yourselves.
1 Samuel 8:19 And the people did not wish to listen to Samuel and said to him, No, but a king shall be over us,
1 Samuel 8:20 and we too shall be like all the nations, and our king shall judge us and go out before us and fight our war.
1 Samuel 8:21 And Samuel heard all the words of the people and spoke them in the ears of the Lord.
1 Samuel 8:22 And the Lord said to Samuel, Listen to their voice and make a king reign over them. And Samuel said to the men of Israel, Let each run away to his city.

## Chapter 9

1 Samuel 9:1 And there was a man from the sons of Benjamin, and his name was Kis son of Abiel son of Sared son of Bachir son of Aphek son of a Ieminite man, a mighty man.
1 Samuel 9:2 And he had a son, and his name was Saul, of good size, a good man, and there was no one among the sons of Israel better than he, tall above all the land from the shoulders upward.
1 Samuel 9:3 And the donkeys of Kis, Saul's father, were lost, and Kis said to Saul his son, Take one of the young men with you, and rise and go and seek the donkeys.
1 Samuel 9:4 And they passed through the hill country of Ephraim and through the land of Selcha and did not find them; and they passed through the land of Easakem, and they were not there; and they passed through the land of Iakim and did not find them.
1 Samuel 9:5 When they came to Siph, Saul said to his young man who was with him, Come and let us return, lest my father, leaving the donkeys, be concerned about us.
1 Samuel 9:6 And the young man said to him, Behold, a man of God is in this city, and the man is honored; everything he speaks will surely come to pass; and now let us go, so that he may tell us our way upon which we have traveled.
1 Samuel 9:7 And Saul said to his young man who was with him, And behold, we shall go, but what shall we bring to the man of God? For the loaves have run out from our vessels, and there is nothing more with us to bring to the man of God from what we have.
1 Samuel 9:8 And the young man answered Saul further and said, Behold, a quarter shekel of silver has been found in my hand, and you shall give it to the man of God, and he will tell us our way.
1 Samuel 9:9 And formerly in Israel each said thus when going to inquire of God: Come, let us go to the one who sees; for formerly the people called the prophet the one who sees.
1 Samuel 9:10 And Saul said to his young man, The word is good; come and let us go. And they went to the city where the man of God was.
1 Samuel 9:11 As they were going up the ascent to the city, they found young women who had come out to draw water and said to them, Is the one who sees here?
1 Samuel 9:12 And the young women answered them and said to them, He is; behold, he is before you. Now, for today he has come to the city, for there is a sacrifice today for the people at Bama;
1 Samuel 9:13 as you enter the city, so you shall find him in the city before he goes up to Bama to eat, for the people shall certainly not eat until he enters, for he blesses the sacrifice, and after this the guests eat; and now go up, for today you shall find him.
1 Samuel 9:14 And they went up to the city. As they entered the midst of the city, behold, Samuel came out to meet them to go up to Bama.
1 Samuel 9:15 And the Lord had uncovered Samuel's ear one day before Saul came to him, saying,
1 Samuel 9:16 About this time tomorrow I shall send you a man from the land of Benjamin, and you shall anoint him as ruler over my people Israel, and he will save my people from the hand of the foreigners; for I looked upon the humiliation of my people, for their cry has come to me.
1 Samuel 9:17 And Samuel saw Saul; and the Lord answered him, Behold the man of whom I said to you, This one shall rule among my people.
1 Samuel 9:18 And Saul approached Samuel in the midst of the city and said, Tell me, please, which is the house of the one who sees.
1 Samuel 9:19 And Samuel answered Saul and said, I am he; go up before me to Bama and eat with me today, and I shall send you away in the morning and tell you everything in your heart;
1 Samuel 9:20 and concerning your donkeys that have been lost three days today, do not set your heart on them, for they have been found; and for whom are the beautiful things of Israel? Are they not for you and your father's house?
1 Samuel 9:21 And Saul answered and said, Am I not a son of a Ieminite man, of the small scepter of a tribe of Israel, and of the least family of the whole scepter of Benjamin? And why have you spoken to me according to this word?
1 Samuel 9:22 And Samuel took Saul and his young man and led them into the lodging and gave them a place among the first of those invited, about seventy men.
1 Samuel 9:23 And Samuel said to the cook, Give me the portion I gave you, which I told you to place beside you.
1 Samuel 9:24 And the cook lifted up the leg and set it before Saul; and Samuel said to Saul, Behold the remainder; place it before you and eat, for it has been set aside for you as a witness beyond the others; gnaw it off. And Saul ate with Samuel on that day.
1 Samuel 9:25 And he went down from Bama into the city; and they spread a bed for Saul on the roof,
1 Samuel 9:26 and he slept. And it happened as dawn rose that Samuel called Saul on the roof, saying, Rise, and I shall send you away; and Saul rose, and he and Samuel went out as far as outside.
1 Samuel 9:27 As they were going down toward a part of the city, Samuel said to Saul, Tell the young man to pass before us, and you stand still as today and hear a word of God.

## Chapter 10

1 Samuel 10:1 And Samuel took the flask of oil and poured it upon his head and kissed him and said to him, Has not the Lord anointed you as ruler over his people, over Israel? And you shall rule among the Lord's people, and you shall save them from the hand of their enemies all around. And this shall be the sign for you that the Lord anointed you as ruler over his inheritance:
1 Samuel 10:2 when you depart from me today, you shall find two men by Rachel's tombs in the territory of Benjamin leaping greatly, and they will say to you, The donkeys which you went to seek have been found, and behold, your father has cast off the matter of the donkeys and has been lavishly concerned for you, saying, What shall I do for my son?
1 Samuel 10:3 And you shall go on from there and arrive at the oak of Thabor and find there three men going up to God at Bethel, one carrying three young goats and one carrying three vessels of bread and one carrying a skin of wine;
1 Samuel 10:4 and they shall ask you the things of peace and give you two first portions of bread, and you shall take them from their hand.
1 Samuel 10:5 And after these things you shall enter the hill of God, where the standing place of the foreigners is, there Nasib the foreigner; and it shall be as you enter the city there that you shall meet a chorus of prophets coming down from Bama, and before them a harp and a tambourine and a flute and a lyre, and they prophesying;
1 Samuel 10:6 and the spirit of the Lord shall leap upon you, and you shall prophesy with them and be turned into another man.
1 Samuel 10:7 And it shall be when these signs come upon you, do whatever your hand finds, for God is with you.
1 Samuel 10:8 And you shall go down before Galgala, and behold, I am coming down to you to offer a whole burnt offering and peace sacrifices; you shall wait seven days until I come to you, and I shall make known to you what you shall do.
1 Samuel 10:9 And it happened when he turned his shoulder to depart from Samuel that God changed for him another heart; and all the signs came on that day.
1 Samuel 10:10 And he came from there to the hill, and behold, a chorus of prophets opposite him; and the spirit of God leaped upon him, and he prophesied among them.
1 Samuel 10:11 And all who knew him yesterday and the third day saw, and behold, he was among the prophets, and the people said, each to his neighbor, What is this that has happened to the son of Kis? Is Saul also among the prophets?
1 Samuel 10:12 And one of them answered and said, And who is his father? Therefore it became a proverb: Is Saul also among the prophets?
1 Samuel 10:13 And he finished prophesying and came to the hill.
1 Samuel 10:14 And his relative said to him and to his young man, Where did you go? And they said, To seek the donkeys; and we saw that they were not there, and we went to Samuel.
1 Samuel 10:15 And the relative said to Saul, Tell me, please, what Samuel said to you.
1 Samuel 10:16 And Saul said to his relative, He indeed told me that the donkeys had been found; but he did not tell him the matter of the kingdom.
1 Samuel 10:17 And Samuel summoned all the people to the Lord at Massepha
1 Samuel 10:18 and said to the sons of Israel, Thus said the Lord God of Israel: I brought the sons of Israel up from Egypt and delivered you from the hand of Pharaoh king of Egypt and from all the kingdoms that oppressed you;
1 Samuel 10:19 and today you despised God, who himself is your savior from all your evils and afflictions, and said, No, but you shall set a king over us; and now stand before the Lord according to your scepters and according to your tribes.
1 Samuel 10:20 And Samuel brought forward all the scepters of Israel, and the scepter of Benjamin was allotted;
1 Samuel 10:21 and he brought forward the scepter of Benjamin by families, and the family of Mattari was allotted; and they brought forward the family of Mattari by men, and Saul son of Kis was allotted. And they sought him, and he was not found.
1 Samuel 10:22 And Samuel inquired of the Lord again, Has the man come here? And the Lord said, Behold, he is hidden among the equipment.
1 Samuel 10:23 And he ran and took him from there and stood him in the midst of the people, and he stood taller than all the people from the shoulders upward.
1 Samuel 10:24 And Samuel said to all the people, Have you seen the one whom the Lord chose for himself, that there is none like him among you all? And all the people acknowledged it and said, Long live the king.
1 Samuel 10:25 And Samuel told the people the ordinance of the king and wrote it in a book and placed it before the Lord. And Samuel sent all the people away, and each departed to his place.
1 Samuel 10:26 And Saul departed to his house in Gabaa; and sons of might whose hearts the Lord touched went with Saul.
1 Samuel 10:27 And pestilent sons said, How will this one save us? And they dishonored him and brought him no gifts.

## Chapter 11

1 Samuel 11:1 And it happened as after a month that Naas the Ammanite went up and encamped against Jabis Galaad. And all the men of Jabis said to Naas the Ammanite, Make a covenant with us, and we will serve you.
1 Samuel 11:2 And Naas the Ammanite said to them, On this condition I will make a covenant with you: by gouging out every right eye of yours; and I will put a reproach upon Israel.
1 Samuel 11:3 And the men of Jabis say to him, Allow us seven days, and we will send messengers into all the territory of Israel; if there is no one to save us, we will come out to you.
1 Samuel 11:4 And the messengers come to Gabaa to Saul and speak the words in the ears of the people, and all the people raised their voice and wept.
1 Samuel 11:5 And behold, Saul was coming from the field after the morning, and Saul said, What is it that the people are weeping? And they recount to him the words of the sons of Jabis.
1 Samuel 11:6 And a spirit of the Lord leaped upon Saul when he heard these words, and his anger was exceedingly kindled against them.
1 Samuel 11:7 And he took two oxen and cut them in pieces and sent them into all the territory of Israel by the hand of messengers, saying, Whoever does not go out after Saul and after Samuel, thus shall they do to his oxen. And a dread of the Lord came upon the people of Israel, and they cried out as one man.
1 Samuel 11:8 And Abiezek musters them in Bama: every man of Israel, six hundred thousand, and the men of Judah, seventy thousand.
1 Samuel 11:9 And he said to the messengers who had come, Thus you shall say to the men of Jabis: Tomorrow salvation shall be yours when the sun has grown hot. And the messengers came into the city and reported to the men of Jabis, and they rejoiced.
1 Samuel 11:10 And the men of Jabis said to Naas the Ammanite, Tomorrow we will come out to you, and you will do to us what is good in your eyes.
1 Samuel 11:11 And it happened on the next day that Saul set the people in three divisions, and they enter the midst of the camp in the morning watch and struck the sons of Ammon until the day grew hot; and it happened that those remaining were scattered, and two of them were not left together.
1 Samuel 11:12 And the people said to Samuel, Who is the one who said that Saul shall not reign over us? Hand over the men, and we will put them to death.
1 Samuel 11:13 And Saul said, No one shall die on this day, because today the Lord has made salvation in Israel.
1 Samuel 11:14 And Samuel said to the people, saying, Let us go to Galgala and renew the kingdom there.
1 Samuel 11:15 And all the people went to Galgala, and Samuel anointed Saul there as king before the Lord in Galgalois and offered sacrifices and peace offerings there before the Lord; and Samuel and all Israel rejoiced exceedingly.

## Chapter 12

1 Samuel 12:1 And Samuel said to every man of Israel, Behold, I listened to your voice in all that you said to me, and I made a king reign over you.
1 Samuel 12:2 And now, behold, the king goes about before you, and I have grown old and shall sit down, and my sons, behold, are among you; and I, behold, have gone about before you from my youth until this day.
1 Samuel 12:3 Behold, here I am. Answer against me before the Lord and before his anointed: whose calf have I taken, or whose donkey have I taken, or whom among you have I oppressed, or whom have I pressed hard, or from whose hand have I taken an atonement and a sandal? Answer against me, and I will repay you.
1 Samuel 12:4 And they said to Samuel, You have not wronged us, nor oppressed us, nor crushed us, nor taken anything from anyone's hand.
1 Samuel 12:5 And Samuel said to the people, The Lord is witness among you, and his anointed is witness today on this day that you have found nothing in my hand. And they said, Witness.
1 Samuel 12:6 And Samuel said to the people, saying, The Lord is witness, who made Moses and Aaron, who brought our fathers up from Egypt.
1 Samuel 12:7 And now stand forth, and I will judge you before the Lord and recount to you all the righteousness of the Lord, what he did among you and among your fathers:
1 Samuel 12:8 When Jacob and his sons entered Egypt, and Egypt humbled them, our fathers cried out to the Lord, and the Lord sent Moses and Aaron and brought our fathers out of Egypt and settled them in this place.
1 Samuel 12:9 And they forgot the Lord their God, and he gave them into the hands of Sisara, commander of the army of Jabin king of Asor, and into the hands of the foreigners, and into the hands of the king of Moab, and they fought against them.
1 Samuel 12:10 And they cried out to the Lord and said, We have sinned, because we abandoned the Lord and served the Baalim and the groves; and now deliver us from the hand of our enemies, and we will serve you.
1 Samuel 12:11 And the Lord sent Jerobaal and Barak and Jephthae and Samuel and delivered you from the hand of your enemies round about, and you dwelt in confidence.
1 Samuel 12:12 And you saw that Naas, king of the sons of Ammon, came against you, and you said, No, but a king shall reign over us; and the Lord our God was our king.
1 Samuel 12:13 And now, behold the king whom you chose, and behold, the Lord has given a king over you.
1 Samuel 12:14 If you fear the Lord and serve him and listen to his voice and do not contend with the mouth of the Lord, and both you and the king who reigns over you go after the Lord;
1 Samuel 12:15 but if you do not listen to the voice of the Lord and contend with the mouth of the Lord, then the hand of the Lord shall be upon you and upon your king.
1 Samuel 12:16 And now stand forth and see this great thing that the Lord will do before your eyes.
1 Samuel 12:17 Is it not wheat harvest today? I will call upon the Lord, and he will give thunderings and rain, and you shall know and see that your evil is great, which you did before the Lord in asking a king for yourselves.
1 Samuel 12:18 And Samuel called upon the Lord, and the Lord gave thunderings and rain on that day; and all the people greatly feared the Lord and Samuel.
1 Samuel 12:19 And all the people said to Samuel, Pray for your servants to the Lord your God, that we may not die, because we have added to all our sins an evil in asking a king for ourselves.
1 Samuel 12:20 And Samuel said to the people, Do not fear. You have done all this evil; only do not turn away from following the Lord, and serve the Lord with all your heart,
1 Samuel 12:21 and do not turn aside after the things that are nothing, which accomplish nothing and which do not deliver, because they are nothing.
1 Samuel 12:22 For the Lord will not reject his people for the sake of his great name, because the Lord was pleased to take you to himself as a people.
1 Samuel 12:23 And as for me, may it by no means be that I sin against the Lord by ceasing to pray for you; and I will serve the Lord and show you the good and straight way.
1 Samuel 12:24 Only fear the Lord and serve him in truth and with all your heart, for you have seen what great things he has done with you.
1 Samuel 12:25 And if you do evil with wickedness, both you and your king shall be added.

## Chapter 13

1 Samuel 13:1 And Saul chooses for himself three thousand men from the men of Israel, and two thousand were with Saul in Machemas and in the mountain of Bethel,
1 Samuel 13:2 and a thousand were with Jonathan in Gabee of Benjamin, and the remainder of the people he sent away, each to his dwelling.
1 Samuel 13:3 And Jonathan struck the Nasib, the foreigner who was on the hill; and the foreigners hear. And Saul sounds a trumpet throughout all the land, saying, The servants have rebelled.
1 Samuel 13:4 And all Israel heard them saying, Saul has struck the Nasib, the foreigner, and Israel was shamed among the foreigners. And the people cried out after Saul in Galgalois.
1 Samuel 13:5 And the foreigners gather for war against Israel, and come up against Israel: thirty thousand chariots and six thousand horsemen and people like the sand by the sea in multitude; and they come up and encamp in Machemas opposite Baithon toward the south.
1 Samuel 13:6 And a man of Israel saw that it was hard pressed for him not to draw near to him, and the people hid in the caves and in the folds and in the rocks and in the pits and in the cisterns,
1 Samuel 13:7 and those crossing crossed the Jordan into the land of Gad and Galaad. And Saul was still in Galgalois, and all the people were beside themselves following him. –
1 Samuel 13:8 And he waited seven days according to the testimony, as Samuel said, and Samuel did not come to Galgala, and his people were scattered away from him.
1 Samuel 13:9 And Saul said, Bring them near, so that I may make a whole burnt offering and peace offerings; and he offered up the whole burnt offering.
1 Samuel 13:10 And it happened as he finished offering up the whole burnt offering that Samuel arrived; and Saul went out to meet him to bless him.
1 Samuel 13:11 And Samuel said, What have you done? And Saul said, Because I saw that the people had scattered away from me and you did not come, as you appointed, within the testimony of the days, and the foreigners had gathered at Machemas,
1 Samuel 13:12 I said, Now the foreigners will come down against me at Galgala, and I have not entreated the face of the Lord; and I constrained myself and offered up the whole burnt offering.
1 Samuel 13:13 And Samuel said to Saul, It has been made vain for you, because you did not keep my commandment, which the Lord commanded you. For now the Lord would have established your kingdom forever over Israel;
1 Samuel 13:14 but now your kingdom shall not stand, and the Lord will seek for himself a man according to his heart, and the Lord will command him to be ruler over his people, because you did not keep what the Lord commanded you.
1 Samuel 13:15 And Samuel rose and departed from Galgalois on his way. – And the remainder of the people went up after Saul to meet, after the people of war. When they had come from Galgalois to Gabaa of Benjamin, Saul mustered the people found with him, about six hundred men.
1 Samuel 13:16 And Saul and Jonathan his son and the people found with them sat in Gabee of Benjamin and wept, and the foreigners had encamped at Machemas.
1 Samuel 13:17 And a destroyer went out from the camp of the foreigners in three divisions: the one division looking toward the road of Gophera toward the land of Sogal,
1 Samuel 13:18 and the one division looking toward the road of Baithoron, and the one division looking toward the road of Gabee, which bends toward Gai of Sabin.
1 Samuel 13:19 And no smith of iron was found in all the land of Israel, because the foreigners said, Let the Hebrews not make sword and spear.
1 Samuel 13:20 And all Israel would go down into the land of the foreigners to forge, each his harvesting tool and his implement and each his axe and his sickle.
1 Samuel 13:21 And the vintage was ready for harvesting; and the implements were three shekels for the tooth, and for the axe and the sickle the support was the same.
1 Samuel 13:22 And it happened in the days of the war of Machemas that neither sword nor spear was found in the hand of any of the people with Saul and with Jonathan, but one was found for Saul and Jonathan his son.
1 Samuel 13:23 And one went out from the outpost of the foreigners, the one beyond Machemas.

## Chapter 14

1 Samuel 14:1 And a day came, and Jonathan son of Saul said to the young man carrying his equipment, Come, and let us cross to the garrison of the foreigners on that far side; and he did not tell his father.
1 Samuel 14:2 And Saul was sitting at the edge of the hill under the pomegranate tree in Magdon, and there were about six hundred men with him;
1 Samuel 14:3 and Achia son of Achitob, brother of Jochabed, son of Phinees, son of Eli, priest of God in Selom, was carrying an ephod. And the people did not know that Jonathan had gone.
1 Samuel 14:4 And between the crossings, where Jonathan sought to cross to the outpost of the foreigners, there was a rocky projection on one side and a rocky projection on the other; the name of the one was Bazes and the name of the other Senna.
1 Samuel 14:5 The one way was from the north for one coming to Machmas, and the other way from the south for one coming to Gabee.
1 Samuel 14:6 And Jonathan said to the young man carrying his equipment, Come, let us cross to the garrison of these uncircumcised, if the Lord might do something for us; for the Lord is not constrained to save by many or by few.
1 Samuel 14:7 And the one carrying his equipment said to him, Do all to which your heart inclines; behold, I am with you, as your heart is my heart.
1 Samuel 14:8 And Jonathan said, Behold, we are crossing to the men and will roll down toward them.
1 Samuel 14:9 If they say thus to us, Stand there until we tell you, then we will stand where we are and will certainly not go up against them;
1 Samuel 14:10 and if they say thus to us, Come up to us, then we will go up, because the Lord has given them into our hands; this shall be the sign for us.
1 Samuel 14:11 And both entered the garrison of the foreigners; and the foreigners say, Behold, the Hebrews are coming out of their holes where they hid.
1 Samuel 14:12 And the men of the garrison answered Jonathan and the one carrying his equipment and say, Come up to us, and we will make a thing known to you. And Jonathan said to the one carrying his equipment, Come up after me, because the Lord has given them into the hands of Israel.
1 Samuel 14:13 And Jonathan went up on his hands and on his feet, and the one carrying his equipment with him; and they looked toward Jonathan's face, and he struck them, and the one carrying his equipment handed them over behind him.
1 Samuel 14:14 And the first blow which Jonathan and the one carrying his equipment struck was about twenty men, among missiles and stone throwers and pebbles of the plain.
1 Samuel 14:15 And there was terror in the camp and in the field, and all the people in the garrison and the destroyers were terrified, and they themselves were unwilling to act; and the land was amazed, and there was terror from the Lord.
1 Samuel 14:16 And Saul's watchmen in Gabee of Benjamin saw, and behold, the camp was in turmoil on this side and that.
1 Samuel 14:17 And Saul said to the people with him, Muster now and see who has gone from you; and they mustered, and behold, Jonathan and the one carrying his equipment were not found.
1 Samuel 14:18 And Saul said to Achia, Bring near the ephod; for he carried the ephod on that day before Israel.
1 Samuel 14:19 And it happened while Saul was speaking to the priest that the sound in the camp of the foreigners went on and increased; and Saul said to the priest, Gather your hands.
1 Samuel 14:20 And Saul and all the people with him cried out and came as far as the battle, and behold, the sword of one man was against his neighbor, a very great confusion.
1 Samuel 14:21 And the servants who had been with the foreigners yesterday and the third day, who had gone up into the camp, turned back to be themselves with the Israelites who were with Saul and Jonathan.
1 Samuel 14:22 And all Israel who were hiding in the mountain of Ephraim also heard that the foreigners had fled, and they too joined after them in battle.
1 Samuel 14:23 And the Lord saved Israel on that day. And the battle passed through Baithon, and all the people with Saul were about ten thousand men; and the battle was scattered through the whole city in the mountain of Ephraim.
1 Samuel 14:24 And Saul committed a great error on that day and put the people under a curse, saying, Cursed is the man who eats bread until evening, and I will avenge myself on my enemy; and none of the people tasted bread.
1 Samuel 14:25 And all the land ate a meal. And Jaar was a forest of bees facing the field,
1 Samuel 14:26 and the people entered the place of bees, and behold, it went along speaking, and behold, no one turned his hand to his mouth, because the people feared the oath of the Lord.
1 Samuel 14:27 And Jonathan had not heard when his father put the people under oath; and he stretched out the end of the staff in his hand and dipped it into the honeycomb and brought his hand back to his mouth, and his eyes looked up.
1 Samuel 14:28 And one of the people answered and said, Your father solemnly put the people under oath, saying, Cursed is the man who eats bread today; and the people were faint.
1 Samuel 14:29 And Jonathan understood and said, My father has troubled the land; see now that my eyes have seen, because I tasted a little of this honey.
1 Samuel 14:30 But if the people had eaten freely today from the spoils of their enemies that they found, surely now the blow among the foreigners would have been greater.
1 Samuel 14:31 And on that day he struck some of the foreigners in Machemas, and the people were exceedingly weary.
1 Samuel 14:32 And the people turned toward the spoils, and the people took flocks and herds and calves and slaughtered them on the ground, and the people ate with the blood.
1 Samuel 14:33 And it was reported to Saul, saying, The people have sinned against the Lord by eating with the blood. And Saul said in Geththem, Roll a large stone here for me.
1 Samuel 14:34 And Saul said, Spread out among the people and tell them to bring here each his calf and each his sheep, and let each slaughter on this, and you shall certainly not sin against the Lord by eating with the blood; and all the people brought, each, what was in his hand and slaughtered there.
1 Samuel 14:35 And Saul built an altar there to the Lord; this was what Saul began to build as an altar to the Lord.
1 Samuel 14:36 And Saul said, Let us go down after the foreigners by night and plunder among them until the day dawns, and let us leave no man among them. And they said, Do whatever is good in your eyes. And the priest said, Let us draw near here to God.
1 Samuel 14:37 And Saul asked God, Shall I go down after the foreigners? Will you give them into the hands of Israel? And he did not answer him on that day.
1 Samuel 14:38 And Saul said, Bring near here all the corners of Israel, and know and see with whom this sin has happened today;
1 Samuel 14:39 for the Lord who saved Israel lives, that even if it answers against Jonathan my son, he shall surely die. And there was no one answering among all the people.
1 Samuel 14:40 And he said to all Israel, You shall be in servitude, and I and Jonathan my son shall be in servitude. And the people said to Saul, Do what is good in your eyes.
1 Samuel 14:41 And Saul said, Lord God of Israel, why have you not answered your servant today?
