If the wrongdoing is in me or in Jonathan my son, Lord God of Israel, give clear signs; and if you say thus, In your people Israel, then give holiness. And Jonathan and Saul were taken by lot, and the people went out.
1 Samuel 14:42 And Saul said, Cast between me and Jonathan my son; let the one whom the Lord selects by lot die. And the people said to Saul, This word is not so. And Saul prevailed over the people, and they cast between him and Jonathan his son, and Jonathan was taken by lot.
1 Samuel 14:43 And Saul said to Jonathan, Tell me what you have done. And Jonathan told him and said, I tasted a little honey with the end of the staff in my hand; behold, I am dying.
1 Samuel 14:44 And Saul said to him, May God do thus to me and add thus, for you shall surely die today.
1 Samuel 14:45 And the people said to Saul, Shall the one who made this great salvation in Israel be put to death today? As the Lord lives, not a hair of his head shall fall to the ground; for the people of God made this day. And the people prayed for Jonathan on that day, and he did not die. –
1 Samuel 14:46 And Saul went up from pursuing the foreigners, and the foreigners went away to their place.
1 Samuel 14:47 And Saul is allotted a task over Israel. And he fought all his enemies round about: Moab and the sons of Ammon and the sons of Edom and Baitheor and the king of Souba and the foreigners; wherever he turned, he was saved.
1 Samuel 14:48 And he made a force and struck Amalek and delivered Israel from the hand of those trampling him. –
1 Samuel 14:49 And the sons of Saul were Jonathan and Jessiou and Melchisa; and the names of his two daughters: the name of the firstborn was Merob, and the name of the second Melchol;
1 Samuel 14:50 and the name of his wife was Achinoom, daughter of Achimaas. And the name of his commander was Abenner, son of Ner, son of a kinsman of Saul;
1 Samuel 14:51 and Kis, Saul's father, and Ner, Abenner's father, son of Jamin son of Abiel. –
1 Samuel 14:52 And the war against the foreigners was strong all the days of Saul, and Saul saw every mighty man and every man who was a son of might and gathered them to himself.

## Chapter 15

1 Samuel 15:1 And Samuel said to Saul, The Lord sent me to anoint you king over Israel, and now hear the voice of the Lord:
1 Samuel 15:2 Thus said the Lord Sabaoth: Now I will avenge what Amalek did to Israel, how he met him on the way as he came up from Egypt;
1 Samuel 15:3 and now go and strike Amalek and Jerim and all that belongs to him, and you shall preserve nothing of his, and you shall destroy him utterly and devote him and all that belongs to him, and you shall not spare him, and you shall kill from man to woman and from infant to suckling and from calf to sheep and from camel to donkey.
1 Samuel 15:4 And Saul gave orders to the people and mustered them in Galgalois, four hundred thousand in companies, and Judah, thirty thousand in companies.
1 Samuel 15:5 And Saul came as far as the cities of Amalek and lay in wait in the torrent bed.
1 Samuel 15:6 And Saul said to the Kenite, Go away and turn aside from the midst of the Amalekite, lest I add you with him, for you showed mercy to the sons of Israel when they came up from Egypt; and the Kenite turned aside from the midst of Amalek.
1 Samuel 15:7 And Saul struck Amalek from Euilat to Sour, facing Egypt.
1 Samuel 15:8 And he captured Agag king of Amalek alive and killed all the people of Jerim by the edge of the sword.
1 Samuel 15:9 And Saul and all the people preserved Agag alive and the good things of the flocks and the herds and the foodstuffs and the vineyards and all the good things, and they did not wish to destroy them utterly; and every work that was dishonored and despised they destroyed utterly.
1 Samuel 15:10 And the word of the Lord came to Samuel, saying,
1 Samuel 15:11 I am grieved that I made Saul king, because he has turned back from following me and has not kept my words. And Samuel was disheartened and cried out to the Lord all night.
1 Samuel 15:12 And Samuel rose early and went to meet Israel in the morning. And it was reported to Samuel, saying, Saul has come to Carmel and has set up a hand for himself and has turned the chariot. And he went down to Galgala to Saul, and behold, he was offering to the Lord as a whole burnt offering the first of the spoils that he had brought from Amalek.
1 Samuel 15:13 And Samuel came to Saul, and Saul said to him, Blessed are you to the Lord; I have established all that the Lord spoke.
1 Samuel 15:14 And Samuel said, And what is this sound of the flock in my ears and the sound of the oxen that I hear?
1 Samuel 15:15 And Saul said, I brought them from Amalek, what the people preserved, the best of the flock and the oxen, so that they might be sacrificed to the Lord your God, and the rest I destroyed utterly.
1 Samuel 15:16 And Samuel said to Saul, Stop, and I will tell you what the Lord spoke to me in the night. And he said to him, Speak.
1 Samuel 15:17 And Samuel said to Saul, Are you not small before him, a leader of the scepter of a tribe of Israel? And the Lord anointed you king over Israel.
1 Samuel 15:18 And the Lord sent you on a way and said to you, Go and destroy utterly those sinning against me, Amalek, and you shall fight them until you finish them.
1 Samuel 15:19 And why did you not listen to the voice of the Lord, but rushed to lay hands on the spoils and did what was evil before the Lord?
1 Samuel 15:20 And Saul said to Samuel, Because I listened to the voice of the people; and I went on the way on which the Lord sent me, and I brought Agag king of Amalek and destroyed Amalek utterly;
1 Samuel 15:21 and the people took from the spoils flocks and herds, the first of what was devoted to destruction, to sacrifice before the Lord our God in Galgalois.
1 Samuel 15:22 And Samuel said, Are whole burnt offerings and sacrifices desired by the Lord as much as listening to the voice of the Lord? Behold, hearing is better than a good sacrifice, and attentive listening better than the fat of rams;
1 Samuel 15:23 for sin is an omen; pain and labors bring teraphim. Because you despised the word of the Lord, the Lord will despise you so that you are not king over Israel.
1 Samuel 15:24 And Saul said to Samuel, I have sinned, because I transgressed the word of the Lord and your saying, because I feared the people and listened to their voice;
1 Samuel 15:25 and now, take away my sin and turn back with me, and I will worship the Lord your God.
1 Samuel 15:26 And Samuel said to Saul, I will not turn back with you, because you despised the word of the Lord, and the Lord will despise you so that you are not king over Israel.
1 Samuel 15:27 And Samuel turned his face to depart. And Saul grasped the edge of his cloak and tore it;
1 Samuel 15:28 and Samuel said to him, The Lord has torn the kingdom of Israel from your hand today and will give it to your neighbor who is better than you;
1 Samuel 15:29 and Israel shall be divided in two, and he will not turn back nor repent, because he is not like a man so as to repent.
1 Samuel 15:30 And Saul said, I have sinned, but honor me now before the elders of Israel and before my people and turn back with me, and I will worship the Lord your God.
1 Samuel 15:31 And Samuel turned back after Saul, and he worshiped the Lord.
1 Samuel 15:32 And Samuel said, Bring Agag king of Amalek to me. And Agag came to him trembling, and Agag said, Is death so bitter?
1 Samuel 15:33 And Samuel said to Agag, As your sword made women childless, so your mother shall be made childless among women. And Samuel slaughtered Agag before the Lord in Galgal.
1 Samuel 15:34 And Samuel departed to Armathaim, and Saul went up to his house in Gabaa.
1 Samuel 15:35 And Samuel did not again see Saul until the day of his death, because Samuel mourned for Saul; and the Lord regretted that he had made Saul king over Israel.

## Chapter 16

1 Samuel 16:1 And the Lord said to Samuel, How long do you mourn over Saul, when I have rejected him from reigning over Israel? Fill your horn with oil, and come, I will send you to Jesse as far as Bethlehem, because I have seen among his sons one to reign for me.
1 Samuel 16:2 And Samuel said, How shall I go? Saul will hear and kill me. And the Lord said, Take a heifer of the cattle in your hand, and you shall say, I have come to sacrifice to the Lord;
1 Samuel 16:3 and you shall call Jesse to the sacrifice, and I will make known to you what you shall do, and you shall anoint the one whom I tell you.
1 Samuel 16:4 And Samuel did all that the Lord spoke to him and came to Bethlehem. And the elders of the city were startled at meeting him and said, Is your coming peace, seer?
1 Samuel 16:5 And he said, Peace. I have come to sacrifice to the Lord; sanctify yourselves and rejoice with me today. And he sanctified Jesse and his sons and called them to the sacrifice.
1 Samuel 16:6 And it happened as they entered that he saw Eliab and said, Surely even before the Lord is his anointed.
1 Samuel 16:7 And the Lord said to Samuel, Do not look upon his appearance nor upon the bearing of his stature, because I have rejected him; for God will not see as a man looks, because a man will look at a face, but God will look at a heart.
1 Samuel 16:8 And Jesse called Aminadab, and he passed before Samuel; and he said, The Lord has not chosen this one either.
1 Samuel 16:9 And Jesse brought Sama forward; and he said, The Lord has not chosen this one either.
1 Samuel 16:10 And Jesse brought his seven sons before Samuel; and Samuel said, The Lord has not chosen among these.
1 Samuel 16:11 And Samuel said to Jesse, Have the young men run out? And he said, There is still the little one; behold, he tends the flock. And Samuel said to Jesse, Send and fetch him, because we will certainly not recline until he comes.
1 Samuel 16:12 And he sent and brought him in; and he was ruddy, with beauty of eyes and good in appearance to the Lord; and the Lord said to Samuel, Rise and anoint David, because this one is good.
1 Samuel 16:13 And Samuel took the horn of oil and anointed him in the midst of his brothers, and a spirit of the Lord leaped upon David from that day onward. And Samuel rose and departed to Armathaim.
1 Samuel 16:14 And a spirit of the Lord departed from Saul, and an evil spirit from the Lord choked him.
1 Samuel 16:15 And Saul's servants said to him, Behold now, an evil spirit of the Lord chokes you;
1 Samuel 16:16 let your servants now speak before you and seek for our lord a man who knows how to play on a lyre, and it shall be, when an evil spirit is upon you, that he will play on his lyre, and it shall be good for you, and he will give you rest.
1 Samuel 16:17 And Saul said to his servants, See now for me a man who plays well and bring him to me.
1 Samuel 16:18 And one of his young men answered and said, Behold, I have seen a son of Jesse the Bethlehemite, and he knows a song, and the man is discerning, and the man is a warrior and wise in speech and a man good in appearance, and the Lord is with him.
1 Samuel 16:19 And Saul sent messengers to Jesse, saying, Send to me your son David who is with your flock.
1 Samuel 16:20 And Jesse took a gomor of bread and a skin of wine and one kid of the goats and sent them by the hand of David his son to Saul.
1 Samuel 16:21 And David came to Saul and stood before him; and he loved him greatly, and he became the one carrying his equipment for him.
1 Samuel 16:22 And Saul sent to Jesse, saying, Let David stand before me, because he has found favor in my eyes.
1 Samuel 16:23 And it happened when an evil spirit was upon Saul that David would take the lyre and play with his hand, and Saul would be refreshed, and it would be good for him, and the evil spirit would depart from him.

## Chapter 17

1 Samuel 17:1 And the foreigners gather their camps for war and gather at Sokchoth of Judea and encamp between Sokchoth and Azeka in Epheremem.
1 Samuel 17:2 And Saul and the men of Israel gather and encamp in the valley; they draw up for war opposite the foreigners.
1 Samuel 17:3 And the foreigners stand on the mountain here, and Israel stands on the mountain here, and the ravine is between them.
1 Samuel 17:4 And a mighty man came out of the battle line of the foreigners, Goliath was his name, from Geth; his height was four cubits and a span;
1 Samuel 17:5 and a helmet was on his head, and he wore a coat of chain mail, and the weight of his coat was five thousand shekels of bronze and iron;
1 Samuel 17:6 and bronze greaves were above his legs, and a bronze shield was between his shoulders;
1 Samuel 17:7 and the shaft of his spear was like a weaver's beam, and its point was six hundred shekels of iron; and the one carrying his weapons went before him.
1 Samuel 17:8 And he stood and cried out to the battle line of Israel and said to them, Why do you go out to draw up for battle opposite us? Am I not a foreigner and you Hebrews of Saul? Choose a man for yourselves and let him come down to me,
1 Samuel 17:9 and if he is able to fight against me and strikes me, we shall be your servants; but if I am able and strike him, you shall be our servants and serve us.
1 Samuel 17:10 And the foreigner said, Behold, I have reproached the battle line of Israel today on this day; give me a man, and we two shall fight in single combat.
1 Samuel 17:11 And Saul and all Israel heard these words of the foreigner and were astonished and very afraid.
1 Samuel 17:32 And David said to Saul, Let not my lord's heart collapse because of him; your servant will go and fight with this foreigner.
1 Samuel 17:33 And Saul said to David, You will certainly not be able to go against the foreigner to fight with him, for you are a young man, and he is a warrior from his youth.
1 Samuel 17:34 And David said to Saul, Your servant was tending the flock for his father, and whenever the lion and the bear came and took a sheep from the herd,
1 Samuel 17:35 I would go out after him and strike him and snatch it from his mouth; and if he rose against me, I grasped his throat and struck and killed him;
1 Samuel 17:36 and your servant struck the bear and the lion, and the uncircumcised foreigner shall be like one of these; shall I not go and strike him and remove reproach from Israel today? For who is this uncircumcised one who has reproached the battle line of the living God?
1 Samuel 17:37 The Lord who delivered me from the hand of the lion and from the hand of the bear, he will deliver me from the hand of this uncircumcised foreigner. And Saul said to David, Go, and may the Lord be with you.
1 Samuel 17:38 And Saul clothed David with a mantle and a bronze helmet about his head
1 Samuel 17:39 and girded David with his sword over his mantle. And he was wearied after walking once and twice; and David said to Saul, I shall certainly not be able to go in these, because I have not tried them. And they take them off him.
1 Samuel 17:40 And he took his staff in his hand and chose for himself five smooth stones from the torrent bed and placed them in the shepherd's bag that he had for collecting, and his sling was in his hand, and he approached the foreign man.
1 Samuel 17:42 And Goliath saw David and dishonored him, because he was a young man and was ruddy with beauty of eyes.
1 Samuel 17:43 And the foreigner said to David, Am I like a dog, that you come against me with a stick and stones? And David said, No, but worse than a dog. And the foreigner cursed David by his gods.
1 Samuel 17:44 And the foreigner said to David, Come to me, and I will give your flesh to the birds of heaven and the beasts of the earth.
1 Samuel 17:45 And David said to the foreigner, You come to me with sword and spear and shield, but I go to you in the name of the Lord Sabaoth, God of the battle line of Israel, which you have reproached today;
1 Samuel 17:46 and the Lord will shut you into my hand today, and I will kill you and take your head from you and give your limbs and the limbs of the camp of the foreigners on this day to the birds of heaven and the beasts of the earth, and all the earth shall know that there is a God in Israel;
1 Samuel 17:47 and all this assembly shall know that the Lord does not save by sword and spear, because the battle is the Lord's, and the Lord will give you into our hands.
1 Samuel 17:48 And the foreigner rose and went to meet David.
1 Samuel 17:49 And David stretched his hand into the bag and took one stone from there and slung it and struck the foreigner on his forehead, and the stone penetrated through the helmet into his forehead, and he fell on his face to the ground.
1 Samuel 17:51 And David ran and stood over him and took his sword and killed him and took off his head. And the foreigners saw that their mighty man had died, and fled.
1 Samuel 17:52 And the men of Israel and Judah rise and shout and pursue after them as far as the entrance of Geth and as far as the gate of Ascalon, and wounded men of the foreigners fell on the road of the gates and as far as Geth and as far as Akkaron.
1 Samuel 17:53 And the men of Israel returned, turning aside after the foreigners, and trampled their camps.
1 Samuel 17:54 And David took the foreigner's head and brought it to Jerusalem and placed his equipment in his dwelling.
1 Samuel 17:6 And the dancing women came out to meet David from all the cities of Israel with drums and with joy and with cymbals,
1 Samuel 17:7 and the women began and said, Saul struck his thousands and David his ten thousands.
1 Samuel 17:8 And the saying appeared evil in Saul's eyes because of this word, and he said, To David they have given the ten thousands and to me they have given the thousands.
1 Samuel 17:9 And Saul was looking askance at David from that day onward.
1 Samuel 17:12 And Saul was afraid before David
1 Samuel 17:13 and removed him from himself and appointed him a commander of a thousand for himself, and he went out and came in before the people.
1 Samuel 17:14 And David was discerning in all his ways, and the Lord was with him.
1 Samuel 17:15 And Saul saw that he was very discerning and was wary before him.
1 Samuel 17:16 And all Israel and Judah loved David, because he went out and came in before the people.
1 Samuel 17:20 And Melchol the daughter of Saul loved David, and it was reported to Saul, and it was right in his eyes.
1 Samuel 17:21 And Saul said, I will give her to him, and she shall be a snare to him. And the hand of the foreigners was upon Saul;
1 Samuel 17:22 and Saul commanded his servants, saying, Speak secretly to David, saying, Behold, the king delights in you, and all his servants love you, and you, become the king's son-in-law.
1 Samuel 17:23 And Saul's servants spoke these words in David's ears, and David said, Is it a light thing in your eyes to become the king's son-in-law? I am a lowly man and not honored.
1 Samuel 17:24 And Saul's servants reported to him according to these words that David had spoken.
1 Samuel 17:25 And Saul said, Thus you shall say to David: The king does not desire a gift, but a hundred foreskins of the foreigners to take vengeance on the king's enemies. And Saul reckoned to cast him into the hands of the foreigners.
1 Samuel 17:26 And Saul's servants report these words to David, and the word was right in David's eyes, to become the king's son-in-law.
1 Samuel 17:27 And David rose and went, he and his men, and struck a hundred men among the foreigners and brought their foreskins to the king and became the king's son-in-law, and he gave him Melchol his daughter as a wife.
1 Samuel 17:28 And Saul saw that the Lord was with David and all Israel loved him,
1 Samuel 17:29 and he continued to be wary of David still.

## Chapter 19

1 Samuel 19:1 And Saul spoke to Jonathan his son and to all his servants to put David to death. And Jonathan son of Saul greatly preferred David,
1 Samuel 19:2 and Jonathan reported to David, saying, Saul seeks to put you to death; therefore guard yourself tomorrow morning and hide and sit in concealment,
1 Samuel 19:3 and I will go out and stand beside my father in the field where you are, and I will speak about you to my father and see what there may be, and I will tell you.
1 Samuel 19:4 And Jonathan spoke good things about David to Saul his father and said to him, Let not the king sin against your servant David, because he has not sinned against you, and his deeds are very good,
1 Samuel 19:5 and he placed his life in his hand and struck the foreigner, and the Lord made a great salvation, and all Israel saw and rejoiced; and why do you sin against innocent blood by putting David to death without cause?
1 Samuel 19:6 And Saul listened to Jonathan's voice, and Saul swore, saying, As the Lord lives, he shall not die.
1 Samuel 19:7 And Jonathan called David and told him all these words, and Jonathan brought David to Saul, and he was before him as yesterday and the third day. –
1 Samuel 19:8 And war continued to come against Saul, and David grew strong and fought the foreigners and struck among them a very great blow, and they fled from before him.
1 Samuel 19:9 And an evil spirit of God came upon Saul, and he was in the house sleeping, with a spear in his hand, and David was playing with his hands;
1 Samuel 19:10 and Saul sought to strike David with the spear, and David withdrew from before Saul, and he struck the spear into the wall, and David withdrew and was saved.
1 Samuel 19:11 And it happened on that night that Saul sent messengers to David's house to watch him so as to put him to death in the morning. And Melchol his wife told David, saying, If you do not save your life tonight, tomorrow you will be put to death.
1 Samuel 19:12 And Melchol lowers David through the window, and he went away and fled and was saved.
1 Samuel 19:13 And Melchol took the empty tombs and placed them on the bed, and she placed the liver of the goats at its head and covered them with a garment.
1 Samuel 19:14 And Saul sent messengers to take David, and they say that he is afflicted.
1 Samuel 19:15 And he sends to David, saying, Bring him on the bed to me to put him to death.
1 Samuel 19:16 And the messengers come, and behold, the empty tombs were on the bed, and the liver of the goats at its head.
1 Samuel 19:17 And Saul said to Melchol, Why did you thus deceive me and send away my enemy, so that he was saved? And Melchol said to Saul, He said, Send me away; otherwise I will put you to death.
1 Samuel 19:18 And David fled and was saved and comes to Samuel in Armathaim and tells him all that Saul did to him, and David and Samuel went and sat in Nauath in Rama.
1 Samuel 19:19 And it was reported to Saul, saying, Behold, David is in Nauath in Rama.
1 Samuel 19:20 And Saul sent messengers to take David, and they saw the assembly of the prophets, and Samuel stood appointed over them, and a spirit of God came upon Saul's messengers, and they prophesy.
1 Samuel 19:21 And it was reported to Saul, and he sent other messengers, and they too prophesied. And Saul continued to send messengers a third time, and they too prophesied.
1 Samuel 19:22 And Saul was angered with anger and he too went to Armathaim and came as far as the well of the threshing floor in Sephi and asked and said, Where are Samuel and David? And they said, Behold, in Nauath in Rama.
1 Samuel 19:23 And he went from there to Nauath in Rama, and a spirit of God came upon him too, and he went prophesying until he came to Nauath in Rama.
1 Samuel 19:24 And he took off his garments and prophesied before them and fell naked all that day and all the night; therefore they said, Is Saul also among the prophets?

## Chapter 20

1 Samuel 20:1 And David escaped from Nauath in Rama and comes before Jonathan and said, What have I done, and what is my wrongdoing, and how have I sinned before your father that he seeks my life?
1 Samuel 20:2 And Jonathan said to him, By no means for you; you shall certainly not die. Behold, my father will certainly not do a great or small thing and not uncover my ear; and why would my father hide this thing? It is not so.
1 Samuel 20:3 And David answered Jonathan and said, Your father knows well that I have found favor in your eyes, and he said, Let Jonathan not know this, lest he be unwilling; but as the Lord lives and as your soul lives, as I said, it is filled between me and death.
1 Samuel 20:4 And Jonathan said to David, What does your soul desire, and what shall I do for you?
1 Samuel 20:5 And David said to Jonathan, Behold now, tomorrow is a new moon, and I shall certainly not sit with the king to eat, and you shall send me away, and I will hide in the plain until evening.
1 Samuel 20:6 If your father seeks me out, then you shall say, David earnestly asked leave of me to run as far as Bethlehem his city, because there is a sacrifice of the days there for the whole tribe.
1 Samuel 20:7 If he says thus, Good, peace to your servant; but if he answers you harshly, know that the evil has been completed by him.
1 Samuel 20:8 And you shall show mercy to your servant, because you brought your servant into a covenant of the Lord with yourself; and if there is wrongdoing in your servant, put me to death yourself; and why do you thus bring me as far as your father?
1 Samuel 20:9 And Jonathan said, By no means for you; for if I know well that the evil has been completed by my father to come upon you, and if not, to your cities I will report to you.
1 Samuel 20:10 And David said to Jonathan, Who will tell me if your father answers harshly?
1 Samuel 20:11 And Jonathan said to David, Go and stay in the field. And both go out to the field. –
1 Samuel 20:12 And Jonathan said to David, The Lord God of Israel knows that I will examine my father when the time is the third time, and behold, if it is good concerning David, and I do not send to you in the field,
1 Samuel 20:13 may God do thus to Jonathan and add thus, because I will bring the evil to you and uncover your ear and send you away, and you shall depart in peace; and may the Lord be with you as he was with my father.
1 Samuel 20:14 And indeed while I am still living, you shall show mercy to me, and if I surely die,
1 Samuel 20:15 you shall not remove your mercy from my house forever; and if not when the Lord removes David's enemies, each from the face of the earth,
1 Samuel 20:16 may Jonathan's name be removed from David's house, and may the Lord seek out David's enemies.
1 Samuel 20:17 And Jonathan continued further to make David swear, because he loved the soul of the one loving him.
1 Samuel 20:18 And Jonathan said, Tomorrow is the new moon, and you will be sought, because your seat will be sought.
1 Samuel 20:19 And you shall do it a third time and look and come to your place where you hid on the working day, and sit by that Ergab.
1 Samuel 20:20 And I shall shoot a third time with the splinters, casting them toward the Amattari;
1 Samuel 20:21 and behold, I will send the young man, saying, Come, find me the splinter; if I say to the young man, Here is the splinter on this side of you, here, take it, come, because there is peace for you and there is no matter, as the Lord lives;
1 Samuel 20:22 but if I say thus to the young man, Here is the splinter beyond you, go, because the Lord has sent you away.
1 Samuel 20:23 And the word that you and I spoke, behold, the Lord is witness between me and you forever.
1 Samuel 20:24 And David hides in the field, and the month arrives, and the king comes to the table to eat.
1 Samuel 20:25 And the king sat on his seat as once and again, on the seat by the wall, and Jonathan arrived before him, and Abenner sat at Saul's side, and David's place was sought.
1 Samuel 20:26 And Saul said nothing on that day, because he said, An accident appears to have made him unclean, because he has not been purified.
1 Samuel 20:27 And it happened on the following day of the month, on the second day, that David's place was sought, and Saul said to Jonathan his son, Why has the son of Jesse not come to the table either yesterday or today?
1 Samuel 20:28 And Jonathan answered Saul and said to him, David has asked leave of me to go as far as Bethlehem his city
1 Samuel 20:29 and said, Send me away now, because we have a sacrifice of the tribe in the city, and my brothers commanded me, and now if I have found favor in your eyes, I will be saved and see my brothers; for this reason he has not come to the king's table.
1 Samuel 20:30 And Saul was exceedingly angered with Jonathan and said to him, Son of girls who desert, do I not know that you are a partner with the son of Jesse, to your shame and to the shame of the uncovering of your mother?
1 Samuel 20:31 For all the days that the son of Jesse lives on the earth, your kingdom shall not be established; now therefore send and take the young man, because he is a son of death.
1 Samuel 20:32 And Jonathan answered Saul, Why is he to die? What has he done?
1 Samuel 20:33 And Saul raised the spear against Jonathan to put him to death. And Jonathan knew that this evil was completed by his father to put David to death,
1 Samuel 20:34 and Jonathan sprang up from the table in angry rage and did not eat bread on the second day of the month, because he was broken over David, because his father had finished the matter against him.
1 Samuel 20:35 And it happened in the morning that Jonathan went out to the field as he had arranged for the testimony to David, and a small young man was with him.
1 Samuel 20:36 And he said to the young man, Run, find me the splinters that I throw; and the young man ran, and he threw the splinter and sent it past him.
1 Samuel 20:37 And the young man came as far as the place of the splinter that Jonathan had thrown, and Jonathan cried out after the young man and said, There is the splinter beyond you;
1 Samuel 20:38 and Jonathan cried out after his young man, saying, Make haste, hurry and do not stand still; and Jonathan's young man gathered the splinters to his master.
1 Samuel 20:39 And the young man knew nothing; only Jonathan and David knew the matter.
1 Samuel 20:40 And Jonathan gave his equipment to his young man and said to his young man, Go, enter the city.
1 Samuel 20:41 And when the young man entered, David rose from the Ergab and fell on his face and bowed to him three times, and each kissed his neighbor and each wept for his neighbor until a great completion.
1 Samuel 20:42 And Jonathan said, Go in peace, and as we both have sworn in the name of the Lord, saying, The Lord shall be witness between me and you and between my seed and your seed forever.

## Chapter 21

1 Samuel 21:1 And David rose and departed, and Jonathan entered the city.
1 Samuel 21:2 And David comes to Nomba to Abimelech the priest. And Abimelech was startled at meeting him and said to him, Why are you alone and no one with you?
1 Samuel 21:3 And David said to the priest, The king has commanded me a thing today and said to me, Let no one know the thing concerning which I send you and concerning which I have commanded you; and to the young men I have borne witness in the place called God's Faithfulness, Phellani Alemoni;
1 Samuel 21:4 and now if there are five loaves under your hand, give into my hand what is found.
1 Samuel 21:5 And the priest answered David and said, There are no common loaves under my hand, but only holy loaves; if the young men have kept themselves from a woman, then he shall eat.
1 Samuel 21:6 And David answered the priest and said to him, But we have abstained from a woman yesterday and the third day; when I went out on the way all the young men became purified, and this way itself is common, because it will be sanctified today through my equipment.
1 Samuel 21:7 And Abimelech the priest gave him the loaves of the presentation, because there was no bread there except the loaves of the face, which had been removed from before the Lord to set out warm bread on the day he took them.
1 Samuel 21:8 And one of Saul's young men was there on that day, detained neessaran before the Lord, and his name was Doek the Syrian, tending Saul's mules.
1 Samuel 21:9 And David said to Abimelech, See if there is here under your hand a spear or sword, because I did not take my sword and the equipment in my hand, because the king's business was urgent.
1 Samuel 21:10 And the priest said, Behold, the sword of Goliath the foreigner, whom you struck in the valley of Ela, and it is wrapped in a garment; if you will take it for yourself, take it, because there is no other besides it here. And David said, Behold, there is none like it; give it to me.
1 Samuel 21:11 And he gave it to him; and David rose and fled on that day from before Saul. And David came to Anchous king of Geth.
1 Samuel 21:12 And Anchous's servants said to him, Is this not David the king of the land? Is it not for him that the dancing women began, saying, Saul struck his thousands and David his ten thousands?
1 Samuel 21:13 And David placed the words in his heart and was very afraid before Anchous king of Geth.
1 Samuel 21:14 And he changed his face before him and pretended on that day and drummed on the city's doors and wandered in his hands and fell upon the doors of the gate, and his spittle flowed down upon his beard.
1 Samuel 21:15 And Anchous said to his servants, Behold, you see an afflicted man; why did you bring him to me?
1 Samuel 21:16 Am I short of afflicted men, that you have brought him in to act afflicted before me? This man shall not enter a house.

## Chapter 22

1 Samuel 22:1 And David departed from there and was saved and comes to the cave of Odollam. And his brothers and his father's house hear and go down to him there.
1 Samuel 22:2 And everyone in distress and everyone in debt and everyone pained in soul gathered to him, and he was a leader over them; and there were about four hundred men with him.
1 Samuel 22:3 And David departed from there to Massepha of Moab and said to the king of Moab, Let my father and my mother be with you until I know what God will do for me.
1 Samuel 22:4 And he entreated the face of the king of Moab, and they dwelt with him all the days that David was in the region.
1 Samuel 22:5 And Gad the prophet said to David, Do not sit in the region; go and come to the land of Judah. And David went and came and sat in the city of Sarich.
1 Samuel 22:6 And Saul heard that David and the men with him had become known; and Saul sat on the hill under the field in Rama, with the spear in his hand, and all his servants stood beside him.
1 Samuel 22:7 And Saul said to his servants standing beside him, Hear now, sons of Benjamin; will the son of Jesse really give fields and vineyards to you all and appoint you all commanders of hundreds and commanders of thousands?
1 Samuel 22:8 For all of you have conspired against me, and there is no one who uncovers my ear when my son makes a covenant with the son of Jesse, and there is none among you pained for me and uncovering my ear that my son has stirred up my servant against me as an enemy, as on this day.
1 Samuel 22:9 And Doek the Syrian, appointed over Saul's mules, answered and said, I have seen the son of Jesse coming to Nomba to Abimelech son of Achitob the priest,
1 Samuel 22:10 and he inquired for him through God and gave him provisions and gave him the sword of Goliath the foreigner.
1 Samuel 22:11 And the king sent to call Abimelech son of Achitob and all the sons of his father's house, the priests in Nomba, and they all came to the king.
1 Samuel 22:12 And Saul said, Hear now, son of Achitob. And he said, Behold, I am here; speak, lord.
1 Samuel 22:13 And Saul said to him, Why did you conspire against me, you and the son of Jesse, by giving him bread and sword and inquiring for him through God, to set him against me as an enemy, as on this day?
1 Samuel 22:14 And he answered the king and said, And who among all your servants is faithful like David, the king's son-in-law and ruler of every command of yours and honored in your house?
1 Samuel 22:15 Did I begin today to inquire for him through God? By no means. Let not the king place a charge against his servant and against all my father's house, because your servant knew nothing small or great of all these things.
1 Samuel 22:16 And King Saul said, You shall surely die, Abimelech, you and all your father's house.
1 Samuel 22:17 And the king said to the runners standing over him, Come forward and put the priests of the Lord to death, because their hand is with David, and because they knew that he was fleeing and did not uncover my ear. And the king's servants did not wish to raise their hands to meet the priests of the Lord.
1 Samuel 22:18 And the king said to Doek, Turn yourself and meet the priests. And Doek the Syrian turned and put the priests of the Lord to death on that day, three hundred and five men, all carrying an ephod.
1 Samuel 22:19 And Nomba, the city of the priests, he struck by the edge of the sword, from man to woman, from infant to suckling, and calf and donkey and sheep. –
1 Samuel 22:20 And one son of Abimelech son of Achitob was saved, and his name was Abiathar, and he fled after David.
1 Samuel 22:21 And Abiathar reported to David that Saul had put all the priests of the Lord to death.
1 Samuel 22:22 And David said to Abiathar, I knew on that day that Doek the Syrian would surely report to Saul; I am responsible for the lives of your father's house;
1 Samuel 22:23 stay with me, do not fear, because wherever I seek a place for my life, I will seek one for your life also, for you are protected with me.

## Chapter 23

1 Samuel 23:1 And it was reported to David, saying, Behold, the foreigners are fighting in Keila, and they are plundering and trampling the threshing floors.
1 Samuel 23:2 And David inquired through the Lord, saying, Shall I go and strike these foreigners? And the Lord said, Go and strike among these foreigners and save Keila.
1 Samuel 23:3 And David's men said to him, Behold, we are afraid here in Judea, and how will it be if we go to Keila? We shall enter among the spoils of the foreigners.
1 Samuel 23:4 And David continued to inquire again through the Lord, and the Lord answered him and said to him, Rise and go down to Keila, because I am giving the foreigners into your hands.
1 Samuel 23:5 And David and the men with him went to Keila and fought among the foreigners, and they fled before him, and he drove away their livestock and struck a great blow among them, and David saved those dwelling in Keila.
1 Samuel 23:6 And it happened when Abiathar son of Abimelech fled to David that he too went down with David to Keila, having an ephod in his hand.
1 Samuel 23:7 And it was reported to Saul that David had come to Keila, and Saul said, God has sold him into my hands, because he has been shut in by entering a city of doors and bars.
1 Samuel 23:8 And Saul ordered all the people to go down to war at Keila to hem in David and his men.
1 Samuel 23:9 And David knew that Saul was not keeping silent about the evil against him, and David said to Abiathar the priest, Bring near the ephod of the Lord.
1 Samuel 23:10 And David said, Lord God of Israel, your servant has surely heard that Saul seeks to come against Keila to destroy the city because of me.
1 Samuel 23:11 Will he be shut in? And now will Saul come down, as your servant has heard? Lord God of Israel, tell your servant. And the Lord said, He will be shut in.
1 Samuel 23:13 And David and the men with him, about four hundred, rose and went out of Keila and went wherever they went; and it was reported to Saul that David had been saved from Keila, and he ceased going out.
1 Samuel 23:14 And David sat in the wilderness in Maserem in the narrow places and sat in the wilderness on Mount Ziph in the parched land; and Saul sought him all the days, and the Lord did not give him into his hands.
1 Samuel 23:15 And David saw that Saul was going out to seek David; and David was on the parched mountain in Kaine Ziph.
1 Samuel 23:16 And Jonathan son of Saul rose and went to David in Kaine and strengthened his hands in the Lord.
1 Samuel 23:17 And he said to him, Do not fear, for the hand of Saul my father shall certainly not find you, and you shall reign over Israel, and I shall be second to you; and Saul my father knows this.
1 Samuel 23:18 And the two made a covenant before the Lord. And David sat in Kaine, and Jonathan departed to his house.
1 Samuel 23:19 And the Ziphites went up from the parched land to Saul on the hill, saying, Is not David, behold, hiding near us in Messara in the narrow places in Kaine on the hill of Echela to the right of Jessaimoun?
1 Samuel 23:20 And now let all that is in the king's soul for coming down come down to us; they have shut him into the king's hands.
1 Samuel 23:21 And Saul said to them, Blessed are you to the Lord, because you have been pained for me;
1 Samuel 23:22 go now and prepare further and know his place, where his foot will be, swiftly there where you said, lest he act craftily;
1 Samuel 23:23 and see and know, and we will go with you, and it shall be, if he is on the land, I will search him out among all the thousands of Judah.
1 Samuel 23:24 And the Ziphites rose and went before Saul; and David and his men were in the wilderness of Maan toward evening to the right of Jessaimoun.
1 Samuel 23:25 And Saul and his men went to seek him; and they reported it to David, and he went down to the rock in the wilderness of Maan; and Saul heard and pursued after David into the wilderness of Maan.
1 Samuel 23:26 And Saul and his men go on one side of this mountain, and David and his men were on one side of this mountain; and David was sheltering himself to go from before Saul, and Saul and his men encamped against David and his men to seize them.
1 Samuel 23:27 And a messenger came to Saul, saying, Hurry and come, for the foreigners have attacked the land.
1 Samuel 23:28 And Saul turned back from pursuing after David and went to meet the foreigners; therefore that place was called the Divided Rock.

## Chapter 24

1 Samuel 24:1 And David went up from there and sat in the narrow places of Engaddi.
1 Samuel 24:2 And it happened when Saul returned from pursuing the foreigners that it was reported to him, saying that David was in the wilderness of Engaddi.
1 Samuel 24:3 And he took with him three thousand chosen men from all Israel and went to seek David and his men facing Sadaiem.
1 Samuel 24:4 And he came to the flocks of sheep by the road, and there was a cave there, and Saul entered to prepare himself; and David and his men were sitting farther inside the cave.
1 Samuel 24:5 And David's men said to him, Behold, this is the day of which the Lord said to you that he would give your enemy into your hands, and you shall do to him as is good in your eyes. And David rose and secretly took off the edge of Saul's cloak.
1 Samuel 24:6 And it happened after this that David's heart struck him, because he had taken off the edge of his cloak,
1 Samuel 24:7 and David said to his men, By no means from the Lord for me, if I do this thing to my lord, the Lord's anointed, to raise my hand against him, because this one is the Lord's anointed;
1 Samuel 24:8 and David persuaded his men with words and did not allow them to rise and put Saul to death. And Saul rose and went down to the road.
1 Samuel 24:9 And David rose after him from the cave, and David cried out after Saul, saying, My lord king; and Saul looked behind him, and David bent his face to the ground and bowed to him.
1 Samuel 24:10 And David said to Saul, Why do you listen to the words of the people saying, Behold, David seeks your life?
1 Samuel 24:11 Behold, on this day your eyes have seen how the Lord gave you into my hand today in the cave, and I did not wish to kill you and I spared you and said, I will not raise my hand against my lord, because this one is the Lord's anointed.
1 Samuel 24:12 And behold, the edge of your cloak is in my hand; I took off the edge and did not kill you. And know and see today that there is no evil in my hand nor impiety nor breach of faith, and I have not sinned against you; and you bind my life to take it.
1 Samuel 24:13 May the Lord judge between me and you, and may the Lord avenge me on you; and my hand shall not be upon you,
1 Samuel 24:14 as the ancient proverb says, From lawless men wrongdoing will come forth; and my hand shall not be upon you.
1 Samuel 24:15 And now after whom do you go out, king of Israel? After whom do you pursue? After a dead dog and after one flea.
1 Samuel 24:16 May the Lord be judge and arbiter between me and you; may the Lord see and judge my case and vindicate me from your hand.
1 Samuel 24:17 And it happened when David finished speaking these words to Saul that Saul said, Is this your voice, child David? And Saul raised his voice and wept.
1 Samuel 24:18 And Saul said to David, You are more righteous than I, because you repaid me good, but I repaid you evil.
1 Samuel 24:19 And you have told me today the good things you did to me, how the Lord shut me into your hands today and you did not kill me;
1 Samuel 24:20 and because if anyone should find his enemy in distress and send him away on a good way, the Lord will repay him good, as you have done today.
1 Samuel 24:21 And now, behold, I know that you shall surely reign and the kingdom of Israel shall stand in your hands.
1 Samuel 24:22 And now swear to me by the Lord that you will not destroy my seed after me and will not obliterate my name from my father's house.
1 Samuel 24:23 And David swore to Saul. And Saul departed to his place, and David and his men went up to the narrow Messara.

## Chapter 25

1 Samuel 25:1 And Samuel died, and all Israel gather and mourn him and bury him at his house in Armathaim. – And David rose and went down to the wilderness of Maan.
1 Samuel 25:2 And there was a man in Maan, and his flocks were in Carmel; and the man was very great, and he had three thousand sheep and a thousand goats; and it happened while he was shearing his flock in Carmel.
1 Samuel 25:3 And the man's name was Nabal, and his wife's name was Abigaia; and his wife was good in understanding and very beautiful in appearance, but the man was harsh and evil in his practices, and the man was doglike.
1 Samuel 25:4 And David heard in the wilderness that Nabal the Carmelite was shearing his flock,
1 Samuel 25:5 and David sent ten young men and said to the young men, Go up to Carmel and go to Nabal and ask him in my name for peace
1 Samuel 25:6 and say thus: For seasons; and may you be well, and your house and all yours be well.
1 Samuel 25:7 And now, behold, I have heard that they are shearing for you; now your shepherds who were with us in the wilderness, we did not hinder them and did not demand anything of them all the days they were in Carmel;
1 Samuel 25:8 ask your young men, and they will tell you. And let the young men find favor in your eyes, for we have come on a good day; give now whatever your hand finds to your son David.
1 Samuel 25:9 And the young men come and speak these words to Nabal according to all these sayings in David's name. And he leaped up
1 Samuel 25:10 and Nabal answered David's servants and said, Who is David, and who is Jesse's son? Today the servants departing, each from before his lord, have multiplied.
1 Samuel 25:11 And shall I take my bread and my wine and my slaughtered animals, which I have slaughtered for those shearing my sheep, and give them to men whom I do not know where they are from?
1 Samuel 25:12 And David's young men turned to their way and returned and came and reported these words to David.
1 Samuel 25:13 And David said to his men, Gird on each his sword; and about four hundred men went up after David, and the two hundred sat with the equipment.
1 Samuel 25:14 And one of the young men reported to Abigaia, Nabal's wife, saying, Behold, David sent messengers from the wilderness to bless our lord, and he turned away from them.
1 Samuel 25:15 And the men were very good to us; they did not hinder us nor demand anything of us all the days we were beside them; and while we were in the field
1 Samuel 25:16 they were like a wall around us both night and day all the days we were beside them tending the flock.
1 Samuel 25:17 And now know and see what you will do, because evil has been completed against our lord and his house; and he is a pestilent son, and there is no speaking to him.
1 Samuel 25:18 And Abigaia hurried and took two hundred loaves and two vessels of wine and five prepared sheep and five oiphi of meal and one gomor of raisins and two hundred cakes of pressed fruit and put them on the donkeys
1 Samuel 25:19 and said to her young men, Go on before me, and behold, I am coming after you. And she did not tell her husband.
1 Samuel 25:20 And it happened while she rode on the donkey and went down under cover of the mountain that behold, David and his men were coming down to meet her, and she met them.
1 Samuel 25:21 And David had said, Perhaps I guarded all his things in the wilderness for nothing and we did not demand to take anything from all his things, and he has repaid me evil for good;
1 Samuel 25:22 may God do thus to David and add thus if I leave of all that belongs to Nabal until morning one who urinates against a wall.
1 Samuel 25:23 And Abigaia saw David and hurried and leaped down from the donkey and fell before David on her face and bowed to him to the ground
1 Samuel 25:24 at his feet and said, On me, my lord, be the wrongdoing; let your servant speak in your ears, and hear a word of your servant.
1 Samuel 25:25 Let not my lord set his heart upon this pestilent man, because as his name is, so he is; Nabal is his name, and folly is with him; and I your servant did not see your young men whom you sent.
1 Samuel 25:26 And now, lord, as the Lord lives and as your soul lives, since the Lord has prevented you from coming into innocent blood and saving your hand for yourself, now may your enemies and those seeking evil for my lord become like Nabal.
1 Samuel 25:27 And now take this blessing that your servant has brought to my lord, and you shall give it to the young men standing beside my lord.
1 Samuel 25:28 Take away your servant's lawlessness, for the Lord will surely make my lord a faithful house, because my lord fights the Lord's war, and evil shall never be found in you.
1 Samuel 25:29 And a man will rise pursuing you and seeking your life, and my lord's life shall be bound in the bundle of life with the Lord God, and the life of your enemies you will sling in the midst of the sling.
1 Samuel 25:30 And it shall be that the Lord will do for my lord all the good things that he spoke over you, and the Lord will command you to be leader over Israel,
1 Samuel 25:31 and this shall not be for you an abomination and a stumbling block to my lord, to shed innocent blood without cause and save my lord's hand for himself. And the Lord will do good to my lord, and you shall remember your servant to do good to her.
1 Samuel 25:32 And David said to Abigaia, Blessed be the Lord God of Israel, who sent you today on this occasion to meet me,
1 Samuel 25:33 and blessed be your manner, and blessed are you who prevented me today on this occasion from coming into bloodshed and saving my hand for myself.
1 Samuel 25:34 But as the Lord God of Israel lives, who prevented me today from doing evil to you, if you had not hurried and come to meet me, then I said, If one who urinates against a wall should be left to Nabal until the light of morning.
1 Samuel 25:35 And David took from her hand all she had brought him and said to her, Go up in peace to your house; see, I have listened to your voice and favored your face.
1 Samuel 25:36 And Abigaia came to Nabal, and behold, he had a drinking feast in his house like a king's feast, and Nabal's heart was good upon him, and he was very drunk; and she did not tell him a small or great thing until the light of morning.
1 Samuel 25:37 And it happened in the morning, when Nabal had sobered up from the wine, that his wife told him these things, and his heart died within him, and he became like a stone.
1 Samuel 25:38 And it happened after about ten days that the Lord struck Nabal, and he died.
1 Samuel 25:39 And David heard and said, Blessed be the Lord, who judged the case of my reproach from Nabal's hand and preserved his servant from the hand of evils, and the Lord returned Nabal's evil upon his head. And David sent and spoke about Abigaia to take her for himself as a wife.
1 Samuel 25:40 And David's servants came to Abigaia in Carmel and spoke to her, saying, David sent us to you to take you as a wife for him.
1 Samuel 25:41 And she rose and bowed to the ground on her face and said, Behold, your servant is a maidservant to wash the feet of your servants.
1 Samuel 25:42 And Abigaia rose and mounted the donkey, and five girls followed her, and she went after David's servants and became his wife.
1 Samuel 25:43 And David took Achinaam from Jezrael, and both were his wives.
1 Samuel 25:44 And Saul gave Melchol his daughter, David's wife, to Phalti son of Lais, from Romma.

## Chapter 26

1 Samuel 26:1 And the Ziphites come from the parched land to Saul on the hill, saying, Behold, David shelters with us on the hill of Echela facing Jessaimoun.
1 Samuel 26:2 And Saul rose and went down to the wilderness of Ziph, and with him three thousand chosen men from Israel, to seek David in the wilderness of Ziph.
1 Samuel 26:3 And Saul encamped on the hill of Echela facing Jessaimoun beside the road, and David sat in the wilderness. And David saw that Saul had come after him into the wilderness,
1 Samuel 26:4 and David sent scouts and learned that Saul had come ready from Keila.
1 Samuel 26:5 And David rose secretly and goes into the place where Saul slept, and there was Abenner son of Ner, his commander, and Saul slept in a covered wagon, and the people were encamped around him.
1 Samuel 26:6 And David answered and said to Achimelech the Chettite and to Abessa son of Sarouia, brother of Joab, saying, Who will enter with me to Saul in the camp? And Abessa said, I will enter with you.
1 Samuel 26:7 And David and Abessa go into the people by night, and behold, Saul was sleeping in sleep in the covered wagon, and the spear was fixed in the ground at his head, and Abenner and his people slept around him.
1 Samuel 26:8 And Abessa said to David, The Lord has shut your enemy into your hands today, and now I will strike him with the spear into the ground once, and I will not do it a second time to him.
1 Samuel 26:9 And David said to Abessa, Do not humble him, for who will raise his hand against the Lord's anointed and be innocent?
1 Samuel 26:10 And David said, As the Lord lives, unless the Lord strikes him, or his day comes and he dies, or he goes down to war and is added;
1 Samuel 26:11 by no means from the Lord for me to raise my hand against the Lord's anointed; and now take the spear from beside his head and the flask of water, and let us depart by ourselves.
1 Samuel 26:12 And David took the spear and the flask of water from beside his head, and they departed by themselves; and no one saw and no one knew and no one awoke, all sleeping, because an astonishment from the Lord had fallen upon them.
1 Samuel 26:13 And David crossed to the far side and stood on the top of the mountain far away, and there was much distance between them.
1 Samuel 26:14 And David called to the people and spoke to Abenner, saying, Will you not answer, Abenner? And Abenner answered and said, Who are you who calls me?
1 Samuel 26:15 And David said to Abenner, Are you not a man? And who is like you in Israel? And why do you not guard your lord the king? For one of the people entered to destroy the king your lord.
1 Samuel 26:16 And this thing you have done is not good; as the Lord lives, you who guard the king your lord, the Lord's anointed, are sons of death. And now look: where are the king's spear and flask of water that were by his head?
1 Samuel 26:17 And Saul recognized David's voice and said, Is this your voice, child David? And David said, Your servant, my lord king.
1 Samuel 26:18 And he said, Why does my lord pursue after his servant thus? For how have I sinned, and what wrongdoing was found in me?
1 Samuel 26:19 And now let my lord the king hear the word of his servant: if God is stirring you up against me, may he smell your sacrifice; but if sons of men, cursed are they before the Lord, because they have driven me out today so that I may not be established in the Lord's inheritance, saying, Go, serve other gods.
1 Samuel 26:20 And now let not my blood fall on the ground opposite the face of the Lord, because the king of Israel has gone out to seek my life, as the night raven pursues in the mountains.
1 Samuel 26:21 And Saul said, I have sinned; return, child David, because I will not do evil to you in return for my life being precious in your eyes today; I have acted vainly and erred very greatly.
1 Samuel 26:22 And David answered and said, Behold, the king's spear; let one of the young men cross and take it.
1 Samuel 26:23 And the Lord will return to each his acts of righteousness and his faithfulness, since the Lord gave you into my hands today and I did not wish to raise my hand against the Lord's anointed;
1 Samuel 26:24 and behold, as your life was magnified in my eyes today, so may my life be magnified before the Lord, and may he shelter me and deliver me from every distress.
1 Samuel 26:25 And Saul said to David, Blessed are you, child, and you shall surely do and being able shall be able. And David departed on his way, and Saul returned to his place.

## Chapter 27

1 Samuel 27:1 And David said in his heart, saying, Now on one day I shall be added into Saul's hands, and there is no good for me unless I am saved in the land of the foreigners and Saul ceases seeking me in all Israel's territory, and I shall be saved from his hand.
1 Samuel 27:2 And David rose, and the four hundred men with him, and went to Anchous son of Ammach king of Geth.
1 Samuel 27:3 And David sat with Anchous in Geth, he and his men, each with his household, and David with both his wives, Achinaam the Jezraelite and Abigaia the wife of Nabal the Carmelite.
1 Samuel 27:4 And it was reported to Saul that David had fled to Geth, and he did not continue to seek him.
1 Samuel 27:5 And David said to Anchous, If now your servant has found favor in your eyes, let them give me a place in one of the country towns and I will sit there; and why should your servant sit in a royal city with you?
1 Samuel 27:6 And he gave him Sekelak on that day; therefore Sekelak belonged to the king of Judea until this day.
1 Samuel 27:7 And the number of the days that David sat in the countryside of the foreigners was four months.
1 Samuel 27:8 And David and his men would go up and attack all the Gesiri and the Amalekite; and behold, the land had been inhabited from those belonging to Gelampsour, fortified, as far as the land of Egypt.
1 Samuel 27:9 And he would strike the land and keep no man or woman alive and take flocks and herds and donkeys and camels and clothing, and they returned and came to Anchous.
1 Samuel 27:10 And Anchous said to David, Against whom did you attack today? And David said to Anchous, Against the south of Judea and against the south of Jesmega and against the south of the Kenezi.
1 Samuel 27:11 And he kept no man or woman alive to bring into Geth, saying, Lest they report against us in Geth, saying, Thus David does. And this was his practice all the days that David sat in the countryside of the foreigners.
1 Samuel 27:12 And David was greatly trusted by Anchous, who said, He has certainly become disgraced among his people in Israel and shall be my servant forever.

## Chapter 28

1 Samuel 28:1 And it happened in those days that the foreigners gather in their camps to go out to fight with Israel, and Anchous said to David, Know assuredly that you and your men will go out with me to war.
1 Samuel 28:2 And David said to Anchous, Thus now you will know what your servant will do; and Anchous said to David, Thus I shall make you chief bodyguard all the days.
1 Samuel 28:3 And Samuel died, and all Israel mourned him and buried him in Armathaim in his city. And Saul removed the ventriloquists and the knowers from the land.
1 Samuel 28:4 And the foreigners gather and come and encamp at Soman, and Saul gathers every man of Israel and they encamp at Gelboue.
1 Samuel 28:5 And Saul saw the camp of the foreigners and was afraid, and his heart was greatly beside itself.
1 Samuel 28:6 And Saul inquired through the Lord, and the Lord did not answer him in dreams or in clear signs or in the prophets.
1 Samuel 28:7 And Saul said to his servants, Seek for me a woman ventriloquist, and I will go to her and seek through her; and his servants said to him, Behold, a woman ventriloquist is in Aendor.
1 Samuel 28:8 And Saul disguised himself and put on other garments and went, he and two men with him, and they came to the woman by night, and he said to her, Divine for me now through the ventriloquist and bring up for me whomever I tell you.
1 Samuel 28:9 And the woman said to him, Behold now, you know what Saul did, how he destroyed the ventriloquists and the knowers from the land; and why are you setting a snare for my life to put it to death?
1 Samuel 28:10 And Saul swore to her, saying, As the Lord lives, no wrongdoing shall befall you in this matter.
1 Samuel 28:11 And the woman said, Whom shall I bring up for you? And he said, Bring up Samuel for me.
1 Samuel 28:12 And the woman saw Samuel and cried out with a great voice; and the woman said to Saul, Why did you deceive me? You are Saul.
1 Samuel 28:13 And the king said to her, Do not fear; say whom you have seen. And she said to him, I have seen gods coming up from the earth.
1 Samuel 28:14 And he said to her, What did you perceive? And she said to him, An upright man coming up from the earth, and he was clothed with a cloak. And Saul knew that this was Samuel, and bowed his face to the ground and worshiped him.
1 Samuel 28:15 And Samuel said, Why have you troubled me to bring me up? And Saul said, I am greatly distressed, and the foreigners fight against me, and God has departed from me and has no longer listened to me, either by the hand of the prophets or in dreams; and now I have called you to make known to me what I shall do.
1 Samuel 28:16 And Samuel said, Why do you ask me? The Lord has departed from you and has become with your neighbor;
1 Samuel 28:17 and the Lord has done to you as he spoke by my hand, and the Lord will tear your kingdom from your hand and give it to your neighbor David.
1 Samuel 28:18 Because you did not listen to the voice of the Lord and did not enact the heat of his anger in Amalek, for this reason the Lord has done this thing to you on this day.
1 Samuel 28:19 And the Lord will give Israel with you into the hands of the foreigners, and tomorrow you and your sons with you shall fall, and the Lord will give Israel's camp into the hands of the foreigners.
1 Samuel 28:20 And Saul hurried and fell while standing upon the ground and was very afraid because of Samuel's words; and there was no strength left in him, for he had eaten no bread all that day and all that night.
1 Samuel 28:21 And the woman came to Saul and saw that he had hurried greatly, and she said to him, Behold now, your servant listened to your voice and placed my life in my hand and listened to the words you spoke to me;
1 Samuel 28:22 and now listen to the voice of your servant, and I will set before you a morsel of bread, and eat, and there shall be strength in you, because you will go on a way.
1 Samuel 28:23 And he did not wish to eat; and his servants and the woman pressed him, and he listened to their voice and rose from the ground and sat on the stool.
1 Samuel 28:24 And the woman had a pasture-fed heifer in the house, and she hurried and slaughtered it and took flour and kneaded it and baked unleavened bread
1 Samuel 28:25 and brought it before Saul and before his servants, and they ate. And they rose and departed that night.

## Chapter 29

1 Samuel 29:1 And the foreigners gather all their camps at Aphek, and Israel encamped in Aendor in Jezrael.
1 Samuel 29:2 And the satraps of the foreigners were passing along in hundreds and thousands, and David and his men were passing along at the rear with Anchous.
1 Samuel 29:3 And the satraps of the foreigners said, Who are these passing along? And Anchous said to the commanders of the foreigners, Is this not David, servant of Saul king of Israel? He has been with us for days, this second year, and I have found nothing in him from the day he fell in with me until this day.
1 Samuel 29:4 And the commanders of the foreigners were grieved over him and say to him, Turn the man back to his place where you appointed him, and let him not come with us to war and not become a plotter against the camp; and by what will this one be reconciled to his lord? Is it not by the heads of those men?
1 Samuel 29:5 Is this not David, for whom they began in dances, saying, Saul struck his thousands and David his ten thousands?
1 Samuel 29:6 And Anchous called David and said to him, As the Lord lives, you are upright and good in my eyes, and your going out and your coming in with me in the camp, and I have found no evil against you from the day you came to me until today; but in the eyes of the satraps you are not good;
1 Samuel 29:7 and now return and go in peace, and you shall certainly not do evil in the eyes of the satraps of the foreigners.
1 Samuel 29:8 And David said to Anchous, What have I done to you, and what have you found in your servant from the day I was before you until this day, that I shall certainly not come to fight the enemies of my lord the king?
1 Samuel 29:9 And Anchous answered David, I know that you are good in my eyes, but the satraps of the foreigners say, He shall not come with us to war.
1 Samuel 29:10 And now rise early in the morning, you and the servants of your lord who came with you, and go to the place where I appointed you, and do not place a pestilent word in your heart, because you are good before me; and rise early on the way, and let it become light for you, and go.
1 Samuel 29:11 And David and his men rose early to depart and guard the land of the foreigners, and the foreigners went up to fight against Israel.

## Chapter 30

1 Samuel 30:1 And it happened when David and his men entered Sekelak on the third day that Amalek had attacked the south and Sekelak and struck Sekelak and burned it with fire;
1 Samuel 30:2 and the women and all in it, from small to great, they did not put man or woman to death, but took them captive and departed on their way.
1 Samuel 30:3 And David and his men came to the city, and behold, it had been burned with fire, and their wives and their sons and their daughters had been taken captive.
1 Samuel 30:4 And David and his men raised their voice and wept until there was no strength in them to weep any more.
1 Samuel 30:5 And both David's wives had been taken captive, Achinoom the Jezraelite and Abigaia the wife of Nabal the Carmelite.
1 Samuel 30:6 And David was greatly distressed, because the people spoke of stoning him, because every person's soul was pained, each over his sons and daughters; and David was strengthened in the Lord his God.
1 Samuel 30:7 And David said to Abiathar the priest, son of Achimelech, Bring near the ephod.
1 Samuel 30:8 And David inquired through the Lord, saying, Shall I pursue after this raiding band? Shall I overtake them? And he said to him, Pursue, because you shall surely overtake and shall surely deliver.
1 Samuel 30:9 And David went, he and the six hundred men with him, and they came as far as the torrent bed Bosor, and the remainder stood still.
1 Samuel 30:10 And he pursued with four hundred men, but two hundred men stayed behind, who sat across the torrent bed Bosor.
1 Samuel 30:11 And they find an Egyptian man in the field and take him and bring him to David in the field; and they give him bread, and he ate, and they gave him water to drink;
1 Samuel 30:12 and they give him a piece of a cake of pressed fruit, and he ate, and his spirit was established within him, because he had not eaten bread or drunk water for three days and three nights.
1 Samuel 30:13 And David said to him, Whose are you and where are you from? And the Egyptian young man said, I am a servant of an Amalekite man, and my lord left me because I became ill three days ago today.
1 Samuel 30:14 And we attacked the south of Cholthi and the parts of Judea and the south of Cheloub, and we burned Sekelak with fire.
1 Samuel 30:15 And David said to him, Will you lead me down to this raiding band? And he said, Swear to me by God that you will not put me to death and will not give me into my lord's hands, and I will lead you down to this raiding band.
1 Samuel 30:16 And he led him down there, and behold, they were spread over the face of all the land, eating and drinking and celebrating among all the great spoils that they had taken from the land of the foreigners and from the land of Judah.
1 Samuel 30:17 And David came upon them and struck them from the morning star until evening and the following day, and not one man of them was saved except four hundred young men who had mounted camels and fled.
1 Samuel 30:18 And David took back all that the Amalekites had taken, and he delivered both his wives.
1 Samuel 30:19 And nothing was missing to them from small to great, from the spoils to sons and daughters and everything they had taken from them; David returned it all.
1 Samuel 30:20 And David took all the flocks and herds and drove them before the spoils, and concerning those spoils it was said, These are David's spoils. –
1 Samuel 30:21 And David comes to the two hundred men who were too weak to go after David and whom he had left by the torrent bed Bosor, and they went out to meet David and to meet the people with him, and David approached the people, and they asked him about peace.
1 Samuel 30:22 And every pestilent and evil man among the fighting men who had gone with David answered and said, Because they did not pursue with us, we will not give them from the spoils we delivered, except that each take away his wife and children and return.
1 Samuel 30:23 And David said, You shall not do thus after the Lord has given to us and guarded us and the Lord has given the raiding band that came against us into our hands.
1 Samuel 30:24 And who will listen to these words of yours? For they are not less than you; therefore as the portion of the one going down to war, so shall be the portion of the one sitting by the equipment; they shall divide alike.
1 Samuel 30:25 And it happened from that day onward and became an ordinance and a judgment for Israel until today.
1 Samuel 30:26 And David came to Sekelak and sent from the spoils to the elders of Judah and to his neighbors, saying, Behold, from the spoils of the Lord's enemies;
1 Samuel 30:27 to those in Baithsour and those in Rama of the south and those in Jeththor
1 Samuel 30:28 and those in Aroer and the Ammadi and those in Saphi and those in Esthie
1 Samuel 30:28 and those in Aroer and the Ammadi and those in Saphi and those in Esthie
1 Samuel 30:29 and those in Carmel and those in the cities of Jerameli and those in the cities of Kenezi
1 Samuel 30:30 and those in Jerimouth and those in Bersabee and those in Noo
1 Samuel 30:31 and those in Chebron and all the places through which David had passed there, he and his men.

## Chapter 31

1 Samuel 31:1 And the foreigners fought against Israel, and the men of Israel fled from before the foreigners, and wounded men fall on Mount Gelboue.
1 Samuel 31:2 And the foreigners close with Saul and his sons, and the foreigners strike Jonathan and Aminadab and Melchisa, Saul's sons.
1 Samuel 31:3 And the battle grows heavy against Saul, and the javelin throwers, men who were archers, find him, and he was wounded in the region below the ribs.
1 Samuel 31:4 And Saul said to the one carrying his equipment, Draw your sword and pierce me with it, lest these uncircumcised men come and pierce me and mock me. And the one carrying his equipment did not wish to, because he was very afraid; and Saul took the sword and fell upon it.
1 Samuel 31:5 And the one carrying his equipment saw that Saul had died, and he too fell upon his sword and died with him.
1 Samuel 31:6 And Saul and his three sons and the one carrying his equipment died together on that day.
1 Samuel 31:7 And the men of Israel across the valley and across the Jordan saw that the men of Israel had fled and that Saul and his sons had died, and they leave their cities and flee; and the foreigners come and dwell in them. –
1 Samuel 31:8 And it happened on the next day that the foreigners come to strip the dead and find Saul and his three sons fallen on the mountains of Gelboue.
1 Samuel 31:9 And they turn him over and strip off his equipment and send it around the land of the foreigners, announcing good news to their idols and their people;
1 Samuel 31:10 and they dedicated his equipment in the Astarte temple and fastened his body to the wall of Baithsan.
1 Samuel 31:11 And those dwelling in Jabis of Galaad hear what the foreigners had done to Saul.
1 Samuel 31:12 And every man of might rose and went all night and took Saul's body and the body of Jonathan his son from the wall of Baithsan and bring them to Jabis and burn them there.
1 Samuel 31:13 And they take their bones and bury them under the field in Jabis and fast for seven days.

# 2 Samuel

## Chapter 1

2 Samuel 1:1 And it happened after Saul died and David returned from striking Amalek that David sat in Sekelak two days.
2 Samuel 1:2 And it happened on the third day that behold, a man came from the camp, from Saul's people, with his garments torn and earth on his head, and it happened when he entered to David that he fell to the ground and bowed to him.
2 Samuel 1:3 And David said to him, Where do you come from? And he said to him, I have escaped from Israel's camp.
2 Samuel 1:4 And David said to him, What is this matter? Tell me. And he said that the people fled from the battle, and many of the people have fallen and died; and Saul has died also, and Jonathan his son has died.
2 Samuel 1:5 And David said to the young man telling him, How do you know that Saul and Jonathan his son have died?
2 Samuel 1:6 And the young man telling him said, By chance I happened upon Mount Gelboue, and behold, Saul leaned upon his spear, and behold, the chariots and horse commanders closed in upon him.
2 Samuel 1:7 And he looked behind him and saw me and called me, and I said, Behold, I am here.
2 Samuel 1:8 And he said to me, Who are you? And I said, I am an Amalekite.
2 Samuel 1:9 And he said to me, Stand over me now and put me to death, because terrible darkness has seized me, because all my life is in me.
2 Samuel 1:10 And I stood over him and put him to death, because I knew that he would not live after his falling; and I took the royal thing on his head and the bracelet on his arm and have brought them here to my lord.
2 Samuel 1:11 And David grasped his garments and tore them, and all the men with him tore their garments.
2 Samuel 1:12 And they mourned and wept and fasted until evening for Saul and Jonathan his son and for the people of Judah and the house of Israel, because they had been struck by the sword.
2 Samuel 1:13 And David said to the young man telling him, Where are you from? And he said, I am the son of a sojourning Amalekite man.
2 Samuel 1:14 And David said to him, How were you not afraid to raise your hand to destroy the Lord's anointed?
2 Samuel 1:15 And David called one of his young men and said, Come forward and meet him; and he struck him, and he died.
2 Samuel 1:16 And David said to him, Your blood is upon your head, because your mouth answered against you, saying, I put the Lord's anointed to death.
2 Samuel 1:17 And David lamented this lament over Saul and Jonathan his son
2 Samuel 1:18 and said to teach the sons of Judah – behold, it is written in the Book of the Upright –
2 Samuel 1:19 Set up a pillar, Israel, for the dead wounded upon your heights; how the mighty have fallen.
2 Samuel 1:20 Do not tell it in Geth and do not announce good news in the exits of Ascalon, lest the daughters of the foreigners rejoice, lest the daughters of the uncircumcised exult.
2 Samuel 1:21 Mountains in Gelboue, let neither dew nor rain come down upon you, nor fields of first fruits, because there the shield of the mighty was abhorred, Saul's shield was not anointed with oil.
2 Samuel 1:22 From the blood of the wounded, from the fat of the mighty, Jonathan's bow did not turn back empty to the rear, and Saul's sword did not return empty.
2 Samuel 1:23 Saul and Jonathan, the beloved and beautiful, not separated, fair in their life and in their death not divided, swifter than eagles and stronger than lions.
2 Samuel 1:24 Daughters of Israel, weep for Saul, who clothed you in scarlet with your adornment, who placed golden adornment on your garments.
2 Samuel 1:25 How the mighty have fallen in the midst of battle; Jonathan, wounded upon your heights.
2 Samuel 1:26 I grieve over you, my brother Jonathan; you were exceedingly beautiful to me, your love to me was wondrous beyond the love of women.
2 Samuel 1:27 How the mighty have fallen and the implements of war perished.

## Chapter 2

2 Samuel 2:1 And it happened after these things that David inquired of the Lord, saying, Shall I go up to one of the cities of Judah? And the Lord said to him, Go up. And David said, Where shall I go up? And he said, To Chebron.
2 Samuel 2:2 And David went up there to Chebron, and both his wives, Achinoom the Jezraelite and Abigaia the wife of Nabal the Carmelite,
2 Samuel 2:3 and the men with him, each with his household, and they dwelt in the cities of Chebron.
2 Samuel 2:4 And men of Judea come and anoint David there to reign over the house of Judah. And they reported to David, saying that the men of Jabis of Galaad buried Saul.
2 Samuel 2:5 And David sent messengers to the leaders of Jabis of Galaad and said to them, Blessed are you to the Lord, because you have done this mercy to your lord, to Saul the Lord's anointed, and buried him and Jonathan his son;
2 Samuel 2:6 and now may the Lord do mercy and truth with you, and I too will do these good things with you, because you did this thing;
2 Samuel 2:7 and now let your hands be strengthened and become mighty sons, because your lord Saul has died, and the house of Judah has also anointed me king over themselves.
2 Samuel 2:8 And Abenner son of Ner, Saul's commander, took Jebosthe son of Saul and brought him up from the camp to Manaem
2 Samuel 2:9 and made him king over Galaaditis and Thasiri and Jezrael and Ephraim and Benjamin and all Israel.
2 Samuel 2:10 Jebosthe son of Saul was forty years old when he reigned over Israel, and he reigned two years, except the house of Judah, who were after David;
2 Samuel 2:11 and the days that David reigned in Chebron over the house of Judah were seven years and six months.
2 Samuel 2:12 And Abenner son of Ner and the servants of Jebosthe son of Saul went out from Manaem to Gabaon;
2 Samuel 2:13 and Joab son of Sarouia and David's servants went out from Chebron and meet them together by the spring of Gabaon, and these sat by the spring of Gabaon on this side and those by the spring on that side.
2 Samuel 2:14 And Abenner said to Joab, Let the young men rise and play before us. And Joab said, Let them rise.
2 Samuel 2:15 And they rose and passed over in number, twelve of the sons of Benjamin belonging to Jebosthe son of Saul and twelve of David's servants.
