2 Samuel 2:16 And each grasped his neighbor's head with his hand and his knife went into his neighbor's side, and they fall together; and the name of that place was called Portion of the Plotters, which is in Gabaon.
2 Samuel 2:17 And the battle was exceedingly harsh on that day, and Abenner and the men of Israel stumbled before David's servants. –
2 Samuel 2:18 And the three sons of Sarouia were there, Joab and Abessa and Asael, and Asael was swift with his feet like a gazelle in the field.
2 Samuel 2:19 And Asael pursued after Abenner and did not turn aside in going to the right or to the left behind Abenner.
2 Samuel 2:20 And Abenner looked behind him and said, Is it you, Asael? And he said, It is I.
2 Samuel 2:21 And Abenner said to him, Turn aside to the right or to the left and seize for yourself one of the young men and take his armor for yourself; and Asael did not wish to turn aside from behind him.
2 Samuel 2:22 And Abenner continued to say to Asael, Depart from me, lest I strike you to the ground; and how shall I lift my face toward Joab? And where are these things? Return to Joab your brother.
2 Samuel 2:23 And he did not wish to depart. And Abenner strikes him with the back of the spear at the loin, and the spear passed out behind him, and he falls there and dies beneath him. And everyone who came as far as the place where Asael fell there and died stopped. –
2 Samuel 2:24 And Joab and Abessa pursued after Abenner; and the sun was setting, and they came as far as the hill Amman, which faces Gai on the wilderness road of Gabaon.
2 Samuel 2:25 And the sons of Benjamin who were after Abenner gather and became one meeting and stood atop one hill.
2 Samuel 2:26 And Abenner called to Joab and said, Shall the sword devour to victory? Do you not know that it will be bitter in the end? And how long will you not tell the people to turn back from following our brothers?
2 Samuel 2:27 And Joab said, As the Lord lives, if you had not spoken, for then from morning the people would have gone up, each after his brother.
2 Samuel 2:28 And Joab sounded the trumpet, and all the people stopped and did not pursue after Israel and did not continue to fight.
2 Samuel 2:29 And Abenner and his men departed westward all that night and crossed the Jordan and went all along the extended stretch and came to the camp.
2 Samuel 2:30 And Joab returned from following Abenner and gathered all the people, and nineteen men of David's servants and Asael were missing.
2 Samuel 2:31 And David's servants struck of the sons of Benjamin, of Abenner's men, three hundred and sixty men besides him.
2 Samuel 2:32 And they took Asael and buried him in his father's tomb in Bethlehem. And Joab and the men with him went all night, and dawn broke for them in Chebron.

## Chapter 3

2 Samuel 3:1 And war continued for a long time between the house of Saul and the house of David; and the house of David went on and grew strong, and the house of Saul went on and grew weak.
2 Samuel 3:2 And sons were born to David in Chebron, and his firstborn was Amnon by Achinoom the Jezraelite,
2 Samuel 3:3 and his second Dalouia by Abigaia the Carmelite, and the third Abessalom son of Maacha daughter of Tholmi king of Gesir,
2 Samuel 3:4 and the fourth Ornia son of Pheggith, and the fifth Sabatia by Abital,
2 Samuel 3:5 and the sixth Jetheraam by Aigla David's wife; these were born to David in Chebron.
2 Samuel 3:6 And it happened while the war was between the house of Saul and the house of David that Abenner was holding the house of Saul.
2 Samuel 3:7 And Saul had a concubine, Respha daughter of Jal; and Memphibosthe son of Saul said to Abenner, Why did you go in to my father's concubine?
2 Samuel 3:8 And Abenner was very angry at Memphibosthe's word, and Abenner said to him, Am I a dog's head? I have shown mercy today to the house of Saul your father and to brothers and acquaintances and have not deserted to the house of David; and you seek against me over a woman's wrongdoing today?
2 Samuel 3:9 May God do thus to Abenner and add thus to him, for as the Lord swore to David, so I will do for him on this day,
2 Samuel 3:10 to remove the kingdom from the house of Saul and raise up David's throne over Israel and over Judah from Dan to Bersabee.
2 Samuel 3:11 And Memphibosthe could no longer answer Abenner a word for fear of him.
2 Samuel 3:12 And Abenner sent messengers to David at Thailam, where he was at once, saying, Make your covenant with me, and behold, my hand is with you to turn all the house of Israel to you.
2 Samuel 3:13 And David said, I will indeed make a covenant with you, except one thing I ask of you, saying, You shall not see my face unless you bring Melchol daughter of Saul when you come to see my face.
2 Samuel 3:14 And David sent messengers to Memphibosthe son of Saul, saying, Give me back my wife Melchol, whom I took for a hundred foreskins of foreigners.
2 Samuel 3:15 And Memphibosthe sent and took her from her husband, from Phaltiel son of Selles.
2 Samuel 3:16 And her husband went with her, weeping behind her as far as Barakim; and Abenner said to him, Go, return; and he returned. –
2 Samuel 3:17 And Abenner said to the elders of Israel, saying, Yesterday and the third day you sought David to reign over you;
2 Samuel 3:18 and now do it, because the Lord spoke concerning David, saying, By the hand of my servant David I will save Israel from the hand of the foreigners and from the hand of all their enemies.
2 Samuel 3:19 And Abenner spoke in the ears of Benjamin. And Abenner went to speak in David's ears in Chebron all that pleased Israel's eyes and the eyes of all the house of Benjamin.
2 Samuel 3:20 And Abenner came to David in Chebron with twenty men. And David made a drinking feast for Abenner and the men with him.
2 Samuel 3:21 And Abenner said to David, I will rise and go and gather all Israel to my lord the king and make a covenant with you, and you shall reign over all that your soul desires. And David sent Abenner away, and he went in peace. –
2 Samuel 3:22 And behold, David's servants and Joab were arriving from the expedition and carried much spoil with them; and Abenner was not with David in Chebron, because he had sent him away and he had departed in peace.
2 Samuel 3:23 And Joab and all his army were brought in, and it was reported to Joab, saying, Abenner son of Ner came to David, and he sent him away and he departed in peace.
2 Samuel 3:24 And Joab came to the king and said, What is this you have done? Behold, Abenner came to you, and why did you send him away so that he departed in peace?
2 Samuel 3:25 Do you not know the evil of Abenner son of Ner, that he came to deceive you and know your going out and your coming in and know all that you do?
2 Samuel 3:26 And Joab returned from David and sent messengers after Abenner, and they bring him back from the well of Seiram; and David did not know.
2 Samuel 3:27 And Abenner returned to Chebron, and Joab turned him aside at the side of the gate to speak to him in ambush and struck him there in the loin, and he died for the blood of Asael, Joab's brother.
2 Samuel 3:28 And David heard after these things and said, I and my kingdom are innocent before the Lord forever of the blood of Abenner son of Ner;
2 Samuel 3:29 may it come down upon Joab's head and all his father's house, and may there not fail from Joab's house one with a discharge and a leper and one holding a staff and one falling by the sword and one lacking bread.
2 Samuel 3:30 And Joab and Abessa his brother had been watching Abenner closely because he put Asael their brother to death in Gabaon in the war. –
2 Samuel 3:31 And David said to Joab and all the people with him, Tear your garments and gird yourselves with sackcloth and mourn before Abenner; and King David went behind the bier.
2 Samuel 3:32 And they bury Abenner in Chebron; and the king raised his voice and wept at his tomb, and all the people wept over Abenner.
2 Samuel 3:33 And the king lamented over Abenner and said, Shall Abenner die like the death of Nabal?
2 Samuel 3:34 Your hands were not bound, your feet were not in fetters; he did not bring forward like Nabal; before sons of wrongdoing you fell. And all the people gathered to weep for him.
2 Samuel 3:35 And all the people came to give David a meal of bread while it was still day, and David swore, saying, May God do thus to me and add thus, if before the sun sets I taste bread or anything at all.
2 Samuel 3:36 And all the people knew, and everything the king did before the people was pleasing before them.
2 Samuel 3:37 And all the people and all Israel knew on that day that it had not been from the king to put Abenner son of Ner to death.
2 Samuel 3:38 And the king said to his servants, Do you not know that a great leader has fallen in Israel on this day?
2 Samuel 3:39 And I am today a kinsman and appointed under a king, but these men, sons of Sarouia, are harder than I; may the Lord repay the one doing evil according to his evil.

## Chapter 4

2 Samuel 4:1 And Memphibosthe son of Saul heard that Abenner had died in Chebron, and his hands grew weak, and all the men of Israel became slack.
2 Samuel 4:2 And two men, leaders of bands for Memphibosthe son of Saul, the name of one was Baana and the name of the second Rechab, sons of Remmon the Berothite, of the sons of Benjamin; for Beroth was reckoned to the sons of Benjamin,
2 Samuel 4:3 and the Berothites fled to Getthaim and were sojourners there until this day. –
2 Samuel 4:4 And Jonathan son of Saul had a son stricken in the feet; he was five years old when the report about Saul and Jonathan his son came from Jezrael, and his nurse took him and fled, and it happened as she hurried and withdrew that he fell and became lame, and his name was Memphibosthe. –
2 Samuel 4:5 And the sons of Remmon the Berothite, Rekcha and Baana, went and entered in the heat of the day into the house of Memphibosthe, and he slept on the midday bed,
2 Samuel 4:6 and behold, the doorkeeper of the house was cleaning wheat and grew drowsy and slept, and Rekcha and Baana the brothers slipped through
2 Samuel 4:7 and entered the house, and Memphibosthe slept on his bed in his bedroom, and they strike him and put him to death and remove his head, and they took his head and departed on the westward road all night.
2 Samuel 4:8 And they brought the head of Memphibosthe to David in Chebron and said to the king, Behold, the head of Memphibosthe son of Saul your enemy, who sought your life, and the Lord gave to my lord the king vengeance upon his enemies as on this day, upon Saul your enemy and his seed.
2 Samuel 4:9 And David answered Rekcha and Baana his brother, sons of Remmon the Berothite, and said to them, As the Lord lives, who redeemed my life from every distress,
2 Samuel 4:10 when the one telling me that Saul had died – and he was like one announcing good news before me – I seized him and killed him in Sekelak, to whom I should have given a reward for good news;
2 Samuel 4:11 and now evil men have killed a righteous man in his house on his bed; and now I will seek his blood from your hands and destroy you from the earth.
2 Samuel 4:12 And David commanded his young men, and they kill them and cut off their hands and their feet and hung them by the spring in Chebron; and the head of Memphibosthe they buried in the tomb of Abenner son of Ner.

## Chapter 5

2 Samuel 5:1 And all the tribes of Israel come to David in Chebron and said to him, Behold, we are your bones and your flesh;
2 Samuel 5:2 and yesterday and the third day, when Saul was king over us, you were the one leading Israel out and bringing them in, and the Lord said to you, You shall shepherd my people Israel, and you shall be a leader over Israel.
2 Samuel 5:3 And all the elders of Israel come to the king in Chebron, and King David made a covenant with them in Chebron before the Lord, and they anoint David king over all Israel. –
2 Samuel 5:4 David was a son of thirty years when he began to reign, and he reigned forty years,
2 Samuel 5:5 seven years and six months he reigned in Chebron over Judah, and thirty-three years he reigned over all Israel and Judah in Jerusalem.
2 Samuel 5:6 And David and his men departed to Jerusalem against the Jebusite dwelling in the land. And it was said to David, You shall not enter here, because the blind and the lame stood against you, saying, David shall not enter here.
2 Samuel 5:7 And David took the stronghold of Sion [this is the city of David].
2 Samuel 5:8 And David said on that day, Everyone striking a Jebusite, let him touch with a dagger both the lame and the blind and those hating David's soul; therefore they will say, Blind and lame shall not enter the house of the Lord.
2 Samuel 5:9 And David sat in the stronghold, and it was called the city of David; and he built the city around from the citadel and his house.
2 Samuel 5:10 And David went on going and growing great, and the Lord Almighty was with him. –
2 Samuel 5:11 And Chiram king of Tyre sent messengers to David and cedar wood and carpenters of wood and masons of stone, and they built a house for David.
2 Samuel 5:12 And David knew that the Lord had established him as king over Israel and that his kingdom was raised up for the sake of his people Israel. –
2 Samuel 5:13 And David took more wives and concubines from Jerusalem after he came from Chebron, and more sons and daughters were born to David.
2 Samuel 5:14 And these are the names of those born to him in Jerusalem: Sammous and Sobab and Nathan and Salomon
2 Samuel 5:15 and Ebear and Elisous and Naphek and Jephies
2 Samuel 5:16 and Elisama and Elidae and Eliphalath,
2 Samuel 5:16 and Elisama and Elidae and Eliphalath,
2 Samuel 5:17 And the foreigners heard that David had been anointed king over Israel, and all the foreigners went up to seek David; and David heard and went down to the stronghold.
2 Samuel 5:18 And the foreigners come and fell together in the valley of the Titans.
2 Samuel 5:19 And David asked through the Lord, saying, Shall I go up against the foreigners, and will you give them into my hands? And the Lord said to David, Go up, because I will surely give the foreigners into your hands.
2 Samuel 5:20 And David came from the Upper Breaches and cut down the foreigners there, and David said, The Lord has broken through my enemies the foreigners before me as waters are broken through; therefore the name of that place was called Upper Breaches.
2 Samuel 5:21 And they leave their gods there, and David and the men with him took them. –
2 Samuel 5:22 And the foreigners continued again to go up and fell together in the valley of the Titans.
2 Samuel 5:23 And David inquired through the Lord, and the Lord said, You shall not go up to meet them; turn away from them and come upon them near the Weeping Place;
2 Samuel 5:24 and it shall be when you hear the sound of the closing together of the grove of the Weeping Place, then you shall go down against them, because then the Lord will go out before you to strike in the battle against the foreigners.
2 Samuel 5:25 And David did as the Lord commanded him and struck the foreigners from Gabaon to the land of Gazera.

## Chapter 6

2 Samuel 6:1 And David again gathered every young man from Israel, about seventy thousand.
2 Samuel 6:2 And David and all the people with him rose and went from the rulers of Judah on an ascent to bring up from there the ark of God, upon which the name of the Lord of hosts, seated upon the cherubim, was invoked.
2 Samuel 6:3 And he put the ark of the Lord upon a new wagon and took it from Aminadab's house on the hill; and Oza and his brothers, sons of Aminadab, drove the wagon
2 Samuel 6:4 with the ark, and his brothers went before the ark.
2 Samuel 6:5 And David and the sons of Israel played before the Lord with tuned instruments with strength and with songs and with lyres and harps and drums and cymbals and flutes.
2 Samuel 6:6 And they come as far as the threshing floor of Nodab, and Oza stretched out his hand upon the ark of God to hold it and grasped it, because the calf had pulled it aside, to hold it.
2 Samuel 6:7 And the Lord was angered with Oza, and God struck him there, and he died there beside the ark of the Lord before God.
2 Samuel 6:8 And David was disheartened because the Lord had made a breach in Oza; and that place was called Breach of Oza until this day.
2 Samuel 6:9 And David feared the Lord on that day, saying, How shall the ark of the Lord come in to me?
2 Samuel 6:10 And David did not wish to turn aside the ark of the Lord's covenant to himself into the city of David, and David turned it aside to the house of Abeddara the Gethite.
2 Samuel 6:11 And the ark of the Lord sat in the house of Abeddara the Gethite for three months; and the Lord blessed all the house of Abeddara and all that belonged to him.
2 Samuel 6:12 And it was reported to King David, saying, The Lord has blessed Abeddara's house and all that belongs to him because of the ark of God. And David went and brought up the ark of the Lord from Abeddara's house to the city of David with joy.
2 Samuel 6:13 And with those carrying the ark were seven dances and a sacrifice, a calf and lambs.
2 Samuel 6:14 And David played with tuned instruments before the Lord, and David wore a striking garment.
2 Samuel 6:15 And David and all the house of Israel brought up the ark of the Lord with shouting and with the sound of a trumpet.
2 Samuel 6:16 And it happened as the ark came as far as the city of David that Melchol daughter of Saul looked through the window and saw King David dancing and playing before the Lord and despised him in her heart.
2 Samuel 6:17 And they carry the ark of the Lord and set it in its place in the middle of the tent that David had pitched for it; and David offered up whole burnt offerings before the Lord and peace offerings.
2 Samuel 6:18 And David finished offering together the whole burnt offerings and peace offerings and blessed the people in the name of the Lord of hosts.
2 Samuel 6:19 And he distributed to all the people, to all the force of Israel from Dan to Bersabee, from man to woman, to each a round loaf of bread and a hearth cake and a cake from a pan; and all the people departed, each to his house. –
2 Samuel 6:20 And David returned to bless his house, and Melchol daughter of Saul went out to meet David and blessed him and said, How glorified today was the king of Israel, who uncovered himself today in the eyes of the maidservants of his servants, as one of the dancers uncovers himself uncovered.
2 Samuel 6:21 And David said to Melchol, Before the Lord I will dance; blessed be the Lord, who chose me above your father and above all his house to appoint me leader over his people, over Israel; and I will play and dance before the Lord
2 Samuel 6:22 and will uncover myself still thus and be worthless in your eyes and with the maidservants among whom you said I was glorified.
2 Samuel 6:23 And Melchol daughter of Saul had no child until the day of her death.

## Chapter 7

2 Samuel 7:1 And it happened when the king sat in his house and the Lord had allotted him rest all around from all his enemies around,
2 Samuel 7:2 that the king said to Nathan the prophet, Behold now, I dwell in a cedar house, and the ark of God sits in the midst of the tent.
2 Samuel 7:3 And Nathan said to the king, All that is in your heart, go and do, because the Lord is with you. –
2 Samuel 7:4 And it happened on that night that the word of the Lord came to Nathan, saying,
2 Samuel 7:5 Go and say to my servant David, Thus says the Lord: You shall not build me a house for me to dwell in;
2 Samuel 7:6 for I have not dwelt in a house from the day I brought the sons of Israel up from Egypt until this day, and I was walking about in a lodging place and in a tent.
2 Samuel 7:7 In all the places through which I passed in all Israel, did I ever speak to one tribe of Israel, whom I commanded to shepherd my people Israel, saying, Why have you not built me a cedar house?
2 Samuel 7:8 And now thus you shall say to my servant David: Thus says the Lord Almighty: I took you from the sheepfold to be a leader over my people, over Israel,
2 Samuel 7:9 and I was with you in all the places where you went, and I destroyed all your enemies from before you and made you renowned like the name of the great ones on earth.
2 Samuel 7:10 And I will set a place for my people Israel and plant them, and they shall dwell by themselves and no longer be anxious, and a son of wrongdoing shall not continue to humble them as from the beginning,
2 Samuel 7:11 from the days when I appointed judges over my people Israel, and I will give you rest from all your enemies, and the Lord will tell you that you will build him a house.
2 Samuel 7:12 And it shall be when your days are fulfilled and you sleep with your fathers that I will raise up your seed after you, who shall be from your belly, and I will establish his kingdom;
2 Samuel 7:13 he shall build me a house for my name, and I will set his throne upright forever.
2 Samuel 7:14 I will be a father to him, and he shall be a son to me; and if his wrongdoing comes, I will reprove him with a rod of men and with the touches of sons of men;
2 Samuel 7:15 but my mercy I will not remove from him as I removed it from those whom I removed from before me.
2 Samuel 7:16 And his house and his kingdom shall be made faithful forever before me, and his throne shall be set upright forever.
2 Samuel 7:17 According to all these words and all this vision, so Nathan spoke to David. –
2 Samuel 7:18 And King David entered and sat before the Lord and said, Who am I, my lord Lord, and what is my house, that you have loved me to this extent?
2 Samuel 7:19 And it was made a little thing before you, my lord Lord, and you spoke concerning your servant's house for a distant time; and this is the law of man, my lord Lord.
2 Samuel 7:20 And what more shall David add to speak to you? And now you know your servant, my lord Lord.
2 Samuel 7:21 For the sake of your word you have done it, and according to your heart you have done all this greatness to make it known to your servant,
2 Samuel 7:22 for the sake of magnifying you, my lord Lord, because there is none like you and no God besides you among all that we have heard with our ears.
2 Samuel 7:23 And who is like your people Israel, another nation on the earth? As God led them to redeem a people for himself, to make you a name, to do greatness and manifestation, to cast out for you from before your people whom you redeemed for yourself from Egypt, nations and dwellings.
2 Samuel 7:24 And you established for yourself your people Israel as a people forever, and you, Lord, became God to them.
2 Samuel 7:25 And now, my lord Lord, the word that you spoke concerning your servant and his house, make faithful forever, Lord Almighty, God of Israel; and now as you spoke,
2 Samuel 7:26 may your name be magnified forever.
2 Samuel 7:27 Lord Almighty, God of Israel, you uncovered your servant's ear, saying, I will build you a house; therefore your servant found his own heart to pray this prayer to you.
2 Samuel 7:28 And now, my lord Lord, you are God, and your words shall be true, and you spoke these good things concerning your servant;
2 Samuel 7:29 and now begin and bless the house of your servant to be before you forever, because you are, my lord Lord, you spoke, and from your blessing your servant's house shall be blessed forever.

## Chapter 8

2 Samuel 8:1 And it happened after these things that David struck the foreigners and routed them; and David took the separated place from the hand of the foreigners.
2 Samuel 8:2 And David struck Moab and measured them with ropes after laying them on the ground, and there were two rope measures for putting to death, and two rope measures he kept alive, and Moab became servants to David bringing gifts.
2 Samuel 8:3 And David struck Adraazar son of Raab king of Souba as he went to establish his hand over the river Euphrates.
2 Samuel 8:4 And David took in advance from him a thousand chariots and seven thousand horsemen and twenty thousand foot soldiers, and David disabled all the chariots and left of them a hundred chariots.
2 Samuel 8:5 And Syria of Damascus comes to help Adraazar king of Souba, and David struck twenty-two thousand men among the Syrians.
2 Samuel 8:6 And David set a garrison in Syria by Damascus, and the Syrian became David's servants bringing gifts. And the Lord saved David in all the places where he went. –
2 Samuel 8:7 And David took the golden bracelets that were on the servants of Adraazar king of Souba and brought them to Jerusalem; and Sousakim king of Egypt took them when he came up to Jerusalem in the days of Roboam son of Solomon.
2 Samuel 8:8 And from Masbak, from Adraazar's chosen cities, King David took very much bronze; with it Salomon made the bronze sea and the pillars and the basins and all the equipment. –
2 Samuel 8:9 And Thoou king of Hamath heard that David had struck all the force of Adraazar,
2 Samuel 8:10 and Thoou sent Jeddouran his son to King David to ask him about peace and bless him because he fought Adraazar and struck him, because he was opposed to Adraazar, and in his hands were silver vessels and gold vessels and bronze vessels.
2 Samuel 8:11 And King David consecrated these to the Lord along with the silver and the gold that he had consecrated from all the cities he had subdued,
2 Samuel 8:12 from Idumea and the land of Moab and the sons of Ammon and the foreigners and Amalek and the spoils of Adraazar son of Raab king of Souba. –
2 Samuel 8:13 And David made a name; and when he returned he struck Idumea in Gaimele, eighteen thousand.
2 Samuel 8:14 And he set a garrison in Idumea, in all Idumea, and all the Idumeans became servants to the king. And the Lord saved David in all the places where he went.
2 Samuel 8:15 And David reigned over Israel, and David was doing judgment and righteousness for all his people.
2 Samuel 8:16 And Joab son of Sarouia was over the army, and Josaphat son of Achia over the records,
2 Samuel 8:17 and Saddouk son of Achitob and Achimelech son of Abiathar were priests, and Asa was the scribe,
2 Samuel 8:18 and Banaias son of Jodae was counselor, and the Cheletthite and the Pheletthite; and David's sons were court leaders.

## Chapter 9

2 Samuel 9:1 And David said, Is anyone still left of Saul's house, that I may show mercy to him for Jonathan's sake?
2 Samuel 9:2 And there was a servant from Saul's house, and his name was Siba, and they call him to David. And the king said to him, Are you Siba? And he said, I am your servant.
2 Samuel 9:3 And the king said, Is a man still left of Saul's house, that I may show him God's mercy? And Siba said to the king, There is still a son of Jonathan, stricken in the feet.
2 Samuel 9:4 And the king said, Where is he? And Siba said to the king, Behold, in the house of Machir son of Amiel, from Ladabar.
2 Samuel 9:5 And King David sent and took him from the house of Machir son of Amiel, from Ladabar.
2 Samuel 9:6 And Memphibosthe son of Jonathan son of Saul comes to King David and fell on his face and bowed to him. And David said to him, Memphibosthe; and he said, Behold, your servant.
2 Samuel 9:7 And David said to him, Do not fear, because I will surely show mercy to you for Jonathan your father's sake and will restore to you every field of Saul, the father of your father, and you shall eat bread at my table always.
2 Samuel 9:8 And Memphibosthe bowed and said, Who am I, your servant, that you looked upon a dead dog like me?
2 Samuel 9:9 And the king called Siba, Saul's servant, and said to him, All that belonged to Saul and all his house I have given to your lord's son;
2 Samuel 9:10 and you shall work the land for him, you and your sons and your servants, and bring bread to your lord's son, and he shall eat it; and Memphibosthe, your lord's son, shall always eat bread at my table. [And Siba had fifteen sons and twenty servants.]
2 Samuel 9:11 And Siba said to the king, According to all that my lord the king has commanded his servant, so your servant will do. And Memphibosthe ate at David's table like one of the king's sons.
2 Samuel 9:12 And Memphibosthe had a little son, and his name was Micha. And all the household of Siba's house were servants of Memphibosthe.
2 Samuel 9:13 And Memphibosthe dwelt in Jerusalem, because he always ate at the king's table; and he was lame in both his feet.

## Chapter 10

2 Samuel 10:1 And it happened after these things that the king of the sons of Ammon died, and Annon his son reigned in his place.
2 Samuel 10:2 And David said, I will show mercy to Annon son of Naas, in the way his father showed mercy to me; and David sent to comfort him by the hand of his servants concerning his father. And David's servants came to the land of the sons of Ammon.
2 Samuel 10:3 And the rulers of the sons of Ammon said to Annon their lord, Is it out of honoring your father before you that David sent comforters to you? Did David not send his servants to you so that they might search the city and spy it out and examine it?
2 Samuel 10:4 And Annon took David's servants and shaved their beards and cut their mantles in half as far as their hips and sent them away.
2 Samuel 10:5 And they reported to David about the men, and he sent to meet them, because the men had been greatly dishonored; and the king said, Sit in Jericho until your beards grow, and you shall return. –
2 Samuel 10:6 And the sons of Ammon saw that they had been shamed by David's people, and the sons of Ammon sent and hired Syria of Baithroob, twenty thousand foot soldiers, and the king of Maacha, a thousand men, and Istob, twelve thousand men.
2 Samuel 10:7 And David heard and sent Joab and all the force, the mighty men.
2 Samuel 10:8 And the sons of Ammon went out and drew up for battle by the door of the gate, and Syria of Souba and Roob and Istob and Maacha were alone in the field.
2 Samuel 10:9 And Joab saw that the face of battle was against him, from the front opposite him and from behind, and chose from all the young men of Israel, and they drew up opposite Syria.
2 Samuel 10:10 And the remainder of the people he placed in the hand of Abessa his brother, and they drew up opposite the sons of Ammon.
2 Samuel 10:11 And he said, If Syria grows strong against me, you shall be for my salvation, and if the sons of Ammon grow strong against you, we shall save you;
2 Samuel 10:12 be a man, and let us grow strong for our people and for the cities of our God, and the Lord will do what is good in his eyes.
2 Samuel 10:13 And Joab and his people with him came forward for battle against Syria, and they fled before him.
2 Samuel 10:14 And the sons of Ammon saw that Syria had fled, and they fled before Abessa and entered the city. And Joab returned from the sons of Ammon, and they came to Jerusalem. –
2 Samuel 10:15 And Syria saw that it had stumbled before Israel, and they gathered together.
2 Samuel 10:16 And Adraazar sent and gathered the Syrians from beyond the river Chalamak, and they came to Ailam, and Sobak, commander of Adraazar's force, was before them.
2 Samuel 10:17 And it was reported to David, and he gathered all Israel and crossed the Jordan and came to Ailam; and Syria drew up opposite David and fought with him.
2 Samuel 10:18 And Syria fled before Israel, and David slew from Syria seven hundred chariots and forty thousand horsemen; and he struck Sobak the commander of his force, and he died there.
2 Samuel 10:19 And all the kings who were servants of Adraazar saw that they had stumbled before Israel, and they deserted to Israel and served them. And Syria feared to save the sons of Ammon any longer.

## Chapter 11

2 Samuel 11:1 And it happened when the year turned at the time of the going out of kings that David sent Joab and his servants with him and all Israel, and they destroyed the sons of Ammon and sat besieging Rabbath; and David sat in Jerusalem.
2 Samuel 11:2 And it happened toward evening that David rose from his bed and walked on the roof of the king's house and saw a woman bathing from the roof, and the woman was very beautiful in appearance.
2 Samuel 11:3 And David sent and sought out the woman, and he said, Is this not Bersabee daughter of Eliab, wife of Ourias the Chettite?
2 Samuel 11:4 And David sent messengers and took her, and she came to him, and he slept with her, and she was being sanctified from her uncleanness, and she returned to her house.
2 Samuel 11:5 And the woman conceived; and she sent and told David and said, I am with child.
2 Samuel 11:6 And David sent to Joab, saying, Send me Ourias the Chettite; and Joab sent Ourias to David.
2 Samuel 11:7 And Ourias comes and entered to him, and David asked about the peace of Joab and the peace of the people and the peace of the war.
2 Samuel 11:8 And David said to Ourias, Go down to your house and wash your feet; and Ourias went out from the king's house, and a gift from the king went out after him.
2 Samuel 11:9 And Ourias slept by the king's door with his lord's servants and did not go down to his house.
2 Samuel 11:10 And they told David, saying that Ourias did not go down to his house. And David said to Ourias, Have you not come from a journey? Why did you not go down to your house?
2 Samuel 11:11 And Ourias said to David, The ark and Israel and Judah dwell in tents, and my lord Joab and my lord's servants are encamped upon the face of the field; and shall I enter my house to eat and drink and sleep with my wife? How? As your soul lives, I shall not do this thing.
2 Samuel 11:12 And David said to Ourias, Sit here today too, and tomorrow I will send you away; and Ourias sat in Jerusalem that day and the next.
2 Samuel 11:13 And David called him, and he ate before him and drank, and he made him drunk; and he went out in the evening to sleep on his bed with his lord's servants, and did not go down to his house.
2 Samuel 11:14 And it happened in the morning that David wrote a letter to Joab and sent it in Ourias's hand.
2 Samuel 11:15 And he wrote in the letter, saying, Bring Ourias opposite the strong battle, and turn back from behind him, and he shall be struck and die.
2 Samuel 11:16 And it happened as Joab watched the city that he placed Ourias in the place where he knew that mighty men were.
2 Samuel 11:17 And the men of the city went out and fought with Joab, and some of the people of David's servants fell, and Ourias the Chettite died too.
2 Samuel 11:18 And Joab sent and reported to the king all the words of the war
2 Samuel 11:19 and commanded the messenger, saying, When you finish speaking all the words of the war to the king,
2 Samuel 11:20 it shall be, if the king's anger rises and he says to you, Why did you approach the city to fight? Did you not know that they would shoot from above the wall?
2 Samuel 11:21 Who struck Abimelech son of Jerobaal? Did a woman not throw a piece of millstone on him from above the wall, and he died in Thamasi? Why did you approach the wall? Then say, Your servant Ourias the Chettite also died.
2 Samuel 11:22 And Joab's messenger went to the king in Jerusalem and came and reported to David all that Joab had reported to him, all the words of the war. And David was angered with Joab and said to the messenger, Why did you approach the city to fight? Did you not know that you would be struck from the wall? Who struck Abimelech son of Jerobaal? Did a woman not throw a piece of millstone on him from the wall, and he died in Thamasi? Why did you approach the wall?
2 Samuel 11:23 And the messenger said to David, Because the men grew strong against us and came out against us into the field, and we came upon them as far as the door of the gate,
2 Samuel 11:24 and the archers shot at your servants from above the wall, and some of the king's servants died, and your servant Ourias the Chettite died too.
2 Samuel 11:25 And David said to the messenger, Thus you shall say to Joab: Let this thing not be evil in your eyes, because sometimes thus and sometimes thus the sword devours; strengthen your battle against the city and pull it down and strengthen him.
2 Samuel 11:26 And Ourias's wife heard that Ourias her husband had died, and she mourned her husband.
2 Samuel 11:27 And the mourning passed, and David sent and gathered her to his house, and she became his wife and bore him a son. And the thing that David had done appeared evil in the eyes of the Lord.

## Chapter 12

2 Samuel 12:1 And the Lord sent Nathan the prophet to David, and he entered to him and said to him, There were two men in one city, one rich and one poor;
2 Samuel 12:2 and the rich man had very many flocks and herds,
2 Samuel 12:3 but the poor man had nothing except one little ewe lamb, which he acquired and kept and raised, and it grew with him and with his sons together, ate from his bread and drank from his cup and slept in his bosom and was like a daughter to him;
2 Samuel 12:4 and a traveler came to the rich man, and he spared taking from his flocks and his herds to prepare for the traveling stranger who had come to him, and he took the poor man's ewe lamb and prepared it for the man who had come to him.
2 Samuel 12:5 And David was very angry with the man, and David said to Nathan, As the Lord lives, the man who did this is a son of death,
2 Samuel 12:6 and he shall repay the ewe lamb sevenfold because he did this thing and because he did not spare.
2 Samuel 12:7 And Nathan said to David, You are the man who did this; thus says the Lord God of Israel: I anointed you king over Israel, and I delivered you from Saul's hand
2 Samuel 12:8 and gave you your lord's house and your lord's wives into your bosom and gave you the house of Israel and Judah; and if it is little, I will add to you according to these things.
2 Samuel 12:9 Why did you slight the word of the Lord to do evil in his eyes? You struck Ourias the Chettite with the sword and took his wife as a wife for yourself, and you killed him by the sword of the sons of Ammon.
2 Samuel 12:10 And now the sword shall not depart from your house forever because you despised me and took the wife of Ourias the Chettite to be your wife.
2 Samuel 12:11 Thus says the Lord: Behold, I am raising up evils against you from your house, and I will take your wives before your eyes and give them to your neighbor, and he shall sleep with your wives before this sun;
2 Samuel 12:12 because you did it secretly, but I will do this thing before all Israel and before this sun.
2 Samuel 12:13 And David said to Nathan, I have sinned against the Lord. And Nathan said to David, And the Lord has passed over your sin; you shall certainly not die;
2 Samuel 12:14 except that by this thing you have surely provoked the Lord's enemies, and your son born to you shall surely die.
2 Samuel 12:15 And Nathan departed to his house. And the Lord struck the child whom Ourias's wife bore to David, and it became sick.
2 Samuel 12:16 And David sought God for the young child, and David fasted a fast and went in and spent the night in sackcloth on the ground.
2 Samuel 12:17 And the elders of his house rose over him to raise him from the ground, and he would not and did not eat bread with them.
2 Samuel 12:18 And it happened on the seventh day that the young child died; and David's servants feared to tell him that the young child had died, because they said, Behold, while the young child still lived we spoke to him and he did not listen to our voice; and how shall we say to him that the young child has died? And he will do evil.
2 Samuel 12:19 And David understood that his servants were whispering, and David perceived that the young child had died; and David said to his servants, Has the young child died? And they said, He has died.
2 Samuel 12:20 And David rose from the ground and washed and anointed himself and changed his garments and entered the house of God and worshiped him; and he entered his house and asked for bread to eat, and they set bread before him, and he ate.
2 Samuel 12:21 And his servants said to him, What is this thing you have done? For the sake of the young child while he was still living you fasted and wept and kept vigil, and when the young child died, you rose and ate bread and drank.
2 Samuel 12:22 And David said, While the young child still lived I fasted and wept, because I said, Who knows if the Lord will have mercy on me and the young child will live?
2 Samuel 12:23 And now he has died; why should I fast? Can I bring him back again? I shall go to him, and he shall not return to me.
2 Samuel 12:24 And David comforted Bersabee his wife and went in to her and slept with her, and she conceived and bore a son, and he called his name Salomon, and the Lord loved him.
2 Samuel 12:25 And he sent by the hand of Nathan the prophet, and he called his name Jededi for the Lord's sake.
2 Samuel 12:26 And Joab fought in Rabbath of the sons of Ammon and took the royal city.
2 Samuel 12:27 And Joab sent messengers to David and said, I fought in Rabbath and took the city of the waters;
2 Samuel 12:28 and now gather the remainder of the people and encamp against the city and take it first, lest I take the city first and my name be called upon it.
2 Samuel 12:29 And David gathered all the people and went to Rabbath and fought in it and took it.
2 Samuel 12:30 And he took the crown of Melchol their king from his head, and its weight was a talent of gold and a precious stone, and it was upon David's head; and he brought out very much spoil from the city.
2 Samuel 12:31 And he brought out the people in it and placed them in the saw and the iron threshing tools and led them through the brickworks; and thus he did to all the cities of the sons of Ammon. And David and all the people returned to Jerusalem.

## Chapter 13

2 Samuel 13:1 And it happened after these things that Abessalom son of David had a sister very beautiful in appearance, and her name was Themar, and Amnon son of David loved her.
2 Samuel 13:2 And Amnon was distressed to the point of becoming ill because of Themar his sister, because she was a virgin, and it was excessive in Amnon's eyes to do anything to her.
2 Samuel 13:3 And Amnon had a companion, and his name was Jonadab son of Samaa, David's brother; and Jonadab was a very clever man.
2 Samuel 13:4 And he said to him, Why are you thus weak, king's son, morning by morning? Will you not tell me? And Amnon said to him, I love Themar, the sister of my brother Abessalom.
2 Samuel 13:5 And Jonadab said to him, Lie on your bed and act ill, and your father will enter to see you, and you shall say to him, Let Themar my sister come and feed me and prepare food before my eyes, so that I may see and eat from her hands.
2 Samuel 13:6 And Amnon lay down and became ill, and the king entered to see him, and Amnon said to the king, Let Themar my sister come to me and make two small loaves before my eyes, and I will eat from her hand.
2 Samuel 13:7 And David sent to Themar in the house, saying, Go now to the house of Amnon your brother and prepare food for him.
2 Samuel 13:8 And Themar went to the house of Amnon her brother, and he was lying down. And she took the dough and kneaded it and made small loaves before his eyes and baked the loaves;
2 Samuel 13:9 and she took the pan and emptied it before him, and he did not wish to eat. And Amnon said, Bring every man out from me; and they brought every man out from him.
2 Samuel 13:10 And Amnon said to Themar, Bring the food into the chamber, and I will eat from your hand. And Themar took the small loaves she had made and brought them to Amnon her brother into the bedroom
2 Samuel 13:11 and brought them to him to eat, and he seized her and said to her, Come, sleep with me, my sister.
2 Samuel 13:12 And she said to him, No, my brother, do not humble me, because this is not done in Israel; do not do this folly;
2 Samuel 13:13 and where shall I carry my reproach? And you shall be like one of the fools in Israel; and now speak to the king, because he will certainly not withhold me from you.
2 Samuel 13:14 And Amnon did not wish to listen to her voice and grew stronger than she and humbled her and slept with her.
2 Samuel 13:15 And Amnon hated her with a very great hatred, because the hatred with which he hated her was greater than the love with which he had loved her. And Amnon said to her, Rise and go.
2 Samuel 13:16 And Themar said to him, No, brother, because this last evil is greater than the first that you did with me, to send me away. And Amnon did not wish to listen to her voice.
2 Samuel 13:17 And he called his young man who stood over his house and said to him, Send this woman out from me now and shut the door behind her.
2 Samuel 13:18 And she wore a many-colored tunic, because thus the king's daughters who were virgins wore their outer garments; and his attendant brought her out and shut the door behind her;
2 Samuel 13:19 and Themar took ashes and put them on her head and tore the many-colored tunic she wore and put her hands upon her head and went on walking and crying out.
2 Samuel 13:20 And Abessalom her brother said to her, Has Amnon your brother been with you? And now, my sister, be silent, for he is your brother; do not set your heart to speak about this thing. And Themar sat desolate in the house of Abessalom her brother.
2 Samuel 13:21 And King David heard all these words and was very angry; and he did not grieve the spirit of Amnon his son, because he loved him, because he was his firstborn.
2 Samuel 13:22 And Abessalom did not speak with Amnon from evil to good, because Abessalom hated Amnon on account of the matter that he had humbled Themar his sister.
2 Samuel 13:23 And it happened after two years of days that they were shearing for Abessalom in Belasor adjoining Ephraim, and Abessalom called all the king's sons.
2 Samuel 13:24 And Abessalom came to the king and said, Behold now, they are shearing for your servant; let the king and his servants go with your servant.
2 Samuel 13:25 And the king said to Abessalom, No, my son, let not all of us go, lest we burden you. And he pressed him, but he did not wish to go and blessed him.
2 Samuel 13:26 And Abessalom said, But if not, let Amnon my brother go with us. And the king said to him, Why should he go with you?
2 Samuel 13:27 And Abessalom pressed him, and he sent Amnon and all the king's sons with him. And Abessalom made a drinking feast like the king's feast.
2 Samuel 13:28 And Abessalom commanded his young men, saying, Watch when Amnon's heart becomes glad with wine and I say to you, Strike Amnon, and put him to death; do not fear, for is it not I who command you? Be men and become sons of strength.
2 Samuel 13:29 And Abessalom's young men did to Amnon as Abessalom commanded them. And all the king's sons rose and each mounted his mule and fled.
2 Samuel 13:30 And it happened while they were on the road that the report came to David, saying, Abessalom has struck all the king's sons, and not even one of them has been left.
2 Samuel 13:31 And the king rose and tore his garments and lay upon the ground, and all his servants standing around him tore their garments.
2 Samuel 13:32 And Jonadab son of Samaa, David's brother, answered and said, Let not my lord the king say that he put to death all the young men, the king's sons, because Amnon alone has died; for it had lain on Abessalom's mouth since the day he humbled Themar his sister;
2 Samuel 13:33 and now let not my lord the king place a word on his heart saying, All the king's sons have died, because only Amnon alone has died.
2 Samuel 13:34 And Abessalom escaped. And the young watchman raised his eyes and saw, and behold, many people going on the road behind him from the side of the mountain on the descent; and the watchman came and reported to the king and said, I have seen men from the road of Oronen from the side of the mountain.
2 Samuel 13:35 And Jonadab said to the king, Behold, the king's sons are present; according to your servant's word, so it happened.
2 Samuel 13:36 And it happened when he finished speaking that behold, the king's sons came and raised their voices and wept, and the king and all his servants also wept with a very great weeping.
2 Samuel 13:37 And Abessalom fled and went to Tholmai son of Emioud king of Gedsour in the land of Machad. And King David mourned his son all the days.
2 Samuel 13:38 And Abessalom escaped and went to Gedsour and was there three years.
2 Samuel 13:39 And the king's spirit ceased from going out after Abessalom, because he was comforted over Amnon, because he had died.

## Chapter 14

2 Samuel 14:1 And Joab son of Sarouia knew that the king's heart was upon Abessalom.
2 Samuel 14:2 And Joab sent to Thekoe and took a wise woman from there and said to her, Mourn now and put on mourning garments and do not anoint yourself with oil, and be like a woman mourning one who has died for many days,
2 Samuel 14:3 and you shall go to the king and speak to him according to this word; and Joab placed the words in her mouth.
2 Samuel 14:4 And the Thekoite woman entered to the king and fell on her face to the ground and bowed to him and said, Save, king, save.
2 Samuel 14:5 And the king said to her, What is it with you? And she said, I am indeed a widow, and my husband died.
2 Samuel 14:6 And your servant had two sons, and they both fought in the field, and there was no one to deliver between them, and the one struck his brother and put him to death.
2 Samuel 14:7 And behold, the whole family rose against your servant and said, Give the one who struck his brother, and we will put him to death in exchange for his brother's life whom he killed, and we will remove your heir too; and they will extinguish my remaining coal so as not to leave my husband a remnant and a name on the face of the earth.
2 Samuel 14:8 And the king said, Go in health to your house, and I will command concerning you.
2 Samuel 14:9 And the Thekoite woman said to the king, Upon me, my lord king, be the lawlessness and upon my father's house, and the king and his throne are innocent.
2 Samuel 14:10 And the king said, Who is the one speaking to you? Bring him to me, and he will no longer continue to touch him.
2 Samuel 14:11 And she said, Let the king remember the Lord his God, lest a kinsman of blood multiply to destroy, and they shall certainly not remove my son. And he said, As the Lord lives, not a hair of your son shall fall to the ground.
2 Samuel 14:12 And the woman said, Let your servant speak a word to my lord the king. And he said, Speak.
2 Samuel 14:13 And the woman said, Why did you reckon such a thing against God's people? Is this word from the king's mouth like an offense, in that the king does not bring back his own banished one?
2 Samuel 14:14 For we shall surely die, and like water poured upon the earth that shall not be gathered; and God will take a life, and he reckons concerning driving away a banished one from himself.
2 Samuel 14:15 And now I have come to speak this word to my lord the king because the people will see me, and your servant will say, Let me now speak to the king, if perhaps the king will do the word of his servant;
2 Samuel 14:16 for the king will listen to deliver his servant from the hand of the man seeking to remove me and my son from God's inheritance.
2 Samuel 14:17 And the woman said, May the word of my lord the king be a sacrifice, because like an angel of God, so is my lord the king in hearing the good and the evil, and the Lord your God shall be with you.
2 Samuel 14:18 And the king answered and said to the woman, Do not hide from me the thing I ask you. And the woman said, Let my lord the king speak.
2 Samuel 14:19 And the king said, Is Joab's hand with you in all this? And the woman said to the king, As your soul lives, my lord king, there is nothing to the right or to the left of all that my lord the king has spoken, because your servant Joab himself commanded me and himself placed all these words in your servant's mouth;
2 Samuel 14:20 for the sake of going around the face of this matter your servant Joab did this thing, and my lord is wise like the wisdom of an angel of God to know all that is in the land.
2 Samuel 14:21 And the king said to Joab, Behold, I have done for you according to this word of yours; go, bring back the young man Abessalom.
2 Samuel 14:22 And Joab fell on his face to the ground and bowed and blessed the king, and Joab said, Today your servant knows that I have found favor in your eyes, my lord king, because my lord the king has done the word of his servant.
2 Samuel 14:23 And Joab rose and went to Gedsour and brought Abessalom to Jerusalem.
2 Samuel 14:24 And the king said, Let him return to his house and not see my face. And Abessalom returned to his house and did not see the king's face. –
2 Samuel 14:25 And there was no man in all Israel so greatly praised as Abessalom; from the sole of his foot to the top of his head there was no blemish in him.
2 Samuel 14:26 And when he sheared his head – and it happened from the beginning of days to days whenever he was sheared, because it weighed heavily upon him – when he sheared it, he weighed the hair of his head, two hundred shekels by the royal shekel.
2 Samuel 14:27 And three sons and one daughter were born to Abessalom, and her name was Themar; she was a very beautiful woman and became the wife of Roboam son of Salomon and bore him Abia.
2 Samuel 14:28 And Abessalom sat in Jerusalem two years of days and did not see the king's face.
2 Samuel 14:29 And Abessalom sent to Joab to send him to the king, and he did not wish to come to him; and he sent to him a second time, and he did not wish to come.
2 Samuel 14:30 And Abessalom said to his servants, See Joab's portion in the field adjoining mine, and he has barley there; go and set it on fire; and Abessalom's servants set it on fire. And Joab's servants come to him with their garments torn and said, Abessalom's servants burned the portion with fire.
2 Samuel 14:31 And Joab rose and came to Abessalom in the house and said to him, Why did your servants burn my portion with fire?
2 Samuel 14:32 And Abessalom said to Joab, Behold, I sent to you, saying, Come here and I will send you to the king, saying, Why did I come from Gedsour? It was good for me to remain there; and now behold, I have not seen the king's face; and if there is wrongdoing in me, put me to death.
2 Samuel 14:33 And Joab entered to the king and told him, and he called Abessalom, and he entered to the king and bowed to him and fell on his face to the ground before the king, and the king kissed Abessalom.

## Chapter 15

2 Samuel 15:1 And it happened after these things that Abessalom made for himself chariots and horses and fifty men to run before him.
2 Samuel 15:2 And Abessalom rose early and stood beside the way of the gate, and it happened that every man who had a case came to the king for judgment, and Abessalom would call to him and say to him, From what city are you? And the man said, Your servant is from one of the tribes of Israel.
2 Samuel 15:3 And Abessalom said to him, Behold, your words are good and easy, but there is no one from the king to hear you;
2 Samuel 15:4 and Abessalom said, Who will appoint me judge in the land, so that every man who has a dispute and judgment may come to me, and I will vindicate him?
2 Samuel 15:5 And it happened when a man drew near to bow to him that he stretched out his hand and took hold of him and kissed him.
2 Samuel 15:6 And Abessalom did according to this thing to all Israel who came to the king for judgment, and Abessalom made the hearts of Israel's men his own.
2 Samuel 15:7 And it happened at the end of forty years that Abessalom said to his father, Let me go now and pay my vows which I vowed to the Lord in Chebron;
2 Samuel 15:8 for your servant vowed a vow while I dwelt in Gedsour in Syria, saying, If the Lord surely returns me to Jerusalem, then I will serve the Lord.
2 Samuel 15:9 And the king said to him, Go in peace; and he rose and went to Chebron.
2 Samuel 15:10 And Abessalom sent scouts among all the tribes of Israel, saying, When you hear the sound of the horn, you shall say, Abessalom has become king in Chebron.
2 Samuel 15:11 And with Abessalom went two hundred invited men from Jerusalem, going in their simplicity, and they knew nothing of the matter.
2 Samuel 15:12 And Abessalom sent and called Achitophel the Gelmonite, David's counselor, from his city, from Gola, while he was sacrificing. And the band became strong, and the people going with Abessalom were many.
2 Samuel 15:13 And one reporting came to David, saying, The heart of Israel's men has gone after Abessalom.
2 Samuel 15:14 And David said to all his servants with him in Jerusalem, Rise and let us flee, because there is no salvation for us from before Abessalom; hurry to go, lest he hurry and overtake us and thrust evil upon us and strike the city with the edge of the sword.
2 Samuel 15:15 And the king's servants said to the king, According to all that our lord the king chooses, behold, your servants.
2 Samuel 15:16 And the king and all his household went out on their feet; and the king left ten women of his concubines to guard the house.
2 Samuel 15:17 And the king and all his servants went out on foot and stood at the distant house.
2 Samuel 15:18 And all his servants passed by his side, and all the Chetti and all the Pheletthe stood by the olive tree in the wilderness; and all the people passed along beside him and all those around him and all the mature men and all the warriors, six hundred men, and stood beside him; and all the Cheretthite and all the Pheletthite and all the Gethites, six hundred men who had come on foot from Geth, went before the king.
2 Samuel 15:19 And the king said to Etthi the Gethite, Why do you too go with us? Return and dwell with the king, because you are a foreigner and have migrated from your place.
2 Samuel 15:20 If you arrived yesterday, shall I move you with us today and will you move from your place? Yesterday was your departure, and today shall I move you with us to go? And I will go wherever I go. Return and take your brothers back with you, and the Lord will show you mercy and truth.
2 Samuel 15:21 And Etthi answered the king and said, As the Lord lives and as my lord the king lives, wherever my lord is, whether for death or for life, there your servant shall be.
2 Samuel 15:22 And the king said to Etthi, Come and cross with me; and Etthi the Gethite passed along and all his servants and all the crowd with him.
2 Samuel 15:23 And all the land wept with a great voice. And all the people were passing through the torrent bed Kedron, and the king crossed the torrent bed Kedron; and all the people and the king passed on toward the wilderness road. –
2 Samuel 15:24 And behold, Saddok too and all the Levites with him carried the ark of the Lord's covenant from Baithar and set down the ark of God, and Abiathar went up, until all the people had finished passing out of the city.
2 Samuel 15:25 And the king said to Saddok, Return the ark of God to the city; if I find favor in the Lord's eyes, he will bring me back and show me it and its beauty;
2 Samuel 15:26 and if he says thus, I have not desired you, behold, here I am, let him do to me what is good in his eyes.
2 Samuel 15:27 And the king said to Saddok the priest, See, you return to the city in peace, and Achimaas your son and Jonathan son of Abiathar, your two sons, with you;
2 Samuel 15:28 see, I will be encamped in the plains of the wilderness until a word comes from you to tell me.
2 Samuel 15:29 And Saddok and Abiathar returned the ark to Jerusalem and sat there.
2 Samuel 15:30 And David went up the ascent of the olives, going up and weeping, his head covered, and he went barefoot, and all the people with him, each man covered his head, and they went up, going up and weeping. –
2 Samuel 15:31 And it was reported to David, saying, Achitophel too is among those conspiring with Abessalom; and David said, Scatter now Achitophel's counsel, Lord my God.
2 Samuel 15:32 And David was coming as far as Roos, where he worshiped God, and behold, Chousi the Archite, David's companion, came to meet him with his tunic torn and earth on his head.
2 Samuel 15:33 And David said to him, If you cross with me, you will be a burden to me;
2 Samuel 15:34 but if you return to the city, you shall say to Abessalom, Your brothers have passed through, and the king, your father, passed through behind me, and now I am your servant, king, let me live; I was your father's servant then and just now, and now I am your servant; and you will scatter Achitophel's counsel for me.
2 Samuel 15:35 And behold, Saddok and Abiathar the priests are there with you, and every word that you hear from the king's house you shall report to Saddok and Abiathar the priests;
2 Samuel 15:36 behold, there with them are their two sons, Achimaas son of Saddok and Jonathan son of Abiathar, and by their hand you shall send me every word that you hear.
2 Samuel 15:37 And Chousi, David's companion, entered the city, and Abessalom was entering Jerusalem. –

## Chapter 16

2 Samuel 16:1 And David passed a little way from Roos, and behold, Siba, Memphibosthe's servant, met him with a pair of saddled donkeys, and on them two hundred loaves and a hundred clusters of raisins and a hundred dates and a skin of wine.
2 Samuel 16:2 And the king said to Siba, What are these for you? And Siba said, The beasts of burden are for the king's household to ride, and the loaves and dates for the young men to eat, and the wine for those who are faint in the wilderness to drink.
2 Samuel 16:3 And the king said, And where is your lord's son? And Siba said to the king, Behold, he sits in Jerusalem, because he said, Today the house of Israel will restore to me my father's kingdom.
2 Samuel 16:4 And the king said to Siba, Behold, all that belongs to Memphibosthe is yours. And Siba bowed and said, May I find favor in your eyes, my lord king. –
2 Samuel 16:5 And King David came as far as Baourim; and behold, a man came out from there, from the kinship of Saul's house, and his name was Semei son of Gera; he came out going and cursing
2 Samuel 16:6 and stoning David and all the servants of King David with stones, and all the people and all the mighty men were on the king's right and left.
2 Samuel 16:7 And thus Semei said as he cursed him, Go out, go out, man of blood and lawless man;
2 Samuel 16:8 the Lord has returned upon you all the blood of Saul's house, because you reigned in his place, and the Lord has given the kingdom into the hand of Abessalom your son; and behold, you are in your evil, because you are a man of blood.
2 Samuel 16:9 And Abessa son of Sarouia said to the king, Why does this dead dog curse my lord the king? Let me cross over now and take off his head.
2 Samuel 16:10 And the king said, What is it to me and to you, sons of Sarouia? Leave him, and let him curse thus, because the Lord said to him to curse David, and who shall say, Why have you done thus?
2 Samuel 16:11 And David said to Abessa and to all his servants, Behold, my son who came from my belly seeks my life, and still more now the son of the Jeminite; leave him to curse, because the Lord said it to him;
2 Samuel 16:12 perhaps the Lord will look on my humiliation and return good to me instead of his curse on this day.
2 Samuel 16:13 And David and his men went on the road, and Semei went beside the mountain next to him, going and cursing and stoning with stones at his side and sprinkling with dust.
2 Samuel 16:14 And the king and all his people came exhausted and refreshed themselves there.
2 Samuel 16:15 And Abessalom and every man of Israel entered Jerusalem, and Achitophel with him.
2 Samuel 16:16 And it happened when Chousi the Archite, David's companion, came to Abessalom that Chousi said to Abessalom, Long live the king.
2 Samuel 16:17 And Abessalom said to Chousi, Is this your mercy to your companion? Why did you not depart with your companion?
2 Samuel 16:18 And Chousi said to Abessalom, No, but I shall be with the one whom the Lord and this people and every man of Israel chose, and sit with him;
2 Samuel 16:19 and secondly, whom shall I serve? Is it not before his son? As I served before your father, so I shall be before you.
2 Samuel 16:20 And Abessalom said to Achitophel, Bring counsel among yourselves about what we shall do.
2 Samuel 16:21 And Achitophel said to Abessalom, Go in to your father's concubines whom he left to guard his house, and all Israel will hear that you have shamed your father, and the hands of all those with you will be strengthened.
2 Samuel 16:22 And they pitched a tent for Abessalom on the roof, and Abessalom went in to his father's concubines before the eyes of all Israel.
2 Samuel 16:23 And Achitophel's counsel, which he counseled in the former days, was as though one inquired by a word of God; so was all Achitophel's counsel both to David and to Abessalom. –

## Chapter 17

2 Samuel 17:1 And Achitophel said to Abessalom, Let me choose twelve thousand men for myself now, and I will rise and pursue after David by night;
2 Samuel 17:2 and I will come upon him while he is weary and weak in his hands, and I will terrify him, and all the people with him will flee, and I will strike the king alone;
2 Samuel 17:3 and I will turn all the people back to you in the way the bride returns to her husband; you seek only the life of one man, and there shall be peace for all the people.
2 Samuel 17:4 And the word was right in the eyes of Abessalom and all the elders of Israel.
2 Samuel 17:5 And Abessalom said, Call Chousi the Arachite too, and let us hear what is in his mouth also.
2 Samuel 17:6 And Chousi entered to Abessalom; and Abessalom said to him, saying, According to this word Achitophel spoke; shall we do according to his word? If not, speak yourself.
2 Samuel 17:7 And Chousi said to Abessalom, This counsel that Achitophel counseled is not good this time.
2 Samuel 17:8 And Chousi said, You know your father and his men, that they are very mighty and bitter in their soul like a bear bereft of young in the field and like a rough pig in the plain, and your father is a warrior and will certainly not lodge with the people;
2 Samuel 17:9 for behold, he is now hidden in one of the hills or in one of the places, and it shall be when he falls upon them at the start and one hearing hears and says, There has been a breaking among the people following Abessalom,
2 Samuel 17:10 then even a son of strength whose heart is like a lion's heart will surely melt, because all Israel knows that your father is mighty and the sons of strength are with him.
2 Samuel 17:11 For thus I counsel: Let all Israel surely gather to you from Dan to Bersabee as numerous as the sand on the sea, and let your face go in their midst,
2 Samuel 17:12 and we shall come to him in one of the places where we find him there and encamp against him as the dew falls upon the land, and we shall leave neither him nor any one of the men with him;
2 Samuel 17:13 and if he is gathered into a city, all Israel will take ropes to that city, and we shall drag it to the torrent bed so that not even a stone is left there.
2 Samuel 17:14 And Abessalom and every man of Israel said, The counsel of Chousi the Arachite is better than Achitophel's counsel; and the Lord commanded that Achitophel's good counsel be scattered, so that the Lord might bring all the evils upon Abessalom. –
2 Samuel 17:15 And Chousi the Arachite said to Saddok and Abiathar the priests, Thus and thus Achitophel counseled Abessalom and the elders of Israel, and thus and thus I counseled;
2 Samuel 17:16 and now send quickly and tell David, saying, Do not spend the night in the plains of the wilderness, but hurry to cross over, lest he swallow up the king and all the people with him.
2 Samuel 17:17 And Jonathan and Achimaas stood by the spring of Rogel, and the young woman went and told them, and they go and tell King David, because they could not be seen entering the city.
2 Samuel 17:18 And a young man saw them and told Abessalom, and the two went quickly and entered a man's house in Baourim, and he had a cistern in the courtyard, and they went down there.
2 Samuel 17:19 And the woman took and spread the covering over the mouth of the cistern and spread araphoth upon it, and nothing was known.
2 Samuel 17:20 And Abessalom's servants came to the woman at the house and said, Where are Achimaas and Jonathan? And the woman said to them, They passed a little beyond the water; and they sought and did not find them and returned to Jerusalem.
2 Samuel 17:21 And it happened after they departed that the two came up from the cistern and went and told King David and said to David, Rise and cross the water quickly, because Achitophel counseled thus concerning you.
2 Samuel 17:22 And David and all the people with him rose and crossed the Jordan by the light of morning; not one escaped notice who had not crossed the Jordan.
2 Samuel 17:23 And Achitophel saw that his counsel had not been followed, and saddled his donkey and rose and departed to his house in his city; and he commanded his house and hanged himself and died and was buried in his father's tomb.
2 Samuel 17:24 And David passed into Manaim, and Abessalom crossed the Jordan, he and every man of Israel with him.
2 Samuel 17:25 And Abessalom appointed Amessai over the army instead of Joab; and Amessai was the son of a man whose name was Jothor the Israelite, who went in to Abigaia daughter of Naas, sister of Sarouia, Joab's mother.
2 Samuel 17:26 And all Israel and Abessalom encamped in the land of Galaad.
2 Samuel 17:27 And it happened when David came to Manaim that Ouesbi son of Naas from Rabbath of the sons of Ammon and Machir son of Amiel from Lodabar and Berzelli the Galaadite from Rogellim
2 Samuel 17:28 brought ten beds and rugs and ten cauldrons and earthen vessels and wheat and barley and flour and meal and beans and lentils
2 Samuel 17:29 and honey and butter and sheep and sapphoth of cattle, and brought them for David and the people with him to eat, because they said, The people are hungry and weary and thirsty in the wilderness.

## Chapter 18

2 Samuel 18:1 And David mustered the people with him and appointed over them commanders of thousands and commanders of hundreds,
2 Samuel 18:2 and David sent the people, a third in Joab's hand and a third in the hand of Abessa son of Sarouia, Joab's brother, and a third in the hand of Etthi the Gethite. And David said to the people, I too shall surely go out with you.
2 Samuel 18:3 And they said, You shall not go out, because if we flee, they will not set their heart upon us, and if half of us die, they will not set their heart upon us, because you are like ten thousand of us; and now it is good for you to be in the city as help to help us.
2 Samuel 18:4 And the king said to them, Whatever is pleasing in your eyes I will do. And the king stood beside the gate, and all the people went out by hundreds and by thousands.
2 Samuel 18:5 And the king commanded Joab and Abessa and Etthi, saying, Spare the young man Abessalom for me; and all the people heard the king commanding all the rulers concerning Abessalom.
2 Samuel 18:6 And all the people went out into the forest opposite Israel, and the battle took place in the forest of Ephraim.
2 Samuel 18:7 And Israel's people stumbled there before David's servants, and the breaking on that day was great, twenty thousand men.
2 Samuel 18:8 And the battle there was scattered over the face of all the land, and the forest exceeded in devouring among the people those whom the sword devoured among the people on that day.
2 Samuel 18:9 And Abessalom met before David's servants, and Abessalom was mounted on his mule, and the mule entered under the thicket of the great oak, and his head was caught in the oak, and he hung between heaven and earth, and the mule beneath him passed on.
2 Samuel 18:10 And one man saw and reported to Joab and said, Behold, I have seen Abessalom hanging in the oak.
2 Samuel 18:11 And Joab said to the man reporting, And behold, you saw; why did you not strike him to the ground? And I would have given you ten pieces of silver and one belt.
2 Samuel 18:12 But the man said to Joab, Even if I stand upon my hands a thousand shekels of silver, I shall certainly not lay my hand upon the king's son, because in our ears the king commanded you and Abessa and Etthi, saying, Guard for me the young man Abessalom,
2 Samuel 18:13 so as not to do wrong to his life; and no matter will be hidden from the king, and you would stand opposite.
2 Samuel 18:14 And Joab said, I will begin this; I shall not remain thus before you. And Joab took three darts in his hand and fixed them in Abessalom's heart while he was still alive in the heart of the oak,
2 Samuel 18:15 and ten young men carrying Joab's equipment surrounded and struck Abessalom and put him to death.
2 Samuel 18:16 And Joab sounded the horn, and the people turned back from pursuing Israel, because Joab spared the people.
2 Samuel 18:17 And he took Abessalom and threw him into a great chasm in the forest, into the great pit, and set up over him a very great heap of stones. And all Israel fled, each man to his dwelling.
2 Samuel 18:18 And Abessalom while still alive had set up a pillar for himself, at which he was taken, and he erected it to take the pillar in the king's valley, because he said, He has no son to make his name remembered; and he called the pillar Hand of Abessalom until this day.
2 Samuel 18:19 And Achimaas son of Saddok said, Let me run now and announce good news to the king that the Lord has judged for him from the hand of his enemies.
2 Samuel 18:20 And Joab said to him, You are not a man of good news on this day, and you shall announce good news on another day, but on this day you shall not, because the king's son has died.
2 Samuel 18:21 And Joab said to Chousi, Go and tell the king what you saw; and Chousi bowed to Joab and went out.
2 Samuel 18:22 And Achimaas son of Saddok continued and said to Joab, And let it be that I too run after Chousi. And Joab said, Why do you run thus, my son? Come, there is no good news for your benefit in going.
2 Samuel 18:23 And he said, For what if I run? And Joab said to him, Run. And Achimaas ran by the road of Kechar and passed Chousi. –
2 Samuel 18:24 And David sat between the two gates. And the watchman went to the roof of the gate by the wall and raised his eyes and saw, and behold, a man running alone before him,
2 Samuel 18:25 and the watchman cried out and told the king. And the king said, If he is alone, there is good news in his mouth. And he went on coming closer.
2 Samuel 18:26 And the watchman saw another man running, and the watchman cried out at the gate and said, Behold, another man running alone. And the king said, This one too brings good news.
2 Samuel 18:27 And the watchman said, I see the running of the first like the running of Achimaas son of Saddok. And the king said, This is a good man, and he will come with good news.
2 Samuel 18:28 And Achimaas cried out and said to the king, Peace; and bowed to the king on his face to the ground; and said, Blessed be the Lord your God, who shut in the men who hated their hand against my lord the king.
2 Samuel 18:29 And the king said, Is there peace for the young man Abessalom? And Achimaas said, I saw a great crowd when Joab sent the king's servant and your servant, and I did not know what was there.
2 Samuel 18:30 And the king said, Turn aside, stand here; and he turned aside and stood.
2 Samuel 18:31 And behold, Chousi arrived and said to the king, Let good news be announced to my lord the king, because the Lord has judged for you today from the hand of all those rising against you.
2 Samuel 18:32 And the king said to Chousi, Is there peace for the young man Abessalom? And Chousi said, May the enemies of my lord the king and all those who rose against him for evil be like the young man.

## Chapter 19

2 Samuel 19:1 And the king was troubled and went up to the upper room of the gate and wept; and thus he said as he went, My son Abessalom, my son, my son Abessalom, who would give my death instead of you, I instead of you? Abessalom, my son, my son.
2 Samuel 19:2 And it was reported to Joab, saying, Behold, the king weeps and mourns over Abessalom.
2 Samuel 19:3 And the salvation on that day became mourning for all the people, because the people heard on that day, saying, The king grieves over his son.
2 Samuel 19:4 And the people stole into the city on that day, as people steal in when ashamed as they flee in battle.
2 Samuel 19:5 And the king covered his face, and the king cried with a great voice, saying, My son Abessalom, Abessalom my son.
2 Samuel 19:6 And Joab came to the king into the house and said, Today you have shamed the faces of all your servants who delivered you today, and the lives of your sons and your daughters, and the lives of your wives and your concubines,
2 Samuel 19:7 by loving those who hate you and hating those who love you; and today you have declared that your rulers and servants are nothing, for I have known today that if Abessalom were alive and all of us dead today, then it would have been right in your eyes.
2 Samuel 19:8 And now arise, go out, and speak to the heart of your servants, for I have sworn by the Lord that if you do not go out today, if a man will lodge with you this night; and know for yourself that this will be worse for you than all the evil that has come upon you from your youth until now.
2 Samuel 19:9 And the king arose and sat in the gate, and all the people were told, saying, Behold, the king sits in the gate; and all the people came before the king. And Israel fled, each man to his tent.
2 Samuel 19:10 And all the people were disputing among all the tribes of Israel, saying, King David rescued us from all our enemies, and he delivered us from the hand of the foreigners, and now he has fled from the land and from his kingdom because of Abessalom.
2 Samuel 19:11 And Abessalom, whom we anointed over us, died in the battle; and now why are you silent about bringing back the king? And the word of all Israel came to the king.
2 Samuel 19:12 And King David sent to Sadok and Abiathar the priests, saying, Speak to the elders of Judah, saying, Why are you the last to bring the king back to his house? And the word of all Israel came to the king.
2 Samuel 19:13 You are my brothers, my bones and my flesh you are; and why are you the last to bring the king back to his house?
2 Samuel 19:14 And to Amessai you shall say, Are you not my bone and my flesh? And now may God do thus to me and thus add, if you are not commander of the force before me all the days instead of Joab.
2 Samuel 19:15 And he inclined the heart of every man of Judah as one man, and they sent to the king, saying, Return, you and all your servants.
2 Samuel 19:16 And the king returned and came as far as the Jordan, and the men of Judah came to Galgala to go to meet the king, to bring the king across the Jordan.
2 Samuel 19:17 And Semei son of Gera, son of the Jemeni, from Baurim, hastened and went down with the man of Judah to meet King David,
2 Samuel 19:18 and a thousand men with him from Benjamin, and Siba, the servant of the house of Saul, and his fifteen sons with him and his twenty servants with him; and they made their way to the Jordan ahead of the king
2 Samuel 19:19 and performed the service of bringing the king across, and the crossing crossed over to move the king's household and to do what was right in his eyes. And Semei son of Gera fell on his face before the king as he crossed the Jordan
