2 Samuel 19:20 and said to the king, Let my lord not reckon lawlessness, and do not remember how your servant did wrong on the day when my lord the king went out from Jerusalem, so that the king should lay it to his heart,
2 Samuel 19:21 because your servant knows that I sinned, and behold, I came today first of all the house of Joseph to go down to meet my lord the king.
2 Samuel 19:22 And Abessa son of Sarouia answered and said, Shall Semei not be put to death for this, because he cursed the Lord's anointed?
2 Samuel 19:23 And David said, What is there between me and you, sons of Sarouia, that you become an adversary to me today? Shall any man of Israel be put to death today? For do I not know that today I reign over Israel?
2 Samuel 19:24 And the king said to Semei, You shall certainly not die; and the king swore to him.
2 Samuel 19:25 And Memphibosthe son of Jonathan son of Saul went down to meet the king; and he had not cared for his feet, nor trimmed his nails, nor tended his mustache, nor washed his garments from the day the king departed until the day he arrived in peace.
2 Samuel 19:26 And it happened when he came into Jerusalem to meet the king that the king said to him, Why did you not go with me, Memphibosthe?
2 Samuel 19:27 And Memphibosthe said to him, My lord king, my servant deceived me, for your servant said to him, Saddle the donkey for me and I will mount it and go with the king, for your servant is lame.
2 Samuel 19:28 And he schemed against your servant before my lord the king; and my lord the king is like an angel of God, so do what is good in your eyes.
2 Samuel 19:29 For all my father's house was nothing but men of death to my lord the king, and you placed your servant among those eating at your table; and what right have I still, even to cry out any more to the king?
2 Samuel 19:30 And the king said to him, Why do you still speak your words? I said, You and Siba shall divide the field.
2 Samuel 19:31 And Memphibosthe said to the king, Let him indeed take everything, now that my lord the king has come in peace to his house.
2 Samuel 19:32 And Berzelli the Galaadite came down from Rogellim and crossed the Jordan with the king to send him across the Jordan.
2 Samuel 19:33 And Berzelli was a very old man, a son of eighty years, and he had sustained the king while he lived in Manaim, for he was a very great man.
2 Samuel 19:34 And the king said to Berzelli, You shall cross with me, and I will sustain your old age with me in Jerusalem.
2 Samuel 19:35 And Berzelli said to the king, How many are the days of the years of my life, that I should go up with the king to Jerusalem?
2 Samuel 19:36 A son of eighty years am I today; shall I discern between good and evil? Or will your servant still taste what I eat or drink? Or will I still hear the voice of men and women singing? Why should your servant still be a burden upon my lord the king?
2 Samuel 19:37 Your servant will cross the Jordan with the king for a little while; and why should the king repay me this recompense?
2 Samuel 19:38 Let your servant stay, and I shall die in my city by the tomb of my father and my mother; and behold, your servant Chamaam shall cross with my lord the king, and do for him what is good in your eyes.
2 Samuel 19:39 And the king said, Let Chamaam cross with me, and I will do for him what is good in your eyes, and all that you choose for me I will do for you.
2 Samuel 19:40 And all the people crossed the Jordan, and the king crossed; and the king kissed Berzelli and blessed him, and he returned to his place.
2 Samuel 19:41 And the king crossed to Galgala, and Chamaam crossed with him, and all the people of Judah crossed with the king, and indeed half the people of Israel.
2 Samuel 19:42 And behold, every man of Israel came to the king and said to the king, Why have our brothers, the men of Judah, stolen you away and brought the king and his household across the Jordan, and all David's men with him?
2 Samuel 19:43 And every man of Judah answered the man of Israel and said, Because the king is close to me; and why are you so angry over this matter? Have we eaten food from the king, or has he given a gift, or has he taken a levy for us?
2 Samuel 19:44 And the man of Israel answered the man of Judah and said, I have ten shares in the king, and I am firstborn rather than you, and indeed I am above you in David; and why have you insulted me in this, and was my word not reckoned first for me to bring back the king for me? And the word of the man of Judah was harsher than the word of the man of Israel.

## Chapter 20

2 Samuel 20:1 And there was a lawless son there, one called Sabee son of Bochori, a man, the Jemeni; and he sounded the horn and said, We have no share in David, nor have we an inheritance in the son of Jessai. Each man to your tents, Israel.
2 Samuel 20:2 And every man of Israel went up from following David after Sabee son of Bochori; and the man of Judah clung to their king from the Jordan as far as Jerusalem.
2 Samuel 20:3 And David entered his house in Jerusalem, and the king took the ten women, his concubines whom he had left to guard the house, and placed them in a house of custody and sustained them, but did not go in to them; and they were confined until the day of their death, living widows.
2 Samuel 20:4 And the king said to Amessai, Call together the man of Judah for me in three days, and you stand here.
2 Samuel 20:5 And Amessai went to call together Judah and delayed beyond the time David had appointed for him.
2 Samuel 20:6 And David said to Abessa, Now Sabee son of Bochori will do us more harm than Abessalom; and now take your lord's servants with you and pursue after him, lest he find fortified cities for himself and overshadow our eyes.
2 Samuel 20:7 And the men of Joab went out after him, and the Chereththi and the Pheleththi and all the mighty men; and they went out from Jerusalem to pursue after Sabee son of Bochori.
2 Samuel 20:8 And they were by the great stone that is in Gabaon, and Amessai came before them. And Joab was girded with his cloak, his garment, and over it he was girded with a sword fastened at his waist in its sheath; and the sword came out and fell.
2 Samuel 20:9 And Joab said to Amessai, Are you well, brother? And Joab's right hand took hold of Amessai's beard to kiss him.
2 Samuel 20:10 And Amessai did not guard against the sword in Joab's hand, and Joab struck him with it in the flank, and his belly spilled onto the ground; and he did not strike him a second time, and he died. And Joab and Abessa his brother pursued after Sabee son of Bochori.
2 Samuel 20:11 And one man of Joab's young servants stood by him and said, Whoever desires Joab and whoever is for David, after Joab!
2 Samuel 20:12 And Amessai lay smeared in blood in the middle of the road, and the man saw that all the people stood still; and he turned Amessai out of the road into a field and threw a garment over him, because he saw everyone coming upon him stop.
2 Samuel 20:13 And when he was removed from the road, every man of Israel passed on after Joab to pursue after Sabee son of Bochori.
2 Samuel 20:14 And he passed through all the tribes of Israel to Abel and to Baithmacha and all in Charri; and they assembled and came after him.
2 Samuel 20:15 And they arrived and besieged him in Abel and Baithmacha, and poured a siege mound against the city, and it stood at the outer wall; and all the people with Joab were thinking of throwing down the wall.
2 Samuel 20:16 And a wise woman cried out from the wall and said, Hear, hear! Say now to Joab, Come near here and I will speak to him.
2 Samuel 20:17 And he came near to her, and the woman said, Are you Joab? And he said, I am. And she said to him, Hear the words of your servant. And Joab said, I am listening.
2 Samuel 20:18 And she said, saying, They spoke a word at the first, saying, They were surely asked in Abel and in Dan whether the things that the faithful of Israel had established had ceased; those asking shall surely ask in Abel, and thus whether they had ceased.
2 Samuel 20:19 I am peaceable among the supports of Israel, but you seek to put to death a city and a mother-city in Israel; why do you sink the Lord's inheritance?
2 Samuel 20:20 And Joab answered and said, Far be it from me, far be it from me, that I should sink or destroy it.
2 Samuel 20:21 That is not the matter, for a man from the hill country of Ephraim, Sabee son of Bochori is his name, has raised his hand against King David. Give me him alone, and I will depart from above the city. And the woman said to Joab, Behold, his head will be thrown to you through the wall.
2 Samuel 20:22 And the woman went in to all the people and spoke to the whole city in her wisdom; and she removed the head of Sabee son of Bochori and threw it to Joab. And he sounded the horn, and they scattered from the city, each man to his tent; and Joab returned to Jerusalem to the king.
2 Samuel 20:23 And Joab was over all the force of Israel, and Banaias son of Jodae over the Chereththi and over the Pheleththi,
2 Samuel 20:24 and Adoniram over the tribute, and Josaphat son of Achilouth as recorder,
2 Samuel 20:25 and Sousa as scribe, and Sadok and Abiathar as priests,
2 Samuel 20:26 and indeed Iras the Jarin was David's priest.

## Chapter 21

2 Samuel 21:1 And there was a famine in David's days for three years, one year following another, and David sought the face of the Lord. And the Lord said, Upon Saul and upon his house is wrongdoing, because of his death of bloods, for which he put the Gabaonites to death.
2 Samuel 21:2 And King David called the Gabaonites and spoke to them; now the Gabaonites are not sons of Israel but rather from the remnant of the Amorite, and the sons of Israel had sworn to them; and Saul sought to strike them in his zeal for the sons of Israel and Judah.
2 Samuel 21:3 And David said to the Gabaonites, What shall I do for you, and by what shall I make atonement, so that you may bless the Lord's inheritance?
2 Samuel 21:4 And the Gabaonites said to him, We have no silver or gold with Saul and with his house, and we have no man to put to death in Israel. And he said, What do you say, and I shall do it for you?
2 Samuel 21:5 And they said to the king, The man made an end of us and pursued us, he who schemed to destroy us; let us make him disappear so that he may not stand in any border of Israel.
2 Samuel 21:6 Let seven men of his sons be given to us, and let us expose them to the sun for the Lord in Gabaon, Saul's chosen ones of the Lord. And the king said, I will give them.
2 Samuel 21:7 And the king spared Memphibosthe son of Jonathan son of Saul because of the oath of the Lord between them, between David and Jonathan son of Saul.
2 Samuel 21:8 And the king took the two sons of Respha daughter of Aia, whom she bore to Saul, Ermoni and Memphibosthe, and the five sons of Michol daughter of Saul, whom she bore to Esriel son of Berzelli the Moulathite,
2 Samuel 21:9 and gave them into the hand of the Gabaonites, and they exposed them to the sun on the mountain before the Lord, and these seven fell together; and they were put to death in the days of harvest, at the first, at the beginning of the barley harvest.
2 Samuel 21:10 And Respha daughter of Aia took sackcloth and fixed it for herself upon the rock at the beginning of the barley harvest, until water dripped upon them from heaven; and she did not allow the birds of heaven to rest upon them by day or the beasts of the field by night.
2 Samuel 21:11 And it was reported to David what Respha daughter of Aia, Saul's concubine, had done, and they were loosened, and Dan son of Joa of the descendants of the giants overtook them.
2 Samuel 21:12 And David went and took the bones of Saul and the bones of Jonathan his son from the men, the sons of Jabis Galaad, who had stolen them from the square of Baithsan, because the foreigners had set them there on the day the foreigners struck Saul in Gelboue.
2 Samuel 21:13 And he brought up from there the bones of Saul and the bones of Jonathan his son, and gathered the bones of those exposed to the sun.
2 Samuel 21:14 And they buried the bones of Saul and the bones of Jonathan his son and of those exposed to the sun in the land of Benjamin, in the side, in the tomb of Kis his father, and they did all that the king commanded. And God listened to the land after these things.
2 Samuel 21:15 And there was again war for the foreigners with Israel. And David and his servants with him went down and fought with the foreigners, and David grew faint.
2 Samuel 21:16 And Jesbi, who was among the offspring of Rapha, and the weight of his spear was three hundred shekels in bronze weight, and he was girded with a club, and he intended to strike David.
2 Samuel 21:17 And Abessa son of Sarouia helped him and struck the foreigner and put him to death. Then David's men swore, saying, You shall no longer go out with us to war, and you shall certainly not extinguish the lamp of Israel.
2 Samuel 21:18 And after these things there was again war in Geth with the foreigners. Then Sebocha the Astatothite struck Seph, who was among the offspring of Rapha.
2 Samuel 21:19 And there was war in Gob with the foreigners. And Eleanan son of Ariorgim the Bethlehemite struck Goliath the Gethite, and the shaft of his spear was like a weavers' beam.
2 Samuel 21:20 And there was again war in Geth. And there was a man of great size, and the fingers of his hands and the toes of his feet were six and six, twenty-four in number; and he too was born to Rapha.
2 Samuel 21:21 And he reproached Israel, and Jonathan son of Semei, David's brother, struck him.
2 Samuel 21:22 These four were born as descendants of the giants in Geth to the house of Rapha, and they fell by the hand of David and by the hand of his servants.

## Chapter 22

2 Samuel 22:1 And David spoke to the Lord the words of this song on the day when the Lord delivered him from the hand of all his enemies and from the hand of Saul,
2 Samuel 22:2 and he said, Lord, my rock and my fortress and my deliverer for me,
2 Samuel 22:3 my God will be my guard; I will trust in him, my defender and the horn of my salvation, my helper and the refuge of my salvation; from the unjust you will save me.
2 Samuel 22:4 I will call upon the Lord, who is praised, and I shall be saved from my enemies.
2 Samuel 22:5 For the crushings of death encompassed me; torrents of lawlessness astonished me.
2 Samuel 22:6 The pangs of death encircled me; the harshnesses of death came before me.
2 Samuel 22:7 In my affliction I will call upon the Lord, and to my God I will cry out; and he will hear my voice from his temple, and my cry will be in his ears.
2 Samuel 22:8 And the earth was troubled and shaken, and the foundations of heaven were troubled together and torn apart, because the Lord was angry with them.
2 Samuel 22:9 Smoke went up in his anger, and fire from his mouth devours; coals were kindled from him.
2 Samuel 22:10 And he bent the heavens and came down, and darkness was beneath his feet.
2 Samuel 22:11 And he sat upon cherubim and flew, and was seen upon the wings of the wind.
2 Samuel 22:12 And he made darkness his hiding place around him, his tent darkness of waters; he thickened it in the clouds of the air.
2 Samuel 22:13 From the brightness before him coals of fire were kindled.
2 Samuel 22:14 The Lord thundered from heaven, and the Most High gave his voice,
2 Samuel 22:15 and sent arrows and scattered them, lightning and dismayed them.
2 Samuel 22:16 And the outlets of the sea appeared, and the foundations of the inhabited world were uncovered at the rebuke of the Lord, at the breath of the spirit of his anger.
2 Samuel 22:17 He sent from on high and took me; he drew me out of many waters.
2 Samuel 22:18 He delivered me from my strong enemies, from those who hate me, because they were stronger than I.
2 Samuel 22:19 They came before me in the day of my affliction, and the Lord became my support
2 Samuel 22:20 and brought me out into a broad place and delivered me, because he took pleasure in me.
2 Samuel 22:21 And the Lord repaid me according to my righteousness; according to the cleanness of my hands he repaid me,
2 Samuel 22:22 because I kept the ways of the Lord and did not act impiously away from my God,
2 Samuel 22:23 because all his judgments are before me, and his ordinances, I did not depart from them.
2 Samuel 22:24 And I will be blameless toward him and guard against my lawlessness.
2 Samuel 22:25 And the Lord will repay me according to my righteousness and according to the cleanness of my hands before his eyes.
2 Samuel 22:26 With the holy you will be holy, and with the perfect man you will be perfect,
2 Samuel 22:27 and with the chosen you will be chosen, and with the crooked you will be crooked.
2 Samuel 22:28 And you will save the poor people, and you will humble eyes upon the exalted.
2 Samuel 22:29 For you are my lamp, Lord, and the Lord will shine upon my darkness for me.
2 Samuel 22:30 For in you I will run as one lightly girded, and in my God I will leap over a wall.
2 Samuel 22:31 The strong one, his way is blameless; the word of the Lord is strong, refined by fire; he is a defender of all those who trust in him.
2 Samuel 22:32 Who is strong besides the Lord? And who will be creator besides our God?
2 Samuel 22:33 The strong one who strengthens me with power, and he shook out my way blameless;
2 Samuel 22:34 setting my feet like those of deer and setting me upon the heights;
2 Samuel 22:35 teaching my hands for war and breaking a bronze bow with my arm.
2 Samuel 22:36 And you gave me the defense of my salvation, and your obedience made me great
2 Samuel 22:37 into a broad place for my steps beneath me, and my legs were not shaken.
2 Samuel 22:38 I will pursue my enemies and make them vanish, and I will not turn back until I finish them;
2 Samuel 22:39 and I will crush them, and they will not rise, and they will fall beneath my feet.
2 Samuel 22:40 And you will strengthen me with power for war; you will bend those who rise against me beneath me.
2 Samuel 22:41 And you gave me my enemies' back, those who hate me, and you put them to death.
2 Samuel 22:42 They will cry out, and there is no helper; to the Lord, and he did not hear them.
2 Samuel 22:43 And I ground them like dust of the earth; like mud of the roads I made them fine.
2 Samuel 22:44 And you will deliver me from the strife of peoples; you will keep me as head of nations; a people whom I did not know served me.
2 Samuel 22:45 Foreign sons lied to me; at the hearing of the ear they listened to me.
2 Samuel 22:46 Foreign sons will be cast away and will stumble out of their enclosures.
2 Samuel 22:47 The Lord lives, and blessed is my guard, and exalted shall be my God, the guard of my salvation.
2 Samuel 22:48 The Lord is strong, the one giving me acts of vengeance, disciplining peoples beneath me
2 Samuel 22:49 and bringing me out from my enemies; and from those rising against me you will exalt me; from a man of wrongdoings you will deliver me.
2 Samuel 22:50 Therefore I will confess you, Lord, among the nations, and to your name I will sing,
2 Samuel 22:51 magnifying the salvations of his king and doing mercy to his anointed, to David and to his seed forever.

## Chapter 23

2 Samuel 23:1 And these are the last words of David: Faithful David son of Jessai, and a faithful man whom the Lord raised up as an anointed of the God of Jacob, and the beautiful psalms of Israel.
2 Samuel 23:2 The spirit of the Lord spoke in me, and his word was upon my tongue.
2 Samuel 23:3 The God of Israel says, the guard of Israel spoke to me: Speak a parable: In a man how will you strengthen fear of God?
2 Samuel 23:4 And in God, with morning light the sun is to rise; the morning did not pass from brightness, and as from rain, grass from the earth.
2 Samuel 23:5 For is not my house thus with the strong one? For he made an everlasting covenant for me, ready at every time, guarded, because all my salvation and every desire, for the lawless one shall certainly not sprout.
2 Samuel 23:6 Like a thorn driven away are all of them, for they shall not be taken by hand,
2 Samuel 23:7 and a man shall not toil among them, and a fullness of iron and a spear's shaft; and in fire by burning they shall be burned in their shame.
2 Samuel 23:8 These are the names of David's mighty men: Jebosthe the Chananite is commander of the third, Adinon the Asonite. This one drew his sword against eight hundred wounded at once.
2 Samuel 23:9 And after him Eleazar son of his father's brother, son of Sousitos, among the three mighty men. This one was with David in Serran; and when he reproached him among the foreigners, they gathered there for war, and the man of Israel went up.
2 Samuel 23:10 He arose and struck among the foreigners until his hand grew weary and his hand clung to the sword, and the Lord made a great salvation on that day; and the people sat behind him except to strip the spoil.
2 Samuel 23:11 And after him Samaia son of Asa the Arouchite. And the foreigners gathered at Theria, and there was a portion of the field full of lentils, and the people fled from before the foreigners.
2 Samuel 23:12 And he stood firmly in the middle of the portion and delivered it and struck the foreigners, and the Lord made a great salvation.
2 Samuel 23:13 And three of the thirty went down and came to Kason to David in the cave of Odollam, and a contingent of the foreigners encamped in the valley of Raphaim.
2 Samuel 23:14 And David was then in the stronghold, and the garrison of the foreigners was then in Bethlehem.
2 Samuel 23:15 And David desired and said, Who will give me water to drink from the pit in Bethlehem at the gate? And the assembly of the foreigners was then in Bethlehem.
2 Samuel 23:16 And the three mighty men broke through the camp of the foreigners and drew water from the pit in Bethlehem at the gate and took it and came to David, and he did not wish to drink it and poured it out to the Lord
2 Samuel 23:17 and said, Far be it from me, Lord, to do this; shall I drink the blood of the men who went at the risk of their lives? And he did not wish to drink it. These things the three mighty men did.
2 Samuel 23:18 And Abessa brother of Joab son of Sarouia, he was a commander among the three; and he raised his spear against three hundred wounded, and he had a name among the three.
2 Samuel 23:19 He was renowned among those three and became their commander, but he did not come up to the three.
2 Samuel 23:20 And Banaias son of Jodae, himself a man of many deeds from Kabeseel. He struck the two sons of Ariel of Moab; and he went down and struck the lion in the middle of the pit on the day of snow.
2 Samuel 23:21 He struck the Egyptian man, a conspicuous man, and in the Egyptian's hand was a spear like the wood of a ladder, and he went down to him with a staff and snatched the spear from the Egyptian's hand and killed him with his own spear.
2 Samuel 23:22 These things Banaias son of Jodae did, and he had a name among the three mighty men.
2 Samuel 23:23 He was renowned among the three, but did not come up to the three; and David appointed him to his hearings.
2 Samuel 23:24 And these are the names of the mighty men of King David: Asael brother of Joab [this one was among the thirty], Eleanan son of Doudi, his father's brother, in Bethlehem,
2 Samuel 23:25 Samai the Aroudaite, Elika the Arodaite,
2 Samuel 23:26 Elles the Phelothite, Iras son of Ekkas the Thekoite,
2 Samuel 23:27 Abiezer the Anathothite from the sons of the Asothite,
2 Samuel 23:28 Selmon the Aoite, Moore the Netophathite,
2 Samuel 23:29 Ela son of Baana the Netophathite, Eththi son of Riba from Gabaeth, son of Benjamin,
2 Samuel 23:30 Banaias the Pharathonite, Ouri from Nachaligaias,
2 Samuel 23:31 Abiel son of the Arabothite, Azmoth the Barsamite,
2 Samuel 23:32 Eliasou the Salabonite, sons of Jasan, Jonathan,
2 Samuel 23:33 Samma the Arodite, Achian son of Sarad the Araourite,
2 Samuel 23:34 Aliphaleth son of the Asbite son of the Maachathite, Eliab son of Achitophel the Gelonite,
2 Samuel 23:35 Asarai the Carmelite, Pharai the Erchite,
2 Samuel 23:36 Igaal son of Nathan from the force, son of Gaddi,
2 Samuel 23:37 Elie the Ammanite, Gelorai the Berothaite, bearer of the equipment of Joab son of Sarouia,
2 Samuel 23:38 Iras the Jethiraite, Gareb the Jethiraite,
2 Samuel 23:39 Ourias the Chettite, all thirty-seven.

## Chapter 24

2 Samuel 24:1 And the anger of the Lord continued to burn in Israel, and he stirred David against them, saying, Go, count Israel and Judah.
2 Samuel 24:2 And the king said to Joab, the commander of the force who was with him, Go now through all the tribes of Israel from Dan as far as Bersabee and inspect the people, and I shall know the number of the people.
2 Samuel 24:3 And Joab said to the king, May the Lord your God add to the people, as they are and as they are, a hundredfold, with the eyes of my lord the king seeing; and why does my lord the king desire this matter?
2 Samuel 24:4 And the king's word prevailed over Joab and over the commanders of the force. And Joab and the commanders of the force went out from before the king to inspect the people of Israel.
2 Samuel 24:5 And they crossed the Jordan and encamped in Aroer, to the right of the city that is in the middle of the ravine of Gad and Eliezer,
2 Samuel 24:6 and came to Galaad and to the land of Thabason, which is Adasai, and arrived at Danidan and Oudan and went around to Sidon,
2 Samuel 24:7 and came to Mapsar of Tyre and all the cities of the Evaite and the Chananite and came south of Judah to Bersabee,
2 Samuel 24:8 and traveled around all the land and arrived in Jerusalem at the end of nine months and twenty days.
2 Samuel 24:9 And Joab gave the number of the inspection of the people to the king, and Israel amounted to eight hundred thousand men of force drawing the sword, and the man of Judah to five hundred thousand fighting men.
2 Samuel 24:10 And David's heart struck him after counting the people, and David said to the Lord, I have sinned greatly in what I have done; now, Lord, pass over the lawlessness of your servant, for I have acted very foolishly.
2 Samuel 24:11 And David rose in the morning. And the word of the Lord came to Gad the prophet, David's seer, saying,
2 Samuel 24:12 Go and speak to David, saying, Thus says the Lord: I am bringing three things upon you; choose for yourself one of them, and I shall do it to you.
2 Samuel 24:13 And Gad came to David and reported to him and said to him, Choose for yourself what shall happen: whether three years of famine shall come upon you in your land, or you shall flee three months before your enemies and they shall pursue you, or three days of death shall occur in your land. Now then know and see what word I shall answer to the one who sent me.
2 Samuel 24:14 And David said to Gad, It is very narrow for me on every side; let me fall into the hand of the Lord, for his mercies are very many, but into the hands of man I shall certainly not fall. And David chose death for himself.
2 Samuel 24:15 And it was the days of wheat harvest, and the Lord gave death in Israel from morning until the hour of the meal, and the breaking began among the people, and seventy thousand men of the people died from Dan as far as Bersabee.
2 Samuel 24:16 And the angel of God stretched out his hand toward Jerusalem to destroy it, and the Lord was moved concerning the evil and said to the angel who was destroying among the people, Enough now; relax your hand. And the angel of the Lord was by the threshing floor of Orna the Jebusite.
2 Samuel 24:17 And David spoke to the Lord when he saw the angel striking among the people and said, Behold, it is I who have done wrong, and I, the shepherd, have done evil; but these sheep, what have they done? Let your hand be upon me and upon my father's house.
2 Samuel 24:18 And Gad came to David on that day and said to him, Go up and set up an altar to the Lord on the threshing floor of Orna the Jebusite.
2 Samuel 24:19 And David went up according to Gad's word, in the manner the Lord commanded him.
2 Samuel 24:20 And Orna looked out and saw the king and his servants passing above him, and Orna went out and bowed before the king with his face to the ground.
2 Samuel 24:21 And Orna said, Why has my lord the king come to his servant? And David said, To acquire from you the threshing floor to build an altar to the Lord, so that the breaking upon the people may be held back.
2 Samuel 24:22 And Orna said to David, Let my lord the king take and offer to the Lord what is good in his eyes; behold, the oxen for a whole burnt offering, and the wheels and the equipment of the oxen for wood.
2 Samuel 24:23 Orna gave everything to the king, and Orna said to the king, May the Lord your God bless you.
2 Samuel 24:24 And the king said to Orna, No, but I shall certainly acquire it from you in exchange, and I shall not offer to the Lord my God a whole burnt offering for nothing. And David acquired the threshing floor and the oxen for fifty shekels of silver.
2 Samuel 24:25 And David built an altar there to the Lord and offered whole burnt offerings and peace offerings; and Solomon added to the altar later, for it was small at first. And the Lord listened to the land, and the breaking was held back from over Israel.

# 1 Kings

## Chapter 1

1 Kings 1:1 And King David was old, advanced in days, and they covered him with garments, but he was not warmed.
1 Kings 1:2 And his servants said, Let them seek a young virgin for our lord the king, and she shall stand before the king and warm him and lie with him, and our lord the king shall be warmed.
1 Kings 1:3 And they sought a beautiful young woman from every border of Israel and found Abisak the Somanite and brought her to the king.
1 Kings 1:4 And the young woman was very beautiful; and she warmed the king and ministered to him, but the king did not know her.
1 Kings 1:5 And Adonias son of Aggith exalted himself, saying, I shall reign; and he made himself chariots and horsemen and fifty men to run before him.
1 Kings 1:6 And his father had never restrained him, saying, Why have you done this? And indeed he was very handsome in appearance, and she bore him after Abessalom.
1 Kings 1:7 And his words were with Joab son of Sarouia and with Abiathar the priest, and they helped, following Adonias.
1 Kings 1:8 But Sadok the priest and Banaias son of Jodae and Nathan the prophet and Semei and Rei and David's mighty men were not following Adonias.
1 Kings 1:9 And Adonias sacrificed sheep and calves and lambs by the stone of Zoelet, which was next to the spring of Rogel, and called all his brothers and all the prominent men of Judah, servants of the king.
1 Kings 1:10 But Nathan the prophet and Banaias and the mighty men and Solomon his brother he did not call.
1 Kings 1:11 And Nathan said to Bersabee, Solomon's mother, saying, Have you not heard that Adonias son of Aggith has become king? And our lord David did not know.
1 Kings 1:12 And now come, let me advise you with counsel, and you shall deliver your life and the life of your son Solomon.
1 Kings 1:13 Come, go in to King David and say to him, Did you not, my lord king, swear to your servant, saying, Solomon your son shall reign after me, and he shall sit on my throne? Why then has Adonias become king?
1 Kings 1:14 And behold, while you are still speaking there with the king, I shall come in after you and complete your words.
1 Kings 1:15 And Bersabee went in to the king in the chamber, and the king was very old, and Abisak the Somanite was ministering to the king.
1 Kings 1:16 And Bersabee bowed and prostrated herself before the king. And the king said, What is it for you?
1 Kings 1:17 And she said, My lord king, you swore by the Lord your God to your servant, saying, Solomon your son shall reign after me, and he shall sit on my throne.
1 Kings 1:18 And now behold, Adonias has become king, and you, my lord king, did not know.
1 Kings 1:19 And he sacrificed calves and lambs and sheep in abundance and called all the king's sons and Abiathar the priest and Joab the commander of the force, but Solomon your servant he did not call.
1 Kings 1:20 And you, my lord king, the eyes of all Israel are toward you to tell them who shall sit upon the throne of my lord the king after him.
1 Kings 1:21 And it shall be, when my lord the king lies down with his fathers, that I and my son Solomon shall be sinners.
1 Kings 1:22 And behold, while she was still speaking with the king, Nathan the prophet came.
1 Kings 1:23 And it was reported to the king, Behold, Nathan the prophet. And he came before the king and prostrated himself before the king with his face to the ground.
1 Kings 1:24 And Nathan said, My lord king, did you say, Adonias shall reign after me, and he shall sit upon my throne?
1 Kings 1:25 For he went down today and sacrificed calves and lambs and sheep in abundance and called all the king's sons and the commanders of the force and Abiathar the priest, and behold, they are eating and drinking before him and have said, Long live King Adonias.
1 Kings 1:26 But me, your servant, and Sadok the priest and Banaias son of Jodae and Solomon your servant he did not call.
1 Kings 1:27 Has this matter come about through my lord the king, and have you not made known to your servant who shall sit upon the throne of my lord the king after him?
1 Kings 1:28 And David answered and said, Call Bersabee for me. And she came before the king and stood before him.
1 Kings 1:29 And the king swore and said, As the Lord lives, who redeemed my life from every affliction,
1 Kings 1:30 as I swore to you by the Lord God of Israel, saying, Solomon your son shall reign after me, and he shall sit upon my throne instead of me, so I shall do this day.
1 Kings 1:31 And Bersabee bowed with her face to the ground and prostrated herself before the king and said, May my lord King David live forever.
1 Kings 1:32 And King David said, Call Sadok the priest and Nathan the prophet and Banaias son of Jodae for me. And they came before the king.
1 Kings 1:33 And the king said to them, Take your lord's servants with you and put my son Solomon upon my mule and bring him down to Gion.
1 Kings 1:34 And let Sadok the priest and Nathan the prophet anoint him there as king over Israel, and sound the horn and say, Long live King Solomon.
1 Kings 1:35 And he shall sit upon my throne and he shall reign instead of me, and I have commanded that he be leader over Israel and Judah.
1 Kings 1:36 And Banaias son of Jodae answered the king and said, So be it; thus may the Lord God of my lord the king confirm it.
1 Kings 1:37 As the Lord was with my lord the king, so may he be with Solomon and make his throne greater than the throne of my lord King David.
1 Kings 1:38 And Sadok the priest and Nathan the prophet and Banaias son of Jodae and the Chereththi and the Pheleththi went down and seated Solomon on King David's mule and led him to Gion.
1 Kings 1:39 And Sadok the priest took the horn of oil from the tent and anointed Solomon and sounded the horn, and all the people said, Long live King Solomon.
1 Kings 1:40 And all the people went up after him and danced in dances and rejoiced with great joy, and the earth split with their sound.
1 Kings 1:41 And Adonias and all his invited guests heard, as they finished eating; and Joab heard the sound of the horn and said, What is the sound of the city resounding?
1 Kings 1:42 While he was still speaking, behold, Jonathan son of Abiathar the priest came, and Adonias said, Come in, for you are a man of strength, and bring good news.
1 Kings 1:43 And Jonathan answered and said, Indeed, our lord King David has made Solomon king.
1 Kings 1:44 And the king sent with him Sadok the priest and Nathan the prophet and Banaias son of Jodae and the Chereththi and the Pheleththi, and they seated him on the king's mule.
1 Kings 1:45 And Sadok the priest and Nathan the prophet anointed him as king at Gion, and they went up from there rejoicing, and the city resounded; that is the sound you heard.
1 Kings 1:46 And Solomon sat upon the throne of the kingdom.
1 Kings 1:47 And the king's servants came in to bless our lord King David, saying, May God make the name of Solomon your son better than your name and make his throne greater than your throne. And the king prostrated himself upon his bed.
1 Kings 1:48 And indeed the king said thus, Blessed is the Lord God of Israel, who today gave one of my seed sitting upon my throne, and my eyes see it.
1 Kings 1:49 And all those invited by Adonias were astonished and rose up and went, each man on his way.
1 Kings 1:50 And Adonias feared Solomon's face and arose and went and took hold of the horns of the altar.
1 Kings 1:51 And it was reported to Solomon, saying, Behold, Adonias fears King Solomon and holds the horns of the altar, saying, Let King Solomon swear to me today that he will not put his servant to death by the sword.
1 Kings 1:52 And Solomon said, If he becomes a son of strength, will a hair of his fall to the ground? But if evil is found in him, he shall be put to death.
1 Kings 1:53 And King Solomon sent and brought him down from above the altar; and he came in and prostrated himself before King Solomon, and Solomon said to him, Go to your house.

## Chapter 2

1 Kings 2:1 And the days drew near for David to die, and he commanded Solomon his son, saying,
1 Kings 2:2 I am going in the way of all the earth; be strong and become a man,
1 Kings 2:3 and keep the charge of the Lord your God, to walk in his ways, to keep his commandments and the ordinances and the judgments written in the law of Moses, so that you may understand what you shall do in everything that I command you,
1 Kings 2:4 so that the Lord may establish his word which he spoke, saying, If your sons keep their way to walk before me in truth with all their heart and with all their soul, saying, A man of yours shall not be cut off from upon the throne of Israel.
1 Kings 2:5 And indeed you know what Joab son of Sarouia did to me, what he did to the two commanders of the forces of Israel, to Abenner son of Ner and Amessai son of Jether, and he killed them and placed the bloods of war in peace and put innocent blood upon his belt at his waist and upon his sandal on his foot.
1 Kings 2:6 And you shall act according to your wisdom and shall not bring his gray hair down to Hades in peace.
1 Kings 2:7 And to the sons of Berzelli the Galaadite you shall show mercy, and they shall be among those eating at your table, because so they drew near to me when I fled from before Abessalom your brother.
1 Kings 2:8 And behold, with you is Semei son of Gera son of the Jemeni from Baurim, and he cursed me with a grievous curse on the day when I went to the Camps, and he went down to meet me at the Jordan, and I swore to him by the Lord, saying, If I put you to death by the sword.
1 Kings 2:9 And you shall certainly not hold him innocent, for you are a wise man and shall know what you shall do to him, and you shall bring his gray hair down to Hades in blood.
1 Kings 2:10 And David lay down with his fathers and was buried in the city of David.
1 Kings 2:11 And the days that David reigned over Israel were forty years; in Hebron he reigned seven years and in Jerusalem thirty-three years.
1 Kings 2:12 And Solomon sat upon the throne of David his father, being a son of twelve years, and his kingdom was made very firm.
1 Kings 2:13 And Adonias son of Aggith went in to Bersabee, Solomon's mother, and bowed to her. And she said, Is your coming peaceful? And he said, Peaceful.
1 Kings 2:14 I have a word for you. And she said to him, Speak.
1 Kings 2:15 And he said to her, You know that the kingdom was mine and all Israel set its face toward me as king, but the kingdom turned and became my brother's, because it became his from the Lord.
1 Kings 2:16 And now I ask one request of you; do not turn away your face. And Bersabee said to him, Speak.
1 Kings 2:17 And he said to her, Say now to King Solomon, for he will not turn away his face from you, and he shall give me Abisak the Somanite as wife.
1 Kings 2:18 And Bersabee said, Good; I shall speak about you to the king.
1 Kings 2:19 And Bersabee went in to King Solomon to speak to him about Adonias. And the king rose to meet her and kissed her and sat upon his throne, and a throne was set for the king's mother and she sat at his right.
1 Kings 2:20 And she said to him, I ask one small request of you; do not turn away your face. And the king said to her, Ask, my mother, for I shall not turn you away.
1 Kings 2:21 And she said, Let Abisak the Somanite be given to Adonias your brother as wife.
1 Kings 2:22 And King Solomon answered and said to his mother, And why did you ask for Abisak for Adonias? Ask the kingdom for him too, for he is my older brother, and for him are Abiathar the priest and Joab son of Sarouia, the commander in chief, as a companion.
1 Kings 2:23 And King Solomon swore by the Lord, saying, May God do thus to me and thus add, for against his own life Adonias spoke this word.
1 Kings 2:24 And now, as the Lord lives, who established me and placed me upon the throne of David my father and made me a house, as the Lord spoke, Adonias shall be put to death today.
1 Kings 2:25 And King Solomon sent by the hand of Banaias son of Jodae, and he killed him, and Adonias died on that day.
1 Kings 2:26 And to Abiathar the priest the king said, Go away to Anathoth, to your field, for you are a man of death on this day; but I shall not put you to death, because you carried the ark of the covenant of the Lord before my father, and because you were afflicted in all that my father was afflicted.
1 Kings 2:27 And Solomon drove Abiathar out from being a priest of the Lord, to fulfill the word of the Lord which he spoke against the house of Eli in Selom.
1 Kings 2:28 And the report reached Joab son of Sarouia [for Joab had inclined after Adonias, but after Solomon he had not inclined], and Joab fled to the tent of the Lord and held onto the horns of the altar.
1 Kings 2:29 And it was reported to Solomon, saying, Joab has fled to the tent of the Lord, and behold, he holds the horns of the altar. And Solomon sent to Joab, saying, What has happened to you, that you have fled to the altar? And Joab said, Because I feared your face, and I fled to the Lord. And King Solomon sent Banaias son of Jodae, saying, Go and kill him and bury him.
1 Kings 2:30 And Banaias son of Jodae came to Joab in the tent of the Lord and said to him, Thus says the king: Come out. And Joab said, I shall not go out, for here I shall die. And Banaias son of Jodae returned and told the king, saying, Thus Joab has spoken, and thus he answered me.
1 Kings 2:31 And the king said to him, Go and do to him as he has said, and kill him and bury him, and remove today the blood that Joab shed without cause from me and from my father's house.
1 Kings 2:32 And the Lord has returned the blood of his wrongdoing upon his head, since he met the two men more righteous and better than he and killed them by the sword, and my father David did not know of their blood: Abenner son of Ner, commander in chief of Israel, and Amessa son of Jether, commander in chief of Judah.
1 Kings 2:33 And their blood shall return upon his head and upon the head of his seed forever, but to David and to his seed and to his house and to his throne may there be peace forever from the Lord.
1 Kings 2:34 And Banaias son of Jodae met Joab and put him to death and buried him in his house in the wilderness.
1 Kings 2:35 And the king placed Banaias son of Jodae in his place over the command of the army; and the kingdom was established in Jerusalem; and the king placed Sadok the priest as first priest instead of Abiathar.
1 Kings 2:35 And the Lord gave Solomon understanding and very great wisdom and breadth of heart like the sand beside the sea,
1 Kings 2:36 and Solomon's understanding greatly increased beyond the understanding of all the ancient sons and beyond all the wise men of Egypt.
1 Kings 2:37 And he took Pharaoh's daughter and brought her into the city of David until he completed his house and the house of the Lord at first and the wall of Jerusalem all around; in seven years he made and completed it.
1 Kings 2:36 And Solomon had seventy thousand burden bearers and eighty thousand stonecutters in the mountain.
1 Kings 2:37 And Solomon made the sea and the supports and the great basins and the pillars and the fountain of the courtyard and the bronze sea.
1 Kings 2:38 And he built the citadel and its battlements and cut through the city of David; thus Pharaoh's daughter went up from the city of David to her house, which he built for her; then he built the citadel.
1 Kings 2:39 And Solomon offered whole burnt offerings and peace offerings three times a year upon the altar which he built for the Lord, and burned incense before the Lord. And he completed the house.
1 Kings 2:40 And these are the officers appointed over Solomon's works: three thousand six hundred overseers of the people doing the work.
1 Kings 2:41 And he built Assour and Magdo and Gazer and upper Baithoron and Baalath.
1 Kings 2:35 But after he built the house of the Lord and the wall of Jerusalem around it, after these things he built these cities.
1 Kings 2:36 And while David was still alive he commanded Solomon, saying, Behold, with you is Semei son of Gera, son of the seed of the Jemeni, from Hebron.
1 Kings 2:37 This one cursed me with a grievous curse on the day when I went to the Camps.
1 Kings 2:38 And he came down to meet me at the Jordan, and I swore to him by the Lord, saying, If he shall be put to death by the sword.
1 Kings 2:39 And now do not hold him innocent, for you are a prudent man and shall know what you shall do to him, and you shall bring his gray hair down to Hades in blood.
1 Kings 2:36 And the king called Semei and said to him, Build yourself a house in Jerusalem and dwell there, and you shall not go out from there anywhere.
1 Kings 2:37 And it shall be on the day you go out and cross the brook Kedron, you shall surely know that you shall die by death; your blood shall be upon your head. And the king made him swear on that day.
1 Kings 2:38 And Semei said to the king, The word you have spoken is good, my lord king; thus your servant shall do. And Semei dwelt in Jerusalem three years.
1 Kings 2:39 And after three years two servants of Semei ran away to Anchous son of Maacha, king of Geth, and Semei was told, Behold, your servants are in Geth.
1 Kings 2:40 And Semei arose and saddled his donkey and went to Geth to Anchous to seek his servants, and Semei went and brought his servants from Geth.
1 Kings 2:41 And Solomon was told, saying, Semei went from Jerusalem to Geth and brought back his servants.
1 Kings 2:42 And the king sent and called Semei and said to him, Did I not make you swear by the Lord and testify to you, saying, On whatever day you go out from Jerusalem and go to the right or to the left, you shall surely know that you shall die by death?
1 Kings 2:43 And why did you not keep the oath of the Lord and the commandment that I commanded you?
1 Kings 2:44 And the king said to Semei, You know all your evil which your heart knew, which you did to David my father, and the Lord has repaid your evil upon your head.
1 Kings 2:45 And King Solomon is blessed, and David's throne shall be established before the Lord forever.
1 Kings 2:46 And King Solomon commanded Banaias son of Jodae, and he went out and killed him, and he died.
1 Kings 2:46 And King Solomon was very prudent and wise, and Judah and Israel were very many, like the sand upon the sea in multitude, eating and drinking and rejoicing.
1 Kings 2:47 And Solomon was ruler in all the kingdoms, and they brought gifts and served Solomon all the days of his life.
1 Kings 2:48 And Solomon began to open the dominions of Lebanon,
1 Kings 2:49 and he built Thermai in the wilderness.
1 Kings 2:50 And this was Solomon's meal: thirty kors of fine flour and sixty kors of ground flour, ten choice calves and twenty pasture oxen and a hundred sheep, besides deer and gazelles and choice pastured birds.
1 Kings 2:51 For he was ruler in all beyond the river, from Raphi to Gaza, over all the kings beyond the river.
1 Kings 2:52 And he had peace from all his parts around him, and Judah and Israel dwelt trusting, each under his vine and under his fig tree, eating and drinking, from Dan as far as Bersabee all the days of Solomon.
1 Kings 2:53 And these were Solomon's officers: Azarion son of Sadok the priest, and Orniou son of Nathan commander of the overseers, and Edram over his house, and Souba the scribe, and Basa son of Achithalam the recorder, and Abi son of Joab commander in chief, and Achire son of Edrai over the burdens, and Banaias son of Jodae over the court command and over the brickworks, and Zachour son of Nathan the counselor.
1 Kings 2:54 And Solomon had forty thousand brood mares for chariots and twelve thousand horsemen.

## Chapter 3

1 Kings 3:1 And when the kingdom was established in Solomon's hand, Solomon made a marriage alliance with Pharaoh king of Egypt and took Pharaoh's daughter and brought her into the city of David, until he completed building his own house and the house of the Lord and the wall around Jerusalem.
1 Kings 3:2 But the people were burning incense on the high places, because a house had not yet been built for the name of the Lord.
1 Kings 3:3 And Solomon loved the Lord, walking in the ordinances of David his father, but he sacrificed and burned incense on the high places.
1 Kings 3:4 And he arose and went to Gabaon to sacrifice there, for it was the highest and great; Solomon offered a thousand whole burnt offerings upon the altar in Gabaon.
1 Kings 3:5 And the Lord appeared to Solomon in sleep at night, and the Lord said to Solomon, Ask some request for yourself.
1 Kings 3:6 And Solomon said, You showed great mercy to your servant David my father, as he walked before you in truth and in righteousness and in uprightness of heart with you, and you kept this great mercy for him, to give his son upon his throne, as on this day.
1 Kings 3:7 And now, Lord my God, you placed your servant instead of David my father, and I am a small child and do not know my going out and my coming in.
1 Kings 3:8 And your servant is in the midst of your people whom you chose, a numerous people who shall not be counted.
1 Kings 3:9 And give your servant a heart to hear and to judge your people in righteousness, to understand between good and evil; for who will be able to judge this weighty people of yours?
1 Kings 3:10 And it was pleasing before the Lord that Solomon asked this matter.
1 Kings 3:11 And the Lord said to him, Because you asked this matter of me and did not ask for yourself many days and did not ask for riches or for the lives of your enemies, but asked for yourself understanding to hear judgment,
1 Kings 3:12 behold, I have done according to your word; behold, I have given you a prudent and wise heart, such that one like you has not existed before you and one like you shall not arise after you.
1 Kings 3:13 And what you did not ask, I have given you, both riches and glory, such that no man like you has existed among kings.
1 Kings 3:14 And if you walk in my way to keep my commandments and my ordinances, as David your father walked, then I shall multiply your days.
1 Kings 3:15 And Solomon awoke, and behold, it was a dream; and he arose and came to Jerusalem and stood before the altar before the ark of the Lord's covenant in Sion and offered whole burnt offerings and made peace offerings and made a great feast for himself and all his servants.
1 Kings 3:16 Then two women, prostitutes, appeared before the king and stood before him.
1 Kings 3:17 And the one woman said, With me, lord; I and this woman dwell in one house, and we gave birth in the house.
1 Kings 3:18 And it happened on the third day after I gave birth that this woman also gave birth; and we were together, and there was no one with us besides the two of us in the house.
1 Kings 3:19 And this woman's son died in the night when she lay upon him.
1 Kings 3:20 And she arose in the middle of the night and took my son from my arms and laid him in her bosom, and her dead son she laid in my bosom.
1 Kings 3:21 And I arose in the morning to nurse my son, and he was dead; and behold, I examined him in the morning, and behold, he was not my son whom I bore.
1 Kings 3:22 And the other woman said, No, but my son is the living one, and your son is the dead one. And they spoke before the king.
1 Kings 3:23 And the king said to them, You say, This is my living son, and hers is the dead son; and you say, No, but my son is the living one, and yours is the dead son.
1 Kings 3:24 And the king said, Bring me a sword; and they brought the sword before the king.
1 Kings 3:25 And the king said, Divide the living nursing child in two and give half of him to this one and half of him to this one.
1 Kings 3:26 And the woman whose son was the living one answered and said to the king, because her womb was troubled over her son, and said, With me, lord, give her the child and do not put him to death; and the other said, Let him be neither mine nor hers; divide him.
1 Kings 3:27 And the king answered and said, Give the child to the one who said, Give him to her and do not put him to death; she is his mother.
1 Kings 3:28 And all Israel heard this judgment which the king judged, and they feared before the king, because they saw that God's understanding was in him to do justice.

## Chapter 4

1 Kings 4:1 And King Solomon was reigning over Israel.
1 Kings 4:2 And these were his officers: Azariou son of Sadok,
1 Kings 4:3 and Eliareph and Achia son of Saba, scribes, and Josaphat son of Achilid, recorder,
1 Kings 4:4 and Sadouch and Abiathar, priests,
1 Kings 4:5 and Ornia son of Nathan over the appointees, and Zabouth son of Nathan, companion of the king,
1 Kings 4:6 and Achiel, steward, and Eliab son of Saph over the family, and Adoniram son of Ephra over the tributes.
1 Kings 4:7 And Solomon had twelve appointees over all Israel to provide for the king and his house; one month in the year fell to each one to provide.
1 Kings 4:8 And these are their names: Benor in the hill country of Ephraim, one;
1 Kings 4:9 son of Rechab in Machemas and Bethalamin and Baithsamys and Ailon as far as Baithanan, one;
1 Kings 4:10 son of Esoth in Berbethnema, Lousamencha and Resphara;
1 Kings 4:11 Chinanadab and Anaphathi, husband of Tableth, Solomon's daughter, who was his wife, one;
1 Kings 4:12 Bakcha son of Achilid, Thaanach and Mekedo and all the house of San beside Sesathan below Esrae, and from Baisaphoud Ebelmaola as far as Maeber Loukam, one;
1 Kings 4:13 son of Gaber in Remath Galaad, to him was allotted Eregaba, which is in Basan, sixty great walled cities with bronze bars, one;
1 Kings 4:14 Achinadab son of Achel in Maanain, one;
1 Kings 4:15 Achimaas in Nephthali, and he took Basemmath daughter of Solomon as wife, one;
1 Kings 4:16 Baana son of Chousi in Maalath, one;
1 Kings 4:17 Samaa son of Ela in Benjamin;
1 Kings 4:18 Gaber son of Adai in the land of Gad, the land of Seon king of Esebon and Og king of Basan; and one nasiph in the land of Judah;
1 Kings 4:19 Josaphat son of Phouasoud in Issachar.

## Chapter 5

1 Kings 5:1 And the appointees thus provided for King Solomon and every order for the king's table, each in his month, not departing from the word; and they carried barley and straw for the horses and chariots to the place where the king would be, each according to his assignment.
1 Kings 5:2 And these were Solomon's daily requirements: thirty kors of fine flour and sixty kors of ground flour,
1 Kings 5:3 and ten choice calves and twenty pasture oxen and a hundred sheep, besides deer and gazelles and choice fattened birds.
1 Kings 5:4 For he was ruler beyond the river, and he had peace from all the parts around him.
1 Kings 5:9 And the Lord gave Solomon understanding and very great wisdom and an outpouring of heart like the sand beside the sea,
1 Kings 5:10 and Solomon greatly increased beyond the understanding of all ancient men and beyond all the wise men of Egypt,
1 Kings 5:11 and he became wiser than all men and wiser than Gaithan the Ezraite and Aiman and Chalkal and Darda, sons of Mal.
1 Kings 5:12 And Solomon spoke three thousand parables, and his songs were five thousand.
1 Kings 5:13 And he spoke about trees, from the cedar in Lebanon as far as the hyssop growing through the wall, and he spoke about beasts and about birds and about creeping things and about fish.
1 Kings 5:14 And all the peoples came to hear Solomon's wisdom, and he received gifts from all the kings of the earth who heard his wisdom.
1 Kings 5:14 And Solomon took Pharaoh's daughter for himself as wife and brought her into the city of David until he completed the house of the Lord and his own house and the wall of Jerusalem.
1 Kings 5:15 Then Pharaoh king of Egypt went up and seized Gazer beforehand and burned it and the Chananite living in Mergab, and Pharaoh gave them as a dispatch to his daughter, Solomon's wife, and Solomon built Gazer. And Chiram king of Tyre sent his servants to anoint Solomon instead of David his father, for Chiram loved David all the days.
1 Kings 5:16 And Solomon sent to Chiram, saying,
1 Kings 5:17 You know that David my father was not able to build a house for the name of the Lord my God because of the wars that surrounded him, until the Lord put them under the tracks of his feet.
1 Kings 5:18 And now the Lord my God has given me rest all around; there is no adversary and no evil occurrence.
1 Kings 5:19 And behold, I say I shall build a house for the name of the Lord my God, as the Lord God spoke to David my father, saying, Your son whom I shall place instead of you upon your throne, he shall build the house for my name.
1 Kings 5:20 And now command them to cut wood for me from Lebanon, and behold, my servants will be with your servants; and I shall give you the wages for your service according to everything you say, for you know that there is no one among us who knows how to cut wood like the Sidonians.
1 Kings 5:21 And it happened when Chiram heard Solomon's words that he rejoiced greatly and said, Blessed is God today, who gave David a prudent son over this numerous people.
1 Kings 5:22 And he sent to Solomon, saying, I have heard concerning all that you sent to me; I shall do all your desire concerning cedar and pine wood.
1 Kings 5:23 My servants shall bring it down from Lebanon to the sea, and I shall set it in rafts as far as the place to which you send me, and I shall unload it there, and you shall take it; and you shall do my desire, to give bread to my house.
1 Kings 5:24 And Chiram was giving Solomon cedars and all his desire.
1 Kings 5:25 And Solomon gave Chiram twenty thousand kors of wheat and machir for his house and twenty thousand baths of beaten oil; thus Solomon gave to Chiram each year.
1 Kings 5:26 And the Lord gave Solomon wisdom, as he spoke to him; and there was peace between Chiram and Solomon, and they made a covenant between themselves.
1 Kings 5:27 And the king raised a levy from all Israel, and the levy was thirty thousand men.
1 Kings 5:28 And he sent them to Lebanon, ten thousand in a month, alternating; one month they were in Lebanon and two months in their house; and Adoniram was over the levy.
1 Kings 5:29 And Solomon had seventy thousand burden bearers and eighty thousand stonecutters in the mountain,
1 Kings 5:30 apart from the officers appointed over Solomon's works, three thousand six hundred overseers who did the works.
1 Kings 5:32 And they prepared the stones and the wood for three years.

## Chapter 6

1 Kings 6:1 And it happened in the four hundred and fortieth year of the departure of the sons of Israel from Egypt, in the fourth year, in the second month, while King Solomon reigned over Israel,
1 Kings 6:1 and the king commanded, and they brought large precious stones for the foundation of the house and hewn stones.
1 Kings 6:2 And Solomon's sons and Chiram's sons hewed them and laid them.
1 Kings 6:3 In the fourth year he laid the foundation of the house of the Lord in the month Niso, the second month.
1 Kings 6:4 In the eleventh year, in the month Baal [this is the eighth month], the house was completed according to every word of it and according to all its arrangement.
1 Kings 6:2 And the house which King Solomon built for the Lord was forty cubits in length and twenty cubits in width and twenty-five cubits in height.
1 Kings 6:3 And the aelam before the temple was twenty cubits in length along the width of the house and ten cubits in width before the house. And he built the house and completed it.
1 Kings 6:4 And he made for the house concealed projecting windows.
1 Kings 6:5 And he placed beams around the wall of the house for the temple and for the dabir, and made side chambers around it.
1 Kings 6:6 The lower side chamber was five cubits in width, and the middle six, and the third seven cubits in width; for he made an offset around the house outside it so that they would not take hold of the walls of the house.
1 Kings 6:7 And the house, while it was being built, was built with rough quarried stones, and hammer and axe and every iron tool were not heard in the house while it was being built.
1 Kings 6:8 And the entrance of the lower side chamber was beneath the right shoulder of the house, and there was a winding ascent to the middle and from the middle to the three stories.
1 Kings 6:9 And he built the house and completed it; and he fitted the house with cedar.
1 Kings 6:10 And he built the bindings throughout the house, five cubits in height, and fastened the binding with cedar timbers.
1 Kings 6:15 And he built the walls of the house with cedar timbers from the floor of the house as far as the beams and as far as the walls; he fitted them continuously with wood inside and enclosed the interior of the house with pine sides.
1 Kings 6:16 And he built the twenty cubits at the end of the house, the one side from the floor to the beams, and made it from the dabir into the holy of holies.
1 Kings 6:17 And the temple was forty cubits before
1 Kings 6:19 the dabir in the middle of the house within, to place there the ark of the covenant of the Lord.
1 Kings 6:20 Twenty cubits was its length and twenty cubits its width and twenty cubits its height, and he covered it with enclosed gold. And he made an altar
1 Kings 6:21 before the dabir and covered it with gold.
1 Kings 6:22 And he covered the entire house with gold until all the house was completed.
1 Kings 6:23 And he made two cherubim in the dabir, each ten cubits in measured size.
1 Kings 6:24 And one wing of the one cherub was five cubits and its second wing five cubits, ten cubits from the edge of its wing to the edge of its wing.
1 Kings 6:25 So also for the second cherub; there was one measure and one completion for both.
1 Kings 6:26 And the height of the one cherub was ten cubits, and so was the second cherub.
1 Kings 6:27 And both cherubim were in the middle of the innermost house; and he spread out their wings, and one wing touched the wall and a wing touched the second wall, and their wings in the middle of the house touched wing to wing.
1 Kings 6:28 And he covered the cherubim with gold.
1 Kings 6:29 And all the walls of the house around he inscribed with a stylus, with carved cherubim and palm trees inside and outside.
1 Kings 6:30 And he covered the floor of the house with gold, of the innermost and of the outermost.
1 Kings 6:31 And for the doorway of the dabir he made doors of juniper wood and fivefold doorposts,
1 Kings 6:32 and two doors of pine wood, with carvings upon them, carved cherubim and palm trees and spread-out petals; and he covered them with gold, and the gold came down upon the cherubim and the palm trees.
1 Kings 6:33 And thus he made for the entrance of the temple, doorposts of juniper wood, fourfold porticoes.
1 Kings 6:34 And in both doors there was pine wood; two folds of the one door and their pivots, and two folds of the second door, turning.
1 Kings 6:35 Carved cherubim and palm trees and spread-out petals, covered with gold drawn down upon the relief.
1 Kings 6:36 And he built the inner courtyard, three courses of hewn stones and a course of worked cedar around it.
1 Kings 6:36 And he built a curtain for the courtyard of the aelam of the house before the temple.

## Chapter 7

1 Kings 7:1 And King Solomon sent and took Chiram from Tyre,
1 Kings 7:2 the son of a widowed woman, who was of the tribe of Nephthali, and his father was a Tyrian man, a worker in bronze, and he was filled with skill and understanding and knowledge to make every work in bronze; and he was brought to King Solomon and made all the works.
1 Kings 7:3 And he cast the two pillars for the aelam of the house; eighteen cubits was the height of a pillar, and a circumference of fourteen cubits surrounded it, and the thickness of the pillar was four fingers in its hollows, and so was the second pillar.
1 Kings 7:4 And he made two capitals to place upon the heads of the pillars, cast bronze; the height of the one capital was five cubits, and the height of the second capital was five cubits.
1 Kings 7:5 And he made two nets to cover the capitals of the pillars, a net for the one capital and a net for the second capital.
1 Kings 7:6 And hanging work, two rows of bronze pomegranates netted, hanging work, row upon row; and so he made for the second capital.
1 Kings 7:7 And he set up the pillars of the aelam of the temple; and he set up the one pillar and called its name Jachoum, and he set up the second pillar and called its name Baaz.
1 Kings 7:8 And on the heads of the pillars was lily work along the aelam, four cubits.
1 Kings 7:9 And a beam was upon both pillars, and above the sides was the capital, the beam in its thickness.
1 Kings 7:10 And he made the sea, ten cubits from its lip to its lip, round all around; its height was five cubits, and thirty-three cubits gathered together encircled it.
1 Kings 7:11 And supports beneath its lip surrounded it all around, ten to a cubit all around, to raise the sea.
1 Kings 7:12 And its lip was like the work of the lip of a cup, a lily shoot, and its thickness a handbreadth.
1 Kings 7:13 And twelve oxen were beneath the sea, three facing north and three facing the sea and three facing south and three facing east, and all their hind parts toward the house, and the sea above upon them.
1 Kings 7:14 And he made ten bronze mechonoth; one mechonoth was five cubits long and four cubits wide and six cubits high.
1 Kings 7:15 And this was the work of the mechonoth: they had enclosures, and enclosures between the projecting parts.
1 Kings 7:16 And on their enclosures between the projecting parts were lions and oxen and cherubim, and on the projecting parts likewise; and above and below the lions and oxen were spaces, work of a descent.
1 Kings 7:17 And four bronze wheels belonged to each mechonoth, and the adjoining parts were bronze, and their four parts were shoulders beneath the basins.
1 Kings 7:18 And there were arms among the wheels in the mechonoth, and the height of one wheel was a cubit and a half.
1 Kings 7:19 And the work of the wheels was the work of chariot wheels; their arms and their backs and their workmanship were all cast.
1 Kings 7:20 The four shoulders on the four corners of each mechonoth, its shoulders were from the mechonoth.
1 Kings 7:21 And upon the head of the mechonoth was a round size of half a cubit all around upon the head of the mechonoth, and the beginnings of its arms and its enclosures, and it was opened upon the beginnings of its arms.
1 Kings 7:22 And its enclosures had cherubim and lions and palm trees standing, each adjoining what faced it inside and around.
1 Kings 7:23 According to it he made all ten mechonoth, one arrangement and one measure for all.
1 Kings 7:24 And he made ten bronze chytrokauloi, each one holding forty choes by measure; one chytrokaulos upon each mechonoth for the ten mechonoth.
1 Kings 7:25 And he placed the ten mechonoth, five by the right shoulder of the house and five by the left shoulder of the house; and the sea by the right shoulder of the house toward the east, from the southern side.
1 Kings 7:26 And Chiram made the cauldrons and the heating vessels and the bowls, and Chiram completed all the works he made for King Solomon in the house of the Lord:
1 Kings 7:27 two pillars and the twisted works of the pillars on the heads of the two pillars and two nets to cover both twisted works of the carvings which were upon the pillars,
1 Kings 7:28 four hundred pomegranates for both nets, two rows of pomegranates for one net to cover both twisted works upon both pillars,
1 Kings 7:29 and the ten mechonoth and the ten chytrokauloi upon the mechonoth,
1 Kings 7:30 and the one sea and the twelve oxen beneath the sea,
1 Kings 7:31 and the cauldrons and the heating vessels and the bowls and all the vessels that Chiram made for King Solomon for the house of the Lord; and the forty-eight pillars of the king's house and the house of the Lord. All the king's works that Chiram made were bronze throughout.
1 Kings 7:32 There was no weight for the bronze from which he made all these works because of its great quantity; there was no limit to the weight of the bronze.
1 Kings 7:33 In the region around the Jordan the king cast them in the thickness of the earth between Sokchoth and Sira.
1 Kings 7:34 And King Solomon placed the vessels which he made in the house of the Lord: the golden altar and the golden table upon which were the loaves of the offering,
1 Kings 7:35 and the lampstands, five on the right and five on the left before the dabir, of enclosed gold, and the lamps and the lights and the golden ladles,
1 Kings 7:36 and the entrances and the nails and the bowls and the dishes and the golden incense vessels, enclosed, and the doorways of the doors of the innermost house, the holy of holies, and the doors of the house of the temple, golden.
1 Kings 7:37 And all the work which Solomon made for the house of the Lord was completed, and Solomon brought in the holy things of David his father and all the holy things of Solomon, the silver and the gold and the vessels, and placed them in the treasuries of the house of the Lord.
1 Kings 7:38 And Solomon built his own house in thirteen years.
1 Kings 7:39 And he built the house of the forest of Lebanon; its length was a hundred cubits and its width fifty cubits and its height thirty cubits; and there were three rows of cedar pillars and cedar shoulders for the pillars.
1 Kings 7:40 And he paneled the house above upon the sides of the pillars, and the number of the pillars was forty-five, fifteen to a row.
1 Kings 7:41 And there were three beams and space upon space threefold.
1 Kings 7:42 And all the doorways and spaces were square and beamed, and from doorway to door threefold.
1 Kings 7:43 And the aelam of the pillars was fifty cubits long and thirty wide, joined, an aelam before them, and pillars and thickness before it for the aelamim.
1 Kings 7:44 And the aelam of the thrones, where he would judge there, was an aelam of judgment.
1 Kings 7:45 And there was a house for him in which he would sit, one courtyard extending for them according to this work; and a house for Pharaoh's daughter, whom Solomon took, according to this aelam.
1 Kings 7:46 All these were of precious stones carved to a measured spacing inside, from the foundation as far as the cornices, and outside to the great courtyard,
1 Kings 7:47 which was founded upon great precious stones, ten-cubit stones and eight-cubit stones,
1 Kings 7:48 and above with precious hewn stones according to the measure and with cedars.
1 Kings 7:49 Around the great courtyard were three courses of hewn stones and a course of carved cedar.
1 Kings 7:50 And Solomon completed all his house.

## Chapter 8

1 Kings 8:1 And when Solomon finished building the house of the Lord and his own house after twenty years, then King Solomon assembled all the elders of Israel in Sion to bring up the ark of the covenant of the Lord from the city of David [this is Sion]
1 Kings 8:2 in the month Athanin.
1 Kings 8:3 And the priests lifted the ark
1 Kings 8:4 and the tent of testimony and all the holy vessels that were in the tent of testimony,
1 Kings 8:5 and the king and all Israel before the ark sacrificed sheep and oxen beyond number.
1 Kings 8:6 And the priests brought the ark into its place, into the dabir of the house, into the holy of holies, beneath the wings of the cherubim.
1 Kings 8:7 For the cherubim spread their wings over the place of the ark, and the cherubim covered the ark and its holy things from above,
1 Kings 8:8 and the consecrated things projected, and the heads of the consecrated things could be seen from the holy place before the dabir, but they were not seen outside.
1 Kings 8:9 There was nothing in the ark except two stone tablets, tablets of the covenant, which Moses placed there in Choreb, which the Lord made with the sons of Israel when they went out from the land of Egypt.
1 Kings 8:10 And it happened when the priests went out of the holy place that the cloud filled the house.
1 Kings 8:11 And the priests could not stand to minister because of the cloud, for the glory of the Lord filled the house.
1 Kings 8:14 And the king turned his face and blessed all Israel, and all the assembly of Israel stood.
1 Kings 8:15 And he said, Blessed is the Lord God of Israel today, who spoke by his mouth concerning David my father and by his hands fulfilled it, saying,
1 Kings 8:16 From the day I brought my people Israel out of Egypt I did not choose a city in any one scepter of Israel to build a house for my name to be there; and I chose Jerusalem for my name to be there and chose David to be over my people Israel.
1 Kings 8:17 And it was upon the heart of David my father to build a house for the name of the Lord God of Israel.
1 Kings 8:18 And the Lord said to David my father, Because it came upon your heart to build a house for my name, you did well that it came upon your heart;
1 Kings 8:19 but you shall not build the house, rather your son who comes out of your sides, he shall build the house for my name.
1 Kings 8:20 And the Lord established his word that he spoke, and I arose instead of David my father and sat upon the throne of Israel, as the Lord spoke, and built the house for the name of the Lord God of Israel.
1 Kings 8:21 And I placed there a place for the ark, in which is the covenant of the Lord there, which the Lord made with our fathers when he brought them out from the land of Egypt.
1 Kings 8:22 And Solomon stood before the altar of the Lord in the presence of all the assembly of Israel and spread out his hands toward heaven
1 Kings 8:23 and said, Lord God of Israel, there is no god like you in heaven above and on earth below, keeping covenant and mercy for your servant who walks before you with all his heart,
1 Kings 8:24 which you kept for your servant David my father, and you spoke with your mouth and fulfilled with your hands, as on this day.
1 Kings 8:25 And now, Lord God of Israel, keep for your servant David my father what you spoke to him, saying, A man of yours shall not be taken from before me, sitting on the throne of Israel, if only your children keep their ways to walk before me, as you walked before me.
1 Kings 8:26 And now, Lord God of Israel, let your word to David my father be confirmed.
1 Kings 8:27 For will God truly dwell with men upon the earth? If heaven and the heaven of heaven will not suffice for you, how much less this house which I built for your name?
1 Kings 8:28 And look upon my supplication, Lord God of Israel, to hear the delight with which your servant prays before you to you today,
1 Kings 8:29 that your eyes may be open toward this house day and night, toward the place of which you said, My name shall be there, to hear the prayer which your servant prays toward this place day and night.
1 Kings 8:30 And hear the supplication of your servant and of your people Israel when they pray toward this place; and you shall hear in the place of your dwelling in heaven and act and be merciful.
1 Kings 8:31 Whenever a person sins against his neighbor and a curse is laid upon him to make him swear, and he comes and confesses before your altar in this house,
1 Kings 8:32 then hear from heaven and act and judge your people Israel, to condemn the lawless one by giving his way upon his head and to justify the righteous one by giving to him according to his righteousness.
1 Kings 8:33 When your people Israel stumble before enemies because they sin against you, and they turn back and confess your name and pray and supplicate in this house,
1 Kings 8:34 then hear from heaven and be merciful to the sins of your people Israel and bring them back to the land which you gave to their fathers.
1 Kings 8:35 When heaven is restrained and there is no rain because they sin against you, and they pray toward this place and confess your name and turn back from their sins when you humble them,
1 Kings 8:36 then hear from heaven and be merciful to the sins of your servant and your people Israel, for you shall show them the good way to walk in it, and give rain upon the land which you gave your people as an inheritance.
1 Kings 8:37 If famine occurs, if death occurs, if there is burning, a locust, if rust occurs, and if their enemy afflicts them in one of their cities, any occurrence, any pain,
1 Kings 8:38 any prayer, any supplication, if it occurs to any man, as each knows the touch of his heart and spreads out his hands toward this house,
1 Kings 8:39 then hear from heaven, from your ready dwelling place, and be merciful and act and give to a man according to his ways, as you know his heart, for you alone know the heart of all sons of men,
1 Kings 8:40 so that they may fear you all the days they live upon the land which you gave to our fathers.
1 Kings 8:41 And for the foreigner who is not of your people,
1 Kings 8:42 when they come and pray toward this place,
1 Kings 8:43 then hear from heaven, from your ready dwelling place, and do according to all that the foreigner calls upon you for, so that all the peoples of the earth may know your name and fear you as your people Israel do and know that your name has been called over this house which I built.
1 Kings 8:44 For when your people go out to war against their enemies in the way in which you turn them, and pray in the name of the Lord toward the city which I chose in it and the house which I built for your name,
1 Kings 8:45 then hear from heaven their supplication and their prayer and do justice for them.
1 Kings 8:46 For they will sin against you, for there is no man who will not sin, and you will bring against them and hand them over before enemies, and those taking them captive will carry them captive to a land far or near,
1 Kings 8:47 and they will turn their hearts in the land to which they were taken, and turn back and supplicate you in the land of their exile, saying, We have sinned, acted lawlessly, done wrong,
1 Kings 8:48 and turn back to you with all their heart and all their soul in the land of their enemies to which you brought them, and pray to you toward their land which you gave their fathers, the city which I chose, and the house which I built for your name,
1 Kings 8:49 then hear from heaven, from your ready dwelling place,
1 Kings 8:50 and be merciful to their wrongdoings by which they sinned against you, and to all their transgressions by which they transgressed against you, and give them compassion before those holding them captive, and they shall have compassion on them.
