1 Kings 8:51 For they are your people and your inheritance, whom you brought out from the land of Egypt, from the midst of an iron furnace.
1 Kings 8:52 And let your eyes and your ears be open to the supplication of your servant and to the supplication of your people Israel, to hear them in everything for which they call upon you,
1 Kings 8:53 for you set them apart for yourself as an inheritance from all the peoples of the earth, as you spoke by the hand of your servant Moses when you brought our fathers out from the land of Egypt, Lord, Lord.
1 Kings 8:53 Then Solomon spoke about the house when he finished building it: The Lord made the sun known in heaven; he said to dwell in gloom. Build my house, a splendid house for yourself, to dwell in newness. Is this not written in the book of song?
1 Kings 8:54 And it happened when Solomon finished praying to the Lord all this prayer and supplication, that he arose from before the altar of the Lord, having knelt upon his knees with his hands spread toward heaven.
1 Kings 8:55 And he stood and blessed all the assembly of Israel with a great voice, saying,
1 Kings 8:56 Blessed is the Lord today, who gave rest to his people Israel according to all he spoke; not one word failed of all his good words which he spoke by the hand of Moses his servant.
1 Kings 8:57 May the Lord our God be with us as he was with our fathers; may he neither abandon us nor turn us away,
1 Kings 8:58 to incline our hearts to him, to walk in all his ways and keep all his commandments and his ordinances which he commanded our fathers.
1 Kings 8:59 And may these words with which I made supplication before the Lord our God be near to the Lord our God day and night, to do justice for your servant and justice for your people Israel, each day's matter in its day,
1 Kings 8:60 so that all the peoples of the earth may know that the Lord is God, he is God and there is no other.
1 Kings 8:61 And let our hearts be complete toward the Lord our God and walk holily in his ordinances and keep his commandments, as on this day.
1 Kings 8:62 And the king and all the sons of Israel sacrificed a sacrifice before the Lord.
1 Kings 8:63 And King Solomon sacrificed the sacrifices of peace offerings that he sacrificed to the Lord, twenty-two thousand oxen and one hundred twenty thousand sheep; and the king and all the sons of Israel dedicated the house of the Lord.
1 Kings 8:64 On that day the king consecrated the middle of the courtyard before the house of the Lord, for there he made the whole burnt offering and the sacrifices and the fats of the peace offerings, because the bronze altar before the Lord was too small to bear the whole burnt offering and the sacrifices of the peace offerings.
1 Kings 8:65 And Solomon held the feast on that day, and all Israel with him, a great assembly from the entrance of Emath as far as the river of Egypt, before the Lord our God in the house he built, eating and drinking and rejoicing before the Lord our God for seven days.
1 Kings 8:66 And on the eighth day he sent the people away and blessed them, and each went to his tent rejoicing and with a good heart over the good things which the Lord had done for David his servant and for Israel his people.

## Chapter 9

1 Kings 9:1 And it happened when Solomon finished building the house of the Lord and the king's house and all Solomon's work which he wished to do,
1 Kings 9:2 that the Lord appeared to Solomon a second time, as he had appeared in Gabaon.
1 Kings 9:3 And the Lord said to him, I have heard the voice of your prayer and your supplication which you made before me; I have done for you according to all your prayer, I have consecrated this house which you built, to set my name there forever, and my eyes and my heart shall be there all the days.
1 Kings 9:4 And you, if you walk before me as David your father walked, in holiness of heart and in uprightness and doing according to all I commanded him, and keep my ordinances and my commandments,
1 Kings 9:5 then I shall establish the throne of your kingdom over Israel forever, as I spoke to David your father, saying, A man of yours leading in Israel shall not be taken away.
1 Kings 9:6 But if you and your children turn away from me and do not keep my commandments and my ordinances which Moses gave before you, and go and serve other gods and bow to them,
1 Kings 9:7 then I shall remove Israel from the land which I gave them, and this house which I consecrated for my name I shall cast away from my face, and Israel shall become a disappearance and a byword among all peoples.
1 Kings 9:8 And this high house, everyone passing through it shall be astonished and whistle and say, Why has the Lord done thus to this land and this house?
1 Kings 9:9 And they shall say, Because they abandoned the Lord their God who brought their fathers out of Egypt, out of a house of bondage, and took hold of foreign gods and bowed to them and served them; therefore the Lord brought this evil upon them.
1 Kings 9:9 Then Solomon brought Pharaoh's daughter up from the city of David into his house which he built for himself in those days.
1 Kings 9:10 Twenty years in which Solomon built the two houses, the house of the Lord and the king's house,
1 Kings 9:11 Chiram king of Tyre supported Solomon with cedar wood and pine wood and gold and all his desire. Then the king gave Chiram twenty cities in the land of Galilee.
1 Kings 9:12 And Chiram went out from Tyre and went to Galilee to see the cities Solomon gave him, and they did not please him.
1 Kings 9:13 And he said, What are these cities that you gave me, brother? And he called them Border to this day.
1 Kings 9:14 And Chiram brought Solomon a hundred and twenty talents of gold,
1 Kings 9:26 and a ship for which King Solomon made in Gasiongaber, which is beside Ailath on the shore of the farthest sea in the land of Edom.
1 Kings 9:27 And Chiram sent in the ship of his servants seafaring men who knew how to sail the sea with Solomon's servants.
1 Kings 9:28 And they came to Sophera and took from there a hundred and twenty talents of gold and brought them to King Solomon.

## Chapter 10

1 Kings 10:1 And the queen of Saba heard the name of Solomon and the name of the Lord and came to test him with riddles.
1 Kings 10:2 And she came to Jerusalem with a very heavy force, and camels carrying spices and very much gold and precious stone, and she went in to Solomon and spoke to him all that was in her heart.
1 Kings 10:3 And Solomon told her all her words; there was no word overlooked by the king that he did not tell her.
1 Kings 10:4 And the queen of Saba saw all Solomon's understanding and the house which he built,
1 Kings 10:5 and Solomon's food and the seating of his servants and the standing of his ministers and his clothing and his cupbearers and his whole burnt offering which he offered in the house of the Lord, and she became beside herself.
1 Kings 10:6 And she said to King Solomon, The word I heard in my land about your word and your understanding was true,
1 Kings 10:7 and I did not believe those who spoke to me until I came and my eyes saw; and behold, there is not half as much as they told me, you have added good things to it beyond all the report I heard in my land.
1 Kings 10:8 Blessed are your women, blessed are these servants of yours who stand before you continually and hear all your understanding.
1 Kings 10:9 May the Lord your God be blessed, who took pleasure in you to place you upon the throne of Israel; because the Lord loves Israel to establish it forever, he placed you as king over them to do judgment in righteousness and in their judgments.
1 Kings 10:10 And she gave Solomon a hundred and twenty talents of gold and very many spices and precious stone; spices like those had not yet come in such quantity as the queen of Saba gave King Solomon.
1 Kings 10:11 [And Chiram's ship that carried gold from Souphir brought very much hewn wood and precious stone.
1 Kings 10:12 And the king made the hewn wood into supports for the house of the Lord and the king's house, and harps and lyres for the singers; such hewn wood had not come upon the earth nor been seen anywhere until this day.]
1 Kings 10:13 And King Solomon gave the queen of Saba all she desired, all she asked, besides all that he had given her by the hand of King Solomon; and she turned and went to her land, she and all her servants.
1 Kings 10:14 And the weight of gold that came to Solomon in one year was six hundred and sixty-six talents of gold,
1 Kings 10:15 apart from the levies of the subjects and of the merchants and of all the kings of the region beyond and the satraps of the land.
1 Kings 10:16 And Solomon made three hundred beaten golden spears; three hundred pieces of gold were upon each spear.
1 Kings 10:17 And three hundred beaten golden arms; three minas of gold were in each arm; and he placed them in the house of the forest of Lebanon.
1 Kings 10:18 And the king made a great ivory throne and overlaid it with refined gold.
1 Kings 10:19 There were six steps to the throne, and heads of calves for the throne at its back, and arms on either side at the seat, and two lions standing beside the arms,
1 Kings 10:20 and twelve lions standing upon the six steps on either side; nothing like it existed in any kingdom.
1 Kings 10:21 And all Solomon's drinking vessels were gold and the basins were gold, all the vessels of the house of the forest of Lebanon enclosed with gold; there was no silver, for it was not reckoned in Solomon's days.
1 Kings 10:22 For the king had a ship of Tharsis at sea with Chiram's ships; once in three years a ship came to the king from Tharsis with gold and silver and carved and hewn stones.
1 Kings 10:22 This was the work of the levy which King Solomon raised to build the house of the Lord and the king's house and the wall of Jerusalem and the citadel, to enclose the enclosure of the city of David, and Assour and Magdan and Gazer and upper Baithoron and Jethermath and all the chariot cities and all the horsemen's cities and the work of Solomon which he undertook to build in Jerusalem and in all the land, so as not to begin it.
1 Kings 10:23 All the people remaining of the Chettite and the Amorite and the Pherezite and the Chananite and the Evaite and the Jebusite and the Gergesaite, who were not of the sons of Israel, their children remaining after them in the land, whom the sons of Israel were not able to destroy, Solomon raised them for tribute until this day.
1 Kings 10:24 And Solomon did not assign the sons of Israel to work, for they were the men who were warriors and his servants and commanders of his chariots and his horsemen.
1 Kings 10:23 And Solomon became greater than all the kings of the earth in riches and understanding.
1 Kings 10:24 And all the kings of the earth sought Solomon's face to hear his understanding which the Lord placed in his heart.
1 Kings 10:25 And each brought his gifts, golden vessels and clothing, stacte and spices and horses and mules, year by year.
1 Kings 10:26 And Solomon had four thousand female horses for chariots and twelve thousand horsemen, and he placed them in the chariot cities and with the king in Jerusalem.
1 Kings 10:26 And he was ruler of all the kings from the river to the land of the foreigners and to the borders of Egypt.
1 Kings 10:27 And the king made gold and silver in Jerusalem like stones, and cedars he made as numerous as the sycamores in the plain.
1 Kings 10:28 And the export of Solomon's horses was from Egypt and from Thekoue; the king's merchants acquired them from Thekoue in exchange.
1 Kings 10:29 And the export came up from Egypt, a chariot for a hundred pieces of silver and a horse for fifty pieces of silver; and thus they went out by sea to all the kings of the Chettiim and the kings of Syria.

## Chapter 11

1 Kings 11:1 And King Solomon was a lover of women. And he had seven hundred ruling women and three hundred concubines. And he took foreign women and Pharaoh's daughter, Moabite women, Ammanite women, Syrian and Idumaean women, Chettite and Amorite women,
1 Kings 11:2 from the nations about which the Lord had forbidden the sons of Israel: You shall not go in to them, and they shall not go in to you, lest they turn your hearts after their idols. To these Solomon clung in love.
1 Kings 11:4 And it happened in the time of Solomon's old age that his heart was not complete with the Lord his God as the heart of David his father was, and the foreign women turned his heart after their gods.
1 Kings 11:5 Then Solomon built a high place for Chamos, an idol of Moab, and for their king, an idol of the sons of Ammon,
1 Kings 11:6 and for Astarte, an abomination of the Sidonians.
1 Kings 11:7 And thus he did for all his foreign women, burning incense and sacrificing to their idols.
1 Kings 11:8 And Solomon did evil before the Lord; he did not walk after the Lord as David his father did.
1 Kings 11:9 And the Lord was angry with Solomon because he turned his heart away from the Lord God of Israel who had appeared to him twice
1 Kings 11:10 and had commanded him concerning this matter not at all to go after other gods, and to take care to do what the Lord God commanded him.
1 Kings 11:11 And the Lord said to Solomon, Because these things happened with you and you did not keep my commandments and my ordinances which I commanded you, I shall surely tear your kingdom from your hand and give it to your servant.
1 Kings 11:12 But in your days I shall not do it for the sake of David your father; from the hand of your son I shall take it.
1 Kings 11:13 Yet I shall certainly not take the whole kingdom; I shall give one scepter to your son for the sake of David my servant and Jerusalem, the city which I chose.
1 Kings 11:14 And the Lord raised up a satan for Solomon, Ader the Idumaean, and Esrom son of Eliadae who was in Raemmath under Adrazar king of Souba, his lord; and men gathered to him, and he was leader of a band and seized Damascus beforehand; and they were satans to Israel all the days of Solomon. And Ader the Idumaean was of the royal seed in Idumaea.
1 Kings 11:15 And it happened when David destroyed Edom, when Joab the commander of the army went to bury the wounded, they cut down every male in Idumaea,
1 Kings 11:16 for Joab and all Israel stayed there six months in Idumaea, until he destroyed every male from Idumaea.
1 Kings 11:17 And Ader fled, he and all the Idumaean men among his father's servants with him, and they entered Egypt; and Ader was a small boy.
1 Kings 11:18 And men arose from the city of Madiam and came to Pharan and took men with them and came to Pharaoh king of Egypt; and Ader went in to Pharaoh, and he gave him a house and appointed bread for him.
1 Kings 11:19 And Ader found very great favor before Pharaoh, and he gave him as wife his wife's sister, the sister of the elder Thekemina.
1 Kings 11:20 And Thekemina's sister bore to Ader her son Ganebath, and Thekemina brought him up among Pharaoh's sons, and Ganebath was among Pharaoh's sons.
1 Kings 11:21 And Ader heard in Egypt that David had lain down with his fathers and that Joab the commander of the army had died; and Ader said to Pharaoh, Send me away, and I shall return to my land.
1 Kings 11:22 And Pharaoh said to Ader, In what are you lacking with me? And behold, you seek to depart to your land. And Ader said to him, But you shall surely send me away. And Ader returned to his land.
1 Kings 11:25 This was the evil which Ader did; and he was heavy in spirit in Israel and reigned in the land of Edom.
1 Kings 11:26 And Jeroboam son of Nabat, the Ephrathite from Sarira, son of a widowed woman, a servant of Solomon,
1 Kings 11:27 and this was the matter when he raised hands against King Solomon: he built the citadel and closed the enclosure of the city of David his father.
1 Kings 11:28 And the man Jeroboam was mighty in strength, and Solomon saw that the young man was a man of works, and appointed him over the burdens of the house of Joseph.
1 Kings 11:29 And it happened at that time that Jeroboam went out from Jerusalem, and Achias the Selonite prophet found him on the road and led him aside from the road; and Achias was clothed in a new garment, and both were in the plain.
1 Kings 11:30 And Achia took hold of his new garment upon him and tore it into twelve tears
1 Kings 11:31 and said to Jeroboam, Take ten tears for yourself, for thus says the Lord God of Israel: Behold, I tear the kingdom from the hand of Solomon and shall give you ten scepters,
1 Kings 11:32 and two scepters shall be his for the sake of David my servant and Jerusalem the city which I chose in it from all the tribes of Israel,
1 Kings 11:33 because he abandoned me and acted for Astarte, the abomination of the Sidonians, and for Chamos and the idols of Moab and their king, the abhorrence of the sons of Ammon, and did not walk in my ways to do what is right before me as David his father did.
1 Kings 11:34 And I shall certainly not take the whole kingdom from his hand, because I shall surely stand against him all the days of his life, for the sake of David my servant whom I chose.
1 Kings 11:35 And I shall take the kingdom from the hand of his son and give you the ten scepters,
1 Kings 11:36 but to his son I shall give the two scepters, so that there may be a place for my servant David all the days before me in Jerusalem, the city which I chose for myself to place my name there.
1 Kings 11:37 And I shall take you, and you shall reign over what your soul desires, and you shall be king over Israel.
1 Kings 11:38 And it shall be, if you keep all that I command you and walk in my ways and do what is right before me, taking care to keep my commandments and my ordinances as David my servant did, then I shall be with you and build you a faithful house, as I built for David.
1 Kings 11:40 And Solomon sought to put Jeroboam to death, and he arose and fled to Egypt to Sousakim king of Egypt and was in Egypt until Solomon died.
1 Kings 11:41 And the rest of Solomon's words and all that he did and all his understanding, are they not written in the book of Solomon's words?
1 Kings 11:42 And the days Solomon reigned in Jerusalem were forty years.
1 Kings 11:43 And Solomon lay down with his fathers, and they buried him in the city of David his father. And it happened when Jeroboam son of Nabat heard, while he was still in Egypt, having fled from before Solomon and dwelt in Egypt, he made his way and came to his city in the land of Sarira in the hill country of Ephraim. And King Solomon lay down with his fathers, and Roboam his son reigned instead of him.

## Chapter 12

1 Kings 12:1 And King Roboam went to Sikima, for all Israel came to Sikima to make him king.
1 Kings 12:3 And the people spoke to King Roboam, saying,
1 Kings 12:4 Your father made our yoke heavy; now you lighten the hard service of your father and his heavy yoke which he placed upon us, and we shall serve you.
1 Kings 12:5 And he said to them, Go away for three days and return to me; and they went away.
1 Kings 12:6 And the king gave notice to the elders who had stood before Solomon his father while he was still alive, saying, How do you advise that I answer this people with a word?
1 Kings 12:7 And they spoke to him, saying, If today you become a servant to this people and serve them and speak good words to them, they will be your servants all the days.
1 Kings 12:8 And he abandoned the counsel of the elders which they had given him and consulted the young men who had grown up with him and stood before him.
1 Kings 12:9 And he said to them, What do you advise, and what shall I answer this people who spoke to me, saying, Lighten the yoke that your father placed upon us?
1 Kings 12:10 And the young men who had grown up with him and stood before him spoke to him, saying, Thus you shall speak to this people who spoke to you, saying, Your father made our yoke heavy, and now you lighten it from us; thus you shall speak to them: My little part is thicker than my father's waist.
1 Kings 12:11 And now my father loaded you with a heavy yoke, and I shall add to your yoke; my father disciplined you with whips, but I shall discipline you with scorpions.
1 Kings 12:12 And all Israel came to King Roboam on the third day, as the king had spoken to them, saying, Return to me on the third day.
1 Kings 12:13 And the king answered the people harshly, and Roboam abandoned the counsel of the elders which they had given him.
1 Kings 12:14 And he spoke to them according to the counsel of the young men, saying, My father made your yoke heavy, and I shall add to your yoke; my father disciplined you with whips, and I shall discipline you with scorpions.
1 Kings 12:15 And the king did not listen to the people, for a turning was from the Lord so that he might establish his word which he spoke by the hand of Achia the Selonite concerning Jeroboam son of Nabat.
1 Kings 12:16 And all Israel saw that their king did not listen to them, and the people answered the king, saying, What share have we in David? And we have no inheritance in the son of Jessai. Go away, Israel, to your tents. Now tend your house, David. And Israel went away to its tents.
1 Kings 12:18 And the king sent Adoniram, the one over the tribute, and all Israel stoned him with stones, and he died; and King Roboam managed to go up to flee to Jerusalem.
1 Kings 12:19 And Israel rejected the house of David until this day.
1 Kings 12:20 And it happened when all Israel heard that Jeroboam had returned from Egypt that they sent and called him to the assembly and made him king over Israel; and there was none following the house of David except the scepter of Judah and Benjamin alone.
1 Kings 12:21 And Roboam came into Jerusalem and assembled the congregation of Judah and the scepter of Benjamin, a hundred and twenty thousand young men who made war, to fight against the house of Israel to return the kingdom to Roboam son of Solomon.
1 Kings 12:22 And the word of the Lord came to Samaia the man of God, saying,
1 Kings 12:23 Say to Roboam son of Solomon, king of Judah, and to all the house of Judah and Benjamin and the remainder of the people, saying,
1 Kings 12:24 Thus says the Lord: You shall not go up nor fight with your brothers, the sons of Israel. Let each return to his own house, for this matter has come from me. And they heard the word of the Lord and stopped going, according to the word of the Lord.
1 Kings 12:24 And King Solomon lay down with his fathers and was buried with his fathers in the city of David. And Roboam his son reigned instead of him in Jerusalem, being a son of sixteen years when he began to reign, and he reigned twelve years in Jerusalem, and the name of his mother was Naanan daughter of Anan son of Naas king of the sons of Ammon; and he did evil before the Lord and did not walk in the way of David his father.
1 Kings 12:25 And there was a man from the hill country of Ephraim, a servant of Solomon, and his name was Jeroboam, and his mother's name was Sarira, a prostitute; and Solomon made him a commander of the staff over the burdens of the house of Joseph, and he built Sarira in the hill country of Ephraim for Solomon, and he had chariots of three hundred horses; he built the citadel among the burdens of the house of Ephraim, he closed the city of David, and he was exalting himself toward the kingdom.
1 Kings 12:26 And Solomon sought to put him to death, and he feared and fled to Sousakim king of Egypt and was with him until Solomon died.
1 Kings 12:27 And Jeroboam heard in Egypt that Solomon had died, and spoke into the ears of Sousakim king of Egypt, saying, Send me away and I shall go to my land. And Sousakim said to him, Ask some request and I shall give it to you.
1 Kings 12:28 And Sousakim gave Jeroboam Ano, sister of Thekemina, the elder of his wife, as wife; she was great among the king's daughters and bore Jeroboam his son Abia.
1 Kings 12:29 And Jeroboam said to Sousakim, Indeed send me away, and I shall go. And Jeroboam went out from Egypt and came to the land of Sarira in the hill country of Ephraim; and all the scepter of Ephraim gathered there; and Jeroboam built a palisade there.
1 Kings 12:30 And his young child became sick with a very severe sickness; and Jeroboam went to inquire about the child; and he said to Ano his wife, Arise and go, inquire of God about the child, whether he will live from his sickness.
1 Kings 12:31 And there was a man in Selo, and his name was Achia, and he was a son of sixty years, and the word of the Lord was with him. And Jeroboam said to his wife, Arise and take in your hand for the man of God loaves and small cakes for his children and a cluster of grapes and a jar of honey.
1 Kings 12:32 And the woman arose and took in her hand loaves and two small cakes and a cluster of grapes and a jar of honey for Achia; and the man was old, and his eyes were dim for seeing.
1 Kings 12:24 And she arose from Sarira and went, and it happened as she entered the city toward Achia the Selonite that Achia said to his young servant, Go out now to meet Ano the wife of Jeroboam and say to her, Come in and do not stand still, for thus says the Lord: I shall send harsh things upon you.
1 Kings 12:25 And Ano went in to the man of God, and Achia said to her, Why have you brought me loaves and a cluster of grapes and small cakes and a jar of honey? Thus says the Lord: Behold, you shall depart from me, and when you enter the gate into Sarira your girls shall come out to meet you and say to you, The child has died.
1 Kings 12:26 For thus says the Lord: Behold, I shall destroy of Jeroboam one who urinates against a wall, and the dogs shall eat those of Jeroboam who die in the city, and the birds of heaven shall eat the one who dies in the field. And they shall lament the child, Alas, lord, for a good word concerning the Lord was found in him.
1 Kings 12:27 And the woman went away as she heard, and it happened as she entered Sarira that the child died, and the cry came out to meet her.
1 Kings 12:28 And Jeroboam went to Sikima in the hill country of Ephraim and gathered the tribes of Israel there, and Roboam son of Solomon went up there. And the word of the Lord came to Samaia the Elamite, saying, Take for yourself a new garment that has not gone into water and tear it into twelve tears and give it to Jeroboam and say to him, Thus says the Lord: Take for yourself ten tears to put around yourself. And Jeroboam took them; and Samaia said, Thus says the Lord concerning the ten tribes of Israel.
1 Kings 12:29 And the people said to Roboam son of Solomon, Your father made his yoke heavy upon us and made the food of his table heavy; and now if you lighten it upon us, we shall serve you. And Roboam said to the people, In three more days I shall answer you with a word.
1 Kings 12:30 And Roboam said, Bring the elders in to me, and I shall consult with them about what word I shall answer the people on the third day. And Roboam spoke into their ears as the people had sent to him, and the elders of the people said, Thus the people spoke to you.
1 Kings 12:25 And Roboam scattered their counsel, and it did not please him; and he sent and brought in his companions and spoke the same things to them: And these things the people sent to me, saying. And his companions said, Thus you shall speak to the people, saying, My little part is thicker than my father's waist; my father whipped you with whips, but I shall rule over you with scorpions.
1 Kings 12:26 And the word pleased Roboam, and he answered the people as his companions, the young men, had counseled him.
1 Kings 12:27 And all the people said as one man, each to his neighbor, and all cried out, saying, We have no share in David nor inheritance in the son of Jessai; to your tents, Israel, for this man is neither a ruler nor a leader.
1 Kings 12:28 And all the people scattered from Sikima, and each went to his tent. And Roboam prevailed and went away and mounted his chariot and entered Jerusalem, and all the scepter of Judah and all the scepter of Benjamin went after him.
1 Kings 12:24 And it happened at the turn of the year that Roboam gathered every man of Judah and Benjamin and went up to fight against Jeroboam in Sikima.
1 Kings 12:25 And the word of the Lord came to Samaia the man of God, saying, Say to Roboam king of Judah and to all the house of Judah and Benjamin and to the remnant of the people, saying, Thus says the Lord: You shall not go up nor fight against your brothers, the sons of Israel. Return each to his house, for this matter has come from me.
1 Kings 12:26 And they heard the word of the Lord and refrained from going, according to the word of the Lord.
1 Kings 12:25 And Jeroboam built Sikima in the hill country of Ephraim and lived in it; and he went out from there and built Phanouel.
1 Kings 12:26 And Jeroboam said in his heart, Behold, now the kingdom shall return to the house of David.
1 Kings 12:27 If this people goes up to offer sacrifices in the house of the Lord in Jerusalem, then the heart of the people will turn to the Lord and to their lord, Roboam king of Judah, and they will kill me.
1 Kings 12:28 And the king took counsel and went and made two golden heifers and said to the people, Let it suffice for you to go up to Jerusalem. Behold your gods, Israel, who brought you up from the land of Egypt.
1 Kings 12:29 And he placed one in Bethel and one he placed in Dan.
1 Kings 12:30 And this matter became a sin; and the people went before the one as far as Dan.
1 Kings 12:31 And he made houses on high places and made priests, a certain portion from the people, who were not of the sons of Levi.
1 Kings 12:32 And Jeroboam made a feast in the eighth month on the fifteenth day of the month like the feast in the land of Judah, and went up on the altar which he made in Bethel to sacrifice to the heifers which he made, and stationed in Bethel the priests of the high places which he made.
1 Kings 12:33 And he went up on the altar which he made on the fifteenth day in the eighth month, at the feast which he devised from his heart, and made a feast for the sons of Israel and went up on the altar to burn sacrifice.

## Chapter 13

1 Kings 13:1 And behold, a man of God from Judah came by the word of the Lord to Bethel, and Jeroboam stood at the altar to burn sacrifice.
1 Kings 13:2 And he called out to the altar by the word of the Lord and said, Altar, altar, thus says the Lord: Behold, a son is born to the house of David; his name is Josias, and he shall sacrifice upon you the priests of the high places who burn sacrifice upon you, and shall burn human bones upon you.
1 Kings 13:3 And he gave a sign on that day, saying, This is the word that the Lord spoke, saying, Behold, the altar is torn apart, and the fatness upon it shall be poured out.
1 Kings 13:4 And it happened when King Jeroboam heard the words of the man of God who called out against the altar in Bethel that the king stretched out his hand from the altar, saying, Seize him; and behold, the hand he stretched toward him withered, and he could not draw it back to himself.
1 Kings 13:5 And the altar was torn apart, and the fatness was poured out from the altar according to the sign which the man of God gave by the word of the Lord.
1 Kings 13:6 And King Jeroboam said to the man of God, Entreat the face of the Lord your God, and let my hand return to me. And the man of God entreated the face of the Lord, and he restored the king's hand to him, and it became as before.
1 Kings 13:7 And the king spoke to the man of God, Come in with me to the house and eat a meal, and I shall give you a gift.
1 Kings 13:8 And the man of God said to the king, If you give me half your house, I shall not go in with you nor eat bread nor drink water in this place.
1 Kings 13:9 For thus the Lord commanded me by word, saying, Do not eat bread and do not drink water and do not return by the way in which you went.
1 Kings 13:10 And he went away by another way and did not return by the way in which he came to Bethel.
1 Kings 13:11 And one old prophet dwelt in Bethel, and his sons came and related to him all the deeds that the man of God did that day in Bethel and the words he spoke to the king; and they turned to the face of their father.
1 Kings 13:12 And their father spoke to them, saying, By which way has he gone? And his sons showed him the way by which the man of God who came from Judah went up.
1 Kings 13:13 And he said to his sons, Saddle the donkey for me; and they saddled the donkey for him, and he mounted it.
1 Kings 13:14 And he went after the man of God and found him sitting under an oak and said to him, Are you the man of God who has come from Judah? And he said to him, I am.
1 Kings 13:15 And he said to him, Come with me and eat bread.
1 Kings 13:16 And he said, I shall certainly not be able to return with you, nor shall I eat bread or drink water in this place.
1 Kings 13:17 For thus the Lord has commanded me by word, saying, Do not eat bread there and do not drink water there and do not return by the way in which you went.
1 Kings 13:18 And he said to him, I too am a prophet as you are, and an angel has spoken to me by the word of the Lord, saying, Bring him back with you to your house, and let him eat bread and drink water. And he lied to him.
1 Kings 13:19 And he brought him back, and he ate bread and drank water in his house.
1 Kings 13:20 And it happened while they sat at the table that the word of the Lord came to the prophet who brought him back,
1 Kings 13:21 and he said to the man of God who came from Judah, saying, Thus says the Lord: Because you provoked the word of the Lord and did not keep the commandment which the Lord your God commanded you,
1 Kings 13:22 and you returned and ate bread and drank water in this place of which he spoke to you, saying, Do not eat bread and do not drink water, your body shall certainly not enter the tomb of your fathers.
1 Kings 13:23 And it happened after eating bread and drinking water that he saddled the donkey for him, and he returned.
1 Kings 13:24 And he went away, and a lion found him on the road and put him to death, and his body was cast upon the road, and the donkey stood beside it, and the lion stood beside the body.
1 Kings 13:25 And behold, men passing by saw the corpse cast upon the road, and the lion stood beside the corpse; and they came in and spoke in the city where the old prophet dwelt.
1 Kings 13:26 And the one who had brought him back from the road heard and said, This is the man of God who provoked the word of the Lord.
1 Kings 13:28 And he went and found his body cast upon the road, and the donkey and the lion stood beside the body, and the lion had not eaten the body of the man of God and had not torn the donkey.
1 Kings 13:29 And the prophet lifted the body of the man of God and placed it upon the donkey, and the prophet brought him back to the city to bury him
1 Kings 13:30 in his own tomb; and they lamented him, Alas, brother.
1 Kings 13:31 And it happened after he lamented him that he said to his sons, saying, When I die, bury me in this tomb in which the man of God is buried; place me beside his bones, so that my bones may be preserved with his bones.
1 Kings 13:32 For the word which he spoke by the word of the Lord against the altar in Bethel and against the houses of the high places in Samaria shall surely come to pass.
1 Kings 13:33 And after this word Jeroboam did not turn back from his evil, and he turned and made priests of the high places from a portion of the people; whoever wished, he filled his hand, and he became a priest for the high places.
1 Kings 13:34 And this matter became sin for the house of Jeroboam and ruin and disappearance from the face of the earth. ... 211 21 And Roboam son of Solomon reigned over Judah; Roboam was a son of forty-one years when he began to reign, and he reigned seventeen years in Jerusalem, the city which the Lord chose to place his name there from all the tribes of Israel; and his mother's name was Naama the Ammanite.

## Chapter 14

1 Kings 14:22 And Roboam did evil before the Lord and provoked him to jealousy in all that his fathers did and in their sins with which they sinned.
1 Kings 14:23 And they built for themselves high places and pillars and groves upon every high hill and beneath every shady tree.
1 Kings 14:24 And a bond came about in the land, and they did some of all the abominations of the nations which the Lord removed from before the sons of Israel.
1 Kings 14:25 And it happened in the fifth year of Roboam's reign that Sousakim king of Egypt went up against Jerusalem
1 Kings 14:26 and took all the treasures of the house of the Lord and the treasures of the king's house and the golden spears which David had taken from the hand of the servants of Adraazar king of Souba and brought into Jerusalem; he took everything, the golden arms.
1 Kings 14:27 And King Roboam made bronze arms instead of them. And the leaders of the runners who guarded the entrance of the king's house placed them upon him.
1 Kings 14:28 And it happened when the king entered the house of the Lord that the runners carried them and leaned them in the thee of the runners.
1 Kings 14:29 And the rest of the words of Roboam and all that he did, behold, are these not written in the book of the words of the days for the kings of Judah?
1 Kings 14:30 And there was war between Roboam and Jeroboam all the days.
1 Kings 14:31 And Roboam lay down with his fathers and was buried with his fathers in the city of David, and Abiou his son reigned instead of him.

## Chapter 15

1 Kings 15:1 And in the eighteenth year of the reign of Jeroboam son of Nabat, Abiou son of Roboam reigned over Judah,
1 Kings 15:2 and he reigned six years, and his mother's name was Maacha daughter of Abessalom.
1 Kings 15:3 And he walked in the sins of his father which he did before him, and his heart was not complete with the Lord his God as the heart of David his father was.
1 Kings 15:4 For David's sake the Lord gave him a remnant, to establish his children after him and establish Jerusalem,
1 Kings 15:5 as David did what was right before the Lord and did not turn aside from all that he commanded him all the days of his life.
1 Kings 15:7 And the rest of Abiou's words and all that he did, behold, are these not written in the book of the words of the days for the kings of Judah? And there was war between Abiou and Jeroboam.
1 Kings 15:8 And Abiou lay down with his fathers in the twenty-fourth year of Jeroboam and was buried with his fathers in the city of David, and Asa his son reigned instead of him.
1 Kings 15:9 In the twenty-fourth year of Jeroboam king of Israel, Asa reigned over Judah,
1 Kings 15:10 and he reigned forty-one years in Jerusalem, and his mother's name was Ana daughter of Abessalom.
1 Kings 15:11 And Asa did what was right before the Lord as David his father did.
1 Kings 15:12 And he removed the rites from the land and sent away all the practices that his fathers had made.
1 Kings 15:13 And he removed Ana his mother from being leader, as she had made an assembly in her grove, and Asa cut down her descents and burned them with fire in the brook Kedron.
1 Kings 15:14 But he did not remove the high places; nevertheless Asa's heart was complete with the Lord all his days.
1 Kings 15:15 And he brought in the pillars of his father and his own pillars into the house of the Lord, silver and gold and vessels.
1 Kings 15:16 And there was war between Asa and Baasa king of Israel all the days.
1 Kings 15:17 And Baasa king of Israel went up against Judah and built Rama so that no one might go out or come in for Asa king of Judah.
1 Kings 15:18 And Asa took the silver and gold found in the treasuries of the king's house and gave them into the hands of his servants, and King Asa sent them to the son of Ader son of Taberemman son of Azin king of Syria, who lived in Damascus, saying,
1 Kings 15:19 Make a covenant between me and you and between my father and your father; behold, I have sent you gifts of silver and gold; come, break your covenant with Baasa king of Israel, and he will go up away from me.
1 Kings 15:20 And the son of Ader listened to King Asa and sent the commanders of his forces against the cities of Israel and struck Ain and Dan and Abelmaa and all Chezrath as far as all the land of Nephthali.
1 Kings 15:21 And it happened when Baasa heard that he stopped building Rama and returned to Thersa.
1 Kings 15:22 And King Asa gave notice to all Judah at Ainakim, and they carried away the stones of Rama and its timbers with which Baasa had built, and King Asa built with them all the hill of Benjamin and the watchtower.
1 Kings 15:23 And the rest of Asa's words and all his power which he exercised, behold, are these not written in the book of the words of the days for the kings of Judah? But in the time of his old age he suffered in his feet.
1 Kings 15:24 And Asa lay down and was buried with his fathers in the city of David, and Josaphat his son reigned instead of him.
1 Kings 15:25 And Nadab son of Jeroboam reigned over Israel in the second year of Asa king of Judah and reigned over Israel two years.
1 Kings 15:26 And he did evil before the Lord and walked in his father's way and in his sins with which he caused Israel to sin.
1 Kings 15:27 And Baasa son of Achia besieged him against the house of Belaan and struck him in Gabathon of the foreigners, and Nadab and all Israel had besieged Gabathon.
1 Kings 15:28 And Baasa put him to death in the third year of Asa son of Abiou king of Judah and reigned.
1 Kings 15:29 And it happened when he reigned that he struck the house of Jeroboam and did not leave any breath of Jeroboam until he destroyed him according to the word of the Lord which he spoke by the hand of his servant Achia the Selonite
1 Kings 15:30 concerning the sins of Jeroboam by which he caused Israel to sin and his provocation by which he provoked the Lord God of Israel.
1 Kings 15:31 And the rest of Nadab's words and all that he did, behold, are these not written in the book of the words of the days for the kings of Israel?
1 Kings 15:33 And in the third year of Asa king of Judah, Baasa son of Achia reigned over Israel in Thersa for twenty-four years.
1 Kings 15:34 And he did evil before the Lord and walked in the way of Jeroboam son of Nabat and in his sins by which he caused Israel to sin.

## Chapter 16

1 Kings 16:1 And the word of the Lord came by the hand of Jou son of Anani to Baasa:
1 Kings 16:2 Because I raised you from the earth and made you leader over my people Israel, and you walked in the way of Jeroboam and caused my people Israel to sin, to provoke me with their vanities,
1 Kings 16:3 behold, I raise up after Baasa and after his house, and I shall make your house like the house of Jeroboam son of Nabat.
1 Kings 16:4 The dogs shall eat the one of Baasa who dies in the city, and the birds of heaven shall eat the one of his who dies in the plain.
1 Kings 16:5 And the rest of Baasa's words and all that he did and his acts of power, behold, are these not written in the book of the words of the days of the kings of Israel?
1 Kings 16:6 And Baasa lay down with his fathers and was buried in Thersa, and Ela his son reigned instead of him in the twentieth year of King Asa.
1 Kings 16:7 And by the hand of Jou son of Anani the Lord spoke against Baasa and his house for all the evil which he did before the Lord to provoke him with the works of his hands, to become like the house of Jeroboam, and because he struck him.
1 Kings 16:8 And Ela son of Baasa reigned over Israel two years in Thersa.
1 Kings 16:9 And Zambri, commander of half the cavalry, conspired against him, and he was in Thersa drinking himself drunk in the house of Osa the steward in Thersa.
1 Kings 16:10 And Zambri entered and struck him and put him to death and reigned instead of him.
1 Kings 16:11 And it happened when he reigned, when he sat on his throne, that he struck the whole house of Baasa
1 Kings 16:12 according to the word which the Lord spoke against the house of Baasa to Jou the prophet,
1 Kings 16:13 concerning all the sins of Baasa and Ela his son, by which he caused Israel to sin, to provoke the Lord God of Israel with their vanities.
1 Kings 16:14 And the rest of Ela's words and all that he did, behold, are these not written in the book of the words of the days of the kings of Israel?
1 Kings 16:15 And Zambri reigned seven days in Thersa. And the camp of Israel was against Gabathon of the foreigners,
1 Kings 16:16 and the people in the camp heard them saying, Zambri has conspired and struck the king; and they made Ambri, the commander of the army, king over Israel on that day in the camp.
1 Kings 16:17 And Ambri and all Israel with him went up from Gabathon and besieged Thersa.
1 Kings 16:18 And it happened when Zambri saw that his city had been seized beforehand, he went into a chamber of the king's house and burned the king's house over himself with fire and died
1 Kings 16:19 for his sins which he committed by doing evil before the Lord, walking in the way of Jeroboam son of Nabat and in his sins by which he caused Israel to sin.
1 Kings 16:20 And the rest of Zambri's words and the plots which he plotted, behold, are these not written in the book of the words of the days of the kings of Israel?
1 Kings 16:21 Then the people of Israel divided; half the people followed Thamni son of Gonath to make him king, and half the people followed Ambri.
1 Kings 16:22 The people following Ambri overpowered the people following Thamni son of Gonath, and Thamni and Joram his brother died at that time, and Ambri reigned after Thamni.
1 Kings 16:23 In the thirty-first year of King Asa, Ambri reigned over Israel twelve years. In Thersa he reigned six years.
1 Kings 16:24 And Ambri acquired Mount Semeron from Semer, owner of the mountain, for two talents of silver and built upon the mountain and called the name of the mountain which he built Saemeron after the name of Semer, owner of the mountain.
1 Kings 16:25 And Ambri did evil before the Lord and acted more wickedly than all who were before him.
1 Kings 16:26 And he walked in every way of Jeroboam son of Nabat and in his sins by which he caused Israel to sin, to provoke the Lord God of Israel with their vanities.
1 Kings 16:27 And the rest of Ambri's words and all that he did and his power, behold, are these not written in the book of the words of the days of the kings of Israel?
1 Kings 16:28 And Ambri lay down with his fathers and was buried in Samaria, and Achaab his son reigned instead of him.
1 Kings 16:28 And in the eleventh year of Ambri, Josaphat son of Asa reigned, being thirty-five years old at his accession, and he reigned twenty-five years in Jerusalem, and his mother's name was Gazouba daughter of Selei.
1 Kings 16:29 And he walked in the way of Asa his father and did not turn aside from it, doing what was right before the Lord; but they did not remove the high places, and they sacrificed on the high places and burned incense.
1 Kings 16:30 And what Josaphat arranged, and all the power which he exercised and those whom he fought, behold, are these not written in the book of the words of the days of the kings of Judah?
1 Kings 16:31 And the rest of the entanglements which they had undertaken in the days of Asa his father he removed from the land.
1 Kings 16:32 And there was no king in Syria, a nasib.
1 Kings 16:33 And King Josaphat made a ship for Tharsis to go to Sophir for gold; and it did not go, because the ship was broken in Gasiongaber.
1 Kings 16:34 Then the king of Israel said to Josaphat, I shall send your servants and my young servants in the ship; and Josaphat did not wish it.
1 Kings 16:29 And Josaphat lay down with his fathers and was buried with his fathers in the city of David, and Joram his son reigned instead of him. In the second year of Josaphat, Achaab son of Ambri reigned; he reigned over Israel in Samaria twenty-two years.
1 Kings 16:30 And Achaab did evil before the Lord; he acted more wickedly than all who were before him.
1 Kings 16:31 And it was not enough for him to walk in the sins of Jeroboam son of Nabat, and he took as wife Jezabel daughter of Jethebaal king of the Sidonians and went and served Baal and bowed to him.
1 Kings 16:32 And he set up an altar to Baal in the house of his abhorrent things, which he built in Samaria.
1 Kings 16:33 And Achaab made a grove, and Achaab added provocations to provoke his own soul to be destroyed; he did evil beyond all the kings of Israel who were before him.
1 Kings 16:34 In his days Achiel the Bethelite built Jericho; with Abiron his firstborn he laid its foundation and with Segoub his younger son he set up its doors, according to the word of the Lord which he spoke by the hand of Joshua son of Naue.

## Chapter 17

1 Kings 17:1 And Eliou the prophet, the Thesbite from Thesbon of Galaad, said to Achaab, As the Lord God of the forces, the God of Israel, lives, before whom I stand, if there shall be dew and rain in these years except by the mouth of my word.
1 Kings 17:2 And the word of the Lord came to Eliou:
1 Kings 17:3 Go from here toward the east and hide by the brook Chorrath facing the Jordan.
1 Kings 17:4 And you shall drink water from the brook, and I shall command the ravens to feed you there.
1 Kings 17:5 And Eliou did according to the word of the Lord and dwelt by the brook Chorrath facing the Jordan.
1 Kings 17:6 And the ravens brought him bread in the morning and meat in the evening, and he drank water from the brook.
1 Kings 17:7 And it happened after days that the brook dried up, because there was no rain upon the land.
1 Kings 17:8 And the word of the Lord came to Eliou:
1 Kings 17:9 Arise and go to Sarepta of Sidonia; behold, I have commanded a widowed woman there to feed you.
1 Kings 17:10 And he arose and went to Sarepta to the entrance of the city, and behold, a widowed woman there was gathering wood. And Eliou called after her and said to her, Take a little water for me in a vessel, and I shall drink.
1 Kings 17:11 And she went to take it, and Eliou called after her and said, Take a piece of bread for me in your hand.
1 Kings 17:12 And the woman said, As the Lord your God lives, if I have a cake, but only about a handful of flour in the jar and a little oil in the flask; and behold, I am gathering two little sticks, and I shall go in and make it for myself and my children, and we shall eat and die.
1 Kings 17:13 And Eliou said to her, Take courage, go in and do according to your word; but first make for me a small cake from it and bring it out to me, and afterward you shall make some for yourself and your children.
1 Kings 17:14 For thus says the Lord: The jar of flour shall not fail and the flask of oil shall not diminish until the day the Lord gives rain upon the land.
1 Kings 17:15 And the woman went and did it; and she and he and her children ate.
1 Kings 17:16 And the jar of flour did not fail and the flask of oil did not diminish according to the word of the Lord which he spoke by the hand of Eliou.
1 Kings 17:17 And it happened after these things that the son of the woman, the mistress of the house, became sick, and his sickness was very severe until no breath was left in him.
1 Kings 17:18 And she said to Eliou, What is there between me and you, man of God? Have you come to me to recall my wrongdoings and put my son to death?
1 Kings 17:19 And Eliou said to the woman, Give me your son. And he took him from her bosom and brought him up to the upper room in which he dwelt and laid him on his bed.
1 Kings 17:20 And Eliou cried out and said, Alas for me, Lord, witness of the widow with whom I dwell, you have afflicted her by putting her son to death.
1 Kings 17:21 And he breathed upon the child three times and called upon the Lord and said, Lord my God, let the life of this child return to him.
1 Kings 17:22 And it happened thus, and the child cried out.
1 Kings 17:23 And he brought him down from the upper room into the house and gave him to his mother; and Eliou said, See, your son lives.
1 Kings 17:24 And the woman said to Eliou, Behold, I know that you are a man of God and that the word of the Lord in your mouth is true.

## Chapter 18

1 Kings 18:1 And it happened after many days that the word of the Lord came to Eliou in the third year, saying, Go and appear to Achaab, and I shall give rain upon the face of the earth.
1 Kings 18:2 And Eliou went to appear to Achaab. And the famine was severe in Samaria.
1 Kings 18:3 And Achaab called Abdiou the steward; [and Abdiou greatly feared the Lord,
1 Kings 18:4 and it happened when Jezabel struck the prophets of the Lord that Abdiou took a hundred men, prophets, and hid them fifty each in a cave and fed them with bread and water.]
1 Kings 18:5 And Achaab said to Abdiou, Come, let us go through the land to the springs of water and the brooks, if perhaps we may find grass and preserve horses and mules, and they shall not perish from among the livestock.
1 Kings 18:6 And they divided the way for themselves to traverse it; Achaab went alone by one way, and Abdiou went alone by another way.
1 Kings 18:7 And Abdiou was alone on the road, and Eliou came alone to meet him; and Abdiou hastened and fell on his face and said, Are you himself, my lord Eliou?
1 Kings 18:8 And Eliou said to him, I am. Go, say to your lord, Behold, Eliou.
1 Kings 18:9 And Abdiou said, What have I sinned, that you give your servant into the hand of Achaab to put me to death?
1 Kings 18:10 As the Lord your God lives, if there is a nation or kingdom to which my lord has not sent to seek you; and they said, He is not here; and he burned the kingdom and its territories, because he had not found you.
1 Kings 18:11 And now you say, Go, announce to your lord, Behold, Eliou.
1 Kings 18:12 And it shall be when I depart from you that a spirit of the Lord will lift you to a land I do not know, and I shall go in to tell Achaab, and he will kill me; and your servant has feared the Lord from his youth.
1 Kings 18:13 Was it not reported to my lord what I did when Jezabel killed the prophets of the Lord, that I hid a hundred men of the Lord's prophets, fifty each in a cave, and fed them with bread and water?
1 Kings 18:14 And now you say to me, Go, say to your lord, Behold, Eliou; and he will kill me.
1 Kings 18:15 And Eliou said, As the Lord of the forces lives, before whom I stand, I shall appear to him today.
1 Kings 18:16 And Abdiou went to meet Achaab and reported to him; and Achaab ran out and went to meet Eliou.
1 Kings 18:17 And it happened when Achaab saw Eliou that Achaab said to Eliou, Are you the one who turns Israel astray?
1 Kings 18:18 And Eliou said, I do not turn Israel astray, but rather you and your father's house, because you abandon the Lord your God and you went after the Baalim.
1 Kings 18:19 And now send, gather all Israel to me at Mount Carmel and the four hundred and fifty prophets of shame and the four hundred prophets of the groves who eat at Jezabel's table.
1 Kings 18:20 And Achaab sent to all Israel and gathered all the prophets to Mount Carmel.
1 Kings 18:21 And Eliou brought them near to all and said to them, How long will you limp on both knees? If the Lord is God, go after him; but if Baal himself is, go after him. And the people did not answer a word.
1 Kings 18:22 And Eliou said to the people, I alone remain a prophet of the Lord, and the prophets of Baal are four hundred and fifty men, and the prophets of the grove four hundred.
1 Kings 18:23 Let them give us two oxen, and let them choose one for themselves and cut it up and place it upon the wood, but place no fire; and I shall prepare the other ox and certainly place no fire.
1 Kings 18:24 And call in the name of your gods, and I shall call in the name of the Lord my God; and the god who hears by fire, he is God. And all the people answered and said, The word you have spoken is good.
1 Kings 18:25 And Eliou said to the prophets of shame, Choose the one calf for yourselves and prepare it first, for you are many, and call in the name of your god, but place no fire.
1 Kings 18:26 And they took the calf and prepared it and called in the name of Baal from morning until noon and said, Hear us, Baal, hear us; and there was no voice and no hearing; and they ran around upon the altar which they made.
1 Kings 18:27 And it happened at noon that Eliou the Thesbite mocked them and said, Call with a great voice, for he is a god, for he has idle talk, and perhaps at the same time he is giving an oracle, or perhaps he is asleep and will wake up.
1 Kings 18:28 And they called with a great voice and cut themselves according to their custom with swords and lances until blood poured over them.
1 Kings 18:29 And they prophesied until the evening passed. And it happened at the time for the sacrifice to go up that there was no voice, and Eliou the Thesbite spoke to the prophets of abhorrent things, saying, Move aside now, and I shall prepare my whole burnt offering; and they moved aside and went away.
1 Kings 18:30 And Eliou said to the people, Bring them near to me; and all the people came near to him.
1 Kings 18:31 And Eliou took twelve stones according to the number of the tribes of Israel, as the Lord had spoken to him, saying, Israel shall be your name.
1 Kings 18:32 And he built the stones in the name of the Lord and repaired the torn-down altar and made a thaala around the altar holding two measures of seed.
1 Kings 18:33 And he piled the split wood upon the altar which he made and cut up the whole burnt offering and placed it upon the split wood and piled it upon the altar.
1 Kings 18:34 And he said, Bring me four jars of water and pour them upon the whole burnt offering and upon the split wood; and they did so. And he said, Do it a second time; and they did it a second time. And he said, Do it a third time; and they did it a third time.
1 Kings 18:35 And the water flowed around the altar, and they filled the thaala with water.
1 Kings 18:36 And Eliou cried out to heaven and said, Lord God of Abraham and Isaac and Israel, hear me, Lord, hear me today by fire, and let all this people know that you are the Lord God of Israel and that I am your servant and that for your sake I have done these works.
1 Kings 18:37 Hear me, Lord, hear me by fire, and let this people know that you are the Lord God and that you turned the heart of this people back.
1 Kings 18:38 And fire fell from the Lord out of heaven and consumed the whole burnt offering and the split wood and the water in the thaala, and the fire rolled up the stones and the dust.
1 Kings 18:39 And all the people fell on their faces and said, Truly the Lord is God; he is God.
1 Kings 18:40 And Eliou said to the people, Seize the prophets of Baal; let none of them be saved. And they seized them, and Eliou brought them down to the brook Kison and slaughtered them there.
1 Kings 18:41 And Eliou said to Achaab, Go up and eat and drink, for there is a sound of the feet of rain.
1 Kings 18:42 And Achaab went up to eat and drink, and Eliou went up on Carmel and bent toward the earth and put his face between his knees.
1 Kings 18:43 And he said to his young servant, Go up and look toward the sea. And the young servant looked and said, There is nothing. And Eliou said, Return seven times; and the young servant returned seven times.
1 Kings 18:44 And it happened on the seventh time, and behold, a small cloud like the track of a man was bringing up water; and he said, Go up and say to Achaab, Harness your chariot and go down, lest the rain overtake you.
1 Kings 18:45 And it happened in a moment that the sky grew dark with clouds and wind, and there was a great rain; and Achaab wept and went to Jezrael.
1 Kings 18:46 And the hand of the Lord was upon Eliou, and he tightened his waist and ran before Achaab as far as Jezrael.

## Chapter 19

1 Kings 19:1 And Achaab reported to Jezabel his wife all that Eliou did and how he killed the prophets with the sword.
1 Kings 19:2 And Jezabel sent to Eliou and said, If you are Eliou and I am Jezabel, may God do thus to me and thus add, for at this hour tomorrow I shall make your life like the life of one of them.
1 Kings 19:3 And Eliou feared and arose and went away for his own life and came to Bersabee of Judah and left his young servant there.
1 Kings 19:4 And he went into the wilderness a day's journey and came and sat beneath one rathm and asked for his life to die and said, Let it suffice now; take my life from me, Lord, for I am not better than my fathers.
1 Kings 19:5 And he lay down and slept there beneath a plant, and behold, someone touched him and said to him, Arise and eat.
1 Kings 19:6 And Eliou looked, and behold, at his head was a spelt cake and a flask of water; and he arose and ate and drank. And turning back, he lay down.
1 Kings 19:7 And the angel of the Lord returned a second time and touched him and said to him, Arise, eat, for the journey is long from you.
1 Kings 19:8 And he arose and ate and drank; and he went in the strength of that food forty days and forty nights as far as Mount Choreb.
1 Kings 19:9 And he went into the cave there and lodged there; and behold, a word of the Lord came to him and said, What are you doing here, Eliou?
1 Kings 19:10 And Eliou said, I have been very zealous for the Lord Almighty, for the sons of Israel have abandoned you; they dug down your altars and killed your prophets with the sword, and I alone remain, and they seek my life to take it.
1 Kings 19:11 And he said, You shall go out tomorrow and stand before the Lord on the mountain; behold, the Lord shall pass by. And a great strong wind breaking apart mountains and crushing rocks before the Lord, but the Lord was not in the wind; and after the wind an earthquake, but the Lord was not in the earthquake;
1 Kings 19:12 and after the earthquake fire, but the Lord was not in the fire; and after the fire a voice of a gentle breeze, and there was the Lord.
1 Kings 19:13 And it happened when Eliou heard that he covered his face with his sheepskin and went out and stood below the cave; and behold, a voice came to him and said, What are you doing here, Eliou?
1 Kings 19:14 And Eliou said, I have been very zealous for the Lord Almighty, for the sons of Israel have abandoned your covenant; they pulled down your altars and killed your prophets with the sword, and I alone remain, and they seek my life to take it.
1 Kings 19:15 And the Lord said to him, Go, return to your way and you shall reach the road of the wilderness of Damascus and anoint Azael as king of Syria.
1 Kings 19:16 And you shall anoint Jou son of Namessi as king over Israel, and you shall anoint Elisaie son of Saphat from Abelmaoula as prophet in your place.
1 Kings 19:17 And it shall be that Jou will put to death the one saved from the sword of Azael, and Elisaie will put to death the one saved from the sword of Jou.
1 Kings 19:18 And you shall leave in Israel seven thousand men, all knees that have not bent a knee to Baal, and every mouth that has not bowed to him.
1 Kings 19:19 And he departed from there and found Elisaie son of Saphat, and he was plowing with oxen, twelve pairs of oxen before him and he among the twelve, and he came to him and threw his sheepskin upon him.
1 Kings 19:20 And Elisaie left the oxen and ran after Eliou and said, I shall kiss my father and follow after you; and Eliou said, Return, for I have done to you.
1 Kings 19:21 And he returned from following him and took the pairs of oxen and sacrificed and cooked them with the equipment of the oxen and gave to the people, and they ate; and he arose and went after Eliou and ministered to him.

## Chapter 20

1 Kings 20:1 And Nabouthai the Jezraelite had a vineyard beside the threshing floor of Achaab king of Samaria.
1 Kings 20:2 And Achaab spoke to Nabouthai, saying, Give me your vineyard and it shall become a garden of vegetables for me, for it is nearer to my house; and I shall give you another vineyard better than it. But if it pleases you, I shall give you silver in exchange for this vineyard of yours, and it shall become a garden of vegetables for me.
1 Kings 20:3 And Nabouthai said to Achaab, May it not happen to me from my God to give you the inheritance of my fathers.
1 Kings 20:4 And Achaab's spirit became troubled, and he lay on his bed and covered his face and did not eat bread.
1 Kings 20:5 And Jezabel his wife came in to him and spoke to him, Why is your spirit troubled and why are you not eating bread?
1 Kings 20:6 And he said to her, Because I spoke to Nabouthai the Jezraelite, saying, Give me your vineyard for silver; but if you wish, I shall give you another vineyard instead of it; and he said, I shall not give you the inheritance of my fathers.
1 Kings 20:7 And Jezabel his wife said to him, Do you now thus act as king over Israel? Arise, eat bread and become yourself; I shall give you the vineyard of Nabouthai the Jezraelite.
1 Kings 20:8 And she wrote a letter in Achaab's name and sealed it with his seal and sent the letter to the elders and the free men who dwelt with Nabouthai.
1 Kings 20:9 And in the letters it was written, saying, Proclaim a fast and seat Nabouthai at the head of the people.
1 Kings 20:10 And seat two men, sons of lawless men, opposite him, and let them bear witness against him, saying, He blessed God and king. And let them bring him out and stone him, and let him die.
1 Kings 20:11 And the men of his city, the elders and free men dwelling in his city, did as Jezabel sent to them, as was written in the letters which she sent to them.
1 Kings 20:12 They proclaimed a fast and seated Nabouthai at the head of the people.
1 Kings 20:13 And two men, sons of lawless men, came and sat opposite him and bore witness against him, saying, You blessed God and king; and they led him outside the city and stoned him with stones, and he died.
1 Kings 20:14 And they sent to Jezabel, saying, Nabouthai has been stoned and has died.
1 Kings 20:15 And it happened when Jezabel heard that she said to Achaab, Arise, inherit the vineyard of Nabouthai the Jezraelite, who did not give it to you for silver, for Nabouthai is not living; he has died.
1 Kings 20:16 And it happened when Achaab heard that Nabouthai the Jezraelite had died that he tore his garments and put on sackcloth; and after these things Achaab arose and went down to the vineyard of Nabouthai the Jezraelite to inherit it.
1 Kings 20:17 And the Lord said to Eliou the Thesbite, saying,
1 Kings 20:18 Arise and go down to meet Achaab king of Israel who is in Samaria; behold, he is in Nabouthai's vineyard, for he has gone down there to inherit it.
1 Kings 20:19 And speak to him, saying, Thus says the Lord: As you murdered and inherited, therefore thus says the Lord: In every place where the swine and the dogs licked Nabouthai's blood, there the dogs shall lick your blood, and the prostitutes shall bathe in your blood.
1 Kings 20:20 And Achaab said to Eliou, Have you found me, my enemy? And he said, I have found you, because you have sold yourself in vain to do evil before the Lord, to provoke him.
1 Kings 20:21 Thus says the Lord: Behold, I bring evils upon you and shall burn up after you and destroy of Achaab one who urinates against a wall and one confined and one abandoned in Israel.
1 Kings 20:22 And I shall make your house like the house of Jeroboam son of Nabat and like the house of Baasa son of Achia because of the provocations with which you provoked and caused Israel to sin.
1 Kings 20:23 And concerning Jezabel the Lord spoke, saying, The dogs shall eat her by the outer wall of Jezrael.
1 Kings 20:24 The dogs shall eat the one of Achaab who dies in the city, and the birds of heaven shall eat the one of his who dies in the plain.
1 Kings 20:25 But Achaab was vainly sold to do evil before the Lord, as Jezabel his wife turned him aside.
1 Kings 20:26 And he became very abhorrent in going after abominations according to all that the Amorite did, whom the Lord destroyed from before the sons of Israel.
1 Kings 20:27 And concerning the matter, when Achaab was pierced before the Lord and went about weeping, he tore his tunic and girded sackcloth upon his body and fasted and wore sackcloth on the day when he struck Nabouthai the Jezraelite.
1 Kings 20:28 And the word of the Lord came by the hand of his servant Eliou concerning Achaab, and the Lord said,
1 Kings 20:29 Have you seen how Achaab was pierced before me? I shall not bring the evil in his days, but in the days of his son I shall bring the evil.

## Chapter 21

1 Kings 21:1 And the son of Ader gathered all his force and went up and besieged Samaria, and thirty-two kings were with him and every horse and chariot; and they went up and besieged Samaria and fought against it.
1 Kings 21:2 And he sent to Achaab king of Israel in the city
1 Kings 21:3 and said to him, Thus says the son of Ader: Your silver and your gold are mine, and your women and your children are mine.
1 Kings 21:4 And the king of Israel answered and said, As you have spoken, my lord king, I am yours and all that is mine.
1 Kings 21:5 And the messengers returned and said, Thus says the son of Ader: I have sent to you, saying, Your silver and your gold and your women and your children you shall give me.
1 Kings 21:6 For at this hour tomorrow I shall send my servants to you, and they shall search your house and the houses of your servants, and whatever their eyes desire, upon which they lay their hands, they shall take.
1 Kings 21:7 And the king of Israel called all the elders and said, Know now and see that this man seeks evil, for he sent to me concerning my women and my sons and my daughters; my silver and my gold I did not withhold from him.
1 Kings 21:8 And the elders and all the people said to him, Do not listen and do not consent.
1 Kings 21:9 And he said to the messengers of the son of Ader, Say to your lord, All that you first sent to your servant I shall do, but this matter I cannot do. And the men departed and returned a word to him.
1 Kings 21:10 And the son of Ader sent back to him, saying, May God do thus to me and thus add, if the dust of Samaria shall suffice for the foxes of all the people on foot with me.
1 Kings 21:11 And the king of Israel answered and said, Let it suffice; let not the bent man boast like the upright man.
1 Kings 21:12 And it happened when he answered him with this word that he and all the kings with him were drinking in tents; and he said to his servants, Build a palisade; and they placed a palisade against the city.
1 Kings 21:13 And behold, one prophet approached the king of Israel and said, Thus says the Lord: Have you seen all this great crowd? Behold, I give it into your hands today, and you shall know that I am the Lord.
1 Kings 21:14 And Achaab said, By whom? And he said, Thus says the Lord: By the young servants of the rulers of the territories. And Achaab said, Who shall begin the war? And he said, You.
1 Kings 21:15 And Achaab inspected the young servants of the rulers of the territories, and they were two hundred and thirty; and after these he inspected the people, every son of strength, sixty thousand.
1 Kings 21:16 And he went out at noon; and the son of Ader was drinking himself drunk in Sokchoth, he and the kings, thirty-two kings aiding him.
1 Kings 21:17 And the young servants of the rulers of the territories went out first. And they sent and reported to the king of Syria, saying, Men have gone out from Samaria.
1 Kings 21:18 And he said to them, If these come out for peace, seize them alive; and if for war, seize them alive.
1 Kings 21:19 And let not the young servants of the rulers of the territories go out from the city. And the force behind them
1 Kings 21:20 struck, each one the man beside him, and each one struck a second time the man beside him, and Syria fled, and Israel pursued them; and the son of Ader king of Syria escaped on a horse of a horseman.
1 Kings 21:21 And the king of Israel went out and took all the horses and chariots and struck a great blow in Syria.
1 Kings 21:22 And the prophet approached the king of Israel and said, Be strong and know and see what you shall do, for at the turn of the year the son of Ader king of Syria will come up against you.
1 Kings 21:23 And the servants of the king of Syria said, The God of Israel is a god of mountains and not a god of valleys; therefore he prevailed over us. But if we fight them on level ground, surely we shall prevail over them.
1 Kings 21:24 And do this thing: remove the kings, each from his place, and put satraps in their stead,
1 Kings 21:25 and we shall replace for you a force corresponding to the force that fell from you, and horse for horse and chariots for chariots; and we shall fight against them on level ground and prevail over them. And he listened to their voice and did so.
1 Kings 21:26 And it happened at the turn of the year that the son of Ader inspected Syria and went up to Apheka for war against Israel.
1 Kings 21:27 And the sons of Israel were inspected and came to meet them; and Israel encamped opposite them like two flocks of goats, and Syria filled the land.
1 Kings 21:28 And the man of God approached and said to the king of Israel, Thus says the Lord: Because Syria said, The Lord God of Israel is a God of mountains and he is not a God of valleys, I shall give this great force into your hand, and you shall know that I am the Lord.
1 Kings 21:29 And these encamped opposite those for seven days; and it happened on the seventh day that the battle drew near, and Israel struck Syria, a hundred thousand foot soldiers in one day.
1 Kings 21:30 And the remainder fled into Apheka, into the city, and the wall fell upon twenty-seven thousand men of the remainder. And the son of Ader fled and entered into the house of the bedchamber, into the storeroom.
1 Kings 21:31 And he said to his servants, I know that the kings of Israel are merciful kings. Let us put sackcloth on our waists and ropes on our heads and go out to the king of Israel; perhaps he will preserve our lives.
1 Kings 21:32 And they girded sackcloth on their waists and put ropes on their heads and said to the king of Israel, Your servant the son of Ader says, Let my life live. And he said, Is he still alive? He is my brother.
1 Kings 21:33 And the men took it as an omen and hastened and caught up the word from his mouth and said, Your brother, the son of Ader. And he said, Go in and take him. And the son of Ader came out to him, and they brought him up to him upon the chariot.
1 Kings 21:34 And he said to him, The cities that my father took from your father I shall restore to you, and you shall establish exits for yourself in Damascus, as my father established in Samaria; and I shall send you away under a covenant. And he made a covenant with him and sent him away.
1 Kings 21:35 And a certain man of the sons of the prophets said to his neighbor by the word of the Lord, Strike me, please. And the man was unwilling to strike him.
1 Kings 21:36 And he said to him, Because you did not listen to the voice of the Lord, behold, as you run away from me a lion will strike you. And he went away from him, and a lion found him and struck him.
1 Kings 21:37 And he found another man and said, Strike me, please. And the man struck him, striking and crushing him.
1 Kings 21:38 And the prophet went and stood before the king of Israel on the road and bound his eyes with a band.
1 Kings 21:39 And it happened as the king was passing by that this man cried out to the king and said, Your servant went out to the army of the war, and behold, a man brought a man to me and said to me, Guard this man; but if he escapes by escaping, then your life shall be in place of his life, or you shall pay a talent of silver.
1 Kings 21:40 And it happened that your servant looked around here and there, and he was not there. And the king of Israel said to him, Behold also the ambushes; in my presence you have murdered.
1 Kings 21:41 And he hastened and removed the band from his eyes, and the king of Israel recognized him, that he was of the prophets.
1 Kings 21:42 And he said to him, Thus says the Lord: Because you brought a man devoted to destruction out of your hand, your life shall be in place of his life and your people in place of his people.
1 Kings 21:43 And the king of Israel departed confused and dispirited and came to Samaria.

## Chapter 22

1 Kings 22:1 And he remained three years, and there was no war between Syria and Israel.
1 Kings 22:2 And it happened in the third year that Josaphat king of Judah came down to the king of Israel.
1 Kings 22:3 And the king of Israel said to his servants, Do you know that Remmath Galaad belongs to us, and we are silent about taking it from the hand of the king of Syria?
1 Kings 22:4 And the king of Israel said to Josaphat, Will you go up with us to Remmath Galaad for war? And Josaphat said, As I am, so are you; as my people, your people; as my horses, your horses.
1 Kings 22:5 And Josaphat king of Judah said to the king of Israel, Inquire of the Lord today, please.
1 Kings 22:6 And the king of Israel gathered all the prophets, about four hundred men, and the king said to them, Shall I go to Remmath Galaad for war, or shall I hold back? And they said, Go up, and the Lord will surely give it into the hands of the king.
1 Kings 22:7 And Josaphat said to the king of Israel, Is there no prophet of the Lord here, that we may inquire of the Lord through him?
1 Kings 22:8 And the king of Israel said to Josaphat, There is still one man through whom to inquire of the Lord, and I have hated him because he does not speak good concerning me, but only evil: Michaias son of Iemla. And Josaphat king of Judah said, Let the king not say so.
1 Kings 22:9 And the king of Israel called one eunuch and said, Quickly, Michaias son of Iemla.
1 Kings 22:10 And the king of Israel and Josaphat king of Judah were sitting, each on his throne, armed, at the gates of Samaria, and all the prophets were prophesying before them.
1 Kings 22:11 And Sedekias son of Chanana made for himself horns of iron and said, Thus says the Lord: With these you shall gore Syria until it is brought to an end.
1 Kings 22:12 And all the prophets prophesied thus, saying, Go up to Remmath Galaad, and it will prosper, and the Lord will give into your hands even the king of Syria.
1 Kings 22:13 And the messenger who had gone to call Michaias spoke to him, saying, Behold now, all the prophets speak good concerning the king with one mouth; let your words also be like the words of one of these, and speak good.
1 Kings 22:14 And Michaias said, As the Lord lives, whatever the Lord says to me, that I shall speak.
1 Kings 22:15 And he came to the king, and the king said to him, Michaias, shall I go up to Remmath Galaad for war, or shall I hold back? And he said, Go up, and it will prosper, and the Lord will give it into the hand of the king.
1 Kings 22:16 And the king said to him, How many times do I put you under oath to speak truth to me in the name of the Lord?
1 Kings 22:17 And Michaias said, Not so. I have seen all Israel scattered on the mountains like a flock that has no shepherd, and the Lord said, These have no master; let each return to his house in peace.
1 Kings 22:18 And the king of Israel said to Josaphat king of Judah, Did I not say to you, He prophesies no good for me, but only evil?
1 Kings 22:19 And Michaias said, Not so, not I; hear the word of the Lord, not so: I saw the Lord God of Israel sitting upon his throne, and all the host of heaven stood around him, on his right and on his left.
1 Kings 22:20 And the Lord said, Who will deceive Achaab king of Israel, so that he will go up and fall at Remmath Galaad? And this one said thus and that one thus.
