1 Kings 22:21 And a spirit came out and stood before the Lord and said, I shall deceive him. And the Lord said to it, By what means?
1 Kings 22:22 And it said, I shall go out and be a lying spirit in the mouth of all his prophets. And he said, You shall deceive him and indeed be able; go out and do so.
1 Kings 22:23 And now behold, the Lord has put a lying spirit in the mouth of all these prophets of yours, and the Lord has spoken evil against you.
1 Kings 22:24 And Sedekiou son of Chanana approached and struck Michaias on the jaw and said, What spirit of the Lord is it that spoke in you?
1 Kings 22:25 And Michaias said, Behold, you shall see on that day when you enter the innermost storeroom to hide.
1 Kings 22:26 And the king of Israel said, Take Michaias and return him to Emer the ruler of the city, and to Joas the king's son
1 Kings 22:27 say to put this man in prison and to feed him bread of affliction and water of affliction until I return in peace.
1 Kings 22:28 And Michaias said, If you do return in peace, the Lord has not spoken in me.
1 Kings 22:29 And the king of Israel went up, and Josaphat king of Judah with him, to Remmath Galaad.
1 Kings 22:30 And the king of Israel said to Josaphat king of Judah, I shall disguise myself and enter into the battle, and you put on my clothing. And the king of Israel disguised himself and entered into the battle.
1 Kings 22:31 And the king of Syria commanded the thirty-two commanders of his chariots, saying, Do not fight small or great, but only the king of Israel.
1 Kings 22:32 And it happened when the commanders of the chariots saw Josaphat king of Judah that they said, This appears to be the king of Israel; and they surrounded him to fight, and Josaphat cried out.
1 Kings 22:33 And it happened when the commanders of the chariots saw that this was not the king of Israel that they turned away from him.
1 Kings 22:34 And one drew the bow with good aim and struck the king of Israel between the lung and the breastplate. And he said to his charioteer, Turn your hands and bring me out of the battle, for I am wounded.
1 Kings 22:35 And the battle turned on that day, and the king stood upon the chariot opposite Syria from morning until evening, and he was pouring the blood from the wound into the hollow of the chariot; and he died in the evening, and the blood of the rout was flowing as far as the hollow of the chariot.
1 Kings 22:36 And the army herald stood as the sun was setting, saying, Each to his own city and to his own land,
1 Kings 22:37 for the king is dead. And they came to Samaria and buried the king in Samaria.
1 Kings 22:38 And they washed the chariot at the spring of Samaria, and the swine and the dogs licked up the blood, and the prostitutes bathed in the blood, according to the word of the Lord that he had spoken.
1 Kings 22:39 And the rest of the deeds of Achaab and all that he did, and the ivory house that he built, and all the cities that he made, behold, are these not written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Israel?
1 Kings 22:40 And Achaab slept with his fathers, and Ochozias his son reigned in his stead.
1 Kings 22:41 And Josaphat son of Asa reigned over Judah. He reigned in the fourth year of Achaab king of Israel.
1 Kings 22:42 Josaphat was a son of thirty-five years when he began to reign, and he reigned twenty-five years in Jerusalem; and his mother's name was Azouba daughter of Selei.
1 Kings 22:43 And he walked in all the way of Asa his father; he did not turn aside from it, doing what was right in the eyes of the Lord;
1 Kings 22:44 but he did not remove the high places; the people still sacrificed and burned incense on the high places.
1 Kings 22:45 And Josaphat made peace with the king of Israel.
1 Kings 22:46 And the rest of the deeds of Josaphat and his acts of power, as many as he did, behold, are these not written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Judah?
1 Kings 22:51 And Josaphat slept with his fathers and was buried with his fathers in the city of David his father; and Joram his son reigned in his stead.
1 Kings 22:52 And Ochozias son of Achaab reigned over Israel in Samaria in the seventeenth year of Josaphat king of Judah; and he reigned in Israel two years.
1 Kings 22:53 And he did evil before the Lord and walked in the way of Achaab his father and in the way of Jezabel his mother and in the sins of the house of Jeroboam son of Nabat, who caused Israel to sin.
1 Kings 22:54 And he served the Baals and worshiped them and provoked the Lord God of Israel according to all that had happened before him.

# 2 Kings

## Chapter 1

2 Kings 1:1 And Moab rebelled against Israel after Achaab died.
2 Kings 1:2 And Ochozias fell through the lattice in his upper room in Samaria and became ill. And he sent messengers and said to them, Come and inquire of Baal Myian, god of Akkaron, whether I shall live from this illness of mine; and they went to inquire through him.
2 Kings 1:3 And an angel of the Lord spoke to Eliou the Thesbite, saying, Arise, come to meet the messengers of Ochozias king of Samaria, and speak to them: Is it because there is no God in Israel that you go to inquire of Baal Myian, god of Akkaron?
2 Kings 1:4 And not so; for thus says the Lord: The bed onto which you went up there, you shall not come down from it, for there you shall surely die. And Eliou went and spoke to them.
2 Kings 1:5 And the messengers returned to him, and he said to them, Why have you returned?
2 Kings 1:6 And they said to him, A man came up to meet us and said to us, Come, return to the king who sent you and speak to him: Thus says the Lord: Is it because there is no God in Israel that you are going to seek Baal Myian, god of Akkaron? Not so; the bed onto which you went up there, you shall not come down from it, for you shall surely die.
2 Kings 1:7 And he spoke to them, saying, What was the appearance of the man who came up to meet you and spoke these words to you?
2 Kings 1:8 And they said to him, A hairy man, with a leather belt girded about his waist. And he said, This is Eliou the Thesbite.
2 Kings 1:9 And he sent to him a leader, a captain of fifty, and his fifty; and he went up and came to him, and behold, Eliou was sitting on the top of the mountain. And the captain of fifty spoke to him and said, Man of God, the king has summoned you; come down.
2 Kings 1:10 And Eliou answered and said to the captain of fifty, And if I am a man of God, fire will come down from heaven and devour you and your fifty. And fire came down from heaven and devoured him and his fifty.
2 Kings 1:11 And the king again sent to him another captain of fifty and his fifty, and he went up, and the captain of fifty spoke to him and said, Man of God, thus says the king: Come down quickly.
2 Kings 1:12 And Eliou answered and spoke to him and said, If I am a man of God, fire will come down from heaven and devour you and your fifty. And fire came down from heaven and devoured him and his fifty.
2 Kings 1:13 And the king again sent a third leader, a captain of fifty, and his fifty; and the third captain of fifty came to him and bent upon his knees before Eliou and entreated him and spoke to him and said, Man of God, let my life and the life of these fifty servants of yours be precious in your eyes;
2 Kings 1:14 behold, fire came down from heaven and devoured the first two captains of fifty and their fifties, and now let the life of your servants be precious in your eyes.
2 Kings 1:15 And an angel of the Lord spoke to Eliou and said, Go down with him; do not be afraid of them. And Eliou arose and went down with him to the king.
2 Kings 1:16 And he spoke to him, and Eliou said, Thus says the Lord: Why did you send messengers to seek Baal Myian, god of Akkaron? Not so; the bed onto which you went up there, you shall not come down from it, for you shall surely die.
2 Kings 1:17 And he died according to the word of the Lord that Eliou had spoken.
2 Kings 1:18 And the rest of the deeds of Ochozias, as many as he did, behold, are these not written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Israel?
2 Kings 1:18 a And Joram son of Achaab reigns over Israel in Samaria for twelve years in the eighteenth year of Josaphat king of Judah.
2 Kings 1:19 And he did evil before the Lord, though not like his brothers or like his mother;
2 Kings 1:20 and he removed the pillars of Baal, which his father had made, and crushed them; but he clung to the sins of the house of Jeroboam, who caused Israel to sin; he did not depart from them.
2 Kings 1:21 And the Lord was angry with anger against the house of Achaab.

## Chapter 2

2 Kings 2:1 And it happened when the Lord was taking Eliou up in a whirlwind as into heaven, that Eliou and Elisaie went from Galgala.
2 Kings 2:2 And Eliou said to Elisaie, Stay here, please, for the Lord has sent me as far as Bethel. And Elisaie said, As the Lord lives and as your soul lives, I shall not leave you. And they came to Bethel.
2 Kings 2:3 And the sons of the prophets in Bethel came to Elisaie and said to him, Do you know that the Lord today is taking your master from above your head? And he said, I too know; be silent.
2 Kings 2:4 And Eliou said to Elisaie, Stay here, please, for the Lord has sent me to Jericho. And Elisaie said, As the Lord lives and as your soul lives, I shall not abandon you. And they came to Jericho.
2 Kings 2:5 And the sons of the prophets in Jericho approached Elisaie and said to him, Do you know that today the Lord is taking your master from above your head? And he said, Indeed I too know; be silent.
2 Kings 2:6 And Eliou said to him, Stay here, please, for the Lord has sent me as far as the Jordan. And Elisaie said, As the Lord lives and as your soul lives, I shall not abandon you. And they both went.
2 Kings 2:7 And fifty men of the sons of the prophets stood opposite at a distance, and the two stood at the Jordan.
2 Kings 2:8 And Eliou took his sheepskin mantle and rolled it up and struck the water, and the water was divided this way and that, and the two crossed in the wilderness.
2 Kings 2:9 And it happened when they crossed that Eliou said to Elisaie, Ask what I shall do for you before I am taken up from you. And Elisaie said, Let there be, please, a double portion of your spirit upon me.
2 Kings 2:10 And Eliou said, You have made a hard request. If you see me being taken up from you, then it shall be so for you; and if not, it shall certainly not happen.
2 Kings 2:11 And it happened as they went along and talked, behold, a chariot of fire and horses of fire separated the two, and Eliou was taken up in a whirlwind as into heaven.
2 Kings 2:12 And Elisaie saw and cried out, Father, father, chariot of Israel and its horseman! And he saw him no more, and he grasped his garments and tore them into two tears.
2 Kings 2:13 And he lifted up the sheepskin mantle of Eliou, which had fallen from above Elisaie, and Elisaie returned and stood on the bank of the Jordan;
2 Kings 2:14 and he took the sheepskin mantle of Eliou, which had fallen from above him, and struck the water, and it did not part. And he said, Where is the God of Eliou, affo? And he struck the waters, and they were split this way and that, and Elisaie crossed.
2 Kings 2:15 And the sons of the prophets in Jericho saw him opposite and said, The spirit of Eliou has rested upon Elisaie. And they came to meet him and bowed to him to the ground.
2 Kings 2:16 And they said to him, Behold now, with your servants are fifty men, sons of strength; let them go, please, and seek your master, lest the spirit of the Lord have lifted him and thrown him into the Jordan or upon one of the mountains or upon one of the hills. And Elisaie said, Do not send them.
2 Kings 2:17 And they pressed him until he was ashamed, and he said, Send them. And they sent fifty men, and they searched three days and did not find him;
2 Kings 2:18 and they returned to him while he was staying in Jericho, and Elisaie said, Did I not say to you, Do not go?
2 Kings 2:19 And the men of the city said to Elisaie, Behold, the dwelling place of the city is good, as my lord sees, but the waters are bad and the land is barren.
2 Kings 2:20 And Elisaie said, Bring me a new small jar and put salt there. And they brought it to him.
2 Kings 2:21 And Elisaie went out to the outlet of the waters and threw salt there and said, Thus says the Lord: I have healed these waters; no longer shall death and barrenness come from there.
2 Kings 2:22 And the waters were healed to this day according to the word of Elisaie that he spoke.
2 Kings 2:23 And he went up from there to Bethel; and as he was going up on the road, small children came out of the city and mocked him and said to him, Go up, bald one, go up.
2 Kings 2:24 And he turned behind them and saw them and cursed them in the name of the Lord, and behold, two bears came out of the thicket and tore forty-two children from among them.
2 Kings 2:25 And he went from there to Mount Carmel and returned from there to Samaria.

## Chapter 3

2 Kings 3:1 And Joram son of Achaab reigned in Israel in the eighteenth year of Josaphat king of Judah, and he reigned twelve years.
2 Kings 3:2 And he did evil in the eyes of the Lord, though not like his father and not like his mother, and he removed the pillars of Baal that his father had made;
2 Kings 3:3 but he clung to the sin of Jeroboam son of Nabat, who caused Israel to sin; he did not depart from it.
2 Kings 3:4 And Mosa king of Moab was a noked, and at the revolt he rendered to the king of Israel a hundred thousand lambs and a hundred thousand rams with fleeces.
2 Kings 3:5 And it happened after Achaab died that the king of Moab rebelled against the king of Israel.
2 Kings 3:6 And King Joram went out from Samaria on that day and inspected Israel;
2 Kings 3:7 and he went and sent to Josaphat king of Judah, saying, The king of Moab has rebelled against me; will you go with me to Moab for war? And he said, I shall go up; I am like you, my people like your people, my horses like your horses.
2 Kings 3:8 And he said, By which road shall I go up? And he said, By the wilderness road of Edom.
2 Kings 3:9 And the king of Israel and the king of Judah and the king of Edom went, and they went around on a road of seven days, and there was no water for the camp and for the beasts following in their steps.
2 Kings 3:10 And the king of Israel said, Alas, for the Lord has called these three kings who are passing through to give them into the hand of Moab.
2 Kings 3:11 And Josaphat said, Is there no prophet of the Lord here, that we may seek the Lord from him? And one of the servants of the king of Israel answered and said, Here is Elisaie son of Saphat, who poured water upon Eliou's hands.
2 Kings 3:12 And Josaphat said, The word of the Lord is with him. And the king of Israel and Josaphat king of Judah and the king of Edom went down to him.
2 Kings 3:13 And Elisaie said to the king of Israel, What is there between me and you? Go to your father's prophets. And the king of Israel said to him, No, for the Lord has called these three kings to deliver them into the hands of Moab.
2 Kings 3:14 And Elisaie said, As the Lord of hosts lives, before whom I stand, if I did not regard the face of Josaphat king of Judah, would I look at you or see you?
2 Kings 3:15 And now bring me someone who plays. And it happened as the player played that the hand of the Lord came upon him,
2 Kings 3:16 and he said, Thus says the Lord: Make this torrent bed pits upon pits;
2 Kings 3:17 for thus says the Lord: You shall see no wind and shall see no rain, yet this torrent bed shall be filled with water, and you and your possessions and your beasts shall drink;
2 Kings 3:18 and this is a light thing in the eyes of the Lord, and I shall deliver Moab into your hand,
2 Kings 3:19 and you shall strike every fortified city and fell every good tree and stop up every spring of water and ruin every good portion with stones.
2 Kings 3:20 And it happened in the morning, as the sacrifice was going up, behold, waters came from the direction of Edom, and the land was filled with water.
2 Kings 3:21 And all Moab heard that the kings had gone up to fight them, and they called out everyone who girded on a belt and upward, and stood at the border.
2 Kings 3:22 And they rose early in the morning, and the sun rose upon the waters; and Moab saw the waters opposite, red like blood,
2 Kings 3:23 and they said, This is blood of the sword; the kings have fought and each man has struck his neighbor, and now to the spoil, Moab.
2 Kings 3:24 And they entered the camp of Israel, and Israel rose and struck Moab, and they fled before them. And they entered, going in and striking Moab,
2 Kings 3:25 and they pulled down the cities, and upon every good portion each man threw a stone and filled it, and they stopped up every spring of water and felled every good tree, until leaving the stones of the wall pulled down; and the slingers surrounded and struck it.
2 Kings 3:26 And the king of Moab saw that the battle had prevailed against him, and he took with him seven hundred men who drew the sword to break through to the king of Edom, and they were unable.
2 Kings 3:27 And he took his firstborn son, who reigned in his stead, and offered him as a whole burnt offering upon the wall; and great regret came upon Israel, and they departed from him and returned to the land.

## Chapter 4

2 Kings 4:1 And one woman of the wives of the sons of the prophets cried out to Elisaie, saying, Your servant my husband has died, and you know that he was a servant fearing the Lord; and the creditor has come to take my two sons as slaves for himself.
2 Kings 4:2 And Elisaie said, What shall I do for you? Tell me what you have in the house. And she said, Your servant has nothing in the house except oil with which I shall anoint myself.
2 Kings 4:3 And he said to her, Go, ask for vessels for yourself from outside, from all your neighbors, empty vessels; do not make them few,
2 Kings 4:4 and you shall enter and shut the door behind you and your sons and pour into these vessels, and what is filled you shall take away.
2 Kings 4:5 And she went from him and did so and shut the door behind herself and her sons; they brought them near to her, and she poured,
2 Kings 4:6 until the vessels were filled. And she said to her sons, Bring another vessel to me. And they said to her, There is no other vessel. And the oil stopped.
2 Kings 4:7 And she came and told the man of God, and Elisaie said, Go and sell the oil and pay your interest, and you and your sons shall live on the remaining oil.
2 Kings 4:8 And a day came when Elisaie passed through Souman, and a great woman was there and pressed him to eat bread. And it happened after some time that whenever he entered he turned aside to eat there.
2 Kings 4:9 And the woman said to her husband, Behold now, I know that this is a holy man of God who passes by us continually;
2 Kings 4:10 let us make for him a small upper room, and let us put there for him a bed and a table and a stool and a lamp, and when he comes to us he will turn aside there.
2 Kings 4:11 And a day came when he entered there and turned aside to the upper room and slept there.
2 Kings 4:12 And he said to Giezi his servant, Call this Somanite woman for me. And he called her, and she stood before him.
2 Kings 4:13 And he said to him, Say to her, Behold, you have gone through all this trouble for us; what must be done for you? Is there a matter for you with the king or with the commander of the force? And she said, I dwell among my people.
2 Kings 4:14 And he said, What must be done for her? And Giezi his servant said, Indeed she has no son, and her husband is old.
2 Kings 4:15 And he called her, and she stood by the door.
2 Kings 4:16 And Elisaie said to her, At this time, as at the hour, while living, you shall be embracing a son. And she said, No, my lord, do not deceive your servant.
2 Kings 4:17 And the woman conceived and bore a son at this time, as at the hour, while living, as Elisaie had spoken to her.
2 Kings 4:18 And the child grew strong; and it happened when the child went out to his father, to the reapers,
2 Kings 4:19 that he said to his father, My head, my head! And he said to the servant, Carry him to his mother.
2 Kings 4:20 And he carried him to his mother, and he lay on her knees until noon and died.
2 Kings 4:21 And she carried him up and laid him on the bed of the man of God and shut the door behind him and went out.
2 Kings 4:22 And she called her husband and said, Send me one of the servants and one of the donkeys, please, and I shall run as far as the man of God and return.
2 Kings 4:23 And he said, Why are you going to him today? It is neither a new moon nor a sabbath. And she said, Peace.
2 Kings 4:24 And she saddled the donkey and said to her servant, Lead on, go; do not hold me back from riding unless I tell you.
2 Kings 4:25 Come, and she went and came to the man of God at Mount Carmel. And it happened when Elisaie saw her coming that he said to Giezi his servant, Behold, that Somanite woman;
2 Kings 4:26 now run to meet her and say, Is it peace with you? Is it peace with your husband? Is it peace with the child? And she said, Peace.
2 Kings 4:27 And she came to Elisaie on the mountain and grasped his feet. And Giezi approached to push her away, and Elisaie said, Leave her, for her soul is in pain within her, and the Lord has hidden it from me and has not told me.
2 Kings 4:28 And she said, Did I ask my lord for a son? Did I not say, Do not mislead me?
2 Kings 4:29 And Elisaie said to Giezi, Gird your waist and take my staff in your hand and go; if you meet a man, do not greet him, and if a man greets you, do not answer him; and place my staff on the child's face.
2 Kings 4:30 And the mother of the child said, As the Lord lives and as your soul lives, I shall not abandon you. And Elisaie arose and went after her.
2 Kings 4:31 And Giezi went ahead of her and placed the staff on the child's face, and there was no voice and no hearing; and he returned to meet him and told him, saying, The child has not awakened.
2 Kings 4:32 And Elisaie entered the house, and behold, the child was dead, lying on his bed.
2 Kings 4:33 And Elisaie entered the house and shut the door behind the two of them and prayed to the Lord;
2 Kings 4:34 and he went up and lay upon the child and put his mouth upon his mouth and his eyes upon his eyes and his hands upon his hands and bent himself over him, and the child's flesh grew warm.
2 Kings 4:35 And he returned and walked in the house back and forth and went up and bent himself over the child seven times, and the child opened his eyes.
2 Kings 4:36 And Elisaie cried out to Giezi and said, Call this Somanite woman. And he called her, and she came in to him. And Elisaie said, Take your son.
2 Kings 4:37 And the woman came in and fell at his feet and bowed to the ground and took her son and went out.
2 Kings 4:38 And Elisaie returned to Galgala, and there was famine in the land, and the sons of the prophets were sitting before him. And Elisaie said to his servant, Set up the large cauldron and cook a stew for the sons of the prophets.
2 Kings 4:39 And one went out to the field to gather arioth and found a vine in the field and gathered from it a wild cluster, filling his garment, and threw it into the cauldron of stew, for they did not know.
2 Kings 4:40 And he poured it out for the men to eat, and it happened as they ate from the stew that, behold, they cried out and said, Death is in the cauldron, man of God! And they could not eat.
2 Kings 4:41 And he said, Take flour and throw it into the cauldron. And Elisaie said to Giezi his servant, Pour it out for the people, and let them eat. And there was no longer any evil thing in the cauldron.
2 Kings 4:42 And a man came from Baithsarisa and brought to the man of God from the firstfruits twenty barley loaves and cakes of pressed fruit, and he said, Give to the people, and let them eat.
2 Kings 4:43 And his attendant said, What shall I set this before a hundred men? And he said, Give to the people, and let them eat, for thus says the Lord: They shall eat and leave some.
2 Kings 4:44 And they ate and left some according to the word of the Lord.

## Chapter 5

2 Kings 5:1 And Naiman commander of the force of Syria was a great man before his master and admired in person, because through him the Lord gave deliverance to Syria; and the man was mighty in strength, afflicted with leprosy.
2 Kings 5:2 And the Syrians went out in bands and took captive from the land of Israel a little young girl, and she was before the wife of Naiman.
2 Kings 5:3 And she said to her mistress, If only my master were before the prophet of God in Samaria, then he would remove him from his leprosy.
2 Kings 5:4 And he went in and reported to his master and said, Thus and thus spoke the girl from the land of Israel.
2 Kings 5:5 And the king of Syria said to Naiman, Come, go in, and I shall send a letter to the king of Israel. And he went and took in his hand ten talents of silver and six thousand gold pieces and ten changes of garments.
2 Kings 5:6 And he brought the letter to the king of Israel, saying, And now when this letter comes to you, behold, I have sent to you Naiman my servant, and you shall remove him from his leprosy.
2 Kings 5:7 And it happened when the king of Israel read the letter that he tore his garments and said, Am I God, to put to death and to make alive, that this man sends to me to remove a man from his leprosy? But know now and see that this man seeks a pretext against me.
2 Kings 5:8 And it happened when Elisaie heard that the king of Israel had torn his garments that he sent to the king of Israel, saying, Why did you tear your garments? Let Naiman come to me, please, and let him know that there is a prophet in Israel.
2 Kings 5:9 And Naiman came with horse and chariot and stood at the door of Elisaie's house.
2 Kings 5:10 And Elisaie sent a messenger to him, saying, Go and wash seven times in the Jordan, and your flesh shall return to you, and you shall be clean.
2 Kings 5:11 And Naiman became angry and went away and said, Behold, I had said that he would come out to me and stand and call upon the name of his God and put his hand upon the place and remove the leprous condition;
2 Kings 5:12 are not Abana and Pharphar, rivers of Damascus, better than the Jordan and all the waters of Israel? Shall I not go and wash in them and be clean? And he turned aside and went away in anger.
2 Kings 5:13 And his servants approached and spoke to him, A great word the prophet spoke to you; would you not do it? And because he said to you, Wash and be clean.
2 Kings 5:14 And Naiman went down and immersed himself in the Jordan seven times according to the word of Elisaie, and his flesh returned like the flesh of a little child, and he was cleansed.
2 Kings 5:15 And he returned to Elisaie, he and all his camp, and came and stood and said, Behold now, I know that there is no God in all the earth except in Israel; and now take the blessing from your servant.
2 Kings 5:16 And Elisaie said, As the Lord lives, before whom I stand, I shall not take it. And he pressed him to take it, but he refused.
2 Kings 5:17 And Naiman said, And if not, let a load of a pair of mules be given to your servant, and you shall give me from the red earth, for your servant shall no longer make whole burnt offering and sacrifice to other gods, but to the Lord alone;
2 Kings 5:18 and may the Lord show mercy to your servant when my master enters the house of Remman to worship him and rests upon my hand and I bow in the house of Remman as he bows in the house of Remman; may the Lord show mercy to your servant in this matter.
2 Kings 5:19 And Elisaie said to Naiman, Go in peace. And he went away from him to debratha of the land.
2 Kings 5:20 And Giezi the servant of Elisaie said, Behold, my master spared this Syrian Naiman by not taking from his hand what he had brought. As the Lord lives, I shall surely run after him and take something from him.
2 Kings 5:21 And Giezi pursued Naiman, and Naiman saw him running after him and turned from the chariot to meet him.
2 Kings 5:22 And he said, Peace. My master sent me, saying, Behold, just now two young men have come to me from Mount Ephraim, from the sons of the prophets; give them, please, a talent of silver and two changes of garments.
2 Kings 5:23 And Naiman said, Take two talents of silver. And he took it in two bags and two changes of garments and gave them to two of his servants, and they carried them before him.
2 Kings 5:24 And they came to the dark place, and he took them from their hands and put them in the house and sent the men away.
2 Kings 5:25 And he himself entered and stood before his master. And Elisaie said to him, Where have you come from, Giezi? And Giezi said, Your servant has gone nowhere at all.
2 Kings 5:26 And Elisaie said to him, Did not my heart go with you when the man turned from the chariot to meet you? And now you have taken the silver and now you have taken the garments, and with it you shall acquire gardens and olive groves and vineyards and sheep and cattle and male and female servants;
2 Kings 5:27 and Naiman's leprosy shall cling to you and your offspring forever. And he went out from before him afflicted with leprosy like snow.

## Chapter 6

2 Kings 6:1 And the sons of the prophets said to Elisaie, Behold now, the place where we dwell before you is too narrow for us;
2 Kings 6:2 let us go as far as the Jordan and take from there, each man, one beam, and make for ourselves a place there to dwell. And he said, Go.
2 Kings 6:3 And one said, Please, come with your servants. And he said, I shall go.
2 Kings 6:4 And he went with them, and they came to the Jordan and were cutting the wood.
2 Kings 6:5 And behold, as one was felling the beam, the iron fell into the water; and he cried out, Alas, master, and it was borrowed.
2 Kings 6:6 And the man of God said, Where did it fall? And he showed him the place. And he broke off a piece of wood and threw it there, and the iron floated.
2 Kings 6:7 And he said, Lift it for yourself. And he stretched out his hand and took it.
2 Kings 6:8 And the king of Syria was warring against Israel and took counsel with his servants, saying, At such and such a place, elmoni, I shall encamp.
2 Kings 6:9 And Elisaie sent to the king of Israel, saying, Beware of passing through this place, for Syria is hidden there.
2 Kings 6:10 And the king of Israel sent to the place of which Elisaie had spoken to him and guarded himself from there, not once or twice.
2 Kings 6:11 And the soul of the king of Syria was shaken over this matter, and he called his servants and said to them, Will you not tell me who betrays me to the king of Israel?
2 Kings 6:12 And one of his servants said, No, my lord king, for Elisaie the prophet in Israel tells the king of Israel all the words you speak in the storeroom of your bedchamber.
2 Kings 6:13 And he said, Go, see where he is, and I shall send and take him. And they told him, saying, Behold, he is in Dothaim.
2 Kings 6:14 And he sent there horse and chariot and a heavy force, and they came by night and surrounded the city.
2 Kings 6:15 And Elisaie's attendant rose early and went out, and behold, a force was surrounding the city, with horse and chariot, and the servant said to him, Alas, master, what shall we do?
2 Kings 6:16 And Elisaie said, Do not fear, for those with us are more than those with them.
2 Kings 6:17 And Elisaie prayed and said, Lord, open the eyes of the servant, and let him see. And the Lord opened his eyes, and he saw, and behold, the mountain was full of horses, and a chariot of fire was around Elisaie.
2 Kings 6:18 And they came down toward him, and Elisaie prayed to the Lord and said, Strike this nation with inability to see, please. And he struck them with inability to see according to the word of Elisaie.
2 Kings 6:19 And Elisaie said to them, This is not the city and this is not the road; come after me, and I shall lead you to the man whom you seek. And he led them to Samaria.
2 Kings 6:20 And it happened when they entered Samaria that Elisaie said, Open their eyes, please, Lord, and let them see. And the Lord opened their eyes, and they saw, and behold, they were in the midst of Samaria.
2 Kings 6:21 And the king of Israel said when he saw them, Shall I strike them down, father?
2 Kings 6:22 And he said, You shall not strike them. Unless you have taken them captive with your sword and your bow, do you strike them? Set bread and water before them, and let them eat and drink and go to their master.
2 Kings 6:23 And he set a great meal before them, and they ate and drank; and he sent them away, and they went to their master. And the Syrian bands no longer continued to come into the land of Israel.
2 Kings 6:24 And it happened after this that the son of Ader king of Syria gathered all his camp and went up and besieged Samaria.
2 Kings 6:25 And there was a great famine in Samaria, and behold, they were besieging it, until a donkey's head was fifty shekels of silver and a fourth of a kab of doves' dung was five shekels of silver.
2 Kings 6:26 And the king of Israel was passing along on the wall, and a woman cried out to him, saying, Save me, my lord king.
2 Kings 6:27 And he said to her, May the Lord not save you; from where shall I save you? From the threshing floor or from the winepress?
2 Kings 6:28 And the king said to her, What is the matter with you? And she said, This woman said to me, Give your son and we shall eat him today, and my son we shall eat tomorrow;
2 Kings 6:29 and we cooked my son and ate him, and I said to her on the second day, Give your son and let us eat him, but she hid her son.
2 Kings 6:30 And it happened when the king of Israel heard the woman's words that he tore his garments, and as he passed along on the wall the people saw sackcloth against his flesh underneath.
2 Kings 6:31 And he said, May God do thus to me and add thus if the head of Elisaie shall remain on him today.
2 Kings 6:32 And Elisaie was sitting in his house, and the elders were sitting with him. And he sent a man before him; before the messenger came to him, he himself said to the elders, Do you know that this son of the murderer has sent to take away my head? See, when the messenger comes, shut the door and press him back at the door; is not the sound of his master's feet behind him?
2 Kings 6:33 While he was still speaking with them, behold, a messenger came down to him and said, Behold, this evil is from the Lord; why should I wait for the Lord any longer?

## Chapter 7

2 Kings 7:1 And Elisaie said, Hear the word of the Lord: Thus says the Lord: At this time tomorrow a measure of fine flour for a shekel and two measures of barley for a shekel at the gates of Samaria.
2 Kings 7:2 And the officer upon whose hand the king leaned answered Elisaie and said, Behold, even if the Lord makes floodgates in heaven, shall this thing happen? And Elisaie said, Behold, you shall see it with your eyes, but from it you shall not eat.
2 Kings 7:3 And four men afflicted with leprosy were by the door of the city, and one said to his neighbor, Why are we sitting here until we die?
2 Kings 7:4 If we say, Let us enter the city, famine is in the city and we shall die there; and if we sit here, we shall also die. And now come, let us fall into the camp of Syria; if they preserve our lives, then we shall live, and if they put us to death, then we shall die.
2 Kings 7:5 And they arose in the darkness to enter the camp of Syria and came to the edge of the Syrian camp, and behold, there was no man there.
2 Kings 7:6 And the Lord made the camp of Syria hear the sound of a chariot and the sound of a horse and the sound of a great force, and one said to his brother, Now the king of Israel has hired against us the kings of the Chettites and the kings of Egypt to come against us.
2 Kings 7:7 And they arose and fled in the darkness and left their tents and their horses and their donkeys in the camp as it was, and fled for their lives.
2 Kings 7:8 And these men afflicted with leprosy entered as far as the edge of the camp and went into one tent and ate and drank and took from there silver and gold and clothing and went away; and they returned and entered another tent and took from there and went and hid it.
2 Kings 7:9 And one said to his neighbor, We are not doing right; this day is a day of good news, and we are silent and wait until the light of morning, and we shall find guilt; and now come, let us enter and report to the king's house.
2 Kings 7:10 And they went in and cried out to the gate of the city and reported to them, saying, We entered the Syrian camp, and behold, there is no man there and no human voice, except a tethered horse and a donkey and their tents as they were.
2 Kings 7:11 And the gatekeepers cried out and reported inside the king's house.
2 Kings 7:12 And the king arose at night and said to his servants, Let me tell you what Syria has done to us: they know that we are hungry, and they have gone out from the camp and hidden in the field, saying, They will come out of the city, and we shall catch them alive and enter the city.
2 Kings 7:13 And one of his servants answered and said, Let them take five of the horses remaining, which have been left here; behold, they are like all the multitude of Israel that is perishing. And we shall send there and see.
2 Kings 7:14 And they took two horse riders, and the king of Israel sent them after the king of Syria, saying, Go and see.
2 Kings 7:15 And they went after them as far as the Jordan, and behold, all the road was full of garments and vessels that Syria had thrown away in their alarm; and the messengers returned and reported to the king.
2 Kings 7:16 And the people went out and plundered the Syrian camp, and a measure of fine flour came to be a shekel and two measures of barley a shekel, according to the word of the Lord.
2 Kings 7:17 And the king appointed the officer upon whose hand the king leaned over the gate, and the people trampled him in the gate, and he died, as the man of God had spoken when the messenger came down to him.
2 Kings 7:18 And it happened as Elisaie had spoken to the king, saying, Two measures of barley for a shekel and a measure of fine flour for a shekel, and it shall be at this time tomorrow in the gate of Samaria;
2 Kings 7:19 and the officer answered Elisaie and said, Behold, even if the Lord makes floodgates in heaven, shall this thing happen? And Elisaie said, Behold, you shall see it with your eyes, but from it you shall not eat.
2 Kings 7:20 And it happened so, and the people trampled him in the gate, and he died.

## Chapter 8

2 Kings 8:1 And Elisaie spoke to the woman whose son he had revived, saying, Arise and go, you and your household, and sojourn wherever you may sojourn, for the Lord has called a famine upon the land, and indeed it has come upon the land for seven years.
2 Kings 8:2 And the woman arose and did according to the word of Elisaie and went, she and her household, and sojourned in the land of the foreigners for seven years.
2 Kings 8:3 And it happened at the end of the seven years that the woman returned from the land of the foreigners to the city and came to cry out to the king concerning her house and her fields.
2 Kings 8:4 And the king was speaking to Giezi, the servant of Elisaie the man of God, saying, Tell me, please, all the great things that Elisaie did.
2 Kings 8:5 And it happened as he was telling the king how he had revived a dead son that, behold, the woman whose son Elisaie had revived was crying out to the king concerning her house and her fields; and Giezi said, My lord king, this is the woman and this is her son whom Elisaie revived.
2 Kings 8:6 And the king questioned the woman, and she told him; and the king gave her a eunuch, saying, Restore all that belongs to her and all the produce of her field from the day she left the land until now.
2 Kings 8:7 And Elisaie came to Damascus, and the son of Ader king of Syria was ill, and they told him, saying, The man of God has come here.
2 Kings 8:8 And the king said to Azael, Take manaa in your hand and go to meet the man of God and inquire of the Lord from him, saying, Shall I live from this illness of mine?
2 Kings 8:9 And Azael went to meet him and took manaa in his hand and all the good things of Damascus, a load of forty camels, and came and stood before him and said to Elisaie, Your son, the son of Ader king of Syria, has sent me to you, saying, Shall I live from this illness of mine?
2 Kings 8:10 And Elisaie said, Go, say to him, You shall surely live; and the Lord has shown me that you shall surely die.
2 Kings 8:11 And he stood before his face and fixed it until shame, and the man of God wept.
2 Kings 8:12 And Azael said, Why does my lord weep? And he said, Because I know what evil things you will do to the sons of Israel: you will send their fortresses into fire and kill their chosen men with the sword and dash their infants and tear open their pregnant women.
2 Kings 8:13 And Azael said, What is your servant, the dead dog, that he should do this thing? And Elisaie said, The Lord has shown me you reigning over Syria.
2 Kings 8:14 And he departed from Elisaie and went in to his master, and he said to him, What did Elisaie say to you? And he said, He said to me, You shall surely live.
2 Kings 8:15 And it happened on the next day that he took the machma and dipped it in water and laid it upon his face, and he died, and Azael reigned in his stead.
2 Kings 8:16 In the fifth year of Joram son of Achaab king of Israel, Joram son of Josaphat reigned as king of Judah.
2 Kings 8:17 He was a son of thirty-two years when he began to reign, and he reigned eight years in Jerusalem.
2 Kings 8:18 And he walked in the way of the kings of Israel, as the house of Achaab had done, for a daughter of Achaab was his wife; and he did evil before the Lord.
2 Kings 8:19 And the Lord was unwilling to destroy Judah because of David his servant, as he had said he would give a lamp to him and to his sons all the days.
2 Kings 8:20 In his days Edom rebelled from under the hand of Judah and they set a king over themselves.
2 Kings 8:21 And Joram went up to Sior with all the chariots with him, and it happened when he arose that he struck Edom that had surrounded him and the commanders of the chariots, and the people fled to their tents.
2 Kings 8:22 And Edom rebelled from under the hand of Judah until this day. Then Lobena rebelled at that time.
2 Kings 8:23 And the rest of the deeds of Joram and all that he did, behold, are these not written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Judah?
2 Kings 8:24 And Joram slept with his fathers and was buried with his fathers in the city of David his father; and Ochozias his son reigned in his stead.
2 Kings 8:25 In the twelfth year of Joram son of Achaab king of Israel, Ochozias son of Joram reigned.
2 Kings 8:26 Ochozias was a son of twenty-two years when he began to reign, and he reigned one year in Jerusalem; and his mother's name was Gotholia daughter of Ambri king of Israel.
2 Kings 8:27 And he walked in the way of the house of Achaab and did evil before the Lord as the house of Achaab had done.
2 Kings 8:28 And he went with Joram son of Achaab to war against Azael king of the foreigners at Remmoth Galaad, and the Syrians struck Joram.
2 Kings 8:29 And King Joram returned to be healed in Jezrael from the wounds with which they had struck him at Remmoth when he fought against Azael king of Syria; and Ochozias son of Joram went down to see Joram son of Achaab in Jezrael, because he was ill.

## Chapter 9

2 Kings 9:1 And Elisaie the prophet called one of the sons of the prophets and said to him, Gird your waist and take this flask of oil in your hand and go to Remmoth Galaad;
2 Kings 9:2 and enter there and see there Jou son of Josaphat son of Namessi, and enter and raise him from among his brothers and bring him into the innermost storeroom;
2 Kings 9:3 and take the flask of oil and pour it upon his head and say, Thus says the Lord: I have anointed you king over Israel. And open the door and flee and do not remain.
2 Kings 9:4 And the young man, the prophet, went to Remmoth Galaad
2 Kings 9:5 and entered, and behold, the commanders of the force were sitting, and he said, I have a word for you, commander. And Jou said, For which of all of us? And he said, For you, commander.
2 Kings 9:6 And he arose and entered the house, and he poured the oil upon his head and said to him, Thus says the Lord God of Israel: I have anointed you king over the people of the Lord, over Israel,
2 Kings 9:7 and you shall destroy the house of Achaab your master from before me and avenge the blood of my servants the prophets and the blood of all the servants of the Lord at the hand of Jezabel
2 Kings 9:8 and at the hand of the whole house of Achaab, and you shall destroy from the house of Achaab anyone who urinates against a wall, and one held and one left in Israel;
2 Kings 9:9 and I shall make the house of Achaab like the house of Jeroboam son of Nabat and like the house of Baasa son of Achia;
2 Kings 9:10 and the dogs shall devour Jezabel in the portion of Jezrael, and there shall be no one to bury her. And he opened the door and fled.
2 Kings 9:11 And Jou came out to his master's servants, and they said to him, Is it peace? Why did this afflicted man enter to you? And he said to them, You know the man and his chatter.
2 Kings 9:12 And they said, Wrong; tell us, please. And Jou said to them, Thus and thus he spoke to me, saying, Thus says the Lord: I have anointed you king over Israel.
2 Kings 9:13 And when they heard, they hurried and each took his garment and placed it beneath him upon the garem of the steps, and sounded a horn and said, Jou has become king.
2 Kings 9:14 And Jou son of Josaphat son of Namessi conspired against Joram; and Joram himself was keeping guard at Remmoth Galaad, he and all Israel, against Azael king of Syria,
2 Kings 9:15 and King Joram had returned to be healed in Jezrael from the wounds with which the Syrians struck him when he fought against Azael king of Syria; and Jou said, If your heart is with me, let no one escape from the city to go and report in Jezrael.
2 Kings 9:16 And Jou rode and went and came down to Jezrael, for Joram king of Israel was being treated in Jezrael for the arrow wounds with which the Aramin had shot him in Rammath in the war with Azael king of Syria, for he was mighty and a man of strength; and Ochozias king of Judah had come down to see Joram.
2 Kings 9:17 And the watchman went up on the tower in Jezrael and saw the dust cloud of Jou as he approached and said, I see a dust cloud. And Joram said, Take a rider and send him before them, and let him say, Is it peace?
2 Kings 9:18 And a horse rider went to meet them and said, Thus says the king: Is it peace? And Jou said, What have you to do with peace? Turn behind me. And the watchman reported, saying, The messenger came to them and did not return.
2 Kings 9:19 And he sent a second horse rider, and he came to him and said, Thus says the king: Is it peace? And Jou said, What have you to do with peace? Turn behind me.
2 Kings 9:20 And the watchman reported, saying, He came to them and did not return; and the driver drives like Jou son of Namessi, for it has become a deviation.
2 Kings 9:21 And Joram said, Harness. And he harnessed a chariot. And Joram king of Israel and Ochozias king of Judah went out, each in his chariot, and went out to meet Jou and found him in the portion of Nabouthai the Jezraelite.
2 Kings 9:22 And it happened when Joram saw Jou that he said, Is it peace, Jou? And Jou said, What peace, while the prostitutions of Jezabel your mother and her many sorceries remain?
2 Kings 9:23 And Joram turned his hands to flee and said to Ochozias, Treachery, Ochozias.
2 Kings 9:24 And Jou filled his hand with the bow and struck Joram between his arms, and the arrow went out through his heart, and he sank upon his knees.
2 Kings 9:25 And Jou said to Badekar his officer, Throw him into the portion of the field of Nabouthai the Jezraelite; for I remember, you and I riding in teams behind Achaab his father, and the Lord laid this pronouncement upon him, saying,
2 Kings 9:26 Surely I saw yesterday the blood of Nabouthai and the blood of his sons, says the Lord, and I shall repay him in this portion, says the Lord. And now lift him, please, and throw him into the portion according to the word of the Lord.
2 Kings 9:27 And Ochozias king of Judah saw and fled by the road of Baithaggan, and Jou pursued after him and said, Him too! And he struck him in the chariot on the ascent to Gai, which is Jeblaam, and he fled to Mageddon and died there.
2 Kings 9:28 And his servants put him on the chariot and brought him to Jerusalem and buried him in his tomb in the city of David.
2 Kings 9:29 And in the eleventh year of Joram king of Israel, Ochozias reigned over Judah.
2 Kings 9:30 And Jou came to Jezrael; and Jezabel heard and painted her eyes and adorned her head and looked out through the window.
2 Kings 9:31 And Jou was entering the city, and she said, Is it peace, Zambri, murderer of his master?
2 Kings 9:32 And he lifted his face toward the window and saw her and said, Who are you? Come down with me. And two eunuchs leaned out toward him;
2 Kings 9:33 and he said, Roll her down. And they rolled her down, and some of her blood was spattered on the wall and on the horses, and they trampled her.
2 Kings 9:34 And Jou went in and ate and drank and said, Attend to this cursed woman, please, and bury her, for she is a king's daughter.
2 Kings 9:35 And they went to bury her and found nothing of her except the skull and the feet and the traces of the hands.
2 Kings 9:36 And they returned and told him, and he said, It is the word of the Lord that he spoke by the hand of his servant Eliou the Thesbite, saying, In the portion of Jezrael the dogs shall devour the flesh of Jezabel,
2 Kings 9:37 and the corpse of Jezabel shall be like dung on the face of the field in the portion of Jezrael, so that they cannot say, Jezabel.

## Chapter 10

2 Kings 10:1 And Achaab had seventy sons in Samaria. And Jou wrote a letter and sent it into Samaria to the rulers of Samaria and to the elders and to the guardians of Achaab's sons, saying,
2 Kings 10:2 And now when this letter comes to you, your master's sons are with you, and chariot and horses and fortified cities and weapons are with you;
2 Kings 10:3 see the good and upright one among your master's sons and set him on his father's throne and fight for your master's house.
2 Kings 10:4 And they were greatly afraid and said, Behold, the two kings did not stand before him, and how shall we stand?
2 Kings 10:5 And those over the house and those over the city and the elders and the guardians sent to Jou, saying, We are your servants, and whatever you say to us we shall do; we shall make no man king; we shall do what is good in your eyes.
2 Kings 10:6 And he wrote a second letter to them, saying, If you are for me and listen to my voice, take the heads of the men, your master's sons, and bring them to me at this time tomorrow in Jezrael. And the king's sons were seventy men; the great men of the city were raising them.
2 Kings 10:7 And it happened when the letter came to them that they took the king's sons and slaughtered them, seventy men, and put their heads in baskets and sent them to him in Jezrael.
2 Kings 10:8 And the messenger came and reported, saying, They have brought the heads of the king's sons. And he said, Put them in two heaps by the entrance of the gate until morning.
2 Kings 10:9 And it happened in the morning that he went out and stood in the gateway of the city and said to all the people, You are righteous. Behold, I conspired against my master and killed him; but who struck all these?
2 Kings 10:10 See, affo, that none of the word of the Lord that the Lord spoke against the house of Achaab shall fall to the ground; and the Lord has done all that he spoke by the hand of his servant Eliou.
2 Kings 10:11 And Jou struck all who remained of the house of Achaab in Jezrael and all his great men and his acquaintances and his priests, so as to leave him no remnant.
2 Kings 10:12 And he arose and went to Samaria. He was at Baithakad of the shepherds on the road,
2 Kings 10:13 and Jou found the brothers of Ochozias king of Judah and said, Who are you? And they said, We are the brothers of Ochozias, and we have come down for the peace of the king's sons and the sons of the ruling woman.
2 Kings 10:14 And he said, Seize them alive. And they seized them alive. And they slaughtered them at Baithakad, forty-two men; he left no man of them.
2 Kings 10:15 And he went from there and found Jonadab son of Rechab on the road to meet him, and he greeted him. And Jou said to him, Is your heart upright with my heart as my heart is with your heart? And Jonadab said, It is. And Jou said, If it is, give me your hand. And he gave his hand, and he brought him up to him upon the chariot
2 Kings 10:16 and said to him, Come with me and see me in my zeal for the Lord Sabaoth. And he seated him in his chariot.
2 Kings 10:17 And he entered Samaria and struck all who remained of Achaab in Samaria until he had destroyed him, according to the word of the Lord that he spoke to Eliou.
2 Kings 10:18 And Jou gathered all the people and said to them, Achaab served Baal a little, but Jou will serve him much;
2 Kings 10:19 and now call to me all the prophets of Baal, all his servants and his priests; let no man be missing, for I have a great sacrifice for Baal; anyone missing shall not live. And Jou acted with deceit, in order to destroy the servants of Baal.
2 Kings 10:20 And Jou said, Consecrate a sacrifice for Baal. And they proclaimed it.
2 Kings 10:21 And Jou sent throughout all Israel, saying, And now all the servants of Baal and all his priests and all his prophets, let none be left out, for I am making a great sacrifice; anyone left out shall not live. And all Baal's servants and all his priests and all his prophets came; not a man was left who did not come. And they entered the house of Baal, and the house of Baal was filled from end to end.
2 Kings 10:22 And Jou said to the one over the house of mesthaal, Bring out garments for all Baal's servants. And the keeper of garments brought them out for them.
2 Kings 10:23 And Jou and Jonadab son of Rechab entered the house of Baal and said to Baal's servants, Search and see whether any of the Lord's servants are among you, but only Baal's servants alone.
2 Kings 10:24 And he entered to perform the sacrifices and the whole burnt offerings. And Jou stationed for himself eighty men outside and said, Any man who escapes from the men whom I bring into your hands, his life shall be in place of his life.
2 Kings 10:25 And it happened when he finished performing the whole burnt offering that Jou said to the runners and the officers, Enter and strike them; let no man come out from among them. And they struck them with the edge of the sword, and the runners and the officers threw them down and went as far as the city of the house of Baal.
2 Kings 10:26 And they brought out the pillar of Baal and burned it.
2 Kings 10:27 And they pulled down the pillars of Baal and demolished the house of Baal and made it into latrines until this day.
2 Kings 10:28 And Jou destroyed Baal from Israel;
2 Kings 10:29 but Jou did not depart from the sins of Jeroboam son of Nabat, who caused Israel to sin: the golden heifers in Bethel and in Dan.
2 Kings 10:30 And the Lord said to Jou, Because you did well to do what was right in my eyes and did to the house of Achaab all that was in my heart, sons to the fourth generation shall sit for you on the throne of Israel.
2 Kings 10:31 And Jou did not take care to walk in the law of the Lord God of Israel with all his heart; he did not depart from the sins of Jeroboam son of Nabat, who caused Israel to sin.
2 Kings 10:32 In those days the Lord began to cut Israel down, and Azael struck them throughout all the territory of Israel,
2 Kings 10:33 from the Jordan toward the rising of the sun, all the land of Galaad of Gad and Reuben and Manasseh, from Aroer, which is on the bank of the torrent Arnon, and Galaad and Basan.
2 Kings 10:34 And the rest of the deeds of Jou and all that he did and all his acts of power and the alliances that he made, are these not written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Israel?
2 Kings 10:35 And Jou slept with his fathers, and they buried him in Samaria; and Joachas his son reigned in his stead.
2 Kings 10:36 And the days that Jou reigned over Israel were twenty-eight years in Samaria.

## Chapter 11

2 Kings 11:1 And Gotholia the mother of Ochozias saw that her sons had died, and she destroyed all the seed of the kingdom.
2 Kings 11:2 And Josabee daughter of King Joram, sister of Ochozias, took Joas the son of her brother and stole him from among the king's sons who were being put to death, him and his nurse, in the storeroom of the beds; and she hid him from Gotholia, and he was not put to death.
2 Kings 11:3 And he was hidden with her in the house of the Lord for six years, while Gotholia reigned over the land.
2 Kings 11:4 And in the seventh year Jodae the priest sent and took the captains of hundreds, Chorri and Rasim, and brought them to him into the house of the Lord and made with them a covenant of the Lord and put them under oath before the Lord; and Jodae showed them the king's son
2 Kings 11:5 and commanded them, saying, This is the thing that you shall do: let a third of you come in on the sabbath and keep guard of the king's house in the gateway,
2 Kings 11:6 and a third at the gate of the roads and a third at the gate behind the runners; and you shall keep guard of the house;
2 Kings 11:7 and two divisions among you, everyone going out on the sabbath, shall keep guard of the house of the Lord for the king;
2 Kings 11:8 and surround the king all around, each man with his equipment in his hand, and whoever enters the saderoth shall die. And be with the king when he goes out and when he comes in.
2 Kings 11:9 And the captains of hundreds did all that Jodae the wise commanded, and each man took his men who came in on the sabbath with those who went out on the sabbath and came to Jodae the priest.
2 Kings 11:10 And the priest gave the captains of hundreds the seiromastai and the trissoi of King David that were in the house of the Lord.
2 Kings 11:11 And the runners stood, each with his equipment in his hand, from the shoulder of the house on the right to the shoulder of the house on the left of the altar and the house, all around the king.
2 Kings 11:12 And he brought out the king's son and put upon him the nezer and the testimony and made him king and anointed him, and they clapped their hands and said, Let the king live.
2 Kings 11:13 And Gotholia heard the sound of the people running and came in to the people in the house of the Lord.
2 Kings 11:14 And she saw, and behold, the king stood by the pillar according to the custom, and the singers and the trumpets were beside the king, and all the people of the land were rejoicing and sounding trumpets; and Gotholia tore her garments and cried out, Conspiracy, conspiracy.
2 Kings 11:15 And Jodae the priest commanded the captains of hundreds, the overseers of the force, and said to them, Bring her out within the saderoth, and whoever enters after her shall surely be put to death by the sword; for the priest said, Let her not die in the house of the Lord.
2 Kings 11:16 And they laid hands on her, and she entered by the road of the horses' entrance of the king's house and died there.
2 Kings 11:17 And Jodae made a covenant between the Lord and the king and the people, that they should be a people for the Lord, and between the king and the people.
2 Kings 11:18 And all the people of the land entered the house of Baal and pulled it down and thoroughly shattered its altars and its images, and they killed Matthan the priest of Baal before the altars, and the priest appointed overseers for the house of the Lord.
2 Kings 11:19 And he took the captains of hundreds and Chorri and Rasim and all the people of the land, and they brought the king down from the house of the Lord, and he entered by the road of the gate of the runners of the king's house, and they seated him upon the throne of the kings.
2 Kings 11:20 And all the people of the land rejoiced, and the city was quiet; and they put Gotholia to death with the sword in the king's house.

## Chapter 12

2 Kings 12:1 Joas was a son of seven years when he began to reign.
2 Kings 12:2 In the seventh year of Jou, Joas reigned, and he reigned forty years in Jerusalem; and his mother's name was Abia from Bersabee.
2 Kings 12:3 And Joas did what was right before the Lord all the days in which Jodae the priest enlightened him;
2 Kings 12:4 but the high places were not removed, and the people still sacrificed and burned incense on the high places there.
2 Kings 12:5 And Joas said to the priests, All the silver of the holy things that is brought into the house of the Lord, silver of assessment, each man's silver received for assessment, all the silver that comes into a man's heart to bring into the house of the Lord,
2 Kings 12:6 let the priests take for themselves, each from his sale, and they themselves shall strengthen the bedek of the house wherever bedek is found there.
2 Kings 12:7 And it happened in the twenty-third year of King Joas that the priests had not strengthened the bedek of the house.
2 Kings 12:8 And King Joas called Jodae the priest and the priests and said to them, Why do you not strengthen the bedek of the house? And now do not take silver from your sales, for you shall give it for the bedek of the house.
2 Kings 12:9 And the priests agreed not to take silver from the people and not to strengthen the bedek of the house.
2 Kings 12:10 And Jodae the priest took one chest and bored a hole in its board and placed it beside iamibin in the house of the man of the house of the Lord, and the priests who kept the station gave all the silver found in the house of the Lord.
2 Kings 12:11 And it happened when they saw that there was much silver in the chest that the king's scribe and the high priest went up and tied up and counted the silver found in the house of the Lord.
2 Kings 12:12 And they gave the prepared silver into the hands of those doing the work of the overseers of the house of the Lord, and they paid it out to the woodworkers and to the builders working in the house of the Lord
2 Kings 12:13 and to the wall builders and to the stonecutters to buy wood and hewn stones to attend to the bedek of the house of the Lord in all that was spent on the house to strengthen it;
2 Kings 12:14 but silver doors, nails, bowls and trumpets, any gold vessel or silver vessel, were not made for the house of the Lord from the silver brought into the house of the Lord,
2 Kings 12:15 for they gave it to those doing the work, and with it they strengthened the house of the Lord.
2 Kings 12:16 And they did not reckon with the men into whose hands they gave the silver to give to those doing the work, for they acted faithfully.
2 Kings 12:17 Silver for sin and silver for wrongdoing, whatever was brought into the house of the Lord, belonged to the priests.
2 Kings 12:18 Then Azael king of Syria went up and fought against Geth and took it first. And Azael set his face to go up against Jerusalem.
2 Kings 12:19 And Joas king of Judah took all the holy things that Josaphat and Joram and Ochozias, his fathers and kings of Judah, had consecrated, and his own holy things and all the gold found in the treasuries of the house of the Lord and the king's house, and sent them to Azael king of Syria, and he went up from Jerusalem.
2 Kings 12:20 And the rest of the deeds of Joas and all that he did, behold, are these not written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Judah?
2 Kings 12:21 And his servants arose and bound every conspiracy and struck Joas in the house of Mallo in Gaalla.
2 Kings 12:22 And Jezechar son of Jemouath and Jezebouth his son Somer, his servants, struck him, and he died; and they buried him with his fathers in the city of David, and Amessias his son reigned in his stead.

## Chapter 13

2 Kings 13:1 In the twenty-third year of Joas son of Ochozias king of Judah, Joachas son of Jou reigned in Samaria for seventeen years.
2 Kings 13:2 And he did evil in the eyes of the Lord and followed the sins of Jeroboam son of Nabat, who caused Israel to sin; he did not depart from them.
2 Kings 13:3 And the Lord was angry with wrath against Israel and gave them into the hand of Azael king of Syria and into the hand of the son of Ader son of Azael all the days.
2 Kings 13:4 And Joachas entreated the face of the Lord, and the Lord heard him, for he saw the affliction of Israel, for the king of Syria oppressed them.
2 Kings 13:5 And the Lord gave deliverance to Israel, and it went out from under the hand of Syria, and the sons of Israel dwelt in their tents as yesterday and the day before;
2 Kings 13:6 but they did not depart from the sins of the house of Jeroboam, who caused Israel to sin; in them they walked, and indeed the grove remained standing in Samaria.
2 Kings 13:7 For no people were left to Joachas except fifty horsemen and ten chariots and ten thousand foot soldiers, for the king of Syria had destroyed them and made them like dust for trampling.
2 Kings 13:8 And the rest of the deeds of Joachas and all that he did and his acts of power, are these not written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Israel?
2 Kings 13:9 And Joachas slept with his fathers, and they buried him with his fathers in Samaria, and Joas his son reigned in his stead.
2 Kings 13:10 In the thirty-seventh year of Joas king of Judah, Joas son of Joachas reigned over Israel in Samaria for sixteen years.
2 Kings 13:11 And he did evil in the eyes of the Lord; he did not depart from any of the sin of Jeroboam son of Nabat, who caused Israel to sin; in them he walked.
2 Kings 13:12 And the rest of the deeds of Joas and all that he did and his acts of power that he performed with Amessias king of Judah, are these not written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Israel?
2 Kings 13:13 And Joas slept with his fathers, and Jeroboam sat on his throne in Samaria with the sons of Israel.
2 Kings 13:14 And Elisaie became ill with the illness from which he died. And Joas king of Israel came down to him and wept upon his face and said, Father, father, chariot of Israel and its horseman.
2 Kings 13:15 And Elisaie said to him, Take a bow and arrows. And he took a bow and arrows to him.
2 Kings 13:16 And he said to the king, Put your hand upon the bow. And Joas put his hand upon the bow, and Elisaie placed his hands upon the king's hands.
2 Kings 13:17 And he said, Open the window toward the east. And he opened it. And Elisaie said, Shoot. And he shot. And he said, An arrow of deliverance for the Lord and an arrow of deliverance in Syria, and you shall strike Syria at Aphek until its end.
2 Kings 13:18 And Elisaie said to him, Take bows. And he took them. And he said to the king of Israel, Strike the ground. And the king struck three times and stopped.
2 Kings 13:19 And the man of God was grieved over him and said, If you had struck five or six times, then you would have struck Syria until its end; but now you shall strike Syria three times.
2 Kings 13:20 And Elisaie died, and they buried him. And bands of Moab came into the land at the coming of the year;
2 Kings 13:21 and it happened as they were burying a man that, behold, they saw the band and threw the man into Elisaie's tomb, and he went and touched Elisaie's bones and lived and stood upon his feet.
2 Kings 13:22 And Azael oppressed Israel all the days of Joachas.
2 Kings 13:23 And the Lord had mercy on them and pitied them and looked toward them because of his covenant with Abraham and Isaac and Jacob, and the Lord did not wish to destroy them and did not cast them away from his face.
2 Kings 13:24 And Azael king of Syria died, and the son of Ader his son reigned in his stead.
2 Kings 13:25 And Joas son of Joachas returned and took the cities from the hand of the son of Ader son of Azael, which he had taken from the hand of Joachas his father in war; three times Joas struck him and restored the cities of Israel.

## Chapter 14

2 Kings 14:1 In the second year of Joas son of Joachas king of Israel, Amessias son of Joas reigned as king of Judah.
2 Kings 14:2 He was a son of twenty-five years when he began to reign, and he reigned twenty-nine years in Jerusalem; and his mother's name was Joadin from Jerusalem.
2 Kings 14:3 And he did what was right in the eyes of the Lord, though not like David his father; he did according to all that Joas his father had done;
2 Kings 14:4 but he did not remove the high places; the people still sacrificed and burned incense on the high places.
2 Kings 14:5 And it happened when the kingdom grew strong in his hand that he struck his servants who had struck his father;
2 Kings 14:6 but he did not put the sons of those who struck him to death, as it is written in the book of the laws of Moses, as the Lord commanded, saying, Fathers shall not die for sons, and sons shall not die for fathers, but each shall die for his own sins.
2 Kings 14:7 He struck Edom in Gaimele, ten thousand, and seized Petra in the war and called its name Kathoel until this day.
2 Kings 14:8 Then Amessias sent messengers to Joas son of Joachas son of Jou king of Israel, saying, Come, let us see each other face to face.
2 Kings 14:9 And Joas king of Israel sent to Amessias king of Judah, saying, The thorn in Lebanon sent to the cedar in Lebanon, saying, Give your daughter to my son as a wife; and the beasts of the field in Lebanon passed through and trampled the thorn.
2 Kings 14:10 Striking, you struck Idoumaia, and your heart lifted you up; be glorified while sitting in your house, and why do you strive in your wickedness? You shall fall, you and Judah with you.
2 Kings 14:11 And Amessias did not listen. And the king of Israel went up, and he and Amessias king of Judah saw each other face to face at Baithsamys of Judah;
2 Kings 14:12 and Judah stumbled before Israel, and each man fled to his tent;
2 Kings 14:13 and Joas son of Joachas king of Israel seized Amessias son of Joas son of Ochozias king of Judah at Baithsamys. And he came to Jerusalem and pulled down four hundred cubits of the wall of Jerusalem from the gate of Ephraim to the corner gate;
2 Kings 14:14 and he took the gold and the silver and all the vessels found in the house of the Lord and in the treasuries of the king's house and the sons of the minglings and returned to Samaria.
2 Kings 14:15 And the rest of the deeds of Joas, what he did in his power, how he fought with Amessias king of Judah, are these not written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Israel?
2 Kings 14:16 And Joas slept with his fathers and was buried in Samaria with the kings of Israel, and Jeroboam his son reigned in his stead.
2 Kings 14:17 And Amessias son of Joas king of Judah lived fifteen years after the death of Joas son of Joachas king of Israel.
2 Kings 14:18 And the rest of the deeds of Amessias and all that he did, are these not written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Judah?
2 Kings 14:19 And they formed a conspiracy against him in Jerusalem, and he fled to Lachis; and they sent after him to Lachis and put him to death there.
2 Kings 14:20 And they carried him on horses, and he was buried in Jerusalem with his fathers in the city of David.
2 Kings 14:21 And all the people of Judah took Azarias, who was a son of sixteen years, and made him king in place of his father Amessias.
2 Kings 14:22 He built Ailoth and restored it to Judah after the king slept with his fathers.
2 Kings 14:23 In the fifteenth year of Amessias son of Joas king of Judah, Jeroboam son of Joas reigned over Israel in Samaria for forty-one years.
2 Kings 14:24 And he did evil before the Lord; he did not depart from all the sins of Jeroboam son of Nabat, who caused Israel to sin.
2 Kings 14:25 He restored the border of Israel from the entrance of Aimath as far as the sea of the Araba, according to the word of the Lord God of Israel that he spoke by the hand of his servant Jona son of Amathi, the prophet from Gethchober.
2 Kings 14:26 For the Lord saw the humiliation of Israel, very bitter, and the few who were held and those who lacked and those left behind, and there was no one helping Israel.
2 Kings 14:27 And the Lord had not spoken of wiping out the seed of Israel from under heaven, and he saved them by the hand of Jeroboam son of Joas.
2 Kings 14:28 And the rest of the deeds of Jeroboam and all that he did and his acts of power, how he fought and how he restored Damascus and Aimath to Judah in Israel, are these not written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Israel?
2 Kings 14:29 And Jeroboam slept with his fathers, with the kings of Israel, and Azarias son of Amessias reigned in place of his father.

## Chapter 15

2 Kings 15:1 In the twenty-seventh year of Jeroboam king of Israel, Azarias son of Amessias king of Judah reigned.
2 Kings 15:2 He was a son of sixteen years when he began to reign, and he reigned fifty-two years in Jerusalem; and his mother's name was Chalia from Jerusalem.
2 Kings 15:3 And he did what was right in the eyes of the Lord according to all that Amessias his father had done;
2 Kings 15:4 but he did not remove the high places; the people still sacrificed and burned incense on the high places.
2 Kings 15:5 And the Lord touched the king, and he was afflicted with leprosy until the day of his death and reigned in the house of affousoth, and Joatham the king's son was over the house, judging the people of the land.
2 Kings 15:6 And the rest of the deeds of Azarias and all that he did, behold, are these not written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Judah?
2 Kings 15:7 And Azarias slept with his fathers, and they buried him with his fathers in the city of David, and Joatham his son reigned in his stead.
2 Kings 15:8 In the thirty-eighth year of Azarias king of Judah, Zacharias son of Jeroboam reigned over Israel in Samaria for six months.
2 Kings 15:9 And he did evil in the eyes of the Lord, as his fathers had done; he did not depart from the sins of Jeroboam son of Nabat, who caused Israel to sin.
2 Kings 15:10 And Selloum son of Jabis and Keblaam conspired against him and struck him and put him to death, and Selloum reigned in his stead.
2 Kings 15:11 And the rest of the deeds of Zacharias, behold, they are written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Israel.
2 Kings 15:12 The word of the Lord that he spoke to Jou, saying, Sons to the fourth generation shall sit for you on the throne of Israel; and so it happened.
2 Kings 15:13 And Selloum son of Jabis reigned; and in the thirty-ninth year of Azarias king of Judah, Selloum reigned for a month of days in Samaria.
2 Kings 15:14 And Manaem son of Gaddi went up from Tharsila and came to Samaria and struck Selloum son of Jabis in Samaria and put him to death.
2 Kings 15:15 And the rest of the deeds of Selloum and the conspiracy that he formed, behold, they are written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Israel.
2 Kings 15:16 Then Manaem struck Thersa and all within it and its territories from Thersa, because they did not open to him; and he struck it and tore open its pregnant women.
2 Kings 15:17 In the thirty-ninth year of Azarias king of Judah, Manaem son of Gaddi reigned over Israel for ten years in Samaria.
2 Kings 15:18 And he did evil in the eyes of the Lord; he did not depart from all the sins of Jeroboam son of Nabat, who caused Israel to sin.
2 Kings 15:19 In his days Phoul king of the Assyrians went up against the land, and Manaem gave Phoul a thousand talents of silver so that his hand would be with him.
2 Kings 15:20 And Manaem brought out the silver upon Israel, upon every man mighty in strength, to give to the king of the Assyrians, fifty shekels per man; and the king of the Assyrians returned and did not stay there in the land.
2 Kings 15:21 And the rest of the deeds of Manaem and all that he did, behold, are these not written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Israel?
2 Kings 15:22 And Manaem slept with his fathers, and Phakeias his son reigned in his stead.
2 Kings 15:23 In the fiftieth year of Azarias king of Judah, Phakeias son of Manaem reigned over Israel in Samaria for two years.
2 Kings 15:24 And he did evil in the eyes of the Lord; he did not depart from the sins of Jeroboam son of Nabat, who caused Israel to sin.
2 Kings 15:25 And Phakee son of Romeliou his officer conspired against him and struck him in Samaria before the king's house, with Argob and Aria, and with him fifty men of the four hundred; and he put him to death and reigned in his stead.
2 Kings 15:26 And the rest of the deeds of Phakeias and all that he did, behold, they are written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Israel.
2 Kings 15:27 In the fifty-second year of Azarias king of Judah, Phakee son of Romeliou reigned over Israel in Samaria for twenty years.
2 Kings 15:28 And he did evil in the eyes of the Lord; he did not depart from all the sins of Jeroboam son of Nabat, who caused Israel to sin.
2 Kings 15:29 In the days of Phakee king of Israel, Thaglathphellasar king of the Assyrians came and took Ain and Abelbaithamaacha and Janoch and Kenez and Asor and Galaad and Galilaia, all the land of Nephthali, and deported them to the Assyrians.
2 Kings 15:30 And Osee son of Ela formed a conspiracy against Phakee son of Romeliou and struck him and put him to death and reigned in his stead in the twentieth year of Joatham son of Azarias.
2 Kings 15:31 And the rest of the deeds of Phakee and all that he did, behold, they are written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Israel.
2 Kings 15:32 In the second year of Phakee son of Romeliou king of Israel, Joatham son of Azarias king of Judah reigned.
2 Kings 15:33 He was a son of twenty-five years when he began to reign, and he reigned sixteen years in Jerusalem; and his mother's name was Jerousa daughter of Sadok.
2 Kings 15:34 And he did what was right in the eyes of the Lord according to all that Ozias his father had done;
2 Kings 15:35 but he did not remove the high places; the people still sacrificed and burned incense on the high places. He built the upper gate of the house of the Lord.
2 Kings 15:36 And the rest of the deeds of Joatham and all that he did, are these not written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Judah?
2 Kings 15:37 In those days the Lord began to send against Judah Raasson king of Syria and Phakee son of Romeliou.
2 Kings 15:38 And Joatham slept with his fathers and was buried with his fathers in the city of David his father, and Achaz his son reigned in his stead.

## Chapter 16

2 Kings 16:1 In the seventeenth year of Phakee son of Romeliou, Achaz son of Joatham king of Judah reigned.
2 Kings 16:2 Achaz was a son of twenty years when he began to reign, and he reigned sixteen years in Jerusalem. And he did not faithfully do what was right in the eyes of the Lord his God as David his father had done,
2 Kings 16:3 and he walked in the way of Jeroboam son of Nabat king of Israel and even made his son pass through fire according to the abominations of the nations whom the Lord had removed before the sons of Israel,
2 Kings 16:4 and he sacrificed and burned incense on the high places and on the hills and under every wooded tree.
