2 Kings 16:5 Then Raasson king of Syria and Phakee son of Romeliou king of Israel went up to Jerusalem for war and besieged Achaz, but they were unable to fight.
2 Kings 16:6 At that time Raasson king of Syria restored Ailath to Syria and drove the Judeans out of Ailath, and Idoumaians came to Ailath and lived there until this day.
2 Kings 16:7 And Achaz sent messengers to Thaglathphellasar king of the Assyrians, saying, I am your servant and your son; come up and save me from the hand of the king of Syria and from the hand of the king of Israel, who are rising against me.
2 Kings 16:8 And Achaz took the silver and the gold found in the treasuries of the house of the Lord and the king's house and sent gifts to the king.
2 Kings 16:9 And the king of the Assyrians listened to him, and the king of the Assyrians went up to Damascus and captured it and deported it and put Raasson to death.
2 Kings 16:10 And King Achaz went to meet Thaglathphellasar king of the Assyrians in Damascus. And he saw the altar in Damascus, and King Achaz sent to Ourias the priest the likeness of the altar and its pattern for all its workmanship;
2 Kings 16:11 and Ourias the priest built the altar according to all that King Achaz had sent from Damascus.
2 Kings 16:12 And the king saw the altar and went up upon it
2 Kings 16:13 and burned his whole burnt offering and his sacrifice and his drink offering and poured the blood of his peace offerings upon the altar.
2 Kings 16:14 And he brought the bronze altar that was before the Lord from before the house of the Lord, from between the altar and the house of the Lord, and placed it on the north side of the altar.
2 Kings 16:15 And King Achaz commanded Ourias the priest, saying, On the great altar offer the morning whole burnt offering and the evening sacrifice and the king's whole burnt offering and his sacrifice and the whole burnt offering of all the people and their sacrifice and their drink offering, and pour upon it all blood of a whole burnt offering and all blood of a sacrifice; and the bronze altar shall be for me for the morning.
2 Kings 16:16 And Ourias the priest did according to all that King Achaz commanded him.
2 Kings 16:17 And King Achaz cut off the fittings of the mechonoth and removed the basin from them, and took down the sea from the bronze oxen beneath it and put it upon a stone base.
2 Kings 16:18 And he built the foundation of the seat in the house of the Lord and turned the king's outer entrance in the house of the Lord because of the king of the Assyrians.
2 Kings 16:19 And the rest of the deeds of Achaz, as many as he did, are these not written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Judah?
2 Kings 16:20 And Achaz slept with his fathers and was buried in the city of David, and Ezekias his son reigned in his stead.

## Chapter 17

2 Kings 17:1 In the twelfth year of Achaz king of Judah, Osee son of Ela reigned in Samaria over Israel for nine years.
2 Kings 17:2 And he did evil in the eyes of the Lord, though not like the kings of Israel who were before him.
2 Kings 17:3 Salamanasar king of the Assyrians went up against him, and Osee became his servant and rendered manaa to him.
2 Kings 17:4 And the king of the Assyrians found wrongdoing in Osee, for he had sent messengers to Segor king of Egypt and had not brought manaa to the king of the Assyrians in that year, and the king of the Assyrians besieged him and bound him in a prison house.
2 Kings 17:5 And the king of the Assyrians went up through all the land and went up to Samaria and besieged it for three years.
2 Kings 17:6 In the ninth year of Osee, the king of the Assyrians captured Samaria and deported Israel to the Assyrians and settled them in Alae and Abor, rivers of Gozan, and the mountains of the Medes.
2 Kings 17:7 And it happened because the sons of Israel sinned against the Lord their God, who had brought them up from the land of Egypt from under the hand of Pharaoh king of Egypt, and they feared other gods
2 Kings 17:8 and walked in the ordinances of the nations whom the Lord had removed before the sons of Israel, and in those of the kings of Israel, as many as had made them,
2 Kings 17:9 and as many as the sons of Israel had clothed themselves with words that were not so against the Lord their God, and they built high places for themselves in all their cities, from a watchmen's tower to a fortified city,
2 Kings 17:10 and set up for themselves pillars and groves on every high hill and under every wooded tree
2 Kings 17:11 and burned incense there on all the high places like the nations whom the Lord had deported before them, and they made associates and carved, to provoke the Lord,
2 Kings 17:12 and served idols, concerning which the Lord had told them, You shall not do this thing to the Lord.
2 Kings 17:13 And the Lord testified to Israel and Judah by the hand of all his prophets, of every seer, saying, Turn away from your evil ways and keep my commandments and my ordinances and all the law that I commanded your fathers, all that I sent to them by the hand of my servants the prophets.
2 Kings 17:14 And they did not listen and made their back harder than the back of their fathers,
2 Kings 17:15 and they did not keep his testimonies with which he testified to them and went after vain things and became vain and after the nations around them, concerning whom he commanded them not to do as they did;
2 Kings 17:16 they abandoned the commandments of the Lord their God and made for themselves a molten image, two heifers, and made groves and bowed to all the host of heaven and served Baal
2 Kings 17:17 and made their sons and daughters pass through fire and practiced divinations and took omens and sold themselves to do evil in the eyes of the Lord, to provoke him.
2 Kings 17:18 And the Lord became very angry with Israel and removed them from before his face, and none remained except the tribe of Judah alone.
2 Kings 17:19 And even Judah did not keep the commandments of the Lord their God and walked in the ordinances of Israel that they made,
2 Kings 17:20 and they rejected the Lord among all the seed of Israel, and he shook them and gave them into the hands of those plundering them, until he cast them away from before his face.
2 Kings 17:21 For Israel departed from the house of David and made Jeroboam son of Nabat king, and Jeroboam drove Israel away from following the Lord and caused them to sin a great sin;
2 Kings 17:22 and the sons of Israel walked in all the sin of Jeroboam that he committed; they did not depart from it,
2 Kings 17:23 until the Lord removed Israel from before his face, as the Lord had spoken by the hand of all his servants the prophets, and Israel was deported from its land to the Assyrians until this day.
2 Kings 17:24 And the king of the Assyrians brought from Babylon the one from Chountha and from Aia and from Aimath and Seppharouain, and they were settled in the cities of Samaria in place of the sons of Israel and inherited Samaria and dwelt in its cities.
2 Kings 17:25 And it happened at the beginning of their dwelling there that they did not fear the Lord, and the Lord sent lions among them, and they were killing among them.
2 Kings 17:26 And they said to the king of the Assyrians, saying, The nations that you deported and settled in the cities of Samaria do not know the judgment of the God of the land, and he sent lions among them, and behold, they are killing them because they do not know the judgment of the God of the land.
2 Kings 17:27 And the king of the Assyrians commanded, saying, Bring them from there, and let them go and dwell there, and they shall teach them the judgment of the God of the land.
2 Kings 17:28 And they brought one of the priests whom they had deported from Samaria, and he dwelt in Bethel and was teaching them how to fear the Lord.
2 Kings 17:29 And the nations made, each nation, their gods and put them in the house of the high places that the Samaritans had made, each nation in its cities where they dwelt;
2 Kings 17:30 and the men of Babylon made Sokchothbainith, and the men of Chouth made Nerigel, and the men of Aimath made Asimath,
2 Kings 17:31 and the Euaioi made Eblazer and Tharthak, and the Seppharouain burned their sons in fire to Adramelech and Anemelech, gods of Seppharouain.
2 Kings 17:32 And they feared the Lord and settled their abominations in the houses of the high places that they had made in Samaria, each nation in the city in which it dwelt; and they feared the Lord and made for themselves priests of the high places and made for themselves in the house of the high places.
2 Kings 17:33 They feared the Lord and served their gods according to the custom of the nations from which he had deported them.
2 Kings 17:34 Until this day they did according to their custom; they fear and they act according to their ordinances and according to their judgment and according to the law and according to the commandment that the Lord commanded the sons of Jacob, whom he named Israel,
2 Kings 17:35 and the Lord made a covenant with them and commanded them, saying, You shall not fear other gods and shall not bow to them and shall not serve them and shall not sacrifice to them,
2 Kings 17:36 but the Lord who brought you up from the land of Egypt with great strength and an uplifted arm, him you shall fear and to him you shall bow and to him you shall sacrifice;
2 Kings 17:37 and the ordinances and the judgments and the law and the commandments that he wrote for you, you shall take care to do all the days, and you shall not fear other gods;
2 Kings 17:38 and the covenant that he made with you, you shall not forget, and you shall not fear other gods,
2 Kings 17:39 but you shall fear the Lord your God, and he will deliver you from all your enemies;
2 Kings 17:40 and you shall not listen regarding their custom that they perform.
2 Kings 17:41 And these nations feared the Lord and served their carved images, and indeed their sons and their sons' sons do as their fathers did until this day.

## Chapter 18

2 Kings 18:1 And it happened in the third year of Osee son of Ela king of Israel that Ezekias son of Achaz king of Judah reigned.
2 Kings 18:2 He was a son of twenty-five years when he began to reign, and he reigned twenty-nine years in Jerusalem; and his mother's name was Abou daughter of Zacharias.
2 Kings 18:3 And he did what was right in the eyes of the Lord according to all that David his father had done.
2 Kings 18:4 He removed the high places and crushed all the pillars and destroyed the groves and the bronze serpent that Moses had made, for until those days the sons of Israel had been burning incense to it, and he called it Neesthan.
2 Kings 18:5 He hoped in the Lord God of Israel, and after him no one like him arose among the kings of Judah or among those who were before him;
2 Kings 18:6 and he clung to the Lord, did not depart from following him, and kept his commandments, as many as he had commanded Moses;
2 Kings 18:7 and the Lord was with him; in all that he did he understood. And he rebelled against the king of the Assyrians and did not serve him.
2 Kings 18:8 He struck the foreigners as far as Gaza and its border, from a watchmen's tower as far as a fortified city.
2 Kings 18:9 And it happened in the fourth year of King Ezekias [the same year was the seventh of Osee son of Ela king of Israel] that Salamanassar king of the Assyrians went up against Samaria and besieged it;
2 Kings 18:10 and he took it at the end of three years, in the sixth year of Ezekias [the same year was the ninth of Osee king of Israel], and Samaria was captured.
2 Kings 18:11 And the king of the Assyrians deported Samaria to the Assyrians and placed them in Alae and Abor by the river Gozan and the mountains of the Medes,
2 Kings 18:12 because they had not listened to the voice of the Lord their God and had transgressed his covenant, all that Moses the servant of the Lord had commanded; and they neither listened nor did it.
2 Kings 18:13 And in the fourteenth year of King Ezekias, Sennacherim king of the Assyrians went up against the fortified cities of Judah and seized them.
2 Kings 18:14 And Ezekias king of Judah sent messengers to the king of the Assyrians at Lachis, saying, I have sinned; turn away from me; whatever you place upon me I shall bear. And the king of the Assyrians placed upon Ezekias king of Judah three hundred talents of silver and thirty talents of gold.
2 Kings 18:15 And Ezekias gave all the silver found in the house of the Lord and in the treasuries of the king's house.
2 Kings 18:16 At that time Ezekias cut off the doors of the temple of the Lord and the supports that Ezekias king of Judah had gilded, and gave them to the king of the Assyrians.
2 Kings 18:17 And the king of the Assyrians sent Tharthan and Raphis and Rapsakes from Lachis to King Ezekias with a heavy force against Jerusalem, and they went up and came to Jerusalem and stood by the aqueduct of the upper pool, which is on the road of the fuller's field.
2 Kings 18:18 And they called to Ezekias, and Eliakim son of Chelkias the steward and Somnas the scribe and Joas son of Asaph the recorder came out to him.
2 Kings 18:19 And Rapsakes said to them, Say, please, to Ezekias: Thus says the great king, king of the Assyrians: What is this trust in which you have trusted?
2 Kings 18:20 You said, Mere words of lips are counsel and strength for war. Now in whom have you trusted, that you have rebelled against me?
2 Kings 18:21 Now behold, you have trusted yourself to this broken reed staff, Egypt; if a man leans upon it, it will enter his hand and pierce it; so is Pharaoh king of Egypt to all who trust in him.
2 Kings 18:22 And if you say to me, We have trusted in the Lord God, is he not the one whose high places and altars Ezekias removed and said to Judah and Jerusalem, Before this altar you shall worship in Jerusalem?
2 Kings 18:23 And now make an agreement, please, with my master the king of the Assyrians, and I shall give you two thousand horses if you can provide riders for yourself upon them.
2 Kings 18:24 And how will you turn away the face of one district governor among the least of my master's servants? And you have trusted yourself to Egypt for chariots and horsemen.
2 Kings 18:25 And now did we come up against this place to destroy it without the Lord? The Lord said to me, Go up against this land and destroy it.
2 Kings 18:26 And Eliakim son of Chelkias and Somnas and Joas said to Rapsakes, Speak, please, to your servants in Syrian, for we understand, and do not speak with us in Judean; why speak in the ears of the people on the wall?
2 Kings 18:27 And Rapsakes said to them, Did my master send me to speak these words to your master and you? Was it not to the men sitting on the wall, to eat their dung and drink their urine together with you?
2 Kings 18:28 And Rapsakes stood and cried out in a great voice in Judean and spoke and said, Hear the words of the great king of the Assyrians:
2 Kings 18:29 Thus says the king: Let Ezekias not lift you up with words, for he shall certainly not be able to deliver you from my hand.
2 Kings 18:30 And let Ezekias not make you hope in the Lord, saying, The Lord will surely deliver us, and this city shall certainly not be given into the hand of the king of the Assyrians.
2 Kings 18:31 Do not listen to Ezekias, for thus says the king of the Assyrians: Make a blessing with me and come out to me, and each man shall drink from his vine and each man shall eat from his fig tree and drink water from his cistern,
2 Kings 18:32 until I come and take you to a land like your land, a land of grain and wine and bread and vineyards, a land of olive oil and honey, and you shall live and certainly not die. And do not listen to Ezekias, for he deceives you, saying, The Lord will rescue us.
2 Kings 18:33 Have the gods of the nations surely rescued, each his own country, from the hand of the king of the Assyrians?
2 Kings 18:34 Where is the god of Aimath and Arphad? Where is the god of Seppharouain? And did they deliver Samaria from my hand?
2 Kings 18:35 Who among all the gods of the lands delivered their lands from my hand, that the Lord should deliver Jerusalem from my hand?
2 Kings 18:36 And they were silent and did not answer him a word, for it was the king's command, saying, You shall not answer him.
2 Kings 18:37 And Eliakim son of Chelkias the steward and Somnas the scribe and Joas son of Asaph the recorder came to Ezekias with their garments torn and reported to him the words of Rapsakes.

## Chapter 19

2 Kings 19:1 And it happened when King Ezekias heard that he tore his garments and put on sackcloth and entered the house of the Lord.
2 Kings 19:2 And he sent Eliakim the steward and Somnas the scribe and the elders of the priests, clothed in sackcloth, to Esaias the prophet son of Amos,
2 Kings 19:3 and they said to him, Thus says Ezekias: This day is a day of affliction and rebuke and provocation, for sons have come to the pangs of birth, but the woman giving birth has no strength;
2 Kings 19:4 perhaps the Lord your God will hear all the words of Rapsakes, whom the king of the Assyrians his master sent to reproach the living God and blaspheme with words that the Lord your God has heard, and you will offer a prayer for the remnant that is found.
2 Kings 19:5 And the servants of King Ezekias came to Esaias,
2 Kings 19:6 and Esaias said to them, Thus shall you say to your master: Thus says the Lord: Do not fear because of the words you have heard, with which the servants of the king of the Assyrians blasphemed;
2 Kings 19:7 behold, I put a spirit in him, and he shall hear a report and return to his land, and I shall bring him down by the sword in his land.
2 Kings 19:8 And Rapsakes returned and found the king of the Assyrians fighting against Lomna, for he had heard that he had departed from Lachis;
2 Kings 19:9 and he heard concerning Tharaka king of the Ethiopians, saying, Behold, he has gone out to fight against you. And he returned and sent messengers to Ezekias, saying,
2 Kings 19:10 Let your God in whom you trust not lift you up, saying, Jerusalem shall certainly not be given into the hands of the king of the Assyrians.
2 Kings 19:11 Behold, you have heard all that the kings of the Assyrians did to all the lands, to devote them to destruction; and will you be delivered?
2 Kings 19:12 Did the gods of the nations whom my fathers destroyed deliver them, Gozan and Charran and Raphes and the sons of Edem who are in Thaesthen?
2 Kings 19:13 Where is the king of Aimath and the king of Arphad? And where are Seppharouain, Ana and Aua?
2 Kings 19:14 And Ezekias took the letters from the hands of the messengers and read them; and he went up to the house of the Lord, and Ezekias spread them out before the Lord
2 Kings 19:15 and said, Lord God of Israel, who sits upon the cherubim, you alone are God in all the kingdoms of the earth; you made heaven and earth.
2 Kings 19:16 Incline your ear, Lord, and hear; open your eyes, Lord, and see, and hear the words of Sennacherim that he sent to reproach the living God.
2 Kings 19:17 For truly, Lord, the kings of the Assyrians have laid waste the nations
2 Kings 19:18 and have given their gods to the fire, for they are not gods but works of human hands, wood and stone, and they destroyed them.
2 Kings 19:19 And now, Lord our God, save us from his hand, and all the kingdoms of the earth shall know that you alone are the Lord God.
2 Kings 19:20 And Esaias son of Amos sent to Ezekias, saying, Thus says the Lord God of hosts, the God of Israel: I have heard what you prayed to me concerning Sennacherim king of the Assyrians.
2 Kings 19:21 This is the word that the Lord spoke against him: Virgin daughter Zion has despised and mocked you; daughter Jerusalem has shaken her head at you.
2 Kings 19:22 Whom did you reproach and blaspheme? And against whom did you lift your voice? And you raised your eyes on high against the Holy One of Israel.
2 Kings 19:23 By the hand of your messengers you reproached the Lord and said, With the multitude of my chariots I shall ascend to the height of the mountains, the flanks of Lebanon, and I cut down the greatness of its cedar, its choice cypresses, and came to the melon of its end, the forest of its Carmel.
2 Kings 19:24 I cooled and drank foreign waters and dried up with the sole of my foot all the rivers of the enclosure.
2 Kings 19:25 I formed it; now I have brought it about, and it became for the raising up of colonies of warriors, fortified cities.
2 Kings 19:26 And those dwelling in them were weak of hand, were terrified and ashamed; they became grass of the field or green herbage, grass of rooftops and a thing trampled before one standing.
2 Kings 19:27 And I have known your sitting and your going out and your coming in and your anger against me.
2 Kings 19:28 Because of your anger against me and your arrogance that rose into my ears, I shall put my hooks in your nostrils and a bridle in your lips and turn you back on the road by which you came.
2 Kings 19:29 And this shall be the sign for you: this year you shall eat what grows of itself and in the second year what springs up; and in the third, sowing and harvest and planting of vineyards, and you shall eat their fruit.
2 Kings 19:30 And the surviving remnant of the house of Judah shall again put a root below and make fruit above.
2 Kings 19:31 For a remnant shall go out from Jerusalem and one escaping from Mount Zion; the zeal of the Lord of hosts shall do this.
2 Kings 19:32 Not so; thus says the Lord concerning the king of the Assyrians: He shall not enter this city and shall not shoot an arrow there, and no shield shall come before it, and he shall certainly not throw up a siege mound against it;
2 Kings 19:33 by the road by which he came he shall return, and into this city he shall not enter, says the Lord.
2 Kings 19:34 And I shall defend this city for my own sake and for the sake of David my servant.
2 Kings 19:35 And it happened by night that an angel of the Lord went out and struck a hundred and eighty-five thousand in the camp of the Assyrians; and they arose early in the morning, and behold, all were dead bodies.
2 Kings 19:36 And Sennacherim king of the Assyrians departed and went and returned and dwelt in Nineveh.
2 Kings 19:37 And it happened while he was worshiping in the house of Nesserach his god that Adramelech and Sarasar his sons struck him with a sword, and they escaped to the land of Ararat; and Asordan his son reigned in his stead.

## Chapter 20

2 Kings 20:1 In those days Ezekias became ill to the point of death. And Esaias son of Amos the prophet came in to him and said to him, Thus says the Lord: Give instructions to your house, for you are dying and shall not live.
2 Kings 20:2 And Ezekias turned his face to the wall and prayed to the Lord, saying,
2 Kings 20:3 Oh Lord, remember, please, how I walked before you in truth and with a full heart and did what was good in your eyes. And Ezekias wept with great weeping.
2 Kings 20:4 And Esaias was in the middle court, and the word of the Lord came to him, saying,
2 Kings 20:5 Return and say to Ezekias the leader of my people, Thus says the Lord God of David your father: I have heard your prayer, I have seen your tears; behold, I shall heal you; on the third day you shall go up to the house of the Lord,
2 Kings 20:6 and I shall add fifteen years to your days, and I shall save you and this city from the hand of the king of the Assyrians, and I shall defend this city for my own sake and for David my servant.
2 Kings 20:7 And he said, Let them take a cake of figs and put it on the sore, and he shall recover.
2 Kings 20:8 And Ezekias said to Esaias, What is the sign that the Lord will heal me and I shall go up to the house of the Lord on the third day?
2 Kings 20:9 And Esaias said, This is the sign from the Lord that the Lord will do the word he spoke: shall the shadow go ten steps, or return ten steps?
2 Kings 20:10 And Ezekias said, It is a light thing for the shadow to incline ten steps; no, but let the shadow return ten steps backward.
2 Kings 20:11 And Esaias the prophet cried out to the Lord, and the shadow returned backward on the steps ten steps.
2 Kings 20:12 At that time Marodachbaladan son of Baladan king of Babylon sent letters and manaa to Ezekias, for he heard that Ezekias had become ill.
2 Kings 20:13 And Ezekias rejoiced over them and showed them the whole house of the nechotha, the silver and the gold, the spices and the good oil, and the house of the vessels and all that was found in his treasuries; there was not a thing that Ezekias did not show them in his house and in all his dominion.
2 Kings 20:14 And Esaias the prophet entered to King Ezekias and said to him, What did these men say, and from where have they come to you? And Ezekias said, They have come to me from a distant land, from Babylon.
2 Kings 20:15 And he said, What did they see in your house? And he said, They saw all that is in my house; there was nothing in my house that I did not show them, including what is in my treasuries.
2 Kings 20:16 And Esaias said to Ezekias, Hear the word of the Lord:
2 Kings 20:17 Behold, days are coming, and all that is in your house and what your fathers stored up until this day shall be taken to Babylon; and not a thing shall remain, as the Lord said;
2 Kings 20:18 and your sons who will come forth from you, whom you shall beget, he shall take, and they shall be eunuchs in the house of the king of Babylon.
2 Kings 20:19 And Ezekias said to Esaias, Good is the word of the Lord that he spoke; let there be peace in my days.
2 Kings 20:20 And the rest of the deeds of Ezekias and all his acts of power and all that he did, the spring and the aqueduct and how he brought the water into the city, are these not written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Judah?
2 Kings 20:21 And Ezekias slept with his fathers and was buried in the city of David, and Manasses his son reigned in his stead.

## Chapter 21

2 Kings 21:1 Manasses was a son of twelve years when he began to reign, and he reigned fifty-five years in Jerusalem; and his mother's name was Opsiba.
2 Kings 21:2 And he did evil in the eyes of the Lord according to the abominations of the nations whom the Lord had removed before the sons of Israel,
2 Kings 21:3 and he turned and built the high places that Ezekias his father had pulled down and raised an altar for Baal and made groves, as Achaab king of Israel had done, and bowed to all the host of heaven and served them,
2 Kings 21:4 and built an altar in the house of the Lord, as he said, In Jerusalem I shall put my name,
2 Kings 21:5 and built an altar to all the host of heaven in the two courts of the house of the Lord,
2 Kings 21:6 and made his sons pass through fire and practiced omens and divination and made a consulter and knowers; he multiplied doing evil in the eyes of the Lord to provoke him.
2 Kings 21:7 And he put the carved image of the grove in the house of which the Lord had said to David and to Salomon his son, In this house and in Jerusalem, which I chose from all the tribes of Israel, I shall put my name there forever,
2 Kings 21:8 and I shall no longer shake the foot of Israel from the land that I gave their fathers, if they keep all that I commanded according to the whole commandment that my servant Moses commanded them.
2 Kings 21:9 And they did not listen, and Manasses led them astray to do evil in the eyes of the Lord beyond the nations whom the Lord had destroyed before the sons of Israel.
2 Kings 21:10 And the Lord spoke by the hand of his servants the prophets, saying,
2 Kings 21:11 Because Manasses king of Judah did these evil abominations beyond all that the Amorite before him had done, and even caused Judah to sin with their idols,
2 Kings 21:12 therefore thus says the Lord God of Israel: Behold, I bring evils upon Jerusalem and Judah so that both ears of everyone hearing shall ring,
2 Kings 21:13 and I shall stretch over Jerusalem the measure of Samaria and the plumb line of the house of Achaab and wipe away Jerusalem as an alabaster vessel is wiped and turned over on its face,
2 Kings 21:14 and I shall reject the remnant of my inheritance and give them into the hands of their enemies, and they shall be for plunder and for spoil to all their enemies,
2 Kings 21:15 because they did evil in my eyes and have been provoking me from the day I brought their fathers out of Egypt until this day.
2 Kings 21:16 And indeed Manasses poured out very much innocent blood until he filled Jerusalem from end to end, besides his sins by which he caused Judah to sin, doing evil in the eyes of the Lord.
2 Kings 21:17 And the rest of the deeds of Manasses and all that he did and the sin that he sinned, are these not written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Judah?
2 Kings 21:18 And Manasses slept with his fathers and was buried in the garden of his house, in the garden of Oza, and Amon his son reigned in his stead.
2 Kings 21:19 Amon was a son of twenty-two years when he began to reign, and he reigned two years in Jerusalem; and his mother's name was Mesollam daughter of Arous from Jeteba.
2 Kings 21:20 And he did evil in the eyes of the Lord, as Manasses his father had done,
2 Kings 21:21 and walked in all the way in which his father had walked and served the idols that his father had served and bowed to them
2 Kings 21:22 and abandoned the Lord God of his fathers and did not walk in the way of the Lord.
2 Kings 21:23 And the servants of Amon conspired against him and put the king to death in his house.
2 Kings 21:24 And all the people of the land struck all those who had conspired against King Amon, and the people of the land made Josias his son king in his stead.
2 Kings 21:25 And the rest of the deeds of Amon, as many as he did, behold, are these not written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Judah?
2 Kings 21:26 And they buried him in his tomb in the garden of Oza, and Josias his son reigned in his stead.

## Chapter 22

2 Kings 22:1 Josias was a son of eight years when he began to reign, and he reigned thirty-one years in Jerusalem; and his mother's name was Jedida daughter of Edeia from Basouroth.
2 Kings 22:2 And he did what was right in the eyes of the Lord and walked in all the way of David his father; he did not depart to the right or the left.
2 Kings 22:3 And it happened in the eighteenth year of King Josias, in the eighth month, that the king sent Saphphan son of Eseliou son of Mesollam, the scribe of the house of the Lord, saying,
2 Kings 22:4 Go up to Chelkias the high priest and seal the silver brought into the house of the Lord, which those keeping the station gathered from the people,
2 Kings 22:5 and let them give it into the hands of the workers appointed in the house of the Lord. And he gave it to the workers in the house of the Lord to strengthen the bedek of the house,
2 Kings 22:6 to the craftsmen and the builders and the wall builders, and to buy wood and hewn stones to strengthen the bedek of the house;
2 Kings 22:7 but they did not reckon the silver given to them with them, for they acted faithfully.
2 Kings 22:8 And Chelkias the high priest said to Saphphan the scribe, I found a book of the law in the house of the Lord. And Chelkias gave the book to Saphphan, and he read it.
2 Kings 22:9 And he brought it to King Josias and returned a word to the king and said, Your servants have melted down the silver found in the house of the Lord and given it into the hands of the workers appointed in the house of the Lord.
2 Kings 22:10 And Saphphan the scribe spoke to the king, saying, Chelkias the priest gave me a book. And Saphphan read it before the king.
2 Kings 22:11 And it happened when the king heard the words of the book of the law that he tore his garments.
2 Kings 22:12 And the king commanded Chelkias the priest and Achikam son of Saphphan and Achobor son of Michaiou and Saphphan the scribe and Asaia the king's servant, saying,
2 Kings 22:13 Go, seek the Lord concerning me and all the people and all Judah concerning the words of this book that was found, for great is the wrath of the Lord kindled among us because our fathers did not listen to the words of this book to do according to all that is written against us.
2 Kings 22:14 And Chelkias the priest and Achikam and Achobor and Saphphan and Asaias went to Olda the prophetess, wife of Sellem son of Thekoue son of Araas the keeper of garments; and she dwelt in Jerusalem in the masena, and they spoke to her.
2 Kings 22:15 And she said to them, Thus says the Lord God of Israel: Say to the man who sent you to me,
2 Kings 22:16 Thus says the Lord: Behold, I am bringing evils upon this place and its inhabitants, all the words of the book that the king of Judah read,
2 Kings 22:17 because they abandoned me and burned incense to other gods so as to provoke me with the works of their hands; and my anger shall be kindled against this place and shall not be quenched.
2 Kings 22:18 And to the king of Judah who sent you to seek the Lord, thus shall you say to him: Thus says the Lord God of Israel: The words that you heard,
2 Kings 22:19 because your heart was softened and you were humbled before the Lord when you heard what I spoke against this place and its inhabitants, that it should become a desolation and a curse, and you tore your garments and wept before me, I too have heard, says the Lord.
2 Kings 22:20 Therefore behold, I am adding you to your fathers, and you shall be gathered to your tomb in peace, and your eyes shall not see all the evils that I am bringing upon this place. And they returned the word to the king.

## Chapter 23

2 Kings 23:1 And the king sent and gathered to himself all the elders of Judah and Jerusalem.
2 Kings 23:2 And the king went up to the house of the Lord, and every man of Judah and all the inhabitants of Jerusalem with him, and the priests and the prophets and all the people from small to great; and he read in their ears all the words of the book of the covenant found in the house of the Lord.
2 Kings 23:3 And the king stood by the pillar and made a covenant before the Lord to walk after the Lord and to keep his commandments and his testimonies and his ordinances with all his heart and all his soul, to establish the words of this covenant written in this book; and all the people stood in the covenant.
2 Kings 23:4 And the king commanded Chelkias the high priest and the priests of the second order and those keeping the station to bring out from the temple of the Lord all the vessels made for Baal and for the grove and for all the host of heaven, and he burned them outside Jerusalem in the sademoth of Kedron and carried their dust to Bethel.
2 Kings 23:5 And he put an end to the chomarim whom the kings of Judah had appointed, who burned incense at the high places and in the cities of Judah and around Jerusalem, and those burning incense to Baal and the sun and the moon and the mazouroth and all the host of heaven.
2 Kings 23:6 And he brought the grove out of the house of the Lord outside Jerusalem to the torrent Kedron and burned it in the torrent Kedron and ground it to dust and threw its dust into the grave of the sons of the people.
2 Kings 23:7 And he demolished the house of the kadesim in the house of the Lord, where the women wove chettiin for the grove.
2 Kings 23:8 And he brought up all the priests from the cities of Judah and defiled the high places where the priests had burned incense, from Gabaa to Bersabee. And he demolished the house of the gates by the entrance of the gate of Jesou ruler of the city, on the left of a man in the gate of the city.
2 Kings 23:9 But the priests of the high places did not go up to the altar of the Lord in Jerusalem; rather, they ate unleavened bread among their brothers.
2 Kings 23:10 And he defiled Tapheth in the ravine of the son of Ennom, so that no man would make his son or his daughter pass through fire for Moloch.
2 Kings 23:11 And he put an end to the horses that the kings of Judah had given to the sun at the entrance of the house of the Lord by the treasury of Nathan the king's eunuch in pharourim, and he burned the chariot of the sun with fire.
2 Kings 23:12 And the altars on the roof of the upper room of Achaz that the kings of Judah had made, and the altars that Manasses had made in the two courts of the house of the Lord, the king demolished and pulled down from there and threw their dust into the torrent Kedron.
2 Kings 23:13 And the king defiled the house facing Jerusalem on the right of Mount Mosoath, which Salomon king of Israel had built for Astarte, an object of offense of the Sidonians, and for Chamos, an object of offense of Moab, and for Molchol, an abomination of the sons of Ammon.
2 Kings 23:14 And he crushed the pillars and destroyed the groves and filled their places with human bones.
2 Kings 23:15 And indeed the altar in Bethel, the high place that Jeroboam son of Nabat, who caused Israel to sin, had made, even that altar and the high place he pulled down and crushed its stones and ground them to dust and burned the grove.
2 Kings 23:16 And Josias turned and saw the tombs there in the city and sent and took the bones from the tombs and burned them upon the altar and defiled it according to the word of the Lord that the man of God spoke when Jeroboam stood at the feast by the altar. And turning, he lifted his eyes to the tomb of the man of God who had spoken these words
2 Kings 23:17 and said, What is that marker that I see? And the men of the city said to him, It is the man of God who came out of Judah and proclaimed these words that he proclaimed against the altar of Bethel.
2 Kings 23:18 And he said, Leave it; let no man move his bones. And his bones were spared with the bones of the prophet who had come from Samaria.
2 Kings 23:19 And also all the houses of the high places in the cities of Samaria that the kings of Israel had made to provoke the Lord, Josias removed, and he did to them all the deeds that he did in Bethel.
2 Kings 23:20 And he sacrificed all the priests of the high places who were there upon the altars and burned human bones upon them; and he returned to Jerusalem.
2 Kings 23:21 And the king commanded all the people, saying, Keep the Passover to the Lord our God as it is written in the book of this covenant;
2 Kings 23:22 for this Passover had not been held since the days of the judges who judged Israel, nor during all the days of the kings of Israel and the kings of Judah,
2 Kings 23:23 but in the eighteenth year of King Josias the Passover to the Lord was held in Jerusalem.
2 Kings 23:24 And indeed the consulters and the knowers and the theraphim and the idols and all the objects of offense that were in the land of Judah and in Jerusalem King Josias removed, to establish the words of the law written in the book that Chelkias the priest found in the house of the Lord.
2 Kings 23:25 Before him there was no king like him who turned to the Lord with all his heart and all his soul and all his strength according to all the law of Moses, and after him none like him arose.
2 Kings 23:26 But the Lord did not turn from the heat of his great anger, with which his anger burned against Judah for the provocations with which Manasses had provoked him.
2 Kings 23:27 And the Lord said, I shall also remove Judah from before my face as I removed Israel, and I shall reject this city that I chose, Jerusalem, and the house of which I said, My name shall be there.
2 Kings 23:28 And the rest of the deeds of Josias and all that he did, are these not written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Judah?
2 Kings 23:29 And in his days Pharaoh Nechao king of Egypt went up against the king of the Assyrians to the river Euphrates; and Josias went to meet him, and Nechao put him to death at Mageddo when he saw him.
2 Kings 23:30 And his servants put him, dead, on a chariot from Mageddo and brought him to Jerusalem and buried him in his tomb in the city of David, and the people of the land took Joachas son of Josias and anointed him and made him king in place of his father.
2 Kings 23:31 Joachas was a son of twenty-three years when he began to reign, and he reigned three months in Jerusalem; and his mother's name was Amital daughter of Jeremias from Lemna.
2 Kings 23:32 And he did evil in the eyes of the Lord according to all that his fathers had done.
2 Kings 23:33 And Pharaoh Nechao removed him at Deblatha in the land of Emath so that he would not reign in Jerusalem, and imposed a fine upon the land of a hundred talents of silver and a hundred talents of gold.
2 Kings 23:34 And Pharaoh Nechao made Eliakim son of Josias king over them in place of Josias his father and changed his name to Joakim; and he took Joachas and brought him to Egypt, and he died there.
2 Kings 23:35 And Joakim gave the silver and the gold to Pharaoh; but he assessed the land to give the silver at the word of Pharaoh; each man according to his assessment gave the silver and the gold with the people of the land to give to Pharaoh Nechao.
2 Kings 23:36 Joakim was a son of twenty-five years when he began to reign, and he reigned eleven years in Jerusalem; and his mother's name was Jeldaph daughter of Phedeia from Rouma.
2 Kings 23:37 And he did evil in the eyes of the Lord according to all that his fathers had done.

## Chapter 24

2 Kings 24:1 In his days Nabouchodonosor king of Babylon went up, and Joakim became his servant for three years; and he turned and rebelled against him.
2 Kings 24:2 And he sent against him the bands of the Chaldeans and the bands of Syria and the bands of Moab and the bands of the sons of Ammon and sent them into the land of Judah to prevail, according to the word of the Lord that he spoke by the hand of his servants the prophets.
2 Kings 24:3 But it was upon the anger of the Lord against Judah to remove it from before his face because of the sins of Manasses, according to all that he did;
2 Kings 24:4 and indeed he poured out innocent blood and filled Jerusalem with innocent blood, and the Lord was unwilling to show mercy.
2 Kings 24:5 And the rest of the deeds of Joakim and all that he did, behold, are these not written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Judah?
2 Kings 24:6 And Joakim slept with his fathers, and Joakim his son reigned in his stead.
2 Kings 24:7 And the king of Egypt no longer continued to go out of his land, for the king of Babylon had taken from the torrent of Egypt to the river Euphrates all that belonged to the king of Egypt.
2 Kings 24:8 Joakim was a son of eighteen years when he began to reign, and he reigned three months in Jerusalem; and his mother's name was Nestha daughter of Ellanathan from Jerusalem.
2 Kings 24:9 And he did evil in the eyes of the Lord according to all that his father had done.
2 Kings 24:10 At that time Nabouchodonosor king of Babylon went up to Jerusalem, and the city came under siege.
2 Kings 24:11 And Nabouchodonosor king of Babylon entered the city, and his servants were besieging it.
2 Kings 24:12 And Joakim king of Judah went out to the king of Babylon, he and his servants and his mother and his commanders and his eunuchs, and the king of Babylon took him in the eighth year of his reign.
2 Kings 24:13 And he brought out from there all the treasures of the house of the Lord and the treasures of the king's house and cut up all the gold vessels that Salomon king of Israel had made in the temple of the Lord, according to the word of the Lord.
2 Kings 24:14 And he deported Jerusalem and all the commanders and the mighty in strength, ten thousand captives, and every craftsman and metalworker, and none remained except the poor of the land.
2 Kings 24:15 And he deported Joakim to Babylon and the king's mother and the king's wives and his eunuchs; and he led the strong men of the land into exile from Jerusalem to Babylon,
2 Kings 24:16 and all the men of the force, seven thousand, and the craftsmen and metalworkers, one thousand, all mighty men making war; and the king of Babylon brought them as exiles to Babylon.
2 Kings 24:17 And the king of Babylon made Matthanias his son king in his stead and gave him the name Sedekias.
2 Kings 24:18 Sedekias was a son of twenty-one years when he began to reign, and he reigned eleven years in Jerusalem; and his mother's name was Amital daughter of Jeremias.
2 Kings 24:19 And he did evil before the Lord according to all that Joakim had done;
2 Kings 24:20 for the anger of the Lord was upon Jerusalem and Judah until he cast them away from before his face. And Sedekias rebelled against the king of Babylon.

## Chapter 25

2 Kings 25:1 And it happened in the ninth year of his reign, in the tenth month, that Nabouchodonosor king of Babylon and all his force came against Jerusalem and encamped against it and built a surrounding wall around it.
2 Kings 25:2 And the city came under siege until the eleventh year of King Sedekias;
2 Kings 25:3 on the ninth of the month the famine grew strong in the city, and there was no bread for the people of the land.
2 Kings 25:4 And the city was breached, and all the men of war went out by night through the gate between the walls, which is by the king's garden, while the Chaldeans were all around the city. And he went by the road to the Araba,
2 Kings 25:5 and the force of the Chaldeans pursued the king and overtook him in the plains of Jericho, and all his force was scattered from him.
2 Kings 25:6 And they captured the king and brought him to the king of Babylon at Deblatha, and he pronounced judgment upon him;
2 Kings 25:7 and he slaughtered the sons of Sedekias before his eyes, and blinded the eyes of Sedekias and bound him in fetters and brought him to Babylon.
2 Kings 25:8 And in the fifth month, on the seventh of the month [the same year was the nineteenth of Nabouchodonosor king of Babylon], Nabouzardan the chief cook, who stood before the king of Babylon, came to Jerusalem.
2 Kings 25:9 And he burned the house of the Lord and the king's house and all the houses of Jerusalem, and every house burned
2 Kings 25:10 the chief cook.
2 Kings 25:11 And the surplus of the people left in the city and those who had gone over to the king of Babylon and the rest of the support Nabouzardan the chief cook removed.
2 Kings 25:12 And the chief cook left some of the poor of the land as vine dressers and as gabin.
2 Kings 25:13 And the Chaldeans crushed the bronze pillars in the house of the Lord and the mechonoth and the bronze sea in the house of the Lord and carried their bronze to Babylon.
2 Kings 25:14 And he took the cauldrons and the iamin and the bowls and the censers and all the bronze vessels with which they ministered;
2 Kings 25:15 and the chief cook took the fire pans and the bowls of gold and of silver,
2 Kings 25:16 two pillars, the one sea and the mechonoth that Salomon had made for the house of the Lord; there was no weighing the bronze of all the vessels.
2 Kings 25:17 The height of the one pillar was eighteen cubits, and the bronze chothar upon it, and the height of the chothar was three cubits, sabacha and roai upon the chothar all around, all bronze; and the second pillar was like it with the sabacha.
2 Kings 25:18 And the chief cook took Saraias the first priest and Sophonias son of the second order and the three who kept the station,
2 Kings 25:19 and from the city he took one eunuch who was overseer of the fighting men, and five men who saw the king's face who were found in the city, and the scribe of the commander of the force who mustered the people of the land, and sixty men of the people of the land found in the city;
2 Kings 25:20 and Nabouzardan the chief cook took them and led them to the king of Babylon at Deblatha,
2 Kings 25:21 and the king of Babylon struck them and put them to death at Deblatha in the land of Aimath. And Judah was deported from its land.
2 Kings 25:22 And the people left in the land of Judah, whom Nabouchodonosor king of Babylon had left, he appointed Godolias son of Achikam son of Saphan over them.
2 Kings 25:23 And all the commanders of the force, they and their men, heard that the king of Babylon had appointed Godolias, and they came to Godolias at Massephath: Ismael son of Nathanias and Joanan son of Karee and Saraias son of Thanemath the Netophathite and Jezonias son of the Machathite, they and their men.
2 Kings 25:24 And Godolias swore to them and to their men and said to them, Do not fear the passage of the Chaldeans; dwell in the land and serve the king of Babylon, and it shall be well with you.
2 Kings 25:25 And it happened in the seventh month that Ismael son of Nathanias son of Elisama, of the royal seed, came with ten men; and he struck Godolias, and he died, and the Judeans and the Chaldeans who were with him at Massephath.
2 Kings 25:26 And all the people from small to great and the commanders of the forces arose and went into Egypt, for they feared the Chaldeans.
2 Kings 25:27 And it happened in the thirty-seventh year of the exile of Joakim king of Judah, in the twelfth month, on the twenty-seventh of the month, that Evilmarodach king of Babylon, in the year of his reign, lifted the head of Joakim king of Judah and brought him out of his prison house
2 Kings 25:28 and spoke good things with him and placed his throne above the thrones of the kings who were with him in Babylon,
2 Kings 25:29 and changed his prison garments, and he ate bread continually before him all the days of his life;
2 Kings 25:30 and his provision, a continual provision, was given him from the king's house, a day's portion on its day, all the days of his life.

1 Chronicles 1:10 And Chous fathered Nebrod; he began to be a giant hunter upon the earth.

1 Chronicles 1:24 Sala,
1 Chronicles 1:25 Eber, Phalek, Ragau,
1 Chronicles 1:26 Serouch, Nachor, Thara,
1 Chronicles 1:27 Abraham.

1 Chronicles 1:30 Masma, Idouma, Masse, Chodad, Thaiman,
1 Chronicles 1:31 Jettour, Naphes and Kedma. These are the sons of Ismael.

1 Chronicles 1:33 And sons of Madiam: Gaipha and Opher and Enoch and Abida and Eldaa. All these are sons of Chettoura.
1 Chronicles 1:34 And Abraham fathered Isaac. And sons of Isaac: Esau and Jacob.
1 Chronicles 1:35 Sons of Esau: Eliphas and Ragouel and Jeoul and Jeglom and Kore.
1 Chronicles 1:36 Sons of Eliphas: Thaiman and Omar, Sophar and Gootham and Kenez and, of Thamna, Amalek.
1 Chronicles 1:37 And sons of Ragouel: Nacheth, Zare, Some and Moze.
1 Chronicles 1:38 Sons of Seir: Lotan, Sobal, Sebegon, Ana, Deson, Osar, Daison.
1 Chronicles 1:39 And sons of Lotan: Chorri and Aiman and Ailath and Namna.
1 Chronicles 1:40 Sons of Sobal: Golam, Manachath, Gaibel, Sob and Onam. And sons of Sebegon: Aia and Ana.
1 Chronicles 1:41 Sons of Ana: Daison. And sons of Deson: Emeron and Eseban and Jethran and Charran.
1 Chronicles 1:42 And sons of Osar: Balaan and Zoukan and Jokan. Sons of Daison: Os and Arran.
1 Chronicles 1:43 And these are their kings: Balak son of Beor, and the name of his city was Dennaba.
1 Chronicles 1:44 And Balak died, and Jobab son of Zara from Bosorra reigned in his stead.
1 Chronicles 1:45 And Jobab died, and Asom from the land of the Thaimanians reigned in his stead.
1 Chronicles 1:46 And Asom died, and Adad son of Barad, who struck Madiam in the plain of Moab, reigned in his stead, and the name of his city was Geththaim.
1 Chronicles 1:47 And Adad died, and Samaa from Masekka reigned in his stead.
1 Chronicles 1:48 And Samaa died, and Saoul from Rooboth by the river reigned in his stead.
1 Chronicles 1:49 And Saoul died, and Balaennon son of Achobor reigned in his stead.
1 Chronicles 1:50 And Balaennon son of Achobor died, and Adad son of Barad reigned in his stead, and the name of his city was Phogor.
1 Chronicles 1:51 And Adad died. And there were leaders of Edom: leader Thamana, leader Gola, leader Jetheth,
1 Chronicles 1:52 leader Elibamas, leader Elas, leader Phinon,
1 Chronicles 1:53 leader Kenez, leader Thaiman, leader Mabsar,
1 Chronicles 1:54 leader Megediel, leader Eram. These are leaders of Edom.

## Chapter 2

1 Chronicles 2:1 These are the names of the sons of Israel: Reuben, Symeon, Levi, Judah, Issachar, Zaboulon,
1 Chronicles 2:2 Dan, Joseph, Benjamin, Nephthali, Gad, Aser.
1 Chronicles 2:3 Sons of Judah: Er, Aunan, Selon, three; they were born to him of the daughter of Saua the Chanaanite. And Er the firstborn of Judah was evil before the Lord, and he killed him.
1 Chronicles 2:4 And Thamar his daughter-in-law bore him Phares and Zara. All the sons of Judah were five.
1 Chronicles 2:5 Sons of Phares: Arson and Jemouel.
1 Chronicles 2:6 And sons of Zara: Zambri and Aithan and Aiman and Chalchal and Dara, five in all.
1 Chronicles 2:7 And sons of Charmi: Achar the hinderer of Israel, who transgressed in the devoted thing.
1 Chronicles 2:8 And sons of Aithan: Azarias.
1 Chronicles 2:9 And sons of Eseron born to him: Jerameel and Ram and Chaleb and Aram.

1 Chronicles 2:11 and Naasson fathered Salmon, and Salmon fathered Boos,
1 Chronicles 2:12 and Boos fathered Obed, and Obed fathered Jessai,
1 Chronicles 2:13 and Jessai fathered Eliab his firstborn; Aminadab the second, Samaa the third,
1 Chronicles 2:14 Nathanael the fourth, Raddai the fifth,
1 Chronicles 2:15 Asom the sixth, David the seventh.
1 Chronicles 2:16 And their sisters were Sarouia and Abigaia. And sons of Sarouia: Abessa and Joab and Asael, three.
1 Chronicles 2:17 And Abigaia bore Amessa; and Amessa's father was Jothor the Ismaelite.
1 Chronicles 2:18 And Chaleb son of Eseron fathered Gazouba a wife and Jerioth. And these were her sons: Joasar and Sobab and Orna.
1 Chronicles 2:19 And Gazouba died, and Chaleb took Ephrath for himself, and she bore him Or;
1 Chronicles 2:20 and Or fathered Ouri, and Ouri fathered Beseleel.
1 Chronicles 2:21 And after these things Eseron went in to the daughter of Machir father of Galaad, and he took her, being sixty years old, and she bore him Segoub.
1 Chronicles 2:22 And Segoub fathered Jair. And he had twenty-three cities in Galaad;
1 Chronicles 2:23 and Gedsour and Aram took the villages of Jair from them, Kanath and its villages, sixty cities; all these belonged to the sons of Machir father of Galaad.
1 Chronicles 2:24 And after Eseron died Chaleb went to Ephratha. And Eseron's wife Abia bore him Aschod father of Thekoe.
1 Chronicles 2:25 And the sons of Jeremeel the firstborn of Eseron were Ram the firstborn, and Baana and Aran and Asom his brother.
1 Chronicles 2:26 And Jeremeel had another wife, and her name was Atara; she was the mother of Ozom.
1 Chronicles 2:27 And the sons of Ram the firstborn of Jeremeel were Maas and Jamin and Akor.
1 Chronicles 2:28 And the sons of Ozom were Samai and Jadae. And sons of Samai: Nadab and Abisour.
1 Chronicles 2:29 And the name of Abisour's wife was Abichail, and she bore him Achabar and Molid.
1 Chronicles 2:30 Sons of Nadab: Salad and Aphphaim. And Salad died without children.
1 Chronicles 2:31 And sons of Aphphaim: Jisemiel. And sons of Jisemiel: Sosan. And sons of Sosan: Achlai.
1 Chronicles 2:32 And sons of Jadae: Achisamai, Jether, Jonathan; and Jether died without children.
1 Chronicles 2:33 And sons of Jonathan: Phaleth and Ozaza. These were sons of Jeremeel.
1 Chronicles 2:34 And Sosan had no sons, only daughters; and Sosan had an Egyptian servant named Jochiel,
1 Chronicles 2:35 and Sosan gave his daughter to his servant Jochiel as a wife, and she bore him Eththi.
1 Chronicles 2:36 And Eththi fathered Nathan, and Nathan fathered Zabed,
1 Chronicles 2:37 and Zabed fathered Aphaleel, and Aphaleel fathered Obed,
1 Chronicles 2:38 and Obed fathered Jeou, and Jeou fathered Azarias,
1 Chronicles 2:39 and Azarias fathered Chelles, and Chelles fathered Eleasa,
1 Chronicles 2:40 and Eleasa fathered Sosomai, and Sosomai fathered Saloum,
1 Chronicles 2:41 and Saloum fathered Jechemias, and Jechemias fathered Elisama.
1 Chronicles 2:42 And sons of Chaleb brother of Jeremeel: Marisa his firstborn, he was father of Ziph; and sons of Marisa father of Chebron.
1 Chronicles 2:43 And sons of Chebron: Kore and Thapous and Rekom and Semaa.
1 Chronicles 2:44 And Semaa fathered Raem father of Jerkaan, and Jerkaan fathered Samai;
1 Chronicles 2:45 and his son was Maon, and Maon was father of Baithsour.
1 Chronicles 2:46 And Gaipha the concubine of Chaleb bore Arran and Mosa and Gezoue. And Arran fathered Gezoue.
1 Chronicles 2:47 And sons of Jadai: Ragem and Joatham and Gersom and Phalet and Gaipha and Sagaph.
1 Chronicles 2:48 And Mocha the concubine of Chaleb bore Saber and Tharchna.
1 Chronicles 2:49 And she bore Sagaph father of Marmina and Saou father of Machabena and father of Gaibaa; and Chaleb's daughter was Ascha.
1 Chronicles 2:50 These were sons of Chaleb. Sons of Or the firstborn of Ephratha: Sobal father of Kariathiarim,
1 Chronicles 2:51 Salomon father of Baithlaem, Arim father of Baithgedor.
1 Chronicles 2:52 And Sobal father of Kariathiarim had sons: Araa, Esi, Ammanith,
1 Chronicles 2:53 Emospheos, city of Jair, Aithalim and Miphithim and Esamathim and Emasaraim; from these came the Sarathaians and the Esthaolaians.

1 Chronicles 2:55 families of scribes dwelling at Jabes: Thargathiim, Samathiim, Sokathiim; these are the Kenites who came from Mesema father of the house of Rechab.

## Chapter 4

1 Chronicles 4:1 And sons of Judah: Phares, Arson and Charmi and Or, Soubal
1 Chronicles 4:2 and Raia his son; and Soubal fathered Jeth, and Jeth fathered Achimi and Laad; these are the generations of the Sarathite.
1 Chronicles 4:3 And these were sons of Aitam: Jezrael and Ragma and Jabas, and their sister's name was Eselebbōn.
1 Chronicles 4:4 And Phanouel father of Gedor, and Azir father of Osan. These were sons of Or the firstborn of Ephratha father of Baithlaem.
1 Chronicles 4:5 And Saour father of Thekoe had two wives, Aoda and Thoada.
1 Chronicles 4:6 And Aoda bore him Ochazam and Ephad and Thaiman and Astheran; all these were sons of Aoda.
1 Chronicles 4:7 And sons of Thoada: Sareth and Saar and Ethnan.
1 Chronicles 4:8 And Kos fathered Enob and Sabeba. And generations of the brother of Rechab son of Jarim.
1 Chronicles 4:9 And Igabes was more honored than his brothers; and his mother called his name Igabes, saying, I bore as gabes.
1 Chronicles 4:10 And Igabes called upon the God of Israel, saying, If you will surely bless me and enlarge my borders and your hand be with me, then you will make knowledge so as not to humble me. And God brought about all that he asked.
1 Chronicles 4:11 And Chaleb father of Ascha fathered Machir; he was father of Assathon.
1 Chronicles 4:12 And Assathon fathered Bathrephan and Phessie and Thana father of the city Naas, brother of Eselon the Kenezite; these were men of Repha.
1 Chronicles 4:13 And sons of Kenez: Gothoniel and Saraia. And sons of Gothoniel: Athath.
1 Chronicles 4:14 And Manathi fathered Gophera. And Saraia fathered Joab father of Ageaddair, for they were craftsmen.
1 Chronicles 4:15 And sons of Chaleb son of Jephonne: Era, Ala and Noom. And sons of Ala: Kenez.
1 Chronicles 4:16 And his son Geseel, Ameachi and Zapha and Zaira and Eserael.
1 Chronicles 4:17 And sons of Esri: Jether, Morad and Apher and Jalon. And Jether fathered Maron and Semai and Mareth father of Esthemon.
1 Chronicles 4:18 And his wife [this is Adia] bore Jared father of Gedor and Aber father of Sochon and Jekthiel father of Zano; and these were sons of Gelia daughter of Pharaoh, whom Mored took.
1 Chronicles 4:19 And sons of the wife of Idouia sister of Nachem. And Dalia father of Keila, and Semeion father of Joman. And sons of Naem father of Keila: Agarmi and Esthemoe the Machathite.
1 Chronicles 4:20 And sons of Semeion: Amnon and Rana, son of Anan and Thilon. And sons of Jesei: Zoath and sons of Zoath.
1 Chronicles 4:21 Sons of Selom son of Judah: Er father of Lecha and Laada father of Maresa and generations of houses, ephrath abak, of the house of Esoba
1 Chronicles 4:22 and Joakim and men of Chozeba and Joas and Saraph, who dwelt in Moab; and he brought them back, abederin athoukiin.
1 Chronicles 4:23 These were potters dwelling in Nataim and Gadera; with the king in his kingdom they became strong and dwelt there.
1 Chronicles 4:24 Sons of Symeon: Namouel and Jamin, Jarib, Zare, Saoul;
1 Chronicles 4:25 Salem his son, Mabasam his son, Masma his son,
1 Chronicles 4:26 Amouel his son, Saboud his son, Zakchour his son, Semei his son.
1 Chronicles 4:27 And Semei had sixteen sons and three daughters; and their brothers had not many sons; and all their families did not increase like the sons of Judah.
1 Chronicles 4:28 And they dwelt in Bersabee and Sama and Molada and Esersoual
1 Chronicles 4:29 and in Balaa and Boasom and Thoulad
1 Chronicles 4:30 and Bathouel and Erma and Seklag
1 Chronicles 4:31 and Baithmarchaboth and half of Sosim and the house of Baroumseorim; these were their cities until King David.
1 Chronicles 4:32 And their settlements: Aitam and Enremmon and Thokkan and Aisan, five cities.
1 Chronicles 4:33 And all their settlements around these cities as far as Baal; this was their holding and their enrollment.
1 Chronicles 4:34 And Mosobab and Jemoloch and Josias son of Amasias
1 Chronicles 4:35 and Joel [and he was son of Isabia], son of Saraia, son of Asiel,
1 Chronicles 4:36 and Elioenai and Jakaba and Jasouia and Asaia and Ediel and Ismael and Banaia
1 Chronicles 4:37 and Zouza son of Sephei son of Allon son of Jedia son of Samari son of Samaiou.
1 Chronicles 4:38 These who passed by in names of rulers in their generations; and in the houses of their families they increased into a multitude.
1 Chronicles 4:39 And they went as far as the entrance of Gerara, to the east of Gai, to seek pastures for their livestock;
1 Chronicles 4:40 and they found rich and good pastures, and the land was broad before them and peaceful and quiet, for those dwelling there before were of the sons of Cham.
1 Chronicles 4:41 And these recorded by name came in the days of Ezekias king of Judah and struck their houses and the Minaeans whom they found there and devoted them to destruction until this day and dwelt in their stead, for there were pastures for their livestock there.
1 Chronicles 4:42 And from them, from the sons of Symeon, five hundred men went to Mount Seir, and Phalettia and Noadia and Raphaia and Oziel sons of Jesi were their leaders;
1 Chronicles 4:43 and they struck the remnant left of Amalek and dwelt there until this day.

## Chapter 5

1 Chronicles 5:1 And sons of Reuben the firstborn of Israel, for he was the firstborn, but when he went up to his father's bed he gave his blessing to his son Joseph son of Israel, and he was not reckoned in the genealogy for the birthright;
1 Chronicles 5:2 for Judah was mighty in strength and among his brothers and a leader came from him, but the blessing belonged to Joseph.
1 Chronicles 5:3 Sons of Reuben the firstborn of Israel: Enoch and Phallous, Arson and Charmi.
1 Chronicles 5:4 Sons of Joel: Semei and Banaia his son. And sons of Goug son of Semei:
1 Chronicles 5:5 his son Micha, his son Recha, his son Baal,
1 Chronicles 5:6 his son Beera, whom Thaglathphalnasar king of Assour deported; he was ruler of the Reubenites.
1 Chronicles 5:7 And his brothers by his family in their enrollments according to their generations: the ruler Joel and Zacharias
1 Chronicles 5:8 and Balek son of Ozouz son of Sama son of Joel; he dwelt in Aroer and as far as Nabau and Beelmaon,
1 Chronicles 5:9 and eastward he dwelt as far as the approaches of the wilderness from the river Euphrates, for their livestock were numerous in the land of Galaad.
1 Chronicles 5:10 And in the days of Saoul they made war against the sojourners, and they fell into their hands, dwelling in tents throughout the east of Galaad.
1 Chronicles 5:11 Sons of Gad dwelt opposite them in Basan as far as Selcha.
1 Chronicles 5:12 Joel the firstborn, Sapham the second, and Jani the scribe in Basan.
1 Chronicles 5:13 And their brothers by the houses of their families: Michael, Mosollam and Sebee and Joree and Jachan and Zoue and Obed, seven.
1 Chronicles 5:14 These were sons of Abichail son of Ouri son of Idai son of Galaad son of Michael son of Isai son of Jouri son of Zaboucham
1 Chronicles 5:15 son of Abdiel son of Gouni, ruler of a family house.
1 Chronicles 5:16 They dwelt in Galaad, in Basan and its villages and all the surrounding lands of Saron as far as the exit.
1 Chronicles 5:17 The enrollment of them all was in the days of Joatham king of Judah and the days of Jeroboam king of Israel.
1 Chronicles 5:18 Sons of Reuben and Gad and half the tribe of Manasseh, of sons of strength, men bearing shields and sword and drawing the bow and trained for war, forty-four thousand seven hundred and sixty going out in battle array.
1 Chronicles 5:19 And they made war with the Agarenes and Ituraeans and Naphisaeans and Nadabaeans
1 Chronicles 5:20 and prevailed over them, and the Agaraeans and all their encampments were given into their hands, for they cried to God in the war, and he heard them because they hoped in him.
1 Chronicles 5:21 And they took their baggage captive: five thousand camels and two hundred fifty thousand sheep, two thousand donkeys and one hundred thousand human souls;
1 Chronicles 5:22 for many wounded fell, for the war was from God. And they dwelt in their stead until the deportation.
1 Chronicles 5:23 And the half tribe of Manasseh dwelt in the land from Basan as far as Baalermon and Sanir and Mount Aermon; and in Lebanon they multiplied.
1 Chronicles 5:24 And these were the heads of their family houses: Opher and Jesei and Eliel and Esdriel and Jermia and Odouia and Jediel, men mighty in strength, men of renown, rulers of their family houses.
1 Chronicles 5:25 And they rebelled against the God of their fathers and prostituted themselves after the gods of the peoples of the land whom God had removed before them.
1 Chronicles 5:26 And the God of Israel stirred up the spirit of Phaloch king of Assour and the spirit of Thaglathphalnasar king of Assour, and he deported Reuben and Gad and the half tribe of Manasseh and led them to Chalach and Chabor and to the river Gozan until this day.
1 Chronicles 5:27 Sons of Levi: Gedson, Kaath and Merari.
1 Chronicles 5:28 And sons of Kaath: Ambram and Issaar, Chebron and Oziel.
1 Chronicles 5:29 And sons of Ambram: Aaron and Moses and Mariam. And sons of Aaron: Nadab and Abioud, Eleazar and Ithamar.
1 Chronicles 5:30 Eleazar fathered Phinees, Phinees fathered Abisou,
1 Chronicles 5:31 Abisou fathered Bokai, Bokai fathered Ozi,
1 Chronicles 5:32 Ozi fathered Zaraia, Zaraia fathered Mariel,
1 Chronicles 5:33 and Mariel fathered Amaria, and Amaria fathered Achitob,
1 Chronicles 5:34 and Achitob fathered Sadok, and Sadok fathered Achimaas,
1 Chronicles 5:35 and Achimaas fathered Azarias, and Azarias fathered Joanan,
1 Chronicles 5:36 and Joanas fathered Azarias; he served as priest in the house that Salomon built in Jerusalem.
1 Chronicles 5:37 And Azarias fathered Amaria, and Amaria fathered Achitob,
1 Chronicles 5:38 and Achitob fathered Sadok, and Sadok fathered Salom,
1 Chronicles 5:39 and Salom fathered Chelkias, and Chelkias fathered Azarias,
1 Chronicles 5:40 and Azarias fathered Saraias, and Saraias fathered Josadak.
1 Chronicles 5:41 And Josadak went into exile with Judah and Jerusalem by the hand of Nabouchodonosor.

## Chapter 7

1 Chronicles 7:1 And for the sons of Issachar: Thola and Phoua and Jasoub and Semeron, four.
1 Chronicles 7:2 And sons of Thola: Ozi and Raphaia and Jeriel and Jemou and Jebasam and Samuel, rulers of their family houses for Thola, mighty in strength according to their generations. Their number in David's days was twenty-two thousand six hundred.
1 Chronicles 7:3 And sons of Ozi: Jezria, and sons of Jezria: Michael and Obdia and Joel and Jesia, five, all rulers.
1 Chronicles 7:4 And with them according to their generations by their ancestral houses were thirty-six thousand mighty men for battle, for they had multiplied wives and sons.
1 Chronicles 7:5 And their brothers in all the families of Issachar, mighty in strength, numbered eighty-seven thousand in all.
1 Chronicles 7:6 Benjamin: Bale and Bachir and Jadiel, three.
1 Chronicles 7:7 And sons of Bale: Asebon and Ozi and Oziel and Jerimoth and Ouri, five rulers of ancestral houses, mighty in strength. And their number was twenty-two thousand and thirty-four.
1 Chronicles 7:8 And sons of Bachir: Zamarias and Joas and Eliezer and Elithenan and Amaria and Jerimoth and Abiou and Anathoth and Gemeeth. All these were sons of Bachir.
1 Chronicles 7:9 And their number according to their generations, rulers of their family houses, mighty in strength, was twenty thousand two hundred.
1 Chronicles 7:10 And sons of Jadiel: Balaan. And sons of Balaan: Jaous and Benjamin and Aoth and Chanana and Zaithan and Ramessai and Achisaar.
1 Chronicles 7:11 All these were sons of Jadiel, rulers of the families, mighty in strength, seventeen thousand two hundred going out in force to fight.
1 Chronicles 7:12 And Sapphin and Apphin and sons of Raom: his son Aer.
1 Chronicles 7:13 Sons of Nephthali: Jasiel and Goni and Issier and Salom, sons of Balaa.
1 Chronicles 7:14 Sons of Manasseh: Aseriel, whom his Syrian concubine bore; she bore Machir father of Galaad.
1 Chronicles 7:15 And Machir took a wife for Amphin and Mamphin; and his sister's name was Moocha. And the second one's name was Salpaad, and daughters were born to Salpaad.
1 Chronicles 7:16 And Moocha wife of Machir bore a son and called his name Phares, and his brother's name was Soros; his son was Oulam.
1 Chronicles 7:17 And sons of Oulam: Badan. These were sons of Galaad son of Machir son of Manasseh.
1 Chronicles 7:18 And his sister Malecheth bore Isadek and Abiezer and Maela.
1 Chronicles 7:19 And the sons of Semira were Jaaim and Sychem and Lakei and Aniam.
1 Chronicles 7:20 And sons of Ephraim: Sothala, and Barad his son, and Thaath his son, Eleada his son, Nomee his son,
1 Chronicles 7:21 Zabed his son, Sothele his son and Ezer and Elead. And the men of Geth born in the land killed them because they went down to take their livestock.
1 Chronicles 7:22 And Ephraim their father mourned many days, and his brothers came to comfort him.
1 Chronicles 7:23 And he went in to his wife, and she conceived and bore a son, and he called his name Baraga, because, In evils it happened in my house.
1 Chronicles 7:24 And among those who remained he built lower and upper Baithoron. And sons of Ozan: Seera
1 Chronicles 7:25 and Raphi his sons, Raseph and Thale his sons, Thaen his son.
1 Chronicles 7:26 Laadan his son, Amioud his son, Elisama his son,
1 Chronicles 7:27 Noum his son, Jesoue his son.
1 Chronicles 7:28 And their holding and dwelling place: Bethel and its villages, to the east Naaran, to the west Gazer and its villages; and Sychem and its villages as far as Gaian and its villages.
1 Chronicles 7:29 And as far as the borders of the sons of Manasseh: Baithsaan and its villages, Thaanach and its villages and Balad and its villages, Mageddo and its villages, Dor and its villages. In these the sons of Joseph son of Israel dwelt.
1 Chronicles 7:30 Sons of Aser: Jemna and Isoua and Isoui and Beriga, and Sore their sister.
1 Chronicles 7:31 And sons of Beriga: Chaber and Melchiel, who was father of Berzaith.
1 Chronicles 7:32 And Chaber fathered Japhalet and Samer and Chotham and Sola their sister.
1 Chronicles 7:33 And sons of Japhalet: Phesechi, Bamael and Asith; these were sons of Japhalet.
1 Chronicles 7:34 And sons of Semmer: Achiouraoga and Oba and Aram
1 Chronicles 7:35 and Baneelam; his brothers were Sophas and Imana and Selles and Amal.
1 Chronicles 7:36 Sons of Sophas: Chouchi, Arnaphar and Soual and Bari and Imari,
1 Chronicles 7:37 Sobal and Od and Semma and Salisa and Jethran and Beera.
1 Chronicles 7:38 And sons of Jether: Iphina and Phaspha and Ara.
1 Chronicles 7:39 And sons of Ola: Orech, Aniel and Rasia.
1 Chronicles 7:40 All these were sons of Aser, all chosen rulers of families mighty in strength, leading rulers; their number in battle array for fighting was twenty-six thousand men.

1 Chronicles 8:2 Noa the fourth and Raphi the fifth.

1 Chronicles 8:4 and Abisoue and Nooma and Achia
