1 Chronicles 11:46 Eliel the Mii and Jaribi and Josia his son, Elnaam and Jethma the Moabite,
1 Chronicles 11:47 Aliel and Obed and Jesiel the Misabia.

## Chapter 12

1 Chronicles 12:1 And these are those who came to David at Sikelag, while he was still being kept away from before Saul son of Kis; and these were among the mighty men helping in the war,
1 Chronicles 12:2 with bow to the right and to the left, and slingers with stones and bows. From the brothers of Saul, from Benjamin:
1 Chronicles 12:3 the ruler Achiezer, and Joas son of Asma the Gebothite, and Joel and Jophalelet sons of Asmoth, and Berchia and Jeuel the Anathothi,
1 Chronicles 12:4 and Samaia the Gabaonite, mighty among the thirty and over the thirty,
1 Chronicles 12:5 Jeremias and Jeziel and Joanan and Jozabad the Gadarathi,
1 Chronicles 12:6 Eliazai and Jarimuth and Baalia and Samaria and Saphatia the Charaiphi,
1 Chronicles 12:7 Elcana and Jesouni and Ozriel and Joazar and Jesboam the Corites,
1 Chronicles 12:8 and Elia and Zabada, sons of Iraam, sons of Gedor. —
1 Chronicles 12:9 And from Gad they separated themselves to David from the wilderness, mighty men of strength, men of battle array, carrying shields and spears; their faces were like the face of a lion, and they were swift as gazelles upon the mountains for speed.
1 Chronicles 12:10 Azer the ruler, Abdia the second, Eliab the third,
1 Chronicles 12:11 Masemannai the fourth, Jeremias the fifth,
1 Chronicles 12:12 Eththi the sixth, Eliab the seventh,
1 Chronicles 12:13 Joanan the eighth, Eleazar the ninth,
1 Chronicles 12:14 Jeremias the tenth, Machabannai the eleventh.
1 Chronicles 12:15 These, from the sons of Gad, were commanders of the army, one for a hundred, small, and great for thousands.
1 Chronicles 12:16 These crossed the Jordan in the first month, when it had overflowed all its banks; and they drove out all the inhabitants of the valleys from east to west. —
1 Chronicles 12:17 And from the sons of Benjamin and Judah they came to David’s aid.
1 Chronicles 12:18 And David went out to meet them and said to them, “If you have come to me in peace, may my heart be with you; but if to hand me over to my enemies, when there is no truth in my hand, may the God of our fathers see and reprove.”
1 Chronicles 12:19 And a spirit clothed Amasai, ruler of the thirty, and he said, “Go, and your people, David son of Jesse. Peace, peace to you, and peace to your helpers, because your God has helped you.” And David received them and appointed them leaders of the armies. —
1 Chronicles 12:20 And from Manasseh some joined David when the foreigners came against Saul for war; but he did not help them, because the rulers of the foreigners took counsel, saying, “At the heads of those men he will return to his lord Saul.”
1 Chronicles 12:21 When he went to Sikelag, from Manasseh there joined him Edna and Jozabad and Jodiel and Michael and Josabeth and Elimuth and Selathi; they were commanders of thousands belonging to Manasseh.
1 Chronicles 12:22 And they fought together with David against Geddur, because they were all mighty in strength, and were leaders in the army in power.
1 Chronicles 12:23 For day by day they came to David for a great force, like a force of God.
1 Chronicles 12:24 And these are the names of the commanders of the army, those who came to David at Hebron to turn the kingdom of Saul over to him according to the word of the Lord.
1 Chronicles 12:25 Sons of Judah, bearers of shields and bearers of spears, six thousand eight hundred mighty men of battle array.
1 Chronicles 12:26 From the sons of Simeon, mighty in strength for battle array, seven thousand one hundred.
1 Chronicles 12:27 From the sons of Levi, four thousand six hundred;
1 Chronicles 12:28 and Joadae, the leader belonging to Aaron, and with him three thousand seven hundred;
1 Chronicles 12:29 and Zadok, a young man mighty in strength, and from his father’s house twenty-two rulers.
1 Chronicles 12:30 And from the sons of Benjamin, the brothers of Saul, three thousand; and most of them still kept watch over the house of Saul.
1 Chronicles 12:31 And from the sons of Ephraim, twenty thousand eight hundred, mighty in strength, men renowned according to their fathers’ houses.
1 Chronicles 12:32 And from half the tribe of Manasseh, eighteen thousand, who were named by name to make David king.
1 Chronicles 12:33 And from the sons of Issachar, knowing understanding for the times, knowing what Israel should do for their leaders: two hundred, and all their brothers with them.
1 Chronicles 12:34 And from Zebulun, going out in battle array with every weapon of war, fifty thousand, to help David without turning aside.
1 Chronicles 12:35 And from Naphtali, one thousand rulers, and with them thirty-seven thousand with shields and spears.
1 Chronicles 12:36 And from the Danites, arrayed for war, twenty-eight thousand eight hundred.
1 Chronicles 12:37 And from Asher, going out to help in war, forty thousand.
1 Chronicles 12:38 And from beyond the Jordan, from Reuben and Gad and half the tribe of Manasseh, with every weapon of war, one hundred twenty thousand.
1 Chronicles 12:39 All these were men of war, arranging themselves for battle with a peaceful soul; and they came to Hebron to make David king over all Israel; and the rest of Israel were of one soul to make David king.
1 Chronicles 12:40 And they were there three days, eating and drinking, because their brothers had prepared for them.
1 Chronicles 12:41 And those neighboring them, as far as Issachar and Zebulun and Naphtali, brought to them on camels and donkeys and mules and calves foods, flour, cakes, raisins, wine and oil, calves and sheep in abundance, because there was joy in Israel.

## Chapter 13

1 Chronicles 13:1 And David consulted with the commanders of thousands and the commanders of hundreds, with every leader,
1 Chronicles 13:2 and David said to the whole assembly of Israel, “If it is good to you, and if it is prospered by the Lord our God, let us send to our brothers who remain in all the land of Israel, and with them the priests, the Levites, in the cities of their possession, and they shall be gathered to us;
1 Chronicles 13:3 and let us bring the ark of our God back to us, for they did not seek it from the days of Saul.”
1 Chronicles 13:4 And the whole assembly said to do so, because the word was right in the eyes of all the people.
1 Chronicles 13:5 And David assembled all Israel from the borders of Egypt and as far as the entrance of Hamath, to bring the ark of God from the city of Jarim.
1 Chronicles 13:6 And David brought it up, and all Israel went up to the city of David, which was of Judah, to bring up from there the ark of the Lord God, who sits upon the cherubim, upon which his name was called.
1 Chronicles 13:7 And they placed the ark of God upon a new cart from the house of Aminadab, and Oza and his brothers drove the cart.
1 Chronicles 13:8 And David and all Israel were playing before God with all their might, and with singers and with lyres and with nablas, with tambourines and with cymbals and with trumpets.
1 Chronicles 13:9 And they came as far as the threshing floor, and Oza stretched out his hand to hold the ark, because the calf had turned it aside.
1 Chronicles 13:10 And the Lord became angry with anger against Oza and struck him there, because he stretched out his hand upon the ark, and he died there before God.
1 Chronicles 13:11 And David was disheartened because the Lord made a breach against Oza, and he called that place Breach of Oza to this day.
1 Chronicles 13:12 And David feared God on that day, saying, “How shall I bring the ark of God to myself?”
1 Chronicles 13:13 And David did not return the ark to himself, to the city of David, and he turned it aside to the house of Abeddara the Geththite.
1 Chronicles 13:14 And the ark of God dwelt in the house of Abeddara three months, and God blessed Abeddaram and all his things.

## Chapter 14

1 Chronicles 14:1 And Hiram king of Tyre sent messengers to David, and cedar timbers, and builders of walls, and workers of wood, to build him a house.
1 Chronicles 14:2 And David knew that the Lord had prepared him over Israel, because his kingdom was exalted to a height for the sake of his people Israel.
1 Chronicles 14:3 And David took still more wives in Jerusalem, and still more sons and daughters were born to David.
1 Chronicles 14:4 And these are the names of those born to him, who were in Jerusalem: Sammaa, Isobaam, Nathan, Solomon,
1 Chronicles 14:5 and Ibaar and Elisae and Eliphalet,
1 Chronicles 14:6 and Nage and Naphag and Janouou,
1 Chronicles 14:7 and Elisamae and Balegdae and Eliphalet.
1 Chronicles 14:8 And foreigners heard that David had been anointed king over all Israel, and all the foreigners went up to seek David. And David heard and went out to meet them.
1 Chronicles 14:9 And foreigners came and gathered in the valley of the giants.
1 Chronicles 14:10 And David inquired through God, saying, “Shall I go up against the foreigners, and will you give them into my hands?” And the Lord said to him, “Go up, and I will give them into your hands.”
1 Chronicles 14:11 And he went up to Baalpharasin, and David struck them there; and David said, “God broke through my enemies by my hand like a breaking through of water.” For this reason he called the name of that place Breach of Pharasin.
1 Chronicles 14:12 And they left their gods there, and David said, “Burn them with fire.” —
1 Chronicles 14:13 And foreigners added still more, and gathered again in the valley of the giants.
1 Chronicles 14:14 And David inquired again in God, and God said to him, “You shall not go after them; turn away from them, and stand by them near the pear trees.
1 Chronicles 14:15 And it shall be, when you hear the sound of the shaking of the tops of the pear trees, then you shall go out to the battle, because God has gone out before you to strike the camp of the foreigners.”
1 Chronicles 14:16 And he did as God commanded him, and struck the camp of the foreigners from Gabaon as far as Gazara.
1 Chronicles 14:17 And David’s name came to be in all the land, and the Lord gave his fear upon all the nations.

## Chapter 15

1 Chronicles 15:1 And he made houses for himself in the city of David; and he prepared a place for the ark of God and made a tent for it.
1 Chronicles 15:2 Then David said, “It is not for anyone to carry the ark of God except the Levites, because the Lord chose them to carry the ark of the Lord and to minister to him forever.”
1 Chronicles 15:3 And David assembled all Israel to Jerusalem to bring up the ark of the Lord to the place which he had prepared for it.
1 Chronicles 15:4 And David gathered the sons of Aaron and the Levites.
1 Chronicles 15:5 From the sons of Caath: Uriel the ruler and his brothers, one hundred twenty.
1 Chronicles 15:6 From the sons of Merari: Asaia the ruler and his brothers, two hundred fifty.
1 Chronicles 15:7 From the sons of Gersam: Joel the ruler and his brothers, one hundred fifty.
1 Chronicles 15:8 From the sons of Elisaphan: Samaia the ruler and his brothers, two hundred.
1 Chronicles 15:9 From the sons of Chebron: Eliel the ruler and his brothers, eighty.
1 Chronicles 15:10 From the sons of Oziel: Aminadab the ruler and his brothers, one hundred twelve. —
1 Chronicles 15:11 And David called Sadoc and Abiathar the priests, and the Levites Uriel, Asaia, Joel, Samaia, Eliel, Aminadab,
1 Chronicles 15:12 and said to them, “You are the rulers of the fathers’ houses of the Levites; sanctify yourselves, you and your brothers, and bring up the ark of the God of Israel to the place which I prepared for it;
1 Chronicles 15:13 because, in the former time, when you were not [there], our God broke through among us, because we did not seek him according to judgment.”
1 Chronicles 15:14 And the priests and the Levites sanctified themselves to bring up the ark of the God of Israel.
1 Chronicles 15:15 And the sons of the Levites took the ark of God as Moses commanded, by the word of God, according to the writing, on carrying poles upon them. —
1 Chronicles 15:16 And David said to the rulers of the Levites, “Set their brothers, the singers, with instruments of songs, nablas and citharas and cymbals, to make a loud sound on high with a voice of gladness.”
1 Chronicles 15:17 And the Levites appointed Heman son of Joel; from his brothers, Asaph son of Barachia; and from the sons of Merari, his brothers, Ethan son of Kisaios.
1 Chronicles 15:18 And with them were their second brothers: Zacharias and Oziel and Semiramoth and Iiel and Oni and Eliab and Banaia and Maasia and Mattathia and Eliphalia and Makenia and Abeddom and Iiel and Ozias, the gatekeepers.
1 Chronicles 15:19 And the singers Heman, Asaph, and Ethan were with bronze cymbals, to make them be heard.
1 Chronicles 15:20 Zacharias and Oziel, Semiramoth, Iiel, Oni, Eliab, Masaias, Banaia, with nablas upon alamoth;
1 Chronicles 15:21 and Mattathias and Eliphalias and Makenias and Abeddom and Iiel and Ozias, with citharas of amasenith, to strengthen.
1 Chronicles 15:22 And Chonenia, ruler of the Levites, was ruler of the songs, because he was understanding.
1 Chronicles 15:23 And Barachia and Elcana were gatekeepers of the ark.
1 Chronicles 15:24 And Sobnia and Josaphat and Nathanael and Amasai and Zacharia and Banai and Eliezer the priests were sounding the trumpets before the ark of God. And Abeddom and Iia were gatekeepers of the ark of God.
1 Chronicles 15:25 And David and the elders of Israel and the commanders of thousands were going to bring up the ark of the covenant of the Lord from the house of Abeddom with gladness.
1 Chronicles 15:26 And it came to pass, when God strengthened the Levites carrying the ark of the covenant of the Lord, that they sacrificed seven calves and seven rams.
1 Chronicles 15:27 And David was girded with a linen garment, and all the Levites carrying the ark of the covenant of the Lord, and the singers, and Chonenias the ruler of the songs of the singers; and upon David was a linen garment.
1 Chronicles 15:28 And all Israel were bringing up the ark of the covenant of the Lord with signals and with the voice of a shofar and with trumpets and with cymbals, sounding aloud with nablas and with citharas.
1 Chronicles 15:29 And the ark of the covenant of the Lord came as far as the city of David, and Melchol daughter of Saul peered through the window and saw King David dancing and playing, and she despised him in her soul.

## Chapter 16

1 Chronicles 16:1 And they brought in the ark of God and set it in the midst of the tent which David had pitched for it, and they brought whole burnt offerings and peace offerings before God.
1 Chronicles 16:2 And David finished offering whole burnt offerings and peace offerings, and blessed the people in the name of the Lord.
1 Chronicles 16:3 And he distributed to every man of Israel, from man to woman, to each one a bread-loaf and a portion.
1 Chronicles 16:4 And he appointed before the ark of the covenant of the Lord from the Levites those ministering, raising their voices, giving thanks, and praising the Lord God of Israel:
1 Chronicles 16:5 Asaph the leader, and second to him Zacharia, Iiel, Semiramoth, Iiel, Mattathias, Eliab, Banaia, Abeddom, and Iiel, with instruments, nablas and citharas; and Asaph with cymbals, sounding aloud;
1 Chronicles 16:6 and Banaia and Oziel the priests with trumpets continually before the ark of the covenant of God.
1 Chronicles 16:7 On that day then David appointed at the beginning of praising the Lord by the hand of Asaph and his brothers:
1 Chronicles 16:8 Give thanks to the Lord, call upon him in his name, make known among the peoples his deeds;
1 Chronicles 16:9 sing to him and hymn to him; recount to all his wonders which the Lord did.
1 Chronicles 16:10 Praise in his holy name; the heart seeking his good pleasure shall rejoice.
1 Chronicles 16:11 Seek the Lord and be strong; seek his face continually.
1 Chronicles 16:12 Remember his wonders which he did, his portents and the judgments of his mouth,
1 Chronicles 16:13 o seed of Israel, his servants, sons of Jacob, his chosen ones.
1 Chronicles 16:14 He himself is the Lord our God; his judgments are in all the earth.
1 Chronicles 16:15 Remembering forever his covenant, his word which he commanded for a thousand generations,
1 Chronicles 16:16 which he made with Abraham, and his oath with Isaac;
1 Chronicles 16:17 he established it for Jacob as an ordinance, for Israel as an eternal covenant,
1 Chronicles 16:18 saying, “To you I will give the land of Chanaan, a measured portion of your inheritance.”
1 Chronicles 16:19 When they were very few in number, when they were diminished, and sojourned in it,
1 Chronicles 16:20 and they went from nation to nation and from kingdom to another people,
1 Chronicles 16:21 he did not allow any man to exercise power over them, and he reproved kings on their account:
1 Chronicles 16:22 “Do not touch my anointed ones, and do not act wickedly among my prophets.”
1 Chronicles 16:23 Sing to the Lord, all the earth; announce his salvation from day to day.
1 Chronicles 16:25 For great is the Lord and exceedingly praiseworthy; he is fearful above all the gods.
1 Chronicles 16:26 For all the gods of the nations are idols, and our God made heaven.
1 Chronicles 16:27 Glory and praise are before him; strength and boasting are in his place.
1 Chronicles 16:28 Give to the Lord, families of the nations; give to the Lord glory and strength.
1 Chronicles 16:29 Give to the Lord the glory of his name; take gifts and bring them before him, and worship the Lord in his holy courts.
1 Chronicles 16:30 Let all the earth fear before him; let the earth be set right and not be shaken.
1 Chronicles 16:31 Let heaven rejoice, and let the earth exult, and let them say among the nations, “The Lord is reigning.”
1 Chronicles 16:32 The sea shall roar with its fullness, and the tree of the field and all that is in it;
1 Chronicles 16:33 then the trees of the forest shall rejoice before the Lord, because he came to judge the earth.
1 Chronicles 16:34 Give thanks to the Lord, because he is good, because his mercy is forever.
1 Chronicles 16:35 And say, “Save us, O God of our salvation, and gather us from among the nations, to praise your holy name and to boast in your praises.”
1 Chronicles 16:36 Blessed be the Lord God of Israel from everlasting and unto everlasting; and all the people shall say, “Amen.” And they praised the Lord.
1 Chronicles 16:37 And they left Asaph and his brothers there before the ark of the covenant of the Lord, to minister before the ark continually, from day to day;
1 Chronicles 16:38 and Abeddom and his brothers, sixty-eight, and Abeddom son of Idithon and Ossa, as gatekeepers.
1 Chronicles 16:39 And Sadoc the priest and his brother priests before the tent of the Lord in Bama, which is in Gabaon,
1 Chronicles 16:40 to offer whole burnt offerings to the Lord upon the altar of whole burnt offerings continually, morning and evening, and according to all that is written in the law of the Lord, as much as he commanded concerning the sons of Israel by the hand of Moses, the servant of God;
1 Chronicles 16:41 and with him Heman and Idithon and the rest chosen by name to praise the Lord, because his mercy is forever,
1 Chronicles 16:42 and with them trumpets and cymbals to sound aloud, and instruments of the songs of God; the sons of Idithon were at the gate.
1 Chronicles 16:43 And all the people went, each to his own house, and David turned back to bless his house.

## Chapter 17

1 Chronicles 17:1 And it came to pass, when David dwelt in his house, that David said to Nathan the prophet, “Behold, I dwell in a house of cedar, and the ark of the covenant of the Lord is under hides.”
1 Chronicles 17:2 And Nathan said to David, “Do all that is in your soul, because God is with you.” —
1 Chronicles 17:3 And it came to pass in that night, and the word of the Lord came to Nathan, saying,
1 Chronicles 17:4 “Go and say to David my servant, ‘Thus says the Lord: You shall not build a house for me to dwell in it;
1 Chronicles 17:5 for I have not dwelt in a house from the day I brought Israel up until this day, but I was in a tent and in a dwelling.
1 Chronicles 17:6 In all the places through which I passed, throughout all Israel, did I ever speak to one tribe of Israel, whom I appointed to shepherd my people, saying, “Why have you not built me a house of cedar?”’
1 Chronicles 17:7 And now thus you shall say to my servant David: ‘Thus says the Lord Almighty: I took you from the sheepfold, from behind the flocks, to be a leader over my people Israel;
1 Chronicles 17:8 and I was with you in all the places where you went, and I destroyed all your enemies from before you, and I made a name for you like the name of the great ones who are upon the earth.
1 Chronicles 17:9 And I will appoint a place for my people Israel and will plant him, and he shall dwell by himself and shall worry no more; and injustice shall no longer continue to humble him as from the beginning,
1 Chronicles 17:10 and from the days when I appointed judges over my people Israel, I humbled all your enemies; and I will increase you, and the Lord will build a house for you.
1 Chronicles 17:11 And it shall be, when your days are fulfilled and you sleep with your fathers, that I will raise up your seed after you, who shall be from your belly, and I will prepare his kingdom.
1 Chronicles 17:12 He himself shall build a house for me, and I will make his throne stand upright forever.
1 Chronicles 17:13 I will be a father to him, and he shall be a son to me; and I will not remove my mercy from him, as I removed it from those who were before you.
1 Chronicles 17:14 And I will make him firm in my house and in his kingdom forever, and his throne shall be established upright forever.’”
1 Chronicles 17:15 According to all these words and according to all this vision, thus Nathan spoke to David. —
1 Chronicles 17:16 And King David came and sat before the Lord, and said, “Who am I, Lord God, and who is my house, that you have loved me forever?
1 Chronicles 17:17 And these things were small in your sight, O God, and you spoke concerning the house of your servant from afar, and looked upon me as a vision of a man, and exalted me, Lord God.
1 Chronicles 17:18 What further will David add to you, to glorify [you]? And you know your servant.
1 Chronicles 17:19 And according to your heart you did all this greatness.
1 Chronicles 17:20 Lord, there is none like you, and there is none besides you in all that we have heard with our ears.
1 Chronicles 17:21 And there is no nation still upon the earth like your people Israel, whom God guided to redeem for himself as a people, to make for himself a great and conspicuous name, to cast out from before your people the nations whom you redeemed from Egypt.
1 Chronicles 17:22 And you gave your people Israel to yourself as a people forever, and you, Lord, became their God.
1 Chronicles 17:23 And now, Lord, let your word which you spoke to your servant and concerning his house be made firm forever,
1 Chronicles 17:24 saying, ‘Lord, Lord Almighty, God of Israel, and the house of David your servant is established before you.’
1 Chronicles 17:25 For you, Lord, opened the ear of your servant to build a house for him; for this reason your servant found [occasion] to pray before you.
1 Chronicles 17:26 And now, Lord, you are yourself God, and you spoke these good things concerning your servant.
1 Chronicles 17:27 And now you began to bless the house of your servant, that it may be forever before you; for you, Lord, blessed it, and bless it forever.

## Chapter 18

1 Chronicles 18:1 And it came to pass after these things that David struck the foreigners and routed them, and took Geth and its villages from the hand of the foreigners.
1 Chronicles 18:2 And he struck Moab, and the Moabites became servants to David, bringing gifts.
1 Chronicles 18:3 And David struck Adraazar king of Souba, Hamath, as he went to establish his hand upon the river Euphrates.
1 Chronicles 18:4 And David captured from them one thousand chariots and seven thousand horses and twenty thousand foot soldiers; and David dismantled all the chariots, and left one hundred chariots from them.
1 Chronicles 18:5 And a Syrian came from Damascus to help Adraazar king of Souba, and David struck among the Syrians twenty-two thousand men.
1 Chronicles 18:6 And David placed a garrison in Syria toward Damascus, and the Syrians became servants to David, bringing gifts. And the Lord saved David in all the places where he went.
1 Chronicles 18:7 And David took the golden collars which were upon the servants of Adraazar, and brought them to Jerusalem.
1 Chronicles 18:8 And from Metabechas and from the chosen cities of Adraazar David took very much bronze; from it Solomon made the bronze sea and the pillars and the bronze vessels.
1 Chronicles 18:9 And Thoa king of Hamath heard that David had struck the whole force of Adraazar king of Souba,
1 Chronicles 18:10 and he sent Idouram his son to King David to inquire of him about peace and to bless him concerning that which he had fought against Adraazar and struck him, because Thoa was a man at war with Adraazar, and all the vessels of silver and gold.
1 Chronicles 18:11 And these David sanctified to the Lord together with the silver and the gold which he took from all the nations, from Idumea and Moab and from the sons of Ammon and from the foreigners and from Amalek.
1 Chronicles 18:12 And Abessa son of Sarouia struck Idumea in the valley of salt, eighteen thousand,
1 Chronicles 18:13 and he placed garrisons in the valley; and all the Idumeans became servants of David. And the Lord saved David in all the places where he went.
1 Chronicles 18:14 And David reigned over all Israel, and he was doing judgment and righteousness for all his people.
1 Chronicles 18:15 And Joab son of Sarouia was over the army, and Josaphat son of Achiloud was the record-writer,
1 Chronicles 18:16 and Sadoc son of Achitob and Achimelech son of Abiathar were priests, and Sousas was the scribe,
1 Chronicles 18:17 and Banaias son of Jodae was over the Chereththi and the Pheleththi, and the sons of David were the first successors of the king.

## Chapter 19

1 Chronicles 19:1 And it came to pass after these things that Naas king of the sons of Ammon died, and Anan his son reigned in his place.
1 Chronicles 19:2 And David said, “I will do mercy with Anan son of Naas, as his father did mercy with me.” And David sent messengers to comfort him concerning his father. And David’s servants came to the land of the sons of Ammon to comfort him.
1 Chronicles 19:3 And the rulers of Ammon said to Anan, “Is David not honoring your father before you, because he sent comforters to you? Have his servants not come to you in order to search out and spy out the land?”
1 Chronicles 19:4 And Anan took David’s servants and shaved them, and cut away half of their garments up to the upper edge, and sent them away.
1 Chronicles 19:5 And they came to report to David about the men, and he sent to meet them, because they were greatly dishonored. And the king said, “Stay in Jericho until your beards grow, and then return.” —
1 Chronicles 19:6 And the sons of Ammon saw that the people of David had been shamed; and Anan and the sons of Ammon sent one thousand talents of silver to hire for themselves from Syria of Mesopotamia, and from Syria of Mocha, and from Soba, chariots and horsemen.
1 Chronicles 19:7 And they hired for themselves thirty-two thousand chariots, and the king of Mocha and his people; and they came and encamped opposite Maidaba. And the sons of Ammon gathered from their cities and came to wage war.
1 Chronicles 19:8 And David heard, and sent Joab and the whole army of the mighty men.
1 Chronicles 19:9 And the sons of Ammon went out and arrayed themselves for war by the gate of the city, and the kings who had come encamped by themselves in the plain.
1 Chronicles 19:10 And Joab saw that the opposing forces had come to fight against him in front and behind, and he selected from every young man of Israel, and they arrayed themselves opposite the Syrian;
1 Chronicles 19:11 and he put the rest of the people in the hand of Abessa his brother, and they arrayed themselves opposite the sons of Ammon.
1 Chronicles 19:12 And he said, “If the Syrian prevails over me, you shall be a salvation for me; and if the sons of Ammon prevail over you, I will save you.
1 Chronicles 19:13 Be manly, and let us grow strong for our people and for the cities of our God; and the Lord will do what is good in his eyes.”
1 Chronicles 19:14 And Joab and the people with him arrayed themselves for war opposite the Syrians, and they fled from him.
1 Chronicles 19:15 And the sons of Ammon saw that the Syrians had fled, and they too fled from before Joab and from before Abessa his brother, and came into the city. And Joab came to Jerusalem. —
1 Chronicles 19:16 And the Syrian saw that Israel had routed him, and he sent messengers, and they brought the Syrian out from beyond the river; and Sophach, chief general of the force of Adraazar, was before them.
1 Chronicles 19:17 And it was reported to David, and he gathered all Israel, and crossed the Jordan, and came upon them and arrayed himself against them; and the Syrian arrayed himself opposite David, and they fought against him.
1 Chronicles 19:18 And the Syrian fled from before David, and David killed from among the Syrians seven thousand chariots and forty thousand foot soldiers; and he killed Sophach, chief general of the force.
1 Chronicles 19:19 And the servants of Adraazar saw that they had stumbled before Israel, and they made an arrangement with David and served him; and the Syrian was no longer willing to help the sons of Ammon.

## Chapter 20

1 Chronicles 20:1 And it came to pass in the coming year, at the going out of the kings, that Joab led out the whole force of the army, and they ravaged the land of the sons of Ammon; and he came and encircled Rabbah. And David was sitting in Jerusalem; and Joab struck Rabbah and demolished it.
1 Chronicles 20:2 And David took the crown of Molchol their king from his head, and its weight was found to be a talent of gold, and there was a precious stone in it, and it was upon David’s head; and he brought out very many spoils of the city.
1 Chronicles 20:3 And he led out the people who were in it, and sawed them with saws and with iron axes; and thus David did to all the sons of Ammon. And David and all his people returned to Jerusalem.
1 Chronicles 20:4 And it came to pass after these things that there was still war in Gezer with the foreigners. Then Sobochai the Ousathi struck Saphu from among the sons of the giants and humbled him. —
1 Chronicles 20:5 And there was still war with the foreigners. And Ellanan son of Iair struck Leemi, brother of Goliath the Geththite, and the wood of his spear was like a weaver’s shuttle. —
1 Chronicles 20:6 And there was still war in Geth, and there was a man exceedingly great, and his fingers were six and six, twenty-four; and this man was a descendant of the giants.
1 Chronicles 20:7 And he reproached Israel, and Jonathan son of Samma, brother of David, struck him. —
1 Chronicles 20:8 These were born of Rapha in Geth; all were four giants, and they fell by the hand of David and by the hand of his servants.

## Chapter 21

1 Chronicles 21:1 And an adversary stood in Israel and stirred David up to count Israel.
1 Chronicles 21:2 And King David said to Joab and to the rulers of the force, “Go, count Israel from Bersabee and as far as Dan, and bring [the count] to me, and I shall know their number.”
1 Chronicles 21:3 And Joab said, “May the Lord add to his people a hundredfold as many as they are, and may the eyes of my lord the king see them. All are servants to my lord. Why does my lord seek this? So that it may not become sin for Israel.”
1 Chronicles 21:4 But the word of the king prevailed over Joab. And Joab went out and passed through every border of Israel, and came to Jerusalem.
1 Chronicles 21:5 And Joab gave David the number of the mustered people; and all Israel was one million one hundred thousand men drawing the sword, and Judah was four hundred eighty thousand men drawing the sword.
1 Chronicles 21:6 But Levi and Benjamin he did not number among them, because the word of the king had prevailed over Joab.
1 Chronicles 21:7 And this matter appeared evil before God, and he struck Israel.
1 Chronicles 21:8 And David said to God, “I have sinned exceedingly, because I did this thing; and now, please remove the evil of your servant, because I have acted foolishly exceedingly.”
1 Chronicles 21:9 And the Lord spoke to Gad, the seer of David, saying,
1 Chronicles 21:10 “Go and speak to David, saying, ‘Thus says the Lord: I am raising up three things against you; choose for yourself one of them, and I will do it to you.’”
1 Chronicles 21:11 And Gad came to David and said to him, “Thus says the Lord: Choose for yourself
1 Chronicles 21:12 either three years of famine, or three months for you to flee from before your enemies, with the sword of your enemies to destroy, or three days of the sword of the Lord and death in the land, with the angel of the Lord destroying in all the inheritance of Israel. And now see what I shall answer the one who sent me with a word.”
1 Chronicles 21:13 And David said to Gad, “All three are distressing for me exceedingly. Let me fall, then, into the hands of the Lord, because his compassions are exceedingly many; and into the hands of men I shall certainly not fall.”
1 Chronicles 21:14 And the Lord gave death in Israel, and seventy thousand men of Israel fell.
1 Chronicles 21:15 And God sent an angel to Jerusalem to destroy it. And as he was destroying, the Lord saw and repented concerning the evil, and said to the destroying angel, “Let it be enough for you; release your hand.” And the angel of the Lord was standing at the threshing floor of Orna the Jebusite.
1 Chronicles 21:16 And David lifted his eyes and saw the angel of the Lord standing between earth and heaven, and his sword drawn in his hand, stretched out over Jerusalem; and David and the elders, clothed in sackcloth, fell upon their faces.
1 Chronicles 21:17 And David said to God, “Was it not I who said to count the people? And I am the one who sinned; doing evil, I did evil. And these sheep, what did they do? Lord God, let your hand be upon me and upon the house of my father, and not upon your people for destruction, O Lord.”
1 Chronicles 21:18 And an angel of the Lord said to Gad to say to David that he should go up to set an altar to the Lord at the threshing floor of Orna the Jebusite.
1 Chronicles 21:19 And David went up according to the word of Gad, which he spoke in the name of the Lord.
1 Chronicles 21:20 And Orna turned and saw the king, and four of his sons with him, methachabin; and Orna was threshing wheat.
1 Chronicles 21:21 And David came to Orna, and Orna went out from the threshing floor and bowed to David, with his face upon the earth.
1 Chronicles 21:22 And David said to Orna, “Give me the place of your threshing floor, and I will build upon it an altar to the Lord. Give it to me for its worthy silver, and the plague shall cease from the people.”
1 Chronicles 21:23 And Orna said to David, “Take it for yourself, and let my lord the king do what is good before him. See, I have given the calves for a burnt offering, and the plow and the wagons for wood, and the grain for an offering; I have given everything.”
1 Chronicles 21:24 And King David said to Orna, “No, for buying I shall buy it for worthy silver, because I shall certainly not take what is yours for the Lord, to offer a burnt offering to the Lord as a gift.”
1 Chronicles 21:25 And David gave to Orna, in his place, six hundred shekels of gold by weight.
1 Chronicles 21:26 And David built an altar to the Lord there and brought up whole burnt offerings and peace offerings; and he cried out to the Lord, and he heard him with fire from heaven upon the altar of burnt offering, and consumed the whole burnt offering.
1 Chronicles 21:27 And the Lord spoke to the angel, and he put the sword into its sheath. —
1 Chronicles 21:28 At that time, when David saw that the Lord had heard him at the threshing floor of Orna the Jebusite, he sacrificed there.
1 Chronicles 21:29 And the tent of the Lord which Moses made in the wilderness, and the altar of whole burnt offerings, were at that time in Bama, in Gabaon;
1 Chronicles 21:30 and David was not able to go before it to seek God, because he hurried away from before the sword of the angel of the Lord.

## Chapter 22

1 Chronicles 22:1 And David said, “This is the house of the Lord God, and this is the altar for whole burnt offerings for Israel.”
1 Chronicles 22:2 And David said to gather all the proselytes in the land of Israel, and he appointed stonecutters to cut dressed stones for building a house for God.
1 Chronicles 22:3 And David prepared much iron for the nails of the doors and of the gates and for the pivots, and bronze in abundance, without weight;
1 Chronicles 22:4 and cedar timbers without number, because the Sidonians and the Tyrians brought many cedar timbers to David.
1 Chronicles 22:5 And David said, “Solomon my son is a tender boy, and the house to be built for the Lord is for greatness on high, for a name and for glory in all the earth; I shall prepare it for him.” And David prepared abundantly before his death. —
1 Chronicles 22:6 And he called Solomon his son and commanded him to build the house for the Lord God of Israel.
1 Chronicles 22:7 And David said to Solomon, “Child, it came upon my soul to build a house for the name of the Lord God.
1 Chronicles 22:8 And the word of the Lord came upon me, saying, ‘You poured out blood in abundance and made great wars; you shall not build a house for my name, because you poured out much blood upon the earth before me.
1 Chronicles 22:9 Behold, a son is born to you; he shall be a man of rest, and I will give him rest from all his enemies round about, because Solomon is his name, and I will give peace and quiet upon Israel in his days.
1 Chronicles 22:10 He shall build a house for my name, and he shall be a son to me, and I shall be a father to him; and I will make upright the throne of his kingdom in Israel forever.’
1 Chronicles 22:11 And now, my son, the Lord shall be with you, and he shall prosper, and you shall build a house for the Lord your God, as he spoke concerning you.
1 Chronicles 22:12 But may the Lord give you wisdom and understanding, and strengthen you over Israel, to keep and to do the law of the Lord your God.
1 Chronicles 22:13 Then you will prosper, if you keep to do the ordinances and the judgments which the Lord commanded Moses concerning Israel. Be manly and be strong; do not fear or be dismayed.
1 Chronicles 22:14 And behold, in my poverty I prepared for the house of the Lord one hundred thousand talents of gold and one thousand thousand talents of silver, and bronze and iron without weight, because it is in abundance; and I prepared wood and stones, and add to these.
1 Chronicles 22:15 And with you are many workers: craftsmen and builders of stones, and workers of wood, and everyone skilled in every work.
1 Chronicles 22:16 In gold, in silver, in bronze, and in iron there is no number. Rise and do, and may the Lord be with you. —
1 Chronicles 22:17 And David commanded all the rulers of Israel to assist Solomon his son,
1 Chronicles 22:18 saying, “Is not the Lord with you? And he gave you rest round about, because he gave the inhabitants of the land into your hands, and the land was subdued before the Lord and before his people.
1 Chronicles 22:19 Now give your hearts and your souls to seek the Lord your God, and rise and build a sanctuary for the Lord your God, to bring the ark of the covenant of the Lord and the holy vessels of God into the house being built for the name of the Lord.”

## Chapter 23

1 Chronicles 23:1 And David was old and full of days, and he made Solomon his son king in his place over Israel.
1 Chronicles 23:2 And he gathered all the rulers of Israel and the priests and the Levites.
1 Chronicles 23:3 And the Levites were counted from thirty years old and above, and their number, by headcount, was thirty-eight thousand men.
1 Chronicles 23:4 From these, overseers over the works of the house of the Lord were twenty-four thousand, and scribes and judges were six thousand,
1 Chronicles 23:5 and gatekeepers were four thousand, and those praising the Lord with the instruments which he had made to praise the Lord were four thousand. —
1 Chronicles 23:6 And David divided them into courses among the sons of Levi: Gedsōn, Caath, and Merari;
1 Chronicles 23:7 and Parosom, Edan, and Semee.
1 Chronicles 23:8 Sons of Edan: the ruler Iiel, and Zethom, and Joel, three.
1 Chronicles 23:9 Sons of Semee: Salomith and Iiel and Aidan, three. These were the rulers of the fathers’ houses belonging to Edan.
1 Chronicles 23:10 And the sons of Semee: Ieth and Ziza and Joas and Beria; these were the sons of Semee, four.
1 Chronicles 23:11 And Ieth was the ruler, and Ziza the second; and Joas and Beria did not multiply sons, and they became one fathers’ house for one enrollment. —
1 Chronicles 23:12 Sons of Caath: Ambram, Issaar, Chebron, Oziel, four.
1 Chronicles 23:13 Sons of Ambram: Aaron and Moses. And Aaron was set apart to sanctify the holy of holies, he and his sons forever, to burn incense before the Lord, to minister, and to pray by his name forever.
1 Chronicles 23:14 And Moses, the man of God, his sons were called into the tribe of Levi.
1 Chronicles 23:15 Sons of Moses: Gersam and Eliezer.
1 Chronicles 23:16 Sons of Gersam: Shubael the ruler.
1 Chronicles 23:17 And Eliezer had sons: Raabia the ruler; and Eliezer had no other sons. And the sons of Raabia increased greatly.
1 Chronicles 23:18 Sons of Issaar: Salomoth the ruler.
1 Chronicles 23:19 Sons of Chebron: Idud the ruler, Amadia the second, Oziel the third, Ikemias the fourth.
1 Chronicles 23:20 Sons of Oziel: Michas the ruler and Isia the second. —
1 Chronicles 23:21 Sons of Merari: Mooli and Mousi. Sons of Mooli: Eleazar and Kis.
1 Chronicles 23:22 And Eleazar died, and he had no sons, but only daughters; and the sons of Kis, their brothers, took them.
1 Chronicles 23:23 Sons of Mousi: Mooli and Eder and Iarimoth, three. —
1 Chronicles 23:24 These are the sons of Levi according to their fathers’ houses, the rulers of their fathers’ houses according to their enrollment, according to the number of their names, by headcount, doing the works of the service of the house of the Lord from twenty years old and above.
1 Chronicles 23:25 For David said, “The Lord God of Israel has given rest to his people, and he has dwelt in Jerusalem forever.
1 Chronicles 23:26 And the Levites were not carrying the tent and all its vessels for its service,
1 Chronicles 23:27 because in the last words of David the number of the sons of Levi is from twenty years old and above,
1 Chronicles 23:28 because he set them under the hand of Aaron to minister in the house of the Lord, over the courts and over the chambers, and over the cleansing of all the holy things, and over the works of the service of the house of God,
1 Chronicles 23:29 for the showbread, for the fine flour of the offering, and for the unleavened cakes, and for the frying pan, and for the mixed dough, and for every measure,
1 Chronicles 23:30 and to stand in the morning to praise and give thanks to the Lord, and likewise in the evening,
1 Chronicles 23:31 and over all the whole burnt offerings brought to the Lord on the Sabbaths and at the new moons and at the feasts, by number, according to the judgment concerning them, continually to the Lord.
1 Chronicles 23:32 And they shall keep the watches of the tent of the testimony and the watches of their brothers, the sons of Aaron, to minister in the house of the Lord.”

## Chapter 24

1 Chronicles 24:1 And for the sons of Aaron were divisions: sons of Aaron, Nadab and Abiud, Eleazar and Ithamar.
1 Chronicles 24:2 And Nadab and Abiud died before their father, and they had no sons; and Eleazar and Ithamar served as priests.
1 Chronicles 24:3 And David divided them, and Sadoc from the sons of Eleazar, and Achimelech from the sons of Ithamar, according to their enrollment, according to their service, according to their fathers’ houses.
1 Chronicles 24:4 And sons of Eleazar were found more numerous as rulers of the mighty than sons of Ithamar, and he divided them: for the sons of Eleazar, sixteen rulers of fathers’ houses, and for the sons of Ithamar, eight according to fathers’ houses.
1 Chronicles 24:5 And he divided them by lots, these with those, because they were rulers of the holy things and rulers of the Lord among the sons of Eleazar and among the sons of Ithamar.
1 Chronicles 24:6 And Samaia son of Nathanael, the scribe from Levi, wrote them before the king and the rulers, and Sadoc the priest and Achimelech son of Abiathar, and the rulers of the fathers’ houses of the priests and of the Levites: one fathers’ house each for Eleazar, and one each for Ithamar. —
1 Chronicles 24:7 And the first lot came out for Iarib, for Ideia the second,
1 Chronicles 24:8 for Charem the third, for Seorim the fourth,
1 Chronicles 24:9 for Melchia the fifth, for Miamin the sixth,
1 Chronicles 24:10 for Cos the seventh, for Abia the eighth,
1 Chronicles 24:11 for Jesus the ninth, for Sechenia the tenth,
1 Chronicles 24:12 for Eliasib the eleventh, for Iakim the twelfth,
1 Chronicles 24:13 for Ochophpha the thirteenth, for Isbaal the fourteenth,
1 Chronicles 24:14 for Belga the fifteenth, for Emmer the sixteenth,
1 Chronicles 24:15 for Chezir the seventeenth, for Aphesse the eighteenth,
1 Chronicles 24:16 for Phetaia the nineteenth, for Ezekiel the twentieth,
1 Chronicles 24:17 for Jachin the twenty-first, for Gamoul the twenty-second,
1 Chronicles 24:18 for Dalaia the twenty-third, for Maasai the twenty-fourth.
1 Chronicles 24:19 This was their enrollment according to their service, to enter the house of the Lord according to their judgment, through the hand of Aaron their father, as the Lord God of Israel commanded.
1 Chronicles 24:20 And for the remaining sons of Levi: for the sons of Ambram, Shubael; for the sons of Shubael, Iadia.
1 Chronicles 24:21 For Raabia, Iesias the ruler.
1 Chronicles 24:22 And for Issari, Salomoth; for the sons of Salomoth, Iath.
1 Chronicles 24:23 Sons of Iediou: Amadia the second, Iaziel the third, Iocom the fourth.
1 Chronicles 24:24 Sons of Oziel: Micha; sons of Micha: Samir.
1 Chronicles 24:25 Brother of Micha: Isia; sons of Isia: Zacharia.
1 Chronicles 24:26 Sons of Merari: Mooli and Mousi; sons of Ozia, sons of Bonni.
1 Chronicles 24:27 Sons of Merari belonging to Ozia: his sons Isoam and Zachour and Abdi.
1 Chronicles 24:28 For Mooli, Eleazar and Ithamar; and Eleazar died, and he had no sons.
1 Chronicles 24:29 For Kis: sons of Kis, Iramel.
1 Chronicles 24:30 And sons of Mousi: Mooli and Eder and Iarimoth. These are the sons of the Levites according to their fathers’ houses.
1 Chronicles 24:31 And they also took lots, like their brothers the sons of Aaron, before the king and Sadoc and Achimelech and the rulers of the fathers’ houses of the priests and the Levites, the patriarchs araab, like his younger brothers.

## Chapter 25

1 Chronicles 25:1 And David the king and the commanders of the force appointed for the works the sons of Asaph and Heman and Idithon, those speaking forth with citharas and nablas and cymbals. And their number came to be by headcount, as they were working in their works:
1 Chronicles 25:2 sons of Asaph: Zachour and Joseph and Nethanias and Erael, sons of Asaph following Asaph the prophet, following the king.
1 Chronicles 25:3 For Idithon, sons of Idithon: Godolia and Souri and Isaias and Semei and Asabia and Mattathias, six, with their father Idithon, playing on the cithara, thanksgiving and praise to the Lord.
1 Chronicles 25:4 For Heman, sons of Heman: Boukias and Manthanias and Azarael and Shubael and Ierimoth and Ananias and Anani and Eliatha and Godollathi and Romemthi — ōd and Jesbacasa and Mallithi and Othēri and Meazoth;
1 Chronicles 25:5 all these were sons of Heman, the one playing for the king in the words of God, to raise up a horn; and God gave Heman fourteen sons and three daughters.
1 Chronicles 25:6 All these were with their father, hymn-singing in the house of the Lord with cymbals and nablas and citharas, following the king and Asaph and Idithon and Heman.
1 Chronicles 25:7 And their number, with their brothers, those taught to sing to the Lord, everyone understanding, came to two hundred eighty-eight. —
1 Chronicles 25:8 And they too cast lots for the courses, for the small and the great, for the skilled and those learning.
1 Chronicles 25:9 And the first lot came out for his sons and brothers, for Asaph, for Joseph, Godolia; the second, Henaia, his brothers and sons, twelve;
1 Chronicles 25:10 the third, Zachour, his sons and brothers, twelve;
1 Chronicles 25:11 the fourth, Jesdri, his sons and brothers, twelve;
1 Chronicles 25:12 the fifth, Nethanias, his sons and brothers, twelve;
1 Chronicles 25:13 the sixth, Boukias, his sons and brothers, twelve;
1 Chronicles 25:14 the seventh, Iseriel, his sons and brothers, twelve;
1 Chronicles 25:15 the eighth, Josia, his sons and brothers, twelve;
1 Chronicles 25:16 the ninth, Manthanias, his sons and brothers, twelve;
1 Chronicles 25:17 the tenth, Semei, his sons and brothers, twelve;
1 Chronicles 25:18 the eleventh, Azaria, his sons and brothers, twelve;
1 Chronicles 25:19 the twelfth, Asabia, his sons and brothers, twelve;
1 Chronicles 25:20 the thirteenth, Shubael, his sons and brothers, twelve;
1 Chronicles 25:21 the fourteenth, Mattathias, his sons and brothers, twelve;
1 Chronicles 25:22 the fifteenth, Ierimoth, his sons and brothers, twelve;
1 Chronicles 25:23 the sixteenth, Ananias, his sons and brothers, twelve;
1 Chronicles 25:24 the seventeenth, Jesbacasa, his sons and brothers, twelve;
1 Chronicles 25:25 the eighteenth, Anani, his sons and brothers, twelve;
1 Chronicles 25:26 the nineteenth, Mellethi, his sons and brothers, twelve;
1 Chronicles 25:27 the twentieth, Eliatha, his sons and brothers, twelve;
1 Chronicles 25:28 the twenty-first, Ethir, his sons and brothers, twelve;
1 Chronicles 25:29 the twenty-second, Godollathi, his sons and brothers, twelve;
1 Chronicles 25:30 the twenty-third, Meazoth, his sons and brothers, twelve;
1 Chronicles 25:31 the twenty-fourth, Romemthi — ōd, his sons and brothers, twelve.

## Chapter 26

1 Chronicles 26:1 For divisions of the gates: for the sons of Koreim, Mosollamia son of Kore, from the sons of Abiasaph.
1 Chronicles 26:2 And Mosollamia had sons: Zacharia the firstborn, Idiel the second, Zabadas the third, Iethnouel the fourth,
1 Chronicles 26:3 Olam the fifth, Joanan the sixth, Eliōenai the seventh.
1 Chronicles 26:4 And for Abeddom, sons: Samaia the firstborn, Jozabad the second, Joaa the third, Sochar the fourth, Nathanael the fifth,
1 Chronicles 26:5 Amiel the sixth, Issachar the seventh, Phollathi the eighth, because God blessed him.
1 Chronicles 26:6 And for Samaia his son, sons were born: sons of the firstborn Rosai, for his fathers’ house, because they were mighty.
1 Chronicles 26:7 Sons of Samaia: Gothni and Raphael and Obed and Elzabad and Achiu, mighty sons; Eliou and Sabchia and Isbakom.
1 Chronicles 26:8 All these were from the sons of Abeddom, they and their brothers and their sons, doing mightily in the work; all of them, sixty-two, belonging to Abeddom.
1 Chronicles 26:9 And for Mosollamia, sons and brothers, eighteen mighty men.
1 Chronicles 26:10 And for Osa, from the sons of Merari, sons keeping the office, because he was not a firstborn, and his father made him ruler
1 Chronicles 26:11 of the second division; Tablai the third, Zacharia the fourth. All these, sons and brothers of Osa, were thirteen. —
1 Chronicles 26:12 These were the divisions of the gatekeepers, for the rulers of the mighty men, courses like their brothers, to minister in the house of the Lord.
1 Chronicles 26:13 And they cast lots, for the small and for the great, according to their fathers’ houses, for gate and gate.
1 Chronicles 26:14 And the lot for the east fell to Salamia and Zacharia; the sons of Joas for Melchia cast lots, and the lot came out for the north;
1 Chronicles 26:15 for Abeddom, the south, opposite the house of esefin;
1 Chronicles 26:16 for the second; for Osa, westward, after the gate of the chamber of the ascent; watch opposite watch.
1 Chronicles 26:17 For the east, six by day; for the north, four by day; for the south, four by day; and for esefin, two;
1 Chronicles 26:18 for those relieving [the watch]; and toward the west, four; and at the path, two relieving [the watch].
1 Chronicles 26:19 These are the divisions of the doorkeepers, for the sons of Kore and for the sons of Merari.
1 Chronicles 26:20 And their brothers the Levites were over the treasures of the house of the Lord and over the treasures of the dedicated things.
1 Chronicles 26:21 Sons of Ladan, sons of Gershoni belonging to Ladan, rulers of fathers’ houses belonging to Ladan the Gershonite: Iiel.
1 Chronicles 26:22 And the sons of Iiel, Zethom and Joel, the brothers, were over the treasures of the house of the Lord.
1 Chronicles 26:23 For Ambram and Issaar, Chebron and Oziel:
1 Chronicles 26:24 and Shubael, of Gersam, of Moses, was leader over the treasures.
1 Chronicles 26:25 And for his brother Eliezer: Raabias his son, and Josaias and Joram and Zechri and Salomoth.
1 Chronicles 26:26 This Salomoth and his brothers were over all the treasures of the holy things which David the king and the rulers of the fathers’ houses, commanders of thousands and of hundreds and leaders of the force, had consecrated,
1 Chronicles 26:27 which he took from the wars and from the spoils, and consecrated from them, so as not to delay the building of the house of God;
1 Chronicles 26:28 and over all the holy things of Samuel the prophet and Saul son of Kis and Abennēr son of Ner and Joab son of Sarouia; everything which they consecrated was by the hand of Salomoth and his brothers.
1 Chronicles 26:29 For Issaar, Chonenia and his sons were over the outside work for Israel, to write and to judge.
1 Chronicles 26:30 For the Chebronite, Asabias and his brothers, mighty sons, one thousand seven hundred, were over the oversight of Israel beyond the Jordan toward the west, for every service of the Lord and work of the king.
1 Chronicles 26:31 For the Chebronite: Ioudias was ruler of the Chebronites according to their generations, according to their fathers’ houses. In the fortieth year of his reign they were enrolled, and a mighty man was found among them in Jazer of the Gileadite region.
1 Chronicles 26:32 And his brothers, mighty sons, were two thousand seven hundred, rulers of fathers’ houses; and King David appointed them over the Reubenite and the Gaddite and half the tribe of Manasseh, for every command of the Lord and word of the king.

## Chapter 27

1 Chronicles 27:1 And the sons of Israel according to their number: rulers of fathers’ houses, commanders of thousands and commanders of hundreds, and scribes serving the people and every matter of the king according to divisions, for every matter of one entering and going out, month by month, for all the months of the year; one division was twenty-four thousand.
1 Chronicles 27:2 And over the first division, for the first month: Iesboam son of Zabdeel; and over his division were twenty-four thousand.
1 Chronicles 27:3 From the sons of Phares, chief of all the rulers of the force for the first month.
1 Chronicles 27:4 And over the division of the second month: Dodia the Echochi; and over his division were twenty-four thousand, rulers of the force.
1 Chronicles 27:5 The third, for the third month: Banaias son of Iodae the priest, the ruler; and over his division were twenty-four thousand.
1 Chronicles 27:6 This Banaias was mightier than the thirty and over the thirty, and over his division was Amizabad his son.
1 Chronicles 27:7 The fourth, for the fourth month: Asael brother of Joab, and Zabdias his son and the brothers; and over his division were twenty-four thousand.
1 Chronicles 27:8 The fifth, for the fifth month: the leader Samaoth the Iesrae; and over his division were twenty-four thousand.
1 Chronicles 27:9 The sixth, for the sixth month: Oduias son of Ekkes the Thecoite; and over his division were twenty-four thousand.
1 Chronicles 27:10 The seventh, for the seventh month: Chelles from Phallous, from the sons of Ephraim; and over his division were twenty-four thousand.
1 Chronicles 27:11 The eighth, for the eighth month: Sobochai the Isathi, the Zarai; and over his division were twenty-four thousand.
1 Chronicles 27:12 The ninth, for the ninth month: Abiezer from Anathoth, from the land of Benjamin; and over his division were twenty-four thousand.
1 Chronicles 27:13 The tenth, for the tenth month: Meira from Netophath, the Zarai; and over his division were twenty-four thousand.
1 Chronicles 27:14 The eleventh, for the eleventh month: Banaias from Pharathon, of the sons of Ephraim; and over his division were twenty-four thousand.
1 Chronicles 27:15 The twelfth, for the twelfth month: Choldai the Netophathi, the Gothoniel; and over his division were twenty-four thousand.
1 Chronicles 27:16 And over the tribes of Israel: for Reuben, Eliezer son of Zechri; for Simeon, Saphatias son of Maacha;
1 Chronicles 27:17 for Levi, Hasabias son of Camouel; for Aaron, Sadoc;
1 Chronicles 27:18 for Judah, Eliab of the brothers of David; for Issachar, Ambri son of Michael;
1 Chronicles 27:19 for Zebulun, Samaia son of Abdiou; for Naphtali, Ierimoth son of Esriel;
1 Chronicles 27:20 for Ephraim, Hosea son of Ozias; for half the tribe of Manasseh, Joel son of Phadaia;
1 Chronicles 27:21 for half the tribe of Manasseh in Gilead, Iaddai son of Zabdiou; for the sons of Benjamin, Asiel son of Abennēr;
1 Chronicles 27:22 for Dan, Azarael son of Ioram. These are the patriarchs of the tribes of Israel. —
1 Chronicles 27:23 And David did not take their number from twenty years old and below, because the Lord said to multiply Israel like the stars of heaven.
1 Chronicles 27:24 And Joab son of Sarouia began to count among the people and did not finish; and in these things wrath came upon Israel, and the number was not entered in the book of the words of the days of King David.
1 Chronicles 27:25 And over the treasures of the king: Asmoth son of Odiel; and over the treasures in the field and in the villages and in the settlements and in the towers: Jonathan son of Ozias.
1 Chronicles 27:26 And over those tilling the land, the workers: Esdri son of Chouloub;
1 Chronicles 27:27 and over the rural lands: Semee from Rama; and over the treasures of wine in the rural lands: Zachri son of Sephni;
1 Chronicles 27:28 and over the olive groves and over the sycamores in the lowland: Balanas the Gedorite; and over the treasures of oil: Joas.
1 Chronicles 27:29 And over the cattle grazing in Asidon: Satrais the Sharonite; and over the cattle in the enclosures: Sophat son of Adli;
1 Chronicles 27:30 and over the camels: Obil the Ishmaelite; and over the donkeys: Iadias from Merathon;
1 Chronicles 27:31 and over the sheep: Iaziz the Agarite. All these were overseers of the possessions of King David. —
1 Chronicles 27:32 And Jonathan, David’s father’s brother, was a counselor, a discerning man and himself a scribe; and Iiel son of Achamani was with the sons of the king,
1 Chronicles 27:33 and Achitophel was the counselor of the king, and Chousi the first friend of the king,
1 Chronicles 27:34 and after this, Achitophel, followed by Jodae son of Banaia and Abiathar; and Joab was chief general of the king.

## Chapter 28

1 Chronicles 28:1 And David assembled all the rulers of Israel: rulers of judges, and the rulers of the courses around the king’s person, and commanders of thousands and of hundreds, and the treasury keepers, and those over his possessions, and the mighty men and the warriors of the army, in Jerusalem.
1 Chronicles 28:2 And David stood in the midst of the assembly and said, “Hear me, my brothers and my people. It came upon my heart to build a house of rest for the ark of the covenant of the Lord, and a standing-place for the feet of the Lord our God; and I prepared the things suitable for the dwelling.
1 Chronicles 28:3 And God said, ‘You shall not build a house for me, to call my name upon it, because you are a warrior man and have poured out blood.’
1 Chronicles 28:4 And the Lord God of Israel chose me from all the house of my father to be king over Israel forever; and in Judah he chose the kingdom, and from the house of Judah the house of my father; and among the sons of my father, in me he was pleased to make me king over all Israel.
1 Chronicles 28:5 And from all my sons [because the Lord gave me many sons] he chose Solomon my son to sit upon the throne of the kingdom of the Lord over Israel.
1 Chronicles 28:6 And God said to me, ‘Solomon your son shall build my house and my court, because I have chosen him to be a son to me, and I shall be a father to him;
1 Chronicles 28:7 and I will make his kingdom upright forever, if he is strong to keep my commandments and my judgments, as on this day.’
1 Chronicles 28:8 And now, before all the assembly of the Lord and in the ears of our God, keep and seek all the commandments of the Lord our God, so that you may inherit the good land and leave it as an inheritance to your sons after you forever.
1 Chronicles 28:9 And now, Solomon my son, know the God of your fathers and serve him with a perfect heart and a willing soul, because the Lord examines all hearts and knows every thought. If you seek him, he will be found by you; and if you forsake him, he will forsake you to the end.
1 Chronicles 28:10 See now that the Lord chose you to build a house for him as a sanctuary. Be strong and do. —
1 Chronicles 28:11 And David gave Solomon his son the plan of the temple and its houses and its zakcho and its upper rooms and its inner storerooms and the house of atonement,
1 Chronicles 28:12 and the plan which he had in his spirit, of the courts of the house of the Lord and all the chambers around, for the storerooms of the house of the Lord and the storerooms of the holy things,
1 Chronicles 28:13 and the dwellings of the courses of the priests and the Levites for every work of service of the house of the Lord, and the storerooms for the serviceable vessels of the service of the house of the Lord.
1 Chronicles 28:14 And the weight of their weighing, both of the gold and of the silver,
1 Chronicles 28:15 he gave him the weight of the lampstands and of the lamps;
1 Chronicles 28:16 likewise he gave him the weight of the tables of the presentation bread, each golden table, and likewise the silver ones,
1 Chronicles 28:17 and of the meat hooks and libation vessels and the golden bowls, and the weight of the gold and silver, kephphoure of each weight.
1 Chronicles 28:18 And he showed him the weight of the altar of incense, of tested gold, and the plan of the chariot of the cherubim, with their wings spread out and overshadowing the ark of the covenant of the Lord.
1 Chronicles 28:19 David gave everything in writing by the hand of the Lord to Solomon, according to the understanding of the working-out of the plan which had come to him. —
1 Chronicles 28:20 And David said to Solomon his son, “Be strong and be manly and do; do not fear or be dismayed, because the Lord my God is with you. He will not release you and will certainly not forsake you until you complete all the work of service of the house of the Lord.
1 Chronicles 28:21 And behold, the courses of the priests and the Levites are for every service of the house of God, and with you in every matter is everyone willing in wisdom according to every craft, and the rulers and all the people are for all your words.”

## Chapter 29

1 Chronicles 29:1 And King David said to the whole assembly, “Solomon my son, the one whom the Lord chose in him, is young and tender, and the work is great, because the building is not for a man, but for the Lord God.
1 Chronicles 29:2 According to all my strength I prepared for the house of my God gold, silver, bronze, iron, wood, stones of soom and of filling, and costly and various stones, and every precious stone, and much Parian stone.
1 Chronicles 29:3 And still, in my taking pleasure in the house of my God, there is for me what I have acquired, gold and silver; and behold, I have given it to the house of my God for height, apart from what I prepared for the house of the holy things:
1 Chronicles 29:4 three thousand talents of gold from Suphir, and seven thousand talents of refined silver, to overlay with them the walls of the temple
1 Chronicles 29:5 by the hand of craftsmen. And who is willing today to fill his hands for the Lord?”
1 Chronicles 29:6 And the rulers of the fathers’ houses were willing, and the rulers of the sons of Israel, and the commanders of thousands and of hundreds, and the overseers of the works, and the stewards of the king;
1 Chronicles 29:7 and they gave for the works of the house of the Lord five thousand talents of gold and ten thousand [pieces] of gold, and ten thousand talents of silver, and eighteen thousand talents of bronze, and one hundred thousand talents of iron.
1 Chronicles 29:8 And those among whom a stone was found gave it for the storerooms of the house of the Lord, by the hand of Iiel the Gershonite.
1 Chronicles 29:9 And the people rejoiced over the willingness, because with a full heart they willingly offered to the Lord; and King David also rejoiced greatly.
1 Chronicles 29:10 And King David blessed the Lord before the assembly, saying, “Blessed are you, Lord God of Israel, our father from everlasting and unto everlasting.
1 Chronicles 29:11 Yours, Lord, is the greatness and the power and the boasting and the victory and the strength, because you rule over all things in heaven and upon the earth; before your face every king and nation is troubled.
1 Chronicles 29:12 From you are wealth and glory; you rule over all, Lord, ruler of every rule; and in your hand are strength and power, and in your hand, Almighty, are the making great and the strengthening of all.
1 Chronicles 29:13 And now, we confess to you and praise the name of your boasting.
1 Chronicles 29:14 And who am I, and who is my people, that we were able to be willing for these things? Because all things are yours, and from what is yours we have given to you.
1 Chronicles 29:15 Because we are sojourners before you and dwellers, as all our fathers were; like a shadow are our days upon the earth, and there is no endurance.
1 Chronicles 29:16 Lord our God, all this abundance which I prepared to build a house for your holy name is from your hand, and all things are yours.
1 Chronicles 29:17 And I knew, Lord, that you are the one testing hearts and loving righteousness. In simplicity of heart I willingly offered all these things, and now I saw your people who were found here willingly offering to you with joy.
1 Chronicles 29:18 Lord God of Abraham and Isaac and Israel our fathers, keep these things forever in the intention of the heart of your people, and direct their hearts toward you.
1 Chronicles 29:19 And to Solomon my son give a good heart to do your commandments and your testimonies and your ordinances, and to bring the construction of your house to completion.
1 Chronicles 29:20 And David said to the whole assembly, “Bless the Lord your God.” And the whole assembly blessed the Lord, the God of their fathers, and bending their knees they worshiped the Lord and the king.
1 Chronicles 29:21 And David sacrificed sacrifices to the Lord and brought whole burnt offerings to God on the day after the first day: one thousand calves, one thousand rams, one thousand lambs, and their libations, and sacrifices in abundance for all Israel.
1 Chronicles 29:22 And they ate and drank before the Lord on that day with joy, and they made Solomon son of David king a second time, and anointed him to the Lord as king and Sadoc as priest.
1 Chronicles 29:23 And Solomon sat upon the throne of David his father and was well-pleasing, and all Israel listened to him.
1 Chronicles 29:24 The rulers and the mighty men and all the sons of King David his father submitted themselves to him.
1 Chronicles 29:25 And the Lord magnified Solomon above before all Israel and gave him the glory of a king, which had not happened upon any king before him.
1 Chronicles 29:26 And David son of Iessai reigned over Israel
1 Chronicles 29:27 forty years: in Hebron seven years, and in Jerusalem thirty-three years.
1 Chronicles 29:28 And he died in a good old age, full of days, wealth, and glory; and Solomon his son reigned in his place.
1 Chronicles 29:29 And the remaining words of King David, the former and the later, are written in the words of Samuel the seer, and upon the words of Nathan the prophet, and upon the words of Gad the seer,
1 Chronicles 29:30 concerning all his kingdom and his might and the times which came upon him and upon Israel and upon all the kingdoms of the earth.

## Chapter 1

2 Chronicles 1:1 And Solomon son of David was strengthened over his kingdom, and the Lord his God was with him and magnified him on high.
2 Chronicles 1:2 And Solomon spoke to all Israel, to the commanders of thousands and to the commanders of hundreds and to the judges and to all the rulers before Israel, the rulers of the fathers’ houses,
2 Chronicles 1:3 and Solomon and all the assembly with him went to the high place in Gabaon, where there was the tent of the testimony of God, which Moses the servant of the Lord had made in the wilderness;
2 Chronicles 1:4 but David had brought up the ark of God from the city of Cariathiarim, because he had prepared a tent for it in Jerusalem,
2 Chronicles 1:5 and the bronze altar, which Beseleel son of Uriou son of Hor had made, was there before the tent of the Lord; and Solomon and the assembly sought it,
2 Chronicles 1:6 and Solomon brought up there upon the bronze altar before the Lord, the one in the tent, and brought up upon it one thousand whole burnt offerings. —
2 Chronicles 1:7 In that night God appeared to Solomon and said to him, “Ask what I shall give you.”
2 Chronicles 1:8 And Solomon said to God, “You have done great mercy with David my father, and have made me king in his place;
2 Chronicles 1:9 and now, Lord God, let your name be established upon David my father, because you have made me king over a numerous people, like the dust of the earth.
2 Chronicles 1:10 Now give me wisdom and understanding, and I shall go out before this people and enter in; for who can judge this great people of yours?”
2 Chronicles 1:11 And God said to Solomon, “Because this came to be in your heart, and you did not ask for wealth of possessions, or glory, or the life of your adversaries, or many days, but asked for yourself wisdom and understanding, in order to judge my people over whom I made you king,
2 Chronicles 1:12 wisdom and understanding I give to you, and wealth and possessions and glory I will give to you, as there has not been one like you among the kings before you, and after you there shall not be such.”
2 Chronicles 1:13 And Solomon came from the high place in Gabaon to Jerusalem, from before the tent of the testimony, and reigned over Israel.
2 Chronicles 1:14 And Solomon gathered chariots and horsemen, and he had one thousand four hundred chariots and twelve thousand horsemen; and he left them in the cities of the chariots, and the people were with the king in Jerusalem.
2 Chronicles 1:15 And the king placed the gold and the silver in Jerusalem like stones, and the cedars in Judea like sycamines in the lowland, in abundance.
2 Chronicles 1:16 And the going out of Solomon’s horses was from Egypt, and the price of the king’s merchants; they bought for trade.
2 Chronicles 1:17 And they went up and brought out of Egypt one chariot for six hundred pieces of silver, and one horse for one hundred fifty; and thus they brought them in their hands to all the kings of the Hittites and the kings of Syria.
2 Chronicles 1:18 And Solomon said to build a house for the name of the Lord and a house for his kingdom.

## Chapter 2

2 Chronicles 2:1 And Solomon assembled seventy thousand men and eighty thousand stonecutters in the mountain, and the overseers over them were three thousand six hundred. —
2 Chronicles 2:2 And Solomon sent to Hiram king of Tyre, saying, “As you did with David my father and sent him cedars to build himself a house to dwell in it,
2 Chronicles 2:3 behold, I, his son, am building a house for the name of the Lord my God, to sanctify it to him, to burn incense before him continually, and the presentation continually, and to offer whole burnt offerings continually, morning and evening and on the Sabbaths and at the new moons and at the feasts of the Lord our God; this is forever for Israel.
2 Chronicles 2:4 And the house which I am building is great, because our God is great above all gods.
2 Chronicles 2:5 And who shall be strong to build a house for him? Because heaven and the heaven of heavens do not bear his glory. And who am I, building a house for him? Is it anything except to burn incense before him?
2 Chronicles 2:6 And now send me a wise man who knows how to work in gold and in silver and in bronze and in iron and in purple and in scarlet and in blue, and who knows how to engrave an engraving, with the wise men who are with me in Judah and in Jerusalem, whom David my father prepared.
2 Chronicles 2:7 And send me cedar timbers and juniper timbers and fir timbers from Lebanon, because I know that your servants know how to cut timbers from Lebanon; and behold, your servants will go with my servants
2 Chronicles 2:8 to prepare for me timbers in abundance, because the house which I am building is great and glorious.
2 Chronicles 2:9 And behold, for the workers who cut timbers for food, I have given wheat as gifts to your servants: twenty thousand kors, and twenty thousand kors of barley, and twenty thousand measures of wine, and twenty thousand measures of oil. —
2 Chronicles 2:10 And Hiram king of Tyre said in writing and sent to Solomon, “Because the Lord loved his people, he gave you over them as king.”
2 Chronicles 2:11 And Hiram said, “Blessed is the Lord God of Israel, who made heaven and earth, who gave to David the king a wise son, knowing understanding and knowledge, who shall build a house for the Lord and a house for his kingdom.
2 Chronicles 2:12 And now I have sent you a wise man, knowing understanding, Hiram my father,
2 Chronicles 2:13 [his mother from the daughters of Dan, and his father a man of Tyre] who knows how to work in gold and in silver and in bronze and in iron, in stones and in wood, and to weave in purple and in blue and in fine linen and in scarlet, and to engrave engravings and to devise every design, whatever you may give him, with your wise men and the wise men of David my lord, your father.
2 Chronicles 2:14 And now, let the wheat and the barley and the oil and the wine which my lord said be sent to his servants.
2 Chronicles 2:15 And we will cut timbers from Lebanon according to all your need, and we will bring them on rafts upon the sea to Ioppe, and you will bring them to Jerusalem.” —
2 Chronicles 2:16 And Solomon assembled all the proselytes in the land of Israel, after the numbering by which David his father had numbered them, and they were found to be one hundred fifty-three thousand six hundred.
2 Chronicles 2:17 And he made from them seventy thousand back-bearers and eighty thousand stonecutters, and three thousand six hundred taskmasters over the people.

## Chapter 3

2 Chronicles 3:1 And Solomon began to build the house of the Lord in Jerusalem, on Mount Amoria, where the Lord appeared to David his father, at the place which David had prepared on the threshing floor of Orna the Jebusite.
2 Chronicles 3:2 And he began to build in the second month, in the fourth year of his kingdom.
2 Chronicles 3:3 And these are the things Solomon began to build for the house of God: the length in cubits, the first measurement, was sixty cubits, and the width was twenty cubits.
2 Chronicles 3:4 And the ailam in front of the house, its length across the front according to the width of the house was twenty cubits, and its height was one hundred twenty cubits; and he overlaid it inside with pure gold.
2 Chronicles 3:5 And he paneled the great house with cedar timbers and overlaid it with pure gold, and carved upon it palms and hanging ornaments.
2 Chronicles 3:6 And he adorned the house with precious stones for glory, and with gold, gold from Pharouaim;
2 Chronicles 3:7 and he gilded the house and the walls and the gates and the ceilings and the doors with gold, and carved cherubim upon the walls. —
2 Chronicles 3:8 And he made the house of the holy of holies; its length, across the front according to the width, was twenty cubits, and its width was twenty cubits; and he overlaid it with pure gold, for the cherubim, to six hundred talents.
2 Chronicles 3:9 And the weight of the nails, the weight of each one, was fifty shekels of gold. And he gilded the upper room with gold.
2 Chronicles 3:10 And he made in the house of the holy of holies two cherubim, wooden work, and gilded them with gold.
2 Chronicles 3:11 And the wings of the cherubim were twenty cubits in length; one wing was five cubits, touching the wall of the house, and the other wing was five cubits, touching the wing of the other cherub;
2 Chronicles 3:12 and the wing of the one cherub was five cubits, touching the wall of the house, and the other wing was five cubits, touching the wing of the other cherub;
2 Chronicles 3:13 and the wings of the cherubim were spread out for twenty cubits; and they were standing upon their feet, and their faces were toward the house.
2 Chronicles 3:14 And he made the veil of blue and purple and scarlet and fine linen, and wove cherubim in it. —
2 Chronicles 3:15 And he made in front of the house two pillars, thirty-five cubits in height, and their capitals were five cubits.
2 Chronicles 3:16 And he made serseroth in the debir and gave them upon the capitals of the pillars; and he made one hundred pomegranates and placed them upon the hanging ornaments.
2 Chronicles 3:17 And he set the pillars in front of the temple, one on the right and one on the left; and he called the name of the one on the right Uprightness, and the name of the one on the left Strength.

## Chapter 4

2 Chronicles 4:1 And he made the bronze altar: twenty cubits in length, and its width twenty cubits, and its height ten cubits.
2 Chronicles 4:2 And he made the cast sea, ten cubits across its diameter, round all around; and its height was five cubits, and its circumference was thirty cubits.
2 Chronicles 4:3 And a likeness of calves was beneath it; they went around it in a circle; ten cubits encompassed the basin all around. Two kinds cast the calves in its casting,
2 Chronicles 4:4 by which they made them: twelve calves, three facing north and three facing west and three facing south and three facing east; and the sea was upon them above, and their backs were inward.
2 Chronicles 4:5 And its thickness was a palm, and its lip was like the lip of a cup, engraved with lily shoots; it held three thousand measures. And he finished it.
