2 Chronicles 4:6 And he made ten lavers and placed five on the right and five on the left, to wash in them the works of the whole burnt offerings and to rinse in them. And the sea was for the priests to wash themselves in it.
2 Chronicles 4:7 And he made ten golden lampstands according to their ordinance and placed them in the temple, five on the right and five on the left.
2 Chronicles 4:8 And he made ten tables and placed them in the temple, five on the right and five on the left. And he made one hundred golden bowls.
2 Chronicles 4:9 And he made the court of the priests and the great court and doors for the court, and their doorways overlaid with bronze.
2 Chronicles 4:10 And he placed the sea at the right corner of the house, eastward, opposite.
2 Chronicles 4:11 And Hiram made the meat hooks and the firepans and the grate of the altar and all its vessels. And Hiram finished making all the work which he made for King Solomon in the house of God:
2 Chronicles 4:12 two pillars, and upon them golath at the chothareth, upon the heads of the two pillars; and two networks to cover the capitals of the chothareth which are upon the heads of the pillars,
2 Chronicles 4:13 and four hundred golden bells for the two networks, and two kinds of pomegranates in the one network, to cover the two golath of the chothareth which are above the pillars.
2 Chronicles 4:14 And he made ten mechonoth, and he made the lavers upon the mechonoth,
2 Chronicles 4:15 and one sea, and the twelve calves beneath it,
2 Chronicles 4:16 and the footstands and the analemptēras and the cauldrons and the meat hooks and all their vessels, which Hiram made and brought to King Solomon in the house of the Lord, of pure bronze.
2 Chronicles 4:17 In the region of the Jordan the king cast them, in the thickness of the earth, in the house of Sokchoth and between Sirdatha.
2 Chronicles 4:18 And Solomon made all these vessels in very great abundance, because the weighing of the bronze did not cease.
2 Chronicles 4:19 And Solomon made all the vessels of the house of the Lord and the golden altar and the tables [and upon them the presentation bread],
2 Chronicles 4:20 and the lampstands and the lamps for the light according to the ordinance, and before the debir, of pure gold,
2 Chronicles 4:21 and their tongs and their lamps and the bowls and the censers and the firepans, of pure gold;
2 Chronicles 4:22 and the inner door of the house to the holy of holies, and the doors of the house of the temple, were gold.

## Chapter 5

2 Chronicles 5:1 And all the work which Solomon did in the house of the Lord was completed. And Solomon brought in the holy things of David his father, the silver and the gold and the vessels, and put them into the treasury of the house of the Lord.
2 Chronicles 5:2 Then Solomon assembled the elders of Israel and all the rulers of the tribes, the leaders of the fathers’ houses of the sons of Israel, to Jerusalem, to bring up the ark of the covenant of the Lord from the city of David [this is Zion];
2 Chronicles 5:3 and all the men of Israel assembled to the king at the feast [this is the seventh month],
2 Chronicles 5:4 and all the elders of Israel came, and all the Levites took the ark,
2 Chronicles 5:5 and they brought up the ark and the tent of the testimony and all the holy vessels which were in the tent; the priests and the Levites brought them up.
2 Chronicles 5:6 And King Solomon and all the assembly of Israel and those fearing and those gathered with them before the ark were sacrificing calves and sheep which could not be numbered and could not be counted because of the multitude.
2 Chronicles 5:7 And the priests brought the ark of the covenant of the Lord to its place, to the debir of the house, into the holy of holies, beneath the wings of the cherubim;
2 Chronicles 5:8 and the cherubim had spread out their wings over the place of the ark, and the cherubim covered the ark and its carrying poles from above.
2 Chronicles 5:9 And the poles projected, and the heads of the poles were visible from the holy place toward the front of the debir; they were not visible outside. And they were there until this day.
2 Chronicles 5:10 There was nothing in the ark except the two tablets which Moses placed in Choreb, which the Lord established with the sons of Israel when they came out of the land of Egypt.
2 Chronicles 5:11 And it came to pass, when the priests went out from the holy place — because all the priests who were found had been sanctified, and they were not assigned according to a course —
2 Chronicles 5:12 and all the Levite singers, the sons of Asaph, Heman, and Idithoun, and their sons and their brothers, clothed in linen garments, were standing with cymbals and nablas and citharas opposite the altar, and with them one hundred twenty priests blowing trumpets,
2 Chronicles 5:13 and there was one voice when they trumpeted and when they sang and raised their voice with one voice, to give thanks and praise to the Lord — and when they raised their voice with trumpets and with cymbals and with the instruments of songs, and said, “Give thanks to the Lord, because he is good, because his mercy is forever,” the house was filled with the cloud of the glory of the Lord;
2 Chronicles 5:14 and the priests were not able to stand to minister because of the cloud, because the glory of the Lord filled the house of God.

## Chapter 6

2 Chronicles 6:1 Then Solomon said: The Lord said to dwell in gloom;
2 Chronicles 6:2 And I have built a house for your name, holy to you and ready to dwell forever.
2 Chronicles 6:3 And the king turned his face and blessed all the assembly of Israel, and all the assembly of Israel was standing by.
2 Chronicles 6:4 And he said, “Blessed is the Lord God of Israel, who spoke with his mouth to David my father, and with his hands fulfilled, saying:
2 Chronicles 6:5 From the day on which I brought my people up from the land of Egypt, I did not choose a city from all the tribes of Israel to build a house for my name to be there, and I did not choose a man to be ruler over my people Israel;
2 Chronicles 6:6 and I chose in David, so as to be over my people Israel.
2 Chronicles 6:7 And it came upon the heart of David my father to build a house for the name of the Lord God of Israel,
2 Chronicles 6:8 and the Lord said to David my father, “Because it came upon your heart to build a house for my name, you did well, because it came upon your heart;
2 Chronicles 6:9 nevertheless, you shall not build the house, because your son, who will come forth from your loins, he shall build the house for my name.
2 Chronicles 6:10 And the Lord raised up his word, which he spoke, and I came to be in place of David my father and sat upon the throne of Israel, as the Lord spoke, and I built the house for the name of the Lord God of Israel
2 Chronicles 6:11 and I placed there the ark, in which there is the covenant of the Lord, which he made with Israel.
2 Chronicles 6:12 And he stood before the altar of the Lord, before all the assembly of Israel, and spread out his hands,
2 Chronicles 6:13 because Solomon had made a bronze base and set it in the midst of the court of the sanctuary, its length five cubits and its breadth five cubits and its height three cubits, and he stood upon it and fell upon his knees before all the assembly of Israel and spread out his hands toward heaven
2 Chronicles 6:14 and he said, “O Lord God of Israel, there is no God like you in heaven or upon the earth, keeping the covenant and the mercy for your servants, those who walk before you with a whole heart.
2 Chronicles 6:15 What you kept for your servant David my father, what you spoke to him saying, and you spoke with your mouth and fulfilled with your hands, as this day.
2 Chronicles 6:16 And now, O Lord God of Israel, keep for your servant David my father what you spoke to him, saying, “A man shall not be lacking to you from before me, sitting upon the throne of Israel, except if your sons keep their way to walk in my law, as you walked before me.”
2 Chronicles 6:17 And now, O Lord God of Israel, let your word, then, be made certain, which you spoke to your servant David.
2 Chronicles 6:18 For will God truly dwell with human beings upon the earth? If the heaven and the heaven of heaven do not suffice you, then what is this house which I built?
2 Chronicles 6:19 And may you look upon the prayer of your servant and upon my petition, O Lord God, to give ear to the petition and to the prayer which your servant prays before you today,
2 Chronicles 6:20 for your eyes to be open upon this house day and night, upon this place which you said your name would be called upon there, to hear the prayer which your servant prays toward this place.
2 Chronicles 6:21 And may you hear the petition of your servant and of your people Israel, whatever they may pray toward this place, and you hear in the place of your dwelling from heaven, and hear and be gracious. —
2 Chronicles 6:22 If a man sins against his neighbor, and he takes a curse against him to curse him, and he comes and curses before the altar in this house,
2 Chronicles 6:23 and you hear from heaven and act and judge your servants, to repay the lawless one and repay his ways upon his own head, to justify the righteous, to repay him according to his righteousness. —
2 Chronicles 6:24 And if your people Israel are shattered before the enemy, if they sin against you, and turn back and confess to your name and pray and make petition before you in this house,
2 Chronicles 6:25 and you hear from heaven and be gracious to the sins of your people Israel, and turn them back to the land which you gave to them and to their fathers. —
2 Chronicles 6:26 when the heaven is shut up and there is no rain, because they will sin against you, and they pray toward this place and praise your name and turn from their sins, because you will humble them,
2 Chronicles 6:27 and you hear from heaven and be gracious to the sins of your servants and of your people Israel, because you will show them the good way in which they will walk in it, and give rain upon your land which you gave to your people as an inheritance. —
2 Chronicles 6:28 famine, if it should happen upon the land; death, if it should happen; wind destruction and jaundice; locust and caterpillar, if they should happen; if the enemy afflicts him before their cities, according to every plague and every pain,
2 Chronicles 6:29 and every prayer and every petition which may happen to any human and to all your people Israel, if a man knows his touch and his weakness and spreads out his hands toward this house,
2 Chronicles 6:30 and you hear from heaven, from your prepared dwelling place, and be propitious, and give to a man according to his ways, as you may know his heart, because you alone know the heart of the sons of humans,
2 Chronicles 6:31 so that they may fear all your ways all the days which they themselves live upon the face of the land which you gave to our fathers. —
2 Chronicles 6:32 And every foreigner, who is not himself from your people Israel, and comes from a distant land because of your great name and your strong hand and your lifted arm, and they come and pray toward this place,
2 Chronicles 6:33 and you hear from heaven, from your prepared dwelling place, and do according to all things whatever the foreigner calls upon you for, so that all the peoples of the earth may know your name and fear you as your people Israel, and know that your name has been called upon this house which I built. —
2 Chronicles 6:34 But if your people go out to war against their enemies on the way by which you send them, and they pray to you toward the direction of this city, which you chose in it, and of the house which I built for your name,
2 Chronicles 6:35 and you hear from heaven their petition and their prayer and do their judgment. —
2 Chronicles 6:36 Because they will sin against you [because there will not be a human who will not sin] and you will strike them and give them over before enemies, and those taking them captive will take them captive into the land of enemies, into a land far or near
2 Chronicles 6:37 and they turn their heart in their land, where they were deported there, and indeed they turn and make petition to you in their captivity, saying, “We have sinned, we have acted unjustly, we have acted lawlessly,”
2 Chronicles 6:38 and they turn toward you with all their heart and with all their soul in the land of those who took them captive, and pray toward the way of their land, which you gave to their fathers, and of the city which you chose, and of the house which I built for your name,
2 Chronicles 6:39 and you hear from heaven, from your prepared dwelling place, their prayer and their petition, and do judgments and be gracious to the people who have sinned against you. —
2 Chronicles 6:40 Now, O Lord, let your eyes then be open and your ears attentive to the petition of this place.
2 Chronicles 6:41 And now arise, O Lord God, to your resting place, you and the ark of your strength. May your priests, O Lord God, be clothed with salvation, and may your sons rejoice in good things.
2 Chronicles 6:42 O Lord God, do not turn away the face of your anointed; remember the mercies of David your servant.

## Chapter 7

2 Chronicles 7:1 And when Solomon completed praying, fire came down from heaven and consumed the burnt offerings and the sacrifices, and the glory of the Lord filled the house.
2 Chronicles 7:2 And the priests were not able to enter into the house of the Lord at that time, because the glory of the Lord filled the house.
2 Chronicles 7:3 And all the sons of Israel saw the fire coming down, and the glory of the Lord upon the house, and they fell upon their faces upon the earth, upon the stone pavement, and worshiped and praised the Lord, because he is good, because his mercy is forever.
2 Chronicles 7:4 And the king and all the people were sacrificing sacrifices before the Lord.
2 Chronicles 7:5 And Solomon sacrificed the sacrifice of twenty-two thousand young bulls and one hundred twenty thousand livestock, and the king and all the people inaugurated the house of God.
2 Chronicles 7:6 And the priests were standing at their watches, and the Levites with the instruments of the songs of the Lord of David the king, for giving thanks before the Lord, because forever is his mercy, with the hymns of David through their hand; and the priests were blowing with the trumpets opposite them, and all Israel was standing.
2 Chronicles 7:7 And Solomon sanctified the middle of the court which is in the house of the Lord; because he made there the burnt offerings and the fats of the peace offerings, because the bronze altar which Solomon made did not suffice to receive the burnt offerings and the manaa and the fats.
2 Chronicles 7:8 And Solomon held the feast at that time for seven days, and all Israel with him, a very great assembly, from the entrance of Hamath and as far as the torrent of Egypt.
2 Chronicles 7:9 And he made a closing assembly on the eighth day, because he made the dedication of the altar a feast for seven days.
2 Chronicles 7:10 And on the twenty-third of the seventh month he sent the people to their tents, rejoicing and with a good heart over the good things which the Lord did to David and to Solomon and to Israel his people.
2 Chronicles 7:11 And Solomon completed the house of the Lord and the house of the king; and all that Solomon desired in his soul to do in the house of the Lord and in his house prospered.
2 Chronicles 7:12 And God appeared to Solomon by night and said to him, “I have heard your prayer and have chosen for myself in this place as a house of sacrifice.
2 Chronicles 7:13 If I shut up the heaven and there is no rain, and if I command the locust to eat the tree, and if I send death among my people,
2 Chronicles 7:14 and if my people are ashamed, upon whom my name has been called, upon them, and they pray and seek my face and turn away from their evil ways, then I will hear from heaven and will be gracious to their sins and will heal their land.
2 Chronicles 7:15 Now my eyes will be open and my ears attentive to the prayer of this place.
2 Chronicles 7:16 And now I have chosen and sanctified this house for my name to be there forever, and my eyes and my heart will be there all the days.
2 Chronicles 7:17 And you, if you walk before me as David your father and do according to all that I commanded you and guard my ordinances and my judgments,
2 Chronicles 7:18 and I will raise up the throne of your kingdom, as I covenanted with David your father, saying, “A man ruling in Israel shall not be removed from you.”
2 Chronicles 7:19 And if you yourselves turn away and abandon my ordinances and my commandments which I gave before you, and go and serve other gods and worship them,
2 Chronicles 7:20 and I will take you out from the land which I gave to them, and this house, which I sanctified for my name, I will turn away from before my face, and I will give it as a parable and as a narrative among all the nations.
2 Chronicles 7:21 And this house, the high one, everyone passing by it will be astonished and will say, “For what reason did the Lord do this to this land and to this house?”
2 Chronicles 7:22 And they will say, “Because they abandoned the Lord, the God of their fathers, who brought them out from the land of Egypt, and took hold of other gods and worshiped them and served them; because of this he brought upon them all this evil.”

## Chapter 8

2 Chronicles 8:1 And it came to pass after twenty years, in which Solomon built the house of the Lord and his own house,
2 Chronicles 8:2 and the cities which Hiram gave to Solomon, Solomon built them and settled the sons of Israel there.
2 Chronicles 8:3 And Solomon came to Aimath Soba and strengthened it.
2 Chronicles 8:4 And he built Thedmor in the wilderness and all the fortified cities which he built in Emath.
2 Chronicles 8:5 And he built Baithoron the Upper and Baithoron the Lower, fortified cities, walls, gates, and bars,
2 Chronicles 8:6 and Baalath and all the fortified cities which belonged to Solomon, and all the cities of the chariots and the cities of the horsemen, and whatever Solomon desired according to the desire to build in Jerusalem and in Lebanon and in all his kingdom.
2 Chronicles 8:7 All the people who remained from the Hittite and the Amorite and the Perizzite and the Hivite and the Jebusite, who are not from Israel —
2 Chronicles 8:8 They were from their sons, those left after them in the land, whom the sons of Israel did not destroy — and Solomon brought them up as tribute until this day.
2 Chronicles 8:9 And from the sons of Israel Solomon did not give any as servants for his kingdom, because they were men of war and rulers and mighty men and leaders of chariots and horsemen.
2 Chronicles 8:10 And these were chiefs of the overseers of King Solomon; two hundred and fifty taskmasters among the people.
2 Chronicles 8:11 And Solomon brought the daughter of Pharaoh up from the city of David to the house which he built for her, because he said, “My wife shall not dwell in the city of David, king of Israel, because it is holy, where the ark of the Lord entered there.”
2 Chronicles 8:12 Then Solomon offered whole burnt offerings to the Lord upon the altar which he built in front of the sanctuary,
2 Chronicles 8:13 and according to the word of each day for offering, according to the commands of Moses, on the Sabbaths and on the months and on the feasts three times of the year: on the feast of unleavened things and on the feast of weeks and on the feast of tents.
2 Chronicles 8:14 And he set in order, according to the judgment of David, the divisions of the priests according to their services, and the Levites at their watches, to praise and to minister before the priests according to the word of the day, day by day, and the gatekeepers according to their divisions, at gate and gate, because thus are the commands of David, man of God;
2 Chronicles 8:15 They did not pass beyond the commands of the king concerning the priests and the Levites in every matter and in the treasuries.
2 Chronicles 8:16 And all the work was prepared from the day on which it was founded until Solomon completed the house of the Lord.
2 Chronicles 8:17 Then Solomon went to Gasiongaber and to Ailath, by the seaside in the land of Idumaea.
2 Chronicles 8:18 And Hiram sent ships and servants who knew the sea by the hand of his servants, and they went with the servants of Solomon to Sophira and took from there four hundred and fifty talents of gold and came to King Solomon.

## Chapter 9

2 Chronicles 9:1 And the queen of Saba heard the name of Solomon and came to test Solomon with riddles in Jerusalem with a very heavy force, and camels carrying spices and gold in great quantity and a precious stone; and she came to Solomon and spoke to him all that was in her heart.
2 Chronicles 9:2 And Solomon declared to her all her words, and no word passed from Solomon which he did not declare to her.
2 Chronicles 9:3 And the queen of Saba saw the wisdom of Solomon and the house which he built,
2 Chronicles 9:4 and the food of the tables and the seating of his servants and the standing of his ministers and their clothing and his cupbearers and their adornment and the burnt offerings which he offered in the house of the Lord, and she came to be outside herself.
2 Chronicles 9:5 And she said to the king, “True was the word which I heard in my land about your words and about your wisdom,
2 Chronicles 9:6 and I did not believe the words until I came and my eyes saw, and behold, half of the abundance of your wisdom was not reported to me; you have added upon the hearing which I heard;
2 Chronicles 9:7 blessed are the men, blessed are these your servants who are standing before you continually and hearing your wisdom;
2 Chronicles 9:8 let the Lord your God be blessed, who desired to give you upon his throne as king for the Lord your God; because the Lord your God loved Israel to establish it forever, and gave you over them as king to do judgment and righteousness.”
2 Chronicles 9:9 And she gave the king one hundred twenty talents of gold and spices in great quantity and a precious stone; and there had not been like those spices which the queen of Saba gave to King Solomon.
2 Chronicles 9:10 [And the servants of Solomon and the servants of Hiram were bringing gold to Solomon from Sophir and pine wood and precious stone;
2 Chronicles 9:11 and the king made the pine wood into stairs for the house of the Lord and for the house of the king, and citharas and nablas for the singers, and such things had not been seen before in the land of Juda.]
2 Chronicles 9:12 And King Solomon gave Queen Saba all her desires which she asked, besides all that she brought to King Solomon; and she returned to her land.
2 Chronicles 9:13 And the weight of the gold brought to Solomon in one year was six hundred sixty-six talents of gold,
2 Chronicles 9:14 except for that of the men subordinated and those trading, from whom they brought, and all the kings of Arabia and the satraps of the land were bringing gold and silver to King Solomon.
2 Chronicles 9:15 And King Solomon made two hundred large beaten gold shields, six hundred pure gold for one shield; six hundred gold were laid upon the one shield;
2 Chronicles 9:16 and three hundred beaten gold shields, three hundred gold were brought upon each shield; and the king gave them in the house of the forest of Lebanon.
2 Chronicles 9:17 And the king made a great throne of elephant teeth, and overlaid it with tested gold;
2 Chronicles 9:18 and six steps were to the throne, bound with gold, and armrests here and there upon the throne of the seat, and two lions standing beside the armrests,
2 Chronicles 9:19 and twelve lions standing there upon the six steps, here and there; it did not come to be so in every kingdom.
2 Chronicles 9:20 And all the vessels of King Solomon were of gold, and all the vessels of the house of the forest of Lebanon were covered with gold; silver was not accounted for anything in the days of Solomon;
2 Chronicles 9:21 because a ship for the king went to Tharsis with the servants of Hiram; once through three years ships came from Tharsis for the king, filled with gold and silver and ivory teeth and apes.
2 Chronicles 9:22 And Solomon was magnified above all the kings both in wealth and in wisdom.
2 Chronicles 9:23 And all the kings of the earth were seeking the face of Solomon to hear his wisdom, which God gave in his heart.
2 Chronicles 9:24 And they were each bringing his gifts: vessels of silver and vessels of gold and clothing, stacte and spices, horses and mules, year by year.
2 Chronicles 9:25 And there were for Solomon four thousand female horses for chariots and twelve thousand horsemen, and he placed them in the cities of the chariots and with the king in Jerusalem.
2 Chronicles 9:26 And he was ruling over all the kings from the river and as far as the land of the foreigners and as far as the boundary of Egypt.
2 Chronicles 9:27 And the king gave the gold and the silver in Jerusalem as stones, and the cedars as sycamores which are in the plain, in great quantity.
2 Chronicles 9:28 And the export of the horses from Egypt for Solomon and from all the land.
2 Chronicles 9:29 And the remaining words of Solomon, the first and the last, behold, they are written in the words of Nathan the prophet and in the words of Achia the Selonite and in the visions of Ioel the seer concerning Ieroboam son of Nabat.
2 Chronicles 9:30 And Solomon the king reigned over all Israel forty years.
2 Chronicles 9:31 And Solomon slept, and they buried him in the city of David his father, and Roboam his son reigned in his place.

## Chapter 10

2 Chronicles 10:1 And Roboam came to Sychem, because all Israel was coming to Sychem to make him king.
2 Chronicles 10:2 And it came to pass, when Ieroboam son of Nabat heard — and he himself was in Egypt, as he fled from before King Solomon and Ieroboam dwelt in Egypt — Ieroboam returned from Egypt.
2 Chronicles 10:3 And they sent and called him, and Ieroboam and all the assembly of Israel came to Roboam, saying,
2 Chronicles 10:4 “Your father made our yoke hard, and now release us from the hard service of your father and from his heavy yoke, which he put upon us, and we will serve you.”
2 Chronicles 10:5 And he said to them, “Go for three days and come to me”; and the people went away.
2 Chronicles 10:6 And King Roboam gathered the elders who had stood before Solomon his father while he was alive, saying, “How do you counsel to answer this people with a word?”
2 Chronicles 10:7 And they spoke to him, saying, “If today you are good to this people and please them and speak good words to them, they will be servants to you all the days.”
2 Chronicles 10:8 And he left behind the counsel of the elders who counseled him, and counseled with the young men who had been brought up with him, those who stood before him.
2 Chronicles 10:9 And he said to them, “What do you counsel, and I shall answer a word to this people who spoke to me, saying, ‘Ease us from the yoke which your father put upon us?’”
2 Chronicles 10:10 And the young men who had been brought up with him spoke to him: “Thus you shall speak to the people who spoke to you, saying, ‘Your father made our yoke heavy, and you, release us from it’; thus you shall say, ‘My little finger is thicker than the loins of my father;
2 Chronicles 10:11 and now my father disciplined you with a heavy yoke, and I will add upon your yoke; my father disciplined you with whips, and I will discipline you with scorpions.’”
2 Chronicles 10:12 And Ieroboam and all the people came to Roboam on the third day, as the king spoke, saying, “Return to me on the third day.”
2 Chronicles 10:13 And the king answered harshly, and King Roboam abandoned the counsel of the elders
2 Chronicles 10:14 and he spoke to them according to the counsel of the younger men, saying, “My father made your yoke heavy, and I will add upon it; my father disciplined you with whips, and I will discipline you with scorpions.”
2 Chronicles 10:15 And the king did not listen to the people, because a turning was from God, saying, The Lord raised up his word, which he spoke by the hand of Achia the Selonite concerning Ieroboam son of Nabat
2 Chronicles 10:16 and all Israel, because their king did not listen. And the people answered the king, saying, “What portion is there for us in David, and inheritance in the son of Iessai? To your tents, Israel; now see to your house, David.” And all Israel went to their tents;
2 Chronicles 10:17 And the men of Israel who dwelt in the cities of Juda, and Roboam reigned over them.
2 Chronicles 10:18 And King Roboam sent Adoniram, the one over the tribute, and the sons of Israel stoned him with stones and he died; and King Roboam hurried to go up upon the chariot to flee to Jerusalem.
2 Chronicles 10:19 And Israel rejected the house of David until this day.

## Chapter 11

2 Chronicles 11:1 And Roboam came to Jerusalem and assembled Juda and Benjamin, one hundred eighty thousand young men making war, and he fought against Israel to turn the kingdom to Roboam.
2 Chronicles 11:2 And the word of the Lord came to Samaias, a man of God, saying,
2 Chronicles 11:3 Say to Roboam son of Solomon and to all Juda and Benjamin, saying,
2 Chronicles 11:4 “Thus says the Lord: You shall not go up and you shall not fight against your brothers; each of you, return to his house, because this word came from me.” And they heeded the word of the Lord and turned back from going against Ieroboam.
2 Chronicles 11:5 And Roboam dwelt in Jerusalem and built walled cities in Judaia.
2 Chronicles 11:6 and he built Baithleem and Aitam and Thekoe
2 Chronicles 11:7 and Baithsoura and Sochchoth and Odollam
2 Chronicles 11:8 and Geth and Marisan and Ziph
2 Chronicles 11:9 and Adoraim and Lachis and Azeika
2 Chronicles 11:10 and Saraa and Aialon and Chebron, which belongs to Juda and Benjamin, walled cities.
2 Chronicles 11:11 And he fortified them with walls and gave in them leaders and stores of provisions, oil and wine,
2 Chronicles 11:12 according to city and according to city, shields and spears, and he strengthened them exceedingly much; and Juda and Benjamin were his. —
2 Chronicles 11:13 And the priests and the Levites, who were in all Israel, gathered to him from all the borders;
2 Chronicles 11:14 because the Levites abandoned the dwellings of their possession and went to Juda, to Jerusalem, because Ieroboam and his sons cast them out so that they would not minister to the Lord,
2 Chronicles 11:15 and he set up for himself priests of the high places and for the idols and the vanities and the calves which Ieroboam made,
2 Chronicles 11:16 and he cast them out from the tribes of Israel, those who gave their heart to seek the Lord God of Israel, and they came to Jerusalem to sacrifice to the Lord God of their fathers
2 Chronicles 11:17 And they strengthened the kingdom of Juda and strengthened Roboam son of Solomon for three years, because he walked in the ways of David and Solomon for three years.
2 Chronicles 11:18 And Roboam took for himself as wife Mollath, daughter of Ierimouth son of David, Abaia daughter of Eliab the Iessai,
2 Chronicles 11:19 and she bore to him sons: Iaous and Samarian and Roollam.
2 Chronicles 11:20 and after these things he took for himself Maacha daughter of Abessalom, and she bore to him Abia and Ieththi and Ziza and Emmoth.
2 Chronicles 11:21 And Roboam loved Maacha daughter of Abessalom above all his wives and his concubines, because he had eighteen wives and thirty concubines; and he begot twenty-eight sons and sixty daughters.
2 Chronicles 11:22 And Roboam appointed Abia son of Maacha as ruler, to be leader among his brothers, because he intended to make him king;
2 Chronicles 11:23 and he grew beyond all his sons in all the borders of Juda and Benjamin and in the fortified cities, and gave them a great abundance of provisions and requested a multitude of wives.

## Chapter 12

2 Chronicles 12:1 And it came to pass when the kingdom of Roboam was prepared and when it was established, he abandoned the commandments of the Lord, and all Israel with him.
2 Chronicles 12:2 And it came to pass in the fifth year of the reign of Roboam, Sousakim king of Egypt went up against Jerusalem, because they had sinned before the Lord,
2 Chronicles 12:3 with one thousand two hundred chariots and sixty thousand horses, and there was no number of the multitude that came with him from Egypt: Libyans, Troglodytes, and Ethiopians.
2 Chronicles 12:4 And they seized the fortified cities that were in Juda, and he came to Jerusalem.
2 Chronicles 12:5 And Samaias the prophet came to Roboam and to the rulers of Juda, who had gathered in Jerusalem from before Sousakim, and said to them, “Thus said the Lord: You have abandoned me, and I will abandon you into the hand of Sousakim.”
2 Chronicles 12:6 And the rulers of Israel and the king were ashamed and said, “The Lord is righteous.”
2 Chronicles 12:7 And when the Lord saw that they were ashamed, the word of the Lord came to Samaias, saying, “They have been ashamed; I will not utterly destroy them, and I will give them a little for salvation, and by no means will my anger drip in Jerusalem,
2 Chronicles 12:8 because they shall be servants, and they shall know my service and the service of the kingdom of the earth.”
2 Chronicles 12:9 And Sousakim king of Egypt went up and took the treasures that were in the house of the Lord and the treasures that were in the house of the king; he took everything; and he took the golden shields which Solomon made,
2 Chronicles 12:10 and Roboam made bronze shields instead of them. And Sousakim appointed over him leaders of runners, those guarding the gate of the king;
2 Chronicles 12:11 And it came to pass, when the king entered the house of the Lord, the guards and the runners and those returning went in to meet the runners.
2 Chronicles 12:12 And when he was humbled, the wrath of the Lord turned away from him, and not to destruction at the end; for there were good words in Juda.
2 Chronicles 12:13 And Roboam strengthened himself in Jerusalem and reigned; Roboam was forty-one years old when he reigned, and he reigned seventeen years in Jerusalem, in the city which the Lord chose to name his name there from all the tribes of the sons of Israel; and the name of his mother was Noomma the Ammanite.
2 Chronicles 12:14 And he did the evil, because he did not direct his heart to seek the Lord.
2 Chronicles 12:15 And the first and last words of Roboam, are they not, behold, written in the words of Samaias the prophet and of Addo the seer, and his deeds? And Roboam was warring against Ieroboam all the days.
2 Chronicles 12:16 And Roboam died and was buried with his fathers, and was buried in the city of David, and Abia his son reigned in his place.

## Chapter 13

2 Chronicles 13:1 In the eighteenth year of the reign of Ieroboam, Abia reigned over Juda;
2 Chronicles 13:2 he reigned three years in Jerusalem, and the name of his mother was Maacha, daughter of Uriel from Gabaon. And there was war between Abia and between Ieroboam.
2 Chronicles 13:3 And Abia arrayed the battle with a force of mighty warriors, four hundred thousand mighty men, and Ieroboam arrayed against him the battle with eight hundred thousand, mighty warriors of force.
2 Chronicles 13:4 And Abia stood up from Mount Somoron, which is in Mount Ephraim, and said: Hear, Ieroboam and all Israel.
2 Chronicles 13:5 Is it not for you to know that the Lord God of Israel gave the kingdom over Israel forever to David and to his sons, a covenant of salt?
2 Chronicles 13:6 And Ieroboam son of Nabat, the servant of Solomon son of David, rose up and rebelled against his lord.
2 Chronicles 13:7 And worthless men, sons of lawlessness, gathered to him and stood against Roboam son of Solomon; and Roboam was younger and cowardly in heart and did not stand before him.
2 Chronicles 13:8 And now you say you yourselves are standing against the kingdom of the Lord by the hand of the sons of David; and you are a great multitude, and with you are golden calves which Ieroboam made for you as gods.
2 Chronicles 13:9 Have you not cast out the priests of the Lord, the sons of Aaron, and the Levites, and made yourselves priests from the people of the land? Everyone approaching to fill the hands with a calf from the cattle and seven rams becomes a priest to what is not God.
2 Chronicles 13:10 But we have not abandoned the Lord our God, and his priests, the sons of Aaron and the Levites, minister to the Lord in their courses;
2 Chronicles 13:11 they make smoke for the Lord: whole burnt offerings morning and evening, and compound incense, and the presentations of bread upon the pure table, and the golden lampstand and the lamps of burning, to kindle in the evening, because we keep the watches of the Lord God of our fathers, and you have abandoned him.
2 Chronicles 13:12 And behold, with us at the head is God and his priests and the trumpets of signaling to signal against you. Sons of Israel, you will fight against the Lord God of our fathers, because it will not prosper for you. —
2 Chronicles 13:13 And Ieroboam turned the ambush to come from behind them; and it came to be before Juda, and the ambush from behind.
2 Chronicles 13:14 And Juda turned, and behold, the battle was before them and from behind, and they shouted to the Lord, and the priests sounded the trumpets.
2 Chronicles 13:15 And the men of Juda shouted, and it came to pass while the men of Juda were shouting that the Lord struck Ieroboam and Israel before Abia and Juda.
2 Chronicles 13:16 And the sons of Israel fled from before Juda, and the Lord delivered them into their hands.
2 Chronicles 13:17 And Abia and his people struck a great blow among them, and wounded men fell from Israel: five hundred thousand mighty men.
2 Chronicles 13:18 And the sons of Israel were humbled on that day, and the sons of Juda were strengthened, because they hoped upon the Lord God of their fathers.
2 Chronicles 13:19 And Abia pursued after Ieroboam and took cities from him in advance: Baithēl and its villages, and Isana and its villages, and Ephron and its villages.
2 Chronicles 13:20 And Ieroboam had no more strength all the days of Abia, and the Lord struck him, and he died.
2 Chronicles 13:21 And Abia strengthened himself and took for himself fourteen wives, and begot twenty-two sons and sixteen daughters.
2 Chronicles 13:22 And the remaining words of Abia and his deeds and his words are written upon the book of the prophet Addo.
2 Chronicles 13:23 And Abia died with his fathers, and they buried him in the city of David, and Asa his son reigned in his place. In the days of Asa, the land of Juda was quiet for ten years.

## Chapter 14

2 Chronicles 14:1 And he did the good and the straight before the Lord his God.
2 Chronicles 14:2 And he removed the altars of the foreign ones and the high places, and broke the pillars and cut down the groves
2 Chronicles 14:3 and said to Juda to seek the Lord God of their fathers and to do the law and the commandments.
2 Chronicles 14:4 And he removed from all the cities of Juda the altars and the idols. And he had peace;
2 Chronicles 14:5 walled cities in the land of Juda, because the land had peace; and there was no war for him in these years, because the Lord gave him rest.
2 Chronicles 14:6 And he said to Juda, “Let us build these cities and make walls and towers and gates and bars, in which we shall rule over the land, because as we sought the Lord our God, he sought us and gave us rest round about and prospered us.”
2 Chronicles 14:7 And there was for Asa a force of arms-bearers carrying shields and spears, in the land of Juda three hundred thousand, and in the land of Benjamin peltasts and archers, two hundred and fifty thousand; all these were warriors of force.
2 Chronicles 14:8 And Zare the Ethiopian went out against them with a force, with a thousand thousands and three hundred chariots, and came as far as Marisa.
2 Chronicles 14:9 And Asa went out to meet him and arrayed battle in the valley to the north of Marisa.
2 Chronicles 14:10 And Asa cried to the Lord his God and said, “Lord, it is not impossible with you to save with many and with few; strengthen us, Lord our God, because on you we have trusted and upon your name we came against this great multitude; Lord our God, let not a man prevail against you.”
2 Chronicles 14:11 And the Lord struck the Ethiopians before Juda, and the Ethiopians fled;
2 Chronicles 14:12 and Asa and his people pursued them as far as Gedor, and the Ethiopians fell, so that there was no preservation among them, because they were crushed before the Lord and before his force; and they plundered much spoil.
2 Chronicles 14:13 And they cut down their villages around Gedor, because a terror of the Lord came upon them, and they plundered all their cities, because much spoil came to them;
2 Chronicles 14:14 and indeed tents of possessions, the Amazoneans, they cut down, and took many sheep and camels and returned to Jerusalem.

## Chapter 15

2 Chronicles 15:1 And Azarias son of Oded, the spirit of the Lord came upon him,
2 Chronicles 15:2 and he went out to meet Asa and all Juda and Benjamin and said, “Hear me, Asa and all Juda and Benjamin; the Lord is with you when you are with him, and if you seek him, he will be found for you, and if you abandon him, he will abandon you.
2 Chronicles 15:3 And many days for Israel with no true God, and no priest teaching, and with no law;
2 Chronicles 15:4 and it will turn to the Lord God of Israel, and he will be found for them.
2 Chronicles 15:5 And in that time there is no peace for the one going out and for the one coming in, because a terror of the Lord is upon all who dwell in the lands.
2 Chronicles 15:6 And nation will fight against nation and city against city, because God astounded them in every affliction.
2 Chronicles 15:7 And you, be strong, and do not let your hands grow slack, because there is a reward for your labor.” –
2 Chronicles 15:8 And upon hearing these words and the prophecy of Adad the prophet, he strengthened himself and cast the abominations out from all the land of Juda and Benjamin and from the cities which he had captured in Mount Ephraim, and dedicated the altar of the Lord which was before the temple of the Lord.
2 Chronicles 15:9 And he assembled Juda and Benjamin and the proselytes who were resident with him from Ephraim and from Manasse and from Symeon, because many of Israel had been added to him when they saw that the Lord his God was with him.
2 Chronicles 15:10 And they gathered to Jerusalem in the third month, in the fifteenth year of the reign of Asa.
2 Chronicles 15:11 And he sacrificed to the Lord on that day from the spoils which they had brought: seven hundred calves and seven thousand sheep.
2 Chronicles 15:12 And he passed into a covenant to seek the Lord God of their fathers with all the heart and with all the soul;
2 Chronicles 15:13 and everyone who should not seek the Lord God of Israel shall die, from younger to older, from man to woman.
2 Chronicles 15:14 And they swore by the Lord with a great voice and with trumpets and with horns.
2 Chronicles 15:15 And all Juda rejoiced over the oath, because with all the soul they swore and with every willingness they sought him, and he was found for them, and the Lord gave them rest round about. –
2 Chronicles 15:16 And Maacha his mother he removed from serving Astarte, and he cut down the idol and burned it in the torrent of Kedron.
2 Chronicles 15:17 Except the high places did not depart; they still existed in Israel; but the heart of Asa became full all his days.
2 Chronicles 15:18 And he brought in the holy things of David his father and the holy things of the house of the Lord God: silver and gold and vessels.
2 Chronicles 15:19 And there was no war with him until the thirty-fifth year of the reign of Asa.

## Chapter 16

2 Chronicles 16:1 And in the thirty-eighth year of the reign of Asa, Baasa king of Israel went up against Juda and built Rama, so as not to give an exit and an entrance to Asa king of Juda.
2 Chronicles 16:2 And Asa took gold and silver from the treasures of the house of the Lord and of the king’s house and sent to the son of Ader king of Syria, who dwelt in Damascus, saying,
2 Chronicles 16:3 “Make a covenant between me and you and between my father and your father; behold, I have sent you gold and silver; come and scatter Baasa king of Israel away from me, and let him depart from me.”
2 Chronicles 16:4 And the son of Ader heard king Asa and sent the rulers of his force against the cities of Israel and struck Ion and Dan and Abelmain and all the surrounding regions of Nephthali.
2 Chronicles 16:5 And it came to pass, when Baasa heard, he left off building Rama any longer and stopped his work.
2 Chronicles 16:6 And Asa the king took all Juda and took the stones of Rama and its timbers, which Baasa had built, and built with them Gabae and Maspha. –
2 Chronicles 16:7 And at that time Anani the prophet came to Asa king of Juda and said to him, “Because you have trusted in the king of Syria and have not trusted in the Lord your God, for this reason the force of Syria escaped from your hand.
2 Chronicles 16:8 Were not the Ethiopians and Libyans a great force in courage, in horsemen an exceedingly great multitude? And when you trusted in the Lord, he delivered into your hands.
2 Chronicles 16:9 For the eyes of the Lord look upon all the earth, to strengthen with every heart full toward him. You have acted ignorantly in this; from now on there will be war with you.”
2 Chronicles 16:10 And Asa became angry with the prophet and placed him in prison, because he was enraged at this; and Asa maltreated among the people at that time.
2 Chronicles 16:11 And behold, the words of Asa, the first and the last, are written in the book of the kings of Juda and Israel.
2 Chronicles 16:12 And Asa became diseased in his feet in the thirty-ninth year of his reign, until he was exceedingly diseased; and in his disease he did not seek the Lord, but the physicians.
2 Chronicles 16:13 And Asa slept with his fathers and died in the thirty-ninth year of his reign,
2 Chronicles 16:14 and they buried him in the tomb which he dug for himself in the city of David, and laid him on the bed and filled with spices and kinds of ointments of perfumers and made for him an exceedingly great funeral procession.

## Chapter 17

2 Chronicles 17:1 And Josaphat his son reigned in his stead, and Josaphat grew strong against Israel.
2 Chronicles 17:2 And he placed a force in all the fortified cities of Juda and appointed leaders in all the cities of Juda and in the cities of Ephraim which Asa his father had previously taken.
2 Chronicles 17:3 And the Lord was with Josaphat, because he walked in the first ways of his father and did not seek the idols,
2 Chronicles 17:4 but sought the Lord, the God of his father, and walked in the commandments of his father, and not according to the works of Israel.
2 Chronicles 17:5 And the Lord established the kingdom in his hand, and all Juda gave gifts to Josaphat, and he had wealth and much glory.
2 Chronicles 17:6 And his heart was exalted in the way of the Lord, and he further removed the high places and the groves from the land of Juda.
2 Chronicles 17:7 And in the third year of his reign he sent his leaders and the sons of the mighty, Abdias and Zacharias and Nathanael and Michaias, to teach in the cities of Juda,
2 Chronicles 17:8 and with them the Levites Samouias and Nathanias and Zabdias and Asiel and Semiramoth and Jonathan and Adonias and Tobias, the Levites, and with them Elisama and Joram the priests,
2 Chronicles 17:9 and they taught in Juda, and with them was a book of the law of the Lord, and they went through the cities of Juda and taught the people.
2 Chronicles 17:10 And a terror of the Lord came upon all the kingdoms of the land around Juda, and they did not wage war against Josaphat;
2 Chronicles 17:11 and from the foreigners they brought Josaphat gifts and silver and presents, and the Arabs brought him seven thousand seven hundred rams of sheep.
2 Chronicles 17:12 And Josaphat went on becoming greater unto a height, and built dwellings in Judea and fortified cities.
2 Chronicles 17:13 And he had many works in Judea and mighty warriors, strong in Jerusalem.
2 Chronicles 17:14 And this was their number according to the houses of their families: for Juda, commanders of thousands, Ednas the ruler, and with him three hundred thousand mighty sons of force;
2 Chronicles 17:15 and after him Joanan the leader, and with him two hundred and eighty thousand;
2 Chronicles 17:16 and after him Amasias, the son of Zachri, who was eager for the Lord, and with him two hundred thousand mighty men of force.
2 Chronicles 17:17 And from Benjamin, a mighty man of force, Eliada, and with him two hundred thousand archers and peltasts;
2 Chronicles 17:18 and after him Jozabad, and with him a hundred and eighty thousand mighty men of war.
2 Chronicles 17:19 These were those serving the king, besides those whom the king placed in the fortified cities in all Judea.

## Chapter 18

2 Chronicles 18:1 And Josaphat still had wealth and much glory, and he allied himself by marriage in the house of Achaab.
2 Chronicles 18:2 And at the end of years he went down to Achaab in Samaria, and Achaab sacrificed many sheep and calves for him and for the people with him, and deceived him into going up with him to Ramoth of Galaaditis.
2 Chronicles 18:3 And Achaab king of Israel said to Josaphat king of Juda, “Will you go with me to Ramoth of Galaaditis?” And he said to him, “As I, so also you; as your people, also my people with you for war.”
2 Chronicles 18:4 And Josaphat said to the king of Israel, “Seek the Lord today, then.”
2 Chronicles 18:5 And the king of Israel gathered the prophets, four hundred men, and said to them, “Shall I go to Ramoth Galaad for war, or hold back?” And they said, “Go up, and God will give into the hands of the king.”
2 Chronicles 18:6 And Josaphat said, “Is there not yet a prophet of the Lord here, and we shall inquire of him?”
2 Chronicles 18:7 And the king of Israel said to Josaphat, “There is yet one man through whom to seek the Lord, and I have hated him, because he is not prophesying good concerning me, because all his days are for evil; this is Michaias son of Jemla.” And Josaphat said, “Let not the king speak thus.”
2 Chronicles 18:8 And the king of Israel called one eunuch and said, “Quickly, Michaias son of Jemla.”
2 Chronicles 18:9 And the king of Israel and Josaphat king of Juda were sitting, each upon his throne, and clothed in robes, sitting in the broad space at the door of the gate of Samaria, and all the prophets were prophesying before them.
2 Chronicles 18:10 And Sedekias son of Chanana made himself iron horns and said, “Thus says the Lord: With these you will gore Syria until it is brought to an end.”
2 Chronicles 18:11 And all the prophets were prophesying thus, saying, “Go up to Ramoth Galaad and you will be prospered, and the Lord will give into the hands of the king.”
2 Chronicles 18:12 And the messenger who went to call Michaias spoke to him, saying, “Behold, the prophets have spoken good concerning the king with one mouth, and let your words, then, be as one of theirs, and you shall speak good.”
2 Chronicles 18:13 And Michaias said, “The Lord lives, that whatever God should say to me, that I shall speak.”
2 Chronicles 18:14 And he came to the king, and the king said to him, “Michaias, shall I go to Ramoth Galaad for war, or hold back?” And he said, “Go up and you will prosper, and they will be given into your hands.”
2 Chronicles 18:15 And the king said to him, “How many times do I adjure you that you speak to me only truth in the name of the Lord?”
2 Chronicles 18:16 And he said, “I saw Israel scattered in the mountains as sheep that have no shepherd, and the Lord said, ‘They have no leader; let them return, each to his house in peace.’”
2 Chronicles 18:17 And the king of Israel said to Josaphat, “Did I not tell you that he does not prophesy good concerning me, but evil?”
2 Chronicles 18:18 And he said, “Not so; hear a word of the Lord: I saw the Lord sitting upon his throne, and all the force of heaven stood at his right and at his left.
2 Chronicles 18:19 And the Lord said, ‘Who will deceive Achaab king of Israel, and he will go up and fall in Ramoth Galaad?’ And this one spoke thus, and this one spoke thus.
2 Chronicles 18:20 And the spirit came out and stood before the Lord and said, ‘I will deceive him.’ And the Lord said, ‘With what?’
2 Chronicles 18:21 And he said, ‘I will go out and be a false spirit in the mouth of all his prophets.’ And he said, ‘You will deceive and will be able; go out and do thus.’
2 Chronicles 18:22 And now behold, the Lord has put a false spirit in the mouth of all these prophets of yours, and the Lord has spoken evil against you.”
2 Chronicles 18:23 And Sedekias son of Chanana drew near and struck Michaias on the jaw and said to him, “By what way did the spirit of the Lord pass from me to speak to you?”
2 Chronicles 18:24 And Michaias said, “Behold, you will see on that day on which you enter a chamber from a chamber to hide yourself.”
2 Chronicles 18:25 And the king of Israel said, “Take Michaias and send him back to Emer ruler of the city and to Joas the ruler, the son of the king,
2 Chronicles 18:26 and you shall say, ‘Thus said the king: Put this one in a house of imprisonment, and let him eat bread of affliction and water of affliction until I return in peace.’”
2 Chronicles 18:27 And Michaias said, “If returning you return in peace, the Lord has not spoken in me; hear, all peoples.”
2 Chronicles 18:28 And the king of Israel and Josaphat king of Juda went up to Ramoth Galaad.
2 Chronicles 18:29 And the king of Israel said to Josaphat, “I will cover myself and enter the war, and you put on my clothing”; and the king of Israel covered himself and entered the war.
2 Chronicles 18:30 And the king of Syria commanded the rulers of the chariots who were with him, saying, “Do not fight the small and the great, but only the king of Israel.”
2 Chronicles 18:31 And it came to pass, when the rulers of the chariots saw Josaphat, they said, “He is the king of Israel,” and surrounded him to fight; and Josaphat cried out, and the Lord saved him, and God turned them away from him.
2 Chronicles 18:32 And it came to pass, when the rulers of the chariots saw that he was not the king of Israel, they turned away from him.
2 Chronicles 18:33 And a man drew a bow with good aim and struck the king of Israel between the lung and the breastplate. And he said to the charioteer, “Turn your hand and take me out of the war, because I have been hurt.”
2 Chronicles 18:34 And the battle was turned to flight on that day, and the king of Israel stood upon the chariot until evening opposite Syria and died as the sun was setting.

## Chapter 19

2 Chronicles 19:1 And Josaphat king of Juda returned to his house in peace, to Jerusalem.
2 Chronicles 19:2 And Ju, the son of Anani, the prophet, went out to meet him and said to him, “King Josaphat, do you help a sinner, or befriend one hated by the Lord? For this reason wrath from the Lord came upon you;
2 Chronicles 19:3 but good words were found in you, because you removed the groves from the land of Juda and directed your heart to seek the Lord.”
2 Chronicles 19:4 And Josaphat dwelt in Jerusalem and again went out to the people from Bersabee as far as Mount Ephraim and turned them to the Lord God of their fathers.
2 Chronicles 19:5 And he appointed judges in all the fortified cities of Juda, in city after city,
2 Chronicles 19:6 and said to the judges, “See what you are doing, because you judge for the Lord, not for man, and with you are the words of the judgment;
2 Chronicles 19:7 and now let the fear of the Lord come upon you, and keep watch and you shall act, because with the Lord our God there is no injustice, nor admiration of a face, nor taking of gifts.”
2 Chronicles 19:8 For also in Jerusalem Josaphat appointed from the priests and the Levites and the patriarchs of Israel for the judgment of the Lord and to judge those dwelling in Jerusalem.
2 Chronicles 19:9 And he commanded them, saying, “Thus you shall act in the fear of the Lord, in truth and with a full heart;
2 Chronicles 19:10 every man, the judgment coming upon you from your brothers dwelling in their cities, between blood and blood and between ordinance and commandment and statutes and judgments, and you shall give them directions, and they will not sin against the Lord, and there will be no wrath upon you and upon your brothers; thus you shall act and will not sin.
2 Chronicles 19:11 And behold, Amarias the priest is leader over you for every word of the Lord, and Zabdias son of Ismael, the leader for the house of Juda, for every word of the king, and the scribes and the Levites before your face; be strong and act, and the Lord will be with the good.”

## Chapter 20

2 Chronicles 20:1 And after these things the sons of Moab and the sons of Ammon, and with them some of the Minaeans, came against Josaphat for war.
2 Chronicles 20:2 And they came and informed Josaphat, saying, “A great multitude has come against you from beyond the sea, from Syria, and behold, they are in Asasanthamar [this is Engaddi].”
2 Chronicles 20:3 And he was afraid, and Josaphat set his face to seek the Lord and proclaimed a fast in all Juda.
2 Chronicles 20:4 And Juda gathered to seek the Lord, and from all the cities of Juda they came to seek the Lord.
2 Chronicles 20:5 And Josaphat stood in the assembly of Juda in Jerusalem, in the house of the Lord, before the new court,
2 Chronicles 20:6 and said, “Lord God of our fathers, are you not God in heaven, and you rule all the kingdoms of the nations, and in your hand is strength of dominion, and it is not possible to stand against you?
2 Chronicles 20:7 Are you not the Lord who destroyed those dwelling in this land from before your people Israel and gave it to the seed of Abraham your beloved forever?
2 Chronicles 20:8 And they dwelt in it and built in it a sanctuary for your name, saying,
2 Chronicles 20:9 ‘If evils come upon us, sword, judgment, death, famine, we shall stand before this house and before you, because your name is upon this house, and we shall cry to you out of affliction, and you will hear and save.’
2 Chronicles 20:10 And now behold, the sons of Ammon and Moab and Mount Seir, among whom you did not allow Israel to pass through them when they came out of the land of Egypt, because they turned aside from them and did not destroy them,
2 Chronicles 20:11 and now behold, they attempt to come out against us, to cast us out of our inheritance which you gave us.
2 Chronicles 20:12 Lord our God, will you not judge among them? Because we have no strength to stand against this great multitude that has come against us, and we do not know what we should do to them, but our eyes are upon you.”
2 Chronicles 20:13 And all Juda stood before the Lord, and their children and the women. –
2 Chronicles 20:14 And for Oziel, the son of Zacharias, of the sons of Banaias, of the sons of Eleel, of Manthanias the Levite, from the sons of Asaph, the spirit of the Lord came upon him in the assembly,
2 Chronicles 20:15 and he said, “Hear, all Juda and those dwelling in Jerusalem and king Josaphat; thus says the Lord to you yourselves: Do not fear nor be terrified before this great crowd, because the battle belongs to God, not to you.
2 Chronicles 20:16 Tomorrow go down against them; behold, they are coming up by the ascent of Asas, and you will find them at the end of the river of the wilderness of Jeriel.
2 Chronicles 20:17 It is not for you to fight; understand these things and see the salvation of the Lord with you, Juda and Jerusalem; do not fear nor be terrified to go out tomorrow to meet them, and the Lord is with you.” –
2 Chronicles 20:18 And Josaphat bowed upon his face, and all Juda and those dwelling in Jerusalem fell before the Lord to worship the Lord.
2 Chronicles 20:19 And the Levites from the sons of Kaath and from the sons of Kore stood up to praise the Lord God of Israel with a great voice on high.
2 Chronicles 20:20 And they rose early in the morning and went out to the wilderness of Thekoe, and as they went out Josaphat stood and cried out and said, “Hear me, Juda and those dwelling in Jerusalem; trust in the Lord your God, and you will be trusted; trust in his prophet, and you will be prospered.”
2 Chronicles 20:21 And he took counsel with the people and appointed psalm-singers and those praising to give thanks and praise the holy things as they went out before the force, and they said, “Give thanks to the Lord, because his mercy is forever.”
2 Chronicles 20:22 And when his praise of thanksgiving began, the Lord caused the sons of Ammon to fight against Moab and Mount Seir, those who had come out against Juda, and they were routed.
2 Chronicles 20:23 And the sons of Ammon and Moab rose against those dwelling on Mount Seir to destroy and wipe out; and when they made an end of those dwelling in Seir, they rose against one another to be destroyed.
2 Chronicles 20:24 And Juda came to the lookout of the wilderness and looked and saw the multitude, and behold, all were dead, fallen upon the ground; there was none escaping.
2 Chronicles 20:25 And Josaphat and his people came to plunder their spoils and found many cattle and baggage and spoils and desirable vessels, and plundered for themselves, and they spent three days plundering the spoils, because they were many.
2 Chronicles 20:26 And on the fourth day they gathered in the valley of blessing, for there they blessed the Lord; for this reason they called the name of that place Valley of Blessing until this day.
2 Chronicles 20:27 And every man of Juda returned to Jerusalem, and Josaphat leading them, with great gladness, because the Lord gladdened them on account of their enemies,
2 Chronicles 20:28 and they entered Jerusalem with nablas and lyres and trumpets, into the house of the Lord.
2 Chronicles 20:29 And a terror of the Lord came upon all the kingdoms of the earth when they heard that the Lord fought against the adversaries of Israel.
2 Chronicles 20:30 And the kingdom of Josaphat had peace, and his God gave him rest round about.
2 Chronicles 20:31 And Josaphat reigned over Juda, thirty-five years old when he became king, and he reigned twenty-five years in Jerusalem, and his mother’s name was Azouba daughter of Sali.
2 Chronicles 20:32 And he walked in the ways of his father Asa and did not turn aside from doing the straight before the Lord;
2 Chronicles 20:33 but the high places still existed, and still the people did not direct their heart toward the Lord God of their fathers.
2 Chronicles 20:34 And the remaining words of Josaphat, the first and the last, behold, are written in the words of Ju the son of Anani, who wrote down a book of the kings of Israel.
2 Chronicles 20:35 And after these things Josaphat king of Juda joined with Ochozias king of Israel [and this one acted lawlessly]
2 Chronicles 20:36 in acting and going to him to make ships to go to Tharsis, and he made ships in Gasiongaber.
2 Chronicles 20:37 And Eliezer, the son of Dodias, from Marisa, prophesied against Josaphat, saying, “As you befriended Ochozias, the Lord shattered your work, and your ships were broken.” And he was unable to go to Tharsis.

## Chapter 21

2 Chronicles 21:1 And Josaphat slept with his fathers and was buried beside his fathers in the city of David, and Joram his son reigned in his stead.
2 Chronicles 21:2 And he had six brothers, sons of Josaphat: Azarias and Jiel and Zacharias and Azarias and Michael and Saphatias; all these were sons of Josaphat king of Juda.
2 Chronicles 21:3 And their father gave them many gifts, silver and gold and arms, with walled cities in Juda; and he gave the kingdom to Joram, because this one was the firstborn.
2 Chronicles 21:4 And Joram rose over his kingdom and became strong and killed all his brothers with a sword, and some of the rulers of Israel.
2 Chronicles 21:5 When he was thirty-two years old, Joram was established over his kingdom, and he reigned eight years in Jerusalem.
2 Chronicles 21:6 And he walked in the way of the kings of Israel, as the house of Achaab did, because a daughter of Achaab was his wife, and he did the evil before the Lord.
2 Chronicles 21:7 And the Lord was unwilling to destroy the house of David because of the covenant which he made with David, and as he told him to give a lamp to him and to his sons all the days.
2 Chronicles 21:8 In those days Edom revolted from Juda, and they made a king reign over themselves.
2 Chronicles 21:9 And Joram went with the rulers, and all the cavalry with him; and it came to pass, he rose by night and struck Edom who surrounded him and the rulers of the chariots, and the people fled to their dwellings.
2 Chronicles 21:10 And Edom revolted from Juda until this day; then Lomna revolted at that time from his hand, because he abandoned the Lord God of his fathers.
2 Chronicles 21:11 For he also made high places in the cities of Juda and caused those dwelling in Jerusalem to commit fornication and led Juda astray.
2 Chronicles 21:12 And a writing came to him from Elias the prophet, saying, “Thus says the Lord, the God of David your father: Because you did not walk in the way of Josaphat your father and in the ways of Asa king of Juda,
2 Chronicles 21:13 and walked in the ways of the kings of Israel and caused Juda and those dwelling in Jerusalem to commit fornication, as the house of Achaab caused fornication, and killed your brothers, the sons of your father, who were better than you,
2 Chronicles 21:14 behold, the Lord will strike you with a great blow among your people and among your sons and among your wives and among all your baggage,
2 Chronicles 21:15 and you with an evil disease, with a disease of the belly, until your bowels come out with the disease from days to days.”
2 Chronicles 21:16 And the Lord stirred up against Joram the foreigners and the Arabs and the neighbors of the Ethiopians,
2 Chronicles 21:17 and they went up against Juda and oppressed and carried away all the baggage which they found in the king’s house, and his sons and his daughters, and no son was left to him except Ochozias, the youngest of his sons.
2 Chronicles 21:18 And after all these things the Lord struck him in the belly with a disease in which there is no healing;
2 Chronicles 21:19 and it came to pass from days to days, and when the time of the days came, two days, his bowels came out with the disease, and he died with an evil disease. And his people did not make a funeral procession as the funeral procession of his fathers.
2 Chronicles 21:20 He was thirty-two years old when he became king, and he reigned eight years in Jerusalem; and he went away without praise and was buried in the city of David and not in the tombs of the kings.

## Chapter 22

2 Chronicles 22:1 And those dwelling in Jerusalem made Ochozias his young son reign in his stead, because the band of robbers that came upon them, the Arabs and the Alimazoneans, killed all the older ones; and Ochozias son of Joram king of Juda reigned.
2 Chronicles 22:2 Ochozias became king when he was twenty years old, and he reigned one year in Jerusalem, and his mother’s name was Gotholia daughter of Ambri.
2 Chronicles 22:3 And this one walked in the way of the house of Achaab, because his mother was a counselor to sin;
2 Chronicles 22:4 and he did the evil before the Lord as the house of Achaab, because after his father died they were counselors to him to destroy him,
2 Chronicles 22:5 and he walked in their counsels. And he went with Joram son of Achaab for war against Azael king of Syria to Rama Galaad; and the archers struck Joram.
2 Chronicles 22:6 And Joram returned to Jezrael to be healed from the wounds with which the Syrians struck him in Rama when he fought against Azael king of Syria; and Ochozias son of Joram king of Juda went down to see Joram son of Achaab in Jezrael, because he was ill.
2 Chronicles 22:7 And from God came the downfall of Ochozias in coming to Joram; and when he came, Joram went out with him to Ju son of Namessi, the Lord’s anointed, the house of Achaab.
2 Chronicles 22:8 And it came to pass, when Ju avenged the house of Achaab, he found the rulers of Juda and the brothers of Ochozias serving Ochozias and killed them.
2 Chronicles 22:9 And he said to seek Ochozias, and they caught him being treated in Samaria and brought him to Ju, and he killed him. And they buried him, because they said, “He is a son of Josaphat, who sought the Lord with all his heart.” And there was none in the house of Ochozias to strengthen a force concerning the kingdom.
2 Chronicles 22:10 And Gotholia the mother of Ochozias saw that her son had died, and rose and destroyed all the seed of the kingdom in the house of Juda.
2 Chronicles 22:11 And Josabeth the king’s daughter took Joas son of Ochozias and stole him from among the king’s sons who were being put to death and placed him and his nurse in the chamber of the beds; and Josabeth, daughter of king Joram, sister of Ochozias, wife of Jodae the priest, hid him and hid him from the face of Gotholia, and she did not kill him.
2 Chronicles 22:12 And he was with her in the house of God, hidden for six years, and Gotholia reigned over the land.

## Chapter 23

2 Chronicles 23:1 And in the seventh year Jodae strengthened himself and took the commanders of hundreds, Azarias son of Joram and Ismael son of Joanan and Azarias son of Obed and Maasaias son of Adaias and Elisaphan son of Zacharias, with him into a house.
2 Chronicles 23:2 And they went around Juda and gathered the Levites from all the cities of Juda and rulers of the families of Israel, and came to Jerusalem.
2 Chronicles 23:3 And all the assembly of Juda made a covenant in the house of God with the king, and he showed them the king’s son and said to them, “Behold, let the king’s son reign, as the Lord spoke concerning the house of David.
2 Chronicles 23:4 Now this is the matter which you shall do: let a third of you, of the priests and the Levites, enter on the sabbath, and into the gates of the entrances,
2 Chronicles 23:5 and a third in the king’s house, and a third in the middle gate, and all the people in the courts of the house of the Lord.
2 Chronicles 23:6 And let none enter the house of the Lord except the priests and the Levites and those serving of the Levites; they shall enter, because they are holy, and let all the people keep the watches of the Lord.
2 Chronicles 23:7 And the Levites shall surround the king round about, a man’s weapon in his hand, and the one entering the house shall die; and they shall be with the king as he enters and goes out.”
2 Chronicles 23:8 And the Levites and all Juda did according to all that Jodae the priest commanded, and each took his men from the beginning of the sabbath until the departure of the sabbath, because Jodae did not dismiss the divisions.
2 Chronicles 23:9 And he gave the swords and the shields and the arms which belonged to king David in the house of God.
2 Chronicles 23:10 And he stationed all the people, each with his arms, from the right flank of the house as far as the left flank of the altar and the house, around the king.
2 Chronicles 23:11 And he brought out the king’s son and put upon him the crown and the testimonies, and Jodae and his sons made him king and anointed him and said, “Let the king live.”
2 Chronicles 23:12 And Gotholia heard the voice of the people running and giving thanks and praising the king, and entered to the king in the house of the Lord.
2 Chronicles 23:13 And she saw, and behold, the king at his station, and at the entrance the rulers and the trumpets around the king, and all the people rejoiced and sounded the trumpets, and the singers with the instruments, singing and hymning praise; and Gotholia tore her robe and cried out and said, “Attacking, you attack.”
2 Chronicles 23:14 And Jodae the priest went out, and Jodae the priest commanded the commanders of hundreds and the leaders of the force and said to them, “Cast her outside the house and go in behind her, and let her die by a sword”; because the priest said, “Let her not die in the house of the Lord.”
2 Chronicles 23:15 And they gave her room, and she went through the gate of the horsemen of the king’s house, and they put her to death there. –
2 Chronicles 23:16 And Jodae made a covenant between himself and the people and the king, to be a people for the Lord.
2 Chronicles 23:17 And all the people of the land entered the house of Baal and tore it down, and pulverized his altars and idols, and put Matthan the priest of Baal to death before his altars.
2 Chronicles 23:18 And Jodae the priest entrusted the works of the house of the Lord through the hand of priests and Levites and established the divisions of the priests and the Levites which David appointed over the house of the Lord, and to offer whole burnt offerings to the Lord, as it is written in the law of Moses, with gladness and with songs through the hand of David.
2 Chronicles 23:19 And the gatekeepers stood at the gates of the house of the Lord, and none unclean in any matter shall enter.
2 Chronicles 23:20 And he took the patriarchs and the mighty men and the rulers of the people and all the people of the land, and they brought the king up into the house of the Lord, and he entered through the inner gate into the king’s house, and they seated the king upon the throne of the kingdom.
2 Chronicles 23:21 And all the people of the land rejoiced, and the city was quiet; and they put Gotholia to death with a sword.

## Chapter 24

2 Chronicles 24:1 Joas was seven years old when he became king, and he reigned forty years in Jerusalem, and his mother’s name was Sabia from Bersabee.
2 Chronicles 24:2 And Joas did the straight before the Lord all the days of Jodae the priest.
2 Chronicles 24:3 And Jodae took two wives for him, and he begot sons and daughters.
2 Chronicles 24:4 And it came to pass after these things, and it came upon the heart of Joas to repair the house of the Lord.
2 Chronicles 24:5 And he gathered the priests and the Levites and said to them, “Go out to the cities of Juda and gather silver from all Israel to strengthen the house of the Lord year by year, and hasten to speak”; and the Levites did not hasten.
2 Chronicles 24:6 And king Joas called Jodae the ruler and said to him, “Why did you not attend to the Levites to bring in from Juda and Jerusalem what was determined by Moses the man of God, when he assembled Israel for the tent of testimony?
2 Chronicles 24:7 For Gotholia was the lawless one, and her sons tore down the house of God, for they also used the holy things of the house of the Lord for the Baalim.”
2 Chronicles 24:8 And the king said, “Let a chest be made and let it be placed outside at the gate of the house of the Lord;
2 Chronicles 24:9 and let them proclaim in Juda and in Jerusalem to bring in for the Lord, as Moses the servant of God said concerning Israel in the wilderness.”
2 Chronicles 24:10 And all the rulers and all the people gave, and brought in and cast into the chest until it was filled.
2 Chronicles 24:11 And it came to pass, as they brought the chest to the king’s overseers through the hand of the Levites, and as they saw that the silver had increased, the king’s scribe and the overseer of the great priest came and emptied the chest and set it in its place; thus they did day by day and gathered much silver.
2 Chronicles 24:12 And the king and Jodae the priest gave it to those doing the works for the work of the house of the Lord, and they hired stonecutters and carpenters to repair the house of the Lord, and smiths of iron and bronze to repair the house of the Lord.
2 Chronicles 24:13 And those doing the works worked, and the extent of the works increased in their hands, and they restored the house of the Lord to its standing and strengthened it.
2 Chronicles 24:14 And when they finished, they brought the remainder of the silver to the king and to Jodae, and made vessels for the house of the Lord, vessels for the service of whole burnt offerings and gold and silver censers. And they offered whole burnt offerings in the house of the Lord continually, all the days of Jodae.
2 Chronicles 24:15 And Jodae grew old, full of days, and died, being a hundred and thirty years old when he died;
2 Chronicles 24:16 and they buried him in the city of David with the kings, because he did goodness with Israel and with God and his house.
2 Chronicles 24:17 And it came to pass after the death of Jodae, the rulers of Juda entered and bowed down to the king; then the king listened to them.
2 Chronicles 24:18 And they abandoned the Lord God of their fathers and served the Astartes and the idols; and wrath came upon Juda and upon Jerusalem on this day.
2 Chronicles 24:19 And he sent prophets to them to turn to the Lord, and they did not hear; and they testified to them, and they did not hear.
2 Chronicles 24:20 And the spirit of God clothed Azarias, the son of Jodae, the priest, and he stood above the people and said, “Thus says the Lord: Why do you pass by the commandments of the Lord? And you will not be prospered, because you abandoned the Lord, and he will abandon you.”
2 Chronicles 24:21 And they attacked him and stoned him by the command of Joas the king in the court of the house of the Lord.
2 Chronicles 24:22 And Joas did not remember the mercy which Jodae his father did with him, and put his son to death. And as he was dying, he said, “May the Lord see, and let him judge.”
2 Chronicles 24:23 And it came to pass after the completion of the year, a force of Syria went up against him and came against Juda and against Jerusalem and destroyed all the rulers of the people among the people, and they sent all their spoils to the king of Damascus.
2 Chronicles 24:24 For the force of Syria came with few men, and God delivered an exceedingly great force into their hands, because they abandoned the Lord God of their fathers; and he executed judgments with Joas.
2 Chronicles 24:25 And after they departed from him, leaving him with great diseases, his servants attacked him for the blood of the son of Jodae the priest and put him to death on his bed, and he died; and they buried him in the city of David, and did not bury him in the tomb of the kings.
2 Chronicles 24:26 And those who attacked him were Zabed, the son of Samath, the Ammanite, and Jozabed, the son of Somaroth, the Moabite,
2 Chronicles 24:27 and all his sons, and the five approached him. And the remaining things, behold, are written in the writing of the kings; and Amasias his son reigned in his stead.

## Chapter 25

2 Chronicles 25:1 Amasias became king when he was twenty-five years old, and he reigned twenty-nine years in Jerusalem, and his mother’s name was Joaden from Jerusalem.
2 Chronicles 25:2 And he did the straight before the Lord, but not with a full heart.
2 Chronicles 25:3 And it came to pass, when the kingdom was established in his hand, he put to death his servants who murdered the king his father;
2 Chronicles 25:4 and he did not kill their sons, according to the covenant of the law of the Lord, as it is written, as the Lord commanded, saying, “Fathers shall not die for children, and sons shall not die for fathers, but each for his own sin they shall die.” –
