2 Chronicles 25:5 And Amasias gathered the house of Juda and stationed them according to the houses of their families under commanders of thousands and commanders of hundreds in all Juda and Jerusalem; and he numbered them from twenty years old and upward and found them three hundred thousand, able to go out to war, holding spear and shield.
2 Chronicles 25:6 And he hired from Israel a hundred thousand mighty in strength for a hundred talents of silver.
2 Chronicles 25:7 And a man of God came to him, saying, “King, the force of Israel shall not go with you, because the Lord is not with Israel, all the sons of Ephraim;
2 Chronicles 25:8 for if you suppose that you will be strong with these, the Lord will also rout you before the enemies, because both being strong and being routed are from the Lord.”
2 Chronicles 25:9 And Amasias said to the man of God, “And what shall I do about the hundred talents which I gave to the force of Israel?” And the man of God said, “The Lord is able to give you much more than these.”
2 Chronicles 25:10 And Amasias set apart the force which had come to him from Ephraim to depart to their place, and they became exceedingly angry against Juda and returned to their place in furious wrath.
2 Chronicles 25:11 And Amasias strengthened himself and took his people and went to the valley of salts and struck there ten thousand of the sons of Seir;
2 Chronicles 25:12 and the sons of Juda captured ten thousand alive and brought them to the top of the cliff and threw them down from the top of the cliff, and all were torn apart.
2 Chronicles 25:13 And the sons of the force whom Amasias sent back so as not to go with him to war attacked the cities of Juda from Samaria as far as Baethoron and struck three thousand among them and plundered much spoil. –
2 Chronicles 25:14 And it came to pass, after Amasias came, having struck Idumea, he brought to them the gods of the sons of Seir and set them up for himself as gods, and bowed down before them, and he himself sacrificed to them.
2 Chronicles 25:15 And the wrath of the Lord came upon Amasias, and he sent prophets to him, and they said to him, “Why did you seek the gods of the people, who did not rescue their people from your hand?”
2 Chronicles 25:16 And it came to pass, as he spoke to him, he said to him, “Have I made you a counselor of the king? Take care that you are not scourged.” And the prophet fell silent. And he said, “I know that he wished concerning you to destroy you, because you did this and did not listen to my counsel.” –
2 Chronicles 25:17 And Amasias took counsel and sent to Joas son of Joachaz son of Ju, king of Israel, saying, “Come, let us be seen face to face.”
2 Chronicles 25:18 And Joas king of Israel sent to Amasias king of Juda, saying, “The achouch in Lebanon sent to the cedar in Lebanon, saying, ‘Give your daughter to my son as a wife.’ And behold, the wild beasts of the field in Lebanon will come; and the wild beasts came and trampled the achouch.
2 Chronicles 25:19 You said, ‘Behold, you struck Idumea,’ and the heavy heart lifts you up; now sit in your house, and why do you engage in evil, and you and Juda with you fall?”
2 Chronicles 25:20 And Amasias did not hear, because it came from the Lord to deliver him into hands, because he sought the gods of the Idumeans.
2 Chronicles 25:21 And Joas king of Israel went up, and he and Amasias king of Juda were seen by one another in Baethsamys, which belongs to Juda.
2 Chronicles 25:22 And Juda was routed before Israel, and each fled to the dwelling.
2 Chronicles 25:23 And Joas king of Israel caught Amasias king of Juda, the son of Joas, in Baethsamys and brought him into Jerusalem and tore down four hundred cubits of the wall of Jerusalem from the gate of Ephraim as far as the corner gate;
2 Chronicles 25:24 and all the gold and the silver and all the vessels found in the house of the Lord and with Abdedom, and the treasures of the king’s house, and the sons of the interminglings, and he returned to Samaria. –
2 Chronicles 25:25 And Amasias, the son of Joas, king of Juda, lived fifteen years after the death of Joas, the son of Joachaz, king of Israel.
2 Chronicles 25:26 And the remaining words of Amasias, the first and the last, behold, are they not written in the book of the kings of Juda and Israel?
2 Chronicles 25:27 And at the time when Amasias departed from the Lord, they attacked him with an attack, and he fled from Jerusalem to Lachis; and they sent after him to Lachis and put him to death there.
2 Chronicles 25:28 And they took him up upon the horses and buried him with his fathers in the city of David.

## Chapter 26

2 Chronicles 26:1 And all the people of the land took Ozias, and he was sixteen years old, and they made him king in the stead of his father Amasias.
2 Chronicles 26:2 He built Ailath; he restored it to Juda after the king slept with his fathers.
2 Chronicles 26:3 Ozias became king as a son of sixteen years, and he reigned fifty-two years in Jerusalem, and his mother’s name was Chalia from Jerusalem.
2 Chronicles 26:4 And he did the straight before the Lord according to all that Amasias his father did.
2 Chronicles 26:5 And he was seeking the Lord in the days of Zacharias, who understood in the fear of the Lord; and in his days he sought the Lord, and the Lord prospered him.
2 Chronicles 26:6 And he went out and fought against the foreigners and tore down the walls of Geth and the walls of Jabne and the walls of Azotus, and built cities of Azotus and among the foreigners.
2 Chronicles 26:7 And the Lord strengthened him against the foreigners and against the Arabs dwelling upon the rock and against the Minaeans.
2 Chronicles 26:8 And the Minaeans gave gifts to Ozias, and his name reached as far as the entrance of Egypt, because he grew strong to a height.
2 Chronicles 26:9 And Ozias built towers in Jerusalem and at the corner gate and at the gate of the valley and upon the corners, and strengthened them.
2 Chronicles 26:10 And he built towers in the wilderness and hewed out many pits, because he had many cattle in Sephela and in the plain, and vine-growers in the hill country and in Carmel, because he was a lover of agriculture.
2 Chronicles 26:11 And Ozias had forces making war and going out to battle by number, and their number was through the hand of Jiel the scribe and Maasaias the judge, through the hand of Ananias the king’s deputy.
2 Chronicles 26:12 The whole number of the patriarchs, the mighty men for war, was two thousand six hundred,
2 Chronicles 26:13 and with them a warlike force, three hundred thousand and seven thousand five hundred; these were those making war with mighty strength to help the king against the adversaries.
2 Chronicles 26:14 And Ozias prepared for them, for all the force, shields and spears and helmets and breastplates and bows and slings for stones.
2 Chronicles 26:15 And in Jerusalem he made machines devised by a designer to be upon the towers and upon the corners, to shoot missiles and great stones; and their construction was heard of far away, because he was made marvelous in being helped, until he grew strong.
2 Chronicles 26:16 And when he grew strong, his heart was lifted up to destruction, and he did injustice against the Lord his God and entered the temple of the Lord to burn incense upon the altar of incense.
2 Chronicles 26:17 And Azarias the priest entered after him, and with him eighty priests of the Lord, mighty sons,
2 Chronicles 26:18 and they stood against Ozias the king and said to him, “It is not for you, Ozias, to burn incense to the Lord, but for the priests, the sons of Aaron, who have been sanctified to burn incense; go out of the sanctuary, because you departed from the Lord, and this will not be for you unto glory from the Lord God.”
2 Chronicles 26:19 And Ozias became angry, and in his hand was the censer to burn incense in the temple, and when he became angry with the priests, leprosy sprang up in his forehead before the priests in the house of the Lord, above the altar of incense.
2 Chronicles 26:20 And the first priest and the priests turned toward him, and behold, he was leprous in the forehead; and they hurried him from there, for he himself also hastened to go out, because the Lord reproved him.
2 Chronicles 26:21 And Ozias the king was leprous until the day of his death, and sat leprous in a house of affousoth, because he was cut off from the house of the Lord; and Joatham his son was over his kingdom, judging the people of the land.
2 Chronicles 26:22 And the remaining words of Ozias, the first and the last, are written by Jessias the prophet.
2 Chronicles 26:23 And Ozias slept with his fathers, and they buried him with his fathers in the field of the burial of the kings, because they said, “He is leprous”; and Joatham his son reigned in his stead.

## Chapter 27

2 Chronicles 27:1 Joatham was a son of twenty-five years when he became king, and he reigned sixteen years in Jerusalem, and his mother’s name was Jerousa daughter of Sadok.
2 Chronicles 27:2 And he did the straight before the Lord according to all that Ozias his father did, but he did not enter the temple of the Lord, and still the people were being corrupted.
2 Chronicles 27:3 He built the high gate of the house of the Lord and built much in the wall of Ophla;
2 Chronicles 27:4 and he built cities in the mountain of Juda, and in the forests both dwellings and towers.
2 Chronicles 27:5 He fought against the king of the sons of Ammon and prevailed against him; and the sons of Ammon gave him each year a hundred talents of silver and ten thousand kors of wheat and ten thousand of barley; these the king of Ammon brought him each year, in the first year and the second and the third.
2 Chronicles 27:6 And Joatham grew strong, because he prepared his ways before the Lord his God.
2 Chronicles 27:7 And the remaining words of Joatham and the war and his deeds, behold, are written in the book of the kings of Juda and Israel.
2 Chronicles 27:9 And Joatham slept with his fathers and was buried in the city of David, and Achaz his son reigned in his stead.

## Chapter 28

2 Chronicles 28:1 Achaz was a son of twenty years when he became king, and he reigned sixteen years in Jerusalem; and he did not do the straight before the Lord as David his father.
2 Chronicles 28:2 And he walked according to the ways of the kings of Israel; for he also made carved things for their idols
2 Chronicles 28:3 and sacrificed in Gaibenenom and led his children through fire according to the abominations of the nations which the Lord destroyed from before the sons of Israel,
2 Chronicles 28:4 and burned incense upon the high places and upon the roofs and underneath every leafy tree.
2 Chronicles 28:5 And the Lord his God delivered him through the hand of the king of Syria, and he struck among him and took a great captivity from them and brought to Damascus; for he also delivered him into the hands of the king of Israel, and he struck among him a great blow.
2 Chronicles 28:6 And Phakee, the son of Romelias, king of Israel, killed in Juda in one day a hundred and twenty thousand men mighty in strength, because they abandoned the Lord God of their fathers.
2 Chronicles 28:7 And Ezekri, the mighty man of Ephraim, killed Maasaias the king’s son and Esdrikam leader of his house and Elkana the king’s deputy.
2 Chronicles 28:8 And the sons of Israel took captive from their brothers three hundred thousand, women, sons and daughters, and plundered much spoil from them and brought the spoils to Samaria. –
2 Chronicles 28:9 And there was the prophet of the Lord, Oded his name, and he went out to meet the force of those coming to Samaria and said to them, “Behold, the wrath of the Lord God of your fathers is upon Juda, and he delivered them into your hands, and you killed among them in wrath; it has reached the heavens.
2 Chronicles 28:10 And now you say that you will acquire the sons of Juda and Jerusalem as male and female slaves; behold, am I not with you to testify to the Lord your God?
2 Chronicles 28:11 And now hear me and send back the captivity which you took captive from your brothers, because the furious wrath of the Lord is upon you.”
2 Chronicles 28:12 And rulers from the sons of Ephraim, Oudias the son of Joanos and Barachias the son of Mosolamoth and Ezekias the son of Sellem and Amasias the son of Chodli, rose against those coming from the war
2 Chronicles 28:13 and said to them, “You shall certainly not bring the captivity here to us, because you say that we should sin against the Lord, to add to our sins and to the ignorance, because our sin is great, and the furious wrath of the Lord is upon Israel.”
2 Chronicles 28:14 And the warriors left the captivity and the spoils before the rulers and all the assembly.
2 Chronicles 28:15 And men who were called by name rose and took hold of the captivity and clothed all the naked from the spoils, and dressed them and shod them and gave them to eat and to anoint themselves, and helped every weak one upon beasts of burden and brought them to Jericho, the city of palms, to their brothers, and returned to Samaria.
2 Chronicles 28:16 At that time Achaz sent to the king of Assour to help him,
2 Chronicles 28:17 also in this, because Idumeans attacked and struck in Juda and took a captivity captive,
2 Chronicles 28:18 and the foreigners attacked the cities of the plain and on the southwest of Juda, and took Baethsamys and Ailon and Gaderoth and Socho and its villages and Thamna and its villages and Gamzo and its villages, and dwelt there.
2 Chronicles 28:19 For the Lord humbled Juda through Achaz king of Juda, because he departed in revolt from the Lord.
2 Chronicles 28:20 And Thaglathphellasar king of Assour came against him and struck him.
2 Chronicles 28:21 And Achaz took the things in the house of the Lord and the things in the house of the king and of the rulers and gave to the king of Assour, and not for help to him.
2 Chronicles 28:22 But in his being afflicted he further departed from the Lord, and the king said,
2 Chronicles 28:23 “I will seek the gods of Damascus who strike me”; and he said, “Because they are the gods of the king of Syria, they will strengthen them; therefore I will sacrifice to them, and they will help me.” And they became a stumbling block to him and to all Israel.
2 Chronicles 28:24 And Achaz removed the vessels of the house of the Lord and cut them up and closed the doors of the house of the Lord and made himself altars in every corner in Jerusalem;
2 Chronicles 28:25 and in every city after city in Juda he made high places to burn incense to foreign gods, and they provoked the Lord, the God of their fathers, to anger.
2 Chronicles 28:26 And his remaining words and his deeds, the first and the last, behold, are written in the book of the kings of Juda and Israel.
2 Chronicles 28:27 And Achaz slept with his fathers and was buried in the city of David, because they did not bring him into the tombs of the kings of Israel; and Ezekias his son reigned in his stead.

## Chapter 29

2 Chronicles 29:1 And Ezekias became king when he was twenty-five years old, and he reigned twenty-nine years in Jerusalem, and his mother’s name was Abba daughter of Zacharias.
2 Chronicles 29:2 And he did the straight before the Lord according to all that David his father did.
2 Chronicles 29:3 And it came to pass, when he stood over his kingdom, in the first month he opened the doors of the house of the Lord and repaired them.
2 Chronicles 29:4 And he brought in the priests and the Levites and stationed them on the side toward the east,
2 Chronicles 29:5 and said to them, “Hear, Levites; now purify yourselves and purify the house of the Lord God of your fathers and cast the uncleanness out of the holy things;
2 Chronicles 29:6 for our fathers departed and did the evil before the Lord and abandoned him and turned their face away from the tent of the Lord and gave the neck,
2 Chronicles 29:7 and closed the doors of the temple and extinguished the lamps and did not burn incense and did not bring whole burnt offerings in the holy place to the God of Israel.
2 Chronicles 29:8 And the Lord was angry with wrath against Juda and against Jerusalem and gave them up to terror and disappearance and hissing, as you see with your eyes.
2 Chronicles 29:9 And behold, your fathers have been struck with a sword, and your sons and your daughters and your wives are in captivity in a land not their own, which is so even now.
2 Chronicles 29:10 On account of these things it is now upon the heart to make a covenant of the Lord God of Israel, and he will turn his furious wrath away from us.
2 Chronicles 29:11 And now do not leave off, because the Lord has chosen among you to stand before him to minister and to be those ministering to him and burning incense.” –
2 Chronicles 29:12 And the Levites rose: Maath the son of Amasi and Joel the son of Azarias from the sons of Kaath, and from the sons of Merari, Kis the son of Abdi and Azarias the son of Jallelel, and from the sons of Gedsoni, Joa the son of Zemmath and Jodan the son of Joacha,
2 Chronicles 29:13 and of the sons of Elisaphan, Sambri and Jiel, and of the sons of Asaph, Zacharias and Maththanias,
2 Chronicles 29:14 and of the sons of Aiman, Jiel and Semei, and of the sons of Idithon, Samaias and Oziel,
2 Chronicles 29:15 and they gathered their brothers and purified themselves according to the king’s command, through an ordinance of the Lord, to cleanse the house of the Lord.
2 Chronicles 29:16 And the priests entered within the house of the Lord to purify and cast out all the uncleanness found in the house of the Lord into the court of the house of the Lord, and the Levites received it to cast out into the torrent of Kedron outside.
2 Chronicles 29:17 And they began to purify on the first day, the new moon of the first month, and on the eighth day of the month they entered the temple of the Lord and purified the house of the Lord in eight days, and on the sixteenth day of the first month they finished.
2 Chronicles 29:18 And they entered within to Ezekias the king and said, “We purified all the things in the house of the Lord, the altar of the whole burnt offering and its vessels, and the table of the setting forth and its vessels;
2 Chronicles 29:19 and all the vessels which king Achaz defiled in his reign, in his revolt, we have prepared and purified; behold, they are before the altar of the Lord.” –
2 Chronicles 29:20 And Ezekias the king rose early and gathered the rulers of the city and went up to the house of the Lord,
2 Chronicles 29:21 and brought up seven calves, seven rams, seven lambs, seven male goats of the goats for sin, for the kingdom and for the holy things and for Israel, and told the sons of Aaron, the priests, to go up upon the altar of the Lord.
2 Chronicles 29:22 And they slaughtered the calves, and the priests received the blood and poured it upon the altar; and they slaughtered the rams and poured the blood upon the altar; and they slaughtered the lambs and poured the blood around the altar;
2 Chronicles 29:23 and they brought the male goats for sin before the king and the assembly, and laid their hands upon them,
2 Chronicles 29:24 and the priests slaughtered them and made atonement with their blood toward the altar, and made atonement for all Israel, because the whole burnt offering and the things for sin were for all Israel, the king said.
2 Chronicles 29:25 And he stationed the Levites in the house of the Lord with cymbals and nablas and lyres according to the command of David the king and Gad the seer for the king and Nathan the prophet, because through the command of the Lord was the ordinance in the hand of the prophets;
2 Chronicles 29:26 and the Levites stood with David’s instruments and the priests with the trumpets.
2 Chronicles 29:27 And Ezekias said to offer the whole burnt offering upon the altar; and when they began to offer the whole burnt offering, they began to sing to the Lord, and the trumpets with the instruments of David king of Israel.
2 Chronicles 29:28 And all the assembly bowed down, and the psalm-singers were singing, and the trumpets sounding, until the whole burnt offering was completed.
2 Chronicles 29:29 And when they finished offering, the king and all those present bent down and worshiped.
2 Chronicles 29:30 And Ezekias the king and the rulers told the Levites to hymn the Lord in the words of David and Asaph the prophet; and they hymned with gladness and fell down and worshiped.
2 Chronicles 29:31 And Ezekias answered and said, “Now you filled your hands for the Lord; bring near and bring sacrifices and offerings of praise into the house of the Lord”; and the assembly brought up sacrifices and offerings of praise into the house of the Lord, and everyone eager in heart, whole burnt offerings.
2 Chronicles 29:32 And the number of the whole burnt offering which the assembly brought up was seventy calves, a hundred rams, two hundred lambs; all these for a whole burnt offering to the Lord.
2 Chronicles 29:33 And the sanctified ones were six hundred calves, three thousand sheep.
2 Chronicles 29:34 But the priests were few and could not skin the whole burnt offering, and their brothers the Levites helped them until the work was completed and until the priests were purified, because the Levites purified themselves more eagerly than the priests.
2 Chronicles 29:35 And the whole burnt offering was great, with the fats of the completion of the salvation offering and the libations of the whole burnt offering; and the work in the house of the Lord was set right.
2 Chronicles 29:36 And Ezekias and all the people rejoiced because God had prepared for the people, because the matter came to pass suddenly.

## Chapter 30

2 Chronicles 30:1 And Ezekias sent to all Israel and Juda and wrote letters to Ephraim and Manasse to come to the house of the Lord in Jerusalem, to keep the Passover for the Lord God of Israel;
2 Chronicles 30:2 and the king and the rulers and all the assembly in Jerusalem took counsel to keep the Passover in the second month;
2 Chronicles 30:3 for they could not keep it at that time, because sufficient priests had not purified themselves, and the people had not gathered to Jerusalem.
2 Chronicles 30:4 And the matter was pleasing before the king and before the assembly.
2 Chronicles 30:5 And they established a word for a proclamation to go through all Israel from Bersabee as far as Dan, to come and keep the Passover for the Lord God of Israel in Jerusalem, because a multitude had not kept it according to the writing.
2 Chronicles 30:6 And the runners went with the letters from the king and the rulers to all Israel and Juda according to the king’s ordinance, saying, “Sons of Israel, turn to the God of Abraham and Isaac and Israel, and he will turn back those who escaped, who were left from the hand of the king of Assour;
2 Chronicles 30:7 and do not become as your fathers and your brothers, who departed from the Lord God of their fathers, and he delivered them to desolation, as you see.
2 Chronicles 30:8 And now do not harden your necks; give glory to the Lord God and enter his sanctuary which he sanctified forever, and serve the Lord your God, and he will turn furious wrath away from you.
2 Chronicles 30:9 For when you turn to the Lord, your brothers and your children will be in compassion before all who took them captive, and he will bring back to this land; because the Lord our God is merciful and compassionate and will not turn his face away from us if we turn to him.”
2 Chronicles 30:10 And the runners were passing from city to city in the mountain of Ephraim and Manasse and as far as Zaboulon, and they became as those laughing at them and mocking;
2 Chronicles 30:11 but men of Aser and from Manasse and from Zaboulon were ashamed and came to Jerusalem.
2 Chronicles 30:12 And in Juda the hand of the Lord came to give them one heart to come to act according to the ordinance of the king and the rulers, by a word of the Lord,
2 Chronicles 30:13 and many people gathered to Jerusalem to keep the feast of the unleavened things in the second month, an exceedingly great assembly.
2 Chronicles 30:14 And they rose and took down the altars in Jerusalem; and all the things upon which they burned incense to the false ones they tore down and cast into the torrent of Kedron.
2 Chronicles 30:15 And they slaughtered the Passover on the fourteenth of the second month; and the priests and the Levites were ashamed and purified themselves and brought whole burnt offerings into the house of the Lord.
2 Chronicles 30:16 And they stood at their station according to their rule, according to the command of Moses the man of God, and the priests received the blood from the hand of the Levites.
2 Chronicles 30:17 For a multitude of the assembly had not purified themselves, and the Levites were to slaughter the Passover for everyone unable to be purified for the Lord.
2 Chronicles 30:18 For most of the people from Ephraim and Manasse and Issachar and Zaboulon had not purified themselves, but ate the Passover contrary to the writing. And Ezekias prayed concerning them, saying, “Let the good Lord make atonement for
2 Chronicles 30:19 every heart directing itself to seek the Lord, the God of their fathers, and not according to the purification of the holy things.”
2 Chronicles 30:20 And the Lord listened to Ezekias and healed the people.
2 Chronicles 30:21 And the sons of Israel who were present in Jerusalem kept the feast of the unleavened things seven days with great gladness, and hymning the Lord day by day, and the priests and the Levites with instruments for the Lord.
2 Chronicles 30:22 And Ezekias spoke to all the heart of the Levites and of those understanding good understanding for the Lord; and they completed the feast of the unleavened things seven days, sacrificing sacrifices of salvation and giving thanks to the Lord God of their fathers.
2 Chronicles 30:23 And the assembly took counsel together to keep another seven days; and they kept seven days with gladness.
2 Chronicles 30:24 For Ezekias contributed for Juda, for the assembly, a thousand calves and seven thousand sheep, and the rulers contributed for the people a thousand calves and ten thousand sheep, and the holy things of the priests were in abundance.
2 Chronicles 30:25 And all the assembly rejoiced, the priests and the Levites and all the assembly of Juda and those present from Israel and the proselytes who came from the land of Israel and those dwelling in Juda.
2 Chronicles 30:26 And there was great gladness in Jerusalem; from the days of Solomon son of David king of Israel there had not been such a feast in Jerusalem.
2 Chronicles 30:27 And the priests, the Levites, rose and blessed the people; and their voice was heard, and their prayer came into his holy dwelling, into heaven.

## Chapter 31

2 Chronicles 31:1 And when all these things were completed, all Israel, those present in the cities of Juda, went out and broke the pillars and cut down the groves and tore down the high places and the altars from all Judea and Benjamin and from Ephraim and from Manasse to the end, and all Israel returned, each to his inheritance and to their cities.
2 Chronicles 31:2 And Ezekias arranged the divisions of the priests and the Levites and the divisions of each according to his own service, for the priests and the Levites for the whole burnt offering and for the sacrifice of salvation, and to praise and give thanks and minister in the gates, in the courts of the house of the Lord.
2 Chronicles 31:3 And the king’s portion from his possessions was for the whole burnt offerings, the morning and the evening, and whole burnt offerings for sabbaths and for the new moons and for the feasts written in the law of the Lord.
2 Chronicles 31:4 And he told the people, those dwelling in Jerusalem, to give the portion of the priests and the Levites, so that they might be strong in the service of the house of the Lord.
2 Chronicles 31:5 And when he commanded the word, the sons of Israel increased the firstfruits of grain and wine and oil and honey and every produce of the field, and all the tithes in abundance were brought by
2 Chronicles 31:6 the sons of Israel and Juda. And those dwelling in the cities of Juda also brought tithes of calves and sheep and tithes of goats and sanctified them to the Lord their God and brought them in and placed heaps upon heaps;
2 Chronicles 31:7 in the third month the heaps began to be founded, and in the seventh month they were completed.
2 Chronicles 31:8 And Ezekias and the rulers came and saw the heaps and blessed the Lord and his people Israel.
2 Chronicles 31:9 And Ezekias inquired of the priests and the Levites concerning the heaps,
2 Chronicles 31:10 and Azarias the priest, the ruler for the house of Sadok, spoke to him and said, “Since the firstfruits began to be brought into the house of the Lord, we ate and drank and left over; because the Lord blessed his people, and we still left over this abundance.”
2 Chronicles 31:11 And Ezekias said to prepare chambers for the house of the Lord, and they prepared them.
2 Chronicles 31:12 And they brought in there the firstfruits and the tithes in faithfulness, and over them was Chonenias the Levite as overseer, and Semei his brother as deputy,
2 Chronicles 31:13 and Jiel and Ozazias and Naeth and Asael and Jerimoth and Jozabath and Eliel and Samachia and Maath and Banaias and his sons were appointed through Chonenias and Semei his brother, as king Ezekias and Azarias the leader of the house of the Lord commanded.
2 Chronicles 31:14 And Kore, the son of Jemna, the Levite, the gatekeeper toward the east, was over the gifts, to give the firstfruits to the Lord and the holy things of the holy things
2 Chronicles 31:15 through the hand of Odom and Benjamin and Jesus and Semei and Amarias and Sechonias, through the hand of the priests in faithfulness, to give to their brothers according to the divisions, to the great and the small,
2 Chronicles 31:16 besides the offspring of the males from three years old and upward, to everyone entering the house of the Lord for the account of days, day by day, for service in the divisions of their arrangement.
2 Chronicles 31:17 This was the enrollment of the priests according to the houses of families, and the Levites in their divisions from twenty years old and upward, in arrangement,
2 Chronicles 31:18 in enrollments, in all the offspring of their sons and their daughters, for all the multitude, because in faithfulness they purified the holy thing
2 Chronicles 31:19 for the sons of Aaron who served as priests, and those from their cities, in every city after city, men who were named by name, to give a portion to every male among the priests and to everyone counted among the Levites.
2 Chronicles 31:20 And Ezekias did thus in all Juda and did the good and the straight before the Lord his God.
2 Chronicles 31:21 And in every work which he began in labor in the house of the Lord, and in the law and in the ordinances, he sought his God with all his soul and acted and was prospered.

## Chapter 32

2 Chronicles 32:1 And after these words and this truth, Sennacherim king of the Assyrians came and came against Juda and encamped against the walled cities and said to seize them.
2 Chronicles 32:2 And Ezekias saw that Sennacherim had come, and his face was to fight against Jerusalem,
2 Chronicles 32:3 and took counsel with his elders and the mighty men to stop up the waters of the springs which were outside the city, and they helped strengthen him.
2 Chronicles 32:4 And he gathered many people and stopped up the waters of the springs and the river that divides through the city, saying, “Let not the king of Assour come and find much water and grow strong.”
2 Chronicles 32:5 And Ezekias strengthened himself and built all the wall that had been demolished, and towers, and outside another outer wall, and strengthened the supporting wall of the city of David and prepared many arms.
2 Chronicles 32:6 And he placed rulers of war over the people, and they gathered to him in the broad place of the gate of the valley, and he spoke to their heart, saying,
2 Chronicles 32:7 “Be strong and act as men; do not be terrified before the king of Assour and before all the nation with him, because more are with us than with him;
2 Chronicles 32:8 with him are arms of flesh, but with us is the Lord our God, to save and to fight our war.” And the people took courage at the words of Ezekias king of Juda. –
2 Chronicles 32:9 And after these things Sennacherim king of the Assyrians sent his servants to Jerusalem, and he was at Lachis and all the army with him, and he sent to Ezekias king of Juda and to all Juda in Jerusalem, saying,
2 Chronicles 32:10 “Thus says Sennacherim the king of the Assyrians: In what have you trusted and sit in the siege in Jerusalem?
2 Chronicles 32:11 Does not Ezekias deceive you to deliver you to death and to famine and to thirst, saying, ‘The Lord our God will save us from the hand of the king of Assour’?
2 Chronicles 32:12 Is this not Ezekias who removed his altars and his high places and spoke to Juda and those dwelling in Jerusalem, saying, ‘Before this altar you shall worship, and upon it you shall burn incense.’
2 Chronicles 32:13 Will you not know what I and my fathers did to all the peoples of the lands? Were the gods of the nations of all the earth at all able to save their people from my hand?
2 Chronicles 32:14 Who among all the gods of these nations which my fathers destroyed? Were they able to save their people from my hand, that your God will be able to save you from my hand?
2 Chronicles 32:15 Now let not Ezekias deceive you nor make you trust according to these things, and do not believe him; because the god of any nation and kingdom can certainly not save his people from my hand and from the hand of my fathers, because your God will certainly not save you from my hand.”
2 Chronicles 32:16 And his servants spoke further against the Lord God and against Ezekias his servant.
2 Chronicles 32:17 And he wrote a book to reproach the Lord God of Israel and spoke concerning him, saying, “As the gods of the nations of the earth did not rescue their peoples from my hand, so the God of Ezekias will certainly not rescue his people from my hand.”
2 Chronicles 32:18 And he cried with a great voice in the Judean tongue to the people of Jerusalem upon the wall, to frighten them and pull them down, so that they might seize the city.
2 Chronicles 32:19 And he spoke against the God of Jerusalem as also against the gods of the peoples of the earth, works of the hands of men. –
2 Chronicles 32:20 And Ezekias the king and Esaias son of Amos the prophet prayed concerning these things and cried to heaven.
2 Chronicles 32:21 And the Lord sent an angel and wiped out every mighty warrior and ruler and general in the camp of the king of Assour, and he returned with shame of face to his land. And he came into the house of his god, and some of those who came out of his belly struck him down with a sword.
2 Chronicles 32:22 And the Lord saved Ezekias and those dwelling in Jerusalem from the hand of Sennacherim king of Assour and from the hand of all, and gave them rest round about.
2 Chronicles 32:23 And many brought gifts to the Lord in Jerusalem and presents to Ezekias king of Juda, and he was exalted in the eyes of all the nations after these things.
2 Chronicles 32:24 In those days Ezekias became ill unto death; and he prayed to the Lord, and he listened to him and gave him a sign.
2 Chronicles 32:25 And Ezekias did not repay according to the recompense which he gave him, but his heart was lifted up; and wrath came upon him and upon Juda and Jerusalem.
2 Chronicles 32:26 And Ezekias was humbled from the height of his heart, and those dwelling in Jerusalem, and the wrath of the Lord did not come upon them in the days of Ezekias.
2 Chronicles 32:27 And Ezekias had wealth and exceedingly great glory, and he made himself treasures of silver and gold and precious stone and for the spices, and armories, and for desirable vessels,
2 Chronicles 32:28 and cities for the produce of grain and oil and wine, and mangers for every beast, and folds for the flocks,
2 Chronicles 32:29 and cities which he built for himself, and possessions of sheep and cattle in abundance, because the Lord gave him exceedingly great possessions.
2 Chronicles 32:30 Ezekias himself stopped up the upper outlet of the water of Gion and directed them down toward the southwest of the city of David; and Ezekias was prospered in all his works.
2 Chronicles 32:31 And thus with the ambassadors of the rulers from Babylon who were sent to him to inquire from him about the wonder which came to pass upon the earth, the Lord also abandoned him to test him, to know the things in his heart.
2 Chronicles 32:32 And the remaining things of the words of Ezekias and his mercy, behold, are written in the prophecy of Esaias son of Amos the prophet and in the book of the kings of Juda and Israel.
2 Chronicles 32:33 And Ezekias slept with his fathers, and they buried him in the ascent of the tombs of the sons of David, and all Juda and those dwelling in Jerusalem gave him glory and honor at his death; and Manasses his son reigned in his stead.

## Chapter 33

2 Chronicles 33:1 Manasses was twelve years old when he became king, and he reigned fifty-five years in Jerusalem.
2 Chronicles 33:2 And he did the evil before the Lord according to all the abominations of the nations whom the Lord destroyed from before the sons of Israel.
2 Chronicles 33:3 And he returned and built the high places which Ezekias his father tore down, and set up pillars for the Baalim and made groves and worshiped all the army of heaven and served them.
2 Chronicles 33:4 And he built altars in the house of the Lord, of which the Lord said, “In Jerusalem my name shall be forever.”
2 Chronicles 33:5 And he built altars for all the army of heaven in the two courts of the house of the Lord.
2 Chronicles 33:6 And he himself led his children through fire in Gai – banai – ennom, and practiced divination from sounds and from birds and sorcery, and made ventriloquists and enchanters; he multiplied doing the evil before the Lord to provoke him to anger.
2 Chronicles 33:7 And he placed the carved thing and the cast thing, an image which he made, in the house of God, of which God said to David and to Solomon his son, “In this house and Jerusalem, which I chose from all the tribes of Israel, I shall put my name forever;
2 Chronicles 33:8 and I shall no longer shake the foot of Israel from the land which I gave to their fathers, provided they keep doing all that I commanded them, according to all the law and the ordinances and the judgments by the hand of Moses.”
2 Chronicles 33:9 And Manasses led Juda and those dwelling in Jerusalem astray to do the evil beyond all the nations which the Lord removed from before the sons of Israel.
2 Chronicles 33:10 And the Lord spoke against Manasses and against his people, and they did not listen.
2 Chronicles 33:11 And the Lord brought against them the rulers of the force of the king of Assour, and they caught Manasses in bonds and bound him in fetters and brought him to Babylon.
2 Chronicles 33:12 And when he was afflicted, he sought the face of the Lord his God and was exceedingly humbled before the God of his fathers;
2 Chronicles 33:13 and he prayed to him, and he listened to him; and he listened to his cry and returned him to Jerusalem over his kingdom; and Manasses knew that the Lord himself is God. –
2 Chronicles 33:14 And after these things he built a wall outside the city of David, on the southwest, along Gion in the torrent, and of those going out the gate round about, and into Ophla, and raised it exceedingly. And he appointed rulers of the force in all the walled cities in Juda.
2 Chronicles 33:15 And he removed the foreign gods and the carved thing from the house of the Lord and all the altars which he built on the mountain of the house of the Lord and in Jerusalem and outside the city.
2 Chronicles 33:16 And he set right the altar of the Lord and sacrificed upon it a sacrifice of salvation and praise, and told Juda to serve the Lord God of Israel;
2 Chronicles 33:17 except the people were still upon the high places, except the Lord was their God.
2 Chronicles 33:18 And the remaining things of the words of Manasses and his prayer to God and the words of the seers speaking to him in the name of the Lord God of Israel, behold, in the words of
2 Chronicles 33:19 his prayer, and how he listened to him, and all his sins and his revolts and the places upon which he built the high places and set up there groves and carved things before turning, behold, are written in the words of the seers.
2 Chronicles 33:20 And Manasses slept with his fathers, and they buried him in the garden of his house; and Amon his son reigned in his stead.
2 Chronicles 33:21 Amon was twenty-two years old when he became king, and he reigned two years in Jerusalem.
2 Chronicles 33:22 And he did the evil before the Lord, as Manasses his father did, and Amon sacrificed to all the idols which Manasses his father made and served them.
2 Chronicles 33:23 And he was not humbled before the Lord, as Manasses his father was humbled, because his son Amon multiplied transgression.
2 Chronicles 33:24 And his servants attacked him and struck him in his house.
2 Chronicles 33:25 And the people of the land struck those who attacked king Amon, and the people of the land made Josias his son king in his stead.

## Chapter 34

2 Chronicles 34:1 Josias was eight years old when he became king, and he reigned thirty-one years in Jerusalem.
2 Chronicles 34:2 And he did what was upright before the Lord and walked in the ways of David his father and did not turn aside to the right and to the left.
2 Chronicles 34:3 And in the eighth year of his reign—and he was still a child—he began to seek the Lord, the God of David his father. And in the twelfth year of his reign he began to cleanse Judah and Jerusalem of the high places and the groves and the cast images,
2 Chronicles 34:4 and he pulled down before his face the altars of the Baalim and the high places upon them, and he cut down the groves, and he shattered the carved images and the cast images and ground them fine and threw them upon the surface of the tombs of those who sacrificed to them,
2 Chronicles 34:5 and he burned bones of priests upon the altars and cleansed Judah and Jerusalem.
2 Chronicles 34:6 And in the cities of Ephraim and Manasseh and Symeon and Nephthali and in their places round about,
2 Chronicles 34:7 and he pulled down the groves and the altars and chopped the idols fine, and he cut down all the high places from all the land of Israel and returned to Jerusalem.
2 Chronicles 34:8 And in the eighteenth year of his reign, to cleanse the land and the house, he sent Saphan son of Eselias and Maasias ruler of the city and Joach son of Joachaz his recorder to strengthen the house of the Lord his God.
2 Chronicles 34:9 And they came to Chelkias the high priest and gave the silver brought into the house of God, which the Levites guarding the gate had gathered from the hand of Manasseh and Ephraim and the rulers and from all the remnant in Israel and the sons of Judah and Benjamin and those dwelling in Jerusalem,
2 Chronicles 34:10 and those appointed in the house of the Lord gave it into the hand of those doing the works, and they gave it to those doing the works, who were working in the house of the Lord, to repair and strengthen the house;
2 Chronicles 34:11 and they gave it to the carpenters and the builders to buy four-sided stones and timber for beams to roof the houses which the kings of Judah had destroyed;
2 Chronicles 34:12 and the men were in faithfulness over the works, and over them were overseers, Jeth and Abdias, the Levites from the sons of Merari, and Zacharias and Mosollam from the sons of Kaath, to oversee, and every Levite, everyone skilled in instruments of songs,
2 Chronicles 34:13 was also over the burden-bearers and over all those doing the works, work by work; and from the Levites were scribes and judges and gatekeepers.
2 Chronicles 34:14 And as they brought out the silver brought into the house of the Lord, Chelkias the priest found a book of the law of the Lord through the hand of Moses.
2 Chronicles 34:15 And Chelkias answered and said to Saphan the scribe, I found a book of the law in the house of the Lord; and Chelkias gave the book to Saphan.
2 Chronicles 34:16 And Saphan brought the book to the king and further returned a report to the king: All the silver given is in the hand of your servants who are doing the work,
2 Chronicles 34:17 and they melted the silver found in the house of the Lord and gave it into the hand of the overseers and into the hand of those doing work.
2 Chronicles 34:18 And Saphan the scribe reported to the king, saying, Chelkias the priest gave me a book; and Saphan read it before the king.
2 Chronicles 34:19 And it happened, when the king heard the words of the law, that he tore his garments.
2 Chronicles 34:20 And the king commanded Chelkias and Achikam son of Saphan and Abdon son of Michaias and Saphan the scribe and Asaias the king's servant, saying,
2 Chronicles 34:21 Go, seek the Lord concerning me and concerning all that is left in Israel and Judah, concerning the words of the book that was found; for great is the wrath of the Lord kindled among us, because our fathers did not heed the words of the Lord, to do according to all that is written in this book.
2 Chronicles 34:22 And Chelkias and those to whom the king spoke went to Olda the prophetess, wife of Sellem son of Thakouath son of Chelles, herself guarding the robes—and she dwelt in Jerusalem in masana—and they spoke to her according to these things.
2 Chronicles 34:23 And she said to them, Thus said the Lord, the God of Israel: Say to the man who sent you to me,
2 Chronicles 34:24 Thus says the Lord: Behold, I am bringing evils upon this place, all the words written in the book read before the king of Judah,
2 Chronicles 34:25 because they forsook me and burned incense to foreign gods, to provoke me to anger with all the works of their hands; and my wrath was kindled in this place and will not be quenched.
2 Chronicles 34:26 And to the king of Judah who sent you to seek the Lord, thus you shall say to him: Thus says the Lord, the God of Israel: The words which you heard,
2 Chronicles 34:27 and your heart was moved to reverence and you humbled yourself before my face when you heard my words against this place and against those dwelling in it, and you humbled yourself before me and tore your garments and wept before me, I also heard, says the Lord;
2 Chronicles 34:28 behold, I am adding you to your fathers, and you shall be added to your tombs in peace, and your eyes shall not look upon all the evils which I am bringing upon this place and upon those dwelling in it. And they returned a report to the king.—
2 Chronicles 34:29 And the king sent and gathered the elders of Judah and Jerusalem.
2 Chronicles 34:30 And the king went up to the house of the Lord, and all Judah and those dwelling in Jerusalem and the priests and the Levites and all the people, from great to small; and he read in their ears all the words of the book of the covenant found in the house of the Lord.
2 Chronicles 34:31 And the king stood upon the pillar and made a covenant before the Lord, to walk before the Lord, to keep his commandments and his testimonies and his ordinances with all the heart and with all the soul, the words of the covenant written in this book.
2 Chronicles 34:32 And he made all those found in Jerusalem and Benjamin stand, and those dwelling in Jerusalem made a covenant in the house of the Lord, the God of their fathers.
2 Chronicles 34:33 And Josias removed all the abominations from all the land which belonged to the sons of Israel, and he made all those found in Jerusalem and in Israel serve the Lord their God all his days; he did not turn aside from following the Lord, the God of his fathers.

## Chapter 35

2 Chronicles 35:1 And Josias kept the Passover to the Lord his God, and they sacrificed the Passover on the fourteenth of the first month.
2 Chronicles 35:2 And he stationed the priests at their watches and strengthened them for the works of the house of the Lord.
2 Chronicles 35:3 And he told the Levites who were able in all Israel to sanctify themselves to the Lord, and they placed the holy ark in the house which Solomon son of David, the king of Israel, built. And the king said, You have nothing to carry upon shoulders; now therefore minister to the Lord your God and to his people Israel,
2 Chronicles 35:4 and prepare yourselves according to the houses of your families and according to your daily divisions, according to the writing of David king of Israel and through the hand of Solomon his son,
2 Chronicles 35:5 and stand in the house according to the divisions of the houses of your families for your brothers, the sons of the people, and a portion of a family house for the Levites,
2 Chronicles 35:6 and sacrifice the Passover and prepare the holy things for your brothers, to do according to the word of the Lord through the hand of Moses.
2 Chronicles 35:7 And Josias contributed for the sons of the people sheep and lambs and kids from the offspring of the goats, all for the Passover for all those found, numbering thirty thousand, and three thousand calves; these were from the king's possessions.
2 Chronicles 35:8 And his rulers contributed to the people and to the priests and Levites; Chelkias and Zacharias and Jiel, the rulers of the house of God, gave to the priests, and they gave for the Passover two thousand six hundred sheep and lambs and kids, and three hundred calves.
2 Chronicles 35:9 And Chonenias and Banaias and Samaias and Nathanael his brother and Asabias and Jiel and Jozabad, rulers of the Levites, contributed to the Levites for the Passover five thousand sheep and five hundred calves.
2 Chronicles 35:10 And the ministry was set in order, and the priests stood at their station and the Levites at their divisions according to the king's commandment.
2 Chronicles 35:11 And they sacrificed the Passover, and the priests poured the blood from their hand, and the Levites flayed.
2 Chronicles 35:12 And they prepared the whole burnt offering to hand over to them according to the division by family houses, to the sons of the people, to bring to the Lord, as it is written in the book of Moses, and thus for the morning.
2 Chronicles 35:13 And they roasted the Passover in fire according to the ordinance, and they boiled the holy things in the bronze vessels and in the cauldrons; and it prospered, and they ran to all the sons of the people.
2 Chronicles 35:14 And after preparing for them and for the priests, because the priests were offering up the fat and the whole burnt offerings until night, the Levites also prepared for themselves and for their brothers, the sons of Aaron.
2 Chronicles 35:15 And the psalm-singers, the sons of Asaph, were at their station according to the commandments of David and Asaph and Aiman and Idithon, the king's prophets, and the rulers and the gatekeepers of gate after gate; they had no need to move from the ministry of holy things, because their brothers the Levites prepared for them.
2 Chronicles 35:16 And all the ministry of the Lord was set in order and prepared on that day, to keep the Passover and bring the whole burnt offerings upon the altar of the Lord according to the commandment of King Josias.
2 Chronicles 35:17 And the sons of Israel who were found kept the Passover at that time and the feast of unleavened bread seven days.
2 Chronicles 35:18 And there had not been a Passover like it in Israel since the days of Samuel the prophet, and all the kings of Israel had not kept one like the Passover which Josias and the priests and the Levites and all Judah and Israel who were found and those dwelling in Jerusalem kept to the Lord
2 Chronicles 35:19 in the eighteenth year of the reign of Josias.
2 Chronicles 35:19 a And the ventriloquists and the knowing ones and the tharaphin and the idols and the karasim which were in the land of Judah and in Jerusalem, King Josias burned, to establish the words of the law written in the book which Chelkias the priest found in the house of the Lord.
2 Chronicles 35:20 There was none like him before him, who turned to the Lord with all his heart and with all his soul and with all his strength according to all the law of Moses, and after him none like him arose;
2 Chronicles 35:21 yet the Lord did not turn from the anger of his great wrath, with which the Lord was wrathfully angered in Judah over all the provocations with which Manasses provoked him.
2 Chronicles 35:22 And the Lord said, Indeed I shall also remove Judah from before my face, as I removed Israel, and I rejected the city which I chose, Jerusalem, and the house of which I said, My name shall be there.
2 Chronicles 35:20 And Pharaoh Nechao king of Egypt went up against the king of the Assyrians at the river Euphrates, and King Josias went to meet him.
2 Chronicles 35:21 And he sent messengers to him, saying, What is there between me and you, king of Judah? I have not come against you today to make war, and God said that I should hasten; beware of the God who is with me, lest he destroy you.
2 Chronicles 35:22 And Josias did not turn his face away from him, but strengthened himself to fight him, and did not heed the words of Nechao through the mouth of God, and came to fight in the plain of Magedon.
2 Chronicles 35:23 And the archers shot at King Josias; and the king said to his servants, Take me out, for I am in great pain.
2 Chronicles 35:24 And his servants took him out of the chariot and brought him up onto the second chariot which he had, and brought him to Jerusalem; and he died and was buried with his fathers. And all Judah and Jerusalem mourned over Josias,
2 Chronicles 35:25 and Jeremias lamented over Josias, and all the male rulers and the female rulers spoke a lament over Josias until today; and they made it an ordinance for Israel, and behold, it is written among the laments.
2 Chronicles 35:26 And the words of Josias and his hope were written in the law of the Lord;
2 Chronicles 35:27 and his first and last words, behold, are written in the book of the kings of Israel and Judah.

## Chapter 36

2 Chronicles 36:1 And the people of the land took Joachaz son of Josias and anointed him and appointed him king in place of his father in Jerusalem.
2 Chronicles 36:2 Joachaz was a son of twenty-three years when he became king, and he reigned three months in Jerusalem,
2 Chronicles 36:2 a and his mother's name was Amital daughter of Jeremias from Lobena.
2 Chronicles 36:3 And he did what was evil before the Lord, according to all that his fathers did.
2 Chronicles 36:4 And Pharaoh Nechao bound him in Deblatha in the land of Emath, so that he would not reign in Jerusalem,
2 Chronicles 36:3 and the king removed him to Egypt, and imposed tribute upon the land, a hundred talents of silver and a talent of gold.
2 Chronicles 36:4 And Pharaoh Nechao appointed Eliakim son of Josias king of Judah in place of Josias his father, and changed his name to Joakim; and Pharaoh Nechao took Joachaz his brother and brought him into Egypt, and he died there.
2 Chronicles 36:4 a And they gave the silver and the gold to Pharaoh; then the land began to be taxed, to give the silver at Pharaoh's word, and each according to ability demanded the silver and the gold from the people of the land to give to Pharaoh Nechao.
2 Chronicles 36:5 Joakim was twenty-five years old when he became king, and he reigned eleven years in Jerusalem, and his mother's name was Zechora daughter of Nerias from Rama. And he did what was evil before the Lord, according to all that his fathers did.
2 Chronicles 36:5 a In his days Nabouchodonosor king of Babylon came into the land, and he was serving him three years and withdrew from him.
2 Chronicles 36:6 And the Lord sent against them the Chaldeans and raiding bands of Syrians and raiding bands of Moabites and sons of Ammon and of Samaria, and they withdrew after this word according to the word of the Lord by the hand of his servants the prophets.
2 Chronicles 36:7 Yet the wrath of the Lord was upon Judah, to remove him from before his face because of the sins of Manasseh in all that he did,
2 Chronicles 36:8 and in the innocent blood which Joakim poured out, and he filled Jerusalem with innocent blood, and the Lord was unwilling to destroy them.
2 Chronicles 36:6 And Nabouchodonosor king of Babylon went up against him and bound him in bronze fetters and led him away to Babylon.
2 Chronicles 36:7 And he carried away part of the vessels of the house of the Lord to Babylon and placed them in his temple in Babylon.
2 Chronicles 36:8 And the rest of the words of Joakim and all that he did, behold, are these not written in the book of the words of the days for the kings of Judah? And Joakim slept with his fathers and was buried in Ganoza with his fathers, and Jechonias his son reigned in his place.
2 Chronicles 36:9 Jechonias was a son of eighteen years when he became king, and he reigned three months and ten days in Jerusalem. And he did what was evil before the Lord.
2 Chronicles 36:10 And at the return of the year King Nabouchodonosor sent and brought him into Babylon with the desirable vessels of the house of the Lord, and made Sedekias, his father's brother, king over Judah and Jerusalem.
2 Chronicles 36:11 Sedekias was twenty-one years old when he became king, and he reigned eleven years in Jerusalem.
2 Chronicles 36:12 And he did what was evil before the Lord his God; he did not show reverence before Jeremias the prophet and from the mouth of the Lord,
2 Chronicles 36:13 in rejecting the obligations toward King Nabouchodonosor, which he had made him swear by God; and he hardened his neck and strengthened his heart so as not to turn to the Lord, the God of Israel.
2 Chronicles 36:14 And all the eminent men of Judah and the priests and the people of the land multiplied rejection in acts of rejection involving the abominations of nations and defiled the house of the Lord in Jerusalem.
2 Chronicles 36:15 And the Lord, the God of their fathers, sent by the hand of prophets, rising early and sending his messengers, because he was sparing his people and his sanctuary;
2 Chronicles 36:16 and they were sneering at his messengers and despising his words and mocking his prophets, until the wrath of the Lord rose among his people, until there was no remedy.
2 Chronicles 36:17 And he brought against them the king of the Chaldeans, and he killed their young men with the sword in the house of his sanctuary and did not spare Sedekias, and they did not pity their virgins and led their elders away; he handed everything over into their hands.
2 Chronicles 36:18 And all the vessels of the house of God, the great and the small, and the treasures and all the treasures of the king and the magnates, everything he brought into Babylon.
2 Chronicles 36:19 And he burned the house of the Lord and pulled down the wall of Jerusalem and burned its fortresses with fire and every beautiful vessel to destruction.
2 Chronicles 36:20 And he deported the remaining ones to Babylon, and they became slaves to him and to his sons until the kingdom of the Medes,
2 Chronicles 36:21 so that the word of the Lord through the mouth of Jeremias would be fulfilled, until the land received its sabbaths to keep sabbath; all the days of its desolation it kept sabbath, to complete seventy years.
2 Chronicles 36:22 In the first year of Cyrus king of the Persians, after the word of the Lord through the mouth of Jeremias was fulfilled, the Lord stirred up the spirit of Cyrus king of the Persians, and he ordered a proclamation throughout all his kingdom in writing, saying,
2 Chronicles 36:23 Thus says Cyrus king of the Persians: The Lord, the God of heaven, gave me all the kingdoms of the earth, and he commanded me to build him a house in Jerusalem in Judea. Who among you is of all his people? His God shall be with him, and let him go up.

# 1 Esdras

The Apostolic Bible. Public domain. https://apostolic-bible.ysys9.chatgpt.site/license.html


## Chapter 1

1 Esdras 1:1 And Josias held the Passover in Jerusalem to his Lord and sacrificed the Passover on the fourteenth day of the first month,
1 Esdras 1:2 having stationed the priests according to daily divisions, robed in the temple of the Lord.
1 Esdras 1:3 And he told the Levites, the temple servants of Israel, to sanctify themselves to the Lord at the placing of the holy ark of the Lord in the house which King Solomon, the son of David, built: You shall not have to carry it upon shoulders;
1 Esdras 1:4 and now worship the Lord your God and serve his nation Israel, and prepare according to your families and your tribes, according to the writing of David king of Israel and according to the greatness of Solomon his son,
1 Esdras 1:5 and standing in the temple according to your ancestral division, you Levites who are before your brothers, the sons of Israel, in order,
1 Esdras 1:6 sacrifice the Passover and prepare the sacrifices for your brothers, and keep the Passover according to the ordinance of the Lord given to Moses.
1 Esdras 1:7 And Josias gave to the people who were found thirty thousand lambs and kids, three thousand calves; these were given from the royal possessions according to promise to the people and to the priests and Levites.
1 Esdras 1:8 And Chelkias and Zacharias and Hesyelos, the superintendents of the temple, gave to the priests for Passover two thousand six hundred sheep, three hundred calves.
1 Esdras 1:9 And Jechonias and Samaias and Nathanael the brother and Asabias and Ochielos and Joram, commanders of thousands, gave to the Levites for Passover five thousand sheep, seven hundred calves.
1 Esdras 1:10 And these were the things that happened: the priests and the Levites stood in good order,
1 Esdras 1:11 having the unleavened bread according to the tribes
1 Esdras 1:12 and according to the divisions of the fathers, before the people, to offer to the Lord according to the things written in the book of Moses, and thus the morning offering.
1 Esdras 1:13 And they roasted the Passover with fire as is fitting, and boiled the sacrifices in the bronze vessels and cauldrons with a sweet smell and carried them to all those from the people.
1 Esdras 1:14 And after these things they prepared both for themselves and for the priests, their brothers, the sons of Aaron; for the priests offered up the fat until a late hour, and the Levites prepared for themselves and for the priests, their brothers, the sons of Aaron.
1 Esdras 1:15 And the temple singers, the sons of Asaph, were at their station according to the things ordered by David and Asaph and Zacharias and Eddinous, those from the king, and the doorkeepers at each gateway; each cannot leave his own daily service, for their brothers the Levites prepared for them.
1 Esdras 1:16 And the matters of the sacrifice of the Lord were completed on that day, the holding of the Passover and the offering of the sacrifices upon the altar of the Lord, according to the command of King Josias.
1 Esdras 1:17 And the sons of Israel who were found at this time held the Passover and the feast of unleavened bread seven days.
1 Esdras 1:18 And such a Passover had not been held in Israel since the times of Samuel the prophet,
1 Esdras 1:19 and all the kings of Israel had not held such a Passover as Josias and the priests and the Levites and the Judeans and all Israel who were found in their dwelling in Jerusalem held;
1 Esdras 1:20 in the eighteenth year of Josias's reign this Passover was held.—
1 Esdras 1:21 And the works of Josias were set upright before his Lord with a heart full of piety.
1 Esdras 1:22 And the matters concerning him are recorded in the earlier times, concerning those who sinned and acted impiously against the Lord beyond every nation and kingdom, and the things which grieved him perceptibly; and the words of the Lord rose against Israel.
1 Esdras 1:23 And after all this action of Josias it happened that Pharaoh king of Egypt came and stirred up war in Charkamys on the Euphrates, and Josias went out to meet him.
1 Esdras 1:24 And the king of Egypt sent to him, saying, What is there between me and you, king of Judea?
1 Esdras 1:25 I have not been sent against you by the Lord God, for my war is on the Euphrates. And now the Lord is with me, and the Lord is with me, urging haste; withdraw and do not oppose the Lord.
1 Esdras 1:26 And Josias did not turn himself back upon his chariot, but attempts to fight him, paying no attention to the words of Jeremias the prophet from the mouth of the Lord;
1 Esdras 1:27 but he engaged in war against him in the plain of Mageddaous, and the rulers came down to King Josias.
1 Esdras 1:28 And the king said to his servants, Remove me from the battle, for I have become very weak. And immediately his servants removed him from the battle line,
1 Esdras 1:29 and he went up onto his second chariot; and, brought back to Jerusalem, he departed this life and was buried in the ancestral tomb.
1 Esdras 1:30 And in all Judea they mourned Josias, and Jeremias the prophet lamented for Josias, and those presiding, together with women, lamented him until this day, and it was decreed that this should always be done among all the race of Israel.
1 Esdras 1:31 And these things are recorded in the book of the accounts concerning the kings of Judea; and each individual deed of the action of Josias and of his glory and of his understanding in the law of the Lord, both the things done by him earlier and the present things, is recounted in the book of the kings of Israel and Judah.
1 Esdras 1:32 And those from the nation took Jechonias son of Josias and appointed him king in place of Josias his father, being twenty-three years old.
1 Esdras 1:33 And he reigned in Judah and Jerusalem three months. And the king of Egypt restored him to reign in Jerusalem,
1 Esdras 1:34 and fined the nation a hundred talents of silver and one talent of gold.
1 Esdras 1:35 And the king of Egypt appointed his brother Joakim king, king of Judea and Jerusalem.
1 Esdras 1:36 And Joakim bound the magnates, and seizing Zarios his brother, he brought him up out of Egypt.
1 Esdras 1:37 And Joakim was twenty-five years old when he became king of Judea and Jerusalem, and he did what was evil before the Lord.
1 Esdras 1:38 And Nabouchodonosor king of Babylon went up against him and, binding him in a bronze bond, led him away to Babylon.
1 Esdras 1:39 And Nabouchodonosor took some of the holy vessels of the Lord and carried them away and deposited them in his temple in Babylon.
1 Esdras 1:40 And the things recounted concerning him and his uncleanness and impiety are recorded in the book of the times of the kings.
1 Esdras 1:41 And Joakim his son reigned in his place; for when he was appointed, he was eighteen years old,
1 Esdras 1:42 and he reigns three months and ten days in Jerusalem, and he did what was evil before the Lord.
1 Esdras 1:43 And after a year Nabouchodonosor sent and removed him to Babylon together with the holy vessels of the Lord,
1 Esdras 1:44 and appointed Sedekias king of Judea and Jerusalem, Sedekias being twenty-one years old, and he reigns eleven years.
1 Esdras 1:45 And he did what was evil before the Lord and did not show reverence at the words spoken by Jeremias the prophet from the mouth of the Lord.
1 Esdras 1:46 And having been put under oath by King Nabouchodonosor in the name of the Lord, he broke his oath and withdrew, and, hardening his neck and his heart, transgressed the ordinances of the Lord, the God of Israel.
1 Esdras 1:47 And the leaders of the people and of the priests acted impiously and lawlessly in many things, beyond all the uncleannesses of all the nations, and defiled the temple of the Lord which was sanctified in Jerusalem.
1 Esdras 1:48 And the God of their fathers sent through his messenger to call them back, since he was sparing them and his dwelling.
1 Esdras 1:49 But they sneered at his messengers, and on the day when the Lord spoke, they were mocking his prophets, until he, angered against his nation because of their impious acts, commanded that the kings of the Chaldeans be brought up against them.
1 Esdras 1:50 These killed their young men with the sword all around their holy temple, and did not spare young man and virgin and elder and younger one, but he handed all over into their hands.
1 Esdras 1:51 And they took all the holy vessels of the Lord, the great and the small, and the chests of the Lord and the royal storehouses, and carried them away to Babylon.
1 Esdras 1:52 And they burned the house of the Lord and dismantled the walls of Jerusalem and burned their towers with fire,
1 Esdras 1:53 and finished rendering all its glorious things useless; and he led the remaining ones away with the sword to Babylon.
1 Esdras 1:54 And they were servants to him and to his sons until the Persians became kings, to fulfill the word of the Lord in the mouth of Jeremias:
1 Esdras 1:55 Until the land takes pleasure in its sabbaths, all the time of its desolation, it will keep sabbath to complete seventy years.

## Chapter 2

1 Esdras 2:1 In the first year of Cyrus's reign over the Persians, for the completion of the word of the Lord in the mouth of Jeremias, the Lord stirred the spirit of Cyrus king of the Persians, and he proclaimed throughout his kingdom and at the same time through writings, saying,
1 Esdras 2:2 Thus says Cyrus king of the Persians: The Lord of Israel, the Lord Most High, appointed me king of the inhabited world, and signified to me that I should build him a house in Jerusalem in Judea.
1 Esdras 2:3 If therefore any of you is of his nation, let his Lord be with him, and let him go up to Jerusalem in Judea and build the house of the Lord of Israel [this is the Lord who dwelt in Jerusalem].
1 Esdras 2:4 As many therefore as dwell in various places, let those in his place help him with gold and silver, with gifts, with horses and livestock, together with the other things added according to vows for the temple of the Lord in Jerusalem.—
1 Esdras 2:5 And the tribal heads of the families of the tribe of Judah and Benjamin and the priests and the Levites and of all whose spirit the Lord stirred arose to go up to build a house for the Lord in Jerusalem,
1 Esdras 2:6 and those around them helped in all things, with silver and gold, horses and livestock, and very many votive offerings from many whose mind was stirred.
1 Esdras 2:7 And King Cyrus brought out the holy vessels of the Lord which Nabouchodonosor removed from Jerusalem and deposited in his own idol temple;
1 Esdras 2:8 and Cyrus king of the Persians brought them out and handed them to Mithridates his own treasurer, and through him they were handed to Sanabassaros, governor of Judea.
1 Esdras 2:9 And their number was: a thousand gold libation vessels, a thousand silver libation vessels, twenty-nine silver censers,
1 Esdras 2:10 thirty gold bowls, two thousand four hundred ten silver ones, and a thousand other vessels.
1 Esdras 2:11 And all the vessels conveyed, gold and silver, were five thousand four hundred sixty-nine, and they were brought up by Sanabassaros together with those from the captivity, from Babylon to Jerusalem.
1 Esdras 2:12 And in the times of Artaxerxes king of the Persians, Beslemos and Mithradates and Tabellios and Raoumos and Beelteemos and Samsaios the scribe and the rest who were associated with them, dwelling in Samaria and the other places, wrote to him against those dwelling in Judea and Jerusalem the letter written below:
1 Esdras 2:13 To King Artaxerxes, lord, your servants Raoumos, the officer of affairs, and Samsaios the scribe and the remaining judges of their council in Coele Syria and Phoenicia:
1 Esdras 2:14 And now let it be known to the lord king that the Judeans who came up from you to us, coming to Jerusalem, are building the rebellious and evil city, and are repairing its marketplaces and walls and laying foundations for a temple.
1 Esdras 2:15 If therefore this city is built and the walls are completed, they will certainly not endure paying taxation, but will even resist kings.
1 Esdras 2:16 And since the matters concerning the temple are being worked on, we consider it good not to overlook such a thing, but to address the lord king, so that, if it seems good to you, an examination may be made in the books from your fathers;
1 Esdras 2:17 and you will find in the records the things written about these matters and know that that city was rebellious and troubling kings and cities, and the Judeans were rebels and were organizing sieges in it from of old, for which reason this city was also desolated.
1 Esdras 2:18 Now therefore we inform you, lord king, that if this city is built and its walls are raised, you will no longer have access to Coele Syria and Phoenicia.—
1 Esdras 2:19 Then the king wrote back to Raoumos, the recorder of affairs, and Beelteemos and Samsaios the scribe and the rest who were associated with them and dwelling in Samaria and Syria and Phoenicia the things written below:
1 Esdras 2:20 I read the letter which you have sent to me.
1 Esdras 2:21 I therefore ordered an examination, and it was found that that city has been opposing kings from of old, and the men were carrying out revolts and wars in it,
1 Esdras 2:22 and strong and harsh kings were in Jerusalem, ruling and taxing Coele Syria and Phoenicia.
1 Esdras 2:23 Now therefore I ordered those men to be prevented from building the city,
1 Esdras 2:24 and provision to be made that nothing happen contrary to these things and that the matters of wickedness not advance further to trouble kings.—
1 Esdras 2:25 Then, when the writings from King Artaxerxes were read, Raoumos and Samsaios the scribe and those associated with them set out in haste to Jerusalem with cavalry and a battle array of people and began to hinder those building.
1 Esdras 2:26 And the building of the temple in Jerusalem was idle until the second year of the reign of Darius king of the Persians.

## Chapter 3

1 Esdras 3:1 And King Darius made a great reception for all those under him and all his household servants and all the magnates of Media and Persia,
1 Esdras 3:2 and all the satraps and generals and local rulers under him, from India to Ethiopia, in the hundred twenty-seven satrapies.
1 Esdras 3:3 And they ate and drank and, filled, departed; and King Darius departed to the bedchamber and slept and became awake.
1 Esdras 3:4 Then the three young men, the bodyguards who guarded the king's body, said to one another,
1 Esdras 3:5 Let each of us speak one word, which will prevail; and whoever's saying appears wiser than the other's, King Darius will give him great gifts and great victory rewards,
1 Esdras 3:6 and purple to put on, and to drink in gold vessels and sleep upon gold, and a chariot with a gold bridle and a fine linen turban and a necklace around the neck,
1 Esdras 3:7 and he will sit second to Darius because of his wisdom and will be called a kinsman of Darius.
1 Esdras 3:8 And then each wrote his own word, and they sealed them and placed them under the pillow of King Darius and said,
1 Esdras 3:9 When the king rises, they will give him the writing, and whoever the king and the three magnates of Persia judge to have the wiser word, to him the victory shall be given, as it is written.
1 Esdras 3:10 The one wrote, Wine prevails.
1 Esdras 3:11 The other wrote, The king prevails.
1 Esdras 3:12 The third wrote, Women prevail, but above all things truth conquers.
1 Esdras 3:13 And when the king rose, they took the writing and gave it to him, and he read it.
1 Esdras 3:14 And he sent and called all the magnates of Persia and Media and satraps and generals and local rulers and high officials, and sat in the council chamber, and the writing was read before them.
1 Esdras 3:15 And he said, Call the young men, and they will explain their words; and they were called and entered.
1 Esdras 3:16 And they said to them, Tell us about the things written.
1 Esdras 3:17 And the first, who had spoken about the strength of wine, began and spoke thus:
1 Esdras 3:18 Men, how does wine prevail? It leads astray the mind of all the people who drink it.
1 Esdras 3:19 It makes the mind of both the king and the orphan one, both that of the servant and that of the free man, both that of the poor man and that of the rich man.
1 Esdras 3:20 And it turns every mind to feasting and gladness, and one remembers no sorrow and no debt.
1 Esdras 3:21 And it makes all hearts rich, and one remembers neither king nor satrap, and it makes one speak of all things in terms of talents.
1 Esdras 3:22 And one does not remember, when they drink, to be friendly with friends and brothers, and after a little while they draw swords;
1 Esdras 3:23 and when they are free of the wine, one does not remember what they did.
1 Esdras 3:24 O men, does wine not prevail, since it compels one to act thus? And he fell silent after speaking thus.

## Chapter 4

1 Esdras 4:1 And the second began to speak, the one who had spoken about the strength of the king:
1 Esdras 4:2 O men, do people not prevail, holding dominion over the land and the sea and all things in them?
1 Esdras 4:3 But the king prevails and rules them and is master over them, and everything he may say to them, they obey.
1 Esdras 4:4 If he tells them to make war against one another, they do so; and if he sends them against the enemies, they go and subdue the mountains and the walls and the towers.
1 Esdras 4:5 They kill and are killed and do not transgress the king's word; and if they conquer, they bring everything to the king, both whatever they plunder and all the other things.
1 Esdras 4:6 And as many as do not serve as soldiers or make war, but cultivate the land, again, when they sow, they harvest and bring up to the king; and compelling one another, they bring up the tributes to the king.
1 Esdras 4:7 And he is one alone; if he says to kill, they kill; he said to release, they release;
1 Esdras 4:8 he said to strike, they strike; he said to desolate, they desolate; he said to build, they build;
1 Esdras 4:9 he said to cut down, they cut down; he said to plant, they plant.
1 Esdras 4:10 And all his people and his forces obey.
1 Esdras 4:11 And besides these things he reclines, eats and drinks and sleeps, but they keep watch all around him, and each cannot go away and do his own works, nor do they disobey him.
1 Esdras 4:12 O men, how does the king not prevail, since he is so obeyed? And he fell silent.
1 Esdras 4:13 And the third, who had spoken about women and truth—this is Zorobabel—began to speak:
1 Esdras 4:14 Men, is the king not great, and are people not many, and is wine not strong? Who then is master over them, or who rules them? Is it not women?
1 Esdras 4:15 Women gave birth to the king and all the people who rule the sea and the land;
1 Esdras 4:16 and from them they came to be, and these reared them, those who plant the vineyards from which wine comes.
1 Esdras 4:17 And these make people's robes, and these give glory to people, and people cannot exist without women.
1 Esdras 4:18 And if they gather gold and silver and every beautiful thing, and see one woman lovely in appearance and beauty,
1 Esdras 4:19 then, leaving all these things, they gape at her and, opening their mouth, gaze at her, and all prefer her to gold and silver and every beautiful thing.
