## Chapter 22

2 Esdras 22:1 And these are the priests and the Levites going up with Zorobabel son of Salathiel and Jesus: Saraia, Jermia, Esdras,
2 Esdras 22:2 Amaria, Malouch,
2 Esdras 22:3 Sechenia;
2 Esdras 22:7 these were rulers of the priests and their brothers in the days of Jesus. –
2 Esdras 22:8 And the Levites: Jesou, Banoui, Kadmiel, Sarabia, Judah, Machania; over the hands, he and his brothers,
2 Esdras 22:9 for the daily divisions.
2 Esdras 22:10 And Jesus begot Joakim, and Joakim begot Eliasib, and Eliasib, Jodae,
2 Esdras 22:11 and Jodae begot Jonathan, and Jonathan begot Jadou.
2 Esdras 22:12 And in the days of Joakim, his brothers the priests and the rulers of the ancestral families: for Saraia, Maraia; for Jermia, Anania;
2 Esdras 22:13 for Esdras, Mesoulam; for Amaria, Joanan;
2 Esdras 22:14 for Malouch, Jonathan; for Sechenia, Joseph;
2 Esdras 22:15 for Arem, Adnas; for Marioth, Elkai;
2 Esdras 22:16 for Addai, Zacharias; for Ganathon, Mosollam;
2 Esdras 22:17 for Abia, Zechri; for Benjamin, at times, for Pheleti;
2 Esdras 22:18 for Balga, Samoue; for Semeia, Jonathan;
2 Esdras 22:19 for Joiarib, Maththanai; for Idia, Ozi;
2 Esdras 22:20 for Sallai, Kallai; for Amouk, Abed;
2 Esdras 22:21 for Elkia, Asabias; for Jedeiou, Nathanael. –
2 Esdras 22:22 The Levites in the days of Eliasib, Joada and Joanan and Idoua were recorded as rulers of ancestral families, and the priests in the reign of Darius the Persian;
2 Esdras 22:23 sons of Levi, rulers of the ancestral families, recorded in the book of words of the days, even until the days of Joanan son of Elisoub.
2 Esdras 22:24 And rulers of the Levites: Asabia and Sarabia and Jesou and sons of Kadmiel and their brothers opposite them, to sing hymns and praise by the commandment of David the man of God, daily division against daily division,
2 Esdras 22:25 when I gathered the gatekeepers,
2 Esdras 22:26 in the days of Joakim son of Jesus son of Josedek and in the days of Neemias, and Esdras the priest, the scribe.
2 Esdras 22:27 And at the dedication of the wall of Jerusalem they sought the Levites in their places to bring them into Jerusalem to make a dedication and rejoicing with thodatha and with songs, sounding cymbals, and psalteries and lyres.
2 Esdras 22:28 And the sons of those singing gathered, also from the surrounding district round about into Jerusalem, and from settlements
2 Esdras 22:29 and from fields; for those singing built settlements for themselves in Jerusalem.
2 Esdras 22:30 And the priests and the Levites were cleansed, and they cleansed the people and the gatekeepers and the wall.
2 Esdras 22:31 And I brought up the rulers of Judah upon the wall and stationed two great ones for praise, and they passed on the right upon the wall of the dung,
2 Esdras 22:32 and Osaia and half the rulers of Judah went behind them,
2 Esdras 22:33 and Azarias, Esdras and Mesoulam,
2 Esdras 22:34 Judah and Benjamin and Samaia and Jermia,
2 Esdras 22:35 and from the sons of the priests, with trumpets, Zacharias son of Jonathan son of Samaia son of Mathania son of Michaia son of Zakchour son of Asaph,
2 Esdras 22:36 and his brothers Samaia and Oziel, to praise with songs of David the man of God, and Esdras the scribe in front of them;
2 Esdras 22:37 at the gate of ain opposite them they went up upon the stairs of the city of David, at the ascent of the wall above the house of David and as far as the water gate eastward. –
2 Esdras 22:38 And the second one for praise was going to meet them, and I behind it, and half the people upon the wall above the tower of the thennourim and as far as the broad wall,
2 Esdras 22:39 and above the gate of Ephraim and to the gate of isana and to the fish gate and at the tower of Ananeel and as far as the sheep gate, and they stood at the gate of the guard.
2 Esdras 22:40 And the two of praise stood in the house of God, and I and half the generals with me,
2 Esdras 22:41 and the priests Eliakim, Maasias, Benjamin, Michaias, Elioenai, Zacharias, Ananias, with trumpets,
2 Esdras 22:42 and Maasias and Semeias and Eleazar and Ozi and Joanan and Melchias and Ailam and Ezour, and those singing were heard and were appointed.
2 Esdras 22:43 And on that day they sacrificed great sacrifices and rejoiced, for God made them rejoice greatly; and their wives and their children rejoiced, and the rejoicing in Jerusalem was heard from far away.
2 Esdras 22:44 And on that day they appointed men over the treasuries for the stores, the first portions and the tithes, and for the rulers of the cities gathered in them, portions for the priests and for the Levites, for there was rejoicing in Judah over the priests and over the Levites standing there.
2 Esdras 22:45 And they kept the watches of their God and the watches of purification, and those singing and the gatekeepers, according to the commandments of David and Solomon his son;
2 Esdras 22:46 for in the days of David, Asaph from the beginning was first of those singing, and a hymn and praise to God,
2 Esdras 22:47 and all Israel in the days of Zorobabel were giving portions of those singing and of the gatekeepers, a day's matter on its day, and consecrating for the Levites, and the Levites consecrating for the sons of Aaron.

## Chapter 23

2 Esdras 23:1 On that day it was read in the book of Moses in the ears of the people, and it was found written in it that Ammanites and Moabites should not enter into the assembly of God forever,
2 Esdras 23:2 for they did not meet the sons of Israel with bread and with water, and they hired Balaam against him to curse, and our God turned the curse into a blessing.
2 Esdras 23:3 And it happened, when they heard the law, every mixed person in Israel was separated.
2 Esdras 23:4 And before this Eliasib the priest, dwelling in a treasury of the house of our God, being near Tobia,
2 Esdras 23:5 made him a great treasury, and there they had formerly been putting the manaan and the frankincense and the vessels and the tenth of grain and of wine and of oil, the commandment of the Levites and of those singing and of the gatekeepers, and first portions of the priests.
2 Esdras 23:6 And during all this I was not in Jerusalem, for in the thirty-second year of Arthasastha king of Babylon I came to the king. And after the end of days I made a request of the king
2 Esdras 23:7 and came into Jerusalem. And I understood the evil which Elisoub did for Tobia, to make him a treasury in the court of the house of God.
2 Esdras 23:8 And it appeared very evil to me, and I threw all the vessels of Tobia's house outside, out of the treasury;
2 Esdras 23:9 and I spoke, and they cleansed the treasuries, and I returned there the vessels of the house of God, the manaa and the frankincense.
2 Esdras 23:10 And I knew that the portions of the Levites had not been given, and the Levites and those singing who were doing the work fled, each man to his field.
2 Esdras 23:11 And I contended with the generals and said, Why was the house of God abandoned? And I gathered them and stationed them at their station.
2 Esdras 23:12 And all Judah brought a tenth of the wheat and of the wine and of the oil into the stores,
2 Esdras 23:13 at the hand of Selemia the priest and Saddouk the scribe and Phadaia from the Levites, and at their hand Anan son of Zakchour son of Mathania, for they were reckoned faithful, to distribute to their brothers.
2 Esdras 23:14 Remember me, God, in this, and let not my mercy be wiped out, which I did in the house of the Lord God.
2 Esdras 23:15 In those days I saw in Judah people treading winepresses on the sabbath and bringing sheaves and loading them upon the donkeys, and wine and grapes and figs and every burden, and bringing them into Jerusalem on the sabbath day; and I testified on the day of their selling.
2 Esdras 23:16 And they settled in it, bringing fish and every article for sale, selling on the sabbath to the sons of Judah and in Jerusalem.
2 Esdras 23:17 And I contended with the free sons of Judah and said to them, What is this evil matter which you do and profane the sabbath day?
2 Esdras 23:18 Did not your fathers act so? And our God brought all these evils upon them and upon us and upon this city; and you add wrath upon Israel by profaning the sabbath.
2 Esdras 23:19 And it happened, when the gates of Jerusalem were set in place before the sabbath, I spoke and they closed the gates, and I said that they should not be opened until after the sabbath; and some of my young servants I stationed at the gates so that burdens should not be lifted on the sabbath day.
2 Esdras 23:20 And they all lodged and carried on selling outside Jerusalem once and twice.
2 Esdras 23:21 And I testified among them and said to them, Why do you lodge opposite the wall? If you do it a second time, I will stretch out my hand against you. From that time they did not come on the sabbath.
2 Esdras 23:22 And I told the Levites, who were cleansing themselves and coming to guard the gates, to sanctify the sabbath day. For these things remember me, God, and spare me according to the abundance of your mercy.
2 Esdras 23:23 And in those days I saw the Jews who settled Azotian, Ammanite, Moabite wives,
2 Esdras 23:24 and their sons, half speaking Azotian, and they do not know how to speak Judean,
2 Esdras 23:25 and I contended with them and cursed them and struck men among them and pulled out their hair and made them swear by God, If you give your daughters to their sons, and if you take from their daughters for your sons.
2 Esdras 23:26 Did not Solomon king of Israel sin so? And among many nations there was no king like him; and he was loved by God, and God made him king over all Israel. And the foreign wives turned even this man aside.
2 Esdras 23:27 And shall we not hear of you doing all this evil, acting faithlessly toward our God, settling foreign wives? –
2 Esdras 23:28 And from the sons of Joada, of Elisoub the great priest, son-in-law of Sanaballat the Oronite, and I drove him out from me.
2 Esdras 23:29 Remember for them, God, concerning the kinship of the priesthood and the covenant of the priesthood, and the Levites. –
2 Esdras 23:30 And I cleansed them from every foreign association and stationed daily divisions for the priests and for the Levites, each man according to his work,
2 Esdras 23:31 and the gift of the wood-bearers at appointed times and among the bakchouria. Remember me, our God, for goodness.

# Ezra

The Apostolic Bible. Public domain. https://apostolic-bible.ysys9.chatgpt.site/license.html


## Chapter 1

Ezra 1:1 And in the first year of Cyrus king of the Persians, so that the word of the Lord from the mouth of Jeremias would be fulfilled, the Lord stirred up the spirit of Cyrus king of the Persians, and he ordered a proclamation throughout his kingdom, indeed also in writing, saying,
Ezra 1:2 Thus said Cyrus king of the Persians: The Lord, the God of heaven, gave me all the kingdoms of the earth, and he charged me to build him a house in Jerusalem in Judea.
Ezra 1:3 Who among you is of all his people? And his God shall be with him, and he shall go up to Jerusalem in Judea, and let him build the house of the God of Israel [he is the God in Jerusalem].
Ezra 1:4 And everyone remaining from all the places where he himself sojourns, the men of his place shall take him up with silver and gold and equipment and livestock, together with the voluntary offering for the house of God in Jerusalem.—
Ezra 1:5 And the rulers of the families of Judah and Benjamin and the priests and the Levites arose, of all whose spirit God stirred to go up to build the house of the Lord in Jerusalem.
Ezra 1:6 And all those round about strengthened their hands with vessels of silver, with gold, with equipment and livestock and gifts, apart from the voluntary offerings.
Ezra 1:7 And King Cyrus brought out the vessels of the house of the Lord which Nabouchodonosor took from Jerusalem and placed in the house of his god,
Ezra 1:8 and Cyrus king of the Persians brought them out into the hand of Mithradates the gasbarenos, and he counted them for Sasabasar ruler of Judah.
Ezra 1:9 And this is their number: thirty gold cooling vessels and a thousand silver cooling vessels, twenty-nine assorted items,
Ezra 1:10 thirty gold kephphoure and two hundred silver ones, and a thousand other vessels.
Ezra 1:11 All the vessels of gold and silver, five thousand four hundred, all going up with Sasabasar from the deportation, from Babylon to Jerusalem.

## Chapter 2

Ezra 2:1 And these are the sons of the country going up from the captivity of the deportation which Nabouchodonosor king of Babylon deported to Babylon, and they returned to Jerusalem and Judah, each man to his city,
Ezra 2:2 who came with Zorobabel: Jesus, Neemias, Saraias, Reelias, Mardochaios, Balasan, Masphar, Bagoui, Reoum, Baana. The number of men of the people of Israel:
Ezra 2:3 sons of Phoros, two thousand one hundred seventy-two.
Ezra 2:4 Sons of Saphatia, three hundred seventy-two.

Ezra 2:27 Men of Machmas, one hundred twenty-two.
Ezra 2:28 Men of Baithel and Aia, four hundred twenty-three.
Ezra 2:29 Sons of Nabou, fifty-two.

Ezra 2:64 And the whole assembly as one, forty-two thousand three hundred sixty,

Ezra 2:66 their horses, seven hundred thirty-six, their mules, two hundred forty-five,

Ezra 2:68 And some of the rulers of families, when they came to the house of the Lord in Jerusalem, made voluntary offerings for the house of God, to establish it upon its prepared site;
Ezra 2:69 according to their ability they gave to the treasury of the work pure gold, sixty-one thousand minas, and silver, five thousand minas, and a hundred kothonoi of the priests.—
Ezra 2:70 And the priests and the Levites and those from the people and the singers and the gatekeepers and the Nathinim settled in their cities, and all Israel in their cities.

## Chapter 3

Ezra 3:1 And the seventh month arrived—and the sons of Israel were in their cities—and the people gathered as one man in Jerusalem.
Ezra 3:2 And Jesus son of Josedek and his brothers the priests and Zorobabel son of Salathiel and his brothers arose and built the altar of the God of Israel, to offer whole burnt offerings upon it according to the things written in the law of Moses, the man of God.
Ezra 3:3 And they prepared the altar upon its prepared site, because terror was upon them from the peoples of the lands, and a whole burnt offering to the Lord went up upon it in the morning and toward evening.
Ezra 3:4 And they kept the feast of tents according to what was written, and whole burnt offerings day by day, in number according to the ordinance, the requirement of a day on its day,
Ezra 3:5 and after this continual whole burnt offerings, and for the new moons and for all the sanctified feasts, and for everyone voluntarily offering a voluntary offering to the Lord.
Ezra 3:6 On day one of the seventh month they began to offer whole burnt offerings to the Lord; and the house of the Lord had not been founded.
Ezra 3:7 And they gave silver to the stonecutters and carpenters, and food and drink and oil to the Sedanin and the Sorin, to bring cedar timber from Lebanon to the sea of Joppe, according to the concession of Cyrus king of the Persians to them.—
Ezra 3:8 And in the second year of their coming to the house of God in Jerusalem, in the second month, Zorobabel son of Salathiel and Jesus son of Josedek and the remaining ones of their brothers, the priests and the Levites, and all those coming from the captivity to Jerusalem began, and they stationed the Levites from twenty years old and upward over those doing the works in the house of the Lord.
Ezra 3:9 And Jesus and his sons and his brothers, Kadmiel and his sons, sons of Judah, stood over those doing the works in the house of God, sons of Enadad, their sons and their brothers, the Levites.
Ezra 3:10 And they laid foundations to build the house of the Lord, and the priests stood robed with trumpets, and the Levites, sons of Asaph, with cymbals, to praise the Lord according to the hands of David king of Israel,
Ezra 3:11 and they answered in praise and thanksgiving to the Lord, because it is good, because his mercy upon Israel is for the age. And all the people sounded a great voice to praise the Lord at the foundation of the house of the Lord.
Ezra 3:12 And many from the priests and the Levites and rulers of the families, the elders who saw the first house at its foundation and this house with their eyes, were weeping with a great voice, and a crowd with shouting and gladness raised a song;
Ezra 3:13 and the people were not distinguishing the sound of the shout of gladness from the sound of the people's weeping, because the people cried out with a great voice, and the sound was heard even from afar.

## Chapter 4

Ezra 4:1 And those afflicting Judah and Benjamin heard that the sons of the deportation were building a house for the Lord, the God of Israel,
Ezra 4:2 and approached Zorobabel and the rulers of the families and said to them, We shall build with you, because like you we seek your God, and we sacrifice to him since the days of Asaraddon king of Assour, who brought us here.
Ezra 4:3 And Zorobabel and Jesus and the remaining rulers of the families of Israel said to them, It is not for us and you to build a house for our God, because we ourselves together shall build for the Lord our God, as Cyrus king of the Persians commanded us.
Ezra 4:4 And the people of the land were weakening the hands of the people of Judah, and they were hindering them from building,
Ezra 4:5 and hiring those deliberating against them to scatter their counsel all the days of Cyrus king of the Persians and until the reign of Darius king of the Persians.
Ezra 4:6 And in the reign of Asoueros, at the beginning of his reign, they wrote a letter against those dwelling in Judah and Jerusalem.
Ezra 4:7 And in the days of Arthasastha, Tabeel wrote in peace to Mithradates, together also with his other fellow servants, to Arthasastha king of the Persians; the tax collector wrote a writing in Syrian and translated.
Ezra 4:8 Raoum baaltam and Samsai the scribe wrote one letter against Jerusalem to King Arthasastha.
Ezra 4:9 These things Raoum baaltam and Samsai the scribe and our remaining fellow servants determined, Dinaioi, Apharsathachaioi, Tarphallaioi, Apharsaioi, Archyaioi, Babylonians, Sousanachaioi [who are Elamites],
Ezra 4:10 and the remaining ones of the nations whom the great and honored Asennaphar deported and settled in the cities of Somoron, and the remnant beyond the river;
Ezra 4:11 this is the arrangement of the letter which they sent to him: To King Arthasastha, your servants, men beyond the river.
Ezra 4:12 Let it be known to the king that the Judeans who came up from you to us came to Jerusalem; they are building the rebellious and evil city, and they have repaired its walls and raised its foundations.
Ezra 4:13 Now therefore let it be known to the king that if that city is rebuilt and its walls repaired, there will be no tribute for you, nor will they give it; and this harms kings.
Ezra 4:14 And it is not permitted for us to see the king's disgrace; because of this we sent and made known to the king,
Ezra 4:15 that he may examine the book of the record of your fathers, and you will find and know that that city is a rebellious city and harms kings and countries, and there have been flights of slaves in its midst from times of old; because of these things this city was desolated.
Ezra 4:16 We therefore make known to the king that if that city is built and its walls repaired, there is no peace for you.
Ezra 4:17 And the king sent peace to Raoum baaltam and Samsai the scribe and their remaining fellow servants dwelling in Samaria and the remaining ones beyond the river, and says,
Ezra 4:18 The tax collector whom you sent to us was called before me.
Ezra 4:19 And a decision was issued by me, and we examined and found that that city rises against kings from days of old, and rebellions and flights occur in it,
Ezra 4:20 and strong kings arise over Jerusalem and rule all the west of the river, and full tribute and a portion are given to them.
Ezra 4:21 And now issue a decision to stop those men, and that city shall no longer be built, so that according to the decision
Ezra 4:22 you may be on guard against allowing relaxation in this matter, lest destruction multiply to the harm of kings.
Ezra 4:23 Then the tax collector of King Arthasastha read before Raoum and Samsai the scribe and their fellow servants; and they went in haste to Jerusalem and into Judah and stopped them with horses and force.
Ezra 4:24 Then the work of the house of God in Jerusalem ceased, and was idle until the second year of the reign of Darius king of the Persians.

## Chapter 5

Ezra 5:1 And Angaios the prophet and Zacharias son of Addo prophesied a prophecy to the Judeans in Judah and Jerusalem in the name of the God of Israel over them.
Ezra 5:2 Then Zorobabel son of Salathiel and Jesus son of Josedek arose and began to build the house of God in Jerusalem, and with them were the prophets of God, helping them.
Ezra 5:3 At that very time Thanthanai governor beyond the river and Satharbouzana and their fellow servants came against them and said such things to them: Who issued you a decision to build this house and complete this provision?
Ezra 5:4 Then they said these things to them: What are the names of the men building this city?
Ezra 5:5 And the eyes of God were upon the captivity of Judah, and they did not stop them until a decision was carried to Darius; and then a message was sent to the tax collector concerning this.
Ezra 5:6 A transcript of the letter which Thanthanai governor beyond the river and Satharbouzana and their fellow servants, the Apharsachaioi beyond the river, sent to King Darius;
Ezra 5:7 they sent a statement to him, and these things are written in it: To King Darius, all peace.
Ezra 5:8 Let it be known to the king that we went into the country of Judea, to the house of the great God, and it is being built with choice stones, and timber is being placed in the walls, and that work is being done skillfully and prospers in their hands.
Ezra 5:9 Then we questioned those elders and said thus to them, Who issued you a decision to build this house and complete this provision?
Ezra 5:10 And we asked them their names to make known to you, so as to write to you the names of the men who are their rulers.
Ezra 5:11 And they answered us with such a statement, saying, We are slaves of the God of heaven and earth, and we are building the house which had been built many years before this, and a great king of Israel built it and completed it
Ezra 5:12 for them. But from the time when our fathers provoked the God of heaven to anger, he gave them into the hands of Nabouchodonosor king of Babylon, the Chaldean, and he demolished this house and deported the people to Babylon.
Ezra 5:13 But in the first year of King Cyrus, King Cyrus issued a decision that this house of God should be built.
Ezra 5:14 And the vessels of the house of God, the gold and silver ones, which Nabouchodonosor brought out of the house in Jerusalem and carried away to the king's temple, King Cyrus brought out of the king's temple and gave to Sasabasar the treasurer over the treasury,
Ezra 5:15 and said to him, Take all the vessels and go, place them in the house in Jerusalem in their own place.
Ezra 5:16 Then that Sasabasar came and laid foundations of the house of God in Jerusalem; and from then until now it has been built and has not been completed.
Ezra 5:17 And now, if it is good to the king, let an examination be made in the treasury house of the king of Babylon, so that you may know that a decision was issued by King Cyrus to build that house of God in Jerusalem; and when the king knows concerning this, let him send to us.

## Chapter 6

Ezra 6:1 Then King Darius issued a decision and examined in the libraries where the treasure is laid in Babylon.
Ezra 6:2 And in a city, in the fortress of the city of the Medes, one scroll was found, and this was written in it: Memorandum:
Ezra 6:3 In the first year of King Cyrus, King Cyrus issued a decision concerning the house of God in Jerusalem: Let a house be built, and a place where they sacrifice the sacrifices; and he set an elevation, a height of sixty cubits, its width sixty cubits;
Ezra 6:4 and three strong stone courses and one wooden course; and the expense shall be given from the king's house;
Ezra 6:5 and the vessels of the house of God, the silver and gold ones, which Nabouchodonosor brought out of the house in Jerusalem and conveyed to Babylon, let them be given and go to the temple in Jerusalem, to the place where they were placed in the house of God.
Ezra 6:6 Now you shall give, governors beyond the river, Satharbouzana and their fellow servants, the Apharsachaioi beyond the river, being far from there,
Ezra 6:7 leave the work of the house of God alone; let the leaders of the Judeans and the elders of the Judeans build that house of God upon its site.
Ezra 6:8 And a decision was issued by me that you should never do anything with the elders of the Judeans toward building that house of God; and from the king's possessions, the tributes beyond the river, let expenses be diligently given to those men, so that it may not be stopped;
Ezra 6:9 and whatever deficiency there may be, both offspring of oxen and rams and lambs for whole burnt offerings to the God of heaven, wheat, salt, wine, oil, according to the word of the priests in Jerusalem, let it be given them day by day, whatever they ask,
Ezra 6:10 so that they may offer sweet smells to the God of heaven and pray for the life of the king and his sons.
Ezra 6:11 And a decision was issued by me that every man who changes this word, a timber shall be taken down from his house, and he shall be raised upright and fixed upon it, and his house shall be dealt with according to me.
Ezra 6:12 And God, whose name dwells there, will overthrow every king and people who stretches out his hand to change or destroy that house of God in Jerusalem. I, Darius, issued a decision; it shall be done diligently.
Ezra 6:13 Then Thanthanai governor beyond the river, Satharbouzana and his fellow servants did thus diligently according to what King Darius sent.
Ezra 6:14 And the elders of the Judeans were building, and the Levites, through the prophecy of Angaios the prophet and Zacharias son of Addo, and they rebuilt and completed it by the decision of the God of Israel and by the decision of Cyrus and Darius and Arthasastha, kings of the Persians.
Ezra 6:15 And they completed this house by the third day of the month Adar, which is the sixth year of the reign of King Darius.
Ezra 6:16 And the sons of Israel, the priests and the Levites and the remaining sons of the deportation, held the dedication of the house of God with gladness.
Ezra 6:17 And they offered for the dedication of the house of God a hundred calves, two hundred rams, four hundred lambs, twelve male goats for sin for all Israel, according to the number of the tribes of Israel.
Ezra 6:18 And they stationed the priests in their divisions and the Levites in their portions for the service of God in Jerusalem, according to the writing of the book of Moses.
Ezra 6:19 And the sons of the deportation kept the Passover on the fourteenth of the first month.
Ezra 6:20 For the priests and the Levites were cleansed to a man, all clean, and slaughtered the Passover for all the sons of the deportation and for their brothers the priests and for themselves.
Ezra 6:21 And the sons of Israel ate the Passover, those from the deportation and everyone separating from the uncleanness of the nations of the land to join them, to seek the Lord, the God of Israel.
Ezra 6:22 And they kept the feast of unleavened bread seven days with gladness, because the Lord gladdened them and turned the heart of the king of Assour toward them, to strengthen their hands in the works of the house of the God of Israel.

## Chapter 7

Ezra 7:1 And after these words, in the reign of Arthasastha king of the Persians, Esdras went up, son of Saraios son of Azarios son of Elkia,
Ezra 7:2 son of Saloum son of Saddouk son of Achitob,
Ezra 7:3 son of Samaria son of Esria son of Mareroth,
Ezra 7:4 son of Zaraia son of Saouia son of Bokki,
Ezra 7:5 son of Abisoue son of Phinees son of Eleazar son of Aaron the first priest;
Ezra 7:6 this Esdras went up from Babylon, and he was a swift scribe in the law of Moses which the Lord, the God of Israel, gave; and the king gave to him, because the hand of the Lord his God was upon him, in all that he himself sought.
Ezra 7:7 And some of the sons of Israel and some of the priests and some of the Levites, and the singers and the gatekeepers and the Nathinim, went up to Jerusalem in the seventh year of King Arthasastha.
Ezra 7:8 And they came to Jerusalem in the fifth month; this is the king's seventh year;
Ezra 7:9 for on the first of the first month he himself laid the foundation of the ascent from Babylon, and on the first of the fifth month they came to Jerusalem, because the hand of his God was good upon him.
Ezra 7:10 For Esdras put it in his heart to seek the law and do it and teach ordinances and judgments in Israel.
Ezra 7:11 And this is the transcript of the decree which Arthasastha gave to Esdras the priest, the scribe of the book of the words of the Lord's commandments and his ordinances for Israel:
Ezra 7:12 Arthasastha king of kings to Esdras, scribe of the law of the God of heaven: The word and the answer are completed.
Ezra 7:13 A decision was issued by me that everyone in my kingdom from the people of Israel and priests and Levites who volunteers to go to Jerusalem should go with you;
Ezra 7:14 he was sent from before the king and the seven counselors to examine concerning Judea and Jerusalem according to the law of their God in your hand.
Ezra 7:15 And for the house of the Lord, silver and gold which the king and the counselors voluntarily offered to the God of Israel dwelling in Jerusalem,
Ezra 7:16 and all silver and gold, whatever you may find in all the country of Babylon, together with the voluntary offering of the people and priests voluntarily offering for the house of God in Jerusalem,
Ezra 7:17 and everything coming in, readily enter this in this book: calves, rams, lambs and their sacrifices and their libations, and you shall offer them upon the altar of the house of your God in Jerusalem.
Ezra 7:18 And if it seems good to you and your brothers to do anything with the remainder of the silver and gold, do as is pleasing to your God.
Ezra 7:19 And the vessels given to you for the ministry of the house of God, hand over before God in Jerusalem.
Ezra 7:20 And the remainder of the need of the house of your God, whatever it seems to you to give, you shall give from the king's treasury houses.
Ezra 7:21 And from me—I, King Arthasastha, issued a decision to all the treasuries beyond the river—that everything which Esdras the priest and scribe of the law of the God of heaven asks of you should be done readily,
Ezra 7:22 up to a hundred talents of silver and up to a hundred kors of wheat and up to a hundred baths of wine and up to a hundred baths of oil, and salt for which there is no written limit.
Ezra 7:23 Let everything which is in the decision of the God of heaven be done. Take care lest anyone attempt anything against the house of the God of heaven, lest wrath come upon the kingdom of the king and his sons.
Ezra 7:24 And it has been made known to you: among all the priests and Levites, singers, gatekeepers, Nathinim and ministers of this house of God, let there be no tribute for you; you shall not have authority to enslave them.
Ezra 7:25 And you, Esdras, according to the wisdom of God in your hand, appoint scribes and judges, so that they may judge all the people beyond the river, all those knowing the law of your God, and to the one not knowing you shall make it known.
Ezra 7:26 And everyone who does not readily do the law of God and the law of the king, judgment shall be executed upon him, whether to death or discipline or loss of possessions or bonds.
Ezra 7:27 Blessed is the Lord, the God of our fathers, who put it thus in the king's heart to glorify the house of the Lord in Jerusalem,
Ezra 7:28 and inclined mercy toward me in the eyes of the king and his counselors and all the king's exalted rulers. And I was strengthened, as the good hand of God was upon me, and gathered rulers from Israel to go up with me.

## Chapter 8

Ezra 8:1 And these are the rulers of their families, the guides going up with me in the reign of Arthasastha king of Babylon:
Ezra 8:2 from the sons of Phinees, Gersom; from the sons of Ithamar, Daniel; from the sons of David, Atous;
Ezra 8:3 from the sons of Sachania, from the sons of Phoros, Zacharias, and with him the company, a hundred fifty;
Ezra 8:4 from the sons of Phaathmoab, Eliana son of Zaraia, and with him two hundred males;
Ezra 8:5 from the sons of Zathoe, Sechenias son of Aziel, and with him three hundred males;
Ezra 8:6 and from the sons of Adin, Obeth son of Jonathan, and with him fifty males;
Ezra 8:7 and from the sons of Elam, Jesia son of Athelia, and with him seventy males;
Ezra 8:8 and from the sons of Saphatia, Zabdia son of Michael, and with him eighty males;
Ezra 8:9 and from the sons of Joab, Abadia son of Jiel, and with him two hundred eighteen males;
Ezra 8:10 and from the sons of Baani, Salimouth son of Josephia, and with him a hundred sixty males;
Ezra 8:11 and from the sons of Babi, Zacharia son of Babi, and with him seventy-eight males;
Ezra 8:12 and from the sons of Asgad, Joanan son of Akatan, and with him a hundred ten males;
Ezra 8:13 and from the sons of Adonikam, the last ones, and these are their names: Aliphalat, Jiel and Samaia, and with them sixty males;
Ezra 8:14 and from the sons of Bago, Outhi, and with him seventy males.
Ezra 8:15 And I gathered them at the river coming toward Eui, and we camped there three days. And I examined among the people and among the priests, and I found none of the sons of Levi there;
Ezra 8:16 and I sent men to Eleazar, Ariel, Samaia and Alonam and Jarib and Elnathan and Nathan and Zacharia and Mesoulam, and discerning men to Joarib and Elnathan,
Ezra 8:17 and brought them out before a ruler in the silver of the place and put words in their mouth to speak to their brothers, the Nathinim in the silver of the place, to bring us singers for the house of our God.
Ezra 8:18 And there came to us, as the hand of our God was good upon us, a man sachol from the sons of Mooli son of Levi son of Israel; and at first his sons and brothers came, eighteen;
Ezra 8:19 and Asebia and Osaia from the sons of Merari, his brothers and their sons, twenty;
Ezra 8:20 and from the Nathinim whom David and the rulers gave for the service of the Levites, two hundred twenty Nathinim; all were gathered by names.
Ezra 8:21 And I proclaimed a fast there at the river Aoue, to humble ourselves before our God, to seek from him a straight way for us and our children and all our possessions.
Ezra 8:22 For I was ashamed to ask the king for a force and horsemen to save us from an enemy on the way, because we said to the king, saying, The hand of our God is upon all those seeking him for good, and his might and his wrath upon all those forsaking him.
Ezra 8:23 And we fasted and sought from our God concerning this, and he heeded us.
Ezra 8:24 And I set apart twelve from the rulers of the priests, for Saraia, Asabia and with them ten from their brothers,
Ezra 8:25 and weighed out to them the silver and gold and the vessels of the first offering of the house of our God, which the king and his counselors and his rulers and all Israel who were found lifted up.
Ezra 8:26 And I weighed out into their hands six hundred fifty talents of silver and a hundred silver vessels and a hundred talents of gold,
Ezra 8:27 and twenty gold kaphoure for the journey, a thousand chamanim, and various vessels of good shining bronze, desirable among gold.
Ezra 8:28 And I said to them, You are holy to the Lord, and the vessels are holy, and the silver and gold are voluntary offerings to the Lord, the God of your fathers;
Ezra 8:29 keep awake and guard them until you stand before the rulers of the priests and the Levites and the rulers of the families in Jerusalem, in the tents of the house of the Lord.
Ezra 8:30 And the priests and the Levites received the weight of the silver and gold and the vessels, to bring to Jerusalem, to the house of our God.
Ezra 8:31 And we set out from the river Aoue on the twelfth of the first month to come to Jerusalem; and the hand of our God was upon us, and he delivered us from the hand of an enemy and foe on the way.
Ezra 8:32 And we came to Jerusalem and stayed there three days.
Ezra 8:33 And it happened on the fourth day that we weighed out the silver and gold and vessels in the house of our God into the hand of Merimoth son of Ouria the priest—and with him Eleazar son of Phinees, and with them Jozabad son of Jesus and Noadia son of Banaia, the Levites—
Ezra 8:34 everything by number and weight, and all the weight was written. At that time,
Ezra 8:35 those who came from the captivity, sons of the sojourning, offered whole burnt offerings to the God of Israel, twelve calves for all Israel, ninety-six rams, seventy-seven lambs, twelve male goats for sin, all whole burnt offerings to the Lord.
Ezra 8:36 And they gave the king's ordinance to the king's administrators and governors beyond the river, and they glorified the people and the house of God.

## Chapter 9

Ezra 9:1 And when these things were completed, the rulers approached me, saying, The people Israel and the priests and the Levites were not separated from the peoples of the lands in their abominations, the Chanani, the Ethi, the Pherezi, the Jebousi, the Ammoni, the Moabi, the Moseri and the Amori,
Ezra 9:2 for they took from their daughters for themselves and for their sons, and the holy seed was brought among peoples of the lands, and the hand of the rulers was foremost in this faithlessness.
Ezra 9:3 And when I heard this word, I tore my garments and was leaping, and I was plucking from the hairs of my head and from my beard, and I sat remaining still.
Ezra 9:4 And everyone pursuing the word of the God of Israel gathered to me over the faithlessness of the exiled community, and I was sitting, remaining still until the evening sacrifice.
Ezra 9:5 And at the evening sacrifice I arose from my humiliation; and as I tore my garments, I was leaping, and I bend upon my knees and spread out my hands toward the Lord God
Ezra 9:6 and said, Lord, I was ashamed and abashed to lift my face toward you, for our lawless deeds multiplied above our head, and our offenses grew great as far as heaven.
Ezra 9:7 From the days of our fathers we are in great offense until this day; and in our lawless deeds we were handed over, we and our kings and our sons, into the hand of kings of the nations, with sword and with captivity and with plunder and with shame of our face, as this day.
Ezra 9:8 And now the Lord our God dealt leniently with us, to leave something for us for salvation and to give us a support in the place of his sanctuary, to enlighten our eyes and give a little quickening in our slavery.
Ezra 9:9 For we are slaves, and in our slavery the Lord our God did not abandon us, and he inclined mercy upon us before kings of Persians, to give us quickening, for them to raise the house of our God and restore her desolate places, and to give us a fence in Judah and in Jerusalem.
Ezra 9:10 What should we say, our God, after this? For we abandoned your commandments,
Ezra 9:11 which you gave us by the hand of your slaves the prophets, saying, The land into which you enter to inherit it is a land being displaced by the displacement of peoples of the nations in their abominations, with which they filled it from mouth to mouth in their uncleannesses;
Ezra 9:12 and now do not give your daughters to their sons, and do not take from their daughters for your sons, and you shall not seek out their peace and their good forever, so that you may grow strong and eat the good things of the land and bequeath them to your sons forever.
Ezra 9:13 And after everything coming upon us in our evil deeds and in our great offense; for there is none like our God, for you lightened our lawless deeds and gave us salvation;
Ezra 9:14 for we turned back to scatter your commandments and to intermarry with the peoples of the lands; do not be provoked against us to the point of consummation, so that there is no remnant and survivor.
Ezra 9:15 Lord, God of Israel, you are righteous, for we were left surviving, as this day; behold, we are before you in our offenses, for it is not possible to stand before you on account of this.

## Chapter 10

Ezra 10:1 And as Esdras prayed and as he confessed, weeping and praying before the house of God, a very great assembly gathered to him from Israel, men and women and young men, for the people wept and raised their voice, weeping.
Ezra 10:2 And Sechenias son of Jiiel, from the sons of Elam, answered and said to Esdras, We acted faithlessly toward our God and settled foreign wives from the peoples of the land; and now there is endurance for Israel in this.
Ezra 10:3 And now let us make a covenant with our God to cast out all the wives and what was born from them, as you wish; arise and frighten them with the commandments of our God, and let it happen according to the law.
Ezra 10:4 Arise, for the matter is upon you, and we are with you; be strong and act.
Ezra 10:5 And Esdras arose and made the rulers, the priests and Levites and all Israel swear to act according to this word, and they swore.
Ezra 10:6 And Esdras arose from before the house of God and went into the treasury of Joanan son of Elisoub, and he went there; he did not eat bread and did not drink water, for he was mourning over the faithlessness of the exiled community.
Ezra 10:7 And they carried a proclamation through Judah and through Jerusalem to all the sons of the exiled community, to be gathered into Jerusalem,
Ezra 10:8 and everyone who does not come within three days, according to the counsel of the rulers and the elders, all his property shall be devoted to destruction, and he shall be separated from the assembly of the exiled community.
Ezra 10:9 And all the men of Judah and Benjamin gathered into Jerusalem within the three days; this was the ninth month. On the twentieth of the month all the people sat in the square of the house of God, because of their disturbance concerning the matter and because of the storm.
Ezra 10:10 And Esdras the priest arose and said to them, You acted faithlessly and settled foreign wives, to add to Israel's offense;
Ezra 10:11 and now give praise to the Lord, the God of your fathers, and do what is pleasing before him, and separate yourselves from the peoples of the land and from the foreign wives.
Ezra 10:12 And the whole assembly answered and said, Great is this word of yours for us to do;
Ezra 10:13 but the people are many, and the season is wintry, and there is no ability to stand outside; and the work is not for one day and not for two, for we multiplied wrongdoing in this matter.
Ezra 10:14 Let our rulers, then, stand for the whole assembly, and let all those in our cities, whoever settled foreign wives, come at times by arrangements, and with them elders of each city and judges, to turn away the wrath of the anger of our God from us concerning this matter.
Ezra 10:15 Only Jonathan son of Asael and Jazia son of Thekoue were with me concerning this, and Mesoulam and Sabbathai the Levite were helping them.
Ezra 10:16 And the sons of the exiled community did so. And Esdras the priest and men who were rulers of ancestral families were set apart by house, and all by names, for they turned on the first day of the tenth month to investigate the matter.
Ezra 10:17 And they finished with all the men who settled foreign wives by the first day of the first month.
Ezra 10:18 And among the sons of the priests were found those who settled foreign wives: from the sons of Jesus son of Josedek and his brothers, Maasea and Eliezer and Jarib and Gadalia,
Ezra 10:19 and they gave their hand to put out their wives, and a ram from the sheep as an offering for offense, concerning their offense;
Ezra 10:20 and from the sons of Emmer, Anani and Zabdia;
Ezra 10:21 and from the sons of Eram, Masaia and Elia and Samaia and Jiiel and Ozia;
Ezra 10:22 and from the sons of Phasour, Elioenai, Maasaia and Ishmael and Nathanael and Jozabad and Elasa. –
Ezra 10:23 And from the Levites: Jozabad and Samou and Kolia [he is Kolitas] and Phathaia and Jodom and Eliezer;
Ezra 10:24 and from those singing, Elisaph; and from the gatekeepers, Sellem and Telem and Odoue. –
Ezra 10:25 And from Israel: from the sons of Phoros, Ramia and Jazia and Melchia and Meamin and Eleazar and Asabia and Banaia;
Ezra 10:26 and from the sons of Elam, Mathania and Zacharia and Jaiel and Abdia and Jarimoth and Elia;
Ezra 10:27 and from the sons of Zathoua, Elioenai, Elisoub, Mathania and Jarmoth and Zabad and Oziza;
Ezra 10:28 and from the sons of Babi, Joanan, Anania and Zabou, Othali;
Ezra 10:29 and from the sons of Banoui, Mesoulam, Malouch, Adaias, Jasoub and Salouia and Remoth;
Ezra 10:30 and from the sons of Phaathmoab, Edene, Chalel, Banaia, Masea, Mathania, Beselel and Banoui and Manasse;
Ezra 10:31 and from the sons of Eram, Eliezer, Jessia, Melchia, Samaia, Semeon,
Ezra 10:32 Benjamin, Malouch, Samaria;
Ezra 10:33 and from the sons of Esam, Mathani, Mathatha, Zabed, Eliphaleth, Jerami, Manasse, Semei;
Ezra 10:34 from the sons of Bani, Moodi, Amram, Ouel,
Ezra 10:35 Banaia, Badaia, Chelia,
Ezra 10:36 Oujechoa, Jeremoth, Eliasib,
Ezra 10:37 Mathania, Mathanai, and they acted,
Ezra 10:38 the sons of Banoui and the sons of Semei
Ezra 10:39 and Selemia and Nathan and Adaia,
Ezra 10:40 Machnadabou, Sesi, Sarou,
Ezra 10:41 Ezerel and Selemia and Samaria
Ezra 10:42 and Saloum, Amaria, Joseph;
Ezra 10:43 from the sons of Nabou, Jiiel, Mathathia, Sedem, Zambina, Jadai and Joel and Banaia. –
Ezra 10:44 All these took foreign wives and begot sons from them.

# Nehemiah

The Apostolic Bible. Public domain. https://apostolic-bible.ysys9.chatgpt.site/license.html


## Chapter 1

Nehemiah 1:1 Words of Neemias son of Achalia. And it happened in the month Chaseelou, in the twentieth year, and I was in Sousan abira,
Nehemiah 1:2 and Anani, one of my brothers, came, he and men of Judah, and I asked them concerning those saved, who were left from the captivity, and concerning Jerusalem.
Nehemiah 1:3 And they said to me, Those remaining, who were left from the captivity there in the country, are in great evil and in reproach, and the walls of Jerusalem are torn down, and her gates were burned with fire.
Nehemiah 1:4 And it happened, when I heard these words, I sat and wept and mourned for days, and I was fasting and praying before the God of heaven
Nehemiah 1:5 and said, Not so, Lord, God of heaven, the strong, the great and the fearsome, keeping the covenant and mercy for those loving him and those keeping his commandments;
Nehemiah 1:6 let your ear, then, be attentive and your eyes opened to hear your slave's prayer, which I pray before you today, day and night, concerning the sons of Israel, your slaves, and I confess concerning the sins of the sons of Israel which we sinned against you. Both I and my father's house sinned;
Nehemiah 1:7 with dissolution we acted dissolutely toward you, and we did not keep the commandments and the ordinances and the judgments which you commanded Moses your servant.
Nehemiah 1:8 Remember, then, the word which you commanded Moses your servant, saying, If you act faithlessly, I will scatter you among the peoples;
Nehemiah 1:9 and if you turn toward me and keep my commandments and do them, if your dispersion is from the end of heaven, from there I will gather them and bring them into the place which I chose for my name to dwell there.
Nehemiah 1:10 And they are your servants and your people, whom you redeemed with your great power and with your mighty hand.
Nehemiah 1:11 Not so, Lord, but let your ear be attentive to the prayer of your slave and to the prayer of your servants who wish to fear your name, and give success, then, to your servant today and give him into compassion before this man. – And I was cupbearer to the king.

## Chapter 2

Nehemiah 2:1 And it happened in the month Nisan, in the twentieth year for King Arthasastha, and the wine was before me, and I took the wine and gave it to the king, and there was no other before him;
Nehemiah 2:2 and the king said to me, Why is your face evil, and are you not being moderate? This is nothing except evil of heart. And I feared very greatly.
Nehemiah 2:3 And I said to the king, Let the king live forever; why should my face certainly not become evil, since the city, the house of my fathers' tombs, was made desolate, and her gates were consumed with fire?
Nehemiah 2:4 And the king said to me, Concerning what do you seek this? And I prayed to the God of heaven
Nehemiah 2:5 and said to the king, If it is good to the king, and if your servant will be favored before you, so as to send him to Judah, to the city of my fathers' tombs, then I will rebuild it.
Nehemiah 2:6 And the king and the concubine sitting beside him said to me, Until when will your journey be, and when will you return? And it was pleasing before the king, and he sent me away, and I gave him a limit.
Nehemiah 2:7 And I said to the king, If it is good to the king, let him give me letters to the governors beyond the river, so as to convey me through until I come to Judah,
Nehemiah 2:8 and a letter to Asaph, keeper of the garden which belongs to the king, so as to give me timber to roof the gates, and for the wall of the city, and for a house which I will enter into it. And the king gave to me according to the good hand of God.
Nehemiah 2:9 And I came to the governors beyond the river and gave them the king's letters, and the king sent commanders of the force and horsemen with me. –
Nehemiah 2:10 And Sanaballat the Aroni and Tobia the slave, the Ammoni, heard, and it became evil to them that a man had come to seek good for the sons of Israel.
Nehemiah 2:11 And I came into Jerusalem and was there three days.
Nehemiah 2:12 And I arose at night, I and a few men with me; and I did not report to a man what God puts into my heart to do with Israel, and there is no beast with me except the beast upon which I ride.
Nehemiah 2:13 And I went out by the gate of the golela and toward the mouth of the spring of the figs and to the gate of the dung, and I was breaking in the wall of Jerusalem which they themselves pull down, and her gates were consumed by fire.
Nehemiah 2:14 And I passed to the gate of Ain and into the king's pool, and there was no place for the beast beneath me to pass through.
Nehemiah 2:15 And I was going up on the wall of the torrent at night, and I was breaking in the wall. And I was at the gate of the ravine and returned.
Nehemiah 2:16 And those guarding did not know what I went for and what I do, and to the Jews and to the priests and to those honored and to the generals and to the remaining ones doing the works, until then I did not report it.
Nehemiah 2:17 And I said to them, You see the evil in which we are in it, how Jerusalem is desolate and her gates were given to fire; come, and let us rebuild the wall of Jerusalem, and we will no longer be a reproach.
Nehemiah 2:18 And I reported to them the hand of God, which is good upon me, and the king's words which he said to me, and I said, Let us arise and build. And their hands were strengthened for good. –
Nehemiah 2:19 And Sanaballat the Aroni and Tobia the slave, the Ammoni, and Gesam the Arabi heard and laughed at us and came against us and said, What is this matter which you do? Are you rebelling against the king?
Nehemiah 2:20 And I returned a word to them and said to them, The God of heaven, he himself will give us success, and we are his clean slaves, and we will build; and for you there is no portion and righteousness and memorial in Jerusalem.

## Chapter 3

Nehemiah 3:1 And Elisoub the great priest and his brothers the priests arose and built the sheep gate; they themselves sanctified it and set up its doors, and as far as the tower of the hundred they sanctified, as far as the tower of Ananeel,
Nehemiah 3:2 and at the hands of sons of men of Jericho, and at the hands of sons of Zakchour son of Amari.
Nehemiah 3:3 And the sons of Asana built the fish gate; they themselves roofed it and set up its doors and its locks and its bars.
Nehemiah 3:4 And at their hand, from Ramoth, a son of Ouria son of Akos held firm. And at their hand Mosollam son of Barachiou son of Masezebel held firm. And at their hand Sadok son of Baana held firm.
Nehemiah 3:5 And at their hand the Thekoin held firm, and adoriem did not bring their neck into their service.
Nehemiah 3:6 And Joida son of Phasek and Mesoulam son of Basodia made firm the gate of Isana; they themselves roofed it and set up its doors and its locks and its bars.
Nehemiah 3:8 And at their hand Ananias son of Rokeim made firm, and they left Jerusalem as far as the broad wall.
Nehemiah 3:9 And at their hand Raphaia, ruler of half the district of Jerusalem, made firm.
Nehemiah 3:10 And at their hand Jedaia son of Eromaph made firm, also opposite his house. And at his hand Atous son of Asbania made firm.
Nehemiah 3:11 And second, Melchias son of Eram and Asoub son of Phaathmoab made firm, also as far as the tower of the thannourim.
Nehemiah 3:12 And at his hand Saloum son of Alloes, ruler of half the district of Jerusalem, made firm, he and his daughters.
Nehemiah 3:13 Anoun and those dwelling in Zano made firm the gate of the ravine; they themselves built it and set up its doors and its locks and its bars, and a thousand cubits in the wall as far as the gate of the dung.
Nehemiah 3:14 And Melchia son of Rechab, ruler of the district of Bethacharm, made firm the gate of the dung, he and his sons, and they covered it and set up its doors and its locks and its bars.
Nehemiah 3:15 And the wall of the pool of the fleeces, at the king's shearing, and as far as the stairs descending from the city of David.
Nehemiah 3:16 Behind him Neemias son of Azabouch, ruler of half the district of Bethsour, made firm as far as the garden of David's tomb and as far as the pool that had been made and as far as Bethanggabarim.
Nehemiah 3:17 Behind him the Levites made firm, Raoum son of Bani. At his hand Asabia, ruler of half the district of Keila, made firm for his district.
Nehemiah 3:18 After him their brothers made firm, Beni son of Enadad, ruler of half the district of Keila.
Nehemiah 3:19 And at his hand Azour son of Jesus, ruler of Masphe, made firm a second measure of the tower of the ascent adjoining the corner.
Nehemiah 3:20 After him Barouch son of Zabou made firm a second measure, from the corner as far as the door of Bethelisoub the great priest.
Nehemiah 3:21 After him Meramoth son of Ouria son of Akos made firm a second measure, from the door of Bethelisoub as far as the end of Bethelisoub.
Nehemiah 3:22 And after him the priests, men of Achechar, made firm.
Nehemiah 3:23 And after him Benjamin and Asoub made firm opposite their house. After him Azaria son of Maasea son of Anania made firm beside his house.
Nehemiah 3:24 After him Bani son of Enadad made firm a second measure, from Bethazaria as far as the corner and as far as the bend,
Nehemiah 3:25 Phalal son of Euzai opposite the corner, and the tower projecting from the king's house, the upper one belonging to the court of the guard. And after him Phadaia son of Phoros.
Nehemiah 3:26 And the nathinim were dwelling in Ophal as far as the garden of the water gate eastward, and the projecting tower.
Nehemiah 3:27 After him the Thekoin made firm a second measure opposite the great projecting tower and as far as the wall of Ophla.
Nehemiah 3:28 Above the gate of the horses the priests made firm, each man opposite his house.
Nehemiah 3:29 After him Saddouk son of Emmer made firm opposite his house. And after him Samaia son of Sechenia, keeper of the gate of the east, made firm.
Nehemiah 3:30 After him Anania son of Selemia and Anoum son of Seleph, the sixth, made firm a second measure. After him Mesoulam son of Barchia made firm opposite his treasury.
Nehemiah 3:31 After him Melchia son of Saraphi made firm as far as Bethanathinim, and the dealers in small wares opposite the gate of Maphekad and as far as the ascent of the bend.
Nehemiah 3:32 And between the ascent of the sheep gate the smiths and the dealers in small wares made firm.
Nehemiah 3:33 And it happened, when Sanaballat heard that we are building the wall, it was evil to him, and he was greatly angered and laughed at the Jews.
Nehemiah 3:34 And he said before his brothers, Is this the power of Somoron, that these Jews build their own city?
Nehemiah 3:35 And Tobias the Ammanite came beside him, and they said to one another, Surely they will not sacrifice or eat at their place? Will not a fox go up and pull down their wall of stones? –
Nehemiah 3:36 Hear, our God, for we became an object of mockery, and turn their reproach upon their head, and give them over to mockery in a land of captivity,
Nehemiah 3:37 and do not cover over lawlessness.

## Chapter 4

Nehemiah 4:1 And it happened, when Sanaballat and Tobia and the Arabs and the Ammanites heard that growth had risen on the walls of Jerusalem, that the breaches began to be blocked up, it appeared very evil to them;
Nehemiah 4:2 and they all gathered together to come to array themselves for battle in Jerusalem.
Nehemiah 4:3 And we prayed to our God and stationed advance guards against them day and night because of them.
Nehemiah 4:4 And Judah said, The strength of the enemies was broken, and the loose earth is much, and we will not be able to build in the wall.
Nehemiah 4:5 And those afflicting us said, They will not know and will not see until we come into their midst and murder them and stop the work.
Nehemiah 4:6 And it happened, when the Jews dwelling beside them came and said to us, They are coming up against us from all the places,
Nehemiah 4:7 then I stationed men in the lowest parts of the place behind the wall in the sheltered places, and I stationed the people by communities with their swords, their spears and their bows.
Nehemiah 4:8 And I saw and arose and said to those honored and to the generals and to the remaining people, Do not fear before them; remember our great and fearsome God, and array yourselves for battle for your brothers, your sons and your daughters, your wives and your houses.
Nehemiah 4:9 And it happened, when our enemies heard that it was known to us, and God scattered their counsel, we all returned to the wall, each man to his work.
Nehemiah 4:10 And it happened, from that day half of those shaken out were doing the work, and half of them were holding out, and spears and shields and the bows and the breastplates and the rulers were behind the whole house of Judah,
Nehemiah 4:11 of those building in the wall. And those lifting with the carrying apparatus were with weapons; with one hand he was doing the work itself, and one was holding the missile.
Nehemiah 4:12 And the builders, each man girded with his sword upon his loin, were building, and the one sounding the horn was beside him.
Nehemiah 4:13 And I said to those honored and to the rulers and to the remaining people, The work is broad and great, and we are scattered upon the wall, each man far from his brother;
Nehemiah 4:14 in whatever place you hear the sound of the horn, there you shall gather to us, and our God will fight for us.
Nehemiah 4:15 And we were doing the work, and half of them were holding the spears, from the rising of dawn until the coming out of the stars.
Nehemiah 4:16 And at that time I said to the people, Lodge in the midst of Jerusalem, and let the night be for you an advance guard and the day work.
Nehemiah 4:17 And I was there, and the men of the advance guard were behind me, and there was not a man among us taking off his garments.

## Chapter 5

Nehemiah 5:1 And there was a great cry of the people and their wives against their brothers the Jews.
Nehemiah 5:2 And there were some saying, With our sons and with our daughters we are many; and we will take grain and eat and live.
Nehemiah 5:3 And there are some saying, Our fields and our vineyards and our houses, we pledge; and we will take grain and eat.
Nehemiah 5:4 And there are some saying, We borrowed silver for the king's taxes, our fields and our vineyards and our houses;
Nehemiah 5:5 and now our flesh is like the flesh of our brothers, our sons like their sons; and behold, we subject our sons and our daughters to oppression as slaves, and some of our daughters are being oppressed, and there is no power in our hands, and our fields and our vineyards belong to those honored. –
Nehemiah 5:6 And I was greatly grieved when I heard their cry and these words.
Nehemiah 5:7 And my heart took counsel within me, and I contended with those honored and the rulers and said to them, By exaction you exact, each man from his brother. And I set a great assembly against them
Nehemiah 5:8 and said to them, We have acquired our brothers the Jews who are sold to the nations, of our own free will; and do you sell your brothers? And they were silent and did not find a word.
Nehemiah 5:9 And I said, The matter which you do is not good; not so, in the fear of our God you shall go away from the reproach of the nations, our enemies.
Nehemiah 5:10 And my brothers and my acquaintances and I placed silver and grain among them; let us abandon this exaction, then.
Nehemiah 5:11 Return to them, then, as of today, their fields, their vineyards, their olive trees and their houses; and from the silver bring out to them the grain and the wine and the oil.
Nehemiah 5:12 And they said, We will give back and will not seek anything from them; thus we will do, as you say. And I called the priests and made them swear to act according to this word.
Nehemiah 5:13 And I shook out my mantle and said, Thus may God shake out every man who will not establish this word, from his house and from his labor, and thus he shall be shaken out and empty. And the whole assembly said, Amen, and they praised the Lord; and the people did this thing.
Nehemiah 5:14 From the day on which he commanded me to be their ruler in the land of Judah, from the twentieth year and until the thirty-second year for Arthasastha, twelve years, I and my brothers did not eat their forced levy;
Nehemiah 5:15 and the former forced levies, which before me they imposed heavily upon them, and they took from them in bread and in wine, in addition silver, forty didrachms, and those of theirs shaken out exercise authority over the people, and I did not act so because of fear of God.
Nehemiah 5:16 And in the work of the wall of these I did not take hold; I did not acquire a field; and all those gathered were there for the work.
Nehemiah 5:17 And the Jews, a hundred and fifty men, and those coming to us from the nations around us were at my table.
Nehemiah 5:18 And what was prepared for one day was one calf and six choice sheep, and a young goat was prepared for me, and at intervals of ten days, among all things, wine in abundance; and with these things I did not seek bread of the forced levy, for the service was heavy upon this people. –
Nehemiah 5:19 Remember for me, God, for good, all that I did for this people.

## Chapter 6

Nehemiah 6:1 And it happened, when it was heard by Sanaballat and Tobia and Gesam the Arabi and the remaining ones of our enemies that I built the wall, no breath was left in them. Until that time I had not set doors in the gates.
Nehemiah 6:2 And Sanaballat and Gesam sent to me, saying, Come, and let us gather together in the villages in the plain of Ono; and they were considering doing evil to me.
Nehemiah 6:3 And I sent messengers to them, saying, I am doing a great work and will not be able to go down, lest the work stop; when I complete it, I will go down to you.
Nehemiah 6:4 And they sent to me according to this word, and I sent to them according to these things.
Nehemiah 6:5 And Sanaballat sent to me his servant, and an opened letter in his hand.
Nehemiah 6:6 And it was written in it, It was heard among nations that you and the Jews consider rebelling; for this reason you build the wall, and you become their king;
Nehemiah 6:7 and in addition to these things you stationed prophets for yourself, so that you may sit in Jerusalem as king in Judah; and now these words will be reported to the king; and now come, let us take counsel together.
Nehemiah 6:8 And I sent to him, saying, It did not happen according to these words which you say, for from your heart you fabricate them.
Nehemiah 6:9 For they all frighten us, saying, Their hands will grow slack from this work, and it will not be done; and now I strengthened my hands.
Nehemiah 6:10 And I entered into the house of Semei son of Dalaia son of Meetabel – and he was confined – and he said, Let us gather into the house of God, into its midst, and close its doors, for they are coming at night to murder you.
Nehemiah 6:11 And I said, Who is the man who will enter into the house and live?
Nehemiah 6:12 And I recognized, and behold, God did not send him, for the prophecy was a word against me, and Tobias and Sanaballat hired
Nehemiah 6:13 a crowd against me, so that I might fear and do thus and sin and become an evil name for them, so that they might reproach me. –
Nehemiah 6:14 Remember, God, for Tobia and Sanaballat according to these deeds of his, and for Noadia the prophet and the remaining prophets who were frightening me.
Nehemiah 6:15 And the wall was completed on the twenty-fifth of Eloul, in fifty-two days.
Nehemiah 6:16 And it happened, when all our enemies heard, all the nations around us feared, and fear fell greatly in their eyes, and they knew that it came about from our God for this work to be completed. –
Nehemiah 6:17 And in those days letters from many honored men of Judah were going to Tobia, and those of Tobia were coming to them,
Nehemiah 6:18 for many in Judah were bound by oath to him, for he was son-in-law of Sechenia son of Erae, and Joanan his son took the daughter of Mesoulam son of Barachia as wife.
Nehemiah 6:19 And they were saying his words to me and carrying out my words to him, and Tobias sent letters to frighten me.

## Chapter 7

Nehemiah 7:1 And it happened, when the wall was built, I set up the doors, and the gatekeepers and those singing and the Levites were appointed.
Nehemiah 7:2 And I gave orders to Anania my brother and to Anania, ruler of the bira in Jerusalem, for he was like a truthful man and one fearing God beyond many,
Nehemiah 7:3 and I said to them, The gates of Jerusalem shall not be opened until the sun is up, and while they are still watching, let the doors be closed and wedged shut; and station advance guards from those dwelling in Jerusalem, each man at his guard post and each man opposite his house.
Nehemiah 7:4 And the city was broad and great, and the people few in it, and there were no houses built.
Nehemiah 7:5 And God put it into my heart, and I gathered those honored and the rulers and the people into companies; and I found a book of the company, those who went up among the first, and I found written in it,
Nehemiah 7:6 And these are sons of the country who went up from the captivity of the exiled community which Nabouchodonosor king of Babylon exiled, and they returned to Jerusalem and to Judah, each man to his city,
Nehemiah 7:7 with Zorobabel and Jesus and Neemias, Azaria, Daemia, Naemani, Mardochaios, Balsan, Maspharath, Esdras, Bagoi, Naoum, Baana, Masphar. Men of the people Israel:
Nehemiah 7:8 sons of Phoros, two thousand one hundred and seventy-two.
