Nehemiah 7:60 All the nathinim and sons of Solomon's slaves, three hundred and ninety-two. –
Nehemiah 7:61 And these went up from Thelmeleth, Aresa, Charoub, Eron, Jemer, and could not report the houses of their ancestral families and their seed, whether they are from Israel:
Nehemiah 7:62 sons of Dalaia, sons of Tobia, sons of Nekoda, six hundred and forty-two.
Nehemiah 7:63 And from the priests: sons of Ebia, sons of Akos, sons of Berzelli, for he took wives from the daughters of Berzelli the Galaadite and was called by their name;
Nehemiah 7:64 these sought their record of the company, and it was not found, and they were ἠγχιστεύθησαν [sense uncertain] from the priesthood,
Nehemiah 7:65 and Athersatha said that they should not eat from the holy of holies until the priest arises to enlighten. –
Nehemiah 7:66 And the whole assembly became as one, forty-two thousand three hundred and sixty,
Nehemiah 7:67 besides their slaves and their female servants, these being seven thousand three hundred and thirty-seven; and male singers and female singers, two hundred and forty-five;
Nehemiah 7:68 horses, seven hundred and thirty-six; mules, two hundred and forty-five;
Nehemiah 7:69 camels, four hundred and thirty-five; donkeys, six thousand seven hundred and twenty. –
Nehemiah 7:70 And some of the chiefs of the ancestral families gave for the work to Neemias, into the treasury, a thousand gold pieces, fifty bowls and thirty chothonoth of the priests.
Nehemiah 7:71 And some of the chiefs of the ancestral families gave into the treasury of the work twenty thousand of gold and two thousand two hundred minas of silver,
Nehemiah 7:72 and the remaining people gave twenty thousand of gold and two thousand two hundred minas of silver and sixty-seven chothonoth of the priests. –
Nehemiah 7:73 And the priests and the Levites and the gatekeepers and those singing and those from the people and the nathinim and all Israel settled in their cities. And the seventh month arrived – and the sons of Israel were in their cities –

## Chapter 8

Nehemiah 8:1 and all the people gathered as one man into the broad space in front of the water gate. And they told Esdras the scribe to bring the book of the law of Moses, which the Lord commanded Israel.
Nehemiah 8:2 And Esdras the priest brought the law before the assembly, from man to woman, and everyone understanding to hear, on the first day of the seventh month,
Nehemiah 8:3 and he read in it from the hour when the sun shines through until the middle of the day, before the men and the women, and they were understanding, and the ears of all the people were toward the book of the law.
Nehemiah 8:4 And Esdras the scribe stood upon a wooden platform, and beside him stood Mattathias and Samaias and Ananias and Ouria and Elkia and Maasaia on his right, and on the left Phadaias and Misael and Melchias and Osam and Asabdana and Zacharias and Mosollam.
Nehemiah 8:5 And Esdras opened the book before all the people – for he was above the people – and it happened, when he opened it, all the people stood.
Nehemiah 8:6 And Esdras blessed the Lord, the great God, and all the people answered and said, Amen, lifting their hands, and they bent down and worshiped the Lord upon their face on the earth.
Nehemiah 8:7 And Jesus and Banaias and Sarabia were instructing the people in the law, and the people were at their station.
Nehemiah 8:8 And they read in the book of the law of God, and Esdras taught and explained distinctly in knowledge of the Lord, and the people understood in the reading. –
Nehemiah 8:9 And Neemias and Esdras the priest and scribe and the Levites instructing the people spoke and said to all the people, The day is holy to the Lord our God; do not mourn or weep; for all the people were weeping when they heard the words of the law.
Nehemiah 8:10 And he said to them, Go, eat rich foods and drink sweet drinks and send portions to those who do not have, for the day is holy to our Lord; and do not fall apart, for it is your strength.
Nehemiah 8:11 And the Levites were quieting all the people, saying, Be silent, for the day is holy, and do not fall down.
Nehemiah 8:12 And all the people went away to eat and drink and send portions and make great rejoicing, for they understood the words which he made known to them.
Nehemiah 8:13 And on the second day the rulers of the ancestral families for all the people, the priests and the Levites, gathered to Esdras the scribe to attend to all the words of the law.
Nehemiah 8:14 And they found written in the law which the Lord commanded Moses, that the sons of Israel should dwell in tents during a feast in the seventh month,
Nehemiah 8:15 and that they should signal with trumpets in all their cities and in Jerusalem. And Esdras said, Go out to the mountain and bring olive leaves and leaves of cypress trees and myrtle leaves and palm leaves and leaves of a dense tree, to make tents according to what is written.
Nehemiah 8:16 And the people went out and brought them and made tents for themselves, each man upon his roof, and in their courts and in the courts of the house of God and in the squares of the city and as far as the gate of Ephraim.
Nehemiah 8:17 And the whole assembly, those returning from the captivity, made tents and settled in tents; for from the days of Jesus son of Naue the sons of Israel had not done so until that day; and there was great rejoicing.
Nehemiah 8:18 And he read in the book of the law of God day by day, from the first day until the last day; and they held a feast for seven days, and on the eighth day a closing observance according to the judgment.

## Chapter 9

Nehemiah 9:1 And on the twenty-fourth day of this month the sons of Israel gathered in fasting and in sackcloth.
Nehemiah 9:2 And the sons of Israel separated themselves from every foreign son and stood and confessed their sins and the lawless deeds of their fathers.
Nehemiah 9:3 And they stood at their station and read in the book of the law of the Lord their God, and they were confessing to the Lord and worshiping the Lord their God.
Nehemiah 9:4 And on the ascent of the Levites stood Jesus and sons of Kadmiel, Sachania son of Sarabia, sons of Chanani, and they cried with a great voice to the Lord their God.
Nehemiah 9:5 And the Levites Jesus and Kadmiel said, Arise, bless the Lord your God from age to age, and they will bless the name of your glory and exalt it above every blessing and praise.
Nehemiah 9:6 And Esdras said, You yourself alone are Lord; you made heaven and the heaven of heaven and all their array, the earth and all that is in it, the seas and all that is in them, and you give life to all things, and the armies of the heavens worship you.
Nehemiah 9:7 You are the Lord God; you made your choice in Abram and brought him out of the country of the Chaldeans and placed upon him the name Abraham;
Nehemiah 9:8 and you found his heart faithful before you and made a covenant with him to give him the land of the Chananites and Chettites and Amorrites and Pherezites and Jebousites and Gergesites, and to his seed; and you established your words, for you are righteous.
Nehemiah 9:9 And you saw the humiliation of our fathers in Egypt and heard their cry at the Red Sea.
Nehemiah 9:10 And you gave signs in Egypt, in Pharaoh and in all his servants and in all the people of his land, for you knew that they acted arrogantly against them, and you made a name for yourself, as this day.
Nehemiah 9:11 And you broke open the sea before them, and they passed through the midst of the sea on dry ground, and those pursuing them you threw into the deep like a stone in mighty water.
Nehemiah 9:12 And in a pillar of cloud you guided them by day, and in a pillar of fire by night, to light for them the way in which they will travel.
Nehemiah 9:13 And you descended upon Mount Sina and spoke to them from heaven and gave them upright judgments and laws of truth, good ordinances and commandments.
Nehemiah 9:14 And you made known to them your holy sabbath; commandments and ordinances and law you commanded them by the hand of Moses your slave.
Nehemiah 9:15 And you gave them bread from heaven for their lack of grain and brought out water from rock for them for their thirst. And you told them to enter to inherit the land concerning which you stretched out your hand to give it to them.
Nehemiah 9:16 And they and our fathers acted arrogantly and hardened their neck and did not hear your commandments;
Nehemiah 9:17 and they refused to listen and did not remember your wonders which you did with them, and they hardened their neck and gave a beginning to return to their slavery in Egypt. And you are a merciful and compassionate God, long-suffering and abundant in mercy, and you did not abandon them.
Nehemiah 9:18 And moreover they also made themselves a cast calf and said, These are the gods who brought us out of Egypt; and they made great provocations to anger.
Nehemiah 9:19 And you in your many compassions did not abandon them in the wilderness; you did not turn away from them the pillar of cloud by day to guide them in the way, and the pillar of fire by night to light for them the way in which they will travel.
Nehemiah 9:20 And you gave your good spirit to instruct them, and you did not withhold your manna from their mouth, and you gave them water for their thirst.
Nehemiah 9:21 And forty years you nourished them in the wilderness; they did not lack; their garments did not grow old, and their feet did not split open.
Nehemiah 9:22 And you gave them kingdoms and peoples and divided them for them, and they inherited the land of Seon king of Esebon and the land of Og king of Basan.
Nehemiah 9:23 And you multiplied their sons like the stars of heaven and brought them into the land which you spoke of to their fathers, and they inherited it.
Nehemiah 9:24 And you wiped out before them those dwelling in the land of the Chananites and gave them into their hands, and their kings and the peoples of the land, to do to them as was pleasing before them.
Nehemiah 9:25 And they seized high cities and inherited houses full of all good things, hewn pits, vineyards and olive groves and every tree for food in abundance; and they ate and were filled and grew fat and lived luxuriously in your great goodness.
Nehemiah 9:26 And they changed and departed from you and threw your law behind their body and killed your prophets, who testified among them to turn them toward you, and they made great provocations to anger.
Nehemiah 9:27 And you gave them into the hand of those afflicting them, and they afflicted them; and they cried out to you at the time of their affliction, and you heard from your heaven and in your great compassions gave them saviors and saved them from the hand of those afflicting them.
Nehemiah 9:28 And when they rested, they turned back to do evil before you; and you abandoned them into the hands of their enemies, and they ruled over them. And again they cried out to you, and you listened from heaven and rescued them in your many compassions.
Nehemiah 9:29 And you testified to them to turn them to your law, and they did not hear, but in your commandments and in your judgments they sinned, which, if a man does them, he will live in them; and they gave a disobedient back and hardened their neck and did not hear.
Nehemiah 9:30 And you prolonged matters over them for many years and testified to them by your spirit through the hand of your prophets; and they did not give ear, and you gave them into the hand of peoples of the land.
Nehemiah 9:31 And you in your many compassions did not make an end of them and did not abandon them, for you are strong and merciful and compassionate.
Nehemiah 9:32 And now, our God, the strong, the great, the mighty and the fearsome, keeping your covenant and your mercy, let not all the hardship be made little before you which found us and our kings and our rulers and our priests and our prophets and our fathers, and among all your people, from the days of kings of Assour and until this day.
Nehemiah 9:33 And you are righteous in all things coming upon us, for you acted in truth, and we sinned.
Nehemiah 9:34 And our kings and our rulers and our priests and our fathers did not do your law and did not attend to your commandments and your testimonies which you testified to them.
Nehemiah 9:35 And they in your kingdom and in your abundant goodness which you gave them, and in the broad and rich land which you gave before them, did not serve you and did not turn away from their evil practices.
Nehemiah 9:36 Behold, today we are slaves, and the land which you gave our fathers to eat its fruit,
Nehemiah 9:37 is for the kings whom you gave over us in our sins, and they exercise authority over our bodies and over our beasts as is pleasing to them, and we are in great affliction.

## Chapter 10

Nehemiah 10:1 And in all these things we make a pledge of faithfulness and write, and all our rulers, our Levites, our priests affix seals.
Nehemiah 10:2 And among those sealing were Neemias son of Achalia and Sedekias
Nehemiah 10:3 son of Saraia, and Azaria and Jermia,
Nehemiah 10:4 Phasour, Amaria, Melchia,
Nehemiah 10:5 Atous, Sebani, Malouch,
Nehemiah 10:6 Iram, Meramoth, Abdia,
Nehemiah 10:7 Daniel, Ganathon, Barouch,
Nehemiah 10:8 Mesoulam, Abia, Miamin,
Nehemiah 10:9 Maazia, Belgai, Samaia; these were priests;

Nehemiah 10:16 Bani, Asgad, Bebai,
Nehemiah 10:17 Edania, Bagoi, Edin,
Nehemiah 10:18 Ater, Ezekia, Azour,

Nehemiah 10:21 Magaphes, Mesoulam, Ezir,
Nehemiah 10:22 Mesozebel, Saddouk, Jeddoua,
Nehemiah 10:23 Phaltia, Anan, Anaia,
Nehemiah 10:24 Osee, Anania, Asoub,
Nehemiah 10:25 Aloes, Phalai, Sobek,
Nehemiah 10:26 Raoum, Esabana, Maasaia
Nehemiah 10:27 and Aia, Ainan, Enan,
Nehemiah 10:28 Malouch, Eram, Baana.
Nehemiah 10:29 And the remaining people, the priests, the Levites, the gatekeepers, those singing, the nathinim and everyone coming from peoples of the land toward the law of God, their wives, their sons, their daughters, everyone knowing and understanding,
Nehemiah 10:30 were strengthening themselves against their brothers, cursed them and entered into a curse and into an oath to walk in the law of God which was given by the hand of Moses the slave of God, and to keep and do all the commandments of our Lord and his judgments,
Nehemiah 10:31 and not to give our daughters to the peoples of the land, and we will not take their daughters for our sons.
Nehemiah 10:32 And the peoples of the land who bring merchandise and every article for sale on the sabbath day to sell, we do not buy from them on the sabbath and on a holy day. And we will release the seventh year and the exaction of every hand.
Nehemiah 10:33 And we will establish commandments upon ourselves, to impose upon ourselves the giving of a third of the didrachm each year for the service of the house of our God,
Nehemiah 10:34 for bread of the presence and the continual sacrifice and for the continual whole burnt offering of the sabbaths, of the new moons, for the feasts and for the holy things, and the offerings for sin to make atonement for Israel, and for works of the house of our God.
Nehemiah 10:35 And we cast lots concerning the lot of wood-bearing, the priests and the Levites and the people, to bring it into the house of our God, by house of our ancestral families, at appointed times, year by year, to burn upon the altar of the Lord our God, as it is written in the law,
Nehemiah 10:36 and to bring the first produce of our land and the first produce of the fruit of every tree, year by year, into the house of the Lord,
Nehemiah 10:37 and the firstborn of our sons and of our beasts, as it is written in the law, and the firstborn of our cattle and our flocks, to bring into the house of our God to the priests ministering in the house of our God.
Nehemiah 10:38 And the first portion of our grain and the fruit of every tree, of wine and of oil, we will bring to the priests into the treasury of the house of God; and a tenth of our land to the Levites. And the Levites themselves collect tithes in all the cities of our service,
Nehemiah 10:39 and the priest, a son of Aaron, shall be with the Levite at the Levite's tithe, and the Levites will bring up the tenth of the tenth into the house of our God, into the treasuries, into the house of God.
Nehemiah 10:40 For into the treasuries the sons of Israel and the sons of Levi will bring the first portions of grain and of wine and of oil, and there are the holy vessels and the priests who minister and the gatekeepers and those singing. And we will not abandon the house of our God.

## Chapter 11

Nehemiah 11:1 And the rulers of the people settled in Jerusalem, and the remaining people cast lots to bring one out of ten to settle in Jerusalem, the holy city, and nine portions in the cities.
Nehemiah 11:2 And the people blessed all the men volunteering to settle in Jerusalem.
Nehemiah 11:3 And these are the rulers of the country who settled in Jerusalem; and in the cities of Judah they settled, each man in his possession in their cities, Israel, the priests and the Levites and the nathinaians and the sons of Solomon's slaves;
Nehemiah 11:4 and in Jerusalem some of the sons of Judah and some of the sons of Benjamin settled. – From the sons of Judah: Athaia son of Azaia son of Zacharia son of Amaria son of Saphatia son of Malelel, and from the sons of Phares.
Nehemiah 11:5 And Maasia son of Barouch son of Chalaza son of Ozia son of Adaia son of Jorib son of Thezia son of the Seloni.
Nehemiah 11:6 All the sons of Phares dwelling in Jerusalem, four hundred and sixty-eight men of strength. –
Nehemiah 11:7 And these are sons of Benjamin: Selo son of Mesoulam son of Joad son of Phadaia son of Kolia son of Masaia son of Aithiel son of Jesia;
Nehemiah 11:8 and behind him Gebi, Seli, nine hundred and twenty-eight.

Nehemiah 11:11 Saraia son of Elkia son of Mesoulam son of Saddouk son of Marioth son of Aitob, opposite the house of God.

Nehemiah 11:17 and Mathania son of Micha and Obed son of Samoui,

Nehemiah 11:23 for the king's commandment was upon them.
Nehemiah 11:24 And Pathaia son of Baseza was at the king's hand for every matter concerning the people. –
Nehemiah 11:25 And toward the settlements in their field. And some of the sons of Judah settled in Kariatharbok
Nehemiah 11:26 and in Jesou
Nehemiah 11:27 and in Beersabee,
Nehemiah 11:30 and their settlements, Lachis and her fields; and they encamped in Beersabee.

## Chapter 12

Nehemiah 12:1 And these are the priests and the Levites going up with Zorobabel son of Salathiel and Jesus: Saraia, Jermia, Esdras,
Nehemiah 12:2 Amaria, Malouch,
Nehemiah 12:3 Sechenia;
Nehemiah 12:7 these were rulers of the priests and their brothers in the days of Jesus. –
Nehemiah 12:8 And the Levites: Jesou, Banoui, Kadmiel, Sarabia, Judah, Machania; over the hands, he and his brothers,
Nehemiah 12:9 for the daily divisions.
Nehemiah 12:10 And Jesus begot Joakim, and Joakim begot Eliasib, and Eliasib, Jodae,
Nehemiah 12:11 and Jodae begot Jonathan, and Jonathan begot Jadou.
Nehemiah 12:12 And in the days of Joakim, his brothers the priests and the rulers of the ancestral families: for Saraia, Maraia; for Jermia, Anania;
Nehemiah 12:13 for Esdras, Mesoulam; for Amaria, Joanan;
Nehemiah 12:14 for Malouch, Jonathan; for Sechenia, Joseph;
Nehemiah 12:15 for Arem, Adnas; for Marioth, Elkai;
Nehemiah 12:16 for Addai, Zacharias; for Ganathon, Mosollam;
Nehemiah 12:17 for Abia, Zechri; for Benjamin, at times, for Pheleti;
Nehemiah 12:18 for Balga, Samoue; for Semeia, Jonathan;
Nehemiah 12:19 for Joiarib, Maththanai; for Idia, Ozi;
Nehemiah 12:20 for Sallai, Kallai; for Amouk, Abed;
Nehemiah 12:21 for Elkia, Asabias; for Jedeiou, Nathanael. –
Nehemiah 12:22 The Levites in the days of Eliasib, Joada and Joanan and Idoua were recorded as rulers of ancestral families, and the priests in the reign of Darius the Persian;
Nehemiah 12:23 sons of Levi, rulers of the ancestral families, recorded in the book of words of the days, even until the days of Joanan son of Elisoub.
Nehemiah 12:24 And rulers of the Levites: Asabia and Sarabia and Jesou and sons of Kadmiel and their brothers opposite them, to sing hymns and praise by the commandment of David the man of God, daily division against daily division,
Nehemiah 12:25 when I gathered the gatekeepers,
Nehemiah 12:26 in the days of Joakim son of Jesus son of Josedek and in the days of Neemias, and Esdras the priest, the scribe.
Nehemiah 12:27 And at the dedication of the wall of Jerusalem they sought the Levites in their places to bring them into Jerusalem to make a dedication and rejoicing with thodatha and with songs, sounding cymbals, and psalteries and lyres.
Nehemiah 12:28 And the sons of those singing gathered, also from the surrounding district round about into Jerusalem, and from settlements
Nehemiah 12:29 and from fields; for those singing built settlements for themselves in Jerusalem.
Nehemiah 12:30 And the priests and the Levites were cleansed, and they cleansed the people and the gatekeepers and the wall.
Nehemiah 12:31 And I brought up the rulers of Judah upon the wall and stationed two great ones for praise, and they passed on the right upon the wall of the dung,
Nehemiah 12:32 and Osaia and half the rulers of Judah went behind them,
Nehemiah 12:33 and Azarias, Esdras and Mesoulam,
Nehemiah 12:34 Judah and Benjamin and Samaia and Jermia,
Nehemiah 12:35 and from the sons of the priests, with trumpets, Zacharias son of Jonathan son of Samaia son of Mathania son of Michaia son of Zakchour son of Asaph,
Nehemiah 12:36 and his brothers Samaia and Oziel, to praise with songs of David the man of God, and Esdras the scribe in front of them;
Nehemiah 12:37 at the gate of ain opposite them they went up upon the stairs of the city of David, at the ascent of the wall above the house of David and as far as the water gate eastward. –
Nehemiah 12:38 And the second one for praise was going to meet them, and I behind it, and half the people upon the wall above the tower of the thennourim and as far as the broad wall,
Nehemiah 12:39 and above the gate of Ephraim and to the gate of isana and to the fish gate and at the tower of Ananeel and as far as the sheep gate, and they stood at the gate of the guard.
Nehemiah 12:40 And the two of praise stood in the house of God, and I and half the generals with me,
Nehemiah 12:41 and the priests Eliakim, Maasias, Benjamin, Michaias, Elioenai, Zacharias, Ananias, with trumpets,
Nehemiah 12:42 and Maasias and Semeias and Eleazar and Ozi and Joanan and Melchias and Ailam and Ezour, and those singing were heard and were appointed.
Nehemiah 12:43 And on that day they sacrificed great sacrifices and rejoiced, for God made them rejoice greatly; and their wives and their children rejoiced, and the rejoicing in Jerusalem was heard from far away.
Nehemiah 12:44 And on that day they appointed men over the treasuries for the stores, the first portions and the tithes, and for the rulers of the cities gathered in them, portions for the priests and for the Levites, for there was rejoicing in Judah over the priests and over the Levites standing there.
Nehemiah 12:45 And they kept the watches of their God and the watches of purification, and those singing and the gatekeepers, according to the commandments of David and Solomon his son;
Nehemiah 12:46 for in the days of David, Asaph from the beginning was first of those singing, and a hymn and praise to God,
Nehemiah 12:47 and all Israel in the days of Zorobabel were giving portions of those singing and of the gatekeepers, a day's matter on its day, and consecrating for the Levites, and the Levites consecrating for the sons of Aaron.

## Chapter 13

Nehemiah 13:1 On that day it was read in the book of Moses in the ears of the people, and it was found written in it that Ammanites and Moabites should not enter into the assembly of God forever,
Nehemiah 13:2 for they did not meet the sons of Israel with bread and with water, and they hired Balaam against him to curse, and our God turned the curse into a blessing.
Nehemiah 13:3 And it happened, when they heard the law, every mixed person in Israel was separated.
Nehemiah 13:4 And before this Eliasib the priest, dwelling in a treasury of the house of our God, being near Tobia,
Nehemiah 13:5 made him a great treasury, and there they had formerly been putting the manaan and the frankincense and the vessels and the tenth of grain and of wine and of oil, the commandment of the Levites and of those singing and of the gatekeepers, and first portions of the priests.
Nehemiah 13:6 And during all this I was not in Jerusalem, for in the thirty-second year of Arthasastha king of Babylon I came to the king. And after the end of days I made a request of the king
Nehemiah 13:7 and came into Jerusalem. And I understood the evil which Elisoub did for Tobia, to make him a treasury in the court of the house of God.
Nehemiah 13:8 And it appeared very evil to me, and I threw all the vessels of Tobia's house outside, out of the treasury;
Nehemiah 13:9 and I spoke, and they cleansed the treasuries, and I returned there the vessels of the house of God, the manaa and the frankincense.
Nehemiah 13:10 And I knew that the portions of the Levites had not been given, and the Levites and those singing who were doing the work fled, each man to his field.
Nehemiah 13:11 And I contended with the generals and said, Why was the house of God abandoned? And I gathered them and stationed them at their station.
Nehemiah 13:12 And all Judah brought a tenth of the wheat and of the wine and of the oil into the stores,
Nehemiah 13:13 at the hand of Selemia the priest and Saddouk the scribe and Phadaia from the Levites, and at their hand Anan son of Zakchour son of Mathania, for they were reckoned faithful, to distribute to their brothers.
Nehemiah 13:14 Remember me, God, in this, and let not my mercy be wiped out, which I did in the house of the Lord God.
Nehemiah 13:15 In those days I saw in Judah people treading winepresses on the sabbath and bringing sheaves and loading them upon the donkeys, and wine and grapes and figs and every burden, and bringing them into Jerusalem on the sabbath day; and I testified on the day of their selling.
Nehemiah 13:16 And they settled in it, bringing fish and every article for sale, selling on the sabbath to the sons of Judah and in Jerusalem.
Nehemiah 13:17 And I contended with the free sons of Judah and said to them, What is this evil matter which you do and profane the sabbath day?
Nehemiah 13:18 Did not your fathers act so? And our God brought all these evils upon them and upon us and upon this city; and you add wrath upon Israel by profaning the sabbath.
Nehemiah 13:19 And it happened, when the gates of Jerusalem were set in place before the sabbath, I spoke and they closed the gates, and I said that they should not be opened until after the sabbath; and some of my young servants I stationed at the gates so that burdens should not be lifted on the sabbath day.
Nehemiah 13:20 And they all lodged and carried on selling outside Jerusalem once and twice.
Nehemiah 13:21 And I testified among them and said to them, Why do you lodge opposite the wall? If you do it a second time, I will stretch out my hand against you. From that time they did not come on the sabbath.
Nehemiah 13:22 And I told the Levites, who were cleansing themselves and coming to guard the gates, to sanctify the sabbath day. For these things remember me, God, and spare me according to the abundance of your mercy.
Nehemiah 13:23 And in those days I saw the Jews who settled Azotian, Ammanite, Moabite wives,
Nehemiah 13:24 and their sons, half speaking Azotian, and they do not know how to speak Judean,
Nehemiah 13:25 and I contended with them and cursed them and struck men among them and pulled out their hair and made them swear by God, If you give your daughters to their sons, and if you take from their daughters for your sons.
Nehemiah 13:26 Did not Solomon king of Israel sin so? And among many nations there was no king like him; and he was loved by God, and God made him king over all Israel. And the foreign wives turned even this man aside.
Nehemiah 13:27 And shall we not hear of you doing all this evil, acting faithlessly toward our God, settling foreign wives? –
Nehemiah 13:28 And from the sons of Joada, of Elisoub the great priest, son-in-law of Sanaballat the Oronite, and I drove him out from me.
Nehemiah 13:29 Remember for them, God, concerning the kinship of the priesthood and the covenant of the priesthood, and the Levites. –
Nehemiah 13:30 And I cleansed them from every foreign association and stationed daily divisions for the priests and for the Levites, each man according to his work,
Nehemiah 13:31 and the gift of the wood-bearers at appointed times and among the bakchouria. Remember me, our God, for goodness.

# Esther

The Apostolic Bible. Public domain. https://apostolic-bible.ysys9.chatgpt.site/license.html


## Chapter 1

Esther 1:1 a In the second year of the reign of Artaxerxes the great, on the first of Nisa, Mardochaios son of Jairos son of Semeios son of Kisaios, from the tribe of Benjamin, saw a dream,
Esther 1:2 a Jewish man dwelling in the city of Sousoi, a great man serving in the king's court;
Esther 1:3 and he was from the captivity which Nabouchodonosor king of Babylon took captive from Jerusalem with Jechonias king of Judea.
Esther 1:4 And this was his dream: and behold, voices and uproar, thunders and an earthquake, tumult upon the earth;
Esther 1:5 and behold, two great dragons came forward, both ready to wrestle, and their voice became great;
Esther 1:6 and at their voice every nation prepared for war, so as to wage war against a nation of righteous people.
Esther 1:7 And behold, a day of darkness and gloom, affliction and distress, maltreatment and great tumult upon the earth;
Esther 1:8 and the whole righteous nation was troubled, fearing their own evils, and they prepared to perish and cried to God.
Esther 1:9 And from their cry there came, as though from a small spring, a great river, much water;
Esther 1:1 k light and the sun rose, and the humble were exalted and devoured the glorious. –
Esther 1:2 And Mardochaios, having awakened, who had seen this dream and what God has resolved to do, held it in his heart and in every matter wished to understand it until night.
Esther 1:3 And Mardochaios rested in the court with Gabatha and Tharra, the king's two eunuchs guarding the court,
Esther 1:4 and he heard their reasonings and investigated their concerns and learned that they are preparing to lay hands upon King Artaxerxes, and he informed the king concerning them;
Esther 1:5 and the king examined the two eunuchs, and after confessing they were led away.
Esther 1:6 And the king wrote these matters as a memorial, and Mardochaios wrote concerning these matters;
Esther 1:7 and the king commanded Mardochaios to serve in the court and gave him gifts for these things.
Esther 1:8 And Aman son of Amadathos, a Bougaian, was glorious before the king; and he sought to do evil to Mardochaios and his people on behalf of the king's two eunuchs.
Esther 1:9 And it happened after these matters in the days of Artaxerxes – this Artaxerxes held sway over a hundred and twenty-seven territories from India –
Esther 1:2 in those very days, when King Artaxerxes was enthroned in the city of Sousoi,
Esther 1:3 in the third year of his reign he made a reception for his friends and the remaining nations and the glorious men of Persians and Medes and the rulers of the satraps.
Esther 1:4 And after these things, after showing them the wealth of his kingdom and the glory of the rejoicing of his wealth for a hundred and eighty days,
Esther 1:5 when the days of the wedding were fulfilled, the king made a drinking feast for the nations found in the city for six days, in the court of the king's house,
Esther 1:6 adorned with fine linen and cotton hangings stretched on fine linen and purple cords on gold and silver cubes upon pillars of Parian stone and stone; gold and silver couches upon a pavement of emerald stone and mother-of-pearl and Parian stone, and translucent coverings variously adorned with flowers, roses sprinkled round about;
Esther 1:7 gold and silver drinking cups and a little carbuncle cup set out, of thirty thousand talents; much sweet wine, which the king himself drank.
Esther 1:8 And this drinking feast did not take place according to an established law, but the king wished so and commanded the stewards to do his will and that of the people.
Esther 1:9 And Astin the queen made a drinking feast for the women in the royal quarters where King Artaxerxes was.
Esther 1:10 And on the seventh day the king, having become merry, told Aman and Bazan and Tharra and Boraze and Zatholtha and Abataza and Tharaba, the seven eunuchs who served King Artaxerxes,
Esther 1:11 to bring the queen in to him, for her to reign, and to place the diadem upon her and to show her to all the rulers and the nations, her beauty, for she was beautiful.
Esther 1:12 And Astin the queen did not heed him, to come with the eunuchs. And the king was grieved and angered
Esther 1:13 and said to his friends, Astin spoke according to these things; make, then, a law and judgment concerning this.
Esther 1:14 And Arkesaios and Sarsathaios and Malesear, the rulers of Persians and Medes, those near the king, those sitting first beside the king, approached him
Esther 1:15 and reported to him according to the laws how one must deal with Astin the queen, for she did not do what was commanded by the king through the eunuchs.
Esther 1:16 And Mouchaios said to the king and the rulers, Astin the queen wronged not the king alone, but also all the rulers and the king's leaders,
Esther 1:17 [for he also related to them the queen's words and how she contradicted the king]. As, then, she contradicted King Artaxerxes,
Esther 1:18 so today the remaining ruling women of the rulers of Persians and Medes, having heard what was said by her to the king, will likewise dare to dishonor their husbands.
Esther 1:19 If, then, it seems good to the king, let him command a royal decree, and let it be written according to the laws of Medes and Persians; and let him not act otherwise, nor let the queen enter to him any longer, and let the king give her queenship to a woman better than she.
Esther 1:20 And let the law from the king, whatever he makes, be heard in his kingdom, and thus all the women will confer honor upon their own husbands, from poor to rich.
Esther 1:21 And the word pleased the king and the rulers, and the king did as Mouchaios spoke;
Esther 1:22 and he sent into the whole kingdom, territory by territory, according to their language, so that there should be fear for them in their houses.

## Chapter 2

Esther 2:1 And after these matters the king ceased from his anger and no longer remembered Astin, remembering what she spoke and how he condemned her.
Esther 2:2 And the king's servants said, Let uncorrupted girls, beautiful in appearance, be sought for the king;
Esther 2:3 and the king will appoint village rulers in all the territories of his kingdom, and let them select virgin girls, beautiful in appearance, into the city of Sousan, into the women's quarters, and let them be handed over to the king's eunuch, the keeper of the women, and let cleansing ointment and the remaining care be given;
Esther 2:4 and the woman who pleases the king will reign instead of Astin. And the matter pleased the king, and he did so.
Esther 2:5 And there was a Jewish man in the city of Sousoi, and his name was Mardochaios son of Jairos son of Semeios son of Kisaios, from the tribe of Benjamin,
Esther 2:6 who was a captive from Jerusalem, which Nabouchodonosor king of Babylon took captive.
Esther 2:7 And he had a foster child, a daughter of Aminadab, his father's brother, and her name was Esther; and when her parents died, he brought her up for himself as a wife; and the girl was beautiful in appearance.
Esther 2:8 And when the king's ordinance was heard, many girls gathered into the city of Sousan under the hand of Gai, and Esther was brought to Gai, the keeper of the women.
Esther 2:9 And the girl pleased him and found favor before him, and he hurried to give her the cleansing ointment and the portion and the seven girls assigned to her from the royal household, and he treated her and her maids well in the women's quarters;
Esther 2:10 and Esther did not reveal her race or her homeland, for Mardochaios commanded her not to report them.
Esther 2:11 And each day Mardochaios walked about the women's court, watching what would happen to Esther.
Esther 2:12 And this was the time for a girl to enter to the king, when she completes twelve months; for thus the days of care are completed, six months being anointed with myrrh oil and six months with aromatics and with the women's cleansing ointments,
Esther 2:13 and then she enters to the king; and whatever she asks for, he will hand over to her to go in with her from the women's quarters to the royal quarters.
Esther 2:14 At evening she enters, and toward day she runs back into the second women's quarters, where Gai, the king's eunuch, the keeper of the women, is, and she no longer enters to the king unless called by name.
Esther 2:15 And when the time was fulfilled for Esther, daughter of Aminadab, the brother of Mardochaios's father, to enter to the king, she rejected none of what the eunuch, the keeper of the women, commanded her; for Esther was finding favor with all those seeing her.
Esther 2:16 And Esther entered to King Artaxerxes in the twelfth month, which is Adar, in the seventh year of his reign.
Esther 2:17 And the king fell in love with Esther, and she found favor beyond all the virgins, and he placed the women's diadem upon her.
Esther 2:18 And the king made a drinking feast for all his friends and the forces for seven days and exalted Esther's wedding and made a remission for those under his reign.
Esther 2:19 And Mardochaios was serving in the court.
Esther 2:20 And Esther did not reveal her homeland; for thus Mardochaios commanded her, to fear God and do his ordinances, as when she was with him, and Esther did not change her conduct.
Esther 2:21 And the king's two eunuchs, the chief bodyguards, were grieved because Mardochaios was promoted, and they sought to kill King Artaxerxes.
Esther 2:22 And the matter was made known to Mardochaios, and he informed Esther, and she disclosed the matters of the plot to the king.
Esther 2:23 And the king examined the two eunuchs and hanged them; and the king commanded it to be recorded as a memorial in the royal library, concerning Mardochaios's goodwill, in a commendation.

## Chapter 3

Esther 3:1 And after these things King Artaxerxes glorified Aman son of Amadathos, the Bougaian, and exalted him, and he held the first rank among all his friends.
Esther 3:2 And all those in the court bowed down to him, for thus the king commanded them to do; but Mardochaios did not bow down to him.
Esther 3:3 And those in the king's court said to Mardochaios, Mardochaios, why do you disobey what is said by the king?
Esther 3:4 Each day they spoke to him, and he did not heed them; and they informed Aman that Mardochaios opposed the king's words; and Mardochaios informed them that he is Jewish.
Esther 3:5 And Aman, recognizing that Mardochaios does not bow down to him, became very angry
Esther 3:6 and resolved to destroy all the Jews under the reign of Artaxerxes.
Esther 3:7 And he made a decree in the twelfth year of the reign of Artaxerxes and cast lots, day by day and month by month, so as to destroy the race of Mardochaios in one day, and the lot fell on the fourteenth of the month which is Adar.
Esther 3:8 And he spoke to King Artaxerxes, saying, There exists a nation dispersed among the nations in all your kingdom, and their laws are different beyond all the nations, and they disobey the king's laws, and it does not benefit the king to leave them;
Esther 3:9 if it seems good to the king, let him decree to destroy them, and I will pay into the king's treasury ten thousand talents of silver.
Esther 3:10 And the king, taking off his ring, gave it into Aman's hand to seal in accordance with what was written against the Jews.
Esther 3:11 And the king said to Aman, Keep the silver, and deal with the nation as you wish.
Esther 3:12 And the king's scribes were called in the first month on the thirteenth, and they wrote, as Aman commanded, to the generals and the rulers in every territory from India to Ethiopia, to the hundred and twenty-seven territories, and to the rulers of the nations according to their own language, by King Artaxerxes.
Esther 3:13 And it was sent by letter-bearers into the kingdom of Artaxerxes, to destroy the race of the Jews on one day of the twelfth month, which is Adar, and to plunder their possessions. –
Esther 3:13 a And this is the copy of the letter: The great King Artaxerxes writes these things to the rulers of the hundred and twenty-seven territories from India to Ethiopia and the local rulers subject to them:
Esther 3:14 Having ruled many nations and prevailed over the whole inhabited world, I wished, without being lifted up by the audacity of authority, but always conducting affairs more reasonably and with gentleness, to establish the lives of those subject to me as ever untroubled by waves, providing the kingdom as peaceful and traversable to its limits, and to renew the peace desired by all people.
Esther 3:15 And when I inquired of the counselors how this might be brought to completion, Aman, who excelled in prudence among us and was proven in unchanging goodwill and firm faithfulness and had carried off the second honor of the kingdoms,
Esther 3:16 showed us that among all the tribes throughout the inhabited world a certain hostile people has been mixed in, opposed in its laws to every nation, continually disregarding the ordinances of the kings, so as not to accept the joint government directed blamelessly by us.
Esther 3:17 Having therefore determined that this nation alone stands continually in opposition to every person, varying in a strange course of laws and ill-disposed toward our affairs, accomplishing the worst evils, even so that the kingdom should not obtain stability;
Esther 3:18 we have therefore commanded that all those indicated to you in what is written by Aman, appointed over affairs and our second father, together with wives and children, be destroyed root and all by the swords of the enemies, without any pity and sparing, on the fourteenth of the twelfth month Adar of the present year,
Esther 3:19 so that those hostile of old and now, having descended violently into Hades in one day, may provide our affairs as stable and untroubled for all subsequent time. –
Esther 3:14 And the copies of the letters were posted territory by territory, and all the nations were commanded to be ready for this day.
Esther 3:15 And the matter was hastened also into Sousan; and the king and Aman were drinking deeply, but the city was troubled.

## Chapter 4

Esther 4:1 But Mardochaios, learning what was being accomplished, tore his garments and put on sackcloth and sprinkled himself with ashes, and rushing out through the city's square, cried with a loud voice, A nation that has done no wrong is being taken away.
Esther 4:2 And he came as far as the king's gate and stood; for he was not permitted to enter the court wearing sackcloth and ashes.
Esther 4:3 And in every region where the letters were posted, there was an outcry and beating of the breast and great mourning for the Jews; they spread sackcloth and ashes for themselves.
Esther 4:4 And the queen's maids and eunuchs came in and reported to her, and she was troubled on hearing what had happened, and sent to clothe Mardochaios and remove his sackcloth, but he was not persuaded.
Esther 4:5 But Esther summoned Achrathaios, her eunuch, who attended her, and sent him to learn for her the exact matter from Mardochaios;
Esther 4:7 and Mardochaios explained to him what had happened and the promise that Aman had promised the king, of ten thousand talents for the treasury, so that he might destroy the Jews;
Esther 4:8 and he gave him the copy posted in Sousa for their destruction, to show Esther, and told him to instruct her to go in and entreat the king and petition him concerning the people: remembering the days of your humiliation, how you were reared in my hand, because Aman, who is second to the king, has spoken against us for death; call upon the Lord and speak to the king concerning us and rescue us from death.
Esther 4:9 And Achrathaios went in and spoke all these words to her.
Esther 4:10 And Esther said to Achrathaios, Go to Mardochaios and say that
Esther 4:11 All the nations of the kingdom know that every man or woman who enters to the king into the inner court uncalled has no deliverance; except that the one to whom the king extends the golden rod will be delivered; and I have not been called to enter to the king these thirty days.
Esther 4:12 And Achrathaios reported all Esther's words to Mardochaios.
Esther 4:13 And Mardochaios said to Achrathaios, Go and say to her, Esther, do not say to yourself that you alone in the kingdom will be delivered above all the Jews;
Esther 4:14 because if you refuse to listen at this time, help and shelter will come to the Jews from elsewhere, but you and your father's house will perish; and who knows whether you became queen for this time?
Esther 4:15 And Esther sent the one who had come to her away to Mardochaios, saying,
Esther 4:16 Go and assemble the Jews in Sousa, and fast for me, and neither eat nor drink for three days, night and day; and I and my maids will go without food, and then I will enter to the king contrary to the law, even if I must perish.
Esther 4:17 And Mardochaios went and did all that Esther had commanded him,
Esther 4:17 a and petitioned the Lord, remembering all the Lord's works, and said,
Esther 4:18 Lord, Lord, king who rules over all, because everything is in your authority, and there is no one opposing you when you wish to save Israel;
Esther 4:19 because you made heaven and earth and everything marveled at in the land under heaven, and you are Lord of all, and there is no one who will oppose you, the Lord.
Esther 4:20 You know everything; you know, Lord, that I did this, not bowing to the arrogant Aman, neither in insolence nor in arrogance nor in love of glory, because I was willing to kiss the soles of his feet for Israel's deliverance;
Esther 4:21 but I did this so that I might not place a man's glory above God's glory, and I will bow to no one except you, my Lord, and I will not do these things in arrogance.
Esther 4:22 And now, Lord God, king, God of Abraam, spare your people, because they look upon us for destruction and have desired to destroy your inheritance from the beginning;
Esther 4:23 do not overlook your portion, which you redeemed for yourself from the land of Egypt;
Esther 4:24 listen to my petition and be gracious to your allotted portion, and turn our mourning into feasting, so that while living we may sing your name, Lord, and do not make the mouth of those praising you disappear. –
Esther 4:25 And all Israel cried out with their strength, because their death was before their eyes.
Esther 4:17 k And Esther the queen took refuge with the Lord, seized in a struggle with death, and taking off the garments of her glory, put on garments of distress and mourning, and instead of proud perfumes filled her head with ashes and dung, and humbled her body greatly, and filled every place of her joyful adornment with her tangled hair, and petitioned the Lord God of Israel and said,
Esther 4:18 My Lord, our king, you alone are; help me who am alone and have no helper except you, because my danger is in my hand.
Esther 4:19 From my birth I heard in the tribe of my family that you, Lord, took Israel from all the nations and our fathers from all their ancestors as an eternal inheritance, and did for them all that you spoke.
Esther 4:20 And now we have sinned before you, and you have handed us over into the hands of our enemies, because we glorified their gods; you are just, Lord.
Esther 4:21 And now they have not been satisfied with the bitterness of our slavery, but have placed their hands upon the hands of their idols to remove the decree of your mouth and make your inheritance disappear and close the mouth of those praising you and extinguish the glory of your house and your altar
Esther 4:22 and open the mouth of nations for the excellences of vain things, and for a fleshly king to be marveled at forever.
Esther 4:23 Do not hand over your scepter, Lord, to those who do not exist, and let them not mock at our fall, but turn their plan upon them, and make an example of the one who began against us.
Esther 4:24 Remember, Lord; make yourself known in the time of our affliction, and give me courage, king of the gods and ruler over every authority;
Esther 4:25 give well-ordered speech into my mouth before the lion, and change his heart to hatred of the one warring against us, for his destruction and that of those of one mind with him;
Esther 4:26 but rescue us by your hand, and help me who am alone and have none except you, Lord.
Esther 4:27 You have knowledge of all things and know that I hated the glory of the lawless and abhor the bed of the uncircumcised and of every foreigner.
Esther 4:17 w You know my necessity, that I abhor the sign of my arrogance, which is upon my head in the days of my appearance; I abhor it as a menstrual rag, and do not wear it in the days of my quiet.
Esther 4:18 And your slave woman has not eaten Aman's table, and I have not glorified a king's drinking party, nor have I drunk wine of libations;
Esther 4:19 and your slave woman has not rejoiced from the day of my change until now except in you, Lord, God of Abraam.
Esther 4:20 God who is powerful over all, hear the voice of those who have lost hope, and rescue us from the hand of those doing evil; and rescue me from my fear.

## Chapter 5

Esther 5:1 And it happened on the third day, when she ceased praying, that she took off the garments of service and clothed herself in her glory
Esther 5:1 a and, becoming splendid, called upon God, the overseer of all and savior, took the two maids, and leaned upon the one as though living delicately, while the other followed, lifting her clothing,
Esther 5:2 and she herself was rosy at the height of her beauty, and her face was cheerful as though lovely, but her heart was constricted by fear.
Esther 5:3 And passing through all the doors, she stood before the king, and he was sitting upon the throne of his kingdom and had put on all the attire of his splendor, entirely in gold and costly stones, and was exceedingly fearsome.
Esther 5:4 And lifting his face, inflamed with glory, he looked in the height of anger, and the queen fell and changed her color in faintness and bent down upon the head of the maid who went before her.
Esther 5:5 And God changed the king's spirit to gentleness, and in anguish he sprang from his throne and took her up into his arms until she recovered, and encouraged her with peaceful words and said to her,
Esther 5:6 What is it, Esther? I am your brother; take courage, you shall certainly not die, because our command is common; approach.
Esther 5:2 And lifting the golden rod, he placed it upon her neck and kissed her and said, Speak to me.
Esther 5:2 a And she said to him, I saw you, lord, as an angel of God, and my heart was troubled from fear of your glory; because you are marvelous, lord, and your face is full of graces.
Esther 5:3 But as she was speaking, she fell from her faintness, and the king was troubled, and all his attendants encouraged her. And the king said, What do you want, Esther, and what is your petition? As far as half my kingdom, and it shall be yours.
Esther 5:4 And Esther said, Today is a distinguished day for me; if therefore it seems good to the king, let both he and Aman come to the reception that I will hold today.
Esther 5:5 And the king said, Hurry Aman along, so that we may do Esther's word; and both arrive at the reception that Esther spoke of.
Esther 5:6 And during the drinking the king said to Esther, What is it, Queen Esther? And all that you request shall be yours.
Esther 5:7 And she said, My request and my petition;
Esther 5:8 if I have found favor before the king, let the king and Aman come tomorrow to the reception that I will hold for them, and tomorrow I will do the same things.
Esther 5:9 And Aman went out from the king exceedingly glad, rejoicing; but when Aman saw Mardochaios the Jew in the court, he became exceedingly angry.
Esther 5:10 And entering his own place, he called his friends and Zosara his wife
Esther 5:11 and showed them his wealth and the glory that the king had bestowed upon him, and how he had made him take first place and lead the kingdom.
Esther 5:12 And Aman said, The queen has called no one to the reception with the king except me, and I have been called for tomorrow;
Esther 5:13 and these things do not please me whenever I see Mardochaios the Jew in the court.
Esther 5:14 And Zosara his wife and his friends said to him, Let a timber of fifty cubits be cut for you, and at dawn speak to the king, and let Mardochaios be hung upon the timber; but you enter the reception with the king and rejoice. And the word pleased Aman, and the timber was prepared.

## Chapter 6

Esther 6:1 But the Lord removed sleep from the king that night, and he told his teacher to bring in writings, memorials of the days, to read to him.
Esther 6:2 And he found the writings written about Mardochaios, how he had reported to the king concerning the king's two eunuchs while they were keeping guard and seeking to lay hands upon Artaxerxes.
Esther 6:3 And the king said, What glory or favor have we done for Mardochaios? And the king's servants said, You have done nothing for him.
Esther 6:4 And while the king was inquiring about Mardochaios's goodwill, behold, Aman was in the court; and the king said, Who is in the court? But Aman had come in to tell the king to hang Mardochaios upon the timber that he had prepared.
Esther 6:5 And the king's servants said, Behold, Aman stands in the court; and the king said, Call him.
Esther 6:6 And the king said to Aman, What shall I do for the man whom I wish to glorify? And Aman said within himself, Whom does the king wish to glorify except me?
Esther 6:7 And he said to the king, A man whom the king wishes to glorify,
Esther 6:8 let the king's servants bring a fine linen robe that the king wears, and a horse upon which the king mounts,
Esther 6:9 and let him give them to one of the king's illustrious friends, and let him clothe the man whom the king loves, and mount him upon the horse and proclaim through the city's square, saying, Thus shall it be for every man whom the king glorifies.
Esther 6:10 And the king said to Aman, As you have spoken, so do for Mardochaios the Jew who serves in the court, and let no word of what you have spoken fall aside from you.
Esther 6:11 And Aman took the robe and the horse and clothed Mardochaios and mounted him upon the horse and went through the city's square and proclaimed, saying, Thus shall it be for every man whom the king wishes to glorify.
Esther 6:12 And Mardochaios returned to the court, but Aman returned to his own place grieving, with his head covered.
Esther 6:13 And Aman recounted what had happened to him to Zosara his wife and his friends, and his friends and his wife said to him, If Mardochaios is of the race of Jews, you have begun to be humbled before him; falling you shall fall; you shall certainly not be able to ward him off, because a living God is with him. –
Esther 6:14 While they were still speaking, the eunuchs arrive, hurrying Aman to the drinking that Esther had prepared.

## Chapter 7

Esther 7:1 And the king and Aman entered to drink with the queen.
Esther 7:2 And on the second day, during the drinking, the king said to Esther, What is it, Queen Esther, and what is your request and what is your petition? And let it be yours, as far as half my kingdom.
Esther 7:3 And answering, she said, If I have found favor before the king, let my life be given at my request, and my people at my petition;
Esther 7:4 for both I and my people were sold for destruction and plundering and slavery, we and our children as male slaves and female slaves, and I kept silent; for the slanderer is not worthy of the king's court.
Esther 7:5 And the king said, Who is this who dared to do this thing?
Esther 7:6 And Esther said, An enemy, this wicked Aman. But Aman was troubled because of the king and the queen.
Esther 7:7 But the king rose from the drinking party into the garden; and Aman entreated the queen, for he saw himself being in troubles.
Esther 7:8 And the king returned from the garden, but Aman had fallen upon the couch, petitioning the queen; and the king said, So you even assault the wife in my house? And on hearing this Aman was confounded in his face.
Esther 7:9 And Bougathan, one of the eunuchs, said to the king, Behold, Aman also prepared a timber for Mardochaios, who spoke concerning the king, and a timber of fifty cubits stands upright at Aman's place. And the king said, Let him be crucified upon it.
Esther 7:10 And Aman was hung upon the timber that he had prepared for Mardochaios. And then the king abated his anger.

## Chapter 8

Esther 8:1 And on that very day King Artaxerxes gave Esther all that belonged to Aman the slanderer, and Mardochaios was summoned by the king, for Esther had explained that he was related to her.
Esther 8:2 And the king took the ring that he had removed from Aman and gave it to Mardochaios, and Esther appointed Mardochaios over all Aman's possessions.
Esther 8:3 And she spoke further to the king and fell at his feet and petitioned him to remove Aman's wickedness and all that he had done to the Jews.
Esther 8:4 And the king extended the golden rod to Esther, and Esther arose to stand before the king.
Esther 8:5 And Esther said, If it seems good to you and I have found favor, let an order be sent to reverse the letters sent by Aman, written for the destruction of the Jews who are in your kingdom;
Esther 8:6 for how shall I be able to see the mistreatment of my people, and how shall I be able to be saved at the destruction of my homeland?
Esther 8:7 And the king said to Esther, If I have given and granted you all Aman's possessions, and hung him upon a timber because he brought his hands against the Jews, what do you still seek?
Esther 8:8 You yourselves also write in my name as seems good to you, and seal with my ring; for whatever is written at the king's command and sealed with my ring cannot be contradicted.
Esther 8:9 And the scribes were called in the first month, which is Nisa, on the twenty-third of the same year, and there was written for the Jews all that he commanded the stewards and the rulers of the satraps, from India to Ethiopia, to one hundred twenty-seven satrapies, region by region, according to their own speech.
Esther 8:10 And it was written through the king and sealed with his ring, and they sent out the letters through letter carriers,
Esther 8:11 as he commanded them to use their laws in every city, both to help themselves and to deal with their adversaries and those opposing them as they wished,
Esther 8:12 on one day throughout Artaxerxes's kingdom, on the thirteenth of the twelfth month, which is Adar.
Esther 8:12 a The following is a copy of their letter:
Esther 8:13 Great King Artaxerxes to the rulers of regions in the one hundred twenty-seven satrapies from India to Ethiopia, and to those who are of our mind, greetings.
Esther 8:14 Many, honored more frequently by the abundant kindness of their benefactors, have become more high-minded, and not only seek to do evil to those subjected to us, but, unable to bear their surfeit, attempt to devise schemes against their own benefactors;
Esther 8:15 and not only abolishing gratitude from among people, but also lifted up by the boasts of those inexperienced in goodness, they suppose they will escape the evil-hating justice of God who always surveys everything.
Esther 8:13 And often the persuasion of friends entrusted to handle affairs has also made many appointed in positions of authority complicit in innocent blood and surrounded them with incurable calamities,
Esther 8:14 when those friends deceived the untainted good judgment of those in power by the false reasoning of their maliciousness.
Esther 8:15 And it is possible to examine, not so much from the older accounts that we have handed down, as by your investigating the things close at hand, what has been impiously accomplished by the pestilence of those wielding power unworthily,
Esther 8:16 and to attend to what follows, with a view to our providing the kingdom undisturbed to all people with peace,
Esther 8:17 making use of changes, but always judging the things coming before our eyes with a more equitable response.
Esther 8:12 k For Aman, son of Amadathos, a Macedonian, truly foreign to the blood of the Persians and far removed from our kindness, having been received as a guest by us,
Esther 8:13 obtained the humanity that we have toward every nation to such an extent that he was proclaimed our father and, bowed to by all, continued as the second person of the royal throne;
Esther 8:14 but not bearing his arrogance, he undertook to deprive us of rule and breath,
Esther 8:15 having requested for destruction, by intricately woven deceptive reasonings of schemes, both Mardochaios, our savior and continual benefactor, and Esther, the blameless partner of the kingdom, together with their entire nation;
Esther 8:16 for by these means he thought, after taking us bereft, to transfer the dominion of the Persians to the Macedonians.
Esther 8:17 But we find that the Jews handed over for disappearance by the thrice-accursed man are not evildoers, but conduct their lives under most just laws,
Esther 8:18 and are sons of the highest, greatest, living God, who directs the kingdom for both us and our ancestors in the finest arrangement.
Esther 8:19 You will therefore do well not to make further use of the letters sent by Aman son of Amadathos, because the very man who accomplished these things has been crucified at the gates of Sousa with his entire household, God who rules over everything having swiftly rendered him the judgment he deserved;
Esther 8:20 but after posting a copy of this letter in every place, to allow the Jews openly to use their own ordinances and to strengthen them together, so that they may ward off those who attacked them in a time of affliction on the thirteenth of the twelfth month, Adar, on that same day;
Esther 8:21 for God who has dominion over all has made this day gladness for them instead of destruction of the chosen race.
Esther 8:22 You yourselves therefore also celebrate a distinguished day with every kind of feasting among your named festivals, so that both now and afterward there may be deliverance for us and for the Persians of goodwill, but for those plotting against us a memorial of destruction.
Esther 8:12 x But every city or region as a whole that does not act according to these things will be consumed with spear and fire in wrath; it will be made not only impassable to people, but also most hateful to beasts and birds for all time.
Esther 8:13 And let the copies be posted visibly throughout the kingdom, and let all the Jews be ready for this day to fight their opponents.
Esther 8:14 The horsemen therefore went out, hastening to accomplish the things spoken by the king; and the command was also posted in Sousa.
Esther 8:15 And Mardochaios went out clothed in the royal robe and wearing a golden crown and a purple fine linen diadem; and those in Sousa rejoiced on seeing him.
Esther 8:16 And light and gladness came to the Jews;
Esther 8:17 in every city and region where the command was posted, where the proclamation was posted, there was joy and gladness for the Jews, drinking and gladness, and many of the nations were circumcised and practiced Judaism because of fear of the Jews.

## Chapter 9

Esther 9:1 For in the twelfth month, on the thirteenth of the month, which is Adar, the letters written by the king were present.
Esther 9:2 On that very day those opposing the Jews perished; for no one resisted, fearing them.
Esther 9:3 For the rulers of the satraps and the potentates and the royal scribes honored the Jews; for the fear of Mardochaios lay upon them.
Esther 9:4 For the king's command came for him to be named throughout the kingdom.
Esther 9:6 And in the city of Sousa the Jews killed five hundred men,
Esther 9:7 both Pharsannestain and Delphon and Phasga
Esther 9:8 and Phardatha and Barea and Sarbacha
Esther 9:9 and Marmasima and Arouphaios and Arsaios and Zabouthaithan,
Esther 9:10 the ten sons of Aman son of Amadathos, the Bougaian, the enemy of the Jews, and plundered. –
Esther 9:11 On that very day the number of those who had perished in Sousa was delivered to the king.
Esther 9:12 And the king said to Esther, The Jews have destroyed five hundred men in the city of Sousa; but how do you think they dealt in the surrounding region? What then do you still petition, and it shall be yours?
Esther 9:13 And Esther said to the king, Let the Jews be permitted to act likewise tomorrow, so as to hang Aman's ten sons.
Esther 9:14 And he permitted it to happen thus and published an order for the Jews of the city to hang the bodies of Aman's sons.
Esther 9:15 And the Jews in Sousa assembled on the fourteenth of Adar and killed three hundred men and plundered nothing. –
Esther 9:16 But the rest of the Jews in the kingdom assembled and helped themselves and rested from their enemies; for they destroyed fifteen thousand of them on the thirteenth of Adar and plundered nothing.
Esther 9:17 And they rested on the fourteenth of the same month and celebrated it as a day of rest with joy and gladness.
Esther 9:18 But the Jews in the city of Sousa assembled also on the fourteenth and did not rest; and they celebrated the fifteenth also with joy and gladness.
Esther 9:19 Therefore the Jews scattered in every region outside celebrate the fourteenth of Adar as a good day with gladness, each sending portions to his neighbor; but those dwelling in the chief cities celebrate the fifteenth of Adar also as a day of good gladness, sending portions to their neighbors.
Esther 9:20 And Mardochaios wrote these words in a book and sent it to the Jews, as many as were in Artaxerxes's kingdom, those near and those far,
Esther 9:21 to establish these days as good days and to celebrate the fourteenth and the fifteenth of Adar –
Esther 9:22 for on these days the Jews rested from their enemies – and the month in which it was turned for them [which was Adar] from mourning to joy and from pain to a good day, to celebrate it entirely as good days of weddings and gladness, sending portions to friends and to the poor.
Esther 9:23 And the Jews accepted, as Mardochaios wrote to them,
Esther 9:24 how Aman son of Amadathos, the Macedonian, warred against them, how he established a decree and a lot to make them disappear,
Esther 9:25 and how he entered to the king, saying to hang Mardochaios; but all the evils he attempted to bring upon the Jews came upon him, and he and his children were hung.
Esther 9:26 Therefore these days were named Phrourai because of the lots, because in their language they are called Phrourai, because of the words of this letter and all that they have suffered because of these things and all that happened to them;
Esther 9:27 and he established it, and the Jews accepted it upon themselves and upon their seed and upon those added to them, and indeed they will not act otherwise; and these days are a memorial performed generation by generation and city and family and region;
Esther 9:28 and these days of Phrourai will be celebrated for all time, and their memorial shall certainly not fail from the generations.
Esther 9:29 And Esther the queen, daughter of Aminadab, and Mardochaios the Jew wrote all that they had done and the confirmation of the letter of Phrourai.
Esther 9:31 And Mardochaios and Esther the queen established for themselves against themselves, and then having established against their health, and their plan;
Esther 9:32 and Esther established it by a word forever, and it was written as a memorial.

## Chapter 10

Esther 10:1 And the king prescribed taxes upon the kingdom of both land and sea.
Esther 10:2 And his strength and valor, and the wealth and glory of his kingdom, behold, it is written in the book of kings of Persians and Medes as a memorial.
Esther 10:3 But Mardochaios succeeded King Artaxerxes and was great in the kingdom and glorified by the Jews; and, being loved, he recounted his conduct to his entire nation.
Esther 10:3 a And Mardochaios said, These things came from God;
Esther 10:4 for I remembered concerning the dream that I saw concerning these matters; for not even a word of them passed away.
Esther 10:5 The little spring that became a river, and there was light and sun and much water; Esther is the river, whom the king married and made queen.
Esther 10:6 And the two dragons are I and Aman.
Esther 10:7 And the nations, those gathered together to destroy the name of the Jews.
Esther 10:8 And my nation, this is Israel, those who cried to God and were saved; and the Lord saved his people, and the Lord rescued us from all these evils, and God did the signs and the great wonders that have not happened among the nations.
Esther 10:9 Therefore he made two lots, one for God's people and one for all the nations;
Esther 10:10 and these two lots came to an hour and a time and to a day of judgment before God and among all the nations,
Esther 10:11 and God remembered his people and vindicated his inheritance.
Esther 10:3 k And these days shall be for them in the month Adar, on the fourteenth and the fifteenth of the same month, with assembly and joy and gladness before God throughout generations forever among his people Israel.
Esther 10:4 In the fourth year of Ptolemy and Cleopatra reigning, Dositheos, who said he was a priest and a Levite, and Ptolemy his son brought in the foregoing letter of Phrourai, which they said was genuine and that Lysimachos son of Ptolemy, of those in Jerusalem, had translated.

# Judith

The Apostolic Bible. Public domain. https://apostolic-bible.ysys9.chatgpt.site/license.html


## Chapter 1

Judith 1:1 In the twelfth year of the kingdom of Nabouchodonosor, who reigned over the Assyrians in Nineue, the great city, in the days of Arphaxad, who reigned over the Medes in Ekbatana,
Judith 1:2 and built walls around Ekbatana from hewn stones three cubits in width and six cubits in length, and made the height of the wall seventy cubits and its width fifty cubits,
Judith 1:3 and set its towers at its gates at one hundred cubits, and founded its width at sixty cubits,
Judith 1:4 and made its gates gates rising to a height of seventy cubits, and its width forty cubits, for the departures of the force of his mighty men and the formations of his infantry.
Judith 1:5 And in those days King Nabouchodonosor made war against King Arphaxad in the great plain, that is, a plain in the territory of Ragau.
Judith 1:6 And all who inhabited the hill country and all who inhabited the Euphrates and the Tigris and the Hydaspes and the plains of Arioch, king of the Elymaians, met with him, and many nations came together for the battle formation of the sons of Cheleoud.
Judith 1:7 And Nabouchodonosor, king of the Assyrians, sent to all who inhabited Persia and to all who inhabited the west, those inhabiting Cilicia and Damascus and Lebanon and Antilebanon, and all who inhabited the coastal frontage,
Judith 1:8 and those among the nations of Carmel and Galaad, and upper Galilee and the great plain of Esdrelon,
Judith 1:9 and all those in Samaria and its cities and beyond the Jordan as far as Jerusalem and Batane and Chelous and Kades and the river of Egypt and Taphnas and Ramesse and all the land of Gesem,
Judith 1:10 as far as coming above Tanis and Memphis, and all who inhabited Egypt as far as coming to the borders of Ethiopia.
Judith 1:11 And all who inhabited the entire land despised the word of Nabouchodonosor, king of the Assyrians, and did not come together with him for the war, because they did not fear him, but he was before them as a single man, and they sent his messengers back empty, with dishonor upon their faces.
Judith 1:12 And Nabouchodonosor became exceedingly angry against all this land and swore by his throne and his kingdom that he would indeed avenge himself upon all the territory of Cilicia and Damascus and Syria, to kill with his sword also all who inhabited the land of Moab and the sons of Ammon and all Judea and all those in Egypt as far as coming to the borders of the two seas.
Judith 1:13 And he drew up his force against King Arphaxad in the seventeenth year and prevailed in his war and overturned all Arphaxad's force and all his cavalry and all his chariots,
Judith 1:14 and became master of his cities and arrived as far as Ekbatana and seized the towers and plundered its squares and made its adornment its reproach,
Judith 1:15 and took Arphaxad in the mountains of Ragau and struck him down with his spears and destroyed him until that day.
Judith 1:16 And he himself and all his mixed company returned with them, an exceedingly great multitude of warrior men, and he was there relaxing and feasting, he and his force, for one hundred twenty days.

## Chapter 2

Judith 2:1 And in the eighteenth year, on the twenty-second of the first month, a word came in the house of Nabouchodonosor, king of the Assyrians, to avenge himself upon all the land, as he had spoken.
Judith 2:2 And he called together all his attendants and all his grandees and laid before them the secret of his plan and concluded with his mouth all the evil for the land,
Judith 2:3 and they judged to destroy all flesh who had not followed the word of his mouth.
Judith 2:4 And it happened, when he concluded his plan, that Nabouchodonosor, king of the Assyrians, called Holophernes, the commander of his force, who was second after him, and said to him,
Judith 2:5 Thus says the great king, the lord of all the land: Behold, you shall go out from my presence and take with yourself men confident in their strength, infantry to one hundred twenty thousand, and a multitude of horses with riders, twelve thousand,
Judith 2:6 and you shall go out to meet all the land toward the west, because they disobeyed the word of my mouth,
Judith 2:7 and you shall tell them to prepare earth and water, because I will go out against them in my anger and cover the entire face of the land with the feet of my force, and I will give them to them for plundering,
Judith 2:8 and their wounded shall fill their ravines, and every torrent and overflowing river shall be filled with their dead;
Judith 2:9 and I will lead their captivity to the extremities of all the land.
Judith 2:10 But you shall go out and occupy all their territory beforehand for me, and they shall surrender themselves to you, and you shall preserve them for me for the day of their reproof;
Judith 2:11 but toward those disobeying, your eye shall not spare in giving them to slaughter and plunder in all your land.
Judith 2:12 Because I live, and the might of my kingdom, I have spoken and will do these things by my hand.
Judith 2:13 And you shall not transgress a single one of your lord's words, but accomplishing you shall accomplish as I have commanded you, and you shall not delay doing them.
Judith 2:14 And Holophernes went out from his lord's presence and called all the potentates and the generals and supervisors of Assour's force,
Judith 2:15 and counted chosen men for battle formation, as his lord commanded him, to one hundred twenty thousand, and mounted archers, twelve thousand,
Judith 2:16 and arranged them in the manner in which a multitude is arrayed for war.
Judith 2:17 And he took camels and asses and mules for their baggage, an exceedingly great multitude, and sheep and cattle and goats for their provision, of which there was no number,
Judith 2:18 and food supplies for every man in abundance, and exceedingly much gold and silver from the king's house.
Judith 2:19 And he himself and all his force went out on a march to go before King Nabouchodonosor and cover the entire face of the land toward the west with chariots and cavalry and their chosen infantry;
Judith 2:20 and a great mixed company went out together with them, like locusts and like the sand of the earth, for there was no number because of their multitude.
Judith 2:21 And they went away from Nineue a journey of three days to the front of the plain of Bektileth, and encamped from Bektileth near the mountain to the left of upper Cilicia.
Judith 2:22 And he took all his force, the infantry and the cavalry and his chariots, and went away from there into the hill country.
Judith 2:23 And he cut through Phoud and Loud and plundered all the sons of Rassis and the sons of Ismael facing the wilderness south of Cheleon.
Judith 2:24 And he crossed the Euphrates and went through Mesopotamia and demolished all the fortified cities upon the torrent Abrona, as far as coming to the sea.
Judith 2:25 And he occupied the territory of Cilicia and cut down all who resisted him and came as far as the territory of Iapheth, toward the south, facing Arabia.
Judith 2:26 And he encircled all the sons of Madiam and burned their dwellings and plundered their enclosures.
Judith 2:27 And he went down into the plain of Damascus in the days of the wheat harvest and burned all their fields and gave the flocks and herds to destruction, and despoiled their cities and winnowed away their plains and struck all their young men with the mouth of the sword. –
Judith 2:28 And fear and trembling of him fell upon those inhabiting the coast, those in Sidon and Tyre and those inhabiting Sour and Okina and all who inhabited Iemnaan, and those inhabiting Azotos and Askalon feared him exceedingly.

## Chapter 3

Judith 3:1 And they sent messengers to him with peaceful words, saying,
Judith 3:2 Behold, we, the servants of Nabouchodonosor the great king, lie before you; deal with us as is pleasing to your face;
Judith 3:3 behold, our farmsteads and every place of ours and every plain of wheat and the flocks and herds and all the enclosures of our tents lie before your face; use them as may please you;
Judith 3:4 behold, our cities also and those dwelling in them are your slaves; come and meet them as is good in your eyes.
Judith 3:5 And the men arrived before Holophernes and reported to him according to these words.
Judith 3:6 And he and his force went down to the coast and garrisoned the fortified cities and took chosen men from them for an alliance;
Judith 3:7 and they and all their surrounding region received him with wreaths and dances and drums.
Judith 3:8 And he demolished all their territory and cut down their groves, and it had been granted him to destroy all the gods of the land, so that all the nations might serve him alone, Nabouchodonosor, and all their tongues and tribes might call upon him as god.
Judith 3:9 And he came facing Esdrelon, near Dotaia, which is opposite the great ridge of Judea,
Judith 3:10 and they encamped between Gaibai and the city of the Scythians, and he was there a month of days to gather all the baggage of his force.

## Chapter 4
