Judith 4:1 And the sons of Israel inhabiting Judea heard everything that Holophernes, the commander of Nabouchodonosor, king of the Assyrians, had done to the nations, and how he had despoiled all their sacred places and given them to destruction,
Judith 4:2 and they feared exceedingly, exceedingly, before him, and were troubled concerning Jerusalem and the temple of the Lord their God.
Judith 4:3 Because they had recently come up from captivity, and all the people of Judea had newly been gathered, and the vessels and the altar and the house had been sanctified from profanation.
Judith 4:4 And they sent into all the territory of Samaria and Kona and Baithoron and Belmain and Iericho, and to Choba and Aisora and the valley of Salem,
Judith 4:5 and occupied beforehand all the summits of the high mountains and walled the villages in them and stored supplies for food in preparation for war, because their plains had recently been harvested.
Judith 4:6 And Ioakim the great priest, who was in Jerusalem in those days, wrote to those dwelling in Baityloua and Baitomesthaim, which is opposite Esdrelon, facing the plain near Dothaim,
Judith 4:7 telling them to hold the ascents of the hill country firmly, because through them was the entrance into Judea, and it was easy to prevent them from approaching, the approach being narrow enough for two men in all.
Judith 4:8 And the sons of Israel did as Ioakim the great priest and the council of elders of the entire populace of Israel, who sat in Jerusalem, had directed them. –
Judith 4:9 And every man of Israel cried to God with great earnestness and humbled their souls with great earnestness.
Judith 4:10 They and their wives and their infants and their cattle and every resident alien and hired worker and purchased slave of theirs put sackcloth upon their loins.
Judith 4:11 And every man of Israel and woman and the children inhabiting Jerusalem fell before the temple and put ashes upon their heads and spread their sackcloth before the Lord;
Judith 4:12 and they clothed the altar with sackcloth and cried earnestly with one accord to the God of Israel, that he should not give their infants to plundering and the women to spoil and the cities of their inheritance to destruction and the holy places to profanation and reproach, an object of malicious joy for the nations.
Judith 4:13 And the Lord heard their voice and looked upon their affliction; and the people were fasting many days throughout Judea and Jerusalem before the holy places of the Lord Almighty.
Judith 4:14 And Ioakim the great priest and all the priests standing before the Lord and those ministering to the Lord, their loins girded with sackcloth, offered the continual whole burnt offering and the vows and the people's voluntary gifts,
Judith 4:15 and ashes were upon their turbans, and they cried to the Lord with all their strength to visit the entire house of Israel for good.

## Chapter 5

Judith 5:1 And it was reported to Holophernes, commander of Assour's force, that the sons of Israel had prepared for war and closed the passes of the hill country and walled every summit of a high mountain and placed obstacles in the plains.
Judith 5:2 And he became exceedingly angry in wrath and called all the rulers of Moab and the generals of Ammon and all the satraps of the coast,
Judith 5:3 and said to them, Tell me now, sons of Chanaan, who this people is that sits in the hill country, and what cities they inhabit, and the multitude of their force, and in what their might and their strength consist, and who has arisen over them as king, leading their army,
Judith 5:4 and why they have turned their backs, so as not to come to meet me, beyond all those dwelling in the west. –
Judith 5:5 And Achior, the leader of all the sons of Ammon, said to him, Let my lord now hear a word from the mouth of your slave, and I will report to you the truth concerning this people that inhabits this hill country, dwelling near you, and no falsehood will go out from the mouth of your slave.
Judith 5:6 This people are descendants of Chaldeans.
Judith 5:7 And formerly they resided in Mesopotamia, because they did not wish to follow the gods of their fathers, who were in the land of the Chaldeans;
Judith 5:8 and they stepped out of the way of their parents and bowed to the God of heaven, a God whom they recognized, and they drove them out from before their gods, and they fled into Mesopotamia and resided there many days.
Judith 5:9 And their God told them to go out from their residence and travel to the land of Chanaan, and they dwelt there and increased in gold and silver and exceedingly many cattle.
Judith 5:10 And they went down into Egypt, for famine covered the face of the land of Chanaan, and they resided there as long as they were sustained; and they became a great multitude there, and there was no number of their race.
Judith 5:11 And the king of Egypt rose against them and dealt craftily with them in toil and brick; they humbled them and made them slaves.
Judith 5:12 And they cried to their God, and he struck all the land of Egypt with plagues in which there was no healing; and the Egyptians drove them out from before them.
Judith 5:13 And God dried up the Red Sea before them
Judith 5:14 and led them into the way of Sina and Kades Barne; and they drove out all those inhabiting the wilderness
Judith 5:15 and dwelt in the land of the Amorrites and destroyed all the Esebonites by their strength. And crossing the Jordan, they inherited all the hill country
Judith 5:16 and drove out from before them the Chanaanite and the Pherezite and the Iebousite and Sychem and all the Gergesaians, and dwelt in it many days.
Judith 5:17 And as long as they did not sin before their God, good things were with them, because a God who hates injustice is with them.
Judith 5:18 But when they departed from the way that he appointed for them, they were destroyed in many wars to an exceedingly great extent and taken captive into a land not their own, and the temple of their God was brought to the ground, and their cities were seized by their adversaries.
Judith 5:19 And now, returning to their God, they came up from the dispersion where they had been scattered, and occupied Jerusalem, where their sanctuary is, and settled in the hill country, because it was deserted.
Judith 5:20 And now, master, lord, if there is an ignorant offense among this people and they sin against their God, and we shall examine whether this obstacle is among them, and we shall go up and wage war against them;
Judith 5:21 but if there is no lawlessness in their nation, let my lord now pass by, lest their Lord and their God shield them, and we shall become a reproach before all the land. –
Judith 5:22 And it happened, when Achior ceased speaking these words, that all the people encircling the tent and standing around grumbled, and Holophernes's grandees and all those inhabiting the coast and Moab said to cut him to pieces:
Judith 5:23 For we shall not fear the sons of Israel, for behold, a people in whom there is neither force nor might for a strong battle formation;
Judith 5:24 therefore we shall now go up, and they shall be food for all your army, Master Holophernes. –

## Chapter 6

Judith 6:1 And when the uproar of the men around the council ceased, Holophernes, commander of Assour's force, said to Achior before the entire populace of foreigners and to all the sons of Moab,
Judith 6:2 And who are you, Achior and the hired men of Ephraim, that you have prophesied among us as today and said not to war against the race of Israel, because their God will shield them? And who is god except Nabouchodonosor? He will send his might and destroy them from the face of the earth, and their God will not rescue them;
Judith 6:3 but we his slaves will strike them as a single person, and they will not withstand the might of our horses.
Judith 6:4 For we shall burn them up with them, and their mountains will be drunk with their blood, and their plains will be filled with their dead, and the footprint of their feet will not resist before us, but with destruction they will perish, says King Nabouchodonosor, lord of all the land; for he has spoken, the utterances of his words will not be made vain.
Judith 6:5 But you, Achior, hired man of Ammon, who spoke these words on the day of your injustice, shall no longer see my face from this day until I avenge myself upon the race of those from Egypt;
Judith 6:6 and then the iron of my army and the people of my attendants will pass through your sides, and you will fall among their wounded when I return.
Judith 6:7 And my slaves will take you back into the hill country and place you in one of the cities of the ascents,
Judith 6:8 and you will not perish until you are destroyed with them.
Judith 6:9 And if indeed you hope in your heart that they will not be seized, let your face not fall; I have spoken, and nothing of my words will fall away. –
Judith 6:10 And Holophernes commanded his slaves who stood in his tent to seize Achior and take him back to Baityloua and hand him over into the hands of the sons of Israel.
Judith 6:11 And his slaves seized him and led him outside the camp into the plain and set out from the midst of the plain into the hill country and arrived at the springs that were below Baityloua.
Judith 6:12 And when the men of the city on the summit of the mountain saw them, they took up their weapons and went out of the city onto the summit of the mountain, and every slinger held their ascent and threw stones at them.
Judith 6:13 And slipping beneath the mountain, they bound Achior and left him thrown down at the foot of the mountain and went away to their lord.
Judith 6:14 But the sons of Israel came down from their city and came upon him, and unbinding him, led him away into Baityloua and placed him before the rulers of their city,
Judith 6:15 who in those days were Ozias son of Micha, from the tribe of Symeon, and Chabris son of Gothoniel and Charmis son of Melchiel.
Judith 6:16 And they called together all the elders of the city, and all their young men and the women ran together into the assembly, and they stood Achior in the midst of all their people, and Ozias asked him what had happened.
Judith 6:17 And answering, he reported to them the words of Holophernes's council and all the words that he spoke in the midst of the rulers of the sons of Assour, and all that Holophernes spoke boastfully against the house of Israel.
Judith 6:18 And falling, the people bowed to God and cried, saying,
Judith 6:19 Lord, God of heaven, look down upon their arrogances and have mercy upon the humiliation of our race, and look upon the face of those sanctified to you on this day.
Judith 6:20 And they encouraged Achior and praised him exceedingly,
Judith 6:21 and Ozias took him from the assembly into his house and held a drinking for the elders, and they called upon the God of Israel for help throughout that night.

## Chapter 7

Judith 7:1 And on the next day Holophernes ordered all his army and all his people who had come for his alliance to break camp toward Baityloua and occupy the ascents of the hill country beforehand and make war against the sons of Israel.
Judith 7:2 And on that day every mighty man of theirs broke camp; and their force of warrior men was one hundred seventy thousand infantry and twelve thousand cavalry, apart from the baggage and the men who were on foot among them, an exceedingly great multitude.
Judith 7:3 And they encamped in the valley near Baityloua, at the spring, and extended in width toward Dothaim as far as Belbaim, and in length from Baityloua as far as Kyamon, which is opposite Esdrelon.
Judith 7:4 But the sons of Israel, when they saw their multitude, were exceedingly troubled, and each said to his neighbor, Now these will lick up the face of all the land, and neither the high mountains nor the ravines nor the hills will withstand their weight.
Judith 7:5 And each took up their war equipment and lit fires upon their towers, and they remained keeping guard throughout that night.
Judith 7:6 And on the second day Holophernes led out all his cavalry before the sons of Israel who were in Baityloua,
Judith 7:7 and inspected the ascents of their city and surveyed the springs of water and occupied them beforehand and stationed camps of warrior men over them, and he himself broke camp toward his people. –
Judith 7:8 And all the rulers of the sons of Esau and all the leaders of the people of Moab and the generals of the coast approached him and said,
Judith 7:9 Let our master now hear a word, so that there may be no crushing in your force.
Judith 7:10 For this people of the sons of Israel trust not in their spears, but in the heights of the mountains in which they dwell; for it is not easy to approach the summits of their mountains.
Judith 7:11 And now, master, do not war against them as a war of battle formation takes place, and not one man of your people will fall.
Judith 7:12 Remain at your camp, preserving every man of your force, and let your servants take possession of the spring of water that goes out from the foot of the mountain,
Judith 7:13 because all who inhabit Baityloua draw water from there, and thirst will kill them, and they will surrender their city; and we and our people will go up onto the nearby summits of the mountains and encamp upon them as an outpost, so that not one man may go out of the city.
Judith 7:14 And they and their wives and their children will waste away in famine, and before the sword comes upon them, they will be laid low in the squares of their dwelling place.
Judith 7:15 And you will repay them an evil repayment because they rebelled and did not meet your face in peace. –
Judith 7:16 And their words pleased Holophernes and all his attendants, and he directed them to do as they had spoken.
Judith 7:17 And a camp of the sons of Ammon set out, and with them five thousand sons of Assour, and they encamped in the valley and occupied beforehand the waters and the springs of the waters of the sons of Israel.
Judith 7:18 And the sons of Esau and the sons of Ammon went up and encamped in the hill country opposite Dothaim. And they sent some of them toward the south and east, opposite Egrebel, which is near Chous, which is upon the torrent Mochmour. And the rest of the army of the Assyrians encamped in the plain and covered the entire face of the land, and their tents and their baggage encamped in a great crowd and were an exceedingly great multitude.
Judith 7:19 And the sons of Israel cried to the Lord their God, because their spirit had become fainthearted, because all their enemies had encircled them and there was no escaping from their midst.
Judith 7:20 And all Assour's camp, the infantry and chariots and their cavalry, remained around them thirty-four days. And all their water vessels failed all who inhabited Baityloua,
Judith 7:21 and the cisterns were being emptied, and they did not have water to drink to satisfaction for a single day, because they gave them drink by measure.
Judith 7:22 And their infants became dispirited, and the women and the young men failed from thirst and fell in the squares of the city and in the passages of the gates, and there was no strength left in them. –
Judith 7:23 And all the people gathered against Ozias and the rulers of the city, the young men and the women and the children, and cried with a loud voice and said before all the elders,
Judith 7:24 May God judge between you and us, because you have done great injustice among us by not speaking peaceful words with the sons of Assour.
Judith 7:25 And now there is no helper for us, but God has sold us into their hands, to be laid low before them in thirst and great destruction.
Judith 7:26 And now call upon them and surrender the entire city as spoil to Holophernes's people and all his force.
Judith 7:27 For it is better for us to become plunder for them; for we shall become slaves, and our life will live, and we shall not see the death of our infants before our eyes and our wives and our children giving up their lives.
Judith 7:28 We call heaven and earth and our God and Lord of our fathers to witness to you, who punishes us according to our sins and according to the sins of our fathers, that he may not act according to these words on this day today.
Judith 7:29 And there was great weeping in the midst of the assembly, all with one accord, and they cried to the Lord God with a loud voice. –
Judith 7:30 And Ozias said to them, Take courage, brothers; let us persevere five more days, in which the Lord our God will turn his mercy upon us, for he will not abandon us completely;
Judith 7:31 but if these pass and help does not come upon us, I will act according to your words.
Judith 7:32 And he dispersed the people to their own encampment, and they went away onto the walls and towers of their city and sent the women and the children into their houses; and they were in great humiliation in the city.

## Chapter 8

Judith 8:1 And in those days Ioudith heard, daughter of Merari, son of Ox, son of Ioseph, son of Oziel, son of Elkia, son of Ananias, son of Gedeon, son of Raphain, son of Achitob, son of Elias, son of Chelkias, son of Eliab, son of Nathanael, son of Salamiel, son of Sarasadai, son of Israel.
Judith 8:2 And her husband Manasses was of her tribe and her family; and he died in the days of the barley harvest;
Judith 8:3 for he stood over those binding the sheaves in the plain, and the scorching heat came upon his head, and he fell upon his bed and died in Baityloua, his city, and they buried him with his fathers in the field between Dothaim and Balamon.
Judith 8:4 And Ioudith was in her house as a widow for three years and four months.
Judith 8:5 And she made herself a tent upon the roof of her house and put sackcloth upon her loins, and the garments of her widowhood were upon her.
Judith 8:6 And she fasted all the days of her widowhood except the days before sabbaths and sabbaths and the days before new moons and new moons and festivals and rejoicings of the house of Israel.
Judith 8:7 And she was beautiful in form and exceedingly lovely in appearance; and Manasses her husband had left her gold and silver and male slaves and female slaves and cattle and fields, and she remained over them.
Judith 8:8 And there was no one who brought an evil word against her, because she feared God exceedingly. –
Judith 8:9 And she heard the people's evil words against the ruler, because they had become fainthearted in the shortage of water, and Ioudith heard all the words that Ozias spoke to them, how he swore to them to hand the city over to the Assyrians after five days;
Judith 8:10 and sending her maid who was in charge of all her possessions, she called Chabris and Charmis, the elders of her city,
Judith 8:11 and they came to her, and she said to them, Hear me now, rulers of those inhabiting Baityloua; because your word that you spoke before the people on this day is not upright, and you established this oath that you spoke between God and yourselves, and said you would surrender the city to our enemies unless the Lord turned help to you within them.
Judith 8:12 And now who are you who have tested God on this day today and stand above God in the midst of the sons of men?
Judith 8:13 And now you examine the Lord Almighty, and you will know nothing forever.
Judith 8:14 Because you will not find the depth of a person's heart and will not discern the words of his mind; and how will you search God, who made all these things, and know his mind and understand his reasoning? By no means, brothers; do not provoke the Lord our God to anger.
Judith 8:15 Because if he does not wish to help us within the five days, he himself has the authority to shelter us on whatever days he wishes, or even to destroy us before our enemies.
Judith 8:16 But do not take the plans of the Lord our God as a pledge, because God is not like a person to be threatened, nor like a son of man to be brought to arbitration.
Judith 8:17 Therefore, awaiting the deliverance from him, let us call upon him for our help, and he will hear our voice if it is pleasing to him.
Judith 8:18 Because neither in our generations has there arisen nor on this day today is there any tribe or family or populace or city among us who bow to gods made by hands, as happened in the former days;
Judith 8:19 on account of which our fathers were given to the sword and to plundering and fell in a great fall before our enemies.
Judith 8:20 But we have known no other God except him; therefore we hope that he will not overlook us, nor any of our race.
Judith 8:21 Because when we are taken, thus all Judea also will be taken, and our holy places will be plundered, and he will exact their profanation from our blood,
Judith 8:22 and he will turn the slaughter of our brothers and the captivity of the land and the desolation of our inheritance upon our head among the nations, wherever we serve as slaves there, and we shall become a stumbling block and a reproach before those acquiring us.
Judith 8:23 Because our slavery will not be directed toward favor, but the Lord our God will make it dishonor.
Judith 8:24 And now, brothers, let us show our brothers that their life hangs upon us, and the holy places and the house and the altar rest upon us.
Judith 8:25 Besides all these things, let us give thanks to the Lord our God, who tests us as he also tested our fathers.
Judith 8:26 Remember all that he did with Abraam and all the ways he tested Isaak and all that happened to Iakob in Mesopotamia of Syria while shepherding the sheep of Laban, his mother's brother.
Judith 8:27 Because not as he tried them by fire for the examination of their heart, and he has not punished us, but the Lord scourges those approaching him for admonition. –
Judith 8:28 And Ozias said to her, All that you said, you spoke with a good heart, and there is no one who will resist your words;
Judith 8:29 because your wisdom is not evident only today, but from the beginning of your days all the people have known your understanding, because the formation of your heart is good.
Judith 8:30 But the people have thirsted exceedingly and compelled us to do as we spoke to them and to bring upon ourselves an oath that we will not transgress.
Judith 8:31 And now petition on our behalf, because you are a devout woman, and the Lord will send rain to fill our cisterns, and we shall no longer fail.
Judith 8:32 And Ioudith said to them, Hear me, and I will do a deed that will reach generations of generations for the sons of our race.
Judith 8:33 You shall stand at the gate this night, and I will go out with my maid, and within the days after which you said you would hand the city over to our enemies, the Lord will visit Israel by my hand;
Judith 8:34 but you shall not investigate my action, for I will not tell you until what I am doing is accomplished.
Judith 8:35 And Ozias and the rulers said to her, Go in peace, and the Lord God be before you for vengeance upon our enemies.
Judith 8:36 And returning from the tent, they went to their appointed posts.

## Chapter 9

Judith 9:1 But Ioudith fell upon her face and put ashes upon her head and uncovered the sackcloth that she had put on, and the incense of that evening was just being offered in Jerusalem in the house of God, and Ioudith cried with a loud voice to the Lord and said,
Judith 9:2 Lord, God of my father Symeon, to whom you gave a sword in his hand for vengeance upon foreigners who loosened a virgin's womb for defilement and uncovered a thigh for shame and profaned a womb for reproach; for you said, It shall not be thus, and they did it;
Judith 9:3 because of which you gave their rulers to slaughter and their bedding, which had respected their deceit, deceived into blood, and struck slaves along with potentates and potentates upon their thrones,
Judith 9:4 and gave their wives as spoil and their daughters into captivity and all their spoils for division among sons loved by you, who also were zealous with your zeal and abhorred the defilement of their blood and called upon you as helper; God, my God, hear me also, the widow.
Judith 9:5 For you made the things before those and those things and the things afterward, and conceived the things now and the things coming, and what you thought came to be,
Judith 9:6 and what you planned stood forth and said, Behold, we are here; for all your ways are ready, and your judgment is in foreknowledge.
Judith 9:7 For behold, the Assyrians have multiplied in their force, have been exalted in horse and rider, have boasted in the arm of infantry, have hoped in shield and spear and bow and sling, and have not known that you are the Lord who crushes wars.
Judith 9:8 Lord is your name; shatter their strength by your power and break their might in your anger; for they have planned to profane your holy places, to defile the dwelling of the resting place of the name of your glory, to cast down the horn of your altar with iron.
Judith 9:9 Look upon their arrogance; send your wrath upon their heads; give into my hand, the widow's, the might that I have conceived.
Judith 9:10 Strike a slave along with a ruler from the lips of my deceit, and a ruler along with his attendant; break their exaltation by the hand of a female.
Judith 9:11 For your might is not in multitude, nor your dominion among the strong, but you are God of the lowly, helper of the lesser, supporter of the weak, shelterer of those given up, savior of the hopeless.
Judith 9:12 Yes, yes, God of my father and God of Israel's inheritance, master of the heavens and the earth, creator of the waters, king of all your creation, hear my petition,
Judith 9:13 and make my speech and deceit a wound and a bruise for those who have planned harsh things against your covenant and your sanctified house and the summit of Sion and the house possessed by your sons.
Judith 9:14 And bring about recognition among all your nation and every tribe, to know that you are God, God of all power and might, and there is no other who shields the race of Israel except you.

## Chapter 10

Judith 10:1 And it happened, when she ceased crying to the God of Israel and concluded all these words,
Judith 10:2 that she rose from her prostration and called her maid and went down into the house in which she stayed on sabbath days and at her festivals,
Judith 10:3 and removed the sackcloth that she had put on and took off the garments of her widowhood and washed her body with water and anointed herself with thick perfume and combed the hair of her head and put a headband upon it and put on the garments of her gladness, in which she clothed herself in the days of the life of her husband Manasses,
Judith 10:4 and took sandals for her feet and put on her anklets and bracelets and rings and earrings and all her adornment, and beautified herself exceedingly to deceive the eyes of men, as many as might see her.
Judith 10:5 And she gave her maid a wineskin of wine and a flask of oil, and filled a bag with barley meal and a cake of pressed fruit and clean loaves, and wrapped all her vessels and placed them upon her.
Judith 10:6 And they went out to the gate of the city of Baityloua and found Ozias and the elders of the city, Chabris and Charmis, standing at it;
Judith 10:7 but when they saw her, and her face was altered and her attire changed, they marveled exceedingly greatly at her beauty and said to her,
Judith 10:8 May the God of our fathers grant you favor and complete your undertakings for the pride of the sons of Israel and the exaltation of Jerusalem.
Judith 10:9 And she bowed to God and said to them, Command that the gate of the city be opened for me, and I will go out to accomplish the words that you spoke with me; and they directed the young men to open it for her as she had spoken.
Judith 10:10 And they did thus. And Ioudith went out, she and her slave girl with her; and the men of the city watched her from afar until she went down the mountain, until she passed through the valley and they no longer saw her. –
Judith 10:11 And they traveled straight ahead in the valley, and an outpost of the Assyrians met her.
Judith 10:12 And they seized her and asked, Of whom are you, and from where do you come, and where do you go? And she said, I am a daughter of the Hebrews, and I am fleeing from before them, because they are about to be given to you as food;
Judith 10:13 and I am coming into the presence of Holophernes, commander of your force, to report words of truth, and I will show before him a way by which he will travel and become master of all the hill country, and not one flesh of his men nor a breath of life will be lost.
Judith 10:14 But when the men heard her words and observed her face – and it was exceedingly marvelous in beauty before them – they said to her,
Judith 10:15 You have saved your life by hastening to come down into the presence of our lord; and now approach his tent, and some of us will escort you until they hand you over into his hands;
Judith 10:16 but when you stand before him, do not fear in your heart, but report according to your words, and he will treat you well.
Judith 10:17 And they chose one hundred men from themselves and joined them to her and her maid, and led them to Holophernes's tent.
Judith 10:18 And there was a running together throughout the camp, for her arrival was proclaimed through the dwellings; and coming, they encircled her as she stood outside Holophernes's tent, until they reported to him concerning her.
Judith 10:19 And they marveled at her beauty and marveled at the sons of Israel because of her, and each said to his neighbor, Who will despise this people, who has such women among itself? For it is not good to leave a single man of them remaining, who, if released, will be able to outwit all the land,
Judith 10:20 and those sleeping beside Holophernes and all his attendants came out and led her into the tent.
Judith 10:21 And Holophernes was resting upon his couch within the mosquito net, which was of purple and gold and emerald and costly stones interwoven.
Judith 10:22 And they reported to him concerning her, and he went out into the front of the tent, and silver lamps went before him.
Judith 10:23 But when Ioudith came before him and his attendants, they all marveled at the beauty of her face; and falling upon her face, she bowed to him, and his slaves raised her.

## Chapter 11

Judith 11:1 And Holophernes said to her, Take courage, woman; do not fear in your heart, because I have not mistreated a person who has chosen to serve King Nabouchodonosor of all the land.
Judith 11:2 And now, if your people inhabiting the hill country had not despised me, I would not have raised my spear against them; but they themselves did these things to themselves.
Judith 11:3 And now tell me for what reason you fled from them and came to us; for you have come for deliverance; take courage, you will live this night and afterward;
Judith 11:4 for there is no one who will wrong you, but he will treat you well, as happens to the slaves of my lord King Nabouchodonosor.
Judith 11:5 And Ioudith said to him, Receive the words of your slave woman, and let your slave girl speak before your face, and I will not report a falsehood to my lord this night.
Judith 11:6 And if you follow the words of your slave girl, God will accomplish a deed with you completely, and my lord will not fall short of his undertakings.
Judith 11:7 For King Nabouchodonosor of all the land lives, and his might lives, who sent you for the setting right of every soul, because not only do people serve him through you, but also the beasts of the field and the cattle and the birds of heaven will live through your strength under Nabouchodonosor and all his house.
Judith 11:8 For we heard your wisdom and the cunning deeds of your soul, and it was reported to all the land that you alone are good in all the kingdom and powerful in knowledge and marvelous in armies of war.
Judith 11:9 And now the word that Achior spoke in your council, we have heard his words, because the men of Baityloua preserved him, and he reported to them all that he spoke out beside you.
Judith 11:10 Therefore, master, lord, do not pass over his word, but place it in your heart, because it is true; for our race is not punished, nor does a sword prevail against them, unless they sin against their God.
Judith 11:11 And now, so that my lord may not become driven off and unsuccessful, and death will fall upon their face, and a sin has overtaken them, by which they will provoke their God to anger whenever they commit an improper deed.
Judith 11:12 Since their foods have failed them and all water has become scarce, they planned to lay hands upon their cattle and resolved to consume everything that God instructed them by his laws not to eat.
Judith 11:13 And the firstfruits of grain and the tithes of wine and oil that they kept safe, consecrating them for the priests standing in Jerusalem before the face of our God, they have judged to consume entirely, things that not even with the hands was it proper for anyone of the people to touch.
Judith 11:14 And they have sent to Jerusalem, because those dwelling there also did these things, those who will bring them the permission from the council of elders.
Judith 11:15 And it will be, when he reports to them and they do it, that they will be given to you for destruction on that day.
Judith 11:16 Therefore I, your slave woman, learning all these things, fled from before them, and God sent me to do deeds with you at which all the land will be astonished, as many as hear them.
Judith 11:17 Because your slave woman is God-fearing and serves the God of heaven night and day; and now I will remain beside you, my lord, and your slave woman will go out by night into the ravine, and I will pray to God, and he will tell me when they have committed their sins.
Judith 11:18 And coming, I will report to you, and you will go out with all your force, and there is no one among them who will resist you.
Judith 11:19 And I will lead you through the midst of Judea as far as coming before Jerusalem, and I will place your seat in its midst, and you will lead them as sheep who have no shepherd, and no dog will growl with its tongue before you; because these things were spoken to me according to my foreknowledge and reported to me, and I was sent to report to you. –
Judith 11:20 And her words pleased Holophernes and all his attendants, and they marveled at her wisdom and said,
Judith 11:21 There is no such woman from end to end of the land in beauty of face and understanding of words.
Judith 11:22 And Holophernes said to her, God did well by sending you before the people, so that might might come into our hands, but destruction among those who despised my lord.
Judith 11:23 And now you are lovely in your form and good in your words; because if you do as you have spoken, your God will be my God, and you will sit in King Nabouchodonosor's house and will be renowned throughout all the land.

## Chapter 12

Judith 12:1 And he commanded that she be brought in where his silverware was placed, and directed that a table be spread for her from his prepared dishes and that she drink from his wine.
Judith 12:2 And Ioudith said, I will not eat of them, so that there may be no stumbling block, but provision will be made from the things that have followed me.
Judith 12:3 And Holophernes said to her, But if the things with you run out, from where shall we bring out for you to give things like them? For there is no one of your race with us.
Judith 12:4 And Ioudith said to him, Your life lives, my lord, that your slave woman will not consume the things with me until the Lord does by my hand what he has planned.
Judith 12:5 And Holophernes's attendants led her into the tent, and she slept until the middle of the night; and she arose toward the morning watch.
Judith 12:6 And she sent to Holophernes, saying, Let my lord now command that your slave woman be allowed to go out for prayer;
Judith 12:7 and Holophernes commanded the bodyguards not to prevent her. And she remained in the camp three days; and she went out by night into the ravine of Baityloua and immersed herself in the camp at the spring of water;
Judith 12:8 and when she came up, she petitioned the Lord God of Israel to direct her way toward the raising up of the sons of his people;
Judith 12:9 and entering clean, she remained in the tent until she took her food toward evening.
Judith 12:10 And it happened on the fourth day that Holophernes held a drinking for his slaves alone and called none of those attending to duties to the invitation.
Judith 12:11 And he said to Bagoas the eunuch, who was in charge of all his possessions, Go now and persuade the Hebrew woman who is beside you to come to us and eat and drink with us;
Judith 12:12 for behold, it is shameful to our face if we let such a woman pass without having intercourse with her; because if we do not draw her to ourselves, she will mock us.
Judith 12:13 And Bagoas went out from Holophernes's presence and came in to her and said, Let this beautiful slave girl now not hesitate to come to my lord to be glorified before his face, and you shall drink wine with us for gladness and become on this day as one daughter of the sons of Assour who stand in Nabouchodonosor's house.
Judith 12:14 And Ioudith said to him, And who am I to contradict my lord? For everything that is pleasing in his eyes I will hasten to do, and this will be my rejoicing until the day of my death.
Judith 12:15 And rising, she adorned herself with clothing and all her feminine adornment, and her slave woman approached and spread on the ground for her opposite Holophernes the fleeces that she had received from Bagoas for her daily way of life, to eat reclining upon them.
Judith 12:16 And entering, Ioudith reclined, and Holophernes's heart was beside itself over her, and his soul was shaken, and he was exceedingly desirous to have intercourse with her; and he watched for an opportunity to deceive her from the day he saw her.
Judith 12:17 And Holophernes said to her, Drink now and be with us in gladness.
Judith 12:18 And Ioudith said, I will indeed drink, lord, because my living has been magnified in me today beyond all the days of my birth.
Judith 12:19 And taking, she ate and drank before him what her slave woman had prepared.
Judith 12:20 And Holophernes rejoiced because of her and drank exceedingly much wine, as much as he had never yet drunk on a single day since he was born.

## Chapter 13

Judith 13:1 But when evening came, his slaves hastened to depart. And Bagoas closed the tent from outside and shut out those attending from before his lord, and they went away to their beds; for they were all wearied because the drinking had gone on longer.
Judith 13:2 But Ioudith was left alone in the tent, and Holophernes fallen forward upon his couch; for the wine had flooded him.
Judith 13:3 And Ioudith told her slave woman to stand outside her bedchamber and watch for her departure as each day, for she said she would go out for her prayer; and she spoke to Bagoas according to these words.
Judith 13:4 And they all went away from before her, and no one was left in the bedchamber, from small to great; and Ioudith, standing beside his couch, said in her heart, Lord, God of all power, look upon the works of my hands at this hour for Jerusalem's exaltation;
Judith 13:5 because now is a time to support your inheritance and to carry out my undertaking for the crushing of enemies who have risen against us.
Judith 13:6 And approaching the bed rail that was at Holophernes's head, she took down his short sword from it,
Judith 13:7 and approaching the couch, grasped the hair of his head and said, Strengthen me, Lord, God of Israel, on this day.
Judith 13:8 And she struck into his neck twice with her strength and removed his head from him.
Judith 13:9 And she rolled his body off the bedding and removed the mosquito net from the posts; and after a little while she went out and handed Holophernes's head to her maid,
Judith 13:10 and she put it into her food bag. And the two went out together for prayer according to their custom; and passing through the camp, they went around that ravine and went up the mountain of Baityloua and came to its gates.
Judith 13:11 And Ioudith said from afar to those guarding at the gates, Open, open the gate now; God, our God, is with us, to do strength again in Israel and might against the enemies, as he has also done today.
Judith 13:12 And it happened, when the men of her city heard her voice, that they hastened to go down to the gate of their city and called together the elders of the city.
Judith 13:13 And they all ran together, from small to great among them, because her coming was unexpected to them, and they opened the gate and received them and, lighting a fire for illumination, encircled them.
Judith 13:14 But she said to them with a loud voice, Praise God, praise; praise God, who has not removed his mercy from the house of Israel, but has crushed our enemies through my hand this night.
Judith 13:15 And taking the head out of the bag, she showed it and said to them, Behold, the head of Holophernes, commander of Assour's force, and behold, the mosquito net in which he lay in his drunkenness; and the Lord struck him by the hand of a female;
Judith 13:16 and the Lord lives, who preserved me in my way on which I traveled, that my face deceived him for his destruction, and he committed no sin with me for defilement and shame.
Judith 13:17 And all the people were exceedingly astonished and bent down and bowed to God and said with one accord, Blessed are you, our God, who has brought the enemies of your people to nothing on this day today.
Judith 13:18 And Ozias said to her, Blessed are you, daughter, by God Most High beyond all the women upon the earth, and blessed is the Lord God who created the heavens and the earth, who directed you to wound the head of the ruler of our enemies;
Judith 13:19 because your hope will not depart from the heart of people remembering God's strength forever;
Judith 13:20 and may God do these things for you for eternal height, to visit you with good things, because you did not spare your life on account of the humiliation of our race, but came forth against our fall, traveling straight before our God. And all the people said, May it be, may it be.

## Chapter 14

Judith 14:1 And Ioudith said to them, Hear me now, brothers, and take this head and hang it upon the battlement of your wall.
Judith 14:2 And it shall be, when dawn shines through and the sun comes out upon the earth, each of you will take up your equipment for war, and every strong man will go out of the city, and you will give them a leader as though going down upon the plain to the outpost of the sons of Assour, and you will not go down.
Judith 14:3 And these men, taking up their full armor, will go to their camp and awaken the generals of the force of Assour; and they will run together to the tent of Olophernes and will not find him, and fear will fall upon them, and they will flee from before you.
Judith 14:4 And you and all who inhabit every territory of Israel, following after them, lay them low in their roads.
Judith 14:5 But before doing these things, call for me Achior the Ammanite, so that, seeing, he may recognize the one who despised the house of Israel and sent him to us as though to death.
Judith 14:6 And they called Achior from the house of Ozias; and when he came and saw the head of Olophernes in the hand of one man in the assembly of the people, he fell upon his face, and his spirit failed.
Judith 14:7 And when they lifted him up, he fell at the feet of Ioudith and bowed before her face and said, Blessed are you in every dwelling of Iouda and in every nation, who, hearing your name, will be troubled;
Judith 14:8 and now tell me all that you did in these days. And Ioudith told him in the midst of the people everything that she had done from the day she went out until she was speaking to them.
Judith 14:9 And when she ceased speaking, the people shouted with a great voice and gave a joyful cry in their city.
Judith 14:10 And Achior, seeing everything that the God of Israel had done, believed in God exceedingly and circumcised the flesh of his foreskin and was added to the house of Israel until this day.
Judith 14:11 And when dawn arose, they hung the head of Olophernes from the wall, and every man took up his weapons, and they went out in companies onto the ascents of the mountain.
Judith 14:12 And when the sons of Assour saw them, they sent to their leaders; and these came to the generals and commanders of thousands and to every ruler of theirs.
Judith 14:13 And they came to the tent of Olophernes and said to the one who was over everything of his, Awaken our lord now, because the slaves have dared to come down against us for war, so that they may be utterly destroyed.
Judith 14:14 And Bagoas went in and struck the curtain of the tent; for he supposed that he was sleeping with Ioudith.
Judith 14:15 And when no one answered, he parted it and entered the bedchamber and found him cast dead upon the bedframe, and his head had been removed from him.
Judith 14:16 And he cried out with a great voice, with weeping and groaning and a mighty cry, and tore his garments.
Judith 14:17 And he went into the tent where Ioudith had been lodging and did not find her; and he sprang out to the people and cried out,
Judith 14:18 The slaves have acted treacherously; one woman of the Hebrews has brought shame upon the house of King Nabouchodonosor; for behold, Olophernes is on the ground, and his head is not upon him.
Judith 14:19 And when the rulers of the force of Assour heard these words, they tore their tunics, and their soul was exceedingly troubled, and their shouting and crying became exceedingly great in the midst of the camp.

## Chapter 15

Judith 15:1 And when those in the dwellings heard, they were astounded at what had happened,
Judith 15:2 and trembling and fear fell upon them, and there was no man remaining before his neighbor any longer, but pouring out with one accord, they fled along every road of the plain and the hill country;
Judith 15:3 and those encamped in the hill country around Baityloua also turned to flight. And then the sons of Israel, every warrior among them, poured out upon them.
Judith 15:4 And Ozias sent to Baitomasthaim and Bebai and Chobai and Kola and to every territory of Israel those who would report concerning the things accomplished, and so that all might pour out upon the enemies to kill them.
Judith 15:5 And when the sons of Israel heard, they all fell upon them with one accord and cut them down as far as Choba. Likewise those from Jerusalem and from all the hill country also arrived, for they had reported to them what had happened to the camp of their enemies; and those in Galaad and those in Galilee outflanked them with a great blow until they passed Damascus and its territories.
Judith 15:6 And the rest who inhabited Baityloua fell upon the camp of Assour and plundered them and became exceedingly rich.
Judith 15:7 And the sons of Israel, returning from the slaughter, took possession of the remaining things, and the villages and farmsteads in the hill country and the plain gained much spoil, for there was an exceedingly great abundance.
Judith 15:8 And Ioakim the great priest and the council of elders of the sons of Israel who inhabited Jerusalem came to behold the good things which the Lord had done for Israel and to see Ioudith and speak peace with her.
Judith 15:9 And when they came in to her, they all blessed her with one accord and said to her, You are the exaltation of Jerusalem, you are the great pride of Israel, you are the great boast of our race;
Judith 15:10 you did all these things by your hand, you did good things with Israel, and God was pleased with them; be blessed by the almighty Lord for everlasting time. And all the people said, May it be.
Judith 15:11 And all the people plundered the camp for thirty days; and they gave Ioudith the tent of Olophernes and all the silverware and the beds and the basins and all his furnishings, and she took them and placed them upon her mule and yoked her wagons and heaped them upon them.
Judith 15:12 And every woman of Israel ran together to see her, and they blessed her and formed a dance of themselves for her, and she took thyrsi in her hands and gave them to the women with her;
Judith 15:13 and they crowned themselves with olive, she and those with her, and she went before all the people in a dance, leading all the women, and every man of Israel followed, armed and with crowns, and they sang hymns with their mouths.
Judith 15:14 And Ioudith led this thanksgiving in all Israel, and all the people sang out this praise

## Chapter 16

Judith 16:1 and Ioudith said, Lead off for my God with tambourines, sing to the Lord with cymbals, fit together for him a psalm and praise, exalt and call upon his name,
Judith 16:2 because the Lord is a God who crushes wars, because into his camps in the midst of the people he rescued me from the hand of those pursuing me.
Judith 16:3 Assour came from mountains from the north; he came with myriads of his force, whose multitude blocked torrents, and their cavalry covered hills;
Judith 16:4 he said he would burn my territories and kill my young men with the sword and put my sucklings upon the ground and give my infants over to plunder and despoil my virgins.
Judith 16:5 The almighty Lord thwarted them by the hand of a female.
Judith 16:6 For their mighty man did not fall by young men, nor did sons of Titans strike him, nor did tall giants attack him, but Ioudith daughter of Merari disabled him by the beauty of her face,
Judith 16:7 for she took off the robe of her widowhood for the exaltation of those toiling in Israel, anointed her face with perfume
Judith 16:8 and bound her hair with a turban and took a linen robe to deceive him;
Judith 16:9 her sandal seized his eye, and her beauty took his soul captive; the short sword passed through his neck.
Judith 16:10 Persians shuddered at her daring, and Medes were troubled at her boldness;
Judith 16:11 then my lowly ones shouted, and my weak ones became afraid and were terrified; they lifted up their voice and were overturned;
Judith 16:12 sons of girls pierced them and wounded them as children of deserters; they perished by the battle array of my Lord.
Judith 16:13 I will sing a new hymn to my God: Lord, you are great and glorious, wonderful in strength, unsurpassable.
Judith 16:14 Let all your creation serve you; because you spoke, and they came to be; you sent forth your spirit, and it built; and there is no one who will resist your voice.
Judith 16:15 For mountains will be shaken from their foundations together with waters, and rocks will melt like wax before you; but still, to those who fear you, you will be gracious to them.
Judith 16:16 Because every sacrifice is a small thing for a fragrant odor, and all fat is a very little thing for a whole burnt offering to you; but the one who fears the Lord is great continually.
Judith 16:17 Woe to nations rising against my race; the almighty Lord will punish them on the day of judgment, to give fire and worms into their flesh, and they will weep in awareness for the age.
Judith 16:18 And when they came to Jerusalem, they worshiped God, and when the people were purified, they offered their whole burnt offerings and their voluntary offerings and gifts.
Judith 16:19 And Ioudith dedicated all the equipment of Olophernes which the people gave her, and the canopy which she took for herself from his bedchamber she gave as a dedication to God.
Judith 16:20 And the people were rejoicing in Jerusalem before the holy things for three months, and Ioudith remained with them.
Judith 16:21 And after these days each departed to his inheritance, and Ioudith went away to Baityloua and remained upon her property; and in her time she became glorious in all the land.
Judith 16:22 And many desired her, and no man knew her all the days of her life from the day Manasses her husband died and was added to his people.
Judith 16:23 And she advanced to a very great age and grew old in the house of her husband, one hundred five years; and she released her maidservant as a free woman. And she died in Baityloua, and they buried her in the cave of her husband Manasses,
Judith 16:24 and the house of Israel mourned her seven days. And she divided her possessions before she died among all the nearest relatives of Manasses her husband and the nearest relatives of her race.
Judith 16:25 And there was no longer anyone who terrified the sons of Israel in the days of Ioudith and for many days after her death.

# 1 Tobit

The Apostolic Bible. Public domain. https://apostolic-bible.ysys9.chatgpt.site/license.html


## Chapter 1

1 Tobit 1:1 Book of the words of Tobit, of Tobiel, of Ananiel, of Adouel, of Gabael, from the seed of Asiel, from the tribe of Nephthalim,
1 Tobit 1:2 who was taken captive in the days of Enemessaros the king of the Assyrians from Thisbe, which is to the right of Kydios of Nephthalim in Galilee, above Aser.
1 Tobit 1:3 I, Tobit, walked in ways of truth and righteousness all the days of my life and performed many acts of mercy for my brothers and the nation, those who traveled together with me to the country of the Assyrians, to Nineue.
1 Tobit 1:4 And when I was in my country in the land of Israel, when I was younger, the whole tribe of Nephthalim my father departed from the house of Jerusalem, which was chosen from all the tribes of Israel for all the tribes to sacrifice; and the temple of the dwelling of the Most High was sanctified and built for all the generations of the age.
1 Tobit 1:5 And all the tribes that departed together sacrificed to Baal the heifer, and the house of Nephthalim my father.
1 Tobit 1:6 And I alone traveled many times to Jerusalem at the feasts, as it is written for all Israel in an eternal ordinance, having the firstfruits and the tithes of the produce and the first shearings;
1 Tobit 1:7 and I gave them to the priests, the sons of Aaron, at the altar; of all the produce I gave the tithe to the sons of Leui who served in Jerusalem. And I sold the second tithe and traveled and spent these things in Jerusalem each year.
1 Tobit 1:8 And I gave the third to those to whom it was due, as Debbora my father's mother commanded, because I was left an orphan by my father.
1 Tobit 1:9 And when I became a man, I took Anna as a wife from the seed of our paternal family and begot Tobias by her.
1 Tobit 1:10 And when I was taken captive to Nineue, all my brothers and those of my race ate of the breads of the nations;
1 Tobit 1:11 but I guarded my soul against eating,
1 Tobit 1:12 because I remembered God with my whole soul.
1 Tobit 1:13 And the Most High gave favor and form before Enemessaros, and I was his buyer;
1 Tobit 1:14 and I traveled to Media and deposited ten talents of silver with Gabael the brother of Gabrias in Ragoi of Media.
1 Tobit 1:15 And when Enemessaros died, Sennacherim his son reigned in his place, and his roads became unsettled, and I was no longer able to travel to Media.
1 Tobit 1:16 And in the days of Enemessaros I performed many acts of mercy for my brothers;
1 Tobit 1:17 I gave my breads to the hungry and my garments to the naked, and if I saw anyone of my race dead and cast behind the wall of Nineue, I buried him.
1 Tobit 1:18 And if Sennacherim the king killed anyone when he came fleeing from Judea, I buried them, stealing them; for he killed many in his anger; and the bodies were sought by the king and were not found.
1 Tobit 1:19 And one of those in Nineue went and informed the king concerning me, that I bury them, and I hid; and learning that I was sought to be put to death, I withdrew in fear.
1 Tobit 1:20 And all my possessions were plundered, and nothing was left to me except Anna my wife and Tobios my son.
1 Tobit 1:21 And fifty days had not passed before his two sons killed him; and they fled to the mountains of Ararat, and Sacherdonos his son reigned in his place. And he appointed Achiacharos of Anael, son of my brother, over all the accounting of his kingdom and over all the administration.
1 Tobit 1:22 And Achiacharos petitioned concerning me, and I came to Nineue. And Achiacharos was the cupbearer and in charge of the ring and administrator and accountant, and Sacherdonos appointed him a second time; and he was my cousin.

## Chapter 2

1 Tobit 2:1 And when I came down to my house and Anna my wife and Tobias my son were restored to me, at Pentecost, the feast which is holy, of seven weeks, a fine meal was prepared for me, and I reclined to eat.
1 Tobit 2:2 And I beheld many dishes and said to my son, Go and bring whoever you find among our brothers in need, who remembers the Lord; and behold, I will wait for you.
1 Tobit 2:3 And coming, he said, Father, one of our race has been strangled and cast into the marketplace.
1 Tobit 2:4 And before tasting anything, I sprang up and took him up into a certain building until the sun set.
1 Tobit 2:5 And returning, I bathed and ate my bread in grief;
1 Tobit 2:6 and I remembered the prophecy of Amos, as he said, Your feasts will be turned into mourning and all your rejoicings into lamentation; and I wept.
1 Tobit 2:7 And when the sun set, I went away and dug and buried him.
1 Tobit 2:8 And the neighbors laughed, saying, He is no longer afraid of being murdered on account of this matter; and he ran away, and behold, again he buries the dead.
1 Tobit 2:9 And that very night I returned after burying him and slept, defiled, beside the wall of the courtyard, and my face was uncovered;
1 Tobit 2:10 and I did not know that little birds were in the wall, and while my eyes were open, the little birds deposited hot droppings into my eyes, and white films developed in my eyes. And I went to physicians, and they did not help me; and Achiacharos supported me until he traveled to Elymais.
1 Tobit 2:11 And Anna my wife worked for hire at women's work;
1 Tobit 2:12 and she sent it to the owners, and they themselves paid her the wage, also giving a kid in addition.
1 Tobit 2:13 And when it came to me, it began to cry; and I said to her, Where is the little kid from? Surely it is not stolen? Return it to the owners; for it is not lawful to eat something stolen.
1 Tobit 2:14 And she said, It has been given to me as a gift in addition to the wage. And I did not believe her and told her to return it to the owners and reddened toward her; and answering, she said to me, Where are your acts of mercy and your righteous deeds? Behold, everything is known with you.

## Chapter 3

1 Tobit 3:1 And grieved, I wept and prayed with anguish, saying,
1 Tobit 3:2 You are righteous, Lord, and all your works and all your ways are acts of mercy and truth, and you judge a true and righteous judgment for the age.
1 Tobit 3:3 Remember me and look upon me; do not punish me for my sins and my unwitting offenses and those of my fathers, which I committed before you;
1 Tobit 3:4 for they disobeyed your commandments. You gave us over to plunder and captivity and death and a proverb of reproach to all the nations among which we have been scattered.
1 Tobit 3:5 And now many of your judgments are true, to execute upon me concerning my sins and those of my fathers, because we did not perform your commandments; for we did not walk in truth before you.
1 Tobit 3:6 And now do with me according to what is pleasing before you; command that my spirit be taken up, so that I may be released and become earth; because it profits me to die rather than live, because I heard false reproaches, and there is much grief in me; command that I be released from distress now to the eternal place; do not turn your face away from me.
1 Tobit 3:7 On the same day it happened to Sarra the daughter of Ragouel in Ekbatana of Media that she too was reproached by her father's maidservants,
1 Tobit 3:8 because she had been given to seven men, and Asmodaus the evil demon killed them before they were with her as with women. And they said to her, Do you not understand, strangling your husbands? You already had seven and benefited from none of them.
1 Tobit 3:9 Why do you scourge us? If they died, go with them; may we not see a son or daughter of yours for the age.
1 Tobit 3:10 Hearing these things, she grieved exceedingly, so as to hang herself. And she said, I am my father's only one; if I do this, it is a reproach to him, and I will bring his old age down with anguish into Hades.
1 Tobit 3:11 And she petitioned beside the window and said, Blessed are you, Lord my God, and blessed is your holy and honored name for the ages; may all your works bless you for the age.
1 Tobit 3:12 And now, Lord, I have directed my eyes and my face toward you;
1 Tobit 3:13 command that I be released from the earth and no longer hear reproach.
1 Tobit 3:14 You know, Lord, that I am clean from every sin of a man
1 Tobit 3:15 and have not defiled my name or my father's name in the land of my captivity. I am my father's only child, and he has no child who will inherit from him, nor a brother nearby nor a son belonging to him, so that I may keep myself as a wife for him. Seven have already perished for me; why should I live? And if it does not seem good to you to kill me, command that I be looked upon and shown mercy and no longer hear reproach.
1 Tobit 3:16 And the prayer of both was heard before the glory of the great Raphael,
1 Tobit 3:17 and he was sent to heal the two, to peel away Tobit's white films and give Sarra of Ragouel to Tobias the son of Tobit as a wife and bind Asmodaus the evil demon, because it falls to Tobias to inherit her. At that very time Tobit returned and entered his house, and Sarra of Ragouel came down from her upper room.

## Chapter 4

1 Tobit 4:1 On that day Tobit remembered concerning the silver which he deposited with Gabael in Rhagoi of Media,
1 Tobit 4:2 and said within himself, I asked for death; why do I not call Tobias my son, so that I may inform him before I die?
1 Tobit 4:3 And calling him, he said, Child, if I die, bury me; and do not disregard your mother; honor her all the days of your life and do what is pleasing to her and do not grieve her.
1 Tobit 4:4 Remember, child, that she has seen many dangers on account of you in the womb; when she dies, bury her beside me in one grave.
1 Tobit 4:5 All the days, child, remember the Lord our God and do not desire to sin and transgress his commandments; do righteousness all the days of your life and do not walk in the ways of injustice;
1 Tobit 4:6 because when you do truth, there will be prosperity in your works.
1 Tobit 4:7 And to all who do righteousness, show mercy from your possessions, and let your eye not begrudge your showing mercy; do not turn your face away from any poor person, and the face of God will certainly not be turned away from you.
1 Tobit 4:8 As you have possessions, according to their abundance show mercy from them; if you have little, do not be afraid to show mercy according to the little;
1 Tobit 4:9 for you store up a good deposit for yourself for a day of distress;
1 Tobit 4:10 because mercy delivers from death and does not allow one to enter into darkness;
1 Tobit 4:11 for mercy is a good gift for all who perform it before the Most High.
1 Tobit 4:12 Guard yourself, child, against all fornication, and first take a wife from the seed of your fathers; do not take a foreign wife who is not from your father's tribe, because we are sons of prophets. Noe, Abraam, Isaak, Iakob, our fathers from of old—remember, child, that all these took wives from their brothers and were blessed in their children, and their seed will inherit land.
1 Tobit 4:13 And now, child, love your brothers and do not be arrogant in your heart toward your brothers and the sons and daughters of your people, to take a wife for yourself from them, because in arrogance there is destruction and much disorder, and in uselessness there is decrease and great need; for uselessness is the mother of famine.
1 Tobit 4:14 Let the wage of every person who works not lodge with you, but pay him immediately, and if you serve God, it will be repaid to you. Guard yourself, child, in all your works, and be disciplined in all your conduct.
1 Tobit 4:15 And what you hate, do to no one. Do not drink wine to drunkenness, and let drunkenness not travel with you on your road.
1 Tobit 4:16 Give from your bread to a hungry person and from your garments to the naked; everything that is surplus for you, give in mercy, and let your eye not begrudge your showing mercy.
1 Tobit 4:17 Pour out your breads upon the grave of the righteous and do not give to sinners.
1 Tobit 4:18 Seek counsel from every prudent person and do not despise any useful counsel.
1 Tobit 4:19 And at every time bless the Lord God and ask of him that your roads may become straight and all your paths and counsels prosper; because no nation has counsel, but the Lord himself gives all good things and humbles whomever he wishes, as he wills. And now, child, remember my commandments, and let them not be erased from your heart.
1 Tobit 4:20 And now I show you the ten talents of silver which I deposited with Gabael of Gabrias in Rhagoi of Media.
1 Tobit 4:21 And do not be afraid, child, because we have become poor; you have much if you fear God and depart from every sin and do what is pleasing before him.

## Chapter 5

1 Tobit 5:1 And answering, Tobias said to him, Father, I will do everything that you have commanded me;
1 Tobit 5:2 but how will I be able to receive the silver, when I do not know him?
1 Tobit 5:3 And he gave him the written bond and said to him, Seek for yourself a man who will travel with you, and I will give him a wage while I live; and go and receive the silver.
1 Tobit 5:4 And he went to seek a man and found Raphael, who was an angel, and he did not know;
1 Tobit 5:5 and he said to him, Can I travel with you in Rhagoi of Media, and are you experienced in the places?
1 Tobit 5:6 And the angel said to him, I will travel with you, and I am experienced in the road, and I lodged with Gabael our brother.
1 Tobit 5:7 And Tobias said to him, Wait for me, and I will tell my father.
1 Tobit 5:8 And he said to him, Go, and do not delay.
1 Tobit 5:9 And going in, he said to his father, Behold, I have found one who will travel with me. And he said, Call him to me, so that I may learn of which tribe he is and whether he is faithful to travel with you.
1 Tobit 5:10 And he called him, and he went in, and they greeted one another.
1 Tobit 5:11 And Tobit said to him, Brother, from which tribe and from which homeland are you? Inform me.
1 Tobit 5:12 And he said to him, Are you seeking a tribe and paternal family or a hired man who will travel with your son? And Tobit said to him, I wish, brother, to learn your race and name.
1 Tobit 5:13 And he said, I am Azarias of Ananias the great, of your brothers.
1 Tobit 5:14 And he said to him, May you come in health, brother; and do not be angry with me because I sought to learn your tribe and paternal family. And you happen to be my brother from the fine and good lineage; for I knew Ananias and Iathan, the sons of Semeias the great, when we traveled together to Jerusalem to worship, bringing up the firstborn and the tithes of the produce, and they did not go astray in the error of our brothers. You are from a good root, brother.
1 Tobit 5:15 But tell me what wage I shall give you: a drachma a day and your necessities, as also for my son?
1 Tobit 5:16 And I will add still more to your wage if you return in health.
1 Tobit 5:17 And they agreed thus. And he said to Tobias, Become ready for the road; and may you prosper. And his son prepared the things for the road. And his father said to him, Go with the man; and God who dwells in heaven will prosper your road, and let his angel travel with you. And both went out to depart, and the boy's dog with them.
1 Tobit 5:18 And Anna his mother wept and said to Tobit, Why have you sent our child away? Is he not the staff of our hand as he goes in and goes out before us?
1 Tobit 5:19 May silver not overtake silver, but may it become a thing cast away for our child;
1 Tobit 5:20 for as living has been given to us by the Lord, this is sufficient for us.
1 Tobit 5:21 And Tobit said to her, Do not be concerned, sister; he will come in health, and your eyes will see him;
1 Tobit 5:22 for a good angel will travel with him, and his road will prosper, and he will return in health.
1 Tobit 5:23 And she ceased weeping.

## Chapter 6

1 Tobit 6:1 And those traveling the road came in the evening to the Tigris river and lodged there.
1 Tobit 6:2 And the boy went down to wash himself, and a fish sprang up from the river and wished to swallow the boy.
1 Tobit 6:3 And the angel said to him, Take hold of the fish. And the boy seized the fish and cast it up onto the land.
1 Tobit 6:4 And the angel said to him, Cut open the fish, and take the heart and the liver and the gall and put them away safely.
1 Tobit 6:5 And the boy did as the angel told him, and roasting the fish, they ate.
1 Tobit 6:6 And both traveled until they drew near in Ekbatana.
1 Tobit 6:7 And the boy said to the angel, Azarias, brother, what are the liver and the heart and the gall of the fish?
1 Tobit 6:8 And he said to him, The heart and the liver, if a demon or an evil spirit troubles anyone, these must be burned to make smoke before a man or woman, and that person will certainly no longer be troubled;
1 Tobit 6:9 and the gall, to anoint a person who has white films in the eyes, and he will be healed.
1 Tobit 6:10 And as they drew near to Rage,
1 Tobit 6:11 the angel said to the boy, Brother, today we will lodge with Ragouel, and he is your relative, and he has an only daughter named Sarra;
1 Tobit 6:12 I will speak concerning her being given to you as a wife, because her inheritance falls to you, and you alone are of her race; and the girl is beautiful and prudent.
1 Tobit 6:13 And now hear me, and I will speak to her father, and when we return from Rhagoi, we will hold the wedding. Because I know Ragouel, that he will certainly not give her to another man according to the law of Moses, or he will owe death, because it belongs to you to receive the inheritance rather than any man.
1 Tobit 6:14 Then the boy said to the angel, Azarias, brother, I have heard that the girl has been given to seven men and that all have perished in the bridal chamber.
1 Tobit 6:15 And now I am my father's only one, and I am afraid lest I go in and die as also the former ones, because a demon loves her, which harms no one except those approaching her. And now I am afraid lest I die and bring the life of my father and my mother down with anguish over me into their grave; and they have no other son who will bury them.
1 Tobit 6:16 And the angel said to him, Do you not remember the words which your father commanded you concerning taking a wife from your race? And now hear me, brother, because she will be your wife, and take no account of the demon, because this night she will be given to you as a wife.
1 Tobit 6:17 And if you enter the bridal chamber, you will take ashes of incense and place some of the heart and the liver of the fish upon them and make smoke, and the demon will smell it and flee and will not return for the age of the age.
1 Tobit 6:18 And when you approach her, arise, both of you, and cry out to the merciful God, and he will save you and have mercy; do not be afraid, because she was prepared for you from of old, and you will save her, and she will travel with you, and I suppose that you will have children by her.
1 Tobit 6:19 And when Tobias heard these things, he loved her, and his soul clung to her exceedingly.

## Chapter 7

1 Tobit 7:1 And they came to Ekbatana and arrived at the house of Ragouel, and Sarra met them and greeted them, and they her, and she brought them into the house.
1 Tobit 7:2 And Ragouel said to Edna his wife, How like Tobit my cousin the young man is.
1 Tobit 7:3 And Ragouel asked them, Where are you from, brothers? And they said to him, From the sons of Nephthali, the captives in Nineue.
1 Tobit 7:4 And he said to them, Do you know Tobit our brother? And they said, We know him.
1 Tobit 7:5 And he said to them, Is he healthy? And they said, He both lives and is healthy; and Tobias said, He is my father.
1 Tobit 7:6 And Ragouel sprang up and kissed him and wept and blessed him and said to him, You of the fine and good man; and hearing that Tobit had lost his eyes, he grieved and wept.
1 Tobit 7:7 And Edna his wife and Sarra his daughter wept and welcomed them eagerly.
1 Tobit 7:8 And they slaughtered a ram of the sheep and set several dishes before them.
1 Tobit 7:9 And Tobias said to Raphael, Azarias, brother, speak concerning the things you were saying on the journey, and let the matter be accomplished.
1 Tobit 7:10 And he communicated the word to Ragouel. And Ragouel said to Tobias, Eat and drink and be glad; for it belongs to you to take my child; nevertheless I will show you the truth.
1 Tobit 7:11 I gave my child to seven men, and whenever they went in to her, they died during the night. But for the present, be glad.
1 Tobit 7:12 And Tobias said, I will taste nothing here until you establish it and stand with me. And Ragouel said, Take her from now according to the judgment; and you are her brother, and she is yours; and the merciful God will prosper the best things for you.
1 Tobit 7:13 And he called Sarra his daughter and took her hand and gave her to Tobias as a wife and said, Behold, according to the law of Moses take her and lead her away to your father; and he blessed them.
1 Tobit 7:14 And he called Edna his wife; and taking a document, he wrote a contract, and they sealed it. And they began to eat.
1 Tobit 7:15 And Ragouel called Edna his wife and said to her, Sister, prepare the other chamber and bring her in.
1 Tobit 7:16 And she did as he said and brought her there and wept; and she received her daughter's tears and said to her,
1 Tobit 7:17 Take courage, child; may the Lord of heaven and earth give you favor in place of this grief of yours; take courage, daughter.

## Chapter 8

1 Tobit 8:1 And when they finished dining, they brought Tobias in to her.
1 Tobit 8:2 And as he went, he remembered Raphael's words and took the ashes of the incense and placed the fish's heart and liver upon them and made smoke.
1 Tobit 8:3 And when the demon smelled the odor, it fled to the uppermost parts of Egypt, and the angel bound it.
1 Tobit 8:4 And when both were shut in together, Tobias arose from the bed and said, Arise, sister, and let us pray, so that the Lord may have mercy on us.
1 Tobit 8:5 And Tobias began to say, Blessed are you, God of our fathers, and blessed is your holy and glorious name for the ages; may the heavens and all your creations bless you.
1 Tobit 8:6 You made Adam and gave him Eua as a helper, a support, his wife; from these came the seed of people. You said, It is not good for the man to be alone; let us make him a helper like him.
1 Tobit 8:7 And now, Lord, I take this sister of mine because of truth, not because of fornication; command that I be shown mercy and grow old together with her.
1 Tobit 8:8 And she said with him, Amen.
1 Tobit 8:9 And both slept the night.
1 Tobit 8:10 And Ragouel arose and went and dug a grave, saying, Lest this one also die.
1 Tobit 8:11 And Ragouel came to his house
1 Tobit 8:12 and said to Edna his wife, Send one of the maidservants, and let them see whether he lives; and if not, so that we may bury him and no one know.
1 Tobit 8:13 And the maidservant went in, opening the door, and found the two sleeping.
1 Tobit 8:14 And going out, she reported to them that he lives.
1 Tobit 8:15 And Ragouel blessed God, saying, Blessed are you, God, with every pure and holy blessing, and let your holy ones and all your creations bless you, and let all your angels and your chosen ones bless you for all the ages.
1 Tobit 8:16 Blessed are you because you gladdened me, and it did not happen to me as I supposed, but according to your abundant mercy you dealt with us.
1 Tobit 8:17 Blessed are you because you showed mercy to two only children; show them mercy, Master; bring their life to completion in health with gladness and mercy.
1 Tobit 8:18 And he ordered the household servants to fill in the grave.
1 Tobit 8:19 And he held a wedding for them of fourteen days.
1 Tobit 8:20 And before the days of the wedding were completed, Ragouel told him under oath that he was not to go out unless the fourteen days of the wedding were fulfilled,
1 Tobit 8:21 and then to take half his possessions and travel in health to his father; and the remaining things, when I and my wife die.

## Chapter 9

1 Tobit 9:1 And Tobias called Raphael and said to him,
1 Tobit 9:2 Azarias, brother, take with yourself a servant and two camels and travel to Gabael in Rhagoi of Media and bring me the silver and lead him to the wedding;
1 Tobit 9:3 because Ragouel has sworn that I am not to go out,
1 Tobit 9:4 and my father counts the days, and if I delay greatly, he will be exceedingly distressed.
1 Tobit 9:5 And Raphael traveled and lodged with Gabael and gave him the written bond; and he brought out the little bags with their seals and gave them to him.
1 Tobit 9:6 And they arose early together and came to the wedding. And Tobias blessed his wife.

## Chapter 10

1 Tobit 10:1 And Tobit his father calculated each day; and when the days of the journey were fulfilled and they did not come,
1 Tobit 10:2 he said, Perhaps they have been put to shame? Or perhaps Gabael died and no one gives him the silver?
1 Tobit 10:3 And he grieved greatly.
1 Tobit 10:4 And his wife said to him, The child has perished, because he has delayed; and she began to lament him and said,
1 Tobit 10:5 Does it not concern me, child, that I let you go, the light of my eyes?
1 Tobit 10:6 And Tobit says to her, Be silent, do not be concerned; he is healthy.
1 Tobit 10:7 And she said to him, Be silent, do not deceive me; my child has perished. And each day she went out to the road by which he had departed, and by day she ate no bread, and at night she did not cease lamenting Tobias her son, until the fourteen days of the wedding were completed, which Ragouel swore to have him spend there.
1 Tobit 10:8 And Tobias said to Ragouel, Send me away, because my father and my mother no longer hope to see me.
1 Tobit 10:9 And his father-in-law said to him, Remain with me, and I will send to your father, and they will tell him the things concerning you. And Tobias says, No, but send me away to my father.
1 Tobit 10:10 And Ragouel arose and gave him Sarra his wife and half the possessions, persons and livestock and silver;
1 Tobit 10:11 and blessing them, he sent them away, saying, The God of heaven will prosper you, children, before I die.
1 Tobit 10:12 And he said to his daughter, Honor your parents-in-law; they are now your parents; may I hear a good report of you. And he kissed her.
1 Tobit 10:13 And Edna said to Tobias, Beloved brother, may the Lord of heaven restore you and grant me to see your children from Sarra my daughter, so that I may rejoice before the Lord; and behold, I entrust my daughter to you as a deposit; do not grieve her.
1 Tobit 10:14 After these things Tobias traveled, blessing God because he prospered his road, and he blessed Ragouel and Edna his wife.

## Chapter 11

1 Tobit 11:1 And he traveled until they drew near to Nineue. And Raphael said to Tobias,
1 Tobit 11:2 Do you not know, brother, how you left your father?
1 Tobit 11:3 Let us run ahead of your wife and prepare the house;
