1 Tobit 11:4 and take the fish's gall ready at hand. And they traveled, and the dog went along behind them.
1 Tobit 11:5 And Anna sat looking about along the road for her child;
1 Tobit 11:6 and she noticed him coming and said to his father, Behold, your son is coming, and the man who traveled with him.
1 Tobit 11:7 And Raphael said, I know that your father will open his eyes;
1 Tobit 11:8 you, therefore, anoint the gall into his eyes, and stung, he will rub them and cast off the white films and see you.
1 Tobit 11:9 And Anna ran forward and fell upon her son's neck and said to him, I have seen you, child; from now I shall die. And both wept.
1 Tobit 11:10 And Tobit went out toward the door and stumbled, and his son ran forward to him
1 Tobit 11:11 and took hold of his father and sprinkled the gall upon his father's eyes, saying, Take courage, father.
1 Tobit 11:12 And when they were stung, he rubbed his eyes, and the white films peeled away from the corners of his eyes.
1 Tobit 11:13 And seeing his son, he fell upon his neck and wept and said,
1 Tobit 11:14 Blessed are you, God, and blessed is your name for the ages, and blessed are all your holy angels; because you scourged me and showed me mercy, behold, I see Tobias my son.
1 Tobit 11:15 And his son entered rejoicing and reported to his father the great things that had happened to him in Media.
1 Tobit 11:16 And Tobit went out to meet his bride, rejoicing and blessing God, at the gate of Nineue; and those who beheld him walking marveled because he could see, and Tobit gave thanks before them because God had shown him mercy.
1 Tobit 11:17 And when Tobit approached Sarra his bride, he blessed her, saying, May you come in health, daughter; blessed is God who brought you to us, and your father and your mother.
1 Tobit 11:18 And there was joy for all his brothers in Nineue.
1 Tobit 11:19 And Achiacharos and Nasbas his cousin arrived, and Tobias's wedding was held with gladness for seven days.

## Chapter 12

1 Tobit 12:1 And Tobit called Tobias his son and said to him, See, child, to a wage for the man who went with you, and it is necessary to add to it for him.
1 Tobit 12:2 And he said to him, Father, I am not harmed by giving him half of what I have brought,
1 Tobit 12:3 because he has brought me to you healthy and healed my wife and brought my silver and likewise healed you.
1 Tobit 12:4 And the old man said, It is his due.
1 Tobit 12:5 And he called the angel and said to him, Take half of everything that you have brought.
1 Tobit 12:6 Then calling the two privately, he said to them, Bless God and give thanks to him; give him greatness and give thanks before all the living concerning what he did with you; it is good to bless God and exalt his name, honorably making known the accounts of God's works, and do not hesitate to give thanks to him.
1 Tobit 12:7 It is good to hide a king's secret, but to reveal God's works gloriously. Do good, and evil will not find you.
1 Tobit 12:8 Prayer with fasting and mercy and righteousness is good; a little with righteousness is better than much with injustice; it is better to show mercy than to store up gold.
1 Tobit 12:9 For mercy delivers from death, and it will cleanse away every sin; those who perform acts of mercy and righteous deeds will be filled with life;
1 Tobit 12:10 but those who sin are enemies of their own life.
1 Tobit 12:11 I will certainly not hide any word from you; I have indeed said, It is good to hide a king's secret, but to reveal God's works gloriously.
1 Tobit 12:12 And now, when you and Sarra your bride prayed, I brought the memorial of your prayer before the Holy One; and when you buried the dead, I was likewise present with you.
1 Tobit 12:13 And when you did not hesitate to arise and leave your meal so that you might go away and wrap the dead man, you did not escape my notice as you did good, but I was with you.
1 Tobit 12:14 And now God sent me to heal you and Sarra your bride.
1 Tobit 12:15 I am Raphael, one of the seven holy angels who bring up the prayers of the holy ones and enter before the glory of the Holy One.
1 Tobit 12:16 And the two were troubled and fell upon their faces, because they were afraid.
1 Tobit 12:17 And he said to them, Do not be afraid; there will be peace for you; and bless God for the age.
1 Tobit 12:18 Because I came by the will of our God, not by my own favor; therefore bless him for the age.
1 Tobit 12:19 All the days I appeared to you, and I neither ate nor drank, but you beheld a vision.
1 Tobit 12:20 And now give thanks to God, because I ascend to the one who sent me, and write everything accomplished in a book.
1 Tobit 12:21 And they arose; and they no longer saw him.
1 Tobit 12:22 And they gave thanks for the great and wonderful works of God and how the angel of the Lord appeared to them.

## Chapter 13

1 Tobit 13:1 And Tobit wrote a prayer for exultation and said,
1 Tobit 13:2 Blessed is God who lives for the ages, and his kingdom, because he scourges and has mercy, brings down into Hades and brings up, and there is no one who will escape his hand.
1 Tobit 13:3 Give thanks to him, sons of Israel, before the nations, because he scattered us among them;
1 Tobit 13:4 there show his greatness; exalt him before every living being, because he is our Lord and God; he is our Father for all the ages.
1 Tobit 13:5 And he will scourge us in our injustices and again have mercy and gather us from all the nations, wherever you may have been scattered among them.
1 Tobit 13:6 If you return to him with your whole heart and with your whole soul to do truth before him, then he will return to you and will certainly not hide his face from you.
1 Tobit 13:7 And behold what he will do with you, and give thanks to him with your whole mouth; and bless the Lord of righteousness and exalt the King of the ages.
1 Tobit 13:8 I give thanks to him in the land of my captivity and show his strength and his greatness to a nation of sinners. Return, sinners, and do righteousness before him; who knows whether he will desire you and show mercy to you?
1 Tobit 13:9 I exalt my God, and my soul the King of heaven, and it will exult in his greatness.
1 Tobit 13:10 Let everyone speak and give thanks to him in Jerusalem. Jerusalem, holy city, he will scourge on account of the works of your sons and again have mercy on the sons of the righteous.
1 Tobit 13:11 Give thanks to the Lord well and bless the King of the ages, so that his tent may again be built for you with joy.
1 Tobit 13:12 And may he gladden the captives in you and love the afflicted in you for all the generations of the age.
1 Tobit 13:13 Many nations will come from afar to the name of the Lord God, having gifts in their hands and gifts for the King of heaven; generations of generations will give you exultation.
1 Tobit 13:14 Accursed are all who hate you; blessed will all who love you be for the age.
1 Tobit 13:15 Rejoice and exult over the sons of the righteous, because they will be gathered and will bless the Lord of the righteous; O blessed are those who love you; they will rejoice over your peace.
1 Tobit 13:16 Blessed are all who grieved over all your scourges, because they will rejoice over you, having beheld all your glory, and will be glad for the age. Let my soul bless God, the great King.
1 Tobit 13:17 Because Jerusalem will be built with sapphire and emerald and precious stone, your walls and the towers and the battlements with pure gold, and the broad streets of Jerusalem will be paved with beryl and carbuncle and stone from Souphir.
1 Tobit 13:18 And all her lanes will say, Alleluia, and will praise, saying, Blessed is God, who exalted all the ages.

## Chapter 14

1 Tobit 14:1 And Tobit ceased giving thanks.
1 Tobit 14:2 And he was fifty-eight years old when he lost his sight, and after eight years he saw again; and he performed acts of mercy and continued to fear the Lord God and give thanks to him.
1 Tobit 14:3 And he grew very old; and he called his son and his sons and said to him, Child, take your sons; behold, I have grown old and am close to departing from life.
1 Tobit 14:4 Go away to Media, child, because I am persuaded of all that Jonas the prophet spoke concerning Nineue, that it will be overthrown, but in Media there will rather be peace until a time, and that our brothers in the land will be scattered from the good land, and Jerusalem will be desolate, and the house of God in it will be burned down and will be desolate for a time.
1 Tobit 14:5 And again God will have mercy on them and return them to the land, and they will build the house, not such as the former one, until the times of the age are fulfilled. And after these things they will return from the captivities and build Jerusalem honorably, and the house of God in it will be built for all the generations of the age with a glorious building, just as the prophets spoke concerning it.
1 Tobit 14:6 And all the nations will truly turn to fear the Lord God and will bury their idols, and all the nations will bless the Lord.
1 Tobit 14:7 And his people will give thanks to God, and the Lord will exalt his people, and all who love the Lord God in truth and righteousness will rejoice, showing mercy to our brothers.
1 Tobit 14:8 And now, child, go away from Nineue, because what the prophet Jonas spoke will certainly happen.
1 Tobit 14:9 But you, keep the law and the ordinances and become merciful and righteous, so that it may be well with you, and bury me well and your mother with me; and no longer lodge in Nineue.
1 Tobit 14:10 Child, see what Aman did to Achiacharos who reared him, how he brought him from the light into the darkness, and all that he repaid him; and Achiacharos was saved, but to that man the repayment was paid, and he himself went down into the darkness. Manasses showed mercy and was saved from a snare of death which he set for him, but Aman fell into the snare and perished.
1 Tobit 14:11 And now, children, see what mercy does, and what righteousness delivers. And while he was saying these things, his soul failed upon the bed; and he was one hundred fifty-eight years old; and he buried him gloriously.
1 Tobit 14:12 And when Anna died, he buried her with his father. And Tobias went away with his wife and his sons to Ekbatana to Ragouel his father-in-law.
1 Tobit 14:13 And he grew old honorably and buried his parents-in-law gloriously and inherited their property and that of Tobit his father.
1 Tobit 14:14 And he died at one hundred twenty-seven years of age in Ekbatana of Media.
1 Tobit 14:15 And before he died he heard of the destruction of Nineue, which Nabouchodonosor and Asyeros took captive; he rejoiced over Nineue before dying.

# 2 Tobit

The Apostolic Bible. Public domain. https://apostolic-bible.ysys9.chatgpt.site/license.html


## Chapter 1

2 Tobit 1:1 Book of the words of Tobith, of Tobiel, of Ananiel, of Adouel, of Gabael, of Raphael, of Ragouel, from the seed of Asiel, from the tribe of Nephthalim,
2 Tobit 1:2 who was taken captive in the days of Enemessaros the king of the Assyrians, from Thisbe, which is on the right of Kydios of Nephthalim in upper Galilee, above Asser, behind the [road] of the settings of the sun, on the left of Phogor.
2 Tobit 1:3 I, Tobith, walked in ways of truth and in righteous deeds all the days of my life, and I did many acts of mercy for my brothers and for my nation, those who went with me in captivity into the country of the Assyrians, into Nineue.
2 Tobit 1:4 And when I was in my country, in the land of Israel, and when I was young, the whole tribe of Nephthalim my father departed from the house of Dauid my father and from Jerusalem, the city [chosen] out of all the tribes of Israel for all the tribes of Israel to sacrifice; and the temple of the dwelling of God was sanctified and built in it for all the generations of the age.
2 Tobit 1:5 All my brothers and the house of Nephthalim my father, they sacrificed to the calf which Ierobeam the king of Israel made in Dan, on all the mountains of Galilee.
2 Tobit 1:6 And I, most alone, often went to Jerusalem at the feasts, as it is written for all Israel in an everlasting ordinance; having the firstfruits and the first produce and the tithes of the livestock and the first shearings of the sheep, I hurried to Jerusalem
2 Tobit 1:7 and gave them to the priests, the sons of Aaron, at the altar, and the tithe of the grain and the wine and oil and pomegranates and figs and the remaining tree fruits to the sons of Leui who ministered in Jerusalem. And I paid the second tithe in silver for the six years, and went and spent it in Jerusalem each year.
2 Tobit 1:8 And I gave these to the orphans and the widows and proselytes who were attached to the sons of Israel; I brought them and gave them to them in the third year, and we ate them according to the ordinance prescribed concerning them in the law of Moses and according to the commands which Debbora, the mother of Ananiel our father, commanded, because my father left me an orphan and died.
2 Tobit 1:9 And when I became a man, I took a wife from the seed of our family, and begot a son from her and called his name Tobias.
2 Tobit 1:10 After I was taken captive among the Assyrians, and when I was taken captive, I went to Nineue; and all my brothers and those of my race ate of the breads of the nations,
2 Tobit 1:11 but I kept my soul from eating of the breads of the nations.
2 Tobit 1:12 And when I remembered my God with my whole soul,
2 Tobit 1:13 and the Most High gave me favor and form before Enemessaros, and I bought for him everything for his use;
2 Tobit 1:14 and I went to Media and bought for him from there until he died. And I deposited bags with Gabael, the brother, Gabri, in the country of Media, ten talents of silver.
2 Tobit 1:15 And when Enemassar died and Sennacherim his son reigned in his place, and the roads of Media withdrew, and I could no longer go to Media.
2 Tobit 1:16 In the days of Enemessaros I did many acts of mercy for my brothers of my race;
2 Tobit 1:17 I gave my breads to the hungry and clothing to the naked, and if I saw anyone of my nation dead and cast behind the wall of Nineue, I buried him.
2 Tobit 1:18 And if Sennacherim killed anyone when he went away fleeing from Judaea in the days of the judgment which the king of heaven executed upon him concerning the blasphemies which he blasphemed, I buried him; for he killed many of the sons of Israel in his wrath, and I stole their bodies and buried them; and Sennacherim sought them and did not find them.
2 Tobit 1:19 And a certain one of those from Nineue went and informed the king about me, that I bury them, and I hid; and when I learned that the king knew about me and that I was being sought to die, I was afraid and ran away.
2 Tobit 1:20 And everything that belonged to me was seized, and nothing was left to me that was not taken into the royal treasury, except Anna my wife and Tobias my son.
2 Tobit 1:21 And forty days did not pass before his two sons killed him; and they fled to the mountains of Ararat, and Sacherdonos his son reigned after him. And he appointed Achicharos, Anael, the son of my brother, over all the accounting of his kingdom, and he had authority over all the administration.
2 Tobit 1:22 Then Achicharos made a request concerning me, and I came down to Nineue. For Achicharos was the chief cupbearer and keeper of the ring and administrator and accountant under Sennacherim king of the Assyrians, and Sacherdonos appointed him a second time; and he was my cousin and of my kin.

## Chapter 2

2 Tobit 2:1 And under King Sacherdonos I came down to my house, and Anna my wife and Tobias my son were restored to me. And at Pentecost, our feast, which is holy, of [seven] weeks, a good meal was prepared for me, and I reclined to eat.
2 Tobit 2:2 And the table was set before me, and more dishes were set before me, and I said to Tobias my son, Child, go, and whomever you find poor among our brothers from the captives in Nineue, who remembers with his whole heart, bring him, and he will eat together with me; and see, I will wait for you, child, until you come.
2 Tobit 2:3 And Tobias went to seek someone poor among our brothers. And returning he says, Father. And I said to him, Here I am, child. And answering he said, Father, behold, one of our nation has been murdered and cast in the marketplace, and there now he has been strangled.
2 Tobit 2:4 And leaping up I left the meal before tasting it, and I take him up from the street and placed him in one of the little houses until the sun sets, and I will bury him.
2 Tobit 2:5 Returning, therefore, I washed myself and ate the bread with mourning;
2 Tobit 2:6 and I remembered the word of the prophet, all that Amos spoke against Baithel, saying, Your feasts will be turned into mourning and all your songs into lamentation, and I wept.
2 Tobit 2:7 And when the sun set, I went away and dug and buried him.
2 Tobit 2:8 And my neighbors laughed at me, saying, He is no longer afraid; for he was already sought to be murdered because of this matter and ran away, and again, behold, he buries the dead.
2 Tobit 2:9 And that very night I washed myself and entered my courtyard and slept beside the wall of the courtyard, and my face was uncovered because of the heat;
2 Tobit 2:10 and I did not know that sparrows were in the wall above me, and their droppings settled warm into my eyes and brought on white films. And I went to the physicians to be healed, and the more they smeared me with the medicines, the more my eyes were blinded by the white films until I became completely blind; and I was disabled in my eyes for four years. And all my brothers grieved about me, and Achiacharos supported me for two years before he went to Elymais.
2 Tobit 2:11 And at that time Anna my wife worked for wages at women's work;
2 Tobit 2:12 and she sent it to its owners, and they paid her the wage. And on the seventh of Dystros she cut the cloth from the loom and sent it to the owners, and they gave her the whole wage and gave her a kid from the goats for the hearth.
2 Tobit 2:13 And when she came in to me, the kid began to cry; and I called her and said, Where is this little kid from? Is it perhaps stolen? Return it to its owners; for we have no authority to eat anything stolen.
2 Tobit 2:14 And she says to me, It has been given to me as a gift in addition to the wage. And I did not believe her and told her to return it to the owners, and I reddened toward her because of this; then answering she says to me, And where are your acts of mercy? Where are your righteous deeds? See, these things are known with you. –

## Chapter 3

2 Tobit 3:1 And becoming deeply grieved in soul and groaning, I wept and began to pray with groans,
2 Tobit 3:2 You are righteous, Lord, and all your works are righteous, and all your ways are mercy and truth; you judge the age.
2 Tobit 3:3 And now you, Lord, remember me and look upon me, and do not exact vengeance on me for my sins and in my ignorant offenses and those of my fathers, with which I sinned before you
2 Tobit 3:4 and disobeyed your commands. And you gave us over to plunder and captivity and death and to a proverb and a topic of talk and reproach among all the nations among whom you scattered us.
2 Tobit 3:5 And now your many judgments are true, to execute upon me concerning my sins, because we did not do your commands and did not walk truly before you.
2 Tobit 3:6 And now do with me according to what is pleasing to you, and command my spirit to be taken from me, so that I may be released from the face of the earth and become earth; therefore it profits me to die rather than live, because I have heard false reproaches, and much grief is with me. Lord, command that I be released from this distress; release me to the everlasting place, and do not turn your face, Lord, away from me; therefore it profits me to die rather than see much distress in my life and not hear reproaches.
2 Tobit 3:7 On this day it happened that Sarra, the daughter of Ragouel who was in Ecbatana of Media, also heard reproaches from one of her father's maidservants,
2 Tobit 3:8 because she had been given to seven men, and Asmodaios the evil demon killed them before they were with her, just as is appointed for women. And the maidservant said to her, You are the one who kills your husbands; behold, you have already been given to seven men and were not named for one of them.
2 Tobit 3:9 Why do you whip us concerning your husbands, because they died? Go with them, and may we never see a son of yours or a daughter forever.
2 Tobit 3:10 On that day she was grieved in soul and wept, and going up into her father's upper room she wanted to hang herself. And again she considered and says, Perhaps they will reproach my father and say to him, You had one beloved daughter, and she hanged herself because of the evils; and I will bring my father's old age down with grief into Hades; it is more useful for me not to hang myself, but to beseech the Lord that I die and no longer hear reproaches in my life.
2 Tobit 3:11 At that very time, spreading her hands toward the window, she beseeched and said, Blessed are you, merciful God, and blessed is your name unto the ages, and let all your works bless you forever.
2 Tobit 3:12 And now I have lifted my face and my eyes toward you;
2 Tobit 3:13 command that I be released from the earth and that I no longer hear reproaches.
2 Tobit 3:14 You know, Master, that I am clean from every uncleanness of a man
2 Tobit 3:15 and I have not defiled my name, nor my father's name, in the land of my captivity. I am my father's only child, and he has no other child to inherit him, nor has he a brother nearby or a relative, that I might keep myself as a wife for him. Already seven have perished for me, and why is it still for me to live? And if it does not seem good to you to kill me, Lord, now listen to my reproach.
2 Tobit 3:16 At that very time the prayer of both was heard before the glory of God,
2 Tobit 3:17 and Raphael was sent to heal the two, to release the white films from Tobin's eyes so that he might see the light of God with his eyes, and to give Sarra, Ragouel's daughter, to Tobias the son of Tobith as a wife, and to release Asmodaios the evil demon from her, because it falls to Tobias to inherit her before all those who want to take her. At that time Tobith returned from the courtyard into his house, and Sarra, Ragouel's daughter, also came down from the upper room.

## Chapter 4

2 Tobit 4:1 On that day Tobith remembered the silver which he had deposited with Gabael in Rhagoi of Media,
2 Tobit 4:2 and said in his heart, Behold, I have asked for death; why do I not call Tobias my son and inform him about this silver before I die?
2 Tobit 4:3 And he called Tobias his son, and he came to him; and he said to him, Bury me well; and honor your mother and do not abandon her all the days of her life, and do what is pleasing before her, and do not grieve her spirit in any matter.
2 Tobit 4:4 Remember her, child, because she saw many dangers for you in her womb; and when she dies, bury her beside me in one grave.
2 Tobit 4:5 And all your days, child, remember the Lord, and do not wish to sin and transgress his commands; do righteous deeds all the days of your life, and do not walk in the ways of unrighteousness;
2 Tobit 4:6 because those who do truth will prosper in their works.
2 Tobit 4:7 And to all those who do righteousness
2 Tobit 4:19 the Lord will give good counsel; and whomever the Lord wishes, he humbles down to lowest Hades. And now, child, remember these commands, and let them not be blotted out of your heart.
2 Tobit 4:20 And now, child, I inform you that I deposited ten talents of silver with Gabael, the son of Gabri, in Rhagoi of Media.
2 Tobit 4:21 And do not fear, child, because we have become poor; you have many good things if you fear God and flee from every sin and do good things before the Lord your God.

## Chapter 5

2 Tobit 5:1 Then answering Tobias said to Tobith his father, Everything that you have commanded me I will do, father;
2 Tobit 5:2 but how will I be able to receive it from him, when he does not know me and I do not know him? What sign should I give him, that he may recognize me and trust me and give me the silver? And I do not know the roads into Media, to go there.
2 Tobit 5:3 Then answering Tobith said to Tobias his son, He gave me his handwritten document, and I gave him a handwritten document; and I divided it into two, and we each took one, and I placed it with the silver; and now, behold, twenty years have passed since I deposited this silver. And now, child, seek for yourself a trustworthy man who will go with you, and we will give him a wage until you come; and receive this silver from him.
2 Tobit 5:4 And Tobias went out to seek a man who would go with him to Media, who was experienced in the road, and he went out and found Raphael the angel standing opposite him, and did not know that he was an angel of God;
2 Tobit 5:5 and he said to him, Where are you from, young man? And he said to him, From the sons of Israel, your brothers, and I have come here to work. And he said to him, Do you know the road to go to Media?
2 Tobit 5:6 And he said to him, Yes, I have often been there and am experienced and know all the roads; many times I went to Media and lodged with Gabael our brother who lives in Rhagoi of Media, and the journey from Ecbatana to Rhaga is two appointed days; for they lie in the mountain.
2 Tobit 5:7 And he said to him, Wait for me, young man, until I go in and inform my father; for I need you to walk with me, and I will give you your wage.
2 Tobit 5:8 And he said to him, Behold, I am waiting; only do not delay.
2 Tobit 5:9 And Tobias went in and informed Tobith his father and said to him, Behold, I have found a man of our brothers, the sons of Israel. And he said to him, Call the man for me, so that I may learn what his race is and from what tribe he is, and whether he is trustworthy to go with you, child.
2 Tobit 5:10 And Tobias went out and called him and said to him, Young man, my father calls you. And he came in to him, and Tobith greeted him first. And he said to him, May much rejoicing come to you. And answering Tobith said to him, What rejoicing do I still have? And I am a man disabled in my eyes and do not see the light of heaven, but lie in darkness like the dead who no longer behold the light; living, I am among the dead; I hear the voice of people and do not see them. And he said to him, Take courage; healing you is near with God; take courage. And Tobith said to him, Tobias my son wants to go to Media; will you be able to go with him and bring him? And I will give you your wage, brother. And he said to him, I will be able to go with him, and I know all the roads, and I often went away to Media and passed through all its plains, and I know its mountains and all its roads.
2 Tobit 5:11 And he said to him, Brother, of what family are you and from what tribe? Inform me, brother.
2 Tobit 5:12 And he said, What need have you of a tribe? And he said to him, I wish to know truly whose you are, brother, and what your name is.
2 Tobit 5:13 And he said to him, I am Azarias, of Ananias the great, of your brothers.
2 Tobit 5:14 And he said to him, May you come in health and safety, brother; and do not be embittered against me, brother, because I wished to know the truth and your family. And you happen to be a brother, and you are from a fine and good lineage; I knew Ananias and Nathan, the two sons of Seme[l]ias the great, and they went with me to Jerusalem and worshiped with me there and did not go astray. Your brothers are good men; you are from a good root, and may you come rejoicing.
2 Tobit 5:15 And he said to him, I give you a wage of a drachma a day and your necessities, just as for my son;
2 Tobit 5:16 and go with my son, and I will add still more to your wage.
2 Tobit 5:17 And he said to him, I will go with him; and do not fear; we will depart in health and return to you in health, because the road is secure. And he said to him, May a blessing come to you, brother. And he called his son and said to him, Child, prepare the things for the road and go out with your brother, and may the God in heaven preserve you there and restore you to me in health, and may his angel accompany you with safety, child. And he went out to travel his road and kissed his father and mother, and Tobith said to him, Go in health. –
2 Tobit 5:18 And his mother wept and said to Tobith, Why is it that you sent my child away? Is he not the staff of our hand, and does he not come in and go out before us?
2 Tobit 5:19 May silver not overtake silver, but may it become the offscouring of our child.
2 Tobit 5:20 As living has been given to us by the Lord, this is sufficient for us.
2 Tobit 5:21 And he said to her, Do not be concerned; our child will go in health and come to us in health, and your eyes will see on the day when he comes to you in health;
2 Tobit 5:22 do not be concerned, do not fear about them, sister; for a good angel will go with him, and his road will prosper, and he will return in health.
2 Tobit 5:23 And she ceased weeping.

## Chapter 6

2 Tobit 6:1 And the child went out, and the angel with him, and the dog went out with him and traveled with them; and both traveled, and one night came upon them, and they lodged by the Tigris river.
2 Tobit 6:2 And the child went down into the Tigris river to wash his feet, and a great fish leaped up from the water and wanted to swallow the boy's foot, and he cried out.
2 Tobit 6:3 And the angel said to the boy, Take hold and gain control of the fish. And the boy took hold of the fish and brought it up onto the earth.
2 Tobit 6:4 And the angel said to him, Split open the fish and take out its gall and heart and liver, and put them aside with you, and throw out the entrails; for its gall and heart and liver are useful as medicine.
2 Tobit 6:5 And the boy split open the fish and gathered the gall and heart and liver, and roasted some of the fish and ate and left some of it salted. –
2 Tobit 6:6 And both traveled together until they drew near to Media.
2 Tobit 6:7 And then the boy asked the angel and said to him, Azarias, brother, what medicine is in the fish's heart and liver and in the gall?
2 Tobit 6:8 And he said to him, The fish's heart and liver, burn them to make smoke before a man or woman who has an encounter with a demon or evil spirit, and every encounter will flee from him, and they will certainly not remain with him forever;
2 Tobit 6:9 and the gall, to anoint a person's eyes upon which white films have come up, to blow upon them, upon the white films, and they become healthy.
2 Tobit 6:10 And when he entered Media and was already drawing near to Ecbatana,
2 Tobit 6:11 Raphael says to the boy, Tobias, brother. And he said to him, Here I am. And he said to him, We must lodge at Ragouel's this night, and the man is your relative, and he has a daughter whose name is Sarra;
2 Tobit 6:12 and he has neither a male son nor a daughter except Sarra alone, and you are nearest to her before all people to inherit her, and you have the right to inherit the possessions of her father; and the girl is prudent and courageous and very beautiful, and her father is good.
2 Tobit 6:13 And he said, You have the right to take her; and listen to me, brother, and I will speak to her father about the girl this night, so that we may take her for you as a bride; and when we return from Rhagoi, we will make her wedding. And I know that Ragouel will certainly not be able to withhold her from you or betroth her to another, that he will incur death according to the judgment of the book of Moses, because he knows that the inheritance falls to you to take his daughter before every man. And now listen to me, brother, and we will speak about the girl this night and betroth her to you; and when we return from Rhagoi, we will take her and lead her away with us to your house.
2 Tobit 6:14 Then answering Tobias said to Raphael, Azarias, brother, I heard that she has already been given to seven men, and they died in their bridal chambers at night, whenever they went in to her, and they died. And I heard them saying that a demon kills them.
2 Tobit 6:15 And now I fear — because it does not wrong her, but whoever wants to approach her, it kills him; I am my father's only child — lest I die and bring down my father's and my mother's life with anguish over me into their grave; and they have no other son to bury them.
2 Tobit 6:16 And he says to him, Do you not remember your father's commands, that he commanded you to take a wife from your father's house? And now listen to me, brother, and do not be concerned about this demon, and take her; and I know that this night she will be given to you as a wife.
2 Tobit 6:17 And when you enter the bridal chamber, take some of the fish's liver and the heart, and place them upon the ashes of the incense, and the odor will go forth, and the demon will smell it and flee and will certainly no longer appear about her for the whole age.
2 Tobit 6:18 And when you are about to be with her, first both rise and pray and beseech the Lord of heaven, that mercy and salvation may come upon you; and do not fear, for she has been allotted to you before the age, and you will save her, and she will go with you, and I suppose that you will have children from her, and they will be as brothers to you; do not be concerned.
2 Tobit 6:19 And when Tobias heard Raphael's words and that she was a sister to him from the seed of his father's house, he loved her greatly, and his heart was joined to her.

## Chapter 7

2 Tobit 7:1 And when he entered Ecbatana, he says to him, Azarias, brother, lead me straight to Ragouel our brother. And he led him to Ragouel's house, and they found him sitting beside the door of the courtyard and greeted him first, and he said to them, Much greeting, brothers, and you have come well, in health. And he brought them into his house.
2 Tobit 7:2 And he said to Edna his wife, How like Tobei my brother this young man is.
2 Tobit 7:3 And Edna asked them and said to them, Where are you from, brothers? And they said to her, We are from the sons of Nephthalim who were taken captive in Nineue.
2 Tobit 7:4 And she said to them, Do you know Tobin our brother? And they said to her, We know him.
2 Tobit 7:5 And she said to them, Is he in health? And they said to her, He is in health and lives; and Tobias said, He is my father.
2 Tobit 7:6 And Ragouel leaped up and kissed him and wept and spoke and said to him, May a blessing come to you, child of a fine and good father; O miserable evils, that a righteous man who does acts of mercy was blinded. And falling upon the neck of Tobias his brother, he wept.
2 Tobit 7:7 And Edna his wife wept for him, and Sarra their daughter also wept.
2 Tobit 7:8 And he slaughtered a ram from the sheep and welcomed them eagerly.
2 Tobit 7:9 And when they had bathed and washed and reclined to dine, Tobias said to Raphael, Azarias, brother, tell Ragouel to give me Sarra my sister.
2 Tobit 7:10 And Ragouel heard the word and said to the child, Eat and drink and be merry this night; for there is no man to whom it falls to take Sarra my daughter except you, brother, and likewise I have no authority to give her to another man except you, because you are nearest to me; and indeed I will inform you of the truth, child.
2 Tobit 7:11 I gave her to seven men of our brothers, and all died at night whenever they went in to her. And now, child, eat and drink, and the Lord will act among you.
2 Tobit 7:12 And Tobias said, I will certainly not eat from here or drink until you settle the things concerning me. And Ragouel said to him, I do so, and she is given to you according to the judgment of the book of Moses, and from heaven it has been judged that she be given to you; take your sister. From now you are her brother and she is your sister; she has been given to you from today and forever; and the Lord of heaven will prosper you, child, this night, and may he bring mercy and peace upon you.
2 Tobit 7:13 And Ragouel called Sarra his daughter, and she came to him, and taking her hand he handed her over to him and said, Take her according to the law and according to the judgment written in the book of Moses, to give you the wife; have her and lead her away to your father in health; and may the God of heaven prosper peace for you.
2 Tobit 7:14 And he called her mother; and he said to bring a document and wrote a written agreement of a document of living together, and how he gives her to him as a wife according to the judgment of the law of Moses. After that they began to eat and drink.
2 Tobit 7:15 And Ragouel called Edna his wife and said to her, Sister, prepare the other chamber and bring her in there.
2 Tobit 7:16 And she went and spread bedding in the chamber, as he said to her, and brought her there and wept over her and wiped away the tears and said to her,
2 Tobit 7:17 Take courage, daughter; may the Lord of heaven give you joy in place of your grief; take courage, daughter. And she went out.

## Chapter 8

2 Tobit 8:1 And when they finished eating and drinking, they wished to sleep. And they led the young man away and brought him into the chamber.
2 Tobit 8:2 And Tobias remembered Raphael's words and took the fish's liver and heart out of the bag which he had, and placed them upon the ashes of the incense.
2 Tobit 8:3 And the odor of the fish hindered, and the demon ran away up into the parts of Egypt, and Raphael went and fettered him there and bound him immediately.
2 Tobit 8:4 And they went out and shut the door of the chamber. And Tobias rose from the bed and said to her, Sister, rise; let us pray and beseech our Lord to bring mercy and salvation upon us.
2 Tobit 8:5 And she rose, and they began to pray and beseech that salvation might come to them, and he began to say, Blessed are you, the God of our fathers, and blessed is your name unto all the ages of the generation; let the heavens and all your creation bless you unto all the ages.
2 Tobit 8:6 You made Adam and made for him a helper, a support, Eua his wife, and from both came the seed of mankind; and you said, It is not good for the man to be alone; let us make him a helper like him.
2 Tobit 8:7 And now I take this sister of mine, not because of fornication, but in truth; command that mercy be shown to me and her, and that we grow old together.
2 Tobit 8:8 And they said with one another, Amen, amen.
2 Tobit 8:9 And they slept that night.
2 Tobit 8:10 And Ragouel rose and called the household servants with him, and they went away and dug a grave; for he said, Perhaps he will die and we will become a laughingstock and a reproach.
2 Tobit 8:11 And when they finished digging the grave, Ragouel came into the house and called his wife
2 Tobit 8:12 and said, Send one of the maidservants, and let her enter and see whether he lives; and if he has died, that we may bury him, that no one may know.
2 Tobit 8:13 And they sent the maidservant and lit the lamp and opened the door, and she entered and found them sleeping and slumbering together.
2 Tobit 8:14 And the maidservant went out and informed them that he lives and there is no evil.
2 Tobit 8:15 And they blessed the God of heaven and said, Blessed are you, God, with every pure blessing; let them bless you unto all the ages.
2 Tobit 8:16 And blessed are you because you have gladdened me, and it did not happen as I suspected, but according to your great mercy you acted with us.
2 Tobit 8:17 And blessed are you because you showed mercy to two only children; bring them mercy and salvation, Master, and bring their life to completion with gladness and mercy.
2 Tobit 8:18 Then he told his household servants to fill in the grave before dawn came.
2 Tobit 8:19 And he told his wife to make many breads; and going to the herd he brought two oxen and four rams and said to finish them, and they began to prepare.
2 Tobit 8:20 And he called Tobias and said to him, For fourteen days you will certainly not move from here, but will remain here eating and drinking with me, and you will gladden the soul of my daughter who has been in anguish;
2 Tobit 8:21 and of all that belongs to me, take half from here and go in health to your father; and the other half, when both I and my wife die, is yours. Take courage, child; I am your father and Edna your mother, and we are with you and your sister from now forever; take courage, child.

## Chapter 9

2 Tobit 9:1 Then Tobias called Raphael and said to him,
2 Tobit 9:2 Azarias, brother, take with you four household servants and two camels, and go to Rhaga and come to Gabael and give him the handwritten document and receive the silver and take him with you to the wedding;
2 Tobit 9:34 for you know that my father will be counting the days, and if I delay one day, I will grieve him greatly; and you see what Ragouel swore, and I cannot transgress his oath.
2 Tobit 9:5 And Raphael and the four household servants and the two camels went to Rhaga of Media and lodged with Gabael; and he gave him his handwritten document and informed him about Tobios the son of Tobith, that he had taken a wife and that he calls him to the wedding. And rising he counted out to him the bags with the seals, and they put them together.
2 Tobit 9:6 And they rose early together and came to the wedding. And they came into Ragouel's and found Tobias reclining, and he leaped up and greeted him and wept and blessed him and said to him, Fine and good one, of a fine and good man, righteous and merciful, may the Lord give you a blessing of heaven, and to your wife and your father and the mother of your wife; blessed is God, because I have seen Tobin my cousin, like him.

## Chapter 10

2 Tobit 10:1 And each day, day after day, Tobith calculated the days, in how many he would travel and in how many he would return; and when the days were completed and his son was not present,
2 Tobit 10:2 he said, Perhaps he has been detained there? Or perhaps Gabael has died and no one gives him the silver?
2 Tobit 10:3 And he began to grieve.
2 Tobit 10:4 And Anna his wife says, My child has perished and is no longer among the living; and she began to weep and lament about her son, and said,
2 Tobit 10:5 Woe to me, child, because I let you go, the light of my eyes.
2 Tobit 10:6 And Tobith said to her, Be silent, do not be concerned, sister; he is in health; and indeed a distraction has come upon them there, and the man who went with him is trustworthy and one of our brothers; do not grieve about him, sister; he will soon be here.
2 Tobit 10:7 And she said to him, Be silent toward me and do not mislead me; my child has perished. And springing out she watched the road by which her son had gone each day and was persuaded by no one, and when the sun set, she went in and lamented and wept the whole night and had no sleep.
2 Tobit 10:8 And when the fourteen days of the wedding were completed, which Ragouel swore to make for his daughter, Tobias came in to him and said, Send me away, for I know that my father and mother do not believe that they will see me again; and now I ask you, father, to send me away and let me go to my father; I have already told you how I left him.
2 Tobit 10:9 And Ragouel said to Tobias, Remain, child, remain with me, and I will send messengers to Tobin your father, and they will inform him about you. And he said to him, By no means; I ask you to send me away from here to my father.
2 Tobit 10:10 And rising Ragouel handed over to Tobias Sarra his wife and half of everything that belonged to him, male servants and maidservants, oxen and sheep, donkeys and camels, clothing and silver and vessels;
2 Tobit 10:11 and he sent them away in health and greeted him and said to him, Be in health, child, go in health; may the Lord of heaven prosper you and Sarra your wife, and may I see children of yours before I die.
2 Tobit 10:12 And he said to Sarra his daughter, Go to your father-in-law, because from now they are your parents as those who begot you; walk into peace, daughter; may I hear a good report of you while I live. And bidding farewell he released them.
2 Tobit 10:13 And Edna says to Tobias, Child and beloved brother, may the Lord restore you, and may I see children of yours while I live, and of Sarra my daughter, before I die; before the Lord I entrust my daughter to you as a deposit; do not grieve her all the days of your life; child, into peace; from now I am your mother and Sarra your sister; may we all prosper together all the days of our life. And she kissed both and sent them away in health.
2 Tobit 10:14 And Tobias departed from Ragouel in health and rejoicing and blessing the Lord of heaven and earth, the king of all things, because he had prospered his road. And he said to him, It has prospered for you to honor them all the days of their life.

## Chapter 11

2 Tobit 11:1 And as they drew near to Kaserin, which is opposite Nineue, Raphael said,
2 Tobit 11:2 You know how we left your father;
2 Tobit 11:3 let us run ahead of your wife and prepare the house while they are coming.
2 Tobit 11:4 And both traveled together, and he said to him, Take the gall at hand. And the dog went with them, from behind him and Tobias.
2 Tobit 11:5 And Anna sat watching her son's road;
2 Tobit 11:6 and she perceived him coming and said to his father, Behold, your son is coming, and the man who went with him.
2 Tobit 11:7 And Raphael said to Tobias before he approached his father, I know that his eyes will be opened;
2 Tobit 11:8 smear the fish's gall into his eyes, and the medicine will make them contract and peel the white films from his eyes, and your father will see again and see the light.
2 Tobit 11:9 And [Anna] ran up and fell upon her son's neck and said to him, I have seen you, child; from now I will die. And she wept.
2 Tobit 11:10 And Tobis rose and stumbled with his feet and went out through the door of the courtyard,
2 Tobit 11:11 and Tobias walked toward him, and the fish's gall was in his hand, and he blew into his eyes and took hold of him and said, Take courage, father; and he applied the medicine upon him and administered it.
2 Tobit 11:12 And he peeled it away with both his hands from the corners of his eyes.
2 Tobit 11:13 And he fell upon his neck and wept and said to him, I have seen you, child, the light of my eyes.
2 Tobit 11:14 And he said, Blessed is God, and blessed is his great name, and blessed are all his holy angels; may his great name be upon us, and blessed are all the angels unto all the ages; because he whipped me, and behold, I see Tobias my son.
2 Tobit 11:15 And Tobias entered rejoicing and blessing God with his whole mouth, and Tobias showed his father that his road had prospered and that he had brought silver, and how he took Sarra the daughter of Ragouel as a wife, and that, behold, she is arriving and is close to the gate of Nineue.
2 Tobit 11:16 And [Tobith] went out to meet his daughter-in-law, rejoicing and blessing God, toward the gate of Nineue; and those in Nineue saw him walking and crossing with all his strength and being led by the hand by no one, and marveled, and Tobith gave thanks before them that God had shown him mercy and had opened his eyes.
2 Tobit 11:17 And Tobith approached Sarra, the wife of Tobias his son, and blessed her and said to her, May you enter in health, daughter, and blessed is your God who brought you to us, daughter; and blessed is your father, and blessed is Tobias my son, and blessed are you, daughter; enter your house in health, in blessing and joy; enter, daughter.
2 Tobit 11:18 On this day there was joy for all the Judeans who were in Nineue.
2 Tobit 11:19 And Achikar and Nabad his cousins came rejoicing to Tobin.

## Chapter 12

2 Tobit 12:1 And when the wedding was completed, Tobith called Tobias his son and said to him, Child, see to giving the wage to the man who went with you [and] adding to his wage.
2 Tobit 12:2 And he said to him, Father, how much wage will I give him? I am not harmed by giving him half the possessions which he has brought with me.
2 Tobit 12:3 He has brought me in health and healed my wife and brought the silver with me and healed you; how much more wage should I give him?
2 Tobit 12:4 And Tobis said to him, He has the right, child, to take half of everything that he came having.
2 Tobit 12:5 And he called him and said, Take half of everything that you came having as your wage, and go in health.
2 Tobit 12:6 Then he called the two privately and said to them, Bless God and give thanks to him before all the living for the good things which he did with you, to bless and hymn his name; make the words of God known honorably to all people, and do not hesitate to give thanks to him.
2 Tobit 12:7 It is good to hide a king's secret, but to uncover the works of God and acknowledge them honorably. Do good, and evil will not find you.
2 Tobit 12:8 Prayer with truth and mercy with righteousness are good, rather than wealth with unrighteousness; it is good to do an act of mercy rather than store up gold.
2 Tobit 12:9 Mercy delivers from death, and it cleanses every sin; those who do acts of mercy will be filled with life;
2 Tobit 12:10 those who do sin and unrighteousness are enemies of their own soul.
2 Tobit 12:11 I will make all the truth known to you and will certainly not hide any word from you; I have already informed you and said, It is good to hide a king's secret and to uncover the works of God gloriously.
2 Tobit 12:12 And now, when you prayed, and Sarra, I brought the memorial of your prayer before the glory of the Lord; and when you buried the dead, likewise;
2 Tobit 12:13 and when you did not hesitate to rise and leave your meal and went away and wrapped the dead man, then I have been sent to you to test you.
2 Tobit 12:14 And at the same time God has sent me to heal [you] and Sarra your daughter-in-law.
2 Tobit 12:15 I am Raphael, one of the seven angels who stand by and enter before the glory of the Lord.
2 Tobit 12:16 And the two were troubled and fell upon their faces and were afraid.
2 Tobit 12:17 And he said to them, Do not fear; peace to you; bless God for the whole age.
2 Tobit 12:18 When I was with you, I was with you, not by my own favor, but by the will of God; bless him every day; hymn him.
2 Tobit 12:19 And you beheld me, that I ate nothing, but a vision was being beheld by you.
2 Tobit 12:20 And now bless the Lord upon the earth and give thanks to God. Behold, I ascend to the one who sent me. Write all these things that happened to you. And he ascended.
2 Tobit 12:21 And they rose; and they could no longer see him.
2 Tobit 12:22 And they blessed and hymned God and gave thanks to him for these great works of his, how an angel of God appeared to them.

## Chapter 13

2 Tobit 13:1 And he said,
2 Tobit 13:2 Blessed is God who lives forever, and his kingdom, because he whips and shows mercy, brings down to Hades, lowest beneath the earth, and he brings up from the great destruction, and there is nothing that will escape his hand.
2 Tobit 13:3 Give thanks to him, sons of Israel, before the nations, because he scattered you among them;
2 Tobit 13:4 and there he showed you his greatness, and exalt him before every living being, because he is our Lord, and he is our God and he is our Father and he is God unto all the ages.
2 Tobit 13:5 He will whip you for your unrighteous deeds and show mercy to all of you from all the nations, wherever you are scattered among them.
2 Tobit 13:6 When you return to him with your whole heart and with your whole soul to do truth before him, then he will return to you and will certainly no longer hide his face from you.
2 Tobit 13:7 And now behold what he did with you, and give thanks to him with your whole mouth; and bless the Lord of righteousness and exalt the king of the ages. –
2 Tobit 13:11 And again your tent will be built for you with joy.
2 Tobit 13:12 And may he gladden in you all the captives and love in you all the afflicted unto all the generations of the age.
2 Tobit 13:13 A bright light will shine to all the ends of the earth; many nations from afar [will come to you], and inhabitants of all the remotest parts of the earth, toward your holy name and having their gifts in their hands for the king of heaven; generations of generations will give exultation in you, and the name of the chosen one unto the generations of the age.
2 Tobit 13:14 Accursed are all who will speak a harsh word; accursed will be all who tear you down and pull down your walls, and all who overthrow your towers and burn your dwellings; and blessed forever will be all who fear you.
2 Tobit 13:15 Then go and exult toward the sons of the righteous, because all will be gathered together and bless the Lord of the age. Blessed are those who love you, and blessed are those who will rejoice over your peace;
2 Tobit 13:16 and blessed are all the people who will grieve over you, over all your scourges, because in you they will rejoice and see all your joy forever. My soul, bless the Lord, the great king.
2 Tobit 13:17 Because Jerusalem will be built, his house in the city unto all the ages. I will be blessed if the remnant of my seed comes to see your glory and give thanks to the king of heaven. And the doors of Jerusalem will be built with sapphire and emerald, and all your walls with precious stone; the towers of Jerusalem will be built with gold, and their battlements with pure gold; the streets of Jerusalem will be paved with carbuncle and stone of Souphir.
2 Tobit 13:18 And the doors of Jerusalem will speak songs of exultation, and all her houses will say, Alleluia, blessed is the God of Israel; and blessed ones will bless the holy name forever and beyond.

## Chapter 14

2 Tobit 14:1 And the words of Tobith's thanksgiving were completed.
2 Tobit 14:2 And he died in peace, one hundred twelve years old, and was buried gloriously in Nineue. And he was sixty-two years old when he became disabled in his eyes, and after seeing again he lived amid good things and did acts of mercy; and he continued still to bless God and acknowledge the greatness of God.
2 Tobit 14:3 And when he was dying, he called Tobias his son and commanded him, saying, Child, take your children away
2 Tobit 14:4 and run away to Media, because I believe the word of God against Nineue, what Naoum spoke, that everything will happen and come upon Athour and Nineue, and everything the prophets of Israel whom God sent spoke will come to pass, and nothing will be diminished from all the words, and everything will happen in its times, and in Media there will be salvation rather than among the Assyrians and in Babylon; therefore I know and believe that everything God said will be completed and happen, and no word from the sayings will fall away; and all our brothers who dwell in the land of Israel will be scattered and taken captive from the good land, and all the land of Israel will be desolate, and Samaria and Jerusalem will be desolate, and the house of God in grief, and it will be burned for a time.
2 Tobit 14:5 And again God will show them mercy, and God will return them to the land of Israel, and again they will build the house, and not like the first, until the time when the time of the seasons is fulfilled. And after these things all will return from their captivity and build Jerusalem honorably, and the house of God in it will be built, as the prophets of Israel spoke about it.
2 Tobit 14:6 And all the nations in the whole earth, all will return and fear God truly, and all will abandon their idols, the false ones that lead them astray in their wandering, and bless the God of the age in righteousness.
2 Tobit 14:7 All the sons of Israel who are saved in those days, remembering God in truth, will be gathered together and come to Jerusalem and dwell forever in the land of Abraam with security, and it will be handed over to them; and those who love God in truth will rejoice, and those who do sin and unrighteousness will vanish from all the earth.
2 Tobit 14:89 And now, children, I command you: serve God in truth and do what is pleasing before him, and it will be enjoined upon your children to do righteousness and mercy, and that they remember God and bless his name at every time in truth and with their whole strength. And now you, child, go out from Nineue and do not remain here; on whatever day you bury your mother with me, on that very day do not lodge within its borders; for I see that much unrighteousness is in it, and much deceit is carried out in it, and they are not ashamed.
2 Tobit 14:10 See, child, all that Nadab did to Achikar who raised him; was he not brought down living into the earth? And God repaid the dishonor before his face, and Achikar came out into the light, and Nadab entered the darkness of the age, because he sought to kill Achikar; by doing an act of mercy he came out from the snare of death which Nadab set for him, and Nadab fell into the snare of death, and it destroyed him.
2 Tobit 14:11 And now, children, see what mercy does, and what unrighteousness does, that it kills; and behold, my soul is failing. – And they placed him upon the bed, and he died; and he was buried gloriously.
2 Tobit 14:12 And when his mother died, Tobias buried her with his father. And he and his wife departed to Media and dwelt in Ecbatana with Ragouel his father-in-law.
2 Tobit 14:13 And he supported them honorably in old age and buried them in Ecbatana of Media and inherited the household of Ragouel and of Tobith his father.
2 Tobit 14:14 And he died gloriously, one hundred seventeen years old.
2 Tobit 14:15 And before he died he saw and heard the destruction of Nineue, and saw its captivity being led into Media, which Achiacharos the king of Media took captive, and he blessed God in all that he did against the sons of Nineue and Athouria; before dying he rejoiced over Nineue and blessed the Lord God unto the ages of the ages.

# 1 Maccabees

The Apostolic Bible. Public domain. https://apostolic-bible.ysys9.chatgpt.site/license.html


## Chapter 1

1 Maccabees 1:1 And it happened after Alexandros, the son of Philippos, the Macedonian, who went out from the land of Chettiim, struck Dareios king of the Persians and Medes and reigned in his place, previously over Greece.
1 Maccabees 1:2 And he established many wars and took hold of fortifications and slaughtered kings of the earth;
1 Maccabees 1:3 and he passed through to the ends of the earth and took spoils of a multitude of nations. And the earth was quiet before him, and he was exalted, and his heart was lifted up.
1 Maccabees 1:4 And he gathered an exceedingly strong army and ruled countries of nations and rulers, and they became tributary to him.
1 Maccabees 1:5 And after these things he fell upon his bed and knew that he was dying.
1 Maccabees 1:6 And he called his glorious servants, those brought up with him from youth, and divided his kingdom among them while he was still living.
1 Maccabees 1:7 And Alexandros reigned twelve years and died.
1 Maccabees 1:8 And his servants took power, each in his own place.
1 Maccabees 1:9 And they all put on diadems after he died, and their sons after them for many years, and they multiplied evils in the earth.
1 Maccabees 1:10 And from them came out a sinful root, Antiochos Epiphanes, son of King Antiochos, who was a hostage in Rome; and he reigned in the one hundred thirty-seventh year of the kingdom of the Greeks.
1 Maccabees 1:11 In those days lawless sons went out from Israel and persuaded many, saying, Let us go and make a covenant with the nations around us, because since we separated from them many evils have found us.
1 Maccabees 1:12 And the word seemed good in their eyes,
1 Maccabees 1:13 and some of the people eagerly went to the king, and he gave them authority to do the ordinances of the nations.
1 Maccabees 1:14 And they built a gymnasium in Jerusalem according to the customs of the nations
1 Maccabees 1:15 and made foreskins for themselves and departed from the holy covenant and were yoked to the nations and sold themselves to do evil.
1 Maccabees 1:16 And the kingdom was established before Antiochos, and he undertook to reign over the land of Egypt, so that he might reign over the two kingdoms.
1 Maccabees 1:17 And he entered Egypt with a heavy multitude, with chariots and elephants and horsemen and a great fleet,
1 Maccabees 1:18 and established war against Ptolemaios king of Egypt; and Ptolemaios was put to flight before him and fled, and many fell wounded.
1 Maccabees 1:19 And they took hold of the fortified cities in the land of Egypt, and he took the spoils of the land of Egypt.
1 Maccabees 1:20 And Antiochos returned after striking Egypt in the one hundred forty-third year, and went up against Israel and went up to Jerusalem with a heavy multitude.
1 Maccabees 1:21 And he entered the sanctuary in arrogance and took the golden altar and the lampstand of light and all its vessels
1 Maccabees 1:22 and the table of the presentation and the libation vessels and the bowls and the golden censers and the curtain and the crowns and the golden ornament on the face of the temple, and stripped everything;
1 Maccabees 1:23 and he took the silver and the gold and the desirable vessels, and took the hidden treasures which he found;
1 Maccabees 1:24 and taking everything he departed to his land. And he committed murder and spoke great arrogance.
1 Maccabees 1:25 And great mourning came upon Israel in every place of theirs.
1 Maccabees 1:26 And rulers and elders groaned, virgins and young men grew weak, and the beauty of the women was altered.
1 Maccabees 1:27 Every bridegroom took up lamentation, and she who sat in the bridal chamber mourned.
1 Maccabees 1:28 And the earth was shaken over its inhabitants, and the whole house of Iakob put on shame.
1 Maccabees 1:29 After two years of days the king sent a ruler of tribute collection to the cities of Iouda, and he came to Jerusalem with a heavy multitude.
1 Maccabees 1:30 And he spoke peaceful words to them in deceit, and they trusted him. And he fell upon the city suddenly and struck it with a great blow and destroyed many people from Israel.
1 Maccabees 1:31 And he took the spoils of the city and burned it with fire and tore down its houses and the walls around it.
1 Maccabees 1:32 And they took the women and children captive, and took possession of the livestock.
1 Maccabees 1:33 And they built up the city of Dauid with a great and strong wall, with strong towers, and it became a citadel for them.
1 Maccabees 1:34 And they placed there a sinful nation, lawless men, and they strengthened themselves in it.
1 Maccabees 1:35 And they stored weapons and food, and gathering the spoils of Jerusalem they put them away there and became a great snare.
1 Maccabees 1:36 And it became an ambush against the sanctuary and an evil adversary against Israel continually.
1 Maccabees 1:37 And they poured out innocent blood around the sanctuary and defiled the sanctuary.
1 Maccabees 1:38 And the inhabitants of Jerusalem fled because of them, and it became a dwelling of strangers; and it became strange to its offspring, and its children abandoned it.
1 Maccabees 1:39 Its sanctuary was laid waste like a wilderness, its feasts were turned into mourning, its sabbaths into reproach, its honor into contempt.
1 Maccabees 1:40 In proportion to its glory its dishonor was multiplied, and its height was turned into mourning.
1 Maccabees 1:41 And the king wrote to his whole kingdom that all should be one people
1 Maccabees 1:42 and each abandon his customs. And all the nations accepted according to the king's word.
1 Maccabees 1:43 And many from Israel approved his worship and sacrificed to the idols and profaned the sabbath.
1 Maccabees 1:44 And the king sent documents by the hand of messengers to Jerusalem and the cities of Iouda, to walk after customs foreign to the land
1 Maccabees 1:45 and to prevent burnt offerings and sacrifice and libation from the sanctuary, and to profane sabbaths and feasts
1 Maccabees 1:46 and defile the sanctuary and holy ones,
1 Maccabees 1:47 to build altars and sacred precincts and shrines of idols, and to sacrifice swine and unclean livestock,
1 Maccabees 1:48 and to leave their sons uncircumcised, to make their souls abominable with everything unclean and with profanation,
1 Maccabees 1:49 so as to forget the law and alter all the ordinances;
1 Maccabees 1:50 and whoever does not act according to the king's word will die.
1 Maccabees 1:51 According to all these words he wrote to his whole kingdom and made overseers over all the people and commanded the cities of Iouda to sacrifice, city by city.
1 Maccabees 1:52 And many from the people gathered to them, everyone who abandoned the law, and they did evils in the land
1 Maccabees 1:53 and placed Israel in hiding, in every refuge of theirs.
1 Maccabees 1:54 And on the fifteenth day of Chaseleu in the one hundred forty-fifth year he built an abomination of desolation upon the altar. And in the cities of Iouda around it they built altars;
1 Maccabees 1:55 and at the doors of the houses and in the streets they burned incense.
1 Maccabees 1:56 And the books of the law which they found they tore apart and burned with fire.
1 Maccabees 1:57 And wherever a book of the covenant was found with anyone, and if anyone approved the law, the king's decree put him to death.
1 Maccabees 1:58 In their strength they acted against Israel, against those found in the cities each and every month.
1 Maccabees 1:59 And on the twenty-fifth of the month, sacrificing upon the altar which was upon the altar of sacrifice.
1 Maccabees 1:60 And the women who had circumcised their children they put to death according to the ordinance
1 Maccabees 1:61 and hung the infants from their necks, and their households and those who had circumcised them.
1 Maccabees 1:62 And many in Israel grew strong and fortified themselves within themselves not to eat unclean things
1 Maccabees 1:63 and accepted death, so that they might not be defiled by the foods or profane the holy covenant, and they died.
1 Maccabees 1:64 And exceedingly great wrath came upon Israel.

## Chapter 2

1 Maccabees 2:1 In those days Mattathias son of Ioannes, of Symeon, a priest of the sons of Ioarib, arose from Jerusalem and settled in Modein.
1 Maccabees 2:2 And he had five sons, Ioannes called Gaddi,
1 Maccabees 2:3 Simon called Thassi,
1 Maccabees 2:4 Ioudas called Makkabaios,
1 Maccabees 2:5 Eleazar called Auaran, Ionathes called Apphous.
1 Maccabees 2:6 And he saw the blasphemies happening in Iouda and Jerusalem
1 Maccabees 2:7 and said, Alas for me, why was I born for this, to see the crushing of my people and the crushing of the holy city, and to sit there when it was given into the hand of enemies, the sanctuary into the hand of strangers?
1 Maccabees 2:8 Its temple became like a man without glory,
1 Maccabees 2:9 the vessels of its glory were led away captive, its infants were killed in its streets, its young men by an enemy's sword.
1 Maccabees 2:10 What nation has not inherited royal possessions and taken hold of its spoils?
1 Maccabees 2:11 All its adornment was removed; instead of free it became a slave.
1 Maccabees 2:12 And behold, our holy things and our beauty and our glory were laid waste, and the nations profaned them.
1 Maccabees 2:13 Why is there still life for us?
1 Maccabees 2:14 And Mattathias and his sons tore their garments and put on sackcloth and mourned exceedingly.
1 Maccabees 2:15 And those from the king who compelled apostasy came to the city of Modein, so that they might sacrifice.
1 Maccabees 2:16 And many from Israel approached them; and Mattathias and his sons were gathered.
1 Maccabees 2:17 And those from the king answered and spoke to Mattathias, saying, You are a ruler and glorious and great in this city, and supported by sons and brothers;
1 Maccabees 2:18 now approach first and do the king's ordinance, as all the nations and the men of Iouda and those left in Jerusalem have done, and you and your sons will be among the king's friends, and you and your sons will be glorified with silver and gold and many gifts.
1 Maccabees 2:19 And Mattathias answered and said with a great voice, If all the nations in the house of the king's kingdom obey him, each to depart from the worship of his fathers, and have chosen his commands,
1 Maccabees 2:20 yet I and my sons and my brothers will walk in the covenant of our fathers;
1 Maccabees 2:21 far be it from us to abandon law and ordinances;
1 Maccabees 2:22 we will not obey the king's words, to depart from our worship to the right or left.
1 Maccabees 2:23 And as he ceased speaking these words, a Judean man approached in the eyes of all to sacrifice upon the altar in Modein according to the king's ordinance.
1 Maccabees 2:24 And Mattathias saw and was zealous, and his kidneys trembled, and he brought up wrath according to the judgment, and running he slaughtered him upon the altar;
1 Maccabees 2:25 and the king's man who compelled sacrifice he killed at that time, and tore down the altar.
1 Maccabees 2:26 And he was zealous for the law, as Phinees did to Zambri son of Salom.
1 Maccabees 2:27 And Mattathias cried out in the city with a great voice, saying, Let everyone zealous for the law and upholding the covenant come out after me.
1 Maccabees 2:28 And he and his sons fled into the mountains and abandoned all they had in the city.
1 Maccabees 2:29 Then many seeking righteousness and judgment went down into the wilderness to settle there,
1 Maccabees 2:30 they and their sons and their wives and their livestock, because the evils grew harsh against them.
1 Maccabees 2:31 And it was reported to the king's men and the armies which were in Jerusalem, the city of Dauid, that men who had rejected the king's command had gone down into the hiding places in the wilderness.
1 Maccabees 2:32 And many ran after them and overtook them and encamped against them and established war against them on the day of the sabbaths
1 Maccabees 2:33 and said to them, Until now; come out and act according to the king's word, and you will live.
1 Maccabees 2:34 And they said, We will not come out or do the king's word, to profane the day of the sabbaths.
1 Maccabees 2:35 And they hastened war against them.
1 Maccabees 2:36 And they did not answer them or throw a stone at them or block up the hiding places,
1 Maccabees 2:37 saying, Let us all die in our integrity; heaven and earth bear witness concerning us that you destroy us without judgment.
1 Maccabees 2:38 And they rose against them in war on the sabbaths, and they and their wives and their children and their livestock died, up to a thousand human souls.
1 Maccabees 2:39 And Mattathias and his friends learned of it and mourned exceedingly over them.
1 Maccabees 2:40 And a man said to his neighbor, If we all do as our brothers did and do not fight against the nations for our soul and our ordinances, now they will more quickly destroy us from the earth.
1 Maccabees 2:41 And they resolved on that day, saying, Every person who comes against us for war on the day of the sabbaths, let us fight against him, and we will certainly not all die as our brothers died in the hiding places.
1 Maccabees 2:42 Then an assembly of Asidaians gathered to them, strong in power from Israel, everyone who willingly offered himself for the law;
1 Maccabees 2:43 and all who fled from the evils joined them and became a support for them.
1 Maccabees 2:44 And they established an army and struck sinners in their anger and lawless men in their wrath; and the rest fled to the nations to be saved.
1 Maccabees 2:45 And Mattathias and his friends went around and tore down the altars
1 Maccabees 2:46 and circumcised the uncircumcised boys, all whom they found within the borders of Israel, by force,
1 Maccabees 2:47 and pursued the sons of arrogance, and the work prospered in their hand;
1 Maccabees 2:48 and they rescued the law from the hand of the nations and the kings, and did not give a horn to the sinner.
1 Maccabees 2:49 And the days for Mattathias to die drew near, and he said to his sons, Now arrogance and rebuke have been established, and a time of overthrow and wrath of anger.
1 Maccabees 2:50 Now, children, be zealous for the law and give your souls for the covenant of our fathers,
1 Maccabees 2:51 and remember the works of the fathers which they did in their generations, and receive great glory and an everlasting name.
1 Maccabees 2:52 Was not Abraam found faithful in trial, and was it not reckoned to him as righteousness?
1 Maccabees 2:53 Ioseph in the time of his distress kept the command and became lord of Egypt.
1 Maccabees 2:54 Phinees our father, in being zealous with zeal, received a covenant of everlasting priesthood.
1 Maccabees 2:55 Iesous, in fulfilling the word, became a judge in Israel.
1 Maccabees 2:56 Chaleb, in bearing witness in the assembly, received an inheritance of land.
1 Maccabees 2:57 Dauid, in his mercy, inherited a throne of kingship unto ages.
1 Maccabees 2:58 Elias, in being zealous with zeal for the law, was taken up into heaven.
1 Maccabees 2:59 Ananias, Azarias, Misael believed and were saved from the flame.
1 Maccabees 2:60 Daniel, in his integrity, was delivered from the mouth of lions.
1 Maccabees 2:61 And thus consider generation by generation, that all who hope in him will not grow weak.
1 Maccabees 2:62 And do not fear the words of a sinful man, because his glory is for dung and worms;
1 Maccabees 2:63 today he will be exalted and tomorrow he will certainly not be found, because he returned to his dust, and his reasoning will perish.
1 Maccabees 2:64 Children, be courageous and strong in the law, because in it you will be glorified.
1 Maccabees 2:65 And behold, Symeon your brother, I know that he is a man of counsel; listen to him all the days; he will be your father.
1 Maccabees 2:66 And Ioudas Makkabaios is strong in power from his youth; he will be your commander of the army and will fight the war of peoples.
1 Maccabees 2:67 And you will bring to yourselves all the doers of the law, and avenge the vengeance of your people;
1 Maccabees 2:68 repay a repayment to the nations, and attend to the ordinance of the law. –
1 Maccabees 2:69 And he blessed them; and was added to his fathers.
1 Maccabees 2:70 And he died in the one hundred forty-sixth year and was buried in the tombs of his fathers in Modein, and all Israel lamented him with a great lamentation.

## Chapter 3

1 Maccabees 3:1 And Ioudas his son, called Makkabaios, arose in his place.
1 Maccabees 3:2 And all his brothers and all who had joined his father helped him, and fought the war of Israel with gladness.
1 Maccabees 3:3 And he enlarged glory for his people and put on a breastplate like a giant and girded on his war equipment and established wars, protecting the army with a sword.
1 Maccabees 3:4 And he was like a lion in his works, and like a young lion roaring for prey.
1 Maccabees 3:5 And he pursued lawless men, searching them out, and burned those who troubled his people.
1 Maccabees 3:6 And lawless men shrank back from fear of him, and all the workers of lawlessness were troubled, and salvation prospered in his hand.
1 Maccabees 3:7 And he embittered many kings and gladdened Iakob with his works, and his memorial is for a blessing forever.
1 Maccabees 3:8 And he passed through the cities of Iouda and destroyed the ungodly out of it and turned wrath away from Israel
1 Maccabees 3:9 and was named to the end of the earth and gathered those who were perishing.
1 Maccabees 3:10 And Apollonios gathered nations and a great army from Samaria to fight against Israel.
1 Maccabees 3:11 And Ioudas learned of it and went out to meet him and struck him and killed him; and many fell wounded, and the remainder fled.
1 Maccabees 3:12 And they took their spoils, and Ioudas took the sword of Apollonios and fought with it all the days.
1 Maccabees 3:13 And Seron, the commander of the army of Syria, heard that Ioudas had gathered a gathering and an assembly of faithful men with him, who went out to war,
1 Maccabees 3:14 and he said, I will make a name for myself and be glorified in the kingdom, and I will fight Ioudas and those with him who despise the king's word.
1 Maccabees 3:15 And he proceeded, and a strong army of ungodly men went up with him to help him execute vengeance upon the sons of Israel.
1 Maccabees 3:16 And he drew near as far as the ascent of Baithoron, and Ioudas went out to meet him with few men.
1 Maccabees 3:17 And when they saw the army coming to meet them, they said to Ioudas, How will we be able, being few, to fight against so strong a multitude? And we are exhausted, having eaten nothing today.
1 Maccabees 3:18 And Ioudas said, It is easy for many to be shut into the hands of few, and there is no difference before heaven in saving by many or by few;
1 Maccabees 3:19 because victory in war is not in the multitude of an army, but strength is from heaven.
1 Maccabees 3:20 They come against us with a multitude of insolence and lawlessness, to remove us and our wives and our children, to despoil us,
1 Maccabees 3:21 but we fight for our souls and our customs.
1 Maccabees 3:22 And he will crush them before our face, but do not fear them.
1 Maccabees 3:23 And when he ceased speaking, he leaped upon them suddenly, and Seron and his army were crushed before him.
1 Maccabees 3:24 And they pursued him on the descent of Baithoron as far as the plain; and about eight hundred men of them fell, and the rest fled to the land of Phylistiim.
1 Maccabees 3:25 And the fear of Ioudas and his brothers began, and terror fell upon the nations around them;
1 Maccabees 3:26 and his name reached as far as the king, and the nations recounted the battles of Ioudas.
1 Maccabees 3:27 And when King Antiochos heard these words, he was angered with wrath and sent and gathered all the armies of his kingdom, an exceedingly strong army.
1 Maccabees 3:28 And he opened his treasury and gave pay to the armies for a year and commanded them to be ready for every need.
1 Maccabees 3:29 And he saw that the silver had run out from the treasuries, and the tributes of the country were few because of the dissension and blow which he had brought about in the land, to remove the customs which had been from the earliest days,
1 Maccabees 3:30 and he feared that he might not have, as once and twice before, for the expenses and the gifts which he formerly gave with a lavish hand, and he had surpassed the kings before him,
1 Maccabees 3:31 and he was exceedingly perplexed in his soul and resolved to go to Persia and take the tributes of the countries and gather much silver.
1 Maccabees 3:32 And he left Lysias, a glorious man and of royal lineage, over the king's affairs from the Euphrates river as far as the borders of Egypt,
1 Maccabees 3:33 and to rear Antiochos his son until he returned;
1 Maccabees 3:34 and he handed over to him half the armies and the elephants and commanded him concerning everything he wished, and concerning the inhabitants of Judaea and Jerusalem,
1 Maccabees 3:35 to send an army against them to wipe out and remove the strength of Israel and the remnant of Jerusalem, and remove their memorial from the place,
1 Maccabees 3:36 and settle sons of foreigners in all their borders and allot their land as an inheritance.
1 Maccabees 3:37 And the king took the remaining half of the armies and departed from Antioch, from the city of his kingdom, in the one hundred forty-seventh year, and crossed the Euphrates river and traveled through the upper countries.
1 Maccabees 3:38 And Lysias chose Ptolemaios son of Dorymenes and Nikanor and Gorgias, powerful men among the king's friends,
