1 Maccabees 3:39 and sent with them forty thousand men and seven thousand cavalry to come into the land of Iouda and destroy it according to the king's word.
1 Maccabees 3:40 And he departed with all their army, and they came and encamped near Ammaous in the level land.
1 Maccabees 3:41 And the merchants of the country heard their name and took exceedingly much silver and gold and fetters and came into the camp to take the sons of Israel as slaves. And an army of Syria and the land of foreigners joined them.
1 Maccabees 3:42 And Ioudas and his brothers saw that the evils had multiplied and the armies were encamping within their borders, and they learned the king's words which he commanded to be done to the people for destruction and annihilation,
1 Maccabees 3:43 and each said to his neighbor, Let us raise up the fallen state of our people, and fight for our people and the holy things.
1 Maccabees 3:44 And the assembly was gathered to be ready for war and to pray and ask for mercy and compassion.
1 Maccabees 3:45 And Jerusalem was uninhabited like a wilderness; there was no one coming in and going out from its offspring, and the sanctuary was being trampled, and sons of foreigners were in the citadel, a lodging for the nations; and delight was removed from Iakob, and flute and lyre ceased.
1 Maccabees 3:46 And they gathered and came to Massepha opposite Jerusalem, because formerly there was a place of prayer in Massepha for Israel.
1 Maccabees 3:47 And they fasted on that day and put on sackcloth and ashes upon their head and tore their garments.
1 Maccabees 3:48 And they spread out the book of the law concerning which the nations searched out the likenesses of their idols.
1 Maccabees 3:49 And they brought the garments of the priesthood and the first produce and the tithes, and brought forward the Nazirites who had fulfilled their days,
1 Maccabees 3:50 and cried with a voice to heaven, saying, What should we do with these, and where should we lead them away,
1 Maccabees 3:51 when your holy things have been trampled and profaned and your priests are in mourning and humiliation?
1 Maccabees 3:52 And behold, the nations have gathered against us to remove us; you know what they devise against us.
1 Maccabees 3:53 How will we be able to stand before their face unless you help us?
1 Maccabees 3:54 And they sounded the trumpets and cried with a great voice.
1 Maccabees 3:55 And after this Ioudas appointed leaders of the people, commanders of thousands and commanders of hundreds and commanders of fifties and commanders of tens.
1 Maccabees 3:56 And he told those building houses and betrothing wives and planting vineyards and the cowardly to return, each to his house, according to the law.
1 Maccabees 3:57 And the army departed, and they encamped south of Ammaous.
1 Maccabees 3:58 And Ioudas said, Gird yourselves and become mighty sons, and be ready for morning to fight against these nations gathered against us to remove us and our holy things;
1 Maccabees 3:59 because it is better for us to die in war than to look upon the evils of our nation and the holy things.
1 Maccabees 3:60 And as the will in heaven may be, so he will do.

## Chapter 4

1 Maccabees 4:1 And Gorgias took five thousand men and a thousand chosen cavalry, and the army departed by night
1 Maccabees 4:2 to fall upon the camp of the Judeans and strike them suddenly; and sons of the citadel were his guides.
1 Maccabees 4:3 And Ioudas heard and departed, he and the mighty men, to strike the king's army in Ammaous,
1 Maccabees 4:4 while the armies were still scattered away from the camp.
1 Maccabees 4:5 And Gorgias came into Ioudas's camp by night and found no one; and he sought them in the mountains, because he said, These men are fleeing from us.
1 Maccabees 4:6 And at daybreak Ioudas appeared in the plain with three thousand men; except they did not have coverings and swords as they wished.
1 Maccabees 4:7 And they saw an army of nations, strong and wearing breastplates, and cavalry surrounding it, and these were trained in war.
1 Maccabees 4:8 And Ioudas said to the men with him, Do not fear their multitude or be cowardly at their assault;
1 Maccabees 4:9 remember how our fathers were saved in the Red Sea when Pharao pursued them with an army;
1 Maccabees 4:10 and now let us cry to heaven, whether he will favor us and remember the covenant of the fathers and crush this army before our face today,
1 Maccabees 4:11 and all the nations will know that there is one who redeems and saves Israel.
1 Maccabees 4:12 And the foreigners lifted their eyes and saw them coming opposite them
1 Maccabees 4:13 and went out of the camp to war; and those with Ioudas sounded the trumpet
1 Maccabees 4:14 and joined battle, and the nations were crushed and fled into the plain,
1 Maccabees 4:15 and all those in the rear fell by the sword. And they pursued them as far as Gazera and as far as the plains of Idumaea and Azotos and Iamneia, and about three thousand men of them fell.
1 Maccabees 4:16 And Ioudas and the army returned from pursuing after them
1 Maccabees 4:17 and he said to the people, Do not desire the spoils, because war is opposite us,
1 Maccabees 4:18 and Gorgias and the army are in the mountain near us; but stand now before our enemies and fight them, and after these things take the spoils with confidence.
1 Maccabees 4:19 While Ioudas was still completing these words, a certain part appeared looking out from the mountain;
1 Maccabees 4:20 and it saw that they had been routed and that they were burning the camp; for the smoke that was seen made what had happened evident.
1 Maccabees 4:21 And seeing these things they became exceedingly cowardly; and seeing also Ioudas's army in the plain ready for battle,
1 Maccabees 4:22 they all fled into the land of foreigners.
1 Maccabees 4:23 And Ioudas returned to the plundering of the camp, and they took much gold and silver and blue cloth and sea-purple and great wealth.
1 Maccabees 4:24 And returning they hymned and blessed toward heaven, because it is good, because his mercy is forever.
1 Maccabees 4:25 And great salvation came to Israel on that day.
1 Maccabees 4:26 And all the foreigners who were preserved came and reported to Lysias everything that had happened.
1 Maccabees 4:27 And hearing it he was confounded and disheartened, because such things had happened to Israel as he did not wish, and it did not turn out as the king had commanded him.
1 Maccabees 4:28 And in the coming year he assembled sixty thousand chosen men and five thousand cavalry to make war upon them.
1 Maccabees 4:29 And they came into Idumaea and encamped in Baithsoura, and Ioudas met them with ten thousand men.
1 Maccabees 4:30 And he saw the strong army and prayed and said, Blessed are you, the savior of Israel, who crushed the assault of the mighty man by the hand of your servant Dauid, and you handed over the army of foreigners into the hands of Ionathes son of Saoul and the bearer of his equipment;
1 Maccabees 4:31 thus shut this army into the hand of your people Israel, and let them be ashamed of their army and their cavalry;
1 Maccabees 4:32 give them cowardice and melt the boldness of their strength, and let them be shaken at their crushing;
1 Maccabees 4:33 cast them down by the sword of those who love you, and let all who know your name praise you with hymns.
1 Maccabees 4:34 And they engaged one another, and about five thousand men fell from Lysias's army, and they fell opposite them.
1 Maccabees 4:35 And Lysias, seeing the rout of his own formation and the courage that had arisen in Ioudas's, and how they were ready either to live or to die nobly, departed to Antioch and recruited more mercenaries to come again into Judaea.
1 Maccabees 4:36 And Ioudas and his brothers said, Behold, our enemies have been crushed; let us go up to cleanse the holy things and dedicate them.
1 Maccabees 4:37 And the whole army gathered, and they went up to Mount Sion.
1 Maccabees 4:38 And they saw the sanctuary laid waste and the altar profaned and the doors burned down, and plants grown in the courts as in a forest or as on one of the mountains, and the chambers torn down.
1 Maccabees 4:39 And they tore their garments and lamented with a great lamentation and put on ashes
1 Maccabees 4:40 and fell face down upon the earth and sounded the signaling trumpets and cried to heaven.
1 Maccabees 4:41 Then Ioudas commanded men to fight those in the citadel until he cleansed the holy things.
1 Maccabees 4:42 And he chose blameless priests who desired the law,
1 Maccabees 4:43 and they cleansed the holy things and took the stones of defilement to an unclean place.
1 Maccabees 4:44 And they deliberated concerning the profaned altar of burnt offering, what they should do with it;
1 Maccabees 4:45 and good counsel came to them to tear it down, lest it become a reproach to them because the nations had defiled it; and they tore down the altar
1 Maccabees 4:46 and put away the stones on the mountain of the house in a suitable place until a prophet came to answer concerning them.
1 Maccabees 4:47 And they took whole stones according to the law and built a new altar like the former one.
1 Maccabees 4:48 And they built the holy things and the interior of the house and sanctified the courts
1 Maccabees 4:49 and made new holy vessels and brought the lampstand and the altar of incense and the table into the temple.
1 Maccabees 4:50 And they burned incense upon the altar and kindled the lamps upon the lampstand, and they shone in the temple.
1 Maccabees 4:51 And they placed breads upon the table and spread out the curtains. And they completed all the works which they did.
1 Maccabees 4:52 And they rose early in the morning on the twenty-fifth of the ninth month [this is the month Chaseleu] of the one hundred forty-eighth year
1 Maccabees 4:53 and offered sacrifice according to the law upon the new altar of burnt offerings which they made.
1 Maccabees 4:54 At the season and on the day on which the nations had profaned it, on that day it was dedicated with songs and harps and lyres and cymbals.
1 Maccabees 4:55 And all the people fell upon their faces and worshiped and blessed toward heaven the one who had prospered them.
1 Maccabees 4:56 And they celebrated the dedication of the altar for eight days and offered burnt offerings with gladness and sacrificed a sacrifice of salvation and praise.
1 Maccabees 4:57 And they adorned the face of the temple with golden crowns and small shields and dedicated the gates and the chambers and fitted them with doors.
1 Maccabees 4:58 And exceedingly great gladness came among the people, and the reproach of the nations was turned away.
1 Maccabees 4:59 And Ioudas and his brothers and the whole assembly of Israel established that the days of the dedication of the altar should be observed at their seasons, year by year, for eight days from the twenty-fifth of the month Chaseleu, with gladness and joy.
1 Maccabees 4:60 And at that time they built high walls and strong towers around Mount Sion, lest the nations come and trample them as they did formerly.
1 Maccabees 4:61 And he stationed an army there to guard it and fortified it to guard Baithsoura, so that the people might have a fortification before Idumaea.

## Chapter 5

1 Maccabees 5:1 And it happened when the surrounding nations heard that the altar had been built and the sanctuary dedicated as formerly, they were exceedingly angry
1 Maccabees 5:2 and resolved to remove the race of Iakob, those among them, and began to put to death among the people and to remove them.
1 Maccabees 5:3 And Ioudas fought against the sons of Esau in Idumaea, Akrabattene, because they besieged Israel, and he struck them with a great blow and subdued them and took their spoils.
1 Maccabees 5:4 And he remembered the wickedness of the sons of Baian, who were a snare and a stumbling block to the people by ambushing them on the roads;
1 Maccabees 5:5 and they were shut up by him in the towers, and he encamped against them and devoted them to destruction and burned its towers with fire together with all who were within.
1 Maccabees 5:6 And he crossed over against the sons of Ammon and found a mighty hand and many people, and Timotheos their leader;
1 Maccabees 5:7 and he joined many battles against them, and they were crushed before his face, and he struck them.
1 Maccabees 5:8 And he seized Iazer and its daughters and returned to Judaea.
1 Maccabees 5:9 And the nations in Galaad gathered against Israel, those within their borders, to remove them, and they fled into Dathema the fortress
1 Maccabees 5:10 and sent letters to Ioudas and his brothers, saying, The nations around us have gathered against us to remove us
1 Maccabees 5:11 and are preparing to come and seize the fortress into which we fled, and Timotheos leads their army;
1 Maccabees 5:12 now therefore come and deliver us from their hand, because a multitude of us has fallen,
1 Maccabees 5:13 and all our brothers in the places of Toubias have been put to death, and they have taken their wives and children and baggage captive, and destroyed there about a thousand-man company.
1 Maccabees 5:14 The letters were still being read, and behold, other messengers arrived from Galilee, having torn their garments, reporting according to these words,
1 Maccabees 5:15 saying that those from Ptolemais and Tyre and Sidon and all Galilee of foreigners had gathered against them to consume us utterly.
1 Maccabees 5:16 And when Ioudas and the people heard these words, a great assembly gathered to deliberate what they should do for their brothers who were in affliction and were being fought by them.
1 Maccabees 5:17 And Ioudas said to Simon his brother, Choose men for yourself and go and deliver your brothers in Galilee, but I and Ionathan my brother will go to Galaaditis.
1 Maccabees 5:18 And he left Iosepos son of Zacharias and Azarias, a leader of the people, with the remainder of the army in Judaea to guard it,
1 Maccabees 5:19 and commanded them, saying, Stand over this people and do not join battle against the nations until we return.
1 Maccabees 5:20 And three thousand men were allotted to Simon to go to Galilee, and eight thousand men to Ioudas for Galaaditis.
1 Maccabees 5:21 And Simon went to Galilee and joined many battles against the nations, and the nations were crushed before him,
1 Maccabees 5:22 and he pursued them as far as the gate of Ptolemais. And about three thousand men fell from the nations, and he took their spoils.
1 Maccabees 5:23 And he took those from Galilee and in Arbatta with their wives and children and everything they had, and brought them into Judaea with great gladness.
1 Maccabees 5:24 And Ioudas Makkabaios and Ionathan his brother crossed the Jordan and traveled a journey of three days in the wilderness.
1 Maccabees 5:25 And they met the Nabataeans, and they met them peacefully and recounted to them everything that had happened to their brothers in Galaaditis,
1 Maccabees 5:26 and that many of them are confined in Bosorra and Bosor, in Alema, Chaspho, Maked and Karnain; all these cities are fortified and great;
1 Maccabees 5:27 and they are confined in the remaining cities of Galaaditis; for tomorrow they are appointed to encamp against the fortifications and seize them and remove all these in one day.
1 Maccabees 5:28 And Ioudas and his army turned their route into the wilderness toward Bosorra suddenly; and he seized the city and killed every male by the mouth of the sword and took all their spoils and burned it with fire.
1 Maccabees 5:29 And he departed from there by night, and they traveled as far as the fortress;
1 Maccabees 5:30 and it happened in the morning, they lifted their eyes, and behold, many people without number, carrying ladders and engines to seize the fortress, and they were fighting them.
1 Maccabees 5:31 And Ioudas saw that the battle had begun and the cry of the city went up to heaven with trumpets and a great cry,
1 Maccabees 5:32 and he said to the men of the army, Fight today for our brothers.
1 Maccabees 5:33 And he went out in three divisions behind them, and they sounded the trumpets and cried in prayer.
1 Maccabees 5:34 And Timotheos's army recognized that it was Makkabaios, and they fled before him, and he struck them with a great blow, and about eight thousand men of them fell on that day.
1 Maccabees 5:35 And he turned aside to Alema and fought it and seized it and killed every male of it and took its spoils and burned it with fire.
1 Maccabees 5:36 From there he departed and seized Chaspho, Maked and Bosor and the remaining cities of Galaaditis.
1 Maccabees 5:37 And after these matters Timotheos gathered another army and encamped opposite Raphon beyond the torrent.
1 Maccabees 5:38 And Ioudas sent to spy out the camp, and they reported to him, saying, All the nations around us have gathered to him, an exceedingly numerous army;
1 Maccabees 5:39 and they have hired Arabs to help them and are encamping beyond the torrent, ready to come against you for war. And Ioudas went to meet them.
1 Maccabees 5:40 And Timotheos said to the commanders of his army as Ioudas and his army approached the torrent of water, If he crosses toward us first, we will not be able to withstand him, because he will surely prevail against us;
1 Maccabees 5:41 but if he becomes cowardly and encamps beyond the river, we will cross over toward him and prevail against him.
1 Maccabees 5:42 And when Ioudas approached the torrent of water, he stationed the scribes of the people at the torrent and commanded them, saying, Do not let any person encamp, but let all come to the battle.
1 Maccabees 5:43 And he crossed against them first, and all the people behind him, and all the nations were crushed before their face and threw down their weapons and fled into the sacred precinct of Karnain.
1 Maccabees 5:44 And they seized the city and burned the sacred precinct with fire together with all those in it; and Karnain was routed, and they could no longer withstand Ioudas before his face.
1 Maccabees 5:45 And Ioudas gathered all Israel in Galaaditis, from small to great, and their wives and their children and their baggage, an exceedingly great company, to come into the land of Iouda.
1 Maccabees 5:46 And they came as far as Ephron, and this was a great city on the road, exceedingly fortified; it was not possible to turn aside from it to the right or left, but only to travel through its midst;
1 Maccabees 5:47 and those from the city shut them out and blocked the gates with stones.
1 Maccabees 5:48 And Ioudas sent to them with peaceful words, saying, We will pass through your land to depart into our land, and no one will harm you; only on our feet will we pass through. And they did not wish to open to him.
1 Maccabees 5:49 And Ioudas commanded a proclamation in the camp that each should encamp in the place where he was;
1 Maccabees 5:50 and the men of the army encamped, and he fought the city all that day and all the night, and the city was handed over into his hand.
1 Maccabees 5:51 And he destroyed every male by the mouth of the sword and uprooted it and took its spoils and passed through the city over those who had been killed.
1 Maccabees 5:52 And they crossed the Jordan into the great plain opposite Baithsan.
1 Maccabees 5:53 And Ioudas was gathering those who fell behind and encouraging the people along the whole road until he came into the land of Iouda.
1 Maccabees 5:54 And they went up to Mount Sion in gladness and joy and offered burnt offerings, because none of them had fallen until they returned in peace.
1 Maccabees 5:55 And in the days when Ioudas and Ionathan were in the land of Galaad and Simon his brother was in Galilee opposite Ptolemais,
1 Maccabees 5:56 Ioseph son of Zacharias and Azarias, commanders of the army, heard of the brave deeds and the war, what things they had done,
1 Maccabees 5:57 and said, Let us also make a name for ourselves and go to fight against the nations around us.
1 Maccabees 5:58 And he gave orders to those of the army with them, and they went against Iamneia.
1 Maccabees 5:59 And Gorgias went out from the city, and his men, to meet them for war.
1 Maccabees 5:60 And Iosepos and Azarias were routed and pursued as far as the borders of Judaea, and about two thousand men of the people of Israel fell on that day.
1 Maccabees 5:61 And a great rout came among the people, because they did not obey Ioudas and his brothers, thinking to perform brave deeds;
1 Maccabees 5:62 but they were not of the seed of those men through whose hand the salvation of Israel was given.
1 Maccabees 5:63 And the man Ioudas and his brothers were exceedingly glorified before all Israel and all the nations wherever their name was heard;
1 Maccabees 5:64 and they gathered to them, speaking praise.
1 Maccabees 5:65 And Ioudas and his brothers went out and fought the sons of Esau in the land toward the south, and he struck Chebron and its daughters and tore down its fortifications and burned its towers all around.
1 Maccabees 5:66 And he departed to go into the land of foreigners and traveled through Marisa.
1 Maccabees 5:67 On that day priests fell in war, wishing to perform brave deeds by going out into war without deliberation.
1 Maccabees 5:68 And Ioudas turned aside to Azotos in the land of foreigners and tore down their altars and burned the carved images of their gods with fire and plundered the spoils of the cities and returned into the land of Iouda.

## Chapter 6

1 Maccabees 6:1 And King Antiochos traveled through the upper countries and heard that Elymais in Persia was a city glorious in wealth, silver and gold;
1 Maccabees 6:2 and the temple in it was exceedingly rich, and there were golden coverings and breastplates and weapons which Alexandros son of Philippos, the Macedonian king who reigned first among the Greeks, left there.
1 Maccabees 6:3 And he came and sought to seize the city and plunder it, and could not, because the matter became known to those of the city,
1 Maccabees 6:4 and they opposed him in war, and he fled and departed from there with great grief to return to Babylon.
1 Maccabees 6:5 And someone came reporting to him in Persia that the armies which went into the land of Iouda had been routed,
1 Maccabees 6:6 and Lysias went with a strong army among the foremost and was put to flight before them, and they grew strong with weapons and an army and many spoils which they took from the armies they cut down,
1 Maccabees 6:7 and tore down the abomination which he built upon the altar in Jerusalem, and surrounded the sanctuary with high walls as formerly, and Baithsoura his city.
1 Maccabees 6:8 And it happened when the king heard these words, he was astonished and exceedingly shaken and fell upon his bed and fell into sickness from grief, because it did not happen for him as he intended.
1 Maccabees 6:9 And he was there for several days, because great grief was renewed upon him, and he reckoned that he was dying.
1 Maccabees 6:10 And he called all his friends and said to them, Sleep departs from my eyes, and I have collapsed in heart from anxiety,
1 Maccabees 6:11 and I said in my heart, To what affliction have I come, and what great surge in which I now am? For I was kind and beloved in my authority.
1 Maccabees 6:12 But now I remember the evils which I did in Jerusalem, and I took all the silver and golden vessels in it and sent to remove the inhabitants of Iouda without cause.
1 Maccabees 6:13 I know that because of these things these evils have found me; and behold, I perish with great grief in a foreign land.
1 Maccabees 6:14 And he called Philippos, one of his friends, and appointed him over his whole kingdom;
1 Maccabees 6:15 and he gave him the diadem and his robe and ring, to guide Antiochos his son and rear him to reign.
1 Maccabees 6:16 And King Antiochos died there in the one hundred forty-ninth year.
1 Maccabees 6:17 And Lysias learned that the king had died, and appointed Antiochos his son, whom he had reared when younger, to reign, and called his name Eupator.
1 Maccabees 6:18 And those from the citadel were shutting Israel in around the holy things and seeking evils throughout and a support for the nations.
1 Maccabees 6:19 And Ioudas resolved to remove them and called all the people into assembly to besiege them;
1 Maccabees 6:20 and they gathered together and besieged it in the one hundred fiftieth year, and he made stations for missiles and engines.
1 Maccabees 6:21 And some of them came out from the confinement, and some of the ungodly from Israel joined them,
1 Maccabees 6:22 and they went to the king and said, How long will you not execute judgment and avenge our brothers?
1 Maccabees 6:23 We willingly serve your father and walk according to what he says and follow his ordinances.
1 Maccabees 6:24 And the sons of our people besieged it because of this and became estranged from us; moreover, all of us who were found were put to death, and our inheritances were plundered.
1 Maccabees 6:25 And they stretched out a hand not only against us but also against all their borders;
1 Maccabees 6:26 and behold, today they have encamped against the citadel in Jerusalem to seize it; and they fortified the sanctuary and Baithsoura;
1 Maccabees 6:27 and unless you forestall them quickly, they will do greater things than these, and you will not be able to restrain them.
1 Maccabees 6:28 And the king became angry when he heard, and gathered all his friends, commanders of his army and those over the reins;
1 Maccabees 6:29 and from other kingdoms and from islands of seas hired armies came to him;
1 Maccabees 6:30 and the number of his armies was a hundred thousand infantry and twenty thousand cavalry and thirty-two elephants that knew war.
1 Maccabees 6:31 And they came through Idumaea and encamped against Baithsoura and fought for many days and made engines; and they went out and burned them with fire and fought manfully.
1 Maccabees 6:32 And Ioudas departed from the citadel and encamped at Baithzacharia opposite the king's army.
1 Maccabees 6:33 And the king rose early in the morning and moved the army in its assault along the road to Baithzacharia, and the armies were prepared for war and sounded the trumpets.
1 Maccabees 6:34 And they showed the elephants the blood of grapes and mulberries to rouse them for war.
1 Maccabees 6:35 And they divided the beasts among the phalanxes and stationed with each elephant a thousand men armored in chain mail, and bronze helmets upon their heads, and five hundred chosen cavalry assigned to each beast;
1 Maccabees 6:36 these were beforehand wherever the beast was, and wherever it went they went together; they did not depart from it.
1 Maccabees 6:37 And strong covered wooden towers were upon them, upon each beast, fastened upon it by devices, and upon each four men of the army who fought upon them, and its Indian.
1 Maccabees 6:38 And he stationed the remaining cavalry on this side and that, on the two sides of the army, brandishing weapons and protecting themselves within the phalanxes.
1 Maccabees 6:39 And as the sun gleamed upon the golden and bronze shields, the mountains gleamed from them and shone like torches of fire.
1 Maccabees 6:40 And a certain part of the king's army extended over the high mountains, and some over the low places; and they came securely and in order.
1 Maccabees 6:41 And all who heard the sound of their multitude and the marching of the multitude and the clash of the weapons were shaken; for the army was exceedingly great and strong.
1 Maccabees 6:42 And Ioudas and his army drew near for battle, and six hundred men fell from the king's army.
1 Maccabees 6:43 And Eleazaros Auaran saw one of the beasts armored with royal breastplates, and it surpassed all the beasts, and he thought that the king was upon it;
1 Maccabees 6:44 and he gave himself to save his people and acquire an everlasting name for himself;
1 Maccabees 6:45 and he ran boldly toward it into the midst of the phalanx and put to death on the right and left, and they split away from him on this side and that;
1 Maccabees 6:46 and he slipped under the elephant and thrust beneath it and killed it, and it fell upon the earth on top of him, and he died there.
1 Maccabees 6:47 And they saw the strength of the kingdom and the assault of the armies and turned away from them.
1 Maccabees 6:48 And those from the king's army went up to meet them in Jerusalem, and the king encamped in Judaea and at Mount Sion.
1 Maccabees 6:49 And he made peace with those from Baithsoura, and they went out from the city, because they had no sustenance there to be shut up in it, because it was a sabbath for the land;
1 Maccabees 6:50 and the king seized Baithsoura and stationed a garrison there to guard it.
1 Maccabees 6:51 And he encamped against the sanctuary for many days and stationed there missile stations and engines and fire throwers and stone throwers and small scorpions for shooting missiles and slings.
1 Maccabees 6:52 And they also made engines against their engines and fought for many days.
1 Maccabees 6:53 But there was no food in the vessels because it was the seventh year, and those who were saved into Judaea from the nations had eaten up the remainder of the stored provisions.
1 Maccabees 6:54 And few men remained in the holy places, because famine overcame them, and they scattered, each to his own place.
1 Maccabees 6:55 And Lysias heard that Philippos, whom King Antiochos appointed while he was still living to rear Antiochos his son so that he might reign,
1 Maccabees 6:56 had returned from Persia and Media, and the armies which went with the king were with him, and that he seeks to take over the affairs.
1 Maccabees 6:57 And he hastened and assented to departing, and said to the king and the leaders of the army and the men, We diminish each day, and our food is little, and the place where we encamp is fortified, and the affairs of the kingdom press upon us;
1 Maccabees 6:58 now therefore let us give right hands to these people and make peace with them and with their whole nation,
1 Maccabees 6:59 and establish for them that they may walk in their customs as formerly; for because of their customs which we abolished they became angry and did all these things.
1 Maccabees 6:60 And the word pleased the king and the rulers, and he sent to them to make peace, and they accepted.
1 Maccabees 6:61 And the king and the rulers swore to them; on these terms they went out from the fortress.
1 Maccabees 6:62 And the king entered Mount Sion and saw the fortification of the place and rejected the oath which he swore and commanded that the wall be torn down all around.
1 Maccabees 6:63 And he departed in haste and returned to Antioch and found Philippos ruling the city and fought against him and seized the city by force.

## Chapter 7

1 Maccabees 7:1 In the one hundred fifty-first year Demetrios son of Seleukos went out from Rome and went up with a few men into a seaside city and reigned there.
1 Maccabees 7:2 And it happened as he entered the house of the kingdom of his fathers, the armies seized Antiochos and Lysias to bring them to him.
1 Maccabees 7:3 And the matter became known to him, and he said, Do not show me their faces.
1 Maccabees 7:4 And the armies killed them, and Demetrios sat upon the throne of his kingdom.
1 Maccabees 7:5 And all the lawless and ungodly men from Israel came to him, and Alkimos led them, wishing to be priest.
1 Maccabees 7:6 And they accused the people before the king, saying, Ioudas and his brothers destroyed all your friends and scattered us from our land;
1 Maccabees 7:7 now therefore send a man whom you trust, and let him go and see all the destruction which he did to us and to the king's country, and let him punish them and all who assist them.
1 Maccabees 7:8 And the king chose Bakchides, of the king's friends, ruling beyond the river and great in the kingdom and faithful to the king,
1 Maccabees 7:9 and sent him and the ungodly Alkimos and established the priesthood for him and commanded him to execute vengeance upon the sons of Israel.
1 Maccabees 7:10 And they departed and came with a numerous army into the land of Iouda; and he sent messengers to Ioudas and his brothers with peaceful words in deceit.
1 Maccabees 7:11 And they did not attend to their words; for they saw that they came with a numerous army.
1 Maccabees 7:12 And an assembly of scribes gathered to Alkimos and Bakchides to seek just things,
1 Maccabees 7:13 and the Asidaians were first among the sons of Israel and sought peace from them;
1 Maccabees 7:14 for they said, A man, a priest of the seed of Aaron, has come with the armies and will not wrong us.
1 Maccabees 7:15 And he spoke peaceful words with them and swore to them, saying, We will not seek evil for you and your friends.
1 Maccabees 7:16 And they trusted him; and he seized sixty men of them and killed them in one day according to the word which he wrote,
1 Maccabees 7:17 The flesh of your holy ones and their blood they poured out around Jerusalem, and there was no one to bury them.
1 Maccabees 7:18 And fear and trembling of them fell upon all the people, because they said, There is no truth and judgment in them, for they transgressed the agreement and the oath which they swore.
1 Maccabees 7:19 And Bakchides departed from Jerusalem and encamped at Bethzaith and sent and seized many of the men who had deserted to him, and some of the people, and slaughtered them into the great well.
1 Maccabees 7:20 And he committed the country to Alkimos and left an army with him to help him; and Bakchides departed to the king.
1 Maccabees 7:21 And Alkimos struggled for the high priesthood,
1 Maccabees 7:22 and all who troubled their people gathered to him and took hold of the land of Iouda and inflicted a great blow in Israel.
1 Maccabees 7:23 And Ioudas saw all the wickedness which Alkimos and those with him did among the sons of Israel, beyond the nations,
1 Maccabees 7:24 and went out into all the borders of Judaea around it and executed vengeance upon the men who deserted, and they were restrained from going out into the country.
1 Maccabees 7:25 And when Alkimos saw that Ioudas and those with him had grown strong, and knew that he could not withstand them, he returned to the king and accused them of evil things.
1 Maccabees 7:26 And the king sent Nikanor, one of his glorious rulers, who hated Israel and was hostile to it, and commanded him to remove the people.
1 Maccabees 7:27 And Nikanor came to Jerusalem with a numerous army and sent to Ioudas and his brothers in deceit with peaceful words, saying,
1 Maccabees 7:28 Let there be no battle between me and you; I will come with a few men so that I may see your faces in peace.
1 Maccabees 7:29 And he came to Ioudas, and they greeted one another peacefully; and the enemies were ready to seize Ioudas.
1 Maccabees 7:30 And the matter became known to Ioudas, that he came against him in deceit, and he was alarmed by him and no longer wished to see his face.
1 Maccabees 7:31 And Nikanor knew that his plan had been uncovered, and went out to meet Ioudas in war near Chapharsalama.
1 Maccabees 7:32 And about five hundred men of those with Nikanor fell, and they fled into the city of Dauid.
1 Maccabees 7:33 And after these words Nikanor went up to Mount Sion. And some of the priests went out from the holy places, and some of the elders of the people, to greet him peacefully and show him the burnt offering being offered for the king.
1 Maccabees 7:34 And he sneered at them and laughed at them and defiled them and spoke arrogantly;
1 Maccabees 7:35 and he swore with wrath, saying, Unless Ioudas and his army are handed over into my hands now, it will happen, if I return in peace, that I will burn this house. And he went out with great wrath.
1 Maccabees 7:36 And the priests entered and stood before the face of the altar and the temple and wept and said,
1 Maccabees 7:37 You chose this house for your name to be invoked upon it, to be a house of prayer and supplication for your people;
1 Maccabees 7:38 execute vengeance upon this man and his army, and let them fall by the sword; remember their evil speech and do not give them continuance.
1 Maccabees 7:39 And Nikanor went out from Jerusalem and encamped in Baithoron, and an army of Syria met him.
1 Maccabees 7:40 And Ioudas encamped in Adasa with three thousand men; and Ioudas prayed and said,
1 Maccabees 7:41 When those from the king spoke evil, your angel went out and struck a hundred eighty-five thousand among them;
1 Maccabees 7:42 thus crush this army before us today, and let the remainder know that he spoke evilly against your holy things, and judge him according to his wickedness.
1 Maccabees 7:43 And the armies joined battle on the thirteenth of the month Adar, and Nikanor's army was crushed, and he fell first in the battle.
1 Maccabees 7:44 And when his army saw that Nikanor had fallen, they threw down their weapons and fled.
1 Maccabees 7:45 And they pursued them a journey of one day from Adasa until coming to Gazera and sounded the signaling trumpets behind them.
1 Maccabees 7:46 And they went out from all the villages of Judaea around it and outflanked them, and these turned back toward those, and they all fell by the sword, and not even one of them was left.
1 Maccabees 7:47 And they took the spoils and plunder, and cut off Nikanor's head and his right hand which he had stretched out arrogantly, and brought them and displayed them beside Jerusalem.
1 Maccabees 7:48 And the people were exceedingly glad, and observed that day as a great day of gladness;
1 Maccabees 7:49 and they established that this day should be observed each year on the thirteenth of Adar.
1 Maccabees 7:50 And the land of Iouda was quiet for a few days.

## Chapter 8

1 Maccabees 8:1 And Ioudas heard the name of the Romans, that they are mighty in strength and they take pleasure in all those joining them, and as many as approach them, they establish friendship with them, and that they are mighty in strength.
1 Maccabees 8:2 And they related to him their wars and the deeds of courage which they do among the Galatians, and that they prevailed over them and brought them under tribute,
1 Maccabees 8:3 and whatever they did in the land of Spain to gain possession of the mines of silver and gold there;
1 Maccabees 8:4 and they gained possession of the whole place by their counsel and their patience, and the place was very far distant from them, and of the kings who came against them from the end of the earth, until they crushed them and struck a great blow among them, and those remaining give them tribute yearly;
1 Maccabees 8:5 and Philip and Perseus, king of the Kitians, and those raised up against them, they crushed them in war and prevailed over them;
1 Maccabees 8:6 and Antiochos, the great king of Asia, who went against them for war, having one hundred and twenty elephants and cavalry and chariots and a very great force, and he was crushed by them,
1 Maccabees 8:7 and they took him alive and established that he and those reigning after him should give them great tribute and give hostages and a stipulated agreement
1 Maccabees 8:8 and the Indian land and Media and Lydia, from their finest lands, and having taken them from him, they gave them to Eumenes the king;
1 Maccabees 8:9 and that those from Greece planned to come and remove them,
1 Maccabees 8:10 and the matter became known to them, and they sent one commander against them and fought against them, and many wounded fell from among them, and they took their wives and their children captive and plundered them and gained possession of the land and pulled down their strongholds and enslaved them until this day;
1 Maccabees 8:11 and the remaining kingdoms and the islands, as many as ever stood against them, they destroyed and enslaved them, but with their friends and those relying on them they maintained friendship;
1 Maccabees 8:12 and they prevailed over the kings nearby and those far away, and as many as heard their name were afraid of them.
1 Maccabees 8:13 And those whom they wish to help and to reign, reign; but those whom they wish, they remove; and they were greatly exalted.
1 Maccabees 8:14 And in all these things not even one of them put on a diadem, nor did they clothe themselves in purple so as to be magnified in it;
1 Maccabees 8:15 and they made themselves a council chamber, and daily three hundred and twenty deliberated, deliberating continually concerning the multitude, that they should be well ordered;
1 Maccabees 8:16 and they entrust one man to rule them yearly and to exercise lordship over all their land, and all obey the one, and there is no envy or jealousy among them.
1 Maccabees 8:17 And Ioudas selected Eupolemos, son of Ioannes, of Akkos, and Iason, son of Eleazar, and sent them to Rome to establish friendship and alliance
1 Maccabees 8:18 and to lift the yoke from them, because they saw the kingdom of the Greeks enslaving Israel with slavery.
1 Maccabees 8:19 And they went to Rome, and the journey was very long, and they entered the council chamber and answered and said,
1 Maccabees 8:20 Ioudas, also called Makkabaios, and his brothers and the multitude of the Judeans sent us to you to establish alliance and peace with you and for us to be registered as your allies and friends.
1 Maccabees 8:21 And the statement was pleasing before them.
1 Maccabees 8:22 And this is the copy of the letter which they copied on bronze tablets and sent to Ierousalem to be with them there as a memorial of peace and alliance:
1 Maccabees 8:23 May it go well with the Romans and the nation of the Judeans on the sea and on the dry land forever, and may sword and enemy be put far from them.
1 Maccabees 8:24 But if war arises first for Rome or for all their allies in all their dominion,
1 Maccabees 8:25 the nation of the Judeans shall act as allies, as the occasion prescribes for them, with a full heart;
1 Maccabees 8:26 and to those waging war they shall not give or supply grain, weapons, silver, ships, as Rome decided; and they shall keep their obligations, taking nothing.
1 Maccabees 8:27 And in the same way, if war happens first to the nation of the Judeans, the Romans shall act as allies from the soul, as the occasion prescribes for them?
1 Maccabees 8:28 And to those allied, grain, weapons, silver, ships shall not be given, as Rome decided; and they shall keep these obligations, and without deceit. —
1 Maccabees 8:29 According to these words the Romans thus established an agreement with the people of the Judeans.
1 Maccabees 8:30 But if after these words these and those decide to add or remove, they shall do so by their own choice, and whatever they add or remove shall be authoritative.
1 Maccabees 8:31 And concerning the evils which King Demetrios carries out against them, we wrote to him, saying, Why have you made your yoke heavy upon our friends, the allied Judeans?
1 Maccabees 8:32 If therefore they petition against you again, we shall execute judgment for them and wage war against you by sea and by dry land.

## Chapter 9

1 Maccabees 9:1 And Demetrios heard that Nikanor and his force had fallen in war, and he proceeded to send Bakchides and Alkimos a second time into the land of Iouda, and the right wing with them.
1 Maccabees 9:2 And they went by the road to Galgala and encamped against Maisaloth in Arbela and seized it beforehand and destroyed many human lives.
1 Maccabees 9:3 And in the first month of the one hundred and fifty-second year they encamped against Ierousalem;
1 Maccabees 9:4 and they departed and went to Berea with twenty thousand men and two thousand cavalry.
1 Maccabees 9:5 And Ioudas was encamped in Elasa, and three thousand chosen men with him.
1 Maccabees 9:6 And they saw the multitude of the forces, that they were many, and were very afraid; and many slipped away from the camp; none were left of them except eight hundred men.
1 Maccabees 9:7 And Ioudas saw that his camp had slipped away and the war was pressing him, and he was crushed in heart, because he had no opportunity to gather them,
1 Maccabees 9:8 and he grew faint and said to those left, Let us arise and go up against our adversaries, if perhaps we can fight against them.
1 Maccabees 9:9 And they tried to turn him back, saying, We certainly cannot, but let us save our own lives now; let us return, and our brothers, and fight against them, but we are few.
1 Maccabees 9:10 And Ioudas said, May it not happen that we do this thing, flee from them; and if our time has drawn near, let us also die with courage for the sake of our brothers and not leave a charge against our glory.
1 Maccabees 9:11 And the force departed from the camp and they stood to meet them, and the cavalry was divided into two parts, and the slingers and the archers went before the force, and the foremost fighters, all the mighty men, but Bakchides was in the right wing.
1 Maccabees 9:12 And the phalanx drew near from the two parts and they sounded with the trumpets, and those with Ioudas also blew with the trumpets;
1 Maccabees 9:13 and the earth was shaken by the sound of the camps, and the battle was joined from morning until evening.
1 Maccabees 9:14 And Ioudas saw that Bakchides and the strength of the camp were on the right, and all those courageous in heart came together with him,
1 Maccabees 9:15 and the right part was crushed by them, and he pursued after them as far as Mount Azotos.
1 Maccabees 9:16 And those in the left wing saw that the right wing was crushed, and they turned on the heels of Ioudas and those with him from behind.
1 Maccabees 9:17 And the battle became heavy, and many wounded fell from these and from those,
1 Maccabees 9:18 and Ioudas fell, and the rest fled.
1 Maccabees 9:19 And Ionathan and Simon lifted Ioudas their brother and buried him in the tomb of his fathers in Modein.
1 Maccabees 9:20 And all Israel wept for him and lamented him with a great lamentation and mourned for many days and said,
1 Maccabees 9:21 How a mighty man has fallen, who saved Israel.
1 Maccabees 9:22 And the remaining accounts of Ioudas and the wars and the deeds of courage which he did, and his greatness, were not recorded; for they were very many.
1 Maccabees 9:23 And it happened after the death of Ioudas that the lawless emerged in all the borders of Israel, and all those working injustice sprang up.
1 Maccabees 9:24 In those days a very great famine occurred, and the land deserted to their side.
1 Maccabees 9:25 And Bakchides chose the impious men and appointed them masters of the land.
1 Maccabees 9:26 And they sought out and searched for the friends of Ioudas and brought them to Bakchides, and he punished them and mocked them.
1 Maccabees 9:27 And great affliction came in Israel, such as had not occurred from the day when a prophet was not seen by them.
1 Maccabees 9:28 And all the friends of Ioudas were gathered and said to Ionathan,
1 Maccabees 9:29 Since your brother Ioudas has died, and there is no man like him to go out and come in against the enemies and Bakchides and among those hostile to our nation;
1 Maccabees 9:30 now therefore we have chosen you today to be for us in his place as ruler and leader, to fight our war.
1 Maccabees 9:31 And Ionathan accepted the leadership at that time and arose in place of Ioudas his brother.
1 Maccabees 9:32 And Bakchides learned of it and sought to kill him.
1 Maccabees 9:33 And Ionathan and Simon his brother and all those with him learned of it and fled into the wilderness of Thekoe and encamped by the water of the pool Asphar.
1 Maccabees 9:34 And Bakchides learned of it on the sabbath day and came, he and all his army, beyond the Iordan. —
1 Maccabees 9:35 And he sent his brother, leader of the crowd, and entreated the Nabateans, his friends, to deposit with them their abundant baggage.
1 Maccabees 9:36 And the sons of Iambri from Medaba came out and seized Ioannes and all that he had and departed with it.
1 Maccabees 9:37 After these matters they reported to Ionathan and Simon his brother that the sons of Iambri are holding a great wedding and are bringing the bride from Nadabath, daughter of one of the great nobles of Chanaan, with a great escort.
1 Maccabees 9:38 And they remembered the blood of Ioannes their brother and went up and hid under the shelter of the mountain.
1 Maccabees 9:39 And they lifted their eyes and saw, and behold, a commotion and abundant baggage, and the bridegroom came out, and his friends and his brothers, to meet them with drums and musicians and many weapons.
1 Maccabees 9:40 And they rose against them from the ambush and killed them, and many wounded fell, and those remaining fled into the mountain; and they took all their spoils.
1 Maccabees 9:41 And the wedding was turned into mourning and the sound of their musicians into lamentation.
1 Maccabees 9:42 And they exacted vengeance for the blood of their brother and returned to the marsh of the Iordan. —
1 Maccabees 9:43 And Bakchides heard and came on the sabbath day as far as the banks of the Iordan with a great force.
1 Maccabees 9:44 And Ionathan said to those with him, Let us now arise and fight for our lives, for today is not as yesterday and the third day;
1 Maccabees 9:45 for behold, the battle is in front and behind us, and the water of the Iordan on this side and that side, and marsh and woodland; there is no place to turn aside;
1 Maccabees 9:46 now therefore cry out to heaven, so that you may be saved from the hand of our enemies.
1 Maccabees 9:47 And the battle joined; and Ionathan stretched out his hand to strike Bakchides, and he turned aside from him backward.
1 Maccabees 9:48 And Ionathan and those with him leaped into the Iordan and swam across to the other side, and they did not cross the Iordan against them.
1 Maccabees 9:49 And on that day about a thousand men fell on Bakchides' side.
1 Maccabees 9:50 And he returned to Ierousalem, and they built fortified cities in Judea, the stronghold in Iericho and Ammaous and Baithoron and Baithel and Thamnatha Pharathon and Tephon, with high walls and gates and bars;
1 Maccabees 9:51 and he placed a garrison in them to act against Israel.
1 Maccabees 9:52 And he fortified the city Baithsoura and Gazara and the citadel and placed forces and stores of food in them.
1 Maccabees 9:53 And he took the sons of the leaders of the land as hostages and placed them in the citadel in Ierousalem under guard.
1 Maccabees 9:54 And in the one hundred and fifty-third year, in the second month, Alkimos ordered the wall of the inner court of the holy places to be pulled down; and he pulled down the works of the prophets and began to pull down.
1 Maccabees 9:55 At that time Alkimos was struck, and his works were hindered, and his mouth was stopped, and he was paralyzed and could no longer speak a word or give orders concerning his house.
1 Maccabees 9:56 And Alkimos died at that time with great torment.
1 Maccabees 9:57 And Bakchides saw that Alkimos had died and returned to the king. And the land of Iouda was quiet for two years.
1 Maccabees 9:58 And all the lawless plotted, saying, Behold, Ionathan and those with him dwell in quiet, confidently; now therefore we shall bring up Bakchides, and he will seize them all in one night.
1 Maccabees 9:59 And they went and counseled him.
1 Maccabees 9:60 And he departed to come with a great force and secretly sent letters to all his allies in Judea, that they should seize Ionathan and those with him; and they could not, because their plan became known.
1 Maccabees 9:61 And they seized about fifty men from the men of the land, the leaders of the wickedness, and killed them.
1 Maccabees 9:62 And Ionathan and Simon and those with him withdrew to Baithbasi in the wilderness, and he rebuilt its demolished parts, and they strengthened it.
1 Maccabees 9:63 And Bakchides learned of it and gathered all his multitude and gave orders to those from Judea;
1 Maccabees 9:64 and he came and encamped against Baithbasi and fought against it for many days and made engines.
1 Maccabees 9:65 And Ionathan left Simon his brother in the city and went out into the country and came with a number of men.
1 Maccabees 9:66 And he struck Odomera and his brothers and the sons of Phasiron in their dwelling, and they began to strike and went up with the forces.
1 Maccabees 9:67 And Simon and those with him came out of the city and burned the engines;
1 Maccabees 9:68 and they fought against Bakchides, and he was crushed by them, and they afflicted him greatly, because his plan and his assault were empty.
1 Maccabees 9:69 And he was angry in wrath with the lawless men who had counseled him to come into the country and killed many of them and decided to depart to his own land.
1 Maccabees 9:70 And Ionathan learned of it and sent ambassadors to him to agree on peace with him and to return the captives to them.
1 Maccabees 9:71 And he accepted and did according to his words and swore to him not to seek harm for him all the days of his life;
1 Maccabees 9:72 and he returned to him the captives whom he had previously taken captive from the land of Iouda, and he turned back and departed to his own land and did not again come into their borders.
1 Maccabees 9:73 And the sword ceased from Israel; and Ionathan dwelt in Machmas, and Ionathan began to judge the people and removed the impious from Israel.

## Chapter 10

1 Maccabees 10:1 And in the one hundred and sixtieth year Alexandros, the son of Antiochos, the Illustrious, went up and seized Ptolemais, and they received him, and he reigned there.
1 Maccabees 10:2 And Demetrios the king heard and gathered very many forces and went out to meet him for war.
1 Maccabees 10:3 And Demetrios sent letters to Ionathan with peaceful words so as to magnify him;
1 Maccabees 10:4 for he said, Let us act first to establish peace with them before he establishes it with Alexandros against us;
1 Maccabees 10:5 for he will remember all the evils which we carried out against him and against his brothers and against the nation.
1 Maccabees 10:6 And he gave him authority to gather forces and prepare weapons and to be his ally, and he said to hand over to him the hostages in the citadel.
1 Maccabees 10:7 And Ionathan came to Ierousalem and read the letters into the ears of all the people and those from the citadel.
1 Maccabees 10:8 And they feared with great fear when they heard that the king had given him authority to gather a force.
1 Maccabees 10:9 And those from the citadel handed the hostages over to Ionathan, and he returned them to their parents.
1 Maccabees 10:10 And Ionathan dwelt in Ierousalem and began to build and renew the city.
1 Maccabees 10:11 And he told those doing the works to build the walls and Mount Sion all around with four-foot stones for fortification, and they did so.
1 Maccabees 10:12 And the foreigners who were in the strongholds which Bakchides had built fled,
1 Maccabees 10:13 and each left his place and departed to his own land;
1 Maccabees 10:14 except in Baithsoura some of those who had abandoned the law and the ordinances remained; for it was a refuge.
1 Maccabees 10:15 And Alexandros the king heard the promises, as many as Demetrios had sent to Ionathan, and they related to him the wars and the deeds of courage which he and his brothers had done, and the labors which they had endured,
1 Maccabees 10:16 and he said, Surely we shall not find one such man? And now we shall make him our friend and ally.
1 Maccabees 10:17 And he wrote letters and sent them to him according to these words, saying,
1 Maccabees 10:18 King Alexandros to his brother Ionathan, greetings.
1 Maccabees 10:19 We have heard concerning you that you are a man mighty in strength and fit to be our friend.
1 Maccabees 10:20 And now we have appointed you today high priest of your nation and for you to be called a friend of the king [and he sent him purple and a golden crown] and to think of our affairs and maintain friendship toward us.
1 Maccabees 10:21 And Ionathan put on the holy robe in the seventh month of the one hundred and sixtieth year, at the feast of tent-pitching, and gathered forces and prepared many weapons.
1 Maccabees 10:22 And Demetrios heard these words and was grieved and said,
1 Maccabees 10:23 What is this we have done, that Alexandros has anticipated us in gaining friendship with the Judeans as a support?
1 Maccabees 10:24 I too shall write them words of encouragement and exaltation and gifts, so that they may be with me for help.
1 Maccabees 10:25 And he sent to them according to these words: King Demetrios to the nation of the Judeans, greetings.
1 Maccabees 10:26 Since you have maintained the agreements with us and remained in our friendship and have not gone over to our enemies, we heard and rejoiced.
1 Maccabees 10:27 And now continue still to maintain faithfulness toward us, and we shall repay you good things in return for what you do with us.
1 Maccabees 10:28 And we shall grant you many remissions and give you gifts.
1 Maccabees 10:29 And now I release you and exempt all the Judeans from the tributes and the price of salt and from the crowns,
1 Maccabees 10:30 and instead of the third of the sowing and instead of the half of the fruit of the trees which falls to me to receive, I remit from today and onward the receiving of it from the land of Iouda and from the three districts added to it from Samaria and Galilee, from today and for all time.
1 Maccabees 10:31 And let Ierousalem be holy and exempt, and its borders, the tithes and the taxes.
1 Maccabees 10:32 I also relinquish authority over the citadel in Ierousalem and give it to the high priest, so that he may appoint in it men whom he himself chooses to guard it.
1 Maccabees 10:33 And every soul of the Judeans taken captive from the land of Iouda into any part of my kingdom I release free without payment; and let all remit the tributes, also those on their livestock.
1 Maccabees 10:34 And all the feasts and the sabbaths and new moons and appointed days, and three days before a feast and three after a feast, let them all be days of exemption and remission for all the Judeans who are in my kingdom,
1 Maccabees 10:35 and no one shall have authority to exact payment and trouble any of them concerning any matter.
1 Maccabees 10:36 And let about thirty thousand men of the Judeans be enrolled in the forces of the king, and allowances shall be given to them, as is fitting for all the forces of the king.
1 Maccabees 10:37 And some of them shall be appointed in the great strongholds of the king, and from these some shall be appointed over affairs of the kingdom that require trust; and let those over them and the rulers be from among them, and let them walk by their own laws, as the king also ordered in the land of Iouda.
1 Maccabees 10:38 And the three districts added to Judea from the country of Samaria, let them be added to Judea to be reckoned as being under one, so as not to obey another authority except the high priest.
1 Maccabees 10:39 I have given Ptolemais and the territory belonging to it as a gift to the holy places in Ierousalem for the expenditure due to the holy places.
1 Maccabees 10:40 And I give yearly fifteen thousand shekels of silver from the accounts of the king, from the appropriate places.
1 Maccabees 10:41 And all the surplus which they did not pay from the revenues as in the first years, from now they shall give for the works of the house.
1 Maccabees 10:42 And besides these, five thousand shekels of silver which they used to receive yearly from the revenues of the holy place from the account, these also are remitted because they belong to the priests who minister.
1 Maccabees 10:43 And as many as flee to the temple in Ierosolyma and within all its borders, owing royal dues or any obligation, let them be released, and all that belongs to them in my kingdom.
1 Maccabees 10:44 And for the works of the holy places to be built and renewed, the expense shall also be given from the account of the king.
1 Maccabees 10:45 And for the walls of Ierousalem to be built and fortified all around, the expense shall also be given from the account of the king, and for the walls in Judea to be built.
1 Maccabees 10:46 But when Ionathan and the people heard these words, they did not believe them or accept them, because they remembered the great wickedness which he had done in Israel and had afflicted them greatly.
1 Maccabees 10:47 And they were pleased with Alexandros, because he had become for them the initiator of peaceful words, and they acted as his allies all the days.
1 Maccabees 10:48 And Alexandros the king gathered great forces and encamped opposite Demetrios.
1 Maccabees 10:49 And the two kings joined battle, and the camp of Demetrios fled, and Alexandros pursued him and prevailed over them;
1 Maccabees 10:50 and he pressed the battle very hard until the sun set, and Demetrios fell on that day.
1 Maccabees 10:51 And Alexandros sent ambassadors to Ptolemaios, king of Egypt, according to these words, saying,
1 Maccabees 10:52 Since I returned to my kingdom and sat on the throne of my fathers and took hold of the rule, and crushed Demetrios and gained possession of our country
1 Maccabees 10:53 and joined battle against him, and he and his camp were crushed by us, and we sat on the throne of his kingdom;
1 Maccabees 10:54 and now let us establish friendship with one another, and now give me your daughter as wife, and I shall become your son-in-law and give gifts to you and to her worthy of you.
1 Maccabees 10:55 And Ptolemaios the king answered, saying, Good is the day on which you returned to the land of your fathers and sat on the throne of their kingdom.
1 Maccabees 10:56 And now I shall do for you what you wrote, but meet me at Ptolemais, so that we may see one another, and I shall become related to you by marriage, as you have said.
1 Maccabees 10:57 And Ptolemaios went out from Egypt, he and Kleopatra his daughter, and came to Ptolemais in the one hundred and sixty-second year.
1 Maccabees 10:58 And Alexandros the king met him, and he gave him Kleopatra his daughter in marriage and held her wedding in Ptolemais as kings do, with great glory. —
1 Maccabees 10:59 And Alexandros the king wrote to Ionathes to come to meet him.
1 Maccabees 10:60 And he went with glory to Ptolemais and met the two kings; and he gave them silver and gold, and to their friends, and many gifts, and found favor before them.
1 Maccabees 10:61 And pestilent men from Israel, lawless men, gathered against him to petition against him, and the king did not pay attention to them.
1 Maccabees 10:62 And the king ordered, and they stripped Ionathan of his garments and clothed him in purple, and they did so.
1 Maccabees 10:63 And the king seated him with himself and said to his rulers, Go out with him into the midst of the city and proclaim that no one is to petition against him concerning any matter, and let no one trouble him concerning any statement.
1 Maccabees 10:64 And it happened when those petitioning saw his glory, as he had proclaimed, and him clothed in purple, that they all fled.
1 Maccabees 10:65 And the king glorified him and registered him among the first friends and appointed him commander and governor of a district.
1 Maccabees 10:66 And Ionathan returned to Ierousalem with peace and gladness.
1 Maccabees 10:67 And in the one hundred and sixty-fifth year Demetrios, son of Demetrios, came from Crete into the land of his fathers.
1 Maccabees 10:68 And Alexandros the king heard and was greatly grieved and returned to Antiocheia.
1 Maccabees 10:69 And Demetrios appointed Apollonios, who was over Coele Syria, and he gathered a great force and encamped against Iamneia; and he sent to Ionathan the high priest, saying,
1 Maccabees 10:70 You alone raise yourself against us, but I have become a laughingstock and a reproach because of you; and why do you exercise power against us in the mountains?
1 Maccabees 10:71 Now therefore, if you trust in your forces, come down to us into the plain, and let us contend with one another there, because with me is a force from the cities.
1 Maccabees 10:72 Ask and learn who I am and the rest who help us, and they say, You have no foothold before us, because your fathers were routed twice in their land.
1 Maccabees 10:73 And now you will not be able to withstand the cavalry and such a force in the plain, where there is no stone or pebble or place to flee.
1 Maccabees 10:74 But when Ionathan heard the words of Apollonios, he was stirred in his mind and selected ten thousand men and went out from Ierousalem, and Simon his brother met him to help him.
1 Maccabees 10:75 And he encamped against Ioppe, and those from the city shut it, because a garrison of Apollonios was in Ioppe; and they fought against it,
1 Maccabees 10:76 and those from the city became afraid and opened it, and Ionathan became master of Ioppe.
1 Maccabees 10:77 And Apollonios heard and encamped with three thousand cavalry and a great force and went to Azotos as though passing through, and at the same time advanced into the plain because he had a multitude of cavalry and trusted in it.
1 Maccabees 10:78 And he pursued after him to Azotos, and the camps joined in battle.
1 Maccabees 10:79 And Apollonios left a thousand cavalry secretly behind them.
1 Maccabees 10:80 And Ionathan knew that there was an ambush behind him, and they surrounded his camp and hurled the shafts at the people from morning until evening;
1 Maccabees 10:81 but the people stood as Ionathan had ordered, and their horses grew weary.
1 Maccabees 10:82 And Simon brought his force forward and joined against the phalanx, for the cavalry had grown faint, and they were crushed by him and fled,
1 Maccabees 10:83 and the cavalry was scattered in the plain. And they fled to Azotos and entered Bethdagon, their idol temple, to be saved.
1 Maccabees 10:84 And Ionathan burned Azotos and the cities around it and took their spoils, and the temple of Dagon and those who had fled together into it he burned with fire.
1 Maccabees 10:85 And those fallen by the sword, together with those burned, amounted to about eight thousand men.
1 Maccabees 10:86 And Ionathan departed from there and encamped against Askalon, and those from the city came out to meet him with great glory.
1 Maccabees 10:87 And Ionathan returned to Ierousalem with those with him, having many spoils.
1 Maccabees 10:88 And it happened when Alexandros the king heard these matters, that he proceeded to glorify Ionathan further;
1 Maccabees 10:89 and he sent him a golden clasp, as it is customary to give to the relatives of kings, and gave him Akkaron and all its borders as an inheritance.

## Chapter 11

1 Maccabees 11:1 And the king of Egypt gathered many forces, like the sand beside the shore of the sea, and many ships, and sought to gain possession of the kingdom of Alexandros by deceit and add it to his own kingdom.
1 Maccabees 11:2 And he went out into Syria with peaceful words, and those from the cities opened to him and met him, because there was a command of Alexandros the king to meet him because he was his father-in-law;
1 Maccabees 11:3 but as Ptolemaios entered the cities, he stationed the forces as a garrison in each city.
1 Maccabees 11:4 But when they drew near Azotos, they showed him the temple of Dagon burned and Azotos and its surrounding towns demolished and the bodies cast down and those burned whom he had burned in the war; for they had made heaps of them in his path.
1 Maccabees 11:5 And they related to the king what Ionathan had done, to blame him; and the king was silent.
1 Maccabees 11:6 And Ionathan met the king at Ioppe with glory, and they greeted one another and slept there.
1 Maccabees 11:7 And Ionathan went with the king as far as the river called Eleutheros and returned to Ierousalem.
1 Maccabees 11:8 But King Ptolemaios became master of the coastal cities as far as Seleukeia by the sea and considered wicked designs concerning Alexandros.
1 Maccabees 11:9 And he sent ambassadors to Demetrios the king, saying, Come, let us make a covenant with one another, and I shall give you my daughter whom Alexandros had, and you shall reign over the kingdom of your father;
1 Maccabees 11:10 for I regret giving him my daughter, for he sought to kill me.
1 Maccabees 11:11 And he blamed him because he desired his kingdom;
1 Maccabees 11:12 and having taken his daughter away from him, he gave her to Demetrios and became estranged from Alexandros, and their enmity became evident.
1 Maccabees 11:13 And Ptolemaios entered Antiocheia and put on the diadem of Asia; and he put two diadems around his head, that of Egypt and of Asia.
1 Maccabees 11:14 But Alexandros the king was in Cilicia at those times, because those from those places were revolting.
1 Maccabees 11:15 And Alexandros heard and came against him in war. And Ptolemaios led out and met him with a strong hand and routed him;
1 Maccabees 11:16 and Alexandros fled into Arabia to be sheltered there, but King Ptolemaios was exalted.
1 Maccabees 11:17 And Zabdiel the Arab removed the head of Alexandros and sent it to Ptolemaios.
1 Maccabees 11:18 And King Ptolemaios died on the third day, and those who were in his strongholds were destroyed by those in the strongholds.
1 Maccabees 11:19 And Demetrios reigned in the one hundred and sixty-seventh year.
1 Maccabees 11:20 In those days Ionathan gathered those from Judea to wage war against the citadel in Ierousalem and made many engines against it.
1 Maccabees 11:21 And some lawless men who hated their nation went to the king and reported to him that Ionathan was besieging the citadel.
1 Maccabees 11:22 And on hearing it he became angry; and when he heard, he immediately set out and came to Ptolemais and wrote to Ionathan not to besiege it and to meet him, to confer with him in Ptolemais as quickly as possible.
1 Maccabees 11:23 But when Ionathan heard, he ordered the siege to continue and selected some of the elders of Israel and of the priests and gave himself to the danger;
1 Maccabees 11:24 and taking silver and gold and clothing and many other gifts, he also went to the king in Ptolemais and found favor before him.
1 Maccabees 11:25 And some lawless men from the nation were petitioning against him.
1 Maccabees 11:26 And the king did for him as those before him had done for him and exalted him before all his friends.
1 Maccabees 11:27 And he confirmed for him the high priesthood and whatever other honors he previously had and caused him to be reckoned among the first friends.
1 Maccabees 11:28 And Ionathan requested the king to make Judea free of tribute, and the three districts and Samaria, and promised him three hundred talents.
1 Maccabees 11:29 And the king consented and wrote letters to Ionathan concerning all these things, having this form:
1 Maccabees 11:30 King Demetrios to Ionathan his brother and to the nation of the Judeans, greetings.
1 Maccabees 11:31 The copy of the letter which we wrote to Lasthenes our relative concerning you we have also written to you, so that you may know.
1 Maccabees 11:32 King Demetrios to Lasthenes his father, greetings.
1 Maccabees 11:33 We decided to do good to the nation of the Judeans, our friends, who maintain their just obligations toward us, because of their goodwill toward us.
1 Maccabees 11:34 We have confirmed for them both the borders of Judea and the three districts Aphairema and Lydda and Rathamin; they were added to Judea from Samaria, and all that belongs to them, for all those sacrificing in Ierosolyma, in place of the royal dues which the king previously received from them yearly from the produce of the land and the fruits of the trees.
1 Maccabees 11:35 And the other things belonging to us from now, of the tithes and the taxes belonging to us, and the salt lakes and the crowns belonging to us, we shall grant them all.
1 Maccabees 11:36 And not even one of these shall be set aside from now for all time.
1 Maccabees 11:37 Now therefore take care to make a copy of these, and let it be given to Ionathan and placed on the holy mountain in a conspicuous place.
1 Maccabees 11:38 And Demetrios the king saw that the land was quiet before him and nothing stood against him, and he discharged all his forces, each to his own place, except the foreign forces which he had recruited from the islands of the nations; and all the forces inherited from the fathers became hostile to him.
1 Maccabees 11:39 But Tryphon was formerly among those with Alexandros and saw that all the forces were murmuring against Demetrios, and he went to Imalkoue the Arab, who was raising Antiochos, the little boy of Alexandros.
1 Maccabees 11:40 And he pressed him to hand him over to him, so that he might reign in place of his father; and he reported to him whatever Demetrios had carried out and the enmity with which his forces were hostile to him, and he remained there many days.
1 Maccabees 11:41 And Ionathan sent to Demetrios the king, that he should expel those from the citadel from Ierousalem and those in the strongholds; for they were fighting Israel.
1 Maccabees 11:42 And Demetrios sent to Ionathan, saying, I shall do not only these things for you and your nation, but with glory I shall glorify you and your nation, if I obtain an opportunity;
1 Maccabees 11:43 now therefore you will do rightly by sending me men who will act as my allies, because all my forces have revolted.
1 Maccabees 11:44 And Ionathan sent him three thousand men mighty in strength to Antiocheia, and they came to the king, and the king rejoiced at their arrival.
1 Maccabees 11:45 And those from the city gathered into the midst of the city, about one hundred and twenty thousand men, and wished to kill the king.
1 Maccabees 11:46 And the king fled into the court, and those from the city seized the passages of the city and began to fight.
1 Maccabees 11:47 And the king called the Judeans for help, and they all gathered to him together and scattered in the city and killed about one hundred thousand on that day;
1 Maccabees 11:48 and they burned the city and took many spoils on that day and saved the king.
1 Maccabees 11:49 And those from the city saw that the Judeans had gained possession of the city as they wished, and they grew weak in their minds and cried out to the king with entreaty, saying,
1 Maccabees 11:50 Give us your right hands, and let the Judeans stop fighting us and the city.
1 Maccabees 11:51 And they threw down their weapons and made peace. And the Judeans were glorified before the king and before all those in his kingdom and returned to Ierousalem with many spoils.
1 Maccabees 11:52 And Demetrios the king sat on the throne of his kingdom, and the land was quiet before him.
1 Maccabees 11:53 And he proved false in everything he had said and became estranged from Ionathan and did not repay the kindnesses which he had rendered him, and afflicted him greatly.
1 Maccabees 11:54 But after these things Tryphon returned, and Antiochos with him, a young boy; and he reigned and put on a diadem.
1 Maccabees 11:55 And all the forces which Demetrios had dismissed gathered to him and fought against him, and he fled and was routed.
1 Maccabees 11:56 And Tryphon took the beasts and gained possession of Antiocheia.
1 Maccabees 11:57 And Antiochos the younger wrote to Ionathes, saying, I confirm the high priesthood for you and appoint you over the four districts and to be among the friends of the king.
1 Maccabees 11:58 And he sent him golden vessels and a table service and gave him authority to drink from golden vessels and to be in purple and to have a golden clasp;
1 Maccabees 11:59 and he appointed Simon his brother commander from the ladder of Tyre as far as the borders of Egypt.
1 Maccabees 11:60 And Ionathan went out and was traveling beyond the river and in the cities, and the entire force of Syria gathered to him for alliance; and he came to Askalon, and those from the city met him gloriously.
1 Maccabees 11:61 And he departed from there to Gaza, and those from Gaza shut it, and he encamped around it and burned its surrounding towns with fire and plundered them.
1 Maccabees 11:62 And those from Gaza entreated Ionathan, and he gave them his right hand and took the sons of their rulers as hostages and sent them away to Ierousalem; and he passed through the country as far as Damascus.
1 Maccabees 11:63 And Ionathan heard that the rulers of Demetrios were present at Kedes in Galilee with a great force, wishing to remove him from his office.
1 Maccabees 11:64 And he met them, but left Simon his brother in the country.
1 Maccabees 11:65 And Simon encamped against Baithsoura and fought against it for many days and shut it in.
1 Maccabees 11:66 And they entreated him to receive right hands, and he gave them to them; and he expelled them from there and seized the city and placed a garrison over it.
1 Maccabees 11:67 And Ionathan and his camp encamped by the water of Gennesar; and they rose early in the morning to the plain of Asor.
1 Maccabees 11:68 And behold, the camp of foreigners met him in the plain, and they sent out an ambush against him in the mountains, but they themselves met him opposite.
1 Maccabees 11:69 And the ambushes rose from their places and joined battle.
1 Maccabees 11:70 And all those with Ionathes fled; not even one of them was left except Mattathias, the son of Apsalomos, and Ioudas, the son of Chalphi, rulers of the army of the forces.
1 Maccabees 11:71 And Ionathan tore his garments and placed earth on his head and prayed.
1 Maccabees 11:72 And he turned back toward them in battle and routed them, and they fled.
1 Maccabees 11:73 And those fleeing from him saw and returned to him and pursued with him as far as Kedes, as far as their camp, and encamped there.
1 Maccabees 11:74 And about three thousand men of the foreigners fell on that day. And Ionathan returned to Ierousalem.

## Chapter 12

1 Maccabees 12:1 And Ionathan saw that the occasion was working with him, and he selected men and sent them to Rome to establish and renew the friendship with them.
1 Maccabees 12:2 And to the Spartans and other places he sent letters in the same way.
1 Maccabees 12:3 And they went to Rome and entered the council chamber and said, Ionathan the high priest and the nation of the Judeans sent us to renew for themselves the friendship and alliance as before.
1 Maccabees 12:4 And they gave them letters to those in each place, so that they might escort them to the land of Iouda with peace.
1 Maccabees 12:5 And this is the copy of the letters which Ionathan wrote to the Spartans:
1 Maccabees 12:6 Ionathan the high priest and the council of elders of the nation and the priests and the rest of the people of the Judeans to the Spartans, their brothers, greetings.
1 Maccabees 12:7 Even earlier letters were sent to Onias the high priest from Areios, who reigned among you, that you are our brothers, as the copy set out below shows.
1 Maccabees 12:8 And Onias received the man who had been sent gloriously and took the letters in which matters of alliance and friendship were made clear.
1 Maccabees 12:9 We therefore, being without need of these things, having as encouragement the holy books in our hands,
1 Maccabees 12:10 attempted to send to renew the brotherhood and friendship with you, so as not to become estranged from you; for many times have passed since you sent to us.
1 Maccabees 12:11 We therefore at every time, unceasingly, both at the feasts and on the other appropriate days, remember you at the sacrifices which we offer and in our prayers, as it is necessary and fitting to remember brothers.
1 Maccabees 12:12 And we rejoice at your glory.
