1 Maccabees 12:13 But many afflictions and many wars surrounded us, and the kings around us fought against us.
1 Maccabees 12:14 We therefore did not wish to trouble you and our other allies and friends in these wars;
1 Maccabees 12:15 for we have the help from heaven helping us, and we were delivered from the enemies, and our enemies were humbled.
1 Maccabees 12:16 We therefore selected Noumenios, son of Antiochos, and Antipatros, son of Iason, and have sent them to the Romans to renew the former friendship and alliance with them.
1 Maccabees 12:17 We therefore also instructed them to go to you and greet you and deliver to you the letters from us concerning the renewal and our brotherhood.
1 Maccabees 12:18 And now you will do well by answering us concerning these things.
1 Maccabees 12:19 And this is the copy of the letters which they sent to Onias:
1 Maccabees 12:20 Areios, king of the Spartans, to Onias the great priest, greetings.
1 Maccabees 12:21 It was found in writing concerning both the Spartans and the Judeans that they are brothers and that they are of the race of Abraam.
1 Maccabees 12:22 And now, since we have learned these things, you will do well by writing to us concerning your peace,
1 Maccabees 12:23 and we also write back to you: Your livestock and your possessions are ours, and ours are yours. We therefore give orders that they report to you according to these things.
1 Maccabees 12:24 And Ionathan heard that the rulers of Demetrios had returned with a great force, greater than before, to fight against him.
1 Maccabees 12:25 And he departed from Ierousalem and met them in the country of Amathitis; for he did not give them an opportunity to enter his country.
1 Maccabees 12:26 And he sent spies into their camp, and they returned and reported to him that they were thus arranging to fall upon them at night.
1 Maccabees 12:27 But when the sun set, Ionathan ordered those with him to stay awake and be at their weapons, preparing for battle throughout the whole night, and he sent out advance guards around the camp.
1 Maccabees 12:28 And the adversaries heard that Ionathan and those with him were prepared for battle, and they feared and cowered in their heart and kindled fires in their camp.
1 Maccabees 12:29 But Ionathan and those with him did not know until morning, for they saw the lights burning.
1 Maccabees 12:30 And Ionathan pursued after them and did not overtake them, for they had crossed the Eleutheros river.
1 Maccabees 12:31 And Ionathan turned aside against the Arabs called the Zabadeans and struck them and took their spoils.
1 Maccabees 12:32 And he set out and came to Damascus and passed through all the country.
1 Maccabees 12:33 And Simon went out and passed through as far as Askalon and the nearby strongholds and turned aside to Ioppe and seized it beforehand;
1 Maccabees 12:34 for he heard that they wished to hand the stronghold over to those with Demetrios; and he placed a garrison there to guard it.
1 Maccabees 12:35 And Ionathan returned and assembled the elders of the people and deliberated with them about building strongholds in Judea
1 Maccabees 12:36 and raising the walls of Ierousalem further and raising a great height between the citadel and the city to separate it from the city, so that it might be alone, so that they might neither buy nor sell.
1 Maccabees 12:37 And they gathered to build the city, and part of the wall of the torrent on the east fell, and he repaired what is called Chaphenatha.
1 Maccabees 12:38 And Simon built Adida in Sephela and fortified it and installed doors and bars.
1 Maccabees 12:39 And Tryphon sought to reign over Asia and put on the diadem and stretch out a hand against Antiochos the king.
1 Maccabees 12:40 And he was wary lest Ionathan should not permit him and lest he fight against him, and sought to seize him to destroy him, and departed and came to Baithsan.
1 Maccabees 12:41 And Ionathan went out to meet him with forty thousand men selected for battle and came to Baithsan.
1 Maccabees 12:42 And Tryphon saw that he had come with a great force, and was wary of stretching out hands against him.
1 Maccabees 12:43 And he received him gloriously and commended him to all his friends and gave him gifts and ordered his friends and his forces to obey him as himself.
1 Maccabees 12:44 And he said to Ionathan, Why have you wearied all this people when no war has arisen for us?
1 Maccabees 12:45 And now send them to their houses, but select for yourself a few men who will be with you, and come with me to Ptolemais, and I shall hand it over to you, and the remaining strongholds and the remaining forces and all those over the affairs, and I shall turn back and depart; for I am here for this purpose.
1 Maccabees 12:46 And he trusted him and did as he said, and sent away the forces, and they departed to the land of Iouda.
1 Maccabees 12:47 But he left with himself three thousand men, of whom he left two thousand in Galilee, but a thousand went with him.
1 Maccabees 12:48 But when Ionathan entered Ptolemais, the people of Ptolemais shut the gates and seized him, and all those who had entered together with him they killed with the sword.
1 Maccabees 12:49 And Tryphon sent forces and cavalry into Galilee and the great plain to destroy all those with Ionathes.
1 Maccabees 12:50 And they learned that he had been seized and had perished, and those with him, and they encouraged one another and were marching closely together, ready for battle.
1 Maccabees 12:51 And those pursuing saw that it was a matter of life for them, and turned back.
1 Maccabees 12:52 And they all came with peace to the land of Iouda and mourned Ionathan and those with him and were greatly afraid; and all Israel mourned with great mourning.
1 Maccabees 12:53 And all the nations around them sought to wipe them out; for they said, They have no ruler or helper; now therefore let us fight them and remove their memorial from among human beings.

## Chapter 13

1 Maccabees 13:1 And Simon heard that Tryphon had gathered a great force to come into the land of Iouda and wipe it out.
1 Maccabees 13:2 And he saw the people, that they were trembling and terrified, and went up to Ierousalem and gathered the people
1 Maccabees 13:3 and encouraged them and said to them, You yourselves know whatever I and my brothers and the house of my father have done for the laws and the holy places, and the wars and the straits which we have seen.
1 Maccabees 13:4 For this reason all my brothers perished for the sake of Israel, and I alone was left.
1 Maccabees 13:5 And now may it not happen to me to spare my life at any time of affliction; for I am not better than my brothers.
1 Maccabees 13:6 But I shall exact vengeance for my nation and for the holy places and for your wives and children, because all the nations have gathered to wipe us out because of enmity.
1 Maccabees 13:7 And the spirit of the people was rekindled as soon as they heard these words,
1 Maccabees 13:8 and they answered with a loud voice, saying, You are our leader in place of Ioudas and Ionathes your brother;
1 Maccabees 13:9 fight our war, and everything that you say to us we shall do.
1 Maccabees 13:10 And he gathered all the fighting men and hastened to finish the walls of Ierousalem and fortified it all around.
1 Maccabees 13:11 And he sent Ionathan, the son of Apsalomos, and with him a sufficient force to Ioppe, and he expelled those in it and remained there in it.
1 Maccabees 13:12 And Tryphon departed from Ptolemais with a great force to come into the land of Iouda, and Ionathan with him under guard.
1 Maccabees 13:13 But Simon encamped in Adida facing the plain.
1 Maccabees 13:14 And Tryphon learned that Simon had arisen in place of Ionathes his brother and that he was about to join battle with him, and sent ambassadors to him, saying,
1 Maccabees 13:15 On account of silver which Ionathan your brother owed to the royal treasury because of the offices he held, we are detaining him;
1 Maccabees 13:16 and now send a hundred talents of silver and two of his sons as hostages, so that when released he may not revolt from us, and we shall release him.
1 Maccabees 13:17 And Simon knew that they were speaking to him deceitfully, and he sends to collect the silver and the boys, lest he incur great enmity with the people,
1 Maccabees 13:18 saying, Because I did not send him the silver and the boys, he perished.
1 Maccabees 13:19 And he sent the boys and the hundred talents, and he proved false and did not release Ionathan.
1 Maccabees 13:20 And after these things Tryphon came to enter the country and wipe it out, and they went around by the road to Adora. And Simon and his camp marched opposite him to every place wherever he went.
1 Maccabees 13:21 But those from the citadel were sending ambassadors to Tryphon, urging him to come to them through the wilderness and send them food.
1 Maccabees 13:22 And Tryphon prepared all his cavalry to come, and on that night there was very much snow, and he did not come because of the snow. And he departed and came to Galaaditis.
1 Maccabees 13:23 But when he drew near Baskama, he killed Ionathan, and he was buried there.
1 Maccabees 13:24 And Tryphon turned back and departed to his own land.
1 Maccabees 13:25 And Simon sent and took the bones of Ionathes his brother and buried him in Modein, the city of his fathers.
1 Maccabees 13:26 And all Israel lamented him with a great lamentation and mourned him for many days.
1 Maccabees 13:27 And Simon built upon the tomb of his father and his brothers and raised it high to the sight with hewn stone at the back and the front.
1 Maccabees 13:28 And he erected seven pyramids, one opposite the other, for his father and his mother and his four brothers.
1 Maccabees 13:29 And for these he made constructions, setting great pillars around them, and on the pillars he made suits of armor for an everlasting name, and beside the suits of armor, carved ships to be seen by all those sailing the sea.
1 Maccabees 13:30 This is the tomb which he made in Modein, until this day.
1 Maccabees 13:31 But Tryphon dealt deceitfully with Antiochos the younger king and killed him
1 Maccabees 13:32 and reigned in his place and put on the diadem of Asia and inflicted a great blow upon the land.
1 Maccabees 13:33 And Simon built the strongholds of Judea and walled them around with high towers and great walls and gates and bars and placed food in the strongholds.
1 Maccabees 13:34 And Simon selected men and sent them to Demetrios the king to grant remission to the country, because all Tryphon's exactions were acts of plunder.
1 Maccabees 13:35 And Demetrios the king sent to him according to these words and answered him and wrote him such a letter:
1 Maccabees 13:36 King Demetrios to Simon, high priest and friend of kings, and to the elders and the nation of the Judeans, greetings.
1 Maccabees 13:37 We have received the golden crown and the palm branch which you sent and are ready to make great peace with you and write to those over the affairs to grant you the remissions.
1 Maccabees 13:38 And whatever we established with you stands, and let the strongholds which you built belong to you.
1 Maccabees 13:39 And we forgive errors of ignorance and the sins until today and the crown which you owed, and if anything else was taxed in Ierousalem, let it no longer be taxed.
1 Maccabees 13:40 And if any of you are fit to be enrolled among those around us, let them be enrolled, and let there be peace between us.
1 Maccabees 13:41 In the one hundred and seventieth year the yoke of the nations was lifted from Israel,
1 Maccabees 13:42 and the people began to write in the contracts and transactions: In the first year under Simon, great high priest and commander and leader of the Judeans.
1 Maccabees 13:43 In those days he encamped against Gazara and surrounded it with camps and made a siege tower and brought it up to the city and struck one tower and seized it.
1 Maccabees 13:44 And those in the siege tower leaped out into the city, and a great disturbance arose in the city.
1 Maccabees 13:45 And those in the city went up with wives and children onto the wall, having torn their garments, and cried out with a loud voice, requesting Simon to give them right hands,
1 Maccabees 13:46 and said, Do not deal with us according to our wickednesses, but according to your mercy.
1 Maccabees 13:47 And Simon relented toward them and did not fight them; and he expelled them from the city and cleansed the houses in which the idols were, and thus entered it, singing hymns and blessing.
1 Maccabees 13:48 And he expelled all uncleanness from it and settled in it men who would do the law and fortified it further and built himself a dwelling in it.
1 Maccabees 13:49 But those from the citadel in Ierousalem were prevented from going out and going into the country to buy and sell and became very hungry, and many of them perished by famine.
1 Maccabees 13:50 And they cried out to Simon to receive right hands, and he gave them to them; and he expelled them from there and cleansed the citadel from its defilements.
1 Maccabees 13:51 And they entered it on the twenty-third of the second month of the one hundred and seventy-first year, with praise and palm branches and with lyres and with cymbals and with harps and with hymns and with songs, because a great enemy had been crushed out of Israel.
1 Maccabees 13:52 And he established that this day should be observed yearly with gladness. And he further fortified the mountain of the temple beside the citadel; and he and those with him dwelt there.
1 Maccabees 13:53 And Simon saw Ioannes his son, that he was a man, and appointed him leader of all the forces; and he dwelt in Gazara.

## Chapter 14

1 Maccabees 14:1 And in the one hundred and seventy-second year Demetrios the king gathered his forces and went to Media to draw help to himself, so that he might fight Tryphon.
1 Maccabees 14:2 And Arsakes, the king of Persia and Media, heard that Demetrios had entered his borders, and sent one of his rulers to seize him alive.
1 Maccabees 14:3 And he went and struck the camp of Demetrios and seized him and brought him to Arsakes, and he placed him under guard.
1 Maccabees 14:4 And the land of Iouda was quiet all the days of Simon, and he sought good things for his nation, and his authority and his glory pleased them all the days.
1 Maccabees 14:5 And with all his glory he took Ioppe as a harbor and made an entrance to the islands of the sea.
1 Maccabees 14:6 And he widened the borders for his nation and held possession of the country.
1 Maccabees 14:7 And he gathered many captives and became master of Gazara and Baithsoura and the citadel; and he removed the uncleannesses from it, and there was none opposing him.
1 Maccabees 14:8 And they were cultivating their land with peace, and the land gave its produce and the trees of the plains their fruit.
1 Maccabees 14:9 Elders sat in the broad streets; all were conversing about good things, and the young men put on glorious garments and robes of war.
1 Maccabees 14:10 He supplied food to the cities and furnished them with equipment for fortification, until the name of his glory was named as far as the end of the earth.
1 Maccabees 14:11 He made peace upon the land, and Israel rejoiced with great gladness.
1 Maccabees 14:12 And each sat under his vine and his fig tree, and there was none terrifying them.
1 Maccabees 14:13 And one fighting them ceased from the land, and the kings were crushed in those days.
1 Maccabees 14:14 And he strengthened all the lowly of his people; he sought out the law and removed every lawless and wicked person;
1 Maccabees 14:15 he glorified the holy places and multiplied the vessels of the holy places.
1 Maccabees 14:16 And it was heard in Rome that Ionathan had died, and as far as Sparta, and they were greatly grieved.
1 Maccabees 14:17 But when they heard that Simon his brother had become high priest in his place and that he held possession of the country and the cities in it,
1 Maccabees 14:18 they wrote to him on bronze tablets to renew with him the friendship and alliance which they had established with Ioudas and Ionathan his brothers.
1 Maccabees 14:19 And they were read before the assembly in Ierousalem.
1 Maccabees 14:20 And this is the copy of the letters which the Spartans sent: The rulers of the Spartans and the city to Simon the great priest and the elders and the priests and the rest of the people of the Judeans, their brothers, greetings.
1 Maccabees 14:21 The ambassadors sent to our people reported to us concerning your glory and honor, and we rejoiced at their arrival.
1 Maccabees 14:22 And we recorded what was said by them in the deliberations of the people thus: Noumenios, son of Antiochos, and Antipatros, son of Iason, ambassadors of the Judeans, came to us renewing the friendship with us.
1 Maccabees 14:23 And it pleased the people to receive the men gloriously and to place the copy of their words in the books designated for the people, so that the people of the Spartans might have a memorial. And they wrote the copy of these things to Simon the high priest.
1 Maccabees 14:24 After these things Simon sent Noumenios to Rome, having a great golden shield weighing a thousand minas, to establish the alliance with them.
1 Maccabees 14:25 But when the people heard these matters, they said, What thanks shall we repay Simon and his sons?
1 Maccabees 14:26 For he and his brothers and the house of his father gave strength and fought the enemies of Israel away from them and established freedom for it. And they recorded it on bronze tablets and placed it on pillars on Mount Sion.
1 Maccabees 14:27 And this is the copy of the writing: On the eighteenth of Eloul of the one hundred and seventy-second year — and this is the third year under Simon the great high priest in asaramel —
1 Maccabees 14:28 at a great gathering of priests and people and rulers of the nation and the elders of the country, he made it known to us;
1 Maccabees 14:29 since wars occurred often in the country, but Simon, son of Mattathias, a priest of the sons of Ioarib, and his brothers gave themselves to the danger and stood against the adversaries of their nation, so that their holy places and the law might stand, and with great glory they glorified their nation.
1 Maccabees 14:30 And Ionathan gathered their nation and became high priest for them and was added to his people,
1 Maccabees 14:31 and their enemies wished to enter their country and stretch out hands against their holy places;
1 Maccabees 14:32 then Simon stood against them and fought for his nation and expended much of his own money and supplied weapons to the men of the force of his nation and gave them pay
1 Maccabees 14:33 and fortified the cities of Judea and Baithsoura on the borders of Judea, where the weapons of the enemies had been previously, and placed a garrison there, Judean men.
1 Maccabees 14:34 And he fortified Ioppe by the sea and Gazara on the borders of Azotos, in which the enemies had previously dwelt, and settled Judeans there, and whatever was suitable for their restoration he placed in them.
1 Maccabees 14:35 And the people saw the faithfulness of Simon and the glory which he had resolved to bring to his nation, and appointed him their leader and high priest because he had done all these things, and the righteousness and the faithfulness which he maintained toward his nation, and he sought in every way to exalt his people.
1 Maccabees 14:36 And in his days it prospered in his hands for the nations to be removed from their country, and those in the city of Dauid in Ierousalem who had made themselves a citadel, from which they went out and defiled the surroundings of the holy places and inflicted a great blow upon purity.
1 Maccabees 14:37 And he settled Judean men in it and fortified it for the security of the country and the city and raised the walls of Ierousalem.
1 Maccabees 14:38 And King Demetrios confirmed the high priesthood for him according to these things
1 Maccabees 14:39 and made him one of his friends and glorified him with great glory.
1 Maccabees 14:40 For he heard that the Judeans had been called friends and allies and brothers by the Romans, and that they had met Simon's ambassadors gloriously,
1 Maccabees 14:41 and that the Judeans and the priests had consented that Simon should be their leader and high priest forever, until a faithful prophet should arise,
1 Maccabees 14:42 and that he should be commander over them, and that he should have care concerning the holy places, to appoint through himself those over their works and over the country and over the weapons and over the strongholds,
1 Maccabees 14:43 and that he should have care concerning the holy places, and that he should be obeyed by all, and that all contracts in the country should be written in his name, and that he should clothe himself in purple and wear gold;
1 Maccabees 14:44 and it shall not be permitted to anyone of the people and the priests to set aside any of these things or contradict what will be spoken by him or gather a gathering in the country without him or clothe himself in purple or fasten on a golden clasp;
1 Maccabees 14:45 but whoever acts contrary to these things or sets aside any of these things shall be liable.
1 Maccabees 14:46 And all the people consented to establish for Simon that he should act according to these words.
1 Maccabees 14:47 And Simon accepted and consented to serve as high priest and to be commander and ruler of the nation of the Judeans and priests and to preside over all.
1 Maccabees 14:48 And they said to place this writing on bronze tablets and erect them in the enclosure of the holy places in a conspicuous place,
1 Maccabees 14:49 but to place their copies in the treasury, so that Simon and his sons might have them.

## Chapter 15

1 Maccabees 15:1 And Antiochos, son of Demetrios the king, sent letters from the islands of the sea to Simon, priest and ruler of the nation of the Judeans, and to the whole nation,
1 Maccabees 15:2 and they contained this form: King Antiochos to Simon the great priest and ruler of the nation and to the nation of the Judeans, greetings.
1 Maccabees 15:3 Since some pestilent men have gained possession of the kingdom of our fathers, but I wish to claim the kingdom, so that I may restore it as it was previously, and I have recruited a multitude of forces and prepared warships,
1 Maccabees 15:4 and I wish to land in the country, so that I may pursue those who have destroyed our country and those who have desolated many cities in my kingdom,
1 Maccabees 15:5 now therefore I confirm for you all the remissions which the kings before me granted you, and whatever other gifts they granted you.
1 Maccabees 15:6 And I have permitted you to make your own coinage, currency for your country,
1 Maccabees 15:7 and for Ierousalem and the holy places to be free; and all the weapons, as many as you prepared, and the strongholds which you built, which you possess, let them remain yours.
1 Maccabees 15:8 And every royal debt and the future royal dues, from now and for all time, let them be remitted to you;
1 Maccabees 15:9 but when we take hold of our kingdom, we shall glorify you and your nation and the temple with great glory, so that your glory may become manifest in all the earth.
1 Maccabees 15:10 In the one hundred and seventy-fourth year Antiochos went out into the land of his fathers, and all the forces came together to him, so that few were with Tryphon.
1 Maccabees 15:11 And Antiochos pursued him, and he came fleeing to Dora, which is by the sea;
1 Maccabees 15:12 for he knew that evils had gathered against him, and the forces had abandoned him.
1 Maccabees 15:13 And Antiochos encamped against Dora, and with him were one hundred and twenty thousand fighting men and eight thousand cavalry.
1 Maccabees 15:14 And he surrounded the city, and the ships joined from the sea, and he pressed the city from the land and the sea and permitted no one to go out or enter.
1 Maccabees 15:15 And Noumenios and those with him came from Rome, having letters to the kings and the countries in which these things had been written:
1 Maccabees 15:16 Leukios, consul of the Romans, to King Ptolemaios, greetings.
1 Maccabees 15:17 The ambassadors of the Judeans came to us, our friends and allies, renewing the friendship and alliance from the beginning, sent from Simon the high priest and the people of the Judeans,
1 Maccabees 15:18 and they brought a golden shield of a thousand minas.
1 Maccabees 15:19 It therefore pleased us to write to the kings and the countries that they should not seek evils for them and should not fight them and their cities and their country, and that they should not act as allies of those fighting against them.
1 Maccabees 15:20 And we decided to receive the shield from them.
1 Maccabees 15:21 If therefore any pestilent men have escaped from their country to you, hand them over to Simon the high priest, so that he may punish them according to their law.
1 Maccabees 15:22 And he wrote the same things to Demetrios the king and Attalos and Ariarathes and Arsakes
1 Maccabees 15:23 and to all the countries, and Sampsame and the Spartans and to Delos and to Myndos and to Sikyon and to Caria and to Samos and to Pamphylia and to Lycia and to Halikarnassos and to Rhodes and to Phaselis and to Kos and to Side and to Arados and Gortyna and Knidos and Cyprus and Kyrene.
1 Maccabees 15:24 And they wrote the copy of these things to Simon the high priest.
1 Maccabees 15:25 But Antiochos the king encamped against Dora a second time, continually bringing his hands against it and making engines, and shut Tryphon in from going out and entering.
1 Maccabees 15:26 And Simon sent him two thousand chosen men to act as his allies, and silver and gold and sufficient equipment.
1 Maccabees 15:27 And he did not wish to receive them, but set aside everything that he had previously agreed with him, and was becoming estranged from him.
1 Maccabees 15:28 And he sent to him Athenobios, one of his friends, to confer with him, saying, You hold possession of Ioppe and Gazara and the citadel in Ierousalem, cities of my kingdom.
1 Maccabees 15:29 You have desolated their borders and inflicted a great blow upon the land and become masters of many places in my kingdom.
1 Maccabees 15:30 Now therefore hand over the cities which you seized and the tributes of the places of which you became masters outside the borders of Judea.
1 Maccabees 15:31 But if not, give in their place five hundred talents of silver, and for the destruction which you have wrought and the tributes of the cities another five hundred talents; but if not, we shall come and wage war against you.
1 Maccabees 15:32 And Athenobios, the friend of the king, came to Ierousalem and saw Simon's glory and a sideboard with golden and silver vessels and a substantial retinue, and was astonished and reported to him the words of the king.
1 Maccabees 15:33 And Simon answered and said to him, We have neither taken foreign land nor gained possession of things belonging to others, but of the inheritance of our fathers; but it was seized by our enemies without judgment at a certain time;
1 Maccabees 15:34 but we, having an opportunity, hold fast to the inheritance of our fathers.
1 Maccabees 15:35 But concerning Ioppe and Gazara, which you demand, these inflicted a great blow upon the people and our country; for these we shall give a hundred talents.
1 Maccabees 15:36 And he did not answer him a word, but returned with wrath to the king and reported to him these words and Simon's glory and everything that he had seen, and the king was angry with great anger.
1 Maccabees 15:37 But Tryphon boarded a ship and fled to Orthosia.
1 Maccabees 15:38 And the king appointed Kendebaios chief commander of the coast and gave him infantry and cavalry forces;
1 Maccabees 15:39 and he ordered him to encamp facing Judea and ordered him to build Kedron and fortify the gates and to fight the people; but the king was pursuing Tryphon.
1 Maccabees 15:40 And Kendebaios arrived at Iamneia and began to provoke the people and enter Judea and take the people captive and murder.
1 Maccabees 15:41 And he built Kedron and stationed horsemen and forces there, so that going out they might traverse the roads of Judea, as the king had ordered him.

## Chapter 16

1 Maccabees 16:1 And Ioannes went up from Gazara and reported to Simon his father what Kendebaios had carried out.
1 Maccabees 16:2 And Simon called his two elder sons, Ioudas and Ioannes, and said to them, I and my brothers and the house of my father have fought the wars of Israel from youth until today, and it prospered in our hands to deliver Israel many times;
1 Maccabees 16:3 but now I have grown old, and you, by mercy, are sufficient in years; take the place of me and my brother, and go out and fight on behalf of our nation, and may the help from heaven be with you.
1 Maccabees 16:4 And he selected from the country twenty thousand fighting men and horsemen, and they went against Kendebaios and slept in Modein.
1 Maccabees 16:5 And they arose in the morning and went into the plain, and behold, a great force to meet them, infantry and horsemen, and a torrent was between them.
1 Maccabees 16:6 And he encamped facing them, he and his people. And he saw the people afraid to cross the torrent and crossed first; and the men saw him and crossed behind him.
1 Maccabees 16:7 And he divided the people, and the horsemen in the midst of the infantry; but the cavalry of the adversaries was very numerous.
1 Maccabees 16:8 And they blew with the trumpets, and Kendebaios and his camp were routed, and many wounded fell from among them; but those left fled into the stronghold.
1 Maccabees 16:9 Then Ioudas, the brother of Ioannes, was wounded; but Ioannes pursued them until he came to Kedron, which he had built.
1 Maccabees 16:10 And they fled into the towers in the fields of Azotos, and he burned it with fire, and about two thousand men fell from among them. And he returned to Judea with peace.
1 Maccabees 16:11 And Ptolemaios, the son of Aboubos, had been appointed commander over the plain of Iericho and had much silver and gold;
1 Maccabees 16:12 for he was the son-in-law of the high priest.
1 Maccabees 16:13 And his heart was exalted, and he wished to gain possession of the country and was plotting deceitfully against Simon and his sons to remove them.
1 Maccabees 16:14 But Simon was visiting the cities in the country and attending to their care; and he went down to Iericho, he and Mattathias and Ioudas his sons, in the one hundred and seventy-seventh year, in the eleventh month [this is the month Sabat].
1 Maccabees 16:15 And the son of Aboubos received them deceitfully in the small stronghold called Dok, which he had built, and made them a great drinking feast and hid men there.
1 Maccabees 16:16 And when Simon and his sons became drunk, Ptolemaios and those with him rose and took their weapons and came in upon Simon at the banquet and killed him and his two sons and some of his servants.
1 Maccabees 16:17 And he committed great treachery and repaid evil things in place of good things.
1 Maccabees 16:18 And Ptolemaios wrote these things and sent them to the king, so that he might send him forces for help and hand over their country and the cities.
1 Maccabees 16:19 And he sent others to Gazara to remove Ioannes, and to the commanders of thousands he sent letters to come to him, so that he might give them silver and gold and gifts,
1 Maccabees 16:20 and he sent others to seize Ierousalem and the mountain of the temple.
1 Maccabees 16:21 And someone ran ahead and reported to Ioannes in Gazara that his father and his brothers had perished, and that he has sent to kill you also.
1 Maccabees 16:22 And on hearing it he was greatly astonished and seized the men who had come to destroy him and killed them; for he learned that they were seeking to destroy him.
1 Maccabees 16:23 And the remaining accounts of Ioannes and his wars and his deeds of courage which he courageously performed, and the building of the walls which he built, and his acts,
1 Maccabees 16:24 behold, these have been written in the book of the days of his high priesthood, from when he became high priest after his father.

# 2 Maccabees

The Apostolic Bible. Public domain. https://apostolic-bible.ysys9.chatgpt.site/license.html


## Chapter 1

2 Maccabees 1:1 To the brothers, the Judeans in Egypt, greetings: the brothers, the Judeans in Ierosolyma and those in the country of Judea, good peace;
2 Maccabees 1:2 and may God do good to you and remember his covenant with Abraam and Isaak and Iakob, his faithful servants;
2 Maccabees 1:3 and may he give you all a heart to revere him and do his wills with a great heart and a willing soul;
2 Maccabees 1:4 and may he open your heart in his law and in the ordinances and make peace
2 Maccabees 1:5 and hear your petitions and be reconciled to you and not abandon you at an evil time.
2 Maccabees 1:6 And now we are here praying for you.
2 Maccabees 1:7 While Demetrios was reigning, in the one hundred and sixty-ninth year, we the Judeans have written to you in the affliction and in the crisis that came upon us in these years, since Iason and those with him revolted from the holy land and the kingdom
2 Maccabees 1:8 and burned the gateway and poured out innocent blood; and we entreated the Lord and were heard and offered sacrifice and fine flour and lit the lamps and set out the loaves.
2 Maccabees 1:9 And now, that you may observe the days of tent-pitching of the month Chaseleu. In the one hundred and eighty-eighth year.
2 Maccabees 1:10 Those in Ierosolyma and those in Judea and the council of elders and Ioudas to Aristoboulos, teacher of Ptolemaios the king, who is of the race of the anointed priests, and to the Judeans in Egypt, greetings and good health.
2 Maccabees 1:11 Having been saved by God from great dangers, we thank him greatly, as being arrayed against a king;
2 Maccabees 1:12 for he himself cast out those arrayed in the holy city.
2 Maccabees 1:13 For the leader, having come to Persia, and the force around him that seemed irresistible were cut down in the temple of Nanaia, the priests of Nanaia having used deception.
2 Maccabees 1:14 For Antiochos and the friends with him arrived at the place as though to dwell with her, for the sake of receiving the greater funds on account of a dowry,
2 Maccabees 1:15 and when the priests of Nanaion had set them out and he had approached with a few into the enclosure of the sacred precinct, having shut the temple as Antiochos entered,
2 Maccabees 1:16 having opened the hidden door of the paneled ceiling, throwing stones they struck down the leader, and having cut them into limbs and removed their heads, they threw them to those outside.
2 Maccabees 1:17 In all things blessed is our God, who handed over those who acted impiously.
2 Maccabees 1:18 Being about to observe the purification of the temple on the twenty-fifth of Chaseleu, we considered it necessary to explain to you, so that you yourselves also may observe the feast of tent-pitching and of the fire, when Neemias, who built both the temple and the altar, offered sacrifices.
2 Maccabees 1:19 For also when our fathers were being led to Persia, the pious priests of that time took some of the fire of the altar and secretly hid it in the hollow of a well having a dry condition, in which they secured it so that the place was unknown to all.
2 Maccabees 1:20 But after many years had passed, when it pleased God, Neemias, sent by the king of Persia, sent the descendants of the priests who had hidden it to fetch the fire; but when they explained to us that they had not found fire but thick water, he ordered them to draw it and bring it.
2 Maccabees 1:21 And when the things for the sacrifices had been brought up, Neemias ordered the priests to sprinkle with the water both the wood and the things laid upon it.
2 Maccabees 1:22 And when this happened and time passed and the sun shone out, having previously been clouded, a great fire was kindled, so that all marveled.
2 Maccabees 1:23 And the priests made prayer while the sacrifice was being consumed, both the priests and all, Ionathes beginning, and the rest responding, as did Neemias;
2 Maccabees 1:24 and the prayer had this form: Lord, Lord God, creator of all, fearful and strong and just and merciful, the only king and kind,
2 Maccabees 1:25 the only provider, the only just and almighty and eternal one, who saves Israel from every evil, who made the fathers chosen and sanctified them,
2 Maccabees 1:26 accept the sacrifice on behalf of all your people Israel and preserve your portion and sanctify it.
2 Maccabees 1:27 Gather together our dispersion, free those enslaved among the nations, look upon those despised and abhorred, and let the nations know that you are our God.
2 Maccabees 1:28 Torment those who oppress and outrage in arrogance.
2 Maccabees 1:29 Plant your people in your holy place, as Moyses said.
2 Maccabees 1:30 And the priests sang the hymns in accompaniment.
2 Maccabees 1:31 And when the things of the sacrifice had been consumed, Neemias also ordered the remaining water to be poured upon larger stones.
2 Maccabees 1:32 And when this happened, a flame was kindled; but when the light from the altar shone back, it was consumed.
2 Maccabees 1:33 And when the matter became manifest, it was also reported to the king of the Persians that in the place where the deported priests had hidden the fire the water appeared, from which those with Neemias also purified the things of the sacrifice,
2 Maccabees 1:34 and the king fenced it around and made it sacred, having examined the matter.
2 Maccabees 1:35 And from those whom the king favored he received many valuable things and shared them.
2 Maccabees 1:36 And those with Neemias called this nephthar, which is interpreted as purification; but it is called nephthai by most.

## Chapter 2

2 Maccabees 2:1 And it is found in the records that Ieremias the prophet ordered those being deported to take some of the fire, as has been indicated,
2 Maccabees 2:2 and how the prophet instructed those being deported, having given them the law, that they should not forget the ordinances of the Lord, and that they should not be led astray in their minds on seeing golden and silver statues and the adornment around them;
2 Maccabees 2:3 and saying other such things, he exhorted that the law should not depart from their heart.
2 Maccabees 2:4 And it was in the writing how the prophet, a divine communication having come to him, ordered the tent and the ark to follow along; and how he went out to the mountain where Moyses had gone up and beheld the inheritance of God.
2 Maccabees 2:5 And Ieremias came and found a cavernous dwelling and brought the tent and the ark and the altar of incense in there and blocked the door.
2 Maccabees 2:6 And some of those following along approached to mark the way, and they could not find it.
2 Maccabees 2:7 But when Ieremias learned of it, he blamed them and said, The place shall also be unknown until God gathers a gathering of the people and becomes merciful;
2 Maccabees 2:8 and then the Lord shall show these things, and the glory of the Lord and the cloud shall be seen, as it was manifested in the time of Moyses, as Salomon also requested that the place should be greatly sanctified.
2 Maccabees 2:9 And it was also explained how, having wisdom, he offered a sacrifice of dedication and of the completion of the temple.
2 Maccabees 2:10 Just as Moyses also prayed to the Lord, and fire came down from heaven and consumed the things of the sacrifice, so Salomon also prayed, and the fire came down and consumed the whole burnt offerings.
2 Maccabees 2:11 And Moyses said, Because the offering concerning sin was not eaten, it was consumed.
2 Maccabees 2:12 In the same way Salomon also observed the eight days.
2 Maccabees 2:13 And in the records and in the memoirs concerning Neemias the same things were also related, and how, founding a library, he gathered the books concerning the kings and prophets and those of Dauid and letters of kings concerning votive offerings.
2 Maccabees 2:14 And in the same way Ioudas also gathered all the things scattered because of the war that had occurred for us, and they are with us;
2 Maccabees 2:15 if therefore you have need of them, send those who will carry them away for you.
2 Maccabees 2:16 Being about to observe the purification, therefore, we wrote to you; you will therefore do well by observing the days.
2 Maccabees 2:17 And God, who saved all his people and restored to all the inheritance and the kingship and the priesthood and the sanctification,
2 Maccabees 2:18 as he promised through the law; for we hope in God that he will quickly have mercy on us and gather us from what is under heaven into the holy place; for he delivered us from great evils and purified the place.
2 Maccabees 2:19 And the matters concerning Ioudas Makkabaios and his brothers and the purification of the very great temple and the dedication of the altar,
2 Maccabees 2:20 and further the wars against Antiochos the Illustrious and his son Eupator,
2 Maccabees 2:21 and the manifestations from heaven that occurred for those who zealously performed courageous deeds on behalf of Judaism, so that, being few, they plundered the whole country and pursued the barbarian multitudes,
2 Maccabees 2:22 and recovered the temple renowned throughout the whole inhabited world and freed the city and restored the laws that were about to be dissolved, the Lord having become merciful to them with all gentleness,
2 Maccabees 2:23 set forth by Iason of Kyrene in five books, we shall attempt to abridge in one composition.
2 Maccabees 2:24 For seeing the mass of the numbers and the existing difficulty for those wishing to enter into the narratives of the history because of the multitude of the material,
2 Maccabees 2:25 we took care for entertainment for those wishing to read, and for ease for those eager to take it up through memory, and for benefit for all those encountering it.
2 Maccabees 2:26 And for us who have accepted the hardship of the abridgment it is not easy, but the undertaking is one of sweat and sleeplessness,
2 Maccabees 2:27 just as it is not easy for one preparing a banquet and seeking the benefit of others; nevertheless, for the gratitude of the many we shall gladly bear the hardship,
2 Maccabees 2:28 leaving the exact examination of each matter to the author, but laboring to follow the outlines of the abridgment.
2 Maccabees 2:29 For just as the architect of a new house must take care of the whole foundation, but the one undertaking encaustic work and painting must examine the things suitable for adornment, so I think it is also with us.
2 Maccabees 2:30 To enter in and make a circuit of accounts and inquire minutely into particulars belongs to the originator of the history;
2 Maccabees 2:31 but to pursue conciseness of expression and decline the elaborate treatment of the subject must be allowed to the one making the recasting.
2 Maccabees 2:32 From here therefore let us begin the narrative, having added this much to what was said before; for it is foolish to multiply what is before the history but abridge the history.

## Chapter 3

2 Maccabees 3:1 While the holy city was inhabited with all peace and the laws were maintained most excellently because of both the piety and hatred of wickedness of Onias the high priest,
2 Maccabees 3:2 it happened that even the kings themselves honored the place and glorified the temple with the finest gifts,
2 Maccabees 3:3 so that even Seleukos, the king of Asia, supplied from his own revenues all the expenses falling due for the services of the sacrifices.
2 Maccabees 3:4 But a certain Simon of the tribe of Beniamin, appointed superintendent of the temple, quarreled with the high priest concerning the supervision of the market in the city;
2 Maccabees 3:5 and being unable to overcome Onias, he came to Apollonios, son of Tharseas, who at that time was commander of Coele Syria and Phoenicia,
2 Maccabees 3:6 and reported that the treasury in Ierosolyma was full of unspeakable wealth, so that the multitude of valuables was innumerable, and that they did not belong to the account of the sacrifices, but that it was possible for these things to fall under the king's authority.
2 Maccabees 3:7 And Apollonios met with the king and informed him concerning the funds reported to him; and he selected Heliodoros, who was over the affairs, and sent him, giving orders to carry away the aforementioned funds.
2 Maccabees 3:8 And immediately Heliodoros undertook the journey, ostensibly to visit the cities in Coele Syria and Phoenicia, but in reality to fulfill the king's intention.
2 Maccabees 3:9 And arriving in Ierosolyma and being kindly received by the high priest of the city, he related the report that had been made and explained why he was present; and he inquired whether these things were actually so.
2 Maccabees 3:10 And the high priest pointed out that they were deposits of both widows and orphans,
2 Maccabees 3:11 and some also of Hyrkanos, son of Tobias, a man placed in very great eminence — thus the impious Simon was misrepresenting it — and the whole was four hundred talents of silver and two hundred of gold;
2 Maccabees 3:12 and that it was entirely impossible that those who had trusted in the holiness of the place and in the dignity and inviolability of the temple honored throughout the whole world should be wronged.
2 Maccabees 3:13 But Heliodoros, because of the royal orders he held, said that these things must in every case be taken up into the royal treasury.
2 Maccabees 3:14 And having appointed a day, he entered to manage the inspection concerning these things; and there was no small anguish throughout the whole city.
2 Maccabees 3:15 And the priests, having cast themselves before the altar in their priestly robes, called toward heaven upon the one who had legislated concerning a deposit, to preserve these things safe for those who had deposited them.
2 Maccabees 3:16 And to see the appearance of the high priest was to be wounded in mind; for his face and the alteration of his complexion manifested the anguish of his soul;
2 Maccabees 3:17 for a certain dread and trembling of body had poured around the man, through which the pain present in his heart became evident to those beholding him.
2 Maccabees 3:18 And further they sprang out of the houses in crowds for a supplication of all the people, because the place was about to come into contempt.
2 Maccabees 3:19 And the women, girded with sackcloth beneath their breasts, filled the roads; and of the secluded virgins, some ran together to the gateways, others to the walls, and some leaned out through the windows;
2 Maccabees 3:20 and all, stretching their hands toward heaven, made their entreaty;
2 Maccabees 3:21 and the mingled prostration of the multitude and the expectation of the greatly anguished high priest were to be pitied.
2 Maccabees 3:22 They therefore called upon the all-powerful Lord to preserve the entrusted things safe for those who had entrusted them, with all security.
2 Maccabees 3:23 But Heliodoros carried out what had been decided.
2 Maccabees 3:24 And when he was already present there with the bodyguards at the treasury, the ruler of the spirits and of all authority made a great manifestation, so that all those who had dared to come together, struck by the power of God, turned to faintness and cowardice;
2 Maccabees 3:25 for a certain horse appeared to them, having a fearful rider and adorned with most beautiful harness, and rushing forcefully it struck at Heliodoros with its front hoofs; and the one seated upon it appeared to have golden armor.
2 Maccabees 3:26 And two other young men appeared to him, outstanding in strength and most beautiful in glory and splendid in dress, who also stood around him on either side and scourged him unceasingly, casting many blows upon him.
2 Maccabees 3:27 And when he suddenly fell to the ground and was enveloped in great darkness, they seized him and placed him on a litter,
2 Maccabees 3:28 and carried the one who had just entered the aforementioned treasury with a great retinue and all his bodyguard, now helpless to himself, having manifestly recognized the power of God.
2 Maccabees 3:29 And he lay cast down because of the divine working, speechless and deprived of all hope and salvation,
2 Maccabees 3:30 but they blessed the Lord who wondrously glorified his own place, and the temple, which a little before had been full of dread and disturbance, was filled with joy and gladness when the almighty Lord appeared.
2 Maccabees 3:31 And quickly some of Heliodoros' associates requested Onias to call upon the Most High and grant life to the one lying utterly at his last breath.
2 Maccabees 3:32 And the high priest, becoming apprehensive lest the king should form an opinion that some wrongdoing concerning Heliodoros had been carried out by the Judeans, offered a sacrifice for the man's salvation.
2 Maccabees 3:33 And while the high priest made the atonement, the same young men appeared again to Heliodoros, clothed in the same garments, and stood and said, Have much gratitude to Onias the high priest, for because of him the Lord has granted you life;
2 Maccabees 3:34 but you, having been scourged from heaven, proclaim to all the magnificent might of God. And having said these things, they became invisible.
2 Maccabees 3:35 And Heliodoros offered a sacrifice to the Lord and vowed very great vows to the one who had preserved his life, and greeted Onias and broke camp to go to the king.
2 Maccabees 3:36 And he testified to all the works of the greatest God which he had beheld with his eyes.
2 Maccabees 3:37 And when the king asked Heliodoros what sort of man would be suitable to be sent once again to Ierosolyma, he said,
2 Maccabees 3:38 If you have any enemy or plotter against your affairs, send him there, and you will receive him scourged, if indeed he is even saved, because some power of God is truly about the place;
2 Maccabees 3:39 for the one who himself has his dwelling in heaven is overseer and helper of that place, and strikes and destroys those arriving to do harm.
2 Maccabees 3:40 And the matters concerning Heliodoros and the preservation of the treasury proceeded thus.

## Chapter 4

2 Maccabees 4:1 But the aforementioned Simon, who had become informer concerning the funds and the fatherland, spoke evil of Onias, as though he himself had shaken Heliodoros and had become the maker of the evils,
2 Maccabees 4:2 and he dared to call the benefactor of the city and guardian of his fellow nationals and zealot for the laws a plotter against the affairs.
2 Maccabees 4:3 And when the enmity advanced so far that even murders were being carried out through one of those approved by Simon,
2 Maccabees 4:4 Onias, seeing the severity of the rivalry and Apollonios, son of Menestheus, the commander of Coele Syria and Phoenicia, increasing Simon's wickedness,
2 Maccabees 4:5 went to the king, becoming no accuser of the citizens, but looking to the advantage, common and individual, of the whole multitude;
2 Maccabees 4:6 for he saw that without royal care it was impossible for affairs still to obtain peace and that Simon would take no pause from his folly.
2 Maccabees 4:7 But when Seleukos departed this life and Antiochos, called the Illustrious, received the kingdom, Iason, the brother of Onias, fraudulently supplanted him in the high priesthood,
2 Maccabees 4:8 promising the king in an interview three hundred and sixty talents of silver and eighty talents from some other revenue.
2 Maccabees 4:9 And besides these he promised to pay another hundred and fifty, if through his authority he were permitted to establish a gymnasium and an institution for youths and register those in Ierosolyma as Antiochenes.
2 Maccabees 4:10 And when the king consented and he took hold of the office, he immediately shifted his fellow tribesmen to the Greek character.
2 Maccabees 4:11 And setting aside the benevolent royal concessions established for the Judeans through Ioannes, the father of Eupolemos, who had made the embassy for friendship and alliance with the Romans, and dissolving the lawful civic institutions, he introduced unlawful customs.
2 Maccabees 4:12 For he gladly established a gymnasium beneath the citadel itself, and subjecting the best of the youths, brought them under the broad-brimmed hat.
2 Maccabees 4:13 And there was thus a certain height of Hellenism and an advance of foreign ways because of the surpassing impurity of the impious Iason, who was no high priest,
2 Maccabees 4:14 so that the priests were no longer eager for the services of the altar, but despising the temple and neglecting the sacrifices, they hurried to participate in the unlawful provision in the wrestling ground after the summons of the discus,
2 Maccabees 4:15 and setting the ancestral honors at nothing, but considering the Greek glories most beautiful.
2 Maccabees 4:16 Because of these things a severe predicament also encompassed them, and those whose ways they envied and to whom they wished to be entirely assimilated, these they had as enemies and punishers;
2 Maccabees 4:17 for to act impiously toward the divine laws is no light thing, but the following time will show these things.
2 Maccabees 4:18 And when the five-year games were being held in Tyre and the king was present,
2 Maccabees 4:19 the polluted Iason sent sacred envoys, being Antiochenes from Ierosolyma, carrying three hundred drachmas of silver for the sacrifice of Herakles, which those carrying them also requested not to use for sacrifice, because it was not fitting, but to put toward another expense.
2 Maccabees 4:20 These things therefore were assigned by the sender to the sacrifice of Herakles, but because of those carrying them to the construction of the triremes.
2 Maccabees 4:21 And when Apollonios, son of Menestheus, had been sent into Egypt for the first enthronement ceremonies of King Philometor, Antiochos learned that he had become estranged from his affairs and took care for his own security; therefore, arriving at Ioppe, he came to Ierosolyma.
2 Maccabees 4:22 And being magnificently received by Iason and the city, he was welcomed with torch-bearing and shouts; then thus he marched to camp in Phoenicia.
2 Maccabees 4:23 And after a period of three years Iason sent Menelaos, brother of the previously mentioned Simon, carrying the funds to the king and to complete reports concerning necessary affairs.
2 Maccabees 4:24 And he, being introduced to the king and glorifying him with the appearance of authority, brought the high priesthood to himself, exceeding Iason by three hundred talents of silver.
2 Maccabees 4:25 And having received the royal orders, he arrived, bringing nothing worthy of the high priesthood, but having the passions of a cruel tyrant and the rages of a barbarous beast.
2 Maccabees 4:26 And Iason, who had fraudulently supplanted his own brother, being fraudulently supplanted by another, was driven as a fugitive into the Ammanite country.
2 Maccabees 4:27 But Menelaos held the office, yet was not keeping anything in order concerning the funds promised to the king;
2 Maccabees 4:28 and Sostratos, the governor of the citadel, was demanding payment, for the collection of the funds belonged to him; for this reason the two were summoned by the king,
2 Maccabees 4:29 and Menelaos left Lysimachos his own brother as successor in the high priesthood, but Sostratos left Krates, who was over the Cyprians.
2 Maccabees 4:30 And while such things were taking place, it happened that the people of Tarsos and Mallos were revolting because they had been given as a gift to Antiochis, the king's concubine.
2 Maccabees 4:31 The king therefore came quickly to settle the affairs, leaving Andronikos, one of those in high rank, as his deputy.
2 Maccabees 4:32 But Menelaos, thinking he had obtained a favorable opportunity, stole some of the golden vessels of the temple and presented them to Andronikos, and had sold others both to Tyre and to the surrounding cities.
2 Maccabees 4:33 And Onias, having learned these things clearly, exposed them, having withdrawn into a place of asylum at Daphne, situated near Antiocheia.
2 Maccabees 4:34 Therefore Menelaos took Andronikos privately and exhorted him to subdue Onias; and he came to Onias, having been persuaded to deceit, and greeted him, giving his right hand with oaths, and although under suspicion, persuaded him to come out of the asylum, and immediately shut him out of life, without reverence for justice.
2 Maccabees 4:35 For this reason not only Judeans but also many of the other nations were indignant and distressed at the unjust murder of the man.
2 Maccabees 4:36 And when the king returned from the places in Cilicia, the Judeans in the city petitioned concerning the unreasonable killing of Onias, the Greeks also sharing their hatred of the wickedness.
2 Maccabees 4:37 Antiochos therefore was grieved in soul and turned to mercy and wept because of the moderation and great good order of the departed,
2 Maccabees 4:38 and inflamed with anger, immediately removed Andronikos' purple and tore his tunics and led him around through the whole city to the very place where he had acted impiously against Onias; there he removed the bloodstained man from life, the Lord having repaid him the fitting punishment.
2 Maccabees 4:39 And when many temple robberies had been committed in the city by Lysimachos with Menelaos' consent, and the report had spread abroad, the multitude gathered against Lysimachos, many golden vessels having already been carried away.
2 Maccabees 4:40 And when the crowds were rising and filling with anger, Lysimachos armed about three thousand and began unjust violence, a certain Auranos leading, advanced in age but no less also in folly;
2 Maccabees 4:41 and seeing Lysimachos' attack, some seized stones, others thick pieces of wood, and some grasped handfuls of the ashes lying nearby, and hurled them indiscriminately at those with Lysimachos;
2 Maccabees 4:42 for this reason they made many of them wounded and also struck some down and drove all into flight, but the temple robber himself they subdued beside the treasury.
2 Maccabees 4:43 And concerning these things a trial arose against Menelaos.
2 Maccabees 4:44 And when the king arrived in Tyre, the three men sent by the council of elders made their plea before him.
2 Maccabees 4:45 But Menelaos, already defeated, promised sufficient money to Ptolemaios, son of Dorymenes, to persuade the king.
2 Maccabees 4:46 Therefore Ptolemaios took the king aside into a certain colonnade as though to refresh him, and changed his mind,
2 Maccabees 4:47 and he released Menelaos, the cause of the whole wickedness, from the accusations, but upon the wretched men, who, even if they had pleaded before Scythians, would have been released uncondemned, upon these he pronounced death.
2 Maccabees 4:48 Quickly therefore those who had spoken for the city and peoples and the sacred vessels underwent the unjust penalty.
2 Maccabees 4:49 For this reason even the Tyrians, hating the wickedness, magnificently supplied the things for their burial.
2 Maccabees 4:50 But Menelaos, because of the greed of those in power, remained in office, growing in wickedness, having become a great plotter against the citizens.

## Chapter 5

2 Maccabees 5:1 And about this time Antiochos undertook the second expedition into Egypt.
2 Maccabees 5:2 And it happened throughout the whole city for almost forty days that horsemen appeared running through the air, having robes interwoven with gold and armed with lances in companies, and drawings of swords,
2 Maccabees 5:3 and squadrons of horses arrayed and assaults taking place and charges of both sides and movements of shields and multitudes of spears and discharges of missiles and flashes of golden adornments and armor of every kind.
2 Maccabees 5:4 Therefore all requested that the manifestation should have occurred for good.
2 Maccabees 5:5 And when a false rumor arose that Antiochos had departed this life, Iason took no fewer than a thousand and suddenly carried out an attack upon the city; and when those upon the wall were driven together and the city was finally already being seized, Menelaos fled into the citadel.
2 Maccabees 5:6 And Iason slaughtered his own citizens unsparingly, not considering that success against his kinsmen was the greatest misfortune, but thinking he was erecting trophies over enemies and not fellow nationals.
2 Maccabees 5:7 He did not take hold of the office, but receiving shame as the end of his plot, departed again as a fugitive into Ammanitis.
2 Maccabees 5:8 Finally therefore he met an evil end. Accused before Aretas, the ruler of the Arabs, fleeing from city to city, pursued by all, hated as an apostate from the laws and abhorred as executioner of his fatherland and citizens, he was cast out into Egypt,
2 Maccabees 5:9 and he who had alienated many from their fatherland perished in a foreign land, having sailed to the Lakedaimonians as though to obtain shelter because of their kinship.
2 Maccabees 5:10 And he who had cast out a multitude unburied became unmourned and shared in no burial whatsoever or ancestral tomb.
2 Maccabees 5:11 And when reports concerning what had happened reached the king, he supposed that Judea was revolting; therefore, setting out from Egypt, made beastlike in soul, he took the city by the spear
2 Maccabees 5:12 and ordered the soldiers to cut down unsparingly those they encountered and slaughter those going up into the houses.
2 Maccabees 5:13 And there was killing of young and elderly, destruction of the immature and women and children, slaughter of virgins and infants.
2 Maccabees 5:14 And eighty thousand were destroyed in the whole three days, forty thousand in attacks of hands, and no fewer than those slaughtered were sold.
2 Maccabees 5:15 And not satisfied with these things, he dared to enter the holiest temple of all the earth, having as guide Menelaos, who had become betrayer of both the laws and the fatherland,
2 Maccabees 5:16 and taking the sacred vessels with his polluted hands and dragging together with his profane hands the things dedicated by other kings for the increase and glory and honor of the place.
2 Maccabees 5:17 And Antiochos was exalted in mind, not seeing that because of the sins of those dwelling in the city the Master had been briefly angered, therefore neglect had occurred concerning the place.
2 Maccabees 5:18 But if it had not happened to be involved in many sins, as was Heliodoros, sent by Seleukos the king for the inspection of the treasury, this man, advancing, would immediately have been scourged and overturned from his audacity.
2 Maccabees 5:19 But the Lord did not choose the nation because of the place, but the place because of the nation.
2 Maccabees 5:20 Therefore the place itself also, having shared in the nation's misfortunes, partook in benefits that occurred afterward, and what had been abandoned in the anger of the Almighty was again restored with all glory in the reconciliation of the great Master.
2 Maccabees 5:21 Antiochos therefore, having carried away eighteen hundred talents from the temple, departed quickly into Antiocheia, supposing in his arrogance that he could make the land navigable and the open sea walkable because of the exaltation of his heart.
2 Maccabees 5:22 And he also left overseers to afflict the race: in Ierosolyma, Philip, a Phrygian by race, but having a character more barbarous than the one who appointed him,
2 Maccabees 5:23 and in Garizin, Andronikos, and besides these Menelaos, who exalted himself against the citizens worst of the others, and having a hateful disposition toward the Judean citizens.
2 Maccabees 5:24 And he sent Apollonios, the commander of the Mysians, with an army of twenty-two thousand, ordering him to slaughter all those of full age, but sell the women and the younger ones.
2 Maccabees 5:25 And he arrived in Ierosolyma and pretended to be peaceful, and waited until the holy day of the sabbath, and finding the Judeans inactive, ordered those under him to parade under arms
2 Maccabees 5:26 and stabbed all those who had come out to view it, and rushing into the city with the weapons, laid low considerable multitudes.
2 Maccabees 5:27 But Ioudas, also called Makkabaios, being one of about ten and withdrawing into the wilderness, lived in the mountains in the manner of beasts with those with him, and they continued eating vegetation as food, so as not to partake of the pollution.

## Chapter 6

2 Maccabees 6:1 And after no long time the king sent out an elderly Athenian to compel the Judeans to depart from the ancestral laws and not conduct their life by the laws of God,
2 Maccabees 6:2 and also to pollute the temple in Ierosolyma and name it after Olympian Zeus, and the one in Garizin, as those dwelling in the place happened to be, after Zeus of Strangers.
2 Maccabees 6:3 And the intensification of the wickedness was severe and altogether grievous.
2 Maccabees 6:4 For the temple was filled with debauchery and revels by the nations, who dallied with courtesans and had intercourse with women in the sacred enclosures, and further brought inside things that were not fitting.
2 Maccabees 6:5 And the altar was filled with unlawful things forbidden by the laws.
2 Maccabees 6:6 And it was not possible to keep the sabbath or preserve ancestral feasts or simply confess oneself to be a Judean,
2 Maccabees 6:7 and they were led with bitter compulsion to eat sacrificial entrails on the monthly birthday of the king, and when the feast of Dionysia occurred, they were compelled to carry ivy and march in procession for Dionysos.
2 Maccabees 6:8 And a decree went out to the neighboring Greek cities, Ptolemaios having proposed that they conduct the same treatment against the Judeans and make them eat sacrificial entrails,
2 Maccabees 6:9 but slaughter those not choosing to change over to Greek ways. It was therefore possible to see the present misery.
2 Maccabees 6:10 For two women were brought up who had circumcised their children; and having hung the infants from their breasts and publicly led the women around the city, they hurled them down from the wall.
2 Maccabees 6:11 And others who had run together into the nearby caves secretly to observe the seventh day were reported to Philip and burned together, because they scrupled to help themselves in view of the dignity of the most solemn day.
2 Maccabees 6:12 I therefore exhort those encountering this book not to shrink back because of the calamities, but to consider the punishments to be for the discipline of our race, not for destruction;
2 Maccabees 6:13 for indeed, that those acting impiously are not permitted a long time, but immediately fall into penalties, is a sign of great beneficence.
2 Maccabees 6:14 For the Master did not judge that it should also be with us as with the other nations, for whom he waits patiently until they reach the fullness of sins, to punish them,
2 Maccabees 6:15 so that he may not afterward punish us when we have reached the completion of our sins.
2 Maccabees 6:16 Therefore he never withdraws mercy from us, but while disciplining through calamity, does not abandon his own people.
2 Maccabees 6:17 But let these things have been said by us as a reminder; and through a few words we must come to the narrative.
2 Maccabees 6:18 A certain Eleazar, one of the foremost scribes, a man already advanced in age and most beautiful in facial appearance, was compelled, with mouth gaping, to eat pork.
2 Maccabees 6:19 But he, embracing death with good fame rather than life with pollution, voluntarily advanced to the torture rack,
2 Maccabees 6:20 but having spat it out, in the way in which those who endure must approach, resisting the tasting of things not lawful because of affection for life.
2 Maccabees 6:21 And those appointed over the unlawful eating of sacrificial entrails, because of their acquaintance with the man from earlier times, took him aside privately and exhorted him to bring meat which it was fitting for him to use, prepared by himself, but to pretend to be eating the meat from the sacrifice ordered by the king,
2 Maccabees 6:22 so that by doing this he might be released from death and because of his old friendship with them obtain humane treatment.
2 Maccabees 6:23 But he took up a noble resolve worthy of his age and the eminence of his old age and the acquired and conspicuous gray hair and his most excellent conduct from childhood, but rather of the holy and God-established legislation, and accordingly declared quickly, saying to send him onward to Hades.
2 Maccabees 6:24 For it is not worthy of our age to pretend, so that many of the young, supposing that the ninety-year-old Eleazar has changed over to foreign ways,
2 Maccabees 6:25 may themselves also be led astray because of me through my pretense and for the sake of a little and momentary life, and I acquire pollution and a stain upon my old age.
2 Maccabees 6:26 For even if for the present I escape the punishment from human beings, yet neither living nor dead shall I escape the hands of the Almighty.
2 Maccabees 6:27 Therefore, courageously departing this life now, I shall appear worthy of my old age,
2 Maccabees 6:28 and having left the young a noble example to die eagerly and nobly for the solemn and holy laws. And having said so much, he immediately came to the torture rack.
2 Maccabees 6:29 And those leading him changed their goodwill toward him of a little before into ill will, because the aforementioned words, as they supposed, were madness,
2 Maccabees 6:30 and being about to die from the blows, he groaned and said, It is manifest to the Lord who has holy knowledge that, though able to be released from death, I endure severe pains in body while being scourged, but in soul I gladly suffer these things because of fear of him.
2 Maccabees 6:31 And he therefore departed in this way, having left his own death as an example of nobility and a memorial of virtue, not only to the young but also to most of the nation.

## Chapter 7

2 Maccabees 7:1 And it also happened that seven brothers with their mother were seized and compelled by the king to partake of unlawful pork, being tortured with whips and sinews.
2 Maccabees 7:2 And one of them became spokesman and said thus, What are you going to ask and learn from us? For we are ready to die rather than transgress the ancestral laws.
2 Maccabees 7:3 And the king became furious and ordered pans and cauldrons to be heated.
2 Maccabees 7:4 And when they were immediately heated, he ordered the tongue of the one who had become their spokesman to be cut out and, after scalping him, to cut off his extremities, the remaining brothers and the mother looking on.
2 Maccabees 7:5 And when he had become entirely helpless, he ordered him to be brought to the fire while breathing and fried in the pan. And as the vapor from the pan spread far, they with their mother exhorted one another to die nobly, saying thus,
2 Maccabees 7:6 The Lord God watches and truly has compassion upon us, as Moyses explained through the song that testifies against them to their face, saying, And he shall have compassion upon his servants.
2 Maccabees 7:7 And when the first departed in this way, they led the second to the mockery, and having torn off the skin of his head with the hair, asked, Will you eat before your body is punished limb by limb?
2 Maccabees 7:8 But he answered in the ancestral tongue and said, No. Therefore this one also received the torture in turn, as the first.
2 Maccabees 7:9 And coming to his last breath, he said, You, accursed one, release us from the present life, but the king of the world will raise us, who die for his laws, to an eternal revival of life.
2 Maccabees 7:10 And after him the third was mocked, and when asked for his tongue, quickly put it forward and confidently stretched out his hands
2 Maccabees 7:11 and nobly said, From heaven I possess these, and because of his laws I disregard these, and from him I hope to receive these again;
2 Maccabees 7:12 so that the king himself and those with him were astonished at the soul of the young man, how he counted the pains as nothing.
2 Maccabees 7:13 And when this one also departed, they tortured the fourth in the same way, maltreating him.
2 Maccabees 7:14 And coming near death, he said thus, It is preferable, departing by human hands, to await the hopes from God, to be raised again by him; for you there shall be no resurrection to life.
2 Maccabees 7:15 And next they brought the fifth and maltreated him.
2 Maccabees 7:16 And looking toward him he said, Having authority among human beings, though corruptible, you do what you wish; but do not think that our race has been abandoned by God;
2 Maccabees 7:17 but you wait and behold his magnificent might, how he will torment you and your seed.
2 Maccabees 7:18 And after him they led the sixth, and being about to die, he said, Do not be deceived in vain, for we suffer these things because of ourselves, having sinned against our own God; things worthy of wonder have happened;
2 Maccabees 7:19 but do not suppose that you will be guiltless, having undertaken to fight God.
2 Maccabees 7:20 And the mother was exceedingly marvelous and worthy of good remembrance, who, seeing seven sons perish within the time of one day, bore it courageously because of her hopes in the Lord.
2 Maccabees 7:21 And she exhorted each of them in the ancestral tongue, filled with noble resolve and stirring her womanly reasoning with manly spirit, saying to them,
2 Maccabees 7:22 I do not know how you appeared in my womb, nor did I grant you spirit and life, and I did not arrange the composition of each;
2 Maccabees 7:23 therefore the creator of the world, who formed the origin of humankind and devised the origin of all things, also gives spirit and life back to you again with mercy, as you now disregard yourselves because of his laws.
2 Maccabees 7:24 But Antiochos, thinking he was despised and suspecting the reproachful voice, while the youngest was still alive, made his exhortation not only through words, but also assured through oaths that he would both enrich him and make him blessed if he changed from the ancestral ways, and would have him as a friend and entrust him with offices.
2 Maccabees 7:25 But when the young man paid no attention at all, the king summoned the mother and urged her to become an adviser to the youth for his salvation.
2 Maccabees 7:26 And when he had urged her greatly, she accepted to persuade her son;
2 Maccabees 7:27 but bending toward him, mocking the cruel tyrant, she said thus in the ancestral tongue, Son, have mercy on me, who carried you in the womb nine months and nursed you three years and raised you and brought you to this age and nourished you.
2 Maccabees 7:28 I request you, child, to look up to heaven and the earth and see all things in them and know that God made them not out of existing things, and the race of human beings comes into being thus.
2 Maccabees 7:29 Do not fear this executioner, but becoming worthy of your brothers, accept death, so that in mercy I may receive you with your brothers.
2 Maccabees 7:30 And while she was still finishing, the young man said, Whom are you waiting for? I do not obey the command of the king, but I obey the ordinance of the law given to our fathers through Moyses.
2 Maccabees 7:31 But you, having become inventor of every wickedness against the Hebrews, shall certainly not escape the hands of God.
2 Maccabees 7:32 For we suffer because of our own sins.
2 Maccabees 7:33 But if for rebuke and discipline our living Lord has been briefly angered, he will also again be reconciled to his own servants.
2 Maccabees 7:34 But you, unholy one and most polluted of all human beings, do not vainly exalt yourself, raging with uncertain hopes, raising a hand against the heavenly children;
2 Maccabees 7:35 for you have not yet escaped the judgment of the almighty, overseeing God.
2 Maccabees 7:36 For now our brothers, having borne a brief pain, have fallen under God's covenant of perpetual life; but you, by God's judgment, shall bear the just penalties of your arrogance.
2 Maccabees 7:37 But I, like the brothers, surrender both body and soul for the ancestral laws, calling upon God to become quickly merciful to the nation and for you, through trials and scourges, to confess that he alone is God,
2 Maccabees 7:38 and in me and my brothers to stop the anger of the Almighty which has justly been brought upon our whole race.
2 Maccabees 7:39 And the king became furious and treated this one worse than the others, bearing the mockery bitterly.
2 Maccabees 7:40 And this one therefore departed pure, trusting entirely in the Lord.
2 Maccabees 7:41 And last after the sons the mother died.
2 Maccabees 7:42 Let the matters concerning the eating of sacrificial entrails and the surpassing tortures therefore have been set forth to this extent.

## Chapter 8

2 Maccabees 8:1 But Ioudas, also called Makkabaios, and those with him secretly entered the villages and called their kinsmen, and taking along those who had remained in Judaism, gathered about six thousand.
2 Maccabees 8:2 And they called upon the Lord to look upon the people trampled by all, and also to pity the temple profaned by the impious men,
2 Maccabees 8:3 and also to have mercy on the city being destroyed and about to become level with the ground, and to hear the blood crying out to him,
2 Maccabees 8:4 and also to remember the unlawful destruction of the sinless infants, and concerning the blasphemies that had occurred against his name, and to hate the wickedness.
2 Maccabees 8:5 And Makkabaios, having formed a body, was already becoming irresistible to the nations, the Lord's anger having turned to mercy.
2 Maccabees 8:6 And coming unexpectedly, he burned cities and villages, and taking the advantageous places and routing not a few of the enemies,
2 Maccabees 8:7 he especially took the nights as fellow workers for such attacks. And talk of his manliness resounded everywhere.
2 Maccabees 8:8 But Philip, seeing the man gradually coming to advancement and progressing more frequently in successes, wrote to Ptolemaios, the commander of Coele Syria and Phoenicia, to help the king's affairs.
2 Maccabees 8:9 And he quickly selected Nikanor, son of Patroklos, one of the first friends, and sent him, subjecting to him nations of all tribes, no fewer than twenty thousand, to remove the entire race of Judea; and he associated with him also Gorgias, a commander and man having experience in warlike affairs.
2 Maccabees 8:10 And Nikanor determined to fulfill the tribute for the king to the Romans, being two thousand talents, from the captivity of the Judeans.
2 Maccabees 8:11 And immediately he sent to the coastal cities, inviting the purchase of Judean bodies, promising to give ninety bodies for a talent, not expecting the judgment from the Almighty that was about to follow upon him.
2 Maccabees 8:12 And news concerning Nikanor's advance reached Ioudas, and when he communicated the presence of the army to those with him,
2 Maccabees 8:13 those acting cowardly and distrusting God's judgment were slipping away and removing themselves.
2 Maccabees 8:14 But the others sold all the things remaining, and together requested the Lord to deliver those who had been sold by the impious Nikanor before meeting him;
