2 Maccabees 8:15 and if not because of themselves, yet because of the covenants with their fathers and because of the invocation upon them of his solemn and magnificent name.
2 Maccabees 8:16 And Makkabaios gathered those around him, being six thousand in number, and exhorted them not to be struck with terror by the enemies or fear the great multitude of the nations unjustly coming against them, but to contend nobly,
2 Maccabees 8:17 having before their eyes the outrage lawlessly carried out by them against the holy place and the maltreatment of the mocked city, and further the dissolution of the ancestral civic order.
2 Maccabees 8:18 For they trust in weapons and audacities together, he said, but we trust in the almighty God, who is able to cast down both those coming against us and the whole world with one nod.
2 Maccabees 8:19 And further recounting to them also the aids that had occurred in the time of the ancestors and that in the time of Sennacherim, how one hundred and eighty-five thousand perished,
2 Maccabees 8:20 and the battle against the Galatians that occurred in Babylonia, how the whole number who came to the affair was eight thousand with four thousand Macedonians, and when the Macedonians were at a loss, the eight thousand destroyed the one hundred and twenty thousand because of the help that came to them from heaven, and received much benefit.
2 Maccabees 8:21 By these things he made them confident and ready to die for the laws and the fatherland, and made the army into four parts.
2 Maccabees 8:22 And appointing his brothers, Simon and Iosepos and Ionathes, to lead each division, subjecting fifteen hundred to each,
2 Maccabees 8:23 and further also Eleazar, having read aloud the sacred book and given the watchword of God's help, himself leading the first company, he joined battle with Nikanor.
2 Maccabees 8:24 And when the Almighty became their ally, they slaughtered more than nine thousand of the enemies and made the greater part of Nikanor's army wounded and disabled in their limbs, and compelled all to flee.
2 Maccabees 8:25 And they took the money of those who had come for their purchase; and having pursued them together for a considerable distance, they returned, being constrained by the hour;
2 Maccabees 8:26 for it was the day before the sabbath, for which reason they did not prolong the pursuit of them.
2 Maccabees 8:27 And having collected their weapons and stripped the spoils from the enemies, they occupied themselves with the sabbath, abundantly blessing and giving thanks to the Lord who had saved them for this day, having appointed for them a beginning of mercy.
2 Maccabees 8:28 And after the sabbath, having apportioned some of the spoils to those maltreated and to the widows and orphans, they themselves and the children divided the rest.
2 Maccabees 8:29 And having accomplished these things and made a common supplication, they requested the merciful Lord to be entirely reconciled to his own servants.
2 Maccabees 8:30 And contending with those around Timotheos and Bakchides, they killed more than twenty thousand of them and gained very firm possession of high strongholds and divided much booty, making themselves and those maltreated and orphans and widows and further also elders equal sharers.
2 Maccabees 8:31 And having carefully collected their own weapons, they deposited everything in the advantageous places, but brought the rest of the spoils to Ierosolyma.
2 Maccabees 8:32 And they killed the tribal leader of those around Timotheos, a most unholy man who had greatly grieved the Judeans.
2 Maccabees 8:33 And celebrating victory in the fatherland, they set fire to those who had burned the sacred gateways and to Kallisthenes, who had fled into one small house, and he received the reward worthy of his impiety.
2 Maccabees 8:34 But the thrice-accursed Nikanor, who had brought the thousand merchants for the sale of the Judeans,
2 Maccabees 8:35 humbled by those considered by him to be least, through the Lord's help, put off his glorious clothing and, making himself solitary, came through the inland country to Antiocheia in the manner of a runaway, having been supremely fortunate at the destruction of the army.
2 Maccabees 8:36 And he who had undertaken to accomplish the tribute to the Romans from the captivity of those in Ierosolyma proclaimed that the Judeans had a champion, and that for this reason the Judeans were invulnerable, because they followed the laws ordained by him.

## Chapter 9

2 Maccabees 9:1 About that time Antiochos happened to have withdrawn in disorder from the regions around Persis.
2 Maccabees 9:2 For he had entered the city called Persepolis and attempted to plunder temples and hold the city; therefore, when the multitudes rushed to the aid of arms, they were routed, and it happened that Antiochos, routed by the inhabitants, made a disgraceful retreat.
2 Maccabees 9:3 While he was at Ekbatana, news of what had happened to Nikanor and those around Timotheos reached him.
2 Maccabees 9:4 Lifted up in anger, he thought to inflict upon the Jews also the malice of those who had put him to flight; therefore he ordered the charioteer to drive without stopping and complete the journey, the judgment from heaven already accompanying him; for he said thus arrogantly, “I will make Hierosolyma a mass grave of Jews when I arrive there.”
2 Maccabees 9:5 But the all-seeing Lord, the God of Israel, struck him with an incurable and invisible blow; and just as he finished the statement, an irremediable pain of the entrails and bitter torments within seized him,
2 Maccabees 9:6 very justly, since he had tormented the entrails of others with many strange calamities.
2 Maccabees 9:7 But he in no way ceased from his haughtiness, and was still filled with arrogance, breathing fire in his anger against the Jews and commanding that the journey be hastened. But it also happened that he fell from the chariot as it sped with a rushing sound, and, suffering a grievous fall, had all the limbs of his body twisted.
2 Maccabees 9:8 He who had just thought to command the waves of the sea because of his arrogance beyond human measure, and imagined he would weigh the heights of the mountains in a balance, having come to the ground, was carried along in a litter, displaying to all the manifest power of God,
2 Maccabees 9:9 so that worms swarmed up from the body of the impious man, and while he lived in anguish and pain his flesh fell away, and the whole camp was burdened with the putrefaction from his smell.
2 Maccabees 9:10 And no one could carry along him who a little earlier thought to touch the heavenly stars, because of the unbearable weight of the smell.
2 Maccabees 9:11 Then, therefore, shattered, he began to cease from his great arrogance and to come to recognition, being intensified in his pains at every moment by a divine scourge.
2 Maccabees 9:12 And unable even to endure his own smell, he said this: “It is just to submit to God and, being mortal, not to think oneself equal to God.”
2 Maccabees 9:13 But the polluted man prayed to the Master who would no longer have mercy on him, saying thus:
2 Maccabees 9:14 that he would declare free the holy city, which he was hastening to reach to level to the ground and build into a mass grave,
2 Maccabees 9:15 and would make all the Jews equal to Athenians, whom he had resolved not even to consider worthy of burial, but to cast out with their infants to beasts, to be eaten by birds;
2 Maccabees 9:16 and would adorn with most beautiful offerings the holy temple which he had previously plundered, and restore all the sacred vessels many times over, and supply from his own revenues the contributions required for the sacrifices;
2 Maccabees 9:17 and besides these things would also become a Jew and go through every inhabited place proclaiming the might of God.
2 Maccabees 9:18 But as the pains in no way ceased, for the just judgment of God had come upon him, despairing of his own situation, he wrote to the Jews the letter written below, having the character of a supplication, and containing the following:
2 Maccabees 9:19 “To the good Jews, the citizens, abundant greetings and health and prosperity, from King and General Antiochos.
2 Maccabees 9:20 If you and the children are well, and your affairs are according to your wishes; having my hope toward heaven,
2 Maccabees 9:21 I remembered your honor and goodwill affectionately. Returning from the regions of Persis and falling into an illness involving difficulty, I considered it necessary to think of the common security of all.
2 Maccabees 9:22 Not despairing of my own situation, but having much hope of escaping the illness,
2 Maccabees 9:23 and observing that my father also, at the times when he campaigned in the upper regions, designated his successor,
2 Maccabees 9:24 so that, if anything unexpected should happen or anything difficult be reported, those throughout the country, knowing to whom affairs have been left, might not be disturbed;
2 Maccabees 9:25 and besides these things considering that the neighboring rulers adjoining the kingdom watch the times and await what will happen, I have designated my son Antiochos king, whom I often entrusted and commended to most of you when going up to the upper satrapies; and I have written to him what is written below.
2 Maccabees 9:26 I therefore exhort you and ask that, remembering the benefits collectively and each individually, you maintain your existing goodwill toward me and my son;
2 Maccabees 9:27 for I am persuaded that he, following my policy with equity and humanity, will accommodate himself to you.”
2 Maccabees 9:28 So the murderer and blasphemer, having suffered the worst things, as he had treated others, ended his life in a foreign land in the mountains by a most pitiable fate.
2 Maccabees 9:29 Philippos, his companion from childhood, was conveying the body; he, fearing the son of Antiochos, also made his way to Ptolemaios Philometor in Egypt.

## Chapter 10

2 Maccabees 10:1 Makkabaios and those with him, the Lord leading them, recovered the sanctuary and the city,
2 Maccabees 10:2 and tore down the altars constructed by the foreigners in the marketplace, and also sacred precincts,
2 Maccabees 10:3 and, purifying the temple, made another altar; and, heating stones and taking fire from them, offered sacrifices after a period of two years, and provided incense and lamps and the setting out of the loaves.
2 Maccabees 10:4 Having done these things, they fell upon their bellies and asked the Lord that they might no longer fall into such evils, but, if ever they should sin, might be disciplined by him with equity and not be handed over to blasphemous and barbarous nations.
2 Maccabees 10:5 On the day on which the temple had been profaned by foreigners, it happened that the purification of the temple took place on the same day, the twenty-fifth of the same month, which is Chaseleu.
2 Maccabees 10:6 And they celebrated eight days with gladness in the manner of booths, remembering how a little time before, at the feast of tents, they had been dwelling in the mountains and caves like beasts.
2 Maccabees 10:7 Therefore, bearing ivy-wreathed rods and beautiful branches, and also palms, they offered hymns to him who had prospered the purification of his own place.
2 Maccabees 10:8 They decreed by a common ordinance and vote that the whole nation of the Jews should celebrate these days yearly.
2 Maccabees 10:9 And thus were the circumstances of the death of Antiochos, who was called Epiphanes.
2 Maccabees 10:10 Now we will make known the affairs of Antiochos Eupator, who was the son of the impious man, abridging the evils attending the wars themselves.
2 Maccabees 10:11 For he, receiving the kingdom, appointed a certain Lysias over affairs, and chief general of Coele Syria and Phoinike.
2 Maccabees 10:12 For Ptolemaios, called Makron, preferring to maintain justice toward the Jews because of the injustice done to them, tried to conduct affairs with them peaceably;
2 Maccabees 10:13 therefore, being accused before Eupator by the Friends, and hearing himself called a traitor at every turn because he had abandoned Kypros, entrusted to him by Philometor, and withdrawn to Antiochos Epiphanes, and having failed to ennoble his authority as noble, he poisoned himself and departed from life.
2 Maccabees 10:14 Gorgias, becoming general of the regions, maintained mercenaries and at every turn fostered war against the Jews.
2 Maccabees 10:15 Together with him the Idoumaians also, holding strategically placed fortifications, harassed the Jews and, taking in those who had banished them from Hierosolyma, attempted to foster war.
2 Maccabees 10:16 Those around Makkabaios, making supplication and asking God to become their ally, rushed upon the fortifications of the Idoumaians,
2 Maccabees 10:17 and, attacking them vigorously, gained control of the places and repelled all those fighting upon the wall, and slaughtered those who fell into their hands; they killed no fewer than twenty thousand.
2 Maccabees 10:18 When no fewer than nine thousand fled together into two exceedingly strong towers, possessing everything needed for a siege,
2 Maccabees 10:19 Makkabaios, leaving Simon and Iosepos, and also Zakchaios and those with him, sufficient for their siege, himself departed to places requiring urgent attention.
2 Maccabees 10:20 But those around Simon, becoming greedy for money, were persuaded with silver by some of those in the towers; and, receiving seventy thousand drachmas, allowed some to slip away.
2 Maccabees 10:21 When what had happened was reported to Makkabaios, he gathered the leaders of the people and accused them of having sold their brothers for silver by releasing their enemies against them.
2 Maccabees 10:22 He therefore killed these men who had become traitors, and immediately took possession of the two towers.
2 Maccabees 10:23 Prospering in everything undertaken with arms in his hands, he destroyed more than twenty thousand in the two fortifications.
2 Maccabees 10:24 Timotheos, previously defeated by the Jews, gathered vast mercenary forces and assembled no few horses from Asia, and came intending to take Ioudaia as a conquest of the spear.
2 Maccabees 10:25 When he approached, those around Makkabaios, for supplication to God, sprinkled their heads with earth and girded their loins with sackcloth,
2 Maccabees 10:26 and, falling upon the step opposite the altar, asked him to become gracious to them, to be an enemy to their enemies and oppose those opposing them, as the law makes clear.
2 Maccabees 10:27 Leaving their prayer and taking up their arms, they advanced farther from the city; and, approaching the enemies, remained by themselves.
2 Maccabees 10:28 Just as the dawn spread, both sides attacked, the one having their refuge in the Lord as a guarantee of success and victory with valor, the other appointing anger as the leader of their contests.
2 Maccabees 10:29 When a fierce battle arose, five distinguished men from heaven upon horses with golden bridles appeared to the adversaries, and led the Jews,
2 Maccabees 10:30 who also took Makkabaios into their midst and, shielding him with their own full armor, kept him unwounded; and they hurled arrows and thunderbolts at the adversaries, who therefore, confused by blindness, were cut down, filled with turmoil.
2 Maccabees 10:31 Twenty thousand and five hundred were slaughtered, and six hundred cavalrymen.
2 Maccabees 10:32 Timotheos himself fled with others into the fortification called Gazara, an exceedingly strong fortress, where Chaireas was commander.
2 Maccabees 10:33 Those around Makkabaios gladly besieged the fortress for four days.
2 Maccabees 10:34 Those within, trusting in the strength of the place, blasphemed exceedingly and uttered unlawful words.
2 Maccabees 10:35 As the fifth day began to appear, twenty young men of those around Makkabaios, inflamed in anger because of the blasphemies, attacked the wall manfully and with beastlike fury cut down whoever they encountered;
2 Maccabees 10:36 others likewise climbed up during the diversion against those within and set the towers on fire, and, kindling fires, burned the blasphemers alive; others broke through the gates and, admitting the rest of the formation, took possession of the city.
2 Maccabees 10:37 And they slaughtered Timotheos, hidden in a certain pit, and his brother Chaireas and Apollophanes.
2 Maccabees 10:38 Having accomplished these things, with hymns and acknowledgments they blessed the Lord, who greatly benefited Israel and gave them the victory.

## Chapter 11

2 Maccabees 11:1 After a very short little interval, Lysias, the king’s guardian and kinsman and the one over affairs, bearing what had happened very heavily,
2 Maccabees 11:2 gathered about eighty thousand and all the cavalry, and came against the Jews, calculating that he would make the city a dwelling place for Greeks,
2 Maccabees 11:3 and the sanctuary subject to a levy of silver, like the other sacred precincts of the nations, and would make the high priesthood purchasable yearly,
2 Maccabees 11:4 in no way reckoning with the might of God, but elated by the tens of thousands of infantry and the thousands of cavalry and the eighty elephants.
2 Maccabees 11:5 Entering Ioudaia and approaching Baithsoura, which was a strong place and about five stadia distant from Hierosolyma, he pressed it hard.
2 Maccabees 11:6 When those around Makkabaios learned that he was besieging the fortifications, with lamentations and tears they supplicated the Lord together with the multitudes to send a good angel for the salvation of Israel.
2 Maccabees 11:7 Makkabaios himself first took up arms and exhorted the others to risk themselves together with him to aid their brothers; and they set out together eagerly.
2 Maccabees 11:8 While they were there near Hierosolyma, a horseman in white clothing appeared, leading them, brandishing golden armor.
2 Maccabees 11:9 Together they all blessed the merciful God and were strengthened in their souls, being ready to pierce not only men, but the wildest beasts and walls of iron.
2 Maccabees 11:10 They advanced in battle array, having their ally from heaven, the Lord having shown them mercy.
2 Maccabees 11:11 Charging like lions into the enemies, they laid low eleven thousand of them, and sixteen hundred cavalrymen; and compelled them all to flee.
2 Maccabees 11:12 Most of them escaped wounded and naked; and Lysias himself also escaped, fleeing disgracefully.
2 Maccabees 11:13 Being no fool, he considered within himself the loss that had befallen him, and realized that the Hebrews were invincible when the powerful God fought alongside them,
2 Maccabees 11:14 and sent to them and persuaded them to settle on all just terms, and that he would also persuade the king, compelling him to become their friend.
2 Maccabees 11:15 Makkabaios consented to all that Lysias requested, taking thought for what was advantageous; for all that Makkabaios submitted to Lysias in writing concerning the Jews, the king granted.
2 Maccabees 11:16 For the letters written to the Jews by Lysias contained the following: “Lysias to the multitude of the Jews, greetings.
2 Maccabees 11:17 Ioannes and Abessalom, sent by you, submitted the communication written below and made requests concerning the matters indicated by it.
2 Maccabees 11:18 Whatever therefore needed to be brought before the king also, I made clear; and what was admissible, he granted.
2 Maccabees 11:19 If therefore you maintain your goodwill toward affairs, I will try in the future also to be instrumental in good things.
2 Maccabees 11:20 Concerning these things and the particulars, I have instructed both these men and those from me to speak with you.
2 Maccabees 11:21 Farewell. Year one hundred and forty-eight, the twenty-fourth of Dios Korinthios.”
2 Maccabees 11:22 The king’s letter contained the following: “King Antiochos to his brother Lysias, greetings.
2 Maccabees 11:23 Our father having departed to the gods, we wish those of the kingdom to be undisturbed in attending to their own affairs,
2 Maccabees 11:24 and have heard that the Jews do not approve of our father’s change to Greek ways, but prefer their own manner of life and ask that their lawful customs be permitted them;
2 Maccabees 11:25 therefore, choosing that this nation also be free from disturbance, we judge that the sanctuary should be restored to them and that they should conduct their life according to the customs of their ancestors.
2 Maccabees 11:26 You will therefore do well to send to them and give pledges, so that, knowing our policy, they may be of good cheer and gladly occupy themselves with the management of their own affairs.”
2 Maccabees 11:27 The king’s letter to the nation was as follows: “King Antiochos to the senate of the Jews and the other Jews, greetings.
2 Maccabees 11:28 If you are well, it would be as we wish; we ourselves also are in health.
2 Maccabees 11:29 Menelaos informed us that you wish to come down and attend to your own affairs.
2 Maccabees 11:30 Therefore, for those coming down by the thirtieth of Xanthikos there will be a pledge with permission
2 Maccabees 11:31 for the Jews to use their own provisions and laws, as formerly also, and none of them will be harassed in any manner concerning the things done in ignorance.
2 Maccabees 11:32 I have also sent Menelaos to encourage you.
2 Maccabees 11:33 Farewell. Year one hundred and forty-eight, the fifteenth of Xanthikos.”
2 Maccabees 11:34 The Romans also sent them a letter containing the following: “Kointos Memmios, Titos Manios, ambassadors of the Romans, to the people of the Jews, greetings.
2 Maccabees 11:35 Concerning what Lysias, the king’s kinsman, granted you, we too approve.
2 Maccabees 11:36 But concerning what he judged should be brought before the king, consider these matters and send someone immediately, so that we may set them forth as is appropriate for you; for we are proceeding toward Antiocheia.
2 Maccabees 11:37 Therefore hasten and send some men, so that we too may know what opinion you hold.
2 Maccabees 11:38 Be in health. Year one hundred and forty-eight, the fifteenth of Xanthikos.”

## Chapter 12

2 Maccabees 12:1 When these agreements had been made, Lysias went away to the king, and the Jews occupied themselves with agriculture.
2 Maccabees 12:2 But of the local generals, Timotheos and Apollonios son of Gennaios, and also Hieronymos and Demophon, and besides these Nikanor the governor of Kypros, did not allow them to remain settled and live quietly.
2 Maccabees 12:3 The Ioppites committed this great impious deed: they invited the Jews dwelling with them to embark with their wives and children in the boats they had provided, as though no hostility toward them existed,
2 Maccabees 12:4 and according to the common vote of the city; and when they accepted, as wishing to live in peace and having no suspicion, they took them out and drowned them, no fewer than two hundred.
2 Maccabees 12:5 Ioudas, learning of the cruelty done to his fellow countrymen, gave orders to the men around him
2 Maccabees 12:6 and, invoking God, the just judge, came against the murderers of his brothers, and burned the harbor by night and set the boats ablaze, and pierced those who had fled together there.
2 Maccabees 12:7 But when the place was shut up, he withdrew, intending to come again and uproot the whole community of the Ioppites.
2 Maccabees 12:8 Learning also that those in Iamneia wished to deal in the same manner with the Jews dwelling among them,
2 Maccabees 12:9 he attacked the Iamnites by night and set the harbor on fire together with the fleet, so that the rays of the light were visible in Hierosolyma, two hundred and forty stadia away.
2 Maccabees 12:10 When they had withdrawn nine stadia from there, while making their journey against Timotheos, Arabs, no fewer than five thousand, and five hundred cavalrymen attacked him.
2 Maccabees 12:11 A fierce battle arose, and those around Ioudas prospered through the help from God; the nomads, defeated, asked Ioudas to give them pledges, promising both to give livestock and to benefit them in other matters.
2 Maccabees 12:12 Ioudas, considering that they were truly useful in many things, agreed to keep peace with them; and, receiving pledges, they departed to their tents.
2 Maccabees 12:13 He also attacked a certain city, strong with earthworks and enclosed by walls and inhabited by a mixture of nations, whose name was Kaspin.
2 Maccabees 12:14 Those within, trusting in the strength of the walls and the stores of food, treated those around Ioudas very rudely, reviling and further blaspheming and saying things that were not lawful.
2 Maccabees 12:15 Those around Ioudas, invoking the great Sovereign of the world, who without rams and mechanical engines had hurled down Iericho in the times of Iesous, hurled themselves fiercely against the wall.
2 Maccabees 12:16 Taking possession of the city by the will of God, they wrought unspeakable slaughter, so that the adjoining lake, two stadia in breadth, appeared flooded and filled with blood.
2 Maccabees 12:17 Withdrawing from there, they completed seven hundred and fifty stadia to Charax, to the Jews called Toubianoi.
2 Maccabees 12:18 They did not find Timotheos in the regions, as he had then withdrawn from the regions without accomplishing anything, but had left a very strong garrison in a certain place.
2 Maccabees 12:19 Dositheos and Sosipatros, commanders of those around Makkabaios, marched out and destroyed those left by Timotheos in the fortification, more than ten thousand men.
2 Maccabees 12:20 Makkabaios, arranging the army around him by companies, appointed them over the companies and rushed against Timotheos, who had around him one hundred and twenty thousand infantry and twenty-five hundred cavalrymen.
2 Maccabees 12:21 Learning of the approach of Ioudas, Timotheos sent ahead the women and children and the other baggage into the place called Karnion; for the place was difficult to besiege and difficult to approach because of the narrowness of all the approaches.
2 Maccabees 12:22 When the first company of Ioudas appeared, and dread came upon the enemies and fear from the manifestation of him who oversees all things came upon them, they rushed into flight, each being carried in a different direction, so that they were often injured by their own men and impaled on the points of their swords.
2 Maccabees 12:23 Ioudas pursued more vigorously, piercing the offenders, and destroyed about thirty thousand men.
2 Maccabees 12:24 Timotheos himself, falling into the hands of those around Dositheos and Sosipatros, requested with much deception that they release him safe, because he held the parents of many and the brothers of some, and it would happen that these would be disregarded.
2 Maccabees 12:25 When he had confirmed through many assurances the agreement to restore these unharmed, they released him for the sake of the safety of their brothers.
2 Maccabees 12:26 Going out against Karnion and the Atergateion, he slaughtered twenty-five thousand persons.
2 Maccabees 12:27 After their rout and destruction he also marched against Ephron, a strong city, in which Lysias and multitudes of every tribe dwelt; strong young men stationed before the walls fought back vigorously, and there were many stores of engines and missiles there.
2 Maccabees 12:28 Invoking the Sovereign who powerfully crushes the strength of enemies, they brought the city under their hand and laid low about twenty-five thousand of those within.
2 Maccabees 12:29 Departing from there, they set out against the city of the Scythians, six hundred stadia distant from Hierosolyma.
2 Maccabees 12:30 The Jews settled there testified to the goodwill which the Scythopolitans had toward them, and their gentle treatment in the times of misfortune,
2 Maccabees 12:31 and, giving thanks and further exhorting them to be well-disposed toward their people in the future also, they arrived in Hierosolyma, the feast of weeks being near.
2 Maccabees 12:32 After the feast called Pentecost, they set out against Gorgias, the general of Idoumaia.
2 Maccabees 12:33 He came out with three thousand infantry and four hundred cavalrymen.
2 Maccabees 12:34 When they engaged in battle, it happened that a few of the Jews fell.
2 Maccabees 12:35 A certain Dositheos of the men of Bakenor, a strong mounted man, held onto Gorgias and, grasping his cloak, dragged him vigorously, wishing to take the accursed man alive; but when one of the Thracian cavalrymen charged him and struck down his shoulder, Gorgias escaped to Marisa.
2 Maccabees 12:36 Those around Esdris having fought for a long time and being exhausted, Ioudas invoked the Lord to appear as an ally and leader of the war;
2 Maccabees 12:37 beginning the shout with hymns in the ancestral language, and charging unexpectedly against those around Gorgias, he brought about their rout.
2 Maccabees 12:38 Ioudas, taking up the army, came to the city of Odollam; and as the seventh day approached, they purified themselves according to custom and passed the sabbath there.
2 Maccabees 12:39 On the following day, when it had become necessary, those around Ioudas came to recover the bodies of those who had fallen and restore them with their relatives to the ancestral tombs.
2 Maccabees 12:40 Under the tunics of each of the dead they found sacred objects of the idols from Iamneia, from which the law forbids the Jews; and it became clear to all that these men had fallen for this reason.
2 Maccabees 12:41 Therefore all, blessing the deeds of the Lord, the just judge who makes hidden things manifest,
2 Maccabees 12:42 turned to supplication, asking that the sin committed be completely blotted out. The noble Ioudas exhorted the multitude to keep themselves without sin, having seen before their eyes what had happened because of the sin of those who had fallen.
2 Maccabees 12:43 Making a collection man by man amounting to two thousand silver drachmas, he sent it to Hierosolyma to offer a sacrifice for sin, acting very well and nobly, taking thought concerning resurrection;
2 Maccabees 12:44 for if he were not expecting those who had fallen to rise, it would be superfluous and foolish to pray for the dead;
2 Maccabees 12:45 or else looking to a most beautiful reward laid up for those who fall asleep in piety, the thought was holy and pious; therefore he made expiation concerning the dead, that they might be released from sin.

## Chapter 13

2 Maccabees 13:1 In the one hundred and forty-ninth year, news reached those around Ioudas that Antiochos Eupator was coming with multitudes against Ioudaia,
2 Maccabees 13:2 and with him Lysias, the guardian and the one over affairs, each having a Greek force of one hundred and ten thousand infantry and five thousand three hundred cavalrymen and twenty-two elephants, and three hundred scythed chariots.
2 Maccabees 13:3 Menelaos also joined them and encouraged Antiochos with much dissimulation, not for the salvation of his homeland, but imagining that he would be established in office.
2 Maccabees 13:4 But the King of kings roused the anger of Antiochos against the offender; and when Lysias pointed out that this man was responsible for all the evils, he commanded them to take him to Beroia and put him to death, as is the custom in the place.
2 Maccabees 13:5 In the place there is a tower of fifty cubits, full of ashes, and it had a circular contrivance, precipitous on every side into the ashes.
2 Maccabees 13:6 There they all push to destruction anyone guilty of temple plundering or one who has committed an excess of certain other evils.
2 Maccabees 13:7 By such a fate it happened that the lawless Menelaos died, obtaining not even earth;
2 Maccabees 13:8 very justly; for since he had committed many sins concerning the altar, whose fire and ashes were pure, he received death in ashes.
2 Maccabees 13:9 The king, made barbarous in his intentions, was coming to show the Jews the worst things that had happened under his father.
2 Maccabees 13:10 Ioudas, learning these things, commanded the multitude to invoke the Lord day and night, if ever at any other time, now also to aid those about to be deprived of law and homeland and holy sanctuary,
2 Maccabees 13:11 and not to allow the people who had just briefly revived to become subject to the ill-speaking nations.
2 Maccabees 13:12 When all had done the same together and petitioned the merciful Lord with weeping and fasts and prostration for three days without ceasing, Ioudas encouraged them and commanded them to assemble.
2 Maccabees 13:13 Meeting privately with the elders, he resolved that before the king’s army invaded Ioudaia and gained control of the city, they should go out and decide matters with the help of God.
2 Maccabees 13:14 Entrusting the direction to the Creator of the world, he exhorted those with him to contend nobly to death for laws, sanctuary, city, homeland, citizenship; and he made his camp around Modein.
2 Maccabees 13:15 Giving those around him the watchword “God’s victory,” with chosen excellent young men he attacked by night the camp at the royal quarters and killed about two thousand men, and pierced the foremost of the elephants together with the one in its housing,
2 Maccabees 13:16 and finally they filled the camp with dread and turmoil and withdrew successfully;
2 Maccabees 13:17 this had happened as day was already beginning to appear, because of the Lord’s protection aiding him.
2 Maccabees 13:18 The king, having received a taste of the Jews’ boldness, tried the places by stratagems.
2 Maccabees 13:19 He advanced against Baithsoura, a strong fortress of the Jews, was routed, encountered resistance, was defeated;
2 Maccabees 13:20 and Ioudas sent the necessities in to those within.
2 Maccabees 13:21 Rodokos of the Jewish ranks reported the secrets to the enemies; he was sought out and seized and confined.
2 Maccabees 13:22 The king spoke a second time to those in Baithsoura, gave a pledge, received one, went away, attacked those around Ioudas, was defeated,
2 Maccabees 13:23 learned that Philippos, left over affairs in Antiocheia, had become desperate, was disturbed, appealed to the Jews, submitted and swore to all just terms, made a settlement and offered a sacrifice, honored the temple and treated the place humanely;
2 Maccabees 13:24 and he received Makkabaios, left Hegemonides as general from Ptolemais as far as the Gerrhenoi.
2 Maccabees 13:25 He came to Ptolemais; the Ptolemaians were displeased with the agreements, for they were indignant over them and wished to annul the stipulations.
2 Maccabees 13:26 Lysias went up to the platform, defended the matter as well as possible, persuaded them, calmed them, made them well-disposed, departed to Antiocheia. Thus proceeded the matters of the king’s advance and departure.

## Chapter 14

2 Maccabees 14:1 After a period of three years, news reached those around Ioudas that Demetrios son of Seleukos, sailing in through the harbor at Tripolis with a strong multitude and a fleet,
2 Maccabees 14:2 had gained control of the country, having killed Antiochos and his guardian Lysias.
2 Maccabees 14:3 A certain Alkimos, formerly high priest, but voluntarily defiled in the times of separation, realizing that in no manner was there safety for him or any longer access to the holy altar,
2 Maccabees 14:4 came to King Demetrios about the one hundred and fifty-first year, bringing him a golden crown and a palm, and besides these some of the customary branches of the sanctuary, and kept quiet that day.
2 Maccabees 14:5 Taking an opportunity as an accomplice of his own folly, when summoned to council by Demetrios and asked in what disposition and intention the Jews stood, he said in response:
2 Maccabees 14:6 “Those of the Jews called Asidaioi, whom Ioudas Makkabaios leads, foster war and raise sedition, not allowing the kingdom to obtain stability.
2 Maccabees 14:7 Therefore, having laid aside my ancestral glory [I mean the high priesthood], I have now come here,
2 Maccabees 14:8 first, genuinely taking thought for the matters belonging to the king, and second, also considering my own fellow citizens; for through the recklessness of the aforementioned men our whole people suffers no small misfortune.
2 Maccabees 14:9 Having learned each of these things, you, O king, take thought both for the country and for our beleaguered people, according to the gracious humanity you have toward all.
2 Maccabees 14:10 For as long as Ioudas survives, it is impossible for affairs to obtain peace.”
2 Maccabees 14:11 When such things were spoken by him, the other Friends, hostile toward Ioudas, quickly inflamed Demetrios further.
2 Maccabees 14:12 Immediately choosing Nikanor, formerly commander of the elephants, and appointing him general of Ioudaia, he sent him out,
2 Maccabees 14:13 giving orders to kill Ioudas himself, scatter those with him, and establish Alkimos as high priest of the greatest sanctuary.
2 Maccabees 14:14 The nations throughout Ioudaia who had put Ioudas to flight joined Nikanor in herds, thinking that the misfortunes and calamities of the Jews would be their own successes.
2 Maccabees 14:15 Hearing of Nikanor’s advance and the attack of the nations, they sprinkled themselves with earth and supplicated him who had established his own people forever and always helps his own portion by manifestation.
2 Maccabees 14:16 At the leader’s command, immediately departing from there, he meets them at the village of Dessaou.
2 Maccabees 14:17 Simon, the brother of Ioudas, had engaged Nikanor, but had stumbled slowly because of the sudden speechlessness of the opponents;
2 Maccabees 14:18 nevertheless Nikanor, hearing of the valor which those around Ioudas possessed and their courage in contests for their homeland, was wary of deciding the matter through bloodshed.
2 Maccabees 14:19 Therefore he sent Posidonios and Theodotos and Mattathias to give and receive pledges.
2 Maccabees 14:20 When considerable examination of these matters had taken place, and the leader had communicated with the multitudes, and a unanimous opinion appeared, they agreed to the terms.
2 Maccabees 14:21 They appointed a day on which they would meet privately in the same place; and a two-seated chariot came forward from each, and they set out seats.
2 Maccabees 14:22 Ioudas stationed armed men ready in strategically placed positions, lest wickedness suddenly arise from the enemies; they held the appropriate conference.
2 Maccabees 14:23 Nikanor stayed in Hierosolyma and did nothing improper, and dismissed the multitudes gathered in herds.
2 Maccabees 14:24 He kept Ioudas continually in his presence; he was attached to the man in soul.
2 Maccabees 14:25 He encouraged him to marry and beget children; he married, settled down, shared in life.
2 Maccabees 14:26 But Alkimos, perceiving their goodwill toward each other and taking the agreements that had been made, came to Demetrios and said that Nikanor was thinking contrary to affairs; for he had designated Ioudas, the plotter against the kingdom, as his own successor.
2 Maccabees 14:27 The king, becoming enraged and provoked by the slanders of the utterly wicked man, wrote to Nikanor, declaring that he was displeased with the agreements, and commanding him to send Makkabaios bound to Antiocheia quickly.
2 Maccabees 14:28 When these things reached Nikanor, he was disturbed and distressed that he would annul the stipulations when the man had done no wrong.
2 Maccabees 14:29 But since it was not possible to act against the king, he watched for a favorable opportunity to accomplish this by stratagem.
2 Maccabees 14:30 Makkabaios, seeing that Nikanor was conducting his dealings with him more harshly and had made their customary meetings more rude, and understanding that the harshness did not come from the best intention, gathered no few of those around him and hid from Nikanor.
2 Maccabees 14:31 The other, recognizing that he had been skillfully outmaneuvered by the man, came to the greatest and holy sanctuary while the priests were offering the due sacrifices and commanded them to hand over the man.
2 Maccabees 14:32 When they declared with oaths that they did not know where the man sought was,
2 Maccabees 14:33 he stretched his right hand toward the temple and swore these things: “Unless you hand Ioudas over to me bound, I will make this enclosure of God into a plain and dig down the altar and raise a conspicuous sanctuary here to Dionysos.”
2 Maccabees 14:34 Having said these things, he went away; the priests, stretching their hands toward heaven, invoked him who continually champions our nation, saying these things:
2 Maccabees 14:35 “You, Lord of all, being in need of nothing, were pleased that a temple for your dwelling should come to be among us;
2 Maccabees 14:36 and now, holy Lord of all sanctification, preserve forever undefiled this house recently purified.”
2 Maccabees 14:37 A certain Razis, one of the elders from Hierosolyma, was denounced to Nikanor, a man who loved his fellow citizens and was exceedingly well spoken of, and for his goodwill was called father of the Jews.
2 Maccabees 14:38 For in the former times of separation he had been brought to judgment for Judaism, and had risked both body and soul for Judaism with all earnestness.
2 Maccabees 14:39 Nikanor, wishing to make evident the hostility he had toward the Jews, sent more than five hundred soldiers to arrest him;
2 Maccabees 14:40 for he thought that by arresting that man he would work calamity upon them.
2 Maccabees 14:41 When the multitudes were about to capture the tower and were forcing the courtyard door and commanding that fire be brought and the doors set alight, being surrounded, he turned his sword against himself,
2 Maccabees 14:42 wishing to die nobly rather than become subject to the offenders and be outraged unworthily of his own nobility.
2 Maccabees 14:43 But not striking true with the blow because of the haste of the contest, and the multitudes invading within the doorways, he ran nobly up onto the wall and manfully hurled himself down into the multitudes.
2 Maccabees 14:44 They quickly stepped back, leaving a space, and he landed in the middle of the empty space.
2 Maccabees 14:45 Still breathing and inflamed in spirit, he rose, his blood flowing in streams and his wounds being grievous, ran through the multitudes and stood upon a precipitous rock,
2 Maccabees 14:46 already becoming wholly drained of blood, pulled out his entrails and took them in both hands and hurled them at the multitudes, and, invoking the Master of life and spirit to restore these to him again, departed in this manner.

## Chapter 15

2 Maccabees 15:1 Nikanor, learning that those around Ioudas were in the regions of Samareia, resolved to attack them with complete security on the day of rest.
2 Maccabees 15:2 When the Jews accompanying him under compulsion said, “By no means destroy so savagely and barbarously, but allot glory to the day honored with holiness by him who oversees all things,”
2 Maccabees 15:3 the thrice-offending man asked whether there was a Sovereign in heaven who had ordered the observance of the sabbath day;
2 Maccabees 15:4 when they declared, “There is the living Lord himself, Sovereign in heaven, who commanded the observance of the seventh day,”
2 Maccabees 15:5 the other says, “I too am a sovereign upon earth, who commands the taking up of arms and the performance of the king’s requirements.” Nevertheless he did not succeed in accomplishing his cruel intention.
2 Maccabees 15:6 Nikanor, lifting his neck with all arrogance, had resolved to set up a common trophy over those around Ioudas.
2 Maccabees 15:7 But Makkabaios was continually confident, with all hope, that he would obtain help from the Lord,
2 Maccabees 15:8 and encouraged those with him not to fear the advance of the nations, but, keeping in mind the helps from heaven that had previously come to them, now also to expect the victory that would be theirs from the Almighty.
2 Maccabees 15:9 Comforting them from the law and the prophets, and further reminding them of the contests they had accomplished, he made them more eager.
2 Maccabees 15:10 Rousing them in spirit, he gave orders, at the same time pointing out the faithlessness of the nations and their violation of oaths.
2 Maccabees 15:11 Arming each of them not so much with the security of shields and spears as with the encouragement in good words, and further relating a trustworthy dream, something like a waking vision, he gladdened them all.
2 Maccabees 15:12 Its vision was as follows: Onias, who had been high priest, a fine and good man, modest in his encounters, gentle in manner and uttering speech fittingly, and from childhood having practiced all things belonging to virtue, stretched out his hands and prayed for the whole body of the Jews.
2 Maccabees 15:13 Then in this manner a man appeared, distinguished by gray hair and glory, and the majesty around him was wondrous and most magnificent.
2 Maccabees 15:14 Onias answered and said, “This is the lover of the brothers, who prays much for the people and the holy city, Ieremias, the prophet of God.”
2 Maccabees 15:15 Ieremias stretched out his right hand and handed Ioudas a golden sword, and, giving it, addressed him thus:
2 Maccabees 15:16 “Take the holy sword, a gift from God, through which you will shatter the adversaries.”
2 Maccabees 15:17 Encouraged by the words of Ioudas, very fine and able to impel to valor and make the souls of the young manly, they resolved not to campaign, but to charge nobly and, engaging with all manliness, decide matters, because the city and the holy things and the sanctuary were in danger;
2 Maccabees 15:18 for concern for wives and children, and also brothers and relatives, occupied a lesser place for them, but the fear for the consecrated temple was greatest and first.
2 Maccabees 15:19 Those confined in the city also had no incidental anxiety, being disturbed about the attack in the open country.
2 Maccabees 15:20 When all were already awaiting the coming decision, and the enemies had already approached, and the army had been drawn out and the beasts stationed at a suitable position and the cavalry arranged on the flank,
2 Maccabees 15:21 Makkabaios, seeing the presence of the multitudes and the varied equipment of arms and the savagery of the beasts, raised his hands toward heaven and invoked the wonder-working Lord, knowing that it is not through arms, but as it may be judged by him, that he secures victory for the worthy.
2 Maccabees 15:22 Invoking him, he spoke in this manner: “You, Master, sent your angel in the time of Ezekias, king of Ioudaia, and he killed about one hundred and eighty-five thousand from the camp of Sennacherim;
2 Maccabees 15:23 and now, Sovereign of the heavens, send a good angel before us for dread and trembling;
2 Maccabees 15:24 by the greatness of your arm may those coming with blasphemy against your holy people be struck with terror.” And he ended with these words.
2 Maccabees 15:25 Those around Nikanor advanced with trumpets and paeans.
2 Maccabees 15:26 Those around Ioudas engaged the enemies with invocation and prayers.
2 Maccabees 15:27 Contending with their hands and praying to God with their hearts, they laid low no fewer than thirty-five thousand, greatly gladdened by the manifestation of God.
2 Maccabees 15:28 Leaving the engagement and withdrawing with joy, they recognized that Nikanor had fallen with his full armor.
2 Maccabees 15:29 A shout and commotion arose, and they blessed the Sovereign in the ancestral language.
2 Maccabees 15:30 He who in every respect was the foremost champion in body and soul for the citizens, who had preserved his lifelong goodwill toward his fellow countrymen, commanded them to cut off Nikanor’s head and his hand with the shoulder and carry them to Hierosolyma.
2 Maccabees 15:31 Arriving there and calling together his fellow countrymen and stationing the priests before the altar, he sent for those from the citadel.
2 Maccabees 15:32 Showing the head of the polluted Nikanor and the hand of the ill-speaking man, which he had stretched out against the holy house of the Almighty and boasted greatly,
2 Maccabees 15:33 and cutting out the tongue of the impious Nikanor, he said he would give it piece by piece to the birds, and hang up the recompense of his folly opposite the temple.
2 Maccabees 15:34 They all blessed toward heaven the manifest Lord, saying, “Blessed is he who preserved his own place undefiled.”
2 Maccabees 15:35 He hung Nikanor’s head from the citadel, a sign visible to all and manifest of the Lord’s help.
2 Maccabees 15:36 They all decreed by a common vote by no means to leave this day unmarked, but to keep conspicuous the thirteenth of the twelfth month — called Adar in the Syrian language — one day before the day of Mardochaios.
2 Maccabees 15:37 The affairs concerning Nikanor having proceeded thus, and the city having been held by the Hebrews from those times, I too will cease the account here.
2 Maccabees 15:38 If well and aptly in composition, this I myself wished; but if cheaply and moderately, this was attainable for me.
2 Maccabees 15:39 For just as drinking wine alone, and likewise water alone again, is harmful, but wine mixed with water is sweet and produces delightful pleasure, so also the construction of the account delights the ears of those who encounter the composition. Here will be the end.

# 3 Maccabees

The Apostolic Bible. Public domain. https://apostolic-bible.ysys9.chatgpt.site/license.html


## Chapter 1

3 Maccabees 1:1 Philopator, learning from those who had returned that the regions under his control had been taken away by Antiochos, gave orders to all the infantry and cavalry forces and, taking along his sister Arsinoe, set out as far as the regions around Raphia, where those around Antiochos had encamped.
3 Maccabees 1:2 A certain Theodotos, intending to fulfill the plot, took the best of the Ptolemaic arms previously assigned to him and made his way by night to Ptolemaios’s tent, intending to kill him single-handedly and thereby end the war.
3 Maccabees 1:3 But Dositheos, called the son of Drimylos, a Jew by birth, but later having changed his lawful customs and become alienated from the ancestral ordinances, had taken him away and laid down an obscure man in the tent, who happened to receive the punishment intended for him.
3 Maccabees 1:4 When a fierce battle arose and affairs were going considerably better for Antiochos, Arsinoe went through the forces and, with compassion and tears and her locks loosened, exhorted them to aid themselves and their children and wives boldly, promising to give each two minas of gold if they conquered.
3 Maccabees 1:5 And thus it happened that the opponents were destroyed in hand-to-hand fighting, and many were also captured as prisoners of the spear.
3 Maccabees 1:6 Having overcome the plot, he decided to visit and encourage the nearby cities.
3 Maccabees 1:7 Having done this and allotted gifts to the sacred precincts, he made his subjects confident.
3 Maccabees 1:8 When the Jews sent to him men from the senate and the elders to greet him and bring gifts of hospitality and congratulate him on what had happened, it happened that he became more eager to visit them as quickly as possible.
3 Maccabees 1:9 Making his way to Hierosolyma and sacrificing to the greatest God and giving thanks and doing something further for the place, and indeed coming to the place and being struck by its dignity and beauty,
3 Maccabees 1:10 and also admiring the good order of the sanctuary, he conceived the intention of entering the temple.
3 Maccabees 1:11 When they said that this ought not to happen, because not even those of the nation were permitted to enter, nor all the priests, but only the high priest who presided over all, and he once a year, he was in no way persuaded.
3 Maccabees 1:12 When the law was read aloud, he did not desist even then, asserting that he ought to enter, saying, “Even if they are deprived of this honor, I ought not to be.”
3 Maccabees 1:13 And he inquired for what reason none of those present had prevented him when he entered every sacred precinct.
3 Maccabees 1:14 And someone heedlessly said that this very thing was wrongly made much of as a marvel.
3 Maccabees 1:15 “But if this happened for some reason,” he says, “will I not certainly enter, whether they wish it or not?”
3 Maccabees 1:16 When the priests fell down in all their vestments and begged the greatest God to aid them in their present circumstances and turn aside the impulse of the one making the wicked attack, and filled the sanctuary with crying and tears,
3 Maccabees 1:17 those remaining throughout the city, disturbed, rushed out, considering what was happening uncertain.
3 Maccabees 1:18 The virgins confined in chambers rushed out with their mothers and, sprinkling their hair, gave it over to dust, and filled the broad streets with lamentation and groans.
3 Maccabees 1:19 Those also who had just been arrayed, abandoning the bridal chambers prepared for the meeting and the appropriate modesty, took to a disorderly course through the city.
3 Maccabees 1:20 The mothers and nurses attending the newborn children abandoned them here and there, some in houses and some in the streets, and gathered without turning back into the supremely exalted sanctuary.
3 Maccabees 1:21 Varied was the supplication of those gathered into it concerning the things impiously undertaken by him.
3 Maccabees 1:22 Together with these, those who had become bold on behalf of the citizens could not endure his pressing on completely and intending to fulfill his purpose,
3 Maccabees 1:23 and, crying out to rush to arms and die boldly for the ancestral law, caused considerable agitation in the place; but, barely turned aside by the aged men and the elders, they came to the same position of supplication.
3 Maccabees 1:24 The multitude continued in these things as before, making supplication.
3 Maccabees 1:25 The elders around the king tried in many ways to turn his haughty mind away from the intended plot.
3 Maccabees 1:26 But, growing bold and dismissing everything, he was already making his approach, thinking to bring the aforementioned matter to completion.
3 Maccabees 1:27 Those around him also, seeing these things, turned to invoking with our people him who possesses all might, to aid those present, not overlooking the lawless and arrogant deed.
3 Maccabees 1:28 From the exceedingly dense and anguished crying of the multitudes gathered together there arose an indescribable clamor;
3 Maccabees 1:29 for it seemed that not only the people, but also the walls and the whole ground resounded, since all were then choosing death in exchange for the profanation of the place.

## Chapter 2

3 Maccabees 2:1 The high priest Simon, bending his knees opposite the temple and stretching out his hands, therefore made this supplication in an orderly manner:
3 Maccabees 2:2 “Lord, Lord, King of the heavens and Master of all creation, holy among holy ones, sole Ruler, Almighty, attend to us, oppressed by an impious and profane man puffed up with audacity and strength.
3 Maccabees 2:3 For you who created all things and rule over everything are a just Sovereign, and judge those who act with insolence and haughtiness.
3 Maccabees 2:4 You destroyed those who formerly committed injustice, among whom were also giants trusting in strength and audacity, bringing immeasurable water upon them.
3 Maccabees 2:5 You burned with fire and sulfur the Sodomites who practiced arrogance and became conspicuous for their wickedness, making them an example for those coming afterward.
3 Maccabees 2:6 You, testing with many and varied punishments the audacious Pharao who had enslaved your holy people Israel, made known your power, whereby you made known your great might;
3 Maccabees 2:7 and when he pursued with chariots and a multitude of crowds, you overwhelmed him in the depth of the sea, but brought safely through those who trusted in you, who rule over all creation,
3 Maccabees 2:8 who also, seeing the works of your hand, praised you, the Almighty.
3 Maccabees 2:9 You, O King, creating the boundless and immeasurable earth, chose this city and sanctified this place for your name, you who need none of all things, and glorified it in a magnificent manifestation, establishing it for the glory of your great and honored name.
3 Maccabees 2:10 Loving the house of Israel, you promised that if we should turn away and distress overtake us, and we should come into this place and supplicate, you would hear our supplication.
3 Maccabees 2:11 And indeed you are faithful and true.
3 Maccabees 2:12 Since, when our fathers were often afflicted, you aided them in their humiliation and rescued them from great evils,
3 Maccabees 2:13 behold now, holy King, because of our many and great sins we are oppressed and have been subjected to our enemies and are enfeebled in weaknesses.
3 Maccabees 2:14 In our downfall this audacious and profane man undertakes to outrage the holy place designated upon earth for the name of your glory.
3 Maccabees 2:15 For your dwelling place is the heaven of heaven, inaccessible to men.
3 Maccabees 2:16 But since, being pleased with your glory among your people Israel, you sanctified this place,
3 Maccabees 2:17 do not punish us through their uncleanness or chastise us through profanation, lest the lawless boast in their anger or exult in the arrogance of their tongue, saying,
3 Maccabees 2:18 ‘We trampled the house of sanctification, as the houses of abominations are trampled.’
3 Maccabees 2:19 Blot out our sins and scatter our errors and manifest your mercy at this hour.
3 Maccabees 2:20 Let your compassions quickly come beforehand to meet us, and put praises in the mouth of those fallen and crushed in soul, making peace for us.”
3 Maccabees 2:21 Then God, the Overseer of all and Forefather, holy among holy ones, hearing the lawful supplication, scourged him who was greatly lifted up in insolence and audacity,
3 Maccabees 2:22 shaking him to and fro like a reed in the wind, so that he lay helpless upon the ground, also paralyzed in his limbs, unable even to speak, struck all around by a just judgment.
3 Maccabees 2:23 Therefore the Friends and bodyguards, seeing the sharp chastisement that had overtaken him and fearing that he might even cease to live, quickly dragged him out, struck with overwhelming fear.
3 Maccabees 2:24 Later, after some time, recovering himself, he in no way came to repentance after being rebuked, but uttered bitter threats and withdrew.
3 Maccabees 2:25 Making his way into Egypt and increasing his wickedness through the previously mentioned drinking companions and associates, separated from all justice,
3 Maccabees 2:26 he was not satisfied merely with countless acts of licentiousness, but advanced to such audacity that ill-speaking arose in the regions, and many of the Friends, looking intently at the king’s purpose, themselves also followed his will.
3 Maccabees 2:27 He proposed to spread public reproach against the nation; setting up a pillar on the tower at the palace, he carved an inscription:
3 Maccabees 2:28 that none of those who did not sacrifice should enter their sanctuaries, and that all the Jews should be brought to registration and the condition of slaves, and that those objecting should be taken by force and removed from life,
3 Maccabees 2:29 and those registered should also be marked on the body by fire with an ivy leaf, the emblem of Dionysos, and enrolled under the previously stipulated authority.
3 Maccabees 2:30 But so that he might not appear hateful to all, he added underneath: “If any of them choose to associate with those initiated in the rites, these shall be equal citizens with the Alexandrians.”
3 Maccabees 2:31 Some therefore, superficially loathing the foundations of the city’s piety, readily gave themselves over, as though they would share some great glory from their coming association with the king.
3 Maccabees 2:32 But most held firm with noble soul and did not depart from piety, and, exchanging their possessions for their life, fearlessly tried to rescue themselves from the registrations;
3 Maccabees 2:33 and they remained hopeful of obtaining help, and abhorred those departing from them and judged them as enemies of the nation, and deprived them of common association and beneficial services.

## Chapter 3

3 Maccabees 3:1 Learning these things, the impious man became so enraged that he was not only furious with those in Alexandreia, but opposed those in the country more grievously, and commanded that they hasten to gather all into the same place and remove them from life by the worst fate.
3 Maccabees 3:2 While these things were being arranged, a hostile report resounded against the people through men united in purpose for evildoing, an occasion being given for their disposition, as though the Jews were preventing them from their lawful customs.
3 Maccabees 3:3 But the Jews had been maintaining unwavering goodwill and faithfulness toward the kings,
3 Maccabees 3:4 and, revering God and conducting their life by his law, kept separate in matters of food, for which reason they appeared hateful to some.
3 Maccabees 3:5 But, adorning their association by the good practice of just deeds, they had become well esteemed by all men.
3 Maccabees 3:6 The foreigners therefore in no way took account of the good conduct of the people, talked of among all,
3 Maccabees 3:7 but kept talking of the difference concerning acts of worship and foods, asserting that these men were allied by treaty neither with the king nor with the forces, but were hostile and greatly opposed affairs; and they attached no ordinary reproach to them.
3 Maccabees 3:8 The Greeks throughout the city, having suffered no wrong, seeing unexpected disturbance concerning these men and heedless gatherings taking place, had no strength to help, for the disposition was tyrannical, but encouraged them and were distressed and supposed that these things would change;
3 Maccabees 3:9 for so great a body, having done nothing wrong, would not be overlooked in this manner.
3 Maccabees 3:10 Already some neighbors and friends and business associates, drawing some aside secretly, gave assurances that they would stand alongside them and bring every earnest effort to their assistance.
3 Maccabees 3:11 He therefore, elated by his present success and not perceiving the might of the greatest God, but supposing that he would continually persist in the same purpose, wrote this letter against them:
3 Maccabees 3:12 “King Ptolemaios Philopator to the generals and soldiers throughout Egypt and in each place, greetings and health;
3 Maccabees 3:13 I myself also am well, and our affairs are well.
3 Maccabees 3:14 Our campaign into Asia, of which you yourselves also know, having been brought duly to completion through the unfailing alliance of the gods,
3 Maccabees 3:15 we thought to nurture the nations inhabiting Coele Syria and Phoinike, not by force of the spear, but by equity and much humanity, and gladly to benefit them.
3 Maccabees 3:16 Allotting very great revenues to the sanctuaries in each city, we proceeded also to go up to Hierosolyma and honor the sanctuary of the offenders who never cease from folly.
3 Maccabees 3:17 They welcomed our presence in word, but in deed insincerely, and when we were eager to enter their temple and honor it with distinguished and most beautiful offerings,
3 Maccabees 3:18 carried away by ancient conceits, they excluded us from entry, falling short of our strength because of the humanity we have toward all men.
3 Maccabees 3:19 Making their hostility toward us evident, as though they alone among the nations lift their necks against kings and their own benefactors, they are unwilling to offer anything genuine.
3 Maccabees 3:20 But we, bearing with their folly and making our way with victory into Egypt, treated all nations humanely, doing as was fitting,
3 Maccabees 3:21 and among these made our freedom from resentment toward their fellow tribesmen known to all; and, because of their alliance and the countless affairs entrusted to them with simplicity from the beginning, daring to alter matters, we wished also to deem them worthy of Alexandrian citizenship and make them participants in the perpetual sacred rites.
3 Maccabees 3:22 But they, taking the contrary view and rejecting what is good through their innate ill nature, and continually inclining toward what is base,
3 Maccabees 3:23 not only turned away from the priceless citizenship, but also abhor in word and silence the few among them genuinely disposed toward us, at every turn suspecting that we will quickly overthrow their affairs, with their most inglorious manner of life.
3 Maccabees 3:24 Therefore, well persuaded by proofs that these men are ill-disposed toward us in every manner, and taking thought lest, if sudden disturbance should arise for us afterward, we have these impious men behind us as traitors and barbarous enemies,
3 Maccabees 3:25 we have commanded that, as soon as this letter arrives, immediately those dwelling there, with wives and children, be sent to us with insults and maltreatment, confined on every side in iron bonds, for an irremediable and inglorious slaughter fitting for enemies.
3 Maccabees 3:26 For with these punished together, we have determined that for the remaining time our affairs will be established completely in stability and the best condition.
3 Maccabees 3:27 Whoever shelters any of the Jews, from an aged man to an infant and even those at the breast, will be beaten to death with the most disgraceful tortures, together with his whole household.
3 Maccabees 3:28 Let whoever wishes inform, on condition that he shall receive the property of the one falling under the punishment and two thousand silver drachmas from the royal treasury, and shall be crowned with freedom.
3 Maccabees 3:29 Every place where a Jew is found sheltered at all shall become inaccessible and burned with fire, and shall appear wholly useless to every mortal creature for all time.”
3 Maccabees 3:30 And the form of the letter had been written thus.

## Chapter 4

3 Maccabees 4:1 Everywhere this ordinance arrived, a public banquet arose among the nations with shouts and joy, as the hatred long hardened in their minds now appeared openly.
3 Maccabees 4:2 But for the Jews there was unceasing grief and a wholly lamentable cry with tears, their hearts everywhere inflamed with groans as they lamented the unexpected destruction suddenly decreed against them.
3 Maccabees 4:3 What district or city or inhabited place at all, or what streets, were not filled with beating of breasts and lamentations for them?
3 Maccabees 4:4 For they were sent away with such bitterness of a merciless soul by the generals in each city, all with one accord, that even some of their enemies, in view of the extraordinary punishments, placing common compassion before their eyes and considering the uncertain end of life, wept at their most miserable deportation.
3 Maccabees 4:5 For a multitude of aged men, covered with gray hair, was led along, their stooping slowness of feet from old age being driven to a swift march by the impulse of violent overthrow, without any respect.
3 Maccabees 4:6 The young women who had just entered the bridal chamber for partnership of life, receiving lamentations instead of delight and mingling their perfume-soaked hair with dust, and being led unveiled, began a lament together instead of wedding songs, as though torn apart by maltreatment from foreign nations;
3 Maccabees 4:7 and bound in public, they were dragged by force until their embarkation into the ship.
3 Maccabees 4:8 Their spouses also, their necks entangled in nooses instead of wreaths, in the prime of youthful age, passed the remaining days of their wedding in lamentations instead of feasting and youthful ease, already seeing Hades lying at their feet.
3 Maccabees 4:9 They were brought down, led like beasts in constraints of iron bonds, some fastened by their necks to the beams of the ships, others secured by their feet in unbreakable fetters,
3 Maccabees 4:10 and with dense planking placed overhead also, so that, their eyes darkened on every side, they might receive the treatment of those plotted against throughout the whole voyage downstream.
3 Maccabees 4:11 When they were brought to the place called Schedia and the voyage was completed, as had been decreed by the king, he commanded them to encamp in the hippodrome before the city, which had an immense circumference and was most suitable for making a public example to all entering the city and those of them departing into the country on a journey, so that they might neither associate with his forces nor be deemed worthy of enclosures at all.
3 Maccabees 4:12 When this happened, hearing that their fellow countrymen from the city were coming out secretly more frequently to lament the inglorious misery of their brothers,
3 Maccabees 4:13 he became furious and commanded that these also be treated together carefully in the same manner as those, falling short of their punishment in no way,
3 Maccabees 4:14 and that the whole tribe be registered by name, not for the laborious service of work mentioned briefly a little before, but that, tortured by the ordered outrages, they should finally be annihilated within the space of one day.
3 Maccabees 4:15 Their registration therefore took place with bitter haste and ambitious persistence from sunrise until sunset for forty days, its completion remaining unaccomplished.
3 Maccabees 4:16 The king, greatly and continually filled with joy, held drinking parties before all the idols, with a mind wandering far from truth and a profane mouth, praising the dumb things unable to speak to them or aid them, but speaking things unfitting against the greatest God.
3 Maccabees 4:17 After the aforementioned interval of time, the scribes reported to the king that they were no longer able to make the registration of the Jews because of their immeasurable multitude,
3 Maccabees 4:18 although most were still throughout the country, some still gathered in houses and others in the locality, as the task had become impossible for all the generals over Egypt.
3 Maccabees 4:19 When he threatened them more harshly, as having been bribed to contrive an escape, it happened that he was clearly assured concerning this,
3 Maccabees 4:20 when they stated with proof that both the writing material and the writing reeds they used had already run out.
3 Maccabees 4:21 This was the working of the invincible providence of him who aids the Jews from heaven.

## Chapter 5

3 Maccabees 5:1 Then, summoning Hermon, who attended to the care of the elephants, filled with heavy anger and wholly inflexible in his rage,
3 Maccabees 5:2 he commanded that for the coming day all the elephants, five hundred in number, be given abundant handfuls of frankincense and much unmixed wine to drink, and, made savage by the plentiful provision of the drink, be brought in to meet the doom of the Jews.
3 Maccabees 5:3 Giving these orders, he turned to the banquet, gathering those of the Friends and the army who were most hostile toward the Jews.
3 Maccabees 5:4 Hermon, the commander of the elephants, carried out the command firmly.
3 Maccabees 5:5 The servants attending these matters went out in the evening and bound the hands of the afflicted, and contrived the rest of their security for the night, thinking that the tribe would together receive the end of its destruction.
3 Maccabees 5:6 But the Jews, who seemed to the nations to be bereft of all protection because of the constraint encompassing them on every side with bonds,
3 Maccabees 5:7 all invoked with tears and a cry difficult to silence the Almighty Lord, who rules over every power, their merciful God and Father, begging
3 Maccabees 5:8 him to turn aside the impious purpose against them and rescue them by a magnificent manifestation from the doom ready at their feet.
3 Maccabees 5:9 Their supplication therefore ascended earnestly into heaven.
3 Maccabees 5:10 Hermon, having given drink to the pitiless elephants, filled with the plentiful supply of wine and saturated with frankincense, came to the palace early to report these things to the king.
3 Maccabees 5:11 But a portion of sleep, the beautiful creation from eternal time, bestowed in night and day by him who grants it to all whom he wishes, he sent upon the king,
3 Maccabees 5:12 and he was held in most pleasant and deep sleep by the working of the Master, greatly thwarted in his lawless purpose and greatly disappointed in his inflexible intention.
3 Maccabees 5:13 The Jews, escaping the previously indicated hour, praised their holy God and again asked him, readily reconciled, to show the might of his very powerful hand to arrogant nations.
3 Maccabees 5:14 When it was already nearly the middle of the tenth hour, the one assigned to the invitations, seeing the invited guests gathered together, approached and nudged the king.
3 Maccabees 5:15 Barely awakening him, he pointed out that the time for the drinking party was already passing, making his report about these things.
3 Maccabees 5:16 The king, considering it and turning to drinking, commanded those who had come to the drinking party to recline opposite him.
3 Maccabees 5:17 When this had happened, he urged them to give themselves to feasting and, being greatly honored, devote the present portion of the drinking party to gladness.
3 Maccabees 5:18 As the conversation proceeded further, the king summoned Hermon and with a bitter threat inquired for what reason the Jews had been allowed to survive the remaining day.
3 Maccabees 5:19 When he pointed out that he had brought the command to completion while it was still night, and the Friends also bore witness to him,
3 Maccabees 5:20 he, possessing cruelty worse than Phalaris, said that they owed thanks to today’s sleep; “But without delay prepare the elephants in the same manner for the following day, for the annihilation of the unlawful Jews.”
3 Maccabees 5:21 When the king had spoken, all those present gladly agreed together with joy, and each withdrew to his own house.
3 Maccabees 5:22 They used the time of night not so much for sleep as for devising every kind of mockery against those thought wretched.
3 Maccabees 5:23 The cock had just crowed early, and Hermon, having armed the beasts, was moving them about in the great colonnade.
3 Maccabees 5:24 The multitudes throughout the city had gathered for the most pitiable spectacle, eagerly awaiting the morning.
3 Maccabees 5:25 The Jews, their souls being drawn out at each indivisible moment, stretching their hands to heaven in a supplication full of tears and lamenting songs, begged the greatest God again to help them speedily.
3 Maccabees 5:26 The rays of the sun had not yet spread, and while the king awaited the Friends, Hermon came forward and called him to go out, pointing out that the king’s eager desire lay ready.
3 Maccabees 5:27 Receiving him and being astonished at the lawless departure, wholly possessed by ignorance, he inquired what the matter was for which this had been eagerly accomplished for him;
3 Maccabees 5:28 this was the working of God, who rules over all, having placed in his mind forgetfulness of the things previously contrived by him.
3 Maccabees 5:29 Hermon and all the Friends explained, “The beasts and the forces have been prepared, O king, according to your earnest purpose.”
3 Maccabees 5:30 Filled with heavy rage at what was said, because through God’s providence all his thought concerning these things had been scattered, he looked intently with a threat and said:
3 Maccabees 5:31 “Whatever parents were present or offspring of children, I would have prepared these as an abundant feast for wild beasts instead of the blameless Jews, who have shown exceptionally complete and steadfast faithfulness to me and my ancestors.
3 Maccabees 5:32 Indeed, were it not for the affection of our upbringing together and your service, you would have been deprived of life instead of these.”
3 Maccabees 5:33 Thus Hermon endured an unexpected dangerous threat, and shrank in gaze and countenance.
3 Maccabees 5:34 Each of the Friends slipped out gloomily, and they dismissed those gathered, each to his own occupation.
3 Maccabees 5:35 The Jews, hearing the things from the king, praised the manifest God, Lord, King of kings, having obtained this help from him also.
3 Maccabees 5:36 According to the same customs, the king assembled the whole drinking party and encouraged them to turn to gladness.
3 Maccabees 5:37 Summoning Hermon, he said with a threat, “How many times must I command you about these very things, most wretched man?
3 Maccabees 5:38 Arm the elephants yet again now for tomorrow, for the annihilation of the Jews.”
3 Maccabees 5:39 The kinsmen reclining with him, wondering at his unstable mind, put forward these words:
3 Maccabees 5:40 “O king, how long do you test us as irrational men, commanding now for the third time that they be annihilated, and again, when it comes to the matter, changing and dissolving your decrees?
3 Maccabees 5:41 Because of these things the city is disturbed by the expectation and, filled with gatherings, already often runs the risk of being plundered.”
3 Maccabees 5:42 Therefore the king, a Phalaris in every respect, filled with recklessness and regarding as nothing the changes of soul arising in him for the visitation of the Jews, firmly declaring a most unfulfilled oath, said that he would send them without delay to Hades, mangled by the knees and feet of beasts,
3 Maccabees 5:43 and, campaigning against Ioudaia, would quickly level it with fire and spear, and would swiftly cast their temple, inaccessible to us, headlong by fire, and make it bereft forever of those performing sacrifices there.
3 Maccabees 5:44 Then the Friends and kinsmen, departing overjoyed, confidently stationed the forces in the most suitable places of the city for guarding.
3 Maccabees 5:45 The commander of the elephants, having brought the beasts almost, so to speak, into a maddened condition with most fragrant drinks of wine infused with frankincense, fearfully adorned with equipment,
3 Maccabees 5:46 entered the palace around dawn, the city already filled with countless multitudes toward the hippodrome, and urged the king on to the matter proposed.
3 Maccabees 5:47 Filling his impious mind with heavy anger, he set out with all his weight together with the beasts, wishing with unwounded heart and the pupils of his eyes to behold the painful and miserable destruction of those previously indicated.
3 Maccabees 5:48 When the elephants were going out near the gate, and the armed force followed and the multitude marched, the Jews, seeing the dust and hearing the deep-sounding tumult,
3 Maccabees 5:49 thinking that this was their last moment of life, the end of their most wretched expectation, turned to compassion and lamentations and kissed one another, embracing their relatives and falling upon their necks, parents upon children and mothers upon young women, while others held newborn infants at their breasts, drawing milk for the last time.
3 Maccabees 5:50 Nevertheless, also perceiving the helps from heaven that had previously come to them, they threw themselves face down with one accord and separated the infants from their breasts,
3 Maccabees 5:51 and cried out with an exceedingly loud voice, supplicating the Sovereign of all power to pity them with a manifestation, already standing at the gates of Hades.

## Chapter 6
