3 Maccabees 6:1 A certain Eleazaros, a distinguished man among the priests from the country, already having attained old age and adorned with every virtue in life, quieted the elders around him to invoke the holy God, and prayed these things:
3 Maccabees 6:2 “King of great might, Most High, Almighty God, governing all creation with compassions,
3 Maccabees 6:3 look upon the seed of Abraam, upon the children of sanctified Iakob, the people of your sanctified portion, strangers in a foreign land being unjustly destroyed, O Father.
3 Maccabees 6:4 You destroyed Pharao, abounding in chariots, the former sovereign of this Egypt, lifted up with lawless audacity and a boastful tongue, together with his arrogant army, drowned in the sea, manifesting a light of mercy to the people of Israel.
3 Maccabees 6:5 You shattered Sennacherim, the grievous king of the Assyrians, elated by countless forces, already having taken all the earth under his hand by the spear and lifted up against your holy city, speaking grievous things with boasting and audacity; you, Master, showed your might manifest to many nations.
3 Maccabees 6:6 You rescued the three companions in Babylonia, who voluntarily gave their lives to fire so as not to serve vain things, cooling the fiery furnace and leaving them unharmed to a hair, sending flame upon all the adversaries.
3 Maccabees 6:7 You brought Daniel unharmed up into the light, who through envious slanders had been thrown underground to lions as food for beasts.
3 Maccabees 6:8 And, seeing Ionas wasting away in the belly of a sea creature nurtured in the depths, you showed him unharmed to all his own people, O Father.
3 Maccabees 6:9 And now, Hater of insolence, abundantly merciful Protector of all, quickly manifest yourself to those of the people of Israel, outraged by abhorred lawless nations.
3 Maccabees 6:10 If our life in our settlement abroad has become entangled in impieties, rescue us from the hand of enemies and destroy us by whatever fate you choose, Master.
3 Maccabees 6:11 Do not let the vain-minded bless vain things over the destruction of your beloved, saying, ‘Not even their God rescued them.’
3 Maccabees 6:12 But you, eternal One possessing all strength and all sovereignty, look now; have mercy on us, who are being removed from life by the reckless insolence of lawless men, in the manner of those plotted against.
3 Maccabees 6:13 Let nations cower before your invincible power today, honored One possessing power for the salvation of the people of Iakob.
3 Maccabees 6:14 The whole multitude of infants and their parents supplicate you with tears.
3 Maccabees 6:15 Let it be shown to all nations that you are with us, Lord, and have not turned your face away from us; but as you said, ‘Not even when they were in the land of their enemies did I overlook them,’ so accomplish it, Lord.”
3 Maccabees 6:16 As Eleazaros was just ending the prayer, the king came along toward the hippodrome with the beasts and all the arrogance of his force.
3 Maccabees 6:17 Seeing him, the Jews cried aloud greatly to heaven, so that the neighboring valleys also resounded and caused an uncontrollable terror in the whole camp.
3 Maccabees 6:18 Then the greatly glorious Almighty and true God, manifesting his holy face, opened the heavenly gates, from which two glorified angels of fearful appearance descended, visible to all except the Jews,
3 Maccabees 6:19 and stood against them and filled the force of the adversaries with turmoil and cowardice and bound them with immovable fetters.
3 Maccabees 6:20 The king’s body also became shuddering, and forgetfulness seized his fiercely angry audacity.
3 Maccabees 6:21 They turned the beasts against the armed forces following, and they trampled and destroyed them.
3 Maccabees 6:22 The king’s anger changed to compassion and tears concerning the things previously contrived by him.
3 Maccabees 6:23 For, hearing the cry and seeing them all face down for destruction, weeping, he threatened the Friends with anger, saying:
3 Maccabees 6:24 “You usurp kingship and have surpassed tyrants in cruelty, and already attempt to remove me myself, your benefactor, from office and from breath, secretly contriving things unprofitable for the kingdom.
3 Maccabees 6:25 Who, removing each from his home, irrationally gathered here those who faithfully held the fortifications of our country?
3 Maccabees 6:26 Who so lawlessly surrounded with outrages those who from the beginning surpassed all nations in every respect in goodwill toward us, and often underwent the worst dangers among men?
3 Maccabees 6:27 Loose, release the unjust bonds; send them to their own homes with peace, asking pardon for the things previously done.
3 Maccabees 6:28 Release the sons of the Almighty heavenly living God, who from our ancestors until now grants unhindered stability with glory to our affairs.”
3 Maccabees 6:29 He therefore spoke these things; and they, released in an indivisible moment, blessed their holy Savior God, having just escaped death.
3 Maccabees 6:30 Then the king, departing into the city, summoned the one over revenues and commanded that wines and the other supplies for a banquet be provided to the Jews for seven days, deciding that in the place where they had thought to receive destruction, in this place they should celebrate deliverance with all gladness.
3 Maccabees 6:31 Then those formerly reproached and near Hades, or rather having stepped upon it, instead of a bitter and grievously lamentable fate, held a drinking feast for deliverance and, full of joy, apportioned with reclining places the place prepared for their downfall and grave.
3 Maccabees 6:32 Ceasing the wholly lamentable melody of dirges, they took up an ancestral song, praising God, their Savior and Wonder-worker; and, dismissing all wailing and shrieking, they formed dances as a sign of peaceful gladness.
3 Maccabees 6:33 Likewise the king also, gathering a great drinking party for these things, continually made magnificent acknowledgment toward heaven for the unexpected deliverance that had occurred for him.
3 Maccabees 6:34 Those who formerly supposed that they would be destroyed and eaten by birds, and had registered them with joy, groaned, clothing themselves with shame, their fire-breathing audacity ingloriously extinguished.
3 Maccabees 6:35 The Jews, as we have said before, forming the aforementioned dance, passed their time with feasting in cheerful acknowledgments and psalms.
3 Maccabees 6:36 Determining a common ordinance concerning these things throughout their whole settlement abroad for generations, they established the observance of the aforementioned days with gladness, not for drinking and gluttony, but for the deliverance which had come to them through God.
3 Maccabees 6:37 They petitioned the king, asking for their release to their own homes.
3 Maccabees 6:38 They register them from the twenty-fifth of Pachon until the fourth of Epiphi, for forty days, and arrange their destruction from the fifth of Epiphi until the seventh, for three days,
3 Maccabees 6:39 in which the Sovereign of all, gloriously manifesting his mercy, rescued them all together without stumbling.
3 Maccabees 6:40 They feasted, everything being supplied by the king, until the fourteenth, on which they also made the petition concerning their release.
3 Maccabees 6:41 Agreeing with them, the king wrote for them the letter written below to the generals in each city, conveying his earnest concern magnanimously:

## Chapter 7

3 Maccabees 7:1 “King Ptolemaios Philopator to the generals throughout Egypt and all those appointed over affairs, greetings and health;
3 Maccabees 7:2 we ourselves and our children are well, the great God having directed affairs for us as we choose.
3 Maccabees 7:3 Some of the Friends, through ill nature, persistently pressing upon us, persuaded us to gather the Jews under the kingdom as a body and punish them with extraordinary punishments of rebels,
3 Maccabees 7:4 asserting that our affairs would never be stable until this was accomplished, because of the hostility these men have toward all nations.
3 Maccabees 7:5 They brought them down bound with maltreatment, as slaves, or rather as plotters, and without any inquiry or examination attempted to kill them, having clothed themselves with cruelty more savage than the custom of Scythians.
3 Maccabees 7:6 But we, threatening them more harshly concerning these things, according to the equity we have toward all men, barely granting them life, and recognizing that the heavenly God has securely defended the Jews, continually fighting for them as a father for sons,
3 Maccabees 7:7 and considering the steadfast goodwill of a friend which they have toward us and our ancestors, have justly released them from every accusation in whatever manner,
3 Maccabees 7:8 and have commanded everyone that all should return to their own homes in every place, no one harming them at all or reproaching them for the things that happened contrary to reason.
3 Maccabees 7:9 For know that if we wickedly contrive any evil against these men or distress them at all, we will have opposing us, not a man, but the Most High God who rules over every power, for vengeance upon affairs, in every respect inescapably and continually. Farewell.”
3 Maccabees 7:10 Receiving this letter, they did not hasten immediately to attend to their departure, but further requested the king that those of the Jewish people who had voluntarily transgressed against the holy God and the law of God should receive through them the punishment owed,
3 Maccabees 7:11 asserting that those who had transgressed the divine ordinances for the sake of the belly would never be well-disposed even toward the king’s affairs.
3 Maccabees 7:12 He, accepting that they spoke the truth and approving, gave them permission for everything, so that they might openly destroy those who had transgressed God’s law throughout every place under his kingdom, without any royal authorization or oversight.
3 Maccabees 7:13 Then, acclaiming him as was fitting, their priests and the whole multitude shouted the allelouia and departed with joy.
3 Maccabees 7:14 Thus they punished any defiled fellow countryman they encountered along the road and killed them with public examples.
3 Maccabees 7:15 On that day they killed more than three hundred men, and celebrated it with gladness and joy, having subdued the profane.
3 Maccabees 7:16 Those who themselves had held to God until death, receiving complete enjoyment of deliverance, departed from the city crowned with every kind of most fragrant flower, with gladness and shouting, in praises and hymns of every melody, giving thanks to the God of their fathers, the eternal Savior of Israel.
3 Maccabees 7:17 Arriving in Ptolemais, called rose-bearing because of the character of the place, where the fleet waited for them seven days according to their common decision,
3 Maccabees 7:18 they held there a drinking feast for deliverance, the king having generously supplied them with everything for each one’s arrival as far as his own home.
3 Maccabees 7:19 Landing with peace and fitting acknowledgments, they likewise established there also the observance of these days with gladness during the time of their settlement abroad.
3 Maccabees 7:20 Consecrating these days on a pillar and establishing a place of prayer at the place of the drinking party, they departed unharmed, free, exceedingly joyful, brought safely back by land and sea and river at the king’s command, each to his own home,
3 Maccabees 7:21 and possessing much greater authority among their enemies than before, with glory and fear, being deprived of none of their possessions by extortion at all.
3 Maccabees 7:22 All recovered all their own things according to the registration, so that those who possessed anything restored it to them with the greatest fear, the greatest God having perfectly accomplished great deeds for their deliverance.
3 Maccabees 7:23 Blessed is the Rescuer of Israel for all time. Amen.

# 4 Maccabees

The Apostolic Bible. Public domain. https://apostolic-bible.ysys9.chatgpt.site/license.html


## Chapter 1

4 Maccabees 1:1 About to present a most philosophical discourse, whether pious reason is sovereign over the passions, I would rightly advise you to attend eagerly to philosophy.
4 Maccabees 1:2 For the discourse is necessary for knowledge to everyone, and moreover contains praise of the greatest virtue, I mean prudence.
4 Maccabees 1:3 If therefore reason appears to prevail over the passions hindering temperance, both gluttony and desire,
4 Maccabees 1:4 it also manifestly rules over the passions obstructing justice, such as ill nature, and the passions obstructing courage, anger and fear and pain.
4 Maccabees 1:5 “How then,” some might perhaps say, “if reason masters the passions, does it not rule over forgetfulness and ignorance?” attempting to say something ridiculous.
4 Maccabees 1:6 For reason does not master its own passions, but those opposed to justice and courage and temperance, and these not so as to abolish them, but so as not to yield to them.
4 Maccabees 1:7 From many sources and elsewhere I could therefore show you that reason is ruler over the passions,
4 Maccabees 1:8 but much more could I demonstrate this from the valor of those who died for virtue, Eleazaros and the seven brothers and their mother.
4 Maccabees 1:9 For all these, disregarding pains unto death, demonstrated that reason completely masters the passions.
4 Maccabees 1:10 For their virtues therefore it falls to me to praise the men who at this time died with their mother for nobility and goodness, and for their honors I would call them blessed.
4 Maccabees 1:11 For, admired not only by all men for their courage and endurance, but also by their tormentors, they became responsible for the overthrow of the tyranny against the nation, conquering the tyrant by endurance, so that the homeland was purified through them.
4 Maccabees 1:12 But it will be possible to speak about this presently also, beginning with the subject, as I am accustomed to do; and thus I will turn to the discourse concerning them, giving glory to the all-wise God.
4 Maccabees 1:13 We therefore inquire whether reason is ruler over the passions.
4 Maccabees 1:14 We distinguish what reason is and what passion is, and how many forms of passions there are, and whether reason prevails over all these.
4 Maccabees 1:15 Reason therefore is a mind which with right reasoning prefers the life of wisdom.
4 Maccabees 1:16 Wisdom therefore is knowledge of divine and human matters and their causes.
4 Maccabees 1:17 This therefore is the instruction of the law, through which we learn divine matters reverently and human matters profitably.
4 Maccabees 1:18 The forms of wisdom are prudence and justice and courage and temperance;
4 Maccabees 1:19 most authoritative of all is prudence, through which reason prevails over the passions.
4 Maccabees 1:20 The two most comprehensive natures of passions are pleasure and pain; each of these naturally concerns both body and soul.
4 Maccabees 1:21 There are also many sequences of passions concerning pleasure and pain.
4 Maccabees 1:22 Before pleasure therefore is desire, and after pleasure joy.
4 Maccabees 1:23 Before pain is fear, and after pain grief.
4 Maccabees 1:24 Anger is a passion common to pleasure and pain, if one considers that he has fallen into it.
4 Maccabees 1:25 In pleasure there is also the ill-natured disposition, which is the most varied of all passions,
4 Maccabees 1:26 and those of the soul are arrogance and love of money and love of glory and contentiousness and envy,
4 Maccabees 1:27 and concerning the body, eating everything and greediness and eating alone.
4 Maccabees 1:28 As therefore there are two plants of body and soul, pleasure and pain, there are many offshoots of these plants,
4 Maccabees 1:29 each of which reason, the universal cultivator, cleanses and prunes and binds and waters and tends in every manner, taming the woodlands of dispositions and passions.
4 Maccabees 1:30 For reason is leader of the virtues and ruler of the passions. Observe therefore first, through the deeds hindering temperance, that reason is sovereign over the passions.
4 Maccabees 1:31 Temperance therefore is mastery of desires,
4 Maccabees 1:32 and of desires some belong to the soul and others to the body, and reason appears to prevail over both these.
4 Maccabees 1:33 For why, when moved toward forbidden foods, do we turn away from their pleasures? Is it not because reason can prevail over appetites? I think so.
4 Maccabees 1:34 Therefore, desiring aquatic creatures and birds and quadrupeds and every kind of food forbidden us according to the law, we abstain through the mastery of reason.
4 Maccabees 1:35 For the passions of appetites are restrained, checked by the temperate mind, and all the movements of the body are muzzled by reason.

## Chapter 2

4 Maccabees 2:1 And what is wondrous if the desires of the soul for participation in beauty are annulled?
4 Maccabees 2:2 In this respect therefore the temperate Ioseph is praised, because by thought he completely mastered sensual pleasure.
4 Maccabees 2:3 For, being young and in his prime for intercourse, he annulled by reason the frenzy of the passions.
4 Maccabees 2:4 Reason appears to prevail not only over the maddening impulse of sensual pleasure, but also over every desire.
4 Maccabees 2:5 The law therefore says, “You shall not desire your neighbor’s wife, nor whatever belongs to your neighbor.”
4 Maccabees 2:6 And indeed, since the law has told us not to desire, I could much more persuade you that reason can master desires. Likewise also the passions hindering justice;
4 Maccabees 2:7 for in what manner is someone whose character is to eat alone and be gluttonous, or also drunken, reeducated, unless it is clear that reason is master of the passions?
4 Maccabees 2:8 For immediately, conducting his life by the law, even if someone loves money, he constrains his own manner, lending to those in need without interest and canceling the loan when the seventh periods arrive;
4 Maccabees 2:9 and even if someone is miserly, he is mastered by the law through reason, neither gleaning his harvests nor gathering the remaining grapes of his vineyards. In the other matters also it is possible to recognize this, that reason masters the passions;
4 Maccabees 2:10 for the law also masters goodwill toward parents, not betraying virtue for their sake,
4 Maccabees 2:11 and prevails over affection toward a wife, reproving her because of lawlessness,
4 Maccabees 2:12 and rules over affection for children, punishing them because of wickedness,
4 Maccabees 2:13 and governs familiarity with friends, exposing them because of evil.
4 Maccabees 2:14 And do not suppose it unexpected, since reason can also prevail over enmity through the law, neither cutting down the cultivated plants of enemies, but preserving the things of enemies for those who lost them and helping raise those that have fallen.
4 Maccabees 2:15 Reason also appears to master the more violent passions, love of rule and vainglory and arrogance and boasting and envy;
4 Maccabees 2:16 for the temperate mind repels all these ill-natured passions, as also anger; for it rules over this also.
4 Maccabees 2:17 Indeed Moyses, angry against Dathan and Abiron, did nothing against them in anger, but regulated his anger by reason.
4 Maccabees 2:18 For the temperate mind is able, as I said, to excel against the passions and alter some of them, and also annul others.
4 Maccabees 2:19 For why does our all-wise father Iakob blame those around Symeon and Leui, who slaughtered the Sikimites as a whole nation without reason, saying, “Accursed is their anger”?
4 Maccabees 2:20 For if reason could not master anger, he would not have spoken thus.
4 Maccabees 2:21 For when God fashioned man, he planted his passions and dispositions around him;
4 Maccabees 2:22 and when he enthroned above all the holy leader, the mind, through the organs of sense,
4 Maccabees 2:23 he also gave it a law, according to which, conducting its life, it will reign with a temperate and just and good and courageous reign.
4 Maccabees 2:24 “How then,” someone might say, “if reason is master of the passions, does it not master forgetfulness and ignorance?”

## Chapter 3

4 Maccabees 3:1 But the argument is altogether ridiculous; for reason appears to prevail not over its own passions, but over those of the body.
4 Maccabees 3:2 For example, none of us can cut out desire, but reason can provide that one not be enslaved to desire.
4 Maccabees 3:3 One cannot cut anger out of your soul, but it is possible for reason to help with anger.
4 Maccabees 3:4 None of us can cut out ill nature, but reason could fight alongside us so that we not be bent by ill nature;
4 Maccabees 3:5 for reason is not an uprooter of the passions, but an antagonist.
4 Maccabees 3:6 It is therefore possible to consider this more clearly through the thirst of King Dauid.
4 Maccabees 3:7 For when Dauid, attacking the foreigners throughout a whole day, killed many of them with the soldiers of the nation,
4 Maccabees 3:8 then, when evening came, sweating and exceedingly weary, he came to the royal tent, around which the whole army of our ancestors had encamped.
4 Maccabees 3:9 All the others therefore were at supper,
4 Maccabees 3:10 but the king, exceedingly thirsty, although having abundant springs, could not cure his thirst through them,
4 Maccabees 3:11 but an irrational desire for the water among the enemies intensified and parched him, and weakened and burned him.
4 Maccabees 3:12 Therefore, when the shield-bearers lamented the king’s desire, two young strong soldiers, respecting the king’s desire, armed themselves with their full equipment and, taking a pitcher, crossed the enemies’ palisades,
4 Maccabees 3:13 and, escaping the notice of the guards at the gates, went through, searching throughout the whole camp of the enemies,
4 Maccabees 3:14 and, discovering the spring, boldly brought the drink from it to the king;
4 Maccabees 3:15 but he, although burning with thirst, reasoned that a drink reckoned equivalent to blood was a most terrible danger to the soul,
4 Maccabees 3:16 and therefore, setting reason against desire, poured the drink as a libation to God.
4 Maccabees 3:17 For the temperate mind is able to conquer the compulsions of the passions and extinguish the inflammations of frenzy,
4 Maccabees 3:18 and wrestle down the exceedingly great pains of bodies, and through the nobility and goodness of reason spit away all the dominions of the passions.
4 Maccabees 3:19 Now the occasion also calls us to the demonstration from history of temperate reason.
4 Maccabees 3:20 For since our fathers had deep peace through good observance of law and prospered, so that even Seleukos Nikanor, king of Asia, allotted them money for sacred service and accepted their constitution,
4 Maccabees 3:21 then some, introducing innovations against the common concord, experienced manifold calamities.

## Chapter 4

4 Maccabees 4:1 For a certain Simon, opposing Onias, who then held the high priesthood for life, a fine and good man, since by slandering in every manner he was unable to harm him before the nation, went away as a fugitive to betray the homeland.
4 Maccabees 4:2 Therefore, coming to Apollonios, the general of Syria and Phoinike and Kilikia, he said:
4 Maccabees 4:3 “Being well-disposed toward the king’s affairs, I come reporting that many tens of thousands in private funds have been stored in the treasuries of Hierosolyma, not belonging to the sacred funds, and that these belong to King Seleukos.”
4 Maccabees 4:4 Learning each of these things, Apollonios praises Simon for his care toward the king, and, going up to Seleukos, reported the treasure of funds.
4 Maccabees 4:5 Receiving authority concerning them, quickly into our homeland with the accursed Simon and a most grievous army,
4 Maccabees 4:6 he came and said he had arrived by the king’s commands to take the private funds of the treasury.
4 Maccabees 4:7 The nation lamented and objected to the statement, and, considering it most terrible if those who entrusted deposits to the sacred treasury should be deprived, they prevented him as far as possible.
4 Maccabees 4:8 But Apollonios went into the sanctuary with threats.
4 Maccabees 4:9 When the priests with women and children in the sanctuary supplicated God to defend the sacred place being treated with contempt,
4 Maccabees 4:10 and Apollonios went up with his fully armed army to seize the funds, mounted angels appeared beforehand from heaven, flashing all around with their arms and instilling much fear and trembling in them.
4 Maccabees 4:11 Indeed Apollonios, falling half dead upon the sanctuary’s enclosure for all tribes, stretched his hands toward heaven and with tears exhorted the Hebrews to pray for him and appease the heavenly army.
4 Maccabees 4:12 For he said that he had sinned so as to deserve even death, and that, if saved, he would hymn to all men the blessedness of the sacred place.
4 Maccabees 4:13 Moved by these words, Onias the high priest, although also wary lest King Seleukos suppose that Apollonios had been killed by a human plot and not divine justice, prayed for him.
4 Maccabees 4:14 Unexpectedly preserved, he departed to make known to the king what had happened to him.
4 Maccabees 4:15 When King Seleukos died, his son Antiochos Epiphanes succeeds to the rule, an arrogant and terrible man,
4 Maccabees 4:16 who removed Onias from the high priesthood and established his brother Iason as high priest,
4 Maccabees 4:17 who agreed to give three thousand six hundred and sixty talents yearly if he entrusted the office to him.
4 Maccabees 4:18 He permitted him both to serve as high priest and to lead the nation;
4 Maccabees 4:19 and he changed the nation’s way of life and constitution toward every lawlessness,
4 Maccabees 4:20 so that he not only constructed a gymnasium upon the very citadel of our homeland, but also dissolved the care of the sanctuary.
4 Maccabees 4:21 Indignant at these things, divine justice made Antiochos himself wage war against them.
4 Maccabees 4:22 For when he was warring in Egypt against Ptolemaios, and heard that, a report of his death having spread, the Hierosolymites rejoiced exceedingly, he quickly marched against them,
4 Maccabees 4:23 and, when he had ravaged them, made a decree that if any of them were found conducting their lives by the ancestral law, they should die.
4 Maccabees 4:24 Since he was in no way able through the decrees to overthrow the nation’s good observance of law, but saw all his threats and punishments being overthrown,
4 Maccabees 4:25 so that even women, because they circumcised their children, were hurled down with their infants, knowing beforehand that they would suffer this;
4 Maccabees 4:26 since therefore his decrees were despised by the people, he himself through tortures compelled each individual of the nation to renounce Judaism by tasting polluted foods.

## Chapter 5

4 Maccabees 5:1 Indeed the tyrant Antiochos, taking his seat with the councilors upon a certain high place, with his armed troops standing around him,
4 Maccabees 5:2 commanded the spear-bearers to drag forward each Hebrew and compel him to taste pork and food sacrificed to idols;
4 Maccabees 5:3 and if any were unwilling to eat polluted food, these should be tortured on the wheel and killed.
4 Maccabees 5:4 Many being seized together, one first from the crowd, named Eleazaros, a priest by birth, learned in the law and advanced in age, and known to many around the tyrant because of his age, was brought near him.
4 Maccabees 5:5 Seeing him, Antiochos said:
4 Maccabees 5:6 “Before beginning the tortures against you, old man, I would advise you these things, that by tasting pork you might be saved;
4 Maccabees 5:7 for I respect your age and gray hair, which you have after so long a time, yet you do not seem to me to practice philosophy, using the religion of the Jews.
4 Maccabees 5:8 For why do you abhor eating the flesh of this animal, when nature has granted it as most excellent?
4 Maccabees 5:9 For this is senseless, not to enjoy pleasant things without reproach, and unjust to turn away the gifts of nature.
4 Maccabees 5:10 And you seem to me likely to act even more senselessly if, vainly boasting concerning the truth, you further despise me also to your own punishment.
4 Maccabees 5:11 Will you not awaken from your prattling philosophy and scatter the nonsense from your reasonings, and, taking up a mind worthy of your age, philosophize upon the truth of what is advantageous,
4 Maccabees 5:12 and, reverencing my humane counsel, pity your own old age?
4 Maccabees 5:13 For consider that, even if there is some overseeing power of this religion of yours, it would pardon you for every transgression arising through compulsion.”
4 Maccabees 5:14 When the tyrant urged him in this manner toward unlawful eating of flesh, Eleazaros asked to speak,
4 Maccabees 5:15 and, receiving permission to speak, began to address them thus:
4 Maccabees 5:16 “We, Antiochos, persuaded to conduct our life by divine law, consider no compulsion stronger than our obedience to the law;
4 Maccabees 5:17 therefore we deem it proper in no manner to transgress the law.
4 Maccabees 5:18 Indeed, if our law were not in truth divine, as you suppose, but we otherwise considered it divine, even so it would not be permissible for us to annul our conviction concerning piety.
4 Maccabees 5:19 Do not therefore suppose that this would be a small sin, if we ate polluted food;
4 Maccabees 5:20 for transgressing the law in small and great things is equivalent,
4 Maccabees 5:21 for through either the law is similarly treated with arrogance.
4 Maccabees 5:22 You mock our philosophy as though we did not live in it with sound reasoning;
4 Maccabees 5:23 for it teaches us temperance so as to master all pleasures and desires, and trains courage so as willingly to endure every pain,
4 Maccabees 5:24 and instructs in justice so as to practice equality of law in all dispositions, and teaches piety so as magnificently to revere only the God who exists.
4 Maccabees 5:25 Therefore we do not eat polluted food; for, believing that the law is established by God, we know that the Creator of the world sympathizes with us according to nature in legislating;
4 Maccabees 5:26 he permitted us to eat what would be suited to our souls, but forbade the eating of flesh of what would be opposed to them.
4 Maccabees 5:27 It is tyrannical not only to compel us to transgress the law, but also to eat, so that you may laugh at us for this most hateful eating of polluted food.
4 Maccabees 5:28 But you will not laugh this laugh against me,
4 Maccabees 5:29 nor will I abandon the holy oaths of the ancestors concerning keeping the law,
4 Maccabees 5:30 not even if you cut out my eyes and melt my entrails.
4 Maccabees 5:31 I am not so old and cowardly that through piety my reason does not remain youthful.
4 Maccabees 5:32 Therefore prepare wheels and blow the fire more fiercely.
4 Maccabees 5:33 I do not pity my own old age so much that through myself I would overthrow the ancestral law.
4 Maccabees 5:34 I will not betray you, instructing law, nor renounce you, beloved self-control,
4 Maccabees 5:35 nor shame you, philosophical reason, nor deny you, honored priesthood and knowledge of legislation;
4 Maccabees 5:36 nor will you defile my reverent mouth of old age or my lifetime of lawful life.
4 Maccabees 5:37 The fathers will receive me pure, not having feared your compulsions unto death.
4 Maccabees 5:38 For you will tyrannize over the impious, but will rule over my reasonings for piety neither by words nor through deeds.”

## Chapter 6

4 Maccabees 6:1 When he had answered the tyrant's exhortations in this manner, the guards standing by dragged Eleazaros bitterly to the instruments of torture.
4 Maccabees 6:2 And first they stripped the aged man, adorned with the dignity belonging to piety;
4 Maccabees 6:3 then, binding his arms behind him, they maltreated him with whips on either side,
4 Maccabees 6:4 while a herald cried out from the other side, “Obey the king's commands.”
4 Maccabees 6:5 But Eleazaros, truly magnanimous and noble, as though being tortured in a dream, did not change in any way,
4 Maccabees 6:6 but, raising his eyes high toward heaven, the old man had his flesh torn by the whips and was drenched with blood, and his sides were pierced through.
4 Maccabees 6:7 And falling to the ground because his body could not bear the pains, he kept his reason upright and unbending.
4 Maccabees 6:8 Indeed, one of the bitter guards, springing at his flanks, struck him with his foot so that he would rise when falling.
4 Maccabees 6:9 But he endured the pains and despised the compulsion and persisted through the maltreatments,
4 Maccabees 6:10 and, like a noble athlete, the old man, while being struck, defeated those torturing him;
4 Maccabees 6:11 indeed, sweating in the face and panting heavily, he was admired even by those torturing him for his courage.
4 Maccabees 6:12 Therefore, partly pitying the circumstances of his old age,
4 Maccabees 6:13 partly feeling sympathy from familiarity, and partly admiring his endurance, some of the king's men approached him and said,
4 Maccabees 6:14 “Why do you unreasonably destroy yourself with these evils, Eleazar?
4 Maccabees 6:15 We will indeed set before you some of the cooked foods, and you, pretending to taste the pork, save yourself.”
4 Maccabees 6:16 And Eleazaros, as though more bitterly maltreated by the counsel, cried out,
4 Maccabees 6:17 “May we, the children of Abraam, not think so badly as to become fainthearted and act out a performance unfitting for us.
4 Maccabees 6:18 For it is also unreasonable if, having lived our life until old age according to truth and lawfully guarded the reputation belonging to it, we should now change
4 Maccabees 6:19 and we ourselves should become a pattern of impiety to the young, so that we become an example of eating defiled food.
4 Maccabees 6:20 And it is shameful if we shall live on for a little time, and that while being laughed at by everyone for cowardice,
4 Maccabees 6:21 and be despised by the tyrant as unmanly, but should not defend our divine law until death.
4 Maccabees 6:22 In view of these things, you, children of Abraam, die nobly for piety.
4 Maccabees 6:23 And you guards of the tyrant, why do you delay?”
4 Maccabees 6:24 Seeing him thus magnanimous in the face of the compulsions and not changing even in response to their pity, they led him up to the fire;
4 Maccabees 6:25 there, burning him with maliciously devised instruments, they flung him about, and poured foul-smelling liquids into his nostrils.
4 Maccabees 6:26 But he, already burned down to his bones and about to faint, raised his eyes toward God and said,
4 Maccabees 6:27 “You know, God, that although I can save myself, I am dying in burning tortures because of the law.
4 Maccabees 6:28 Be gracious to your nation, being satisfied with our punishment on their behalf.
4 Maccabees 6:29 Make my blood their purification, and take my life as an exchange for their lives.”
4 Maccabees 6:30 And having said these things, the holy man died nobly in the tortures, and until the tortures of death resisted by reason because of the law.
4 Maccabees 6:31 Therefore, admittedly, pious reason is master of the passions.
4 Maccabees 6:32 For if the passions had prevailed over reason, we would have given them the testimony of supremacy;
4 Maccabees 6:33 but now, since reason has defeated the passions, we suitably assign to it the authority of leadership.
4 Maccabees 6:34 And it is just for us to acknowledge that the might belongs to reason, since it prevails even over pains from outside, for it is also ridiculous.
4 Maccabees 6:35 And I demonstrate that reason has not only prevailed over pains, but also rules pleasures and yields nothing to them.

## Chapter 7

4 Maccabees 7:1 For like an excellent pilot, the reason of our father Eleazaros, steering the ship of piety in the sea of the passions
4 Maccabees 7:2 and being maltreated by the tyrant's threats and flooded by the stormy waves of the tortures,
4 Maccabees 7:3 did not in any way turn the tillers of piety until it sailed into the harbor of immortal victory.
4 Maccabees 7:4 No city, besieged with many and varied engines, ever held out in this way, as did that most holy man. Being set on fire in his sacred soul with maltreatments and racks, he defeated those besieging him through reason, which defends piety.
4 Maccabees 7:5 For father Eleazar, extending his own understanding like a headland with steep cliffs, broke the raging surges of the passions.
4 Maccabees 7:6 O priest worthy of the priesthood, you did not defile your sacred teeth, nor did you profane with defiled eating the belly that had made room for reverence for God and purification.
4 Maccabees 7:7 O one in accord with the law and philosopher of divine life.
4 Maccabees 7:8 Such must be those who put the law into practice, defending it with their own blood and noble sweat against sufferings unto death.
4 Maccabees 7:9 You, father, confirmed our observance of law unto glory through your endurance, and, having spoken reverently of holiness, you did not overthrow it, and through deeds you made credible the discourses of your divine philosophy,
4 Maccabees 7:10 O old man more forceful than tortures, aged man stronger than fire, and greatest king of the passions, Eleazar.
4 Maccabees 7:11 For just as father Aaron, armed with the censer and running through the multitude of the nation, defeated the burning angel,
4 Maccabees 7:12 so Eleazar, the descendant of Aaron, being melted away by the fire, did not change his reason.
4 Maccabees 7:13 And indeed, most wondrous of all, although an old man, with the tensions of his body already loosened, his flesh slackened all around, and his sinews also exhausted, he became young again
4 Maccabees 7:14 in spirit through reason, and through reason like Isaak's he rendered the many-headed rack powerless.
4 Maccabees 7:15 O blessed old age and venerable gray hair and lawful life, which a faithful seal of death brought to completion.
4 Maccabees 7:16 If, therefore, an old man despised tortures unto death because of piety, admittedly pious reason is leader of the passions.
4 Maccabees 7:17 But perhaps some might say, “Not everyone masters the passions, because not everyone has prudent reason.”
4 Maccabees 7:18 But all who take thought for piety with their whole heart, these alone can rule the passions of the flesh,
4 Maccabees 7:19 believing that they do not die to God, just as neither do our patriarchs Abraam and Isaak and Iakob, but they live to God.
4 Maccabees 7:20 Therefore, the fact that some appear to be ruled by passions because of weak reason presents no opposition;
4 Maccabees 7:21 for who, pursuing philosophy according to the whole rule of philosophy and having trusted God,
4 Maccabees 7:22 and knowing that it is blessed to endure every pain because of virtue, would not master the passions because of reverence for God?
4 Maccabees 7:23 For the wise and courageous man alone is lord of the passions.

## Chapter 8

4 Maccabees 8:1 Indeed, for this reason youths also, pursuing philosophy by the reason of piety, prevailed over harsher instruments of torture.
4 Maccabees 8:2 For when, at the first trial, the tyrant was conspicuously defeated, being unable to compel an old man to eat defiled food, then, with exceedingly great passion, he commanded that others be brought from the captive Hebrews, and that, if they ate defiled food, they be released after eating, but if they spoke against it, they be tortured more bitterly.
4 Maccabees 8:3 When the tyrant had ordered these things, seven brothers were brought in with an aged mother, handsome and modest and noble and gracious in everything.
4 Maccabees 8:4 Seeing them surrounding their mother in the middle, as in a chorus, the tyrant took pleasure in them, and, struck by their good appearance and nobility, smiled at them and called them near and said,
4 Maccabees 8:5 “O young men, I admire each one of you with goodwill; esteeming highly the beauty and the number of so many brothers, I not only counsel you not to go mad with the same madness as the old man tortured before you, but also urge you to yield to me and enjoy my friendship;
4 Maccabees 8:6 and just as I could punish those disobeying my commands, so also could I benefit those readily obeying me.
4 Maccabees 8:7 Trust, therefore, and you will receive leading offices over my affairs, having denied your ancestral ordinance of citizenship;
4 Maccabees 8:8 and, having partaken of Greek life and changed your way of living, luxuriate in your youth;
4 Maccabees 8:9 for if you make me angry through disobedience, you will compel me, with dreadful punishments, to destroy each one of you through tortures.
4 Maccabees 8:10 Have pity on yourselves, therefore, whom even I, your enemy, pity for your age and beauty.
4 Maccabees 8:11 Will you not consider this, that if you disobey, nothing is laid up for you except to die with tortures?”
4 Maccabees 8:12 Saying these things, he commanded that the instruments of torture be placed before them, so that through fear also he might persuade them to eat defiled food.
4 Maccabees 8:13 And when the guards had set out wheels and joint-presses, racks and rollers and catapults and cauldrons, frying pans and finger-sheaths and iron hands and wedges and the glowing embers of the fire, the tyrant took up the speech and said,
4 Maccabees 8:14 “Youths, be afraid, and the justice you revere will be gracious to you when you transgress the law through compulsion.”
4 Maccabees 8:15 But they, hearing enticing things and seeing dreadful things, not only were not afraid, but also answered the tyrant with philosophy and through sound reasoning overthrew his tyranny.
4 Maccabees 8:16 And indeed, let us consider: if some among them had been cowardly and unmanly, what words would they have used? Would they not have been these?
4 Maccabees 8:17 “O wretched and exceedingly senseless us! Since the king calls us and invites us to benefits if we should obey him,
4 Maccabees 8:18 why do we delight ourselves with empty wishes and dare death-bearing disobedience?
4 Maccabees 8:19 Shall we not fear the instruments of torture, men, brothers, and consider the threats of tortures, and flee this vainglory and destruction-bearing arrogance?
4 Maccabees 8:20 Let us pity our own ages and have compassion on our mother's old age,
4 Maccabees 8:21 and reflect that, if we disobey, we shall be dead.
4 Maccabees 8:22 And divine justice also will forgive us for fearing the king through compulsion.
4 Maccabees 8:23 Why do we lead ourselves out of sweetest life and deprive ourselves of the sweet world?
4 Maccabees 8:24 Let us not contend by force against compulsion, nor be vainglorious over our own torture.
4 Maccabees 8:25 Neither does the law itself willingly put us to death for fearing the instruments of torture.
4 Maccabees 8:26 From where has such great contentiousness melted into us, and why does death-bearing endurance please us, when it is possible to live without disturbance by obeying the king?”
4 Maccabees 8:27 But the young men about to be tortured neither said nor considered any of these things.
4 Maccabees 8:28 For they were disdainful of the passions and sovereign over the pains,
4 Maccabees 8:29 so that, as soon as the tyrant ceased counseling them to eat defiled food, they all said together with one voice, as though from the same soul,

## Chapter 9

4 Maccabees 9:1 “Why do you delay, tyrant? For we are ready to die rather than transgress our ancestral commandments;
4 Maccabees 9:2 for we would rightly be ashamed before our forefathers if we did not employ obedience to the law and Moyses as counselor.
4 Maccabees 9:3 Tyrant, counselor of lawlessness, do not, while hating us, pity us beyond ourselves.
4 Maccabees 9:4 For we consider your pity concerning our unlawful preservation to be harsher than death itself.
4 Maccabees 9:5 And you terrify us by threatening us with death through tortures, as though you had not learned from Eleazaros a little while ago.
4 Maccabees 9:6 But if the old men of the Hebrews practiced piety by enduring even tortures because of piety, more justly would we young men die, disregarding the tortures of your compulsions, which our aged instructor also defeated.
4 Maccabees 9:7 Make trial, therefore, tyrant; and if you put our lives to death because of piety, do not think you harm us by torturing us.
4 Maccabees 9:8 For through this suffering and endurance we shall have the prizes of virtue and shall be with God, because of whom we also suffer;
4 Maccabees 9:9 but because of your bloodshed against us, you will endure sufficient eternal torture by fire from divine justice.”
4 Maccabees 9:10 When they had said these things, the tyrant not only raged against them as disobedient, but also became angry against them as ungrateful.
4 Maccabees 9:11 Therefore, having been commanded, the shield-bearers brought forward the eldest of them, and, tearing his tunic, bound his hands and arms with straps on either side.
4 Maccabees 9:12 And when they grew weary of striking him with whips, accomplishing nothing, they threw him up onto the wheel;
4 Maccabees 9:13 stretched upon it, the noble young man was being dislocated.
4 Maccabees 9:14 And being broken in every limb, he reviled him, saying,
4 Maccabees 9:15 “Most defiled tyrant and enemy of heavenly justice and savage-minded one, you maltreat me in this manner although I have not murdered nor acted impiously, but defend divine law.”
4 Maccabees 9:16 And when the guards said, “Agree to eat, so that you may be released from the tortures,”
4 Maccabees 9:17 he said, “Your wheel is not so strong, defiled servants, as to strangle my reason; cut my limbs and burn my flesh and rack my joints.
4 Maccabees 9:18 For through all the tortures I will convince you that the children of the Hebrews alone are invincible for virtue.”
4 Maccabees 9:19 As he said these things, they spread fire beneath him and tightened further what set the wheel in motion;
4 Maccabees 9:20 and the wheel was stained everywhere with blood, and the heap of charcoal was being quenched by drops of bodily fluids, and his flesh flowed around the axles of the instrument.
4 Maccabees 9:21 And already having the framework of his bones cut all around, the magnanimous young man of Abraam did not groan,
4 Maccabees 9:22 but, as though being transformed in fire into incorruption, nobly endured the racks,
4 Maccabees 9:23 saying, “Imitate me, brothers; do not desert my contest, nor disown my brotherhood of courage.
4 Maccabees 9:24 Wage a sacred and noble campaign for piety, through which our just and ancestral providence, becoming gracious to the nation, might punish the accursed tyrant.”
4 Maccabees 9:25 And having said these things, the young man worthy of holiness breathed out his soul.
4 Maccabees 9:26 And while everyone admired his steadfastness of soul, the guards brought the second in age after the first, and, fitting iron hands with sharp claws, bound him to an instrument and catapult.
4 Maccabees 9:27 And when, asking whether he wished to eat before being tortured, they heard his noble resolve,
4 Maccabees 9:28 pulling with the iron hands from the sinews as far as the cheeks, the leopard-like beasts dragged away all his flesh and the skin of his head. But he, enduring this grievous pain, said,
4 Maccabees 9:29 “How sweet is every manner of death because of our ancestral piety.” And he said to the tyrant,
4 Maccabees 9:30 “Do you not think, cruelest tyrant of all, that you are being tortured more than I, seeing your arrogant reason of tyranny defeated by our endurance because of piety?
4 Maccabees 9:31 For I lighten my pain with the pleasures arising from virtue,
4 Maccabees 9:32 but you are tortured among the threats of impiety. And you will not escape, most defiled tyrant, the punishments of divine wrath.”

## Chapter 10

4 Maccabees 10:1 And when this one had endured the death celebrated in song, the third was brought, being urged much by many to save himself by tasting.
4 Maccabees 10:2 But he cried out and said, “Do you not know that the same father begot me as those who died, and the same mother gave birth to me, and I was brought up in the same teachings?
4 Maccabees 10:3 I do not disown the noble kinship of the brotherhood.”
4 Maccabees 10:5 But they, taking the man's frank speech bitterly, dislocated his hands and feet with joint-pressing instruments, and, levering them out of their joints, tore his limbs apart,
4 Maccabees 10:6 and broke his fingers and arms and legs and elbows all around.
4 Maccabees 10:7 And being unable in any way to strangle him, they loosened the instruments and scalped him along with the very tips of his fingers.
4 Maccabees 10:8 And immediately they brought him onto the wheel, upon which, being torn apart at the vertebrae, he saw his own flesh torn all around and drops of blood flowing down over his entrails.
4 Maccabees 10:9 And being about to die, he said,
4 Maccabees 10:10 “We, most defiled tyrant, suffer these things because of the instruction and virtue of God;
4 Maccabees 10:11 but you, because of impiety and bloodshed, will endure tortures that cannot be ended.”
4 Maccabees 10:12 And when this one had died in a manner worthy of his brothers, they dragged forward the fourth, saying,
4 Maccabees 10:13 “Do not you also go mad with the same madness as your brothers, but obey the king and save yourself.”
4 Maccabees 10:14 But he said to them, “You do not have fire so much more burning against me as to make me act cowardly.
4 Maccabees 10:15 By the blessed death of my brothers and the eternal destruction of the tyrant and the everlasting life of the pious, I will not deny the noble brotherhood.
4 Maccabees 10:16 Devise tortures, tyrant, so that through them also you may learn that I am a brother of those tortured before me.”
4 Maccabees 10:17 Hearing these things, the blood-devouring and murderous and utterly most defiled Antiochos commanded that his tongue be cut out.
4 Maccabees 10:18 But he said, “Even if you take away the instrument of the voice, God hears even those who are silent;
4 Maccabees 10:19 look, the tongue is stretched out; cut it, for you will not thereby cut out the tongue of our reason.
4 Maccabees 10:20 Gladly we have the limbs of our body mutilated for God.
4 Maccabees 10:21 But God will swiftly pursue you, for you cut out the tongue that sings divine hymns.”

## Chapter 11

4 Maccabees 11:1 And when this one also, maltreated by the tortures, died in them, the fifth sprang forward, saying,
4 Maccabees 11:2 “I am not going to beg off from torture for virtue, tyrant,
4 Maccabees 11:3 but I came forward myself, of my own accord, so that, killing me also, you may owe heavenly justice punishment for more wrongdoings.
4 Maccabees 11:4 O hater of virtue and hater of humanity, what have we done that you ravage us in this manner?
4 Maccabees 11:5 Is it because we reverence the creator of all and live according to his virtuous law?
4 Maccabees 11:6 But these things are worthy of honors, not tortures.”
4 Maccabees 11:9 And as he said such things, the guards bound him and dragged him onto the catapult,
4 Maccabees 11:10 upon which, binding him at the knees and fitting these into iron foot-traps, they bent his waist around a wedge on the wheel, around which, being bent backward in his entirety around the wheel in the manner of a scorpion, he was being torn limb from limb.
4 Maccabees 11:11 In this manner, being constricted in breath and strangled in body also,
4 Maccabees 11:12 he said, “Unwillingly you grant us fine favors, tyrant, providing us through nobler pains the opportunity to show our endurance toward the law.”
4 Maccabees 11:13 And when this one also had died, the sixth youth was brought, who, when the tyrant asked whether he wished to eat and be released, said,
4 Maccabees 11:14 “I am younger than my brothers in age, but of their age in understanding;
4 Maccabees 11:15 for having been born and brought up for the same things, we also ought likewise to die for the same things;
4 Maccabees 11:16 so, if it seems good to you to torture one who does not eat defiled food, torture.”
4 Maccabees 11:17 When he had said these things, they brought him onto the wheel,
4 Maccabees 11:18 upon which, being carefully stretched and having his vertebrae dislocated, he was burned from beneath.
4 Maccabees 11:19 And heating sharp skewers, they applied them to his back and, piercing his sides, burned through his entrails.
4 Maccabees 11:20 But while being tortured he said, “O contest worthy of holiness, to which so many brothers were called because of piety for an exercise in pains, and we were not defeated.
4 Maccabees 11:21 For pious knowledge is invincible, tyrant.
4 Maccabees 11:22 Armed with nobility and goodness, I too shall die with my brothers,
4 Maccabees 11:23 myself also bringing a great avenging spirit against you, inventor of tortures and enemy of those who truly practice piety.
4 Maccabees 11:24 Six youths have overthrown your tyranny;
4 Maccabees 11:25 for is your inability to persuade our reason to change or to force it toward defiled eating not your overthrow?
4 Maccabees 11:26 Your fire is cold to us, and the catapults painless, and your force powerless.
4 Maccabees 11:27 For our guards have stood in defense of divine law, not of a tyrant; because of this we have invincible reason.”

## Chapter 12

4 Maccabees 12:1 And when this one also died blessedly, having been thrown into a cauldron, the seventh, youngest of all, came forward.
4 Maccabees 12:2 Pitying him, although terribly reviled by his brothers, and seeing the bonds already placed around him, the tyrant summoned him nearer and tried to exhort him, saying,
4 Maccabees 12:3 “You see the end of your brothers' madness; for, racked because of disobedience, they are dead.
4 Maccabees 12:4 But if you do not obey, wretched one, you too will be tortured and will be dead before your time,
4 Maccabees 12:5 but if you obey, you will be a friend and will lead the affairs of the kingdom.”
4 Maccabees 12:6 And urging these things, he summoned the child's mother, so that, pitying her who had been deprived of so many sons, he might urge the remaining one toward saving obedience.
4 Maccabees 12:7 But when his mother had exhorted him in the Hebrew tongue, as we shall say a little later,
4 Maccabees 12:8 he says, “Release me, that I may speak to the king and all the friends with him.”
4 Maccabees 12:9 And exceedingly pleased at the child's promise, they quickly released him.
4 Maccabees 12:10 And running near the frying pans,
4 Maccabees 12:11 he says, “Unholy tyrant and most impious of all wicked men, having received good things and the kingdom from God, were you not ashamed to kill his servants and rack those who exercise piety?
4 Maccabees 12:12 In return for these things, justice will reserve you for more intense and eternal fire and tortures, which will not release you for the whole age.
4 Maccabees 12:13 Were you not ashamed, being human, most beastly one, to cut out the tongues of those with like feelings and made from the same elements, and to torture them, maltreating them in this manner?
4 Maccabees 12:14 But they, dying nobly, fulfilled their piety toward God, while you will wail grievously for killing the contenders for virtue without cause.”
4 Maccabees 12:15 Therefore, being about to die himself also, he said,
4 Maccabees 12:16 “I do not desert the valor of my brothers;
4 Maccabees 12:17 but I call upon the ancestral God, that he may become gracious to our nation.
4 Maccabees 12:18 And he will punish you both in the present life and when you have died.”
4 Maccabees 12:19 And having prayed these things, he threw himself onto the frying pans, and thus gave up his life.

## Chapter 13

4 Maccabees 13:1 If, therefore, the seven brothers despised pains unto death, it is agreed from every side that pious reason is sovereign master of the passions.
4 Maccabees 13:2 For if, enslaved to the passions, they had eaten defiled food, we would say that they had been defeated by them;
4 Maccabees 13:3 but now it was not so; rather, by reason praised before God, they overcame the passions,
4 Maccabees 13:4 and their leadership of understanding cannot be overlooked, for they prevailed over both passion and pains.
4 Maccabees 13:5 How, therefore, can one fail to acknowledge in these men sound reasoning's rule over the passions, when they did not turn back from the pains through fire?
4 Maccabees 13:6 For just as towers projecting at harbors, checking the threats of the waves, provide a calm anchorage for those sailing in,
4 Maccabees 13:7 so the seven-towered sound reasoning of the young men, fortifying the harbor of piety, defeated the licentiousness of the passions.
4 Maccabees 13:8 For, forming a sacred chorus of piety, they encouraged one another, saying,
4 Maccabees 13:9 “Let us die as brothers, brothers, for the law; let us imitate the three young men in Assyria, who despised the furnace that shared their citizenship.
4 Maccabees 13:10 Let us not act cowardly in the demonstration of piety.”
4 Maccabees 13:11 And one said, “Take courage, brother,” and another, “Endure nobly,”
4 Maccabees 13:12 and another, recalling, said, “Remember where you are from, or by the hand of what father Isaak endured being slaughtered because of piety.”
4 Maccabees 13:13 And each one, all together looking at one another, cheerful and very courageous, said, “Let us dedicate ourselves with the whole heart to God, who gave our lives, and let us lend our bodies to the guarding of the law.
4 Maccabees 13:14 Let us not fear the one who seems to kill;
4 Maccabees 13:15 for great is the contest of the soul and the danger lying in eternal torture for those who transgress the commandment of God.
4 Maccabees 13:16 Let us therefore arm ourselves with divine reason's rule over the passions.
4 Maccabees 13:17 For when we have died in this manner, Abraam and Isaak and Iakob will receive us, and all the fathers will praise us.”
4 Maccabees 13:18 And to each one of their brothers being dragged away, those remaining said, “Do not put us to shame, brother, nor prove false to our brothers who died before us.”
4 Maccabees 13:19 And you are not ignorant of the affections of brotherhood, which divine and all-wise providence apportioned through fathers to those being born, having planted them also through the maternal womb,
4 Maccabees 13:20 in which brothers dwelt for an equal time and were formed in the same time and grew from the same blood and were brought to completion through the same soul,
4 Maccabees 13:21 and were delivered after equal periods and drank milk from the same springs, from which embraces brother-loving souls are nourished together;
4 Maccabees 13:22 and they grow more strongly through upbringing together and daily familiarity and the other instruction and our exercise in God's law.
4 Maccabees 13:23 Thus, therefore, brotherly love being established in sympathy, the seven brothers had greater sympathy toward one another.
4 Maccabees 13:24 For, instructed in the same law and having exercised the same virtues and been brought up together in righteous life, they loved one another more.
4 Maccabees 13:25 For shared zeal for nobility and goodness intensified their goodwill and concord toward one another;
4 Maccabees 13:26 for together with piety they made brotherly love more desirable to themselves.
4 Maccabees 13:27 But nevertheless, although nature and familiarity and the habits of virtue increased the affections of brotherhood for them, those remaining endured their brothers because of piety, seeing those maltreated being tortured unto death,

## Chapter 14

4 Maccabees 14:1 further urging them on toward maltreatment, so that they not only despised the pains, but also ruled the passions of brotherly love.
4 Maccabees 14:2 O reasons more royal than kings and freer than free men.
4 Maccabees 14:3 O sacred and well-harmonized concord of the seven brothers concerning piety.
4 Maccabees 14:4 None of the seven youths became cowardly or hesitated before death,
4 Maccabees 14:5 but all, as though running onto a road of immortality, hastened toward death through tortures.
4 Maccabees 14:6 Just as the hands and feet move in accord with the soul's directions, so those holy youths, as though under the immortal soul of piety, agreed together upon death for it.
4 Maccabees 14:7 O most holy seven of brothers in concord. For just as the seven days of the creation of the world around piety,
4 Maccabees 14:8 so the youths, dancing around the seven, circled, overthrowing the fear of tortures.
4 Maccabees 14:9 Now we shudder on hearing the affliction of those young men; but they, not merely seeing, nor merely hearing the immediate word of threat, but also suffering, persisted, and this in pains through fire;
4 Maccabees 14:10 what could be more painful than these? For the force of fire, being sharp and swift, quickly dissolved their bodies.
4 Maccabees 14:11 And do not consider it wondrous if reason mastered those men in the tortures, since even a woman's mind despised pains of more varied kinds;
4 Maccabees 14:12 for the mother of the seven young men bore the tortures upon each one of her children.
4 Maccabees 14:13 And observe how intricate is the affection of love for children, drawing everything toward heartfelt sympathy,
4 Maccabees 14:14 since even irrational animals have sympathy and affection toward those born from them similar to humans.
4 Maccabees 14:15 For among the birds, the tame ones walking on roofs around the houses defend their nestlings,
4 Maccabees 14:16 while the others, having built nests on mountaintops and in the clefts of ravines and the hollows of trees and their summits, lay their young and hinder anyone approaching;
4 Maccabees 14:17 and if they cannot hinder them, flying all around them, grieving in their affection and crying out in their own voice, they help their children as they can.
4 Maccabees 14:18 And why must one demonstrate sympathy toward children through irrational animals,
4 Maccabees 14:19 when even bees, about the time of wax-making, defend themselves against those approaching and strike with their sting, as though with iron, those approaching their nest, and ward them off until death?
4 Maccabees 14:20 But sympathy for children did not move the young men's mother, who shared Abraam's soul.

## Chapter 15

4 Maccabees 15:1 O reason, tyrant over passions concerning children, and piety more desirable to a mother than children.
4 Maccabees 15:2 The mother, with two things set before her, piety and the temporary preservation of seven sons according to the tyrant's promise,
4 Maccabees 15:3 loved piety more, which saves unto eternal life according to God.
4 Maccabees 15:4 O in what manner might I describe parents' passions of love for children? We impress a likeness of both soul and form into the wondrous small image of a child, especially because mothers are more sympathetic than fathers to the sufferings of those born.
4 Maccabees 15:5 For insofar as mothers are weaker in soul and more prolific, so much more do they love their children.
4 Maccabees 15:6 And the mother of the seven children became more loving of children than all mothers, who, through seven pregnancies, planting further her affection toward them,
4 Maccabees 15:7 and compelled through the many birth pains for each one of them to have sympathy toward them,
4 Maccabees 15:8 disregarded the temporary preservation of her children because of her fear toward God.
4 Maccabees 15:9 Indeed, also because of her sons' nobility and goodness and their obedience toward the law, she had greater affection for them.
4 Maccabees 15:10 For they were righteous and temperate and courageous and magnanimous and loving of brothers and loving of their mother, so as to obey her even unto death while keeping the ordinances.
4 Maccabees 15:11 But nevertheless, although there were so many things concerning love for children drawing the mother toward sympathy, the tortures of every varied kind were unable to change her reason in the case of any of them,
4 Maccabees 15:12 but the mother exhorted both each child and all together toward the death of piety.
4 Maccabees 15:13 O sacred nature and parents' affections and affectionate generation and nurture and mothers' untamable passions.
4 Maccabees 15:14 Seeing each one racked and burned, the mother did not change because of piety.
4 Maccabees 15:15 She saw her children's flesh melting around the fire and the toes and fingers twitching upon the earth and the flesh of their heads as far as the cheeks laid out like masks.
4 Maccabees 15:16 O mother, now tried by more bitter pains than the birth pains for them.
4 Maccabees 15:17 O woman who alone gave birth to piety in its entirety.
4 Maccabees 15:18 Your firstborn breathing his last did not change you, nor the second looking piteously toward you in tortures, nor the third expiring,
4 Maccabees 15:19 and seeing the eyes of each one looking like a bull upon the same maltreatment in the tortures, and their nostrils giving signs beforehand of their death, you did not weep.
4 Maccabees 15:20 Seeing children's flesh burned away upon children's flesh, and hands cut off upon hands, and heads severed from their necks upon heads, and dead falling upon dead, and seeing the place become a common grave of your children through the tortures, you did not shed tears.
4 Maccabees 15:21 Neither sirens' melodies nor swans' voices draw listeners toward delight in hearing as do the voices of children calling their mother amid tortures.
4 Maccabees 15:22 With how great and how many tortures was the mother then tortured, while her sons were tortured with wheels and burning irons.
4 Maccabees 15:23 But pious reason, making her heart courageous in the very passions, urged her to disregard temporary love for children.
4 Maccabees 15:24 Although seeing the destruction of seven children and the intricate variety of racks, the noble mother rendered them all powerless through faith toward God.
4 Maccabees 15:25 For, as though in a council chamber, seeing in her own soul dreadful counselors, nature and generation and love for children and the tortures of children,
4 Maccabees 15:26 the mother, holding two votes for her children, one death-bearing and one saving,
4 Maccabees 15:27 did not choose the preservation that saved seven sons for a little time,
4 Maccabees 15:28 but the daughter remembered the God-revering endurance of Abraam.
4 Maccabees 15:29 O mother of a nation, vindicator of the law and defender of piety and prize-bearer of the contest through the heart;
4 Maccabees 15:30 O nobler than males in steadfastness and more courageous than men in endurance.
4 Maccabees 15:31 For just as Noe's ark, bearing the world in the world-filling flood, steadfastly endured the surges,
4 Maccabees 15:32 so you, guardian of the law, flooded from every side in the deluge of the passions and beset by strong winds, the tortures of your sons, nobly endured the storms for piety.

## Chapter 16

4 Maccabees 16:1 If, therefore, even a woman, aged and mother of seven children, endured while seeing her children's tortures unto death, admittedly pious reason is sovereign over the passions.
4 Maccabees 16:2 Therefore I demonstrated that not only men ruled the passions, but also a woman despised the greatest tortures.
4 Maccabees 16:3 And neither were the lions around Daniel so savage, nor the furnace of Misael blazing with most furious fire, as the nature of love for children burned around her while she saw her seven sons tortured in such varied ways.
4 Maccabees 16:4 But by the reason of piety the mother quenched passions so many and so great.
4 Maccabees 16:5 For consider this also, that if the woman had been cowardly, although being a mother, she would have lamented over them and perhaps would have said these things:
4 Maccabees 16:6 “O miserable me and many times thrice-wretched, who, having borne seven children, have become mother of none.
4 Maccabees 16:7 O vain seven pregnancies and profitless seven periods of ten months and fruitless nursing and wretched milk-feeding.
4 Maccabees 16:8 And in vain for you, children, I endured many birth pains and the harsher cares of upbringing.
4 Maccabees 16:9 O my children, some unmarried, others married without profit; I shall not see your children nor be called grandmother and pronounced blessed.
4 Maccabees 16:10 O I, the woman with many children and beautiful children, widowed and alone, full of mourning;
4 Maccabees 16:11 nor, if I die, will I have any of my sons to bury me.”
4 Maccabees 16:12 But the sacred and God-revering mother lamented for none with this lament, nor turned any of them aside so that they might not die, nor grieved as though they were dying,
4 Maccabees 16:13 but, as though having an adamantine mind and giving birth anew to the number of her sons unto immortality, she rather exhorted them toward death for piety, entreating them.
4 Maccabees 16:14 O mother, soldier of God through piety, aged woman and wife, through steadfastness you defeated even a tyrant and were found mightier than a man in both deeds and words.
4 Maccabees 16:15 For when you were seized with your children, you stood seeing Eleazaros being tortured and said to your children in the Hebrew tongue,
4 Maccabees 16:16 “O children, noble is the contest to which you were called for the testimony of the nation; contend eagerly in it for the ancestral law;
4 Maccabees 16:17 for it is shameful that this old man should endure the pains because of piety, but you young men be struck with terror by the tortures.
4 Maccabees 16:18 Remember that because of God you partook of the world and enjoyed life,
4 Maccabees 16:19 and because of this you ought to endure every pain because of God,
4 Maccabees 16:20 because of whom our father Abraam also hastened to slaughter his son Isaak, father of the nation, and he, seeing his father's sword-bearing hand descending upon him, did not cower.
4 Maccabees 16:21 And righteous Daniel was thrown among lions, and Ananias and Azarias and Misael were hurled into a furnace of fire and endured because of God.
4 Maccabees 16:22 Therefore you also, having the same faith toward God, do not be distressed.
4 Maccabees 16:23 For it is unreasonable, knowing piety, not to withstand the pains.”
4 Maccabees 16:24 Through these words the mother of seven, exhorting each one of her sons, persuaded them to die rather than transgress the commandment of God,
4 Maccabees 16:25 and further knowing these things also, that those dying because of God live to God, as do Abraam and Isaak and Iakob and all the patriarchs.

## Chapter 17

4 Maccabees 17:1 And some of the guards also said that, when she herself was about to be seized for death, so that no one might touch her body, she threw herself onto the pyre.
4 Maccabees 17:2 O mother who, with seven children, overthrew the tyrant's force and rendered his evil designs powerless and showed the nobility of faith.
4 Maccabees 17:3 For like a roof, you, nobly established upon the pillars of your children, bore without bending the earthquake through the tortures.
4 Maccabees 17:4 Take courage, therefore, mother of a sacred soul, having the hope of endurance firm toward God.
4 Maccabees 17:5 The moon has not stood so venerable in heaven with stars as you, having guided your seven star-like children with light toward piety, have stood honored by God and have been established with them in heaven;
4 Maccabees 17:6 for your childbearing was from Abraam the father.
4 Maccabees 17:7 But if it were possible for us to paint the history of your piety as upon something, would not the spectators shudder, seeing a mother of seven children who endured varied tortures unto death because of piety?
4 Maccabees 17:8 For it was also worthy to inscribe upon the tomb itself these things also, said for remembrance to those of the nation:
4 Maccabees 17:9 “Here an old priest and an aged woman and seven children have been buried through the force of a tyrant wishing to overthrow the citizenship of the Hebrews,
4 Maccabees 17:10 who also vindicated the race, looking toward God and enduring the tortures unto death.”
4 Maccabees 17:11 For truly divine was the contest that took place through them.
4 Maccabees 17:12 For virtue then presided over the contest, testing through endurance. The victory: incorruption in long-lasting life.
4 Maccabees 17:13 And Eleazar contended first, and the mother of the seven children competed, and the brothers contended;
4 Maccabees 17:14 the tyrant contended against them, while the world and human life watched;
4 Maccabees 17:15 and reverence for God was victorious, crowning its own athletes.
4 Maccabees 17:16 Who did not admire the athletes of the divine legislation? Who were not astounded?
4 Maccabees 17:17 Indeed, the tyrant himself and the whole council admired their endurance,
4 Maccabees 17:18 through which they also now stand beside the divine throne and live the blessed age.
4 Maccabees 17:19 For Moyses also says, “And all those sanctified under your hands.”
4 Maccabees 17:20 And these, therefore, having been sanctified because of God, have been honored, not only with this honor, but also by the fact that through them the enemies did not prevail over our nation,
4 Maccabees 17:21 and the tyrant was punished and the homeland purified, as though they had become an exchange of lives for the nation's sin.
4 Maccabees 17:22 And through the blood of those pious men and the propitiation of their death, divine providence preserved Israel, who had previously been afflicted.
4 Maccabees 17:23 For looking toward their courage in virtue and their endurance in the tortures, the tyrant Antiochos proclaimed their endurance as an example to his soldiers,
4 Maccabees 17:24 and he had them noble and courageous for infantry battle and siege, and, having ravaged, defeated all the enemies.

## Chapter 18

4 Maccabees 18:1 O descendant children of the seeds of Abraam, Israelites, obey this law and practice piety in every manner,
4 Maccabees 18:2 knowing that pious reason is master of the passions, and not only of those within, but also of the pains from outside.
4 Maccabees 18:3 In return for these things, having surrendered their bodies to pains because of piety, those men were not only admired by humans, but also deemed worthy of a divine portion.
4 Maccabees 18:4 And because of them the nation was at peace, and, having renewed observance of law in the homeland, they have ravaged the enemies.
4 Maccabees 18:5 And the tyrant Antiochos has been punished on earth also, and, having died, is being chastised; for when he was utterly unable in any way to compel the inhabitants of Ierosolyma to adopt foreign ways and depart from their ancestral customs of living, then, departing from Ierosolyma, he campaigned against the Persians.
4 Maccabees 18:6 And the mother of the seven children also said these ordinances to her children:
4 Maccabees 18:7 “I became a pure virgin and did not go beyond my father's house, but guarded the built rib.
4 Maccabees 18:8 Neither did a ravager of the wilderness, a corrupter in the plain, corrupt me, nor did a ravager of deceit, a serpent, ruin the pure things of my virginity.
4 Maccabees 18:9 And I remained with a husband for the time of my prime; but when these had come of age, their father died, blessed indeed was he, for having lived through the life of having good children, he did not suffer the time of childlessness.
4 Maccabees 18:10 He taught you the law and the prophets while still being with you.
4 Maccabees 18:11 And he read to you of Abel killed by Kain and Isaak being offered as a whole offering and Ioseph in prison.
4 Maccabees 18:12 And he told you of the zealous Phinees, and taught you of Ananias and Azarias and Misael in fire.
4 Maccabees 18:13 And he also glorified Daniel in the lions' pit, whom he pronounced blessed.
4 Maccabees 18:14 And he also reminded you of the writing of Esaias that says, ‘Even if you pass through fire, a flame will not burn you up.’
4 Maccabees 18:15 He sang to you the hymn-writer Dauid, saying, ‘Many are the afflictions of the righteous.’
4 Maccabees 18:16 He recited proverbs to you from Salomon, saying, ‘It is a tree of life to those who do his will.’
4 Maccabees 18:17 He made credible Iezekiel, who says, ‘Will these dry bones live?’
4 Maccabees 18:18 For he did not forget to teach the song that Moyses taught, which says,
4 Maccabees 18:19 ‘I will kill and make alive; this is your life and the length of your days.’”
4 Maccabees 18:20 O bitter day then and not bitter, when the bitter tyrant of the Greeks, quenching fire with fire in cruel cauldrons and with boiling rages, brought the seven children of the woman of Abraam onto the catapult and again to his tortures,
4 Maccabees 18:21 maimed the pupils of their eyes and cut out their tongues and killed them with varied tortures.
4 Maccabees 18:22 For these things divine justice pursued and will pursue the accursed tyrant.
4 Maccabees 18:23 But the children of Abraam, with their prize-bearing mother, gather together into the chorus of the fathers, having received pure and immortal souls from God.
4 Maccabees 18:24 To whom be the glory unto the ages of the ages; amen.

# Psalms

The Apostolic Bible. Public domain. https://apostolic-bible.ysys9.chatgpt.site/license.html


## Chapter 1

Psalms 1:1 Blessed is the man who did not walk in the counsel of the impious and did not stand in the way of sinners and did not sit on the seat of pestilent men,
Psalms 1:2 but his will is in the law of the Lord, and in his law he will meditate by day and by night.
Psalms 1:3 And he will be like the tree planted beside the outlets of the waters, which will give its fruit in its season, and its leaf will not fall off; and everything he does will be prospered.
Psalms 1:4 Not so the impious, not so, but like the chaff that the wind casts away from the face of the earth.
Psalms 1:5 Because of this the impious will not rise in judgment, nor sinners in the counsel of the righteous;
Psalms 1:6 for the Lord knows the way of the righteous, and the way of the impious will perish.

## Chapter 2

Psalms 2:1 Why did nations rage and peoples meditate on empty things?
Psalms 2:2 The kings of the earth stood forth, and the rulers gathered together against the Lord and against his anointed one. Interlude.
Psalms 2:3 “Let us tear apart their bonds and cast away their yoke from us.”
Psalms 2:4 The one dwelling in the heavens will laugh at them, and the Lord will mock them.
Psalms 2:5 Then he will speak to them in his wrath and in his anger will trouble them.
Psalms 2:6 “But I was appointed king by him upon Sion, his holy mountain,
Psalms 2:7 proclaiming the ordinance of the Lord. The Lord said to me, ‘You are my son; I have begotten you today;
Psalms 2:8 ask of me, and I will give you nations as your inheritance and the ends of the earth as your possession;
Psalms 2:9 you will shepherd them with an iron rod; like a potter's vessel you will shatter them.’”
Psalms 2:10 And now, kings, understand; be instructed, all who judge the earth.
Psalms 2:11 Serve the Lord in fear and exult in him with trembling.
Psalms 2:12 Take hold of instruction, lest the Lord become angry and you perish from a righteous way. When his anger is quickly kindled, blessed are all who have trusted in him.

## Chapter 3
