Psalms 3:1 A psalm for Dauid, when he was fleeing from the presence of Abessalom his son.
Psalms 3:2 Lord, why have those afflicting me multiplied? Many rise up against me;
Psalms 3:3 many say to my soul, “There is no salvation for him in his God.” Interlude.
Psalms 3:4 But you, Lord, are my helper, my glory and the one lifting up my head.
Psalms 3:5 With my voice I cried to the Lord, and he heard me from his holy mountain. Interlude.
Psalms 3:6 I lay down and slept; I awoke, for the Lord will help me.
Psalms 3:7 I will not fear myriads of people who together attack me all around.
Psalms 3:8 Rise, Lord; save me, my God, for you struck all those who are my enemies without cause; you shattered sinners' teeth.
Psalms 3:9 Salvation belongs to the Lord, and your blessing is upon your people.

## Chapter 4

Psalms 4:1 For the end, in psalms; a song for Dauid.
Psalms 4:2 When I called, the God of my righteousness heard me; in affliction you made room for me; have compassion on me and hear my prayer.
Psalms 4:3 Sons of humans, how long will you be heavy-hearted? Why do you love vanity and seek falsehood? Interlude.
Psalms 4:4 And know that the Lord made his holy one wondrous; the Lord will hear me when I cry to him.
Psalms 4:5 Be angry and do not sin; speak in your hearts and upon your beds be pierced with remorse. Interlude.
Psalms 4:6 Sacrifice a sacrifice of righteousness and hope in the Lord.
Psalms 4:7 Many say, “Who will show us good things?” The light of your face was marked upon us, Lord.
Psalms 4:8 You gave gladness into my heart; from the season of their grain and wine and oil they were multiplied.
Psalms 4:9 In peace I will both lie down and sleep, for you, Lord, alone made me dwell in hope.

## Chapter 5

Psalms 5:1 For the end, concerning her who inherits; a psalm for Dauid.
Psalms 5:2 Give ear to my words, Lord; understand my cry;
Psalms 5:3 attend to the voice of my petition, my king and my God. For to you I will pray, Lord;
Psalms 5:4 in the morning you will hear my voice; in the morning I will stand before you and watch.
Psalms 5:5 For you are not a God willing lawlessness, nor will one doing evil sojourn with you;
Psalms 5:6 lawless men will not remain before your eyes; you hated all who work lawlessness.
Psalms 5:7 You will destroy all who speak falsehood; the Lord abhors a man of bloodshed and deceit.
Psalms 5:8 But I, in the abundance of your mercy, will enter your house; I will bow toward your holy temple in fear of you.
Psalms 5:9 Lord, guide me in your righteousness because of my enemies; make your way straight before me.
Psalms 5:10 For there is no truth in their mouth; their heart is vain; their throat is an opened grave; with their tongues they practiced deceit.
Psalms 5:11 Judge them, God; let them fall away from their counsels; according to the abundance of their impieties cast them out, for they embittered you, Lord.
Psalms 5:12 And let all who hope in you be glad; they will exult forever, and you will dwell among them, and all who love your name will boast in you.
Psalms 5:13 For you will bless a righteous man; Lord, as with a shield of favor you crowned us.

## Chapter 6

Psalms 6:1 For the end, in hymns, concerning the eighth; a psalm for Dauid.
Psalms 6:2 Lord, do not rebuke me in your anger nor instruct me in your wrath.
Psalms 6:3 Have mercy on me, Lord, for I am weak; heal me, Lord, for my bones were troubled,
Psalms 6:4 and my soul was exceedingly troubled; and you, Lord, how long?
Psalms 6:5 Return, Lord; rescue my soul; save me for the sake of your mercy.
Psalms 6:6 For in death there is no one remembering you; and in Hades who will give thanks to you?
Psalms 6:7 I grew weary in my groaning; every night I will wash my bed; with my tears I will wet my bedding.
Psalms 6:8 My eye was troubled from anger; I grew old among all my enemies.
Psalms 6:9 Depart from me, all who work lawlessness, for the Lord heard the voice of my weeping;
Psalms 6:10 the Lord heard my petition; the Lord accepted my prayer.
Psalms 6:11 May all my enemies be ashamed and exceedingly troubled; may they turn back and be exceedingly put to shame swiftly.

## Chapter 7

Psalms 7:1 A psalm for Dauid, which he sang to the Lord concerning the words of Chousi son of Iemeni.
Psalms 7:2 Lord my God, in you I hoped; save me from all who pursue me and rescue me,
Psalms 7:3 lest he seize my soul like a lion, with no one redeeming or saving.
Psalms 7:4 Lord my God, if I did this, if there is injustice in my hands,
Psalms 7:5 if I repaid evil to those repaying me, then may I fall away empty from my enemies,
Psalms 7:6 then may the enemy pursue my soul and overtake it and trample my life into the earth and make my glory dwell in dust. Interlude.
Psalms 7:7 Rise, Lord, in your wrath; be exalted at the boundaries of my enemies; awake, Lord my God, in the ordinance that you commanded,
Psalms 7:8 and a gathering of peoples will surround you, and for its sake return on high.
Psalms 7:9 The Lord will judge peoples; judge me, Lord, according to my righteousness and according to my innocence upon me.
Psalms 7:10 Let the wickedness of sinners now come to an end, and you will direct a righteous man; God examines hearts and kidneys.
Psalms 7:11 My help is righteous, from God who saves the upright in heart.
Psalms 7:12 God is a righteous judge and strong and long-suffering, not bringing wrath every day.
Psalms 7:13 If you do not turn back, he will polish his sword; he drew his bow and prepared it,
Psalms 7:14 and on it he prepared instruments of death; he fashioned his arrows for those being burned.
Psalms 7:15 Look, he labored with injustice, conceived trouble and gave birth to lawlessness;
Psalms 7:16 he dug a pit and excavated it and will fall into the hole that he made;
Psalms 7:17 his trouble will return upon his head, and his injustice will descend upon his crown.
Psalms 7:18 I will give thanks to the Lord according to his righteousness and sing to the name of the Lord Most High.

## Chapter 8

Psalms 8:1 For the end, concerning the winepresses; a psalm for Dauid.
Psalms 8:2 Lord our Lord, how wondrous is your name in all the earth, for your magnificence was lifted above the heavens.
Psalms 8:3 From the mouth of infants and nursing children you established praise because of your enemies, to overthrow an enemy and an avenger.
Psalms 8:4 For I will see the heavens, works of your fingers, the moon and stars, which you founded.
Psalms 8:5 What is a human that you remember him, or a son of a human that you visit him?
Psalms 8:6 You made him a little less than angels; with glory and honor you crowned him;
Psalms 8:7 and you appointed him over the works of your hands; you subjected everything beneath his feet,
Psalms 8:8 sheep and all oxen, and also the beasts of the plain,
Psalms 8:9 the birds of heaven and the fish of the sea, the things passing along paths of seas.
Psalms 8:10 Lord our Lord, how wondrous is your name in all the earth.

## Chapter 9

Psalms 9:1 For the end, concerning the hidden things of the son; a psalm for Dauid.
Psalms 9:2 I will give thanks to you, Lord, with my whole heart; I will recount all your wonders;
Psalms 9:3 I will be glad and exult in you; I will sing to your name, Most High.
Psalms 9:4 When my enemy turns backward, they will weaken and perish from your presence,
Psalms 9:5 for you carried out my judgment and my cause; you sat upon a throne, judging righteousness.
Psalms 9:6 You rebuked nations, and the impious one perished; you erased their name forever and for the age of the age;
Psalms 9:7 the enemy's swords failed completely, and you pulled down cities; their remembrance perished with a sound.
Psalms 9:8 And the Lord remains forever; he prepared his throne in judgment,
Psalms 9:9 and he himself will judge the inhabited world in righteousness; he will judge peoples in uprightness.
Psalms 9:10 And the Lord became a refuge for the needy, a helper at opportune times in affliction;
Psalms 9:11 and let those knowing your name hope in you, for you did not abandon those seeking you, Lord.
Psalms 9:12 Sing to the Lord who dwells in Sion; proclaim his practices among the nations,
Psalms 9:13 for, seeking out bloodshed, he remembered them; he did not forget the cry of the needy.
Psalms 9:14 Have mercy on me, Lord; see my humiliation from my enemies, you who lift me from the gates of death,
Psalms 9:15 so that I may proclaim all your praises in the gates of the daughter of Sion; I will exult in your salvation.
Psalms 9:16 Nations were caught in the destruction that they made; in this trap that they hid their foot was seized;
Psalms 9:17 the Lord is known by executing judgments; in the works of his hands the sinner was seized. A song of interlude.
Psalms 9:18 Let sinners turn back into Hades, all the nations forgetting God;
Psalms 9:19 for the poor will not be forgotten completely; the endurance of the needy will not perish forever.
Psalms 9:20 Rise, Lord; let a human not grow strong; let nations be judged before you;
Psalms 9:21 appoint, Lord, a lawgiver over them; let nations know that they are humans. Interlude.
Psalms 9:22 Why, Lord, have you stood far away, overlooking at opportune times in affliction?
Psalms 9:23 When the impious one acts arrogantly, the poor one is set on fire; they are caught in the counsels that they devise.
Psalms 9:24 For the sinner is praised in the desires of his soul, and the one doing injustice is blessed;
Psalms 9:25 the sinner provoked the Lord: “According to the abundance of his wrath he will not seek out”; God is not before him.
Psalms 9:26 His ways are profaned at every time; your judgments are removed from his presence; he will lord it over all his enemies;
Psalms 9:27 for he said in his heart, “I will certainly not be shaken, from generation to generation without evil.”
Psalms 9:28 His mouth is full of a curse and bitterness and deceit; under his tongue are toil and trouble.
Psalms 9:29 He sits in ambush with rich men, in hidden places to kill an innocent man; his eyes look toward the needy;
Psalms 9:30 he lies in ambush in a hidden place like a lion in his enclosure; he lies in ambush to seize a poor man, to seize a poor man by dragging him;
Psalms 9:31 in his trap he will humble him; he will stoop and fall when he lords it over the needy.
Psalms 9:32 For he said in his heart, “God has forgotten; he turned away his face so as not to see at all.”
Psalms 9:33 Rise, Lord God; let your hand be lifted up; do not forget the needy;
Psalms 9:34 for what reason did the impious one provoke God? For he said in his heart, “He will not seek out.”
Psalms 9:35 You see, for you observe trouble and anger, to deliver them into your hands; to you, therefore, the poor one has been left; you were helping the orphan.
Psalms 9:36 Shatter the arm of the sinful and wicked one; his sin will be sought, and he will certainly not be found because of it;
Psalms 9:37 the Lord will reign forever and for the age of the age; you will perish, nations, from his earth.
Psalms 9:38 The Lord heard the desire of the needy; your ear attended to the preparation of their heart,
Psalms 9:39 to judge for the orphan and the lowly, so that a human upon the earth may no longer continue boasting greatly.

## Chapter 10

Psalms 10:1 For the end; a psalm for Dauid. In the Lord I have trusted; everyone, will you say to my soul, “Migrate to the mountains like a little bird”?
Psalms 10:2 For look, sinners drew a bow; they prepared arrows for a quiver, to shoot in the dark moon at the upright in heart.
Psalms 10:3 For what you established they pulled down; but what did the righteous one do?
Psalms 10:4 The Lord is in his holy temple; the Lord, his throne is in heaven. His eyes look toward the needy; his eyelids examine the sons of humans.
Psalms 10:5 The Lord examines the righteous and the impious, but the one loving injustice hates his own soul.
Psalms 10:6 He will rain traps upon sinners; fire and sulfur and a storm wind are the portion of their cup.
Psalms 10:7 For the Lord is righteous and loved righteous deeds; his face saw uprightness.

## Chapter 11

Psalms 11:1 For the end, concerning the eighth; a psalm for Dauid.
Psalms 11:2 Save me, Lord, for a holy one has failed, for truths have diminished among the sons of humans.
Psalms 11:3 Each spoke vain things to his neighbor; deceitful lips spoke with a heart and with a heart.
Psalms 11:4 May the Lord destroy all deceitful lips and a boastful tongue,
Psalms 11:5 those who said, “We magnify our tongue; our lips are from us; who is our lord?”
Psalms 11:6 “Because of the misery of the poor and because of the groaning of the needy, now I will rise,” says the Lord; “I will place in salvation; I will speak openly in it.”
Psalms 11:7 The sayings of the Lord are pure sayings, silver tried by fire, tested for the earth, purified sevenfold.
Psalms 11:8 You, Lord, will guard us and preserve us from this generation and forever.
Psalms 11:9 The impious walk all around; according to your height you cared greatly for the sons of humans.

## Chapter 12

Psalms 12:1 For the end; a psalm for Dauid.
Psalms 12:2 How long, Lord, will you forget me completely? How long will you turn your face away from me?
Psalms 12:3 Until when will I set counsels in my soul, pains in my heart by day? How long will my enemy be exalted over me?
Psalms 12:4 Look upon me; hear me, Lord my God; enlighten my eyes, lest I sleep unto death,
Psalms 12:5 lest my enemy say, “I prevailed against him”; those afflicting me will exult if I am shaken.
Psalms 12:6 But I hoped in your mercy; my heart will exult in your salvation; I will sing to the Lord who benefited me and sing to the name of the Lord Most High.

## Chapter 13

Psalms 13:1 For the end; a psalm for Dauid. A fool said in his heart, “There is no God”; they corrupted and became abominable in their practices; there is no one doing goodness, there is not even one.
Psalms 13:2 The Lord looked down from heaven upon the sons of humans to see whether there is one understanding or seeking God.
Psalms 13:3 All turned aside; together they became worthless; there is no one doing goodness, there is not even one. [Their throat is an opened grave; with their tongues they practiced deceit; the venom of asps is under their lips, whose mouth is full of a curse and bitterness; their feet are swift to shed blood; destruction and misery are in their ways, and they did not know a way of peace; there is no fear of God before their eyes.]
Psalms 13:4 Will not all who work lawlessness know? Those devouring my people as a meal of bread did not call upon the Lord.
Psalms 13:5 There they became cowardly with fear where there was no fear, for God is in a righteous generation.
Psalms 13:6 You put a poor man's counsel to shame, for the Lord is his hope.
Psalms 13:7 Who will give the salvation of Israel from Sion? When the Lord returns the captivity of his people, let Iakob exult and let Israel be glad.

## Chapter 14

Psalms 14:1 A psalm for Dauid. Lord, who will sojourn in your dwelling, and who will dwell on your holy mountain?
Psalms 14:2 One walking blamelessly and working righteousness, speaking truth in his heart,
Psalms 14:3 who did not practice deceit with his tongue nor do evil to his neighbor and did not take up reproach against those nearest him;
Psalms 14:4 one doing evil is despised before him, but he glorifies those fearing the Lord; one swearing to his neighbor and not setting it aside;
Psalms 14:5 he did not give his silver at interest and did not take gifts against innocent people. One doing these things will not be shaken forever.

## Chapter 15

Psalms 15:1 An inscription on a pillar for Dauid. Guard me, Lord, for in you I hoped.
Psalms 15:2 I said to the Lord, “You are my Lord, for you have no need of my good things.”
Psalms 15:3 For the holy ones in his earth he made all his wishes wondrous among them.
Psalms 15:4 Their weaknesses were multiplied; after these things they hastened; I will certainly not gather their gatherings from bloodshed, nor will I remember their names through my lips.
Psalms 15:5 The Lord is the portion of my inheritance and of my cup; you are the one restoring my inheritance to me.
Psalms 15:6 Measuring cords fell to me among the best things; for indeed my inheritance is best for me.
Psalms 15:7 I will bless the Lord who gave me understanding; moreover, even until night my kidneys instructed me.
Psalms 15:8 I kept seeing the Lord before me continually, for he is at my right, so that I may not be shaken.
Psalms 15:9 Because of this my heart was glad and my tongue exulted; moreover, my flesh also will dwell in hope,
Psalms 15:10 for you will not abandon my soul to Hades nor allow your holy one to see corruption.
Psalms 15:11 You made known to me ways of life; you will fill me with gladness with your presence; delights are in your right hand to the end.

## Chapter 16

Psalms 16:1 A prayer of Dauid. Hear my righteousness, Lord; attend to my petition; give ear to my prayer, not with deceitful lips.
Psalms 16:2 May my judgment come out from your presence; let my eyes see upright things.
Psalms 16:3 You tested my heart; you visited by night; you tried me by fire, and injustice was not found in me.
Psalms 16:4 So that my mouth might not speak the works of humans, because of the words of your lips I guarded hard ways.
Psalms 16:5 Establish my steps in your paths, so that my steps may not be shaken.
Psalms 16:6 I cried, for you heard me, God; incline your ear to me and hear my words.
Psalms 16:7 Make your mercies wondrous, you who save those hoping in you from those resisting your right hand.
Psalms 16:8 Guard me like the pupil of an eye; in the shelter of your wings you will shelter me
Psalms 16:9 from the presence of the impious who made me miserable. My enemies surrounded my soul;
Psalms 16:10 they enclosed their fat; their mouth spoke arrogance.
Psalms 16:11 Casting me out, now they surrounded me; they set their eyes to turn aside upon the earth.
Psalms 16:12 They took me like a lion ready for prey and like a young lion dwelling in hidden places.
Psalms 16:13 Rise, Lord; get ahead of them and trip them up; rescue my soul from an impious man, your sword from the enemies of your hand.
Psalms 16:14 Lord, separate them from a few, from the earth, in their life. And their belly was filled with your hidden things; they were satisfied with sons and left the remnants to their infants.
Psalms 16:15 But I will appear before your face in righteousness; I will be satisfied when your glory appears.

## Chapter 17

Psalms 17:1 For the end; for the Lord's servant Dauid, the words of this song that he spoke to the Lord on the day when the Lord rescued him from the hand of all his enemies and from the hand of Saoul,
Psalms 17:2 and he said, “I will love you, Lord my strength.”
Psalms 17:3 The Lord is my firmness and my refuge and my rescuer; my God is my helper, and I will hope in him, my defender and the horn of my salvation, my helper.
Psalms 17:4 Praising, I will call upon the Lord, and I will be saved from my enemies.
Psalms 17:5 Birth pains of death surrounded me, and torrents of lawlessness greatly troubled me;
Psalms 17:6 birth pains of Hades encircled me; traps of death got ahead of me.
Psalms 17:7 And when I was afflicted I called upon the Lord and cried to my God; he heard my voice from his holy temple, and my cry before him will enter his ears.
Psalms 17:8 And the earth was shaken and became trembling, and the foundations of the mountains were troubled and shaken, for God became angry with them.
Psalms 17:9 Smoke went up in his wrath, and fire from his presence burned fiercely; coals were kindled from him.
Psalms 17:10 And he bent heaven and descended, and darkness was under his feet.
Psalms 17:11 And he mounted upon cheroubin and flew; he flew upon wings of winds.
Psalms 17:12 And he made darkness his hiding place; his tent was around him, dark water in clouds of the air.
Psalms 17:13 From the radiance before him the clouds passed, hail and coals of fire.
Psalms 17:14 And the Lord thundered from heaven, and the Most High gave his voice;
Psalms 17:15 and he sent out arrows and scattered them, and multiplied lightning flashes and threw them into confusion.
Psalms 17:16 And the springs of the waters appeared, and the foundations of the inhabited world were uncovered at your rebuke, Lord, at the blowing of the breath of your wrath.
Psalms 17:17 He sent out from on high and took me; he took me to himself out of many waters.
Psalms 17:18 He will rescue me from my mighty enemies and from those hating me, for they became stronger than I.
Psalms 17:19 They got ahead of me on the day of my affliction, and the Lord became my support
Psalms 17:20 and brought me out into a broad place; he will rescue me, for he wanted me. [He will rescue me from my mighty enemies and from those hating me.]
Psalms 17:21 And the Lord will repay me according to my righteousness, and according to the cleanness of my hands he will repay me,
Psalms 17:22 for I guarded the ways of the Lord and did not act impiously away from my God,
Psalms 17:23 for all his judgments are before me, and I did not put his ordinances away from me.
Psalms 17:24 And I will be blameless with him and guard myself from my lawlessness.
Psalms 17:25 And the Lord will repay me according to my righteousness and according to the cleanness of my hands before his eyes.
Psalms 17:26 With a holy one you will act holily, and with an innocent man you will be innocent,
Psalms 17:27 and with a chosen one you will be chosen, and with a crooked one you will act crookedly.
Psalms 17:28 For you will save a lowly people and humble the eyes of the arrogant.
Psalms 17:29 For you will light my lamp, Lord; my God, you will enlighten my darkness.
Psalms 17:30 For in you I will be rescued from a band of raiders, and in my God I will pass over a wall.
Psalms 17:31 My God, his way is blameless; the sayings of the Lord are tried by fire; he is defender of all who hope in him.
Psalms 17:32 For who is God except the Lord? And who is God except our God?
Psalms 17:33 God is the one girding me with power, and he made my way blameless,
Psalms 17:34 the one establishing my feet like a deer's and setting me upon the heights,
Psalms 17:35 teaching my hands for war; and you made my arms a bronze bow;
Psalms 17:36 and you gave me the defense of my salvation, and your right hand helped me, and your instruction set me upright completely, and your instruction itself will teach me.
Psalms 17:37 You broadened my steps beneath me, and my footprints did not weaken.
Psalms 17:38 I will pursue my enemies and overtake them and will not turn back until they fail;
Psalms 17:39 I will crush them, and they will certainly not be able to stand; they will fall under my feet.
Psalms 17:40 And you girded me with power for war; you fettered all who rose against me beneath me,
Psalms 17:41 and you gave me my enemies' back and destroyed those hating me.
Psalms 17:42 They cried, and there was no one saving; to the Lord, and he did not hear them.
Psalms 17:43 And I will grind them fine like dust before the wind; like mud of streets I will smooth them down.
Psalms 17:44 You will rescue me from the contradictions of a people; you will appoint me head of nations; a people whom I did not know served me,
Psalms 17:45 at the hearing of an ear it obeyed me; foreign sons lied to me,
Psalms 17:46 foreign sons grew old and limped away from their paths.
Psalms 17:47 The Lord lives, and blessed is my God, and let the God of my salvation be exalted,
Psalms 17:48 God who gives me acts of vengeance and subjected peoples beneath me,
Psalms 17:49 my rescuer from my angry enemies; you will exalt me above those rising against me; you will rescue me from an unjust man.
Psalms 17:50 Because of this I will give thanks to you among nations, Lord, and sing to your name,
Psalms 17:51 he who magnifies the salvations of his king and does mercy to his anointed one, to Dauid and to his seed forever.

## Chapter 18

Psalms 18:1 For the end; a psalm for Dauid.
Psalms 18:2 The heavens recount God's glory, and the firmament proclaims the making of his hands;
Psalms 18:3 day pours forth a word to day, and night proclaims knowledge to night.
Psalms 18:4 There are no speeches nor words whose voices are not heard;
Psalms 18:5 their sound went out into all the earth, and their words to the ends of the inhabited world. In the sun he set his dwelling;
Psalms 18:6 and he himself, like a bridegroom coming out of his bridal chamber, will exult like a giant to run his way.
Psalms 18:7 His departure is from the end of heaven, and his arrival as far as the end of heaven, and there is no one who will be hidden from his heat.
Psalms 18:8 The law of the Lord is blameless, turning souls back; the testimony of the Lord is faithful, making infants wise;
Psalms 18:9 the ordinances of the Lord are upright, gladdening a heart; the commandment of the Lord is radiant, enlightening eyes;
Psalms 18:10 the fear of the Lord is pure, remaining for the age of the age; the judgments of the Lord are true, justified together,
Psalms 18:11 desirable beyond gold and much precious stone, and sweeter than honey and honeycomb.
Psalms 18:12 For indeed your servant guards them; in guarding them there is much repayment.
Psalms 18:13 Who will understand trespasses? Cleanse me from my hidden things.
Psalms 18:14 And spare your servant from foreign ones; if they do not lord it over me, then I will be blameless and will be cleansed from great sin.
Psalms 18:15 And the sayings of my mouth and the meditation of my heart will be for acceptance before you continually, Lord, my helper and my redeemer.

## Chapter 19

Psalms 19:1 For the end; a psalm for Dauid.
Psalms 19:2 May the Lord hear you in a day of affliction; may the name of the God of Iakob defend you.
Psalms 19:3 May he send help to you from the holy place and help you from Sion.
Psalms 19:4 May he remember all your sacrifice, and let him make your whole burnt offering fat. Interlude.
Psalms 19:5 May he give you according to your heart and fulfill all your counsel.
Psalms 19:6 We will exult in your salvation and be magnified in the name of our God. May the Lord fulfill all your requests.
Psalms 19:7 Now I knew that the Lord saved his anointed one; he will hear him from his holy heaven; the salvation of his right hand is in mighty acts.
Psalms 19:8 These in chariots and these in horses, but we will be magnified in the name of the Lord our God.
Psalms 19:9 They were fettered together and fell, but we rose and were set upright.
Psalms 19:10 Lord, save your king and hear us on whatever day we call upon you.

## Chapter 20

Psalms 20:1 For the end; a psalm for Dauid.
Psalms 20:2 Lord, in your power the king will be glad and in your salvation he will exult exceedingly.
Psalms 20:3 You gave him the desire of his soul and did not deprive him of the wish of his lips. Interlude.
Psalms 20:4 For you went before him with blessings of goodness; you placed a crown of precious stone upon his head.
Psalms 20:5 He asked you for life, and you gave it to him, length of days for the age of the age.
Psalms 20:6 Great is his glory in your salvation; you will place glory and magnificence upon him;
Psalms 20:7 for you will give him blessing for the age of the age; you will gladden him with joy in your presence.
Psalms 20:8 For the king hopes in the Lord, and in the mercy of the Most High he will certainly not be shaken.
Psalms 20:9 May your hand be found by all your enemies; may your right hand find all who hate you.
Psalms 20:10 You will make them like an oven of fire at the time of your presence; the Lord in his wrath will throw them into confusion, and fire will devour them.
Psalms 20:11 You will destroy their fruit from the earth and their seed from the sons of humans,
Psalms 20:12 for they inclined evils against you; they devised a counsel that they will certainly not be able to establish.
Psalms 20:13 For you will make them turn their back; among your remnants you will prepare their face.
Psalms 20:14 Be exalted, Lord, in your power; we will sing and make music of your mighty acts.

## Chapter 21

Psalms 21:1 For the end, concerning the morning help; a psalm for Dauid.
Psalms 21:2 God, my God, attend to me; why did you abandon me? Far from my salvation are the words of my trespasses.
Psalms 21:3 My God, I will cry by day, and you will not hear, and by night, and it is not unto folly for me.
Psalms 21:4 But you dwell among holy ones, the praise of Israel.
Psalms 21:5 In you our fathers hoped; they hoped, and you rescued them;
Psalms 21:6 to you they cried and were saved; in you they hoped and were not put to shame.
Psalms 21:7 But I am a worm and not a human, a reproach of a human and a despised thing of a people.
Psalms 21:8 All who see me mocked me; they spoke with lips, they moved their head:
Psalms 21:9 “He hoped in the Lord; let him rescue him; let him save him, for he wants him.”
Psalms 21:10 For you are the one who drew me from the belly, my hope from my mother's breasts;
Psalms 21:11 upon you I was cast from the womb; from my mother's belly you are my God.
Psalms 21:12 Do not depart from me, for affliction is near, for there is no one helping.
Psalms 21:13 Many calves encircled me; fat bulls surrounded me;
Psalms 21:14 they opened their mouth against me like a lion seizing and roaring.
Psalms 21:15 Like water I was poured out, and all my bones were scattered; my heart became like wax melting in the midst of my belly;
Psalms 21:16 my strength dried up like a potsherd, and my tongue has stuck to my throat, and you brought me down into dust of death.
Psalms 21:17 For many dogs surrounded me; a gathering of evildoers surrounded me; they dug through my hands and feet.
Psalms 21:18 I counted all my bones, but they observed and looked upon me.
Psalms 21:19 They divided my garments among themselves and cast a lot for my clothing.
Psalms 21:20 But you, Lord, do not put my help far away; attend to my assistance.
Psalms 21:21 Rescue my soul from a sword and my only one from the hand of a dog;
Psalms 21:22 save me from a lion's mouth, and my humiliation from the horns of one-horned beasts.
Psalms 21:23 I will recount your name to my brothers; in the midst of an assembly I will hymn you:
Psalms 21:24 “You who fear the Lord, praise him; all the seed of Iakob, glorify him; let all the seed of Israel fear him,
Psalms 21:25 for he did not despise nor become vexed at the petition of the poor, nor turn his face away from me, and when I cried to him he heard me.”
Psalms 21:26 My praise is from you in a great assembly; I will pay my vows before those fearing him.
Psalms 21:27 The needy will eat and be filled, and those seeking him will praise the Lord; their hearts will live for the age of the age.
Psalms 21:28 All the ends of the earth will remember and turn back to the Lord, and all the families of the nations will bow before you,
Psalms 21:29 for the kingdom belongs to the Lord, and he rules the nations.
Psalms 21:30 All the fat ones of the earth ate and bowed; all those descending into the earth will fall before him. And my soul lives to him,
Psalms 21:31 and my seed will serve him; the coming generation will be proclaimed to the Lord,
Psalms 21:32 and they will proclaim his righteousness to a people who will be born, for the Lord did it.

## Chapter 22

Psalms 22:1 A psalm for Dauid. The Lord shepherds me, and nothing will be lacking to me.
Psalms 22:2 In a place of green grass, there he made me dwell; at water of rest he nourished me;
Psalms 22:3 he turned my soul back. He guided me upon paths of righteousness for the sake of his name.
Psalms 22:4 For even if I walk in the midst of a shadow of death, I will not fear evils, for you are with me; your rod and your staff, these comforted me.
Psalms 22:5 You prepared a table before me opposite those afflicting me; you enriched my head with oil, and your cup intoxicates like the best.
Psalms 22:6 And your mercy will pursue me all the days of my life, and my dwelling in the Lord's house will be for length of days.

## Chapter 23

Psalms 23:1 A psalm for Dauid; of the first day of the week. The earth belongs to the Lord and its fullness, the inhabited world and all who dwell in it;
Psalms 23:2 he founded it upon seas and prepared it upon rivers.
Psalms 23:3 Who will ascend to the mountain of the Lord, and who will stand in his holy place?
Psalms 23:4 One innocent in hands and pure in heart, who did not take his soul for vanity and did not swear deceitfully to his neighbor.
Psalms 23:5 This one will receive blessing from the Lord and mercy from God his savior.
Psalms 23:6 This is the generation of those seeking him, seeking the face of the God of Iakob. Interlude.
Psalms 23:7 Raise gates, your rulers, and be lifted up, eternal gates, and the king of glory will enter.
Psalms 23:8 Who is this king of glory? The Lord strong and mighty, the Lord mighty in war.
Psalms 23:9 Raise gates, your rulers, and be lifted up, eternal gates, and the king of glory will enter.
Psalms 23:10 Who is this king of glory? The Lord of powers, he is the king of glory.

## Chapter 24

Psalms 24:1 A psalm for Dauid. To you, Lord, I lifted my soul, my God.
Psalms 24:2 In you I have trusted; may I not be put to shame, nor let my enemies laugh at me.
Psalms 24:3 For indeed all who wait for you will certainly not be put to shame; let all who act lawlessly without cause be ashamed.
Psalms 24:4 Make your ways known to me, Lord, and teach me your paths.
Psalms 24:5 Guide me into your truth and teach me, for you are God my savior, and I waited for you the whole day.
Psalms 24:6 Remember your compassions, Lord, and your mercies, for they are from eternity.
Psalms 24:7 Do not remember the sins of my youth and my ignorance; according to your mercy remember me yourself, for the sake of your goodness, Lord.
Psalms 24:8 Good and upright is the Lord; because of this he will instruct sinners in the way.
Psalms 24:9 He will guide the meek in judgment; he will teach the meek his ways.
Psalms 24:10 All the Lord's ways are mercy and truth for those seeking his covenant and his testimonies.
Psalms 24:11 For the sake of your name, Lord, you will also be gracious toward my sin, for it is great.
Psalms 24:12 Who is the human fearing the Lord? He will instruct him in the way that he chose.
Psalms 24:13 His soul will lodge among good things, and his seed will inherit earth.
Psalms 24:14 The Lord is the strength of those fearing him, [and the name of the Lord belongs to those fearing him,] and his covenant is to make it plain to them.
Psalms 24:15 My eyes are continually toward the Lord, for he himself will draw my feet out of a trap.
Psalms 24:16 Look upon me and have mercy on me, for I am alone and poor.
Psalms 24:17 The afflictions of my heart were broadened; bring me out of my necessities.
Psalms 24:18 See my humiliation and my toil and forgive all my sins.
Psalms 24:19 See my enemies, for they multiplied and hated me with unjust hatred.
Psalms 24:20 Guard my soul and rescue me; may I not be put to shame, for I hoped in you.
Psalms 24:21 Innocent and upright men clung to me, for I waited for you, Lord.
Psalms 24:22 Redeem Israel, God, from all his afflictions.

## Chapter 25

Psalms 25:1 Of Dauid. Judge me, Lord, for I walked in my innocence, and hoping in the Lord I will certainly not weaken.
Psalms 25:2 Test me, Lord, and try me; try my kidneys and my heart by fire.
Psalms 25:3 For your mercy is before my eyes, and I was well pleasing in your truth.
Psalms 25:4 I did not sit with a council of vanity, and I will certainly not enter with those transgressing the law;
Psalms 25:5 I hated an assembly of evildoers, and I will certainly not sit with the impious.
Psalms 25:6 I will wash my hands among innocent people and circle your altar, Lord,
Psalms 25:7 to hear a voice of praise and recount all your wonders.
Psalms 25:8 Lord, I loved the beauty of your house and the place of the dwelling of your glory.
Psalms 25:9 Do not destroy my soul together with the impious, nor my life with men of bloodshed,
Psalms 25:10 in whose hands are lawless deeds; their right hand was filled with gifts.
Psalms 25:11 But I walked in my innocence; redeem me and have mercy on me.
Psalms 25:12 For my foot stood in uprightness; in assemblies I will bless you, Lord.

## Chapter 26

Psalms 26:1 Of Dauid; before being anointed. The Lord is my enlightenment and my savior; whom will I fear? The Lord is defender of my life; of whom will I be afraid?
Psalms 26:2 When evildoers drew near against me to eat my flesh, those afflicting me and my enemies themselves weakened and fell;
Psalms 26:3 if an encampment arrays itself against me, my heart will not fear; if war rises against me, in this I hope.
Psalms 26:4 One thing I asked from the Lord, this I will seek: that I dwell in the Lord's house all the days of my life, that I see the delight of the Lord and visit his temple.
Psalms 26:5 For he hid me in a tent on a day of my evils; he sheltered me in the hidden place of his tent; on a rock he exalted me;
Psalms 26:6 and now look, he lifted my head over my enemies; I circled and sacrificed a sacrifice of shouting in his tent; I will sing and make music to the Lord.
Psalms 26:7 Hear, Lord, my voice with which I cried; have mercy on me and hear me.
Psalms 26:8 My heart said to you, “It sought my face”; your face, Lord, I will seek.
Psalms 26:9 Do not turn your face away from me; do not turn aside in wrath from your servant; become my helper; do not spurn me and do not abandon me, God my savior.
Psalms 26:10 For my father and my mother abandoned me, but the Lord took me to himself.
Psalms 26:11 Instruct me, Lord, in your way and guide me in a straight path because of my enemies.
Psalms 26:12 Do not deliver me into the souls of those afflicting me, for unjust witnesses rose against me, and injustice lied to itself.
Psalms 26:13 I believe that I will see the good things of the Lord in the land of the living.
Psalms 26:14 Wait for the Lord; be courageous, and let your heart grow strong, and wait for the Lord.

## Chapter 27

Psalms 27:1 Of Dauid. To you, Lord, I cried, my God; do not keep silence toward me, lest you keep silence toward me and I become like those descending into a pit.
Psalms 27:2 Hear the voice of my petition when I petition you, when I lift my hands toward your holy temple.
Psalms 27:3 Do not drag my soul away with sinners, and do not destroy me together with those working injustice, who speak peace with their neighbors but have evils in their hearts.
Psalms 27:4 Give them according to their works and according to the wickedness of their practices; according to the works of their hands give them; repay their repayment to them.
Psalms 27:5 For they did not understand the works of the Lord and the works of his hands; you will pull them down and will certainly not build them up.
Psalms 27:6 Blessed is the Lord, for he heard the voice of my petition.
Psalms 27:7 The Lord is my helper and my defender; my heart hoped in him, and I was helped, and my flesh flourished anew; and from my will I will give thanks to him.
Psalms 27:8 The Lord is the strength of his people and defender of the salvations of his anointed one.
Psalms 27:9 Save your people and bless your inheritance and shepherd them and lift them up forever.

## Chapter 28

Psalms 28:1 A psalm for Dauid; of the departure of the tent. Bring to the Lord, sons of God; bring to the Lord sons of rams; bring to the Lord glory and honor,
Psalms 28:2 bring to the Lord glory for his name; bow to the Lord in his holy court.
Psalms 28:3 The Lord's voice is over the waters; the God of glory thundered; the Lord is over many waters.
Psalms 28:4 The Lord's voice is in strength; the Lord's voice is in magnificence.
Psalms 28:5 The voice of the Lord who shatters cedars; and the Lord will shatter the cedars of Libanos
Psalms 28:6 and grind them fine like the calf, Libanos, and the beloved one like a son of one-horned beasts.
Psalms 28:7 The voice of the Lord who cuts through a flame of fire,
Psalms 28:8 the voice of the Lord who shakes a wilderness; and the Lord will shake the wilderness of Kades.
Psalms 28:9 The voice of the Lord who establishes deer; and he will uncover forests; and in his temple everyone speaks glory.
Psalms 28:10 The Lord will settle the flood, and the Lord sits as king forever.
Psalms 28:11 The Lord will give strength to his people; the Lord will bless his people in peace.

## Chapter 29

Psalms 29:1 For the end; a psalm of a song of the dedication of the house; for Dauid.
Psalms 29:2 I will exalt you, Lord, for you took me up and did not gladden my enemies over me.
Psalms 29:3 Lord my God, I cried to you, and you healed me;
Psalms 29:4 Lord, you brought my soul up from Hades; you saved me from those descending into a pit.
Psalms 29:5 Sing to the Lord, his holy ones, and give thanks at the remembrance of his holiness;
Psalms 29:6 for wrath is in his anger, and life in his will; weeping will lodge in the evening, and exultation in the morning.
Psalms 29:7 But I said in my prosperity, “I will certainly not be shaken forever.”
Psalms 29:8 Lord, in your will you provided strength for my beauty; but you turned away your face, and I became troubled.
Psalms 29:9 To you, Lord, I will cry, and to my God I will petition:
Psalms 29:10 “What profit is there in my blood, in my descending into corruption? Will dust give thanks to you or proclaim your truth?”
Psalms 29:11 The Lord heard and had mercy on me; the Lord became my helper.
Psalms 29:12 You turned my mourning into dancing for me; you tore apart my sackcloth and girded me with gladness,
Psalms 29:13 so that my glory may sing to you and I may certainly not be pierced with grief; Lord my God, forever I will give thanks to you.

## Chapter 30

Psalms 30:1 For the end; a psalm for Dauid; of bewilderment.
Psalms 30:2 In you, Lord, I hoped; may I not be put to shame forever; in your righteousness rescue me and deliver me.
Psalms 30:3 Incline your ear toward me; hasten to deliver me; become for me a defending God and a house of refuge to save me.
Psalms 30:4 For you are my strength and my refuge, and for the sake of your name you will guide me and nourish me;
Psalms 30:5 you will bring me out of this trap that they hid for me, for you are my defender.
Psalms 30:6 Into your hands I will entrust my spirit; you redeemed me, Lord, God of truth.
Psalms 30:7 You hated those guarding vanities in vain; but I hoped in the Lord.
Psalms 30:8 I will exult and be glad in your mercy, for you looked upon my humiliation; you saved my soul from necessities
Psalms 30:9 and did not enclose me in an enemy's hands; you set my feet in a spacious place.
Psalms 30:10 Have mercy on me, Lord, for I am afflicted; my eye was troubled in anger, my soul and my belly.
Psalms 30:11 For my life failed in pain and my years in groanings; my strength weakened in poverty, and my bones were troubled.
Psalms 30:12 Among all my enemies I became a reproach, and exceedingly to my neighbors, and a fear to my acquaintances; those seeing me outside fled from me.
Psalms 30:13 I was forgotten from the heart like a dead man; I became like a lost vessel.
Psalms 30:14 For I heard the reproach of many dwelling all around; when they gathered together against me, they counseled to take my soul.
Psalms 30:15 But I hoped in you, Lord; I said, “You are my God.”
Psalms 30:16 My times are in your hands; rescue me from the hand of my enemies and from those pursuing me.
Psalms 30:17 Make your face shine upon your servant; save me in your mercy.
Psalms 30:18 Lord, may I not be put to shame, for I called upon you; may the impious be ashamed and brought down into Hades.
Psalms 30:19 Let deceitful lips become speechless, those speaking lawlessness against the righteous in arrogance and contempt.
Psalms 30:20 How great is the abundance of your goodness, Lord, which you hid for those fearing you, which you worked for those hoping in you before the sons of humans.
Psalms 30:21 You will hide them in the hidden place of your presence from the turmoil of humans; you will shelter them in a tent from the contradiction of tongues.
Psalms 30:22 Blessed is the Lord, for he made his mercy wondrous in a city under siege.
Psalms 30:23 But I said in my bewilderment, “Then I have been cast away from before your eyes.” Because of this you heard the voice of my petition when I cried to you.
Psalms 30:24 Love the Lord, all his holy ones, for the Lord seeks truths and repays those acting with excessive arrogance.
Psalms 30:25 Be courageous, and let your heart grow strong, all who hope in the Lord.

## Chapter 31

Psalms 31:1 For Dauid; of understanding. Blessed are those whose lawless deeds were forgiven and whose sins were covered;
Psalms 31:2 blessed is the man whose sin the Lord will certainly not reckon, nor is there deceit in his mouth.
Psalms 31:3 For I kept silence; my bones grew old from my crying the whole day;
Psalms 31:4 for by day and by night your hand weighed heavily upon me; I was turned into misery when a thorn was fixed in me. Interlude.
Psalms 31:5 I made my sin known and did not cover my lawlessness; I said, “I will declare against myself my lawlessness to the Lord”; and you forgave the impiety of my sin. Interlude.
Psalms 31:6 For this every holy one will pray to you at a suitable time; surely in a flood of many waters they will not draw near him.
Psalms 31:7 You are my refuge from the affliction surrounding me; my exultation, redeem me from those encircling me. Interlude.
Psalms 31:8 I will give you understanding and instruct you in this way that you will walk; I will fix my eyes upon you.
Psalms 31:9 Do not become like a horse and mule, in whom there is no understanding; with bridle and muzzle tighten their jaws, of those not drawing near you.
Psalms 31:10 Many are the scourges of the sinner, but mercy will surround the one hoping in the Lord.
Psalms 31:11 Be glad in the Lord and exult, righteous ones, and boast, all the upright in heart.

## Chapter 32

Psalms 32:1 For Dauid. Exult, righteous ones, in the Lord; praise befits the upright.
Psalms 32:2 Give thanks to the Lord with a lyre; with a ten-stringed psaltery sing to him.
Psalms 32:3 Sing him a new song; make music well with shouting.
Psalms 32:4 For the word of the Lord is upright, and all his works are in faithfulness;
Psalms 32:5 he loves mercy and judgment; the earth is full of the Lord's mercy.
Psalms 32:6 By the Lord's word the heavens were established, and by the breath of his mouth all their host;
Psalms 32:7 he gathers the sea's waters like a wineskin, placing abysses in treasuries.
Psalms 32:8 Let all the earth fear the Lord, and let all who inhabit the inhabited world be shaken before him;
Psalms 32:9 for he himself spoke, and they came to be; he himself commanded, and they were created.
Psalms 32:10 The Lord scatters nations' counsels, and sets aside peoples' reasonings and sets aside rulers' counsels;
Psalms 32:11 but the Lord's counsel remains forever, the reasonings of his heart from generation to generation.
Psalms 32:12 Blessed is the nation whose God is the Lord, the people whom he chose as an inheritance for himself.
Psalms 32:13 From heaven the Lord looked down; he saw all the sons of humans;
Psalms 32:14 from his prepared dwelling he looked upon all who inhabit the earth,
Psalms 32:15 he who formed their hearts individually, who understands all their works.
Psalms 32:16 A king is not saved through a great host, and a giant will not be saved by the abundance of his strength;
Psalms 32:17 a horse is false for salvation, and in the abundance of its power it will not be saved.
Psalms 32:18 Look, the Lord's eyes are upon those fearing him, those hoping in his mercy,
Psalms 32:19 to rescue their souls from death and nourish them in famine.
Psalms 32:20 Our soul waits for the Lord, for he is our helper and defender;
Psalms 32:21 for in him our heart will be glad, and in his holy name we hoped.
Psalms 32:22 May your mercy, Lord, be upon us, just as we hoped in you.

## Chapter 33

Psalms 33:1 For Dauid, when he altered his face before Abimelech, and he released him, and he departed.
Psalms 33:2 I will bless the Lord at every time; continually his praise is in my mouth.
Psalms 33:3 In the Lord my soul will be praised; let the meek hear and be glad.
Psalms 33:4 Magnify the Lord with me, and let us exalt his name together.
Psalms 33:5 I sought the Lord, and he heard me and rescued me from all my sojournings.
Psalms 33:6 Draw near him and be enlightened, and your faces will certainly not be put to shame.
Psalms 33:7 This poor man cried, and the Lord heard him and saved him from all his afflictions.
Psalms 33:8 An angel of the Lord will encamp around those fearing him and rescue them.
Psalms 33:9 Taste and see that the Lord is good; blessed is the man who hopes in him.
Psalms 33:10 Fear the Lord, his holy ones, for there is no lack for those fearing him.
Psalms 33:11 Rich men became poor and hungry, but those seeking the Lord will not be deprived of any good thing. Interlude.
Psalms 33:12 Come, children, hear me; I will teach you fear of the Lord.
Psalms 33:13 Who is the human desiring life, loving to see good days?
Psalms 33:14 Stop your tongue from evil and your lips from speaking deceit.
Psalms 33:15 Turn aside from evil and do good; seek peace and pursue it.
Psalms 33:16 The Lord's eyes are upon the righteous, and his ears toward their petition.
Psalms 33:17 But the Lord's face is against those doing evils, to destroy their remembrance from the earth.
Psalms 33:18 The righteous cried, and the Lord heard them and rescued them from all their afflictions.
Psalms 33:19 The Lord is near those broken in heart, and he will save the lowly in spirit.
Psalms 33:20 Many are the afflictions of the righteous, and from all of them he will rescue them.
Psalms 33:21 The Lord guards all their bones; not one of them will be shattered.
Psalms 33:22 The death of sinners is evil, and those hating the righteous one will offend.
Psalms 33:23 The Lord will redeem the souls of his servants, and all who hope in him will certainly not offend.

## Chapter 34

Psalms 34:1 For Dauid. Judge, Lord, those wronging me; wage war against those warring against me.
Psalms 34:2 Take hold of a shield and a large shield, and rise to my help;
Psalms 34:3 draw out a sword and close off against those pursuing me; say to my soul, “I am your salvation.”
Psalms 34:4 Let those seeking my soul be ashamed and abashed; let those devising evils for me turn backward and be put to shame.
Psalms 34:5 Let them become like chaff before the wind, and an angel of the Lord pressing them out;
Psalms 34:6 let their way become darkness and slipping, and an angel of the Lord pursuing them;
Psalms 34:7 for without cause they hid the destruction of their trap for me; in vain they reproached my soul.
Psalms 34:8 Let a trap come to them that they do not know, and let the snare that they hid catch them, and they will fall in the trap, in it.
Psalms 34:9 But my soul will exult in the Lord; it will delight in his salvation;
Psalms 34:10 all my bones will say, “Lord, who is like you, rescuing a poor man from the hand of those stronger than he, and a poor and needy man from those plundering him?”
Psalms 34:11 Unjust witnesses rose and questioned me about things I did not know;
Psalms 34:12 they repaid me wicked things for good things, and childlessness for my soul.
Psalms 34:13 But when they troubled me I clothed myself in sackcloth and humbled my soul with fasting, and my prayer will return into my bosom.
Psalms 34:14 As for a neighbor, as for our brother, so I was well pleasing; as one mourning and looking gloomy, so I humbled myself.
Psalms 34:15 And they were glad against me and gathered; scourges gathered against me, and I did not know; they were torn apart and were not pierced with remorse.
Psalms 34:16 They tried me; they mocked me with mockery; they gnashed their teeth against me.
Psalms 34:17 Lord, when will you look upon this? Restore my soul from their villainy, my only one from lions.
Psalms 34:18 I will give thanks to you, Lord, in a large assembly; among a mighty people I will praise you.
Psalms 34:19 May those unjustly hostile to me not rejoice over me, those hating me without cause and signaling with their eyes.
Psalms 34:20 For they spoke peaceful things to me, but devised deceits toward anger,
Psalms 34:21 and opened their mouth wide against me; they said, “Well done, well done, our eyes saw.”
Psalms 34:22 You saw, Lord; do not keep silence; Lord, do not depart from me;
Psalms 34:23 awake, Lord, and attend to my judgment, my God and my Lord, to my cause.
Psalms 34:24 Judge me according to your righteousness, Lord my God, and may they not rejoice over me;
Psalms 34:25 may they not say in their hearts, “Well done, well done for our soul”; nor may they say, “We swallowed him.”
Psalms 34:26 May those rejoicing at my evils be ashamed and abashed together; let those boasting greatly against me clothe themselves in shame and disgrace.
Psalms 34:27 May those desiring my righteousness exult and be glad, and let those desiring the peace of his servant say continually, “Let the Lord be magnified.”
Psalms 34:28 And my tongue will meditate on your righteousness, on your praise the whole day.

## Chapter 35

Psalms 35:1 For the end; for the Lord's servant Dauid.
Psalms 35:2 The lawless man speaks of sinning within himself; there is no fear of God before his eyes;
Psalms 35:3 for he practiced deceit before him, to find his lawlessness and hate it.
Psalms 35:4 The words of his mouth are lawlessness and deceit; he did not wish to understand so as to do good;
Psalms 35:5 he devised lawlessness upon his bed; he stood in every way that is not good, but was not vexed at wickedness.
Psalms 35:6 Lord, your mercy is in heaven, and your truth as far as the clouds;
Psalms 35:7 your righteousness is like mountains of God; your judgments are a great abyss; you will save humans and beasts, Lord.
Psalms 35:8 How you multiplied your mercy, God; and the sons of humans will hope in the shelter of your wings.
Psalms 35:9 They will be intoxicated with the richness of your house, and you will give them the torrent of your delight to drink;
Psalms 35:10 for with you is a spring of life; in your light we will see light.
Psalms 35:11 Extend your mercy to those knowing you and your righteousness to the upright in heart.
Psalms 35:12 Let a foot of arrogance not come to me, and may a hand of sinners not shake me.
Psalms 35:13 There those working lawlessness fell; they were cast out and will certainly not be able to stand.

## Chapter 36

Psalms 36:1 Of Dauid. Do not be jealous among evildoers, nor envy those doing lawlessness;
Psalms 36:2 for like grass they will quickly dry up, and like green herbs they will quickly fall away.
Psalms 36:3 Hope in the Lord and do goodness and dwell in the earth, and you will be shepherded upon its wealth;
Psalms 36:4 delight in the Lord, and he will give you the requests of your heart.
Psalms 36:5 Uncover your way to the Lord and hope in him, and he himself will act
Psalms 36:6 and bring out your righteousness like light and your judgment like midday.
Psalms 36:7 Be subjected to the Lord and entreat him; do not be jealous of the one prospering in his way, of a human committing lawless acts.
Psalms 36:8 Cease from wrath and abandon anger; do not be jealous so as to do evil;
Psalms 36:9 for evildoers will be destroyed, but those waiting for the Lord themselves will inherit earth.
Psalms 36:10 And yet a little while, and the sinner will certainly not exist, and you will seek his place and certainly not find it;
Psalms 36:11 but the meek will inherit earth and delight in an abundance of peace.
Psalms 36:12 The sinner will watch the righteous one and gnash his teeth against him;
Psalms 36:13 but the Lord will laugh at him, for he foresees that his day will come.
Psalms 36:14 Sinners drew a sword; they drew their bow to cast down a poor and needy man, to slaughter the upright in heart;
Psalms 36:15 may their sword enter their heart, and may their bows be shattered.
Psalms 36:16 A little for the righteous one is better than great wealth of sinners;
Psalms 36:17 for sinners' arms will be shattered, but the Lord supports the righteous.
Psalms 36:18 The Lord knows the ways of the blameless, and their inheritance will be forever;
Psalms 36:19 they will not be put to shame in an evil time, and in days of famine they will be satisfied.
Psalms 36:20 For sinners will perish, and the Lord's enemies, as soon as they are glorified and exalted, failing like smoke, failed.
Psalms 36:21 The sinner borrows and will not repay, but the righteous one has compassion and gives;
Psalms 36:22 for those blessing him will inherit earth, but those cursing him will be destroyed.
Psalms 36:23 A human's steps are directed by the Lord, and he will desire his way;
Psalms 36:24 when he falls, he will not be dashed down, for the Lord supports his hand.
Psalms 36:25 I was younger and indeed grew old, and I did not see a righteous man abandoned, nor his seed seeking loaves;
Psalms 36:26 the whole day he has mercy and lends, and his seed will be for a blessing.
Psalms 36:27 Turn aside from evil and do good and dwell for the age of the age;
Psalms 36:28 for the Lord loves judgment and will not abandon his holy ones; they will be guarded forever. But lawless ones will be driven out, and the seed of the impious will be destroyed;
Psalms 36:29 but the righteous will inherit earth and dwell upon it for the age of the age.
Psalms 36:30 A righteous one's mouth will meditate on wisdom, and his tongue will speak judgment;
Psalms 36:31 the law of his God is in his heart, and his steps will not be tripped up.
Psalms 36:32 The sinner observes the righteous one and seeks to put him to death,
Psalms 36:33 but the Lord will certainly not abandon him into his hands, nor condemn him when he is judged against him.
Psalms 36:34 Wait for the Lord and guard his way, and he will exalt you to inherit earth; when sinners are destroyed, you will see.
Psalms 36:35 I saw an impious man greatly exalted and lifted up like the cedars of Libanos;
Psalms 36:36 and I passed by, and look, he was not there, and I sought him, and his place was not found.
Psalms 36:37 Guard innocence and see uprightness, for there is a remnant for a peaceful human;
Psalms 36:38 but lawless men will be destroyed together; the remnants of the impious will be destroyed.
Psalms 36:39 But the salvation of the righteous is from the Lord, and he is their defender in a time of affliction,
Psalms 36:40 and the Lord will help them and rescue them and deliver them from sinners and save them, for they hoped in him.

## Chapter 37

Psalms 37:1 A psalm for Dauid; for remembrance concerning the sabbath.
Psalms 37:2 Lord, do not rebuke me in your anger nor instruct me in your wrath.
Psalms 37:3 For your arrows were fixed in me, and you pressed your hand upon me;
Psalms 37:4 there is no healing in my flesh because of your wrath; there is no peace for my bones because of my sins.
Psalms 37:5 For my lawless deeds rose over my head; like a heavy burden they weighed heavily upon me.
Psalms 37:6 My bruises stank and rotted because of my folly;
Psalms 37:7 I became miserable and was bowed down completely; the whole day I walked looking gloomy.
Psalms 37:8 For my loins were filled with mockeries, and there is no healing in my flesh;
Psalms 37:9 I was afflicted and humbled exceedingly; I roared from the groaning of my heart.
Psalms 37:10 Lord, all my desire is before you, and my groaning was not hidden from you.
Psalms 37:11 My heart was troubled; my strength abandoned me, and the light of my eyes, even it is not with me.
Psalms 37:12 My friends and my neighbors drew near opposite me and stood, and those nearest me stood far away;
Psalms 37:13 and those seeking my soul used force, and those seeking evils for me spoke vanities and meditated on deceits the whole day.
Psalms 37:14 But I, like a deaf man, did not hear, and like a speechless man not opening his mouth,
Psalms 37:15 and I became like a human not hearing and not having rebukes in his mouth.
Psalms 37:16 For in you, Lord, I hoped; you will hear, Lord my God.
Psalms 37:17 For I said, “Lest my enemies rejoice over me”; and when my feet were shaken they boasted greatly against me.
Psalms 37:18 For I am ready for scourges, and my pain is before me continually.
Psalms 37:19 For I will proclaim my lawlessness and be anxious about my sin.
Psalms 37:20 But my enemies live and have become stronger than I, and those unjustly hating me multiplied;
Psalms 37:21 those repaying evils for good things slandered me, since I pursued righteousness, [and they cast me, the beloved one, away like an abhorred dead man.]
Psalms 37:22 Do not abandon me, Lord; my God, do not depart from me;
Psalms 37:23 attend to my help, Lord of my salvation.

## Chapter 38

Psalms 38:1 For the end, for Idithoun; a song for Dauid.
Psalms 38:2 I said, “I will guard my ways so as not to sin with my tongue”; I placed a guard at my mouth when the sinner stood before me.
Psalms 38:3 I became deaf and was humbled and kept silence from good things, and my pain was renewed.
Psalms 38:4 My heart grew hot within me, and in my meditation fire will be kindled. I spoke with my tongue:
Psalms 38:5 “Make known to me, Lord, my end and the number of my days, what it is, so that I may know what I lack.
Psalms 38:6 Look, you made my days handbreadths, and my existence is like nothing before you; surely all things are vanity, every living human.” Interlude.
Psalms 38:7 Indeed, a human passes along in an image; surely they are troubled in vain; he treasures up and does not know for whom he will gather them.
Psalms 38:8 And now what is my waiting? Is it not the Lord? And my existence is from you.
Psalms 38:9 Rescue me from all my lawless deeds; you gave me as a reproach to a fool.
Psalms 38:10 I became deaf and did not open my mouth, for you are the one who made me.
Psalms 38:11 Remove your scourges from me; from the strength of your hand I failed.
Psalms 38:12 With rebukes for lawlessness you instructed a human and melted his soul like a spider; surely every human is troubled in vain. Interlude.
Psalms 38:13 Hear my prayer, Lord, and give ear to my petition; do not keep silence at my tears, for I am a sojourner with you and a stranger, as all my fathers.
Psalms 38:14 Release me, so that I may be refreshed before I depart and no longer exist.

## Chapter 39

Psalms 39:1 For the end; a psalm for Dauid.
Psalms 39:2 Waiting, I waited for the Lord, and he attended to me and heard my petition
Psalms 39:3 and brought me up from a pit of misery and from mud of mire, and set my feet upon a rock and directed my steps,
Psalms 39:4 and put a new song into my mouth, a hymn to our God; many will see and fear and hope in the Lord.
Psalms 39:5 Blessed is the man whose hope is the Lord's name, and who did not look toward vanities and false frenzies.
Psalms 39:6 You did many things, Lord my God, your wonders, and in your thoughts there is no one who will be likened to you; I proclaimed and spoke; they multiplied beyond number.
Psalms 39:7 You did not desire sacrifice and offering, but you fashioned ears for me; you did not ask for a whole burnt offering and an offering for sin.
Psalms 39:8 Then I said, “Look, I have come; in a scroll of a book it has been written concerning me;
Psalms 39:9 I wished to do your will, my God, and your law is in the midst of my belly.”
Psalms 39:10 I proclaimed righteousness as good news in a great assembly; look, I will certainly not restrain my lips; Lord, you knew.
Psalms 39:11 I did not hide your righteousness in my heart; I spoke your truth and your salvation; I did not hide your mercy and your truth from a large gathering.
Psalms 39:12 But you, Lord, do not put your compassions far from me; your mercy and your truth helped me continually.
Psalms 39:13 For evils surrounded me, of which there is no number; my lawless deeds overtook me, and I could not see; they multiplied beyond the hairs of my head, and my heart abandoned me.
Psalms 39:14 Be pleased, Lord, to rescue me; Lord, attend to helping me.
Psalms 39:15 May those seeking my soul to remove it be put to shame and abashed together; may those desiring evils for me turn backward and be abashed;
Psalms 39:16 let those saying to me, “Well done, well done,” receive their shame immediately.
Psalms 39:17 May all who seek you exult and be glad in you, Lord, and let those loving your salvation say continually, “Let the Lord be magnified.”
Psalms 39:18 But I am poor and needy; the Lord will care for me. You are my helper and my defender; my God, do not delay.

## Chapter 40

Psalms 40:1 For the end; a psalm for Dauid.
Psalms 40:2 Blessed is the one understanding concerning a poor and needy man; in an evil day the Lord will rescue him.
Psalms 40:3 May the Lord preserve him and make him live and pronounce him blessed on the earth, and may he not deliver him into his enemy's hands.
Psalms 40:4 May the Lord help him upon his bed of pain; you turned his whole bed in his sickness.
Psalms 40:5 I said, “Lord, have mercy on me; heal my soul, for I sinned against you.”
Psalms 40:6 My enemies spoke evils against me: “When will he die and his name perish?”
Psalms 40:7 And if he entered to see, he spoke vainly; his heart gathered lawlessness for itself; he went outside and spoke.
Psalms 40:8 All my enemies whispered together against me; against me they devised evils for me;
Psalms 40:9 they laid down a lawless word against me: “Surely the one lying down will not rise again?”
Psalms 40:10 For even the human of my peace, in whom I hoped, the one eating my loaves, magnified a heel-trip against me;
Psalms 40:11 but you, Lord, have mercy on me and raise me, and I will repay them.
Psalms 40:12 By this I knew that you have desired me, for my enemy will certainly not rejoice over me.
Psalms 40:13 But you helped me because of innocence, and you established me before you forever.
Psalms 40:14 Blessed is the Lord, the God of Israel, from eternity and unto eternity. May it be, may it be. – –

## Chapter 41

Psalms 41:1 For the end; for understanding, for the sons of Kore.
Psalms 41:2 As the deer longs for the springs of the waters, so my soul longs for you, God.
Psalms 41:3 My soul thirsted for the living God; when will I come and appear before God's face?
Psalms 41:4 My tears became bread for me by day and by night, while it was said to me every day, “Where is your God?”
Psalms 41:5 I remembered these things and poured out my soul upon me, for I will pass through the place of a wondrous tent as far as God's house, with a voice of exultation and thanksgiving, a sound of one celebrating a feast.
Psalms 41:6 Why are you sorrowful, soul, and why do you trouble me? Hope in God, for I will give thanks to him; my God is the salvation of my face.
Psalms 41:7 My soul was troubled within myself; because of this I will remember you from the land of Iordanes and Ermoniim, from a small mountain.
Psalms 41:8 Abyss calls upon abyss at the sound of your waterfalls; all your surges and your waves passed over me.
Psalms 41:9 By day the Lord will command his mercy, and by night a song is with me, a prayer to the God of my life.
Psalms 41:10 I will say to God, “You are my helper; why did you forget me? Why do I walk looking gloomy while my enemy oppresses?”
Psalms 41:11 While my bones were crushed, those afflicting me reproached me, saying to me every day, “Where is your God?”
Psalms 41:12 Why are you sorrowful, soul, and why do you trouble me? Hope in God, for I will give thanks to him; my God is the salvation of my face.

## Chapter 42

Psalms 42:1 A psalm for Dauid. Judge me, God, and judge my cause against an unholy nation; rescue me from an unjust and deceitful human.
Psalms 42:2 For you, God, are my strength; why did you reject me? And why do I walk looking gloomy while my enemy oppresses?
Psalms 42:3 Send out your light and your truth; these guided me and brought me to your holy mountain and to your dwellings.
Psalms 42:4 And I will enter toward God's altar, toward God who gladdens my youth; I will give thanks to you with a lyre, God, my God.
Psalms 42:5 Why are you sorrowful, soul, and why do you trouble me? Hope in God, for I will give thanks to him; my God is the salvation of my face.

## Chapter 43

Psalms 43:1 For the end; for the sons of Kore, a psalm for understanding.
Psalms 43:2 God, we heard with our ears; our fathers proclaimed to us a work that you worked in their days, in ancient days.
Psalms 43:3 Your hand destroyed nations, and you planted them; you afflicted peoples and cast them out.
Psalms 43:4 For they did not inherit earth by their sword, and their arm did not save them, but your right hand and your arm and the enlightenment of your face, for you were pleased with them.
Psalms 43:5 You yourself are my king and my God, commanding the salvations of Iakob;
Psalms 43:6 in you we will gore our enemies, and in your name we will despise those rising against us.
Psalms 43:7 For I will not hope in my bow, and my sword will not save me;
Psalms 43:8 for you saved us from those afflicting us and put those hating us to shame.
Psalms 43:9 In God we will be praised the whole day, and in your name we will give thanks forever. Interlude.
Psalms 43:10 But now you rejected and put us to shame, and you will not go out with our hosts;
Psalms 43:11 you turned us backward before our enemies, and those hating us plundered for themselves.
Psalms 43:12 You gave us like sheep for eating and scattered us among the nations;
Psalms 43:13 you sold your people without a price, and there was no abundance in their exchanges.
Psalms 43:14 You made us a reproach to our neighbors, mockery and ridicule to those around us;
Psalms 43:15 you made us a parable among the nations, a movement of the head among the peoples.
Psalms 43:16 The whole day my disgrace is before me, and the shame of my face covered me,
Psalms 43:17 from the voice of one reproaching and speaking abusively, from the presence of an enemy and persecutor.
Psalms 43:18 All these things came upon us, and we did not forget you and did not act unjustly in your covenant,
Psalms 43:19 and our heart did not depart backward; and you turned our paths aside from your way.
Psalms 43:20 For you humbled us in a place of affliction, and a shadow of death covered us.
Psalms 43:21 If we forgot the name of our God and if we spread out our hands toward a foreign god,
Psalms 43:22 will not God seek these things out? For he himself knows the hidden things of the heart.
Psalms 43:23 For because of you we are put to death the whole day; we were reckoned like sheep for slaughter.
Psalms 43:24 Awake; why do you sleep, Lord? Rise and do not reject completely.
Psalms 43:25 Why do you turn away your face, forget our poverty and our affliction?
Psalms 43:26 For our soul was humbled into dust; our belly stuck to the earth.
Psalms 43:27 Rise, Lord; help us and redeem us for the sake of your name.

## Chapter 44

Psalms 44:1 For the end, concerning those who will be changed; for the sons of Kore, for understanding; a song concerning the beloved one.
Psalms 44:2 My heart poured forth a good word; I speak my works to the king; my tongue is a reed of a swift-writing scribe.
Psalms 44:3 Beautiful in beauty beyond the sons of humans, grace was poured out on your lips; because of this God blessed you forever.
Psalms 44:4 Gird your sword upon your thigh, mighty one, in your beauty and your comeliness,
Psalms 44:5 and draw and prosper and reign for the sake of truth and meekness and righteousness, and your right hand will guide you wondrously.
Psalms 44:6 Your arrows are sharpened, mighty one—peoples will fall beneath you—in the heart of the king's enemies.
Psalms 44:7 Your throne, God, is for the age of the age; a rod of uprightness is the rod of your kingdom.
Psalms 44:8 You loved righteousness and hated lawlessness; because of this God, your God, anointed you with oil of exultation beyond your companions.
Psalms 44:9 Myrrh and stacte and cassia are from your garments, from ivory palaces, from which they gladdened you.
Psalms 44:10 Kings' daughters are in your honor; the queen stood at your right, clothed in gold-woven clothing, adorned in varied colors.
Psalms 44:11 Hear, daughter, and see and incline your ear, and forget your people and your father's house,
Psalms 44:12 for the king desired your beauty, for he himself is your lord.
Psalms 44:13 And daughters of Tyros will bow to him with gifts; the rich of the people will entreat your face.
Psalms 44:14 All her glory, a king's daughter, is within, clothed in golden fringes, adorned in varied colors.
Psalms 44:15 Virgins will be brought to the king behind her; her companions will be brought to you;
Psalms 44:16 they will be brought with gladness and exultation; they will be led into a king's temple.
Psalms 44:17 In place of your fathers sons came to be for you; you will appoint them rulers over all the earth.
Psalms 44:18 They will remember your name in every generation and generation; because of this peoples will give thanks to you forever and for the age of the age.

## Chapter 45

Psalms 45:1 For the end; concerning the sons of Kore, a psalm concerning the hidden things.
Psalms 45:2 Our God is refuge and power, a helper in the afflictions that found us exceedingly.
Psalms 45:3 Because of this we will not fear when the earth is troubled and mountains are moved into the hearts of seas.
Psalms 45:4 Their waters roared and were troubled; the mountains were troubled in his might. Interlude.
Psalms 45:5 The river's rushes gladden God's city; the Most High sanctified his dwelling.
Psalms 45:6 God is in its midst; it will not be shaken; God will help it toward morning.
Psalms 45:7 Nations were troubled; kingdoms inclined; he gave his voice; the earth was shaken.
Psalms 45:8 The Lord of powers is with us; our helper is the God of Iakob. Interlude.
Psalms 45:9 Come, see the Lord's works, the wonders he placed upon the earth.
Psalms 45:10 Removing wars as far as the ends of the earth, he will shatter a bow and break a weapon and burn shields in fire.
Psalms 45:11 Be at rest and know that I am God; I will be exalted among the nations; I will be exalted on the earth.
Psalms 45:12 The Lord of powers is with us; our helper is the God of Iakob.

## Chapter 46

Psalms 46:1 For the end; concerning the sons of Kore, a psalm.
Psalms 46:2 All the nations, clap your hands; shout to God with a voice of exultation,
Psalms 46:3 because the Lord Most High is fearsome, a great king over all the earth.
Psalms 46:4 He subjected peoples to us and nations beneath our feet;
Psalms 46:5 he chose for us his inheritance, the beauty of Iakob, which he loved. Interlude.
Psalms 46:6 God ascended with a shout, the Lord with the sound of a trumpet.
Psalms 46:7 Sing to our God, sing; sing to our king, sing,
Psalms 46:8 because God is king of all the earth; sing with understanding.
Psalms 46:9 God reigned over the nations; God sits upon his holy throne.
Psalms 46:10 Rulers of peoples were gathered with the God of Abraam, because the mighty ones of the earth belong to God; they were greatly exalted.

## Chapter 47

Psalms 47:1 A psalm of a song for the sons of Kore; on the second day of the week.
Psalms 47:2 Great is the Lord and greatly praiseworthy in the city of our God, his holy mountain,
Psalms 47:3 taking root well for the rejoicing of all the earth. Mountains of Sion, the sides of the north, the city of the great king,
Psalms 47:4 God is known in her citadels when he takes hold of her.
Psalms 47:5 Because, behold, the kings were gathered; they came together;
Psalms 47:6 they, seeing thus, marveled; they were troubled, they were shaken;
Psalms 47:7 trembling took hold of them; there were birth pangs there, as of a woman giving birth.
Psalms 47:8 With a violent wind you will shatter ships of Tharsis.
Psalms 47:9 Just as we heard, so we saw in the city of the Lord of powers, in the city of our God; God founded her forever. Interlude.
Psalms 47:10 We received your mercy, God, in the midst of your temple.
Psalms 47:11 According to your name, God, so also is your praise to the ends of the earth; your right hand is full of righteousness.
Psalms 47:12 Let Mount Sion rejoice; let the daughters of Ioudaia exult because of your judgments, Lord.
Psalms 47:13 Circle Sion and encompass her; recount her towers;
Psalms 47:14 Set your hearts upon her strength and examine her citadels, so that you may recount to another generation.
Psalms 47:15 Because this is God, our God, forever and for the age of the age; he will shepherd us for the ages.

## Chapter 48

Psalms 48:1 For the end; for the sons of Kore, a psalm.
Psalms 48:2 Hear these things, all the nations; give ear, all who inhabit the inhabited world,
Psalms 48:3 both the earthborn and the sons of humans, rich and poor together.
Psalms 48:4 My mouth will speak wisdom, and the meditation of my heart, understanding;
Psalms 48:5 I will incline my ear to a parable; I will open my riddle with a psaltery.
Psalms 48:6 Why am I afraid on an evil day? The lawlessness of my heel will surround me.
Psalms 48:7 Those who trust in their strength and boast in the multitude of their wealth,
Psalms 48:8 a brother is not redeemed; will a human redeem? He will not give God his propitiation
Psalms 48:9 and the price of the redemption of his soul.
Psalms 48:10 And he ceased forever and will live to the end, because he will not see destruction when he sees wise ones dying.
Psalms 48:11 Together the foolish and the senseless will perish and will leave their wealth to strangers,
Psalms 48:12 and their graves are their houses forever, their dwellings to generation and generation. They called their names upon their lands.
Psalms 48:13 And a human, being in honor, did not understand; he was compared to the senseless beasts and became like them.
Psalms 48:14 This way of theirs is a stumbling block to them, and after these things they will take pleasure in their mouth. Interlude.
Psalms 48:15 Like sheep they were placed in Hades; death shepherds them. And the upright will rule over them in the morning, and their help will grow old in Hades away from their glory.
Psalms 48:16 But God will redeem my soul from the hand of Hades when he takes me. Interlude.
Psalms 48:17 Do not be afraid when a human becomes rich and when the glory of his house is multiplied,
Psalms 48:18 because when he dies he will not take everything, nor will his glory descend with him.
Psalms 48:19 Because his soul will be blessed in his life; he will acknowledge you when you do good to him.
Psalms 48:20 He will enter as far as the generation of his fathers; forever he will not see light.
Psalms 48:21 A human, being in honor, did not understand; he was compared to the senseless beasts and became like them.

## Chapter 49

Psalms 49:1 A psalm for Asaph. The God of gods, the Lord, spoke and called the earth from the rising of the sun and as far as its setting.
Psalms 49:2 From Sion is the magnificence of his beauty; God will come visibly,
Psalms 49:3 our God, and he will not keep silent. Fire will burn before him, and around him a very great storm.
Psalms 49:4 He will summon heaven above and the earth to judge his people:
Psalms 49:5 Gather to him his holy ones, those making his covenant upon sacrifices,
Psalms 49:6 and the heavens will announce his righteousness, because God is judge. Interlude.
Psalms 49:7 Hear, my people, and I will speak to you, Israel, and I testify to you; I am God, your God.
Psalms 49:8 I will not reprove you for your sacrifices, and your whole burnt offerings are before me continually;
Psalms 49:9 I will not receive calves from your house or he-goats from your flocks.
Psalms 49:10 Because all the wild beasts of the forest are mine, beasts on the mountains and oxen;
