Psalms 49:11 I have known all the birds of heaven, and the beauty of the field is with me.
Psalms 49:12 If I hunger, I will certainly not tell you; for the inhabited world is mine, and its fullness.
Psalms 49:13 Surely I will not eat the flesh of bulls or drink the blood of goats?
Psalms 49:14 Sacrifice to God a sacrifice of praise, and pay your vows to the Most High;
Psalms 49:15 and call upon me on a day of affliction, and I will deliver you, and you will glorify me. Interlude.
Psalms 49:16 But to the sinner God said: Why do you recount my ordinances and take up my covenant through your mouth?
Psalms 49:17 But you hated discipline and cast my words behind you.
Psalms 49:18 If you saw a thief, you ran together with him, and you placed your portion with adulterers;
Psalms 49:19 your mouth abounded in evil, and your tongue wove deceit;
Psalms 49:20 sitting, you spoke against your brother, and against the son of your mother you placed a stumbling block.
Psalms 49:21 You did these things, and I kept silent; you supposed lawlessness, that I would be like you; I will reprove you and set it before your face.
Psalms 49:22 Understand these things, then, you who forget God, lest he seize and there be no one delivering;
Psalms 49:23 A sacrifice of praise will glorify me, and there is a way there by which I will show him the salvation of God.

## Chapter 50

Psalms 50:1 For the end; a psalm for Dauid,
Psalms 50:2 when Nathan the prophet came to him, when he went in to Bersabee.
Psalms 50:3 Have mercy on me, God, according to your great mercy, and according to the multitude of your compassions blot out my lawless deed;
Psalms 50:4 Wash me still more from my lawlessness, and cleanse me from my sin.
Psalms 50:5 Because I know my lawlessness, and my sin is before me continually.
Psalms 50:6 Against you alone I sinned and did what is evil before you, so that you may be justified in your words and prevail when you are judged.
Psalms 50:7 For behold, in lawless deeds I was conceived, and in sins my mother conceived me.
Psalms 50:8 For behold, you loved truth; the unrevealed and hidden things of your wisdom you made known to me.
Psalms 50:9 You will sprinkle me with hyssop, and I will be cleansed; you will wash me, and I will be made whiter than snow.
Psalms 50:10 You will make me hear exultation and gladness; humbled bones will exult.
Psalms 50:11 Turn your face away from my sins, and blot out all my lawless deeds.
Psalms 50:12 Create a clean heart in me, God, and renew an upright spirit in my inward parts.
Psalms 50:13 Do not cast me away from your face, and do not take your holy spirit away from me.
Psalms 50:14 Restore to me the exultation of your salvation, and support me with a ruling spirit.
Psalms 50:15 I will teach lawless ones your ways, and impious ones will turn back to you.
Psalms 50:16 Deliver me from bloods, God, the God of my salvation; my tongue will exult in your righteousness.
Psalms 50:17 Lord, you will open my lips, and my mouth will announce your praise.
Psalms 50:18 Because if you had wanted a sacrifice, I would have given it; you will not take pleasure in whole burnt offerings.
Psalms 50:19 A sacrifice to God is a broken spirit; a broken and humbled heart God will not despise.
Psalms 50:20 Do good to Sion, Lord, in your good pleasure, and let the walls of Ierousalem be built;
Psalms 50:21 then you will take pleasure in a sacrifice of righteousness, an offering and whole burnt offerings; then they will offer calves upon your altar.

## Chapter 51

Psalms 51:1 For the end; of understanding, for Dauid,
Psalms 51:2 when Doek the Idumaian came and announced to Saoul and said to him: Dauid came into the house of Abimelech.
Psalms 51:3 Why do you boast in evil, mighty one, of lawlessness all day?
Psalms 51:4 Your tongue devised injustice; like a sharpened razor you worked deceit.
Psalms 51:5 You loved evil more than goodness, injustice more than speaking righteousness. Interlude.
Psalms 51:6 You loved all words of drowning, a deceitful tongue.
Psalms 51:7 For this reason God will pull you down to the end; may he pluck you out and remove you from your dwelling, and your root from the land of the living. Interlude.
Psalms 51:8 And righteous ones will see and be afraid, and will laugh at him and say:
Psalms 51:9 Behold, a human who did not make God his helper, but hoped in the multitude of his wealth and was strengthened in his vanity.
Psalms 51:10 But I am like a fruitful olive tree in the house of God; I hoped in the mercy of God forever and for the age of the age.
Psalms 51:11 I will acknowledge you forever, because you acted, and I will wait for your name, because it is good before your holy ones.

## Chapter 52

Psalms 52:1 For the end, concerning maeleth; of understanding, for Dauid.
Psalms 52:2 A fool said in his heart: There is no God. They became corrupt and abominable in lawless deeds; there is no one doing good.
Psalms 52:3 God leaned down from heaven upon the sons of humans to see whether there is anyone understanding or seeking out God.
Psalms 52:4 All turned aside; together they became useless; there is no one doing good, there is not even one.
Psalms 52:5 Will not all who work lawlessness know? Those eating my people as food of bread did not call upon God.
Psalms 52:6 There they will fear a fear where there was no fear, because God scattered the bones of those pleasing humans; they were put to shame, because God despised them.
Psalms 52:7 Who will give the salvation of Israel from Sion? When the Lord turns back the captivity of his people, Iakob will exult and Israel will rejoice.

## Chapter 53

Psalms 53:1 For the end, in hymns; of understanding, for Dauid,
Psalms 53:2 when the Ziphaians came and said to Saoul: Behold, is not Dauid hidden among us?
Psalms 53:3 God, save me by your name, and judge me by your strength.
Psalms 53:4 God, hear my prayer; give ear to the words of my mouth.
Psalms 53:5 Because strangers rose against me, and mighty ones sought my soul; they did not set God before them. Interlude.
Psalms 53:6 For behold, God helps me, and the Lord is the supporter of my soul.
Psalms 53:7 He will turn the evils back upon my enemies; in your truth destroy them.
Psalms 53:8 Willingly I will sacrifice to you; I will acknowledge your name, Lord, because it is good;
Psalms 53:9 because you delivered me from every affliction, and my eye looked upon my enemies.

## Chapter 54

Psalms 54:1 For the end, in hymns; of understanding, for Dauid.
Psalms 54:2 Give ear, God, to my prayer, and do not overlook my supplication;
Psalms 54:3 attend to me and hear me. I was grieved in my meditation and troubled
Psalms 54:4 by the voice of an enemy and by the affliction of a sinner, because they turned lawlessness upon me and bore a grudge against me in wrath.
Psalms 54:5 My heart was troubled within me, and dread of death fell upon me;
Psalms 54:6 fear and trembling came upon me, and darkness covered me.
Psalms 54:7 And I said: Who will give me wings like a dove, and I will fly and rest?
Psalms 54:8 Behold, I went far away in flight and lodged in the wilderness. Interlude.
Psalms 54:9 I awaited the one saving me from faintheartedness and storm.
Psalms 54:10 Drown them, Lord, and divide their tongues, because I saw lawlessness and contradiction in the city.
Psalms 54:11 Day and night it will circle her upon her walls; lawlessness and toil are in her midst, and injustice,
Psalms 54:12 and interest and deceit did not cease from her squares.
Psalms 54:13 Because if an enemy had reproached me, I would have endured it, and if the one hating me had spoken boastfully against me, I would have hidden from him.
Psalms 54:14 But you, human of equal soul, my leader and my acquaintance,
Psalms 54:15 who together with me made foods sweet, we walked in the house of God in concord;
Psalms 54:16 let death come upon them, and let them descend alive into Hades, because evils are in their sojournings, in their midst.
Psalms 54:17 But I cried out to God, and the Lord heard me.
Psalms 54:18 At evening and morning and midday I will recount; I will report, and he will hear my voice.
Psalms 54:19 He will redeem my soul in peace from those approaching me, because among many they were with me.
Psalms 54:20 God will hear and humble them, the one existing before the ages. Interlude. For there is no exchange for them, and they did not fear God.
Psalms 54:21 He stretched out his hand in repaying; they profaned his covenant.
Psalms 54:22 They were divided by the wrath of his face, and his heart drew near; his words were softened more than oil, and they are missiles.
Psalms 54:23 Cast your care upon the Lord, and he will sustain you; he will never give shaking to the righteous one.
Psalms 54:24 But you, God, will bring them down into a pit of corruption; men of bloods and deceit will certainly not reach half their days. But I will hope in you, Lord.

## Chapter 55

Psalms 55:1 For the end, concerning the people removed far from the holy places; for Dauid, for an inscription on a pillar, when the foreigners seized him in Geth.
Psalms 55:2 Have mercy on me, Lord, because a human trampled me; fighting all day, he afflicted me.
Psalms 55:3 My enemies trampled me all day, because many are those fighting me from a height.
Psalms 55:4 By day I will be afraid, but I will hope in you.
Psalms 55:5 In God I will praise my words all day. In God I hoped; I will not be afraid. What will flesh do to me?
Psalms 55:6 All day they abhorred my words; all their reasonings against me are for evil.
Psalms 55:7 They will sojourn and hide; they will watch my heel, just as they waited for my soul.
Psalms 55:8 For nothing you will save them; in wrath you will bring peoples down, God.
Psalms 55:9 I declared my life to you; you placed my tears before you, as also in your promise.
Psalms 55:10 My enemies will turn backward on whatever day I call upon you; behold, I knew that you are my God.
Psalms 55:11 In God I will praise an utterance; in the Lord I will praise a word.
Psalms 55:12 In God I hoped; I will not be afraid. What will a human do to me?
Psalms 55:13 Within me, God, are the vows of praise that I will pay to you,
Psalms 55:14 because you delivered my soul from death and my feet from slipping, to be pleasing before God in the light of the living.

## Chapter 56

Psalms 56:1 For the end; do not destroy; for Dauid, for an inscription on a pillar, when he fled from the face of Saoul into the cave.
Psalms 56:2 Have mercy on me, God, have mercy on me, because my soul has trusted in you, and in the shadow of your wings I will hope until lawlessness passes away.
Psalms 56:3 I will cry out to God Most High, the God who benefited me.
Psalms 56:4 He sent forth from heaven and saved me; he gave those trampling me to reproach. Interlude. God sent forth his mercy and his truth
Psalms 56:5 and delivered my soul from the midst of young lions. I lay down troubled; sons of humans, their teeth are a weapon and arrows, and their tongue a sharp sword.
Psalms 56:6 Be exalted above the heavens, God, and your glory above all the earth.
Psalms 56:7 They prepared a trap for my feet and bent down my soul; they dug a pit before my face and fell into it. Interlude.
Psalms 56:8 My heart is ready, God, my heart is ready; I will sing and make music.
Psalms 56:9 Awake, my glory; awake, psaltery and lyre; I will awake at dawn.
Psalms 56:10 I will acknowledge you among peoples, Lord; I will sing to you among nations,
Psalms 56:11 because your mercy was magnified as far as the heavens, and your truth as far as the clouds.
Psalms 56:12 Be exalted above the heavens, God, and your glory above all the earth.

## Chapter 57

Psalms 57:1 For the end; do not destroy; for Dauid, for an inscription on a pillar.
Psalms 57:2 Do you truly, then, speak righteousness? Do you judge upright things, sons of humans?
Psalms 57:3 For indeed you work lawless deeds in your heart on the earth; your hands weave injustice.
Psalms 57:4 Sinners were estranged from the womb; they strayed from the belly; they spoke lies.
Psalms 57:5 Their fury is according to the likeness of the serpent, like a deaf asp stopping its ears,
Psalms 57:6 which will not hear the voice of enchanters or a charm worked by a wise one.
Psalms 57:7 God shattered their teeth in their mouth; the Lord crushed the molars of lions.
Psalms 57:8 They will be brought to nothing like water passing through; he will draw his bow until they grow weak.
Psalms 57:9 Like melted wax they will be taken away; fire fell upon them, and they did not see the sun.
Psalms 57:10 Before your thorns understand the buckthorn, he will swallow you as though alive, as though in wrath.
Psalms 57:11 A righteous one will rejoice when he sees vengeance upon impious ones; he will wash his hands in the blood of the sinner.
Psalms 57:12 And a human will say: Indeed, then, there is fruit for the righteous one; indeed, there is God judging them on the earth.

## Chapter 58

Psalms 58:1 For the end; do not destroy; for Dauid, for an inscription on a pillar, when Saoul sent and watched his house to put him to death.
Psalms 58:2 Deliver me from my enemies, God, and redeem me from those rising against me;
Psalms 58:3 deliver me from those working lawlessness, and save me from men of bloods.
Psalms 58:4 Because, behold, they hunted my soul; mighty ones attacked me. Neither my lawlessness nor my sin, Lord;
Psalms 58:5 without lawlessness they ran and directed their course; awake to meet me and see.
Psalms 58:6 And you, Lord, the God of powers, the God of Israel, attend to visiting all the nations; do not pity all those working lawlessness. Interlude.
Psalms 58:7 They will return toward evening and hunger like a dog and circle a city.
Psalms 58:8 Behold, they will utter with their mouth, and a sword is in their lips; because who heard?
Psalms 58:9 And you, Lord, will laugh at them; you will despise all the nations.
Psalms 58:10 My strength, I will watch toward you, because you, God, are my supporter.
Psalms 58:11 My God, his mercy will go before me; God will show me among my enemies.
Psalms 58:12 Do not kill them, lest they forget my people; scatter them by your strength and bring them down, Lord, my defender.
Psalms 58:13 The sin of their mouth, the word of their lips, and let them be caught in their arrogance; and from curse and falsehood ends will be proclaimed
Psalms 58:14 in wrath of an end, and they will certainly not exist; and they will know that God rules Iakob, the ends of the earth. Interlude.
Psalms 58:15 They will return toward evening and hunger like a dog and circle a city.
Psalms 58:16 They will be scattered to eat; but if they are not filled, they will also grumble.
Psalms 58:17 But I will sing of your strength and exult in your mercy in the morning, because you became my supporter and a refuge on the day of my affliction.
Psalms 58:18 My helper, I will sing to you, because you, God, are my supporter, my God, my mercy.

## Chapter 59

Psalms 59:1 For the end; for those who will yet be changed, for an inscription on a pillar, for Dauid, for teaching,
Psalms 59:2 when he burned the Mesopotamia of Syria and Syria Soba, and Ioab returned and struck the ravine of salts, twelve thousand.
Psalms 59:3 God, you rejected us and pulled us down; you were angry and pitied us.
Psalms 59:4 You shook the earth and troubled it; heal its fractures, because it was shaken.
Psalms 59:5 You showed your people hard things; you gave us wine of stupefaction to drink.
Psalms 59:6 You gave those fearing you a signal to flee from the face of a bow. Interlude.
Psalms 59:7 So that your beloved ones may be delivered, save with your right hand and hear me.
Psalms 59:8 God spoke in his holy place: I will exult and divide Sikima, and I will measure out the valley of tents;
Psalms 59:9 Galaad is mine, and Manasse is mine, and Ephraim is the strengthening of my head, Ioudas my king;
Psalms 59:10 Moab is the cauldron of my hope; upon Idumaia I will extend my sandal; foreigners were subjected to me.
Psalms 59:11 Who will lead me into a fortified city? Who will guide me as far as Idumaia?
Psalms 59:12 Is it not you, God, who rejected us? And you will not go out, God, with our forces.
Psalms 59:13 Give us help out of affliction; and a human's salvation is vain.
Psalms 59:14 But in God we will do mighty deeds, and he will bring to nothing those afflicting us.

## Chapter 60

Psalms 60:1 For the end, in hymns; for Dauid.
Psalms 60:2 Hear, God, my supplication; attend to my prayer.
Psalms 60:3 From the ends of the earth I cried out to you when my heart grew weary; upon a rock you raised me,
Psalms 60:4 you guided me, because you became my hope, a tower of strength from the face of an enemy.
Psalms 60:5 I will sojourn in your dwelling for the ages; I will be sheltered in the shelter of your wings. Interlude.
Psalms 60:6 Because you, God, heard my vows; you gave an inheritance to those fearing your name.
Psalms 60:7 You will add days to the days of a king, his years as far as the days of generation and generation.
Psalms 60:8 He will remain forever before God; who will seek out his mercy and truth?
Psalms 60:9 Thus I will sing to your name for the age of the age, that I may pay my vows day by day.

## Chapter 61

Psalms 61:1 For the end, concerning Idithoun; a psalm for Dauid.
Psalms 61:2 Will not my soul be subjected to God? For from him is my salvation;
Psalms 61:3 for indeed he is my God and my savior, my supporter; I will certainly not be shaken further.
Psalms 61:4 Until when do you attack a human? You all murder, as against a leaning wall and a fence thrust aside.
Psalms 61:5 But they planned to thrust away my honor; they ran in falsehood; with their mouth they blessed, and with their heart they cursed. Interlude.
Psalms 61:6 But be subjected to God, my soul, because from him is my endurance;
Psalms 61:7 because he is my God and my savior, my supporter; I will certainly not be displaced.
Psalms 61:8 Upon God depend my salvation and my glory; the God of my help, and my hope is upon God.
Psalms 61:9 Hope in him, every assembly of a people; pour out your hearts before him; God is our helper. Interlude.
Psalms 61:10 But vain are the sons of humans, false are the sons of humans in balances for doing injustice; they are from vanity together.
Psalms 61:11 Do not hope in injustice, and do not long for plunder; if wealth flows, do not set your heart upon it.
Psalms 61:12 Once God spoke; these two things I heard:
Psalms 61:13 that strength belongs to God, and to you, Lord, belongs mercy, because you will repay each one according to his works.

## Chapter 62

Psalms 62:1 A psalm for Dauid when he was in the wilderness of Ioudaia.
Psalms 62:2 God, my God, toward you I rise early; my soul thirsted for you. How manifold is my flesh's longing for you in a land deserted and untrodden and waterless?
Psalms 62:3 Thus in the holy place I appeared to you, to see your strength and your glory.
Psalms 62:4 Because your mercy is better than lives; my lips will praise you.
Psalms 62:5 Thus I will bless you in my life; in your name I will lift my hands.
Psalms 62:6 May my soul be filled as with fat and richness, and with lips of exultation my mouth will praise.
Psalms 62:7 If I remembered you upon my bed, at dawn I meditated upon you;
Psalms 62:8 because you became my helper, and in the shelter of your wings I will exult.
Psalms 62:9 My soul clung behind you; your right hand took hold of me.
Psalms 62:10 But they sought my soul in vain; they will enter the lowest parts of the earth;
Psalms 62:11 they will be handed over to the hands of a sword; they will be portions of foxes.
Psalms 62:12 But the king will rejoice in God; everyone swearing by him will be praised, because the mouth of those speaking unjust things was stopped.

## Chapter 63

Psalms 63:1 For the end; a psalm for Dauid.
Psalms 63:2 Hear, God, my voice when I supplicate; deliver my soul from fear of an enemy.
Psalms 63:3 You sheltered me from a conspiracy of those doing evil, from a multitude of those working lawlessness,
Psalms 63:4 who sharpened their tongues like a sword, drew their bow, a bitter thing,
Psalms 63:5 to shoot down a blameless one in hidden places; suddenly they will shoot him down and will not be afraid.
Psalms 63:6 They strengthened an evil word for themselves; they spoke of hiding traps; they said: Who will see them?
Psalms 63:7 They searched out lawless deeds; they failed while searching with a search. A human will approach, and a deep heart,
Psalms 63:8 and God will be exalted. Their blows became an arrow of infants,
Psalms 63:9 and their tongues grew weak against them. All who saw them were troubled,
Psalms 63:10 and every human was afraid. And they announced the works of God and understood his deeds.
Psalms 63:11 A righteous one will rejoice in the Lord and hope in him, and all the upright in heart will be praised.

## Chapter 64

Psalms 64:1 For the end; a psalm for Dauid, a song; of Ieremias and Iezekiel, from the account of the sojourning, when they were about to go out.
Psalms 64:2 A hymn befits you, God, in Sion, and a vow will be paid to you in Ierousalem.
Psalms 64:3 Hear my prayer; all flesh will come to you.
Psalms 64:4 Words of lawless deeds overpowered us, and you will atone for our impieties.
Psalms 64:5 Blessed is the one whom you chose and took to yourself; he will dwell in your courts. We will be filled with the good things of your house; your temple is holy, marvelous in righteousness.
Psalms 64:6 Hear us, God our savior, the hope of all the ends of the earth and of those far away at sea,
Psalms 64:7 preparing mountains by his strength, girded with might,
Psalms 64:8 the one troubling the hollow of the sea, the sounds of its waves. The nations will be troubled,
Psalms 64:9 and those inhabiting the ends will be afraid because of your signs; you will delight the departures of morning and evening.
Psalms 64:10 You visited the earth and drenched it; you multiplied its enrichment; the river of God was filled with waters; you prepared their food, because thus is your preparation.
Psalms 64:11 Drench its furrows; multiply its produce; in its drops it will rejoice as it sprouts.
Psalms 64:12 You will bless the crown of the year of your goodness, and your plains will be filled with richness;
Psalms 64:13 the beautiful places of the wilderness will grow fat, and the hills will gird themselves with exultation.
Psalms 64:14 The rams of the sheep clothed themselves, and the valleys multiply grain; they will cry out, for indeed they will sing hymns.

## Chapter 65

Psalms 65:1 For the end; a song of a psalm; [of resurrection.] Shout to God, all the earth,
Psalms 65:2 sing, then, to his name; give glory to his praise.
Psalms 65:3 Say to God: How fearsome are your works; in the multitude of your strength your enemies will lie to you;
Psalms 65:4 let all the earth bow to you and sing to you; let them sing to your name. Interlude.
Psalms 65:5 Come and see the works of God; fearsome in counsels beyond the sons of humans,
Psalms 65:6 the one turning the sea into dry land; in a river they will pass through on foot. There we will rejoice in him,
Psalms 65:7 the one ruling by his might forever; his eyes look upon the nations; let those provoking bitterness not exalt themselves. Interlude.
Psalms 65:8 Bless our God, nations, and make the voice of his praise heard,
Psalms 65:9 the one who placed my soul into life and did not give my feet to shaking.
Psalms 65:10 Because you tested us, God; you refined us by fire, as silver is refined by fire;
Psalms 65:11 you brought us into the trap; you placed afflictions upon our back.
Psalms 65:12 You mounted humans upon our heads; we passed through fire and water, and you brought us out into refreshment.
Psalms 65:13 I will enter your house with whole burnt offerings; I will pay you my vows,
Psalms 65:14 which my lips declared and my mouth spoke in my affliction;
Psalms 65:15 whole burnt offerings full of marrow I will offer to you with incense and rams; I will prepare oxen with he-goats for you. Interlude.
Psalms 65:16 Come, hear, all who fear God, and I will recount all that he did for my soul.
Psalms 65:17 To him I cried out with my mouth and exalted beneath my tongue:
Psalms 65:18 If I beheld injustice in my heart, let the Lord not hear.
Psalms 65:19 For this reason God heard me; he attended to the voice of my supplication.
Psalms 65:20 Blessed is God, who did not remove my prayer and his mercy from me.

## Chapter 66

Psalms 66:1 For the end, in hymns; a psalm of a song.
Psalms 66:2 May God pity us and bless us; may he make his face shine upon us. Interlude.
Psalms 66:3 That your way may be known on the earth, your salvation among all nations.
Psalms 66:4 Let peoples acknowledge you, God; let all peoples acknowledge you.
Psalms 66:5 Let nations rejoice and exult, because you will judge peoples in uprightness and guide nations on the earth. Interlude.
Psalms 66:6 Let peoples acknowledge you, God; let all peoples acknowledge you.
Psalms 66:7 The earth gave its fruit; may God, our God, bless us.
Psalms 66:8 May God bless us, and let all the ends of the earth fear him.

## Chapter 67

Psalms 67:1 For the end; for Dauid, a psalm of a song.
Psalms 67:2 Let God arise, and let his enemies be scattered, and let those hating him flee from his face.
Psalms 67:3 As smoke fails, let them fail; as wax melts before the face of fire, so may sinners perish before the face of God.
Psalms 67:4 And let the righteous rejoice; let them exult before God; let them delight in gladness.
Psalms 67:5 Sing to God; sing to his name; make a road for the one riding upon the west; Lord is his name, and exult before him. They will be troubled before his face,
Psalms 67:6 the father of orphans and judge of widows; God is in his holy place.
Psalms 67:7 God settles solitary ones in a house, bringing out those bound in fetters with courage, likewise those provoking bitterness, those dwelling in graves.
Psalms 67:8 God, when you went out before your people, when you passed through the wilderness, Interlude.
Psalms 67:9 the earth shook, for indeed the heavens dripped before the face of God, this Sina, before the face of the God of Israel.
Psalms 67:10 You will set apart a willing rain, God, for your inheritance, and it grew weak, but you restored it.
Psalms 67:11 Your living creatures dwell in it; you prepared for the poor one in your goodness, God.
Psalms 67:12 The Lord will give an utterance to those announcing good news with much power,
Psalms 67:13 the king of the forces of the beloved, and for the beauty of the house to divide spoils.
Psalms 67:14 If you lie down between the allotted portions, wings of a dove overlaid with silver, and her back with the greenish hue of gold. Interlude.
Psalms 67:15 When the heavenly one distinguishes kings upon it, they will be made snowy in Selmon.
Psalms 67:16 A mountain of God, a rich mountain, a curdled mountain, a rich mountain.
Psalms 67:17 Why do you suppose, curdled mountains, the mountain in which God was pleased to dwell? For indeed the Lord will dwell to the end.
Psalms 67:18 The chariot of God is ten-thousandfold, thousands of those flourishing; the Lord is among them, in Sina, in the holy place.
Psalms 67:19 You ascended to a height; you took captivity captive; you received gifts among humans, for indeed disobedient ones, to dwell. The Lord God is blessed,
Psalms 67:20 blessed is the Lord day by day; the God of our salvations will prosper our way. Interlude.
Psalms 67:21 Our God is a God of saving, and to the Lord, the Lord, belong the exits of death.
Psalms 67:22 But God will crush the heads of his enemies, the hairy crown of those walking in their transgressions.
Psalms 67:23 The Lord said: From Basan I will turn back; I will turn back in the depths of the sea,
Psalms 67:24 so that your foot may be dipped in blood, the tongue of your dogs from enemies, from him.
Psalms 67:25 Your processions were seen, God, the processions of my God, the king in the holy place.
Psalms 67:26 Rulers went ahead, followed by those making music, in the midst of young women playing tambourines.
Psalms 67:27 In assemblies bless God, the Lord, from the springs of Israel.
Psalms 67:28 There is Beniamin the younger in ecstasy, rulers of Iouda, their leaders, rulers of Zaboulon, rulers of Nephthali.
Psalms 67:29 Command, God, your strength; strengthen, God, this which you accomplished for us.
Psalms 67:30 From your temple at Ierousalem kings will bring gifts to you.
Psalms 67:31 Rebuke the wild beasts of the reed; the assembly of bulls among the heifers of the peoples, so that those tested by silver may not be shut out; scatter nations that desire wars.
Psalms 67:32 Ambassadors will come from Egypt; Ethiopia will hasten her hand to God.
Psalms 67:33 Kingdoms of the earth, sing to God; sing to the Lord. Interlude.
Psalms 67:34 Sing to God, the one riding upon the heaven of heaven toward the east; behold, he will give with his voice a voice of power.
Psalms 67:35 Give glory to God; his magnificence is over Israel, and his strength is in the clouds.
Psalms 67:36 Marvelous is God in his holy places; the God of Israel himself will give strength and strengthening to his people. Blessed is God.

## Chapter 68

Psalms 68:1 For the end, concerning those who will be changed; for Dauid.
Psalms 68:2 Save me, God, because waters entered as far as my soul.
Psalms 68:3 I became stuck in the mud of the deep, and there is no firm footing; I came into the depths of the sea, and a storm drowned me.
Psalms 68:4 I grew weary crying out; my throat became hoarse; my eyes failed from hoping in my God.
Psalms 68:5 Those hating me without cause were multiplied beyond the hairs of my head; my enemies, those pursuing me unjustly, grew strong; what I did not seize, then I repaid.
Psalms 68:6 God, you knew my folly, and my transgressions were not hidden from you.
Psalms 68:7 May those waiting for you not be put to shame because of me, Lord, Lord of powers; may those seeking you not be disgraced because of me, God of Israel,
Psalms 68:8 because for your sake I endured reproach; disgrace covered my face.
Psalms 68:9 I became estranged from my brothers and a stranger to the sons of my mother,
Psalms 68:10 because zeal for your house devoured me, and the reproaches of those reproaching you fell upon me.
Psalms 68:11 And I bent down my soul in fasting, and it became a reproach to me;
Psalms 68:12 and I made sackcloth my clothing, and I became a parable to them.
Psalms 68:13 Those sitting at the gate talked against me, and those drinking wine sang about me.
Psalms 68:14 But I, with my prayer, am toward you, Lord; a time of good pleasure, God, in the multitude of your mercy; hear me in the truth of your salvation.
Psalms 68:15 Save me from mud, so that I may not become stuck; may I be delivered from those hating me and from the depth of the waters;
Psalms 68:16 let a storm of water not drown me, nor let the deep swallow me, nor let a well close its mouth over me.
Psalms 68:17 Hear me, Lord, because your mercy is good; according to the multitude of your compassions look upon me.
Psalms 68:18 Do not turn your face away from your servant, because I am afflicted; hear me quickly.
Psalms 68:19 Attend to my soul and redeem it; because of my enemies deliver me.
Psalms 68:20 For you know my reproach and my shame and my disgrace; all those afflicting me are before you.
Psalms 68:21 My soul expected reproach and misery, and I waited for one grieving with me, and there was none, and for those comforting, and I found none.
Psalms 68:22 And they gave gall for my food, and for my thirst they gave me vinegar to drink.
Psalms 68:23 Let their table before them become a trap and a repayment and a stumbling block;
Psalms 68:24 let their eyes be darkened so as not to see, and bend their back continually;
Psalms 68:25 pour out your wrath upon them, and may the fury of your wrath overtake them.
Psalms 68:26 Let their homestead become deserted, and let there be no one dwelling in their dwellings;
Psalms 68:27 because the one you struck, they pursued, and they added to the pain of your wounded ones.
Psalms 68:28 Add lawlessness to their lawlessness, and let them not enter into your righteousness;
Psalms 68:29 let them be blotted out of the book of the living, and let them not be written with righteous ones.
Psalms 68:30 I am poor and in pain, and the salvation of your face, God, took hold of me.
Psalms 68:31 I will praise the name of God with a song; I will magnify him with praise,
Psalms 68:32 and it will please God more than a young calf bringing forth horns and hoofs.
Psalms 68:33 Let poor ones see and rejoice; seek out God, and your soul will live,
Psalms 68:34 because the Lord heard the needy and did not despise his fettered ones.
Psalms 68:35 Let the heavens and the earth praise him, the sea and all things creeping in them.
Psalms 68:36 Because God will save Sion, and the cities of Ioudaia will be built, and they will dwell there and inherit it;
Psalms 68:37 and the seed of his slaves will possess it, and those loving his name will dwell in it.

## Chapter 69

Psalms 69:1 For the end; for Dauid, for remembrance,
Psalms 69:2 for the Lord to save me. God, attend to my help.
Psalms 69:3 May those seeking my soul be ashamed and disgraced; may those wishing me evils turn backward and be put to shame;
Psalms 69:4 may those saying to me: Well done, well done, turn back immediately in shame.
Psalms 69:5 Let all those seeking you exult and rejoice in you, and let those loving your salvation say continually: Let God be magnified.
Psalms 69:6 But I am poor and needy; God, help me. You are my helper and my deliverer; Lord, do not delay.

## Chapter 70

Psalms 70:1 For Dauid; of the sons of Ionadab and of those first taken captive. God, in you I hoped; may I not be put to shame forever.
Psalms 70:2 In your righteousness deliver me and rescue me; incline your ear toward me and save me.
Psalms 70:3 Become for me a defending God and a strong place to save me, because you are my firmness and my refuge.
Psalms 70:4 My God, deliver me from a sinner's hand, from the hand of one acting lawlessly and unjustly;
Psalms 70:5 because you are my endurance, Lord; the Lord is my hope from my youth.
Psalms 70:6 Upon you I was supported from the belly; from my mother's womb you are my shelterer; in you is my hymn continually.
Psalms 70:7 I became like a portent to the many, and you are a mighty helper.
Psalms 70:8 Let my mouth be filled with praise, so that I may sing of your glory, all day of your magnificence.
Psalms 70:9 Do not cast me away at a time of old age; when my strength fails, do not abandon me.
Psalms 70:10 Because my enemies spoke to me, and those watching my soul planned together,
Psalms 70:11 saying: God abandoned him; pursue and overtake him, because there is no one delivering.
Psalms 70:12 God, do not go far from me; my God, attend to my help.
Psalms 70:13 Let those slandering my soul be ashamed and fail; let those seeking evils for me clothe themselves in shame and disgrace.
Psalms 70:14 But I will hope continually and add to all your praise.
Psalms 70:15 My mouth will declare your righteousness, all day your salvation, because I did not know writings.
Psalms 70:16 I will enter in the might of the Lord; Lord, I will remember your righteousness alone.
Psalms 70:17 You taught me, God, from my youth, and until now I will report your wonders.
Psalms 70:18 And until old age and advanced years, God, do not abandon me, until I report your arm to every coming generation, your might and your righteousness.
Psalms 70:19 God, as far as the highest places, the great things you did; God, who is like you?
Psalms 70:20 How many afflictions, many and evil, you showed me, and turning back, you gave me life, and from the abysses of the earth you brought me up again.
Psalms 70:21 You increased your greatness, and turning back, you comforted me [and from the abysses of the earth you brought me up again.]
Psalms 70:22 For indeed I will acknowledge your truth to you with an instrument of music, God; I will sing to you with a lyre, Holy One of Israel.
Psalms 70:23 My lips will exult when I sing to you, and my soul, which you redeemed.
Psalms 70:24 And moreover my tongue will meditate upon your righteousness all day, when those seeking evils for me are ashamed and disgraced.

## Chapter 71

Psalms 71:1 For Salomon. God, give your judgment to the king and your righteousness to the king's son,
Psalms 71:2 to judge your people in righteousness and your poor ones in judgment.
Psalms 71:3 Let the mountains take up peace for your people, and the hills in righteousness.
Psalms 71:4 He will judge the poor of the people and save the sons of the needy and humble a false accuser,
Psalms 71:5 and he will remain with the sun and before the moon for generations of generations,
Psalms 71:6 and he will descend like rain upon a fleece and like drops dripping upon the earth.
Psalms 71:7 Righteousness will rise in his days, and a multitude of peace, until the moon is taken away.
Psalms 71:8 And he will rule from sea to sea and from a river to the ends of the inhabited world.
Psalms 71:9 Before him Ethiopians will fall down, and his enemies will lick dust;
Psalms 71:10 kings of Tharsis and the islands will offer gifts; kings of Arabs and Saba will bring gifts;
Psalms 71:11 and all kings will bow to him; all nations will serve him.
Psalms 71:12 Because he delivered a poor one from the hand of a powerful one, and a needy one who had no helper;
Psalms 71:13 he will spare a poor and needy one and save the souls of the needy;
Psalms 71:14 from interest and from injustice he will redeem their souls, and their name is honored before him.
Psalms 71:15 And he will live, and some of the gold of Arabia will be given to him, and they will pray concerning him continually; all day they will bless him.
Psalms 71:16 There will be support in the land upon the tops of the mountains; his fruit will be exalted beyond Libanos, and they will blossom out of a city like grass of the earth.
Psalms 71:17 Let his name be blessed for the ages; before the sun his name will remain; and all the tribes of the earth will be blessed in him; all nations will call him blessed.
Psalms 71:18 Blessed is the Lord God, the God of Israel, who alone does wonders,
Psalms 71:19 and blessed is the name of his glory forever and for the age of the age, and all the earth will be filled with his glory. May it be, may it be.
Psalms 71:20 The hymns of Dauid the son of Iessai ended. – –

## Chapter 72

Psalms 72:1 A psalm for Asaph. How good God is to Israel, to the upright in heart.
Psalms 72:2 But my feet were nearly shaken; my steps almost poured away.
Psalms 72:3 Because I envied the lawless, seeing the peace of sinners,
Psalms 72:4 because there is no refusal at their death, and firmness in their scourge;
Psalms 72:5 they are not in the toils of humans, and with humans they will not be scourged.
Psalms 72:6 For this reason arrogance seized them; they clothed themselves with their injustice and impiety.
Psalms 72:7 Their injustice will come out as from fat; they passed into a disposition of heart;
Psalms 72:8 they thought and spoke in wickedness; they spoke injustice on high;
Psalms 72:9 they set their mouth toward heaven, and their tongue passed over the earth.
Psalms 72:10 For this reason my people will return here, and full days will be found for them.
Psalms 72:11 And they said: How did God know, and is there knowledge in the Most High?
Psalms 72:12 Behold, these are sinners and prosper; forever they possessed wealth.
Psalms 72:13 And I said: Then in vain I made my heart righteous and washed my hands among innocent ones;
Psalms 72:14 and I became scourged all day, and my reproof was in the mornings.
Psalms 72:15 If I said: I will recount thus, behold, I have broken faith with the generation of your sons.
Psalms 72:16 And I undertook to know this; it is toil before me,
Psalms 72:17 until I enter the sanctuary of God and understand their last things.
Psalms 72:18 But because of their deceits you set things for them; you cast them down when they were exalted.
Psalms 72:19 How they became a desolation suddenly; they failed, they perished because of their lawlessness.
Psalms 72:20 Like a dream of one waking, Lord, in your city you will despise their image.
Psalms 72:21 Because my heart was inflamed, and my kidneys were changed,
Psalms 72:22 and I was brought to nothing and did not know; I became beastlike before you.
Psalms 72:23 And I am continually with you; you grasped my right hand;
Psalms 72:24 with your counsel you guided me, and with glory you took me to yourself.
Psalms 72:25 For what do I have in heaven, and from you what did I desire upon the earth?
Psalms 72:26 My heart and my flesh failed; God is the God of my heart and my portion forever.
Psalms 72:27 Because, behold, those distancing themselves from you will perish; you destroyed everyone prostituting himself away from you.
Psalms 72:28 But for me, to cling to God is good, to place my hope in the Lord, to declare all your praises in the gates of the daughter of Sion.

## Chapter 73

Psalms 73:1 Of understanding, for Asaph. Why did you reject us to the end, God; why was your fury angry against the sheep of your pasture?
Psalms 73:2 Remember your assembly, which you acquired from the beginning; you redeemed the rod of your inheritance, this Mount Sion in which you dwelt.
Psalms 73:3 Lift your hands against their arrogances to the end, all the evils the enemy worked in your holy places.
Psalms 73:4 And those hating you boasted in the midst of your feast; they set their signs as signs and did not know.
Psalms 73:5 As at the entrance above,
Psalms 73:6 as in a forest of trees, with axes they cut out her doors; together with axe and chisel they broke her down.
Psalms 73:7 They burned your sanctuary with fire; to the ground they profaned the dwelling of your name.
Psalms 73:8 Their kinship together said in their heart: Come, and let us burn all the feasts of God from the earth.
Psalms 73:9 We did not see our signs; there is no longer a prophet, and he will no longer know us.
Psalms 73:10 Until when, God, will the enemy reproach; will the adversary provoke your name to the end?
Psalms 73:11 Why do you turn away your hand and your right hand from the midst of your bosom to the end?
Psalms 73:12 But God is our king before the age; he worked salvation in the midst of the earth.
Psalms 73:13 You strengthened the sea by your power; you shattered the heads of the dragons upon the water.
Psalms 73:14 You crushed the heads of the dragon; you gave him as food to the Ethiopian peoples.
Psalms 73:15 You broke open springs and torrents; you dried up rivers of Etham.
Psalms 73:16 The day is yours, and the night is yours; you established light and sun.
Psalms 73:17 You made all the boundaries of the earth; summer and spring, you formed them.
Psalms 73:18 Remember this: an enemy reproached the Lord, and a foolish people provoked your name.
Psalms 73:19 Do not hand over to the wild beasts a soul acknowledging you; do not forget the souls of your needy ones to the end.
Psalms 73:20 Look upon your covenant, because the darkened places of the earth were filled with houses of lawless deeds.
Psalms 73:21 Let a humbled one not turn back ashamed; a poor and needy one will praise your name.
Psalms 73:22 Arise, God; judge your case; remember your reproaches from a fool all day.
Psalms 73:23 Do not forget the voice of your suppliants; the arrogance of those hating you went up to you continually.

## Chapter 74

Psalms 74:1 For the end; do not destroy; a psalm of a song for Asaph.
Psalms 74:2 We will acknowledge you, God; we will acknowledge and call upon your name.
Psalms 74:3 I will recount all your wonders when I receive a time; I will judge upright things.
Psalms 74:4 The earth melted, and all those dwelling in it; I made its pillars firm. Interlude.
Psalms 74:5 I said to those acting lawlessly: Do not act lawlessly; and to those sinning: Do not exalt a horn;
Psalms 74:6 do not lift your horn on high; do not speak injustice against God.
Psalms 74:7 Because neither from departures nor from the west nor from deserted mountains,
Psalms 74:8 because God is judge; he humbles this one and exalts this one.
Psalms 74:9 Because a cup is in the Lord's hand, of unmixed wine, full of a mixture, and he tipped from this into this; but its dregs were not emptied out; all the sinners of the earth will drink.
Psalms 74:10 But I will exult forever; I will sing to the God of Iakob;
Psalms 74:11 and I will break all the horns of sinners, and the horns of the righteous one will be exalted.

## Chapter 75

Psalms 75:1 For the end, in hymns; a psalm for Asaph, a song against the Assyrian.
Psalms 75:2 God is known in Ioudaia; in Israel his name is great.
Psalms 75:3 And his place came to be in peace, and his dwelling in Sion;
Psalms 75:4 there he shattered the powers of bows, weapon and sword and war. Interlude.
Psalms 75:5 You give light marvelously from everlasting mountains.
Psalms 75:6 All those senseless in heart were troubled; they slept their sleep, and all the men of wealth found nothing with their hands.
Psalms 75:7 At your rebuke, God of Iakob, those mounted on horses slumbered.
Psalms 75:8 You are fearsome, and who will withstand you? From then is your wrath.
Psalms 75:9 From heaven you made judgment heard; the earth was afraid and quiet
Psalms 75:10 when God arose for judgment, to save all the meek of the earth. Interlude.
Psalms 75:11 Because a human's thought will acknowledge you, and a remnant of thought will keep a feast for you.
Psalms 75:12 Make vows and pay them to the Lord your God; all those around him will bring gifts
Psalms 75:13 to the fearsome one who takes away spirits of rulers, fearsome among the kings of the earth.

## Chapter 76

Psalms 76:1 For the end, concerning Idithoun; for Asaph, a psalm.
Psalms 76:2 With my voice I cried out to the Lord, with my voice to God, and he attended to me.
Psalms 76:3 On the day of my affliction I sought out God, with my hands at night before him, and I was not deceived; my soul refused to be comforted.
Psalms 76:4 I remembered God and rejoiced; I meditated, and my spirit grew fainthearted. Interlude.
Psalms 76:5 My eyes anticipated watches; I was troubled and did not speak.
Psalms 76:6 I considered ancient days, and I remembered everlasting years and meditated;
Psalms 76:7 at night I meditated with my heart, and my spirit searched.
Psalms 76:8 Surely the Lord will not reject for the ages and no longer continue to take pleasure?
Psalms 76:9 Or will he cut off his mercy to the end, from generation to generation?
Psalms 76:10 Or will God forget to pity, or will he restrain his compassions in his wrath? Interlude.
Psalms 76:11 And I said: Now I began; this is the change of the right hand of the Most High.
Psalms 76:12 I remembered the works of the Lord, because I will remember your wonders from the beginning,
Psalms 76:13 and I will meditate on all your works, and on your practices I will ponder.
Psalms 76:14 God, your way is in the holy place; what god is great like our God?
Psalms 76:15 You are the God doing wonders; you made your strength known among the peoples;
Psalms 76:16 with your arm you redeemed your people, the sons of Iakob and Ioseph. Interlude.
Psalms 76:17 Waters saw you, God; waters saw you and were afraid, and abysses were troubled, a multitude of the sound of waters.
Psalms 76:18 The clouds gave a voice, for indeed your arrows pass through;
Psalms 76:19 the voice of your thunder is in the wheel; your lightnings shone upon the inhabited world; the earth was shaken and became trembling.
Psalms 76:20 Your way is in the sea, and your paths in many waters, and your tracks will not be known.
Psalms 76:21 You guided your people like sheep by the hand of Moyses and Aaron.

## Chapter 77

Psalms 77:1 Of understanding, for Asaph. Attend to my law, my people; incline your ear to the words of my mouth;
Psalms 77:2 I will open my mouth in parables; I will utter riddles from the beginning.
Psalms 77:3 All that we heard and knew, and our fathers recounted to us,
Psalms 77:4 was not hidden from their children, to another generation, reporting the praises of the Lord and his mighty deeds and his wonders which he did.
Psalms 77:5 And he raised up a testimony in Iakob and established a law in Israel, all that he commanded our fathers to make known to their sons,
Psalms 77:6 so that another generation might know, sons who will be born, and they will arise and report them to their sons,
Psalms 77:7 so that they may place their hope upon God and not forget the works of God, and they will seek out his commandments,
Psalms 77:8 so that they may not become like their fathers, a crooked generation provoking bitterness, a generation that did not direct its heart, and its spirit was not faithful with God.
Psalms 77:9 Sons of Ephraim, drawing and shooting with bows, turned back on a day of war.
Psalms 77:10 They did not keep the covenant of God and did not wish to walk in his law,
Psalms 77:11 and they forgot his benefits and his wonders which he showed them,
Psalms 77:12 the wonders he did before their fathers in the land of Egypt, in the plain of Tanis.
Psalms 77:13 He broke open a sea and led them through; he made waters stand like a wineskin,
Psalms 77:14 and he guided them with a cloud by day and all night with illumination of fire.
Psalms 77:15 He broke open a rock in a wilderness and gave them drink as in a great abyss,
Psalms 77:16 and brought water out of a rock and brought waters down like rivers.
Psalms 77:17 And they continued still to sin against him; they provoked the Most High to bitterness in a waterless place,
Psalms 77:18 and they tested God in their hearts by asking foods for their souls,
Psalms 77:19 and they spoke against God and said: Surely God cannot prepare a table in a wilderness?
Psalms 77:20 Since he struck a rock and waters flowed and torrents flooded, can he also give bread or prepare a table for his people?
Psalms 77:21 For this reason the Lord heard and deferred, and fire was kindled in Iakob, and wrath rose against Israel,
Psalms 77:22 because they did not believe in God or hope in his salvation.
Psalms 77:23 And he commanded clouds above and opened doors of heaven,
Psalms 77:24 and rained manna upon them to eat, and gave them bread of heaven;
Psalms 77:25 a human ate bread of angels; he sent them provisions to fullness.
Psalms 77:26 He moved a south wind from heaven and brought a southwest wind by his might,
Psalms 77:27 and rained flesh upon them like dust, and winged birds like sand of seas,
Psalms 77:28 and they fell into the midst of their camp, around their dwellings,
Psalms 77:29 and they ate and were greatly filled, and he brought their desire to them;
Psalms 77:30 they were not deprived of their desire. While their food was still in their mouth,
Psalms 77:31 the wrath of God also rose against them and killed among their fat ones and fettered the chosen ones of Israel.
Psalms 77:32 In all these things they still sinned and did not believe in his wonders,
Psalms 77:33 and their days failed in vanity, and their years with haste.
Psalms 77:34 When he killed them, they sought him out and turned back and rose early toward God,
Psalms 77:35 and remembered that God is their helper and God Most High is their redeemer.
Psalms 77:36 And they deceived him with their mouth and lied to him with their tongue,
Psalms 77:37 but their heart was not upright with him, nor were they faithful in his covenant.
Psalms 77:38 But he is compassionate and will atone for their sins and will not destroy, and will multiply the turning away of his fury, and will not kindle all his wrath;
Psalms 77:39 and he remembered that they are flesh, a spirit going and not returning.
Psalms 77:40 How often did they provoke him to bitterness in the wilderness, anger him in a waterless land?
Psalms 77:41 And they turned back and tested God and provoked the Holy One of Israel.
Psalms 77:42 They did not remember his hand, the day on which he redeemed them from the hand of an afflicter,
Psalms 77:43 how he established his signs in Egypt and his portents in the plain of Tanis;
Psalms 77:44 and he turned their rivers and their rainwaters into blood, so that they might not drink;
Psalms 77:45 he sent a dog-fly against them, and it devoured them, and a frog, and it destroyed them;
Psalms 77:46 and he gave their fruit to rust and their labors to the locust;
Psalms 77:47 he killed their vine with hail and their mulberry trees with frost;
Psalms 77:48 and he handed their beasts over to hail and their possessions to fire;
Psalms 77:49 he sent upon them the wrath of his fury, fury and wrath and affliction, a sending through evil angels;
Psalms 77:50 he made a road for his wrath; he did not spare their souls from death, and he shut up their beasts to death,
Psalms 77:51 and struck every firstborn in Egypt, the firstfruits of their labors in the dwellings of Cham.
Psalms 77:52 And he moved his people like sheep and led them up like a flock in a wilderness,
Psalms 77:53 and guided them in hope, and they were not afraid, and a sea covered their enemies.
Psalms 77:54 And he brought them into the boundary of his sanctuary, this mountain which his right hand acquired,
Psalms 77:55 and cast nations out from before their face and allotted them with a measuring cord of inheritance, and settled the tribes of Israel in their dwellings.
Psalms 77:56 And they tested and provoked God Most High to bitterness, and did not keep his testimonies,
Psalms 77:57 and turned away and broke faith, just as their fathers also did, and were turned into a crooked bow,
Psalms 77:58 and angered him with their hills and provoked him to jealousy with their carved things.
Psalms 77:59 God heard and overlooked and greatly despised Israel,
Psalms 77:60 and rejected the tent of Selom, his dwelling where he dwelt among humans.
Psalms 77:61 And he handed their strength over to captivity and their beauty into an enemy's hands,
Psalms 77:62 and shut up his people to a sword and overlooked his inheritance.
Psalms 77:63 Fire devoured their young men, and their virgins were not mourned;
Psalms 77:64 their priests fell by a sword, and their widows will not be wept for.
Psalms 77:65 And the Lord awoke like one sleeping, like a mighty one intoxicated with wine,
Psalms 77:66 and struck his enemies backward; he gave them everlasting reproach.
Psalms 77:67 And he rejected the dwelling of Ioseph and did not choose the tribe of Ephraim;
Psalms 77:68 and he chose the tribe of Iouda, Mount Sion which he loved,
Psalms 77:69 and built his sanctuary like that of one-horned beasts; in the earth he founded it forever.
Psalms 77:70 And he chose Dauid his slave and took him up from the flocks of sheep;
Psalms 77:71 from behind those giving birth he took him to shepherd Iakob his people and Israel his inheritance,
Psalms 77:72 and he shepherded them in the innocence of his heart and guided them with the understandings of his hands.

## Chapter 78

Psalms 78:1 A psalm for Asaph. God, nations came into your inheritance; they defiled your holy temple; they made Ierousalem into a fruit-watch hut.
Psalms 78:2 They made the corpses of your slaves food for the birds of heaven, the flesh of your holy ones for the wild beasts of the earth;
Psalms 78:3 they poured out their blood like water around Ierousalem, and there was no one burying.
Psalms 78:4 We became a reproach to our neighbors, a sneer and mockery to those around us.
Psalms 78:5 Until when, Lord, will you be angry to the end; will your jealousy be kindled like fire?
Psalms 78:6 Pour out your wrath upon nations that do not know you and upon kingdoms that did not call upon your name,
Psalms 78:7 because they devoured Iakob and deserted his place.
Psalms 78:8 Do not remember our ancient lawless deeds; let your compassions quickly anticipate us, because we became very poor.
Psalms 78:9 Help us, God our savior; because of the glory of your name, Lord, deliver us and atone for our sins because of your name,
Psalms 78:10 lest the nations say: Where is their God? And let the vengeance for the poured-out blood of your slaves be known among the nations before our eyes.
Psalms 78:11 Let the groaning of those fettered enter before you; according to the greatness of your arm preserve the sons of those put to death.
Psalms 78:12 Repay our neighbors sevenfold into their bosom their reproach with which they reproached you, Lord.
Psalms 78:13 But we, your people and sheep of your pasture, will acknowledge you forever; to generation and generation we will declare your praise.

## Chapter 79

Psalms 79:1 For the end, concerning those who will be changed; a testimony for Asaph, a psalm concerning the Assyrian.
Psalms 79:2 You who shepherd Israel, attend; you who guide Ioseph like sheep, you who sit upon the cheroubin, appear.
Psalms 79:3 Before Ephraim and Beniamin and Manasse awaken your might and come to save us.
Psalms 79:4 God, turn us back and make your face shine, and we will be saved.
Psalms 79:5 Lord, God of powers, until when are you angry against the prayer of your slave,
Psalms 79:6 will you feed us bread of tears and give us tears to drink in measure?
Psalms 79:7 You made us a contradiction to our neighbors, and our enemies sneered at us.
Psalms 79:8 Lord, God of powers, turn us back and make your face shine, and we will be saved. Interlude.
Psalms 79:9 You removed a vine from Egypt; you cast out nations and planted it;
Psalms 79:10 you made a road before it and planted its roots, and the earth was filled.
Psalms 79:11 Its shadow covered mountains, and its climbing branches the cedars of God;
Psalms 79:12 it extended its shoots as far as a sea, and its offshoots as far as a river.
Psalms 79:13 Why did you pull down its fence, and all those passing along the road harvest it?
Psalms 79:14 A boar from a forest ravaged it, and a solitary wild beast grazed it down.
Psalms 79:15 God of powers, turn back, then; look from heaven and see and visit this vine,
Psalms 79:16 and restore it, which your right hand planted, and upon a son of a human whom you strengthened for yourself.
Psalms 79:17 Burned with fire and dug up; at the rebuke of your face they will perish.
Psalms 79:18 Let your hand be upon a man of your right hand and upon a son of a human whom you strengthened for yourself;
Psalms 79:19 and we will certainly not depart from you; you will give us life, and we will call upon your name.
Psalms 79:20 Lord, God of powers, turn us back and make your face shine, and we will be saved.

## Chapter 80

Psalms 80:1 For the end, concerning the winepresses; for Asaph, a psalm.
Psalms 80:2 Exult in God our helper; shout to the God of Iakob;
Psalms 80:3 take up a psalm and give a tambourine, a delightful psaltery with a lyre;
Psalms 80:4 blow a trumpet at the new moon, on the marked day of our feast;
Psalms 80:5 because it is an ordinance for Israel and a judgment for the God of Iakob.
Psalms 80:6 He established it as a testimony in Ioseph when he went out from the land of Egypt; he heard a tongue that he did not know;
Psalms 80:7 he removed his back from burdens; his hands served in the basket.
Psalms 80:8 In affliction you called upon me, and I delivered you; I heard you in the hidden place of a storm; I tested you at water of contradiction. Interlude.
Psalms 80:9 Hear, my people, and I testify to you; Israel, if you hear me,
Psalms 80:10 there will be no new god among you, nor will you bow to a foreign god;
Psalms 80:11 for I am the Lord your God who brought you up from the land of Egypt; widen your mouth, and I will fill it.
Psalms 80:12 And my people did not hear my voice, and Israel did not attend to me;
Psalms 80:13 and I sent them away according to the practices of their hearts; they will walk in their practices.
Psalms 80:14 If my people had heard me, if Israel had walked in my ways,
Psalms 80:15 in no time I would have humbled their enemies and laid my hand upon those afflicting them.
Psalms 80:16 The enemies of the Lord lied to him, and their time will be forever.
Psalms 80:17 And he fed them from the fat of wheat and filled them with honey from a rock.

## Chapter 81

Psalms 81:1 A psalm for Asaph. God stood in an assembly of gods, and in the midst he judges gods:
Psalms 81:2 Until when do you judge injustice and accept faces of sinners? Interlude.
Psalms 81:3 Judge an orphan and a poor one; justify a humbled and needy one;
Psalms 81:4 rescue a needy and poor one; deliver from a sinner's hand.
Psalms 81:5 They did not know or understand; they walk in darkness; all the foundations of the earth will be shaken.
Psalms 81:6 I said: You are gods and all sons of the Most High;
Psalms 81:7 but you die like humans and fall like one of the rulers.
Psalms 81:8 Arise, God; judge the earth, because you will inherit among all the nations.

## Chapter 82

Psalms 82:1 A song of a psalm for Asaph.
Psalms 82:2 God, who will be likened to you? Do not be silent or grow calm, God;
Psalms 82:3 because, behold, your enemies made a noise, and those hating you lifted a head;
Psalms 82:4 against your people they cunningly devised a plan, and they counseled against your holy ones;
Psalms 82:5 they said: Come, and let us destroy them from being a nation, and the name of Israel will certainly no longer be remembered.
Psalms 82:6 Because they counseled together in concord; they made a covenant against you,
Psalms 82:7 the dwellings of the Idumaians and the Ismaelites, Moab and the Agarenes,
Psalms 82:8 Gebal and Ammon and Amalek and foreigners with those inhabiting Tyros;
Psalms 82:9 for indeed Assour also joined them; they became a support to the sons of Lot. Interlude.
Psalms 82:10 Do to them as to Madiam and Sisara, as Iabin at the torrent Kison;
Psalms 82:11 they were destroyed in Aendor; they became like dung for the earth.
Psalms 82:12 Make their rulers like Oreb and Zeb and Zebee and Salmana, all their rulers,
Psalms 82:13 who said: Let us inherit the sanctuary of God for ourselves.
Psalms 82:14 My God, make them like a wheel, like straw before the face of wind;
Psalms 82:15 like fire which will burn through a forest, as though a flame might burn mountains,
Psalms 82:16 thus you will pursue them with your storm and trouble them with your wrath.
Psalms 82:17 Fill their faces with dishonor, and they will seek your name, Lord.
Psalms 82:18 Let them be ashamed and troubled for the age of the age, and let them be disgraced and perish,
Psalms 82:19 and let them know that your name is Lord; you alone are Most High over all the earth.

## Chapter 83

Psalms 83:1 For the end, concerning the winepresses; for the sons of Kore, a psalm.
Psalms 83:2 How beloved are your dwellings, Lord of powers.
Psalms 83:3 My soul longs and fails for the courts of the Lord; my heart and my flesh exulted in the living God.
Psalms 83:4 For indeed a sparrow found itself a house, and a turtledove a nest for herself, where she will put her young, your altars, Lord of powers, my king and my God.
Psalms 83:5 Blessed are those dwelling in your house; for the ages of the ages they will praise you. Interlude.
Psalms 83:6 Blessed is a man whose support is from you, Lord; he arranged ascents in his heart
Psalms 83:7 in the valley of weeping, to the place he established; for indeed the lawgiver will give blessings.
Psalms 83:8 They will go from strength to strength; the God of gods will appear in Sion.
Psalms 83:9 Lord, God of powers, hear my prayer; give ear, God of Iakob. Interlude.
Psalms 83:10 Our defender, see, God, and look upon the face of your anointed one.
Psalms 83:11 Because one day in your courts is better than thousands; I chose to be cast aside in the house of God rather than dwell in dwellings of sinners.
Psalms 83:12 Because the Lord God loves mercy and truth; he will give grace and glory; the Lord will not deprive those walking in innocence of good things.
Psalms 83:13 Lord of powers, blessed is the human hoping in you.

## Chapter 84

Psalms 84:1 For the end; for the sons of Kore, a psalm.
Psalms 84:2 You took pleasure in your land, Lord; you turned back the captivity of Iakob;
Psalms 84:3 you forgave the lawless deeds of your people; you covered all their sins. Interlude.
Psalms 84:4 You stopped all your wrath; you turned away from the wrath of your fury.
Psalms 84:5 Turn us back, God of our salvations, and turn your fury away from us.
Psalms 84:6 Surely you will not be angry with us forever, or extend your wrath from generation to generation?
Psalms 84:7 God, turning back, you will give us life, and your people will rejoice in you.
Psalms 84:8 Show us your mercy, Lord, and may you give us your salvation.
Psalms 84:9 I will hear what the Lord God will speak within me, because he will speak peace upon his people and upon his holy ones and upon those turning their heart toward him.
Psalms 84:10 But his salvation is near those fearing him, that glory may dwell in our land.
Psalms 84:11 Mercy and truth met; righteousness and peace kissed;
Psalms 84:12 truth rose from the earth, and righteousness leaned down from heaven.
Psalms 84:13 For indeed the Lord will give goodness, and our land will give its fruit;
Psalms 84:14 righteousness will go before him and set his steps upon a way.

## Chapter 85

Psalms 85:1 A prayer for Dauid. Incline your ear, Lord, and hear me, because I am poor and needy.
Psalms 85:2 Guard my soul, because I am holy; save your slave, my God, the one hoping in you.
Psalms 85:3 Have mercy on me, Lord, because I will cry out to you all day.
Psalms 85:4 Gladden the soul of your slave, because toward you, Lord, I lifted my soul.
Psalms 85:5 Because you, Lord, are good and gentle and abundant in mercy to all those calling upon you.
Psalms 85:6 Give ear, Lord, to my prayer, and attend to the voice of my supplication.
Psalms 85:7 On the day of my affliction I cried out to you, because you heard me.
Psalms 85:8 There is none like you among gods, Lord, and there is nothing according to your works.
Psalms 85:9 All the nations that you made will come and bow before you, Lord, and glorify your name,
Psalms 85:10 because you are great and do wonders; you alone are the great God.
Psalms 85:11 Guide me, Lord, in your way, and I will walk in your truth; let my heart rejoice to fear your name.
Psalms 85:12 I will acknowledge you, Lord my God, with my whole heart, and glorify your name forever,
Psalms 85:13 because your mercy is great upon me, and you delivered my soul from the lowest Hades.
Psalms 85:14 God, lawless ones rose against me, and an assembly of mighty ones sought my soul and did not set you before them.
Psalms 85:15 And you, Lord God, are compassionate and merciful, patient and abundant in mercy and true.
Psalms 85:16 Look upon me and have mercy on me; give your strength to your servant and save the son of your maidservant.
Psalms 85:17 Make with me a sign for good, and let those hating me see and be ashamed, because you, Lord, helped me and comforted me.

## Chapter 86

Psalms 86:1 For the sons of Kore, a psalm of a song. His foundations are in the holy mountains;
Psalms 86:2 the Lord loves the gates of Sion more than all the dwellings of Iakob.
Psalms 86:3 Glorious things were spoken concerning you, city of God. Interlude.
Psalms 86:4 I will remember Raab and Babylon to those knowing me; and behold, foreigners and Tyros and a people of Ethiopians, these were born there.
Psalms 86:5 Mother Sion, a human will say, and a human was born in her, and the Most High himself founded her.
Psalms 86:6 The Lord will recount in a register of peoples and rulers these who have been born in her. Interlude.
Psalms 86:7 As of all rejoicing, the dwelling is in you.

## Chapter 87

Psalms 87:1 A song of a psalm for the sons of Kore; for the end, concerning maeleth, to respond; of understanding, for Aiman the Israelite.
Psalms 87:2 Lord, God of my salvation, by day I cried out and by night before you;
Psalms 87:3 let my prayer enter before you; incline your ear to my supplication, Lord.
Psalms 87:4 Because my soul was filled with evils, and my life drew near to Hades;
Psalms 87:5 I was counted with those descending into a pit; I became like a human without help, free among the dead,
Psalms 87:6 like wounded ones cast away, sleeping in a grave, whom you remembered no longer, and they were thrust away from your hand.
Psalms 87:7 They placed me in a lowest pit, in dark places and in a shadow of death.
Psalms 87:8 Your fury rested upon me, and you brought all your billows upon me. Interlude.
Psalms 87:9 You distanced my acquaintances from me; they made me an abomination to themselves; I was handed over and did not go out.
Psalms 87:10 My eyes grew weak from poverty; I cried out to you, Lord, all day; I spread out my hands toward you:
Psalms 87:11 Surely you will not do wonders for the dead? Or will physicians raise them, and they will acknowledge you?
Psalms 87:12 Surely someone will not recount your mercy in a grave and your truth in destruction?
Psalms 87:13 Surely your wonders will not be known in the darkness, and your righteousness in a forgotten land?
Psalms 87:14 And I cried out to you, Lord, and in the morning my prayer will go before you.
Psalms 87:15 Why, Lord, do you thrust away my soul, turn your face away from me?
Psalms 87:16 I am poor and in toils from my youth, but having been exalted, I was humbled and utterly at a loss.
Psalms 87:17 Your wraths passed over me, and your terrors greatly troubled me;
Psalms 87:18 they circled me like water all day; they encompassed me together.
Psalms 87:19 You distanced friend and neighbor from me, and my acquaintances from misery.

## Chapter 88

Psalms 88:1 Of understanding, for Aithan the Israelite.
Psalms 88:2 Your mercies, Lord, I will sing forever; to generation and generation I will report your truth with my mouth,
Psalms 88:3 because you said: Forever mercy will be built; in the heavens your truth will be prepared.
Psalms 88:4 I made a covenant with my chosen ones; I swore to Dauid my slave:
Psalms 88:5 Forever I will prepare your seed and build your throne to generation and generation. Interlude.
Psalms 88:6 The heavens will acknowledge your wonders, Lord, and your truth in an assembly of holy ones.
Psalms 88:7 Because who in clouds will be equal to the Lord, and who among sons of God will be likened to the Lord?
Psalms 88:8 God is glorified in a council of holy ones, great and fearsome over all those around him.
Psalms 88:9 Lord, God of powers, who is like you? You are mighty, Lord, and your truth is around you.
Psalms 88:10 You rule the strength of the sea, and you calm the tossing of its waves.
Psalms 88:11 You humbled a proud one like a wounded one, and with the arm of your strength you scattered your enemies.
Psalms 88:12 The heavens are yours, and the earth is yours; you founded the inhabited world and its fullness.
Psalms 88:13 You created the north and seas; Thabor and Ermon will exult in your name.
Psalms 88:14 Yours is the arm with might; let your hand be strengthened; let your right hand be exalted.
Psalms 88:15 Righteousness and judgment are the preparation of your throne; mercy and truth will go before your face.
Psalms 88:16 Blessed is the people knowing a shout; Lord, they will walk in the light of your face,
Psalms 88:17 and exult in your name all day, and be exalted in your righteousness.
Psalms 88:18 Because you are the boast of their strength, and in your good pleasure our horn will be exalted.
Psalms 88:19 Because support belongs to the Lord, and to the Holy One of Israel, our king.
Psalms 88:20 Then you spoke in a vision to your holy ones and said: I placed help upon a mighty one; I exalted a chosen one from my people;
Psalms 88:21 I found Dauid my slave; with my holy oil I anointed him.
Psalms 88:22 For my hand will support him, and my arm will strengthen him;
Psalms 88:23 an enemy will not gain advantage over him, and a son of lawlessness will not continue to harm him;
Psalms 88:24 and I will cut down his enemies from before his face and rout those hating him.
Psalms 88:25 And my truth and my mercy are with him, and in my name his horn will be exalted;
Psalms 88:26 and I will place his hand in a sea and his right hand in rivers.
Psalms 88:27 He will call upon me: You are my father, my God and supporter of my salvation;
Psalms 88:28 and I will make him firstborn, high among the kings of the earth.
Psalms 88:29 Forever I will keep my mercy for him, and my covenant is faithful to him;
Psalms 88:30 and I will establish his seed for the age of the age, and his throne like the days of heaven.
Psalms 88:31 If his sons abandon my law and do not walk in my judgments,
Psalms 88:32 if they profane my ordinances and do not keep my commandments,
Psalms 88:33 I will visit their lawless deeds with a rod and their sins with scourges,
Psalms 88:34 but I will certainly not scatter my mercy away from him, nor will I act unjustly in my truth,
Psalms 88:35 nor will I profane my covenant, and I will certainly not reject the things proceeding through my lips.
Psalms 88:36 Once I swore in my holy place: If I lie to Dauid—
Psalms 88:37 His seed will remain forever, and his throne like the sun before me,
Psalms 88:38 and like the moon established forever; and the witness in heaven is faithful. Interlude.
Psalms 88:39 But you rejected and despised; you put off your anointed one;
Psalms 88:40 you overturned the covenant of your slave; you profaned his sanctuary to the ground.
Psalms 88:41 You pulled down all his fences; you made his fortifications a terror;
Psalms 88:42 all those traveling a road plundered him; he became a reproach to his neighbors.
Psalms 88:43 You exalted the right hand of his enemies; you gladdened all his enemies;
Psalms 88:44 you turned away the help of his sword and did not support him in the war.
Psalms 88:45 You removed him from purification; you broke his throne down to the ground;
Psalms 88:46 you shortened the days of his time; you poured shame upon him. Interlude.
Psalms 88:47 Until when, Lord, will you turn away to the end; will your wrath be kindled like fire?
Psalms 88:48 Remember what my existence is; for surely you did not create all the sons of humans in vain?
Psalms 88:49 Who is a human who will live and not see death, who will deliver his soul from the hand of Hades? Interlude.
Psalms 88:50 Where are your ancient mercies, Lord, which you swore to Dauid in your truth?
Psalms 88:51 Remember, Lord, the reproach of your slaves, which I bore in my bosom, of many nations,
Psalms 88:52 with which your enemies reproached, Lord, with which they reproached the exchange of your anointed one.
Psalms 88:53 Blessed is the Lord forever. May it be, may it be. – –

## Chapter 89

Psalms 89:1 A prayer of Moyses, a human of God. Lord, you became a refuge for us in generation and generation;
Psalms 89:2 before mountains came to be and the earth and inhabited world were formed, and from the age to the age, you are.
Psalms 89:3 Do not turn a human back to humiliation; and you said: Turn back, sons of humans.
Psalms 89:4 Because a thousand years in your eyes are like yesterday's day which passed, and a watch in the night.
Psalms 89:5 Their things of no account will be years. In the morning may he pass away like green grass,
Psalms 89:6 in the morning may he blossom and pass away, in the evening may he fall off, grow hard and dry.
Psalms 89:7 Because we failed in your wrath and were troubled in your fury.
Psalms 89:8 You placed our lawless deeds before you; our lifetime is in the illumination of your face.
Psalms 89:9 Because all our days failed, and in your wrath we failed; they pondered our years like a spider.
Psalms 89:10 The days of our years, in them are seventy years, but if in strength, eighty years, and most of them toil and pain; because gentleness came upon us, and we will be disciplined.
Psalms 89:11 Who knows the strength of your wrath, and from fear of you, your fury?
Psalms 89:12 Thus make known how to number your right hand, and those fettered in heart in wisdom.
Psalms 89:13 Turn back, Lord; until when? And be comforted concerning your slaves.
Psalms 89:14 We were filled in the morning with your mercy and exulted and rejoiced in all our days;
Psalms 89:15 we rejoiced in return for the days in which you humbled us, the years in which we saw evils.
Psalms 89:16 And look upon your slaves and your works, and guide their sons,
Psalms 89:17 and let the splendor of the Lord our God be upon us, and direct the works of our hands upon us.

## Chapter 90

Psalms 90:1 Praise of a song for Dauid. The one dwelling in the help of the Most High will lodge in the shelter of the God of heaven.
Psalms 90:2 He will say to the Lord: You are my supporter and my refuge, my God; I will hope in him,
Psalms 90:3 because he will deliver me from a trap of hunters and from a troubling word.
Psalms 90:4 With his back he will overshadow you, and beneath his wings you will hope; his truth will encircle you with a weapon.
Psalms 90:5 You will not be afraid of a fear by night, of an arrow flying by day,
Psalms 90:6 of a thing passing through in darkness, of calamity and a midday demon.
Psalms 90:7 A thousand will fall from your side and ten thousand from your right, but it will not approach you;
Psalms 90:8 but with your eyes you will perceive and see the repayment of sinners.
Psalms 90:9 Because you, Lord, are my hope; you made the Most High your refuge.
Psalms 90:10 Evils will not approach you, and a scourge will not approach your dwelling,
Psalms 90:11 because he will command his angels concerning you, to guard you in all your ways;
Psalms 90:12 upon hands they will lift you, lest you strike your foot against a stone;
Psalms 90:13 upon an asp and a basilisk you will step, and you will trample a lion and a dragon.
Psalms 90:14 Because he hoped in me, I will also deliver him; I will shelter him, because he knew my name.
Psalms 90:15 He will call upon me, and I will hear him; I am with him in affliction, and I will deliver and glorify him.
Psalms 90:16 I will fill him with length of days and show him my salvation.

## Chapter 91

Psalms 91:1 A psalm of a song, for the day of the sabbath.
Psalms 91:2 It is good to acknowledge the Lord and sing to your name, Most High,
Psalms 91:3 to announce your mercy in the morning and your truth by night,
Psalms 91:4 with a ten-stringed psaltery, with a song on a lyre.
Psalms 91:5 Because you gladdened me, Lord, with your deed, and in the works of your hands I will exult.
Psalms 91:6 How your works were magnified, Lord; your reasonings became very deep.
Psalms 91:7 A foolish man will not know, and a senseless one will not understand these things.
Psalms 91:8 When sinners sprouted like grass, and all those working lawlessness leaned down, so that they might be destroyed for the age of the age.
Psalms 91:9 But you are Most High forever, Lord;
Psalms 91:10 because, behold, your enemies will perish, and all those working lawlessness will be scattered,
Psalms 91:11 and my horn will be exalted like that of a one-horned beast, and my old age in rich oil,
Psalms 91:12 and my eye looked upon my enemies, and my ear will hear among those rising against me, doing evil.
Psalms 91:13 A righteous one will blossom like a palm; like the cedar in Libanos he will multiply.
Psalms 91:14 Planted in the house of the Lord, they will blossom in the courts of our God;
Psalms 91:15 they will still multiply in rich old age and will be flourishing,
Psalms 91:16 to announce that the Lord my God is upright and there is no injustice in him.

## Chapter 92

Psalms 92:1 For the day before the sabbath, when the earth has been settled; praise of a song for Dauid. The Lord reigned; he clothed himself with magnificence; the Lord clothed himself with strength and girded himself; for indeed he made the inhabited world firm, which will not be shaken.
Psalms 92:2 Your throne is ready from then; you are from the age.
