## Chapter 1

Odes 1:1 t A song of Moyses in Exodus.
Odes 1:1 LET US SING to the Lord, for he has been gloriously glorified; horse and rider he threw into the sea.
Odes 1:2 He became a helper and shelterer to me for salvation; this is my God, and I shall glorify him, the God of my father, and I shall exalt him.
Odes 1:3 The Lord shatters wars; Lord is his name.
Odes 1:4 Pharao's chariots and his force he threw into the sea; chosen riders, officers of the third rank, he drowned in the Red Sea;
Odes 1:5 he covered them with the sea; they sank into the depth like a stone.
Odes 1:6 Your right hand, Lord, has been glorified in strength; your right hand, Lord, shattered enemies.
Odes 1:7 And by the abundance of your glory you shattered the adversaries; you sent out your wrath, and it devoured them like stubble.
Odes 1:8 And through the breath of your anger the water parted; the waters congealed like a wall; the waves congealed in the midst of the sea.
Odes 1:9 The enemy said, Pursuing, I shall overtake; I shall divide spoils; I shall fill my soul; I shall kill with my sword; my hand will rule.
Odes 1:10 You sent out your wind; the sea covered them; they sank like lead in violent water.
Odes 1:11 Who is like you among gods, Lord? Who is like you, glorified among holy ones, marvelous in glories, doing wonders?
Odes 1:12 You stretched out your right hand, and the earth swallowed them.
Odes 1:13 With your righteousness you led this people of yours whom you redeemed; with your strength you encouraged them toward your holy lodging.
Odes 1:14 Nations heard and were angered; pangs seized those dwelling in Phylistiim.
Odes 1:15 Then leaders of Edom hastened, and rulers of the Moabites; trembling seized them; all who dwell in Chanaan melted.
Odes 1:16 May fear and trembling fall upon them; by the greatness of your arm let them be turned to stone, until your people pass through, Lord, until this people of yours whom you acquired pass through.
Odes 1:17 Bring them in and plant them on a mountain of your inheritance, in your prepared dwelling which you made, Lord, a sanctuary, Lord, which your hands prepared.
Odes 1:18 The Lord reigns for the age and unto an age and still further.
Odes 1:19 Because Pharao's horse entered the sea with chariots and riders, and the Lord brought upon them the water of the sea; but the sons of Israel walked through dry land in the midst of the sea.

## Chapter 2

Odes 2:1 t A song of Moyses in Deuteronomy.
Odes 2:1 ATTEND, heaven, and I shall speak, and let earth hear words from my mouth.
Odes 2:2 Let my utterance be awaited like rain, and let my words descend like dew, like a shower upon grass and like snowfall upon herbage.
Odes 2:3 Because I called the name of the Lord; give greatness to our God.
Odes 2:4 God, his works are true, and all his ways are judgment; a faithful God, and there is no injustice; righteous and holy is the Lord.
Odes 2:5 Blameworthy children sinned, not against him, a crooked and perverted generation.
Odes 2:6 Do you thus repay these things to the Lord, foolish and unwise people? Did not this one himself, your father, acquire you and make you and create you?
Odes 2:7 Remember days of an age; understand years of a generation of generations; ask your father, and he will announce to you, your elders, and they will tell you.
Odes 2:8 When the Most High was dividing nations, as he scattered sons of Adam, he set boundaries of nations according to the number of angels of God,
Odes 2:9 and his people Iakob became the Lord's portion, Israel the measured allotment of his inheritance.
Odes 2:10 He made him sufficient in the wilderness, in thirst of burning heat in a waterless place; he surrounded him and disciplined him and guarded him like the pupil of an eye,
Odes 2:11 like an eagle to shelter its nest, and he yearned over his nestlings; spreading his wings, he received them and took them up upon his back.
Odes 2:12 The Lord alone led them, and there was no foreign god with them.
Odes 2:13 He brought them up upon the strength of the earth; he fed them produce of fields; they sucked honey from rock and oil from solid rock,
Odes 2:14 butter of cattle and milk of sheep with fat of lambs and rams, offspring of bulls and goats, with fat of kidneys of wheat; and they drank blood of a grape as wine.
Odes 2:15 And Iakob ate and was filled, and the beloved one kicked away; he grew fat, grew thick, grew broad; and he forsook God who made him and departed from God his savior.
Odes 2:16 They provoked me over foreign things; with their abominations they embittered me;
Odes 2:17 they sacrificed to demons and not to God, to gods whom they did not know; new and recent ones have come whom their fathers did not know.
Odes 2:18 You forsook God who begot you, and forgot God who nourishes you.
Odes 2:19 And the Lord saw and grew jealous and was provoked because of the wrath of his sons and daughters,
Odes 2:20 and said, I shall turn my face away from them and show what will happen to them at the last; because it is a perverted generation, sons in whom there is no faith.
Odes 2:21 They made me jealous over what is no god; they angered me with their idols; and I shall make them jealous over what is no nation; over a nation without understanding I shall anger them.
Odes 2:22 Because a fire has been kindled from my anger, it will burn down to Hades below, devour earth and its produce, set ablaze foundations of mountains.
Odes 2:23 I shall gather evils upon them, and expend my arrows upon them.
Odes 2:24 Wasting away with hunger and the devouring of birds, and incurable backward convulsion; I shall send out upon them teeth of wild beasts, with the fury of things crawling upon earth.
Odes 2:25 Outside, a sword will bereave them, and from the chambers, fear; a young man with a virgin, a suckling with an established elder.
Odes 2:26 I said, I shall scatter them; I shall indeed put an end to their memorial among humans,
Odes 2:27 were it not for the wrath of enemies, so that they may not last long, and so that the adversaries may not attack together, lest they say, Our hand is high, and the Lord did not do all these things.
Odes 2:28 Because it is a nation that has lost counsel, and there is no knowledge among them.
Odes 2:29 They did not take thought to understand these things; let them receive them for the coming time.
Odes 2:30 How will one pursue a thousand, and two move tens of thousands, unless God sold them and the Lord handed them over?
Odes 2:31 For their gods are not like our God; but our enemies are senseless.
Odes 2:32 For their vine is from a vine of Sodoma, and their vine branch from Gomorra; their grape is a grape of gall, a cluster of bitterness for them;
Odes 2:33 their wine is the venom of dragons and the incurable venom of asps.
Odes 2:34 Behold, have not all these things been gathered with me and sealed in my treasuries?
Odes 2:35 On a day of vengeance I shall repay, at a time when their foot slips; because the day of their destruction is near, and things prepared for you are present.
Odes 2:36 Because the Lord will judge his people, and concerning his slaves he will be comforted; for he saw them enfeebled and failing under attack and slackened.
Odes 2:37 And the Lord said, Where are their gods, in whom they had trusted,
Odes 2:38 whose fat of their sacrifices you were eating and whose wine of their libations you were drinking? Let them rise and help you and become shelterers for you.
Odes 2:39 See, see that I am, and there is no god except me; I shall kill and make alive; I shall strike, and I shall heal; and there is no one who will rescue from my hands.
Odes 2:40 Because I shall lift my hand to heaven and swear by my right hand and say, I live unto the age,
Odes 2:41 because I shall sharpen my sword like lightning, and my hand will hold fast to judgment, and I shall repay justice to the enemies, and to those who hate me I shall repay;
Odes 2:42 I shall make my arrows drunk with blood, and my sword will devour flesh, from the blood of wounded ones and captivity, from the head of rulers of nations.
Odes 2:43 Rejoice, heavens, together with him, and let all the angels of God bow down to him; rejoice, nations, with his people, and let all sons of God strengthen themselves for him; because the blood of his sons is avenged, and he will avenge and repay justice to the enemies, and repay those who hate, and the Lord will cleanse the land of his people.

## Chapter 3

Odes 3:1 t A prayer of Anna, mother of Samouel.
Odes 3:1 MY HEART WAS STRENGTHENED in the Lord; my horn was exalted in my God; my mouth was widened against my enemies; I rejoiced in your salvation.
Odes 3:2 Because there is no holy one like the Lord, and there is no righteous one like our God; there is no holy one except you.
Odes 3:3 Do not boast and do not speak lofty things, nor let grand speech come out of your mouth, because the Lord is a God of knowledge, and God prepares his practices.
Odes 3:4 The bow of mighty ones grew weak, and those who are weak girded themselves with strength;
Odes 3:5 those full of bread were diminished, and the hungry left the land; because a barren woman bore seven, and she who was abundant in children grew weak.
Odes 3:6 The Lord puts to death and brings to life, brings down to Hades and brings up;
Odes 3:7 the Lord makes poor and makes rich, humbles and lifts up.
Odes 3:8 He raises a needy one from earth and lifts a poor one from a dung heap, to seat him with rulers of a people, and assigns a throne of glory to them as an inheritance.
Odes 3:9 Giving a prayer to the one who prays, and he blessed the years of a righteous one; because a man is not mighty by strength,
Odes 3:10 the Lord will make his adversary weak; the Lord is holy. Let the wise one not boast in his wisdom, and let the mighty one not boast in his might, and let the rich one not boast in his riches, but let him who boasts boast only in this: to understand and know the Lord, and to do judgment and righteousness in the midst of the earth. The Lord went up into heavens and thundered; he himself will judge the ends of earth, being righteous, and gives strength to our kings, and will exalt the horn of his anointed one.

## Chapter 4

Odes 4:1 t A prayer of Ionas.
Odes 4:1 I CRIED in my affliction to the Lord my God, and he heard my cry from the belly of Hades; you heard my voice.
Odes 4:2 You cast me into depths of the heart of the sea, and rivers surrounded me; all your billows and your waves passed over me.
Odes 4:3 And I said, I have been thrust away from your eyes; shall I again look toward your holy temple?
Odes 4:4 Water poured around me as far as my soul; the utmost abyss surrounded me; my head sank into clefts of mountains.
Odes 4:5 I descended into a land whose bars are eternal restraints, and let my life ascend from corruption, Lord my God.
Odes 4:6 When my soul failed from me, I remembered the Lord, and may my prayer come to you, into your holy temple.
Odes 4:7 Those who guard vain and false things forsook their mercy.
Odes 4:8 But I shall sacrifice to you with a voice of praise and acknowledgment; whatever I vowed, I shall repay you for my salvation, to the Lord.

## Chapter 5

Odes 5:1 t A song of Esaias.
Odes 5:1 I SHALL SING, then, to the beloved one a song of the loved one for my vineyard; a vineyard came to be for the beloved one on a horn, in a fertile place,
Odes 5:2 and I put a fence around it and planted a vine in Sorek and built a tower in its midst and dug a wine-vat in it; and I waited for it to produce a grape, but it produced thorns.
Odes 5:3 And now, person of Iouda and those dwelling in Ierousalem, judge between me and my vineyard.
Odes 5:4 What shall I yet do to my vineyard that I did not do to it? Because I waited for it to produce a grape, but it produced thorns.
Odes 5:5 But now I shall announce to you what I shall do to my vineyard; I shall remove its fence, and it will be for plunder, and I shall tear down its wall, and it will be for trampling,
Odes 5:6 and I shall abandon my vineyard, and it will certainly not be pruned nor dug, and thorns will come up into it as into waste land, and I shall command the clouds not to rain rain upon it.
Odes 5:7 For the vineyard of the Lord Sabaoth is the house of Israel, and a person of Iouda a beloved new plant, and I waited for it to do judgment, but it did lawlessness, and not righteousness, but a cry.
Odes 5:8 Woe to those who join house to house and bring field near to field, so that they may take away their neighbor's property; will you dwell alone upon the earth?
Odes 5:9 For all these things were heard in the ears of the Lord Sabaoth.

## Chapter 6

Odes 6:1 t A prayer of Esaias.
Odes 6:1 FROM NIGHT my spirit rises early toward you, God, because your commands are light upon the earth; learn righteousness, you who dwell upon the earth.
Odes 6:2 For the ungodly one has ceased; he will certainly not learn righteousness upon the earth; he will certainly not do truth; let the ungodly one be removed, so that he may not see the glory of the Lord.
Odes 6:3 Lord, your arm is high, and they did not know, but having known, let them be ashamed; zeal will seize an undisciplined people, and now fire will devour the adversaries.
Odes 6:4 Lord our God, give us peace; for you repaid all things to us.
Odes 6:5 Lord our God, acquire us; Lord, apart from you we know no other; we name your name.
Odes 6:6 But the dead will certainly not see life, nor will physicians certainly raise them; because of this you brought calamity and destroyed and removed every male of theirs.
Odes 6:7 Add evils to them, Lord; add evils to the glorious ones of the earth.
Odes 6:8 Lord, in affliction I remembered you; in small affliction your discipline is for us.
Odes 6:9 And as she who is in labor draws near to giving birth and cries out in her pang, so we became to your beloved one.
Odes 6:10 Because of your fear, Lord, we conceived in the womb and labored and gave birth; we made a spirit of your salvation upon the earth; we shall not fall, but those dwelling upon the earth will fall.
Odes 6:11 The dead will rise, and those in the tombs will be raised, and those in the earth will rejoice; for the dew from you is a healing for them, but the land of the ungodly will fall.
Odes 6:12 Go, my people, enter your chambers, shut your door, hide yourself for a little while, until the wrath of the Lord passes by.

## Chapter 7

Odes 7:1 t A prayer of Ezekias.
Odes 7:1 I said, At the height of my days I shall go in the gates of Hades; I shall leave behind the remaining years.
Odes 7:2 I said, No longer shall I see the salvation of God upon the earth; I shall certainly not see a human among those dwelling.
Odes 7:3 I failed from my kindred; I left behind the rest of my life; it went out and departed from me like one who takes down a tent after pitching it; my spirit within me became like a web, with a weaving woman drawing near to cut it off.
Odes 7:4 On that day I was handed over until morning as to a lion; thus he shattered all my bones; for from day until night I was handed over.
Odes 7:5 Like a swallow, so I shall utter a sound, and like a dove, so I shall murmur; for my eyes failed from looking to the height of heaven toward the Lord,
Odes 7:6 who rescued me and removed from me the pain of my soul.
Odes 7:7 Lord, for concerning it an announcement was made to you, and you roused my breath, and being comforted, I lived;
Odes 7:8 for you chose my soul, so that it may not perish, and cast behind me all my sins.
Odes 7:9 For those in Hades will not praise you, nor will those who died bless you, nor will those in Hades hope in your mercy;
Odes 7:10 the living will bless you, as I also do. For from today I shall make children who will announce your righteousness, Lord of my salvation,
Odes 7:11 and I shall not cease blessing you with a psaltery all the days of my life before the house of God.

## Chapter 8

Odes 8:1 t A prayer of Manasse.
Odes 8:1 LORD almighty, God of our fathers, of Abraam and Isaak and Iakob and of their righteous seed,
Odes 8:2 who made heaven and earth with all their adornment,
Odes 8:3 who fettered the sea by the word of your command, who shut the abyss and sealed it with your fearful and glorious name;
Odes 8:4 whom all things shudder at and tremble before the face of your power,
Odes 8:5 because the magnificence of your glory is unbearable, and the wrath of your threat against sinners cannot be withstood,
Odes 8:6 and the mercy of your promise is immeasurable and unsearchable,
Odes 8:7 because you are Lord Most High, compassionate, long-suffering and abundant in mercy, and repenting over the evils of humans;
Odes 8:8 you, therefore, Lord, God of the righteous, did not set repentance for the righteous, for Abraam and Isaak and Iakob, who have not sinned against you, but you set repentance for me the sinner,
Odes 8:9 because I sinned beyond the number of sand of the sea; my lawless deeds multiplied, Lord, multiplied, and I am not worthy to gaze and see the height of heaven because of the abundance of my injustices,
Odes 8:10 bent down by a great bond of iron, to lift my head on account of my sins, and there is no relief for me, because I provoked your anger and did evil before you, setting up abominations and multiplying offenses.
Odes 8:11 And now I bend the knee of my heart, begging for the kindness from you:
Odes 8:12 I have sinned, Lord, I have sinned, and I know my lawless deeds.
Odes 8:13 I ask, begging you, Release me, Lord, release me; do not destroy me together with my lawless deeds, nor, being angry unto the age, keep evils for me, nor condemn me in the lowest parts of the earth. Because you are, Lord, the God of those who repent,
Odes 8:14 and may you show your goodness in me; because, though I am unworthy, you will save me according to your abundant mercy,
Odes 8:15 and I shall praise you continually in the days of my life. Because all the power of the heavens hymns you, and yours is the glory unto the ages. Amen.

## Chapter 9

Odes 9:1 t A prayer of Ambakoum.
Odes 9:1 LORD, I have heard your report and was afraid; I considered your works and was astonished. In the midst of two living creatures you will be known; when the years draw near you will be recognized; when the time is present you will be shown forth; when my soul is troubled, in wrath you will remember mercy.
Odes 9:2 God will come from Thaiman, and the Holy One from Mount Pharan, shaded and thickly wooded. Interlude. His excellence covered heavens, and the earth is full of his praise.
Odes 9:3 And his radiance will be like light, horns in his hands, and he set a mighty love of his strength.
Odes 9:4 A word will go before his face, and he will go out, his feet in sandals.
Odes 9:5 He stood, and the earth was shaken; he looked, and nations melted. The mountains were shattered by force; eternal hills melted.
Odes 9:6 I saw his eternal paths in place of toils; dwellings of Ethiopians will be terrified, and the tents of the land of Madiam.
Odes 9:7 Were you angered at rivers, Lord, or was your anger at rivers, or your onrush at the sea? Because you will mount your horses, and your riding is salvation.
Odes 9:8 Stretching, you will stretch your bow against scepters, says the Lord. Interlude. Earth will be broken open by rivers.
Odes 9:9 Peoples will see you and be in labor. Scattering waters of a passage; the abyss gave its voice; the height of its apparition was raised.
Odes 9:10 The sun and the moon stood in her station; your missiles will go into light, into the radiance of the lightning of your weapons.
Odes 9:11 With your threat you will diminish earth, and with anger you will bring down nations.
Odes 9:12 You went out for the salvation of your people, to save your anointed ones; you cast death upon heads of lawless ones; you raised bonds as far as the neck. Interlude.
Odes 9:13 You cut through heads of rulers in astonishment; they will be shaken in it; they will open their bridles like a poor one eating secretly.
Odes 9:14 And you drove your horses into the sea, troubling many waters.
Odes 9:15 I kept watch, and my belly was terrified at the voice of the prayer of my lips, and trembling entered my bones, and beneath me my condition was troubled. I shall rest on the day of my affliction, to go up to a people of my sojourning.
Odes 9:16 Because a fig tree will not bear fruit, and there will be no produce on the vines; the work of an olive tree will prove false, and the plains will not produce food; sheep failed from lack of food, and oxen do not exist at the mangers of their propitiation.
Odes 9:17 But I shall exult in the Lord; I shall rejoice in God my savior.
Odes 9:18 The Lord my God is my strength, and will set my feet for completion; upon the high places he brings me up, to conquer in his song.

## Chapter 10

Odes 10:1 t A prayer of Azarias.
Odes 10:1 BLESSED are you, Lord, God of our fathers, and praiseworthy and glorified is your name unto the ages,
Odes 10:2 because you are righteous in all things you did to us, and all your works are true, and your ways upright, and all your judgments true,
Odes 10:3 and you executed judgments of truth in all things you brought upon us, and upon the holy city of our fathers, Ierousalem, because in truth and judgment you brought all these things because of our sins.
Odes 10:4 Because we sinned and acted lawlessly in departing from you, and sinned in all things, and did not hear your commandments,
Odes 10:5 nor kept them nor did as you commanded us, so that it may be well with us.
Odes 10:6 And all things you brought upon us, and all things you did to us, you did in true judgment,
Odes 10:7 and handed us over into hands of lawless enemies, most hateful apostates, and to a king unjust and most evil beyond all the earth.
Odes 10:8 And now it is not possible for us to open our mouth; shame and reproach came upon your slaves and those who revere you.
Odes 10:9 Do not, then, hand us over to the end, for the sake of your name, and do not scatter your covenant,
Odes 10:10 and do not remove your mercy from us, for the sake of Abraam who was loved by you, and for the sake of Isaak your slave and Israel your holy one,
Odes 10:11 to whom you spoke, saying that you would multiply their seed like the stars of heaven and like the sand by the lip of the sea.
Odes 10:12 Because, Master, we were made smaller than all the nations, and are lowly in all the earth today because of our sins,
Odes 10:13 and at this time there is no ruler and prophet and leader, nor a whole burnt offering nor sacrifice nor offering nor incense, no place to offer firstfruits before you and find mercy.
Odes 10:14 But with a broken soul and a spirit of humility may we be received, as with whole burnt offerings of rams and bulls and as with tens of thousands of fat lambs;
Odes 10:15 thus let our sacrifice be before you today, and let us follow after you completely, because there is no shame for those who trust in you.
Odes 10:16 And now we follow with a whole heart and fear you and seek your face; do not put us to shame,
Odes 10:17 but act with us according to your gentleness and according to the abundance of your mercy,
Odes 10:18 and rescue us according to your marvelous things and give glory to your name, Lord.
Odes 10:19 And may all who show evils to your slaves be abashed, and may they be put to shame from all power and might, and may their strength be shattered,
Odes 10:20 and let them know that you are Lord, the only God, and glorious over the whole inhabited world.

# Proverbs

The Apostolic Bible. Public domain. https://apostolic-bible.ysys9.chatgpt.site/license.html


## Chapter 1

Proverbs 1:1 Proverbs of Salomon, son of Dauid, who reigned in Israel,
Proverbs 1:2 to know wisdom and discipline, and to understand words of prudence,
Proverbs 1:3 and to receive turns of words, and to understand true righteousness and direct judgment,
Proverbs 1:4 so that he may give shrewdness to the innocent, and perception and thought to a young child;
Proverbs 1:5 for a wise one who hears these things will be wiser, and the understanding one will acquire guidance,
Proverbs 1:6 and will understand a parable and a dark saying, sayings of the wise and riddles.
Proverbs 1:7 The beginning of wisdom is fear of God, and understanding is good for all who practice it; reverence toward God is the beginning of perception, but the ungodly will despise wisdom and discipline.
Proverbs 1:8 Hear, son, your father's discipline, and do not thrust away your mother's ordinances;
Proverbs 1:9 for you will receive a crown of graces for your head and a golden collar around your neck.
Proverbs 1:10 Son, let ungodly men not lead you astray, nor consent if they exhort you, saying,
Proverbs 1:11 Come with us, share in blood, and let us hide a righteous man unjustly in the earth,
Proverbs 1:12 and let us swallow him alive like Hades, and remove his memory from the earth;
Proverbs 1:13 let us seize his costly possession, and fill our houses with spoils;
Proverbs 1:14 cast your lot among us, and let us all acquire a common purse, and let there be one pouch for us.
Proverbs 1:15 Do not walk on a way with them, but turn your foot aside from their paths;
Proverbs 1:16 for their feet run toward evil, and are swift to shed blood;
Proverbs 1:17 for nets are not unjustly spread for winged creatures.
Proverbs 1:18 For those who share in murder themselves store up evils for themselves, and the overthrow of lawless men is evil.
Proverbs 1:19 These are the ways of all who carry out lawless things; for by ungodliness they take away their own soul.
Proverbs 1:20 Wisdom is hymned at exits, and in squares she practices frank speech,
Proverbs 1:21 and on the tops of walls she is proclaimed, and at rulers' gates she sits beside them, and at city gates she confidently says,
Proverbs 1:22 As long as the innocent hold fast to righteousness, they will not be ashamed; but the foolish, being desirers of insolence, became ungodly and hated perception,
Proverbs 1:23 and became liable to reproofs. Behold, I shall send forth to you an utterance of my breath, and teach you my word.
Proverbs 1:24 Since I was calling and you did not obey, and I was extending words and you did not attend,
Proverbs 1:25 but you were rendering my counsels void, and disobeyed my reproofs,
Proverbs 1:26 therefore I also shall laugh at your destruction, and rejoice over you when ruin comes to you,
Proverbs 1:27 and when tumult reaches you suddenly, and overthrow is present like a storm, and when affliction and siege come to you, or when ruin comes to you.
Proverbs 1:28 For it will be when you call upon me, but I shall not hear you; evil ones will seek me and not find me.
Proverbs 1:29 For they hated wisdom, and did not choose the fear of the Lord,
Proverbs 1:30 nor wished to attend to my counsels, but were sneering at my reproofs.
Proverbs 1:31 Therefore they will eat the fruits of their own way, and be filled with their own ungodliness;
Proverbs 1:32 for in return for wronging infants they will be murdered, and examination will destroy the ungodly.
Proverbs 1:33 But the one who hears me will encamp in hope, and rest without fear from every evil.

## Chapter 2

Proverbs 2:1 Son, if, receiving an utterance of my commandment, you hide it with yourself,
Proverbs 2:2 your ear will obey wisdom, and you will apply your heart to understanding, and apply it to admonition for your son.
Proverbs 2:3 For if you call upon wisdom and give your voice to understanding, and seek perception with a great voice,
Proverbs 2:4 and if you seek her like silver and search her out like treasures,
Proverbs 2:5 then you will understand fear of the Lord and find knowledge of God.
Proverbs 2:6 Because the Lord gives wisdom, and from his face come knowledge and understanding;
Proverbs 2:7 and he stores up salvation for those who act rightly; he will defend their journey,
Proverbs 2:8 to guard ways of ordinances, and he will preserve the way of those who revere him.
Proverbs 2:9 Then you will understand righteousness and judgment, and set straight all good tracks.
Proverbs 2:10 For if wisdom comes into your thought, and perception seems beautiful to your soul,
Proverbs 2:11 good counsel will guard you, and holy thought will keep you,
Proverbs 2:12 so that she may deliver you from an evil way and from a man who speaks nothing trustworthy.
Proverbs 2:13 O you who forsake straight ways to walk in ways of darkness,
Proverbs 2:14 who rejoice over evils and delight in evil perversity,
Proverbs 2:15 whose paths are crooked, and their tracks curved,
Proverbs 2:16 to make you far from a straight way and a stranger to righteous judgment.
Proverbs 2:17 Son, let evil counsel not overtake you, which leaves behind the teaching of youth and has forgotten a divine covenant;
Proverbs 2:18 for she set her house beside death, and her tracks beside Hades with the earthborn;
Proverbs 2:19 all who walk in her will not return, nor will they attain straight paths; for they are not overtaken by years of life.
Proverbs 2:20 For if they were walking good paths, they would have found smooth paths of righteousness.
Proverbs 2:21 The kind will be inhabitants of earth, and the innocent will remain in it, because the upright will encamp on earth, and the holy will remain in it;
Proverbs 2:22 ways of the ungodly will perish from earth, and the lawless will be thrust out of it.

## Chapter 3

Proverbs 3:1 Son, do not forget my laws, and let your heart keep my words;
Proverbs 3:2 for they will add to you length of life and years of life and peace.
Proverbs 3:3 Let mercies and faithfulnesses not fail you, but fasten them upon your neck, and you will find grace;
Proverbs 3:4 and take thought for good things before the Lord and humans.
Proverbs 3:5 Be trusting in God with a whole heart, but do not be exalted over your own wisdom;
Proverbs 3:6 in all your ways make her known, so that she may cut your ways straight, [and your foot will certainly not stumble.]
Proverbs 3:7 Do not be prudent in your own estimation, but fear God and turn aside from every evil;
Proverbs 3:8 then there will be healing for your body and care for your bones.
Proverbs 3:9 Honor the Lord from your righteous labors, and offer firstfruits to him from your fruits of righteousness,
Proverbs 3:10 so that your storehouses may be filled with an abundance of grain, and your winepresses overflow with wine.
Proverbs 3:11 Son, do not make light of the Lord's discipline, nor grow faint when reproved by him;
Proverbs 3:12 for whom the Lord loves he disciplines, and he scourges every son whom he receives.
Proverbs 3:13 Blessed is a human who found wisdom, and a mortal who saw prudence;
Proverbs 3:14 for trading in her is better than treasures of gold and silver.
Proverbs 3:15 And she is more precious than costly stones; nothing evil will oppose her; she is well known to all who draw near to her, and everything precious is not worthy of her.
Proverbs 3:16 For length of life and years of life are in her right hand, and in her left hand riches and glory;
Proverbs 3:16 a From her mouth righteousness goes out, and she carries law and mercy upon her tongue.
Proverbs 3:17 Her ways are beautiful ways, and all her paths are in peace;
Proverbs 3:18 she is a tree of life to all who hold fast to her, and secure for those leaning upon her as upon the Lord.
Proverbs 3:19 God founded the earth by wisdom, and prepared heavens with prudence;
Proverbs 3:20 with perception abysses were broken open, and clouds flowed with dews.
Proverbs 3:21 Son, do not drift away, but keep my counsel and thought,
Proverbs 3:22 so that your soul may live, and grace be around your neck.
Proverbs 3:22 a And there will be healing for your flesh and care for your bones,
Proverbs 3:23 so that you may walk confidently in peace on all your ways, and your foot will certainly not stumble.
Proverbs 3:24 For if you sit, you will be fearless, and if you lie down, you will sleep pleasantly;
Proverbs 3:25 and you will not fear terror coming upon you, nor onrushes of ungodly ones coming upon you;
Proverbs 3:26 for the Lord will be upon all your ways, and will support your foot, so that you may not be shaken.
Proverbs 3:27 Do not withhold doing good to a needy one whenever your hand has the means to help;
Proverbs 3:28 do not say, Go away and return, and tomorrow I shall give, when you are able to do good; for you do not know what the coming day will bear.
Proverbs 3:29 Do not devise evils against your friend who sojourns and trusts in you.
Proverbs 3:30 Do not be hostile toward a human in vain, lest he do some evil to you.
Proverbs 3:31 Do not acquire reproaches of evil men, nor be jealous of their ways;
Proverbs 3:32 for every lawless one is unclean before the Lord, and he does not sit in council among the righteous.
Proverbs 3:33 God's curse is in houses of the ungodly, but dwellings of the righteous are blessed.
Proverbs 3:34 The Lord opposes the arrogant, but gives grace to the humble.
Proverbs 3:35 The wise will inherit glory, but the ungodly exalted dishonor.

## Chapter 4

Proverbs 4:1 Hear, children, a father's discipline, and attend to know thought;
Proverbs 4:2 for I give you a good gift; do not forsake my law.
Proverbs 4:3 For I also became a son obedient to a father and loved before a mother's face,
Proverbs 4:4 who were saying and teaching me, Let our word be fixed in your heart;
Proverbs 4:5 guard commandments; do not forget nor overlook an utterance of my mouth,
Proverbs 4:6 nor forsake her, and she will hold fast to you; love her, and she will keep you;
Proverbs 4:8 fortify her, and she will exalt you; honor her, so that she may embrace you,
Proverbs 4:9 so that she may give your head a crown of graces, and defend you with a crown of delight.
Proverbs 4:10 Hear, son, and receive my words, and years of your life will be multiplied, so that there may be many ways of life for you;
Proverbs 4:11 for I teach you ways of wisdom, and set you on straight tracks.
Proverbs 4:12 For if you walk, your steps will not be confined; and if you run, you will not grow weary.
Proverbs 4:13 Take hold of my discipline; do not let go, but guard her for yourself for your life.
Proverbs 4:14 Do not enter ways of the ungodly, nor be jealous of ways of the lawless;
Proverbs 4:15 in whatever place they encamp, do not enter there, but turn aside from them and pass by.
Proverbs 4:16 For they will certainly not sleep unless they do evil; their sleep has been taken away, and they do not lie down;
Proverbs 4:17 for these feed on food of ungodliness, and become drunk with lawless wine.
Proverbs 4:18 But the ways of the righteous shine like light; they go forward and illuminate until the day comes fully right;
Proverbs 4:19 but the ways of the ungodly are dark; they do not know how they stumble.
Proverbs 4:20 Son, attend to my utterance, and apply your ear to my words,
Proverbs 4:21 so that your springs may not fail you; guard them in your heart;
Proverbs 4:22 for they are life to those who find them, and healing to all flesh.
Proverbs 4:23 With every guard keep your heart; for from these are exits of life.
Proverbs 4:24 Remove a crooked mouth from yourself, and thrust unjust lips far from you.
Proverbs 4:25 Let your eyes look straight, and let your eyelids incline toward righteous things.
Proverbs 4:26 Make straight tracks for your feet, and direct your ways.
Proverbs 4:27 Do not turn aside to the right or to the left, but turn your foot away from an evil way;
Proverbs 4:27 a For God knows the ways on the right, but those on the left are perverted;
Proverbs 4:28 and he himself will make your tracks straight, and lead your journeys forward in peace.

## Chapter 5

Proverbs 5:1 Son, attend to my wisdom, and apply your ear to my words,
Proverbs 5:2 so that you may guard good thought; and I command you perception of my lips.
Proverbs 5:3 Do not attend to a worthless woman; for honey drips from a prostitute's lips, who for a time makes your throat smooth,
Proverbs 5:4 yet afterward you will find it more bitter than gall and sharpened more than a two-edged sword.
Proverbs 5:5 For the feet of folly bring those who use her down with death into Hades, and her footsteps are not firmly fixed;
Proverbs 5:6 for she does not enter ways of life, and her tracks are slippery and not well known.
Proverbs 5:7 Now therefore, son, hear me, and do not render my words void;
Proverbs 5:8 make your way far from her; do not draw near the doors of her houses,
Proverbs 5:9 so that you may not give away your life to others and your livelihood to the merciless,
Proverbs 5:10 so that strangers may not be filled with your strength, and your labors enter strangers' houses,
Proverbs 5:11 and you will regret it at the last, when the flesh of your body is worn away,
Proverbs 5:12 and say, How I hated discipline, and my heart turned aside from reproofs;
Proverbs 5:13 I was not hearing the voice of him who disciplined me, and was not applying my ear to him who taught me;
Proverbs 5:14 I came close to being in every evil in the midst of assembly and congregation.
Proverbs 5:15 Drink waters from your vessels and from your spring's wells.
Proverbs 5:16 Let the waters from your spring not overflow for you, but let your waters pass through your squares;
Proverbs 5:17 let them belong to you alone, and let no stranger share with you;
Proverbs 5:18 let your spring of water be your own, and rejoice together with the wife of your youth.
Proverbs 5:19 Let a deer of friendship and a foal of your graces consort with you, and let your own woman lead you and be with you at every time; for going about with her in her friendship, you will be greatly increased.
Proverbs 5:20 Do not be much with a foreign woman, nor be held in the embraces of one who is not your own;
Proverbs 5:21 for a man's ways are before God's eyes, and he observes all his tracks.
Proverbs 5:22 Lawless acts hunt a man, and each is bound tightly by cords of his own sins;
Proverbs 5:23 this one dies with the undisciplined, and from the abundance of his own livelihood he was cast out, and perished through folly.

## Chapter 6

Proverbs 6:1 Son, if you become surety for your friend, you will hand your hand over to an enemy;
Proverbs 6:2 for a man's own lips are a strong snare, and he is caught by the lips of his own mouth.
Proverbs 6:3 Do, son, what I command you, and save yourself – for you have come into hands of evil ones through your friend – go without growing faint, and urge your friend also, for whom you became surety;
Proverbs 6:4 do not give sleep to your eyes, nor slumber with your eyelids,
Proverbs 6:5 so that you may be saved like a gazelle from nooses and like a bird from a snare.
Proverbs 6:6 Go to the ant, O sluggard, and seeing its ways, emulate it, and become wiser than it;
Proverbs 6:7 for though no cultivated field belongs to it, and it has no one compelling it, nor is under a master,
Proverbs 6:8 it prepares its food in summer, and makes abundant provision at harvest.
Proverbs 6:8 a Or go to the bee and learn how she is a worker, and how nobly she performs her work,
Proverbs 6:9 whose labors kings and private people take for health, and she is desired by all and held in esteem;
Proverbs 6:10 although weak in strength, having honored wisdom, she was advanced.
Proverbs 6:9 How long, sluggard, do you lie down? And when will you rise from sleep?
Proverbs 6:10 You sleep a little, and sit a little, and slumber a little, and embrace your chest with your hands a little;
Proverbs 6:11 then poverty comes upon you like an evil traveler, and need like a good runner.
Proverbs 6:11 a But if you are diligent, your harvest will come like a spring, and need will desert you like an evil runner.
Proverbs 6:12 A foolish and lawless man walks ways that are not good;
Proverbs 6:13 and he himself winks with an eye, signals with a foot, and teaches with gestures of fingers,
Proverbs 6:14 and with a perverted heart devises evils at every time; such a one sets up disturbances for a city.
Proverbs 6:15 Because of this his destruction comes suddenly, a breaking apart and incurable shattering.
Proverbs 6:16 Because he delights in all things the Lord hates, and is shattered through uncleanness of soul;
Proverbs 6:17 the eye of an insolent one, an unjust tongue, hands shedding a righteous one's blood,
Proverbs 6:18 and a heart devising evil reasonings, and feet hastening to do evil;
Proverbs 6:19 an unjust witness kindles lies, and sends disputes between brothers.
Proverbs 6:20 Son, guard your father's laws, and do not thrust away your mother's ordinances;
Proverbs 6:21 fasten them upon your soul continually, and hang them as a collar upon your neck.
Proverbs 6:22 Whenever you walk, bring her along, and let her be with you; and when you lie down, let her guard you, so that she may speak with you when you rise;
Proverbs 6:23 because a commandment of law is a lamp and light, and reproof and discipline are a way of life,
Proverbs 6:24 to preserve you from a married woman and from slander of a foreign tongue.
Proverbs 6:25 Let desire for beauty not conquer you, nor be hunted by your eyes, nor seized by her eyelids;
Proverbs 6:26 for a prostitute's price is as much as even one loaf, but a woman of men hunts precious souls.
Proverbs 6:27 Will someone bind fire in his bosom, yet not burn up his garments?
Proverbs 6:28 Or will someone walk upon coals of fire, yet not burn up his feet?
Proverbs 6:29 Thus the one who goes in to a married woman; he will not be acquitted, nor anyone who touches her.
Proverbs 6:30 It is not surprising if someone is caught stealing, for he steals to fill his soul when hungry;
Proverbs 6:31 but if he is caught, he will repay sevenfold, and giving all his possessions, will deliver himself.
Proverbs 6:32 But the adulterer, through lack of sense, procures destruction for his soul,
Proverbs 6:33 and bears pains and dishonors, and his reproach will not be erased unto the age.
Proverbs 6:34 For her husband's anger is full of jealousy; he will not spare on a day of judgment;
Proverbs 6:35 he will not exchange his enmity for any ransom, nor be reconciled by many gifts.

## Chapter 7

Proverbs 7:1 Son, guard my words, and hide my commandments with yourself;
Proverbs 7:1 a Son, honor the Lord, and you will be strong, and apart from him fear no other.
Proverbs 7:2 Guard my commandments, and you will live, and my words like pupils of eyes;
Proverbs 7:3 put them around your fingers, and inscribe them upon the breadth of your heart.
Proverbs 7:4 Say that wisdom is your sister, and procure prudence as an acquaintance for yourself,
Proverbs 7:5 so that she may keep you from a foreign and evil woman, if she assails you with pleasing words.
Proverbs 7:6 For from a window of her house, peering out into the squares,
Proverbs 7:7 whatever young man among the foolish children she sees lacking sense,
Proverbs 7:8 passing by a corner in the passages of her houses,
Proverbs 7:9 and speaking in evening darkness, when the silence of night is gloomy,
Proverbs 7:10 the woman meets him, having a prostitute's appearance, who makes young men's hearts fly away.
Proverbs 7:11 And she is excited and prodigal, and her feet do not rest in a house;
Proverbs 7:12 for at one time she roams outside, and at another in squares she lies in wait beside every corner.
Proverbs 7:13 Then taking hold of him, she kissed him, and with a shameless face said to him,
Proverbs 7:14 I have a peace sacrifice; today I repay my vows;
Proverbs 7:15 because of this I came out to meet you; longing for your face, I have found you;
Proverbs 7:16 I have arranged my bed with bands, and spread it with double-sided coverings from Egypt;
Proverbs 7:17 I have sprinkled my couch with saffron, and my house with cinnamon;
Proverbs 7:18 come, and let us enjoy friendship until dawn; come here, and let us roll in love;
Proverbs 7:19 for my husband is not present in the house, but has gone on a long journey,
Proverbs 7:20 taking a bundle of silver in his hand; after many days he will return to his house.
Proverbs 7:21 And she led him astray with much conversation, and with nooses from her lips ran him aground.
Proverbs 7:22 And he followed her, made a fool, as an ox is led to slaughter, and as a dog to bonds,
Proverbs 7:23 or as a deer struck by an arrow in the liver, and he hastens like a bird into a snare, not knowing that he runs concerning his soul.
Proverbs 7:24 Now therefore, son, hear me, and attend to words of my mouth;
Proverbs 7:25 let your heart not incline to her ways;
Proverbs 7:26 for she has wounded and cast down many, and innumerable are those she has murdered;
Proverbs 7:27 her house is ways of Hades, leading down into the chambers of death.

## Chapter 8

Proverbs 8:1 You will proclaim wisdom, so that prudence may obey you;
Proverbs 8:2 for she is upon the high summits, and has stood in the midst of the paths;
Proverbs 8:3 for she sits beside rulers' gates, and at entrances she is hymned:
Proverbs 8:4 You, O humans, I exhort, and send forth my voice to sons of humans;
Proverbs 8:5 understand shrewdness, innocent ones, and you undisciplined ones, put in a heart.
Proverbs 8:6 Hear me, for I shall speak noble things, and bring forth straight things from my lips;
Proverbs 8:7 because my throat will meditate truth, and lying lips are abhorred before me.
Proverbs 8:8 All the words of my mouth are with righteousness; nothing in them is crooked or twisted;
Proverbs 8:9 all are plain to those who understand, and straight to those who find knowledge.
Proverbs 8:10 Take discipline and not silver, and knowledge above tested gold, and choose perception instead of pure gold;
Proverbs 8:11 for wisdom is better than costly stones, and everything precious is not worthy of her.
Proverbs 8:12 I, wisdom, encamped in counsel, and I called upon knowledge and thought.
Proverbs 8:13 Fear of the Lord hates injustice, both insolence and arrogance and ways of evil ones; and I have hated perverted ways of evil ones.
Proverbs 8:14 Mine are counsel and security, mine prudence, and mine strength;
Proverbs 8:15 through me kings reign, and rulers write righteousness;
Proverbs 8:16 through me magnates are magnified, and tyrants through me hold power over earth.
Proverbs 8:17 I love those who love me, and those who seek me will find me.
Proverbs 8:18 Riches and glory belong to me, and possession of many things and righteousness;
Proverbs 8:19 it is better to reap fruit from me than gold and a precious stone, and my produce is better than choice silver.
Proverbs 8:20 I walk in ways of righteousness, and move about in the midst of paths of an ordinance,
Proverbs 8:21 so that I may apportion substance to those who love me, and fill their treasuries with good things.
Proverbs 8:21 a If I announce to you the things happening daily, I shall remember to number the things from an age.
Proverbs 8:22 The Lord created me as a beginning of his ways for his works;
Proverbs 8:23 before the age he founded me in the beginning,
Proverbs 8:24 before making the earth and before making the abysses, before the springs of waters came forth,
Proverbs 8:25 before mountains were established, and before all hills he begets me.
Proverbs 8:26 The Lord made regions and uninhabited places and inhabited extremities of the world under heaven.
Proverbs 8:27 When he was preparing heaven, I was present with him, and when he was setting apart his own throne upon winds.
Proverbs 8:28 When he was making the clouds above strong, and when he was setting secure springs of the world under heaven,
Proverbs 8:29 and was making the foundations of the earth strong,
Proverbs 8:30 I was beside him, fitting together; I was she in whom he delighted. And daily I was rejoicing before his face at every time,
Proverbs 8:31 when he was rejoicing, having completed the inhabited world, and was delighting in sons of humans.
Proverbs 8:32 Now therefore, son, hear me.
Proverbs 8:34 Blessed is a man who will hear me, and a human who will guard my ways, keeping awake at my doors daily, keeping the posts of my entrances;
Proverbs 8:35 for my exits are exits of life, and favor is prepared from the Lord.
Proverbs 8:36 But those who sin against me act ungodly toward their own souls, and those who hate me love death.

## Chapter 9

Proverbs 9:1 Wisdom built a house for herself, and supported it with seven pillars;
Proverbs 9:2 she slaughtered her own sacrificial animals, mixed her own wine in a mixing bowl, and prepared her own table;
Proverbs 9:3 she sent out her own slaves, summoning with a loud proclamation to a mixing bowl, saying,
Proverbs 9:4 Whoever is foolish, let him turn aside to me; and to those lacking sense she said,
Proverbs 9:5 Come, eat of my bread, and drink wine which I mixed for you;
Proverbs 9:6 leave folly, and you will live, and seek prudence, so that you may live, and set understanding right with knowledge.
Proverbs 9:7 He who disciplines evil ones will receive dishonor for himself, and he who reproves the ungodly will blame himself.
Proverbs 9:8 Do not reprove evil ones, so that they may not hate you; reprove a wise one, and he will love you.
Proverbs 9:9 Give a wise one opportunity, and he will be wiser; make things known to a righteous one, and he will increase in receiving.
Proverbs 9:10 The beginning of wisdom is fear of the Lord, and counsel of holy ones is understanding;
Proverbs 9:10 a For knowing law belongs to good thought;
Proverbs 9:11 for in this manner you will live a long time, and years of your life will be added to you.
Proverbs 9:12 Son, if you become wise for yourself, you will be wise also for your neighbors; but if you turn out evil, you alone will draw up evils.
Proverbs 9:12 a He who leans upon lies will shepherd winds, and he himself will pursue flying birds;
Proverbs 9:13 for he forsook the ways of his own vineyard, and has strayed from the tracks of his own cultivated field;
Proverbs 9:14 and he passes through waterless wilderness and land laid out in thirsty places, and gathers fruitlessness with his hands.
Proverbs 9:13 A foolish and bold woman comes to lack a morsel, who does not know shame;
Proverbs 9:14 she sat at the doors of her own house upon a seat, conspicuously in squares,
Proverbs 9:15 calling to those passing by and going straight on their ways:
Proverbs 9:16 Whoever among you is most foolish, let him turn aside to me; and to those lacking prudence I exhort, saying,
Proverbs 9:17 Pleasantly partake of hidden bread and sweet water of theft.
Proverbs 9:18 But he does not know that earthborn ones perish beside her, and he meets with a ledge of Hades.
Proverbs 9:18 a But leap away; do not linger in the place, nor fix your eye toward her;
Proverbs 9:19 for thus you will cross foreign water and pass over a foreign river;
Proverbs 9:20 but abstain from foreign water, and do not drink from a foreign spring,
Proverbs 9:21 so that you may live a long time, and years of life be added to you. – –

## Chapter 10

Proverbs 10:1 A wise son gladdens a father, but a foolish son is grief to his mother.
Proverbs 10:2 Treasures will not benefit lawless ones, but righteousness will deliver from death.
Proverbs 10:3 The Lord will not starve a righteous soul, but will overturn the life of the ungodly.
Proverbs 10:4 Poverty humbles a man, but hands of the valiant make rich.
Proverbs 10:4 a A disciplined son will be wise, and will use the foolish one as a servant.
Proverbs 10:5 An understanding son was preserved from burning heat, but a lawless son becomes wind-damaged at harvest.
Proverbs 10:6 The Lord's blessing is upon a righteous one's head, but untimely mourning will cover the mouth of the ungodly.
Proverbs 10:7 The memory of the righteous is with praises, but an ungodly one's name is extinguished.
Proverbs 10:8 One wise in heart will receive commandments, but one unrestrained in lips, speaking crookedly, will be tripped.
Proverbs 10:9 He who walks simply walks confidently, but he who perverts his ways will be known.
Proverbs 10:10 He who winks with eyes with deceit gathers griefs for men, but he who reproves with frankness makes peace.
Proverbs 10:11 A spring of life is in a righteous one's hand, but destruction will cover an ungodly one's mouth.
Proverbs 10:12 Hatred raises strife, but friendship covers all who are not contentious.
Proverbs 10:13 He who brings forth wisdom from lips strikes a man without heart with a rod.
Proverbs 10:14 The wise will hide perception, but a rash one's mouth draws near to shattering.
Proverbs 10:15 The possession of the rich is a fortified city, but poverty is the shattering of the ungodly.
Proverbs 10:16 Works of the righteous produce life, but fruits of the ungodly sins.
Proverbs 10:17 Discipline guards righteous ways of life, but discipline without reproof goes astray.
Proverbs 10:18 Righteous lips cover enmity, but those who bring forth abuse are most foolish.
Proverbs 10:19 From much speaking you will not escape sin, but sparing your lips, you will be understanding.
Proverbs 10:20 A righteous one's tongue is fire-tested silver, but an ungodly one's heart will fail.
Proverbs 10:21 Lips of the righteous know lofty things, but the foolish die in need.
Proverbs 10:22 The Lord's blessing is upon a righteous one's head; this makes rich, and grief in the heart will certainly not be added to it.
Proverbs 10:23 A foolish one does evils in laughter, but wisdom gives birth to prudence for a man.
Proverbs 10:24 An ungodly one is carried about in destruction, but a righteous one's desire is accepted.
Proverbs 10:25 When a storm passes by, an ungodly one vanishes, but a righteous one, turning aside, is saved unto the age.
Proverbs 10:26 As an unripe grape is harmful to teeth and smoke to eyes, so is lawlessness to those who use it.
Proverbs 10:27 Fear of the Lord adds days, but years of the ungodly will be diminished.
Proverbs 10:28 Gladness lingers for the righteous, but hope of the ungodly perishes.
Proverbs 10:29 Fear of the Lord is a holy one's stronghold, but shattering for those who work evils.
Proverbs 10:30 A righteous one will not give way unto the age, but the ungodly will not inhabit earth.
Proverbs 10:31 A righteous one's mouth drips wisdom, but an unjust one's tongue will be destroyed.
Proverbs 10:32 Lips of righteous men drip graces, but the mouth of the ungodly turns away.

## Chapter 11

Proverbs 11:1 Deceitful scales are an abomination before the Lord, but a just weight is accepted by him.
Proverbs 11:2 Wherever insolence enters, there also is dishonor; but the mouth of the humble meditates wisdom.
Proverbs 11:3 A righteous one who died left regret, but destruction of the ungodly becomes ready and a cause of rejoicing.
Proverbs 11:5 Righteousness cuts blameless ways straight, but ungodliness falls into injustice.
Proverbs 11:6 Righteousness of upright men delivers them, but lawless ones are caught in their destruction.
Proverbs 11:7 When a righteous man dies, hope does not perish, but the boast of the ungodly perishes.
Proverbs 11:8 A righteous one escapes from a hunt, but the ungodly one is handed over in his place.
Proverbs 11:9 In the mouth of the ungodly is a snare for citizens, but perception of the righteous has a good way.
Proverbs 11:10 By good things of the righteous a city prospered,
Proverbs 11:11 but by mouths of the ungodly it was razed.
Proverbs 11:12 One lacking sense sneers at citizens, but a prudent man keeps quiet.
Proverbs 11:13 A double-tongued man reveals counsels in a council, but one faithful in breath hides matters.
Proverbs 11:14 Those who have no guidance fall like leaves, but salvation exists in much counsel.
Proverbs 11:15 An evil one does evil when he mingles with a righteous one, and hates the sound of security.
Proverbs 11:16 A gracious woman raises glory for a husband, but a woman who hates righteous things is a throne of dishonor. Sluggards come to lack riches, but the valiant are supported by riches.
Proverbs 11:17 A merciful man does good to his soul, but the merciless destroys his body.
Proverbs 11:18 An ungodly one does unjust works, but the seed of the righteous is a reward of truth.
Proverbs 11:19 A righteous son is born for life, but pursuit of an ungodly one is for death.
Proverbs 11:20 Perverted ways are an abomination to the Lord, but all blameless in their ways are acceptable to him.
Proverbs 11:21 He who puts hands into a hand unjustly will not be unpunished, but he who sows righteousness will receive a faithful reward.
Proverbs 11:22 As an earring in a pig's nose, so is beauty to an evil-minded woman.
Proverbs 11:23 Every desire of the righteous is good, but hope of the ungodly will perish.
Proverbs 11:24 There are those who sow their own things and make more, and there are also those who gather and are diminished.
Proverbs 11:25 Every blessed soul is simple, but an angry man is not seemly.
Proverbs 11:26 May he who holds grain back leave it to the nations, but blessing is upon the head of him who shares.
Proverbs 11:27 He who devises good things seeks good grace; but him who seeks out evils, they will overtake.
Proverbs 11:28 He who trusts in riches will fall, but he who takes hold of righteous ones will spring up.
Proverbs 11:29 He who does not go along with his own house will inherit wind, and a foolish one will serve a prudent one.
Proverbs 11:30 From the fruit of righteousness grows a tree of life, but souls of lawless ones are taken away untimely.
Proverbs 11:31 If the righteous one is scarcely saved, where will the ungodly and sinful one appear?

## Chapter 12

Proverbs 12:1 He who loves discipline loves perception, but he who hates reproofs is foolish.
Proverbs 12:2 Better is he who found grace with the Lord, but a lawless man will be passed over in silence.
Proverbs 12:3 A human will not prosper from a lawless thing, but roots of the righteous will not be uprooted.
Proverbs 12:4 A valiant woman is a crown for her husband; but as a worm in wood, so an evildoing woman destroys a man.
Proverbs 12:5 Reasonings of the righteous are judgments, but the ungodly steer deceits.
Proverbs 12:6 Words of the ungodly are deceitful, but the mouth of the upright will deliver them.
Proverbs 12:7 Wherever he turns, an ungodly one vanishes, but houses of the righteous remain.
Proverbs 12:8 An understanding one's mouth is praised by a man, but the dull-hearted is sneered at.
Proverbs 12:9 Better is a man in dishonor serving himself than one putting honor around himself and needing bread.
Proverbs 12:10 A righteous one has compassion on souls of his beasts, but the bowels of the ungodly are merciless.
Proverbs 12:11 He who works his own land will be filled with bread, but those pursuing vain things lack sense.
Proverbs 12:11 a He who is pleased in pastimes of wine will leave dishonor in his own strongholds.
Proverbs 12:12 Desires of the ungodly are evil, but roots of the reverent are in strongholds.
Proverbs 12:13 Through sin of lips a sinner falls into snares, but a righteous one escapes from them.
Proverbs 12:13 a He who looks at smooth things will be shown mercy, but he who meets at gates will oppress souls.
Proverbs 12:14 From fruits of a mouth a man's soul will be filled with good things, and repayment of his lips will be given to him.
Proverbs 12:15 Ways of foolish ones are straight before them, but a wise one hears counsel.
Proverbs 12:16 A foolish one announces his wrath on the same day, but a shrewd one hides his own dishonor.
Proverbs 12:17 A righteous one announces displayed faithfulness, but the witness of unjust ones is deceitful.
Proverbs 12:18 There are those who, speaking, wound with a sword, but tongues of the wise heal.
Proverbs 12:19 True lips set testimony right, but a hasty witness has an unjust tongue.
Proverbs 12:20 Deceit is in the heart of one devising evils, but those wishing peace will rejoice.
Proverbs 12:21 Nothing unjust will please a righteous one, but the ungodly will be filled with evils.
Proverbs 12:22 Lying lips are an abomination to the Lord, but he who practices faithfulness is accepted by him.
Proverbs 12:23 An understanding man is a throne of perception, but the heart of foolish ones will meet curses.
Proverbs 12:24 The hand of chosen ones will rule easily, but deceitful ones will be for plunder.
Proverbs 12:25 A fearful word troubles a righteous man's heart, but a good announcement gladdens him.
Proverbs 12:26 A discerning righteous one will be his own friend, but judgments of the ungodly are ungentle. Evils will pursue those who sin, and the way of the ungodly will lead them astray.
Proverbs 12:27 A deceitful one will not attain prey, but a pure man is a precious possession.
Proverbs 12:28 In ways of righteousness is life, but ways of those bearing grudges lead to death.

## Chapter 13

Proverbs 13:1 A shrewd son is obedient to a father, but a disobedient son is in destruction.
Proverbs 13:2 A good one will eat from fruits of righteousness, but souls of lawless ones will perish untimely.
Proverbs 13:3 He who guards his own mouth keeps his own soul, but one rash in lips will terrify himself.
Proverbs 13:4 Every idle one is in desires, but hands of the valiant are in diligence.
Proverbs 13:5 A righteous one hates an unjust word, but an ungodly one is ashamed and will have no frankness.
Proverbs 13:6 Righteousness guards the innocent, but sin makes the ungodly worthless.
Proverbs 13:7 There are those who make themselves rich, having nothing, and those who humble themselves amid much wealth.
Proverbs 13:8 A man's own wealth is the ransom of his soul, but a poor one does not endure a threat.
Proverbs 13:9 Light is for the righteous continually, but the light of the ungodly is extinguished.
Proverbs 13:9 a Deceitful souls wander in sins, but the righteous have compassion and show mercy.
Proverbs 13:10 An evil one does evils with insolence, but those discerning themselves are wise.
Proverbs 13:11 Substance hastily sought with lawlessness becomes less, but he who gathers for himself with reverence will be multiplied; a righteous one has compassion and lends.
Proverbs 13:12 Better is one who begins helping with heart than one who promises and leads into hope; for a good desire is a tree of life.
Proverbs 13:13 He who despises a matter will be despised by it, but he who fears a commandment is healthy.
Proverbs 13:13 a Nothing good will be for a deceitful son, but a wise household servant's deeds will prosper, and his way will be directed.
Proverbs 13:14 A wise one's law is a spring of life, but the senseless will die by a snare.
Proverbs 13:15 Good understanding gives grace, and knowing law belongs to good thought, but ways of despisers are in destruction.
Proverbs 13:16 Every shrewd one acts with knowledge, but a foolish one spread out his own evil.
Proverbs 13:17 A bold king will fall into evils, but a faithful messenger will deliver him.
Proverbs 13:18 Discipline takes away poverty and dishonor, but he who guards reproofs will be glorified.
Proverbs 13:19 Desires of the reverent sweeten a soul, but works of the ungodly are far from knowledge.
Proverbs 13:20 He who walks with wise ones will be wise, but he who walks with foolish ones will be known.
Proverbs 13:21 Evils will pursue sinners, but good things will overtake the righteous.
Proverbs 13:22 A good man will inherit sons of sons, but wealth of the ungodly is stored up for the righteous.
Proverbs 13:23 The righteous will spend many years in wealth, but the unjust will perish swiftly.
Proverbs 13:24 He who spares the staff hates his son, but he who loves disciplines diligently.
Proverbs 13:25 A righteous one, eating, fills his soul, but souls of the ungodly are needy.

## Chapter 14

Proverbs 14:1 Wise women built houses, but the foolish woman razed them with her hands.
Proverbs 14:2 He who walks rightly fears the Lord, but he who is crooked in his ways will be dishonored.
Proverbs 14:3 From the mouth of foolish ones comes a staff of insolence, but lips of the wise guard them.
Proverbs 14:4 Where there are no oxen, mangers are clean; but where there is much produce, an ox's strength is evident.
Proverbs 14:5 A faithful witness does not lie, but an unjust witness kindles lies.
Proverbs 14:6 You will seek wisdom among evil ones and not find it, but perception is easy among the prudent.
Proverbs 14:7 All things are contrary to a foolish man, but wise lips are weapons of perception.
Proverbs 14:8 Wisdom of the shrewd will recognize their ways, but folly of foolish ones is in wandering.
Proverbs 14:9 Houses of lawless ones will owe cleansing, but houses of the righteous are accepted.
Proverbs 14:10 A man's heart is perceptive, his soul sorrowful; but when he rejoices, he does not mingle with insolence.
Proverbs 14:11 Houses of the ungodly will vanish, but tents of those acting rightly will stand.
Proverbs 14:12 There is a way which seems straight among humans, but its ends come to the bottom of Hades.
Proverbs 14:13 Grief does not mingle with gladnesses, but final joy comes to mourning.
Proverbs 14:14 The bold-hearted will be filled with his own ways, and a good man from his thoughts.
Proverbs 14:15 An innocent one believes every word, but a shrewd one comes to repentance.
Proverbs 14:16 A wise one, fearing, turned aside from evil, but a foolish one, trusting himself, mingles with a lawless one.
Proverbs 14:17 A quick-tempered one acts without counsel, but a prudent man bears many things.
Proverbs 14:18 Foolish ones will apportion evil, but the shrewd will take hold of perception.
Proverbs 14:19 Evil ones will slip before good ones, and the ungodly will attend at doors of the righteous.
Proverbs 14:20 Friends will hate poor friends, but friends of the rich are many.
Proverbs 14:21 He who dishonors needy ones sins, but he who shows mercy to the poor is blessed.
Proverbs 14:22 Those wandering devise evils, but good ones devise mercy and truth. Makers of evils do not know mercy and faithfulness, but mercies and faithfulnesses are with good makers.
Proverbs 14:23 In everyone taking care there is abundance, but the pleasure-loving and insensible will be in need.
Proverbs 14:24 A shrewd one is a crown of the wise, but the pastime of foolish ones is evil.
Proverbs 14:25 A faithful witness will deliver a soul from evils, but a deceitful one kindles lies.
Proverbs 14:26 In fear of the Lord is hope of strength, and for his children he leaves support.
Proverbs 14:27 A command of the Lord is a spring of life, and makes one turn aside from a snare of death.
Proverbs 14:28 In a numerous nation is a king's glory, but in a people's failing is a ruler's shattering.
Proverbs 14:29 A long-suffering man is abundant in prudence, but the faint-hearted is exceedingly foolish.
Proverbs 14:30 A mild-tempered man is a physician of hearts, but a perceptive heart is a moth of bones.
Proverbs 14:31 He who oppresses a needy one provokes him who made him, but he who honors him shows mercy to a poor one.
Proverbs 14:32 In his evil an ungodly one will be thrust away, but he who trusts in his own holiness is righteous.
Proverbs 14:33 Wisdom is in a man's good heart, but in a heart of foolish ones it is not discerned.
Proverbs 14:34 Righteousness exalts a nation, but sins diminish tribes.
Proverbs 14:35 An understanding attendant is accepted by a king, and through his own adaptability takes away dishonor.

## Chapter 15

Proverbs 15:1 Wrath destroys even prudent ones, but a submissive answer turns away anger, and a grievous word raises wraths.
Proverbs 15:2 A tongue of wise ones knows good things, but a mouth of foolish ones will announce evils.
Proverbs 15:3 The Lord's eyes are in every place; they observe both evil and good ones.
Proverbs 15:4 Healing of a tongue is a tree of life, and he who preserves it will be filled with spirit.
Proverbs 15:5 A foolish one sneers at a father's discipline, but he who guards commandments is shrewder.
Proverbs 15:6 In abundant righteousness is much strength, but the ungodly will perish from earth, roots and all. In houses of the righteous is much strength, but fruits of the ungodly will perish.
Proverbs 15:7 Lips of the wise are bound to perception, but hearts of foolish ones are not secure.
Proverbs 15:8 Sacrifices of the ungodly are an abomination to the Lord, but prayers of those directing rightly are accepted by him.
Proverbs 15:9 Ways of an ungodly one are an abomination to the Lord, but he loves those pursuing righteousness.
Proverbs 15:10 An innocent one's discipline is recognized by those passing by, but those who hate reproofs die shamefully.
Proverbs 15:11 Hades and destruction are evident with the Lord; how not also hearts of humans?
Proverbs 15:12 An undisciplined one will not love those who reprove him, and will not converse with wise ones.
Proverbs 15:13 When a heart rejoices, a face flourishes, but when it is in griefs, it grows gloomy.
Proverbs 15:14 An upright heart seeks perception, but a mouth of the undisciplined will know evils.
Proverbs 15:15 All the time the eyes of evil ones await evils, but good ones rest continually.
Proverbs 15:16 Better is a small portion with fear of the Lord than great treasures with fearlessness.
Proverbs 15:17 Better is hospitality of vegetables with friendship and grace than a serving of calves with enmity.
Proverbs 15:18 An angry man prepares battles, but a long-suffering one calms even a coming one.
Proverbs 15:18 a A long-suffering man will extinguish disputes, but the ungodly one raises them more.
Proverbs 15:19 Ways of the idle are strewn with thorns, but those of the valiant are worn smooth.
Proverbs 15:20 A wise son gladdens a father, but a foolish son sneers at his mother.
Proverbs 15:21 Paths of a senseless one lack sense, but a prudent man walks directing rightly.
Proverbs 15:22 Those who do not honor councils postpone reasonings, but counsel remains in hearts of those deliberating.
Proverbs 15:23 The evil one will certainly not obey it, nor say anything timely and good for the community.
Proverbs 15:24 An understanding one's thoughts are ways of life, so that, turning aside from Hades, he may be saved.
Proverbs 15:25 The Lord tears down houses of insolent ones, but he established a widow's boundary.
Proverbs 15:26 An unjust reasoning is an abomination to the Lord, but utterances of the pure are noble.
Proverbs 15:27 The bribe-taker destroys himself, but he who hates taking gifts is saved.
Proverbs 15:27 a By mercies and faithfulnesses sins are cleansed away, and by fear of the Lord everyone turns aside from evil.
Proverbs 15:28 Hearts of the righteous meditate faithfulnesses, but a mouth of the ungodly answers evils.
Proverbs 15:28 a Ways of righteous humans are accepted by the Lord, and through them even enemies become friends.
Proverbs 15:29 God is far distant from the ungodly, but he hears prayers of the righteous.
Proverbs 15:29 a Better is a little receipt with righteousness than much produce with injustice.
Proverbs 15:30 Let a man's heart reason righteous things, so that his steps may be set right by God. An eye observing good things gladdens a heart, and a good report fattens bones.
Proverbs 15:32 He who thrusts discipline away hates himself, but he who keeps reproofs loves his soul.
Proverbs 15:33 Fear of God is discipline and wisdom, and a beginning of glory will answer her.

## Chapter 16

Proverbs 16:2 2 All the works of the humble are manifest before God, but the ungodly will perish on an evil day.
Proverbs 16:5 Every high-hearted person is unclean before God, and one who has unjustly put hands into a hand will not be acquitted.
Proverbs 16:7 The beginning of a good way is to do righteous things, and they are more acceptable before God than sacrificing sacrifices.
Proverbs 16:8 The one seeking the Lord will find knowledge with righteousness, and those rightly seeking him will find peace.
Proverbs 16:9 All the works of the Lord are with righteousness, but the ungodly is kept for an evil day.
Proverbs 16:10 An oracle is on a king's lips, and in judgment his mouth will certainly not go astray.
Proverbs 16:11 The balance's inclination is righteousness with the Lord, and his works are righteous weights.
Proverbs 16:12 The one doing evil things is an abomination to a king, for a throne of rule is prepared with righteousness.
Proverbs 16:13 Righteous lips are acceptable to a king, and he loves upright words.
Proverbs 16:14 A king's wrath is a messenger of death, but a wise man will appease him.
Proverbs 16:15 In the light of life is a king's son, and those acceptable to him are like a late cloud.
Proverbs 16:16 Nests of wisdom are more desirable than gold, and nests of prudence are more desirable than silver.
Proverbs 16:17 Paths of life turn away from evil things, and ways of righteousness are length of life. The one receiving discipline will be amid good things, and the one keeping reproofs will be made wise. Whoever keeps his own ways preserves his own soul; and loving his life, he will spare his mouth.
Proverbs 16:18 Arrogance leads before shattering, and evil-mindedness before a fall.
Proverbs 16:19 Better is a gentle-tempered person with humility than one who divides spoils with arrogant people.
Proverbs 16:20 One understanding in matters is a finder of good things, and one trusting in God is blessed.
Proverbs 16:21 They call the wise and understanding worthless, but those sweet in speech will hear more.
Proverbs 16:22 Thought is a spring of life to those possessing it, but the discipline of senseless people is evil.
Proverbs 16:23 A wise person's heart will understand the things from his own mouth, and on his lips he will carry discernment.
Proverbs 16:24 Good words are honeycombs, and their sweetness is healing of a soul.
Proverbs 16:25 There are ways seeming to be upright to a man, yet their last things look toward the bottom of Hades.
Proverbs 16:26 A man in labors labors for himself and forces his own destruction, yet the crooked person carries destruction on his own mouth.
Proverbs 16:27 A senseless man digs evil things for himself, and on his own lips he stores up fire.
Proverbs 16:28 A crooked man sends evil things abroad and lights a torch of deceit for evil people and separates friends.
Proverbs 16:29 A lawless man tries friends and leads them away along ways that are not good.
Proverbs 16:30 Fixing his eyes, he reckons perverted things, and with his lips he determines all evil things; this person is a furnace of wickedness.
Proverbs 16:31 Old age is a crown of boasting, and it is found in ways of righteousness.
Proverbs 16:32 A long-tempered man is better than a strong one, and the one controlling anger is better than one taking a city.
Proverbs 16:33 Everything comes into the bosoms of the unjust, but all righteous things are from the Lord.

## Chapter 17

Proverbs 17:1 Better is a morsel with pleasure in peace than a house full of many good things and unjust sacrifices with fighting.
Proverbs 17:2 An intelligent servant will rule senseless masters, and among brothers he will divide shares.
Proverbs 17:3 Just as silver and gold are tested in a furnace, so hearts are chosen before the Lord.
Proverbs 17:4 An evil person listens to the tongue of lawless people, but a righteous person does not attend to lying lips.
Proverbs 17:5 The one laughing at a poor person provokes the one who made him, and the one rejoicing over someone being destroyed will not be acquitted; but the one having compassion will receive mercy.
Proverbs 17:6 Children's children are a crown of old people, and their fathers are the boast of children.
Proverbs 17:6 a The whole world of possessions belongs to the faithful person, but not even an obol to the unfaithful.
Proverbs 17:7 Faithful lips will not suit a senseless person, nor lying lips a righteous person.
Proverbs 17:8 Discipline is a reward of graces to those using it, and wherever it turns, it will prosper.
Proverbs 17:9 Whoever hides wrongdoings seeks friendship; but whoever hates hiding them separates friends and kin.
Proverbs 17:10 A threat shatters a prudent person's heart, but a senseless person, having been whipped, does not perceive.
Proverbs 17:11 Every evil person raises disputes, but the Lord will send out a merciless messenger to him.
Proverbs 17:12 Anxiety will fall upon an intelligent man, but the senseless will reason about evil things.
Proverbs 17:13 Whoever repays evil things for good things, evil things will not be moved from his house.
Proverbs 17:14 The beginning of righteousness gives authority to words, but dissension and fighting precede want.
Proverbs 17:15 Whoever judges the unjust person righteous, but the righteous person unjust, is unclean and abominable before God.
Proverbs 17:16 Why did possessions belong to a senseless person? For one without a heart will not be able to acquire wisdom.
Proverbs 17:16 a Whoever makes his own house high seeks shattering; but the one turning crookedly away from learning will fall into evil things.
Proverbs 17:17 Let a friend belong to you at every time, and let brothers be useful in necessities; for this reason they are born.
Proverbs 17:18 A senseless man claps and rejoices over himself, as also the one guaranteeing his own friend with a guarantee.
Proverbs 17:19 A lover of sin rejoices in fights,
Proverbs 17:20 but the hard-hearted person does not encounter good things. A man changeable in tongue will fall into evil things,
Proverbs 17:21 and a senseless person's heart is pain to the one possessing it. A father is not gladdened over an undisciplined son, but a prudent son gladdens his mother.
Proverbs 17:22 A gladdened heart makes one be in good condition, but a sorrowful man's bones are dried up.
Proverbs 17:23 The ways of one unjustly receiving gifts in his bosom do not prosper, and an ungodly person turns aside ways of righteousness.
Proverbs 17:24 An understanding face belongs to a wise man, but the senseless person's eyes are at the ends of the earth.
Proverbs 17:25 A senseless son is anger to a father and pain to her who bore him.
Proverbs 17:26 To punish a righteous man is not good, nor is it holy to plot against righteous rulers.
Proverbs 17:27 Whoever refrains from uttering a harsh word is discerning; and a long-tempered man is prudent.
Proverbs 17:28 To an unintelligent person who has asked about wisdom, it will be reckoned as wisdom, and someone who has made himself mute will seem to be prudent.

## Chapter 18

Proverbs 18:1 A man wishing to separate himself from friends seeks pretexts, and at every time he will be reproached.
Proverbs 18:2 One lacking sense has no need of wisdom; for he is rather led by senselessness.
Proverbs 18:3 When an ungodly person comes into a depth of evil things, he despises, and dishonor and reproach come upon him.
Proverbs 18:4 A word in a man's heart is deep water, and a river and a spring of life well up.
Proverbs 18:5 To admire an ungodly person's face is not good, nor is it holy to turn aside what is just in judgment.
Proverbs 18:6 A senseless person's lips lead him into evil things, and his rash mouth calls upon death.
Proverbs 18:7 A senseless person's mouth is shattering to him, and his lips are a trap to his soul.
Proverbs 18:8 Fear casts down the slothful, and the souls of effeminate men will hunger.
Proverbs 18:9 The one not healing himself in his works is brother to the one ruining himself.
Proverbs 18:10 The Lord's name is from greatness of strength, and righteous people, having run to it, are exalted.
Proverbs 18:11 A rich man's possessions are a fortified city, and its glory greatly overshadows.
Proverbs 18:12 Before shattering a man's heart is exalted, and before glory it is humbled.
Proverbs 18:13 Whoever answers a word before hearing, it is senselessness and reproach to him.
Proverbs 18:14 A prudent attendant soothes a man's temper; but who will bear a faint-hearted man?
Proverbs 18:15 A prudent person's heart acquires perception, and wise people's ears seek thought.
Proverbs 18:16 A person's gift makes room for him and seats him beside rulers.
