Proverbs 18:17 A righteous person is his own accuser in his first speech; but when the opponent comes against him, he is reproved.
Proverbs 18:18 A lot stops disputes, and among rulers it determines.
Proverbs 18:19 A brother helped by a brother is like a fortified and high city, and he is strong like a founded palace.
Proverbs 18:20 From fruits of a mouth a man fills his belly, and from fruits of his lips he will be filled.
Proverbs 18:21 Death and life are in the hand of a tongue, and those controlling it will eat its fruits.
Proverbs 18:22 Whoever found a good wife found graces, and received cheerfulness from God.
Proverbs 18:22 a Whoever casts out a good wife casts out good things; but the one retaining an adulteress is senseless and ungodly.

## Chapter 19

Proverbs 19:3 3 A man's senselessness ruins his ways, but he blames God in his heart.
Proverbs 19:4 Wealth adds many friends, but the poor person is left even by his existing friend.
Proverbs 19:5 A false witness will not be unpunished, and the one accusing unjustly will not escape.
Proverbs 19:6 Many attend upon kings' faces, but every evil person becomes a reproach to a man.
Proverbs 19:7 Everyone who hates a poor brother will also be far from friendship. Good thought will draw near to those knowing it, and a prudent man will find it. The one doing many evil things brings wickedness to completion; but whoever provokes words will not be saved.
Proverbs 19:8 The one acquiring prudence loves himself; but whoever keeps prudence will find good things.
Proverbs 19:9 A false witness will not be unpunished; but whoever kindles wickedness will be destroyed by it.
Proverbs 19:10 Luxury does not benefit a senseless person, nor if a servant begins to exercise power with arrogance.
Proverbs 19:11 A merciful man is long-tempered, and his boast comes upon lawless people.
Proverbs 19:12 A king's threat is like a lion's growling; but as dew on grass, so is his cheerfulness.
Proverbs 19:13 A senseless son is shame to a father, and vows from a courtesan's hire are not pure.
Proverbs 19:14 Fathers apportion a house and possessions to children, but a wife is joined to a man by God.
Proverbs 19:15 Cowardice holds an effeminate man, and an idle person's soul will hunger.
Proverbs 19:16 Whoever keeps a commandment preserves his own soul; but the one despising his own ways will perish.
Proverbs 19:17 The one showing mercy to a poor person lends to God, and according to his gift he will repay him.
Proverbs 19:18 Discipline your son, for thus he will be hopeful; but do not be lifted up toward arrogance in your soul.
Proverbs 19:19 An evil-minded man will suffer many penalties; but if he acts pestilently, he will also add his soul.
Proverbs 19:20 Hear, son, your father's discipline, so that you may become wise at your last things.
Proverbs 19:21 Many reasonings are in a man's heart, but the Lord's counsel remains forever.
Proverbs 19:22 Mercifulness is fruit for a man, and a righteous poor person is better than a rich liar.
Proverbs 19:23 Fear of the Lord is for life to a man, but the fearless person will lodge in places where knowledge is not visited.
Proverbs 19:24 The one unjustly hiding hands in his bosom will certainly not even bring them to his mouth.
Proverbs 19:25 When a pestilent person is whipped, a senseless person becomes shrewder; but if you reprove a prudent man, he will understand perception.
Proverbs 19:26 The one dishonoring a father and thrusting away his mother will be put to shame and will be reproached.
Proverbs 19:27 A son neglecting to keep a father's discipline will practice evil utterances.
Proverbs 19:28 The one guaranteeing a senseless child insults a righteous requirement, and the mouth of ungodly people swallows judgments.
Proverbs 19:29 Whips are prepared for the undisciplined, and punishments for the shoulders of senseless people.

## Chapter 20

Proverbs 20:1 Wine is undisciplined and drunkenness arrogant, and everyone mingling with it will not be wise.
Proverbs 20:2 A king's threat does not differ from a lion's wrath, and the one provoking him sins against his own soul.
Proverbs 20:3 It is glory for a man to turn away from insults, but every senseless person becomes entangled in such things.
Proverbs 20:4 A slothful person being reproached is not ashamed, likewise also the one borrowing grain at harvest.
Proverbs 20:5 Counsel in a man's heart is deep water, but a prudent man will draw it out.
Proverbs 20:6 A person is a great thing, and a merciful man a precious thing, but to find a faithful man is a task.
Proverbs 20:7 Whoever conducts himself blameless in righteousness will leave his children blessed.
Proverbs 20:8 When a righteous king sits on a throne, every evil thing does not oppose him before his eyes.
Proverbs 20:9 Who will boast of having a pure heart? Or who will speak frankly of being clean from sins?
Proverbs 20:9 a The lamp of one speaking evil of a father or mother will be extinguished, and the pupils of his eyes will see darkness.
Proverbs 20:10 A portion eagerly pursued at the first will not be blessed at the last.
Proverbs 20:11 Do not say, I will punish the enemy; but wait for the Lord, so that he may help you.
Proverbs 20:10 A great and a small weight and double measures, both are unclean before the Lord.
Proverbs 20:11 And the one doing them will be fettered in his practices, a young man with a holy person, and his way is straight.
Proverbs 20:12 An ear hears and an eye sees; both are works of the Lord.
Proverbs 20:13 Do not love speaking against others, so that you may not be removed; open your eyes and be filled with breads.
Proverbs 20:23 A double weight is an abomination to the Lord, and a deceitful balance is not good before him.
Proverbs 20:24 A man's steps are directed by the Lord; but how could a mortal understand his ways?
Proverbs 20:25 It is a trap for a man hastily to consecrate something of his own; for after making a vow, repenting happens.
Proverbs 20:26 A wise king is a winnower of ungodly people, and he will bring a wheel upon them.
Proverbs 20:27 The breath of humans is a light of the Lord, who searches chambers of a belly.
Proverbs 20:28 Mercifulness and truth are a guard for a king, and they will surround his throne in righteousness.
Proverbs 20:29 Wisdom is an ornament to young men, and gray hairs the glory of elders.
Proverbs 20:30 Bruises and fractures encounter evil people, and blows reach chambers of a belly.

## Chapter 21

Proverbs 21:1 As a rush of water, so a king's heart is in God's hand; wherever, willing, he nods, there he inclined it.
Proverbs 21:2 Every man appears righteous to himself, but the Lord directs hearts.
Proverbs 21:3 To do righteous things and speak truth are more pleasing before God than blood of sacrifices.
Proverbs 21:4 A lofty-minded person is bold-hearted toward arrogance, and the lamp of ungodly people is sin.
Proverbs 21:6 The one producing treasures with a lying tongue pursues vain things toward traps of death.
Proverbs 21:7 Destruction will lodge with ungodly people; for they do not wish to practice righteous things.
Proverbs 21:8 God sends crooked ways toward the crooked; for his works are pure and upright.
Proverbs 21:9 It is better to dwell on a corner in the open air than in plastered places with injustice and in a shared house.
Proverbs 21:10 An ungodly person's soul will receive mercy from none of the humans.
Proverbs 21:11 When an undisciplined person is punished, the innocent person becomes shrewder, and a wise person, understanding, will receive knowledge.
Proverbs 21:12 A righteous person understands the hearts of ungodly people and despises ungodly people amid evil things.
Proverbs 21:13 Whoever blocks his ears so as not to hear a weak person, he himself too will call, and there will be no one listening.
Proverbs 21:14 A secret gift overturns angers, but the one sparing gifts raises strong wrath.
Proverbs 21:15 It is the gladness of righteous people to execute judgment, but a holy person is unclean before evildoers.
Proverbs 21:16 A man wandering from a way of righteousness will rest in an assembly of giants.
Proverbs 21:17 A needy man loves gladness, loving wine and oil for wealth;
Proverbs 21:18 and a lawless person is a cleansing-offering for a righteous person.
Proverbs 21:19 It is better to dwell in a desert land than with a quarrelsome and talkative and irascible woman.
Proverbs 21:20 A desirable treasure will rest on a wise person's mouth, but senseless men swallow it.
Proverbs 21:21 A way of righteousness and mercifulness will find life and glory.
Proverbs 21:22 A wise person climbed fortified cities and pulled down the stronghold in which ungodly people had trusted.
Proverbs 21:23 Whoever guards his mouth and tongue preserves his soul from affliction.
Proverbs 21:24 A rash and self-willed and boastful person is called pestilent; but whoever bears a grudge is lawless.
Proverbs 21:25 Desires kill a slothful person; for his hands do not choose to do anything.
Proverbs 21:26 An ungodly person desires evil desires the whole day, but the righteous person shows mercy and compassion unsparingly.
Proverbs 21:27 Sacrifices of ungodly people are an abomination to the Lord; for they also offer them lawlessly.
Proverbs 21:28 A false witness will perish, but an obedient man, being guarded, will speak.
Proverbs 21:29 An ungodly man stands shamelessly with his face, but the upright person himself understands his ways.
Proverbs 21:30 There is no wisdom, there is no courage, there is no counsel against the ungodly person.
Proverbs 21:31 A horse is prepared for a day of war, but help is from the Lord.

## Chapter 22

Proverbs 22:1 A good name is more desirable than much wealth, and good grace above silver and gold.
Proverbs 22:2 A rich person and a poor person met one another, and the Lord made both.
Proverbs 22:3 A shrewd person, seeing an evil person being severely punished, is himself disciplined, but the senseless passed by and were punished.
Proverbs 22:4 The offspring of wisdom are fear of the Lord and wealth and glory and life.
Proverbs 22:5 Thistles and traps are in crooked ways, but the one guarding his own soul will abstain from them.
Proverbs 22:7 Rich people will rule poor people, and servants will lend to their own masters.
Proverbs 22:8 The one sowing worthless things will reap evil things, and he will bring to completion the blow of his works.
Proverbs 22:8 a God blesses a cheerful man and giver, and he will bring to completion the vanity of his works.
Proverbs 22:9 The one showing mercy to a poor person will himself be nourished; for he gave of his own breads to the poor person.
Proverbs 22:9 a The one giving gifts obtains victory and honor, yet he takes away the soul of those possessing them.
Proverbs 22:10 Cast a pestilent person out of a council, and strife will go out together with him; for whenever he sits in a council, he dishonors everyone.
Proverbs 22:11 The Lord loves holy hearts, and all blameless people are acceptable to him; a king shepherds with lips.
Proverbs 22:12 And the Lord's eyes preserve perception, but a lawless person despises words.
Proverbs 22:13 A slothful person makes excuses and says, A lion is in the ways, and murderers in the broad streets.
Proverbs 22:14 A lawless person's mouth is a deep pit, and the one hated by the Lord will fall into it.
Proverbs 22:14 a Evil ways are before a man, and he does not love turning away from them; but one must turn away from a crooked and evil way.
Proverbs 22:15 Unintelligence is attached to a young person's heart, but a rod and discipline are far from him.
Proverbs 22:16 The one extorting from a needy person makes his own things many; but he gives to a rich person for less. – –
Proverbs 22:17 Bring your ear alongside wise people's words and hear my word, and apply your heart, so that you may know that they are good;
Proverbs 22:18 and if you put them into your heart, they will gladden you together on your lips,
Proverbs 22:19 so that your hope may be upon the Lord and he may make his way known to you.
Proverbs 22:20 And you too copy them for yourself threefold for counsel and knowledge upon the breadth of your heart.
Proverbs 22:21 I therefore teach you a true word and good knowledge to heed, to answer words of truth to those putting questions to you.
Proverbs 22:22 Do not oppress a needy person, for he is poor, and do not dishonor a weak person in gates;
Proverbs 22:23 for the Lord will judge his case, and you will deliver your soul safe from seizure.
Proverbs 22:24 Do not be a companion to a wrathful man, and do not lodge together with an irascible friend,
Proverbs 22:25 lest you learn his ways and take snares for your soul.
Proverbs 22:26 Do not give yourself as a guarantee out of shame before a face;
Proverbs 22:27 for if you have nothing from which to repay, they will take the bedding beneath your sides.
Proverbs 22:28 Do not move everlasting boundaries which your fathers set.
Proverbs 22:29 A perceptive man and keen in his works must stand before kings and not stand before sluggish men.

## Chapter 23

Proverbs 23:1 If you sit to dine at a table of rulers, understand intelligently the things set before you
Proverbs 23:2 and put forth your hand, knowing that you must prepare such things;
Proverbs 23:3 but if you are more insatiable, do not desire his dishes, for these belong to a false life.
Proverbs 23:4 Do not stretch yourself alongside a rich person, being needy, but abstain in your thought;
Proverbs 23:5 if you fix your eye toward him, he will appear nowhere, for wings like an eagle's have been prepared for him, and he returns to the house of the one presiding over him.
Proverbs 23:6 Do not dine together with an envious man, nor desire his foods;
Proverbs 23:7 for in the way that someone might swallow a hair, so he eats and drinks.
Proverbs 23:8 Nor bring him in to you and eat your morsel with him; for he will vomit it out and ruin your good words.
Proverbs 23:9 Say nothing into a senseless person's ears, lest he sneer at your understanding words.
Proverbs 23:10 Do not shift everlasting boundaries, and do not enter into orphans' property;
Proverbs 23:11 for the Lord redeeming them is mighty and will judge their case with you.
Proverbs 23:12 Give your heart to discipline, and prepare your ears for words of perception.
Proverbs 23:13 Do not refrain from disciplining an infant, because if you strike him with a rod, he will certainly not die;
Proverbs 23:14 for you will strike him with a rod, but you will deliver his soul from death.
Proverbs 23:15 Son, if your heart becomes wise, you will gladden my heart also,
Proverbs 23:16 and your lips will spend time in words with my lips, if they are upright.
Proverbs 23:17 Let your heart not envy sinners, but be in fear of the Lord the whole day;
Proverbs 23:18 for if you keep them, you will have offspring, and your hope will not depart.
Proverbs 23:19 Hear, son, and become wise and direct the thoughts of your heart;
Proverbs 23:20 do not be a wine-drinker, nor stretch yourself to contributions and purchases of meats;
Proverbs 23:21 for every drunkard and frequenter of prostitutes will become poor, and every sleepy person will clothe himself in torn and ragged things.
Proverbs 23:22 Hear, son, the father who begot you, and do not despise your mother because she has grown old.
Proverbs 23:24 A righteous father nourishes well, and his soul is gladdened over a wise son;
Proverbs 23:25 let the father and mother be gladdened over you, and let her who bore you rejoice.
Proverbs 23:26 Give me, son, your heart, and let your eyes keep my ways;
Proverbs 23:27 for a stranger's house is a pierced jar, and a stranger's well is narrow;
Proverbs 23:28 for this one will quickly perish, and every lawless person will be consumed.
Proverbs 23:29 For whom is woe? For whom tumult? For whom judgment? For whom unpleasantness and chatter? For whom fractures for nothing? Whose eyes are livid?
Proverbs 23:30 Are they not those lingering among wines? Are they not those tracking where drinking parties take place?
Proverbs 23:31 Do not become drunk with wine, but associate with righteous humans and associate on walks; for if you give your eyes to the bowls and cups, afterward you will walk about more naked than a pestle,
Proverbs 23:32 and at the last he stretches out as though struck by a snake, and as though by a horned snake the venom is poured through him.
Proverbs 23:33 When your eyes see a strange woman, your mouth will then speak crooked things,
Proverbs 23:34 and you will lie down as in the heart of the sea and as a helmsman in much surging;
Proverbs 23:35 and you will say, They strike me, and I did not suffer, and they mocked me, but I did not know; when will dawn be, so that I may come and seek those with whom I will meet?

## Chapter 24

Proverbs 24:1 Son, do not envy evil men, nor desire to be with them;
Proverbs 24:2 for their heart practices lies, and their lips speak troubles.
Proverbs 24:3 With wisdom a house is built, and with understanding it is set upright;
Proverbs 24:4 with perception chambers are filled with all precious and good wealth.
Proverbs 24:5 A wise person is better than a strong one, and a man having prudence than a great farm;
Proverbs 24:6 with guidance war takes place, and help with a deliberative heart.
Proverbs 24:7 Wisdom and good thought are in wise people's gates; wise people do not turn aside from the Lord's mouth,
Proverbs 24:8 but deliberate in councils. Death encounters the undisciplined,
Proverbs 24:9 and a senseless person dies in sins; and uncleanness will be polluted for a pestilent man
Proverbs 24:10 on an evil day and on a day of affliction, until it fails.
Proverbs 24:11 Deliver those being led to death and ransom those being killed; do not spare;
Proverbs 24:12 but if you say, I do not know this person, know that the Lord knows everyone's hearts, and the one fashioning breath for all himself knows everything, who repays each according to his works.
Proverbs 24:13 Eat honey, son, for a honeycomb is good, so that your throat may be sweetened;
Proverbs 24:14 thus you will perceive wisdom for your soul; for if you find it, your end will be good, and hope will not abandon you.
Proverbs 24:15 Do not bring an ungodly person to righteous people's pasture, nor be deceived by a belly's fullness;
Proverbs 24:16 for the righteous person will fall seven times and rise, but ungodly people will become weak amid evil things.
Proverbs 24:17 If your enemy falls, do not rejoice over him, and at his stumbling do not be lifted up;
Proverbs 24:18 because the Lord will see, and it will not please him, and he will turn his wrath away from him.
Proverbs 24:19 Do not rejoice over evildoers, nor envy sinners;
Proverbs 24:20 for there will certainly not be offspring of evil people, and the lamp of ungodly people will be extinguished.
Proverbs 24:21 Fear God, son, and a king, and disobey neither of them;
Proverbs 24:22 for suddenly they will punish the ungodly, and who will know the punishments of both?
Proverbs 24:22 a A son keeping a word will be outside destruction, and receiving, he received it.
Proverbs 24:23 Let no lie from a tongue be spoken to a king, and no lie will certainly come out from his tongue.
Proverbs 24:24 A king's tongue is a sword and not fleshy, and whoever is handed over will be shattered;
Proverbs 24:25 for if his wrath is sharpened, it consumes humans together with sinews
Proverbs 24:26 and devours humans' bones and burns them together like a flame, so that they are uneatable for young eagles. – –

## Chapter 30

Proverbs 30:1 Fear my words, son, and having received them, repent; these things the man says to those trusting God, and I cease;
Proverbs 30:2 for I am the most senseless of all humans, and humans' prudence is not in me;
Proverbs 30:3 God has taught me wisdom, and I have known knowledge of holy things.
Proverbs 30:4 Who went up into heaven and came down? Who gathered winds in a bosom? Who wrapped water in a garment? Who held all the ends of the earth? What is his name, or what is the name of his children, so that you may know?
Proverbs 30:5 All God's words have been tried by fire, and he himself shields those revering him;
Proverbs 30:6 do not add to his words, so that he may not reprove you and you become false.
Proverbs 30:7 I ask two things from you; do not take grace away from me before I die;
Proverbs 30:8 make a vain and false word far from me, and do not give me wealth and poverty, but appoint for me necessary and sufficient things,
Proverbs 30:9 so that, filled, I may not become false and say, Who sees me? Or, made needy, steal and swear the name of God.
Proverbs 30:10 Do not hand a servant into a master's hands, lest he curse you and you disappear.
Proverbs 30:11 An evil offspring curses a father, but does not bless the mother;
Proverbs 30:12 an evil offspring judges itself righteous, but did not wash away its discharge;
Proverbs 30:13 an evil offspring has lofty eyes, and is lifted up in its eyelids;
Proverbs 30:14 an evil offspring has swords as teeth and knives as molars, so as to consume and devour the humble from the earth and their needy from among humans. – –
Proverbs 30:23 And these things I say to you wise people to recognize: to respect a face in judgment is not good;
Proverbs 30:24 the one saying of the ungodly person, He is righteous, will be accursed among peoples and hated among nations;
Proverbs 30:25 but those reproving will appear better, and a good blessing will come upon them;
Proverbs 30:26 and lips answering good words will kiss.
Proverbs 30:27 Prepare your works for going out and make ready for the field and go behind me, and you will rebuild your house.
Proverbs 30:28 Do not be a false witness against your fellow citizen, nor widen with your lips;
Proverbs 30:29 do not say, In the way he treated me I will treat him, and I will punish him for the things in which he wronged me.
Proverbs 30:30 A senseless man is like a farm, and a human lacking sense like a vineyard;
Proverbs 30:31 if you leave him, he will become waste and wholly overgrown with grass and becomes abandoned, and his stone fences are demolished.
Proverbs 30:32 Afterward I repented; I looked to choose discipline.
Proverbs 30:33 I doze a little, and sleep a little, and embrace my breast with hands a little;
Proverbs 30:34 but if you do this, your poverty will come walking ahead, and your want like a good runner. – –
Proverbs 30:15 The leech had three daughters loved with love, and these three did not fill her, and the fourth was not content to say, Sufficient;
Proverbs 30:16 Hades and a woman's love and Tartarus and earth not filled with water and water and fire will certainly not say, It suffices.
Proverbs 30:17 An eye laughing at a father and dishonoring a mother's old age, may ravens from the ravines cut it out, and may young eagles devour it.
Proverbs 30:18 And there are three things impossible for me to understand, and the fourth I do not recognize;
Proverbs 30:19 tracks of an eagle flying and ways of a snake on a rock and paths of a ship crossing the sea and ways of a man in youth.
Proverbs 30:20 Such is the way of an adulterous woman who, whenever she acts, having washed herself, says she has done nothing improper.
Proverbs 30:21 Through three things the earth is shaken, and the fourth it cannot bear;
Proverbs 30:22 if a servant becomes king, and a senseless person is filled with foods,
Proverbs 30:23 and if a maidservant casts out her own mistress, and if a hated woman obtains a good man.
Proverbs 30:24 And there are four smallest things on the earth, and these are wiser than the wise;
Proverbs 30:25 the ants, which have no strength and prepare food in summer;
Proverbs 30:26 and the rock-rabbits, a nation not strong, which made their own houses in rocks;
Proverbs 30:27 the locust is without a king and marches out orderly from one command;
Proverbs 30:28 and a lizard, supporting itself with hands and being easily caught, dwells in a king's strongholds.
Proverbs 30:29 And there are three things that proceed well, and the fourth that walks well;
Proverbs 30:30 a lion's cub stronger than beasts, which does not turn away nor cower before a beast,
Proverbs 30:31 and a cock walking among females, spirited, and a he-goat leading a goat herd, and a king addressing an assembly among a nation.
Proverbs 30:32 If you give yourself up to gladness and stretch out your hand with fighting, you will be dishonored.
Proverbs 30:33 Milk milk, and there will be butter; but if you squeeze nostrils, blood will come out; and if you draw out words, judgments and fights will come out. – –

## Chapter 31

Proverbs 31:1 My words have been spoken by God, an oracle of a king whom his mother disciplined.
Proverbs 31:2 What, child, will you keep? What? Utterances of God; firstborn, I speak to you, son; what, child of my belly? What, child of my vows?
Proverbs 31:3 Do not give your wealth to women, and your mind and life to later regret.
Proverbs 31:4 Do everything with counsel, drink wine with counsel; rulers are wrathful, and let them not drink wine,
Proverbs 31:5 so that, having drunk, they may not forget wisdom and certainly be unable to judge weak people rightly.
Proverbs 31:6 Give drunkenness to those in griefs and wine to drink to those in pains,
Proverbs 31:7 so that they may forget poverty and remember troubles no longer.
Proverbs 31:8 Open your mouth with God's word and judge everyone soundly;
Proverbs 31:9 open your mouth and judge righteously, and distinguish a needy and weak person. – –

## Chapter 25

Proverbs 25:1 These are the unseparated disciplines of Salomon, which the friends of Ezekias the king of Ioudaia copied out.
Proverbs 25:2 God's glory hides a word, but a king's glory honors matters.
Proverbs 25:3 Heaven is high and earth deep, and a king's heart unsearchable.
Proverbs 25:4 Beat unapproved silver, and it will all be purified clean;
Proverbs 25:5 kill ungodly people from a king's presence, and his throne will be set right in righteousness.
Proverbs 25:6 Do not boast before a king, nor stand in rulers' places;
Proverbs 25:7 for it is better for you to be told, Come up to me, than for him to humble you in a ruler's presence. Say what your eyes saw.
Proverbs 25:8 Do not rush into a fight quickly, so that you may not regret it at the last. Whenever your friend reproaches you,
Proverbs 25:9 withdraw backward; do not despise,
Proverbs 25:10 lest the friend reproach you, and your fight and enmity will not depart, but will be equal to death for you.
Proverbs 25:10 a Grace and friendship set free; keep them for yourself, so that you may not become reproached, but guard your ways conciliatorily.
Proverbs 25:11 A golden apple in a little necklace of sardius, so is speaking a word.
Proverbs 25:12 A costly sardius has been bound into a golden earring, a wise word into a readily hearing ear.
Proverbs 25:13 Just as an outflow of snow at harvest in heat benefits, so a faithful messenger benefits those sending him; for he benefits the souls of those using him.
Proverbs 25:14 Like winds and clouds and most conspicuous rains, so are those boasting over a false gift.
Proverbs 25:15 In long-temperedness is prosperity for kings, and a soft tongue shatters bones.
Proverbs 25:16 Having found honey, eat what is sufficient, lest, filled, you vomit it out.
Proverbs 25:17 Bring your foot to your own friend rarely, lest, filled with you, he hate you.
Proverbs 25:18 A club and a sword and a pointed arrow, so also is the man testifying a false testimony against his friend.
Proverbs 25:19 An evil person's tooth and a lawless person's foot will perish on an evil day.
Proverbs 25:20 Just as vinegar is disadvantageous to a wound, so a suffering befalling a body grieves a heart.
Proverbs 25:20 a Just as a moth harms a garment and a worm wood, so a man's grief harms a heart.
Proverbs 25:21 If your enemy hungers, feed him; if he thirsts, give him drink;
Proverbs 25:22 for doing this you will heap coals of fire on his head, and the Lord will repay you good things.
Proverbs 25:23 A north wind raises clouds, and a shameless face provokes a tongue.
Proverbs 25:24 It is better to dwell on a corner of a roof than with an abusive woman in a shared house.
Proverbs 25:25 Just as cold water is pleasant to a thirsty soul, so is good news from a land far away.
Proverbs 25:26 As if someone were to block a spring and ruin an outflow of water, so it is unseemly for a righteous person to have fallen before an ungodly person.
Proverbs 25:27 To eat much honey is not good, but one must honor glorious words.
Proverbs 25:28 Like a city with its walls cast down and unwalled, so is a man who does anything without counsel.

## Chapter 26

Proverbs 26:1 Like dew at harvest and like rain in summer, so honor is not for a senseless person.
Proverbs 26:2 Just as birds and sparrows fly, so a vain curse will come upon no one.
Proverbs 26:3 Like a whip for a horse and a goad for a donkey, so is a rod for a lawless nation.
Proverbs 26:4 Do not answer a senseless person in relation to his senselessness, so that you may not become like him;
Proverbs 26:5 but answer a senseless person according to his senselessness, so that he may not appear wise to himself.
Proverbs 26:6 The one sending a word through a senseless messenger will drink reproach from his own feet.
Proverbs 26:7 Take away the walking of legs and a proverb from the mouth of senseless people.
Proverbs 26:8 Whoever binds a stone in a sling is like the one giving glory to a senseless person.
Proverbs 26:9 Thorns grow in a drunkard's hand, and slavery in the hand of senseless people.
Proverbs 26:10 All flesh of senseless people is greatly storm-tossed; for their bewilderment is shattered.
Proverbs 26:11 Just as a dog, whenever it comes upon its own vomit and becomes hated, so is a senseless person who by his own wickedness has returned to his own sin.
Proverbs 26:11 a There is shame bringing sin, and there is shame that is glory and grace.
Proverbs 26:12 I saw a man who thought himself wise, yet a senseless person had more hope than he.
Proverbs 26:13 A slothful person being sent on a way says, A lion is in the ways.
Proverbs 26:14 Just as a door turns on its hinge, so a slothful person on his bed.
Proverbs 26:15 A slothful person, having hidden his hand in his bosom, will not be able to bring it to his mouth.
Proverbs 26:16 A slothful person appears to himself wiser than the one bringing back a message in fullness.
Proverbs 26:17 Like the one holding a dog's tail, so is the one presiding over a stranger's case.
Proverbs 26:18 Just as those healing put words before humans, and the first one encountering the word will be tripped,
Proverbs 26:19 so are all those ambushing their own friends, but whenever they are detected, they say, I did it playing.
Proverbs 26:20 Among many pieces of wood a fire flourishes, but where there is no double-minded person, a fight is quiet.
Proverbs 26:21 A hearth for coals and wood for fire, and an abusive man for the disturbance of a fight.
Proverbs 26:22 Words of rogues are soft, but these strike into chambers of the inward parts.
Proverbs 26:23 Silver given with deceit must be considered like a potsherd. Smooth lips cover a sorrowful heart.
Proverbs 26:24 An enemy lamenting assents to everything with lips, but in his heart he devises deceits;
Proverbs 26:25 if the enemy begs you with a loud voice, do not be persuaded; for seven evils are in his soul.
Proverbs 26:26 The one hiding enmity establishes deceit, but one readily known in councils reveals his own sins.
Proverbs 26:27 The one digging a pit for his neighbor will fall into it, and the one rolling a stone rolls it upon himself.
Proverbs 26:28 A lying tongue hates truth, and an unrestrained mouth makes disorders.

## Chapter 27

Proverbs 27:1 Do not boast of the things for tomorrow; for you do not know what the coming day will bear.
Proverbs 27:2 Let the neighbor praise you and not your mouth, a stranger and not your lips.
Proverbs 27:3 A stone is heavy and sand hard to bear, but a senseless person's anger is heavier than both.
Proverbs 27:4 Wrath is merciless and anger sharp, but jealousy withstands no one.
Proverbs 27:5 Revealed reproofs are better than hidden friendship.
Proverbs 27:6 A friend's wounds are more trustworthy than an enemy's willing kisses.
Proverbs 27:7 A soul being in fullness mocks honeycombs, but to a needy soul even bitter things appear sweet.
Proverbs 27:8 Just as when a bird flies down out of its own nest, so a human is enslaved whenever he is estranged from his own places.
Proverbs 27:9 A heart is delighted by ointments and wines and incenses, but a soul is torn apart by misfortunes.
Proverbs 27:10 Do not abandon your friend or an ancestral friend, and do not enter your brother's house when unfortunate; a friend nearby is better than a brother dwelling far away.
Proverbs 27:11 Become wise, son, so that my heart may be gladdened, and turn reproachful words away from yourself.
Proverbs 27:12 A shrewd person hid himself when evil things were coming, but senseless people, having come upon them, will pay a penalty.
Proverbs 27:13 Take away his garment, for he passed by; whoever ruins others' things is arrogant.
Proverbs 27:14 Whoever blesses a friend early with a loud voice will seem to differ in nothing from one cursing.
Proverbs 27:15 Drops cast a human out of his house on a winter day, likewise also an abusive woman out of his own house.
Proverbs 27:16 The north wind is a harsh wind, but by name it is called favorable.
Proverbs 27:17 Iron sharpens iron, and a man provokes a companion's face.
Proverbs 27:18 Whoever plants a fig tree will eat its fruits; but whoever guards his own master will be honored.
Proverbs 27:19 Just as faces are not alike to faces, so neither are humans' hearts.
Proverbs 27:20 Hades and destruction are not filled, likewise also humans' eyes are insatiable.
Proverbs 27:20 a One fixing an eye is an abomination to the Lord, and the undisciplined are unrestrained in tongue.
Proverbs 27:21 Burning is a test for silver and gold, but a man is tested through the mouth of those praising him.
Proverbs 27:21 a A lawless person's heart seeks out evil things, but an upright heart seeks out knowledge.
Proverbs 27:22 If you were to whip a senseless person in the midst of a council, dishonoring him, you would certainly not remove his senselessness.
Proverbs 27:23 You will knowingly recognize the souls of your flock and apply your heart to your herds;
Proverbs 27:24 because dominion and strength are not forever for a man, nor does he hand them down from generation to generation.
Proverbs 27:25 Attend to the green things in the plain, and you will cut grass, and gather mountain fodder,
Proverbs 27:26 so that you may have sheep for clothing; honor a plain, so that you may have lambs.
Proverbs 27:27 Son, from me you have strong utterances for your life and for the life of your attendants.

## Chapter 28

Proverbs 28:1 An ungodly person flees with no one pursuing, but a righteous person has confidence like a lion.
Proverbs 28:2 Through ungodly people's sins judgments are raised, but a shrewd man will extinguish them.
Proverbs 28:3 One courageous in ungodliness extorts from poor people. Like a violent and unprofitable rain,
Proverbs 28:4 so those abandoning the law praise ungodliness, but those loving the law put a wall around themselves.
Proverbs 28:5 Evil men will not understand judgment, but those seeking the Lord will understand in everything.
Proverbs 28:6 A poor person walking in truth is better than a false rich person.
Proverbs 28:7 An understanding son keeps law; but whoever shepherds dissipation dishonors a father.
Proverbs 28:8 The one multiplying his wealth with interest and excesses gathers it for the one showing mercy to poor people.
Proverbs 28:9 The one turning aside his ear so as not to hear law has himself also made his prayer abominable.
Proverbs 28:10 Whoever leads upright people astray in an evil way will himself fall into corruption; but the lawless will pass through good things and will not enter into them.
Proverbs 28:11 A rich man is wise to himself, but an intelligent needy person will condemn him.
Proverbs 28:12 Through the help of righteous people much glory arises, but in ungodly people's places humans are caught.
Proverbs 28:13 The one covering his own ungodliness will not prosper, but the one explaining reproofs will be loved.
Proverbs 28:14 Blessed is a man who cowers before everything through reverence, but the one hard in heart will fall into evil things.
Proverbs 28:15 A hungry lion and a thirsty wolf is the one who, being poor, tyrannizes over an impoverished nation.
Proverbs 28:16 A king lacking revenues is a great extortioner, but the one hating injustice will live a long time.
Proverbs 28:17 The one guaranteeing a man under a charge of murder will be a fugitive and not in safety.
Proverbs 28:17 a Discipline a son, and he will love you and give ornament to your soul; you shall certainly not listen to a lawless nation.
Proverbs 28:18 The one walking righteously has been helped, but the one walking in crooked ways will be entangled.
Proverbs 28:19 The one working his own land will be filled with breads, but the one pursuing leisure will be filled with poverty.
Proverbs 28:20 A trustworthy man will be greatly blessed, but the evil person will not be unpunished.
Proverbs 28:21 Whoever does not respect righteous people's faces is not good; such a person will sell a man for a morsel of bread.
Proverbs 28:22 An envious man hastens to become rich and does not know that a merciful person will rule him.
Proverbs 28:23 The one reproving a human's ways will have graces more than the one flattering with a tongue.
Proverbs 28:24 Whoever rejects a father or mother and thinks he is not sinning, this person is a partner of an ungodly man.
Proverbs 28:25 An insatiable man judges at random; but whoever has trusted in the Lord will be under care.
Proverbs 28:26 Whoever has trusted in a rash heart, such a person is senseless; but whoever walks in wisdom will be saved.
Proverbs 28:27 Whoever gives to poor people will not lack; but whoever turns away his eye will be in much difficulty.
Proverbs 28:28 In ungodly people's places righteous people groan, but in those people's destruction righteous people will multiply.

## Chapter 29

Proverbs 29:1 A reproving man is better than a stiff-necked man; for when he suddenly burns, there is no healing.
Proverbs 29:2 When righteous people are praised, peoples will be gladdened, but when ungodly people rule, men groan.
Proverbs 29:3 The father of a man loving wisdom is gladdened; but whoever shepherds prostitutes will destroy wealth.
Proverbs 29:4 A righteous king raises up a country, but a lawless man demolishes it.
Proverbs 29:5 Whoever prepares a net against his own friend's face puts it around his own feet.
Proverbs 29:6 For a sinning man there is a great trap, but a righteous person will be in joy and gladness.
Proverbs 29:7 A righteous person knows how to judge for the impoverished, but the ungodly person will not understand knowledge, and a discerning mind does not belong to a poor person.
Proverbs 29:8 Pestilent men burned a city, but wise people turned away anger.
Proverbs 29:9 A wise man judges nations, but a worthless man, being angry, is laughed at and does not cower.
Proverbs 29:10 Men sharing in blood will hate a holy person, but the upright will seek out his soul.
Proverbs 29:11 A senseless person brings out his whole wrath, but a wise person stores it portion by portion.
Proverbs 29:12 When a king listens to an unjust word, all those under him are lawless.
Proverbs 29:13 When a lender and debtor come together with one another, the Lord makes a visitation of both.
Proverbs 29:14 When a king judges poor people in truth, his throne will be established for a testimony.
Proverbs 29:15 Blows and reproofs give wisdom, but a wandering child shames his parents.
Proverbs 29:16 When ungodly people are many, sins become many, but righteous people become greatly afraid when those people fall.
Proverbs 29:17 Discipline your son, and he will give you rest and give ornament to your soul.
Proverbs 29:18 There will certainly not be an interpreter for a lawless nation, but the one keeping the law is blessed.
Proverbs 29:19 A harsh servant will not be disciplined by words; for even if he understands, yet he will not listen.
Proverbs 29:20 If you see a man quick in words, know that a senseless person has more hope than he.
Proverbs 29:21 Whoever lives lavishly from childhood will be a servant, and at the last will be pained over himself.
Proverbs 29:22 A wrathful man digs strife, and an irascible man dug out sins.
Proverbs 29:23 Arrogance humbles a man, but the Lord supports the humble-minded with glory.
Proverbs 29:24 Whoever shares with a thief hates his own soul; but if, when an oath has been put forth, they hear and do not report,
Proverbs 29:25 having feared and been ashamed before humans, they were tripped; but the one trusting in the Lord will be gladdened. Ungodliness gives a man a fall; but whoever has trusted in the Master will be saved.
Proverbs 29:26 Many attend upon leaders' faces, but what is just for a man comes from the Lord.
Proverbs 29:27 An unjust man is an abomination to righteous people, but a directing way is an abomination to a lawless person. – –
Proverbs 29:10 Who will find a courageous woman? And such a woman is more precious than costly stones.
Proverbs 29:11 Her husband's heart has confidence in her; such a woman will not lack good spoils;
Proverbs 29:12 for she produces good things for her husband all her life.
Proverbs 29:13 Winding wool and flax, she made it useful with her hands.
Proverbs 29:14 She became like a ship trading from afar, and she gathers livelihood.
Proverbs 29:15 And she rises from nights and gave foods to the household and tasks to the maidservants.
Proverbs 29:16 Having considered a farm, she bought it, and from fruits of her hands she planted a property.
Proverbs 29:17 Having strongly girded her loins, she braced her arms for work.
Proverbs 29:18 She tasted that working is good, and her lamp is not extinguished the whole night.
Proverbs 29:19 She stretches her forearms toward beneficial things, and braces her hands upon a spindle.
Proverbs 29:20 And she opened her hands to a needy person, and stretched out a wrist to a poor person.
Proverbs 29:21 Her husband does not worry about those in the house whenever he lingers somewhere; for all those with her are clothed.
Proverbs 29:22 She made double cloaks for her husband, and garments for herself from fine linen and purple.
Proverbs 29:23 And her husband becomes conspicuous in gates whenever he sits in council with the elder inhabitants of the land.
Proverbs 29:24 She made linen cloths and sold them, and girdles to the Chanaanites.
Proverbs 29:25 She opened her mouth attentively and lawfully and appointed order for her tongue.
Proverbs 29:26 She clothed herself in strength and comeliness and was gladdened in last days.
Proverbs 29:27 The dwellings of her houses are sheltered, and she did not eat idle foods.
Proverbs 29:28 And she opens her mouth wisely and according to law, and her mercifulness raised up her children, and they became rich, and her husband praised her:
Proverbs 29:29 Many daughters acquired wealth, many did mighty things, but you lie above and surpassed all.
Proverbs 29:30 Pleasing qualities are false and a woman's beauty vain; for an understanding woman is blessed, and let her praise fear of the Lord.
Proverbs 29:31 Give her from fruits of her hands, and let her husband be praised in gates.

# Ecclesiastes

The Apostolic Bible. Public domain. https://apostolic-bible.ysys9.chatgpt.site/license.html


## Chapter 1

Ecclesiastes 1:1 Utterances of the Ecclesiast, son of Dauid, king of Israel in Ierousalem.
Ecclesiastes 1:2 Vanity of vanities, said the Ecclesiast, vanity of vanities, everything is vanity.
Ecclesiastes 1:3 What surplus is there for the human in all his toil in which he toils under the sun?
Ecclesiastes 1:4 A generation goes and a generation comes, and the earth has stood forever.
Ecclesiastes 1:5 And the sun rises and the sun sets and draws toward its place;
Ecclesiastes 1:6 rising there, it goes toward the south and circles toward the north; circling it circles, the wind goes, and the wind returns upon its circuits.
Ecclesiastes 1:7 All the torrents go into the sea, and the sea will not be filled; to the place where the torrents go, there they return to go.
Ecclesiastes 1:8 All words are wearisome; a man will not be able to speak, and an eye will not be filled with seeing, and an ear will not be filled from hearing.
Ecclesiastes 1:9 What has happened? The same is what will happen; and what has been done? The same is what will be done; and there is nothing fresh under the sun.
Ecclesiastes 1:10 Whoever will speak and say, See, this is new, it has already happened in the ages that came before us.
Ecclesiastes 1:11 There is no remembrance of the first, and indeed of the last who have come there will be no remembrance of them among those who will come at the last.
Ecclesiastes 1:12 I, the Ecclesiast, became king over Israel in Ierousalem;
Ecclesiastes 1:13 and I gave my heart to seek out and to examine in wisdom concerning all the things happening under heaven; because God gave an evil distraction to the sons of the human to be distracted in it.
Ecclesiastes 1:14 I saw all the works done under the sun, and behold, everything is vanity and choice of spirit.
Ecclesiastes 1:15 What has been perverted will not be able to be set in order, and a deficiency will not be able to be numbered.
Ecclesiastes 1:16 I spoke in my heart, saying, I, behold, was magnified and added wisdom above all who came before me in Ierousalem, and my heart saw much, wisdom and knowledge.
Ecclesiastes 1:17 And I gave my heart to know wisdom and knowledge; I knew parables and understanding, that indeed this too is choice of spirit;
Ecclesiastes 1:18 because in abundance of wisdom is abundance of knowledge, and the one adding knowledge will add pain.

## Chapter 2

Ecclesiastes 2:1 I said in my heart, Come now, I will test you in gladness, and see in good; and behold, indeed this too is vanity.
Ecclesiastes 2:2 To laughter I said, Derangement, and to gladness, Why do you do this?
Ecclesiastes 2:3 I examined in my heart drawing my flesh into wine – and my heart guided in wisdom – and taking hold of senselessness, until I see what is the good for the sons of the human which they will do under the sun for the number of days of their life.
Ecclesiastes 2:4 I enlarged my work, I built houses for myself, I planted vineyards for myself,
Ecclesiastes 2:5 I made gardens and parks for myself and planted in them every fruit tree;
Ecclesiastes 2:6 I made pools of waters for myself to water from them a wood sprouting trees;
Ecclesiastes 2:7 I acquired male slaves and female slaves, and homeborn slaves came to belong to me, and indeed much possession of cattle and flock came to belong to me above all who came before me in Ierousalem;
Ecclesiastes 2:8 I gathered for myself also silver and gold and abundances of kings and of countries; I made for myself male singers and female singers and delights of the sons of the human, a male wine-pourer and female wine-pourers;
Ecclesiastes 2:9 and I was magnified and increased beyond all who came before me in Ierousalem; and indeed my wisdom stood with me.
Ecclesiastes 2:10 And everything that my eyes asked, I did not withhold from them; I did not prevent my heart from any gladness, because my heart was gladdened in all my toil, and this became my portion from all my toil.
Ecclesiastes 2:11 And I looked upon all my works which my hands did, and upon toil in which I toiled to do them, and behold, everything is vanity and choice of spirit, and there is no surplus under the sun.
Ecclesiastes 2:12 And I looked to see wisdom and derangement and senselessness; because who is the human who will come after the counsel, all the things that made it?
Ecclesiastes 2:13 And I saw that wisdom has a surplus above senselessness, as the surplus of light above darkness;
Ecclesiastes 2:14 the wise person's eyes are in his head, and the senseless person walks in darkness. And indeed I knew that one occurrence will occur to them all.
Ecclesiastes 2:15 And I said in my heart, As the occurrence of the senseless person, indeed it will occur to me also, and why did I become wise? I then spoke excessively in my heart, because a senseless person speaks from excess, that indeed this too is vanity.
Ecclesiastes 2:16 Because there is no remembrance of the wise person with the senseless person forever, inasmuch as already in the coming days everything was forgotten; and how will the wise person die with the senseless person?
Ecclesiastes 2:17 And I hated life, because the work done under the sun is evil upon me, because everything is vanity and choice of spirit.
Ecclesiastes 2:18 And I hated all my toil which I toil under the sun, because I leave it to the human coming after me;
Ecclesiastes 2:19 and who knows whether he will be wise or senseless? And he exercises authority over all my toil in which I toiled and in which I acted wisely under the sun. Indeed this too is vanity.
Ecclesiastes 2:20 And I turned to renounce in my heart all the toil in which I toiled under the sun,
Ecclesiastes 2:21 because there is a human whose toil is in wisdom and in knowledge and in courage, and to a human who did not toil in it he will give his portion. Indeed this too is vanity and great evil.
Ecclesiastes 2:22 Because what comes to the human in all his toil and in the choice of his heart in which he himself toils under the sun?
Ecclesiastes 2:23 Because all his days are of pains, and his distraction of wrath, and indeed at night his heart does not sleep. Indeed this too is vanity.
Ecclesiastes 2:24 There is no good in a human; what he will eat and what he will drink and what he will show his soul is good in his toil. Indeed this too I saw, that it is from God's hand;
Ecclesiastes 2:25 because who will eat and who will spare apart from him?
Ecclesiastes 2:26 Because to the human good before his face he gave wisdom and knowledge and gladness; and to the sinner he gave distraction to add and to gather to give to the good person before God's face; because indeed this too is vanity and choice of spirit.

## Chapter 3

Ecclesiastes 3:1 For everything there is a time, and a season for every matter under heaven.
Ecclesiastes 3:2 A season to give birth and a season to die, a season to plant and a season to pull out what has been planted,
Ecclesiastes 3:3 a season to kill and a season to heal, a season to pull down and a season to build,
Ecclesiastes 3:4 a season to weep and a season to laugh, a season to mourn and a season to dance,
Ecclesiastes 3:5 a season to cast stones and a season to gather stones, a season to embrace and a season to be far from an embrace,
Ecclesiastes 3:6 a season to seek and a season to lose, a season to keep and a season to cast out,
Ecclesiastes 3:7 a season to tear and a season to sew, a season to be silent and a season to speak,
Ecclesiastes 3:8 a season to love and a season to hate, a season of war and a season of peace.
Ecclesiastes 3:9 What surplus has the one doing in the things in which he himself toils?
Ecclesiastes 3:10 I saw the distraction which God gave to the sons of the human to be distracted in it.
Ecclesiastes 3:11 He made everything good in its season, and indeed he gave eternity in their heart, so that the human may not find the work which God did, from beginning and until end.
Ecclesiastes 3:12 I knew that there is no good in them except to be gladdened and to do good in his life;
Ecclesiastes 3:13 and indeed every human who will eat and drink and see good in all his toil, it is God's gift.
Ecclesiastes 3:14 I knew that everything, as much as God did, will be forever; there is no adding to it and there is no taking away from it, and God did it so that they may fear before his face.
Ecclesiastes 3:15 What happened already is, and as much as is to happen has already happened, and God will seek the one being pursued.
Ecclesiastes 3:16 And still I saw under the sun a place of judgment, there the ungodly person, and a place of the righteous person, there the ungodly person.
Ecclesiastes 3:17 I said in my heart, God will judge the righteous person and the ungodly person, because there is a season for every matter and over every work.
Ecclesiastes 3:18 There I said in my heart concerning the speech of the sons of the human, that God will distinguish them, and to show that they are beasts, indeed to themselves.
Ecclesiastes 3:19 Because the occurrence of the sons of the human and the occurrence of the beast are one occurrence for them; as the death of this one, so the death of that one, and one spirit for all; and what surplus had the human beyond the beast? Nothing, because everything is vanity.
Ecclesiastes 3:20 Everything goes to one place; everything came from dust, and everything returns to dust;
Ecclesiastes 3:21 and who knows the spirit of the sons of the human, whether it ascends above, and the spirit of the beast, whether it descends below into earth?
Ecclesiastes 3:22 And I saw that there is no good except that the human will be gladdened in his works, because that is his portion; because who will lead him to see what may happen after him?

## Chapter 4

Ecclesiastes 4:1 And I turned and saw all the oppressions happening under the sun; and behold, the tear of those being oppressed, and they have no comforter, and strength is from the hand of those oppressing them, and they have no comforter.
Ecclesiastes 4:2 And I praised the dead who had already died above the living, as many as themselves live until now;
Ecclesiastes 4:3 and better than these two is whoever has not yet come to be, who did not see the evil work done under the sun.
Ecclesiastes 4:4 And I saw all toil and all prowess of the work, that it is a man's envy from his companion; indeed this too is vanity and choice of spirit.
Ecclesiastes 4:5 The senseless person folded his hands and ate his flesh.
Ecclesiastes 4:6 A handful of rest is better than two handfuls of toil and choice of spirit.
Ecclesiastes 4:7 And I turned and saw vanity under the sun.
Ecclesiastes 4:8 There is one, and there is no second, and indeed he has neither son nor brother; and there is no end to all his toil, and indeed his eye is not filled with wealth. And for whom do I toil and deprive my soul of goodness? Indeed this too is vanity and an evil distraction.
Ecclesiastes 4:9 The two are better than the one, who have a good reward in their toil;
Ecclesiastes 4:10 because if they fall, the one will raise his partner, and woe to him who is one, whenever he falls and there is no second to raise him.
Ecclesiastes 4:11 And indeed if two sleep, there is also warmth for them; and how may the one be warmed?
Ecclesiastes 4:12 And if the one is overpowered, the two will stand against him, and the threefold cord will not quickly be torn apart.
Ecclesiastes 4:13 A needy and wise child is better than an older and senseless king who did not know how to attend any longer;
Ecclesiastes 4:14 because from a house of prisoners he will come out to reign, because indeed in his kingdom he was born needy.
Ecclesiastes 4:15 I saw all the living walking under the sun with the second young man who will stand in his place,
Ecclesiastes 4:16 there is no end to all the people, to all, as many as came before them; and indeed the last will not be gladdened in him; because indeed this too is vanity and choice of spirit.
Ecclesiastes 4:17 Guard your foot whenever you go into God's house, and be near to hearing; your sacrifice is above a gift of senseless people, because they do not know how to do evil.

## Chapter 5

Ecclesiastes 5:1 Do not hasten with your mouth, and let your heart not hurry to bring forth a word before God's face; because God is in heaven and you upon earth, therefore let your words be few.
Ecclesiastes 5:2 Because a dream comes in abundance of distraction, and a senseless person's voice in abundance of words.
Ecclesiastes 5:3 Whenever you vow a vow to God, do not delay repaying it; because there is no pleasure in senseless people; repay whatever you vow.
Ecclesiastes 5:4 It is better for you not to vow than for you to vow and not repay.
Ecclesiastes 5:5 Do not give your mouth to make your flesh sin, and do not say before God's face that it is ignorance, so that God may not be angered at your voice and destroy the works of your hands.
Ecclesiastes 5:6 Because in abundance of dreams are also vanities and many words; because fear God.
Ecclesiastes 5:7 If you see oppression of a needy person and seizure of judgment and righteousness in a country, do not marvel at the matter; because a high one above a high one is to watch, and high ones over them.
Ecclesiastes 5:8 And the surplus of land is in everything, a king of the cultivated field.
Ecclesiastes 5:9 One loving silver will not be filled with silver; and who loved produce in their abundance? Indeed this too is vanity.
Ecclesiastes 5:10 In abundance of goodness those eating it were multiplied; and what prowess has the one possessing it except to see with his eyes?
Ecclesiastes 5:11 A slave's sleep is sweet, whether he eats little or much; and for the one filled with becoming rich there is nothing allowing him to sleep.
Ecclesiastes 5:12 There is a sickness which I saw under the sun, wealth being kept by its possessor to his harm,
Ecclesiastes 5:13 and that wealth will perish in an evil distraction, and he begot a son, and there is nothing in his hand.
Ecclesiastes 5:14 As he came out naked from his mother's womb, he will return to go as he comes, and he will take nothing in his toil to go in his hand.
Ecclesiastes 5:15 Indeed this too is an evil sickness; for just as he came, so also he will go away, and what surplus has he in that he toils for wind?
Ecclesiastes 5:16 And indeed all his days are in darkness and mourning and much wrath and sickness and anger.
Ecclesiastes 5:17 Behold what I saw as good, what is fine: to eat and to drink and to see goodness in all his toil in which he may toil under the sun for the number of days of his life which God gave him; because that is his portion.
Ecclesiastes 5:18 And indeed every human to whom God gave wealth and possessions and empowered him to eat from it and to take his share and to be gladdened in his toil, this is God's gift.
Ecclesiastes 5:19 Because he will not much remember the days of his life; because God distracts him in gladness of his heart.

## Chapter 6

Ecclesiastes 6:1 There is an evil which I saw under the sun, and it is great upon the human;
Ecclesiastes 6:2 a man to whom God will give wealth and possessions and glory, and he is not lacking for his soul in any of the things he will desire, and God will not empower him to eat from it, because a strange man will eat it; this is vanity and an evil sickness.
Ecclesiastes 6:3 If a man begets a hundred and will live many years, and however many the days of his years will be, and his soul will not be filled with goodness, and indeed no burial came to him, I said, The miscarriage is better than he,
Ecclesiastes 6:4 because it came in vanity and goes in darkness, and in darkness its name will be covered,
Ecclesiastes 6:5 and indeed it did not see the sun and did not know; there is rest for this one beyond that one.
Ecclesiastes 6:6 And if he lived courses of a thousand years and did not see goodness, does not everything go to one place?
Ecclesiastes 6:7 All the human's toil is for his mouth, and indeed the soul will not be filled.
Ecclesiastes 6:8 Because what surplus has the wise person above the senseless person? Because the needy person knows how to walk before life.
Ecclesiastes 6:9 A sight of eyes is better than what goes in the soul. Indeed this too is vanity and choice of spirit.
Ecclesiastes 6:10 If anything happened, its name has already been called, and it was known what a human is, and he will not be able to contend in judgment with the one stronger than he;
Ecclesiastes 6:11 because there are many words multiplying vanity. What surplus has the human?
Ecclesiastes 6:12 Because who knows what is good for the human in life, for the number of days of the life of his vanity? And he made them in a shadow; because who will tell the human what will be after him under the sun?

## Chapter 7

Ecclesiastes 7:1 A good name is better than good oil, and a day of death than the day of his birth.
Ecclesiastes 7:2 It is better to go into a house of mourning than to go into a house of drinking, inasmuch as this is the end of every human, and the living person will put it into his heart.
Ecclesiastes 7:3 Wrath is better than laughter, because in badness of face a heart will be made good.
Ecclesiastes 7:4 Wise people's heart is in a house of mourning, and senseless people's heart in a house of gladness.
Ecclesiastes 7:5 To hear a wise person's rebuke is better than a man hearing a song of senseless people;
Ecclesiastes 7:6 because as the sound of thorns under a cauldron, so is the laughter of senseless people; indeed this too is vanity.
Ecclesiastes 7:7 Because oppression deranges a wise person and destroys the heart of his vigor.
Ecclesiastes 7:8 The last of words is better than its beginning; a long-tempered person is better than one lofty in spirit.
Ecclesiastes 7:9 Do not hasten in your spirit to be wrathful, because wrath will rest in senseless people's bosom.
Ecclesiastes 7:10 Do not say, What happened, that the former days were better than these? Because you did not ask about this in wisdom.
Ecclesiastes 7:11 Wisdom is good with an inheritance, and a surplus for those beholding the sun;
Ecclesiastes 7:12 because wisdom in its shadow is like the shadow of silver, and a surplus of the knowledge of wisdom will give life to its possessor.
Ecclesiastes 7:13 See God's works; because who will be able to set in order the one whom God may pervert?
Ecclesiastes 7:14 On a day of goodness live in good, and on a day of evil see; indeed God made this in accord with that concerning speech, so that the human may find nothing after him.
Ecclesiastes 7:15 I saw everything in the days of my vanity; there is a righteous person perishing in his righteousness, and there is an ungodly person remaining in his wickedness.
Ecclesiastes 7:16 Do not become greatly righteous and do not act excessively wise, lest you be astounded.
Ecclesiastes 7:17 Do not act greatly ungodly and do not become harsh, so that you may not die when it is not your season.
Ecclesiastes 7:18 It is good for you to hold fast to this, and indeed do not release your hand from that, because the one fearing God will come out of everything.
Ecclesiastes 7:19 Wisdom will help the wise person above ten persons exercising authority who are in the city;
Ecclesiastes 7:20 because there is no righteous human on the earth who will do good and will not sin.
Ecclesiastes 7:21 And indeed do not set your heart upon all the words they will speak, so that you may not hear your slave cursing you,
Ecclesiastes 7:22 because very often he will act wickedly against you and on many occasions harm your heart, as indeed you too cursed others.
Ecclesiastes 7:23 I tested all these things in wisdom; I said, I will be made wise,
Ecclesiastes 7:24 and it went far from me beyond what it was, and a deep depth, who will find it?
Ecclesiastes 7:25 I circled, and my heart, to know and to examine and seek wisdom and reckoning and to know an ungodly person's senselessness and harshness and derangement.
Ecclesiastes 7:26 And I find more bitter than death the woman who is snares, and her heart nets, her hands bonds; the good person before God's face will be rescued from her, and a sinner will be caught in her.
Ecclesiastes 7:27 See, this I found, said the Ecclesiast, one by one to find a reasoning,
Ecclesiastes 7:28 which my soul still sought and I did not find; one human from a thousand I found, and a woman among all these I did not find.
Ecclesiastes 7:29 Only see, this I found, that God made the human upright, and they sought many reasonings.

## Chapter 8

Ecclesiastes 8:1 Who knows wise people? And who knows the solution of an utterance? A human's wisdom will illuminate his face, and one shameless in his face will be hated.
Ecclesiastes 8:2 Keep a king's mouth, and concerning a word of an oath of God do not hasten;
Ecclesiastes 8:3 you will go from his face; do not stand in an evil word; because everything that he may wish he will do,
Ecclesiastes 8:4 as a king exercising authority speaks, and who will say to him, What will you do?
Ecclesiastes 8:5 The one keeping a commandment will not know an evil utterance, and a wise person's heart knows a season of judgment;
Ecclesiastes 8:6 because for every matter there is a season and judgment, because the human's knowledge is great upon him;
Ecclesiastes 8:7 because he does not know what will be, because who will tell him how it will be?
Ecclesiastes 8:8 There is no human exercising authority over spirit to restrain the spirit; and there is no authority on the day of death, and there is no discharge in war, and ungodliness will not preserve its possessor.
Ecclesiastes 8:9 And all this I saw and gave my heart to every work that has been done under the sun, all the things in which the human exercised authority over a human to harm him;
Ecclesiastes 8:10 and then I saw ungodly people brought into tombs, and they went from a holy place and were praised in the city because they did thus. Indeed this too is vanity.
Ecclesiastes 8:11 Because contradiction does not arise quickly from those doing evil; therefore the heart of the sons of the human was fully assured in them to do evil.
Ecclesiastes 8:12 The one who sinned did evil from then and from length of time for him; because indeed I know that it will be good for those fearing God, so that they may fear before his face;
Ecclesiastes 8:13 and it will not be good for the ungodly person, and he will not lengthen days in a shadow, who does not fear before God's face.
Ecclesiastes 8:14 There is vanity which has been done upon earth, that there are righteous people to whom it comes as the work of ungodly people, and there are ungodly people to whom it comes as the work of righteous people; I said that indeed this too is vanity.
Ecclesiastes 8:15 And I praised gladness, because there is no good for the human under the sun except to eat and to drink and to be gladdened, and it will accompany him in his toil for the days of his life, as many as God gave him under the sun.
Ecclesiastes 8:16 When I gave my heart to know wisdom and to see the distraction that has been made upon the earth, because indeed by day and by night he does not see sleep in his eyes,
Ecclesiastes 8:17 and I saw all God's works, that a human will not be able to find the work done under the sun; however much the human may toil to seek, he will not find; and indeed however much the wise person may say that he knows, he will not be able to find.

## Chapter 9

Ecclesiastes 9:1 Because I put all this into my heart, and my heart saw all this, that the righteous and the wise and their labors are in God's hand, and indeed the human does not know either love or hatred; everything is before their face,
Ecclesiastes 9:2 vanity in everything. One occurrence for the righteous person and the ungodly person, for the good and the evil and the clean and the unclean and the one sacrificing and the one not sacrificing; as the good person, so the sinner; as the one swearing, so the one fearing the oath.
Ecclesiastes 9:3 This is evil in everything done under the sun, that there is one occurrence for all; and indeed the heart of the sons of the human was filled with evil, and derangement is in their heart in their life, and after them, toward the dead.
Ecclesiastes 9:4 Because who is the one sharing with all the living? There is hope, because the living dog is itself better than the dead lion.
Ecclesiastes 9:5 Because the living will know that they will die, and the dead do not know anything; and they have no reward any longer, because their remembrance was forgotten;
Ecclesiastes 9:6 and indeed their love and their hatred and their jealousy have already perished, and they have no portion any longer forever in everything done under the sun.
Ecclesiastes 9:7 Come, eat your bread in gladness and drink your wine with a good heart, because God has already approved your works.
Ecclesiastes 9:8 At every season let your garments be white, and let oil upon your head not be lacking.
Ecclesiastes 9:9 See life with a woman whom you loved all the days of the life of your vanity given to you under the sun, all the days of your vanity, because that is your portion in your life and in your toil in which you toil under the sun.
Ecclesiastes 9:10 Everything, as much as your hand may find to do, do according to your power, because there is no work and reasoning and knowledge and wisdom in Hades, where you are going.
Ecclesiastes 9:11 I turned and saw under the sun that the race is not for the swift, and war not for the powerful, and indeed bread not for the wise, and indeed wealth not for the understanding, and indeed grace not for those knowing, because a season and an encounter will occur to them all.
Ecclesiastes 9:12 Because indeed the human did not know his season; as the fish caught in an evil casting-net and as birds caught in a trap, like them the sons of the human are trapped at an evil season whenever it falls upon them suddenly.
Ecclesiastes 9:13 Indeed this too I saw as wisdom under the sun, and it is great to me;
Ecclesiastes 9:14 a small city and few men in it, and a great king may come against it and encircle it and build great siegeworks against it;
Ecclesiastes 9:15 and he may find in it a needy wise man, and he himself will preserve the city in his wisdom; and no human remembered that needy man.
Ecclesiastes 9:16 And I said, Wisdom is better than power; and the needy person's wisdom is despised, and his words are not heard.
Ecclesiastes 9:17 Words of wise people in rest are heard above the cry of those exercising authority in senselessnesses.
Ecclesiastes 9:18 Wisdom is better than implements of war, and one sinner will destroy much goodness.

## Chapter 10

Ecclesiastes 10:1 Flies that kill will rot a preparation of fragrant oil; a little wisdom is precious above glory of great senselessness.
Ecclesiastes 10:2 A wise person's heart is toward his right, and a senseless person's heart toward his left;
Ecclesiastes 10:3 and indeed on a way whenever a senseless person walks, his heart will lack, and everything he will reckon is senselessness.
Ecclesiastes 10:4 If the spirit of the one exercising authority rises against you, do not leave your place, because healing will stop great sins.
Ecclesiastes 10:5 There is an evil which I saw under the sun, like an involuntary thing which came from the face of the one exercising authority;
Ecclesiastes 10:6 the senseless person was set in great heights, and rich people will sit in a low place;
Ecclesiastes 10:7 I saw slaves on horses and rulers walking like slaves upon the earth.
Ecclesiastes 10:8 The one digging a pit will fall into it, and the one pulling down a fence, a snake will bite him;
Ecclesiastes 10:9 one removing stones will be distressed by them, one splitting wood will be endangered by it.
Ecclesiastes 10:10 If the iron falls out, and he himself disturbed its face, he will also strengthen forces, and wisdom is the courageous person's surplus.
Ecclesiastes 10:11 If the snake bites without whispering, there is also no surplus for the one chanting a charm.
Ecclesiastes 10:12 Words of a wise person's mouth are grace, and a senseless person's lips will drown him;
Ecclesiastes 10:13 the beginning of his mouth's words is senselessness, and the last of his mouth evil derangement;
Ecclesiastes 10:14 and the senseless person multiplies words. The human did not know what happened, and what will be after him, who will tell him?
Ecclesiastes 10:15 The toil of senseless people will weary them, one who did not know how to go to a city.
Ecclesiastes 10:16 Woe to you, city, whose king is younger and whose rulers eat in the morning;
Ecclesiastes 10:17 blessed are you, land, whose king is a son of free people and whose rulers will eat at a season in strength and will not be ashamed.
Ecclesiastes 10:18 Through slothfulnesses the framework will be lowered, and through idleness of hands the house will drip.
Ecclesiastes 10:19 For laughter they make bread, and wine gladdens the living, and everything will heed silver.
Ecclesiastes 10:20 And indeed in your consciousness do not curse a king, and in chambers of your bedrooms do not curse a rich person; because a bird of heaven will carry away the voice, and the one having wings will report a word.

## Chapter 11

Ecclesiastes 11:1 Send your bread upon the face of the water, because in abundance of days you will find it;
Ecclesiastes 11:2 give a portion to the seven and indeed to the eight, because you do not know what evil will be upon the earth.
Ecclesiastes 11:3 If the clouds are filled with rain, they pour out upon the earth; and if a tree falls in the south and if in the north, in the place where the tree will fall, there it will be.
Ecclesiastes 11:4 One watching wind will not sow, and one looking among the clouds will not reap,

Ecclesiastes 11:6 In the morning sow your seed, and toward evening let your hand not cease, because you do not know which will succeed, whether this or that, and whether the two together are good.
Ecclesiastes 11:7 And light is sweet, and it is good for the eyes to see the sun;
Ecclesiastes 11:8 because even if the human will live many years, in all of them he will be gladdened and will remember the days of darkness, because they will be many; everything coming is vanity.
Ecclesiastes 11:9 Be gladdened, young man, in your youth, and let your heart make you glad in the days of your youth, and walk in ways of your heart and in the sight of your eyes, and know that for all these things God will bring you into judgment.
Ecclesiastes 11:10 And remove wrath from your heart and turn evil away from your flesh, because youth and unintelligence are vanity.

## Chapter 12

Ecclesiastes 12:1 And remember the one who created you in the days of your youth, before the days of evil come and years arrive in which you will say, I have no pleasure in them;
Ecclesiastes 12:2 before the sun and the light and the moon and the stars are darkened, and the clouds return after the rain;
Ecclesiastes 12:3 on a day when guards of the house may be shaken and men of strength bent, and the women grinding ceased, because they became few, and the women looking through the openings will grow dark;
Ecclesiastes 12:4 and they will close doors in the marketplace in the weakness of the voice of the woman grinding, and he will rise at the voice of the sparrow, and all the daughters of song will be lowered;
Ecclesiastes 12:5 and indeed they will see from a height, and terrors are on the way; and the almond may blossom, and the locust grow fat, and the caper be scattered, because the human went to the house of his eternity, and the mourners circled in the marketplace;
Ecclesiastes 12:6 before a silver cord is overturned, and a golden flower ornament crushed, and a water jar shattered at the spring, and the wheel run together upon the pit,
Ecclesiastes 12:7 and the dust return to the earth as it was, and the spirit return to God who gave it.
Ecclesiastes 12:8 Vanity of vanities, said the Ecclesiast, everything is vanity.
Ecclesiastes 12:9 And furthermore, because the Ecclesiast became wise, he still taught the people knowledge, and an ear will trace out an orderly arrangement of parables.
Ecclesiastes 12:10 The Ecclesiast sought much to find words of pleasure and what has been written of uprightness, words of truth.
Ecclesiastes 12:11 Words of wise people are like the ox-goads and like planted nails, which from the collections were given from one shepherd, and a surplus from them.
Ecclesiastes 12:12 My son, guard yourself against making many books; there is no end, and much study is weariness of flesh.
Ecclesiastes 12:13 The end of a word, the whole is heard: Fear God and keep his commandments, because this is the whole human.
Ecclesiastes 12:14 Because God will bring every work into judgment, in everything overlooked, whether good or evil.
