# Job

The Apostolic Bible. Public domain. https://apostolic-bible.ysys9.chatgpt.site/license.html


## Chapter 1

Job 1:1 There was a certain human in the country of Ausitis whose name was Iob, and that human was true, blameless, righteous, God-revering, abstaining from every evil matter.
Job 1:2 And seven sons and three daughters came to belong to him.
Job 1:3 And his livestock were seven thousand sheep, three thousand camels, five hundred pairs of oxen, five hundred grazing female donkeys, and he had very much service and great works upon the earth; and that human was noble among those from the sun's risings.
Job 1:4 And his sons, going together to one another, made a drinking feast each day, taking along together also their three sisters to eat and drink with them.
Job 1:5 And whenever the days of the drinking feast were completed, Iob sent and purified them, rising in the morning, and offered sacrifices for them according to their number and one calf for sin for their souls; for Iob said, Lest my sons in their thought conceived evil things toward God. Thus therefore Iob did all the days.
Job 1:6 And when this day came, behold, God's angels came to stand before the Lord, and the devil came with them.
Job 1:7 And the Lord said to the devil, From where have you come? And answering the Lord, the devil said, Having gone around the earth and walked about what is under heaven, I am here.
Job 1:8 And the Lord said to him, Did you attend in your thought to my servant Iob, because there is no human like him among those upon the earth, blameless, true, God-revering, abstaining from every evil matter?
Job 1:9 And the devil answered and said before the Lord, Does Iob revere God for nothing?
Job 1:10 Did you not fence around his outside and the inside of his house and the outside of everything belonging to him round about? You blessed the works of his hands and made his livestock many upon the earth.
Job 1:11 But send forth your hand and touch everything he has; surely he will bless you to your face.
Job 1:12 Then the Lord said to the devil, Behold, everything belonging to him I give into your hand, but do not touch him. And the devil went out from the Lord.
Job 1:13 And it was on this day that Iob's sons and his daughters were drinking wine in the house of their older brother.
Job 1:14 And behold, a messenger came to Iob and said to him, The pairs of oxen were plowing, and the female donkeys grazing beside them;
Job 1:15 and the captors came and took them captive and killed the servants with swords; but I alone, having been saved, came to tell you.
Job 1:16 While this one was still speaking, another messenger came and said to Iob, Fire fell from heaven and burned the sheep and likewise devoured the shepherds; and I alone, having been saved, came to tell you.
Job 1:17 While this one was still speaking, another messenger came and said to Iob, The horsemen made three bands against us and encircled the camels and took them captive and killed the servants with swords; but I alone was saved and came to tell you.
Job 1:18 While this one was still speaking, another messenger comes, saying to Iob, While your sons and your daughters were eating and drinking at their older brother's,
Job 1:19 suddenly a great wind came from the wilderness and touched the four corners of the house, and the house fell upon your children, and they died; but I alone was saved and came to tell you.
Job 1:20 Thus Iob rose and tore his garments and sheared the hair of his head and fell to the ground and worshiped and said,
Job 1:21 I myself came out naked from my mother's belly, and naked I will also go away there; the Lord gave, the Lord took away; as it seemed good to the Lord, so it also happened; may the Lord's name be blessed.
Job 1:22 In all these things that had happened to him, Iob sinned in nothing before the Lord and did not give senselessness to God.

## Chapter 2

Job 2:1 And it happened on this day that God's angels came to stand before the Lord, and the devil came in their midst to stand before the Lord.
Job 2:2 And the Lord said to the devil, From where do you come? Then the devil said before the Lord, Having passed through what is under heaven and walked about the whole of it, I am here.
Job 2:3 And the Lord said to the devil, Did you therefore attend to my attendant Iob, because there is no human like him among those upon the earth, innocent, true, blameless, God-revering, abstaining from every evil? And he still holds to innocence; but you said to destroy his possessions for nothing.
Job 2:4 And taking it up, the devil said to the Lord, Skin for skin; everything belonging to a human he will pay out for his soul;
Job 2:5 nevertheless, send forth your hand and touch his bones and his flesh; surely he will bless you to your face.
Job 2:6 And the Lord said to the devil, Behold, I hand him over to you; only preserve his soul.
Job 2:7 And the devil went out from the Lord and struck Iob with an evil sore from feet to head.
Job 2:8 And he took a potsherd to scrape the discharge, and sat upon the dung heap outside the city.
Job 2:9 And when much time had passed, his wife said to him, Until when will you endure, saying, 9a Behold, I wait a little time still, expecting the hope of my salvation? 9b For behold, your memorial has vanished from the earth, sons and daughters, birth pangs and pains of my belly, for whom I labored in vain with toils. 9c And you yourself sit in the putrefaction of worms, spending the night in the open air; 9d and I am a wanderer and servant, going around from place to place and house to house, waiting for the sun, when it will set, so that I may rest from the toils and pains which now constrain me. 9e But say some utterance to the Lord and die.
Job 2:10 But looking at her, he said to her, You spoke like one of the senseless women; if we received good things from the Lord's hand, shall we not bear evil things? In all these things that had happened to him, Iob sinned in nothing with his lips before God.
Job 2:11 And his three friends, having heard all the evil things that came upon him, came to him, each from his own country, Eliphas the king of the Thaimans, Baldad the tyrant of the Sauchites, Sophar the king of the Minaites, and they came to him with one accord to comfort and visit him.
Job 2:12 And seeing him from far away, they did not recognize him, and shouting with a loud voice they wept, each tearing his own robe and sprinkling earth upon themselves.
Job 2:13 They sat beside him seven days and seven nights, and none of them spoke; for they saw that the blow was terrible and very great.

## Chapter 3

Job 3:1 After this Iob opened his mouth
Job 3:2 and cursed his day, saying,
Job 3:3 May the day perish on which I was born, and the night in which they said, Behold, a male.

Job 3:5 and may darkness and a shadow of death take it, may gloom come upon it.

Job 3:12 And why did knees meet me? And why did I nurse at breasts?
Job 3:13 Now, having lain down, I would have been quiet, and having slept, I would have rested
Job 3:14 with kings, counselors of earth, who exulted over swords,
Job 3:15 or with rulers whose gold was much, who filled their houses with silver,
Job 3:16 or like a miscarriage coming out from a mother's womb, or like infants who did not see light.

Job 3:19 small and great are there, and an attendant not fearing his master.
Job 3:20 For why has light been given to those in bitterness, and life to souls in pains?
Job 3:21 Who yearn for death and do not obtain it, digging it out like treasures,

Job 3:23 Death is a rest for a man, for God shut in against him;
Job 3:24 for before my foods a groan comes to me, and I weep, constrained by fear;
Job 3:25 for the fear which I pondered came to me, and what I had feared met me.

## Chapter 4

Job 4:1 And taking it up, Eliphas the Thaimanite says,
Job 4:2 Has it not often been spoken to you in weariness? And who will bear the strength of your utterances?
Job 4:3 For if you admonished many and encouraged a weak person's hands
Job 4:4 and raised up weak people with utterances and put confidence around powerless knees,
Job 4:5 but now trouble comes upon you and touched you, and you were agitated.
Job 4:6 Is not your fear in senselessness, and your hope and the innocence of your way?
Job 4:7 Remember therefore who, being clean, perished, or when true people perished root and all.

Job 4:9 From the Lord's command they will perish, and from the breath of his anger they will vanish.
Job 4:10 A lion's might and a lioness's voice and dragons' exultation were extinguished;
Job 4:11 the ant-lion perished through not having food, and lions' cubs left one another.
Job 4:12 And if any true utterance had occurred in your words, none of these evils would have met you. Will my ear not receive extraordinary things from him?
Job 4:13 And fears and a nocturnal sound, fear falling upon humans,
Job 4:14 and shuddering met me and trembling and greatly shook my bones,
Job 4:15 and a spirit came upon my face, and my hair and flesh bristled.

Job 4:17 For what? Will a mortal be clean before the Lord, or a man blameless from his works?
Job 4:18 If he does not trust his servants, and conceived something crooked against his angels,
Job 4:19 and those dwelling in clay houses, from whom we ourselves also are of the same clay, he struck them in the manner of a moth;
Job 4:20 and from morning until evening they are no longer; through not being able to help themselves they perished;
Job 4:21 for he blew upon them and they were dried up, they perished through not having wisdom.

## Chapter 5

Job 5:1 And call, if anyone will listen to you, or if you will see any of the holy angels.
Job 5:2 For anger also kills a senseless person, and jealousy puts an erring person to death.
Job 5:3 And I have seen senseless people putting down a root, but immediately their dwelling was devoured.
Job 5:4 May their sons be far from salvation, and may they be crushed at inferior people's doors, and there will be no rescuer;
Job 5:5 for what they gathered, righteous people will eat, but they themselves will not be rescued from evils; may their strength be siphoned out.
Job 5:6 For weariness will certainly not come out from the earth, nor will trouble sprout from mountains;
Job 5:7 but a human is born for weariness, and a vulture's young fly in the heights.
Job 5:8 Nevertheless I will beseech the Lord, and I will call upon the Lord, the Master of all,
Job 5:9 the one doing great and untraceable things, glorious and extraordinary things which have no number;
Job 5:10 the one giving rain upon the earth, sending water upon what is under heaven;
Job 5:11 the one making lowly people high and rousing those who have perished;
Job 5:12 altering shrewd people's counsels, and their hands will certainly not do what is true.
Job 5:13 The one catching wise people in prudence, and he confounded the counsel of those with many intrigues;
Job 5:14 by day darkness will meet them, and at midday may they grope as at night.
Job 5:15 And may they perish in war, but may a powerless person come out from a ruler's hand;
Job 5:16 and may a powerless person have hope, but may an unjust person's mouth be blocked.
Job 5:17 And blessed is a human whom the Lord reproved; and do not refuse an admonition of the Almighty.
Job 5:18 For he himself makes one suffer and restores again; he struck, and his hands healed.
Job 5:19 Six times he will rescue you from necessities, and at the seventh evil will certainly not touch you.
Job 5:20 In famine he will deliver you from death, and in war he will release you from the hand of iron.
Job 5:21 He will hide you from the scourge of a tongue, and you will certainly not fear coming evils.
Job 5:22 You will laugh at unjust and lawless people, and you will certainly not fear wild beasts;
Job 5:23 for wild beasts will be at peace with you.
Job 5:24 Then you will know that your house will be at peace, and the dwelling of your tent will certainly not fail.
Job 5:25 And you will know that your seed is much, and your children will be like all the vegetation of the field.
Job 5:26 And you will come into a tomb like ripe grain harvested in season or like a heap of a threshing floor gathered in at its time.
Job 5:27 Behold, these things we traced out thus, these are what we have heard; but know for yourself whether you did anything.

## Chapter 6

Job 6:1 And taking it up, Iob says,
Job 6:2 For if someone weighing would weigh my anger, and lift my pains in a balance together,
Job 6:3 it will indeed be heavier than sand of the seashore; but as it seems, my utterances are worthless.
Job 6:4 For the Lord's arrows are in my body, whose fury drinks up my blood; whenever I begin to speak, they prick me.
Job 6:5 For what? Will a wild donkey cry out for nothing, except seeking foods? And will an ox burst into sound at a manger, having its foods?
Job 6:6 Will bread be eaten without salt? And is there taste in empty utterances?
Job 6:7 For my soul cannot cease; for I see my foods as a stench, like a lion's smell.
Job 6:8 For if he would grant it, and my request would come, and the Lord would grant my hope.
Job 6:9 Having begun, let the Lord wound me, but let him not destroy me utterly.
Job 6:10 And may my city be a tomb, upon whose walls I leaped; I will certainly not spare it; for I did not falsify my God's holy utterances.
Job 6:11 For what is my strength, that I endure? Or what is my time, that my soul holds out?
Job 6:12 Is my strength the strength of stones? Or is my flesh bronze?
Job 6:13 Had I not trusted in him? But help is absent from me.
Job 6:14 Mercy disowned me, and the Lord's visitation overlooked me.
Job 6:15 Those nearest me did not look upon me; like a failing torrent or like a wave they passed me by;
Job 6:16 those who respected me now have fallen upon me like snow or frozen ice;
Job 6:17 as, having melted when heat came, it was not recognized as what it was,
Job 6:18 so I too was abandoned by all, and I perished and became homeless.
Job 6:19 See the ways of the Thaimans, the paths of the Sabans, you who discern;
Job 6:20 and those trusting in cities and possessions will owe shame.
Job 6:21 And moreover you too came upon me mercilessly, so that, seeing my wound, you feared.
Job 6:22 For what? Did I ask you for anything, or do I need the strength from you
Job 6:23 to save me from enemies or deliver me from rulers' hands?
Job 6:24 Teach me, and I will be silent; if I have erred in anything, tell me.
Job 6:25 But as it seems, a true person's utterances are worthless, for I do not ask strength from you;
Job 6:26 nor will your reproof stop me with utterances, for neither will I bear a sound of an utterance from you.
Job 6:27 Only that you fall upon an orphan, and leap upon your friend.
Job 6:28 But now, looking into your faces, I will not lie.
Job 6:29 Sit now, and let there be nothing unjust, and again come together with the righteous person.
Job 6:30 For there is nothing unjust in my tongue; or does my throat not practice understanding?

## Chapter 7

Job 7:1 Is not a human's life upon the earth a trial, and his life like that of a day laborer?
Job 7:2 Or like an attendant fearing his master and obtaining shade, or like a hired worker awaiting his wages.
Job 7:3 Thus I too endured empty months, and nights of pains have been given to me.
Job 7:4 If I lie down, I say, When is day? And whenever I rise, again, When is evening? And I become full of pains from evening until morning.
Job 7:5 And my body is befouled in the putrefaction of worms, and I dissolve clods of earth, scraping them from the discharge.
Job 7:6 And my life is lighter than speech, and has perished in empty hope.
Job 7:7 Remember therefore that my life is breath, and my eye will no longer return to see good.
Job 7:8 An eye of one seeing me will not look upon me; your eyes are upon me, and I am no longer,
Job 7:9 like a cloud cleared away from heaven. For if a human descends into Hades, he will certainly not ascend any longer,
Job 7:10 nor will he certainly return again to his own house, nor will his place recognize him any longer.
Job 7:11 Therefore neither will I spare my mouth; I will speak, being in necessity, I will open the bitterness of my soul, being constrained.
Job 7:12 Am I a sea or a dragon, that you assigned a guard over me?
Job 7:13 I said that my bed will comfort me, and I will bring up a word privately to myself on my couch;
Job 7:14 you terrify me with dreams and appall me with visions.
Job 7:15 You will release my soul from my spirit, and my bones from death.
Job 7:16 For I will not live forever to be long-tempered; depart from me, for my life is empty.
Job 7:17 For what is a human, that you magnified him, or that you attend your mind to him
Job 7:18 or make a visitation of him until morning, and judge him for rest?
Job 7:19 Until when do you not leave me, nor release me until I swallow my saliva in pain?
Job 7:20 If I sinned, what can I do to you, you who know humans' mind? Why did you set me as your opponent, and I am a burden upon you?
Job 7:21 And why did you not make a forgetting of my lawlessness and a cleansing of my sin? But now I will go away into earth, and when you rise early, I am no longer.

## Chapter 8

Job 8:1 And taking it up, Baldad the Sauchite says,
Job 8:2 Until when will you speak these things? The breath of your mouth is wordy.
Job 8:3 Will the Lord act unjustly when judging, or will the one who made everything disturb what is just?
Job 8:4 If your sons sinned before him, he sent them away into the hand of their lawlessness.
Job 8:5 But rise early toward the Lord Almighty, beseeching.
Job 8:6 If you are clean and true, he will listen to your petition, and restore for you a dwelling of righteousness;
Job 8:7 therefore your first things will be few, but your last things untold.
Job 8:8 For ask a former generation, and trace out according to fathers' lineage;
Job 8:9 for we are of yesterday and do not know, for our life upon the earth is a shadow.
Job 8:10 Will these not teach you and report and bring forth utterances from a heart?
Job 8:11 Does papyrus flourish without water, or will a rush grow high without drink?
Job 8:12 While still upon a root and certainly not harvested, before drinking, does not all vegetation dry up?
Job 8:13 Thus therefore will be the last things of all those forgetting the Lord; for an ungodly person's hope will perish.
Job 8:14 For his house will be uninhabited, and his tent will turn out to be a spider's web.
Job 8:15 If he props up his house, it will certainly not stand; and when he takes hold, it will certainly not endure;
Job 8:16 for he is moist under the sun, and from his rottenness his shoot will come out.
Job 8:17 He lies upon a gathering of stones, and will live in the midst of pebbles.
Job 8:18 If it swallows, the place will deny him; you have not seen such things.
Job 8:19 Because such is an ungodly person's overthrow, and from earth he will cause another to sprout.
Job 8:20 For the Lord will certainly not reject the innocent person, but he will not receive any gift of an ungodly person.
Job 8:21 And he will fill true people's mouth with laughter, and their lips with confession;
Job 8:22 but their enemies will clothe themselves with shame, and an ungodly person's dwelling will not exist.

## Chapter 9

Job 9:1 And taking it up, Iob says,
Job 9:2 In truth I know that it is thus; for how will a mortal be righteous before the Lord?
Job 9:3 For if he wishes to contend in judgment with him, he will certainly not listen to him, so that he may not contradict one word of his out of a thousand.
Job 9:4 For he is wise in thought, both mighty and great; who, becoming hard before him, endured?
Job 9:5 The one making mountains old, and they do not know, the one overturning them in anger;
Job 9:6 the one shaking what is under heaven from foundations, and its pillars are shaken;
Job 9:7 the one speaking to the sun, and it does not rise, and he seals up the stars;
Job 9:8 the one stretching heaven alone and walking upon sea as upon ground;
Job 9:9 the one making the Pleiad and the Evening Star and Arcturus and chambers of the south;
Job 9:10 the one doing great and untraceable things, glorious and extraordinary things which have no number.
Job 9:11 If he passes over me, I will certainly not see; and if he passes me by, neither thus did I know.
Job 9:12 If he takes away, who will turn him back? Or who will say to him, What did you do?
Job 9:13 For he himself has turned away anger; by him the sea creatures under heaven were bent.
Job 9:14 And if he listens to me, surely he will distinguish my utterances.
Job 9:15 For even if I am righteous, he will not listen to me; I will beseech his judgment;
Job 9:16 and if I call and he listens, I do not believe that he has heard me.
Job 9:17 Will he crush me with gloom? And he has made my fractures many for nothing.
Job 9:18 For he does not allow me to breathe, and filled me with bitterness.
Job 9:19 For indeed he prevails in strength; who therefore will resist his judgment?
Job 9:20 For if I am righteous, my mouth will act ungodly; and if I am blameless, I will turn out crooked.
Job 9:21 For whether I acted ungodly, I do not know in my soul, except that my life is taken away.
Job 9:22 Therefore I said, Anger destroys a great man and a ruler,
Job 9:23 because worthless people are in an extraordinary death, but righteous people are laughed at;
Job 9:24 for they have been handed into an ungodly person's hands. He covers the faces of its judges; but if not he, who is it?
Job 9:25 And my life is lighter than a runner; they ran away and did not see.
Job 9:26 And is there a track of a way for ships, or for an eagle flying, seeking food?
Job 9:27 For if I speak, I will forget while speaking; bending down in face, I will groan.
Job 9:28 I am shaken in all my limbs, for I know that you will not leave me innocent.
Job 9:29 And since I am ungodly, why did I not die?
Job 9:30 For if I wash myself with snow and purify myself with clean hands,
Job 9:31 you dipped me sufficiently in filth, and my robe abhorred me.
Job 9:32 For you are not a human like me with whom I will contend in judgment, so that we may come with one accord into judgment.
Job 9:33 Would that there were our mediator, both reproving and hearing between both;
Job 9:34 let him remove the rod from me, and let his fear not whirl me about,
Job 9:35 and I will certainly not fear, but will speak; for I am not conscious thus.

## Chapter 10

Job 10:1 Weary in my soul, groaning, I will release my utterances upon him; I will speak, constrained by bitterness of my soul,
Job 10:2 and say to the Lord, Do not teach me to act ungodly; and why did you judge me thus?
Job 10:3 Is it good for you if I act unjustly, that I disown works of your hands, but you attended to ungodly people's counsel?
Job 10:4 Do you look as a mortal sees, or will you look as a human sees?
Job 10:5 Is your life human, or your years a man's?
Job 10:6 Because you sought out my lawlessness and traced out my sins.
Job 10:7 For you know that I did not act ungodly; but who is the one rescuing from your hands?
Job 10:8 Your hands fashioned me and made me; after these things, changing, you struck me.
Job 10:9 Remember that you fashioned me as clay, and you turn me back into earth again.
Job 10:10 Did you not milk me like milk, and curdle me like cheese?
Job 10:11 You clothed me in skin and flesh, and threaded me with bones and sinews.
Job 10:12 And you placed life and mercy with me, and your visitation guarded my spirit.
Job 10:13 Having these things in yourself, I know that you can do everything, and nothing is impossible for you.
Job 10:14 For if I sin, you guard me, and you have not made me innocent from lawlessness.
Job 10:15 For if I am ungodly, woe to me; and if I am righteous, I cannot lift my head, for I am full of dishonor.
Job 10:16 For I am hunted like a lion for slaughter, and changing again you terribly destroy me,
Job 10:17 renewing my examination against me; and you treated me with great anger, and brought trials upon me.
Job 10:18 Why therefore did you bring me out from a belly, and I did not die, and an eye did not see me,
Job 10:19 and I became as though not existing? For why was I not carried from womb to tomb?
Job 10:20 Is not the time of my life little? Allow me to rest a little
Job 10:21 before I go where I will not return, into a dark and gloomy land,
Job 10:22 into a land of everlasting darkness, where there is no brightness nor seeing of mortals' life.

## Chapter 11

Job 11:1 And taking it up, Sophar the Minaite says,
Job 11:2 The one saying many things will also hear in reply; or does the fluent speaker also think he is righteous? Blessed is one born of a woman, short-lived.
Job 11:3 Do not become abundant in utterances, for there is no one contending in judgment with you.
Job 11:4 For do not say, I am clean in works and blameless before him.
Job 11:5 But how might the Lord speak to you? And he will open his lips with you.
Job 11:6 Then he will report to you the power of wisdom, because he will be double the things with you; and then you will know that things worthy of what you have sinned befell you from the Lord.
Job 11:7 Will you find a track of the Lord, or did you reach the last things which the Almighty made?
Job 11:8 Heaven is high, and what will you do? And what do you know deeper than the things in Hades?
Job 11:9 Or longer than the measure of earth or the breadth of sea?
Job 11:10 And if he overturns everything, who will say to him, What did you do?
Job 11:11 For he himself knows lawless people's works, and seeing improper things he will not overlook them.
Job 11:12 But a human vainly swims in words, and a mortal born of a woman is like a wilderness donkey.
Job 11:13 For if you made your heart clean, and turn your hands upward toward him,
Job 11:14 if anything lawless is in your hands, make it far from you, and let injustice not lodge in your dwelling.
Job 11:15 For thus your face will shine like clean water, and you will put off filth and certainly not fear;
Job 11:16 and you will forget weariness like a wave that passed, and will not be frightened;
Job 11:17 and your prayer is like the morning star, and from midday life will rise for you;
Job 11:18 and you will be confident because you have hope, and from anxiety and concern peace will appear for you.
Job 11:19 For you will be quiet, and there will be no one warring against you; and many, having changed, will beseech you.
Job 11:20 But salvation will abandon them; for their hope is destruction, and ungodly people's eyes will melt.

## Chapter 12

Job 12:1 And taking it up, Iob says,
Job 12:2 Then you are humans; surely wisdom will die with you.
Job 12:3 Indeed I too have a heart like you.
Job 12:4 For a righteous and blameless man became a mockery;
Job 12:5 for at an appointed time he had been prepared to fall under others, and his houses to be ravaged by lawless people.
Job 12:6 Nevertheless let no one, being evil, trust that he will be innocent, as many as provoke the Lord, as though there will not also be an examination of them.
Job 12:7 But now ask quadrupeds if they may tell you, and birds of heaven if they may report to you;
Job 12:8 and relate to earth if it may tell you, and the fish of the sea will explain to you.
Job 12:9 Who did not know among all these things that the Lord's hand did these things?
Job 12:10 Is not the soul of all the living and the spirit of every human in his hand?
Job 12:11 For an ear distinguishes utterances, and a throat tastes foods.
Job 12:12 In much time is wisdom, and in much life understanding.
Job 12:13 With him are wisdom and power, to him belong counsel and understanding.
Job 12:14 If he casts down, who will build? If he closes against humans, who will open?
Job 12:15 If he restrains the water, he will dry the earth; but if he releases it, he destroyed it, overturning it.
Job 12:16 With him are dominion and strength, to him belong knowledge and understanding.
Job 12:17 Leading counselors captive, and he confounded judges of earth.
Job 12:18 Seating kings upon thrones, and he bound their loins with a belt.
Job 12:19 Sending priests away captive, and he overturned rulers of earth.
Job 12:20 Changing faithful people's lips, and he knew elders' understanding.
Job 12:21 Pouring dishonor upon rulers, and he healed lowly people.
Job 12:22 Uncovering deep things from darkness, and he brought a shadow of death into light.
Job 12:23 Leading nations astray and destroying them, laying nations low and guiding them.
Job 12:24 Changing the hearts of rulers of earth, and he led them astray on a way which they did not know;
Job 12:25 may they grope in darkness and not light, and may they be led astray like the drunkard.

## Chapter 13

Job 13:1 Behold, my eye has seen these things and my ear has heard;
Job 13:2 and I know as much as you also know, and I am not less understanding than you.
Job 13:3 Nevertheless I will speak to the Lord, and I will argue before him if he wishes.
Job 13:4 But you are unjust physicians and all healers of evils.
Job 13:5 May you be silent, and it will turn out as wisdom for you.
Job 13:6 Hear the argument of my mouth, and attend to the judgment of my lips.
Job 13:7 Do you not speak before the Lord, and utter deceit before him?
Job 13:8 Will you shrink back? But become judges yourselves.
Job 13:9 It is indeed good if he traces you out; for if, doing everything, you will be added to him,
Job 13:10 he will reprove you no less; and if you also secretly admire faces,
Job 13:11 will not his terrors whirl you about, and fear from him fall upon you?
Job 13:12 And your exultation will turn out like ashes, and the body clay.
Job 13:13 Be silent, so that I may speak and rest from wrath,
Job 13:14 taking up my flesh with my teeth, and I will put my soul in my hand.
Job 13:15 If the ruler subdues me, since he has also begun, surely I will speak and argue before him;
Job 13:16 and this will turn out as salvation for me, for deceit will not enter before him.
Job 13:17 Hear, hear my utterances; for I will report while you hear.
Job 13:18 Behold, I am near my judgment, I know that I will appear righteous.
Job 13:19 For who is the one who will contend in judgment with me? Because now I will be silent and fail.
Job 13:20 And you will grant me two things; then I will not hide from your face;
Job 13:21 keep your hand away from me, and let your fear not appall me.
Job 13:22 Then you will call and I will listen to you; or you will speak and I will give you an answer.
Job 13:23 How many are my sins and my lawless deeds? Teach me what they are.
Job 13:24 Why do you hide from me, and regard me as opposed to you?
Job 13:25 Will you be wary as of a leaf moved by wind, or are you opposed to me as to grass carried by a breeze?
Job 13:26 Because you wrote evil things against me, and put sins of youth around me,
Job 13:27 and put my foot in a restraint, and guarded all my works, and reached the roots of my feet;
Job 13:28 which grows old like a wineskin or like a moth-eaten garment.

## Chapter 14

Job 14:1 For a mortal born of a woman is short-lived and full of anger,
Job 14:2 or like a flower that blossomed he fell away, and fled like a shadow and will certainly not stand.
Job 14:3 Did you not also take account of this one and make him enter into judgment before you?
Job 14:4 For who will be clean from filth? But no one.
Job 14:5 Even if his life upon the earth is one day, and his months are numbered with you, you set a time, and he will certainly not exceed it.
Job 14:6 Depart from him, so that he may be quiet and be pleased with life like the hired worker.
Job 14:7 For a tree has hope; for if it is cut down, it will blossom again, and its shoot will certainly not fail;
Job 14:8 for if its root grows old in earth and its stem dies in rock,
Job 14:9 from the fragrance of water it will blossom, and make a harvest like a newly planted tree.
Job 14:10 But a man, having died, went away, and a mortal, having fallen, is no longer.
Job 14:11 For in time a sea dwindles, and a river, having become desolate, dried up;
Job 14:12 but a human, having lain down, will certainly not rise until heaven is no longer stitched together; and they will not be awakened from their sleep.
Job 14:13 For would that you guarded me in Hades, and hid me until your anger ceases, and appoint me a time in which you may make remembrance of me.
Job 14:14 For if a human dies, he will live, having completed days of his life; I will endure until I come to be again.
Job 14:15 Then you will call and I will listen to you, and do not reject the works of your hands.
Job 14:16 And you numbered my practices, and none of my sins will certainly pass you by;
Job 14:17 and you sealed my lawless deeds in a purse, and marked whether I transgressed anything unwillingly.
Job 14:18 And yet a falling mountain will fall apart, and a rock will be worn away from its place;
Job 14:19 waters smoothed stones, and waters flooded the flat places of the earth's mound; and you destroyed a human's endurance.
Job 14:20 You thrust him utterly, and he went away; you set your face upon him and sent him away;
Job 14:21 and when his sons become many, he does not know, and if they become few, he does not understand;
Job 14:22 except his flesh suffered, and his soul mourned.

## Chapter 15

Job 15:1 And taking it up, Eliphas the Thaimanite says,
Job 15:2 Will a wise person give an answer of understanding of spirit, and filled trouble of a belly,
Job 15:3 arguing with utterances with which one ought not, with words in which there is no benefit?
Job 15:4 Did you not also reject fear, and complete such utterances before the Lord?
Job 15:5 You are guilty by your mouth's utterances, nor did you distinguish rulers' utterances;
Job 15:6 may your own mouth reprove you and not I, and your lips will testify against you.
Job 15:7 For what? Did you become the first of humans? Or were you fixed before dunes?
Job 15:8 Have you heard the Lord's ordinance, and did wisdom reach you?
Job 15:9 For what do you know that we do not know? Or what do you understand that we do not also?
Job 15:10 Indeed both an elder and an ancient one are among us, weightier in days than your father.
Job 15:11 You have been whipped little for what you have sinned; you have spoken greatly beyond measure.
Job 15:12 What did your heart dare, or what did your eyes bring on,
Job 15:13 that you burst into wrath before the Lord, and brought such utterances out from your mouth?
Job 15:14 For who is a mortal that he will be blameless, or how will one born of a woman be righteous?
Job 15:15 If he does not trust holy ones, and heaven is not clean before him.
Job 15:16 But leave aside one abhorred and unclean, a man drinking injustices like a drink.
Job 15:17 And I will report to you; hear me; what indeed I have seen I will report to you,
Job 15:18 what wise people will say, and they did not hide their fathers;
Job 15:19 to them alone the earth was given, and no foreigner came upon them.
Job 15:20 An ungodly person's whole life is in concern, and numbered years given to a ruler,
Job 15:21 and his fear in his ears; whenever he thinks he is already at peace, his overthrow will come.
Job 15:22 Let him not trust that he will turn back from darkness; for he has already been appointed into the hands of iron,
Job 15:23 and has been assigned as food for vultures; and he knows in himself that he remains for a fall. And a dark day will whirl him about,
Job 15:24 and necessity and affliction will hold him like a general falling in the front rank.
Job 15:25 Because he has raised hands before the Lord, and acted stiff-necked before the Lord Almighty,
Job 15:26 and ran against him with arrogance in the thickness of the back of his shield,
Job 15:27 because he covered his face in his fat and made a covering upon his thighs.
Job 15:28 And may he lodge in deserted cities, and enter uninhabited houses; and what those people prepared, others will carry away.
Job 15:29 Neither will he certainly be made rich, nor will his possessions certainly remain; he will certainly not cast a shadow upon the earth,
Job 15:30 nor will he escape darkness; may wind wither his shoot, and may his flower fall away.
Job 15:31 Let him not trust that he will endure, for empty things will turn out for him;
Job 15:32 his cutting will be destroyed before its time, and his shoot will certainly not grow thick;
Job 15:33 and may he be harvested like an unripe grape before its time, and fall away like an olive's flower.
Job 15:34 For an ungodly person's testimony is death, and fire will burn bribe-takers' houses.
Job 15:35 And in the womb he will conceive pains, and empty things will turn out for him, and his belly will bear deceit.

## Chapter 16

Job 16:1 And taking it up, Iob says,
Job 16:2 I have heard many such things; all are comforters of evils.
Job 16:3 For what? Is there an order to utterances of wind? Or what will trouble you, that you answer?
Job 16:4 I too will speak like you, if indeed your soul were in place of mine; then I will leap upon you with utterances, and shake my head against you;
Job 16:5 and may there be strength in my mouth, and I will not spare movement of lips.
Job 16:6 For if I speak, I will not suffer the wound; and if I also keep silent, how much less will I be wounded?
Job 16:7 But now he has made me exhausted, foolish, rotten,
Job 16:8 and you seized me; it became a testimony; and my falsehood rose within me, it answered against my face.
Job 16:9 Having used anger, he cast me down, he gnashed his teeth against me, arrows of his raiders fell upon me.
Job 16:10 With points of eyes he leaped upon me, with a sharp thing he struck me on the cheek, and with one accord they rushed upon me.
Job 16:11 For the Lord handed me into an unjust person's hands, and cast me upon ungodly people;
Job 16:12 while I was at peace he scattered me, taking me by the hair he tore it out, he set me like a target.
Job 16:13 They encircled me with spears, throwing at my kidneys, not sparing, they poured my gall upon the earth;
Job 16:14 they cast me down, fall upon fall, they ran toward me, being powerful.
Job 16:15 I sewed sackcloth upon my hide, and my might was extinguished in earth.
Job 16:16 My belly has been burned from weeping, and upon my eyelids is a shadow.
Job 16:17 And nothing unjust was in my hands, and my prayer is clean.
Job 16:18 Earth, do not cover over the blood of my flesh, nor let there be a place for my cry.
Job 16:19 And now behold, my witness is in heavens, and the one knowing with me in the highest places.
Job 16:20 May my petition reach the Lord, and may my eye drip before him.
Job 16:21 And may there be an argument for a man before the Lord, and a son of a human for his neighbor.
Job 16:22 And numbered years have come, and I will go on a way on which I will not return.

## Chapter 17

Job 17:1 I perish, carried by a wind, and need burial and do not obtain it.
Job 17:2 I implore, being weary, and having done what?
Job 17:3 And strangers stole my possessions. Who is this one? Let him be bound to my hand.
Job 17:4 Because you hid their heart from prudence, therefore you will certainly not exalt them.
Job 17:5 He will report evils to the portion, and my eyes melted over sons.
Job 17:6 And you made me a byword among nations, and I turned out a laughingstock for them;
Job 17:7 for my eyes have been hardened from anger, I have been greatly besieged by all.
Job 17:8 Amazement held true people at this; and may a righteous person rise against a lawless person;
Job 17:9 and may a faithful person hold his own way, and one clean in hands take up confidence.
Job 17:10 Nevertheless all of you press on, and come now; for I find no truth among you.
Job 17:11 My days passed in a stench, and the joints of my heart were torn.
Job 17:12 They made night into day, light near from the face of darkness.
Job 17:13 For if I endure, Hades is my house, and in gloom my bedding has been spread.
Job 17:14 I called upon death to be my father, and rottenness my mother and sister.
Job 17:15 Where therefore is my hope any longer? Will I see my good things?
Job 17:16 Will they descend with me into Hades, or will we descend with one accord upon a mound?

## Chapter 18

Job 18:1 And taking it up, Baldad the Sauchite says,
Job 18:2 Until when will you not cease? Hold back, so that we ourselves also may speak.
Job 18:3 Why have we been silent like quadrupeds before you?
Job 18:4 Anger has treated you. For what? If you die, is what is under heaven uninhabited? Or will mountains be overturned from foundations?
Job 18:5 And ungodly people's light will be extinguished, and their flame will not come forth;
Job 18:6 his light is darkness in a dwelling, and the lamp over him will be extinguished.
Job 18:7 May the least people hunt his possessions, and may his counsel trip him.
Job 18:8 And his foot has been cast into a trap; may he be entangled in a net.
Job 18:9 And may traps come upon him; it will make thirsty ones prevail against him.
Job 18:10 His cord has been hidden in the earth, and his capture upon paths.
Job 18:11 May pains destroy him round about, and may many come around his feet in severe famine.
Job 18:12 And an extraordinary fall has been prepared for him.
Job 18:13 May the branches of his feet be devoured, and death will devour his beautiful things.
Job 18:14 And may healing be torn out from his dwelling, and may necessity hold him by a royal charge.
Job 18:15 It will dwell in his tent in his night, his comely things will be strewn with sulfur.
Job 18:16 Below, his roots will be dried, and above, his harvest will fall down.
Job 18:17 May his memorial perish from earth, and a name belongs to him upon the face outside.
Job 18:18 May he thrust him from light into darkness.
Job 18:19 He will not be known among his people, nor his house saved in what is under heaven, but others will live in his things.
Job 18:20 The last groaned over him, and amazement held the first.
Job 18:21 These are unjust people's houses, and this the place of those not knowing the Lord.

## Chapter 19

Job 19:1 And taking it up, Iob says,
Job 19:2 Until when will you make my soul weary and pull me down with words?
Job 19:3 Know only that the Lord made me thus; you speak against me, not respecting me you press upon me.
Job 19:4 Yes indeed, in truth I erred, and error lodges with me,
Job 19:4 a to speak an utterance which one ought not, and my utterances wander and are not in season.
Job 19:5 But leave aside that you magnify yourselves over me, and leap upon me with reproach.
Job 19:6 Know therefore that it is the Lord who disturbed me, and he raised his stronghold against me.
Job 19:7 Behold, I laugh at reproach and will not speak; I will cry out, and judgment is nowhere.
Job 19:8 I have been built around on all sides and will certainly not pass through, he set darkness before my face.
Job 19:9 And he stripped glory from me, and took a crown away from my head.
Job 19:10 He tore me apart round about, and I went away; and he cut out my hope like a tree.
Job 19:11 And he treated me terribly with anger, and regarded me like an enemy.
Job 19:12 And his trials came with one accord upon me on my ways, ambushers encircled me.
Job 19:13 And my brothers departed from me, they knew strangers rather than me; and my friends have become merciless.
Job 19:14 Those nearest me did not acknowledge me, and those knowing my name forgot me.
Job 19:15 Neighbors of the house and my maidservants, I was a foreigner before them.
Job 19:16 I called my attendant, and he did not listen; and my mouth was beseeching.
Job 19:17 And I implored my wife, and called upon sons of my concubines, flattering;
Job 19:18 but they rejected me forever; whenever I rise, they speak against me.
Job 19:19 And those knowing me abhorred me; those whom I had loved rose against me.
Job 19:20 My flesh rotted in my skin, and my bones are held in teeth.
Job 19:21 Have mercy on me, have mercy on me, friends; for it is the Lord's hand that touched me.
Job 19:22 And why do you pursue me like the Lord also, and are not filled from my flesh?
Job 19:23 For who might grant that my utterances be written, and set in a book forever,
Job 19:24 with an iron stylus and lead, or engraved in rocks?
Job 19:25 For I know that the one about to release me upon earth is everlasting.
Job 19:26 May he raise my skin which endures these things; for these things were accomplished for me by the Lord,
Job 19:27 which I know with myself, which my eye has seen and not another; and everything has been accomplished for me in my bosom.
Job 19:28 And if you also will say, What will we say before him? And we will find a root of a word in him;
Job 19:29 be wary now, you too, of a covering; for wrath will come upon lawless people, and then they will know where their material is.

## Chapter 20

Job 20:1 And taking it up, Sophar the Minaite says,
Job 20:2 I did not suppose you would contradict these things thus, and you do not understand more than I also.
Job 20:3 I will hear discipline of my shame, and a spirit from understanding answers me.
Job 20:4 Did you not know these things from of old, from when a human was set upon the earth?
Job 20:5 For ungodly people's gladness is an extraordinary fall, and lawless people's joy destruction,
Job 20:6 if his gifts ascend into heaven and his sacrifice touches clouds.
Job 20:7 For whenever he thinks he has already been established, then he will perish utterly; and those seeing him will say, Where is he?
Job 20:8 Like a dream flown away he will certainly not be found, and he flew like a nocturnal apparition.
Job 20:9 An eye looked upon him and will not do so again, and his place will no longer perceive him.
Job 20:10 May inferior people destroy his sons, and may his hands kindle pains.
Job 20:11 His bones were filled with his youth, and it will lie with him upon a mound.
Job 20:12 If wickedness is sweetened in his mouth, he will hide it under his tongue;
Job 20:13 he will not spare it and will not abandon it and will hold it in the midst of his throat.
Job 20:14 And he will certainly not be able to help himself; an asp's gall is in his belly.
Job 20:15 Wealth gathered unjustly will be vomited out; an angel will draw it out from his house.
Job 20:16 And may he suck dragons' fury, and may a snake's tongue kill him.
Job 20:17 May he not see milking of grazing herds, nor pastures of honey and butter.
Job 20:18 For empty and vain things he labored for wealth, from which he will not taste, like something astringent, unchewable, unswallowable.
Job 20:19 For he crushed many powerless people's houses, and seized a dwelling and did not establish it.
Job 20:20 There is no salvation for him in possessions, in his desire he will not be saved.
Job 20:21 There is no remnant of his foods; therefore his good things will not blossom.
Job 20:22 And whenever he thinks he has already been filled, he will be afflicted, and every necessity will come upon him.
Job 20:23 If somehow he might fill his belly, may he send upon him a fury of anger, may he rain pains upon him;
Job 20:24 and he will certainly not be saved from the hand of iron, may a bronze bow wound him;
Job 20:25 and may an arrow pass through his body, and may lightnings walk in his dwellings; fears are upon him.
Job 20:26 And may all darkness remain for him; an unkindled fire will devour him, and may a stranger harm his house.
Job 20:27 And may heaven uncover his lawless deeds, and earth rise against him.
Job 20:28 May destruction drag his house utterly away, may a day of anger come upon him.
Job 20:29 This is the portion of an ungodly human from the Lord, and the estate of possessions belonging to him from the overseer.

## Chapter 21

Job 21:1 And taking it up, Iob says,
Job 21:2 Hear, hear my words, so that this comfort from you may not be mine.
Job 21:3 Bear me, and I will speak, then you will not laugh at me.
Job 21:4 For what? Is my argument against a human? Or why will I not be wrathful?
Job 21:5 Look at me and marvel, putting a hand upon a cheek.
Job 21:6 For if I remember, I am agitated, and pains hold my flesh.
Job 21:7 Why do ungodly people live, and have grown old even in wealth?
Job 21:8 Their seed is according to their soul, and their children before their eyes.
Job 21:9 Their houses flourish, and fear is nowhere, and there is no scourge from the Lord upon them.
Job 21:10 Their cow did not give birth prematurely, and their pregnant one was preserved and did not miscarry.
Job 21:11 And they remain like everlasting sheep, and their children play,
Job 21:12 taking up a psaltery and lyre, and they are gladdened by a sound of a psalm.
Job 21:13 And they completed their life amid good things, and slept in the rest of Hades.
Job 21:14 And he says to the Lord, Depart from me, I do not wish to know your ways;
Job 21:15 what is the Sufficient One, that we will serve him? And what benefit, that we will meet him?
Job 21:16 For their good things were in their hands, and he does not look upon ungodly people's works.
Job 21:17 Nevertheless ungodly people's lamp also will be extinguished, and their overthrow will come upon them, and birth pangs will hold them from anger.
Job 21:18 And they will be like chaff before wind, or like dust which a tempest took away.
Job 21:19 May his possessions abandon sons; he will repay him and he will know.
Job 21:20 May his eyes see his own slaughter, and may he not be preserved from the Lord;
Job 21:21 because what pleasure has he in his house after him? And the numbers of his months were divided.
Job 21:22 Is it not the Lord who teaches understanding and knowledge? And he himself will distinguish murders.
Job 21:23 This one will die in the dominion of his simplicity, and wholly enjoying himself and flourishing;
Job 21:24 and his inward parts full of fat, and his marrow is poured out.
Job 21:25 But that one dies through bitterness of soul, having eaten nothing good.
Job 21:26 And with one accord they lie upon earth, and rottenness covered them.
Job 21:27 So I know you, that you press upon me with daring;
Job 21:28 because you will say, Where is a ruler's house? And where is the shelter of ungodly people's tents?
Job 21:29 Ask those passing along a way, and you will not disown their signs;
Job 21:30 because the evil person is spared for a day of destruction, they will be led away for a day of his anger.
Job 21:31 Who will report his way to his face? And he himself did it, who will repay him?
Job 21:32 And he himself was carried into tombs and kept vigil upon a coffin.
Job 21:33 Pebbles of a torrent were sweetened for him, and after him every human will go away, and before him innumerable ones.
Job 21:34 And how do you comfort me with empty things? And my ceasing from you is nothing.

## Chapter 22

Job 22:1 And taking it up, Eliphas the Thaimanite says,
Job 22:2 Is it not the Lord who teaches understanding and knowledge?
Job 22:3 For what does the Lord care if you were blameless in works? Or what benefit, that you make your way simple?
Job 22:4 Will he, taking account of you, reprove you and enter into judgment together with you?
Job 22:5 Is not your wickedness much, and are not your sins innumerable?
Job 22:6 And you took pledges from your brothers for nothing, and took away naked people's clothing;
Job 22:7 nor did you give thirsty people water to drink, but deprived hungry people of a morsel;
Job 22:8 and you admired certain people's face, and settled those upon the earth;
Job 22:9 and you sent widows away empty, and harmed orphans.
Job 22:10 Therefore traps encircled you, and an extraordinary war agitated you;
Job 22:11 light turned into darkness for you, and water covered you as you lay down.
Job 22:12 Does not the one dwelling in the heights look upon things, and he humbled those carried by arrogance?
Job 22:13 And you said, What did the Strong One know? Will he judge through gloom?
Job 22:14 Clouds are his hiding place, and he will not be seen, and he will pass through the circle of heaven.
Job 22:15 Will you keep an everlasting path which unjust men trod,
Job 22:16 who were seized before their time? Their foundations are a flowing river,
Job 22:17 those saying, What will the Lord do to us? Or what will the Almighty bring upon us?
Job 22:18 But he filled their houses with good things, and ungodly people's counsel is far from him.
Job 22:19 Righteous people saw and laughed, and a blameless person sneered.
Job 22:20 Unless their substance vanished, and fire will devour their remnant.
Job 22:21 Become firm now, if you endure; then your fruit will be amid good things.
Job 22:22 And receive a declaration from his mouth and take up his utterances in your heart.
Job 22:23 And if you turn and humble yourself before the Lord, you made injustice far from your dwelling.
Job 22:24 You will place upon a mound in rock, and like rock torrents of Ophir.
Job 22:25 Therefore the Almighty will be your helper against enemies, and will render you clean like silver tried by fire.
Job 22:26 Then you will speak frankly before the Lord, looking up into heaven cheerfully;
Job 22:27 and when you pray to him, he will listen to you, and grant you to repay the vows;
Job 22:28 and he will restore for you a dwelling of righteousness, and upon your ways there will be brightness.
Job 22:29 Because he humbled him, and you will say, He acted proudly, and he will save one downcast in eyes;
Job 22:30 he will deliver an innocent person, and be preserved through your clean hands.

## Chapter 23

Job 23:1 And taking it up, Iob says,
Job 23:2 And indeed I know that the argument is out of my hand, and his hand has become heavy upon my groaning.
Job 23:3 And who therefore might know that I would find him and come to the end?
Job 23:4 And may I speak my own judgment, and fill my mouth with arguments;
Job 23:5 and may I know utterances which he will say to me, and perceive what he will report to me.
Job 23:6 And if he will come upon me with much strength, then he will not treat me with a threat;
Job 23:7 for truth and argument are from him, and may he bring my judgment out to the end.
Job 23:8 For I will go to the first things and am no longer; and what do I know of the last things?
Job 23:9 When he worked on the left, I did not grasp him; he will cover the right, and I will not see.
Job 23:10 For he already knows my way, and he tested me like gold.
Job 23:11 And I will go out in his commandments; for I kept his ways and will certainly not turn aside
Job 23:12 from his commandments, and I will certainly not pass beyond, and in my bosom I hid his utterances.
Job 23:13 And if he himself also judged thus, who is the one who contradicted him? For what he himself wished, he also did.
Job 23:15 Therefore I am agitated at him; and being admonished, I was concerned about him.
Job 23:15 a At this may I be agitated before his face; I will consider and be frightened by him.
Job 23:16 And the Lord softened my heart, and the Almighty agitated me.
Job 23:17 For I did not know that darkness would come upon me, and gloom covered before my face.

## Chapter 24

Job 24:1 And why did hours escape the Lord's notice,
Job 24:2 and ungodly people crossed a boundary, seizing a flock with a shepherd?
Job 24:3 They led away orphans' beast of burden, and took a widow's ox as a pledge.
Job 24:4 They turned powerless people aside from a righteous way, the meek of earth hid with one accord.
Job 24:5 And they went out like donkeys in a field, going forth upon their own business beyond me; bread was sweetened for him for younger ones.
Job 24:6 They harvested a field not theirs before its time; and powerless people worked ungodly people's vineyards without wages and without food.
Job 24:7 They made many naked people lie down without garments, and took away the clothing of their soul.
Job 24:8 They are wet from drops of mountains; through not having shelter they embraced a rock.
Job 24:9 They seized an orphan from a breast, and humbled a fallen person.
Job 24:10 And they unjustly made naked people lie down, and took a morsel away from hungry people.
Job 24:11 In narrow places they unjustly ambushed, and did not know a righteous way.
Job 24:12 Those who were being cast out from a city and their own houses, and infants' soul groaned greatly, but why has he himself not made a visitation of these things?
Job 24:13 While they were upon earth, they did not recognize, and did not know a way of righteousness, nor walk its paths.
Job 24:14 And knowing their works, he handed them over into darkness, and at night he will be like a thief.
Job 24:15 And an adulterer's eye watched for darkness, saying, An eye will not perceive me, and he made a hiding of his face.
Job 24:16 He dug through houses in darkness; by day they sealed themselves, they did not recognize light;
Job 24:17 because with one accord the morning is a shadow of death for them, because he will recognize disturbances of a shadow of death.
Job 24:18 He is light upon the face of water; may their portion upon earth be cursed.
Job 24:19 And may their plants upon earth appear dry; for they seized orphans' armful.
Job 24:20 Then his sin was remembered, and like a mist of dew he became invisible; and may what he did be repaid to him, and may every unjust person be shattered like incurable wood.
Job 24:21 For he did not treat a barren woman well and did not show mercy to a woman,
Job 24:22 and with wrath he overturned powerless people. Therefore when he rises, he will certainly not trust in his own life;
Job 24:23 having become weak, let him not hope to be made healthy, but he will fall by sickness.
Job 24:24 For his elevation harmed many; and he withered like mallow in heat or like an ear of grain falling by itself from a stalk.
Job 24:25 But if not, who is the one saying I speak falsely and will make my utterances nothing?

## Chapter 25

Job 25:1 And taking it up, Baldad the Sauchite says,
Job 25:2 For what prelude or fear is from him, the one making the whole in the highest place?
Job 25:3 For might anyone suppose there is delay for raiders? And upon whom will an ambush from him not come?
Job 25:4 For how will a mortal be righteous before the Lord? Or who born of a woman might purify himself?
Job 25:5 If he commands the moon, and it does not shine; and stars are not clean before him.
Job 25:6 But leave aside a human, rottenness, and a son of a human, a worm.

## Chapter 26

Job 26:1 And taking it up, Iob says,
Job 26:2 To whom do you attach yourself, or whom are you about to help? Is it not one whose strength is much and whose arm is mighty?
Job 26:3 Whom have you advised? Is it not one who has all wisdom? Or whom will you follow? Is it not one who has greatest power?
Job 26:4 To whom did you report utterances? And whose breath is that which came out from you?
Job 26:5 Will giants be brought to birth beneath water and its neighbors?
Job 26:6 Hades is naked before him, and destruction has no covering.
Job 26:7 Stretching north upon nothing, hanging earth upon nothing;
Job 26:8 binding water in his clouds, and a cloud was not torn beneath it;
Job 26:9 the one holding the face of a throne, spreading his cloud upon it.
Job 26:10 He circled a command upon the face of water until the completion of light with darkness.
Job 26:11 Heaven's pillars spread out and were confounded by his rebuke.
Job 26:12 With strength he quieted the sea, and with knowledge wounded the sea creature;
Job 26:13 and heaven's bolts fear him, and by command he put an apostate dragon to death.
Job 26:14 Behold, these are parts of his way, and we will hear but a drop of a word in him; and who knows the might of his thunder whenever he will do it?

## Chapter 27

Job 27:1 And Iob, adding still, said in the prelude,
Job 27:2 The Lord lives, who has judged me thus, and the Almighty who embittered my soul,
Job 27:3 surely while my breath is still within, and a divine spirit remaining in my nostrils,
Job 27:4 my lips will not speak lawless things, nor will my soul practice unjust things.
Job 27:5 May it not be mine to declare you righteous until I die; for I will not put away my innocence.
Job 27:6 And holding fast to righteousness, I will certainly not let it go; for I am not conscious of having done improper things.
Job 27:7 Nevertheless may my enemies be like ungodly people's overthrow, and those rising against me like lawless people's destruction.
Job 27:8 For what hope has an ungodly person that he holds on? Trusting in the Lord, will he indeed be saved?
Job 27:9 Will the Lord listen to his petition? Or when necessity comes upon him,
Job 27:10 does he have any frankness before him? Or when he calls upon him, will he listen to him?
Job 27:11 But now I will report to you what is in the Lord's hand; what is with the Almighty, I will not falsify.
Job 27:12 Behold now, you all know that you heap empty things upon empty things.
Job 27:13 This is an ungodly human's portion from the Lord, and rulers' estate will come upon them from the Almighty.
Job 27:14 And if his sons become many, they will be for slaughter; and if they also become men, they will beg;
Job 27:15 and his survivors will die in death, and no one will show mercy to their widows.
Job 27:16 If he gathers silver like earth, and prepares gold like clay,
Job 27:17 righteous people will acquire all these things, and true people will hold his possessions.
Job 27:18 And his house turned out like moths and like a spider's web.
Job 27:19 A rich person lay down and will not do so again; he opened his eyes and is not.
Job 27:20 Pains met him like water, and at night gloom took him away;
Job 27:21 a burning wind will take him up and he will go away, and it will winnow him from his place.
Job 27:22 And it will cast upon him and will not spare; from its hand he will flee in flight;
Job 27:23 it will clap its hands over him and hiss him out of his place.

## Chapter 28

Job 28:1 For silver has a place from which it comes, and gold a place from which it is refined.
Job 28:2 For iron comes from earth, and copper is quarried like stone.
Job 28:3 He set an order for darkness, and he himself examines every limit precisely: stone, darkness, and shadow of death,
Job 28:4 a cutting of a torrent from dust; but those who forget a righteous way became weak among mortals.
Job 28:5 Earth—from it bread will come forth; beneath it, it was turned as though by fire.
Job 28:6 Its stones are a place of sapphire, and its mound has gold.
Job 28:7 A path—a bird has not known it, and a vulture's eye has not looked upon it;
Job 28:8 sons of arrogant ones have not trodden it; a lion has not passed upon it.
Job 28:9 He stretched out his hand upon sheer rock, and overturned mountains from their roots;
Job 28:10 and he broke through the eddies of rivers, and my eye saw every precious thing;
Job 28:11 and he uncovered the depths of rivers, and showed his own power into light.
Job 28:12 But from where was wisdom found? And what is the place of knowledge?
Job 28:13 A mortal does not know its way, nor will it ever be found among humans.
Job 28:14 13 The abyss said, It is not in me; and the sea said, It is not with me.
Job 28:15 He will not give a thing shut away for it, and silver will not be weighed as its exchange;
Job 28:16 and it will not be weighed together with gold of Ophir, with precious onyx and sapphire;
Job 28:17 gold and glass will not be equaled to it, nor golden vessels as its exchange;
Job 28:18 lofty things and gabis will not be mentioned, and draw wisdom beyond the innermost things;
Job 28:19 topaz of Ethiopia will not be equaled to it; with pure gold it will not be weighed together.
Job 28:20 But from where was wisdom found? And what is the place of understanding?
Job 28:21 It has escaped every human's notice, and was hidden from the birds of heaven;
Job 28:22 destruction and death said, But we have heard its fame.
Job 28:23 God established its way well, and he himself knows its place;
Job 28:24 for he himself surveys everything beneath heaven, knowing all the things in the earth which he made,
Job 28:25 the weight of winds and measures of water;
Job 28:26 when he made thus, he numbered rain and a way for voices in a shaking;
Job 28:27 then he saw it and explained it; having prepared it, he traced it out.
Job 28:28 And he said to a human, Behold, reverence for God is wisdom, and abstaining from evils is knowledge.

## Chapter 29

Job 29:1 And Iob, adding yet again, said in his prelude,
Job 29:2 Who would place me according to a month before the days in which God guarded me?
Job 29:3 As when his lamp shone above my head, when by his light I walked in darkness;
Job 29:4 when I was weighty in ways, when God made an inspection of my house;
Job 29:5 when I was very flourishing, and my children were around me;
Job 29:6 when my ways flowed with butter, and my mountains flowed with milk;
Job 29:7 when I went out early in the city, and my seat was set in the squares.
Job 29:8 Young men, seeing me, hid themselves, and all the old men stood;
Job 29:9 and the great ceased speaking, placing a finger upon their mouth.
Job 29:10 And those who heard pronounced me blessed, and their tongue stuck to their throat;
Job 29:11 because an ear heard and pronounced me blessed, and an eye, seeing me, turned aside.
Job 29:12 For I rescued a poor man from a ruler's hand, and helped an orphan who had no helper;
Job 29:13 may a perishing man's blessing come upon me, and a widow's mouth blessed me.
Job 29:14 And I had put on righteousness, and clothed myself with judgment as with a double cloak.
Job 29:15 I was an eye of the blind, and a foot of the lame.
Job 29:16 I was a father of the powerless, and a case which I did not know I traced out;
Job 29:17 and I crushed the molars of the unjust, and tore plunder from between their teeth.
Job 29:18 And I said, My age will grow old; like the trunk of a palm I will live a long time;
Job 29:19 my root has opened out upon water, and dew will lodge in my harvest;
Job 29:20 my glory is fresh with me, and my bow will go in his hand.
Job 29:21 Hearing me, they attended, and were silent at my counsel;
Job 29:22 and they added nothing to my word, and became overjoyed whenever I spoke to them;
Job 29:23 as thirsty earth awaiting the rain, so these awaited my speech.
Job 29:24 If I laugh toward them, they will certainly not believe, and the light of my face did not fall away;
Job 29:25 I chose their way and sat as ruler, and encamped like a king among men wearing a single belt, in the manner of one comforting sufferers.

## Chapter 30

Job 30:1 But now they laughed at me; the least now admonish me in turn, whose fathers I despised, whom I did not consider worthy of the dogs of my flocks.
Job 30:2 And indeed, the strength of their hands—what is it to me? Completion perished upon them,
Job 30:3 barren in want and famine; those fleeing a waterless land yesterday, distress and misery,
Job 30:4 those breaking off saltwort upon a sounding place, whose food was saltwort, dishonored and despised, lacking every good thing, who also chewed roots of trees from great famine.
Job 30:5 Thieves rose against me,
Job 30:6 whose houses were holes in rocks;
Job 30:7 among well-sounding places they will shout; those who lived beneath wild brushwood,
Job 30:8 sons of senseless and dishonored men, a name and fame extinguished from earth.
Job 30:9 But now I am their lyre, and they have me as a tale;
Job 30:10 and they abhorred me, standing far away, and did not spare spittle from my face.
Job 30:11 For, opening his quiver, he afflicted me, and they sent away the bridle of my face.
Job 30:12 On the right of a shoot they rose, stretched out their foot, and made ways against me, paths of their destruction.
Job 30:13 My paths were worn away, for he stripped off my robe;
Job 30:14 with his missiles he speared me; he has treated me as he wishes; I am drenched in pains.
Job 30:15 And my pains return; my hope departed like wind, and my salvation like a cloud.
Job 30:16 And now my soul will be poured out upon me, and days of pains hold me;
Job 30:17 and by night my bones have been burned together, and my sinews have been loosened.
Job 30:18 With great strength he seized my robe; like the collar of my tunic he enclosed me.
Job 30:19 And you have considered me equal to clay; in earth and ashes is my portion;
Job 30:20 and I have cried to you, and you do not hear me; they stood and observed me;
Job 30:21 and you assailed me mercilessly; with a mighty hand you scourged me;
Job 30:22 and you placed me in pains and cast me away from salvation.
Job 30:23 For I know that death will wear me away; for earth is a house for every mortal.
Job 30:24 For if only I could subdue myself, or at least ask another, and he will do this for me.
Job 30:25 But I wept over every powerless person, and groaned on seeing a man in necessities.
Job 30:26 But I, looking for good things—behold, days of evils met me instead.
Job 30:27 My belly boiled over and will not be silent; days of poverty came before me.
Job 30:28 I have walked groaning without a muzzle, and have stood in an assembly crying out.
Job 30:29 I have become a brother of sirens, and a companion of sparrows.
Job 30:30 And my skin has become greatly darkened, and my bones from burning heat.
Job 30:31 And my lyre turned to suffering, and my psalm to weeping for me.

## Chapter 31

Job 31:1 I made a covenant with my eyes, and I will not give attention to a virgin.
Job 31:2 And what did God apportion from above, and what is the inheritance of the Sufficient One from the highest places?
Job 31:3 Is it not destruction for the unjust, and estrangement for those doing lawlessness?
Job 31:4 Will he himself not see my way and count all my steps?
Job 31:5 But if I had walked with jesters, and if my foot also hastened into deceit,
Job 31:6 then may he weigh me in a righteous balance; and the Lord knows my innocence.
Job 31:7 If my foot turned aside from the way, and if my heart also followed my eye, and if with my hands I also touched gifts,
Job 31:8 then may I sow and others eat, and may I become rootless upon earth.
Job 31:9 If my heart followed another man's wife, if I also became one lying in wait at her doors,
Job 31:10 then may my wife also please another, and may my little children be humbled;
Job 31:11 for defiling a man's wife is an unrestrainable fury of anger;
Job 31:12 for it is a fire burning upon all parts, and wherever it comes, it destroyed from the roots.
Job 31:13 And if I also despised the case of my attendant or maidservant when they were in judgment with me,
Job 31:14 for what will I do if the Lord makes an examination of me? And if also an inspection, what answer will I make?
Job 31:15 Were they not also brought into being as I was in a womb? And we have been brought into being in the same belly.
Job 31:16 And the powerless did not fail to obtain a need which they ever had, and I did not waste away a widow's eye.
Job 31:17 And if I also ate my morsel alone, and did not share with an orphan;
Job 31:18 because from my youth I reared as a father, and from my mother's womb I guided;
Job 31:19 and if I also overlooked a naked man perishing, and did not clothe him,
Job 31:20 and if the powerless did not bless me, and their shoulders were warmed from the shearing of my lambs,
Job 31:21 if I raised a hand against an orphan, trusting that much help was available to me,
Job 31:22 then may my shoulder depart from the collarbone, and may my arm be crushed from my elbow.
Job 31:23 For fear of the Lord held me fast, and before his taking hold I will not endure.
Job 31:24 If I appointed gold as my strength, and if I also trusted in a costly stone,
Job 31:25 and if I also rejoiced when much wealth came to me, and if I also placed my hand upon uncountable things,
Job 31:26 do I not indeed see the shining sun failing, and the moon waning? For it is not in their power.
Job 31:27 And if my heart was deceived secretly, and if I also placed my hand upon my mouth and kissed it,
Job 31:28 then may this also be reckoned to me as the greatest lawlessness, because I lied before the Lord Most High.
Job 31:29 And if I also became joyful at my enemies' fall, and my heart said, Well done,
Job 31:30 then may my ear hear my curse, and then may I be talked about by my people as one afflicted.
Job 31:31 And if my maidservants also often said, Who would grant us to be filled with his flesh?—since I was very kind;
Job 31:32 and a stranger did not lodge outside, and my door stood open to everyone coming.
Job 31:33 And if, sinning unwillingly, I also hid my sin,
Job 31:34 for I did not shrink from the multitude's great crowd so as not to declare it before them; and if I also let a powerless man go out my door with an empty bosom,
Job 31:35 who would grant me someone hearing me? And if I had not feared the Lord's hand, a written bond which I held against someone,
Job 31:36 placing it upon my shoulders as a crown, I would read it,
Job 31:37 and if I did not tear it up and return it, taking nothing from a debtor,
Job 31:38 if the earth ever groaned against me, and if its furrows also wept with one accord,
Job 31:39 and if I also ate its strength alone without payment, and if I also cast out the soul of the earth's owner and grieved him,
Job 31:40 then may nettle come forth for me instead of wheat, and bramble instead of barley. And Iob ceased with words.

## Chapter 32

Job 32:1 And his three friends also ceased opposing Iob further; for Iob was righteous before them.
Job 32:2 And Elious, the son of Barachiel, the Bouzite, of the kindred of Ram, of the land of Ausitis, became angry; and he became exceedingly angry with Iob because he declared himself righteous before the Lord;
Job 32:3 and against the three friends he also became exceedingly angry because they were unable to answer Iob with opposing arguments, and determined him to be ungodly.
Job 32:4 And Elious waited to give Iob an answer, because they are older than he in days.
Job 32:5 And Elious saw that there is no answer in the mouth of the three men, and his anger grew furious.
Job 32:6 And Elious, the son of Barachiel, the Bouzite, taking up the discourse, said, I am indeed younger in time, and you are older; therefore I kept quiet, afraid to announce my own knowledge to you;
Job 32:7 and I said that time is what speaks, and in many years they know wisdom.
Job 32:8 But there is a spirit in mortals, and it is the Almighty's breath which teaches;
Job 32:9 those of many years are not wise, nor do the aged know judgment.
Job 32:10 Therefore I said, Hear me, and I will announce to you what I know;
Job 32:11 give ear to my words; for I will speak while you hear, until you examine words.
Job 32:12 And I will attend as far as you, and behold, there was no one reproving Iob, answering his words, from among you,
Job 32:13 so that you may not say, We found wisdom by adding to the Lord;
Job 32:14 and you permitted a human to speak such words. –
Job 32:15 They were terrified; they answered no further; they made words old from themselves.
Job 32:16 I waited, for they did not speak; because they stood, they did not answer.
Job 32:17 And Elious, taking up the discourse, says,
Job 32:18 I will speak again; for I am full of words, for the spirit of the belly is destroying me;
Job 32:19 and my belly is like a wineskin of new wine, boiling, tied up, or like a smith's bellows, burst.
Job 32:20 I will speak, so that I may rest, opening my lips;
Job 32:21 for I will certainly not be ashamed before a human, nor indeed will I show deference to a mortal;
Job 32:22 for I do not know how to admire a face; otherwise, moths will eat me too.

## Chapter 33

Job 33:1 Nevertheless, hear my words, Iob, and give ear to my speech;
Job 33:2 for behold, I opened my mouth, and my tongue spoke.
Job 33:3 My heart is pure in words, and the understanding of my lips is pure in thought.
Job 33:4 A divine spirit is what made me, and the Almighty's breath is what teaches me.
Job 33:5 If you can, give me an answer to these things; wait, stand against me, and I against you.
Job 33:6 You have been formed from clay as I also have; from the same thing we have been formed.
Job 33:7 Fear of me will not whirl you about, nor will my hand be heavy upon you.
Job 33:8 Yet you spoke in my ears; I have heard the voice of your words;
Job 33:9 because you say, I am pure, not having sinned, and I am blameless, for I did not act lawlessly;
Job 33:10 but he found blame against me, and has considered me as an adversary;
Job 33:11 and he placed my foot in wood, and watched all my ways.
Job 33:12 For how do you say, I am righteous, and he has not heard me? For the one above mortals is everlasting.
Job 33:13 And you say, Why has he not heard every word of my case?
Job 33:14 For in the Lord's speaking once, and in the second time, a dream,
Job 33:15 or in a nocturnal meditation, as when dreadful fear falls upon humans during slumbers upon a bed;
Job 33:16 then he uncovers humans' mind; in such forms of fear he frightened them greatly,
Job 33:17 to turn a human away from injustice, and he rescued his body from a fall.
Job 33:18 And he spared his soul from death, and from his falling in war.
Job 33:19 And again he reproved him with sickness upon a bed, and the multitude of his bones grew numb,
Job 33:20 and he will certainly not be able to receive any edible food, and his soul will desire eating,
Job 33:21 until his flesh rots and he shows his bones bare;
Job 33:22 and his soul drew near to death, and his life is in Hades.
Job 33:23 If there are a thousand death-bearing angels, one of them will certainly not wound him; if he understands in his heart to turn to the Lord, and declares to a human his own blame, and shows his folly,
Job 33:24 he will hold fast to preventing his falling into death, and will renew his body like plaster upon a wall, and will fill his bones with marrow;
Job 33:25 and he will soften his flesh like an infant's, and will restore him, grown to manhood, among humans.
Job 33:26 And having prayed to the Lord, it will also be acceptable to him, and he will enter with a pure face, with confession; and he will render righteousness to humans.
Job 33:27 Then at that time the human himself will blame himself, saying, What things I was accomplishing, and he did not examine me in a manner worthy of the things in which I sinned.
Job 33:28 Save my soul from coming into corruption, and my life will see light.
Job 33:29 Behold, the strong one works all these things three ways with a man.
Job 33:30 But he rescued my soul from death, so that my life may praise him in light.
Job 33:31 Give ear, Iob, and hear me; be silent, and I myself will speak.
Job 33:32 If there are words, answer me; speak, for I want you to be justified.
Job 33:33 If not, you hear me; be silent, and I will teach you wisdom.

## Chapter 34

Job 34:1 And Elious, taking up the discourse, says,
Job 34:2 Hear me, wise ones; knowledgeable ones, give ear to what is good;
Job 34:3 because an ear tests words, and a throat tastes food.
Job 34:4 Let us choose judgment for ourselves; let us know among ourselves what is good.
Job 34:5 Because Iob has said, I am righteous; the Lord removed my judgment,
Job 34:6 and lied in my judgment; my arrow is violent, without injustice.
Job 34:7 What man is like Iob, drinking derision like water,
Job 34:8 not having sinned or acted ungodly, or shared a way with those doing lawless things, to walk with the ungodly?
Job 34:9 For do not say that there will be no inspection of a man; and there is an inspection for him from the Lord.
Job 34:10 Therefore, understanding ones in heart, hear me: May it not be mine to act ungodly before the Lord, and to disturb what is righteous before the Almighty;
Job 34:11 but he repays a human according as each of them does, and in a man's path he will find him.
Job 34:12 And do you think the Lord will do improper things? Or will the Almighty disturb judgment?
Job 34:13 He who made the earth; and who is the one making what is beneath heaven and all the things within it?
