Job 34:14 For if he wished to hold fast and to retain the spirit with himself,
Job 34:15 all flesh will die together, and every mortal will depart into earth, from which he also was formed.
Job 34:16 And if he does not admonish, hear these things; give ear to a voice of words.
Job 34:17 See for yourself the one hating lawless things, and the one destroying the wicked, being everlastingly righteous.
Job 34:18 Ungodly is the one saying to a king, You act lawlessly; Most ungodly one, to the rulers;
Job 34:19 who was not ashamed before an honored one's face, nor knows how to assign honor to the great so that their faces may be admired.
Job 34:20 And their crying out and begging a man will turn out empty for them; for they acted unlawfully while the powerless were being turned aside.
Job 34:21 For he himself is an observer of humans' works, and none of what they do has escaped his notice,
Job 34:22 nor will there be a place for those doing lawless things to hide;
Job 34:23 because he will not place upon a man any further; for the Lord surveys all,
Job 34:24 the one comprehending untraceable things, glorious and extraordinary, of which there is no number;
Job 34:25 the one knowing their works, and he will turn night, and they will be humbled.
Job 34:26 And he extinguished the ungodly, and they are visible before him,
Job 34:27 because they turned aside from God's law, and did not recognize his ordinances,
Job 34:28 so as to bring upon him a needy man's cry, and he will hear a cry of the poor.
Job 34:29 And he himself will provide quiet, and who will condemn? And he will hide a face, and who will see him? Both against a nation and against a human together,
Job 34:30 making a hypocritical human king because of a people's difficulty.
Job 34:31 Because the one saying to the strong one, I have taken; I will not take a pledge;
Job 34:32 apart from myself I will see; you show me; if I worked injustice, I will certainly not add to it.
Job 34:33 Will he repay it from you? Because you will reject, because you will choose, and not I; and what you have known, speak.
Job 34:34 Therefore understanding ones in heart will say these things, and a wise man has heard my word.
Job 34:35 But Iob did not speak with understanding, and his words were not with knowledge.
Job 34:36 Nevertheless, learn, Iob; do not give an answering reply any further, like the senseless,
Job 34:37 so that we may not add to our sins; and lawlessness will be reckoned upon us, as we speak many words against the Lord.

## Chapter 35

Job 35:1 And Elious, taking up the discourse, says,
Job 35:2 What is this you considered in judgment? Who are you, that you said, I am righteous before the Lord?
Job 35:3 Or will you say, What will I do, having sinned?
Job 35:4 I will give an answer to you and to your three friends.
Job 35:5 Look up into heaven and see, and observe clouds, how high they are above you.
Job 35:6 If you sinned, what will you do? And if you also acted lawlessly in many things, what can you do?
Job 35:7 But since, then, you are righteous, what will you give him? Or what will he receive from your hand?
Job 35:8 Your ungodliness is for a man like you, and your righteousness for a son of man.
Job 35:9 Slandered by a multitude, they will cry out; they will shout because of the arm of many.
Job 35:10 And he did not say, Where is God who made me, who appoints night watches,
Job 35:11 who distinguishes me from earth's quadrupeds, and from heaven's birds?
Job 35:12 There they will cry out, and he will certainly not hear, also because of the insolence of wicked ones.
Job 35:13 For the Lord does not wish to see improper things; for the Almighty himself is an observer
Job 35:14 of those accomplishing lawless things, and will save me. And be judged before him, if you can praise him as he is.
Job 35:15 And now, because there is no one inspecting his anger, and he did not know greatly in a transgression;
Job 35:16 and Iob opens his mouth vainly; in ignorance he weighs down words.

## Chapter 36

Job 36:1 And Elious, adding still further, says,
Job 36:2 Wait for me a little longer, so that I may teach you; for there is still speech in me.
Job 36:3 Taking up my knowledge from afar, and by my works I will speak righteous things,
Job 36:4 in truth, and not unjust words; you understand unjustly.
Job 36:5 And know that the Lord will certainly not reject the innocent. Mighty in strength of heart,
Job 36:6 he will certainly not give life to an ungodly man, and will give judgment for the poor.
Job 36:7 He will not take his eyes away from a righteous man; and with kings upon a throne, and he will seat them for strife, and they will be exalted.
Job 36:8 And if, bound in fetters, they are held fast in cords of poverty,
Job 36:9 he will also announce to them their works and their transgressions, because they will be strong.
Job 36:10 But he will hear the righteous man; and he said that they will turn from injustice.
Job 36:11 If they hear and serve, they will finish their days in good things, and their years in comeliness.
Job 36:12 But he does not save the ungodly, because they do not wish to know the Lord, and because, being admonished, they were disobedient.
Job 36:13 And hypocrites in heart will appoint wrath; they will not shout, because he bound them.
Job 36:14 Therefore may their soul die in youth, and their life be wounded by angels,
Job 36:15 in return for their afflicting a weak and powerless man; and he will set forth judgment for the meek.
Job 36:16 And furthermore he deceived you out of an enemy's mouth; an abyss, a pouring down beneath it; and your table came down full of fatness.
Job 36:17 And judgment will not be lacking from the righteous,
Job 36:18 and wrath will be upon the ungodly because of the ungodliness of gifts which they received for injustices.
Job 36:19 Let not the mind willingly turn you aside from the supplication of powerless ones in necessity, and all those strengthening strength.
Job 36:20 Do not draw out the night for peoples to go up in their place;
Job 36:21 but guard yourself lest you do improper things; for this you chose out of poverty.
Job 36:22 Behold, the strong one will strengthen in his strength; for who is a ruler like him?
Job 36:23 And who is the one examining his works? Or who is the one saying, He did unjust things?
Job 36:24 Remember that his works are great, of which men began;
Job 36:25 every human saw in himself, as many mortals as are wounded.
Job 36:26 Behold, the strong one is great, and we will not know; the number of his years is also limitless.
Job 36:27 And drops of rain are numbered by him, and will be poured forth as rain into a cloud;
Job 36:28 old things will flow, and he overshadowed clouds upon unspeakably many mortals.
Job 36:28 a He set a season for cattle, and they know the order of a resting place.
Job 36:29 At all these things, does your thought not stand astonished, nor does your heart depart from your body? And if he understands extensions of a cloud, the evenness of his tent,
Job 36:30 behold, he stretches edo upon him, and covered the roots of the sea.
Job 36:31 For by them he will judge peoples; he will give food to the strong.
Job 36:32 Upon hands he covered light, and gave a command concerning it at its meeting;
Job 36:33 he will announce concerning it to his friend; possession, also concerning injustice.

## Chapter 37

Job 37:1 And at this my heart was troubled, and flowed away from its place.
Job 37:2 Hear a report in the anger of the Lord's wrath, and a meditation will come forth from his mouth.
Job 37:3 Beneath all heaven is his rule, and his light is upon the wings of the earth.
Job 37:4 Behind him a voice will shout; he will thunder with the voice of his insolence, and will not exchange them, because he will hear his voice.
Job 37:5 The strong one will thunder wondrous things with his voice; for he did great things which we did not know,
Job 37:6 commanding snow, Be upon the earth; and a storm of rain, and a storm of rains of his dominion.
Job 37:7 In the hand of every human he seals up, so that every human may know his own weakness.
Job 37:8 And beasts entered beneath a shelter, and rested upon a bed.
Job 37:9 Whirlwinds come from chambers, and cold from extremities.
Job 37:10 And from the strong one's breath he will give frost, and steers the water however he wishes;
Job 37:11 and a cloud molds a chosen thing; a cloud will scatter his light.
Job 37:12 And he himself will turn circuits about in theeboulatho for their works; all things, whatever he commands them, these have been appointed by him upon the earth,
Job 37:13 whether for discipline, whether for his earth, whether for mercy he will find him.
Job 37:14 Give ear to these things, Iob; stand, consider the Lord's power.
Job 37:15 We know that God established his works, making light out of darkness.
Job 37:16 And he knows a distinction of clouds, and the extraordinary falls of wicked ones.
Job 37:17 And your robe is warm; and there is quiet upon the earth.
Job 37:18 You will make firm with him for old things, strong as the appearance of a casting.
Job 37:19 Why? Teach me what we will say to him; and let us cease saying many things.
Job 37:20 Has a book or a scribe stood beside me, so that, standing, I may silence a human?
Job 37:21 And the light is not visible to all; it shines afar in the old things, like that from him upon clouds.
Job 37:22 From the north, clouds gleaming with gold; upon these are the Almighty's great glory and honor.
Job 37:23 And we do not find another like him in strength; the one judging righteous things—do you not think he hears?
Job 37:24 Therefore humans will fear him, and the wise in heart will also fear him.

## Chapter 38

Job 38:1 And after Elious ceased his speech, the Lord said to Iob through a tempest and clouds,
Job 38:2 Who is this who hides counsel from me, and holds words in his heart, and thinks to hide them from me?
Job 38:3 Gird your loin like a man, and I will ask you, and you answer me.
Job 38:4 Where were you when I founded the earth? And tell me, if you know understanding.
Job 38:5 Who set its measures, if you know? Or who is the one bringing a cord upon it?
Job 38:6 Upon what have its rings been fixed? And who is the one laying a cornerstone upon it?
Job 38:7 When stars came into being, all my angels praised me with a great voice.
Job 38:8 And I fenced in the sea with gates, when it raged, coming forth from its mother's belly;
Job 38:9 and I appointed a cloud as its clothing, and swaddled it in mist;
Job 38:10 and I appointed boundaries for it, placing bars and gates around it;
Job 38:11 and I said to it, Until this point you will come, and will not pass beyond, but in yourself your waves will be crushed.
Job 38:12 Have I appointed morning brightness in your time, and did the dawn-bringer see its own order,
Job 38:13 to seize the wings of earth, to shake the ungodly out of it?
Job 38:14 Did you take earth, mold clay into a living being, and place him upon earth able to speak?
Job 38:15 And did you remove the light from the ungodly, and crush the arm of the arrogant?
Job 38:16 And did you come upon a spring of the sea, and walk in the tracks of an abyss?
Job 38:17 And are the gates of death opened to you in fear, and did the gatekeepers of Hades cower on seeing you?
Job 38:18 And have you considered the breadth of what is beneath heaven? Tell me, then, how great it is.
Job 38:19 And in what land does light lodge, and what is the place of darkness?
Job 38:20 Would you lead me into their boundaries? And do you also know their paths?
Job 38:21 I know, then, that you have been born at that time, and the number of your years is great.
Job 38:22 And you came upon treasuries of snow, and have seen treasuries of hail.
Job 38:23 And it is laid away for you for a time of enemies, for a day of war and battle.
Job 38:24 And from where does frost come forth, or a south wind disperse into what is beneath heaven?
Job 38:25 And who prepared a flow for violent rain, and a way for uproars,
Job 38:26 to rain upon a land where there is no man, a wilderness where no human exists in it,
Job 38:27 to satisfy an untrodden and uninhabited place, and to make a sprouting of grass grow forth?
Job 38:28 Who is rain's father? And who is the one who has begotten lumps of dew?
Job 38:29 And from whose womb does ice come forth? And who has begotten frost in heaven,
Job 38:30 which descends like flowing water? And who froze the face of an abyss?
Job 38:31 And did you understand the bond of the Pleiad, and open Orion's barrier?
Job 38:32 Will you open mazouroth in its time, and lead the evening star by its hair—these things?
Job 38:33 And do you know heaven's turnings, or the things happening together beneath heaven?
Job 38:34 And will you call a cloud with a voice, and will it obey you with a trembling of violent water?
Job 38:35 And will you send thunderbolts, and will they go? And will they say to you, What is it?
Job 38:36 And who gave women wisdom of weaving, or knowledge of embroidery?
Job 38:37 And who is the one numbering clouds with wisdom, and inclined heaven to earth?
Job 38:38 And dust has been poured out like earth, and I have glued it together like a cube to a stone.
Job 38:39 And will you hunt food for lions, and fill the souls of dragons?
Job 38:40 For they have been afraid in their beds, and sit in woods lying in wait.
Job 38:41 And who prepared food for a raven? For its young have cried to the Lord, wandering, seeking food.

## Chapter 39

Job 39:1 Have you known the time of birth of rock goat-stags, and watched the birth-pains of deer?
Job 39:2 And did you count their months fulfilled for birth, and release their birth-pains?
Job 39:3 And did you rear their little ones outside fear? Will you send away their birth-pains?
Job 39:4 They will break away their children; they will multiply in offspring, will go forth, and will certainly not return to them.
Job 39:5 And who is the one letting a wild ass go free, and who loosened its bonds?
Job 39:6 And I appointed its dwelling a wilderness, and its habitations a salt land;
Job 39:7 laughing at a city's great crowd, and not hearing a tax collector's blame,
Job 39:8 it will survey mountains as its pasture, and seeks after every green thing.
Job 39:9 And will a unicorn wish to serve you, or sleep at your manger?
Job 39:10 And will you bind its yoke with straps, or will it draw your furrows in a plain?
Job 39:11 And have you trusted in it because its strength is great, and will you leave your works to it?
Job 39:12 And will you believe that it will return the seed to you, and bring in your threshing floor?
Job 39:13 A wing of rejoicing ones, neelasa, if it takes together asida and nessa;
Job 39:14 because she will leave her eggs upon earth, and will warm them upon dust,
Job 39:15 and forgot that a foot will scatter them and beasts of a field will trample them;
Job 39:16 she hardened herself against her children as though they were not hers; she toiled in vain without fear;
Job 39:17 because God kept wisdom silent for her, and did not give her a share in understanding.
Job 39:18 At a time she will lift high on high; she will laugh at a horse and its rider.
Job 39:19 Did you clothe a horse with power, and clothe its neck with fear?
Job 39:20 And did you clothe it with full armor, and the glory of its breast with daring?
Job 39:21 Digging up in a plain, it exults, and goes forth into a plain in strength;
Job 39:22 meeting a missile, it laughs, and will certainly not turn away from iron;
Job 39:23 upon it a bow and sword exult,
Job 39:24 and in anger it will obliterate the earth, and will certainly not believe until a trumpet signals;
Job 39:25 and when a trumpet signals, it says, Well done; and from afar it smells war, with leaping and shouting.
Job 39:26 And by your knowledge has a hawk stood, spreading its wings, motionless, looking down upon the things toward the south?
Job 39:27 And at your command does an eagle rise high, and a vulture, seated upon its nest, lodge
Job 39:28 upon a prominence of rock and a hidden place?
Job 39:29 Being there, it seeks food; from afar its eyes watch;
Job 39:30 and its young are drenched in blood, and wherever dead ones are, they are found immediately.

## Chapter 40

Job 40:1 And the Lord God answered Iob and said,
Job 40:2 Will he turn aside judgment with the Sufficient One? Will one reproving God answer it?
Job 40:3 And Iob, taking up the discourse, says to the Lord,
Job 40:4 Why am I still being judged, being admonished and reproving the Lord, hearing such things, being nothing? And what answer should I give to these things? I will place a hand upon my mouth;
Job 40:5 I have spoken once, and at the second time I will not add.
Job 40:6 And the Lord, taking up the discourse again, said to Iob from the cloud,
Job 40:7 No, but gird your loin like a man, and I will ask you, and you answer me;
Job 40:8 do not reject my judgment. And do you think I have spoken to you otherwise than so that you may be shown righteous?
Job 40:9 Do you have an arm against the Lord, or do you thunder with a voice like him?
Job 40:10 Take up, then, loftiness and power, and clothe yourself with glory and honor;
Job 40:11 and send angels in anger, and humble every insolent one,
Job 40:12 and extinguish an arrogant one, and rot the ungodly immediately,
Job 40:13 and hide them in earth outside together, and fill their faces with dishonor;
Job 40:14 then I will acknowledge that your right hand can save. –
Job 40:15 But indeed, behold, beasts beside you; it eats grass like oxen.
Job 40:16 Behold, indeed, its strength is upon its loin, and its power upon the navel of its belly;
Job 40:17 it set up a tail like a cypress, and its sinews have been interwoven;
Job 40:18 its ribs are bronze ribs, and its spine is cast iron.
Job 40:19 This is the beginning of the Lord's formation, made to be played with by his angels.
Job 40:20 And coming upon a sheer mountain, it made joy for quadrupeds in Tartarus;
Job 40:21 it sleeps beneath trees of every sort, beside papyrus and reed and flowering rush;
Job 40:22 and great trees with shoots, and branches of chaste tree, are shaded in it.
Job 40:23 If a flood occurs, it will certainly not perceive it; it has trusted that the Iordan will strike against its mouth.
Job 40:24 In its eye will he receive it, and, ensnaring it, pierce a nose? –
Job 40:25 And will you lead a dragon with a hook, and place a halter around its nose?
Job 40:26 Will you bind a ring in its nostril, and pierce its lip with a bracelet?
Job 40:27 And will it speak to you with entreaty, with supplication softly?
Job 40:28 And will it make a covenant with you, and will you take it as an everlasting slave?
Job 40:29 And will you play with it like a bird, or bind it like a little sparrow for a child?
Job 40:30 And do nations feed upon it, and do races of Phoenicians divide it?
Job 40:31 And every floating vessel, gathered together—they will certainly not carry one skin of its tail, nor its head in fishermen's boats.
Job 40:32 And will you lay a hand upon it, remembering the war occurring in its body? And let it happen no longer.

## Chapter 41

Job 41:1 Have you not seen it, nor marveled at the things spoken?
Job 41:2 Have you not been afraid because it has been prepared for me? For who is the one standing against me?
Job 41:3 Or who will stand against me and endure, if everything beneath heaven is mine?
Job 41:4 I will not be silent because of it, and it will pity its equal as regards a word of power.
Job 41:5 Who will uncover the face of its clothing? And who would enter into the fold of its breastplate?
Job 41:6 Who will open the gates of its face? Around its teeth is fear.
Job 41:7 Its inward parts are bronze shields, and its bond is like an emery stone;
Job 41:8 one sticks to another, and breath will certainly not pass through it;
Job 41:9 a man will stick to his brother; they are held together and will certainly not be pulled apart.
Job 41:10 In its sneezing brightness shines, and its eyes are the appearance of the dawn-bringer.
Job 41:11 Burning torches come forth from its mouth, and hearths of fire are hurled about;
Job 41:12 from its nostrils comes smoke of a furnace burning with a fire of coals;
Job 41:13 its soul is coals, and a flame comes forth from its mouth.
Job 41:14 And power lodges in its neck; destruction runs before it.
Job 41:15 And the flesh of its body has been glued together; he pours upon it; it will not be shaken.
Job 41:16 Its heart has been fixed like a stone, and stands like an unhammered anvil.
Job 41:17 And when it turns, there is fear for quadruped beasts leaping upon earth.
Job 41:18 If lances meet it, they will certainly do nothing, a raised spear and breastplate;
Job 41:19 for it has considered iron straw, and copper like rotten wood;
Job 41:20 a bronze bow will certainly not wound it; it has considered a stone-thrower grass;
Job 41:21 hammers were reckoned as stubble, and it laughs at the shaking of a fire-bearer.
Job 41:22 Its bedding is sharp spits, and all the gold of the sea beneath it is like unspeakably much clay.
Job 41:23 It makes the abyss boil like a bronze pot, and has considered the sea like an ointment vessel,
Job 41:24 and the Tartarus of the abyss like a captive; it reckoned the abyss a walking place.
Job 41:25 There is nothing upon earth like it, made to be played with by my angels;
Job 41:26 it sees every lofty thing, and it is king of all those in the waters.

## Chapter 42

Job 42:1 And Iob, taking up the discourse, says to the Lord,
Job 42:2 I know that you can do all things, and nothing is impossible for you.
Job 42:3 For who is the one hiding counsel from you? And, sparing words, does he think to hide it from you too? And who will announce to me what I did not know, great and wondrous things which I did not understand?
Job 42:4 And hear me, Lord, so that I too may speak; and I will ask you, and you teach me.
Job 42:5 Indeed, formerly I heard you by an ear's hearing, but now my eye has seen you;
Job 42:6 therefore I despised myself and melted away, and have considered myself earth and ashes.
Job 42:7 And it happened after the Lord spoke all these words to Iob, the Lord said to Eliphas the Thaimanite, You sinned, and your two friends; for you did not speak anything true before me, as my attendant Iob did.
Job 42:8 But now take seven calves and seven rams, and go to my attendant Iob, and he will make a burnt offering for you; and Iob my attendant will pray for you, for surely I will accept his face; for if not for him, I would have destroyed you; for you did not speak what is true against my attendant Iob. –
Job 42:9 And Eliphas the Thaimanite and Baldad the Sauchite and Sophar the Minaite went and did as the Lord commanded them, and he released their sin for them through Iob.
Job 42:10 And the Lord increased Iob; and when he also prayed for his friends, he forgave them their sin; and the Lord gave double whatever Iob had before, for a doubling.
Job 42:11 And all his brothers and his sisters heard all the things that had happened to him, and came to him, and all who knew him from the first; and eating and drinking with him, they comforted him, and marveled at all the things which the Lord brought upon him; and each gave him one ewe-lamb and an unstamped golden tetradrachm.
Job 42:12 And the Lord blessed Iob's latter things more than the former; and his cattle were fourteen thousand sheep, six thousand camels, a thousand yokes of oxen, a thousand grazing female asses.
Job 42:13 And seven sons and three daughters are born to him;
Job 42:14 and he called the first Day, the second Cassia, and the third Amaltheia's Horn;
Job 42:15 and none better than Iob's daughters were found, compared with them, beneath heaven; and their father gave them an inheritance among their brothers.
Job 42:16 And Iob lived a hundred seventy years after the stroke, and in all lived two hundred forty-eight years; and Iob saw his sons and his sons' sons, a fourth generation;
Job 42:17 and Iob died, old and full of days.
Job 42:17 a And it has been written that he will rise again with those whom the Lord raises. – –
Job 42:18 This man is interpreted from the Syriac book as dwelling in the land of Ausitis, upon the boundaries of Idoumaia and Arabia, and his name previously was Iobab;
Job 42:19 and taking an Arabian wife, he begets a son, whose name is Ennon; and he himself was a son of his father Zare, of the sons of Esau, and of his mother Bosorra, so that he was fifth from Abraam.
Job 42:18 And these are the kings who reigned in Edom, which land he himself also ruled: first Balak the son of Beor, and the name of his city was Dennaba; and after Balak, Iobab, who is called Iob; and after this man, Asom, who was a ruler from the land of Thaimanitis; and after this man, Adad son of Barad, who cut down Madiam in the plain of Moab, and the name of his city was Getthaim.
Job 42:19 And the friends who came to him: Eliphas, of the sons of Esau, king of the Thaimans; Baldad, the tyrant of the Sauchaians; Sophar, the king of the Minaians.

# Wisdom of Solomon

The Apostolic Bible. Public domain. https://apostolic-bible.ysys9.chatgpt.site/license.html


## Chapter 1

Wisdom of Solomon 1:1 Love righteousness, you who judge the earth; think concerning the Lord in goodness, and seek him in simplicity of heart.
Wisdom of Solomon 1:2 Because he is found by those who do not test him, and appears to those who do not disbelieve him.
Wisdom of Solomon 1:3 For crooked reasonings separate from God, and power, when tested, reproves the senseless.
Wisdom of Solomon 1:4 Because wisdom will not enter a soul devising evil, nor dwell in a body indebted to sin.
Wisdom of Solomon 1:5 For a holy spirit of discipline will flee deceit, and depart from reasonings without understanding, and will be reproved when injustice comes upon it.
Wisdom of Solomon 1:6 For wisdom is a spirit loving humans, and will not acquit a blasphemer of his lips; because God is a witness of his kidneys, and a true overseer of his heart, and a hearer of his tongue.
Wisdom of Solomon 1:7 Because the Lord's spirit has filled the inhabited world, and that which holds all things together has knowledge of a voice.
Wisdom of Solomon 1:8 Therefore no one uttering unjust things will escape notice, nor will justice, reproving, pass him by.
Wisdom of Solomon 1:9 For there will be an examination into an ungodly man's counsels, and a hearing of his words will come to the Lord for reproof of his lawless deeds;
Wisdom of Solomon 1:10 because an ear of jealousy listens to all things, and a murmur of grumblings is not hidden.
Wisdom of Solomon 1:11 Therefore guard yourselves against unprofitable grumbling, and spare your tongue from speaking against others; because a secret utterance will not go empty, and a mouth telling lies destroys a soul.
Wisdom of Solomon 1:12 Do not pursue death in the wandering of your life, nor draw destruction upon yourselves by the works of your hands;
Wisdom of Solomon 1:13 because God did not make death, nor delights in the destruction of the living.
Wisdom of Solomon 1:14 For he created all things to exist, and the world's origins are salutary, and there is no poison of destruction in them, nor a kingdom of Hades upon earth.
Wisdom of Solomon 1:15 For righteousness is immortal.
Wisdom of Solomon 1:16 But the ungodly summoned him with their hands and words; considering him a friend, they melted away, and made an agreement with him, because they are worthy to be of his portion.

## Chapter 2

Wisdom of Solomon 2:1 For they said among themselves, reasoning incorrectly, Our life is short and sorrowful, and there is no healing at a human's death, and no one who returned from Hades was known.
Wisdom of Solomon 2:2 Because we came into being by chance, and after this we will be as though we had not existed; because the breath in our nostrils is smoke, and reason a spark in the movement of our heart,
Wisdom of Solomon 2:3 which, when extinguished, the body will become ash, and the spirit will be dispersed like loose air.
Wisdom of Solomon 2:4 And our name will be forgotten in time, and no one will remember our works; and our life will pass away like traces of a cloud, and will be scattered like mist, chased by rays of the sun and weighed down by its heat.
Wisdom of Solomon 2:5 For our time is a shadow's passing, and there is no returning of our end, because it was sealed, and no one turns back.
Wisdom of Solomon 2:6 Come, then, and let us enjoy the good things that exist, and use creation eagerly as in youth;
Wisdom of Solomon 2:7 let us be filled with costly wine and perfumes, and let no flower of spring pass us by;
Wisdom of Solomon 2:8 let us crown ourselves with rosebuds before they wither;
Wisdom of Solomon 2:9 let none of us be without a share of our arrogance; everywhere let us leave tokens of gladness, because this is our portion and this our lot.
Wisdom of Solomon 2:10 Let us oppress a needy righteous man, let us not spare a widow, nor show deference to an old man's gray hair of many years;
Wisdom of Solomon 2:11 and let our strength be a law of righteousness, for what is weak is proved useless.
Wisdom of Solomon 2:12 Let us lie in wait for the righteous man, because he is inconvenient to us, and opposes our works, and reproaches us with sins against law, and charges us with sins against our discipline;
Wisdom of Solomon 2:13 he professes to have knowledge of God, and calls himself a servant of the Lord;
Wisdom of Solomon 2:14 he became for us a reproof of our thoughts; he is burdensome to us even when seen,
Wisdom of Solomon 2:15 because his life is unlike the others', and his paths are different;
Wisdom of Solomon 2:16 we were reckoned counterfeit by him, and he abstains from our ways as from impurities; he pronounces the last things of the righteous blessed, and boasts of God as father.
Wisdom of Solomon 2:17 Let us see if his words are true, and test the things at his outcome;
Wisdom of Solomon 2:18 for if the righteous man is a son of God, he will help him, and rescue him from the hand of those opposing him.
Wisdom of Solomon 2:19 With insult and torture let us examine him, so that we may know his gentleness, and test his endurance of evil;
Wisdom of Solomon 2:20 let us condemn him to a shameful death, for there will be an inspection of him according to his words.
Wisdom of Solomon 2:21 These things they reasoned, and were led astray; for their wickedness blinded them,
Wisdom of Solomon 2:22 and they did not know God's mysteries, nor hope for a wage of holiness, nor discern an honor of blameless souls.
Wisdom of Solomon 2:23 Because God created the human for incorruptibility, and made him an image of his own eternity;
Wisdom of Solomon 2:24 but through the devil's envy death entered the world, and those who are of his portion experience it.

## Chapter 3

Wisdom of Solomon 3:1 But the souls of the righteous are in God's hand, and torture will certainly not touch them.
Wisdom of Solomon 3:2 They seemed in the eyes of the senseless to have died, and their departure was reckoned affliction,
Wisdom of Solomon 3:3 and their journey from us, ruin; but they are in peace.
Wisdom of Solomon 3:4 For even if they are punished in humans' sight, their hope is full of immortality;
Wisdom of Solomon 3:5 and disciplined in a few things, they will be benefited in great things, because God tested them and found them worthy of himself;
Wisdom of Solomon 3:6 like gold in a crucible he tested them, and like a whole burnt offering of sacrifice he accepted them.
Wisdom of Solomon 3:7 And in the time of their inspection they will shine forth, and like sparks in stubble they will run through;
Wisdom of Solomon 3:8 they will judge nations and rule peoples, and the Lord will reign over them for the ages.
Wisdom of Solomon 3:9 Those who have trusted in him will understand truth, and those faithful in love will remain with him; because grace and mercy are for his chosen ones.
Wisdom of Solomon 3:10 But the ungodly will have punishment according as they reasoned, those who neglected the righteous man and departed from the Lord;
Wisdom of Solomon 3:11 for the one despising wisdom and discipline is miserable, and their hope is empty, and their labors unprofitable, and their works useless;
Wisdom of Solomon 3:12 their wives are senseless, and their children wicked; their offspring is accursed.
Wisdom of Solomon 3:13 Because blessed is the barren woman who is undefiled, who did not know a bed in transgression; she will have fruit in the inspection of souls,
Wisdom of Solomon 3:14 and the eunuch who did not work a lawless deed with his hand, nor think wicked things against the Lord; for a choice grace of faith will be given him, and a more pleasing lot in the Lord's temple.
Wisdom of Solomon 3:15 For the fruit of good toils is glorious, and the root of prudence unfailing.
Wisdom of Solomon 3:16 But adulterers' children will be unfulfilled, and seed from an unlawful bed will be obliterated.
Wisdom of Solomon 3:17 For even if they become long-lived, they will be reckoned as nothing, and their old age dishonored at the last;
Wisdom of Solomon 3:18 and if they die swiftly, they will have no hope, nor consolation in a day of discernment;
Wisdom of Solomon 3:19 for the ends of an unjust generation are harsh.

## Chapter 4

Wisdom of Solomon 4:1 Better is childlessness with virtue; for immortality is in its remembrance, because it is known both with God and with humans.
Wisdom of Solomon 4:2 And when present they imitate it, and long for it when departed; and in the age it proceeds in procession wearing a crown, having won the contest of undefiled prizes.
Wisdom of Solomon 4:3 But a prolific multitude of the ungodly will not be useful, and from illegitimate shoots it will not give a root into depth, nor establish a secure foundation;
Wisdom of Solomon 4:4 for even if it flourishes in branches for a time, being insecurely established, it will be shaken by wind, and uprooted by the force of winds.
Wisdom of Solomon 4:5 Unfulfilled branches will be broken off, and their fruit is useless, unripe for eating, and suitable for nothing;
Wisdom of Solomon 4:6 for children born from lawless sleeps are witnesses of wickedness against parents in their examination.
Wisdom of Solomon 4:7 But a righteous man, if he dies early, will be in rest;
Wisdom of Solomon 4:8 for honored old age is not that of many years, nor has it been measured by a number of years,
Wisdom of Solomon 4:9 but prudence is gray hair for humans, and a spotless life is an age of old age.
Wisdom of Solomon 4:10 Becoming well-pleasing to God, he was loved, and living among sinners, he was transferred;
Wisdom of Solomon 4:11 he was snatched away, lest wickedness change his understanding, or deceit deceive his soul;
Wisdom of Solomon 4:12 for the fascination of baseness obscures good things, and the wandering of desire alters an innocent mind.
Wisdom of Solomon 4:13 Perfected in a little time, he fulfilled long times;
Wisdom of Solomon 4:14 for his soul was pleasing to the Lord; therefore he hastened out of the midst of wickedness; but the peoples, seeing and not understanding, nor placing such a thing upon their thought,
Wisdom of Solomon 4:15 that grace and mercy are among his chosen ones, and inspection among his holy ones.
Wisdom of Solomon 4:16 And a righteous man who has died will condemn the living ungodly, and youth swiftly completed, an unjust man's old age of many years;
Wisdom of Solomon 4:17 for they will see a wise man's end, and will not understand what the Lord planned concerning him, and for what he secured him.
Wisdom of Solomon 4:18 They will see and despise; but the Lord will laugh at them,
Wisdom of Solomon 4:19 and after this they will become a dishonored corpse, and an insult among the dead throughout an age, because he will dash them headlong, speechless, and shake them from foundations, and they will be laid waste to the last, and will be in pain, and their remembrance will perish.
Wisdom of Solomon 4:20 They will come timid in a reckoning of their sins, and their lawless deeds will reprove them from opposite them.

## Chapter 5

Wisdom of Solomon 5:1 Then the righteous man will stand with great boldness before the face of those who afflicted him, and those rejecting his toils.
Wisdom of Solomon 5:2 Seeing him, they will be troubled with dreadful fear, and will be astonished at the unexpectedness of his salvation;
Wisdom of Solomon 5:3 they will say among themselves, repenting, and through anguish of spirit they will groan, and will say,
Wisdom of Solomon 5:4 This was he whom we, the senseless, once held for laughter and for a proverb of reproach; we reckoned his life madness and his end dishonored.
Wisdom of Solomon 5:5 How was he numbered among sons of God, and is his lot among holy ones?
Wisdom of Solomon 5:6 Then we were led astray from a way of truth, and the light of righteousness did not shine upon us, and the sun did not rise for us;
Wisdom of Solomon 5:7 we were filled with paths of lawlessness and destruction, and traversed untrodden wildernesses, but did not recognize the Lord's way.
Wisdom of Solomon 5:8 What did arrogance benefit us? And what has wealth with boastfulness contributed to us?
Wisdom of Solomon 5:9 All those things passed like a shadow and like a message running past;
Wisdom of Solomon 5:10 like a ship passing through billowing water, of which, when it has crossed, it is not possible to find a trace, nor a track of its keel in waves;
Wisdom of Solomon 5:11 or as, when a bird flies through air, no proof of a journey is found, but light wind, lashed by the beating of wings and split by the force of the whirring of moving wings, was traversed, and after this no sign of passage was found in it;
Wisdom of Solomon 5:12 or as, when an arrow was shot at a target, the air, cut, immediately returned into itself, so that its passage was unknown;
Wisdom of Solomon 5:13 so we too, having been born, ceased, and had no sign of virtue to show, but were wholly consumed in our wickedness.
Wisdom of Solomon 5:14 Because an ungodly man's hope is like chaff carried by wind, and like fine frost chased by a tempest, and like smoke it was dispersed by wind, and like the remembrance of a guest of one day it passed away.
Wisdom of Solomon 5:15 But the righteous live for the age, and their wage is in the Lord, and care for them is with the Most High.
Wisdom of Solomon 5:16 Therefore they will receive the kingdom of comeliness and the diadem of beauty from the Lord's hand, because with his right hand he will shelter them, and with his arm defend them.
Wisdom of Solomon 5:17 He will take his zeal as full armor, and arm creation for repelling enemies;
Wisdom of Solomon 5:18 he will put on righteousness as a breastplate, and place unhypocritical judgment as a helmet;
Wisdom of Solomon 5:19 he will take holiness as an unconquerable shield,
Wisdom of Solomon 5:20 and sharpen severe anger into a sword, and the world will wage war together with him against the deranged.
Wisdom of Solomon 5:21 Well-aimed missiles of lightning will go forth, and from the clouds, as from a well-curved bow, they will leap toward a target,
Wisdom of Solomon 5:22 and hailstones full of wrath will be hurled from a stone-thrower; water of the sea will be indignant against them, and rivers will flood harshly;
Wisdom of Solomon 5:23 a wind of power will stand against them, and like a tempest will winnow them out; and lawlessness will lay all the earth waste, and evildoing will overturn rulers' thrones.

## Chapter 6

Wisdom of Solomon 6:1 Hear, then, kings, and understand; learn, judges of the ends of earth;
Wisdom of Solomon 6:2 give ear, you who rule a multitude and have exulted over crowds of nations;
Wisdom of Solomon 6:3 because rule was given you from the Lord, and dominion from the Most High, who will examine your works and search out your counsels;
Wisdom of Solomon 6:4 because, being servants of his kingdom, you did not judge rightly, nor guard law, nor walk according to God's counsel.
Wisdom of Solomon 6:5 Terribly and swiftly he will come upon you, because severe judgment occurs among those in high places.
Wisdom of Solomon 6:6 For the least is pardonable through mercy, but the mighty will be examined mightily;
Wisdom of Solomon 6:7 for the Master of all will not shrink before a face, nor defer to greatness, because he himself made small and great, and alike provides for all,
Wisdom of Solomon 6:8 but a strong investigation comes upon the strong.
Wisdom of Solomon 6:9 To you, then, O tyrants, are my words, so that you may learn wisdom and not fall aside;
Wisdom of Solomon 6:10 for those who have guarded holy things holily will be made holy, and those taught them will find a defense.
Wisdom of Solomon 6:11 Desire, then, my words; long for them, and you will be disciplined.
Wisdom of Solomon 6:12 Wisdom is radiant and unfading, and is easily beheld by those loving her, and found by those seeking her;
Wisdom of Solomon 6:13 she anticipates those desiring her, to be known beforehand.
Wisdom of Solomon 6:14 The one rising early for her will not labor; for he will find her seated beside his gates.
Wisdom of Solomon 6:15 For thinking concerning her is perfection of prudence, and the one keeping watch because of her will swiftly be without care;
Wisdom of Solomon 6:16 because she herself goes about seeking those worthy of her, and appears to them favorably in their paths, and meets them in every thought.
Wisdom of Solomon 6:17 For her beginning is the truest desire for discipline, and care for discipline is love,
Wisdom of Solomon 6:18 and love is keeping her laws, and attention to laws is confirmation of incorruptibility,
Wisdom of Solomon 6:19 and incorruptibility makes one near God;
Wisdom of Solomon 6:20 therefore desire for wisdom leads up to a kingdom.
Wisdom of Solomon 6:21 If, then, you delight in thrones and scepters, tyrants of peoples, honor wisdom, so that you may reign for the age.
Wisdom of Solomon 6:22 And what wisdom is, and how she came into being, I will announce, and will not hide mysteries from you, but will trace her from the beginning of her origin, and place the knowledge of her in the open, and will certainly not pass truth by.
Wisdom of Solomon 6:23 Nor indeed will I journey with wasting envy, because this will not share in wisdom.
Wisdom of Solomon 6:24 And a multitude of wise ones is salvation of a world, and a prudent king stability of a people.
Wisdom of Solomon 6:25 Therefore be disciplined by my words, and you will be benefited.

## Chapter 7

Wisdom of Solomon 7:1 Indeed I too am a mortal human, equal to all, and a descendant of the earth-born first-formed man; and in a mother's belly I was sculpted as flesh,
Wisdom of Solomon 7:2 congealed in blood in a time of ten months, from a man's seed and pleasure accompanying sleep.
Wisdom of Solomon 7:3 And I too, having come into being, drew the common air, and fell upon the earth sharing like experiences, crying as my first voice, the same as all alike;
Wisdom of Solomon 7:4 I was reared in swaddling clothes and cares.
Wisdom of Solomon 7:5 For none of the kings had another beginning of birth,
Wisdom of Solomon 7:6 but the entrance into life is one for all, and the departure equal.
Wisdom of Solomon 7:7 Therefore I prayed, and prudence was given me; I called upon him, and a spirit of wisdom came to me.
Wisdom of Solomon 7:8 I preferred her to scepters and thrones, and considered wealth nothing in comparison with her;
Wisdom of Solomon 7:9 nor did I liken a priceless stone to her, because all gold in her sight is a little sand, and silver will be reckoned as clay before her;
Wisdom of Solomon 7:10 above health and beauty of form I loved her, and chose to have her instead of light, because the brightness from her is unsleeping.
Wisdom of Solomon 7:11 And all good things came to me together with her, and uncountable wealth in her hands;
Wisdom of Solomon 7:12 and I rejoiced over all, because wisdom leads them, but I did not know that she was their mother.
Wisdom of Solomon 7:13 And without deceit I learned, and without envy I share; I do not hide her wealth;
Wisdom of Solomon 7:14 for she is an unfailing treasure for humans, which those acquiring prepared friendship with God, being commended through the gifts from discipline.
Wisdom of Solomon 7:15 And may God grant me to speak according to judgment, and think worthily of the things given, because he himself is both wisdom's guide and the corrector of the wise.
Wisdom of Solomon 7:16 For in his hand are both we and our words, and all prudence and knowledge of crafts.
Wisdom of Solomon 7:17 For he himself gave me unlying knowledge of things existing, to know the world's constitution and the working of elements,
Wisdom of Solomon 7:18 the beginning and end and middle of times, changes of turnings and alterations of seasons,
Wisdom of Solomon 7:19 cycles of a year and positions of stars,
Wisdom of Solomon 7:20 natures of living beings and tempers of beasts, forces of spirits and reasonings of humans, differences of plants and powers of roots,
Wisdom of Solomon 7:21 and whatever things are hidden and manifest I knew; for wisdom, the craftswoman of all, taught me.
Wisdom of Solomon 7:22 For in her is a spirit intelligent, holy, only-begotten, of many parts, fine, easily moving, clear, undefiled, plain, unharmed, loving good, sharp,
Wisdom of Solomon 7:23 unhindered, beneficent, loving humans, firm, secure, without care, all-powerful, overseeing all, and passing through all intelligent, pure, finest spirits.
Wisdom of Solomon 7:24 For wisdom is more mobile than every movement, and penetrates and passes through all things because of her purity;
Wisdom of Solomon 7:25 for she is a vapor of God's power, and a pure outflow of the Almighty's glory; therefore nothing defiled falls into her.
Wisdom of Solomon 7:26 For she is a radiance of everlasting light, and a spotless mirror of God's working, and an image of his goodness.
Wisdom of Solomon 7:27 And being one, she can do all things, and remaining in herself, renews all things, and passing into holy souls generation by generation, makes friends of God and prophets;
Wisdom of Solomon 7:28 for God loves nothing except the one dwelling together with wisdom.
Wisdom of Solomon 7:29 For she is more comely than the sun, and above every position of stars. Compared with light, she is found prior;
Wisdom of Solomon 7:30 for night succeeds this, but wickedness does not prevail over wisdom.

## Chapter 8

Wisdom of Solomon 8:1 And she extends strongly from end to end, and administers all things kindly.
Wisdom of Solomon 8:2 Her I loved and sought out from my youth, and sought to take as a bride for myself, and became a lover of her beauty.
Wisdom of Solomon 8:3 She glorifies noble birth, having life together with God, and the Master of all loved her;
Wisdom of Solomon 8:4 for she is an initiate in God's knowledge, and a chooser of his works.
Wisdom of Solomon 8:5 And if wealth is a desirable possession in life, what is richer than wisdom, who works all things?
Wisdom of Solomon 8:6 And if prudence works, who of the things existing is more a craftswoman than she?
Wisdom of Solomon 8:7 And if someone loves righteousness, her toils are virtues; for she teaches self-control and prudence, righteousness and courage, than which nothing is more useful in life for humans.
Wisdom of Solomon 8:8 And if someone also longs for much experience, she knows ancient things and conjectures future things, understands turns of words and solutions of riddles, foreknows signs and wonders, and outcomes of seasons and times.
Wisdom of Solomon 8:9 Therefore I decided to take her to live together, knowing that she will be for me a counselor of good things, and an exhortation in cares and sorrow.
Wisdom of Solomon 8:10 Through her I will have glory among crowds, and honor with elders, being young;
Wisdom of Solomon 8:11 I will be found sharp in judgment, and admired in rulers' sight;
Wisdom of Solomon 8:12 when I am silent, they will wait for me, and when I utter, they will attend, and when I speak at greater length, they will place a hand upon their mouth.
Wisdom of Solomon 8:13 Through her I will have immortality, and leave an everlasting remembrance to those after me.
Wisdom of Solomon 8:14 I will administer peoples, and nations will be subjected to me;
Wisdom of Solomon 8:15 terrible tyrants, hearing, will fear me; among a multitude I will appear good, and in war courageous.
Wisdom of Solomon 8:16 Entering my house, I will rest beside her; for her company has no bitterness, nor living together with her pain, but gladness and joy.
Wisdom of Solomon 8:17 Reasoning these things in myself, and considering in my heart that there is immortality in kinship with wisdom,
Wisdom of Solomon 8:18 and good delight in friendship with her, and unfailing wealth in the toils of her hands, and prudence in training together in her company, and good fame in sharing her words, I went about seeking how I might take her to myself.
Wisdom of Solomon 8:19 And I was a child of good nature, and obtained a good soul,
Wisdom of Solomon 8:20 or rather, being good, I came into an undefiled body.
Wisdom of Solomon 8:21 And knowing that I will not otherwise possess her unless God gives her—and this too was of prudence, to know whose the grace is—I petitioned the Lord and begged him, and said from my whole heart,

## Chapter 9

Wisdom of Solomon 9:1 God of fathers and Lord of mercy, who made all things by your word,
Wisdom of Solomon 9:2 and by your wisdom made a human, so that he may master the creatures brought into being by you,
Wisdom of Solomon 9:3 and govern the world in holiness and righteousness, and judge judgment in uprightness of soul,
Wisdom of Solomon 9:4 give me wisdom, seated beside your thrones, and do not reject me from your servants.
Wisdom of Solomon 9:5 Because I am your slave and a son of your maidservant, a weak and short-lived human, and deficient in understanding of judgment and laws;
Wisdom of Solomon 9:6 for even if someone is perfect among sons of humans, with wisdom from you absent he will be reckoned as nothing.
Wisdom of Solomon 9:7 You chose me as king of your people and judge of your sons and daughters;
Wisdom of Solomon 9:8 you said to build a temple on your holy mountain, and an altar in the city of your dwelling, an imitation of a holy tent which you prepared beforehand from the beginning.
Wisdom of Solomon 9:9 And with you is wisdom, who knows your works and was present when you were making the world, and understands what is pleasing in your eyes and what is upright in your commandments.
Wisdom of Solomon 9:10 Send her out from holy heavens, and from your throne of glory send her, so that, present together with me, she may labor, and I may know what is well-pleasing with you.
Wisdom of Solomon 9:11 For she knows all things and understands, and will guide me with self-control in my actions, and guard me in her glory;
Wisdom of Solomon 9:12 and my works will be acceptable, and I will judge your people righteously, and be worthy of my father's thrones.
Wisdom of Solomon 9:13 For what human will know God's counsel? Or who will consider what the Lord wills?
Wisdom of Solomon 9:14 For mortals' reasonings are timid, and our thoughts insecure;
Wisdom of Solomon 9:15 for a corruptible body weighs down a soul, and the earthy tent burdens a mind of many cares.
Wisdom of Solomon 9:16 And with difficulty we conjecture things upon earth, and find the things at hand with toil; but who traced the things in heavens?
Wisdom of Solomon 9:17 And who knew your counsel, unless you gave wisdom and sent your holy spirit from the highest places?
Wisdom of Solomon 9:18 And thus the paths of those upon earth were made straight, and humans were taught the things pleasing to you, and were saved by wisdom.

## Chapter 10

Wisdom of Solomon 10:1 She guarded the first-formed father of the world, created alone, and delivered him from his own transgression,
Wisdom of Solomon 10:2 and gave him strength to rule all things.
Wisdom of Solomon 10:3 But an unjust man, departing from her in his anger, perished together with brother-murdering furies.
Wisdom of Solomon 10:4 Because of him, when earth was being flooded, wisdom saved it again, piloting the righteous man through cheap wood.
Wisdom of Solomon 10:5 She also, when nations in agreement of wickedness were confused, knew the righteous man, and kept him blameless before God, and guarded him strong against compassion for a child.
Wisdom of Solomon 10:6 She rescued a righteous man when the ungodly were being destroyed, fleeing the descending fire of the Five Cities,
Wisdom of Solomon 10:7 of which a smoking waste still stands as witness of the wickedness, and plants bearing fruit in unfulfilled seasons, and a standing pillar of salt as a memorial of a disbelieving soul.
Wisdom of Solomon 10:8 For, passing wisdom by, they were not only harmed by not knowing good things, but also left life a memorial of their senselessness, so that they could not even escape notice in the things in which they stumbled.
Wisdom of Solomon 10:9 But wisdom rescued those serving her from toils.
Wisdom of Solomon 10:10 She guided a righteous man, a fugitive from a brother's anger, in straight paths; she showed him God's kingdom, and gave him knowledge of holy things; she prospered him in hardships, and multiplied his toils;
Wisdom of Solomon 10:11 in the greed of those overpowering him, she stood beside him and made him rich;
Wisdom of Solomon 10:12 she guarded him from enemies, and secured him from those lying in wait; and she awarded him a strong contest, so that he might know that piety is mightier than everything.
Wisdom of Solomon 10:13 She did not abandon a righteous man who was sold, but rescued him from sin;
Wisdom of Solomon 10:14 she went down with him into a pit, and did not leave him in bonds, until she brought him scepters of kingship, and authority over those tyrannizing him; and she showed those blaming him false, and gave him everlasting glory.
Wisdom of Solomon 10:15 She rescued a holy people and a blameless seed from a nation of oppressors;
Wisdom of Solomon 10:16 she entered a soul of the Lord's attendant, and opposed fearsome kings with wonders and signs.
Wisdom of Solomon 10:17 She rendered to holy ones a wage of their labors, guided them in a wondrous way, and became for them a shelter by day, and a flame of stars by night.
Wisdom of Solomon 10:18 She brought them across a red sea, and led them through much water;
Wisdom of Solomon 10:19 but she flooded their enemies, and cast them up from the depth of an abyss.
Wisdom of Solomon 10:20 Therefore righteous ones plundered ungodly ones, and sang hymns to your holy name, Lord, and praised with one accord your hand fighting for them;
Wisdom of Solomon 10:21 because wisdom opened the mouth of the mute, and made infants' tongues clear.

## Chapter 11

Wisdom of Solomon 11:1 She prospered their works in a holy prophet's hand.
Wisdom of Solomon 11:2 They traversed an uninhabited wilderness, and pitched tents in untrodden places;
Wisdom of Solomon 11:3 they stood against opponents in war, and repelled enemies.
Wisdom of Solomon 11:4 They thirsted and called upon you, and water was given them from a sheer rock, and a healing of thirst from a hard stone.
Wisdom of Solomon 11:5 For through the things by which their enemies were punished, through these they themselves, being in want, were benefited.
Wisdom of Solomon 11:6 Instead of a spring of an ever-flowing river troubled with gore-filled blood,
Wisdom of Solomon 11:7 for reproof of a decree murdering infants, you gave them abundant water unexpectedly,
Wisdom of Solomon 11:8 showing through the thirst then how you punished the adversaries.
Wisdom of Solomon 11:9 For when they were tested, though disciplined in mercy, they knew how ungodly men, judged with anger, were tortured;
Wisdom of Solomon 11:10 for these you tested as a father admonishing, but those you examined as a severe king condemning.
Wisdom of Solomon 11:11 And absent and present alike they were worn away;
Wisdom of Solomon 11:12 for a double sorrow seized them, and a groaning from memories of things past;
Wisdom of Solomon 11:13 for when they heard that through their own punishments the others were benefited, they perceived the Lord.
Wisdom of Solomon 11:14 For him whom long ago they rejected with mockery, cast out in exposure, at the end of the outcomes they marveled at, having thirsted unlike the righteous.
Wisdom of Solomon 11:15 And in return for the uncomprehending reasonings of their injustice, in which, led astray, they worshiped irrational creeping things and cheap beasts, you sent upon them a multitude of irrational living beings for vengeance,
Wisdom of Solomon 11:16 so that they might know that by the things through which someone sins, by these he is punished.
Wisdom of Solomon 11:17 For your all-powerful hand, which also created the world from formless matter, was not at a loss to send upon them a multitude of bears, or bold lions,
Wisdom of Solomon 11:18 or newly-created unknown beasts full of wrath, either blowing a fire-breathing breath, or winnowing a roar of smoke, or flashing dreadful sparks from their eyes,
Wisdom of Solomon 11:19 of which not only the harm could destroy them altogether, but also the sight, frightening them greatly, destroy them utterly.
Wisdom of Solomon 11:20 And even without these they could fall by one breath, pursued by justice and winnowed by the spirit of your power; but you arranged all things by measure and number and weight.
Wisdom of Solomon 11:21 For to be greatly strong is present with you always, and who will stand against the might of your arm?
Wisdom of Solomon 11:22 Because the whole world before you is like a tipping of scales, and like a morning drop of dew that descended upon earth.
Wisdom of Solomon 11:23 But you have mercy on all, because you can do all things, and overlook humans' sins for repentance.
Wisdom of Solomon 11:24 For you love all things existing, and abhor nothing of what you made; for neither would you have made something while hating it.
Wisdom of Solomon 11:25 And how would anything have remained if you had not willed, or what was not called by you have been preserved?
Wisdom of Solomon 11:26 But you spare all things, because they are yours, Master who loves souls;

## Chapter 12

Wisdom of Solomon 12:1 for your incorruptible spirit is in all things.
Wisdom of Solomon 12:2 Therefore you reprove those falling aside little by little, and, reminding them of the things in which they sin, admonish them, so that, freed from wickedness, they may believe in you, Lord.
Wisdom of Solomon 12:3 For also the former inhabitants of your holy land,
Wisdom of Solomon 12:4 hating them for doing most hateful things, works of sorceries and unholy rites,
Wisdom of Solomon 12:5 and merciless murders of children, and a feast eating entrails of human flesh and blood, initiates from the midst of a ritual band,
Wisdom of Solomon 12:6 and parents, murderers of helpless souls, you wished to destroy through our fathers' hands,
Wisdom of Solomon 12:7 so that the land most honored of all with you might receive a worthy colony of God's servants.
Wisdom of Solomon 12:8 But you spared even these as humans, and sent wasps as forerunners of your army, so that they might destroy them little by little.
Wisdom of Solomon 12:9 Not being unable to give the ungodly into the hands of the righteous in battle, or to wipe them out at once with dreadful beasts or a severe word,
Wisdom of Solomon 12:10 but judging little by little, you gave a place of repentance, not being ignorant that their origin is wicked, and their wickedness innate, and that their reasoning will certainly not be changed for the age.
Wisdom of Solomon 12:11 For it was a seed accursed from the beginning, nor did you give immunity for the things in which they sinned through being wary of anyone.
Wisdom of Solomon 12:12 For who will say, What did you do? Or who will stand against your judgment? And who will accuse you concerning nations that have perished, which you made? Or who will come to confront you as an avenger against unjust humans?
Wisdom of Solomon 12:13 For neither is there a god except you, who cares for all, so that you should show that you did not judge unjustly,
Wisdom of Solomon 12:14 nor will a king or tyrant be able to look you in the face concerning those whom you punished.
Wisdom of Solomon 12:15 But being righteous, you govern all things righteously, considering it foreign to your power to condemn the one who ought not to be punished.
Wisdom of Solomon 12:16 For your strength is the beginning of righteousness, and your mastering all things makes you spare all things.
Wisdom of Solomon 12:17 For you display strength when disbelieved concerning perfection of power, and among those who know, you expose boldness;
Wisdom of Solomon 12:18 but you, mastering strength, judge in gentleness, and administer us with much sparing; for the ability is present with you whenever you will.
Wisdom of Solomon 12:19 And you taught your people through such works that the righteous man must love humans, and made your sons hopeful, because you give repentance for sins.
Wisdom of Solomon 12:20 For if you punished enemies of your servants and those owing death with such attention and indulgence, giving times and a place through which they might be freed from wickedness,
Wisdom of Solomon 12:21 with how much exactness did you judge your sons, to whose fathers you gave oaths and agreements of good promises?
Wisdom of Solomon 12:22 Therefore, disciplining us, you scourge our enemies ten-thousandfold, so that, judging, we may consider your goodness, and being judged, expect mercy.
Wisdom of Solomon 12:23 Therefore also those who lived unjustly in life's senselessness you tortured through their own abominations;
Wisdom of Solomon 12:24 for they wandered farther than the ways of error, supposing as gods even the dishonored things among shameful living beings, deceived like senseless infants.
Wisdom of Solomon 12:25 Therefore, as to unreasoning children, you sent judgment for mockery.
Wisdom of Solomon 12:26 But those not admonished by games of rebuke will experience judgment worthy of God.
Wisdom of Solomon 12:27 For at the things through which they themselves, suffering, were indignant, at these, whom they considered gods, being punished by them, seeing him whom long ago they denied knowing, they recognized a true God; therefore also the end of condemnation came upon them.

## Chapter 13

Wisdom of Solomon 13:1 For all humans were vain by nature, in whom ignorance of God was present, and from the good things seen they were not strong enough to know the one who is, nor, attending to the works, recognized the craftsman,
Wisdom of Solomon 13:2 but considered either fire or wind or swift air or a circle of stars or violent water or heaven's luminaries as gods, governors of the world.
Wisdom of Solomon 13:3 If, delighting in their beauty, they supposed these gods, let them know how much better than these the Master is, for the originator of beauty created them;
Wisdom of Solomon 13:4 but if astonished at power and working, let them understand from them how much mightier the one making them is;
Wisdom of Solomon 13:5 for from the greatness and beauty of creatures, their originator is beheld proportionately.
Wisdom of Solomon 13:6 But nevertheless upon these there is little blame, for perhaps they themselves also wander while seeking God and wishing to find him;
Wisdom of Solomon 13:7 for, moving among his works, they search out, and are persuaded by the sight, because the things seen are beautiful.
Wisdom of Solomon 13:8 But again, neither are they pardonable;
Wisdom of Solomon 13:9 for if they were strong enough to know so much that they could conjecture the world, how did they not find the Master of these things more swiftly?
Wisdom of Solomon 13:10 But miserable are they, and their hopes among the dead, who called works of human hands gods, gold and silver, a work of skill, and likenesses of living beings, or a useless stone, a work of an ancient hand.
Wisdom of Solomon 13:11 And if also some woodcutting craftsman, sawing out an easily moved tree, skillfully scraped all its bark around, and, crafting it comely, made a useful vessel for life's service,
Wisdom of Solomon 13:12 and, consuming the scraps of the work for preparing food, was filled,
Wisdom of Solomon 13:13 but taking the scrap from them useful for nothing, crooked wood grown together with knots, carved it in the care of his leisure, and shaped it with skill of understanding, likened it to a human's image,
Wisdom of Solomon 13:14 or made it like some cheap living being, smearing it with red ocher and reddening its color with pigment, and smearing every stain in it,
Wisdom of Solomon 13:15 and making for it a dwelling worthy of it, placed it in a wall, securing it with iron.
Wisdom of Solomon 13:16 So that it might not fall, then, he provided for it beforehand, knowing that it is unable to help itself; for it is indeed an image, and has need of help.
Wisdom of Solomon 13:17 But praying concerning his possessions and marriages and children, he is not ashamed to speak to the soulless thing, and concerning health he calls upon the weak thing,
Wisdom of Solomon 13:18 and concerning life asks the dead thing, and concerning assistance supplicates the most inexperienced thing, and concerning a journey, that which cannot even use a step,
Wisdom of Solomon 13:19 and concerning gain and work and success of hands, he asks vigor of the thing most inactive with its hands.

## Chapter 14

Wisdom of Solomon 14:1 Again, someone preparing a voyage, and about to traverse wild waves, calls upon wood more rotten than the boat carrying him.
Wisdom of Solomon 14:2 For desire for gains devised that, and wisdom, the craftswoman, made it;
Wisdom of Solomon 14:3 but your providence, Father, pilots it, because you gave a way even in sea, and a secure path in waves,
Wisdom of Solomon 14:4 showing that you can save from everything, so that someone may embark even without skill.
Wisdom of Solomon 14:5 And you wish the works of your wisdom not to be idle; therefore humans entrust souls even to the smallest wood, and passing through a surge on a raft, were saved.
Wisdom of Solomon 14:6 For also in the beginning, when arrogant giants were perishing, the world's hope, taking refuge upon a raft, left the world a seed of birth, piloted by your hand.
Wisdom of Solomon 14:7 For blessed is wood through which righteousness comes;
Wisdom of Solomon 14:8 but the handmade thing is accursed, both it and the one making it, because the one was working, and the corruptible thing was named a god.
Wisdom of Solomon 14:9 For equally hateful to God are both the one acting ungodly and his ungodliness;
Wisdom of Solomon 14:10 for what was done will also be punished together with the doer.
Wisdom of Solomon 14:11 Therefore there will also be an inspection upon idols of nations, because in God's creation they became an abomination, and stumbling blocks for humans' souls, and a snare for feet of the senseless.
Wisdom of Solomon 14:12 For the devising of idols is a beginning of fornication, and their invention corruption of life.
Wisdom of Solomon 14:13 For neither did they exist from the beginning, nor will they be for the age;
Wisdom of Solomon 14:14 for through humans' vainglory they entered the world, and therefore their swift end was devised.
Wisdom of Solomon 14:15 For a father worn away by untimely grief, making an image of a child swiftly taken away, honored the formerly dead human now as a god, and handed down mysteries and rites to those under his hand;
Wisdom of Solomon 14:16 then, strengthened with time, the ungodly custom was guarded as law.
Wisdom of Solomon 14:17 And by tyrants' commands carved things were worshiped; those whom humans could not honor in sight because they dwelt far away, reproducing their appearance from afar, they made a visible image of the honored king, so that through their zeal they might flatter the absent one as present.
Wisdom of Solomon 14:18 And the craftsman's ambition urged even those ignorant toward intensified worship;
Wisdom of Solomon 14:19 for he, perhaps wishing to please a ruler, forced the likeness toward greater beauty by his skill;
Wisdom of Solomon 14:20 and the multitude, drawn by the charm of the workmanship, reckoned the human honored a little before now an object of reverence.
Wisdom of Solomon 14:21 And this became an ambush for life, because humans, enslaved either to misfortune or tyranny, placed the incommunicable name upon stones and wood.
Wisdom of Solomon 14:22 Then it was not enough to wander concerning the knowledge of God, but also, living in a great war of ignorance, they call such great evils peace.
Wisdom of Solomon 14:23 For conducting either child-murdering rites or secret mysteries or frenzied revels of strange customs,
Wisdom of Solomon 14:24 they no longer guard either lives or marriages pure, and one either kills another by ambushing, or pains him by adultery.
Wisdom of Solomon 14:25 And blood and murder, theft and deceit, corruption, unfaithfulness, disturbance, perjury hold all things mingled together,
Wisdom of Solomon 14:26 tumult of good things, forgetfulness of grace, defilement of souls, alteration of birth, disorder of marriages, adultery and licentiousness.
Wisdom of Solomon 14:27 For the worship of nameless idols is a beginning and cause and end of every evil;
Wisdom of Solomon 14:28 for either rejoicing, they have gone mad, or prophesy false things, or live unjustly, or swear falsely readily;
Wisdom of Solomon 14:29 for trusting in soulless idols, having sworn evilly, they do not expect to be harmed.
Wisdom of Solomon 14:30 But justice will pursue them for both things, because they thought evilly concerning God, attending to idols, and swore unjustly in deceit, despising holiness;
Wisdom of Solomon 14:31 for it is not the power of those by whom they swear, but the justice of sinners, that always pursues the transgression of the unjust.

## Chapter 15

Wisdom of Solomon 15:1 But you, our God, are kind and true, long-suffering, and administering all things in mercy.
Wisdom of Solomon 15:2 For even if we sin, we are yours, knowing your might; but we will not sin, knowing that we have been reckoned to you.
Wisdom of Solomon 15:3 For understanding you is whole righteousness, and knowing your might a root of immortality.
Wisdom of Solomon 15:4 For neither did humans' evil-devising invention lead us astray, nor the fruitless toil of shadow-painters, a form stained with varied colors,
Wisdom of Solomon 15:5 the sight of which comes to the senseless as desire, and he longs for the breathless form of a dead image.
Wisdom of Solomon 15:6 Lovers of evils and worthy of such hopes are both those making them and those longing for them and those revering them.
Wisdom of Solomon 15:7 For also a potter, pressing soft earth, laboriously molds each thing for our service; but from the same clay he molded both vessels serving clean works and the opposite ones, all alike; and of these, what the use of each of either sort is, the clay-worker is judge.
Wisdom of Solomon 15:8 And laboring evilly, he molds a vain god from the same clay, he who, coming into being from earth a little before, after a little goes to that from which he was taken, having been required to pay the debt of his soul.
Wisdom of Solomon 15:9 But his care is not that he is about to die, nor that he has a life ending shortly, but he contends with gold-workers and silver-casters, and imitates bronze-molders, and considers it glory that he molds counterfeit things.
Wisdom of Solomon 15:10 His heart is ashes, and his hope cheaper than earth, and his life more dishonored than clay,
Wisdom of Solomon 15:11 because he did not know the one molding him, and the one breathing into him a working soul, and breathing in a life-giving spirit,
Wisdom of Solomon 15:12 but they reckoned our life to be a game, and living a profitable festival, for he says one must gain from wherever, even from evil.
Wisdom of Solomon 15:13 For this man, beyond all, knows that he sins, making easily broken vessels and carved things from earthy matter.
Wisdom of Solomon 15:14 And all the enemies of your people, who oppressed it, are most senseless and more wretched than an infant's soul,
Wisdom of Solomon 15:15 because they reckoned even all the nations' idols gods, which have neither use of eyes for seeing, nor nostrils for drawing air, nor ears to hear, nor fingers of hands for feeling, and their feet are idle for stepping.
Wisdom of Solomon 15:16 For a human made them, and one who has borrowed the spirit molded them; for no human is strong enough to mold a god like himself;
Wisdom of Solomon 15:17 but being mortal, he works a dead thing with lawless hands; for he is better than his objects of reverence, in that he indeed lived, but those never. –
Wisdom of Solomon 15:18 And they revere the most hateful living beings; for compared in folly, they are worse than the others;
Wisdom of Solomon 15:19 nor do they happen to be beautiful enough to be desired, as in the appearance of living beings, but they have also escaped God's praise and his blessing.

## Chapter 16

Wisdom of Solomon 16:1 Therefore through like things they were punished worthily, and through a multitude of beasts were tortured.
Wisdom of Solomon 16:2 Instead of which punishment, benefiting your people, you prepared for the desire of appetite a strange taste as food, a quail,
Wisdom of Solomon 16:3 so that those, desiring food, through the hideousness of the things sent upon them, might turn away even necessary appetite, but these, becoming needy for a little time, might share even in a strange taste.
Wisdom of Solomon 16:4 For it was necessary that unavoidable want come upon those tyrannizing, but that these only be shown how their enemies were tortured.
Wisdom of Solomon 16:5 For also when a dreadful fury of beasts came upon them, and they were being destroyed by bites of crooked serpents, your anger did not remain to the end;
Wisdom of Solomon 16:6 but for admonition they were troubled for a little time, having a token of salvation for remembrance of the commandment of your law;
Wisdom of Solomon 16:7 for the one turning was saved not through what was beheld, but through you, the Savior of all.
Wisdom of Solomon 16:8 And by this too you persuaded our enemies that you are the one rescuing from every evil;
Wisdom of Solomon 16:9 for bites of locusts and flies killed those, and no healing was found for their soul, because they were worthy to be punished by such things;
Wisdom of Solomon 16:10 but not even teeth of venomous dragons overcame your sons, for your mercy came against them and healed them.
Wisdom of Solomon 16:11 For they were stung for a reminder of your oracles, and were swiftly saved, so that, falling into deep forgetfulness, they might not become withdrawn from your beneficence.
Wisdom of Solomon 16:12 For neither herb nor poultice healed them, but your word, Lord, which heals all.
Wisdom of Solomon 16:13 For you have authority over life and death, and bring down into gates of Hades, and bring up;
Wisdom of Solomon 16:14 and a human indeed kills by his wickedness, but does not turn back a spirit that has gone out, nor release a soul taken away.
Wisdom of Solomon 16:15 But to flee your hand is impossible;
Wisdom of Solomon 16:16 for ungodly men, denying knowing you, were scourged in the strength of your arm, pursued by strange rains and hails and unavoidable showers, and consumed by fire.
Wisdom of Solomon 16:17 For the most unexpected thing—in water which extinguishes all, the fire worked more, for the world fights for the righteous;
Wisdom of Solomon 16:18 for at one time a flame was tamed, so that it might not burn up the living beings sent against the ungodly, but that they themselves, seeing, might know that they are driven by God's judgment;
Wisdom of Solomon 16:19 and at another time, even amid water, it burns beyond fire's power, so that it may destroy an unjust land's produce.
Wisdom of Solomon 16:20 Instead of these things, you fed your people angels' food, and provided them ready bread from heaven without toil, capable of every pleasure and suited to every taste;
Wisdom of Solomon 16:21 for your substance manifested your sweetness toward children, and, serving the desire of the one taking it, it was transformed into whatever someone wished.
Wisdom of Solomon 16:22 And snow and ice endured fire and were not melted, so that they might know that fire destroyed the enemies' fruits, burning in the hail and flashing in the rains;
Wisdom of Solomon 16:23 but this again, so that righteous ones might be nourished, has forgotten even its own power.
Wisdom of Solomon 16:24 For creation, serving you who made it, is intensified for punishment against the unjust, and relaxed for beneficence on behalf of those who have trusted in you.
Wisdom of Solomon 16:25 Therefore also then, being altered into all things, it served your all-nourishing gift according to the will of those needing it,
Wisdom of Solomon 16:26 so that your sons, whom you loved, Lord, might learn that it is not the origins of fruits that nourish a human, but your word preserves those believing you.
Wisdom of Solomon 16:27 For that which was not destroyed by fire, simply being warmed by a short ray of sun, melted,
Wisdom of Solomon 16:28 so that it might be known that one must anticipate the sun for thanksgiving to you, and petition you toward the rising of light;
Wisdom of Solomon 16:29 for an ungrateful man's hope will melt like wintry frost, and flow like useless water.

## Chapter 17

Wisdom of Solomon 17:1 For your judgments are great and difficult to recount; therefore undisciplined souls were led astray.
Wisdom of Solomon 17:2 For lawless men, supposing they could oppress a holy nation, lay as prisoners of darkness and captives of a long night, shut beneath roofs, fugitives from everlasting providence.
Wisdom of Solomon 17:3 For, thinking to escape notice in secret sins beneath a lightless covering of forgetfulness, they were scattered, terribly astonished, and disturbed by apparitions.
Wisdom of Solomon 17:4 For neither did the recess holding them guard them without fear, but sounds disturbing them resounded around them, and gloomy phantoms with unsmiling faces appeared.
Wisdom of Solomon 17:5 And no force of fire prevailed to illuminate, nor did bright flames of stars endure to light that gloomy night.
Wisdom of Solomon 17:6 But only a spontaneous blaze full of fear shone through for them, and, greatly terrified, they considered the things seen worse than that sight not beheld.
Wisdom of Solomon 17:7 And mockeries of magical skill lay low, and an insulting exposure of boastfulness concerning prudence;
Wisdom of Solomon 17:8 for those promising to drive away terrors and disturbances of a sick soul, these were sick with a laughable apprehension.
Wisdom of Solomon 17:9 For even if nothing disturbing frightened them, scared away by beasts passing and creeping things hissing, they perished trembling, refusing even to look upon the air, which can be fled from nowhere.
Wisdom of Solomon 17:10 For wickedness, condemned by its own witness, is a timid thing, and, held fast by conscience, has always taken on harsh things;
Wisdom of Solomon 17:11 for fear is nothing except a betrayal of the helps from reasoning,
Wisdom of Solomon 17:12 and expectation, being weaker within, reckons ignorance greater than the cause providing the torture.
Wisdom of Solomon 17:13 But those, sleeping the same sleep through the truly powerless night which also came from the recesses of powerless Hades,
