Wisdom of Solomon 17:14 were at one time driven by marvels of phantoms, and at another paralyzed by betrayal of the soul; for sudden and unexpected fear was poured upon them.
Wisdom of Solomon 17:15 Then thus, whoever indeed was there, falling down, was guarded, shut in the prison without iron;
Wisdom of Solomon 17:16 for whether someone was a farmer or shepherd or worker of labors in solitude, overtaken, he endured the necessity difficult to escape, for all were bound with one chain of darkness;
Wisdom of Solomon 17:17 whether a hissing wind, or a melodious sound of birds about luxuriant branches, or the rhythm of water going violently, or a harsh crash of rocks hurled down,
Wisdom of Solomon 17:18 or an unseen running of leaping living beings, or a voice of roaring, harshest beasts, or an echo reflected from a hollow of mountains, frightening them greatly, paralyzed them.
Wisdom of Solomon 17:19 For the whole world was lit by radiant light, and held fast by unhindered works;
Wisdom of Solomon 17:20 but upon those alone a heavy night was spread, an image of the darkness about to receive them, and to themselves they were heavier than darkness.

## Chapter 18

Wisdom of Solomon 18:1 But for your holy ones there was greatest light; hearing their voice but not seeing their form, they pronounced them blessed because those too had not suffered,
Wisdom of Solomon 18:2 and because, previously wronged, they do not harm, they gave thanks, and begged favor for the difference.
Wisdom of Solomon 18:3 Instead of these things, you provided a pillar burning with fire, a guide of an unknown journey, and a harmless sun of an honorable sojourn abroad.
Wisdom of Solomon 18:4 For those were worthy to be deprived of light and imprisoned in darkness, who guarded your sons shut in, through whom the incorruptible light of law was about to be given to the world.
Wisdom of Solomon 18:5 And when they planned to kill the infants of the holy ones, and one child was exposed and saved, for reproof you took away their multitude of children, and destroyed them together in violent water.
Wisdom of Solomon 18:6 That night was foreknown by our fathers, so that, knowing securely the oaths which they trusted, they might be encouraged.
Wisdom of Solomon 18:7 Salvation of righteous ones, and destruction of enemies, was awaited by your people;
Wisdom of Solomon 18:8 for by that with which you punished the adversaries, by this you glorified us, calling us to yourself.
Wisdom of Solomon 18:9 For in secret holy children of good men sacrificed, and in agreement established the law of divinity, that the holy ones would share alike in the same good things and dangers, already singing beforehand the fathers' praises.
Wisdom of Solomon 18:10 And the discordant shout of enemies echoed back, and a pitiable voice of lamented children was carried abroad;
Wisdom of Solomon 18:11 and with like justice a slave was punished together with a master, and a commoner suffered the same things as a king,
Wisdom of Solomon 18:12 and all together, under one name of death, had uncountable dead; for neither were the living sufficient for burying, since at one tipping their more honored offspring had been destroyed.
Wisdom of Solomon 18:13 For disbelieving all things because of the sorceries, at the destruction of the firstborn they acknowledged the people to be God's son.
Wisdom of Solomon 18:14 For while quiet silence encompassed all things, and night in its own swiftness was at its middle,
Wisdom of Solomon 18:15 your all-powerful word leaped from heavens, from royal thrones, a severe warrior, into the midst of the doomed land, carrying your unhypocritical command as a sharp sword,
Wisdom of Solomon 18:16 and, standing, filled all things with death, and indeed touched heaven, but stood upon earth.
Wisdom of Solomon 18:17 Then immediately visions of dreadful dreams disturbed them, and unexpected fears came upon them,
Wisdom of Solomon 18:18 and one here, another there, flung half-dead, disclosed the cause through which they were dying;
Wisdom of Solomon 18:19 for the dreams troubling them indicated this beforehand, so that they might not perish ignorant of that through which they suffer evilly.
Wisdom of Solomon 18:20 And an experience of death touched even the righteous, and a breaking of a multitude occurred in a wilderness. But the anger did not remain for long;
Wisdom of Solomon 18:21 for a blameless man, hastening, fought for them, bringing the weapon of his own service, prayer and propitiation of incense; he stood against the wrath, and placed an end to the misfortune, showing that he is your attendant;
Wisdom of Solomon 18:22 and he overcame the anger not by bodily strength, not by the working of weapons, but by a word subjected the punisher, reminding him of fathers' oaths and covenants.
Wisdom of Solomon 18:23 For when dead men had already fallen in heaps upon one another, standing between, he cut off the anger, and severed the way toward the living.
Wisdom of Solomon 18:24 For upon a robe reaching the feet was the whole world, and fathers' glories upon a carving of stones in four rows, and your majesty upon the diadem of his head.
Wisdom of Solomon 18:25 To these the destroyer yielded, and these he feared; for the experience of the anger alone was sufficient.

## Chapter 19

Wisdom of Solomon 19:1 But upon the ungodly merciless wrath came to the end; for he also foreknew their future things,
Wisdom of Solomon 19:2 that they themselves, permitting departure and sending them forth eagerly, would pursue them, having changed their minds.
Wisdom of Solomon 19:3 For still holding their griefs in their hands, and lamenting at graves of the dead, they drew upon themselves another reasoning of folly, and those whom, supplicating, they expelled, these they pursued as fugitives.
Wisdom of Solomon 19:4 For deserving necessity drew them to this end, and cast in forgetfulness of the things that had happened, so that they might further complete the punishment lacking to the tortures,
Wisdom of Solomon 19:5 and your people might experience an unexpected journey, but those find a strange death.
Wisdom of Solomon 19:6 For the whole creation in its own kind was again shaped anew, serving your commands, so that your servants might be guarded unharmed.
Wisdom of Solomon 19:7 The cloud overshadowing the camp, and an emergence of dry land from previously existing water was beheld, an unhindered way from a red sea, and a grass-bearing plain from a violent surge;
Wisdom of Solomon 19:8 through which those sheltered by your hand passed as an entire nation, beholding wondrous marvels.
Wisdom of Solomon 19:9 For like horses they grazed, and like lambs leaped about, praising you, Lord, who rescued them.
Wisdom of Solomon 19:10 For they still remembered the things in their sojourn, how instead of the birth of living beings the earth brought forth a gnat, and instead of aquatic beings the river belched forth a multitude of frogs.
Wisdom of Solomon 19:11 And later they also saw a new birth of birds, when, led on by desire, they asked for foods of luxury;
Wisdom of Solomon 19:12 for as consolation a quail came up for them from sea.
Wisdom of Solomon 19:13 And the punishments came upon sinners not without the preceding proofs in the violence of thunderbolts; for they suffered righteously for their own wickednesses, for they also practiced harsher hatred of strangers.
Wisdom of Solomon 19:14 For the former did not receive the unknown ones present; but these enslaved strangers who were benefactors.
Wisdom of Solomon 19:15 And not only this, but indeed there will be some inspection of them, since they received the outsiders hatefully;
Wisdom of Solomon 19:16 but those receiving with festivities the ones who had already shared the same rights afflicted them with dreadful toils.
Wisdom of Solomon 19:17 And they were also struck with blindness, like those at the righteous man's doors, when, clothed in gaping darkness, each sought the passage of his own doors.
Wisdom of Solomon 19:18 For the elements, being retuned through one another, as notes in a psaltery change the name of the rhythm, always remaining in sound, which it is possible to conjecture precisely from the sight of the things that have happened;
Wisdom of Solomon 19:19 for land beings were changed into aquatic beings, and swimming beings went upon earth;
Wisdom of Solomon 19:20 fire prevailed in water with its own power, and water forgot its extinguishing nature;
Wisdom of Solomon 19:21 conversely, flames did not wither the flesh of easily destroyed living beings walking among them, nor the meltable, ice-like, easily melted kind of ambrosial food.
Wisdom of Solomon 19:22 For in all things, Lord, you magnified your people, and glorified them, and did not overlook them, standing beside them in every time and place.

# Sirach

The Apostolic Bible. Public domain. https://apostolic-bible.ysys9.chatgpt.site/license.html


## Chapter 0

Sirach 0:1 Many and great things having been given to us through the law and the prophets
Sirach 0:2 and the others who have followed in their manner,
Sirach 0:3 for which it is necessary to praise Israel for discipline and wisdom,
Sirach 0:4 and since it is necessary that not only the readers themselves become knowledgeable,
Sirach 0:5 but also that those loving learning be able to be useful to those outside,
Sirach 0:6 both speaking and writing,
Sirach 0:7 my grandfather Iesous, having given himself more fully
Sirach 0:8 to the reading of the law
Sirach 0:9 and of the prophets
Sirach 0:10 and of the other ancestral books,
Sirach 0:11 and having acquired sufficient proficiency in these,
Sirach 0:12 was led himself also to write something of the things pertaining to discipline and wisdom,
Sirach 0:13 so that those loving learning, becoming engaged in these things also,
Sirach 0:14 might advance much more through lawful living.
Sirach 0:15 Therefore you have been exhorted
Sirach 0:16 with goodwill and attention
Sirach 0:17 to do the reading,
Sirach 0:18 and to have forgiveness
Sirach 0:19 for the things in which we may seem,
Sirach 0:20 in some of the expressions labored over in the translation, to be unable;
Sirach 0:21 for they do not have equal force,
Sirach 0:22 the things themselves said in Hebrew in themselves, and when transferred into another tongue;
Sirach 0:23 and not only these things,
Sirach 0:24 but also the law itself and the prophecies
Sirach 0:25 and the rest of the books
Sirach 0:26 have no small difference when said in themselves.
Sirach 0:27 For in the thirty-eighth year under King Euergetes,
Sirach 0:28 having arrived in Egypt and spent time there,
Sirach 0:29 finding a likeness of no little discipline,
Sirach 0:30 I considered it most necessary myself also to bring some zeal and diligence to translate this book,
Sirach 0:31 bringing much wakefulness and knowledge
Sirach 0:32 in the interval of time,
Sirach 0:33 in order, having brought the book to an end, to publish it,
Sirach 0:34 and for those in the sojourn wishing to love learning,
Sirach 0:35 preparing their characters beforehand,
Sirach 0:36 to live lawfully.

## Chapter 1

Sirach 1:1 All wisdom is from the Lord, and is with him for the age.
Sirach 1:2 Who will count the sand of seas and drops of rain and days of an age?
Sirach 1:3 Who will trace heaven's height and earth's breadth and an abyss and wisdom?
Sirach 1:4 Wisdom has been created prior to all things, and understanding of prudence from an age.
Sirach 1:6 To whom was wisdom's root revealed? And who knew her skillful deeds?
Sirach 1:8 One is wise, exceedingly fearsome, seated upon his throne.
Sirach 1:9 The Lord himself created her, and saw and counted her, and poured her out upon all his works,
Sirach 1:10 with all flesh according to his giving, and supplied her to those loving him.
Sirach 1:11 Fear of the Lord is glory and boasting and gladness and a crown of exultation.
Sirach 1:12 Fear of the Lord will delight a heart, and give gladness and joy and length of days.
Sirach 1:13 For the one fearing the Lord it will be well at the last, and on the day of his end he will be blessed.
Sirach 1:14 A beginning of wisdom is fearing the Lord, and with faithful ones she was created together for them in a womb.
Sirach 1:15 Among humans she nested an everlasting foundation, and with their seed she will be entrusted.
Sirach 1:16 Fullness of wisdom is fearing the Lord, and she makes them drunk from her fruits;
Sirach 1:17 she will fill their whole house with desirable things, and the storehouses with her produce.
Sirach 1:18 A crown of wisdom is fear of the Lord, making peace and health of healing flourish.
Sirach 1:19 And he saw and counted her; he showered knowledge and understanding of comprehension, and raised the glory of those holding her.
Sirach 1:20 A root of wisdom is fearing the Lord, and her branches are length of days.
Sirach 1:22 Unjust wrath will not be able to be justified; for the tipping of his wrath is a fall for him.
Sirach 1:23 A long-suffering man will hold fast until a time, and afterward gladness will spring up for him;
Sirach 1:24 until a time he will hide his words, and lips of many will recount his understanding.
Sirach 1:25 In treasures of wisdom are parables of knowledge, but reverence for God is an abomination to a sinner.
Sirach 1:26 Desiring wisdom, preserve commandments, and the Lord will supply her to you.
Sirach 1:27 For wisdom and discipline are fear of the Lord, and his good pleasure is faith and meekness.
Sirach 1:28 Do not disobey fear of the Lord, and do not approach him with a double heart.
Sirach 1:29 Do not act hypocritically in humans' mouths, and attend to your lips.
Sirach 1:30 Do not exalt yourself, so that you may not fall and bring dishonor upon your soul; and the Lord will uncover your hidden things, and cast you down in the midst of an assembly, because you did not approach in fear of the Lord, and your heart is full of deceit.

## Chapter 2

Sirach 2:1 Child, if you approach to serve the Lord, prepare your soul for testing;
Sirach 2:2 make your heart straight, and endure, and do not hasten in a time of affliction;
Sirach 2:3 cling to him, and do not depart, so that you may be increased at your last things.
Sirach 2:4 Receive everything which may be brought upon you, and be long-suffering in changes of your humiliation;
Sirach 2:5 because gold is tested in fire, and acceptable humans in a furnace of humiliation.
Sirach 2:6 Believe him, and he will help you; make your ways straight, and hope in him.
Sirach 2:7 You who fear the Lord, await his mercy, and do not turn aside, so that you may not fall.
Sirach 2:8 You who fear the Lord, believe him, and your wage will certainly not fail.
Sirach 2:9 You who fear the Lord, hope for good things and for gladness of an age and mercy.
Sirach 2:10 Look into ancient generations and see; who trusted in the Lord and was put to shame? Or who remained in his fear and was abandoned? Or who called upon him, and he overlooked him?
Sirach 2:11 Because the Lord is compassionate and merciful, and forgives sins and saves in a time of affliction.
Sirach 2:12 Woe to timid hearts and slack hands and a sinner stepping upon two paths.
Sirach 2:13 Woe to a slack heart, because it does not believe; therefore it will not be sheltered.
Sirach 2:14 Woe to you who have lost endurance; and what will you do when the Lord inspects?
Sirach 2:15 Those fearing the Lord will not disobey his words, and those loving him will keep his ways.
Sirach 2:16 Those fearing the Lord will seek his good pleasure, and those loving him will be filled with the law.
Sirach 2:17 Those fearing the Lord will prepare their hearts, and humble their souls before him.
Sirach 2:18 We will fall into the Lord's hands, and not into humans' hands; for as his majesty is, so also is his mercy.

## Chapter 3

Sirach 3:1 Hear me, the father, children, and do thus, so that you may be saved;
Sirach 3:2 for the Lord glorified a father over children, and confirmed a mother's judgment over sons.
Sirach 3:3 The one honoring a father makes atonement for sins,
Sirach 3:4 and the one glorifying his mother is like the one storing treasure.
Sirach 3:5 The one honoring a father will be gladdened by children, and will be heard on the day of his prayer.
Sirach 3:6 The one glorifying a father will have long days, and the one hearing the Lord will give his mother rest;
Sirach 3:7 and he will serve those who begot him as masters.
Sirach 3:8 In deed and word honor your father, so that a blessing from him may come upon you;
Sirach 3:9 for a father's blessing establishes children's houses, but a mother's curse uproots foundations.
Sirach 3:10 Do not be glorified in your father's dishonor, for a father's dishonor is no glory for you;
Sirach 3:11 for a human's glory comes from his father's honor, and a mother in disrepute is a reproach to children.
Sirach 3:12 Child, help your father in old age, and do not grieve him in his life;
Sirach 3:13 and even if he fails in understanding, have forgiveness, and do not dishonor him in all your strength.
Sirach 3:14 For mercy toward a father will not be forgotten, and will be built up for you instead of sins.
Sirach 3:15 In the day of your affliction you will be remembered; as fair weather upon frost, so your sins will be dissolved.
Sirach 3:16 The one abandoning a father is like a blasphemer, and the one angering his mother has been accursed by the Lord.
Sirach 3:17 Child, conduct your works in meekness, and you will be loved by an acceptable human.
Sirach 3:18 As great as you are, so much humble yourself, and before the Lord you will find grace;
Sirach 3:20 because the Lord's dominion is great, and he is glorified by the humble.
Sirach 3:21 Do not seek things harder than you, and do not examine things stronger than you;
Sirach 3:22 what was commanded you, consider these things, for you have no need of hidden things.
Sirach 3:23 Do not meddle in things beyond your works; for things greater than humans' understanding were shown you.
Sirach 3:24 For their supposition led many astray, and an evil suspicion made their thoughts slip.
Sirach 3:26 A hard heart will be afflicted at the last, and the one loving danger will perish in it.
Sirach 3:27 A hard heart will be burdened with toils, and the sinner will add sin upon sins.
Sirach 3:28 For an arrogant man's affliction there is no healing; for a plant of wickedness has taken root in him.
Sirach 3:29 An understanding man's heart will consider a parable, and a hearer's ear is a wise man's desire.
Sirach 3:30 Water will extinguish a flaming fire, and almsgiving will make atonement for sins.
Sirach 3:31 The one repaying favors remembers for the things after these, and in the time of his fall will find support.

## Chapter 4

Sirach 4:1 Child, do not deprive the poor man's life, and do not delay needy eyes.
Sirach 4:2 Do not grieve a hungry soul, and do not anger a man in his want.
Sirach 4:3 Do not further trouble an angered heart, and do not delay a gift to one needing it.
Sirach 4:4 Do not refuse an afflicted suppliant, and do not turn your face away from a poor man.
Sirach 4:5 Do not turn an eye away from one begging, and do not give a human a place to curse you;
Sirach 4:6 for when he curses you in bitterness of his soul, the one who made him will hear his entreaty.
Sirach 4:7 Make yourself beloved by an assembly, and humble your head before a great man.
Sirach 4:8 Incline your ear to a poor man, and answer him peaceable things in meekness.
Sirach 4:9 Deliver one wronged from the hand of one wronging, and do not lose heart when you judge.
Sirach 4:10 Become like a father to orphans, and in place of a husband to their mother; and you will be like a son of the Most High, and he will love you more than your mother.
Sirach 4:11 Wisdom raised her sons, and takes hold of those seeking her.
Sirach 4:12 The one loving her loves life, and those rising early for her will be filled with gladness.
Sirach 4:13 The one holding her will inherit glory, and where he enters, the Lord blesses.
Sirach 4:14 Those serving her will minister to a holy one, and the Lord loves those loving her.
Sirach 4:15 The one obeying her will judge nations, and the one attending to her will dwell confidently.
Sirach 4:16 If he trusts, he will inherit her, and his generations will be in possession;
Sirach 4:17 because at first she will walk with him crookedly, bring fear and timidity upon him, and torment him with her discipline, until she trusts his soul, and will test him with her ordinances;
Sirach 4:18 and again she will return straight toward him, and gladden him, and reveal her hidden things to him.
Sirach 4:19 If he wanders away, she will abandon him, and deliver him into the hands of his fall.
Sirach 4:20 Keep a time, and guard yourself from evil, and do not be ashamed concerning your soul;
Sirach 4:21 for there is shame bringing sin, and there is shame which is glory and grace.
Sirach 4:22 Do not accept a face against your soul, and do not show deference to your fall.
Sirach 4:23 Do not withhold a word in a time of need;
Sirach 4:24 for in a word wisdom will be known, and discipline in an utterance of a tongue.
Sirach 4:25 Do not contradict the truth, and be ashamed concerning your lack of discipline.
Sirach 4:26 Do not be ashamed to confess your sins, and do not force a river's flow.
Sirach 4:27 And do not lay yourself beneath a foolish human, and do not accept a ruler's face.
Sirach 4:28 Struggle for the truth until death, and the Lord God will fight for you.
Sirach 4:29 Do not become bold in your tongue, and sluggish and slack in your works.
Sirach 4:30 Do not be like a lion in your house, and creating terrors among your household servants.
Sirach 4:31 Let your hand not be stretched out for receiving, and drawn in when repaying.

## Chapter 5

Sirach 5:1 Do not rely upon your wealth, and do not say, It is sufficient for me.
Sirach 5:2 Do not follow your soul and your strength to walk in your heart's desires;
Sirach 5:3 and do not say, Who will rule me? For the Lord, avenging, will avenge.
Sirach 5:4 Do not say, I sinned, and what happened to me? For the Lord is long-suffering.
Sirach 5:5 Concerning atonement, do not become fearless to add sin upon sins;
Sirach 5:6 and do not say, His compassion is great; he will make atonement for the multitude of my sins; for mercy and anger are with him, and his wrath will rest upon sinners.
Sirach 5:7 Do not wait to turn to the Lord, and do not postpone from day to day; for suddenly the Lord's anger will come forth, and in a time of vengeance you will perish.
Sirach 5:8 Do not rely upon unjust wealth; for it will benefit you nothing in a day of affliction.
Sirach 5:9 Do not winnow in every wind, and do not walk in every path; thus is the double-tongued sinner.
Sirach 5:10 Be established in your understanding, and let your word be one.
Sirach 5:11 Become swift in your hearing, and utter an answer in long-suffering.
Sirach 5:12 If you have understanding, answer your neighbor; but if not, let your hand be upon your mouth.
Sirach 5:13 Glory and dishonor are in speech, and a human's tongue is a fall for him.
Sirach 5:14 Do not be called a whisperer, and do not lie in wait with your tongue; for shame is upon the thief, and evil condemnation upon the double-tongued.
Sirach 5:15 In great and in small do not be ignorant, and instead of a friend do not become an enemy; for an evil name will inherit shame and reproach; thus is the double-tongued sinner.

## Chapter 6

Sirach 6:1 And instead of a friend do not become an enemy; for an evil name will inherit shame and reproach; thus is the double-tongued sinner.
Sirach 6:2 Do not exalt yourself in your soul's counsel, so that your soul may not be torn apart like a bull;
Sirach 6:3 you will devour your leaves and destroy your fruits, and leave yourself like a dry tree.
Sirach 6:4 An evil soul will destroy the one acquiring it, and make him a delight of enemies.
Sirach 6:5 A sweet throat will multiply its friends, and a well-speaking tongue will multiply friendly greetings.
Sirach 6:6 Let those at peace with you be many, but your counselors one out of a thousand.
Sirach 6:7 If you acquire a friend, acquire him in testing, and do not trust him swiftly.
Sirach 6:8 For there is a friend in his own time, and he will certainly not remain in the day of your affliction.
Sirach 6:9 And there is a friend changing into enmity, and he will reveal a quarrel for your reproach.
Sirach 6:10 And there is a friend sharing tables, and he will certainly not remain in the day of your affliction;
Sirach 6:11 and in your good things he will be like you, and speak boldly to your household servants;
Sirach 6:12 if you are humbled, he will be against you, and hide from your face.
Sirach 6:13 Separate yourself from your enemies, and be attentive concerning your friends.
Sirach 6:14 A faithful friend is a strong shelter, and the one finding him found a treasure.
Sirach 6:15 There is no exchange for a faithful friend, and no weight of his beauty.
Sirach 6:16 A faithful friend is a medicine of life, and those fearing the Lord will find him.
Sirach 6:17 The one fearing the Lord will make his friendship straight, because according to himself, so also is his neighbor.
Sirach 6:18 Child, from your youth choose discipline, and until gray hairs you will find wisdom.
Sirach 6:19 Like the one plowing and the one sowing, approach her, and await her good fruits; for in her work you will labor a little, and swiftly eat of her produce.
Sirach 6:20 How exceedingly harsh she is to the undisciplined, and a fainthearted man will not remain in her;
Sirach 6:21 like a strong testing stone she will be upon him, and he will not delay to cast her away.
Sirach 6:22 For wisdom is according to her name, and is not manifest to many.
Sirach 6:23 Hear, child, and receive my judgment, and do not refuse my counsel;
Sirach 6:24 and bring your feet into her fetters, and your neck into her collar;
Sirach 6:25 put your shoulder beneath her and carry her, and do not be vexed with her bonds;
Sirach 6:26 with all your soul approach her, and with your whole power keep her ways;
Sirach 6:27 trace and seek, and she will be known to you, and having taken hold, do not let her go;
Sirach 6:28 for at the last you will find her rest, and she will turn into gladness for you;
Sirach 6:29 and the fetters will be for you a shelter of strength, and her collars a robe of glory.
Sirach 6:30 For a golden adornment is upon her, and her bonds are hyacinth-colored thread;
Sirach 6:31 you will put her on as a robe of glory, and place a crown of exultation upon yourself.
Sirach 6:32 If you will, child, you will be disciplined, and if you give your soul, you will be skillful;
Sirach 6:33 if you love hearing, you will receive, and if you incline your ear, you will be wise.
Sirach 6:34 Stand among a multitude of elders; and who is wise? Cling to him.
Sirach 6:35 Wish to hear every divine account, and let no proverbs of understanding escape you.
Sirach 6:36 If you see an understanding man, rise early to him, and let your foot wear away the steps of his doors.
Sirach 6:37 Consider the Lord's ordinances, and meditate in his commandments continually; he himself will establish your heart, and the desire of wisdom will be given you.

## Chapter 7

Sirach 7:1 Do not do evils, and evil will certainly not overtake you;
Sirach 7:2 depart from injustice, and it will turn away from you.
Sirach 7:3 Son, do not sow upon furrows of injustice, and you will certainly not reap them sevenfold.
Sirach 7:4 Do not seek leadership from the Lord, nor a seat of glory from a king.
Sirach 7:5 Do not justify yourself before the Lord, and do not display wisdom before a king.
Sirach 7:6 Do not seek to become a judge, lest you be unable to remove injustices, lest you become wary before a ruler's face, and place a stumbling block in your uprightness.
Sirach 7:7 Do not sin against a city's multitude, and do not cast yourself down in a crowd.
Sirach 7:8 Do not bind sin twice; for even in the one you will not be innocent.
Sirach 7:9 Do not say, He will look upon the multitude of my gifts, and when I offer to God Most High, he will accept.
Sirach 7:10 Do not lose heart in your prayer, and do not overlook doing almsgiving.
Sirach 7:11 Do not laugh at a human who is in bitterness of his soul; for there is one who humbles and raises.
Sirach 7:12 Do not plow a lie against your brother, nor do the like to a friend.
Sirach 7:13 Do not wish to lie any lie; for persistence in it is not for good.
Sirach 7:14 Do not chatter in a multitude of elders, and do not repeat a word in your prayer.
Sirach 7:15 Do not hate laborious work and farming, created by the Most High.
Sirach 7:16 Do not number yourself among a multitude of sinners; remember that anger will not delay.
Sirach 7:17 Humble your soul exceedingly, because vengeance upon an ungodly man is fire and a worm.
Sirach 7:18 Do not exchange a friend for gain, nor a true brother for gold of Souphir.
Sirach 7:19 Do not miss a wise and good wife; for her grace is above gold.
Sirach 7:20 Do not afflict a household servant working in truth, nor a hired man giving his soul;
Sirach 7:21 let your soul love an understanding household servant; do not deprive him of freedom.
Sirach 7:22 Do you have cattle? Inspect them; and if they are useful to you, let them remain with you.
Sirach 7:23 Do you have children? Discipline them, and bend their neck from youth.
Sirach 7:24 Do you have daughters? Attend to their body, and do not make your face cheerful toward them.
Sirach 7:25 Give a daughter in marriage, and you will have completed a great work, and give her to an understanding man.
Sirach 7:26 Do you have a wife according to your soul? Do not cast her out; and do not entrust yourself to one hated.
Sirach 7:27 With your whole heart glorify your father, and do not forget your mother's birth-pains;
Sirach 7:28 remember that through them you were born, and what will you repay them as they did for you?
Sirach 7:29 With your whole soul revere the Lord, and admire his priests.
Sirach 7:30 With your whole power love the one who made you, and do not abandon his ministers.
Sirach 7:31 Fear the Lord and glorify a priest, and give him the portion, as you have been commanded, firstfruit and that concerning transgression, and a gift of shoulders, and a sacrifice of sanctification, and firstfruit of holy things.
Sirach 7:32 And stretch out your hand to a poor man, so that your blessing may be perfected.
Sirach 7:33 Let the grace of a gift be before every living one, and do not withhold grace upon a dead one.
Sirach 7:34 Do not fail those weeping, and mourn with those mourning.
Sirach 7:35 Do not hesitate to inspect a sick human; for from such things you will be loved.
Sirach 7:36 In all your words remember your last things, and you will not sin for the age.

## Chapter 8

Sirach 8:1 Do not battle with a powerful human, lest you fall into his hands.
Sirach 8:2 Do not quarrel with a rich human, lest he oppose your weight; for gold destroyed many and turned aside kings' hearts.
Sirach 8:3 Do not battle with a talkative human, and do not heap wood upon his fire.
Sirach 8:4 Do not jest with an undisciplined man, so that your ancestors may not be dishonored.
Sirach 8:5 Do not reproach a human turning away from sin; remember that we all are under penalties.
Sirach 8:6 Do not dishonor a human in his old age; for some of us too grow old.
Sirach 8:7 Do not rejoice over a dead one; remember that we all die.
Sirach 8:8 Do not overlook an account of wise ones, and move among their proverbs; because from them you will learn discipline, and to minister to great men.
Sirach 8:9 Do not miss an account of elders, for they too learned from their fathers; because from them you will learn understanding, and to give an answer in a time of need.
Sirach 8:10 Do not kindle a sinner's coals, lest you be burned in the fire of his flame.
Sirach 8:11 Do not rise up before an insolent man's face, so that he may not sit as an ambush for your mouth.
Sirach 8:12 Do not lend to a human stronger than you; and if you lend, become as one who has lost it.
Sirach 8:13 Do not stand surety beyond your power; and if you stand surety, consider yourself as one who will repay.
Sirach 8:14 Do not litigate with a judge; for according to his opinion they will judge for him.
Sirach 8:15 Do not walk on a way with a reckless man, so that he may not become burdensome against you; for he himself will do according to his will, and you will perish together with his senselessness.
Sirach 8:16 Do not make a quarrel with a wrathful man, and do not traverse the wilderness with him; because blood is as nothing in his eyes, and where there is no help, he will cast you down.
Sirach 8:17 Do not take counsel with a fool; for he will not be able to keep a word.
Sirach 8:18 Do not do a hidden thing before a stranger; for you do not know what he will bring forth.
Sirach 8:19 Do not disclose your heart to every human, and let him not render you favor.

## Chapter 9

Sirach 9:1 Do not be jealous of the wife of your bosom, nor teach evil discipline against yourself.
Sirach 9:2 Do not give your soul to a woman for her to step upon your strength.
Sirach 9:3 Do not meet a woman prostituting herself, lest you fall into her snares.
Sirach 9:4 Do not linger with a woman playing music, lest you be caught in her attempts.
Sirach 9:5 Do not observe a virgin closely, lest you stumble in her penalties.
Sirach 9:6 Do not give your soul to prostitutes, so that you may not destroy your inheritance.
Sirach 9:7 Do not look around in streets of a city, and do not wander in its deserted places.
Sirach 9:8 Turn an eye away from a beautiful woman, and do not observe another's beauty closely; many were led astray by a woman's beauty, and from this affection is kindled like fire.
Sirach 9:9 Do not sit at all with a married woman, and do not feast together with her over wine, lest your soul incline toward her, and in your spirit you slip into destruction.
Sirach 9:10 Do not abandon an old friend, for a recent one is not equal to him; new wine is a new friend; if it grows old, you will drink it with gladness.
Sirach 9:11 Do not envy a sinner's glory; for you do not know what his downfall will be.
Sirach 9:12 Do not delight in the good fortune of the ungodly; remember that until Hades they will certainly not be justified.
Sirach 9:13 Keep far away from a human who has authority to murder, and you will certainly not suspect fear of death; and even if you approach, do not transgress, so that he may not take away your life; recognize that you cross amid snares, and walk upon a city's battlements.
Sirach 9:14 According to your strength, appraise those near you, and take counsel with wise ones.
Sirach 9:15 Let your reasoning be with understanding ones, and all your account in the Most High's law.
Sirach 9:16 Let righteous men be your fellow diners, and let your boasting be in fear of the Lord.
Sirach 9:17 A work will be praised in craftsmen's hands, and a people's leader is wise in his word.
Sirach 9:18 A talkative man is fearsome in his city, and the rash in his word will be hated.

## Chapter 10

Sirach 10:1 A wise judge will discipline his people, and an understanding man's leadership will be ordered.
Sirach 10:2 According to the people's judge, so also are his ministers, and according to the city's leader, all its inhabitants.
Sirach 10:3 An undisciplined king will destroy his people, and a city will be inhabited in rulers' understanding.
Sirach 10:4 The earth's authority is in the Lord's hand, and he will raise the useful one over it at a time.
Sirach 10:5 A man's prosperity is in the Lord's hand, and upon a scribe's face he will place his glory.
Sirach 10:6 Do not be wrathful with your neighbor for every wrong, and do nothing in works of insolence.
Sirach 10:7 Arrogance is hateful before the Lord and humans, and injustice is offensive to both.
Sirach 10:8 A kingdom is transferred from nation to nation through injustices and insults and wealth.
Sirach 10:9 Why are earth and ashes arrogant? Because in life I cast out his inward parts.
Sirach 10:10 A long sickness, a physician mocks; and a king today, and tomorrow he will die.
Sirach 10:11 For when a human dies, he will inherit creeping things and beasts and worms.
Sirach 10:12 A beginning of human arrogance is departing from the Lord, and his heart departed from the one making him.
Sirach 10:13 Because a beginning of arrogance is sin, and the one holding it will shower an abomination; therefore the Lord made the afflictions extraordinary, and overturned them to the end.
Sirach 10:14 The Lord took down rulers' thrones, and seated meek ones in their place;
Sirach 10:15 the Lord plucked out nations' roots, and planted humble ones in their place;
Sirach 10:16 the Lord overturned nations' lands, and destroyed them to earth's foundations;
Sirach 10:17 he removed from them and destroyed them, and caused their memorial to cease from earth.
Sirach 10:18 Arrogance has not been created for humans, nor anger of wrath for women's offspring.
Sirach 10:19 What seed is honored? A human's seed. What seed is honored? Those fearing the Lord. What seed is dishonored? A human's seed. What seed is dishonored? Those transgressing commandments.
Sirach 10:20 Among brothers their leader is honored, and those fearing the Lord in his eyes.
Sirach 10:22 Rich and glorious and poor—their boasting is fear of the Lord.
Sirach 10:23 It is not righteous to dishonor an understanding poor man, and it is not fitting to glorify a sinful man.
Sirach 10:24 A great man and judge and ruler will be glorified, and none of them is greater than the one fearing the Lord.
Sirach 10:25 Free men will minister to a wise household servant, and a knowledgeable man will not grumble.
Sirach 10:26 Do not display wisdom in doing your work, and do not be glorified in a time of your distress.
Sirach 10:27 Better is one working and abounding in all things than one walking about glorified and lacking bread.
Sirach 10:28 Child, in meekness glorify your soul, and give it honor according to its worth.
Sirach 10:29 Who will justify the one sinning against his soul? And who will glorify the one dishonoring his life?
Sirach 10:30 A poor man is glorified through his knowledge, and a rich man is glorified through his wealth.
Sirach 10:31 The one glorified in poverty, how much more in wealth? And the one without glory in wealth, how much more in poverty?

## Chapter 11

Sirach 11:1 A humble man's wisdom will raise his head, and seat him among great men.
Sirach 11:2 Do not praise a man in his beauty, and do not abhor a human in his appearance.
Sirach 11:3 A bee is small among flying things, and its fruit is first among sweet things.
Sirach 11:4 Do not boast in clothing of garments, and do not exalt yourself in a day of glory; because the Lord's works are wondrous, and his works hidden from humans.
Sirach 11:5 Many tyrants sat upon ground, but the unsuspected one wore a diadem.
Sirach 11:6 Many rulers were exceedingly dishonored, and glorious ones were delivered into others' hands.
Sirach 11:7 Before you examine, do not blame; understand first, and then rebuke.
Sirach 11:8 Before hearing, do not answer, and do not interrupt amid words.
Sirach 11:9 Do not quarrel concerning a matter of which you have no need, and do not sit together in sinners' judgment.
Sirach 11:10 Child, let your actions not be concerning many things; if you multiply them, you will not be acquitted; and if you pursue, you will certainly not overtake; and you will certainly not escape by running away.
Sirach 11:11 There is one laboring and toiling and hastening, and so much more he is lacking.
Sirach 11:12 There is a sluggish man needing help, lacking strength and abounding in poverty; and the Lord's eyes looked upon him for good things, and he raised him from his humiliation,
Sirach 11:13 and raised his head, and many marveled at him.
Sirach 11:14 Good things and evils, life and death, poverty and wealth are from the Lord.
Sirach 11:17 The Lord's gift remains with the pious, and his good pleasure will prosper for the age.
Sirach 11:18 There is one becoming rich from his attention and tightness, and this is the portion of his wage;
Sirach 11:19 when he says, I found rest, and now I will eat of my good things, and he does not know what time will pass, and he will leave them to others and die.
Sirach 11:20 Stand in your covenant and occupy yourself with it, and grow old in your work.
Sirach 11:21 Do not marvel at a sinner's works, but believe the Lord and remain in your toil; because it is easy in the Lord's eyes to make a needy man rich swiftly, suddenly.
Sirach 11:22 The Lord's blessing is in a pious man's wage, and in a swift hour he makes his blessing flourish.
Sirach 11:23 Do not say, What is my need, and what will my good things be from now?
Sirach 11:24 Do not say, I have sufficient things, and what harm will I suffer from now?
Sirach 11:25 In a day of good things there is forgetfulness of evils, and in a day of evils he will not remember good things;
Sirach 11:26 because it is easy before the Lord on a day of an end to repay a human according to his ways.
Sirach 11:27 Affliction of an hour makes forgetfulness of luxury, and at a human's completion is a revelation of his works.
Sirach 11:28 Before an end pronounce no one blessed, and a man will be known in his children.
Sirach 11:29 Do not bring every human into your house; for the deceitful man's ambushes are many.
Sirach 11:30 A hunting partridge in a basket—thus is an arrogant man's heart, and like the spy he watches a fall;
Sirach 11:31 for turning good things into evils, he lies in wait, and upon choice things will place blame.
Sirach 11:32 From a spark of fire a bed of coals multiplies, and a sinful human lies in wait for blood.
Sirach 11:33 Be attentive concerning an evildoer, for he devises wicked things, lest he give you blame for the age.
Sirach 11:34 House a stranger, and he will twist you in disturbances, and estrange you from your own things.

## Chapter 12

Sirach 12:1 If you do good, know to whom you do it, and there will be gratitude for your good things.
Sirach 12:2 Do good to a pious man, and you will find repayment, and if not from him, then from the Most High.
Sirach 12:3 There will be no good things for the one persisting in evils, and for the one not granting almsgiving.
Sirach 12:4 Give to the pious man, and do not help the sinner.
Sirach 12:5 Do good to a humble man, and do not give to an ungodly man; hinder his bread, and do not give him, so that by it he may not rule you; for you will find double evils in all good things which you may do for him.
Sirach 12:6 Because the Most High also hated sinners, and will repay vengeance to the ungodly.
Sirach 12:7 Give to the good man, and do not help the sinner.
Sirach 12:8 A friend will not be avenged in good things, and an enemy will not be hidden in evils.
Sirach 12:9 In a man's good things his enemies are in sorrow, and in his evils even the friend will separate himself.
Sirach 12:10 Do not trust your enemy for the age; for as bronze rusts, so is his wickedness;
Sirach 12:11 and if he is humbled and walks bent down, set your soul on guard, and guard yourself from him, and you will be to him like one polishing a mirror, and know that he has not rusted away to the end.
Sirach 12:12 Do not stand him beside yourself, lest, overturning you, he stand in your place; do not seat him at your right, lest he seek your seat, and at the last you recognize my words, and be pierced at my utterances.
Sirach 12:13 Who will have mercy on an enchanter bitten by a serpent, and all those approaching beasts?
Sirach 12:14 Thus also on the one approaching a sinful man, and mingling in his sins.
Sirach 12:15 For an hour he will remain with you, and if you turn aside, he will certainly not endure.
Sirach 12:16 And with his lips the enemy will sweeten, and in his heart plan to overturn you into a pit; with his eyes the enemy will weep, and if he finds a time, he will not be filled with blood.
Sirach 12:17 If evils meet you, you will find him there before you, and as though helping, he will trip your heel;
Sirach 12:18 he will shake his head and clap his hands, and whisper many things, and alter his face.

## Chapter 13

Sirach 13:1 The one touching pitch will be defiled, and the one sharing with an arrogant man will be made like him.
Sirach 13:2 Do not lift a weight beyond you, and do not share with one stronger and richer than you. What will an earthen pot share with a cauldron? This will strike against it, and this will be crushed.
Sirach 13:3 A rich man did wrong, and he himself further threatened; a poor man has been wronged, and he himself will further entreat.
Sirach 13:4 If you are useful, he works with you; and if you lack, he will leave you.
Sirach 13:5 If you have, he will live with you and empty you, and he himself will not toil.
Sirach 13:6 He has had need of you, and will lead you astray and smile upon you and give you hope; he will speak good things to you, and say, What is your need?
Sirach 13:7 And he will shame you with his foods, until he empties you twice or thrice, and at the last mock you; after these things he will see you and leave you, and shake his head at you.
Sirach 13:8 Be attentive lest you be led astray, and do not be humbled in your senselessness.
Sirach 13:9 When a ruler calls you, become one withdrawing, and so much more he will call you;
Sirach 13:10 do not thrust yourself in, lest you be rejected, and do not stand far away, so that you may not be forgotten.
Sirach 13:11 Do not insist on speaking with him as an equal, and do not trust his many words; for from much speech he will test you, and as though smiling he will examine you.
Sirach 13:12 Merciless is the one not keeping words, and he will certainly not spare concerning affliction and bonds.
Sirach 13:13 Keep watch and attend exceedingly, because you walk with your fall.
Sirach 13:15 Every living being loves what is like it, and every human his neighbor;
Sirach 13:16 all flesh gathers according to kind, and a man will cling to his like.
Sirach 13:17 What will a wolf share with a lamb? Thus is a sinner toward a pious man.
Sirach 13:18 What peace has a hyena with a dog? And what peace has a rich man with a needy man?
Sirach 13:19 Wild asses in a wilderness are lions' prey; thus poor men are rich men's pastures.
Sirach 13:20 Humility is an abomination to an arrogant man; thus a poor man is an abomination to a rich man.
Sirach 13:21 A rich man shaken is supported by friends, but a humble man fallen is further rejected by friends.
Sirach 13:22 When a rich man stumbled, many were helpers; he spoke forbidden things, and they justified him. A humble man stumbled, and they further rebuked him; he uttered understanding, and no place was given him.
Sirach 13:23 A rich man spoke, and all were silent, and raised his word to the clouds. A poor man spoke, and they said, Who is this? And if he stumbles, they will further overturn him.
Sirach 13:24 Wealth is good in which there is no sin, and poverty is evil in an ungodly man's mouth.
Sirach 13:25 A human's heart alters his face, whether for good things or for evils.
Sirach 13:26 A trace of a heart in good things is a cheerful face, and finding parables is reasonings with toils.

## Chapter 14

Sirach 14:1 Blessed is a man who did not slip with his mouth, and was not pierced by sorrow of sins;
Sirach 14:2 blessed is he whom his soul did not condemn, and who did not fall from his hope.
Sirach 14:3 Wealth is not good for a petty man, and for an envious human, why wealth?
Sirach 14:4 The one gathering at his soul's expense gathers for others, and others will live luxuriously in his good things.
Sirach 14:5 The one evil to himself, to whom will he be good? And he will certainly not rejoice in his wealth.
Sirach 14:6 There is none more evil than the one begrudging himself, and this is repayment of his wickedness;
Sirach 14:7 and even if he does good, he does it in forgetfulness, and at the last discloses his wickedness.
Sirach 14:8 Evil is the one begrudging with an eye, turning a face away and overlooking souls.
Sirach 14:9 A greedy man's eye is not filled with a portion, and evil injustice dries up a soul.
Sirach 14:10 An evil eye is envious over bread, and deficient at its table.
Sirach 14:11 Child, according as you have, do good to yourself, and bring offerings to the Lord worthily;
Sirach 14:12 remember that death will not delay, and a covenant of Hades was not shown you;
Sirach 14:13 before you die, do good to a friend, and according to your strength stretch out and give him.
Sirach 14:14 Do not deprive yourself of a good day, and let no portion of good desire pass you by.
Sirach 14:15 Will you not leave your toils to another, and your labors for division of a lot?
Sirach 14:16 Give and take and deceive your soul, because in Hades it is not possible to seek luxury.
Sirach 14:17 All flesh grows old like a garment; for the covenant from an age is, By death you will die.
Sirach 14:18 Like a leaf flourishing upon a leafy tree, some it casts down, but others it grows, so is a generation of flesh and blood, one dies, but another is born.
Sirach 14:19 Every work rotting ceases, and the one working it will depart with it.
Sirach 14:20 Blessed is a man who will meditate in wisdom, and who will converse in his understanding,
Sirach 14:21 the one considering her ways in his heart, and he will ponder in her hidden things.
Sirach 14:22 Go out after her like a tracker, and lie in wait in her ways.
Sirach 14:23 The one peering through her windows, and he will listen at her doorways,
Sirach 14:24 the one lodging near her house, and he will fix a peg in her walls,
Sirach 14:25 will stand his tent beside her hands, and lodge in a lodging of good things,
Sirach 14:26 will place his children in her shelter, and lodge beneath her branches,
Sirach 14:27 will be sheltered by her from burning heat, and lodge in her glory.

## Chapter 15

Sirach 15:1 The one fearing the Lord will do it, and the one holding the law will take hold of her;
Sirach 15:2 and she will meet him like a mother, and like a wife of virginity receive him;
Sirach 15:3 she will feed him bread of understanding, and give him water of wisdom to drink;
Sirach 15:4 he will be supported upon her and certainly not incline, and will rely upon her and certainly not be put to shame;
Sirach 15:5 and she will exalt him above his neighbors, and open his mouth in the midst of an assembly;
Sirach 15:6 he will find gladness and a crown of exultation, and inherit an everlasting name.
Sirach 15:7 Humans without understanding will certainly not take hold of her, and sinful men will certainly not see her;
Sirach 15:8 she is far from arrogance, and lying men will certainly not remember her.
Sirach 15:9 Praise is not beautiful in a sinner's mouth, because it was not sent from the Lord;
Sirach 15:10 for praise will be said in wisdom, and the Lord will prosper it.
Sirach 15:11 Do not say that, Because of the Lord I departed; for what he hated he will not do.
Sirach 15:12 Do not say that, He himself led me astray; for he has no need of a sinful man.
Sirach 15:13 The Lord hated every abomination, and it is not beloved by those fearing him.
Sirach 15:14 He himself made a human from the beginning, and left him in the hand of his counsel.
Sirach 15:15 If you will, you will keep commandments, and to do faithfulness is of good pleasure.
Sirach 15:16 He placed fire and water beside you; to whichever you will, you will stretch out your hand.
Sirach 15:17 Before humans are life and death, and whatever he may delight in will be given him.
Sirach 15:18 Because the Lord's wisdom is great; strong in dominion and seeing all things,
Sirach 15:19 and his eyes are upon those fearing him, and he himself will recognize every human's work.
Sirach 15:20 He commanded no one to act ungodly, and gave no one license to sin.

## Chapter 16

Sirach 16:1 Do not desire a multitude of useless children, nor rejoice over ungodly sons;
Sirach 16:2 if they multiply, do not rejoice over them, unless fear of the Lord is with them.
Sirach 16:3 Do not trust their life, and do not rely upon their multitude; for one is better than a thousand, and to die childless than to have ungodly children.
Sirach 16:4 For from one understanding man a city will be populated, but a tribe of lawless men will be laid waste.
Sirach 16:5 My eye has seen many such things, and my ear has heard stronger things than these.
Sirach 16:6 In an assembly of sinners fire will be kindled, and in a disobedient nation anger was kindled.
Sirach 16:7 He did not make atonement concerning the ancient giants, who departed in their strength;
Sirach 16:8 he did not spare concerning Lot's sojourn, whom he abhorred through their arrogance;
Sirach 16:9 he did not have mercy on a nation of destruction, those lifted up in their sins,
Sirach 16:10 and thus six hundred thousand footmen, those gathered together in their hardness of heart.
Sirach 16:11 And even if there is one stiff-necked man, it is wondrous if he will be acquitted; for mercy and anger are with him, a ruler of atonements and one pouring out anger.
Sirach 16:12 According to his great mercy, so also is his reproof great; he will judge a man according to his works.
Sirach 16:13 A sinner will not escape with plunder, and a pious man's endurance will certainly not fall behind.
Sirach 16:14 He will make a place for every act of almsgiving; each will find according to his works.
Sirach 16:17 Do not say that, I will be hidden from the Lord, and who will remember me from on high? Among a greater people I will certainly not be known, for what is my soul in immeasurable creation?
Sirach 16:18 Behold, heaven and the heaven of heaven, abyss and earth will be shaken at his inspection;
Sirach 16:19 together the mountains and earth's foundations, when he looks upon them, are shaken together with trembling.
Sirach 16:20 And a heart will not consider these things, and who will ponder his ways?
Sirach 16:21 And a tempest which a human will not see, and most of his works are in hidden places.
Sirach 16:22 Who will announce works of righteousness? Or who will endure? For the covenant is far away.
Sirach 16:23 One deficient in heart considers these things, and a senseless and wandering man considers foolish things.
Sirach 16:24 Hear me, child, and learn knowledge, and with your heart attend to my words;
Sirach 16:25 I will disclose discipline by weight, and announce knowledge with exactness.
Sirach 16:26 In the Lord's judgment are his works from the beginning, and from their making he distinguished their portions.
Sirach 16:27 He ordered his works for an age, and their beginnings for their generations; neither did they hunger nor labor, and they did not cease from their works;
Sirach 16:28 each did not oppress his neighbor, and for an age they will not disobey his word.
Sirach 16:29 And after these things the Lord looked upon the earth, and filled it with his good things;
Sirach 16:30 with the soul of every living being he covered its face, and into it is their return.

## Chapter 17

Sirach 17:1 The Lord created a human from earth, and again returned him into it.
Sirach 17:2 He gave them numbered days and a time, and gave them authority over the things upon it.
Sirach 17:3 According to himself he clothed them with strength, and according to his image made them.
Sirach 17:4 He placed his fear upon all flesh, and to master beasts and birds.
Sirach 17:6 Counsel and tongue and eyes, ears and heart he gave them to consider.
Sirach 17:7 He filled them with knowledge of understanding, and showed them good things and evils.
Sirach 17:8 He placed his eye upon their hearts, to show them the greatness of his works,
Sirach 17:10 and they will praise a name of sanctification, so that they may recount the great things of his works.
Sirach 17:11 He added knowledge to them, and gave them a law of life as inheritance.
Sirach 17:12 He established an everlasting covenant with them, and showed them his judgments.
Sirach 17:13 Their eyes saw a greatness of glory, and their ear heard glory of his voice.
Sirach 17:14 And he said to them, Be attentive against every injustice; and he commanded each of them concerning his neighbor.
Sirach 17:15 Their ways are before him continually; they will not be hidden from his eyes.
Sirach 17:17 For each nation he appointed a leader, and Israel is the Lord's portion.
Sirach 17:19 All their works are like the sun before him, and his eyes continually upon their ways.
Sirach 17:20 Their injustices were not hidden from him, and all their sins are before the Lord.
Sirach 17:22 A man's almsgiving is like a seal with him, and he will keep a human's kindness like a pupil.
Sirach 17:23 After these things he will rise up and repay them, and render their repayment upon their head;
Sirach 17:24 yet to those repenting he gave a return, and encouraged those failing in endurance.
Sirach 17:25 Turn to the Lord and leave sins, entreat before his face and lessen stumbling;
Sirach 17:26 return to the Most High and turn from injustice, and exceedingly hate an abomination.
Sirach 17:27 Who will praise the Most High in Hades instead of those living and giving thanksgiving?
Sirach 17:28 From a dead one, as from one not even existing, confession perishes; one living and healthy will praise the Lord.
Sirach 17:29 How great is the Lord's mercy, and atonement for those turning to him.
Sirach 17:30 For not all things can be in humans, because a son of man is not immortal.
Sirach 17:31 What is brighter than the sun? And even this fails; and flesh and blood will think evil.
Sirach 17:32 He himself inspects the power of heaven's height, and all humans are earth and ashes.

## Chapter 18

Sirach 18:1 The one living for the age created all things together;
Sirach 18:2 the Lord alone will be justified.
Sirach 18:4 To no one did he give the ability to declare his works; and who will trace his great things?
Sirach 18:5 Who will count the might of his majesty? And who will add to recounting his mercies?
Sirach 18:6 It is not possible to lessen or add, and it is not possible to trace the Lord's wondrous things;
Sirach 18:7 when a human finishes, then he begins; and when he ceases, then he will be at a loss.
Sirach 18:8 What is a human, and what is his use? What is his good, and what his evil?
Sirach 18:9 The number of a human's days, many years, is a hundred;
Sirach 18:10 like a drop of water from sea and a pebble of sand, so are few years in a day of an age.
Sirach 18:11 Therefore the Lord was long-suffering toward them, and poured his mercy upon them.
Sirach 18:12 He saw and recognized their downfall, that it is evil; therefore he multiplied his atonement.
Sirach 18:13 A human's mercy is upon his neighbor, but the Lord's mercy upon all flesh; reproving and disciplining and teaching and turning back, like a shepherd his flock.
Sirach 18:14 He has mercy on those receiving discipline, and those hastening to his judgments.
Sirach 18:15 Child, in good things do not give blame, and in every gift sorrow of words.
Sirach 18:16 Will dew not give rest from burning heat? Thus a word is better than a gift.
Sirach 18:17 Behold, is not a word above a good gift? And both are with a gracious man.
Sirach 18:18 A fool will reproach ungraciously, and an envious man's gift wastes away eyes.
Sirach 18:19 Before speaking, learn, and before sickness, be treated.
Sirach 18:20 Before judgment examine yourself, and in an hour of inspection you will find atonement.
Sirach 18:21 Before you become sick, be humbled, and in a time of sins show a turning back.
Sirach 18:22 Do not be hindered from repaying a vow at a fitting time, and do not wait until death to be justified.
Sirach 18:23 Before praying prepare yourself, and do not become like a human testing the Lord.
Sirach 18:24 Remember wrath in days of an end, and a time of vengeance in a turning away of a face.
Sirach 18:25 Remember a time of famine in a time of fullness, poverty and want in days of wealth.
Sirach 18:26 From morning until evening a time changes, and all things are swift before the Lord.
Sirach 18:27 A wise human will be wary in everything, and in days of sins will be attentive against transgression.
Sirach 18:28 Every understanding man knew wisdom, and will give praise to the one finding her.
Sirach 18:29 Understanding ones in words themselves also became wise, and showered exact proverbs.
Sirach 18:30 Do not walk after your desires, and restrain yourself from your appetites;
Sirach 18:31 if you supply your soul with the pleasure of desire, it will make you a delight of your enemies.
Sirach 18:32 Do not rejoice over much luxury, lest you be bound to its expense.
Sirach 18:33 Do not become poor feasting on borrowed money, and you have nothing in a purse.

## Chapter 19

Sirach 19:1 A drunken worker will not be made rich; the one despising small things will fall little by little.
Sirach 19:2 Wine and women will make understanding ones depart, and the one clinging to prostitutes will be more reckless;
Sirach 19:3 rot and worms will inherit him, and a reckless soul will be removed.
Sirach 19:4 The one trusting swiftly is light in heart, and the one sinning will transgress against his soul.
Sirach 19:5 The one rejoicing in heart will be condemned,
Sirach 19:6 and the one hating speech is lessened in wickedness.
Sirach 19:7 Never repeat a word, and nothing will certainly be diminished for you.
Sirach 19:8 With friend and enemy do not recount, and unless it is sin for you, do not disclose;
Sirach 19:9 for he has heard you and guarded himself against you, and in a time will hate you.
Sirach 19:10 Have you heard a word? Let it die with you; be confident, it will certainly not burst you.
Sirach 19:11 Before a word a fool will suffer birth-pains, like a woman giving birth before an infant.
Sirach 19:12 An arrow fixed in a thigh of flesh—thus is a word in a fool's belly.
Sirach 19:13 Reprove a friend, perhaps he did not do it, and if he did something, lest he add to it.
Sirach 19:14 Reprove your neighbor, perhaps he did not say it, and if he has said it, so that he may not repeat it.
Sirach 19:15 Reprove a friend, for often slander occurs, and do not believe every word.
Sirach 19:16 There is one slipping and not from the soul, and who did not sin with his tongue?
Sirach 19:17 Reprove your neighbor before threatening, and give place to the Most High's law.
Sirach 19:20 All wisdom is fear of the Lord, and in all wisdom is doing law;
Sirach 19:22 and knowledge of wickedness is not wisdom, and there is no prudence where sinners' counsel is.
Sirach 19:23 There is cunning, and this is an abomination, and there is a senseless man deficient in wisdom;
Sirach 19:24 better is one inferior in understanding, fearful, than one abounding in prudence and transgressing law.
Sirach 19:25 There is exact cunning, and this is unjust, and there is one twisting a favor to disclose a judgment.
Sirach 19:26 There is one acting wickedly, bent down in gloom, and his inward things full of deceit;
Sirach 19:27 hiding a face and choosing to be deaf, where he was not recognized he will forestall you;
Sirach 19:28 and if through a deficiency of strength he is hindered from sinning, if he finds a time, he will do evil.
Sirach 19:29 A man will be recognized from appearance, and a thoughtful man recognized from the meeting of a face;
Sirach 19:30 a man's attire and laughter of teeth and a human's steps will announce the things concerning him.

## Chapter 20

Sirach 20:1 There is a reproof which is not beautiful, and there is one silent who is himself prudent.
Sirach 20:2 How good it is to reprove rather than be wrathful,
Sirach 20:3 and the one confessing will be hindered from loss.
Sirach 20:4 A eunuch's desire to deprive a young woman of virginity—thus is the one making judgments with force.
Sirach 20:5 There is one silent found wise, and there is one hateful from much speech.
Sirach 20:6 There is one silent, for he has no answer, and there is one silent knowing a time.
Sirach 20:7 A wise human will be silent until a time, but the babbler and senseless man will pass beyond a time.
Sirach 20:8 The one abounding in word will be abhorred, and the one exercising authority will be hated.
Sirach 20:9 There is prosperity for a man in evils, and there is a finding for loss.
Sirach 20:10 There is a gift which will not profit you, and there is a gift whose repayment is double.
Sirach 20:11 There is a loss for glory's sake, and there is one who raised a head from humiliation.
Sirach 20:12 There is one buying many things for little, and repaying them sevenfold.
Sirach 20:13 The wise man in words will make himself beloved, but fools' favors will be poured away.
Sirach 20:14 A senseless man's gift will not profit you, for his eyes are many instead of one;
Sirach 20:15 he will give little and reproach much, and open his mouth like a herald; today he will lend and tomorrow demand back; such a human is hateful.
Sirach 20:16 A fool will say, I have no friend, and there is no gratitude for my good things;
Sirach 20:17 those eating his bread are base in tongue; how often and how many will laugh at him?
Sirach 20:18 A slip from ground rather than from a tongue; thus a fall of evil ones will come swiftly.
Sirach 20:19 An ungracious human, an untimely tale; in mouths of undisciplined ones it will persist.
Sirach 20:20 A parable from a fool's mouth will be rejected; for he will certainly not say it in its time.
Sirach 20:21 There is one hindered from sinning through want, and in his rest he will not be pierced.
Sirach 20:22 There is one destroying his soul through shame, and through a senseless face he will destroy it.
Sirach 20:23 There is one promising a friend for shame's sake, and he acquired him as an enemy for nothing.
Sirach 20:24 A lie is an evil blemish in a human; in mouths of undisciplined ones it will persist.
Sirach 20:25 A thief is preferable to the one persisting in a lie, but both will inherit destruction.
Sirach 20:26 A lying human's character is dishonor, and his shame is with him continually.
Sirach 20:27 The wise man in words will advance himself, and a prudent human will please great men.
Sirach 20:28 The one working earth will raise his heap, and the one pleasing great men will make atonement for injustice.
Sirach 20:29 Guest-gifts and gifts blind wise ones' eyes, and like a muzzle in a mouth turn away reproofs.
Sirach 20:30 Hidden wisdom and an unseen treasure—what benefit is in both?
Sirach 20:31 Better is a human hiding his foolishness than a human hiding his wisdom.

## Chapter 21

Sirach 21:1 Child, did you sin? Add no longer, and entreat concerning your former things.
Sirach 21:2 Flee from sin as from a serpent's face; for if you approach, it will bite you; her teeth are a lion's teeth, destroying humans' souls.
Sirach 21:3 All lawlessness is like a two-edged sword; for its wound there is no healing.
Sirach 21:4 Terror and insolence will lay wealth waste; thus an arrogant man's house will be laid waste.
Sirach 21:5 A poor man's entreaty is from mouth to his ears, and his judgment comes swiftly.
Sirach 21:6 The one hating reproof is in a sinner's track, and the one fearing the Lord will turn in heart.
Sirach 21:7 The mighty in tongue is known from afar, but the thoughtful man knows when he slips.
Sirach 21:8 The one building his house with others' wealth is like one gathering his stones for winter.
Sirach 21:9 An assembly of lawless men is gathered tow, and their completion a flame of fire.
Sirach 21:10 Sinners' way is smoothed with stones, and at its last is a pit of Hades.
Sirach 21:11 The one guarding law masters his thought, and wisdom is completion of fear of the Lord.
Sirach 21:12 The one who is not skillful will not be disciplined, but there is cunning multiplying bitterness.
Sirach 21:13 A wise man's knowledge will multiply like a flood, and his counsel is like a spring of life.
Sirach 21:14 A fool's inward parts are like a broken vessel, and he will not retain any knowledge.
Sirach 21:15 If a knowledgeable man hears a wise word, he will praise it and add to it; the prodigal heard, and it displeased him, and he turned it behind his back.
Sirach 21:16 A fool's explanation is like a burden on a way, but grace will be found upon an understanding man's lip.
Sirach 21:17 A prudent man's mouth will be sought in an assembly, and they will consider his words in heart.
Sirach 21:18 As a destroyed house, so is wisdom to a fool, and an uncomprehending man's knowledge is unexamined words.
Sirach 21:19 Discipline is fetters upon an unthinking man's feet, and like handcuffs upon a right hand.
Sirach 21:20 A fool raises his voice in laughter, but a skillful man will scarcely smile quietly.
Sirach 21:21 Discipline is like a golden adornment to a prudent man, and like a bracelet upon a right arm.
Sirach 21:22 A fool's foot is swift into a house, but an experienced human will be ashamed before a face.
Sirach 21:23 A senseless man peers from a door into a house, but a disciplined man will stand outside.
Sirach 21:24 It is a human's lack of discipline to listen beside a door, but the prudent man will be burdened with dishonor.
Sirach 21:25 Strangers' lips will recount these things, but prudent men's words will be weighed in a balance.
Sirach 21:26 Their heart is in fools' mouth, but wise ones' heart is their mouth.
Sirach 21:27 When an ungodly man curses Satan, he himself curses his own soul.
Sirach 21:28 The whisperer defiles his own soul, and will be hated in a sojourn.

## Chapter 22

Sirach 22:1 A lazy man was compared to a soiled stone, and everyone will hiss at his dishonor.
Sirach 22:2 A lazy man was compared to a lump of dung; everyone taking him up will shake a hand.
Sirach 22:3 A father's shame is in begetting an undisciplined child, and a daughter comes for loss.
Sirach 22:4 A prudent daughter will inherit her husband, and the one causing shame is for sorrow of the one begetting her;
Sirach 22:5 the bold woman shames father and husband, and will be dishonored by both.
Sirach 22:6 An untimely account is music in mourning, but scourges and discipline are of wisdom at every time.
Sirach 22:9 The one teaching a fool is gluing a potsherd, awakening a sleeper from deep sleep.
Sirach 22:10 The one recounting to a fool is recounting to one slumbering, and at completion he will say, What is it?
Sirach 22:11 Weep over a dead one, for he lost light, and weep over a fool, for he lost understanding; weep more gladly over a dead one, because he rested, but the fool's life is worse than death.
Sirach 22:12 Mourning for a dead one is seven days, but for a fool and ungodly man all the days of his life.
Sirach 22:13 Do not multiply word with a senseless man, and do not go to one without understanding; guard yourself from him, so that you may not have labor, and you will certainly not be defiled in his shaking; turn away from him and you will find rest, and certainly not become weary in his folly.
Sirach 22:14 What will be heavier than lead? And what is its name except Fool?
Sirach 22:15 Sand and salt and a lump of iron are easier to bear than a human without understanding.
Sirach 22:16 Wooden bracing bound into a building will not be loosened in a shaking; thus a heart established upon a thought of counsel will not become timid in a time.
Sirach 22:17 A heart founded upon thought of understanding is like a sandy adornment of a polished wall.
Sirach 22:18 Stakes lying on a high place will certainly not endure before wind; thus a timid heart upon a fool's thought will certainly not endure before every fear.
Sirach 22:19 The one pricking an eye will bring down tears, and one pricking a heart discloses perception.
Sirach 22:20 One throwing a stone at birds scares them away, and the one reproaching a friend will dissolve friendship.
Sirach 22:21 If you draw a sword against a friend, do not despair, for there is a return;
Sirach 22:22 if you open a mouth against a friend, do not be wary, for there is reconciliation; except reproach and arrogance and disclosure of a secret and a deceitful blow, in these every friend will flee.
Sirach 22:23 Acquire faithfulness with your neighbor in poverty, so that you may be filled together in his good things; in a time of affliction remain with him, so that you may inherit together in his inheritance.
Sirach 22:24 Before fire are vapor of a furnace and smoke; thus before bloodshed are revilings.
Sirach 22:25 I will not be ashamed to shelter a friend, and will certainly not hide from his face,
Sirach 22:26 and if evils happen to me through him, everyone hearing will guard himself from him.
Sirach 22:27 Who will give a guard upon my mouth, and a skillful seal upon my lips, so that I may not fall through it, and my tongue destroy me?

## Chapter 23

Sirach 23:1 Lord, Father and Master of my life, do not abandon me to their counsel, do not let me fall in them.
Sirach 23:2 Who will set scourges over my thought, and discipline of wisdom over my heart, so that they may not spare my acts of ignorance, and he will certainly not overlook their sins,
Sirach 23:3 so that my ignorances may not multiply, and my sins abound, and I will fall before the adversaries, and my enemy rejoice over me?
Sirach 23:4 Lord, Father and God of my life, do not give me loftiness of eyes,
Sirach 23:5 and turn desire away from me;
Sirach 23:6 let appetite of belly and intercourse not overtake me, and do not deliver me to a shameless soul.
Sirach 23:7 Hear discipline of mouth, children, and the one guarding it will certainly not be caught.
Sirach 23:8 A sinner will be caught in his lips, and a reviler and arrogant man will stumble in them.
Sirach 23:9 Do not accustom your mouth to an oath, and do not become accustomed to naming the Holy One;
Sirach 23:10 for just as a household servant continually examined will not be free of a bruise, so also the one swearing and naming continually will certainly not be cleansed from sin.
Sirach 23:11 A man of many oaths will be filled with lawlessness, and a scourge will not depart from his house; if he transgresses, his sin is upon him, and if he overlooks, he sinned doubly; and if he swore vainly, he will not be justified, for his house will be filled with afflictions.
Sirach 23:12 There is an expression comparable to death; let it not be found in Iakob's inheritance; for all these things will depart from the pious, and they will not wallow in sins.
Sirach 23:13 Do not accustom your mouth to coarse lack of discipline; for in it is a word of sin.
Sirach 23:14 Remember your father and mother, for you sit among great men, lest you forget before them, and become foolish through your habit, and wish that you had not been born, and curse the day of your birth.
Sirach 23:15 A human accustomed to words of reproach will certainly not be disciplined in all his days.
Sirach 23:16 Two kinds multiply sins, and the third will bring anger;
Sirach 23:17 a hot soul is like burning fire, it will certainly not be extinguished until it is swallowed; a fornicating human in the body of his flesh will certainly not cease until he kindles fire; to a fornicating human every bread is sweet, he will certainly not cease until he dies.
Sirach 23:18 A human transgressing from his bed, saying in his soul, Who sees me? Darkness is around me, and walls cover me, and no one sees me; why am I wary? The Most High will certainly not remember my sins.
Sirach 23:19 And humans' eyes are his fear, and he did not know that the Lord's eyes are ten-thousandfold brighter than the sun, looking upon all humans' ways and observing into hidden places.
Sirach 23:20 Before all things were created they have been known to him, so also after they were completed.
Sirach 23:21 This man will be punished in a city's squares, and where he did not suspect, he will be seized.
Sirach 23:22 Thus also a woman leaving her husband, and presenting an heir from a stranger.
Sirach 23:23 For first she disobeyed in the Most High's law, and second transgressed against her husband, and third committed adultery in fornication, and presented children from a strange man.
Sirach 23:24 She will be brought out into an assembly, and there will be an inspection upon her children.
Sirach 23:25 Her children will not spread into a root, and her branches will not bear fruit.
Sirach 23:26 She will leave her memorial as a curse, and her reproach will not be wiped out,
Sirach 23:27 and those left behind will recognize that nothing is better than fear of the Lord, and nothing sweeter than attending to the Lord's commandments.

## Chapter 24

Sirach 24:1 Wisdom will praise her soul and boast in the midst of her people;
Sirach 24:2 in the assembly of the Most High she will open her mouth and boast before his power.
Sirach 24:3 I came forth from the mouth of the Most High and covered the earth like mist;
Sirach 24:4 I encamped in the heights, and my throne was in a pillar of cloud;
Sirach 24:5 I alone circled the circuit of heaven and walked in the depth of abysses;
Sirach 24:6 in the waves of the sea and in all the earth and in every people and nation I acquired possession.
Sirach 24:7 Among all these I sought rest, and in whose inheritance shall I lodge?
Sirach 24:8 Then the creator of all commanded me, and he who created me gave my tent rest and said, Encamp in Iakob, and receive an inheritance in Israel.
Sirach 24:9 Before the age, from the beginning, he created me, and until the age I shall certainly not cease.
Sirach 24:10 In a holy tent before him I ministered, and thus I was established in Sion;
Sirach 24:11 in a beloved city likewise he gave me rest, and in Ierusalem is my authority;
Sirach 24:12 and I took root in a glorified people, in the Lord's portion, his inheritance.
Sirach 24:13 Like a cedar I was raised up in Lebanon and like a cypress in the mountains of Aermon;
Sirach 24:14 like a palm I was raised up in Aiggadois and like rose plants in Iericho, like a comely olive in a plain, and I was raised up like a plane tree.
Sirach 24:15 Like cinnamon and aromatic aspalathus I have given a scent, and like choice myrrh I spread fragrance, like galbanum and onycha and stacte and like a vapor of frankincense in a tent.
Sirach 24:16 I, like a terebinth, extended my branches, and my branches are branches of glory and grace.
Sirach 24:17 I, like a vine, sprouted grace, and my blossoms are fruit of glory and wealth.
Sirach 24:19 Come to me, you who desire me, and be filled from my produce;
Sirach 24:20 for my remembrance is sweeter than honey, and my inheritance than a honeycomb.
Sirach 24:21 Those eating me will still hunger, and those drinking me will still thirst.
Sirach 24:22 He who listens to me will not be ashamed, and those working in me will not sin.
Sirach 24:23 All these things are the book of the covenant of God Most High, a law which Moyses commanded us as an inheritance for the congregations of Iakob,
Sirach 24:25 he who fills with wisdom like Phison and like Tigris in the days of new produce,
Sirach 24:26 he who fills with understanding like Euphrates and like Iordanes in the days of harvest,
Sirach 24:27 he who manifests discipline like light, like Geon in the days of vintage.
Sirach 24:28 The first did not finish knowing her, and likewise the last did not trace her out;
Sirach 24:29 for her thought increased from the sea, and her counsel from a great abyss.
Sirach 24:30 And I, like a canal from a river and like a water conduit, came forth into a garden;
Sirach 24:31 I said, I will water my garden and drench my garden bed; and behold, my canal became a river for me, and my river became a sea.
Sirach 24:32 Still I will illuminate discipline like dawn and manifest them far away;
Sirach 24:33 still I will pour out teaching like prophecy and leave it for generations of ages.
