Sirach 50:23 May he give us gladness of heart, and may there be peace in our days in Israel according to the days of the age;
Sirach 50:24 may he entrust his mercy to us, and in our days let him redeem us.
Sirach 50:25 At two nations my soul was offended, and the third is not a nation;
Sirach 50:26 those sitting on a mountain of Samareia, and Phylistiim, and the foolish people dwelling in Sikima.
Sirach 50:27 Discipline of understanding and knowledge Iesous son of Sirach Eleazar, the Ierusalemite, inscribed in this book, who rained down wisdom from his heart.
Sirach 50:28 Blessed is he who will be occupied with these things, and having placed them upon his heart he will become wise;
Sirach 50:29 for if he does them, he will be strong for everything; because the Lord's light is his trace.

## Chapter 51

Sirach 51:1 I will confess to you, Lord, king, and praise you, God my savior; I confess to your name,
Sirach 51:2 because you became my shelter and helper and redeemed my body from destruction and from a snare of a tongue's slander, from lips working falsehood; and before those standing nearby you became a helper and redeemed me,
Sirach 51:3 according to the abundance of your mercy and name, from gnashing, ready for food, from the hand of those seeking my soul, from the many afflictions which I had,
Sirach 51:4 from the choking of a pyre all around and from the midst of fire which I did not kindle,
Sirach 51:5 from the depth of the belly of Hades and from an unclean tongue and a false word.
Sirach 51:6 To a king, slander of an unjust tongue. My soul drew near as far as death, and my life was close to Hades below.
Sirach 51:7 They surrounded me on every side, and there was no helper; I looked to assistance from human beings, and there was none.
Sirach 51:8 And I remembered your mercy, Lord, and your work from an age, that you deliver those awaiting you and save them from the hand of enemies.
Sirach 51:9 And I raised my petition from earth and made supplication for rescue from death;
Sirach 51:10 I called upon the Lord, father of my lord, not to abandon me in days of affliction, at a time of proud acts, of helplessness; I will praise your name continually and sing hymns in confession.
Sirach 51:11 And my supplication was heard; for you saved me from destruction and delivered me from an evil time.
Sirach 51:12 For this reason I will confess to you and praise you and bless the Lord's name.
Sirach 51:13 While still younger, before I wandered, I sought wisdom openly in my prayer.
Sirach 51:14 Before a temple I asked concerning her, and until the last I will seek her out.
Sirach 51:15 From blossom, as of a ripening grape, my heart rejoiced in her. My foot stepped in uprightness; from my youth I tracked her.
Sirach 51:16 I inclined my ear a little and received, and found much discipline for myself.
Sirach 51:17 Progress came to me in her; to him who gives me wisdom I will give glory.
Sirach 51:18 For I considered doing her, and I was zealous for the good and will certainly not be ashamed.
Sirach 51:19 My soul has struggled in her, and in doing the law I was exact. I spread my hands toward the height and mourned the ignorances of her.
Sirach 51:20 I directed my soul toward her and in cleansing found her. I acquired a heart with her from the beginning; for this reason I will certainly not be abandoned.
Sirach 51:21 And my belly was troubled to seek her out; for this reason I acquired a good possession.
Sirach 51:22 The Lord gave me a tongue as my wage, and with it I will praise him.
Sirach 51:23 Draw near to me, undisciplined ones, and lodge in a house of discipline.
Sirach 51:24 Why do you say you are lacking in these things, and your souls thirst exceedingly?
Sirach 51:25 I opened my mouth and spoke, Acquire for yourselves without silver.
Sirach 51:26 Put your neck beneath a yoke, and let your soul receive discipline. She is near to find.
Sirach 51:27 See with your eyes that I labored little and found much rest for myself.
Sirach 51:28 Partake of discipline with a great number of silver, and acquire much gold in her.
Sirach 51:29 May your soul rejoice in his mercy, and may you not be ashamed in his praise.
Sirach 51:30 Work your work before the time, and he will give your wage in his time.

# Psalms of Solomon

The Apostolic Bible. Public domain. https://apostolic-bible.ysys9.chatgpt.site/license.html


## Chapter 1

Psalms of Solomon 1:1 I cried to the Lord when I was afflicted to the utmost, to God when sinners attacked;
Psalms of Solomon 1:2 suddenly a cry of war was heard before me; [I said] He will listen to me, because I was filled with righteousness.
Psalms of Solomon 1:3 I reasoned in my heart that I was filled with righteousness, when I prospered and became abundant in children.
Psalms of Solomon 1:4 Their wealth was spread into all the earth, and their glory to the extremity of the earth.
Psalms of Solomon 1:5 They were raised as far as the stars; they said, They will certainly not fall;
Psalms of Solomon 1:6 and they acted insolently in their good things and did not bear it.
Psalms of Solomon 1:7 Their sins were in hidden places, and I did not know;
Psalms of Solomon 1:8 their lawlessness exceeded the nations before them; they profaned the Lord's holy things with profanation.

## Chapter 2

Psalms of Solomon 2:1 t A psalm for Salomon; concerning Ierusalem.
Psalms of Solomon 2:1 When the sinner acted proudly, with a battering ram he cast down fortified walls, and you did not hinder him.
Psalms of Solomon 2:2 Foreign nations ascended upon your altar; they trampled with their sandals in pride,
Psalms of Solomon 2:3 because the sons of Ierusalem defiled the Lord's holy things; they profaned God's gifts with lawlessness.
Psalms of Solomon 2:4 Because of these things he said, Cast them far away from me; I take no pleasure in them.
Psalms of Solomon 2:5 The beauty of her glory was despised before God; it was dishonored to the utmost.
Psalms of Solomon 2:6 The sons and daughters are in evil captivity; their neck is under a seal, under a mark among the nations.
Psalms of Solomon 2:7 According to their sins he did to them, because he abandoned them into the hands of those prevailing.
Psalms of Solomon 2:8 For he turned his face away from mercy toward them, young and old and their children altogether, because they did evil things altogether, not listening.
Psalms of Solomon 2:9 And heaven was deeply grieved, and earth abhorred them, because no person upon it did as much as they did.
Psalms of Solomon 2:10 And earth will know all your righteous judgments, O God.
Psalms of Solomon 2:11 They set the sons of Ierusalem for mockery in place of prostitutes in her; everyone passing by entered before the sun.
Psalms of Solomon 2:12 They mocked their lawlessness just as they themselves were doing; before the sun they exposed their injustices.
Psalms of Solomon 2:13 And the daughters of Ierusalem were profane according to your judgment, because they themselves defiled themselves in the mire of mingling.
Psalms of Solomon 2:14 I suffer pain in my belly and my inward parts over these things.
Psalms of Solomon 2:15 I will justify you, O God, in uprightness of heart, because in your judgments is your righteousness, O God.
Psalms of Solomon 2:16 Because you repaid sinners according to their works and according to their exceedingly wicked sins.
Psalms of Solomon 2:17 You uncovered their sins, that your judgment might appear; you erased their remembrance from earth.
Psalms of Solomon 2:18 God is a righteous judge and will not admire a face.
Psalms of Solomon 2:19 For nations reproached Ierusalem in trampling; her beauty was dragged down from a throne of glory.
Psalms of Solomon 2:20 She girded herself with sackcloth instead of a garment of comeliness, a cord around her head instead of a crown.
Psalms of Solomon 2:21 She removed a turban of glory, which God had put around her; her beauty is in dishonor; she was cast upon the earth.
Psalms of Solomon 2:22 And I saw and made supplication before the Lord's face and said, Let it suffice, Lord, that your hand is heavy upon Ierusalem in the bringing of nations;
Psalms of Solomon 2:23 because they mocked and did not spare, in wrath and fury with resentment; and they will be brought to an end unless you, Lord, rebuke them in your wrath.
Psalms of Solomon 2:24 Because they did not do it in zeal, but in desire of soul to pour out their wrath upon us in plunder.
Psalms of Solomon 2:25 Do not delay, O God, in repaying upon their heads, in declaring the dragon's pride in dishonor.
Psalms of Solomon 2:26 And I did not wait long until God showed me his insolence, pierced upon the mountains of Egypt, despised beyond the least upon earth and sea;
Psalms of Solomon 2:27 his body carried about upon waves in great insult, and there was no one burying him, because he despised him in dishonor.
Psalms of Solomon 2:28 He did not reckon that he is a human being, and he did not reckon the later end.
Psalms of Solomon 2:29 He said, I will be lord of earth and sea; and he did not recognize that God is great, mighty in his great strength.
Psalms of Solomon 2:30 He is king upon the heavens and judges kings and rulers;
Psalms of Solomon 2:31 he who raises me to glory and puts the proud to sleep in destruction of an age, in dishonor, because they did not know him.
Psalms of Solomon 2:32 And now see, great men of the earth, the Lord's judgment, because he is a great king and righteous, judging what is beneath heaven.
Psalms of Solomon 2:33 Bless God, you who fear the Lord with knowledge, because the Lord's mercy is upon those fearing him, with judgment
Psalms of Solomon 2:34 to distinguish between righteous person and sinner, to repay sinners into the age according to their works
Psalms of Solomon 2:35 and have mercy on a righteous person from a sinner's humiliation, and repay a sinner for what he did to a righteous person.
Psalms of Solomon 2:36 Because the Lord is kind to those calling upon him with endurance, to do according to his mercy for his holy ones, to stand continually before him in strength.
Psalms of Solomon 2:37 Blessed is the Lord into the age before his servants.

## Chapter 3

Psalms of Solomon 3:1 t A psalm for Salomon; concerning righteous people.
Psalms of Solomon 3:1 Why do you sleep, soul, and not bless the Lord? Sing a new hymn to God, who is to be praised.
Psalms of Solomon 3:2 Sing and keep watch for his watching, because a psalm to God from a good heart is good.
Psalms of Solomon 3:3 The righteous remember the Lord continually, in confession and justification the Lord's judgments.
Psalms of Solomon 3:4 A righteous person will not disregard being disciplined by the Lord; his good will is continually before the Lord.
Psalms of Solomon 3:5 The righteous person stumbled and justified the Lord; he fell and looks to what God will do to him; he watches from where his salvation will come.
Psalms of Solomon 3:6 The truth of the righteous is from God their savior; sin upon sin does not lodge in a righteous person's house;
Psalms of Solomon 3:7 the righteous person continually inspects his house to remove injustice in his transgression.
Psalms of Solomon 3:8 He made atonement for ignorance with fasting and humiliation of his soul, and the Lord cleanses every holy man and his house.
Psalms of Solomon 3:9 A sinner stumbled and curses his life, the day of his birth and his mother's labor pains.
Psalms of Solomon 3:10 He added sins upon sins to his life; he fell, because his fall is evil, and he will not rise.
Psalms of Solomon 3:11 The sinner's destruction is into the age, and he will not be remembered when he inspects the righteous.
Psalms of Solomon 3:12 This is the portion of sinners into the age; but those fearing the Lord will rise to eternal life, and their life is in the Lord's light and will no longer cease.

## Chapter 4

Psalms of Solomon 4:1 t A discourse of Salomon; for people-pleasers.
Psalms of Solomon 4:1 Why do you, profane one, sit in a council of holy ones, and your heart has departed far from the Lord, provoking the God of Israel with unlawful deeds?
Psalms of Solomon 4:2 Excessive in words, excessive in signaling beyond everyone, he who is harsh in words to condemn sinners in judgment;
Psalms of Solomon 4:3 and his hand is among the first against him, as in zeal, and he himself is guilty of a variety of sins and of lack of self-control.
Psalms of Solomon 4:4 His eyes are upon every woman without distinction; his tongue is false in a transaction with an oath.
Psalms of Solomon 4:5 At night and in hidden places he sins as though unseen; with his eyes he speaks to every woman in a compact of evil; quick to enter every house cheerfully, as though innocent.
Psalms of Solomon 4:6 May God remove those living hypocritically with holy ones, with corruption of his flesh and poverty in his life;
Psalms of Solomon 4:7 may God uncover the works of people-pleasing human beings, his works in derision and mockery.
Psalms of Solomon 4:8 And may holy ones justify their God's judgment when sinners are removed from before a righteous person, a people-pleaser speaking law with deceit.
Psalms of Solomon 4:9 And their eyes are upon a man's house in stability, like a snake, to dissolve each other's wisdom with words of the unlawful.
Psalms of Solomon 4:10 His words are deceptions for the practice of unjust desire; he did not depart until he prevailed, to scatter as in orphanhood;
Psalms of Solomon 4:11 and he made a house desolate because of unlawful desire; he deceived with words, because there is none seeing and judging;
Psalms of Solomon 4:12 he was filled with this unlawful deed, and his eyes are upon another house, to destroy with words of encouragement.
Psalms of Solomon 4:13 His soul, like Hades, is not filled with all these things.
Psalms of Solomon 4:14 May his portion, Lord, be in dishonor before you, his departure with sighs and his entrance with a curse;
Psalms of Solomon 4:15 his life in pains and poverty and want, Lord, his sleep in griefs and his awakening in perplexities.
Psalms of Solomon 4:16 May sleep be taken away from his temples at night; may he fail in every work of his hands in dishonor.
Psalms of Solomon 4:17 May he enter his house empty-handed, and his house be deficient in everything with which he will fill his soul;
Psalms of Solomon 4:18 his old age in the solitude of childlessness until his taking away.
Psalms of Solomon 4:19 May the flesh of people-pleasers be scattered by beasts, and the bones of the unlawful before the sun in dishonor.
Psalms of Solomon 4:20 May ravens gouge out the eyes of hypocrites, because they made many people's houses desolate in dishonor and scattered them in desire
Psalms of Solomon 4:21 and did not remember God and did not fear God in all these things, and provoked God to wrath and exasperated him.
Psalms of Solomon 4:22 May he remove them from the earth, because they deceived souls of the innocent with false reasoning.
Psalms of Solomon 4:23 Blessed are those fearing the Lord in their innocence; the Lord will rescue them from deceitful people and sinners, and rescue us from every unlawful stumbling block.
Psalms of Solomon 4:24 May God remove those proudly doing every injustice, because the Lord our God is a great and mighty judge in righteousness.
Psalms of Solomon 4:25 May your mercy, Lord, be upon all those loving you.

## Chapter 5

Psalms of Solomon 5:1 t A psalm for Salomon.
Psalms of Solomon 5:1 Lord God, I will praise your name in exultation, among those knowing your righteous judgments;
Psalms of Solomon 5:2 because you are kind and merciful, the refuge of the poor; when I cry to you, do not remain silent toward me.
Psalms of Solomon 5:3 For [anyone] will not take spoils from a powerful man; and who will take from all that you made, unless you give?
Psalms of Solomon 5:4 Because a person and his portion are from you by weight; he will not add to increase beyond your judgment, O God.
Psalms of Solomon 5:5 When we are afflicted we will call upon you for help, and you will not turn away our supplication, because you are our God.
Psalms of Solomon 5:6 Do not make your hand heavy upon us, that we may not sin through necessity.
Psalms of Solomon 5:7 And if you do not turn us back, we will not hold back, but we will come to you.
Psalms of Solomon 5:8 For if I hunger, I will cry to you, O God, and you will give to me.
Psalms of Solomon 5:9 The birds and fish you feed when you give rain to deserts for the sprouting of green grass;
Psalms of Solomon 5:10 you prepared fodder in a desert for every living being, and if they hunger, they will raise their face toward you.
Psalms of Solomon 5:11 Kings and rulers and peoples you feed, O God, and who is the hope of poor and needy except you, Lord?
Psalms of Solomon 5:12 And you will listen; because who is kind and equitable except you, to gladden a lowly person's soul when you open your hand in mercy?
Psalms of Solomon 5:13 A person's kindness is with sparing, and tomorrow's too, and if he repeats it without murmuring, even this you might marvel at.
Psalms of Solomon 5:14 But your gift is abundant with kindness and rich, and he whose hope is upon you will not spare in giving.
Psalms of Solomon 5:15 Upon all the earth is your mercy, Lord, in kindness.
Psalms of Solomon 5:16 Blessed is he whom God remembers in a proportion of sufficiency; if a person increases excessively, he sins.
Psalms of Solomon 5:17 What is moderate with righteousness is sufficient, and in this is the Lord's blessing unto fullness with righteousness.
Psalms of Solomon 5:18 May those fearing the Lord rejoice in good things, and your kindness be upon Israel in your kingdom.
Psalms of Solomon 5:19 Blessed is the Lord's glory, because he is our king.

## Chapter 6

Psalms of Solomon 6:1 t In hope; for Salomon.
Psalms of Solomon 6:1 Blessed is a man whose heart is ready to call upon the Lord's name; when he remembers the Lord's name he will be saved.
Psalms of Solomon 6:2 His ways are directed by the Lord, and the works of his hands have been guarded by the Lord his God.
Psalms of Solomon 6:3 From a vision of his evil dreams his soul will not be troubled; in crossing rivers and in the tumult of seas he will not be terrified.
Psalms of Solomon 6:4 He rose from his sleep and blessed the Lord's name; for the stability of his heart he sang hymns to his God's name;
Psalms of Solomon 6:5 and he made supplication before the Lord's face concerning all his house, and the Lord heard the prayer of everyone in fear of God.
Psalms of Solomon 6:6 And every request of a soul hoping toward him the Lord fulfills; blessed is the Lord who does mercy to those loving him in truth.

## Chapter 7

Psalms of Solomon 7:1 t For Salomon; of turning back.
Psalms of Solomon 7:1 Do not move your tent away from us, O God, that those who hated us without cause may not attack us.
Psalms of Solomon 7:2 Because you repelled them, O God; let their foot not tread the inheritance of your sanctuary.
Psalms of Solomon 7:3 You, by your will, discipline us, and do not give us to nations.
Psalms of Solomon 7:4 For if you send death, you will command it concerning us;
Psalms of Solomon 7:5 because you are merciful and will not be angered so as to bring us to an end.
Psalms of Solomon 7:6 When your name encamps in our midst, we will be shown mercy, and a nation will not prevail against us.
Psalms of Solomon 7:7 Because you are our shield, and we will call upon you, and you will listen to us.
Psalms of Solomon 7:8 Because you will have pity on the race of Israel into the age and will not repel it.
Psalms of Solomon 7:9 And we are beneath your yoke for the age, and the scourge of your discipline.
Psalms of Solomon 7:10 You will direct us at the time of your assistance, to have mercy on the house of Iakob for the day on which you promised them.

## Chapter 8

Psalms of Solomon 8:1 t For Salomon; for strife.
Psalms of Solomon 8:1 Affliction and a voice of war my ear heard, a voice of a trumpet sounding slaughter and destruction;
Psalms of Solomon 8:2 a voice of many people like a very great wind, like a storm of much fire carried through a desert.
Psalms of Solomon 8:3 And I said [in] my heart, Where then will God judge him?
Psalms of Solomon 8:4 A voice I heard toward Ierusalem, a city of a sanctuary;
Psalms of Solomon 8:5 my loins were shattered from the hearing, my knees were paralyzed, my heart was afraid, my bones were troubled like flax.
Psalms of Solomon 8:6 I said, They will direct their ways in righteousness.
Psalms of Solomon 8:7 I considered God's judgments from the creation of heaven and earth; I justified God in his judgments from an age.
Psalms of Solomon 8:8 God uncovered their sins before the sun; all the earth knew God's righteous judgments.
Psalms of Solomon 8:9 In underground hidden places were their unlawful deeds, provoking wrath; son with mother and father with daughter were mingled together.
Psalms of Solomon 8:10 Each committed adultery with his neighbor's wife; they made agreements among themselves with an oath concerning these things.
Psalms of Solomon 8:11 They plundered God's holy things as though there were no heir redeeming.
Psalms of Solomon 8:12 They trod the Lord's altar from every uncleanness, and with a discharge of blood they defiled the sacrifices as profane meats.
Psalms of Solomon 8:13 They left no sin which they did not do beyond the nations.
Psalms of Solomon 8:14 For this reason God mixed for them a spirit of wandering; he gave them a cup of unmixed wine to drink unto drunkenness.
Psalms of Solomon 8:15 He brought him from the extremity of the earth, him who strikes mightily; he decreed war upon Ierusalem and her land.
Psalms of Solomon 8:16 The rulers of the land met him with joy; they said to him, Your way is wished for; come, enter with peace.
Psalms of Solomon 8:17 They smoothed rough ways for his entrance, opened gates toward Ierusalem, crowned her walls.
Psalms of Solomon 8:18 He entered like a father into his sons' house with peace; he set his feet with great security.
Psalms of Solomon 8:19 He seized her tower citadels and the wall of Ierusalem, because God brought him with security in their wandering.
Psalms of Solomon 8:20 He destroyed their rulers and everyone wise in counsel; he poured out the blood of those dwelling in Ierusalem like water of uncleanness.
Psalms of Solomon 8:21 He led away their sons and daughters, whom they begot in profanation.
Psalms of Solomon 8:22 They did according to their uncleanness, just as their fathers; they defiled Ierusalem and the things sanctified for God's name.
Psalms of Solomon 8:23 God was justified in his judgments among the nations of the earth, and God's holy ones were like lambs in innocence in their midst.
Psalms of Solomon 8:24 Praiseworthy is the Lord who judges all the earth in his righteousness.
Psalms of Solomon 8:25 Behold now, O God, you showed us your judgment in your righteousness; our eyes saw your judgments, O God.
Psalms of Solomon 8:26 We justified your honored name into ages, because you are the God of righteousness, judging Israel with discipline.
Psalms of Solomon 8:27 Turn your mercy toward us, O God, and have pity on us;
Psalms of Solomon 8:28 gather the dispersion of Israel with mercy and kindness, because your faithfulness is with us.
Psalms of Solomon 8:29 And we hardened our neck, and you are our disciplinarian.
Psalms of Solomon 8:30 Do not overlook us, our God, that nations may not swallow us as though there were no redeemer.
Psalms of Solomon 8:31 And you are our God from the beginning, and our hope is upon you, Lord;
Psalms of Solomon 8:32 and we will not hold back from you, because your judgments upon us are kind.
Psalms of Solomon 8:33 For us and our children is favor into the age; Lord our savior, we will no longer be shaken for the time of the age.
Psalms of Solomon 8:34 Praiseworthy is the Lord in his judgments in the mouth of holy ones, and blessed is Israel by the Lord into the age.

## Chapter 9

Psalms of Solomon 9:1 t For Salomon; for reproof.
Psalms of Solomon 9:1 When Israel was led away in exile into a foreign land, when they departed from the Lord who redeemed them, they were cast away from the inheritance which the Lord gave them.
Psalms of Solomon 9:2 In every nation is the dispersion of Israel according to God's utterance, that you may be justified, O God, in your righteousness amid our lawlessness, because you are a righteous judge over all the peoples of the earth.
Psalms of Solomon 9:3 For no one doing unjust things will be hidden from your knowledge, and the righteous deeds of your holy ones are before you, Lord; and where will a person be hidden from your knowledge, O God?
Psalms of Solomon 9:4 Our works are in the choice and authority of our soul, to do righteousness and injustice by the works of our hands; and in your righteousness you inspect sons of human beings.
Psalms of Solomon 9:5 He who does righteousness treasures up life for himself with the Lord, and he who does injustice is himself responsible for his soul in destruction; for the Lord's judgments are in righteousness upon each man and house.
Psalms of Solomon 9:6 To whom will you show kindness, O God, except those calling upon the Lord? You will cleanse a soul amid sins in confession, in declarations, because shame is ours and our faces' concerning everything.
Psalms of Solomon 9:7 And to whom will you forgive sins except those who have sinned? You will bless righteous people and not hold them accountable for what they sinned, and your kindness is upon those sinning in repentance.
Psalms of Solomon 9:8 And now you are God, and we are the people whom you loved; see and have pity, God of Israel, because we are yours, and do not remove your mercy from us, that they may not attack us.
Psalms of Solomon 9:9 Because you chose the seed of Abraam above all the nations and placed your name upon us, Lord, and you will not repel us into the age.
Psalms of Solomon 9:10 In a covenant you made a disposition with our fathers concerning us, and we will hope upon you in the turning of our soul.
Psalms of Solomon 9:11 The Lord's mercy is upon the house of Israel into the age and beyond.

## Chapter 10

Psalms of Solomon 10:1 t In hymns; for Salomon.
Psalms of Solomon 10:1 Blessed is a man whom the Lord remembered in reproof, and he was turned around from an evil way by a scourge, to be cleansed from sin so as not to multiply it.
Psalms of Solomon 10:2 He who prepares a back for scourges will be cleansed; for the Lord is kind to those enduring discipline.
Psalms of Solomon 10:3 For he will straighten the ways of righteous people and will not distort them in discipline, and the Lord's mercy is upon those loving him in truth.
Psalms of Solomon 10:4 And the Lord will remember his servants in mercy; for the testimony is in the law of an eternal covenant, the Lord's testimony is upon human ways in inspection.
Psalms of Solomon 10:5 Righteous and holy is our Lord in his judgments into the age, and Israel will praise the Lord's name in gladness.
Psalms of Solomon 10:6 And holy ones will confess in an assembly of the people, and God will have mercy on poor people in Israel's gladness;
Psalms of Solomon 10:7 because God is kind and merciful into the age, and congregations of Israel will glorify the Lord's name.
Psalms of Solomon 10:8 The Lord's salvation is upon the house of Israel unto eternal gladness.

## Chapter 11

Psalms of Solomon 11:1 t For Salomon; for expectation.
Psalms of Solomon 11:1 Blow a trumpet in Sion, a trumpet signaling holy things; proclaim in Ierusalem a voice of one announcing good news; because God had mercy on Israel in their inspection.
Psalms of Solomon 11:2 Stand, Ierusalem, on a height and see your children from east and west gathered together by the Lord.
Psalms of Solomon 11:3 From the north they come with the gladness of their God; from distant islands God gathered them.
Psalms of Solomon 11:4 High mountains he lowered to level ground for them; the hills fled from their entrance;
Psalms of Solomon 11:5 the woods shaded them in their passage; every fragrant tree God caused to spring up for them,
Psalms of Solomon 11:6 that Israel might pass in an inspection of their God's glory.
Psalms of Solomon 11:7 Put on, Ierusalem, the garments of your glory; prepare the robe of your sanctuary; because God spoke good things for Israel into the age and beyond.
Psalms of Solomon 11:8 May the Lord do what he spoke concerning Israel and Ierusalem; may the Lord raise Israel in the name of his glory;
Psalms of Solomon 11:9 the Lord's mercy is upon Israel into the age and beyond.

## Chapter 12

Psalms of Solomon 12:1 t For Salomon; on the tongue of the unlawful.
Psalms of Solomon 12:1 Lord, rescue my soul from an unlawful and wicked man, from an unlawful and whispering tongue speaking false and deceitful things.
Psalms of Solomon 12:2 In a variety of turns are the words of a wicked man's tongue, like fire among a people kindling its beauty.
Psalms of Solomon 12:3 His dwelling is to burn houses with a false tongue, to cut down trees of gladness that flames against the unlawful, to confound houses in war with whispering lips.
Psalms of Solomon 12:4 May God put the lips of the unlawful far from innocent people in perplexity, and may the bones of whisperers be scattered away from those fearing the Lord; in a fire of flame may a whispering tongue perish away from holy ones.
Psalms of Solomon 12:5 May the Lord guard a quiet soul hating unjust people, and may the Lord direct a man making peace at home.
Psalms of Solomon 12:6 The Lord's salvation is upon Israel his servant into the age; and may sinners perish altogether from before the Lord, and may the Lord's holy ones inherit the Lord's promises.

## Chapter 13

Psalms of Solomon 13:1 t A psalm for Salomon; consolation of the righteous.
Psalms of Solomon 13:1 The Lord's right hand sheltered me; the Lord's right hand spared us;
Psalms of Solomon 13:2 the Lord's arm saved us from a passing sword, from famine and the death of sinners.
Psalms of Solomon 13:3 Evil beasts ran against them; with their teeth they tore their flesh, and with their molars they crushed their bones;
Psalms of Solomon 13:4 and from all these things the Lord rescued us.
Psalms of Solomon 13:5 The pious person was troubled because of his transgressions, lest he be taken away together with the sinners;
Psalms of Solomon 13:6 because terrible is the sinner's overthrow, and none of all these things will touch a righteous person.
Psalms of Solomon 13:7 Because the discipline of the righteous in ignorance and the overthrow of sinners are not alike.
Psalms of Solomon 13:8 With restraint a righteous person is disciplined, that the sinner may not rejoice over the righteous person;
Psalms of Solomon 13:9 because he will admonish a righteous person as a beloved son, and his discipline is as that of a firstborn.
Psalms of Solomon 13:10 Because the Lord will spare his holy ones and erase their transgressions by discipline.
Psalms of Solomon 13:11 For the life of the righteous is into the age; but sinners will be taken away to destruction, and their remembrance will no longer be found;
Psalms of Solomon 13:12 but upon the holy ones is the Lord's mercy, and upon those fearing him his mercy.

## Chapter 14

Psalms of Solomon 14:1 t A hymn for Salomon.
Psalms of Solomon 14:1 The Lord is faithful to those loving him in truth, to those enduring his discipline,
Psalms of Solomon 14:2 to those walking in the righteousness of his commands, in the law which he commanded us for our life.
Psalms of Solomon 14:3 The Lord's holy ones will live in him into the age; the Lord's garden, the trees of life, are his holy ones.
Psalms of Solomon 14:4 Their planting is rooted into the age; they will not be plucked out all the days of heaven;
Psalms of Solomon 14:5 because Israel is God's portion and inheritance.
Psalms of Solomon 14:6 And not so are the sinners and unlawful, who loved a day in participation in their sin;
Psalms of Solomon 14:7 in the smallness of rottenness is their desire, and they did not remember God.
Psalms of Solomon 14:8 Because human ways are continually known before him, and he knows the heart's chambers before they come to be.
Psalms of Solomon 14:9 For this reason their inheritance is Hades and darkness and destruction, and they will not be found on the day of mercy for the righteous;
Psalms of Solomon 14:10 but the Lord's holy ones will inherit life in gladness.

## Chapter 15

Psalms of Solomon 15:1 t A psalm for Salomon with a song.
Psalms of Solomon 15:1 When I was afflicted I called upon the Lord's name; I hoped for help from the God of Iakob and was saved; because you are the hope and refuge of the poor, O God.
Psalms of Solomon 15:2 For who has strength, O God, except to confess to you in truth? And in what is a person powerful except confessing to your name?
Psalms of Solomon 15:3 A new psalm with a song in gladness of heart, fruit of lips with the tuned instrument of a tongue, a firstfruit of lips from a holy and righteous heart,
Psalms of Solomon 15:4 he who does these things will not be shaken into the age by evil; a flame of fire and the wrath of unjust people will not touch him,
Psalms of Solomon 15:5 when it goes forth against sinners from before the Lord to destroy every substance of sinners;
Psalms of Solomon 15:6 because God's sign is upon righteous people for salvation.
Psalms of Solomon 15:7 Famine and sword and death are far from righteous people, for they will flee from holy ones like those pursued in war;
Psalms of Solomon 15:8 but they will pursue sinners and overtake them, and those doing lawlessness will not escape the Lord's judgment;
Psalms of Solomon 15:9 they will be overtaken as by experienced enemies, for the sign of destruction is upon their forehead.
Psalms of Solomon 15:10 And the inheritance of sinners is destruction and darkness, and their lawlessness will pursue them as far as Hades below.
Psalms of Solomon 15:11 Their inheritance will not be found for their children, for sins will make sinners' houses desolate;
Psalms of Solomon 15:12 and sinners will perish into the age on the day of the Lord's judgment, when God inspects the earth with his judgment;
Psalms of Solomon 15:13 but those fearing the Lord will be shown mercy on it and live in the mercy of their God; and sinners will perish for the time of the age.

## Chapter 16

Psalms of Solomon 16:1 t A hymn for Salomon; for assistance to holy ones.
Psalms of Solomon 16:1 When my soul grew drowsy away from the Lord, I nearly slipped in the deep sleep of those sleeping far from God,
Psalms of Solomon 16:2 my soul was nearly poured out into death, close to the gates of Hades with a sinner,
Psalms of Solomon 16:3 when my soul was carried away from the Lord God of Israel, had the Lord not helped me by his mercy into the age.
Psalms of Solomon 16:4 He pricked me like a horse's goad for his watching; my savior and helper at every time saved me.
Psalms of Solomon 16:5 I will confess to you, O God, because you helped me unto salvation and did not reckon me with sinners unto destruction.
Psalms of Solomon 16:6 Do not remove your mercy from me, O God, nor remembrance of you from my heart until death.
Psalms of Solomon 16:7 Hold me back, O God, from evil sin and from every wicked woman causing a senseless person to stumble.
Psalms of Solomon 16:8 And let not the beauty of a woman acting unlawfully deceive me, nor that of anything subject to unprofitable sin.
Psalms of Solomon 16:9 Direct the works of my hands in your place, and preserve my steps in remembrance of you.
Psalms of Solomon 16:10 Enclose my tongue and my lips in words of truth; put wrath and irrational fury far from me.
Psalms of Solomon 16:11 Put murmuring and faintheartedness in affliction far from me, if I sin when you discipline for turning back.
Psalms of Solomon 16:12 But with good will and cheerfulness support my soul; when you strengthen my soul, what is given will suffice for me.
Psalms of Solomon 16:13 Because unless you strengthen, who will endure discipline in poverty?
Psalms of Solomon 16:14 When a soul is reproved by the hand of his rottenness, your testing is in his flesh and in the affliction of poverty;
Psalms of Solomon 16:15 when a righteous person endures in these things, he will be shown mercy by the Lord.

## Chapter 17

Psalms of Solomon 17:1 t A psalm for Salomon with a song; for the king.
Psalms of Solomon 17:1 Lord, you yourself are our king into the age and beyond; because in you, O God, our soul will boast.
Psalms of Solomon 17:2 And what is the span of a person's life upon the earth? According to his span is his hope upon him too.
Psalms of Solomon 17:3 But we will hope upon God our savior; because our God's might is into the age with mercy, and our God's kingdom is into the age over the nations in judgment.
Psalms of Solomon 17:4 You, Lord, chose David as king over Israel, and you swore to him concerning his seed into the age, that his royal house should not cease before you.
Psalms of Solomon 17:5 And in our sins sinners rose against us; they attacked us and drove us out, those to whom you did not promise; with violence they took away and did not glorify your honored name.
Psalms of Solomon 17:6 In glory they established a royal house in place of their height; they made David's throne desolate in the pride of exchange.
Psalms of Solomon 17:7 And you, O God, will cast them down and remove their seed from the earth when a person foreign to our race rises against them.
Psalms of Solomon 17:8 According to their sins you will repay them, O God, for it to be found for them according to their works.
Psalms of Solomon 17:9 God did not have mercy on them; he searched out their seed and did not leave one of them.
Psalms of Solomon 17:10 Faithful is the Lord in all his judgments which he executes upon the earth.
Psalms of Solomon 17:11 The lawless one made our land desolate of its inhabitants; they made young and old and their children vanish together;
Psalms of Solomon 17:12 in the wrath of his beauty he sent them out as far as the west, and the rulers of the land for mockery, and did not spare.
Psalms of Solomon 17:13 In estrangement the enemy acted proudly, and his heart is estranged from our God.
Psalms of Solomon 17:14 And all that he did in Ierusalem was just as the nations too do in the cities of their strength.
Psalms of Solomon 17:15 And the sons of the covenant dominated them among mixed nations; there was none among them doing mercy and truth in Ierusalem.
Psalms of Solomon 17:16 Those loving congregations of holy ones fled from them; like sparrows they flew out from their resting place.
Psalms of Solomon 17:17 They wandered in deserts to save their souls from evil, and precious in the eyes of sojourning was a soul saved from among them.
Psalms of Solomon 17:18 Into all the earth came their scattering by lawless people, because heaven held back from dripping rain upon the earth.
Psalms of Solomon 17:19 Perennial springs from abysses, from high mountains, were restrained, because there was none among them doing righteousness and judgment.
Psalms of Solomon 17:20 From their ruler and the least of the people they were in every sin, the king in unlawful conduct and the judge in disobedience and the people in sin.
Psalms of Solomon 17:21 See, Lord, and raise for them their king, a son of David, for the time which you chose, O God, for him to reign over Israel your servant;
Psalms of Solomon 17:22 and gird him with strength to shatter unjust rulers, to cleanse Ierusalem from nations trampling in destruction,
Psalms of Solomon 17:23 in wisdom of righteousness to drive sinners out of the inheritance, to wipe out a sinner's pride like a potter's vessels,
Psalms of Solomon 17:24 with an iron rod to shatter all their substance, to destroy unlawful nations with the word of his mouth,
Psalms of Solomon 17:25 at his threat for nations to flee from before him, and to reprove sinners by the word of their heart.
Psalms of Solomon 17:26 And he will gather a holy people whom he will lead in righteousness, and judge the tribes of a people sanctified by the Lord his God;
Psalms of Solomon 17:27 and he will not allow injustice to lodge any longer in their midst, and no person knowing evil will dwell with them; for he will know them, that all of them are sons of God.
Psalms of Solomon 17:28 And he will apportion them in their tribes upon the earth, and a sojourner and one of another race will no longer sojourn with them;
Psalms of Solomon 17:29 he will judge peoples and nations in the wisdom of his righteousness. Musical interlude.
Psalms of Solomon 17:30 And he will have peoples of nations serve him beneath his yoke, and he will glorify the Lord prominently in all the earth and cleanse Ierusalem in sanctification as also from the beginning,
Psalms of Solomon 17:31 for nations to come from the extremity of the earth to see his glory, bringing as gifts her exhausted sons, and to see the Lord's glory with which God glorified her.
Psalms of Solomon 17:32 And he is a righteous king taught by God over them, and there is no injustice in his days among them, because all are holy, and their king is the Lord's anointed.
Psalms of Solomon 17:33 For he will not hope upon horse and rider and bow, nor multiply gold or silver for himself for war, and with many [peoples] he will not gather hopes for a day of war.
Psalms of Solomon 17:34 The Lord himself is his king, the hope of him who is powerful through hope in God, and he will have mercy on all the nations before him in fear.
Psalms of Solomon 17:35 For he will strike earth with the word of his mouth into an age; he will bless the Lord's people with wisdom and gladness;
Psalms of Solomon 17:36 and he is clean from sin to rule a great people, to reprove rulers and remove sinners by the strength of a word.
Psalms of Solomon 17:37 And he will not weaken in his days, relying on his God; because God made him powerful in a holy spirit and wise in counsel of understanding with strength and righteousness.
Psalms of Solomon 17:38 And the Lord's blessing is with him in strength, and he will not weaken.
Psalms of Solomon 17:39 His hope is upon the Lord, and who can prevail against him?
Psalms of Solomon 17:40 Strong in his works and mighty in fear of God, shepherding the Lord's flock in faithfulness and righteousness, and he will not allow weakness among them in their pasture.
Psalms of Solomon 17:41 In equality he will lead them all, and there will be no pride among them, for oppression to occur among them.
Psalms of Solomon 17:42 This is the comeliness of the king of Israel, which God knew, to raise him over the house of Israel to discipline it.
Psalms of Solomon 17:43 His utterances have been refined beyond the foremost precious gold; in congregations he will distinguish the tribes of a sanctified people; his words are like words of holy ones among sanctified peoples.
Psalms of Solomon 17:44 Blessed are those who come to be in those days to see the good things of Israel in a congregation of tribes, which God will do.
Psalms of Solomon 17:45 May God hasten his mercy upon Israel; may he rescue us from the uncleanness of profane enemies.
Psalms of Solomon 17:46 The Lord himself is our king into the age and beyond.

## Chapter 18

Psalms of Solomon 18:1 t A psalm for Salomon; further concerning the Lord's anointed.
Psalms of Solomon 18:1 Lord, your mercy is upon the works of your hands into the age, your kindness with a rich gift upon Israel;
Psalms of Solomon 18:2 your eyes look upon them, and none of them will lack; your ears listen to a poor person's supplication in hope.
Psalms of Solomon 18:3 Your judgments are upon all the earth with mercy, and your love upon the seed of Abraam, the sons of Israel.
Psalms of Solomon 18:4 Your discipline is upon us as upon a firstborn, only-begotten son, to turn a listening soul from lack of learning in ignorance.
Psalms of Solomon 18:5 May God cleanse Israel for a day of mercy with blessing, for a day of choosing when he brings up his anointed.
Psalms of Solomon 18:6 Blessed are those who come to be in those days to see the Lord's good things which he will do for the coming generation
Psalms of Solomon 18:7 beneath the rod of discipline of the Lord's anointed, in fear of his God, in wisdom of spirit and righteousness and strength,
Psalms of Solomon 18:8 to direct a man in works of righteousness by fear of God, to establish them all before the Lord,
Psalms of Solomon 18:9 a good generation in fear of God, in days of mercy. Musical interlude.
Psalms of Solomon 18:10 Great is our God and glorious, dwelling in the heights, who arranged luminaries in their course for seasons of hours from days to days, and they did not transgress the way which you commanded them;
Psalms of Solomon 18:11 in fear of God is their way each day, from the day on which God created them and until an age;
Psalms of Solomon 18:12 and they did not wander from the day on which he created them; from ancient generations they did not depart from their ways, unless God commanded them at the bidding of his servants.

# Hosea

The Apostolic Bible. Public domain. https://apostolic-bible.ysys9.chatgpt.site/license.html


## Chapter 1

Hosea 1:1 The Lord's word which came to Osee son of Beeri in the days of Ozias and Ioatham and Achaz and Ezekias, kings of Iouda, and in the days of Ieroboam son of Ioas, king of Israel.
Hosea 1:2 The beginning of the Lord's word to Osee; and the Lord said to Osee, Go, take for yourself a wife of prostitution and children of prostitution, because the land will surely prostitute itself away from following the Lord.
Hosea 1:3 And he went and took Gomer daughter of Debelaim, and she conceived and bore him a son.
Hosea 1:4 And the Lord said to him, Call his name Iezrael, because yet a little while and I will avenge the blood of Iezrael upon the house of Iou and make the kingdom of the house of Israel cease;
Hosea 1:5 and it will be on that day, I will shatter Israel's bow in the valley of Iezrael. –
Hosea 1:6 And she conceived again and bore a daughter. And he said to him, Call her name Not – shown-mercy, because I will certainly no longer continue to have mercy on the house of Israel, but I will surely oppose them.
Hosea 1:7 But I will have mercy on the sons of Iouda and save them by the Lord their God, and I will not save them by bow or sword or war or chariots or horses or horsemen. –
Hosea 1:8 And she weaned Not – shown-mercy and conceived again and bore a son.
Hosea 1:9 And he said, Call his name Not – my – people, because you are not my people, and I am not yours.

## Chapter 2

Hosea 2:1 And the number of the sons of Israel was like the sand of the sea, which will not be measured out or counted; and it will be in the place where it was said to them, You are not my people, there they will be called sons of a living God.
Hosea 2:2 And the sons of Iouda and the sons of Israel will be gathered together and appoint for themselves one leadership and ascend from the land, because great is the day of Iezrael.
Hosea 2:3 Say to your brother, My – people, and to your sister, Shown-mercy.
Hosea 2:4 Dispute with your mother, dispute, because she is not my wife, and I am not her husband; and I will remove her prostitution from before my face and her adultery from between her breasts,
Hosea 2:5 so that I may strip her naked and restore her as on the day of her birth; and I will make her like a desert and set her like a waterless land and kill her with thirst;
Hosea 2:6 and her children I will certainly not show mercy, because they are children of prostitution.
Hosea 2:7 Because their mother prostituted herself, she who bore them acted shamefully; for she said, I will follow after my lovers who give me my breads and my water and my garments and my linens and my oil and everything that is due me.
Hosea 2:8 For this reason behold, I fence her way with stakes and will build up her ways, and she will certainly not find her path;
Hosea 2:9 and she will pursue her lovers and certainly not overtake them; and she will seek them and certainly not find them; and she will say, I will go and return to my former husband, because it was better for me then than now.
Hosea 2:10 And she did not know that I have given her the grain and wine and oil, and I multiplied silver for her; but she made silver and gold things for Baal.
Hosea 2:11 For this reason I will return and recover my grain at its hour and my wine at its season and take away my garments and my linens so as not to cover her indecency;
Hosea 2:12 and now I will uncover her uncleanness before her lovers, and no one will certainly deliver her from my hand;
Hosea 2:13 and I will turn away all her gladness, her festivals and her new moons and her sabbaths and all her festal assemblies;
Hosea 2:14 and I will make her vine and her fig trees vanish, of which she said, These are my wages which my lovers gave me, and I will make them a testimony, and the beasts of the field and the birds of heaven and the creeping things of earth will devour them;
Hosea 2:15 and I will avenge upon her the days of the Baalim, on which she sacrificed to them and put on her earrings and her necklaces and went after her lovers, but forgot me, says the Lord.
Hosea 2:16 For this reason behold, I lead her astray and will set her in a desert and speak to her heart
Hosea 2:17 and give her her possessions from there and the valley of Achor to open her understanding, and she will be humbled there as in the days of her infancy and as in the days of her ascent from the land of Egypt.
Hosea 2:18 And it will be on that day, says the Lord, she will call me, My husband, and no longer call me Baalim;
Hosea 2:19 and I will remove the names of the Baalim from her mouth, and their names will certainly no longer be remembered.
Hosea 2:20 And I will make for them on that day a covenant with the beasts of the field and with the birds of heaven and with the creeping things of earth; and bow and sword and war I will shatter out of the land and settle you in hope.
Hosea 2:21 And I will betroth you to myself into the age, and I will betroth you to myself in righteousness and judgment and mercy and compassion
Hosea 2:22 and I will betroth you to myself in faithfulness, and you will know the Lord.
Hosea 2:23 And it will be on that day, says the Lord, I will listen to heaven, and heaven will listen to earth,
Hosea 2:24 and earth will listen to grain and wine and oil, and they will listen to Iezrael.
Hosea 2:25 And I will sow her for myself upon the earth and have mercy on Not – shown-mercy and say to Not – my – people, You are my people, and he will say, You are the Lord my God.

## Chapter 3

Hosea 3:1 And the Lord said to me, Go again and love a woman loving evil things and an adulteress, just as God loves the sons of Israel, and they look to foreign gods and love cakes with raisins,
Hosea 3:2 and I hired for myself for fifteen of silver and a gomor of barley and a nebel of wine
Hosea 3:3 and said to her, Many days you will stay with me and certainly not prostitute yourself or belong to another man, and I will be with you.
Hosea 3:4 Because many days the sons of Israel will stay without king or ruler or sacrifice or altar or priesthood or manifestations.
Hosea 3:5 And after these things the sons of Israel will return and seek the Lord their God and David their king; and they will be astounded at the Lord and at his good things in the last days.

## Chapter 4

Hosea 4:1 Hear the Lord's word, sons of Israel, because the Lord has a judgment against those dwelling in the land, because there is no truth or mercy or knowledge of God upon the earth;
Hosea 4:2 curse and falsehood and murder and theft and adultery have been poured upon the earth, and they mingle blood with blood.
Hosea 4:3 For this reason the earth will mourn and be diminished with all those dwelling in it, with the beasts of the field and with the creeping things of earth and with the birds of heaven, and the fish of the sea will cease,
Hosea 4:4 so that no one may either litigate or reprove anyone; but my people is like a priest contradicted.
Hosea 4:5 And you will weaken by day, and a prophet too will weaken with you; to night I likened your mother.
Hosea 4:6 My people was likened to one not having knowledge; because you rejected knowledge, I too will reject you from serving me as priest; and you forgot your God's law, and I too will forget your children.
Hosea 4:7 According to their multitude, so they sinned against me; their glory I will make dishonor.
Hosea 4:8 They will eat the sins of my people, and in their injustices they will take their souls.
Hosea 4:9 And it will be, as the people, so also the priest, and I will avenge his ways upon him and repay him his counsels.
Hosea 4:10 And they will eat and certainly not be filled; they prostituted themselves and certainly will not prosper, because they abandoned the Lord, to keep him.
Hosea 4:11 Prostitution and wine and intoxicating drink the heart of my people received.
Hosea 4:12 With signs they inquired, and with his rods they reported to him; by a spirit of prostitution they were led astray and prostituted themselves away from their God.
Hosea 4:13 Upon the summits of mountains they sacrificed, and upon hills they offered sacrifices, beneath oak and poplar and a shading tree, because shelter is good. For this reason your daughters will prostitute themselves, and your daughters-in-law will commit adultery;
Hosea 4:14 and I will certainly not inspect your daughters when they prostitute themselves, and your daughters-in-law when they commit adultery, because they themselves too mingled with prostitutes and sacrificed with the initiated, and the people that understands entangled itself with a prostitute.
Hosea 4:15 But you, Israel, do not be ignorant, and Iouda, do not enter Galgala and do not ascend to the house of On and do not swear by the living Lord.
Hosea 4:16 Because like a frenzied heifer Israel became frenzied; now the Lord will pasture them like a lamb in a broad place.
Hosea 4:17 Ephraim, a partner of idols, set stumbling blocks for himself.
Hosea 4:18 He chose Chananites; they surely prostituted themselves; they loved dishonor out of their arrogance.
Hosea 4:19 You are a whirlwind in her wings, and they will be ashamed because of their altars.

## Chapter 5

Hosea 5:1 Hear these things, priests, and attend, house of Israel, and house of the king, give ear, because judgment is against you, because you became a snare at the lookout and like a net stretched upon Itabyrion,
Hosea 5:2 which those hunting prey fixed. But I am your disciplinarian;
Hosea 5:3 I knew Ephraim, and Israel is not absent from me, because now Ephraim prostituted himself, Israel was defiled;
Hosea 5:4 they did not give their counsels to returning to their God, because a spirit of prostitution is in them, but they did not know the Lord.
Hosea 5:5 And Israel's insolence will be humbled before his face, and Israel and Ephraim will weaken in their injustices, and Ioudas too will weaken with them.
Hosea 5:6 With sheep and calves they will go to seek out the Lord and certainly not find him, because he turned away from them,
Hosea 5:7 because they abandoned the Lord, because foreign children were born to them; now mildew will devour them and their allotted portions.
Hosea 5:8 Blow a trumpet upon the hills, sound upon the heights, proclaim in the house of On; Beniamin was astounded,
Hosea 5:9 Ephraim became a desolation in days of reproof; among the tribes of Israel I showed faithful things.
Hosea 5:10 The rulers of Iouda became like those moving boundaries; upon them I will pour my onslaught like water.
Hosea 5:11 Ephraim oppressed his adversary, trampled judgment, because he began to walk after vain things.
Hosea 5:12 And I am like trouble to Ephraim and like a goad to the house of Iouda.
Hosea 5:13 And Ephraim saw his disease, and Ioudas his pain, and Ephraim went to Assyrians and sent ambassadors to King Iarim; and he was unable to heal you, and pain will certainly not cease from you.
Hosea 5:14 Because I am like a panther to Ephraim and like a lion to the house of Iouda; and I seize and will go and take, and there will be no deliverer.
Hosea 5:15 I will go and return to my place until they vanish; and they will seek my face; in their affliction they will rise early toward me, saying,

## Chapter 6

Hosea 6:1 Let us go and return to the Lord our God, because he has seized and will heal us; he will strike and dress our wounds;
Hosea 6:2 he will make us healthy after two days; on the third day we will rise and live before him;
Hosea 6:3 and we will know, we will pursue knowing the Lord; like prepared dawn we will find him, and he will come to us like early and late rain upon the earth. –
Hosea 6:4 What shall I do to you, Ephraim? What shall I do to you, Iouda? But your mercy is like a morning cloud and like departing early dew.
Hosea 6:5 For this reason I reaped your prophets, killed them by the utterances of my mouth, and my judgment will go forth like light.
Hosea 6:6 Because I desire mercy and not sacrifice, and knowledge of God rather than whole burnt offerings.
Hosea 6:7 But they are like a person transgressing a covenant; there he despised me.
Hosea 6:8 Galaad is a city working vain things, troubling water,
Hosea 6:9 and your strength is that of a pirate; priests hid the Lord's way, murdered Sikima, because they did lawlessness.
Hosea 6:10 In the house of Israel I saw horrifying things, there Ephraim's prostitution; Israel and Iouda were defiled.
Hosea 6:11 Begin to gather a vintage for yourself when I turn back the captivity of my people,

## Chapter 7

Hosea 7:1 when I heal Israel. And the injustice of Ephraim and the evil of Samareia will be uncovered, because they worked false things; and a thief will enter toward him, a robber stripping on his way,
Hosea 7:2 so that they may sing together as those singing together with their heart. All their evils I remembered; now their counsels surrounded them; they came before my face.
Hosea 7:3 With their evils they gladdened kings, and with their falsehoods rulers;
Hosea 7:4 all committing adultery, like an oven burning for baking, with a burning heat from the flame, from the kneading of fat until it is leavened.
Hosea 7:5 The days of your kings, the rulers began to become furious from wine; he stretched his hand with pestilent people;
Hosea 7:6 because their hearts were kindled like an oven when they dashed them down; all night Ephraim was filled with sleep; morning came, he was kindled like the glow of fire.
Hosea 7:7 All were heated like an oven and devoured their judges; all their kings fell; there was none among them calling upon me.
Hosea 7:8 Ephraim mingled together among his peoples; Ephraim became a cake not turned.
Hosea 7:9 Strangers devoured his strength, but he did not recognize it; and gray hairs blossomed upon him, and he did not know.
Hosea 7:10 And Israel's insolence will be humbled before his face, and they did not return to the Lord their God or seek him out in all these things.
Hosea 7:11 And Ephraim was like a mindless dove not having a heart; he called upon Egypt, and they went to Assyrians.
Hosea 7:12 As they go, I will throw my net upon them; like the birds of heaven I will bring them down; I will discipline them at the hearing of their affliction.
Hosea 7:13 Woe to them, because they leaped away from me; they are wretched, because they acted impiously against me; but I redeemed them, and they spoke falsehoods against me.
Hosea 7:14 And their hearts did not cry to me, but they wailed upon their beds; over grain and wine they cut themselves. They were disciplined by me,
Hosea 7:15 and I strengthened their arms, and against me they devised evil things.
Hosea 7:16 They turned away to nothing, became like a drawn bow; their rulers will fall by a sword because of their tongue's lack of discipline; this is their contempt in the land of Egypt.

## Chapter 8

Hosea 8:1 Into their bosom like earth, like an eagle upon the Lord's house, because they transgressed my covenant and acted impiously against my law.
Hosea 8:2 They will cry to me, O God, we have known you.
Hosea 8:3 Because Israel turned away good things, they pursued an enemy.
Hosea 8:4 They reigned for themselves and not through me; they ruled and did not make it known to me; their silver and gold they made into idols for themselves, so that they might be destroyed.
Hosea 8:5 Wipe away your calf, Samareia; my fury was provoked against them; how long will they be unable to be cleansed
Hosea 8:6 in Israel? And an artisan made it, and it is not God; because your calf was leading astray, Samareia.
Hosea 8:7 Because they sowed wind-blighted things, and their overthrow will receive them; a sheaf not having strength to make flour; but even if it makes it, strangers will devour it.
Hosea 8:8 Israel was swallowed; now he became among the nations like a useless vessel.
Hosea 8:9 Because they ascended to Assyrians; Ephraim blossomed by himself; they loved gifts;
Hosea 8:10 for this reason they will be handed over among the nations. Now I will receive them, and they will cease a little from anointing a king and rulers.
Hosea 8:11 Because Ephraim multiplied altars, beloved altars became sins for him.
Hosea 8:12 I will record for him a multitude and his ordinances; the beloved altars were reckoned as foreign things.
Hosea 8:13 Because if they sacrifice a sacrifice and eat meat, the Lord will not accept them; now he will remember their injustices and avenge their sins; they returned to Egypt and will eat unclean things among Assyrians.
Hosea 8:14 And Israel forgot him who made him, and they built sacred precincts, and Ioudas multiplied walled cities; and I will send fire into his cities, and it will devour their foundations.

## Chapter 9

Hosea 9:1 Do not rejoice, Israel, or be glad like the peoples; because you prostituted yourself away from your God, you loved gifts upon every threshing floor of grain.
Hosea 9:2 Threshing floor and winepress did not know them, and wine deceived them.
Hosea 9:3 They did not dwell in the Lord's land; Ephraim dwelt in Egypt, and among Assyrians they will eat unclean things.
Hosea 9:4 They did not pour wine to the Lord or please him; their sacrifices are like bread of mourning for them; all eating them will be defiled, because their breads for their souls will not enter the Lord's house.
Hosea 9:5 What will you do on a day of festal assembly and on a day of the Lord's festival?
Hosea 9:6 For this reason behold, they will go out of Egypt's misery, and Memphis will receive them, and Machmas will bury them; destruction will inherit their silver, thorns in their tents.
Hosea 9:7 The days of vengeance have come, the days of your repayment have come, and Israel will be afflicted like the deranged prophet, the spirit-bearing person; by the multitude of your injustices your madness increased.
Hosea 9:8 Ephraim's watcher is with God; a prophet, a crooked snare upon all his ways; they fixed madness in the Lord's house.
Hosea 9:9 They were corrupted as in the days of the hill; he will remember his injustice, avenge his sins.
Hosea 9:10 Like a grape in a desert I found Israel, and like an early lookout in a fig tree I saw their fathers; they entered toward Beelphegor and were estranged unto shame, and the beloved became like the abhorred.
Hosea 9:11 Ephraim flew out like a bird, their glories from births and labor pains and conceptions;
Hosea 9:12 because even if they rear their children, they will be bereaved of human beings; because woe too is theirs, my flesh from them.
Hosea 9:13 Ephraim, as I saw, they presented their children for prey, and Ephraim is to bring out his children for piercing.
Hosea 9:14 Give them, Lord; what will you give them? Give them a childless womb and dry breasts.
Hosea 9:15 All their evils are at Galgal, because there I hated them; because of the evils of their practices I will cast them out of my house; I will certainly no longer continue to love them; all their rulers are disobedient.
Hosea 9:16 Ephraim suffered pain, was dried up in his roots; he will certainly no longer bear fruit; because even if they beget, I will kill the desired things of their belly.
Hosea 9:17 God will reject them, because they did not listen to him, and they will be wanderers among the nations.

## Chapter 10

Hosea 10:1 Israel is a vine with good branches, its fruit flourishing; according to the abundance of his fruits he multiplied altars; according to the good things of his land he built pillars.
Hosea 10:2 They divided their hearts; now they will vanish; he will demolish their altars; their pillars will suffer misery.
Hosea 10:3 Because now they will say, We have no king, because we did not fear the Lord, and what will the king do for us?
Hosea 10:4 Speaking utterances, false pretexts, he will make a covenant; judgment will spring up like couch grass upon a fallow field.
Hosea 10:5 Those dwelling in Samareia will sojourn with the calf of the house of On, because its people mourned over it; and as they embittered it, they will rejoice over its glory, because it was removed from it.
Hosea 10:6 And having bound it they carried it away to Assyrians as gifts for King Iarim; Ephraim will receive in a gift, and Israel will be ashamed in his counsel.
Hosea 10:7 Samareia cast away her king like brushwood upon the face of water.
Hosea 10:8 And the altars of On, the sins of Israel, will be removed; thorns and thistles will grow upon their altars; and they will say to mountains, Cover us, and to hills, Fall upon us.
Hosea 10:9 Since the hills, Israel sinned, there they stood; will war against the children of injustice certainly not overtake them on the hill?
Hosea 10:10 He came to discipline them, and peoples will gather against them when they are disciplined for their two injustices.
Hosea 10:11 Ephraim is a heifer taught to love strife, but I will come upon the most beautiful part of her neck; I will mount Ephraim and pass over Iouda in silence; Iakob will strengthen him.
Hosea 10:12 Sow for yourselves unto righteousness, gather a vintage unto fruit of life, illuminate for yourselves a light of knowledge, seek out the Lord until produce of righteousness comes to you.
Hosea 10:13 Why did you pass over impiety in silence and gather its injustices as a vintage, eat false fruit? Because you hoped in your chariots, in the multitude of your force.
Hosea 10:14 And destruction will arise among your people, and all your walled places will be gone; as ruler Salaman from the house of Ierobaal, in days of war they dashed a mother upon her children.
Hosea 10:15 Thus I will do to you, house of Israel, because of your evils; at dawn they were cast away, the king of Israel was cast away.

## Chapter 11

Hosea 11:1 Because Israel was an infant, and I loved him and called back his children from Egypt.
Hosea 11:2 As I called them back, so they departed from before me; they sacrificed to the Baalim and burned incense to carved things.
Hosea 11:3 And I bound Ephraim's feet together, took him upon my arm, and they did not know that I have healed them.
Hosea 11:4 In human corruption I stretched them with bonds of my love, and I will be to them like a person slapping upon his cheeks; and I will look toward him, I will be able for him.
Hosea 11:5 Ephraim dwelt in Egypt, and Assour himself is his king, because he did not wish to return.
Hosea 11:6 And a sword weakened in his cities and ceased in his hands, and they will eat from their counsels.
Hosea 11:7 And his people is hanging from his dwelling, and God will be furious over his precious things and certainly not exalt him.
Hosea 11:8 How shall I dispose of you, Ephraim? Shall I shield you, Israel? How shall I dispose of you? Shall I make you like Adama and like Seboim? My heart turned within itself; my regret was troubled together.
Hosea 11:9 I will certainly not do according to the wrath of my fury; I will certainly not abandon Ephraim to be erased; because I am God and not a human being; holy among you, and I will not enter a city.
Hosea 11:10 I will walk after the Lord; like a lion he will roar, because he will roar, and children of waters will be astounded.
Hosea 11:11 And they will be astounded like a bird from Egypt and like a dove from the land of Assyrians; and I will restore them to their houses, says the Lord.

## Chapter 12

Hosea 12:1 Ephraim surrounded me with falsehood, and the house of Israel and Iouda with impieties. Now God knew them, and it will be called God's holy people.
Hosea 12:2 But Ephraim is an evil spirit; he pursued scorching heat all day; he multiplied empty and vain things and made a covenant with Assyrians, and oil was traded into Egypt.
Hosea 12:3 And the Lord has a judgment against Iouda, to avenge Iakob according to his ways, and according to his practices he will repay him.
Hosea 12:4 In the womb he took his brother by the heel, and in his labors he prevailed against God
Hosea 12:5 and prevailed with an angel and had strength; they wept and made supplication to me; in the house of On they found me, and there it was spoken to him.
Hosea 12:6 But the Lord God Almighty will be his remembrance.
Hosea 12:7 And you will return by your God; keep mercy and judgment and draw near to your God continually.
Hosea 12:8 Chanaan, in his hand is a balance of injustice; he loved to oppress.
Hosea 12:9 And Ephraim said, Nevertheless I have become rich, I have found refreshment for myself. All his labors will not be found for him because of injustices which he sinned.
Hosea 12:10 But I, the Lord your God, brought you up from the land of Egypt; still I will settle you in tents as on a day of festival.
Hosea 12:11 And I will speak to prophets, and I multiplied visions and was likened by the hands of prophets.
Hosea 12:12 Unless it is Galaad; then the rulers sacrificing in Galgal were false, and their altars are like turtles upon a fallow field.
Hosea 12:13 And Iakob withdrew to the plain of Syria, and Israel served for a wife and guarded for a wife.
Hosea 12:14 And by a prophet the Lord brought Israel up from Egypt, and by a prophet he was preserved.
Hosea 12:15 Ephraim enraged and provoked to wrath, and his blood will be poured upon him, and the Lord will repay him his reproach.

## Chapter 13

Hosea 13:1 According to Ephraim's word he received ordinances in Israel, and he assigned them to Baal and died.
Hosea 13:2 And he continued to sin still, and they made for themselves a molten thing from their silver according to an image of idols, works of artisans completed for them; they say, Sacrifice human beings, for calves have ceased.
Hosea 13:3 For this reason they will be like a morning cloud and like departing early dew, like chaff blown from a threshing floor and like vapor from locusts.
Hosea 13:4 But I am the Lord your God, establishing heaven and creating earth, whose hands created all the host of heaven, and I did not show them to you for you to walk after them; and I brought you up from the land of Egypt, and you will know no God except me, and there is no savior apart from me.
Hosea 13:5 I shepherded you in the desert, in an uninhabited land,
Hosea 13:6 according to their pastures. And they were filled unto fullness, and their hearts were exalted; because of this they forgot me.
Hosea 13:7 And I will be to them like a panther and like a leopard along the way of Assyrians;
Hosea 13:8 I will meet them like a bear in want and tear open the enclosure of their heart, and there cubs of the forest will devour them; beasts of the field will tear them apart.
Hosea 13:9 In your corruption, Israel, who will help?
Hosea 13:10 Where is this king of yours? And let him preserve you in all your cities; let him judge you, he of whom you said, Give me a king and a ruler.
Hosea 13:11 And I gave you a king in my wrath, and in my fury I held
Hosea 13:12 a gathering of injustice. Ephraim, his sin is hidden away.
Hosea 13:13 Labor pains like those of a woman giving birth will come to him; this son of yours is not prudent, because he will certainly not withstand the crushing of children.
Hosea 13:14 From the hand of Hades I will rescue them, and from death I will redeem them; where is your penalty, death? Where is your goad, Hades? Consolation has been hidden from my eyes.
Hosea 13:15 Because this one will distinguish among brothers. The Lord will bring a scorching wind from the desert upon him and dry up his veins, make his springs desolate; he will dry up his land and all his desirable vessels.

## Chapter 14

Hosea 14:1 Samareia will vanish, because she resisted her God; they will fall by a sword, and their sucklings will be dashed upon the ground, and their pregnant women will be torn open.
Hosea 14:2 Return, Israel, to the Lord your God, because you weakened in your injustices.
Hosea 14:3 Take words with yourselves and return to the Lord your God; say to him, so that you may not receive injustice and may receive good things, and we will repay the fruit of our lips.
Hosea 14:4 Assour will certainly not save us; we will not mount a horse; we will certainly no longer say, Our gods, to the works of our hands; he who is in you will have mercy on an orphan.
Hosea 14:5 I will heal their dwellings, love them openly, because my wrath turned away from them.
Hosea 14:6 I will be like dew to Israel; he will blossom like a lily and put forth his roots like Lebanon;
Hosea 14:7 his branches will spread, and he will be like a fruitful olive, and his scent like Lebanon;
Hosea 14:8 they will return and sit beneath his shelter, live and be drenched with grain; and his remembrance will blossom like a vine, like wine of Lebanon.
Hosea 14:9 For Ephraim, what has he still to do with idols? I humbled him, and I will strengthen him; I am like a leafy juniper; from me your fruit has been found.
Hosea 14:10 Who is wise and will understand these things? Or understanding and will know them? Because the Lord's ways are straight, and righteous people will walk in them, but the ungodly will weaken in them.

# Amos

The Apostolic Bible. Public domain. https://apostolic-bible.ysys9.chatgpt.site/license.html


## Chapter 1

Amos 1:1 Words of Amos, which came to be among the nakkarim from Thekoue, which he saw concerning Ierusalem in the days of Ozias king of Iouda and in the days of Ieroboam son of Ioas, king of Israel, two years before the earthquake.
Amos 1:2 And he said: The Lord uttered from Sion and gave his voice from Ierusalem, and the pastures of the shepherds mourned, and the summit of Karmel dried up.
Amos 1:3 And the Lord said: For the three impieties of Damascus and for the four I will not turn him away, because they were sawing with iron saws the pregnant women among those in Galaad;
Amos 1:4 and I will send out fire into the house of Azael, and it will devour the foundations of the son of Ader;
Amos 1:5 and I will shatter the bars of Damascus and destroy inhabitants from the plain of On, and cut down a tribe from the men of Charran, and the people of Syria called by name will be taken captive, says the Lord.
Amos 1:6 Thus says the Lord: For the three impieties of Gaza and for the four I will not turn them away, because they took captive the captivity of Salomon to shut it up into Idoumaia;
Amos 1:7 and I will send out fire upon the walls of Gaza, and it will devour her foundations;
Amos 1:8 and I will destroy inhabitants from Azotos, and a tribe will be removed from Askalon, and I will bring my hand upon Akkaron, and the remaining ones of the foreigners will perish, says the Lord.
Amos 1:9 Thus says the Lord: For the three impieties of Tyre and for the four I will not turn her away, because they shut up the captivity of Salomon into Idoumaia and did not remember a covenant of brothers;
Amos 1:10 and I will send out fire upon the walls of Tyre, and it will devour her foundations.
Amos 1:11 Thus says the Lord: For the three impieties of Idoumaia and for the four I will not turn them away, because they pursued his brother with a sword, and he ravaged a womb upon the earth, and seized his shuddering for a testimony, and kept his impulse for strife;
Amos 1:12 and I will send out fire into Thaiman, and it will devour the foundations of her walls.
Amos 1:13 Thus says the Lord: For the three impieties of the sons of Ammon and for the four I will not turn him away, because they ripped open the pregnant women of the Galaadites, so that they might widen their boundaries;
Amos 1:14 and I will kindle fire upon the walls of Rabba, and it will devour her foundations with shouting on a day of war, and she will be shaken on the day of her consummation;
Amos 1:15 and her kings will go into captivity, their priests and their rulers together, says the Lord.

## Chapter 2

Amos 2:1 Thus says the Lord: For the three impieties of Moab and for the four I will not turn him away, because they burned the bones of the king of Idoumaia into lime;
Amos 2:2 and I will send out fire upon Moab, and it will devour the foundations of her cities, and Moab will die in weakness, with shouting and with the sound of a trumpet;
Amos 2:3 and I will destroy a judge from her, and I will kill all her rulers with him, says the Lord.
Amos 2:4 Thus says the Lord: For the three impieties of the sons of Iouda and for the four I will not turn him away, because they rejected the law of the Lord and did not keep his ordinances, and their vain things which they made led them astray, after which their fathers followed;
Amos 2:5 and I will send out fire upon Iouda, and it will devour the foundations of Ierusalem.
Amos 2:6 Thus says the Lord: For the three impieties of Israel and for the four I will not turn him away, because they sold a righteous one for silver and a needy one for the sake of sandals,
Amos 2:7 which tread upon the dust of the earth, and they struck the heads of the poor with their fists and turned aside the way of the lowly, and a son and his father were going in to the same girl, so that they might profane the name of their God,
Amos 2:8 and, binding their garments with cords, they made curtains adjoining the altar, and they drank wine from extortions in the house of their God.
Amos 2:9 But I removed the Amorrite from before them, whose height was like the height of a cedar, and he was strong as an oak, and I removed his fruit from above and his roots from below;
Amos 2:10 and I brought you up from the land of Egypt and led you about in the wilderness forty years, to inherit the land of the Amorrites;
Amos 2:11 and I took from your sons for prophets and from your young men for sanctification. Are these things not so, sons of Israel? says the Lord.
Amos 2:12 And you were giving the sanctified ones wine to drink, and commanding the prophets, saying: You shall certainly not prophesy.
Amos 2:13 Therefore, behold, I roll beneath you, as the wagon full of straw rolls;
Amos 2:14 and escape will perish from a runner, and the strong one will certainly not retain his strength, and the warrior will certainly not save his soul,
Amos 2:15 and the archer will certainly not stand firm, and the one swift on his feet will certainly not be saved, nor will the horseman save his soul,
Amos 2:16 and he will find his heart in mighty deeds; the naked one will pursue on that day, says the Lord.

## Chapter 3

Amos 3:1 Hear this word which the Lord spoke against you, house of Israel, and against every tribe which I brought up from the land of Egypt, saying:
Amos 3:2 Only you have I known out of all the tribes of the earth; therefore I will punish all your sins upon you.
Amos 3:3 Will two go together at all unless they make themselves known?
Amos 3:4 Will a lion roar from his thicket without having prey? Will a young lion give his voice from his enclosure at all unless he seizes something?
