Amos 3:5 Will a bird fall upon the earth without a birdcatcher? Will a snare be sprung upon the earth without catching something?
Amos 3:6 Will a trumpet sound in a city and the people not be terrified? Will there be evil in a city which the Lord has not done?
Amos 3:7 For the Lord God will certainly not do a thing unless he reveals his discipline to his servants the prophets.
Amos 3:8 A lion will roar, and who will not fear? The Lord God has spoken, and who will not prophesy?
Amos 3:9 Report to regions among the Assyrians and to the regions of Egypt, and say: Gather upon the mountain of Samareia, and see many astonishing things in her midst and the oppression in her;
Amos 3:10 and he did not know what will be against her, says the Lord, those treasuring injustice and misery in their regions.
Amos 3:11 Therefore thus says the Lord God: Tyre, your land will be laid waste round about, and he will bring down your strength from you, and your regions will be plundered.
Amos 3:12 Thus says the Lord: As when the shepherd pulls two legs or a lobe of an ear from the mouth of the lion, so will the sons of Israel be pulled out, those dwelling in Samareia opposite a tribe, and priests in Damascus.
Amos 3:13 Hear and bear witness to the house of Iakob, says the Lord God the Almighty,
Amos 3:14 for on the day when I punish the impieties of Israel upon him, I will also punish the altars of Baithel, and the horns of the altar will be torn down and fall upon the earth;
Amos 3:15 I will demolish and strike the house surrounded by columns upon the summer house, and ivory houses will perish, and many other houses will be added, says the Lord.

## Chapter 4

Amos 4:1 Hear this word, heifers of Basanitis who are on the mountain of Samareia, who oppress the poor and trample the needy, who say to their lords: Give to us so that we may drink;
Amos 4:2 The Lord swears by his holy things: For behold, days are coming upon you, and they will take you with weapons, and fiery plagues will cast those with you into cauldrons heated from beneath,
Amos 4:3 and you will be carried out naked, opposite one another, and cast away onto the mountain Remman, says the Lord God.
Amos 4:4 You entered Baithel and acted lawlessly, and in Galgala you multiplied impiety, and brought your sacrifices in the morning, your tithes on the third day;
Amos 4:5 and they read a law outside and called for pledges; report that the sons of Israel loved these things, says the Lord God.
Amos 4:6 And I will give you aching teeth in all your cities and lack of bread in all your places; and you did not return to me, says the Lord.
Amos 4:7 And I withheld the rain from you three months before the harvest; and I will rain upon one city, but upon one city I will not rain; one portion will be rained upon, and a portion upon which I will not rain will dry up;
Amos 4:8 and two and three cities will gather into one city to drink water and will certainly not be filled; and you did not return to me, says the Lord.
Amos 4:9 I struck you with scorching and with jaundice; you multiplied your gardens; the caterpillar devoured your vineyards and your fig orchards and your olive groves; and not even thus did you return to me, says the Lord.
Amos 4:10 I sent out death among you on the way of Egypt, and killed your young men with a sword, along with the captivity of your horses, and brought up your camps in fire in my wrath; and not even thus did you return to me, says the Lord.
Amos 4:11 I overturned you, as God overturned Sodoma and Gomorra, and you became like a firebrand pulled out of fire; and not even thus did you return to me, says the Lord.
Amos 4:12 Therefore I will do thus to you, Israel; nevertheless, because I will do thus to you, prepare to call upon your God, Israel.
Amos 4:13 For behold, I am the one establishing thunder and creating spirit and announcing his anointed one to men, making dawn and mist and stepping upon the heights of the earth; the Lord God the Almighty is his name.

## Chapter 5

Amos 5:1 Hear this word of the Lord, which I take up as a lament against you, house of Israel:
Amos 5:2 The virgin of Israel has fallen; she will certainly no longer rise again; she stumbled upon her land; there is no one who will raise her.
Amos 5:3 For thus says the Lord Lord: The city from which a thousand were going out will have a hundred left, and that from which a hundred were going out will have ten left for the house of Israel.
Amos 5:4 For thus says the Lord to the house of Israel: Seek me out and you will live;
Amos 5:5 and do not seek out Baithel, and do not enter Galgala, and do not cross over to the well of the oath, because Galgala, being taken captive, will be taken captive, and Baithel will be as though not existing;
Amos 5:6 seek out the Lord and live, so that the house of Ioseph may not blaze up like fire, and it will devour him, and there will be no one to quench it for the house of Israel.
Amos 5:7 The Lord, who makes judgment on high, and he placed righteousness upon the earth,
Amos 5:8 making all things and refashioning them and turning the shadow of death into morning and darkening day into night, who summons the water of the sea and pours it out upon the face of the earth; the Lord God the Almighty is his name;
Amos 5:9 who apportions crushing upon strength and brings misery upon a stronghold.
Amos 5:10 They hated one reproving in the gates and abhorred a holy word.
Amos 5:11 Therefore, because you were striking the poor with your fists and received choice gifts from them, you built houses of dressed stone and will certainly not dwell in them; you planted desirable vineyards and will certainly not drink the wine from them.
Amos 5:12 For I knew your many impieties, and your sins are mighty, trampling a righteous one, taking payments and turning aside the needy in the gates.
Amos 5:13 Therefore the one who understands will be silent at that time, because it is an evil time.
Amos 5:14 Seek out the good and not the evil, so that you may live; and thus the Lord God the Almighty will be with you, as you said:
Amos 5:15 We have hated evil things and loved good things; and restore judgment in the gates, so that the Lord God the Almighty may have mercy on the remaining ones of Ioseph.
Amos 5:16 Therefore thus says the Lord God the Almighty: In all squares, beating of the breast, and in all streets it will be said: Woe, woe; a farmer will be called to mourning and beating of the breast, and to those who know lamentation,
Amos 5:17 and in all streets, beating of the breast, because I will pass through your midst, said the Lord.
Amos 5:18 Woe to those desiring the day of the Lord; why is this day of the Lord for you? And it is darkness and not light,
Amos 5:19 as when a man flees from before the lion and the bear encounters him, and he leaps into his house and rests his hands against the wall, and the serpent bites him.
Amos 5:20 Is not the day of the Lord darkness and not light? And gloom, having no brightness in it.
Amos 5:21 I have hated, I have rejected your feasts, and I will certainly not smell at your assemblies;
Amos 5:22 for even if you bring me whole burnt offerings and your sacrifices, I will not accept them, and I will not look upon your splendid offerings of salvation.
Amos 5:23 Remove from me the sound of your songs, and I will not hear the music of your instruments;
Amos 5:24 and judgment will roll like water, and righteousness like an impassable torrent.
Amos 5:25 Did you offer me slaughtered offerings and sacrifices in the wilderness forty years, house of Israel?
Amos 5:26 And you took up the tent of Moloch and the star of your god Raiphan, their figures which you made for yourselves.
Amos 5:27 And I will resettle you beyond Damascus, says the Lord; God the Almighty is his name.

## Chapter 6

Amos 6:1 Woe to those despising Sion and those trusting in the mountain of Samareia; they harvested the firstfruits of nations, and they entered. House of Israel,
Amos 6:2 cross over, all of you, and see, and pass from there into Emath Rabba, and go down from there into Geth of the foreigners, the strongest of all these kingdoms, whether their boundaries are greater than your boundaries.
Amos 6:3 Those coming to an evil day, those approaching and laying hold of false sabbaths,
Amos 6:4 those sleeping upon ivory beds and living luxuriously upon their couches, and eating kids from flocks and suckling calves from the midst of herds,
Amos 6:5 those clapping to the sound of the instruments reckoned them as standing and not as fleeing;
Amos 6:6 those drinking the filtered wine and anointing themselves with the foremost perfumes, and they suffered nothing over the crushing of Ioseph.
Amos 6:7 Therefore now they will be captives from the foremost of the potentates, and the neighing of horses will be removed from Ephraim.
Amos 6:8 For the Lord swore by himself: For I abhor all the arrogance of Iakob and have hated his regions, and I will remove a city together with all who dwell in it;
Amos 6:9 and it will be, if ten men are left in one house, they too will die, and the remaining ones will be left,
Amos 6:10 and their relatives will take them and force themselves to carry their bones out of the house; and he will say to those in charge of the house: Is there still anyone with you? And he will say: No longer; and he will say: Be silent, so as not to name the name of the Lord.
Amos 6:11 For behold, the Lord commands, and he will strike the great house with crushings and the small house with fissures.
Amos 6:12 Will horses pursue on rocks? Will they keep silent among mares? For you turned judgment into wrath and the fruit of righteousness into bitterness,
Amos 6:13 those rejoicing over no matter, those saying: Did we not acquire horns by our strength?
Amos 6:14 For behold, I raise up a nation against you, house of Israel, and they will press you out so that you do not enter Emath, and as far as the torrent of the west.

## Chapter 7

Amos 7:1 Thus the Lord showed me, and behold, a brood of locusts coming in the morning, and behold, one locust, Gog the king.
Amos 7:2 And it will be, if it finishes devouring the grass of the earth, and I said: Lord Lord, be gracious; who will raise Iakob? For he is very small;
Amos 7:3 change your mind, Lord, over this. And this will not be, says the Lord.
Amos 7:4 Thus the Lord showed me, and behold, the Lord called for punishment by fire, and it devoured the great abyss and devoured the portion.
Amos 7:5 And I said: Lord Lord, cease now; who will raise Iakob? For he is very small;
Amos 7:6 change your mind, Lord, over this. And this will certainly not happen, says the Lord.
Amos 7:7 Thus the Lord showed me, and behold, a man standing upon an adamantine wall, and adamant in his hand.
Amos 7:8 And the Lord said to me: What do you see, Amos? And I said: Adamant. And the Lord said to me: Behold, I place adamant in the midst of my people Israel; I will certainly no longer pass him by;
Amos 7:9 and altars of laughter will disappear, and the rites of Israel will be laid waste, and I will rise against the house of Ieroboam with a sword.
Amos 7:10 And Amasias the priest of Baithel sent to Ieroboam king of Israel, saying: Amos is making conspiracies against you in the midst of the house of Israel; the land will certainly not be able to endure all his words;
Amos 7:11 for thus says Amos: Ieroboam will die by a sword, but Israel will be led captive from his land.
Amos 7:12 And Amasias said to Amos: Seer, go, withdraw into the land of Iouda, and live there, and there you will prophesy;
Amos 7:13 but in Baithel you shall certainly no longer prophesy, because it is a king's sanctuary and a house of a kingdom.
Amos 7:14 And Amos answered and said to Amasias: I was not a prophet, nor a prophet's son, but I was a goatherd and one scratching mulberries;
Amos 7:15 and the Lord took me up from the sheep, and the Lord said to me: Go, prophesy against my people Israel.
Amos 7:16 And now hear a word of the Lord: You say: Do not prophesy against Israel, and you shall certainly not address a crowd against the house of Iakob;
Amos 7:17 therefore thus says the Lord: Your wife will prostitute herself in the city, and your sons and your daughters will fall by a sword, and your land will be measured out with a cord, and you will die in an unclean land, but Israel will be led captive from his land.

## Chapter 8

Amos 8:1 Thus the Lord showed me, and behold, a birdcatcher's vessel.
Amos 8:2 And he said: What do you see, Amos? And I said: A birdcatcher's vessel. And the Lord said to me: The end has come upon my people Israel; I will certainly no longer pass him by;
Amos 8:3 and the panels of the temple will howl; on that day, says the Lord, many are the fallen in every place; I will cast silence upon them.
Amos 8:4 Hear now these things, those wearing down a needy one in the morning and oppressing the poor from the earth,
Amos 8:5 those saying: When will the month pass and we trade, and the sabbaths, and we open storehouses, to make a measure small and enlarge weights and make an unjust balance,
Amos 8:6 to acquire the poor with silver and a lowly one in exchange for sandals, and we will trade from every kind of produce?

Amos 8:8 And over these things will the earth not be troubled? And everyone dwelling in it will mourn, and consummation will rise like a river and go down like the river of Egypt.
Amos 8:9 And it will be on that day, says the Lord God, that the sun will set at noon, and the light will grow dark upon the earth in daytime;
Amos 8:10 and I will turn your feasts into mourning and all your songs into lamentation, and I will bring sackcloth upon every waist and baldness upon every head, and I will make him like mourning for a beloved one and those with him like a day of anguish.
Amos 8:11 Behold, days are coming, says the Lord, and I will send out famine upon the earth, not a famine of bread nor a thirst for water, but a famine of hearing a word of the Lord;
Amos 8:12 and waters will be shaken as far as the sea, and from the north as far as the east they will run about seeking the word of the Lord and will certainly not find it.
Amos 8:13 On that day the beautiful virgins and the young men will fail with thirst,
Amos 8:14 those swearing by the atonement of Samareia and those saying: Your god lives, Dan, and your god lives, Bersabee; and they will fall and certainly no longer rise.

## Chapter 9

Amos 9:1 I saw the Lord standing over the altar, and he said: Strike upon the mercy seat, and the gateways will be shaken, and cut through onto the heads of all; and I will kill their remaining ones with a sword; no fleeing one among them will escape, and no one among them saving himself will be saved.
Amos 9:2 If they dig down into Hades, from there my hand will pull them up; and if they go up into heaven, from there I will bring them down;
Amos 9:3 if they hide in the summit of Karmel, from there I will search out and take them; and if they sink from my eyes into the depths of the sea, there I will command the dragon, and it will bite them;
Amos 9:4 and if they go into captivity before their enemies, there I will command the sword, and it will kill them; and I will fix my eyes upon them for evil things and not for good things.
Amos 9:5 And the Lord Lord God the Almighty, who touches the earth and shakes it, and all who dwell in it will mourn, and its consummation will rise like a river and go down like the river of Egypt;
Amos 9:6 who builds his ascent into heaven and establishes his promise upon the earth, who summons the water of the sea and pours it out upon the face of the earth; the Lord God the Almighty is his name.
Amos 9:7 Are you not like sons of Ethiopians to me, sons of Israel? says the Lord. Did I not bring Israel up from the land of Egypt, and the foreigners from Kappadokia, and the Syrians from a pit?
Amos 9:8 Behold, the eyes of the Lord God are upon the kingdom of the sinners, and I will remove it from the face of the earth; nevertheless, I will not completely remove the house of Iakob, says the Lord.
Amos 9:9 For behold, I command, and I will winnow the house of Israel among all the nations, as it is winnowed in the winnowing basket, and a fragment will certainly not fall upon the earth.
Amos 9:10 All sinners of my people will die by a sword, those saying: The evil things will certainly not approach or come upon us.
Amos 9:11 On that day I will raise the fallen tent of David and rebuild its fallen parts, and raise its demolished parts and rebuild it as in the days of the age,
Amos 9:12 so that the remaining ones of men and all the nations upon whom my name has been called may seek out, says the Lord God who does these things.
Amos 9:13 Behold, days are coming, says the Lord, and the threshing will overtake the grape harvest, and the grape will ripen at the sowing, and the mountains will drip sweetness, and all the hills will be grown together;
Amos 9:14 and I will turn back the captivity of my people Israel, and they will build the cities that have disappeared and dwell in them, and plant vineyards and drink their wine, and plant gardens and eat their fruit;
Amos 9:15 and I will plant them upon their land, and they will certainly no longer be pulled out from their land which I gave them, says the Lord God the Almighty.

# Micah

## Chapter 1

Micah 1:1 And a word of the Lord came to Michaias of Morasthi in the days of Ioatham and Achaz and Ezekias, kings of Iouda, concerning what he saw about Samareia and about Ierusalem.
Micah 1:2 Hear words, peoples, and let the earth and all who are in it pay attention, and the Lord will be among you for a testimony, the Lord from his holy house;
Micah 1:3 for behold, the Lord goes out from his place, and he will descend and step upon the heights of the earth,
Micah 1:4 and the mountains will be shaken beneath him, and the valleys will melt like wax before fire and like water carried down a descent.
Micah 1:5 All these things are because of the impiety of Iakob and because of the sin of the house of Israel. What is the impiety of Iakob? Is it not Samareia? And what is the sin of the house of Iouda? Is it not Ierusalem?
Micah 1:6 And I will make Samareia a fruit watchman's hut in a field and a planting of a vineyard, and I will pull her stones down into a chasm and uncover her foundations;
Micah 1:7 and they will cut down all her carved images and burn all her wages with fire, and I will consign all her idols to disappearance; for she gathered from wages of prostitution and amassed from wages of prostitution.
Micah 1:8 Because of this she will beat her breast and lament; she will go barefoot and naked; she will make a beating of the breast like that of dragons and mourning like that of daughters of sirens;
Micah 1:9 for her wound has prevailed, because it came as far as Iouda and reached as far as the gate of my people, as far as Ierusalem.
Micah 1:10 Those in Geth, do not magnify yourselves; those in Akim, do not rebuild from a house for laughter; sprinkle earth upon yourselves for your laughter.
Micah 1:11 Dwelling well in her cities, the one dwelling in Sennaan did not go out to mourn a house adjoining her; she will receive from you a wound of anguish.
Micah 1:12 Who began good things for her who dwells in pains? For evil things came down from the Lord upon the gates of Ierusalem,
Micah 1:13 a sound of chariots and horsemen. She who dwells in Lachis is the originator of sin for the daughter of Sion, because the impieties of Israel were found in you.
Micah 1:14 Therefore you will give those being sent away, as far as the inheritance of Geth, vain houses; it became empty things for the kings of Israel.
Micah 1:15 Until I bring the heirs to you, inheritance dwelling in Lachis, the glory of the daughter of Israel will come as far as Odollam.
Micah 1:16 Shave yourself and shear yourself over your delicate children; widen your widowhood like an eagle, because they were taken captive from you.

## Chapter 2

Micah 2:1 They became those devising troubles and working evil things in their beds, and at daybreak they accomplished them, because they did not lift their hands to God;
Micah 2:2 and they were desiring fields and plundering orphans and oppressing houses, and plundering a man and his house, a man and his inheritance.
Micah 2:3 Therefore thus says the Lord: Behold, I devise evil things against this tribe, from which you will certainly not lift your necks, and you will certainly not suddenly walk upright, because it is an evil time.
Micah 2:4 On that day a parable will be taken up against you, and a lament will be lamented in song, saying: With misery we have been made miserable; the portion of my people was measured out with a cord, and there was no one to prevent him from turning it away; our fields were divided.
Micah 2:5 Therefore you will have no one casting a cord by lot in the assembly of the Lord.
Micah 2:6 Do not weep with tears, nor let them shed tears over these things; for he will not put away reproaches.
Micah 2:7 The one saying: The house of Iakob provoked the spirit of the Lord to anger; are these his practices? Are not his words good with him, and have they not proceeded upright?
Micah 2:8 And formerly my people stood against him in enmity; against his peace they flayed his skin, to take away hope, a crushing of war.
Micah 2:9 Therefore the leaders of my people will be cast out of their houses of luxury; because of their evil practices they were thrust out; approach everlasting mountains.
Micah 2:10 Rise and go, because this is not your rest on account of uncleanness. You were destroyed with destruction,
Micah 2:11 you were pursued with no one pursuing; a spirit established a lie; it dripped for you into wine and intoxicating drink. And it will be from the drop of this people:
Micah 2:12 being gathered, Iakob will be gathered with all; awaiting, I will await the remaining ones of Israel; I will place their return together; like sheep in affliction, like a flock in the midst of their resting place, they will leap out from men.
Micah 2:13 Through the breach before them they broke through and passed through a gate and went out through it, and their king went out before them, but the Lord will lead them.

## Chapter 3

Micah 3:1 And he will say: Hear now these things, the rulers of the house of Iakob and the remaining ones of the house of Israel. Is it not yours to know judgment?
Micah 3:2 Those hating good things and seeking evil things, seizing their skins from them and their flesh from their bones.
Micah 3:3 As they devoured the flesh of my people and flayed their skins from their bones, and crushed their bones and cut them into pieces like flesh for a cauldron and like meat for a pot,
Micah 3:4 so they will cry to the Lord, and he will not hear them; and he will turn his face from them at that time, because they acted wickedly in their practices against them.
Micah 3:5 Thus says the Lord against the prophets who lead my people astray, who bite with their teeth and proclaim peace over him, and nothing was given into their mouth, they raised war against him;
Micah 3:6 therefore night will be yours instead of vision, and darkness will be yours instead of divination, and the sun will set upon the prophets, and the day will grow dark upon them;
Micah 3:7 and those seeing dreams will be put to shame, and the diviners will be laughed at, and all of them will speak against them, because there will be no one hearing them.
Micah 3:8 Unless I fill up strength in the spirit of the Lord and of judgment and of power, to announce to Iakob his impieties and to Israel his sins.
Micah 3:9 Hear now these things, the leaders of the house of Iakob and the remaining ones of the house of Israel, who abhor judgment and distort all upright things,
Micah 3:10 who build Sion with bloodshed and Ierusalem with injustices;
Micah 3:11 her leaders judged with gifts, and her priests answered with payment, and her prophets divined with silver, and they rested upon the Lord, saying: Is not the Lord among us? Evil things will certainly not come upon us.
Micah 3:12 Therefore, because of you, Sion will be plowed like a field, and Ierusalem will be like a fruit watchman's hut, and the mountain of the house like a grove of a thicket.

## Chapter 4

Micah 4:1 And in the last days the mountain of the Lord will be manifest, ready upon the summits of the mountains, and it will be raised above the hills; and peoples will hasten to it,
Micah 4:2 and many nations will go and say: Come, let us go up to the mountain of the Lord and to the house of the God of Iakob, and they will show us his way, and we will walk in his paths; for a law will go out from Sion, and a word of the Lord from Ierusalem.
Micah 4:3 And he will judge between many peoples and reprove strong nations as far as a distant land, and they will cut down their swords into plows and their spears into sickles, and nation will certainly no longer raise a sword against nation, and they will certainly no longer learn to wage war.
Micah 4:4 And each will rest beneath his vine and each beneath his fig tree, and there will be no one frightening them, because the mouth of the Lord Almighty spoke these things.
Micah 4:5 For all the peoples will go, each his own way, but we will go in the name of the Lord our God into the age and beyond.
Micah 4:6 On that day, says the Lord, I will gather her who has been crushed, and receive her who has been thrust out and those whom I rejected;
Micah 4:7 and I will make her who has been crushed a remnant, and her who has been rejected a strong nation, and the Lord will reign over them on mount Sion from now and into the age.
Micah 4:8 And you, parched tower of a flock, daughter of Sion, to you will come and enter the first dominion, a kingdom from Babylon for the daughter of Ierusalem.
Micah 4:9 And now, why did you know evil things? Did you not have a king? Or did your counsel perish, that birth pangs seized you like one giving birth?
Micah 4:10 Be in labor and be courageous and draw near, daughter of Sion, like one giving birth; for now you will go out from a city and encamp in a plain and come as far as Babylon; from there he will rescue you, and from there the Lord your God will redeem you from the hand of your enemies.
Micah 4:11 And now many nations gathered against you, those saying: We will rejoice over her, and our eyes will look upon Sion.
Micah 4:12 But they did not know the thought of the Lord and did not understand his counsel, that he gathered them like sheaves of a threshing floor.
Micah 4:13 Rise and thresh them, daughter of Sion, for I will make your horns iron and your hooves bronze, and with them you will melt down nations and grind many peoples fine, and you will dedicate their multitude to the Lord and their strength to the Lord of all the earth.
Micah 4:14 Now the daughter of Ephraim will be shut in with a barrier; he appointed confinement against us; with a rod they will strike the tribes of Israel upon the cheek.

## Chapter 5

Micah 5:1 And you, Bethlehem, house of Ephratha, are very small to be among the thousands of Iouda; from you one will go out for me to be a ruler in Israel, and his goings out are from the beginning, from days of an age.

Micah 5:3 And he will stand and see and shepherd his flock in the strength of the Lord, and they will exist in the glory of the name of the Lord their God; for now he will be magnified as far as the ends of the earth.
Micah 5:4 And this will be peace; when an Assyrian comes upon your land and when he steps upon your region, seven shepherds and eight bites of men will be raised against him;
Micah 5:5 and they will shepherd Assour with a sword and the land of Nebrod in its trench; and he will rescue from Assour when he comes upon your land and when he steps upon your boundaries.
Micah 5:6 And the remnant of Iakob will be among the nations in the midst of many peoples like dew falling from the Lord and like lambs upon grass, so that no one may be gathered or stand among sons of men.
Micah 5:7 And the remnant of Iakob will be among the nations in the midst of many peoples like a lion among beasts in the thicket and like a young lion among flocks of sheep, as when he passes through and, separating, seizes, and there is no one rescuing.

## Chapter 6

Micah 6:2 Hear, hills, the judgment of the Lord, and you ravines, foundations of the earth, for the Lord has a case against his people, and he will dispute with Israel.
Micah 6:3 My people, what did I do to you, or how did I grieve you, or how did I trouble you? Answer me.
Micah 6:4 For I brought you up from the land of Egypt and redeemed you from a house of slavery, and sent out before you Moyses and Aaron and Mariam.
Micah 6:5 My people, remember now what Balak king of Moab planned against you, and what Balaam son of Beor answered him, from the rushes as far as Galgal, so that the righteousness of the Lord may be known.
Micah 6:6 With what shall I reach the Lord, shall I take hold of my God Most High? Shall I reach him with whole burnt offerings, with year-old calves?
Micah 6:7 Will the Lord accept with thousands of rams or with myriads of fat torrents? Shall I give my firstborn for impiety, the fruit of my womb for the sin of my soul?
Micah 6:8 Was it announced to you, man, what is good? Or what does the Lord seek from you except to do judgment and love mercy and be ready to walk with the Lord your God?
Micah 6:9 A voice of the Lord will be called to the city, and he will save those fearing his name. Hear, tribe, and who will adorn a city?
Micah 6:10 Is there not fire and a house of a lawless one treasuring lawless treasures, and injustice with arrogance?
Micah 6:11 Will a lawless one be justified with a balance, and weights of deceit in a purse?
Micah 6:12 From which they filled their wealth with impiety, and those dwelling in it were speaking false things, and their tongue was raised in their mouth.
Micah 6:13 And I will begin to strike you; I will make you disappear on account of your sins.
Micah 6:14 You will eat and certainly not be filled; and it will grow dark within you and turn aside, and you will certainly not be saved; and as many as are saved will be handed over to a sword.
Micah 6:15 You will sow and certainly not reap; you will press olives and certainly not anoint with oil, and wine, and you will certainly not drink, and the ordinances of my people will disappear.
Micah 6:16 And you kept the statutes of Zambri and all the works of the house of Achaab, and you walked in their counsels, so that I may hand you over to disappearance and those dwelling in it to hissing; and you will receive reproaches of peoples.

## Chapter 7

Micah 7:1 Alas for me, for I became like one gathering straw at harvest and like a grape gleaning at vintage, with no cluster existing to eat the first fruits. Alas, soul,

# Joel

The Apostolic Bible. Public domain. https://apostolic-bible.ysys9.chatgpt.site/license.html


## Chapter 1

Joel 1:1 A word of the Lord, which came to Ioel son of Bathouel.
Joel 1:2 Hear now these things, elders, and give ear, all who dwell in the land. Have such things happened in your days or in the days of your fathers?
Joel 1:3 Tell your children about them, and your children their children, and their children another generation.
Joel 1:4 The locust devoured what remained of the caterpillar, and the locust grub devoured what remained of the locust, and the mildew devoured what remained of the locust grub.
Joel 1:5 Sober up from their wine, you who are drunk, and weep; lament, all who drink wine to drunkenness, because gladness and joy have been removed from your mouth.
Joel 1:6 For a nation came up upon my land, strong and innumerable; its teeth are a lion's teeth, and its molars those of a young lion;
Joel 1:7 it consigned my vine to disappearance and my fig trees to breaking; searching, it searched her out and cast her away; it whitened her branches.
Joel 1:8 Lament to me more than a bride girded with sackcloth over the husband of her virginity.
Joel 1:9 Sacrifice and libation have been removed from the house of the Lord. Mourn, priests who minister at the altar,
Joel 1:10 for the plains have suffered misery; let the earth mourn, for grain has suffered misery, wine dried up, oil diminished.
Joel 1:11 The farmers dried up; lament, estates, over wheat and barley, because the harvest has perished from the field;
Joel 1:12 the vine dried up, and the fig trees diminished; pomegranate and palm and apple tree and all the trees of the field dried up, because the sons of men put joy to shame.
Joel 1:13 Gird yourselves and beat your breasts, priests; lament, those ministering at the altar; enter, sleep in sackcloth, those ministering to God, because sacrifice and libation have withdrawn from the house of your God.
Joel 1:14 Sanctify a fast, proclaim a service, gather elders, all who dwell in the land, into the house of your God, and cry earnestly to the Lord:
Joel 1:15 Alas, alas, alas for the day, because the day of the Lord is near, and it will come like misery out of misery.
Joel 1:16 Before your eyes food was destroyed, gladness and joy from the house of your God.
Joel 1:17 Heifers leaped at their mangers; storehouses disappeared; winepresses were torn down, because grain dried up.
Joel 1:18 What shall we store up for ourselves? Herds of cattle wept because there was no pasture for them, and the flocks of sheep disappeared.
Joel 1:19 To you, Lord, I will cry, because fire consumed the beautiful things of the wilderness, and a flame kindled all the trees of the field;
Joel 1:20 and the beasts of the plain looked up to you, because outlets of waters dried up, and fire devoured the beautiful things of the wilderness.

## Chapter 2

Joel 2:1 Sound a trumpet in Sion, proclaim on my holy mountain, and let all who dwell in the land be confounded, because the day of the Lord is present, because it is near,
Joel 2:2 a day of darkness and gloom, a day of cloud and mist. Like dawn, a numerous and strong people will be poured upon the mountains; its like has not come to be from the age, and after it none will be added for years into generations of generations.
Joel 2:3 Before it, a consuming fire, and behind it, a kindled flame; the land before it is like a paradise of delight, and behind it a plain of disappearance, and it will have no survivor.
Joel 2:4 Their appearance is like the sight of horses, and like horsemen, so they will pursue;
Joel 2:5 like the sound of chariots they will leap upon the summits of the mountains, and like the sound of a flame of fire devouring straw, and like a numerous and strong people drawn up for war.
Joel 2:6 Before it peoples will be crushed; every face is like the scorching of a pot.
Joel 2:7 Like fighters they will run, and like warrior men they will climb upon the walls, and each will go in his way, and they will certainly not turn aside their paths,
Joel 2:8 and each will not keep away from his brother; weighed down with their weapons, they will go and fall among their missiles and certainly not be brought to an end.
Joel 2:9 They will take hold of the city and run upon the walls and climb upon the houses and enter through windows like thieves.
Joel 2:10 Before them the earth will be confounded and heaven shaken; the sun and the moon will grow dark, and the stars will cause their brightness to set.
Joel 2:11 And the Lord will give his voice before his force, because his camp is exceedingly numerous, because the works of his words are strong; for the day of the Lord is great, great and exceedingly manifest, and who will be sufficient for it?
Joel 2:12 And now the Lord your God says: Return to me with your whole heart and with fasting and with weeping and with beating of the breast;
Joel 2:13 and tear your hearts and not your garments, and return to the Lord your God, because he is merciful and compassionate, long-suffering and abundant in mercy, and changes his mind over evil things.
Joel 2:14 Who knows whether he will turn and change his mind and leave behind him a blessing, a sacrifice and a libation to the Lord our God?
Joel 2:15 Sound a trumpet in Sion, sanctify a fast, proclaim a service,
Joel 2:16 gather a people, sanctify an assembly, choose elders, gather infants sucking breasts; let a bridegroom go out from his bedroom and a bride from her bridal chamber.
Joel 2:17 In the midst of the base of the altar the priests ministering to the Lord will weep and say: Spare, Lord, your people, and do not give your inheritance to reproach, for nations to rule them, so that they may not say among the nations: Where is their God?
Joel 2:18 And the Lord was zealous for his land and spared his people.
Joel 2:19 And the Lord answered and said to his people: Behold, I send out to you grain and wine and oil, and you will be filled with them, and I will no longer give you to reproach among the nations;
Joel 2:20 and I will drive away from you the one from the north, and thrust him into a waterless land, and make his front disappear into the first sea and his rear into the last sea; and his decay will rise, and his stench will rise, because he magnified his works.
Joel 2:21 Take courage, earth, rejoice and be glad, because the Lord magnified his doing.
Joel 2:22 Take courage, beasts of the plain, because plains of the wilderness have sprouted, because a tree bore its fruit; vine and fig tree gave their strength.
Joel 2:23 And children of Sion, rejoice and be glad in the Lord your God, because he gave you food for righteousness, and he will rain upon you early and late rain as before,
Joel 2:24 and the threshing floors will be filled with grain, and the winepresses will overflow with wine and oil.
Joel 2:25 And I will repay you for the years which the locust and the locust grub and the mildew and the caterpillar devoured, my great force which I sent out among you;
Joel 2:26 and eating, you will eat and be filled, and praise the name of the Lord your God, for what he did with you as wonders, and my people will certainly not be put to shame into the age;
Joel 2:27 and you will know that I am in the midst of Israel, and I am the Lord your God, and there is no other except me, and all my people will certainly no longer be put to shame into the age.

## Chapter 4

Joel 4:1 For behold, I, in those days and at that time, when I turn back the captivity of Iouda and Ierusalem,

Joel 4:8 and sell your sons and your daughters into the hands of sons of Iouda, and they will sell them into captivity to a nation far away, because the Lord spoke.
Joel 4:9 Proclaim these things among the nations, sanctify war, rouse the fighters; bring them forward and go up, all warrior men.

Joel 4:12 Let all the nations be roused and go up into the valley of Iosaphat, for there I will sit to judge all the nations round about.
Joel 4:13 Send out sickles, because the harvest is present; enter, tread, because the winepress is full; the vats overflow, because their evil things have multiplied.

Joel 4:17 And you will know that I am the Lord your God who dwells in Sion on my holy mountain; and Ierusalem will be a holy city, and foreigners will no longer pass through her.
Joel 4:18 And it will be on that day that the mountains will drip sweetness, and the hills will flow with milk, and all the outlets of Iouda will flow with waters, and a spring will go out from the house of the Lord and water the torrent of the rushes.

## Chapter 1

Obadiah 1:1 A vision of Abdias. Thus says the Lord God to Idoumaia: I heard a report from the Lord, and he sent out a dispatch to the nations: Rise, and let us rise up against her for war.

Obadiah 1:3 The arrogance of your heart lifted you up, dwelling in the openings of the rocks, raising his dwelling, saying in his heart: Who will bring me down to the earth?
Obadiah 1:4 If you are raised aloft like an eagle, and if you place your nest among the stars, from there I will bring you down, says the Lord.
Obadiah 1:5 If thieves entered to you, or robbers by night, where would you have been cast away? Would they not have stolen what was sufficient for themselves? And if grape harvesters entered to you, would they not have left a gleaning?
Obadiah 1:6 How Esau was searched out, and his hidden things seized.
Obadiah 1:7 All the men of your covenant sent you out as far as your boundaries; your men of peace opposed you, prevailed against you; they placed ambushes beneath you; there is no understanding in them.
Obadiah 1:8 On that day, says the Lord, I will destroy wise men from Idoumaia and understanding from the mountain of Esau;
Obadiah 1:9 and your fighters from Thaiman will be terrified, so that a man may be removed from the mountain of Esau
Obadiah 1:10 because of the slaughter and the impiety against your brother Iakob, and shame will cover you, and you will be removed into the age.
Obadiah 1:11 From the day you stood opposed, on a day when foreigners were taking his force captive, and strangers entered his gates and cast lots over Ierusalem, you too were like one of them.
Obadiah 1:12 And do not look upon your brother's day on a day of strangers, and do not rejoice over the sons of Iouda on the day of their destruction, and do not speak boastfully on a day of affliction;
Obadiah 1:13 nor enter the gates of peoples on the day of their troubles, nor yourself look upon their gathering on the day of their ruin, nor join in attacking their force on the day of their destruction;
Obadiah 1:14 nor stand over their passageways to destroy their survivors, nor shut in those fleeing from them on a day of affliction.
Obadiah 1:15 For the day of the Lord is near upon all the nations; as you did, so it will be for you; your recompense will be repaid upon your head;
Obadiah 1:16 for as you drank upon my holy mountain, all the nations will drink wine; they will drink and go down, and they will be as though not existing.
Obadiah 1:17 But on mount Sion there will be salvation, and it will be holy; and the house of Iakob will inherit those who inherited them.
Obadiah 1:18 And the house of Iakob will be fire, but the house of Ioseph a flame, and the house of Esau straw, and they will blaze against them and devour them, and there will be no fire-bearer in the house of Esau, because the Lord spoke.
Obadiah 1:19 And those in Nageb will inherit the mountain of Esau, and those in Sephela the foreigners, and they will inherit the mountain of Ephraim and the plain of Samareia and Beniamin and Galaaditis.
Obadiah 1:20 And this is the beginning of the resettlement: for the sons of Israel, the land of the Chananites as far as Sarepta, and the resettlement of Ierusalem as far as Ephratha, and they will inherit the cities of Nageb.
Obadiah 1:21 And saved men will go up from mount Sion to punish the mountain of Esau, and the kingdom will belong to the Lord.

# Jonah

The Apostolic Bible. Public domain. https://apostolic-bible.ysys9.chatgpt.site/license.html


## Chapter 1

Jonah 1:1 And a word of the Lord came to Ionas son of Amathi, saying:
Jonah 1:2 Rise and go to Nineue, the great city, and proclaim in it, because the cry of its wickedness came up to me.
Jonah 1:3 And Ionas rose to flee to Tharsis from the presence of the Lord, and went down to Ioppe and found a ship going to Tharsis, and paid its fare and boarded it to sail with them to Tharsis from the presence of the Lord.
Jonah 1:4 And the Lord stirred up a wind upon the sea, and a great surge arose in the sea, and the ship was in danger of being shattered.
Jonah 1:5 And the sailors feared and were crying out, each to their god, and cast the equipment in the ship into the sea to be lightened of it; but Ionas went down into the hollow of the ship and was sleeping and snoring.
Jonah 1:6 And the lookout approached him and said to him: Why are you snoring? Rise and call upon your god, so that God may save us and we may not perish.
Jonah 1:7 And each said to his neighbor: Come, let us cast lots and learn on whose account this evil is among us. And they cast lots, and the lot fell upon Ionas.
Jonah 1:8 And they said to him: Tell us on whose account this evil is among us. What is your work? And from where do you come, and from what region and what people are you?
Jonah 1:9 And he said to them: I am a slave of the Lord, and I worship the Lord God of heaven, who made the sea and the dry land.
Jonah 1:10 And the men feared a great fear and said to him: What is this you have done? For the men knew that he was fleeing from the presence of the Lord, because he told them.
Jonah 1:11 And they said to him: What shall we do to you, and the sea will abate from us? For the sea was continuing and stirring up a greater surge.
Jonah 1:12 And Ionas said to them: Lift me and cast me into the sea, and the sea will abate from you; for I know that this great surge is upon you because of me.
Jonah 1:13 And the men were forcing themselves to return to the land and could not, because the sea was continuing and being stirred up more against them.
Jonah 1:14 And they cried out to the Lord and said: By no means, Lord, let us not perish on account of this man's soul, and do not place righteous blood upon us, because you, Lord, have done as you wished.
Jonah 1:15 And they took Ionas and cast him out into the sea, and the sea ceased from its tossing.
Jonah 1:16 And the men feared the Lord with great fear, and sacrificed a sacrifice to the Lord and vowed vows.

## Chapter 2

Jonah 2:1 And the Lord commanded a great sea creature to swallow Ionas; and Ionas was in the belly of the sea creature three days and three nights.
Jonah 2:2 And Ionas prayed to the Lord his God from the belly of the sea creature,
Jonah 2:3 and said: I cried in my affliction to the Lord my God, and he heard me; from the belly of Hades, of my cry, you heard my voice.
Jonah 2:4 You cast me away into the depths of the heart of the sea, and rivers surrounded me; all your billows and your waves passed over me.
Jonah 2:5 And I said: I have been rejected from your eyes; shall I again look toward your holy temple?
Jonah 2:6 Water poured around me as far as my soul; the utmost abyss surrounded me; my head sank into clefts of mountains.
Jonah 2:7 I went down into a land whose bars are everlasting restraints, and let the corruption of my life rise up, Lord my God.
Jonah 2:8 When my soul was failing from me, I remembered the Lord, and may my prayer come to you into your holy temple.
Jonah 2:9 Those guarding vain and false things abandoned their mercy.
Jonah 2:10 But I will sacrifice to you with a voice of praise and confession; whatever I vowed, I will repay to you, of salvation to the Lord.
Jonah 2:11 And the sea creature was commanded, and it cast Ionas out upon the dry land.

## Chapter 3

Jonah 3:1 And a word of the Lord came to Ionas a second time, saying:
Jonah 3:2 Rise and go to Nineue, the great city, and proclaim in it according to the former proclamation which I spoke to you.
Jonah 3:3 And Ionas rose and went to Nineue, as the Lord spoke; but Nineue was a city great to God, about a journey of three days' road.
Jonah 3:4 And Ionas began to enter the city about a day's journey, and proclaimed and said: Yet three days, and Nineue will be overturned.
Jonah 3:5 And the men of Nineue believed God and proclaimed a fast and put on sackcloth, from their great to their small.
Jonah 3:6 And the word reached the king of Nineue, and he rose from his throne and removed his robe from himself and clothed himself in sackcloth and sat upon ashes.
Jonah 3:7 And it was proclaimed and said in Nineue by the king and by his grandees, saying: Let men and beasts and cattle and sheep taste nothing, nor graze, nor drink water.
Jonah 3:8 And the men and the beasts clothed themselves in sackcloth and cried earnestly to God; and each turned from his evil way and from the injustice in their hands, saying:
Jonah 3:9 Who knows whether God will change his mind and turn from the wrath of his anger, and we will certainly not perish?
Jonah 3:10 And God saw their works, that they turned from their evil ways, and God changed his mind over the evil which he spoke of doing to them, and did not do it.

## Chapter 4

Jonah 4:1 And Ionas was grieved with great grief and was confounded.
Jonah 4:2 And he prayed to the Lord and said: O Lord, were these not my words while I was still in my land? Therefore I made haste to flee to Tharsis, for I knew that you are merciful and compassionate, long-suffering and abundant in mercy, and change your mind over evil things.
Jonah 4:3 And now, Master Lord, take my soul from me, because it is better for me to die than for me to live.
Jonah 4:4 And the Lord said to Ionas: Have you been exceedingly grieved?
Jonah 4:5 And Ionas went out from the city and sat opposite the city; and he made himself a tent there and was sitting beneath it in shade, until he should see what would happen to the city.
Jonah 4:6 And the Lord God commanded a gourd, and it rose above the head of Ionas to be shade above his head, to shade him from his evils; and Ionas rejoiced over the gourd with great joy.
Jonah 4:7 And God commanded a worm at dawn the next day, and it struck the gourd, and it dried up.
Jonah 4:8 And it happened as the sun rose that God commanded a scorching wind of burning heat, and the sun struck upon the head of Ionas; and he grew faint and was renouncing his soul, and said: It is better for me to die than to live.
Jonah 4:9 And God said to Ionas: Have you been exceedingly grieved over the gourd? And he said: I have been exceedingly grieved unto death.
Jonah 4:10 And the Lord said: You had pity on the gourd, for which you suffered no hardship and which you did not nourish, which came to be in a night and perished in a night.
Jonah 4:11 But shall I not have pity on Nineue, the great city, in which dwell more than twelve myriads of men, who did not know their right hand or their left hand, and many beasts?

# Nahum

## Chapter 1

Nahum 1:1 An oracle of Nineue; a book of the vision of Naoum the Elkesite.
Nahum 1:2 A jealous God and an avenger is the Lord, the Lord avenging with anger, the Lord avenging his adversaries, and he himself removing his enemies.
Nahum 1:3 The Lord is long-suffering, and his strength is great, and acquitting, the Lord will not acquit. His way is in consummation and shaking together, and clouds are the dust of his feet.
Nahum 1:4 Threatening the sea and drying it, and laying waste all the rivers; Basanitis and Karmel diminished, and the blossoming things of Lebanon failed.
Nahum 1:5 The mountains were shaken by him, and the hills were moved; and the earth recoiled before him, the whole earth and all who dwell in it.
Nahum 1:6 Who will stand before his wrath? And who will resist in the wrath of his anger? His anger melts dominions, and the rocks were shattered by him.
Nahum 1:7 The Lord is kind to those awaiting him on a day of affliction, and knows those revering him;
Nahum 1:8 and in a flood in its course he will make an end of those rising up, and darkness will pursue his enemies.
Nahum 1:9 What do you devise against the Lord? He himself will make an end; he will not punish twice for the same thing with affliction;
Nahum 1:10 for it will be laid barren as far as their foundation, and consumed like an entwined bindweed and like straw full of dryness.
Nahum 1:11 From you will go out a thought against the Lord, devising evil things in opposition.
Nahum 1:12 Thus says the Lord who rules many waters: And thus they will be separated, and your report will no longer be heard.
Nahum 1:13 And now I will shatter his rod from you and tear your bonds;
Nahum 1:14 and the Lord will command concerning you; no longer will anything be sown from your name; from the house of your god I will destroy the carved and cast images; I will appoint your burial, because you are swift.

## Chapter 2

Nahum 2:1 Behold, upon the mountains the feet of one announcing good news and reporting peace; celebrate your feasts, Iouda, repay your vows, because they will certainly no longer pass through you unto old age. It has been brought to an end, removed.

Nahum 2:4 the weapons of their power from men, mighty men mocking amid fire; the reins of their chariots on the day of his preparation, and the horsemen will be disturbed
Nahum 2:5 in the roads, and the chariots will be confounded and entangled in the squares; their appearance is like torches of fire and like lightning running through.
Nahum 2:6 And their grandees will remember and flee by day and grow weak in their journey and hasten to the walls and prepare their outposts.
Nahum 2:7 The gates of the rivers were opened, and the palaces collapsed,
Nahum 2:8 and the foundation was uncovered, and she was going up, and her female slaves were being led, like doves uttering in their hearts.
Nahum 2:9 And Nineue, her waters are like a pool of water, and they, fleeing, did not stop, and there was no one looking back.
Nahum 2:10 They were plundering silver, plundering gold, and there was no end to her adornment; they have been weighed down beyond all her desirable vessels.
Nahum 2:11 A shaking out and a shaking up and a boiling out and a breaking of heart and a loosening of knees and birth pangs upon every waist, and the face of all like the scorching of a pot.
Nahum 2:12 Where is the dwelling place of the lions and the pasture belonging to the young lions, where a lion went to enter there, a young lion, and there was no one frightening it?
Nahum 2:13 A lion seized what was sufficient for his young lions and strangled for his lions, and filled his nest with prey and his dwelling with plunder.
Nahum 2:14 Behold, I am against you, says the Lord Almighty, and I will burn your multitude into smoke, and a sword will devour your lions, and I will destroy your prey from the earth, and your works will certainly no longer be heard.

## Chapter 3

Nahum 3:1 O city of bloodshed, wholly false, full of injustice; prey will not be felt for.
Nahum 3:2 A sound of whips and a sound of the shaking of wheels and of a horse pursuing and of a chariot bounding,

Nahum 3:11 And you will be made drunk and be disregarded, and you will seek for yourself a stand against enemies.

Nahum 3:13 Behold, your people are like women within you; opening, the gates of your land will be opened to your enemies, and fire will devour your bars.

Nahum 3:19 There is no healing for your crushing; your wound became inflamed; all who hear your report will clap hands over you; for upon whom has your wickedness not come continually?

# Habakkuk

The Apostolic Bible. Public domain. https://apostolic-bible.ysys9.chatgpt.site/license.html


## Chapter 1

Habakkuk 1:1 The oracle which Ambakoum the prophet saw.
Habakkuk 1:2 How long, Lord, will I cry and you certainly not hear? Will I cry to you, being wronged, and you not save?
Habakkuk 1:3 Why did you show me troubles and pains, to look upon misery and impiety? Judgment has arisen against me, and the judge takes.
Habakkuk 1:4 Therefore law has been dispersed, and judgment is not carried through to completion, because the impious one oppresses the righteous one; because of this judgment will go out distorted.
Habakkuk 1:5 See, despisers, and look and marvel at wonders and disappear, because I work a work in your days which you will certainly not believe if someone recounts it.
Habakkuk 1:6 For behold, I rouse against you the Chaldeans, the fighters, the bitter and swift nation going over the breadths of the earth to inherit dwellings not its own;
Habakkuk 1:7 he is fearsome and manifest; his judgment will be from himself, and his oracle will go out from himself;
Habakkuk 1:8 and his horses will leap beyond leopards and are swifter than the wolves of Arabia; and his horsemen will ride out and rush from afar and fly like an eagle eager to eat.
Habakkuk 1:9 An end will come to the impious who stand opposed to their faces, and he will gather captivity like sand.
Habakkuk 1:10 And he will revel among kings, and tyrants are his playthings, and he will mock every stronghold and throw up a mound and seize it.
Habakkuk 1:11 Then the spirit will change and pass through and make atonement; this strength belongs to my God. –
Habakkuk 1:12 Are you not from the beginning, Lord, my holy God? And we will certainly not die. Lord, you have appointed him for judgment; and he formed me to reprove his discipline.
Habakkuk 1:13 The eye is pure so as not to see evil things, and you will not be able to look upon pains; why do you look upon despisers? Will you remain silent when an impious one swallows the righteous one?
Habakkuk 1:14 And you will make men like the fish of the sea and like the creeping things having no leader.
Habakkuk 1:15 He pulled up an entirety with a hook and dragged him in a casting net and gathered him in his drag nets; because of this his heart will be glad and rejoice;
Habakkuk 1:16 because of this he will sacrifice to his drag net and burn incense to his casting net, because with them he fattened his portion, and his food is choice;
Habakkuk 1:17 therefore he will cast his casting net and will not spare to kill nations continually.

## Chapter 2

Habakkuk 2:1 I will stand upon my watch and step upon a rock, and look out to see what he will speak in me and what I will answer concerning my reproof.
Habakkuk 2:2 And the Lord answered me and said: Write a vision, and clearly upon a tablet, so that the one reading these things may run.
Habakkuk 2:3 For the vision is still for an appointed time, and it will rise toward an end and not in vain; if he is late, await him, because coming, he will come and certainly not delay.
Habakkuk 2:4 If he draws back, my soul takes no pleasure in him; but the righteous one will live by my faith.
Habakkuk 2:5 But the wine-soaked and contemptuous man, a boaster, will certainly accomplish nothing, who widened his soul like Hades, and he, like death, is not filled, and he will gather all the nations to himself and receive all the peoples to himself.
Habakkuk 2:6 Will not all these take up a parable against him and a riddle for his narration? And they will say: Woe to the one multiplying for himself what is not his – how long? – and heavily weighing down his collar.
Habakkuk 2:7 For suddenly those biting him will rise, and your plotters will sober up, and you will become plunder for them.
Habakkuk 2:8 Because you despoiled many nations, all the remaining peoples will despoil you because of bloodshed of men and impieties of land and city and all who dwell in it. –
Habakkuk 2:9 O one gaining an evil gain for his house, to place his nest on high, to be pulled out from the hand of evil things.
Habakkuk 2:10 You planned shame for your house; you brought many peoples to an end, and your soul sinned;
Habakkuk 2:11 for a stone will cry from a wall, and a beetle from wood will utter these things. –
Habakkuk 2:12 Woe to the one building a city with bloodshed and preparing a city with injustices.
Habakkuk 2:13 Are these things not from the Lord Almighty? And considerable peoples failed in fire, and many nations grew faint.
Habakkuk 2:14 For the earth will be filled with knowing the glory of the Lord; like water it will cover them. –

Haggai 1:5 And now thus says the Lord Almighty: Set now your hearts upon your ways;
Haggai 1:6 you sowed much and brought in little, ate and not to fullness, drank and not to drunkenness, clothed yourselves and were not warmed in them, and the one gathering wages gathered into a pierced bundle.
Haggai 1:7 Thus says the Lord Almighty: Place your hearts upon your ways;
Haggai 1:8 go up upon the mountain and cut wood and build the house, and I will take pleasure in it and be glorified, said the Lord.
Haggai 1:9 You looked for much, and it became little; and it was brought into the house, and I blew it away. Therefore thus says the Lord Almighty: Because my house is desolate, but you hurry, each to his house,

Haggai 1:14 And the Lord roused the spirit of Zorobabel son of Salathiel, of the tribe of Iouda, and the spirit of Iesous son of Iosedek, the great priest, and the spirit of the remaining ones of all the people, and they entered and were doing works in the house of the Lord Almighty their God,

Zechariah 6:4 And I answered and said to the angel speaking in me: What are these, lord?
Zechariah 6:5 And the angel speaking in me answered and said: These are the four winds of heaven; they go out to stand beside the Lord of all the earth;
Zechariah 6:6 that in which the black horses were, they were going out to the land of the north, and the white ones were going out behind them, and the variegated ones were going out to the land of the south,
Zechariah 6:7 and the gray ones were going out and looking to go, to go around the earth. And he said: Go and go around the earth; and they went around the earth.
Zechariah 6:8 And he cried out and spoke to me, saying: Behold, those going out to the land of the north brought my anger to rest in the land of the north.
Zechariah 6:9 And a word of the Lord came to me, saying:
Zechariah 6:10 Take the things from the captivity from its rulers and from its useful ones and from those who have known it, and you will enter on that day into the house of Iosias son of Sophonias, who has come from Babylon,
Zechariah 6:11 and take silver and gold and make crowns and place them upon the head of Iesous son of Iosedek, the great priest,
Zechariah 6:12 and say to him: Thus says the Lord Almighty: Behold, a man, Rising is his name, and beneath him he will rise, and he will build the house of the Lord;
Zechariah 6:13 and he will receive excellence and sit and rule upon his throne, and the priest will be at his right, and peaceful counsel will be between both.
Zechariah 6:14 But the crown will be for those awaiting and for its useful ones and for those who have known it, and for the favor of the son of Sophonias and for a song in the house of the Lord.
Zechariah 6:15 And those far from them will come and build in the house of the Lord, and you will know that the Lord Almighty has sent me to you; and it will be, if hearing, you hear the voice of the Lord your God.

## Chapter 7

Zechariah 7:1 And it happened in the fourth year under Dareios the king that a word of the Lord came to Zacharias on the fourth of the ninth month, which is Chaseleu,
Zechariah 7:2 and the king sent Sarasar and Arbeseer and his men to Baithel to propitiate the Lord,
Zechariah 7:3 saying to the priests in the house of the Lord Almighty and to the prophets, saying: The sanctification has entered here in the fifth month, as I have already done for considerable years.
Zechariah 7:4 And a word of the Lord of forces came to me, saying:
Zechariah 7:5 Say to all the people of the land and to the priests, saying: If you fast or beat your breasts on the fifths or on the sevenths, and behold, seventy years, did you fast a fast for me?
Zechariah 7:6 And if you eat or drink, is it not you who eat and you who drink?
Zechariah 7:7 Are these not the words which the Lord spoke by the hands of the former prophets, when Ierusalem was inhabited and prospering, and her cities round about, and the hill country and the plain were inhabited?
Zechariah 7:8 And a word of the Lord came to Zacharias, saying:
Zechariah 7:9 Thus says the Lord Almighty: Judge righteous judgment and do mercy and compassion, each toward his brother,
Zechariah 7:10 and do not oppress widow and orphan and proselyte and needy one, and let no one bear a grudge for his brother's evil in your hearts.
Zechariah 7:11 And they refused to pay attention and gave a deranged back and made their ears heavy so as not to hear,
Zechariah 7:12 and appointed their heart disobedient so as not to hear my law and the words which the Lord Almighty sent out in his spirit by the hands of the former prophets; and great wrath came from the Lord Almighty.
Zechariah 7:13 And it will be, as he spoke and they did not hear him, so they will cry, and I will certainly not hear, says the Lord Almighty.
Zechariah 7:14 And I will cast them out into all the nations which they did not know, and the land will disappear behind them, without anyone passing through or returning; and they consigned a choice land to disappearance.

## Chapter 8

Zechariah 8:1 And a word of the Lord Almighty came, saying:
Zechariah 8:2 Thus says the Lord Almighty: I was jealous for Ierusalem and Sion with great jealousy, and with great anger I was jealous for her.
Zechariah 8:3 Thus says the Lord: And I will return to Sion and dwell in the midst of Ierusalem, and Ierusalem will be called the true city, and the mountain of the Lord Almighty a holy mountain.
Zechariah 8:4 Thus says the Lord Almighty: Old men and old women will yet sit in the squares of Ierusalem, each having his staff in his hand because of a multitude of days;
Zechariah 8:5 and the squares of the city will be filled with boys and girls playing in her squares.
Zechariah 8:6 Thus says the Lord Almighty: For if it is impossible before the remaining ones of this people in those days, will it also be impossible before me? says the Lord Almighty.
Zechariah 8:7 Thus says the Lord Almighty: Behold, I save my people from the land of the east and from the land of the west,
Zechariah 8:8 and I will bring them in and dwell in the midst of Ierusalem, and they will be a people for me, and I will be a God for them in truth and righteousness.
Zechariah 8:9 Thus says the Lord Almighty: Let your hands be strong, those hearing in these days these words from the mouth of the prophets, from the day when the house of the Lord Almighty has been founded, and the temple from when it has been built.
Zechariah 8:10 For before those days the wage of men will not be for benefit, and the wage of beasts will not exist, and for the one going out and the one entering there will be no peace because of affliction; and I will send out all men, each against his neighbor.
Zechariah 8:11 And now I do not act for the remaining ones of this people as in the former days, says the Lord Almighty,
Zechariah 8:12 but I will show peace; the vine will give its fruit, and the earth its produce, and heaven its dew, and I will give all these things as an inheritance to the remaining ones of my people.
Zechariah 8:13 And as you were under a curse among the nations, house of Iouda and house of Israel, so I will save you, and you will be under a blessing; take courage and be strong in your hands.
Zechariah 8:14 For thus says the Lord Almighty: As I intended to harm you when your fathers provoked me to anger, says the Lord Almighty, and did not change my mind,
Zechariah 8:15 so I have drawn myself up and intended in these days to do well for Ierusalem and the house of Iouda; take courage.
Zechariah 8:16 These are the words which you will do: Speak truth, each to his neighbor, and judge peaceful judgment in your gates,
Zechariah 8:17 and do not devise, each, the evil of his neighbor in your hearts, and do not love a false oath, because I hated all these things, says the Lord Almighty.
Zechariah 8:18 And a word of the Lord Almighty came to me, saying:
Zechariah 8:19 Thus says the Lord Almighty: The fourth fast and the fifth fast and the seventh fast and the tenth fast will be joy and gladness and good feasts for the house of Iouda, and you will be glad; and love truth and peace.
Zechariah 8:20 Thus says the Lord Almighty: Many peoples will yet come, and those dwelling in many cities;
Zechariah 8:21 and those dwelling in five cities will come together into one city, saying: Let us go to beseech the face of the Lord and seek out the face of the Lord Almighty; I too will go.
Zechariah 8:22 And many peoples and many nations will come to seek out the face of the Lord Almighty in Ierusalem and to propitiate the face of the Lord.
Zechariah 8:23 Thus says the Lord Almighty: In those days, if ten men from all the tongues of the nations take hold and take hold of the fringe of a Ioudaian man's garment, saying: We will go with you, because we have heard that God is with you.

## Chapter 9

Zechariah 9:1 An oracle of a word of the Lord; in the land of Sedrach and Damascus is his sacrifice, because the Lord watches men and all the tribes of Israel.
Zechariah 9:2 And Emath in her boundaries, Tyre and Sidon, because they were exceedingly wise.
Zechariah 9:3 And Tyre built strongholds for herself and treasured silver like dust and gathered gold like mud of roads.
Zechariah 9:4 Therefore the Lord will inherit her and strike her force into the sea, and she will be consumed with fire.
Zechariah 9:5 Askalon will see and fear, and Gaza too, and suffer exceedingly, and Akkaron, because she was put to shame at her fall; and a king will perish from Gaza, and Askalon will certainly not be inhabited.
Zechariah 9:6 And foreigners will dwell in Azotos, and I will bring down the arrogance of foreigners.
Zechariah 9:7 And I will remove their blood from their mouth and their abominations from between their teeth, and this one too will remain for our God, and they will be like a commander of a thousand in Iouda, and Akkaron like the Iebousite.
Zechariah 9:8 And I will establish a defense for my house, so that none passes through or returns, and one driving out will certainly no longer come upon them, because now I have seen with my eyes.
Zechariah 9:9 Rejoice exceedingly, daughter of Sion; proclaim, daughter of Ierusalem; behold, your king comes to you, righteous and saving, meek and mounted upon a beast of burden and a young colt.
Zechariah 9:10 And he will destroy chariots from Ephraim and a horse from Ierusalem, and a war bow will be destroyed, and a multitude and peace from nations; and he will rule waters as far as the sea, and rivers, the outlets of the earth.
Zechariah 9:11 And you, by blood of a covenant, sent out your prisoners from a pit having no water.
Zechariah 9:12 You will sit in a stronghold, prisoners of the gathering, and for one day of your sojourning I will repay you double;
Zechariah 9:13 for I stretched you, Iouda, as a bow for myself, filled Ephraim, and will rouse your children, Sion, against the children of the Greeks and handle you like a fighter's sword;
Zechariah 9:14 and the Lord will be over them, and a missile will go out like lightning, and the Lord Almighty will sound a trumpet and go in the tossing of his threat.
Zechariah 9:15 The Lord Almighty will shield them, and they will consume them and bury them with sling stones and drink them down like wine and fill an altar like bowls.
Zechariah 9:16 And the Lord will save them on that day, his people like sheep, because holy stones roll upon his land.
Zechariah 9:17 For if anything is good of his and if anything beautiful from him, grain for young men and fragrant wine for virgins.

## Chapter 10

Zechariah 10:1 Ask rain from the Lord in season, early and late; the Lord made apparitions, and will give them winter rain, to each vegetation in a field.
Zechariah 10:2 For the utterers spoke troubles, and the diviners false visions, and they were speaking false dreams, vainly consoling; therefore they were removed like sheep and harmed, because there was no healing.
Zechariah 10:3 My anger was provoked against the shepherds, and I will visit the lambs; and the Lord God the Almighty will visit his flock, the house of Iouda, and appoint them like his splendid horse in war.
Zechariah 10:4 And from him he looked, and from him he appointed, and from him a bow in anger; from him everyone driving out will go out together.
Zechariah 10:5 And they will be like fighters treading mud in the roads in war, and draw themselves up, because the Lord is with them, and riders of horses will be put to shame.
Zechariah 10:6 And I will strengthen the house of Iouda and save the house of Ioseph and settle them, because I loved them, and they will be as though I had not turned them away, because I am the Lord their God and will hear them.
Zechariah 10:7 And they will be like fighters of Ephraim, and their heart will rejoice as with wine; and their children will see and be glad, and their heart will rejoice in the Lord.
Zechariah 10:8 I will signal to them and receive them, because I will redeem them, and they will be multiplied as they were numerous;
Zechariah 10:9 and I will sow them among peoples, and those far away will remember me, nourish their children and return.
Zechariah 10:10 And I will return them from the land of Egypt and receive them from Assyrians and bring them into Galaaditis and into Lebanon, and not even one of them will certainly be left behind;
Zechariah 10:11 and they will pass through a narrow sea and strike waves in the sea, and all the depths of rivers will dry up, and all the arrogance of Assyrians will be removed, and a scepter of Egypt taken away.
Zechariah 10:12 And I will strengthen them in the Lord their God, and they will boast in his name, says the Lord.

## Chapter 11

Zechariah 11:1 Open your doors, Lebanon, and let fire devour your cedars;
Zechariah 11:2 let a pine howl, because a cedar has fallen, because grandees suffered great misery; howl, oaks of Basanitis, because the closely grown thicket was pulled down.
Zechariah 11:3 A sound of lamenting shepherds, because their greatness has suffered misery; a sound of roaring lions, because the pride of the Iordan has suffered misery.
Zechariah 11:4 Thus says the Lord Almighty: Shepherd the sheep of slaughter,
Zechariah 11:5 which their possessors were slaughtering and did not regret, and those selling them were saying: Blessed is the Lord, and we have become rich, and their shepherds suffered nothing over them.
Zechariah 11:6 Therefore I will no longer spare those dwelling in the earth, says the Lord, and behold, I hand over men, each into the hands of his neighbor and into the hands of his king, and they will cut down the earth, and I will certainly not rescue from their hand.
Zechariah 11:7 And I will shepherd the sheep of slaughter into Chanaanitis; and I will take two staffs for myself – the one I called Beauty and the other I called Measured Portion – and I will shepherd the sheep.
Zechariah 11:8 And I will remove the three shepherds in one month, and my soul will be weighed down over them, for their souls too were roaring against me.
Zechariah 11:9 And I said: I will not shepherd you; let the dying one die, and let the failing one fail, and let the remaining ones devour, each, the flesh of his neighbor.
Zechariah 11:10 And I will take my beautiful staff and cast it away, to disperse my covenant which I made with all the peoples;
Zechariah 11:11 and it will be dispersed on that day, and the Chananites will know the sheep that are guarded, because it is a word of the Lord.
Zechariah 11:12 And I will say to them: If it is good before you, give my wage, weighing it, or refuse; and they weighed my wage, thirty silver pieces.
Zechariah 11:13 And the Lord said to me: Put them down into the smelting furnace, and consider whether it is approved, as I was tested on their behalf. And I took the thirty silver pieces and cast them into the house of the Lord, into the smelting furnace.
Zechariah 11:14 And I cast away the second staff, Measured Portion, to disperse the possession between Iouda and Israel.
Zechariah 11:15 And the Lord said to me: Yet take for yourself the shepherd's equipment of an inexperienced shepherd.
Zechariah 11:16 For behold, I rouse a shepherd upon the land; he will certainly not visit the failing one or seek the scattered one or heal the crushed one or guide the whole one, and he will devour the flesh of the choice ones and wrench their ankle bones out.
Zechariah 11:17 O those shepherding vain things and those who have abandoned the sheep; a sword upon his arms and upon his right eye; drying, his arm will dry up, and blinding, his right eye will be blinded.

## Chapter 12

Zechariah 12:1 An oracle of a word of the Lord against Israel; says the Lord, who stretches heaven and founds earth and forms the spirit of man within him:
Zechariah 12:2 Behold, I make Ierusalem like shaking doorways for all the peoples round about, and in Ioudaia there will be a siege against Ierusalem.
Zechariah 12:3 And on that day I will make Ierusalem a stone trampled by all the nations; everyone trampling her, mocking, will be mocked, and all the nations of the earth will gather against her.
Zechariah 12:4 On that day, says the Lord Almighty, I will strike every horse with astonishment and its rider with derangement, but over the house of Iouda I will open my eyes, and strike all the horses of the peoples with blindness.
Zechariah 12:5 And the commanders of thousands of Iouda will say in their hearts: We will find for ourselves those dwelling in Ierusalem in the Lord Almighty their God.
Zechariah 12:6 On that day I will make the commanders of thousands of Iouda like a firebrand among wood and like a torch of fire among straw, and they will devour to the right and to the left all the peoples round about, and Ierusalem will yet dwell by herself.
Zechariah 12:7 And the Lord will save the dwellings of Iouda as from the beginning, so that the boast of the house of David and the exaltation of those dwelling in Ierusalem may not be magnified over Iouda.
Zechariah 12:8 And on that day the Lord will shield those dwelling in Ierusalem, and the weak one among them on that day will be like the house of David, but the house of David like the house of God, like an angel of the Lord before them.
Zechariah 12:9 And on that day I will seek to remove all the nations coming against Ierusalem.
Zechariah 12:10 And I will pour upon the house of David and upon those dwelling in Ierusalem a spirit of grace and compassion, and they will look toward me because they danced in triumph against me, and beat their breasts over him as over a beloved one, and suffer anguish as over a firstborn.
Zechariah 12:11 On that day the beating of the breast will be magnified in Ierusalem like mourning for a pomegranate grove cut down in a plain,
Zechariah 12:12 and the land will beat its breast tribe by tribe, a tribe by itself and their women by themselves, the tribe of the house of David by itself and their women by themselves, the tribe of the house of Nathan by itself and their women by themselves,
Zechariah 12:13 the tribe of the house of Leui by itself and their women by themselves, the tribe of Symeon by itself and their women by themselves,
Zechariah 12:14 all the remaining tribes, a tribe by itself and their women by themselves.

## Chapter 13

Zechariah 13:1 On that day every place will be opened in the house of David.
Zechariah 13:2 And on that day, says the Lord, I will destroy the names of the idols from the land, and there will no longer be remembrance of them; and I will remove the false prophets and the unclean spirit from the land.
Zechariah 13:3 And if a man yet prophesies, his father and his mother who begot him will say to him: You will not live, because you spoke false things in the name of the Lord; and his father and his mother who begot him will bind his feet together when he prophesies.
Zechariah 13:4 And on that day the prophets will be put to shame, each for his vision when he prophesies, and they will put on a hairy skin because they lied.
Zechariah 13:5 And he will say: I am not a prophet, for I am a man working the earth, because a man begot me from my youth.
Zechariah 13:6 And I will say to him: What are these wounds between your hands? And he will say: Those with which I was wounded in my beloved house.
Zechariah 13:7 Sword, be roused against my shepherds and against a man, my fellow citizen, says the Lord Almighty; strike the shepherds and pull out the sheep, and I will bring my hand upon the shepherds.
Zechariah 13:8 And in all the land, says the Lord, the two parts will be destroyed and fail, but the third will remain in it;
Zechariah 13:9 and I will bring the third through fire and refine them as silver is refined and test them as gold is tested; he will call upon my name, and I will hear him and say: This is my people, and he will say: The Lord is my God.

## Chapter 14
