Zechariah 14:1 Behold, days of the Lord are coming, and your spoils will be divided within you.
Zechariah 14:2 And I will gather all the nations against Ierusalem for war, and the city will be taken, and the houses plundered, and the women defiled, and half the city will go out into captivity, but the remaining ones of my people will certainly not be destroyed from the city.
Zechariah 14:3 And the Lord will go out and draw himself up among those nations, as on the day of his battle array on a day of war.
Zechariah 14:4 And his feet will stand on that day upon the mountain of olives opposite Ierusalem to the east; and the mountain of olives will be split, half of it toward the east and half toward the sea, an exceedingly great chasm; and half the mountain will incline toward the north and half toward the south.
Zechariah 14:5 And the ravine of my mountains will be blocked, and a ravine of mountains will be joined as far as Iasol and be blocked as it was blocked in the days of the earthquake in the days of Ozias king of Iouda; and the Lord my God will come, and all the holy ones with him.
Zechariah 14:6 On that day there will be no light and cold and frost;
Zechariah 14:7 it will be one day, and that day known to the Lord, and neither day nor night, and toward evening there will be light.
Zechariah 14:8 And on that day living water will go out from Ierusalem, half of it into the first sea and half of it into the last sea, and in summer and in spring it will be thus.
Zechariah 14:9 And the Lord will be king over all the earth; on that day the Lord will be one and his name one.
Zechariah 14:10 Encircling all the land and the wilderness from Gabe as far as Remmon south of Ierusalem; but Rama will remain in place from the gate of Beniamin as far as the place of the first gate, as far as the gate of the corners and as far as the tower of Ananeel, as far as the king's vats.
Zechariah 14:11 They will dwell in her, and there will no longer be a thing devoted to destruction, and Ierusalem will dwell confidently.
Zechariah 14:12 And this will be the fall with which the Lord will strike all the peoples that marched against Ierusalem; their flesh will melt while they stand upon their feet, and their eyes will flow from their sockets, and their tongue will melt in their mouth.
Zechariah 14:13 And on that day a great astonishment from the Lord will be upon them, and each will take hold of his neighbor's hand, and his hand will be entangled with the hand of his neighbor.
Zechariah 14:14 And Ioudas will draw himself up in Ierusalem and gather the strength of all the peoples round about, gold and silver and clothing in an exceedingly great multitude.
Zechariah 14:15 And this will be the fall of the horses and the mules and the camels and the donkeys and all the beasts in those camps, according to this fall.
Zechariah 14:16 And as many as are left of all the nations which came against Ierusalem will go up yearly to bow down to the king, the Lord Almighty, and celebrate the feast of tent pitching.
Zechariah 14:17 And as many as do not go up from all the tribes of the earth to Ierusalem to bow down to the king, the Lord Almighty, these too will be added to those.
Zechariah 14:18 But if the tribe of Egypt does not go up or come there, upon these too will be the fall with which the Lord will strike all the nations that do not go up to celebrate the feast of tent pitching.
Zechariah 14:19 This will be the sin of Egypt and the sin of all the nations that do not go up to celebrate the feast of tent pitching.
Zechariah 14:20 On that day what is upon the bridle of the horse will be holy to the Lord Almighty, and the cauldrons in the house of the Lord will be like bowls before the altar,
Zechariah 14:21 and every cauldron in Ierusalem and in Iouda will be holy to the Lord Almighty; and all those sacrificing will come and take of them and boil in them. And there will no longer be a Chananite in the house of the Lord Almighty on that day.

# Malachi

The Apostolic Bible. Public domain. https://apostolic-bible.ysys9.chatgpt.site/license.html


## Chapter 1

Malachi 1:1 An oracle of a word of the Lord against Israel by the hand of his messenger; place it now upon your hearts.
Malachi 1:2 I loved you, says the Lord. And you said: In what did you love us? Was Esau not Iakob's brother? says the Lord; and I loved Iakob,
Malachi 1:3 but hated Esau and consigned his boundaries to disappearance and his inheritance to gifts of a wilderness.
Malachi 1:4 For Idoumaia will say: It has been overturned, and let us return and rebuild the desolate places; thus says the Lord Almighty: They will build, and I will overturn; and they will be called boundaries of lawlessness and a people against whom the Lord has drawn himself up until an age.
Malachi 1:5 And your eyes will see, and you will say: The Lord was magnified beyond the boundaries of Israel.
Malachi 1:6 A son glorifies a father and a slave his lord. And if I am a father, where is my glory? And if I am a lord, where is my fear? says the Lord Almighty. You priests who disparage my name; and you said: In what did we disparage your name?
Malachi 1:7 Bringing polluted loaves to my altar. And you said: In what did we pollute them? In your saying: The table of the Lord is despised, and the food placed upon it despised.
Malachi 1:8 For if you bring a blind one for sacrifice, is it not evil? And if you bring a lame or sick one, is it not evil? Bring it now to your governor, whether he will accept it, whether he will receive your face, says the Lord Almighty.
Malachi 1:9 And now propitiate the face of your God and beseech him; these things have happened by your hands; shall I receive your faces from you? says the Lord Almighty.
Malachi 1:10 For doors will also be shut among you, and you will not kindle my altar for nothing; I have no pleasure in you, says the Lord Almighty, and I will not accept a sacrifice from your hands.
Malachi 1:11 For from the rising of the sun to its setting my name has been glorified among the nations, and in every place incense is brought to my name and a pure sacrifice, because my name is great among the nations, says the Lord Almighty.
Malachi 1:12 But you profane it by saying: The table of the Lord is polluted, and its food placed upon it has been despised.
Malachi 1:13 And you said: These things are from hardship, and I blew them away, says the Lord Almighty; and you were bringing plunder and lame things and afflicted things; and if you bring the sacrifice, shall I accept them from your hands? says the Lord Almighty.
Malachi 1:14 And cursed is one who was able, and a male existed in his flock, and his vow was upon it, and he sacrifices a spoiled one to the Lord; for I am a great king, says the Lord Almighty, and my name is manifest among the nations.

## Chapter 2

Malachi 2:1 And now this command is for you, priests;
Malachi 2:2 if you do not hear, and if you do not place in your heart to give glory to my name, says the Lord Almighty, I will also send the curse upon you and curse your blessing and curse it; and I will disperse your blessing, and it will not be among you, because you do not place it in your heart.
Malachi 2:3 Behold, I set apart the shoulder for you and will scatter the stomach upon your faces, the stomach of your feasts, and I will take you to the same place;
Malachi 2:4 and you will know that I have sent this command to you, so that my covenant may be with the Leuites, says the Lord Almighty.
Malachi 2:5 My covenant was with him, of life and peace, and I gave it to him in fear, to fear me and shrink before my name.
Malachi 2:6 A law of truth was in his mouth, and injustice was not found on his lips; directing rightly in peace, he walked with me and turned many from injustice.
Malachi 2:7 For a priest's lips will guard knowledge, and they will seek out law from his mouth, because he is a messenger of the Lord Almighty.
Malachi 2:8 But you turned aside from the way and made many weak in law; you destroyed the covenant of Leui, says the Lord Almighty.
Malachi 2:9 And I have made you despised and slack among all the nations, because you did not guard my ways, but were receiving faces in law.
Malachi 2:10 Did not one God create you? Is there not one father of all of you? Why did you abandon, each, his brother, to profane the covenant of your fathers?
Malachi 2:11 Ioudas was abandoned, and an abomination arose in Israel and in Ierusalem, because Ioudas profaned the holy things of the Lord which he loved, and practiced toward foreign gods.
Malachi 2:12 The Lord will destroy the man doing these things, until he is also humbled from the dwellings of Iakob and from those bringing a sacrifice to the Lord Almighty.
Malachi 2:13 And these things which I hated you were doing; you were covering the altar of the Lord with tears and weeping and groaning from troubles. Is it still fitting to look upon a sacrifice or take an acceptable thing from your hands?
Malachi 2:14 And you said: For what reason? Because the Lord solemnly testified between you and the wife of your youth, whom you abandoned, and she is your companion and the wife of your covenant.
Malachi 2:15 And no other did it, and a remnant of his spirit. And you said: What else but seed does God seek? And guard yourselves in your spirit, and do not abandon the wife of your youth;
Malachi 2:16 but if, hating, you send her away, says the Lord God of Israel, impiety will also cover your thoughts, says the Lord Almighty. And guard yourselves in your spirit, and you will certainly not abandon.
Malachi 2:17 Those provoking God with your words, and you said: In what did we provoke him? In your saying: Everyone doing evil is good before the Lord, and he took pleasure in them; and: Where is the God of righteousness?

## Chapter 3

Malachi 3:1 Behold, I send out my messenger, and he will look upon a way before me, and suddenly the Lord whom you seek will come to his own temple, and the messenger of the covenant whom you desire; behold, he comes, says the Lord Almighty.
Malachi 3:2 And who will endure the day of his entry? Or who will stand at his appearance? For he enters like fire of a smelting furnace and like the herb of washers.
Malachi 3:3 And he will sit smelting and purifying like silver and like gold; and he will purify the sons of Leui and melt them like gold and like silver; and they will be bringing a sacrifice to the Lord in righteousness.
Malachi 3:4 And a sacrifice of Iouda and Ierusalem will please the Lord as in the days of the age and as in the former years.
Malachi 3:5 And I will draw near to you in judgment and be a swift witness against the sorceresses and the adulteresses and those swearing falsely by my name, and those withholding a hired worker's wage and those oppressing a widow and those striking orphans with their fists and those turning aside the judgment of a proselyte and those not fearing me, says the Lord Almighty.
Malachi 3:6 For I am the Lord your God, and I have not changed; and you, sons of Iakob, do not refrain
Malachi 3:7 from the injustices of your fathers; you turned aside from my ordinances and did not guard them. Return to me, and I will return to you, says the Lord Almighty. And you said: In what shall we return?
Malachi 3:8 Will a man supplant God? For you supplant me. And you will say: In what have we supplanted you? Because the tithes and the firstfruits are with you;
Malachi 3:9 and looking away, you look away, and you supplant me; the nation was brought to an end.
Malachi 3:10 And you brought all the produce into the storehouses, and in his house will be his plunder. Examine now by this, says the Lord Almighty, whether I will not open for you the floodgates of heaven and pour my blessing upon you until there is sufficiency;
Malachi 3:11 and I will set apart for you for food and certainly not destroy your fruit of the earth, and your vine in the field will certainly not grow weak, says the Lord Almighty.
Malachi 3:12 And all the nations will call you blessed, because you will be a desired land, says the Lord Almighty.
Malachi 3:13 You made your words heavy against me, says the Lord, and you said: In what did we speak against you?
Malachi 3:14 You said: Vain is the one serving God, and what more is there, that we guarded his observances and went as suppliants before the Lord Almighty?
Malachi 3:15 And now we call strangers blessed, and all those doing lawless things are built up, and they resisted God and were saved.
Malachi 3:16 Those fearing the Lord spoke these things, each to his neighbor; and the Lord attended and heard and wrote a book of remembrance before him for those fearing the Lord and revering his name.
Malachi 3:17 And they will be mine, says the Lord Almighty, for a day which I make for a possession, and I will choose them as a man chooses his son serving him.
Malachi 3:18 And you will return and see between righteous and lawless, and between the one serving God and the one not serving.
Malachi 3:19 For behold, the day of the Lord comes burning like an oven and will burn them, and all the foreigners and all those doing lawless things will be straw, and the coming day will kindle them, says the Lord Almighty, and neither root nor branch will certainly remain of them.
Malachi 3:20 And for you who fear my name a sun of righteousness will rise, and healing in its wings, and you will go out and leap like calves released from bonds.
Malachi 3:21 And you will trample lawless ones, because they will be ashes beneath your feet on the day which I make, says the Lord Almighty.
Malachi 3:22 And behold, I send you Elias the Thesbite before the great and manifest day of the Lord comes,
Malachi 3:23 who will restore a father's heart to a son and a man's heart to his neighbor, lest I come and strike the earth utterly.
Malachi 3:24 Remember the law of Moyses my slave, as I commanded him at Choreb for all Israel, ordinances and statutes.

# Isaiah

The Apostolic Bible. Public domain. https://apostolic-bible.ysys9.chatgpt.site/license.html


## Chapter 1

Isaiah 1:1 A vision which Esaias son of Amos saw, which he saw against Ioudaia and against Ierusalem in the reign of Ozias and Ioatham and Achaz and Ezekias, who reigned over Ioudaia.
Isaiah 1:2 Hear, heaven, and give ear, earth, because the Lord spoke: I begot sons and raised them, but they rejected me.
Isaiah 1:3 An ox knew its owner and a donkey its lord's manger; but Israel did not know me, and the people did not understand me.
Isaiah 1:4 Woe, sinful nation, people full of sins, evil seed, lawless sons; you abandoned the Lord and provoked the holy one of Israel to anger.
Isaiah 1:5 Why should you yet be struck, adding lawlessness? Every head is in pain and every heart in grief.
Isaiah 1:6 From feet to head, neither wound nor bruise nor inflamed injury; there is no poultice to apply, nor oil nor bandages.
Isaiah 1:7 Your land is desolate, your cities burned with fire; strangers devour your region before you, and it has been laid waste, overturned by foreign peoples.
Isaiah 1:8 The daughter of Sion will be left like a tent in a vineyard and like a fruit watchman's hut in a cucumber patch, like a besieged city;
Isaiah 1:9 and if the Lord Sabaoth had not left us seed, we would have become like Sodoma and been made like Gomorra.
Isaiah 1:10 Hear a word of the Lord, rulers of Sodoma; attend to a law of God, people of Gomorra.
Isaiah 1:11 What is the multitude of your sacrifices to me? says the Lord; I am full of whole burnt offerings of rams, and I do not desire fat of lambs and blood of bulls and goats,
Isaiah 1:12 not even if you come to appear to me. For who sought these things from your hands? To tread my court
Isaiah 1:13 you will no longer proceed; if you bring fine flour, it is vain; incense is an abomination to me; your new moons and sabbaths and a great day I do not endure; fasting and idleness
Isaiah 1:14 and your new moons and your feasts my soul hates; you became a surfeit to me; I will no longer release your sins.
Isaiah 1:15 When you stretch your hands toward me, I will turn my eyes from you, and if you multiply supplication, I will not hear you; for your hands are full of blood.
Isaiah 1:16 Wash yourselves, become clean, remove wickednesses from your souls before my eyes, cease from your wickednesses,
Isaiah 1:17 learn to do good, seek out judgment, rescue one being wronged, judge for an orphan and vindicate a widow;
Isaiah 1:18 and come and let us dispute, says the Lord, and if your sins are like purple, I will whiten them like snow, but if they are like scarlet, I will whiten them like wool.
Isaiah 1:19 And if you are willing and hear me, you will eat the good things of the earth;
Isaiah 1:20 but if you are unwilling and do not hear me, a sword will devour you; for the mouth of the Lord spoke these things.
Isaiah 1:21 How faithful city Sion became a prostitute, full of judgment, in which righteousness slept, but now murderers.
Isaiah 1:22 Your silver is unapproved; your retailers mix wine with water;
Isaiah 1:23 your rulers disobey, partners of thieves, loving gifts, pursuing recompense, not judging for orphans and not attending to the judgment of widows.
Isaiah 1:24 Therefore thus says the Master, the Lord Sabaoth: Woe to the strong ones of Israel; for my anger will not cease against adversaries, and I will exact judgment from my enemies.
Isaiah 1:25 And I will bring my hand upon you and refine you to purity, but destroy the disobedient and remove all lawless ones from you and humble all arrogant ones.
Isaiah 1:26 And I will appoint your judges as formerly and your counselors as from the beginning; and after these things you will be called City of righteousness, faithful mother-city Sion.
Isaiah 1:27 For her captivity will be saved with judgment and with mercy;
Isaiah 1:28 and the lawless and the sinners will be crushed together, and those abandoning the Lord will be brought to an end.
Isaiah 1:29 For they will be ashamed of their idols which they desired, and were put to shame over their gardens which they coveted;
Isaiah 1:30 for they will be like a terebinth that has shed its leaves and like a garden having no water;
Isaiah 1:31 and their strength will be like straw of tow and their works like sparks of fire, and the lawless and the sinners will be burned together, and there will be no one quenching.

## Chapter 2

Isaiah 2:1 The word which came from the Lord to Esaias son of Amos concerning Ioudaia and concerning Ierusalem.
Isaiah 2:2 For in the last days the mountain of the Lord will be manifest, and the house of God upon the summits of the mountains, and it will be raised above the hills; and all the nations will come to it,
Isaiah 2:3 and many nations will go and say: Come, and let us go up to the mountain of the Lord and to the house of the God of Iakob, and he will announce his way to us, and we will walk in it; for a law will go out from Sion, and a word of the Lord from Ierusalem.
Isaiah 2:4 And he will judge between the nations and reprove a numerous people, and they will beat their swords into plows and their spears into sickles, and nation will no longer take a sword against nation, and they will certainly no longer learn to wage war.
Isaiah 2:5 And now, house of Iakob, come, let us walk in the light of the Lord.
Isaiah 2:6 For he abandoned his people, the house of Israel, because their region was filled, as from the beginning, with divinations like that of the foreigners, and many foreign children came to be for them.
Isaiah 2:7 For their region was filled with silver and gold, and there was no number to their treasures; and the land was filled with horses, and there was no number to their chariots;
Isaiah 2:8 and the land was filled with abominations, the works of their hands, and they bowed down to what their fingers made;
Isaiah 2:9 and a man bowed and a man was humbled, and I will certainly not release them.
Isaiah 2:10 And now enter the rocks and hide in the earth before the fear of the Lord and the glory of his strength, when he rises to shatter the earth.
Isaiah 2:11 For the eyes of the Lord are high, but man is lowly; and the height of men will be humbled, and the Lord alone will be raised on that day.
Isaiah 2:12 For a day of the Lord Sabaoth is against every arrogant and proud one and against every high and lofty one, and they will be humbled,
Isaiah 2:13 and against every cedar of Lebanon among the high and lofty ones, and against every acorn tree of Basan,
Isaiah 2:14 and against every mountain and against every high hill,
Isaiah 2:15 and against every high tower and against every high wall,
Isaiah 2:16 and against every ship of the sea and against every sight of beautiful ships;
Isaiah 2:17 and every man will be humbled, and the height of men will fall, and the Lord alone will be raised on that day.
Isaiah 2:18 And they will conceal all the handmade things,
Isaiah 2:19 bringing them into the caves and into the clefts of the rocks and into the holes of the earth, before the fear of the Lord and the glory of his strength, when he rises to shatter the earth.
Isaiah 2:20 For on that day a man will cast out his silver and gold abominations which they made to worship, to vain things and to bats,
Isaiah 2:21 to enter the holes of the solid rock and the clefts of the rocks, before the fear of the Lord and the glory of his strength, when he rises to shatter the earth.

## Chapter 3

Isaiah 3:1 Behold now, the Master, the Lord Sabaoth, will remove from Ioudaia and from Ierusalem a strong man and a strong woman, strength of bread and strength of water,
Isaiah 3:2 a giant and a strong one and a warrior man and a judge and a prophet and a conjecturer and an elder,
Isaiah 3:3 and a commander of fifty and a marvelous counselor and a wise master builder and an understanding hearer;
Isaiah 3:4 and I will appoint young men as their rulers, and mockers will lord over them.
Isaiah 3:5 And the people will collide, man against man and man against his neighbor; the child will clash with the old man, the dishonored with the honored.
Isaiah 3:6 For a man will take hold of his brother or his father's relative, saying: You have a garment; become our leader, and let my food be under you.
Isaiah 3:7 And answering, he will say on that day: I will not be your leader; for there is neither bread nor a garment in my house; I will not be leader of this people.
Isaiah 3:8 For Ierusalem has been abandoned, and Ioudaia has collapsed, and their tongues are with lawlessness, disobeying in things toward the Lord; for now their glory was humbled,
Isaiah 3:9 and the shame of their face opposed them; but they announced their sin like that of Sodoma and made it manifest. Woe to their soul, because they have planned an evil plan against themselves,
Isaiah 3:10 saying: Let us bind the righteous one, because he is inconvenient to us; therefore they will eat the produce of their works.
Isaiah 3:11 Woe to the lawless one; evil things according to the works of his hands will happen to him.
Isaiah 3:12 My people, your collectors glean you, and those exacting payment lord over you; my people, those calling you blessed lead you astray and trouble the path of your feet.
Isaiah 3:13 But now the Lord will take his stand for judgment and set his people for judgment;
Isaiah 3:14 the Lord himself will come to judgment with the elders of the people and with its rulers: But why did you burn my vineyard, and the plunder of the poor is in your houses?
Isaiah 3:15 Why do you wrong my people and put the face of the poor to shame?
Isaiah 3:16 Thus says the Lord: Because the daughters of Sion were exalted and walked with a high neck and with gestures of eyes, and in the going of their feet were dragging their tunics and playing with their feet together,
Isaiah 3:17 God will also humble ruling daughters of Sion, and the Lord will uncover their form
Isaiah 3:18 on that day, and the Lord will remove the glory of their clothing and their ornaments and their braided ornaments and their fringes and their crescent ornaments,
Isaiah 3:19 and the necklace and the ornament of their face,
Isaiah 3:20 and the arrangement of glorious adornment and the armlets and the bracelets and the braided ornament and the wristbands and the rings and the earrings,
Isaiah 3:21 and the purple-bordered garments and the garments purple in the middle,
Isaiah 3:22 and the coverings for the house and the transparent Laconian garments,
Isaiah 3:23 and the fine linen and the hyacinth-colored and the scarlet things and the fine linen interwoven with gold and hyacinth, and flowing summer coverings.
Isaiah 3:24 And instead of a sweet scent there will be dust, and instead of a belt you will gird yourself with a cord, and instead of the golden ornament of the head you will have baldness because of your works, and instead of the tunic purple in the middle you will gird yourself with sackcloth.
Isaiah 3:25 And your most beautiful son whom you love will fall by a sword, and your strong ones will fall by a sword.
Isaiah 3:26 And the cases of your adornment will be humbled and mourn, and you will be left alone and dashed to the ground.

## Chapter 4

Isaiah 4:1 And seven women will take hold of one man, saying, We will eat our bread and put on our garments; only let your name be called upon us; take away our reproach.
Isaiah 4:2 But on that day God will shine forth in counsel with glory upon the earth, to exalt and glorify what is left of Israel,
Isaiah 4:3 and it shall be that what remains in Sion and what is left in Ierusalem will be called holy, all those written for life in Ierusalem;
Isaiah 4:4 because the Lord will wash away the filth of the sons and daughters of Sion and cleanse the blood from their midst with a spirit of judgment and a spirit of burning.
Isaiah 4:5 And he will come, and it shall be that a cloud will shade every place of Mount Sion and all that surrounds her by day, and as smoke and as the light of a burning fire by night; with all the glory it will be covered;
Isaiah 4:6 and it will be for shade from heat and in shelter and in a hiding place from harshness and rain.

## Chapter 5

Isaiah 5:1 I will indeed sing to the beloved a song of the beloved for my vineyard. A vineyard came to be for the beloved on a horn, in a fertile place.
Isaiah 5:2 And I put a fence around it and palisaded it and planted a Sorech vine and built a tower in its midst and dug a vat in it; and I waited for it to produce a grape cluster, but it produced thorns.
Isaiah 5:3 And now, man of Iouda and those dwelling in Ierusalem, judge between me and my vineyard.
Isaiah 5:4 What shall I still do for my vineyard that I have not done for it? For I waited for it to produce a grape cluster, but it produced thorns.
Isaiah 5:5 But now I will announce to you what I will do to my vineyard: I will take away its fence, and it will be for plundering, and I will pull down its wall, and it will be for trampling,
Isaiah 5:6 and I will abandon my vineyard, and it will certainly not be pruned or dug, and a thorn will come up in it as in waste ground; and I will command the clouds not to rain rain upon it.
Isaiah 5:7 For the vineyard of the Lord Sabaoth is the house of Israel, and the man of Iouda a beloved new planting; I waited for it to do justice, but it did lawlessness, and not righteousness but an outcry.
Isaiah 5:8 Woe to those joining house to house and bringing field near to field, so that they may take something away from their neighbor; will you dwell alone upon the earth?
Isaiah 5:9 For these things were heard in the ears of the Lord Sabaoth: for if many houses come to be, great and beautiful ones will be for desolation, and there will be none dwelling in them.
Isaiah 5:10 For where ten yokes of oxen work, it will produce one jar, and the one sowing six artabas will produce three measures. —
Isaiah 5:11 Woe to those rising in the morning and pursuing sikera, those remaining late; for the wine will burn them up.
Isaiah 5:12 For they drink wine with lyre and harp and drums and pipes, but they do not look at the works of the Lord and do not consider the works of his hands.
Isaiah 5:13 Therefore my people became captive because they did not know the Lord, and there came to be a multitude of dead because of famine and thirst for water.
Isaiah 5:14 And Hades enlarged its soul and opened its mouth without ceasing, and her glorious and great and rich and pestilent ones will go down.
Isaiah 5:15 And a human will be humbled, and a man will be dishonored, and the lofty eyes will be humbled;
Isaiah 5:16 and the Lord Sabaoth will be exalted in judgment, and the holy God will be glorified in righteousness.
Isaiah 5:17 And those plundered will graze like bulls, and lambs will eat the deserted places of those taken away. —
Isaiah 5:18 Woe to those dragging sins as with a long rope, and lawless deeds as with the strap of a heifer's yoke,
Isaiah 5:19 those saying, Let what he will do draw near quickly, so that we may see, and let the counsel of the Holy One of Israel come, so that we may know. —
Isaiah 5:20 Woe to those calling evil good and good evil, those making darkness light and light darkness, those making bitter sweet and sweet bitter. —
Isaiah 5:21 Woe to those intelligent in themselves and knowledgeable before themselves. —
Isaiah 5:22 Woe to your strong ones who drink wine and the powerful ones who mix sikera,
Isaiah 5:23 those justifying the impious because of gifts and taking away the right of the righteous.
Isaiah 5:24 Therefore, in the manner that stubble will be burned by a coal of fire and burned up by a spreading flame, their root will be like chaff, and their flower will rise like dust; for they did not desire the law of the Lord Sabaoth, but provoked the utterance of the Holy One of Israel.
Isaiah 5:25 And the Lord Sabaoth was angered with wrath against his people, and he laid his hand upon them and struck them, and the mountains were provoked, and their carcasses became like dung in the midst of a road. And in all these things the fury did not turn away, but still the hand is raised.
Isaiah 5:26 Therefore he will raise a signal among the nations far away and whistle to them from the end of the earth, and behold, they come quickly, lightly;
Isaiah 5:27  they will not hunger or grow weary or doze or sleep or loosen their belts from their waist, nor will the straps of their sandals be broken;
Isaiah 5:28 whose arrows are sharp and their bows drawn, the feet of their horses were reckoned as solid rock, the wheels of their chariots as a tempest;
Isaiah 5:29 they charge like lions and have stood by like a lion's cub; and it will seize and cry out as a beast and cast out, and there will be no one rescuing them.
Isaiah 5:30 And it will cry out because of them on that day like the sound of a surging sea; and they will look toward the earth, and behold, harsh darkness in their perplexity.

## Chapter 6

Isaiah 6:1 And it happened in the year in which Ozias the king died, I saw the Lord sitting upon a high and lifted throne, and the house full of his glory.
Isaiah 6:2 And seraphin stood around him, six wings to the one and six wings to the one, and with two they covered their face and with two they covered their feet and with two they flew.
Isaiah 6:3 And they cried out, one to the other, and said, Holy, holy, holy is the Lord Sabaoth; all the earth is full of his glory.
Isaiah 6:4 And the lintel was lifted by the voice with which they cried out, and the house was filled with smoke.
Isaiah 6:5 And I said, O wretched me, because I am pierced, because, being a human and having unclean lips, I dwell in the midst of a people having unclean lips, and I saw the King, the Lord Sabaoth, with my eyes.
Isaiah 6:6 And one of the seraphin was sent to me, and in its hand it had a coal, which it took with the tongs from the altar,
Isaiah 6:7 and it touched my mouth and said, Behold, this touched your lips and will take away your lawless deeds and thoroughly cleanse your sins.
Isaiah 6:8 And I heard the voice of the Lord saying, Whom shall I send, and who will go to this people? And I said, Behold, here I am; send me.
Isaiah 6:9 And he said, Go and say to this people, By hearing you will hear and certainly not understand, and looking you will look and certainly not see;
Isaiah 6:10 for the heart of this people grew thick, and with their ears they heard heavily and shut their eyes, lest they see with their eyes and hear with their ears and understand with their heart and turn back, and I will heal them.
Isaiah 6:11 And I said, Until when, Lord? And he said, Until cities are desolated through not being inhabited, and houses through there being no humans, and the earth will be left desolate.
Isaiah 6:12 And after these things God will remove the humans far away, and those left will be multiplied upon the earth;
Isaiah 6:13 and still upon it there is the tenth part, and again it will be for plunder, like a terebinth and like an acorn when it falls out of its casing.

## Chapter 7

Isaiah 7:1 And it happened in the days of Achaz, son of Ioatham, son of Ozias, king of Iouda, Raasson king of Aram and Phakee son of Romelias, king of Israel, went up against Ierusalem to war against her, and they were not able to besiege her.
Isaiah 7:2 And it was announced to the house of David, saying, Aram has agreed with Ephraim; and his soul and the soul of his people were astounded, as when a tree in a wood is shaken by wind.
Isaiah 7:3 And the Lord said to Esaias, Go out to meet Achaz, you and the remaining Iasoub your son, toward the pool of the upper road of the fuller's field,
Isaiah 7:4 and you will say to him, Take care to be quiet and do not fear, nor let your soul be weak because of these two pieces of wood, these smoking firebrands; for when the wrath of my fury comes, I will heal again.
Isaiah 7:5 And the son of Aram and the son of Romelias, because they counseled an evil counsel concerning you, saying,
Isaiah 7:6 We will go up into Ioudaia and, speaking together with them, turn them toward us, and we will make the son of Tabeel king over her,
Isaiah 7:7 thus says the Lord Sabaoth, This counsel will certainly not endure, nor will it be;
Isaiah 7:8 but the head of Aram is Damascus, but within yet sixty-five years the kingdom of Ephraim will cease from being a people,
Isaiah 7:9 and the head of Ephraim is Somoron, and the head of Somoron the son of Romelias; and if you do not believe, you will certainly not understand either.
Isaiah 7:10 And the Lord proceeded to speak to Achaz, saying,
Isaiah 7:11 Ask for yourself a sign from the Lord your God, into depth or into height.
Isaiah 7:12 And Achaz said, I will certainly not ask, nor will I certainly test the Lord.
Isaiah 7:13 And he said, Hear indeed, house of David; is it a small thing for you to cause humans a struggle? And how do you cause the Lord a struggle?
Isaiah 7:14 Therefore the Lord himself will give you a sign: behold, the virgin will have in the womb and bear a son, and you will call his name Emmanouel;
Isaiah 7:15 he will eat butter and honey; before he knows or chooses evil things, he will choose the good;
Isaiah 7:16 because before the child knows good or bad, he disobeys wickedness so as to choose the good, and the land which you fear will be abandoned before the two kings.
Isaiah 7:17 But God will bring upon you and upon your people and upon your father's house days which have not yet come since the day he took Ephraim away from Iouda—the king of the Assyrians.
Isaiah 7:18 And it shall be on that day that the Lord will whistle to flies, that which rules a part of the river of Egypt, and to the bee which is in the country of the Assyrians,
Isaiah 7:19 and they will all come and rest in the ravines of the country and in the holes of the rocks and in the caves and in every fissure and in every tree.
Isaiah 7:20 On that day the Lord will shave with the great and drunken razor, which is beyond the river of the king of the Assyrians, the head and the hair of the feet, and he will take away the beard.
Isaiah 7:21 And it shall be on that day that a human will rear a heifer of the cattle and two sheep,
Isaiah 7:22 and it shall be that, because of the producing of very much milk, everyone left upon the earth will eat butter and honey.
Isaiah 7:23 And it shall be on that day that every place where there are a thousand vines worth a thousand shekels will become waste ground and thorns;
Isaiah 7:24 with arrow and bow they will enter there, because all the earth will be waste ground and thorns.
Isaiah 7:25 And every mountain being plowed will be plowed, and fear will certainly not come there; for from waste ground and thorns it will become a pasture for sheep and a trampling place for cattle.

## Chapter 8

Isaiah 8:1 And the Lord said to me, Take for yourself a volume of a large new scroll and write in it with a human's stylus, To make a swift plundering of spoils; for it is present.
Isaiah 8:2 And make faithful humans witnesses for me, Ourias and Zacharias son of Barachias.
Isaiah 8:3 And I approached the prophetess, and she conceived in the womb and bore a son. And the Lord said to me, Call his name, Spoil quickly, plunder swiftly;
Isaiah 8:4 because before the child knows to call father or mother, he will take the power of Damascus and the spoils of Samaria before the king of the Assyrians.
Isaiah 8:5 And the Lord proceeded to speak to me again,
Isaiah 8:6 Because this people does not desire the water of Siloam which goes quietly, but desires to have Raasson and the son of Romelias as king over you,
Isaiah 8:7 therefore behold, the Lord brings up upon you the water of the river, strong and abundant, the king of the Assyrians and his glory, and it will go up upon every ravine of yours and walk upon every wall of yours,
Isaiah 8:8 and he will take away from Ioudaia a human who will be able to raise a head or one able to accomplish something, and his encampment will be such as to fill the breadth of your country; God is with us.
Isaiah 8:9 Know, nations, and be defeated; listen as far as the end of the earth; having become strong, be defeated; for if you become strong again, you will be defeated again.
Isaiah 8:10 And whatever counsel you may counsel, the Lord will scatter it, and whatever word you may speak will certainly not endure for you, because the Lord God is with us.
Isaiah 8:11 Thus says the Lord, With the strong hand they disobey the course of the way of this people, saying,
Isaiah 8:12 Never say, Hard; for everything which this people may say is hard; but you will certainly not fear its fear or be troubled;
Isaiah 8:13 sanctify the Lord himself, and he will be your fear.
Isaiah 8:14 And if you are trusting in him, he will be for you a sanctuary, and you will not encounter him as a stumbling against a stone or as a falling against a rock; but the house of Iakob is in a snare, and those sitting in Ierusalem in a hollow.
Isaiah 8:15 Therefore many among them will be powerless and will fall and be shattered, and humans who are in security will draw near and be captured.
Isaiah 8:16 Then those sealing the law so that it may not be learned will be manifest.
Isaiah 8:17 And he will say, I will wait for God, who turned his face away from the house of Iakob, and I will be trusting in him.
Isaiah 8:18 Behold, I and the children whom God gave me, and it will be for signs and wonders in the house of Israel from the Lord Sabaoth, who dwells on Mount Sion.
Isaiah 8:19 And if they say to you, Seek those speaking from the earth and the ventriloquists, those speaking empty words who speak from the belly—is not a nation toward its God? Why do they seek the dead concerning the living?
Isaiah 8:20 For he gave a law for help, so that they may speak unlike this utterance, concerning which there are no gifts to give concerning it.
Isaiah 8:21 And a harsh famine will come upon you, and it shall be that when you hunger, you will be grieved and speak evil of the ruler and the patachra, and they will look up toward heaven above
Isaiah 8:22 and look toward the earth below, and behold, affliction and confinement and darkness, constricted perplexity and darkness so as not to see,
Isaiah 8:23 and the one in confinement will not be perplexed until a time. Do this first, do it quickly, country of Zaboulon, land of Nephthalim, the way of the sea, and the remaining ones inhabiting the coast and beyond the Iordan, Galilaia of the nations, the parts of Ioudaia.

## Chapter 9

Isaiah 9:1 The people walking in darkness, see a great light; those dwelling in a country and shadow of death, light will shine upon you.
Isaiah 9:2 The greatest part of the people, which you brought down in your gladness, and they will be glad before you as those glad at harvest and in the manner of those dividing spoils.
Isaiah 9:3 Because the yoke lying upon them has been taken away, and the rod upon their neck; for the Lord scattered the rod of those exacting payment, as on the day against Madiam.
Isaiah 9:4 Because they will repay every robe gathered by deceit and a garment with restitution, and they will wish that they had become burned by fire.
Isaiah 9:5 Because a child was born to us, a son was also given to us, whose rule came to be upon his shoulder, and his name is called Messenger of Great Counsel; for I will bring peace upon the rulers, peace and health to him.
Isaiah 9:6 Great is his rule, and there is no limit to his peace upon the throne of David and his kingdom, to establish it and uphold it in righteousness and in judgment from now and for eternal time; the zeal of the Lord Sabaoth will do these things.
Isaiah 9:7 The Lord sent death upon Iakob, and it came upon Israel,
Isaiah 9:8 and all the people of Ephraim and those sitting in Samaria will know, saying in insolence and a lofty heart,
Isaiah 9:9 Bricks have fallen, but come, let us hew stones and cut down sycamores and cedars and build ourselves a tower.
Isaiah 9:10 And God will dash those rising against Mount Sion upon them and scatter their enemies,
Isaiah 9:11 Syria from the rising of the sun and the Greeks from the setting of the sun, those devouring Israel with the whole mouth. In all these things the fury did not turn away, but still the hand is raised. —
Isaiah 9:12 And the people did not turn back until it was struck, and they did not seek the Lord.
Isaiah 9:13 And the Lord took away from Israel head and tail, great and small, in one day,
Isaiah 9:14 an elder and those admiring faces [this is the rule], and a prophet teaching lawless things [this is the tail].
Isaiah 9:15 And those blessing this people will be leading astray, and they lead astray so that they may swallow them.
Isaiah 9:16 Therefore God will not be glad over their young men and will not have mercy on their orphans and their widows, because all are lawless and evil, and every mouth speaks unjust things. In all these things the fury did not turn away, but still the hand is raised. —
Isaiah 9:17 And lawlessness will burn like fire and like dry grass will be eaten by fire; and it will burn in the thickets of the wood, and it will devour together everything around the hills.
Isaiah 9:18 Because of the fury of the Lord's wrath, the whole earth has been burned up, and the people will be as burned up by fire; a human will not have mercy on his brother,
Isaiah 9:19 but will turn aside to the right because he will hunger, and will eat from the left, and a human eating the flesh of his arm will certainly not be filled.
Isaiah 9:20 For Manasse will eat of Ephraim, and Ephraim of Manasse, because together they will besiege Ioudas. In all these things the fury did not turn away, but still the hand is raised. —

## Chapter 10

Isaiah 10:1 Woe to those writing wickedness; for, writing, they write wickedness,
Isaiah 10:2 turning aside the justice of the poor, snatching the judgment of the needy of my people, so that a widow may be for them for seizure and an orphan for plunder.
Isaiah 10:3 And what will they do on the day of visitation? For affliction will come to you from far away; and to whom will you flee for help? And where will you leave your glory,
Isaiah 10:4 so as not to fall into calamity? In all these things the fury did not turn away, but still the hand is raised.
Isaiah 10:5 Woe to the Assyrians; the rod of my fury and wrath is in their hands.
Isaiah 10:6 I will send my wrath against a lawless nation, and I will order my people to make spoils and plunder and trample the cities and turn them into dust.
Isaiah 10:7 But he did not consider it thus and has not reckoned it thus in his soul, but his mind will turn to doing away with and destroying not a few nations.
Isaiah 10:8 And if they say to him, You alone are ruler,
Isaiah 10:9 he will also say, Did I not take the country above Babylon and Chalanne, where the tower was built? And I took Arabia and Damascus and Samaria;
Isaiah 10:10 in the manner that I took these in my hand, I will also take all the dominions. Wail, carved things in Ierusalem and in Samaria;
Isaiah 10:11 for in the manner that I did to Samaria and her handmade things, thus I will also do to Ierusalem and her idols. —
Isaiah 10:12 And it shall be, when the Lord finishes doing everything on Mount Sion and in Ierusalem, he will bring it upon the great mind, the ruler of the Assyrians, and upon the height of the glory of his eyes.
Isaiah 10:13 For he said, By strength I will do it, and by the wisdom of understanding; I will take away the boundaries of nations and plunder their strength and shake inhabited cities,
Isaiah 10:14 and I will seize the whole inhabited world with my hand like a nest and lift it like abandoned eggs, and there is no one who will escape me or contradict me.
Isaiah 10:15 Will an axe be glorified without the one cutting with it? Or will a saw be exalted without the one pulling it? Likewise, if someone lifts a rod or a piece of wood.
Isaiah 10:16 And not thus, but the Lord Sabaoth will send dishonor into your honor, and into your glory a burning fire will burn;
Isaiah 10:17 and the light of Israel will become fire, and he will sanctify him in burning fire and eat the woodland like grass. On that day
Isaiah 10:18 the mountains and hills and woods will be extinguished, and it will devour from soul to flesh; and the one fleeing will be like the one fleeing from a burning flame;
Isaiah 10:19 and those left of them will be a number, and a child will write them.
Isaiah 10:20 And it shall be on that day that what is left of Israel will no longer continue, and those saved of Iakob will certainly no longer be trusting in those who wronged them, but they will be trusting in God, the Holy One of Israel, in truth,
Isaiah 10:21 and what is left of Iakob will be toward a strong God.
Isaiah 10:22 And if the people Israel become like the sand of the sea, their remnant will be saved; for, completing and cutting short a word in righteousness,
Isaiah 10:23 because God will do a word cut short in the whole inhabited world.
Isaiah 10:24 Therefore thus says the Lord Sabaoth, Do not fear, my people, those dwelling in Sion, because of the Assyrians, because he will strike you with a rod; for I bring a blow upon you to see the way of Egypt.
Isaiah 10:25 For yet a little while and the wrath will cease, but my fury will be against their counsel;
Isaiah 10:26 and God will raise up against them according to the blow against Madiam in a place of affliction, and his fury by the way along the sea into the way toward Egypt.
Isaiah 10:27 And it shall be on that day that his fear will be taken away from you and his yoke from your shoulder, and the yoke will be destroyed from your shoulders.
Isaiah 10:28 For he will come into the city Aggai and pass into Magedo and place his equipment in Machmas;
Isaiah 10:29 and he will pass a ravine and come into Aggai; fear will seize Rama, the city of Saoul; she will flee,
Isaiah 10:30 the daughter of Gallim; Laisa will listen; Anathoth will listen;
Isaiah 10:31 Madebena was astounded, and those dwelling in Gibbir; encourage
Isaiah 10:32 today on the way to remain; with the hand encourage the mountain, the daughter Sion, and the hills in Ierusalem.
Isaiah 10:33 For behold, the Master, the Lord Sabaoth, throws the glorious ones into turmoil with strength, and the lofty in insolence will be shattered, and the lofty will be humbled,
Isaiah 10:34 and the lofty will fall by a sword, and Lebanon will fall with the lofty.

## Chapter 11

Isaiah 11:1 And a rod will come forth from the root of Iessai, and a flower will come up from the root.
Isaiah 11:2 And the spirit of God will rest upon him, a spirit of wisdom and understanding, a spirit of counsel and strength, a spirit of knowledge and piety;
Isaiah 11:3 a spirit of the fear of God will fill him. He will not judge according to appearance or reprove according to talk,
Isaiah 11:4 but he will judge a judgment for a humble one and reprove the humble of the earth; and he will strike the earth with the word of his mouth and with a breath through his lips kill an impious one;
Isaiah 11:5 and he will be girded at his waist with righteousness and wrapped at his sides with truth.
Isaiah 11:6 And a wolf will graze together with a lamb, and a leopard will rest together with a kid, and a calf and a bull and a lion will graze together, and a small child will lead them;
Isaiah 11:7 and an ox and a bear will graze together, and their children will be together, and a lion and an ox will eat straw together.
Isaiah 11:8 And an infant child will put its hand upon a hole of asps and upon a bed of the offspring of asps.
Isaiah 11:9 And they will certainly not do evil or be able to destroy anyone upon my holy mountain, because the whole earth was filled with knowing the Lord, as much water covers seas.
Isaiah 11:10 And it shall be on that day that the root of Iessai and the one rising to rule nations—in him nations will hope, and his rest will be honor.
Isaiah 11:11 And it shall be on that day that the Lord will proceed to show his hand, to be zealous for the remaining remnant of the people, whatever may be left from the Assyrians and from Egypt and Babylonia and Ethiopia and from the Ailamites and from the rising of the sun and from Arabia.
Isaiah 11:12 And he will raise a sign to the nations and gather the lost ones of Israel, and he will gather the scattered ones of Iouda from the four wings of the earth.
Isaiah 11:13 And the jealousy of Ephraim will be taken away, and the enemies of Iouda will perish; Ephraim will not be jealous of Ioudas, and Ioudas will not afflict Ephraim.
Isaiah 11:14 And they will fly in ships of foreigners over the sea; together they will plunder both those from the rising of the sun and Idoumaia; and upon Moab they will first lay their hands, and the sons of Ammon will first obey.
Isaiah 11:15 And the Lord will desolate the sea of Egypt and lay his hand upon the river with a violent wind and strike seven ravines so that one may pass through it in sandals;
Isaiah 11:16 and there will be a passage for my people left in Egypt, and it will be for Israel like the day when it came out of the land of Egypt.

## Chapter 12

Isaiah 12:1 And you will say on that day, I will bless you, Lord, because you were angry with me and turned away your fury and had mercy on me.
Isaiah 12:2 Behold, my God, my Savior, is the Lord; I will be trusting in him and will be saved in him and will not fear, because the Lord is my glory and my praise, and he became salvation for me.
Isaiah 12:3 And you will draw water with gladness from the springs of salvation.
Isaiah 12:4 And you will say on that day, Hymn the Lord, cry out his name, announce his glorious things among the nations, remember that his name was exalted.
Isaiah 12:5 Hymn the name of the Lord, because he did lofty things; announce these things in all the earth.
Isaiah 12:6 Exult and be glad, those dwelling in Sion, because the Holy One of Israel was exalted in her midst.

## Chapter 13

Isaiah 13:1 A vision which Esaias son of Amos saw against Babylon.
Isaiah 13:2 Upon a level mountain raise a sign; lift the voice to them; do not fear; encourage with the hand, Open, rulers.
Isaiah 13:3 I give orders, and I lead them; they are sanctified, and I lead them; giants come to fulfill my fury, rejoicing together and acting insolently.
Isaiah 13:4 A sound of many nations upon the mountains, like many nations, a sound of kings and nations gathered together. The Lord Sabaoth has commanded an armed fighting nation
Isaiah 13:5 to come from a land far away, from the end of the foundation of heaven, the Lord and his armed fighters, to destroy the whole inhabited world.
Isaiah 13:6 Wail, for the day of the Lord is near, and destruction will come from God.
Isaiah 13:7 Therefore every hand will be slackened, and every human soul will be cowardly;
Isaiah 13:8 and the elders will be troubled, and pangs will hold them like those of a woman giving birth; and they will lament to one another and be astounded and change their face like a flame.
Isaiah 13:9 For behold, an incurable day of the Lord comes, of fury and wrath, to make the whole inhabited world desolate and destroy the sinners from it.
Isaiah 13:10 For the stars of heaven and Orion and all the adornment of heaven will not give light, and it will be darkened as the sun rises, and the moon will not give her light.
Isaiah 13:11 And I will command evils for the whole inhabited world and their sins for the impious; and I will destroy the insolence of the lawless and humble the insolence of the proud.
Isaiah 13:12 And those left will be more precious than unfired gold, and the human will be more precious than the stone from Souphir.
Isaiah 13:13 For heaven will be angered, and the earth will be shaken from her foundations because of the fury of the wrath of the Lord Sabaoth on the day when his fury comes upon it.
Isaiah 13:14 And those left will be like a fleeing little gazelle and like a wandering sheep, and there will be no one gathering, so that a human turns back to his people and a human hastens to his country.
Isaiah 13:15 For whoever is captured will be defeated, and whoever are gathered will fall by a sword;
Isaiah 13:16 and they will dash their children before them and plunder their houses and have their wives.
Isaiah 13:17 Behold, I raise up against you the Medes, who do not reckon silver or have need of gold.
Isaiah 13:18 They will shatter young men's bows and will certainly not have mercy on your children, nor will their eyes spare the children.
Isaiah 13:19 And Babylon, which is called glorious by the king of the Chaldeans, will be as when God overturned Sodoma and Gomorra;
Isaiah 13:20 she will not be inhabited for eternal time, nor will they enter her through many generations, nor will Arabs pass through her, nor will shepherds rest in her;
Isaiah 13:21 and beasts will rest there, and the houses will be filled with noise, and sirens will rest there, and demons will dance there,
Isaiah 13:22 and donkey-centaurs will dwell there, and hedgehogs will make nests in their houses; it comes quickly and will not delay.

## Chapter 14

Isaiah 14:1 And the Lord will have mercy on Iakob and will yet choose Israel, and they will rest upon their land, and the sojourner will be added to them and will be added to the house of Iakob,
Isaiah 14:2 and nations will take them and bring them into their place, and they will inherit and be multiplied upon God's land as male slaves and female slaves; and those who took them captive will be captives, and those who ruled them will be ruled.
Isaiah 14:3 And it shall be on that day that God will give you rest from the pain and your fury and your harsh slavery, in which you served them.
Isaiah 14:4 And you will take up this lament over the king of Babylon and say on that day, How has the one exacting payment rested, and the taskmaster rested?
Isaiah 14:5 God shattered the yoke of sinners, the yoke of rulers;
Isaiah 14:6 having struck a nation in fury with an incurable blow, beating a nation with a blow of fury which did not spare,
Isaiah 14:7 he rested in confidence. All the earth cries out with gladness,
Isaiah 14:8 and the trees of Lebanon were glad over you, and the cedar of Lebanon: Since you have fallen asleep, the one cutting us has not come up.
Isaiah 14:9 Hades below was embittered, meeting you; all the giants who ruled the earth were raised up together for you, those raising all kings of nations from their thrones.
Isaiah 14:10 All will answer and say to you, You too were captured, just as we were, and you were reckoned among us.
Isaiah 14:11 But your glory went down into Hades, your abundant gladness; below you they will spread decay, and your covering is a worm.
Isaiah 14:12 How did the dawn-bearer who rises in the morning fall from heaven? The one sending to all the nations was shattered to the earth.
Isaiah 14:13 But you said in your mind, I will go up into heaven; above the stars of heaven I will place my throne; I will sit on a high mountain, upon the high mountains toward the north;
Isaiah 14:14 I will go up above the clouds; I will be like the Most High.
Isaiah 14:15 But now you will go down into Hades and into the foundations of the earth.
Isaiah 14:16 Those seeing you will marvel at you and say, Is this the human who provokes the earth, shaking kings?
Isaiah 14:17 The one who made the whole inhabited world desolate and pulled down the cities did not release those in calamity.
Isaiah 14:18 All the kings of the nations fell asleep in honor, each human in his house;
Isaiah 14:19 but you will be thrown in the mountains like an abhorred corpse with many dead, pierced by swords, going down into Hades. In the manner that a garment stained with blood will not be clean,
Isaiah 14:20 thus neither will you be clean, because you destroyed my land and killed my people; you will certainly not remain for eternal time, evil seed.
Isaiah 14:21 Prepare your children to be slaughtered for the sins of your father, so that they may not rise and inherit the earth and fill the earth with cities.
Isaiah 14:22 And I will rise against them, says the Lord Sabaoth, and destroy their name and remnant and seed—thus says the Lord—
Isaiah 14:23 and I will make Babylonia desolate so that hedgehogs dwell there, and she will become nothing; and I will make her a pit of mud for destruction. —
Isaiah 14:24 Thus says the Lord Sabaoth, In the manner that I have spoken, thus it will be, and in the manner that I have counseled, thus it will remain,
Isaiah 14:25 to destroy the Assyrians from my land and from my mountains, and they will be for trampling, and their yoke will be taken away from them, and their renown will be taken away from the shoulders.
Isaiah 14:26 This is the counsel which the Lord has counseled against the whole inhabited world, and this the raised hand against all the nations of the inhabited world.
Isaiah 14:27 For what the holy God has counseled, who will scatter it? And who will turn back the raised hand?
Isaiah 14:28 In the year in which Achaz the king died, this utterance came to be.
Isaiah 14:29 Do not be glad, all you foreigners, because the yoke of the one beating you was shattered; for from the seed of snakes will come offspring of asps, and their offspring will come forth as flying snakes.
Isaiah 14:30 And poor people will graze through him, and poor men will rest in peace; but he will kill your seed by famine and kill your remnant.
Isaiah 14:31 Wail, gates of cities; let troubled cities cry out, all the foreigners, because smoke comes from the north, and there is no remaining.
Isaiah 14:32 And what will kings of nations answer? That the Lord founded Sion, and through him the humble of the people will be saved.

## Chapter 15

Isaiah 15:1 The utterance against Moabitis. At night Moabitis will perish, for at night the wall of Moabitis will perish.
Isaiah 15:2 Be grieved for yourselves, for Debon too will perish; where your altar is, there you will go up to weep; over Nabau of Moabitis wail—baldness upon every head, all arms cut;
Isaiah 15:3 in her squares gird yourselves with sackcloth and beat yourselves; upon her roofs and in her streets all wail with weeping.
Isaiah 15:4 Because Esebon and Eleale have cried out, their voice was heard as far as Iassa; therefore the waist of Moabitis cries out; her soul will know.
Isaiah 15:5 The heart of Moabitis cries out within her as far as Segor, for she is a three-year-old heifer; but on the ascent of Louith they will go up toward you weeping; on the road of Aroniim destruction and shaking cry out.
Isaiah 15:6 The water of Nemrim will be desolate, and her grass will cease; for there will be no green grass.
Isaiah 15:7 Will she perhaps be saved even thus? For I will bring Arabs against the ravine, and they will take her.
Isaiah 15:8 For the cry reached the boundary of Moabitis, of Agallim, and her wailing as far as the well of Ailim.
Isaiah 15:9 But the water of Remmon will be filled with blood; for I will bring Arabs upon Remmon and take away the seed of Moab and Ariel and the remnant of Adama.

## Chapter 16

Isaiah 16:1 I will send like creeping things upon the earth; is Mount Sion not a desolate rock?
Isaiah 16:2 For you will be like a removed chick of a flying bird, daughter of Moab. But then, Arnon,
Isaiah 16:3 counsel more; make a shelter of mourning for her continually; in midday darkness they flee; they were astounded; do not be carried away.
Isaiah 16:4 The fugitives of Moab will sojourn with you; they will be a shelter for you from the face of a pursuer, because your alliance was taken away, and the ruler who tramples upon the earth perished.
Isaiah 16:5 And a throne will be established with mercy, and he will sit upon it with truth in the tent of David, judging and seeking judgment and hastening righteousness.
Isaiah 16:6 We heard the insolence of Moab—exceedingly insolent; you raised up pride. Your divination is not thus,
Isaiah 16:7 not thus. Moab will wail, for in Moabitis all will wail; you will meditate for those dwelling in Deseth and will not be ashamed.
Isaiah 16:8 You will mourn the plains of Esebon, vine of Sebama; swallowing the nations, trample her vines as far as Iazer; you will certainly not reach; wander the desert; those sent were abandoned, for they crossed the desert.
Isaiah 16:9 Therefore I will weep as with the weeping of Iazer for the vine of Sebama; he cast down your trees, Esebon and Eleale, because at your harvest and at your vintage I will trample, and everything will fall.
Isaiah 16:10 And gladness and exultation will be taken away from your vineyards, and in your vineyards they will certainly not be glad or tread wine into the vats, for it has ceased.
Isaiah 16:11 Therefore my belly will sound over Moab like a lyre, and my inward parts like a wall which you renewed.
Isaiah 16:12 And it will result in your being ashamed, because Moab grew weary upon the altars, and she will enter her handmade things to pray, and it will certainly not be able to deliver him.
Isaiah 16:13 This is the utterance which the Lord spoke against Moab, whenever he also spoke it.
Isaiah 16:14 And now I say, Within three years, years of a hired worker, the glory of Moab will be dishonored with all the abundant wealth, and he will be left very small and not honored.

## Chapter 17

Isaiah 17:1 The utterance against Damascus. Behold, Damascus will be removed from among cities and will become a ruin,
Isaiah 17:2 abandoned forever, a bed and resting place for flocks, and there will be no pursuer.
Isaiah 17:3 And there will no longer be a stronghold for Ephraim to flee to, and there will no longer be a kingdom in Damascus, and the remainder of the Syrians will perish; for you are not better than the sons of Israel and their glory; thus says the Lord Sabaoth.
Isaiah 17:4 On that day there will be a failing of the glory of Iakob, and the fat things of his glory will be shaken.
Isaiah 17:5 And it will be as when someone gathers a standing harvest and reaps the seed of ears in his arm, and it will be as when someone gathers an ear in a solid ravine
Isaiah 17:6 and stubble is left in it, or as two or three olive berries are left upon a lofty top, or four or five upon their branches; thus says the Lord, the God of Israel.
Isaiah 17:7 On that day a human will be trusting in the one who made him, and his eyes will look toward the Holy One of Israel,
Isaiah 17:8 and they will certainly not be trusting in the altars or in the works of their hands which their fingers made, and they will not see their trees or their abominations.
Isaiah 17:9 On that day your cities will be abandoned, in the manner that the Amorraians and the Euaians abandoned them before the sons of Israel, and they will be desolate,
Isaiah 17:10 because you abandoned God your Savior and did not remember the Lord your helper. Therefore you will plant an unfaithful planting and unfaithful seed;
Isaiah 17:11 but on the day when you plant, you will be led astray; and in the morning, if you sow, it will flower for a harvest on whatever day you allot, and as a human's father you will allot to your sons.
Isaiah 17:12 Woe, multitude of many nations; like a surging sea, thus you will be troubled, and the back of many nations will sound like water.
Isaiah 17:13 Like much water are many nations, like much water borne down violently; and he will drive him away and pursue him far away like chaff of straw from those winnowing before wind, and like dust of a wheel borne by a tempest.
Isaiah 17:14 Toward evening there will be mourning; before morning it will also be no more. This is the portion of those who plundered you and an inheritance for those who inherited you.

## Chapter 18

Isaiah 18:1 Woe, wings of a land of ships beyond rivers of Ethiopia,
Isaiah 18:2 the one sending hostages on the sea and papyrus letters upon the water; for swift messengers will go to a lofty nation and a strange and harsh people—who is beyond it?—a hopeless and trampled nation. Now the rivers of the land,
Isaiah 18:3 all like an inhabited country; their country will be inhabited; as though a sign is raised from a mountain, like the sound of a trumpet it will be audible.
Isaiah 18:4 Because thus the Lord said to me, There will be security in my city like the light of midday heat, and it will be like a cloud of dew on a harvest day.
Isaiah 18:5 Before the harvest, when a flower is completed and an unripe grape flowers a flower, becoming an unripe grape, he will also take away the small clusters with sickles and take away and cut down the vine shoots
Isaiah 18:6 and leave them together to the birds of heaven and to the beasts of the earth, and the birds of heaven will be gathered upon them, and all the beasts of the earth will come upon him.
Isaiah 18:7 At that time gifts will be brought up to the Lord Sabaoth from an afflicted and plucked people and from a great people from now and for eternal time, a hoping and trampled nation, which is in a part of the river of its country, to the place where the name of the Lord Sabaoth was called upon, Mount Sion.

## Chapter 19

Isaiah 19:1 A vision of Egypt. Behold, the Lord sits upon a light cloud and will come into Egypt, and the handmade things of Egypt will be shaken before him, and their heart will be defeated within them.
Isaiah 19:2 And Egyptians will be raised against Egyptians, and a human will war against his brother and a human against his neighbor, city against city and district against district.
Isaiah 19:3 And the spirit of the Egyptians will be troubled within them, and I will scatter their counsel, and they will inquire of their gods and their images and those speaking from the earth and the ventriloquists.
Isaiah 19:4 And I will deliver Egypt into the hands of humans, harsh masters, and harsh kings will rule them; thus says the Lord Sabaoth.
Isaiah 19:5 And the Egyptians will drink the water beside the sea, but the river will fail and dry up;
Isaiah 19:6 and the rivers and the channels of the river will fail, and every gathering of water will dry up, also in every marsh of reed and papyrus;
Isaiah 19:7 and all the green achi around the river and everything sown through the river will dry up, destroyed by wind.
Isaiah 19:8 And the fishermen will groan, and all those casting a hook into the river will groan, and those casting dragnets and those casting nets will mourn.
Isaiah 19:9 And shame will seize those working the split flax and those working the fine linen,
Isaiah 19:10 and those warping them will be in pain, and all those making beer will be grieved and suffer in their souls.
Isaiah 19:11 And the rulers of Tanis will be foolish; the wise counselors of the king—their counsel will be made foolish. How will you say to the king, We are sons of intelligent ones, sons of kings from the beginning?
Isaiah 19:12 Where are your wise ones now? And let them announce to you and say what the Lord Sabaoth has counseled against Egypt.
Isaiah 19:13 The rulers of Tanis failed, and the rulers of Memphis were exalted, and they will lead Egypt astray by tribes.
Isaiah 19:14 For the Lord mixed for them a spirit of wandering, and they led Egypt astray in all their works, as one who is drunk and vomiting together wanders.
Isaiah 19:15 And there will be no work for the Egyptians which will make head and tail, beginning and end.
Isaiah 19:16 But on that day the Egyptians will be like women in fear and trembling before the hand of the Lord Sabaoth which he himself will lay upon them.
Isaiah 19:17 And the country of the Ioudaians will be a terror to the Egyptians; everyone who may name it to them—they will fear because of the counsel which the Lord has counseled against her. —
Isaiah 19:18 On that day there will be five cities in Egypt speaking in the Chanaanite tongue and swearing by the name of the Lord; the one city will be called City-Asedek. —
Isaiah 19:19 On that day there will be an altar to the Lord in the country of the Egyptians and a pillar toward her boundary to the Lord,
Isaiah 19:20 and it will be a sign forever to the Lord in the country of Egypt, because they will cry out to the Lord because of those afflicting them, and the Lord will send them a human who will save them; judging, he will save them.
Isaiah 19:21 And the Lord will be known to the Egyptians, and the Egyptians will know the Lord on that day and make sacrifices and vow vows to the Lord and pay them.
Isaiah 19:22 And the Lord will strike the Egyptians with a great blow and heal them with healing, and they will turn to the Lord, and he will listen to them and heal them. —
Isaiah 19:23 On that day there will be a road from Egypt to the Assyrians, and Assyrians will enter Egypt, and Egyptians will go to the Assyrians, and the Egyptians will serve the Assyrians. —
Isaiah 19:24 On that day Israel will be third among the Assyrians and among the Egyptians, blessed in the land,
Isaiah 19:25 which the Lord Sabaoth blessed, saying, Blessed is my people in Egypt and among the Assyrians and my inheritance Israel.

## Chapter 20

Isaiah 20:1 In the year when Tanathan entered Azotos, when he was sent by Arna king of the Assyrians and warred against Azotos and seized her,
Isaiah 20:2 then the Lord spoke to Esaias, saying, Go and take away the sackcloth from your waist and unfasten your sandals from your feet; and he did thus, going naked and barefoot.
Isaiah 20:3 And the Lord said, In the manner that Esaias my servant has gone naked and barefoot three years, there will be signs and wonders for the Egyptians and Ethiopians;
Isaiah 20:4 because thus the king of the Assyrians will lead the captivity of Egypt and of the Ethiopians, young men and elders, naked and barefoot, uncovered—the shame of Egypt.
Isaiah 20:5 And the Egyptians will be ashamed, defeated, over the Ethiopians in whom the Egyptians had been trusting, for they were a glory to them.
Isaiah 20:6 And those dwelling on this island will say, Behold, we had been trusting in fleeing to them for help, who were not able to be saved from the king of the Assyrians; and how will we be saved?

## Chapter 21

Isaiah 21:1 The vision of the desert. As a tempest might pass through a desert, coming from a desert, from a land, fearful
Isaiah 21:2 and harsh was the vision announced to me. The one setting aside sets aside; the one acting lawlessly acts lawlessly. Against me are the Ailamites, and the elders of the Persians come against me. Now I will groan and comfort myself.
Isaiah 21:3 Therefore my waist was filled with weakness, and pangs took me like a woman giving birth; I did wrong so as not to hear; I was eager not to see.
Isaiah 21:4 My heart wanders, and lawlessness immerses me; my soul has come to fear.
Isaiah 21:5 Prepare the table; drink, eat; rising, rulers, prepare shields.
Isaiah 21:6 Because thus the Lord said to me, Going, station a watchman for yourself and announce whatever you see;
Isaiah 21:7 and I saw riders, two horsemen, a rider of a donkey and a rider of a camel. Listen with much listening,
Isaiah 21:8 and call Ourias to the Lord's lookout. And he said, I stood continually by day, and I stood at the encampment the whole night,
Isaiah 21:9 and behold, he himself comes, a rider of a pair of horses. And answering, he said, Babylon has fallen, and all her images and her handmade things were shattered to the earth.
Isaiah 21:10 Hear, those left and those suffering pain; hear what I heard from the Lord Sabaoth; the God of Israel announced it to us.
Isaiah 21:11 The vision of Idoumaia. To me he calls from Seir, Guard the battlements.
Isaiah 21:12 I guard the morning and the night; if you seek, seek and dwell with me;
Isaiah 21:13 in the wood at evening you will sleep on the road of Daidan.
Isaiah 21:14 Bring water to meet a thirsty one, those dwelling in the country of Thaiman; meet the fugitives with bread,
Isaiah 21:15 because of the multitude of those fleeing and because of the multitude of those wandering and because of the multitude of the sword and because of the multitude of the drawn bows and because of the multitude of those fallen in the war.
Isaiah 21:16 Because thus the Lord said to me, Yet a year, like a hired worker's year, and the glory of the sons of Kedar will cease,
Isaiah 21:17 and the remainder of the bows of the strong sons of Kedar will be few, because the Lord, the God of Israel, spoke.

## Chapter 22

Isaiah 22:1 The utterance of the ravine of Sion. What happened to you now, that you all went up to roofs,
Isaiah 22:2 empty ones? The city was filled with those shouting; your wounded are not wounded by a sword, nor are your dead dead in war.
Isaiah 22:3 All your rulers have fled, and those captured are harshly bound, and the strong among you have fled far away.
Isaiah 22:4 Therefore I said, Leave me; I will weep bitterly; do not strive to comfort me over the destruction of the daughter of my race.
Isaiah 22:5 Because it is a day of trouble and destruction and trampling and wandering from the Lord Sabaoth in the ravine of Sion; they wander from small to great; they wander upon the mountains.
Isaiah 22:6 And the Ailamites took quivers, humans riding upon horses and a gathering of a battle formation.
Isaiah 22:7 And it shall be that your chosen ravines will be filled with chariots, and the horsemen will block your gates;
Isaiah 22:8 and they will uncover the gates of Iouda and look on that day toward the chosen houses of the city,
Isaiah 22:9 and they will uncover the hidden things of the houses of the citadel of David. And they saw that they are more numerous and that they turned the water of the old pool into the city
Isaiah 22:10 and that they pulled down the houses of Ierusalem for a fortification of the wall for the city.
Isaiah 22:11 And you made water for yourselves between the two walls, inward of the old pool, and you did not look toward the one who made her from the beginning and did not see the one who created her.
Isaiah 22:12 And the Lord Sabaoth called on that day for weeping and beating and shaving and girding with sackcloth,
Isaiah 22:13 but they made gladness and exultation, slaughtering calves and sacrificing sheep so as to eat meat and drink wine, saying, Let us eat and drink, for tomorrow we die.
Isaiah 22:14 And these things have been uncovered in the ears of the Lord Sabaoth, that this sin will not be forgiven you until you die.
Isaiah 22:15 Thus says the Lord Sabaoth, Go into the temple chamber to Somnas the treasurer and say to him,
Isaiah 22:16 What are you here, and what is there for you here, that you hewed yourself a tomb here and made yourself a tomb in a high place and inscribed yourself a tent in a rock?
Isaiah 22:17 Behold indeed, the Lord Sabaoth will cast out and crush a man and take away your robe
Isaiah 22:18 and your glorious crown and throw you into a great and immeasurable country, and there you will die; and he will put your beautiful chariot into dishonor and your ruler's house into trampling,
Isaiah 22:19 and you will be removed from your stewardship and from your station.
Isaiah 22:20 And it shall be on that day that I will call my servant Eliakim, the son of Chelkias,
Isaiah 22:21 and clothe him in your robe and give him your crown, and I will give your might and stewardship into his hands, and he will be like a father to those dwelling in Ierusalem and those dwelling in Iouda.
Isaiah 22:22 And I will give him the glory of David, and he will rule, and there will be no one contradicting.
Isaiah 22:23 And I will station him as ruler in a faithful place, and he will be a throne of glory for the house of his father.
Isaiah 22:24 And every glorious one in the house of his father will be trusting in him, from small to great, and they will be hanging upon him.
Isaiah 22:25 On that day—thus says the Lord Sabaoth—the human established in a faithful place will be moved and will fall, and the glory upon him will be taken away, because the Lord spoke.

## Chapter 23

Isaiah 23:1 The vision of Tyre. Wail, ships of Carthage, because she perished, and they no longer come from the land of the Kitiaians; she has been led captive.
Isaiah 23:2 To whom have those dwelling on the island become like, merchants of Phoinike crossing the sea
Isaiah 23:3 in much water, seed of merchants? Like a harvest being brought in are the merchants of the nations.
Isaiah 23:4 Be ashamed, Sidon, the sea said; and the strength of the sea said, I did not labor in birth or give birth or rear young men or raise up virgins.
Isaiah 23:5 But when it becomes heard in Egypt, pain will seize them concerning Tyre.
Isaiah 23:6 Go away into Carthage; wail, those dwelling on this island.
Isaiah 23:7 Was this not your insolence from the beginning, before she was delivered over?
Isaiah 23:8 Who counseled these things against Tyre? Is she inferior or without strength? Her merchants are glorious, rulers of the earth.
Isaiah 23:9 The Lord Sabaoth counseled to loosen all the insolence of the glorious ones and dishonor every glorious thing upon the earth.
Isaiah 23:10 Work your land, for ships no longer come from Carthage either.
Isaiah 23:11 And your hand no longer has strength over the sea, the one provoking kings; the Lord Sabaoth commanded concerning Chanaan to destroy her strength.
Isaiah 23:12 And they will say, You will certainly no longer continue to act insolently and wrong the daughter of Sidon; and if you go away to the Kitieis, not even there will there be rest for you;
Isaiah 23:13 and into the land of the Chaldeans—this too has been desolated by the Assyrians—not even there will there be rest for you, because her wall has fallen.
Isaiah 23:14 Wail, ships of Carthage, because your stronghold perished.
Isaiah 23:15 And it shall be on that day that Tyre will be abandoned seventy years, like the time of a king, like the time of a human; and it shall be after seventy years that Tyre will be like a prostitute's song:
Isaiah 23:16 Take a lyre, wander cities, forgotten prostitute; play the lyre well, sing much, so that a remembrance of you may come to be.
