Isaiah 23:17 And it shall be after seventy years that God will make a visitation of Tyre, and she will again be restored to the former state and will be a trading place for all the kingdoms of the inhabited world.
Isaiah 23:18 And her trade and wage will be holy to the Lord; it will not be gathered for themselves, but all her trade will be for those dwelling before the Lord, to eat and drink and be filled, for a contribution, a memorial before the Lord.

## Chapter 24

Isaiah 24:1 Behold, the Lord destroys the inhabited world and will desolate her and uncover her face and scatter those dwelling in her.
Isaiah 24:2 And the people will be like the priest, and the servant like the master, and the maidservant like the mistress; the buyer will be like the seller, and the lender like the borrower, and the debtor like the one to whom he owes.
Isaiah 24:3 With destruction the earth will be destroyed, and with plunder the earth will be plundered; for the mouth of the Lord spoke these things.
Isaiah 24:4 The earth mourned, and the inhabited world was destroyed; the lofty of the earth mourned.
Isaiah 24:5 But the earth acted lawlessly because of those dwelling in her, because they transgressed the law and changed the ordinances, an eternal covenant.
Isaiah 24:6 Therefore a curse will eat the earth, because those dwelling in her sinned; therefore those dwelling in the earth will be poor, and few humans will be left.
Isaiah 24:7 Wine will mourn, a vine will mourn, all those gladdening the soul will groan.
Isaiah 24:8 The gladness of drums has ceased, the self-will and wealth of the impious have ceased, the sound of a lyre has ceased.
Isaiah 24:9 They were ashamed; they did not drink wine; sikera became bitter to those drinking.
Isaiah 24:10 Every city was desolated; he will shut a house so that no one enters.
Isaiah 24:11 Wail concerning the wine everywhere; all the gladness of the earth has ceased.
Isaiah 24:12 And cities will be left desolate, and abandoned houses will perish.
Isaiah 24:13 All these things will be in the earth in the midst of the nations; in the manner that someone gleans an olive tree, thus they will glean them, and if the vintage ceases.
Isaiah 24:14 These will cry out with a voice, and those left upon the earth will be glad together with the glory of the Lord. The water of the sea will be troubled;
Isaiah 24:15 therefore the glory of the Lord will be in the islands of the sea; the name of the Lord will be glorious: Lord, the God of Israel.
Isaiah 24:16 From the wings of the earth we heard wonders: Hope for the pious. And they will say, Woe to those setting aside, those setting aside the law.
Isaiah 24:17 Fear and pit and snare are upon you who dwell upon the earth;
Isaiah 24:18 and it shall be that the one fleeing fear will fall into the pit, and the one coming out of the pit will be captured by the snare, because windows from heaven were opened, and the foundations of the earth will be shaken.
Isaiah 24:19 With trouble the earth will be troubled, and with perplexity the earth will be perplexed;
Isaiah 24:20 the earth inclined and will be shaken like a fruit watchman's hut, like one drunk and hung over, and will fall and certainly not be able to rise, for lawlessness prevailed upon her.
Isaiah 24:21 And God will bring the hand upon the adornment of heaven and upon the kings of the earth;
Isaiah 24:22 and they will gather and shut them into a stronghold and into a prison; after many generations there will be a visitation of them.
Isaiah 24:23 And the brick will melt, and the wall will fall, because the Lord will reign in Sion and in Ierusalem and will be glorified before the elders.

## Chapter 25

Isaiah 25:1 Lord my God, I will glorify you, I will hymn your name, because you did wonderful deeds, an ancient true counsel; may it be, Lord.
Isaiah 25:2 Because you made cities into a mound, strong cities so that their foundations fall; a city of the impious will certainly not be built forever.
Isaiah 25:3 Therefore the poor people will bless you, and cities of humans being wronged will bless you;
Isaiah 25:4 for you became a helper to every humble city and a shelter to those discouraged because of want; you will rescue them from evil humans, a shelter for the thirsty and a breath for humans being wronged.
Isaiah 25:5 They will bless you like fainthearted humans thirsting in Sion because of impious humans to whom you delivered us.
Isaiah 25:6 And the Lord Sabaoth will do it for all the nations upon this mountain. They will drink gladness, they will drink wine, they will anoint themselves with ointment.
Isaiah 25:7 On this mountain deliver all these things to the nations; for this counsel is against all the nations.
Isaiah 25:8 Death swallowed, having prevailed, and again God took away every tear from every face; he took away the reproach of the people from all the earth, for the mouth of the Lord spoke.
Isaiah 25:9 And they will say on that day, Behold, our God in whom we hoped and exulted, and we will be glad at our salvation.
Isaiah 25:10 Because God will give rest upon this mountain, and Moabitis will be trampled, in the manner that they tread a threshing floor with wagons;
Isaiah 25:11 and he will relax his hands, in the manner that he himself also humbled to destroy, and he will humble his insolence over the things on which he laid his hands;
Isaiah 25:12 and he will humble the height of the refuge of your wall, and it will go down as far as the ground.

## Chapter 26

Isaiah 26:1 On that day they will sing this song upon the land of Iouda, saying, Behold, a strong city, and our salvation will set a wall and an outer wall.
Isaiah 26:2 Open gates; let a people enter, guarding righteousness and guarding truth,
Isaiah 26:3 upholding truth and guarding peace. Because in you
Isaiah 26:4 they hoped, Lord, forever, the great, eternal God,
Isaiah 26:5 who, humbling, brought down those dwelling in lofty places; you will cast down strong cities and bring them down as far as the ground,
Isaiah 26:6 and feet of gentle and humble ones will tread them.
Isaiah 26:7 The way of the pious became straight, and the way of the pious is prepared.
Isaiah 26:8 For the way of the Lord is judgment; we hoped in your name and in the remembrance
Isaiah 26:9 which our soul desires. From night my spirit rises early toward you, God, because your ordinances are light upon the earth. Learn righteousness, those dwelling upon the earth.
Isaiah 26:10 For the impious one has ceased; he will certainly not learn righteousness upon the earth; he will certainly not do truth; let the impious one be taken away so that he may not see the glory of the Lord.
Isaiah 26:11 Lord, your arm is raised, and they did not know, but knowing, they will be ashamed; zeal will seize an undisciplined people, and now fire will eat the adversaries. —
Isaiah 26:12 Lord our God, give us peace, for you repaid everything to us.
Isaiah 26:13 Lord our God, acquire us; Lord, apart from you we do not know another; we name your name.
Isaiah 26:14 But the dead will certainly not see life, nor will physicians raise them; therefore you brought upon them and destroyed and took away every male of theirs.
Isaiah 26:15 Add evils to them, Lord; add evils to all the glorious ones of the earth.
Isaiah 26:16 Lord, in affliction I remembered you; in little affliction your discipline was for us.
Isaiah 26:17 And as a woman in labor draws near to giving birth and cried out in her labor, thus we became to your beloved because of your fear, Lord.
Isaiah 26:18 We conceived in the womb and labored and gave birth; we made a spirit of your salvation upon the earth, but those dwelling upon the earth will fall.
Isaiah 26:19 The dead will rise, and those in the tombs will be raised, and those in the earth will be glad; for the dew from you is healing for them, but the earth of the impious will fall. —
Isaiah 26:20 Go, my people, enter your chambers, shut your door, hide yourself a little, a very little, until the wrath of the Lord passes;
Isaiah 26:21 for behold, the Lord from the holy place brings wrath upon those dwelling upon the earth, and the earth will uncover her blood and will not cover those killed.

## Chapter 27

Isaiah 27:1 On that day God will bring the holy and great and strong sword upon the dragon, a fleeing snake, upon the dragon, a crooked snake, and will kill the dragon.
Isaiah 27:2 On that day a beautiful vineyard; a desire to lead a song against her.
Isaiah 27:3 I am a strong city, a city under siege; in vain I will water her; for she will be captured by night, and by day the wall will fall.
Isaiah 27:4 There is none that did not take hold of her; who will set me to guard stubble in a field? Because of this hostility I rejected her. Therefore because of this the Lord God did everything that he ordered. I have been burned up,
Isaiah 27:5 those dwelling in her will cry out, Let us make peace with him, let us make peace.
Isaiah 27:6 Those coming, children of Iakob—Israel will sprout and blossom, and the inhabited world will be filled with his fruit.
Isaiah 27:7 Will he not be struck thus, as he himself struck, and be killed thus, as he himself killed?
Isaiah 27:8 Fighting and reproaching, he will send them away; were you not the one meditating with a harsh spirit to kill them with a spirit of fury?
Isaiah 27:9 Therefore the lawlessness of Iakob will be taken away, and this is his blessing, when I take away his sin, when they make all the stones of the altars chopped up like fine dust; and their trees will certainly not remain, and their idols cut down like a wood far away.
Isaiah 27:10 The inhabited flock will be abandoned like a flock left behind; and it will be for a long time for grazing, and there they will rest.
Isaiah 27:11 And after a time there will not be anything green in her, because of drying up. Women coming from a spectacle, come; for it is not a people having understanding; therefore the one who made them will certainly not pity, nor will the one who formed them have mercy.
Isaiah 27:12 And it shall be on that day that the Lord will close up from the channel of the river as far as Rhinokoroura, but you gather the sons of Israel one by one.
Isaiah 27:13 And it shall be on that day that they will trumpet with the great trumpet, and those lost in the country of the Assyrians and those lost in Egypt will come and worship the Lord upon the holy mountain in Ierusalem.

## Chapter 28

Isaiah 28:1 Woe to the crown of insolence, the hired workers of Ephraim; the flower fallen from glory upon the summit of the fertile mountain, those drunk without wine.
Isaiah 28:2 Behold, the fury of the Lord is strong and harsh, like hail borne down without shelter, borne down violently; like a great multitude of water dragging a country, it will make rest on the earth for the hands.
Isaiah 28:3 And the crown of insolence, the hired workers of Ephraim, will be trampled by the feet.
Isaiah 28:4 And the flower fallen from the hope of glory upon the top of the high mountain will be like an early fig; the one seeing it will desire to swallow it before taking it into his hand.
Isaiah 28:5 On that day the Lord Sabaoth will be the crown of hope, the woven crown of glory, for my people left behind;
Isaiah 28:6 they will be left with a spirit of judgment for judgment and strength, he preventing killing. —
Isaiah 28:7 For these have been led astray by wine; they were led astray because of sikera; priest and prophet were astounded because of wine; they were shaken by the drunkenness of sikera; they were led astray; this is an apparition.
Isaiah 28:8 A curse will eat this counsel; for this counsel is for the sake of greed.
Isaiah 28:9 To whom did we announce evils, and to whom did we announce a message, those weaned from milk, those drawn away from a breast?
Isaiah 28:10 Expect affliction upon affliction, hope upon hope, yet a little, yet a little,
Isaiah 28:11 because of contempt of lips, through another tongue, because they will speak to this people,
Isaiah 28:12 saying to it, This is the resting place for the hungry, and this the destruction, and they did not desire to hear.
Isaiah 28:13 And the utterance of the Lord God will be for them affliction upon affliction, hope upon hope, yet a little, yet a little, so that they may go and fall backward, and they will be endangered and shattered and captured. —
Isaiah 28:14 Therefore hear a word of the Lord, afflicted men and rulers of this people in Ierusalem:
Isaiah 28:15 Because you said, We made a covenant with Hades and agreements with death; if a borne tempest passes, it will certainly not come upon us; we made falsehood our hope, and we will be sheltered by falsehood,
Isaiah 28:16 therefore thus says the Lord, Behold, I will cast into the foundations of Sion a costly, chosen, precious cornerstone into her foundations, and the one believing in it will certainly not be put to shame.
Isaiah 28:17 And I will make judgment into hope, and my mercy into weights, and those trusting vainly in falsehood; because a tempest will certainly not pass you by,
Isaiah 28:18 will it not also take away your covenant of death? And your hope toward Hades will certainly not endure; if a borne tempest comes upon you, you will be for its trampling.
Isaiah 28:19 When it passes, it will take you; morning by morning it will pass by day, and by night there will be an evil hope; learn to hear.
Isaiah 28:20 Being confined, we cannot fight, and we ourselves are too weak for us to be gathered.
Isaiah 28:21 Like a mountain of impious ones he will rise and be in the ravine of Gabaon; with fury he will do his works, a work of bitterness; but his fury will act strangely, and his bitterness is strange.
Isaiah 28:22 And do not be glad, nor let your bonds grow strong, because I heard completed and cut-short deeds from the Lord Sabaoth which he will do upon all the earth.
Isaiah 28:23 Give ear and hear my voice; pay attention and hear my words.
Isaiah 28:24 Is the one plowing going to plow all day? Or will he prepare seed before working the earth?
Isaiah 28:25 Is it not when he levels her face that he then sows a little black cumin and cumin, and again sows wheat and barley and spelt in your boundaries?
Isaiah 28:26 And you will be disciplined by your God's judgment and be glad.
Isaiah 28:27 For black cumin is not cleansed with harshness, nor will a wagon wheel go around upon cumin, but black cumin is shaken out with a rod, and cumin
Isaiah 28:28 will be eaten with bread. For I will not be angry with you forever, nor will the voice of my bitterness trample you.
Isaiah 28:29 And these wonders came forth from the Lord Sabaoth; take counsel; exalt vain encouragement.

## Chapter 29

Isaiah 29:1 Woe, city Ariel, against which David warred; gather produce year upon year, for you will eat with Moab.
Isaiah 29:2 For I will oppress Ariel, and her strength and wealth will be mine.
Isaiah 29:3 And I will encircle you like David and cast a palisade around you and set towers around you,
Isaiah 29:4 and your words will be humbled to the earth, and your words will sink into the earth; and your voice will be like those speaking from the earth, and your voice will weaken toward the ground.
Isaiah 29:5 And the wealth of the impious will be like dust from a wheel and like borne chaff, and it will be like a moment, immediately,
Isaiah 29:6 from the Lord Sabaoth; for there will be a visitation with thunder and shaking and a great voice, a borne tempest and a devouring flame of fire.
Isaiah 29:7 And the wealth of all the nations, all who campaigned against Ariel, and all those campaigning against Ierusalem and all those gathered against her and afflicting her, will be like one dreaming in sleep.
Isaiah 29:8 And they will be like those drinking and eating in sleep, and when they rise, their dream is empty, and in the manner that the thirsty one dreams as though drinking and, rising, still thirsts, and his soul hoped in emptiness, thus will be the wealth of all the nations, all who campaigned against Mount Sion.
Isaiah 29:9 Grow weak and be astounded and be hung over, not from sikera or from wine;
Isaiah 29:10 because the Lord has given you a spirit of stupor to drink and will shut their eyes and those of their prophets and their rulers, those seeing hidden things.
Isaiah 29:11 And all these utterances will be for you like the words of this sealed book, which, if they give it to a human knowing letters, saying, Read these things, he will also say, I cannot read, for it has been sealed.
Isaiah 29:12 And this book will be given into the hands of a human not knowing letters, and he will say to him, Read this; and he will say, I do not know letters.
Isaiah 29:13 And the Lord said, This people draws near to me; with their lips they honor me, but their heart is far away from me, and in vain they revere me, teaching human commands and teachings.
Isaiah 29:14 Therefore behold, I will proceed to transfer this people and will transfer them and destroy the wisdom of the wise and hide the understanding of the intelligent.
Isaiah 29:15 Woe to those making counsel deeply and not through the Lord; woe to those making counsel in secret, and their works will be in darkness, and they will say, Who has seen us, and who will know us or what we do?
Isaiah 29:16 Will you not be reckoned as the potter's clay? Will the thing formed say to the one forming it, You did not form me? Or the thing made to the one making it, You did not make me intelligently?
Isaiah 29:17 Is it not yet a little while, and Lebanon will be transferred like Mount Chermel, and Mount Chermel will be reckoned as a wood?
Isaiah 29:18 And on that day deaf ones will hear words of a book, and in darkness and in gloom the eyes of blind ones will see;
Isaiah 29:19 and poor ones will exult because of the Lord in gladness, and the hopeless among humans will be filled with gladness.
Isaiah 29:20 A lawless one failed, and a proud one perished, and those acting lawlessly in wickedness were destroyed,
Isaiah 29:21 and those making humans sin with a word; and they will make all those reproving in gates a stumbling block, and they turned aside a righteous one among unjust things.
Isaiah 29:22 Therefore thus says the Lord concerning the house of Iakob, whom he separated from Abraam, Iakob will not now be ashamed, nor will Israel now change his face;
Isaiah 29:23 but when their children see my works, because of me they will sanctify my name and sanctify the Holy One of Iakob and fear the God of Israel.
Isaiah 29:24 And those wandering in spirit will know understanding, and those grumbling will learn to obey, and stammering tongues will learn to speak peace.

## Chapter 30

Isaiah 30:1 Woe, rebellious children, thus says the Lord, you made counsel not through me and agreements not through my spirit, to add sins upon sins,
Isaiah 30:2 those going to go down into Egypt, but they did not inquire of me, to be helped by Pharao and sheltered by Egyptians.
Isaiah 30:3 For the shelter of Pharao will become shame for you, and reproach for those trusting in Egypt.
Isaiah 30:4 Because in Tanis there are leaders, evil messengers; in vain they will labor
Isaiah 30:5 toward a people which will not benefit them, neither for help nor for benefit, but for shame and reproach.
Isaiah 30:6 The vision of the four-footed animals in the desert. In affliction and confinement, a lion and a lion's cub from there, and asps and offspring of flying asps, who carried their wealth upon donkeys and camels toward a nation which will not benefit them for help, but for shame and reproach.
Isaiah 30:7 Egyptians will benefit you with vain and empty things; announce to them that, This encouragement of yours is vain.
Isaiah 30:8 Now therefore, sitting, write these things on a tablet and in a book, because these things will be for days of times and forever.
Isaiah 30:9 Because it is a disobedient people, false sons, who did not desire to hear the law of God,
Isaiah 30:10 those saying to the prophets, Do not announce to us, and to those seeing the visions, Do not speak to us, but speak to us and announce to us another wandering,
Isaiah 30:11 and turn us away from this way; take this path away from us and take the Holy One of Israel away from us.
Isaiah 30:12 Therefore thus says the Lord, the Holy One of Israel, Because you disobeyed these words and hoped in falsehood and because you grumbled and became trusting in this word,
Isaiah 30:13 therefore this sin will be for you like a wall falling immediately, of a strong city captured, whose fall is immediately present,
Isaiah 30:14 and her fall will be like the shattering of an earthen vessel, small pieces from a jar, so as not to find among them a shard in which you will lift fire and in which you will draw a little water.
Isaiah 30:15 Thus says the Lord, the Holy One of Israel, When you turn back and groan, then you will be saved and know where you were; when you had trusted in vain things, your strength became vain. And you did not desire to hear,
Isaiah 30:16 but said, We will flee upon horses; therefore you will flee; and you said, Upon swift ones we will be riders; therefore those pursuing you will be swift.
Isaiah 30:17 Because of the voice of one, a thousand will flee, and because of the voice of five, many will flee, until you are left like a mast on a mountain and like one bearing a banner on a hill.
Isaiah 30:18 And again God will wait to pity you, and therefore he will be exalted to have mercy on you, because the Lord our God is a judge, and where will you leave your glory? Blessed are those abiding in him.
Isaiah 30:19 Because a holy people will dwell in Sion, and Ierusalem wept with weeping, Have mercy on me; he will have mercy on you at the voice of your cry; when he saw, he listened to you.
Isaiah 30:20 And the Lord will give you bread of affliction and scant water, and those leading you astray will certainly no longer draw near you, because your eyes will see those leading you astray,
Isaiah 30:21 and your ears will hear the words of those who led you astray from behind, those saying, This is the way; let us go in it, whether right or left.
Isaiah 30:22 And you will remove the silver-covered and gold-covered idols; you will make them small and winnow them like the fluid of a menstruating woman and push them away like dung.
Isaiah 30:23 Then there will be rain for the seed of your land, and the bread of the produce of your land will be abundant and rich; and your livestock will graze on that day in a fertile and spacious place;
Isaiah 30:24 your bulls and the oxen working the earth will eat straw prepared with barley, winnowed.
Isaiah 30:25 And there will be water passing through upon every high mountain and upon every lofty hill on that day, when many perish and when towers fall.
Isaiah 30:26 And the light of the moon will be like the light of the sun, and the light of the sun will be sevenfold on the day when the Lord heals the destruction of his people, and he will heal the pain of your wound.
Isaiah 30:27 Behold, the name of the Lord comes after a long time, the fury burning, the utterance of his lips with glory, the utterance full of wrath, and the wrath of fury will eat like fire.
Isaiah 30:28 And his spirit will come like water dragging in a ravine, as far as the neck, and will be divided to trouble nations in vain wandering, and wandering will pursue them and seize them before their face.
Isaiah 30:29 Must you not continually be glad and enter my holy places continually as though celebrating a festival and as though rejoicing to enter with a pipe into the mountain of the Lord toward the God of Israel?
Isaiah 30:30 And God will make the glory of his voice audible and show the fury of his arm with fury and wrath and a devouring flame; he will thunder violently, and like water and hail borne down together violently.
Isaiah 30:31 For because of the voice of the Lord the Assyrians will be defeated by the blow with which he strikes them.
Isaiah 30:32 And it will be around him, from where his hope of help was, in which he himself had trusted; they themselves with pipes and lyre will war against him in a reversal.
Isaiah 30:33 For you will be called to account before days; was it not also prepared for you to reign over a deep ravine, wood lying there, fire and much wood? The fury of the Lord is like a ravine burning with sulfur.

## Chapter 31

Isaiah 31:1 Woe to those going down into Egypt for help, those trusting in horses and in chariots, for they are many, and in horses, a very great multitude, and they had not been trusting in the Holy One of Israel and did not seek God.
Isaiah 31:2 And he himself, wise, brought evils upon them, and his word will certainly not be set aside, and he will rise against houses of evil humans and against their vain hope,
Isaiah 31:3 an Egyptian human and not a god, horses' flesh, and there is no help; but the Lord will bring his hand upon them, and those helping will grow weary, and all together will perish.
Isaiah 31:4 Because thus the Lord said to me, In the manner that a lion or a cub cries out over the prey which it took and cries over it until the mountains are filled with its voice, and they were defeated and frightened by the abundance of fury, thus the Lord Sabaoth will go down to campaign against Mount Sion, against her mountains.
Isaiah 31:5 Like flying birds, thus the Lord will shield Ierusalem and deliver and preserve and save.
Isaiah 31:6 Turn back, those counseling the deep and lawless counsel.
Isaiah 31:7 Because on that day humans will renounce their silver and gold handmade things which their hands made.
Isaiah 31:8 And Assour will fall; no sword of a man or sword of a human will devour him, and he will flee, not before a sword; and the young men will become a defeat,
Isaiah 31:9 for they will be enclosed by a rock as by a palisade and be defeated, and the one fleeing will be captured. Thus says the Lord, Blessed is the one who has seed in Sion and household members in Ierusalem.

## Chapter 32

Isaiah 32:1 For behold, a righteous king will reign, and rulers will rule with judgment.
Isaiah 32:2 And the human will be hiding his words and will be hidden as from rushing water; and he will appear in Sion like a rushing river, glorious in a thirsty land.
Isaiah 32:3 And they will no longer be trusting in humans, but will give their ears to hear.
Isaiah 32:4 And the heart of the weak will pay attention to hearing, and stammering tongues will quickly learn to speak peace.
Isaiah 32:5 And they will certainly no longer tell the fool to rule, and your attendants will certainly no longer say, Be silent.
Isaiah 32:6 For the fool will speak foolish things, and his heart will think vain things, to accomplish lawless things and speak wandering against the Lord, to scatter hungry souls and make thirsty souls empty.
Isaiah 32:7 For the counsel of the evil ones will counsel lawless things, to destroy humble ones with unjust words and scatter words of humble ones in judgment.
Isaiah 32:8 But the pious counseled intelligent things, and this counsel will remain.
Isaiah 32:9 Rich women, rise and hear my voice; daughters in hope, hear my words.
Isaiah 32:10 Make remembrance of days of a year in pain with hope; the vintage has been consumed, the sowing has ceased and will certainly no longer come.
Isaiah 32:11 Be astounded, be grieved, confident women; strip yourselves, become naked, gird your waists with sackcloth,
Isaiah 32:12 and beat yourselves upon the breasts because of a desirable field and a fruitful vine.
Isaiah 32:13 The land of my people—thorn and grass will come up, and gladness will be taken away from every house; a rich city,
Isaiah 32:14 abandoned houses will leave the wealth of a city and desirable houses; and the villages will be caves forever, a gladness of wild donkeys, pastures of shepherds,
Isaiah 32:15 until a spirit from on high comes upon you. And Chermel will be desolate, and Chermel will be reckoned as a wood.
Isaiah 32:16 And judgment will rest in the desert, and righteousness will dwell in Karmel;
Isaiah 32:17 and the works of righteousness will be peace, and righteousness will hold rest, and they will be confident forever;
Isaiah 32:18 and his people will dwell in a city of peace and dwell confidently, and they will rest with wealth.
Isaiah 32:19 But if hail goes down, it will not come upon you. And those dwelling in the woods will be confident like those in the plain.
Isaiah 32:20 Blessed are those sowing beside every water, where an ox and a donkey tread.

## Chapter 33

Isaiah 33:1 Woe to those making you miserable, but no one makes you miserable, and the one rejecting you does not reject; those rejecting will be captured and delivered over and defeated thus, like a moth upon a garment.
Isaiah 33:2 Lord, have mercy on us, for in you we have trusted; the seed of the disobedient became destruction, but our salvation is in a time of affliction.
Isaiah 33:3 Because of the voice of your terror, peoples were astounded by your terror, and the nations were scattered.
Isaiah 33:4 But now your spoils will be gathered, of small and great; in the manner that someone gathers locusts, thus they will mock you.
Isaiah 33:5 Holy is God who dwells in lofty places; Sion was filled with judgment and righteousness.
Isaiah 33:6 In law they will be delivered over; our salvation is in treasures; there are wisdom and knowledge and piety toward the Lord; these are treasures of righteousness.
Isaiah 33:7 Behold indeed, at your fear they themselves will fear; those whom you feared will fear because of you; for messengers will be sent requesting peace, weeping bitterly, pleading for peace.
Isaiah 33:8 For their ways will be desolated; the fear of the nations has ceased, and the covenant with these is taken away, and you will certainly not reckon them humans.
Isaiah 33:9 The earth mourned, Lebanon was ashamed, Saron became marshes; Galilaia and Karmel will be manifest.
Isaiah 33:10 Now I will rise, says the Lord, now I will be glorified, now I will be exalted;
Isaiah 33:11 now you will see, now you will perceive; the strength of your spirit will be vain; fire will devour you.
Isaiah 33:12 And nations will be burned up like a thorn thrown in a field and burned up.
Isaiah 33:13 Those far away will hear what I did; those drawing near will know my strength.
Isaiah 33:14 The lawless in Sion departed; trembling will seize the impious; who will announce to you that fire burns? Who will announce to you the eternal place?
Isaiah 33:15 One walking in righteousness, speaking a straight way, hating lawlessness and injustice and shaking his hands free of gifts, making his ears heavy so that he may not hear a judgment of blood, shutting his eyes so that he may not see injustice,
Isaiah 33:16 this one will dwell in a high cave of a strong rock; bread will be given to him, and his water is faithful.
Isaiah 33:17 You will see a king with glory, and your eyes will see a land far away.
Isaiah 33:18 Your soul will meditate on fear; where are the scribes? Where are those counseling? Where is the one counting those being fed,
Isaiah 33:19 a small and great people? To whom they did not give counsel, nor did he know a deep voice so that a despised people did not hear, and there is no understanding for the one hearing.
Isaiah 33:20 Behold Sion, the city, our salvation; your eyes will see Ierusalem, a rich city, tents which will certainly not be shaken, nor will the stakes of her tent be moved for eternal time, nor will her ropes be torn apart.
Isaiah 33:21 Because the name of the Lord is great for you; there will be a place for you, rivers and channels, broad and spacious; you will not go this way, nor will a rowing ship go.
Isaiah 33:22 For my God is great; the Lord will not pass me by; the Lord is our judge, the Lord our ruler, the Lord our king; this one will save us.
Isaiah 33:23 Your ropes were torn because it was not strong; your mast inclined; it will not lower the sails; it will not raise a sign until it is delivered to plunder; therefore many lame ones will make plunder.
Isaiah 33:24 And the people dwelling among them will certainly not say, I am weary; for their sin was forgiven them.

## Chapter 34

Isaiah 34:1 Draw near, nations, and hear, rulers; let the earth and those in her hear, the inhabited world and the people in her.
Isaiah 34:2 Because the fury of the Lord is against all the nations and wrath against their number, to destroy them and deliver them to slaughter.
Isaiah 34:3 And their wounded and dead will be thrown out, and their odor will rise, and the mountains will be wetted by their blood.
Isaiah 34:4 And heaven will be rolled like a book, and all the stars will fall like leaves from a vine and as leaves fall from a fig tree.
Isaiah 34:5 My sword became drunk in heaven; behold, it will go down upon Idoumaia and upon the people of destruction with judgment.
Isaiah 34:6 The sword of the Lord was filled with blood; it grew fat with the fat of lambs and with the fat of male goats and rams, because there is a sacrifice to the Lord in Bosor and a great slaughter in Idoumaia.
Isaiah 34:7 And the stout ones will fall together with them, and the rams and bulls, and the earth will become drunk with blood and be filled with their fat.
Isaiah 34:8 For it is a day of the Lord's judgment and a year of recompense for the judgment of Sion.
Isaiah 34:9 And her ravines will be turned into pitch and her land into sulfur, and her land will be burning like pitch
Isaiah 34:10 night and day and will not be extinguished for eternal time, and her smoke will rise upward; for generations and for a long time she will be desolated.
Isaiah 34:11 And birds and hedgehogs and ibises and ravens will dwell in her, and a measuring cord of desolation will be laid upon her, and donkey-centaurs will dwell in her.
Isaiah 34:12 Her rulers will not be; for her kings and her rulers and her magnates will be for destruction.
Isaiah 34:13 And thorny trees will sprout into their cities and into her strongholds, and she will be a dwelling of sirens and a court of ostriches.
Isaiah 34:14 And demons will meet donkey-centaurs and cry out to one another; there donkey-centaurs will rest, for they found rest for themselves.
Isaiah 34:15 There a hedgehog nested, and the earth saved her children with security; there deer met and saw one another's faces;
Isaiah 34:16 they passed by number, and not one of them perished; one did not seek another; because the Lord commanded them, and his spirit gathered them.
Isaiah 34:17 And he himself will cast lots for them, and his hand divided for grazing; for eternal time you will inherit; for generations of generations they will rest upon her.

## Chapter 35

Isaiah 35:1 Be glad, thirsty desert; let a desert exult and flower like a lily,
Isaiah 35:2 and the deserted places of the Iordan will blossom and exult; and the glory of Lebanon was given to her and the honor of Karmel, and my people will see the glory of the Lord and the height of God.
Isaiah 35:3 Grow strong, slack hands and paralyzed knees;
Isaiah 35:4 give encouragement, those fainthearted in mind; grow strong, do not fear; behold, our God repays judgment and will repay; he himself will come and save us.
Isaiah 35:5 Then eyes of blind ones will be opened, and ears of deaf ones will hear.
Isaiah 35:6 Then the lame one will leap like a deer, and the tongue of those speaking with difficulty will be clear, because water burst forth in the desert and a ravine in a thirsty land,
Isaiah 35:7 and the waterless land will become marshes, and there will be a spring of water in the thirsty land; there will be gladness of birds, a dwelling of reed and marshes.
Isaiah 35:8 There will be a clean way there, and it will be called a holy way, and an unclean one will certainly not pass there, nor will there be an unclean way there; but the scattered ones will go upon it and certainly not wander.
Isaiah 35:9 And there will be no lion there, nor will any of the evil beasts go up upon it or be found there, but redeemed ones will go in it.
Isaiah 35:10 And those gathered because of the Lord will turn back and come into Sion with gladness, and eternal gladness above their head; for upon their head are praise and exultation, and gladness will seize them; pain and grief and groaning fled away.

## Chapter 36

Isaiah 36:1 And it happened in the fourteenth year of Ezekias reigning, Sennacherim king of the Assyrians went up against the strong cities of Ioudaia and took them.
Isaiah 36:2 And the king of the Assyrians sent Rapsakes from Lachis into Ierusalem to King Ezekias with much force, and he stood at the aqueduct of the upper pool on the road of the fuller's field.
Isaiah 36:3 And Eliakim the son of Chelkias, the steward, and Somnas the scribe and Ioach the son of Asaph, the recorder, went out to him.
Isaiah 36:4 And Rapsakes said to them, Say to Ezekias, Thus says the king, the great king of the Assyrians, In what are you trusting?
Isaiah 36:5 Does a battle formation come to be by counsel or words of lips? And now in whom have you trusted, that you disobey me?
Isaiah 36:6 Behold, you are trusting in this broken reed rod, in Egypt; whoever leans upon it, it will enter his hand; thus are Pharao king of Egypt and all those trusting in him.
Isaiah 36:7 But if you say, In the Lord our God we have trusted,
Isaiah 36:8 now make an agreement with my master, the king of the Assyrians, and I will give you two thousand horses, if you will be able to provide riders upon them.
Isaiah 36:9 And how can you turn against the face of one district ruler? Those trusting in Egyptians for horse and rider are servants.
Isaiah 36:10 And now, did we go up against this country to war against her without the Lord?
Isaiah 36:11 And Eliakim and Somnas and Ioach said to him, Speak to your servants in Syrian, for we understand, and do not speak to us in Ioudaian; and why do you speak into the ears of the humans upon the wall?
Isaiah 36:12 And Rapsakes said to them, Has my master sent me to your master or to you to speak these words? Not to the humans sitting upon the wall, so that they may eat dung and drink urine together with you?
Isaiah 36:13 And Rapsakes stood and cried out with a great voice in Ioudaian and said, Hear the words of the king, the great king of the Assyrians:
Isaiah 36:14 Thus says the king, Do not let Ezekias deceive you with words which will not be able to rescue you;
Isaiah 36:15 and do not let Ezekias say to you that, God will rescue you, and this city will certainly not be delivered into the hand of the king of the Assyrians;
Isaiah 36:16 do not listen to Ezekias. Thus says the king of the Assyrians, If you desire to be blessed, come out to me, and each will eat his vine and the fig trees and drink water of your cistern,
Isaiah 36:17 until I come and take you into a land like your land, a land of grain and wine and bread and vineyards.
Isaiah 36:18 Do not let Ezekias deceive you, saying, Your God will rescue you. Did the gods of the nations rescue, each, his own country from the hand of the king of the Assyrians?
Isaiah 36:19 Where is the god of Aimath and Arphath? And where the god of the city Seppharim? Were they able to rescue Samaria from my hand?
Isaiah 36:20 Who among the gods of all these nations rescued his land from my hand, that God will rescue Ierusalem from my hand?
Isaiah 36:21 And they were silent, and no one answered him a word, because the king ordered no one to answer.
Isaiah 36:22 And Eliakim the son of Chelkias, the steward, and Somnas the scribe of the force and Ioach the son of Asaph, the recorder, entered to Ezekias with their tunics torn and announced to him the words of Rapsakes.

## Chapter 37

Isaiah 37:1 And it happened, when King Ezekias heard, he tore his garments and put on sackcloth and went up into the house of the Lord.
Isaiah 37:2 And he sent Eliakim the steward and Somnas the scribe and the elders of the priests, clothed in sackcloth, to Esaias son of Amos, the prophet,
Isaiah 37:3 and they said to him, Thus says Ezekias, Today is a day of affliction and reproach and rebuke and wrath, because the pang has come to the woman giving birth, but she has no strength to give birth.
Isaiah 37:4 May the Lord your God hear the words of Rapsakes, whom the king of the Assyrians sent to reproach a living God and to reproach words which the Lord your God heard; and you will make supplication to the Lord your God concerning these who are left.
Isaiah 37:5 And the servants of the king came to Esaias,
Isaiah 37:6 and Esaias said to them, Thus you will say to your master, Thus says the Lord, Do not fear because of the words which you heard, with which the envoys of the king of the Assyrians reproached me;
Isaiah 37:7 behold, I will cast a spirit into him, and hearing a message he will turn back to his country and fall by a sword in his land.
Isaiah 37:8 And Rapsakes returned and found the king besieging Lomna. And the king of the Assyrians heard that
Isaiah 37:9 Tharaka king of the Ethiopians went out to besiege him; and hearing, he turned back and sent messengers to Ezekias, saying,
Isaiah 37:10 Thus you will say to Ezekias king of Ioudaia, Do not let your God in whom you are trusting deceive you, saying, Ierusalem will certainly not be delivered into the hands of the king of the Assyrians.
Isaiah 37:11 Or did you not hear what the kings of the Assyrians did, how they destroyed all the earth?
Isaiah 37:12 Did the gods of the nations whom my fathers destroyed rescue them, both Gozan and Charran and Raphes, which are in the country of Themad?
Isaiah 37:13 Where are the kings of Aimath and Arphath and of the city Seppharim, Anag, Ougaua? —
Isaiah 37:14 And Ezekias took the document from the messengers and opened it before the Lord,
Isaiah 37:15 and Ezekias prayed to the Lord, saying,
Isaiah 37:16 Lord Sabaoth, the God of Israel, who sits upon the cheroubin, you alone are God of every kingdom of the inhabited world; you made heaven and earth.
Isaiah 37:17 Hear, Lord; look, Lord, and see the words which Sennacherim sent to reproach a living God.
Isaiah 37:18 For in truth the kings of the Assyrians desolated the whole inhabited world and their country
Isaiah 37:19 and cast their idols into the fire, for they were not gods but works of human hands, wood and stones, and they destroyed them.
Isaiah 37:20 But you, Lord our God, save us from their hand, so that every kingdom of the earth may know that you alone are God.
Isaiah 37:21 And Esaias son of Amos was sent to Ezekias and said to him, Thus says the Lord, the God of Israel, I heard what you prayed to me concerning Sennacherim king of the Assyrians.
Isaiah 37:22 This is the word which God spoke concerning him: A virgin daughter of Sion despised you and sneered at you; a daughter of Ierusalem shook a head at you.
Isaiah 37:23 Whom did you reproach and provoke? Or against whom did you lift your voice? And you did not lift your eyes on high toward the Holy One of Israel.
Isaiah 37:24 Because through messengers you reproached the Lord; for you said, With the multitude of chariots I went up to the height of mountains and into the furthest parts of Lebanon and cut the height of its cedar and the beauty of the cypress and entered the height of a part of the wood
Isaiah 37:25 and set a bridge and desolated waters and every gathering of water.
Isaiah 37:26 Did you not hear long ago these things which I did? From ancient days I ordered them, but now I showed the desolating of nations in strongholds and those dwelling in strong cities;
Isaiah 37:27 I relaxed the hands, and they dried up and became like dry grass upon roofs and like wild grass.
Isaiah 37:28 But now I know your rest and your going out and your coming in;
Isaiah 37:29 and your fury with which you were angered and your bitterness rose to me, and I will cast a muzzle into your nose and a bridle into your lips and turn you back by the way in which you came.
Isaiah 37:30 And this is the sign for you: eat this year what you have sown, and in the second year the remnant, and in the third, sowing, reap and plant vineyards and eat their fruit.
Isaiah 37:31 And it shall be that those left in Ioudaia will grow a root below and make seed above.
Isaiah 37:32 Because those left will come out of Ierusalem, and those being saved out of Mount Sion; the zeal of the Lord Sabaoth will do these things.
Isaiah 37:33 Therefore thus says the Lord concerning the king of the Assyrians, He will certainly not enter this city or cast an arrow upon her or lay a shield upon her or encircle her with a palisade,
Isaiah 37:34 but by the way in which he came, by it he will turn back; thus says the Lord.
Isaiah 37:35 I will shield this city to save her because of me and because of David my servant.
Isaiah 37:36 And an angel of the Lord went out and killed one hundred eighty-five thousand from the encampment of the Assyrians, and rising in the morning, they found all the bodies dead.
Isaiah 37:37 And turning back, the king of the Assyrians departed and dwelt in Nineue.
Isaiah 37:38 And while he was worshiping his patachron in the house of Nasarach, Adramelech and Sarasar his sons struck him with swords, and they themselves escaped into Armenia; and Asordan his son reigned in his place.

## Chapter 38

Isaiah 38:1 And it happened at that time that Ezekias became sick unto death; and Esaias son of Amos, the prophet, came to him and said to him, Thus says the Lord, Put your house in order, for you are dying and will not live.
Isaiah 38:2 And Ezekias turned his face toward the wall and prayed to the Lord,
Isaiah 38:3 saying, Remember, Lord, how I walked before you with truth in a true heart and did the pleasing things before you; and Ezekias wept with great weeping.
Isaiah 38:4 And a word of the Lord came to Esaias, saying,
Isaiah 38:5 Go and say to Ezekias, Thus says the Lord, the God of David your father, I heard the voice of your prayer and saw your tears; behold, I add fifteen years to your time;
Isaiah 38:6 and I will save you from the hand of the king of the Assyrians and shield this city.
Isaiah 38:7 And this is the sign for you from the Lord, that God will do this utterance;
Isaiah 38:8 the shadow of the steps which the sun went down, the ten steps of your father's house—I will turn the sun back the ten steps. And the sun went up the ten steps which the shadow went down.
Isaiah 38:9 A prayer of Ezekias king of Ioudaia, when he became sick and rose from his sickness.
Isaiah 38:10 I said, At the height of my days, at the gates of Hades, I will leave the remaining years.
Isaiah 38:11 I said, I will certainly no longer see the salvation of God upon the earth; I will certainly no longer see a human
Isaiah 38:12 from my kinship. I left the remainder of my life; it went out and departed from me like one dismantling a tent which he pitched; my spirit with me became like the web of a weaving woman drawing near to cut it off. On that day I was delivered over
Isaiah 38:13 until morning as to a lion; thus he shattered my bones, for from day until night I was delivered over.
Isaiah 38:14 Like a swallow, thus I will sound, and like a dove, thus I will murmur; for my eyes failed from looking toward the height of heaven, toward the Lord, who delivered me
Isaiah 38:15 and took away the pain of my soul.
Isaiah 38:16 Lord, for concerning her it was announced to you, and you roused my breath, and, comforted, I lived.
Isaiah 38:17 For you chose my soul so that it may not perish, and you cast all my sins behind me.
Isaiah 38:18 For those in Hades will not praise you, nor will those dead bless you, nor will those in Hades hope for your mercy;
Isaiah 38:19 the living will bless you in the manner that I too do. For from today I will make children who will announce your righteousness,
Isaiah 38:20 Lord of my salvation; and I will not cease blessing you with a harp all the days of my life before the house of God.
Isaiah 38:21 And Esaias said to Ezekias, Take a cake of figs and crush it and apply it as a poultice, and you will be healthy.
Isaiah 38:22 And Ezekias said, This is the sign, that I will go up into the house of the Lord God.

## Chapter 39

Isaiah 39:1 At that time Marodach son of Laadan, the king of Babylonia, sent letters and envoys and gifts to Ezekias; for he heard that he became sick unto death and rose.
Isaiah 39:2 And Ezekias rejoiced over them with great joy and showed them the house of the nechotha and of the stacte and of the incenses and of the ointment and of the silver and of the gold, and all the houses of the equipment of the treasury and everything which was in his treasures; and there was nothing which Ezekias did not show in his house.
Isaiah 39:3 And Esaias the prophet came to King Ezekias and said to him, What do these humans say, and from where have they come to you? And Ezekias said, From a land far away they have come to me, from Babylon.
Isaiah 39:4 And Esaias said, What did they see in your house? And Ezekias said, They saw everything in my house, and there is nothing in my house which they did not see, but also the things in my treasures.
Isaiah 39:5 And Esaias said to him, Hear the word of the Lord Sabaoth:
Isaiah 39:6 Behold, days come, says the Lord, and they will take everything in your house, and whatever your fathers gathered until this day will come to Babylon, and they will certainly leave nothing; and God said
Isaiah 39:7 that they will also take from your children whom you begot and make them eunuchs in the house of the king of the Babylonians.
Isaiah 39:8 And Ezekias said to Esaias, Good is the word of the Lord which he spoke; let there indeed be peace and righteousness in my days.

## Chapter 40

Isaiah 40:1 Comfort, comfort my people, says God.
Isaiah 40:2 Priests, speak into the heart of Ierusalem; comfort her, because her humiliation was fulfilled, her sin has been loosed, because she received from the hand of the Lord her sins double.
Isaiah 40:3 A voice of one crying in the desert, Prepare the way of the Lord; make straight the paths of our God;
Isaiah 40:4 every ravine will be filled, and every mountain and hill will be humbled, and all the crooked things will become straight, and the rough way plains;
Isaiah 40:5 and the glory of the Lord will be seen, and all flesh will see the salvation of God, because the Lord spoke.
Isaiah 40:6 A voice of one saying, Cry out; and I said, What shall I cry? All flesh is grass, and all human glory like a flower of grass;
Isaiah 40:7 the grass dried up, and the flower fell,
Isaiah 40:8 but the utterance of our God remains forever.
Isaiah 40:9 Go up upon a high mountain, the one announcing good news to Sion; lift your voice with strength, the one announcing good news to Ierusalem; lift it, do not fear; say to the cities of Iouda, Behold, your God.
Isaiah 40:10 Behold, the Lord comes with strength, and the arm with dominion; behold, his wage is with him and the work before him.
Isaiah 40:11 Like a shepherd he will shepherd his flock and gather lambs with his arm and comfort those having in the womb.
Isaiah 40:12 Who measured the water with the hand and heaven with a span and all the earth with a handful? Who weighed the mountains with a weight and the valleys with a balance?
Isaiah 40:13 Who knew the mind of the Lord, and who became his counselor, who instructs him?
Isaiah 40:14 Or with whom did he take counsel, and who instructed him? Or who showed him judgment? Or who showed him a way of understanding?
Isaiah 40:15 If all the nations were reckoned like a drop from a bucket and like a tilt of a balance, they will also be reckoned like saliva;
Isaiah 40:16 and Lebanon is not sufficient for burning, and all the four-footed animals are not sufficient for a whole burnt offering,
Isaiah 40:17 and all the nations are like nothing and were reckoned as nothing.
Isaiah 40:18 To whom did you liken the Lord, and to what likeness did you liken him?
Isaiah 40:19 Did a craftsman make an image, or did a goldsmith, melting gold, gild him, fashion him as a likeness?
Isaiah 40:20 For a craftsman chooses wood that does not rot and wisely seeks how he will set up his image, and so that it may not be shaken.
Isaiah 40:21 Will you not know? Will you not hear? Was it not announced to you from the beginning? Did you not know the foundations of the earth?
Isaiah 40:22 The one holding the circle of the earth, and those dwelling in her are like locusts, the one setting heaven like a vault and stretching it like a tent to dwell in,
Isaiah 40:23 the one giving rulers nothing to rule, and he made the earth like nothing.
Isaiah 40:24 For they will certainly not sow or plant, nor will their root be rooted into the earth; he blew upon them, and they dried up, and a tempest will take them up like brushwood.
Isaiah 40:25 Now therefore, to whom did you liken me, and I will be exalted? said the Holy One.
Isaiah 40:26 Look up on high with your eyes and see; who showed all these things? The one bringing forth his adornment by number will call all by name; because of much glory and in the might of strength, nothing escaped you.
Isaiah 40:27 For do not say, Iakob—and what did you speak, Israel?—My way was hidden from God, and my God took away the judgment and departed?
Isaiah 40:28 And now, did you not know, if you did not hear? An eternal God is the God who fashioned the ends of the earth; he will not hunger or grow weary, nor is there a searching out of his understanding;
Isaiah 40:29 giving strength to the hungry and grief to those not suffering pain.
Isaiah 40:30 For younger ones will hunger, and young men will grow weary, and chosen ones will be powerless;
Isaiah 40:31 but those waiting for God will exchange strength; they will grow wings like eagles; they will run and not grow weary; they will walk and not hunger.

## Chapter 41

Isaiah 41:1 Be renewed toward me, islands, for the rulers will exchange strength; let them draw near and speak together; then let them announce judgment.
Isaiah 41:2 Who raised righteousness from the east, called her to his feet, and she will go? He will give her before nations and astound kings and put their swords into the earth and their bows like driven-out brushwood;
Isaiah 41:3 and he will pursue them, and the way of his feet will pass through in peace.
Isaiah 41:4 Who worked and did these things? The one calling her from generations of the beginning called her; I am God, first, and for the things coming I am.
Isaiah 41:5 Nations saw and feared; the ends of the earth drew near and came together,
Isaiah 41:6 each judging to help the neighbor and the brother, and he will say,
Isaiah 41:7 A man, a craftsman, grew strong, and a smith striking with a hammer, beating together; at one time he will say, The joint is good; they strengthened them with nails; they will set them, and they will not be moved.
Isaiah 41:8 But you, Israel, my servant Iakob whom I chose, seed of Abraam whom I loved,
Isaiah 41:9 of whom I took hold from the ends of the earth, and from her lookouts I called you and said to you, You are my servant; I chose you and did not abandon you,
Isaiah 41:10 do not fear, for I am with you; do not wander, for I am your God who strengthened you, and I helped you and secured you with my righteous right hand.
Isaiah 41:11 Behold, all those opposing you will be ashamed and abashed; for they will be as though not existing, and all your adversaries will perish.
Isaiah 41:12 You will seek them and certainly not find the humans who will act insolently toward you; for they will be as though not existing, and those warring against you will not be.
Isaiah 41:13 Because I am your God, the one holding your right hand, the one saying to you, Do not fear,
Isaiah 41:14 Iakob, very small Israel; I helped you, says God who redeems you, Israel.
Isaiah 41:15 Behold, I made you like new, saw-shaped threshing wheels of a wagon, and you will thresh mountains and make hills small and turn them into chaff;
Isaiah 41:16 and you will winnow, and wind will take them, and a tempest will scatter them, but you will be glad in the holy ones of Israel. And they will exult,
Isaiah 41:17 the poor and the needy; for they will seek water, and there will be none; their tongue dried up from thirst; I am the Lord God; I will listen, the God of Israel, and will not abandon them,
Isaiah 41:18 but will open rivers upon the mountains and springs in the midst of plains, make the desert into marshes and the thirsty land into aqueducts;
Isaiah 41:19 I will put cedar and box and myrtle and cypress and poplar into the waterless land,
Isaiah 41:20 so that they may see and know and consider and understand together that the hand of the Lord did all these things, and the Holy One of Israel showed them.
Isaiah 41:21 Your judgment draws near, says the Lord God; your counsels drew near, says the king of Iakob.
Isaiah 41:22 Let them draw near and announce to you what will happen, or say what the former things were, and we will apply the mind and know what the last things are, and tell us the things coming.
Isaiah 41:23 Announce to us the things coming at the end, and we will know that you are gods; do good and do harm, and we will marvel and see together;
Isaiah 41:24 because from where are you, and from where is your work? From earth; they chose you, an abomination.
Isaiah 41:25 But I raised the one from the north and the one from the rising of the sun; they will be called by my name; let rulers come, and like potter's clay and like a potter treading clay, thus you will be trampled.
Isaiah 41:26 For who will announce the things from the beginning, so that we may know, and the things beforehand, and we will say that they are true? There is no one foretelling or hearing your words.
Isaiah 41:27 I will give a beginning to Sion and encourage Ierusalem for a way.
Isaiah 41:28 For from the nations, behold, no one, and from their idols there was no one announcing; and if I ask them, From where are you? they will certainly not answer me.
Isaiah 41:29 For those making you exist, and those leading you astray do so in vain.

## Chapter 42

Isaiah 42:1 Iakob is my servant; I will uphold him; Israel is my chosen one; my soul accepted him; I gave my spirit upon him; he will bring forth judgment to the nations.
Isaiah 42:2 He will not cry out or raise his voice, nor will his voice be heard outside.
Isaiah 42:3 He will not shatter a broken reed or extinguish smoking flax, but he will bring forth judgment in truth.
Isaiah 42:4 He will shine forth and not be crushed until he sets judgment upon the earth; and nations will hope in his name.
Isaiah 42:5 Thus says the Lord God who made heaven and pitched it, who established the earth and the things in her, and gives breath to the people upon her and spirit to those treading her;
Isaiah 42:6 I, the Lord God, called you in righteousness and will hold your hand and strengthen you, and I gave you for a covenant of a race, for a light of nations,
Isaiah 42:7 to open eyes of blind ones, to bring bound ones out of bonds and those sitting in darkness out of a prison house. —
Isaiah 42:8 I am the Lord God; this is my name; I will not give my glory to another or my excellences to carved things.
Isaiah 42:9 Behold, the things from the beginning have come, and new things which I will announce, and before springing up they were made clear to you.
Isaiah 42:10 Hymn a new hymn to the Lord, his dominion; glorify his name from the end of the earth, those going down into the sea and sailing it, the islands and those dwelling in them.
Isaiah 42:11 Be glad, desert and her villages, dwellings and those dwelling in Kedar; those dwelling in Petra will be glad; from the tops of the mountains they will cry out;
Isaiah 42:12 they will give glory to God; they will announce his excellences in the islands.
Isaiah 42:13 The Lord, the God of forces, will go out and shatter war; he will rouse zeal and cry out against his enemies with strength.
Isaiah 42:14 I was silent; will I also always be silent and endure? I persevered like a woman giving birth; I will astound and dry up together.
Isaiah 42:15 And I will make rivers into islands and dry up marshes.
Isaiah 42:16 And I will lead blind ones in a way which they did not know and make them tread paths which they did not know; I will make darkness into light for them and crooked things into straight; I will do these utterances and will not abandon them.
Isaiah 42:17 But they themselves turned backward; be ashamed with shame, those trusting in carved things, those saying to cast things, You are our gods.
Isaiah 42:18 Deaf ones, hear, and blind ones, look up to see.
Isaiah 42:19 And who is blind but my servants, and deaf but those ruling them? And the slaves of God were blinded.
Isaiah 42:20 You saw many times and did not guard yourselves; the ears are open, and you did not hear.
Isaiah 42:21 The Lord God desired that he be justified and magnify praise. And I saw,
Isaiah 42:22 and the people became plundered and pillaged; for the snare is in the chambers everywhere, and together in houses where they hid them; they became plunder, and there was no one delivering what was seized, and there was no one saying, Give it back.
Isaiah 42:23 Who among you will give ear to these things, will listen for the things coming?
Isaiah 42:24 Who gave Iakob to pillaging and Israel to those plundering him? Was it not God, against whom they sinned and did not desire to go in his ways or hear his law?
Isaiah 42:25 And he brought upon them the wrath of his fury, and war prevailed against them and those burning them up all around, and each of them did not know or lay it upon the soul.

## Chapter 43

Isaiah 43:1 And now thus says the Lord God who made you, Iakob, who formed you, Israel, Do not fear, because I redeemed you; I called you by your name; you are mine.
Isaiah 43:2 And if you cross through water, I am with you, and rivers will not overwhelm you; and if you pass through fire, you will certainly not be burned up; a flame will not burn you up.
Isaiah 43:3 Because I am the Lord your God, the Holy One of Israel who saves you; I made Egypt your exchange, and Ethiopia and Soene for you.
Isaiah 43:4 Since you became precious before me, you were glorified, and I loved you; and I will give many humans for you and rulers for your head.
Isaiah 43:5 Do not fear, because I am with you; from the east I will bring your seed and from the west gather you.
Isaiah 43:6 I will say to the north, Bring, and to the southwest, Do not hinder; bring my sons from a land far away and my daughters from the ends of the earth,
Isaiah 43:7 all who have been called by my name. For in my glory I fashioned him and formed and made him;
Isaiah 43:8 and I brought out a blind people, and eyes are likewise blind, and they are deaf, having ears.
Isaiah 43:9 All the nations were gathered together, and rulers will be gathered from them; who will announce these things? Or who will announce to you the things from the beginning? Let them bring their witnesses and be justified and say true things.
Isaiah 43:10 Become witnesses for me, and I am a witness, says the Lord God, and the servant whom I chose, so that you may know and believe and understand that I am; before me no other god came to be, and after me there will be none;
Isaiah 43:11 I am God, and there is no one saving apart from me.
Isaiah 43:12 I announced and saved, I reproached, and there was no stranger among you; you are witnesses for me, and I am a witness, says the Lord God.
Isaiah 43:13 Yet from the beginning, and there is no one delivering from my hands; I will do it, and who will turn it back?
Isaiah 43:14 Thus says the Lord God who redeems you, the Holy One of Israel, For your sake I will send into Babylon and raise up all who flee, and Chaldeans will be bound in ships.
Isaiah 43:15 I am the Lord God, your Holy One, who showed Israel as your king.
Isaiah 43:16 Thus says the Lord who gives a way in a sea and a path in strong water,
Isaiah 43:17 who brought out chariots and horse and a strong crowd, but they fell asleep and will not rise; they were extinguished like extinguished flax:
Isaiah 43:18 Do not remember the first things, and do not reckon together the ancient things.
Isaiah 43:19 Behold, I make new things which will now spring up, and you will know them; and I will make a way in the desert and rivers in the waterless land.
Isaiah 43:20 The beasts of the field will bless me, sirens and daughters of ostriches, because I gave water in the desert and rivers in the waterless land to give drink to my chosen race,
Isaiah 43:21 my people whom I acquired to recount my excellences.
Isaiah 43:22 I did not now call you, Iakob, nor did I make you weary, Israel;
Isaiah 43:23 the sheep of your whole burnt offering were not for me, nor did you glorify me in your sacrifices, nor did I make you labor with frankincense,
Isaiah 43:24 nor did you acquire incense for me with silver, nor did I desire the fat of your sacrifices, but in your sins and in your injustices I stood before you.
Isaiah 43:25 I am, I am the one wiping out your lawless deeds, and I will certainly not remember.
Isaiah 43:26 But you remember, and let us be judged; you say your lawless deeds first, so that you may be justified.
Isaiah 43:27 Your first fathers and their rulers acted lawlessly against me,
Isaiah 43:28 and the rulers defiled my holy things, and I gave Iakob to destruction and Israel to reproach.

## Chapter 44

Isaiah 44:1 But now hear, my servant Iakob and Israel whom I chose;
Isaiah 44:2 thus says the Lord God who made you and who formed you from the womb, You will yet be helped; do not fear, my servant Iakob and beloved Israel whom I chose;
Isaiah 44:3 because I will give water in thirst to those going in a waterless land; I will put my spirit upon your seed and my blessings upon your children,
Isaiah 44:4 and they will spring up like grass in the midst of water and like a willow beside flowing water.
Isaiah 44:5 This one will say, I am God's, and this one will cry out in the name of Iakob, and another will inscribe, I am God's, in the name of Israel.
Isaiah 44:6 Thus says God, the king of Israel, who rescued him, God Sabaoth, I am first, and I am after these things; apart from me there is no god.
Isaiah 44:7 Who is like me? Let him stand, call and prepare for me since I made a human forever, and let them announce to you the things coming before they come.
Isaiah 44:8 Do not cover yourselves; did you not give ear from the beginning, and I announced to you? You are witnesses whether there is a god apart from me; and they were not then.
Isaiah 44:9 Those forming and carving are all vain, those making the things they desire, which will not benefit them; but they will be ashamed,
Isaiah 44:10 all those forming a god and carving useless things,
Isaiah 44:11 and all from whom they came to be dried up, and let deaf ones from among humans all be gathered and stand together, be abashed and ashamed together.
Isaiah 44:12 Because a craftsman sharpened iron, worked it with an adze and bored it with a drill, worked it with the arm of his strength; and he will hunger and be weak and certainly not drink water. Having chosen
Isaiah 44:13 wood, a craftsman set it by measure and fitted it with glue; he made it like the form of a man and like the beauty of a human, to set it in a house.
Isaiah 44:14 The wood which he cut from the wood, which the Lord planted and rain lengthened,
Isaiah 44:15 so that it may be for humans for burning; and taking from it, he warmed himself, and burning it, they baked bread upon them; but they worked the remainder into gods and worship them.
Isaiah 44:16 Half of it they burned up in fire and, burning it, baked bread upon them; and roasting meat upon it, he ate and was filled; and, warmed, he said, It is pleasant for me, because I was warmed and saw fire.
Isaiah 44:17 But the remainder he made into a carved god and worships it and prays, saying, Deliver me, because you are my god.
Isaiah 44:18 They did not know to understand, because they were dimmed from seeing with their eyes and thinking with their heart.
Isaiah 44:19 And he did not reckon in his heart or consider in his soul or know in his understanding that he burned half of it in fire and baked bread upon its coals and roasted meat and ate, and made its remainder into an abomination, and they worship it.
Isaiah 44:20 Know that their heart is ash, and they wander, and no one can deliver his soul; see, will you not say that, Falsehood is in my right hand?
Isaiah 44:21 Remember these things, Iakob and Israel, because you are my servant; I formed you as my servant, and you, Israel, do not forget me.
Isaiah 44:22 For behold, I wiped away your lawless deeds like a cloud and your sins like gloom; turn to me, and I will redeem you.
Isaiah 44:23 Be glad, heavens, because God had mercy on Israel; trumpet, foundations of the earth; cry out gladness, mountains, the hills and all the trees in them, because God redeemed Iakob, and Israel will be glorified.
Isaiah 44:24 Thus says the Lord who redeems you and who forms you from the womb, I, the Lord who accomplishes everything, stretched heaven alone and established the earth. Who else
Isaiah 44:25 will scatter signs of ventriloquists and divinations from a heart, turning intelligent ones backward and making their counsel foolish,
Isaiah 44:26 and establishing utterances of his servant and making the counsel of his messengers true? The one saying to Ierusalem, You will be inhabited, and to the cities of Ioudaia, You will be built, and her deserted places will spring up;
Isaiah 44:27 the one saying to the abyss, You will be desolated, and I will dry up your rivers;
Isaiah 44:28 the one telling Kyros to be wise, and, He will do all my desires; the one saying to Ierusalem, You will be built, and I will found my holy house.

## Chapter 45

Isaiah 45:1 Thus says the Lord God to my anointed Kyros, whose right hand I held so that nations may obey before him, and I will tear apart the strength of kings, open doors before him, and cities will not be shut:
Isaiah 45:2 I will go before you and level mountains; I will shatter bronze doors and break iron bars,
Isaiah 45:3 and give you dark treasures; I will open hidden, unseen ones to you, so that you may know that I am the Lord God who calls your name, the God of Israel.
Isaiah 45:4 For the sake of Iakob my servant and Israel my chosen one, I will call you by your name and accept you, but you did not know me.
Isaiah 45:5 Because I am the Lord God, and there is no god besides me any longer, and you did not know me,
Isaiah 45:6 so that those from the rising of the sun and those from the west may know that there is none apart from me; I am the Lord God, and there is no other;
Isaiah 45:7 I am the one who fashioned light and made darkness, who makes peace and creates evils; I am the Lord God who does all these things.
Isaiah 45:8 Let heaven be glad from above, and let the clouds sprinkle righteousness; let the earth bring forth mercy and bring forth righteousness together; I am the Lord who created you.
Isaiah 45:9 What better thing did I fashion like potter's clay? Will the one plowing plow the earth all day? Will the clay say to the potter, What are you doing, because you do not work or have hands?
Isaiah 45:10 The one saying to the father, What will you beget? and to the mother, What will you labor to bear?
Isaiah 45:11 Because thus says the Lord God, the Holy One of Israel who made the things coming, Ask me concerning my sons and concerning my daughters, and command me concerning the works of my hands.
Isaiah 45:12 I made earth and a human upon her; I established heaven with my hand; I commanded all the stars.
Isaiah 45:13 I raised him as king with righteousness, and all his ways are straight; this one will build my city and turn back the captivity of my people, not with ransoms or with gifts, said the Lord Sabaoth.
Isaiah 45:14 Thus says the Lord Sabaoth, Egypt labored, and trade of Ethiopians, and the Seboin, tall men, will cross over to you and be slaves to you and follow behind you, bound with handcuffs, and worship you and pray in you, because God is in you, and they will say, There is no god apart from you;
Isaiah 45:15 for you are God, and we did not know, the God of Israel, a Savior.
Isaiah 45:16 All those opposing him will be ashamed and abashed and go in shame. Be renewed toward me, islands.
Isaiah 45:17 Israel is saved by the Lord with eternal salvation; they will not be ashamed or abashed forever.
Isaiah 45:18 Thus says the Lord who made heaven—this is the God who showed the earth and made her; he himself marked her out; he did not make her for emptiness but to be inhabited—I am, and there is no other.
Isaiah 45:19 I have not spoken in secret or in a dark place of earth; I did not say to the seed of Iakob, Seek a vain thing; I am, I am the Lord speaking righteousness and announcing truth.
Isaiah 45:20 Be gathered and come; take counsel together, those being saved from the nations. Those lifting the wood, their carving, and praying as to gods who do not save did not know.
Isaiah 45:21 If they will announce, let them draw near, so that they may know together who made these things audible from the beginning. Then it was announced to you, I am God, and there is no other apart from me; there is no righteous one and Savior besides me.
Isaiah 45:22 Turn to me, and you will be saved, those from the furthest part of the earth; I am God, and there is no other.
Isaiah 45:23 By myself I swear, Surely righteousness will come out of my mouth; my words will not turn back, that every knee will bend to me, and every tongue will confess to God,
Isaiah 45:24 saying, Righteousness and glory will come to him, and all those separating themselves will be ashamed;
Isaiah 45:25 from the Lord all the seed of the sons of Israel will be justified and glorified in God.

## Chapter 46

Isaiah 46:1 Bel fell, Dagon was shattered, their carved things became for beasts and livestock; lift them, tied up like a burden for one weary
Isaiah 46:2 and hungry and weakened, without strength, together, who will not be able to be saved from war, but they themselves were led captive.
Isaiah 46:3 Hear me, house of Iakob and all the remnant of Israel, those lifted from the womb and disciplined from childhood;
Isaiah 46:4 until old age I am, and until you grow very old, I am; I endure you, I made and I will release, I will take up and save you.
Isaiah 46:5 To whom did you liken me? See, devise, those wandering.
Isaiah 46:6 Those contributing gold from a purse will weigh silver with a balance by weight, and hiring a goldsmith, they made handmade things and, bowing, worship them.
Isaiah 46:7 They lift it upon the shoulders and go; but if they set it down, it remains in its place; it will certainly not be moved; and whoever cries out to it, it will certainly not listen; it will certainly not save him from evils.
Isaiah 46:8 Remember these things and groan; repent, those led astray; turn back in heart.
Isaiah 46:9 And remember the former things from eternity, because I am God, and there is no other apart from me,
Isaiah 46:10 announcing the last things beforehand, before they come to be, and together they were accomplished; and I said, All my counsel will stand, and everything which I have counseled I will do;
Isaiah 46:11 calling a bird from the east and from a land far away concerning the things which I have counseled, I spoke and brought, I created and did, I brought him and prospered his way.
Isaiah 46:12 Hear me, those who have lost the heart, those far from righteousness.
Isaiah 46:13 I brought my righteousness near and will not delay the salvation from me; I have given salvation in Sion to Israel for glory.

## Chapter 47

Isaiah 47:1 Go down, sit upon the earth, virgin daughter of Babylon; enter darkness, daughter of the Chaldeans, because you will no longer continue to be called delicate and tender.
Isaiah 47:2 Take a mill, grind flour, uncover your veil, uncover the gray hairs, bare the shins, cross rivers;
Isaiah 47:3 your shame will be uncovered, your reproaches will appear; I will take justice from you; I will certainly no longer deliver it to humans.
Isaiah 47:4 The one who rescued you said, the Lord Sabaoth is his name, the Holy One of Israel:
Isaiah 47:5 Sit stricken, enter darkness, daughter of the Chaldeans; you will certainly no longer be called strength of a kingdom.
Isaiah 47:6 I was provoked against my people; you defiled my inheritance; I gave into your hand, but you did not give them mercy; you made the elder's yoke very heavy.
Isaiah 47:7 And you said, Forever I will be a ruler; you did not consider these things in your heart or remember the last things.
Isaiah 47:8 But now hear these things, tender woman sitting confidently, saying in her heart, I am, and there is no other; I will not sit as a widow or know orphanhood.
Isaiah 47:9 But now these two things will come suddenly upon you in one day; widowhood and childlessness will come suddenly upon you in your sorcery, in the strength of your enchantments, exceedingly,
Isaiah 47:10 in the hope of your wickedness. For you said, I am, and there is no other. Know that the understanding of these things and your prostitution will be shame for you. And you said in your heart, I am, and there is no other.
Isaiah 47:11 And destruction will come upon you, and you will certainly not know, a pit, and you will fall into it; and misery will come upon you, and you will certainly not be able to become clean; and destruction will come upon you suddenly, and you will certainly not know.
Isaiah 47:12 Stand now in your enchantments and your abundant sorcery, which you learned from your youth, if you will be able to be benefited.
Isaiah 47:13 You have grown weary in your counsels; let the astrologers of heaven stand and save you; let those seeing the stars announce to you what is going to come upon you.
Isaiah 47:14 Behold, all will be burned up like brushwood upon fire and will certainly not deliver their soul from a flame; because you have coals of fire, sit upon them.
Isaiah 47:15 These will be a help to you; you labored in your trade from youth; each human wandered by himself, but there will be no salvation for you.

## Chapter 48

Isaiah 48:1 Hear these things, house of Iakob, those called by the name of Israel and those who came out of Iouda, those swearing by the name of the Lord God of Israel, remembering not with truth or with righteousness,
Isaiah 48:2 and clinging to the name of the holy city and leaning upon the God of Israel; the Lord Sabaoth is his name.
Isaiah 48:3 I announced the former things beforehand, and they came out of my mouth and became audible; suddenly I did them, and they came upon you.
Isaiah 48:4 I know that you are harsh, and your neck is an iron sinew, and your forehead bronze.
Isaiah 48:5 And I announced to you long ago; before it came upon you I made it audible to you; do not say that, My idols did it, and do not say that, The carved things and the cast things commanded me.
Isaiah 48:6 You heard everything, and you did not know; but I also made audible to you the new things from now, which are going to happen, and you did not speak.
Isaiah 48:7 Now they happen and not long ago, and you did not hear them in former days; do not say that, Yes, I know them.
Isaiah 48:8 You neither knew nor understood, nor did I open your ears from the beginning; for I knew that, rejecting, you will reject, and, lawless still from the womb, you will be beguiled.
Isaiah 48:9 For the sake of my name I will show you my fury and bring my glorious things upon you, so that I may not destroy you.
Isaiah 48:10 Behold, I have sold you, not for the sake of silver, but I delivered you from a furnace of poverty;
Isaiah 48:11 for my sake I will do it for you, because my name is profaned, and I will not give my glory to another.
Isaiah 48:12 Hear me, Iakob and Israel whom I call; I am first, and I am forever,
