Jeremiah 6:5 Because if, correcting, you correct your ways and your practices and, doing, you do judgment between a man and his neighbor,
Jeremiah 6:6 and do not oppress a proselyte and an orphan and a widow and do not pour out innocent blood in this place and do not go after foreign gods to your harm,
Jeremiah 6:7 I will also settle you in this place, in a land which I gave to your fathers from eternity and until eternity.
Jeremiah 6:8 But if you have trusted in false words from which you will not be benefited,
Jeremiah 6:9 and you murder and commit adultery and steal and swear unjustly and burned incense to Baal and went after foreign gods whom you do not know, so that it may be bad for you,
Jeremiah 6:10 and you came and stood before me in the house upon which my name has been called, and said, We have refrained from not doing all these abominations,
Jeremiah 6:11 is my house upon which my name has been called there a cave of robbers before you? And behold, I too have seen, says the Lord.
Jeremiah 6:12 Because go into my place in Selom, where I made my name dwell formerly, and see what I did to it because of the wickedness of my people Israel.
Jeremiah 6:13 And now, because you did all these works, and I spoke to you and you did not hear me, and I called you and you did not answer,
Jeremiah 6:14 I will also do to this house upon which my name has been called, in which you have trusted, and to the place which I gave to you and to your fathers, just as I did to Selom.
Jeremiah 6:15 And I will cast you away from before me, just as I cast away your brothers, all the seed of Ephraim.
Jeremiah 6:16 And you do not pray concerning this people and do not request that they be shown mercy and do not make supplication and do not approach me concerning them, because I will not hear.
Jeremiah 6:17 Do you not see what they do in the cities of Iouda and in the ways of Ierusalem?
Jeremiah 6:18 Their sons gather wood, and their fathers kindle fire, and their wives knead dough to make chauon cakes for the host of heaven, and they poured libations to foreign gods, so that they may provoke me to anger.
Jeremiah 6:19 Do they provoke me to anger? says the Lord; not themselves, so that their faces may be put to shame?
Jeremiah 6:20 Therefore thus says the Lord, Behold, my wrath and fury pour upon this place and upon the humans and upon the livestock and upon every tree of their field and upon all the produce of the land, and it will burn and not be extinguished.
Jeremiah 6:21 Thus says the Lord, Gather your whole burnt offerings with your sacrifices and eat meat.
Jeremiah 6:22 Because I did not speak to your fathers and did not command them on the day when I brought them up from the land of Egypt concerning whole burnt offerings and sacrifice;
Jeremiah 6:23 but only this utterance I commanded them, saying, Hear my voice, and I will be God for you, and you will be a people for me; and go in all my ways which I command you, so that it may be well for you.
Jeremiah 6:24 And they did not hear me, and their ear did not pay attention, but they went in the thoughts of their evil heart and became backward and not forward.
Jeremiah 6:25 From the day when their fathers came out of the land of Egypt and until this day I also sent away to you all my slaves the prophets by day and at dawn, and I sent,
Jeremiah 6:26 and they did not hear me, and their ear did not pay attention, and they hardened their neck beyond their fathers.
Jeremiah 6:27-28 And you will say this word to them, This is the nation which did not hear the voice of the Lord or accept discipline; faithfulness failed from their mouth.
Jeremiah 6:29 Shear your head and cast it away and take up a lament upon lips, because the Lord rejected and repudiated the generation doing these things.
Jeremiah 6:30 Because the sons of Iouda did evil before me, says the Lord; they placed their abominations in the house upon which my name has been called, to defile it;
Jeremiah 6:31 and they built the altar of Tapheth, which is in the ravine of the son of Ennom, to burn up their sons and their daughters in fire, which I did not command them and did not conceive in my heart.
Jeremiah 6:32 Therefore behold, days come, says the Lord, and they will no longer say, Altar of Tapheth and Ravine of the Son of Ennom, but only Ravine of the Killed, and they will bury in Tapheth because there is no place.
Jeremiah 6:33 And the dead of this people will be food for the birds of heaven and the beasts of the earth, and there will be no one driving them away.
Jeremiah 6:34 And I will abolish from the cities of Iouda and from the passages of Ierusalem a voice of those glad and a voice of those rejoicing, a voice of a bridegroom and a voice of a bride, because all the earth will be for desolation. —

## Chapter 8

Jeremiah 8:1 At that time, says the Lord, they will bring out the bones of the kings of Iouda and the bones of its rulers and the bones of the priests and the bones of the prophets and the bones of those dwelling in Ierusalem from their tombs
Jeremiah 8:2 and will cool them toward the sun and the moon and toward all the stars and toward all the army of heaven, which they loved and which they served and after which they went and to which they held fast and which they worshipped; they will not be lamented and will not be buried and will be for an example upon the face of the earth,
Jeremiah 8:3 because they chose death rather than life, and for all the remaining ones left from that generation in every place wherever I drive them out there.
Jeremiah 8:4 For thus says the Lord: Does the one falling not rise? Or does the one turning away not return?
Jeremiah 8:5 Why did this people of mine turn away with a shameless turning away, and were they held fast in their choice and did not wish to return?
Jeremiah 8:6 Give ear now and hear; they will not speak thus; there is no person repenting of his wickedness, saying, What have I done? The runner ceased from his course like a sweating horse in its neighing.
Jeremiah 8:7 And the asida in heaven knew its time; turtledove and swallow, sparrows of the field, kept the times of their entrances, but my people did not know the judgments of the Lord.
Jeremiah 8:8 How will you say, We are wise, and the law of the Lord is with us? In vain a false reed came to be for scribes.
Jeremiah 8:9 Wise ones were put to shame and were terrified and were captured, because they rejected the word of the Lord; what wisdom is in them?
Jeremiah 8:10 Therefore I will give their wives to others and their fields to the heirs,
Jeremiah 8:13 and they will gather their produce, says the Lord; there is no grape on the vines, and there are no figs on the fig trees, and the leaves have fallen.
Jeremiah 8:14 Why are we sitting? Gather together, and let us enter the fortified cities and be cast away, because God cast us away and gave us water of gall to drink, because we sinned before him.
Jeremiah 8:15 We gathered for peace, and there were no good things; for a time of healing, and behold, haste.
Jeremiah 8:16 From Dan we will hear the sound of the sharpness of his horses; from the sound of the neighing of the riding of his horses all the earth was shaken; and he will come and devour the earth and its fullness, a city and those dwelling in it.
Jeremiah 8:17 For behold, I am sending out among you snakes that kill, which cannot be charmed, and they will bite you.
Jeremiah 8:18 Incurable things with pain of your heart being at a loss.
Jeremiah 8:19 Behold, a sound of the cry of the daughter of my people from a land far away: Is the Lord not in Sion? Or is there no king there? Why did they provoke me with their carved images and with foreign vanities?
Jeremiah 8:20 Summer passed through, harvest passed by, and we were not saved.
Jeremiah 8:21 At the crushing of the daughter of my people I was darkened; in perplexity pangs overpowered me like those of a woman giving birth.
Jeremiah 8:22 Is there no resin in Galaad, or is there no physician there? Why did healing of the daughter of my people not arise?
Jeremiah 8:23 Who will give water to my head and a fountain of tears to my eyes, and I will weep for this people of mine day and night, the wounded of the daughter of my people? —

## Chapter 9

Jeremiah 9:1 Who might give me a remotest lodging in the wilderness, and I will leave my people and go away from them? Because all commit adultery, an assembly of those breaking faith.
Jeremiah 9:2 And they stretched their tongue like a bow; falsehood and not faithfulness prevailed upon the earth, because they went out from evils to evils and did not know me.
Jeremiah 9:3 Each of you guard yourselves against his neighbor, and do not trust in their brothers, because every brother will trip with the heel, and every friend will walk deceitfully.
Jeremiah 9:4 Each will mock his friend; they will certainly not speak truth; their tongue has learned to speak false things; they acted unjustly and did not cease to turn back.
Jeremiah 9:5 Interest upon interest, deceit upon deceit; they did not wish to know me.
Jeremiah 9:6 Therefore thus says the Lord: Behold, I will refine them by fire and test them, because I will act on account of the wickedness of the daughter of my people.
Jeremiah 9:7 Their tongue is a dart that wounds; the words of their mouth are deceitful; he speaks peaceful things to his neighbor and has hostility within himself.
Jeremiah 9:8 Will I not visit for these things, says the Lord, or will my soul not exact vengeance on such a people?
Jeremiah 9:9 Take up lamentation over the mountains and mourning over the paths of the wilderness, because they failed for lack of people; they did not hear a sound of possessions; from birds of heaven even to cattle they departed, they went away.
Jeremiah 9:10 And I will give Ierusalem over to removal and to a dwelling place of dragons, and I will make the cities of Iouda a disappearance, so that they are not inhabited.
Jeremiah 9:11 Who is the understanding person? And let him understand this, and the one to whom the word of the mouth of the Lord comes, let him announce to you: On account of what was the land destroyed, kindled like a wilderness, so that it is not traversed?
Jeremiah 9:12 And the Lord said to me: Because they forsook my law, which I gave before their face, and did not hear my voice,
Jeremiah 9:13 but went after the things pleasing to their evil heart and after the idols which their fathers taught them,
Jeremiah 9:14 therefore thus says the Lord, the God of Israel: Behold, I will feed them constraints and give them water of gall to drink
Jeremiah 9:15 and scatter them among the nations which they and their fathers did not know, and I will send the sword after them until I consume them with it.
Jeremiah 9:16 Thus says the Lord: Call the mourning women, and let them come, and send to the wise women, and let them utter a sound
Jeremiah 9:17 and take up a mourning over you, and let your eyes bring down tears, and let your eyelids flow with water.
Jeremiah 9:18 Because a sound of lament was heard in Sion: How we suffered misery, we were put greatly to shame, because we forsook the land and cast away our dwellings.
Jeremiah 9:19 Hear now, women, a word of God, and let your ears receive words of his mouth, and teach your daughters lament, and each woman her neighbor mourning.
Jeremiah 9:20 Because death went up through your windows, entered your land to wipe out infants outside and young men from the broad streets.
Jeremiah 9:21 And the dead of the people will be for an example upon the face of the plain of your land and like grass behind a reaper, and there will be no one gathering.
Jeremiah 9:22 Thus says the Lord: Let the wise one not boast in his wisdom, and let the strong one not boast in his strength, and let the rich one not boast in his wealth,
Jeremiah 9:23 but let the one boasting boast in this: to understand and know that I am the Lord doing mercy and judgment and righteousness upon the earth, because in these is my will, says the Lord.
Jeremiah 9:24 Behold, days are coming, says the Lord, and I will visit upon all those circumcised in their foreskins,
Jeremiah 9:25 upon Egypt and upon Ioudaia and upon Edom and upon the sons of Ammon and upon the sons of Moab and upon everyone clipping the parts about his face, those dwelling in the wilderness; because all the nations are uncircumcised in flesh, and all the house of Israel are uncircumcised in their hearts.

## Chapter 10

Jeremiah 10:1 Hear the word of the Lord which he spoke concerning you, house of Israel;
Jeremiah 10:2 thus says the Lord: Do not learn according to the ways of the nations, and do not fear the signs of heaven, because they fear them in their faces.
Jeremiah 10:3 Because the customs of the nations are vain; it is wood cut out of the forest, a carpenter's work and a casting;
Jeremiah 10:4 they are adorned with silver and gold; with hammers and nails they secured them, and they will not move;
Jeremiah 10:9 it is worked silver; they will not walk; applied silver will come from Tharsis, gold of Mophaz and the hand of goldsmiths, all works of craftsmen; they will clothe them in blue and purple;
Jeremiah 10:5 being lifted they will be carried, because they will not step. Do not fear them, because they will certainly not do harm, and there is no good in them.
Jeremiah 10:11 Thus you will say to them: Gods who did not make heaven and earth, let them perish from the earth and from beneath this heaven.
Jeremiah 10:12 The Lord who made the earth in his strength, who set upright the inhabited world in his wisdom, and in his understanding stretched out heaven
Jeremiah 10:13 and an abundance of water in heaven, and brought up clouds from the end of the earth, made lightning for rain and brought out light from his treasuries.
Jeremiah 10:14 Every person became foolish away from knowledge; every goldsmith was put to shame over his carved images, because they cast false things; there is no spirit in them;
Jeremiah 10:15 they are vain, works made a mockery of; at the time of their visitation they will perish.
Jeremiah 10:16 Such is not the portion for Iakob, because he who formed all things is himself his inheritance; the Lord is his name.
Jeremiah 10:17 He gathered your substance from outside, you dwelling among chosen ones.
Jeremiah 10:18 Because thus says the Lord: Behold, I am tripping those dwelling in this land in affliction, so that your wound may be found;
Jeremiah 10:19 woe over your crushing; your wound is painful. And I said, Truly this is my injury, and it overtook me;
Jeremiah 10:20 my tent suffered misery, perished, and all my skins were torn apart; my sons and my sheep are no more; there is no longer a place for my tent, a place for my skins.
Jeremiah 10:21 Because the shepherds acted foolishly and did not seek out the Lord; therefore all the pasture did not understand, and they were scattered.
Jeremiah 10:22 A sound of a report, behold, is coming, and a great shaking from the land of the north, to make the cities of Iouda a disappearance and a bed of sparrows.
Jeremiah 10:23 I know, Lord, that a person's way is not his own, nor will a man walk and direct his course rightly.
Jeremiah 10:24 Discipline us, Lord, only with judgment and not with wrath, so that you do not make us few.
Jeremiah 10:25 Pour out your wrath upon nations that do not know you and upon generations that did not call upon your name, because they devoured Iakob and consumed him and desolated his pasture.

## Chapter 11

Jeremiah 11:1 The word that came from the Lord to Ieremias, saying,
Jeremiah 11:2 Hear the words of this covenant. And you will speak to the men of Iouda and to those dwelling in Ierusalem;
Jeremiah 11:3 and you will say to them: Thus says the Lord, the God of Israel: Cursed is the person who will not hear the words of this covenant,
Jeremiah 11:4 which I commanded your fathers on the day on which I brought them up from the land of Egypt, from the iron furnace, saying, Hear my voice and do everything that I command you, and you will be a people for me, and I will be a God for you,
Jeremiah 11:5 so that I may establish my oath which I swore to your fathers, to give them a land flowing with milk and honey, as this day. And I answered and said, May it be, Lord.
Jeremiah 11:6 And the Lord said to me: Read these words in the cities of Iouda and outside Ierusalem, saying, Hear the words of this covenant and do them.
Jeremiah 11:8 And they did not do them.
Jeremiah 11:9 And the Lord said to me: A conspiracy was found among the men of Iouda and among those dwelling in Ierusalem;
Jeremiah 11:10 they returned to the injustices of their former fathers, who did not wish to listen to my words, and behold, they walk after foreign gods to serve them, and the house of Israel and the house of Iouda broke apart my covenant which I made with their fathers.
Jeremiah 11:11 Therefore thus says the Lord: Behold, I am bringing upon this people evils from which they will not be able to come out, and they will cry to me, and I will not listen to them.
Jeremiah 11:12 And the cities of Iouda and those dwelling in Ierusalem will go and cry to the gods to whom they burn incense; will they save them at the time of their evils?
Jeremiah 11:13 Because according to the number of your cities were your gods, Iouda, and according to the number of the exits of Ierusalem you arranged altars to burn incense to Baal.
Jeremiah 11:14 And you, do not pray concerning this people and do not petition for them in supplication and prayer, because I will not listen at the time at which they call upon me, at the time of their mistreatment.
Jeremiah 11:15 Why did the beloved woman in my house do an abomination? Will vows and holy meats remove your wickednesses from you, or will you escape by these?
Jeremiah 11:16 The Lord called your name a beautiful olive tree, well shaded in appearance; at the sound of its cutting fire was kindled upon it; great is the affliction upon you; its branches were made useless.
Jeremiah 11:17 And the Lord who planted you spoke evils against you in return for the wickedness of the house of Israel and the house of Iouda, because they acted for themselves to provoke me by their burning incense to Baal.
Jeremiah 11:18 Lord, make known to me, and I will know; then I saw their practices.
Jeremiah 11:19 But I, like an innocent lamb being led to be sacrificed, did not know; against me they devised an evil design, saying, Come, and let us put wood into his bread and wipe him out from the land of the living, and his name will certainly not be remembered any longer.
Jeremiah 11:20 Lord, judging just things, testing kidneys and hearts, may I see the vengeance from you upon them, because to you I revealed my just claim.
Jeremiah 11:21 Therefore thus says the Lord concerning the men of Anathoth seeking my life, saying, You shall certainly not prophesy in the name of the Lord; otherwise you will die in our hands.
Jeremiah 11:22 Behold, I will visit upon them; their young men will die by the sword, and their sons and their daughters will end in famine,
Jeremiah 11:23 and there will be no remnant of them, because I will bring evils upon those dwelling in Anathoth in the year of their visitation.

## Chapter 12

Jeremiah 12:1 You are righteous, Lord, when I make my defense to you; nevertheless I will speak judgments to you: Why does the way of the impious prosper? Why did all those breaking faith with breaches of faith flourish?
Jeremiah 12:2 You planted them, and they took root, they produced children and made fruit; you are near their mouth and far from their kidneys.
Jeremiah 12:3 And you, Lord, know me; you have tested my heart before you; consecrate them for the day of their slaughter.
Jeremiah 12:4 Until when will the land mourn and all the grass of the field dry up because of the wickedness of those dwelling in it? Cattle and birds disappeared, because they said, God will not see our ways.
Jeremiah 12:5 Your feet run and exhaust you; how will you prepare yourself against horses? And in a land of peace you have trusted; how will you act in the raging of the Iordan?
Jeremiah 12:6 Because even your brothers and the house of your father, even these rejected you, and they cried out, from behind you they gathered together; do not trust in them, because they will speak good things to you.
Jeremiah 12:7 I have forsaken my house, left my inheritance, given my beloved soul into the hands of her enemies.
Jeremiah 12:8 My inheritance became to me like a lion in a forest; she raised her voice against me; therefore I hated her.
Jeremiah 12:9 Is my inheritance to me a hyena's cave, or a cave around her? Go, gather all the wild beasts of the field, and let them come to eat her.
Jeremiah 12:10 Many shepherds destroyed my vineyard, defiled my portion, made my desirable portion an impassable wilderness;
Jeremiah 12:11 it was made a disappearance of destruction; because of me all the land disappeared with disappearance, because there is no man laying it in his heart.
Jeremiah 12:12 Upon every passage in the wilderness came those causing misery, because the sword of the Lord will devour from the end of the earth to the end of the earth; there is no peace for any flesh.
Jeremiah 12:13 Sow wheat and reap thorns; their allotments will not benefit them; be ashamed of your boasting, of reproach before the Lord.
Jeremiah 12:14 For thus says the Lord concerning all the evil neighbors who touch my inheritance which I apportioned to my people Israel: Behold, I tear them away from their land, and I will cast Iouda out from their midst.
Jeremiah 12:15 And it will be after I cast them out, I will return and have mercy on them and settle them, each in his inheritance and each in his land.
Jeremiah 12:16 And it will be, if learning they learn the way of my people, to swear by my name, The Lord lives, as they taught my people to swear by Baal, they also will be built up in the midst of my people;
Jeremiah 12:17 but if they do not return, I will also remove that nation with removal and destruction.

## Chapter 13

Jeremiah 13:1 Thus says the Lord: Go and acquire for yourself a linen loincloth and put it around your waist, and it will not pass through water.
Jeremiah 13:2 And I acquired the loincloth according to the word of the Lord and put it around my waist.
Jeremiah 13:3 And a word of the Lord came to me, saying,
Jeremiah 13:4 Take the loincloth around your waist and rise and go to the Euphrates and hide it there in the hole of the rock.
Jeremiah 13:5 And I went and hid it at the Euphrates, as the Lord commanded me.
Jeremiah 13:6 And it happened after many days, and the Lord said to me: Rise, go to the Euphrates and take from there the loincloth which I commanded you to hide there.
Jeremiah 13:7 And I went to the Euphrates river and dug and took the loincloth from the place where I buried it there, and behold, it was ruined, which will certainly not be used for anything.
Jeremiah 13:8 And a word of the Lord came to me, saying,
Jeremiah 13:9 Thus says the Lord: Thus I will ruin the arrogance of Iouda and the arrogance of Ierusalem,
Jeremiah 13:10 this great arrogance, those not willing to obey my words and who went after foreign gods to serve them and to worship them, and they will be like this loincloth, which will not be used for anything.
Jeremiah 13:11 Because just as the loincloth clings around a person's waist, thus I caused the house of Israel and all the house of Iouda to cling to myself, to become for me a renowned people and a boast and a glory, and they did not listen to me.
Jeremiah 13:12 And you will say to this people: Every skin will be filled with wine. And it will be, if they say to you, Shall we not surely know that every skin will be filled with wine?
Jeremiah 13:13 And you will say to them: Thus says the Lord: Behold, I am filling those dwelling in this land and their kings, the sons of David sitting upon his throne, and the priests and the prophets and Iouda and all those dwelling in Ierusalem with drunkenness
Jeremiah 13:14 and will scatter them, a man and his brother and their fathers and their sons together; I will not yearn, says the Lord, and will not spare and will not pity them so as to refrain from their destruction.
Jeremiah 13:15 Hear and give ear and do not exalt yourselves, because the Lord spoke.
Jeremiah 13:16 Give glory to the Lord your God before it becomes dark and before your feet stumble upon dark mountains, and you will wait for light, and there is a shadow of death, and they will be put into darkness.
Jeremiah 13:17 But if you do not hear, your soul will weep secretly because of arrogance, and your eyes will bring down tears, because the flock of the Lord was crushed.
Jeremiah 13:18 Say to the king and those ruling: Be humbled and sit down, because the crown of your glory was taken down from your head.
Jeremiah 13:19 The cities toward the south were shut up, and there was no one opening; Ioudas was deported; he completed a complete deportation.
Jeremiah 13:20 Lift up your eyes, Ierusalem, and see those coming from the north; where is the flock which was given to you, the sheep of your glory?
Jeremiah 13:21 What will you say when they visit you? And you taught them lessons against yourself for rule; will not pangs hold you fast as a woman giving birth?
Jeremiah 13:22 And if you say in your heart, Why did these things meet me? Because of the abundance of your injustice your hind parts were uncovered, for your heels to be exposed as an example.
Jeremiah 13:23 If an Ethiopian will change his skin and a leopard her markings, you also will be able to do well, having learned evil things.
Jeremiah 13:24 And I scattered them like brushwood carried by wind into a wilderness.
Jeremiah 13:25 This is your lot and a portion for your disobeying me, says the Lord, because you forgot me and hoped in falsehoods.
Jeremiah 13:26 And I will uncover your hind parts upon your face, and your dishonor will be seen.
Jeremiah 13:27 And your adultery and your neighing and the estrangement of your prostitution, upon the hills and in the fields I have seen your abominations; woe to you, Ierusalem, because you were not cleansed after me; until when still?

## Chapter 14

Jeremiah 14:1 And a word of the Lord came to Ieremias concerning the lack of rain:
Jeremiah 14:2 Ioudaia mourned, and her gates were emptied and darkened upon the earth, and the cry of Ierusalem went up.
Jeremiah 14:3 And her great ones sent their younger ones for water; they came to the wells and did not find water and brought back their vessels empty.
Jeremiah 14:4 And the works of the earth failed, because there was no rain; farmers were put to shame, covered their head.
Jeremiah 14:5 And deer in the field gave birth and abandoned, because there was no vegetation.
Jeremiah 14:6 Wild asses stood upon wooded valleys; they drew in wind; their eyes failed, because there was no grass on account of a people of injustice. —
Jeremiah 14:7 If our sins stood against us, Lord, act for us for your sake, because our sins before you are many, because we sinned against you.
Jeremiah 14:8 Endurance of Israel, Lord, and you save in a time of evils; why did you become like a sojourner upon the earth and like a native turning aside into a lodging?
Jeremiah 14:9 Will you be like a person sleeping or like a man unable to save? And you are among us, Lord, and your name has been called upon us; do not forget us. —
Jeremiah 14:10 Thus says the Lord to this people: They loved to move their feet and did not restrain them, and God was not pleased with them; now he will remember their injustices.
Jeremiah 14:11 And the Lord said to me: Do not pray concerning this people for good things;
Jeremiah 14:12 because if they fast, I will not listen to their supplication, and if they offer whole burnt offerings and sacrifices, I will not be pleased with them, because by sword and by famine and by death I will bring them to an end.
Jeremiah 14:13 And I said: O Lord, behold, their prophets prophesy and say, You will not see a sword, nor will famine be among you, because I will give truth and peace upon the earth and in this place.
Jeremiah 14:14 And the Lord said to me: The prophets prophesy false things in my name; I did not send them and did not command them and did not speak to them; because false visions and divinations and omens and choices of their heart they themselves prophesy to you.
Jeremiah 14:15 Therefore thus says the Lord concerning the prophets prophesying false things in my name, and I did not send them, who say, Sword and famine will not be upon this land: By diseased death they will die, and by famine the prophets will be brought to an end;
Jeremiah 14:16 and the people to whom they prophesy, they also will be cast in the passageways of Ierusalem because of sword and famine, and there will be no one burying them, and their wives and their sons and their daughters; and I will pour their evils upon them.
Jeremiah 14:17 And you will say this word to them: Bring down tears upon your eyes day and night, and let them not cease, because with crushing the daughter of my people was crushed and with an exceedingly painful wound.
Jeremiah 14:18 If I go out into the plain, then behold, wounded ones of the sword, and if I enter the city, then behold, suffering of famine; because priest and prophet went to a land which they did not know. —
Jeremiah 14:19 Did you utterly reject Iouda, and did your soul withdraw from Sion? Why did you strike us, and there is no healing for us? We waited for peace, and there were no good things; for a time of healing, and behold, disturbance.
Jeremiah 14:20 We knew, Lord, our sins, the injustices of our fathers, because we sinned before you.
Jeremiah 14:21 Cease for your name's sake; do not destroy the throne of your glory; remember, do not break apart your covenant with us.
Jeremiah 14:22 Is there among the idols of the nations one making rain? And will heaven give its fullness? Are you not he? And we will wait for you, because you made all these things.

## Chapter 15

Jeremiah 15:1 And the Lord said to me: If Moyses and Samouel stand before my face, my soul is not toward them; send out this people, and let them go out.
Jeremiah 15:2 And it will be, if they say to you, Where will we go out? You will say to them: Thus says the Lord: Those for death, to death; and those for sword, to sword; and those for famine, to famine; and those for captivity, to captivity.
Jeremiah 15:3 And I will exact vengeance upon them with four kinds, says the Lord: the sword for slaughter and the dogs for tearing apart and the wild beasts of the earth and the birds of heaven for eating and for destruction.
Jeremiah 15:4 And I will hand them over to constraints for all the kingdoms of the earth because of Manasse, son of Ezekias, king of Iouda, concerning all that he did in Ierusalem.
Jeremiah 15:5 Who will spare you, Ierusalem? And who will be fearful over you? Or who will turn back for peace for you?
Jeremiah 15:6 You turned away from me, says the Lord; you will go backward, and I will stretch out my hand and destroy you, and I will no longer let them go.
Jeremiah 15:7 And I will scatter them in a scattering; at the gates of my people they were bereaved of children; they destroyed my people because of their wickednesses.
Jeremiah 15:8 Their widows were multiplied beyond the sand of the sea; I brought misery upon the mother of a young man at midday; I cast upon her suddenly trembling and haste.
Jeremiah 15:9 She who gave birth to seven was emptied; her soul grew faint; her sun set while the day was still at its middle; she was put to shame and reproached; their remaining ones I will give to the sword before their enemies.
Jeremiah 15:10 Alas for me, mother, as what did you bear me? A man judged and disputed with by all the earth; neither did I benefit, nor did anyone benefit me; my strength failed among those cursing me.
Jeremiah 15:11 May it be, Master, as they direct their course, if I did not stand by you in the time of their evils and in the time of their affliction for good things toward the enemy. —
Jeremiah 15:12 Will iron be known? And a bronze covering
Jeremiah 15:13 is your strength. And your treasuries I will give as plunder, an exchange for all your sins and in all your borders.
Jeremiah 15:14 And I will enslave you to your enemies around you in the land which you did not know; because fire has been kindled from my wrath; upon you it will burn.
Jeremiah 15:15 Lord, remember me and visit me and acquit me from those pursuing me, not unto longsuffering; know how I received reproach concerning you
Jeremiah 15:16 from those rejecting your words; bring them to an end, and your word will be for me gladness and joy of my heart, because your name has been called upon me, Lord Almighty.
Jeremiah 15:17 I did not sit in their assembly as they played, but was reverent before your hand; I sat alone, because I was filled with bitterness.
Jeremiah 15:18 Why do those grieving me overpower me? My wound is firm; from where will I be healed? Coming to be, it became to me like false water having no faithfulness. —
Jeremiah 15:19 Therefore thus says the Lord: If you return, I will also restore you, and you will stand before my face; and if you bring out what is precious from what is unworthy, you will be as my mouth; and they will turn back to you, and you will not turn back to them.
Jeremiah 15:20 And I will make you for this people like a fortified bronze wall, and they will fight against you and will certainly not prevail against you, because I am with you to save you
Jeremiah 15:21 and to deliver you from the hand of evil ones, and I will redeem you from the hand of pestilent ones.

## Chapter 16

Jeremiah 16:1 And you shall not take a wife, says the Lord, the God of Israel,
Jeremiah 16:2 and no son or daughter will be born to you in this place.
Jeremiah 16:3 Because thus says the Lord concerning the sons and concerning the daughters born in this place and concerning their mothers who bore them and concerning their fathers who begot them in this land:
Jeremiah 16:4 By diseased death they will die; they will not be lamented and will not be buried; they will be for an example upon the face of the earth and for the wild beasts of the earth and for the birds of heaven; by sword they will fall and by famine they will be brought to an end.
Jeremiah 16:5 Thus says the Lord: Do not enter their gathering and do not go to lament and do not mourn them, because I have withdrawn my peace from this people.
Jeremiah 16:6 They will certainly not lament them, nor will they make incisions, and they will not shave,
Jeremiah 16:7 and bread will certainly not be broken in their mourning for consolation over one who has died; they will not give him a cup to drink for consolation over his father and mother.
Jeremiah 16:8 You will not enter a house of drinking to sit together with them to eat and drink.
Jeremiah 16:9 For thus says the Lord, the God of Israel: Behold, I am abolishing from this place before your eyes and in your days a voice of joy and a voice of gladness, a voice of bridegroom and a voice of bride.
Jeremiah 16:10 And it will be, when you announce to this people all these words, and they say to you, Why did the Lord speak all these evils against us? What is our injustice? And what is our sin which we sinned before the Lord our God?
Jeremiah 16:11 And you will say to them: Because your fathers forsook me, says the Lord, and went away after foreign gods and served them and worshipped them and forsook me and did not keep my law,
Jeremiah 16:12 and you acted more wickedly than your fathers, and behold, you go, each after the things pleasing to your evil heart, so as not to obey me,
Jeremiah 16:13 and I will cast you away from this land into the land which you and your fathers did not know, and there you will serve other gods who will not give you mercy.
Jeremiah 16:14 Therefore behold, days are coming, says the Lord, and they will no longer say, The Lord lives, who brought up the sons of Israel from the land of Egypt,
Jeremiah 16:15 but, The Lord lives, who brought up the house of Israel from the land of the north and from all the regions where they were driven out there; and I will restore them to their land which I gave to their fathers. —
Jeremiah 16:16 Behold, I am sending the many fishers, says the Lord, and they will fish for them; and after these things I will send the many hunters, and they will hunt them upon every mountain and upon every hill and out of the holes of the rocks.
Jeremiah 16:17 Because my eyes are upon all their ways, and their unjust deeds were not hidden from before my eyes.
Jeremiah 16:18 And I will repay their injustices and their sins double, for which they profaned my land with the carcasses of their abominations and with their lawless deeds, by which they offended against my inheritance. —
Jeremiah 16:19 Lord, my strength and my help and my refuge in a day of evils, nations will come to you from the end of the earth and say, How our fathers acquired false idols, and there is no benefit in them.
Jeremiah 16:20 Will a person make gods for himself? And these are not gods.
Jeremiah 16:21 Therefore behold, I will show them my hand at this time and make known my power to them, and they will know that my name is the Lord.
Jeremiah 16:5 Cursed is the person who has his hope in a person and will support the flesh of his arm upon him, and his heart departs from the Lord;
Jeremiah 16:6 and he will be like the wild tamarisk in the wilderness; he will not see when good things come, and will dwell among salt plants and in a wilderness, in a salty land which is not inhabited.
Jeremiah 16:7 And blessed is the person who has trusted in the Lord, and the Lord will be his hope;
Jeremiah 16:8 and he will be like a tree flourishing beside waters and will cast its roots into moisture and will not fear when heat comes, and upon it will be leafy trunks; in a year without rain it will not fear and will not cease making fruit. —
Jeremiah 16:9 The heart is deep beyond all things, and he is a person; and who will know him?
Jeremiah 16:10 I am the Lord examining hearts and testing kidneys, to give each according to his ways and according to the fruits of his practices. —
Jeremiah 16:11 A partridge called, gathered what she did not bear; making his wealth not with judgment, in the middle of his days they will leave him, and at his end he will be foolish.
Jeremiah 16:12 A throne of glory exalted is our sanctuary,
Jeremiah 16:13 endurance of Israel, Lord; let all those who left you be put to shame; let those who have departed be written upon the earth, because they forsook the fountain of life, the Lord. —
Jeremiah 16:14 Heal me, Lord, and I will be healed; save me, and I will be saved; because you are my boast.
Jeremiah 16:15 Behold, they say to me, Where is the word of the Lord? Let it come.
Jeremiah 16:16 But I did not weary in following after you, and I did not desire a person's day; you know; the things coming out through my lips are before your face.
Jeremiah 16:17 Do not become an estrangement for me, sparing me in an evil day.
Jeremiah 16:18 Let those pursuing me be put to shame, and may I not be put to shame; may they be terrified, and may I not be terrified; bring an evil day upon them; crush them with a double crushing.
Jeremiah 16:19 Thus says the Lord: Go and stand in the gates of the sons of your people, through which the kings of Iouda enter and through which they go out, and in all the gates of Ierusalem,
Jeremiah 16:20 and you will say to them: Hear a word of the Lord, kings of Iouda and all Ioudaia and all Ierusalem, those entering through these gates;
Jeremiah 16:21 thus says the Lord: Guard your souls and do not lift burdens on the day of the sabbaths and do not go out through the gates of Ierusalem
Jeremiah 16:22 and do not bring out burdens from your houses on the day of the sabbaths, and you shall not do any work; sanctify the day of the sabbaths, as I commanded your fathers. And they did not hear and did not incline their ear
Jeremiah 16:23 and hardened their neck beyond their fathers, so as not to hear me and not to receive discipline.
Jeremiah 16:24 And it will be, if you surely hear me, says the Lord, so as not to bring burdens through the gates of this city on the day of the sabbaths and to sanctify the day of the sabbaths so as not to do any work,
Jeremiah 16:25 then kings and rulers sitting upon the throne of David and riding upon their chariots and horses will enter through the gates of this city, they and their rulers, men of Iouda and those dwelling in Ierusalem, and this city will be inhabited forever.
Jeremiah 16:26 And they will come from the cities of Iouda and from around Ierusalem and from the land of Beniamin and from the plain and from the mountain and from the region toward the south, bringing whole burnt offerings and sacrifice and incense and manaa and frankincense, bringing praise into the house of the Lord.
Jeremiah 16:27 And it will be, if you do not listen to me to sanctify the day of the sabbaths, so as not to lift burdens and not to enter through the gates of Ierusalem on the day of the sabbaths, I will also kindle a fire in her gates, and it will devour the quarters of Ierusalem and will not be extinguished.

## Chapter 18

Jeremiah 18:1 The word that came from the Lord to Ieremias, saying,
Jeremiah 18:2 Rise and go down to the potter's house, and there you will hear my words.
Jeremiah 18:3 And I went down to the potter's house, and behold, he was doing work upon the stones;
Jeremiah 18:4 and the vessel which he was making fell apart in his hands, and again he made it another vessel, as it pleased him to make.
Jeremiah 18:5 And a word of the Lord came to me, saying,
Jeremiah 18:6 Will I not be able to make you as this potter does, house of Israel? Behold, like the potter's clay you are in my hands.
Jeremiah 18:7 At a moment I will speak concerning a nation or concerning a kingdom to remove them and to destroy,
Jeremiah 18:8 and that nation turns from all their evils, then I will change my mind concerning the evils which I planned to do to them;
Jeremiah 18:9 and at a moment I will speak concerning a nation and concerning a kingdom to be built up and to be planted,
Jeremiah 18:10 and they do evil things before me, so as not to hear my voice, then I will change my mind concerning the good things which I spoke of doing to them.
Jeremiah 18:11 And now say to the men of Iouda and to those dwelling in Ierusalem: Behold, I am forming evils against you and devising a design against you; let each now turn from his evil way, and you will make your practices better.
Jeremiah 18:12 And they said, We will act boldly, because we will go after our turnings away and each of us will do the things pleasing to his evil heart.
Jeremiah 18:13 Therefore thus says the Lord: Ask now among nations: Who heard such dreadful things as the virgin Israel did exceedingly?
Jeremiah 18:14 Will breasts cease from a rock, or snow from Libanos? Will water turn aside, carried violently by wind?
Jeremiah 18:15 Because my people forgot me, burned incense in vain; and they will weaken in their ways, ancient measured courses, to step onto paths having no road for travel,
Jeremiah 18:16 to make their land a disappearance and an everlasting hissing; all those passing through it will be astonished and will shake their head.
Jeremiah 18:17 Like a scorching wind I will scatter them before their enemies; I will show them the day of their destruction.
Jeremiah 18:18 And they said, Come, let us devise a design against Ieremias, because law will not perish from a priest and counsel from an understanding one and word from a prophet; come, and let us strike him with a tongue, and we will hear all his words. —
Jeremiah 18:19 Listen to me, Lord, and listen to the voice of my just claim.
Jeremiah 18:20 Are evils repaid in return for good things? Because they spoke words together against my soul and hid their punishment for me; remember my standing before your face to speak good things on their behalf, to turn your wrath away from them.
Jeremiah 18:21 Therefore give their sons to famine and gather them into the hands of the sword; let their wives become childless and widows, and let their men become slain by death and their young men fallen by sword in war.
Jeremiah 18:22 Let a cry arise in their houses; you will bring robbers upon them suddenly, because they undertook a plan for my capture and hid traps against me.
Jeremiah 18:23 And you, Lord, knew all their counsel against me for death; do not acquit their injustices, and do not wipe out their sins from before your face; let their weakness be before you; at the time of your wrath act among them.

## Chapter 19

Jeremiah 19:1 Then the Lord said to me: Go and acquire a molded earthenware jar, and you will bring some of the elders of the people and some of the elders of the priests
Jeremiah 19:2 and go out to the burial ground of the sons of their children, which is at the entrance of the charsith gate, and read there all the words which I speak to you,
Jeremiah 19:3 and you will say to them: Hear the word of the Lord, kings of Iouda and men of Iouda and those dwelling in Ierusalem and those entering through these gates: Thus says the Lord, the God of Israel: Behold, I am bringing evils upon this place, so that both ears of everyone hearing them will ring,
Jeremiah 19:4 because they forsook me and estranged this place and burned incense in it to foreign gods which they and their fathers did not know, and the kings of Iouda filled this place with innocent blood
Jeremiah 19:5 and built high places for Baal to burn up their sons in fire, things which I did not command or speak or think in my heart.
Jeremiah 19:6 Therefore behold, days are coming, says the Lord, and this place will no longer be called Falling and Burial Ground of the Son of Ennom, but rather Burial Ground of Slaughter.
Jeremiah 19:7 And I will slaughter the counsel of Iouda and the counsel of Ierusalem in this place and cast them down by sword before their enemies and into the hands of those seeking their lives, and I will give their dead as food to the birds of heaven and to the wild beasts of the earth.
Jeremiah 19:8 And I will make this city a disappearance and a hissing; everyone passing by it will become gloomy and hiss over all its wound.
Jeremiah 19:9 And they will eat the flesh of their sons and the flesh of their daughters, and each will eat the flesh of his neighbor in the enclosure and in the siege with which their enemies will besiege them.
Jeremiah 19:10 And you will crush the jar before the eyes of the men going out with you
Jeremiah 19:11 and say: Thus says the Lord: Thus I will crush this people and this city, as an earthenware vessel is crushed, which will no longer be able to be healed.
Jeremiah 19:12 Thus I will do, says the Lord, to this place and to those dwelling in it, to make this city like the falling one.
Jeremiah 19:13 And the houses of Ierusalem and the houses of the kings of Iouda will be like the place falling with the uncleannesses in all the houses in which they burned incense upon their roofs to all the army of heaven and poured libations to foreign gods. —
Jeremiah 19:14 And Ieremias came from the falling place where the Lord sent him there to prophesy, and stood in the courtyard of the house of the Lord and said to all the people:
Jeremiah 19:15 Thus says the Lord: Behold, I am bringing upon this city and upon all its cities and upon its villages all the evils which I spoke against it, because they hardened their neck so as not to listen to my words.

## Chapter 20

Jeremiah 20:1 And Paschor, son of Emmer, the priest, heard Ieremias prophesying these words, and this man was appointed leader of the house of the Lord.
Jeremiah 20:2 And he struck him and put him into the confinement which was at the gate of the assigned house of the upper room, which was in the house of the Lord.
Jeremiah 20:3 And Paschor brought Ieremias out of the confinement, and Ieremias said to him: The Lord did not call your name Paschor, but rather Migrant;
Jeremiah 20:4 for thus says the Lord: Behold, I am giving you over to migration with all your friends, and they will fall by the sword of their enemies, and your eyes will see, and I will give you and all Iouda into the hands of the king of Babylon, and they will deport them and cut them down with swords;
Jeremiah 20:5 and I will give all the strength of this city and all its labors and all the treasuries of the king of Iouda into the hands of his enemies, and they will bring them to Babylon.
Jeremiah 20:6 And you and all those dwelling in your house will go into captivity, and in Babylon you will die and there you will be buried, you and all your friends to whom you prophesied false things.
Jeremiah 20:7 You deceived me, Lord, and I was deceived; you prevailed and were strong; I became an object of laughter, all day I continued being mocked;
Jeremiah 20:8 because with my bitter word I will be laughed at, I will call out breach of faith and misery, because the word of the Lord became a reproach to me and a mockery all my day.
Jeremiah 20:9 And I said, I will certainly not name the name of the Lord and will certainly not speak any longer in his name; and it became like burning fire blazing in my bones, and I am exhausted on every side and cannot bear it.
Jeremiah 20:10 Because I heard the reproach of many gathering together all around: Rise against him, and let us rise against him, all men his friends; watch his intention, whether he will be deceived and we will prevail against him and take our vengeance upon him.
Jeremiah 20:11 And the Lord is with me like a strong warrior; therefore they pursued and could not understand; they were put greatly to shame, because they did not understand their dishonors, which will not be forgotten forever.
Jeremiah 20:12 Lord, testing just things, understanding kidneys and hearts, may I see the vengeance from you among them, because to you I revealed my defenses. —
Jeremiah 20:13 Sing to the Lord, praise him, because he delivered the soul of a poor person from the hand of those acting wickedly. —
Jeremiah 20:14 Cursed is the day on which I was born; the day on which my mother bore me, let it not be wished for.
Jeremiah 20:15 Cursed is the person who announced good news to my father, saying, A male was born to you, making him glad.
Jeremiah 20:16 Let that person be like the cities which the Lord overturned in wrath and did not regret; let him hear a cry in the morning and a shout at midday,
Jeremiah 20:17 because he did not kill me in my mother's womb, and my mother became my grave for me, and the womb one of everlasting conception.
Jeremiah 20:18 Why was it that I came out of the womb to see toils and sufferings, and my days continued in shame?

## Chapter 21

Jeremiah 21:1 The word that came from the Lord to Ieremias when King Sedekias sent to him Paschor, son of Melchias, and Sophonias, son of Maasaias, the priest, saying,
Jeremiah 21:2 Inquire of the Lord concerning us, because the king of Babylon has come against us, whether the Lord will act according to all his wonders, and he will go away from us.
Jeremiah 21:3 And Ieremias said to them: Thus you will say to Sedekias, king of Iouda:
Jeremiah 21:4 Thus says the Lord: Behold, I am turning the weapons of war with which you fight against the Chaldeans who have enclosed you outside the wall into the middle of this city,
Jeremiah 21:5 and I myself will fight you with an outstretched hand and with a mighty arm, with wrath and anger and great provocation,
Jeremiah 21:6 and I will strike all those dwelling in this city, the people and the cattle, with a great death, and they will die.
Jeremiah 21:7 And after these things — thus says the Lord — I will give Sedekias, king of Iouda, and his servants and the people left in this city from death and from famine and from sword into the hands of their enemies seeking their lives, and they will cut them down with the edge of the sword; I will not spare them and will certainly not pity them.
Jeremiah 21:8 And to this people you will say: Thus says the Lord: Behold, I have given before your face the way of life and the way of death;
Jeremiah 21:9 the one remaining in this city will die by sword and by famine, and the one going out to go over to the Chaldeans who have enclosed you will live, and his soul will be as spoils, and he will live.
Jeremiah 21:10 Because I have set my face upon this city for evils and not for good things; it will be handed over into the hands of the king of Babylon, and he will burn it up with fire. —
Jeremiah 21:11 House of the king of Iouda, hear a word of the Lord;
Jeremiah 21:12 house of David, thus says the Lord: Judge a judgment in the morning and direct rightly and deliver one plundered from the hand of the one wronging him, so that my anger is not kindled like fire and burns, and there will be no one extinguishing it.
Jeremiah 21:13 Behold, I am against you dwelling in the valley of Sor, the plain, those saying, Who will terrify us? Or who will enter into our dwelling place?
Jeremiah 21:14 And I will kindle a fire in her forest, and it will eat everything around her.

## Chapter 22

Jeremiah 22:1 Thus says the Lord: Go and descend to the house of the king of Iouda, and you will speak this word there
Jeremiah 22:2 and say: Hear a word of the Lord, king of Iouda sitting upon the throne of David, you and your house and your people and those entering through these gates:
Jeremiah 22:3 Thus says the Lord: Do judgment and righteousness and deliver one plundered from the hand of the one wronging him, and do not oppress a newcomer and an orphan and a widow, and do not act impiously, and do not pour out innocent blood in this place.
Jeremiah 22:4 For if you surely do this word, kings sitting upon the throne of David and riding upon chariots and horses will also enter through the gates of this house, they and their servants and their people;
Jeremiah 22:5 but if you do not do these words, by myself I swore, says the Lord, that this house will be for desolation.
Jeremiah 22:6 Because thus says the Lord against the house of the king of Iouda: You are Galaad to me, the summit of Libanos; surely I will make you a wilderness, cities that will not be inhabited;
Jeremiah 22:7 and I will bring upon you a man destroying and his axe, and they will cut down your chosen cedars and throw them into the fire.
Jeremiah 22:8 And nations will pass through this city and say, each to his neighbor, Why did the Lord do thus to this great city?
Jeremiah 22:9 And they will say, Because they forsook the covenant of the Lord their God and worshipped foreign gods and served them.
Jeremiah 22:10 Do not weep for the dead one or mourn him; weep with weeping for the one going out, because he will not return any longer and will certainly not see the land of his homeland.
Jeremiah 22:11 For thus says the Lord concerning Sellem, son of Iosias, reigning instead of Iosias his father, who went out from this place: He will not return there any longer,
Jeremiah 22:12 but in the place where I deported him, there he will die and will not see this land any longer.
Jeremiah 22:13 O the one building his house not with righteousness and his upper rooms not with judgment, he employs his neighbor without payment and will certainly not pay him his wage.
Jeremiah 22:14 You built for yourself a well-proportioned house, airy upper rooms divided by windows and paneled in cedar and painted with vermilion.
Jeremiah 22:15 Will you reign, because you are provoked with Achaz your father? They will not eat and will not drink; it was better for you to do judgment and good righteousness.
Jeremiah 22:16 They did not know, did not judge a judgment for a lowly one or a judgment of a poor one; is this not your not knowing me? says the Lord.
Jeremiah 22:17 Behold, your eyes are not good, nor is your heart, but toward your greed and toward innocent blood to pour it out and toward injustice and toward murder to do them.
Jeremiah 22:18 Therefore thus says the Lord concerning Ioakim, son of Iosias, king of Iouda: Woe upon this man; they will certainly not lament him, O brother, nor will they weep for him, Alas, lord.
Jeremiah 22:19 With an ass's burial he will be buried; dragged together, he will be thrown beyond the gate of Ierusalem.
Jeremiah 22:20 Go up to Libanos and cry out, and in Basan raise your voice, and shout to the other side of the sea, because all your lovers were crushed.
Jeremiah 22:21 I spoke to you in your transgression, and you said, I will not hear; this is your way from your youth; you did not hear my voice.
Jeremiah 22:22 Wind will shepherd all your shepherds, and your lovers will go out into captivity; because then you will be ashamed and dishonored by all those loving you.
Jeremiah 22:23 You dwelling in Libanos, nesting in the cedars, will groan when pangs come to you as to a woman giving birth.
Jeremiah 22:24 I live, says the Lord; even if Iechonias, son of Ioakim, king of Iouda, should become a seal upon my right hand, from there I will tear you away
Jeremiah 22:25 and hand you over into the hands of those seeking your life, before whose face you are fearful, into the hands of the Chaldeans;
Jeremiah 22:26 and I will cast you and your mother who bore you into a land where you were not born, and there you will die;
Jeremiah 22:27 but to the land which they long for in their souls they will certainly not return.
Jeremiah 22:28 Iechonias was dishonored like a vessel for which there is no use, because he was thrown out and cast into a land which he did not know.
Jeremiah 22:29 Earth, earth, hear a word of the Lord:
Jeremiah 22:30 Write this man down as an outlawed person, because there will certainly not grow from his seed a man sitting upon the throne of David, ruling any longer in Iouda.

## Chapter 23

Jeremiah 23:1 O the shepherds scattering and destroying the sheep of my pasture.
Jeremiah 23:2 Therefore thus says the Lord concerning those shepherding my people: You scattered my sheep and drove them out and did not visit them; behold, I am exacting vengeance upon you according to your evil practices;
Jeremiah 23:3 and I will receive the remaining ones of my people from all the land where I drove them out there, and I will restore them to their pasture, and they will increase and multiply;
Jeremiah 23:4 and I will raise up shepherds for them who will shepherd them, and they will no longer fear or be terrified, says the Lord.
Jeremiah 23:5 Behold, days are coming, says the Lord, and I will raise up for David a righteous shoot, and a king will reign and understand and do judgment and righteousness upon the earth.
Jeremiah 23:6 In his days Ioudas will be saved, and Israel will dwell confidently, and this is his name which the Lord will call him: Iosedek.
Jeremiah 23:9 Among the prophets my heart was crushed; within me all my bones were shaken; I became like a crushed man and like a person held fast by wine, because of the face of the Lord and because of the face of the splendor of his glory.
Jeremiah 23:10 Because on account of these the land mourned, the pastures of the wilderness dried up, and their course became evil and their strength not thus.
Jeremiah 23:11 Because priest and prophet were defiled, and in my house I saw their wickednesses.
Jeremiah 23:12 Therefore let their way become for them a slipping place in gloom, and they will be tripped and fall in it; for I will bring evils upon them in the year of their visitation, says the Lord.
Jeremiah 23:13 And among the prophets of Samareia I saw lawless deeds; they prophesied through Baal and led my people Israel astray.
Jeremiah 23:14 And among the prophets of Ierusalem I have seen dreadful things, committing adultery and walking in falsehoods and supporting the hands of evil ones, so that each does not turn from his evil way; they all became to me like Sodoma, and those dwelling in her like Gomorra.
Jeremiah 23:15 Therefore thus says the Lord: Behold, I will feed them pain and give them bitter water to drink, because from the prophets of Ierusalem defilement went out to all the earth.
Jeremiah 23:16 Thus says the Lord Almighty: Do not hear the words of the prophets, because they make a vision vain for themselves; they speak from their heart and not from the mouth of the Lord.
Jeremiah 23:17 They say to those thrusting away the word of the Lord, Peace will be for you; and to all those walking by their own wishes, to everyone walking in the error of his heart they said, Evils will not come upon you.
Jeremiah 23:18 Because who stood in the council of the Lord and saw his word? Who gave ear and heard?
Jeremiah 23:19 Behold, a shaking from the Lord, and anger goes out into a convulsion; whirling, it will come upon the impious.
Jeremiah 23:20 And the wrath of the Lord will no longer turn back until he does it and until he raises it up from the undertaking of his heart; at the end of the days they will understand these things.
Jeremiah 23:21 I was not sending the prophets, and they were running; I did not speak to them, and they were prophesying.
Jeremiah 23:22 And if they had stood in my council and listened to my words, they would also have turned my people away from their evil practices.
Jeremiah 23:23 I am a God drawing near, says the Lord, and not a God from far away.
Jeremiah 23:24 Will a person hide in hidden places, and I will not see him? Do I not fill heaven and earth? says the Lord.
Jeremiah 23:25 I heard what the prophets speak, what false things they prophesy in my name, saying, I dreamed a dream.
Jeremiah 23:26 Until when will it be in the heart of the prophets prophesying false things, and in their prophesying the wishes of their heart?
Jeremiah 23:27 Of those planning to forget my law in their dreams which they related, each to his neighbor, just as their fathers forgot my name through Baal.
Jeremiah 23:28 The prophet in whom the dream is, let him relate his dream, and the one to whom my word comes, let him relate my word in truth. What is chaff to grain? Thus are my words, says the Lord;
Jeremiah 23:29 are not my words like blazing fire, says the Lord, and like an axe cutting a rock?
Jeremiah 23:30 Therefore behold, I am against the prophets, says the Lord God, those stealing my words, each from his neighbor.
Jeremiah 23:31 Behold, I am against the prophets bringing forth prophecies of a tongue and dozing with their own dozing.
Jeremiah 23:32 Behold, I am against the prophets prophesying false dreams, and they related them and led my people astray with their falsehoods and with their errors, and I did not send them and did not command them, and they will not benefit this people with any benefit.
Jeremiah 23:33 And if this people or priest or prophet asks you, saying, What is the burden of the Lord? You will say to them, You are the burden, and I will dash you down, says the Lord.
Jeremiah 23:34 And the prophet and the priest and the people who say, Burden of the Lord, I will also exact vengeance on that person and his house.
Jeremiah 23:35 Because thus you will say, each to his neighbor and each to his brother: What did the Lord answer, and what did the Lord speak?
Jeremiah 23:36 And do not name Burden of the Lord any longer, because his word will be the burden for the person;
Jeremiah 23:37 and why did the Lord our God speak?
Jeremiah 23:38 Therefore thus says the Lord God: Because you said this word, Burden of the Lord, and I sent to you, saying, You shall not say Burden of the Lord,
Jeremiah 23:39 therefore behold, I am taking and dashing down you and the city which I gave to you and to your fathers,
Jeremiah 23:40 and I will put upon you everlasting reproach and everlasting dishonor, which will not be forgotten.
Jeremiah 23:7 Therefore behold, days are coming, says the Lord, and they will no longer say, The Lord lives, who brought up the house of Israel from the land of Egypt,
Jeremiah 23:8 but, The Lord lives, who gathered all the seed of Israel from the land of the north and from all the regions where he drove them out there, and restored them to their land.

## Chapter 24

Jeremiah 24:1 The Lord showed me two baskets of figs lying before the temple of the Lord, after Nabouchodonosor, king of Babylon, deported Iechonias, son of Ioakim, king of Iouda, and the rulers and the craftsmen and the prisoners and the rich from Ierusalem and brought them to Babylon;
Jeremiah 24:2 one basket of very good figs, like the early figs, and the other basket of very bad figs, which will not be eaten because of their badness.
Jeremiah 24:3 And the Lord said to me: What do you see, Ieremias? And I said, Figs; the good ones very good, and the bad ones very bad, which will not be eaten because of their badness.
Jeremiah 24:4 And a word of the Lord came to me, saying,
Jeremiah 24:5 Thus says the Lord, the God of Israel: Like these good figs, thus I will recognize the deported ones of Iouda whom I have sent out from this place into the land of the Chaldeans for good things.
Jeremiah 24:6 And I will set my eyes upon them for good things and restore them to this land for good things and build them up and will certainly not pull them down and plant them and will certainly not pluck them out;
Jeremiah 24:7 and I will give them a heart for them to know me, that I am the Lord, and they will be a people for me, and I will be a God for them, because they will return to me with all their heart.
Jeremiah 24:8 And like the bad figs which will not be eaten because of their badness, thus says the Lord, thus I will hand over Sedekias, king of Iouda, and his great ones and the remnant of Ierusalem, those left in this land and those dwelling in Egypt;
Jeremiah 24:9 and I will give them over to scattering into all the kingdoms of the earth, and they will be for reproach and for a parable and for hatred and for a curse in every place where I drove them out there;
Jeremiah 24:10 and I will send famine and death and sword among them until they cease from the land which I gave them.

## Chapter 25

Jeremiah 25:1 The word that came to Ieremias concerning all the people of Iouda in the fourth year of Ioakim, son of Iosias, king of Iouda,
Jeremiah 25:2 which he spoke to all the people of Iouda and to those dwelling in Ierusalem, saying,
Jeremiah 25:3 In the thirteenth year of Iosias, son of Amos, king of Iouda, and until this day, twenty-three years, and I spoke to you, rising early and saying,
Jeremiah 25:4 and I was sending to you my servants the prophets, sending at dawn, and you did not listen and did not attend with your ears,
Jeremiah 25:5 saying, Turn, each from his evil way and from your evil practices, and you will dwell upon the land which I gave to you and to your fathers from eternity and unto eternity;
Jeremiah 25:6 do not go after foreign gods to serve them and to worship them, so that you do not provoke me with the works of your hands, for me to harm you.
Jeremiah 25:7 And you did not hear me.
Jeremiah 25:8 Therefore thus says the Lord: Since you did not believe my words,
Jeremiah 25:9 behold, I am sending and will take the family from the north and bring them upon this land and upon those dwelling in it and upon all the nations around it, and I will utterly desolate them and give them over to disappearance and to hissing and to everlasting reproach;
Jeremiah 25:10 and I will destroy from them a voice of joy and a voice of gladness, a voice of bridegroom and a voice of bride, a smell of myrrh and a light of a lamp.
Jeremiah 25:11 And all the land will be for disappearance, and they will serve among the nations seventy years.
Jeremiah 25:12 And when the seventy years are fulfilled, I will exact vengeance on that nation, says the Lord, and make them an everlasting disappearance;
Jeremiah 25:13 and I will bring upon that land all my words which I spoke against it, all the things written in this book.
Jeremiah 25:14 What Ieremias prophesied concerning the nations, Ailam.
Jeremiah 25:15 Thus says the Lord: Let the bow of Ailam be crushed, the beginning of their dominion.
Jeremiah 25:16 And I will bring upon Ailam four winds from the four ends of heaven and scatter them among all these winds, and there will be no nation where the outcasts of Ailam will not come.
Jeremiah 25:17 And I will terrify them before their enemies seeking their life and bring evils upon them according to the anger of my wrath and send my sword after them until I consume them.
Jeremiah 25:18 And I will set my throne in Ailam and send out from there king and great ones.
Jeremiah 25:19 And it will be at the end of the days, I will turn back the captivity of Ailam, says the Lord. —
Jeremiah 25:20 At the beginning of King Sedekias reigning, this word came concerning Ailam.
Jeremiah 25:2 For Egypt, concerning the force of Pharao Nechao, king of Egypt, who was at the Euphrates river in Charchamis, whom Nabouchodonosor, king of Babylon, struck in the fourth year of Ioakim, king of Iouda.
Jeremiah 25:3 Take up weapons and shields and bring them forward into war;
Jeremiah 25:4 saddle the horses; mount, horsemen, and take your stand in your helmets; put forward the spears and put on your breastplates.
Jeremiah 25:5 Why are they terrified and retreating backward? Because their strong ones will be cut down. They fled with flight and did not turn back, surrounded all around, says the Lord.
Jeremiah 25:6 Let the swift one not flee, and let the strong one not escape; toward the north, the things beside the Euphrates grew weak, have fallen.
Jeremiah 25:7 Who is this that will rise like a river, and like rivers water surges?
Jeremiah 25:8 The waters of Egypt will rise like a river, and he said, I will rise and cover land and destroy those dwelling in it.
Jeremiah 25:9 Mount the horses, prepare the chariots; go out, the warriors of Ethiopians and Libyans fully armed with weapons; and Lydians, go up, stretch a bow.
Jeremiah 25:10 And that day is for the Lord our God a day of vengeance to exact vengeance on his enemies, and the sword of the Lord will devour and be filled and be drunk from their blood, because there is a sacrifice for the Lord Sabaoth from the land of the north upon the Euphrates river.
Jeremiah 25:11 Go up, Galaad, and take resin for the virgin daughter of Egypt; in vain you multiplied your remedies; there is no benefit for you.
Jeremiah 25:12 Nations heard your voice, and the earth was filled with your cry, because warrior against warrior grew weak; together both fell.
Jeremiah 25:13 What the Lord spoke by the hand of Ieremias concerning Nabouchodonosor, the king of Babylon, coming to strike the land of Egypt.
Jeremiah 25:14 Announce in Magdolon and proclaim in Memphis; say, Stand ready and prepare, because a sword devoured your smilax.
Jeremiah 25:15 Why did Apis flee? Your chosen calf did not remain, because the Lord disabled him.
Jeremiah 25:16 And your multitude grew weak and fell, and each spoke to his neighbor: Let us rise and return to our people into our homeland from before a Greek sword.
Jeremiah 25:17 Call the name of Pharao Nechao, king of Egypt, Saon — esbi — emoed.
Jeremiah 25:18 I live, says the Lord God, because like Itabyrion among the mountains and like Karmel in the sea he will come.
Jeremiah 25:19 Make equipment for deportation for yourself, dwelling daughter of Egypt, because Memphis will be for disappearance and will be called Woe, because there are no inhabitants in her.
Jeremiah 25:20 Egypt is an adorned heifer; a detachment from the north came upon her.
Jeremiah 25:21 And her hired men in her are like fattened calves fed in her, because they too turned back and fled with one accord, did not stand, because a day of destruction came upon them and a time of their vengeance.
Jeremiah 25:22 A voice like a snake hissing, because they will travel in sand; with axes they will come upon her like those cutting wood.
Jeremiah 25:23 They will cut down her forest, says the Lord God, because it will certainly not be estimated, because it multiplies beyond a locust, and they have no number.
Jeremiah 25:24 The daughter of Egypt was put to shame, handed over into the hands of a people from the north.
Jeremiah 25:25 Behold, I am exacting vengeance on Amon her son, upon Pharao and upon those trusting in him.
Jeremiah 25:27 But you, do not fear, my servant Iakob, nor be terrified, Israel, because behold, I am saving you from far away and your seed from their captivity, and Iakob will return and be quiet and sleep, and there will be no one troubling him.
Jeremiah 25:28 Do not fear, my servant Iakob, says the Lord, because I am with you; because I will make an end among every nation into which I drove you out there, but I will certainly not make you cease; and I will discipline you with judgment and will not acquit you as innocent.

## Chapter 27

Jeremiah 27:1 A word of the Lord which he spoke concerning Babylon.
Jeremiah 27:2 Announce among the nations and make heard and do not hide; say, Babylon has been captured; Belos was put to shame, the fearless one; the delicate one, Marodach, was handed over.
Jeremiah 27:3 Because a nation went up against her from the north; this one will make her land a disappearance, and there will be no inhabitant in her, from person even to cattle.
Jeremiah 27:4 In those days and at that time the sons of Israel will come, they and the sons of Iouda together; walking and weeping they will go, seeking the Lord their God.
Jeremiah 27:5 As far as Sion they will ask the way, for toward here they will turn their face; and they will come and take refuge with the Lord God, for an everlasting covenant will not be forgotten.
Jeremiah 27:6 My people became lost sheep; their shepherds drove them out, led them astray onto the mountains; from mountain to hill they went, forgot their bed.
Jeremiah 27:7 All those finding them consumed them; their enemies said, Let us not let them go, because they sinned against the Lord, the pasture of righteousness, who gathered their fathers.
Jeremiah 27:8 Be estranged from the midst of Babylon and from the land of the Chaldeans, and go out and become like dragons before sheep.
Jeremiah 27:9 Because behold, I am raising assemblies of nations against Babylon from the land of the north, and they will array themselves against her; from there she will be captured, like a dart of an understanding warrior it will not return empty.
Jeremiah 27:10 And Chaldaia will be for plunder; all those plundering her will be filled.
Jeremiah 27:11 Because you were glad and boasted, plundering my inheritance, because you were leaping like young cattle in vegetation and butting like bulls.
Jeremiah 27:12 Your mother was put greatly to shame, a mother for good things, last of nations, a wilderness.
Jeremiah 27:13 Because of the anger of the Lord she will not be inhabited and will be entirely for disappearance, and everyone traversing Babylon will become gloomy, and they will hiss over all her wound.
Jeremiah 27:14 Array yourselves against Babylon all around, all those stretching a bow; shoot at her, do not spare your arrows.
Jeremiah 27:15 Clap against her; her hands were disabled, her battlements fell, and her wall was razed; because it is vengeance from God, exact vengeance upon her; as she did, do to her.
Jeremiah 27:16 Destroy seed from Babylon, the one holding a sickle at harvest time; from before a Greek sword each will return to his people and each will flee to his land.
Jeremiah 27:17 Israel is a wandering sheep; lions drove him out; the first ate him, the king of Assour, and this one afterward his bones, the king of Babylon.
Jeremiah 27:18 Therefore thus says the Lord: Behold, I am exacting vengeance upon the king of Babylon and upon his land, as I exacted vengeance upon the king of Assour.
Jeremiah 27:19 And I will restore Israel to his pasture, and he will graze in Karmel and on the mountain of Ephraim and in Galaad, and his soul will be filled.
Jeremiah 27:20 In those days and at that time they will seek the injustice of Israel, and it will not exist, and the sins of Iouda, and they will certainly not be found, because I will be merciful to those left upon the earth, says the Lord.
Jeremiah 27:21 Bitterly advance upon her and upon those dwelling upon her; exact vengeance, sword, and make disappear, says the Lord, and do according to everything that I command you.
Jeremiah 27:22 A sound of war and great crushing in the land of the Chaldeans.
Jeremiah 27:23 How was the hammer of all the earth broken together and crushed? How did Babylon become a disappearance among nations?
Jeremiah 27:24 They will attack you, and you will be captured, O Babylon, and you will not know; you were found and taken, because you opposed the Lord.
Jeremiah 27:25 The Lord opened his treasury and brought out the instruments of his anger, because there is work for the Lord God in the land of the Chaldeans,
Jeremiah 27:26 because her times have come. Open her storehouses, search her like a cave and destroy her; let there be no remnant of her;
Jeremiah 27:27 dry up all her fruits, and let them go down to slaughter; woe to them, because their day has come and the time of their vengeance.
Jeremiah 27:28 A voice of those fleeing and escaping from the land of Babylon, to announce in Sion the vengeance from the Lord our God.
Jeremiah 27:29 Give orders against Babylon to many, to everyone stretching a bow; encamp against her all around; let there be no one escaping from her; repay her according to her works; according to all that she did, do to her, because she opposed the Lord, the holy God of Israel.
Jeremiah 27:30 Therefore her young men will fall in her broad streets, and all her men of war will be cast down, said the Lord.
Jeremiah 27:31 Behold, I am against you, the arrogant woman, says the Lord, because your day has come and the time of your vengeance;
Jeremiah 27:32 and your arrogance will grow weak and fall, and there will be no one raising her; and I will kindle fire in her forest, and it will devour everything around her.
Jeremiah 27:33 Thus says the Lord: The sons of Israel and the sons of Iouda have been oppressed together; all those taking them captive oppressed them, because they did not wish to send them away.
Jeremiah 27:34 And the one redeeming them is strong; the Lord Almighty is his name; he will judge a judgment against his adversaries, so that he may remove the earth, and he will provoke those dwelling in Babylon.
Jeremiah 27:35 A sword upon the Chaldeans and upon those dwelling in Babylon and upon her great ones and upon her understanding ones;
Jeremiah 27:36 a sword upon her warriors, and they will be disabled;
Jeremiah 27:37 a sword upon their horses and upon their chariots; a sword upon their warriors and upon the mixed multitude in her midst, and they will be like women; a sword upon her treasuries, and they will be scattered.
Jeremiah 27:38 She had trusted in her water, and they will be put to shame, because it is a land of carved images, and in the islands where they boasted.
Jeremiah 27:39 Therefore phantoms will dwell in the islands, and daughters of sirens will dwell in her; she will certainly not be inhabited any longer forever.
Jeremiah 27:40 As God overturned Sodoma and Gomorra and those bordering them, said the Lord, a person will certainly not dwell there, and a son of man will certainly not sojourn there.
Jeremiah 27:41 Behold, a people is coming from the north, and a great nation and many kings will be raised from the end of the earth,
Jeremiah 27:42 having bow and dagger; it is rash and will certainly not show mercy; their voice will resound like a sea; they will ride upon horses, prepared like fire for war against you, daughter of Babylon.
Jeremiah 27:43 The king of Babylon heard the report of them, and his hands were disabled; affliction held him fast, pangs like those of a woman giving birth.
