Jeremiah 27:44 Behold, like a lion he will go up from the Iordan to a place of Aitham, because swiftly I will drive them away from her and set every young man over her. Because who is like me? And who will oppose me? And who is this shepherd who will stand before my face?
Jeremiah 27:45 Therefore hear the counsel of the Lord which he has counseled against Babylon and his designs which he devised against the Chaldean inhabitants; surely the lambs of their sheep will be destroyed, surely pasture will disappear from them.
Jeremiah 27:46 Because from the sound of the capture of Babylon the earth will be shaken, and a cry will be heard among nations.

## Chapter 28

Jeremiah 28:1 Thus says the Lord: Behold, I am raising against Babylon and against the Chaldean inhabitants a scorching wind destroying.
Jeremiah 28:2 And I will send insolent ones into Babylon, and they will outrage her and ravage her land; woe upon Babylon all around in the day of her mistreatment.
Jeremiah 28:3 Against her let the one stretching stretch his bow, and let the one who has weapons put them on, and do not spare her young men, and make all her force disappear,
Jeremiah 28:4 and wounded ones will fall in the land of the Chaldeans and pierced ones outside her.
Jeremiah 28:5 Because Israel and Ioudas were not widowed from their God, from the Lord Almighty; because their land was filled with injustice from the holy things of Israel.
Jeremiah 28:6 Flee from the midst of Babylon, and save, each, his soul, and do not be cast away in her injustice, because it is the time of her vengeance from the Lord; he repays her a repayment.
Jeremiah 28:7 Babylon is a golden cup in the hand of the Lord, making all the earth drunk; nations drank from her wine; therefore they were shaken.
Jeremiah 28:8 And suddenly Babylon fell and was crushed; mourn her, take resin for her destruction, if somehow she will be healed.
Jeremiah 28:9 We treated Babylon, and she was not healed; let us leave her and go away, each to his land, because her judgment reached heaven, rose up to the stars.
Jeremiah 28:10 The Lord brought forth his judgment; come, and let us announce in Sion the works of the Lord our God.
Jeremiah 28:11 Prepare the arrows, fill the quivers; the Lord raised the spirit of the king of the Medes, because his anger is toward Babylon to destroy her, because it is the Lord's vengeance, it is vengeance for his people.
Jeremiah 28:12 Upon the walls of Babylon raise a sign, set up quivers, raise guards, prepare weapons, because the Lord undertook and will do what he spoke against those dwelling in Babylon,
Jeremiah 28:13 dwelling upon many waters and upon the abundance of her treasuries; your end has come truly into your inward parts.
Jeremiah 28:14 Because the Lord swore by his arm: For I will fill you with people like locusts, and those descending will raise their voice against you. —
Jeremiah 28:15 Making earth in his strength, preparing the inhabited world in his wisdom, in his understanding he stretched out heaven,
Jeremiah 28:16 at a voice he established a sound of water in heaven and brought up clouds from the end of the earth, made lightning for rain and brought out light from his treasuries.
Jeremiah 28:17 Every person became foolish away from knowledge; every goldsmith was put to shame by his carved images, because they cast false things; there is no spirit in them;
Jeremiah 28:18 they are vain, works made a mockery of; at the time of their visitation they will perish.
Jeremiah 28:19 Such is not the portion for Iakob, because he who formed all things is himself his inheritance; the Lord is his name. —
Jeremiah 28:20 You scatter instruments of war for me, and I will scatter nations in you and remove kings from you
Jeremiah 28:21 and scatter in you horse and its rider and scatter in you chariots and their riders
Jeremiah 28:22 and scatter in you young man and virgin and scatter in you man and woman
Jeremiah 28:23 and scatter in you shepherd and his flock and scatter in you farmer and his cultivation and scatter in you your leaders and commanders.
Jeremiah 28:24 And I will repay Babylon and all the Chaldean inhabitants all their wickednesses which they did to Sion before your eyes, says the Lord.
Jeremiah 28:25 Behold, I am against you, the destroyed mountain destroying all the earth, and I will stretch out my hand upon you and roll you down from the rocks and make you like a burned mountain,
Jeremiah 28:26 and they will certainly not take from you a stone for a corner and a stone for a foundation, because you will be for disappearance forever, says the Lord.
Jeremiah 28:27 Raise a sign upon the earth, trumpet among nations with a trumpet, consecrate nations against her, give orders against her to the kingdoms of Ararat from me and to the Aschanazaians, set up arrow engines against her, bring up against her horses like a multitude of locusts.
Jeremiah 28:28 Consecrate nations against her, the king of the Medes and of all the earth, his leaders and all his commanders.
Jeremiah 28:29 The earth was shaken and suffered, because the design of the Lord rose against Babylon to make the land of Babylon a disappearance and for her not to be inhabited.
Jeremiah 28:30 The warrior of Babylon ceased fighting; they will sit there in an enclosure; their dominion was shattered; they became like women; her dwellings were burned, her bars were crushed;
Jeremiah 28:31 one pursuing will pursue to meet one pursuing, and one announcing to meet one announcing, to announce to the king of Babylon that his city has been captured,
Jeremiah 28:32 from the end of his crossings they were taken, and their assembled structures they burned with fire, and his men of war are going out.
Jeremiah 28:33 For thus says the Lord: The houses of the king of Babylon will be threshed like a ripe threshing floor; yet a little while, and her harvest will come.
Jeremiah 28:34 Nabouchodonosor, king of Babylon, devoured me, divided me, seized me, a delicate vessel; he swallowed me like a dragon, filled his belly, drove me out from my luxury;
Jeremiah 28:35 my toils and my miseries upon Babylon, she dwelling in Sion will say, and my blood upon the Chaldean inhabitants, Ierusalem will say.
Jeremiah 28:36 Therefore thus says the Lord: Behold, I will judge your adversary and exact your vengeance and desolate her sea and dry up her fountain,
Jeremiah 28:37 and Babylon will be for disappearance and will not be inhabited.
Jeremiah 28:38 Together they were roused like lions and like young lions.
Jeremiah 28:39 In their heat I will give them a drink and make them drunk, so that they are stupefied and sleep an everlasting sleep and certainly do not rise, says the Lord;
Jeremiah 28:40 I will bring them down like lambs to slaughter and like rams with kids.
Jeremiah 28:41 How was the boast of all the earth captured and hunted? How did Babylon become a disappearance among the nations?
Jeremiah 28:42 The sea went up over Babylon with the sound of its waves, and she was covered.
Jeremiah 28:43 Her cities became a waterless and impassable land; not even one will dwell in her, nor will a son of man lodge in her.
Jeremiah 28:44 And I will exact vengeance upon Babylon and bring out what she swallowed from her mouth, and the nations will certainly not gather to her any longer.
Jeremiah 28:49 And in Babylon wounded ones of all the earth will fall.
Jeremiah 28:50 You escaping from the land, go and do not stand; those far away, remember the Lord, and let Ierusalem come up upon your heart.
Jeremiah 28:51 We were put to shame, because we heard our reproach; dishonor covered our face; foreigners entered our holy places, into the house of the Lord.
Jeremiah 28:52 Therefore behold, days are coming, says the Lord, and I will exact vengeance upon her carved images, and in all her land wounded ones will fall.
Jeremiah 28:53 Because if Babylon goes up like heaven and if she fortifies the height of her strength, from me those destroying her will come, says the Lord.
Jeremiah 28:54 A sound of a cry in Babylon, and great crushing in the land of the Chaldeans,
Jeremiah 28:55 because the Lord destroyed Babylon and destroyed from her a great voice resounding like many waters; he gave her voice over to ruin.
Jeremiah 28:56 Because misery came upon Babylon, her warriors were captured, their bow is terrified, because God repays them; the Lord repays her the repayment;
Jeremiah 28:57 and he will make her leaders and her wise ones and her commanders drunk with drunkenness, says the king; the Lord Almighty is his name.
Jeremiah 28:58 Thus says the Lord: The wall of Babylon was widened; being razed it will be razed, and her high gates will be burned, and peoples will not toil in vain, and nations will fail at the beginning.
Jeremiah 28:59 The word which the Lord commanded Ieremias the prophet to say to Saraias, son of Nerias, son of Maasaias, when he went from Sedekias, king of Iouda, to Babylon in the fourth year of his reign, and Saraias was ruler of gifts;
Jeremiah 28:60 and Ieremias wrote all the evils which will come upon Babylon in one book, all these words written concerning Babylon.
Jeremiah 28:61 And Ieremias said to Saraias: When you come to Babylon, you will also see and read all these words
Jeremiah 28:62 and say: Lord, Lord, you spoke against this place to destroy it and for there to be no inhabitants in it, from person to cattle, because it will be a disappearance forever.
Jeremiah 28:63 And it will be, when you cease reading this book, you will also bind a stone upon it and throw it into the midst of the Euphrates
Jeremiah 28:64 and say: Thus Babylon will sink and will certainly not rise because of the evils which I am bringing upon her.

## Chapter 29

Jeremiah 29:1 Concerning the foreigners.
Jeremiah 29:2 Thus says the Lord: Behold, waters rise from the north and will become an overflowing torrent and flood land and its fullness, a city and those dwelling in it; and the people will cry, and all those dwelling in the land will shout.
Jeremiah 29:3 From the sound of his rush, from the hooves of his feet and from the shaking of his chariots, the sound of his wheels, fathers did not turn back to their sons because of the failing of their hands
Jeremiah 29:4 on the coming day to destroy all the foreigners; and I will make Tyre and Sidon and all the remaining ones of their help disappear, because the Lord will destroy the remaining ones of the islands.
Jeremiah 29:5 Baldness has come upon Gaza; Askalon was cast away, and the remaining ones of Enakim. Until when will you cut,
Jeremiah 29:6 sword of the Lord? Until when will you not be quiet? Return to your sheath, rest and be lifted up.
Jeremiah 29:7 How will it be quiet? And the Lord commanded it against Askalon and against the seaside places, against the remaining ones, to rise up.

## Chapter 30

Jeremiah 30:1 For Idoumaia. Thus says the Lord: There is no longer wisdom in Thaiman; counsel perished from understanding ones; their wisdom went away,
Jeremiah 30:2 their place was deceived. Go deep for dwelling, those dwelling in Daidan, because he did difficult things; I brought them upon him at the time at which I visited upon him.
Jeremiah 30:3 Because grape gatherers came to you, they will not leave remnants for you; like thieves in the night they will lay on their hand.
Jeremiah 30:4 Because I stripped Esau, uncovered their hidden things; they will certainly not be able to hide; they perished through the hand of his brother and his neighbor, and it is not possible
Jeremiah 30:5 for your orphan to remain so that he may live; and I will live, and widows have trusted in me.
Jeremiah 30:6 Because thus said the Lord: Those for whom it was not a law to drink the cup drank; and you, being acquitted, will certainly not be acquitted, because you will surely drink;
Jeremiah 30:7 because by myself I swore, says the Lord, that you will be for an impassable place and for reproach and for a curse in her midst, and all her cities will be desolate forever.
Jeremiah 30:8 I heard a report from the Lord, and he sent messengers to nations: Gather and come to her, rise for war.
Jeremiah 30:9 I made you small among nations, easily despised among people.
Jeremiah 30:10 Your mockery undertook against you; the rashness of your heart lodged in holes of rocks, seized the strength of a high hill; because he raised his nest like an eagle, from there I will bring you down.
Jeremiah 30:11 And Idoumaia will be an impassable place; everyone passing by her will hiss.
Jeremiah 30:12 Just as Sodoma and Gomorra and her neighboring places were overturned, said the Lord Almighty, a person will certainly not sit there, and a son of man will certainly not dwell there.
Jeremiah 30:13 Behold, like a lion he will go up from the midst of the Iordan to a place of Aitham, because swiftly I will drive them away from her; and set the young men over her. Because who is like me? And who will oppose me? And who is this shepherd who will stand before my face?
Jeremiah 30:14 Therefore hear the counsel of the Lord which he counseled against Idoumaia, and his design which he devised against those dwelling in Thaiman: Surely the least of the sheep will be dragged together, surely their lodging upon her will be made impassable;
Jeremiah 30:15 because from the sound of their fall the earth was shaken, and your cry was heard in the sea.
Jeremiah 30:16 Behold, like an eagle he will look and stretch his wings over her fortifications; and the heart of the strong ones of Idoumaia on that day will be like the heart of a woman in labor.
Jeremiah 30:17 For the sons of Ammon. Thus said the Lord: Are there no sons in Israel, or have they no one to inherit? Why did Melchom inherit Gad, and their people will dwell in their cities?
Jeremiah 30:18 Therefore behold, days are coming, says the Lord, and I will cause a clamor of wars to be heard against Rabbath, and they will be for an impassable place and for destruction, and her altars will be burned up with fire, and Israel will inherit his rule.
Jeremiah 30:19 Shout, Esebon, because Gai perished; cry out, daughters of Rabbath, gird yourselves with sackcloths and lament and mourn over Melchom, because he will go into deportation, his priests and his rulers together.
Jeremiah 30:20 Why will you exult in the plains of Enakim, daughter of rashness, trusting in her treasuries, saying, Who will come against me?
Jeremiah 30:21 Behold, I am bringing fear upon you, said the Lord, from all your surrounding region, and you will be scattered, each straight before him, and there will be no one gathering.
Jeremiah 30:23 For Kedar, queen of the courtyard, whom Nabouchodonosor, king of Babylon, struck. Thus said the Lord: Rise and go up against Kedar and fill the sons of Kedem;
Jeremiah 30:24 they will take their tents and their sheep; their garments and all their equipment and their camels they will take for themselves; and call destruction upon them all around.
Jeremiah 30:25 Flee exceedingly, go deep for dwelling, those sitting in the courtyard, because the king of Babylon counseled counsel against you and devised a design against you.
Jeremiah 30:26 Rise and go up against a stable nation sitting at rest, who have no doors, no bolts, no bars; they lodge alone.
Jeremiah 30:27 And their camels will be for plunder and the multitude of their cattle for destruction; and I will winnow them with every wind, those shorn before their face; from every side of them I will bring their rout, said the Lord.
Jeremiah 30:28 And the courtyard will be a dwelling of sparrows and impassable forever; a person will certainly not sit there, and a son of man will certainly not dwell there.
Jeremiah 30:29 For Damascus. Emath and Arphad were put to shame, because they heard an evil report; they were astonished, became angry, will certainly not be able to rest.
Jeremiah 30:30 Damascus grew faint, turned to flight; trembling seized her.
Jeremiah 30:31 How did he not leave my city? They loved a village.
Jeremiah 30:32 Therefore young men will fall in your broad streets, and all your men of war will fall, says the Lord;
Jeremiah 30:33 and I will burn a fire in the wall of Damascus, and it will devour the quarters of the son of Ader.

## Chapter 31

Jeremiah 31:1 For Moab. Thus said the Lord: Woe upon Nabau, because it perished; Kariathaim was taken; Amath was put to shame and defeated.
Jeremiah 31:2 There is no longer healing for Moab, a proud boast in Esebon; they devised evils against her; we cut her off from a nation, and she will surely cease; a sword will go behind you.
Jeremiah 31:3 Because a voice of those crying out from Oronaim, ruin and great crushing:
Jeremiah 31:4 Moab was crushed; announce in Zogora.
Jeremiah 31:5 Because Alaoth was filled with weeping, he will go up weeping on the way of Oronaim; you heard a cry of crushing:
Jeremiah 31:6 Flee and save your souls, and you will be like a wild ass in a wilderness.
Jeremiah 31:7 Since you had trusted in your fortifications, you too will be captured; and Chamos will go out into deportation, his priests and his rulers together.
Jeremiah 31:8 And ruin will come upon every city, and a city will certainly not be saved, and the valley will perish, and the plain will be destroyed, as the Lord said.
Jeremiah 31:9 Give signs to Moab, because with a kindling she will be kindled, and all her cities will be for an impassable place; from where is an inhabitant for her?
Jeremiah 31:10 Cursed is the one doing the works of the Lord carelessly, withdrawing his sword from blood.
Jeremiah 31:11 Moab rested from childhood and was trusting in his glory; he did not pour from vessel into vessel and did not go into deportation; therefore his taste remained in him, and his smell did not cease.
Jeremiah 31:12 Therefore behold, days are coming, says the Lord, and I will send to him those tipping, and they will tip him and thin his vessels and cut together his horns.
Jeremiah 31:13 And Moab will be put to shame by Chamos, just as the house of Israel was put to shame by Baithel, their hope, trusting in them.
Jeremiah 31:14 How will you say, We are strong, and a person strong for warfare?
Jeremiah 31:15 Moab perished, his city, and his chosen young men went down to slaughter;
Jeremiah 31:16 near is the day of Moab to come, and his wickedness exceedingly swift.
Jeremiah 31:17 Stir for him, all those around him, all those knowing his name; say, How was a renowned staff crushed, a rod of grandeur?
Jeremiah 31:18 Come down from glory and sit in dampness, you sitting in Daibon; be wiped out, because Moab perished; one ravaging your fortification went up against you.
Jeremiah 31:19 Stand upon a road and look, you sitting in Aroer, and ask one fleeing and one being saved, and say, What happened?
Jeremiah 31:20 Moab was put to shame, because he was crushed; wail and cry out; announce in Arnon that Moab perished.
Jeremiah 31:21 And judgment is coming into the land of Misor, upon Chailon and upon Iassa and upon Mophath
Jeremiah 31:22 and upon Daibon and upon Nabau and upon the house of Deblathaim
Jeremiah 31:23 and upon Kariathaim and upon the house of Gamol and upon the house of Maon
Jeremiah 31:24 and upon Karioth and upon Bosor and upon all the cities of Moab, those far and those near.
Jeremiah 31:25 The horn of Moab was broken, and his undertaking was crushed.
Jeremiah 31:26 Make him drunk, because he magnified himself against the Lord; and Moab will strike with his hand and will himself also be an object of laughter.
Jeremiah 31:27 And was Israel not a mockery to you? Was he found among your thefts, because you were fighting him?
Jeremiah 31:28 Those dwelling in Moab left the cities and dwelt among rocks, became like doves nesting among rocks at the mouth of a pit.
Jeremiah 31:29 I heard the arrogance of Moab; he was exceedingly arrogant; his arrogance and his haughtiness, and his heart was exalted.
Jeremiah 31:30 But I knew his works; not his sufficiency, not thus did he do.
Jeremiah 31:31 Therefore wail over Moab on every side, shout over the men of Kiradas of drought.
Jeremiah 31:32 Like the weeping of Iazer I will weep for you, vine of Sebema; your branches crossed a sea, reached Iazer; upon your late fruit, upon your grape gatherers ruin fell.
Jeremiah 31:33 Joyfulness and gladness were swept together from Moabitis, and wine was upon your winepresses; in the morning they did not tread, nor in the evening; they did not make aidad.
Jeremiah 31:34 From the cry of Esebon to Eleale their cities raised their voice, from Zogor to Oronaim and Aglath — salisia, because the water of Nebrim also will be for burning.
Jeremiah 31:35 And I will destroy Moab, says the Lord, going up upon an altar and burning incense to his gods.
Jeremiah 31:36 Therefore my heart, Moab, will hum like pipes; my heart over the people of Kiradas will hum like a pipe; therefore what he acquired perished from a person.
Jeremiah 31:37 Every head in every place they will shave, and every beard will be shaved, and all hands will be cut, and upon every waist sackcloth.
Jeremiah 31:38 And upon all the roofs of Moab and upon her broad streets, because I crushed Moab, says the Lord, like a vessel for which there is no use.
Jeremiah 31:39 How did he change? How did Moab turn his back? He was put to shame, and Moab became an object of laughter and resentment to all those around her.
Jeremiah 31:40 Because thus said the Lord:
Jeremiah 31:41 Akkarioth was taken, and the fortifications were captured;
Jeremiah 31:42 and Moab will perish from a multitude, because he magnified himself against the Lord.
Jeremiah 31:43 Trap and fear and pit upon you, you sitting in Moab;
Jeremiah 31:44 the one fleeing from before fear will fall into the pit, and the one coming up out of the pit will be captured in the trap, because I will bring these things upon Moab in the year of her visitation.
Jeremiah 31:13 All that Ieremias prophesied concerning all the nations.
Jeremiah 31:15 Thus said the Lord, the God of Israel: Take the cup of this unmixed wine from my hand, and you will give all the nations to drink to whom I am sending you,
Jeremiah 31:16 and they will drink and vomit and go mad because of the sword which I am sending among them.
Jeremiah 31:17 And I took the cup from the hand of the Lord and gave the nations to drink to whom the Lord sent me,
Jeremiah 31:18 Ierusalem and the cities of Iouda and the kings of Iouda and his rulers, to make them a desolation and an impassable place and a hissing,
Jeremiah 31:19 and Pharao, king of Egypt, and his servants and his great ones and all his people,
Jeremiah 31:20 and all his mixed peoples and all the kings of foreigners, Askalon and Gaza and Akkaron and the remainder of Azotos,
Jeremiah 31:21 and Idoumaia and Moabitis and the sons of Ammon,
Jeremiah 31:22 and all the kings of Tyre and kings of Sidon and kings on the other side of the sea,
Jeremiah 31:23 and Daidan and Thaiman and Ros and everything clipped about its face,
Jeremiah 31:24 and all the mixed peoples lodging in the wilderness,
Jeremiah 31:25 and all the kings of Ailam and all the kings of Persians,
Jeremiah 31:26 and all the kings from the east, those far and those near, each with his brother, and all the kingdoms upon the face of the earth.
Jeremiah 31:27 And you will say to them: Thus said the Lord Almighty: Drink and become drunk and vomit, and you will fall and certainly not rise because of the sword which I am sending among you.
Jeremiah 31:28 And it will be, when they do not wish to receive the cup from your hand to drink, you will also say: Thus said the Lord: You will surely drink;
Jeremiah 31:29 because in the city upon which my name was named I am beginning to do harm, and you will certainly not be cleansed with cleansing, because I am calling a sword upon those sitting upon the earth.
Jeremiah 31:30 And you will prophesy these words against them and say: The Lord will pronounce from on high, from his holy place he will raise his voice; he will pronounce a word upon his place, and they will answer aidad like grape gatherers; and upon those sitting upon the earth
Jeremiah 31:31 ruin has come upon a part of the earth, because the Lord has a judgment among the nations; he himself contends with all flesh, but the impious were given to a sword, says the Lord.
Jeremiah 31:32 Thus said the Lord: Behold, evils come from nation to nation, and a great storm goes out from the end of the earth.
Jeremiah 31:33 And there will be wounded ones by the Lord on the day of the Lord from a part of the earth even to a part of the earth; they will certainly not be buried; they will be as dung upon the face of the earth.
Jeremiah 31:34 Shout, shepherds, and cry out; and lament, rams of the sheep; because your days were fulfilled for slaughter, and you will fall like the chosen rams;
Jeremiah 31:35 and flight will perish from the shepherds and salvation from the rams of the sheep.
Jeremiah 31:36 A sound of a cry of the shepherds and a shout of the sheep and of the rams, because the Lord destroyed their pastures,
Jeremiah 31:37 and the remaining things of peace will cease because of the anger of my wrath.
Jeremiah 31:38 Like a lion he left his lodging, because their land became impassable because of the great sword.

## Chapter 33

Jeremiah 33:1 At the beginning of King Ioakim, son of Iosias, this word came from the Lord:
Jeremiah 33:2 Thus said the Lord: Stand in the courtyard of the house of the Lord and pronounce to all the Ioudaians and to all those coming to worship in the house of the Lord all the words which I ordered you to pronounce to them; do not remove a word;
Jeremiah 33:3 perhaps they will hear and turn, each from his evil way, and I will cease from the evils which I am planning to do to them because of their evil practices.
Jeremiah 33:4 And you will say: Thus said the Lord: If you do not hear me, to walk in my ordinances which I gave before your face,
Jeremiah 33:5 to listen to the words of my servants the prophets whom I am sending to you at dawn, and I sent and you did not listen to me,
Jeremiah 33:6 then I will make this house like Selom and make the city a curse for all the nations of all the earth.
Jeremiah 33:7 And the priests and the false prophets and all the people heard Ieremias speaking these words in the house of the Lord.
Jeremiah 33:8 And it happened, when Ieremias ceased speaking everything which the Lord ordered him to speak to all the people, the priests and the false prophets and all the people seized him, saying, By death you will die,
Jeremiah 33:9 because you prophesied in the name of the Lord, saying, Like Selom this house will be, and this city will be desolated of inhabitants; and all the people assembled against Ieremias in the house of the Lord.
Jeremiah 33:10 And the rulers of Iouda heard this word and went up from the king's house to the house of the Lord and sat at the entrance of the new gate of the Lord.
Jeremiah 33:11 And the priests and the false prophets said to the rulers and to all the people: A judgment of death for this person, because he prophesied against this city, as you heard with your ears.
Jeremiah 33:12 And Ieremias said to the rulers and to all the people, saying, The Lord sent me to prophesy concerning this house and concerning this city all these words which you heard.
Jeremiah 33:13 And now make your ways and your works better and hear the voice of the Lord, and the Lord will cease from the evils which he spoke against you.
Jeremiah 33:14 And behold, I am in your hands; do to me as is advantageous and as is better for you.
Jeremiah 33:15 Only you will surely know that if you kill me, you put innocent blood upon yourselves and upon this city and upon those dwelling in it; because in truth the Lord has sent me to you to speak all these words into your ears.
Jeremiah 33:16 And the rulers and all the people said to the priests and to the false prophets: There is no judgment of death for this person, because in the name of the Lord our God he spoke to us.
Jeremiah 33:17 And men from the elders of the land rose and said to all the assembly of the people:
Jeremiah 33:18 Michaias the Morathite was in the days of Ezekias, king of Iouda, and said to all the people of Iouda: Thus said the Lord: Sion will be plowed like a field, and Ierusalem will be for an impassable place and the mountain of the house for a grove of a forest.
Jeremiah 33:19 Did Ezekias and all Iouda utterly kill him? Was it not that they feared the Lord and entreated the face of the Lord, and the Lord ceased from the evils which he spoke against them? And we did great evils against our souls. —
Jeremiah 33:20 And there was a person prophesying in the name of the Lord, Ourias, son of Samaias, from Kariathiarim, and he prophesied concerning this land according to all the words of Ieremias.
Jeremiah 33:21 And King Ioakim and all the rulers heard all his words and were seeking to kill him, and Ourias heard and entered Egypt.
Jeremiah 33:22 And the king sent out men to Egypt,
Jeremiah 33:23 and they brought him out from there and brought him in to the king, and he struck him with a sword and threw him into the tomb of the sons of his people.
Jeremiah 33:24 Nevertheless the hand of Achikam, son of Saphan, was with Ieremias, so as not to hand him over into the hands of the people, so as not to kill him.
Jeremiah 33:2 Thus said the Lord: Make bonds and collars and put them around your neck;
Jeremiah 33:3 and you will send them to the king of Idoumaia and to the king of Moab and to the king of the sons of Ammon and to the king of Tyre and to the king of Sidon by the hands of their messengers coming to meet them in Ierusalem, to Sedekias, king of Iouda.
Jeremiah 33:4 And you will order them to say to their lords: Thus said the Lord, the God of Israel: Thus you will say to your lords,
Jeremiah 33:5 that I made the earth with my great strength and with my high undertaking, and I will give it to whomever it seems good in my eyes.
Jeremiah 33:6 I gave the earth to Nabouchodonosor, king of Babylon, to serve him, and the wild beasts of the field to work for him.
Jeremiah 33:8 And the nation and the kingdom, all who do not put their neck under the yoke of the king of Babylon, by sword and by famine I will visit them, said the Lord, until they cease in his hand.
Jeremiah 33:9 And you, do not hear your false prophets and those divining for you and those dreaming for you and your omens and your sorcerers saying, You will certainly not work for the king of Babylon;
Jeremiah 33:10 because they prophesy false things to you to remove you far from your land.
Jeremiah 33:11 And the nation which brings its neck under the yoke of the king of Babylon and works for him, I will also leave him upon his land, and he works for him and will dwell in it. —
Jeremiah 33:12 And to Sedekias, king of Iouda, I spoke according to all these words, saying, Bring in your neck
Jeremiah 33:14 and work for the king of Babylon, because they prophesy unjust things to you;
Jeremiah 33:15 because I did not send them, says the Lord, and they prophesy in my name unjustly to destroy you, and you will perish, you and your prophets prophesying false things to you unjustly.
Jeremiah 33:16 To you and to all this people and to the priests I spoke, saying, Thus said the Lord: Do not hear the words of the prophets prophesying to you, saying, Behold, vessels of the house of the Lord will return from Babylon; because they prophesy unjust things to you; I did not send them.
Jeremiah 33:18 If they are prophets and if a word of the Lord is in them, let them meet me;
Jeremiah 33:19 because thus said the Lord: Even of the remaining vessels,
Jeremiah 33:20 which the king of Babylon did not take when he deported Iechonias from Ierusalem,
Jeremiah 33:22 it will enter Babylon, says the Lord.

## Chapter 35

Jeremiah 35:1 And it happened in the fourth year of Sedekias, king of Iouda, in the fifth month, Ananias, son of Azor, the false prophet from Gabaon, said to me in the house of the Lord before the eyes of the priests and all the people, saying,
Jeremiah 35:2 Thus said the Lord: I crushed the yoke of the king of Babylon;
Jeremiah 35:3 yet two years of days, I will return to this place the vessels of the house of the Lord
Jeremiah 35:4 and Iechonias and the deported people of Iouda, because I will crush the yoke of the king of Babylon.
Jeremiah 35:5 And Ieremias said to Ananias before the eyes of all the people and before the eyes of the priests standing in the house of the Lord,
Jeremiah 35:6 and Ieremias said, Truly; may the Lord do thus; may he establish your word which you prophesy, to return the vessels of the house of the Lord and all the deported people from Babylon to this place.
Jeremiah 35:7 Nevertheless hear the word of the Lord which I speak into your ears and into the ears of all the people:
Jeremiah 35:8 The prophets who came before me and before you from of old also prophesied concerning much land and concerning great kingdoms for war;
Jeremiah 35:9 the prophet who prophesied for peace, when the word comes, they will know the prophet whom the Lord sent to them in faithfulness.
Jeremiah 35:10 And Ananias took the collars from the neck of Ieremias before the eyes of all the people and crushed them.
Jeremiah 35:11 And Ananias said before the eyes of all the people, saying, Thus said the Lord: Thus I will crush the yoke of the king of Babylon from the necks of all the nations. And Ieremias went on his way. —
Jeremiah 35:12 And a word of the Lord came to Ieremias after Ananias crushed the collars from his neck, saying,
Jeremiah 35:13 Go and say to Ananias, saying, Thus said the Lord: You crushed wooden collars, and I will make iron collars instead of them;
Jeremiah 35:14 because thus said the Lord: I put an iron yoke upon the neck of all the nations to work for the king of Babylon.
Jeremiah 35:15 And Ieremias said to Ananias: The Lord has not sent you, and you made this people trust in injustice;
Jeremiah 35:16 therefore thus said the Lord: Behold, I am sending you away from the face of the earth; in this year you will die.
Jeremiah 35:17 And he died in the seventh month.

## Chapter 36

Jeremiah 36:1 And these are the words of the book which Ieremias sent from Ierusalem to the elders of the deported people and to the priests and to the false prophets, a letter to Babylon to the deported people and to all the people,
Jeremiah 36:2 after King Iechonias and the queen and the eunuchs and every free person and prisoner and craftsman went out from Ierusalem,
Jeremiah 36:3 by the hand of Eleasa, son of Saphan, and Gamarias, son of Chelkias, whom Sedekias, king of Iouda, sent to the king of Babylon in Babylon, saying,
Jeremiah 36:4 Thus said the Lord, the God of Israel, concerning the deported people whom I deported from Ierusalem:
Jeremiah 36:5 Build houses and dwell, and plant gardens and eat their fruits,
Jeremiah 36:6 and take wives and produce sons and daughters and take wives for your sons and give your daughters to men, and multiply and do not be diminished,
Jeremiah 36:7 and seek for the peace of the land into which I deported you there, and pray concerning them to the Lord, because in her peace there will be peace for you.
Jeremiah 36:8 Because thus said the Lord: Let the false prophets among you not persuade you, and let your diviners not persuade you, and do not listen to your dreams which you dream,
Jeremiah 36:9 because they prophesy unjust things to you in my name, and I did not send them.
Jeremiah 36:10 Because thus said the Lord: When seventy years are about to be fulfilled for Babylon, I will visit you and establish my words upon you, to return your people to this place;
Jeremiah 36:11 and I will devise a design of peace concerning you and not evils, to give you these things.
Jeremiah 36:12 And pray to me, and I will listen to you;
Jeremiah 36:13 and seek me out, and you will find me, because you will seek me with all your heart,
Jeremiah 36:14 and I will appear to you. —
Jeremiah 36:15 Because you said, The Lord appointed prophets for us in Babylon,
Jeremiah 36:21 thus said the Lord concerning Achiab and concerning Sedekias: Behold, I am giving them into the hands of the king of Babylon, and he will strike them before your eyes.
Jeremiah 36:22 And from them they will take a curse among all the deported people of Iouda in Babylon, saying, May the Lord make you as he made Sedekias and as Achiab, whom the king of Babylon roasted in fire
Jeremiah 36:23 because of the lawlessness which they did in Israel, and they committed adultery with the wives of their fellow citizens and pronounced a word in my name which I did not order them, and I am witness, says the Lord. —
Jeremiah 36:24 And to Samaias the Nelamite you will say,
Jeremiah 36:25 I did not send you in my name. And to Sophonias, son of Maasaias, the priest, say,
Jeremiah 36:26 The Lord made you a priest instead of Iodae the priest, to become an overseer in the house of the Lord over every person prophesying and every person raving, and you will put him into the enclosure and into the confinement.
Jeremiah 36:27 And now why did you revile together Ieremias from Anathoth who prophesied to you?
Jeremiah 36:28 Was it not for this reason that he sent to you in Babylon, saying, It is long; build houses and dwell, and plant gardens and you will eat their fruit? —
Jeremiah 36:29 And Sophonias read the book into the ears of Ieremias.
Jeremiah 36:30 And a word of the Lord came to Ieremias, saying,
Jeremiah 36:31 Send to the deported people, saying, Thus said the Lord concerning Samaias the Nelamite: Since Samaias prophesied to you, and I did not send him, and he made you trust in unjust things,
Jeremiah 36:32 therefore thus said the Lord: Behold, I will visit upon Samaias and upon his family, and there will be no person of theirs in your midst to see the good things which I will do for you; they will not see.

## Chapter 37

Jeremiah 37:1 The word that came to Ieremias from the Lord, to say,
Jeremiah 37:2 Thus said the Lord, the God of Israel, saying, Write all the words which I pronounced to you in a book;
Jeremiah 37:3 because behold, days are coming, says the Lord, and I will turn back the deportation of my people Israel and Iouda, said the Lord, and return them to the land which I gave to their fathers, and they will rule it.
Jeremiah 37:4 And these are the words which the Lord spoke concerning Israel and Iouda:
Jeremiah 37:5 Thus said the Lord: You will hear a voice of fear; fear, and there is no peace.
Jeremiah 37:6 Ask and see whether a male gave birth, and concerning fear, in which they will hold fast waist and salvation; because I have seen every person and his hands upon his waist; faces turned, into jaundice
Jeremiah 37:7 it became. Because that day is great, and there is none like it, and it is a narrow time for Iakob, and from this he will be saved.
Jeremiah 37:8 On that day, said the Lord, I will crush the yoke from their neck and tear their bonds apart, and they do not work any longer for foreigners;
Jeremiah 37:9 and they work for the Lord their God, and I will raise up David their king for them.
Jeremiah 37:12 Thus said the Lord: I raised a crushing; your wound is painful;
Jeremiah 37:13 there is no one judging your judgment; you were treated unto a painful thing; there is no benefit for you.
Jeremiah 37:14 All your friends forgot you; they will certainly not inquire; because I struck you with an enemy's wound, a firm discipline; over all your injustice your sins multiplied.
Jeremiah 37:16 Therefore all those eating you will be eaten, and all your enemies, all their flesh they will eat; over the multitude of your injustices your sins were multiplied; they did these things to you; and those plundering you will be for plunder, and all those despoiling you I will give over to spoils.
Jeremiah 37:17 Because I will bring up your remedy, I will treat you for a painful wound, says the Lord, because you were called Scattered; she is your prey, because there is no one seeking her.
Jeremiah 37:18 Thus said the Lord: Behold, I will turn back the deportation of Iakob and have mercy on his captivity; and a city will be built upon its height, and the temple will sit according to its judgment.
Jeremiah 37:19 And from them will come out those singing and a voice of those playing; and I will multiply them, and they will certainly not be diminished.
Jeremiah 37:20 And their sons will enter as formerly, and their testimonies will be set upright before my face; and I will visit those afflicting them.
Jeremiah 37:21 And his stronger ones will be over them, and his ruler will come out from him; and I will gather them, and they will return to me; because who is this who gave his heart to return to me? says the Lord.
Jeremiah 37:23 Because the anger of the Lord went out wrathful; whirling anger went out; it will come upon impious ones.
Jeremiah 37:24 The anger of the wrath of the Lord will certainly not turn away until he does and until he establishes the undertaking of his heart; at the end of the days you will know these things.

## Chapter 38

Jeremiah 38:1 At that time, said the Lord, I will be a God for the family of Israel, and they will be a people for me.
Jeremiah 38:2 Thus said the Lord: I found warmth in a wilderness with those perished by sword; go and do not destroy Israel.
Jeremiah 38:3 The Lord appeared to him from far away: With an everlasting love I loved you; therefore I drew you into compassion.
Jeremiah 38:4 Again I will build you, and you will be built, virgin Israel; again you will take your drum and go out with an assembly of those playing.
Jeremiah 38:5 Again plant vineyards on the mountains of Samareia; plant and praise.
Jeremiah 38:6 Because there is a day of calling of those answering on the mountains of Ephraim: Rise and go up to Sion to the Lord our God. —
Jeremiah 38:7 Because thus said the Lord to Iakob: Be glad and neigh over the head of nations, make heard and praise; say, The Lord saved his people, the remnant of Israel.
Jeremiah 38:8 Behold, I am bringing them from the north and will gather them from the end of the earth at the feast of phasek; and you will produce a great multitude, and they will return here.
Jeremiah 38:9 With weeping they went out, and with consolation I will bring them up, lodging them beside channels of waters on a straight way, and they will certainly not stray in it; because I became a father to Israel, and Ephraim is my firstborn.
Jeremiah 38:10 Hear a word of the Lord, nations, and announce to the farther islands; say, The one who winnowed Israel will gather him and guard him as one feeding his flock.
Jeremiah 38:11 Because the Lord redeemed Iakob, delivered him from the hand of those firmer than he.
Jeremiah 38:12 And they will come and be glad on the mountain of Sion; and they will come to the good things of the Lord, to a land of grain and wine and fruits and cattle and sheep, and their soul will be like a fruitful tree, and they will hunger no longer.
Jeremiah 38:13 Then virgins will rejoice in an assembly of young men, and old men will rejoice, and I will turn their mourning into joy and make them glad.
Jeremiah 38:14 I will magnify and make drunk the soul of the priests, sons of Leui, and my people will be filled with my good things.
Jeremiah 38:15 Thus said the Lord: A voice was heard in Rama of mourning and weeping and lament; Rachel weeping did not wish to cease over her sons, because they are no more.
Jeremiah 38:16 Thus said the Lord: Let your voice cease from weeping and your eyes from your tears, because there is a wage for your works, and they will return from a land of enemies,
Jeremiah 38:17 a lasting thing for your children.
Jeremiah 38:18 I surely heard Ephraim lamenting: You disciplined me, and I was disciplined; like a calf I was not taught; turn me, and I will return, because you are the Lord my God.
Jeremiah 38:19 Because after my captivity I repented, and after I came to know I groaned over days of shame and showed you that I received reproach from my youth.
Jeremiah 38:20 Ephraim is a beloved son to me, a child delighting, because since my words are in him, I will surely remember him; therefore I hastened over him; I will surely have mercy on him, says the Lord.
Jeremiah 38:21 Set yourself up, Sion, make retribution, set your heart upon the shoulders; turn back along the way which you traveled, virgin Israel; turn back to your cities, mourning.
Jeremiah 38:22 Until when will you turn away, dishonored daughter? Because the Lord created salvation for a new planting; in salvation people will go about.
Jeremiah 38:23 Thus said the Lord: Again they will say this word in the land of Iouda and in his cities when I turn back his captivity: Blessed is the Lord upon a righteous mountain, his holy one,
Jeremiah 38:24 and those dwelling in the cities of Iouda and in all his land together with a farmer, and he will be lifted up among a flock.
Jeremiah 38:25 Because I made every thirsty soul drunk and filled every hungry soul.
Jeremiah 38:26 Therefore I awoke and saw, and my sleep became sweet to me.
Jeremiah 38:27 Therefore behold, days are coming, says the Lord, and I will sow Israel and Iouda with seed of person and seed of cattle.
Jeremiah 38:28 And it will be, as I was watching over them to pull down and to harm, thus I will watch over them to build and plant, says the Lord.
Jeremiah 38:29 In those days they will certainly not say, The fathers ate an unripe grape, and the teeth of the children were set on edge;
Jeremiah 38:30 but each will die in his own sin, and the teeth of the one eating the unripe grape will be set on edge.
Jeremiah 38:31 Behold, days are coming, says the Lord, and I will make a new covenant with the house of Israel and with the house of Iouda,
Jeremiah 38:32 not according to the covenant which I made with their fathers on the day when I took hold of their hand to bring them out from the land of Egypt, because they did not remain in my covenant, and I disregarded them, says the Lord;
Jeremiah 38:33 because this is the covenant which I will make with the house of Israel after those days, says the Lord: I will surely give my laws into their understanding and write them upon their hearts; and I will be a God for them, and they will be a people for me;
Jeremiah 38:34 and they will certainly not teach, each his fellow citizen and each his brother, saying, Know the Lord; because all will know me, from their small one even to their great one, because I will be merciful to their injustices and will certainly not remember their sins any longer. —
Jeremiah 38:35 If heaven is raised into the heights, says the Lord, and if the foundation of the earth is lowered below, I also will not reject the family of Israel, says the Lord, concerning all that they did.
Jeremiah 38:36 Thus said the Lord, who gave the sun for light of the day, moon and stars for light of the night, and a cry in the sea, and its waves roared; the Lord Almighty is his name:
Jeremiah 38:37 If these laws cease from before my face, says the Lord, the family of Israel will also cease to be a nation before my face all the days. —
Jeremiah 38:38 Behold, days are coming, says the Lord, and a city will be built for the Lord from the tower of Anameel to the corner gate;
Jeremiah 38:39 and its measurement will go out opposite them as far as the hills of Gareb, and it will be surrounded all around with chosen stones;
Jeremiah 38:40 and all asaremoth as far as nachal Kedron, as far as the corner of the horse gate of the east, a sanctuary for the Lord, and it will certainly not cease any longer and will certainly not be pulled down forever.

## Chapter 39

Jeremiah 39:1 The word that came from the Lord to Ieremias in the tenth year for King Sedekias; this is the eighteenth year for King Nabouchodonosor, king of Babylon,
Jeremiah 39:2 and the force of the king of Babylon made a siegework against Ierusalem, and Ieremias was guarded in the courtyard of the prison which is in the king's house,
Jeremiah 39:3 in which King Sedekias shut him up, saying, Why do you prophesy, saying, Thus said the Lord: Behold, I am giving this city into the hands of the king of Babylon, and he will take it,
Jeremiah 39:4 and Sedekias will certainly not be saved from the hand of the Chaldeans, because he will surely be handed over into the hands of the king of Babylon, and his mouth will speak to his mouth, and his eyes will see his eyes,
Jeremiah 39:5 and Sedekias will enter Babylon and sit there.
Jeremiah 39:6 And a word of the Lord came to Ieremias, saying,
Jeremiah 39:7 Behold, Anameel, son of Salom, your father's brother, is coming to you, saying, Acquire for yourself my field in Anathoth, because yours is the right to receive it as a possession.
Jeremiah 39:8 And Anameel, son of Salom, my father's brother, came to me in the courtyard of the prison and said to me, Acquire my field in the land of Beniamin, in Anathoth, because yours is the right to acquire, and you are the elder. And I knew that it is a word of the Lord,
Jeremiah 39:9 and I acquired the field of Anameel, son of my father's brother, and weighed out for him seven shekels and ten of silver;
Jeremiah 39:10 and I wrote in a book and sealed it and called witnesses to testify and weighed the silver in a balance.
Jeremiah 39:11 And I took the book of the acquisition, the sealed one and the read one,
Jeremiah 39:12 and gave it to Barouch, son of Nerias, son of Maasaias, before the eyes of Anameel, son of my father's brother, and before the eyes of those standing and writing in the book of the acquisition and before the eyes of the Ioudaians in the courtyard of the prison.
Jeremiah 39:13 And I ordered Barouch before their eyes, saying,
Jeremiah 39:14 Thus said the Lord Almighty: Take this book of the acquisition and the read book, and you will put it into an earthenware vessel, so that it remains many days.
Jeremiah 39:15 Because thus said the Lord: Again fields and houses and vineyards will be acquired in this land.
Jeremiah 39:16 And I prayed to the Lord after I gave the book of the acquisition to Barouch, son of Nerias, saying,
Jeremiah 39:17 O Lord, you made heaven and earth by your great strength and by your high and lofty arm; nothing will certainly be hidden from you,
Jeremiah 39:18 doing mercy unto thousands and repaying sins of fathers into the bosoms of their children after them, the great and strong God,
Jeremiah 39:19 Lord of great counsel and powerful in works, the great God, the Almighty and the Lord of a great name; your eyes are upon the ways of the sons of people, to give each according to his way;
Jeremiah 39:20 you who made signs and wonders in the land of Egypt until this day and in Israel and among those born of earth, and made yourself a name as this day,
Jeremiah 39:21 and brought out your people Israel from the land of Egypt with signs and with wonders and with a mighty hand and with a high arm and with great visions,
Jeremiah 39:22 and gave them this land which you swore to their fathers, a land flowing with milk and honey;
Jeremiah 39:23 and they entered and took it and did not hear your voice and did not walk in your ordinances; all that you commanded them they did not do; and you made all these evils happen to them.
Jeremiah 39:24 Behold, a multitude has come into this city to capture it, and the city was given into the hands of the Chaldeans fighting it because of sword and famine; as you spoke, thus it happened.
Jeremiah 39:25 And you say to me, Acquire for yourself a field for silver; and I wrote a book and sealed it and called witnesses to testify; and the city was given into the hands of the Chaldeans.
Jeremiah 39:26 And a word of the Lord came to me, saying,
Jeremiah 39:27 I am the Lord, the God of all flesh; will anything be hidden from me?
Jeremiah 39:28 Therefore thus said the Lord, the God of Israel: Being given, this city will be handed over into the hands of the king of Babylon, and he will take it,
Jeremiah 39:29 and the Chaldeans fighting will come against this city and burn this city with fire and burn up the houses in which they were burning incense upon their roofs to Baal and pouring libations to other gods to embitter me.
Jeremiah 39:30 Because the sons of Israel and the sons of Iouda alone were doing evil before my eyes from their youth;
Jeremiah 39:31 because this city was for my anger and for my wrath from the day on which they built it and until this day, to remove it from before my face
Jeremiah 39:32 because of all the wickednesses of the sons of Israel and Iouda which they did to embitter me, they and their kings and their rulers and their priests and their prophets, men of Iouda and those dwelling in Ierusalem,
Jeremiah 39:33 and they turned a back to me and not a face, and I taught them at dawn and taught, and they did not hear to receive discipline;
Jeremiah 39:34 and they placed their defilements in the house upon which my name was called, in their uncleannesses,
Jeremiah 39:35 and built the altars to Baal in the ravine of the son of Ennom to offer up their sons and their daughters to Moloch the king, things which I did not order them and which did not come up upon my heart, to do this abomination so that Iouda should sin. —
Jeremiah 39:36 And now thus said the Lord, the God of Israel, concerning the city of which you say, It will be handed over into the hands of the king of Babylon by sword and by famine and by sending away:
Jeremiah 39:37 Behold, I am gathering them from all the land where I scattered them there in my anger and my wrath and great provocation, and I will return them to this place and settle them confidently,
Jeremiah 39:38 and they will be a people for me, and I will be a God for them.
Jeremiah 39:39 And I will give them another way and another heart to fear me all the days, for good for them and for their children after them.
Jeremiah 39:40 And I will make an everlasting covenant with them which I will certainly not turn back behind them; and I will put my fear into their heart so that they do not depart from me.
Jeremiah 39:41 And I will visit to do good to them and plant them in this land in faithfulness and with all heart and with all soul.
Jeremiah 39:42 Because thus said the Lord: As I brought all these great evils upon this people, thus I will bring upon them all the good things which I spoke concerning them.
Jeremiah 39:43 And again fields will be acquired in the land of which you say, It is impassable, without people and cattle, and they were handed over into the hands of the Chaldeans.
Jeremiah 39:44 And they will acquire fields with silver, and you will write a book and seal it and call witnesses to testify in the land of Beniamin and around Ierusalem and in the cities of Iouda and in the cities of the mountain and in the cities of Sephela and in the cities of Nageb, because I will turn back their deportations.

## Chapter 40

Jeremiah 40:1 And a word of the Lord came to Ieremias a second time, and he was still bound in the courtyard of the prison, saying,
Jeremiah 40:2 Thus said the Lord, making earth and forming it to set it upright; the Lord is his name:
Jeremiah 40:3 Cry to me, and I will answer you and report to you great and strong things which you did not know.
Jeremiah 40:4 Because thus said the Lord, the God of Israel, concerning the houses of this city and concerning the houses of the king of Iouda pulled down for siegeworks and ramparts,
Jeremiah 40:5 to fight against the Chaldeans and fill it with the dead of the people whom I struck in my anger and in my wrath, and I turned my face away from them concerning all their wickednesses:
Jeremiah 40:6 Behold, I am bringing up for her closing of wounds and a remedy and will reveal to them to listen, and I will treat her and make peace and faithfulness for them;
Jeremiah 40:7 and I will return the deported people of Iouda and the deported people of Israel and build them as formerly;
Jeremiah 40:8 and I will cleanse them from all their injustices which they sinned against me, and I will certainly not remember their sins which they sinned against me and departed from me.
Jeremiah 40:9 And it will be for gladness and for praise and for greatness for all the people of the earth, who will hear all the good things which I will do, and they will fear and be embittered concerning all the good things and concerning all the peace which I will make for them. —
Jeremiah 40:10 Thus said the Lord: Again there will be heard in this place of which you say, It is desolate, without people and cattle, in the cities of Iouda and outside Ierusalem, the desolated places for lack of person and cattle,
Jeremiah 40:11 a voice of gladness and a voice of joyfulness, a voice of bridegroom and a voice of bride, a voice of those saying, Give thanks to the Lord Almighty, because the Lord is good, because his mercy is forever; and they will bring gifts into the house of the Lord; because I will turn back all the deportation of that land as formerly, said the Lord.
Jeremiah 40:12 Thus said the Lord of the forces: Again there will be in this place desolate for lack of person and cattle and in all its cities lodgings of shepherds laying sheep down;
Jeremiah 40:13 in the cities of the hill country and in the cities of Sephela and in the cities of Nageb and in the land of Beniamin and in those around Ierusalem and in the cities of Iouda again sheep will pass under the hand of one counting, said the Lord.

## Chapter 41

Jeremiah 41:1 The word that came to Ieremias from the Lord, and Nabouchodonosor, king of Babylon, and all his army and all the land of his rule were fighting against Ierusalem and against all the cities of Iouda, saying,
Jeremiah 41:2 Thus said the Lord: Go to Sedekias, king of Iouda, and you will say to him: Thus said the Lord: This city will surely be handed over into the hands of the king of Babylon, and he will capture it and burn it with fire;
Jeremiah 41:3 and you will certainly not be saved from his hand, and you will surely be captured and be given into his hands, and your eyes will see his eyes, and his mouth will speak with your mouth, and you will enter Babylon.
Jeremiah 41:4 But hear the word of the Lord, Sedekias, king of Iouda: Thus says the Lord:
Jeremiah 41:5 In peace you will die, and as they wept for your fathers who reigned before you, they will weep for you also, and, O adon, they will lament you; because I spoke a word, said the Lord.
Jeremiah 41:6 And Ieremias spoke all these words to King Sedekias in Ierusalem;
Jeremiah 41:7 and the force of the king of Babylon was fighting against Ierusalem and against the cities of Iouda, against Lachis and against Azeka, because these were left among the cities of Iouda as fortified cities.
Jeremiah 41:8 The word that came to Ieremias from the Lord after King Sedekias completed a covenant with the people to proclaim release,
Jeremiah 41:9 for each to send out his male servant and each his female servant, the Hebrew man and the Hebrew woman, free, so that a man from Iouda should not be enslaved,
Jeremiah 41:10 and all the great ones and all the people who entered into the covenant to send away, each, his male servant and, each, his female servant turned back
Jeremiah 41:11 and put them as male servants and female servants.
Jeremiah 41:12 And a word of the Lord came to Ieremias, saying,
Jeremiah 41:13 Thus said the Lord, the God of Israel: I made a covenant with your fathers on the day on which I delivered them from the land of Egypt, from a house of slavery, saying,
Jeremiah 41:14 When six years are fulfilled, you will send away your Hebrew brother who will be sold to you; and he works for you six years, and you will send him out free. And they did not hear me and did not incline their ear.
Jeremiah 41:15 And today they returned to do what is straight before my eyes, to proclaim release, each of his neighbor, and completed a covenant before my face in the house upon which my name was called.
Jeremiah 41:16 And you turned back and profaned my name by bringing back, each, his male servant and, each, his female servant whom you sent out free according to their soul, as male servants and female servants for you.
Jeremiah 41:17 Therefore thus said the Lord: You did not hear me to proclaim release, each to his neighbor; behold, I proclaim release for you to sword and to death and to famine, and I will give you over to scattering for all the kingdoms of the earth.
Jeremiah 41:18 And I will give the men who transgressed my covenant, who did not establish my covenant which they made before my face, the calf which they made to work for him,
Jeremiah 41:19 the rulers of Iouda and the powerful ones and the priests and the people,
Jeremiah 41:20 and I will give them to their enemies, and their carcasses will be food for the birds of heaven and for the wild beasts of the earth.
Jeremiah 41:21 And Sedekias, king of Ioudaia, and their rulers I will give into the hands of their enemies, and the force of the king of Babylon, to those running away from them.
Jeremiah 41:22 Behold, I am ordering, says the Lord, and I will return them to this land, and they will fight against it and take it and burn it up with fire, and the cities of Iouda, and I will make them desolate of inhabitants.

## Chapter 42

Jeremiah 42:1 The word that came to Ieremias from the Lord in the days of Ioakim, king of Iouda, saying,
Jeremiah 42:2 Go to the house of Archabin and bring them into the house of the Lord into one of the courtyards, and you will give them wine to drink.
Jeremiah 42:3 And I brought out Iezonias, son of Ieremin, son of Chabasin, and his brothers and his sons and all the household of Archabin
Jeremiah 42:4 and brought them into the house of the Lord into the chamber of the sons of Ananias, son of Godolias, a man of God, which is near the house of the rulers above the house of Maasaias, son of Selom, guarding the courtyard,
Jeremiah 42:5 and set before their face a jar of wine and cups and said, Drink wine.
Jeremiah 42:6 And they said, We will certainly not drink wine, because Ionadab, son of Rechab, our father, commanded us, saying, You shall certainly not drink wine, you and your sons forever,
Jeremiah 42:7 and you shall certainly not build a house and certainly not sow seed, and you will have no vineyard, because in tents you will dwell all your days, so that you may live many days upon the land upon which you stay.
Jeremiah 42:8 And we heard the voice of Ionadab our father so as not to drink wine all our days, we and our wives and our sons and our daughters,
Jeremiah 42:9 and so as not to build houses to dwell there, and vineyard and field and seed did not come to be for us,
Jeremiah 42:10 and we dwelt in tents and heard and did according to everything which Ionadab our father commanded us.
Jeremiah 42:11 And it happened, when Nabouchodonosor went up against the land, we also said, Enter, and let us enter Ierusalem from before the force of the Chaldeans and from before the force of the Assyrians, and we dwelt there. —
Jeremiah 42:12 And a word of the Lord came to me, saying,
Jeremiah 42:13 Thus says the Lord: Go and say to a person of Iouda and to those dwelling in Ierusalem: Will you not receive discipline to hear my words?
Jeremiah 42:14 The sons of Ionadab, son of Rechab, established the word which he commanded his children so as not to drink wine, and they did not drink; and I spoke to you at dawn and spoke, and you did not hear.
Jeremiah 42:15 And I sent to you my servants the prophets, saying, Turn, each from his evil way, and make your practices better, and you will not go after other gods to serve them, and you will dwell upon the land which I gave to you and to your fathers; and you did not incline your ears and did not hear.
Jeremiah 42:16 And the sons of Ionadab, son of Rechab, established the commandment of their father, but this people did not hear me.
Jeremiah 42:17 Therefore thus said the Lord: Behold, I am bringing upon Iouda and upon those dwelling in Ierusalem all the evils which I spoke against them.
Jeremiah 42:18 Therefore thus said the Lord: Since the sons of Ionadab, son of Rechab, heard the commandment of their father to do as their father commanded them,
Jeremiah 42:19 a man of the sons of Ionadab, son of Rechab, standing before my face will certainly not cease all the days of the earth.

## Chapter 43

Jeremiah 43:1 And in the fourth year of Ioakim, son of Iosias, king of Iouda, a word of the Lord came to me, saying,
Jeremiah 43:2 Take for yourself a book roll and write upon it all the words which I pronounced to you concerning Ierusalem and concerning Iouda and concerning all the nations from the day of my speaking to you, from the days of Iosias, king of Iouda, and until this day;
Jeremiah 43:3 perhaps the house of Iouda will hear all the evils which I am planning to do to them, so that they turn from their evil way, and I will be merciful to their injustices and their sins. —
Jeremiah 43:4 And Ieremias called Barouch, son of Nerias, and he wrote from the mouth of Ieremias all the words of the Lord which he pronounced to him in a book roll.
Jeremiah 43:5 And Ieremias commanded Barouch, saying, I am guarded; I certainly cannot enter the house of the Lord;
Jeremiah 43:6 and you will read in this roll into the ears of the people in the house of the Lord on a day of fasting, and in the ears of all Iouda coming from their city you will read to them;
Jeremiah 43:7 perhaps their plea for mercy will fall before the face of the Lord, and they will turn from their evil way, because great is the wrath and anger of the Lord which he spoke against this people.
Jeremiah 43:8 And Barouch did according to everything which Ieremias commanded him, to read in the book words of the Lord in the house of the Lord. —
Jeremiah 43:9 And it happened in the eighth year for King Ioakim, in the ninth month, all the people in Ierusalem and the house of Iouda assembled for a fast before the face of the Lord.
Jeremiah 43:10 And Barouch was reading in the book the words of Ieremias in the house of the Lord, in the house of Gamarias, son of Saphan, the scribe, in the upper courtyard, at the entrance of the new gate of the house of the Lord, in the ears of all the people. —
Jeremiah 43:11 And Michaias, son of Gamarias, son of Saphan, heard all the words of the Lord from the book;
Jeremiah 43:12 and he went down to the king's house, to the house of the scribe, and behold, there all the rulers were sitting, Elisama the scribe and Dalaias, son of Selemias, and Elnathan, son of Akchobor, and Gamarias, son of Saphan, and Sedekias, son of Ananias, and all the rulers,
Jeremiah 43:13 and Michaias announced to them all the words which he heard Barouch reading into the ears of the people.
Jeremiah 43:14 And all the rulers sent to Barouch, son of Nerias, Ioudin, son of Nathanias, son of Selemias, son of Chousi, saying, The roll in which you read in the ears of the people, take it into your hand and come; and Barouch took the roll and went down to them.
Jeremiah 43:15 And they said to him, Again read into our ears; and Barouch read.
Jeremiah 43:16 And it happened, when they heard all the words, they counseled together, each with his neighbor, and said, Let us surely announce to the king all these words.
Jeremiah 43:17 And they asked Barouch, saying, From where did you write all these words?
Jeremiah 43:18 And Barouch said, From his mouth Ieremias announced all these words to me, and I was writing in a book.
Jeremiah 43:19 And they said to Barouch, Go, hide, you and Ieremias; let no person know where you are.
Jeremiah 43:20 And they entered to the king in the courtyard, and gave the roll to be guarded in the house of Elisama, and announced to the king all the words. —
Jeremiah 43:21 And the king sent Ioudin to take the roll, and he took it from the house of Elisama; and Ioudin read into the ears of the king and into the ears of all the rulers standing around the king.
Jeremiah 43:22 And the king was sitting in a winter house, and a hearth of fire was before his face.
Jeremiah 43:23 And it happened, as Ioudin read three pages and four, he cut them off with the scribe's razor and threw them into the fire upon the hearth, until all the roll was consumed in the fire upon the hearth.
Jeremiah 43:24 And they did not seek and did not tear their garments, the king and his servants hearing all these words;
Jeremiah 43:25 and Elnathan and Godolias and Gamarias urged the king not to burn up the roll.
Jeremiah 43:26 And the king commanded Ieremeel, son of the king, and Saraias, son of Esriel, to seize Barouch and Ieremias; and they were hidden.
Jeremiah 43:27 And a word of the Lord came to Ieremias after the king burned up the roll, all the words which Barouch wrote from the mouth of Ieremias, saying,
Jeremiah 43:28 Again take another roll and write all the words that were upon the roll which King Ioakim burned up.
Jeremiah 43:29 And you will say: Thus said the Lord: You burned up this roll, saying, Why did you write upon it, saying, The king of Babylon will surely enter and destroy this land, and person and cattle will cease from it?
Jeremiah 43:30 Therefore thus said the Lord concerning Ioakim, king of Iouda: He will have no one sitting upon the throne of David, and his carcass will be cast in the heat of the day and in the frost of the night;
Jeremiah 43:31 and I will visit upon him and upon his family and upon his servants and bring upon them and upon those dwelling in Ierusalem and upon the land of Iouda all the evils which I spoke to them, and they did not hear.
Jeremiah 43:32 And Barouch took another roll and wrote upon it from the mouth of Ieremias all the words of the book which Ioakim burned up; and still more words like these were added to it.

## Chapter 44

Jeremiah 44:1 And Sedekias, son of Iosias, reigned instead of Ioakim, whom Nabouchodonosor made king to reign over Iouda;
Jeremiah 44:2 and he and his servants and the people of the land did not hear the words of the Lord which he spoke by the hand of Ieremias. —
Jeremiah 44:3 And King Sedekias sent Ioachal, son of Selemias, and Sophonias, son of Maasaias, the priest, to Ieremias, saying, Pray now concerning us to the Lord.
Jeremiah 44:4 And Ieremias came and passed through the midst of the city, and they did not put him into a house of the prison.
Jeremiah 44:5 And Pharao's force went out from Egypt, and the Chaldeans heard the report of them and withdrew from Ierusalem.
Jeremiah 44:6 And a word of the Lord came to Ieremias, saying,
Jeremiah 44:7 Thus said the Lord: Thus you will say to the king of Iouda who sent to you to seek me out: Behold, Pharao's force that came out to help you will return to the land of Egypt,
Jeremiah 44:8 and the Chaldeans themselves will return and fight against this city and capture it and burn it with fire.
Jeremiah 44:9 Because thus said the Lord: Do not suppose in your souls, saying, The Chaldeans will surely run away from us, because they will certainly not go away;
Jeremiah 44:10 and if you strike all the force of the Chaldeans fighting you, and some pierced ones are left, each in his place, these will rise and burn this city with fire.
Jeremiah 44:11 And it happened, when the force of the Chaldeans withdrew from Ierusalem before Pharao's force,
Jeremiah 44:12 Ieremias went out from Ierusalem to go to the land of Beniamin to buy from there in the midst of the people.
Jeremiah 44:13 And he came to be at the gate of Beniamin, and there was a person with whom he lodged, Sarouias, son of Selemias, son of Ananias, and he seized Ieremias, saying, You are fleeing to the Chaldeans.
Jeremiah 44:14 And he said, Falsehood; I am not fleeing to the Chaldeans. And he did not hear him, and Sarouias seized Ieremias and brought him to the rulers.
Jeremiah 44:15 And the rulers were embittered against Ieremias and struck him and sent him to the house of Ionathan the scribe, because they made this a prison house.
Jeremiah 44:16 And Ieremias came into the house of the pit and into the chereth and sat there many days.
Jeremiah 44:17 And Sedekias sent and called him, and the king asked him secretly to say whether there is a word from the Lord, and he said, There is; you will be handed over into the hands of the king of Babylon.
Jeremiah 44:18 And Ieremias said to the king: What wrong did I do to you and your servants and this people, that you put me into a prison house?
Jeremiah 44:19 And where are your prophets who prophesied to you, saying that the king of Babylon will certainly not come upon this land?
Jeremiah 44:20 And now, lord king, let my plea for mercy fall before your face, and why do you return me to the house of Ionathan the scribe, and shall I certainly not die there?
Jeremiah 44:21 And the king ordered, and they put him into a house of the prison and gave him one loaf a day from outside where they bake, until the loaves ceased from the city; and Ieremias sat in the courtyard of the prison.

## Chapter 45

Jeremiah 45:1 And Saphatias, son of Mathan, and Godolias, son of Paschor, and Ioachal, son of Selemias, heard the words which Ieremias was speaking to the people, saying,
Jeremiah 45:2 Thus said the Lord: The one dwelling in this city will die by sword and by famine, and the one going out to the Chaldeans will live, and his soul will be as a find, and he will live;
Jeremiah 45:3 because thus said the Lord: Being handed over, this city will be handed over into the hands of the force of the king of Babylon, and he will capture it.
Jeremiah 45:4 And they said to the king: Let that person now be killed, because he weakens the hands of the people fighting who remain in the city and the hands of all the people, speaking to them according to these words, because this person does not pronounce peace for this people but rather evil things.
Jeremiah 45:5 And the king said, Behold, he is in your hands; because the king could not prevail against them.
Jeremiah 45:6 And they threw him into the pit of Melchias, son of the king, which was in the courtyard of the prison, and lowered him into the pit, and in the pit there was no water but rather mud, and he was in the mud.
Jeremiah 45:7 And Abdemelech the Ethiopian heard, and he was in the king's house, that they put Ieremias into the pit; and the king was at the gate of Beniamin;
Jeremiah 45:8 and he went out to him and spoke to the king and said,
Jeremiah 45:9 You acted wickedly in what you did, to kill this person because of famine, because there are no longer loaves in the city.
Jeremiah 45:10 And the king commanded Abdemelech, saying, Take into your hands from here thirty people and bring him up out of the pit, so that he does not die.
Jeremiah 45:11 And Abdemelech took the people and entered the underground house of the king and took from there old rags and old ropes and threw them to Ieremias into the pit
Jeremiah 45:12 and said, Put these beneath the ropes; and Ieremias did thus.
Jeremiah 45:13 And they drew him with the ropes and brought him up out of the pit; and Ieremias sat in the courtyard of the prison.
Jeremiah 45:14 And the king sent and called him to himself into the aselisi house in the house of the Lord; and the king said to him, I will ask you a word, and do not now hide a word from me.
Jeremiah 45:15 And Ieremias said to the king: If I announce to you, will you not surely put me to death? And if I counsel you, you will certainly not hear me.
Jeremiah 45:16 And the king swore to him, saying, The Lord lives, who made this soul for us; surely I will not kill you and will not give you into the hands of these people.
Jeremiah 45:17 And Ieremias said to him: Thus said the Lord: If you surely go out to the leaders of the king of Babylon, your soul will also live, and this city will certainly not be burned up with fire, and you will live, you and your household;
Jeremiah 45:18 and if you do not go out, this city will be given into the hands of the Chaldeans, and they will burn it with fire, and you will certainly not be saved.
Jeremiah 45:19 And the king said to Ieremias: I have concern about the Ioudaians who have fled to the Chaldeans, lest they give me into their hands, and they will mock me.
Jeremiah 45:20 And Ieremias said: They will certainly not hand you over; hear the word of the Lord which I speak to you, and it will be better for you, and your soul will live.
Jeremiah 45:21 And if you do not wish to go out, this is the word which the Lord showed me:
Jeremiah 45:22 And behold, all the women left in the house of the king of Iouda were being brought out to the rulers of the king of Babylon, and these were saying, Your men of peace deceived you and will prevail against you and lodge your feet in slipping places; they turned away from you.
Jeremiah 45:23 And they will bring out your wives and your children to the Chaldeans, and you will certainly not be saved, because you will be captured in the hand of the king of Babylon, and this city will be burned up.
Jeremiah 45:24 And the king said to him: Let no person know of these words, and you will certainly not die.
Jeremiah 45:25 And if the rulers hear that I spoke to you and come to you and say to you, Announce to us what the king spoke to you; do not hide from us, and we will certainly not kill you; and what did the king speak to you?
Jeremiah 45:26 You will also say to them, I cast my plea for mercy before the eyes of the king, so as not to return me to the house of Ionathan to die there.
Jeremiah 45:27 And all the rulers came to Ieremias and asked him, and he announced to them according to all these words which the king commanded him; and they kept silent, because a word of the Lord was not heard.
Jeremiah 45:28 And Ieremias sat in the courtyard of the prison until the time when Ierusalem was captured.

## Chapter 46

Jeremiah 46:1 And it happened in the ninth year of Sedekias, king of Iouda, in the tenth month, Nabouchodonosor, king of Babylon, and all his force came against Ierusalem and were besieging her.
Jeremiah 46:2 And in the eleventh year of Sedekias, in the fourth month, on the ninth of the month, the city was breached.
Jeremiah 46:3 And all the leaders of the king of Babylon entered and sat in the middle gate, Nargalasar and Samagoth and Nabousachar and Nabousaris and Nagargasnaser Rabamag and the remaining leaders of the king of Babylon;
Jeremiah 46:14 and they sent and took Ieremias from the courtyard of the prison and gave him to Godolias, son of Achikam, son of Saphan; and they brought him out, and he sat in the midst of the people.
Jeremiah 46:15 And a word of the Lord came to Ieremias in the courtyard of the prison, saying,
Jeremiah 46:16 Go and say to Abdemelech the Ethiopian: Thus said the Lord, the God of Israel: Behold, I am bringing my words upon this city for evils and not for good things;
Jeremiah 46:17 and I will save you on that day and will certainly not give you into the hands of the people before whose face you fear.
Jeremiah 46:18 Because I will surely save you, and you will certainly not fall by sword; and your soul will be as a find, because you had trusted in me, says the Lord.

## Chapter 47

Jeremiah 47:1 The word that came from the Lord to Ieremias afterward, after Nabouzardan the chief cook sent him away from Daman, when he took him in handcuffs in the midst of the deported people of Iouda being brought to Babylon.
Jeremiah 47:2 And the chief cook took him and said to him: The Lord your God spoke these evils against this place,
Jeremiah 47:3 and the Lord did them, because you sinned against him and did not hear his voice.
Jeremiah 47:4 Behold, I released you from the handcuffs upon your hands; if it is good before you to come with me to Babylon, come, and I will set my eyes upon you;
Jeremiah 47:5 but if not, go away and return to Godolias, son of Achikam, son of Saphan, whom the king of Babylon appointed in the land of Iouda, and dwell with him in the midst of the people in the land of Iouda; to all that is good in your eyes to go to, go. And the chief cook gave him gifts and sent him away.
