Jeremiah 47:6 And he came to Godolias in Massepha and sat in the midst of the people left in the land.
Jeremiah 47:7 And all the leaders of the force in the field heard, they and their men, that the king of Babylon appointed Godolias in the land and entrusted to him men and their wives whom he did not deport to Babylon.
Jeremiah 47:8 And Ismael, son of Nathanias, and Ioanan, son of Karee, and Saraias, son of Thanaemeth, and the sons of Ophe the Netophati and Iezonias, son of the Mochati, came to Godolias in Massepha, they and their men.
Jeremiah 47:9 And Godolias swore to them and to their men, saying, Do not fear before the servants of the Chaldeans; dwell in the land and work for the king of Babylon, and it will be better for you;
Jeremiah 47:10 and behold, I sit before you in Massepha to stand before the face of the Chaldeans who come upon you, and you, gather wine and late fruit and gather oil and put them into your vessels and dwell in the cities which you held fast.
Jeremiah 47:11 And all the Ioudaians in the land of Moab and among the sons of Ammon and those in Idoumaia and those in all the land heard that the king of Babylon gave a remnant to Iouda and that he appointed over them Godolias, son of Achikam,
Jeremiah 47:12 and they came to Godolias in the land of Iouda in Massepha and gathered wine and exceedingly much late fruit and oil.
Jeremiah 47:13 And Ioanan, son of Karee, and all the leaders of the force in the fields came to Godolias in Massepha
Jeremiah 47:14 and said to him: Do you surely know that Belisa, king of the sons of Ammon, sent Ismael to you to strike your soul? And Godolias did not believe them.
Jeremiah 47:15 And Ioanan said to Godolias secretly in Massepha: Let me now go and strike Ismael, and let no one know, lest he strike your soul and all Iouda gathered to you be scattered, and the remaining ones of Iouda will perish.
Jeremiah 47:16 And Godolias said to Ioanan: Do not do this thing, because you speak false things concerning Ismael.

## Chapter 48

Jeremiah 48:1 And it happened in the seventh month, Ismael, son of Nathanias, son of Elasa, from the king's family, and ten men with him came to Godolias in Massepha, and they ate bread together there.
Jeremiah 48:2 And Ismael and the ten men who were with him rose and struck Godolias, whom the king of Babylon appointed over the land,
Jeremiah 48:3 and all the Ioudaians with him in Massepha and all the Chaldeans found there. —
Jeremiah 48:4 And it happened on the second day after he struck Godolias, and no person knew,
Jeremiah 48:5 men came from Sychem and from Salem and from Samareia, eighty men, with beards shaved and garments torn and lamenting, and manaa and frankincense in their hands to bring into the house of the Lord.
Jeremiah 48:6 And Ismael went out to meet them; they were going and weeping, and he said to them, Enter to Godolias.
Jeremiah 48:7 And it happened, when they entered into the middle of the city, he slaughtered them into the well.
Jeremiah 48:8 And ten men were found there and said to Ismael: Do not kill us, because we have treasuries in a field, wheat and barley, honey and oil; and he passed by and did not kill them in the midst of their brothers.
Jeremiah 48:9 And the well into which Ismael threw there all whom he struck, this is a great well which King Asa made because of Baasa, king of Israel; this Ismael filled with wounded ones.
Jeremiah 48:10 And Ismael turned back all the people left in Massepha and the daughters of the king whom the chief cook entrusted to Godolias, son of Achikam, and went away to the region of the sons of Ammon. —
Jeremiah 48:11 And Ioanan, son of Karee, and all the leaders of the force with him heard all the evils which Ismael did,
Jeremiah 48:12 and they brought all their army and went to fight him and found him beside much water in Gabaon.
Jeremiah 48:13 And it happened, when all the people with Ismael saw Ioanan and the leaders of the force with him,
Jeremiah 48:14 they also returned to Ioanan.
Jeremiah 48:15 And Ismael escaped with eight men and went away to the sons of Ammon. —
Jeremiah 48:16 And Ioanan and all the leaders of the force with him took all the remaining ones of the people whom he brought back from Ismael, men mighty in war and the women and the other things and the eunuchs whom he brought back from Gabaon,
Jeremiah 48:17 and they went and sat in Gaberoth — chamaam, toward Bethleem, to go to enter Egypt,
Jeremiah 48:18 from before the Chaldeans, because they feared before them, because Ismael struck Godolias, whom the king of Babylon appointed in the land.

## Chapter 49

Jeremiah 49:1 And all the leaders of the force and Ioanan and Azarias, son of Maasaias, and all the people from small to great approached
Jeremiah 49:2 Ieremias the prophet and said to him: Let our plea for mercy now fall before your face, and pray to the Lord your God concerning these remaining ones, because we were left few from many, as your eyes see;
Jeremiah 49:3 and let the Lord your God announce to us the way on which we will go and a word which we will do.
Jeremiah 49:4 And Ieremias said to them: I heard; behold, I will pray to the Lord our God according to your words; and it will be, the word which the Lord answers I will announce to you; I will certainly not hide a word from you.
Jeremiah 49:5 And they said to Ieremias: Let the Lord be among us as a righteous and faithful witness, if we do not do thus according to every word with which the Lord sends you to us;
Jeremiah 49:6 and whether good or evil, we will hear the voice of the Lord our God to whom we send you, so that it becomes better for us, because we will hear the voice of the Lord our God. —
Jeremiah 49:7 And it happened after ten days, a word of the Lord came to Ieremias.
Jeremiah 49:8 And he called Ioanan and the leaders of the force and all the people from small to great
Jeremiah 49:9 and said to them: Thus said the Lord:
Jeremiah 49:10 If you surely dwell in this land, I will build you and certainly not pull down, and plant you and certainly not pluck out; because I have rested from the evils which I did to you.
Jeremiah 49:11 Do not fear before the king of Babylon before whom you fear; do not fear, says the Lord, because I am with you to deliver you and save you from his hand;
Jeremiah 49:12 and I will give you mercy and have mercy on you and return you to your land.
Jeremiah 49:13 And if you say, We will certainly not dwell in this land, so as not to hear the voice of the Lord,
Jeremiah 49:14 because we will enter the land of Egypt and certainly not see war and certainly not hear a sound of a trumpet and certainly not hunger for bread, and there we will dwell,
Jeremiah 49:15 therefore hear a word of the Lord: Thus said the Lord: If you set your face toward Egypt and enter there to dwell,
Jeremiah 49:16 it will also be, the sword before which you fear will find you in the land of Egypt, and the famine about which you have concern will overtake you behind you in Egypt, and there you will die.
Jeremiah 49:17 And all the people and all the foreigners who set their face toward the land of Egypt to dwell there will cease by sword and by famine, and there will be none of them saved from the evils which I am bringing upon them.
Jeremiah 49:18 Because thus said the Lord: As my wrath dripped upon those dwelling in Ierusalem, thus my wrath will drip upon you when you enter Egypt, and you will be for an impassable place and subject to others and for a curse and for reproach, and you will certainly not see this place any longer,
Jeremiah 49:19 things which the Lord spoke concerning you, the remaining ones of Iouda: Do not enter Egypt. And now you will surely know
Jeremiah 49:20 that you acted wickedly in your souls, sending me, saying, Pray concerning us to the Lord, and according to everything which the Lord speaks to you we will do.
Jeremiah 49:21 And you did not hear the voice of the Lord with which he sent me to you.
Jeremiah 49:22 And now by sword and by famine you will cease in the place where you wish to enter to dwell there.

## Chapter 50

Jeremiah 50:1 And it happened, when Ieremias ceased saying to the people all the words of the Lord with which the Lord sent him to them, all these words,
Jeremiah 50:2 Azarias, son of Maasaias, and Ioanan, son of Karee, and all the men said, those saying to Ieremias, saying, Falsehoods; the Lord did not send you to us, saying, Do not enter Egypt to dwell there,
Jeremiah 50:3 but rather Barouch, son of Nerias, sets you against us, so that you give us into the hands of the Chaldeans to put us to death and deport us to Babylon.
Jeremiah 50:4 And Ioanan and all the leaders of the force and all the people did not hear the voice of the Lord to dwell in the land of Iouda.
Jeremiah 50:5 And Ioanan and all the leaders of the force took all the remaining ones of Iouda who returned to dwell in the land,
Jeremiah 50:6 the mighty men and the women and the infants and the daughters of the king and the souls whom Nabouzardan left with Godolias, son of Achikam, and Ieremias the prophet and Barouch, son of Nerias,
Jeremiah 50:7 and entered Egypt, because they did not hear the voice of the Lord; and they entered Taphnas.
Jeremiah 50:8 And a word of the Lord came to Ieremias in Taphnas, saying,
Jeremiah 50:9 Take for yourself great stones and hide them at the entrance, in the gate of Pharao's house in Taphnas, before the eyes of the men of Iouda,
Jeremiah 50:10 and you will say: Thus said the Lord: Behold, I am sending and will bring Nabouchodonosor, king of Babylon, and he will set his throne above these stones which you hid and raise his weapons over them
Jeremiah 50:11 and enter and strike the land of Egypt: those for death, to death, and those for deportation, to deportation, and those for sword, to sword.
Jeremiah 50:12 And he will burn a fire in the houses of their gods and burn them and deport them and delouse the land of Egypt, just as a shepherd delouses his garment, and he will go out in peace.
Jeremiah 50:13 And he will crush the pillars of the City of the Sun in On and burn up their houses with fire.

## Chapter 51

Jeremiah 51:1 The word that came to Ieremias for all the Ioudaians dwelling in the land of Egypt and those sitting in Magdolon and in Taphnas and in the land of Pathoures, saying,
Jeremiah 51:2 Thus said the Lord, the God of Israel: You have seen all the evils which I brought upon Ierusalem and upon the cities of Iouda, and behold, they are desolate of inhabitants
Jeremiah 51:3 because of their wickedness which they did to embitter me, going to burn incense to other gods which you did not know.
Jeremiah 51:4 And I sent to you my servants the prophets at dawn and sent, saying, Do not do the thing of this defilement which I hated.
Jeremiah 51:5 And they did not hear me and did not incline their ear to turn from their evils so as not to burn incense to other gods.
Jeremiah 51:6 And my anger and my wrath dripped and blazed in the cities of Iouda and outside Ierusalem, and they became a desolation and an impassable place as this day.
Jeremiah 51:7 And now thus said the Lord Almighty: Why do you do great evils against your souls, to cut off from you man and woman, infant and nursing one, from the midst of Iouda, so that none of you is left,
Jeremiah 51:8 to embitter me with the works of your hands, burning incense to other gods in the land of Egypt into which you entered to dwell there, so that you are cut off and become a curse and a reproach among all the nations of the earth?
Jeremiah 51:9 Have you forgotten the evils of your fathers and the evils of the kings of Iouda and the evils of your rulers and the evils of your wives which they did in the land of Iouda and outside Ierusalem?
Jeremiah 51:10 And they did not cease until this day and did not hold fast to my ordinances which I gave before the face of their fathers.
Jeremiah 51:11 Therefore thus said the Lord: Behold, I am setting my face
Jeremiah 51:12 to destroy all the remaining ones in Egypt, and they will fall; by sword and by famine they will cease from small to great and will be for reproach and for destruction and for a curse.
Jeremiah 51:13 And I will visit upon those sitting in the land of Egypt as I visited upon Ierusalem, by sword and by famine and by death,
Jeremiah 51:14 and none of the remaining ones of Iouda sojourning in the land of Egypt will be saved to return to the land of Iouda, to which they hope in their souls to return there; they will certainly not return except those escaped. —
Jeremiah 51:15 And all the men knowing that their wives burn incense to other gods and all the women, a great assembly, and all the people sitting in the land of Egypt in Pathoure answered Ieremias, saying,
Jeremiah 51:16 The word which you spoke to us in the name of the Lord, we will not hear you,
Jeremiah 51:17 because we will surely do every word which comes out of our mouth, to burn incense to the queen of heaven and pour libations to her, as we and our fathers and our kings and our rulers did in the cities of Iouda and outside Ierusalem, and we were filled with bread and became well and did not see evils;
Jeremiah 51:18 and when we ceased burning incense to the queen of heaven, we were all diminished and ceased by sword and by famine.
Jeremiah 51:19 And because we burn incense to the queen of heaven and poured libations to her, did we make chauonas for her and pour libations to her without our husbands? —
Jeremiah 51:20 And Ieremias said to all the people, to the mighty ones and to the women and to all the people who answered him words, saying,
Jeremiah 51:21 Did the Lord not remember the incense which you burned in the cities of Iouda and outside Ierusalem, you and your fathers and your kings and your rulers and the people of the land, and did it not come up upon his heart?
Jeremiah 51:22 And the Lord could no longer bear because of the wickedness of your deeds, because of the abominations which you did; and your land became a desolation and an impassable place and a curse, as on this day,
Jeremiah 51:23 because you were burning incense and sinned against the Lord and did not hear the voice of the Lord and did not walk in his ordinances and in his law and in his testimonies, and these evils overtook you.
Jeremiah 51:24 And Ieremias said to the people and to the women: Hear the word of the Lord;
Jeremiah 51:25 thus said the Lord, the God of Israel: You women spoke with your mouth and fulfilled with your hands, saying, We will surely do our vows which we vowed, to burn incense to the queen of heaven and pour libations to her; you surely remained in your vows and surely did them.
Jeremiah 51:26 Therefore hear a word of the Lord, all Iouda sitting in the land of Egypt: Behold, I swore by my great name, said the Lord, that my name will no longer be in the mouth of all Iouda, to say, The Lord, the Lord lives, in all the land of Egypt.
Jeremiah 51:27 Because behold, I have watched over them to harm them and not to do good, and all Iouda dwelling in the land of Egypt will cease by sword and by famine until they cease.
Jeremiah 51:28 And those saved from sword will return to the land of Iouda few in number, and the remaining ones of Iouda who settled in the land of Egypt to dwell there will know whose word will remain.
Jeremiah 51:29 And this is the sign for you, that I will visit upon you for evil things;
Jeremiah 51:30 thus said the Lord: Behold, I am giving Ouaphre, king of Egypt, into the hands of his enemy and into the hands of those seeking his soul, as I gave Sedekias, king of Iouda, into the hands of Nabouchodonosor, king of Babylon, his enemy and the one seeking his soul.
Jeremiah 51:31 The word which Ieremias the prophet spoke to Barouch, son of Nerias, when he was writing these words in the book from the mouth of Ieremias in the fourth year for Ioakim, son of Iosias, king of Iouda:
Jeremiah 51:32 Thus said the Lord concerning you, Barouch:
Jeremiah 51:33 Because you said, Alas, alas, because the Lord added toil to suffering for me; I slept in groanings, I did not find rest,
Jeremiah 51:34 say to him: Thus said the Lord: Behold, those whom I built, I am pulling down, and those whom I planted, I am plucking out;
Jeremiah 51:35 and do you seek great things for yourself? Do not seek, because behold, I am bringing evils upon all flesh, says the Lord, and I will give your soul as a find in every place wherever you go there.

## Chapter 52

Jeremiah 52:1 Sedekias being twenty-one years old when he began to reign, and he reigned eleven years in Ierusalem, and the name of his mother was Amitaal, daughter of Ieremias, from Lobena,
Jeremiah 52:4 and it happened in the ninth year of his reign, in the tenth month, on the tenth of the month, Nabouchodonosor, king of Babylon, and all his force came against Ierusalem and made siegeworks around her and built around her with four-foot stones all around.
Jeremiah 52:5 And the city came into confinement until the eleventh year for King Sedekias;
Jeremiah 52:6 on the ninth of the month famine became firm in the city, and there were no loaves for the people of the land.
Jeremiah 52:7 And the city was broken through, and all the men of war went out by night along the way of the gate between the wall and the outer wall, which was by the king's garden, and the Chaldeans were upon the city all around. And they went along the way to Araba,
Jeremiah 52:8 and the force of the Chaldeans pursued after the king and overtook him in the region of Iericho, and all his servants were scattered from him.
Jeremiah 52:9 And they seized the king and brought him to the king of Babylon in Deblatha, and he spoke to him with judgment;
Jeremiah 52:10 and the king of Babylon slaughtered the sons of Sedekias before his eyes, and all the rulers of Iouda he slaughtered in Deblatha;
Jeremiah 52:11 and he blinded the eyes of Sedekias and bound him in fetters, and the king of Babylon brought him to Babylon and put him into a mill house until the day on which he died.
Jeremiah 52:12 And in the fifth month, on the tenth of the month, Nabouzardan the chief cook, standing before the face of the king of Babylon, came to Ierusalem.
Jeremiah 52:13 And he burned the house of the Lord and the house of the king and all the houses of the city, and every great house he burned with fire.
Jeremiah 52:14 And all the wall of Ierusalem all around the force of the Chaldeans with the chief cook pulled down.
Jeremiah 52:16 And the remaining ones of the people the chief cook left as vine workers and farmers.
Jeremiah 52:17 And the bronze pillars in the house of the Lord and the bases and the bronze sea in the house of the Lord the Chaldeans crushed and took their bronze and carried it away to Babylon.
Jeremiah 52:18 And the crown and the bowls and the meat hooks and all the bronze vessels with which they ministered,
Jeremiah 52:19 and the sapphoth and the masmaroth and the pouring vessels and the lampstands and the incense dishes and the ladles, those which were gold, gold, and those which were silver, silver, the chief cook took.
Jeremiah 52:20 And the two pillars and the one sea and the twelve bronze calves beneath the sea, which King Salomon made for the house of the Lord; there was no weight for their bronze.
Jeremiah 52:21 And the pillars, thirty-five cubits the height of the one pillar, and a cord of twelve cubits encircled it, and its thickness four fingers all around,
Jeremiah 52:22 and a bronze cornice upon them, and five cubits the length, the projection of the one cornice, and a net and pomegranates upon the cornice all around, all bronze; and according to these for the second pillar, eight pomegranates to the cubit for the twelve cubits.
Jeremiah 52:23 And the pomegranates were ninety-six on the one part, and all the pomegranates upon the net all around were a hundred.
Jeremiah 52:24 And the chief cook took the first priest and the second priest and the three guarding the way
Jeremiah 52:25 and one eunuch who was overseer of the men of war, and seven renowned men before the face of the king found in the city and the scribe of the forces serving as scribe for the people of the land, and sixty people from the people of the land found in the midst of the city;
Jeremiah 52:26 and Nabouzardan the chief cook took them and brought them to the king of Babylon in Deblatha,
Jeremiah 52:27 and the king of Babylon struck them in Deblatha in the land of Aimath.
Jeremiah 52:31 And it happened in the thirty-seventh year after Ioakim, king of Iouda, was deported, in the twelfth month, on the twenty-fourth of the month, Oulaimaradach, king of Babylon, in the year in which he reigned, lifted the head of Ioakim, king of Iouda, and brought him out of the house in which he was guarded;
Jeremiah 52:32 and he spoke good things to him and placed his throne above the thrones of the kings with him in Babylon;
Jeremiah 52:33 and he changed his prison robe, and he ate bread continually before his face all the days which he lived;
Jeremiah 52:34 and his allowance was given continually by the king of Babylon, day by day, until the day on which he died.

# Baruch

The Apostolic Bible. Public domain. https://apostolic-bible.ysys9.chatgpt.site/license.html


## Chapter 1

Baruch 1:1 And these are the words of the book which Barouch son of Nerias son of Maasaias son of Sedekias son of Asadias son of Chelkias wrote in Babylon
Baruch 1:2 in the fifth year, on the seventh of the month, at the time when the Chaldeans took Ierusalem and burned it with fire.
Baruch 1:3 And Barouch read the words of this book in the ears of Iechonias son of Ioakim king of Iouda and in the ears of all the people who came to the book,
Baruch 1:4 and in the ears of the mighty and sons of the kings and in the ears of the elders and in the ears of all the people, from small to great, all who dwelt in Babylon by the river Soud.
Baruch 1:5 And they wept and fasted and prayed before the Lord,
Baruch 1:6 and gathered silver according as each one's hand was able,
Baruch 1:7 and sent to Ierusalem to Ioakim son of Chelkias son of Salom, the priest, and to the priests and to all the people who were found with him in Ierusalem,
Baruch 1:8 when he took the vessels of the Lord's house which had been brought out of the temple, to return them to the land of Iouda on the tenth of Siouan, silver vessels which Sedekias son of Iosias king of Iouda made,
Baruch 1:9 after Nabouchodonosor king of Babylon deported Iechonias and the rulers and the prisoners and the mighty and the people of the land from Ierusalem and brought him to Babylon.
Baruch 1:10 And they said, Behold, we have sent silver to you; and buy with the silver whole burnt offerings and offerings concerning sin and frankincense, and make manna and offer upon the altar of the Lord our God,
Baruch 1:11 and pray concerning the life of Nabouchodonosor king of Babylon and for the life of Baltasar his son, that their days may be as the days of heaven upon the earth.
Baruch 1:12 And the Lord will give us strength and illuminate our eyes, and we shall live under the shadow of Nabouchodonosor king of Babylon and under the shadow of Baltasar his son, and serve them many days and find favor before them.
Baruch 1:13 And pray concerning us to the Lord our God, because we sinned against the Lord our God, and the Lord's wrath and his anger have not turned away from us until this day.
Baruch 1:14 And you shall read this book which we sent to you, to declare in the Lord's house on a feast day and on days of an appointed time,
Baruch 1:15 and you shall say, To the Lord our God belongs righteousness, but to us shame of faces, as this day, to the person of Iouda and those dwelling in Ierusalem,
Baruch 1:16 and to our kings and to our rulers and to our priests and to our prophets and to our fathers,
Baruch 1:17 inasmuch as we sinned before the Lord
Baruch 1:18 and disobeyed him and did not hear the voice of the Lord our God, to walk in the Lord's ordinances which he gave before our face.
Baruch 1:19 From the day when the Lord brought our fathers out of the land of Egypt until this day, we were disobedient toward the Lord our God and acted heedlessly so as not to hear his voice.
Baruch 1:20 And the evils clung to us, and the curse which the Lord prescribed to Moyses his servant on the day when he brought our fathers out of the land of Egypt to give us a land flowing with milk and honey, as this day.
Baruch 1:21 And we did not hear the voice of the Lord our God according to all the words of the prophets whom he sent to us,
Baruch 1:22 and we went, each in the thought of his evil heart, to serve other gods, to do evil things before the eyes of the Lord our God.

## Chapter 2

Baruch 2:1 And the Lord established his word which he spoke against us and against our judges who judged Israel and against our kings and against our rulers and against the person of Israel and Iouda.
Baruch 2:2 It was not done beneath all heaven as he did in Ierusalem, according to the things written in the law of Moyses,
Baruch 2:3 that we should eat, a person the flesh of his son and a person the flesh of his daughter.
Baruch 2:4 And he gave them into the hands of all the kingdoms around us, for reproach and for an untrodden place among all the peoples round about, where the Lord scattered them there.
Baruch 2:5 And they became beneath and not above, because we sinned against the Lord our God by not hearing his voice. —
Baruch 2:6 To the Lord our God belongs righteousness, but to us and to our fathers shame of faces, as this day.
Baruch 2:7 What the Lord spoke against us, all these evils came upon us.
Baruch 2:8 And we did not entreat the face of the Lord, that each should turn from the thoughts of their evil heart.
Baruch 2:9 And the Lord watched over the evils, and the Lord brought them upon us, because the Lord is righteous in all his works which he commanded us.
Baruch 2:10 And we did not hear his voice, to walk in the Lord's ordinances which he gave before our face. —
Baruch 2:11 And now, Lord, God of Israel, who brought your people out of the land of Egypt with a mighty hand and with signs and with wonders and with great power and with a high arm, and made yourself a name, as this day,
Baruch 2:12 we sinned, we acted impiously, we acted unjustly, Lord our God, against all your just requirements.
Baruch 2:13 Let your wrath turn away from us, because we were left few among the nations where you scattered us there.
Baruch 2:14 Hear, Lord, our prayer and our supplication, and deliver us for your sake and give us favor before the face of those who deported us,
Baruch 2:15 that all the earth may know that you are the Lord our God, because your name was called upon Israel and upon his race.
Baruch 2:16 Lord, look down from your holy house and consider us; incline, Lord, your ear and hear;
Baruch 2:17 open, Lord, your eyes and see; because the dead in Hades, whose spirit was taken from their inward parts, will not give glory and a just acknowledgment to the Lord,
Baruch 2:18 but the soul grieving greatly, that which walks stooping and weak, and the failing eyes and the hungry soul will give you glory and righteousness, Lord.
Baruch 2:19 Because it is not upon the just deeds of our fathers and our kings that we lay down our plea for mercy before your face, Lord our God,
Baruch 2:20 because you let your wrath and your anger into us, just as you spoke by the hand of your servants the prophets, saying,
Baruch 2:21 Thus said the Lord, Incline your shoulder and serve the king of Babylon and dwell upon the land which I gave to your fathers;
Baruch 2:22 and if you do not hear the voice of the Lord, to serve the king of Babylon,
Baruch 2:23 I will cause to cease from the cities of Iouda and outside Ierusalem the voice of gladness and the voice of joy, the voice of bridegroom and the voice of bride, and all the land will be untrodden, without inhabitants.
Baruch 2:24 And we did not hear your voice, to serve the king of Babylon, and you established your words which you spoke by the hands of your servants the prophets, that the bones of our kings and the bones of our fathers should be brought out of their place,
Baruch 2:25 and behold, they are cast out to the heat of the day and to the frost of the night, and they died in evil afflictions, in famine and by the sword and by a sending away.
Baruch 2:26 And you made the house upon which your name was called as this day, because of the wickedness of the house of Israel and the house of Iouda. —
Baruch 2:27 And you dealt with us, Lord our God, according to all your forbearance and according to all your great compassion,
Baruch 2:28 as you spoke by the hand of your servant Moyses on the day when you commanded him to write your law before the sons of Israel, saying,
Baruch 2:29 If you do not hear my voice, surely this great, abundant clamor will turn to a small one among the nations where I shall scatter them there;
Baruch 2:30 because I knew that they would certainly not hear me, because they are a stiff-necked people. And they will return to their heart in the land of their deportation
Baruch 2:31 and know that I am the Lord their God. And I will give them a heart and ears that hear,
Baruch 2:32 and they will praise me in the land of their deportation and remember my name
Baruch 2:33 and turn away from their stiff back and from their evil deeds, because they will remember the way of their fathers who sinned before the Lord.
Baruch 2:34 And I will return them to the land which I swore to their fathers, to Abraam and to Isaak and to Iakob, and they shall rule over it; and I will multiply them, and they shall certainly not be diminished;
Baruch 2:35 and I will establish an everlasting covenant for them, that I should be God to them and they shall be a people to me; and I will no longer move my people Israel from the land which I gave them. —

## Chapter 3

Baruch 3:1 Lord Almighty, God of Israel, a soul in straits and a spirit of despondency has cried to you.
Baruch 3:2 Hear, Lord, and have mercy, because we sinned before you;
Baruch 3:3 because you sit forever, and we perish forever.
Baruch 3:4 Lord Almighty, God of Israel, hear indeed the prayer of the dead of Israel and of the sons of those who sin before you, who did not hear the voice of the Lord their God, and the evils clung to us.
Baruch 3:5 Do not remember our fathers' injustices, but remember your hand and your name at this time;
Baruch 3:6 because you are the Lord our God, and we shall praise you, Lord.
Baruch 3:7 Because for this reason you gave your fear upon our heart, to call upon your name, and we shall praise you in our exile, because we turned away from our heart all the injustice of our fathers who sinned before you.
Baruch 3:8 Behold, we today are in our exile, where you scattered us there, for reproach and for a curse and for a liability, according to all the injustices of our fathers who departed from the Lord our God.
Baruch 3:9 Hear, Israel, commandments of life; give ear to know understanding.
Baruch 3:10 What is it, Israel? Why is it that you are in the land of enemies, you grew old in a foreign land,
Baruch 3:11 you were defiled with the dead, you were counted with those in Hades?
Baruch 3:12 You abandoned the fountain of wisdom.
Baruch 3:13 If you had walked in the way of God, you would have dwelt in peace forever.
Baruch 3:14 Learn where understanding is, where strength is, where comprehension is, to know at once where length of days and life are, where light of eyes and peace are. —
Baruch 3:15 Who found her place, and who entered her treasuries?
Baruch 3:16 Where are the rulers of the nations and those who rule over the beasts upon the earth,
Baruch 3:17 those who sport with the birds of heaven and treasure up silver and gold in which people had trusted, and there is no end of their acquisition,
Baruch 3:18 those who fashion silver and take pains, and there is no finding out of their works?
Baruch 3:19 They vanished and went down to Hades, and others rose in their place.
Baruch 3:20 Younger ones saw light and dwelt upon the earth, but they did not know the way of knowledge,
Baruch 3:21 nor comprehend her paths nor lay hold of her; their sons became far from their way.
Baruch 3:22 Nor was she heard in Chanaan nor seen in Thaiman,
Baruch 3:23 nor did the sons of Agar who seek out comprehension upon the earth, the merchants of Merran and Thaiman, the tellers of tales and the seekers of comprehension, know the way of wisdom, nor did they remember her paths. —
Baruch 3:24 O Israel, how great is the house of God and how extensive the place of his possession!
Baruch 3:25 Great and it has no end, high and immeasurable.
Baruch 3:26 There were born the renowned giants of the beginning, who became of great size, skilled in war.
Baruch 3:27 God did not choose these, nor give them the way of knowledge;
Baruch 3:28 and they perished through not having understanding, they perished because of their lack of counsel. —
Baruch 3:29 Who ascended into heaven and took her and brought her down from the clouds?
Baruch 3:30 Who crossed beyond the sea and found her and will bring her for choice gold?
Baruch 3:31 There is none who knows her way nor who considers her path;
Baruch 3:32 but he who knows all things knows her; he found her by his comprehension; he who prepared the earth for everlasting time filled it with four-footed animals;
Baruch 3:33 he who sends out the light, and it goes, called it, and it obeyed him with trembling;
Baruch 3:34 and the stars shone in their watches and were glad;
Baruch 3:35 he called them and they said, We are here; they shone with gladness for him who made them.
Baruch 3:36 This is our God; no other shall be reckoned beside him.
Baruch 3:37 He found every way of knowledge and gave it to Iakob his servant and Israel who was loved by him;
Baruch 3:38 after this he appeared upon the earth and lived among people.

## Chapter 4

Baruch 4:1 This is the book of the ordinances of God and the law which exists forever; all who hold fast to her are for life, but those who abandon her will die. —
Baruch 4:2 Return, Iakob, and take hold of her; go through toward the radiance, facing her light.
Baruch 4:3 Do not give your glory to another and the things beneficial to you to a foreign nation.
Baruch 4:4 Blessed are we, Israel, because the things pleasing to God are known to us.
Baruch 4:5 Take courage, my people, memorial of Israel.
Baruch 4:6 You were sold to the nations, not for destruction, but because you provoked God to anger you were handed over to adversaries;
Baruch 4:7 for you provoked him who made you, sacrificing to demons and not to God.
Baruch 4:8 And you forgot the everlasting God who nourished you, and you also grieved Ierusalem who reared you;
Baruch 4:9 for she saw the anger which came upon you from God and said, Hear, neighboring women of Sion, God brought great mourning upon me;
Baruch 4:10 for I saw the captivity of my sons and daughters which the Everlasting brought upon them;
Baruch 4:11 for I nourished them with gladness, but sent them away with weeping and mourning.
Baruch 4:12 Let no one rejoice over me, the widow abandoned by many; I was made desolate because of the sins of my children, because they turned aside from God's law,
Baruch 4:13 and did not know his just requirements nor walk in the ways of God's commandments nor tread paths of discipline in his righteousness.
Baruch 4:14 Let the neighboring women of Sion come, and remember the captivity of my sons and daughters which the Everlasting brought upon them;
Baruch 4:15 for he brought upon them a nation from afar, a shameless nation of another tongue, who did not respect an elder nor have mercy on a child,
Baruch 4:16 and led away the widow's beloved ones and left the solitary woman bereft of her daughters.
Baruch 4:17 But how am I able to help you?
Baruch 4:18 For he who brought the evils upon you will deliver you from the hand of your enemies.
Baruch 4:19 Go, children, go; for I was left desolate;
Baruch 4:20 I took off the robe of peace, and put on the sackcloth of my supplication; I shall cry to the Everlasting in my days. —
Baruch 4:21 Take courage, children; cry to God, and he will deliver you from domination, from the hand of enemies.
Baruch 4:22 For I hoped in the Everlasting for your salvation, and joy came to me from the Holy One at the mercy which will come to you quickly from your everlasting Savior.
Baruch 4:23 For I sent you out with mourning and weeping, but God will give you back to me with joy and gladness forever.
Baruch 4:24 For just as the neighboring women of Sion have now seen your captivity, so they will quickly see the salvation from your God which will come upon you with great glory and splendor of the Everlasting.
Baruch 4:25 Children, endure patiently the anger from God which came upon you; your enemy pursued you, and you will see his destruction quickly and tread upon their necks.
Baruch 4:26 My delicate ones went rough ways; they were taken away as a flock seized by enemies. —
Baruch 4:27 Take courage, children, and cry to God; for there will be remembrance of you by him who brought it upon you.
Baruch 4:28 For just as your thought was to stray from God, multiply tenfold, having returned, your seeking of him.
Baruch 4:29 For he who brought the evils upon you will bring everlasting gladness upon you with your salvation.
Baruch 4:30 Take courage, Ierusalem; he who named you will comfort you.
Baruch 4:31 Wretched are those who afflicted you and rejoiced over your fall,
Baruch 4:32 wretched the cities which your children served, wretched she who received your sons.
Baruch 4:33 For just as she rejoiced at your fall and was glad at your downfall, so she will grieve at her own desolation.
Baruch 4:34 And I will remove from her the exultation of her great throng, and her pride will become mourning.
Baruch 4:35 For fire will come upon her from the Everlasting for long days, and she will be inhabited by demons for a longer time. —
Baruch 4:36 Look around toward the east, Ierusalem, and see the gladness coming to you from God.
Baruch 4:37 Behold, your sons whom you sent away are coming; they come gathered from east to west at the word of the Holy One, rejoicing in the glory of God. —

## Chapter 5

Baruch 5:1 Take off, Ierusalem, the robe of mourning and of your affliction, and put on the comeliness of the glory from God forever.
Baruch 5:2 Wrap yourself in the double cloak of the righteousness from God; set upon your head the headdress of the glory of the Everlasting.
Baruch 5:3 For God will show your splendor to all that is under heaven.
Baruch 5:4 For your name will be called by God forever, Peace of righteousness and glory of reverence for God. —
Baruch 5:5 Rise, Ierusalem, and stand upon the height and look around toward the east and see your children gathered from the setting of the sun to its rising at the word of the Holy One, rejoicing in the remembrance of God.
Baruch 5:6 For they went out from you on foot, led by enemies, but God brings them in to you, borne with glory as a throne of kingship.
Baruch 5:7 For God commanded every high mountain and everlasting dunes to be lowered and ravines to be filled for the leveling of the earth, that Israel might walk safely in the glory of God;
Baruch 5:8 and the woods and every fragrant tree shaded Israel at the command of God;
Baruch 5:9 for God will lead Israel with gladness by the light of his glory, with mercy and righteousness from him.

# Lamentations

The Apostolic Bible. Public domain. https://apostolic-bible.ysys9.chatgpt.site/license.html


## Chapter 1

Lamentations 1:1 t And it happened after Israel was taken captive and Ierusalem made desolate, Ieremias sat weeping and lamented this lament over Ierusalem and said,
Lamentations 1:1 How did the city filled with peoples sit alone? She became like a widow, filled among nations; ruling among countries, she became subject to tribute.
Lamentations 1:2 Weeping, she wept in the night, and her tears were upon her cheeks, and there is none comforting her among all who love her; all her friends dealt faithlessly with her, became enemies to her.
Lamentations 1:3 Ioudaia was removed from her humiliation and from the abundance of her servitude; she sat among nations, found no rest; all who pursued her overtook her amid those who afflict her.
Lamentations 1:4 The ways of Sion mourn because there are none coming at a feast; all her gates are destroyed, her priests groan, her virgins are led away, and she is embittered within herself.
Lamentations 1:5 Those who afflict her became the head, and her enemies prospered, because the Lord humbled her for the multitude of her impieties; her infants went into captivity before the face of an afflicter.
Lamentations 1:6 And all her comeliness went out from daughter Sion; her rulers became like rams finding no pasture, and went without strength before the face of a pursuer.
Lamentations 1:7 Ierusalem remembered the days of her humiliation and her rejection, all her desirable things which were from ancient days, when her people fell into the hands of an afflicter and there was none helping her; her enemies saw and laughed at her removal.
Lamentations 1:8 Ierusalem sinned a sin; therefore she became a shaking; all who honored her humbled her, for they saw her indecency, and indeed she herself groaned and turned backward.
Lamentations 1:9 Her uncleanness is at her feet; she did not remember her last things; and she brought down things exceedingly great; there is none comforting her. See, Lord, my humiliation, because an enemy was magnified.
Lamentations 1:10 An afflicter spread his hand over all her desirable things; for she saw nations enter her sanctuary, whom you commanded not to enter your assembly.
Lamentations 1:11 All her people groan, seeking bread; they gave her desirable things for food, to restore a soul. See, Lord, and look, because I became dishonored.
Lamentations 1:12 Not to you, all who pass along the way; turn and see whether there is pain like my pain which came about; speaking against me, the Lord humbled me on the day of the anger of his wrath.
Lamentations 1:13 From his height he sent fire, into my bones he brought it down; he spread a net for my feet, turned me backward, made me destroyed, suffering all the day.
Lamentations 1:14 Watch was kept over my impieties; in my hands they were intertwined, they rose upon my neck; my strength grew weak, because the Lord gave pains into my hands; I shall not be able to stand.
Lamentations 1:15 The Lord removed all my strong ones from my midst, called an appointed time against me to crush my chosen ones; the Lord trod a winepress for the virgin daughter of Iouda; for these things I weep.
Lamentations 1:16 My eye brought down water, because he who comforts me, who restores my soul, was far from me; my sons became destroyed, because the enemy grew strong.
Lamentations 1:17 Sion spread her hands; there is none comforting her; the Lord commanded concerning Iakob, those who afflict him round about him; Ierusalem became as a woman sitting apart among them.
Lamentations 1:18 The Lord is righteous, because I provoked his mouth to bitterness. Hear indeed, all peoples, and see my pain; my virgins and my young men went into captivity.
Lamentations 1:19 I called my lovers, but they deceived me; my priests and my elders failed in the city, because they sought food for themselves to restore their souls, and found none.
Lamentations 1:20 See, Lord, because I am afflicted; my belly was troubled, and my heart turned within me, because provoking to bitterness, I provoked to bitterness; outside a sword bereaved me, as death in the house.
Lamentations 1:21 Hear indeed that I groan; there is none comforting me; all my enemies heard my evils and rejoiced, because you did it; you brought a day, called an appointed time, and they became like me.
Lamentations 1:22 May all their wickedness come before your face, and glean them as they made a gleaning concerning all my sins, because my groans are many, and my heart grieves.

## Chapter 2

Lamentations 2:1 How did the Lord darken daughter Sion in his anger? He cast down Israel's glory from heaven to earth and did not remember the footstool of his feet on the day of his anger.
Lamentations 2:2 The Lord engulfed without sparing all the beautiful things of Iakob, pulled down in his wrath the strongholds of daughter Iouda, fastened them to the earth, profaned her king and her rulers.
Lamentations 2:3 He broke every horn of Israel in the anger of his wrath, turned his right hand backward from the face of an enemy and kindled in Iakob as fire a flame, and it devoured all things round about.
Lamentations 2:4 He stretched his bow like an enemy, made his right hand firm like an adversary and killed all the desirable things of my eyes in the tent of daughter Sion; he poured out his wrath like fire.
Lamentations 2:5 The Lord became like an enemy, engulfed Israel, engulfed all her citadels, destroyed his strongholds and multiplied for daughter Iouda humiliation upon humiliation.
Lamentations 2:6 And he spread his dwelling like a vine, destroyed his feast; the Lord forgot what he made in Sion, feast and sabbath, and provoked king and priest and ruler with the vehemence of his anger.
Lamentations 2:7 The Lord rejected his altar, shook off his sanctuary, crushed the wall of her citadels in the hand of an enemy; they gave a voice in the Lord's house as on a feast day.
Lamentations 2:8 And the Lord turned to destroy the wall of daughter Sion; he stretched a measure, did not turn his hand away from trampling, and the outer wall mourned, and the wall together grew weak.
Lamentations 2:9 Her gates were fixed into the earth; he destroyed and crushed her bars; her king and her rulers among the nations; there is no law, and indeed her prophets saw no vision from the Lord.
Lamentations 2:10 The elders of daughter Sion sat upon the earth, kept silent, put dust upon their head, girded themselves with sackcloth; they brought down to earth the leading virgins in Ierusalem.
Lamentations 2:11 My eyes failed in tears, my heart was troubled, my glory was poured out upon the earth over the crushing of the daughter of my people, when infant and suckling failed in the city's squares.
Lamentations 2:12 They said to their mothers, Where are grain and wine? When they fainted like wounded ones in the city's squares, when their souls were poured out into their mothers' bosom.
Lamentations 2:13 What shall I testify to you, or what shall I liken to you, daughter Ierusalem? Who will save you and comfort you, virgin daughter Sion? Because the cup of your crushing was made great; who will heal you?
Lamentations 2:14 Your prophets saw vain things and folly for you and did not uncover your injustice to turn back your captivity, and saw vain pronouncements and expulsions for you.
Lamentations 2:15 All who pass along the way clapped hands over you, hissed and shook their head over daughter Ierusalem: Is this the city which they will call Crown of glory, gladness of all the earth?
Lamentations 2:16 All your enemies opened their mouth wide against you, hissed and gnashed teeth, said, We swallowed her; surely this is the day which we expected; we found it, we saw.
Lamentations 2:17 The Lord did what he considered, fulfilled his words which he commanded from ancient days, pulled down and did not spare, and made an enemy glad over you, raised the horn of him who afflicts you.
Lamentations 2:18 Their heart cried to the Lord, Walls of Sion, bring down tears like torrents by day and night; give yourself no respite; let your eye not be silent, daughter.
Lamentations 2:19 Rise, exult in the night at the beginnings of your watch; pour out your heart like water before the face of the Lord; lift your hands toward him concerning the soul of your infants who faint with famine at the beginning of all the exits.
Lamentations 2:20 See, Lord, and look upon whom you gleaned thus; shall women eat the fruit of their womb? A cook made a gleaning; shall infants sucking breasts be murdered? Will you kill priest and prophet in the Lord's sanctuary?
Lamentations 2:21 Child and elder lay down at the exit; my virgins and my young men went into captivity; by sword and by famine you killed, on the day of your anger you slaughtered, you did not spare.
Lamentations 2:22 He called a feast day of my sojourning from round about, and on the day of the Lord's anger there were none escaping and remaining, as I prevailed and multiplied all my enemies.

## Chapter 3

Lamentations 3:1 I am the man who sees poverty under the rod of his wrath upon me;
Lamentations 3:2 he took me and led me away into darkness and not light,
Lamentations 3:3 surely against me he turned his hand all the day.
Lamentations 3:4 He made my flesh and my skin old, crushed my bones;
Lamentations 3:5 he built against me and encircled my head and labored,
Lamentations 3:6 in dark places he seated me like the dead of old.
Lamentations 3:7 He built against me, and I shall not go out; he made my bronze heavy;
Lamentations 3:8 and indeed I shall cry and shout; he blocked my prayer;
Lamentations 3:9 he built up my ways, blocked my paths, troubled them.
Lamentations 3:10 He is a bear lying in wait for me, a lion in hidden places;
Lamentations 3:11 he pursued me when I stood apart and brought me to a halt, made me destroyed;
Lamentations 3:12 he stretched his bow and set me up as a target for an arrow.
Lamentations 3:13 He brought the arrows of his quiver into my kidneys;
Lamentations 3:14 I became a laughingstock to all my people, their song all the day;
Lamentations 3:15 he filled me with bitterness, made me drunk with gall.
Lamentations 3:16 And he knocked out my teeth with a pebble, fed me ash;
Lamentations 3:17 and he thrust my soul away from peace; I forgot good things
Lamentations 3:18 and said, My strife perished, and my hope from the Lord.
Lamentations 3:19 I remembered from my poverty and from my persecution my bitterness and gall;
Lamentations 3:20 my soul will remember and ponder over me;
Lamentations 3:21 this I shall set in my heart; therefore I shall wait.
Lamentations 3:25 The Lord is good to those who wait for him, to the soul which will seek him, good,
Lamentations 3:26 and will wait and be quiet for the salvation of the Lord.
Lamentations 3:27 It is good for a man when he takes up a yoke in his youth.
Lamentations 3:28 He will sit alone and keep silent, because he took it upon himself;
Lamentations 3:30 he will give a cheek to him who strikes him, will be filled with reproaches.
Lamentations 3:31 Because the Lord will not reject forever;
Lamentations 3:32 because he who humbled will have compassion according to the abundance of his mercy;
Lamentations 3:33 because he did not answer from his heart and humbled sons of man.
Lamentations 3:34 To humble beneath his feet all prisoners of earth,
Lamentations 3:35 to turn aside the judgment of a man before the face of the Most High,
Lamentations 3:36 to condemn a person when he is judged, the Lord did not say.
Lamentations 3:37 Who spoke thus, and it happened? The Lord did not command,
Lamentations 3:38 will not the evils and the good come out of the mouth of the Most High?
Lamentations 3:39 Why will a living person grumble, a man concerning his sin?
Lamentations 3:40 Our way was searched out and examined, and let us return to the Lord;
Lamentations 3:41 let us lift our hearts upon hands toward the High One in heaven.
Lamentations 3:42 We sinned, acted impiously, and you were not propitiated.
Lamentations 3:43 You covered in wrath and pursued us; you killed, did not spare.
Lamentations 3:44 You covered yourself with a cloud on account of prayer,
Lamentations 3:45 to shut my eyes and to be thrust away, you placed us amid the peoples.
Lamentations 3:46 All our enemies opened their mouth wide against us;
Lamentations 3:47 fear and wrath came to us, lifting up and crushing;
Lamentations 3:48 my eye will bring down outflows of water over the crushing of the daughter of my people.
Lamentations 3:49 My eye was swallowed up, and I shall not keep silent, because there is no respite,
Lamentations 3:50 until the Lord bends down and sees from heaven;
Lamentations 3:51 my eye will glean upon my soul beyond all the daughters of a city.
Lamentations 3:52 Hunting, my enemies hunted me like a sparrow without cause,
Lamentations 3:53 they put my life to death in a pit and laid a stone upon me,
Lamentations 3:54 water poured over my head; I said, I am rejected.
Lamentations 3:55 I called upon your name, Lord, from the lowest pit;
Lamentations 3:56 you heard my voice: Do not hide your ears from my supplication.
Lamentations 3:57 You drew near to my help on the day when I called upon you; you said to me, Do not fear.
Lamentations 3:58 You judged, Lord, the cases of my soul, redeemed my life;
Lamentations 3:59 you saw, Lord, my troubles, judged my judgment;
Lamentations 3:60 you saw all their vengeance, in all their designs against me.
Lamentations 3:61 You heard their reproach, all their designs against me,
Lamentations 3:62 the lips of those rising against me and their meditations against me all the day,
Lamentations 3:63 their sitting and their rising; look upon their eyes.
Lamentations 3:64 You will give them recompense, Lord, according to the works of their hands,
Lamentations 3:65 you will give them a shield of heart, your toil to them,
Lamentations 3:66 you will pursue in anger and consume them beneath heaven, Lord.

## Chapter 4

Lamentations 4:1 How will gold be dimmed, the good silver altered? Holy stones were poured out at the beginning of all the exits.
Lamentations 4:2 The precious sons of Sion, exalted in gold, how were they reckoned as earthen vessels, works of a potter's hands?
Lamentations 4:3 And indeed dragons uncovered breasts, their cubs suckled; daughters of my people became incurable, like a sparrow in a wilderness.
Lamentations 4:4 The suckling's tongue clung to his throat in thirst; infants asked for bread, there is none breaking it for them.
Lamentations 4:5 Those eating delicacies vanished in the exits; those nursed upon scarlet wrapped themselves in dung heaps.
Lamentations 4:6 And the lawlessness of the daughter of my people was made greater than the lawlessness of Sodoma, overthrown as in haste, and they did not labor with hands in her.
Lamentations 4:7 Her Nazirites were made purer than snow, shone beyond milk; they were made red beyond sapphire stones in their cut form.
Lamentations 4:8 Their appearance darkened beyond soot, they were not recognized in the exits; their skin was fixed upon their bones, they dried up, became like wood.
Lamentations 4:9 Those wounded by sword were better than those wounded by famine; they went pierced through, deprived of the produce of fields.
Lamentations 4:10 Hands of compassionate women boiled their children; they became food for them in the crushing of the daughter of my people.
Lamentations 4:11 The Lord completed his wrath, poured out the wrath of his anger and kindled fire in Sion, and it devoured her foundations.
Lamentations 4:12 Kings of earth did not believe, all who inhabit the inhabited world, that an enemy and an afflicter would enter through the gates of Ierusalem.
Lamentations 4:13 From the sins of her prophets, the injustices of her priests who pour out righteous blood in her midst.
Lamentations 4:14 Her watchers were shaken in the exits, defiled with blood; when they could not, they touched their garments.
Lamentations 4:15 Depart from unclean ones — call them — depart, depart, do not touch, because they were kindled and indeed shaken; say among the nations, They shall certainly not continue to sojourn.
Lamentations 4:16 The face of the Lord is their portion; he will not continue to look upon them; they did not regard the face of priests, did not have mercy on elders.
Lamentations 4:17 While we still existed, our eyes failed toward our help in vain; watching from afar, we watched for a nation that does not save.
Lamentations 4:18 We hunted our little ones, so that they should not walk in our squares; our time has drawn near, our days were fulfilled, our time is present.
Lamentations 4:19 Those pursuing us became swifter than eagles of heaven; upon the mountains they were kindled, in a wilderness they lay in wait for us.
Lamentations 4:20 The breath of our face, the Lord's anointed, was captured in their destructions, of whom we said, In his shadow we shall live among the nations.
Lamentations 4:21 Rejoice and be glad, daughter of Idoumaia who dwells upon earth; indeed the cup of the Lord will pass to you, and you will be made drunk and pour out.
Lamentations 4:22 Your lawlessness ceased, daughter Sion; he will no longer deport you. He visited your lawlessnesses, daughter Edom; he uncovered your impieties.

## Chapter 5

Lamentations 5:1 Remember, Lord, what happened to us; look and see our reproach.
Lamentations 5:2 Our inheritance was turned over to foreigners, our houses to strangers.
Lamentations 5:3 We became orphans, there is no father; our mothers are like widows.
Lamentations 5:4 From our days our wood came in exchange.
Lamentations 5:5 Upon our neck we were pursued; we labored, did not rest.
Lamentations 5:6 Egypt gave a hand, Assour for their fullness.
Lamentations 5:7 Our fathers sinned, they do not exist; we bore their lawless deeds.
Lamentations 5:8 Slaves ruled over us; there is none redeeming from their hand.
Lamentations 5:9 At the cost of our souls we shall bring in our bread from the face of the sword of the wilderness.
Lamentations 5:10 Our skin became livid like an oven; they shriveled from the face of storms of famine.
Lamentations 5:11 They humbled women in Sion, virgins in the cities of Iouda.
Lamentations 5:12 Rulers were hung by their hands, elders were not honored.
Lamentations 5:13 Chosen ones took up weeping, and young men grew weak with wood.
Lamentations 5:14 And elders ceased from the gate, chosen ones ceased from their songs.
Lamentations 5:15 The joy of our heart ceased, our dance turned to mourning.
Lamentations 5:16 The crown of our head fell; woe indeed to us, because we sinned.
Lamentations 5:17 Concerning this our heart became painful, concerning this our eyes darkened;
Lamentations 5:18 over mount Sion, because it was destroyed; foxes passed through her.
Lamentations 5:19 But you, Lord, will dwell forever, your throne to generation and generation.
Lamentations 5:20 Why will you forget us for strife, abandon us for length of days?
Lamentations 5:21 Return us, Lord, to you, and we shall return; and renew our days as before.
Lamentations 5:22 Because rejecting, you rejected us, you were exceedingly angry against us.

# Letter of Jeremiah

The Apostolic Bible. Public domain. https://apostolic-bible.ysys9.chatgpt.site/license.html


## Chapter 1

Letter of Jeremiah 1:1 Copy of a letter which Ieremias sent to those who would be led captive to Babylon by the king of the Babylonians, to announce to them according as he was commanded by God.
Letter of Jeremiah 1:1 Because of the sins which you sinned before God, you will be led captive to Babylon by Nabouchodonosor king of the Babylonians.
Letter of Jeremiah 1:2 Therefore, having entered Babylon, you will be there many years and a long time, until seven generations; but after this I will bring you out from there with peace.
Letter of Jeremiah 1:3 And now you will see in Babylon silver and golden and wooden gods borne upon shoulders, displaying fear to the nations.
Letter of Jeremiah 1:4 Therefore beware lest you too, being made like the foreigners, should be made like them, and fear should seize you concerning them,
Letter of Jeremiah 1:5 when you see a crowd before and behind them worshiping them; but say in your thought, You must be worshiped, Master.
Letter of Jeremiah 1:6 For my angel is with you, and he seeks out your souls.
Letter of Jeremiah 1:7 For their tongue is scraped by a craftsman, and they are overlaid with gold and silver, but are false and cannot speak.
Letter of Jeremiah 1:8 And taking gold, as for a maiden fond of adornment, they fashion crowns upon the heads of their gods;
Letter of Jeremiah 1:9 and sometimes the priests secretly take gold and silver from their gods and spend it on themselves, and they will give some of it also to the prostitutes upon the roof.
Letter of Jeremiah 1:10 And they adorn them with garments like people, silver and golden and wooden gods; but these are not preserved from corrosion and things that eat them.
Letter of Jeremiah 1:11 Though they are clothed in purple apparel, they wipe their face because of the dust from the house, which is abundant upon them.
Letter of Jeremiah 1:12 And it has a scepter like a person judging a country, who will not kill him who sins against it.
Letter of Jeremiah 1:13 And it has a dagger in its right hand and an axe, but it will not deliver itself from war and robbers.
Letter of Jeremiah 1:14 From this they are known to be no gods; therefore do not fear them.
Letter of Jeremiah 1:15 For just as a person's vessel, when broken, becomes useless, such are their gods, when they are installed in the houses.
Letter of Jeremiah 1:16 Their eyes are full of dust from the feet of those entering.
Letter of Jeremiah 1:17 And just as the courts are fenced around for someone who has wronged a king, as for one led away to death, the priests fortify their houses with doors and locks and bars, so that they may not be plundered by robbers.
Letter of Jeremiah 1:18 They burn lamps, even more than for themselves, not one of which they can see.
Letter of Jeremiah 1:19 It is indeed like a beam from the house, and they say that their hearts are licked away; when creeping things from the earth devour them and their apparel, they do not perceive it.
Letter of Jeremiah 1:20 Their face is blackened from the smoke from the house.
Letter of Jeremiah 1:21 Upon their body and upon their head bats, swallows and birds alight, and likewise also cats.
Letter of Jeremiah 1:22 From this you will know that they are not gods; therefore do not fear them.
Letter of Jeremiah 1:23 For the gold which they wear for beauty, unless someone wipes off the corrosion, they shall certainly not shine; for neither, when they were being cast, did they perceive it.
Letter of Jeremiah 1:24 They are bought at every price, and there is no spirit in them.
Letter of Jeremiah 1:25 Without feet they are carried upon shoulders, displaying their own dishonor to people, and those who attend them are also ashamed because, if it should fall to the earth, it must rise through them;
Letter of Jeremiah 1:26 neither if someone stands it upright will it move of itself, nor if it is tilted will it certainly be set upright, but gifts are set before them as before dead ones.
Letter of Jeremiah 1:27 And their priests sell their sacrifices and use them for themselves; likewise also their wives preserve some of them and share neither with a poor person nor with a powerless one; a woman sitting apart and a woman in childbirth touch their sacrifices.
Letter of Jeremiah 1:28 Therefore, knowing from these things that they are not gods, do not fear them.
Letter of Jeremiah 1:29 For how could they be called gods? Because women set offerings before silver and golden and wooden gods;
Letter of Jeremiah 1:30 and in their houses the priests sit upon seats with their tunics torn and their heads and beards shaved, whose heads are uncovered,
Letter of Jeremiah 1:31 and they howl, shouting before their gods like some at a funeral banquet for a dead person.
Letter of Jeremiah 1:32 The priests take from their apparel and clothe their wives and children.
Letter of Jeremiah 1:33 Neither if they suffer evil from someone nor if good will they be able to repay; neither can they appoint a king nor remove one.
Letter of Jeremiah 1:34 Likewise they shall certainly not be able to give wealth or bronze; if someone, having vowed a vow to them, does not pay it, they shall certainly not demand it.
Letter of Jeremiah 1:35 They shall certainly not rescue a person from death nor deliver a weaker one from a strong one.
Letter of Jeremiah 1:36 They shall certainly not bring a blind person to sight, nor deliver a person who is in distress.
Letter of Jeremiah 1:37 They shall certainly not have mercy on a widow nor do good to an orphan.
Letter of Jeremiah 1:38 The wooden and gold-overlaid and silver-overlaid ones are likened to stones from the mountain, and those who attend them will be put to shame.
Letter of Jeremiah 1:39 How then must they be considered or called to be gods?
Letter of Jeremiah 1:40 And further, even the Chaldeans themselves dishonor them, who, whenever they see a mute unable to speak, bring him to Bel and ask him to utter a sound, as though he were able to perceive,
Letter of Jeremiah 1:41 and they themselves cannot, having understood, abandon them, for they have no perception.
Letter of Jeremiah 1:42 And the women, having put cords around themselves, sit in the roads burning bran as incense;
Letter of Jeremiah 1:43 and whenever one of them, drawn away by one of those passing by, lies with him, she reproaches her neighbor because she was not deemed worthy as she herself was, nor was her cord torn.
Letter of Jeremiah 1:44 All the things done for them are false; how then must it be considered or said that they are gods?
Letter of Jeremiah 1:45 They are fashioned by craftsmen and goldsmiths; they shall become nothing else than what the artisans wish them to become.
Letter of Jeremiah 1:46 And those who fashion them themselves shall certainly not become long-lived; how indeed are the things fashioned by them going to be gods?
Letter of Jeremiah 1:47 For they left falsehoods and reproach to those coming after.
Letter of Jeremiah 1:48 For whenever war and evils come upon them, the priests deliberate among themselves where they may hide together with them.
Letter of Jeremiah 1:49 How then is it not possible to perceive that they are not gods, who save themselves neither from war nor from evils?
Letter of Jeremiah 1:50 For being wooden and overlaid with gold and silver, it will be known after these things that they are false; to all the nations and to the kings it will be manifest that they are not gods but works of human hands, and there is no work of God in them.
Letter of Jeremiah 1:51 By what then must it be known that they are not gods?
Letter of Jeremiah 1:52 For they shall certainly not raise up a king of a country nor give rain to people,
Letter of Jeremiah 1:53 and they shall certainly not decide their judgment nor rescue one who is wronged, being powerless; for they are like crows between heaven and earth.
Letter of Jeremiah 1:54 For also whenever fire falls into a house of wooden or gold-overlaid or silver-overlaid gods, their priests will flee and be saved, but they themselves will be burned up like beams in the midst.
Letter of Jeremiah 1:55 And they shall certainly not withstand a king and enemies.
Letter of Jeremiah 1:56 How then must it be accepted or considered that they are gods?
Letter of Jeremiah 1:57 Neither from thieves nor from robbers shall wooden and silver-overlaid and gold-overlaid gods be saved, whose gold and silver and apparel which surrounds them the strong will strip off and go away possessing, nor shall they certainly help themselves;
Letter of Jeremiah 1:58 so that a king displaying his own courage, or a useful vessel in a house which its possessor will use, is better than the false gods; or also a door in a house preserving the things in it is better than the false gods, and a wooden pillar in royal dwellings than the false gods.
Letter of Jeremiah 1:59 For sun and moon and stars, being bright and sent forth for needs, are obedient;
Letter of Jeremiah 1:60 likewise also lightning, whenever it appears, is plainly seen; and the same wind blows in every country;
Letter of Jeremiah 1:61 and whenever the clouds are commanded by God to go over all the inhabited world, they fulfill what was ordered; and the fire sent forth from above to consume mountains and woods does what was commanded.
Letter of Jeremiah 1:62 But these are likened to them neither in appearances nor in powers.
Letter of Jeremiah 1:63 From this they must neither be considered nor called gods, since they are able neither to judge a judgment nor to do good to people.
Letter of Jeremiah 1:64 Therefore, knowing that they are not gods, do not fear them.
Letter of Jeremiah 1:65 For neither shall they curse kings nor bless them.
Letter of Jeremiah 1:66 And they shall certainly not show signs among nations in heaven, nor shine like the sun nor illuminate like the moon.
Letter of Jeremiah 1:67 The beasts are better than they, which can benefit themselves by fleeing into shelter.
Letter of Jeremiah 1:68 Therefore in no manner is it manifest to us that they are gods; therefore do not fear them.
Letter of Jeremiah 1:69 For just as a scarecrow in a cucumber bed guards nothing, so are their wooden and gold-overlaid and silver-overlaid gods.
Letter of Jeremiah 1:70 In the same manner also their wooden and gold-overlaid and silver-overlaid gods are likened to a thorn bush in a garden upon which every bird sits, and likewise also to a dead person cast in darkness.
Letter of Jeremiah 1:71 And from the purple and the marble upon them which decays you will know that they are not gods; and they themselves afterward will be eaten away, and there will be reproach in the country.
Letter of Jeremiah 1:72 Therefore a righteous person who has no idols is better, for he will be far from reproach.

# Ezekiel

The Apostolic Bible. Public domain. https://apostolic-bible.ysys9.chatgpt.site/license.html


## Chapter 1

Ezekiel 1:1 And it happened in the thirtieth year, in the fourth month, on the fifth of the month, and I was amid the captivity by the river Chobar, and the heavens were opened, and I saw visions of God;
Ezekiel 1:2 on the fifth of the month [this was the fifth year of the captivity of king Ioakim]
Ezekiel 1:3 and the word of the Lord came to Iezekiel son of Bouzi, the priest, in the land of the Chaldeans by the river Chobar; and the hand of the Lord came upon me,
Ezekiel 1:4 and I saw, and behold, a lifting wind was coming from the north, and a great cloud in it, and radiance around it and flashing fire, and in its midst like the appearance of electrum amid the fire, and radiance in it.
Ezekiel 1:5 And in the midst was as the likeness of four living creatures; and this was their appearance: a human likeness upon them,
Ezekiel 1:6 and four faces to each, and four wings to each.
Ezekiel 1:7 And their legs were straight, and their feet winged, and sparks like flashing bronze, and their wings light.
Ezekiel 1:8 And a human hand beneath their wings upon their four sides; and the faces of the four of them
Ezekiel 1:9 did not turn when they walked; each went facing their face.
Ezekiel 1:10 And the likeness of their faces: a human face and a lion's face on the right for the four, and a calf's face on the left for the four, and an eagle's face for the four.
Ezekiel 1:11 And their wings were stretched upward for the four, for each two joined to one another, and two covered over their body.
Ezekiel 1:12 And each went facing its face; wherever the spirit went, they went and did not turn.
Ezekiel 1:13 And amid the living creatures an appearance like burning coals of fire, like the sight of torches whirling among the living creatures, and radiance of fire, and lightning went out from the fire.
Ezekiel 1:15 And I saw, and behold, one wheel upon the earth adjoining the living creatures, for the four;
Ezekiel 1:16 and the form of the wheels like the form of tharsis, and one likeness for the four, and their workmanship was as though a wheel were within a wheel.
Ezekiel 1:17 They went upon their four sides; they did not turn as they went,
Ezekiel 1:18 nor did their backs, and they had height; and I saw them, and their backs were full of eyes round about, for the four.
Ezekiel 1:19 And when the living creatures went, the wheels went adjoining them, and when the living creatures rose from the earth, the wheels rose.
Ezekiel 1:20 Wherever the cloud was, there was the spirit of going; the living creatures and the wheels went and rose with them, because a spirit of life was in the wheels.
Ezekiel 1:21 When they went, they went, and when they stood, they stood, and when they rose from the earth, they rose with them, because a spirit of life was in the wheels.
Ezekiel 1:22 And a likeness above the head of the living creatures, as a firmament like the appearance of crystal, stretched over their wings above;
Ezekiel 1:23 and beneath the firmament their wings were stretched, fluttering one against another, two joined for each, covering their bodies.
Ezekiel 1:24 And I heard the sound of their wings as they went, like the sound of much water; and when they stood, their wings ceased.
Ezekiel 1:25 And behold, a voice above the firmament which was above their head.
Ezekiel 1:26 Like the appearance of a sapphire stone, a likeness of a throne upon it, and upon the likeness of the throne a likeness as the form of a person above.
Ezekiel 1:27 And I saw as the sight of electrum from the appearance of the waist and upward, and from the appearance of the waist downward I saw as the appearance of fire and its radiance round about.
Ezekiel 1:28 Like the appearance of a bow when it is in the cloud on a day of rain, so was the standing of the radiance round about. This was the appearance of the likeness of the Lord's glory; and I saw and fall upon my face and heard the voice of one speaking.

## Chapter 2

Ezekiel 2:1 And he said to me, Son of man, stand upon your feet, and I will speak to you.
Ezekiel 2:2 And a spirit came upon me and took me up and raised me and stood me upon my feet, and I heard him speaking to me,
Ezekiel 2:3 and he said to me, Son of man, I send you out to the house of Israel, those provoking me to bitterness, who provoked me to bitterness, they and their fathers, until this day,
Ezekiel 2:4 and you shall say to them, Thus says the Lord,
Ezekiel 2:5 Whether indeed they hear or are terrified — because it is a house provoking to bitterness — and they will know that you are a prophet in their midst.
Ezekiel 2:6 And you, son of man, do not fear them nor be dismayed before their face, because they will rage and gather against you round about, and you dwell amid scorpions; do not fear their words and do not be dismayed before their face, because it is a house provoking to bitterness.
Ezekiel 2:7 And you shall speak my words to them, whether indeed they hear or are terrified, because it is a house provoking to bitterness.
Ezekiel 2:8 And you, son of man, hear him who speaks to you; do not become one provoking to bitterness like the house provoking to bitterness; open your mouth wide and eat what I give you.
Ezekiel 2:9 And I saw, and behold, a hand stretched toward me, and in it a scroll of a book;
Ezekiel 2:10 and he unrolled it before me, and in it were things written on the back and on the front, and upon it were written lament and song and woe.

## Chapter 3

Ezekiel 3:1 And he said to me, Son of man, devour this scroll and go and speak to the sons of Israel.
Ezekiel 3:2 And I opened my mouth wide, and he fed me the scroll.
Ezekiel 3:3 And he said to me, Son of man, your mouth shall eat, and your belly shall be filled with this scroll given to you. And I ate it, and it became in my mouth like sweet honey.
Ezekiel 3:4 And he said to me, Son of man, go, enter the house of Israel and speak my words to them;
Ezekiel 3:5 because you are not sent out to a people deep of lip and heavy of tongue, to the house of Israel,
Ezekiel 3:6 nor to many peoples of another voice or another tongue, nor to those weighty in tongue, whose words you will not understand; and if I had sent you out to such ones, these would have heard you.
Ezekiel 3:7 But the house of Israel will certainly not wish to hear you, because they do not wish to hear me; because all the house of Israel are contentious and hardhearted.
Ezekiel 3:8 And behold, I have made your face strong before their faces, and I will strengthen your contention against their contention,
Ezekiel 3:9 and it will be continually stronger than rock; do not fear them nor be terrified before their face, because it is a house provoking to bitterness.
Ezekiel 3:10 And he said to me, Son of man, all the words which I have spoken with you, receive into your heart and hear with your ears,
Ezekiel 3:11 and go, enter the captivity, to the sons of your people, and you shall speak to them and say to them, Thus says the Lord, whether indeed they hear, whether indeed they yield.
Ezekiel 3:12 And a spirit took me up, and I heard behind me a sound of a great shaking: Blessed is the glory of the Lord from his place.
Ezekiel 3:13 And I saw the sound of the wings of the living creatures fluttering one against another, and the sound of the wheels adjoining them and the sound of the shaking.
Ezekiel 3:14 And the spirit raised me and took me up, and I went in the impulse of my spirit, and the hand of the Lord became mighty upon me.
Ezekiel 3:15 And I entered the captivity aloft and went round those dwelling by the river Chobar, those who were there, and sat there seven days moving about in their midst.
Ezekiel 3:16 And it happened after the seven days, the word of the Lord came to me, saying,
Ezekiel 3:17 Son of man, I have made you a watchman for the house of Israel, and you shall hear a word from my mouth and warn them from me.
Ezekiel 3:18 When I say to the lawless one, By death you shall be put to death, and you did not warn him nor speak to warn the lawless one to turn from his ways that he might live, that lawless one will die in his injustice, and I will require his blood from your hand.
Ezekiel 3:19 And if you warn the lawless one, and he does not turn from his lawlessness and his way, that lawless one will die in his injustice, and you will rescue your soul.
Ezekiel 3:20 And when a righteous one turns from his righteous deeds and commits a transgression, and I give torment before his face, he will die, because you did not warn him, and he will die in his sins, because his righteous deeds which he did shall certainly not be remembered, and I will require his blood from your hand.
Ezekiel 3:21 But if you warn the righteous one not to sin, and he does not sin, the righteous one will live with life, because you warned him, and you will rescue your own soul.
Ezekiel 3:22 And the hand of the Lord came upon me, and he said to me, Rise and go out to the plain, and there speech will be made to you.
Ezekiel 3:23 And I rose and went out to the plain, and behold, there the glory of the Lord stood, like the vision and like the glory which I saw by the river Chobar, and I fall upon my face.
Ezekiel 3:24 And a spirit came upon me and stood me upon my feet, and spoke to me and said to me, Enter and be shut up amid your house.
Ezekiel 3:25 And you, son of man, behold, bonds have been given upon you, and they will bind you in them, and you shall certainly not go out from their midst.
Ezekiel 3:26 And I will bind your tongue, and you will be made mute and will not be to them a man reproving, because it is a house provoking to bitterness.
Ezekiel 3:27 And when I speak to you, I will open your mouth, and you shall say to them, Thus says the Lord, Let him who hears hear, and let him who disobeys disobey, because it is a house provoking to bitterness.

## Chapter 4

Ezekiel 4:1 And you, son of man, take a brick for yourself and place it before your face and draw upon it the city Ierusalem,
Ezekiel 4:2 and set a siege against it and build outworks against it and cast a rampart against it and set camps against it and arrange the missile stations round about;
