1 Daniel 1:15 And after the ten days their appearance seemed beautiful and the condition of their body better than the other young men eating the royal dinner.
1 Daniel 1:16 And Abiesdri was taking away their dinner and their wine, and giving them pulses instead.
1 Daniel 1:17 And the Lord gave the young men knowledge and understanding and prudence in every literary art; and to Daniel he gave understanding in every word and vision and dreams and in all wisdom.
1 Daniel 1:18 And after these days the king ordered them to be brought in, and they were brought by the chief eunuch to King Nabouchodonosor.
1 Daniel 1:19 And the king conversed with them, and among the wise none was found like Daniel and Ananias and Misael and Azarias; and they were with the king.
1 Daniel 1:20 And in every matter and understanding and education, as much as the king sought from them, he found them tenfold wiser than the sophists and philosophers in all his kingdom; and the king glorified them and appointed them rulers and designated them wise beyond all his men in affairs in all his land and in his kingdom.
1 Daniel 1:21 And Daniel continued until the first year of the reign of Cyrus king of the Persians.

## Chapter 2

1 Daniel 2:1 And in the second year of the reign of Nabouchodonosor, it happened that the king fell into visions and dreams and was disturbed in his dream, and his sleep departed from him.
1 Daniel 2:2 And the king ordered the enchanters and the magi and the sorcerers of the Chaldeans to be brought in to tell the king his dreams, and arriving, they stood beside the king.
1 Daniel 2:3 And the king said to them, I have seen a dream and my spirit was moved; therefore I want to know the dream.
1 Daniel 2:4 And the Chaldeans spoke to the king in Syrian, Lord king, live forever; tell your dream to your servants, and we shall explain its interpretation to you.
1 Daniel 2:5 And answering, the king said to the Chaldeans, If you do not truly tell me the dream and make its interpretation clear to me, you shall be made an example, and your possessions shall be taken into the royal treasury;
1 Daniel 2:6 but if you explain the dream to me and tell its interpretation, you shall receive gifts of every kind and shall be glorified by me; make the dream clear to me and interpret it.
1 Daniel 2:7 And they answered a second time, saying, King, say the vision, and your servants shall interpret concerning these things.
1 Daniel 2:8 And the king said to them, Truly I know that you are buying time, just as you have seen that the matter has departed from me; therefore just as I have ordered, so it shall be;
1 Daniel 2:9 if you do not truly tell me the dream and make its interpretation clear, you shall fall into death; for you agreed to make false statements before me until the time is changed; now then, if you tell me the matter which I saw in the night, I shall know that you shall also make its interpretation clear.
1 Daniel 2:10 And the Chaldeans answered before the king, No one of those upon the earth shall be able to tell the king what he has seen, as you ask, and every king and every ruler does not ask such a thing of any wise man and magus and Chaldean;
1 Daniel 2:11 and the word which you seek, king, is difficult and extraordinary, and there is no one who shall make these things clear to the king, except perhaps an angel whose dwelling is not with any flesh; therefore it cannot happen as you suppose.
1 Daniel 2:12 Then the king, becoming gloomy and deeply grieved, ordered all the wise men of Babylonia to be led out;
1 Daniel 2:13 and it was decreed to kill them all, and Daniel and all those with him were sought in order to perish together.
1 Daniel 2:14 Then Daniel told the counsel and opinion which he had to Arioches, the king's chief cook, whom he had ordered to lead out the sophists of Babylonia,
1 Daniel 2:15 and was inquiring of him, saying, Concerning what is a decree issued bitterly by the king? Then Arioches made the ordinance known to Daniel.
1 Daniel 2:16 And Daniel quickly entered before the king and petitioned that time be given him by the king, and that he might make everything clear before the king.
1 Daniel 2:17 Then Daniel went away to his house and showed everything to Ananias and Misael and Azarias, his companions;
1 Daniel 2:18 and he prescribed fasting and petition and seeking help from the Lord Most High concerning this mystery, so that Daniel and those with him might not be given over to destruction together with the sophists of Babylon.
1 Daniel 2:19 Then in a vision in that very night the king's mystery was clearly revealed to Daniel; then Daniel blessed the Lord Most High,
1 Daniel 2:20 and speaking out, said, The name of the great Lord shall be blessed forever, because wisdom and greatness are his;
1 Daniel 2:21 and he changes seasons and times, removing kings and appointing them, giving wisdom to the wise and understanding to those with knowledge;
1 Daniel 2:22 revealing deep and dark things, and knowing the things in darkness and the things in light, and with him is a lodging;
1 Daniel 2:23 to you, Lord of my fathers, I give thanks and praise, because you gave me wisdom and prudence, and now made known to me as much as I petitioned to make clear to the king concerning these things.
1 Daniel 2:24 And Daniel entered before Arioch, who had been appointed by the king to kill all the sophists of Babylonia, and said to him, Do not destroy the sophists of Babylonia, but bring me in before the king, and I will make each thing clear to the king.
1 Daniel 2:25 Then Arioch hastily brought Daniel in before the king and said to him, I have found a wise man from the captivity of the sons of Ioudaia, who shall make each thing clear to the king.
1 Daniel 2:26 And answering, the king said to Daniel, who was called Baltasar in Chaldean, Shall you be able to make clear to me the vision which I saw, and its interpretation?
1 Daniel 2:27 And Daniel, speaking out before the king, said, The disclosure of the mystery which the king has seen does not belong to wise men and sorcerers and enchanters and Gazarenes,
1 Daniel 2:28 but there is a God in heaven revealing mysteries, who made clear to King Nabouchodonosor what must happen at the end of the days. King, live forever; the dream and the vision of your head upon your bed are these.
1 Daniel 2:29 You, king, lying down upon your bed, have seen everything that must happen at the end of the days, and the one revealing mysteries made clear to you what must happen.
1 Daniel 2:30 And to me this mystery was not revealed because of wisdom existing in me beyond all men, but for the sake of its being made clear to the king, what you conceived in your heart was made known to me in knowledge.
1 Daniel 2:31 And you, king, have seen, and behold, one image, and that image was very great, and its surpassing appearance stood before you, and the appearance of the image was fearful;
1 Daniel 2:32 and its head was of fine gold, the chest and the arms silver, the belly and the thighs bronze,
1 Daniel 2:33 and the legs iron, the feet partly of iron and partly earthenware.
1 Daniel 2:34 You were watching until a stone was cut from a mountain without hands and struck the image upon its iron and earthenware feet and ground them down.
1 Daniel 2:35 Then together the iron and the earthenware and the bronze and the silver and the gold became fine, and became as though finer than chaff on a threshing floor, and the wind blew them away so that nothing was left of them; and the stone which struck the image became a great mountain and struck all the earth.
1 Daniel 2:36 This is the vision; and we shall also tell the interpretation before the king.
1 Daniel 2:37 You, king, are a king of kings, and to you the Lord of heaven gave dominion and kingdom and strength and honor and glory,
1 Daniel 2:38 in the whole inhabited world, from men and wild beasts and birds of heaven and the fish of the sea, he delivered under your hands to rule over all; you are the golden head.
1 Daniel 2:39 And after you a kingdom less than you shall arise, and a third, another bronze kingdom, which shall rule over all the earth.
1 Daniel 2:40 And a fourth kingdom, strong like iron which subdues everything and cuts down every tree, and all the earth shall be shaken.
1 Daniel 2:41 And as you have seen its feet partly of potter's earthenware and partly of iron, another kingdom shall be in it, in two parts, just as you saw the iron mixed together with the clay earthenware;
1 Daniel 2:42 and the toes of the feet partly iron and partly earthenware, a certain part of the kingdom shall be strong and a certain part shall be shattered.
1 Daniel 2:43 And as you saw the iron mixed together with the clay earthenware, they shall be mingled in the generation of men, but shall not be of one mind or well disposed to one another, just as neither can iron be blended with earthenware.
1 Daniel 2:44 And in the times of these kings the God of heaven shall establish another kingdom, which shall exist forever and shall not be destroyed, and this kingdom shall certainly not permit another nation, but shall strike and make these kingdoms disappear, and shall itself stand forever,
1 Daniel 2:45 just as you have seen a stone cut from a mountain without hands, and it crushed together the earthenware, the iron and the bronze and the silver and the gold. The great God made known to the king the things that shall be at the end of the days, and the vision is exact, and its interpretation trustworthy.
1 Daniel 2:46 Then King Nabouchodonosor fell upon his face to the ground and worshiped Daniel, and ordered sacrifices and libations to be made for him.
1 Daniel 2:47 And the king, speaking out to Daniel, said, Truly your God is a God of gods and Lord of kings, who alone reveals hidden mysteries, because you were able to make this mystery clear.
1 Daniel 2:48 Then King Nabouchodonosor exalted Daniel and gave great and many gifts and appointed him over the affairs of Babylonia and designated him ruler and leader of all the sophists of Babylonia.
1 Daniel 2:49 And Daniel petitioned the king that Sedrach, Misach, Abdenago be appointed over the affairs of Babylonia; and Daniel was in the royal court.

## Chapter 3

1 Daniel 3:1 In the eighteenth year, King Nabouchodonosor, governing cities and countries and all those dwelling upon the earth from India to Ethiopia, made a golden image, its height sixty cubits and its breadth six cubits, and set it in a plain of the enclosure of the country of Babylonia.
1 Daniel 3:2 And Nabouchodonosor, king of kings and ruling over the whole inhabited world, sent to gather together all the nations and tribes and tongues, satraps, generals, local rulers and consuls, administrators and those in authority by country, and all those throughout the inhabited world, to come to the dedication of the golden image which King Nabouchodonosor set up;
1 Daniel 3:3 and those written before stood opposite the image.
1 Daniel 3:4 And the herald proclaimed to the crowds, It is commanded you, nations and countries, peoples and tongues:
1 Daniel 3:5 when you hear the sound of the trumpet, pipe and lyre, sambyke and psaltery, symphony and every kind of musical instrument, fall down and worship the golden image which King Nabouchodonosor set up;
1 Daniel 3:6 and everyone who does not fall down and worship, they shall throw him into the burning furnace of fire.
1 Daniel 3:7 And at that time, when all the nations heard the sound of the trumpet and every sound of musical instruments, all the nations, tribes and tongues fell down and worshiped the golden image which Nabouchodonosor set up, before it.
1 Daniel 3:8 At that time Chaldean men approached and accused the Jews,
1 Daniel 3:9 and taking up the matter, said, Lord king, live forever;
1 Daniel 3:10 you, king, ordered and decreed that every man who hears the sound of the trumpet and every sound of musical instruments should fall down and worship the golden image,
1 Daniel 3:11 and whoever does not fall down and worship shall be thrown into the burning furnace of fire;
1 Daniel 3:12 but there are certain Jewish men whom you appointed over the country of Babylonia, Sedrach, Misach, Abdenago; those men did not fear your command and did not serve your idol and did not worship your golden image which you set up.
1 Daniel 3:13 Then Nabouchodonosor, enraged with anger, ordered Sedrach, Misach, Abdenago to be brought; then the men were brought before the king.
1 Daniel 3:14 And seeing them together, King Nabouchodonosor said to them, Why, Sedrach, Misach, Abdenago, do you not serve my gods and not worship the golden image which I set up?
1 Daniel 3:15 And now, if indeed you are ready, upon hearing the trumpet and every sound of musical instruments, to fall down and worship the golden image which I set up; but if indeed not, know that if you do not worship, you shall immediately be thrown into the burning furnace of fire; and what god shall rescue you from my hands?
1 Daniel 3:16 And answering, Sedrach, Misach, Abdenago said to King Nabouchodonosor, King, we have no need to answer you concerning this command;
1 Daniel 3:17 for there is a God in the heavens, one Lord of ours whom we fear, who is able to rescue us from the furnace of fire, and from your hands, king, he shall rescue us;
1 Daniel 3:18 and then it shall be evident to you that we neither serve your idol nor worship your golden image which you set up.
1 Daniel 3:19 Then Nabouchodonosor was filled with wrath, and the form of his face was changed, and he ordered the furnace to be heated sevenfold beyond what it ought to be heated;
1 Daniel 3:20 and he ordered the strongest men in the force to bind Sedrach, Misach, Abdenago together and throw them into the burning furnace of fire.
1 Daniel 3:21 Then those men were bound together, having their footwear and their tiaras upon their heads with their clothing, and were thrown into the furnace.
1 Daniel 3:22 Since the king's ordinance was urgent and the furnace was heated sevenfold beyond its former heat, the men appointed bound them together and brought them to the furnace and threw them into it.
1 Daniel 3:23 So the flame, coming out of the furnace, burned and killed the men who bound those with Azarias together, but they themselves were preserved.
1 Daniel 3:24 Thus then Ananias and Azarias and Misael prayed and sang a hymn to the Lord when the king ordered them to be thrown into the furnace.
1 Daniel 3:25 And Azarias stood and prayed thus, and opening his mouth, was giving thanks to the Lord together with his companions in the midst of the fire, while the furnace was heated greatly by the Chaldeans, and they said,
1 Daniel 3:26 Blessed are you, Lord, the God of our fathers, and praiseworthy and glorified is your name forever,
1 Daniel 3:27 because you are righteous in everything you did to us, and all your works are true, and your ways straight, and all your judgments true,
1 Daniel 3:28 and you executed judgments of truth according to everything you brought upon us and upon your holy city of our fathers, Ierusalem, because in truth and judgment you did all these things because of our sins.
1 Daniel 3:29 For we sinned in everything and acted lawlessly in departing from you, and sinned greatly in everything, and did not obey the commandments of your law,
1 Daniel 3:30 nor preserve them nor do as you commanded us, so that it might go well for us.
1 Daniel 3:31 And now everything you brought upon us and everything you did to us, you did in true judgment,
1 Daniel 3:32 and delivered us into the hands of our lawless enemies and most hostile apostates, and to an unjust king, most wicked beyond all the earth.
1 Daniel 3:33 And now we cannot open our mouth; shame and reproach have come to your servants and to those revering you.
1 Daniel 3:34 Do not deliver us up completely because of your name, and do not scatter your covenant,
1 Daniel 3:35 and do not remove your mercy from us because of Abraam, beloved by you, and because of Isaak your servant and Israel your holy one,
1 Daniel 3:36 as you spoke to them, saying that you would multiply their seed like the stars of heaven and like the sand beside the shore of the sea.
1 Daniel 3:37 For, Master, we have been made smaller than all the nations, and are lowly in all the earth today because of our sins,
1 Daniel 3:38 and at this time there is no ruler or prophet or leader or whole burnt offering or sacrifice or offering or incense or place to offer fruit before you and find mercy;
1 Daniel 3:39 but with a shattered soul and humbled spirit may we be accepted, as with whole burnt offerings of rams and bulls and as with myriads of fat lambs;
1 Daniel 3:40 thus let our sacrifice be before you today, and make atonement behind you, because there is no shame for those trusting in you, and bring to completion behind you.
1 Daniel 3:41 And now we follow with a whole heart and fear you and seek your face; do not put us to shame,
1 Daniel 3:42 but deal with us according to your clemency and according to the multitude of your mercy,
1 Daniel 3:43 and rescue us according to your wonders, and give glory to your name, Lord.
1 Daniel 3:44 And may all those displaying evils to your servants be abashed and put to shame from all their dominion, and may their strength be shattered;
1 Daniel 3:45 let them know that you alone are Lord God and glorious over the whole inhabited world.
1 Daniel 3:46 And the king's attendants who threw them in did not cease heating the furnace. And when they threw the three into the furnace at once, and the furnace was red-hot in its heat sevenfold, and when they threw them in, those throwing them in were above them, and the others were burning naphtha and tow and pitch and vine branches beneath them.
1 Daniel 3:47 And the flame spread above the furnace for forty-nine cubits,
1 Daniel 3:48 and went through and burned those of the Chaldeans whom it found around the furnace.
1 Daniel 3:49 But an angel of the Lord descended together with those with Azarias into the furnace and shook the flame of fire out of the furnace,
1 Daniel 3:50 and made the midst of the furnace like a whistling breeze of dew, and the fire did not touch them at all and did not hurt or trouble them.
1 Daniel 3:51 And the three, taking up the song as from one mouth, were singing hymns and glorifying and blessing and exalting God in the furnace, saying,
1 Daniel 3:52 Blessed are you, Lord, the God of our fathers, and praiseworthy and highly exalted forever, and blessed is the holy name of your glory, and exceedingly praiseworthy and highly exalted for all ages.
1 Daniel 3:53 Blessed are you in the temple of your holy glory, and exceedingly hymned and exceedingly glorious forever.
1 Daniel 3:54 Blessed are you upon the throne of your kingdom, and hymned and highly exalted forever.
1 Daniel 3:55 Blessed are you who looks upon abysses, seated upon cheroubim, and praiseworthy and glorified forever.
1 Daniel 3:56 Blessed are you in the firmament, and hymned and glorified forever.
1 Daniel 3:57 Bless the Lord, all the works of the Lord; sing hymns and highly exalt him forever.
1 Daniel 3:58 Bless the Lord, angels of the Lord; sing hymns and highly exalt him forever.
1 Daniel 3:59 Bless the Lord, heavens; sing hymns and highly exalt him forever.
1 Daniel 3:60 Bless the Lord, all waters above heaven; sing hymns and highly exalt him forever.
1 Daniel 3:61 Bless the Lord, all the powers of the Lord; sing hymns and highly exalt him forever.
1 Daniel 3:62 Bless the Lord, sun and moon; sing hymns and highly exalt him forever.
1 Daniel 3:63 Bless the Lord, stars of heaven; sing hymns and highly exalt him forever.
1 Daniel 3:64 Bless the Lord, every shower and dew; sing hymns and highly exalt him forever.
1 Daniel 3:65 Bless the Lord, all winds; sing hymns and highly exalt him forever.
1 Daniel 3:66 Bless the Lord, fire and heat; sing hymns and highly exalt him forever.
1 Daniel 3:67 Bless the Lord, chill and cold; sing hymns and highly exalt him forever.
1 Daniel 3:68 Bless the Lord, dews and snowfalls; sing hymns and highly exalt him forever.
1 Daniel 3:69 Bless the Lord, frosts and cold; sing hymns and highly exalt him forever.
1 Daniel 3:70 Bless the Lord, hoarfrosts and snows; sing hymns and highly exalt him forever.
1 Daniel 3:71 Bless the Lord, nights and days; sing hymns and highly exalt him forever.
1 Daniel 3:72 Bless the Lord, light and darkness; sing hymns and highly exalt him forever.
1 Daniel 3:73 Bless the Lord, lightnings and clouds; sing hymns and highly exalt him forever.
1 Daniel 3:74 Let the earth bless the Lord; let it sing hymns and highly exalt him forever.
1 Daniel 3:75 Bless the Lord, mountains and hills; sing hymns and highly exalt him forever.
1 Daniel 3:76 Bless the Lord, everything growing upon the earth; sing hymns and highly exalt him forever.
1 Daniel 3:77 Bless the Lord, springs; sing hymns and highly exalt him forever.
1 Daniel 3:78 Bless the Lord, seas and rivers; sing hymns and highly exalt him forever.
1 Daniel 3:79 Bless the Lord, sea monsters and all things moving in the waters; sing hymns and highly exalt him forever.
1 Daniel 3:80 Bless the Lord, all birds of heaven; sing hymns and highly exalt him forever.
1 Daniel 3:81 Bless the Lord, quadrupeds and beasts of the earth; sing hymns and highly exalt him forever.
1 Daniel 3:82 Bless the Lord, sons of men; sing hymns and highly exalt him forever.
1 Daniel 3:83 Bless the Lord, Israel; sing hymns and highly exalt him forever.
1 Daniel 3:84 Bless the Lord, priests; sing hymns and highly exalt him forever.
1 Daniel 3:85 Bless the Lord, servants; sing hymns and highly exalt him forever.
1 Daniel 3:86 Bless the Lord, spirits and souls of righteous ones; sing hymns and highly exalt him forever.
1 Daniel 3:87 Bless the Lord, holy ones and humble in heart; sing hymns and highly exalt him forever.
1 Daniel 3:88 Bless the Lord, Ananias, Azarias, Misael; sing hymns and highly exalt him forever, because he rescued us from Hades and saved us from the hand of death and delivered us from the midst of a burning flame and redeemed us from the fire.
1 Daniel 3:89 Give thanks to the Lord, because he is good, because his mercy is forever.
1 Daniel 3:90 Bless, all those revering the God of gods; sing hymns and give thanks, because his mercy is forever and forever and ever.
1 Daniel 3:91 And it happened when the king heard them singing hymns, and standing, he watched them alive, then King Nabouchodonosor marveled and rose hastily and said to his friends,
1 Daniel 3:92 Behold, I see four men unbound walking in the fire, and no destruction has occurred in them, and the appearance of the fourth is the likeness of an angel of God.
1 Daniel 3:93 And the king approached the door of the furnace [which was] burning with fire and called them by name, Sedrach, Misach, Abdenago, servants of the Most High God of gods, come out of the fire. Thus then the men came out from the midst of the fire.
1 Daniel 3:94 And the consuls, local rulers and chiefs of clans and the king's friends were gathered, and watched those men, that the fire did not touch their body, and their hair was not burned, and their trousers were not changed, nor was a smell of fire in them.
1 Daniel 3:95 And King Nabouchodonosor took up the matter and said, Blessed is the Lord, the God of Sedrach, Misach, Abdenago, who sent his angel and saved his servants who hoped in him, for they rejected the king's command and delivered their bodies to burning, so that they might not serve or worship any other god except their God;
1 Daniel 3:96 and now I decree that every nation and all tribes and all tongues, whoever blasphemes against the Lord, the God of Sedrach, Misach, Abdenago, shall be dismembered and his house confiscated, because there is no other god who shall be able to rescue thus.
1 Daniel 3:97 Thus then the king gave authority to Sedrach, Misach, Abdenago over the whole country and appointed them rulers.
1 Daniel 3:4 In the eighteenth year of the reign of Nabouchodonosor he said, I was at peace in my house and flourishing upon my throne.
1 Daniel 3:5 I saw a dream and became apprehensive, and fear fell upon me.
1 Daniel 3:10 I was sleeping, and behold, a high tree growing upon the earth; its appearance great, and there was no other like it.
1 Daniel 3:12 Its branches in length were about thirty stadia, and beneath it all the beasts of the earth took shade, and in it the birds of heaven nested; its fruit was abundant and good, and supplied all the living creatures.
1 Daniel 3:11 And its appearance was great; its top reached as far as heaven, and its bulk as far as the clouds, filling the things beneath heaven; the sun and the moon dwelt in it and illuminated all the earth.
1 Daniel 3:13 I was watching in my sleep, and behold, an angel was sent in strength from heaven,
1 Daniel 3:14 and he called out and said to it, Cut it down and destroy it; for it has been ordered by the Most High to uproot it and make it useless.
1 Daniel 3:15 And thus he said, Leave one root of it in the earth, so that with the beasts of the earth in the mountains he may graze grass like an ox;
1 Daniel 3:16 and his body may be changed by the dew of heaven, and for seven years he may be fed with them,
1 Daniel 3:17 until he knows that the Lord of heaven has authority over everything in heaven and upon the earth, and does among them whatever he wishes.
1 Daniel 3:17 a Before me it was cut down in one day, and its destruction in one hour of the day, and its branches were given to every wind, and it was dragged and thrown down; and he was eating the grass of the earth with the beasts of the earth, and was delivered into custody, and was bound by them in fetters and bronze handcuffs. I greatly marveled at all these things, and my sleep departed from my eyes.
1 Daniel 3:18 And rising in the morning from my bed, I called Daniel, the ruler of the sophists and the leader of those interpreting dreams, and related the dream to him, and he showed me its whole interpretation.
1 Daniel 3:19 And Daniel marveled greatly, and suspicion pressed upon him, and becoming afraid, trembling taking him and his appearance changing, shaking his head, for one hour he was astonished and answered me with a gentle voice, King, may this dream come upon those hating you, and its interpretation upon your enemies.
1 Daniel 3:20 The tree planted in the earth, whose appearance is great, is you, king.
1 Daniel 3:21 And all the birds of heaven nesting in it: the strength of the earth and of the nations and of all the tongues as far as the ends of the earth, and all the countries serve you.
1 Daniel 3:22 And that that tree was raised high and drew near to heaven and its bulk touched the clouds: you, king, were raised high above all men upon the face of all the earth; your heart was exalted with arrogance and strength concerning the Holy One and his angels; your works were seen, because you desolated the house of the living God on account of the sins of the sanctified people.
1 Daniel 3:23 And the vision which you saw, that an angel was sent in strength from the Lord, and that he said to remove the tree and cut it down: the judgment of the great God shall come upon you,
1 Daniel 3:24 and the Most High and his angels run against you;
1 Daniel 3:25 they shall lead you away into custody and send you into a deserted place.
1 Daniel 3:26 And the root of the tree left, since it was not uprooted: the place of your throne shall be preserved for you for a season and an hour. Behold, they prepare against you and shall scourge you and bring upon you the things judged.
1 Daniel 3:27 The Lord lives in heaven, and his authority is over all the earth; petition him concerning your sins, and redeem all your injustices with alms, so that clemency may be given you and you may be long-lived upon the throne of your kingdom, and he may not destroy you. Love these words; for my word is exact, and your time full.
1 Daniel 3:28 And at the completion of the words, Nabouchodonosor, when he heard the interpretation of the vision, kept the words in his heart. –
1 Daniel 3:29 And after twelve months the king was walking upon the walls of the city with all his glory and passing upon its towers,
1 Daniel 3:30 and answering, said, This is great Babylon, which I built, and it shall be called the house of my kingdom by the strength of my might, for the honor of my glory.
1 Daniel 3:31 And at the completion of his word he heard a voice from heaven, To you it is said, King Nabouchodonosor, the kingdom of Babylon has been taken from you and is given to another, a despised man in your house; behold, I appoint him over your kingdom, and he shall receive your authority and your glory and your luxury, so that you may know that the God of heaven has authority in the kingdom of men, and to whomever he wishes he shall give it; and by sunrise another king shall rejoice in your house and possess your glory and your strength and your authority.
1 Daniel 3:32 And the angels shall pursue you for seven years, and you shall certainly not be seen, nor shall you certainly speak with any man; they shall feed you grass like an ox, and your pasture shall be from the greenery of the earth; behold, in place of your glory they shall bind you, and another shall have the house of your luxury and your kingdom.
1 Daniel 3:33 And by morning everything shall be accomplished upon you, Nabouchodonosor king of Babylon, and nothing of all these things shall fall short. –
1 Daniel 3:33 a I, Nabouchodonosor king of Babylon, was bound for seven years; they fed me grass like an ox, and I ate from the greenery of the earth. And after seven years I gave my soul to petition and pleaded concerning my sins before the Lord, the God of heaven, and concerning my ignorances I petitioned the great God of gods.
1 Daniel 3:34 And my hair became like an eagle's wings, my nails like a lion's; my flesh and my heart were changed, I walked naked with the beasts of the earth. I saw a dream, and suspicions have seized me, and after a time much sleep took me and drowsiness fell upon me. And at the completion of the seven years my time of redemption came, and my sins and my ignorances were fulfilled before the God of heaven; and concerning my ignorances I petitioned the great God of gods, and behold, one angel called me from heaven, saying, Nabouchodonosor, serve the holy God of heaven and give glory to the Most High; the kingdom of your nation is restored to you.
1 Daniel 3:36 At that time my kingdom was restored to me, and my glory was returned to me.
1 Daniel 3:37 I give thanks to the Most High and praise the one who created heaven and earth and the seas and the rivers and everything in them; I give thanks and praise, because he is God of gods and Lord of lords and King of kings, because he performs signs and wonders and changes seasons and times, removing the kingdom of kings and appointing others instead of them.
1 Daniel 3:37 a From now on I will serve him, and from fear of him trembling has seized me, and I praise all his holy ones; for the gods of the nations do not have strength in themselves to turn a king's kingdom to another king, and to kill and make alive and perform signs and great and fearful wonders and change exceedingly great affairs, as the God of heaven did in me and changed great affairs concerning me. All the days of my kingdom I will present sacrifices concerning my soul to the Most High, for a fragrant odor to the Lord, and do what is pleasing before him, I and my people, my nation and my countries in my authority. And as many as spoke against the God of heaven, and as many as are caught saying anything, these I will condemn to death. –
1 Daniel 3:38 And King Nabouchodonosor wrote a circular letter to all the nations by place and countries and all tongues dwelling in all the countries, through generations and generations: Praise the Lord, the God of heaven, and present sacrifice and offering to him gloriously; I, king of kings, give thanks to him gloriously, because he did thus with me; on that very day he seated me upon my throne, and I gained possession of my authority and my kingdom among my people, and my greatness was restored to me.
1 Daniel 3:39 King Nabouchodonosor to all nations and all countries and all those dwelling in them: May peace be multiplied to you at every time. And now I will show you the deeds which the great God did with me; and it seemed good to me to demonstrate to you and to your sophists that there is a God, and his wonders are great, his kingdom a kingdom forever, his authority from generations to generations. And he sent letters concerning everything that had happened to him in his kingdom to all the nations under his kingdom.

## Chapter 5

1 Daniel 5:1 t King Baltasar made a great reception on the day of the dedication of his royal palaces, and called two thousand men from his magnates. On that day Baltasar, exalted by the wine and boasting, praised all the gods of the nations, the cast and carved ones in his place, and did not give praise to God Most High. In that very night fingers like a man's came out and inscribed upon the wall of his house, upon the plaster opposite the lamp, Mane phares thekel. And their interpretation is: mane, it has been numbered; phares, it has been removed; thekel, it has been weighed.
1 Daniel 5:1 King Baltasar made a great banquet for his companions and was drinking wine.
1 Daniel 5:2 And his heart was exalted, and he said to bring the gold and silver vessels of the house of God which Nabouchodonosor his father brought from Ierusalem, and to pour wine in them for his companions.
1 Daniel 5:3 And they were brought, and they were drinking in them,
1 Daniel 5:4 and blessing their handmade idols, and did not bless the eternal God who has authority over their spirit.
1 Daniel 5:5 In that very hour fingers like those of a man's hand came out and wrote upon the wall of his house, upon the plaster opposite the light, before King Baltasar, and he saw a hand writing.
1 Daniel 5:6 And his appearance was changed, and fears and suspicions were pressing upon him. So the king hastened and stood up and was looking at that writing, and the companions around him were boasting.
1 Daniel 5:7 And the king called out with a great voice to summon the enchanters and sorcerers and Chaldeans and Gazarenes to announce the interpretation of the writing. And they were entering to inspect and see the writing, and could not interpret the interpretation of the writing for the king. Then the king issued an ordinance, saying, Every man who shows the interpretation of the writing, he shall clothe him in purple and put a golden necklace upon him, and authority over the third part of the kingdom shall be given to him.
1 Daniel 5:8 And the enchanters and sorcerers and Gazarenes were entering, and no one could announce the interpretation of the writing.
1 Daniel 5:9 Then the king called the queen concerning the sign and showed her how great it was, and that no man could announce to the king the interpretation of the writing.
1 Daniel 5:10 Then the queen mentioned to him Daniel, who was from the captivity of Ioudaia,
1 Daniel 5:11 and said to the king, The man was knowledgeable and wise and surpassing all the wise men of Babylon,
1 Daniel 5:12 and a holy spirit is in him, and in the days of your father the king he showed extraordinary interpretations to Nabouchodonosor your father.
1 Daniel 5:13 Then Daniel was brought before the king, and answering, the king said to him,
1 Daniel 5:16 O Daniel, can you show me the interpretation of the writing? And I will clothe you in purple and put a golden necklace upon you, and you shall have authority over the third part of my kingdom.
1 Daniel 5:17 Then Daniel stood opposite the writing and read, and thus answered the king, This is the writing: It has been numbered, reckoned, removed; and the hand which wrote stood still. And this is their interpretation.
1 Daniel 5:23 King, you made a banquet for your friends and were drinking wine, and the vessels of the house of the living God were brought to you, and you were drinking in them, you and your magnates, and praised all the handmade idols of men; and you did not bless the living God, and your spirit is in his hand, and he himself gave you your kingdom, and you did not bless him or praise him.
1 Daniel 5:26-28 This is the interpretation of the writing: Your time of the kingdom has been numbered, your kingdom is ending, your kingdom has been cut short and completed, it is given to the Medes and the Persians.
1 Daniel 5:29 Then King Baltasar clothed Daniel in purple and put a golden necklace upon him and gave him authority over the third part of his kingdom.
1 Daniel 5:30 And the interpretation came upon King Baltasar, and the kingdom has been removed from the Chaldeans and was given to the Medes and the Persians.

## Chapter 6

1 Daniel 6:1 And Artaxerxes of the Medes received the kingdom. And Dareios was full of days and glorious in old age;
1 Daniel 6:2 and he appointed a hundred twenty-seven satraps over all his kingdom,
1 Daniel 6:3 and over them three men as their leaders, and Daniel was one of the three men,
1 Daniel 6:4 having authority above all in the kingdom. And Daniel was clothed in purple and great and glorious before King Dareios, because he was glorious and knowledgeable and intelligent, and a holy spirit was in him, and he prospered in the king's affairs which he conducted. Then the king resolved to appoint Daniel over all his kingdom, and the two men whom he appointed with him, and a hundred twenty-seven satraps.
1 Daniel 6:5 And when the king resolved to appoint Daniel over all his kingdom, then the two young men devised a counsel and opinion among themselves, speaking to one another, since they found no sin or ignorance against Daniel concerning which they might accuse him before the king,
1 Daniel 6:6 and said, Come, let us establish a decree among ourselves, that no man shall make a request and shall certainly not pray a prayer to any god for thirty days, but only to King Dareios; but if not, he shall die; so that they might overcome Daniel before the king, and he might be thrown into the pit of the lions. For they knew that Daniel prays and petitions the Lord his God three times a day.
1 Daniel 6:7 Then those men approached and said before the king,
1 Daniel 6:8 We have established a decree and enactment, that every man who prays a prayer or makes any request to any god for thirty days, except to King Dareios, shall be thrown into the pit of the lions.
1 Daniel 6:9 And they petitioned the king to establish the decree and not change it, because they knew that Daniel prays and petitions three times a day, so that he might be overcome through the king and thrown into the pit of the lions.
1 Daniel 6:10 And thus King Dareios established and ratified it.
1 Daniel 6:11 And Daniel, learning the decree which he established against him, opened windows in his upper room opposite Ierusalem, and would fall upon his face three times a day, as he did formerly, and petition.
1 Daniel 6:12 And they watched Daniel and caught him praying three times a day each day.
1 Daniel 6:13 Then these men appealed to the king and said, King Dareios, did you not issue a decree that no man should pray a prayer or make a request to any god for thirty days, but to you, king; but if not, he shall be thrown into the pit of the lions? And answering, the king said to them, The word is exact, and the decree shall remain.
1 Daniel 6:13 a And they said to him, We adjure you by the decrees of the Medes and Persians not to change the ordinance or show partiality, and not to diminish anything of what has been said, and to punish the man who did not abide by this decree. And he said, Thus I will do as you say, and this stands for me.
1 Daniel 6:14 And they said, Behold, we found Daniel your friend praying and petitioning the face of his God three times a day.
1 Daniel 6:15 And the king, grieving, said that Daniel should be thrown into the pit of the lions according to the decree which he established against him. Then the king was greatly grieved over Daniel and was helping to rescue him from the hands of the satraps until sunset,
1 Daniel 6:16 and could not rescue him from them.
1 Daniel 6:17 And King Dareios cried out and said to Daniel, Your God, whom you serve continually three times a day, he himself shall rescue you from the hand of the lions; until morning take courage.
1 Daniel 6:18 Then Daniel was thrown into the pit of the lions, and a stone was brought and placed at the mouth of the pit, and the king sealed it with his own ring and with the rings of his magnates, so that Daniel might not be taken away by them, or the king draw him up out of the pit.
1 Daniel 6:19 Then the king returned to his royal palaces and spent the night fasting, and was grieving concerning Daniel. Then the God of Daniel, exercising providence for him, shut the mouths of the lions, and they did not trouble Daniel.
1 Daniel 6:20 And King Dareios rose early in the morning and took the satraps with him, and going, stood at the mouth of the pit of the lions.
1 Daniel 6:21 Then the king called Daniel with a great voice, with weeping, saying, O Daniel, are you indeed alive, and has your God whom you serve continually saved you from the lions, and have they not destroyed you?
1 Daniel 6:22 Then Daniel answered with a great voice and said, King, I am still living,
1 Daniel 6:23 and God has saved me from the lions, because righteousness was found in me before him; and before you also, king, neither ignorance nor sin was found in me; but you listened to men misleading kings and threw me into the pit of the lions for destruction.
1 Daniel 6:24 Then all the forces were gathered and saw Daniel, how the lions did not trouble him.
1 Daniel 6:25 Then those two men who testified against Daniel, they and their wives and their children, were thrown to the lions, and the lions killed them and crushed their bones.
1 Daniel 6:26 Then Dareios wrote to all nations and countries and tongues, to those dwelling in all his land, saying,
1 Daniel 6:27 Let all men in my kingdom worship and serve the God of Daniel, for he is God, enduring and living through generations of generations forever;
1 Daniel 6:28 I, Dareios, shall worship and serve him all my days, for handmade idols cannot save as the God of Daniel redeemed Daniel.
1 Daniel 6:29 And King Dareios was added to his family, and Daniel was appointed over the kingdom of Dareios; and Cyrus the Persian received his kingdom.

## Chapter 7

1 Daniel 7:1 In the first year of Baltasar reigning over the country of Babylonia, Daniel saw a vision beside his head upon his bed; then Daniel wrote the vision which he saw in headings of words:
1 Daniel 7:2 Upon my bed I was watching during sleeps of the night, and behold, four winds of heaven fell upon the great sea.
1 Daniel 7:3 And four beasts were coming up out of the sea, differing one from another.
1 Daniel 7:4 The first was like a lioness having wings like an eagle's; I was watching until its wings were plucked, and it was lifted from the earth and stood upon human feet, and a human heart was given to it.
1 Daniel 7:5 And behold, after it another beast having a likeness of a bear, and it stood upon one side, and three ribs were in its mouth, and thus he said, Rise, devour much flesh.
1 Daniel 7:6 And after these things I was watching another beast like a leopard, and four wings were stretching out above it, and the beast had four heads, and a tongue was given to it.
1 Daniel 7:7 And after these things I was watching in a vision of the night a fourth beast, fearful, and its terror surpassing in strength, having great iron teeth, eating and pounding, trampling round about with its feet, acting differently from all the beasts before it; and it had ten horns,
1 Daniel 7:8 and many counsels in its horns. And behold, another single horn grew up among them, small among its horns, and three of the first horns were dried up through it; and behold, eyes like human eyes in this horn, and a mouth speaking great things, and it was making war against the holy ones.
1 Daniel 7:9 I was watching until thrones were placed, and an ancient of days was seated, having a garment like snow, and the hair of his head like clean white wool, the throne like a flame of fire,
1 Daniel 7:10 and a river of fire was going out before his face; a thousand thousands were attending him and ten thousand ten thousands stood beside him; and a court sat, and books were opened.
1 Daniel 7:11 I was watching then the sound of the great words which the horn was speaking, and the beast was beaten to death, and its body perished and was given to burning with fire.
1 Daniel 7:12 And he removed those around it from their authority, and a time of life was given to them until a time and season.
1 Daniel 7:13 I was watching in a vision of the night, and behold, upon the clouds of heaven one like a son of man was coming, and he was present as an ancient of days, and those standing beside were present to him.
1 Daniel 7:14 And authority was given to him, and all the nations of the earth according to families and all glory were serving him; and his authority is an everlasting authority which shall certainly not be taken away, and his kingdom one which shall certainly not be destroyed. –
1 Daniel 7:15 And I, Daniel, becoming distressed at these things in the vision of the night,
1 Daniel 7:16 approached one of those standing and was seeking from him the exact truth concerning all these things. And answering, he speaks to me and made clear to me the interpretation of the words:
1 Daniel 7:17 These great beasts are four kingdoms which shall perish from the earth;
1 Daniel 7:18 and holy ones of the Most High shall receive the kingdom and possess the kingdom forever and forever and ever.
1 Daniel 7:19 Then I wanted to ascertain exactly concerning the fourth beast, destroying everything and exceedingly fearful, and behold, its teeth iron and its claws bronze, devouring everyone round about and trampling with its feet,
1 Daniel 7:20 and concerning its ten horns upon its head and the other one which grew up, and three fell out through it, and that horn had eyes and a mouth speaking great things, and its appearance surpassed the others.
1 Daniel 7:21 And I was observing that horn engaging in war against the holy ones and routing them,
1 Daniel 7:22 until the ancient of days came, and he gave judgment to the holy ones of the Most High, and the season was given, and the holy ones possessed the kingdom.
1 Daniel 7:23 And it was said to me concerning the fourth beast, that a fourth kingdom shall be upon the earth, which shall differ beyond all the earth and overturn it and grind it down.
1 Daniel 7:24 And the ten horns of the kingdom, ten kings shall stand, and the other king shall stand after these, and he shall differ in evils beyond the first and humble three kings;
1 Daniel 7:25 and he shall speak words against the Most High and wear down the holy ones of the Most High and expect to change seasons and law, and everything shall be delivered into his hands until a season and seasons and until half a season.
1 Daniel 7:26 And the judgment shall sit, and they shall destroy the authority and resolve to defile and destroy until the end.
1 Daniel 7:27 And he gave the kingdom and authority and their magnificence and the dominion of all the kingdoms under heaven to a holy people of the Most High, to reign an everlasting kingdom, and all [the] authorities shall be subjected to him and obey him.
1 Daniel 7:28 Until the conclusion of the word I, Daniel, was greatly held in consternation, and my condition changed for me, and I fixed the matter in my heart.

## Chapter 8

1 Daniel 8:1 In the third year of Baltasar reigning, a vision which I, Daniel, saw after I saw the first.
1 Daniel 8:2 And I saw in the vision of my dream, while I was in the city of Sousa, which is in the country of Elymais, while I was still beside the gate Ailam,
1 Daniel 8:3 looking up, I saw one great ram standing opposite the gate, and it had horns, and one higher than the other, and the higher one was rising.
1 Daniel 8:4 And after these things I saw the ram butting toward the east and toward the north and toward the west and south, and all the beasts did not stand before it, and there was no one delivering from its hands, and it did as it wished and was exalted.
1 Daniel 8:5 And I was considering, and behold, a male goat was coming from the west upon the face of the earth and was not touching the earth, and the goat had one horn between its eyes.
1 Daniel 8:6 And it came against the ram having the horns which I saw standing beside the gate, and ran toward it in wrathful anger.
1 Daniel 8:7 And I saw it approaching the ram, and it became enraged against it and struck and shattered its two horns, and there was no longer strength in the ram to stand opposite the goat; and it dashed it to the earth and shattered it, and there was no one delivering the ram from the goat.
1 Daniel 8:8 And the male goat grew exceedingly strong, and when it grew strong, its great horn was shattered, and four other horns came up behind it toward the four winds of heaven.
1 Daniel 8:9 And from one of them one strong horn grew up and grew strong and struck toward the south and toward the east and toward the north;
1 Daniel 8:10 and it was raised high as far as the stars of heaven, and was dashed to the earth by the stars and trampled by them,
1 Daniel 8:11 until the chief commander delivers the captivity, and through him the mountains from of old were dashed down, and their place and sacrifice were removed, and he placed it down upon the earth, and it became fragrant and came to be, and the holy place shall be desolated;
1 Daniel 8:12 and sins came upon the sacrifice, and righteousness was thrown to the ground, and it acted and became fragrant.
1 Daniel 8:13 And I was hearing another holy one speaking, and the other said to the phelmouni who was speaking, Until when shall the vision stand, and the sacrifice which was taken away and the sin of desolation which was given, and shall the holy places be desolated for trampling?
1 Daniel 8:14 And he said to him, Until evening and morning, two thousand three hundred days, and the holy place shall be cleansed.
1 Daniel 8:15 And it happened while I was watching, I, Daniel, was seeking to understand the vision, and behold, one stood opposite me like the appearance of a man.
1 Daniel 8:16 And I heard a man's voice in the midst of Oulai, and he called and said, Gabriel, make that one understand the vision. And crying out, the man said, The vision pertains to that ordinance.
1 Daniel 8:17 And he came and stood beside my position, and when he came I was alarmed and fell upon my face, and he said to me, Understand, son of man, for this vision is yet for an hour of a season.
1 Daniel 8:18 And while he spoke with me, I fell asleep upon my face to the ground, and touching me, he raised me upon the place,
1 Daniel 8:19 and said to me, Behold, I tell you what shall be at the end of the anger for the sons of your people; for it shall yet remain for hours of a season of completion.
1 Daniel 8:20 The ram which you saw, which has the horns, is a king of Medes and Persians.
1 Daniel 8:21 And the male goat is a king of the Greeks; and the great horn between its eyes is the first king himself.
1 Daniel 8:22 And the four horns which were shattered and came up behind it, four kings of his nation shall arise, not according to his strength.
1 Daniel 8:23 And at the end of their kingdom, when their sins are being fulfilled, a king shameless in face, understanding riddles, shall arise.
1 Daniel 8:24 And his strength shall be established, and not by his strength, and he shall destroy wonderfully and prosper and act and destroy rulers and a people of holy ones.
1 Daniel 8:25 And his thought is against the holy ones, and falsehood shall prosper in his hands, and his heart shall be exalted, and by deceit he shall make many disappear, and he shall stand for destructions of men and make a gathering of a hand and sell himself.
1 Daniel 8:26 The vision of evening and morning was found to be true; and now the vision is closed up, for it is yet for many days.
1 Daniel 8:27 I, Daniel, became weak for many days, and rising, was again conducting royal affairs. And I was fainting over the vision, and there was no one understanding.

## Chapter 9

1 Daniel 9:1 In the first year under Dareios of Xerxes, from the Median race, who reigned over the kingdom of the Chaldeans,
1 Daniel 9:2 in the first year of his reign I, Daniel, considered in the books the number of the years, when an ordinance came to the land concerning Ieremias the prophet, to raise up for the completion of the reproach of Ierusalem, seventy years.
1 Daniel 9:3 And I set my face toward the Lord God to find prayer and mercy with fasts and sackcloth and ashes.
1 Daniel 9:4 And I prayed to the Lord God and confessed and said, Behold, Lord, you are the great and strong and fearful God, keeping the covenant and mercy for those loving you and those keeping your ordinances;
1 Daniel 9:5 we sinned, acted unjustly, acted ungodly and departed and transgressed your commandments and your judgments,
1 Daniel 9:6 and did not hear your servants the prophets, the things they spoke in your name to our kings and our rulers and our fathers and every nation upon the earth.
1 Daniel 9:7 To you, Lord, belongs righteousness, and to us shame of face as on this day, to men of Iouda and those seated in Ierusalem and all the people Israel, the nearest and the farther away, in all the countries into which you scattered them there in the offense with which they offended before you.
1 Daniel 9:8 Master, to us belongs shame of face, and to our kings and rulers and our fathers, because we sinned against you.
1 Daniel 9:9 To the Lord belong righteousness and mercy, because we departed from you,
1 Daniel 9:10 and did not hear the voice of the Lord our God to follow your law which you gave before Moses and us through your servants the prophets.
1 Daniel 9:11 And all Israel abandoned your law and departed so as not to hear your voice, and the curse and the oath written in the law of Moses, servant of God, came upon us, because we sinned against him.
1 Daniel 9:12 And he established for us his ordinances, as much as he spoke against us and against our judges, as much as you judged for us, to bring great evils upon us, such as did not occur under heaven as occurred in Ierusalem.
1 Daniel 9:13 According to what is written in the covenant of Moses, all the evils came upon us, and we did not seek out the face of the Lord our God, to depart from our sins and understand your righteousness, Lord.
1 Daniel 9:14 And the Lord God kept watch over the evils and brought them upon us, because the Lord our God is righteous in everything he may do, and we did not hear his voice.
1 Daniel 9:15 And now, Master, Lord our God, who brought your people out of Egypt with your high arm and made a name for yourself as on this day, we sinned, we have acted in ignorance.
1 Daniel 9:16 Master, according to your righteousness let your wrath and your anger turn away from your city Ierusalem, your holy mountain, because in our sins and in the ignorances of our fathers, Ierusalem and your people, Lord, are a reproach among all those around us.
1 Daniel 9:17 And now hear, Master, the prayer of your servant and attend to my petitions, and let your face look upon your desolate holy mountain for the sake of your servants, Master.
1 Daniel 9:18 Incline your ear, Lord, and hear me; open your eyes and see our desolation and that of your city upon which your name has been called; for it is not on account of our righteous deeds that we petition in our prayers before you, but because of your mercy,
1 Daniel 9:19 Lord, be propitious yourself. Lord, hear and act and do not delay for your own sake, Master, because your name has been called upon your city Sion and upon your people Israel. –
1 Daniel 9:20 And while I was speaking, praying and confessing my sins and the sins of my people Israel and petitioning in prayers before the Lord my God and also for the holy mountain of our God,
1 Daniel 9:21 and while I was still speaking in my prayer, and behold, the man whom I saw in my sleep at the beginning, Gabriel, moving swiftly, approached me at the hour of the evening sacrifice.
1 Daniel 9:22 And he approached and spoke with me and said, Daniel, I have now come out to show you understanding.
1 Daniel 9:23 At the beginning of your petition an ordinance went out from the Lord, and I came to show you, because you are deserving of pity; and understand the ordinance.
1 Daniel 9:24 Seventy weeks were determined for your people and for the city Sion, for sin to be completed and injustices to become scarce and injustices to be wiped away and the vision to be understood and everlasting righteousness to be given and the vision to be completed and a holy of holies to be gladdened.
1 Daniel 9:25 And you shall know and understand and rejoice and find ordinances to be answered, and you shall build Ierusalem as a city for the Lord.
1 Daniel 9:26 And after seven and seventy and sixty-two, an anointing shall be removed and shall not exist, and a kingdom of nations shall destroy the city and the holy place together with the anointed one, and his completion shall come with anger and until a season of completion; from war it shall be warred against.
1 Daniel 9:27 And the covenant shall prevail over many, and again it shall return and be rebuilt in breadth and length; and at the completion of seasons and after seven and seventy seasons and sixty-two years until a season of completion of war, the desolation shall also be removed when the covenant prevails over many weeks; and at the end of the week the sacrifice and the libation shall be taken away, and upon the temple shall be an abomination of desolations until completion, and a completion shall be given upon the desolation.

## Chapter 10

1 Daniel 10:1 In the first year of Cyrus king of the Persians, an ordinance was shown to Daniel, whose name was called Baltasar, and the vision and the ordinance are true, and the strong multitude shall understand the ordinance, and I understood it in a vision.
1 Daniel 10:2 In those days I, Daniel, was mourning for three weeks;
1 Daniel 10:3 I did not eat bread of desires, and meat and wine did not enter my mouth; I did not anoint myself with oil until I completed the three weeks of days.
1 Daniel 10:4 And it happened on the twenty-fourth day of the first month, and I was upon the bank of the great river, which is Tigris,
1 Daniel 10:5 and I lifted my eyes and saw, and behold, one man clothed in fine linen and girded at the waist with fine linen, and light from his midst,
1 Daniel 10:6 and his body like tharsis, and his face like an appearance of lightning, and his eyes like torches of fire, and his arms and feet like flashing bronze, and the sound of his speech like the sound of a tumult.
1 Daniel 10:7 And I, Daniel, saw this great vision, and the men with me did not see this vision, and strong fear fell upon them, and they fled in haste;
1 Daniel 10:8 and I was left alone and saw this great vision, and no strength was left in me, and behold, a spirit turned upon me for destruction, and I did not prevail.
1 Daniel 10:9 And I did not hear the sound of his speech; I had fallen upon my face upon the earth.
1 Daniel 10:10 And behold, he brought a hand to me and raised me upon my knees, upon the footprints of my feet.
1 Daniel 10:11 And he said to me, Daniel, you are a man deserving of pity; understand the ordinances which I speak to you, and stand upon your place, for I have now been sent to you. And when he spoke this ordinance with me, I stood trembling.
1 Daniel 10:12 And he said to me, Do not fear, Daniel; for from the first day when you set your face to understand and humble yourself before the Lord your God, your word was heard, and I entered [at] your word.
1 Daniel 10:13 And the general of the king of the Persians had stood opposed before me for twenty-one days, and behold, Michael, one of the first rulers, came to help me, and I left him there with the general of the king of the Persians.
1 Daniel 10:14 And he said to me, I came to show you what shall meet your people at the end of the days, for there is yet a vision for days.
1 Daniel 10:15 And when he spoke these ordinances with me, I put my face upon the earth and was silent.
1 Daniel 10:16 And behold, something like a likeness of a man's hand touched my lips; and I opened my mouth and spoke and said to the one standing opposite me, Lord, and like a vision it turned to my side upon me, and there was no strength in me;
1 Daniel 10:17 and how shall the servant be able to speak with his lord? And I became weak, and there is no strength in me, and no spirit was left in me.
1 Daniel 10:18 And one like an appearance of a man again touched me and strengthened me,
1 Daniel 10:19 and said to me, You are a man deserving of pity; do not fear, be well; be courageous and strong. And when he spoke with me, I became strong and said, Let my lord speak, because he strengthened me.
1 Daniel 10:20 And he said to me, Do you know why I came to you? And now I will return to fight with the general of the king of the Persians; and I was going out, and behold, a general of the Greeks was entering.
1 Daniel 10:21 And indeed I will show you the first things in a record of truth, and there was no one helping with me concerning these things except Michael the angel;

## Chapter 11

1 Daniel 11:1 And in the first year of King Cyrus he told me to become strong and courageous. –
1 Daniel 11:2 And now I came to show you the truth. Behold, three kings have stood opposed in Persia, and the fourth shall be rich with great wealth beyond all; and when he grows strong in his wealth, he shall rise against every king of the Greeks.
1 Daniel 11:3 And a powerful king shall stand and rule with much dominion and do as he wishes.
1 Daniel 11:4 And when he arises, his kingdom shall be shattered and divided toward the four winds of heaven, not according to his might or according to his dominion with which he ruled, because his kingdom shall be removed, and he shall teach these things to others.
1 Daniel 11:5 And he shall strengthen a kingdom of Egypt; and one of the rulers shall overpower him and rule; his dominion is a great dominion.
1 Daniel 11:6 And he shall bring them to a completion of years, and a king of Egypt shall enter the northern kingdom to make agreements; and he shall certainly not prevail, because his arm shall not establish strength, and his arm shall become numb, and that of those going with him, and he shall remain for hours.
1 Daniel 11:7 And a plant shall arise from his root by itself, and a king of the north shall come against his force in his strength and make a disturbance and prevail.
1 Daniel 11:8 And he shall overthrow their gods with their cast images, and their crowds with the vessels of their desires, silver and gold, they shall carry away in captivity into Egypt; and there shall be a year for a king of the north.
1 Daniel 11:9 And he shall enter the kingdom of Egypt for days; and he shall return to his land,
1 Daniel 11:10 and his son. And he shall be provoked and gather an assembly of a great crowd and enter against it, sweeping along; he shall pass through and return and be greatly incited.
1 Daniel 11:11 And a king of Egypt shall become angry and war with a king of the north, and the assembly shall be delivered into his hands;
1 Daniel 11:12 and he shall take the assembly, and his heart shall be exalted, and he shall disturb many and shall certainly not fear.
1 Daniel 11:13 And a king of the north shall return and gather an assembly of a city greater than the first at the completion of a season of a year, and enter into it against him with a great crowd and with much money.
1 Daniel 11:14 And in those seasons thoughts shall arise against the king of Egypt; and he shall rebuild the fallen things of your nation and arise to establish the prophecy, and they shall stumble.
1 Daniel 11:15 And a king of the north shall come and turn his spears and take the fortified city, and the arms of a king of Egypt shall stand with his rulers, and he shall have no strength to oppose him.
1 Daniel 11:16 And the one coming against him shall do according to his will, and there shall be no one standing opposed before him; and he shall stand in the country, and everything shall be accomplished in his hands.
1 Daniel 11:17 And he shall set his face to come forcibly with all his work, and make agreements with him; and he shall give him a daughter of man to destroy her, and she shall not obey, and it shall not be.
1 Daniel 11:18 And he shall set his face toward the sea and take many, and turn back the anger of their reproach with an oath according to his reproach.
1 Daniel 11:19 He shall turn his face to strengthen his country, and stumble and fall and not be found.
1 Daniel 11:20 And from his root a plant of a kingdom shall arise to stand, a man striking the glory of a king; and in the last days he shall be shattered, and not in anger or in war.
1 Daniel 11:21 And one readily despised shall arise in his place, and glory of a king shall not be given to him; and he shall come suddenly, a king shall prevail in his inheritance.
1 Daniel 11:22 And he shall shatter the shattered arms from before his face;
1 Daniel 11:23 and with the covenant and a people arrayed with him he shall practice falsehood, also against a strong nation with a small nation.
1 Daniel 11:24 Suddenly he shall desolate a city and do what his fathers did not do, nor his fathers' fathers; he shall give them plunder and spoils and money, and devise against the strong city, and his thoughts are in vain.
1 Daniel 11:25 And his strength and his heart shall be roused against the king of Egypt with a great crowd, and the king of Egypt shall be provoked to war with an exceedingly very strong crowd; and he shall not stand, because he shall devise against him with a thought;
1 Daniel 11:26 and his cares shall consume him and turn him back, and he shall pass through and sweep along, and many wounded ones shall fall.
1 Daniel 11:27 And two kings alone shall dine together and eat at one table and speak lies and shall not prosper; for completion is yet for a season.
1 Daniel 11:28 And he shall return to his country with much money, and his heart is against the covenant of the holy place; he shall act and return to his country
1 Daniel 11:29 for a season. And he shall enter Egypt, and it shall not be as the first and the last.
1 Daniel 11:30 And Romans shall come and thrust him out and rebuke him; and he shall return and become angry against the covenant of the holy place; and he shall act and return and devise against them, because they abandoned the covenant of the holy place.
1 Daniel 11:31 And arms from him shall stand and defile the holy place of fear and remove the sacrifice and place an abomination of desolation.
1 Daniel 11:32 And in sins of a covenant they shall defile among a harsh people, and the people knowing these things shall prevail and act.
1 Daniel 11:33 And thoughtful ones of the nation shall bring understanding to many; and they shall stumble by a sword and grow old in it, and be stained in captivity and in plunder of days.
1 Daniel 11:34 And when they are shattered, they shall gather a little strength, and many shall gather to them upon a city, and many as in an inheritance.
1 Daniel 11:35 And some of those understanding shall consider purifying themselves and being chosen and being cleansed until a season of completion; for there is yet a season for hours.
1 Daniel 11:36 And the king shall do according to his will and be provoked to anger and exalted over every god, and shall speak extraordinary things against the God of gods and prosper until the anger is completed; for a completion is coming upon him.
1 Daniel 11:37 And he shall certainly not regard the gods of his fathers and shall certainly not regard a woman's desire, because he shall be exalted in everything, and strong nations shall be subjected to him;
1 Daniel 11:38 in his place he shall also move a god whom his fathers did not know; he shall honor him with gold and silver and precious stone. And with desirable things
1 Daniel 11:39 he shall act concerning cities, and come into a strong fortress; with a foreign god whom he recognizes, he shall multiply glory and rule over him greatly and divide a country as a gift.
1 Daniel 11:40 And at an hour of completion the king of Egypt shall lock horns with him, and a king of the north shall become enraged against him with chariots and many horses and many ships, and enter the country of Egypt,
1 Daniel 11:41 and come into my country,
1 Daniel 11:42 and in the country of Egypt there shall be no one escaping in it.
1 Daniel 11:43 And he shall gain possession of the place of gold and the place of silver and everything desired of Egypt, and Libyans and Ethiopians shall be in his crowd.
1 Daniel 11:44 And a report shall disturb him from the east and north, and he shall go out in strong wrath and with a sword to make many disappear and kill them.
1 Daniel 11:45 And then he shall set his tent between the seas and the mountain of the will of the Holy One; and the hour of his completion shall come, and there shall be no one helping him.

## Chapter 12

1 Daniel 12:1 And at that hour Michael, the great angel standing over the sons of your people, shall pass by; that is a day of affliction such as did not occur from when they came into being until that day; and on that day all the people found inscribed in the book shall be exalted.
1 Daniel 12:2 And many of those sleeping in the breadth of the earth shall arise, some to everlasting life, some to reproach, and some to dispersion and everlasting shame.
1 Daniel 12:3 And those understanding shall shine like luminaries of heaven, and those strengthening my words like the stars of heaven forever and ever.
1 Daniel 12:4 And you, Daniel, cover the ordinances and seal the book until a season of completion, until the many go mad and the earth is filled with injustice. –
1 Daniel 12:5 And I, Daniel, saw, and behold, two others stood, one on this side of the river and one on that side.
1 Daniel 12:6 And I said to the one clothed in fine linen above, When then is the completion of the wonders you have told me, and their purification?
1 Daniel 12:7 And I heard the one clothed in fine linen who was above the water of the river, Until a season of completion; and he raised his right and left hands to heaven and swore by God who lives forever, that for a season and seasons and half a season is the completion of hands of release of a holy people, and all these things shall be completed.
1 Daniel 12:8 And I heard and did not understand at that very time, and said, Lord, what is the resolution of this word, and of what are these parables?
1 Daniel 12:9 And he said to me, Go away, Daniel, because the ordinances are covered and sealed, until
1 Daniel 12:10 many are tested and sanctified, and sinners sin; and all the sinners shall certainly not understand, and those understanding shall pay attention.
1 Daniel 12:11 From when the continual sacrifice is removed and the abomination of desolation is prepared to be placed, a thousand two hundred ninety days.
1 Daniel 12:12 Blessed is the one remaining, and he shall reach a thousand three hundred thirty-five days.
1 Daniel 12:13 And you, go, rest; for there are yet days and hours for the fulfillment of completion, and you shall rest and arise to your glory at the completion of days.

# 2 Daniel
