## Chapter 1

2 Daniel 1:1 In the third year of the reign of Ioakim king of Iouda, Nabouchodonosor king of Babylon came to Ierusalem and was besieging it.
2 Daniel 1:2 And the Lord gave into his hand Ioakim king of Iouda and some of the vessels of the house of God, and he brought them to the land of Sennaar, to the house of his god; and he brought the vessels into the treasury house of his god.
2 Daniel 1:3 And the king told Asphanez his chief eunuch to bring in from the sons of the captivity of Israel and from the seed of the kingdom and from the phorthommin,
2 Daniel 1:4 young men in whom there is no blemish, and beautiful in appearance and understanding in all wisdom and knowing knowledge and comprehending prudence, and in whom there is strength to stand in the king's house, and to teach them letters and the language of the Chaldeans.
2 Daniel 1:5 And the king appointed for them the daily portion each day from the king's table and from the wine of his drinking, and to nourish them for three years, and after these things to stand before the king.
2 Daniel 1:6 And among them, from the sons of Iouda, were Daniel and Ananias and Misael and Azarias.
2 Daniel 1:7 And the chief eunuch put names upon them, upon Daniel, Baltasar, and upon Ananias, Sedrach, and upon Misael, Misach, and upon Azarias, Abdenago.
2 Daniel 1:8 And Daniel set upon his heart that he should certainly not be polluted with the king's table and with the wine of his drinking, and petitioned the chief eunuch that he should certainly not be polluted.
2 Daniel 1:9 And God gave Daniel mercy and compassion before the chief eunuch.
2 Daniel 1:10 And the chief eunuch said to Daniel, I fear my lord the king, who appointed your food and your drink, lest he see your faces gloomy beside the boys of your age, and you condemn my head before the king.
2 Daniel 1:11 And Daniel said to Amelsad, whom the chief eunuch appointed over Daniel, Ananias, Misael, Azarias,
2 Daniel 1:12 Test your servants now for ten days, and let them give us some of the seeds, and we shall eat and drink water;
2 Daniel 1:13 and let our appearances be seen before you, and the appearances of the boys eating the king's table, and as you see, deal with your servants.
2 Daniel 1:14 And he listened to them and tested them for ten days.
2 Daniel 1:15 And after the end of the ten days their appearances were seen to be good and strong in flesh beyond the boys eating the king's table.
2 Daniel 1:16 And Amelsad was taking away their dinner and the wine of their drink, and was giving them seeds.
2 Daniel 1:17 And these boys, the four of them, God gave them understanding and prudence in all literature and wisdom; and Daniel understood in every vision and dreams.
2 Daniel 1:18 And after the end of the days when the king said to bring them in, the chief eunuch also brought them before Nabouchodonosor.
2 Daniel 1:19 And the king spoke with them, and from all of them none was found like Daniel and Ananias and Misael and Azarias; and they stood before the king.
2 Daniel 1:20 And in every matter of wisdom and knowledge which the king sought from them, he found them tenfold beyond all the enchanters and magi in all his kingdom.
2 Daniel 1:21 And Daniel continued until the first year of King Cyrus.

## Chapter 2

2 Daniel 2:1 In the second year of the reign of Nabouchodonosor, Nabouchodonosor dreamed a dream, and his spirit was beside itself, and his sleep departed from him.
2 Daniel 2:2 And the king said to call the enchanters and the magi and the sorcerers and the Chaldeans to tell the king his dreams, and they came and stood before the king.
2 Daniel 2:3 And the king said to them, I dreamed, and my spirit was beside itself to know the dream.
2 Daniel 2:4 And the Chaldeans spoke to the king in Syrian, King, live forever; you tell the dream to your servants, and we shall announce the interpretation.
2 Daniel 2:5 The king answered and said to the Chaldeans, The word has departed from me; if you do not make known to me the dream and its interpretation, you shall be for destruction, and your houses shall be plundered;
2 Daniel 2:6 but if you make known to me the dream and its interpretation, you shall receive gifts and presents and much honor from me; only tell me the dream and its interpretation.
2 Daniel 2:7 They answered a second time and said, Let the king tell the dream to his servants, and we shall announce its interpretation.
2 Daniel 2:8 The king answered and said, Truly I know that you are buying time, because you saw that the matter departed from me;
2 Daniel 2:9 therefore if you do not tell me the dream, I know that you agreed to say a false and corrupt word before me until the season passes; tell me my dream, and I shall know that you shall tell me its interpretation.
2 Daniel 2:10 The Chaldeans answered before the king and say, There is no man upon dry land who shall be able to make known the king's matter, because no great king and ruler asks such a matter of an enchanter, magus and Chaldean;
2 Daniel 2:11 for the word which the king asks is difficult, and there is no other who shall announce it before the king except gods, whose dwelling is not with any flesh.
2 Daniel 2:12 Then the king, in wrath and much anger, said to destroy all the wise men of Babylon;
2 Daniel 2:13 and the decree went out, and the wise men were being killed, and they sought Daniel and his friends to kill them.
2 Daniel 2:14 Then Daniel answered with counsel and opinion to Arioch, the king's chief cook, who went out to kill the wise men of Babylon:
2 Daniel 2:15 Officer of the king, concerning what did the shameless decision go out from the presence of the king? And Arioch made the matter known to Daniel.
2 Daniel 2:16 And Daniel entered and petitioned the king to give him time, and that he might announce its interpretation to the king.
2 Daniel 2:17 And Daniel entered his house and made the matter known to Ananias and Misael and Azarias, his friends;
2 Daniel 2:18 and they were seeking compassion from the God of heaven concerning this mystery, so that Daniel and his friends might not perish with the remaining wise men of Babylon.
2 Daniel 2:19 Then the mystery was revealed to Daniel in a vision of the night; and he blessed the God of heaven,
2 Daniel 2:20 Daniel, and said, May the name of God be blessed from everlasting and to everlasting, because wisdom and understanding are his;
2 Daniel 2:21 and he changes seasons and times, appoints kings and removes them, giving wisdom to the wise and prudence to those knowing understanding;
2 Daniel 2:22 he reveals deep and hidden things, knowing the things in darkness, and the light is with him;
2 Daniel 2:23 to you, the God of my fathers, I give thanks and praise, because you gave me wisdom and power and now made known to me what we petitioned from you, and made known to me the king's vision.
2 Daniel 2:24 And Daniel came to Arioch, whom the king appointed to destroy the wise men of Babylon, and said to him, Do not destroy the wise men of Babylon, but bring me before the king, and I will tell the interpretation to the king.
2 Daniel 2:25 Then Arioch hastily brought Daniel before the king and said to him, I have found a man from the sons of the captivity of Ioudaia who shall announce the interpretation to the king.
2 Daniel 2:26 And the king answered and said to Daniel, whose name was Baltasar, Are you able to tell me the dream which I saw and its interpretation?
2 Daniel 2:27 And Daniel answered before the king and says, The mystery which the king asks is not for wise men, magi, enchanters, Gazarenes to announce to the king,
2 Daniel 2:28 but there is a God in heaven revealing mysteries, and he made known to King Nabouchodonosor what must happen at the end of the days. Your dream and the visions of your head upon your bed are these.
2 Daniel 2:29 You, king, your thoughts upon your bed came up, what must happen after these things, and the one revealing mysteries made known to you what must happen.
2 Daniel 2:30 And to me this mystery was not revealed by wisdom existing in me beyond all the living, but for the sake of making the interpretation known to the king, so that you may know the thoughts of your heart.
2 Daniel 2:31 You, king, were watching, and behold, one image; that image was great and its appearance surpassing, standing before your face, and its sight fearful;
2 Daniel 2:32 the image, whose head was of fine gold, its hands and chest and arms silver, the belly and the thighs bronze,
2 Daniel 2:33 the shins iron, the feet partly iron and partly earthenware.
2 Daniel 2:34 You were watching until a stone was cut from a mountain without hands and struck the image upon the iron and earthenware feet and reduced them to fineness completely.
2 Daniel 2:35 Then the earthenware, the iron, the bronze, the silver, the gold were reduced to fineness at once and became like dust from a summer threshing floor; and the abundance of wind carried them away, and no place was found for them; and the stone which struck the image became a great mountain and filled all the earth.
2 Daniel 2:36 This is the dream; and we shall tell its interpretation before the king.
2 Daniel 2:37 You, king, are a king of kings, to whom the God of heaven gave a strong and mighty and honored kingdom;
2 Daniel 2:38 in every place where the sons of men dwell, both beasts of the field and birds of heaven he gave into your hand, and appointed you lord of all; you are the golden head.
2 Daniel 2:39 And after you another kingdom inferior to you shall arise, and a third kingdom which is the bronze, which shall rule over all the earth.
2 Daniel 2:40 And a fourth kingdom shall be strong like iron; in the manner that iron reduces to fineness and subdues everything, so it shall reduce everything to fineness and subdue it.
2 Daniel 2:41 And because you saw the feet and the toes partly earthenware and partly iron, it shall be a divided kingdom, and some of the iron root shall be in it, in the manner that you saw the iron mixed with the earthenware;
2 Daniel 2:42 and the toes of the feet partly iron and partly earthenware, some part of the kingdom shall be strong, and some of it shall be shattered.
2 Daniel 2:43 Because you saw the iron mixed with the earthenware, they shall be mingled in the seed of men and shall not cling one to another, as iron does not mix with earthenware.
2 Daniel 2:44 And in the days of those kings the God of heaven shall raise up a kingdom which shall not be destroyed forever, and his kingdom shall not be left to another people; it shall reduce to fineness and winnow all the kingdoms, and it shall itself arise forever,
2 Daniel 2:45 in the manner that you saw that a stone was cut from a mountain without hands and reduced to fineness the earthenware, the iron, the bronze, the silver, the gold. The great God made known to the king what must happen after these things, and the dream is true, and its interpretation trustworthy.
2 Daniel 2:46 Then King Nabouchodonosor fell upon his face and worshiped Daniel, and said to pour out a manaa and fragrances for him.
2 Daniel 2:47 And answering, the king said to Daniel, Truly your God himself is God of gods and Lord of kings and a revealer of mysteries, because you were able to reveal this mystery.
2 Daniel 2:48 And the king exalted Daniel and gave him great and many gifts, and appointed him over the whole country of Babylon and ruler of satraps over all the wise men of Babylon.
2 Daniel 2:49 And Daniel requested from the king, and he appointed Sedrach, Misach, Abdenago over the works of the country of Babylon; and Daniel was in the king's court.

## Chapter 3

2 Daniel 3:1 In the eighteenth year Nabouchodonosor the king made a golden image, its height sixty cubits, its breadth six cubits, and set it up in the plain of Deira in the country of Babylon.
2 Daniel 3:2 And he sent to gather the consuls and the generals and the local governors, leaders and tyrants and those in authority and all the rulers of the countries, to come to the dedication of the image which Nabouchodonosor the king had set up;
2 Daniel 3:3 and the local governors, consuls, generals, leaders, great tyrants, those in authority and all the rulers of the countries gathered for the dedication of the image which Nabouchodonosor the king had set up, and stood before the image which Nabouchodonosor had set up.
2 Daniel 3:4 And the herald cried with strength: To you it is said, peoples, tribes, tongues:
2 Daniel 3:5 at whatever hour you hear the sound of the trumpet and pipe and lyre, sambyke and psaltery and symphony and every kind of musical instrument, fall down and worship the golden image which Nabouchodonosor the king has set up;
2 Daniel 3:6 and whoever does not fall down and worship shall at that very hour be thrown into the burning furnace of fire.
2 Daniel 3:7 And it happened, when the peoples heard the sound of the trumpet and pipe and lyre, sambyke and psaltery and symphony and every kind of musical instrument, all the peoples, tribes, tongues fell down and worshipped the golden image which Nabouchodonosor the king had set up.
2 Daniel 3:8 Then Chaldean men approached and accused the Jews
2 Daniel 3:9 before King Nabouchodonosor: King, live unto the ages;
2 Daniel 3:10 you, king, established a decree that every person who hears the sound of the trumpet and pipe and lyre, sambyke and psaltery and symphony and every kind of musical instrument
2 Daniel 3:11 and does not fall down and worship the golden image shall be thrown into the burning furnace of fire;
2 Daniel 3:12 there are Jewish men whom you appointed over the affairs of the country of Babylon, Sedrach, Misach, Abdenago. Those men have not obeyed your decree, king; they do not serve your gods and do not worship the golden image which you set up.
2 Daniel 3:13 Then Nabouchodonosor in wrath and anger said to bring Sedrach, Misach and Abdenago, and they were brought before the king.
2 Daniel 3:14 And Nabouchodonosor answered and said to them: Is it truly so, Sedrach, Misach, Abdenago, that you do not serve my gods and do not worship the golden image which I set up?
2 Daniel 3:15 Now therefore, if you are ready, so that whenever you hear the sound of the trumpet and pipe and lyre, sambyke and psaltery and symphony and every kind of musical instrument, you fall down and worship the image which I made; but if you do not worship, at that very hour you shall be thrown into the burning furnace of fire; and who is the god who will deliver you from my hands?
2 Daniel 3:16 And Sedrach, Misach, Abdenago answered, saying to King Nabouchodonosor: We have no need to answer you concerning this matter;
2 Daniel 3:17 for there is a God whom we serve, able to deliver us from the burning furnace of fire, and from your hands, king, he will rescue us;
2 Daniel 3:18 and if not, let it be known to you, king, that we do not serve your gods and do not worship the golden image which you set up.
2 Daniel 3:19 Then Nabouchodonosor was filled with wrath, and the appearance of his face was changed against Sedrach, Misach and Abdenago, and he said to heat the furnace sevenfold, until it was completely heated;
2 Daniel 3:20 and he told men mighty in strength to bind Sedrach, Misach and Abdenago and throw them into the burning furnace of fire.
2 Daniel 3:21 Then those men were bound with their trousers and tiaras and greaves and their garments, and were thrown into the midst of the burning furnace of fire.
2 Daniel 3:22 Since the king's word prevailed, and the furnace was heated exceedingly.
2 Daniel 3:23 And these three, Sedrach, Misach and Abdenago, fell into the midst of the burning furnace of fire, bound.
2 Daniel 3:24 And they walked in the midst of the flame, hymning God and blessing the Lord.
2 Daniel 3:25 And Azarias stood up and prayed thus, and opened his mouth in the midst of the fire and said:
2 Daniel 3:26 Blessed are you, Lord, the God of our fathers, and praiseworthy, and your name is glorified unto the ages,
2 Daniel 3:27 because you are righteous in all that you have done to us, and all your works are true, and your ways straight, and all your judgments truth,
2 Daniel 3:28 and you made judgments of truth in all that you brought upon us and upon the holy city of our fathers, Ierusalem, because in truth and judgment you brought all these things upon us because of our sins.
2 Daniel 3:29 Because we sinned and acted lawlessly in departing from you, and we sinned in all things and did not listen to your commandments
2 Daniel 3:30 nor keep them nor do as you commanded us, that it might be well with us.
2 Daniel 3:31 And all that you brought upon us, and all that you did to us, you did in true judgment
2 Daniel 3:32 and handed us over into the hands of lawless enemies, most hateful apostates, and to a king unjust and most wicked beyond all the earth.
2 Daniel 3:33 And now it is not possible for us to open our mouth; shame and reproach have come upon your servants and those who revere you.
2 Daniel 3:34 Do not indeed hand us over completely, for your name's sake, and do not scatter your covenant

2 Daniel 3:36 to whom you spoke, saying to them that you would multiply their seed as the stars of heaven and as the sand beside the shore of the sea.

2 Daniel 3:40 thus let our sacrifice be before you today, and to accomplish it behind you, because there shall be no shame for those who trust in you.

2 Daniel 3:42 but do with us according to your forbearance and according to the multitude of your mercy
2 Daniel 3:43 and deliver us according to your wonders and give glory to your name, Lord.
2 Daniel 3:44 And may all who display evils toward your servants be ashamed, and may they be put to shame away from all power and dominion, and may their strength be broken;
2 Daniel 3:45 let them know that you alone are the Lord God and glorious over the whole inhabited world.

## Chapter 4

2 Daniel 4:1 Nabouchodonosor the king to all the peoples, tribes and tongues dwelling in all the earth: May peace be multiplied to you;
2 Daniel 4:2 the signs and wonders which the Most High God did with me, it pleased me to announce to you
2 Daniel 4:3 how great and mighty they are; his kingdom is an eternal kingdom, and his authority unto generation and generation.
2 Daniel 4:4 I, Nabouchodonosor, was prospering in my house and flourishing.
2 Daniel 4:5 I saw a dream, and it frightened me, and I was troubled upon my bed, and the visions of my head disturbed me.
2 Daniel 4:6 And through me a decree was established to bring before me all the wise men of Babylon, that they might make known to me the interpretation of the dream.
2 Daniel 4:7 And the enchanters, magicians, Gazarenes, Chaldeans came in, and I told the dream before them, and they did not make its interpretation known to me,
2 Daniel 4:8 until Daniel came, whose name is Baltasar according to the name of my god, who has a holy spirit of God in himself, and I told the dream before him:
2 Daniel 4:9 Baltasar, ruler of the enchanters, whom I knew, that a holy spirit of God is in you and no mystery is beyond your ability, hear the vision of the dream which I saw, and tell me its interpretation.
2 Daniel 4:10 Upon my bed I was observing, and behold, a tree in the midst of the earth, and its height great.
2 Daniel 4:11 The tree grew great and strong, and its height reached heaven and its bulk the ends of all the earth;
2 Daniel 4:12 its leaves beautiful, and its fruit abundant, and food for all in it; and beneath it the wild beasts encamped, and in its branches the birds of heaven dwelt, and all flesh was fed from it.
2 Daniel 4:13 I was observing in a vision of the night upon my bed, and behold, an ir and holy one descended from heaven
2 Daniel 4:14 and called with strength and said thus: Cut down the tree and pluck off its branches and shake off its leaves and scatter its fruit; let the beasts be moved from beneath it and the birds from its branches;
2 Daniel 4:15 only leave the growth of its roots in the earth, and in a bond of iron and bronze and in the grass outside, and in the dew of heaven he shall lie, and with the beasts his portion shall be in the grass of the earth.
2 Daniel 4:16 His heart shall be changed from that of humans, and a beast's heart shall be given to him, and seven times shall pass over him.
2 Daniel 4:17 By a decision of ir is the word, and the demand a saying of holy ones, that the living may know that the Most High is lord of the kingdom of humans, and to whomever he pleases he will give it, and the despised among humans he will raise over it.
2 Daniel 4:18 This is the dream which I, Nabouchodonosor the king, saw; and you, Baltasar, tell the interpretation, because all the wise men of my kingdom cannot show me its interpretation, but you, Daniel, can, because a holy spirit of God is in you.
2 Daniel 4:19 Then Daniel, whose name is Baltasar, was stunned for about one hour, and his thoughts disturbed him. And the king answered and said: Baltasar, let the dream and the interpretation not alarm you. And Baltasar answered and said: Lord, may the dream be for those who hate you, and its interpretation for your enemies.
2 Daniel 4:20 The tree which you saw, which grew great and strong, whose height reached heaven and its bulk all the earth,
2 Daniel 4:21 and its leaves flourishing and its fruit abundant and food for all in it, beneath which the wild beasts dwelt and in whose branches the birds of heaven encamped,
2 Daniel 4:22 is you, king, because you grew great and strong, and your greatness grew and reached heaven and your dominion the ends of the earth.
2 Daniel 4:23 And because the king saw an ir and holy one descending from heaven, and he said: Pluck off the tree and destroy it, only leave the growth of its roots in the earth, and in a bond of iron and bronze and in the grass outside, and in the dew of heaven he shall lodge, and with wild beasts his portion shall be, until seven times pass over him,
2 Daniel 4:24 this is its interpretation, king, and it is a decision of the Most High which has reached my lord the king,
2 Daniel 4:25 and they shall drive you out from humans, and your dwelling shall be with wild beasts, and they shall feed you grass like an ox, and you shall lodge in the dew of heaven, and seven times shall pass over you, until you know that the Most High rules the kingdom of humans, and to whomever he pleases he will give it.
2 Daniel 4:26 And because they said: Leave the growth of the tree's roots, your kingdom shall remain for you from the time you know the heavenly authority.
2 Daniel 4:27 Therefore, king, let my counsel please you, and redeem your sins with almsgiving and your injustices with compassion for the poor; perhaps God will be patient with your transgressions. –
2 Daniel 4:28 All these things reached Nabouchodonosor the king.
2 Daniel 4:29 After twelve months, walking upon the palace of his kingdom in Babylon,
2 Daniel 4:30 the king answered and said: Is this not Babylon the great, which I built for a house of kingship by the might of my strength, for the honor of my glory?
2 Daniel 4:31 While the word was still in the king's mouth, a voice came from heaven: To you they say, King Nabouchodonosor: The kingdom has passed from you,
2 Daniel 4:32 and they shall drive you out from humans, and your dwelling shall be with wild beasts, and they shall feed you grass like an ox, and seven times shall pass over you, until you know that the Most High rules the kingdom of humans, and to whomever he pleases he will give it.
2 Daniel 4:33 At that very hour the word was accomplished upon Nabouchodonosor, and he was driven out from humans and ate grass like an ox, and his body was drenched by the dew of heaven, until his hair grew like lions' and his nails like birds'.
2 Daniel 4:34 And after the end of the days I, Nabouchodonosor, lifted my eyes to heaven, and my understanding returned to me, and I blessed the Most High and praised and glorified him who lives unto the age, because his authority is eternal authority and his kingdom unto generation and generation,
2 Daniel 4:35 and all who dwell on the earth were reckoned as nothing, and he does according to his will in the power of heaven and in the dwelling of the earth, and there is none who will oppose his hand and say to him: What have you done?
2 Daniel 4:36 At that very time my understanding returned to me, and I came into the honor of my kingdom, and my form returned to me, and my tyrants and my magnates sought me, and I was strengthened over my kingdom, and greater greatness was added to me.
2 Daniel 4:37 Now therefore I, Nabouchodonosor, praise and highly exalt and glorify the King of heaven, because all his works are true and his paths judgment, and all who walk in arrogance he is able to humble.

## Chapter 5

2 Daniel 5:1 Baltasar the king made a great dinner for his thousand magnates, and before the thousand was the wine. And drinking,
2 Daniel 5:2 Baltasar said, at the taste of the wine, to bring the golden and silver vessels which Nabouchodonosor his father had taken out of the temple in Ierusalem, and let the king and his magnates and his concubines and his wives drink in them.
2 Daniel 5:3 And the golden and silver vessels which he had taken out of the temple of God in Ierusalem were brought, and the king and his magnates and his concubines and his wives drank in them;
2 Daniel 5:4 they drank wine and praised the golden and silver and bronze and iron and wooden and stone gods.
2 Daniel 5:5 At that very hour fingers of a human hand came out and wrote opposite the lamp upon the plaster of the wall of the king's house, and the king observed the joints of the hand that was writing.
2 Daniel 5:6 Then the king's form was changed, and his thoughts disturbed him, and the joints of his loins were loosened, and his knees knocked together.
2 Daniel 5:7 And the king cried with strength to bring in magicians, Chaldeans, Gazarenes, and said to the wise men of Babylon: Whoever reads this writing and makes its interpretation known to me shall be clothed in purple, and the golden necklace shall be upon his neck, and he shall rule third in my kingdom.
2 Daniel 5:8 And all the king's wise men came in and could not read the writing nor make its interpretation known to the king.
2 Daniel 5:9 And King Baltasar was greatly troubled, and his form was changed upon him, and his magnates were disturbed.
2 Daniel 5:10 And the queen entered the drinking house and said: King, live unto the ages; let your thoughts not trouble you, and let your form not be changed;
2 Daniel 5:11 there is a man in your kingdom in whom is a spirit of God, and in the days of your father wakefulness and understanding were found in him, and King Nabouchodonosor your father appointed him ruler of enchanters, magicians, Chaldeans, Gazarenes,
2 Daniel 5:12 because an extraordinary spirit is in him, and prudence and understanding, interpreting dreams and announcing concealed things and loosing bonds, Daniel, and the king put upon him the name Baltasar; now therefore let him be called, and he will announce its interpretation to you.
2 Daniel 5:13 Then Daniel was brought before the king, and the king said to Daniel: Are you Daniel, of the sons of the captivity of Ioudaia which the king my father brought?
2 Daniel 5:14 I heard about you that a spirit of God is in you, and wakefulness and understanding and extraordinary wisdom were found in you.
2 Daniel 5:15 And now the wise men, magicians, Gazarenes came before me, that they might read this writing and make its interpretation known to me, and they could not announce it to me.
2 Daniel 5:16 And I heard about you that you can interpret judgments; now therefore if you can read the writing and make its interpretation known to me, you shall be clothed in purple, and the golden necklace shall be upon your neck, and you shall rule third in my kingdom.
2 Daniel 5:17 Then Daniel answered and said before the king: Let your gifts be yours, and give the gift of your house to another; but I shall read the writing to the king and make its interpretation known to you.
2 Daniel 5:18 King, the Most High God gave the kingdom and greatness and honor and glory to Nabouchodonosor your father,
2 Daniel 5:19 and because of the greatness which he gave him, all the peoples, tribes, tongues trembled and feared before him; whom he wished, he killed, and whom he wished, he struck, and whom he wished, he exalted, and whom he wished, he humbled.
2 Daniel 5:20 And when his heart was exalted and his spirit grew strong to act arrogantly, he was brought down from the throne of his kingdom, and his honor was taken away from him,
2 Daniel 5:21 and he was driven out from humans, and his heart was given with the beasts, and his dwelling was with wild asses, and they fed him grass like an ox, and his body was drenched by the dew of heaven, until he knew that the Most High God rules the kingdom of humans, and to whomever he pleases he will give it.
2 Daniel 5:22 And you, his son Baltasar, did not humble your heart before him, although you knew all these things,
2 Daniel 5:23 and you exalted yourself against the Lord God of heaven, and they brought the vessels of his house before you, and you and your magnates and your concubines and your wives drank wine in them, and you praised the golden and silver and bronze and iron and wooden and stone gods, which do not see and do not hear and do not know, and the God in whose hand is your breath and all your ways, him you did not glorify.
2 Daniel 5:24 Therefore from before him a joint of a hand was sent, and it inscribed this writing.
2 Daniel 5:25 And this is the writing inscribed: Mane thekel phares.
2 Daniel 5:26 This is the interpretation of the saying: mane, God measured your kingdom and completed it;
2 Daniel 5:27 thekel, it was weighed in a balance and found deficient;
2 Daniel 5:28 phares, your kingdom has been divided and given to Medes and Persians.
2 Daniel 5:29 And Baltasar spoke, and they clothed Daniel in purple and put the golden necklace around his neck, and he proclaimed concerning him that he should be third ruler in the kingdom.
2 Daniel 5:30 On that very night Baltasar the king of the Chaldeans was killed.

## Chapter 6

2 Daniel 6:1 And Dareios the Mede received the kingdom, being sixty-two years old.
2 Daniel 6:2 And it pleased Dareios, and he appointed over the kingdom a hundred and twenty satraps to be in his whole kingdom,
2 Daniel 6:3 and above them three administrators, of whom Daniel was one, for the satraps to render account to them, so that the king might not be troubled;
2 Daniel 6:4 and Daniel was above them, because an extraordinary spirit was in him, and the king appointed him over his whole kingdom.
2 Daniel 6:5 And the administrators and the satraps sought to find a pretext against Daniel; and they found no pretext or transgression or fault against him, because he was faithful.
2 Daniel 6:6 And the administrators said: We shall not find a pretext against Daniel except in the ordinances of his God.
2 Daniel 6:7 Then the administrators and the satraps stood before the king and said to him: King Dareios, live unto the ages;
2 Daniel 6:8 all the generals and satraps, consuls and local governors over your kingdom have taken counsel to establish by a royal enactment and strengthen a restriction, that whoever asks a request from any god or human for thirty days except from you, king, shall be thrown into the pit of lions;
2 Daniel 6:9 now therefore, king, establish the restriction and issue a writing, so that the decree of Medes and Persians may not be changed.
2 Daniel 6:10 Then King Dareios commanded the decree to be written.
2 Daniel 6:11 And Daniel, when he knew that the decree had been inscribed, entered his house, and his windows were open in his upper rooms opposite Ierusalem, and three times a day he bent upon his knees and prayed and gave thanks before his God, as he had been doing before.
2 Daniel 6:12 Then those men watched and found Daniel making request and supplicating his God.
2 Daniel 6:13 And approaching, they say to the king: King, did you not establish a restriction, that every person who asks a request from any god or human for thirty days except from you, king, shall be thrown into the pit of lions? And the king said: The word is true, and the decree of Medes and Persians shall not pass away.
2 Daniel 6:14 Then they answered and say before the king: Daniel, of the sons of the captivity of Ioudaia, has not submitted to your decree concerning the restriction which you established, and three times a day he asks his requests from his God.
2 Daniel 6:15 Then the king, when he heard the saying, was greatly grieved at it and struggled concerning Daniel to deliver him, and until evening he was struggling to deliver him.
2 Daniel 6:16 Then those men say to the king: Know, king, that it is a decree for Medes and Persians that no restriction and enactment which the king establishes must be altered.
2 Daniel 6:17 Then the king spoke, and they brought Daniel and threw him into the pit of lions; and the king said to Daniel: Your God, whom you serve continually, he will deliver you.
2 Daniel 6:18 And they brought a stone and placed it upon the mouth of the pit, and the king sealed it with his ring and with the ring of his magnates, so that nothing might be changed concerning Daniel.
2 Daniel 6:19 And the king went away to his house and lay down without dinner, and they did not bring foods to him, and sleep departed from him. And God shut the mouths of the lions, and they did not trouble Daniel.
2 Daniel 6:20 Then the king rose early in the light and came in haste to the pit of lions;
2 Daniel 6:21 and as he drew near the pit he cried with a strong voice: Daniel, servant of the living God, has your God, whom you serve continually, been able to deliver you from the mouth of the lions?
2 Daniel 6:22 And Daniel said to the king: King, live unto the ages;
2 Daniel 6:23 my God sent his angel and blocked the mouths of the lions, and they did not injure me, because uprightness was found in me before him; and also before you, king, I did no transgression.
2 Daniel 6:24 Then the king was greatly gladdened at it and said to bring Daniel up from the pit; and Daniel was brought up from the pit, and no destruction was found in him, because he believed in his God.
2 Daniel 6:25 And the king spoke, and they brought the men who had accused Daniel, and they were thrown into the pit of lions, they and their sons and their wives; and they had not reached the floor of the pit before the lions ruled over them and crushed all their bones.
2 Daniel 6:26 Then Dareios the king wrote to all the peoples, tribes, tongues dwelling in all the earth: May peace be multiplied to you;
2 Daniel 6:27 from before me a decree was established, that in every domain of my kingdom they should tremble and fear before the God of Daniel, because he is the living God and remains unto the ages, and his kingdom shall not be destroyed, and his dominion is unto the end;
2 Daniel 6:28 he takes hold and rescues and does signs and wonders in heaven and upon the earth, he who delivered Daniel from the hand of the lions.
2 Daniel 6:29 And Daniel prospered in the kingdom of Dareios and in the kingdom of Cyrus the Persian.

## Chapter 7

2 Daniel 7:1 In the first year of Baltasar king of the Chaldeans, Daniel saw a dream, and the visions of his head upon his bed, and he wrote the dream:
2 Daniel 7:2 I, Daniel, was observing in my vision of the night, and behold, the four winds of heaven struck against the great sea.
2 Daniel 7:3 And four great beasts came up from the sea, differing from one another.
2 Daniel 7:4 The first was like a lioness, and its wings like an eagle's; I was observing until its wings were plucked out, and it was lifted from the earth and stood upon human feet, and a human heart was given to it.
2 Daniel 7:5 And behold, a second beast like a bear, and it stood upon one side, and three ribs were in its mouth between its teeth, and thus they said to it: Rise, eat much flesh.
2 Daniel 7:6 After this I was observing, and behold, another beast like a leopard, and it had four bird's wings above it, and the beast had four heads, and authority was given to it.
2 Daniel 7:7 After this I was observing, and behold, a fourth beast, fearful and terrifying and exceedingly strong, and its teeth great and iron, eating and crushing, and it trampled the remainder with its feet, and it differed exceedingly from all the beasts before it, and it had ten horns.
2 Daniel 7:8 I considered its horns, and behold, another small horn came up in their midst, and three of the horns before it were uprooted before it, and behold, eyes like human eyes were in this horn, and a mouth speaking great things.
2 Daniel 7:9 I was observing until thrones were placed, and an ancient of days sat, and his garment was white like snow, and the hair of his head like clean wool; his throne a flame of fire, its wheels burning fire;
2 Daniel 7:10 a river of fire flowed before him, a thousand thousands ministered to him, and ten thousand myriads stood before him; a court sat, and books were opened.
2 Daniel 7:11 I was observing then because of the sound of the great words which that horn spoke, until the beast was killed and perished, and its body was given to burning by fire.
2 Daniel 7:12 And the rule of the remaining beasts was removed, and length of life was given to them until a time and a time.
2 Daniel 7:13 I was observing in a vision of the night, and behold, with the clouds of heaven one like a son of man was coming, and he reached the ancient of days and was brought before him.
2 Daniel 7:14 And to him were given rule and honor and the kingdom, and all the peoples, tribes, tongues shall serve him; his authority is eternal authority, which shall not pass away, and his kingdom shall not be destroyed. –
2 Daniel 7:15 My spirit shuddered within my condition, I, Daniel, and the visions of my head troubled me.
2 Daniel 7:16 And I approached one of those standing and sought from him the exact truth concerning all these things, and he told me the exact truth and made known to me the interpretation of the words:
2 Daniel 7:17 These four great beasts, four kingdoms shall arise upon the earth, which shall be taken away;
2 Daniel 7:18 and holy ones of the Most High shall receive the kingdom and hold it unto the age of the ages.
2 Daniel 7:19 And I sought precisely concerning the fourth beast, because it differed from every beast, exceedingly fearful, its teeth iron and its claws bronze, eating and crushing, and it trampled the remainder with its feet,
2 Daniel 7:20 and concerning its ten horns upon its head and the other which came up and shook out three of the earlier ones, that horn which had eyes and a mouth speaking great things, and its appearance greater than the remaining ones.
2 Daniel 7:21 I was observing, and that horn made war with the holy ones and prevailed against them,
2 Daniel 7:22 until the ancient of days came and gave judgment to holy ones of the Most High, and the time arrived and the holy ones possessed the kingdom.
2 Daniel 7:23 And he said: The fourth beast shall be a fourth kingdom in the earth, which shall surpass all the kingdoms and devour all the earth and trample it and cut it down.
2 Daniel 7:24 And its ten horns, ten kings shall arise, and after them another shall arise, who shall surpass in evils all those before him, and shall humble three kings;
2 Daniel 7:25 and he shall speak words against the Most High and wear out the holy ones of the Most High and intend to change times and law, and it shall be given into his hand until a time and times and half a time.
2 Daniel 7:26 And the court shall sit, and they shall remove the rule to annihilate and destroy unto the end.
2 Daniel 7:27 And the kingdom and authority and greatness of the kings beneath all heaven were given to holy ones of the Most High, and his kingdom is an eternal kingdom, and all the rulers shall serve and obey him.
2 Daniel 7:28 Thus far is the end of the word. I, Daniel, my thoughts greatly disturbed me, and my form was changed upon me, and I kept the saying in my heart.

## Chapter 8

2 Daniel 8:1 In the third year of the kingdom of Baltasar the king a vision appeared to me, I, Daniel, after the one which appeared to me at the beginning.
2 Daniel 8:2 And I was in Sousa the citadel, which is in the country of Ailam, and I saw in a vision, and I was upon the Oubal,
2 Daniel 8:3 and I lifted my eyes and saw, and behold, one ram standing before the Oubal, and it had horns, and the horns were high, and the one higher than the other, and the high one came up last.
2 Daniel 8:4 I saw the ram butting toward the sea and north and south, and none of the beasts shall stand before it, and there was none delivering from its hand, and it did according to its will and grew great.
2 Daniel 8:5 And I was considering, and behold, a male goat came from the southwest over the face of all the earth and was not touching the earth, and the goat had a conspicuous horn between its eyes.
2 Daniel 8:6 And it came to the ram which had the horns, which I had seen standing before the Oubal, and ran toward it in the impulse of its strength.
2 Daniel 8:7 And I saw it reach the ram, and it became fierce against it and struck the ram and broke both its horns, and the ram had no strength to stand before it; and it threw it upon the earth and trampled it, and there was none delivering the ram from its hand.
2 Daniel 8:8 And the male goat grew exceedingly great, and when it became strong its great horn was broken, and four horns came up beneath it toward the four winds of heaven.
2 Daniel 8:9 And from one of them came out one strong horn, and it grew exceedingly great toward the south and toward the east and toward the host;
2 Daniel 8:10 it grew great unto the host of heaven, and fell upon the earth from the host of heaven and from the stars, and trampled them,
2 Daniel 8:11 and until the chief commander rescues the captivity, and because of it sacrifice was dashed down, and it happened and prospered for it, and the sanctuary shall be desolated;
2 Daniel 8:12 and sin was given against the sacrifice, and righteousness was thrown to the ground, and it acted and prospered.
2 Daniel 8:13 And I heard one holy one speaking, and one holy one said to the phelmouni who was speaking: Until when shall the vision stand, the sacrifice taken away and the sin of desolation given, and the sanctuary and the host be trampled?
2 Daniel 8:14 And he said to him: Until evening and morning, two thousand and three hundred days, and the sanctuary shall be cleansed.
2 Daniel 8:15 And it happened, when I, Daniel, saw the vision and sought understanding, and behold, there stood before me something like the appearance of a man.
2 Daniel 8:16 And I heard a man's voice between the Oubal, and it called and said: Gabriel, cause that one to understand the vision.
2 Daniel 8:17 And he came and stood beside where I stood, and when he came I was terrified and fall upon my face, and he said to me: Understand, son of man, for the vision is still for the end of a time.
2 Daniel 8:18 And when he spoke with me I fall upon my face upon the earth, and he touched me and stood me upon my feet
2 Daniel 8:19 and said: Behold, I make known to you the things which shall be at the last of the wrath; for the vision is still for the end of a time.
2 Daniel 8:20 The ram which you saw, which has the horns, is king of Medes and Persians.
2 Daniel 8:21 And the male goat is king of Greeks; and the great horn which was between its eyes, it is the first king.
2 Daniel 8:22 And of the broken one, beneath which four horns stood, four kings shall arise from his nation, and not in his strength.
2 Daniel 8:23 And at the last of their kingdom, when their sins are being fulfilled, a king shameless in face and understanding riddles shall arise.
2 Daniel 8:24 And his strength shall be mighty, and not in his own strength, and he shall destroy wondrously and prosper and act and destroy mighty ones and a holy people.
2 Daniel 8:25 And the yoke of his collar shall prosper; deceit is in his hand, and he shall grow great in his heart and destroy many by deceit and stand for the destruction of many and break them like eggs with a hand.
2 Daniel 8:26 And the vision of the evening and the morning which was spoken is true; and you, seal the vision, because it is for many days.
2 Daniel 8:27 And I, Daniel, lay down and was sick for days, and rose and did the king's affairs; and I wondered at the vision, and there was none understanding.

## Chapter 9

2 Daniel 9:1 In the first year of Dareios the son of Asoueros, of the seed of the Medes, who reigned over the kingdom of the Chaldeans,
2 Daniel 9:2 in year one of his kingdom I, Daniel, understood in the books the number of the years concerning which the word of the Lord came to Ieremias the prophet for the completion of the desolation of Ierusalem, seventy years.
2 Daniel 9:3 And I gave my face toward the Lord God to seek prayer and supplications with fastings and sackcloth and ashes.
2 Daniel 9:4 And I prayed to the Lord my God and confessed and said: Lord, the great and wonderful God, who keeps your covenant and mercy for those who love you and those who keep your commandments,
2 Daniel 9:5 we sinned, acted unjustly, acted lawlessly and departed and turned aside from your commandments and from your judgments
2 Daniel 9:6 and did not listen to your servants the prophets, who spoke in your name to our kings and our rulers and our fathers and to all the people of the land.
2 Daniel 9:7 To you, Lord, belongs righteousness, and to us shame of face as this day, to the man of Iouda and those dwelling in Ierusalem and all Israel, those near and those far in all the earth, where you scattered them there in their unfaithfulness with which they were unfaithful to you.
2 Daniel 9:8 Lord, to us belongs shame of face, and to our kings and our rulers and our fathers, we who sinned against you.
2 Daniel 9:9 To the Lord our God belong compassions and propitiations, because we departed
2 Daniel 9:10 and did not listen to the voice of the Lord our God, to walk in his laws which he gave before us by the hands of his servants the prophets.
2 Daniel 9:11 And all Israel transgressed your law and turned aside so as not to hear your voice, and the curse and the oath written in the law of Moyses the servant of God came upon us, because we sinned against him.
2 Daniel 9:12 And he established his words which he spoke against us and against our judges who judged us, to bring great evils upon us, such as have not happened beneath all heaven according to what happened in Ierusalem.
2 Daniel 9:13 As it is written in the law of Moyses, all these evils came upon us, and we did not supplicate the face of the Lord our God, to turn from our injustices and to understand in all your truth.
2 Daniel 9:14 And the Lord watched and brought them upon us, because the Lord our God is righteous in all his doing which he did, and we did not listen to his voice.
2 Daniel 9:15 And now, Lord our God, who brought your people out of the land of Egypt with a mighty hand and made yourself a name as this day, we sinned, we acted lawlessly.
2 Daniel 9:16 Lord, in all your mercy let your wrath and your anger indeed turn away from your city Ierusalem, your holy mountain, because we sinned, and through our injustices and those of our fathers Ierusalem and your people became a reproach among all those around us.
2 Daniel 9:17 And now hear, Lord our God, the prayer of your servant and his supplications, and make your face shine upon your desolate sanctuary for your sake, Lord.
2 Daniel 9:18 Incline your ear, my God, and hear; open your eyes and see our annihilation and that of your city upon which your name has been called; because it is not on our righteous acts that we cast our plea for compassion before you, but on your many compassions.
2 Daniel 9:19 Lord, hear; Lord, be propitious; Lord, attend and act; do not delay, for your sake, my God, because your name has been called upon your city and upon your people. –
2 Daniel 9:20 And while I was still speaking and praying and confessing my sins and the sins of my people Israel and casting my plea for mercy before the Lord my God concerning the holy mountain of my God,
2 Daniel 9:21 and while I was still speaking in prayer, and behold, the man Gabriel, whom I saw in the vision at the beginning, flying, touched me about the hour of the evening sacrifice.
2 Daniel 9:22 And he caused me to understand and spoke with me and said: Daniel, now I came out to instruct you in understanding.
2 Daniel 9:23 At the beginning of your supplication a word came out, and I came to announce it to you, because you are a man of desires; and consider the saying and understand the apparition.
2 Daniel 9:24 Seventy weeks were cut short upon your people and upon your holy city, for sin to be completed and to seal sins and wipe away lawless acts and to make atonement for injustices and to bring eternal righteousness and to seal vision and prophet and to anoint a holy of holies.
2 Daniel 9:25 And you shall know and understand: from the going out of a word to answer and to build Ierusalem until an anointed leader, seven weeks and sixty-two weeks; and it shall return, and street and wall shall be built, and the times shall be emptied out.
2 Daniel 9:26 And after the sixty-two weeks an anointing shall be utterly destroyed, and there is no judgment in it; and he shall destroy the city and the sanctuary together with the leader who comes, and they shall be cut off in a flood, and until the end of a shortened war he shall appoint desolations.
2 Daniel 9:27 And he shall strengthen a covenant for many, one week; and in the half of the week my sacrifice and libation shall be taken away, and upon the temple an abomination of desolations, and until the completion of a time a completion shall be given upon the desolation.

## Chapter 10

2 Daniel 10:1 In the third year of Cyrus king of the Persians a word was revealed to Daniel, whose name was called Baltasar, and the word was true, and great power and understanding were given to him in the apparition.
2 Daniel 10:2 In those days I, Daniel, was mourning three weeks of days;
2 Daniel 10:3 bread of desires I did not eat, and meat and wine did not enter my mouth, and I did not anoint myself with ointment until the completion of three weeks of days.
2 Daniel 10:4 On the twenty-fourth day of the first month, and I was beside the great river, it is Eddekel,
2 Daniel 10:5 and I lifted my eyes and saw, and behold, one man clothed in baddin, and his loins girded with gold of Ophaz,
2 Daniel 10:6 and his body like tharsis, and his face like the appearance of lightning, and his eyes like torches of fire, and his arms and legs like the appearance of gleaming bronze, and the sound of his words like the sound of a crowd.
2 Daniel 10:7 And I, Daniel, alone saw the apparition, and the men with me did not see the apparition, but a great astonishment fell upon them, and they fled in fear;
2 Daniel 10:8 and I was left alone and saw this great apparition, and no strength was left in me, and my glory was changed into destruction, and I retained no strength.

## Chapter 1

1 Bel and the Dragon 1:1 From the prophecy of Ambakoum son of Iesous, of the tribe of Levi.

1 Bel and the Dragon 1:3 And there was an idol, Bel, which the Babylonians revered; and twelve artabas of fine flour and four sheep and six measures of oil were expended for it each day.
1 Bel and the Dragon 1:4 And the king revered it, and the king went each day and worshipped it; but Daniel prayed to the Lord.
1 Bel and the Dragon 1:5 And the king said to Daniel: Why do you not worship Bel? And Daniel said to the king: I revere no one except the Lord God, who created heaven and earth and has dominion over all flesh.
1 Bel and the Dragon 1:6 And the king said to him: Is this, then, not a god? Do you not see how much is spent on it each day?
1 Bel and the Dragon 1:7 And Daniel said to him: By no means; let no one deceive you; for this is clay within and bronze without; and I swear to you by the Lord, the God of gods, that this has never eaten anything.
1 Bel and the Dragon 1:8 And the king, enraged, called those presiding over the temple and said to them: Show the one eating what is prepared for Bel; but if not, you shall die, or Daniel who asserts that these things are not eaten by it. And they said: Bel himself is the one devouring them.
1 Bel and the Dragon 1:9 And Daniel said to the king: Let it be thus; if I do not show that Bel is not the one devouring these things, I shall die, and all those with me. And there were seventy priests for Bel, apart from women and children.
1 Bel and the Dragon 1:10 And they brought the king into the idol's shrine.
1 Bel and the Dragon 1:11 And the foods were set before the king and Daniel, and mixed wine was brought in and set before Bel. And Daniel said: You yourself see that these things are laid here, king; therefore you seal the locks of the temple when it is closed.
1 Bel and the Dragon 1:13 And the word pleased the king.
1 Bel and the Dragon 1:14 And Daniel commanded his people, after putting everyone out of the temple, to sprinkle the whole temple with ashes, with none outside him knowing. And then he commanded the temple to be sealed with the king's ring and the rings of certain distinguished priests; and it happened thus.
1 Bel and the Dragon 1:15-17 And it happened on the next day that they arrived at the place; and the priests of Bel had entered through concealed doors and devoured everything laid beside Bel and drunk up the wine. And Daniel said: Look upon your seals, whether they remain, men who are priests; and you also, king, consider whether anything inconsistent has happened for you. And they found the seal as it had been, and removed the seal.
1 Bel and the Dragon 1:18 And opening the doors, they saw everything set out consumed and the tables empty; and the king rejoiced and said to Daniel: Bel is great, and there is no deceit with him.

1 Bel and the Dragon 1:20 And the king said: Of men and women and children.
1 Bel and the Dragon 1:21 And he went to the house in which the priests were staying and found the foods of Bel and the wine; and Daniel showed the king the concealed doors through which the priests entered and consumed what was set before Bel.
1 Bel and the Dragon 1:22 And the king brought them out of the shrine of Bel and handed them over to Daniel; and he gave Daniel the expenditure for it, and overthrew Bel.
1 Bel and the Dragon 1:23 And there was a dragon in the same place, and the Babylonians revered it.
1 Bel and the Dragon 1:24 And the king said to Daniel: Surely you will not also say that this is bronze? Behold, it lives and eats and drinks; worship it.
1 Bel and the Dragon 1:25 And Daniel said: King, give me the authority, and I shall kill the dragon without iron and staff.
1 Bel and the Dragon 1:26 And the king granted it to him and said to him: It is given to you.
1 Bel and the Dragon 1:27 And Daniel took thirty minas of pitch and fat and hairs, boiled them together and made a cake and threw it into the dragon's mouth, and after eating it burst apart. And he showed it to the king, saying: Do you not revere these things, king?
1 Bel and the Dragon 1:28 And all those from the country gathered against Daniel and said: The king has become a Jew; he overthrew Bel and killed the dragon.
1 Bel and the Dragon 1:30 And the king, seeing that the crowd of the country had gathered against him, called his companions and said: I give Daniel for destruction.

And the crowds threw Daniel into that pit, so that he might be devoured and not even obtain burial. And Daniel was in the pit six days.
1 Bel and the Dragon 1:33 And it happened on the sixth day, and Ambakoum had breads crumbled in a bowl in a boiled dish and a jar of mixed wine, and was going into the plain to the reapers.
1 Bel and the Dragon 1:34 And an angel of the Lord spoke to Ambakoum, saying: Thus says the Lord God to you: The meal which you have, take away to Daniel in the pit of lions in Babylon.
1 Bel and the Dragon 1:35 And Ambakoum said: Lord God, I have not seen Babylon, and I do not know where the pit is.

1 Bel and the Dragon 1:39 And Daniel ate; and the angel of the Lord set Ambakoum where he had taken him from, on the same day. And the Lord God remembered Daniel.
1 Bel and the Dragon 1:40 And after these things the king came out mourning Daniel and, bending into the pit, sees him sitting.
1 Bel and the Dragon 1:41 And the king cried out and said: Great is the Lord God, and there is no other except him.

## Chapter 1

Matthew 1:1 Book of the origin of Jesus Christ, son of Dabid, son of Abraam.

Matthew 1:7 and Solomon begot Roboam, and Roboam begot Abia, and Abia begot Asa,
Matthew 1:8 and Asa begot Iosaphat, and Iosaphat begot Ioram, and Ioram begot Ozias,
Matthew 1:9 and Ozias begot Ioatham, and Ioatham begot Achaz, and Achaz begot Ezekias,
Matthew 1:10 and Ezekias begot Manasses, and Manasses begot Amon, and Amon begot Iosias,
Matthew 1:11 and Iosias begot Iechonias and his brothers at the deportation to Babylon.
Matthew 1:12 And after the deportation to Babylon Iechonias begot Salathiel, and Salathiel begot Zorobabel,
Matthew 1:13 and Zorobabel begot Abioud, and Abioud begot Eliakeim, and Eliakeim begot Azor,
Matthew 1:14 and Azor begot Sadok, and Sadok begot Acheim, and Acheim begot Elioud,
Matthew 1:15 and Elioud begot Eleazar, and Eleazar begot Matthan, and Matthan begot Iakob,
Matthew 1:16 and Iakob begot Joseph, the husband of Maria, from whom Jesus was born, who is called Christ.
Matthew 1:17 Therefore all the generations from Abraam until Dabid are fourteen generations, and from Dabid until the deportation to Babylon fourteen generations, and from the deportation to Babylon until the Christ fourteen generations.
Matthew 1:18 And the birth of Jesus Christ was thus: for when his mother Maria was betrothed to Joseph, before they came together, she was found having a child in the womb from the Holy Spirit.
Matthew 1:19 And Joseph her husband, being righteous and not wishing to expose her publicly, resolved to release her secretly.
Matthew 1:20 And when he considered these things, behold, an angel of the Lord appeared to him in a dream, saying: Joseph, son of Dabid, do not fear to take Mariam your wife, for what was begotten in her is from the Holy Spirit.
Matthew 1:21 And she shall bear a son, and you shall call his name Jesus, for he shall save his people from their sins.
Matthew 1:22 And this whole thing has happened so that what was spoken by the Lord through the prophet might be fulfilled, saying:
Matthew 1:23 Behold, the virgin shall have a child in the womb and bear a son, and they shall call his name Emmanuel, which translated is: God with us.
Matthew 1:24 And Joseph, awakened from sleep, did as the angel of the Lord commanded him and took his wife,
Matthew 1:25 and did not know her until she bore her firstborn son, and he called his name Jesus.

## Chapter 2

Matthew 2:2 saying: Where is the one born king of the Jews? For we saw his star in the east and came to worship him.
Matthew 2:3 And Herod the king, hearing, was troubled, and all Hierosolyma with him,
Matthew 2:4 and gathering all the chief priests and scribes of the people, he inquired from them where the Christ is born.
Matthew 2:5 And they said to him: In Bethlehem of Ioudaia, for thus it is written through the prophet:
Matthew 2:6 And you, Bethlehem, land of Iouda, are by no means least among the rulers of Iouda; for from you shall come out a leader who shall shepherd my people Israel.
Matthew 2:7 Then Herod, secretly calling the magi, ascertained precisely from them the time of the star appearing,
Matthew 2:8 and sending them to Bethlehem said: Go and inquire precisely concerning the child, and when you find him, announce it to me, so that I also may come and worship him.
Matthew 2:9 And hearing the king, they went, and behold, the star which they saw in the east went before them until it came and stood above where the child was.
Matthew 2:10 And seeing the star, they rejoiced with exceedingly great joy,
Matthew 2:11 and coming into the house they found the child with Maria his mother, and falling down they worshipped him, and opening their treasures they offered him gifts, gold and frankincense and myrrh.
Matthew 2:12 And being instructed in a dream not to return to Herod, they withdrew to their country by another way.
Matthew 2:13 And when they withdrew, behold, an angel of the Lord appears in a dream to Joseph, saying: Rise, take the child and his mother and flee into Egypt, and be there until I tell you; for Herod is about to seek the child to destroy him.
Matthew 2:14 And he rose and took the child and his mother by night and withdrew into Egypt,
Matthew 2:15 and was there until the death of Herod, so that what was spoken by the Lord through the prophet might be fulfilled, saying: Out of Egypt I called my son.

Matthew 2:17 Then what was spoken by Ieremias the prophet was fulfilled, saying:
Matthew 2:18 A voice was heard in Rama, lamentation and weeping and much wailing, Rachel weeping for her children, and she did not wish to be comforted, because they are not.
Matthew 2:19 And when Herod died, behold, an angel of the Lord appears in a dream to Joseph in Egypt,
Matthew 2:20 saying: Rise, take the child and his mother and go into the land of Israel; for those seeking the soul of the child have died.
Matthew 2:21 And he rose and took the child and his mother and came into the land of Israel.
Matthew 2:22 And hearing that Archelaos reigns over Ioudaia instead of Herod his father, he feared to go there; and being instructed in a dream, he withdrew into the parts of Galilee,
Matthew 2:23 and coming, he dwelt in a city called Nazaret, so that what was spoken through the prophets might be fulfilled: He shall be called a Nazorean.

## Chapter 3

Matthew 3:1 And in those days John the Baptist arrives, proclaiming in the wilderness of Ioudaia
Matthew 3:2 and saying: Repent, for the kingdom of the heavens has drawn near.
Matthew 3:3 For this is the one spoken of by Esaias the prophet, saying: A voice of one crying in the wilderness: Prepare the way of the Lord, make his paths straight.
Matthew 3:4 And John himself had his garment of camel's hairs and a leather belt around his loins, and his food was locusts and wild honey.
Matthew 3:5 Then Hierosolyma and all Ioudaia and all the surrounding country of the Jordan went out to him,
Matthew 3:6 and were baptized in the Jordan by him, confessing their sins.
Matthew 3:7 And seeing many of the Pharisees and Sadducees coming to his baptism, he said to them: Offspring of vipers, who showed you to flee from the coming wrath?
Matthew 3:8 Therefore produce fruits worthy of repentance,
Matthew 3:9 and do not think to say within yourselves: We have Abraam as father; for I say to you that God can raise up children for Abraam from these stones.
Matthew 3:10 And already the axe also lies at the root of the trees; therefore every tree not producing good fruit is cut down and thrown into fire.
Matthew 3:11 I indeed baptize you in water for repentance, but the one coming after me is stronger than I, whose sandals I am not sufficient to carry; he shall baptize you in the Holy Spirit and fire,
Matthew 3:12 whose winnowing shovel is in his hand, and he shall thoroughly cleanse his threshing floor and gather his grain into the storehouse, but burn up the chaff with unquenchable fire.
Matthew 3:13 Then Jesus arrives from Galilee at the Jordan to John, to be baptized by him.
Matthew 3:14 But John tried to prevent him, saying: I have need to be baptized by you, and you come to me?
Matthew 3:15 And Jesus answered and said to him: Permit it now, for thus it is fitting for us to fulfill all righteousness. Then he permits him.
Matthew 3:16 And Jesus, baptized, came up immediately from the water, and behold, the heavens were opened to him, and he saw the Spirit of God descending like a dove and coming upon him,
Matthew 3:17 and behold, a voice from the heavens, saying: This is my beloved son, in whom I was well pleased.

## Chapter 4

Matthew 4:1 Then Jesus was led up into the wilderness by the Spirit to be tempted by the devil.
Matthew 4:2 And fasting forty days and forty nights, afterward he hungered.
Matthew 4:3 And the tempter approached him and said: If you are a son of God, say that these stones become breads.
Matthew 4:4 And he answered and said: It is written: A human shall not live on bread alone, but on every saying coming out through the mouth of God.
Matthew 4:5 Then the devil takes him to the holy city and sets him upon the pinnacle of the temple,
Matthew 4:6 and says to him: If you are a son of God, throw yourself down; for it is written that he shall command his angels concerning you, and upon their hands they shall lift you, lest you strike your foot against a stone.
Matthew 4:7 Jesus said to him: Again it is written: You shall not put the Lord your God to the test.
Matthew 4:8 Again the devil takes him to an exceedingly high mountain and shows him all the kingdoms of the world and their glory,
Matthew 4:9 and says to him: All these things I shall give you, if you fall down and worship me.
Matthew 4:10 Then Jesus says to him: Go away, Satan; for it is written: You shall worship the Lord your God and serve him alone.
Matthew 4:11 Then the devil leaves him, and behold, angels approached and ministered to him.
Matthew 4:12 And Jesus, hearing that John was handed over, withdrew into Galilee,
Matthew 4:13 and leaving Nazaret, he came and dwelt in Capernaoum beside the sea, in the boundaries of Zaboulon and Nephthaleim,
Matthew 4:14 so that what was spoken through Esaias the prophet might be fulfilled, saying:
Matthew 4:15 Land of Zaboulon and land of Nephthaleim, way of the sea, beyond the Jordan, Galilee of the nations,
Matthew 4:16 the people sitting in darkness saw a great light, and for those sitting in a country and shadow of death, light arose for them.
Matthew 4:17 From then Jesus began to proclaim and say: Repent, for the kingdom of the heavens has drawn near.
Matthew 4:18 And Jesus, walking beside the sea of Galilee, saw two brothers, Simon who is called Peter and Andrew his brother, throwing a casting net into the sea, for they were fishermen,
Matthew 4:19 and says to them: Come after me, and I shall make you fishermen of humans.
Matthew 4:20 And immediately leaving the nets, they followed him.
Matthew 4:21 And going on from there, he saw two other brothers, Iakobos the son of Zebedaios and John his brother, in the boat with Zebedaios their father, mending their nets, and called them.
Matthew 4:22 And immediately leaving the boat and their father, they followed him.
Matthew 4:23 And Jesus went around all Galilee, teaching in their synagogues and proclaiming the good news of the kingdom and healing every disease and every infirmity among the people.
Matthew 4:24 And the report of him went into all Syria, and they brought to him all those who were ill, afflicted with various diseases and torments, and those possessed by demons and those moonstruck and paralytics, and he healed them.
Matthew 4:25 And many crowds followed him from Galilee and Decapolis and Hierosolyma and Ioudaia and beyond the Jordan.

## Chapter 5

Matthew 5:1 And seeing the crowds, he went up onto the mountain, and when he sat down his disciples approached him,
Matthew 5:2 and opening his mouth he taught them, saying:
Matthew 5:3 Blessed are the poor in spirit, because theirs is the kingdom of the heavens.
Matthew 5:4 Blessed are those mourning, because they shall be comforted.
Matthew 5:5 Blessed are the meek, because they shall inherit the earth.
Matthew 5:6 Blessed are those hungering and thirsting for righteousness, because they shall be filled.
Matthew 5:7 Blessed are the merciful, because they shall receive mercy.
Matthew 5:8 Blessed are the clean in heart, because they shall see God.
Matthew 5:9 Blessed are the peacemakers, because they shall be called sons of God.
Matthew 5:10 Blessed are those persecuted for righteousness, because theirs is the kingdom of the heavens.
Matthew 5:11 Blessed are you when they reproach you and persecute and say every evil saying against you, lying, for my sake.
Matthew 5:12 Rejoice and exult, because your reward is great in the heavens; for thus they persecuted the prophets before you.
Matthew 5:13 You are the salt of the earth; but if the salt becomes tasteless, with what shall it be salted? It has strength for nothing any longer except to be thrown outside and trampled by humans.
Matthew 5:14 You are the light of the world. A city lying above a mountain cannot be hidden,
Matthew 5:15 nor do they light a lamp and place it under the bushel measure, but upon the lampstand, and it shines for all in the house.
Matthew 5:16 Thus let your light shine before humans, so that they may see your good works and glorify your Father in the heavens.
Matthew 5:17 Do not think that I came to dissolve the law or the prophets; I did not come to dissolve but to fulfill.
Matthew 5:18 For amen, I say to you: until heaven and earth pass away, one iota or one stroke shall certainly not pass away from the law until everything happens.
Matthew 5:19 Therefore whoever loosens one of these least commandments and teaches humans thus shall be called least in the kingdom of the heavens; but whoever does and teaches, this one shall be called great in the kingdom of the heavens.
Matthew 5:20 For I say to you that unless your righteousness abounds beyond that of the scribes and Pharisees, you shall certainly not enter the kingdom of the heavens.
Matthew 5:21 You heard that it was said to the ancients: You shall not murder; and whoever murders shall be liable to the judgment.
Matthew 5:22 But I say to you that everyone angry with his brother without cause shall be liable to the judgment; and whoever says to his brother: Raka, shall be liable to the council; and whoever says: Fool, shall be liable to the Gehenna of fire.
Matthew 5:23 Therefore if you offer your gift upon the altar and there remember that your brother has something against you,
Matthew 5:24 leave your gift there before the altar and go, first be reconciled to your brother, and then come and offer your gift.
Matthew 5:25 Be well disposed to your adversary quickly, while you are on the way with him, lest the adversary hand you over to the judge and the judge hand you over to the attendant and you be thrown into prison.
Matthew 5:26 Amen, I say to you: you shall certainly not come out from there until you repay the last quadrans.
Matthew 5:27 You heard that it was said to the ancients: You shall not commit adultery.
Matthew 5:28 But I say to you that everyone looking at a woman to desire her has already committed adultery with her in his heart.
Matthew 5:29 And if your right eye causes you to stumble, take it out and throw it away from you; for it benefits you that one of your members perish and your whole body not be thrown into Gehenna.
Matthew 5:30 And if your right hand causes you to stumble, cut it off and throw it away from you; for it benefits you that one of your members perish and your whole body not be thrown into Gehenna.
Matthew 5:31 And it was said: Whoever releases his wife, let him give her a document of divorce.
Matthew 5:32 But I say to you that whoever releases his wife, except for a matter of fornication, causes her to commit adultery, and whoever marries a released woman commits adultery.
Matthew 5:33 Again you heard that it was said to the ancients: You shall not swear falsely, but shall render your oaths to the Lord.
Matthew 5:34 But I say to you not to swear at all, neither by heaven, because it is God's throne,
Matthew 5:35 nor by earth, because it is the footstool of his feet, nor toward Hierosolyma, because it is the city of the great King,
Matthew 5:36 nor shall you swear by your head, because you cannot make one hair white or black.
Matthew 5:37 And let your word be: Yes, yes; no, no; and what exceeds these is from the evil one.
Matthew 5:38 You heard that it was said: An eye for an eye and a tooth for a tooth.
Matthew 5:39 But I say to you not to resist the evil one; but whoever slaps you upon your right cheek, turn to him the other also,
Matthew 5:40 and to the one wishing to litigate with you and take your tunic, leave him your cloak also,
Matthew 5:41 and whoever compels you to go one mile, go with him two.
Matthew 5:42 Give to the one asking you, and do not turn away the one wishing to borrow from you.
Matthew 5:43 You heard that it was said: You shall love your neighbor and hate your enemy.
Matthew 5:44 But I say to you: Love your enemies, bless those cursing you, do good to those hating you, and pray for those abusing you and persecuting you,
Matthew 5:45 so that you may become sons of your Father in the heavens, because he makes his sun rise upon evil and good people and sends rain upon righteous and unrighteous people.
Matthew 5:46 For if you love those loving you, what reward do you have? Do not even the tax collectors do the same?
Matthew 5:47 And if you greet only your brothers, what more do you do? Do not even the tax collectors do thus?
Matthew 5:48 Therefore you shall be perfect, just as your Father in the heavens is perfect.

## Chapter 6

Matthew 6:1 Take heed not to do your almsgiving before humans to be seen by them; otherwise you have no reward with your Father in the heavens.
Matthew 6:2 Therefore when you do almsgiving, do not trumpet before you, just as the hypocrites do in the synagogues and in the lanes, so that they may be glorified by humans; amen, I say to you: they have received their reward.
Matthew 6:3 But when you do almsgiving, let your left hand not know what your right hand does,
Matthew 6:4 so that your almsgiving may be in secret, and your Father who sees in secret, he shall repay you openly.
Matthew 6:5 And when you pray, you shall not be just as the hypocrites, because they love to pray standing in the synagogues and at the corners of the streets, so that they may appear to humans; amen, I say to you that they have received their reward.
Matthew 6:6 But you, when you pray, enter your inner chamber, and closing your door, pray to your Father in secret, and your Father who sees in secret shall repay you openly.
Matthew 6:7 And when praying, do not babble just as the nations do; for they think that they shall be heard through their many words.
Matthew 6:8 Therefore do not become like them, for your Father knows what you have need of before you ask him.
Matthew 6:9 Therefore pray thus: Our Father in the heavens, let your name be sanctified;
Matthew 6:10 let your kingdom come; let your will be done, as in heaven, also upon the earth;
Matthew 6:11 give us today our daily bread;
Matthew 6:12 and forgive us our debts, as we also forgive our debtors;
Matthew 6:13 and do not bring us into temptation, but rescue us from the evil one.
Matthew 6:14 For if you forgive humans their transgressions, your heavenly Father shall forgive you also;
Matthew 6:15 but if you do not forgive humans their transgressions, neither shall your Father forgive your transgressions.
Matthew 6:16 And when you fast, do not become gloomy just as the hypocrites, for they disfigure their faces so that they may appear to humans to be fasting; amen, I say to you that they have received their reward.
Matthew 6:17 But you, fasting, anoint your head and wash your face,
Matthew 6:18 so that you may not appear to humans to be fasting, but to your Father in secret; and your Father who sees in secret shall repay you openly.
Matthew 6:19 Do not store up treasures for yourselves upon the earth, where moth and consumption destroy and where thieves dig through and steal;
Matthew 6:20 but store up treasures for yourselves in heaven, where neither moth nor consumption destroys and where thieves do not dig through or steal.
Matthew 6:21 For where your treasure is, there your heart shall be also.
Matthew 6:22 The lamp of the body is the eye; therefore if your eye is simple, your whole body shall be luminous;
Matthew 6:23 but if your eye is evil, your whole body shall be dark. Therefore if the light in you is darkness, how great the darkness!
Matthew 6:24 No one can serve two lords; for either he shall hate the one and love the other, or hold to one and despise the other. You cannot serve God and mammon.
Matthew 6:25 Therefore I say to you: Do not be anxious for your soul, what you shall eat and what you shall drink, nor for your body, what you shall put on. Is not the soul more than food and the body than clothing?
Matthew 6:26 Look at the birds of heaven, because they do not sow or reap or gather into storehouses, and your heavenly Father feeds them. Do you not differ from them much more?
Matthew 6:27 And who among you, being anxious, can add one cubit to his stature?
Matthew 6:28 And why are you anxious concerning clothing? Consider the lilies of the field, how they grow; they do not toil or spin;
Matthew 6:29 and I say to you that not even Solomon in all his glory was clothed like one of these.
Matthew 6:30 And if God thus clothes the grass of the field, which is today and tomorrow is thrown into an oven, shall he not much more clothe you, you of little faith?
Matthew 6:31 Therefore do not be anxious, saying: What shall we eat? Or: What shall we drink? Or: What shall we put on?
Matthew 6:32 For the nations seek all these things; for your heavenly Father knows that you need all these things.
Matthew 6:33 But seek first the kingdom of God and his righteousness, and all these things shall be added to you.
Matthew 6:34 Therefore do not be anxious for tomorrow, for tomorrow shall be anxious for its own things; sufficient for the day is its evil.

## Chapter 7

Matthew 7:1 Do not judge, so that you may not be judged;
Matthew 7:2 for with the judgment with which you judge you shall be judged, and with the measure with which you measure it shall be measured back to you.
Matthew 7:3 And why do you look at the speck in your brother's eye, but do not consider the beam in your own eye?
Matthew 7:4 Or how shall you say to your brother: Let me cast the speck out of your eye, and behold, the beam is in your eye?
Matthew 7:5 Hypocrite, first cast the beam out of your eye, and then you shall see clearly to cast the speck out of your brother's eye.
Matthew 7:6 Do not give what is holy to the dogs, nor throw your pearls before the pigs, lest they trample them with their feet and turn and tear you.
Matthew 7:7 Ask, and it shall be given to you; seek, and you shall find; knock, and it shall be opened to you.
Matthew 7:8 For everyone asking receives, and the one seeking finds, and to the one knocking it shall be opened.
Matthew 7:9 Or what human is there among you who, if his son asks for bread, shall give him a stone?
Matthew 7:10 And if he asks for a fish, shall he give him a serpent?
Matthew 7:11 Therefore if you, being evil, know to give good gifts to your children, how much more shall your Father in the heavens give good things to those asking him?
Matthew 7:12 Therefore all things whatsoever you wish humans to do to you, thus also do to them; for this is the law and the prophets.
Matthew 7:13 Enter through the narrow gate, because broad is the gate and spacious the way leading away to destruction, and many are those entering through it;
Matthew 7:14 because narrow is the gate and constricted the way leading away to life, and few are those finding it.
Matthew 7:15 And take heed of the false prophets, who come to you in sheep's garments, but within are ravenous wolves.
Matthew 7:16 From their fruits you shall recognize them. Do they gather grapes from thorns or figs from thistles?
Matthew 7:17 Thus every good tree produces good fruits, but the rotten tree produces evil fruits.
