Matthew 7:18 A good tree cannot produce evil fruits, nor a rotten tree produce good fruits.
Matthew 7:19 Every tree not producing good fruit is cut down and thrown into fire.
Matthew 7:20 Therefore indeed from their fruits you shall recognize them.
Matthew 7:21 Not everyone saying to me: Lord, Lord, shall enter the kingdom of the heavens, but the one doing the will of my Father in the heavens.
Matthew 7:22 Many shall say to me on that day: Lord, Lord, did we not prophesy in your name and cast out demons in your name and do many mighty works in your name?
Matthew 7:23 And then I shall declare to them: I never knew you; depart from me, you who work lawlessness.
Matthew 7:24 Therefore everyone who hears these words of mine and does them, I shall liken him to a prudent man who built his house upon the rock;
Matthew 7:25 and the rain descended and the rivers came and the winds blew and fell against that house, and it did not fall, for it had been founded upon the rock.
Matthew 7:26 And everyone hearing these words of mine and not doing them shall be likened to a foolish man who built his house upon the sand;
Matthew 7:27 and the rain descended and the rivers came and the winds blew and struck that house, and it fell, and its fall was great.
Matthew 7:28 And it happened, when Jesus completed these words, the crowds were astonished at his teaching,
Matthew 7:29 for he was teaching them as one having authority and not as the scribes.

## Chapter 8

Matthew 8:1 And when he came down from the mountain, many crowds followed him.
Matthew 8:2 And behold, a leper came and worshipped him, saying: Lord, if you wish, you can cleanse me.
Matthew 8:3 And Jesus stretched out his hand and touched him, saying: I wish; be cleansed. And immediately his leprosy was cleansed.
Matthew 8:4 And Jesus says to him: See that you tell no one, but go, show yourself to the priest and offer the gift which Moses commanded, for a testimony to them.
Matthew 8:5 And when Jesus entered Capernaoum, a centurion approached him, appealing to him
Matthew 8:6 and saying: Lord, my servant lies in the house paralyzed, terribly tormented.
Matthew 8:7 And Jesus says to him: I shall come and heal him.
Matthew 8:8 And the centurion answered and said: Lord, I am not sufficient for you to enter under my roof, but only say a word, and my servant shall be healed.
Matthew 8:9 For I also am a human under authority, having soldiers under myself, and I say to this one: Go, and he goes, and to another: Come, and he comes, and to my slave: Do this, and he does it.
Matthew 8:10 And Jesus, hearing, wondered and said to those following: Amen, I say to you: not even in Israel did I find such faith.
Matthew 8:11 And I say to you that many shall come from east and west and recline with Abraam and Isaak and Iakob in the kingdom of the heavens;
Matthew 8:12 but the sons of the kingdom shall be cast out into the outer darkness; there shall be weeping and gnashing of teeth.
Matthew 8:13 And Jesus said to the centurion: Go, and as you believed, let it happen for you. And his servant was healed at that hour.
Matthew 8:14 And Jesus came into Peter's house and saw his mother-in-law lying down and feverish,
Matthew 8:15 and touched her hand, and the fever left her, and she rose and ministered to them.
Matthew 8:16 And when evening came, they brought to him many possessed by demons, and he cast out the spirits with a word and healed all those who were ill,
Matthew 8:17 so that what was spoken through Esaias the prophet might be fulfilled, saying: He took our weaknesses and bore the diseases.
Matthew 8:18 And Jesus, seeing many crowds around him, commanded to depart to the other side.
Matthew 8:19 And one scribe approached and said to him: Teacher, I shall follow you wherever you go.
Matthew 8:20 And Jesus says to him: The foxes have dens and the birds of heaven dwelling places, but the Son of man has nowhere to lay his head.
Matthew 8:21 And another of his disciples said to him: Lord, permit me first to go away and bury my father.
Matthew 8:22 But Jesus said to him: Follow me, and leave the dead to bury their own dead.
Matthew 8:23 And when he entered the boat, his disciples followed him.
Matthew 8:24 And behold, a great shaking happened in the sea, so that the boat was covered by the waves; but he slept.
Matthew 8:25 And his disciples approached and awakened him, saying: Lord, save us, we are perishing.
Matthew 8:26 And he says to them: Why are you cowardly, you of little faith? Then rising, he rebuked the winds and the sea, and a great calm came.
Matthew 8:27 And the humans wondered, saying: What sort of one is this, that even the winds and the sea obey him?
Matthew 8:28 And when he came to the other side, to the country of the Gergesenes, two possessed by demons met him, coming out of the tombs, exceedingly fierce, so that no one could pass by that way.
Matthew 8:29 And behold, they cried, saying: What is there between us and you, Jesus, son of God? Did you come here before the time to torment us?
Matthew 8:30 And far from them there was a herd of many pigs feeding.
Matthew 8:31 And the demons appealed to him, saying: If you cast us out, permit us to go into the herd of pigs.
Matthew 8:32 And he said to them: Go. And coming out, they went into the herd of pigs, and behold, the whole herd of pigs rushed down the cliff into the sea and died in the waters.
Matthew 8:33 And those feeding them fled, and going into the city announced everything, and the things concerning those possessed by demons.
Matthew 8:34 And behold, the whole city came out to meet Jesus, and seeing him they appealed that he depart from their boundaries.

## Chapter 9

Matthew 9:1 And entering the boat he crossed over and came into his own city.
Matthew 9:2 And behold, they brought to him a paralytic lying upon a bed, and Jesus, seeing their faith, said to the paralytic: Take courage, child; your sins are forgiven you.
Matthew 9:3 And behold, some of the scribes said within themselves: This one blasphemes.
Matthew 9:4 And Jesus, seeing their thoughts, said: Why do you think evil things in your hearts?
Matthew 9:5 For which is easier, to say: Your sins are forgiven you, or to say: Rise and walk?
Matthew 9:6 But so that you may know that the Son of man has authority upon the earth to forgive sins—then he says to the paralytic: Rise, take up your bed and go to your house.
Matthew 9:7 And rising, he went away to his house.
Matthew 9:8 And the crowds, seeing, wondered and glorified God who gave such authority to humans.
Matthew 9:9 And Jesus, passing on from there, saw a human sitting at the tax office, called Matthew, and says to him: Follow me. And rising, he followed him.
Matthew 9:10 And it happened, as he reclined in the house, and behold, many tax collectors and sinners came and reclined together with Jesus and his disciples.
Matthew 9:11 And the Pharisees, seeing, said to his disciples: Why does your teacher eat with tax collectors and sinners?
Matthew 9:12 And Jesus, hearing, said to them: Those who are strong have no need of a physician, but those who are ill.
Matthew 9:13 But go and learn what this is: I wish mercy and not sacrifice; for I did not come to call righteous people, but sinners to repentance.
Matthew 9:14 Then John's disciples approach him, saying: Why do we and the Pharisees fast much, but your disciples do not fast?
Matthew 9:15 And Jesus said to them: Can the sons of the bridal chamber mourn as long as the bridegroom is with them? But days shall come when the bridegroom is taken away from them, and then they shall fast.
Matthew 9:16 And no one puts a patch of unfulled cloth upon an old garment, for its filling pulls away from the garment, and a worse tear happens.
Matthew 9:17 Nor do they put new wine into old wineskins; otherwise the wineskins burst and the wine is poured out and the wineskins perish; but they put new wine into fresh wineskins, and both are preserved.
Matthew 9:18 While he spoke these things to them, behold, a ruler came and worshipped him, saying: My daughter has just died, but come and place your hand upon her, and she shall live.
Matthew 9:19 And Jesus rose and followed him, and his disciples.
Matthew 9:20 And behold, a woman hemorrhaging twelve years approached from behind and touched the fringe of his garment,
Matthew 9:21 for she said within herself: If I only touch his garment, I shall be saved.
Matthew 9:22 And Jesus turned and saw her and said: Take courage, daughter; your faith has saved you. And the woman was saved from that hour.
Matthew 9:23 And Jesus came into the ruler's house and saw the flute players and the crowd in an uproar,
Matthew 9:24 and says to them: Withdraw, for the girl did not die, but sleeps. And they laughed at him.
Matthew 9:25 But when the crowd was cast out, he entered and took hold of her hand, and the girl was raised.
Matthew 9:26 And this report went out into all that land.
Matthew 9:27 And as Jesus passed on from there, two blind men followed him, crying and saying: Have mercy on us, son of Dabid.
Matthew 9:28 And when he came into the house, the blind men approached him, and Jesus says to them: Do you believe that I can do this? They say to him: Yes, Lord.
Matthew 9:29 Then he touched their eyes, saying: According to your faith let it happen for you.
Matthew 9:30 And their eyes were opened, and Jesus sternly warned them, saying: See that no one knows.
Matthew 9:31 But going out, they spread the report of him in all that land.
Matthew 9:32 And as they went out, behold, they brought to him a mute human possessed by a demon,
Matthew 9:33 and when the demon was cast out, the mute spoke, and the crowds wondered, saying: Never did it appear thus in Israel.
Matthew 9:34 But the Pharisees said: By the ruler of the demons he casts out demons.
Matthew 9:35 And Jesus went around all the cities and the villages, teaching in their synagogues and proclaiming the good news of the kingdom and healing every disease and every infirmity among the people.
Matthew 9:36 And seeing the crowds, he had compassion concerning them, because they were exhausted and cast down, like sheep not having a shepherd.
Matthew 9:37 Then he says to his disciples: The harvest indeed is great, but the workers few;
Matthew 9:38 therefore supplicate the Lord of the harvest, that he send out workers into his harvest.

## Chapter 10

Matthew 10:1 And calling his twelve disciples to him, he gave them authority over unclean spirits, so as to cast them out and heal every disease and every infirmity.
Matthew 10:2 And the names of the twelve apostles are these: first Simon called Peter, and Andrew his brother, Iakobos the son of Zebedaios and John his brother,
Matthew 10:3 Philip and Bartholomaios, Thomas and Matthew the tax collector, Iakobos the son of Alphaios and Lebbaios surnamed Thaddaios,
Matthew 10:4 Simon the Kananite and Ioudas Iskariotes, who also handed him over.
Matthew 10:5 These twelve Jesus sent out, commanding them, saying: Do not go into a way of nations, and do not enter a city of Samaritans;
Matthew 10:6 but go rather to the lost sheep of the house of Israel.
Matthew 10:7 And as you go, proclaim, saying that the kingdom of the heavens has drawn near.
Matthew 10:8 Heal the sick, cleanse lepers, raise the dead, cast out demons; freely you received, freely give.
Matthew 10:9 Do not acquire gold or silver or bronze for your belts,
Matthew 10:10 no bag for the way, nor two tunics nor sandals nor a staff; for the worker is worthy of his food.
Matthew 10:11 And whatever city or village you enter, inquire who in it is worthy, and remain there until you go out.
Matthew 10:12 And as you enter the house, greet it,
Matthew 10:13 and if the house is worthy, let your peace come upon it; but if it is not worthy, let your peace return to you.
Matthew 10:14 And whoever does not receive you or hear your words, as you go out of that house or city, shake off the dust of your feet.
Matthew 10:15 Amen, I say to you: it shall be more tolerable for the land of Sodoma and Gomorra on the day of judgment than for that city.
Matthew 10:16 Behold, I send you as sheep in the midst of wolves; therefore become prudent as the serpents and unmixed as the doves.
Matthew 10:17 And take heed of humans, for they shall hand you over to councils and flog you in their synagogues,
Matthew 10:18 and you shall also be brought before governors and kings for my sake, for a testimony to them and the nations.
Matthew 10:19 And when they hand you over, do not be anxious how or what you shall speak, for what you shall speak shall be given to you at that hour;
Matthew 10:20 for you are not those speaking, but the Spirit of your Father who speaks in you.
Matthew 10:21 And brother shall hand over brother to death, and father a child, and children shall rise against parents and put them to death,
Matthew 10:22 and you shall be hated by all because of my name; but the one enduring to the end, this one shall be saved.
Matthew 10:23 And when they persecute you in this city, flee to the other; for amen, I say to you: you shall certainly not finish the cities of Israel until the Son of man comes.
Matthew 10:24 A disciple is not above the teacher, nor a slave above his lord.
Matthew 10:25 It is sufficient for the disciple to become as his teacher and the slave as his lord. If they called the master of the house Beelzeboul, how much more his household members?
Matthew 10:26 Therefore do not fear them, for there is nothing covered which shall not be uncovered, and hidden which shall not be known.
Matthew 10:27 What I say to you in the darkness, say in the light, and what you hear in the ear, proclaim upon the housetops.
Matthew 10:28 And do not fear those killing the body but unable to kill the soul; but fear rather the one able to destroy both soul and body in Gehenna.
Matthew 10:29 Are not two sparrows sold for an assarion? And one of them shall not fall upon the earth without your Father.
Matthew 10:30 And even the hairs of your head are all numbered.
Matthew 10:31 Therefore do not fear; you differ from many sparrows.
Matthew 10:32 Therefore everyone who acknowledges me before humans, I also shall acknowledge him before my Father in the heavens;
Matthew 10:33 but whoever denies me before humans, I also shall deny him before my Father in the heavens.
Matthew 10:34 Do not think that I came to cast peace upon the earth; I did not come to cast peace, but a sword.
Matthew 10:35 For I came to divide a human against his father, and a daughter against her mother, and a daughter-in-law against her mother-in-law,
Matthew 10:36 and a human's enemies are his household members.
Matthew 10:37 The one loving father or mother above me is not worthy of me, and the one loving son or daughter above me is not worthy of me,
Matthew 10:38 and whoever does not take his cross and follow after me is not worthy of me.
Matthew 10:39 The one finding his soul shall lose it, and the one losing his soul for my sake shall find it.
Matthew 10:40 The one receiving you receives me, and the one receiving me receives the one who sent me.
Matthew 10:41 The one receiving a prophet in the name of a prophet shall receive a prophet's reward, and the one receiving a righteous person in the name of a righteous person shall receive a righteous person's reward.
Matthew 10:42 And whoever gives one of these little ones only a cup of cold water to drink in the name of a disciple, amen, I say to you: he shall certainly not lose his reward.

## Chapter 11

Matthew 11:1 And it happened, when Jesus finished giving orders to his twelve disciples, he departed from there to teach and proclaim in their cities.
Matthew 11:2 And John, hearing in prison the works of the Christ, sent two of his disciples
Matthew 11:3 and said to him: Are you the coming one, or do we await another?
Matthew 11:4 And Jesus answered and said to them: Go and announce to John what you hear and see:
Matthew 11:5 blind people regain sight and lame people walk, lepers are cleansed and deaf people hear, dead people are raised and poor people are given good news,
Matthew 11:6 and blessed is whoever does not stumble because of me.
Matthew 11:7 And as these went, Jesus began to say to the crowds concerning John: What did you go out into the wilderness to behold? A reed shaken by wind?
Matthew 11:8 But what did you go out to see? A human clothed in soft garments? Behold, those wearing soft things are in the houses of kings.
Matthew 11:9 But what did you go out to see? A prophet? Yes, I say to you, and more than a prophet.
Matthew 11:10 For this is the one concerning whom it is written: Behold, I send my messenger before your face, who shall prepare your way before you.
Matthew 11:11 Amen, I say to you: among those born of women none greater than John the Baptist has arisen; but the lesser in the kingdom of the heavens is greater than he.
Matthew 11:12 And from the days of John the Baptist until now the kingdom of the heavens suffers violence, and violent ones seize it.
Matthew 11:13 For all the prophets and the law prophesied until John,
Matthew 11:14 and if you wish to receive it, he is Elias who is to come.
Matthew 11:15 The one having ears to hear, let him hear.
Matthew 11:16 And to what shall I liken this generation? It is like children sitting in marketplaces and calling to their companions
Matthew 11:17 and saying: We played the flute for you, and you did not dance; we lamented for you, and you did not beat your breasts.
Matthew 11:18 For John came neither eating nor drinking, and they say: He has a demon.
Matthew 11:19 The Son of man came eating and drinking, and they say: Behold, a gluttonous human and a wine drinker, a friend of tax collectors and sinners. And wisdom was justified by her children.
Matthew 11:20 Then he began to reproach the cities in which most of his mighty works happened, because they did not repent:
Matthew 11:21 Woe to you, Chorazin; woe to you, Bethsaida; because if the mighty works which happened in you had happened in Tyre and Sidon, they would have repented long ago in sackcloth and ashes.
Matthew 11:22 Nevertheless I say to you: it shall be more tolerable for Tyre and Sidon on the day of judgment than for you.
Matthew 11:23 And you, Capernaoum, who were exalted unto heaven, shall be brought down unto Hades; because if the mighty works which happened in you had happened in Sodoma, they would have remained until today.
Matthew 11:24 Nevertheless I say to you that it shall be more tolerable for the land of Sodoma on the day of judgment than for you.
Matthew 11:25 At that time Jesus answered and said: I give thanks to you, Father, Lord of heaven and earth, because you hid these things from wise and understanding people and revealed them to infants.
Matthew 11:26 Yes, Father, because thus it became pleasing before you.
Matthew 11:27 All things were handed over to me by my Father, and no one knows the Son except the Father, nor does anyone know the Father except the Son and whoever the Son wishes to reveal him to.
Matthew 11:28 Come to me, all who toil and are burdened, and I shall give you rest.
Matthew 11:29 Take my yoke upon you and learn from me, because I am meek and lowly in heart, and you shall find rest for your souls;
Matthew 11:30 for my yoke is good and my burden light.

## Chapter 12

Matthew 12:1 At that time Jesus went through the grainfields on the sabbaths, and his disciples hungered and began to pluck ears of grain and eat.
Matthew 12:2 And the Pharisees, seeing, said to him: Behold, your disciples do what it is not lawful to do on a sabbath.
Matthew 12:3 And he said to them: Did you not read what Dabid did when he hungered, he and those with him,
Matthew 12:4 how he entered the house of God and ate the breads of presentation, which it was not lawful for him to eat, nor for those with him, except for the priests alone?
Matthew 12:5 Or did you not read in the law that on the sabbaths the priests in the temple profane the sabbath and are guiltless?
Matthew 12:6 And I say to you that one greater than the temple is here.
Matthew 12:7 But if you had known what this is: I wish mercy and not sacrifice, you would not have condemned the guiltless.
Matthew 12:8 For the Son of man is lord even of the sabbath.
Matthew 12:9 And departing from there he came into their synagogue,
Matthew 12:10 and behold, there was a human having a withered hand, and they questioned him, saying: Is it lawful to heal on the sabbaths? So that they might accuse him.
Matthew 12:11 And he said to them: What human shall there be among you who shall have one sheep, and if it falls into a pit on the sabbaths, shall he not take hold of it and raise it?
Matthew 12:12 Therefore how much does a human differ from a sheep! So it is lawful to do good on the sabbaths.
Matthew 12:13 Then he says to the human: Stretch out your hand. And he stretched it out, and it was restored healthy as the other.
Matthew 12:14 And the Pharisees went out and took counsel against him, how they might destroy him.
Matthew 12:15 But Jesus, knowing, withdrew from there, and many crowds followed him, and he healed them all
Matthew 12:16 and rebuked them so that they might not make him manifest,
Matthew 12:17 so that what was spoken through Esaias the prophet might be fulfilled, saying:
Matthew 12:18 Behold, my servant whom I chose, my beloved in whom my soul was well pleased; I shall place my Spirit upon him, and he shall announce judgment to the nations.
Matthew 12:19 He shall not quarrel or cry out, nor shall anyone hear his voice in the streets;
Matthew 12:20 a broken reed he shall not break off, and smoking flax he shall not extinguish, until he brings out judgment unto victory,
Matthew 12:21 and in his name nations shall hope.
Matthew 12:22 Then one possessed by a demon, blind and mute, was brought to him, and he healed him, so that the blind and mute one both spoke and saw.
Matthew 12:23 And all the crowds were astonished and said: Could this be the son of Dabid?
Matthew 12:24 But the Pharisees, hearing, said: This one does not cast out demons except by Beelzeboul, ruler of the demons.
Matthew 12:25 And Jesus, knowing their thoughts, said to them: Every kingdom divided against itself is desolated, and every city or house divided against itself shall not stand.
Matthew 12:26 And if Satan casts out Satan, he was divided against himself; therefore how shall his kingdom stand?
Matthew 12:27 And if I cast out demons by Beelzeboul, by whom do your sons cast them out? Therefore they shall be your judges.
Matthew 12:28 But if I cast out demons by the Spirit of God, then the kingdom of God has reached you.
Matthew 12:29 Or how can anyone enter the house of the strong one and plunder his goods, unless he first binds the strong one? And then he shall plunder his house.
Matthew 12:30 The one not being with me is against me, and the one not gathering with me scatters.
Matthew 12:31 Therefore I say to you: every sin and blasphemy shall be forgiven humans, but the blasphemy of the Spirit shall not be forgiven humans.
Matthew 12:32 And whoever says a word against the Son of man, it shall be forgiven him; but whoever speaks against the Holy Spirit, it shall not be forgiven him, neither in this age nor in the coming one.
Matthew 12:33 Either make the tree good and its fruit good, or make the tree rotten and its fruit rotten; for from the fruit the tree is known.
Matthew 12:34 Offspring of vipers, how can you speak good things, being evil? For from the abundance of the heart the mouth speaks.
Matthew 12:35 The good human brings out good things from the good treasure of the heart, and the evil human brings out evil things from the evil treasure.
Matthew 12:36 And I say to you that every idle saying which humans speak, they shall render an account concerning it on the day of judgment;
Matthew 12:37 for from your words you shall be justified, and from your words you shall be condemned.
Matthew 12:38 Then some of the scribes and Pharisees answered, saying: Teacher, we wish to see a sign from you.
Matthew 12:39 And he answered and said to them: An evil and adulterous generation seeks a sign, and a sign shall not be given to it except the sign of Ionas the prophet.
Matthew 12:40 For just as Ionas was in the belly of the sea creature three days and three nights, thus the Son of man shall be in the heart of the earth three days and three nights.
Matthew 12:41 Ninevite men shall rise in the judgment with this generation and condemn it, because they repented at the proclamation of Ionas, and behold, more than Ionas is here.
Matthew 12:42 A queen of the south shall be raised in the judgment with this generation and condemn it, because she came from the ends of the earth to hear the wisdom of Solomon, and behold, more than Solomon is here.
Matthew 12:43 And when the unclean spirit comes out from the human, it passes through waterless places seeking rest and does not find it.
Matthew 12:44 Then it says: I shall return to my house from which I came out. And coming, it finds it unoccupied, swept and adorned.
Matthew 12:45 Then it goes and takes with itself seven other spirits more evil than itself, and entering they dwell there, and the last things of that human become worse than the first. Thus it shall be also for this evil generation.
Matthew 12:46 And while he still spoke to the crowds, behold, his mother and brothers stood outside, seeking to speak to him.
Matthew 12:47 And someone said to him: Behold, your mother and your brothers stand outside, seeking to speak to you.
Matthew 12:48 And he answered and said to the one who told him: Who is my mother, and who are my brothers?
Matthew 12:49 And stretching out his hand toward his disciples, he said: Behold, my mother and my brothers;
Matthew 12:50 for whoever does the will of my Father in the heavens, he is my brother and sister and mother.

## Chapter 13

Matthew 13:1 And on that day Jesus went out of the house and was sitting beside the sea.
Matthew 13:2 And many crowds gathered to him, so that he entered the boat and sat down, and the whole crowd stood on the shore.
Matthew 13:3 And he spoke many things to them in parables, saying: Behold, the sower went out to sow.
Matthew 13:4 And as he sowed, some fell beside the road, and the birds came and devoured them.
Matthew 13:5 And others fell on the rocky places, where they did not have much earth, and immediately sprang up because they had no depth of earth.
Matthew 13:6 And when the sun rose, they were scorched, and because they had no root, they withered.
Matthew 13:7 And others fell upon the thorns, and the thorns grew up and choked them.
Matthew 13:8 And others fell upon the good earth and were giving fruit, one a hundred, another sixty, and another thirty.
Matthew 13:9 He who has ears to hear, let him hear.
Matthew 13:10 And the disciples approached and said to him: Why do you speak to them in parables?
Matthew 13:11 And he answered and said to them: Because to you it has been given to know the mysteries of the kingdom of the heavens, but to them it has not been given.
Matthew 13:12 For whoever has, to him it shall be given, and he shall have abundance; but whoever does not have, even what he has shall be taken from him.
Matthew 13:13 For this reason I speak to them in parables: because seeing they do not see, and hearing they do not hear, nor do they understand.
Matthew 13:14 And in them the prophecy of Isaiah is fulfilled, which says: With hearing you shall hear and shall certainly not understand, and seeing you shall see and shall certainly not perceive.
Matthew 13:15 For the heart of this people has grown fat, and with their ears they heard heavily, and they closed their eyes, lest they see with their eyes and hear with their ears and understand with their heart and turn, and I heal them.
Matthew 13:16 But blessed are your eyes, because they see, and your ears, because they hear.
Matthew 13:17 For amen, I say to you that many prophets and righteous men desired to see what you see and did not see, and to hear what you hear and did not hear.
Matthew 13:18 You, therefore, hear the parable of the sower.
Matthew 13:19 When anyone hears the word of the kingdom and does not understand, the evil one comes and snatches away what was sown in his heart. This is the one sown beside the road.
Matthew 13:20 And the one sown on the rocky places, this is the one who hears the word and immediately receives it with joy.
Matthew 13:21 But he has no root in himself, but is temporary; and when affliction or persecution arises because of the word, immediately he is made to stumble.
Matthew 13:22 And the one sown among the thorns, this is the one who hears the word, and the care of this age and the deceit of wealth choke the word, and he becomes unfruitful.
Matthew 13:23 And the one sown upon the good earth, this is the one who hears the word and understands, who indeed bears fruit and produces, one a hundred, another sixty, and another thirty.
Matthew 13:24 He set another parable before them, saying: The kingdom of the heavens was likened to a man sowing good seed in his field.
Matthew 13:25 But while the men slept, his enemy came and sowed darnel among the wheat and went away.
Matthew 13:26 And when the blade sprouted and produced fruit, then the darnel also appeared.
Matthew 13:27 And the slaves of the master of the house approached and said to him: Lord, did you not sow good seed in your field? From where, then, does it have the darnel?
Matthew 13:28 And he said to them: An enemy man did this. And the slaves said to him: Do you wish, then, that we go and gather them?
Matthew 13:29 But he said: No, lest in gathering the darnel you uproot the wheat together with them.
Matthew 13:30 Let both grow together until the harvest, and at the time of the harvest I shall say to the harvesters: Gather the darnel first and bind them into bundles to burn them up, but gather the wheat into my storehouse.
Matthew 13:31 He set another parable before them, saying: The kingdom of the heavens is like a grain of mustard, which a man took and sowed in his field.
Matthew 13:32 Which is indeed smaller than all the seeds, but when it grows, it is greater than the garden plants and becomes a tree, so that the birds of the heaven come and dwell in its branches.
Matthew 13:33 He spoke another parable to them: The kingdom of the heavens is like leaven, which a woman took and hid in three sata of flour, until the whole was leavened.
Matthew 13:34 Jesus spoke all these things to the crowds in parables, and without a parable he did not speak to them,
Matthew 13:35 so that what was spoken through the prophet might be fulfilled, saying: I shall open my mouth in parables; I shall utter things hidden from the foundation of the world.
Matthew 13:36 Then Jesus left the crowds and came into the house, and his disciples approached him, saying: Explain to us the parable of the darnel of the field.
Matthew 13:37 And he answered and said to them: The one sowing the good seed is the Son of man.
Matthew 13:38 And the field is the world, and the good seed, these are the sons of the kingdom; and the darnel are the sons of the evil one.
Matthew 13:39 And the enemy who sowed them is the devil, and the harvest is the completion of the age, and the harvesters are angels.
Matthew 13:40 Therefore, just as the darnel is gathered and burned up with fire, so shall it be at the completion of this age.
Matthew 13:41 The Son of man shall send his angels, and they shall gather out of his kingdom all the stumbling blocks and those who practice lawlessness,
Matthew 13:42 and shall cast them into the furnace of fire. There shall be the weeping and the grinding of teeth.
Matthew 13:43 Then the righteous shall shine out like the sun in the kingdom of their Father. He who has ears to hear, let him hear.
Matthew 13:44 Again, the kingdom of the heavens is like a treasure hidden in the field, which a man found and hid, and from his joy he goes and sells everything he has and buys that field.
Matthew 13:45 Again, the kingdom of the heavens is like a merchant man seeking beautiful pearls,
Matthew 13:46 who, having found one very precious pearl, went away and sold everything he had and bought it.
Matthew 13:47 Again, the kingdom of the heavens is like a dragnet cast into the sea and gathering from every kind,
Matthew 13:48 which, when it was filled, they drew up onto the shore, and sitting down they gathered the good into vessels, but cast the rotten outside.
Matthew 13:49 So shall it be at the completion of the age: the angels shall come out and separate the evil from the midst of the righteous,
Matthew 13:50 and shall cast them into the furnace of fire. There shall be the weeping and the grinding of teeth.
Matthew 13:51 Jesus says to them: Have you understood all these things? They say to him: Yes, Lord.
Matthew 13:52 And he said to them: For this reason every scribe who has been made a disciple for the kingdom of the heavens is like a master of a house who brings out of his treasure new things and old.
Matthew 13:53 And it happened, when Jesus finished these parables, he departed from there.
Matthew 13:54 And coming into his homeland, he was teaching them in their synagogue, so that they were astonished and said: From where does this man have this wisdom and the mighty works?
Matthew 13:55 Is this not the carpenter's son? Is his mother not called Mariam, and his brothers James and Joses and Simon and Judas?
Matthew 13:56 And his sisters, are they not all with us? From where, then, does this man have all these things?
Matthew 13:57 And they were made to stumble at him. But Jesus said to them: A prophet is not without honor except in his homeland and in his house.
Matthew 13:58 And he did not perform many mighty works there because of their unbelief.

## Chapter 14

Matthew 14:1 At that time Herod the tetrarch heard the report of Jesus,
Matthew 14:2 and said to his servants: This is John the Baptist; he was raised from the dead, and for this reason the powers work in him.
Matthew 14:3 For Herod had seized John and bound him and put him in prison because of Herodias, the wife of Philip his brother.
Matthew 14:4 For John was saying to him: It is not lawful for you to have her.
Matthew 14:5 And wishing to kill him, he feared the crowd, because they held him as a prophet.
Matthew 14:6 And while Herod's birthday was being celebrated, the daughter of Herodias danced in the midst and pleased Herod,
Matthew 14:7 whereupon he promised her with an oath to give whatever she might ask.
Matthew 14:8 And she, prompted by her mother, says: Give me here on a platter the head of John the Baptist.
Matthew 14:9 And the king was grieved, but because of the oaths and those reclining with him, he commanded it to be given.
Matthew 14:10 And sending, he beheaded John in the prison.
Matthew 14:11 And his head was brought on a platter and given to the girl, and she brought it to her mother.
Matthew 14:12 And his disciples approached and took the body and buried it, and came and reported to Jesus.
Matthew 14:13 And hearing, Jesus withdrew from there in a boat to a deserted place privately. And hearing, the crowds followed him on foot from the cities.
Matthew 14:14 And coming out, Jesus saw a great crowd and had compassion on them and healed their sick.
Matthew 14:15 And when evening came, his disciples approached him, saying: The place is deserted, and the hour has already passed; dismiss the crowds so that they may go into the villages and buy food for themselves.
Matthew 14:16 But Jesus said to them: They have no need to go away; you give them something to eat.
Matthew 14:17 And they say to him: We have nothing here except five loaves and two fish.
Matthew 14:18 And he said: Bring them here to me.
Matthew 14:19 And commanding the crowds to recline on the grass, and taking the five loaves and the two fish, he looked up into the heaven and blessed, and breaking, he gave the loaves to the disciples, and the disciples to the crowds.
Matthew 14:20 And all ate and were filled, and they took up the surplus of the fragments, twelve baskets full.
Matthew 14:21 And those eating were about five thousand men, apart from women and children.
Matthew 14:22 And immediately Jesus compelled his disciples to enter the boat and go ahead of him to the other side, until he should dismiss the crowds.
Matthew 14:23 And dismissing the crowds, he went up into the mountain privately to pray. And when evening came, he was there alone.
Matthew 14:24 But the boat was already in the middle of the sea, tormented by the waves, for the wind was contrary.
Matthew 14:25 And in the fourth watch of the night Jesus went toward them, walking upon the sea.
Matthew 14:26 And the disciples, seeing him walking upon the sea, were troubled, saying: It is an apparition. And they cried out from fear.
Matthew 14:27 But immediately Jesus spoke to them, saying: Take courage; I am; do not fear.
Matthew 14:28 And Peter answered him and said: Lord, if it is you, command me to come to you upon the waters.
Matthew 14:29 And he said: Come. And Peter went down from the boat and walked upon the waters to come to Jesus.
Matthew 14:30 But seeing the strong wind, he feared, and beginning to sink, he cried out, saying: Lord, save me.
Matthew 14:31 And immediately Jesus stretched out his hand and took hold of him, and says to him: You of little faith, why did you doubt?
Matthew 14:32 And when they entered the boat, the wind ceased.
Matthew 14:33 And those in the boat came and worshiped him, saying: Truly you are God's Son.
Matthew 14:34 And crossing over, they came into the land of Gennesaret.
Matthew 14:35 And recognizing him, the men of that place sent into that whole surrounding region, and brought to him all who were ill,
Matthew 14:36 and begged him that they might only touch the fringe of his garment; and as many as touched were saved.

## Chapter 15

Matthew 15:1 Then the scribes and Pharisees from Jerusalem approach Jesus, saying:
Matthew 15:2 Why do your disciples transgress the tradition of the elders? For they do not wash their hands when they eat bread.
Matthew 15:3 And he answered and said to them: Why do you also transgress the commandment of God because of your tradition?
Matthew 15:4 For God commanded, saying: Honor your father and mother; and: He who speaks evil of father or mother, let him die by death.
Matthew 15:5 But you say: Whoever says to his father or mother: Whatever you might benefit from me is a gift,
Matthew 15:6 and shall certainly not honor his father or his mother. And you made the commandment of God void because of your tradition.
Matthew 15:7 Hypocrites, Isaiah prophesied well concerning you, saying:
Matthew 15:8 This people approaches me with their mouth and honors me with their lips, but their heart is far from me.
Matthew 15:9 And in vain they worship me, teaching teachings, commandments of men.
Matthew 15:10 And calling the crowd to him, he said to them: Hear and understand.
Matthew 15:11 What enters into the mouth does not defile the man, but what goes out of the mouth, this defiles the man.
Matthew 15:12 Then his disciples approached and said to him: Do you know that the Pharisees, hearing the word, were made to stumble?
Matthew 15:13 And he answered and said: Every planting which my heavenly Father did not plant shall be uprooted.
Matthew 15:14 Leave them; they are blind guides of the blind. And if a blind man guides a blind man, both shall fall into a pit.
Matthew 15:15 And Peter answered and said to him: Explain this parable to us.
Matthew 15:16 And Jesus said: Are you also still without understanding?
Matthew 15:17 Do you not yet perceive that everything entering into the mouth goes into the belly and is cast out into the latrine?
Matthew 15:18 But the things going out of the mouth come out of the heart, and those defile the man.
Matthew 15:19 For out of the heart come evil reasonings, murders, adulteries, fornications, thefts, false testimonies, blasphemies.
Matthew 15:20 These are the things defiling the man, but eating with unwashed hands does not defile the man.
Matthew 15:21 And Jesus went out from there and withdrew into the regions of Tyre and Sidon.
Matthew 15:22 And behold, a Canaanite woman came out from those borders and cried out to him, saying: Have mercy on me, Lord, Son of David; my daughter is badly demon-possessed.
Matthew 15:23 But he did not answer her a word. And his disciples approached and asked him, saying: Dismiss her, because she cries out behind us.
Matthew 15:24 And he answered and said: I was not sent except to the lost sheep of the house of Israel.
Matthew 15:25 And she came and worshiped him, saying: Lord, help me.
Matthew 15:26 And he answered and said: It is not good to take the children's bread and cast it to the little dogs.
Matthew 15:27 And she said: Yes, Lord, for even the little dogs eat from the crumbs falling from their masters' table.
Matthew 15:28 Then Jesus answered and said to her: O woman, great is your faith; let it happen to you as you wish. And her daughter was healed from that hour.
Matthew 15:29 And departing from there, Jesus came beside the sea of Galilee, and going up into the mountain, he was sitting there.
Matthew 15:30 And many crowds approached him, having with them lame, blind, mute, maimed, and many others, and cast them beside Jesus' feet, and he healed them,
Matthew 15:31 so that the crowds marveled, seeing the mute speaking, the maimed healthy, the lame walking, and the blind seeing; and they glorified the God of Israel.
Matthew 15:32 And Jesus called his disciples to him and said: I have compassion on the crowd, because already they remain with me three days and have nothing to eat; and I do not wish to dismiss them fasting, lest they faint on the road.
Matthew 15:33 And his disciples say to him: From where do we have so many loaves in a deserted place as to fill so great a crowd?
Matthew 15:34 And Jesus says to them: How many loaves do you have? And they said: Seven, and a few little fish.
Matthew 15:35 And he commanded the crowds to recline upon the earth.
Matthew 15:36 And taking the seven loaves and the fish, he gave thanks and broke them and gave to his disciples, and the disciples to the crowd.
Matthew 15:37 And all ate and were filled, and they took up the surplus of the fragments, seven large baskets full.
Matthew 15:38 And those eating were four thousand men, apart from women and children.
Matthew 15:39 And dismissing the crowds, he entered the boat and came into the borders of Magdala.

## Chapter 16

Matthew 16:1 And the Pharisees and Sadducees approached, testing him, and asked him to show them a sign from the heaven.
Matthew 16:2 And he answered and said to them: When evening comes, you say: Fair weather, for the heaven is red.
Matthew 16:3 And in the morning: Today a storm, for the heaven is red and gloomy. Hypocrites, you know how to discern the face of the heaven, but you cannot discern the signs of the times.
Matthew 16:4 An evil and adulterous generation seeks a sign, and a sign shall not be given to it except the sign of Jonah the prophet. And leaving them, he went away.
Matthew 16:5 And his disciples came to the other side and forgot to take loaves.
Matthew 16:6 And Jesus said to them: See and beware of the leaven of the Pharisees and Sadducees.
Matthew 16:7 And they were reasoning among themselves, saying: Because we did not take loaves.
Matthew 16:8 And Jesus knew and said to them: Why do you reason among yourselves, you of little faith, because you did not take loaves?
Matthew 16:9 Do you not yet perceive, nor remember the five loaves of the five thousand, and how many baskets you took?
Matthew 16:10 Nor the seven loaves of the four thousand, and how many large baskets you took?
Matthew 16:11 How do you not perceive that I did not speak to you concerning bread, to beware of the leaven of the Pharisees and Sadducees?
Matthew 16:12 Then they understood that he did not say to beware of the leaven of bread, but of the teaching of the Pharisees and Sadducees.
Matthew 16:13 And Jesus came into the regions of Caesarea Philippi and was asking his disciples, saying: Who do men say that I, the Son of man, am?
Matthew 16:14 And they said: Some John the Baptist, and others Elijah, and others Jeremiah or one of the prophets.
Matthew 16:15 He says to them: But you, who do you say that I am?
Matthew 16:16 And Simon Peter answered and said: You are the Christ, the Son of the living God.
Matthew 16:17 And Jesus answered and said to him: Blessed are you, Simon Bar-Jonah, because flesh and blood did not reveal this to you, but my Father who is in the heavens.
Matthew 16:18 And I also say to you that you are Peter, and upon this rock I shall build my church, and the gates of Hades shall not prevail against it.
Matthew 16:19 And I shall give you the keys of the kingdom of the heavens, and whatever you bind upon the earth shall be bound in the heavens, and whatever you loose upon the earth shall be loosed in the heavens.
Matthew 16:20 Then he charged his disciples that they should tell no one that he is Jesus the Christ.
Matthew 16:21 From then Jesus began to show his disciples that he must go to Jerusalem and suffer many things from the elders and chief priests and scribes, and be killed, and be raised on the third day.
Matthew 16:22 And Peter took him aside and began to rebuke him, saying: Mercy to you, Lord; this shall certainly not happen to you.
Matthew 16:23 But he turned and said to Peter: Go behind me, Satan; you are my stumbling block, because you do not mind the things of God, but the things of men.
Matthew 16:24 Then Jesus said to his disciples: If anyone wishes to come behind me, let him deny himself and take up his cross and follow me.
Matthew 16:25 For whoever wishes to save his soul shall lose it, but whoever loses his soul because of me shall find it.
Matthew 16:26 For what does a man profit if he gains the whole world but suffers the loss of his soul? Or what shall a man give in exchange for his soul?
Matthew 16:27 For the Son of man is about to come in the glory of his Father with his angels, and then he shall repay each according to his conduct.
Matthew 16:28 Amen, I say to you: There are some of those standing here who shall certainly not taste death until they see the Son of man coming in his kingdom.

## Chapter 17

Matthew 17:1 And after six days Jesus takes Peter and James and John his brother with him, and brings them up into a high mountain privately.
Matthew 17:2 And he was transfigured before them, and his face shone like the sun, and his garments became white like the light.
Matthew 17:3 And behold, Moses and Elijah appeared to them, conversing with him.
Matthew 17:4 And Peter answered and said to Jesus: Lord, it is good for us to be here; if you wish, let us make three tents here, one for you and one for Moses and one for Elijah.
Matthew 17:5 While he was still speaking, behold, a bright cloud overshadowed them, and behold, a voice from the cloud, saying: This is my beloved Son, in whom I was well pleased; hear him.
Matthew 17:6 And hearing, the disciples fell upon their face and feared exceedingly.
Matthew 17:7 And Jesus approached and touched them and said: Rise, and do not fear.
Matthew 17:8 And lifting their eyes, they saw no one except Jesus alone.
Matthew 17:9 And as they were descending from the mountain, Jesus commanded them, saying: Tell the vision to no one until the Son of man rises from the dead.
Matthew 17:10 And his disciples questioned him, saying: Why, then, do the scribes say that Elijah must come first?
Matthew 17:11 And Jesus answered and said to them: Elijah indeed comes first and shall restore all things.
Matthew 17:12 But I say to you that Elijah already came, and they did not recognize him, but did to him whatever they wished. So also the Son of man is about to suffer by them.
Matthew 17:13 Then the disciples understood that he spoke to them concerning John the Baptist.
Matthew 17:14 And when they came to the crowd, a man approached him, kneeling to him,
Matthew 17:15 and saying: Lord, have mercy on my son, because he is moon-struck and suffers badly; for often he falls into the fire and often into the water.
Matthew 17:16 And I brought him to your disciples, and they were not able to heal him.
Matthew 17:17 And Jesus answered and said: O unbelieving and perverted generation, until when shall I be with you? Until when shall I bear with you? Bring him here to me.
Matthew 17:18 And Jesus rebuked him, and the demon came out from him, and the boy was healed from that hour.
Matthew 17:19 Then the disciples approached Jesus privately and said: Why were we not able to cast it out?
Matthew 17:20 And Jesus said to them: Because of your unbelief. For amen, I say to you: If you have faith like a grain of mustard, you shall say to this mountain: Move from here to there, and it shall move; and nothing shall be impossible for you.
Matthew 17:21 But this kind does not go out except in prayer and fasting.
Matthew 17:22 And while they were staying in Galilee, Jesus said to them: The Son of man is about to be handed over into the hands of men,
Matthew 17:23 and they shall kill him, and on the third day he shall be raised. And they were exceedingly grieved.
Matthew 17:24 And when they came to Capernaum, those receiving the two-drachma payments approached Peter and said: Does your teacher not pay the two drachmas?
Matthew 17:25 He says: Yes. And when he entered the house, Jesus anticipated him, saying: What do you think, Simon? From whom do the kings of the earth receive duties or tax? From their sons or from strangers?
Matthew 17:26 Peter says to him: From strangers. Jesus said to him: Then the sons are free.
Matthew 17:27 But so that we do not make them stumble, go to the sea and cast a hook, and take the first fish that comes up, and opening its mouth you shall find a stater. Take that and give it to them for me and you.

## Chapter 18

Matthew 18:1 In that hour the disciples approached Jesus, saying: Who, then, is greater in the kingdom of the heavens?
Matthew 18:2 And Jesus called a child to him and stood it in their midst,
Matthew 18:3 and said: Amen, I say to you: Unless you turn and become like the children, you shall certainly not enter into the kingdom of the heavens.
Matthew 18:4 Whoever, therefore, humbles himself like this child, this one is the greater in the kingdom of the heavens.
Matthew 18:5 And whoever receives one such child in my name receives me.
Matthew 18:6 But whoever makes one of these little ones who believe in me stumble, it is advantageous for him that a donkey millstone be hung around his neck and he be drowned in the depth of the sea.
Matthew 18:7 Woe to the world because of the stumbling blocks! For it is necessary that the stumbling blocks come; nevertheless, woe to that man through whom the stumbling block comes!
Matthew 18:8 And if your hand or your foot makes you stumble, cut them off and cast them from you. It is good for you to enter into life lame or maimed, rather than having two hands or two feet to be cast into the eternal fire.
Matthew 18:9 And if your eye makes you stumble, take it out and cast it from you. It is good for you to enter into life one-eyed, rather than having two eyes to be cast into the Gehenna of fire.
Matthew 18:10 See that you do not despise one of these little ones; for I say to you that their angels in the heavens continually see the face of my Father who is in the heavens.
Matthew 18:11 For the Son of man came to save what was lost.
Matthew 18:12 What do you think? If a certain man has a hundred sheep, and one of them wanders, does he not leave the ninety-nine upon the mountains and go and seek the wandering one?
Matthew 18:13 And if he happens to find it, amen, I say to you that he rejoices over it more than over the ninety-nine that have not wandered.
Matthew 18:14 So it is not the will before your Father who is in the heavens that one of these little ones perish.
Matthew 18:15 And if your brother sins against you, go and reprove him between you and him alone. If he hears you, you have gained your brother.
Matthew 18:16 But if he does not hear, take with you one or two more, so that upon the mouth of two witnesses or three every word may be established.
Matthew 18:17 And if he refuses to hear them, tell the church; and if he also refuses to hear the church, let him be to you as the gentile and the tax collector.
Matthew 18:18 Amen, I say to you: Whatever you bind upon the earth shall be bound in the heaven, and whatever you loose upon the earth shall be loosed in the heaven.
Matthew 18:19 Again I say to you that if two of you agree upon the earth concerning any matter which they ask, it shall happen for them from my Father who is in the heavens.
Matthew 18:20 For where two or three are gathered into my name, there I am in their midst.
Matthew 18:21 Then Peter approached him and said: Lord, how often shall my brother sin against me and I forgive him? Until seven times?
Matthew 18:22 Jesus says to him: I do not say to you until seven times, but until seventy times seven.
Matthew 18:23 For this reason the kingdom of the heavens was likened to a king who wished to settle an account with his slaves.
Matthew 18:24 And when he began to settle it, one debtor of ten thousand talents was brought to him.
Matthew 18:25 And as he had nothing to repay, his lord commanded that he be sold, and his wife and the children and everything he had, and repayment be made.
Matthew 18:26 Therefore the slave fell down and worshiped him, saying: Lord, be patient with me, and I shall repay you everything.
Matthew 18:27 And the lord of that slave, having compassion, released him and forgave him the loan.
Matthew 18:28 But that slave went out and found one of his fellow slaves who owed him a hundred denarii, and seizing him, he was choking him, saying: Repay me whatever you owe.
Matthew 18:29 Therefore his fellow slave fell at his feet and begged him, saying: Be patient with me, and I shall repay you everything.
Matthew 18:30 But he was unwilling, and went away and cast him into prison until he should repay what was owed.
Matthew 18:31 And his fellow slaves, seeing what happened, were exceedingly grieved, and came and explained to their lord everything that happened.
Matthew 18:32 Then his lord called him to him and says to him: Evil slave, I forgave you all that debt because you begged me.
Matthew 18:33 Should you not also have had mercy on your fellow slave, as I also had mercy on you?
Matthew 18:34 And his lord became angry and handed him over to the torturers until he should repay everything owed to him.
Matthew 18:35 So also my heavenly Father shall do to you, unless you each forgive your brother their trespasses from your hearts.

## Chapter 19

Matthew 19:1 And it happened, when Jesus finished these words, he departed from Galilee and came into the borders of Judea beyond the Jordan.
Matthew 19:2 And many crowds followed him, and he healed them there.
Matthew 19:3 And the Pharisees approached him, testing him and saying to him: Is it lawful for a man to dismiss his wife for every cause?
Matthew 19:4 And he answered and said to them: Have you not read that he who made them from the beginning made them male and female,
Matthew 19:5 and said: Because of this a man shall leave father and mother and be joined to his wife, and the two shall be into one flesh?
Matthew 19:6 So that they are no longer two, but one flesh. What, therefore, God joined together, let man not separate.
Matthew 19:7 They say to him: Why, then, did Moses command to give a document of divorce and dismiss her?
Matthew 19:8 He says to them: Because Moses, in view of your hardness of heart, permitted you to dismiss your wives; but from the beginning it has not been so.
Matthew 19:9 But I say to you that whoever dismisses his wife, except for fornication, and marries another commits adultery, and he who marries a dismissed woman commits adultery.
Matthew 19:10 His disciples say to him: If the case of the man with the wife is so, it is not advantageous to marry.
Matthew 19:11 And he said to them: Not all make room for this word, but those to whom it has been given.
Matthew 19:12 For there are eunuchs who were born so from their mother's womb, and there are eunuchs who were made eunuchs by men, and there are eunuchs who made themselves eunuchs because of the kingdom of the heavens. He who is able to make room, let him make room.
Matthew 19:13 Then children were brought to him, so that he might lay his hands upon them and pray; but the disciples rebuked them.
Matthew 19:14 But Jesus said: Allow the children, and do not hinder them from coming to me, for of such is the kingdom of the heavens.
Matthew 19:15 And laying his hands upon them, he went from there.
Matthew 19:16 And behold, one approached and said to him: Good teacher, what good thing shall I do so that I may have eternal life?
Matthew 19:17 And he said to him: Why do you call me good? No one is good except one, God. But if you wish to enter into life, keep the commandments.
Matthew 19:18 He says to him: Which? And Jesus said: You shall not murder; you shall not commit adultery; you shall not steal; you shall not testify falsely;
Matthew 19:19 honor your father and mother; and: You shall love your neighbor as yourself.
Matthew 19:20 The young man says to him: All these I have kept from my youth; what do I still lack?
Matthew 19:21 Jesus said to him: If you wish to be perfect, go, sell your possessions and give to the poor, and you shall have treasure in heaven; and come, follow me.
Matthew 19:22 But hearing the word, the young man went away grieving, for he had many possessions.
Matthew 19:23 And Jesus said to his disciples: Amen, I say to you that a rich man shall enter into the kingdom of the heavens with difficulty.
Matthew 19:24 And again I say to you: It is easier for a camel to pass through the hole of a needle than for a rich man to enter into the kingdom of God.
Matthew 19:25 And hearing, his disciples were exceedingly astonished, saying: Who, then, can be saved?
Matthew 19:26 And Jesus looked at them and said to them: With men this is impossible, but with God all things are possible.
Matthew 19:27 Then Peter answered and said to him: Behold, we left everything and followed you; what, then, shall there be for us?
Matthew 19:28 And Jesus said to them: Amen, I say to you that you who followed me, in the regeneration, when the Son of man sits upon his throne of glory, you also shall sit upon twelve thrones, judging the twelve tribes of Israel.
Matthew 19:29 And everyone who left houses or brothers or sisters or father or mother or wife or children or fields because of my name shall receive a hundredfold and shall inherit eternal life.
Matthew 19:30 But many first shall be last, and last first.

## Chapter 20

Matthew 20:1 For the kingdom of the heavens is like a master of a house who went out early in the morning to hire workers into his vineyard.
Matthew 20:2 And agreeing with the workers for a denarius for the day, he sent them into his vineyard.
Matthew 20:3 And going out about the third hour, he saw others standing idle in the marketplace,
Matthew 20:4 and said to those: You also go into the vineyard, and whatever is just I shall give you.
Matthew 20:5 And they went away. Again going out about the sixth and ninth hour, he did likewise.
Matthew 20:6 And going out about the eleventh hour, he found others standing idle, and says to them: Why have you stood here idle the whole day?
Matthew 20:7 They say to him: Because no one hired us. He says to them: You also go into the vineyard, and whatever is just you shall receive.
Matthew 20:8 And when evening came, the lord of the vineyard says to his steward: Call the workers and repay them the wage, beginning from the last until the first.
Matthew 20:9 And those of about the eleventh hour came and received a denarius each.
Matthew 20:10 And the first came and supposed that they would receive more, and they also received a denarius each.
Matthew 20:11 And receiving it, they were grumbling against the master of the house,
Matthew 20:12 saying: These last worked one hour, and you made them equal to us who bore the burden of the day and the scorching heat.
Matthew 20:13 And he answered and said to one of them: Friend, I do not wrong you; did you not agree with me for a denarius?
Matthew 20:14 Take what is yours and go; but I wish to give to this last one as also to you.
Matthew 20:15 Or is it not lawful for me to do what I wish with my own things? Is your eye evil because I am good?
Matthew 20:16 So the last shall be first, and the first last; for many are called, but few chosen.
Matthew 20:17 And going up to Jerusalem, Jesus took the twelve disciples privately on the road and said to them:
Matthew 20:18 Behold, we go up to Jerusalem, and the Son of man shall be handed over to the chief priests and scribes, and they shall condemn him to death,
Matthew 20:19 and shall hand him over to the gentiles to mock and scourge and crucify, and on the third day he shall rise.
Matthew 20:20 Then the mother of the sons of Zebedee approached him with her sons, worshiping and asking something from him.
Matthew 20:21 And he said to her: What do you wish? She says to him: Say that these two sons of mine may sit, one at your right and one at your left, in your kingdom.
Matthew 20:22 And Jesus answered and said: You do not know what you ask. Are you able to drink the cup which I am about to drink, and to be baptized with the baptism with which I am baptized? They say to him: We are able.
Matthew 20:23 And he says to them: My cup indeed you shall drink, and with the baptism with which I am baptized you shall be baptized; but to sit at my right and at my left is not mine to give, but to those for whom it has been prepared by my Father.
Matthew 20:24 And hearing, the ten were indignant concerning the two brothers.
Matthew 20:25 And Jesus called them to him and said: You know that the rulers of the nations lord over them, and the great exercise authority over them.
Matthew 20:26 But it shall not be so among you; rather, whoever wishes to become great among you, let him be your servant.
Matthew 20:27 And whoever wishes to be first among you, let him be your slave,
Matthew 20:28 just as the Son of man did not come to be served, but to serve, and to give his soul as a ransom for many.
Matthew 20:29 And as they were going out from Jericho, a great crowd followed him.
Matthew 20:30 And behold, two blind men sitting beside the road, hearing that Jesus was passing by, cried out, saying: Have mercy on us, Lord, Son of David.
Matthew 20:31 And the crowd rebuked them so that they should be silent; but they cried out more, saying: Have mercy on us, Lord, Son of David.
Matthew 20:32 And Jesus stood and called them and said: What do you wish me to do for you?
Matthew 20:33 They say to him: Lord, that our eyes may be opened.
Matthew 20:34 And Jesus had compassion and touched their eyes, and immediately their eyes saw again, and they followed him.

## Chapter 21

Matthew 21:1 And when they drew near to Jerusalem and came to Bethphage, toward the mountain of Olives, then Jesus sent two disciples,
Matthew 21:2 saying to them: Go into the village opposite you, and immediately you shall find a donkey bound and a colt with her; loose them and bring them to me.
Matthew 21:3 And if anyone says anything to you, you shall say: Their Lord has need of them; and immediately he shall send them.
Matthew 21:4 And this whole thing has happened so that what was spoken through the prophet might be fulfilled, saying:
Matthew 21:5 Say to the daughter of Zion: Behold, your king comes to you, meek and mounted upon a donkey and a colt, the son of a beast of burden.
Matthew 21:6 And the disciples went and did as Jesus commanded them,
Matthew 21:7 and brought the donkey and the colt, and laid their garments upon them, and he sat upon them.
Matthew 21:8 And the very great crowd spread their own garments in the road, and others were cutting branches from the trees and spreading them in the road.
Matthew 21:9 And the crowds going before and those following were crying out, saying: Hosanna to the Son of David! Blessed is he who comes in the name of the Lord! Hosanna in the highest!
Matthew 21:10 And when he entered Jerusalem, the whole city was shaken, saying: Who is this?
Matthew 21:11 And the crowds were saying: This is Jesus the prophet, the one from Nazareth of Galilee.
Matthew 21:12 And Jesus entered into the temple of God and cast out all those selling and buying in the temple, and overturned the tables of the money changers and the seats of those selling the doves.
Matthew 21:13 And he says to them: It is written: My house shall be called a house of prayer; but you made it a cave of robbers.
Matthew 21:14 And blind and lame people approached him in the temple, and he healed them.
Matthew 21:15 But the chief priests and the scribes, seeing the wonderful things he did and the children crying out in the temple and saying: Hosanna to the Son of David, were indignant,
Matthew 21:16 and said to him: Do you hear what these say? And Jesus says to them: Yes; have you never read that out of the mouth of infants and nursing children you prepared praise?
Matthew 21:17 And leaving them, he went out of the city to Bethany and lodged there.
Matthew 21:18 And in the morning, returning to the city, he was hungry.
Matthew 21:19 And seeing one fig tree upon the road, he came to it and found nothing on it except leaves only, and says to it: Let fruit no longer come from you forever. And immediately the fig tree withered.
Matthew 21:20 And seeing, the disciples marveled, saying: How did the fig tree wither immediately?
Matthew 21:21 And Jesus answered and said to them: Amen, I say to you: If you have faith and do not doubt, you shall do not only the thing of the fig tree, but even if you say to this mountain: Be lifted and cast into the sea, it shall happen.
Matthew 21:22 And all things, whatever you ask in prayer, believing, you shall receive.
Matthew 21:23 And when he came into the temple, the chief priests and the elders of the people approached him as he taught, saying: By what authority do you do these things? And who gave you this authority?
Matthew 21:24 And Jesus answered and said to them: I also shall ask you one word, which, if you tell me, I also shall tell you by what authority I do these things.
Matthew 21:25 The baptism of John, from where was it? From heaven or from men? And they were reasoning among themselves, saying: If we say: From heaven, he shall say to us: Why, then, did you not believe him?
Matthew 21:26 But if we say: From men, we fear the crowd, for all hold John as a prophet.
Matthew 21:27 And answering Jesus, they said: We do not know. He also said to them: Neither do I tell you by what authority I do these things.
Matthew 21:28 But what do you think? A man had two children, and approaching the first, he said: Child, go, work today in my vineyard.
Matthew 21:29 And he answered and said: I do not wish to. But afterward he regretted it and went.
Matthew 21:30 And approaching the second, he said likewise. And he answered and said: I, lord; and did not go.
Matthew 21:31 Which of the two did the will of the father? They say to him: The first. Jesus says to them: Amen, I say to you that the tax collectors and the prostitutes go before you into the kingdom of God.
Matthew 21:32 For John came to you in a way of righteousness, and you did not believe him; but the tax collectors and the prostitutes believed him. But you, seeing, did not afterward regret it so as to believe him.
Matthew 21:33 Hear another parable: There was a certain master of a house who planted a vineyard and put a fence around it and dug a winepress in it and built a tower, and leased it to farmers and went abroad.
Matthew 21:34 And when the season of the fruits drew near, he sent his slaves to the farmers to receive his fruits.
Matthew 21:35 And the farmers took his slaves, and beat one, and killed another, and stoned another.
Matthew 21:36 Again he sent other slaves, more than the first, and they did to them likewise.
Matthew 21:37 But afterward he sent his son to them, saying: They shall respect my son.
Matthew 21:38 But the farmers, seeing the son, said among themselves: This is the heir; come, let us kill him and take possession of his inheritance.
Matthew 21:39 And taking him, they cast him outside the vineyard and killed him.
Matthew 21:40 Therefore, when the lord of the vineyard comes, what shall he do to those farmers?
Matthew 21:41 They say to him: He shall destroy those evil men evilly, and shall lease the vineyard to other farmers, who shall repay him the fruits in their seasons.
Matthew 21:42 Jesus says to them: Have you never read in the Scriptures: The stone which the builders rejected, this became the head of the corner; this came from the Lord, and it is marvelous in our eyes?
Matthew 21:43 For this reason I say to you that the kingdom of God shall be taken from you and given to a nation producing its fruits.
Matthew 21:44 And he who falls upon this stone shall be shattered, but upon whomever it falls, it shall crush him.
Matthew 21:45 And the chief priests and the Pharisees, hearing his parables, knew that he speaks concerning them.
Matthew 21:46 And seeking to seize him, they feared the crowds, since they held him as a prophet.

## Chapter 22

Matthew 22:1 And Jesus answered and again spoke to them in parables, saying:
Matthew 22:2 The kingdom of the heavens was likened to a king who made a wedding feast for his son,
Matthew 22:3 and sent his slaves to call those invited to the wedding feast, and they were unwilling to come.
Matthew 22:4 Again he sent other slaves, saying: Tell those invited: Behold, I prepared my meal; my bulls and the fattened beasts are slaughtered, and everything is ready; come to the wedding feast.
Matthew 22:5 But they disregarded it and went away, one to his own field, another to his trade.
Matthew 22:6 And the rest seized his slaves and mistreated and killed them.
Matthew 22:7 And the king heard and became angry, and sending his armies, he destroyed those murderers and burned their city.
Matthew 22:8 Then he says to his slaves: The wedding feast indeed is ready, but those invited were not worthy.
Matthew 22:9 Therefore go to the outlets of the roads, and as many as you find, invite to the wedding feast.
Matthew 22:10 And those slaves went out into the roads and gathered all whom they found, both evil and good, and the wedding feast was filled with those reclining.
Matthew 22:11 And the king entered to look upon those reclining and saw there a man not clothed in a wedding garment.
Matthew 22:12 And he says to him: Friend, how did you enter here without having a wedding garment? And he was silenced.
Matthew 22:13 Then the king said to the servants: Bind his feet and hands, take him away and cast him into the outer darkness. There shall be the weeping and the grinding of teeth.
Matthew 22:14 For many are called, but few chosen.
Matthew 22:15 Then the Pharisees went and took counsel so that they might trap him in a word.
Matthew 22:16 And they send their disciples to him with the Herodians, saying: Teacher, we know that you are true and teach the way of God in truth, and you care concerning no one, for you do not look upon the face of men.
Matthew 22:17 Tell us, therefore, what you think: Is it lawful to give tax to Caesar or not?
Matthew 22:18 And Jesus knew their wickedness and said: Why do you test me, hypocrites?
Matthew 22:19 Show me the coin of the tax. And they brought him a denarius.
Matthew 22:20 And he says to them: Whose is this image and the inscription?
Matthew 22:21 They say to him: Caesar's. Then he says to them: Therefore repay the things of Caesar to Caesar, and the things of God to God.
Matthew 22:22 And hearing, they marveled, and leaving him, they went away.
Matthew 22:23 On that day Sadducees approached him, who say there is no resurrection, and questioned him,
Matthew 22:24 saying: Teacher, Moses said: If anyone dies without having children, his brother shall marry his wife and raise up seed for his brother.
Matthew 22:25 And there were seven brothers among us, and the first married and died, and having no seed, left his wife to his brother.
Matthew 22:26 Likewise also the second and the third, until the seven.
Matthew 22:27 And last of all the woman also died.
Matthew 22:28 In the resurrection, therefore, whose wife of the seven shall she be? For all had her.
Matthew 22:29 And Jesus answered and said to them: You wander, not knowing the Scriptures nor the power of God.
Matthew 22:30 For in the resurrection they neither marry nor are given in marriage, but are like angels of God in heaven.
Matthew 22:31 But concerning the resurrection of the dead, have you not read what was spoken to you by God, saying:
Matthew 22:32 I am the God of Abraham and the God of Isaac and the God of Jacob? God is not God of the dead, but of the living.
Matthew 22:33 And hearing, the crowds were astonished at his teaching.
Matthew 22:34 And the Pharisees, hearing that he silenced the Sadducees, gathered together.
Matthew 22:35 And one of them, a lawyer, questioned him, testing him and saying:
Matthew 22:36 Teacher, which commandment is great in the law?
Matthew 22:37 And Jesus said to him: You shall love the Lord your God with your whole heart and with your whole soul and with your whole mind.
Matthew 22:38 This is the first and great commandment.
Matthew 22:39 And a second is like it: You shall love your neighbor as yourself.
Matthew 22:40 On these two commandments hang the whole law and the prophets.
Matthew 22:41 And while the Pharisees were gathered, Jesus questioned them,
Matthew 22:42 saying: What do you think concerning the Christ? Whose son is he? They say to him: David's.
Matthew 22:43 He says to them: How, then, does David in spirit call him Lord, saying:
Matthew 22:44 The Lord said to my Lord: Sit at my right until I place your enemies as a footstool of your feet?
Matthew 22:45 If, therefore, David calls him Lord, how is he his son?
Matthew 22:46 And no one was able to answer him a word, nor did anyone dare from that day to question him any longer.

## Chapter 23

Matthew 23:1 Then Jesus spoke to the crowds and to his disciples,
Matthew 23:2 saying: The scribes and the Pharisees sat upon the seat of Moses.
Matthew 23:3 Therefore everything, whatever they tell you to keep, keep and do; but do not do according to their works, for they say and do not do.
Matthew 23:4 For they bind heavy burdens and hard to bear, and lay them upon the shoulders of men, but with their finger they are unwilling to move them.
Matthew 23:5 And all their works they do to be seen by men; and they broaden their phylacteries and enlarge the fringes of their garments.
Matthew 23:6 And they love the first reclining place at the suppers and the first seats in the synagogues,
Matthew 23:7 and the greetings in the marketplaces, and to be called by men: Rabbi, Rabbi.
Matthew 23:8 But you, do not be called Rabbi, for one is your guide, the Christ, and you are all brothers.
Matthew 23:9 And do not call anyone your father upon the earth, for one is your Father, the one in the heavens.
Matthew 23:10 Nor be called guides, for one is your guide, the Christ.
Matthew 23:11 But the greater of you shall be your servant.
Matthew 23:12 And whoever exalts himself shall be humbled, and whoever humbles himself shall be exalted.
Matthew 23:13 But woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites, because you devour the houses of the widows, and with a pretext pray long; for this reason you shall receive greater judgment.
Matthew 23:14 Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites, because you shut the kingdom of the heavens before men; for you do not enter, nor do you allow those entering to enter.
Matthew 23:15 Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites, because you go around the sea and the dry land to make one proselyte, and when he becomes one, you make him a son of Gehenna twice as much as you.
Matthew 23:16 Woe to you, blind guides, who say: Whoever swears by the sanctuary, it is nothing; but whoever swears by the gold of the sanctuary is obligated.
Matthew 23:17 Fools and blind men! For which is greater, the gold or the sanctuary sanctifying the gold?
Matthew 23:18 And: Whoever swears by the altar, it is nothing; but whoever swears by the gift upon it is obligated.
Matthew 23:19 Fools and blind men! For which is greater, the gift or the altar sanctifying the gift?
Matthew 23:20 Therefore he who swears by the altar swears by it and by all the things upon it.
Matthew 23:21 And he who swears by the sanctuary swears by it and by the one dwelling in it.
Matthew 23:22 And he who swears by the heaven swears by the throne of God and by the one sitting upon it.
Matthew 23:23 Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites, because you tithe the mint and the dill and the cumin, and left the weightier things of the law: judgment and mercy and faith. These you ought to have done, and not leave those.
Matthew 23:24 Blind guides, straining out the gnat but swallowing the camel!
Matthew 23:25 Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites, because you cleanse the outside of the cup and the dish, but inside they are full from plunder and lack of self-control.
Matthew 23:26 Blind Pharisee, cleanse first the inside of the cup and the dish, so that their outside also may become clean.
Matthew 23:27 Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites, because you resemble whitewashed tombs, which indeed appear beautiful outside, but inside are full of bones of the dead and all uncleanness.
Matthew 23:28 So also you indeed appear righteous to men outside, but inside you are full of hypocrisy and lawlessness.
Matthew 23:29 Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites, because you build the tombs of the prophets and adorn the monuments of the righteous,
Matthew 23:30 and say: If we had been in the days of our fathers, we would not have been their partners in the blood of the prophets.
Matthew 23:31 So that you testify to yourselves that you are sons of those who murdered the prophets.
Matthew 23:32 And you, fill up the measure of your fathers.
Matthew 23:33 Serpents, offspring of vipers, how shall you flee from the judgment of Gehenna?
Matthew 23:34 For this reason, behold, I send to you prophets and wise men and scribes, and some of them you shall kill and crucify, and some of them you shall scourge in your synagogues and persecute from city to city,
Matthew 23:35 so that upon you may come all righteous blood poured out upon the earth, from the blood of righteous Abel until the blood of Zechariah son of Barachiah, whom you murdered between the sanctuary and the altar.
Matthew 23:36 Amen, I say to you: All these things shall come upon this generation.
Matthew 23:37 Jerusalem, Jerusalem, who kills the prophets and stones those sent to her, how often I wished to gather your children together in the manner that a hen gathers her chicks together under her wings, and you were unwilling!
Matthew 23:38 Behold, your house is left to you deserted.
Matthew 23:39 For I say to you: You shall certainly not see me from now until you say: Blessed is he who comes in the name of the Lord.

## Chapter 24

Matthew 24:1 And Jesus went out and was going away from the temple, and his disciples approached to show him the buildings of the temple.
Matthew 24:2 And Jesus said to them: Do you not see all these things? Amen, I say to you: There shall certainly not be left here a stone upon a stone which shall certainly not be demolished.
Matthew 24:3 And while he sat upon the mountain of Olives, the disciples approached him privately, saying: Tell us, when shall these things be, and what is the sign of your coming and of the completion of the age?
Matthew 24:4 And Jesus answered and said to them: See that no one leads you astray.
