Matthew 24:5 For many shall come in my name, saying: I am the Christ, and shall lead many astray.
Matthew 24:6 And you shall be about to hear wars and reports of wars; see that you are not alarmed, for all must happen, but the end is not yet.
Matthew 24:7 For nation shall rise against nation and kingdom against kingdom, and there shall be famines and pestilences and earthquakes in places.
Matthew 24:8 And all these things are the beginning of birth pains.
Matthew 24:9 Then they shall hand you over to affliction and shall kill you, and you shall be hated by all the nations because of my name.
Matthew 24:10 And then many shall be made to stumble, and shall hand one another over and hate one another.
Matthew 24:11 And many false prophets shall rise and shall lead many astray.
Matthew 24:12 And because lawlessness is multiplied, the love of the many shall grow cold.
Matthew 24:13 But he who endures until the end, this one shall be saved.
Matthew 24:14 And this good news of the kingdom shall be proclaimed in the whole inhabited world as a testimony to all the nations, and then the end shall come.
Matthew 24:15 Therefore, when you see the abomination of desolation, spoken of through Daniel the prophet, standing in a holy place, let the reader perceive,
Matthew 24:16 then let those in Judea flee to the mountains.
Matthew 24:17 Let the one upon the roof not descend to take anything out of his house.
Matthew 24:18 And let the one in the field not turn back to take his garments.
Matthew 24:19 And woe to those having in the womb and those nursing in those days!
Matthew 24:20 And pray that your flight may not happen in winter nor on a Sabbath.
Matthew 24:21 For then there shall be great affliction, such as has not happened from the beginning of the world until now, nor shall certainly happen.
Matthew 24:22 And unless those days were shortened, no flesh would be saved; but because of the chosen, those days shall be shortened.
Matthew 24:23 Then if anyone says to you: Behold, here is the Christ, or: Here, do not believe.
Matthew 24:24 For false christs and false prophets shall rise and shall give great signs and wonders, so as to lead astray, if possible, even the chosen.
Matthew 24:25 Behold, I have told you beforehand.
Matthew 24:26 Therefore, if they say to you: Behold, he is in the desert, do not go out; behold, in the inner rooms, do not believe.
Matthew 24:27 For just as the lightning comes out from the east and appears until the west, so also shall be the coming of the Son of man.
Matthew 24:28 For wherever the corpse may be, there the eagles shall be gathered.
Matthew 24:29 And immediately after the affliction of those days the sun shall be darkened, and the moon shall not give its light, and the stars shall fall from the heaven, and the powers of the heavens shall be shaken.
Matthew 24:30 And then the sign of the Son of man shall appear in the heaven, and then all the tribes of the earth shall mourn, and they shall see the Son of man coming upon the clouds of the heaven with power and much glory.
Matthew 24:31 And he shall send his angels with a trumpet of a great voice, and they shall gather his chosen together from the four winds, from the extremities of the heavens until their extremities.
Matthew 24:32 And learn the parable from the fig tree: When its branch already becomes tender and puts forth the leaves, you know that summer is near.
Matthew 24:33 So also you, when you see all these things, know that it is near, at the doors.
Matthew 24:34 Amen, I say to you: This generation shall certainly not pass until all these things happen.
Matthew 24:35 The heaven and the earth shall pass away, but my words shall certainly not pass away.
Matthew 24:36 But concerning that day and the hour no one knows, not even the angels of the heavens, except my Father alone.
Matthew 24:37 And just as the days of Noah, so also shall be the coming of the Son of man.
Matthew 24:38 For just as they were in the days before the flood, eating and drinking, marrying and giving in marriage, until the day on which Noah entered into the ark,
Matthew 24:39 and did not know until the flood came and took all away, so also shall be the coming of the Son of man.
Matthew 24:40 Then two shall be in the field; the one is taken along and the one is left.
Matthew 24:41 Two women grinding at the mill; one is taken along and one is left.
Matthew 24:42 Therefore keep watch, because you do not know at what hour your Lord comes.
Matthew 24:43 But know this, that if the master of the house had known in which watch the thief comes, he would have kept watch and would not have allowed his house to be dug through.
Matthew 24:44 For this reason you also become ready, because at an hour you do not think, the Son of man comes.
Matthew 24:45 Who, then, is the faithful and prudent slave whom his lord appointed over his household to give them food in season?
Matthew 24:46 Blessed is that slave whom his lord, coming, shall find doing so.
Matthew 24:47 Amen, I say to you that he shall appoint him over all his possessions.
Matthew 24:48 But if that evil slave says in his heart: My lord delays to come,
Matthew 24:49 and begins to beat the fellow slaves, and to eat and drink with those who are drunk,
Matthew 24:50 the lord of that slave shall come on a day which he does not expect and at an hour which he does not know,
Matthew 24:51 and shall cut him in two and place his portion with the hypocrites. There shall be the weeping and the grinding of teeth.

## Chapter 25

Matthew 25:1 Then the kingdom of the heavens shall be likened to ten virgins who took their lamps and went out to meet the bridegroom.
Matthew 25:2 And five of them were prudent, and the five foolish.
Matthew 25:3 Those who were foolish took their own lamps and did not take oil with themselves.
Matthew 25:4 But the prudent took oil in their vessels with their lamps.
Matthew 25:5 And while the bridegroom delayed, all grew drowsy and slept.
Matthew 25:6 And in the middle of the night a cry has arisen: Behold, the bridegroom comes; go out to meet him.
Matthew 25:7 Then all those virgins rose and put their lamps in order.
Matthew 25:8 And the foolish said to the prudent: Give us from your oil, because our lamps are going out.
Matthew 25:9 But the prudent answered, saying: Lest it not suffice for us and you; go rather to those selling and buy for yourselves.
Matthew 25:10 And while they were going away to buy, the bridegroom came, and those ready entered with him into the wedding feast, and the door was shut.
Matthew 25:11 And afterward the remaining virgins also come, saying: Lord, Lord, open to us.
Matthew 25:12 But he answered and said: Amen, I say to you: I do not know you.
Matthew 25:13 Therefore keep watch, because you do not know the day nor the hour in which the Son of man comes.
Matthew 25:14 For just as a man going abroad called his own slaves and handed his possessions over to them,
Matthew 25:15 and to one he gave five talents, and to another two, and to another one, to each according to his own ability, and immediately went abroad.
Matthew 25:16 And the one who received the five talents went and worked with them and made another five talents.
Matthew 25:17 Likewise also the one with the two, he also gained another two.
Matthew 25:18 But the one who received the one went away and dug in the earth and hid his lord's silver.
Matthew 25:19 And after much time the lord of those slaves comes and settles an account with them.
Matthew 25:20 And the one who received the five talents approached and brought another five talents, saying: Lord, you handed over five talents to me; see, I gained another five talents upon them.
Matthew 25:21 And his lord said to him: Well, good and faithful slave; over few things you were faithful, over many I shall appoint you. Enter into the joy of your lord.
Matthew 25:22 And the one who received the two talents also approached and said: Lord, you handed over two talents to me; see, I gained another two talents upon them.
Matthew 25:23 His lord said to him: Well, good and faithful slave; over few things you were faithful, over many I shall appoint you. Enter into the joy of your lord.
Matthew 25:24 And the one who had received the one talent also approached and said: Lord, I knew you, that you are a hard man, harvesting where you did not sow and gathering from where you did not scatter.
Matthew 25:25 And fearing, I went away and hid your talent in the earth; see, you have what is yours.
Matthew 25:26 And his lord answered and said to him: Evil and lazy slave, you knew that I harvest where I did not sow and gather from where I did not scatter.
Matthew 25:27 Therefore you ought to have put my silver with the bankers, and coming, I would have received what is mine with interest.
Matthew 25:28 Therefore take the talent from him and give it to the one having the ten talents.
Matthew 25:29 For to everyone who has it shall be given, and he shall have abundance; but from the one who does not have, even what he has shall be taken from him.
Matthew 25:30 And cast the useless slave into the outer darkness. There shall be the weeping and the grinding of teeth.
Matthew 25:31 And when the Son of man comes in his glory and all the holy angels with him, then he shall sit upon his throne of glory.
Matthew 25:32 And all the nations shall be gathered before him, and he shall separate them from one another, just as the shepherd separates the sheep from the goats.
Matthew 25:33 And he shall stand the sheep at his right, but the little goats at the left.
Matthew 25:34 Then the king shall say to those at his right: Come, those blessed by my Father, inherit the kingdom prepared for you from the foundation of the world.
Matthew 25:35 For I was hungry and you gave me to eat; I thirsted and you gave me to drink; I was a stranger and you gathered me in;
Matthew 25:36 naked and you clothed me; I was sick and you visited me; I was in prison and you came to me.
Matthew 25:37 Then the righteous shall answer him, saying: Lord, when did we see you hungry and feed you, or thirsting and give you to drink?
Matthew 25:38 And when did we see you a stranger and gather you in, or naked and clothe you?
Matthew 25:39 And when did we see you sick or in prison and come to you?
Matthew 25:40 And the king shall answer and say to them: Amen, I say to you: Insofar as you did it to one of these least brothers of mine, you did it to me.
Matthew 25:41 Then he shall also say to those at the left: Go from me, those cursed, into the eternal fire prepared for the devil and his angels.
Matthew 25:42 For I was hungry and you did not give me to eat; I thirsted and you did not give me to drink;
Matthew 25:43 I was a stranger and you did not gather me in; naked and you did not clothe me; sick and in prison and you did not visit me.
Matthew 25:44 Then they also shall answer him, saying: Lord, when did we see you hungry or thirsting or a stranger or naked or sick or in prison, and did not serve you?
Matthew 25:45 Then he shall answer them, saying: Amen, I say to you: Insofar as you did not do it to one of these least, neither did you do it to me.
Matthew 25:46 And these shall go away into eternal punishment, but the righteous into eternal life.

## Chapter 26

Matthew 26:1 And it happened, when Jesus finished all these words, he said to his disciples:
Matthew 26:2 You know that after two days the Passover takes place, and the Son of man is handed over to be crucified.
Matthew 26:3 Then the chief priests and the scribes and the elders of the people gathered into the courtyard of the high priest called Caiaphas,
Matthew 26:4 and took counsel so that they might seize Jesus by deceit and kill him.
Matthew 26:5 But they were saying: Not during the feast, so that an uproar may not arise among the people.
Matthew 26:6 And while Jesus was in Bethany in the house of Simon the leper,
Matthew 26:7 a woman approached him, having an alabaster vessel of very costly ointment, and poured it upon his head as he reclined.
Matthew 26:8 But his disciples, seeing, were indignant, saying: Why this waste?
Matthew 26:9 For this ointment could have been sold for much and given to the poor.
Matthew 26:10 And Jesus knew and said to them: Why do you give troubles to the woman? For she worked a good work toward me.
Matthew 26:11 For you always have the poor with yourselves, but you do not always have me.
Matthew 26:12 For she, in putting this ointment upon my body, did it to bury me.
Matthew 26:13 Amen, I say to you: Wherever this good news is proclaimed in the whole world, what she did shall also be spoken of as a memorial of her.
Matthew 26:14 Then one of the twelve, called Judas Iscariot, went to the chief priests,
Matthew 26:15 and said: What do you wish to give me, and I shall hand him over to you? And they weighed out thirty silver pieces for him.
Matthew 26:16 And from then he was seeking an opportunity to hand him over.
Matthew 26:17 And on the first day of the unleavened bread, the disciples approached Jesus, saying to him: Where do you wish us to prepare for you to eat the Passover?
Matthew 26:18 And he said: Go into the city to a certain man and tell him: The teacher says: My time is near; with you I hold the Passover with my disciples.
Matthew 26:19 And the disciples did as Jesus directed them and prepared the Passover.
Matthew 26:20 And when evening came, he was reclining with the twelve.
Matthew 26:21 And while they were eating, he said: Amen, I say to you that one of you shall hand me over.
Matthew 26:22 And being exceedingly grieved, each of them began to say to him: Surely it is not I, Lord?
Matthew 26:23 And he answered and said: The one who dipped his hand with me in the dish, this one shall hand me over.
Matthew 26:24 The Son of man indeed goes as it is written concerning him, but woe to that man through whom the Son of man is handed over! It was good for him if that man had not been born.
Matthew 26:25 And Judas, the one handing him over, answered and said: Surely it is not I, Rabbi? He says to him: You said it.
Matthew 26:26 And while they were eating, Jesus took the bread and blessed and broke it and was giving it to the disciples, and said: Take, eat; this is my body.
Matthew 26:27 And taking the cup and giving thanks, he gave it to them, saying: Drink from it, all of you.
Matthew 26:28 For this is my blood, that of the new covenant, poured out concerning many for forgiveness of sins.
Matthew 26:29 But I say to you that I shall certainly not drink from now of this produce of the vine until that day when I drink it new with you in the kingdom of my Father.
Matthew 26:30 And having sung a hymn, they went out to the mountain of Olives.
Matthew 26:31 Then Jesus says to them: All of you shall be made to stumble at me in this night, for it is written: I shall strike the shepherd, and the sheep of the flock shall be scattered.
Matthew 26:32 But after I am raised, I shall go before you into Galilee.
Matthew 26:33 And Peter answered and said to him: Even if all shall be made to stumble at you, I shall never be made to stumble.
Matthew 26:34 Jesus said to him: Amen, I say to you that in this night, before a rooster calls, you shall deny me three times.
Matthew 26:35 Peter says to him: Even if I must die with you, I shall certainly not deny you. Likewise also all the disciples said.
Matthew 26:36 Then Jesus comes with them into a place called Gethsemane and says to the disciples: Sit here until I go and pray there.
Matthew 26:37 And taking Peter and the two sons of Zebedee with him, he began to be grieved and distressed.
Matthew 26:38 Then he says to them: My soul is exceedingly sorrowful until death; remain here and keep watch with me.
Matthew 26:39 And going forward a little, he fell upon his face, praying and saying: My Father, if it is possible, let this cup pass from me; nevertheless, not as I wish, but as you.
Matthew 26:40 And he comes to the disciples and finds them sleeping, and says to Peter: So, were you not strong enough to keep watch with me one hour?
Matthew 26:41 Keep watch and pray so that you may not enter into temptation; the spirit indeed is willing, but the flesh weak.
Matthew 26:42 Again, going away a second time, he prayed, saying: My Father, if this cup cannot pass from me unless I drink it, let your will happen.
Matthew 26:43 And coming, he finds them sleeping again, for their eyes were weighed down.
Matthew 26:44 And leaving them, he went away and again prayed a third time, saying the same word.
Matthew 26:45 Then he comes to his disciples and says to them: Sleep the rest and take your rest; behold, the hour has drawn near, and the Son of man is handed over into the hands of sinners.
Matthew 26:46 Rise, let us go; behold, the one handing me over has drawn near.
Matthew 26:47 And while he was still speaking, behold, Judas, one of the twelve, came, and with him a great crowd with swords and clubs from the chief priests and elders of the people.
Matthew 26:48 And the one handing him over gave them a sign, saying: Whomever I kiss, he is the one; seize him.
Matthew 26:49 And immediately approaching Jesus, he said: Greetings, Rabbi; and kissed him fervently.
Matthew 26:50 And Jesus said to him: Friend, for what are you here? Then they approached and laid their hands upon Jesus and seized him.
Matthew 26:51 And behold, one of those with Jesus stretched out his hand and drew his sword, and striking the slave of the high priest, took off his ear.
Matthew 26:52 Then Jesus says to him: Return your sword to its place, for all who take a sword shall perish by a sword.
Matthew 26:53 Or do you think that I cannot now appeal to my Father, and he shall provide me more than twelve legions of angels?
Matthew 26:54 How, then, should the Scriptures be fulfilled, that it must happen so?
Matthew 26:55 In that hour Jesus said to the crowds: As against a robber you came out with swords and clubs to arrest me. Daily I sat with you teaching in the temple, and you did not seize me.
Matthew 26:56 But this whole thing has happened so that the Scriptures of the prophets might be fulfilled. Then all the disciples left him and fled.
Matthew 26:57 And those who seized Jesus led him away to Caiaphas the high priest, where the scribes and the elders were gathered.
Matthew 26:58 And Peter was following him from afar until the courtyard of the high priest, and entering inside, he was sitting with the attendants to see the end.
Matthew 26:59 And the chief priests and the elders and the whole council were seeking false testimony against Jesus so that they might put him to death,
Matthew 26:60 and did not find it; and though many false witnesses approached, they did not find it.
Matthew 26:61 But afterward two false witnesses approached and said: This man said: I am able to demolish the sanctuary of God and to build it through three days.
Matthew 26:62 And the high priest stood up and said to him: Do you answer nothing? What do these testify against you?
Matthew 26:63 But Jesus was silent. And the high priest answered and said to him: I adjure you by the living God that you tell us whether you are the Christ, the Son of God.
Matthew 26:64 Jesus says to him: You said it. Nevertheless, I say to you: From now you shall see the Son of man sitting at the right of the Power and coming upon the clouds of the heaven.
Matthew 26:65 Then the high priest tore his garments, saying: He blasphemed! What further need do we have of witnesses? See, now you heard his blasphemy.
Matthew 26:66 What do you think? And they answered and said: He is liable to death.
Matthew 26:67 Then they spat into his face and struck him with fists, and others slapped him,
Matthew 26:68 saying: Prophesy to us, Christ; who is the one who struck you?
Matthew 26:69 And Peter was sitting outside in the courtyard, and one servant girl approached him, saying: You also were with Jesus the Galilean.
Matthew 26:70 But he denied before all, saying: I do not know what you say.
Matthew 26:71 And when he went out to the gateway, another saw him and says to those there: This man also was with Jesus the Nazarene.
Matthew 26:72 And again he denied with an oath: I do not know the man.
Matthew 26:73 And after a little while those standing approached and said to Peter: Truly you also are one of them, for even your speech makes you evident.
Matthew 26:74 Then he began to curse and swear: I do not know the man. And immediately a rooster called.
Matthew 26:75 And Peter remembered the saying of Jesus, who had said to him: Before a rooster calls, you shall deny me three times. And going outside, he wept bitterly.

## Chapter 27

Matthew 27:1 And when morning came, all the chief priests and the elders of the people took counsel against Jesus so as to put him to death.
Matthew 27:2 And binding him, they led him away and handed him over to Pontius Pilate the governor.
Matthew 27:3 Then Judas, the one handing him over, seeing that he was condemned, regretted it and returned the thirty silver pieces to the chief priests and the elders,
Matthew 27:4 saying: I sinned, handing over innocent blood. And they said: What is that to us? You shall see to it.
Matthew 27:5 And throwing the silver pieces in the sanctuary, he withdrew, and going away, he hanged himself.
Matthew 27:6 And the chief priests took the silver pieces and said: It is not lawful to put them into the treasury, since it is the price of blood.
Matthew 27:7 And taking counsel, they bought with them the potter's field for burial for strangers.
Matthew 27:8 Therefore that field was called Field of Blood until today.
Matthew 27:9 Then what was spoken through Jeremiah the prophet was fulfilled, saying: And they took the thirty silver pieces, the price of the one priced, whom they priced from the sons of Israel,
Matthew 27:10 and gave them for the potter's field, as the Lord directed me.
Matthew 27:11 And Jesus stood before the governor, and the governor questioned him, saying: Are you the king of the Jews? And Jesus said to him: You say it.
Matthew 27:12 And while he was accused by the chief priests and the elders, he answered nothing.
Matthew 27:13 Then Pilate says to him: Do you not hear how many things they testify against you?
Matthew 27:14 And he did not answer him concerning even one word, so that the governor marveled exceedingly.
Matthew 27:15 And at a feast the governor was accustomed to release to the crowd one prisoner whom they wished.
Matthew 27:16 And they then had a notable prisoner called Barabbas.
Matthew 27:17 Therefore, when they gathered, Pilate said to them: Whom do you wish me to release to you, Barabbas or Jesus called Christ?
Matthew 27:18 For he knew that because of envy they handed him over.
Matthew 27:19 And while he sat upon the judgment seat, his wife sent to him, saying: Nothing between you and that righteous man, for I suffered many things today in a dream because of him.
Matthew 27:20 But the chief priests and the elders persuaded the crowds that they should ask for Barabbas, but destroy Jesus.
Matthew 27:21 And the governor answered and said to them: Which of the two do you wish me to release to you? And they said: Barabbas.
Matthew 27:22 Pilate says to them: What, then, shall I do with Jesus called Christ? They all say to him: Let him be crucified.
Matthew 27:23 And the governor said: For what evil did he do? But they cried out exceedingly, saying: Let him be crucified.
Matthew 27:24 And Pilate, seeing that he profits nothing, but rather an uproar arises, took water and washed his hands before the crowd, saying: I am innocent of the blood of this righteous man; you shall see to it.
Matthew 27:25 And all the people answered and said: His blood upon us and upon our children.
Matthew 27:26 Then he released Barabbas to them, but scourged Jesus and handed him over to be crucified.
Matthew 27:27 Then the soldiers of the governor took Jesus into the praetorium and gathered the whole cohort against him.
Matthew 27:28 And stripping him, they put a scarlet cloak around him.
Matthew 27:29 And weaving a crown from thorns, they put it upon his head, and a reed in his right hand, and kneeling before him, they were mocking him, saying: Greetings, king of the Jews.
Matthew 27:30 And spitting upon him, they took the reed and were striking his head.
Matthew 27:31 And when they mocked him, they stripped the cloak from him and clothed him in his garments and led him away to crucify him.
Matthew 27:32 And going out, they found a Cyrenian man named Simon; they compelled this man to take up his cross.
Matthew 27:33 And coming into a place called Golgotha, which is called Place of a Skull,
Matthew 27:34 they gave him vinegar mixed with gall to drink, and tasting it, he was unwilling to drink.
Matthew 27:35 And crucifying him, they divided his garments among themselves, casting a lot, so that what was spoken by the prophet might be fulfilled: They divided my garments among themselves, and upon my clothing they cast a lot.
Matthew 27:36 And sitting, they were guarding him there.
Matthew 27:37 And they placed above his head his accusation, written: This is Jesus the king of the Jews.
Matthew 27:38 Then two robbers are crucified with him, one at the right and one at the left.
Matthew 27:39 And those passing by were blaspheming him, moving their heads,
Matthew 27:40 and saying: You who demolish the sanctuary and build it in three days, save yourself; if you are God's Son, descend from the cross.
Matthew 27:41 And likewise also the chief priests, mocking with the scribes and elders, were saying:
Matthew 27:42 He saved others; he cannot save himself. If he is king of Israel, let him descend now from the cross, and we shall believe him.
Matthew 27:43 He has trusted in God; let him rescue him now, if he wants him, for he said: I am God's Son.
Matthew 27:44 And the robbers crucified with him were also reproaching him with the same thing.
Matthew 27:45 And from the sixth hour darkness came upon the whole earth until the ninth hour.
Matthew 27:46 And about the ninth hour Jesus cried out with a great voice, saying: Eli, Eli, lama sabachthani? This is: My God, my God, why did you forsake me?
Matthew 27:47 And some of those standing there, hearing, were saying: This man calls Elijah.
Matthew 27:48 And immediately one of them ran and took a sponge and filled it with vinegar and put it on a reed and was giving him to drink.
Matthew 27:49 But the rest were saying: Leave it; let us see whether Elijah comes to save him.
Matthew 27:50 And Jesus again cried out with a great voice and released the spirit.
Matthew 27:51 And behold, the veil of the sanctuary was torn into two from above until below, and the earth was shaken and the rocks were split,
Matthew 27:52 and the tombs were opened, and many bodies of the saints who had fallen asleep were raised,
Matthew 27:53 and coming out of the tombs after his resurrection, they entered into the holy city and appeared to many.
Matthew 27:54 And the centurion and those with him guarding Jesus, seeing the earthquake and the things that happened, feared exceedingly, saying: Truly this was God's Son.
Matthew 27:55 And many women were there, watching from afar, who followed Jesus from Galilee, serving him,
Matthew 27:56 among whom was Mary Magdalene and Mary the mother of James and Joses and the mother of the sons of Zebedee.
Matthew 27:57 And when evening came, a rich man from Arimathea came, named Joseph, who himself also became a disciple of Jesus.
Matthew 27:58 This man approached Pilate and asked for the body of Jesus. Then Pilate commanded the body to be given back.
Matthew 27:59 And Joseph took the body and wrapped it in a clean linen cloth,
Matthew 27:60 and put it in his new tomb, which he hewed in the rock, and rolling a great stone to the door of the tomb, he went away.
Matthew 27:61 And Mary Magdalene and the other Mary were there, sitting opposite the tomb.
Matthew 27:62 And on the next day, which is after the Preparation, the chief priests and the Pharisees gathered to Pilate,
Matthew 27:63 saying: Lord, we remembered that that deceiver said while still living: After three days I rise.
Matthew 27:64 Therefore command the tomb to be secured until the third day, lest his disciples come by night and steal him and tell the people: He was raised from the dead; and the last deception shall be worse than the first.
Matthew 27:65 And Pilate said to them: You have a guard; go, secure it as you know.
Matthew 27:66 And they went and secured the tomb, sealing the stone with the guard.

## Chapter 28

Matthew 28:1 And late on the Sabbath, as it was dawning toward the first day of the week, Mary Magdalene and the other Mary came to look upon the tomb.
Matthew 28:2 And behold, a great earthquake happened, for an angel of the Lord descended from heaven and approached and rolled the stone away from the door, and was sitting upon it.
Matthew 28:3 And his appearance was like lightning, and his garment white as snow.
Matthew 28:4 And from fear of him those guarding were shaken and became like dead men.
Matthew 28:5 And the angel answered and said to the women: Do not fear, you; for I know that you seek Jesus who has been crucified.
Matthew 28:6 He is not here, for he was raised as he said; come, see the place where the Lord lay.
Matthew 28:7 And go quickly and tell his disciples that he was raised from the dead, and behold, he goes before you into Galilee; there you shall see him. Behold, I told you.
Matthew 28:8 And going out quickly from the tomb with fear and great joy, they ran to report to his disciples.
Matthew 28:9 And as they were going to report to his disciples, behold, Jesus met them, saying: Rejoice. And they approached and took hold of his feet and worshiped him.
Matthew 28:10 Then Jesus says to them: Do not fear; go, report to my brothers that they should go away into Galilee, and there they shall see me.
Matthew 28:11 And while they were going, behold, some of the guard came into the city and reported to the chief priests all the things that happened.
Matthew 28:12 And gathering with the elders and taking counsel, they gave sufficient silver pieces to the soldiers,
Matthew 28:13 saying: Say that his disciples came by night and stole him while we slept.
Matthew 28:14 And if this is heard before the governor, we shall persuade him and make you free from care.
Matthew 28:15 And they took the silver pieces and did as they were taught; and this word was spread abroad among Jews until today.
Matthew 28:16 And the eleven disciples went into Galilee, to the mountain where Jesus appointed them.
Matthew 28:17 And seeing him, they worshiped him; but some doubted.
Matthew 28:18 And Jesus approached and spoke to them, saying: All authority was given to me in heaven and upon earth.
Matthew 28:19 Therefore go and make disciples of all the nations, baptizing them into the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit,
Matthew 28:20 teaching them to keep everything, whatever I commanded you; and behold, I am with you all the days until the completion of the age. Amen.

# Mark

The Apostolic Bible. Public domain. https://apostolic-bible.ysys9.chatgpt.site/license.html


## Chapter 1

Mark 1:1 Beginning of the good news of Jesus Christ, Son of God.
Mark 1:2 As it is written in the prophets: Behold, I send my messenger before your face, who shall prepare your way before you.
Mark 1:3 A voice of one crying in the desert: Prepare the way of the Lord; make his paths straight.
Mark 1:4 John came, baptizing in the desert and proclaiming a baptism of repentance for forgiveness of sins.
Mark 1:5 And the whole Judean region and the Jerusalemites were going out to him, and all were being baptized by him in the Jordan river, confessing their sins.
Mark 1:6 And John was clothed in camel's hair and a leather belt around his waist, and eating locusts and wild honey.
Mark 1:7 And he was proclaiming, saying: The one stronger than I comes behind me, whose strap of his sandals I am not sufficient to stoop and loose.
Mark 1:8 I indeed baptized you in water, but he shall baptize you in the Holy Spirit.
Mark 1:9 And it happened in those days, Jesus came from Nazareth of Galilee and was baptized by John into the Jordan.
Mark 1:10 And immediately, coming up from the water, he saw the heavens being torn and the Spirit like a dove descending upon him.
Mark 1:11 And a voice came from the heavens: You are my beloved Son, in whom I was well pleased.
Mark 1:12 And immediately the Spirit drives him out into the desert.
Mark 1:13 And he was there in the desert forty days, being tempted by Satan, and was with the wild beasts, and the angels were serving him.
Mark 1:14 And after John was handed over, Jesus came into Galilee, proclaiming the good news of the kingdom of God,
Mark 1:15 and saying: The time has been fulfilled, and the kingdom of God has drawn near; repent and believe in the good news.
Mark 1:16 And walking beside the sea of Galilee, he saw Simon and Andrew his brother casting a casting net in the sea, for they were fishermen.
Mark 1:17 And Jesus said to them: Come behind me, and I shall make you become fishers of men.
Mark 1:18 And immediately leaving their nets, they followed him.
Mark 1:19 And going forward a little from there, he saw James the son of Zebedee and John his brother, and they were in the boat mending the nets.
Mark 1:20 And immediately he called them, and leaving their father Zebedee in the boat with the hired men, they went away behind him.
Mark 1:21 And they enter into Capernaum, and immediately on the Sabbath he entered into the synagogue and was teaching.
Mark 1:22 And they were astonished at his teaching, for he was teaching them as one having authority, and not as the scribes.
Mark 1:23 And in their synagogue there was a man in an unclean spirit, and he cried out,
Mark 1:24 saying: Ah! What is between us and you, Jesus the Nazarene? Did you come to destroy us? I know you, who you are: the Holy One of God.
Mark 1:25 And Jesus rebuked him, saying: Be silenced, and come out of him.
Mark 1:26 And the unclean spirit convulsed him and cried with a great voice and came out of him.
Mark 1:27 And all were amazed, so that they debated among themselves, saying: What is this? What is this new teaching, that with authority he commands even the unclean spirits, and they obey him?
Mark 1:28 And his report immediately went out into the whole surrounding region of Galilee.
Mark 1:29 And immediately going out from the synagogue, they came into the house of Simon and Andrew with James and John.
Mark 1:30 And Simon's mother-in-law lay sick with a fever, and immediately they tell him concerning her.
Mark 1:31 And approaching, he raised her, taking hold of her hand, and the fever left her immediately, and she was serving them.
Mark 1:32 And when evening came, when the sun set, they were bringing to him all who were ill and those demon-possessed.
Mark 1:33 And the whole city was gathered together at the door.
Mark 1:34 And he healed many who were ill with various diseases and cast out many demons, and did not allow the demons to speak, because they knew him.
Mark 1:35 And early, while it was very much night, he rose and went out and went away into a deserted place, and there he was praying.
Mark 1:36 And Simon and those with him pursued him,
Mark 1:37 and finding him, they say to him: All seek you.
Mark 1:38 And he says to them: Let us go into the neighboring village towns, so that I may proclaim there also, for to this end I have come out.
Mark 1:39 And he was proclaiming in their synagogues throughout all Galilee and casting out the demons.
Mark 1:40 And a leper comes to him, begging him and kneeling to him and saying to him: If you wish, you are able to cleanse me.
Mark 1:41 And Jesus had compassion and stretched out his hand and touched him, and says to him: I wish; be cleansed.
Mark 1:42 And when he spoke, immediately the leprosy went away from him, and he was cleansed.
Mark 1:43 And sternly admonishing him, immediately he sent him out,
Mark 1:44 and says to him: See that you say nothing to anyone, but go, show yourself to the priest and offer concerning your cleansing what Moses commanded, as a testimony to them.
Mark 1:45 But he went out and began to proclaim much and spread the word abroad, so that he could no longer openly enter into a city, but was outside in deserted places, and they were coming to him from everywhere.

## Chapter 2

Mark 2:1 And again he entered into Capernaum after some days, and it was heard that he is in a house.
Mark 2:2 And immediately many gathered, so that there was no longer room, not even at the door, and he was speaking the word to them.
Mark 2:3 And they come to him, bringing a paralytic, carried by four.
Mark 2:4 And being unable to draw near to him because of the crowd, they unroofed the roof where he was, and digging through, they lower the pallet upon which the paralytic lay.
Mark 2:5 And Jesus, seeing their faith, says to the paralytic: Child, your sins have been forgiven you.
Mark 2:6 And some of the scribes were sitting there and reasoning in their hearts:
Mark 2:7 Why does this man speak blasphemies so? Who is able to forgive sins except one, God?
Mark 2:8 And immediately Jesus, recognizing in his spirit that they reason so among themselves, said to them: Why do you reason these things in your hearts?
Mark 2:9 Which is easier, to say to the paralytic: Your sins have been forgiven you, or to say: Rise and take up your pallet and walk?
Mark 2:10 But so that you may know that the Son of man has authority to forgive sins upon the earth, he says to the paralytic:
Mark 2:11 I say to you: Rise and take up your pallet and go into your house.
Mark 2:12 And he rose immediately and took up the pallet and went out before all, so that all were astonished and glorified God, saying: We never saw so.
Mark 2:13 And he went out again beside the sea, and the whole crowd was coming to him, and he was teaching them.
Mark 2:14 And passing by, he saw Levi the son of Alphaeus sitting at the tax office, and says to him: Follow me. And rising, he followed him.
Mark 2:15 And it happened, while he reclined in his house, many tax collectors and sinners also reclined with Jesus and his disciples, for they were many and followed him.
Mark 2:16 And the scribes and the Pharisees, seeing him eating with the tax collectors and sinners, were saying to his disciples: Why is it that he eats and drinks with the tax collectors and sinners?
Mark 2:17 And hearing, Jesus says to them: Those who are strong have no need of a physician, but those who are ill. I did not come to call righteous men, but sinners to repentance.
Mark 2:18 And John's disciples and those of the Pharisees were fasting, and they come and say to him: Why do John's disciples and those of the Pharisees fast, but your disciples do not fast?
Mark 2:19 And Jesus said to them: Can the sons of the bridal chamber fast while the bridegroom is with them? As long as they have the bridegroom with themselves, they cannot fast.
Mark 2:20 But days shall come when the bridegroom is taken away from them, and then they shall fast in those days.
Mark 2:21 And no one sews a patch of unfulled cloth upon an old garment; otherwise its filling, the new, takes away from the old, and a worse tear happens.
Mark 2:22 And no one puts new wine into old wineskins; otherwise the new wine bursts the wineskins, and the wine is poured out and the wineskins shall perish; but new wine must be put into fresh wineskins.
Mark 2:23 And it happened that he passed through the grainfields on the Sabbath, and his disciples began to make a way, plucking the ears of grain.
Mark 2:24 And the Pharisees were saying to him: See, why do they do on the Sabbath what is not lawful?
Mark 2:25 And he was saying to them: Have you never read what David did when he had need and was hungry, he and those with him,
Mark 2:26 how he entered into the house of God in the time of Abiathar the high priest, and ate the loaves of the presentation, which it is not lawful to eat except for the priests, and also gave to those who were with him?
Mark 2:27 And he was saying to them: The Sabbath came into being because of man, not man because of the Sabbath.
Mark 2:28 So that the Son of man is Lord also of the Sabbath.

## Chapter 3

Mark 3:1 And he entered again into the synagogue, and a man was there having his hand withered.
Mark 3:2 And they were watching him, whether he would heal him on the Sabbath, so that they might accuse him.
Mark 3:3 And he says to the man having the withered hand: Rise into the midst.
Mark 3:4 And he says to them: Is it lawful on the Sabbath to do good or to do evil, to save a soul or to kill? But they were silent.
Mark 3:5 And looking around at them with anger, grieving at the hardening of their heart, he says to the man: Stretch out your hand. And he stretched it out, and his hand was restored healthy as the other.
Mark 3:6 And the Pharisees went out and immediately with the Herodians were taking counsel against him, so that they might destroy him.
Mark 3:7 And Jesus withdrew with his disciples toward the sea, and a great multitude from Galilee followed him, and from Judea,
Mark 3:8 and from Jerusalem and from Idumea and beyond the Jordan, and those around Tyre and Sidon, a great multitude, hearing how many things he was doing, came to him.
Mark 3:9 And he told his disciples that a little boat should remain ready for him because of the crowd, so that they might not press him.
Mark 3:10 For he healed many, so that as many as had afflictions fell upon him to touch him.
Mark 3:11 And the unclean spirits, whenever they saw him, were falling before him and crying out, saying: You are the Son of God.
Mark 3:12 And he was rebuking them much, so that they might not make him manifest.
Mark 3:13 And he goes up into the mountain and calls to him those whom he himself wished, and they went to him.
Mark 3:14 And he made twelve, so that they might be with him and so that he might send them to proclaim,
Mark 3:15 and to have authority to heal the diseases and cast out the demons.
Mark 3:16 And he put upon Simon the name Peter,
Mark 3:17 and James the son of Zebedee and John the brother of James, and he put upon them names, Boanerges, which is: Sons of thunder;
Mark 3:18 and Andrew and Philip and Bartholomew and Matthew and Thomas and James the son of Alphaeus and Thaddaeus and Simon the Cananite,
Mark 3:19 and Judas Iscariot, who also handed him over. And they come into a house.
Mark 3:20 And a crowd comes together again, so that they are not able even to eat bread.
Mark 3:21 And those belonging to him heard and went out to seize him, for they were saying: He is out of his mind.
Mark 3:22 And the scribes who came down from Jerusalem were saying: He has Beelzebul, and: By the ruler of the demons he casts out the demons.
Mark 3:23 And calling them to him, he was saying to them in parables: How can Satan cast out Satan?
Mark 3:24 And if a kingdom is divided against itself, that kingdom cannot stand.
Mark 3:25 And if a house is divided against itself, that house cannot stand.
Mark 3:26 And if Satan rose against himself and has been divided, he cannot stand, but has an end.
Mark 3:27 No one can enter into the house of the strong man and plunder his goods unless he first binds the strong man, and then he shall plunder his house.
Mark 3:28 Amen, I say to you that all sins shall be forgiven the sons of men, and blasphemies, as many as they may blaspheme.
Mark 3:29 But whoever blasphemes against the Holy Spirit has no forgiveness forever, but is liable to eternal judgment.
Mark 3:30 Because they were saying: He has an unclean spirit.
Mark 3:31 Therefore his brothers and his mother come, and standing outside, they sent to him, calling him.
Mark 3:32 And a crowd was sitting around him, and they said to him: Behold, your mother and your brothers outside seek you.
Mark 3:33 And he answered them, saying: Who is my mother or my brothers?
Mark 3:34 And looking around in a circle at those sitting around him, he says: See, my mother and my brothers.
Mark 3:35 For whoever does the will of God, this one is my brother and my sister and mother.

## Chapter 4

Mark 4:1 And again he began to teach beside the sea, and a great crowd gathered to him, so that he entered into the boat and sat on the sea, and the whole crowd was upon the earth beside the sea.
Mark 4:2 And he was teaching them many things in parables and was saying to them in his teaching:
Mark 4:3 Hear; behold, the sower went out to sow.
Mark 4:4 And it happened as he sowed, some fell beside the road, and the birds of the heaven came and devoured it.
Mark 4:5 And other fell upon the rocky ground, where it did not have much earth, and immediately sprang up because it had no depth of earth.
Mark 4:6 And when the sun rose, it was scorched, and because it had no root, it withered.
Mark 4:7 And other fell into the thorns, and the thorns grew up and choked it, and it gave no fruit.
Mark 4:8 And other fell into the good earth and was giving fruit, rising and growing, and was bearing, one thirty and one sixty and one a hundred.
Mark 4:9 And he was saying to them: He who has ears to hear, let him hear.
Mark 4:10 And when he was alone, those around him with the twelve asked him about the parable.
Mark 4:11 And he was saying to them: To you it has been given to know the mystery of the kingdom of God, but to those outside all things happen in parables,
Mark 4:12 so that seeing they may see and not perceive, and hearing they may hear and not understand, lest they turn and their sins be forgiven them.
Mark 4:13 And he says to them: Do you not know this parable? And how shall you know all the parables?
Mark 4:14 The sower sows the word.
Mark 4:15 And these are those beside the road where the word is sown, and when they hear, immediately Satan comes and takes away the word sown in their hearts.
Mark 4:16 And these likewise are those sown upon the rocky places, who, when they hear the word, immediately receive it with joy,
Mark 4:17 and have no root in themselves, but are temporary; then, when affliction or persecution arises because of the word, immediately they are made to stumble.
Mark 4:18 And these are those sown into the thorns; these are those hearing the word,
Mark 4:19 and the cares of this age and the deceit of wealth and the desires concerning the remaining things enter in and choke the word, and it becomes unfruitful.
Mark 4:20 And these are those sown upon the good earth, who hear the word and receive it and bear fruit, one thirty and one sixty and one a hundred.
Mark 4:21 And he was saying to them: Does the lamp come so that it may be placed under the bushel or under the bed? Is it not so that it may be placed upon the lampstand?
Mark 4:22 For there is nothing hidden unless it should be manifested, nor did anything become concealed except so that it might come into the open.
Mark 4:23 If anyone has ears to hear, let him hear.
Mark 4:24 And he was saying to them: See what you hear; with the measure with which you measure it shall be measured to you, and it shall be added to you who hear.
Mark 4:25 For whoever has, to him it shall be given, and whoever does not have, even what he has shall be taken from him.
Mark 4:26 And he was saying: So is the kingdom of God, as if a man casts the seed upon the earth,
Mark 4:27 and sleeps and rises night and day, and the seed sprouts and grows long, how he himself does not know.
Mark 4:28 For the earth bears fruit of itself, first a blade, then an ear, then full grain in the ear.
Mark 4:29 And when the fruit yields, immediately he sends the sickle, because the harvest has arrived.
Mark 4:30 And he was saying: To what shall we liken the kingdom of God, or in what parable shall we set it forth?
Mark 4:31 As to a grain of mustard, which, when sown upon the earth, is smaller than all the seeds upon the earth.
Mark 4:32 And when it is sown, it rises and becomes greater than all the garden plants and makes great branches, so that the birds of the heaven can dwell under its shade.
Mark 4:33 And with many such parables he was speaking the word to them, as they were able to hear.
Mark 4:34 But without a parable he was not speaking to them, and privately he was explaining everything to his disciples.
Mark 4:35 And he says to them on that day, when evening came: Let us pass through to the other side.
Mark 4:36 And leaving the crowd, they take him along as he was in the boat, and other little boats also were with him.
Mark 4:37 And a great windstorm arises, and the waves were beating into the boat, so that it was already being filled.
Mark 4:38 And he was in the stern, sleeping upon the cushion, and they wake him and say to him: Teacher, do you not care that we perish?
Mark 4:39 And waking, he rebuked the wind and said to the sea: Be silent; be silenced. And the wind ceased, and a great calm came.
Mark 4:40 And he said to them: Why are you so cowardly? How do you have no faith?
Mark 4:41 And they feared a great fear and were saying to one another: Who, then, is this, that even the wind and the sea obey him?

## Chapter 5

Mark 5:1 And they came to the other side of the sea, into the region of the Gadarenes.
Mark 5:2 And when he went out from the boat, immediately a man from the tombs in an unclean spirit met him,
Mark 5:3 who had his dwelling in the tombs, and no one could bind him, not even with chains,
Mark 5:4 because he had often been bound with shackles and chains, and the chains had been torn apart by him and the shackles shattered, and no one was strong enough to tame him.
Mark 5:5 And continually, night and day, in the mountains and in the tombs, he was crying out and cutting himself with stones.
Mark 5:6 And seeing Jesus from afar, he ran and worshiped him,
Mark 5:7 and crying with a great voice, said: What is between me and you, Jesus, Son of the Most High God? I adjure you by God, do not torture me.
Mark 5:8 For he was saying to him: Come out of the man, unclean spirit.
Mark 5:9 And he was questioning him: What is your name? And he answered, saying: Legion is my name, because we are many.
Mark 5:10 And he was begging him much that he might not send them outside the region.
Mark 5:11 And there was there by the mountains a great herd of pigs feeding.
Mark 5:12 And all the demons begged him, saying: Send us into the pigs so that we may enter into them.
Mark 5:13 And immediately Jesus permitted them, and the unclean spirits came out and entered into the pigs, and the herd rushed down the precipice into the sea; and they were about two thousand, and were drowning in the sea.
Mark 5:14 And those feeding the pigs fled and reported into the city and into the fields, and they went out to see what has happened.
Mark 5:15 And they come to Jesus and see the demon-possessed man sitting and clothed and in his right mind, the one who had had the legion, and they feared.
Mark 5:16 And those who saw recounted to them how it happened to the demon-possessed man, and concerning the pigs.
Mark 5:17 And they began to beg him to depart from their borders.
Mark 5:18 And when he entered into the boat, the man who had been demon-possessed was begging him that he might be with him.
Mark 5:19 But Jesus did not allow him, but says to him: Go into your house to your own people, and report to them how many things the Lord did for you and had mercy on you.
Mark 5:20 And he went away and began to proclaim in the Decapolis how many things Jesus did for him, and all were marveling.
Mark 5:21 And when Jesus crossed over in the boat again to the other side, a great crowd gathered to him, and he was beside the sea.
Mark 5:22 And behold, one of the synagogue rulers comes, named Jairus, and seeing him, falls at his feet,
Mark 5:23 and was begging him much, saying: My little daughter is at the point of death; that you come and lay your hands upon her, so that she may be saved, and she shall live.
Mark 5:24 And he went away with him, and a great crowd was following him, and they were pressing him together.
Mark 5:25 And a certain woman, being in a flow of blood twelve years,
Mark 5:26 and having suffered many things by many physicians, and having spent everything she had, and having benefited nothing, but rather having come into the worse,
Mark 5:27 heard concerning Jesus and came in the crowd from behind and touched his garment.
Mark 5:28 For she was saying: Even if I touch his garments, I shall be saved.
Mark 5:29 And immediately the fountain of her blood dried up, and she knew in her body that she has been healed from the affliction.
Mark 5:30 And immediately Jesus, recognizing in himself the power which had gone out from him, turned in the crowd and was saying: Who touched my garments?
Mark 5:31 And his disciples were saying to him: You see the crowd pressing you together, and you say: Who touched me?
Mark 5:32 And he was looking around to see the one who did this.
Mark 5:33 And the woman, fearing and trembling, knowing what had happened to her, came and fell before him and told him all the truth.
Mark 5:34 And he said to her: Daughter, your faith has saved you; go into peace, and be healthy from your affliction.
Mark 5:35 While he was still speaking, they come from the synagogue ruler, saying: Your daughter died; why do you still trouble the teacher?
Mark 5:36 And Jesus immediately heard the word being spoken and says to the synagogue ruler: Do not fear; only believe.
Mark 5:37 And he allowed no one to follow together with him except Peter and James and John the brother of James.
Mark 5:38 And he comes into the house of the synagogue ruler and sees an uproar, people weeping and wailing much.
Mark 5:39 And entering, he says to them: Why do you make an uproar and weep? The child did not die, but sleeps.
Mark 5:40 And they were laughing at him. But he cast all out and takes the father of the child and the mother and those with him, and enters where the child was lying.
Mark 5:41 And taking hold of the child's hand, he says to her: Talitha koumi, which is translated: Girl, I say to you, rise.
Mark 5:42 And immediately the girl rose and was walking, for she was twelve years old; and they were astonished with great astonishment.
Mark 5:43 And he charged them much that no one should know this, and said that something should be given her to eat.

## Chapter 6

Mark 6:1 And he went out from there and came into his homeland, and his disciples follow him.
Mark 6:2 And when the Sabbath came, he began to teach in the synagogue, and many hearing were astonished, saying: From where does this man have these things? And what is the wisdom given to him, that even such mighty works happen through his hands?
Mark 6:3 Is this not the carpenter, the son of Mary, and brother of James and Joses and Judas and Simon? And are not his sisters here with us? And they were made to stumble at him.
Mark 6:4 And Jesus was saying to them: A prophet is not without honor except in his homeland and among his relatives and in his house.
Mark 6:5 And he could do no mighty work there, except he laid his hands upon a few sick people and healed them.
Mark 6:6 And he was marveling because of their unbelief. And he was going around the villages in a circle, teaching.
Mark 6:7 And he calls the twelve to him and began to send them two by two, and was giving them authority over the unclean spirits.
Mark 6:8 And he commanded them to take nothing for a journey except a staff only, no bag, no bread, no copper in the belt,
Mark 6:9 but to be shod with sandals, and: Do not put on two tunics.
Mark 6:10 And he was saying to them: Wherever you enter into a house, remain there until you go out from there.
Mark 6:11 And as many as do not receive you nor hear you, going out from there, shake off the dust from beneath your feet as a testimony to them. Amen, I say to you: It shall be more bearable for Sodom or Gomorrah on the day of judgment than for that city.
Mark 6:12 And going out, they were proclaiming that they should repent.
Mark 6:13 And they were casting out many demons and anointing many sick people with oil and healing.
Mark 6:14 And king Herod heard, for his name became manifest, and he was saying: John the baptizer was raised from the dead, and for this reason the powers work in him.
Mark 6:15 Others were saying: He is Elijah. And others were saying: He is a prophet, or as one of the prophets.
Mark 6:16 But Herod heard and said: John, whom I beheaded, this is he; he was raised from the dead.
Mark 6:17 For Herod himself sent and seized John and bound him in the prison because of Herodias, the wife of Philip his brother, because he married her.
Mark 6:18 For John was saying to Herod: It is not lawful for you to have your brother's wife.
Mark 6:19 And Herodias held a grudge against him and wished to kill him, and could not.
Mark 6:20 For Herod feared John, knowing him as a righteous and holy man, and was protecting him, and hearing him, he was doing many things and was hearing him gladly.
Mark 6:21 And an opportune day came, when Herod on his birthday was making a supper for his great men and the commanders of thousands and the first men of Galilee,
Mark 6:22 and the daughter of Herodias herself entered and danced and pleased Herod and those reclining with him; the king said to the girl: Ask me whatever you wish, and I shall give it to you.
Mark 6:23 And he swore to her: Whatever you ask me, I shall give you, until half my kingdom.
Mark 6:24 And she went out and said to her mother: What shall I ask? And she said: The head of John the Baptist.
Mark 6:25 And immediately entering with haste to the king, she asked, saying: I wish that you give me at once on a platter the head of John the Baptist.
Mark 6:26 And the king became exceedingly sorrowful, but because of the oaths and those reclining with him, he was unwilling to refuse her.
Mark 6:27 And immediately the king sent an executioner and commanded his head to be brought.
Mark 6:28 And he went away and beheaded him in the prison, and brought his head on a platter and gave it to the girl, and the girl gave it to her mother.
Mark 6:29 And his disciples heard and came and took his corpse and placed it in the tomb.
Mark 6:30 And the apostles gather to Jesus and reported to him everything, both whatever they did and whatever they taught.
Mark 6:31 And he said to them: Come, you yourselves, privately into a deserted place, and rest a little. For those coming and those going were many, and they did not even have opportunity to eat.
Mark 6:32 And they went away into a deserted place by the boat privately.
Mark 6:33 And the crowds saw them going, and many recognized him, and on foot from all the cities they ran together there and went ahead of them and came together to him.
Mark 6:34 And coming out, Jesus saw a great crowd and had compassion on them, because they were like sheep not having a shepherd, and began to teach them many things.
Mark 6:35 And when the hour had already grown late, his disciples approached him and say: The place is deserted, and the hour is already late.
Mark 6:36 Dismiss them so that they may go into the surrounding fields and villages and buy loaves for themselves, for they have nothing to eat.
Mark 6:37 And he answered and said to them: You give them something to eat. And they say to him: Shall we go and buy two hundred denarii of loaves and give them to eat?
Mark 6:38 And he says to them: How many loaves do you have? Go and see. And knowing, they say: Five, and two fish.
Mark 6:39 And he commanded them to make all recline, dining group by dining group, upon the green grass.
Mark 6:40 And they reclined, row by row, by hundreds and by fifties.
Mark 6:41 And taking the five loaves and the two fish, he looked up into the heaven and blessed and broke the loaves, and was giving them to his disciples so that they might set them before them; and the two fish he divided to all.
Mark 6:42 And all ate and were filled.
Mark 6:43 And they took up twelve baskets full of fragments, and from the fish.
Mark 6:44 And those who ate the loaves were about five thousand men.
Mark 6:45 And immediately he compelled his disciples to enter into the boat and go ahead to the other side toward Bethsaida, until he himself should dismiss the crowd.
Mark 6:46 And taking leave of them, he went away into the mountain to pray.
Mark 6:47 And when evening came, the boat was in the midst of the sea, and he alone upon the earth.
Mark 6:48 And he saw them tormented in rowing, for the wind was contrary to them; and about the fourth watch of the night he comes to them, walking upon the sea, and wished to pass by them.
Mark 6:49 But they, seeing him walking upon the sea, thought it was an apparition, and cried out.
Mark 6:50 For all saw him and were troubled, and immediately he spoke with them and says to them: Take courage; I am; do not fear.
Mark 6:51 And he went up to them into the boat, and the wind ceased; and they were exceedingly beyond measure astonished in themselves and marveling.
Mark 6:52 For they did not understand concerning the loaves, for their heart was hardened.
Mark 6:53 And crossing over, they came upon the land of Gennesaret and moored.
Mark 6:54 And when they went out of the boat, immediately recognizing him,
Mark 6:55 they ran around that whole surrounding region and began to carry around on pallets those who were ill, wherever they heard that he is there.
Mark 6:56 And wherever he entered into villages or cities or fields, they were placing the sick in the marketplaces and begging him that they might touch even the fringe of his garment; and as many as touched him were being saved.

## Chapter 7

Mark 7:1 And the Pharisees and some of the scribes, coming from Jerusalem, gather to him.
Mark 7:2 And seeing some of his disciples eating loaves with common hands, that is, unwashed, they found fault.
Mark 7:3 For the Pharisees and all the Jews, unless they wash their hands with a fist, do not eat, holding the tradition of the elders.
Mark 7:4 And from the marketplace, unless they wash themselves, they do not eat; and there are many other things which they received to hold: washings of cups and pitchers and copper vessels and beds.
Mark 7:5 Then the Pharisees and the scribes question him: Why do your disciples not walk according to the tradition of the elders, but eat the bread with unwashed hands?
Mark 7:6 And he answered and said to them: Isaiah prophesied well concerning you hypocrites, as it is written: This people honors me with their lips, but their heart is far from me.
Mark 7:7 And in vain they worship me, teaching teachings, commandments of men.
Mark 7:8 For leaving the commandment of God, you hold the tradition of men, washings of pitchers and cups, and many other such similar things you do.
Mark 7:9 And he was saying to them: Well do you reject the commandment of God so that you may keep your tradition.
Mark 7:10 For Moses said: Honor your father and your mother; and: He who speaks evil of father or mother, let him die by death.
Mark 7:11 But you say: If a man says to his father or mother: Corban, which is a gift, whatever you might benefit from me,
Mark 7:12 and you no longer allow him to do anything for his father or his mother,
Mark 7:13 making the word of God void by your tradition which you handed down; and many such similar things you do.
Mark 7:14 And calling the whole crowd to him, he was saying to them: Hear me, all, and understand.
Mark 7:15 There is nothing from outside the man entering into him which can defile him, but the things coming out from him, those are the things defiling the man.
Mark 7:16 If anyone has ears to hear, let him hear.
Mark 7:17 And when he entered into a house from the crowd, his disciples were questioning him concerning the parable.
Mark 7:18 And he says to them: Are you also so without understanding? Do you not perceive that everything from outside entering into the man cannot defile him,
Mark 7:19 because it does not enter into his heart, but into the belly, and goes out into the latrine, cleansing all the foods?
Mark 7:20 And he was saying: What comes out of the man, that defiles the man.
Mark 7:21 For from within, out of the heart of men, the evil reasonings come out, adulteries, fornications, murders,
Mark 7:22 thefts, greed, wickednesses, deceit, licentiousness, an evil eye, blasphemy, arrogance, foolishness.
Mark 7:23 All these evil things come out from within and defile the man.
Mark 7:24 And rising from there, he went away into the border regions of Tyre and Sidon, and entering into the house, he wished no one to know, and could not remain hidden.
Mark 7:25 For a woman heard concerning him, whose little daughter had an unclean spirit, and came and fell at his feet.
Mark 7:26 And the woman was a Greek, a Syrophoenician by race, and was asking him to cast the demon out of her daughter.
Mark 7:27 But Jesus said to her: Allow the children first to be filled, for it is not good to take the children's bread and cast it to the little dogs.
Mark 7:28 And she answered and says to him: Yes, Lord, for even the little dogs under the table eat from the crumbs of the children.
Mark 7:29 And he said to her: Because of this word, go; the demon has come out of your daughter.
Mark 7:30 And going away into her house, she found the demon gone out and the daughter lying upon the bed.
Mark 7:31 And again going out from the borders of Tyre and Sidon, he came toward the sea of Galilee through the midst of the borders of the Decapolis.
Mark 7:32 And they bring him a deaf man with difficulty speaking, and beg him to lay his hand upon him.
Mark 7:33 And taking him away from the crowd privately, he put his fingers into his ears and spat and touched his tongue.
Mark 7:34 And looking up into the heaven, he sighed and says to him: Ephphatha, which is: Be opened.
Mark 7:35 And immediately his ears were opened, and the bond of his tongue was loosed, and he was speaking correctly.
Mark 7:36 And he charged them to tell no one; but as much as he charged them, they were proclaiming more abundantly.
Mark 7:37 And they were exceedingly beyond measure astonished, saying: He has done all things well; he makes both the deaf hear and the speechless speak.

## Chapter 8

Mark 8:1 In those days, there being a very great crowd and having nothing to eat, Jesus called his disciples to him and says to them:
Mark 8:2 I have compassion on the crowd, because already they remain with me three days and have nothing to eat.
Mark 8:3 And if I dismiss them fasting into their house, they shall faint on the road, for some of them have come from afar.
Mark 8:4 And his disciples answered him: From where shall anyone be able to fill these with loaves here in a deserted place?
Mark 8:5 And he was questioning them: How many loaves do you have? And they said: Seven.
Mark 8:6 And he commanded the crowd to recline upon the earth, and taking the seven loaves, he gave thanks and broke them and was giving them to his disciples so that they might set them forth, and they set them before the crowd.
Mark 8:7 And they had a few little fish, and blessing, he said to set those forth also.
Mark 8:8 And they ate and were filled, and took up surpluses of fragments, seven large baskets.
Mark 8:9 And those who ate were about four thousand, and he dismissed them.
Mark 8:10 And immediately entering into the boat with his disciples, he came into the regions of Dalmanutha.
Mark 8:11 And the Pharisees came out and began to debate with him, seeking from him a sign from the heaven, testing him.
Mark 8:12 And sighing deeply in his spirit, he says: Why does this generation seek a sign? Amen, I say to you: If a sign shall be given to this generation!
Mark 8:13 And leaving them, he entered again into the boat and went away to the other side.
Mark 8:14 And they forgot to take loaves, and except for one loaf they had none with themselves in the boat.
Mark 8:15 And he was charging them, saying: See, beware of the leaven of the Pharisees and the leaven of Herod.
Mark 8:16 And they were reasoning with one another, saying: Because we have no loaves.
Mark 8:17 And Jesus knew and says to them: Why do you reason because you have no loaves? Do you not yet perceive nor understand? Do you still have your heart hardened?
Mark 8:18 Having eyes, do you not see? And having ears, do you not hear? And do you not remember,
Mark 8:19 when I broke the five loaves for the five thousand, how many baskets full of fragments you took up? They say to him: Twelve.
Mark 8:20 And when the seven for the four thousand, how many large basketfuls of fragments did you take up? And they said: Seven.
Mark 8:21 And he was saying to them: How do you not understand?
Mark 8:22 And he comes into Bethsaida, and they bring him a blind man and beg him to touch him.
Mark 8:23 And taking hold of the blind man's hand, he brought him outside the village, and spitting into his eyes and laying his hands upon him, he was questioning him whether he sees anything.
Mark 8:24 And looking up, he was saying: I see the men, because I behold them like trees walking.
Mark 8:25 Then again he laid his hands upon his eyes and made him look up, and he was restored and looked clearly upon all.
Mark 8:26 And he sent him into his house, saying: Neither enter into the village nor tell anyone in the village.
Mark 8:27 And Jesus and his disciples went out into the villages of Caesarea Philippi, and on the road he was questioning his disciples, saying to them: Who do men say that I am?
Mark 8:28 And they answered: John the Baptist; and others Elijah; and others one of the prophets.
Mark 8:29 And he says to them: But you, who do you say that I am? And Peter answered and says to him: You are the Christ.
Mark 8:30 And he rebuked them so that they should tell no one concerning him.
Mark 8:31 And he began to teach them that the Son of man must suffer many things and be rejected by the elders and chief priests and scribes, and be killed, and after three days rise.
Mark 8:32 And he was speaking the word openly. And Peter took him aside and began to rebuke him.
Mark 8:33 But he turned and saw his disciples and rebuked Peter, saying: Go behind me, Satan, because you do not mind the things of God, but the things of men.
Mark 8:34 And calling the crowd to him with his disciples, he said to them: Whoever wishes to come behind me, let him deny himself and take up his cross and follow me.
Mark 8:35 For whoever wishes to save his soul shall lose it, but whoever loses his soul because of me and the good news, this one shall save it.
Mark 8:36 For what shall it profit a man if he gains the whole world and suffers the loss of his soul?
Mark 8:37 Or what shall a man give in exchange for his soul?
Mark 8:38 For whoever is ashamed of me and my words in this adulterous and sinful generation, the Son of man also shall be ashamed of him when he comes in the glory of his Father with the holy angels.

## Chapter 9

Mark 9:1 And he was saying to them: Amen, I say to you that there are some of those standing here who shall certainly not taste death until they see the kingdom of God having come in power.
Mark 9:2 And after six days Jesus takes Peter and James and John with him, and brings them up into a high mountain privately, alone, and he was transfigured before them.
Mark 9:3 And his garments became shining, exceedingly white as snow, such as a fuller upon the earth cannot whiten.
Mark 9:4 And Elijah with Moses appeared to them, and they were conversing with Jesus.
Mark 9:5 And Peter answered and says to Jesus: Rabbi, it is good for us to be here, and let us make three tents, one for you and one for Moses and one for Elijah.
Mark 9:6 For he did not know what to speak, for they were terrified.
Mark 9:7 And a cloud came, overshadowing them, and a voice came from the cloud, saying: This is my beloved Son; hear him.
Mark 9:8 And suddenly looking around, they no longer saw anyone, but Jesus alone with themselves.
Mark 9:9 And as they descended from the mountain, he charged them to recount to no one what they saw, except when the Son of man rises from the dead.
Mark 9:10 And they held the word to themselves, debating what rising from the dead is.
Mark 9:11 And they were questioning him, saying: Why do the scribes say that Elijah must come first?
Mark 9:12 And he answered and said to them: Elijah indeed comes first and restores all things; and how is it written concerning the Son of man, that he should suffer many things and be treated as nothing?
Mark 9:13 But I say to you that Elijah also has come, and they did to him whatever they wished, as it is written concerning him.
Mark 9:14 And coming to the disciples, he saw a great crowd around them and scribes debating with them.
Mark 9:15 And immediately the whole crowd, seeing him, was greatly amazed, and running to him, they were greeting him.
Mark 9:16 And he questioned the scribes: What do you debate with them?
Mark 9:17 And one from the crowd answered and said: Teacher, I brought my son to you, having a speechless spirit.
Mark 9:18 And wherever it seizes him, it throws him down, and he foams and grinds his teeth and withers; and I told your disciples to cast it out, and they were not strong enough.
Mark 9:19 And he answered him and says: O unbelieving generation, until when shall I be with you? Until when shall I bear with you? Bring him to me.
Mark 9:20 And they brought him to him; and seeing him, immediately the spirit convulsed him, and falling upon the earth, he was rolling, foaming.
Mark 9:21 And he questioned his father: How much time is it since this has happened to him? And he said: From childhood.
Mark 9:22 And often it cast him both into fire and into waters to destroy him; but if you are able to do anything, help us, having compassion on us.
Mark 9:23 And Jesus said to him: If you are able to believe; all things are possible for the one who believes.
Mark 9:24 And immediately the father of the child cried out with tears and was saying: I believe, Lord; help my unbelief.
Mark 9:25 And Jesus, seeing that a crowd runs together, rebuked the unclean spirit, saying to it: Speechless and deaf spirit, I command you, come out of him and no longer enter into him.
Mark 9:26 And crying out and convulsing him much, it came out, and he became like a dead man, so that many said: He died.
Mark 9:27 But Jesus took hold of him by the hand and raised him, and he rose.
Mark 9:28 And when he entered into a house, his disciples were questioning him privately: Why were we not able to cast it out?
Mark 9:29 And he said to them: This kind can come out by nothing except by prayer and fasting.
Mark 9:30 And going out from there, they were passing through Galilee, and he did not wish anyone to know.
Mark 9:31 For he was teaching his disciples and was saying to them: The Son of man is handed over into the hands of men, and they shall kill him, and being killed, on the third day he shall rise.
Mark 9:32 But they did not understand the saying and feared to question him.
Mark 9:33 And he came into Capernaum, and being in the house, he was questioning them: What were you reasoning among yourselves on the road?
Mark 9:34 But they were silent, for they discussed with one another on the road who was greater.
Mark 9:35 And sitting down, he called the twelve and says to them: If anyone wishes to be first, he shall be last of all and servant of all.
Mark 9:36 And taking a child, he stood it in their midst, and embracing it, he said to them:
Mark 9:37 Whoever receives one of such children in my name receives me; and whoever receives me does not receive me, but the one who sent me.
Mark 9:38 And John answered him, saying: Teacher, we saw someone casting out demons in your name, who does not follow us, and we hindered him because he does not follow us.
Mark 9:39 But Jesus said: Do not hinder him, for there is no one who shall perform a mighty work in my name and shall be able quickly to speak evil of me.
Mark 9:40 For he who is not against you is for you.
Mark 9:41 For whoever gives you a cup of water to drink in my name because you are Christ's, amen, I say to you: He shall certainly not lose his reward.
Mark 9:42 And whoever makes one of the little ones who believe in me stumble, it is better for him rather if a millstone lies around his neck and he has been cast into the sea.
Mark 9:43 And if your hand makes you stumble, cut it off; it is good for you to enter into life maimed, rather than having the two hands to go away into Gehenna, into the unquenchable fire,
Mark 9:44 where their worm does not die and the fire is not quenched.
Mark 9:45 And if your foot makes you stumble, cut it off; it is good for you to enter into life lame, rather than having the two feet to be cast into Gehenna, into the unquenchable fire,
Mark 9:46 where their worm does not die and the fire is not quenched.
Mark 9:47 And if your eye makes you stumble, cast it out; it is good for you to enter into the kingdom of God one-eyed, rather than having two eyes to be cast into the Gehenna of fire,
Mark 9:48 where their worm does not die and the fire is not quenched.
Mark 9:49 For everyone shall be salted with fire, and every sacrifice shall be salted with salt.
Mark 9:50 The salt is good; but if the salt becomes saltless, with what shall you season it? Have salt in yourselves, and be at peace with one another.

## Chapter 10

Mark 10:1 And rising from there, he comes into the borders of Judea through the region beyond the Jordan, and crowds come together to him again, and as he was accustomed, again he was teaching them.
Mark 10:2 And the Pharisees approached and questioned him whether it is lawful for a man to dismiss a wife, testing him.
Mark 10:3 And he answered and said to them: What did Moses command you?
Mark 10:4 And they said: Moses permitted to write a document of divorce and dismiss her.
Mark 10:5 And Jesus answered and said to them: In view of your hardness of heart he wrote this commandment for you.
Mark 10:6 But from the beginning of creation God made them male and female.
Mark 10:7 Because of this a man shall leave his father and mother and be joined to his wife,
Mark 10:8 and the two shall be into one flesh; so that they are no longer two, but one flesh.
Mark 10:9 What, therefore, God joined together, let man not separate.
Mark 10:10 And in the house his disciples again questioned him concerning the same thing.
Mark 10:11 And he says to them: Whoever dismisses his wife and marries another commits adultery against her.
Mark 10:12 And if a woman dismisses her husband and is married to another, she commits adultery.
Mark 10:13 And they were bringing children to him so that he might touch them, but the disciples were rebuking those bringing them.
Mark 10:14 And Jesus, seeing, was indignant and said to them: Allow the children to come to me, and do not hinder them, for of such is the kingdom of God.
Mark 10:15 Amen, I say to you: Whoever does not receive the kingdom of God as a child shall certainly not enter into it.
Mark 10:16 And embracing them, laying his hands upon them, he was blessing them.
Mark 10:17 And as he went out onto a road, one ran to him and knelt to him and was questioning him: Good teacher, what shall I do so that I may inherit eternal life?
Mark 10:18 And Jesus said to him: Why do you call me good? No one is good except one, God.
Mark 10:19 You know the commandments: Do not commit adultery; do not murder; do not steal; do not testify falsely; do not defraud; honor your father and mother.
Mark 10:20 And he answered and said to him: Teacher, all these I have kept from my youth.
Mark 10:21 And Jesus looked at him and loved him and said to him: One thing is lacking to you; go, sell whatever you have and give to the poor, and you shall have treasure in heaven; and come, follow me, taking up the cross.
Mark 10:22 But he grew gloomy at the word and went away grieving, for he had many possessions.
Mark 10:23 And Jesus looked around and says to his disciples: How with difficulty shall those having wealth enter into the kingdom of God!
