Mark 10:24 And the disciples were amazed at his words. And Jesus again answered and says to them: Children, how difficult it is for those who have trusted in wealth to enter into the kingdom of God!
Mark 10:25 It is easier for a camel to enter through the hole of the needle than for a rich man to enter into the kingdom of God.
Mark 10:26 And they were exceedingly astonished, saying among themselves: And who can be saved?
Mark 10:27 And looking at them, Jesus says: With men it is impossible, but not with God, for all things are possible with God.
Mark 10:28 And Peter began to say to him: Behold, we left everything and followed you.
Mark 10:29 And Jesus answered and said: Amen, I say to you: There is no one who left house or brothers or sisters or father or mother or wife or children or fields because of me and the good news,
Mark 10:30 unless he receives a hundredfold now in this time, houses and brothers and sisters and mothers and children and fields, with persecutions, and in the coming age eternal life.
Mark 10:31 But many first shall be last, and the last first.
Mark 10:32 And they were on the road going up to Jerusalem, and Jesus was going before them, and they were amazed, and following, they were fearing; and again taking the twelve with him, he began to tell them the things about to happen to him:
Mark 10:33 Behold, we go up to Jerusalem, and the Son of man shall be handed over to the chief priests and the scribes, and they shall condemn him to death and hand him over to the gentiles,
Mark 10:34 and they shall mock him and scourge him and spit upon him and kill him, and on the third day he shall rise.
Mark 10:35 And James and John, the sons of Zebedee, approach him, saying: Teacher, we wish that you do for us whatever we ask.
Mark 10:36 And he said to them: What do you wish me to do for you?
Mark 10:37 And they said to him: Give us that we may sit, one at your right and one at your left, in your glory.
Mark 10:38 And Jesus said to them: You do not know what you ask. Are you able to drink the cup which I drink, and to be baptized with the baptism with which I am baptized?
Mark 10:39 And they said to him: We are able. And Jesus said to them: The cup which I drink indeed you shall drink, and with the baptism with which I am baptized you shall be baptized.
Mark 10:40 But to sit at my right and at my left is not mine to give, but to those for whom it has been prepared.
Mark 10:41 And hearing, the ten began to be indignant concerning James and John.
Mark 10:42 And Jesus called them to him and says to them: You know that those considered to rule the nations lord over them, and their great men exercise authority over them.
Mark 10:43 But it shall not be so among you; rather, whoever wishes to become great among you shall be your servant.
Mark 10:44 And whoever wishes to become first of you shall be slave of all.
Mark 10:45 For even the Son of man did not come to be served, but to serve, and to give his soul as a ransom for many.
Mark 10:46 And they come into Jericho; and as he went out from Jericho, and his disciples and a considerable crowd, the son of Timaeus, Bartimaeus the blind man, was sitting beside the road begging.
Mark 10:47 And hearing that it is Jesus the Nazarene, he began to cry out and say: Son of David, Jesus, have mercy on me.
Mark 10:48 And many were rebuking him so that he should be silent; but he was crying out much more: Son of David, have mercy on me.
Mark 10:49 And Jesus stood and said that he should be called; and they call the blind man, saying to him: Take courage; rise, he calls you.
Mark 10:50 And casting away his garment, he rose and came to Jesus.
Mark 10:51 And Jesus answered and says to him: What do you wish me to do for you? And the blind man said to him: Rabboni, that I may see again.
Mark 10:52 And Jesus said to him: Go; your faith has saved you. And immediately he saw again and was following Jesus on the road.

## Chapter 11

Mark 11:1 And when they draw near to Jerusalem, to Bethphage and Bethany, toward the mountain of Olives, he sends two of his disciples,
Mark 11:2 and says to them: Go into the village opposite you, and immediately entering into it, you shall find a colt bound, upon which no man has sat; loose it and bring it.
Mark 11:3 And if anyone says to you: Why do you do this? Say: Its Lord has need of it, and immediately he shall send it here.
Mark 11:4 And they went away and found the colt bound at the door outside upon the street, and they loose it.
Mark 11:5 And some of those standing there were saying to them: What do you do, loosing the colt?
Mark 11:6 And they told them as Jesus commanded, and they allowed them.
Mark 11:7 And they brought the colt to Jesus and cast their garments upon it, and he sat upon it.
Mark 11:8 And many spread their garments into the road, and others were cutting leafy branches from the trees and spreading them into the road.
Mark 11:9 And those going before and those following were crying out, saying: Hosanna! Blessed is he who comes in the name of the Lord!
Mark 11:10 Blessed is the coming kingdom in the name of the Lord, of our father David! Hosanna in the highest!
Mark 11:11 And Jesus entered into Jerusalem and into the temple, and looking around at everything, the hour being already late, he went out into Bethany with the twelve.
Mark 11:12 And on the next day, when they went out from Bethany, he was hungry.
Mark 11:13 And seeing a fig tree from afar having leaves, he came, if perhaps he would find anything on it, and coming to it, found nothing except leaves, for it was not a season of figs.
Mark 11:14 And Jesus answered and said to it: May no one any longer eat fruit from you forever. And his disciples were hearing.
Mark 11:15 And they come into Jerusalem, and Jesus entered into the temple and began to cast out those selling and buying in the temple, and overturned the tables of the money changers and the seats of those selling the doves.
Mark 11:16 And he was not allowing anyone to carry a vessel through the temple.
Mark 11:17 And he was teaching, saying to them: Is it not written that my house shall be called a house of prayer for all the nations? But you made it a cave of robbers.
Mark 11:18 And the scribes and the chief priests heard, and were seeking how they would destroy him, for they feared him, because the whole crowd was astonished at his teaching.
Mark 11:19 And when it became late, he was going out of the city.
Mark 11:20 And in the morning, passing by, they saw the fig tree withered from the roots.
Mark 11:21 And Peter remembered and says to him: Rabbi, see, the fig tree which you cursed has withered.
Mark 11:22 And Jesus answered and says to them: Have faith in God.
Mark 11:23 For amen, I say to you that whoever says to this mountain: Be lifted and cast into the sea, and does not doubt in his heart, but believes that what he says happens, he shall have whatever he says.
Mark 11:24 For this reason I say to you: All things, whatever you ask praying, believe that you receive, and they shall be yours.
Mark 11:25 And whenever you stand praying, forgive if you have anything against anyone, so that your Father who is in the heavens also may forgive you your trespasses.
Mark 11:26 But if you do not forgive, neither shall your Father who is in the heavens forgive your trespasses.
Mark 11:27 And they come again into Jerusalem, and while he walks in the temple, the chief priests and the scribes and the elders come to him,
Mark 11:28 and say to him: By what authority do you do these things? And who gave you this authority so that you do these things?
Mark 11:29 And Jesus answered and said to them: I also shall question you with one word, and answer me, and I shall tell you by what authority I do these things.
Mark 11:30 Was the baptism of John from heaven or from men? Answer me.
Mark 11:31 And they were reasoning among themselves, saying: If we say: From heaven, he shall say: Why, then, did you not believe him?
Mark 11:32 But if we say: From men; they feared the people, for all held John, that he truly was a prophet.
Mark 11:33 And answering, they say to Jesus: We do not know. And Jesus answered and says to them: Neither do I tell you by what authority I do these things.

## Chapter 12

Mark 12:1 And he began to speak to them in parables: A man planted a vineyard and put a fence around it and dug a winepress vat and built a tower, and leased it to farmers and went abroad.
Mark 12:2 And he sent a slave to the farmers in the season, so that from the farmers he might receive from the fruit of the vineyard.
Mark 12:3 But they took him and beat him and sent him away empty.
Mark 12:4 And again he sent another slave to them, and that one they stoned and wounded in the head and sent away dishonored.
Mark 12:5 And again he sent another, and that one they killed, and many others, beating some and killing others.
Mark 12:6 Therefore, still having one son, his beloved, he sent him also to them last, saying: They shall respect my son.
Mark 12:7 But those farmers said among themselves: This is the heir; come, let us kill him, and the inheritance shall be ours.
Mark 12:8 And taking him, they killed him and cast him outside the vineyard.
Mark 12:9 What, therefore, shall the lord of the vineyard do? He shall come and destroy the farmers and give the vineyard to others.
Mark 12:10 Have you not even read this Scripture: The stone which the builders rejected, this became the head of the corner;
Mark 12:11 this came from the Lord, and it is marvelous in our eyes?
Mark 12:12 And they were seeking to seize him, and feared the crowd, for they knew that he spoke the parable against them; and leaving him, they went away.
Mark 12:13 And they send to him some of the Pharisees and of the Herodians, so that they might catch him in a word.
Mark 12:14 And they came and say to him: Teacher, we know that you are true and care concerning no one, for you do not look upon the face of men, but in truth teach the way of God. Is it lawful to give tax to Caesar or not?
Mark 12:15 Shall we give or not give? But knowing their hypocrisy, he said to them: Why do you test me? Bring me a denarius so that I may see.
Mark 12:16 And they brought it, and he says to them: Whose is this image and the inscription? And they said to him: Caesar's.
Mark 12:17 And Jesus answered and said to them: Repay the things of Caesar to Caesar, and the things of God to God. And they marveled at him.
Mark 12:18 And Sadducees come to him, who say there is no resurrection, and questioned him, saying:
Mark 12:19 Teacher, Moses wrote to us that if anyone's brother dies and leaves a wife and leaves no children, his brother should take his wife and raise up seed for his brother.
Mark 12:20 There were seven brothers, and the first took a wife, and dying, left no seed.
Mark 12:21 And the second took her and died, and neither did he leave seed, and the third likewise.
Mark 12:22 And the seven took her and left no seed; last of all the woman also died.
Mark 12:23 In the resurrection, therefore, when they rise, whose wife of them shall she be? For the seven had her as wife.
Mark 12:24 And Jesus answered and said to them: Is it not because of this that you wander, not knowing the Scriptures nor the power of God?
Mark 12:25 For when they rise from the dead, they neither marry nor are given in marriage, but are like angels who are in the heavens.
Mark 12:26 But concerning the dead, that they are raised, have you not read in the book of Moses, at the bush, how God spoke to him, saying: I am the God of Abraham and the God of Isaac and the God of Jacob?
Mark 12:27 He is not God of the dead, but God of the living; therefore you wander greatly.
Mark 12:28 And one of the scribes approached and heard them debating, and knowing that he answered them well, questioned him: Which is the first commandment of all?
Mark 12:29 And Jesus answered him: The first of all the commandments: Hear, Israel; the Lord our God is one Lord.
Mark 12:30 And you shall love the Lord your God from your whole heart and from your whole soul and from your whole mind and from your whole strength. This is the first commandment.
Mark 12:31 And a second like it: You shall love your neighbor as yourself. There is no other commandment greater than these.
Mark 12:32 And the scribe said to him: Well, teacher, in truth you said that God is one, and there is no other except him.
Mark 12:33 And to love him from the whole heart and from the whole understanding and from the whole soul and from the whole strength, and to love the neighbor as oneself, is more than all the whole burnt offerings and the sacrifices.
Mark 12:34 And Jesus, seeing that he answered intelligently, said to him: You are not far from the kingdom of God. And no one any longer dared to question him.
Mark 12:35 And Jesus answered and was saying, teaching in the temple: How do the scribes say that the Christ is David's son?
Mark 12:36 For David himself said in the Holy Spirit: The Lord said to my Lord: Sit at my right until I place your enemies as a footstool of your feet.
Mark 12:37 Therefore David himself calls him Lord, and from where is he his son? And the great crowd was hearing him gladly.
Mark 12:38 And he was saying to them in his teaching: Beware of the scribes, who wish to walk in robes, and greetings in the marketplaces,
Mark 12:39 and first seats in the synagogues and first reclining places at the suppers,
Mark 12:40 who devour the houses of the widows, and with a pretext pray long; these shall receive greater judgment.
Mark 12:41 And Jesus sat opposite the treasury and was watching how the crowd casts copper into the treasury, and many rich men were casting much.
Mark 12:42 And one poor widow came and cast two lepta, which is a quadrans.
Mark 12:43 And calling his disciples to him, he says to them: Amen, I say to you that this poor widow has cast more than all those who cast into the treasury.
Mark 12:44 For all cast from what abounds to them, but she from her lack cast everything she had, her whole livelihood.

## Chapter 13

Mark 13:1 And as he went out from the temple, one of his disciples says to him: Teacher, see, what manner of stones and what manner of buildings!
Mark 13:2 And Jesus answered and said to him: Do you see these great buildings? There shall certainly not be left a stone upon a stone which shall certainly not be demolished.
Mark 13:3 And while he sat on the mountain of Olives opposite the temple, Peter and James and John and Andrew were questioning him privately:
Mark 13:4 Tell us, when shall these things be, and what is the sign when all these things are about to be completed?
Mark 13:5 And Jesus answered them and began to say: See that no one leads you astray.
Mark 13:6 For many shall come in my name, saying: I am, and shall lead many astray.
Mark 13:7 And when you hear wars and reports of wars, do not be alarmed, for it must happen, but the end is not yet.
Mark 13:8 For nation shall rise against nation and kingdom against kingdom, and there shall be earthquakes in places, and there shall be famines and disturbances; these are beginnings of birth pains.
Mark 13:9 But you, beware for yourselves, for they shall hand you over to councils, and in synagogues you shall be beaten, and before governors and kings you shall stand because of me, as a testimony to them.
Mark 13:10 And the good news must first be proclaimed to all the nations.
Mark 13:11 And when they lead you, handing you over, do not be anxious beforehand what to speak, nor rehearse, but whatever is given you in that hour, speak this; for it is not you who speak, but the Holy Spirit.
Mark 13:12 And brother shall hand brother over to death, and father a child, and children shall rise against parents and put them to death.
Mark 13:13 And you shall be hated by all because of my name; but he who endures until the end, this one shall be saved.
Mark 13:14 And when you see the abomination of desolation, spoken of by Daniel the prophet, standing where it ought not, let the reader perceive; then let those in Judea flee into the mountains.
Mark 13:15 And let the one upon the roof not descend into the house, nor enter to take anything out of his house.
Mark 13:16 And let the one who is in the field not turn back to take his garment.
Mark 13:17 And woe to those having in the womb and those nursing in those days!
Mark 13:18 And pray that your flight may not happen in winter.
Mark 13:19 For those days shall be affliction, such as has not happened from the beginning of creation which God created until now, and shall certainly not happen.
Mark 13:20 And unless the Lord shortened the days, no flesh would be saved; but because of the chosen whom he chose, he shortened the days.
Mark 13:21 And then if anyone says to you: Behold, here is the Christ, or: Behold, there, do not believe.
Mark 13:22 For false christs and false prophets shall rise and shall give signs and wonders to lead astray, if possible, even the chosen.
Mark 13:23 But you, beware; behold, I have told you everything beforehand.
Mark 13:24 But in those days, after that affliction, the sun shall be darkened and the moon shall not give its light,
Mark 13:25 and the stars of the heaven shall be falling out, and the powers in the heavens shall be shaken.
Mark 13:26 And then they shall see the Son of man coming in clouds with much power and glory.
Mark 13:27 And then he shall send his angels and gather his chosen together from the four winds, from the extremity of earth until the extremity of heaven.
Mark 13:28 And learn the parable from the fig tree: When its branch already becomes tender and puts forth the leaves, you know that summer is near.
Mark 13:29 So also you, when you see these things happening, know that it is near, at the doors.
Mark 13:30 Amen, I say to you that this generation shall certainly not pass until all these things happen.
Mark 13:31 The heaven and the earth shall pass away, but my words shall certainly not pass away.
Mark 13:32 But concerning that day and the hour no one knows, not even the angels who are in heaven, nor the Son, except the Father.
Mark 13:33 Beware, stay awake and pray, for you do not know when the time is.
Mark 13:34 As a man abroad, leaving his house and giving his slaves the authority and to each his work, and commanding the doorkeeper to keep watch.
Mark 13:35 Therefore keep watch, for you do not know when the lord of the house comes, late or at midnight or at rooster-crowing or early,
Mark 13:36 lest coming suddenly he find you sleeping.
Mark 13:37 And what I say to you I say to all: Keep watch.

## Chapter 14

Mark 14:1 And the Passover and the unleavened bread were after two days, and the chief priests and the scribes were seeking how they might seize him by deceit and kill him.
Mark 14:2 But they were saying: Not during the feast, lest there be an uproar of the people.
Mark 14:3 And while he was in Bethany in the house of Simon the leper, reclining, a woman came having an alabaster vessel of very costly ointment of genuine nard, and breaking the alabaster vessel, she poured it down upon his head.
Mark 14:4 And some were indignant among themselves and saying: Why has this waste of the ointment happened?
Mark 14:5 For this could have been sold for above three hundred denarii and given to the poor. And they were sternly scolding her.
Mark 14:6 But Jesus said: Leave her; why do you give her troubles? She has worked a good work toward me.
Mark 14:7 For you always have the poor with yourselves, and whenever you wish, you can do them good; but you do not always have me.
Mark 14:8 What she had, she did; she anticipated anointing my body for the burial.
Mark 14:9 Amen, I say to you: Wherever this good news is proclaimed into the whole world, what she did also shall be spoken of as a memorial of her.
Mark 14:10 And Judas Iscariot, one of the twelve, went away to the chief priests to hand him over to them.
Mark 14:11 And hearing, they rejoiced and promised to give him silver; and he was seeking how he might opportunely hand him over.
Mark 14:12 And on the first day of the unleavened bread, when they were sacrificing the Passover, his disciples say to him: Where do you wish us to go and prepare so that you may eat the Passover?
Mark 14:13 And he sends two of his disciples and says to them: Go into the city, and a man carrying a pitcher of water shall meet you; follow him.
Mark 14:14 And wherever he enters, tell the master of the house: The teacher says: Where is the lodging where I may eat the Passover with my disciples?
Mark 14:15 And he shall show you a great upper room, furnished, ready; there prepare for us.
Mark 14:16 And his disciples went out and came into the city and found as he told them, and prepared the Passover.
Mark 14:17 And when evening came, he comes with the twelve.
Mark 14:18 And while they reclined and ate, Jesus said: Amen, I say to you that one of you shall hand me over, the one eating with me.
Mark 14:19 And they began to be grieved and to say to him one by one: Surely not I? And another: Surely not I?
Mark 14:20 And he answered and said to them: One of the twelve, the one dipping with me into the dish.
Mark 14:21 The Son of man indeed goes as it is written concerning him, but woe to that man through whom the Son of man is handed over! It was good for him if that man had not been born.
Mark 14:22 And while they ate, Jesus took bread and blessed and broke it and gave it to them, and said: Take, eat; this is my body.
Mark 14:23 And taking the cup, he gave thanks and gave it to them, and all drank from it.
Mark 14:24 And he said to them: This is my blood, that of the new covenant, poured out concerning many.
Mark 14:25 Amen, I say to you that I shall certainly no longer drink from the produce of the vine until that day when I drink it new in the kingdom of God.
Mark 14:26 And having sung a hymn, they went out to the mountain of Olives.
Mark 14:27 And Jesus says to them: All shall be made to stumble at me in this night, because it is written: I shall strike the shepherd, and the sheep shall be scattered.
Mark 14:28 But after I am raised, I shall go before you into Galilee.
Mark 14:29 And Peter said to him: Even if all shall be made to stumble, yet not I.
Mark 14:30 And Jesus says to him: Amen, I say to you that today in this night, before a rooster calls twice, you shall deny me three times.
Mark 14:31 But he was saying more exceedingly: If I must die together with you, I shall certainly not deny you. And likewise all also were saying.
Mark 14:32 And they come into a place whose name is Gethsemane, and he says to his disciples: Sit here until I pray.
Mark 14:33 And he takes Peter and James and John with himself, and began to be greatly troubled and distressed.
Mark 14:34 And he says to them: My soul is exceedingly sorrowful until death; remain here and keep watch.
Mark 14:35 And going forward a little, he fell upon the earth and was praying that, if it is possible, the hour might pass from him.
Mark 14:36 And he was saying: Abba, Father, all things are possible for you; carry this cup away from me; but not what I wish, but what you.
Mark 14:37 And he comes and finds them sleeping, and says to Peter: Simon, do you sleep? Were you not strong enough to keep watch one hour?
Mark 14:38 Keep watch and pray so that you may not enter into temptation; the spirit indeed is willing, but the flesh weak.
Mark 14:39 And again going away, he prayed, saying the same word.
Mark 14:40 And returning, he found them sleeping again, for their eyes were weighed down, and they did not know what to answer him.
Mark 14:41 And he comes the third time and says to them: Sleep the rest and take your rest; it is enough, the hour came; behold, the Son of man is handed over into the hands of sinners.
Mark 14:42 Rise, let us go; behold, the one handing me over has drawn near.
Mark 14:43 And immediately, while he was still speaking, Judas arrives, being one of the twelve, and with him a great crowd with swords and clubs from the chief priests and the scribes and the elders.
Mark 14:44 And the one handing him over had given them an agreed sign, saying: Whomever I kiss, he is the one; seize him and lead him away securely.
Mark 14:45 And coming, immediately approaching him, he says: Rabbi, Rabbi; and kissed him fervently.
Mark 14:46 And they laid their hands upon him and seized him.
Mark 14:47 And a certain one of those standing by drew the sword and struck the slave of the high priest and took off his ear.
Mark 14:48 And Jesus answered and said to them: As against a robber you came out with swords and clubs to arrest me.
Mark 14:49 Daily I was with you in the temple, teaching, and you did not seize me; but so that the Scriptures might be fulfilled.
Mark 14:50 And leaving him, all fled.
Mark 14:51 And a certain young man was following him, clothed in a linen cloth upon his naked body, and the young men seize him.
Mark 14:52 But he left the linen cloth and fled naked from them.
Mark 14:53 And they led Jesus away to the high priest, and all the chief priests and the elders and the scribes come together to him.
Mark 14:54 And Peter followed him from afar until inside into the courtyard of the high priest, and was sitting together with the attendants and warming himself by the light.
Mark 14:55 And the chief priests and the whole council were seeking testimony against Jesus to put him to death, and were not finding it.
Mark 14:56 For many were testifying falsely against him, and the testimonies were not equal.
Mark 14:57 And some stood up and were testifying falsely against him, saying:
Mark 14:58 We heard him saying: I shall demolish this sanctuary made by hands, and through three days I shall build another not made by hands.
Mark 14:59 And not even so was their testimony equal.
Mark 14:60 And the high priest stood up into the midst and questioned Jesus, saying: Do you answer nothing? What do these testify against you?
Mark 14:61 But he was silent and answered nothing. Again the high priest was questioning him and says to him: Are you the Christ, the Son of the Blessed One?
Mark 14:62 And Jesus said: I am, and you shall see the Son of man sitting at the right of the Power and coming with the clouds of the heaven.
Mark 14:63 And the high priest tore his tunics and says: What further need do we have of witnesses?
Mark 14:64 You heard the blasphemy; what does it appear to you? And all condemned him to be liable to death.
Mark 14:65 And some began to spit upon him and cover his face and strike him with fists and say to him: Prophesy; and the attendants were striking him with slaps.
Mark 14:66 And while Peter was below in the courtyard, one of the servant girls of the high priest comes,
Mark 14:67 and seeing Peter warming himself, she looked at him and says: You also were with Jesus the Nazarene.
Mark 14:68 But he denied, saying: I do not know nor understand what you say. And he went outside into the forecourt, and a rooster called.
Mark 14:69 And the servant girl saw him again and began to say to those standing by: This man is one of them.
Mark 14:70 But he was denying again. And after a little while, again those standing by were saying to Peter: Truly you are one of them, for you are also a Galilean, and your speech resembles theirs.
Mark 14:71 But he began to curse and swear: I do not know this man of whom you speak.
Mark 14:72 And a rooster called a second time, and Peter remembered the saying which Jesus said to him: Before a rooster calls twice, you shall deny me three times; and thinking upon it, he was weeping.

## Chapter 15

Mark 15:1 And immediately in the morning the chief priests took counsel with the elders and scribes and the whole council, and binding Jesus, carried him away and handed him over to Pilate.
Mark 15:2 And Pilate questioned him: Are you the king of the Jews? And he answered and said to him: You say it.
Mark 15:3 And the chief priests were accusing him of many things.
Mark 15:4 And Pilate again questioned him, saying: Do you answer nothing? See how many things they testify against you.
Mark 15:5 But Jesus no longer answered anything, so that Pilate marveled.
Mark 15:6 And at a feast he was releasing to them one prisoner whom they asked for.
Mark 15:7 And the one called Barabbas was bound with the fellow insurgents, who in the insurrection had committed murder.
Mark 15:8 And the crowd cried aloud and began to ask as he always did for them.
Mark 15:9 And Pilate answered them, saying: Do you wish me to release to you the king of the Jews?
Mark 15:10 For he knew that because of envy the chief priests had handed him over.
Mark 15:11 But the chief priests stirred up the crowd so that he should rather release Barabbas to them.
Mark 15:12 And Pilate answered and again said to them: What, therefore, do you wish me to do with the one you call king of the Jews?
Mark 15:13 And they again cried out: Crucify him.
Mark 15:14 And Pilate was saying to them: For what evil did he do? But they cried out more abundantly: Crucify him.
Mark 15:15 And Pilate, wishing to do what was sufficient for the crowd, released Barabbas to them, and scourged Jesus and handed him over to be crucified.
Mark 15:16 And the soldiers led him away inside the courtyard, which is the praetorium, and they call together the whole cohort.
Mark 15:17 And they clothe him in purple and put around him a crown of thorns which they wove,
Mark 15:18 and began to greet him: Greetings, king of the Jews.
Mark 15:19 And they were striking his head with a reed and spitting upon him, and bending their knees, were worshiping him.
Mark 15:20 And when they mocked him, they stripped the purple from him and clothed him in his own garments, and lead him out to crucify him.
Mark 15:21 And they compel a certain passerby, Simon a Cyrenian, coming from a field, the father of Alexander and Rufus, to take up his cross.
Mark 15:22 And they bring him to a place, Golgotha, which is translated: Place of a Skull.
Mark 15:23 And they were giving him wine mixed with myrrh to drink, but he did not take it.
Mark 15:24 And crucifying him, they were dividing his garments, casting a lot upon them, who should take what.
Mark 15:25 And it was the third hour, and they crucified him.
Mark 15:26 And the inscription of his accusation was inscribed: The king of the Jews.
Mark 15:27 And with him they crucify two robbers, one at his right and one at his left.
Mark 15:28 And the Scripture was fulfilled which says: And he was reckoned with the lawless.
Mark 15:29 And those passing by were blaspheming him, moving their heads and saying: Ah! You who demolish the sanctuary and build it in three days,
Mark 15:30 save yourself and descend from the cross.
Mark 15:31 And likewise also the chief priests, mocking with one another with the scribes, were saying: He saved others; he cannot save himself.
Mark 15:32 Let the Christ, the king of Israel, descend now from the cross so that we may see and believe. And those crucified together with him were reproaching him.
Mark 15:33 And when the sixth hour came, darkness came upon the whole earth until the ninth hour.
Mark 15:34 And at the ninth hour Jesus cried with a great voice, saying: Eloi, Eloi, lamma sabachthani? Which is translated: My God, my God, for what did you forsake me?
Mark 15:35 And some of those standing by heard and were saying: Behold, he calls Elijah.
Mark 15:36 And one ran and filled a sponge with vinegar and put it on a reed and was giving him to drink, saying: Leave it; let us see whether Elijah comes to take him down.
Mark 15:37 And Jesus uttered a great voice and breathed out.
Mark 15:38 And the veil of the sanctuary was torn into two from above until below.
Mark 15:39 And the centurion standing opposite him, seeing that crying out so he breathed out, said: Truly this man was God's Son.
Mark 15:40 And there were also women watching from afar, among whom was also Mary Magdalene and Mary the mother of James the little and Joses, and Salome,
Mark 15:41 who also, when he was in Galilee, were following him and serving him, and many others who came up with him into Jerusalem.
Mark 15:42 And evening having already come, since it was Preparation, which is the day before the Sabbath,
Mark 15:43 Joseph from Arimathea came, an honorable councilor, who himself also was awaiting the kingdom of God; taking courage, he entered to Pilate and asked for the body of Jesus.
Mark 15:44 And Pilate marveled whether he has already died, and calling the centurion to him, questioned him whether he died some time ago.
Mark 15:45 And knowing from the centurion, he granted the body to Joseph.
Mark 15:46 And buying a linen cloth and taking him down, he wrapped him in the linen cloth and laid him in a tomb which had been hewn from rock, and rolled a stone against the door of the tomb.
Mark 15:47 And Mary Magdalene and Mary of Joses were watching where he is laid.

## Chapter 16

Mark 16:1 And when the Sabbath had passed, Mary Magdalene and Mary of James and Salome bought spices so that they might come and anoint him.
Mark 16:2 And very early on the first day of the week they come to the tomb, the sun having risen.
Mark 16:3 And they were saying among themselves: Who shall roll away the stone for us from the door of the tomb?
Mark 16:4 And looking up, they see that the stone has been rolled away, for it was exceedingly great.
Mark 16:5 And entering into the tomb, they saw a young man sitting on the right, clothed in a white robe, and were greatly amazed.
Mark 16:6 And he says to them: Do not be greatly amazed; you seek Jesus the Nazarene, the one crucified; he was raised, he is not here; see the place where they laid him.
Mark 16:7 But go, tell his disciples and Peter that he goes before you into Galilee; there you shall see him, as he told you.
Mark 16:8 And going out quickly, they fled from the tomb, and trembling and astonishment held them, and they said nothing to anyone, for they feared.
Mark 16:9 And rising early on the first day of the week, he appeared first to Mary Magdalene, from whom he had cast out seven demons.
Mark 16:10 She went and reported to those who had been with him, mourning and weeping.
Mark 16:11 And they, hearing that he lives and was seen by her, disbelieved.
Mark 16:12 And after these things he was manifested in another form to two of them walking, going into a field.
Mark 16:13 And they went away and reported to the rest; neither did they believe those.
Mark 16:14 Afterward he was manifested to the eleven themselves as they reclined, and reproached their unbelief and hardness of heart, because they did not believe those who saw him raised.
Mark 16:15 And he said to them: Go into the whole world and proclaim the good news to all the creation.
Mark 16:16 He who believes and is baptized shall be saved, but he who disbelieves shall be condemned.
Mark 16:17 And these signs shall accompany those who believe: In my name they shall cast out demons; they shall speak with new tongues;
Mark 16:18 they shall take up serpents, and even if they drink anything deadly, it shall certainly not harm them; they shall lay hands upon the sick, and they shall be well.
Mark 16:19 Therefore the Lord indeed, after speaking to them, was taken up into the heaven and sat at the right of God.
Mark 16:20 And they went out and proclaimed everywhere, the Lord working together and confirming the word through the accompanying signs. Amen.

# Luke

The Apostolic Bible. Public domain. https://apostolic-bible.ysys9.chatgpt.site/license.html


## Chapter 1

Luke 1:1 Since indeed many undertook to arrange a narrative concerning the matters fulfilled among us,
Luke 1:2 as those who from the beginning became eyewitnesses and attendants of the word handed down to us,
Luke 1:3 it seemed good to me also, having followed everything accurately from the beginning, to write to you in order, most excellent Theophilus,
Luke 1:4 so that you may recognize the certainty concerning the words in which you were instructed.
Luke 1:5 In the days of Herod king of Judea there was a certain priest named Zechariah, of the division of Abijah, and his wife was of the daughters of Aaron, and her name Elizabeth.
Luke 1:6 And both were righteous before God, walking blameless in all the commandments and ordinances of the Lord.
Luke 1:7 And they had no child, because Elizabeth was barren, and both were advanced in their days.
Luke 1:8 And it happened, while he served as priest in the order of his division before God,
Luke 1:9 according to the custom of the priesthood, he obtained by lot to burn incense, entering into the sanctuary of the Lord.
Luke 1:10 And the whole multitude of the people was praying outside at the hour of the incense.
Luke 1:11 And an angel of the Lord appeared to him, standing at the right of the altar of incense.
Luke 1:12 And Zechariah was troubled, seeing, and fear fell upon him.
Luke 1:13 But the angel said to him: Do not fear, Zechariah, because your petition was heard, and your wife Elizabeth shall bear you a son, and you shall call his name John.
Luke 1:14 And you shall have joy and exultation, and many shall rejoice at his birth.
Luke 1:15 For he shall be great before the Lord, and shall certainly not drink wine and strong drink, and shall be filled with the Holy Spirit even from his mother's womb.
Luke 1:16 And he shall turn many of the sons of Israel to the Lord their God.
Luke 1:17 And he shall go before him in the spirit and power of Elijah, to turn hearts of fathers to children, and the disobedient in the understanding of the righteous, to prepare for the Lord a people made ready.
Luke 1:18 And Zechariah said to the angel: By what shall I know this? For I am an old man, and my wife advanced in her days.
Luke 1:19 And the angel answered and said to him: I am Gabriel, who stands before God, and I was sent to speak to you and announce these good things to you.
Luke 1:20 And behold, you shall be silent and unable to speak until the day these things happen, because you did not believe my words, which shall be fulfilled in their time.
Luke 1:21 And the people were awaiting Zechariah, and were marveling at his delaying in the sanctuary.
Luke 1:22 But going out, he could not speak to them, and they recognized that he has seen a vision in the sanctuary; and he was making signs to them and remained mute.
Luke 1:23 And it happened, when the days of his ministry were fulfilled, he went away into his house.
Luke 1:24 And after these days Elizabeth his wife conceived, and was hiding herself five months, saying:
Luke 1:25 Thus the Lord has done for me in days in which he looked upon me to take away my reproach among men.
Luke 1:26 And in the sixth month the angel Gabriel was sent by God into a city of Galilee named Nazareth,
Luke 1:27 to a virgin betrothed to a man named Joseph, of the house of David, and the virgin's name was Mariam.
Luke 1:28 And the angel entered to her and said: Rejoice, you who have been graced; the Lord is with you; blessed are you among women.
Luke 1:29 And seeing, she was greatly troubled at his word, and was reasoning what manner of greeting this might be.
Luke 1:30 And the angel said to her: Do not fear, Mariam, for you found grace with God.
Luke 1:31 And behold, you shall conceive in the womb and bear a son, and shall call his name Jesus.
Luke 1:32 He shall be great and shall be called Son of the Most High, and the Lord God shall give him the throne of David his father,
Luke 1:33 and he shall reign over the house of Jacob into the ages, and of his kingdom there shall be no end.
Luke 1:34 And Mariam said to the angel: How shall this be, since I do not know a man?
Luke 1:35 And the angel answered and said to her: The Holy Spirit shall come upon you, and power of the Most High shall overshadow you; therefore also the holy thing being born shall be called Son of God.
Luke 1:36 And behold, Elizabeth your relative, she also has conceived a son in her old age, and this is the sixth month for her who is called barren.
Luke 1:37 Because no word shall be impossible with God.
Luke 1:38 And Mariam said: Behold, the slave woman of the Lord; may it happen to me according to your saying. And the angel went away from her.
Luke 1:39 And Mariam rose in these days and went into the hill country with haste, into a city of Judah,
Luke 1:40 and entered into the house of Zechariah and greeted Elizabeth.
Luke 1:41 And it happened, when Elizabeth heard the greeting of Mary, the infant leaped in her womb, and Elizabeth was filled with the Holy Spirit,
Luke 1:42 and cried aloud with a great voice and said: Blessed are you among women, and blessed is the fruit of your womb.
Luke 1:43 And from where is this for me, that the mother of my Lord should come to me?
Luke 1:44 For behold, when the voice of your greeting came into my ears, the infant in my womb leaped in exultation.
Luke 1:45 And blessed is she who believed, because there shall be a fulfillment of the things spoken to her from the Lord.
Luke 1:46 And Mariam said: My soul magnifies the Lord,
Luke 1:47 and my spirit exulted in God my Savior,
Luke 1:48 because he looked upon the lowliness of his slave woman; for behold, from now all generations shall call me blessed,
Luke 1:49 because the Mighty One did great things for me, and holy is his name,
Luke 1:50 and his mercy is into generations of generations to those fearing him.
Luke 1:51 He made strength with his arm; he scattered the arrogant in the thought of their heart.
Luke 1:52 He took rulers down from thrones and exalted the lowly.
Luke 1:53 He filled the hungry with good things and sent the rich away empty.
Luke 1:54 He helped Israel his servant, to remember mercy,
Luke 1:55 as he spoke to our fathers, to Abraham and to his seed forever.
Luke 1:56 And Mariam remained with her about three months, and returned into her house.
Luke 1:57 And for Elizabeth the time was fulfilled for her to give birth, and she bore a son.
Luke 1:58 And her neighbors and relatives heard that the Lord magnified his mercy with her, and were rejoicing with her.
Luke 1:59 And it happened on the eighth day, they came to circumcise the child, and were calling it by the name of its father, Zechariah.
Luke 1:60 And his mother answered and said: No, but he shall be called John.
Luke 1:61 And they said to her: There is no one among your relatives who is called by this name.
Luke 1:62 And they were making signs to his father, what he might wish him to be called.
Luke 1:63 And asking for a little tablet, he wrote, saying: John is his name. And all marveled.
Luke 1:64 And immediately his mouth was opened, and his tongue, and he was speaking, blessing God.
Luke 1:65 And fear came upon all those dwelling around them, and in the whole hill country of Judea all these sayings were being discussed.
Luke 1:66 And all who heard put them in their heart, saying: What, then, shall this child be? And the hand of the Lord was with him.
Luke 1:67 And Zechariah his father was filled with the Holy Spirit and prophesied, saying:
Luke 1:68 Blessed is the Lord God of Israel, because he visited and made redemption for his people,
Luke 1:69 and raised a horn of salvation for us in the house of David his servant,
Luke 1:70 as he spoke through the mouth of his holy prophets from of old,
Luke 1:71 salvation from our enemies and from the hand of all who hate us,
Luke 1:72 to do mercy with our fathers and to remember his holy covenant,
Luke 1:73 the oath which he swore to Abraham our father,
Luke 1:74 to give us, rescued from the hand of our enemies, to serve him without fear,
Luke 1:75 in holiness and righteousness before him all the days of our life.
Luke 1:76 And you, child, shall be called prophet of the Most High, for you shall go before the face of the Lord to prepare his ways,
Luke 1:77 to give knowledge of salvation to his people in forgiveness of their sins,
Luke 1:78 because of the inward mercy of our God, in which the dawn from on high visited us,
Luke 1:79 to shine upon those sitting in darkness and shadow of death, to direct our feet into a way of peace.
Luke 1:80 And the child was growing and becoming strong in spirit, and was in the deserts until the day of his manifestation to Israel.

## Chapter 2

Luke 2:1 And it happened in those days, a decree went out from Caesar Augustus that the whole inhabited world be registered.
Luke 2:2 This registration first happened while Quirinius governed Syria.
Luke 2:3 And all were going to be registered, each into his own city.
Luke 2:4 And Joseph also went up from Galilee, from the city Nazareth, into Judea, into David's city which is called Bethlehem, because he was of the house and family of David,
Luke 2:5 to be registered with Mariam, the wife betrothed to him, who was pregnant.
Luke 2:6 And it happened, while they were there, the days were fulfilled for her to give birth.
Luke 2:7 And she bore her firstborn son and swaddled him and laid him in the manger, because there was no place for them in the lodging.
Luke 2:8 And there were shepherds in the same region staying in the fields and keeping watches of the night over their flock.
Luke 2:9 And behold, an angel of the Lord stood by them, and the glory of the Lord shone around them, and they feared a great fear.
Luke 2:10 And the angel said to them: Do not fear, for behold, I announce to you great joy which shall be for all the people,
Luke 2:11 because a Savior was born for you today, who is Christ the Lord, in David's city.
Luke 2:12 And this is the sign for you: You shall find an infant swaddled, lying in the manger.
Luke 2:13 And suddenly with the angel there was a multitude of a heavenly army, praising God and saying:
Luke 2:14 Glory to God in the highest, and upon earth peace, goodwill among men.
Luke 2:15 And it happened, when the angels went away from them into the heaven, the men, the shepherds, said to one another: Let us indeed pass through until Bethlehem and see this saying which has happened, which the Lord made known to us.
Luke 2:16 And they came hastening and found both Mariam and Joseph, and the infant lying in the manger.
Luke 2:17 And seeing, they made known concerning the saying spoken to them concerning this child.
Luke 2:18 And all who heard marveled concerning the things spoken to them by the shepherds.
Luke 2:19 But Mariam was keeping all these sayings, bringing them together in her heart.
Luke 2:20 And the shepherds returned, glorifying and praising God over everything which they heard and saw, as it was spoken to them.
Luke 2:21 And when eight days were fulfilled for circumcising the child, his name also was called Jesus, the name called by the angel before he was conceived in the womb.
Luke 2:22 And when the days of their cleansing were fulfilled according to the law of Moses, they brought him up into Jerusalem to present him to the Lord,
Luke 2:23 as it is written in the law of the Lord: Every male opening a womb shall be called holy to the Lord,
Luke 2:24 and to give a sacrifice according to what is said in the law of the Lord: A pair of turtledoves or two young pigeons.
Luke 2:25 And behold, there was a man in Jerusalem named Simeon, and this man was righteous and devout, awaiting the consolation of Israel, and the Holy Spirit was upon him.
Luke 2:26 And it had been revealed to him by the Holy Spirit not to see death before he should see the Christ of the Lord.
Luke 2:27 And he came in the Spirit into the temple, and when the parents brought in the child Jesus to do concerning him according to the custom of the law,
Luke 2:28 he also received him into his arms and blessed God and said:
Luke 2:29 Now you release your slave, Master, according to your saying, in peace,
Luke 2:30 because my eyes saw your salvation,
Luke 2:31 which you prepared before the face of all the peoples,
Luke 2:32 a light for revelation of nations and glory of your people Israel.
Luke 2:33 And Joseph and his mother were marveling at the things spoken concerning him.
Luke 2:34 And Simeon blessed them and said to Mariam his mother: Behold, this one is appointed for falling and rising of many in Israel, and for a sign spoken against,
Luke 2:35 and a sword shall pass through your own soul also, so that reasonings from many hearts may be revealed.
Luke 2:36 And there was Anna a prophetess, daughter of Phanuel, of the tribe of Asher; she was advanced in many days, having lived with a husband seven years from her virginity,
Luke 2:37 and she was a widow of about eighty-four years, who did not depart from the temple, serving with fastings and petitions night and day.
Luke 2:38 And she, standing by in that very hour, was giving thanks to the Lord and speaking concerning him to all those awaiting redemption in Jerusalem.
Luke 2:39 And when they finished everything according to the law of the Lord, they returned into Galilee, into their city Nazareth.
Luke 2:40 And the child was growing and becoming strong in spirit, being filled with wisdom, and grace of God was upon him.
Luke 2:41 And his parents were going yearly into Jerusalem at the feast of the Passover.
Luke 2:42 And when he became twelve years old, they went up into Jerusalem according to the custom of the feast,
Luke 2:43 and having completed the days, as they returned, the boy Jesus remained in Jerusalem, and Joseph and his mother did not know.
Luke 2:44 And supposing him to be in the company, they came a day's journey and were searching for him among the relatives and acquaintances.
Luke 2:45 And not finding him, they returned into Jerusalem, seeking him.
Luke 2:46 And it happened after three days, they found him in the temple, sitting in the midst of the teachers, both hearing them and questioning them.
Luke 2:47 And all hearing him were astonished at his understanding and answers.
Luke 2:48 And seeing him, they were amazed, and his mother said to him: Child, why did you do so to us? Behold, your father and I were seeking you in pain.
Luke 2:49 And he said to them: Why is it that you were seeking me? Did you not know that I must be in the things of my Father?
Luke 2:50 And they did not understand the saying which he spoke to them.
Luke 2:51 And he descended with them and came into Nazareth and was subject to them; and his mother was keeping all these sayings in her heart.
Luke 2:52 And Jesus was advancing in wisdom and age and grace with God and men.

## Chapter 3

Luke 3:1 And in the fifteenth year of the rule of Tiberius Caesar, Pontius Pilate governing Judea, and Herod being tetrarch of Galilee, and Philip his brother being tetrarch of the region of Iturea and Trachonitis, and Lysanias being tetrarch of Abilene,
Luke 3:2 under high priests Annas and Caiaphas, a word of God came upon John the son of Zechariah in the desert.
Luke 3:3 And he came into the whole surrounding region of the Jordan, proclaiming a baptism of repentance for forgiveness of sins,
Luke 3:4 as it is written in the book of words of Isaiah the prophet, saying: A voice of one crying in the desert: Prepare the way of the Lord; make his paths straight.
Luke 3:5 Every ravine shall be filled, and every mountain and hill shall be humbled, and the crooked things shall become straight, and the rough ways smooth ways,
Luke 3:6 and all flesh shall see the salvation of God.
Luke 3:7 Therefore he was saying to the crowds going out to be baptized by him: Offspring of vipers, who showed you to flee from the coming wrath?
Luke 3:8 Therefore produce fruits worthy of repentance, and do not begin to say among yourselves: We have Abraham as father; for I say to you that God can raise children for Abraham from these stones.
Luke 3:9 And already the axe also lies at the root of the trees; therefore every tree not producing good fruit is cut down and cast into fire.
Luke 3:10 And the crowds were questioning him, saying: What, therefore, shall we do?
Luke 3:11 And he answered and says to them: He who has two tunics, let him share with the one not having, and he who has foods, let him do likewise.
Luke 3:12 And tax collectors also came to be baptized and said to him: Teacher, what shall we do?
Luke 3:13 And he said to them: Collect nothing more than what has been directed for you.
Luke 3:14 And soldiers also were questioning him, saying: And we, what shall we do? And he said to them: Extort no one nor accuse falsely, and be content with your wages.
Luke 3:15 And while the people awaited, and all were reasoning in their hearts concerning John, whether he might be the Christ,
Luke 3:16 John answered all, saying: I indeed baptize you with water, but the one stronger than I comes, whose strap of his sandals I am not sufficient to loose; he shall baptize you in the Holy Spirit and fire,
Luke 3:17 whose winnowing shovel is in his hand, and he shall thoroughly cleanse his threshing floor and gather the wheat into his storehouse, but the chaff he shall burn up with unquenchable fire.
Luke 3:18 Therefore, exhorting with many other things also, he was announcing good news to the people.
Luke 3:19 But Herod the tetrarch, being reproved by him concerning Herodias, the wife of Philip his brother, and concerning all the evil things which Herod did,
Luke 3:20 added this also to all, and shut John in the prison.
Luke 3:21 And it happened, when all the people were baptized, and Jesus was baptized and praying, the heaven was opened,
Luke 3:22 and the Holy Spirit descended in bodily form like a dove upon him, and a voice came from heaven, saying: You are my beloved Son; in you I was well pleased.
Luke 3:23 And Jesus himself was about thirty years old, beginning, being, as was supposed, son of Joseph, of Heli,
Luke 3:24 of Matthat, of Levi, of Melchi, of Janna, of Joseph,
Luke 3:25 of Mattathias, of Amos, of Nahum, of Esli, of Naggai,
Luke 3:26 of Maath, of Mattathias, of Semei, of Joseph, of Judah,
Luke 3:27 of Joanna, of Rhesa, of Zerubbabel, of Salathiel, of Neri,
Luke 3:28 of Melchi, of Addi, of Cosam, of Elmodam, of Er,
Luke 3:29 of Joses, of Eliezer, of Joreim, of Matthat, of Levi,
Luke 3:30 of Simeon, of Judah, of Joseph, of Jonan, of Eliakim,
Luke 3:31 of Melea, of Mainan, of Mattatha, of Nathan, of David,
Luke 3:32 of Jesse, of Obed, of Boaz, of Salmon, of Naasson,
Luke 3:33 of Aminadab, of Aram, of Esrom, of Phares, of Judah,
Luke 3:34 of Jacob, of Isaac, of Abraham, of Thara, of Nachor,
Luke 3:35 of Saruch, of Ragau, of Phalek, of Eber, of Sala,
Luke 3:36 of Cainan, of Arphaxad, of Shem, of Noah, of Lamech,
Luke 3:37 of Mathusala, of Enoch, of Jared, of Maleleel, of Cainan,
Luke 3:38 of Enos, of Seth, of Adam, of God.

## Chapter 4

Luke 4:1 And Jesus, full of the Holy Spirit, returned from the Jordan and was being led in the Spirit into the desert,
Luke 4:2 forty days being tempted by the devil; and he ate nothing in those days, and when they were completed, afterward he was hungry.
Luke 4:3 And the devil said to him: If you are God's Son, tell this stone to become bread.
Luke 4:4 And Jesus answered him, saying: It is written that man shall not live upon bread alone, but upon every word of God.
Luke 4:5 And the devil brought him up into a high mountain and showed him all the kingdoms of the inhabited world in a moment of time.
Luke 4:6 And the devil said to him: I shall give you all this authority and their glory, because it has been handed over to me, and I give it to whomever I wish.
Luke 4:7 Therefore, if you worship before me, everything shall be yours.
Luke 4:8 And Jesus answered him and said: Go behind me, Satan, for it is written: You shall worship the Lord your God, and him alone you shall serve.
Luke 4:9 And he led him into Jerusalem and stood him upon the pinnacle of the temple and said to him: If you are God's Son, cast yourself down from here,
Luke 4:10 for it is written that he shall command his angels concerning you to guard you,
Luke 4:11 and that upon hands they shall take you up, lest you strike your foot against a stone.
Luke 4:12 And Jesus answered and said to him: It is said: You shall not test the Lord your God.
Luke 4:13 And completing every temptation, the devil departed from him until a time.
Luke 4:14 And Jesus returned in the power of the Spirit into Galilee, and a report concerning him went out throughout the whole surrounding region.
Luke 4:15 And he was teaching in their synagogues, being glorified by all.
Luke 4:16 And he came into Nazareth, where he had been brought up, and entered according to his custom on the Sabbath day into the synagogue, and rose to read.
Luke 4:17 And a book of Isaiah the prophet was handed to him, and unrolling the book, he found the place where it was written:
Luke 4:18 The Spirit of the Lord is upon me, because he anointed me to announce good news to the poor; he has sent me to heal those broken in heart, to proclaim release to captives and recovery of sight to the blind, to send those crushed away in release,
Luke 4:19 to proclaim an acceptable year of the Lord.
Luke 4:20 And rolling the book and giving it back to the attendant, he sat down, and the eyes of all in the synagogue were gazing at him.
Luke 4:21 And he began to say to them: Today this Scripture has been fulfilled in your ears.
Luke 4:22 And all were testifying to him and marveling at the words of grace coming out of his mouth, and were saying: Is this not Joseph's son?
Luke 4:23 And he said to them: Certainly you shall say this parable to me: Physician, heal yourself; whatever we heard happened in Capernaum, do also here in your homeland.
Luke 4:24 And he said: Amen, I say to you that no prophet is acceptable in his homeland.
Luke 4:25 But in truth I say to you: Many widows were in Israel in Elijah's days, when the heaven was shut for three years and six months, when a great famine came upon the whole earth,
Luke 4:26 and Elijah was sent to none of them except to Sarepta of Sidon, to a widow woman.
Luke 4:27 And many lepers were in Israel under Elisha the prophet, and none of them was cleansed except Naaman the Syrian.
Luke 4:28 And all in the synagogue were filled with rage, hearing these things,
Luke 4:29 and rising, cast him outside the city and led him until the brow of the mountain upon which their city had been built, to throw him down the precipice.
Luke 4:30 But he passed through their midst and was going away.
Luke 4:31 And he descended into Capernaum, a city of Galilee, and was teaching them on the Sabbath.
Luke 4:32 And they were astonished at his teaching, because his word was with authority.
Luke 4:33 And in the synagogue was a man having a spirit of an unclean demon, and he cried out with a great voice,
Luke 4:34 saying: Ah! What is between us and you, Jesus the Nazarene? Did you come to destroy us? I know you, who you are: the Holy One of God.
Luke 4:35 And Jesus rebuked him, saying: Be silenced and come out of him. And the demon threw him into the midst and came out from him, harming him nothing.
Luke 4:36 And amazement came upon all, and they were speaking with one another, saying: What is this word, that with authority and power he commands the unclean spirits, and they come out?
Luke 4:37 And a report concerning him was going out into every place of the surrounding region.
Luke 4:38 And rising from the synagogue, he entered into Simon's house; and Simon's mother-in-law was held by a great fever, and they asked him concerning her.
Luke 4:39 And standing over her, he rebuked the fever, and it left her; and immediately rising, she was serving them.
Luke 4:40 And as the sun set, all who had people sick with various diseases brought them to him; and laying his hands upon each one of them, he healed them.
Luke 4:41 And demons also were coming out from many, crying and saying: You are the Christ, the Son of God. And rebuking, he did not allow them to speak, because they knew him to be the Christ.
Luke 4:42 And when day came, he went out and went into a deserted place; and the crowds were seeking him and came to him and were holding him back from going away from them.
Luke 4:43 But he said to them: I must announce the kingdom of God to the other cities also, because for this I have been sent.
Luke 4:44 And he was proclaiming in the synagogues of Galilee.

## Chapter 5

Luke 5:1 And it happened, while the crowd pressed upon him to hear the word of God, he was standing beside the lake of Gennesaret,
Luke 5:2 and saw two boats standing beside the lake, but the fishermen had gone out of them and were washing the nets.
Luke 5:3 And entering into one of the boats, which was Simon's, he asked him to put out a little from the earth; and sitting down, he was teaching the crowds from the boat.
Luke 5:4 And when he ceased speaking, he said to Simon: Put out into the deep, and lower your nets for a catch.
Luke 5:5 And Simon answered and said to him: Master, laboring through the whole night, we took nothing; but upon your saying I shall lower the net.
Luke 5:6 And doing this, they enclosed a great multitude of fish, and their net was tearing.
Luke 5:7 And they signaled to the partners in the other boat to come and help them; and they came and filled both boats, so that they were sinking.
Luke 5:8 And Simon Peter, seeing, fell at Jesus' knees, saying: Go out from me, because I am a sinful man, Lord.
Luke 5:9 For amazement encompassed him and all those with him at the catch of fish which they took,
Luke 5:10 and likewise James and John, sons of Zebedee, who were partners with Simon. And Jesus said to Simon: Do not fear; from now you shall be catching men alive.
Luke 5:11 And bringing the boats to the earth, they left everything and followed him.
Luke 5:12 And it happened while he was in one of the cities, behold, a man full of leprosy; and seeing Jesus, he fell upon his face and petitioned him, saying: Lord, if you wish, you can cleanse me.
Luke 5:13 And stretching out his hand, he touched him, saying: I wish; be cleansed. And immediately the leprosy went away from him.
Luke 5:14 And he commanded him to tell no one, but: Go, show yourself to the priest, and offer concerning your cleansing as Moses commanded, as a testimony to them.
Luke 5:15 But the word concerning him was spreading more, and many crowds were gathering to hear and to be healed by him from their illnesses.
Luke 5:16 But he was withdrawing in the deserts and praying.
Luke 5:17 And it happened on one of the days, he was teaching, and Pharisees and teachers of the law were sitting, who had come from every village of Galilee and Judea and Jerusalem; and power of the Lord was there to heal them.
Luke 5:18 And behold, men carrying upon a bed a man who was paralyzed, and they were seeking to bring him in and place him before him.
Luke 5:19 And not finding by what way to bring him in because of the crowd, they went up upon the roof and through the tiles let him down with the little bed into the midst before Jesus.
Luke 5:20 And seeing their faith, he said to him: Man, your sins have been forgiven you.
Luke 5:21 And the scribes and the Pharisees began to reason, saying: Who is this who speaks blasphemies? Who can forgive sins except God alone?
Luke 5:22 And Jesus recognized their reasonings and answered and said to them: What do you reason in your hearts?
Luke 5:23 Which is easier, to say: Your sins have been forgiven you, or to say: Rise and walk?
Luke 5:24 But so that you may know that the Son of man has authority upon the earth to forgive sins, he said to the paralyzed man: I say to you: Rise, and taking up your little bed, go into your house.
Luke 5:25 And immediately rising before them, he took up what he lay upon and went into his house, glorifying God.
Luke 5:26 And astonishment took all, and they were glorifying God and were filled with fear, saying: We saw extraordinary things today.
Luke 5:27 And after these things he went out and beheld a tax collector named Levi sitting at the tax office, and said to him: Follow me.
Luke 5:28 And leaving everything, he rose and followed him.
Luke 5:29 And Levi made a great reception for him in his house, and there was a great crowd of tax collectors and others who were reclining with them.
Luke 5:30 And their scribes and the Pharisees were grumbling to his disciples, saying: Why do you eat and drink with tax collectors and sinners?
Luke 5:31 And Jesus answered and said to them: Those healthy have no need of a physician, but those ill.
Luke 5:32 I have not come to call righteous men, but sinners to repentance.
Luke 5:33 And they said to him: Why do John's disciples fast often and make petitions, and likewise those of the Pharisees, but yours eat and drink?
Luke 5:34 And he said to them: Can you make the sons of the bridal chamber fast while the bridegroom is with them?
Luke 5:35 But days shall come, and when the bridegroom is taken away from them, then they shall fast in those days.
Luke 5:36 And he also was telling them a parable: No one puts a patch of a new garment upon an old garment; otherwise he both tears the new, and the patch from the new does not agree with the old.
Luke 5:37 And no one puts new wine into old wineskins; otherwise the new wine shall burst the wineskins, and it shall be poured out, and the wineskins shall perish.
Luke 5:38 But new wine must be put into fresh wineskins, and both are preserved.
Luke 5:39 And no one who drinks old immediately wishes new, for he says: The old is better.

## Chapter 6

Luke 6:1 And it happened on a second-first Sabbath, he passed through the grainfields, and his disciples were plucking the ears of grain and eating, rubbing them with their hands.
Luke 6:2 And some of the Pharisees said to them: Why do you do what is not lawful to do on the Sabbath?
Luke 6:3 And Jesus answered them and said: Have you not even read this which David did when he was hungry, he and those with him,
Luke 6:4 how he entered into the house of God and took the loaves of the presentation and ate, and also gave to those with him, which it is not lawful to eat except for the priests alone?
Luke 6:5 And he was saying to them that the Son of man is Lord also of the Sabbath.
Luke 6:6 And it happened also on another Sabbath, he entered into the synagogue and taught, and there was a man there, and his right hand was withered.
Luke 6:7 And the scribes and the Pharisees were watching him, whether he would heal on the Sabbath, so that they might find an accusation against him.
Luke 6:8 But he knew their reasonings and said to the man having the withered hand: Rise and stand in the midst. And rising, he stood.
Luke 6:9 Therefore Jesus said to them: I shall question you: What is lawful on the Sabbath, to do good or to do evil, to save a soul or to destroy?
Luke 6:10 And looking around at them all, he said to the man: Stretch out your hand. And he did so, and his hand was restored healthy as the other.
Luke 6:11 But they were filled with madness and were discussing with one another what they might do to Jesus.
Luke 6:12 And it happened in these days, he went out into the mountain to pray, and was spending the night in prayer to God.
Luke 6:13 And when day came, he called his disciples to him, and chose twelve from them, whom he also named apostles:
Luke 6:14 Simon, whom he also named Peter, and Andrew his brother, James and John, Philip and Bartholomew,
Luke 6:15 Matthew and Thomas, James the son of Alphaeus, and Simon called Zealot,
Luke 6:16 Judas of James, and Judas Iscariot, who also became a betrayer.
Luke 6:17 And descending with them, he stood upon a level place, and a crowd of his disciples and a great multitude of the people from all Judea and Jerusalem and the coast of Tyre and Sidon, who came to hear him and be healed from their diseases,
Luke 6:18 and those troubled by unclean spirits, and they were being healed.
Luke 6:19 And the whole crowd was seeking to touch him, because power was coming out from him and healing all.
Luke 6:20 And he lifted his eyes toward his disciples and was saying: Blessed are the poor, because yours is the kingdom of God.
Luke 6:21 Blessed are those hungry now, because you shall be filled. Blessed are those weeping now, because you shall laugh.
Luke 6:22 Blessed are you when men hate you, and when they separate you and reproach and cast out your name as evil because of the Son of man.
Luke 6:23 Rejoice in that day and leap, for behold, your reward is great in the heaven; for according to these things their fathers were doing to the prophets.
Luke 6:24 Nevertheless, woe to you rich, because you have your consolation in full.
Luke 6:25 Woe to you who have been filled, because you shall hunger. Woe to you laughing now, because you shall mourn and weep.
Luke 6:26 Woe to you when all men speak well of you, for according to these things their fathers were doing to the false prophets.
Luke 6:27 But I say to you who hear: Love your enemies; do well to those who hate you;
Luke 6:28 bless those who curse you, and pray for those who mistreat you.
Luke 6:29 To the one striking you upon the cheek, offer the other also; and from the one taking your garment, do not withhold the tunic also.
Luke 6:30 And give to everyone asking you, and from the one taking your things, do not demand them back.
Luke 6:31 And as you wish men to do to you, you also do to them likewise.
Luke 6:32 And if you love those loving you, what grace is yours? For even sinners love those loving them.
Luke 6:33 And if you do good to those doing good to you, what grace is yours? For even sinners do the same.
Luke 6:34 And if you lend to those from whom you hope to receive back, what grace is yours? For even sinners lend to sinners to receive back equal things.
Luke 6:35 Nevertheless, love your enemies and do good and lend, despairing of nothing; and your reward shall be great, and you shall be sons of the Most High, because he is kind to the ungrateful and evil.
Luke 6:36 Therefore become compassionate, as your Father also is compassionate.
Luke 6:37 And do not judge, and you shall certainly not be judged; do not condemn, and you shall certainly not be condemned; release, and you shall be released.
Luke 6:38 Give, and it shall be given to you; a good measure, pressed down and shaken and overflowing, they shall give into your bosom; for with the same measure with which you measure, it shall be measured back to you.
Luke 6:39 And he told them a parable: Can a blind man guide a blind man? Shall not both fall into a pit?
Luke 6:40 A disciple is not above his teacher, but everyone fully prepared shall be as his teacher.
Luke 6:41 And why do you see the speck in your brother's eye, but do not consider the beam in your own eye?
Luke 6:42 Or how can you say to your brother: Brother, allow me to cast out the speck in your eye, yourself not seeing the beam in your eye? Hypocrite, first cast out the beam from your eye, and then you shall see clearly to cast out the speck in your brother's eye.
Luke 6:43 For there is no good tree producing rotten fruit, nor a rotten tree producing good fruit.
Luke 6:44 For each tree is known from its own fruit; for they do not gather figs from thorns, nor harvest a grape from a bramble.
Luke 6:45 The good man brings forth the good from the good treasure of his heart, and the evil man brings forth the evil from the evil treasure of his heart; for his mouth speaks from the abundance of the heart.
Luke 6:46 And why do you call me: Lord, Lord, and do not do what I say?
Luke 6:47 Everyone coming to me and hearing my words and doing them, I shall show you whom he is like.
Luke 6:48 He is like a man building a house, who dug and deepened and placed a foundation upon the rock; and when a flood came, the river broke against that house and was not strong enough to shake it, for it had been founded upon the rock.
Luke 6:49 But the one hearing and not doing is like a man who built a house upon the earth without a foundation, against which the river broke, and immediately it fell, and the collapse of that house became great.

## Chapter 7

Luke 7:1 And when he fulfilled all his sayings in the hearing of the people, he entered into Capernaum.
Luke 7:2 And a certain centurion's slave, who was precious to him, was ill and about to die.
Luke 7:3 And hearing concerning Jesus, he sent elders of the Jews to him, asking him to come and save his slave.
Luke 7:4 And arriving at Jesus, they were begging him earnestly, saying: He is worthy for whom you shall grant this,
Luke 7:5 for he loves our nation, and he himself built the synagogue for us.
Luke 7:6 And Jesus was going with them; and already, when he was not far from the house, the centurion sent friends to him, saying to him: Lord, do not trouble yourself, for I am not sufficient that you enter under my roof.
Luke 7:7 Therefore neither did I deem myself worthy to come to you, but speak with a word, and my servant shall be healed.
Luke 7:8 For I also am a man placed under authority, having soldiers under myself, and I say to this one: Go, and he goes; and to another: Come, and he comes; and to my slave: Do this, and he does.
Luke 7:9 And Jesus heard these things and marveled at him, and turning to the crowd following him, said: I say to you, not even in Israel did I find such faith.
Luke 7:10 And those sent returned into the house and found the sick slave healthy.
Luke 7:11 And it happened on the next day, he was going into a city called Nain, and many of his disciples and a great crowd were going with him.
Luke 7:12 And when he drew near to the gate of the city, behold, a dead man was being carried out, the only son of his mother, and she was a widow; and a considerable crowd of the city was with her.
Luke 7:13 And the Lord saw her and had compassion on her and said to her: Do not weep.
Luke 7:14 And approaching, he touched the bier, and those carrying stood still; and he said: Young man, I say to you, rise.
Luke 7:15 And the dead man sat up and began to speak, and he gave him to his mother.
Luke 7:16 And fear took all, and they were glorifying God, saying: A great prophet has been raised among us; and: God visited his people.
Luke 7:17 And this word concerning him went out in the whole of Judea and in the whole surrounding region.
Luke 7:18 And his disciples reported to John concerning all these things.
Luke 7:19 And John called two of his disciples to him and sent to Jesus, saying: Are you the one coming, or do we await another?
Luke 7:20 And the men arrived at him and said: John the Baptist has sent us to you, saying: Are you the one coming, or do we await another?
Luke 7:21 And in that very hour he healed many from diseases and afflictions and evil spirits, and granted many blind people to see.
Luke 7:22 And Jesus answered and said to them: Go and report to John what you saw and heard: that blind people see again, lame people walk, lepers are cleansed, deaf people hear, dead people are raised, poor people receive good news.
Luke 7:23 And blessed is whoever is not made to stumble at me.
Luke 7:24 And when John's messengers went away, he began to say to the crowds concerning John: What have you gone out into the desert to behold? A reed shaken by wind?
Luke 7:25 But what have you gone out to see? A man clothed in soft garments? Behold, those living in glorious clothing and luxury are in the royal palaces.
Luke 7:26 But what have you gone out to see? A prophet? Yes, I say to you, and more than a prophet.
Luke 7:27 This is he concerning whom it is written: Behold, I send my messenger before your face, who shall prepare your way before you.
Luke 7:28 For I say to you: Among those born of women there is no prophet greater than John the Baptist, but the lesser in the kingdom of God is greater than he.
Luke 7:29 And all the people hearing, and the tax collectors, justified God, being baptized with John's baptism.
Luke 7:30 But the Pharisees and the lawyers rejected the counsel of God for themselves, not being baptized by him.
Luke 7:31 And the Lord said: To what, therefore, shall I liken the men of this generation, and what are they like?
Luke 7:32 They are like children sitting in a marketplace and calling to one another and saying: We played the flute for you and you did not dance; we lamented for you and you did not weep.
Luke 7:33 For John the Baptist has come neither eating bread nor drinking wine, and you say: He has a demon.
Luke 7:34 The Son of man has come eating and drinking, and you say: Behold, a gluttonous man and wine-drinker, a friend of tax collectors and sinners.
Luke 7:35 And wisdom was justified by all her children.
Luke 7:36 And one of the Pharisees was asking him to eat with him; and entering into the Pharisee's house, he reclined.
Luke 7:37 And behold, a woman in the city who was a sinner, recognizing that he reclines in the Pharisee's house, brought an alabaster vessel of ointment,
Luke 7:38 and standing behind at his feet, weeping, began to wet his feet with her tears, and was wiping them with the hairs of her head and kissing his feet fervently and anointing with the ointment.
Luke 7:39 And the Pharisee who invited him saw and said in himself, saying: If this man were a prophet, he would know who and what manner of woman touches him, that she is a sinner.
Luke 7:40 And Jesus answered and said to him: Simon, I have something to tell you. And he says: Teacher, speak.
Luke 7:41 A certain lender had two debtors; the one owed five hundred denarii, and the other fifty.
Luke 7:42 And as they had nothing to repay, he freely forgave both; therefore tell me, which of them shall love him more?
Luke 7:43 And Simon answered and said: I suppose the one to whom he forgave more. And he said to him: You judged correctly.
Luke 7:44 And turning to the woman, he said to Simon: Do you see this woman? I entered into your house; you gave no water for my feet, but she wet my feet with tears and wiped them with the hairs of her head.
Luke 7:45 You gave me no kiss, but she, from when I entered, did not cease kissing my feet fervently.
Luke 7:46 You did not anoint my head with oil, but she anointed my feet with ointment.
Luke 7:47 For which reason I say to you: Her many sins have been forgiven, because she loved much; but he to whom little is forgiven loves little.
Luke 7:48 And he said to her: Your sins have been forgiven.
Luke 7:49 And those reclining with him began to say among themselves: Who is this who even forgives sins?
Luke 7:50 And he said to the woman: Your faith has saved you; go into peace.

## Chapter 8

Luke 8:1 And it happened afterward, he was traveling through city and village, proclaiming and announcing the kingdom of God, and the twelve with him,
Luke 8:2 and certain women who had been healed from evil spirits and illnesses: Mary called Magdalene, from whom seven demons had gone out,
Luke 8:3 and Joanna, wife of Chuza, Herod's steward, and Susanna and many others, who were serving him from their possessions.
Luke 8:4 And a great crowd was gathering, and those from each city were coming to him; he spoke through a parable:
Luke 8:5 The sower went out to sow his seed, and as he sowed, some fell beside the road and was trampled, and the birds of the heaven devoured it.
Luke 8:6 And other fell upon the rock, and growing, withered because it had no moisture.
Luke 8:7 And other fell in the midst of the thorns, and the thorns grew together and choked it.
Luke 8:8 And other fell upon the good earth, and growing, produced fruit a hundredfold. Saying these things, he was calling: He who has ears to hear, let him hear.
Luke 8:9 And his disciples were questioning him, saying what this parable might be.
Luke 8:10 And he said: To you it has been given to know the mysteries of the kingdom of God, but to the rest in parables, so that seeing they may not see, and hearing may not understand.
Luke 8:11 And this is the parable: The seed is the word of God.
Luke 8:12 And those beside the road are those hearing; then the devil comes and takes the word from their heart, so that they may not believe and be saved.
Luke 8:13 And those upon the rock, who, when they hear, receive the word with joy, and these have no root, who believe for a time and in a time of temptation depart.
