Luke 8:14 And what fell into the thorns, these are those who heard, and going along are choked by cares and wealth and pleasures of life, and do not bring fruit to completion.
Luke 8:15 And what is in the good earth, these are those who, hearing the word in a beautiful and good heart, hold it and bear fruit in endurance.
Luke 8:16 And no one lighting a lamp covers it with a vessel or puts it beneath a bed, but sets it upon a lampstand, so that those entering may see the light.
Luke 8:17 For there is nothing hidden which shall not become manifest, nor concealed which shall not be known and come into the open.
Luke 8:18 Therefore see how you hear; for whoever has, to him it shall be given, and whoever does not have, even what he seems to have shall be taken from him.
Luke 8:19 And his mother and brothers arrived at him, and could not meet him because of the crowd.
Luke 8:20 And it was reported to him, saying: Your mother and brothers stand outside, wishing to see you.
Luke 8:21 And he answered and said to them: My mother and my brothers are these who hear the word of God and do it.
Luke 8:22 And it happened on one of the days, he entered into a boat, and his disciples, and said to them: Let us pass through to the other side of the lake. And they put out.
Luke 8:23 And while they sailed, he fell asleep, and a windstorm descended into the lake, and they were being filled and were in danger.
Luke 8:24 And approaching, they woke him, saying: Master, Master, we perish. And rising, he rebuked the wind and the surge of the water, and they ceased, and a calm came.
Luke 8:25 And he said to them: Where is your faith? And fearing, they marveled, saying to one another: Who, then, is this, that he commands even the winds and the water, and they obey him?
Luke 8:26 And they sailed down into the region of the Gadarenes, which is opposite Galilee.
Luke 8:27 And when he went out upon the earth, a certain man from the city met him, who had demons for considerable times and was not putting on a garment and was not remaining in a house, but in the tombs.
Luke 8:28 And seeing Jesus and crying out, he fell before him and said with a great voice: What is between me and you, Jesus, Son of the Most High God? I petition you, do not torture me.
Luke 8:29 For he was commanding the unclean spirit to come out from the man; for it had seized him many times, and he was bound with chains and shackles, being guarded; and tearing the bonds, he was being driven by the demon into the deserts.
Luke 8:30 And Jesus questioned him, saying: What is your name? And he said: Legion, because many demons entered into him.
Luke 8:31 And he was begging him not to command them to go away into the abyss.
Luke 8:32 And there was a herd of many pigs feeding in the mountain, and they were begging him to permit them to enter into those; and he permitted them.
Luke 8:33 And the demons came out from the man and entered into the pigs, and the herd rushed down the precipice into the lake and was drowned.
Luke 8:34 And those feeding saw what had happened and fled, and went and reported into the city and into the fields.
Luke 8:35 And they went out to see what has happened, and came to Jesus and found the man from whom the demons had gone out sitting clothed and in his right mind at Jesus' feet, and they feared.
Luke 8:36 And those who saw also reported to them how the demon-possessed man was saved.
Luke 8:37 And the whole multitude of the surrounding region of the Gadarenes asked him to go away from them, because they were held by great fear; and he entered into the boat and returned.
Luke 8:38 And the man from whom the demons had gone out was petitioning him to be with him; but Jesus dismissed him, saying:
Luke 8:39 Return into your house and recount how many things God did for you. And he went away, proclaiming throughout the whole city how many things Jesus did for him.
Luke 8:40 And it happened, when Jesus returned, the crowd received him, for all were awaiting him.
Luke 8:41 And behold, a man came named Jairus, and he was a ruler of the synagogue; and falling at Jesus' feet, he was begging him to enter into his house,
Luke 8:42 because he had an only daughter of about twelve years, and she was dying. And as he went, the crowds were choking him together.
Luke 8:43 And a woman being in a flow of blood for twelve years, who had spent her whole livelihood upon physicians, could not be healed by anyone,
Luke 8:44 approached from behind and touched the fringe of his garment, and immediately the flow of her blood stopped.
Luke 8:45 And Jesus said: Who touched me? And while all denied, Peter and those with him said: Master, the crowds hold you and press you, and you say: Who touched me?
Luke 8:46 But Jesus said: Someone touched me, for I knew power going out from me.
Luke 8:47 And the woman, seeing that she was not hidden, came trembling and fell before him and reported to him before all the people for what cause she touched him, and how she was healed immediately.
Luke 8:48 And he said to her: Take courage, daughter; your faith has saved you; go into peace.
Luke 8:49 While he was still speaking, someone comes from the synagogue ruler, saying to him: Your daughter has died; do not trouble the teacher.
Luke 8:50 But Jesus heard and answered him, saying: Do not fear; only believe, and she shall be saved.
Luke 8:51 And entering into the house, he allowed no one to enter except Peter and James and John, and the girl's father and mother.
Luke 8:52 And all were weeping and mourning her, but he said: Do not weep; she did not die, but sleeps.
Luke 8:53 And they were laughing at him, knowing that she died.
Luke 8:54 But he cast all outside and took hold of her hand and called, saying: Girl, rise.
Luke 8:55 And her spirit returned, and she rose immediately; and he directed that something be given her to eat.
Luke 8:56 And her parents were astonished, but he commanded them to tell no one what has happened.

## Chapter 9

Luke 9:1 And calling his twelve disciples together, he gave them power and authority over all the demons, and to heal diseases.
Luke 9:2 And he sent them to proclaim the kingdom of God and heal the sick.
Luke 9:3 And he said to them: Take nothing for the road, neither staffs nor bag nor bread nor silver, nor have two tunics each.
Luke 9:4 And into whatever house you enter, remain there and go out from there.
Luke 9:5 And as many as do not receive you, going out from that city, shake off even the dust from your feet as a testimony against them.
Luke 9:6 And going out, they were passing through the villages, announcing good news and healing everywhere.
Luke 9:7 And Herod the tetrarch heard all the things happening by him, and was perplexed because some said that John has been raised from the dead,
Luke 9:8 and some that Elijah appeared, and others that one prophet of the ancients rose.
Luke 9:9 And Herod said: John I beheaded; but who is this concerning whom I hear such things? And he was seeking to see him.
Luke 9:10 And the apostles returned and recounted to him whatever they did; and taking them with him, he withdrew privately into a deserted place of a city called Bethsaida.
Luke 9:11 But the crowds knew and followed him; and receiving them, he was speaking to them concerning the kingdom of God and healing those having need of healing.
Luke 9:12 And the day began to decline, and the twelve approached and said to him: Dismiss the crowd so that they may go into the surrounding villages and fields and lodge and find provisions, because here we are in a deserted place.
Luke 9:13 And he said to them: You give them something to eat. And they said: We have no more than five loaves and two fish, unless we go and buy foods for all this people.
Luke 9:14 For they were about five thousand men. And he said to his disciples: Make them recline in reclining groups of fifty each.
Luke 9:15 And they did so and made all recline.
Luke 9:16 And taking the five loaves and the two fish, he looked up into the heaven and blessed them and broke them, and was giving to the disciples to set before the crowd.
Luke 9:17 And all ate and were filled, and what remained of fragments for them was taken up, twelve baskets.
Luke 9:18 And it happened while he was praying alone, the disciples were with him, and he questioned them, saying: Who do the crowds say that I am?
Luke 9:19 And they answered and said: John the Baptist; and others Elijah; and others that a certain prophet of the ancients rose.
Luke 9:20 And he said to them: But you, who do you say that I am? And Peter answered and said: The Christ of God.
Luke 9:21 And rebuking them, he commanded to tell no one this,
Luke 9:22 saying that the Son of man must suffer many things and be rejected by the elders and chief priests and scribes, and be killed, and on the third day be raised.
Luke 9:23 And he was saying to all: If anyone wishes to come behind me, let him deny himself and take up his cross daily and follow me.
Luke 9:24 For whoever wishes to save his soul shall lose it, but whoever loses his soul because of me, this one shall save it.
Luke 9:25 For what does a man profit, gaining the whole world but destroying himself or suffering loss?
Luke 9:26 For whoever is ashamed of me and my words, of this one the Son of man shall be ashamed when he comes in his glory and that of the Father and of the holy angels.
Luke 9:27 But I say to you truly: There are some standing here who shall certainly not taste death until they see the kingdom of God.
Luke 9:28 And it happened about eight days after these words, he took Peter and John and James with him and went up into the mountain to pray.
Luke 9:29 And it happened while he prayed, the appearance of his face was different, and his clothing white, flashing.
Luke 9:30 And behold, two men were conversing with him, who were Moses and Elijah,
Luke 9:31 who appeared in glory and were speaking of his departure which he was about to fulfill in Jerusalem.
Luke 9:32 But Peter and those with him were weighed down with sleep; and staying awake, they saw his glory and the two men standing with him.
Luke 9:33 And it happened as they were parting from him, Peter said to Jesus: Master, it is good for us to be here, and let us make three tents, one for you and one for Moses and one for Elijah, not knowing what he says.
Luke 9:34 And while he said these things, a cloud came and overshadowed them; and they feared as those entered into the cloud.
Luke 9:35 And a voice came from the cloud, saying: This is my beloved Son; hear him.
Luke 9:36 And when the voice came, Jesus was found alone; and they were silent and reported to no one in those days anything of what they have seen.
Luke 9:37 And it happened on the next day, when they descended from the mountain, a great crowd met him.
Luke 9:38 And behold, a man from the crowd cried aloud, saying: Teacher, I petition you, look upon my son, because he is my only child.
Luke 9:39 And behold, a spirit takes him, and suddenly he cries, and it convulses him with foam, and scarcely withdraws from him, crushing him.
Luke 9:40 And I petitioned your disciples to cast it out, and they could not.
Luke 9:41 And Jesus answered and said: O unbelieving and perverted generation, until when shall I be with you and bear with you? Bring your son here.
Luke 9:42 And while he still approached, the demon threw him down and convulsed him; but Jesus rebuked the unclean spirit and healed the boy and gave him back to his father.
Luke 9:43 And all were astonished at the majesty of God. And while all marveled at everything which Jesus did, he said to his disciples:
Luke 9:44 You, put these words into your ears, for the Son of man is about to be handed over into the hands of men.
Luke 9:45 But they did not understand this saying, and it was concealed from them so that they might not perceive it, and they feared to ask him concerning this saying.
Luke 9:46 And a reasoning entered among them, who might be greater of them.
Luke 9:47 But Jesus, seeing the reasoning of their heart, took a child and stood it beside himself,
Luke 9:48 and said to them: Whoever receives this child in my name receives me, and whoever receives me receives the one who sent me; for he who is lesser among all of you, this one shall be great.
Luke 9:49 And John answered and said: Master, we saw someone casting out the demons in your name, and we hindered him because he does not follow with us.
Luke 9:50 And Jesus said to him: Do not hinder, for he who is not against us is for us.
Luke 9:51 And it happened as the days of his taking up were being fulfilled, he set his face to go into Jerusalem,
Luke 9:52 and sent messengers before his face; and they went and entered into a village of Samaritans, to prepare for him.
Luke 9:53 And they did not receive him, because his face was going into Jerusalem.
Luke 9:54 And his disciples James and John saw and said: Lord, do you wish us to say that fire descend from the heaven and consume them, as Elijah also did?
Luke 9:55 But turning, he rebuked them and said: You do not know of what manner of spirit you are.
Luke 9:56 For the Son of man did not come to destroy men's souls, but to save. And they went into another village.
Luke 9:57 And it happened as they went on the road, someone said to him: I shall follow you wherever you go, Lord.
Luke 9:58 And Jesus said to him: The foxes have dens and the birds of the heaven dwelling places, but the Son of man has nowhere to lay his head.
Luke 9:59 And he said to another: Follow me. But he said: Lord, permit me first to go and bury my father.
Luke 9:60 And Jesus said to him: Leave the dead to bury their own dead, but you go and announce the kingdom of God.
Luke 9:61 And another also said: I shall follow you, Lord, but first permit me to take leave of those in my house.
Luke 9:62 And Jesus said to him: No one putting his hand upon a plow and looking backward is fit for the kingdom of God.

## Chapter 10

Luke 10:1 And after these things the Lord appointed another seventy also and sent them two by two before his face into every city and place where he himself was about to come.
Luke 10:2 Therefore he was saying to them: The harvest indeed is great, but the workers few; therefore petition the Lord of the harvest to send out workers into his harvest.
Luke 10:3 Go; behold, I send you as lambs in the midst of wolves.
Luke 10:4 Do not carry a purse, nor bag, nor sandals, and greet no one along the road.
Luke 10:5 And into whatever house you enter, first say: Peace to this house.
Luke 10:6 And if a son of peace is there, your peace shall rest upon him; otherwise it shall return upon you.
Luke 10:7 And remain in the same house, eating and drinking the things from them, for the worker is worthy of his wage; do not move from house to house.
Luke 10:8 And into whatever city you enter and they receive you, eat the things set before you,
Luke 10:9 and heal the sick in it and say to them: The kingdom of God has drawn near upon you.
Luke 10:10 But into whatever city you enter and they do not receive you, go out into its streets and say:
Luke 10:11 Even the dust from your city which clung to us we wipe off for you; nevertheless know this, that the kingdom of God has drawn near upon you.
Luke 10:12 And I say to you that it shall be more bearable for Sodom in that day than for that city.
Luke 10:13 Woe to you, Chorazin! Woe to you, Bethsaida! Because if the mighty works which happened in you had happened in Tyre and Sidon, long ago they would have repented, sitting in sackcloth and ashes.
Luke 10:14 Nevertheless, it shall be more bearable for Tyre and Sidon in the judgment than for you.
Luke 10:15 And you, Capernaum, exalted until the heaven, shall be brought down until Hades.
Luke 10:16 He who hears you hears me, and he who rejects you rejects me, and he who rejects me rejects the one who sent me.
Luke 10:17 And the seventy returned with joy, saying: Lord, even the demons are subject to us in your name.
Luke 10:18 And he said to them: I was beholding Satan falling like lightning from the heaven.
Luke 10:19 Behold, I give you authority to tread upon serpents and scorpions and upon all the power of the enemy, and nothing shall certainly harm you.
Luke 10:20 Nevertheless, do not rejoice in this, that the spirits are subject to you, but rejoice rather that your names were written in the heavens.
Luke 10:21 In that very hour Jesus exulted in the spirit and said: I acknowledge you, Father, Lord of the heaven and the earth, because you hid these things from wise and understanding men and revealed them to infants; yes, Father, because so it became goodwill before you.
Luke 10:22 And turning to the disciples, he said: All things were handed over to me by my Father, and no one knows who the Son is except the Father, and who the Father is except the Son and whomever the Son wishes to reveal him to.
Luke 10:23 And turning to the disciples privately, he said: Blessed are the eyes seeing what you see.
Luke 10:24 For I say to you that many prophets and kings wished to see what you see and did not see, and to hear what you hear and did not hear.
Luke 10:25 And behold, a certain lawyer rose, testing him and saying: Teacher, doing what shall I inherit eternal life?
Luke 10:26 And he said to him: What is written in the law? How do you read?
Luke 10:27 And he answered and said: You shall love the Lord your God from your whole heart and from your whole soul and from your whole strength and from your whole mind, and your neighbor as yourself.
Luke 10:28 And he said to him: You answered correctly; do this and you shall live.
Luke 10:29 But wishing to justify himself, he said to Jesus: And who is my neighbor?
Luke 10:30 And Jesus took it up and said: A certain man was descending from Jerusalem into Jericho and fell among robbers, who stripped him and inflicted blows and went away, leaving him half dead.
Luke 10:31 And by coincidence a certain priest was descending on that road, and seeing him, passed by opposite.
Luke 10:32 And likewise also a Levite, coming to the place and seeing, passed by opposite.
Luke 10:33 But a certain Samaritan traveling came upon him, and seeing him, had compassion,
Luke 10:34 and approached and bound his wounds, pouring oil and wine; and mounting him upon his own beast, brought him into an inn and cared for him.
Luke 10:35 And on the next day, going out, he took out two denarii and gave them to the innkeeper and said to him: Care for him, and whatever you spend additionally, I shall repay you when I return.
Luke 10:36 Which, therefore, of these three seems to you to have become neighbor of the one who fell among the robbers?
Luke 10:37 And he said: The one who did mercy with him. Therefore Jesus said to him: Go, and you do likewise.
Luke 10:38 And it happened as they went, he entered into a certain village; and a certain woman named Martha received him into her house.
Luke 10:39 And she had a sister called Mary, who also sat at Jesus' feet and was hearing his word.
Luke 10:40 But Martha was distracted about much service; and standing by, she said: Lord, do you not care that my sister left me alone to serve? Therefore tell her to help me.
Luke 10:41 And Jesus answered and said to her: Martha, Martha, you are anxious and troubled about many things,
Luke 10:42 but there is need of one; and Mary chose the good portion, which shall not be taken away from her.

## Chapter 11

Luke 11:1 And it happened while he was praying in a certain place, when he ceased, one of his disciples said to him: Lord, teach us to pray, as John also taught his disciples.
Luke 11:2 And he said to them: When you pray, say: Our Father who is in the heavens, let your name be sanctified; let your kingdom come; let your will happen, as in heaven, also upon the earth.
Luke 11:3 Give us our daily bread day by day,
Luke 11:4 and forgive us our sins, for we ourselves also forgive everyone owing us; and do not bring us into temptation, but rescue us from the evil one.
Luke 11:5 And he said to them: Who of you shall have a friend and go to him at midnight and say to him: Friend, lend me three loaves,
Luke 11:6 because a friend of mine arrived at me from a journey, and I have nothing to set before him;
Luke 11:7 and that one answering from within says: Do not give me troubles; already the door has been shut, and my children are with me in the bed; I cannot rise and give you?
Luke 11:8 I say to you: Even if he shall not rise and give him because he is his friend, yet because of his shamelessness he shall rise and give him as many as he needs.
Luke 11:9 And I say to you: Ask, and it shall be given to you; seek, and you shall find; knock, and it shall be opened to you.
Luke 11:10 For everyone asking receives, and the one seeking finds, and to the one knocking it shall be opened.
Luke 11:11 And which father of you shall the son ask for bread, and he shall give him a stone? Or even a fish, and he shall give him a serpent instead of a fish?
Luke 11:12 Or even if he asks for an egg, shall he give him a scorpion?
Luke 11:13 Therefore, if you, being evil, know to give good gifts to your children, how much more shall the Father from heaven give the Holy Spirit to those asking him?
Luke 11:14 And he was casting out a demon, and it was mute; and it happened when the demon came out, the mute man spoke, and the crowds marveled.
Luke 11:15 But some of them said: By Beelzebul, ruler of the demons, he casts out the demons.
Luke 11:16 And others, testing, were seeking from him a sign from heaven.
Luke 11:17 But he knew their thoughts and said to them: Every kingdom divided against itself is desolated, and house falls upon house.
Luke 11:18 And if Satan also was divided against himself, how shall his kingdom stand? Because you say I cast out the demons by Beelzebul.
Luke 11:19 And if I cast out the demons by Beelzebul, by whom do your sons cast them out? For this reason they shall be your judges.
Luke 11:20 But if I cast out the demons by God's finger, then the kingdom of God has reached you.
Luke 11:21 When the strong man, fully armed, guards his own courtyard, his possessions are in peace.
Luke 11:22 But when one stronger than he comes upon him and conquers him, he takes away his full armor upon which he had trusted and distributes his spoils.
Luke 11:23 He who is not with me is against me, and he who does not gather with me scatters.
Luke 11:24 When the unclean spirit comes out from the man, it passes through waterless places seeking rest, and not finding, says: I shall return into my house from where I came out.
Luke 11:25 And coming, it finds it swept and adorned.
Luke 11:26 Then it goes and takes with it seven other spirits more evil than itself, and entering, they dwell there, and the last things of that man become worse than the first.
Luke 11:27 And it happened while he said these things, a certain woman lifted a voice from the crowd and said to him: Blessed is the womb which carried you and the breasts which you nursed.
Luke 11:28 But he said: Indeed rather, blessed are those hearing the word of God and keeping it.
Luke 11:29 And while the crowds gathered thickly, he began to say: This generation is evil; it seeks a sign, and a sign shall not be given it except the sign of Jonah the prophet.
Luke 11:30 For as Jonah became a sign to the Ninevites, so also shall the Son of man be to this generation.
Luke 11:31 The queen of the south shall be raised in the judgment with the men of this generation and shall condemn them, because she came from the ends of the earth to hear Solomon's wisdom; and behold, more than Solomon is here.
Luke 11:32 Men of Nineveh shall rise in the judgment with this generation and shall condemn it, because they repented at Jonah's proclamation; and behold, more than Jonah is here.
Luke 11:33 And no one lighting a lamp places it in a hidden place nor under the bushel, but upon the lampstand, so that those entering may see the light.
Luke 11:34 The lamp of the body is the eye; therefore when your eye is single, your whole body also is bright; but when it is evil, your body also is dark.
Luke 11:35 Therefore watch lest the light in you is darkness.
Luke 11:36 Therefore, if your whole body is bright, not having any dark part, it shall be wholly bright, as when the lamp lights you with its brightness.
Luke 11:37 And while he spoke, a certain Pharisee was asking him to dine with him; and entering, he reclined.
Luke 11:38 And the Pharisee saw and marveled that he did not first wash before the meal.
Luke 11:39 And the Lord said to him: Now you Pharisees cleanse the outside of the cup and the platter, but your inside is full of plunder and wickedness.
Luke 11:40 Fools, did not the one making the outside make the inside also?
Luke 11:41 Nevertheless, give the things within as alms, and behold, everything is clean for you.
Luke 11:42 But woe to you Pharisees, because you tithe the mint and the rue and every garden plant, and pass by judgment and the love of God; these you ought to have done, and not leave those.
Luke 11:43 Woe to you Pharisees, because you love the first seat in the synagogues and the greetings in the marketplaces.
Luke 11:44 Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites, because you are like the unmarked tombs, and the men walking above do not know.
Luke 11:45 And one of the lawyers answered and says to him: Teacher, saying these things, you insult us also.
Luke 11:46 And he said: Woe to you lawyers also, because you load men with burdens hard to bear, and you yourselves do not touch the burdens with one of your fingers.
Luke 11:47 Woe to you, because you build the monuments of the prophets, but your fathers killed them.
Luke 11:48 Therefore you testify and approve the works of your fathers, because they indeed killed them, but you build their monuments.
Luke 11:49 For this reason the wisdom of God also said: I shall send to them prophets and apostles, and some of them they shall kill and persecute,
Luke 11:50 so that the blood of all the prophets, poured out from the foundation of the world, may be demanded from this generation,
Luke 11:51 from Abel's blood until the blood of Zechariah, who perished between the altar and the house; yes, I say to you, it shall be demanded from this generation.
Luke 11:52 Woe to you lawyers, because you took away the key of knowledge; you yourselves did not enter, and you hindered those entering.
Luke 11:53 And while he said these things to them, the scribes and the Pharisees began to hold fiercely against him and question him about more things,
Luke 11:54 lying in wait for him and seeking to catch something out of his mouth so that they might accuse him.

## Chapter 12

Luke 12:1 Meanwhile, when the myriads of the crowd gathered together, so that they trampled one another, he began to say first to his disciples: Beware for yourselves of the leaven of the Pharisees, which is hypocrisy.
Luke 12:2 And there is nothing covered which shall not be revealed, and hidden which shall not be known.
Luke 12:3 Therefore whatever you said in the darkness shall be heard in the light, and what you spoke to the ear in the inner rooms shall be proclaimed upon the roofs.
Luke 12:4 And I say to you my friends: Do not fear those killing the body and after these things having nothing further to do.
Luke 12:5 But I shall show you whom to fear: Fear the one who after killing has authority to cast into Gehenna; yes, I say to you, fear this one.
Luke 12:6 Are not five sparrows sold for two assaria? And one of them is not forgotten before God.
Luke 12:7 But even all the hairs of your head have been numbered; therefore do not fear, you surpass many sparrows.
Luke 12:8 And I say to you: Everyone who acknowledges me before men, the Son of man also shall acknowledge him before the angels of God.
Luke 12:9 But the one denying me before men shall be denied before the angels of God.
Luke 12:10 And everyone who shall speak a word against the Son of man, it shall be forgiven him, but to the one blaspheming against the Holy Spirit it shall not be forgiven.
Luke 12:11 And when they bring you before the synagogues and the rulers and the authorities, do not be anxious how or what to answer in defense, or what to say,
Luke 12:12 for the Holy Spirit shall teach you in that very hour what must be said.
Luke 12:13 And someone from the crowd said to him: Teacher, tell my brother to divide the inheritance with me.
Luke 12:14 But he said to him: Man, who appointed me judge or divider over you?
Luke 12:15 And he said to them: See and guard yourselves from greed, because a man's life is not in his abundance from his possessions.
Luke 12:16 And he told them a parable, saying: The land of a certain rich man bore plentifully,
Luke 12:17 and he was reasoning in himself, saying: What shall I do, because I have nowhere to gather my fruits?
Luke 12:18 And he said: I shall do this: I shall take down my storehouses and build greater ones, and gather there all my produce and my goods.
Luke 12:19 And I shall say to my soul: Soul, you have many goods laid up for many years; rest, eat, drink, rejoice.
Luke 12:20 But God said to him: Fool, in this night they demand your soul from you; and what you prepared, whose shall it be?
Luke 12:21 So is the one storing treasure for himself and not being rich toward God.
Luke 12:22 And he said to his disciples: For this reason I say to you: Do not be anxious for your soul, what to eat, nor for the body, what to put on.
Luke 12:23 The soul is more than food, and the body than the garment.
Luke 12:24 Consider the ravens, that they neither sow nor harvest, which have neither storeroom nor storehouse, and God feeds them; how much more do you surpass the birds!
Luke 12:25 And which of you, being anxious, can add one cubit to his stature?
Luke 12:26 Therefore, if you cannot do even the least, why are you anxious concerning the rest?
Luke 12:27 Consider the lilies, how they grow; they neither labor nor spin; but I say to you, not even Solomon in all his glory was clothed as one of these.
Luke 12:28 But if God so clothes the grass in the field, being today and tomorrow cast into an oven, how much more you, you of little faith!
Luke 12:29 And you, do not seek what to eat or what to drink, and do not be unsettled.
Luke 12:30 For the nations of the world seek all these things, but your Father knows that you need these.
Luke 12:31 Nevertheless, seek the kingdom of God, and all these things shall be added to you.
Luke 12:32 Do not fear, little flock, because your Father was well pleased to give you the kingdom.
Luke 12:33 Sell your possessions and give alms; make for yourselves purses not growing old, unfailing treasure in the heavens, where a thief does not draw near nor a moth destroy.
Luke 12:34 For where your treasure is, there your heart also shall be.
Luke 12:35 Let your waists be girded and the lamps burning,
Luke 12:36 and you like men awaiting their own lord, when he returns from the wedding feast, so that when he comes and knocks, they may immediately open to him.
Luke 12:37 Blessed are those slaves whom the lord, coming, shall find keeping watch; amen, I say to you that he shall gird himself and make them recline, and come and serve them.
Luke 12:38 And if he comes in the second watch, and comes in the third watch, and finds so, blessed are those slaves.
Luke 12:39 And know this, that if the master of the house had known at what hour the thief comes, he would have kept watch and would not have allowed his house to be dug through.
Luke 12:40 Therefore you also become ready, because at an hour you do not think, the Son of man comes.
Luke 12:41 And Peter said to him: Lord, do you say this parable to us, or also to all?
Luke 12:42 And the Lord said: Who, then, is the faithful and prudent steward whom the lord shall appoint over his household to give the grain ration in season?
Luke 12:43 Blessed is that slave whom his lord, coming, shall find doing so.
Luke 12:44 Truly I say to you that he shall appoint him over all his possessions.
Luke 12:45 But if that slave says in his heart: My lord delays coming, and begins to beat the male servants and the female servants, and to eat and drink and be drunk,
Luke 12:46 the lord of that slave shall come on a day which he does not expect and at an hour which he does not know, and shall cut him in two and place his portion with the unbelievers.
Luke 12:47 And that slave who knew his own lord's will and did not prepare nor do according to his will shall be beaten with many blows.
Luke 12:48 But the one not knowing, but doing things worthy of blows, shall be beaten with few; and from everyone to whom much was given, much shall be sought, and from the one to whom they entrusted much, they shall ask more.
Luke 12:49 I came to cast fire into the earth, and what do I wish if it was already kindled!
Luke 12:50 But I have a baptism to be baptized with, and how I am held until it is completed!
Luke 12:51 Do you think that I came to give peace on the earth? No, I say to you, but rather division.
Luke 12:52 For from now five in one house shall be divided, three against two and two against three.
Luke 12:53 Father shall be divided against son and son against father, mother against daughter and daughter against mother, mother-in-law against her daughter-in-law and daughter-in-law against her mother-in-law.
Luke 12:54 And he also was saying to the crowds: When you see the cloud rising from the west, immediately you say: A rainstorm comes, and it happens so.
Luke 12:55 And when a south wind blows, you say that there shall be scorching heat, and it happens.
Luke 12:56 Hypocrites, you know to examine the face of the earth and the heaven, but how do you not examine this time?
Luke 12:57 And why do you not also judge what is just from yourselves?
Luke 12:58 For as you go with your adversary before a ruler, on the road give effort to be released from him, lest he drag you to the judge, and the judge hand you over to the officer, and the officer cast you into prison.
Luke 12:59 I say to you: You shall certainly not come out from there until you repay even the last lepton.

## Chapter 13

Luke 13:1 And some were present at that very time, reporting to him concerning the Galileans whose blood Pilate mixed with their sacrifices.
Luke 13:2 And Jesus answered and said to them: Do you think that these Galileans became sinners beyond all the Galileans because they have suffered such things?
Luke 13:3 No, I say to you, but unless you repent, you shall all likewise perish.
Luke 13:4 Or those eighteen upon whom the tower in Siloam fell and killed them, do you think that these became debtors beyond all men dwelling in Jerusalem?
Luke 13:5 No, I say to you, but unless you repent, you shall all similarly perish.
Luke 13:6 And he was telling this parable: Someone had a fig tree planted in his vineyard, and came seeking fruit on it and did not find.
Luke 13:7 And he said to the vine dresser: Behold, three years I come seeking fruit on this fig tree and do not find; cut it down; why does it also render the earth idle?
Luke 13:8 And he answered and says to him: Lord, leave it this year also, until I dig around it and put manure,
Luke 13:9 and if it produces fruit; but otherwise, in the future you shall cut it down.
Luke 13:10 And he was teaching in one of the synagogues on the Sabbath.
Luke 13:11 And behold, there was a woman having a spirit of illness eighteen years, and she was bent together and unable to straighten up completely.
Luke 13:12 And Jesus saw her and called her and said to her: Woman, you have been released from your illness.
Luke 13:13 And he laid his hands upon her, and immediately she was straightened and was glorifying God.
Luke 13:14 But the synagogue ruler answered, indignant because Jesus healed on the Sabbath, and was saying to the crowd: There are six days in which one must work; therefore come and be healed in these, and not on the Sabbath day.
Luke 13:15 Therefore the Lord answered him and said: Hypocrite, does not each of you on the Sabbath loose his ox or donkey from the manger and lead it away and give it to drink?
Luke 13:16 But this woman, being Abraham's daughter, whom Satan bound, behold, eighteen years, ought she not to be loosed from this bond on the Sabbath day?
Luke 13:17 And while he said these things, all those opposing him were being put to shame, and the whole crowd was rejoicing over all the glorious things happening by him.
Luke 13:18 And he was saying: What is the kingdom of God like, and to what shall I liken it?
Luke 13:19 It is like a grain of mustard which a man took and cast into his own garden, and it grew and became a great tree, and the birds of the heaven dwelt in its branches.
Luke 13:20 And again he said: To what shall I liken the kingdom of God?
Luke 13:21 It is like leaven which a woman took and hid in three sata of flour, until the whole was leavened.
Luke 13:22 And he was passing through cities and villages, teaching and making a journey into Jerusalem.
Luke 13:23 And someone said to him: Lord, are those being saved few? And he said to them:
Luke 13:24 Struggle to enter through the narrow gate, because many, I say to you, shall seek to enter and shall not be strong enough.
Luke 13:25 From when the master of the house rises and shuts the door, and you begin to stand outside and knock at the door, saying: Lord, Lord, open to us, he shall answer and say to you: I do not know you, from where you are.
Luke 13:26 Then you shall begin to say: We ate and drank before you, and you taught in our streets.
Luke 13:27 And he shall say: I say to you, I do not know you, from where you are; depart from me, all workers of unrighteousness.
Luke 13:28 There shall be the weeping and the grinding of teeth, when you see Abraham and Isaac and Jacob and all the prophets in the kingdom of God, but yourselves being cast outside.
Luke 13:29 And they shall come from east and west and from north and south, and shall recline in the kingdom of God.
Luke 13:30 And behold, there are last who shall be first, and there are first who shall be last.
Luke 13:31 In that very day some Pharisees approached, saying to him: Go out and depart from here, because Herod wishes to kill you.
Luke 13:32 And he said to them: Go and tell this fox: Behold, I cast out demons and complete healings today and tomorrow, and on the third I am completed.
Luke 13:33 Nevertheless I must go today and tomorrow and the following day, because it is not possible for a prophet to perish outside Jerusalem.
Luke 13:34 Jerusalem, Jerusalem, who kills the prophets and stones those sent to her, how often I wished to gather your children together in the manner that a hen gathers her own brood under the wings, and you were unwilling!
Luke 13:35 Behold, your house is left to you deserted; and amen, I say to you that you shall certainly not see me until it comes when you say: Blessed is he who comes in the name of the Lord.

## Chapter 14

Luke 14:1 And it happened when he came into the house of one of the rulers of the Pharisees on a Sabbath to eat bread, they were watching him.
Luke 14:2 And behold, a certain man with dropsy was before him.
Luke 14:3 And Jesus answered and said to the lawyers and Pharisees, saying: Is it lawful to heal on the Sabbath?
Luke 14:4 But they were quiet; and taking hold of him, he healed him and released him.
Luke 14:5 And answering them, he said: Whose donkey or ox of you shall fall into a well, and he shall not immediately pull it up on the Sabbath day?
Luke 14:6 And they were not strong enough to answer him concerning these things.
Luke 14:7 And he was telling a parable to those invited, observing how they chose the first reclining places, saying to them:
Luke 14:8 When you are invited by someone to a wedding feast, do not recline in the first reclining place, lest someone more honored than you has been invited by him,
Luke 14:9 and the one inviting you and him comes and shall say to you: Give this one a place; and then you shall begin with shame to occupy the last place.
Luke 14:10 But when you are invited, go and recline in the last place, so that when the one inviting you comes, he may say to you: Friend, come up higher; then you shall have glory before those reclining with you.
Luke 14:11 Because everyone exalting himself shall be humbled, and the one humbling himself shall be exalted.
Luke 14:12 And he also was saying to the one inviting him: When you make a meal or supper, do not call your friends nor your brothers nor your relatives nor rich neighbors, lest they also invite you back and a repayment come to you.
Luke 14:13 But when you make a reception, invite poor, crippled, lame, blind people,
Luke 14:14 and you shall be blessed, because they have nothing to repay you, for it shall be repaid you in the resurrection of the righteous.
Luke 14:15 And one of those reclining with him heard these things and said to him: Blessed is whoever shall eat bread in the kingdom of God.
Luke 14:16 And he said to him: A certain man made a great supper and invited many,
Luke 14:17 and sent his slave at the hour of the supper to tell those invited: Come, because everything is already ready.
Luke 14:18 And all began from one accord to excuse themselves; the first said to him: I bought a field and have necessity to go out and see it; I ask you, hold me excused.
Luke 14:19 And another said: I bought five pairs of oxen and go to examine them; I ask you, hold me excused.
Luke 14:20 And another said: I married a wife, and for this reason I cannot come.
Luke 14:21 And that slave arrived and reported these things to his lord; then the master of the house became angry and said to his slave: Go out quickly into the streets and lanes of the city, and bring here the poor and crippled and lame and blind.
Luke 14:22 And the slave said: Lord, it has happened as you commanded, and there is still room.
Luke 14:23 And the lord said to the slave: Go out into the roads and fences and compel them to enter, so that my house may be filled.
Luke 14:24 For I say to you that none of those men invited shall taste my supper.
Luke 14:25 And many crowds were going with him, and turning, he said to them:
Luke 14:26 If anyone comes to me and does not hate his own father and mother and wife and children and brothers and sisters, and further even his own soul, he cannot be my disciple.
Luke 14:27 And whoever does not carry his cross and come behind me cannot be my disciple.
Luke 14:28 For which of you, wishing to build a tower, does not first sit and calculate the expense, whether he has the things for completion,
Luke 14:29 lest when he has placed a foundation and is not strong enough to finish, all who behold begin to mock him,
Luke 14:30 saying: This man began to build and was not strong enough to finish?
Luke 14:31 Or what king, going to meet another king in war, does not first sit and take counsel whether he is able with ten thousand to meet the one coming against him with twenty thousand?
Luke 14:32 Otherwise, while he is still far off, he sends an embassy and asks the things for peace.
Luke 14:33 So therefore everyone of you who does not take leave of all his own possessions cannot be my disciple.
Luke 14:34 The salt is good, but if the salt becomes tasteless, with what shall it be seasoned?
Luke 14:35 It is fit neither for earth nor for manure; they cast it outside. He who has ears to hear, let him hear.

## Chapter 15

Luke 15:1 And all the tax collectors and sinners were drawing near to him to hear him.
Luke 15:2 And the Pharisees and scribes were grumbling, saying: This man receives sinners and eats with them.
Luke 15:3 And he told them this parable, saying:
Luke 15:4 What man of you, having a hundred sheep and losing one of them, does not leave the ninety-nine in the desert and go after the lost one until he finds it?
Luke 15:5 And finding, he places it upon his own shoulders, rejoicing.
Luke 15:6 And coming into the house, he calls together the friends and neighbors, saying to them: Rejoice with me, because I found my sheep which was lost.
Luke 15:7 I say to you that so there shall be joy in the heaven over one sinner repenting, rather than over ninety-nine righteous men who have no need of repentance.
Luke 15:8 Or what woman having ten drachmas, if she loses one drachma, does not light a lamp and sweep the house and seek diligently until she finds?
Luke 15:9 And finding, she calls together the female friends and neighbors, saying: Rejoice with me, because I found the drachma which I lost.
Luke 15:10 So, I say to you, joy happens before the angels of God over one sinner repenting.
Luke 15:11 And he said: A certain man had two sons,
Luke 15:12 and the younger of them said to the father: Father, give me the portion of the property falling to me. And he divided the livelihood for them.
Luke 15:13 And after not many days, the younger son gathered everything and went abroad into a distant region, and there scattered his property, living wastefully.
Luke 15:14 And when he spent everything, a strong famine came throughout that region, and he began to lack.
Luke 15:15 And going, he joined himself to one of the citizens of that region, and he sent him into his fields to feed pigs.
Luke 15:16 And he was desiring to fill his belly from the pods which the pigs ate, and no one was giving to him.
Luke 15:17 And coming to himself, he said: How many hired men of my father abound in loaves, but I perish with famine!
Luke 15:18 I shall rise and go to my father and say to him: Father, I sinned against the heaven and before you,
Luke 15:19 and I am no longer worthy to be called your son; make me as one of your hired men.
Luke 15:20 And rising, he came to his own father; but while he was still far off, his father saw him and had compassion, and ran and fell upon his neck and kissed him fervently.
Luke 15:21 And the son said to him: Father, I sinned against the heaven and before you, and I am no longer worthy to be called your son.
Luke 15:22 But the father said to his slaves: Bring out the first robe and clothe him, and give a ring onto his hand and sandals onto his feet,
Luke 15:23 and bring the fattened calf and slaughter it, and let us eat and rejoice,
Luke 15:24 because this son of mine was dead and lived again, and was lost and was found. And they began to rejoice.
Luke 15:25 And his elder son was in a field, and as he came and drew near to the house, he heard music and dancing,
Luke 15:26 and calling one of his servants, he was inquiring what these things might be.
Luke 15:27 And he said to him: Your brother has come, and your father slaughtered the fattened calf, because he received him back healthy.
Luke 15:28 But he became angry and was unwilling to enter; therefore his father went out and was begging him.
Luke 15:29 But he answered and said to the father: Behold, so many years I slave for you, and never passed by your commandment, and you never gave me a young goat so that I might rejoice with my friends.
Luke 15:30 But when this son of yours came, who devoured your livelihood with prostitutes, you slaughtered the fattened calf for him.
Luke 15:31 And he said to him: Child, you are always with me, and all my things are yours.
Luke 15:32 But it was necessary to rejoice and be glad, because this brother of yours was dead and lived again, and was lost and was found.

## Chapter 16

Luke 16:1 And he was also saying to his disciples, A certain man was rich, who had a steward, and this man was accused before him of scattering his possessions.
Luke 16:2 And having called him, he said to him, What is this I hear about you? Give the account of your stewardship, for you will no longer be able to act as steward.
Luke 16:3 And the steward said within himself, What shall I do, because my master is taking the stewardship away from me? I am not strong enough to dig; I am ashamed to beg.
Luke 16:4 I know what I shall do, so that when I am removed from the stewardship, they may receive me into their houses.
Luke 16:5 And having summoned each one of his master's debtors, he was saying to the first, How much do you owe my master?
Luke 16:6 And he said, A hundred baths of oil. And he said to him, Take your document, and having sat down, quickly write fifty.
Luke 16:7 Then he said to another, And how much do you owe? And he said, A hundred cors of wheat. And he says to him, Take your document and write eighty.
Luke 16:8 And the master praised the steward of unrighteousness because he had acted prudently, because the sons of this age are more prudent toward their own generation than the sons of the light.
Luke 16:9 And I say to you, Make friends for yourselves from the mammon of unrighteousness, so that when you fail, they may receive you into the eternal tents.
Luke 16:10 The one faithful in the least is faithful also in much, and the one unrighteous in the least is unrighteous also in much.
Luke 16:11 If therefore you did not become faithful in unrighteous mammon, who will entrust the true thing to you?
Luke 16:12 And if you did not become faithful in what belongs to another, who will give you what is yours?
Luke 16:13 No household servant can serve two masters, for either he will hate the one and love the other, or he will hold to one and despise the other. You cannot serve God and mammon.
Luke 16:14 And the Pharisees, being lovers of money, were also hearing all these things, and were sneering at him.
Luke 16:15 And he said to them, You are those who justify yourselves before people, but God knows your hearts, because what is exalted among people is an abomination before God.
Luke 16:16 The law and the prophets were until John. From then the kingdom of God is proclaimed as good news, and everyone forces his way into it.
Luke 16:17 But it is easier for heaven and earth to pass away than for one stroke of the law to fall.
Luke 16:18 Everyone who dismisses his wife and marries another commits adultery, and everyone who marries a woman dismissed from a husband commits adultery.
Luke 16:19 And a certain man was rich, and was dressing in purple and fine linen, rejoicing splendidly every day.
Luke 16:20 And there was a certain poor man named Lazarus, who had been laid at his gateway, covered with sores,
Luke 16:21 and desiring to be filled from the crumbs falling from the rich man's table. But even the dogs, coming, were licking his sores.
Luke 16:22 And it happened that the poor man died and was carried away by the angels into Abraham's bosom. And the rich man also died and was buried.
Luke 16:23 And in Hades, having lifted up his eyes, being in torments, he sees Abraham from far away and Lazarus in his bosom.
Luke 16:24 And having called out, he said, Father Abraham, have mercy on me, and send Lazarus so that he may dip the tip of his finger in water and cool my tongue, because I am in anguish in this flame.
Luke 16:25 But Abraham said, Child, remember that you received your good things in your life, and Lazarus likewise the bad things. But now he is comforted, and you are in anguish.
Luke 16:26 And besides all these things, between us and you a great chasm has been fixed, so that those wishing to cross from here to you cannot, nor may those from there cross over to us.
Luke 16:27 And he said, I ask you therefore, father, that you send him to my father's house,
Luke 16:28 for I have five brothers, so that he may testify solemnly to them, so that they too may not come into this place of torment.
Luke 16:29 Abraham says to him, They have Moses and the prophets; let them hear them.
Luke 16:30 And he said, No, father Abraham, but if someone from the dead goes to them, they will repent.
Luke 16:31 But he said to him, If they do not hear Moses and the prophets, neither will they be persuaded if someone rises from the dead.

## Chapter 17

Luke 17:1 And he said to the disciples, It is impossible for stumbling blocks not to come, but woe to him through whom they come.
Luke 17:2 It is better for him if a donkey millstone is placed around his neck and he is thrown into the sea than that he cause one of these little ones to stumble.
Luke 17:3 Pay attention to yourselves. And if your brother sins against you, rebuke him; and if he repents, forgive him.
Luke 17:4 And if he sins against you seven times in the day, and seven times in the day turns back to you, saying, I repent, you shall forgive him.
Luke 17:5 And the apostles said to the Lord, Add faith to us.
Luke 17:6 And the Lord said, If you had faith as a mustard seed, you would say to this mulberry tree, Be uprooted and be planted in the sea, and it would obey you.
Luke 17:7 And which of you, having a slave plowing or tending a flock, will say to him when he has come in from the field, Immediately come over and recline?
Luke 17:8 But will he not say to him, Prepare what I shall dine on, and having girded yourself, serve me until I eat and drink, and after these things you shall eat and drink?
Luke 17:9 Does he have gratitude to that slave because he did the things commanded him? I do not think so.
Luke 17:10 Thus also you, when you have done all the things commanded you, say, We are useless slaves, because we have done what we owed to do.
Luke 17:11 And it happened as he was going to Jerusalem that he was passing through the midst of Samaria and Galilee.
Luke 17:12 And as he was entering a certain village, ten leprous men met him, who stood far away.
Luke 17:13 And they raised their voice, saying, Jesus, Master, have mercy on us.
Luke 17:14 And having seen them, he said to them, Go and show yourselves to the priests. And it happened that as they were going, they were cleansed.
Luke 17:15 And one of them, having seen that he was healed, returned, glorifying God with a loud voice.
Luke 17:16 And he fell on his face at his feet, giving thanks to him. And he was a Samaritan.
Luke 17:17 And answering, Jesus said, Were not the ten cleansed? But where are the nine?
Luke 17:18 Were none found who returned to give glory to God except this foreigner?
Luke 17:19 And he said to him, Rise and go; your faith has saved you.
Luke 17:20 And having been asked by the Pharisees when the kingdom of God comes, he answered them and said, The kingdom of God does not come with observation.
Luke 17:21 Nor will they say, Look, here, or, Look, there; for look, the kingdom of God is within you.
Luke 17:22 And he said to the disciples, Days will come when you will desire to see one of the days of the Son of Man, and you will not see it.
Luke 17:23 And they will say to you, Look, here, or, Look, there. Do not go away, nor pursue.
Luke 17:24 For just as the lightning, flashing from one place under heaven, shines to another under heaven, so also will the Son of Man be in his day.
Luke 17:25 But first he must suffer many things and be rejected by this generation.
Luke 17:26 And just as it happened in the days of Noah, so also will it be in the days of the Son of Man.
Luke 17:27 They were eating, drinking, marrying, being given in marriage, until the day Noah entered the ark, and the flood came and destroyed them all.
Luke 17:28 Likewise also, as it happened in the days of Lot, they were eating, drinking, buying, selling, planting, building.
Luke 17:29 But on the day Lot went out from Sodom, it rained fire and sulfur from heaven and destroyed them all.
Luke 17:30 It will be according to these things on the day the Son of Man is revealed.
Luke 17:31 On that day, whoever will be on the housetop, and his goods in the house, let him not go down to take them; and the one in the field, likewise let him not turn back to the things behind.
Luke 17:32 Remember Lot's wife.
Luke 17:33 Whoever seeks to save his life will lose it, and whoever loses it will preserve it alive.
Luke 17:34 I say to you, On this night two will be on one bed; the one will be taken along, and the other will be left.
Luke 17:35 Two women will be grinding together; one will be taken along, and the other will be left.
Luke 17:36 
Luke 17:37 And answering, they say to him, Where, Lord? And he said to them, Where the body is, there the eagles will be gathered.

## Chapter 18

Luke 18:1 And he was also telling them a parable about the necessity of always praying and not losing heart,
Luke 18:2 saying, A certain judge was in a certain city, not fearing God and not respecting a person.
Luke 18:3 And a widow was in that city, and was coming to him, saying, Give me justice against my adversary.
Luke 18:4 And he was unwilling for a time. But after these things he said within himself, Even though I do not fear God and do not respect a person,
Luke 18:5 yet because this widow causes me trouble, I will give her justice, so that by coming continually she may not strike me under the eye.
Luke 18:6 And the Lord said, Hear what the judge of unrighteousness says.
Luke 18:7 And will God not give justice to his chosen ones, who cry to him day and night, and be patient over them?
Luke 18:8 I say to you that he will give them justice quickly. Nevertheless, when the Son of Man comes, will he find faith on the earth?
Luke 18:9 And he also told this parable to certain people who trusted in themselves that they were righteous and despised the rest:
Luke 18:10 Two men went up into the temple to pray, the one a Pharisee and the other a tax collector.
Luke 18:11 The Pharisee, having stood, was praying these things to himself, God, I thank you that I am not as the rest of people, rapacious, unrighteous, adulterers, or even as this tax collector.
Luke 18:12 I fast twice in the week; I give a tenth of all that I acquire.
Luke 18:13 And the tax collector, standing far away, was unwilling even to lift his eyes to heaven, but was striking his chest, saying, God, be propitious to me, the sinner.
Luke 18:14 I say to you, This man went down to his house justified rather than that man, because everyone who exalts himself will be humbled, but the one who humbles himself will be exalted.
Luke 18:15 And they were also bringing the infants to him so that he might touch them. But having seen it, the disciples rebuked them.
Luke 18:16 But Jesus, having called them to him, said, Allow the children to come to me, and do not hinder them, for of such is the kingdom of God.
Luke 18:17 Amen, I say to you, Whoever does not receive the kingdom of God as a child will certainly not enter into it.
Luke 18:18 And a certain ruler asked him, saying, Good teacher, having done what shall I inherit eternal life?
Luke 18:19 And Jesus said to him, Why do you call me good? No one is good except one, God.
Luke 18:20 You know the commandments: Do not commit adultery; do not murder; do not steal; do not bear false witness; honor your father and your mother.
Luke 18:21 And he said, All these things I have kept from my youth.
Luke 18:22 And having heard these things, Jesus said to him, One thing still is lacking to you. Sell all that you have and distribute to the poor, and you will have treasure in heaven; and come, follow me.
Luke 18:23 But having heard these things, he became deeply sorrowful, for he was exceedingly rich.
Luke 18:24 And Jesus, having seen him become deeply sorrowful, said, How difficultly those having wealth will enter into the kingdom of God!
Luke 18:25 For it is easier for a camel to enter through a needle's hole than for a rich man to enter into the kingdom of God.
Luke 18:26 And those who heard said, And who can be saved?
Luke 18:27 And he said, The things impossible with people are possible with God.
Luke 18:28 And Peter said, Look, we left everything and followed you.
Luke 18:29 And he said to them, Amen, I say to you that there is no one who left a house or parents or brothers or a wife or children for the sake of the kingdom of God,
Luke 18:30 who will not certainly receive many times more in this time, and in the coming age eternal life.
Luke 18:31 And having taken the twelve along, he said to them, Look, we are going up to Jerusalem, and all the things written through the prophets concerning the Son of Man will be completed.
Luke 18:32 For he will be handed over to the nations, and will be mocked and insulted and spat upon.
Luke 18:33 And having scourged him, they will kill him, and on the third day he will rise.
Luke 18:34 And they understood none of these things, and this saying was hidden from them, and they did not know the things being said.
Luke 18:35 And it happened as he was drawing near to Jericho that a certain blind man was sitting beside the road, begging.
Luke 18:36 And having heard a crowd passing through, he was asking what this might be.
Luke 18:37 And they reported to him that Jesus the Nazarene was passing by.
Luke 18:38 And he cried out, saying, Jesus, Son of David, have mercy on me.
Luke 18:39 And those going ahead were rebuking him so that he would be silent, but he was crying out much more, Son of David, have mercy on me.
Luke 18:40 And having stood still, Jesus commanded him to be brought to him. And when he had drawn near, he asked him,
Luke 18:41 saying, What do you wish me to do for you? And he said, Lord, that I may see again.
Luke 18:42 And Jesus said to him, See again; your faith has saved you.
Luke 18:43 And immediately he saw again, and was following him, glorifying God; and all the people, having seen it, gave praise to God.

## Chapter 19

Luke 19:1 And having entered, he was passing through Jericho.
Luke 19:2 And look, a man called by the name Zacchaeus, and he was a chief tax collector, and he was rich.
Luke 19:3 And he was seeking to see Jesus, who he is, and could not because of the crowd, because he was small in stature.
Luke 19:4 And having run ahead, he climbed up onto a sycamore tree so that he might see him, because he was about to pass through that way.
Luke 19:5 And when he came to the place, Jesus, having looked up, saw him and said to him, Zacchaeus, hurry and come down, for today I must stay in your house.
Luke 19:6 And having hurried, he came down and received him joyfully.
Luke 19:7 And having seen it, all were murmuring, saying that he went in to lodge with a sinful man.
Luke 19:8 But Zacchaeus, having stood, said to the Lord, Look, half of my possessions, Lord, I give to the poor, and if I extorted anything from anyone, I repay fourfold.
Luke 19:9 And Jesus said to him, Today salvation has come to this house, because he too is a son of Abraham.
Luke 19:10 For the Son of Man came to seek and to save what was lost.
Luke 19:11 And while they were hearing these things, he added and told a parable, because he was near Jerusalem and they supposed that the kingdom of God was about to appear immediately.
Luke 19:12 He said therefore, A certain man of noble birth went into a distant country to receive a kingdom for himself and to return.
Luke 19:13 And having called ten slaves of his, he gave them ten minas and said to them, Do business until I come.
Luke 19:14 But his citizens hated him, and sent a delegation after him, saying, We do not wish this man to reign over us.
Luke 19:15 And it happened when he returned, having received the kingdom, that he said that these slaves to whom he gave the silver should be called to him, so that he might know what each had gained by business.
Luke 19:16 And the first came, saying, Master, your mina gained ten minas.
Luke 19:17 And he said to him, Well done, good slave. Because you became faithful in the least, have authority over ten cities.
Luke 19:18 And the second came, saying, Master, your mina made five minas.
Luke 19:19 And he said also to this one, And you, be over five cities.
Luke 19:20 And another came, saying, Master, look, your mina, which I had laid away in a handkerchief.
Luke 19:21 For I feared you because you are a severe man. You take up what you did not lay down, and reap what you did not sow.
Luke 19:22 And he says to him, From your mouth I will judge you, wicked slave. You knew that I am a severe man, taking up what I did not lay down and reaping what I did not sow.
Luke 19:23 And why did you not give my silver to the bank, and I, having come, would have collected it with interest?
Luke 19:24 And he said to those standing by, Take the mina from him and give it to the one having the ten minas.
Luke 19:25 And they said to him, Master, he has ten minas.
Luke 19:26 For I say to you that to everyone having, it will be given, but from the one not having, even what he has will be taken from him.
Luke 19:27 Nevertheless, those enemies of mine who did not wish me to reign over them, bring here and slaughter before me.
Luke 19:28 And having said these things, he was going ahead, going up to Jerusalem.
Luke 19:29 And it happened when he drew near to Bethphage and Bethany, toward the mountain called Olives, that he sent two of his disciples,
Luke 19:30 saying, Go into the village opposite, in which, entering, you will find a colt tied, on which no person ever sat. Having untied it, bring it.
Luke 19:31 And if anyone asks you, Why do you untie it? thus you shall say to him, The Lord has need of it.
Luke 19:32 And those sent, having gone away, found it just as he said to them.
Luke 19:33 And as they were untying the colt, its owners said to them, Why do you untie the colt?
Luke 19:34 And they said, The Lord has need of it.
Luke 19:35 And they brought it to Jesus, and having thrown their own garments upon the colt, they mounted Jesus on it.
Luke 19:36 And as he was going, they were spreading their garments in the road.
Luke 19:37 And as he was already drawing near to the descent of the Mount of Olives, the whole multitude of the disciples began rejoicing to praise God with a loud voice concerning all the mighty works they had seen,
Luke 19:38 saying, Blessed is the King who comes in the name of the Lord. Peace in heaven, and glory in the highest.
Luke 19:39 And some of the Pharisees from the crowd said to him, Teacher, rebuke your disciples.
Luke 19:40 And answering, he said to them, I say to you that if these are silent, the stones will cry out.
Luke 19:41 And when he drew near, having seen the city, he wept over it,
Luke 19:42 saying, If you too had known, even in this your day, the things for your peace! But now they were hidden from your eyes.
Luke 19:43 Because days will come upon you, and your enemies will throw a rampart around you, and will surround you and hem you in from every side,
Luke 19:44 and will dash you to the ground, and your children within you, and will not leave in you a stone upon a stone, because you did not know the time of your visitation.
Luke 19:45 And having entered into the temple, he began to cast out those selling in it and buying,
Luke 19:46 saying to them, It is written, My house is a house of prayer, but you made it a cave of robbers.
Luke 19:47 And he was teaching daily in the temple. But the chief priests and the scribes were seeking to destroy him, and the foremost of the people.
Luke 19:48 And they were not finding what they might do, for all the people were hanging upon him, listening.

## Chapter 20

Luke 20:1 And it happened on one of those days, as he was teaching the people in the temple and proclaiming good news, that the chief priests and the scribes came upon him with the elders.
Luke 20:2 And they spoke to him, saying, Tell us by what authority you do these things, or who is the one who gave you this authority?
Luke 20:3 And answering, he said to them, I too will ask you one matter, and tell me:
Luke 20:4 Was the baptism of John from heaven or from people?
Luke 20:5 And they reasoned together among themselves, saying, If we say, From heaven, he will say, Why then did you not believe him?
Luke 20:6 But if we say, From people, all the people will stone us to death, for they are persuaded that John is a prophet.
Luke 20:7 And they answered that they did not know from where.
Luke 20:8 And Jesus said to them, Neither do I tell you by what authority I do these things.
Luke 20:9 And he began to tell this parable to the people: A certain man planted a vineyard, and leased it to farmers, and went abroad for a considerable time.
Luke 20:10 And at the season he sent a slave to the farmers so that they might give him from the fruit of the vineyard, but the farmers, having beaten him, sent him away empty.
Luke 20:11 And he proceeded to send another slave, but they, having beaten and dishonored that one also, sent him away empty.
Luke 20:12 And he proceeded to send a third, but they, having wounded this one also, cast him out.
Luke 20:13 And the master of the vineyard said, What shall I do? I will send my beloved son; perhaps, having seen him, they will respect him.
Luke 20:14 But having seen him, the farmers were reasoning among themselves, saying, This is the heir. Come, let us kill him, so that the inheritance may become ours.
Luke 20:15 And having cast him outside the vineyard, they killed him. What therefore will the master of the vineyard do to them?
Luke 20:16 He will come and destroy these farmers and give the vineyard to others. And having heard, they said, May it not happen.
Luke 20:17 But having looked at them, he said, What therefore is this that is written: The stone which the builders rejected, this became the head of the corner?
Luke 20:18 Everyone who falls upon that stone will be shattered, but upon whomever it falls, it will crush him.
Luke 20:19 And the chief priests and the scribes sought to lay hands on him in that very hour, and feared the people, for they knew that he told this parable against them.
Luke 20:20 And having watched closely, they sent spies pretending themselves to be righteous, so that they might seize upon his word, to hand him over to the rule and the authority of the governor.
Luke 20:21 And they asked him, saying, Teacher, we know that you speak and teach rightly, and do not show partiality, but teach the way of God in truth.
Luke 20:22 Is it lawful for us to give tribute to Caesar or not?
Luke 20:23 But having perceived their craftiness, he said to them, Why do you test me?
Luke 20:24 Show me a denarius. Whose image and inscription does it have? And answering, they said, Caesar's.
Luke 20:25 And he said to them, Therefore give back the things of Caesar to Caesar, and the things of God to God.
Luke 20:26 And they were not able to seize upon his saying before the people, and having marveled at his answer, they were silent.
Luke 20:27 And some of the Sadducees, those disputing that there is a resurrection, having approached, asked him,
Luke 20:28 saying, Teacher, Moses wrote to us, If anyone's brother dies having a wife, and he dies childless, that his brother should take the wife and raise up seed for his brother.
Luke 20:29 There were therefore seven brothers, and the first, having taken a wife, died childless.
Luke 20:30 And the second took the wife, and he died childless.
Luke 20:31 And the third took her, and likewise also the seven did not leave children and died.
Luke 20:32 And later than all, the woman also died.
Luke 20:33 In the resurrection, therefore, of which of them does she become the wife? For the seven had her as wife.
Luke 20:34 And answering, Jesus said to them, The sons of this age marry and are given in marriage.
Luke 20:35 But those counted worthy to attain that age and the resurrection from the dead neither marry nor are given in marriage.
Luke 20:36 For neither can they die any longer, for they are equal to angels and are sons of God, being sons of the resurrection.
Luke 20:37 But that the dead are raised, even Moses disclosed at the bush, when he calls the Lord the God of Abraham and the God of Isaac and the God of Jacob.
Luke 20:38 And he is not God of the dead, but of the living, for all live to him.
Luke 20:39 And answering, some of the scribes said, Teacher, you spoke well.
Luke 20:40 And they no longer dared to ask him anything.
Luke 20:41 And he said to them, How do they say that the Christ is David's son?
Luke 20:42 And David himself says in the book of Psalms, The Lord said to my Lord, Sit at my right,
Luke 20:43 until I place your enemies as a footstool for your feet.
Luke 20:44 David therefore calls him Lord, and how is he his son?
Luke 20:45 And while all the people were hearing, he said to his disciples,
Luke 20:46 Beware of the scribes who wish to walk in robes, and love greetings in the marketplaces, and first seats in the synagogues, and first places at dinners,
Luke 20:47 who devour the houses of widows and as a pretext pray at length. These will receive greater judgment.

## Chapter 21

Luke 21:1 And having looked up, he saw the rich putting their gifts into the treasury.
Luke 21:2 And he also saw a certain needy widow putting two lepta there.
Luke 21:3 And he said, Truly I say to you that this poor widow put in more than all.
Luke 21:4 For all these put into the gifts of God from what abounded to them, but she, from her lack, put in all the livelihood she had.
Luke 21:5 And as some were speaking about the temple, that it was adorned with beautiful stones and dedicated offerings, he said,
Luke 21:6 These things which you behold, days will come in which a stone will not be left upon a stone that will not be torn down.
Luke 21:7 And they asked him, saying, Teacher, when therefore will these things be, and what is the sign when these things are about to happen?
Luke 21:8 And he said, See that you are not led astray, for many will come in my name, saying, I am, and, The time has drawn near. Do not therefore go after them.
Luke 21:9 And when you hear of wars and disorders, do not be terrified, for these things must happen first, but the end is not immediately.
Luke 21:10 Then he was saying to them, Nation will rise against nation, and kingdom against kingdom.
Luke 21:11 And there will be great earthquakes in various places, and famines and plagues, and there will be terrors and great signs from heaven.
Luke 21:12 But before all these things they will lay their hands on you and persecute you, handing you over to synagogues and prisons, being led before kings and governors for the sake of my name.
Luke 21:13 And it will turn out for you as a testimony.
Luke 21:14 Settle therefore in your hearts not to rehearse beforehand how to defend yourselves.
Luke 21:15 For I will give you a mouth and wisdom which all those opposing you will not be able to contradict or resist.
Luke 21:16 And you will be handed over even by parents and brothers and relatives and friends, and they will put some of you to death.
Luke 21:17 And you will be hated by all because of my name.
Luke 21:18 And a hair from your head will certainly not perish.
Luke 21:19 In your endurance acquire your lives.
Luke 21:20 And when you see Jerusalem being encircled by armies, then know that her desolation has drawn near.
Luke 21:21 Then let those in Judea flee into the mountains, and let those in her midst depart, and let those in the countryside not enter into her.
Luke 21:22 Because these are days of vengeance, for all the things written to be fulfilled.
Luke 21:23 But woe to those having a child in the womb and to those nursing in those days, for there will be great distress upon the land and wrath among this people.
Luke 21:24 And they will fall by the mouth of the sword, and will be taken captive into all the nations, and Jerusalem will be trampled by nations until the times of nations are fulfilled.
Luke 21:25 And there will be signs in sun and moon and stars, and upon the earth distress of nations in perplexity, the sea and the surge resounding,
Luke 21:26 people fainting from fear and expectation of the things coming upon the inhabited world, for the powers of the heavens will be shaken.
Luke 21:27 And then they will see the Son of Man coming in a cloud with power and much glory.
Luke 21:28 And when these things begin to happen, straighten up and lift up your heads, because your redemption draws near.
Luke 21:29 And he told them a parable: See the fig tree and all the trees.
Luke 21:30 When they already put forth growth, seeing it, you know from yourselves that summer is already near.
Luke 21:31 Thus also you, when you see these things happening, know that the kingdom of God is near.
Luke 21:32 Amen, I say to you that this generation will certainly not pass away until all things happen.
Luke 21:33 Heaven and earth will pass away, but my words will certainly not pass away.
Luke 21:34 But pay attention to yourselves, lest your hearts be weighed down in dissipation and drunkenness and cares of life, and that day come upon you suddenly.
Luke 21:35 For as a snare it will come upon all those sitting upon the face of all the earth.
Luke 21:36 Stay awake therefore at every time, pleading that you may be counted worthy to escape all these things about to happen and to stand before the Son of Man.
Luke 21:37 And during the days he was teaching in the temple, but during the nights, going out, he was lodging on the mountain called Olives.
Luke 21:38 And all the people were coming early in the morning to him in the temple to hear him.

## Chapter 22

Luke 22:1 And the feast of Unleavened Bread, called Passover, was drawing near.
Luke 22:2 And the chief priests and the scribes were seeking how they might kill him, for they feared the people.
Luke 22:3 And Satan entered into Judas, surnamed Iscariot, being of the number of the twelve.
Luke 22:4 And having gone away, he spoke together with the chief priests and the captains about how he might hand him over to them.
Luke 22:5 And they rejoiced, and agreed to give him silver.
Luke 22:6 And he consented, and was seeking an opportunity to hand him over to them apart from a crowd.
Luke 22:7 And the day of Unleavened Bread came, on which the Passover had to be sacrificed.
Luke 22:8 And he sent Peter and John, saying, Go and prepare the Passover for us, so that we may eat.
Luke 22:9 And they said to him, Where do you wish us to prepare?
Luke 22:10 And he said to them, Look, when you have entered into the city, a man carrying a jar of water will meet you. Follow him into the house where he enters.
Luke 22:11 And you shall say to the master of the house, The Teacher says to you, Where is the lodging room where I may eat the Passover with my disciples?
Luke 22:12 And he will show you a large upper room furnished; prepare there.
Luke 22:13 And having gone away, they found it just as he had said to them, and prepared the Passover.
Luke 22:14 And when the hour came, he reclined, and the twelve apostles with him.
Luke 22:15 And he said to them, With desire I desired to eat this Passover with you before I suffer.
Luke 22:16 For I say to you that I will certainly no longer eat of it until it is fulfilled in the kingdom of God.
Luke 22:17 And having received a cup, having given thanks, he said, Take this and divide it among yourselves.
Luke 22:18 For I say to you that I will certainly not drink from the produce of the vine until the kingdom of God comes.
Luke 22:19 And having taken bread, having given thanks, he broke it and gave it to them, saying, This is my body, which is given for you. Do this for my remembrance.
Luke 22:20 Likewise also the cup after dining, saying, This cup is the new covenant in my blood, which is poured out for you.
Luke 22:21 Nevertheless, look, the hand of the one handing me over is with me upon the table.
Luke 22:22 And the Son of Man indeed goes according to what has been determined; nevertheless, woe to that man through whom he is handed over.
Luke 22:23 And they began to discuss among themselves who then it might be of them who was about to do this.
Luke 22:24 And a contention also arose among them as to which of them is considered to be greater.
Luke 22:25 And he said to them, The kings of the nations lord it over them, and those exercising authority over them are called benefactors.
Luke 22:26 But you shall not be thus; rather, let the greater among you become as the younger, and the one leading as the one serving.
Luke 22:27 For who is greater, the one reclining or the one serving? Is it not the one reclining? But I am in your midst as the one serving.
Luke 22:28 And you are those who have remained with me in my trials.
Luke 22:29 And I appoint to you a kingdom, just as my Father appointed to me,
