Luke 22:30 so that you may eat and drink at my table in my kingdom, and sit on thrones judging the twelve tribes of Israel.
Luke 22:31 And the Lord said, Simon, Simon, look, Satan demanded you all, to sift you as wheat.
Luke 22:32 But I pleaded concerning you, so that your faith may not fail; and you, when you have turned back, strengthen your brothers.
Luke 22:33 And he said to him, Lord, with you I am ready to go both into prison and into death.
Luke 22:34 And he said, I say to you, Peter, a rooster will certainly not call today before you deny three times that you know me.
Luke 22:35 And he said to them, When I sent you without purse and bag and sandals, did you lack anything? And they said, Nothing.
Luke 22:36 He said therefore to them, But now let the one having a purse take it, likewise also a bag; and let the one not having sell his garment and buy a sword.
Luke 22:37 For I say to you that this thing written must still be completed in me: And he was reckoned with lawless ones. For also the things concerning me have an end.
Luke 22:38 And they said, Lord, look, here are two swords. And he said to them, It is enough.
Luke 22:39 And having gone out, he went according to his custom to the Mount of Olives, and his disciples also followed him.
Luke 22:40 And having come to the place, he said to them, Pray not to enter into temptation.
Luke 22:41 And he withdrew from them about a stone's throw, and having placed his knees down, was praying,
Luke 22:42 saying, Father, if you will, to take this cup away from me; nevertheless, let not my will, but yours, happen.
Luke 22:43 And an angel from heaven appeared to him, strengthening him.
Luke 22:44 And having come into agony, he was praying more earnestly; and his sweat became as clots of blood coming down upon the ground.
Luke 22:45 And having risen from prayer, having come to the disciples, he found them sleeping from sorrow.
Luke 22:46 And he said to them, Why do you sleep? Rise and pray, so that you may not enter into temptation.
Luke 22:47 And while he was still speaking, look, a crowd, and the one called Judas, one of the twelve, was going before them, and drew near to Jesus to kiss him.
Luke 22:48 But Jesus said to him, Judas, do you hand over the Son of Man with a kiss?
Luke 22:49 And those around him, having seen what would happen, said to him, Lord, shall we strike with a sword?
Luke 22:50 And a certain one of them struck the slave of the high priest, and took off his right ear.
Luke 22:51 But answering, Jesus said, Allow it as far as this. And having touched his ear, he healed him.
Luke 22:52 And Jesus said to the chief priests and captains of the temple and elders who had come against him, Did you come out as against a robber, with swords and clubs?
Luke 22:53 When I was with you daily in the temple, you did not stretch out your hands against me. But this is your hour, and the authority of darkness.
Luke 22:54 And having seized him, they led him and brought him into the house of the high priest. But Peter was following far away.
Luke 22:55 And when they had kindled a fire in the midst of the courtyard and had sat down together, Peter was sitting in their midst.
Luke 22:56 And a certain servant girl, having seen him sitting toward the light and having looked intently at him, said, This man also was with him.
Luke 22:57 But he denied him, saying, Woman, I do not know him.
Luke 22:58 And after a little while, another, having seen him, said, You too are of them. But Peter said, Man, I am not.
Luke 22:59 And about one hour having elapsed, a certain other was insisting, saying, In truth, this man too was with him, for he is also a Galilean.
Luke 22:60 But Peter said, Man, I do not know what you say. And immediately, while he was still speaking, the rooster called.
Luke 22:61 And having turned, the Lord looked at Peter, and Peter was reminded of the word of the Lord, how he said to him, Before a rooster calls, you will deny me three times.
Luke 22:62 And having gone outside, Peter wept bitterly.
Luke 22:63 And the men holding Jesus were mocking him, beating him.
Luke 22:64 And having covered him, they were striking his face, and asking him, saying, Prophesy: Who is the one who struck you?
Luke 22:65 And blaspheming, they were saying many other things against him.
Luke 22:66 And when day came, the eldership of the people was gathered, both chief priests and scribes, and they brought him up into their council, saying,
Luke 22:67 If you are the Christ, tell us. But he said to them, If I tell you, you will certainly not believe.
Luke 22:68 And if I also ask, you will certainly not answer me or release me.
Luke 22:69 From now the Son of Man will be sitting at the right of the power of God.
Luke 22:70 And all said, Are you therefore the Son of God? And he said to them, You say that I am.
Luke 22:71 And they said, What further need do we have of testimony? For we ourselves heard from his mouth.

## Chapter 23

Luke 23:1 And the whole multitude of them, having risen, led him before Pilate.
Luke 23:2 And they began to accuse him, saying, We found this man perverting the nation and forbidding tribute to be given to Caesar, saying that he himself is Christ, a king.
Luke 23:3 And Pilate asked him, saying, Are you the King of the Jews? And answering him, he said, You say it.
Luke 23:4 And Pilate said to the chief priests and the crowds, I find no fault in this man.
Luke 23:5 But they were insisting, saying that he stirs up the people, teaching throughout all Judea, having begun from Galilee as far as here.
Luke 23:6 And Pilate, having heard Galilee, asked if the man is a Galilean.
Luke 23:7 And having learned that he is of Herod's authority, he sent him up to Herod, who himself was also in Jerusalem in these days.
Luke 23:8 And Herod, having seen Jesus, rejoiced greatly, for he had been wishing for a considerable time to see him, because of hearing many things about him; and he was hoping to see some sign done by him.
Luke 23:9 And he was questioning him with many words, but he answered him nothing.
Luke 23:10 And the chief priests and the scribes stood, vehemently accusing him.
Luke 23:11 And Herod, having despised him with his troops and having mocked him, having clothed him in a splendid garment, sent him up to Pilate.
Luke 23:12 And both Pilate and Herod became friends with each other on that very day, for previously they had been in enmity toward each other.
Luke 23:13 And Pilate, having called together the chief priests and the rulers and the people,
Luke 23:14 said to them, You brought this man to me as one turning the people away, and look, I, having examined him before you, found in this man no fault of the things you accuse him of.
Luke 23:15 But neither did Herod, for I sent you up to him, and look, nothing worthy of death has been done by him.
Luke 23:16 Having therefore chastised him, I will release him.
Luke 23:17 And he had a necessity to release one to them at the feast.
Luke 23:18 And they cried out with the whole multitude, saying, Take this man away, but release Barabbas to us,
Luke 23:19 who had been thrown into prison because of a certain uprising that happened in the city and murder.
Luke 23:20 Again therefore Pilate addressed them, wishing to release Jesus.
Luke 23:21 But they were shouting, saying, Crucify, crucify him.
Luke 23:22 And a third time he said to them, For what evil did this man do? I found no fault deserving death in him. Having therefore chastised him, I will release him.
Luke 23:23 But they were pressing with loud voices, demanding that he be crucified, and their voices and those of the chief priests were prevailing.
Luke 23:24 And Pilate decided that their demand should happen.
Luke 23:25 And he released to them the one who had been thrown into the prison because of uprising and murder, whom they were demanding, but Jesus he handed over to their will.
Luke 23:26 And as they led him away, having seized a certain Simon of Cyrene, coming from the countryside, they laid the cross upon him to carry behind Jesus.
Luke 23:27 And a great multitude of the people was following him, and of women, who were also beating themselves and lamenting him.
Luke 23:28 But Jesus, having turned to them, said, Daughters of Jerusalem, do not weep over me, but weep over yourselves and over your children.
Luke 23:29 Because look, days are coming in which they will say, Blessed are the barren, and wombs that did not bear, and breasts that did not nurse.
Luke 23:30 Then they will begin to say to the mountains, Fall upon us, and to the hills, Cover us.
Luke 23:31 Because if they do these things in the moist wood, what may happen in the dry?
Luke 23:32 And two others also, criminals, were being led with him to be killed.
Luke 23:33 And when they came to the place called Skull, there they crucified him and the criminals, one on the right and one on the left.
Luke 23:34 But Jesus was saying, Father, forgive them, for they do not know what they do. And dividing his garments, they cast a lot.
Luke 23:35 And the people stood beholding, and the rulers also were sneering with them, saying, He saved others; let him save himself, if this is the Christ, the chosen one of God.
Luke 23:36 And the soldiers also were mocking him, approaching and offering him vinegar,
Luke 23:37 and saying, If you are the King of the Jews, save yourself.
Luke 23:38 And there was also an inscription written over him in Greek and Roman and Hebrew letters: This is the King of the Jews.
Luke 23:39 And one of the criminals who had been hung was blaspheming him, saying, If you are the Christ, save yourself and us.
Luke 23:40 But answering, the other was rebuking him, saying, Do you not even fear God, because you are in the same judgment?
Luke 23:41 And we indeed justly, for we receive things worthy of what we did, but this man did nothing improper.
Luke 23:42 And he was saying to Jesus, Remember me, Lord, when you come in your kingdom.
Luke 23:43 And Jesus said to him, Amen, I say to you, Today you will be with me in Paradise.
Luke 23:44 And it was about the sixth hour, and darkness came upon all the earth until the ninth hour.
Luke 23:45 And the sun was darkened, and the veil of the sanctuary was torn in the middle.
Luke 23:46 And having called with a loud voice, Jesus said, Father, into your hands I will entrust my spirit. And having said these things, he breathed out.
Luke 23:47 And the centurion, having seen what happened, glorified God, saying, Indeed this man was righteous.
Luke 23:48 And all the crowds who had come together to this spectacle, beholding the things that happened, were returning, striking their own chests.
Luke 23:49 And all his acquaintances stood far away, and women who had followed him from Galilee, seeing these things.
Luke 23:50 And look, a man named Joseph, being a council member, a good and righteous man,
Luke 23:51 this man had not consented to their counsel and action, from Arimathea, a city of the Jews, who himself also was awaiting the kingdom of God.
Luke 23:52 This man, having approached Pilate, asked for the body of Jesus.
Luke 23:53 And having taken it down, he wrapped it in linen and placed it in a rock-hewn tomb, where no one had yet been laid.
Luke 23:54 And it was the day of Preparation, and the Sabbath was dawning.
Luke 23:55 And women also who had come with him from Galilee, having followed after, beheld the tomb and how his body was placed.
Luke 23:56 And having returned, they prepared spices and ointments, and on the Sabbath indeed they rested according to the commandment.

## Chapter 24

Luke 24:1 And on the first day of the week, at deep dawn, they came to the tomb, bringing the spices they prepared, and some others with them.
Luke 24:2 And they found the stone rolled away from the tomb.
Luke 24:3 And having entered, they did not find the body of the Lord Jesus.
Luke 24:4 And it happened as they were greatly perplexed about this that look, two men stood by them in flashing garments.
Luke 24:5 And as they became fearful and bowed their face to the ground, they said to them, Why do you seek the living one among the dead?
Luke 24:6 He is not here, but was raised. Remember how he spoke to you while still being in Galilee,
Luke 24:7 saying that the Son of Man must be handed over into the hands of sinful people and be crucified, and on the third day rise.
Luke 24:8 And they remembered his sayings.
Luke 24:9 And having returned from the tomb, they reported all these things to the eleven and to all the rest.
Luke 24:10 And they were Mary Magdalene and Joanna and Mary of James and the rest with them, who were telling these things to the apostles.
Luke 24:11 And their sayings appeared before them as nonsense, and they were disbelieving them.
Luke 24:12 But Peter, having risen, ran to the tomb, and having stooped to look, sees the linen cloths lying alone; and he went away to himself, marveling at what had happened.
Luke 24:13 And look, two of them were going on that very day to a village sixty stadia distant from Jerusalem, whose name was Emmaus.
Luke 24:14 And they were conversing with each other about all these things that had happened.
Luke 24:15 And it happened as they were conversing and discussing that Jesus himself, having drawn near, was going with them.
Luke 24:16 But their eyes were held from recognizing him.
Luke 24:17 And he said to them, What are these words which you exchange with each other while walking, and you are gloomy?
Luke 24:18 And answering, the one whose name was Cleopas said to him, Do you alone sojourn in Jerusalem and not know the things that happened in it in these days?
Luke 24:19 And he said to them, What things? And they said to him, The things concerning Jesus the Nazarene, who became a man, a prophet mighty in deed and word before God and all the people,
Luke 24:20 and how the chief priests and our rulers handed him over to a judgment of death and crucified him.
Luke 24:21 But we were hoping that he is the one about to redeem Israel. But indeed, with all these things, today brings this third day since these things happened.
Luke 24:22 But also some women from among us astonished us, having been at the tomb early,
Luke 24:23 and not having found his body, they came, saying also that they had seen a vision of angels who say that he lives.
Luke 24:24 And some of those with us went away to the tomb and found it thus, just as the women also said, but they did not see him.
Luke 24:25 And he said to them, O foolish and slow in heart to believe all that the prophets spoke!
Luke 24:26 Did not the Christ have to suffer these things and enter into his glory?
Luke 24:27 And having begun from Moses and from all the prophets, he was interpreting to them in all the Scriptures the things concerning himself.
Luke 24:28 And they drew near to the village where they were going, and he was acting as though going farther.
Luke 24:29 And they urged him strongly, saying, Stay with us, because it is toward evening and the day has declined. And he entered to stay with them.
Luke 24:30 And it happened when he reclined with them that having taken the bread, he blessed, and having broken it, was giving it to them.
Luke 24:31 And their eyes were opened, and they recognized him, and he became invisible from them.
Luke 24:32 And they said to each other, Was not our heart burning within us as he was speaking to us on the road, and as he was opening the Scriptures to us?
Luke 24:33 And having risen in that very hour, they returned to Jerusalem and found the eleven and those with them gathered,
Luke 24:34 saying that the Lord was truly raised and appeared to Simon.
Luke 24:35 And they were relating the things on the road, and how he was known to them in the breaking of the bread.
Luke 24:36 And as they were speaking these things, Jesus himself stood in their midst and says to them, Peace to you.
Luke 24:37 But having been terrified and having become fearful, they supposed they were beholding a spirit.
Luke 24:38 And he said to them, Why are you troubled, and why do reasonings rise in your hearts?
Luke 24:39 See my hands and my feet, that I myself am he. Feel me and see, because a spirit does not have flesh and bones as you behold me having.
Luke 24:40 And having said this, he showed them his hands and feet.
Luke 24:41 And while they were still disbelieving from joy and marveling, he said to them, Do you have anything edible here?
Luke 24:42 And they gave him a portion of broiled fish and some from a honeycomb.
Luke 24:43 And having taken it, he ate before them.
Luke 24:44 And he said to them, These are the words which I spoke to you while still being with you, that all the things written in the law of Moses and prophets and Psalms concerning me must be fulfilled.
Luke 24:45 Then he opened their mind to understand the Scriptures.
Luke 24:46 And he said to them that thus it is written, and thus the Christ had to suffer and rise from the dead on the third day,
Luke 24:47 and repentance and forgiveness of sins to be proclaimed in his name to all the nations, beginning from Jerusalem.
Luke 24:48 And you are witnesses of these things.
Luke 24:49 And look, I send the promise of my Father upon you. But you, remain in the city of Jerusalem until you are clothed with power from on high.
Luke 24:50 And he led them out as far as Bethany, and having lifted his hands, blessed them.
Luke 24:51 And it happened as he was blessing them that he parted from them and was carried up into heaven.
Luke 24:52 And they, having worshiped him, returned to Jerusalem with great joy.
Luke 24:53 And they were continually in the temple, praising and blessing God. Amen.

# John

The Apostolic Bible. Public domain. https://apostolic-bible.ysys9.chatgpt.site/license.html


## Chapter 1

John 1:1 In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God.
John 1:2 He was in the beginning with God.
John 1:3 All things came into being through him, and apart from him not even one thing came into being that has come into being.
John 1:4 In him was life, and the life was the light of people.
John 1:5 And the light shines in the darkness, and the darkness did not grasp it.
John 1:6 There came a man sent from God; his name was John.
John 1:7 He came for testimony, so that he might testify concerning the light, so that all might believe through him.
John 1:8 He was not the light, but came so that he might testify concerning the light.
John 1:9 He was the true light, which illuminates every person coming into the world.
John 1:10 He was in the world, and the world came into being through him, and the world did not know him.
John 1:11 He came to his own things, and his own people did not receive him.
John 1:12 But as many as received him, he gave them authority to become children of God, to those believing in his name,
John 1:13 who were born not from bloods, nor from the will of flesh, nor from the will of a man, but from God.
John 1:14 And the Word became flesh and dwelt in a tent among us, and we beheld his glory, glory as of an only-begotten one from the Father, full of grace and truth.
John 1:15 John testifies concerning him and has cried out, saying, This was the one of whom I said, The one coming after me has come to be before me, because he was before me.
John 1:16 And from his fullness we all received, and grace in place of grace.
John 1:17 Because the law was given through Moses; grace and truth came through Jesus Christ.
John 1:18 No one has ever seen God; the only-begotten Son, who is in the bosom of the Father, he explained him.
John 1:19 And this is the testimony of John, when the Jews sent priests and Levites from Jerusalem so that they might ask him, Who are you?
John 1:20 And he confessed and did not deny, and confessed that I am not the Christ.
John 1:21 And they asked him, What then? Are you Elijah? And he says, I am not. Are you the Prophet? And he answered, No.
John 1:22 They said therefore to him, Who are you, so that we may give an answer to those who sent us? What do you say concerning yourself?
John 1:23 He said, I am a voice of one crying in the wilderness, Make straight the way of the Lord, just as Isaiah the prophet said.
John 1:24 And those sent were from the Pharisees.
John 1:25 And they asked him and said to him, Why then do you baptize, if you are not the Christ, nor Elijah, nor the Prophet?
John 1:26 John answered them, saying, I baptize in water, but in your midst stands one whom you do not know.
John 1:27 He is the one coming after me, who has come to be before me, whose sandal strap I am not worthy to untie.
John 1:28 These things happened in Bethabara beyond the Jordan, where John was baptizing.
John 1:29 On the next day John sees Jesus coming to him and says, See, the Lamb of God, who takes away the sin of the world.
John 1:30 This is he concerning whom I said, After me comes a man who has come to be before me, because he was before me.
John 1:31 And I did not know him, but so that he might be manifested to Israel, for this I came baptizing in water.
John 1:32 And John testified, saying, I have beheld the Spirit descending as a dove from heaven, and it remained upon him.
John 1:33 And I did not know him, but the one who sent me to baptize in water, he said to me, Upon whomever you see the Spirit descending and remaining upon him, this is the one baptizing in the Holy Spirit.
John 1:34 And I have seen and have testified that this is the Son of God.
John 1:35 On the next day John again stood, and two of his disciples.
John 1:36 And having looked at Jesus walking, he says, See, the Lamb of God.
John 1:37 And the two disciples heard him speaking and followed Jesus.
John 1:38 But Jesus, having turned and having beheld them following, says to them, What do you seek? And they said to him, Rabbi, which translated is said, Teacher, where do you stay?
John 1:39 He says to them, Come and see. They came and saw where he stays, and stayed with him that day; and it was about the tenth hour.
John 1:40 Andrew, the brother of Simon Peter, was one of the two who heard from John and followed him.
John 1:41 This man first finds his own brother Simon and says to him, We have found the Messiah, which translated is the Christ.
John 1:42 And he brought him to Jesus. And Jesus, having looked at him, said, You are Simon, the son of Jonah; you will be called Cephas, which is translated Peter.
John 1:43 On the next day Jesus wished to go out into Galilee, and finds Philip and says to him, Follow me.
John 1:44 And Philip was from Bethsaida, from the city of Andrew and Peter.
John 1:45 Philip finds Nathanael and says to him, We have found the one of whom Moses wrote in the law, and the prophets: Jesus, the son of Joseph, from Nazareth.
John 1:46 And Nathanael said to him, Can anything good be from Nazareth? Philip says to him, Come and see.
John 1:47 Jesus saw Nathanael coming to him and says concerning him, See, truly an Israelite in whom there is no deceit.
John 1:48 Nathanael says to him, From where do you know me? Jesus answered and said to him, Before Philip called you, being under the fig tree, I saw you.
John 1:49 Nathanael answered and says to him, Rabbi, you are the Son of God; you are the King of Israel.
John 1:50 Jesus answered and said to him, Because I said to you, I saw you beneath the fig tree, do you believe? You will see greater things than these.
John 1:51 And he says to him, Amen, amen, I say to you, From now you will see heaven opened, and the angels of God ascending and descending upon the Son of Man.

## Chapter 2

John 2:1 And on the third day a wedding took place in Cana of Galilee, and the mother of Jesus was there.
John 2:2 And Jesus also was invited, and his disciples, to the wedding.
John 2:3 And when wine was lacking, the mother of Jesus says to him, They have no wine.
John 2:4 Jesus says to her, What is there to me and to you, woman? My hour has not yet come.
John 2:5 His mother says to the servants, Whatever he says to you, do.
John 2:6 And six stone water jars were lying there, according to the purification of the Jews, holding two or three measures each.
John 2:7 Jesus says to them, Fill the water jars with water. And they filled them to the top.
John 2:8 And he says to them, Draw now and carry to the master of the feast. And they carried it.
John 2:9 And when the master of the feast tasted the water that had become wine, and did not know from where it is, but the servants who had drawn the water knew, the master of the feast calls the bridegroom,
John 2:10 and says to him, Every person sets out the good wine first, and when they have become drunk, then the inferior. You have kept the good wine until now.
John 2:11 Jesus did this beginning of the signs in Cana of Galilee, and manifested his glory, and his disciples believed in him.
John 2:12 After this he went down to Capernaum, he and his mother and his brothers and his disciples, and they stayed there not many days.
John 2:13 And the Passover of the Jews was near, and Jesus went up to Jerusalem.
John 2:14 And he found in the temple those selling oxen and sheep and doves, and the money changers sitting.
John 2:15 And having made a whip from cords, he cast all out of the temple, both the sheep and the oxen, and poured out the coins of the money changers and overturned the tables.
John 2:16 And he said to those selling the doves, Take these things away from here; do not make my Father's house a house of trade.
John 2:17 And his disciples remembered that it is written, The zeal of your house devoured me.
John 2:18 The Jews therefore answered and said to him, What sign do you show us, because you do these things?
John 2:19 Jesus answered and said to them, Destroy this sanctuary, and in three days I will raise it.
John 2:20 The Jews therefore said, In forty-six years this sanctuary was built, and will you raise it in three days?
John 2:21 But he was speaking concerning the sanctuary of his body.
John 2:22 When therefore he was raised from the dead, his disciples remembered that he was saying this to them, and believed the Scripture and the word which Jesus said.
John 2:23 And when he was in Jerusalem at the Passover, at the feast, many believed in his name, beholding his signs which he was doing.
John 2:24 But Jesus himself was not entrusting himself to them, because he knew all,
John 2:25 and because he had no need that anyone testify concerning the person, for he himself knew what was in the person.

## Chapter 3

John 3:1 And there was a man from the Pharisees, Nicodemus his name, a ruler of the Jews.
John 3:2 This man came to Jesus by night and said to him, Rabbi, we know that you have come from God as a teacher, for no one can do these signs which you do unless God is with him.
John 3:3 Jesus answered and said to him, Amen, amen, I say to you, Unless someone is born from above, he cannot see the kingdom of God.
John 3:4 Nicodemus says to him, How can a person be born, being old? He cannot enter a second time into his mother's womb and be born, can he?
John 3:5 Jesus answered, Amen, amen, I say to you, Unless someone is born from water and Spirit, he cannot enter into the kingdom of God.
John 3:6 What has been born from the flesh is flesh, and what has been born from the Spirit is spirit.
John 3:7 Do not marvel that I said to you, You must be born from above.
John 3:8 The spirit blows where it wishes, and you hear its voice, but do not know from where it comes and where it goes. Thus is everyone who has been born from the Spirit.
John 3:9 Nicodemus answered and said to him, How can these things happen?
John 3:10 Jesus answered and said to him, Are you the teacher of Israel, and do not know these things?
John 3:11 Amen, amen, I say to you that what we know we speak, and what we have seen we testify, and you do not receive our testimony.
John 3:12 If I told you the earthly things and you do not believe, how will you believe if I tell you the heavenly things?
John 3:13 And no one has ascended into heaven except the one who descended from heaven, the Son of Man, who is in heaven.
John 3:14 And just as Moses lifted up the serpent in the wilderness, thus the Son of Man must be lifted up,
John 3:15 so that everyone believing in him may not perish, but have eternal life.
John 3:16 For thus God loved the world, so that he gave his only-begotten Son, so that everyone believing in him may not perish, but have eternal life.
John 3:17 For God did not send his Son into the world so that he might judge the world, but so that the world might be saved through him.
John 3:18 The one believing in him is not judged, but the one not believing has already been judged, because he has not believed in the name of the only-begotten Son of God.
John 3:19 And this is the judgment, that the light has come into the world, and people loved the darkness rather than the light, for their works were wicked.
John 3:20 For everyone practicing base things hates the light and does not come to the light, so that his works may not be exposed.
John 3:21 But the one doing the truth comes to the light, so that his works may be manifested, that they have been worked in God.
John 3:22 After these things Jesus and his disciples came into the land of Judea, and there he was spending time with them and baptizing.
John 3:23 And John also was baptizing in Aenon near Salim, because there were many waters there, and they were coming and being baptized.
John 3:24 For John had not yet been thrown into the prison.
John 3:25 There arose therefore a dispute from John's disciples with Jews concerning purification.
John 3:26 And they came to John and said to him, Rabbi, the one who was with you beyond the Jordan, to whom you have testified, see, this man baptizes, and all come to him.
John 3:27 John answered and said, A person can receive nothing unless it has been given to him from heaven.
John 3:28 You yourselves testify to me that I said, I am not the Christ, but that I have been sent before him.
John 3:29 The one having the bride is the bridegroom, but the friend of the bridegroom, who stands and hears him, rejoices with joy because of the bridegroom's voice. This joy of mine therefore has been fulfilled.
John 3:30 He must increase, but I must decrease.
John 3:31 The one coming from above is above all. The one being from the earth is from the earth and speaks from the earth. The one coming from heaven is above all.
John 3:32 And what he has seen and heard, this he testifies, and no one receives his testimony.
John 3:33 The one who received his testimony sealed that God is true.
John 3:34 For the one whom God sent speaks the sayings of God, for God does not give the Spirit by measure.
John 3:35 The Father loves the Son and has given all things in his hand.
John 3:36 The one believing in the Son has eternal life, but the one disobeying the Son will not see life, but the wrath of God remains upon him.

## Chapter 4

John 4:1 When therefore the Lord knew that the Pharisees heard that Jesus makes and baptizes more disciples than John,
John 4:2 although Jesus himself was not baptizing, but his disciples,
John 4:3 he left Judea and went away again into Galilee.
John 4:4 And he had to pass through Samaria.
John 4:5 He comes therefore into a city of Samaria called Sychar, near the field which Jacob gave to Joseph his son.
John 4:6 And Jacob's spring was there. Jesus therefore, having become wearied from the journey, was sitting thus at the spring. It was about the sixth hour.
John 4:7 A woman from Samaria comes to draw water. Jesus says to her, Give me to drink.
John 4:8 For his disciples had gone away into the city so that they might buy food.
John 4:9 The Samaritan woman therefore says to him, How do you, being a Jew, ask to drink from me, being a Samaritan woman? For Jews do not associate with Samaritans.
John 4:10 Jesus answered and said to her, If you knew the gift of God, and who is the one saying to you, Give me to drink, you would have asked him, and he would have given you living water.
John 4:11 The woman says to him, Sir, you do not even have a drawing vessel, and the well is deep. From where therefore do you have the living water?
John 4:12 You are not greater than our father Jacob, who gave us the well and drank from it himself, and his sons and his livestock, are you?
John 4:13 Jesus answered and said to her, Everyone drinking from this water will thirst again.
John 4:14 But whoever drinks from the water which I will give him will certainly not thirst forever, but the water which I will give him will become in him a spring of water leaping into eternal life.
John 4:15 The woman says to him, Sir, give me this water, so that I may not thirst nor come here to draw.
John 4:16 Jesus says to her, Go, call your husband, and come here.
John 4:17 The woman answered and said, I have no husband. Jesus says to her, You said well, I have no husband.
John 4:18 For you had five husbands, and the one you now have is not your husband. This you have spoken truly.
John 4:19 The woman says to him, Sir, I behold that you are a prophet.
John 4:20 Our fathers worshiped on this mountain, and you say that in Jerusalem is the place where one must worship.
John 4:21 Jesus says to her, Woman, believe me that an hour comes when neither on this mountain nor in Jerusalem will you worship the Father.
John 4:22 You worship what you do not know; we worship what we know, because salvation is from the Jews.
John 4:23 But an hour comes, and now is, when the true worshipers will worship the Father in spirit and truth, for the Father also seeks such as those worshiping him.
John 4:24 God is spirit, and those worshiping him must worship in spirit and truth.
John 4:25 The woman says to him, I know that Messiah comes, the one called Christ. When he comes, he will announce all things to us.
John 4:26 Jesus says to her, I am, the one speaking to you.
John 4:27 And upon this his disciples came, and marveled that he was speaking with a woman. Nevertheless no one said, What do you seek? or, Why do you speak with her?
John 4:28 The woman therefore left her water jar and went away into the city, and says to the people,
John 4:29 Come, see a man who told me all things that I did. Could this be the Christ?
John 4:30 They therefore went out from the city and were coming to him.
John 4:31 And in the meantime the disciples were asking him, saying, Rabbi, eat.
John 4:32 But he said to them, I have food to eat which you do not know.
John 4:33 The disciples therefore were saying to each other, Did anyone bring him something to eat?
John 4:34 Jesus says to them, My food is that I may do the will of the one who sent me and complete his work.
John 4:35 Do you not say that there are still four months, and the harvest comes? Look, I say to you, Lift up your eyes and behold the fields, because they are already white for harvest.
John 4:36 And the one reaping receives wages and gathers fruit into eternal life, so that both the one sowing and the one reaping may rejoice together.
John 4:37 For in this the saying is true, that one is the one sowing and another the one reaping.
John 4:38 I sent you to reap what you have not labored for. Others have labored, and you have entered into their labor.
John 4:39 And from that city many of the Samaritans believed in him because of the word of the woman testifying that he told me all things that I did.
John 4:40 When therefore the Samaritans came to him, they were asking him to stay with them, and he stayed there two days.
John 4:41 And many more believed because of his word.
John 4:42 And they were saying to the woman, We no longer believe because of your speech, for we ourselves have heard and know that this is truly the Savior of the world, the Christ.
John 4:43 And after the two days he went out from there and went away into Galilee.
John 4:44 For Jesus himself testified that a prophet has no honor in his own homeland.
John 4:45 When therefore he came into Galilee, the Galileans received him, having seen all the things he did in Jerusalem at the feast, for they also came to the feast.
John 4:46 Jesus therefore came again into Cana of Galilee, where he made the water wine. And there was a certain royal official whose son was sick in Capernaum.
John 4:47 This man, having heard that Jesus has come from Judea into Galilee, went away to him and was asking him to come down and heal his son, for he was about to die.
John 4:48 Jesus therefore said to him, Unless you see signs and wonders, you will certainly not believe.
John 4:49 The royal official says to him, Sir, come down before my child dies.
John 4:50 Jesus says to him, Go; your son lives. And the man believed the word which Jesus said to him, and was going.
John 4:51 And as he was already going down, his slaves met him and reported, saying that your boy lives.
John 4:52 He therefore inquired from them the hour in which he became better, and they said to him, Yesterday at the seventh hour the fever left him.
John 4:53 The father therefore knew that it was in that hour in which Jesus said to him, Your son lives, and he himself believed, and his whole house.
John 4:54 This again Jesus did as a second sign, having come from Judea into Galilee.

## Chapter 5

John 5:1 After these things there was a feast of the Jews, and Jesus went up to Jerusalem.
John 5:2 And in Jerusalem at the Sheep Gate there is a pool, called in Hebrew Bethesda, having five porticoes.
John 5:3 In these lay a great multitude of the sick, blind, lame, withered, awaiting the movement of the water.
John 5:4 For an angel at a season was descending in the pool and troubling the water. Therefore the first who stepped in after the troubling of the water became healthy, with whatever disease he was held.
John 5:5 And a certain man was there, having thirty-eight years in sickness.
John 5:6 Jesus, having seen him lying and having known that he already has much time, says to him, Do you wish to become healthy?
John 5:7 The sick man answered him, Sir, I have no person to put me into the pool when the water is troubled; but while I am coming, another goes down before me.
John 5:8 Jesus says to him, Rise, take up your pallet, and walk.
John 5:9 And immediately the man became healthy, and took up his pallet and was walking. And it was Sabbath on that day.
John 5:10 The Jews therefore were saying to the one healed, It is Sabbath; it is not lawful for you to take up the pallet.
John 5:11 He answered them, The one who made me healthy, he said to me, Take up your pallet and walk.
John 5:12 They therefore asked him, Who is the man who said to you, Take up your pallet and walk?
John 5:13 But the one healed did not know who he is, for Jesus slipped away, a crowd being in the place.
John 5:14 After these things Jesus finds him in the temple and said to him, See, you have become healthy. Sin no longer, so that something worse may not happen to you.
John 5:15 The man went away and announced to the Jews that Jesus is the one who made him healthy.
John 5:16 And because of this the Jews were persecuting Jesus and seeking to kill him, because he was doing these things on Sabbath.
John 5:17 But Jesus answered them, My Father works until now, and I work.
John 5:18 Because of this therefore the Jews were seeking still more to kill him, because he was not only breaking the Sabbath, but also calling God his own Father, making himself equal to God.
John 5:19 Jesus therefore answered and said to them, Amen, amen, I say to you, The Son can do nothing from himself unless he sees the Father doing something, for whatever he does, these things the Son also does likewise.
John 5:20 For the Father loves the Son and shows him all things which he himself does, and will show him greater works than these, so that you may marvel.
John 5:21 For just as the Father raises the dead and makes them alive, thus also the Son makes alive those whom he wishes.
John 5:22 For neither does the Father judge anyone, but has given all judgment to the Son,
John 5:23 so that all may honor the Son just as they honor the Father. The one not honoring the Son does not honor the Father who sent him.
John 5:24 Amen, amen, I say to you that the one hearing my word and believing the one who sent me has eternal life, and does not come into judgment, but has passed from death into life.
John 5:25 Amen, amen, I say to you that an hour comes, and now is, when the dead will hear the voice of the Son of God, and those who heard will live.
John 5:26 For just as the Father has life in himself, thus he also gave to the Son to have life in himself.
John 5:27 And he also gave him authority to execute judgment, because he is Son of Man.
John 5:28 Do not marvel at this, because an hour comes in which all those in the tombs will hear his voice,
John 5:29 and will go out, those who did the good things into a resurrection of life, but those who practiced the base things into a resurrection of judgment.
John 5:30 I can do nothing from myself. Just as I hear, I judge, and my judgment is righteous, because I do not seek my own will, but the will of the Father who sent me.
John 5:31 If I testify concerning myself, my testimony is not true.
John 5:32 There is another who testifies concerning me, and I know that the testimony which he testifies concerning me is true.
John 5:33 You have sent to John, and he has testified to the truth.
John 5:34 But I do not receive testimony from a person; rather, I say these things so that you may be saved.
John 5:35 He was the lamp burning and shining, but you wished to exult for an hour in his light.
John 5:36 But I have testimony greater than John's, for the works which the Father gave me so that I may complete them, the very works which I do, testify concerning me that the Father has sent me.
John 5:37 And the Father who sent me has himself testified concerning me. You have neither ever heard his voice nor seen his form.
John 5:38 And you do not have his word remaining in you, because the one whom he sent, this one you do not believe.
John 5:39 Search the Scriptures, because you suppose you have eternal life in them, and they are those testifying concerning me.
John 5:40 And you do not wish to come to me so that you may have life.
John 5:41 I do not receive glory from people.
John 5:42 But I have known you, that you do not have the love of God in yourselves.
John 5:43 I have come in the name of my Father, and you do not receive me. If another comes in his own name, you will receive that one.
John 5:44 How can you believe, receiving glory from each other, and you do not seek the glory from the only God?
John 5:45 Do not suppose that I will accuse you before the Father. There is one accusing you, Moses, in whom you have hoped.
John 5:46 For if you believed Moses, you would believe me, for he wrote concerning me.
John 5:47 But if you do not believe his writings, how will you believe my sayings?

## Chapter 6

John 6:1 After these things Jesus went away beyond the sea of Galilee, of Tiberias.
John 6:2 And a great crowd was following him, because they were seeing his signs which he was doing upon the sick.
John 6:3 And Jesus went up into the mountain, and there was sitting with his disciples.
John 6:4 And the Passover, the feast of the Jews, was near.
John 6:5 Jesus therefore, having lifted his eyes and having beheld that a great crowd comes to him, says to Philip, From where shall we buy breads so that these may eat?
John 6:6 And he was saying this testing him, for he himself knew what he was about to do.
John 6:7 Philip answered him, Breads of two hundred denarii are not enough for them, so that each of them may receive a little.
John 6:8 One of his disciples, Andrew, the brother of Simon Peter, says to him,
John 6:9 There is one little boy here who has five barley breads and two small fish, but what are these for so many?
John 6:10 And Jesus said, Make the people recline. And there was much grass in the place. The men therefore reclined, about five thousand in number.
John 6:11 And Jesus took the breads, and having given thanks, distributed to the disciples, and the disciples to those reclining; likewise also from the small fish, as much as they wished.
John 6:12 And when they were filled, he says to his disciples, Gather the fragments that remained over, so that nothing may perish.
John 6:13 They therefore gathered and filled twelve baskets with fragments from the five barley breads, which remained over to those who had eaten.
John 6:14 The people therefore, having seen the sign which Jesus did, were saying that this is truly the Prophet coming into the world.
John 6:15 Jesus therefore, having known that they are about to come and seize him so that they may make him king, withdrew again into the mountain, himself alone.
John 6:16 And when evening came, his disciples went down to the sea,
John 6:17 and having entered into the boat, were coming beyond the sea to Capernaum. And darkness had already come, and Jesus had not come to them.
John 6:18 And the sea was being stirred up, a great wind blowing.
John 6:19 Having therefore rowed about twenty-five or thirty stadia, they behold Jesus walking upon the sea and coming near the boat, and they were afraid.
John 6:20 But he says to them, I am; do not fear.
John 6:21 They therefore wished to receive him into the boat, and immediately the boat came to the land to which they were going.
John 6:22 On the next day the crowd standing beyond the sea, having seen that no other little boat was there except that one into which his disciples entered, and that Jesus did not enter together with his disciples into the little boat, but his disciples alone went away,
John 6:23 but other little boats came from Tiberias near the place where they ate the bread after the Lord had given thanks,
John 6:24 when therefore the crowd saw that Jesus is not there, nor his disciples, they themselves also entered into the boats and came to Capernaum, seeking Jesus.
John 6:25 And having found him beyond the sea, they said to him, Rabbi, when have you come here?
John 6:26 Jesus answered them and said, Amen, amen, I say to you, You seek me not because you saw signs, but because you ate from the breads and were filled.
John 6:27 Work not for the food that perishes, but for the food that remains into eternal life, which the Son of Man will give you, for him the Father, God, sealed.
John 6:28 They therefore said to him, What do we do so that we may work the works of God?
John 6:29 Jesus answered and said to them, This is the work of God, that you believe in the one whom he sent.
John 6:30 They therefore said to him, What sign therefore do you do, so that we may see and believe you? What do you work?
John 6:31 Our fathers ate the manna in the wilderness, just as it is written, He gave them bread from heaven to eat.
John 6:32 Jesus therefore said to them, Amen, amen, I say to you, Moses has not given you the bread from heaven, but my Father gives you the true bread from heaven.
John 6:33 For the bread of God is the one descending from heaven and giving life to the world.
John 6:34 They therefore said to him, Lord, always give us this bread.
John 6:35 And Jesus said to them, I am the bread of life. The one coming to me will certainly not hunger, and the one believing in me will certainly never thirst.
John 6:36 But I said to you that you have both seen me and do not believe.
John 6:37 Everything which the Father gives me will come to me, and the one coming to me I will certainly not cast outside.
John 6:38 Because I have descended from heaven not so that I may do my own will, but the will of the one who sent me.
John 6:39 And this is the will of the Father who sent me, that of everything which he has given me I may lose nothing, but raise it on the last day.
John 6:40 And this is the will of the one who sent me, that everyone beholding the Son and believing in him may have eternal life, and I will raise him on the last day.
John 6:41 The Jews therefore were murmuring concerning him, because he said, I am the bread that descended from heaven.
John 6:42 And they were saying, Is this not Jesus, the son of Joseph, whose father and mother we know? How therefore does this man say, I have descended from heaven?
John 6:43 Jesus therefore answered and said to them, Do not murmur with each other.
John 6:44 No one can come to me unless the Father who sent me draws him, and I will raise him on the last day.
John 6:45 It is written in the prophets, And all will be taught by God. Everyone therefore who heard from the Father and learned comes to me.
John 6:46 Not that anyone has seen the Father except the one being from God; he has seen the Father.
John 6:47 Amen, amen, I say to you, The one believing in me has eternal life.
John 6:48 I am the bread of life.
John 6:49 Your fathers ate the manna in the wilderness and died.
John 6:50 This is the bread descending from heaven, so that someone may eat from it and not die.
John 6:51 I am the living bread that descended from heaven. If anyone eats from this bread, he will live forever. And also the bread which I will give is my flesh, which I will give for the life of the world.
John 6:52 The Jews therefore were fighting with each other, saying, How can this man give us his flesh to eat?
John 6:53 Jesus therefore said to them, Amen, amen, I say to you, Unless you eat the flesh of the Son of Man and drink his blood, you do not have life in yourselves.
John 6:54 The one chewing my flesh and drinking my blood has eternal life, and I will raise him on the last day.
John 6:55 For my flesh truly is food, and my blood truly is drink.
John 6:56 The one chewing my flesh and drinking my blood remains in me, and I in him.
John 6:57 Just as the living Father sent me, and I live because of the Father, also the one chewing me, that one too will live because of me.
John 6:58 This is the bread that descended from heaven, not as your fathers ate the manna and died. The one chewing this bread will live forever.
John 6:59 He said these things in a synagogue, teaching in Capernaum.
John 6:60 Many therefore of his disciples, having heard, said, This word is hard; who can hear it?
John 6:61 But Jesus, knowing in himself that his disciples murmur concerning this, said to them, Does this cause you to stumble?
John 6:62 If therefore you behold the Son of Man ascending where he was before?
John 6:63 The Spirit is the one making alive; the flesh benefits nothing. The sayings which I speak to you are spirit and are life.
John 6:64 But there are some of you who do not believe. For Jesus knew from the beginning who are those not believing, and who is the one who will hand him over.
John 6:65 And he was saying, Because of this I have said to you that no one can come to me unless it has been given to him from my Father.
John 6:66 From this many of his disciples went away backward, and were no longer walking with him.
John 6:67 Jesus therefore said to the twelve, You too do not wish to go away, do you?
John 6:68 Simon Peter therefore answered him, Lord, to whom shall we go away? You have sayings of eternal life.
John 6:69 And we have believed and have known that you are the Christ, the Son of the living God.
John 6:70 Jesus answered them, Did I not choose you, the twelve? And one of you is a devil.
John 6:71 And he was speaking of Judas Iscariot of Simon, for this man was about to hand him over, being one of the twelve.

## Chapter 7

John 7:1 And after these things Jesus was walking in Galilee, for he did not wish to walk in Judea, because the Jews were seeking to kill him.
John 7:2 And the feast of the Jews, the Tent-pitching, was near.
John 7:3 His brothers therefore said to him, Depart from here and go into Judea, so that your disciples also may behold your works which you do.
John 7:4 For no one does anything in secret and himself seeks to be in openness. If you do these things, manifest yourself to the world.
John 7:5 For not even his brothers were believing in him.
John 7:6 Jesus therefore says to them, My time is not yet present, but your time is always ready.
John 7:7 The world cannot hate you, but hates me, because I testify concerning it that its works are wicked.
John 7:8 You go up to this feast; I do not yet go up to this feast, because my time has not yet been fulfilled.
John 7:9 And having said these things to them, he remained in Galilee.
John 7:10 But when his brothers went up, then he himself also went up to the feast, not openly, but as in secret.
John 7:11 The Jews therefore were seeking him at the feast, and were saying, Where is he?
John 7:12 And there was much murmuring concerning him among the crowds. Some were saying that he is good, but others were saying, No, but he leads the crowd astray.
John 7:13 Nevertheless no one was speaking openly concerning him because of the fear of the Jews.
John 7:14 And when the feast was already at its middle, Jesus went up into the temple and was teaching.
John 7:15 And the Jews were marveling, saying, How does this man know letters, not having learned?
John 7:16 Jesus answered them and said, My teaching is not mine, but of the one who sent me.
John 7:17 If anyone wishes to do his will, he will know concerning the teaching, whether it is from God or I speak from myself.
John 7:18 The one speaking from himself seeks his own glory, but the one seeking the glory of the one who sent him, this one is true, and there is no unrighteousness in him.
John 7:19 Has Moses not given you the law? And none of you does the law. Why do you seek to kill me?
John 7:20 The crowd answered and said, You have a demon. Who seeks to kill you?
John 7:21 Jesus answered and said to them, I did one work, and you all marvel.
John 7:22 Because of this Moses has given you circumcision, not that it is from Moses, but from the fathers, and on Sabbath you circumcise a person.
John 7:23 If a person receives circumcision on Sabbath so that the law of Moses may not be broken, are you angry with me because I made a whole person healthy on Sabbath?
John 7:24 Do not judge according to appearance, but judge the righteous judgment.
John 7:25 Some of the Jerusalemites therefore were saying, Is this not the one whom they seek to kill?
John 7:26 And see, he speaks openly, and they say nothing to him. Could the rulers truly have known that this is truly the Christ?
John 7:27 But we know this man, from where he is; but when the Christ comes, no one knows from where he is.
John 7:28 Jesus therefore cried out in the temple, teaching and saying, You both know me and know from where I am. And I have not come from myself, but the one who sent me is true, whom you do not know.
John 7:29 But I know him, because I am from him, and he sent me.
John 7:30 They therefore were seeking to seize him, and no one laid a hand upon him, because his hour had not yet come.
John 7:31 But many from the crowd believed in him, and were saying, When the Christ comes, will he do more signs than these which this man did?
John 7:32 The Pharisees heard the crowd murmuring these things concerning him, and the Pharisees and the chief priests sent officers so that they might seize him.
John 7:33 Jesus therefore said to them, I am with you still a little time, and go to the one who sent me.
John 7:34 You will seek me and will not find, and where I am you cannot come.
John 7:35 The Jews therefore said among themselves, Where is this man about to go, that we will not find him? Is he about to go into the dispersion of the Greeks and teach the Greeks?
John 7:36 What is this word which he said, You will seek me and will not find, and where I am you cannot come?
John 7:37 And on the last day, the great one of the feast, Jesus stood and cried out, saying, If anyone thirsts, let him come to me and drink.
John 7:38 The one believing in me, just as the Scripture said, rivers of living water will flow from his belly.
John 7:39 And he said this concerning the Spirit, which those believing in him were about to receive, for there was not yet Holy Spirit, because Jesus was not yet glorified.
John 7:40 Many therefore from the crowd, having heard the word, were saying, This is truly the Prophet.
John 7:41 Others were saying, This is the Christ. But others were saying, Does the Christ come from Galilee?
John 7:42 Did not the Scripture say that the Christ comes from the seed of David and from Bethlehem, the village where David was?
John 7:43 A division therefore arose in the crowd because of him.
John 7:44 And some of them wished to seize him, but no one laid hands upon him.
John 7:45 The officers therefore came to the chief priests and Pharisees, and those said to them, Why did you not bring him?
John 7:46 The officers answered, Never did a person speak thus, as this person.
John 7:47 The Pharisees therefore answered them, Have you too been led astray?
John 7:48 Has anyone from the rulers believed in him, or from the Pharisees?
John 7:49 But this crowd, not knowing the law, they are accursed.
John 7:50 Nicodemus says to them, the one who came to him by night, being one of them,
John 7:51 Does our law judge the person unless it first hears from him and knows what he does?
John 7:52 They answered and said to him, Are you too from Galilee? Search and see that a prophet has not arisen from Galilee.
John 7:53 And each went to his house.

## Chapter 8

John 8:1 But Jesus went to the Mount of Olives.
John 8:2 And at dawn he came again into the temple, and all the people were coming to him, and having sat down, he was teaching them.
John 8:3 And the scribes and the Pharisees bring to him a woman caught in adultery, and having stood her in the midst,
John 8:4 they say to him, Teacher, this woman was caught in the very act of committing adultery.
John 8:5 And in the law Moses commanded us that such women be stoned. What therefore do you say?
John 8:6 And they were saying this testing him, so that they might have something to accuse him of. But Jesus, having bent down, was writing with his finger into the ground.
John 8:7 And as they persisted in asking him, having straightened up, he said to them, Let the sinless one of you first throw the stone at her.
John 8:8 And again having bent down, he was writing into the ground.
John 8:9 But having heard, and being convicted by conscience, they were going out one by one, having begun from the elders to the last, and Jesus was left alone, and the woman standing in the midst.
John 8:10 And Jesus, having straightened up and having beheld no one except the woman, said to her, Woman, where are those accusers of yours? Did no one condemn you?
John 8:11 And she said, No one, Lord. And Jesus said to her, Neither do I condemn you. Go, and sin no longer.
John 8:12 Jesus therefore spoke to them again, saying, I am the light of the world. The one following me will certainly not walk in the darkness, but will have the light of life.
John 8:13 The Pharisees therefore said to him, You testify concerning yourself; your testimony is not true.
John 8:14 Jesus answered and said to them, Even if I testify concerning myself, my testimony is true, because I know from where I came and where I go. But you do not know from where I come and where I go.
John 8:15 You judge according to the flesh; I judge no one.
John 8:16 And even if I judge, my judgment is true, because I am not alone, but I and the Father who sent me.
John 8:17 And in your law also it is written that the testimony of two people is true.
John 8:18 I am the one testifying concerning myself, and the Father who sent me testifies concerning me.
John 8:19 They therefore were saying to him, Where is your Father? Jesus answered, You know neither me nor my Father. If you knew me, you would also know my Father.
John 8:20 Jesus spoke these sayings in the treasury, teaching in the temple, and no one seized him, because his hour had not yet come.
John 8:21 Jesus therefore said again to them, I go away, and you will seek me and die in your sin. Where I go, you cannot come.
John 8:22 The Jews therefore were saying, Will he kill himself, because he says, Where I go, you cannot come?
John 8:23 And he said to them, You are from the things below; I am from the things above. You are from this world; I am not from this world.
John 8:24 I therefore said to you that you will die in your sins, for unless you believe that I am, you will die in your sins.
John 8:25 They therefore were saying to him, Who are you? And Jesus said to them, From the beginning, what I also speak to you.
John 8:26 I have many things to speak and judge concerning you, but the one who sent me is true, and what I heard from him, these things I say to the world.
John 8:27 They did not know that he was speaking to them of the Father.
John 8:28 Jesus therefore said to them, When you lift up the Son of Man, then you will know that I am, and I do nothing from myself, but just as my Father taught me, these things I speak.
John 8:29 And the one who sent me is with me; the Father did not leave me alone, because I always do the things pleasing to him.
John 8:30 As he was speaking these things, many believed in him.
John 8:31 Jesus therefore was saying to the Jews who had believed him, If you remain in my word, you are truly my disciples,
John 8:32 and you will know the truth, and the truth will free you.
John 8:33 They answered him, We are Abraham's seed, and have never been enslaved to anyone. How do you say that you will become free?
John 8:34 Jesus answered them, Amen, amen, I say to you that everyone doing sin is a slave of sin.
John 8:35 And the slave does not remain in the house forever; the son remains forever.
John 8:36 If therefore the Son frees you, you will be truly free.
John 8:37 I know that you are Abraham's seed, but you seek to kill me, because my word finds no room in you.
John 8:38 I speak what I have seen with my Father, and you therefore do what you have seen with your father.
John 8:39 They answered and said to him, Our father is Abraham. Jesus says to them, If you were Abraham's children, you would do Abraham's works.
John 8:40 But now you seek to kill me, a man who has spoken to you the truth which I heard from God. Abraham did not do this.
John 8:41 You do the works of your father. They therefore said to him, We have not been born from fornication; we have one Father, God.
John 8:42 Jesus therefore said to them, If God were your Father, you would love me, for I went out from God and have come; for neither have I come from myself, but he sent me.
John 8:43 Why do you not know my speech? Because you cannot hear my word.
John 8:44 You are from your father the devil, and you wish to do the desires of your father. He was a murderer from the beginning and has not stood in the truth, because there is no truth in him. When he speaks the lie, he speaks from his own things, because he is a liar and its father.
John 8:45 But because I say the truth, you do not believe me.
John 8:46 Who of you convicts me concerning sin? But if I say truth, why do you not believe me?
John 8:47 The one being from God hears the sayings of God. Because of this you do not hear, because you are not from God.
John 8:48 The Jews therefore answered and said to him, Do we not say well that you are a Samaritan and have a demon?
John 8:49 Jesus answered, I do not have a demon, but honor my Father, and you dishonor me.
John 8:50 But I do not seek my glory; there is one seeking and judging.
John 8:51 Amen, amen, I say to you, If anyone keeps my word, he will certainly not behold death forever.
John 8:52 The Jews therefore said to him, Now we have known that you have a demon. Abraham died, and the prophets, and you say, If anyone keeps my word, he will certainly not taste death forever.
John 8:53 You are not greater than our father Abraham, who died, are you? And the prophets died. Whom do you make yourself?
John 8:54 Jesus answered, If I glorify myself, my glory is nothing. It is my Father who glorifies me, of whom you say that he is your God.
John 8:55 And you have not known him, but I know him. And if I say that I do not know him, I will be like you, a liar. But I know him and keep his word.
John 8:56 Abraham your father exulted so that he might see my day, and he saw and rejoiced.
John 8:57 The Jews therefore said to him, You do not yet have fifty years, and have you seen Abraham?
John 8:58 Jesus said to them, Amen, amen, I say to you, Before Abraham came into being, I am.
John 8:59 They therefore took up stones so that they might throw them at him. But Jesus was hidden and went out of the temple, having passed through their midst, and was passing by thus.

## Chapter 9

John 9:1 And passing by, he saw a person blind from birth.
John 9:2 And his disciples asked him, saying, Rabbi, who sinned, this man or his parents, so that he was born blind?
John 9:3 Jesus answered, Neither this man sinned nor his parents, but so that the works of God might be manifested in him.
John 9:4 I must work the works of the one who sent me while it is day. Night comes, when no one can work.
John 9:5 When I am in the world, I am light of the world.
John 9:6 Having said these things, he spat on the ground and made clay from the spittle, and smeared the clay upon the eyes of the blind man.
John 9:7 And he said to him, Go, wash in the pool of Siloam, which is translated Sent. He therefore went away and washed, and came seeing.
John 9:8 The neighbors therefore, and those beholding him before, that he was blind, were saying, Is this not the one sitting and begging?
John 9:9 Others were saying that this is he, but others that he is like him. He was saying, I am he.
John 9:10 They therefore were saying to him, How were your eyes opened?
John 9:11 He answered and said, A man called Jesus made clay and smeared my eyes, and said to me, Go to the pool of Siloam and wash. And having gone away and washed, I received sight.
John 9:12 They therefore said to him, Where is he? He says, I do not know.
John 9:13 They bring him to the Pharisees, the one formerly blind.
John 9:14 And it was Sabbath when Jesus made the clay and opened his eyes.
John 9:15 Again therefore the Pharisees also were asking him how he received sight. And he said to them, He placed clay upon my eyes, and I washed, and I see.
John 9:16 Some of the Pharisees therefore were saying, This man is not from God, because he does not keep the Sabbath. Others were saying, How can a sinful man do such signs? And there was division among them.
John 9:17 They say to the blind man again, What do you say concerning him, because he opened your eyes? And he said that he is a prophet.
John 9:18 The Jews therefore did not believe concerning him that he was blind and received sight, until they called his parents, of the one who received sight,
John 9:19 and asked them, saying, Is this your son, whom you say was born blind? How therefore does he now see?
John 9:20 His parents answered them and said, We know that this is our son, and that he was born blind.
John 9:21 But how he now sees we do not know, or who opened his eyes we do not know. He has age; ask him. He will speak concerning himself.
John 9:22 His parents said these things because they feared the Jews, for the Jews had already agreed that if anyone confessed him as Christ, he should become expelled from the synagogue.
John 9:23 Because of this his parents said, He has age; ask him.
John 9:24 They therefore called a second time the man who was blind, and said to him, Give glory to God. We know that this man is sinful.
John 9:25 He therefore answered and said, If he is sinful, I do not know. One thing I know, that being blind, now I see.
John 9:26 And they said to him again, What did he do to you? How did he open your eyes?
John 9:27 He answered them, I told you already, and you did not hear. Why do you wish to hear again? You too do not wish to become his disciples, do you?
John 9:28 They therefore reviled him and said, You are that man's disciple, but we are Moses' disciples.
John 9:29 We know that God has spoken to Moses, but this man, we do not know from where he is.
John 9:30 The man answered and said to them, For in this is the marvelous thing, that you do not know from where he is, and he opened my eyes.
John 9:31 And we know that God does not hear sinners, but if anyone is God-revering and does his will, he hears this one.
John 9:32 From the age it was not heard that anyone opened the eyes of one born blind.
John 9:33 If this man were not from God, he could do nothing.
John 9:34 They answered and said to him, You were born wholly in sins, and do you teach us? And they cast him outside.
John 9:35 Jesus heard that they cast him outside, and having found him, said to him, Do you believe in the Son of God?
John 9:36 He answered and said, Who is he, Lord, so that I may believe in him?
John 9:37 And Jesus said to him, You have both seen him, and the one speaking with you is he.
John 9:38 And he said, I believe, Lord, and worshiped him.
John 9:39 And Jesus said, For judgment I came into this world, so that those not seeing may see, and those seeing may become blind.
John 9:40 And those of the Pharisees being with him heard these things and said to him, We too are not blind, are we?
John 9:41 Jesus said to them, If you were blind, you would not have sin. But now you say that we see; therefore your sin remains.

## Chapter 10

John 10:1 Amen, amen, I say to you, The one not entering through the door into the enclosure of the sheep, but climbing up from elsewhere, that one is a thief and a robber.
John 10:2 But the one entering through the door is shepherd of the sheep.
John 10:3 To him the doorkeeper opens, and the sheep hear his voice, and he calls his own sheep by name and leads them out.
John 10:4 And when he brings out his own sheep, he goes before them, and the sheep follow him, because they know his voice.
John 10:5 But they will certainly not follow a stranger, but will flee from him, because they do not know the voice of strangers.
John 10:6 Jesus said this figure to them, but they did not know what the things were which he was speaking to them.
John 10:7 Jesus therefore said again to them, Amen, amen, I say to you that I am the door of the sheep.
John 10:8 All who came before me are thieves and robbers, but the sheep did not hear them.
John 10:9 I am the door. If anyone enters through me, he will be saved, and will enter and go out and find pasture.
John 10:10 The thief does not come except so that he may steal and slaughter and destroy. I came so that they may have life, and have abundance.
John 10:11 I am the good shepherd. The good shepherd lays down his life for the sheep.
John 10:12 But the hired man, and not being a shepherd, whose sheep are not his own, beholds the wolf coming and leaves the sheep and flees, and the wolf seizes them and scatters the sheep.
John 10:13 And the hired man flees because he is a hired man, and he does not care concerning the sheep.
John 10:14 I am the good shepherd, and know my own, and am known by my own,
John 10:15 just as the Father knows me, and I know the Father; and I lay down my life for the sheep.
John 10:16 And I have other sheep which are not from this enclosure. Those also I must bring, and they will hear my voice, and there will be one flock, one shepherd.
John 10:17 Because of this the Father loves me, because I lay down my life so that I may take it again.
John 10:18 No one takes it from me, but I lay it down from myself. I have authority to lay it down, and I have authority to take it again. This commandment I received from my Father.
John 10:19 A division therefore arose again among the Jews because of these words.
John 10:20 And many of them were saying, He has a demon and is mad. Why do you hear him?
John 10:21 Others were saying, These sayings are not of one demon-possessed. A demon cannot open blind people's eyes, can it?
John 10:22 And the Dedication took place in Jerusalem, and it was winter.
John 10:23 And Jesus was walking in the temple, in Solomon's portico.
John 10:24 The Jews therefore surrounded him and were saying to him, Until when do you keep our soul in suspense? If you are the Christ, tell us openly.
John 10:25 Jesus answered them, I told you, and you do not believe. The works which I do in my Father's name, these testify concerning me.
John 10:26 But you do not believe, for you are not from my sheep, just as I said to you.
John 10:27 My sheep hear my voice, and I know them, and they follow me.
John 10:28 And I give them eternal life, and they will certainly not perish forever, and no one will snatch them from my hand.
John 10:29 My Father, who has given to me, is greater than all, and no one can snatch from my Father's hand.
John 10:30 I and the Father are one.
John 10:31 The Jews therefore took up stones again so that they might stone him.
John 10:32 Jesus answered them, I showed you many good works from my Father. For which work of them do you stone me?
John 10:33 The Jews answered him, saying, We do not stone you concerning a good work, but concerning blasphemy, and because you, being a man, make yourself God.
John 10:34 Jesus answered them, Is it not written in your law, I said, You are gods?
John 10:35 If he called those gods to whom the word of God came, and the Scripture cannot be broken,
John 10:36 do you say to the one whom the Father sanctified and sent into the world, You blaspheme, because I said, I am Son of God?
John 10:37 If I do not do the works of my Father, do not believe me.
John 10:38 But if I do, even if you do not believe me, believe the works, so that you may know and believe that the Father is in me, and I in him.
John 10:39 They therefore were seeking again to seize him, and he went out from their hand.
John 10:40 And he went away again beyond the Jordan, to the place where John was first baptizing, and remained there.
John 10:41 And many came to him, and were saying that John indeed did no sign, but all things which John said concerning this man were true.
John 10:42 And many believed in him there.

## Chapter 11

John 11:1 And a certain man was sick, Lazarus from Bethany, from the village of Mary and Martha her sister.
John 11:2 And Mary was the one who anointed the Lord with ointment and wiped his feet with her hair, whose brother Lazarus was sick.
John 11:3 The sisters therefore sent to him, saying, Lord, see, the one whom you love is sick.
John 11:4 And Jesus, having heard, said, This sickness is not toward death, but for the glory of God, so that the Son of God may be glorified through it.
John 11:5 And Jesus loved Martha and her sister and Lazarus.
John 11:6 When therefore he heard that he is sick, then indeed he stayed two days in the place where he was.
John 11:7 Then after this he says to the disciples, Let us go into Judea again.
John 11:8 The disciples say to him, Rabbi, just now the Jews were seeking to stone you, and do you go there again?
John 11:9 Jesus answered, Are there not twelve hours of the day? If anyone walks in the day, he does not stumble, because he sees the light of this world.
John 11:10 But if anyone walks in the night, he stumbles, because the light is not in him.
John 11:11 He said these things, and after this says to them, Lazarus our friend has fallen asleep, but I go so that I may awaken him.
John 11:12 His disciples therefore said, Lord, if he has fallen asleep, he will be saved.
John 11:13 But Jesus had spoken concerning his death, while they supposed that he speaks concerning the resting of sleep.
John 11:14 Then therefore Jesus said to them openly, Lazarus died.
John 11:15 And I rejoice because of you, so that you may believe, that I was not there. But let us go to him.
John 11:16 Thomas therefore, the one called Twin, said to the fellow disciples, Let us also go, so that we may die with him.
John 11:17 Having therefore come, Jesus found him already having four days in the tomb.
John 11:18 And Bethany was near Jerusalem, about fifteen stadia away.
John 11:19 And many of the Jews had come to those around Martha and Mary, so that they might console them concerning their brother.
John 11:20 Martha therefore, when she heard that Jesus comes, met him, but Mary was sitting in the house.
John 11:21 Martha therefore said to Jesus, Lord, if you were here, my brother would not have died.
John 11:22 But even now I know that whatever you ask God, God will give you.
John 11:23 Jesus says to her, Your brother will rise.
John 11:24 Martha says to him, I know that he will rise in the resurrection on the last day.
John 11:25 Jesus said to her, I am the resurrection and the life. The one believing in me, even if he dies, will live.
John 11:26 And everyone living and believing in me will certainly not die forever. Do you believe this?
John 11:27 She says to him, Yes, Lord, I have believed that you are the Christ, the Son of God, the one coming into the world.
John 11:28 And having said these things, she went away and called Mary her sister secretly, saying, The Teacher is present and calls you.
John 11:29 When she heard, she rises quickly and comes to him.
John 11:30 And Jesus had not yet come into the village, but was in the place where Martha met him.
John 11:31 The Jews therefore who were with her in the house and consoling her, having seen Mary, that she rose quickly and went out, followed her, saying that she goes to the tomb so that she may weep there.
John 11:32 Mary therefore, when she came where Jesus was, having seen him, fell at his feet, saying to him, Lord, if you were here, my brother would not have died.
John 11:33 Jesus therefore, when he saw her weeping, and the Jews who came with her weeping, was indignant in spirit and troubled himself,
John 11:34 and said, Where have you placed him? They say to him, Lord, come and see.
John 11:35 Jesus shed tears.
John 11:36 The Jews therefore were saying, See how he loved him.
John 11:37 But some of them said, Could not this man who opened the eyes of the blind man have done so that this man too might not die?
John 11:38 Jesus therefore, again being indignant within himself, comes to the tomb. And it was a cave, and a stone lay upon it.
John 11:39 Jesus says, Take away the stone. Martha, the sister of the one who has died, says to him, Lord, he already smells, for he is four days dead.
John 11:40 Jesus says to her, Did I not say to you that if you believe, you will see the glory of God?
John 11:41 They therefore took away the stone where the one who had died was lying. And Jesus lifted his eyes upward and said, Father, I thank you that you heard me.
John 11:42 And I knew that you always hear me, but because of the crowd standing around I said it, so that they may believe that you sent me.
John 11:43 And having said these things, he cried out with a loud voice, Lazarus, come outside.
John 11:44 And the one who had died came out, bound as to feet and hands with bands, and his face had been bound around with a handkerchief. Jesus says to them, Unbind him and allow him to go.
John 11:45 Many therefore of the Jews who came to Mary and beheld what Jesus did believed in him.
John 11:46 But some of them went away to the Pharisees and told them what Jesus did.
John 11:47 The chief priests and the Pharisees therefore gathered a council, and were saying, What do we do, because this man does many signs?
John 11:48 If we allow him thus, all will believe in him, and the Romans will come and take away both our place and nation.
John 11:49 But a certain one of them, Caiaphas, being high priest that year, said to them, You know nothing,
John 11:50 nor do you consider that it benefits us that one man die for the people, and not the whole nation perish.
John 11:51 And he did not say this from himself, but being high priest that year, prophesied that Jesus was about to die for the nation,
John 11:52 and not for the nation only, but so that he might also gather into one the children of God who had been scattered.
John 11:53 From that day therefore they took counsel so that they might kill him.
