John 11:54 Jesus therefore was no longer walking openly among the Jews, but went away from there into the country near the wilderness, into a city called Ephraim, and there was spending time with his disciples.
John 11:55 And the Passover of the Jews was near, and many went up to Jerusalem from the country before the Passover, so that they might purify themselves.
John 11:56 They therefore were seeking Jesus, and were saying with each other, standing in the temple, What do you think, that he will certainly not come to the feast?
John 11:57 And both the chief priests and the Pharisees had given a commandment that if anyone knows where he is, he should disclose it, so that they might seize him.

## Chapter 12

John 12:1 Jesus therefore, six days before the Passover, came into Bethany, where Lazarus was, the one who had died, whom he raised from the dead.
John 12:2 They therefore made him a dinner there, and Martha was serving, and Lazarus was one of those reclining together with him.
John 12:3 Mary therefore, having taken a pound of ointment of genuine nard, very costly, anointed the feet of Jesus and wiped his feet with her hair. And the house was filled from the smell of the ointment.
John 12:4 One of his disciples therefore says, Judas Iscariot of Simon, the one about to hand him over,
John 12:5 Why was this ointment not sold for three hundred denarii and given to the poor?
John 12:6 And he said this not because he cared concerning the poor, but because he was a thief, and had the money box, and was carrying off the things put in.
John 12:7 Jesus therefore said, Allow her; she has kept it for the day of my burial.
John 12:8 For you always have the poor with yourselves, but you do not always have me.
John 12:9 A great crowd from the Jews therefore knew that he is there, and they came not because of Jesus only, but so that they might also see Lazarus, whom he raised from the dead.
John 12:10 But the chief priests took counsel so that they might kill Lazarus also,
John 12:11 because many of the Jews were going away because of him and believing in Jesus.
John 12:12 On the next day a great crowd that came to the feast, having heard that Jesus comes into Jerusalem,
John 12:13 took the branches of the palms and went out to meet him, and were crying out, Hosanna! Blessed is the one coming in the name of the Lord, the King of Israel.
John 12:14 And Jesus, having found a little donkey, sat upon it, just as it is written,
John 12:15 Do not fear, daughter of Zion; look, your King comes, sitting upon a donkey's colt.
John 12:16 But his disciples did not know these things at first; but when Jesus was glorified, then they remembered that these things had been written concerning him, and they did these things to him.
John 12:17 The crowd therefore that was with him when he called Lazarus from the tomb and raised him from the dead was testifying.
John 12:18 Because of this also the crowd met him, because it heard that he had done this sign.
John 12:19 The Pharisees therefore said among themselves, You behold that you benefit nothing. See, the world went away after him.
John 12:20 And there were some Greeks from those going up so that they might worship at the feast.
John 12:21 These therefore approached Philip, the one from Bethsaida of Galilee, and were asking him, saying, Sir, we wish to see Jesus.
John 12:22 Philip comes and tells Andrew, and again Andrew and Philip tell Jesus.
John 12:23 And Jesus answered them, saying, The hour has come so that the Son of Man may be glorified.
John 12:24 Amen, amen, I say to you, Unless the grain of wheat, having fallen into the earth, dies, it remains alone; but if it dies, it bears much fruit.
John 12:25 The one loving his life will lose it, and the one hating his life in this world will guard it into eternal life.
John 12:26 If anyone serves me, let him follow me, and where I am, there my servant also will be. And if anyone serves me, the Father will honor him.
John 12:27 Now my soul has been troubled, and what shall I say? Father, save me from this hour? But because of this I came into this hour.
John 12:28 Father, glorify your name. A voice therefore came from heaven, I both glorified it and will glorify it again.
John 12:29 The crowd therefore standing and having heard was saying that thunder had happened. Others were saying, An angel has spoken to him.
John 12:30 Jesus answered and said, This voice has come not because of me, but because of you.
John 12:31 Now is judgment of this world; now the ruler of this world will be cast outside.
John 12:32 And I, if I am lifted up from the earth, will draw all to myself.
John 12:33 And he was saying this signifying by what death he was about to die.
John 12:34 The crowd answered him, We heard from the law that the Christ remains forever, and how do you say that the Son of Man must be lifted up? Who is this Son of Man?
John 12:35 Jesus therefore said to them, The light is with you still a little time. Walk while you have the light, so that darkness may not overtake you; and the one walking in the darkness does not know where he goes.
John 12:36 While you have the light, believe in the light, so that you may become sons of light. Jesus spoke these things, and having gone away, was hidden from them.
John 12:37 But though he had done so many signs before them, they were not believing in him,
John 12:38 so that the word of Isaiah the prophet might be fulfilled which he said, Lord, who believed our report? And to whom was the arm of the Lord revealed?
John 12:39 Because of this they could not believe, because Isaiah said again,
John 12:40 He has blinded their eyes and has hardened their heart, so that they may not see with the eyes and understand with the heart and turn back, and I may heal them.
John 12:41 Isaiah said these things when he saw his glory and spoke concerning him.
John 12:42 Nevertheless, however, many even from the rulers believed in him, but because of the Pharisees they were not confessing, so that they might not become expelled from the synagogue.
John 12:43 For they loved the glory of people rather than the glory of God.
John 12:44 And Jesus cried out and said, The one believing in me does not believe in me, but in the one who sent me.
John 12:45 And the one beholding me beholds the one who sent me.
John 12:46 I have come as light into the world, so that everyone believing in me may not remain in the darkness.
John 12:47 And if anyone hears my sayings and does not believe, I do not judge him, for I did not come so that I might judge the world, but so that I might save the world.
John 12:48 The one rejecting me and not receiving my sayings has the one judging him. The word which I spoke, that will judge him on the last day.
John 12:49 Because I did not speak from myself, but the Father who sent me, he gave me a commandment, what I should say and what I should speak.
John 12:50 And I know that his commandment is eternal life. The things therefore which I speak, just as the Father has said to me, thus I speak.

## Chapter 13

John 13:1 And before the feast of the Passover, Jesus, knowing that his hour has come so that he may pass from this world to the Father, having loved his own who were in the world, loved them to the end.
John 13:2 And dinner having taken place, the devil having already put into the heart of Judas Iscariot of Simon that he should hand him over,
John 13:3 Jesus, knowing that the Father has given all things to him into his hands, and that he went out from God and goes to God,
John 13:4 rises from the dinner and lays down the garments, and having taken a towel, girded himself.
John 13:5 Then he puts water into the basin and began to wash the feet of the disciples and wipe them with the towel with which he was girded.
John 13:6 He comes therefore to Simon Peter, and he says to him, Lord, do you wash my feet?
John 13:7 Jesus answered and said to him, What I do you do not know now, but you will know after these things.
John 13:8 Peter says to him, You will certainly not wash my feet forever. Jesus answered him, Unless I wash you, you have no part with me.
John 13:9 Simon Peter says to him, Lord, not my feet only, but also the hands and the head.
John 13:10 Jesus says to him, The one who has bathed has no need except to wash the feet, but is wholly clean. And you are clean, but not all.
John 13:11 For he knew the one handing him over; because of this he said, You are not all clean.
John 13:12 When therefore he washed their feet and took his garments, having reclined again, he said to them, Do you know what I have done to you?
John 13:13 You call me the Teacher and the Lord, and you say well, for I am.
John 13:14 If therefore I, the Lord and the Teacher, washed your feet, you also owe to wash each other's feet.
John 13:15 For I gave you an example, so that just as I did to you, you also may do.
John 13:16 Amen, amen, I say to you, A slave is not greater than his master, nor a messenger greater than the one who sent him.
John 13:17 If you know these things, you are blessed if you do them.
John 13:18 I do not speak concerning all of you; I know whom I chose. But so that the Scripture may be fulfilled, The one chewing the bread with me lifted his heel against me.
John 13:19 From now I tell you before it happens, so that when it happens, you may believe that I am.
John 13:20 Amen, amen, I say to you, The one receiving whomever I may send receives me, and the one receiving me receives the one who sent me.
John 13:21 Having said these things, Jesus was troubled in spirit, and testified and said, Amen, amen, I say to you that one of you will hand me over.
John 13:22 The disciples therefore were looking at each other, being perplexed concerning whom he speaks.
John 13:23 And one of his disciples was reclining in the bosom of Jesus, whom Jesus loved.
John 13:24 Simon Peter therefore motions to this one to inquire who it might be concerning whom he speaks.
John 13:25 And he, having leaned upon the chest of Jesus, says to him, Lord, who is it?
John 13:26 Jesus answers, It is he to whom I, having dipped the morsel, will give it. And having dipped the morsel, he gives it to Judas Iscariot of Simon.
John 13:27 And after the morsel, then Satan entered into him. Jesus therefore says to him, What you do, do more quickly.
John 13:28 But no one of those reclining knew for what he said this to him.
John 13:29 For some were supposing, since Judas had the money box, that Jesus says to him, Buy the things of which we have need for the feast, or that he should give something to the poor.
John 13:30 Having therefore received the morsel, he immediately went out. And it was night.
John 13:31 When he went out, Jesus says, Now the Son of Man was glorified, and God was glorified in him.
John 13:32 If God was glorified in him, God also will glorify him in himself, and will glorify him immediately.
John 13:33 Little children, I am with you still a little while. You will seek me, and just as I said to the Jews, Where I go you cannot come, also to you I say it now.
John 13:34 I give you a new commandment, that you love each other, just as I loved you, that you also love each other.
John 13:35 In this all will know that you are my disciples, if you have love among each other.
John 13:36 Simon Peter says to him, Lord, where do you go? Jesus answered him, Where I go, you cannot follow me now, but later you will follow me.
John 13:37 Peter says to him, Lord, why can I not follow you now? I will lay down my life for you.
John 13:38 Jesus answered him, Will you lay down your life for me? Amen, amen, I say to you, A rooster will certainly not call until you deny me three times.

## Chapter 14

John 14:1 Let not your heart be troubled. Believe in God, and believe in me.
John 14:2 In my Father's house are many dwelling places. But if not, I would have told you. I go to prepare a place for you.
John 14:3 And if I go and prepare a place for you, I come again and will receive you to myself, so that where I am, you also may be.
John 14:4 And where I go you know, and the way you know.
John 14:5 Thomas says to him, Lord, we do not know where you go, and how can we know the way?
John 14:6 Jesus says to him, I am the way and the truth and the life. No one comes to the Father except through me.
John 14:7 If you had known me, you would also have known my Father. And from now you know him and have seen him.
John 14:8 Philip says to him, Lord, show us the Father, and it suffices for us.
John 14:9 Jesus says to him, I am with you so much time, and have you not known me, Philip? The one who has seen me has seen the Father, and how do you say, Show us the Father?
John 14:10 Do you not believe that I am in the Father and the Father is in me? The sayings which I speak to you I do not speak from myself, but the Father remaining in me, he does the works.
John 14:11 Believe me that I am in the Father and the Father in me; but if not, believe me because of the works themselves.
John 14:12 Amen, amen, I say to you, The one believing in me, that one too will do the works which I do, and will do greater things than these, because I go to my Father.
John 14:13 And whatever you ask in my name, this I will do, so that the Father may be glorified in the Son.
John 14:14 If you ask anything in my name, I will do it.
John 14:15 If you love me, keep my commandments.
John 14:16 And I will ask the Father, and he will give you another Advocate, so that he may remain with you forever,
John 14:17 the Spirit of truth, whom the world cannot receive, because it does not behold him nor know him. But you know him, because he remains with you and will be in you.
John 14:18 I will not leave you orphans; I come to you.
John 14:19 Still a little while, and the world no longer beholds me, but you behold me. Because I live, you also will live.
John 14:20 On that day you will know that I am in my Father, and you in me, and I in you.
John 14:21 The one having my commandments and keeping them, he is the one loving me. And the one loving me will be loved by my Father, and I will love him and manifest myself to him.
John 14:22 Judas, not the Iscariot, says to him, Lord, what has happened, that you are about to manifest yourself to us and not to the world?
John 14:23 Jesus answered and said to him, If anyone loves me, he will keep my word, and my Father will love him, and we will come to him and make a dwelling place with him.
John 14:24 The one not loving me does not keep my words, and the word which you hear is not mine, but of the Father who sent me.
John 14:25 I have spoken these things to you, remaining with you.
John 14:26 But the Advocate, the Holy Spirit, whom the Father will send in my name, he will teach you all things and remind you of all things which I said to you.
John 14:27 I leave peace to you; I give my peace to you. Not just as the world gives do I give to you. Let not your heart be troubled, nor let it be cowardly.
John 14:28 You heard that I said to you, I go away and come to you. If you loved me, you would have rejoiced because I said, I go to the Father, because my Father is greater than I.
John 14:29 And now I have told you before it happens, so that when it happens, you may believe.
John 14:30 I will no longer speak many things with you, for the ruler of this world comes, and has nothing in me.
John 14:31 But so that the world may know that I love the Father, and just as the Father commanded me, thus I do. Rise, let us go from here.

## Chapter 15

John 15:1 I am the true vine, and my Father is the farmer.
John 15:2 Every branch in me not bearing fruit, he takes it away, and every one bearing fruit, he cleans it, so that it may bear more fruit.
John 15:3 You are already clean because of the word which I have spoken to you.
John 15:4 Remain in me, and I in you. Just as the branch cannot bear fruit from itself unless it remains in the vine, thus neither can you unless you remain in me.
John 15:5 I am the vine; you the branches. The one remaining in me, and I in him, this one bears much fruit, because apart from me you can do nothing.
John 15:6 If anyone does not remain in me, he was cast outside as the branch and was withered, and they gather them and cast into fire, and it is burned.
John 15:7 If you remain in me and my sayings remain in you, whatever you wish you will ask, and it will happen for you.
John 15:8 In this my Father was glorified, that you bear much fruit, and you will become my disciples.
John 15:9 Just as the Father loved me, I also loved you. Remain in my love.
John 15:10 If you keep my commandments, you will remain in my love, just as I have kept my Father's commandments and remain in his love.
John 15:11 I have spoken these things to you so that my joy may remain in you and your joy may be fulfilled.
John 15:12 This is my commandment, that you love each other just as I loved you.
John 15:13 No one has greater love than this, that someone lay down his life for his friends.
John 15:14 You are my friends if you do whatever I command you.
John 15:15 I no longer call you slaves, because the slave does not know what his master does, but I have called you friends, because all things which I heard from my Father I made known to you.
John 15:16 You did not choose me, but I chose you and appointed you, so that you may go and bear fruit and your fruit may remain, so that whatever you ask the Father in my name, he may give you.
John 15:17 These things I command you, that you love each other.
John 15:18 If the world hates you, know that it has hated me before you.
John 15:19 If you were from the world, the world would love its own. But because you are not from the world, but I chose you out of the world, because of this the world hates you.
John 15:20 Remember the word which I said to you, A slave is not greater than his master. If they persecuted me, they will also persecute you; if they kept my word, they will also keep yours.
John 15:21 But they will do all these things to you because of my name, because they do not know the one who sent me.
John 15:22 If I had not come and spoken to them, they would not have sin. But now they have no excuse concerning their sin.
John 15:23 The one hating me also hates my Father.
John 15:24 If I had not done among them the works which no other has done, they would not have sin. But now they have both seen and hated both me and my Father.
John 15:25 But so that the word written in their law may be fulfilled, They hated me without cause.
John 15:26 But when the Advocate comes, whom I will send you from the Father, the Spirit of truth who proceeds from the Father, he will testify concerning me.
John 15:27 And you also testify, because you are with me from the beginning.

## Chapter 16

John 16:1 I have spoken these things to you so that you may not be caused to stumble.
John 16:2 They will make you expelled from the synagogue. But an hour comes so that everyone who kills you may suppose he offers worship to God.
John 16:3 And they will do these things to you because they did not know the Father nor me.
John 16:4 But I have spoken these things to you so that when the hour comes, you may remember them, that I told you. And I did not tell you these things from the beginning, because I was with you.
John 16:5 But now I go to the one who sent me, and none of you asks me, Where do you go?
John 16:6 But because I have spoken these things to you, sorrow has filled your heart.
John 16:7 But I say the truth to you, It benefits you that I go away. For unless I go away, the Advocate will not come to you; but if I go, I will send him to you.
John 16:8 And having come, he will convict the world concerning sin and concerning righteousness and concerning judgment:
John 16:9 concerning sin indeed, because they do not believe in me;
John 16:10 and concerning righteousness, because I go to my Father and you no longer behold me;
John 16:11 and concerning judgment, because the ruler of this world has been judged.
John 16:12 I still have many things to say to you, but you cannot bear them now.
John 16:13 But when he comes, the Spirit of truth, he will guide you into all the truth. For he will not speak from himself, but whatever he hears he will speak, and he will announce to you the coming things.
John 16:14 He will glorify me, because he will receive from what is mine and announce it to you.
John 16:15 All things which the Father has are mine. Because of this I said that he will receive from what is mine and announce it to you.
John 16:16 A little while, and you do not behold me, and again a little while, and you will see me, because I go to the Father.
John 16:17 Some of his disciples therefore said to each other, What is this which he says to us, A little while, and you do not behold me, and again a little while, and you will see me, and, Because I go to the Father?
John 16:18 They therefore were saying, What is this which he says, The little while? We do not know what he speaks.
John 16:19 Jesus therefore knew that they wished to ask him, and said to them, Do you inquire with each other concerning this, because I said, A little while, and you do not behold me, and again a little while, and you will see me?
John 16:20 Amen, amen, I say to you that you will weep and lament, but the world will rejoice. And you will be grieved, but your sorrow will become joy.
John 16:21 The woman, when she gives birth, has sorrow, because her hour came. But when she bears the child, she no longer remembers the affliction because of the joy that a person was born into the world.
John 16:22 And you therefore indeed have sorrow now, but I will see you again, and your heart will rejoice, and no one takes your joy from you.
John 16:23 And on that day you will ask me nothing. Amen, amen, I say to you that whatever you ask the Father in my name, he will give you.
John 16:24 Until now you asked nothing in my name. Ask, and you will receive, so that your joy may be fulfilled.
John 16:25 I have spoken these things to you in figures, but an hour comes when I will no longer speak to you in figures, but will announce to you openly concerning the Father.
John 16:26 On that day you will ask in my name, and I do not say to you that I will ask the Father concerning you.
John 16:27 For the Father himself loves you, because you have loved me and have believed that I went out from God.
John 16:28 I went out from the Father and have come into the world. Again I leave the world and go to the Father.
John 16:29 His disciples say to him, See, now you speak openly and say no figure.
John 16:30 Now we know that you know all things and have no need that anyone ask you. In this we believe that you went out from God.
John 16:31 Jesus answered them, Do you believe now?
John 16:32 Look, an hour comes, and has now come, so that you may be scattered, each to his own things, and leave me alone. And I am not alone, because the Father is with me.
John 16:33 I have spoken these things to you so that in me you may have peace. In the world you have affliction, but take courage; I have conquered the world.

## Chapter 17

John 17:1 Jesus spoke these things, and lifted his eyes to heaven and said, Father, the hour has come. Glorify your Son, so that your Son also may glorify you,
John 17:2 just as you gave him authority over all flesh, so that everything which you have given him, he may give them eternal life.
John 17:3 And this is eternal life, that they know you, the only true God, and the one whom you sent, Jesus Christ.
John 17:4 I glorified you upon the earth; I completed the work which you have given me so that I may do it.
John 17:5 And now you, Father, glorify me with yourself, with the glory which I had with you before the world was.
John 17:6 I manifested your name to the people whom you have given me from the world. They were yours, and you have given them to me, and they have kept your word.
John 17:7 Now they have known that all things which you have given me are from you.
John 17:8 Because the sayings which you have given me I have given them, and they received and truly knew that I went out from you, and believed that you sent me.
John 17:9 I ask concerning them. I do not ask concerning the world, but concerning those whom you have given me, because they are yours.
John 17:10 And all my things are yours, and your things mine, and I have been glorified in them.
John 17:11 And I am no longer in the world, and these are in the world, and I come to you. Holy Father, keep them in your name, those whom you have given me, so that they may be one just as we.
John 17:12 When I was with them in the world, I was keeping them in your name. Those whom you have given me I guarded, and none of them perished except the son of destruction, so that the Scripture may be fulfilled.
John 17:13 But now I come to you, and speak these things in the world, so that they may have my joy fulfilled in themselves.
John 17:14 I have given them your word, and the world hated them because they are not from the world, just as I am not from the world.
John 17:15 I do not ask that you take them out of the world, but that you keep them from the evil one.
John 17:16 They are not from the world, just as I am not from the world.
John 17:17 Sanctify them in your truth; your word is truth.
John 17:18 Just as you sent me into the world, I also sent them into the world.
John 17:19 And for them I sanctify myself, so that they also may be sanctified in truth.
John 17:20 And I ask not concerning these only, but also concerning those who will believe in me through their word,
John 17:21 so that all may be one, just as you, Father, in me, and I in you, so that they also may be one in us, so that the world may believe that you sent me.
John 17:22 And I have given them the glory which you have given me, so that they may be one just as we are one.
John 17:23 I in them, and you in me, so that they may be perfected into one, and so that the world may know that you sent me and loved them just as you loved me.
John 17:24 Father, those whom you have given me, I wish that where I am, they too may be with me, so that they may behold my glory which you gave me, because you loved me before the foundation of the world.
John 17:25 Righteous Father, even the world did not know you, but I knew you, and these knew that you sent me.
John 17:26 And I made known to them your name, and will make it known, so that the love with which you loved me may be in them, and I in them.

## Chapter 18

John 18:1 Having said these things, Jesus went out with his disciples beyond the winter torrent of Kedron, where there was a garden, into which he entered and his disciples.
John 18:2 And Judas also, the one handing him over, knew the place, because Jesus often gathered there with his disciples.
John 18:3 Judas therefore, having received the cohort and officers from the chief priests and Pharisees, comes there with lanterns and torches and weapons.
John 18:4 Jesus therefore, knowing all things coming upon him, having gone out, said to them, Whom do you seek?
John 18:5 They answered him, Jesus the Nazarene. Jesus says to them, I am. And Judas also, the one handing him over, stood with them.
John 18:6 When therefore he said to them, I am, they went backward and fell to the ground.
John 18:7 Again therefore he asked them, Whom do you seek? And they said, Jesus the Nazarene.
John 18:8 Jesus answered, I told you that I am. If therefore you seek me, allow these to go,
John 18:9 so that the word which he said might be fulfilled, Those whom you have given me, I lost none of them.
John 18:10 Simon Peter therefore, having a sword, drew it and struck the slave of the high priest, and cut off his right ear. And the slave's name was Malchus.
John 18:11 Jesus therefore said to Peter, Put your sword into the sheath. The cup which the Father has given me, shall I not drink it?
John 18:12 The cohort therefore, and the commander of a thousand and the officers of the Jews, seized Jesus and bound him,
John 18:13 and led him away to Annas first, for he was father-in-law of Caiaphas, who was high priest that year.
John 18:14 And Caiaphas was the one who advised the Jews that it benefits them that one man perish for the people.
John 18:15 And Simon Peter was following Jesus, and the other disciple. And that disciple was known to the high priest, and entered together with Jesus into the courtyard of the high priest.
John 18:16 But Peter stood at the door outside. The other disciple therefore, who was known to the high priest, went out and spoke to the doorkeeper, and brought Peter in.
John 18:17 The servant girl, the doorkeeper, therefore says to Peter, You too are not from the disciples of this man, are you? He says, I am not.
John 18:18 And the slaves and the officers stood, having made a charcoal fire, because it was cold, and were warming themselves. And Peter was with them, standing and warming himself.
John 18:19 The high priest therefore asked Jesus concerning his disciples and concerning his teaching.
John 18:20 Jesus answered him, I spoke openly to the world. I always taught in the synagogue and in the temple, where the Jews always gather, and in secret I spoke nothing.
John 18:21 Why do you question me? Question those who have heard what I spoke to them. See, these know what I said.
John 18:22 And as he said these things, one of the officers standing by gave Jesus a slap, saying, Do you answer the high priest thus?
John 18:23 Jesus answered him, If I spoke badly, testify concerning the bad; but if well, why do you beat me?
John 18:24 Annas sent him bound to Caiaphas the high priest.
John 18:25 And Simon Peter was standing and warming himself. They therefore said to him, You too are not from his disciples, are you? He denied and said, I am not.
John 18:26 One of the slaves of the high priest says, being a relative of the one whose ear Peter cut off, Did I not see you in the garden with him?
John 18:27 Peter therefore denied again, and immediately a rooster called.
John 18:28 They therefore lead Jesus from Caiaphas into the praetorium. And it was early morning, and they themselves did not enter into the praetorium, so that they might not be defiled, but so that they might eat the Passover.
John 18:29 Pilate therefore went out to them and said, What accusation do you bring against this man?
John 18:30 They answered and said to him, If this man were not an evildoer, we would not have handed him over to you.
John 18:31 Pilate therefore said to them, You take him, and judge him according to your law. The Jews therefore said to him, It is not lawful for us to kill anyone,
John 18:32 so that the word of Jesus might be fulfilled which he said, signifying by what death he was about to die.
John 18:33 Pilate therefore entered into the praetorium again and called Jesus, and said to him, Are you the King of the Jews?
John 18:34 Jesus answered him, Do you say this from yourself, or did others tell you concerning me?
John 18:35 Pilate answered, I am not a Jew, am I? Your nation and the chief priests handed you over to me. What did you do?
John 18:36 Jesus answered, My kingdom is not from this world. If my kingdom were from this world, my officers would be fighting so that I might not be handed over to the Jews. But now my kingdom is not from here.
John 18:37 Pilate therefore said to him, Therefore are you a king? Jesus answered, You say that I am a king. For this I have been born, and for this I have come into the world, so that I may testify to the truth. Everyone being from the truth hears my voice.
John 18:38 Pilate says to him, What is truth? And having said this, he went out again to the Jews and says to them, I find no fault in him.
John 18:39 And you have a custom that I release one to you at the Passover. Do you therefore wish that I release to you the King of the Jews?
John 18:40 All therefore cried out again, saying, Not this man, but Barabbas. And Barabbas was a robber.

## Chapter 19

John 19:1 Then therefore Pilate took Jesus and scourged him.
John 19:2 And the soldiers, having woven a crown from thorns, placed it upon his head, and clothed him in a purple garment.
John 19:3 And they were saying, Hail, King of the Jews, and were giving him slaps.
John 19:4 Pilate therefore went outside again and says to them, See, I bring him outside to you, so that you may know that I find no fault in him.
John 19:5 Jesus therefore went outside, wearing the thorny crown and the purple garment. And he says to them, See, the man.
John 19:6 When therefore the chief priests and the officers saw him, they cried out, saying, Crucify, crucify. Pilate says to them, You take him and crucify, for I do not find fault in him.
John 19:7 The Jews answered him, We have a law, and according to our law he owes to die, because he made himself Son of God.
John 19:8 When therefore Pilate heard this word, he feared more,
John 19:9 and entered into the praetorium again and says to Jesus, From where are you? But Jesus gave him no answer.
John 19:10 Pilate therefore says to him, Do you not speak to me? Do you not know that I have authority to crucify you, and have authority to release you?
John 19:11 Jesus answered, You would have no authority against me unless it had been given you from above. Because of this the one handing me over to you has greater sin.
John 19:12 From this Pilate was seeking to release him, but the Jews were crying out, saying, If you release this man, you are not Caesar's friend. Everyone making himself king speaks against Caesar.
John 19:13 Pilate therefore, having heard this word, brought Jesus outside, and sat upon the judgment seat, at a place called Stone-paved, but in Hebrew Gabbatha.
John 19:14 And it was Preparation of the Passover, and about the sixth hour. And he says to the Jews, See, your King.
John 19:15 But they cried out, Take away, take away, crucify him. Pilate says to them, Shall I crucify your King? The chief priests answered, We have no king except Caesar.
John 19:16 Then therefore he handed him over to them so that he might be crucified. And they received Jesus and led him away.
John 19:17 And carrying his cross, he went out to the place called Place of a Skull, which is called in Hebrew Golgotha,
John 19:18 where they crucified him, and with him two others, on this side and on that side, and Jesus in the middle.
John 19:19 And Pilate also wrote a title and placed it upon the cross. And it was written, Jesus the Nazarene, the King of the Jews.
John 19:20 Many of the Jews therefore read this title, because the place where Jesus was crucified was near the city, and it was written in Hebrew, Greek, Roman.
John 19:21 The chief priests of the Jews therefore were saying to Pilate, Do not write, The King of the Jews, but that he said, I am King of the Jews.
John 19:22 Pilate answered, What I have written, I have written.
John 19:23 The soldiers therefore, when they crucified Jesus, took his garments and made four parts, to each soldier a part, and the tunic. And the tunic was seamless, woven from the top throughout.
John 19:24 They therefore said to each other, Let us not tear it, but cast lots concerning it, whose it will be, so that the Scripture may be fulfilled which says, They divided my garments among themselves, and upon my clothing they cast a lot. The soldiers therefore indeed did these things.
John 19:25 And by the cross of Jesus stood his mother, and his mother's sister, Mary of Clopas, and Mary Magdalene.
John 19:26 Jesus therefore, having seen the mother and the disciple standing by whom he loved, says to his mother, Woman, look, your son.
John 19:27 Then he says to the disciple, Look, your mother. And from that hour the disciple received her into his own things.
John 19:28 After this, Jesus, knowing that all things have already been completed, so that the Scripture may be completed, says, I thirst.
John 19:29 A vessel therefore lay full of vinegar, and they, having filled a sponge with vinegar and having put it around hyssop, brought it to his mouth.
John 19:30 When therefore Jesus received the vinegar, he said, It has been completed. And having bowed the head, he handed over the spirit.
John 19:31 The Jews therefore, so that the bodies might not remain upon the cross on the Sabbath, since it was Preparation, for the day of that Sabbath was great, asked Pilate that their legs be broken and they be taken away.
John 19:32 The soldiers therefore came and broke the legs of the first and of the other crucified with him.
John 19:33 But having come to Jesus, when they saw him already dead, they did not break his legs.
John 19:34 But one of the soldiers pierced his side with a spear, and immediately blood and water came out.
John 19:35 And the one who has seen has testified, and his testimony is true, and he knows that he says true things, so that you may believe.
John 19:36 For these things happened so that the Scripture may be fulfilled, A bone of him will not be broken.
John 19:37 And again another Scripture says, They will look upon the one whom they pierced.
John 19:38 And after these things Joseph from Arimathea, being a disciple of Jesus, but hidden because of the fear of the Jews, asked Pilate that he might take away the body of Jesus, and Pilate permitted. He therefore came and took away the body of Jesus.
John 19:39 And Nicodemus also came, the one who came to Jesus by night at first, carrying a mixture of myrrh and aloe, about a hundred pounds.
John 19:40 They therefore took the body of Jesus and bound it in linen cloths with the spices, just as it is a custom for the Jews to bury.
John 19:41 And in the place where he was crucified there was a garden, and in the garden a new tomb, in which no one had yet been placed.
John 19:42 There therefore, because of the Preparation of the Jews, because the tomb was near, they placed Jesus.

## Chapter 20

John 20:1 And on the first day of the week Mary Magdalene comes early, darkness still being, to the tomb, and sees the stone taken away from the tomb.
John 20:2 She therefore runs and comes to Simon Peter and to the other disciple whom Jesus loved, and says to them, They took the Lord away from the tomb, and we do not know where they placed him.
John 20:3 Peter therefore went out, and the other disciple, and they were coming to the tomb.
John 20:4 And the two were running together, and the other disciple ran ahead more quickly than Peter and came first to the tomb.
John 20:5 And having stooped to look, he sees the linen cloths lying; nevertheless he did not enter.
John 20:6 Simon Peter therefore comes, following him, and entered into the tomb, and beholds the linen cloths lying,
John 20:7 and the handkerchief which was upon his head, not lying with the linen cloths, but apart, wrapped up in one place.
John 20:8 Then therefore the other disciple also entered, the one who came first to the tomb, and saw and believed.
John 20:9 For they did not yet know the Scripture, that he must rise from the dead.
John 20:10 The disciples therefore went away again to themselves.
John 20:11 But Mary stood at the tomb, weeping outside. As therefore she was weeping, she stooped to look into the tomb,
John 20:12 and beholds two angels in white sitting, one toward the head and one toward the feet, where the body of Jesus was lying.
John 20:13 And they say to her, Woman, why do you weep? She says to them, Because they took away my Lord, and I do not know where they placed him.
John 20:14 And having said these things, she turned backward and beholds Jesus standing, and did not know that it is Jesus.
John 20:15 Jesus says to her, Woman, why do you weep? Whom do you seek? She, supposing that he is the gardener, says to him, Sir, if you carried him away, tell me where you placed him, and I will take him away.
John 20:16 Jesus says to her, Mary. She, having turned, says to him, Rabbouni, which is said, Teacher.
John 20:17 Jesus says to her, Do not touch me, for I have not yet ascended to my Father. But go to my brothers and tell them, I ascend to my Father and your Father, and my God and your God.
John 20:18 Mary Magdalene comes, reporting to the disciples that she has seen the Lord, and he said these things to her.
John 20:19 Evening therefore being on that day, the first of the week, and the doors having been shut where the disciples were gathered because of the fear of the Jews, Jesus came and stood in the midst and says to them, Peace to you.
John 20:20 And having said this, he showed them his hands and his side. The disciples therefore rejoiced, having seen the Lord.
John 20:21 Jesus therefore said to them again, Peace to you. Just as the Father has sent me, I also send you.
John 20:22 And having said this, he breathed upon them and says to them, Receive Holy Spirit.
John 20:23 If you forgive the sins of any, they are forgiven them; if you retain those of any, they have been retained.
John 20:24 But Thomas, one of the twelve, the one called Twin, was not with them when Jesus came.
John 20:25 The other disciples therefore were saying to him, We have seen the Lord. But he said to them, Unless I see in his hands the mark of the nails, and put my finger into the mark of the nails, and put my hand into his side, I will certainly not believe.
John 20:26 And after eight days his disciples were inside again, and Thomas with them. Jesus comes, the doors having been shut, and stood in the midst and said, Peace to you.
John 20:27 Then he says to Thomas, Bring your finger here and see my hands, and bring your hand and put it into my side, and do not become unbelieving, but believing.
John 20:28 And Thomas answered and said to him, My Lord and my God.
John 20:29 Jesus says to him, Because you have seen me, Thomas, you have believed. Blessed are those who did not see and believed.
John 20:30 Many therefore indeed other signs also Jesus did before his disciples, which are not written in this book.
John 20:31 But these have been written so that you may believe that Jesus is the Christ, the Son of God, and so that believing you may have life in his name.

## Chapter 21

John 21:1 After these things Jesus manifested himself again to the disciples at the sea of Tiberias, and manifested himself thus.
John 21:2 Simon Peter and Thomas the one called Twin, and Nathanael from Cana of Galilee, and those of Zebedee, and two others of his disciples were together.
John 21:3 Simon Peter says to them, I go to fish. They say to him, We too come with you. They went out and immediately went up into the boat, and on that night caught nothing.
John 21:4 And early morning having already come, Jesus stood on the shore; nevertheless the disciples did not know that it is Jesus.
John 21:5 Jesus therefore says to them, Children, you do not have any food to eat with bread, do you? They answered him, No.
John 21:6 And he said to them, Cast the net into the right parts of the boat, and you will find. They therefore cast, and were no longer strong enough to draw it because of the multitude of the fish.
John 21:7 That disciple therefore whom Jesus loved says to Peter, It is the Lord. Simon Peter therefore, having heard that it is the Lord, girded on the outer garment, for he was naked, and cast himself into the sea.
John 21:8 And the other disciples came by the little boat, for they were not far from the land, but about two hundred cubits away, dragging the net of the fish.
John 21:9 When therefore they stepped off onto the land, they see a charcoal fire lying, and a small fish lying upon it, and bread.
John 21:10 Jesus says to them, Bring from the small fish which you caught now.
John 21:11 Simon Peter went up and drew the net upon the land, full of large fish, one hundred fifty-three; and though there were so many, the net was not torn.
John 21:12 Jesus says to them, Come, breakfast. And none of the disciples dared to question him, Who are you? knowing that it is the Lord.
John 21:13 Jesus therefore comes and takes the bread and gives to them, and the small fish likewise.
John 21:14 This was already the third time Jesus was manifested to his disciples, having been raised from the dead.
John 21:15 When therefore they breakfasted, Jesus says to Simon Peter, Simon of Jonah, do you love me more than these? He says to him, Yes, Lord, you know that I love you. He says to him, Feed my lambs.
John 21:16 He says to him again a second time, Simon of Jonah, do you love me? He says to him, Yes, Lord, you know that I love you. He says to him, Shepherd my sheep.
John 21:17 He says to him the third time, Simon of Jonah, do you love me? Peter was grieved because he said to him the third time, Do you love me? And he said to him, Lord, you know all things; you know that I love you. Jesus says to him, Feed my sheep.
John 21:18 Amen, amen, I say to you, When you were younger, you were girding yourself and walking where you wished. But when you grow old, you will stretch out your hands, and another will gird you and carry you where you do not wish.
John 21:19 And he said this signifying by what death he will glorify God. And having said this, he says to him, Follow me.
John 21:20 And Peter, having turned back, sees the disciple whom Jesus loved following, who also reclined at the dinner upon his chest and said, Lord, who is the one handing you over?
John 21:21 Peter, having seen this man, says to Jesus, Lord, and this man, what?
John 21:22 Jesus says to him, If I wish him to remain until I come, what is it to you? You follow me.
John 21:23 This word therefore went out among the brothers, that that disciple does not die. And Jesus did not say to him that he does not die, but, If I wish him to remain until I come, what is it to you?
John 21:24 This is the disciple testifying concerning these things and having written these things, and we know that his testimony is true.
John 21:25 And there are also many other things which Jesus did, which, if they are written one by one, I suppose not even the world itself to contain the books being written. Amen.

# The Acts

The Apostolic Bible. Public domain. https://apostolic-bible.ysys9.chatgpt.site/license.html


## Chapter 1

The Acts 1:1 The first account indeed I made concerning all things, O Theophilus, which Jesus began both to do and to teach,
The Acts 1:2 until the day on which, having commanded through Holy Spirit the apostles whom he chose, he was taken up.
The Acts 1:3 To them also he presented himself alive after he suffered, with many proofs, appearing to them through forty days and speaking the things concerning the kingdom of God.
The Acts 1:4 And assembling together, he commanded them not to depart from Jerusalem, but to await the promise of the Father, which you heard from me.
The Acts 1:5 Because John indeed baptized with water, but you will be baptized in Holy Spirit not after many of these days.
The Acts 1:6 Those therefore who came together were asking him, saying, Lord, do you at this time restore the kingdom to Israel?
The Acts 1:7 And he said to them, It is not yours to know times or seasons which the Father set in his own authority.
The Acts 1:8 But you will receive power when the Holy Spirit has come upon you, and you will be witnesses to me both in Jerusalem and in all Judea and Samaria and as far as the end of the earth.
The Acts 1:9 And having said these things, while they were looking, he was lifted up, and a cloud received him from their eyes.
The Acts 1:10 And as they were looking intently into heaven while he was going, look, two men stood by them in white clothing,
The Acts 1:11 who also said, Men of Galilee, why do you stand looking into heaven? This Jesus, who was taken up from you into heaven, will come thus, in the manner you beheld him going into heaven.
The Acts 1:12 Then they returned to Jerusalem from the mountain called Olivet, which is near Jerusalem, having a Sabbath's journey.
The Acts 1:13 And when they entered, they went up into the upper room where they were staying, both Peter and James and John and Andrew, Philip and Thomas, Bartholomew and Matthew, James of Alphaeus and Simon the Zealot and Judas of James.
The Acts 1:14 All these were persevering with one accord in prayer and supplication, with women and Mary the mother of Jesus, and with his brothers.
The Acts 1:15 And in these days Peter, having risen in the midst of the disciples, said, and the crowd of names together was about a hundred twenty,
The Acts 1:16 Men, brothers, this Scripture had to be fulfilled, which the Holy Spirit spoke beforehand through David's mouth concerning Judas, who became a guide to those who seized Jesus.
The Acts 1:17 Because he had been numbered with us and obtained the lot of this service.
The Acts 1:18 This man therefore indeed acquired a field from the wages of unrighteousness, and having become headlong, burst open in the middle, and all his inward parts were poured out.
The Acts 1:19 And it became known to all those dwelling in Jerusalem, so that that field was called in their own dialect Akeldama, that is, Field of Blood.
The Acts 1:20 For it is written in the book of Psalms, Let his dwelling become desolate, and let there be no one dwelling in it, and, Let another take his oversight.
The Acts 1:21 It is necessary therefore, of the men who came together with us during all the time in which the Lord Jesus entered and went out among us,
The Acts 1:22 having begun from John's baptism until the day on which he was taken up from us, that one of these become with us a witness of his resurrection.
The Acts 1:23 And they put forward two, Joseph called Barsabas, who was surnamed Justus, and Matthias.
The Acts 1:24 And having prayed, they said, You, Lord, knower of the hearts of all, show one of these two whom you chose,
The Acts 1:25 to receive the lot of this service and apostleship, from which Judas turned aside to go to his own place.
The Acts 1:26 And they gave their lots, and the lot fell upon Matthias, and he was counted together with the eleven apostles.

## Chapter 2

The Acts 2:1 And when the day of Pentecost was being fulfilled, they were all with one accord together.
The Acts 2:2 And suddenly there came from heaven a sound as of a violent breath being borne along, and it filled the whole house where they were sitting.
The Acts 2:3 And tongues dividing apart, as of fire, appeared to them, and it sat upon each one of them.
The Acts 2:4 And all were filled with Holy Spirit and began to speak in other tongues, just as the Spirit was giving them to utter.
The Acts 2:5 And there were Jews dwelling in Jerusalem, devout men from every nation under heaven.
The Acts 2:6 And when this sound occurred, the multitude came together and was confounded, because each one was hearing them speaking in his own dialect.
The Acts 2:7 And all were astonished and marveling, saying to each other, Look, are not all these who speak Galileans?
The Acts 2:8 And how do we hear, each in our own dialect in which we were born?
The Acts 2:9 Parthians and Medes and Elamites, and those dwelling in Mesopotamia, both Judea and Cappadocia, Pontus and Asia,
The Acts 2:10 both Phrygia and Pamphylia, Egypt and the parts of Libya toward Cyrene, and visiting Romans, both Jews and proselytes,
The Acts 2:11 Cretans and Arabs, we hear them speaking in our tongues the great things of God.
The Acts 2:12 And all were astonished and greatly perplexed, saying one to another, What might this wish to be?
The Acts 2:13 But others, mocking, were saying that they are filled with sweet wine.
The Acts 2:14 But Peter, having stood with the eleven, raised his voice and uttered to them, Jewish men, and all those dwelling in Jerusalem, let this be known to you, and give ear to my sayings.
The Acts 2:15 For these are not drunk as you suppose, for it is the third hour of the day.
The Acts 2:16 But this is what was said through the prophet Joel:
The Acts 2:17 And it will be in the last days, God says, I will pour out from my Spirit upon all flesh, and your sons and your daughters will prophesy, and your young men will see visions, and your elders will dream dreams.
The Acts 2:18 And indeed upon my male slaves and upon my female slaves in those days I will pour out from my Spirit, and they will prophesy.
The Acts 2:19 And I will give wonders in heaven above and signs upon the earth below, blood and fire and vapor of smoke.
The Acts 2:20 The sun will be turned into darkness and the moon into blood before the great and manifest day of the Lord comes.
The Acts 2:21 And it will be that everyone who calls upon the name of the Lord will be saved.
The Acts 2:22 Israelite men, hear these words: Jesus the Nazarene, a man demonstrated to you by God with mighty works and wonders and signs which God did through him in your midst, just as you yourselves also know,
The Acts 2:23 this man, delivered up by the determined counsel and foreknowledge of God, having taken, having fastened through the hands of lawless ones, you killed.
The Acts 2:24 Whom God raised, having loosed the birth pains of death, because it was not possible for him to be held by it.
The Acts 2:25 For David says concerning him, I was seeing the Lord before me continually, because he is at my right, so that I may not be shaken.
The Acts 2:26 Because of this my heart was gladdened and my tongue exulted, and furthermore my flesh also will dwell in hope,
The Acts 2:27 because you will not abandon my soul to Hades, nor give your holy one to see corruption.
The Acts 2:28 You made known to me ways of life; you will fill me with gladness with your face.
The Acts 2:29 Men, brothers, it is permitted to speak to you with openness concerning the patriarch David, that he both died and was buried, and his tomb is among us until this day.
The Acts 2:30 Being therefore a prophet, and knowing that God swore to him with an oath to raise the Christ according to flesh from the fruit of his loins to sit upon his throne,
The Acts 2:31 having seen beforehand, he spoke concerning the resurrection of the Christ, that his soul was not left to Hades, nor did his flesh see corruption.
The Acts 2:32 This Jesus God raised, of whom we all are witnesses.
The Acts 2:33 Having therefore been exalted by the right hand of God, and having received the promise of the Holy Spirit from the Father, he poured out this which you now see and hear.
The Acts 2:34 For David did not ascend into the heavens, but he himself says, The Lord said to my Lord, Sit at my right,
The Acts 2:35 until I place your enemies as a footstool of your feet.
The Acts 2:36 Let all the house of Israel therefore know assuredly that God made him both Lord and Christ, this Jesus whom you crucified.
The Acts 2:37 And having heard, they were pierced in the heart, and said to Peter and the remaining apostles, What shall we do, men, brothers?
The Acts 2:38 And Peter said to them, Repent, and let each of you be baptized upon the name of Jesus Christ for forgiveness of sins, and you will receive the gift of the Holy Spirit.
The Acts 2:39 For the promise is to you and to your children and to all those far away, as many as the Lord our God calls to himself.
The Acts 2:40 And with many other words he was solemnly testifying and exhorting, saying, Be saved from this crooked generation.
The Acts 2:41 Those therefore indeed who gladly received his word were baptized, and on that day about three thousand souls were added.
The Acts 2:42 And they were persevering in the teaching of the apostles and in fellowship and in the breaking of bread and in prayers.
The Acts 2:43 And fear came to every soul, and many wonders and signs were occurring through the apostles.
The Acts 2:44 And all those believing were together and had all things common.
The Acts 2:45 And they were selling their properties and possessions and dividing them to all, according as anyone had need.
The Acts 2:46 And daily persevering with one accord in the temple, and breaking bread house by house, they were partaking of food in exultation and simplicity of heart,
The Acts 2:47 praising God and having favor toward all the people. And the Lord was adding daily to the church those being saved.

## Chapter 3

The Acts 3:1 And Peter and John together were going up into the temple at the hour of prayer, the ninth.
The Acts 3:2 And a certain man, being lame from his mother's womb, was being carried, whom they placed daily at the door of the temple called Beautiful, to ask alms from those entering into the temple.
The Acts 3:3 Who, having seen Peter and John about to enter into the temple, was asking to receive alms.
The Acts 3:4 And Peter, having looked intently at him with John, said, Look at us.
The Acts 3:5 And he was attending to them, expecting to receive something from them.
The Acts 3:6 But Peter said, Silver and gold do not belong to me, but what I have, this I give you. In the name of Jesus Christ the Nazarene, rise and walk.
The Acts 3:7 And having seized him by the right hand, he raised him, and immediately his feet and ankles were strengthened.
The Acts 3:8 And leaping up, he stood and was walking, and entered with them into the temple, walking and leaping and praising God.
The Acts 3:9 And all the people saw him walking and praising God.
The Acts 3:10 And they recognized him, that this was the one sitting for alms at the Beautiful Gate of the temple, and they were filled with amazement and astonishment at what had happened to him.
The Acts 3:11 And as the healed lame man was holding Peter and John, all the people ran together to them at the portico called Solomon's, greatly amazed.
The Acts 3:12 And Peter, having seen, answered the people, Israelite men, why do you marvel at this, or why do you look intently at us as though by our own power or piety we have made him walk?
The Acts 3:13 The God of Abraham and Isaac and Jacob, the God of our fathers, glorified his servant Jesus, whom you handed over and denied before Pilate's face, when he had decided to release him.
The Acts 3:14 But you denied the Holy and Righteous One, and asked that a man, a murderer, be granted to you.
The Acts 3:15 And you killed the author of life, whom God raised from the dead, of whom we are witnesses.
The Acts 3:16 And upon faith in his name, his name strengthened this man whom you behold and know, and the faith through him gave him this wholeness before all of you.
The Acts 3:17 And now, brothers, I know that you acted according to ignorance, just as also your rulers.
The Acts 3:18 But God thus fulfilled the things which he announced beforehand through the mouth of all his prophets, that the Christ should suffer.
The Acts 3:19 Repent therefore and turn back, for your sins to be wiped away, so that seasons of refreshing may come from the face of the Lord,
The Acts 3:20 and he may send Jesus Christ, who was proclaimed beforehand to you,
The Acts 3:21 whom heaven indeed must receive until times of restoration of all things which God spoke through the mouth of all his holy prophets from the age.
The Acts 3:22 For Moses indeed said to the fathers that the Lord your God will raise for you a prophet from your brothers as me; you shall hear him according to all things which he may speak to you.
The Acts 3:23 And it will be that every soul who does not hear that prophet will be utterly destroyed from the people.
The Acts 3:24 And all the prophets also from Samuel and those in succession, as many as spoke, also announced these days beforehand.
The Acts 3:25 You are sons of the prophets and of the covenant which God covenanted with our fathers, saying to Abraham, And in your seed all the families of the earth will be blessed.
The Acts 3:26 To you first God, having raised his servant Jesus, sent him blessing you in turning each from your wickednesses.

## Chapter 4

The Acts 4:1 And as they were speaking to the people, the priests and the captain of the temple and the Sadducees came upon them,
The Acts 4:2 being greatly troubled because they teach the people and proclaim in Jesus the resurrection from the dead.
The Acts 4:3 And they laid hands upon them and put them into custody until the next day, for it was already evening.
The Acts 4:4 But many of those who heard the word believed, and the number of the men became about five thousand.
The Acts 4:5 And it happened on the next day that their rulers and elders and scribes were gathered
The Acts 4:6 in Jerusalem, and Annas the high priest and Caiaphas and John and Alexander, and as many as were from high-priestly kin.
The Acts 4:7 And having stood them in the midst, they were inquiring, In what power or in what name did you do this?
The Acts 4:8 Then Peter, having been filled with Holy Spirit, said to them, Rulers of the people and elders of Israel,
The Acts 4:9 if we are examined today concerning a good deed to a sick person, by what this man has been saved,
The Acts 4:10 let it be known to all of you and to all the people of Israel that in the name of Jesus Christ the Nazarene, whom you crucified, whom God raised from the dead, in him this man stands before you healthy.
The Acts 4:11 This is the stone despised by you, the builders, which became the head of the corner.
The Acts 4:12 And salvation is in no other, for neither is there another name under heaven given among people in which we must be saved.
The Acts 4:13 And beholding the openness of Peter and John, and having perceived that they are unlettered people and ordinary men, they were marveling, and recognizing them, that they were with Jesus.
The Acts 4:14 And seeing the man who had been healed standing with them, they had nothing to contradict.
The Acts 4:15 And having commanded them to go outside the council, they conferred with each other,
The Acts 4:16 saying, What shall we do to these people? For indeed that a known sign has occurred through them is manifest to all those dwelling in Jerusalem, and we cannot deny it.
The Acts 4:17 But so that it may not spread further among the people, let us threaten them with a threat no longer to speak upon this name to any person.
The Acts 4:18 And having called them, they commanded them not to utter at all nor teach upon the name of Jesus.
The Acts 4:19 But Peter and John, answering them, said, Whether it is righteous before God to hear you rather than God, judge.
The Acts 4:20 For we cannot but speak the things which we saw and heard.
The Acts 4:21 And having threatened further, they released them, finding nothing as to how they might punish them because of the people, because all were glorifying God at what had happened.
The Acts 4:22 For the man upon whom this sign of healing had occurred was more than forty years old.
The Acts 4:23 And having been released, they came to their own and reported all that the chief priests and the elders said to them.
The Acts 4:24 And having heard, they raised a voice to God with one accord and said, Master, you are God, who made heaven and earth and the sea and all things in them,
The Acts 4:25 who through the mouth of David your servant said, Why did nations rage, and peoples ponder empty things?
The Acts 4:26 The kings of the earth stood forth, and the rulers were gathered together against the Lord and against his Christ.
The Acts 4:27 For in truth both Herod and Pontius Pilate were gathered against your holy servant Jesus, whom you anointed, with nations and peoples of Israel,
The Acts 4:28 to do all things which your hand and your counsel determined beforehand to happen.
The Acts 4:29 And now, Lord, look upon their threats, and give to your slaves to speak your word with all openness,
The Acts 4:30 while you stretch out your hand for healing, and signs and wonders happen through the name of your holy servant Jesus.
The Acts 4:31 And when they had pleaded, the place in which they were gathered was shaken, and all were filled with Holy Spirit and were speaking the word of God with openness.
The Acts 4:32 And of the multitude of those who believed the heart and soul were one, and not even one was saying that anything of his possessions was his own, but all things were common to them.
The Acts 4:33 And with great power the apostles were giving the testimony of the resurrection of the Lord Jesus, and great grace was upon them all.
The Acts 4:34 For neither was there anyone needy among them, for as many as were possessors of fields or houses, selling, were bringing the prices of the things sold,
The Acts 4:35 and placing them at the feet of the apostles, and it was distributed to each according as anyone had need.
The Acts 4:36 And Joses, who was surnamed Barnabas by the apostles, which translated is Son of Exhortation, a Levite, a Cypriot by birth,
The Acts 4:37 a field belonging to him, having sold it, brought the money and placed it at the feet of the apostles.

## Chapter 5

The Acts 5:1 And a certain man, Ananias by name, with Sapphira his wife, sold a property,
The Acts 5:2 and kept back from the price, his wife also knowing, and having brought a certain part, placed it at the feet of the apostles.
The Acts 5:3 But Peter said, Ananias, why did Satan fill your heart for you to lie to the Holy Spirit and keep back from the price of the field?
The Acts 5:4 Remaining, did it not remain yours, and having been sold, was it not in your authority? Why did you put this deed in your heart? You did not lie to people, but to God.
The Acts 5:5 And Ananias, hearing these words, having fallen, expired, and great fear came upon all those hearing these things.
The Acts 5:6 And the younger men, having risen, wrapped him up, and having carried him out, buried him.
The Acts 5:7 And an interval of about three hours passed, and his wife entered, not knowing what had happened.
The Acts 5:8 And Peter answered her, Tell me whether you sold the field for so much. And she said, Yes, for so much.
The Acts 5:9 But Peter said to her, Why was it agreed by you to test the Spirit of the Lord? Look, the feet of those who buried your husband are at the door, and they will carry you out.
The Acts 5:10 And immediately she fell at his feet and expired. And the young men, having entered, found her dead, and having carried her out, buried her beside her husband.
The Acts 5:11 And great fear came upon the whole church and upon all those hearing these things.
The Acts 5:12 And through the hands of the apostles many signs and wonders were occurring among the people, and all were with one accord in Solomon's portico.
The Acts 5:13 But none of the rest dared to join them, but the people were magnifying them.
The Acts 5:14 And still more believers were being added to the Lord, multitudes both of men and women,
The Acts 5:15 so that they were carrying out the sick into the broad streets and placing them upon beds and pallets, so that as Peter came, even the shadow might overshadow some of them.
The Acts 5:16 And the multitude from the surrounding cities also was coming together into Jerusalem, bringing sick people and those troubled by unclean spirits, who were all being healed.
The Acts 5:17 But the high priest, having risen, and all those with him, being the sect of the Sadducees, were filled with jealousy,
The Acts 5:18 and laid their hands upon the apostles and put them in public custody.
The Acts 5:19 But an angel of the Lord through the night opened the doors of the prison, and having led them out, said,
The Acts 5:20 Go, and having stood, speak in the temple to the people all the sayings of this life.
The Acts 5:21 And having heard, they entered into the temple toward dawn and were teaching. But the high priest and those with him, having come, called together the council and all the eldership of the sons of Israel, and sent to the prison for them to be brought.
The Acts 5:22 But the officers, having come, did not find them in the prison, and having returned, reported,
The Acts 5:23 saying, We indeed found the prison shut in all security, and the guards standing outside before the doors, but having opened, we found no one inside.
The Acts 5:24 And when both the priest and the captain of the temple and the chief priests heard these words, they were greatly perplexed concerning them, what this might become.
The Acts 5:25 And someone, having come, reported to them, saying, Look, the men whom you put in the prison are standing in the temple and teaching the people.
The Acts 5:26 Then the captain, having gone away with the officers, brought them, not with violence, for they feared the people, lest they be stoned.
The Acts 5:27 And having brought them, they stood them in the council, and the high priest asked them,
The Acts 5:28 saying, Did we not command you with a command not to teach upon this name? And look, you have filled Jerusalem with your teaching, and wish to bring upon us the blood of this man.
The Acts 5:29 But Peter and the apostles, answering, said, It is necessary to obey God rather than people.
The Acts 5:30 The God of our fathers raised Jesus, whom you killed, having hung him upon wood.
The Acts 5:31 This one God exalted by his right hand as leader and Savior, to give repentance to Israel and forgiveness of sins.
The Acts 5:32 And we are his witnesses of these sayings, and also the Holy Spirit, whom God gave to those obeying him.
The Acts 5:33 But having heard, they were being cut through, and were taking counsel to kill them.
The Acts 5:34 But a certain Pharisee in the council, Gamaliel by name, a teacher of law honored by all the people, having risen, commanded that the apostles be put outside for a little while.
The Acts 5:35 And he said to them, Israelite men, pay attention to yourselves concerning these people, what you are about to do.
The Acts 5:36 For before these days Theudas rose, saying that he himself was someone, to whom a number of about four hundred men joined themselves, who was killed, and all who were obeying him were dissolved and came to nothing.
The Acts 5:37 After this man Judas the Galilean rose in the days of the registration and drew away a considerable people after him; and he perished, and all who were obeying him were scattered.
The Acts 5:38 And now I say to you, Stand away from these people and allow them, because if this counsel or this work is from people, it will be destroyed.
The Acts 5:39 But if it is from God, you cannot destroy it, lest you even be found fighting against God.
The Acts 5:40 And they were persuaded by him, and having called the apostles, having beaten them, commanded them not to speak upon the name of Jesus, and released them.
The Acts 5:41 They therefore indeed were going rejoicing from the face of the council, because they were counted worthy to be dishonored for his name.
The Acts 5:42 And every day in the temple and house by house, they were not ceasing to teach and proclaim Jesus the Christ as good news.

## Chapter 6

The Acts 6:1 And in these days, as the disciples were multiplying, there arose a murmuring of the Hellenists against the Hebrews, because their widows were being overlooked in the daily service.
The Acts 6:2 And the twelve, having summoned the multitude of the disciples, said, It is not pleasing for us, having left the word of God, to serve tables.
The Acts 6:3 Look out therefore, brothers, seven men from you, well attested, full of Holy Spirit and wisdom, whom we will appoint over this need.
The Acts 6:4 But we will persevere in prayer and in the service of the word.
The Acts 6:5 And the word pleased the whole multitude, and they chose Stephen, a man full of faith and Holy Spirit, and Philip and Prochorus and Nicanor and Timon and Parmenas and Nicolaus, an Antiochene proselyte,
The Acts 6:6 whom they stood before the apostles, and having prayed, laid hands upon them.
The Acts 6:7 And the word of God was increasing, and the number of the disciples was multiplying greatly in Jerusalem, and a great crowd of the priests were obeying the faith.
The Acts 6:8 And Stephen, full of faith and power, was doing great wonders and signs among the people.
The Acts 6:9 But some of those from the synagogue called of the Freedmen, and of Cyrenians and Alexandrians and those from Cilicia and Asia, rose, disputing with Stephen.
The Acts 6:10 And they were not strong enough to resist the wisdom and the Spirit by which he was speaking.
The Acts 6:11 Then they instigated men saying, We have heard him speaking blasphemous sayings against Moses and God.
The Acts 6:12 And they stirred up the people and the elders and the scribes, and having come upon him, seized him and brought him into the council.
The Acts 6:13 And they set up false witnesses saying, This man does not cease speaking blasphemous sayings against this holy place and the law.
The Acts 6:14 For we have heard him saying that this Jesus the Nazarene will destroy this place and change the customs which Moses handed over to us.
The Acts 6:15 And all those sitting in the council, having looked intently at him, saw his face as a face of an angel.

## Chapter 7

The Acts 7:1 And the high priest said, Are these things then thus?
The Acts 7:2 And he said, Men, brothers and fathers, hear. The God of glory appeared to our father Abraham while he was in Mesopotamia, before he dwelt in Haran,
The Acts 7:3 and said to him, Go out from your land and from your kin, and come into a land which I will show you.
The Acts 7:4 Then having gone out from the land of Chaldeans, he dwelt in Haran, and from there, after his father died, he moved him into this land in which you now dwell.
The Acts 7:5 And he gave him no inheritance in it, not even a foot's step, and promised to give it to him for possession and to his seed after him, when he had no child.
The Acts 7:6 And God spoke thus, that his seed will be a sojourner in a foreign land, and they will enslave it and mistreat it four hundred years.
The Acts 7:7 And the nation which they serve I will judge, God said, and after these things they will go out and worship me in this place.
The Acts 7:8 And he gave him a covenant of circumcision, and thus he begot Isaac and circumcised him on the eighth day, and Isaac Jacob, and Jacob the twelve patriarchs.
The Acts 7:9 And the patriarchs, having become jealous of Joseph, sold him into Egypt, and God was with him,
The Acts 7:10 and delivered him from all his afflictions, and gave him favor and wisdom before Pharaoh king of Egypt, and appointed him ruler over Egypt and all his house.
The Acts 7:11 And famine came upon all the land of Egypt and Canaan, and great affliction, and our fathers were finding no provisions.
The Acts 7:12 But Jacob, having heard that there was grain in Egypt, sent out our fathers first.
The Acts 7:13 And on the second occasion Joseph was recognized by his brothers, and Joseph's family became manifest to Pharaoh.
The Acts 7:14 And Joseph, having sent, called for his father Jacob and all his kin, seventy-five souls.
The Acts 7:15 And Jacob went down into Egypt and died, he and our fathers.
The Acts 7:16 And they were transferred to Shechem and placed in the tomb which Abraham bought for a price of silver from the sons of Emmor, Emor of Shechem.
The Acts 7:17 And just as the time of the promise which God swore to Abraham was drawing near, the people increased and multiplied in Egypt,
The Acts 7:18 until another king rose who did not know Joseph.
The Acts 7:19 This man, having dealt craftily with our race, mistreated our fathers, making their infants exposed so that they might not be preserved alive.
The Acts 7:20 At which time Moses was born, and was beautiful to God, who was reared three months in his father's house.
The Acts 7:21 And when he was exposed, Pharaoh's daughter took him up and reared him for herself as a son.
The Acts 7:22 And Moses was educated in all wisdom of Egyptians, and was mighty in words and in works.
The Acts 7:23 And when a forty-year time was being fulfilled for him, it came upon his heart to visit his brothers, the sons of Israel.
The Acts 7:24 And having seen someone being wronged, he defended him and made vengeance for the one being oppressed, having struck the Egyptian.
The Acts 7:25 And he was supposing his brothers understood that God through his hand gives them salvation, but they did not understand.
The Acts 7:26 And on the following day he appeared to them fighting, and was driving them together into peace, saying, Men, you are brothers. Why do you wrong each other?
The Acts 7:27 But the one wronging his neighbor pushed him away, saying, Who appointed you ruler and judge over us?
The Acts 7:28 You do not wish to kill me in the manner you killed the Egyptian yesterday, do you?
The Acts 7:29 And Moses fled at this word, and became a sojourner in the land of Midian, where he begot two sons.
The Acts 7:30 And forty years having been fulfilled, an angel of the Lord appeared to him in the wilderness of Mount Sinai, in a flame of fire of a bush.
The Acts 7:31 And Moses, having seen, marveled at the vision, and as he was approaching to observe, a voice of the Lord came to him,
The Acts 7:32 I am the God of your fathers, the God of Abraham and the God of Isaac and the God of Jacob. And Moses, having become trembling, did not dare to observe.
The Acts 7:33 And the Lord said to him, Untie the sandal of your feet, for the place in which you stand is holy ground.
The Acts 7:34 Having seen, I saw the mistreatment of my people in Egypt, and heard their groaning, and descended to deliver them. And now come, I will send you into Egypt.
The Acts 7:35 This Moses whom they denied, saying, Who appointed you ruler and judge? this man God sent as ruler and redeemer by the hand of the angel who appeared to him in the bush.
The Acts 7:36 This man led them out, having done wonders and signs in the land of Egypt and in the Red Sea and in the wilderness forty years.
The Acts 7:37 This is the Moses who said to the sons of Israel, The Lord your God will raise for you a prophet from your brothers as me; you shall hear him.
The Acts 7:38 This is the one who was in the assembly in the wilderness with the angel speaking to him on Mount Sinai and our fathers, who received living oracles to give us,
The Acts 7:39 to whom our fathers did not wish to become obedient, but pushed him away, and turned in their hearts into Egypt,
The Acts 7:40 saying to Aaron, Make us gods who will go before us, for this Moses, who led us out from the land of Egypt, we do not know what has happened to him.
The Acts 7:41 And they made a calf in those days, and brought up a sacrifice to the idol, and were rejoicing in the works of their hands.
The Acts 7:42 But God turned and handed them over to worship the host of heaven, just as it is written in the book of the prophets, You did not offer me slaughtered animals and sacrifices forty years in the wilderness, house of Israel, did you?
The Acts 7:43 And you took up the tent of Moloch and the star of your god Remphan, the forms which you made to worship them, and I will relocate you beyond Babylon.
The Acts 7:44 The tent of testimony was among our fathers in the wilderness, just as the one speaking to Moses commanded to make it according to the pattern which he had seen.
The Acts 7:45 Which our fathers also, having received in succession, brought in with Joshua in the possession of the nations whom God drove out from the face of our fathers, until the days of David,
The Acts 7:46 who found favor before God and asked to find a dwelling for the God of Jacob.
The Acts 7:47 But Solomon built him a house.
The Acts 7:48 But the Most High does not dwell in sanctuaries made by hands, just as the prophet says,
The Acts 7:49 Heaven is my throne, and the earth a footstool of my feet. What kind of house will you build me, the Lord says, or what is the place of my rest?
The Acts 7:50 Did not my hand make all these things?
The Acts 7:51 Stiff-necked and uncircumcised in heart and ears, you always resist the Holy Spirit; as your fathers, also you.
The Acts 7:52 Which of the prophets did your fathers not persecute? And they killed those announcing beforehand concerning the coming of the Righteous One, of whom you have now become betrayers and murderers,
The Acts 7:53 you who received the law as ordinances of angels and did not keep it.
