The Acts 7:54 And hearing these things, they were being cut through in their hearts, and were grinding their teeth against him.
The Acts 7:55 But being full of Holy Spirit, having looked intently into heaven, he saw glory of God, and Jesus standing at the right of God,
The Acts 7:56 and said, Look, I behold the heavens opened, and the Son of Man standing at the right of God.
The Acts 7:57 But having cried out with a loud voice, they closed their ears and rushed upon him with one accord.
The Acts 7:58 And having cast him outside the city, they were stoning him, and the witnesses put off their garments at the feet of a young man called Saul.
The Acts 7:59 And they were stoning Stephen, calling upon and saying, Lord Jesus, receive my spirit.
The Acts 7:60 And having placed his knees down, he cried out with a loud voice, Lord, do not set this sin against them. And having said this, he fell asleep.

## Chapter 8

The Acts 8:1 And Saul was consenting to his killing. And on that day a great persecution arose against the church in Jerusalem, and all were scattered throughout the regions of Judea and Samaria except the apostles.
The Acts 8:2 And devout men carried Stephen to burial and made a great lamentation over him.
The Acts 8:3 But Saul was ravaging the church, entering house by house, and dragging men and women, was handing them over into prison.
The Acts 8:4 Those therefore indeed who were scattered went through, proclaiming the word as good news.
The Acts 8:5 And Philip, having gone down into a city of Samaria, was proclaiming the Christ to them.
The Acts 8:6 And the crowds with one accord were attending to the things said by Philip, as they heard and saw the signs which he was doing.
The Acts 8:7 For from many of those having unclean spirits they were coming out, crying with a loud voice, and many paralyzed and lame were healed.
The Acts 8:8 And great joy came in that city.
The Acts 8:9 But a certain man named Simon was previously in the city practicing magic and astonishing the nation of Samaria, saying that he himself was someone great,
The Acts 8:10 to whom all were attending, from small to great, saying, This man is the great power of God.
The Acts 8:11 And they were attending to him because for a considerable time he had astonished them with the magic arts.
The Acts 8:12 But when they believed Philip proclaiming the things concerning the kingdom of God and the name of Jesus Christ as good news, both men and women were being baptized.
The Acts 8:13 And Simon himself also believed, and having been baptized, was persevering with Philip, and beholding signs and great mighty works occurring, was astonished.
The Acts 8:14 And the apostles in Jerusalem, having heard that Samaria has received the word of God, sent Peter and John to them,
The Acts 8:15 who, having gone down, prayed concerning them, so that they might receive Holy Spirit.
The Acts 8:16 For he had not yet fallen upon any of them, but they had only been baptized into the name of the Lord Jesus.
The Acts 8:17 Then they were laying hands upon them, and they were receiving Holy Spirit.
The Acts 8:18 And Simon, having beheld that the Holy Spirit is given through the laying on of the apostles' hands, offered them money,
The Acts 8:19 saying, Give me also this authority, so that whomever I lay hands upon may receive Holy Spirit.
The Acts 8:20 But Peter said to him, May your silver with you be for destruction, because you supposed the gift of God to be acquired through money.
The Acts 8:21 You have no part nor lot in this matter, for your heart is not straight before God.
The Acts 8:22 Repent therefore from this wickedness of yours, and plead with God whether perhaps the intent of your heart will be forgiven you.
The Acts 8:23 For I see you being in gall of bitterness and a bond of unrighteousness.
The Acts 8:24 But Simon, answering, said, You plead for me to the Lord, so that nothing of what you have said may come upon me.
The Acts 8:25 They therefore indeed, having solemnly testified and spoken the word of the Lord, returned to Jerusalem, and proclaimed good news to many villages of the Samaritans.
The Acts 8:26 And an angel of the Lord spoke to Philip, saying, Rise and go toward the south upon the road descending from Jerusalem into Gaza. This is deserted.
The Acts 8:27 And having risen, he went. And look, an Ethiopian man, a eunuch, an official of Candace the queen of Ethiopians, who was over all her treasury, who had come to Jerusalem to worship,
The Acts 8:28 and was returning, and sitting upon his chariot, and was reading the prophet Isaiah.
The Acts 8:29 And the Spirit said to Philip, Approach and join yourself to this chariot.
The Acts 8:30 And Philip, having run up, heard him reading the prophet Isaiah and said, Do you indeed know what you read?
The Acts 8:31 And he said, For how could I, unless someone guides me? And he invited Philip to come up and sit with him.
The Acts 8:32 And the passage of the Scripture which he was reading was this: As a sheep he was led to slaughter, and as a lamb voiceless before the one shearing it, thus he does not open his mouth.
The Acts 8:33 In his humiliation his judgment was taken away, and who will recount his generation? Because his life is taken away from the earth.
The Acts 8:34 And the eunuch, answering Philip, said, I plead with you, concerning whom does the prophet say this, concerning himself or concerning someone else?
The Acts 8:35 And Philip, having opened his mouth and having begun from this Scripture, proclaimed Jesus to him as good news.
The Acts 8:36 And as they were going along the road, they came upon some water, and the eunuch says, Look, water. What hinders me from being baptized?
The Acts 8:37 And Philip said, If you believe from the whole heart, it is lawful. And answering, he said, I believe Jesus Christ to be the Son of God.
The Acts 8:38 And he commanded the chariot to stand, and both went down into the water, both Philip and the eunuch, and he baptized him.
The Acts 8:39 And when they came up from the water, the Spirit of the Lord snatched Philip away, and the eunuch saw him no longer, for he was going his way rejoicing.
The Acts 8:40 But Philip was found at Azotus, and passing through, was proclaiming good news to all the cities until he came to Caesarea.

## Chapter 9

The Acts 9:1 But Saul, still breathing threat and murder against the disciples of the Lord, having approached the high priest,
The Acts 9:2 asked from him letters to Damascus, to the synagogues, so that if he found any being of the Way, both men and women, he might bring them bound into Jerusalem.
The Acts 9:3 And as he was going, it happened that he drew near to Damascus, and suddenly a light from heaven flashed around him.
The Acts 9:4 And having fallen upon the earth, he heard a voice saying to him, Saul, Saul, why do you persecute me?
The Acts 9:5 And he said, Who are you, Lord? And the Lord said, I am Jesus whom you persecute. It is hard for you to kick against goads.
The Acts 9:6 And trembling and astonished, he said, Lord, what do you wish me to do? And the Lord said to him, Rise and enter into the city, and it will be spoken to you what you must do.
The Acts 9:7 And the men journeying with him stood speechless, hearing indeed the voice, but beholding no one.
The Acts 9:8 And Saul was raised from the earth, and though his eyes were opened, he was seeing no one; and leading him by hand, they brought him into Damascus.
The Acts 9:9 And he was three days not seeing, and did not eat nor drink.
The Acts 9:10 And there was a certain disciple in Damascus named Ananias, and the Lord said to him in a vision, Ananias. And he said, Look, I am here, Lord.
The Acts 9:11 And the Lord said to him, Rise and go to the street called Straight, and seek in the house of Judas a man named Saul, a Tarsian, for look, he prays,
The Acts 9:12 and saw in a vision a man named Ananias entering and laying a hand upon him, so that he might receive sight.
The Acts 9:13 But Ananias answered, Lord, I have heard from many concerning this man, how many evil things he did to your saints in Jerusalem.
The Acts 9:14 And here he has authority from the chief priests to bind all those calling upon your name.
The Acts 9:15 But the Lord said to him, Go, because this man is to me a vessel of election, to carry my name before nations and kings and sons of Israel.
The Acts 9:16 For I will show him how many things he must suffer for my name.
The Acts 9:17 And Ananias went away and entered into the house, and having laid hands upon him, said, Saul, brother, the Lord has sent me, Jesus, who appeared to you on the road by which you were coming, so that you may receive sight and be filled with Holy Spirit.
The Acts 9:18 And immediately there fell away from his eyes as scales, and he received sight at once, and having risen, was baptized.
The Acts 9:19 And having received food, he was strengthened. And Saul was with the disciples in Damascus some days.
The Acts 9:20 And immediately in the synagogues he was proclaiming the Christ, that this is the Son of God.
The Acts 9:21 And all those hearing were astonished, and were saying, Is this not the one who devastated in Jerusalem those calling upon this name, and had come here for this, so that he might bring them bound before the chief priests?
The Acts 9:22 But Saul was being empowered more, and was confounding the Jews dwelling in Damascus, proving that this is the Christ.
The Acts 9:23 And when considerable days were being fulfilled, the Jews took counsel together to kill him.
The Acts 9:24 But their plot became known to Saul, and they were watching the gates both day and night, so that they might kill him.
The Acts 9:25 But the disciples, having taken him by night, let him down through the wall, having lowered him in a basket.
The Acts 9:26 And Saul, having come to Jerusalem, was trying to join himself to the disciples, and all were fearing him, not believing that he is a disciple.
The Acts 9:27 But Barnabas, having taken hold of him, brought him to the apostles, and recounted to them how on the road he saw the Lord, and that he spoke to him, and how in Damascus he spoke openly in the name of Jesus.
The Acts 9:28 And he was with them, entering and going out in Jerusalem,
The Acts 9:29 and speaking openly in the name of the Lord Jesus, and was speaking and disputing with the Hellenists, but they were attempting to kill him.
The Acts 9:30 And the brothers, having learned it, brought him down to Caesarea and sent him out to Tarsus.
The Acts 9:31 The churches therefore indeed throughout all Judea and Galilee and Samaria had peace, being built up and walking in the fear of the Lord, and were multiplying in the encouragement of the Holy Spirit.
The Acts 9:32 And it happened that Peter, passing through all, went down also to the saints dwelling in Lydda.
The Acts 9:33 And there he found a certain person named Aeneas, lying upon a pallet for eight years, who was paralyzed.
The Acts 9:34 And Peter said to him, Aeneas, Jesus the Christ heals you. Rise and spread a bed for yourself. And immediately he rose.
The Acts 9:35 And all those dwelling in Lydda and Sharon saw him, who turned to the Lord.
The Acts 9:36 And in Joppa there was a certain female disciple named Tabitha, which interpreted is said Dorcas. She was full of good works and alms which she was doing.
The Acts 9:37 And it happened in those days that she became sick and died, and having washed her, they placed her in an upper room.
The Acts 9:38 And Lydda being near Joppa, the disciples, having heard that Peter is in it, sent two men to him, exhorting him not to delay to come through as far as them.
The Acts 9:39 And Peter, having risen, went with them, whom, having come, they brought up into the upper room. And all the widows stood by him, weeping and showing tunics and garments, as many as Dorcas was making while being with them.
The Acts 9:40 But Peter, having cast all outside, having placed his knees down, prayed, and having turned to the body, said, Tabitha, rise. And she opened her eyes, and having seen Peter, sat up.
The Acts 9:41 And having given her a hand, he raised her, and having called the saints and the widows, presented her alive.
The Acts 9:42 And it became known throughout all Joppa, and many believed upon the Lord.
The Acts 9:43 And it happened that he remained considerable days in Joppa with a certain Simon, a tanner.

## Chapter 10

The Acts 10:1 And there was a certain man in Caesarea named Cornelius, a centurion from the cohort called Italian,
The Acts 10:2 pious and fearing God with all his house, and doing many alms for the people and pleading with God continually.
The Acts 10:3 He saw clearly in a vision, about the ninth hour of the day, an angel of God entering to him and saying to him, Cornelius.
The Acts 10:4 And he, having looked intently at him and having become fearful, said, What is it, Lord? And he said to him, Your prayers and your alms ascended as a memorial before God.
The Acts 10:5 And now send men to Joppa, and summon Simon, who is surnamed Peter.
The Acts 10:6 This man lodges with a certain Simon, a tanner, whose house is by the sea. He will speak to you what you must do.
The Acts 10:7 And when the angel speaking to Cornelius went away, having called two of his household servants and a pious soldier of those attending him,
The Acts 10:8 and having explained all things to them, he sent them to Joppa.
The Acts 10:9 And on the next day, while they were journeying and drawing near the city, Peter went up upon the housetop to pray about the sixth hour.
The Acts 10:10 And he became hungry and wished to taste food, but while they were preparing, a trance fell upon him.
The Acts 10:11 And he beholds heaven opened, and a certain vessel descending upon him, as a great sheet bound at four corners and being lowered upon the earth,
The Acts 10:12 in which were all the four-footed creatures of the earth, and the wild beasts and the creeping things and the birds of heaven.
The Acts 10:13 And a voice came to him, Rise, Peter, slaughter and eat.
The Acts 10:14 But Peter said, By no means, Lord, because I never ate anything common or unclean.
The Acts 10:15 And a voice again a second time came to him, What God cleansed, do not make common.
The Acts 10:16 And this happened three times, and again the vessel was taken up into heaven.
The Acts 10:17 And as Peter was greatly perplexed within himself as to what the vision which he saw might be, look, the men sent from Cornelius, having inquired for Simon's house, stood at the gateway,
The Acts 10:18 and having called, were inquiring whether Simon surnamed Peter lodges here.
The Acts 10:19 And while Peter was considering the vision, the Spirit said to him, Look, three men seek you.
The Acts 10:20 But rise, go down and go with them, doubting nothing, because I have sent them.
The Acts 10:21 And Peter, having gone down to the men sent from Cornelius to him, said, Look, I am the one whom you seek. What is the reason because of which you are present?
The Acts 10:22 And they said, Cornelius, a centurion, a righteous man and fearing God, and attested by the whole nation of the Jews, was divinely instructed by a holy angel to summon you into his house and hear sayings from you.
The Acts 10:23 Having therefore called them in, he lodged them. And on the next day Peter went out with them, and some of the brothers from Joppa went with him.
The Acts 10:24 And on the next day they entered into Caesarea, and Cornelius was expecting them, having called together his relatives and close friends.
The Acts 10:25 And when Peter came to enter, Cornelius, having met him, having fallen at his feet, worshiped.
The Acts 10:26 But Peter raised him, saying, Rise; I myself also am a person.
The Acts 10:27 And conversing with him, he entered, and finds many gathered.
The Acts 10:28 And he said to them, You know how it is unlawful for a Jewish man to join or approach a foreigner, and God showed me to call no person common or unclean.
The Acts 10:29 Because of this also I came without objection when summoned. I inquire therefore, For what reason did you summon me?
The Acts 10:30 And Cornelius said, From the fourth day until this hour I was fasting, and at the ninth hour praying in my house, and look, a man stood before me in splendid clothing,
The Acts 10:31 and says, Cornelius, your prayer was heard, and your alms were remembered before God.
The Acts 10:32 Send therefore to Joppa, and call for Simon, who is surnamed Peter. He lodges in the house of Simon a tanner by the sea, who, having come, will speak to you.
The Acts 10:33 Immediately therefore I sent to you, and you did well having come. Now therefore we all are present before God to hear all things commanded you by God.
The Acts 10:34 And Peter, having opened his mouth, said, In truth I perceive that God is not a respecter of persons,
The Acts 10:35 but in every nation the one fearing him and working righteousness is acceptable to him.
The Acts 10:36 The word which he sent to the sons of Israel, proclaiming peace as good news through Jesus Christ, he is Lord of all,
The Acts 10:37 you know the saying that occurred throughout all Judea, having begun from Galilee after the baptism which John proclaimed:
The Acts 10:38 Jesus from Nazareth, how God anointed him with Holy Spirit and power, who went through doing good and healing all those oppressed by the devil, because God was with him.
The Acts 10:39 And we are witnesses of all things which he did both in the country of the Jews and in Jerusalem, whom they killed, having hung him upon wood.
The Acts 10:40 This one God raised on the third day and gave him to become manifest,
The Acts 10:41 not to all the people, but to witnesses appointed beforehand by God, to us who ate together and drank together with him after he rose from the dead.
The Acts 10:42 And he commanded us to proclaim to the people and testify solemnly that he is the one determined by God as judge of living and dead.
The Acts 10:43 To him all the prophets testify, that everyone believing in him receives forgiveness of sins through his name.
The Acts 10:44 While Peter was still speaking these sayings, the Holy Spirit fell upon all those hearing the word.
The Acts 10:45 And the believers from circumcision, as many as came with Peter, were astonished, because upon the nations also the gift of the Holy Spirit has been poured out.
The Acts 10:46 For they were hearing them speaking in tongues and magnifying God. Then Peter answered,
The Acts 10:47 Can anyone forbid the water so that these may not be baptized, who received the Holy Spirit just as we also?
The Acts 10:48 And he commanded them to be baptized in the name of the Lord. Then they asked him to remain some days.

## Chapter 11

The Acts 11:1 And the apostles and the brothers who were throughout Judea heard that the nations also received the word of God.
The Acts 11:2 And when Peter went up to Jerusalem, those from circumcision were disputing with him,
The Acts 11:3 saying, You entered to men having uncircumcision and ate with them.
The Acts 11:4 But Peter, having begun, was setting it out to them in succession, saying,
The Acts 11:5 I was in the city of Joppa praying, and in a trance I saw a vision, a certain vessel descending as a great sheet, being lowered by four corners from heaven, and it came as far as me.
The Acts 11:6 Into which, having looked intently, I was observing, and saw the four-footed creatures of the earth and the wild beasts and the creeping things and the birds of heaven.
The Acts 11:7 And I heard a voice saying to me, Rise, Peter, slaughter and eat.
The Acts 11:8 But I said, By no means, Lord, because anything common or unclean never entered into my mouth.
The Acts 11:9 And a voice answered me a second time from heaven, What God cleansed, do not make common.
The Acts 11:10 And this happened three times, and all things were drawn up again into heaven.
The Acts 11:11 And look, immediately three men stood at the house in which I was, sent from Caesarea to me.
The Acts 11:12 And the Spirit said to me to go with them, doubting nothing. And these six brothers also came with me, and we entered into the man's house.
The Acts 11:13 And he reported to us how he saw the angel standing in his house and saying to him, Send men to Joppa and summon Simon surnamed Peter,
The Acts 11:14 who will speak sayings to you in which you and all your house will be saved.
The Acts 11:15 And as I began to speak, the Holy Spirit fell upon them, just as also upon us in the beginning.
The Acts 11:16 And I remembered the saying of the Lord, how he was saying, John indeed baptized with water, but you will be baptized in Holy Spirit.
The Acts 11:17 If therefore God gave them the equal gift as also to us who believed upon the Lord Jesus Christ, but who was I, able to hinder God?
The Acts 11:18 And having heard these things, they became quiet and were glorifying God, saying, Then indeed God gave to the nations also repentance into life.
The Acts 11:19 Those therefore indeed scattered from the affliction that arose over Stephen went through as far as Phoenicia and Cyprus and Antioch, speaking the word to no one except Jews only.
The Acts 11:20 But some of them were Cypriot and Cyrenian men, who, having entered into Antioch, were speaking to the Hellenists, proclaiming the Lord Jesus as good news.
The Acts 11:21 And the hand of the Lord was with them, and a great number, having believed, turned to the Lord.
The Acts 11:22 And the account concerning them was heard in the ears of the church in Jerusalem, and they sent out Barnabas to go through as far as Antioch,
The Acts 11:23 who, having come and having seen the grace of God, rejoiced, and was exhorting all to remain with the Lord with purpose of heart.
The Acts 11:24 Because he was a good man and full of Holy Spirit and faith, and a considerable crowd was added to the Lord.
The Acts 11:25 And Barnabas went out to Tarsus to seek out Saul,
The Acts 11:26 and having found him, brought him to Antioch. And it happened that they gathered in the church a whole year and taught a considerable crowd, and that the disciples were first called Christians in Antioch.
The Acts 11:27 And in these days prophets came down from Jerusalem to Antioch.
The Acts 11:28 And one of them, Agabus by name, having risen, signified through the Spirit that a great famine was about to be upon all the inhabited world, which also happened under Claudius Caesar.
The Acts 11:29 And the disciples, according as anyone had means, determined, each of them, to send for service to the brothers dwelling in Judea,
The Acts 11:30 which they also did, having sent to the elders through the hand of Barnabas and Saul.

## Chapter 12

The Acts 12:1 And at that season Herod the king laid hands on some from the church to mistreat them.
The Acts 12:2 And he killed James, the brother of John, with a sword.
The Acts 12:3 And having seen that it is pleasing to the Jews, he proceeded to seize Peter also. And they were days of Unleavened Bread.
The Acts 12:4 Whom, having also seized, he put into prison, having handed him over to four squads of four soldiers to guard him, wishing after the Passover to bring him up to the people.
The Acts 12:5 Peter therefore indeed was being kept in the prison, but earnest prayer was being made by the church to God for him.
The Acts 12:6 And when Herod was about to bring him forward, on that night Peter was sleeping between two soldiers, bound with two chains, and guards before the door were keeping the prison.
The Acts 12:7 And look, an angel of the Lord stood by, and light shone in the dwelling, and having struck Peter's side, raised him, saying, Rise quickly. And his chains fell off from his hands.
The Acts 12:8 And the angel said to him, Gird yourself and bind on your sandals. And he did thus. And he says to him, Put on your garment and follow me.
The Acts 12:9 And having gone out, he was following him, and did not know that what was happening through the angel is true, but was supposing he sees a vision.
The Acts 12:10 And having passed through a first guard and a second, they came to the iron gate leading into the city, which opened of itself to them, and having gone out, they went along one street, and immediately the angel departed from him.
The Acts 12:11 And Peter, having come to himself, said, Now I truly know that the Lord sent out his angel and delivered me from Herod's hand and all the expectation of the people of the Jews.
The Acts 12:12 And having considered, he came to the house of Mary, the mother of John surnamed Mark, where considerable numbers were gathered and praying.
The Acts 12:13 And when Peter knocked at the door of the gateway, a servant girl named Rhoda approached to answer.
The Acts 12:14 And having recognized Peter's voice, from joy she did not open the gateway, but having run in, reported that Peter stands before the gateway.
The Acts 12:15 But they said to her, You are mad. But she was insisting that it is thus. And they were saying, It is his angel.
The Acts 12:16 But Peter was persisting in knocking, and having opened, they saw him and were astonished.
The Acts 12:17 And having motioned to them with the hand to be silent, he recounted to them how the Lord led him out of the prison, and said, Report these things to James and the brothers. And having gone out, he went into another place.
The Acts 12:18 And when day came, there was no little disturbance among the soldiers as to what then Peter had become.
The Acts 12:19 And Herod, having sought him and not having found, having examined the guards, commanded them to be led away. And having gone down from Judea to Caesarea, he was spending time there.
The Acts 12:20 And Herod was fighting angrily with Tyrians and Sidonians, but they came to him with one accord, and having persuaded Blastus, the one over the king's bedchamber, were asking peace, because their country was fed from the royal country.
The Acts 12:21 And on an appointed day Herod, having clothed himself in royal clothing and having sat upon the judgment seat, was addressing them publicly.
The Acts 12:22 And the populace was shouting, A god's voice, and not a person's.
The Acts 12:23 And immediately an angel of the Lord struck him, because he did not give the glory to God, and having become eaten by worms, he expired.
The Acts 12:24 But the word of God was increasing and multiplying.
The Acts 12:25 And Barnabas and Saul returned from Jerusalem, having fulfilled the service, having also taken along John surnamed Mark.

## Chapter 13

The Acts 13:1 And there were some prophets and teachers in Antioch, in the church there, both Barnabas and Simeon called Niger and Lucius the Cyrenian, and Manaen, a foster companion of Herod the tetrarch, and Saul.
The Acts 13:2 And as they were ministering to the Lord and fasting, the Holy Spirit said, Separate for me now both Barnabas and Saul for the work to which I have called them.
The Acts 13:3 Then having fasted and prayed and laid hands upon them, they released them.
The Acts 13:4 These therefore indeed, having been sent out by the Holy Spirit, went down to Seleucia, and from there sailed away to Cyprus.
The Acts 13:5 And having come to Salamis, they were proclaiming the word of God in the synagogues of the Jews, and had John also as an attendant.
The Acts 13:6 And having passed through the island as far as Paphos, they found a certain magician, a false prophet, a Jew whose name was Bar-Jesus,
The Acts 13:7 who was with the proconsul Sergius Paulus, an understanding man. This man, having summoned Barnabas and Saul, sought to hear the word of God.
The Acts 13:8 But Elymas the magician, for thus his name is translated, was resisting them, seeking to turn the proconsul away from the faith.
The Acts 13:9 But Saul, who is also Paul, having been filled with Holy Spirit and having looked intently at him,
The Acts 13:10 said, O full of all deceit and all villainy, son of the devil, enemy of all righteousness, will you not cease perverting the straight ways of the Lord?
The Acts 13:11 And now look, the hand of the Lord is upon you, and you will be blind, not seeing the sun until a season. And immediately mist and darkness fell upon him, and going around, he was seeking people to lead him by hand.
The Acts 13:12 Then the proconsul, having seen what happened, believed, being astounded at the teaching of the Lord.
The Acts 13:13 And those around Paul, having put out from Paphos, came to Perga of Pamphylia, but John, having departed from them, returned to Jerusalem.
The Acts 13:14 But they, having passed through from Perga, came to Antioch of Pisidia, and having entered into the synagogue on the Sabbath day, sat down.
The Acts 13:15 And after the reading of the law and the prophets, the rulers of the synagogue sent to them, saying, Men, brothers, if there is in you a word of exhortation to the people, speak.
The Acts 13:16 And Paul, having risen and having motioned with the hand, said, Israelite men and those fearing God, hear.
The Acts 13:17 The God of this people Israel chose our fathers, and exalted the people in the sojourn in the land of Egypt, and with an uplifted arm led them out from it.
The Acts 13:18 And for about a forty-year time he bore their conduct in the wilderness.
The Acts 13:19 And having overthrown seven nations in the land of Canaan, he gave their land to them as an inheritance.
The Acts 13:20 And after these things, for about four hundred fifty years, he gave judges until Samuel the prophet.
The Acts 13:21 And from then they asked for a king, and God gave them Saul, son of Kish, a man from the tribe of Benjamin, forty years.
The Acts 13:22 And having removed him, he raised David for them as king, to whom also, having testified, he said, I found David of Jesse, a man according to my heart, who will do all my wills.
The Acts 13:23 From this man's seed God, according to promise, raised for Israel a Savior, Jesus,
The Acts 13:24 John having proclaimed beforehand, before the face of his entrance, a baptism of repentance to all the people of Israel.
The Acts 13:25 And as John was fulfilling the course, he was saying, Whom do you suppose me to be? I am not he. But look, there comes after me one whose sandal of the feet I am not worthy to untie.
The Acts 13:26 Men, brothers, sons of the race of Abraham, and those among you fearing God, to you the word of this salvation was sent.
The Acts 13:27 For those dwelling in Jerusalem and their rulers, having not known this one and the voices of the prophets read every Sabbath, having judged him, fulfilled them.
The Acts 13:28 And having found no cause of death, they asked Pilate that he be killed.
The Acts 13:29 And when they completed all things written concerning him, having taken him down from the wood, they placed him into a tomb.
The Acts 13:30 But God raised him from the dead,
The Acts 13:31 who appeared for many days to those who came up with him from Galilee into Jerusalem, who are his witnesses to the people.
The Acts 13:32 And we proclaim to you as good news the promise made to the fathers,
The Acts 13:33 that God has fulfilled this to their children, to us, having raised Jesus, as it is also written in the second Psalm, You are my Son; I today have begotten you.
The Acts 13:34 And that he raised him from the dead, no longer about to return into corruption, he has spoken thus, I will give you the holy things of David, the faithful things.
The Acts 13:35 Because of this also in another he says, You will not give your holy one to see corruption.
The Acts 13:36 For David indeed, having served his own generation by the counsel of God, fell asleep and was added to his fathers, and saw corruption.
The Acts 13:37 But the one whom God raised did not see corruption.
The Acts 13:38 Let it therefore be known to you, men, brothers, that through this one forgiveness of sins is proclaimed to you,
The Acts 13:39 and from all things from which you could not be justified in the law of Moses, in this one everyone believing is justified.
The Acts 13:40 See therefore that what was said in the prophets does not come upon you:
The Acts 13:41 See, despisers, and marvel and vanish, because I work a work in your days, a work which you will certainly not believe if anyone recounts it to you.
The Acts 13:42 And as they were going out from the synagogue of the Jews, the nations were asking that these sayings be spoken to them on the intervening Sabbath.
The Acts 13:43 And when the synagogue was dismissed, many of the Jews and the worshiping proselytes followed Paul and Barnabas, who, speaking to them, were persuading them to remain in the grace of God.
The Acts 13:44 And on the coming Sabbath almost all the city was gathered to hear the word of God.
The Acts 13:45 But the Jews, having seen the crowds, were filled with jealousy, and were contradicting the things said by Paul, contradicting and blaspheming.
The Acts 13:46 And Paul and Barnabas, having spoken openly, said, It was necessary that the word of God be spoken first to you, but since you push it away and judge yourselves unworthy of eternal life, look, we turn to the nations.
The Acts 13:47 For thus the Lord has commanded us, I have placed you as a light of nations, for you to be for salvation as far as the end of the earth.
The Acts 13:48 And the nations, hearing, were rejoicing and glorifying the word of the Lord, and as many as had been appointed to eternal life believed.
The Acts 13:49 And the word of the Lord was being carried through the whole country.
The Acts 13:50 But the Jews incited the worshiping women and the prominent women and the foremost of the city, and stirred up persecution against Paul and Barnabas, and cast them out from their borders.
The Acts 13:51 But they, having shaken off the dust of their feet against them, came to Iconium.
The Acts 13:52 And the disciples were being filled with joy and Holy Spirit.

## Chapter 14

The Acts 14:1 And it happened in Iconium that they entered together into the synagogue of the Jews and spoke thus, so that a great multitude both of Jews and Greeks believed.
The Acts 14:2 But the disobeying Jews stirred up and embittered the souls of the nations against the brothers.
The Acts 14:3 They therefore indeed spent considerable time speaking openly upon the Lord, who was testifying to the word of his grace and giving signs and wonders to occur through their hands.
The Acts 14:4 But the multitude of the city was divided, and some were with the Jews, but others with the apostles.
The Acts 14:5 And when a rush arose of both nations and Jews with their rulers to abuse and stone them,
The Acts 14:6 having perceived it, they fled to the cities of Lycaonia, Lystra and Derbe, and the surrounding region,
The Acts 14:7 and there were proclaiming good news.
The Acts 14:8 And a certain man in Lystra, powerless in the feet, was sitting, being lame from his mother's womb, who had never walked.
The Acts 14:9 This man was hearing Paul speaking, who, having looked intently at him and having seen that he has faith to be saved,
The Acts 14:10 said with a loud voice, Rise upright upon your feet. And he was leaping and walking.
The Acts 14:11 And the crowds, having seen what Paul did, raised their voice, saying in Lycaonian, The gods, having become like people, came down to us.
The Acts 14:12 And they were calling Barnabas Zeus, but Paul Hermes, since he was the one leading the speech.
The Acts 14:13 And the priest of Zeus who was before their city, having brought bulls and garlands to the gateways, wished to sacrifice with the crowds.
The Acts 14:14 But the apostles Barnabas and Paul, having heard, having torn their garments, leaped into the crowd, crying out,
The Acts 14:15 and saying, Men, why do you do these things? We also are people of like passions with you, proclaiming good news to you to turn from these vain things to the living God, who made heaven and earth and the sea and all things in them,
The Acts 14:16 who in the generations gone by allowed all the nations to go in their ways.
The Acts 14:17 And yet indeed he did not leave himself without witness, doing good, giving us rains from heaven and fruit-bearing seasons, filling our hearts with food and gladness.
The Acts 14:18 And saying these things, they scarcely restrained the crowds from sacrificing to them.
The Acts 14:19 But Jews came from Antioch and Iconium, and having persuaded the crowds and having stoned Paul, they were dragging him outside the city, supposing him to have died.
The Acts 14:20 But when the disciples encircled him, having risen, he entered into the city, and on the next day went out with Barnabas to Derbe.
The Acts 14:21 And having proclaimed good news to that city and made considerable disciples, they returned to Lystra and Iconium and Antioch,
The Acts 14:22 strengthening the souls of the disciples, exhorting them to remain in the faith, and that through many afflictions we must enter into the kingdom of God.
The Acts 14:23 And having appointed elders for them church by church, having prayed with fastings, they entrusted them to the Lord in whom they had believed.
The Acts 14:24 And having passed through Pisidia, they came to Pamphylia.
The Acts 14:25 And having spoken the word in Perga, they went down to Attalia.
The Acts 14:26 And from there they sailed away to Antioch, from where they had been handed over to the grace of God for the work which they fulfilled.
The Acts 14:27 And having come and having gathered the church, they announced all things which God did with them, and that he opened a door of faith to the nations.
The Acts 14:28 And there they were spending no little time with the disciples.

## Chapter 15

The Acts 15:1 And some, having come down from Judea, were teaching the brothers that unless you are circumcised by the custom of Moses, you cannot be saved.
The Acts 15:2 When therefore no little dissension and dispute arose for Paul and Barnabas with them, they appointed Paul and Barnabas and some others of them to go up to the apostles and elders into Jerusalem concerning this question.
The Acts 15:3 They therefore indeed, having been sent onward by the church, were passing through Phoenicia and Samaria, recounting the conversion of the nations, and were making great joy for all the brothers.
The Acts 15:4 And having come to Jerusalem, they were received by the church and the apostles and the elders, and announced all things which God did with them.
The Acts 15:5 But some of those from the sect of the Pharisees who had believed rose up, saying that it is necessary to circumcise them and command them to keep the law of Moses.
The Acts 15:6 And the apostles and the elders were gathered to see concerning this matter.
The Acts 15:7 And much dispute having occurred, Peter, having risen, said to them, Men, brothers, you know that from ancient days God chose among us that through my mouth the nations should hear the word of the good news and believe.
The Acts 15:8 And God, the heart-knower, testified to them, having given them the Holy Spirit just as also to us,
The Acts 15:9 and distinguished nothing between both us and them, having cleansed their hearts by faith.
The Acts 15:10 Now therefore why do you test God, to lay a yoke upon the neck of the disciples which neither our fathers nor we were strong enough to bear?
The Acts 15:11 But through the grace of the Lord Jesus Christ we believe to be saved, in the manner they also are.
The Acts 15:12 And all the multitude became silent and were hearing Barnabas and Paul explaining all the signs and wonders God did among the nations through them.
The Acts 15:13 And after they became silent, James answered, saying, Men, brothers, hear me.
The Acts 15:14 Simeon explained how God first visited to take from nations a people upon his name.
The Acts 15:15 And with this the words of the prophets agree, just as it is written,
The Acts 15:16 After these things I will return and rebuild the tent of David which has fallen, and its demolished things I will rebuild, and I will set it upright,
The Acts 15:17 so that the remaining ones of people may seek out the Lord, and all the nations upon whom my name has been called upon them, says the Lord who does all these things.
The Acts 15:18 All his works are known to God from the age.
The Acts 15:19 Because of this I judge not to trouble those from the nations turning to God,
The Acts 15:20 but to write to them to abstain from the pollutions of the idols and fornication and what is strangled and blood.
The Acts 15:21 For Moses from ancient generations has those proclaiming him city by city, being read in the synagogues every Sabbath.
The Acts 15:22 Then it seemed good to the apostles and the elders with the whole church, having chosen men from them, to send to Antioch with Paul and Barnabas Judas surnamed Barsabas and Silas, leading men among the brothers,
The Acts 15:23 having written through their hand these things: The apostles and the elders and the brothers, to the brothers from nations throughout Antioch and Syria and Cilicia, greetings.
The Acts 15:24 Since we heard that some going out from us troubled you with words, unsettling your souls, saying to be circumcised and keep the law, to whom we gave no instruction,
The Acts 15:25 it seemed good to us, having become of one accord, having chosen men, to send to you with our beloved Barnabas and Paul,
The Acts 15:26 people who have handed over their lives for the name of our Lord Jesus Christ.
The Acts 15:27 We have therefore sent Judas and Silas, themselves also reporting the same things through speech.
The Acts 15:28 For it seemed good to the Holy Spirit and to us to lay upon you no further burden except these necessary things:
The Acts 15:29 to abstain from things sacrificed to idols and blood and what is strangled and fornication, from which keeping yourselves, you will do well. Be strong.
The Acts 15:30 They therefore indeed, having been released, came to Antioch, and having gathered the multitude, delivered the letter.
The Acts 15:31 And having read, they rejoiced at the encouragement.
The Acts 15:32 And Judas and Silas, themselves also being prophets, exhorted the brothers through much speech and strengthened them.
The Acts 15:33 And having spent time, they were released with peace from the brothers to the apostles.
The Acts 15:34 But it seemed good to Silas to remain there.
The Acts 15:35 But Paul and Barnabas were spending time in Antioch, teaching and proclaiming as good news the word of the Lord, with many others also.
The Acts 15:36 And after some days Paul said to Barnabas, Let us now return and visit our brothers in every city in which we proclaimed the word of the Lord, how they are.
The Acts 15:37 And Barnabas took counsel to take along John called Mark.
The Acts 15:38 But Paul was considering it fitting not to take along this man, who departed from them from Pamphylia and did not go with them into the work.
The Acts 15:39 There arose therefore a sharp contention, so that they separated from each other, and Barnabas, having taken Mark, sailed out to Cyprus.
The Acts 15:40 But Paul, having chosen Silas, went out, having been entrusted to the grace of God by the brothers.
The Acts 15:41 And he was passing through Syria and Cilicia, strengthening the churches.

## Chapter 16

The Acts 16:1 And he arrived at Derbe and Lystra, and look, a certain disciple was there named Timothy, son of a certain believing Jewish woman, but of a Greek father,
The Acts 16:2 who was attested by the brothers in Lystra and Iconium.
The Acts 16:3 Paul wished this man to go out with him, and having taken him, circumcised him because of the Jews in those places, for all knew his father, that he was a Greek.
The Acts 16:4 And as they were passing through the cities, they were delivering to them to keep the decrees decided by the apostles and elders in Jerusalem.
The Acts 16:5 The churches therefore indeed were being strengthened in the faith and abounding in number daily.
The Acts 16:6 And having passed through Phrygia and the Galatian country, having been forbidden by the Holy Spirit to speak the word in Asia,
The Acts 16:7 having come toward Mysia, they were trying to go toward Bithynia, and the Spirit did not allow them.
The Acts 16:8 And having passed by Mysia, they went down to Troas.
The Acts 16:9 And a vision appeared to Paul through the night: a certain Macedonian man was standing, exhorting him and saying, Cross into Macedonia and help us.
The Acts 16:10 And when he saw the vision, immediately we sought to go out into Macedonia, concluding that the Lord has called us to proclaim good news to them.
The Acts 16:11 Having therefore put out from Troas, we sailed straight to Samothrace, and on the following day to Neapolis,
The Acts 16:12 and from there to Philippi, which is a foremost city of the district of Macedonia, a colony. And we were spending some days in this city.
The Acts 16:13 And on the Sabbath day we went out outside the city by a river, where a place of prayer was supposed to be, and having sat down, we were speaking to the women who came together.
The Acts 16:14 And a certain woman named Lydia, a seller of purple from the city of Thyatira, worshiping God, was hearing, whose heart the Lord opened to attend to the things spoken by Paul.
The Acts 16:15 And when she was baptized, and her house, she exhorted us, saying, If you have judged me to be faithful to the Lord, enter into my house and stay. And she urged us strongly.
The Acts 16:16 And it happened as we were going to prayer that a certain servant girl having a spirit of Python met us, who was providing much profit to her masters by divining.
The Acts 16:17 She, having followed after Paul and us, was crying out, saying, These people are slaves of the Most High God, who proclaim to us a way of salvation.
The Acts 16:18 And she was doing this for many days. But Paul, having become greatly troubled and having turned, said to the spirit, I command you in the name of Jesus Christ to come out from her. And it came out in that very hour.
The Acts 16:19 But her masters, having seen that the hope of their profit went out, having seized Paul and Silas, dragged them into the marketplace before the rulers.
The Acts 16:20 And having brought them to the magistrates, they said, These people greatly disturb our city, being Jews,
The Acts 16:21 and proclaim customs which it is not lawful for us to receive or do, being Romans.
The Acts 16:22 And the crowd rose together against them, and the magistrates, having torn off their garments, were commanding them to be beaten with rods.
The Acts 16:23 And having laid many blows upon them, they cast them into prison, having commanded the jailer to keep them securely,
The Acts 16:24 who, having received such a command, cast them into the inner prison and secured their feet in the wood.
The Acts 16:25 And about midnight Paul and Silas, praying, were singing hymns to God, and the prisoners were listening to them.
The Acts 16:26 And suddenly a great earthquake occurred, so that the foundations of the prison were shaken, and immediately all the doors were opened, and the bonds of all were loosed.
The Acts 16:27 And the jailer, having become awake and having seen the prison doors opened, having drawn a sword, was about to kill himself, supposing the prisoners to have escaped.
The Acts 16:28 But Paul called with a loud voice, saying, Do no evil to yourself, for we all are here.
The Acts 16:29 And having asked for lights, he leaped in, and having become trembling, fell before Paul and Silas.
The Acts 16:30 And having brought them forward outside, he said, Sirs, what must I do so that I may be saved?
The Acts 16:31 And they said, Believe upon the Lord Jesus Christ, and you will be saved, you and your house.
The Acts 16:32 And they spoke to him the word of the Lord, and to all those in his house.
The Acts 16:33 And having taken them in that hour of the night, he washed them from the wounds, and he himself and all his people were baptized immediately.
The Acts 16:34 And having brought them up into his house, he set a table before them, and exulted with all the house, having believed God.
The Acts 16:35 And when day came, the magistrates sent the rod-bearers, saying, Release those people.
The Acts 16:36 And the jailer reported these words to Paul, that the magistrates have sent so that you may be released. Now therefore go out and go in peace.
The Acts 16:37 But Paul said to them, Having beaten us publicly, uncondemned people, being Romans, they cast us into prison, and now do they cast us out secretly? No indeed, but let them themselves come and lead us out.
The Acts 16:38 And the rod-bearers announced these sayings to the magistrates, and they feared, having heard that they are Romans.
The Acts 16:39 And having come, they entreated them, and having led them out, were asking them to go out from the city.
The Acts 16:40 And having gone out from the prison, they entered to Lydia, and having seen the brothers, encouraged them and went out.

## Chapter 17

The Acts 17:1 And having journeyed through Amphipolis and Apollonia, they came to Thessalonica, where the synagogue of the Jews was.
The Acts 17:2 And according to Paul's custom, he entered to them, and for three Sabbaths was reasoning with them from the Scriptures,
The Acts 17:3 opening and setting forth that the Christ had to suffer and rise from the dead, and that this is the Christ, Jesus whom I proclaim to you.
The Acts 17:4 And some of them were persuaded and joined to Paul and Silas, and a great multitude of the worshiping Greeks, and not a few of the foremost women.
The Acts 17:5 But the disobeying Jews, having become jealous and having taken some wicked men from the marketplace idlers, and having made a crowd, were disturbing the city, and having come upon Jason's house, were seeking to bring them to the populace.
The Acts 17:6 But not having found them, they were dragging Jason and some brothers before the city rulers, crying that these who upset the inhabited world are present here also,
The Acts 17:7 whom Jason has received, and all these act against Caesar's decrees, saying that there is another king, Jesus.
The Acts 17:8 And they troubled the crowd and the city rulers hearing these things.
The Acts 17:9 And having received the security from Jason and the rest, they released them.
The Acts 17:10 And the brothers immediately through the night sent out both Paul and Silas to Berea, who, having come, were going into the synagogue of the Jews.
The Acts 17:11 And these were nobler than those in Thessalonica, who received the word with all eagerness, daily examining the Scriptures whether these things were thus.
The Acts 17:12 Many therefore indeed of them believed, and not a few of the prominent Greek women and men.
The Acts 17:13 But when the Jews from Thessalonica knew that in Berea also the word of God was proclaimed by Paul, they came there also, shaking the crowds.
The Acts 17:14 And then immediately the brothers sent Paul out to go as toward the sea, but both Silas and Timothy were remaining there.
The Acts 17:15 And those conducting Paul brought him as far as Athens, and having received a command to Silas and Timothy that they should come to him as quickly as possible, were going out.
The Acts 17:16 And in Athens, while Paul was awaiting them, his spirit was being provoked within him as he beheld the city being full of idols.
The Acts 17:17 He therefore indeed was reasoning in the synagogue with the Jews and those worshiping, and in the marketplace every day with those happening to be there.
The Acts 17:18 And some of the Epicurean and Stoic philosophers were encountering him, and some were saying, What might this seed-picker wish to say? But others, He seems to be a proclaimer of foreign divinities, because he was proclaiming Jesus and the resurrection to them as good news.
The Acts 17:19 And having taken hold of him, they brought him upon the Areopagus, saying, Can we know what is this new teaching spoken by you?
The Acts 17:20 For you bring some strange things into our hearing. We wish therefore to know what these things might mean.
The Acts 17:21 And all Athenians and the visiting strangers were spending leisure in nothing else than saying something and hearing something newer.
The Acts 17:22 And Paul, having stood in the midst of the Areopagus, said, Athenian men, in all things I behold you as more reverent toward divinities.
The Acts 17:23 For passing through and observing your objects of worship, I found also an altar on which had been inscribed, To an unknown god. The one therefore whom you worship in ignorance, this one I proclaim to you.
The Acts 17:24 God, who made the world and all things in it, this one, being Lord of heaven and earth, does not dwell in sanctuaries made by hands,
The Acts 17:25 nor is he served by people's hands as needing anything, himself giving all life and breath in all things.
The Acts 17:26 And he made from one blood every nation of people to dwell upon all the face of the earth, having determined seasons appointed beforehand and the boundaries of their dwelling,
The Acts 17:27 to seek the Lord, whether perhaps they might feel for him and find him, although indeed he is not far from each one of us.
The Acts 17:28 For in him we live and move and are, as also some of the poets among you have said, For we also are his offspring.
The Acts 17:29 Being therefore offspring of God, we ought not to suppose the divine to be like gold or silver or stone, an engraving of a person's art and thought.
The Acts 17:30 God therefore indeed, having overlooked the times of ignorance, now commands all people everywhere to repent,
The Acts 17:31 because he set a day in which he is about to judge the inhabited world in righteousness by a man whom he determined, having provided assurance to all, having raised him from the dead.
The Acts 17:32 But having heard a resurrection of dead people, some were mocking, but others said, We will hear you again concerning this.
The Acts 17:33 And thus Paul went out from their midst.
The Acts 17:34 But some men, having joined themselves to him, believed, among whom also were Dionysius the Areopagite and a woman named Damaris, and others with them.

## Chapter 18

The Acts 18:1 And after these things Paul, having departed from Athens, came to Corinth.
The Acts 18:2 And having found a certain Jew named Aquila, a Pontian by birth, recently come from Italy, and Priscilla his wife, because Claudius had commanded all the Jews to depart from Rome, he approached them.
The Acts 18:3 And because he was of the same trade, he was remaining with them and working, for they were tentmakers by trade.
The Acts 18:4 And he was reasoning in the synagogue every Sabbath, and persuading Jews and Greeks.
The Acts 18:5 And when both Silas and Timothy came down from Macedonia, Paul was constrained in spirit, solemnly testifying to the Jews that Jesus is the Christ.
The Acts 18:6 But as they were opposing and blaspheming, having shaken off the garments, he said to them, Your blood upon your head; I am clean. From now I will go to the nations.
The Acts 18:7 And having departed from there, he came into the house of someone named Justus, worshiping God, whose house was adjoining the synagogue.
The Acts 18:8 And Crispus, the ruler of the synagogue, believed the Lord with all his house, and many of the Corinthians, hearing, were believing and being baptized.
The Acts 18:9 And the Lord said through a vision in the night to Paul, Do not fear, but speak and do not become silent,
The Acts 18:10 because I am with you, and no one will set upon you to harm you, because I have many people in this city.
The Acts 18:11 And he stayed a year and six months, teaching among them the word of God.
The Acts 18:12 And while Gallio was proconsul of Achaia, the Jews rose against Paul with one accord and brought him before the judgment seat,
The Acts 18:13 saying that this man persuades people to worship God contrary to the law.
The Acts 18:14 And when Paul was about to open the mouth, Gallio said to the Jews, If therefore indeed it were some injustice or wicked villainy, O Jews, according to reason I would bear with you.
The Acts 18:15 But if it is a question concerning a word and names and the law among you, you yourselves shall see to it, for I do not wish to be a judge of these things.
The Acts 18:16 And he drove them away from the judgment seat.
The Acts 18:17 But all the Greeks, having seized Sosthenes the ruler of the synagogue, were striking him before the judgment seat, and Gallio cared for none of these things.
The Acts 18:18 And Paul, having remained still considerable days, having bid farewell to the brothers, was sailing out to Syria, and with him Priscilla and Aquila, having shorn the head in Cenchreae, for he had a vow.
The Acts 18:19 And he arrived at Ephesus and left them there, but he himself, having entered into the synagogue, reasoned with the Jews.
The Acts 18:20 And when they asked him to stay a longer time with them, he did not consent,
The Acts 18:21 but bade farewell to them, saying, I must by all means keep the coming feast in Jerusalem, but I will return again to you, God willing. And he put out from Ephesus.
The Acts 18:22 And having come down to Caesarea, having gone up and greeted the church, he went down to Antioch.
The Acts 18:23 And having spent some time, he went out, passing through in succession the Galatian country and Phrygia, strengthening all the disciples.
The Acts 18:24 And a certain Jew named Apollos, an Alexandrian by birth, an eloquent man, arrived at Ephesus, being mighty in the Scriptures.
The Acts 18:25 This man had been instructed in the way of the Lord, and boiling in spirit, was speaking and teaching accurately the things concerning the Lord, knowing only the baptism of John.
The Acts 18:26 And this man began to speak openly in the synagogue, and Aquila and Priscilla, having heard him, took him to themselves and set out to him more accurately the way of God.
The Acts 18:27 And when he wished to pass into Achaia, the brothers, having encouraged him, wrote to the disciples to receive him, who, having come, contributed much to those who had believed through grace.
The Acts 18:28 For he was vehemently refuting the Jews publicly, showing through the Scriptures that Jesus is the Christ.

## Chapter 19

The Acts 19:1 And it happened while Apollos was in Corinth that Paul, having passed through the upper parts, came to Ephesus, and having found some disciples,
The Acts 19:2 he said to them, Did you receive Holy Spirit, having believed? And they said to him, But we did not even hear whether there is Holy Spirit.
The Acts 19:3 And he said to them, Into what therefore were you baptized? And they said, Into John's baptism.
The Acts 19:4 And Paul said, John indeed baptized a baptism of repentance, saying to the people that they should believe in the one coming after him, that is, in Christ Jesus.
The Acts 19:5 And having heard, they were baptized into the name of the Lord Jesus.
The Acts 19:6 And when Paul laid hands upon them, the Holy Spirit came upon them, and they were speaking in tongues and prophesying.
The Acts 19:7 And all the men were about twelve.
The Acts 19:8 And having entered into the synagogue, he was speaking openly for three months, reasoning and persuading the things concerning the kingdom of God.
The Acts 19:9 But when some were being hardened and disobeying, speaking evil of the Way before the multitude, having departed from them, he separated the disciples, reasoning daily in the school of a certain Tyrannus.
The Acts 19:10 And this happened for two years, so that all those dwelling in Asia heard the word of the Lord Jesus, both Jews and Greeks.
The Acts 19:11 And God was doing no ordinary mighty works through Paul's hands,
The Acts 19:12 so that even handkerchiefs or aprons from his skin were being carried to the sick, and the diseases were departing from them, and the wicked spirits were going out from them.
The Acts 19:13 But some of the itinerant Jewish exorcists attempted to name upon those having the wicked spirits the name of the Lord Jesus, saying, We adjure you by Jesus whom Paul proclaims.
The Acts 19:14 And there were certain seven sons of Sceva, a Jewish chief priest, doing this.
The Acts 19:15 But the wicked spirit, answering, said, Jesus I know, and Paul I am acquainted with, but who are you?
The Acts 19:16 And the man in whom the wicked spirit was, having leaped upon them and having mastered them, prevailed against them, so that they fled out from that house naked and wounded.
The Acts 19:17 And this became known to all, both Jews and Greeks dwelling in Ephesus, and fear fell upon them all, and the name of the Lord Jesus was being magnified.
The Acts 19:18 And many of those who had believed were coming, confessing and announcing their deeds.
The Acts 19:19 And considerable numbers of those who practiced the magic arts, having brought the books together, were burning them before all, and they counted together their prices and found fifty thousand of silver.
The Acts 19:20 Thus the word of the Lord was increasing mightily and prevailing.
The Acts 19:21 And when these things were fulfilled, Paul set in the spirit, having passed through Macedonia and Achaia, to go to Jerusalem, saying that after I have come there, I must also see Rome.
The Acts 19:22 And having sent to Macedonia two of those serving him, Timothy and Erastus, he himself stayed a time in Asia.
The Acts 19:23 And at that season there arose no little disturbance concerning the Way.
The Acts 19:24 For a certain man named Demetrius, a silversmith, making silver sanctuaries of Artemis, was providing no little profit to the craftsmen,
The Acts 19:25 whom, having gathered together, and the workers about such things, he said, Men, you know that our prosperity is from this work.
The Acts 19:26 And you behold and hear that not only of Ephesus, but of almost all Asia, this Paul, having persuaded, turned aside a considerable crowd, saying that those made through hands are not gods.
The Acts 19:27 And not only does this trade of ours risk coming into disrepute, but also the temple of the great goddess Artemis being reckoned as nothing, and her majesty also about to be taken down, whom all Asia and the inhabited world worship.
The Acts 19:28 And having heard and having become full of anger, they were crying out, saying, Great is Artemis of the Ephesians.
The Acts 19:29 And the whole city was filled with confusion, and they rushed with one accord into the theater, having seized Gaius and Aristarchus, Macedonians, fellow travelers of Paul.
The Acts 19:30 And when Paul wished to enter to the populace, the disciples were not allowing him.
The Acts 19:31 And some also of the Asiarchs, being his friends, having sent to him, were exhorting him not to give himself into the theater.
The Acts 19:32 Some therefore indeed were crying one thing, others another, for the assembly was confused, and most did not know for what reason they had come together.
The Acts 19:33 And from the crowd they brought forward Alexander, the Jews having put him forward, and Alexander, having motioned with the hand, wished to defend himself to the populace.
The Acts 19:34 But when they recognized that he is a Jew, one voice came from all, for about two hours crying, Great is Artemis of the Ephesians.
The Acts 19:35 And the secretary, having quieted the crowd, says, Ephesian men, for who is a person who does not know that the city of the Ephesians is temple-keeper of the great goddess Artemis and of the thing fallen from Zeus?
The Acts 19:36 These things therefore being indisputable, it is necessary that you be quieted and do nothing rash.
The Acts 19:37 For you brought these men, neither temple-robbers nor blaspheming your goddess.
The Acts 19:38 If therefore indeed Demetrius and the craftsmen with him have a matter against anyone, court days are being held and there are proconsuls; let them accuse each other.
The Acts 19:39 But if you seek anything concerning other matters, it will be resolved in the lawful assembly.
The Acts 19:40 For we also risk being accused of uprising concerning today, no cause existing concerning which we will be able to give an account of this gathering.
The Acts 19:41 And having said these things, he dismissed the assembly.

## Chapter 20

The Acts 20:1 And after the uproar ceased, Paul, having summoned the disciples and having greeted them, went out to go to Macedonia.
The Acts 20:2 And having passed through those parts and having exhorted them with much speech, he came to Greece.
The Acts 20:3 And having spent three months, when a plot was made against him by the Jews as he was about to put out to Syria, he resolved to return through Macedonia.
The Acts 20:4 And Sopater of Berea was accompanying him as far as Asia, and of Thessalonians Aristarchus and Secundus, and Gaius of Derbe and Timothy, and Asians Tychicus and Trophimus.
The Acts 20:5 These, having gone ahead, were awaiting us in Troas.
The Acts 20:6 But we sailed out after the days of Unleavened Bread from Philippi, and came to them into Troas within five days, where we spent seven days.
The Acts 20:7 And on the first day of the week, when the disciples were gathered to break bread, Paul was reasoning with them, about to go out on the next day, and was prolonging the speech until midnight.
The Acts 20:8 And there were considerable lamps in the upper room where they were gathered.
The Acts 20:9 And a certain young man named Eutychus, sitting upon the window, being borne down by deep sleep as Paul was reasoning longer, having been borne down by the sleep, fell down from the third story and was taken up dead.
The Acts 20:10 But Paul, having gone down, fell upon him, and having embraced him, said, Do not be disturbed, for his soul is in him.
The Acts 20:11 And having gone up and having broken bread and tasted, and having conversed for a considerable time until dawn, thus he went out.
The Acts 20:12 And they brought the boy alive, and were comforted not moderately.
The Acts 20:13 But we, having gone ahead to the boat, put out to Assos, about to take up Paul from there, for thus he had arranged, himself about to go on foot.
The Acts 20:14 And when he met us at Assos, having taken him up, we came to Mitylene.
The Acts 20:15 And having sailed away from there, on the following day we arrived opposite Chios, and on the next we approached Samos, and having remained in Trogyllium, on the following day we came to Miletus.
The Acts 20:16 For Paul decided to sail past Ephesus, so that he might not come to spend time in Asia, for he was hurrying, if it were possible for him, to be in Jerusalem on the day of Pentecost.
The Acts 20:17 And from Miletus, having sent to Ephesus, he summoned the elders of the church.
The Acts 20:18 And when they came to him, he said to them, You know from the first day on which I stepped into Asia how I was with you all the time,
The Acts 20:19 serving the Lord with all humility and many tears and trials which happened to me in the plots of the Jews,
The Acts 20:20 how I withheld nothing of the beneficial things from announcing to you and teaching you publicly and house by house,
The Acts 20:21 solemnly testifying to both Jews and Greeks repentance toward God and faith toward our Lord Jesus Christ.
The Acts 20:22 And now look, I, bound in the spirit, go to Jerusalem, not knowing the things that will meet me in it,
The Acts 20:23 except that the Holy Spirit city by city solemnly testifies, saying that bonds and afflictions await me.
The Acts 20:24 But I make account of none of these things, nor hold my life precious to myself, so as to complete my course with joy and the service which I received from the Lord Jesus, to testify solemnly to the good news of the grace of God.
The Acts 20:25 And now look, I know that you all, among whom I went through proclaiming the kingdom of God, will no longer see my face.
The Acts 20:26 Because of this I testify to you on today's day that I am clean from the blood of all.
The Acts 20:27 For I did not withhold from announcing to you all the counsel of God.
The Acts 20:28 Pay attention therefore to yourselves and to all the flock in which the Holy Spirit placed you as overseers, to shepherd the church of God, which he acquired through his own blood.
The Acts 20:29 For I know this, that after my departure heavy wolves will enter among you, not sparing the flock.
The Acts 20:30 And from you yourselves men will rise, speaking perverted things to draw away the disciples after them.
The Acts 20:31 Because of this stay awake, remembering that for three years night and day I did not cease admonishing each one with tears.
The Acts 20:32 And now I entrust you, brothers, to God and to the word of his grace, which is able to build up and give you inheritance among all those sanctified.
The Acts 20:33 I desired no one's silver or gold or clothing.
The Acts 20:34 And you yourselves know that these hands served my needs and those being with me.
The Acts 20:35 I showed you all things, that laboring thus it is necessary to help the weak, and remember the words of the Lord Jesus, that he himself said, It is blessed to give rather than receive.
The Acts 20:36 And having said these things, having placed his knees down, he prayed with them all.
The Acts 20:37 And considerable weeping of all occurred, and having fallen upon Paul's neck, they were kissing him,
The Acts 20:38 being pained especially at the word which he had said, that they are no longer about to behold his face. And they were sending him onward to the boat.

## Chapter 21

The Acts 21:1 And when it happened that we put out, having been torn away from them, having sailed straight, we came to Cos, and on the next day to Rhodes, and from there to Patara.
The Acts 21:2 And having found a boat crossing to Phoenicia, having embarked, we put out.
The Acts 21:3 And having sighted Cyprus and having left it on the left, we were sailing to Syria and landed at Tyre, for there the boat was unloading the cargo.
The Acts 21:4 And having found the disciples, we remained there seven days, who were saying to Paul through the Spirit not to go up to Jerusalem.
The Acts 21:5 And when it happened that we completed the days, having gone out, we were going, all sending us onward with wives and children as far as outside the city, and having placed our knees down upon the shore, we prayed.
The Acts 21:6 And having greeted each other, we embarked into the boat, but they returned to their own things.
The Acts 21:7 And we, having completed the voyage from Tyre, arrived at Ptolemais, and having greeted the brothers, stayed one day with them.
The Acts 21:8 And on the next day those around Paul, having gone out, came to Caesarea, and having entered into the house of Philip the evangelist, being of the seven, we stayed with him.
The Acts 21:9 And this man had four virgin daughters prophesying.
The Acts 21:10 And while we were remaining many days, a certain prophet named Agabus came down from Judea,
The Acts 21:11 and having come to us and having taken Paul's belt, and having bound his own hands and feet, said, These things the Holy Spirit says: The man whose belt this is, thus the Jews in Jerusalem will bind and hand over into hands of nations.
The Acts 21:12 And when we heard these things, both we and the local people were exhorting him not to go up to Jerusalem.
The Acts 21:13 But Paul answered, What do you do, weeping and crushing my heart? For I am ready not only to be bound, but also to die in Jerusalem for the name of the Lord Jesus.
The Acts 21:14 And when he was not being persuaded, we became quiet, having said, Let the will of the Lord happen.
The Acts 21:15 And after these days, having packed up, we were going up to Jerusalem.
The Acts 21:16 And some of the disciples from Caesarea also went with us, bringing us to one with whom we might lodge, a certain Mnason, a Cypriot, an early disciple.
The Acts 21:17 And when we came to Jerusalem, the brothers gladly received us.
The Acts 21:18 And on the following day Paul was going in with us to James, and all the elders came.
The Acts 21:19 And having greeted them, he was explaining one by one each of the things which God did among the nations through his service.
The Acts 21:20 And having heard, they were glorifying the Lord, and said to him, You behold, brother, how many tens of thousands there are of Jews who have believed, and all are zealots of the law.
The Acts 21:21 But they were informed concerning you that you teach apostasy from Moses to all the Jews throughout the nations, saying that they should not circumcise the children nor walk in the customs.
The Acts 21:22 What therefore is it? A multitude must by all means come together, for they will hear that you have come.
The Acts 21:23 Do therefore this which we say to you. We have four men having a vow upon themselves.
The Acts 21:24 Having taken these, purify yourself with them and spend on them, so that they may shave the head, and all may know that the things of which they have been informed concerning you are nothing, but you yourself also walk in order, keeping the law.
The Acts 21:25 But concerning the nations who have believed, we wrote, having judged that they keep nothing of this sort, except to guard themselves from both the thing sacrificed to idols and blood and what is strangled and fornication.
The Acts 21:26 Then Paul, having taken the men, on the following day, having been purified with them, was entering into the temple, announcing the fulfillment of the days of purification, until the offering was offered for each one of them.
The Acts 21:27 And when the seven days were about to be completed, the Jews from Asia, having beheld him in the temple, were confounding all the crowd and laid hands upon him,
The Acts 21:28 crying, Israelite men, help! This is the person teaching all everywhere against the people and the law and this place, and furthermore he also brought Greeks into the temple and has made this holy place common.
The Acts 21:29 For they had previously seen Trophimus the Ephesian in the city with him, whom they were supposing Paul brought into the temple.
The Acts 21:30 And the whole city was stirred, and a running together of the people occurred, and having seized Paul, they were dragging him outside the temple, and immediately the doors were shut.
The Acts 21:31 And while they were seeking to kill him, a report went up to the commander of a thousand of the cohort that all Jerusalem has been confounded,
The Acts 21:32 who, immediately having taken soldiers and centurions, ran down upon them, but they, having seen the commander of a thousand and the soldiers, ceased striking Paul.
The Acts 21:33 Then the commander of a thousand, having drawn near, seized him and commanded him to be bound with two chains, and was inquiring who he might be and what he has done.
The Acts 21:34 But some were crying one thing, others another, in the crowd, and not being able to know the certainty because of the uproar, he commanded him to be led into the barracks.
The Acts 21:35 And when he came upon the steps, it happened that he was carried by the soldiers because of the violence of the crowd.
The Acts 21:36 For the multitude of the people was following, crying, Take him away.
The Acts 21:37 And Paul, about to be brought into the barracks, says to the commander of a thousand, Is it lawful for me to say something to you? And he said, Do you know Greek?
The Acts 21:38 Are you not then the Egyptian who before these days caused an uprising and led out into the wilderness the four thousand men of the dagger-men?
The Acts 21:39 But Paul said, I indeed am a Jewish person, a Tarsian of Cilicia, a citizen of no insignificant city. And I plead with you, permit me to speak to the people.
The Acts 21:40 And when he permitted, Paul, standing upon the steps, motioned with the hand to the people, and when much silence came, he addressed them in the Hebrew dialect, saying,

## Chapter 22

The Acts 22:1 Men, brothers and fathers, hear my defense to you now.
The Acts 22:2 And having heard that he was addressing them in the Hebrew dialect, they provided more quiet. And he says,
The Acts 22:3 I indeed am a Jewish man, born in Tarsus of Cilicia, but reared in this city at the feet of Gamaliel, educated according to exactness of the ancestral law, being a zealot of God, just as you all are today,
The Acts 22:4 who persecuted this Way as far as death, binding and handing over into prisons both men and women,
The Acts 22:5 as also the high priest testifies to me, and all the eldership, from whom also, having received letters to the brothers, I was going to Damascus to bring those there also bound into Jerusalem so that they might be punished.
The Acts 22:6 And it happened to me, going and drawing near Damascus about midday, that suddenly a considerable light from heaven flashed around me.
The Acts 22:7 And I fell to the ground and heard a voice saying to me, Saul, Saul, why do you persecute me?
The Acts 22:8 And I answered, Who are you, Lord? And he said to me, I am Jesus the Nazarene whom you persecute.
The Acts 22:9 And those being with me indeed beheld the light and became fearful, but did not hear the voice of the one speaking to me.
The Acts 22:10 And I said, What shall I do, Lord? And the Lord said to me, Rise and go to Damascus, and there it will be spoken to you concerning all things appointed for you to do.
The Acts 22:11 And as I was not seeing because of the glory of that light, being led by hand by those being with me, I came to Damascus.
The Acts 22:12 And a certain Ananias, a man pious according to the law, attested by all the Jews dwelling there,
The Acts 22:13 having come to me and having stood by, said to me, Saul, brother, receive sight. And I in that very hour received sight toward him.
The Acts 22:14 And he said, The God of our fathers appointed you beforehand to know his will and see the Righteous One and hear a voice from his mouth,
The Acts 22:15 because you will be a witness to him before all people of the things which you have seen and heard.
The Acts 22:16 And now why do you delay? Rise, be baptized and wash away your sins, having called upon the name of the Lord.
The Acts 22:17 And it happened to me, having returned to Jerusalem and while I was praying in the temple, that I came into a trance,
The Acts 22:18 and saw him saying to me, Hurry and go out quickly from Jerusalem, because they will not receive your testimony concerning me.
The Acts 22:19 And I said, Lord, they themselves know that I was imprisoning and beating in the synagogues those believing upon you.
The Acts 22:20 And when the blood of Stephen your witness was being poured out, I myself also was standing by and consenting to his killing, and guarding the garments of those killing him.
The Acts 22:21 And he said to me, Go, because I will send you out far away to nations.
The Acts 22:22 And they were hearing him until this word, and raised their voice, saying, Take such a man away from the earth, for it was not fitting for him to live.
The Acts 22:23 And as they were crying out and throwing the garments and casting dust into the air,
The Acts 22:24 the commander of a thousand commanded him to be led into the barracks, having said that he be examined with scourges, so that he might know for what reason they were shouting thus against him.
The Acts 22:25 And as he stretched him out with the straps, Paul said to the centurion standing by, Is it lawful for you to scourge a Roman person, and uncondemned?
The Acts 22:26 And the centurion, having heard, having approached, reported to the commander of a thousand, saying, See what you are about to do, for this person is a Roman.
