The Acts 22:27 And the commander of a thousand, having approached, said to him, Tell me whether you are a Roman. And he said, Yes.
The Acts 22:28 And the commander of a thousand answered, I acquired this citizenship for much money. But Paul said, But I have even been born to it.
The Acts 22:29 Immediately therefore those about to examine him departed from him, and the commander of a thousand also feared, having learned that he is a Roman and that he had bound him.
The Acts 22:30 And on the next day, wishing to know the certainty as to why he is accused by the Jews, he loosed him from the bonds, and commanded the chief priests and all their council to come, and having brought Paul down, stood him before them.

## Chapter 23

The Acts 23:1 And Paul, having looked intently at the council, said, Men, brothers, I have conducted myself for God with all good conscience until this day.
The Acts 23:2 But the high priest Ananias commanded those standing by him to strike his mouth.
The Acts 23:3 Then Paul said to him, God is about to strike you, whitewashed wall. And do you sit judging me according to the law, and breaking the law command me to be struck?
The Acts 23:4 And those standing by said, Do you revile God's high priest?
The Acts 23:5 And Paul said, I did not know, brothers, that he is high priest, for it is written, You shall not speak badly of a ruler of your people.
The Acts 23:6 And Paul, having known that the one part is of Sadducees and the other of Pharisees, cried in the council, Men, brothers, I am a Pharisee, a son of a Pharisee. Concerning hope and resurrection of the dead I am judged.
The Acts 23:7 And when he spoke this, dissension arose of the Pharisees and the Sadducees, and the multitude was divided.
The Acts 23:8 For Sadducees indeed say there is no resurrection, nor angel nor spirit, but Pharisees confess both.
The Acts 23:9 And a great outcry arose, and the scribes of the part of the Pharisees, having risen, were fighting fiercely, saying, We find no evil in this person, but if a spirit spoke to him, or an angel, let us not fight against God.
The Acts 23:10 And much dissension having arisen, the commander of a thousand, having feared lest Paul be torn apart by them, commanded the troops to go down and snatch him from their midst and bring him into the barracks.
The Acts 23:11 And on the following night the Lord, having stood by him, said, Take courage, Paul, for as you testified solemnly to the things concerning me in Jerusalem, thus you must also testify in Rome.
The Acts 23:12 And when day came, some of the Jews, having made a gathering, put themselves under a curse, saying neither to eat nor drink until they kill Paul.
The Acts 23:13 And those having made this conspiracy were more than forty,
The Acts 23:14 who, having approached the chief priests and the elders, said, With a curse we put ourselves under a curse to taste nothing until we kill Paul.
The Acts 23:15 Now therefore you with the council make it known to the commander of a thousand that he should bring him down to you tomorrow, as though you are about to determine more accurately the things concerning him, but we are ready to kill him before he draws near.
The Acts 23:16 But the son of Paul's sister, having heard the ambush, having come and entered into the barracks, reported to Paul.
The Acts 23:17 And Paul, having summoned one of the centurions, said, Bring this young man to the commander of a thousand, for he has something to report to him.
The Acts 23:18 He therefore indeed, having taken him, brought him to the commander of a thousand and says, The prisoner Paul, having summoned me, asked to bring this young man to you, having something to speak to you.
The Acts 23:19 And the commander of a thousand, having taken hold of his hand and having withdrawn privately, was inquiring, What is it which you have to report to me?
The Acts 23:20 And he said that the Jews agreed to ask you that tomorrow you bring Paul down into the council, as though they are about to inquire something more accurately concerning him.
The Acts 23:21 You therefore do not be persuaded by them, for more than forty men from them lie in ambush for him, who put themselves under a curse neither to eat nor drink until they kill him, and now they are ready, awaiting the promise from you.
The Acts 23:22 The commander of a thousand therefore indeed released the young man, having commanded him to tell no one that you made these things known to me.
The Acts 23:23 And having summoned a certain two of the centurions, he said, Prepare two hundred soldiers so that they may go as far as Caesarea, and seventy horsemen and two hundred spearmen, from the third hour of the night,
The Acts 23:24 and provide beasts, so that having mounted Paul, they may bring him safely to Felix the governor,
The Acts 23:25 having written a letter containing this form:
The Acts 23:26 Claudius Lysias, to the most excellent governor Felix, greetings.
The Acts 23:27 This man, having been seized by the Jews and about to be killed by them, having come upon them with the troops, I delivered him, having learned that he is a Roman.
The Acts 23:28 And wishing to know the cause for which they were accusing him, I brought him down into their council,
The Acts 23:29 whom I found accused concerning questions of their law, but having no charge worthy of death or bonds.
The Acts 23:30 And when it was disclosed to me that a plot against the man was about to be made by the Jews, immediately I sent to you, having commanded his accusers also to say the things against him before you. Be strong.
The Acts 23:31 The soldiers therefore indeed, according to what had been commanded them, having taken Paul, brought him through the night to Antipatris.
The Acts 23:32 And on the next day, having allowed the horsemen to go with him, they returned to the barracks,
The Acts 23:33 who, having entered into Caesarea and delivered the letter to the governor, presented Paul also to him.
The Acts 23:34 And the governor, having read and having asked from what province he is, and having learned that he is from Cilicia,
The Acts 23:35 said, I will hear you thoroughly when your accusers also come. And he commanded him to be guarded in Herod's praetorium.

## Chapter 24

The Acts 24:1 And after five days the high priest Ananias came down with the elders and a certain orator Tertullus, who made a complaint to the governor against Paul.
The Acts 24:2 And when he was called, Tertullus began to accuse, saying,
The Acts 24:3 Obtaining much peace through you, and improvements occurring for this nation through your foresight, in every way and everywhere we receive it, most excellent Felix, with all thanksgiving.
The Acts 24:4 But so that I may not hinder you further, I entreat you to hear us briefly in your fairness.
The Acts 24:5 For having found this man a plague, and stirring dissension among all the Jews throughout the inhabited world, and a ringleader of the sect of the Nazarenes,
The Acts 24:6 who also attempted to profane the temple, whom we also seized and wished to judge according to our law,
The Acts 24:7 but Lysias the commander of a thousand, having come, with much violence led him away from our hands,
The Acts 24:8 having commanded his accusers to come before you, from whom you yourself, having examined, will be able to learn concerning all these things of which we accuse him.
The Acts 24:9 And the Jews also agreed, asserting that these things are thus.
The Acts 24:10 And Paul answered, when the governor motioned to him to speak, Knowing that you have been a judge for this nation for many years, I defend the things concerning myself more cheerfully,
The Acts 24:11 you being able to know that it is not more than twelve days for me since I went up to worship in Jerusalem.
The Acts 24:12 And neither in the temple did they find me reasoning with anyone or making a gathering of a crowd, nor in the synagogues nor throughout the city,
The Acts 24:13 nor can they present me concerning the things of which they now accuse me.
The Acts 24:14 But I confess this to you, that according to the Way which they call a sect, thus I worship the ancestral God, believing all the things according to the law and written in the prophets,
The Acts 24:15 having hope toward God, which these themselves also await, that there is about to be a resurrection of the dead, both righteous and unrighteous.
The Acts 24:16 And in this I myself practice to have a conscience without offense toward God and people continually.
The Acts 24:17 And after many years I came to make alms to my nation and offerings,
The Acts 24:18 in which they found me purified in the temple, not with a crowd nor with uproar, but some Jews from Asia,
The Acts 24:19 who ought to be present before you and accuse, if they should have anything against me.
The Acts 24:20 Or let these themselves say whether they found any injustice in me when I stood before the council,
The Acts 24:21 except concerning this one utterance which I cried out, standing among them, that concerning resurrection of the dead I am judged today by you.
The Acts 24:22 But Felix, having heard these things, deferred them, knowing more accurately the things concerning the Way, having said, When Lysias the commander of a thousand comes down, I will determine the things concerning you,
The Acts 24:23 and having commanded the centurion that Paul be kept and have relaxation, and to forbid none of his own people to serve or approach him.
The Acts 24:24 And after some days Felix, having come with Drusilla his wife, being Jewish, summoned Paul and heard him concerning faith in Christ.
The Acts 24:25 And as he was reasoning concerning righteousness and self-control and the judgment about to be, Felix, having become fearful, answered, For the present, go, and having obtained a season, I will call for you.
The Acts 24:26 At the same time also hoping that money would be given him by Paul, so that he might release him, because of this also, summoning him more frequently, he was conversing with him.
The Acts 24:27 And two years having been fulfilled, Felix received a successor, Porcius Festus, and wishing to lay up favors with the Jews, Felix left Paul bound.

## Chapter 25

The Acts 25:1 Festus therefore, having entered upon the province, after three days went up to Jerusalem from Caesarea.
The Acts 25:2 And the high priest and the foremost of the Jews made a complaint to him against Paul, and were entreating him,
The Acts 25:3 asking a favor against him, that he summon him to Jerusalem, making an ambush to kill him along the road.
The Acts 25:4 Festus therefore indeed answered that Paul is kept in Caesarea, and that he himself is about to go out quickly.
The Acts 25:5 Those therefore able among you, he says, having gone down together, if there is anything in this man, let them accuse him.
The Acts 25:6 And having spent more than ten days among them, having gone down to Caesarea, on the next day, having sat upon the judgment seat, he commanded Paul to be brought.
The Acts 25:7 And when he came, the Jews who had come down from Jerusalem stood around, bringing many and heavy accusations against Paul, which they were not strong enough to demonstrate,
The Acts 25:8 while he was defending himself, that neither against the law of the Jews nor against the temple nor against Caesar did I sin in anything.
The Acts 25:9 But Festus, wishing to lay up a favor with the Jews, answering Paul, said, Do you wish, having gone up to Jerusalem, to be judged there concerning these things before me?
The Acts 25:10 But Paul said, I am standing before Caesar's judgment seat, where I must be judged. I wronged Jews in nothing, as you also know better.
The Acts 25:11 For if indeed I wrong and have done anything worthy of death, I do not refuse to die. But if there is nothing of the things of which these accuse me, no one can grant me to them. I appeal to Caesar.
The Acts 25:12 Then Festus, having spoken together with the council, answered, You have appealed to Caesar; to Caesar you will go.
The Acts 25:13 And some days having elapsed, Agrippa the king and Bernice arrived at Caesarea to greet Festus.
The Acts 25:14 And as they were spending many days there, Festus laid before the king the things concerning Paul, saying, There is a certain man left by Felix as a prisoner,
The Acts 25:15 concerning whom, when I came to Jerusalem, the chief priests and the elders of the Jews made a complaint, asking a judgment against him.
The Acts 25:16 To whom I answered that it is not a custom for Romans to grant any person to destruction before the accused has the accusers face to face and receives an opportunity of defense concerning the charge.
The Acts 25:17 When therefore they came together here, having made no delay, on the next day, having sat upon the judgment seat, I commanded the man to be brought,
The Acts 25:18 concerning whom the accusers, having stood, were bringing no accusation of the things which I was supposing,
The Acts 25:19 but had some questions against him concerning their own reverence toward divinities and concerning a certain Jesus who had died, whom Paul was asserting to live.
The Acts 25:20 And I, being perplexed concerning the inquiry about this, was saying whether he would wish to go to Jerusalem and there be judged concerning these things.
The Acts 25:21 But when Paul appealed that he be kept for the determination of the Augustus, I commanded him to be kept until I send him to Caesar.
The Acts 25:22 And Agrippa said to Festus, I myself also would wish to hear the person. And he says, Tomorrow you will hear him.
The Acts 25:23 On the next day therefore, when Agrippa and Bernice came with much display and entered into the hearing hall with both the commanders of thousands and the prominent men of the city, and when Festus commanded, Paul was brought.
The Acts 25:24 And Festus says, King Agrippa and all the men present with us, you behold this man, concerning whom all the multitude of the Jews petitioned me both in Jerusalem and here, shouting that he must no longer live.
The Acts 25:25 But I, having perceived that he has done nothing worthy of death, and this man himself also having appealed to the Augustus, decided to send him.
The Acts 25:26 Concerning whom I have nothing certain to write to the lord, because of which I brought him forward before you, and especially before you, King Agrippa, so that when the examination has occurred, I may have something to write.
The Acts 25:27 For it seems unreasonable to me, sending a prisoner, not also to signify the accusations against him.

## Chapter 26

The Acts 26:1 And Agrippa said to Paul, You are permitted to speak for yourself. Then Paul was defending himself, having stretched out the hand.
The Acts 26:2 Concerning all things of which I am accused by Jews, King Agrippa, I consider myself blessed, being about to defend myself before you today,
The Acts 26:3 especially you being a knower of all the customs and questions among Jews, because of which I plead with you to hear me patiently.
The Acts 26:4 My manner of life therefore indeed from youth, which occurred from the beginning among my nation in Jerusalem, all the Jews know,
The Acts 26:5 knowing me beforehand from the start, if they wish to testify, that according to the most exact sect of our religion I lived a Pharisee.
The Acts 26:6 And now upon hope of the promise made to the fathers by God I stand being judged,
The Acts 26:7 to which our twelve-tribe people, worshiping in earnestness night and day, hopes to attain. Concerning which hope I am accused, King Agrippa, by the Jews.
The Acts 26:8 Why is it judged incredible among you if God raises the dead?
The Acts 26:9 I therefore indeed supposed to myself that I must do many opposing things against the name of Jesus the Nazarene,
The Acts 26:10 which I also did in Jerusalem, and I shut up many of the saints in prisons, having received authority from the chief priests, and when they were being killed, I cast a vote.
The Acts 26:11 And throughout all the synagogues, often punishing them, I was compelling them to blaspheme, and being exceedingly mad against them, was persecuting as far as even the outside cities.
The Acts 26:12 In which things also, going to Damascus with authority and commission from the chief priests,
The Acts 26:13 at midday along the road I saw, king, a light from heaven beyond the brightness of the sun, shining around me and those going with me.
The Acts 26:14 And when we all fell down to the earth, I heard a voice speaking to me and saying in the Hebrew dialect, Saul, Saul, why do you persecute me? It is hard for you to kick against goads.
The Acts 26:15 And I said, Who are you, Lord? And he said, I am Jesus whom you persecute.
The Acts 26:16 But rise and stand upon your feet, for I appeared to you for this, to appoint you an attendant and witness both of the things which you saw and of the things in which I will appear to you,
The Acts 26:17 delivering you from the people and the nations, to whom I now send you,
The Acts 26:18 to open their eyes, for them to turn from darkness into light and from the authority of Satan to God, for them to receive forgiveness of sins and a lot among those sanctified by faith in me.
The Acts 26:19 Because of which, King Agrippa, I did not become disobedient to the heavenly vision,
The Acts 26:20 but to those in Damascus first, and Jerusalem, and into all the country of Judea, and to the nations, announcing to repent and turn to God, doing works worthy of repentance.
The Acts 26:21 Because of these things the Jews, having seized me in the temple, were trying to kill me.
The Acts 26:22 Having therefore obtained assistance from God, until this day I stand, testifying to both small and great, saying nothing outside the things which both the prophets and Moses spoke as about to happen,
The Acts 26:23 whether the Christ is subject to suffering, whether first from resurrection of the dead he is about to proclaim light to the people and to the nations.
The Acts 26:24 And while he was defending these things, Festus said with a loud voice, You are mad, Paul; the many writings turn you into madness.
The Acts 26:25 But he says, I am not mad, most excellent Festus, but utter sayings of truth and soundness of mind.
The Acts 26:26 For the king knows concerning these things, to whom also I speak openly, for I am persuaded that none of these things escapes him, for this has not been done in a corner.
The Acts 26:27 Do you believe the prophets, King Agrippa? I know that you believe.
The Acts 26:28 But Agrippa said to Paul, In a little you persuade me to become a Christian.
The Acts 26:29 And Paul said, I would pray to God, both in a little and in much, that not only you, but also all those hearing me today become such as I also am, except these bonds.
The Acts 26:30 And when he said these things, the king rose, and the governor, and Bernice and those sitting with them.
The Acts 26:31 And having withdrawn, they were speaking to each other, saying that this person does nothing worthy of death or bonds.
The Acts 26:32 And Agrippa said to Festus, This person could have been released if he had not appealed to Caesar.

## Chapter 27

The Acts 27:1 And when it was decided that we sail away into Italy, they were handing over both Paul and some other prisoners to a centurion named Julius, of the Augustan cohort.
The Acts 27:2 And having embarked in an Adramyttian boat, about to sail to the places throughout Asia, we put out, Aristarchus, a Macedonian of Thessalonica, being with us.
The Acts 27:3 And on the next day we landed at Sidon, and Julius, having treated Paul humanely, permitted him to go to friends and obtain care.
The Acts 27:4 And having put out from there, we sailed under the lee of Cyprus, because the winds were contrary.
The Acts 27:5 And having sailed through the open sea along Cilicia and Pamphylia, we came down to Myra of Lycia.
The Acts 27:6 And there the centurion, having found an Alexandrian boat sailing to Italy, put us into it.
The Acts 27:7 And sailing slowly for considerable days and having scarcely come along Cnidus, the wind not allowing us forward, we sailed under the lee of Crete along Salmone.
The Acts 27:8 And scarcely sailing along it, we came into a certain place called Fair Havens, near which was the city Lasaea.
The Acts 27:9 And considerable time having elapsed, and the voyage being already dangerous because the fast also had already passed, Paul was advising,
The Acts 27:10 saying to them, Men, I behold that the voyage is about to be with violence and much loss, not only of the cargo and the boat, but also of our lives.
The Acts 27:11 But the centurion was being persuaded by the pilot and the shipowner rather than by the things said by Paul.
The Acts 27:12 And the harbor being unsuitable for wintering, most took counsel to put out from there also, if somehow they might be able, having arrived at Phoenix, to winter, a harbor of Crete looking toward southwest and toward northwest.
The Acts 27:13 And a south wind having blown gently, having supposed they had secured the purpose, having weighed anchor, they were sailing close along Crete.
The Acts 27:14 But after not much time a typhonic wind called Euroclydon struck down from it.
The Acts 27:15 And the boat having been seized and not being able to face the wind, having yielded, we were being carried along.
The Acts 27:16 And having run under the lee of a certain little island called Clauda, we were scarcely strong enough to gain control of the small boat,
The Acts 27:17 which, having raised, they were using helps, undergirding the boat, and fearing lest they fall into the Syrtis, having lowered the gear, thus they were being carried along.
The Acts 27:18 And as we were being severely storm-tossed, on the next day they were making a jettison,
The Acts 27:19 and on the third day with our own hands we threw the equipment of the boat.
The Acts 27:20 And neither sun nor stars appearing for many days, and no little storm pressing, henceforth all hope of our being saved was being taken away.
The Acts 27:21 And much abstinence from food existing, then Paul, having stood in their midst, said, You indeed ought, O men, having obeyed me, not to have put out from Crete, and to have avoided this violence and loss.
The Acts 27:22 And now I advise you to be cheerful, for there will be no loss of life from you, except of the boat.
The Acts 27:23 For there stood by me this night an angel of God, whose I am, whom I also worship,
The Acts 27:24 saying, Do not fear, Paul; you must stand before Caesar, and look, God has granted you all those sailing with you.
The Acts 27:25 Because of this be cheerful, men, for I believe God that it will be thus, in the manner it has been spoken to me.
The Acts 27:26 But we must fall upon a certain island.
The Acts 27:27 And when the fourteenth night came, as we were being driven about in the Adriatic, about the middle of the night the sailors were supposing that some land was approaching them.
The Acts 27:28 And having sounded, they found twenty fathoms, and having gone a little farther and having sounded again, they found fifteen fathoms.
The Acts 27:29 And fearing lest somehow they fall upon rough places, having thrown four anchors from the stern, they were praying for day to come.
The Acts 27:30 And as the sailors were seeking to flee from the boat and had lowered the small boat into the sea under a pretext as though about to stretch out anchors from the bow,
The Acts 27:31 Paul said to the centurion and the soldiers, Unless these remain in the boat, you cannot be saved.
The Acts 27:32 Then the soldiers cut off the ropes of the small boat and allowed it to fall away.
The Acts 27:33 And until day was about to come, Paul was exhorting all to partake of food, saying, Today, the fourteenth day, expecting, you continue without food, having taken nothing.
The Acts 27:34 Because of this I exhort you to take food, for this is for your salvation, for a hair from the head of none of you will fall.
The Acts 27:35 And having said these things and having taken bread, he gave thanks to God before all, and having broken it, began to eat.
The Acts 27:36 And all, having become cheerful, themselves also took food.
The Acts 27:37 And we were in the boat, all the souls, two hundred seventy-six.
The Acts 27:38 And having been satisfied with food, they were lightening the boat, casting out the wheat into the sea.
The Acts 27:39 And when day came, they were not recognizing the land, but were observing a certain bay having a shore, into which they took counsel, if they could, to drive the boat.
The Acts 27:40 And having taken off the anchors, they were leaving them in the sea, at the same time having loosed the lashings of the rudders, and having raised the foresail to the blowing wind, were making toward the shore.
The Acts 27:41 But having fallen upon a place between two seas, they grounded the ship, and the bow, having stuck fast, remained unshaken, but the stern was being broken up by the violence of the waves.
The Acts 27:42 And the soldiers' counsel was to kill the prisoners, lest anyone, having swum out, escape.
The Acts 27:43 But the centurion, wishing to save Paul, hindered them from the purpose, and commanded those able to swim, having thrown themselves out first, to go out upon the land,
The Acts 27:44 and the rest, some upon boards, but others upon some of the things from the boat. And thus it happened that all were brought safely upon the land.

## Chapter 28

The Acts 28:1 And having been brought safely, then they learned that the island is called Melite.
The Acts 28:2 And the barbarians were providing no ordinary humanity to us, for having kindled a fire, they received us all because of the rain that had come and because of the cold.
The Acts 28:3 And when Paul gathered a multitude of sticks and placed them upon the fire, a viper, having come out from the heat, fastened upon his hand.
The Acts 28:4 And when the barbarians saw the beast hanging from his hand, they were saying to each other, By all means this person is a murderer, whom, having been brought safely from the sea, Justice did not allow to live.
The Acts 28:5 He therefore indeed, having shaken off the beast into the fire, suffered no evil.
The Acts 28:6 But they were expecting that he was about to swell or fall down suddenly dead. And when they were expecting for a long time and beholding nothing improper occurring to him, having changed, they were saying that he is a god.
The Acts 28:7 And around that place there were properties belonging to the foremost of the island, named Publius, who, having received us, lodged us kindly three days.
The Acts 28:8 And it happened that the father of Publius was lying down, held by fevers and dysentery, to whom Paul, having entered and having prayed, having laid hands upon him, healed him.
The Acts 28:9 When therefore this happened, the rest also having sicknesses on the island were approaching and being healed,
The Acts 28:10 who also honored us with many honors, and when we were putting out, supplied the things for the need.
The Acts 28:11 And after three months we put out in an Alexandrian boat that had wintered on the island, with the Dioscuri as its sign.
The Acts 28:12 And having landed at Syracuse, we remained three days,
The Acts 28:13 from where, having gone around, we arrived at Rhegium, and after one day, a south wind having arisen, on the second day we came to Puteoli,
The Acts 28:14 where, having found brothers, we were invited to remain with them seven days, and thus we came to Rome.
The Acts 28:15 And from there the brothers, having heard the things concerning us, came out to meet us as far as Appius Forum and Three Taverns, whom Paul, having seen and having given thanks to God, took courage.
The Acts 28:16 And when we came to Rome, the centurion handed the prisoners over to the commander of the camp, but Paul was permitted to remain by himself with the soldier guarding him.
The Acts 28:17 And it happened after three days that Paul called together the foremost of the Jews, and when they came together, he was saying to them, Men, brothers, I, having done nothing contrary to the people or the ancestral customs, was handed over as a prisoner from Jerusalem into the hands of the Romans,
The Acts 28:18 who, having examined me, wished to release me, because no cause of death existed in me.
The Acts 28:19 But when the Jews were contradicting, I was compelled to appeal to Caesar, not as having anything to accuse my nation of.
The Acts 28:20 Because of this reason therefore I called for you to see and speak with you, for because of the hope of Israel I wear this chain.
The Acts 28:21 And they said to him, We neither received letters concerning you from Judea, nor did any of the brothers, having come, report or speak anything wicked concerning you.
The Acts 28:22 But we consider it fitting to hear from you the things which you think, for concerning this sect indeed it is known to us that everywhere it is spoken against.
The Acts 28:23 And having appointed a day for him, more came to him into the lodging, to whom he was setting it out, solemnly testifying to the kingdom of God and persuading them of the things concerning Jesus from both the law of Moses and the prophets, from morning until evening.
The Acts 28:24 And some were being persuaded by the things said, but others were disbelieving.
The Acts 28:25 And being in disagreement with each other, they were departing, Paul having said one saying, that the Holy Spirit spoke well through Isaiah the prophet to our fathers,
The Acts 28:26 saying, Go to this people and say, With hearing you will hear and certainly not understand, and looking you will look and certainly not see.
The Acts 28:27 For the heart of this people was thickened, and with the ears they heard heavily, and they closed their eyes, lest they see with the eyes and hear with the ears and understand with the heart and turn back, and I may heal them.
The Acts 28:28 Let it therefore be known to you that the salvation of God was sent to the nations; they also will hear.
The Acts 28:29 And when he said these things, the Jews went away, having much dispute among themselves.
The Acts 28:30 And Paul remained a whole two years in his own rented dwelling, and was receiving all those entering to him,
The Acts 28:31 proclaiming the kingdom of God and teaching the things concerning the Lord Jesus Christ with all openness, unhindered.

# Romans

The Apostolic Bible. Public domain. https://apostolic-bible.ysys9.chatgpt.site/license.html


## Chapter 1

Romans 1:1 Paul, a slave of Jesus Christ, a called apostle, set apart for God's gospel,
Romans 1:2 which he promised beforehand through his prophets in holy writings,
Romans 1:3 concerning his Son, who came from David's seed according to flesh,
Romans 1:4 who was designated Son of God in power according to the spirit of holiness by resurrection of the dead, Jesus Christ our Lord,
Romans 1:5 through whom we received grace and apostleship for obedience of faith among all the nations for his name,
Romans 1:6 among whom you too are called of Jesus Christ,
Romans 1:7 to all who are in Rome, beloved of God, called saints: grace to you and peace from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ.
Romans 1:8 First, I thank my God through Jesus Christ for all of you, because your faith is proclaimed in the whole world.
Romans 1:9 For God is my witness, whom I serve in my spirit in the gospel of his Son, how unceasingly I make mention of you,
Romans 1:10 always in my prayers asking whether somehow at last I will be granted a successful journey in God's will to come to you.
Romans 1:11 For I long to see you, that I may share some spiritual gift with you for you to be strengthened,
Romans 1:12 that is, to be encouraged together among you through one another's faith, both yours and mine.
Romans 1:13 But I do not want you to be ignorant, brothers, that I often intended to come to you, and was prevented until now, that I might have some fruit among you too, as among the other nations.
Romans 1:14 I am a debtor both to Greeks and to barbarians, both to the wise and to the senseless.
Romans 1:15 Thus, for my part, I am eager to proclaim the gospel also to you who are in Rome.
Romans 1:16 For I am not ashamed of the gospel of Christ, for it is God's power for salvation to everyone who believes, to the Jew first and also to the Greek.
Romans 1:17 For in it God's righteousness is revealed from faith to faith, as it is written, “But the righteous one will live by faith.”
Romans 1:18 For God's wrath is revealed from heaven against all ungodliness and unrighteousness of people who suppress the truth in unrighteousness,
Romans 1:19 because what is known of God is manifest among them, for God manifested it to them.
Romans 1:20 For his invisible things, both his eternal power and divinity, are clearly seen from the creation of the world, understood through the things made, so that they are without excuse,
Romans 1:21 because, having known God, they did not glorify him as God or give thanks, but became futile in their reasonings, and their uncomprehending heart was darkened.
Romans 1:22 Claiming to be wise, they became fools,
Romans 1:23 and exchanged the glory of the incorruptible God for a likeness of an image of corruptible man and birds and four-footed animals and reptiles.
Romans 1:24 Therefore God also handed them over, in the desires of their hearts, to impurity, for their bodies to be dishonored among themselves,
Romans 1:25 who exchanged God's truth for the lie, and revered and served the creation rather than the Creator, who is blessed forever. Amen.
Romans 1:26 For this reason God handed them over to passions of dishonor. For even their females exchanged natural use for that contrary to nature,
Romans 1:27 and likewise the males too, leaving the natural use of the female, burned in their desire toward one another, males with males performing the indecency and receiving in themselves the recompense of their error that was due.
Romans 1:28 And as they did not approve of retaining God in knowledge, God handed them over to a disapproved mind, to do things that are not fitting,
Romans 1:29 filled with all unrighteousness, sexual immorality, wickedness, greed, malice; full of envy, murder, strife, deceit, ill will; whisperers,
Romans 1:30 backbiters, God-haters, insolent, arrogant, boastful, inventors of evil things, disobedient to parents,
Romans 1:31 uncomprehending, covenant-breaking, without natural affection, implacable, merciless,
Romans 1:32 who, knowing God's righteous decree that those who practice such things are worthy of death, not only do them but also approve of those who practice them.

## Chapter 2

Romans 2:1 Therefore you are without excuse, O man, everyone who judges; for in what you judge the other, you condemn yourself, for you who judge practice the same things.
Romans 2:2 But we know that God's judgment is according to truth against those who practice such things.
Romans 2:3 And do you reckon this, O man, you who judge those who practice such things and do them yourself, that you will escape God's judgment?
Romans 2:4 Or do you despise the riches of his kindness and forbearance and patience, not knowing that God's kindness leads you to repentance?
Romans 2:5 But according to your hardness and unrepentant heart, you store up wrath for yourself on the day of wrath and revelation of God's righteous judgment,
Romans 2:6 who will repay each according to his works:
Romans 2:7 to those who through endurance in good work seek glory and honor and incorruptibility, eternal life;
Romans 2:8 but to those of selfish ambition, who disobey the truth but obey unrighteousness, fury and wrath.
Romans 2:9 Affliction and distress upon every soul of man who works evil, of the Jew first and also of the Greek,
Romans 2:10 but glory and honor and peace to everyone who works good, to the Jew first and also to the Greek.
Romans 2:11 For there is no partiality with God.
Romans 2:12 For as many as sinned without law will also perish without law, and as many as sinned in law will be judged through law.
Romans 2:13 For the hearers of the law are not righteous before God, but the doers of the law will be justified.
Romans 2:14 For whenever nations that do not have law do by nature the things of the law, these, not having law, are a law to themselves,
Romans 2:15 who demonstrate the work of the law written in their hearts, their conscience bearing witness together, and their thoughts among one another accusing or even defending,
Romans 2:16 on the day when God judges people's hidden things, according to my gospel, through Jesus Christ.
Romans 2:17 Look, you are named a Jew, and rest upon the law and boast in God,
Romans 2:18 and know the will and approve the things that differ, being instructed from the law,
Romans 2:19 and are convinced that you yourself are a guide of the blind, a light of those in darkness,
Romans 2:20 an instructor of the foolish, a teacher of infants, having the form of knowledge and truth in the law.
Romans 2:21 You, then, who teach another, do you not teach yourself? You who preach not to steal, do you steal?
Romans 2:22 You who say not to commit adultery, do you commit adultery? You who abhor idols, do you rob temples?
Romans 2:23 You who boast in law, do you dishonor God through transgression of the law?
Romans 2:24 For “God's name is blasphemed among the nations because of you,” as it is written.
Romans 2:25 For circumcision indeed benefits if you practice law; but if you are a transgressor of law, your circumcision has become uncircumcision.
Romans 2:26 Therefore, if the uncircumcision keeps the righteous decrees of the law, will not his uncircumcision be reckoned as circumcision?
Romans 2:27 And the uncircumcision by nature, fulfilling the law, will judge you who, through letter and circumcision, are a transgressor of law.
Romans 2:28 For the one outwardly is not a Jew, nor is the outward circumcision in flesh circumcision,
Romans 2:29 but the one inwardly is a Jew, and circumcision is of the heart, in spirit, not letter, whose praise is not from people but from God.

## Chapter 3

Romans 3:1 What, then, is the advantage of the Jew, or what is the benefit of circumcision?
Romans 3:2 Much in every way. For first, they were entrusted with God's oracles.
Romans 3:3 For what if some were unfaithful? Will their unfaithfulness nullify God's faithfulness?
Romans 3:4 May it never be! But let God be true, and every man a liar, as it is written, “So that you may be justified in your words and prevail when you are judged.”
Romans 3:5 But if our unrighteousness demonstrates God's righteousness, what will we say? Is God unrighteous who brings wrath? I speak in human terms.
Romans 3:6 May it never be! Otherwise, how will God judge the world?
Romans 3:7 For if God's truth abounded through my lie to his glory, why am I also still judged as a sinner?
Romans 3:8 And why not, as we are slandered and as some claim we say, “Let us do evil things so that good things may come”? Their judgment is just.
Romans 3:9 What, then? Do we have an advantage? Not at all. For we previously charged both Jews and Greeks with all being under sin,
Romans 3:10 as it is written, “There is no righteous one, not even one;
Romans 3:11 there is no one who understands; there is no one who seeks out God.
Romans 3:12 All turned aside; together they became useless. There is no one who does kindness; there is not even one.
Romans 3:13 Their throat is an opened grave; with their tongues they were deceitful; venom of asps is under their lips,
Romans 3:14 whose mouth is full of curse and bitterness.
Romans 3:15 Their feet are swift to shed blood;
Romans 3:16 devastation and misery are in their ways,
Romans 3:17 and a way of peace they did not know.
Romans 3:18 There is no fear of God before their eyes.”
Romans 3:19 But we know that whatever the law says, it speaks to those in the law, so that every mouth may be stopped and the whole world become accountable to God,
Romans 3:20 because from works of law no flesh will be justified before him; for through law comes knowledge of sin.
Romans 3:21 But now, apart from law, God's righteousness has been manifested, witnessed by the law and the prophets,
Romans 3:22 and God's righteousness through faith of Jesus Christ to all and upon all who believe, for there is no distinction.
Romans 3:23 For all sinned and fall short of God's glory,
Romans 3:24 being justified freely by his grace through the redemption in Christ Jesus,
Romans 3:25 whom God set forth as a propitiatory offering through faith in his blood, for a demonstration of his righteousness because of the passing over of sins previously committed,
Romans 3:26 in God's forbearance, for a demonstration of his righteousness at the present time, so that he may be righteous and justify the one of faith of Jesus.
Romans 3:27 Where, then, is boasting? It was excluded. Through what law? Of works? No, but through a law of faith.
Romans 3:28 We reckon, therefore, that a man is justified by faith apart from works of law.
Romans 3:29 Or is God of Jews only? Is he not also of nations? Yes, of nations also,
Romans 3:30 since God is one, who will justify circumcision from faith and uncircumcision through faith.
Romans 3:31 Do we, then, nullify law through faith? May it never be! Rather, we establish law.

## Chapter 4

Romans 4:1 What, then, will we say Abraham our father has found according to flesh?
Romans 4:2 For if Abraham was justified from works, he has a boast, but not before God.
Romans 4:3 For what does the Scripture say? “And Abraham believed God, and it was reckoned to him as righteousness.”
Romans 4:4 But to the one who works, the wage is not reckoned according to grace but according to debt.
Romans 4:5 But to the one who does not work but believes in the one who justifies the ungodly, his faith is reckoned as righteousness,
Romans 4:6 just as David also speaks of the blessedness of the man to whom God reckons righteousness apart from works:
Romans 4:7 “Blessed are those whose lawless deeds were forgiven and whose sins were covered over.
Romans 4:8 Blessed is the man to whom the Lord will certainly not reckon sin.”
Romans 4:9 Is this blessedness, then, upon the circumcision, or also upon the uncircumcision? For we say that faith was reckoned to Abraham as righteousness.
Romans 4:10 How, then, was it reckoned? While he was in circumcision, or in uncircumcision? Not in circumcision, but in uncircumcision.
Romans 4:11 And he received a sign of circumcision, a seal of the righteousness of the faith in uncircumcision, so that he might be father of all who believe through uncircumcision, for righteousness to be reckoned to them too,
Romans 4:12 and father of circumcision to those not of circumcision only, but also to those who walk in the footsteps of the faith of our father Abraham in uncircumcision.
Romans 4:13 For the promise to Abraham or to his seed, that he should be heir of the world, was not through law but through righteousness of faith.
Romans 4:14 For if those of law are heirs, faith has been emptied and the promise nullified.
Romans 4:15 For the law works wrath; for where there is no law, neither is there transgression.
Romans 4:16 For this reason it is from faith, so that it may be according to grace, for the promise to be firm to all the seed, not to that of the law only but also to that of Abraham's faith, who is father of us all,
Romans 4:17 as it is written, “I have made you father of many nations,” before God whom he believed, who gives life to the dead and calls things that are not as things that are,
Romans 4:18 who beyond hope believed upon hope, so that he might become father of many nations, according to what was said, “So will your seed be.”
Romans 4:19 And not becoming weak in faith, he did not consider his own body already dead, being about a hundred years old, and the deadness of Sarah's womb.
Romans 4:20 But concerning God's promise he did not waver in unbelief, but was empowered in faith, giving glory to God,
Romans 4:21 and being fully convinced that what he has promised he is also able to do.
Romans 4:22 Therefore it was also reckoned to him as righteousness.
Romans 4:23 But it was not written for him alone that it was reckoned to him,
Romans 4:24 but also for us, to whom it is to be reckoned, who believe in the one who raised Jesus our Lord from the dead,
Romans 4:25 who was handed over because of our trespasses and was raised because of our justification.

## Chapter 5

Romans 5:1 Therefore, having been justified from faith, we have peace with God through our Lord Jesus Christ,
Romans 5:2 through whom we have also obtained access by faith into this grace in which we stand, and we boast upon hope of God's glory.
Romans 5:3 And not only this, but we also boast in afflictions, knowing that affliction works endurance,
Romans 5:4 and endurance proven character, and proven character hope.
Romans 5:5 And hope does not put to shame, because God's love has been poured out in our hearts through the Holy Spirit who was given to us.
Romans 5:6 For while we were still weak, Christ died at the appointed time for the ungodly.
Romans 5:7 For scarcely will someone die for a righteous one; for perhaps someone even dares to die for the good one.
Romans 5:8 But God demonstrates his own love toward us, in that while we were still sinners, Christ died for us.
Romans 5:9 Much more, then, having now been justified in his blood, we will be saved through him from wrath.
Romans 5:10 For if, being enemies, we were reconciled to God through the death of his Son, much more, having been reconciled, we will be saved in his life.
Romans 5:11 And not only this, but also boasting in God through our Lord Jesus Christ, through whom we now received reconciliation.
Romans 5:12 For this reason, just as through one man sin entered the world, and through sin death, and thus death passed to all people, because all sinned—
Romans 5:13 for until law, sin was in the world, but sin is not charged when there is no law.
Romans 5:14 Nevertheless, death reigned from Adam until Moses, even over those who did not sin in the likeness of Adam's transgression, who is a pattern of the coming one.
Romans 5:15 But the gracious gift is not as the trespass. For if by the trespass of the one the many died, much more God's grace and the gift in the grace of the one man Jesus Christ abounded to the many.
Romans 5:16 And the gift is not as through one who sinned; for the judgment is from one to condemnation, but the gracious gift is from many trespasses to a righteous verdict.
Romans 5:17 For if by the trespass of the one death reigned through the one, much more those who receive the abundance of grace and of the gift of righteousness will reign in life through the one, Jesus Christ.
Romans 5:18 So then, as through one trespass to all people to condemnation, so also through one righteous act to all people to justification of life.
Romans 5:19 For just as through the disobedience of the one man the many were constituted sinners, so also through the obedience of the one the many will be constituted righteous.
Romans 5:20 But law entered alongside, so that the trespass might increase; but where sin increased, grace abounded beyond measure,
Romans 5:21 so that just as sin reigned in death, so also grace might reign through righteousness to eternal life through Jesus Christ our Lord.

## Chapter 6

Romans 6:1 What, then, will we say? Will we continue in sin so that grace may increase?
Romans 6:2 May it never be! We who died to sin, how will we still live in it?
Romans 6:3 Or do you not know that as many of us as were baptized into Christ Jesus were baptized into his death?
Romans 6:4 Therefore we were buried together with him through baptism into death, so that just as Christ was raised from the dead through the Father's glory, so we too might walk in newness of life.
Romans 6:5 For if we have become united with the likeness of his death, we will also be of his resurrection,
Romans 6:6 knowing this, that our old man was crucified together with him, so that the body of sin might be rendered powerless, for us no longer to be slaves to sin.
Romans 6:7 For the one who died has been justified from sin.
Romans 6:8 But if we died with Christ, we believe that we will also live with him,
Romans 6:9 knowing that Christ, raised from the dead, no longer dies; death no longer rules over him.
Romans 6:10 For the death he died, he died to sin once for all; but the life he lives, he lives to God.
Romans 6:11 Thus you too reckon yourselves to be dead to sin, but living to God in Christ Jesus our Lord.
Romans 6:12 Therefore do not let sin reign in your mortal body, to obey it in its desires,
Romans 6:13 nor present your members to sin as weapons of unrighteousness, but present yourselves to God as living from the dead, and your members to God as weapons of righteousness.
Romans 6:14 For sin will not rule over you, for you are not under law but under grace.
Romans 6:15 What, then? Will we sin because we are not under law but under grace? May it never be!
Romans 6:16 Do you not know that to whom you present yourselves as slaves for obedience, you are slaves to whom you obey, either of sin to death or of obedience to righteousness?
Romans 6:17 But thanks to God that you were slaves of sin, but obeyed from the heart the pattern of teaching to which you were handed over,
Romans 6:18 and having been freed from sin, you were enslaved to righteousness.
Romans 6:19 I speak in human terms because of the weakness of your flesh. For just as you presented your members as slaves to impurity and to lawlessness unto lawlessness, so now present your members as slaves to righteousness unto sanctification.
Romans 6:20 For when you were slaves of sin, you were free with respect to righteousness.
Romans 6:21 What fruit, then, did you have then in the things of which you are now ashamed? For the end of those things is death.
Romans 6:22 But now, having been freed from sin and enslaved to God, you have your fruit unto sanctification, and the end, eternal life.
Romans 6:23 For the wages of sin are death, but God's gracious gift is eternal life in Christ Jesus our Lord.

## Chapter 7

Romans 7:1 Or do you not know, brothers—for I speak to those who know law—that the law rules over a man for as long a time as he lives?
Romans 7:2 For the married woman is bound by law to the living husband; but if the husband dies, she has been released from the law of the husband.
Romans 7:3 So then, while the husband lives, she will be called an adulteress if she becomes another man's; but if the husband dies, she is free from the law, so that she is not an adulteress when she becomes another man's.
Romans 7:4 So, my brothers, you too were put to death to the law through the body of Christ, for you to become another's, his who was raised from the dead, so that we might bear fruit to God.
Romans 7:5 For when we were in the flesh, the passions of sins, which were through the law, were at work in our members to bear fruit to death.
Romans 7:6 But now we have been released from the law, having died in that in which we were held, so that we serve as slaves in newness of spirit and not in oldness of letter.
Romans 7:7 What, then, will we say? Is the law sin? May it never be! But I did not know sin except through law; for I would not have known desire either unless the law said, “You shall not desire.”
Romans 7:8 But sin, taking an opportunity through the commandment, worked every desire in me. For apart from law, sin is dead.
Romans 7:9 But I was once living apart from law; but when the commandment came, sin came to life again, and I died.
Romans 7:10 And the commandment that was unto life was found for me to be unto death.
Romans 7:11 For sin, taking an opportunity through the commandment, deceived me and through it killed me.
Romans 7:12 So the law is holy, and the commandment holy and righteous and good.
Romans 7:13 Did the good, then, become death to me? May it never be! But sin, so that it might appear as sin, working death for me through the good, so that through the commandment sin might become exceedingly sinful.
Romans 7:14 For we know that the law is spiritual, but I am fleshly, sold under sin.
Romans 7:15 For what I work I do not understand; for I do not practice what I want, but what I hate, this I do.
Romans 7:16 But if what I do not want, this I do, I agree with the law that it is good.
Romans 7:17 But now it is no longer I who work it, but the sin dwelling in me.
Romans 7:18 For I know that good does not dwell in me, that is, in my flesh; for willing is present with me, but working the good I do not find.
Romans 7:19 For I do not do the good I want, but the evil I do not want, this I practice.
Romans 7:20 But if what I do not want, this I do, it is no longer I who work it, but the sin dwelling in me.
Romans 7:21 I find, then, the law that, for me who wants to do the good, evil is present with me.
Romans 7:22 For I delight together with God's law according to the inner man,
Romans 7:23 but I see another law in my members, waging war against the law of my mind and taking me captive to the law of sin that is in my members.
Romans 7:24 Wretched man that I am! Who will rescue me from the body of this death?
Romans 7:25 I thank God through Jesus Christ our Lord. So then I myself, with the mind, serve as a slave to God's law, but with the flesh to sin's law.

## Chapter 8

Romans 8:1 There is therefore now no condemnation for those in Christ Jesus who walk not according to flesh but according to spirit.
Romans 8:2 For the law of the Spirit of life in Christ Jesus freed me from the law of sin and death.
Romans 8:3 For what was impossible for the law, in that it was weak through the flesh, God, sending his own Son in the likeness of flesh of sin and concerning sin, condemned sin in the flesh,
Romans 8:4 so that the righteous requirement of the law might be fulfilled in us, who walk not according to flesh but according to spirit.
Romans 8:5 For those who are according to flesh mind the things of the flesh, but those according to spirit the things of the Spirit.
Romans 8:6 For the mind of the flesh is death, but the mind of the Spirit is life and peace,
Romans 8:7 because the mind of the flesh is hostility toward God, for it does not submit to God's law, for neither can it.
Romans 8:8 And those who are in flesh cannot please God.
Romans 8:9 But you are not in flesh but in spirit, if indeed God's Spirit dwells in you. But if someone does not have Christ's Spirit, this one is not his.
Romans 8:10 But if Christ is in you, the body is dead because of sin, but the spirit is life because of righteousness.
Romans 8:11 But if the Spirit of the one who raised Jesus from the dead dwells in you, the one who raised Christ from the dead will also give life to your mortal bodies because of his Spirit dwelling in you.
Romans 8:12 So then, brothers, we are debtors, not to the flesh to live according to flesh.
Romans 8:13 For if you live according to flesh, you are about to die; but if by spirit you put to death the practices of the body, you will live.
Romans 8:14 For as many as are led by God's Spirit, these are sons of God.
Romans 8:15 For you did not receive a spirit of slavery again unto fear, but you received a spirit of adoption as sons, in which we cry, “Abba, Father.”
Romans 8:16 The Spirit himself bears witness together with our spirit that we are children of God.
Romans 8:17 And if children, also heirs: heirs of God and fellow heirs of Christ, if indeed we suffer together so that we may also be glorified together.
Romans 8:18 For I reckon that the sufferings of the present time are not worthy in comparison with the coming glory to be revealed to us.
Romans 8:19 For the eager expectation of creation awaits the revelation of the sons of God.
Romans 8:20 For creation was subjected to futility, not willingly, but because of the one who subjected it, upon hope
Romans 8:21 that creation itself too will be freed from the slavery of corruption into the freedom of the glory of God's children.
Romans 8:22 For we know that all creation groans together and suffers birth pains together until now.
Romans 8:23 And not only this, but we ourselves too, having the firstfruits of the Spirit, also groan within ourselves, awaiting adoption as sons, the redemption of our body.
Romans 8:24 For in hope we were saved; but hope that is seen is not hope, for what someone sees, why does he also hope for it?
Romans 8:25 But if we hope for what we do not see, we await it through endurance.
Romans 8:26 And likewise the Spirit also helps with our weaknesses; for we do not know what to pray as we ought, but the Spirit himself intercedes for us with unutterable groanings.
Romans 8:27 And the one who searches the hearts knows what the mind of the Spirit is, because he intercedes for saints according to God.
Romans 8:28 And we know that all things work together for good for those who love God, for those who are called according to purpose,
Romans 8:29 because those whom he foreknew he also predestined to be conformed to the image of his Son, so that he might be firstborn among many brothers.
Romans 8:30 And those whom he predestined, these he also called; and those whom he called, these he also justified; and those whom he justified, these he also glorified.
Romans 8:31 What, then, will we say to these things? If God is for us, who is against us?
Romans 8:32 He who indeed did not spare his own Son but handed him over for us all, how will he not also with him freely give us all things?
Romans 8:33 Who will bring a charge against God's chosen ones? God is the one who justifies.
Romans 8:34 Who is the one who condemns? Christ is the one who died, and rather also was raised, who also is at God's right hand, who also intercedes for us.
Romans 8:35 Who will separate us from Christ's love? Affliction or distress or persecution or famine or nakedness or danger or sword?
Romans 8:36 As it is written, “For your sake we are put to death all the day; we were reckoned as sheep for slaughter.”
Romans 8:37 But in all these things we more than conquer through the one who loved us.
Romans 8:38 For I am convinced that neither death nor life nor angels nor rulers nor powers nor present things nor coming things,
Romans 8:39 nor height nor depth nor any other creation will be able to separate us from God's love in Christ Jesus our Lord.

## Chapter 9

Romans 9:1 I speak truth in Christ, I do not lie, my conscience bearing witness together with me in the Holy Spirit,
Romans 9:2 that I have great grief and unceasing pain in my heart.
Romans 9:3 For I could wish that I myself were accursed away from Christ for my brothers, my kinsmen according to flesh,
Romans 9:4 who are Israelites, whose are the adoption as sons and the glory and the covenants and the giving of the law and the service and the promises,
Romans 9:5 whose are the fathers, and from whom is Christ according to flesh, who is over all, God blessed forever. Amen.
Romans 9:6 But it is not as though God's word has fallen away. For not all those from Israel are Israel,
Romans 9:7 nor, because they are Abraham's seed, are they all children, but “In Isaac seed will be called for you.”
Romans 9:8 That is, the children of the flesh are not the children of God, but the children of the promise are reckoned as seed.
Romans 9:9 For this is the word of promise: “At this time I will come, and Sarah will have a son.”
Romans 9:10 And not only this, but also Rebecca, having conceived by one, Isaac our father—
Romans 9:11 for before they had been born or done anything good or evil, so that God's purpose according to choice might remain, not from works but from the one who calls—
Romans 9:12 it was said to her, “The greater will serve as a slave to the lesser,”
Romans 9:13 as it is written, “Jacob I loved, but Esau I hated.”
Romans 9:14 What, then, will we say? Is there unrighteousness with God? May it never be!
Romans 9:15 For he says to Moses, “I will have mercy on whomever I have mercy, and I will have compassion on whomever I have compassion.”
Romans 9:16 So then it is not of the one who wills, nor of the one who runs, but of God who has mercy.
Romans 9:17 For the Scripture says to Pharaoh, “For this very thing I raised you up, that I might demonstrate my power in you, and that my name might be proclaimed in all the earth.”
Romans 9:18 So then he has mercy on whom he wills, and he hardens whom he wills.
Romans 9:19 You will say to me, then, “Why does he still find fault? For who has resisted his will?”
Romans 9:20 Indeed, O man, who are you who answers back to God? Will the thing formed say to the one who formed it, “Why did you make me thus?”
Romans 9:21 Or does the potter not have authority over the clay, to make from the same lump one vessel for honor and another for dishonor?
Romans 9:22 But if God, willing to demonstrate wrath and make known his power, bore with much patience vessels of wrath fitted for destruction,
Romans 9:23 and so that he might make known the riches of his glory upon vessels of mercy, which he prepared beforehand for glory,
Romans 9:24 whom he also called, us, not only from Jews but also from nations?
Romans 9:25 As he also says in Hosea, “I will call the one not my people my people, and the one not beloved beloved.
Romans 9:26 And it will be in the place where it was said to them, ‘You are not my people,’ there they will be called sons of the living God.”
Romans 9:27 And Isaiah cries out concerning Israel, “If the number of Israel's sons is as the sand of the sea, the remnant will be saved.
Romans 9:28 For he completes and cuts short a word in righteousness, because the Lord will make a shortened word upon the earth.”
Romans 9:29 And as Isaiah has said beforehand, “Unless the Lord Sabaoth had left us seed, we would have become as Sodom and would have been made like Gomorrah.”
Romans 9:30 What, then, will we say? That nations that did not pursue righteousness attained righteousness, and righteousness from faith,
Romans 9:31 but Israel, pursuing a law of righteousness, did not reach a law of righteousness.
Romans 9:32 Why? Because not from faith, but as from works of law. For they stumbled against the stone of stumbling,
Romans 9:33 as it is written, “Look, I place in Zion a stone of stumbling and a rock of offense, and everyone who believes upon him will not be put to shame.”

## Chapter 10

Romans 10:1 Brothers, the good pleasure of my heart and my petition to God for Israel are for salvation.
Romans 10:2 For I bear witness to them that they have zeal for God, but not according to knowledge.
Romans 10:3 For, not knowing God's righteousness and seeking to establish their own righteousness, they did not submit to God's righteousness.
Romans 10:4 For Christ is the end of law unto righteousness for everyone who believes.
Romans 10:5 For Moses writes the righteousness from the law, that “The man who does them will live in them.”
Romans 10:6 But the righteousness from faith speaks thus: “Do not say in your heart, ‘Who will ascend into heaven?’” That is, to bring Christ down.
Romans 10:7 Or, “‘Who will descend into the abyss?’” That is, to bring Christ up from the dead.
Romans 10:8 But what does it say? “The word is near you, in your mouth and in your heart.” That is, the word of faith which we preach,
Romans 10:9 that if you confess with your mouth Jesus as Lord and believe in your heart that God raised him from the dead, you will be saved.
Romans 10:10 For with the heart one believes unto righteousness, and with the mouth one confesses unto salvation.
Romans 10:11 For the Scripture says, “Everyone who believes upon him will not be put to shame.”
Romans 10:12 For there is no distinction between Jew and Greek, for the same Lord of all is rich toward all who call upon him.
Romans 10:13 For “Everyone who calls upon the Lord's name will be saved.”
Romans 10:14 How, then, will they call upon one in whom they did not believe? And how will they believe one whom they did not hear? And how will they hear without one who preaches?
Romans 10:15 And how will they preach unless they are sent? As it is written, “How beautiful are the feet of those who proclaim peace, of those who proclaim good things.”
Romans 10:16 But not all obeyed the gospel. For Isaiah says, “Lord, who believed our report?”
Romans 10:17 So faith is from hearing, and hearing through God's word.
Romans 10:18 But I say, did they not hear? Indeed, “Their sound went out into all the earth, and their words to the ends of the inhabited world.”
Romans 10:19 But I say, did Israel not know? First Moses says, “I will provoke you to jealousy over a non-nation; over an uncomprehending nation I will provoke you to anger.”
Romans 10:20 And Isaiah is very bold and says, “I was found by those who did not seek me; I became manifest to those who did not ask for me.”
Romans 10:21 But to Israel he says, “All the day I stretched out my hands to a disobedient and contradicting people.”

## Chapter 11

Romans 11:1 I say, then, did God reject his people? May it never be! For I too am an Israelite, from Abraham's seed, of Benjamin's tribe.
Romans 11:2 God did not reject his people whom he foreknew. Or do you not know what the Scripture says in Elijah, how he appeals to God against Israel, saying,
Romans 11:3 “Lord, they killed your prophets and tore down your altars, and I alone was left, and they seek my life”?
Romans 11:4 But what does the divine response say to him? “I left for myself seven thousand men who did not bend a knee to Baal.”
Romans 11:5 Thus, then, also at the present time a remnant has come to be according to a choice of grace.
Romans 11:6 But if by grace, no longer from works, otherwise grace no longer becomes grace. But if from works, it is no longer grace, otherwise work is no longer work.
Romans 11:7 What, then? What Israel seeks, this it did not obtain, but the chosen obtained it, and the rest were hardened,
Romans 11:8 as it is written, “God gave them a spirit of stupor, eyes not to see and ears not to hear, until this very day.”
Romans 11:9 And David says, “Let their table become a snare and a trap and an offense and a recompense to them.
Romans 11:10 Let their eyes be darkened so as not to see, and bend their back continually.”
Romans 11:11 I say, then, did they stumble so that they might fall? May it never be! But by their trespass salvation is for the nations, to provoke them to jealousy.
Romans 11:12 But if their trespass is riches of the world, and their loss riches of nations, how much more their fullness!
Romans 11:13 For I speak to you, the nations. Insofar as I am an apostle of nations, I glorify my ministry,
Romans 11:14 if somehow I may provoke my flesh to jealousy and save some of them.
Romans 11:15 For if their rejection is reconciliation of the world, what is the acceptance except life from the dead?
Romans 11:16 And if the firstfruits are holy, so is the lump; and if the root is holy, so are the branches.
Romans 11:17 But if some of the branches were broken off, and you, being a wild olive, were grafted in among them and became a fellow sharer of the root and richness of the olive,
Romans 11:18 do not boast against the branches. But if you boast against them, you do not carry the root, but the root you.
Romans 11:19 You will say, then, “The branches were broken off so that I might be grafted in.”
Romans 11:20 Well, they were broken off through unbelief, but you stand by faith. Do not be high-minded, but fear.
Romans 11:21 For if God did not spare the branches according to nature, beware lest he not spare you either.
Romans 11:22 See, then, God's kindness and severity: severity upon those who fell, but kindness upon you, if you remain in the kindness; otherwise you too will be cut off.
Romans 11:23 And they too, if they do not remain in unbelief, will be grafted in; for God is able to graft them in again.
Romans 11:24 For if you were cut off from the olive wild by nature and were grafted contrary to nature into a cultivated olive, how much more will these, who are according to nature, be grafted into their own olive!
Romans 11:25 For I do not want you to be ignorant, brothers, of this mystery, so that you may not be wise in your own estimation, that a hardening in part has come to Israel until the fullness of the nations enters,
Romans 11:26 and thus all Israel will be saved, as it is written, “The rescuer will come from Zion, and will turn away ungodliness from Jacob.
Romans 11:27 And this is the covenant from me for them, when I take away their sins.”
Romans 11:28 According to the gospel, enemies for your sake, but according to the choice, beloved because of the fathers.
Romans 11:29 For God's gracious gifts and calling are without regret.
Romans 11:30 For just as you too once disobeyed God, but now received mercy through their disobedience,
Romans 11:31 so these too now disobeyed, so that through the mercy to you they too might receive mercy.
Romans 11:32 For God shut up all in disobedience so that he might have mercy on all.
Romans 11:33 O depth of riches and wisdom and knowledge of God! How unsearchable his judgments and untraceable his ways!
Romans 11:34 For who knew the Lord's mind? Or who became his counselor?
Romans 11:35 Or who gave to him beforehand, and it will be repaid to him?
Romans 11:36 Because from him and through him and to him are all things. To him the glory forever. Amen.

## Chapter 12

Romans 12:1 Therefore I urge you, brothers, through God's compassions, to present your bodies as a living sacrifice, holy, pleasing to God, your rational service.
Romans 12:2 And do not be conformed to this age, but be transformed by the renewal of your mind, for you to discern what God's will is, the good and pleasing and perfect.
Romans 12:3 For through the grace given to me I say to everyone among you not to think more highly than he ought to think, but to think so as to think soundly, to each as God apportioned a measure of faith.
Romans 12:4 For just as in one body we have many members, but all the members do not have the same function,
Romans 12:5 so we, the many, are one body in Christ, and individually members of one another.
Romans 12:6 And having gracious gifts differing according to the grace given to us, whether prophecy, according to the proportion of faith,
Romans 12:7 or ministry, in ministry; or the one who teaches, in teaching;
Romans 12:8 or the one who encourages, in encouragement; the one who shares, in simplicity; the one who leads, in diligence; the one who shows mercy, in cheerfulness.
Romans 12:9 Love without hypocrisy; abhorring the evil, clinging to the good;
Romans 12:10 in brotherly love, affectionately devoted to one another; in honor, taking the lead toward one another;
Romans 12:11 in diligence, not sluggish; boiling in spirit; serving the time;
Romans 12:12 rejoicing in hope; enduring in affliction; persevering in prayer;
Romans 12:13 sharing in the needs of the saints; pursuing hospitality.
Romans 12:14 Bless those who persecute you; bless and do not curse.
Romans 12:15 Rejoice with those who rejoice, and weep with those who weep.
Romans 12:16 Thinking the same toward one another; not thinking high things, but being carried along with the lowly. Do not become wise in your own estimation.
Romans 12:17 Repaying no one evil for evil; taking forethought for good things before all people;
Romans 12:18 if possible, as far as it depends on you, being at peace with all people.
Romans 12:19 Not avenging yourselves, beloved, but give place to wrath; for it is written, “Vengeance is mine; I will repay, says the Lord.”
Romans 12:20 Therefore, if your enemy is hungry, feed him; if he is thirsty, give him drink; for doing this you will heap coals of fire upon his head.
Romans 12:21 Do not be conquered by evil, but conquer evil with good.

## Chapter 13

Romans 13:1 Let every soul submit to the higher authorities. For there is no authority except from God, and the authorities that exist have been appointed by God.
Romans 13:2 So the one who opposes the authority has resisted God's ordinance, and those who have resisted will receive judgment for themselves.
Romans 13:3 For rulers are not a fear to good works but to evil ones. And do you want not to fear the authority? Do the good, and you will have praise from it.
Romans 13:4 For it is God's minister to you for good. But if you do the evil, fear; for it does not bear the sword in vain, for it is God's minister, an avenger unto wrath upon the one who practices evil.
Romans 13:5 Therefore it is necessary to submit, not only because of wrath but also because of conscience.
Romans 13:6 For because of this you also pay taxes; for they are God's public servants, persevering in this very thing.
Romans 13:7 Therefore repay all their dues: to the one due tax, tax; to the one due toll, toll; to the one due fear, fear; to the one due honor, honor.
Romans 13:8 Owe no one anything except to love one another, for the one who loves the other has fulfilled law.
Romans 13:9 For “You shall not commit adultery, you shall not murder, you shall not steal, you shall not bear false witness, you shall not desire,” and if there is any other commandment, it is summed up in this word, in “You shall love your neighbor as yourself.”
Romans 13:10 Love does not work evil to the neighbor; therefore love is the fulfillment of law.
Romans 13:11 And this, knowing the time, that it is already the hour for us to be raised from sleep; for now our salvation is nearer than when we believed.
Romans 13:12 The night advanced, and the day has drawn near. Therefore let us put off the works of darkness and put on the weapons of light.
Romans 13:13 Let us walk decently, as in day, not in revelries and drunkenness, not in sexual beds and licentious acts, not in strife and jealousy.
Romans 13:14 But put on the Lord Jesus Christ, and do not make provision for the flesh unto desires.

## Chapter 14

Romans 14:1 But receive the one who is weak in faith, not for disputes over reasonings.
Romans 14:2 One believes he may eat all things, but the weak one eats vegetables.
Romans 14:3 Let the one who eats not despise the one who does not eat, and let the one who does not eat not judge the one who eats, for God received him.
Romans 14:4 Who are you who judges another's household servant? To his own lord he stands or falls. And he will be made to stand, for God is able to make him stand.
Romans 14:5 One judges a day above a day, but another judges every day. Let each be fully convinced in his own mind.
Romans 14:6 The one who regards the day regards it to the Lord, and the one who does not regard the day does not regard it to the Lord. The one who eats eats to the Lord, for he gives thanks to God; and the one who does not eat does not eat to the Lord and gives thanks to God.
Romans 14:7 For none of us lives to himself, and none dies to himself.
Romans 14:8 For if we live, we live to the Lord, and if we die, we die to the Lord. Therefore, whether we live or whether we die, we are the Lord's.
Romans 14:9 For to this end Christ both died and rose and lived again, so that he might rule over both dead and living.
Romans 14:10 But why do you judge your brother? Or why do you also despise your brother? For we will all stand before Christ's judgment seat.
Romans 14:11 For it is written, “I live, says the Lord, that to me every knee will bend, and every tongue will confess to God.”
Romans 14:12 So then each of us will give an account concerning himself to God.
Romans 14:13 Therefore let us no longer judge one another, but rather judge this: not to place a stumbling block or an offense for the brother.
Romans 14:14 I know and am convinced in the Lord Jesus that nothing is common through itself, except that to the one who reckons something to be common, to that one it is common.
Romans 14:15 But if your brother is grieved because of food, you no longer walk according to love. Do not destroy with your food that one for whom Christ died.
Romans 14:16 Therefore do not let your good be blasphemed.
Romans 14:17 For God's kingdom is not eating and drinking, but righteousness and peace and joy in the Holy Spirit.
Romans 14:18 For the one who in these things serves as a slave to Christ is pleasing to God and approved by people.
Romans 14:19 So then let us pursue the things of peace and the things of building up one another.
Romans 14:20 Do not tear down God's work for the sake of food. All things indeed are clean, but it is evil for the man who eats through a stumbling block.
Romans 14:21 It is good not to eat meat or drink wine or anything by which your brother stumbles or is offended or is weakened.
Romans 14:22 Do you have faith? Have it to yourself before God. Blessed is the one who does not judge himself in what he approves.
Romans 14:23 But the one who doubts, if he eats, has been condemned, because it is not from faith; and everything that is not from faith is sin.

## Chapter 15

Romans 15:1 But we who are strong ought to carry the weaknesses of those who are not strong, and not please ourselves.
Romans 15:2 For let each of us please the neighbor for good, toward building up.
Romans 15:3 For Christ too did not please himself, but as it is written, “The reproaches of those who reproach you fell upon me.”
Romans 15:4 For whatever was written beforehand was written beforehand for our teaching, so that through endurance and through the encouragement of the writings we might have hope.
Romans 15:5 And may the God of endurance and encouragement grant you to think the same among one another according to Christ Jesus,
Romans 15:6 so that with one accord, with one mouth, you may glorify the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ.
Romans 15:7 Therefore receive one another, just as Christ also received us, unto God's glory.
Romans 15:8 And I say that Jesus Christ has become a minister of circumcision for God's truth, to confirm the promises of the fathers,
Romans 15:9 and for the nations to glorify God for mercy, as it is written, “For this reason I will confess to you among nations and sing to your name.”
Romans 15:10 And again he says, “Rejoice, nations, with his people.”
Romans 15:11 And again, “Praise the Lord, all the nations, and praise him, all the peoples.”
Romans 15:12 And again Isaiah says, “There will be the root of Jesse, and the one who rises to rule nations; upon him nations will hope.”
Romans 15:13 And may the God of hope fill you with all joy and peace in believing, for you to abound in hope in the power of the Holy Spirit.
Romans 15:14 And I myself too am convinced concerning you, my brothers, that you yourselves too are full of goodness, filled with all knowledge, able also to admonish one another.
Romans 15:15 But I wrote to you more boldly in part, brothers, as reminding you again, because of the grace given to me by God,
Romans 15:16 for me to be a public minister of Jesus Christ to the nations, performing priestly service for God's gospel, so that the offering of the nations might become acceptable, sanctified in the Holy Spirit.
Romans 15:17 Therefore I have boasting in Christ Jesus in the things toward God.
Romans 15:18 For I will not dare to speak of anything that Christ did not work through me for obedience of nations, in word and deed,
Romans 15:19 in power of signs and wonders, in power of God's Spirit, so that from Jerusalem and around as far as Illyricum I have fulfilled Christ's gospel,
Romans 15:20 and thus aspiring to proclaim the gospel where Christ had not been named, so that I might not build upon another's foundation,
Romans 15:21 but as it is written, “Those to whom it was not announced concerning him will see, and those who have not heard will understand.”
Romans 15:22 Therefore I was also hindered many times from coming to you.
