Romans 15:23 But now, no longer having a place in these regions, and having a longing to come to you for many years,
Romans 15:24 whenever I travel to Spain, I will come to you. For I hope, passing through, to see you and to be sent on there by you, if first I am in part filled with you.
Romans 15:25 But now I travel to Jerusalem, ministering to the saints.
Romans 15:26 For Macedonia and Achaia were pleased to make a contribution for the poor among the saints in Jerusalem.
Romans 15:27 For they were pleased, and they are their debtors. For if the nations shared in their spiritual things, they ought also to serve them in fleshly things.
Romans 15:28 Therefore, having completed this and sealed this fruit to them, I will go away through you to Spain.
Romans 15:29 And I know that when I come to you, I will come in the fullness of the blessing of Christ's gospel.
Romans 15:30 And I urge you, brothers, through our Lord Jesus Christ and through the love of the Spirit, to strive together with me in prayers for me to God,
Romans 15:31 so that I may be rescued from those who disobey in Judea, and so that my ministry to Jerusalem may become acceptable to the saints,
Romans 15:32 so that I may come to you in joy through God's will and find rest together with you.
Romans 15:33 And the God of peace be with you all. Amen.

## Chapter 16

Romans 16:1 And I commend to you Phoebe our sister, who is a minister of the church in Cenchreae,
Romans 16:2 so that you may receive her in the Lord worthily of the saints, and stand by her in whatever matter she may need you; for she herself also became a patron of many and of me myself.
Romans 16:3 Greet Priscilla and Aquila, my fellow workers in Christ Jesus,
Romans 16:4 who laid down their own neck for my life, to whom not only I give thanks, but also all the churches of the nations,
Romans 16:5 and the church in their house. Greet Epaenetus my beloved, who is the firstfruits of Achaia unto Christ.
Romans 16:6 Greet Mariam, who labored much for us.
Romans 16:7 Greet Andronicus and Junia, my kinsmen and fellow captives, who are notable among the apostles, who also have been in Christ before me.
Romans 16:8 Greet Amplias, my beloved in the Lord.
Romans 16:9 Greet Urbanus, our fellow worker in Christ, and Stachys my beloved.
Romans 16:10 Greet Apelles, the approved one in Christ. Greet those of Aristobulus.
Romans 16:11 Greet Herodion my kinsman. Greet those of Narcissus who are in the Lord.
Romans 16:12 Greet Tryphaena and Tryphosa, who labor in the Lord. Greet Persis the beloved, who labored much in the Lord.
Romans 16:13 Greet Rufus, the chosen one in the Lord, and his mother and mine.
Romans 16:14 Greet Asyncritus, Phlegon, Hermas, Patrobas, Hermes, and the brothers with them.
Romans 16:15 Greet Philologus and Julia, Nereus and his sister, and Olympas, and all the saints with them.
Romans 16:16 Greet one another with a holy kiss. The churches of Christ greet you.
Romans 16:17 And I urge you, brothers, to watch those who make divisions and offenses contrary to the teaching you learned, and turn away from them.
Romans 16:18 For such people do not serve as slaves to our Lord Jesus Christ, but to their own belly, and through smooth speech and flattering speech deceive the hearts of the innocent.
Romans 16:19 For your obedience reached all. Therefore I rejoice over you, but I want you to be wise toward good and unmixed toward evil.
Romans 16:20 And the God of peace will crush Satan under your feet shortly. The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with you.
Romans 16:21 Timothy my fellow worker greets you, and Lucius and Jason and Sosipater, my kinsmen.
Romans 16:22 I, Tertius, who wrote the letter, greet you in the Lord.
Romans 16:23 Gaius, my host and that of the whole church, greets you. Erastus, the city's steward, greets you, and Quartus the brother.
Romans 16:24 The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with you all. Amen.
Romans 16:25 And to the one who is able to strengthen you according to my gospel and the proclamation of Jesus Christ, according to revelation of a mystery kept silent in eternal times,
Romans 16:26 but now manifested, and through prophetic writings, according to the command of the eternal God, made known to all the nations for obedience of faith,
Romans 16:27 to the only wise God, through Jesus Christ, to whom be the glory forever. Amen.

# 1 Corinthians

The Apostolic Bible. Public domain. https://apostolic-bible.ysys9.chatgpt.site/license.html


## Chapter 1

1 Corinthians 1:1 Paul, a called apostle of Jesus Christ through God's will, and Sosthenes the brother,
1 Corinthians 1:2 to God's church in Corinth, sanctified in Christ Jesus, called saints, with all who call upon the name of our Lord Jesus Christ in every place, both theirs and ours:
1 Corinthians 1:3 grace to you and peace from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ.
1 Corinthians 1:4 I thank my God always concerning you for God's grace given to you in Christ Jesus,
1 Corinthians 1:5 that in everything you were enriched in him, in every word and all knowledge,
1 Corinthians 1:6 just as Christ's testimony was confirmed among you,
1 Corinthians 1:7 so that you lack no gracious gift, awaiting the revelation of our Lord Jesus Christ,
1 Corinthians 1:8 who will also confirm you until the end, unaccused on the day of our Lord Jesus Christ.
1 Corinthians 1:9 God is faithful, through whom you were called into fellowship of his Son Jesus Christ our Lord.
1 Corinthians 1:10 But I urge you, brothers, through the name of our Lord Jesus Christ, that you all say the same thing and that there be no divisions among you, but that you be fitted together in the same mind and the same judgment.
1 Corinthians 1:11 For it was made clear to me concerning you, my brothers, by those of Chloe, that there are quarrels among you.
1 Corinthians 1:12 And I mean this: each of you says, “I am Paul's,” “I am Apollos's,” “I am Cephas's,” “I am Christ's.”
1 Corinthians 1:13 Has Christ been divided? Was Paul crucified for you? Or were you baptized into Paul's name?
1 Corinthians 1:14 I thank God that I baptized none of you except Crispus and Gaius,
1 Corinthians 1:15 so that no one may say that I baptized into my own name.
1 Corinthians 1:16 And I also baptized Stephanas's household; beyond that I do not know whether I baptized anyone else.
1 Corinthians 1:17 For Christ did not send me to baptize but to proclaim the gospel, not in wisdom of speech, so that Christ's cross might not be emptied.
1 Corinthians 1:18 For the word of the cross is foolishness to those perishing, but to us being saved it is God's power.
1 Corinthians 1:19 For it is written, “I will destroy the wisdom of the wise, and reject the understanding of the understanding.”
1 Corinthians 1:20 Where is the wise one? Where is the scribe? Where is the debater of this age? Did God not make the wisdom of this world foolish?
1 Corinthians 1:21 For since, in God's wisdom, the world did not know God through wisdom, God was pleased through the foolishness of the proclamation to save those who believe.
1 Corinthians 1:22 Since Jews also ask for a sign, and Greeks seek wisdom,
1 Corinthians 1:23 but we preach Christ crucified, an offense to Jews and foolishness to Greeks,
1 Corinthians 1:24 but to the called themselves, both Jews and Greeks, Christ, God's power and God's wisdom.
1 Corinthians 1:25 Because God's foolish thing is wiser than people, and God's weak thing is stronger than people.
1 Corinthians 1:26 For see your calling, brothers, that not many are wise according to flesh, not many powerful, not many wellborn.
1 Corinthians 1:27 But God chose the foolish things of the world to shame the wise, and God chose the weak things of the world to shame the strong things,
1 Corinthians 1:28 and God chose the lowborn things of the world and the despised things and the things that are not, to nullify the things that are,
1 Corinthians 1:29 so that no flesh may boast before him.
1 Corinthians 1:30 But from him you are in Christ Jesus, who became for us wisdom from God, and righteousness and sanctification and redemption,
1 Corinthians 1:31 so that, as it is written, “Let the one who boasts boast in the Lord.”

## Chapter 2

1 Corinthians 2:1 And I, coming to you, brothers, did not come with superiority of speech or wisdom, proclaiming God's testimony to you.
1 Corinthians 2:2 For I decided not to know anything among you except Jesus Christ, and him crucified.
1 Corinthians 2:3 And I was with you in weakness and fear and much trembling.
1 Corinthians 2:4 And my speech and my proclamation were not in persuasive words of human wisdom, but in demonstration of spirit and power,
1 Corinthians 2:5 so that your faith might not be in people's wisdom but in God's power.
1 Corinthians 2:6 But we speak wisdom among the mature, yet wisdom not of this age nor of the rulers of this age who are being nullified,
1 Corinthians 2:7 but we speak God's wisdom in a mystery, the hidden wisdom which God predestined before the ages for our glory,
1 Corinthians 2:8 which none of the rulers of this age has known; for if they had known, they would not have crucified the Lord of glory.
1 Corinthians 2:9 But as it is written, “Things an eye did not see and an ear did not hear and that did not rise upon a man's heart, things God prepared for those who love him.”
1 Corinthians 2:10 But God revealed them to us through his Spirit; for the Spirit searches everything, even God's depths.
1 Corinthians 2:11 For who among people knows a man's things except the man's spirit within him? Thus also no one knows God's things except God's Spirit.
1 Corinthians 2:12 But we received not the world's spirit but the Spirit from God, so that we may know the things freely given us by God,
1 Corinthians 2:13 which we also speak, not in words taught by human wisdom but in those taught by the Holy Spirit, comparing spiritual things with spiritual things.
1 Corinthians 2:14 But a natural man does not receive the things of God's Spirit, for they are foolishness to him, and he cannot know them, because they are examined spiritually.
1 Corinthians 2:15 But the spiritual one examines everything, but he himself is examined by no one.
1 Corinthians 2:16 For who knew the Lord's mind, who will instruct him? But we have Christ's mind.

## Chapter 3

1 Corinthians 3:1 And I, brothers, could not speak to you as spiritual people, but as fleshly people, as infants in Christ.
1 Corinthians 3:2 I gave you milk to drink and not food, for you were not yet able; but neither are you able even now,
1 Corinthians 3:3 for you are still fleshly. For where there are jealousy and strife and divisions among you, are you not fleshly and walking according to man?
1 Corinthians 3:4 For whenever someone says, “I am Paul's,” and another, “I am Apollos's,” are you not fleshly?
1 Corinthians 3:5 Who, then, is Paul, and who is Apollos, but ministers through whom you believed, and to each as the Lord gave?
1 Corinthians 3:6 I planted, Apollos watered, but God gave growth.
1 Corinthians 3:7 So neither the one who plants is anything nor the one who waters, but God who gives growth.
1 Corinthians 3:8 And the one who plants and the one who waters are one, but each will receive his own wage according to his own labor.
1 Corinthians 3:9 For we are God's fellow workers; you are God's cultivated field, God's building.
1 Corinthians 3:10 According to God's grace given to me, as a wise master builder I have laid a foundation, but another builds upon it. But let each watch how he builds upon it.
1 Corinthians 3:11 For no one can lay another foundation besides the one laid, which is Jesus Christ.
1 Corinthians 3:12 But if someone builds upon this foundation gold, silver, precious stones, wood, grass, straw,
1 Corinthians 3:13 each one's work will become manifest, for the day will make it clear, because it is revealed in fire, and the fire will test what sort each one's work is.
1 Corinthians 3:14 If someone's work which he built upon it remains, he will receive a wage.
1 Corinthians 3:15 If someone's work is burned up, he will suffer loss; but he himself will be saved, yet thus as through fire.
1 Corinthians 3:16 Do you not know that you are God's temple and God's Spirit dwells in you?
1 Corinthians 3:17 If someone destroys God's temple, God will destroy this one; for God's temple is holy, which you are.
1 Corinthians 3:18 Let no one deceive himself. If someone among you thinks he is wise in this age, let him become foolish so that he may become wise.
1 Corinthians 3:19 For this world's wisdom is foolishness with God. For it is written, “The one who catches the wise in their cunning,”
1 Corinthians 3:20 and again, “The Lord knows the reasonings of the wise, that they are futile.”
1 Corinthians 3:21 So let no one boast in people, for everything is yours,
1 Corinthians 3:22 whether Paul or Apollos or Cephas or world or life or death or present things or coming things; everything is yours,
1 Corinthians 3:23 and you are Christ's, and Christ is God's.

## Chapter 4

1 Corinthians 4:1 Thus let a man reckon us as servants of Christ and stewards of God's mysteries.
1 Corinthians 4:2 And furthermore it is sought among stewards that one be found faithful.
1 Corinthians 4:3 But to me it is a very small thing that I should be examined by you or by a human day; but neither do I examine myself.
1 Corinthians 4:4 For I am conscious of nothing against myself, but I have not been justified by this; and the one who examines me is the Lord.
1 Corinthians 4:5 So judge nothing before the time, until the Lord comes, who will both illuminate the hidden things of darkness and manifest the counsels of hearts; and then each one's praise will come from God.
1 Corinthians 4:6 And these things, brothers, I transferred in form to myself and Apollos because of you, so that in us you may learn not to think beyond what is written, so that you may not be puffed up, one for the one against the other.
1 Corinthians 4:7 For who distinguishes you? And what do you have that you did not receive? And if you also received it, why do you boast as though not having received?
1 Corinthians 4:8 Already you are filled, already you became rich, apart from us you reigned; and indeed I wish you had reigned, so that we too might reign with you.
1 Corinthians 4:9 For I think God displayed us apostles last, as sentenced to death, because we became a spectacle to the world and to angels and to people.
1 Corinthians 4:10 We are fools because of Christ, but you prudent in Christ; we weak, but you strong; you honored, but we dishonored.
1 Corinthians 4:11 Until this present hour we both hunger and thirst and are poorly clothed and are struck and are without a settled home,
1 Corinthians 4:12 and labor, working with our own hands. Reviled, we bless; persecuted, we bear it;
1 Corinthians 4:13 slandered, we encourage. We became as the world's refuse, everyone's scrapings, until now.
1 Corinthians 4:14 I write these things not to shame you, but admonish you as my beloved children.
1 Corinthians 4:15 For even if you have ten thousand tutors in Christ, yet not many fathers; for in Christ Jesus through the gospel I begot you.
1 Corinthians 4:16 Therefore I urge you, become imitators of me.
1 Corinthians 4:17 For this reason I sent you Timothy, who is my beloved child and faithful in the Lord, who will remind you of my ways in Christ, just as I teach everywhere in every church.
1 Corinthians 4:18 But some were puffed up as though I were not coming to you.
1 Corinthians 4:19 But I will come to you quickly, if the Lord wills, and know not the speech of those puffed up, but the power.
1 Corinthians 4:20 For God's kingdom is not in speech but in power.
1 Corinthians 4:21 What do you want? Should I come to you with a rod, or in love and a spirit of gentleness?

## Chapter 5

1 Corinthians 5:1 Sexual immorality is actually reported among you, and such sexual immorality as is not even named among the nations, that someone has his father's wife.
1 Corinthians 5:2 And you are puffed up, and did not rather mourn, so that the one who did this deed might be removed from your midst.
1 Corinthians 5:3 For I, though absent in body but present in spirit, have already judged, as present, the one who performed this thus,
1 Corinthians 5:4 in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ, when you and my spirit are assembled, with the power of our Lord Jesus Christ,
1 Corinthians 5:5 to hand such a one over to Satan for destruction of the flesh, so that the spirit may be saved on the day of the Lord Jesus.
1 Corinthians 5:6 Your boasting is not good. Do you not know that a little leaven leavens the whole lump?
1 Corinthians 5:7 Therefore clean out the old leaven, so that you may be a new lump, as you are unleavened. For Christ our Passover was also sacrificed for us.
1 Corinthians 5:8 So let us keep the feast, not with old leaven nor with leaven of malice and wickedness, but with unleavened things of sincerity and truth.
1 Corinthians 5:9 I wrote to you in the letter not to mix together with sexually immoral people,
1 Corinthians 5:10 and not altogether with the sexually immoral of this world or the greedy or robbers or idolaters, since then you would have to go out of the world.
1 Corinthians 5:11 But now I wrote to you not to mix together if someone named a brother is sexually immoral or greedy or an idolater or a reviler or a drunkard or a robber, not even to eat with such a one.
1 Corinthians 5:12 For what is it to me to judge those outside also? Do you not judge those inside?
1 Corinthians 5:13 But God judges those outside. And remove the evil one from among yourselves.

## Chapter 6

1 Corinthians 6:1 Does someone among you, having a matter against the other, dare to be judged before the unrighteous and not before the saints?
1 Corinthians 6:2 Do you not know that the saints will judge the world? And if the world is judged by you, are you unworthy of the smallest tribunals?
1 Corinthians 6:3 Do you not know that we will judge angels, let alone matters of life?
1 Corinthians 6:4 Therefore, if you have tribunals concerning matters of life, do you seat those despised in the church?
1 Corinthians 6:5 I say this to your shame. Is there thus no wise one among you, not even one, who will be able to decide between his brother?
1 Corinthians 6:6 But brother goes to judgment with brother, and this before unbelievers.
1 Corinthians 6:7 Therefore there is already altogether a defeat among you, that you have judgments with yourselves. Why not rather be wronged? Why not rather be defrauded?
1 Corinthians 6:8 But you wrong and defraud, and that brothers.
1 Corinthians 6:9 Or do you not know that the unrighteous will not inherit God's kingdom? Do not be deceived: neither sexually immoral people nor idolaters nor adulterers nor effeminate men nor men who bed males,
1 Corinthians 6:10 nor thieves nor greedy people nor drunkards nor revilers nor robbers will inherit God's kingdom.
1 Corinthians 6:11 And some of you were these things; but you washed yourselves, but you were sanctified, but you were justified in the name of the Lord Jesus and in the Spirit of our God.
1 Corinthians 6:12 Everything is permitted to me, but not everything benefits. Everything is permitted to me, but I will not be brought under authority by anything.
1 Corinthians 6:13 Foods for the belly, and the belly for foods, but God will nullify both it and them. But the body is not for sexual immorality but for the Lord, and the Lord for the body.
1 Corinthians 6:14 And God both raised the Lord and will raise us through his power.
1 Corinthians 6:15 Do you not know that your bodies are Christ's members? Therefore, taking Christ's members, will I make them a prostitute's members? May it never be!
1 Corinthians 6:16 Or do you not know that the one who joins himself to the prostitute is one body? For, he says, “The two will be one flesh.”
1 Corinthians 6:17 But the one who joins himself to the Lord is one spirit.
1 Corinthians 6:18 Flee sexual immorality. Every sin that a man does is outside the body, but the sexually immoral one sins against his own body.
1 Corinthians 6:19 Or do you not know that your body is a temple of the Holy Spirit within you, whom you have from God, and you are not your own?
1 Corinthians 6:20 For you were bought at a price. Therefore glorify God in your body and in your spirit, which are God's.

## Chapter 7

1 Corinthians 7:1 And concerning what you wrote to me: it is good for a man not to touch a woman.
1 Corinthians 7:2 But because of sexual immoralities, let each have his own wife, and let each woman have her own husband.
1 Corinthians 7:3 Let the husband repay the wife the goodwill owed, and likewise also the wife the husband.
1 Corinthians 7:4 The wife does not have authority over her own body, but the husband; and likewise the husband also does not have authority over his own body, but the wife.
1 Corinthians 7:5 Do not deprive one another, except perhaps by agreement for a time, so that you may devote yourselves to fasting and prayer, and come together again, so that Satan may not tempt you because of your lack of self-control.
1 Corinthians 7:6 But I say this by concession, not by command.
1 Corinthians 7:7 For I want all people to be as myself also; but each has his own gracious gift from God, one thus, another thus.
1 Corinthians 7:8 And I say to the unmarried and the widows, it is good for them if they remain as I also am.
1 Corinthians 7:9 But if they do not exercise self-control, let them marry; for it is better to marry than to burn.
1 Corinthians 7:10 But to the married I command, not I but the Lord, that a wife not separate from a husband,
1 Corinthians 7:11 but if she does separate, let her remain unmarried or be reconciled to the husband, and that a husband not leave a wife.
1 Corinthians 7:12 But to the rest I say, not the Lord: if some brother has an unbelieving wife and she agrees to dwell with him, let him not leave her.
1 Corinthians 7:13 And a woman who has an unbelieving husband, and he agrees to dwell with her, let her not leave him.
1 Corinthians 7:14 For the unbelieving husband has been sanctified in the wife, and the unbelieving wife has been sanctified in the husband; otherwise your children are unclean, but now they are holy.
1 Corinthians 7:15 But if the unbeliever separates, let him separate. The brother or sister has not been enslaved in such things; but God has called us in peace.
1 Corinthians 7:16 For how do you know, wife, whether you will save the husband? Or how do you know, husband, whether you will save the wife?
1 Corinthians 7:17 Only, as God apportioned to each, as the Lord has called each, thus let him walk. And thus I direct in all the churches.
1 Corinthians 7:18 Was someone called circumcised? Let him not draw the foreskin over. Was someone called in uncircumcision? Let him not be circumcised.
1 Corinthians 7:19 Circumcision is nothing, and uncircumcision is nothing, but keeping God's commandments.
1 Corinthians 7:20 Let each remain in the calling in which he was called.
1 Corinthians 7:21 Were you called a slave? Do not let it concern you; but if you can also become free, rather make use of it.
1 Corinthians 7:22 For the slave called in the Lord is the Lord's freedman; likewise also the free one called is Christ's slave.
1 Corinthians 7:23 You were bought at a price; do not become slaves of people.
1 Corinthians 7:24 Brothers, let each remain with God in that in which he was called.
1 Corinthians 7:25 And concerning virgins, I have no command of the Lord, but give judgment as one who has received mercy from the Lord to be faithful.
1 Corinthians 7:26 Therefore I consider this to be good because of the present necessity, that it is good for a man to be thus.
1 Corinthians 7:27 Have you been bound to a wife? Do not seek release. Have you been released from a wife? Do not seek a wife.
1 Corinthians 7:28 But even if you marry, you did not sin; and if the virgin marries, she did not sin. But such will have affliction in the flesh, and I spare you.
1 Corinthians 7:29 But I say this, brothers: the time has been shortened; henceforth, so that even those who have wives may be as not having,
1 Corinthians 7:30 and those who weep as not weeping, and those who rejoice as not rejoicing, and those who buy as not possessing,
1 Corinthians 7:31 and those who use this world as not using it fully; for the form of this world passes away.
1 Corinthians 7:32 But I want you to be without anxiety. The unmarried one is anxious about the Lord's things, how he will please the Lord,
1 Corinthians 7:33 but the married one is anxious about the world's things, how he will please the wife.
1 Corinthians 7:34 The wife and the virgin are distinguished. The unmarried woman is anxious about the Lord's things, so that she may be holy both in body and in spirit; but the married woman is anxious about the world's things, how she will please the husband.
1 Corinthians 7:35 But I say this for your own benefit, not to cast a noose upon you, but for propriety and devoted attendance upon the Lord without distraction.
1 Corinthians 7:36 But if someone thinks he behaves indecently toward his virgin, if she is past her prime and it ought to happen thus, let him do what he wants; he does not sin; let them marry.
1 Corinthians 7:37 But the one who stands firm in his heart, having no necessity, but has authority concerning his own will, and has judged this in his heart, to keep his own virgin, does well.
1 Corinthians 7:38 So also the one who gives in marriage does well, but the one who does not give in marriage does better.
1 Corinthians 7:39 A wife is bound by law for as long as her husband lives; but if her husband falls asleep, she is free to be married to whom she wants, only in the Lord.
1 Corinthians 7:40 But she is more blessed if she remains thus, according to my judgment; and I think I too have God's Spirit.

## Chapter 8

1 Corinthians 8:1 And concerning things sacrificed to idols, we know that we all have knowledge. Knowledge puffs up, but love builds up.
1 Corinthians 8:2 But if someone thinks he knows something, he has not yet known anything as he ought to know.
1 Corinthians 8:3 But if someone loves God, this one has been known by him.
1 Corinthians 8:4 Therefore concerning the eating of things sacrificed to idols, we know that an idol is nothing in the world, and that there is no other God except one.
1 Corinthians 8:5 For even if there are so-called gods, whether in heaven or upon earth, as there are many gods and many lords,
1 Corinthians 8:6 yet for us one God, the Father, from whom are all things and we unto him, and one Lord, Jesus Christ, through whom are all things and we through him.
1 Corinthians 8:7 But knowledge is not in everyone; and some, with consciousness of the idol until now, eat as a thing sacrificed to an idol, and their conscience, being weak, is defiled.
1 Corinthians 8:8 But food does not present us to God; for neither if we eat do we abound, nor if we do not eat do we lack.
1 Corinthians 8:9 But watch lest this authority of yours become a stumbling block to the weak.
1 Corinthians 8:10 For if someone sees you who have knowledge reclining in an idol's temple, will not his conscience, being weak, be built up to eat things sacrificed to idols?
1 Corinthians 8:11 And the weak brother will perish upon your knowledge, for whom Christ died.
1 Corinthians 8:12 And thus, sinning against the brothers and striking their weak conscience, you sin against Christ.
1 Corinthians 8:13 Therefore, if food offends my brother, I will certainly never eat meat, so that I may not offend my brother.

## Chapter 9

1 Corinthians 9:1 Am I not an apostle? Am I not free? Have I not seen Jesus Christ our Lord? Are you not my work in the Lord?
1 Corinthians 9:2 If to others I am not an apostle, yet indeed to you I am; for you are the seal of my apostleship in the Lord.
1 Corinthians 9:3 My defense to those who examine me is this:
1 Corinthians 9:4 Do we not have authority to eat and drink?
1 Corinthians 9:5 Do we not have authority to take along a sister as wife, as also the other apostles and the Lord's brothers and Cephas?
1 Corinthians 9:6 Or do only I and Barnabas not have authority not to work?
1 Corinthians 9:7 Who ever serves as a soldier at his own wages? Who plants a vineyard and does not eat from its fruit? Or who shepherds a flock and does not eat from the flock's milk?
1 Corinthians 9:8 Do I speak these things according to man? Or does not the law also say these things?
1 Corinthians 9:9 For in Moses's law it is written, “You shall not muzzle an ox threshing.” Is God concerned about oxen?
1 Corinthians 9:10 Or does he speak altogether for us? For it was written for us, that the plower ought to plow upon hope, and the thresher to share in his hope upon hope.
1 Corinthians 9:11 If we sowed spiritual things for you, is it a great thing if we reap your fleshly things?
1 Corinthians 9:12 If others share in authority over you, do not we more? But we did not use this authority, but bear everything so that we may give no hindrance to Christ's gospel.
1 Corinthians 9:13 Do you not know that those who work the sacred things eat from the sacred place, and those who attend the altar share with the altar?
1 Corinthians 9:14 Thus the Lord also directed those who proclaim the gospel to live from the gospel.
1 Corinthians 9:15 But I used none of these things. And I did not write these things so that it might happen thus for me; for it is better for me to die than for someone to empty my boast.
1 Corinthians 9:16 For if I proclaim the gospel, I have no boast; for necessity lies upon me, and woe is mine if I do not proclaim the gospel.
1 Corinthians 9:17 For if willingly I practice this, I have a wage; but if unwillingly, I have been entrusted with a stewardship.
1 Corinthians 9:18 What, then, is my wage? That, proclaiming the gospel, I may offer Christ's gospel without expense, so as not to use fully my authority in the gospel.
1 Corinthians 9:19 For being free from all, I enslaved myself to all so that I may gain the more.
1 Corinthians 9:20 And to the Jews I became as a Jew so that I may gain Jews; to those under law as under law so that I may gain those under law;
1 Corinthians 9:21 to those without law as without law, not being without law to God but within law to Christ, so that I may gain those without law.
1 Corinthians 9:22 To the weak I became as weak so that I may gain the weak. To all I have become all things so that by all means I may save some.
1 Corinthians 9:23 And I do this because of the gospel, so that I may become a fellow sharer of it.
1 Corinthians 9:24 Do you not know that those running in a stadium all run, but one receives the prize? Run thus so that you may obtain it.
1 Corinthians 9:25 And everyone who competes exercises self-control in everything; they, therefore, to receive a corruptible crown, but we an incorruptible.
1 Corinthians 9:26 Therefore I run thus, as not uncertainly; I box thus, as not beating air,
1 Corinthians 9:27 but I batter my body and enslave it, lest, having preached to others, I myself become disapproved.

## Chapter 10

1 Corinthians 10:1 But I do not want you to be ignorant, brothers, that our fathers were all under the cloud and all passed through the sea,
1 Corinthians 10:2 and all were baptized into Moses in the cloud and in the sea,
1 Corinthians 10:3 and all ate the same spiritual food,
1 Corinthians 10:4 and all drank the same spiritual drink; for they drank from a spiritual rock following them, and the rock was Christ.
1 Corinthians 10:5 But God was not pleased with most of them, for they were strewn in the wilderness.
1 Corinthians 10:6 And these things became patterns for us, so that we may not be desirers of evil things, as those also desired.
1 Corinthians 10:7 Nor become idolaters, as some of them, as it is written, “The people sat down to eat and drink, and rose to play.”
1 Corinthians 10:8 Nor let us commit sexual immorality, as some of them committed sexual immorality, and twenty-three thousand fell in one day.
1 Corinthians 10:9 Nor let us test Christ, as some of them also tested him, and perished by the serpents.
1 Corinthians 10:10 Nor grumble, as some of them also grumbled and perished by the destroyer.
1 Corinthians 10:11 And all these things happened to them as patterns, and were written for our admonition, to whom the ends of the ages have come.
1 Corinthians 10:12 So let the one who thinks he stands watch lest he fall.
1 Corinthians 10:13 No temptation has taken you except a human one; but God is faithful, who will not allow you to be tempted beyond what you can bear, but will also make the way out with the temptation, so that you may be able to endure.
1 Corinthians 10:14 Therefore, my beloved, flee from idolatry.
1 Corinthians 10:15 I speak as to prudent people; judge yourselves what I say.
1 Corinthians 10:16 The cup of blessing which we bless, is it not fellowship of Christ's blood? The bread which we break, is it not fellowship of Christ's body?
1 Corinthians 10:17 Because there is one bread, we the many are one body; for we all share from the one bread.
1 Corinthians 10:18 See Israel according to flesh: are not those who eat the sacrifices sharers of the altar?
1 Corinthians 10:19 What, then, do I say? That an idol is anything, or that a thing sacrificed to an idol is anything?
1 Corinthians 10:20 But that what the nations sacrifice, they sacrifice to demons and not to God; and I do not want you to become sharers of demons.
1 Corinthians 10:21 You cannot drink the Lord's cup and demons' cup; you cannot share in the Lord's table and demons' table.
1 Corinthians 10:22 Or do we provoke the Lord to jealousy? Are we stronger than he?
1 Corinthians 10:23 Everything is permitted to me, but not everything benefits; everything is permitted to me, but not everything builds up.
1 Corinthians 10:24 Let no one seek his own, but each the other's.
1 Corinthians 10:25 Eat everything sold in the meat market, examining nothing because of conscience,
1 Corinthians 10:26 for “The earth is the Lord's, and its fullness.”
1 Corinthians 10:27 And if someone of the unbelievers invites you and you want to go, eat everything set before you, examining nothing because of conscience.
1 Corinthians 10:28 But if someone says to you, “This is sacrificed to an idol,” do not eat, because of that one who disclosed it and conscience; for “The earth is the Lord's, and its fullness.”
1 Corinthians 10:29 And I mean conscience, not one's own but the other's. For why is my freedom judged by another conscience?
1 Corinthians 10:30 But if I partake with thanks, why am I slandered for that for which I give thanks?
1 Corinthians 10:31 Therefore, whether you eat or drink or do anything, do everything unto God's glory.
1 Corinthians 10:32 Become without offense both to Jews and Greeks and to God's church,
1 Corinthians 10:33 just as I too please all in everything, not seeking my own benefit but that of the many, so that they may be saved.

## Chapter 11

1 Corinthians 11:1 Become imitators of me, just as I also of Christ.
1 Corinthians 11:2 And I praise you, brothers, that you remember me in everything and hold the traditions just as I handed them over to you.
1 Corinthians 11:3 But I want you to know that Christ is the head of every man, and the man the head of a woman, and God the head of Christ.
1 Corinthians 11:4 Every man praying or prophesying with something down over his head shames his head.
1 Corinthians 11:5 But every woman praying or prophesying with her head uncovered shames her own head; for it is one and the same with the shaved woman.
1 Corinthians 11:6 For if a woman is not covered, let her also be shorn; but if it is shameful for a woman to be shorn or shaved, let her be covered.
1 Corinthians 11:7 For a man ought not to cover his head, being God's image and glory; but the woman is man's glory.
1 Corinthians 11:8 For man is not from woman, but woman from man;
1 Corinthians 11:9 for neither was man created because of the woman, but woman because of the man.
1 Corinthians 11:10 For this reason the woman ought to have authority upon her head because of the angels.
1 Corinthians 11:11 Nevertheless, neither man apart from woman nor woman apart from man in the Lord.
1 Corinthians 11:12 For just as the woman is from the man, so also the man through the woman, but all things from God.
1 Corinthians 11:13 Judge among yourselves: is it fitting for a woman to pray to God uncovered?
1 Corinthians 11:14 Or does not nature itself teach you that if a man has long hair, it is dishonor to him,
1 Corinthians 11:15 but if a woman has long hair, it is glory to her, because the hair has been given to her instead of a covering?
1 Corinthians 11:16 But if someone thinks to be contentious, we have no such custom, nor God's churches.
1 Corinthians 11:17 But in commanding this I do not praise you, because you assemble not for the better but for the worse.
1 Corinthians 11:18 For first, when you assemble in the church, I hear that divisions exist among you, and in some part I believe it.
1 Corinthians 11:19 For there must also be factions among you, so that the approved may become manifest among you.
1 Corinthians 11:20 Therefore, when you assemble together, it is not to eat the Lord's supper.
1 Corinthians 11:21 For each takes his own supper beforehand in eating, and one is hungry, but another is drunk.
1 Corinthians 11:22 For do you not have houses for eating and drinking? Or do you despise God's church and shame those who have nothing? What should I say to you? Will I praise you in this? I do not praise you.
1 Corinthians 11:23 For I received from the Lord what I also handed over to you, that the Lord Jesus, on the night in which he was handed over, took bread,
1 Corinthians 11:24 and having given thanks, broke it and said, “Take, eat; this is my body, broken for you; do this for my remembrance.”
1 Corinthians 11:25 Likewise also the cup after supping, saying, “This cup is the new covenant in my blood; do this, as often as you drink, for my remembrance.”
1 Corinthians 11:26 For as often as you eat this bread and drink this cup, you proclaim the Lord's death until he comes.
1 Corinthians 11:27 So whoever eats this bread or drinks the Lord's cup unworthily will be guilty of the Lord's body and blood.
1 Corinthians 11:28 But let a man examine himself, and thus let him eat from the bread and drink from the cup.
1 Corinthians 11:29 For the one who eats and drinks unworthily eats and drinks judgment to himself, not discerning the Lord's body.
1 Corinthians 11:30 Because of this many among you are weak and sick, and quite a few sleep.
1 Corinthians 11:31 For if we discerned ourselves, we would not be judged.
1 Corinthians 11:32 But being judged by the Lord, we are disciplined, so that we may not be condemned with the world.
1 Corinthians 11:33 So, my brothers, when assembling to eat, wait for one another.
1 Corinthians 11:34 But if someone is hungry, let him eat at home, so that you may not assemble unto judgment; and the remaining things I will direct when I come.

## Chapter 12

1 Corinthians 12:1 And concerning spiritual things, brothers, I do not want you to be ignorant.
1 Corinthians 12:2 You know that you were nations, carried away to the voiceless idols however you were led.
1 Corinthians 12:3 Therefore I make known to you that no one speaking in God's Spirit says, “Jesus accursed,” and no one can say, “Jesus Lord,” except in the Holy Spirit.
1 Corinthians 12:4 And there are varieties of gracious gifts, but the same Spirit,
1 Corinthians 12:5 and varieties of ministries, and the same Lord,
1 Corinthians 12:6 and varieties of workings, but the same God who works all things in all.
1 Corinthians 12:7 And to each is given the manifestation of the Spirit for benefit.
1 Corinthians 12:8 For to one through the Spirit is given a word of wisdom, and to another a word of knowledge according to the same Spirit,
1 Corinthians 12:9 and to another faith in the same Spirit, and to another gracious gifts of healings in the same Spirit,
1 Corinthians 12:10 and to another workings of powers, and to another prophecy, and to another discernings of spirits, and to another kinds of tongues, and to another interpretation of tongues.
1 Corinthians 12:11 And all these the one and the same Spirit works, distributing individually to each just as he wills.
1 Corinthians 12:12 For just as the body is one and has many members, and all the members of the one body, being many, are one body, so also Christ.
1 Corinthians 12:13 For also in one Spirit we all were baptized into one body, whether Jews or Greeks, whether slaves or free, and all were given one Spirit to drink.
1 Corinthians 12:14 For also the body is not one member but many.
1 Corinthians 12:15 If the foot says, “Because I am not a hand, I am not of the body,” it is not on this account not of the body.
1 Corinthians 12:16 And if the ear says, “Because I am not an eye, I am not of the body,” it is not on this account not of the body.
1 Corinthians 12:17 If the whole body were an eye, where the hearing? If the whole hearing, where the smelling?
1 Corinthians 12:18 But now God placed the members, each one of them, in the body just as he wanted.
1 Corinthians 12:19 But if all were one member, where the body?
1 Corinthians 12:20 But now many members, yet one body.
1 Corinthians 12:21 And the eye cannot say to the hand, “I have no need of you,” or again the head to the feet, “I have no need of you.”
1 Corinthians 12:22 But much rather the members of the body that seem to be weaker are necessary,
1 Corinthians 12:23 and those we think to be less honorable of the body, upon these we put more abundant honor, and our indecent parts have more abundant decency,
1 Corinthians 12:24 but our decent parts have no need. But God blended the body together, giving more abundant honor to the lacking part,
1 Corinthians 12:25 so that there may be no division in the body, but the members may have the same concern for one another.
1 Corinthians 12:26 And whether one member suffers, all the members suffer together; or one member is glorified, all the members rejoice together.
1 Corinthians 12:27 But you are Christ's body, and members individually.
1 Corinthians 12:28 And God placed some in the church: first apostles, second prophets, third teachers, then powers, then gracious gifts of healings, helps, governings, kinds of tongues.
1 Corinthians 12:29 Are all apostles? Are all prophets? Are all teachers? Are all powers?
1 Corinthians 12:30 Do all have gracious gifts of healings? Do all speak in tongues? Do all interpret?
1 Corinthians 12:31 But be zealous for the better gracious gifts; and I show you a way beyond measure.

## Chapter 13

1 Corinthians 13:1 If I speak in the tongues of people and angels but have no love, I have become sounding bronze or a clanging cymbal.
1 Corinthians 13:2 And if I have prophecy and know all mysteries and all knowledge, and if I have all faith so as to move mountains, but have no love, I am nothing.
1 Corinthians 13:3 And if I distribute all my possessions as food, and if I hand over my body so that I may be burned, but have no love, I benefit nothing.
1 Corinthians 13:4 Love is patient, love acts kindly; love is not jealous, does not boast, is not puffed up,
1 Corinthians 13:5 does not behave indecently, does not seek its own things, is not provoked, does not reckon the evil,
1 Corinthians 13:6 does not rejoice over unrighteousness, but rejoices together with the truth;
1 Corinthians 13:7 bears everything, believes everything, hopes everything, endures everything.
1 Corinthians 13:8 Love never falls away; but whether prophecies, they will be nullified; whether tongues, they will cease; whether knowledge, it will be nullified.
1 Corinthians 13:9 For we know in part and prophesy in part,
1 Corinthians 13:10 but when the perfect comes, then the partial will be nullified.
1 Corinthians 13:11 When I was an infant, I spoke as an infant, thought as an infant, reasoned as an infant; but when I have become a man, I have nullified the infant's things.
1 Corinthians 13:12 For now we see through a mirror in a riddle, but then face to face; now I know in part, but then I will know fully, just as I also was fully known.
1 Corinthians 13:13 But now faith, hope, love remain, these three; but greater than these is love.

## Chapter 14

1 Corinthians 14:1 Pursue love, and be zealous for spiritual things, but rather that you may prophesy.
1 Corinthians 14:2 For the one speaking in a tongue speaks not to people but to God, for no one hears, but in spirit he speaks mysteries.
1 Corinthians 14:3 But the one prophesying speaks to people building up and encouragement and consolation.
1 Corinthians 14:4 The one speaking in a tongue builds himself up, but the one prophesying builds up a church.
1 Corinthians 14:5 And I want you all to speak in tongues, but rather that you may prophesy; for greater is the one prophesying than the one speaking in tongues, unless he interprets, so that the church may receive building up.
1 Corinthians 14:6 But now, brothers, if I come to you speaking in tongues, what will I benefit you unless I speak to you either in revelation or knowledge or prophecy or teaching?
1 Corinthians 14:7 Even lifeless things giving a sound, whether flute or lyre, if they do not give a distinction in the notes, how will what is played on the flute or lyre be known?
1 Corinthians 14:8 For also if a trumpet gives an unclear sound, who will prepare for war?
1 Corinthians 14:9 Thus you too, unless through the tongue you give a clear word, how will what is spoken be known? For you will be speaking into air.
1 Corinthians 14:10 There are, perhaps, so many kinds of sounds in the world, and none of them voiceless.
1 Corinthians 14:11 Therefore, if I do not know the force of the sound, I will be a barbarian to the one speaking, and the one speaking a barbarian to me.
1 Corinthians 14:12 Thus you too, since you are zealous for spirits, seek to abound toward building up the church.
1 Corinthians 14:13 Therefore let the one speaking in a tongue pray that he may interpret.
1 Corinthians 14:14 For if I pray in a tongue, my spirit prays, but my mind is fruitless.
1 Corinthians 14:15 What, then, is it? I will pray with the spirit, but also pray with the mind; I will sing with the spirit, but also sing with the mind.
1 Corinthians 14:16 Otherwise, if you bless with the spirit, how will the one filling the place of the untrained say the Amen at your thanksgiving, since he does not know what you say?
1 Corinthians 14:17 For you indeed give thanks well, but the other is not built up.
1 Corinthians 14:18 I thank my God, speaking in tongues more than all of you;
1 Corinthians 14:19 but in church I want to speak five words through my mind, so that I may also instruct others, rather than ten thousand words in a tongue.
1 Corinthians 14:20 Brothers, do not become children in understanding, but be infants in malice, and become mature in understanding.
1 Corinthians 14:21 In the law it is written, “In other tongues and in other lips I will speak to this people, and not even thus will they listen to me, says the Lord.”
1 Corinthians 14:22 So tongues are for a sign, not to believers but to unbelievers, but prophecy not to unbelievers but to believers.
1 Corinthians 14:23 Therefore, if the whole church assembles together and all speak in tongues, and untrained people or unbelievers enter, will they not say that you are mad?
1 Corinthians 14:24 But if all prophesy, and some unbeliever or untrained person enters, he is convicted by all, examined by all,
1 Corinthians 14:25 and thus the hidden things of his heart become manifest, and thus, falling upon his face, he will worship God, announcing that God really is among you.
1 Corinthians 14:26 What, then, is it, brothers? Whenever you assemble, each of you has a psalm, has a teaching, has a tongue, has a revelation, has an interpretation; let everything happen for building up.
1 Corinthians 14:27 If someone speaks in a tongue, by two or at most three, and in turn, and let one interpret.
1 Corinthians 14:28 But if there is no interpreter, let him be silent in church, but speak to himself and to God.
1 Corinthians 14:29 And let two or three prophets speak, and let the others discern.
1 Corinthians 14:30 But if it is revealed to another sitting, let the first be silent.
1 Corinthians 14:31 For you can all prophesy one by one, so that all may learn and all be encouraged.
1 Corinthians 14:32 And prophets' spirits submit to prophets.
1 Corinthians 14:33 For God is not of disorder but of peace, as in all the churches of the saints.
1 Corinthians 14:34 Let your women be silent in the churches; for it has not been permitted them to speak, but to submit, as the law also says.
1 Corinthians 14:35 But if they want to learn anything, let them ask their own husbands at home; for it is shameful for women to speak in church.
1 Corinthians 14:36 Or did God's word go out from you? Or did it reach you alone?
1 Corinthians 14:37 If someone thinks he is a prophet or spiritual, let him acknowledge that what I write to you are the Lord's commandments.
1 Corinthians 14:38 But if someone is ignorant, let him be ignorant.
1 Corinthians 14:39 So, brothers, be zealous to prophesy, and do not prevent speaking in tongues.
1 Corinthians 14:40 Let everything happen decently and according to order.

## Chapter 15

1 Corinthians 15:1 And I make known to you, brothers, the gospel which I proclaimed to you, which you also received, in which you also stand,
1 Corinthians 15:2 through which you are also saved, if you hold to the word with which I proclaimed it to you, unless you believed in vain.
1 Corinthians 15:3 For I handed over to you among the first things what I also received, that Christ died for our sins according to the writings,
1 Corinthians 15:4 and that he was buried, and that he has been raised on the third day according to the writings,
1 Corinthians 15:5 and that he appeared to Cephas, then to the twelve,
1 Corinthians 15:6 then appeared to above five hundred brothers at once, of whom most remain until now, but some also fell asleep,
1 Corinthians 15:7 then appeared to James, then to all the apostles,
1 Corinthians 15:8 and last of all, as to the aborted one, he appeared to me also.
1 Corinthians 15:9 For I am the least of the apostles, who am not fit to be called an apostle, because I persecuted God's church.
1 Corinthians 15:10 But by God's grace I am what I am, and his grace toward me did not become empty, but I labored more abundantly than them all; yet not I, but God's grace with me.
1 Corinthians 15:11 Therefore, whether I or they, thus we preach, and thus you believed.
1 Corinthians 15:12 But if Christ is preached that he has been raised from the dead, how do some among you say that there is no resurrection of the dead?
1 Corinthians 15:13 But if there is no resurrection of the dead, neither has Christ been raised.
1 Corinthians 15:14 And if Christ has not been raised, then our proclamation is empty, and your faith also empty.
1 Corinthians 15:15 And we are also found false witnesses of God, because we testified against God that he raised Christ, whom he did not raise, if indeed the dead are not raised.
1 Corinthians 15:16 For if the dead are not raised, neither has Christ been raised.
1 Corinthians 15:17 And if Christ has not been raised, your faith is futile; you are still in your sins.
1 Corinthians 15:18 Then those who fell asleep in Christ also perished.
1 Corinthians 15:19 If in this life only we have hoped in Christ, we are more pitiable than all people.
1 Corinthians 15:20 But now Christ has been raised from the dead; he became firstfruits of those who have fallen asleep.
1 Corinthians 15:21 For since through man came death, also through man resurrection of the dead.
1 Corinthians 15:22 For just as in Adam all die, so also in Christ all will be made alive.
1 Corinthians 15:23 But each in his own order: Christ firstfruits, then those of Christ at his coming,
1 Corinthians 15:24 then the end, when he hands over the kingdom to God and Father, when he nullifies every rule and every authority and power.
1 Corinthians 15:25 For he must reign until he places all the enemies under his feet.
1 Corinthians 15:26 The last enemy nullified is death.
1 Corinthians 15:27 For he subjected all things under his feet; but when he says that all things have been subjected, it is clear that the one who subjected all things to him is excepted.
1 Corinthians 15:28 But when all things are subjected to him, then the Son himself also will be subjected to the one who subjected all things to him, so that God may be all things in all.
1 Corinthians 15:29 Otherwise, what will those baptized for the dead do? If the dead are not raised at all, why are they also baptized for the dead?
1 Corinthians 15:30 Why do we also face danger every hour?
1 Corinthians 15:31 Daily I die, by our boasting which I have in Christ Jesus our Lord.
1 Corinthians 15:32 If according to man I fought beasts in Ephesus, what is the benefit to me? If the dead are not raised, let us eat and drink, for tomorrow we die.
1 Corinthians 15:33 Do not be deceived: bad associations corrupt good habits.
1 Corinthians 15:34 Become sober righteously and do not sin; for some have ignorance of God; I say this to your shame.
1 Corinthians 15:35 But someone will say, “How are the dead raised? And with what sort of body do they come?”
1 Corinthians 15:36 Fool, what you sow is not made alive unless it dies.
1 Corinthians 15:37 And what you sow, you do not sow the body that will become, but a bare grain, perhaps of wheat or of some of the others.
1 Corinthians 15:38 But God gives it a body just as he wanted, and to each of the seeds its own body.
1 Corinthians 15:39 Not all flesh is the same flesh, but one flesh of people, another flesh of livestock, another of fish, another of birds.
1 Corinthians 15:40 And heavenly bodies and earthly bodies, but different is the glory of the heavenly and different that of the earthly.
1 Corinthians 15:41 One glory of sun, and another glory of moon, and another glory of stars; for star differs from star in glory.
1 Corinthians 15:42 Thus also the resurrection of the dead: it is sown in corruption, raised in incorruptibility;
1 Corinthians 15:43 sown in dishonor, raised in glory; sown in weakness, raised in power;
1 Corinthians 15:44 sown a natural body, raised a spiritual body. There is a natural body, and there is a spiritual body.
1 Corinthians 15:45 Thus it is also written, “The first man Adam became a living soul”; the last Adam a life-giving spirit.
1 Corinthians 15:46 But the spiritual is not first, but the natural, then the spiritual.
1 Corinthians 15:47 The first man from earth, made of dust; the second man, the Lord from heaven.
1 Corinthians 15:48 As the one of dust, such also those of dust; and as the heavenly one, such also the heavenly ones.
1 Corinthians 15:49 And just as we bore the image of the one of dust, we will also bear the image of the heavenly one.
1 Corinthians 15:50 But I say this, brothers, that flesh and blood cannot inherit God's kingdom, nor does corruption inherit incorruptibility.
1 Corinthians 15:51 Look, I tell you a mystery: we will not all sleep, but we will all be changed,
1 Corinthians 15:52 in an instant, in a blink of an eye, at the last trumpet; for it will sound, and the dead will be raised incorruptible, and we will be changed.
1 Corinthians 15:53 For this corruptible must put on incorruptibility, and this mortal put on immortality.
1 Corinthians 15:54 But when this corruptible puts on incorruptibility and this mortal puts on immortality, then will come the word that is written, “Death was swallowed unto victory.”
1 Corinthians 15:55 Where, death, is your sting? Where, Hades, is your victory?
1 Corinthians 15:56 And the sting of death is sin, and the power of sin the law.
1 Corinthians 15:57 But thanks to God who gives us the victory through our Lord Jesus Christ.
1 Corinthians 15:58 So, my beloved brothers, become firm, immovable, always abounding in the Lord's work, knowing that your labor is not empty in the Lord.

## Chapter 16

1 Corinthians 16:1 And concerning the collection for the saints, just as I directed the churches of Galatia, so you too do.
1 Corinthians 16:2 On the first of the week, let each of you lay aside with himself, storing up whatever he prospers in, so that collections may not happen then when I come.
1 Corinthians 16:3 And when I arrive, whomever you approve, these I will send through letters to carry your gift to Jerusalem.
1 Corinthians 16:4 But if it is worthy for me also to go, they will go with me.
1 Corinthians 16:5 And I will come to you when I pass through Macedonia, for I am passing through Macedonia.
1 Corinthians 16:6 And perhaps I will remain with you or even winter, so that you may send me onward wherever I go.
1 Corinthians 16:7 For I do not want to see you now in passing, but hope to remain with you some time, if the Lord permits.
1 Corinthians 16:8 But I remain in Ephesus until Pentecost.
1 Corinthians 16:9 For a great and effective door has opened for me, and many opponents.
1 Corinthians 16:10 And if Timothy comes, watch that he may be with you without fear, for he works the Lord's work, as I also do.
1 Corinthians 16:11 Therefore let no one despise him, but send him onward in peace so that he may come to me, for I await him with the brothers.
1 Corinthians 16:12 And concerning Apollos the brother, I urged him much to come to you with the brothers, and it was altogether not his will to come now, but he will come when he has opportunity.
1 Corinthians 16:13 Keep watch, stand in the faith, act as men, be strengthened.
1 Corinthians 16:14 Let all your things happen in love.
1 Corinthians 16:15 And I urge you, brothers—you know Stephanas's household, that it is firstfruits of Achaia, and they appointed themselves to ministry to the saints—
1 Corinthians 16:16 that you too submit to such people and to everyone working together and laboring.
1 Corinthians 16:17 And I rejoice at the presence of Stephanas and Fortunatus and Achaicus, because these filled up your lack.
1 Corinthians 16:18 For they refreshed my spirit and yours; therefore acknowledge such people.
1 Corinthians 16:19 The churches of Asia greet you. Aquila and Priscilla greet you much in the Lord, with the church in their house.
1 Corinthians 16:20 All the brothers greet you. Greet one another with a holy kiss.
1 Corinthians 16:21 The greeting by my own hand, Paul's.
1 Corinthians 16:22 If someone does not love the Lord Jesus Christ, let him be accursed. Maran atha.
1 Corinthians 16:23 The grace of the Lord Jesus Christ be with you.
1 Corinthians 16:24 My love be with all of you in Christ Jesus. Amen.

# 2 Corinthians

The Apostolic Bible. Public domain. https://apostolic-bible.ysys9.chatgpt.site/license.html


## Chapter 1

2 Corinthians 1:1 Paul, an apostle of Jesus Christ through God's will, and Timothy the brother, to God's church in Corinth, with all the saints in all Achaia:
2 Corinthians 1:2 grace to you and peace from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ.
2 Corinthians 1:3 Blessed is the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, the Father of compassions and God of all encouragement,
2 Corinthians 1:4 who encourages us in all our affliction, so that we may be able to encourage those in every affliction through the encouragement with which we ourselves are encouraged by God.
2 Corinthians 1:5 Because just as Christ's sufferings abound toward us, so through Christ our encouragement also abounds.
2 Corinthians 1:6 And whether we are afflicted, it is for your encouragement and salvation, which works in endurance of the same sufferings that we also suffer; or whether we are encouraged, it is for your encouragement and salvation, and our hope is firm concerning you,
2 Corinthians 1:7 knowing that just as you are sharers of the sufferings, so also of the encouragement.
2 Corinthians 1:8 For we do not want you to be ignorant, brothers, concerning our affliction that happened to us in Asia, that we were burdened exceedingly, beyond power, so that we despaired even of living.
2 Corinthians 1:9 But we ourselves have had the sentence of death within ourselves, so that we may not trust in ourselves but in God who raises the dead,
2 Corinthians 1:10 who rescued us from so great a death and rescues, in whom we have hoped that he will also still rescue,
2 Corinthians 1:11 you also helping together for us in petition, so that the gracious gift toward us from many persons may be thanked for by many on our behalf.
2 Corinthians 1:12 For our boasting is this, the testimony of our conscience, that in simplicity and sincerity of God, not in fleshly wisdom but in God's grace, we conducted ourselves in the world, and more abundantly toward you.
2 Corinthians 1:13 For we write no other things to you than what you read or also acknowledge, and I hope that you will also acknowledge until the end,
2 Corinthians 1:14 just as you also acknowledged us in part, that we are your boast, just as you also ours on the day of the Lord Jesus.
2 Corinthians 1:15 And in this confidence I intended to come to you earlier, so that you might have a second grace,
2 Corinthians 1:16 and pass through you to Macedonia, and again from Macedonia come to you, and be sent onward by you to Judea.
2 Corinthians 1:17 Therefore, intending this, did I then use fickleness? Or do I plan what I plan according to flesh, so that with me there may be the Yes, yes and the No, no?
2 Corinthians 1:18 But God is faithful, that our word toward you did not become Yes and No.
2 Corinthians 1:19 For God's Son Jesus Christ, who was preached among you through us, through me and Silvanus and Timothy, did not become Yes and No, but in him has become Yes.
2 Corinthians 1:20 For as many as are God's promises, in him is the Yes and in him the Amen, to God for glory through us.
2 Corinthians 1:21 And the one who confirms us with you unto Christ and anointed us is God,
2 Corinthians 1:22 who also sealed us and gave the pledge of the Spirit in our hearts.
2 Corinthians 1:23 But I call upon God as witness upon my soul, that sparing you I no longer came to Corinth.
2 Corinthians 1:24 Not that we rule over your faith, but we are fellow workers of your joy, for by faith you stand.

## Chapter 2

2 Corinthians 2:1 But I decided this for myself, not to come to you again in grief.
2 Corinthians 2:2 For if I grieve you, who then is the one who gladdens me except the one grieved by me?
2 Corinthians 2:3 And I wrote this very thing to you, so that when I come I may not have grief from those from whom I ought to rejoice, trusting in all of you that my joy is that of you all.
2 Corinthians 2:4 For from much affliction and anguish of heart I wrote to you through many tears, not so that you may be grieved, but so that you may know the love which I have more abundantly toward you.
2 Corinthians 2:5 But if someone has caused grief, he has grieved not me, but in part, so that I may not burden you all.
2 Corinthians 2:6 Sufficient for such a one is this punishment by the majority,
2 Corinthians 2:7 so that on the contrary you should rather forgive and encourage, lest such a one be swallowed by more abundant grief.
2 Corinthians 2:8 Therefore I urge you to confirm love toward him.
2 Corinthians 2:9 For to this end I also wrote, so that I may know your proven character, whether you are obedient in everything.
2 Corinthians 2:10 And to whom you forgive anything, I also; for also I, if I have forgiven anything, what I have forgiven, it is because of you in Christ's presence,
2 Corinthians 2:11 so that we may not be exploited by Satan, for we are not ignorant of his designs.
2 Corinthians 2:12 And coming to Troas for Christ's gospel, and a door having been opened for me in the Lord,
2 Corinthians 2:13 I have had no relief in my spirit because I did not find Titus my brother, but taking leave of them I went out to Macedonia.
2 Corinthians 2:14 But thanks to God, who always leads us in triumph in Christ and manifests through us the odor of his knowledge in every place,
2 Corinthians 2:15 because we are Christ's fragrance to God among those being saved and among those perishing,
2 Corinthians 2:16 to these an odor of death unto death, but to those an odor of life unto life. And who is sufficient for these things?
2 Corinthians 2:17 For we are not as the many, peddling God's word, but as from sincerity, but as from God, before God, we speak in Christ.

## Chapter 3

2 Corinthians 3:1 Are we beginning again to commend ourselves? Or do we need, as some, commendatory letters to you or commendatory letters from you?
2 Corinthians 3:2 You are our letter, inscribed in our hearts, known and read by all people,
2 Corinthians 3:3 being manifested that you are Christ's letter ministered by us, inscribed not with ink but with the Spirit of the living God, not on stone tablets but on fleshly tablets of heart.
2 Corinthians 3:4 And we have such confidence through Christ toward God,
2 Corinthians 3:5 not that we are sufficient from ourselves to reckon anything as from ourselves, but our sufficiency is from God,
2 Corinthians 3:6 who also made us sufficient as ministers of a new covenant, not of letter but of spirit; for the letter kills, but the spirit gives life.
2 Corinthians 3:7 But if the ministry of death, imprinted in letters on stones, came in glory, so that Israel's sons could not gaze upon Moses's face because of the glory of his face, which was being nullified,
2 Corinthians 3:8 how will the ministry of the Spirit not rather be in glory?
2 Corinthians 3:9 For if the ministry of condemnation is glory, much more the ministry of righteousness abounds in glory.
2 Corinthians 3:10 For even what has been glorified has not been glorified in this respect, because of the surpassing glory.
2 Corinthians 3:11 For if what is being nullified is through glory, much more what remains is in glory.
2 Corinthians 3:12 Therefore, having such hope, we use much boldness,
2 Corinthians 3:13 and not as Moses put a veil upon his own face so that Israel's sons might not gaze upon the end of what was being nullified.
2 Corinthians 3:14 But their minds were hardened; for until today the same veil remains at the reading of the old covenant, not unveiled, because it is nullified in Christ.
2 Corinthians 3:15 But until today, whenever Moses is read, a veil lies upon their heart.
2 Corinthians 3:16 But whenever it turns toward the Lord, the veil is taken away.
2 Corinthians 3:17 And the Lord is the Spirit, and where the Lord's Spirit is, there is freedom.
2 Corinthians 3:18 But we all, with unveiled face beholding as in a mirror the Lord's glory, are transformed into the same image from glory to glory, as from the Lord, the Spirit.

## Chapter 4

2 Corinthians 4:1 For this reason, having this ministry, just as we received mercy, we do not lose heart,
2 Corinthians 4:2 but renounced the hidden things of shame, not walking in cunning nor adulterating God's word, but by manifestation of the truth commending ourselves to every conscience of people before God.
2 Corinthians 4:3 But even if our gospel is veiled, it is veiled among those perishing,
2 Corinthians 4:4 among whom the god of this age blinded the minds of the unbelievers, so that the illumination of the gospel of Christ's glory, who is God's image, might not shine upon them.
2 Corinthians 4:5 For we preach not ourselves but Christ Jesus as Lord, and ourselves your slaves because of Jesus,
2 Corinthians 4:6 because God, who said for light to shine from darkness, is the one who shone in our hearts for illumination of the knowledge of God's glory in Jesus Christ's face.
2 Corinthians 4:7 But we have this treasure in earthen vessels, so that the excess of power may be God's and not from us,
2 Corinthians 4:8 afflicted in everything, but not confined; perplexed, but not despairing;
2 Corinthians 4:9 persecuted, but not abandoned; struck down, but not perishing;
2 Corinthians 4:10 always carrying around in the body the dying of the Lord Jesus, so that Jesus's life also may be manifested in our body.
2 Corinthians 4:11 For we who live are always handed over to death because of Jesus, so that Jesus's life also may be manifested in our mortal flesh.
2 Corinthians 4:12 So death works in us, but life in you.
2 Corinthians 4:13 And having the same spirit of faith, according to what is written, “I believed, therefore I spoke,” we too believe, therefore also speak,
2 Corinthians 4:14 knowing that the one who raised the Lord Jesus will also raise us through Jesus and present us with you.
2 Corinthians 4:15 For all things are because of you, so that grace, increasing through the more, may cause thanksgiving to abound unto God's glory.
2 Corinthians 4:16 Therefore we do not lose heart; but even if our outer man is being destroyed, yet the inner is renewed day by day.
2 Corinthians 4:17 For the momentary lightness of our affliction works for us, beyond measure unto beyond measure, an eternal weight of glory,
2 Corinthians 4:18 while we look not at the things seen but the things not seen; for the things seen are temporary, but the things not seen eternal.

## Chapter 5

2 Corinthians 5:1 For we know that if our earthly house of the tent is torn down, we have a building from God, a house not made by hands, eternal in the heavens.
2 Corinthians 5:2 For also in this we groan, longing to put on over ourselves our dwelling from heaven,
2 Corinthians 5:3 if indeed, having put it on, we will not be found naked.
2 Corinthians 5:4 For also we who are in the tent groan, burdened, because we do not want to be unclothed but clothed over, so that the mortal may be swallowed by life.
2 Corinthians 5:5 And the one who worked us for this very thing is God, who also gave us the pledge of the Spirit.
2 Corinthians 5:6 Therefore always being confident, and knowing that while at home in the body we are away from the Lord—
2 Corinthians 5:7 for we walk through faith, not through sight—
2 Corinthians 5:8 but we are confident and rather pleased to be away from the body and at home with the Lord.
2 Corinthians 5:9 Therefore we also aspire, whether at home or away, to be pleasing to him.
2 Corinthians 5:10 For we all must be manifested before Christ's judgment seat, so that each may receive the things through the body according to what he practiced, whether good or evil.
2 Corinthians 5:11 Therefore, knowing the Lord's fear, we persuade people, but have been manifested to God; and I hope also to have been manifested in your consciences.
2 Corinthians 5:12 For we do not again commend ourselves to you, but give you an opportunity of boasting for us, so that you may have an answer to those boasting in face and not heart.
2 Corinthians 5:13 For whether we were out of our minds, it is to God; whether we are sound-minded, to you.
2 Corinthians 5:14 For Christ's love constrains us, having judged this, that if one died for all, then all died;
2 Corinthians 5:15 and he died for all, so that those living may no longer live to themselves but to the one who died and was raised for them.
2 Corinthians 5:16 So from now we know no one according to flesh; and even if we have known Christ according to flesh, yet now we no longer know him thus.
2 Corinthians 5:17 So if someone is in Christ, a new creation; the ancient things passed away; look, all things have become new.
2 Corinthians 5:18 And all things are from God, who reconciled us to himself through Jesus Christ and gave us the ministry of reconciliation,
2 Corinthians 5:19 that God was in Christ reconciling a world to himself, not reckoning their trespasses to them, and placing in us the word of reconciliation.
2 Corinthians 5:20 Therefore we act as ambassadors for Christ, as God urges through us; we petition for Christ: be reconciled to God.
2 Corinthians 5:21 For he made the one who did not know sin sin for us, so that we may become God's righteousness in him.

## Chapter 6

2 Corinthians 6:1 And working together, we also urge you not to receive God's grace in vain.
2 Corinthians 6:2 For he says, “At an acceptable time I listened to you, and on a day of salvation I helped you.” Look, now an acceptable time; look, now a day of salvation.
2 Corinthians 6:3 Giving no stumbling in anything, so that the ministry may not be blamed,
2 Corinthians 6:4 but in everything commending ourselves as God's ministers, in much endurance, in afflictions, in necessities, in distresses,
2 Corinthians 6:5 in blows, in prisons, in disorders, in labors, in sleeplessness, in fastings,
2 Corinthians 6:6 in purity, in knowledge, in patience, in kindness, in the Holy Spirit, in unhypocritical love,
2 Corinthians 6:7 in a word of truth, in God's power, through the weapons of righteousness on the right and left,
2 Corinthians 6:8 through glory and dishonor, through ill repute and good repute; as deceivers and true,
2 Corinthians 6:9 as unknown and fully known, as dying and look, we live, as disciplined and not put to death,
2 Corinthians 6:10 as grieving but always rejoicing, as poor but enriching many, as having nothing and possessing everything.
2 Corinthians 6:11 Our mouth has opened toward you, Corinthians; our heart has been widened.
2 Corinthians 6:12 You are not confined in us, but are confined in your inward affections.
2 Corinthians 6:13 And for the same recompense—I speak as to children—be widened, you too.
2 Corinthians 6:14 Do not become unequally yoked with unbelievers. For what partnership is there for righteousness and lawlessness? And what fellowship for light with darkness?
2 Corinthians 6:15 And what agreement for Christ with Beliar? Or what portion for a believer with an unbeliever?
2 Corinthians 6:16 And what accord for God's temple with idols? For you are a temple of the living God, just as God said, “I will dwell in them and walk among them, and I will be their God, and they will be my people.”
2 Corinthians 6:17 Therefore, “Come out from their midst and be set apart, says the Lord, and do not touch an unclean thing, and I will receive you,
2 Corinthians 6:18 and will be a Father to you, and you will be sons and daughters to me, says the Lord Almighty.”

## Chapter 7

2 Corinthians 7:1 Therefore, having these promises, beloved, let us cleanse ourselves from every defilement of flesh and spirit, completing holiness in God's fear.
2 Corinthians 7:2 Make room for us. We wronged no one, corrupted no one, exploited no one.
2 Corinthians 7:3 I do not speak for condemnation, for I have said beforehand that you are in our hearts, to die together and live together.
2 Corinthians 7:4 Much is my boldness toward you, much my boasting for you; I have been filled with encouragement, I overflow with joy in all our affliction.
2 Corinthians 7:5 For also when we came to Macedonia, our flesh has had no relief, but being afflicted in everything: fights outside, fears within.
2 Corinthians 7:6 But God, who encourages the lowly, encouraged us by Titus's presence,
2 Corinthians 7:7 and not only by his presence but also by the encouragement with which he was encouraged over you, reporting to us your longing, your lamentation, your zeal for me, so that I rejoiced more.
2 Corinthians 7:8 Because even if I grieved you with the letter, I do not regret it, even if I did regret it; for I see that that letter grieved you, even if for an hour.
2 Corinthians 7:9 Now I rejoice, not that you were grieved, but that you were grieved unto repentance; for you were grieved according to God, so that you might suffer loss in nothing from us.
2 Corinthians 7:10 For grief according to God works repentance unto salvation without regret, but the world's grief works death.
2 Corinthians 7:11 For look, this very thing, your being grieved according to God, how much diligence it worked in you, indeed defense, indeed indignation, indeed fear, indeed longing, indeed zeal, indeed vengeance! In everything you commended yourselves as pure in the matter.
2 Corinthians 7:12 Therefore, even if I wrote to you, it was not because of the one who wronged nor because of the one wronged, but for your diligence for us to be manifested to you before God.
2 Corinthians 7:13 For this reason we have been encouraged in your encouragement, and much more we rejoiced over Titus's joy, because his spirit has been refreshed by you all.
2 Corinthians 7:14 Because if I have boasted anything to him for you, I was not shamed; but as we spoke everything in truth to you, so also our boasting before Titus became truth.
2 Corinthians 7:15 And his inward affections are more abundantly toward you, as he remembers the obedience of you all, how with fear and trembling you received him.
2 Corinthians 7:16 I rejoice that in everything I have confidence in you.

## Chapter 8

2 Corinthians 8:1 And we make known to you, brothers, God's grace given in the churches of Macedonia,
2 Corinthians 8:2 that in much trial of affliction the abundance of their joy and their deep poverty abounded unto the riches of their simplicity.
2 Corinthians 8:3 Because according to power, I testify, and beyond power, of their own choice,
2 Corinthians 8:4 with much urging petitioning us to receive the gift and the fellowship of the ministry to the saints,
2 Corinthians 8:5 and not as we hoped, but they gave themselves first to the Lord and to us through God's will,
2 Corinthians 8:6 so that we urged Titus that just as he began beforehand, so he might also complete this grace toward you.
2 Corinthians 8:7 But just as you abound in everything, faith and word and knowledge and all diligence and the love from you in us, so also abound in this grace.
2 Corinthians 8:8 I speak not by command, but through the diligence of others also testing the genuineness of your love.
2 Corinthians 8:9 For you know the grace of our Lord Jesus Christ, that because of you he became poor, being rich, so that by his poverty you may become rich.
2 Corinthians 8:10 And I give judgment in this, for this benefits you, who began beforehand from last year not only to do but also to will.
2 Corinthians 8:11 But now also complete the doing, so that just as the eagerness to will, so also the completing may be from what you have.
2 Corinthians 8:12 For if the eagerness is present, it is acceptable according to whatever someone has, not according to what he does not have.
2 Corinthians 8:13 For not so that others have relief and you affliction, but from equality, at the present time your abundance for their lack,
2 Corinthians 8:14 so that their abundance also may become for your lack, so that equality may come,
2 Corinthians 8:15 as it is written, “The one with much did not have excess, and the one with little did not have less.”
2 Corinthians 8:16 But thanks to God who gives the same diligence for you in Titus's heart,
2 Corinthians 8:17 because he received the urging, but being more diligent, of his own choice he went out to you.
2 Corinthians 8:18 And we sent together with him the brother whose praise in the gospel is through all the churches,
2 Corinthians 8:19 and not only this, but also appointed by the churches as our fellow traveler with this gift ministered by us, for the Lord's own glory and your eagerness,
2 Corinthians 8:20 avoiding this, that someone may blame us in this abundance ministered by us,
2 Corinthians 8:21 taking forethought for good things not only before the Lord but also before people.
2 Corinthians 8:22 And we sent with them our brother, whom we tested in many things often as diligent, but now much more diligent through much confidence toward you.
2 Corinthians 8:23 Whether concerning Titus, he is my partner and fellow worker toward you; whether our brothers, apostles of churches, Christ's glory.
