2 Corinthians 8:24 Therefore demonstrate to them, and before the churches, the demonstration of your love and our boasting for you.

## Chapter 9

2 Corinthians 9:1 For concerning the ministry to the saints, it is superfluous for me to write to you.
2 Corinthians 9:2 For I know your eagerness, which I boast of for you to Macedonians, that Achaia has been prepared from last year, and the zeal from you stirred up the majority.
2 Corinthians 9:3 But I sent the brothers, so that our boast for you may not be emptied in this respect, so that, as I said, you may be prepared,
2 Corinthians 9:4 lest, if Macedonians come with me and find you unprepared, we—to avoid saying you—may be shamed in this confidence of boasting.
2 Corinthians 9:5 Therefore I considered it necessary to urge the brothers to come beforehand to you and prepare beforehand your blessing announced beforehand, for this to be ready thus as a blessing and not as greed.
2 Corinthians 9:6 But this: the one sowing sparingly will also reap sparingly, and the one sowing upon blessings will also reap upon blessings.
2 Corinthians 9:7 Each just as he chooses in his heart, not from grief or necessity; for God loves a cheerful giver.
2 Corinthians 9:8 And God is able to make all grace abound toward you, so that in everything, always having all sufficiency, you may abound unto every good work,
2 Corinthians 9:9 as it is written, “He scattered, he gave to the poor; his righteousness remains forever.”
2 Corinthians 9:10 And may the one supplying seed to the sower and bread for eating supply and multiply your seed and increase the produce of your righteousness,
2 Corinthians 9:11 being enriched in everything unto all simplicity, which works thanksgiving to God through us.
2 Corinthians 9:12 Because the ministry of this service not only fills up the lacks of the saints, but also abounds through many thanksgivings to God,
2 Corinthians 9:13 through the proof of this ministry glorifying God for the submission of your confession to Christ's gospel and simplicity of fellowship toward them and toward all,
2 Corinthians 9:14 and in their petition for you, longing for you because of God's surpassing grace upon you.
2 Corinthians 9:15 But thanks to God for his indescribable gift.

## Chapter 10

2 Corinthians 10:1 And I myself, Paul, urge you through Christ's gentleness and fairness, who face to face am lowly among you, but absent am confident toward you.
2 Corinthians 10:2 But I petition that when present I may not be confident with the confidence with which I reckon to dare against some who reckon us as walking according to flesh.
2 Corinthians 10:3 For walking in flesh, we do not wage war according to flesh,
2 Corinthians 10:4 for the weapons of our warfare are not fleshly, but powerful with God for pulling down strongholds,
2 Corinthians 10:5 pulling down reasonings and every height raised against God's knowledge, and taking every thought captive to Christ's obedience,
2 Corinthians 10:6 and having readiness to avenge every disobedience, when your obedience is fulfilled.
2 Corinthians 10:7 Look at the things before your face. If someone trusts himself to be Christ's, let him reckon this again from himself, that just as he is Christ's, so we too are Christ's.
2 Corinthians 10:8 For even if I boast something more abundantly concerning our authority, which the Lord gave us for building up and not for pulling you down, I will not be shamed,
2 Corinthians 10:9 so that I may not seem as though to frighten you through the letters.
2 Corinthians 10:10 Because, he says, “The letters are weighty and strong, but the presence of the body weak and the speech despised.”
2 Corinthians 10:11 Let such a one reckon this, that as we are in word through letters when absent, such also when present in deed.
2 Corinthians 10:12 For we do not dare to class or compare ourselves with some of those commending themselves; but they, measuring themselves among themselves and comparing themselves with themselves, do not understand.
2 Corinthians 10:13 But we will not boast beyond measure, but according to the measure of the rule which God apportioned to us, a measure to reach even as far as you.
2 Corinthians 10:14 For we do not overstretch ourselves as though not reaching you, for we reached even you in Christ's gospel,
2 Corinthians 10:15 not boasting beyond measure in others' labors, but having hope, as your faith grows, to be enlarged among you according to our rule unto abundance,
2 Corinthians 10:16 to proclaim the gospel to the regions beyond you, not to boast in another's rule in things ready.
2 Corinthians 10:17 But let the one boasting boast in the Lord.
2 Corinthians 10:18 For not the one commending himself is approved, but the one whom the Lord commends.

## Chapter 11

2 Corinthians 11:1 I wish you would bear with me a little in foolishness; but indeed bear with me.
2 Corinthians 11:2 For I am jealous for you with God's jealousy, for I betrothed you to one husband, to present a pure virgin to Christ.
2 Corinthians 11:3 But I fear lest, as the serpent deceived Eve in his cunning, so your minds be corrupted from the simplicity toward Christ.
2 Corinthians 11:4 For if the one coming preaches another Jesus whom we did not preach, or you receive a different spirit which you did not receive, or a different gospel which you did not accept, you bore it well.
2 Corinthians 11:5 For I reckon to have lacked nothing of the exceedingly great apostles.
2 Corinthians 11:6 But even if untrained in speech, yet not in knowledge; but in everything we were manifested in all things toward you.
2 Corinthians 11:7 Or did I commit sin, humbling myself so that you may be exalted, because I proclaimed God's gospel to you freely?
2 Corinthians 11:8 I robbed other churches, receiving wages for ministry to you.
2 Corinthians 11:9 And present with you and lacking, I burdened no one, for the brothers coming from Macedonia filled up my lack; and in everything I kept myself unburdensome to you and will keep myself so.
2 Corinthians 11:10 Christ's truth is in me, that this boasting will not be sealed up for me in the regions of Achaia.
2 Corinthians 11:11 Why? Because I do not love you? God knows.
2 Corinthians 11:12 But what I do I will also do, so that I may cut off the opportunity of those wanting an opportunity, so that in what they boast they may be found just as we also.
2 Corinthians 11:13 For such people are false apostles, deceitful workers, transforming themselves into Christ's apostles.
2 Corinthians 11:14 And no wonder, for Satan himself transforms himself into an angel of light.
2 Corinthians 11:15 Therefore no great thing if his ministers also transform themselves as ministers of righteousness, whose end will be according to their works.
2 Corinthians 11:16 Again I say, let no one think me foolish; but otherwise receive me even as foolish, so that I too may boast a little.
2 Corinthians 11:17 What I speak I speak not according to the Lord, but as in foolishness, in this confidence of boasting.
2 Corinthians 11:18 Since many boast according to flesh, I too will boast.
2 Corinthians 11:19 For gladly you bear with the foolish, being prudent.
2 Corinthians 11:20 For you bear it if someone enslaves you, if someone devours, if someone takes, if someone exalts himself, if someone beats you in the face.
2 Corinthians 11:21 I speak according to dishonor, as though we were weak; but in whatever someone dares—I speak in foolishness—I too dare.
2 Corinthians 11:22 Are they Hebrews? I too. Are they Israelites? I too. Are they Abraham's seed? I too.
2 Corinthians 11:23 Are they Christ's ministers? I speak as deranged: I more; in labors more abundantly, in blows exceedingly, in prisons more abundantly, in deaths often.
2 Corinthians 11:24 From Jews five times I received forty less one.
2 Corinthians 11:25 Three times I was beaten with rods, once stoned, three times shipwrecked; I have spent a night and day in the deep;
2 Corinthians 11:26 in journeys often, in dangers of rivers, dangers of robbers, dangers from kin, dangers from nations, dangers in city, dangers in wilderness, dangers in sea, dangers among false brothers;
2 Corinthians 11:27 in labor and toil, in sleeplessness often, in hunger and thirst, in fastings often, in cold and nakedness.
2 Corinthians 11:28 Apart from the things besides, my daily pressure, the concern of all the churches.
2 Corinthians 11:29 Who is weak, and I am not weak? Who is offended, and I do not burn?
2 Corinthians 11:30 If I must boast, I will boast of the things of my weakness.
2 Corinthians 11:31 The God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, who is blessed forever, knows that I do not lie.
2 Corinthians 11:32 In Damascus the ethnarch of Aretas the king guarded the city of the Damascenes, wanting to seize me,
2 Corinthians 11:33 and through a window in a basket I was lowered through the wall, and escaped his hands.

## Chapter 12

2 Corinthians 12:1 Indeed, boasting does not benefit me, for I will come to visions and revelations of the Lord.
2 Corinthians 12:2 I know a man in Christ fourteen years ago—whether in body I do not know, or outside the body I do not know, God knows—such a one caught up as far as the third heaven.
2 Corinthians 12:3 And I know such a man—whether in body or outside the body I do not know, God knows—
2 Corinthians 12:4 that he was caught up into paradise and heard unutterable words which it is not permitted for a man to speak.
2 Corinthians 12:5 For such a one I will boast, but for myself I will not boast except in my weaknesses.
2 Corinthians 12:6 For if I want to boast, I will not be foolish, for I will speak truth; but I refrain, lest someone reckon concerning me beyond what he sees me to be or hears anything from me.
2 Corinthians 12:7 And because of the excess of the revelations, so that I may not exalt myself beyond measure, a thorn in the flesh was given to me, a messenger of Satan, to strike me, so that I may not exalt myself beyond measure.
2 Corinthians 12:8 Concerning this I urged the Lord three times that it might depart from me.
2 Corinthians 12:9 And he has said to me, “My grace suffices for you, for my power is perfected in weakness.” Therefore most gladly I will rather boast in my weaknesses, so that Christ's power may dwell upon me.
2 Corinthians 12:10 Therefore I am pleased in weaknesses, in insults, in necessities, in persecutions, in distresses for Christ; for when I am weak, then I am powerful.
2 Corinthians 12:11 I have become foolish in boasting; you compelled me. For I ought to have been commended by you, for I lacked nothing of the exceedingly great apostles, even if I am nothing.
2 Corinthians 12:12 Indeed the signs of the apostle were worked among you in all endurance, in signs and wonders and powers.
2 Corinthians 12:13 For what is there in which you were made inferior to the other churches, except that I myself did not burden you? Forgive me this injustice.
2 Corinthians 12:14 Look, a third time I am ready to come to you, and I will not burden you, for I seek not your things but you; for the children ought not to store up for the parents, but the parents for the children.
2 Corinthians 12:15 But most gladly I will spend and be spent completely for your souls, even if, loving you more abundantly, I am loved less.
2 Corinthians 12:16 But let it be: I did not burden you, but being cunning, I took you by deceit.
2 Corinthians 12:17 Did I exploit you through anyone whom I have sent to you?
2 Corinthians 12:18 I urged Titus and sent the brother with him. Did Titus exploit you? Did we not walk in the same spirit? In the same footsteps?
2 Corinthians 12:19 Again do you think that we defend ourselves to you? Before God we speak in Christ; but all things, beloved, are for your building up.
2 Corinthians 12:20 For I fear lest, coming, I find you not such as I want, and I be found by you such as you do not want; lest there be strifes, jealousies, furies, selfish ambitions, backbitings, whisperings, puffings up, disorders;
2 Corinthians 12:21 lest when I come again my God humble me before you, and I mourn many of those who sinned beforehand and did not repent of the impurity and sexual immorality and licentiousness which they practiced.

## Chapter 13

2 Corinthians 13:1 This third time I come to you. Upon the mouth of two witnesses and three every word will stand.
2 Corinthians 13:2 I have said beforehand and say beforehand, as present the second time, and absent now I write to those who sinned beforehand and all the rest, that if I come again I will not spare,
2 Corinthians 13:3 since you seek proof of Christ speaking in me, who is not weak toward you but powerful among you.
2 Corinthians 13:4 For even if he was crucified from weakness, yet he lives from God's power; for we too are weak in him, but will live with him from God's power toward you.
2 Corinthians 13:5 Test yourselves whether you are in the faith; examine yourselves. Or do you not recognize yourselves, that Jesus Christ is in you, unless perhaps you are disapproved?
2 Corinthians 13:6 But I hope that you will know that we are not disapproved.
2 Corinthians 13:7 And I pray to God that you do no evil, not so that we may appear approved, but so that you may do the good and we be as disapproved.
2 Corinthians 13:8 For we can do nothing against the truth, but for the truth.
2 Corinthians 13:9 For we rejoice when we are weak and you are powerful; and this we also pray, your restoration.
2 Corinthians 13:10 For this reason I write these things absent, so that present I may not act severely according to the authority which the Lord gave me for building up and not for pulling down.
2 Corinthians 13:11 Finally, brothers, rejoice, be restored, be encouraged, think the same, be at peace, and the God of love and peace will be with you.
2 Corinthians 13:12 Greet one another with a holy kiss. All the saints greet you.
2 Corinthians 13:13 The grace of the Lord Jesus Christ and God's love and the fellowship of the Holy Spirit be with you all. Amen.

# Galatians

The Apostolic Bible. Public domain. https://apostolic-bible.ysys9.chatgpt.site/license.html


## Chapter 1

Galatians 1:1 Paul, an apostle not from people nor through a man, but through Jesus Christ and God the Father who raised him from the dead,
Galatians 1:2 and all the brothers with me, to the churches of Galatia:
Galatians 1:3 grace to you and peace from God the Father and our Lord Jesus Christ,
Galatians 1:4 who gave himself for our sins, so that he may rescue us from the present evil age, according to the will of our God and Father,
Galatians 1:5 to whom the glory unto the ages of the ages. Amen.
Galatians 1:6 I marvel that you so quickly transfer from the one who called you in Christ's grace to a different gospel,
Galatians 1:7 which is not another, except that there are some who trouble you and want to overturn Christ's gospel.
Galatians 1:8 But even if we or an angel from heaven proclaims a gospel to you contrary to what we proclaimed to you, let him be accursed.
Galatians 1:9 As we have said beforehand, now I also say again: if someone proclaims a gospel to you contrary to what you received, let him be accursed.
Galatians 1:10 For now do I persuade people or God? Or do I seek to please people? For if I still pleased people, I would not be Christ's slave.
Galatians 1:11 But I make known to you, brothers, that the gospel proclaimed by me is not according to man.
Galatians 1:12 For neither did I receive it from a man nor was I taught it, but through revelation of Jesus Christ.
Galatians 1:13 For you heard my former conduct in Judaism, that exceedingly I persecuted God's church and ravaged it,
Galatians 1:14 and advanced in Judaism beyond many contemporaries in my race, being more abundantly zealous for my ancestral traditions.
Galatians 1:15 But when God, who set me apart from my mother's womb and called me through his grace, was pleased
Galatians 1:16 to reveal his Son in me, so that I may proclaim him among the nations, immediately I did not consult flesh and blood,
Galatians 1:17 nor did I go up to Jerusalem to the apostles before me, but went away to Arabia and again returned to Damascus.
Galatians 1:18 Then after three years I went up to Jerusalem to visit Peter, and remained with him fifteen days.
Galatians 1:19 But I saw no other of the apostles except James the Lord's brother.
Galatians 1:20 And what I write to you, look, before God, I do not lie.
Galatians 1:21 Then I came to the regions of Syria and Cilicia.
Galatians 1:22 But I was unknown by face to the churches of Judea in Christ,
Galatians 1:23 and they were only hearing that “The one formerly persecuting us now proclaims the faith which he formerly ravaged,”
Galatians 1:24 and they glorified God in me.

## Chapter 2

Galatians 2:1 Then after fourteen years I again went up to Jerusalem with Barnabas, also taking Titus along.
Galatians 2:2 And I went up according to revelation, and set before them the gospel which I preach among the nations, but privately to those of repute, lest I run or ran in vain.
Galatians 2:3 But not even Titus with me, being Greek, was compelled to be circumcised,
Galatians 2:4 but because of the false brothers brought in, who slipped in to spy upon our freedom which we have in Christ Jesus, so that they may enslave us,
Galatians 2:5 to whom we did not yield in submission even for an hour, so that the truth of the gospel may remain with you.
Galatians 2:6 But from those reputed to be something—whatever they once were makes no difference to me; God does not accept a man's face—for those of repute added nothing to me,
Galatians 2:7 but on the contrary, seeing that I have been entrusted with the gospel of uncircumcision, just as Peter of circumcision,
Galatians 2:8 for the one who worked in Peter for apostleship of circumcision also worked in me for the nations,
Galatians 2:9 and knowing the grace given to me, James and Cephas and John, reputed to be pillars, gave right hands of fellowship to me and Barnabas, so that we should go to the nations, but they to circumcision,
Galatians 2:10 only that we remember the poor, which very thing I was also diligent to do.
Galatians 2:11 But when Peter came to Antioch, I opposed him to his face, because he stood condemned.
Galatians 2:12 For before some came from James, he ate together with the nations; but when they came, he withdrew and separated himself, fearing those of circumcision.
Galatians 2:13 And the remaining Jews also joined in hypocrisy with him, so that even Barnabas was carried away with their hypocrisy.
Galatians 2:14 But when I saw that they did not walk straight toward the truth of the gospel, I said to Peter before all, “If you, being a Jew, live as the nations and not as Jews, why do you compel the nations to live as Jews?
Galatians 2:15 We, Jews by nature and not sinners from nations,
Galatians 2:16 knowing that a man is not justified from works of law except through faith of Jesus Christ, we too believed in Christ Jesus, so that we may be justified from faith of Christ and not from works of law, because from works of law no flesh will be justified.
Galatians 2:17 But if, seeking to be justified in Christ, we ourselves also were found sinners, is Christ then a minister of sin? May it never be!
Galatians 2:18 For if I build again the things I tore down, I demonstrate myself a transgressor.
Galatians 2:19 For through law I died to law, so that I may live to God.
Galatians 2:20 I have been crucified with Christ; and no longer I live, but Christ lives in me; and what I now live in flesh, I live in faith of the Son of God, who loved me and handed himself over for me.
Galatians 2:21 I do not reject God's grace; for if righteousness is through law, then Christ died without cause.”

## Chapter 3

Galatians 3:1 O senseless Galatians, who bewitched you not to obey the truth, before whose eyes Jesus Christ was depicted among you crucified?
Galatians 3:2 I want to learn this only from you: did you receive the Spirit from works of law or from hearing of faith?
Galatians 3:3 Are you so senseless? Having begun by spirit, are you now completed by flesh?
Galatians 3:4 Did you suffer so many things in vain, if indeed even in vain?
Galatians 3:5 Therefore the one supplying the Spirit to you and working powers among you, is it from works of law or from hearing of faith?
Galatians 3:6 Just as Abraham believed God, and it was reckoned to him as righteousness.
Galatians 3:7 Know, then, that those from faith, these are Abraham's sons.
Galatians 3:8 And the Scripture, foreseeing that God justifies the nations from faith, proclaimed the gospel beforehand to Abraham, that “All the nations will be blessed in you.”
Galatians 3:9 So those from faith are blessed with faithful Abraham.
Galatians 3:10 For as many as are from works of law are under a curse; for it is written, “Cursed is everyone who does not remain in all things written in the book of the law, to do them.”
Galatians 3:11 And that no one is justified in law before God is clear, because “The righteous one will live from faith.”
Galatians 3:12 And the law is not from faith, but “The man who does them will live in them.”
Galatians 3:13 Christ bought us out from the curse of the law, becoming a curse for us, for it is written, “Cursed is everyone hanging upon wood,”
Galatians 3:14 so that Abraham's blessing may come to the nations in Christ Jesus, so that we may receive the promise of the Spirit through faith.
Galatians 3:15 Brothers, I speak according to man: even a man's ratified covenant no one rejects or adds provisions to.
Galatians 3:16 And the promises were spoken to Abraham and to his seed. He does not say, “And to seeds,” as concerning many, but as concerning one, “And to your seed,” who is Christ.
Galatians 3:17 But I say this: a covenant ratified beforehand by God unto Christ, the law which came four hundred and thirty years later does not invalidate, so as to nullify the promise.
Galatians 3:18 For if the inheritance is from law, it is no longer from promise; but God has freely given it to Abraham through promise.
Galatians 3:19 What, then, the law? It was added because of transgressions, until the seed should come to whom it has been promised, ordained through angels in a mediator's hand.
Galatians 3:20 And the mediator is not of one, but God is one.
Galatians 3:21 Is the law, then, against God's promises? May it never be! For if a law was given which could give life, righteousness would indeed have been from law.
Galatians 3:22 But the Scripture shut up all things under sin, so that the promise from faith of Jesus Christ may be given to those who believe.
Galatians 3:23 But before faith came, we were guarded under law, shut up unto the faith about to be revealed.
Galatians 3:24 So the law has become our tutor unto Christ, so that we may be justified from faith.
Galatians 3:25 But faith having come, we are no longer under a tutor.
Galatians 3:26 For you are all God's sons through faith in Christ Jesus.
Galatians 3:27 For as many as were baptized into Christ put on Christ.
Galatians 3:28 There is no Jew nor Greek, there is no slave nor free, there is no male and female; for you are all one in Christ Jesus.
Galatians 3:29 But if you are Christ's, then you are Abraham's seed and heirs according to promise.

## Chapter 4

Galatians 4:1 And I say, for as long as the heir is an infant, he differs nothing from a slave, being lord of all,
Galatians 4:2 but is under guardians and stewards until the father's appointed time.
Galatians 4:3 Thus we too, when we were infants, were enslaved under the world's elements.
Galatians 4:4 But when the fullness of time came, God sent out his Son, born from a woman, born under law,
Galatians 4:5 so that he may buy out those under law, so that we may receive adoption as sons.
Galatians 4:6 And because you are sons, God sent out the Spirit of his Son into your hearts, crying, “Abba, Father.”
Galatians 4:7 So you are no longer a slave but a son; and if a son, also God's heir through Christ.
Galatians 4:8 But then, not knowing God, you served as slaves to those not being gods by nature.
Galatians 4:9 But now, knowing God, or rather being known by God, how do you turn again to the weak and poor elements, to which you want to serve as slaves again anew?
Galatians 4:10 You observe days and months and seasons and years.
Galatians 4:11 I fear for you, lest I have labored toward you in vain.
Galatians 4:12 Become as I, because I too as you, brothers, I petition you. You wronged me in nothing.
Galatians 4:13 And you know that because of weakness of the flesh I proclaimed the gospel to you formerly,
Galatians 4:14 and my trial in my flesh you did not despise nor spit out, but received me as God's angel, as Christ Jesus.
Galatians 4:15 What, then, was your blessedness? For I testify to you that, if possible, having dug out your eyes, you would have given them to me.
Galatians 4:16 So have I become your enemy by speaking truth to you?
Galatians 4:17 They are zealous for you, not well, but want to exclude you, so that you may be zealous for them.
Galatians 4:18 But it is good to be sought zealously in a good thing always, and not only when I am present with you.
Galatians 4:19 My little children, for whom I again suffer birth pains until Christ is formed in you,
Galatians 4:20 and I wanted to be present with you now and change my voice, because I am perplexed about you.
Galatians 4:21 Tell me, you who want to be under law, do you not hear the law?
Galatians 4:22 For it is written that Abraham had two sons, one from the slave woman and one from the free woman.
Galatians 4:23 But the one from the slave woman has been born according to flesh, and the one from the free woman through the promise.
Galatians 4:24 These are being allegorized, for these are the two covenants, one from Mount Sinai, bearing children unto slavery, which is Hagar.
Galatians 4:25 For Hagar is Mount Sinai in Arabia, and corresponds to the present Jerusalem, and serves as a slave with her children.
Galatians 4:26 But the Jerusalem above is free, which is mother of us all.
Galatians 4:27 For it is written, “Rejoice, barren one who does not bear; break forth and cry, you who do not suffer birth pains; because more are the children of the desolate than of the one having the husband.”
Galatians 4:28 But we, brothers, according to Isaac, are children of promise.
Galatians 4:29 But just as then the one born according to flesh persecuted the one according to spirit, so also now.
Galatians 4:30 But what does the Scripture say? “Cast out the slave woman and her son, for the slave woman's son will certainly not inherit with the free woman's son.”
Galatians 4:31 Therefore, brothers, we are not children of a slave woman but of the free woman.

## Chapter 5

Galatians 5:1 Therefore stand in the freedom with which Christ freed us, and do not be held again in a yoke of slavery.
Galatians 5:2 Look, I, Paul, say to you that if you are circumcised, Christ will benefit you nothing.
Galatians 5:3 And I testify again to every man being circumcised that he is a debtor to do the whole law.
Galatians 5:4 You were severed from Christ, you who are justified in law; you fell away from grace.
Galatians 5:5 For we by spirit from faith await hope of righteousness.
Galatians 5:6 For in Christ Jesus neither circumcision has any strength nor uncircumcision, but faith working through love.
Galatians 5:7 You ran well; who hindered you from obeying the truth?
Galatians 5:8 The persuasion is not from the one calling you.
Galatians 5:9 A little leaven leavens the whole lump.
Galatians 5:10 I trust concerning you in the Lord that you will think nothing else; but the one troubling you will carry the judgment, whoever he may be.
Galatians 5:11 And I, brothers, if I still preach circumcision, why am I still persecuted? Then the offense of the cross has been nullified.
Galatians 5:12 I wish those unsettling you would even cut themselves off.
Galatians 5:13 For you were called upon freedom, brothers; only do not make freedom an opportunity for the flesh, but through love serve one another as slaves.
Galatians 5:14 For the whole law is fulfilled in one word, in “You shall love your neighbor as yourself.”
Galatians 5:15 But if you bite and devour one another, watch lest you be consumed by one another.
Galatians 5:16 And I say, walk by spirit, and you will certainly not fulfill desire of flesh.
Galatians 5:17 For the flesh desires against the spirit, and the spirit against the flesh; and these oppose one another, so that whatever you want, these things you may not do.
Galatians 5:18 But if you are led by spirit, you are not under law.
Galatians 5:19 And the works of the flesh are manifest, which are adultery, sexual immorality, impurity, licentiousness,
Galatians 5:20 idolatry, sorcery, enmities, strifes, jealousies, furies, selfish ambitions, divisions, factions,
Galatians 5:21 envies, murders, drunkenness, revelries, and things like these, which I tell you beforehand, just as I also said beforehand, that those practicing such things will not inherit God's kingdom.
Galatians 5:22 But the fruit of the Spirit is love, joy, peace, patience, kindness, goodness, faith,
Galatians 5:23 gentleness, self-control; against such things there is no law.
Galatians 5:24 And those of Christ crucified the flesh with the passions and desires.
Galatians 5:25 If we live by spirit, let us also walk in line by spirit.
Galatians 5:26 Let us not become conceited, provoking one another, envying one another.

## Chapter 6

Galatians 6:1 Brothers, even if a man is overtaken in some trespass, you who are spiritual restore such a one in a spirit of gentleness, watching yourself lest you too be tempted.
Galatians 6:2 Carry one another's burdens, and thus fulfill Christ's law.
Galatians 6:3 For if someone thinks to be something, being nothing, he deceives his own mind.
Galatians 6:4 But let each examine his own work, and then he will have the boast toward himself only and not toward the other.
Galatians 6:5 For each will carry his own load.
Galatians 6:6 And let the one instructed in the word share in all good things with the one instructing.
Galatians 6:7 Do not be deceived; God is not mocked, for whatever a man sows, this he will also reap.
Galatians 6:8 Because the one sowing unto his own flesh will reap corruption from the flesh, but the one sowing unto the Spirit will reap eternal life from the Spirit.
Galatians 6:9 And doing the good, let us not lose heart, for in its own time we will reap, not giving up.
Galatians 6:10 So then, as we have time, let us work the good toward all, and especially toward the household of faith.
Galatians 6:11 See with how large letters I wrote to you with my own hand.
Galatians 6:12 As many as want to make a good showing in flesh, these compel you to be circumcised, only so that they may not be persecuted for Christ's cross.
Galatians 6:13 For neither do those being circumcised themselves keep law, but want you to be circumcised so that they may boast in your flesh.
Galatians 6:14 But may it never be for me to boast except in the cross of our Lord Jesus Christ, through whom a world has been crucified to me and I to a world.
Galatians 6:15 For in Christ Jesus neither circumcision has any strength nor uncircumcision, but a new creation.
Galatians 6:16 And as many as will walk in line by this rule, peace upon them and mercy, and upon God's Israel.
Galatians 6:17 Henceforth let no one cause me troubles, for I carry the marks of the Lord Jesus in my body.
Galatians 6:18 The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with your spirit, brothers. Amen.

# Ephesians

The Apostolic Bible. Public domain. https://apostolic-bible.ysys9.chatgpt.site/license.html


## Chapter 1

Ephesians 1:1 Paul, an apostle of Jesus Christ through God's will, to the saints who are in Ephesus and faithful in Christ Jesus:
Ephesians 1:2 grace to you and peace from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ.
Ephesians 1:3 Blessed is the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, who blessed us with every spiritual blessing in the heavenly places in Christ,
Ephesians 1:4 just as he chose us in him before the foundation of a world, for us to be holy and blameless before him in love,
Ephesians 1:5 having predestined us unto adoption as sons through Jesus Christ unto himself, according to the good pleasure of his will,
Ephesians 1:6 unto praise of the glory of his grace, in which he graced us in the beloved one,
Ephesians 1:7 in whom we have redemption through his blood, forgiveness of trespasses, according to the riches of his grace,
Ephesians 1:8 which he made abound toward us in all wisdom and understanding,
Ephesians 1:9 having made known to us the mystery of his will, according to his good pleasure which he purposed in him,
Ephesians 1:10 for a stewardship of the fullness of the times, to sum up all things in Christ, both the things in the heavens and those upon earth,
Ephesians 1:11 in him, in whom we also received an allotted inheritance, predestined according to the purpose of the one working all things according to the counsel of his will,
Ephesians 1:12 for us to be unto praise of his glory, who have hoped beforehand in Christ,
Ephesians 1:13 in whom you too, having heard the word of truth, the gospel of your salvation, in whom also having believed, were sealed with the Holy Spirit of promise,
Ephesians 1:14 who is a pledge of our inheritance, unto redemption of the possession, unto praise of his glory.
Ephesians 1:15 For this reason I too, having heard your faith in the Lord Jesus and the love toward all the saints,
Ephesians 1:16 do not cease giving thanks for you, making mention of you in my prayers,
Ephesians 1:17 so that the God of our Lord Jesus Christ, the Father of glory, may give you a spirit of wisdom and revelation in knowledge of him,
Ephesians 1:18 the eyes of your understanding having been illuminated, so that you may know what is the hope of his calling, and what the riches of the glory of his inheritance among the saints,
Ephesians 1:19 and what the surpassing greatness of his power toward us who believe, according to the working of the might of his strength,
Ephesians 1:20 which he worked in Christ, raising him from the dead, and seated him at his right hand in the heavenly places,
Ephesians 1:21 far above every rule and authority and power and lordship and every name named, not only in this age but also in the coming one,
Ephesians 1:22 and subjected all things under his feet, and gave him as head over all things to the church,
Ephesians 1:23 which is his body, the fullness of the one filling all things in all.

## Chapter 2

Ephesians 2:1 And you, being dead in trespasses and sins,
Ephesians 2:2 in which you once walked according to the age of this world, according to the ruler of the authority of the air, of the spirit now working in the sons of disobedience,
Ephesians 2:3 among whom we all also once conducted ourselves in the desires of our flesh, doing the wills of the flesh and the thoughts, and were by nature children of wrath, as also the rest;
Ephesians 2:4 but God, being rich in mercy, because of his great love with which he loved us,
Ephesians 2:5 even when we were dead in trespasses, made us alive together with Christ—by grace you have been saved—
Ephesians 2:6 and raised us together and seated us together in the heavenly places in Christ Jesus,
Ephesians 2:7 so that in the coming ages he may demonstrate the surpassing riches of his grace in kindness toward us in Christ Jesus.
Ephesians 2:8 For by grace you have been saved through faith, and this not from you, God's gift,
Ephesians 2:9 not from works, so that no one may boast.
Ephesians 2:10 For we are his workmanship, created in Christ Jesus for good works which God prepared beforehand, so that we may walk in them.
Ephesians 2:11 Therefore remember that you once were the nations in flesh, called uncircumcision by the so-called circumcision in flesh made by hands,
Ephesians 2:12 that at that time you were apart from Christ, alienated from Israel's citizenship and strangers to the covenants of promise, having no hope and godless in the world.
Ephesians 2:13 But now in Christ Jesus you who once were far became near in Christ's blood.
Ephesians 2:14 For he himself is our peace, who made both one and broke down the middle wall of the barrier,
Ephesians 2:15 the enmity in his flesh, nullifying the law of commandments in decrees, so that he may create the two in himself into one new man, making peace,
Ephesians 2:16 and reconcile both in one body to God through the cross, killing the enmity in it.
Ephesians 2:17 And coming, he proclaimed peace to you who were far and to those near,
Ephesians 2:18 because through him we both have access in one Spirit to the Father.
Ephesians 2:19 So then you are no longer strangers and resident aliens, but fellow citizens of the saints and God's household,
Ephesians 2:20 built upon the foundation of the apostles and prophets, Jesus Christ himself being the cornerstone,
Ephesians 2:21 in whom the whole building, fitted together, grows into a holy temple in the Lord,
Ephesians 2:22 in whom you too are built together into God's dwelling in spirit.

## Chapter 3

Ephesians 3:1 For this reason I, Paul, the prisoner of Christ Jesus for you, the nations—
Ephesians 3:2 if indeed you heard the stewardship of God's grace given to me for you,
Ephesians 3:3 that according to revelation he made the mystery known to me, just as I wrote beforehand briefly,
Ephesians 3:4 by which, reading, you can understand my comprehension in Christ's mystery,
Ephesians 3:5 which in other generations was not made known to the sons of people as it has now been revealed to his holy apostles and prophets in spirit,
Ephesians 3:6 that the nations are fellow heirs and of the same body and fellow sharers of his promise in Christ through the gospel,
Ephesians 3:7 of which I became a minister according to the gift of God's grace given to me according to the working of his power.
Ephesians 3:8 To me, less than the least of all saints, this grace was given, to proclaim among the nations the untraceable riches of Christ,
Ephesians 3:9 and illuminate all as to what is the fellowship of the mystery hidden from the ages in God who created all things through Jesus Christ,
Ephesians 3:10 so that now God's manifold wisdom may be made known to the rulers and authorities in the heavenly places through the church,
Ephesians 3:11 according to the purpose of the ages which he made in Christ Jesus our Lord,
Ephesians 3:12 in whom we have boldness and access in confidence through his faith.
Ephesians 3:13 Therefore I ask not to lose heart in my afflictions for you, which are your glory.
Ephesians 3:14 For this reason I bend my knees to the Father of our Lord Jesus Christ,
Ephesians 3:15 from whom every family in heavens and upon earth is named,
Ephesians 3:16 so that he may give you, according to the riches of his glory, to be strengthened with power through his Spirit unto the inner man,
Ephesians 3:17 for Christ to dwell through faith in your hearts,
Ephesians 3:18 rooted and founded in love, so that you may have strength to grasp with all the saints what is the breadth and length and depth and height,
Ephesians 3:19 and to know Christ's love surpassing knowledge, so that you may be filled unto all God's fullness.
Ephesians 3:20 And to the one able to do above all things, exceedingly beyond what we ask or think, according to the power working in us,
Ephesians 3:21 to him the glory in the church in Christ Jesus unto all generations of the age of the ages. Amen.

## Chapter 4

Ephesians 4:1 Therefore I, the prisoner in the Lord, urge you to walk worthily of the calling with which you were called,
Ephesians 4:2 with all humility and gentleness, with patience, bearing with one another in love,
Ephesians 4:3 being diligent to keep the unity of the Spirit in the bond of peace.
Ephesians 4:4 One body and one Spirit, just as you were also called in one hope of your calling;
Ephesians 4:5 one Lord, one faith, one baptism;
Ephesians 4:6 one God and Father of all, who is over all and through all and in you all.
Ephesians 4:7 But to each one of us grace was given according to the measure of Christ's gift.
Ephesians 4:8 Therefore he says, “Ascending into height, he took captivity captive, and gave gifts to people.”
Ephesians 4:9 And “He ascended,” what is it except that he also first descended into the lower parts of the earth?
Ephesians 4:10 The one descending is himself also the one ascending far above all the heavens, so that he may fill all things.
Ephesians 4:11 And he himself gave some as apostles, some as prophets, some as evangelists, some as shepherds and teachers,
Ephesians 4:12 for the fitting of the saints, unto work of ministry, unto building up Christ's body,
Ephesians 4:13 until we all attain the unity of faith and knowledge of God's Son, unto a mature man, unto a measure of stature of Christ's fullness,
Ephesians 4:14 so that we may no longer be infants, tossed by waves and carried around by every wind of teaching, in people's trickery, in cunning toward the scheming of error,
Ephesians 4:15 but speaking truth in love, may grow in all things unto him who is the head, Christ,
Ephesians 4:16 from whom the whole body, fitted together and joined together through every joint of supply, according to working in the measure of each single part, makes the growth of the body unto building itself up in love.
Ephesians 4:17 Therefore I say this and testify in the Lord, that you no longer walk as also the remaining nations walk in the futility of their mind,
Ephesians 4:18 being darkened in understanding, alienated from God's life because of the ignorance within them, because of the hardness of their heart,
Ephesians 4:19 who, having become insensible, handed themselves over to licentiousness for the working of every impurity in greed.
Ephesians 4:20 But you did not thus learn Christ,
Ephesians 4:21 if indeed you heard him and were taught in him, just as truth is in Jesus,
Ephesians 4:22 for you to put off, according to the former conduct, the old man being corrupted according to the desires of deceit,
Ephesians 4:23 and to be renewed in the spirit of your mind,
Ephesians 4:24 and put on the new man created according to God in righteousness and holiness of truth.
Ephesians 4:25 Therefore, having put off the lie, speak truth, each with his neighbor, because we are members of one another.
Ephesians 4:26 Be angry and do not sin; do not let the sun set upon your provocation,
Ephesians 4:27 nor give place to the devil.
Ephesians 4:28 Let the one stealing no longer steal, but rather labor, working the good with the hands, so that he may have to share with the one having need.
Ephesians 4:29 Let no rotten word go out from your mouth, but if there is a good one for building up the need, so that it may give grace to those hearing.
Ephesians 4:30 And do not grieve God's Holy Spirit, in whom you were sealed unto a day of redemption.
Ephesians 4:31 Let all bitterness and fury and wrath and shouting and slander be taken away from you with all malice.
Ephesians 4:32 And become kind toward one another, compassionate, forgiving one another, just as God also in Christ forgave you.

## Chapter 5

Ephesians 5:1 Therefore become imitators of God as beloved children,
Ephesians 5:2 and walk in love, just as Christ also loved us and handed himself over for us, an offering and sacrifice to God unto an odor of fragrance.
Ephesians 5:3 But sexual immorality and every impurity or greed, let it not even be named among you, as is fitting for saints,
Ephesians 5:4 and shamefulness and foolish speech or coarse jesting, things not fitting, but rather thanksgiving.
Ephesians 5:5 For you know this, that every sexually immoral or unclean or greedy one, who is an idolater, has no inheritance in the kingdom of Christ and God.
Ephesians 5:6 Let no one deceive you with empty words, for because of these things God's wrath comes upon the sons of disobedience.
Ephesians 5:7 Therefore do not become fellow sharers with them.
Ephesians 5:8 For you once were darkness, but now light in the Lord; walk as children of light,
Ephesians 5:9 for the fruit of the Spirit is in all goodness and righteousness and truth,
Ephesians 5:10 examining what is pleasing to the Lord,
Ephesians 5:11 and do not share together in the fruitless works of darkness, but rather also expose them.
Ephesians 5:12 For the things done secretly by them are shameful even to speak of.
Ephesians 5:13 But all things exposed are manifested by the light, for everything manifested is light.
Ephesians 5:14 Therefore he says, “Awake, sleeper, and rise from the dead, and Christ will shine upon you.”
Ephesians 5:15 Therefore watch how carefully you walk, not as unwise but as wise,
Ephesians 5:16 buying out the time, because the days are evil.
Ephesians 5:17 For this reason do not become foolish, but understanding what the Lord's will is.
Ephesians 5:18 And do not become drunk with wine, in which is dissipation, but be filled in spirit,
Ephesians 5:19 speaking to one another in psalms and hymns and spiritual songs, singing and making melody in your heart to the Lord,
Ephesians 5:20 always giving thanks for all things in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ to God and Father,
Ephesians 5:21 submitting to one another in God's fear.
Ephesians 5:22 Wives, submit to your own husbands as to the Lord,
Ephesians 5:23 because the husband is head of the wife, as also Christ head of the church, and he himself is savior of the body.
Ephesians 5:24 But just as the church submits to Christ, so also the wives to their own husbands in everything.
Ephesians 5:25 Husbands, love your own wives, just as Christ also loved the church and handed himself over for her,
Ephesians 5:26 so that he may sanctify her, cleansing her with the washing of water in a word,
Ephesians 5:27 so that he may present her to himself as the glorious church, not having spot or wrinkle or anything of such things, but so that she may be holy and blameless.
Ephesians 5:28 Thus husbands ought to love their own wives as their own bodies. The one loving his own wife loves himself.
Ephesians 5:29 For no one ever hated his own flesh, but nourishes and cherishes it, just as the Lord also the church,
Ephesians 5:30 because we are members of his body, from his flesh and from his bones.
Ephesians 5:31 For this reason a man will leave his father and mother and join himself to his wife, and the two will be one flesh.
Ephesians 5:32 This mystery is great, but I speak unto Christ and unto the church.
Ephesians 5:33 Nevertheless, you too individually, let each thus love his own wife as himself, and the wife fear the husband.

## Chapter 6

Ephesians 6:1 Children, obey your parents in the Lord, for this is righteous.
Ephesians 6:2 “Honor your father and mother,” which is the first commandment with a promise,
Ephesians 6:3 “so that it may be well with you and you may be long-lived upon the earth.”
Ephesians 6:4 And fathers, do not provoke your children to anger, but nourish them in the Lord's discipline and admonition.
Ephesians 6:5 Slaves, obey the lords according to flesh with fear and trembling, in simplicity of your heart, as Christ,
Ephesians 6:6 not according to eye-service as people-pleasers, but as Christ's slaves, doing God's will from the soul,
Ephesians 6:7 serving as slaves with goodwill to the Lord and not to people,
Ephesians 6:8 knowing that whatever good each does, this he will receive from the Lord, whether slave or free.
Ephesians 6:9 And lords, do the same toward them, giving up the threat, knowing that your own Lord also is in heavens, and there is no partiality with him.
Ephesians 6:10 Finally, my brothers, be empowered in the Lord and in the might of his strength.
Ephesians 6:11 Put on God's full armor, so that you may be able to stand against the devil's schemes,
Ephesians 6:12 because our wrestling is not against blood and flesh, but against the rulers, against the authorities, against the world-rulers of the darkness of this age, against the spiritual things of wickedness in the heavenly places.
Ephesians 6:13 For this reason take up God's full armor, so that you may be able to withstand on the evil day, and having worked everything, to stand.
Ephesians 6:14 Therefore stand, having girded your waist in truth and put on the breastplate of righteousness,
Ephesians 6:15 and shod your feet in readiness of the gospel of peace,
Ephesians 6:16 above all taking up the shield of faith, in which you will be able to quench all the burning arrows of the evil one,
Ephesians 6:17 and receive the helmet of salvation and the Spirit's sword, which is God's word,
Ephesians 6:18 through every prayer and petition, praying at every time in spirit, and keeping watch unto this very thing in all perseverance and petition concerning all the saints,
Ephesians 6:19 and for me, so that a word may be given me in opening my mouth, in boldness to make known the mystery of the gospel,
Ephesians 6:20 for which I act as ambassador in a chain, so that in it I may speak boldly as I ought to speak.
Ephesians 6:21 And so that you too may know the things concerning me, what I practice, Tychicus the beloved brother and faithful minister in the Lord will make all things known to you,
Ephesians 6:22 whom I sent to you for this very thing, so that you may know the things concerning us and he may encourage your hearts.
Ephesians 6:23 Peace to the brothers and love with faith from God the Father and the Lord Jesus Christ.
Ephesians 6:24 Grace be with all who love our Lord Jesus Christ in incorruptibility. Amen.

# Philippians

The Apostolic Bible. Public domain. https://apostolic-bible.ysys9.chatgpt.site/license.html


## Chapter 1

Philippians 1:1 Paul and Timothy, slaves of Jesus Christ, to all the saints in Christ Jesus in Philippi, with overseers and ministers:
Philippians 1:2 grace to you and peace from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ.
Philippians 1:3 I thank my God at every remembrance of you,
Philippians 1:4 always in every petition of mine for you all, making the petition with joy,
Philippians 1:5 for your fellowship unto the gospel from the first day until now,
Philippians 1:6 trusting this very thing, that the one who began a good work in you will complete it until Jesus Christ's day.
Philippians 1:7 Just as it is righteous for me to think this for you all, because I have you in my heart, both in my bonds and in the defense and confirmation of the gospel, you all being my fellow sharers of grace.
Philippians 1:8 For God is my witness, how I long for you all in Jesus Christ's inward affections.
Philippians 1:9 And this I pray, that your love may abound still more and more in knowledge and all perception,
Philippians 1:10 for you to discern the things that differ, so that you may be sincere and without offense unto Christ's day,
Philippians 1:11 filled with fruits of righteousness through Jesus Christ, unto God's glory and praise.
Philippians 1:12 But I want you to know, brothers, that the things concerning me have rather come unto the gospel's advancement,
Philippians 1:13 so that my bonds became manifest in Christ in the whole praetorium and to all the rest,
Philippians 1:14 and most of the brothers in the Lord, trusting through my bonds, dare more abundantly to speak the word fearlessly.
Philippians 1:15 Some indeed preach Christ even because of envy and strife, but some also because of goodwill.
Philippians 1:16 These proclaim Christ from selfish ambition, not purely, thinking to bring affliction upon my bonds,
Philippians 1:17 but those from love, knowing that I am set for defense of the gospel.
Philippians 1:18 For what? Except that in every way, whether in pretense or truth, Christ is proclaimed, and in this I rejoice; but I will also rejoice.
Philippians 1:19 For I know that this will turn out for me unto salvation through your petition and supply of Jesus Christ's Spirit,
Philippians 1:20 according to my eager expectation and hope, that in nothing I will be shamed, but in all boldness, as always, now also Christ will be magnified in my body, whether through life or through death.
Philippians 1:21 For to me, to live is Christ and to die gain.
Philippians 1:22 But if to live in flesh, this is fruit of work for me, and what I will choose I do not make known.
Philippians 1:23 For I am constrained by the two, having the desire to depart and be with Christ, much more better,
Philippians 1:24 but to remain in the flesh is more necessary because of you.
Philippians 1:25 And trusting this, I know that I will remain and stay with you all for your advancement and joy of faith,
Philippians 1:26 so that your boast may abound in Christ Jesus in me through my presence again with you.
Philippians 1:27 Only conduct yourselves as citizens worthily of Christ's gospel, so that whether coming and seeing you or absent, I may hear the things concerning you, that you stand in one spirit, with one soul striving together for the faith of the gospel,
Philippians 1:28 and frightened in nothing by the opponents, which is to them a demonstration of destruction, but to you of salvation, and this from God,
Philippians 1:29 because to you was freely given, for Christ, not only to believe in him but also to suffer for him,
Philippians 1:30 having the same struggle as you saw in me and now hear in me.

## Chapter 2

Philippians 2:1 Therefore, if any encouragement in Christ, if any consolation of love, if any fellowship of spirit, if any inward affections and compassions,
Philippians 2:2 fulfill my joy, that you think the same, having the same love, united in soul, thinking the one thing,
Philippians 2:3 nothing according to selfish ambition or conceit, but in humility considering one another above yourselves,
Philippians 2:4 each looking not to your own things but each also to others' things.
Philippians 2:5 For let this be thought among you which was also in Christ Jesus,
Philippians 2:6 who, being in God's form, did not consider being equal to God a seizure,
Philippians 2:7 but emptied himself, taking a slave's form, becoming in people's likeness,
Philippians 2:8 and being found in appearance as a man, humbled himself, becoming obedient until death, and death of a cross.
Philippians 2:9 Therefore God also exalted him beyond measure and freely gave him a name above every name,
Philippians 2:10 so that in Jesus's name every knee may bend, of heavenly and earthly and subterranean beings,
Philippians 2:11 and every tongue confess that Jesus Christ is Lord, unto God the Father's glory.
Philippians 2:12 So, my beloved, just as you always obeyed, not as in my presence only, but now much more in my absence, work out your own salvation with fear and trembling.
Philippians 2:13 For God is the one working in you both the willing and the working for the good pleasure.
Philippians 2:14 Do everything without grumblings and reasonings,
Philippians 2:15 so that you may become blameless and unmixed, God's children without blemish in the midst of a crooked and distorted generation, among whom you appear as luminaries in a world,
Philippians 2:16 holding forth a word of life, for a boast to me unto Christ's day, that I did not run in vain nor labor in vain.
Philippians 2:17 But even if I am poured out upon the sacrifice and service of your faith, I rejoice and rejoice together with you all.
Philippians 2:18 And the same, you too rejoice and rejoice together with me.
Philippians 2:19 And I hope in the Lord Jesus to send Timothy quickly to you, so that I too may be heartened, knowing the things concerning you.
Philippians 2:20 For I have no one of equal soul who will genuinely care for the things concerning you,
Philippians 2:21 for all seek their own things, not those of Christ Jesus.
Philippians 2:22 But you know his proven character, that as a child with a father he served as a slave with me unto the gospel.
Philippians 2:23 Therefore I hope to send this one immediately, whenever I see the things concerning me,
Philippians 2:24 and I trust in the Lord that I myself also will come quickly.
Philippians 2:25 But I considered it necessary to send to you Epaphroditus, my brother and fellow worker and fellow soldier, but your apostle and servant of my need,
Philippians 2:26 since he was longing for you all and distressed because you heard that he was sick.
Philippians 2:27 For indeed he was sick near death; but God had mercy on him, and not him only but also me, so that I might not have grief upon grief.
Philippians 2:28 Therefore I sent him more diligently, so that seeing him you may rejoice again and I be less grieved.
Philippians 2:29 Therefore receive him in the Lord with all joy, and hold such people in honor,
Philippians 2:30 because for Christ's work he drew near until death, risking his life so that he may fill up your lack of service toward me.

## Chapter 3

Philippians 3:1 Finally, my brothers, rejoice in the Lord. To write the same things to you is not tedious for me, but safe for you.
Philippians 3:2 Watch the dogs, watch the evil workers, watch the mutilation.
Philippians 3:3 For we are the circumcision, who serve God in spirit and boast in Christ Jesus and do not trust in flesh,
Philippians 3:4 though I also have confidence in flesh. If someone else thinks to trust in flesh, I more:
Philippians 3:5 circumcision on the eighth day, from Israel's race, of Benjamin's tribe, a Hebrew from Hebrews, according to law a Pharisee,
Philippians 3:6 according to zeal persecuting the church, according to righteousness in law having become blameless.
Philippians 3:7 But whatever things were gains to me, these I have considered loss because of Christ.
Philippians 3:8 But indeed I also consider everything to be loss because of the surpassing knowledge of Christ Jesus my Lord, because of whom I suffered loss of all things, and consider them refuse so that I may gain Christ,
Philippians 3:9 and be found in him, not having my own righteousness from law, but that through faith of Christ, the righteousness from God upon faith,
Philippians 3:10 to know him and the power of his resurrection and fellowship of his sufferings, being conformed to his death,
Philippians 3:11 if somehow I may attain the resurrection from the dead.
Philippians 3:12 Not that I already received or have already been perfected, but I pursue, if I may also grasp that for which I was also grasped by Christ Jesus.
Philippians 3:13 Brothers, I do not reckon myself to have grasped it; but one thing, forgetting the things behind and stretching toward those before,
Philippians 3:14 I pursue according to the goal for the prize of God's upward calling in Christ Jesus.
Philippians 3:15 Therefore, as many as are mature, let us think this; and if you think anything differently, God will also reveal this to you.
Philippians 3:16 Nevertheless, unto what we attained, walk in line by the same rule, think the same thing.
Philippians 3:17 Become fellow imitators of me, brothers, and watch those walking thus, just as you have us as a pattern.
Philippians 3:18 For many walk, of whom I often told you, but now also weeping say, the enemies of Christ's cross,
Philippians 3:19 whose end is destruction, whose god the belly and glory in their shame, who mind earthly things.
Philippians 3:20 For our citizenship is in heavens, from which we also await a savior, the Lord Jesus Christ,
Philippians 3:21 who will transform the body of our humiliation, for it to become conformed to the body of his glory, according to the working of his ability also to subject all things to himself.

## Chapter 4

Philippians 4:1 So, my beloved and longed-for brothers, my joy and crown, stand thus in the Lord, beloved.
Philippians 4:2 I urge Euodia and urge Syntyche to think the same in the Lord.
Philippians 4:3 And I ask you also, genuine yokefellow, help them, who strove together with me in the gospel, also with Clement and my remaining fellow workers, whose names are in a book of life.
Philippians 4:4 Rejoice in the Lord always; again I will say, rejoice.
Philippians 4:5 Let your fairness be known to all people. The Lord is near.
Philippians 4:6 Be anxious about nothing, but in everything by prayer and petition with thanksgiving let your requests be made known to God.
Philippians 4:7 And God's peace, surpassing every mind, will guard your hearts and thoughts in Christ Jesus.
Philippians 4:8 Finally, brothers, whatever things are true, whatever dignified, whatever righteous, whatever pure, whatever lovable, whatever well spoken of, if any virtue and if any praise, reckon these things.
Philippians 4:9 What you also learned and received and heard and saw in me, practice these things, and the God of peace will be with you.
Philippians 4:10 And I rejoiced greatly in the Lord, that now at last you revived your thinking for me, about which you also were thinking, but lacked opportunity.
Philippians 4:11 Not that I speak according to lack, for I learned to be sufficient in the things in which I am.
Philippians 4:12 And I know to be humbled, and know to abound; in everything and in all things I have been initiated both to be filled and to hunger, both to abound and to lack.
Philippians 4:13 I have strength for all things in Christ who empowers me.
Philippians 4:14 Nevertheless you did well, sharing together in my affliction.
Philippians 4:15 And you too know, Philippians, that at the beginning of the gospel, when I went out from Macedonia, no church shared with me in an account of giving and receiving except you alone,
Philippians 4:16 because even in Thessalonica you sent both once and twice for my need.
Philippians 4:17 Not that I seek the gift, but I seek the fruit increasing unto your account.
Philippians 4:18 But I have received everything and abound; I have been filled, receiving from Epaphroditus the things from you, an odor of fragrance, an acceptable sacrifice, pleasing to God.
Philippians 4:19 And my God will fill every need of yours according to his riches in glory in Christ Jesus.
Philippians 4:20 And to our God and Father the glory unto the ages of the ages. Amen.
Philippians 4:21 Greet every saint in Christ Jesus. The brothers with me greet you.
Philippians 4:22 All the saints greet you, and especially those of Caesar's household.
Philippians 4:23 The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with you all. Amen.

# Colossians

The Apostolic Bible. Public domain. https://apostolic-bible.ysys9.chatgpt.site/license.html


## Chapter 1

Colossians 1:1 Paul, an apostle of Jesus Christ through God's will, and Timothy the brother,
Colossians 1:2 to the saints and faithful brothers in Christ in Colossae: grace to you and peace from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ.
Colossians 1:3 We thank the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, always praying concerning you,
Colossians 1:4 having heard your faith in Christ Jesus and the love toward all the saints,
Colossians 1:5 because of the hope laid away for you in the heavens, which you heard beforehand in the word of the truth of the gospel,
Colossians 1:6 which is present with you, just as also in all the world, and is bearing fruit, just as also among you from the day you heard and fully knew God's grace in truth,
Colossians 1:7 just as you also learned from Epaphras our beloved fellow slave, who is a faithful minister of Christ for you,
Colossians 1:8 who also made clear to us your love in spirit.
Colossians 1:9 For this reason we too, from the day we heard, do not cease praying for you and asking that you may be filled with knowledge of his will in all spiritual wisdom and understanding,
Colossians 1:10 for you to walk worthily of the Lord unto all pleasing, bearing fruit in every good work and growing unto knowledge of God,
Colossians 1:11 empowered with all power according to the might of his glory, unto all endurance and patience with joy,
Colossians 1:12 giving thanks to the Father who made us fit for the portion of the inheritance of the saints in the light,
Colossians 1:13 who rescued us from the authority of darkness and transferred us into the kingdom of the Son of his love,
Colossians 1:14 in whom we have redemption through his blood, forgiveness of sins,
Colossians 1:15 who is an image of the invisible God, firstborn of all creation,
Colossians 1:16 because in him all things were created, those in the heavens and those upon earth, visible and invisible, whether thrones or lordships or rulers or authorities; all things have been created through him and unto him,
Colossians 1:17 and he is before all things, and all things have held together in him,
Colossians 1:18 and he is the head of the body, the church, who is beginning, firstborn from the dead, so that he may become first in all things,
Colossians 1:19 because in him all the fullness was pleased to dwell,
Colossians 1:20 and through him to reconcile all things unto him, making peace through the blood of his cross, through him, whether the things upon earth or those in the heavens.
Colossians 1:21 And you, once being alienated and enemies in thought in evil works, but now he reconciled,
Colossians 1:22 in the body of his flesh through death, to present you holy and blameless and unaccused before him,
Colossians 1:23 if indeed you remain in faith, founded and firm, and not moved away from the hope of the gospel which you heard, proclaimed in all creation under heaven, of which I, Paul, became a minister.
Colossians 1:24 Now I rejoice in my sufferings for you, and fill up in turn the lacks of Christ's afflictions in my flesh for his body, which is the church,
Colossians 1:25 of which I became a minister according to God's stewardship given to me for you, to fulfill God's word,
Colossians 1:26 the mystery hidden from the ages and from the generations, but now manifested to his saints,
Colossians 1:27 to whom God wanted to make known what are the riches of the glory of this mystery among the nations, which is Christ in you, the hope of glory,
Colossians 1:28 whom we proclaim, admonishing every man and teaching every man in all wisdom, so that we may present every man mature in Christ Jesus,
Colossians 1:29 for which I also labor, struggling according to his working which works in me in power.

## Chapter 2

Colossians 2:1 For I want you to know how great a struggle I have concerning you and those in Laodicea and as many as have not seen my face in flesh,
Colossians 2:2 so that their hearts may be encouraged, being joined together in love and unto all riches of the full assurance of understanding, unto knowledge of the mystery of God and Father and of Christ,
Colossians 2:3 in whom all the treasures of wisdom and knowledge are hidden.
Colossians 2:4 And I say this so that no one may deceive you with persuasive speech.
Colossians 2:5 For even if I am absent in flesh, yet in spirit I am with you, rejoicing and seeing your order and the firmness of your faith toward Christ.
Colossians 2:6 Therefore, as you received Christ Jesus the Lord, walk in him,
Colossians 2:7 rooted and built upon in him and confirmed in the faith, just as you were taught, abounding in it in thanksgiving.
Colossians 2:8 Watch lest there be someone carrying you off as spoil through philosophy and empty deceit, according to people's tradition, according to the world's elements and not according to Christ,
Colossians 2:9 because in him all the fullness of deity dwells bodily,
Colossians 2:10 and you have been filled in him, who is the head of every rule and authority,
Colossians 2:11 in whom you were also circumcised with a circumcision not made by hands, in the stripping off of the body of the sins of the flesh, in Christ's circumcision,
Colossians 2:12 buried together with him in baptism, in which you were also raised together through faith of the working of God who raised him from the dead.
Colossians 2:13 And you, being dead in trespasses and the uncircumcision of your flesh, he made alive together with him, forgiving us all the trespasses,
Colossians 2:14 wiping out the handwritten document against us in decrees, which was opposed to us, and he has taken it out of the midst, nailing it to the cross,
Colossians 2:15 stripping off the rulers and authorities, he displayed them in boldness, triumphing over them in it.
Colossians 2:16 Therefore let no one judge you in eating or drinking or in respect of a feast or new moon or sabbaths,
Colossians 2:17 which are a shadow of the coming things, but the body is Christ's.
Colossians 2:18 Let no one disqualify you, wanting in humility and worship of angels, entering into things he has not seen, vainly puffed up by the mind of his flesh,
Colossians 2:19 and not holding the head, from whom the whole body, supplied and joined together through joints and bonds, grows with God's growth.
Colossians 2:20 Therefore, if you died with Christ from the world's elements, why, as living in a world, are you subjected to decrees,
Colossians 2:21 “Do not handle, nor taste, nor touch,”
Colossians 2:22 which are all unto corruption through use, according to people's commandments and teachings?
Colossians 2:23 These indeed have an appearance of wisdom in self-chosen worship and humility and unsparing treatment of body, not in any honor toward satisfaction of the flesh.

## Chapter 3

Colossians 3:1 Therefore, if you were raised together with Christ, seek the things above, where Christ is, seated at God's right hand.
Colossians 3:2 Mind the things above, not those upon earth,
Colossians 3:3 for you died, and your life has been hidden with Christ in God.
Colossians 3:4 When Christ, our life, is manifested, then you too will be manifested with him in glory.
Colossians 3:5 Therefore put to death your members upon earth: sexual immorality, impurity, passion, evil desire, and greed, which is idolatry,
Colossians 3:6 because of which God's wrath comes upon the sons of disobedience,
Colossians 3:7 in which you too once walked, when you lived in them.
Colossians 3:8 But now you too put off everything: wrath, fury, malice, slander, shameful speech from your mouth.
Colossians 3:9 Do not lie to one another, having stripped off the old man with his practices,
Colossians 3:10 and put on the new, renewed unto knowledge according to the image of the one who created him,
Colossians 3:11 where there is no Greek and Jew, circumcision and uncircumcision, barbarian, Scythian, slave, free, but Christ all things and in all.
Colossians 3:12 Therefore put on, as God's chosen ones, holy and beloved, inward affections of compassion, kindness, humility, gentleness, patience,
Colossians 3:13 bearing with one another and forgiving one another, if someone has a complaint against someone; just as Christ also forgave you, so you too.
Colossians 3:14 And above all these, love, which is the bond of perfection.
Colossians 3:15 And let God's peace arbitrate in your hearts, unto which you were also called in one body, and become thankful.
Colossians 3:16 Let Christ's word dwell in you richly, in all wisdom teaching and admonishing one another, in psalms and hymns and spiritual songs, in grace singing in your heart to the Lord.
Colossians 3:17 And everything, whatever you do in word or deed, all in the Lord Jesus's name, giving thanks to God and Father through him.
Colossians 3:18 Wives, submit to your own husbands, as was fitting in the Lord.
Colossians 3:19 Husbands, love the wives and do not be embittered toward them.
Colossians 3:20 Children, obey the parents in everything, for this is pleasing to the Lord.
Colossians 3:21 Fathers, do not provoke your children, so that they may not lose heart.
Colossians 3:22 Slaves, obey in everything the lords according to flesh, not in eye-services as people-pleasers, but in simplicity of heart, fearing God.
Colossians 3:23 And everything, whatever you do, work from the soul, as to the Lord and not to people,
Colossians 3:24 knowing that from the Lord you will receive the recompense of the inheritance, for you serve as slaves to the Lord Christ.
Colossians 3:25 But the one wronging will receive what he wronged, and there is no partiality.

## Chapter 4

Colossians 4:1 Lords, provide the righteous thing and equality to the slaves, knowing that you too have a Lord in heavens.
Colossians 4:2 Persevere in prayer, keeping watch in it in thanksgiving,
Colossians 4:3 praying together also concerning us, so that God may open to us a door of the word, to speak Christ's mystery, because of which I have also been bound,
Colossians 4:4 so that I may manifest it as I ought to speak.
Colossians 4:5 Walk in wisdom toward those outside, buying out the time.
Colossians 4:6 Let your word always be in grace, seasoned with salt, to know how you ought to answer each one.
Colossians 4:7 Tychicus, the beloved brother and faithful minister and fellow slave in the Lord, will make known to you all the things concerning me,
Colossians 4:8 whom I sent to you for this very thing, so that he may know the things concerning you and encourage your hearts,
Colossians 4:9 with Onesimus the faithful and beloved brother, who is from you. They will make known to you all the things here.
Colossians 4:10 Aristarchus my fellow captive greets you, and Mark, Barnabas's cousin, concerning whom you received commands: if he comes to you, receive him,
Colossians 4:11 and Jesus called Justus, who are of circumcision. These alone are fellow workers unto God's kingdom, who became consolation to me.
Colossians 4:12 Epaphras, who is from you, Christ's slave, greets you, always struggling for you in prayers, so that you may stand mature and filled in every will of God.
Colossians 4:13 For I testify to him that he has much zeal for you and those in Laodicea and those in Hierapolis.
Colossians 4:14 Luke the beloved physician greets you, and Demas.
Colossians 4:15 Greet the brothers in Laodicea, and Nymphas and the church in his house.
Colossians 4:16 And when the letter is read among you, make it also be read in the church of the Laodiceans, and you too read the one from Laodicea.
Colossians 4:17 And say to Archippus, “Watch the ministry which you received in the Lord, so that you may fulfill it.”
Colossians 4:18 The greeting by my own hand, Paul's. Remember my bonds. Grace be with you. Amen.

# 1 Thessalonians

The Apostolic Bible. Public domain. https://apostolic-bible.ysys9.chatgpt.site/license.html


## Chapter 1

1 Thessalonians 1:1 Paul and Silvanus and Timothy, to the church of Thessalonians in God the Father and the Lord Jesus Christ: grace to you and peace from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ.
1 Thessalonians 1:2 We thank God always concerning you all, making mention of you in our prayers,
1 Thessalonians 1:3 unceasingly remembering your work of faith and labor of love and endurance of hope of our Lord Jesus Christ, before our God and Father,
1 Thessalonians 1:4 knowing, brothers beloved by God, your choice,
1 Thessalonians 1:5 because our gospel came to you not in word only, but also in power and in the Holy Spirit and in much full assurance, just as you know what sort we became among you because of you.
1 Thessalonians 1:6 And you became imitators of us and of the Lord, receiving the word in much affliction with joy of the Holy Spirit,
1 Thessalonians 1:7 so that you became patterns to all those believing in Macedonia and Achaia.
1 Thessalonians 1:8 For from you the Lord's word has sounded out, not only in Macedonia and Achaia, but also in every place your faith toward God has gone out, so that we have no need to speak anything.
1 Thessalonians 1:9 For they themselves report concerning us what sort of entrance we have to you, and how you turned to God from the idols to serve as slaves to a living and true God,
1 Thessalonians 1:10 and await his Son from the heavens, whom he raised from the dead, Jesus who rescues us from the coming wrath.

## Chapter 2

1 Thessalonians 2:1 For you yourselves know, brothers, our entrance to you, that it has not become empty,
1 Thessalonians 2:2 but even having suffered beforehand and been insulted, as you know, in Philippi, we were bold in our God to speak God's gospel to you in much struggle.
1 Thessalonians 2:3 For our exhortation is not from error nor from impurity nor in deceit,
1 Thessalonians 2:4 but just as we have been approved by God to be entrusted with the gospel, so we speak, not as pleasing people but God who examines our hearts.
1 Thessalonians 2:5 For neither did we ever come in a word of flattery, as you know, nor in a pretext of greed, God is witness,
1 Thessalonians 2:6 nor seeking glory from people, neither from you nor from others, being able to be a burden as Christ's apostles.
1 Thessalonians 2:7 But we became gentle in your midst, as a nurse cherishes her own children.
1 Thessalonians 2:8 Thus yearning for you, we were pleased to share with you not only God's gospel but also our own souls, because you have become beloved to us.
1 Thessalonians 2:9 For you remember, brothers, our labor and toil, for working night and day so as not to burden any of you, we preached God's gospel to you.
1 Thessalonians 2:10 You are witnesses, and God, how holily and righteously and blamelessly we became toward you who believe,
1 Thessalonians 2:11 just as you know how, as a father his own children, we encouraged each one of you and consoled you,
1 Thessalonians 2:12 and testified, for you to walk worthily of God who calls you into his own kingdom and glory.
1 Thessalonians 2:13 For this reason we too thank God unceasingly, because receiving a word of hearing from us, of God, you accepted not a word of people but, just as it truly is, God's word, which also works in you who believe.
1 Thessalonians 2:14 For you became imitators, brothers, of God's churches in Judea in Christ Jesus, because you too suffered the same things from your own countrymen as they also from the Jews,
1 Thessalonians 2:15 who both killed the Lord Jesus and their own prophets and drove you out, and do not please God and are opposed to all people,
1 Thessalonians 2:16 preventing us from speaking to the nations so that they may be saved, to fill up their sins always; but wrath came upon them unto the end.
1 Thessalonians 2:17 But we, brothers, orphaned from you for an hour's time, in face, not heart, were more abundantly diligent to see your face in much desire.
1 Thessalonians 2:18 Therefore we wanted to come to you, I, Paul, both once and twice, and Satan hindered us.
1 Thessalonians 2:19 For what is our hope or joy or crown of boasting? Or is it not also you before our Lord Jesus Christ at his coming?
1 Thessalonians 2:20 For you are our glory and joy.

## Chapter 3

1 Thessalonians 3:1 Therefore, no longer bearing it, we were pleased to be left in Athens alone,
1 Thessalonians 3:2 and sent Timothy, our brother and God's minister and our fellow worker in Christ's gospel, to strengthen you and encourage you concerning your faith,
1 Thessalonians 3:3 so that no one be shaken in these afflictions, for you yourselves know that we are appointed to this.

## Chapter 1
