2 Timothy 2:19 Nevertheless God's firm foundation stands, having this seal: “The Lord knew those who are his,” and “Let everyone naming Christ's name depart from unrighteousness.”
2 Timothy 2:20 And in a great house there are not only gold and silver vessels, but also wooden and earthen, and some for honor, some for dishonor.
2 Timothy 2:21 Therefore if someone cleanses himself from these, he will be a vessel for honor, sanctified and useful to the master, prepared for every good work.
2 Timothy 2:22 And flee youthful desires, but pursue righteousness, faith, love, peace with those calling upon the Lord from a pure heart.
2 Timothy 2:23 But refuse foolish and uninstructed inquiries, knowing that they bear fights.
2 Timothy 2:24 And the Lord's slave must not fight, but be gentle toward all, able to teach, patient under evil,
2 Timothy 2:25 in gentleness disciplining those opposing, lest perhaps God give them repentance unto knowledge of truth,
2 Timothy 2:26 and they become sober again out of the devil's snare, having been captured alive by him unto his will.

## Chapter 3

2 Timothy 3:1 And know this, that in last days difficult times will come.
2 Timothy 3:2 For people will be self-lovers, silver-lovers, boastful, arrogant, blasphemers, disobedient to parents, unthankful, unholy,
2 Timothy 3:3 without natural affection, implacable, slanderers, without self-control, untamed, not loving good,
2 Timothy 3:4 traitors, reckless, puffed up, pleasure-lovers rather than God-lovers,
2 Timothy 3:5 having a form of piety but having denied its power; and turn away from these.
2 Timothy 3:6 For from these are those entering the houses and taking captive the little women heaped with sins, led by various desires,
2 Timothy 3:7 always learning and never able to come unto knowledge of truth.
2 Timothy 3:8 And in the way Jannes and Jambres opposed Moses, so these too oppose the truth, people corrupted in mind, disapproved concerning faith.
2 Timothy 3:9 But they will not advance further, for their senselessness will be evident to all, as that of those also became.
2 Timothy 3:10 But you have followed my teaching, conduct, purpose, faith, patience, love, endurance,
2 Timothy 3:11 persecutions, sufferings, such as happened to me in Antioch, in Iconium, in Lystra, what sort of persecutions I endured; and from all the Lord rescued me.
2 Timothy 3:12 And also all those wanting to live piously in Christ Jesus will be persecuted.
2 Timothy 3:13 But evil people and impostors will advance toward the worse, deceiving and being deceived.
2 Timothy 3:14 But you remain in what you learned and were assured of, knowing from whom you learned,
2 Timothy 3:15 and that from infancy you know the sacred letters, able to make you wise unto salvation through faith in Christ Jesus.
2 Timothy 3:16 Every writing is God-breathed and beneficial for teaching, for conviction, for correction, for discipline in righteousness,
2 Timothy 3:17 so that God's man may be complete, equipped for every good work.

## Chapter 4

2 Timothy 4:1 Therefore I solemnly testify before God and the Lord Jesus Christ, who is about to judge living and dead according to his manifestation and his kingdom:
2 Timothy 4:2 preach the word, stand ready opportunely, inopportunely, convict, rebuke, exhort in all patience and teaching.
2 Timothy 4:3 For a time will be when they will not bear the healthy teaching, but according to their own desires will heap up teachers for themselves, itching in hearing,
2 Timothy 4:4 and will turn their hearing away from the truth, but turn aside to the myths.
2 Timothy 4:5 But you be sober in everything, suffer hardship, do an evangelist's work, fulfill your ministry.
2 Timothy 4:6 For I am already being poured out, and the time of my departure has come.
2 Timothy 4:7 I have struggled the good struggle, completed the race, kept the faith.
2 Timothy 4:8 Henceforth the crown of righteousness is laid away for me, which the Lord, the righteous judge, will repay me on that day, and not to me only but also to all who have loved his manifestation.
2 Timothy 4:9 Be diligent to come to me quickly,
2 Timothy 4:10 for Demas abandoned me, loving the present age, and traveled to Thessalonica, Crescens to Galatia, Titus to Dalmatia.
2 Timothy 4:11 Luke alone is with me. Taking Mark, bring him with yourself, for he is useful to me for ministry.
2 Timothy 4:12 And I sent Tychicus to Ephesus.
2 Timothy 4:13 When coming, bring the cloak which I left in Troas with Carpus, and the books, especially the parchments.
2 Timothy 4:14 Alexander the coppersmith demonstrated many evil things to me; may the Lord repay him according to his works.
2 Timothy 4:15 You too guard against him, for he greatly opposed our words.
2 Timothy 4:16 At my first defense no one stood with me, but all abandoned me; may it not be reckoned to them.
2 Timothy 4:17 But the Lord stood by me and empowered me, so that through me the proclamation may be fulfilled and all the nations hear; and I was rescued from a lion's mouth.
2 Timothy 4:18 And the Lord will rescue me from every evil work and save me unto his heavenly kingdom, to whom the glory unto the ages of the ages. Amen.
2 Timothy 4:19 Greet Prisca and Aquila and Onesiphorus's household.
2 Timothy 4:20 Erastus remained in Corinth, but I left Trophimus in Miletus sick.
2 Timothy 4:21 Be diligent to come before winter. Eubulus greets you, and Pudens and Linus and Claudia and all the brothers.
2 Timothy 4:22 The Lord Jesus Christ be with your spirit. Grace be with you. Amen.

# Titus

## Chapter 1

Titus 1:1 Paul, God's slave and an apostle of Jesus Christ, according to faith of God's chosen ones and knowledge of truth according to piety,
Titus 1:2 upon hope of eternal life, which God who does not lie promised before eternal times,
Titus 1:3 but manifested his word in its own times in proclamation, with which I was entrusted according to the command of God our Savior,
Titus 1:4 to Titus, genuine child according to common faith: grace, mercy, peace from God the Father and the Lord Jesus Christ our Savior.
Titus 1:5 For this reason I left you in Crete, so that you may set right the things lacking and appoint elders city by city, as I directed you,
Titus 1:6 if someone is unaccused, husband of one wife, having faithful children, not in accusation of dissipation or unsubmissive.
Titus 1:7 For the overseer must be unaccused as God's steward, not self-willed, not prone to anger, not given to wine, not a striker, not greedy for shameful gain,
Titus 1:8 but hospitable, loving good, sound-minded, righteous, holy, self-controlled,
Titus 1:9 holding to the faithful word according to the teaching, so that he may be able both to exhort in the healthy teaching and convict those contradicting.
Titus 1:10 For there are also many unsubmissive people, futile speakers and mind-deceivers, especially those of circumcision,
Titus 1:11 whose mouths must be stopped, who overturn whole households, teaching what they ought not, for shameful gain.
Titus 1:12 Someone from them, their own prophet, said, “Cretans always liars, evil beasts, idle bellies.”
Titus 1:13 This testimony is true; for which reason convict them severely, so that they may be healthy in faith,
Titus 1:14 not attending to Jewish myths and commandments of people turning away from the truth.
Titus 1:15 All things indeed are clean to the clean, but to the defiled and unbelieving nothing is clean, but both their mind and conscience have been defiled.
Titus 1:16 They confess to know God, but deny him in works, being abominable and disobedient and disapproved for every good work.

## Chapter 2

Titus 2:1 But you speak what is fitting for the healthy teaching,
Titus 2:2 for older men to be sober, dignified, sound-minded, healthy in faith, in love, in endurance;
Titus 2:3 older women likewise reverent in demeanor, not slanderers, not enslaved to much wine, teachers of good,
Titus 2:4 so that they may train the young women to be husband-lovers, child-lovers,
Titus 2:5 sound-minded, pure, keepers at home, good, submitting to their own husbands, so that God's word may not be blasphemed.
Titus 2:6 Likewise urge the younger men to be sound-minded,
Titus 2:7 in everything providing yourself as a pattern of good works, in the teaching incorruption, dignity, incorruptibility,
Titus 2:8 a healthy word not condemnable, so that the one on the opposing side may be shamed, having nothing bad to say concerning you.
Titus 2:9 Slaves to submit to their own masters, to be pleasing in everything, not contradicting,
Titus 2:10 not pilfering, but demonstrating all good faithfulness, so that they may adorn the teaching of God your Savior in everything.
Titus 2:11 For God's grace appeared, saving for all people,
Titus 2:12 disciplining us, so that denying ungodliness and worldly desires, we may live sound-mindedly and righteously and piously in the present age,
Titus 2:13 awaiting the blessed hope and manifestation of the glory of our great God and Savior Jesus Christ,
Titus 2:14 who gave himself for us, so that he may redeem us from all lawlessness and cleanse for himself a special people, zealous for good works.
Titus 2:15 Speak these things and exhort and convict with all command. Let no one despise you.

## Chapter 3

Titus 3:1 Remind them to submit to rulers and authorities, to obey, to be ready for every good work,
Titus 3:2 to slander no one, to be unquarrelsome, fair, demonstrating all gentleness toward all people.
Titus 3:3 For we too once were senseless, disobedient, deceived, serving as slaves to various desires and pleasures, living in malice and envy, hateful, hating one another.
Titus 3:4 But when the kindness and love for humanity of God our Savior appeared,
Titus 3:5 not from works in righteousness which we did, but according to his mercy he saved us, through washing of rebirth and renewal of the Holy Spirit,
Titus 3:6 whom he poured out upon us richly through Jesus Christ our Savior,
Titus 3:7 so that justified by his grace we may become heirs according to hope of eternal life.
Titus 3:8 The word is faithful, and concerning these things I want you to affirm, so that those who have believed God may care to lead in good works. These things are good and beneficial for people.
Titus 3:9 But avoid foolish inquiries and genealogies and strifes and legal fights, for they are unbeneficial and futile.
Titus 3:10 Refuse a heretical man after a first and second admonition,
Titus 3:11 knowing that such a one has been perverted and sins, being self-condemned.
Titus 3:12 When I send Artemas to you or Tychicus, be diligent to come to me in Nicopolis, for there I have decided to winter.
Titus 3:13 Send onward Zenas the lawyer and Apollos diligently, so that nothing may lack to them.
Titus 3:14 And let our people too learn to lead in good works for necessary needs, so that they may not be fruitless.
Titus 3:15 All those with me greet you. Greet those loving us in faith. Grace be with you all. Amen.

# Philemon

The Apostolic Bible. Public domain. https://apostolic-bible.ysys9.chatgpt.site/license.html


## Chapter 1

Philemon 1:1 Paul, Christ Jesus's prisoner, and Timothy the brother, to Philemon our beloved and fellow worker,
Philemon 1:2 and Apphia the beloved and Archippus our fellow soldier and the church in your house:
Philemon 1:3 grace to you and peace from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ.
Philemon 1:4 I thank my God always, making mention of you in my prayers,
Philemon 1:5 hearing your love and faith which you have toward the Lord Jesus and toward all the saints,
Philemon 1:6 so that the fellowship of your faith may become effective in knowledge of every good thing in you unto Christ Jesus.
Philemon 1:7 For we have much thanks and encouragement for your love, because the inward affections of the saints have been refreshed through you, brother.
Philemon 1:8 Therefore, having much boldness in Christ to command you what is fitting,
Philemon 1:9 because of love I rather urge, being such a one as Paul, an old man, and now also Jesus Christ's prisoner.
Philemon 1:10 I urge you concerning my child whom I begot in my bonds, Onesimus,
Philemon 1:11 formerly useless to you, but now useful to you and me,
Philemon 1:12 whom I sent back; but you receive him, that is, my inward affections,
Philemon 1:13 whom I wanted to keep with myself, so that for you he may minister to me in the bonds of the gospel.
Philemon 1:14 But without your judgment I wanted to do nothing, so that your good may not be as according to necessity but according to willingness.
Philemon 1:15 For perhaps for this reason he was separated for an hour, so that you may have him eternally,
Philemon 1:16 no longer as a slave but beyond a slave, a beloved brother, especially to me, but how much more to you, both in flesh and in the Lord.
Philemon 1:17 Therefore if you hold me as a partner, receive him as me.
Philemon 1:18 But if he wronged you anything or owes, charge this to me.
Philemon 1:19 I, Paul, wrote with my own hand, I will repay, so that I may not tell you that you also owe yourself to me besides.
Philemon 1:20 Yes, brother, may I benefit from you in the Lord; refresh my inward affections in the Lord.
Philemon 1:21 Trusting your obedience, I wrote to you, knowing that you will also do beyond what I say.
Philemon 1:22 And at the same time also prepare lodging for me, for I hope that through your prayers I will be freely given to you.
Philemon 1:23 Epaphras my fellow captive in Christ Jesus greets you,
Philemon 1:24 Mark, Aristarchus, Demas, Luke, my fellow workers.
Philemon 1:25 The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with your spirit. Amen.

# Hebrews

The Apostolic Bible. Public domain. https://apostolic-bible.ysys9.chatgpt.site/license.html


## Chapter 1

Hebrews 1:1 In many portions and many ways, God, having spoken long ago to the fathers in the prophets,
Hebrews 1:2 at the last of these days spoke to us in a Son, whom he appointed heir of all things, through whom he also made the ages,
Hebrews 1:3 who, being radiance of the glory and imprint of his substance, and carrying all things by the word of his power, having made purification of our sins through himself, sat at the right hand of the Majesty in high places,
Hebrews 1:4 becoming so much better than the angels as he has inherited a name more excellent than theirs.
Hebrews 1:5 For to which of the angels did he ever say, “You are my Son, I today have begotten you,” and again, “I will be a Father to him, and he will be a Son to me”?
Hebrews 1:6 And when he again brings the firstborn into the inhabited world, he says, “And let all God's angels worship him.”
Hebrews 1:7 And concerning the angels he says, “The one making his angels spirits and his servants a flame of fire,”
Hebrews 1:8 but concerning the Son, “Your throne, O God, is unto the age of the age; a rod of uprightness is the rod of your kingdom.
Hebrews 1:9 You loved righteousness and hated lawlessness; for this reason God, your God, anointed you with oil of exultation beyond your partners.”
Hebrews 1:10 And, “You, at the beginnings, Lord, founded the earth, and the heavens are works of your hands.
Hebrews 1:11 They will perish, but you remain, and all will grow old as a garment,
Hebrews 1:12 and as a covering you will roll them up, and they will be changed; but you are the same, and your years will not fail.”
Hebrews 1:13 But to which of the angels has he ever said, “Sit at my right hand until I place your enemies as a footstool of your feet”?
Hebrews 1:14 Are they not all serving spirits, sent out for ministry because of those about to inherit salvation?

## Chapter 2

Hebrews 2:1 For this reason we must attend more abundantly to the things heard, lest we drift away.
Hebrews 2:2 For if the word spoken through angels became firm, and every transgression and disobedience received a just recompense,
Hebrews 2:3 how will we escape, neglecting so great a salvation, which, beginning to be spoken through the Lord, was confirmed to us by those who heard,
Hebrews 2:4 God bearing witness together with signs and wonders and various powers and distributions of the Holy Spirit according to his own will?
Hebrews 2:5 For not to angels did he subject the coming inhabited world, concerning which we speak.
Hebrews 2:6 But someone somewhere solemnly testified, saying, “What is man, that you remember him, or a son of man, that you visit him?
Hebrews 2:7 You made him a little lower than angels; you crowned him with glory and honor and appointed him over the works of your hands;
Hebrews 2:8 you subjected all things beneath his feet.” For in subjecting all things to him, he left nothing unsubmissive to him; but now we do not yet see all things subjected to him.
Hebrews 2:9 But we see Jesus, made a little lower than angels, crowned with glory and honor because of the suffering of death, so that by God's grace he may taste death for everyone.
Hebrews 2:10 For it was fitting for him, because of whom are all things and through whom are all things, bringing many sons into glory, to perfect the founder of their salvation through sufferings.
Hebrews 2:11 For both the one sanctifying and those being sanctified are all from one, for which reason he is not ashamed to call them brothers,
Hebrews 2:12 saying, “I will announce your name to my brothers; in the midst of an assembly I will hymn you.”
Hebrews 2:13 And again, “I will be trusting upon him,” and again, “Look, I and the children whom God gave me.”
Hebrews 2:14 Therefore, since the children have shared flesh and blood, he himself also similarly partook of the same, so that through death he may nullify the one having the might of death, that is, the devil,
Hebrews 2:15 and release those who through fear of death were liable to slavery throughout all their living.
Hebrews 2:16 For surely he does not take hold of angels, but takes hold of Abraham's seed.
Hebrews 2:17 Therefore he ought to be made like the brothers in everything, so that he may become a merciful and faithful high priest in the things toward God, to make propitiation for the people's sins.
Hebrews 2:18 For in that he himself has suffered, being tempted, he is able to help those being tempted.

## Chapter 3

Hebrews 3:1 Therefore, holy brothers, partners of a heavenly calling, consider the apostle and high priest of our confession, Christ Jesus,
Hebrews 3:2 being faithful to the one who made him, as also Moses in all his house.
Hebrews 3:3 For this one has been counted worthy of more glory than Moses, insofar as the one who constructed the house has more honor than it.
Hebrews 3:4 For every house is constructed by someone, but the one who constructed all things is God.
Hebrews 3:5 And Moses indeed faithful in all his house as an attendant, for a testimony of the things to be spoken,
Hebrews 3:6 but Christ as a Son over his house, whose house we are, if indeed we hold firm the boldness and boast of hope until the end.
Hebrews 3:7 Therefore, just as the Holy Spirit says, “Today, if you hear his voice,
Hebrews 3:8 do not harden your hearts as in the provocation, on the day of temptation in the wilderness,
Hebrews 3:9 where your fathers tempted me, tested me, and saw my works forty years.
Hebrews 3:10 Therefore I was indignant with that generation and said, ‘They always err in heart, and they did not know my ways.’
Hebrews 3:11 As I swore in my wrath, ‘They shall not enter my rest.’”
Hebrews 3:12 Watch, brothers, lest there be in someone of you an evil heart of unbelief in departing from the living God,
Hebrews 3:13 but encourage one another each day, as long as it is called Today, so that no one of you may be hardened by sin's deceit.
Hebrews 3:14 For we have become partners of Christ, if indeed we hold firm the beginning of the confidence until the end,
Hebrews 3:15 in its being said, “Today, if you hear his voice, do not harden your hearts as in the provocation.”
Hebrews 3:16 For who, having heard, provoked? But was it not all those who came out from Egypt through Moses?
Hebrews 3:17 And with whom was he indignant forty years? Was it not those who sinned, whose limbs fell in the wilderness?
Hebrews 3:18 And to whom did he swear that they would not enter his rest, except those who disobeyed?
Hebrews 3:19 And we see that they could not enter because of unbelief.

## Chapter 4

Hebrews 4:1 Therefore let us fear lest, a promise of entering his rest being left, someone of you may seem to have fallen short.
Hebrews 4:2 For we too have had good news proclaimed, just as those also; but the word of hearing did not benefit those, not having been mixed with faith for those who heard.
Hebrews 4:3 For we who believed enter the rest, just as he has said, “As I swore in my wrath, ‘They shall not enter my rest,’” although the works had come to be from a world's foundation.
Hebrews 4:4 For he has said somewhere concerning the seventh thus, “And God rested on the seventh day from all his works,”
Hebrews 4:5 and in this again, “They shall not enter my rest.”
Hebrews 4:6 Therefore, since it remains for some to enter it, and those formerly receiving good news did not enter because of disobedience,
Hebrews 4:7 again he designates some day, Today, saying in David after so much time, just as it has been said, “Today, if you hear his voice, do not harden your hearts.”
Hebrews 4:8 For if Joshua gave them rest, he would not speak after these things concerning another day.
Hebrews 4:9 Therefore a sabbath rest remains for God's people.
Hebrews 4:10 For the one entering his rest also himself rested from his works, just as God from his own.
Hebrews 4:11 Therefore let us be diligent to enter that rest, so that no one may fall in the same example of disobedience.
Hebrews 4:12 For God's word is living and effective and sharper than every two-edged sword, and penetrating until division of both soul and spirit, both joints and marrows, and judging thoughts and intentions of heart.
Hebrews 4:13 And there is no creation invisible before him, but all things naked and laid bare to his eyes, to whom our account is.
Hebrews 4:14 Therefore, having a great high priest who has passed through the heavens, Jesus God's Son, let us hold the confession.
Hebrews 4:15 For we do not have a high priest unable to sympathize with our weaknesses, but one tempted in everything according to likeness, without sin.
Hebrews 4:16 Therefore let us approach the throne of grace with boldness, so that we may receive mercy and find grace for timely help.

## Chapter 5

Hebrews 5:1 For every high priest, taken from among men, is appointed on behalf of men in the things pertaining to God, so that he may offer both gifts and sacrifices for sins,
Hebrews 5:2 being able to deal moderately with those who are ignorant and wandering, since he himself is also surrounded by weakness.
Hebrews 5:3 And because of this he is obliged, just as for the people, so also for himself, to offer for sins.
Hebrews 5:4 And no one takes the honor for himself, but the one called by God, just as Aaron also was.
Hebrews 5:5 So also Christ did not glorify himself to become high priest, but the one who spoke to him: You are my Son; today I have begotten you.
Hebrews 5:6 As he also says in another place: You are a priest forever according to the order of Melchizedek.
Hebrews 5:7 Who, in the days of his flesh, having offered both petitions and supplications to the one able to save him out of death, with a strong cry and tears, and having been heard because of his reverence,
Hebrews 5:8 although being a Son, learned obedience from the things he suffered.
Hebrews 5:9 And having been perfected, he became the cause of eternal salvation to all those obeying him,
Hebrews 5:10 being designated by God high priest according to the order of Melchizedek.
Hebrews 5:11 Concerning whom we have much to say, and difficult to explain in speaking, since you have become sluggish in hearing.
Hebrews 5:12 For although you ought to be teachers because of the time, you again have need of someone to teach you the elements of the beginning of the oracles of God, and you have come to have need of milk and not solid food.
Hebrews 5:13 For everyone partaking of milk is inexperienced in the word of righteousness, for he is an infant.
Hebrews 5:14 But solid food belongs to the mature, those who through practice have their senses trained for distinguishing both good and evil.

## Chapter 6

Hebrews 6:1 Therefore, leaving the word of the beginning of Christ, let us be carried on to perfection, not laying down again a foundation of repentance from dead works and faith toward God,
Hebrews 6:2 of instruction concerning washings, and laying on of hands, and resurrection of the dead, and eternal judgment.
Hebrews 6:3 And this we will do, if indeed God permits.
Hebrews 6:4 For it is impossible for those once enlightened, who have tasted the heavenly gift and become partakers of the Holy Spirit,
Hebrews 6:5 and tasted the good word of God and powers of the coming age,
Hebrews 6:6 and fallen away, to renew them again to repentance, crucifying again for themselves the Son of God and exposing him publicly.
Hebrews 6:7 For land that has drunk the rain often coming upon it, and produces vegetation useful to those for whom it is also cultivated, partakes of blessing from God.
Hebrews 6:8 But producing thorns and thistles, it is rejected and near a curse, whose end is for burning.
Hebrews 6:9 But we are persuaded concerning you, beloved, of better things and things belonging to salvation, even if we speak thus.
Hebrews 6:10 For God is not unjust to forget your work and the labor of love which you displayed toward his name, having served the saints and serving them.
Hebrews 6:11 But we desire each of you to display the same diligence toward the full assurance of hope until the end,
Hebrews 6:12 so that you may not become sluggish, but imitators of those inheriting the promises through faith and patience.
Hebrews 6:13 For God, having made a promise to Abraham, since he had no one greater by whom to swear, swore by himself,
Hebrews 6:14 saying: Surely, blessing I will bless you, and multiplying I will multiply you.
Hebrews 6:15 And thus, having been patient, he obtained the promise.
Hebrews 6:16 For men indeed swear by the greater, and the oath for confirmation is an end to all dispute for them.
Hebrews 6:17 In which God, wishing more abundantly to show the heirs of the promise the unchangeableness of his purpose, intervened with an oath,
Hebrews 6:18 so that through two unchangeable things, in which it is impossible for God to lie, we who have fled for refuge might have strong encouragement to take hold of the hope set before us,
Hebrews 6:19 which we have as an anchor of the soul, both secure and firm, and entering into the interior of the curtain,
Hebrews 6:20 where Jesus entered as a forerunner on our behalf, having become high priest forever according to the order of Melchizedek.

## Chapter 7

Hebrews 7:1 For this Melchizedek, king of Salem, priest of God Most High, who met Abraham returning from the slaughter of the kings and blessed him,
Hebrews 7:2 to whom Abraham also apportioned a tenth from everything, is first, by interpretation, king of righteousness, and then also king of Salem, which is king of peace,
Hebrews 7:3 without father, without mother, without genealogy, having neither beginning of days nor end of life, but having been made like the Son of God, remains a priest continually.
Hebrews 7:4 But consider how great this man was, to whom even Abraham the patriarch gave a tenth from the spoils.
Hebrews 7:5 And indeed those from the sons of Levi receiving the priesthood have a commandment to take tithes from the people according to the law, that is, their brothers, although they have come out of the loins of Abraham.
Hebrews 7:6 But the one not tracing his genealogy from them has taken tithes from Abraham and has blessed the one having the promises.
Hebrews 7:7 But without any dispute the lesser is blessed by the better.
Hebrews 7:8 And here indeed dying men receive tithes, but there one who is testified to that he lives.
Hebrews 7:9 And, so to speak, through Abraham even Levi, who receives tithes, has been tithed.
Hebrews 7:10 For he was still in the loins of his father when Melchizedek met him.
Hebrews 7:11 If therefore perfection was through the Levitical priesthood, for the people had received the law on its basis, what further need was there for another priest to arise according to the order of Melchizedek and not to be called according to the order of Aaron?
Hebrews 7:12 For when the priesthood is changed, of necessity a change of law also takes place.
Hebrews 7:13 For the one of whom these things are said has partaken of another tribe, from which no one has attended to the altar.
Hebrews 7:14 For it is evident that our Lord has sprung from Judah, concerning which tribe Moses spoke nothing about priesthood.
Hebrews 7:15 And it is still more abundantly evident if another priest arises according to the likeness of Melchizedek,
Hebrews 7:16 who has become such, not according to a law of a fleshly commandment, but according to the power of an indestructible life.
Hebrews 7:17 For he testifies: You are a priest forever according to the order of Melchizedek.
Hebrews 7:18 For indeed a setting aside of the preceding commandment takes place because of its weakness and uselessness,
Hebrews 7:19 for the law perfected nothing, but there is a bringing in of a better hope, through which we draw near to God.
Hebrews 7:20 And insofar as it was not without an oath,
Hebrews 7:21 for they indeed have become priests without an oath, but he with an oath through the one saying to him: The Lord swore and will not change his mind: You are a priest forever according to the order of Melchizedek,
Hebrews 7:22 by so much Jesus has become guarantor of a better covenant.
Hebrews 7:23 And they indeed have become many priests because they are prevented by death from remaining.
Hebrews 7:24 But he, because he remains forever, has the priesthood that does not pass to another.
Hebrews 7:25 Therefore he is also able to save completely those approaching God through him, always living to intercede on their behalf.
Hebrews 7:26 For such a high priest was fitting for us, holy, innocent, undefiled, separated from sinners, and having become higher than the heavens,
Hebrews 7:27 who does not have a daily necessity, like the high priests, first to offer sacrifices for his own sins, then for those of the people; for this he did once for all, having offered himself.
Hebrews 7:28 For the law appoints men as high priests who have weakness, but the word of the oath, which came after the law, appoints a Son perfected forever.

## Chapter 8

Hebrews 8:1 Now the main point in the things being said: we have such a high priest, who sat down at the right hand of the throne of the Majesty in the heavens,
Hebrews 8:2 a minister of the holy places and of the true tent, which the Lord erected, and not man.
Hebrews 8:3 For every high priest is appointed to offer both gifts and sacrifices; therefore it is necessary for this one also to have something which he may offer.
Hebrews 8:4 For if he were on earth, he would not even be a priest, since there are priests offering the gifts according to the law,
Hebrews 8:5 who serve a copy and shadow of the heavenly things, just as Moses was instructed when about to complete the tent; for he says: See that you make everything according to the pattern shown to you on the mountain.
Hebrews 8:6 But now he has obtained a more excellent ministry, by as much as he is also mediator of a better covenant, which has been established as law upon better promises.
Hebrews 8:7 For if that first one were faultless, a place would not have been sought for a second.
Hebrews 8:8 For finding fault with them, he says: Behold, days are coming, says the Lord, and I will conclude a new covenant with the house of Israel and with the house of Judah,
Hebrews 8:9 not according to the covenant which I made with their fathers on the day when I took hold of their hand to lead them out of the land of Egypt, because they did not remain in my covenant, and I disregarded them, says the Lord.
Hebrews 8:10 For this is the covenant which I will make with the house of Israel after those days, says the Lord: Putting my laws into their understanding, I will also inscribe them upon their hearts, and I will be God to them, and they will be a people to me.
Hebrews 8:11 And they will certainly not teach, each his neighbor and each his brother, saying: Know the Lord; because all will know me, from their small to their great.
Hebrews 8:12 Because I will be merciful to their unrighteousness, and their sins and their lawless deeds I will certainly remember no more.
Hebrews 8:13 In saying: New, he has made the first old. But what is becoming old and aging is near disappearance.

## Chapter 9

Hebrews 9:1 Therefore the first tent also indeed had ordinances of worship and the earthly sanctuary.
Hebrews 9:2 For a tent was prepared, the first, in which were both the lampstand and the table and the presentation of the loaves, which is called the Holy Place.
Hebrews 9:3 But after the second curtain was a tent called the Holy of Holies,
Hebrews 9:4 having a golden censer and the ark of the covenant covered on all sides with gold, in which were a golden jar containing the manna, and Aaron's rod that sprouted, and the tablets of the covenant.
Hebrews 9:5 And above it were cherubim of glory overshadowing the place of atonement, concerning which it is not now possible to speak in detail.
Hebrews 9:6 Now these things having been thus prepared, the priests continually enter into the first tent, performing the services of worship.
Hebrews 9:7 But into the second, the high priest alone once a year, not without blood, which he offers for himself and the ignorant offenses of the people,
Hebrews 9:8 the Holy Spirit indicating this: that the way of the holy places has not yet been manifested while the first tent still has standing,
Hebrews 9:9 which is a parable for the present time, according to which both gifts and sacrifices are offered that cannot perfect the worshiper with respect to conscience,
Hebrews 9:10 being imposed only in foods and drinks and various washings and ordinances of flesh until a time of rectification.
Hebrews 9:11 But Christ, having come as high priest of the coming good things, through the greater and more perfect tent, not made by hands, that is, not of this creation,
Hebrews 9:12 nor through the blood of goats and calves, but through his own blood, entered once for all into the holy places, having obtained eternal redemption.
Hebrews 9:13 For if the blood of bulls and goats, and ashes of a heifer sprinkling those who have been defiled, sanctify for the cleanness of the flesh,
Hebrews 9:14 how much more will the blood of Christ, who through the eternal Spirit offered himself without blemish to God, cleanse your conscience from dead works to serve the living God?
Hebrews 9:15 And because of this he is mediator of a new covenant, so that, a death having taken place for redemption of the transgressions under the first covenant, those called may receive the promise of the eternal inheritance.
Hebrews 9:16 For where there is a testament, it is necessary that the death of the one who made it be brought forward.
Hebrews 9:17 For a testament is firm upon the dead, since it never has force while the one who made it lives.
Hebrews 9:18 Therefore not even the first has been inaugurated without blood.
Hebrews 9:19 For when every commandment according to the law had been spoken by Moses to all the people, taking the blood of the calves and goats with water and scarlet wool and hyssop, he sprinkled both the book itself and all the people,
Hebrews 9:20 saying: This is the blood of the covenant which God commanded for you.
Hebrews 9:21 And he likewise sprinkled with the blood both the tent and all the vessels of the ministry.
Hebrews 9:22 And almost everything is cleansed with blood according to the law, and without shedding of blood forgiveness does not take place.
Hebrews 9:23 Therefore it was necessary for the copies of the things in the heavens to be cleansed with these, but the heavenly things themselves with better sacrifices than these.
Hebrews 9:24 For Christ did not enter holy places made by hands, counterparts of the true ones, but into heaven itself, now to appear before the face of God on our behalf,
Hebrews 9:25 nor so that he might offer himself often, as the high priest enters into the holy places year by year with another's blood.
Hebrews 9:26 Since then he would have had to suffer often from the foundation of the world; but now once, at the consummation of the ages, he has been manifested for the setting aside of sin through his sacrifice.
Hebrews 9:27 And just as it is appointed for men to die once, and after this judgment,
Hebrews 9:28 so Christ also, having been offered once to bear the sins of many, will appear a second time, apart from sin, to those eagerly awaiting him, for salvation.

## Chapter 10

Hebrews 10:1 For the law, having a shadow of the coming good things, not the very image of the things, can never, by the same sacrifices which they offer continually year by year, perfect those approaching.
Hebrews 10:2 Otherwise, would they not have ceased being offered, because the worshipers, having been cleansed once, would no longer have any consciousness of sins?
Hebrews 10:3 But in them there is a reminder of sins year by year.
Hebrews 10:4 For it is impossible for the blood of bulls and goats to take away sins.
Hebrews 10:5 Therefore, entering into the world, he says: Sacrifice and offering you did not desire, but a body you prepared for me.
Hebrews 10:6 In whole burnt offerings and offerings for sin you did not take pleasure.
Hebrews 10:7 Then I said: Behold, I have come, in the roll of the book it is written concerning me, to do your will, O God.
Hebrews 10:8 Saying above: Sacrifice and offering and whole burnt offerings and offerings for sin you did not desire, nor did you take pleasure in them, which are offered according to the law,
Hebrews 10:9 then he has said: Behold, I have come to do your will, O God. He takes away the first so that he may establish the second.
Hebrews 10:10 By this will we are sanctified through the offering of the body of Jesus Christ once for all.
Hebrews 10:11 And every priest indeed stands daily ministering and often offering the same sacrifices, which can never take away sins.
Hebrews 10:12 But he, having offered one sacrifice for sins continually, sat down at the right hand of God,
Hebrews 10:13 from then on awaiting until his enemies are placed as a footstool for his feet.
Hebrews 10:14 For by one offering he has perfected continually those being sanctified.
Hebrews 10:15 And the Holy Spirit also testifies to us; for after having said beforehand:
Hebrews 10:16 This is the covenant which I will make with them after those days, says the Lord: Putting my laws upon their hearts, I will also inscribe them upon their understandings,
Hebrews 10:17 and their sins and their lawless deeds I will certainly remember no more.
Hebrews 10:18 Now where there is forgiveness of these, there is no longer an offering for sin.
Hebrews 10:19 Therefore, brothers, having boldness for entrance into the holy places by the blood of Jesus,
Hebrews 10:20 which he inaugurated for us as a new and living way through the curtain, that is, his flesh,
Hebrews 10:21 and a great priest over the house of God,
Hebrews 10:22 let us approach with a true heart in full assurance of faith, having our hearts sprinkled from an evil conscience and our body washed with pure water.
Hebrews 10:23 Let us hold fast the confession of hope without wavering, for the one who promised is faithful.
Hebrews 10:24 And let us consider one another for the stirring up of love and good works,
Hebrews 10:25 not abandoning the gathering together of ourselves, as is the custom of some, but encouraging, and so much more as you see the day approaching.
Hebrews 10:26 For if we sin willingly after receiving the knowledge of the truth, there no longer remains a sacrifice for sins,
Hebrews 10:27 but a certain fearful expectation of judgment and a zeal of fire about to devour the adversaries.
Hebrews 10:28 Anyone having set aside the law of Moses dies without mercies upon two or three witnesses.
Hebrews 10:29 Of how much worse punishment do you think the one will be deemed worthy who has trampled the Son of God, and regarded as common the blood of the covenant by which he was sanctified, and insulted the Spirit of grace?
Hebrews 10:30 For we know the one who said: Vengeance is mine; I will repay, says the Lord. And again: The Lord will judge his people.
Hebrews 10:31 It is fearful to fall into the hands of the living God.
Hebrews 10:32 But recall the earlier days in which, having been enlightened, you endured a great struggle of sufferings,
Hebrews 10:33 partly being publicly exposed to both reproaches and afflictions, and partly having become partners of those living thus.
Hebrews 10:34 For you also sympathized with my bonds, and accepted with joy the plundering of your possessions, knowing that you have in yourselves a better and abiding possession in the heavens.
Hebrews 10:35 Therefore do not throw away your boldness, which has a great recompense.
Hebrews 10:36 For you have need of endurance, so that, having done the will of God, you may receive the promise.
Hebrews 10:37 For yet a very little while, the coming one will come and will not delay.
Hebrews 10:38 But the righteous one will live by faith, and if he draws back, my soul takes no pleasure in him.
Hebrews 10:39 But we are not of drawing back to destruction, but of faith to the preservation of the soul.

## Chapter 11

Hebrews 11:1 Now faith is the substance of things hoped for, the proof of things not seen.
Hebrews 11:2 For by this the elders were testified to.
Hebrews 11:3 By faith we understand that the ages have been fitted together by the word of God, so that the things seen have not come into being from things appearing.
Hebrews 11:4 By faith Abel offered to God a greater sacrifice than Cain, through which he was testified to be righteous, God testifying concerning his gifts; and through it, having died, he is still spoken of.
Hebrews 11:5 By faith Enoch was transferred so as not to see death, and he was not found because God transferred him; for before his transfer he has been testified to have pleased God.
Hebrews 11:6 But without faith it is impossible to please him; for the one approaching God must believe that he exists and becomes a rewarder of those seeking him out.
Hebrews 11:7 By faith Noah, having been warned concerning things not yet seen, moved with reverence, prepared an ark for the salvation of his household, through which he condemned the world and became an heir of the righteousness according to faith.
Hebrews 11:8 By faith Abraham, being called, obeyed to go out to the place which he was about to receive as an inheritance, and he went out not knowing where he was going.
Hebrews 11:9 By faith he sojourned in the land of the promise as in a foreign land, dwelling in tents with Isaac and Jacob, the fellow heirs of the same promise.
Hebrews 11:10 For he was awaiting the city having the foundations, whose craftsman and maker is God.
Hebrews 11:11 By faith Sarah herself also received power for the depositing of seed, and beyond the time of age she gave birth, since she regarded the one who promised as faithful.
Hebrews 11:12 Therefore also from one, and that one having been deadened, were born as the stars of heaven in multitude and as the innumerable sand beside the lip of the sea.
Hebrews 11:13 According to faith all these died, not having received the promises, but having seen them from afar and been persuaded and greeted them, and confessed that they are strangers and sojourners upon the earth.
Hebrews 11:14 For those saying such things make evident that they seek a homeland.
Hebrews 11:15 And if indeed they were remembering that one from which they went out, they would have had opportunity to return.
Hebrews 11:16 But now they desire a better one, that is, a heavenly one; therefore God is not ashamed of them, to be called their God, for he prepared a city for them.
Hebrews 11:17 By faith Abraham, being tested, has offered Isaac, and the one who received the promises was offering his only-begotten,
Hebrews 11:18 to whom it was spoken: In Isaac a seed will be called for you,
Hebrews 11:19 reckoning that God is able even to raise from the dead, from where he also received him back in a parable.
Hebrews 11:20 By faith Isaac blessed Jacob and Esau concerning coming things.
Hebrews 11:21 By faith Jacob, dying, blessed each of the sons of Joseph and bowed in worship upon the top of his staff.
Hebrews 11:22 By faith Joseph, coming to his end, made mention of the exodus of the sons of Israel and gave orders concerning his bones.
Hebrews 11:23 By faith Moses, having been born, was hidden for three months by his parents, because they saw that the child was beautiful, and they did not fear the decree of the king.
Hebrews 11:24 By faith Moses, having become grown, refused to be called a son of Pharaoh's daughter,
Hebrews 11:25 having chosen rather to suffer ill treatment with the people of God than to have temporary enjoyment of sin,
Hebrews 11:26 having regarded the reproach of Christ as greater wealth than the treasures in Egypt, for he was looking toward the recompense.
Hebrews 11:27 By faith he left Egypt, not fearing the wrath of the king, for he persevered as seeing the invisible one.
Hebrews 11:28 By faith he has kept the Passover and the sprinkling of the blood, so that the one destroying the firstborn might not touch them.
Hebrews 11:29 By faith they crossed the Red Sea as through dry land, of which the Egyptians, having made an attempt, were swallowed up.
Hebrews 11:30 By faith the walls of Jericho fell, having been encircled for seven days.
Hebrews 11:31 By faith Rahab the prostitute did not perish together with those who disobeyed, having received the spies with peace.
Hebrews 11:32 And what more do I say? For time will fail me while recounting concerning Gideon, and Barak and Samson and Jephthah, and David and Samuel and the prophets,
Hebrews 11:33 who through faith conquered kingdoms, worked righteousness, obtained promises, shut the mouths of lions,
Hebrews 11:34 quenched the power of fire, escaped the edges of the sword, were strengthened from weakness, became strong in war, put to flight armies of foreigners.
Hebrews 11:35 Women received their dead by resurrection; but others were tortured, not accepting release, so that they might obtain a better resurrection.
Hebrews 11:36 And others received trial of mockings and scourges, and further of bonds and imprisonment.
Hebrews 11:37 They were stoned, they were sawn apart, they were tempted, they died by slaughter of the sword; they went about in sheepskins, in goatskins, being in need, afflicted, ill-treated,
Hebrews 11:38 of whom the world was not worthy, wandering in deserts and mountains and caves and the holes of the earth.
Hebrews 11:39 And all these, having been testified to through faith, did not receive the promise,
Hebrews 11:40 God having foreseen something better concerning us, so that they might not be perfected apart from us.

## Chapter 12

Hebrews 12:1 Therefore we also, having so great a cloud of witnesses surrounding us, having laid aside every weight and the easily entangling sin, let us run with endurance the contest set before us,
Hebrews 12:2 looking away to Jesus, the founder and perfecter of faith, who for the joy set before him endured a cross, despising shame, and has sat down at the right hand of the throne of God.
Hebrews 12:3 For consider the one who has endured such opposition from sinners against himself, so that you may not grow weary, fainting in your souls.
Hebrews 12:4 You have not yet resisted to the point of blood, struggling against sin.
Hebrews 12:5 And you have forgotten the exhortation which addresses you as sons: My son, do not regard lightly the discipline of the Lord, nor faint when reproved by him.
Hebrews 12:6 For whom the Lord loves he disciplines, and he scourges every son whom he receives.
Hebrews 12:7 If you endure discipline, God deals with you as sons; for what son is there whom a father does not discipline?
Hebrews 12:8 But if you are without discipline, of which all have become partakers, then you are illegitimate and not sons.
Hebrews 12:9 Furthermore, we had the fathers of our flesh as disciplinarians and respected them; will we not much more be subjected to the Father of spirits and live?
Hebrews 12:10 For they indeed disciplined for a few days according to what seemed good to them, but he for what is beneficial, for partaking of his holiness.
Hebrews 12:11 Now all discipline for the present does not seem to be of joy but of grief; but afterward it gives back a peaceful fruit of righteousness to those trained through it.
Hebrews 12:12 Therefore straighten the hanging hands and the paralyzed knees,
Hebrews 12:13 and make straight paths for your feet, so that the lame thing may not be turned aside, but rather be healed.
Hebrews 12:14 Pursue peace with all, and sanctification, without which no one will see the Lord,
Hebrews 12:15 watching lest anyone fall short of the grace of God, lest any root of bitterness growing upward cause trouble, and through this many be defiled,
Hebrews 12:16 lest anyone be a fornicator or profane like Esau, who for one meal sold his birthright.
Hebrews 12:17 For you know that even afterward, wishing to inherit the blessing, he was rejected; for he found no place for repentance, although he sought it out with tears.
Hebrews 12:18 For you have not approached a mountain that can be touched and burned with fire, and gloom and darkness and tempest,
Hebrews 12:19 and a trumpet's sound and a voice of words, which those hearing begged that no further word be added to them.
Hebrews 12:20 For they could not bear what was commanded: Even if a beast touches the mountain, it will be stoned or shot down with a missile.
Hebrews 12:21 And so fearful was what appeared that Moses said: I am terrified and trembling.
Hebrews 12:22 But you have approached Mount Zion and the city of the living God, heavenly Jerusalem, and myriads of angels,
Hebrews 12:23 a festal assembly and church of firstborn ones enrolled in the heavens, and God the judge of all, and spirits of righteous ones perfected,
Hebrews 12:24 and Jesus, mediator of a new covenant, and blood of sprinkling speaking better things than Abel.
Hebrews 12:25 See that you do not refuse the one speaking. For if those did not escape who refused the one giving warning on earth, much more we who turn away from the one from the heavens.
Hebrews 12:26 Whose voice shook the earth then, but now he has promised, saying: Yet once I shake not only the earth but also heaven.
Hebrews 12:27 Now the phrase: Yet once, indicates the removal of the things shaken, as things made, so that the things not shaken may remain.
Hebrews 12:28 Therefore, receiving an unshakable kingdom, let us have grace, through which we may serve God acceptably with modesty and reverence.
Hebrews 12:29 For our God is also a consuming fire.

## Chapter 13

Hebrews 13:1 Let brotherly love remain.
Hebrews 13:2 Do not forget hospitality, for through this some entertained angels without knowing it.
Hebrews 13:3 Remember the prisoners as bound together with them, those being ill-treated as being yourselves also in a body.
Hebrews 13:4 Marriage is honorable among all, and the bed undefiled; but fornicators and adulterers God will judge.
Hebrews 13:5 Let your manner be without love of money, being content with the things present; for he himself has said: I will certainly not leave you, nor will I certainly abandon you.
Hebrews 13:6 So that, being confident, we say: The Lord is my helper, and I will not fear; what will man do to me?
Hebrews 13:7 Remember your leaders, who spoke the word of God to you, whose faith imitate, considering the outcome of their conduct.
Hebrews 13:8 Jesus Christ is the same yesterday and today and forever.
Hebrews 13:9 Do not be carried about by various and foreign teachings; for it is good for the heart to be established by grace, not by foods, in which those who walked were not benefited.
Hebrews 13:10 We have an altar from which those serving the tent have no authority to eat.
Hebrews 13:11 For the bodies of those animals whose blood is brought into the holy places for sin through the high priest are burned outside the camp.
Hebrews 13:12 Therefore Jesus also, so that he might sanctify the people through his own blood, suffered outside the gate.
Hebrews 13:13 Therefore let us go out to him outside the camp, bearing his reproach.
Hebrews 13:14 For we do not have here an abiding city, but we seek the coming one.
Hebrews 13:15 Through him therefore let us continually offer a sacrifice of praise to God, that is, fruit of lips confessing his name.
Hebrews 13:16 But do not forget doing good and sharing, for with such sacrifices God is pleased.
Hebrews 13:17 Obey your leaders and yield, for they keep watch over your souls as those who will give an account, so that they may do this with joy and not groaning, for this is unprofitable for you.
Hebrews 13:18 Pray concerning us, for we are persuaded that we have a good conscience, wishing to conduct ourselves well in all things.
Hebrews 13:19 But I more abundantly urge you to do this, so that I may be restored to you more quickly.
Hebrews 13:20 Now the God of peace, who brought up from the dead the great shepherd of the sheep, in the blood of an eternal covenant, our Lord Jesus,
Hebrews 13:21 may he fit you in every good work to do his will, doing in you what is pleasing before him through Jesus Christ, to whom be the glory forever and ever. Amen.
Hebrews 13:22 But I urge you, brothers, bear with the word of exhortation, for I have also written to you briefly.
Hebrews 13:23 Know that our brother Timothy has been released, with whom, if he comes more quickly, I will see you.
Hebrews 13:24 Greet all your leaders and all the saints. Those from Italy greet you.
Hebrews 13:25 Grace be with all of you. Amen.

# James

The Apostolic Bible. Public domain. https://apostolic-bible.ysys9.chatgpt.site/license.html


## Chapter 1

James 1:1 James, a slave of God and of the Lord Jesus Christ, to the twelve tribes in the dispersion: Greetings.
James 1:2 Consider it all joy, my brothers, whenever you fall into various trials,
James 1:3 knowing that the testing of your faith produces endurance.
James 1:4 But let endurance have a perfect work, so that you may be perfect and complete, lacking in nothing.
James 1:5 But if any of you lacks wisdom, let him ask from God, who gives to all generously and does not reproach, and it will be given to him.
James 1:6 But let him ask in faith, doubting nothing; for the one doubting resembles a wave of the sea driven and tossed by wind.
James 1:7 For let that man not suppose that he will receive anything from the Lord,
James 1:8 a double-minded man, unstable in all his ways.
James 1:9 But let the lowly brother boast in his elevation,
James 1:10 and the rich in his humiliation, because like a flower of grass he will pass away.
James 1:11 For the sun rose with the scorching heat and dried the grass, and its flower fell off, and the beauty of its appearance perished; so also the rich man will wither in his journeys.
James 1:12 Blessed is a man who endures trial, because, having become approved, he will receive the crown of life which the Lord promised to those loving him.
James 1:13 Let no one being tempted say: I am tempted by God; for God is not tempted by evils, and he himself tempts no one.
James 1:14 But each is tempted, being drawn out and enticed by his own desire.
James 1:15 Then desire, having conceived, gives birth to sin; and sin, having been completed, brings forth death.
James 1:16 Do not be deceived, my beloved brothers.
James 1:17 Every good giving and every perfect gift is from above, coming down from the Father of lights, with whom there is no variation or shadow of turning.
James 1:18 Having willed it, he brought us forth by a word of truth, so that we might be a kind of firstfruits of his creatures.
James 1:19 Therefore, my beloved brothers, let every man be swift to hear, slow to speak, slow to wrath.
James 1:20 For a man's wrath does not produce God's righteousness.
James 1:21 Therefore, laying aside all filthiness and abundance of wickedness, receive in gentleness the implanted word, which is able to save your souls.
James 1:22 But become doers of the word and not hearers only, deceiving yourselves.
James 1:23 Because if anyone is a hearer of the word and not a doer, he resembles a man considering the face of his birth in a mirror.
James 1:24 For he considered himself and has gone away, and immediately forgot what he was like.
James 1:25 But the one having looked into the perfect law, that of freedom, and remained, this one, having become not a forgetful hearer but a doer of work, will be blessed in his doing.
James 1:26 If anyone among you seems to be religious, not bridling his tongue but deceiving his heart, this one's religion is vain.
James 1:27 Religion pure and undefiled before God and the Father is this: to visit orphans and widows in their affliction, to keep oneself unspotted from the world.

## Chapter 2

James 2:1 My brothers, do not hold the faith of our Lord Jesus Christ of glory with partialities.
James 2:2 For if a man with a gold ring enters your assembly in splendid clothing, and a poor man also enters in filthy clothing,
James 2:3 and you look upon the one wearing the splendid clothing and say to him: You sit here in a good place; and to the poor man you say: You stand there, or sit here beneath my footstool,
James 2:4 have you not also made distinctions among yourselves and become judges of evil reasonings?
James 2:5 Listen, my beloved brothers: Did not God choose the poor of this world, rich in faith and heirs of the kingdom which he promised to those loving him?
James 2:6 But you dishonored the poor man. Do not the rich oppress you, and do they themselves not drag you into courts?
James 2:7 Do they themselves not blaspheme the good name invoked upon you?
James 2:8 If indeed you fulfill the royal law according to the Scripture: You shall love your neighbor as yourself, you do well.
James 2:9 But if you show partiality, you work sin, being convicted by the law as transgressors.
James 2:10 For whoever will keep the whole law but stumble in one thing has become guilty of all.
James 2:11 For the one who said: Do not commit adultery, also said: Do not murder. But if you will not commit adultery, but will murder, you have become a transgressor of law.
James 2:12 So speak and so do, as those about to be judged through a law of freedom.
James 2:13 For judgment is merciless to the one who has not done mercy, and mercy boasts over judgment.
James 2:14 What is the benefit, my brothers, if anyone says he has faith but does not have works? Can faith save him?
James 2:15 But if a brother or sister are naked and lacking daily food,
James 2:16 and anyone among you says to them: Go in peace, be warmed and filled, but you do not give them the necessities of the body, what is the benefit?
James 2:17 So also faith, if it does not have works, is dead by itself.
James 2:18 But someone will say: You have faith, and I have works. Show me your faith from your works, and I will show you my faith from my works.
James 2:19 You believe that God is one; you do well. The demons also believe and shudder.
James 2:20 But do you wish to know, O empty man, that faith apart from works is dead?
James 2:21 Was not Abraham our father justified from works, having offered Isaac his son upon the altar?
James 2:22 You see that faith was working together with his works, and from the works faith was perfected.
James 2:23 And the Scripture was fulfilled which says: Abraham believed God, and it was reckoned to him as righteousness; and he was called a friend of God.
James 2:24 Therefore you see that a man is justified from works and not from faith alone.
James 2:25 And likewise was not Rahab the prostitute also justified from works, having received the messengers and sent them out by another way?
James 2:26 For just as the body apart from spirit is dead, so also faith apart from works is dead.

## Chapter 3

James 3:1 Do not become many teachers, my brothers, knowing that we will receive a greater judgment.
James 3:2 For we all stumble in many things. If anyone does not stumble in word, this one is a perfect man, able to bridle also the whole body.
James 3:3 Behold, we put the bridles into the mouths of horses so that they obey us, and we direct their whole body.
James 3:4 Behold also the ships, being so great and driven by harsh winds, are directed by a very small rudder wherever the impulse of the one steering wishes.
James 3:5 So also the tongue is a small member and boasts greatly. Behold, how small a fire kindles how great a forest!
James 3:6 And the tongue is a fire, the world of unrighteousness. So the tongue is set among our members, staining the whole body and setting on fire the wheel of birth, and being set on fire by Gehenna.
James 3:7 For every nature of both beasts and birds, both reptiles and sea creatures, is tamed and has been tamed by human nature.
James 3:8 But no one among men can tame the tongue, an unrestrainable evil, full of death-bearing poison.
James 3:9 With it we bless God and the Father, and with it we curse men who have been made according to God's likeness.
James 3:10 From the same mouth come out blessing and curse. These things ought not to happen thus, my brothers.
James 3:11 Does the spring from the same opening pour forth the sweet and the bitter?
James 3:12 Can a fig tree, my brothers, produce olives, or a vine figs? So no spring can produce salty and sweet water.
James 3:13 Who is wise and knowledgeable among you? Let him show from good conduct his works in gentleness of wisdom.
James 3:14 But if you have bitter jealousy and selfish ambition in your heart, do not boast and lie against the truth.
James 3:15 This is not the wisdom coming down from above, but earthly, natural, demonic.
James 3:16 For where there are jealousy and selfish ambition, there are disorder and every base thing.
James 3:17 But the wisdom from above is first pure, then peaceable, forbearing, readily persuaded, full of mercy and good fruits, without partiality and without hypocrisy.
James 3:18 And a fruit of righteousness is sown in peace by those making peace.

## Chapter 4

James 4:1 From where are wars and battles among you? Are they not from here, from your pleasures waging war in your members?
James 4:2 You desire and do not have; you murder and are jealous and cannot obtain; you battle and wage war. But you do not have because you do not ask.
James 4:3 You ask and do not receive because you ask badly, so that you may spend on your pleasures.
James 4:4 Adulterers and adulteresses, do you not know that friendship with the world is enmity with God? Therefore whoever wishes to be a friend of the world is made an enemy of God.
James 4:5 Or do you think that the Scripture speaks vainly: The spirit which dwelt in us yearns toward envy?
James 4:6 But he gives greater grace; therefore he says: God opposes the proud, but gives grace to the humble.
James 4:7 Therefore be subjected to God; resist the devil, and he will flee from you.
James 4:8 Draw near to God, and he will draw near to you. Cleanse your hands, sinners, and purify your hearts, double-minded ones.
James 4:9 Be miserable and mourn and weep. Let your laughter be turned to mourning and your joy to dejection.
James 4:10 Be humbled before the Lord, and he will exalt you.
James 4:11 Do not speak against one another, brothers. The one speaking against a brother and judging his brother speaks against law and judges law. But if you judge law, you are not a doer of law but a judge.
James 4:12 There is one lawgiver, the one able to save and destroy. Who are you who judge the other?
James 4:13 Come now, those saying: Today and tomorrow let us go to this city and spend one year there and trade and gain,
James 4:14 who do not know the thing of tomorrow. For what is your life? For it is a vapor appearing for a little while, then disappearing.
James 4:15 Instead of your saying: If the Lord wills, we shall both live and do this or that.
James 4:16 But now you boast in your arrogances. All such boasting is evil.
James 4:17 Therefore to one knowing to do good and not doing it, it is sin to him.

## Chapter 5

James 5:1 Come now, the rich, weep, howling over your coming miseries.
James 5:2 Your wealth has rotted, and your garments have become moth-eaten.
James 5:3 Your gold and silver have corroded, and their rust will be a testimony to you and will eat your flesh like fire. You stored up treasure in the last days.
James 5:4 Behold, the wage of the workers who reaped your fields, withheld by you, cries out, and the cries of those who harvested have entered into the ears of the Lord of hosts.
James 5:5 You lived luxuriously upon the earth and indulged yourselves; you nourished your hearts as in a day of slaughter.
James 5:6 You condemned, you murdered the righteous one; he does not oppose you.
James 5:7 Therefore be patient, brothers, until the coming of the Lord. Behold, the farmer awaits the precious fruit of the earth, being patient over it until he receives early and late rain.
James 5:8 You also be patient; establish your hearts, because the coming of the Lord has drawn near.
James 5:9 Do not groan against one another, brothers, so that you may not be condemned. Behold, a judge has stood before the doors.
James 5:10 Take as an example of suffering and patience, my brothers, the prophets who spoke in the name of the Lord.
James 5:11 Behold, we call blessed those enduring. You heard the endurance of Job and saw the end of the Lord, that the Lord is very compassionate and merciful.
James 5:12 But before all things, my brothers, do not swear, neither by heaven nor by earth nor any other oath; but let your yes be yes and your no be no, so that you may not fall into hypocrisy.
James 5:13 Does anyone among you suffer? Let him pray. Is anyone cheerful? Let him sing praise.
James 5:14 Is anyone among you sick? Let him call for the elders of the church, and let them pray over him, having anointed him with oil in the name of the Lord.
James 5:15 And the prayer of faith will save the one suffering, and the Lord will raise him; and even if he has committed sins, it will be forgiven him.
James 5:16 Confess to one another the trespasses, and pray for one another so that you may be healed. A righteous man's petition has much strength when at work.
James 5:17 Elijah was a man of like passions with us, and with prayer he prayed that it not rain, and it did not rain upon the earth for three years and six months.
James 5:18 And again he prayed, and heaven gave rain, and the earth sprouted its fruit.
James 5:19 Brothers, if anyone among you wanders from the truth and someone turns him back,
James 5:20 let him know that the one turning a sinner back from the wandering of his way will save a soul from death and cover a multitude of sins.

## Chapter 1

1 Peter 1:4 to an inheritance incorruptible and undefiled and unfading, kept in the heavens for us,

## Chapter 2

1 Peter 2:1 Therefore, laying aside all wickedness and all deceit and hypocrisies and envies and all evil speakings,
1 Peter 2:2 as newborn infants, desire the pure rational milk, so that by it you may grow,
1 Peter 2:3 if indeed you tasted that the Lord is kind.
1 Peter 2:4 Approaching him, a living stone, indeed rejected by men but chosen and honorable before God,
1 Peter 2:5 you yourselves also, as living stones, are being built as a spiritual house, a holy priesthood, to offer spiritual sacrifices acceptable to God through Jesus Christ.
1 Peter 2:6 Therefore it also contains in the Scripture: Behold, I place in Zion a cornerstone, chosen, honorable, and the one believing upon him will certainly not be put to shame.
1 Peter 2:7 Therefore the honor is to you who believe; but to those disobeying: The stone which the builders rejected, this became the head of the corner,
1 Peter 2:8 and a stone of stumbling and a rock of offense; who stumble at the word, disobeying, to which they were also appointed.
1 Peter 2:9 But you are a chosen race, a royal priesthood, a holy nation, a people for possession, so that you may proclaim the excellences of the one who called you out of darkness into his marvelous light,
1 Peter 2:10 who once were not a people, but now a people of God; who had not received mercy, but now have received mercy.
1 Peter 2:11 Beloved, I urge you as strangers and sojourners to abstain from fleshly desires, which wage war against the soul,
1 Peter 2:12 having your conduct good among the nations, so that in what they speak against you as evildoers, having observed the good works, they may glorify God in a day of visitation.
1 Peter 2:13 Therefore be subjected to every human institution because of the Lord, whether to a king as being superior,
1 Peter 2:14 or to governors as sent through him for vengeance upon evildoers but praise of those doing good.
1 Peter 2:15 Because thus is the will of God, by doing good to muzzle the ignorance of foolish men,
1 Peter 2:16 as free, and not having freedom as a covering of wickedness, but as slaves of God.
1 Peter 2:17 Honor all; love the brotherhood; fear God; honor the king.
1 Peter 2:18 Household slaves, being subjected with all fear to the masters, not only to the good and forbearing but also to the crooked.
1 Peter 2:19 For this is grace, if because of consciousness of God someone bears griefs, suffering unjustly.
1 Peter 2:20 For what credit is there if, sinning and being struck, you endure? But if, doing good and suffering, you endure, this is grace before God.
1 Peter 2:21 For to this you were called, because Christ also suffered on our behalf, leaving us an example so that you might follow his footsteps,
1 Peter 2:22 who did not commit sin, nor was deceit found in his mouth,
1 Peter 2:23 who, being reviled, did not revile in return; suffering, did not threaten, but entrusted to the one judging righteously,
1 Peter 2:24 who himself bore our sins in his body upon the wood, so that, having departed from sins, we might live to righteousness; by whose wound you were healed.
1 Peter 2:25 For you were like wandering sheep, but now you turned back to the shepherd and overseer of your souls.

## Chapter 3

1 Peter 3:1 Likewise, wives, being subjected to your own husbands, so that even if any disobey the word, through the conduct of the wives they may be gained without a word,
1 Peter 3:2 having observed your pure conduct in fear.
1 Peter 3:3 Whose adornment let it not be the outward one of braiding hair and putting around gold ornaments or putting on garments,
1 Peter 3:4 but the hidden man of the heart, in the incorruptibility of the gentle and quiet spirit, which is very precious before God.
1 Peter 3:5 For thus once also the holy women hoping upon God adorned themselves, being subjected to their own husbands,

1 Peter 3:9 not giving back evil for evil or reviling for reviling, but on the contrary blessing, knowing that to this you were called, so that you might inherit a blessing.
1 Peter 3:10 For the one wishing to love life and see good days, let him stop his tongue from evil and his lips from speaking deceit.
1 Peter 3:11 Let him turn away from evil and do good; let him seek peace and pursue it.
1 Peter 3:12 Because the eyes of the Lord are upon the righteous, and his ears toward their petition, but the face of the Lord is upon those doing evils.
1 Peter 3:13 And who is the one who will harm you if you become imitators of the good?
1 Peter 3:14 But even if you should suffer because of righteousness, you are blessed. But do not fear their fear, nor be troubled.
1 Peter 3:15 But sanctify the Lord God in your hearts, and be always ready for a defense to everyone asking you an account concerning the hope in you, with gentleness and fear,
1 Peter 3:16 having a good conscience, so that in what they speak against you as evildoers, those abusing your good conduct in Christ may be put to shame.
1 Peter 3:17 For it is better, doing good, if the will of God wills it, to suffer than doing evil.
1 Peter 3:18 Because Christ also suffered once for sins, righteous on behalf of unrighteous, so that he might bring us to God, indeed put to death in flesh but made alive in the Spirit,
1 Peter 3:19 in which also, having gone, he proclaimed to the spirits in prison,
1 Peter 3:20 who once disobeyed, when once the patience of God was waiting in the days of Noah, an ark being prepared, into which a few, that is, eight souls, were brought safely through water.
1 Peter 3:21 Which also now saves us as a counterpart, baptism, not a removal of dirt of flesh, but a request of a good conscience toward God, through the resurrection of Jesus Christ,
1 Peter 3:22 who is at the right hand of God, having gone into heaven, angels and authorities and powers having been subjected to him.

## Chapter 4

1 Peter 4:10 Each, as he received a gift, ministering it to yourselves as good stewards of the varied grace of God.

1 Peter 4:18 And if the righteous one is scarcely saved, where will the ungodly and sinner appear?
1 Peter 4:19 Therefore also let those suffering according to the will of God entrust their own souls to a faithful creator in doing good.

## Chapter 5
